summary:
Collagen is a structural protein that supports skin, tendons, bones, cartilage, muscles, blood vessels and organs, but its natural production declines with age. The body makes collagen from amino acids, including glycine and proline, plus vitamin C, zinc and copper. Types I, II and III are the main forms in oral supplements, while 28 types exist in the body.

Supplements are most commonly animal-derived, including marine collagen from fish and collagen from cows, pigs and chickens. They may also be unprocessed, gelatin or hydrolysed; research indicates hydrolysed collagen is quickly digested and absorbed and may be the most effective form.

Reported benefits include improved skin firmness and wrinkle reduction, stronger nails, bone support, reduced joint pain, and support for tendons, ligaments and muscle repair. Evidence for thicker hair is limited to mouse studies. Suggested daily doses range from 2.5 grams for joint, skin and hydration benefits to 15 grams for muscle mass with resistance training; 5 grams may improve bone density in postmenopausal people with osteopenia. Research remains ongoing, and third-party-tested products are recommended.

A balanced diet rich in animal proteins, vitamin C foods and bone broth is described as the most reliable way to support natural collagen production.

XYZprinting invited customers and qualified resellers to see the MfgPro220 xPF ultrafast 3D printer at booth #2142 in the Fort Worth Convention Center, April 24–28, 2018. Priced at $19,950, it has a 16-liter build volume, twice that of other contenders, and supports functional prototyping, production tooling, and end-use parts. Its software and integrated sensors optimize performance, provide diagnostics, and enable monitoring, while machine-learning algorithms slice, optimize, and adaptively compile complex geometries. On-board and cloud controls support local or remote operation of one or multiple printers for mass production. The printer uses LSPc technology and a structured light matrix to reach 1Z cm per minute, reducing precision-part print cycles from hours to minutes. XYZprinting also announced a dental-printing partnership with BEGO and Nexa3D, under which BEGO will exclusively market and sell a special-purpose Nexa3D dental printer manufactured by XYZprinting, while Nexa3D will develop the required technology and products.

Sensient Technologies reported quarterly EPS of $0.80, beating the Zacks consensus of $0.78 by $0.02. It posted a 9.13% net margin and 16.73% ROE, with a $3.48 billion market cap. The company announced a $0.30 quarterly dividend, annualized at $1.20 with a 1.53% yield and 42.70% payout ratio. KeyCorp raised its price target to $84 with an “overweight” rating, while Zacks upgraded the shares from “sell” to “hold.”

The medRxiv technical report, posted January 3, 2024, is titled “Phase angle clusters in bioimpedance: An alternative to body mass index.” It covers an introduction, objective, methodology, cluster analysis, discussion, and conclusion. The preprint has not been peer reviewed and should not be used to guide clinical practice.

The lecturer introduces MIT’s course on discrete stochastic processes, emphasizing that the central challenge in probability is not solving well-posed exercises but choosing appropriate models for real-world problems. He stresses that no model is perfect and should balance explanatory power against complexity, citing Alfred North Whitehead’s advice to “seek simplicity and distrust it.” He warns that sound mathematics can still produce poor decisions when underlying models are flawed. Planned topics include probability and stochastic-process models, applications, axioms, independence, experiments, and random variables, followed by counting and Poisson processes, renewal processes, Markov chains, random walks, and martingales. Applications include communications and networks, computer systems, queuing, risk and catastrophe management, biology, medicine, operations research, and control systems.

A probability model consists of a sample space, events as subsets of that space, and a probability measure satisfying Kolmogorov’s axioms: the whole space has probability one, event probabilities are nonnegative, and probabilities are additive over disjoint countable sequences. Consequences include zero probability for the empty set, complement and containment rules, and the union bound. The lecture also reviews independent events and Cartesian products of probability models, noting that independent combinations preserve the axioms. A random variable is defined as a function from sample points to finite real values whose inverse threshold sets are events. Its distribution function therefore always exists and accommodates discrete, continuous, and mixed variables. The lecture concludes by encouraging rigorous, self-critical proofs that combine intuition with formal reasoning for analyzing complex systems.

The Weather Channel is launching a 3.2MB Android app for emerging markets in Asia, Latin America and Africa. It uses IBM mesh networking over Bluetooth and Wi-Fi to relay information directly between phones 200–500 feet apart, allowing alerts to spread when centralized networks fail. Designed for developing countries and slow 2G networks, it adds no more battery burden than an app and needs no network reconfiguration. Digital signatures verify trusted sources and unmodified messages; wider mesh use depends on enough users running the app.

Tesla Motors, Inc.’s unaudited Form 10-Q for the quarter ended March 31, 2016 reported revenue of $1.15 billion, up from $939.9 million, primarily due to Model X deliveries and growth in vehicles accounted for as leases. Automotive revenue was $1.03 billion, while services and other revenue rose to $121.0 million from $46.6 million. Gross profit declined to $252.5 million from $260.1 million, and gross margin fell to 22.0% from 27.7%, mainly because of a product mix shift toward Model X and lower-priced Model S variants. Operating expenses increased to $500.7 million, including $182.5 million of R&D and $318.2 million of selling, general and administrative expenses. The company reported an operating loss of $248.2 million, net loss of $282.3 million, or $2.13 per share, and comprehensive loss of $265.1 million.

At March 31, 2016, Tesla had $1.44 billion in cash and cash equivalents, total assets of $9.19 billion, total liabilities of $8.18 billion, and stockholders’ equity of $970.4 million. Operating activities used $249.6 million of cash, investing activities used $233.8 million, and financing activities provided $715.4 million, resulting in a $244.9 million increase in cash.

Tesla reported producing 15,510 vehicles in the quarter, including about 2,650 Model X vehicles, and had delivered more than 122,000 vehicles through March 31. It unveiled the lower-priced Model 3 and received more than 325,000 reservations within one week. Management expected 80,000–90,000 Model S and Model X deliveries in 2016, Model 3 volume production and deliveries in late 2017, and an overall production goal of 500,000 vehicles in 2018. The company planned more than 70 additional retail and service locations and approximately 250 additional Supercharger locations in 2016. Capital expenditures were expected to be about 50% above the prior $1.5 billion estimate, while operating expenses were expected to increase approximately 20%–25%.

The Gigafactory was being developed to integrate battery-material, cell, module and pack production, with cell production expected in the fourth quarter of 2016 and Panasonic identified as a production partner. Tesla also disclosed residual-value and customer-credit risks from its financing and leasing programs, Model X ramp challenges and supplier constraints, and a pending appeal in a dismissed securities class-action lawsuit.

The message returns a House bill that would donate public lands to the states to establish colleges emphasizing agriculture and mechanic arts. Each state would receive 20,000 acres for every senator and representative in the current Congress, plus 20,000 acres for each additional representative apportioned under the 1860 census. The Interior Department estimated the grants at 6.06 million acres, worth $7.575 million at the minimum government price of $1.25 per acre. States lacking qualifying public lands would receive land scrip to sell for equivalent funds. States would have five years to establish at least one college; otherwise, the grant would terminate, previously received proceeds would be repaid, and titles to purchasers would remain valid. States would also have to replace any losses or reductions in the funds.

The message argues that the bill is inexpedient and unconstitutional. It contends that the grants would flood the land market with scrip, depress government land prices, and nearly eliminate an estimated $5 million in annual public-land revenue. This would impair the Treasury precisely when federal finances were strained and could reduce the value of public lands used as security for loans during war.

It further argues that transferring public lands for state educational purposes would blur the constitutional boundary between federal and state governments, encourage states to rely on the federal Treasury, remove the incentive to raise taxes responsibly, and weaken the federal government’s ability to perform its duties. The grants could also harm new states by allowing speculators to acquire choice lands cheaply and resell them to actual settlers at higher prices.

The message also questions whether the colleges would effectively advance agriculture and the mechanic arts. Although state legislatures would be required to administer the trusts properly, the federal government would have no practical power to enforce their use of the funds. The bill might instead create federally supported rival colleges that undermine existing state institutions, which already taught agriculture and depended on limited resources. Direct grants for agricultural and mechanical professorships in existing colleges would be preferable and would permit enforcement through the courts. Moreover, congressional representatives might compete over how to distribute funds within their states.

Constitutionally, the message maintains that Congress cannot tax the public to educate state populations and that the power to “dispose of” federal property does not authorize unlimited land grants. Congress is a trustee of the public domain and may sell or otherwise manage it to advance legitimate federal purposes, but not give it away for any desired state purpose. Land purchased with federal funds remains subject to the same constitutional limits as the money used to buy it. Earlier educational land grants to new states were defended as prudent measures to encourage settlement and increase land values, but the message distinguishes them from grants to colleges in every state, which would not serve that limited purpose.

Blue Cross Blue Shield of Mississippi awarded Bell Academy a November 2016 grant that enabled construction of a new indoor P.E. building behind the school. Parent and community volunteers built the steel structure, which includes basketballs, exercise mats, stack cups, hula hoops and more. Teacher Joyce Aycock and students said the dedicated space allows more activities and reduces noise. A rock-climbing wall is planned before Friday’s ribbon-cutting ceremony.

Bethesda announced that Wolfenstein II: The New Colossus will release on Nintendo Switch on June 29, digitally and physically. Cartridge-based play will still require a download, and the Switch’s limited internal storage may necessitate a microSD card.

The Drive concept pairs a tight end’s 10–12-yard in-cut with a slot receiver’s 3–4-yard shallow crossing route from the same side. It creates a natural triangle read, stresses linebackers, and can function as either a primary or secondary read. It is most effective against man coverage, where the routes force defenders to keep moving, and against Cover 4, where the post route can stress the safety. It is less effective against Cover 2 and Cover 3 because their underneath defenders outnumber the offense’s short options.

Against zone, the tight end and slot receiver should sit their routes in open voids. The quarterback may consider the post route presnap, then progress from the X receiver’s go route to the slot shallow cross, tight end basic route, and running back check-down. Variations include using Drive with bunch formations to create picks and rubs or attaching it to backside schemes as a quick throw against blitzes and a reliable outlet.

Council traffic officials are coordinating roadworks and adjusting traffic management around Southway, Tamerton Foliot, Tavistock Road, Budshead Roundabout and the Derriford Transport Scheme to reduce congestion. They are working with utility companies to schedule disruptive work during off-peak periods, monitoring traffic, changing signal timings, adjusting lane arrangements and suspending bus lane restrictions where necessary. Temporary signals on Tamerton Foliot Road are limited to 9.30am–2.30pm, while proposed lane-marking changes at Budshead Roundabout are under safety review. Disruptive works are publicized through the council’s roadworks page, alerts, media, social media, digital signs and warning boards.

The Department of Higher Education and Training is working to integrate NSFAS with college and university systems ahead of free higher education, amid delayed payments and protests. Minister Naledi Pandor instructed NSFAS and institutions to urgently resolve outstanding funding cases. Integration problems have impeded registration data, bursary agreements and funding allocations. The department plans to review NSFAS processes, strengthen coordination and expand administrative capacity, with R105 million allocated over the medium term. Nearly R7.2 billion in additional 2018 funding will increase NSFAS support to just over R35.3 billion by 2020–21. The DA requested an urgent meeting after the minister failed to specify how many students remain unpaid, why, and when they will receive funding.

ADT is presented as undervalued relative to newly listed peer Verisure due to strong revenue growth, improving profitability, high recurring revenue, partnerships with Google and State Farm, debt reduction, and aggressive buybacks contributing to an 11% shareholder yield. Customer churn and flat subscriber numbers remain challenges, though AI, remote-assistance, and smart-home investments aim to improve retention. Applying a 12–14x P/E suggests potential upside exceeding 33%. The author discloses a long ADT position and states that the article expresses personal views.

U.S. Minister H. N. Allen reported that Kim Ok-kiun, leader of the 1884 revolution, was assassinated in Shanghai by Korean Hong Chong-oo. China surrendered Hong to Korean authorities, and he and Kim’s body arrived at Chemulpo aboard a Chinese gunboat. Kim’s body was taken to Seoul, mutilated, and parts were distributed around Korea. Japanese police had seized Hong from the Korean legation, and Japanese minister Otori protested the mutilation, while diplomatic representatives advised against interference in the Korean custom.

U.S. official Sill also reported unrest in Korea’s three southern provinces, where people had risen against oppressive officials, killing some and destroying property. Similar conditions existed elsewhere, prompting fears of a wider uprising. At the Korean government’s request, Sill informed Admiral Skerrett and sought a ship at Chemulpo, recalled American missionaries from the interior, and recommended more frequent U.S. ship visits to maintain an American presence.

Joe Bryant’s Week 10 Cheatsheets issue evaluates NFL fantasy-football passing and rushing matchups using four-week performance and season fantasy points allowed. Bryant cautions that matchup information is only one tool for start/sit decisions. A new “On Target” feature links to first-half 2000 intended-pass targets for wide receivers.

The passing guide assesses each offense in 15 games. Offensive locks are New Orleans over San Francisco, San Diego over Seattle, Oakland over Kansas City, Green Bay over Minnesota, and Indianapolis over Chicago; Kansas City–Oakland is favorable to both offenses. Prime offensive matchups are Carolina–St. Louis, Buffalo–New England, Miami–Detroit, Chicago–Indianapolis, New England–Buffalo, Seattle–San Diego, and Minnesota–Green Bay. Even games are Detroit–Miami, St. Louis–Carolina, Baltimore–Cincinnati, Denver–New York Jets, New York Jets–Denver, and Tampa Bay–Atlanta. Downside matchups favor Washington over Arizona, Atlanta over Tampa Bay, Dallas and Philadelphia over each other, San Francisco over New Orleans, and the New York Giants over Cleveland. Defensive slam dunks are Tennessee–Pittsburgh, Cincinnati–Baltimore, Cleveland–New York Giants, Arizona–Washington, and Pittsburgh–Tennessee.

Prominent passing projections include quarterbacks Jeff Blake, Jim Harbaugh, Rich Gannon, Brett Favre, Peyton Manning, Elvis Grbac, Doug Flutie, Jim Miller, Daunte Culpepper, Trent Green, Trent Dilfer, Brian Greise, Vinny Testeverde, and Shaun King. Highlighted receivers include Joe Horn, Freddie Jones, Tim Brown, Bill Schroeder, Marvin Harrison, Tony Gonzalez, Eric Moulds, Marcus Robinson, Wayne Chrebet, Laveranues Coles, Cris Carter, Randy Moss, and Keyshawn Johnson. Brad Johnson’s knee injury made Jeff George Washington’s starter; Irving Fryar was questionable, while Albert Connell and James Thrash were probable. Jon Kitna started for Seattle while Brock Huard recovered from a concussion, and Ricky Watters was questionable. Carolina lacked receiver Wesley Walls and had uncertainty at tight end, while Terrell Davis was expected to return for Denver.

The rushing guide lists six offensive locks: Stephen Davis against Arizona, Ron Dayne and Tiki Barber against Cleveland, Curtis Martin against Denver, Edgerrin James against Chicago, Ricky Williams against San Francisco, and Warrick Dunn and Mike Alstott against Atlanta. Prime offensive matchups favor Terrell Davis against the Jets, Marshall Faulk against Carolina, a San Diego committee against Seattle, and an unclear Philadelphia committee against Dallas. Even matchups list Jamal Anderson, Sammy Morris and Shawn Bryson, Lamar Smith, Jamal Lewis, Emmitt Smith, James Allen, Napoleon Kaufman, and Ahman Green. Downside rushing matchups include Tshimanga Biakabutuka, Robert Smith, the Oakland committee against Oakland, Seattle’s Shaun Alexander and Ricky Watters, James Stewart, Corey Dillon, and Arizona’s Thomas Jones and Michael Pittman. Defensive slam dunks are Travis Prentice against the Giants, Charlie Garner against the Saints, J.R. Redmond and Kevin Faulk against Buffalo, Eddie George against Pittsburgh, and Jerome Bettis against Tennessee.

This document specifies the Versioned Chip Endorsement Key (VCEK) certificate and AMD Key Distribution System (KDS) interface used to retrieve certificate information for SEV-SNP environments. It defines terms including the product-specific AMD Root Key (ARK), which serves as the root certificate authority, and the AMD SEV Key (ASK), which acts as the intermediate authority that signs VCEK certificates.

VCEK certificates are X.509v3 certificates associated with an ECDSA key unique to each AMD chip running a specific Trusted Compute Base (TCB) version. Certificates are generated when requested and are not stored by KDS. They are backdated one day and remain valid for seven years; ARK and ASK certificates are valid for 25 years. Custom extensions describe TCB components. Family 19h products use 128-character hexadecimal hardware IDs, while Family 1Ah products such as Turin use 16-character IDs. Product names are determined from CPUID Family/Model/Stepping information.

The KDS provides an HTTPS interface using TLS 1.2 for retrieving individual VCEK certificates, product-specific ARK and ASK certificate chains, and certificate revocation lists. Certificates are returned in PEM format, while CRLs use DER format. The interface documents parameter ranges, HTTP error responses, and rate-limit handling, including honoring `Retry-After` for HTTP 429 responses.

The service accepts legal SPL values beyond currently released firmware levels, allowing customers to pre-fetch and cache certificates for anticipated TCB upgrades. The document also covers PSN-based hardware IDs, Turin support, updated TCB structures, and certificate validity guard-band changes.

Mauricio Pochettino named a 26-player U.S. men’s national team roster for October friendlies in Austin on Oct. 10 and Commerce City four days later. Players report for training camp in Austin on Oct. 4. The squad is composed mostly of expected regulars after September’s experimental selections. Christian Pulisic headlines the roster after scoring six goals and adding two assists for AC Milan; Pochettino called him the team’s “most important” player. Weston McKennie returns after missing the March Concacaf Nations League, while Antonee Robinson received his first 2025 call-up following knee surgery. All three opponents have already qualified for the 2026 World Cup.

UPMSP will declare the 2018 Class 10 and Class 12 results on April 29 at 12:30 p.m. Results will be available at upresults.nic.in and upmspresults.up.nic.in. Students can check results using their roll numbers via the websites, SMS to 56263, or other listed result portals.

The team has played three tight, defensive games, but Hasek’s puck-moving and forechecking have made it difficult to establish possession without drawing penalties. Despite some frustration and defensive breakdowns, the players believe the issue can be corrected through video review, tighter play from the defensive zone, and renewed focus. The coaching staff’s adjustments and line combinations are supported, with responsibility for execution resting on the players.

The passage describes a vehicle sensing and driver-assistance system using exterior-facing radar sensors and optional cameras or other sensors. The radar sensor arranges transmitting and receiving antennas as a two-dimensional array. Each transmitter radiates an independently distinguishable waveform, allowing received echoes to be associated with individual transmitters. A control or ECU applies two-dimensional MIMO processing to the receiver outputs, creating an enlarged virtual aperture and enhancing angular accuracy and resolution in both horizontal and vertical directions.

In one embodiment, 12 transmitting antennas arranged in three rows of four and 16 receiving antennas arranged in four columns of four produce 192 virtual receivers. Radar processing detects objects in the sensor’s exterior field and may support object detection, parking assistance, driver alerts, and control of systems such as steering or braking. Listed applications include autonomous or semi-autonomous driving, automated parking, blind-spot and cross-traffic detection, lane-change and merge assistance, emergency braking, pedestrian detection, turn assist, and intersection collision mitigation. Camera data may optionally be fused with radar data and displayed using forward, rearward, side, or surround-view imagery with detected objects highlighted. The application is a continuation of U.S. patent application Ser. No. 16/315,794, now U.S. Patent No. 11,454,719, and claims priority from PCT Application No. PCT/IB2017/054120 and provisional application Ser. No. 62/359,913.

Jennifer Thompson was raped at knifepoint while a college student and identified Ronald Cotton through a composite sketch and lineups, leading to his conviction. Eleven years later, DNA testing showed Bobby Poole was the rapist; while Cotton was imprisoned, Poole raped six other women. Thompson described how questioning can alter traumatic memories and the lasting harm of wrongful conviction. She and Cotton became close friends, finding mutual forgiveness and healing. Thompson found Healing Justice, which brings harmed parties together to share their stories, and Cotton regularly attends its retreats.

Russia’s central bank cut its key rate to 9.25% from 9.75%, signaling possible further reductions as inflation fell. It projected 4% annual consumer inflation by end-2017 and maintained plans for gradual cuts.

The government shutdown continued with little progress as Congress and the White House remained deadlocked over funding. An Oct. 15 pay date for 1.3 million active-duty troops could pressure both sides toward compromise because missing it could trigger public anger and political costs. Economists expected either a short-term continuing resolution or an end to the shutdown by mid-October, though prediction markets assigned a 71% chance it would extend beyond Oct. 14. Other pressures include TSA staffing, delayed mortgage payments for service members, benefit expirations and potential permanent layoffs. Pimco called the first full shutdown since 2013 particularly intractable.

The study develops a CMOS-compatible hybrid quantum-circuit platform combining 100 nm NbN coplanar-waveguide resonators with an n-doped Si/Si₀.₇Ge₀.₃ quantum-well wafer. Four resonators share common feedlines; two λ/4 resonators were characterized, while two λ/2 resonators were excluded because their simulated frequencies were outside the 4–8 GHz band. Fabrication included native-oxide removal, reactive DC sputtering of NbN, electron-beam lithography, CF₄/Ar etching of the superconducting film, and a deep SF₆/C₄F₈ etch of CPW gaps. The approximately 1 μm substrate etch stopped at the graded SiGe buffer and was intended to move substrate–vacuum interfaces and quantum-well charge-noise sources away from high-field regions. TEM/STEM analysis showed atomically resolved, epitaxial SiGe/Si/SiGe layers, while oxygenation and loss of crystallinity were observed in the Si cap, likely due to air exposure during transport.

Two geometrically identical chips with 8 μm resonator widths, 5 μm gaps, and 100 nm NbN films were measured over four cooldowns spanning two years. At 50 mK, the measured fundamental frequencies were approximately 5.04 and 5.57 GHz for sample S1 and 5.08 and 5.60 GHz for S2. A notch-type circle-fit model closely reproduced the S21 measurements and extracted internal, coupling, and loaded quality factors. Across input powers from −140 to −115 dBm, increasing power produced a more pronounced resonance dip and an upward frequency shift of up to 700 kHz, attributed to two-level-system saturation. Coupling quality factors remained nearly constant, whereas loaded quality factors followed internal quality factors, indicating that internal loss dominated.

For S1, internal quality factor increased from about 860 in the single-photon regime to 1064 at higher powers; S2 values were approximately 500–600. Low-power saturation was absent in the first two measurements but appeared in a later lower-power run. Internal quality factors remained stable over measurements separated by eight months and two years, showing no measurable long-term degradation or surface-oxide regrowth effect.

An RLC model used an effective permittivity of 6.35, geometrical inductance of 0.44 μH/m, and geometrical capacitance of 0.159 nF/m. Extracted kinetic inductance and resistance varied among resonances, and measured frequencies were below their design values. Comparison with prior Ge/SiGe resonators found comparable internal quality factors, with smaller uncertainty than reverse-graded undoped Ge/SiGe devices and values similar to forward-graded devices with thick SiGe buffers.

The measured loss was modeled as the sum of power- and temperature-independent loss, TLS loss, and quasiparticle loss. Quasiparticle loss was negligible at 50 mK. Fitted TLS parameters showed that TLS loss contributed but was smaller than the constant internal-loss term, which was associated primarily with scattering centers, structural imperfections, and the wafer’s comparatively low surface resistivity of 127 Ω/□. The authors therefore emphasized controlling impurity concentration, carrier density, surface roughness, strain, dislocations, and quantum-well proximity effects.

Temperature-dependent measurements from 150 mK to 1.7 K showed a resonance blue shift from 150 to 900 mK, attributed to TLS effects, followed by a redshift from 900 mK to 1.7 K, attributed to increased quasiparticle density and its effect on kinetic inductance. At low power, internal quality factor increased with temperature as TLS defects thermally saturated; at higher temperatures it approached a power-independent plateau. Coupling quality factors remained stable, while loaded quality factors tracked internal quality factors.

The highest projected relaxation time for a gatemon using this wafer and resonator design was approximately 14 ns, comparable to recent Ge/SiGe-based gatemons but insufficient for scalable architectures. The results identify impurity and interface-related losses as key targets and motivate thinner buffers, improved surface quality, and optimized Si/SiGe growth. The platform remained stable above two years and at temperatures up to 1.7 K, while NbN provided magnetic-field tolerance, environmental robustness, and a superconducting gap near 1 THz compatible with future semiconductor, spin-qubit, topological-qubit, and large-scale superconducting quantum-circuit integration.

Day 1 of the 2025 World Grand Prix features wins for Rob Cross, Ratajski, Menzies and Cullen. Cross survives a final-leg decider, Ratajski averages 95.94 in a 2–0 victory, Menzies eliminates the eighth seed, and Cullen rallies to beat Wade 2–0. Scheduled matches include Noppert–Wattimena and Anderson–van Barneveld.

Ghana’s government added export certification tests for major gold miners, including Newmont, Gold Fields and AngloGold Ashanti, to tighten oversight and tax collection. PMMC officials can inspect gold rooms, take samples and join pre-shipment sealing. Gold exports earned $5.78 billion last year amid concerns over smuggling and unaccounted revenues.

The Edina, Minnesota, school district introduces kindergarten students to “white privilege,” with K–2 pupils participating in the Melanin Project and emphasizing that no skin color is superior. Separately, a Michigan State University professor linked U.S. yoga practice to white supremacy, colonialism, exploitation, and cultural appropriation.

In his farewell address, the outgoing President thanks Vice President Mondale, his Cabinet, staff, and the American people for their service during four difficult years. He reflects that the presidency is powerful but constrained by law, public consent, scrutiny, and democratic participation. Special-interest pressures distort politics, so the common good must remain a shared responsibility, and the constitutional authority of the president—elected to represent everyone—must be preserved. He pledges support to the President-elect and wishes him success.

Speaking as a citizen of the world, he identifies three challenges: nuclear destruction, environmental degradation and resource scarcity, and protection of human rights. He warns that expanding nuclear arsenals increase the risk of catastrophe, calls for strong U.S. defense and international efforts to control and reduce nuclear weapons, and expresses hope that humanity’s shared planetary perspective will prevail. He urges action on pollution, depletion of natural resources, and growing demands on water, food, farmland, forests, and the environment, arguing that courage and foresight can address them.

He argues that human rights, democracy, and the value of the individual must guide American policy at home and abroad. The struggle remains unfinished, and the United States must continue advancing education, medical care, equality, employment, and freedom from injustice and religious intolerance. He urges Americans not to abandon these principles during a period of transition and tension, describing nuclear survival, human rights, and responsible stewardship of the planet as the contemporary applications of life, liberty, and the pursuit of happiness. He promises to support the presidential transition, continue praying for American hostages held in Iran, and return home to work as a citizen for the nation’s founding values.

Subconscious biases can narrow hiring decisions and lead qualified applicants to be overlooked. Cited studies found disadvantages for women in math-related positions, applicants with African American–sounding names, and applicants with non-English surnames. To improve hiring, the article recommends using inclusive job-post language, describing behaviors rather than personality types, removing names from résumés, and testing required skills before collecting personal information. Employers should also review rejected résumés and examine interview “gut feelings” to ensure prejudice did not influence decisions.

Teach For America’s Ignite Fellowship demonstrates that high-dosage virtual tutoring can improve academic performance, strengthen students’ confidence and belonging, support teachers, and encourage participants to pursue teaching. The program has reached more than 40 communities, trained over 5,500 tutors, and delivered nearly 200,000 hours of customized learning. Middle school math test scores grew at up to 2.5 times the expected rate, while elementary reading scores grew up to three times faster than average. The author emphasizes three requirements: structured training and ongoing support, technology that expands human relationships, and recognition of tutoring as a teacher-pipeline strategy. Research using TFA programs found that Ignite tutoring nearly triples the likelihood of applying to TFA’s teacher program. Since launching, 550 fellows have joined TFA’s teaching corps, including 280 new teachers this year.

China’s foreign exchange regulator said capital-outflow pressure eased somewhat in 2016 and the yuan would become more flexible in 2017. SAFE said reforms would promote two-way cross-border flows, and authorities planned measures to attract inflows. SAFE reported 2016 surpluses of $196.4 billion on the current account and $26.3 billion on the capital and financial account.

Founded by Jeff Bezos, Amazon launched as an online bookstore in Seattle on July 16, 1995, distinguishing itself through discounts, customer reviews, and easy ordering. Its May 1997 IPO priced shares at $18, raised $54 million, and ended the day at $23.50. Amazon expanded beyond books into numerous product categories and acquisitions, including Audible, Zappos, and Quidsi. It introduced Prime in 2005 and Prime Day in 2015; by 2017, Prime membership had reached nearly 50% of U.S. households.

Amazon also developed the Kindle, Fire tablets, Fire TV, and Echo devices, and launched Amazon Web Services from its decision to rent excess computer capacity. AWS initially served internet startups but later attracted major established companies. Some initiatives failed, including the Fire Phone, Amazon Destinations, WebPay, Amazon Auctions, and premium diapers. Bezos nevertheless maintained a culture that tolerated failed experiments as necessary for creating successful inventions.

Amazon’s strategy emphasized expansion, research and development, customer experience, and long-term sustainable cash-flow growth rather than short-term accounting profits. Over its first 20 years, shareholders earned a nearly 64,000% return, and Amazon reached a $458 billion market capitalization, although cumulative net income from 1997 through 2016 was only $4.9 billion, with 60% earned in 2015–16.

Financial statements show Amazon’s sales and profitability rising sharply in 2014–16. In 2016, total net sales were $135.99 billion, operating income was $4.19 billion, net income was $2.37 billion, and operating cash flow was $16.44 billion. AWS generated $12.22 billion in sales and $3.11 billion in operating income, compared with retail’s $123.77 billion in sales and $1.08 billion in operating income. Reported free cash flow reached $9.71 billion in 2016, while free cash flow after lease-related adjustments was lower. Expenses were categorized primarily as cost of sales, fulfillment, marketing, technology and content, and general and administrative costs.

Microsoft Corporation’s Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended June 30, 2020 describes a technology company founded in 1975 that provides software, cloud services, devices, solutions, and online advertising. Its stated ambitions are to reinvent productivity and business processes, build the intelligent cloud and edge platform, and create more personal computing. The company reports through three segments: Productivity and Business Processes, comprising Office, LinkedIn, and Dynamics; Intelligent Cloud, comprising Azure, server products, GitHub, and enterprise services; and More Personal Computing, comprising Windows, devices, gaming, and search.

Microsoft identifies opportunities in accelerated digital transformation, cloud computing, AI, mixed reality, IoT, gaming, and remote work. Its cloud strategy includes Azure and Azure Stack, while its personal-computing strategy integrates Windows, Office, Surface devices, Xbox, and Project xCloud. The company distributes products through OEMs, direct sales, distributors, resellers, digital marketplaces, and partner programs, and it closed its physical Microsoft Store locations in June 2020. Operations are supported globally, while most devices are manufactured by third parties. Microsoft reported approximately 163,000 full-time employees as of June 30, 2020, including 55,000 in research and development.

COVID-19 required office closures, remote-work policies, and virtual-only conferences and marketing events through fiscal 2021. Microsoft also announced a four-year, $1 billion sustainability investment, a goal of becoming carbon negative by 2030, and a $50 million AI for Earth initiative. Other initiatives address racial injustice, digital-skills access, and $20 million in nonprofit partnerships.

Principal risks include intense competition across platforms and business models, cloud-strategy execution, uncertain returns on product investments, acquisition integration, goodwill and intangible-asset impairment, cybersecurity vulnerabilities, data breaches, privacy concerns, and third-party security dependencies. Ethereum’s current Proposer–Builder Separation uses MEV-Boost and trusted third-party relays, while the forthcoming EIP-7732 enshrine PBS (ePBS) in the Glamsterdam upgrade. Under ePBS, staked builders have their bids debited, proposers commit to winning builder headers, and separate Payload Timeliness Committee deadlines cover execution payloads and blobs. This removes relay trust and supports pipelined blob propagation, but creates a “free option”: after commitment, a winning builder can withhold content, leave the slot empty, and avoid unfavorable trades without a protocol penalty. With blobs requiring roughly two seconds to propagate, the effective option window is about eight seconds.

The paper models this option through DEX trades priced against external CEX signals. Because the builder’s bid is already committed, it can reveal only when inclusion is favorable and otherwise withhold blobs, effectively treating the bid as a sunk cost. The model predicts that option value and exercise probability generally rise with volatility, liquidity, option-window length, and the share of block value derived from CEX–DEX arbitrage. Option value also increases with atomic on-chain MEV, while exercise probability decreases. DEX prices overshoot CEX prices after the builder’s trade, creating losses for liquidity providers and weakening price-oracle reliability. The same vulnerability could affect prediction markets and other applications whose value depends on late-arriving information.

Using historical Ethereum blocks from January 2024 through March 2025, including 6,930,821 relevant CEX–DEX transactions from 23 major searchers across 1,877,729 blocks, the study estimates block values from builder payments and DEX position values from post-slot Binance mid prices. For an eight-second window, exercising the option would be profitable in 0.82% of observed blocks and account for 34.6% of missed blocks. Exercise rates spike during volatile periods, when missed blocks reach 5.5% of a day and represent 80% of missed blocks. Median daily option value is 0.84 ETH, but highly volatile days produce values above 40 ETH. Builders dependent on CEX–DEX order flow exhibit much higher exercise probabilities; CEX–DEX value share has a 0.846 correlation with daily exercise probability. Blob fees do not materially deter exercise, while trailing MEV discourages repeated exercise after an empty slot.

Two principal mitigations are evaluated. Shortening the option window from eight to six, four, or two seconds reduces average exercise probability by more than 33%, 50%, and 77%, respectively, but reduces time for L1 execution and L2 blob propagation. Static penalties also reduce exercise: costs of 0.075, 0.15, and 0.5 ETH reduce it by roughly 75%, 83%, and 87%, though they raise builder entry barriers and may increase blob fees or reduce builder competition. A dynamic penalty based on projected online gradient descent and observed exercise outcomes achieves a 0.096% average exercise probability with a 0.1% target and an average penalty of 0.104 ETH, including substantial reductions on high-volatility days.

The 2025 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine was awarded to Mary Brunkow, Fred Ramsdell and Shimon Sakaguchi for discovering regulatory T cells (T-regs), immune cells that prevent the immune system from attacking the body. Sakaguchi identified T-regs in 1995. Brunkow and Ramsdell, working at Celltech Chiroscience in Bothell, Wash., in the 1990s, traced a mutation causing a fatal autoimmune disease in male mouse pups to the scurfy gene; mutations in the human equivalent were linked in 2001 to IPEX syndrome. The prize, worth 11 million Swedish kronor (over $1.1 million), was announced October 6 by the Nobel Assembly at the Karolinska Institute in Stockholm. Researchers are working to harness T-regs to treat autoimmune disease, cancer and other conditions where the immune system is overactive or misdirected.

An October 25, 2001 email compiled news reports about Enron replacing CFO Andrew Fastow, who was placed on leave, with Jeff McMahon, head of its Industrial Markets group. CEO Kenneth Lay said the change was required to restore investor confidence. The move followed an SEC informal inquiry into LJM Cayman and LJM2 Co-Investment, partnerships formerly managed by Fastow that conducted complex transactions with Enron. Enron ended the LJM relationships, recording a $35 million loss and a $1.2 billion reduction in shareholder equity. Investors also questioned Enron’s disclosure, off-balance-sheet financing, liquidity, credit rating, and possible obligations to issue shares.

Enron shares fell 17% to $16.41 and roughly halved over less than a week, affecting other energy traders as well. Analysts issued downgrades and a sell recommendation, saying the CFO change alone did not resolve concerns about hidden liabilities and transparency; some viewed it as a positive acknowledgment of investor concerns. Enron denied wrongdoing and said operations and liquidity remained normal. Class-action suits alleged that Enron misled investors and that executives profited through insider trading, while the company said it would cooperate with regulators.
Deputies investigated a truck whose passenger allegedly waved a gun. Isaac Torgerson was arrested at Estes Gate on suspicion of aggravated assault.

The Yankees will start Paul Goldschmidt at first base and bat sixth in ALDS Game 4 against Toronto, benching Ben Rice. With Louis Varland opening, they plan a bullpen game. Rice’s benching adds lineup and pinch-hitting flexibility, including catching replacement and potential matchup substitutions.
A Temu shopper’s direct-from-China order arrived without additional duty fees after a tariff truce, though several products were disappointing and average Shein prices rose about 30%.

Donnell Gibson, known as “Mr. D,” is a behavior intervention specialist at Como Park Senior High who motivates students through basketball and his own experiences. After running three times into a burning house to save a family of 10, he received the fire department’s highest honor and founded the Gibson Foundation. The program mentors young African-American urban men through speakers, college tours, and basketball.

An Oct. 23, 2001 email titled “Enron Mentions” compiles reports on Enron’s financial, accounting and management troubles, with additional brief business news.

Cauley Geller Bowman & Coates filed a class-action lawsuit on behalf of Enron shareholders who bought the stock between Jan. 18, 2000 and Oct. 17, 2001. The complaint alleges that Enron and certain officers and directors violated federal securities laws by materially misstating bandwidth demand, overstating operating results, and failing to timely write down investments and impaired assets. It cites Enron’s Oct. 16 announcement of a $1.01 billion after-tax charge, a related reduction of more than $1 billion in shareholder equity, and insider sales of over $73 million. The lead-plaintiff deadline was Dec. 21, 2001.

The SEC made an informal inquiry into Enron transactions with limited partnerships managed by senior executive and CFO Andrew Fastow. The 1999–2000 transactions were intended to hedge merchant investments and other assets, producing a $16 million pretax gain in 1999 and a $36 million loss in 2000. Enron said it had supplied information, that auditors, attorneys and the board had reviewed the arrangements, and that they were disclosed in SEC filings. Kenneth Lay said the company would cooperate, while a spokesman characterized the request as an inquiry rather than an investigation. Enron shares fell $5.40, or more than 20 percent, to $20.65, and later closed at $19.79.

Enron reportedly sought a $750 million loan arranged by Citigroup to preserve access to credit if it were cut off from the commercial-paper market. The company relied on a $3 billion commercial-paper program, had $3.5 billion in bank credit lines, and faced a Moody's review of $13 billion in long-term debt. Partnerships and affiliated companies enabled debt to be kept off Enron’s books; unwinding Fastow-related partnerships involved buying back 62 million shares and reduced equity by $1.2 billion. Whitewing was financed with $1.4 billion in bond proceeds used to buy Enron power plants, with investors concerned that asset-sale shortfalls could require support from shareholders.

Although investors abandoned Enron shares and its value fell 42 percent in one week, most major analysts retained strong ratings. Two downgraded the stock, citing vague partnership disclosures and management credibility concerns. Lay and other executives met investors in Boston, Houston and New York, sought to reassure them that no further surprises were expected, and pledged greater transparency. Critics questioned the absence of the $1.2 billion equity reduction from Enron’s press release and noted potential conflicts arising from investment banks’ underwriting relationships with Enron.

A Texas Monthly feature traced Enron’s transformation from a pipeline company into a major energy trader under Lay and Jeff Skilling. Skilling introduced the Gas Bank, expanded trading into electricity, commodities, broadband and online trading, and cultivated an aggressive, knowledge-based workforce with uncapped bonuses and mark-to-market accounting. The article said the culture became increasingly competitive and workaholic, featuring forced ranking, monitored email and limited employee loyalty. Rebecca Mark’s water business, Azurix, struggled amid political complexity and Enron’s preference for short-term returns. After California energy criticism, the telecommunications downturn and scrutiny of accounting practices, Skilling resigned after six months as CEO. Lay returned as CEO and promised greater transparency and innovation closer to Enron’s core business. Skilling defended his record and said his interests were aligned with shareholders.

On a special investor call, Enron disclosed little additional information and said its diluted share count would fall by 60 million in the fourth quarter because of the LJM2 termination, but did not raise earnings guidance of $1.80 per share for 2001 and $2.15 for 2002. Investors questioned the Marlin II and Whitewing trusts, against which Enron had borrowed about $3.4 billion. Lay disputed an investor’s estimate that Marlin’s water assets were worth only $100 million, creating a dispute during the call. Enron cited at least $3.35 billion in available credit lines, while one analyst estimated its debt-to-capital ratio at 50–55 percent, meaning roughly $3 billion in additional charges could breach certain credit covenants.

Brief business reports said the WTO would hold its Nov. 9–13 conference in Qatar to begin negotiations on removing global trade barriers despite security concerns. 3M reported a 21 percent third-quarter profit decline and was eliminating 5,000 jobs; copper approached a 15-year low on weak demand expectations; Groupe SEB’s takeover of Moulinex was approved; Bombardier said its regional jets were being used more despite falling air traffic; and Aliant Telecom planned to eliminate 140 nonunion jobs.

Separately, AES asked Indian Prime Minister Atal Bihari Vajpayee to intervene in alleged expropriation, contract violations, intimidation and management interference by Orissa’s state government, which owed AES 2.1 billion rupees in unpaid bills. AES offered to withdraw from the state’s power-distribution company while retaining generation operations. Its potential exit followed Cogentrix and Enron, with Lay having threatened legal claims of up to $5 billion over the stalled Dabhol power project.

The manuscript examines microtubule (MT) dynamics as a basis for understanding and anticipating treatment resistance in advanced prostate cancer. Approximately one-third of metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancers (mCRPC) are intrinsically refractory to systemic therapy, and resistance eventually develops in initially responsive tumors. Docetaxel and cabazitaxel are the only approved chemotherapy options, but their differential activity and resistance mechanisms remain poorly understood. The work links androgen receptor (AR) activity, including castration-resistant splice variants ARv567 and ARv7, to MT organization and dynamics.

A computational method tracks fluorescent EB1 or EB3 comets marking growing MT tips in live-cell confocal images. Comet detection, Kalman-filter tracking, and spatial-temporal clustering of collinear tracks are used to quantify MT growth, pausing, shortening, catastrophe, and rescue. In isogenic M12 prostate cancer cells, wild-type AR had little effect on overall MT speed, whereas ARv7 increased average EB1 speed by more than 40%, largely localized AR to the nucleus, eliminated the slowdown of MT growth near cell edges, and produced tracks that rarely overlapped nuclear regions.

The authors propose applying MT-dynamics signatures to patient-derived organoids from primary, lymph-node, and metastatic prostate tumors. Organoids from 16 patients were developed to identify tumor-specific signatures that could predict taxane susceptibility. Because primary prostate samples contain benign and malignant epithelial cells, culture conditions were optimized using the ROCK inhibitor Y-27632; benign cells depended more strongly on the inhibitor, so reducing its concentration fourfold temporarily selected for apoptosis-resistant high-grade tumor cells. Low-grade tumor cells reportedly reverted to normal epithelium ex vivo, whereas high-grade tumor cells were difficult to maintain and were often overgrown by normal cells.

Androgen-independent circulating tumor cells in mCRPC can be smaller than leukocyte-based capture criteria would recognize, including cells of 6.2–7.0 μm, and may be identified through PSMA despite absent AR expression. AR-null metastatic disease can bypass AR through epigenetic plasticity and active FGF/MAPK signaling; MAPK-directed ferroptosis is proposed as a possible approach for TP53-altered AR-null tumors. Upregulation of the MT regulator Op18 in resistant organoids was associated with slower MT polymerization and may contribute to reduced cell size and therapeutic resilience.

ERG was linked to altered MT dynamics and reduced docetaxel or cabazitaxel target engagement. Taxane-induced MT bundling occurred in 62% and 78% of circulating tumor cells from an ERG-negative patient after docetaxel and cabazitaxel, respectively, but not in cells from an ERG-positive patient. Paclitaxel reduced MT growth rates in MDA-MB-231 breast cancer cells, while normal breast epithelial cells had faster MT growth than cancer cells. Higher EB1 density, smaller cell and spindle size, and both unusually fast and slow MT turnover were associated with drug resistance. NAD+ was proposed as a compound that may restore MT homeostasis and alter the susceptibility of persister cells, while GPX4 inhibitors RSL3 and ML210 were investigated as ferroptosis inducers in drug-tolerant prostate cancer organoids.

Mutations and altered expression of VHL and GSK3β were shown to affect MT turnover. Loss of pVHL increased MT dynamics, whereas reconstitution with pVHL isoforms reduced growth and altered pause behavior. During serum starvation, GSK3β phosphorylated pVHL and impaired its MT-stabilizing functions; inhibiting GSK3β restored dynamics toward those of exponentially growing cells. Specific VHL mutation domains were associated with either altered MT turnover or catastrophe/rescue frequencies, suggesting possible matching to destabilizing or stabilizing tubulin drugs. CLASP proteins, GSK3β, tubulin acetylation, and detyrosination were also linked to MT stabilization and drug resistance.

Circular Hough transformation was used to quantify taxane-induced circular MT bundles. Paclitaxel produced bundles in 83% of parental A549 cells but only 27% of BRCA1-knockdown cells, with ring brightness about 70% higher in parental cells, demonstrating distinct resistance mechanisms. Proposed validation will correlate organoid MT dynamics with gene-expression and clinical-response data, test knockdown organoids in patient-derived xenografts, culture prostate tissue slices in a bioreactor, and use transcriptomic and 3D image-analysis approaches. Expanded tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes and chemical screens in tumor–immune co-cultures may identify agents that enhance immune responses.

The manuscript concludes that MT image analysis could help identify resistance, select tubulin inhibitors and doses, and screen compounds that correct abnormal MT homeostasis or target AR, GSK3, and MT-associated proteins. It emphasizes that tubulin-inhibitor effects are dose-dependent and nonlinear: low doses of nocodazole or paclitaxel can increase MT polymerization, whereas high doses depolymerize or stabilize MTs. Live-cell imaging, organoid methods, and statistical analysis provide the experimental and computational framework for these proposed strategies.

An upbeat meeting addressed adjustments to the game plan. The speaker said the team won many hits last game and noted the playoffs' physical style, while stressing the need to improve speed and skating. The goaltender has performed well throughout the playoffs. The team knows it must bring its best game and rely on leadership, individual focus, and home crowd energy to win.

A forwarded email titled “Energy Issues” compiles February 23, 2001 reporting on California’s electricity crisis, utility negotiations, political responses, and related energy projects.

California briefly lifted all power alerts for the first time since January 13, aided by warmer weather, increased imports, generators returning from maintenance, and state agencies purchasing more power in advance. Supply remained tight, conservation was still urged, and officials warned of greater shortages in summer.

Gov. Gray Davis was negotiating with Southern California Edison, Pacific Gas & Electric, and Sempra Energy to buy 26,000 miles of transmission lines for an estimated $4.5 billion to $7 billion. The transaction was intended to help the utilities address nearly $13 billion in debts. Davis announced an agreement in principle with Edison for $2.7 billion, coupled with long-term low-cost power commitments and the dismissal of utility litigation. PG&E remained far from agreement, while Sempra made more progress. Utilities also weighed whether selling their grids at state-offered prices was preferable to bankruptcy.

The state was spending roughly $50 million to $55 million daily buying electricity on behalf of the utilities and sought additional funds that could bring total spending above $2.6 billion by early March. Long-term contracts, including one with Williams Cos., and legislation reducing prices paid to small generators were expected to lower costs. Disputes remained over whether state power-purchase costs would be repaid through bonds, ratepayers, or other sources; the PUC shifted responsibility for revenue shortfalls away from PG&E and Edison but did not settle the ultimate funding question.

Politically, Republicans sought to blame Davis for the crisis but lacked a clear alternative. Polls cited in the articles showed strong support for regulated electricity and the state grid purchase, while Davis’s approval rating had risen. Potential Republican gubernatorial entrants included Secretary of State Bill Jones, investor Bill Simon Jr., and Arnold Schwarzenegger. Other reports criticized expanding political control over utility decisions, documented a lawmaker’s return of utility campaign contributions, and proposed giving residents near power plants electricity discounts and blackout exemptions.

The compilation also reported residents’ opposition to Enron North America’s proposed $450 million Lake Elsinore hydroelectric project and associated power lines through Cleveland National Forest and the San Mateo Wilderness Area. The local water district was studying whether to finance, build, or own the lines, while Enron said the final route remained undecided.

The article examines Hungary’s education system, emphasizing how its demographics, government, economy, laws, and teacher preparation affect students with and without disabilities. Hungary has 9.7 million residents, a declining population and natural growth rate, and a multiparty parliamentary democracy. Its economy shifted from agriculture to centrally planned industry and services and later underwent recession and policy changes under Viktor Orbán, including reduced unemployment.

Public education is compulsory from ages six to sixteen. Students progress through pre-primary, primary, secondary, and postsecondary education, with language requirements beginning in primary school. School choice is formally broad, but applications and selective admissions affect access; 15.4% of primary pupils attend private schools. Secondary admission is rigorous and generally based on primary performance and mathematics and Hungarian examinations. Students must complete community service and a school-leaving examination, which influences higher-education admission.

General education teacher preparation varies by school level and subject. Preschool qualification requires three years of theory and one year of practice, while primary and secondary programs have traditionally lasted four and six years, respectively. Since 2013, primary programs have lasted five years and secondary programs six, with final-year teaching practice, school mentors, and increased emphasis on pedagogy and psychology.

Hungary established special education in 1802 and the world’s first special education teacher-training college in 1906. Disability services address physical, sensory, intellectual, speech, and developmental disabilities, autism, emotional and behavioral difficulties, and multiple disabilities. Committees of educators, specialists, and physicians diagnose students and recommend services and placement, while parents make the final placement decision. Available supports include counseling, early intervention, developmental and speech services, gifted education, and specialized physical education. In 2019, more than 88,000 students had special education needs, and 60% attended inclusive settings.

Special education teachers complete four-year university programs in one or two of eight disability areas. New teachers undergo a compulsory two-year traineeship with mentoring, evaluation, and a written portfolio. The 2013 career model established progression from novice through researcher teacher, and certification is followed by continuing in-service training.

Legislation includes the 1868 Education Act, Act III of 1993, which provided disability-related family allowances and care funding, and the 2011 Act on Public Education, which established free compulsory primary education, generally accessible secondary education, vocational options, and eligibility standards for special education services. Hungary’s disability principles emphasize dignity, autonomy, nondiscrimination, participation, inclusion, accessibility, equality, and respect for children’s evolving capacities.

Remaining problems include difficult and delayed diagnoses, especially for autism, inadequate accessibility in older school buildings and public spaces, continued reliance on specialized schools, limited disability training for general teachers, lecture-heavy instruction, low teacher pay, and attrition. The article recommends school-based referral and autism-diagnostic systems, improved building and transportation access, stronger collaboration and disability training for staff, more varied teaching methods, higher teacher compensation and retention incentives, and examination of church-run universities’ approaches to supporting teacher retention.

Donchian Channels, invented by Richard Donchian, use upper and lower bands based on the highest high and lowest low of the last N bars. Traditionally used for breakout-based trend following, they are reported to work better for commodities, currencies, and Treasuries than for stocks. Trend-following applications can produce large drawdowns and may be unsuitable for scalping.

Backtests cited from Curtis Faith’s *The Way of the Turtle* covered 1996–2007 and reported annual returns of 29.4% and 57.2% for two strategies. A long-only S&P 500 test from 1960 to October 2021 produced a 4.57% CAGR versus 7.15% for buy-and-hold, but with a significantly lower maximum drawdown. When inverted into a mean-reversion strategy for SPY from 1993 to October 2021, the channels produced a 9.16% CAGR with small drawdowns and a high win rate.

The channels resemble Bollinger Bands in appearance but are calculated differently and may produce different backtest results. Overall, the passage concludes that Donchian Channels work as trend-following indicators for commodities and currencies and as mean-reversion indicators for stocks.

The passage cautions that strong earnings and technical bounces do not make every stock a buy. Nvidia’s impressive results were already reflected in expectations, creating a “sell the news” situation before the stock bounced from an upward-trending 50-day trendline. Since NVDA is not overbought and is viewed as a technical value, it may move toward new highs. Micron’s rally is likely short-lived: it remains below a bearish 50-day moving average, is rebounding from an oversold RSI, and faces resistance at $84. Western Digital is mentioned but not analyzed.

Stock futures were little changed after the S&P 500 ended a seven-day winning streak. On the seventh day of the government shutdown, President Trump said some furloughed federal workers may not receive back pay, though most would be cared for. His comments followed a draft White House memo stating that furloughed employees are not guaranteed retroactive pay, despite prior administration guidance and a 2019 law requiring payment. The administration said Congress must specifically appropriate funds, and the signal was viewed as pressure on Senate Democrats. Democrats seek an extension of enhanced Affordable Care Act premium tax credits, while Republicans need seven votes to overcome the filibuster. Trump also warned that permanent layoffs could be substantial if the shutdown continues. The federal workers’ union AFGE rejected the administration’s interpretation.

Canadian lumber stocks fell after BMO downgraded West Fraser, Interfor and Canfor to “market perform,” citing U.S. duties, a stronger dollar, litigation and limited negotiation progress. Their shares dropped 4.7%, 6.7% and 2.4%, respectively, although BMO remained positive on three- to five-year prospects.

At the University of Virginia, President Ronald Reagan praised Thomas Jefferson’s legacy in higher education, reason, religious freedom, popular government, and the balance between government authority and individual liberty. He drew parallels between Jefferson-era partisan conflict and contemporary populism, arguing that the “new populism” opposed excessive regulation, taxation, judicial activism, and an insulated foreign policy.

Reagan described the 1980s as a linked democratic and free-market revolution. He cited expanding freedom, democratic movements, and market reforms abroad, along with U.S. progress in arms reduction, regional conflicts, human rights, Soviet-American exchanges, and Middle East diplomacy. He highlighted the INF treaty, negotiations concerning START, nuclear testing, chemical weapons, and European conventional forces, as well as developments in Afghanistan, Cambodia, Angola, and the Persian Gulf.

Acknowledging improved Soviet-American dialogue and Gorbachev’s reforms, Reagan warned that Soviet progress remained uncertain. He called for continued negotiations, military strength, “trust, but verify,” and public candor about differences between democracy and authoritarianism. He argued that Soviet change was not inevitable and that Western strength and resolve had helped prompt it.

Reagan also urged cooperation between the president and Congress while preserving their distinct constitutional roles. He opposed foreign-policy disputes and legislation that weakened presidential flexibility, arguing that effective foreign policy required strong, consistent leadership and support for military modernization and treaty negotiations. Concluding with the renewed correspondence of Jefferson and John Adams, he emphasized tolerance, charity, and the survival of partisan divisions.

In the question-and-answer session, Reagan said Soviet Most-Favored-Nation status should depend on actions matching proclaimed reforms; described the PLO’s acceptance of conditions for dialogue as only a step toward Middle East peace; defended his administration’s resistance to terrorism; and urged young people to register and vote. He cited restored military readiness, a stronger volunteer force, tax reductions, deregulation, nearly 19 million new jobs, rising disposable income and tax revenue, and reduced regulatory paperwork as major accomplishments. He expected to remain active after leaving office, advocating a line-item veto and balanced-budget amendment while promoting strong national defense and possibly writing a book.

Japan’s GDP grew at an annualized 4% in the second quarter, exceeding forecasts, as private consumption rose 0.9% and capital investment increased. Strong domestic demand, exports, and Tokyo 2020 Olympics spending supported the economy’s decade-long expansion.
Select Security acquired Intelligent Technology and Carolina Security Group in Charlotte, adding nearly 1,000 customers and staff and consolidating western North Carolina operations downtown.

Newcastle University scientists reported the first 3D printing of human corneas using a bio-ink made from donor corneal stem cells, alginate, and collagen. A low-cost printer formed the cornea in concentric circles in under 10 minutes, and the cells remained viable. Using eye-scan data, the researchers also printed a cornea matching a patient’s size and shape. The technique aims to address severe global shortages of transplantable corneas, but printed corneas require further testing and could take years to become available for transplantation.

Galveston County regularly tests Gulf Coast beach water at 52 locations and issues advisories for fecal bacteria, often after heavy-rain runoff. A warning near 57th Street was lifted after samples cleared. Officials advise avoiding flagged water, checking conditions through TexasBeachWatch.com or GCHD.org, and noting water typically clears within 48 hours.

The passage lists archival and published sources used for a compilation of Ronald Reagan's 1975–1980 foreign policy statements. Archival holdings include Secretary of State Haig's personal papers at the Library of Congress, which illuminate his world view, and Donald Regan's papers, which describe forward planning and Executive-Legislative relations management; the Office of the Historian also maintains a website list of Internet resources. Unpublished sources include the State Department's Central Foreign Policy File and lot files (transferred or being transferred to the National Archives in College Park, Maryland), the Reagan Presidential Library in Simi Valley, the National Security Council, and the Washington National Records Center in Suitland. Published sources include the Chicago Tribune, Christian Science Monitor, Commentary, Congressional Record, Current Digest of the Soviet Press, Foreign Affairs, New York Times and Magazine, Wall Street Journal, Washington Post, and Weekly Compilation of Presidential Documents. Individual entries document campaign addresses from Florence (January 24, 1980) through a televised Arlington speech, "Strategy of Peace for the 80s" (October 19, 1980), with source locations and related press reports.

A radar blob over Colorado, initially mistaken for birds, was identified as a 70-mile-wide swarm of migrating Painted Lady butterflies after NWS meteorologist Paul Schlatter solicited public help. The three-inch insects, often confused with monarchs, migrate across the continental U.S. to northern Mexico and the Southwest, follow wind patterns, and can glide hundreds of miles daily.

This study developed and evaluated a reproducible, data-driven method for prioritising AI-detected chest X-ray abnormalities to support lung cancer diagnosis. Across seven Greater Manchester acute care trusts, 1,282 retrospective CXRs from patients with confirmed lung cancer were compared with 13,802 consecutive, prospective GP-referred CXRs. The Annalise AI system assessed 124 findings in shadow mode. An Excel tool compared finding prevalence between cohorts and tested three strategies: 19 findings with prevalence ratios above 5, all 41 HIGH findings, and a 32-finding set refined through clinical review.

Strategy 1 achieved 92.82% sensitivity and 87.21% specificity; Strategy 2 achieved 97.27% sensitivity and 62.68% specificity; Strategy 3 achieved 95.87% sensitivity, 79.11% specificity, and 99.95% negative predictive value. The clinically refined strategy balanced sensitivity and specificity and detected 1,229 of 1,282 cancer cases. Specificity estimates assumed 1% detectable cancer prevalence in the referral cohort.

The findings indicate that combining empirical prevalence data with clinical judgement can improve cancer prioritisation while maintaining a high negative predictive value, although positive predictive value was low. Limitations include regional data, lack of external validation, assumed referral-cohort prevalence, and count-level rather than individual-level reference standards. Further prospective, multicentre validation is needed, including assessment of reporting workflows, possible delays for non-cancer findings, and patient perspectives.

The article explains that the Non-Farm Payrolls (NFP) report, published by the US Bureau of Labor Statistics, tracks monthly changes in US non-agricultural employment and is released on the first Friday of each month at 8:30 a.m. Eastern Time. It includes data on jobs added or lost, unemployment, hours worked, wages, sectoral employment, and prior-month revisions. Traders consider NFP an important indicator of US economic health and potential Federal Reserve interest-rate decisions.

Markets typically react to whether payrolls exceed, fall below, or closely match consensus expectations. Stronger-than-expected figures generally support the US economy and USD, encourage investment in US equities, and raise expectations for rate hikes. Higher yields can then depress bond prices. Weaker-than-expected figures generally weigh on the USD and equities while potentially supporting bonds by increasing expectations of rate cuts. The lecture examines pseudorandomness in regular graphs through their adjacency eigenvalues. For an \((n,d,\lambda)\)-graph, the graph is \(d\)-regular, its largest eigenvalue is \(d\), and every other eigenvalue has absolute value at most \(\lambda\). The expander mixing lemma shows that a smaller \(\lambda\) gives stronger control of edge counts between vertex sets relative to their random-graph expectation.

Cayley graphs are introduced as deterministic examples of pseudorandom graphs. For a finite group \(\Gamma\) and symmetric subset \(S\), the vertices are the group elements and edges connect \(g\) to \(gs\). For Abelian groups, Cayley-graph eigenvalues are Fourier coefficients; non-Abelian analogues involve representation theory. A Paley graph is a Cayley graph over the cyclic group modulo a prime \(p\equiv1\pmod4\), with \(S\) the nonzero quadratic residues. Fourier eigenvectors and a Gauss-sum calculation show that its nontrivial eigenvalues are small relative to its degree \((p-1)/2\), establishing its pseudorandomness.

A theorem of Conlon and Zhao states that discrepancy (DISC) and small second eigenvalue (EIG) are equivalent, up to constant-factor changes in parameters, for all Cayley graphs, including non-Abelian ones. If DISC holds with parameter \(\epsilon\), then \(\lambda\le 8\epsilon d\); conversely, the eigenvalue condition implies the corresponding discrepancy bound. This equivalence fails for general graphs: joining two large random \(d\)-regular components preserves small discrepancy but produces two eigenvalues equal to \(d\). The implication from eigenvalues to discrepancy still holds generally through the expander mixing lemma.

The Cayley-graph theorem is proved using Grothendieck’s inequality. Discrepancy bounds the relevant bilinear form for sign-valued vectors by \(4\epsilon dn\). Grothendieck’s inequality controls this difficult sign-vector optimization by a semidefinite relaxation involving unit vectors, losing only a constant factor. Symmetrizing coordinates using the group action converts the relaxed expression into the spectral characterization of the largest nonleading eigenvalue. The proof therefore yields the \(8\epsilon d\) bound. The lecture also notes that the exact real Grothendieck constant is unknown, though the best known upper bound is about \(1.78\).

Finally, the lecture discusses how small \(\lambda\) can be for fixed degree \(d\) and large \(n\). The Alon–Boppana bound gives
\[
\lambda_2\ge 2\sqrt{d-1}-o(1),
\]
so pseudorandomness cannot make the second eigenvalue arbitrarily small. One proof constructs weighted vectors on distance layers around vertices, combines vectors centered at two sufficiently distant vertices to obtain orthogonality to the all-ones vector, and applies the Courant–Fischer characterization. A second, slightly weaker proof uses the trace or moment method: \(2k\)-th spectral moments count closed walks, and these are bounded below using the infinite \(d\)-regular tree and Catalan numbers. The constant \(2\sqrt{d-1}\) is the spectral radius of that tree. Tightness of the bound and related open problems are deferred to the next lecture, which will also introduce graph limits.

Bridgton National Bank sued Ellas Q. Hepner on a $1,400 promissory note issued to Kil-Tone Company for stock that Hepner alleged the company fraudulently induced him to purchase, promising that the note would not be negotiated unless the stock was resold at a profit. Hepner sought to show the bank knew of these facts through its cashier, Hitchner, who was also Kil-Tone’s treasurer and had participated in the fraud. The trial court excluded that testimony and directed a verdict for the bank. On review, the court held that an agent’s knowledge is attributable to a principal only if the principal would have received notice when acting personally. Because the bank’s board would not necessarily have been informed of the fraud if Kil-Tone sought discount, Hitchner’s knowledge was not chargeable to the bank. The exclusion was therefore not error, and the rule to show cause was discharged.
