The Appellate Division reversed Solomon Montlake’s conviction for first-degree grand larceny and ordered a new trial. The court found no former-jeopardy bar from the first jury’s dismissal after the prosecutor repeatedly accused defense counsel of being a pickpocket; dismissal was a proper exercise of judicial discretion and was effectively requested by counsel. Although allowing cross-examination about an alibi witness’s unpaid rent was an unwise exercise of discretion, it did not alone warrant reversal. The conviction was reversed because the judge erroneously instructed that an alibi required proof excluding any possibility of the defendants’ presence at the crime scene. The prosecution retained the burden of proving guilt beyond a reasonable doubt, and reasonable doubt from the alibi evidence required acquittal.

The passage documents AMD AGESA boot-time interfaces, initialization procedures, host-environment call-outs, and platform customization controls. Published entry-point names are supported for compatibility, while internal procedure names may change.

`AmdReadEventLog` retrieves the oldest event from a circular buffer, advances the buffer pointers, and returns an application-defined identifier and four logging values; an empty buffer is indicated by a zero `EventInfo` value. Applications may create multiple entries, so the first entry need not correspond to the reported error. `AmdReleaseStruct` releases interface-structure storage previously allocated through `AmdCreateStruct`.

Early initialization routines reside in protected boot-block flash and establish a common minimum level of capability rather than optimizing for particular future upgrades. `AmdInitReset` performs basic processor initialization on all cores: the BSP initializes a non-coherent HyperTransport link and checks for Recovery Mode, while APs wait for BSP commands and may initialize extended PCI MMIO configuration. Up to three execution-cache regions may be allocated under specified 32-KByte alignment, address, size, boundary, and processor-resource rules; regions cannot be deallocated but may be expanded. Enabling instruction cache outside this interface can cause data corruption. The host must establish a stack, allocate reset-parameter storage before the heap is operational, and avoid modifying cache controls during the Cache-as-RAM period. Status codes report success, adjusted allocation-rule violations, failed allocations, insufficient storage, and detected BIST errors.

A subsequent environment stage provides platform, processor, VRM, PCIe, C-state, power, and graphics-related settings, performs full processor initialization, configures processor power management, and may request a warm reset. Because processor cores run in parallel, the host must avoid actions that interfere with inter-core communication, including MTRR changes or APIC-register writes.

System-memory initialization locates, configures, and brings main memory online; it supports interleaving, ECC, power-down, UMA allocation, memory training, voltage, refresh, and AMP-related options and returns memory-map, hole, voltage, and status information. The BSP performs and controls full initialization, transfers HOB and artifact data from pre-memory storage, and disables the pre-memory stack. APs execute directed initialization steps and halt. After initialization, the system enables write-back caching for memory while preserving designated fixed and variable MTRRs and execution-cache regions.

A later post-memory procedure closes pre-memory operations and uses `AgesaAllocateBuffer` to obtain permanent protected storage for UEFI HOBs and artifact data previously held in temporary memory. It must run after full memory initialization and host memory-allocation takeover, but before PCI enumeration. Graphics configuration is performed after PCI resource allocation and before video BIOS execution, including internal-graphics resource handling, PCIe ACS exposure, GNB IOAPIC programming, and audio-endpoint limits.

Late initialization generates operating-system informational tables, including DMI, ACPI PState, WHEA-MCE, WHEA-CMC, ACPI ASL library, IVRS, CRAT, and CDIT data. Buffers are allocated through `AgesaAllocateBuffer`, and the host must link the resulting tables into its ACPI and SMBIOS frameworks. The BSP ensures a known-good CPU power state; APs receive final register settings and PState configuration. The routine runs near OS handoff after memory initialization, PCI enumeration, ACPI startup, and host takeover of AP execution.

Suspend support saves critical processor and silicon state, including nonvolatile and volatile storage areas, but does not itself initiate suspend. Resume procedures use the saved context to bring memory out of self-refresh, restore processor and critical silicon registers after PCI control structures are re-established, and perform final reinitialization before OS handoff. The host supplies or locates the saved data, performs the OS restart, restores MTRRs where applicable, and establishes the required stack.

Required host call-outs include buffer allocation, deallocation, and lookup; cold or warm reset initiation; DIMM SPD reading over SMBus; AP task dispatch; PCIe port reset; AP completion checks; and AP idling. SPD reading supplies all 256 bytes for the selected DIMM, although newer Family 17h and 21h APUs with a PSP may perform memory initialization without it. AP dispatch must route the requested function to one or all APs and execute it in 32-bit mode. Invalid handles or missing resources return bounds-check status, while unsupported results from required call-outs cause critical errors.

Optional call-outs include IDS data retrieval from nonvolatile storage, heap rebasing, memory-timing hooks before DRAM initialization or training, external-Vref control, resume self-refresh hooks, video BIOS repost, FCH customization, MBIST voltage adjustment, and platform-specific device actions such as PCIe CLKREQ support. IDS storage access becomes required when IDS features are included, and MBIST voltage adjustment is required when that feature is used.

Platforms can customize AGESA through four mechanisms: platform build settings and register tables, parameter modification after `AmdCreateStruct`, IDS controls during bring-up and debugging, and defined call-outs at specific initialization points. Boolean build options in `<plat>Options.c` can remove unused memory-type, feature, socket, family, table, training, interleaving, and power-management support to reduce ROM code size; `AGESA_OptsDir` identifies the options file. Platform descriptive elements specify VRM current, low-power thresholds, slew rates, overcurrent behavior, high-speed operation, CPU frequency limits, PCI MMIO configuration, IOAPIC count, ACPI table content, OEM identifiers, PState independence, and processor scope names.

The passage specifies SD Memory Card command procedures from Physical Layer Simplified Specification Version 6.00. CMD55 (APP_CMD) causes the next command to be interpreted as an application-specific command (ACMD). The APP_CMD status bit indicates whether a defined ACMD was accepted; legal undefined ACMDs are treated as regular commands, while illegal commands produce an Illegal Command Error. Several ACMD numbers are reserved, and ACMD41 has special response and status behavior.

CMD6 switches among functions in six function groups covering access speed, command-system extension, driver strength, and power limit. Mode 0 checks supported functions and maximum current or power, while Mode 1 switches ready functions and reports results and busy status. Invalid selections cause all changes to be ignored. CMD6 returns a 512-bit status block and has a 100 ms timeout; default functions are restored by CMD0 or a power cycle. Power Limit defaults to 0.72 W, and UHS-I higher-performance modes require an appropriate limit. Optional High-Speed mode uses 50 MHz for 25 MB/s and requires one card with one-to-one CLK, CMD, and DAT connections.

CMD8 checks the host supply voltage during idle-state initialization and echoes the voltage range and check pattern. CCS distinguishes SDSC from SDHC/SDXC: SDSC uses byte addressing, while SDHC/SDXC use 512-byte block addressing and fixed 512-byte blocks; partial and misaligned access are disabled for SDHC/SDXC.

Commands and responses use CRC protection, with CRC7 for commands and most responses and CRC16 for data. CRC failures and illegal commands are not executed and set error status. Read, write, and erase timeout rules vary by capacity and bus mode, including standard busy limits, SDXC exceptions, and UHS-II Data Burst limits. The host may stop or vary the clock subject to polling and required completion-clock intervals.

Commands are fixed 48-bit CRC-protected codewords, while command classes and the CCC field advertise supported functionality. Response types include R1/R1b, R2/R3, R6, and R7. Card Status reports command errors and state, SD Status is a 512-bit block returned through ACMD13, and Task Status reports queued work in command-queue mode.

The speed-class sections define standard, UHS, and Video Speed Classes for SDHC/SDXC cards. They organize storage into allocation and recording units, define write, move, and random-read performance, address fragmented-AU behavior, specify FAT, directory, bitmap, and Continuous Information updates, and describe optional CMD20 support for preparing and controlling speed-class recording.

Using CDC death-certificate data and national life tables from 1999–2020, researchers compared age-adjusted excess mortality and years of potential life lost (YPLL) among non-Hispanic Black and White Americans under age 85, with analyses by sex, age, cause of death, and year. Over 22 years, estimated excess deaths totaled 658,356 among Black females and 1,154,108 among Black males. Estimated excess YPLL totaled 34.9 million for females and 47.0 million for males. Disparities declined through the early 2010s, plateaued through 2019, and rose sharply in 2020, largely erasing prior gains. Heart disease produced the highest excess mortality, while perinatal deaths had the highest YPLL rates by cause. Excess YPLL was greatest among infants, and mortality gaps generally increased from adolescence or early adulthood into older age groups. The authors identify social determinants, access to care, structural barriers, and bias as candidate factors and note uncertainties in death-certificate race and cause-of-death data. They propose excess deaths and YPLL as publicly reported national and local metrics for monitoring health-equity progress.

A simple moving average (SMA) averages an asset’s closing prices over a specified number of periods and updates the calculation as new data arrives. It is a widely available technical indicator used to smooth price data, identify trend direction, and mark potential support and resistance. A rising, falling, or flat SMA generally indicates an upward, downward, or sideways trend, respectively. Price crossovers can generate buy or sell signals, and combining multiple SMA periods may help confirm trends or reversals.

The averaging period determines the indicator’s sensitivity. Short-period SMAs react quickly to recent prices but produce more signals and potential whipsaws, while long-period SMAs are smoother, less responsive, and generally produce fewer trades. A 200-day SMA can help define longer-term trends, but all moving averages lag because they rely on past prices. There is no universally best SMA period; traders should backtest settings appropriate to the asset and strategy.

Backtests presented in the passage support two complementary rules. Short-term SMAs work best for mean reversion: buy when the close crosses below the average and sell when it crosses above. Longer SMAs work best for trend following: buy when the close crosses above the average and sell when it crosses below. A five-day strategy produced an 8.34% CAGR, compared with 9% for buy and hold. A 200-day strategy returned 7.89% with a 28% maximum drawdown, versus 56% for buy and hold. The strongest result came from buying after a close crossed above the 200-day average and holding for 200 days, averaging 10.93% per trade; dividend reinvestment was excluded.

An exponential moving average (EMA) weights recent prices more heavily and generally responds faster with less lag than an SMA. The passage recommends the SMA in the discussed context but notes that both indicators are used and are not substantially different. SMAs can also serve as trend filters within broader strategies.

SMA interpretation depends on market context. It can confirm strong directional trends but generate false signals in range-bound markets. It may lag during high volatility, obscure meaningful movements during low volatility, or misrepresent seasonal and cyclical patterns. Its starting point can influence its initial value, particularly when extreme prices are included. An SMA could theoretically be zero only if every closing price in its period were zero, making the scenario practically impossible under normal trading conditions. Traders may mitigate weaknesses by adjusting the period, combining several SMA lengths, or adding volume, momentum, or other indicators. SMAs can also be applied to trading volume and economic data to reveal underlying trends in otherwise volatile series.

The disclosure describes carrier aggregation and scheduling in multicarrier communication systems. Physical-layer examples include CDMA, OFDM, TDMA, wavelet, and hybrid mechanisms, using phase, amplitude, code, and combinations of modulation, including BPSK, QPSK, and multiple QAM levels. Modulation and coding may be dynamically or semi-dynamically adjusted according to transmission requirements and radio conditions.

OFDM systems may use contiguous, non-contiguous, or mixed carriers. Example frame structures cover FDD and TDD, including 10 ms radio frames, configurable subframes, slots, mini-slots, and scalable numerologies from 15 to 480 kHz. OFDM resources are organized into resource elements, resource blocks, and resource-block groups. Uplink and downlink processing chains include scrambling, modulation, layer mapping, precoding, resource-element mapping, and OFDM or DFTS-OFDM/SC-FDMA waveform generation.

Example base stations and wireless devices contain communication interfaces, processors, and executable program instructions and may communicate over multiple carriers using wireless links. In 5G networks, base stations may connect through Xn, NG-C, and NG-U interfaces to an NGC. A primary cell may contain the PCell and primary component carriers, while configured secondary cells may provide additional downlink or uplink component carriers.

NR multi-connectivity may connect a UE through one master gNB and one or more secondary gNBs over Xn links. Serving cells are divided into a Master Cell Group and Secondary Cell Groups, with bearer types including MCG, SCG, and split bearers. Master and secondary gNBs coordinate RRM configuration, UE capabilities, serving-cell resources, RRC containers, PSCell selection, and timing information. SCG failure handling may stop uplink transmission, notify the master gNB, retain split-bearer downlink traffic, and avoid deactivating the PSCell.

Timing advance groups organize serving cells that use a common timing reference. A primary TAG contains the PCell, while secondary TAGs may contain other cells; up to four TAGs may be supported in a cell group. An SCell assigned to an sTAG may use non-contention-based random access initiated by a PDCCH order. Its random-access response may be addressed using RA-RNTI in the PCell common search space, and initial timing alignment may be established through the random-access procedure. TAG mappings may be configured or reconfigured through RRC signaling, and moving an SCell between TAGs may require releasing and re-adding it. PUCCH may be configured on an SCell to offload the PCell, and a MAC entity may maintain a separate time-alignment timer for each TAG.

Tight interworking may connect an LTE eNB and a gNB using Xx or Xn interfaces. The base stations may serve as master and secondary nodes, with separate master and secondary cell groups, bearer options, and MAC entities. Several control- and user-plane connection arrangements between LTE RAN, 5G RAN, EPC, and NGC are described.

Centralized gNB deployment may divide protocol functions between a central unit and distributed units through control- and user-plane Fs interfaces. Eight example functional splits place different combinations of NR RRC, PDCP, RLC, MAC, PHY, and RF functions in the CU or DU. Splits may be configured per CU, DU, UE, bearer, or network slice. The new RAN may also support multiple network slices identified by slice IDs or NSSAI, route initial NAS signaling to appropriate core-network functions, and isolate RAN resources between slices.

Licensed Assisted Access may use unlicensed spectrum with listen-before-talk and clear-channel assessment, including energy detection, adaptive thresholds, fixed or variable contention windows, random backoff, and distinct uplink and downlink procedures. Discontinuous transmissions may reserve a channel, support UE detection and synchronization, and operate with LTE carrier-aggregation timing.

The disclosure further describes mapping logical channels to bearers, cells, TTIs, and numerologies. Configuration may use logical-channel identifiers, group identifiers, bitmaps, priorities, minimum- and maximum-TTI parameters, and grants or DCIs. Logical-channel prioritization may multiplex data from multiple channels into a MAC PDU while considering bearer QoS, channel priority, and the numerology or TTI indicated by a grant.

A UE may be configured with downlink and uplink bandwidth parts specifying subcarrier spacing, cyclic prefix, PRB count and offset, and control-resource sets. Initial and default bandwidth parts may support initial access, fallback, connected-mode paging, load balancing, and bandwidth adaptation. A deactivation timer may cause fallback to the default downlink BWP when scheduling control is not received. BWPs may share a common CORESET or common search space to reduce switching overhead and improve robustness. Alternatively, group-common search spaces may carry random-access responses, paging control, pre-emption indications, and other group commands.

Wall Street Lunch highlighted Yahoo’s advanced talks to sell AOL to Italy’s Bending Spoons for about $1.4 billion, though no final agreement has been signed. The deal would expand Bending Spoons’ user base and advertising reach; AOL’s traffic among younger users has risen 20% year over year. Music labels are also negotiating with AI firms, Google, and Spotify over licensing songs for AI-generated tracks and model training, seeking per-use micropayments.

Berkshire Hathaway is buying Occidental Petroleum’s chemical business for $9.7 billion in cash. About $6.5 billion of proceeds will reduce debt, generating more than $350 million in estimated annual interest savings. Tesla delivered a record 497,100 vehicles in Q3, exceeding estimates as buyers secured the expiring $7,500 EV tax credit.

September job cuts fell 37% to 54,064, but year-to-date cuts were the highest since 2020; hiring plans also declined, prompting recession warnings. Caterpillar gained 32% this year as investors linked its turbines, mining equipment, and data-center machinery to AI-driven infrastructure demand. Wedbush identified Tenable, Qualys, SentinelOne, Elastic, and C3.ai as potential takeover targets as rising AI costs pressure smaller technology firms.

Tesla Motors, Inc. filed a Form 8-K dated April 3, 2015, reporting under Items 2.02 and 7.01 that it had published a press release the same day, attached as Exhibit 99.1 and incorporated by reference. The information was furnished, not deemed filed for Section 18 purposes, and not incorporated by reference into other filings except by specific reference. Chief Financial Officer Deepak Ahuja signed the filing on behalf of Tesla.

The speaker, giving an inaugural address, thanks his predecessor, cites his high school teacher's counsel to "adjust to changing times and still hold to unchanging principles," and notes taking the oath on two Bibles — one used by the first President in 1789 and one from his mother, opened to Micah 6:8 ("do justly, and to love mercy, and to walk humbly with thy God"). He presents the ceremony as a new beginning and urges renewed faith in the founding dream of freedom, which remains incomplete, calling for a national spirit of unity and trust in which citizens' strength and wisdom offset the president's weakness.

He urges a government that is competent and compassionate, absolute commitment to human rights, fair laws, equality of opportunity, preservation of natural beauty, and protection of the weak from the powerful, while acknowledging the nation's limits and rejecting drift, failure, and mediocrity. Abroad, he calls for shaping a just, humane, and peaceful world, maintaining strength sufficient that it need not be proven in combat, fighting wars against poverty, ignorance, and injustice, and refusing to intimidate others. He pledges efforts to limit armaments and a step toward eliminating nuclear weapons, urging other nations to join, and hopes the world will find that the nation built a lasting peace on policies reflecting its most precious values, affirming America's continuing moral strength and an undiminished American dream.

The DAWN-plasma study was a prospective, multicenter, randomized, open-label phase II trial comparing standard of care plus convalescent plasma with standard of care alone in hospitalized adults with COVID-19. Of 489 randomized participants, 483 were included in the full analysis set: 320 received convalescent plasma and 163 were controls. The plasma group received four units totaling 800–1,000 mL within 12 hours of randomization and again 24–36 hours later. Median administered volume was 884 mL, and 80.7% of units had neutralizing-antibody titers of at least 1/320.

The primary endpoint, the proportion alive without mechanical ventilation on day 15, did not differ significantly between groups: 83.7% with plasma versus 84.1% with control (odds ratio 0.99; p=0.976). No significant differences were found in secondary endpoints, including mortality and day-30 outcomes. Safety outcomes were similar between groups; transfusion-related side effects occurred in 19 of 320 plasma recipients, with no TRALI cases. Antibody titers increased by day 6 independently of the intervention, and higher titers at baseline and day 6 correlated with better outcomes. The investigators concluded that early, high-volume transfusion of high-titer convalescent plasma did not significantly improve clinical status in hospitalized COVID-19 patients.

This prospective observational study assessed surgical diagnoses and postoperative outcomes among 228 adults undergoing laparotomy for suspected acute intestinal obstruction at Amana, Mwananyamala, and Temeke regional referral hospitals in Dar es Salaam from December 2021 to July 2022. Participants were followed to discharge. Most were male (75.4%), the median age was 34 years, and median hospital stay was four days. Adhesions were the most frequent surgical diagnosis (98 patients), followed by hernia (48), volvulus (37), and abdominal tumors (20); some patients had multiple diagnoses. Adhesions, abdominal tumors, hernia, and volvulus were significantly associated with obstruction. Seventy-six percent were discharged home, 9% developed superficial surgical-site infections, and mortality was 5.3%. Wound dehiscence, anastomotic leak, referral to another facility, and unknown outcomes were also documented. Surgical outcomes did not differ significantly among hospitals. The authors noted possible referral bias because the study involved tertiary facilities, recommended including socioeconomic variables to explain unknown outcomes, and highlighted the need for further research on mortality risk among older adults.

Averaging down means buying additional shares of a declining stock to lower the average purchase price. This reduces the price increase required to recover the position’s cost but does not eliminate the original loss or guarantee breakeven. For example, buying 100 shares at $45 and 100 more at $30 lowers the average price to $37.50, reducing the required rise from $30 to 25%. Breakeven is calculated by dividing total purchase cost by total shares, excluding trading fees.

Whether averaging down is appropriate depends on the investor’s circumstances, strategy, conviction, and risk tolerance. It may fit a long-term investor who understands the company and is scaling into a planned position size, or a trader using a backtested strategy. However, it can increase exposure to a deteriorating stock, particularly if strong selling reflects serious problems. Without sufficient knowledge or a sound plan, it can amount to buying a falling knife and deepen losses. Averaging up presents different risks and is generally more suited to short-term trading, while long-term contrarian traders may favor averaging down.

A backtest using SPY and RSI signals split equity into two 50% purchases and exited fully on a sell signal. Compared with entering the full position at once, averaging down produced nearly the same final capital with a smoother equity curve, improved performance metrics, reduced drawdowns, and less time invested in the market.

The passage identifies stocks as the best asset class for averaging down because of their tendency to mean-revert, while warning that other markets may perform poorly. It recommends backtesting and maintaining a margin of safety.

San Francisco State University’s Department of Biology, alumni, and the City of South San Francisco have hosted the Personalized Medicine Conference since 2008, promoting genomic health and professional networking. On June 2, 2017, SFSU will host Personalized Medicine 10.0, themed “Has It Changed Your Life?”, to review the past decade, assess earlier predictions, and consider the future of personalized medicine. Topics include bioinformatics, data management, oncology, epigenetics, rare diseases, sequencing technologies, the microbiome, gene therapy, genome editing, clinical applications, business, regulation, and ethical and cultural impacts. Opening keynote speaker Amylynne Santiago Volker will highlight precision-medicine milestones and the need for appropriate use and accurate interpretation of genetic sequencing, as well as insurance coverage for testing and care.

The passage introduces Bayesian optimization for antibody engineering, where generated antibodies require refinement for binding and developability properties such as thermostability, low hydrophobicity, and strong expression. Small datasets and costly wet-lab experiments make uncertainty-guided optimization well suited to the problem, but performance depends on surrogate-model and acquisition-function choices. Prior studies have not incorporated structural information, whose relevance remains uncertain for intrinsic developability versus binding when antibody–antigen poses are unknown. The work investigates how to add structural information to Bayesian optimization, which tasks benefit, whether antibody-specific models outperform general protein models, and whether structural data are necessary. It also proposes a protein-language-model soft constraint that incorporates sequence-only prior information. Bayesian optimization uses an uncertainty-aware surrogate and an acquisition function to balance exploration and exploitation while iteratively querying an expensive black-box function, commonly with a noisy Gaussian process surrogate.

The Fund was created through the reorganization of seven Aberdeen emerging-markets equity funds into Aberdeen Chile Fund, Inc. Effective April 30, 2018, it was renamed Aberdeen Emerging Markets Equity Income Fund, Inc. and began trading on NYSE American under “AEF.” It pursues a multi-cap emerging-markets equity income strategy, although leverage was not currently used, seeking current income and long-term capital appreciation by investing at least 80% of its net assets, plus investment borrowings, in emerging-markets equity securities under normal market conditions.

As of May 25, 2018, its largest listed holdings were Tencent Holdings (6.45%), China Mobile (2.96%), SAIC Motor (2.59%), Samsung Electronics preferred shares (2.54%), and Samsung Electro GDR preferred shares (2.53%). Cash and cash equivalents represented 5.81%, while other securities below 0.5% represented 3.80%. A tender offer and special capital-gains distribution together accounted for approximately 41% of assets as of April 27, 2018, and could further change the portfolio.

The figures were unaudited and not guaranteed accurate. Closed-end fund shares may fluctuate in value and trade at premiums or discounts to net asset value, and no assurance was given that the Fund would achieve its objective.

Cleveland police sought Steve Stephens, 37, who they say randomly shot and killed 74-year-old Robert Godwin Sr. and streamed the murder on Facebook Live, making Godwin say his ex-girlfriend Joy Lane’s name. Lane broke her silence while police searched for Stephens and his vehicle.

In a retrospective analysis of 2,097 Project Baseline Health Study participants, researchers compared a chest-radiograph-based biological age model (CXR-Age) with the first-generation Horvath and second-generation DNAm PhenoAge epigenetic clocks. CXR-Age correlated moderately with chronological age, whereas the epigenetic clocks correlated strongly; CXR-Age acceleration was not significantly associated with either epigenetic age-acceleration measure.

After adjustment for age, BMI, sex, smoking, race, and study site, higher CXR-Age acceleration was associated with greater coronary artery calcium, poorer pulmonary function, lower performance on all five physical-function tests, and greater disability. Associations with functional decline were also evident among adults aged 45 and older. DNAm PhenoAge showed similar associations with cardiovascular disease, frailty, and disability, generally more strongly in older adults, while Horvath Age had few significant associations.

Plasma proteomics identified lower CDH13 and ApoD abundance with increasing CXR-Age acceleration, while 13 proteins were significantly associated with DNAm PhenoAge acceleration; CDH13 was associated with both clocks. Manual radiograph review found clearer, often normal lung fields in low-acceleration cases and pulmonary or cardiothoracic abnormalities in many high-acceleration cases, although some high-acceleration radiographs had no clear correlate.

The findings suggest that CXR-Age may capture biological processes associated with subclinical cardiopulmonary and functional decline and could potentially support opportunistic screening using routinely obtained radiographs. Limitations include the retrospective observational design, absence of longitudinal data, incomplete smoking and socioeconomic adjustment, limited generalizability, and the model’s lack of interpretability.

This preprint describes PhenoID, a transformer-based pipeline for extracting abnormal dysmorphic findings from clinical examination free text and normalizing them to Human Phenotype Ontology (HPO) terms. The study created a manually annotated corpus of 3,826 organ-system observations, including 3,126 unique entries from 1,655 individuals. Four physician annotators double-annotated 890 observations, achieving an average F1 score of 0.844.

PhenoID separates extraction from normalization. A Bio-ClinicalBERT sequence labeler identifies phenotype spans, while a second Bio-ClinicalBERT model assigns each span one of 11,988 observable HPO term IDs or marks it as not applicable. Noisy-BIO and Recast-BIO heuristics address disjoint and overlapping phenotype mentions.

PhenoID achieved an F1 score of 0.717 for joint extraction and normalization, outperforming six comparison systems, whose scores ranged from 0.515 to 0.633. With gold-standard spans supplied, normalization reached an F1 score of 0.820, indicating that span extraction was a major performance limitation. The extractor correctly ignored 186 of 189 negated findings. Error analysis identified ontology deficiencies, descriptive clinical phrases, misplaced model attention, and overly general terms as common causes of mistakes. The authors note that the system’s limited semantic understanding and the diversity of data authors may restrict performance across specialties, institutions, and documentation practices.

A SpaceX Falcon 9 is scheduled to carry Hewlett Packard Enterprise’s “Spaceborne Computer,” an off-the-shelf commercial supercomputer, to the International Space Station. Capable of one trillion calculations per second, it is designed to process data in orbit, potentially reducing the need to transmit large high-resolution satellite-image datasets to Earth. Special software is intended to detect hazards such as radiation and make protective adjustments, though some doubt it will survive space conditions. After powering up, the computer will undergo about 2.5 hours of tests, followed by a year of operational testing. If successful, it could lead NASA to send more powerful computers and eventually support Mars missions, where communication delays or outages may limit astronauts’ ability to solve problems independently.

Researchers tested an ecological strategy against drug resistance by combining conventional antimalarial treatment with limiting a nutrient in mice’s drinking water. Extra nutrient caused infections to rebound in 40% of treated mice as resistant strains emerged, while nutrient limitation prevented rebound and resistance. In mixed infections, limiting the nutrient stopped resistant parasites from growing, although resistant parasites survived when infected alone, showing that competition with drug-sensitive parasites produced the effect.

The study provides proof of principle that exploiting competition among pathogens can prolong existing drugs and prevent resistance. Future work for diseases such as tuberculosis and malaria must identify resources that resistant strains need more strongly, confirm that limiting them eliminates resistance, and determine the best intervention method and timing. The authors suggest incorporating resource-limiting measures into drug development to extend a drug’s useful life. The research appeared in PNAS.

StatsCan reported that more London-area residents stayed outside the labour market in September as unemployment rose to 5.5% and participation among 25- to 54-year-olds fell to 75%, the lowest among 15 major Ontario cities. A King’s University College study found that only about half of working adults had full-time permanent jobs with benefits, while precarious work was associated with stress, poor health, depression, anger and family strain, especially among young people and minorities.

The patent application is a continuation of U.S. patent application Ser. No. 16/464,063 and claims priority to PCT/US2017/062721 and U.S. Provisional Application No. 62/427,573. The invention was made with Department of Navy support under contract N00014-16-C-1026.

The disclosure describes real-time and near-real-time classification of objects represented by three-dimensional point clouds, including long-range objects measured by chirped LIDAR. In chirped LIDAR, range is determined from the frequency difference between a transmitted reference chirp and a returned optical signal. Heterodyne embodiments perform electronic de-chirping, while homodyne embodiments perform de-chirping within the photodetector. Multiple reflected signals can provide ranges to multiple object portions, which are combined into point clouds.

The classification method obtains a point cloud, estimates a surface normal at selected points, and uses the normal and a tangent plane to define a translation- and rotation-invariant coordinate system. Feature variables such as angular, radial, and tangential distances are extracted in that coordinate system. Two classification statistics may then be computed: spin images, which histogram feature values over point-cloud segments, and covariance matrices, which represent relationships among feature variables.

Spin images are trained using linear discriminant analysis, optionally dimensionality-reduced through principal component analysis, and matched to labeled classes using k-d-tree nearest-neighbor searches. Covariance matrices are grouped into class-associated clusters during training and matched to input matrices using matrix distance and nearest-neighbor techniques. If both classifiers assign the same class, that class is accepted. If they disagree, an iterative closest-point statistic compares the input point cloud only with occluded or non-occluded model point clouds for the two candidate classes. The better-fitting class is assigned, while an excessive fit distance can result in no classification. A device may then be operated according to the assigned class, such as displaying the result, controlling a vehicle, or directing a projectile.

Experimental results using a commercial LIDAR system at ranges of 400–2,000 meters showed strong classification performance for cones, cubes, pipes, boxes, pistols, and similar toy guns, with reported correct-class rates ranging from 89% to 100% in the described examples.

Apple Inc.’s Form 10-Q for the fiscal quarter ended April 1, 2017 reported quarterly net sales of $52.896 billion, up 5% from $50.557 billion a year earlier. Net income was $11.029 billion, diluted earnings per share were $2.10, and operating income was $14.097 billion. For the first six months, net sales totaled $131.247 billion, net income was $28.920 billion, and diluted earnings per share were $5.46. Fiscal 2017 contains 53 weeks, with an additional week included in the first quarter.

Second-quarter net sales increased 11% in the Americas, 10% in Europe, 5% in Japan, and 20% in the Rest of Asia Pacific, while Greater China sales declined 14%. By product, quarterly net sales rose 14% for Mac, 18% for Services, and 31% for Other Products; iPhone sales increased 1%, while iPad sales fell 12%. Management attributed overall growth primarily to Services, Mac, and Other Products, partly offset by foreign-currency weakness.

Gross margin decreased to 38.9% for the quarter and 38.7% for the six-month period, primarily because of higher product costs and currency weakness, partly offset by product and services mix. Apple anticipated a third-quarter gross margin of 37.5% to 38.5% and expected continued pressure from competition, pricing, product transitions, component and manufacturing costs, and a stronger U.S. dollar. Research and development and selling, general and administrative expenses increased, primarily due to higher headcount and related expenses, as well as increased marketing and advertising. The quarterly effective tax rate was 24.9%.

At April 1, 2017, Apple held $15.157 billion in cash and cash equivalents and $241.684 billion in short- and long-term marketable securities. Total assets were $334.532 billion, and shareholders’ equity was $134.082 billion. Six-month operating cash flow was $39.579 billion, investing activities used $33.324 billion, and financing activities used $11.582 billion, resulting in a $5.327 billion decrease in cash. Apple had $9.992 billion of commercial paper and $84.531 billion of long-term debt outstanding. During the quarter, the company repurchased $7.0 billion of stock, paid $3.0 billion in dividends and dividend equivalents, and issued $11.0 billion of long-term debt. Its share-repurchase authorization totaled $175 billion, of which $151 billion had been used.

Apple uses derivatives to manage foreign-currency and interest-rate exposure and reported no other-than-temporary impairment of its marketable securities. Unrecognized tax benefits totaled $8.8 billion. Apple and Ireland were appealing the European Commission’s State Aid Decision, under which Ireland may seek recovery of up to €13 billion plus interest. The company also disclosed concentrated component and outsourced-manufacturing supply arrangements, foreign-exchange risks, lease commitments, employee equity compensation, and continuing legal proceedings, including the remanded Apple-Samsung patent case.

The passage describes NVIDIA's Blackwell GPU architecture and the GeForce RTX 50 Series. Fifth-generation Tensor Cores add FP4 support, a quantization method that uses less than half the memory of FP16 with virtually no quality loss using NVIDIA's TensorRT Model Optimizer; as a result, the FLUX.dev model drops from over 23GB of VRAM at FP16 to under 10GB with FP4, and image generation on an RTX 5090 takes just over five seconds versus 15 seconds on an RTX 4090 at FP16.

Fourth-generation Blackwell RT Cores deliver double the ray-triangle intersection throughput of third-generation cores and add an Opacity Micromap Engine, a Triangle Cluster Intersection Engine, and hardware-accelerated Linear Swept Spheres (LSS), which renders hair about 2x faster than DOTS with roughly 5x less VRAM. Mega Geometry, a new RTX technology, enables ray tracing of full-fidelity geometry in engines such as Unreal Engine 5 with Nanite, via cluster-based LOD updates (Cluster-Level Acceleration Structures), a Partitioned Top-Level Acceleration Structure for high object counts, and support for subdivision surfaces. It is available through DirectX 12 (NVAPI), Vulkan extensions, and OptiX 9.0, and runs on all RTX GPUs from Turing onward. Shader Execution Reordering 2.0 is twice as efficient, with higher precision, and routes coherent neural workloads to Tensor Cores. The AI Management Processor, a programmable RISC-V core at the front of the GPU pipeline, offloads GPU context scheduling from the CPU and aligns with the Windows HAGS model.

For video and display, Blackwell adds hardware encode/decode for 4:2:2 chroma sampling. Ninth-generation NVENC improves AV1 and HEVC quality by 5% BD-BR PSNR, with an AV1 Ultra High Quality mode adding a further 5% (up to 15% combined); the RTX 5090 supports three encoders and two decoders for over 50% generational export-speed gains and 4x the RTX 3090. Sixth-generation NVDEC doubles H.264 decode speed, and DisplayPort 2.1b provides up to 80 Gbps via UHBR 20, supporting 8K at 165Hz and 4K at 480Hz with DSC.

Max-Q power improvements include advanced clock, power, and rail gating (including separate voltage rails for cores and memory), frequency switching 1000x faster than prior architectures, and entering the deepest sleep state 10x faster than Ada, yielding up to 50% power savings in small language model inference.

DLSS 4 introduces Multi Frame Generation, which creates up to three additional frames per rendered frame using an AI model that is 40% faster and uses 30% less VRAM, with frame pacing moved to the display engine via Enhanced Flip Metering. DLSS 4 also adopts transformer-based models for Super Resolution, Ray Reconstruction, and Deep Learning Anti-Aliasing, with twice the parameters, improving stability, detail in motion, and lighting quality.

Blackwell introduces developer-created neural shaders, enabled by the new Cooperative Vectors API for DX12 and Vulkan plus Slang features. Neural applications include RTX Neural Materials, Neural Texture Compression (up to 7:1 VRAM compression; one demo fell from 1110MB to 333MB), Neural Radiance Cache for indirect lighting, RTX Skin for subsurface scattering, and RTX Neural Faces, which uses generative AI to infer realistic faces from rasterized input and pose data.

GPU specifications given: GB202 (flagship, RTX 5090) has 92.2 billion transistors, 192 SMs, 24,576 CUDA cores, 192 RT Cores, 768 Tensor Cores, and 512-bit memory; GB203 (RTX 5080 and RTX 5070 Ti) has 45.6 billion transistors, 84 SMs, 10,752 CUDA cores, 84 RT Cores, and 336 Tensor Cores; GB205 (RTX 5070) has 31 billion transistors, 50 SMs, 6,400 CUDA cores, 50 RT Cores, and 200 Tensor Cores. The passage concludes with NVIDIA's standard specification disclaimers, terms of sale, and trademark notices.

Children’s ownership of personal phones varies widely by country and age. In Germany, 51% of children ages 6–13 reported having their own mobile phone. In the United States, 45% of children ages 10–12 had smartphones with service plans, and 42% of children 8 and younger had their own tablets. Sara Zaske’s daughter, who had few classmates with phones in Berlin, became the only student without a smartphone in California; her parents planned to give her a flip phone before high school.

A seven-country European study found that 46% of children ages 9–16 owned smartphones and 33% owned other mobile phones. Restrictions differed by country, while children commonly saved money by using Wi-Fi and disabling mobile data.

In South Korea, 72% of children had smartphones by ages 11–12 and spent up to 5.4 hours daily on them. Taiwanese phone use rose from 45% among 11-year-olds to 71% among 15-year-olds. Turkish parents were divided over when children should receive phones, with 59.8% choosing ages 12–17. In Africa, 81% of South African secondary students owned or had access to a phone; ownership among children in Ghana and Malawi was much lower but increased substantially from 2007 to 2014. In Australia, 43% of fourth-grade children used or owned a phone after one year, with a median first-phone age of eight.

The American Academy of Pediatrics says there is no ideal age for giving children phones or exposing them to screens. It recommends avoiding digital media for children under 18–24 months except video calls, limiting ages 2–5 to one hour daily, monitoring content and apps, avoiding screens before bed, keeping meals screen-free, and not using media as the sole way to calm children.

Fusion-reactor plasma-facing tungsten will accumulate irradiation damage, helium and hydrogen bubbles, and dislocation-related hardening and embrittlement, while retaining tritium. Because experimental data under relevant conditions are scarce, computational modeling is essential. Density functional theory resolves atomic-scale defects but is computationally limited, while molecular dynamics can model larger microstructures using interatomic potentials.

The work develops a generalized Finnis–Sinclair EAM potential for the W–H–He system, extending the Mason W–H potential with helium interactions. It targets defect formation energies, light-gas binding energies, and relaxation volumes because vacancies and voids dominate gas trapping, while relaxation volumes strongly influence irradiation-induced swelling. Existing Li and Yang potentials describe defect energetics but tend to overestimate relaxation volumes and insufficiently represent tungsten surfaces and voids.

A weighted loss function compares potential predictions with DFT formation energies, binding energies, relaxation volumes, and gaseous-state energies. A parallel global-minimization algorithm uses Gaussian-mixture importance sampling followed by Simplex refinement; parameters were initially fitted for W–He and then jointly refined. Most reference data came from literature, supplemented by VASP calculations for hydrogen–helium clusters and high-pressure helium.

The pair potentials use ZBL short-range behavior, spline corrections, and smooth cutoffs. Constraints reproduce weak W–He binding near 3 Å, helium’s repulsive embedding response, and stable H–He interactions. The revised He–He potential combines dilute-gas virial data with DFT energy and stress curves for high-pressure hcp helium, sacrificing some low-pressure accuracy to improve small interstitial clusters. The resulting potential agrees well with high-pressure helium and H–He dimer data. An initial DFT charge-density analysis indicates that helium’s electronic interactions within tungsten are non-negligible.

Renewable Energy Alaska Project and Southeast tribal partners are training residents from five communities as household energy assessors through the Home Energy Leader Program. Participants provide less-detailed assessments than private audits, which can cost thousands of dollars, for $25. In a Juneau demonstration, they inventoried appliances, windows, lighting and other energy use and recommended improvements such as LED bulbs and insulated coffee pots. These changes could reduce one household’s electric bill by nearly 10 percent. The program seeks to ease diesel-related energy burdens while larger upgrades and alternative energy remain limited. It runs through July 31.

Andrew Hagger called advisers falsely witnessing superannuation death documents “sloppy and unprofessional.” The royal commission exposed bank and AMP misconduct—including conflicted advice, commissions, insurance rorts and fees—amid years of scandals, whistleblower testimony and inquiries.

The Las Vegas City Council plans to introduce an ordinance codifying several trash fees Republic Services has charged commercial property owners without explicit approval. Republic is the exclusive waste-management provider in Clark County, Las Vegas, North Las Vegas and Henderson. Local ordinances require city councils, or county commissioners, to approve fees outside existing agreements, but elected officials said they were unaware of the disputed charges, including container delivery, removal and exchange fees and an industrial dry-run fee. Republic maintains it reports such fees annually through supplemental-service lists and follows required approval procedures. Clark County says commissioner approval is unnecessary, while Henderson plans to investigate possible violations. One waste-management company said it disputed and avoided paying some fees that could have totaled thousands of dollars.

This non-peer-reviewed medRxiv preprint used bidirectional and multivariable Mendelian randomization of European-population GWAS summary data to assess causal relationships among gut microbiota, plasma metabolites, and fibromyalgia (FM). Six gut taxa were associated with FM: family Enterobacteriaceae, genus Butyricicoccus, genus Coprococcus1, and order Enterobacteriales had protective associations, while genus Eggerthella and genus Ruminococcaceae UCG005 were associated with increased susceptibility. No reverse causality was detected.

Eighty-two plasma metabolites were associated with FM, with enrichment in caffeine metabolism, α-linolenic acid metabolism, and GLP-1 and incretin synthesis, secretion, and inactivation pathways. AFMU was classified as protective, while 7-methylxanthine, 1-methylxanthine, and oleoyl ethanolamide were risk-associated metabolites; EPA and stearidonic acid were protective. Multivariable analysis indicated that 2,3-dihydroxypyridine and palmitoylcholine partially mediated associations between Enterobacteriaceae/Enterobacteriales and FM, accounting for 14.91% and 12.34% of total effects, respectively.

The authors proposed limiting caffeine, increasing omega-3 fatty acids and reducing omega-6 intake, following a low-glycemic-index diet, and reducing high-oxalate foods, with supplements considered under medical supervision. Limitations included unavailable demographic data, limited generalizability beyond predominantly European-ancestry populations, and the need for experimental and clinical validation.

Guinness partnered with Thierry Henry, its first footballer ambassador, for the Made of Black campaign in Nigeria and across Africa. Launched on MTV Base in 2014, the campaign celebrates African artists and performers; this season features fan activations with live football and music while continuing EPL broadcast sponsorship through DStv.

This continuation application addresses magnet management for implantable medical devices, particularly cochlear implants exposed to MRI-generated magnetic fields. It describes cochlear implant components for inductive power and data transfer, sound processing, electrical stimulation, and cochlear electrode arrays. Embodiments position a magnet apparatus between rigid plates within an elastomeric housing. Torque from an external magnetic field causes initial magnet rotation and separates the plates, stretching the housing or compressing resilient elements to create a restoring force that opposes further rotation. Alternative designs use springs, rigid housings, rails, compliant or hinged plates, curved surfaces, low-friction interfaces, bumpers, tracks, and adjustable plate materials, dimensions, and stiffness. The magnet may be coated or hermetically contained and permitted to revolve about its longitudinal axis while resisting tilting. Plate holes or grooves can anchor the elastomer, and a slit or pocket can permit magnet insertion and removal. The disclosed teachings may also apply to other hearing prostheses, pacemakers, muscle or auditory-brain stimulators, visual prostheses, and other implanted devices containing magnets.
TCI valued Zodiac Aerospace at €7–€10 per share after a first-half loss, criticizing margin forecasts and urging Safran to drop its bid because offers above €10 destroy value.

Stock futures were little changed after the S&P 500 ended its seven-day win streak. Dell Technologies CEO Michael Dell said AI computing demand remains “tremendous” and sees no sign yet of excess data-center capacity, though he expects there eventually could be too many. Dell’s server networking business grew 58% last year and 69% last quarter. After raising long-term guidance, Dell shares rose more than 3%. The company now expects annual revenue growth of 7%–9%, up from 3%–4%, and diluted earnings-per-share growth of 15%, up from 8%. The agreement sets minimum quantities for scheduled Congolese products while permitting additional purchases. Prices are to be agreed between Belgium and the United Kingdom or United States, with payment made in the usual manner. The United Kingdom must protect Congolese products from less favorable customs treatment than British colonial products, while the United Kingdom and United States will endeavor to supply specified industrial and other goods to the Congo. Belgium must prohibit transactions aiding wartime enemies and maintain export licensing coordinated with British African systems. The agreement takes effect upon signature.

The United States approved possible revision before December 31, 1943, if Belgian territory was liberated, and requested details of agreed prices and unfinished transactions. It questioned paying for and obtaining title to unshipped commodities in December 1943, favoring warehouse receipts at export points, and opposed a specific Belgian shipping guarantee. It also proposed an option on the entire output of scheduled products and an article promoting development work in the Congo. Reported possible pyrethrum production was 539 long tons in 1942 and 1,470 tons in 1943.

The passage presents three bullish candlestick patterns—Bearish Engulfing, Three Outside Down, and Bullish Harami—that performed well in quantitative backtests. Testing used SPY from its 1993 inception through October 2021, investing all equity per trade and exiting when the day’s close exceeded the previous day’s high. Bearish Engulfing produced 296 trades, a 0.53% average gain, 5% CAGR, 71% win rate, 16% maximum drawdown, and 2.5 profit factor. Three Outside Down produced 112 trades, a 0.7% average gain, 2.3% CAGR, 78% win rate, 14% drawdown, and 2.6 profit factor. Bullish Harami produced 306 trades, a 0.33% average gain, 3.1% CAGR, 76% win rate, 25% drawdown, and 1.65 profit factor. These were selected for their strong results among 23 previously tested patterns, although the author says adding another variable may improve them. The passage notes that most candlestick patterns lack quantified evidence despite widespread charting use. It also mentions a separate course with code and backtests for all 75 candlestick patterns.

The article describes RSI, ADX, and IBS as the “Big Three” complementary short-term trading indicators. RSI measures the speed and magnitude of price movements, ranges from 0 to 100, and signals overbought conditions above 70 and oversold conditions below 30; it also provides bullish and bearish divergence signals. IBS measures where the close falls within the bar’s high-low range on a 0-to-1 scale, with low values indicating mean-reversion buy opportunities and high values sell opportunities. ADX, developed by Welles Wilder, identifies trending markets and measures trend strength without indicating direction. The article reports that a 5–10-day ADX period and a strong-trend threshold around 30–40 performed best in backtests.

Backtests of simple strategies produced an average gain per trade of 0.78% and a 12.1% CAGR for IBS, 0.98% and 7.5% for RSI, and 6.5% for ADX. A combined strategy recorded an average gain of 0.86% across 270 SPY trades, with only 14% market exposure and a stated risk-adjusted return of 56%. In QQQ, the combined strategy averaged 1.3% per trade with no losing years since 2000. The article stresses that no “Holy Grail” or guaranteed strategy exists, recommends keeping strategies simple, and advises traders to formulate and backtest rules suited to the security being traded.

The Chaikin Oscillator, developed by Marc Chaikin in the 1980s, measures accumulation and distribution by subtracting a longer exponential moving average of the Accumulation/Distribution Line from a shorter one, typically using 3- and 10-day averages. It oscillates around zero, with positive values indicating buying pressure and negative values indicating selling pressure. Bullish and bearish divergences may signal potential reversals but require confirmation.

Quantified testing of ten strategies found little value or significant profitability. On the S&P 500, buying when the oscillator crossed above zero and selling below it produced a 2.4% CAGR over 20 years. Reversing the criteria improved results because of mean reversion, yielding 287 trades, a 1.76 profit factor, and a 37% maximum drawdown. Two RSI-based strategies each produced 216 trades, a 0.3% average per trade, a 1.6 profit factor, and maximum drawdowns of 18% and 17%. The tests indicate limited predictive value, although the oscillator may still help gauge buying and selling pressure.

University of Kansas researcher Brock Ternes surveyed 864 Kansans—48% private well owners and 52% municipal-water users—and found that well ownership is significantly associated with increased watering during droughts, with practices varying by well type. He attributes this largely to well owners’ reliance on groundwater for crops when precipitation is insufficient, rather than a lack of environmental concern. Ternes argues that groundwater stewardship requires carefully timed extractions. He also noted that overpumping of the High Plains Aquifer could threaten southwestern Kansas irrigation wells within 25 years unless pumping is curtailed.

The disclosure describes an autonomous vehicle management system that safely controls autonomous vehicles or machines performing operations such as driving, navigation, excavation, lifting, and transporting materials. Its subsystems include sensor interfacing, localization, perception, planning, controls, and information output.

Onboard or remote sensors supply environmental data. The perception subsystem normalizes and checks the data, detects and tracks objects, and maintains a compact, layered three-dimensional internal map of the vehicle and surrounding environment. The planning subsystem uses this map, localization information, goals, routes, safety constraints, and operational history to generate and update action plans. It simulates “what-if” scenarios by modifying maps and predicting behavior, then selects safe action sequences, potentially using pruned decision trees.

The system can dynamically control sensors, including their field of view, resolution, data volume, transmission rate, timing, and on/off status, to obtain information needed for planning while reducing unnecessary data processing.

AI techniques include convolutional neural networks for object detection and reinforcement learning for action selection. Confidence scores measure similarity between inference data and training data; low-confidence predictions may be disregarded or overridden. For reinforcement learning, a safety indicator and interruptible commands allow unsafe actions to be blocked. The controls subsystem executes plans through braking, steering, propulsion, electrical, and auxiliary systems, while the information subsystem communicates vehicle state, planned actions, and their reasons to users, enabling informed manual intervention.

The passage describes a continuation patent application concerning ACK/NACK feedback in wireless communication systems, particularly 5G NR networks using multiple transmission reception points (TRPs). A base station may signal a UE the PDCCH monitoring occasions for each TRP, whether ACK/NACK feedback across TRPs is permitted, rules for bundling that feedback, and whether downlink assignment indices (DAIs) are joint across TRPs or independently maintained by each TRP. The UE may then transmit a joint ACK/NACK in a PUCCH using a determined codebook size, or provide separate feedback for individual TRPs. The disclosure describes determining codebook size from PDCCH monitoring occasions, DCI timing information, and DAIs, including dynamic HARQ-ACK codebooks and codeblock-group feedback. Cross-TRP bundling rules may provide a joint ACK when identical data from at least one TRP is decoded, or require both transmissions to succeed when the data differs. Joint DAIs count grants across TRPs and carriers, while independent DAIs count only grants from the transmitting TRP. Individual PUCCHs may be transmitted at different times, on separate resources, or concurrently through multiple uplink TRPs. The passage also describes the related 5G NR network architecture, frame structure, channels, and base-station and UE processing components.

C-BerryTrans is a GNU General Public License 3.0 C++ program for computing intrinsic Berry curvature and anomalous Hall and Nernst conductivities directly from WIEN2k DFT output. It extracts eigenvalues and momentum-matrix elements, evaluates band-resolved Berry curvature using a Kubo-like formula, and integrates it over a dense, uniform full Brillouin-zone mesh. AHC calculations use Fermi–Dirac occupation weights, while ANC calculations use entropy-related weighting. This interpolation-free approach avoids Wannierization errors and supports efficient evaluation over ranges of temperature and chemical potential.

The program requires self-consistent, SOC-enabled WIEN2k calculations. Without spin–orbit coupling, separate real spin subsystems produce Berry curvature whose Brillouin-zone integral vanishes, so SOC is necessary for these intrinsic transverse responses. Because momentum matrices do not follow the same symmetry relations as eigenvalues, calculations are performed over the full Brillouin zone rather than the irreducible zone. OpenMP parallelization distributes k-points among threads, while batching limits RAM use.

Berry curvature is stored with k-point coordinates in binary files, reducing storage requirements and enabling faster post-processing than recalculating it for each parameter set. The workflow generates the full-zone k-list, obtains eigenvalues and momentum matrices from WIEN2k, calculates band-resolved curvature, and then computes either AHC or ANC for specified temperature and chemical-potential ranges. Inputs also define the crystal structure, k-mesh, spin polarization, thread count, batch size, and energy window; an interval of approximately ±1.5 eV around the chemical potential is suggested for temperatures up to 300 K. Transport properties generally require k-meshes of about 400×400×400 or finer.

The code was tested for AHC in Fe and ANC in Pd, Fe₃Al, and Co₂FeAl, with results compared against published values. It also includes an interactive Python visualization module, `berryTrans plot.py`, for displaying Berry curvature combined with Fermi-distribution or entropy-distribution weighting. The implementation is material-independent and currently interfaces with WIEN2k, though it can also be linked to packages such as ELK and Quantum ESPRESSO. The intrinsic framework is physically applicable in clean to moderately dirty, generally low-temperature regimes; it does not capture extrinsic transport mechanisms or scattering effects that can dominate at higher temperatures.

The paper proposes a hybrid method-of-moments (MoM) and generalized scattering matrix (GSM) framework for multiscale antenna problems. Unlike conventional MoM–T-matrix approaches, it models the electrically large environment—radome, reflector, or implantation medium—with MoM while representing the antenna through a compact GSM. This reduces the MoM system size and supports analytic transformations, efficient array synthesis, and modular reuse of antenna data.

Specialized variants include a fully coupled GSM–physical-optics hybrid for large reflectors that captures higher-order antenna–reflector interactions, and a GSM–T-matrix hybrid for environments amenable to spherical-wave expansion.

For a penetrable structure, total fields are decomposed into incident, structure-scattered, and antenna-generated components. Equivalent electric and magnetic currents on the structure are obtained using PMCHWT integral equations solved by MoM with Rao–Wilton–Glisson basis functions and Galerkin testing. Antenna fields are expanded in outgoing vector spherical waves, while structure-generated fields within the antenna region use regular-wave expansions. These modal coefficients are related to the MoM currents and combined through the antenna’s source-scattering GSM representation, which connects free-space and waveguide excitations with corresponding antenna responses.

The Single/Double Offense uses bigs to set double and down screens for smaller shooters. Because switching would leave a smaller defender against the screener in the post, NBA defenses generally prefer “show and recover,” though tactics vary. Defenders influence shooters away from their preferred side and pressure the ballhandler toward the sideline. Against double screens, defenders show, chase shooters, and recover to deny passes; against single screens, they show hard, chase, recover, pressure wing catches, deny post entry, and pack toward the ball. Post mismatches may be trapped.

An “All Out SOS” disruption has the defense initiate action and trap wing shooters, using contact switches, aggressive pressure, post fronts, and Triangle “I” help positions. The ballhandler is pushed toward the sideline, ideally the weak hand and before midcourt, to restrict penetration and lengthen passing lanes. Closeouts and rotations occur as passes leave the passer’s hands, with additional traps available after drives, passes over post fronts, or screening action.

Captain Scullen alleged that his crew was left without food or shelter, though Russian naval testimony stated that he had declined customary lodging and food. U.S. diplomat George Wurts requested aid and an investigation while suggesting that the account of deprivation was exaggerated.
