President Trump addressed world leaders, arguing that global freedom, democracy, and peace depend on strong, sovereign nations that defend their cultures, citizens, and national interests rather than erase them through globalism. He cited U.S. economic gains, including lower unemployment, six million additional jobs, reduced poverty, and leading oil and natural gas production, while presenting the United States as the world’s most powerful nation and calling on allies to share defense costs.

He advocated “fair and reciprocal” trade, replacing NAFTA with the U.S.-Mexico-Canada Agreement, pursuing new agreements with Japan and the United Kingdom, and reforming the World Trade Organization. He accused China of barriers, subsidies, currency manipulation, forced technology transfers, intellectual-property theft, and other unfair practices, citing Micron Technology’s alleged loss of designs worth up to $8.7 billion. He defended tariffs on more than $500 billion in Chinese goods, called for balance in U.S.-China relations, and said Hong Kong’s handling would affect China’s global role.

Trump withdrew the United States from the Iran nuclear deal and imposed sanctions, including on Iran’s central bank after an attack on Saudi oil facilities. He condemned Iran as a terrorism sponsor and nuclear proliferator, criticized its anti-Semitic rhetoric and regional wars, and supported normalized relations between Israel and its neighbors. He also called for North Korean denuclearization, continued coalition work in Afghanistan, and diplomacy based on peace, cooperation, and mutual gain.

In the Western Hemisphere, he called illegal migration unsafe and unsustainable, condemned human smuggling, and demanded stronger borders and regional cooperation to end trafficking. He criticized Venezuela’s Maduro government, described conditions under its rule, pledged humanitarian aid, and expressed support for a coalition recognizing Venezuela’s legitimate government. He also rejected socialism and communism and announced tighter screening of foreign technology and investments.

Domestically and abroad, Trump defended free speech, warned against concentrated social-media power, supported LGBTQ people and women’s economic empowerment, and promoted religious freedom. He opposed taxpayer-funded abortion and rejected the U.N. Arms Trade Treaty while affirming the Second Amendment. He closed by calling on leaders to strengthen and cherish their nations, protect citizens and liberty, and pursue peace, progress, and justice at home.
Justice Wolfe delivered the opinion in two appeals involving the Guehler estate.

The lecture reviews the Weierstrass M-test: if a sequence of functions satisfies \(|f_j(x)|\le M_j\) and \(\sum M_j\) converges, then the partial sums of \(\sum f_j\) converge uniformly. As an example, a series involving scaled cosine terms converges uniformly on \(\mathbb R\), and its sum is continuous because it is a uniform limit of continuous functions.

For a power series \(\sum_{j=0}^{\infty}a_j(x-x_0)^j\) with radius of convergence \(\rho\), the series converges uniformly on every closed interval \([x_0-R,x_0+R]\) with \(R<\rho\). This follows from the M-test by bounding each term by \(|a_j|R^j\) and applying the root test. Within the radius of convergence, the series may therefore be differentiated and integrated term by term. The formally differentiated series has the same radius of convergence as the original, allowing this procedure to be repeated for every derivative. In particular, \(f^{(k)}(x_0)=k!a_k\), so the power series is the Taylor series of the function it defines.

The lecture then introduces Weierstrass’s approximation theorem: every continuous function on \([0,1]\) can be uniformly approximated by a sequence of polynomials. It suffices to prove the result for functions vanishing at both endpoints, because the general case can be reduced to this one by modifying the function with a linear term.

For the special case, the function is extended by zero outside \([0,1]\). A sequence of polynomials
\[
q_n(x)=c_n(1-x^2)^n
\]
is normalized so that \(\int_{-1}^{1}q_n(t)\,dt=1\). These polynomials are nonnegative, concentrate their mass near zero like an approximate identity, and converge uniformly to zero on regions bounded away from zero. The proof uses estimates such as \(c_n\le\sqrt n\) and the fact that \(\sqrt n(1-\delta^2)^n\to0\).

Polynomials
\[
p_n(x)=\int_0^1 f(t)q_n(t-x)\,dt
\]
are then constructed. Expanding \(q_n(t-x)\) shows that each \(p_n\) is a polynomial. Uniform continuity and boundedness of \(f\), together with the concentration of \(q_n\) near zero, are used to prove that \(p_n\to f\) uniformly on \([0,1]\), establishing the approximation theorem.

Louisville officials advise residents against neighborhood fireworks on Independence Day, saying smoke worsens particle pollution, can exceed federal limits, and aggravate respiratory problems. Airborne and exploding fireworks are illegal in city limits; the last exceedance was in 2015.

In an infringement suit over the Curtis and Cook patent for portable elevated railroads, the court held claims 1–3 anticipated by a substantially similar single-track overhead railway used in 1866. Claim 4, covering a main overhead track combined with branch tracks, a switch, and a traveler, was held valid and infringed by the defendant’s structure. A decree was directed for the plaintiff on claim 4.

At Kenyon College, a student-led Whiteness Group educates participants about white privilege and white allyship. Its rules prohibit white members from asking people of color questions and require white participants to answer questions themselves; members may voice unpopular opinions but may not spread rumors about meeting discussions. Founder Juniper Cruz, who describes racism as “a white people problem,” aims to create sustainable activism beyond social-media posts. Chaplain Rachel Kessler said shame over racial privilege or fear of saying something problematic can impede efforts to combat racism and white supremacy.

During Tuesday's Supreme Court oral argument, a majority of justices appeared sympathetic to Colorado counselor Kaley Chiles, who is challenging the state's 2019 Minor Conversion Therapy Law barring mental health professionals from providing conversion therapy to clients under 18, with an exception for religious ministry. Several justices suggested remanding to the lower courts rather than striking the law down outright.

A federal trial judge denied Chiles's request to temporarily block enforcement, and the 10th Circuit affirmed, applying rational basis review. Chiles's lawyer argued that this lenient standard would let states silence speech and turn counselors into government "mouthpieces," while the Trump administration's solicitor general urged the Court to invalidate the law. Colorado Solicitor General Stevenson countered that the bipartisan law narrowly regulates a risky medical treatment without restricting a professional's expression of viewpoint.

Justices debated whether Chiles has standing, given Colorado's non-enforcement of the ban, and whether the law regulates medical treatment or speech. Sotomayor found no "credible threat of prosecution," while Jackson called it odd that talk therapy and medication for the same condition could receive different constitutional protection. Alito questioned whether medical consensus has been shaped by ideology and called the law "blatant viewpoint discrimination." Sotomayor, Jackson, and possibly Barrett favored having the lower courts apply strict scrutiny. Kavanaugh asked no questions during the roughly 90-minute argument.

The passage describes terminal functions and reset behavior for DDR2/DDR3 Memory Controllers 0 and 1. Data strobes support each byte of the 32-bit DDR[0] and DDR[1] buses, acting as outputs during writes and inputs during reads to synchronize transfers. DQS[3] serves bits [31:24], DQS[0] serves bits [7:0], and DDR[1] DQM signals identify byte lanes. Pins use DVDD_DDR[0] or DVDD_DDR[1], with specified pullup, pulldown, and on-die termination behavior during and after reset.

A medRxiv preprint presents a cost-effective, culture-independent citizen science approach for monitoring household drinking water in China. Between December 2020 and August 2021, 25 student volunteers collected 50 tap-water samples from 32 administrative regions across 19 provinces/regions, including opportunistic samples after the 2021 Henan Floods and Typhoon In-Fa. A standardized Chinese-language toolkit, protocol, video tutorial, demonstrations, and direct communication supported sampling, filtration, freezing, shipping, and quality control. DNA was extracted from 0.20-micrometer syringe filters, and 16S rRNA gene metabarcoding was performed on pooled PCR-positive samples using DADA2 and the Silva database. Of 50 samples, 22 tested positive for microbial DNA, yielding 7,635 amplicon sequence variants and a diverse tap-water microbiome. All PCR-positive samples contained detected pathogenic bacteria, including Mycobacterium, Acinetobacter, and Legionella. Post-event samples also detected Salmonella enterica in Zhengzhou and toxin-producing Microcystis in Changzhou. Despite the limited sample size, the study concludes that citizen science can expand microbial monitoring and inform public-health strategies for water safety.

Reaching the finals and falling short disappointed the speaker, but they were happy their brother won. Time with the brother’s family and seeing his kids grow up mattered most. Trust was key; Randy kept their line together. Both goalies played well, with Giggy unflappable and Ray expected to excel.

Participants debated whether to state explicitly in the Dumbarton Oaks Proposals that the Organization should respect international obligations and treaties. Honduras supported including such language; Chile agreed but questioned whether it was an established principle of international law. Venezuela corrected the record on a prior unanimity remark, after which the minutes were approved.

Discussion then turned to Security Council composition. Pasvolsky emphasized efficiency, effectiveness, and representativeness, linking permanent seats to members’ capacity and willingness to bear Council responsibilities and noting that the five proposed permanent members held most of the world’s military and industrial power. He cited the League of Nations’ growth from nine to fifteen members and supported having more nonpermanent than permanent members so decisions could not be made solely by permanent members. He opposed prematurely prescribing Assembly selection rules because other criteria had been proposed. Brazil advocated permanent Latin American representation and emphasized the Organization’s preventive purpose. Ambassador Martins then sought permission to present Brazil’s views on matters likely to be negotiated at the forthcoming Mexico and United Nations conferences.

A severely injured Mexican boy, aged 18–20, was found unconscious in a vegetative state at a San Diego hospital sixteen years ago after a pickup carrying illegal travelers crashed near the Mexican border. Unable to communicate his name or origins, he carried only a phone card and some pesos and dollars, and hospital staff nicknamed him Pancho for paperwork purposes. His story spread online, where websites track missing would-be immigrants; two years ago, a woman in McAllen, Texas, recognized a photo of a man in a San Diego hospital bed with a breathing tube and wondered if it was Gilberto, forwarding it to her cousin in Houston. The Guardian has published the full story.

Quarters coverage is a 4-deep, 3-underneath scheme used against pass-heavy offenses while employing safeties to contain the run. Both cornerbacks cover the #1 receiver, safeties track the #2, outside linebackers defend the flats, and the middle linebacker covers the hook. It combines zone droppers with man-style matchups, allowing defenders to play fast and adjust to offensive threats. Its main weaknesses are the flats and middle of the field. Offenses can attack these areas through play action, shallow crossing routes, option routes, and overload concepts that create favorable one-on-one matchups. Five examples include a boundary sluggo, backside option route, shallow sting, leak route, and play-action slot cross.

Child care academies in at least 11 North Carolina counties provide accelerated, locally tailored training for early childhood educators, often at little or no cost to participants. Programs typically last two to six weeks and require 20 to 64 hours of class time, offering a faster alternative to traditional teacher preparation amid widespread staffing shortages.

Two models are operating. The classroom-ready model provides at least 20 hours of instruction, required health and safety training, background checks and help with registration, qualifying graduates to work in licensed child care facilities but not as lead teachers. The teaching credential model also replaces the semester-long EDU 119 course with a transferable continuing-education credit, EDU 3119. Graduates qualify to serve as lead teachers or elementary teaching assistants and can continue toward an associate degree. Academies also provide access to local resources, apprenticeships and employment opportunities.

The North Carolina House included $1.476 million for a state-funded expansion pilot in its budget, but the funding did not reach the final budget signed by Gov. Josh Stein. DCDEE separately offers grants of up to $50,000 to as many as 10 UNC System institutions to operate academies through July 31, 2026.

Local programs have reported positive results. In Wayne and Johnston counties, Camber Foundation funding covered training and helped 63 graduates enter child care or higher education. McDowell County’s teaching credential program graduated six lead-teacher candidates, with four entering child care classrooms and two continuing their education. Durham’s six-week, bilingual academy received 140 applications for 20 slots. Stanly County has graduated 13 classroom-ready students, with five to 10 finding jobs.

The application describes automated systems and methods for sorting mixed objects using robotic manipulators, perception and scanning units, conveyors, movable carriages, and centrally controlled bin assignments. Objects are acquired from input areas or buffers, identified, and moved to intermediate stations or collection bins dynamically associated with their destinations. Unlike conventional systems with fixed bin-to-destination mappings, assignments can change during operation using heuristics, historical trends, current inventory, expected arrivals, item characteristics, throughput, and downstream demand. Completed bins are sent to output conveyors or bagging stations, while unidentified or ungraspable objects can be routed for manual handling.

Disclosed embodiments include multiple sorting stations, circulating or multiple input conveyors, human-fed hoppers, and shuttle-wing sortation stations using an articulated arm, multi-view cameras, and reciprocating carriages. Parallel wings and dynamic allocation place high-volume destinations near carriage home positions to reduce cycle times and preserve throughput. The system can scale by adding robots, wings, or parallel stations. Stated benefits include greater flexibility, fewer required outputs, reduced space and labor, lower capital and operating costs, improved handling order, and resilience to individual sorter failures.

HuffPost, CSPI, and EnergyFiend.com found caffeine per ounce varies widely among chain coffees: McDonald’s has 9 mg, Starbucks 20.6 mg, and Death Wish 54.2 mg. The site says one Death Wish cup is not lethal.

The passage argues that the Trump-driven reflation rally faces two major risks: Trump’s ability to deliver promised policies and historically high stock valuations. The healthcare bill failure raises doubts about tax cuts, infrastructure spending, and deregulation, while Federal Reserve tightening and elevated S&P 500 valuation ratios leave little room for disappointment. Investor confidence has surged, but economic data and post-election earnings revisions are weaker. Fed officials have cited rich or frothy asset prices and could tighten faster, potentially checking the rally. Historically, high valuations have implied poor future equity returns, potentially only marginally exceeding bonds. Tax reform is expected to be piecemeal, with cash repatriation and buybacks supporting stocks, but broad reflation is considered unlikely; stock prices should ultimately reflect these realities.

The passage specifies SEV-ES and SEV-SNP guest-hypervisor communication through the Guest-Hypervisor Communication Block (GHCB), GHCB MSR protocol, and VMGEXIT. Protocol functions cover AP reset hold, preferred and registered GHCB GPAs, page state changes, Run VMPL, hypervisor feature support, and guest termination with reason codes.

SEV-SNP guests must register a GHCB GPA before first using a GHCB for VMGEXIT. The protocol defines requests and responses for obtaining the hypervisor-preferred GPA, registering a GPA, and unregistering the current GPA. Registered GHCB pages are hypervisor-owned and shared. Registration replaces any existing registration; a GPA mismatch requires guest termination. With SEV-SNP Multi-VMPL support, each VMPL level may register a GPA.

During negotiation, the hypervisor supplies the GHCB GPA through VMCB offset 0x00a0 and provides protocol-version and page-table encryption information. Guests use CPUID, MSR reads, and SEV Information requests to obtain this data, configure encrypted page tables, allocate and share the GHCB page, and write its GPA to MSR 0xc001_0130 before VMGEXIT. SEV-SNP guests also register the GHCB GPA. Guests establish #VC handlers and populate the GHCB before invoking VMGEXIT; hypervisors translate the GHCB GPA, process the request, return results, and resume the guest.

Non-automatic exit events generate a #VC for SEV-ES guests. The guest or hypervisor copies required register state through GHCB fields governed by the VALID_BITMAP. Guests must set SW_EXITCODE, SW_EXITINFO1, and SW_EXITINFO2 validity bits, while hypervisors return SW_EXITINFO1 and SW_EXITINFO2. Hypervisor errors may request an injected exception. Documented event handling includes IOIO_PROT, MSR_PROT, VMMCALL, NPF/MMIO access, Page State Change, and SNP Guest Request. Software should disable interrupts and preemption while accessing the GHCB.

Page State Change requests use structures in the shared buffer, which can hold up to 253 entries. Guests may request private or shared pages, including SEV-SNP RMP updates, and may provide PSMASH and UNSMASH hints. Progress is tracked for interruption and resumption, with reason codes describing failures.

SNP Guest Request uses separate shared request and response pages. The hypervisor translates them, assigns the response page to firmware, processes the request, reclaims the page, and returns the firmware result. Sequence-number synchronization, retry handling, and rate limiting are required or recommended to prevent request failures or denial of service.

SEV-SNP launch also provides secrets and CPUID pages. The secrets page contains a guest-reserved area for operating-environment communication and VMPL message sequence numbers. On EFI systems, firmware can communicate these pages through the EFI SEV-SNP Confidential Computing Blob configuration table.

The lecture introduces smart contracts as digitally expressed promises backed by protocols, algorithms, and conditional rules. It emphasizes that they may be neither especially “smart” nor legally binding contracts. Their core technical features include cryptography, decentralization, consensus, and transaction design. Unlike Bitcoin’s transaction-based ledger, Ethereum uses an account-based balance ledger with state transitions, supports several programming languages, and is Turing complete. Ethereum also has faster block production, a changing block-reward policy, greater inflation than Bitcoin, and more centralized development and leadership. Other platforms discussed include EOS, NEO, and Ethereum Classic.

Decentralized applications generally use native tokens, but adoption remained limited, with gambling, gaming, exchanges, and finance among the leading examples. Initial coin offerings raise funds for new networks before their tokens are fully usable; their valuations depend largely on expectations of future use and appreciation. The lecture reports tens of billions raised through ICOs, but also substantial failure and fraud rates.

Larry Lessig explains that contract law allocates risk, includes express and implied terms, and depends on enforcement by the state. Although code can perform obligations automatically, it can also conflict with legal limits, as illustrated by digital rights management and fair use. Blockchain-based systems may substitute for weak legal infrastructure and lower transaction costs, enabling contracts such as automatically paid flight-delay insurance. However, they are best suited to narrow, clearly defined outcomes; ambiguity can also serve a useful role by allowing later judicial interpretation. The state cannot be entirely bypassed, especially regarding enforceability, taxation, regulation, and jurisdiction. Courts will need technically knowledgeable lawyers capable of interpreting code, and the legal treatment of smart contracts remains unsettled.

In Morris v. Scott, the court held that a malicious-prosecution action may proceed despite the complained-of court’s lack of jurisdiction when malice and falsity are the gravamen and the arrest or other trespass is pleaded as a consequence. Morris was arrested, tried, and acquitted after Scott accused him of aiding the fraudulent removal of a third party’s property. The lower court nonsuited Morris for failure to aver jurisdiction, but the judgment was reversed, with a venire de novo ordered and costs to abide the event.

The passage examines lower-high and lower-low patterns through backtests of SPY, GLD, and TLT. A one-bar strategy enters long at the close and exits after 1–10 bars; longer holding periods produced better average returns across the three assets because of their long-term upward drift, while trade frequency declined as signals appeared in clusters. A two-day pattern modestly improved SPY results but did little for GLD or TLT. A final strategy entered long after three consecutive lower highs and lower lows, increasing average gains and profit factor, with a 9.9% maximum drawdown for one-day holds. The passage concludes that the pattern is typically a short-term reversal that works best in stocks, though other strategies may offer greater short-term rewards. It also identifies pattern identification, entry selection, backtesting, confirmation signals, and risk management as key trading-rule considerations.

Charlton fans released numerous smoke bomb canisters inside Milton End during their 1-0 win over Pompey at Fratton Park. Pompey await FA observations and may be fined; chief executive Mark Catlin called the incidents isolated and noted that flares and smoke bombs are prohibited.

The court denied plaintiffs’ motion to enforce a purported settlement reached five days before trial. Plaintiffs, former D.C. Department of Corrections employees, alleged they were terminated in retaliation for discussing the halfway-house system with the media. The parties had agreed that the plaintiffs would dismiss their claims in exchange for $625,000, and the court had dismissed the case without prejudice and vacated the trial date.

Under District of Columbia contract law, the plaintiffs had to show mutual assent on all material terms. The court found that the parties never reached agreement concerning the plaintiffs’ re-enrollment in the retirement system. Defendants’ subsequent uncertainty, failure to initiate the re-enrollment process, and statements questioning participation while the plaintiffs were not working demonstrated the absence of a meeting of the minds. The retirement application form and an earlier assurance that “no problems were anticipated” were insufficient to establish an agreement. Plaintiffs also could not invoke an automatic right to retirement benefits because their dismissals had not been adjudicated unwarranted or unjustified. The court declined to enforce a separate settlement for Susie Thomas because her individual monetary share had not been determined. Plaintiffs were given until September 9, 2002, to accept the $625,000 offer without retirement benefits or reject it and proceed toward trial.

Niantic will add 80 second-generation Pokémon to Pokémon Go, bringing the total to 88. The update also adds Nanab and Pinap Berries, avatar clothing and purchasable items. New Pokémon will appear in the real world using location data and react differently during battles. Twelve remain absent, including six legendaries, while Niantic has not detailed plans for adding them.

The team aims to regroup, regain confidence, and return home with a split in the series. Their strategy is to create traffic in Roberto’s vision, challenge him more, and study opponents’ tendencies after the first game.

Collagen is a structural protein made from amino acids and nutrients including vitamin C, zinc and copper. Its natural production declines with age, prompting interest in supplements. The passage describes 28 collagen types, with oral supplements mainly containing types I, II and III to support the skin, bones, joints, tendons, ligaments, blood vessels and organs.

Supplements vary by source and processing. Most are animal-derived, including marine collagen and collagen from cows, pigs and chicken cartilage. Hydrolysed collagen is broken into smaller molecules for easier digestion and absorption. Potential benefits include improved skin firmness and hydration, reduced wrinkles, stronger nails and bones, reduced joint pain, and support for muscle-related tissues, though evidence for thicker hair is limited to mice. Suggested daily doses vary by goal, from 2.5 grams for joint pain, skin and hydration to 5 grams for bone density and 15 grams for muscle mass alongside resistance training. Manufacturers often recommend at least 12 weeks. The passage also emphasizes a balanced diet with foods that support collagen production and recommends third-party-tested products, while noting that research is ongoing.

The Midline Option is an option run in which the quarterback reads an interior defensive lineman, handing off to a fullback for an A-gap dive or keeping through the B-gap. It requires no dedicated block on the read defender and complements inside-and-outside veer offenses, but exposes the quarterback to heavy contact. Common variations include Flexbone Midline and Midline “Follow,” a short-yardage concept used by Army, Navy, and Air Force.

Backtests of the Santa Claus Rally showed strong year-end performance in German DAX and Euro Stoxx 50 stocks. Using the EWG and FEZ ETFs, EWG averaged a 2.1% gain per trade with an 81% win rate and 13 profit factor, while FEZ averaged 1.5%, with an 81% win rate and 9 profit factor. Holiday-period performance substantially exceeded random weekly averages of 0.12% for DAX 40 and 0.18% for Euro Stoxx 50, though recent returns have fallen below historical averages. The article cautions that these results do not guarantee future performance.

Plasmodium falciparum PfEMP1 is encoded by approximately 60 mutually exclusive var genes and is a major ligand mediating infected erythrocyte sequestration. This study examined how pre-existing malaria immunity influences var-gene expression, infection outcome, and antibody responses during controlled human malaria infection (CHMI).

Nineteen semi-immune Gambian men were classified as sero-high or sero-low based on antibodies against six malaria antigens before receiving 3,200 NF54/3D7 sporozoites. Sero-low participants had higher peak parasitaemia and total var-transcript levels. Two “controllers,” both sero-high, had the longest latency, lowest parasite multiplication rates, and more restricted, low-entropy var repertoires. Sero-high participants also recognized a broader range of PfEMP1 domains. Whole-transcriptome analysis of parasites from ten participants identified var genes as the main source of expression heterogeneity, with RT-qPCR confirming the sequencing results.

In vivo var-gene turnover was rapid: in one controller, all genes detected on day 14 were undetectable after three life cycles. Estimated transition rates varied by var group, with group A among the fastest. In vitro, cultures from sero-low participants converged rapidly toward a shared high-entropy steady state, whereas sero-high cultures converged more slowly and retained evidence of their initial expression state. A four-state Markov-chain model fitted the in-vitro dynamics; group C and B/C switching rates were close to their in-vivo turnover rates, while group A and B rates were lower.

Protein-array analysis of 213 PfEMP1 domains and 18 other antigens showed that sero-low participants more than doubled their breadth of PfEMP1 recognition after infection, while sero-high participants showed little change. A random-forest model classified the groups with 98% accuracy. Broader pre-existing recognition was associated with longer latency and lower peak parasitaemia. Pre-existing PfEMP1 recognition was moderately associated with lower var-expression diversity, particularly for groups A, B, and B/C, but antibody acquisition after infection was not evidently related to the intensity of PfEMP1 expression during the challenge.

The authors proposed that intrinsic var-gene switching establishes and maintains a diverse repertoire, while immune negative selection narrows this repertoire in strongly immune hosts; poorly immunogenic PfEMP1 domains may persist and support parasite survival.

Musk said the Model 3 had over half a million advance reservations as he handed the first 30 cars to employee buyers at Tesla's Fremont factory. The $35,000 base model has a 220-mile range; a $44,000 version offers 310 miles. Reservations rose from about 373,000 in April 2016, and buyers likely won't receive cars until late 2018. Musk warned of at least six months of "manufacturing hell," citing production problems that marred the Model S and Model X. Tesla has burned over $2 billion in cash this year; shares have surged 54% since January.

Dr. Edward Kwapong, newly elected IHRMP President, urged HR practitioners at the institute's ninth graduation ceremony in Accra to adopt professional certification over raw academic qualifications. Executive Director Ebenezer Agbetor reported 136 associate and nine certified graduands, up 32%, while guest speaker Irene Asare said AI and robotics must combine with human workers to boost productivity.

Trend Micro identified 89 malicious Chrome extensions affecting more than 423,000 users and forming the “Droidclub” botnet. Distributed through malvertising and social engineering, the extensions displayed ads and exploit kits, injected cryptocurrency mining code, and used Yandex Metrica session-replay scripts to observe browsing and capture form data, though not passwords. An earlier version mined Monero via Coinhive. The extensions also hindered reporting and removal through deceptive redirects. Google removed and disabled them, while Cloudflare took down their command-and-control servers. Similar threats included four ICEBRG extensions with over 500,000 installs and Archive Poster, which also ran Coinhive.

Soccer formations organize players for effective defense and attack. Selection depends on team size, player skills, and the coach’s familiarity with the tactics. Over the past century, soccer has shifted toward fewer forwards, balanced spacing, versatile players, greater fitness, and more short passes. Standard full-side formations count 10 field players as defenders, midfielders, and forwards, listed from the defensive goal outward—for example, 4-3-3 or 4-4-2. Newer notations distinguish roles further, such as 4-3-2-1 or 4-6.

U.S. Soccer recommends 4-3-3 and 4-4-2 for ages 15–19, 4-3-3 for ages 13–14, and 3-2-3 for ages 9–12; no formations are specified for younger groups. Coaches may adapt formations for smaller-sided play, such as 2-2-2 for seven-a-side or 2-1 for four-a-side. Effective use requires knowledge of position names, player placement, tactics, teamwork, and clear team communication. Formations can also help young children progress from unstructured play to team-oriented play.

Billy Caldwell, 12, received a short-term Home Office licence for medicinal cannabis oil to control seizures from rare epilepsy while in London. His return to Co Tyrone awaits Northern Ireland Department of Health approval. His mother says officials are unresponsive, while the department says it is working with the Home Office to resolve the delay.

A NASA/ESA Hubble Space Telescope image shows NGC 6000, a spiral galaxy 102 million light-years away in Scorpius. Its golden center contains older, smaller stars, while blue spiral arms feature clusters of young, massive stars; the colors reflect stellar ages, masses, and temperatures. Hubble detected faint remnants of two supernovae observed in 2007 and 2010, data that can help constrain the progenitor stars’ masses and identify possible companions. Four thin yellow-and-blue streaks on the galaxy’s right side come from a Solar System asteroid crossing Hubble’s field during four sequential, filtered exposures.

On May 12, 2021, Amazon.com, Inc. closed the sale of eight series of notes pursuant to an underwriting agreement dated May 10, 2021 among the Company and J.P. Morgan Securities LLC, Citigroup Global Markets Inc., Morgan Stanley & Co. Exhibits include the underwriting agreement, officers' certificate, forms of each note, an opinion and consent of Gibson, Dunn & Crutcher LLP, and the cover page.

Patterns for distributed systems let teams reuse proven approaches to recurring reliability, agility, and scalability problems. They help developers learn from previous mistakes, provide a shared vocabulary, and identify reusable components. At the single-node level, splitting applications into containers enables resource isolation, clear ownership, separation of concerns, independent testing and deployment, and modular reuse.

The sidecar pattern coschedules an application container with a helper container that augments it. Examples include adding HTTPS to a legacy service, synchronizing dynamic configuration, exposing process and resource data, and building a Git-based PaaS. Ambassador containers broker communication with external systems, including shard routing, service discovery, and request splitting. Adapter containers translate heterogeneous application interfaces into standard interfaces for monitoring, logging, and health checks. Reusable containers require parameterization, stable APIs, and documentation.

Multi-node patterns use replicated, load-balanced stateless services with readiness probes, optional session tracking, caching, rate limiting, and SSL termination. Sharded services divide state and requests among shards, commonly through a root or ambassador; sharding functions use hashing and modulo to route requests. Sharded caches use memory more efficiently than replicated caches, but shard failures affect assigned requests, so individual shards may be replicated and scaled independently. Microservices provide focused components, stable API contracts, team autonomy, and independent scaling, but make debugging, architecture, and coordination more difficult.

The speaker outlines principles for governing as president, emphasizing popular sovereignty, constitutional limits, and individual rights. He holds that government derives its authority solely from the consent of the governed, protects unalienable liberties, and must remain within its proper sphere. Constitutional ambiguities often reflect difficult questions of intent rather than disloyal motives, but concentrating granted powers in one department would be especially dangerous.

He pledges never to serve a second presidential term, viewing indefinite tenure as corrupting and incompatible with republican government. He argues that legislative power belongs exclusively to Congress and that presidential vetoes should be used conservatively to uphold the Constitution, guard against hasty legislation, and protect minorities from sectional oppression.

To prevent executive overreach, he promises to keep the Treasury independent of presidential control, prohibit public officers from interfering in elections, defend press freedom, and avoid executive participation in originating legislation or financial policy. He strongly opposes an exclusively metallic currency, believing it would deepen inequality and promote usury.

He affirms that residents of the District of Columbia are free American citizens rather than subjects and should have their rights protected. He also stresses the need for harmony among federal and state authorities, respect for states’ reserved powers, and patient resolution of jurisdictional disputes. State efforts to fulfill legitimate financial obligations should be supported, but one state must not control another’s domestic institutions.

The speaker warns that factional violence and the concentration of power threaten liberty. Genuine liberty requires patriotism, moderation, tolerance, and constant public vigilance; false appeals to democracy can conceal designs to establish monarchy or aristocratic rule. Political parties are useful only while they hold officials accountable, and national union should take precedence over party loyalty.

In foreign affairs, he pledges to preserve peace and friendly relations while defending American rights and honor. Relations with Indigenous nations should follow strict principles of justice and liberality. He concludes by affirming Christian religion, sound morals, religious liberty, and religious responsibility as foundations of lasting national happiness, and promises to discharge presidential duties with confidence in public support.
IDC expects HPCaaS to gain importance as global collaboration and digitalization advance; efficient, data-based product development requires common infrastructure providing a single source of truth.
The Alabama Supreme Court dismissed Riley’s certiorari petition as abated after his death; all justices concurred.

Thirteen-year-old Benje Choucroun asked White House press secretary Sarah Huckabee Sanders what the administration is doing to prevent school shootings. Sanders said a presidential school safety commission was meeting to discuss protecting students and making schools feel safe.

HRO Today’s October 18, 2017 webinar features Elliot Clark, Katy Theroux, and Cory Kruse examining how HR strategy, recruitment metrics, and candidate experience affect hiring productivity, quality, fit, and retention.

The Milwaukee Brewers beat the Chicago Cubs 6-3 Monday, winning six of their last seven games. Eric Thames tied a club record with his fifth consecutive homer, while Ryan Braun and Jeff Bandy also homered. The Cubs lost their fourth straight game and fourth straight at Wrigley Field since May 2014. Chase Anderson earned the win, and Neftali Felix recorded his fifth save in five attempts. Three former Cubs received their 2016 World Series rings, and both teams provided injury and roster updates.
The team hung on after opponents tied the game and did not collapse. Sergei’s timely, decisive play proved crucial as both teams contributed to a balanced game.

Riverton Investment Corporation sued the United States for a tax refund after the IRS disallowed deductions for its 1990s repurchases of stock from management employees. The court held that Paragraph 9 of the Management Stockholder’s Agreement was ambiguous and admitted parol evidence, which showed that permanent restrictions limited sales to Riverton or permitted family transferees, capped repurchase prices at 60% of book value, and guaranteed employees at least their original purchase price. These non-lapse restrictions prevented a taxable transfer of stock to the employees in the 1980s, so the 1990s payments were deductible compensation rather than non-deductible stock redemptions. The court granted Riverton’s summary-judgment motion, denied the government’s summary-judgment and motion-to-strike motions, rejected the magistrate judge’s recommendation, and entered judgment for Riverton. The parties were directed to stipulate to appropriate damages and interest or report their inability to agree.

Conformis Inc. (CFMS) shares fell 6.47% in the latest session, closing at $1.30. Analysts’ mean 52-week target is $5, based on six opinions, with targets ranging from $4 to $6. The average brokerage recommendation is 2.43 across seven recommendations: two Buy, one Outperform, three Hold, one Underperform and no Sell. ATR-14 is 0.16; weekly and monthly volatility are 7.15% and 6.12%. RSI is 18.89. Market capitalization is $56.95 million, with 43.81 million shares outstanding.

Six teachers were suspended: three from Haoreibi Makha Leikai LP Madrasa for unauthorized private operation and missed classes, and three from Thoudam Wangmata Primary School for unexplained absences.

The passage traces the evolution of software patterns from procedural programming and object-oriented design to distributed-system architecture. The “gang of four” *Design Patterns* established reusable, interface-based solutions and a shared vocabulary for programmers. Open-source communities further promoted shared development and reusable container technology. Patterns are presented as general blueprints rather than technology-specific instructions, offering three main benefits: learning from others’ mistakes, providing a common language, and enabling reusable components.

Modern applications may be divided into containers to isolate resources, establish ownership, separate concerns, and create independently owned and reusable modules. Single-node container groups are tightly coupled, typically coscheduled and able to share filesystems, networks, and other resources; in Kubernetes, such a group is called a pod.

The sidecar pattern pairs an application container with a colocated container that augments it. Examples include adding HTTPS termination to a legacy service, synchronizing dynamic configuration, exposing process-resource information, and building a simple Git-driven PaaS. Reusable sidecars should be parameterized—preferably through environment variables—expose stable APIs, and be documented through Dockerfile directives such as `EXPOSE`, `ENV`, and `LABEL`.

The ambassador pattern uses a colocated container to broker an application’s interactions with external systems while the application connects to a local endpoint. Applications include routing requests among storage shards, discovering and connecting to environment-specific services, and splitting traffic between production and experimental implementations. The pattern separates concerns and allows ambassador containers to be reused across applications.

The adapter pattern modifies an application’s external interface to match a common convention without changing the application container. It can adapt monitoring outputs to a standard such as Prometheus, normalize heterogeneous logging formats through tools such as Fluentd, and provide richer database health checks. Separate adapters are especially useful for third-party containers because they avoid maintaining modified application images and permit independent reuse, updates, and resource allocation.

The passage then introduces microservices, which divide an application into independently developed services connected through stable APIs. This approach improves team autonomy, independent release schedules, reliability, and targeted scaling, but makes debugging and system design more difficult because failures span many services and machines.

Multi-node patterns include replicated load-balanced services and sharded services. A replicated service consists of identical, stateless instances behind a load balancer, providing redundancy and horizontal scaling; readiness probes indicate when instances can accept traffic. Session tracking can preserve user affinity through hashing or cookies. Additional replicated tiers can provide caching, rate limiting and denial-of-service protection, and SSL termination, as illustrated with Kubernetes deployments of application servers, Varnish, and nginx.

In contrast, each shard of a sharded service handles only a subset of requests, with a root routing requests to the appropriate shard. Sharding is primarily used for stateful data too large for one machine and can improve cache memory utilization by eliminating duplicate cached data. Because shard failure can reduce cache hit rates and increase latency or load, critical caches may use replicated shards, combining shard distribution with redundancy and independent scaling. Kubernetes examples illustrate these patterns using Redis, memcached, StatefulSets, Services, ConfigMaps, and ambassador proxies.

At media day, LeBron James said his expiring contract will have no impact on his performance as he enters his 23rd NBA season, a record he will share with Vince Carter. James exercised his $52.6 million player option and expressed excitement about the Lakers’ revamped roster while saying he is not worried about his contract or future. Still recovering from a Grade 2 left MCL sprain and foot problems, he may be limited during training camp but aims to be ready for an 82-game season. James said the Lakers must play championship basketball every day, while Luka Doncic identified winning the championship as the goal. He also said his retirement decision will depend on whether he remains excited by the process, not on whether his son Bryce reaches the NBA.

Facebook acquired the team of London-based Bloomsbury AI in an “acquihire,” rather than the company or its products. The startup, founded in 2015, specializes in natural language processing and developed “Cape,” which reads documents and answers questions about them. Facebook said the team will support its NLP research; Bloomsbury AI’s future remains unclear.

Patrick Cullen, 33, received a four-year prison sentence, suspended for the final 12 months, after pleading guilty to snatching a 21-year-old woman’s handbag in Limerick. The woman fell and cut her finger when the strap broke. The judge cited Cullen’s prior record, cooperation, remorse, and the recovery of the bag, noting that the robbery was opportunistic and unpremeditated.

Under Comp. St. 1911, ch. 53, § 1, a married woman’s nonexempt separate property cannot be sold for family necessaries until an execution against her husband for the debt has been issued and returned unsatisfied. This is a condition precedent that may be asserted before sale, even when the wife’s judgment recites that it involved necessaries. Ida C. Scott successfully enjoined enforcement of a $61.50 judgment against her property because no judgment had first been obtained against her husband, Frank Scott. Her failure to raise coverture and the absence of a husband judgment in the original action did not preclude the defense. The district court’s injunction was affirmed. The court did not decide whether her land was exempt under federal law governing Omaha Tribe property.

This study evaluates and ranks the effects of digitalization on online higher education quality in Vietnam using the spherical fuzzy analytic hierarchy process (SFAHP). Nine education experts provided pairwise judgments across five criteria: pedagogical integration, student engagement, accessibility of digital resources, adaptability and innovation, and technological infrastructure. Pedagogical integration ranked highest with a priority weight of 0.236, followed by student engagement (0.212), resource accessibility (0.203), adaptability and innovation (0.184), and technological infrastructure (0.165). The results emphasize integrating teaching methods with technology rather than prioritizing infrastructure alone. Recommended strategies include training educators in digital pedagogy, supporting interactive and personalized learning, building learner communities, improving equitable access to digital resources, investing in reliable infrastructure, and enabling experimentation with emerging technologies. The authors note that reliance on expert evaluations may not represent all stakeholders and recommend broader research.

Reuters table shows Asian currency rates against the dollar at 0134 GMT on Feb 2, with latest bids, previous-day and year-to-date percentage moves versus end-2017; the yen fell 109.3, won 1072.8, yuan 6.28, with ringgit and baht up about 4% and peso down 3.39% so far in 2018.

Ottawa defeated Philadelphia 4-3 in a shootout at Wells Fargo Center, with Mike Hoffman ending the sixth round using Peter Forsberg’s forehand-backhand-one-hand move. Coach Guy Boucher credited Hoffman’s high-risk approach, while the winger suggested the successful move might be called “The Hoff.” Rookie Colin White earned his first NHL point with an assist on Matt Duchene’s first-period goal; Sean Couturier scored for Philadelphia.

The column also noted Philadelphia Eagles–New England Patriots Super Bowl enthusiasm in Ottawa, with Craig Anderson backing the Eagles and Mike Condon and Colin White favoring New England. Defenseman Johnny Oduya earned a $250,000 bonus by appearing in his 41st game and could earn two more $250,000 bonuses. With the trade deadline approaching, Calgary was reportedly interested in Ottawa’s Zack Smith and Jean-Gabriel Pageau, though a high price was expected.

The Mets missed the playoffs despite offseason additions Juan Soto and Pete Alonso, struggling after a strong first half as their starters and bullpen faltered. Kodai Senga endured injuries, a Triple-A stint and two inconsistent seasons. GM David Stearns said Senga has potential but called it foolish to expect 30 starts next season.

SCDNR biologists caught and satellite-tagged “Harry-Etta,” an 820-pound female tiger shark, in St. Helena Sound. The tag will track her movements for a year, providing data on tiger shark longevity, reproduction and migration. Ultrasound confirmed she is pregnant—the first known pregnant female in the agency’s satellite-tagging program—allowing researchers to study her gestation habitats. Southern sounds have been identified as important foraging and potentially nursing and reproductive areas. Harry-Etta’s movements are available through the OCEARCH Global Shark Tracker.

Offensive linemen form a five-player unit responsible for creating rushing lanes, protecting the quarterback, and enabling the offense to score. They must communicate and work together while handling one-on-one blocks, combinations, pulls, blitzes, stunts, and defensive alignments. Their required skills include run- and pass-blocking, athleticism, strength, awareness, and technique; a general body estimate is 6'2"–6'8" and 300–340 pounds, with variations among centers, guards, and tackles.

The position is portrayed as selfless and rarely spotlighted, allowing star skill players to receive attention, but linemen are often blamed when an offense struggles. Their steady, coordinated play is presented as a major factor in offensive success and in the performances of players such as Patrick Mahomes, Derrick Henry, and Davante Adams. The passage also identifies Jim Otto as an outstanding center, John Hannah as a dominant guard, and Hall of Fame tackle Anthony Munoz as among the best offensive linemen.

A Concordia University review of more than 140 studies estimates that people consume 39,000–52,000 microplastic particles annually, with bottled-water drinkers ingesting about 90,000 more particles than tap-water consumers. Microplastics shed from single-use bottles during manufacturing, storage, transportation and degradation can be ingested directly. Once swallowed, these particles may enter the bloodstream and reach organs, potentially contributing to chronic inflammation, oxidative stress, hormonal disruption, reproductive impairment, neurological damage and cancer. However, long-term effects remain uncertain because testing and standardized measurement methods are limited, while the most reliable detection tools are costly. Although governments are limiting plastic waste, few policies specifically address water bottles. Sajedi says bottled water is acceptable in emergencies but should not be a daily option, emphasizing education and chronic rather than acute toxicity concerns.

President Martin Van Buren reported growing unrest along the northern U.S. frontier amid a civil war in Canada, with American citizens organizing an armed force at Navy Island and procuring arms and supplies. He urged citizens to return home peaceably and warned that unlawful interference in British Provinces would result in arrest and punishment without government assistance.

University of Pennsylvania researchers randomly assigned 81 healthy adults to 20 minutes of transcranial direct-current stimulation or a brief control pulse. The next day, stimulated participants reported lower stated likelihoods of physical assault (47%) and sexual assault (70%) than controls and judged both acts more morally wrong. However, outside experts cautioned that stated intentions may not predict actual violence. Repeated sessions might change behavior, beginning with changes in intent, and the procedure was considered low-risk despite uncertainty about its effects.

An elk hunter’s 2010 discovery in Montana’s Charles M. Russell National Wildlife Refuge led to identification of a new elasmosaur species that lived about 70 million years ago in an inland sea. The well-preserved, nearly complete fossil had a roughly 7½-foot neck and about 40 vertebrae, unlike most elasmosaurs, whose necks reached 18 feet and contained as many as 76 vertebrae. Its coexistence with larger-necked elasmosaurs contradicted the belief that the group did not evolve longer necks over millions of years. The carnivorous marine reptile had a small head and paddle-like limbs and could reach 30 feet long. The species was described in the Journal of Vertebrate Paleontology.

The professor gives a compressed algebra course aimed at understanding finite fields and preparing for Reed–Solomon codes. He reviews integer factorization and Euclidean division, modular arithmetic and \(Z_n\), then groups and their axioms, emphasizing the permutation property. Finite cyclic groups are described as isomorphic to \(Z_n\).

A subgroup is presented as a subset that is itself a group under the parent group’s operation, with examples including \(\{0,5\}\), the even residues in \(Z_{10}\), and \(nZ\) within the integers. A coset is a translate of a subgroup. Distinct cosets are either identical or disjoint and collectively partition the group. In finite groups, Lagrange’s theorem follows: the size of a subgroup divides the size of the group. Cosets can be added to form the quotient group \(G/H\). In particular, \(Z/nZ\) is isomorphic to \(Z_n\), and residue classes are interpreted as cosets of \(nZ\).

Fields are then defined as sets with two operations: addition forms an abelian group with identity \(0\), while multiplication on the nonzero elements forms an abelian group with identity \(1\); multiplication must also distribute over addition. The real, complex, and binary fields are given as examples. These axioms imply additive and multiplicative inverses, subtraction, division, and cancellation.

For a prime \(p\), the elements \(0,\ldots,p-1\) with addition and multiplication modulo \(p\) form the prime field \(F_p\). Primality ensures that multiplying two nonzero residues cannot produce zero and that every nonzero element has an inverse; this fails for composite moduli such as \(10\). Every finite field with prime size is isomorphic to \(F_p\), and every finite field contains a prime subfield isomorphic to \(F_p\). The size of this subfield is the field’s characteristic \(p\), which satisfies \(p\beta=0\) for every field element \(\beta\). In characteristic two, \(1+1=0\), addition equals subtraction, and every element added to itself gives zero.

The lecture concludes by introducing polynomials over a field. Coefficients lie in the field, while \(x\) is an indeterminate whose distinction from field elements is important in finite fields. Polynomial addition is coefficientwise, and multiplication expands and collects terms. Degrees add under multiplication when both polynomials are nonzero; defining the zero polynomial’s degree as \(-\infty\) preserves this rule. The set of all polynomials is an abelian group under addition but not a field under multiplication because only nonzero constant polynomials have multiplicative inverses.

Middle States, SACSCOC, and WASC presidents held a webinar on credit transfer and AI. The author found the proposals vague: accreditors favor a “default to yes” approach unless evidence supports denial, but offered no concrete standards, enforcement mechanism, or implementation plan. AI could speed transcript assessment and transfer decisions alongside admissions and financial aid, though hallucinations raise concerns. Credit-transfer resistance often reflects departments’ economic interests, and stronger mandates from provosts, legislatures, or accreditors can change practice. However, regional accreditors lost their de facto monopolies after the first Trump administration, and colleges can now choose among alternative, potentially more lenient or ideologically aligned accreditors, weakening their authority. Overall, the direction was welcomed, but more concrete action was requested.

A security aide to Ebonyi State Governor David Umahi allegedly slapped FRSC officer Soji after the officer delayed Umahi’s convoy at an Eagle Square checkpoint established to restrict unauthorized access to the PDP convention. FRSC spokesman Bisi Kazeem said no official report had been filed. Separately, security personnel at the venue were observed accepting cash from unaccredited party members in exchange for passage.

After digesting tonight and traveling, the speaker expects another close game. They praised a strong first period despite a goal on a marginal offensive-zone call and stressed finishing opportunities. The Devils face home-ice pressure; first goals have mattered in the close series, as the speaker’s team scored first in the first three games.

The seventh annual Julia’s Hope Cup and Carnival will take place at Chippawa Park in Welland on Feb. 17, featuring pond hockey, a children’s tournament, food, games, a silent auction and other activities. Created in memory of Paul Turner’s daughter Julia, who died of cancer in 2011, it raises money for The Hope Centre. Last year’s event raised $20,000 and drew about 1,000 people.

CBS’ new drama *Doubt* premieres February 15 at 10/9c and airs Wednesdays at 10/9c. It follows Isaiah Roth and Associates, a defense firm handling high-stakes cases. Attorney Sadie Ellis takes on pediatric surgeon Billy Brennan, accused of a murder committed 24 years earlier, while questioning her personal feelings and professional duty.

Tesla, Inc. filed its FY2021 Form 10-K for the year ended December 31, 2021. The Delaware corporation is headquartered in Austin, Texas; its common stock trades as TSLA on Nasdaq. It was a large accelerated filer, reported $541.28 billion in non-affiliate market value as of June 30, 2021, and had 1,033,507,611 shares outstanding as of January 31, 2022.

Tesla designs, manufactures, sells and leases electric vehicles and energy generation and storage systems and provides related services. Its two reportable segments are automotive and energy generation and storage. Automotive offerings include Model 3, Model Y, Model S and Model X, with Cybertruck, the new Tesla Roadster and Tesla Semi planned. Energy products include Powerwall, Megapack, retrofit solar systems and Solar Roof. The company develops battery and powertrain technology, vehicle control and infotainment software, and vision-based Autopilot and Full Self-Driving systems, with an intended autonomous ride-hailing network. It sells directly through its website and company-owned stores and locations and operates service centers, mobile technicians, Superchargers and Destination Chargers.

Manufacturing facilities include Fremont and Gigafactory Shanghai for vehicles, Gigafactory Nevada for batteries and components, and Gigafactory New York for Solar Roof, energy-storage and Supercharger components; Gigafactory Berlin and Gigafactory Texas were scheduled to begin production in 2022. Tesla also offers vehicle financing, leasing and insurance, energy-system financing and PPAs, warranties and extended service plans.

The filing describes supply-chain, regulatory, competitive and operational risks. Key concerns include pandemic and macroeconomic disruption, component and semiconductor shortages, raw-material volatility, battery-cell dependence, demand uncertainty, production-ramp delays, new-factory construction and localization, international operations, product and software defects, battery safety, product liability, regulatory restrictions on self-driving vehicles, and residual-value, financing and credit risks. Tesla also reports a 99,290-person worldwide workforce and describes its ESG, responsible-sourcing, safety, employee-development, diversity and governance practices.
Houston Dash captain Carli Lloyd injured her ankle against FC Kansas City. X-rays were negative, and she said she was “down but not out.” The Dash had not said how many games she might miss.

The speaker said Jersey played solidly and shut opponents down after taking the lead, though the team generated too little offense. With the series continuing, Jersey must focus on a strong road game, find a solution without Peter, and rely on its successful power play.

Two teens were arrested after allegedly stealing a Smoky Mountain Children's Home van and leading a multijurisdictional chase that ended when they hit a vehicle and a Chickamauga Dam barrier wall. No serious injuries occurred.

Via HID AMDI0095, the OS binds a driver to the ACPI-defined TMPM device, whose resources are declared in ACPI. A page-migration driver must enable PAGEMIGRATION_EN once in every IOMMU’s IOMMU_MMIO_CNTRL_1. TMPM uses mailboxes and a ring buffer for parallel command processing; the firmware advances the read pointer upon completion.
Cirque du Soleil will donate $1 million and 5,000 tickets following the Las Vegas shooting, supporting victims’ families and first responders and planning a benefit show.

President Ram Nath Kovind, in his first address as president on the eve of Independence Day, commemorated 70 years of freedom and paid tribute to those who sacrificed for independence. He urged citizens to take responsibility for national development, including ensuring government benefits reach the needy, supporting sanitation and girl-child initiatives, embracing GST, and paying taxes honestly. He called for a compassionate, rapidly developing “New India” by 2022 and urged support for underprivileged children’s education and a better future for the next generation.

A WIRED podcast episode hosted by Zoë Schiffer with politics editor Leah Feiger highlights five stories: Rutgers professor Mark Bray’s flight to Europe after threats over his antifa book and his family’s blocked airline reservation; ICE’s planned 24/7 social-media surveillance operation, including AI-assisted monitoring for immigration enforcement; a Harvard study finding that AI companion apps used emotional manipulation in 37% of goodbye conversations; misinformation and speculation surrounding the FDA’s announcement of leucovorin calcium as an unproven autism treatment; and an OpenAI announcement about internal business tools that prompted declines in DocuSign, HubSpot, and Salesforce shares.

Feiger and Schiffer also discuss signs of an AI bubble, contrasting projected data-center spending of $500 billion for 2026–2027 with roughly $12 billion in consumer spending, while noting AI’s potentially transformative impact and the possibility that financial speculation could collapse without halting technological progress.

Former Southport MP John Pugh warned that Sainsbury’s planned 60,000 sq ft Meols Cop store, replacing Homebase and promising 400 jobs, could cause further town-centre job losses. He criticised Sefton Council’s support for the project and called for a fallback plan for Lord Street.
GoDaddy gave The Daily Stormer 24 hours to transfer its domain after a post denigrating Heather Heyer violated its terms of service.

The 2017 Lexus LC500 and LC500h start at £76,595 each, with over one-third of UK units pre-ordered. The V8 produces 467hp; the hybrid has 354hp. Optional Sport and Sport+ packages provide additional upgrades.

A 12-month study of more than 24,000 Slimming World members found that those pursuing ambitious “dream weight” targets lost an average of 19% of their starting weight, compared with 11% among those targeting less than 10%. Experts called for public-health guidance to encourage ambitious, personally chosen goals alongside regular support, rather than conservative 5–10% targets. Members who set their own target were 10 times more likely to succeed. Participant Hollie Barrett credited her 8-stone 6-pound loss to committing fully to her plan and receiving weekly group support.

WIRED tested carry-ons, personal items, and travel backpacks by examining airline fit, weight, materials, storage, handles, wheels, durability, price, and warranty. The Travelpro Maxlite 5 was highlighted as the best bag in the $100–$150 range for its light weight, strong zippers, smooth wheels, and exterior toiletry pocket, though its handle extensions and grab-handle stitching were criticized. The premium Travelpro Platinum line was considered less worthwhile because of its added weight and price. Peak Design’s Roller Pro received praise for its creative “drawbridge” opening, hybrid construction, and expandable storage, but concerns included its weight and limited warranty.

Rimowa’s aluminum suitcase was described as exceptionally durable, balanced, weather-resistant, and increasingly attractive as it develops scratches. Briggs & Riley was recommended for its comprehensive lifetime warranty, durable ballistic nylon, and low-profile components, while Yeti’s Crossroads 35L was praised for rugged construction and pockets. Antler’s carry-on was noted for smooth, quiet wheels, a useful front-access pocket, recycled lining, and compliance with US and European size limits. The Beis weekender offered a detachable compartment for use as a personal item, and Tom Bihn, Six Moon Designs, and Aer backpacks were praised for versatility, comfort, organization, and under-seat sizing.

The guide also advises checking each airline’s size rules, using soft-sided bags when flexibility is needed, following the TSA’s 3-1-1 liquids rule, and giving older children their own luggage. Reviewers took at least two flights with each featured bag and tested it in overhead bins or under seats.

Colorado’s Prescription Drug Affordability Board voted to cap payments for Amgen’s arthritis drug Enbrel at $600 per unit for government agencies and commercial health plans covering state residents. The cap equals about $30,350 annually per person, compared with roughly $53,000 paid by the average state insurance plan in 2023.

Long snappers are specialized NFL players who must deliver quick, accurate snaps despite minimal room for error. They snap about seven yards to holders for extra points and field goals and roughly 15 yards to punters, whose three-step approach makes precise placement essential. Long snappers also pursue punt coverage, requiring accuracy, consistency, balance, athleticism, physicality, and the toughness to handle larger players and make tackles. Their build is generally comparable to linebackers. NFL rosters reserve one roster spot for the position, making performance highly competitive. Poor snaps can contribute to missed field goals or blocked punts; the passage cites analytics showing that teams blocking a punt win about 90% of the time. Notable long snappers include two-time Pro Bowl selection Zak DeOssie and Don Mulbach, who ranked second in Lions history for games played.

The October 5 “Inside UT Football” Q&A from Dallas Morning News writer Chip Brown focused on Texas’s upcoming game against Oklahoma. Brown predicted a 24-20 Texas victory, citing the Longhorns’ defense and recent offensive confidence, while identifying Oklahoma’s passing attack against Texas’s secondary as the key matchup. Quotes from Oklahoma coach Bob Stoops addressed the Sooners’ 4-0 start, improved running game, and turnovers in the previous 38-28 loss to Texas.

Brown expected Major Applewhite to start against Oklahoma and play most or all of the game. Chris Simms could return against Missouri as Texas continued rotating quarterbacks. Brown noted that gap blocking helped the offense against Oklahoma State but said the offensive line and punt protection for Kris Stockton remained concerns. Sean Rogers’s availability was doubtful because of a sprained ankle.

Other topics included possible expansion of Royal-Memorial Stadium, Adam Doiron’s possible redshirt, UT’s Big 12-record 231-game scoring streak, David Aaron leaving football for track, potential punt-return changes, and the October 14 Colorado game at 2:30 p.m. Central time with no television coverage.

Brown characterized Texas as talented but inexperienced, needing greater chemistry, leadership, and line development. He defended coach Mack Brown amid criticism, attributing the negative reaction to heightened expectations following the 1998 season and 1999 victory over Nebraska, and advised patience with the quarterback rotation and offensive-line coach.

Attendance at Biloxi's Shuckers opening series rose 21%, with a record 4,006 fans for Jackie Robinson Day and ESPN spotlighting Johnny Davis' home-run-robbing play. The team returns home April 22 with a March of Dimes jersey auction and weekly promotions.

Shelley forwarded Ricki a 24-message PAKK Yahoo Group digest (No. 529) and asked her to add the sender to her contacts. Topics included Russian and Kazakhstan HIV-testing requirements, discounted adoption airfare, accommodations, adoption experiences from Taraz, school placement, and adjusting children’s ages or birth dates. Travel-On offered Delta fares at 70% off for adults and 50% off for adopted children returning to the United States, effective October 15, 2001, through May 31, 2002. Members shared positive experiences with host families, apartments, and hotels in Kazakhstan and detailed travel through Moscow, Almaty, and Taraz. Several parents debated whether to alter or conceal a child’s age, citing educational, social, physical, and legal considerations. The digest also included member introductions, discussion of children’s tantrums and self-harm, and instructions for removing mistakenly posted messages from the group archive.

This medRxiv preprint reports the development and evaluation of the 15-item Language Phenotype Assessment (LPA), a 10-minute clinician-administered test of language comprehension in children aged 2–5 years. The LPA uses manipulatives and brief spoken instructions to assess three developmental phenotypes: Command, Modifier, and Syntactic. It contains three command, five modifier, and seven syntactic items; each item includes four tasks, with at least three correct responses required for a score of 1. Total scores range from 0 to 15. A parent-reported Language Phenotype Evaluation Checklist (LPEC) with the same structure was also developed.

The study evaluated 116 neurotypical children aged 1.5–7 years and separately assessed 79 children aged 2–8 years diagnosed with Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD). Quantile generalized additive models and sigmoidal curves were used to estimate age-related scores and phenotype acquisition. Neurotypical LPA scores increased nearly linearly from ages 1.5 to 5 before reaching a ceiling. By age 1.6, 50% of children had attained the Command Phenotype; by age 3.0, 50% had attained the Modifier Phenotype; and by age 3.7, 50% had attained the Syntactic Phenotype. All neurotypical children had attained these phenotypes by ages 3, 4, and 5, respectively. Parent-reported median ages were 1.6, 2.7, and 3.0 years.

LPA reliability was high, with Cronbach’s alpha of 0.92, four-month test-retest correlation of 0.96, and inter-observer kappa of 0.97. The LPEC also had high internal consistency and test-retest reliability, and LPA and LPEC scores correlated at r = 0.78. Among children aged 5 and older with ASD, 39% reached the Syntactic Phenotype on the LPA, compared with all neurotypical children; parent reports showed a similar gap.

Among neurotypical children aged 4 and older who understood canonical instructions, 92% also understood noncanonical cup-stacking directions and 88% understood noncanonical spatial-preposition directions. The corresponding rates among autistic children were 76% and 60%. The authors conclude that the LPA may support early identification of language deficits, characterization of comprehension independently of verbal output, and monitoring of language therapy, including minimally verbal children. Limitations include the logistical demands of using manipulatives and the need for children to understand basic color, size, number, and spatial terms before integration can be assessed.

The Trump administration’s nuclear posture review largely retains Obama-era modernization and arms-control policies while taking a more aggressive approach toward Russia. It calls for no net increase in strategic nuclear weapons, but endorses new bombers, submarines and land-based missiles and adherence to New START, which limits the U.S. and Russia to 1,550 warheads each. It calls North Korea a “clear and grave threat,” warns that a North Korean nuclear attack would mean “the end of that regime,” and identifies China as a potential nuclear adversary.

The doctrine gives nuclear weapons a fuller deterrent role while maintaining ambiguity over “extreme circumstances.” The administration proposes modifying a small number of Trident-launched ballistic missiles with smaller-yield warheads near term and developing a nuclear-armed sea-launched cruise missile longer term. It also seeks to deter major nonnuclear attacks, including catastrophic cyberattacks. Arms-control groups criticized the review for blurring nuclear and conventional warfare.

Ministers forming a working administration with the DUP conceded that abolishing line dancing may be necessary for progress because the party condemned it as sinful. Brexit minister David Davis defended the compromise and preferred it to Nigel Farage joining negotiations. Leave voter Nigel Walker also supported it.

An EducationNext national poll found support for charter schools fell from 51% to 39% in one year, while support for universal vouchers (45%) and tax-credit scholarships (55%) rebounded slightly. The charter decline occurred across party, racial and ethnic groups, with no clear explanation. Republicans increasingly favored vouchers over Democrats, but Trump’s influence on responses was minimal. Support for local public schools remained bipartisan, with 55% of Republicans and 54% of Democrats rating them A or B.

The disclosed technology describes robotic systems and methods for selectively gripping and transporting objects using multi-gripper assemblies. It addresses difficulties robots have when selecting objects from groups containing adjacent, irregularly shaped, or differently sized items. The systems can operate in warehouses, distribution or shipping hubs, manufacturing, assembly, packaging, healthcare, and other automation environments, with unloading, transfer, transport, loading, depalletizing, container-switching, packaging, sorting, and piece-picking units.

A robotic transfer assembly includes an imaging system, robotic arm, end effector, vision sensor, and multi-gripper assembly. The gripper assembly has multiple independently addressable vacuum regions or suction-channel banks connected through manifolds to a vacuum source. Selected regions can draw air to hold only targeted objects, even when other gripper portions contact neighboring objects. One or multiple objects may be gripped and released simultaneously or sequentially. Suction elements within a region may be activated individually or in subsets according to an object’s geometry. Vacuum levels and airflow can be adjusted according to object size, weight, contact area, and task requirements.

Imaging data—including video, still images, lidar, radar, depth maps, and point clouds—can identify target objects, determine their poses and locations, recognize object groupings, and locate suitable spaces at drop-off locations. Controllers can select target objects according to accessibility, exposed surfaces, predetermined sequences, stacking patterns, available drop-off space, carrying capacity, and transport plans. Vision sensors associated with the end effector can monitor held objects, verify pickup and relative positioning, count objects, detect obstructions, and support collision avoidance and real-time end-effector adjustments.

A force detector assembly measures forces, moments, pressures, and other contact characteristics associated with gripping and carrying objects. These measurements can be used to determine grip adequacy, object weight and center of mass, and the relative positions or number of retained objects. During transfers, the system can compare grip measurements and image data against thresholds, adjust measurements for orientation, and modify speed, acceleration, location, or handling behavior. If a grip is insufficient, the system can pause a motion plan, release and regrip an object, and retry up to a configured iteration limit; after repeated failure, it can notify an operator, record an error, or select another object.

A registration data store can contain object dimensions, shapes, weights, identifying information, center-of-mass data, expected sensor readings, and template or vision data. It can also store vacuum-gripper characteristics, including region count, capacity, and vacuum settings, and can be updated with operational data for previously unknown packages or conditions. Gripper manifolds may include valves, regulators, sensors, passages, and vacuum chambers, while sealing members, bellowed suction elements, suction cups, and compressible or porous materials accommodate varied surfaces and limit excessive vacuum. In operational use, the system scans pickup and drop areas, identifies targets and destinations, activates selected vacuum regions, executes a planned motion path, monitors the grip before and during transport, releases objects at the destination, and repeats the cycle.

The Fraser Institute will release a study assessing whether B.C.’s carbon tax revenues are offset by tax reductions and how much the government collects, examining a neutrality promise made in 2008 amid federal carbon-pricing requirements by 2018.

The lecture reviews pointwise and uniform convergence for sequences of functions \(f_n:S\to\mathbb R\). Pointwise convergence requires \(f_n(x)\to f(x)\) for every \(x\in S\).
