Uniform convergence requires that, for every \(\varepsilon>0\), one index \(M\) works simultaneously for all \(x\in S\). Uniform convergence implies pointwise convergence, but the converse is false.

For \(f_n(x)=x^n\) on \([0,1]\), the pointwise limit is \(0\) for \(x<1\) and \(1\) at \(x=1\). The convergence is uniform on every \([0,b]\) with \(b<1\), but not on \([0,1]\). A second example of pointwise but not uniform convergence consists of increasingly tall triangular functions that converge pointwise to zero.

The lecture emphasizes that limits cannot always be interchanged, illustrating this with the double limit involving \(n/[k(n+1)]\): taking the \(n\)-limit first gives \(1\), while reversing the order gives \(0\). It frames three related questions: whether a limit of continuous functions is continuous, whether the limit of derivatives equals the derivative of the limit, and whether the limit of integrals equals the integral of the limit. Uniform convergence gives affirmative answers to all three, whereas pointwise convergence alone does not. Counterexamples include \(x^n\), \(x^n/n\), and the triangular functions, whose integrals remain \(1\) despite pointwise convergence to zero.

Several theorems are proved. First, the uniform limit of continuous functions is continuous, using an \(\varepsilon/3\) argument. Second, if continuous functions converge uniformly on \([a,b]\), then the limit of their integrals equals the integral of their limit. Third, if continuously differentiable functions converge uniformly to \(f\) and their derivatives converge uniformly to \(g\), then \(f\) is differentiable and \(f'=g\), using the fundamental theorem of calculus.

Finally, the Weierstrass \(M\)-test is presented: if functions satisfy \(|f_j(x)|\le M_j\) for all \(x\in S\) and the positive series \(\sum M_j\) converges, then \(\sum f_j(x)\) converges absolutely for every \(x\), and its partial sums converge uniformly on \(S\). This provides a broad way to establish uniform convergence and continuity of function series.

The De’Longhi Rivelia automatic latte maker is $200 off, priced at $1,300. Its touchscreen automates drink preparation from grinding beans to frothing milk for options such as lattes, cortados, and flat whites. It features a swappable bean hopper, bean-specific settings and test cups, and a milk frother that produces silky micro-foam. It is easier to use than a manual portafilter machine, though it may not match its coffee quality.

Imran Mohammad, a Rohingya refugee from Myanmar, recounts four years in Manus prison in Papua New Guinea after arriving in 2013 at age 19. He describes severe overcrowding, harsh heat, shipping-container quarters, constant queues, inadequate toilets and washing facilities, shortages of basic supplies, limited phone access, and few opportunities for recreation. He experienced hunger, isolation, despair, and thoughts of suicide, but found strength through education, writing, prayer, and the motto “the pen is mightier than the sword.” He concludes that refugees seeking safety in Australia instead encountered pain, anguish, and, in some cases, death.

Total solar eclipses have long inspired fear and religious interpretation: ancient Greeks saw divine anger, Vikings feared apocalypse, and ancient Chinese believed a dragon was consuming the sun. During the 1878 eclipse, some Americans feared Judgment Day; one terrified father killed his young son and then himself while fleeing perceived Armageddon. Astronomers reject the idea that Jesus’s crucifixion was accompanied by an eclipse, though some Christians fear eclipses may signal the end times. In Islam, an eclipse coinciding with Ibrahim’s death was explained as a sign of God rather than worship or divine recognition. A Missouri nun reassured Catholics that the 2017 eclipse was not a bad omen. David Baron called the experience awe-inspiring and profound, evoking religious feelings and a sense of humanity’s smallness.

The Diamond & One Triangle offense attacks a chaser by placing the star player at the high post for isolation and triangle action. The star can drive for drop passes and layups, kick out to open shots or dribble penetration, or use a lob exchange when the defender overplays the entry pass. Other players rotate into specified alignments, occupy the short corner or low post, flash into the middle, and maintain open spot-up opportunities. Success depends on coordinated execution, interior passing, back cuts, spot-up shooting, defensive recognition, communication, timing, and experience. Coaches should scout when possible, identify expected defensive reads and matchups, observe in-game adjustments, vary alignments and entries, and attack weaker defenders. The Diamond & One defense uses four defenders in a zone and a fifth player focused on pass denial against the opponent’s primary scorer.

A funnel-web spider, described as the world’s most venomous spider, was found inside a Springwood, NSW, home in the Blue Mountains near Sydney. About 5 cm in diameter, it had large fangs capable of piercing a fingernail. Bites can cause nausea, muscle cramps, profuse sweating and numbness around the mouth; the Australian Museum has recorded 13 deaths in Australia. Funnel-webs live along Australia’s east coast and are often found in cool, damp places such as pools, bathrooms and laundries. They are generally defensive and tend to bite when threatened. No human death has occurred since antivenene was introduced in 1981. Taronga Zoo’s Paul Hare advised people not to handle them, wear gloves while gardening and use caution around pool filters. He also noted their ecological role in controlling cockroaches, flies and mosquitoes.

The speaker pledges to preserve, protect, and defend the Constitution and govern according to its principles: forming a more perfect union, establishing justice, ensuring domestic tranquility, providing for common defense, promoting general welfare, and securing liberty. The Constitution is presented as a successful republican compact whose laws and institutions have advanced national growth, expanded territory, strengthened commerce, and promoted liberty, law, and union, despite wars, disease, foreign conflicts, and domestic dissent.

The address acknowledges that both major political parties have contributed talent, integrity, patriotism, and sacrifice, while urges citizens to discard partisan rancor and place confidence in talent and virtue alone. It affirms popular elections, limited and coordinate federal and state governments, civilian control of the military, freedom of speech and religion, fiscal accountability, national defense, and peaceful foreign policy. The federal structure is praised for protecting individual state authority while preserving national sovereignty, and national representation is said to reduce regional prejudice and strengthen unity.

Reviewing the prior administration’s eight years, the speaker credits it with maintaining peace, defending national rights, reducing taxes and debt, limiting military expenditures, improving accountability, expanding territory, promoting the independence of southern nations, suppressing the slave trade, encouraging Indigenous peoples toward agriculture and education, exploring the interior, and advancing national resources. These accomplishments define the speaker’s continuing duty.

The speaker particularly emphasizes federally supported internal improvements, including roads, citing Rome’s enduring public works and widespread public benefit. Although acknowledging constitutional objections, the speaker hopes continued national deliberation will resolve them. Concluding with humility and confidence, the speaker commits to serving the country through cooperation with Congress, executive departments, state governments, and the people, while placing the nation’s future in divine providence.

KGI’s Ming-Chi Kuo expects Apple’s 2017 Apple Watch to retain its existing form factor, marking three generations with the same design. It will reportedly come in 38mm and 42mm sizes, with LTE and non-LTE versions comprising four models. The article notes that only thickness has changed since 2014 and that a major redesign would require substantial work from Apple and app developers. With LTE expected, Apple could prioritize a thinner watch by reducing battery size rather than extending battery life.

A recent music-education graduate faces tuition and certification costs while starting a three-month job earning $1,600 monthly. After a conflict worsened by his hearing impairment, his mother imposed $480 in monthly rent and phone charges, despite previously taking $3,000 from a $5,000 school refund and allegedly keeping the remainder.

The columnist advises budgeting carefully, considering additional work, exploring alternatives before becoming a teacher, and honestly assessing his role in their conflict. The columnist questions his mother’s conduct, suggests professional help if his account is accurate, and asks what she would say has strained their relationship.

President James Madison issued a proclamation on September 1, 1814, condemning the British invasion and destruction of public buildings in Washington, the threatened devastation of coastal towns, and the plunder of Alexandria. While peace negotiations were underway, he urged Americans and government officers to defend their country, authorized militia commanders to summon local forces to protect threatened areas, and called for united resistance to expel the invaders.

The speaker called the loss tough, praised the team’s tenacity and comeback, but said they surrendered too many chances and failed to execute late. They credited Detroit’s effort and said the team must rebound in the playoffs.

After a tight, mistake-filled hockey game, the speaker said his team generated chances but failed to convert several opportunities, while the opponent executed well and took a one-goal lead. He described one goal as a chaotic sequence involving a blocked shot, a rebound off the boards and the puck striking a player’s leg. Another puck remained on a goalie’s back and was held there, though it did not count as a goal and the applicable penalty was unclear. The speaker also discussed shorter forward shifts, line-deployment decisions and the importance of not conceding early or late goals. He said his team did not slow down in the third period but lacked quality on some chances, including a second-period breakaway. Both teams made mistakes and benefited from unpredictable board bounces. He also admitted striking another man’s foot with a two-handed stick after the man continued talking. Despite the loss, he remained confident the team could win the next game at home.

The May 9, 2001 compilation reports that Questia Media, an online college library and research service backed by Enron Chairman Ken Lay, laid off 139 employees, reducing its staff to about 140, and slowed book digitization because of difficulties raising capital and attracting subscribers. Questia said paid subscriptions had risen above 5,000, positive cash flow was expected in about 18 months, and another funding round was planned.

U.S. markets were mixed ahead of a Federal Reserve meeting. The Dow fell 51.66 points to 10,883.51, while the Nasdaq gained 25.20 points to 2,198.77. A 0.1% first-quarter decline in worker productivity raised inflation concerns and pushed long-term yields higher, while short-term yields fell in anticipation of another rate cut. Enron shares fell $1.93 to $56.11.

Enron said Japan’s newly deregulated electricity market remained uncompetitive because of regulations, transmission costs and other barriers. New entrants held only 0.2% of the market, and Enron called for an independent regulator, citing concerns that the Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry could not act impartially because of its relationship with incumbent utilities. Enron Japan also planned an LNG-fired power plant and said increased market liquidity would create competition without destroying existing utilities.

Williams began expanding into European gas and power markets with a 25-person London operation covering the UK, Germany, Scandinavia and Benelux. It planned to use structured transactions, futures and options to manage utilities’ commodity and financial risks, without acquiring physical power assets, and was targeting contracts in Spain and Italy.

The principal coverage concerned Enron’s Dabhol Power project in India. The Maharashtra State Electricity Board disputed the cost of Dabhol power, delayed and defaulted on payments, and invoked force majeure, while Enron pursued arbitration and authorized termination of the power-purchase agreement. Each side appointed an arbitrator, with disputes expected to be heard in London. Lenders with about $200 crore exposed to the project supported termination after the state and central governments failed to resolve the crisis; the DPC board approved termination by 7–1, with IDBI dissenting. An unsourced report said Enron executives’ families had moved from Mumbai to Singapore and security had been tightened, although it was unclear whether this reflected a corporate decision, and more than 15,000 jobs were reportedly at risk if the project or second phase was stopped.

MSEB denied underusing its own capacity to justify buying Dabhol power, citing hydro constraints and inadequate LNG at the Uran plant, and said 95% of Dabhol electricity was used to maintain grid frequency. It also said the federal government was not pressuring it to continue the Enron agreement. MSEB maintained that expanding generation at Uran was uneconomic because of furnace-oil costs. The Swadeshi Jagran Manch demanded a judicial inquiry, alleging that inflated or fabricated demand figures had supported the original deal, and continued seeking its cancellation.

Prize Petroleum also sought to acquire Enron’s 30% interest in the offshore Panna, Mukta and Tapti fields. It valued the stake at about Rs600 crore and planned Rs1,900 crore of investment, including Rs1,300 crore in debt, as Enron sought to farm out its share.

In the MOST optimization phase, researchers tested a Way to Health mobile platform for sleep promotion among 97 children aged 9–12 years in southeastern Pennsylvania and southern New Jersey. Following a two-week run-in, participants were randomized in a 2⁵ factorial design to seven weeks of core sleep tracking and weekly feedback, with varying sleep goals, child- and caregiver-directed loss-framed incentives, screen-time reduction messages, and daily-routine messages, followed by two weeks of follow-up.

Baseline weeknight sleep averaged 7.7 hours and increased by an average of 24 minutes during intervention and 21 minutes at follow-up. No individual component setting achieved the prespecified goal of at least 30 additional minutes. Interaction analysis identified two qualifying combinations. Core intervention plus a caregiver-directed incentive and routine messaging, with either sleep goal, increased sleep by 32.0 minutes during intervention and 26.6 minutes at follow-up; adding screen-time reduction messaging produced increases of 39.6 and 33.2 minutes. Gains began in week one and were maintained during intervention, while sufficient-sleep nights increased by 19–20%.

Child-directed incentives were unfavorable and appeared redundant, whereas caregiver-directed incentives were beneficial. Guideline and personalized sleep goals performed similarly in the top two combinations. The next step is an evaluation-phase randomized controlled trial. Limitations included the single-site, predominantly non-Hispanic White sample, fewer tracker nights among Black participants, short follow-up, and use of a single-sensor tracker with a proprietary algorithm.

At least 30 children died at Gorakhpur's BRD Hospital, which housed patients at ten times its admission capacity, a central team found on Saturday. Concerns arose over SNCUs, where infant warmers were shared and oxygen came from standby cylinders; units in Basti and Ballia were non-existent or non-functional. J P Nadda, Anupriya Patel and C K Mishra announced an Rs 85 crore medical centre in Gorakhpur.

The paper examines deontic argumentation, particularly the concept of weak permission: an action is weakly permitted when an obligation to the contrary cannot be derived. It shows that grounded and stable semantics fail to justify weak permissions when two applicable rules impose conflicting obligations, preventing conclusions that the disputed actions are weakly facultative.

The authors define a Deontic Argumentation Theory in terms of facts, deontic rules, arguments, and an attack relation. Arguments are either natural arguments or imaginary arguments representing weak permission. Building on Defeasible Logic, they introduce a wp-semantics based on support, undercutting, wp-acceptable arguments, and wp-rejected arguments, computed through a fixed-point construction.

The proposed semantics has a unique extension; no argument is both accepted and rejected; and the accepted arguments form a conflict-free set. It also extends grounded semantics because every argument justified under grounded semantics remains justified under wp-semantics. Unlike grounded and stable semantics, wp-semantics can justify weak permissions for both sides of an unresolved obligation conflict when the relevant subarguments are justified. Consequently, weakly facultative conclusions can be derived, and the paper’s main example yields justified weak permissions for both disputed actions and the downstream obligation.

The paper argues that, within a single legal system, unresolved conflicting obligations should neither be individually justified, because doing so would require an unavailable or potentially ad hoc conflict-resolution mechanism. Their cancellation instead supports weak permissions for both actions. It distinguishes weak from strong permission and notes that legal usage and context determine the intended reading. Related work largely does not provide an argumentation semantics for weak permission, while future work aims to integrate wp-semantics with Defeasible Deontic Logic and possible-world semantics.

The global aluminum foil packaging market is expected to grow at approximately 4.5% CAGR, driven by packaging innovation, sustainable and smart designs, rising purchasing power, changing consumer lifestyles, and demand from pharmaceutical and cosmetic industries. Asia Pacific is expected to be the fastest-growing region. Aluminum packaging protects products, reduces waste, and is corrosion-resistant, hygienic, and non-toxic. However, inadequate recycling processes in some countries may hinder growth.

MyWorld is a platform where players build their own games, choosing genres, rules, and single-player, PvP, or Co-Op modes. Objects are placed in design mode and shaped in a model editor, enabling functional elements like turrets, sensors, and robots. Builds can be stored locally or shared with the community, and leveling unlocks pre-built materials. Still unfinished, MyWorld launched a Kickstarter campaign rewarding early backers with exclusive materials.

The passage argues that successful Forex trading does not require exceptional talent, outside opinions, or promises of quick profits. Novices should understand the market, wait for suitable profitable setups, make independent decisions, and develop mental stability by accepting losses and avoiding excessive risk. Profitability requires mastering technical, fundamental, and sentiment analysis. Traders may learn from experts but should not simply copy them, as this can weaken independent judgment. Beginners should take small steps, evaluate advice critically, and gradually build experience.

Tesla, Inc.'s Form 8-K (event date October 7, 2021) reported certified voting results from its 2021 Annual Meeting, where stockholders voted on nine proposals. Class II directors James Murdoch and Kimbal Musk were elected to three-year terms. Management proposals to amend Tesla's certificate of incorporation to reduce director terms to two years and to eliminate supermajority voting requirements failed to reach the required 66 2/3% of outstanding shares. Ratification of PricewaterhouseCoopers LLP as independent auditor for fiscal 2021 was approved. Advisory proposals on reducing director terms to one year and on diversity and inclusion reporting were approved; proposals on employee arbitration reporting, human capital oversight by an independent board committee, and human rights reporting were not approved.

Apple Inc. filed an 8-K dated February 5, 2019, signed by Katherine Adams, Senior Vice President, General Counsel and Secretary, reporting under Item 5.02 that Angela Ahrendts, Senior Vice President, Retail, will depart Apple effective April 15, 2019. She is succeeded by Deirdre O'Brien, who assumed the role of Senior Vice President, Retail + People, effective February 5, 2019.

The NTSC and CSA partnered to improve cloud security vendor reviews by promoting CSA’s Security, Trust & Assurance Registry (STAR) and related tools as recommended practices. The organizations seek to streamline vendor assessments, reduce review time and effort, and recognize vendors that follow best practices. They will develop a STAR-based questionnaire aligned with widely used compliance frameworks and publish a whitepaper explaining how CISOs and vendors can incorporate the program. The groups will also participate in each other’s events, address industry issues through working groups, and collaborate on cloud security research. The NTSC advocates for CISOs and cybersecurity policy, while CSA promotes secure cloud computing practices through research, education, certification, events, and products.

CGCEL submitted a September 20, 2017 expression of interest for Videocon’s brand and business after a September 6 invitation. The bid price is undisclosed; no result, negotiations or binding documents exist. Videocon, carrying over Rs 40,000 crore in debt, has pursued asset sales, including a Rs 4,428 crore spectrum sale.

Daniella Teutsch and Sara Wolf founded HydroChic in 2007 after finding modest swimwear for religious Jewish women lacking. Customer research revealed demand from women who had undergone mastectomies or bariatric surgery and those with skin cancer or psoriasis, prompting products including mastectomy swim tops, compression workout gear, and skin-protecting suits. The New Rochelle, New York, entrepreneurs were formerly educators who developed the company after brainstorming at the beach in 2006.

As the Supreme Court begins its new term, legal experts expect higher education to be a frequent subject, although only two college-related cases, both involving transgender rights, are on the main docket. West Virginia v. B.P.J. and Little v. Hecox. concern transgender athletes barred from participating in track and cross-country. Hecox has asked the court to dismiss her case because of illness, her father’s death and the publicity surrounding the litigation. West Virginia is expected to remain before the court and could affect how courts interpret Title IX’s equal-protection provisions, potentially reaching bathrooms, locker rooms and other sex-segregated activities.

Experts are also closely watching the increasingly used shadow docket, which permits rapid decisions without traditional briefs, oral arguments or written opinions. The lack of notice and explanation can leave institutions little time to prepare and may allow policies to take effect before full judicial review. The court has already granted stays concerning Trump administration policies involving federal-agency staffing, immigration and international enrollment, while experts anticipate disputes over visas, academic freedom, First Amendment rights and federal funding.

The shadow docket also includes Trump v. Orr., concerning passports for transgender or nonbinary people. A ruling extending beyond passports could create inconsistencies between government identification and gender presentation, raising challenges for university housing and operations. Even eventual merits decisions may not reverse harms caused while policies were temporarily allowed to proceed.

Riley Oil Company, a family-run full-service station in Paoli, Indiana, has offered complimentary gas pumping, windshield washing, and oil checks since Glendon Riley opened it in 1971. Six relatives work there, and owners Jo Ann and Jeff Riley expect the business to remain family-owned for generations while emphasizing customer service, fair pricing, and personal interactions with residents.

Police arrested 52-year-old Zette Madden after she allegedly threatened Taco Bell employees with a tire iron, smashed registers and windows, and caused thousands in damage. Tased after ignoring commands, she remains jailed on robbery, malicious injury, and property-destruction charges.

Molecular dynamics simulations were used to study nanoindentation of single-crystalline HCP α-titanium at 10, 300, and 600 K for the [0001], [10̅10], and [2̅110] orientations. An EAM potential, rigid spherical indenter, load–displacement measurements, DXA dislocation analysis, atom-resolved Schmid-factor mapping, shear-strain mapping, strain-tensor analysis, and surface morphology observations were combined to examine orientation- and temperature-dependent plasticity.

All orientations initially showed Hertzian elastic behavior before plasticity onset. The [0001] orientation exhibited pronounced pop-in events, greater residual indentation depths, and the highest dislocation densities. The prismatic orientations showed smoother dislocation nucleation, lower residual depths, and fewer residual dislocations as temperature increased. Beyond approximately 3 nm indentation depth, contact pressure decreased systematically with temperature because of enhanced atomic mobility and thermally activated deformation.

Basal a-type dislocations dominated the deformation, accompanied by c-type, prismatic, and pyramidal c+a dislocations. Stress-induced HCP-to-BCC transformation and transient FCC-like stacking sequences occurred locally, with transformation propensity highest at low temperature. Schmid-factor maps showed that high resolved shear-stress regions coincided with the plastic zone beneath the indenter. Deformation was mainly accommodated by basal and prismatic slip, while pyramidal slip became more active under elevated stress or temperature.

The [0001] orientation developed a circular pile-up pattern at 300 K, while low-temperature deformation was highly localized and 600 K produced diffuse, partially recovered traces. The [10̅10] orientation formed characteristic two-lobe pile-ups and prismatic “lasso” loops composed mainly of a-type and c+a dislocations. The [2̅110] orientation developed asymmetric, curved pile-up features, with loops nucleating directly beneath the indenter and expanding across multiple slip planes.

Increasing temperature generally enhanced dislocation mobility, broadened deformation zones, and promoted recovery and annihilation. The exception was [0001], where dislocation density rose from 0.86 to 1.09 to 1.52 × 10¹⁶ m⁻²; corresponding densities decreased with temperature for [10̅10] and [2̅110]. The simulations provide an atomistic link between temperature, crystallographic orientation, slip activation, residual dislocation structures, and surface pile-up morphology, with the predicted room-temperature features reported to closely match AFM observations.

Microsoft Corporation updated its guidance for the quarter ending June 30, 2022 due to unfavorable foreign exchange movements through May. A slide deck with the revised guidance was furnished as Exhibit 99.1. The filing cautioned that forward-looking statements are subject to risks and uncertainties and noted that the furnished information was not deemed “filed” under Section 18 of the Exchange Act or incorporated by reference except by specific reference.

Unregulated high-seas fishing limits information on vessels, catches, species composition, and sizes, constraining stock assessments and increasing overfishing risks. In the Southwest Atlantic, more than 250 jiggers and trawlers annually catch hundreds of thousands of tons of squid, hake, and rock cod, while nearly 300 foreign jiggers have recently targeted jumbo squid in the Eastern Pacific, raising regional concerns. Falkland Islands scientist Alexander Arkhipkin advised a 2017 IMARPE workshop on jumbo squid stock assessment, helping produce recommendations for acoustic surveys, stock-structure analysis, improved understanding of squid life cycles, international collaboration, and assessment of high-seas fishing impacts.

The passage describes a continuation patent application titled “Physical Layer Preamble and Signaling for Wireless Communication,” addressing wireless preamble designs for current and future communication protocols, including IEEE 802.11be and later versions. It explains WLANs composed of access points and stations, including BSS operation, beacon broadcasts, scanning, association, roaming, ad hoc networks, and communication through PPDUs over bonded channels.

Existing preamble structures are reviewed, including legacy, VHT, and HE formats. Because legacy signal fields have limited capacity and become saturated as new protocol versions are introduced, the disclosure proposes a universal signal field (U-SIG) to identify the PPDU format, wireless protocol version, bandwidth, puncturing, and related properties. A U-SIG may contain version-independent fields, such as a version identifier, uplink/downlink indicator, BSS color, transmission-opportunity duration, and bandwidth or punctured-channel information, plus version-dependent fields that describe the U-SIG and subsequent EHT-SIG structures.

According to the disclosed method, a receiver obtains a packet containing a preamble and data portion, determines from the U-SIG the packet format and which subchannels contain version-specific signaling, and decodes an EHT-SIG on those subchannels. The EHT-SIG may be common across content channels or may carry different information in different subchannels. It can include resource-unit allocations, per-user MCS and scheduling data, spatial-stream configuration, overflow signaling from the U-SIG, and information needed to decode the data portion.

Separate formats are described for trigger-based, single-user, multi-user, and unified single-user/multi-user PPDUs. Trigger-based PPDUs may omit the EHT-SIG; single-user PPDUs may use a compact fixed-format EHT-SIG; multi-user PPDUs may use variable-length common and user-specific fields; and unified formats may support either traffic type under a consistent structure. Resource-allocation signaling may support OFDMA and MU-MIMO, including aggregated or non-contiguous allocations and tables intended to reduce signaling overhead.

The disclosure also addresses subchannel puncturing, content-channel structures, EHT-SIG compression, parallelized signaling, and support for channels up to 320 MHz and more than 16 spatial streams. Proposed bandwidth and puncturing indications use lookup values, bitmaps, separate fields, or patterns that vary by an 80 MHz portion. Additional U-SIG options provide 52 signaling bits across two symbols. Proposed EHT-SIG layouts address punctured and non-punctured channels, partial-bandwidth MU-MIMO, OFDMA resource assignments, and different compression modes.

Implementations may be provided as methods, processors, apparatus, systems, and computer-readable media. Example AP and STA implementations include wireless communication devices with modems, radios, processors, memory, antennas, and optional application processors, displays, sensors, and network interfaces. The drawings depict wireless networks, PPDU formats, channel bonding, OFDM and OFDMA, punctured transmissions, AP and STA architectures, EHT-SIG encoding and layouts, resource-allocation options, and compression tables.

Nintendo’s Labo includes Toy Con Garage, a basic workshop for building cardboard robots and accessories. The virtual mech launches April 20, while demonstrations featured a cardboard guitar and electronic tennis; access requirements remain unclear.

Darren Till won a controversial unanimous decision over Stephen Thompson at UFC Fight Night 130 in Liverpool, though many believed the bout could have gone either way. Till offered a U.S. rematch, saying he could be more aggressive and knock Thompson out.

The Justice Department referred the University of Nevada at Reno to the Education Department for an investigation of its UndocuPack program for undocumented students, citing reports that it assists "illegal immigrants" through referrals, aid, and academic and career support, including help finding jobs that don't require a Social Security number. The letter invoked the 1996 Personal Responsibility and Work Opportunity Reconciliation Act. UNR president Brian Sandoval, a former Republican governor, pushed back, saying the program serves all students regardless of citizenship status, uses no federal funds, and complies with federal and state law, and that the university would respond through legal channels. Advocates see the move as an escalation of the Trump administration's efforts to curb benefits for undocumented students, warning campuses might scale back or close lawful programs. The DOJ has sued five states over in-state tuition policies, and the Education Department has investigated five universities over scholarships and issued guidance on adult and technical education. Diego Sánchez said no court has interpreted PRWORA to bar such support offices, while Gaby Pacheco said institutions must choose whether to hide or stand together, noting that scaling back sends students a message they don't belong.

The passage describes systems, methods, and computer program products for processing mobile payments while a user device or merchant payment system is disconnected from a payment server. An e-wallet linked to one or more user devices may support an offline payment mode that permits payments without server connectivity, while still allowing online payments when connectivity is available. Only one device associated with a given e-wallet may have offline mode enabled at a time to prevent account overdrafts or excessive use of reserved funds.

A payment server may maintain e-wallet configurations, offline-mode statuses, and payment-account information, including reserved offline balances and vendor preferences. When enabling offline mode for a device, the server checks whether another device for the same e-wallet is enabled. It transfers the mode by disabling the other device when online; otherwise, it rejects the request. Users may also reserve an available amount for offline payments, which the server pre-authorizes.

For an offline transaction, the merchant system generates a payment request and communicates it to the user device over a local connection, such as Bluetooth, NFC, ZigBee, Z-Wave, LAN, USB, or scanned QR or bar codes. The device verifies that its remaining offline balance covers the amount, obtains user approval, subtracts the transaction amount, and sends an approval message to the merchant. The message can include the e-wallet ID, transaction amount, payment account, and transaction identifier. The merchant stores the message until connectivity is restored.

Both the user device and merchant system may submit the stored transaction information to the payment server when connectivity returns. The server checks transaction identifiers to prevent duplicate processing, debits the payer, updates the preauthorized offline amount, and credits the merchant.

When two associated devices are offline, they can transfer offline mode through local communications. The current device generates handover data identifying the e-wallet and remaining account balances, suspends its mode, and sends the data. The receiving device enters a suspended state and confirms receipt. The original device then disables its mode and reports that status, after which the receiving device enables offline mode. Implementations may operate in conventional or cloud-computing environments.

The High Post Split Offense uses a 2–3 high alignment built around high-post splits, down screens, back cuts, and post-ups. Its simplicity allows players to focus on execution, while creating scoring opportunities for all five players, limiting weak-side help, and producing strong offensive-rebounding opportunities. Entries can be adjusted to exploit individual strengths.

The offense progresses through four phases. First, one guard enters the high post and splits while the other cuts off a moving screen; the post can feed either guard, fake the split, back cut directly, or take both cutters to the same side. Second, wings set down screens for the guards. The post can pass to a guard, feed a screener rolling after a switch, or attack in isolation. Defensive counters include curling against chase-and-trail coverage, fading against early overplays, back cutting when defenders cheat over screens, rolling when defenders switch, and slipping the screen against show-and-recover defense.

Third, the high post establishes a triple-threat position and can drive, shoot, or pass. Because the post operates in the middle of the court without defensive help, the post is isolated one-on-one. Counteroptions against overplay include an overhead lob, wing feeds, post exchange, screen exchange, and player interchange. Fourth, the offense can exploit smaller defenders with strong post-ups when the defense focuses on shooters.

Variations include wing flop/back-cut entries, wing-pass entries, wing double-away actions, and post single/double screens. Success depends on spacing, execution, coordination, communication, timing, and defensive recognition. Players must box out, pursue second, third, and fourth efforts, and practice individual fundamentals. Coaches must recognize defensive adjustments, and players should understand how to defend the offense even if they do not use it.

This patent disclosure describes a tonneau cover for pickup truck beds and is a continuation of earlier “Tonneau Cover” applications, whose subject matter is incorporated by reference. The cover spans the bed between the side walls and tailgate to create a compartment for storing items out of view.

The cover includes a fixed base panel and multiple pivotally attached, movable panel sections. Each panel section has a latching assembly with pinch-latch mechanisms on opposite sides. Squeezing the latch and inner pinch handles together retracts spring-biased latches from clips on the bed rails. A longitudinal connector links the two mechanisms so operating one releases both latches from one side of the truck, while the springs return the latches to a locked position when released.

Additional disclosed features include pivoting vertical support gussets that hold folded panels upright, a channel bracket and buckle system that secures folded panels in horizontal or vertical positions, and integrated lights near the pinch handles. The hinge assemblies include resilient seals, seal spacers, and seal rods to permit folding and improve sealing. Adjustable side rails, brackets, clips, fasteners, and D-seals attach the cover to the truck bed and help limit water intrusion. The drawings illustrate the cover in closed, folded, and stowed configurations and depict the latch, hinge, gusset, buckle, and rail components and their operation.

BoE regulator Vicky Saporta said major capital and liquidity requirement changes are unlikely, as Basel III's finalization ends post-crisis bank reform. Future focus: new risks, unintended effects, cyber-attack resilience, and leverage rules deterring central clearing of OTC derivatives.

Aaron Judge injured his elbow in late July, missed 10 days and later returned to the outfield with reduced arm strength. His hitting remained strong. With the season over, Judge said the elbow would be evaluated but could not say whether surgery would be necessary.

Microsoft Corporation’s Form 10-K covers the fiscal year ended June 30, 2021. The company identifies itself as a technology company founded in 1975 that develops software, services, devices, cloud offerings, and online advertising. Its R&D priorities are to reinvent productivity and business processes, build intelligent cloud and edge platforms, and create more personal computing.

Key offerings include Microsoft 365, Teams, Viva, Dynamics 365, and the Power Platform; Azure and related hybrid-cloud services; AI and data tools; Windows 10 and the newly announced Windows 11; Edge; Surface devices; and Xbox, Game Pass, and cloud gaming. Microsoft entered into a definitive agreement to acquire Nuance Communications in April 2021 and completed the acquisition of ZeniMax Media in March 2021.

Microsoft reports three operating segments: Productivity and Business Processes, covering Office, LinkedIn, and Dynamics; Intelligent Cloud, covering Azure, server products, GitHub, and enterprise services; and More Personal Computing, covering Windows, devices, gaming, and search advertising. It competes across these markets with companies such as Apple, Google, Amazon, IBM, Oracle, Salesforce, SAP, VMware, Sony, and Nintendo, as well as numerous software, cloud, device, advertising, and open-source providers.

The report states that COVID-19 continued to affect Microsoft’s employees, customers, partners, communities, and operations, with future effects dependent on evolving factors. Microsoft’s sustainability commitments include becoming carbon negative by 2030, removing all carbon emitted since 1975 by 2050, investing $1 billion in climate technologies, becoming water positive by 2030, and achieving zero waste by 2030. Its racial-equity initiatives include increasing Black and African American representation and leadership, a five-year $50 million justice-reform effort, and expanded broadband, device, education, and nonprofit support. Its digital-skills initiatives have provided free training to more than 42 million people and included $20 million in nonprofit partnerships.

As of June 30, 2021, Microsoft employed approximately 181,000 people: 103,000 in the United States and 78,000 internationally. Its workforce priorities include inclusive culture, pay-equity monitoring, employee health and safety, extensive learning and development, and flexible or hybrid work.

Microsoft develops most products internally through groups focused on cloud and AI, experiences and devices, AI research, LinkedIn, and gaming. It reported more than 65,000 issued patents and over 21,000 pending patents. Products are distributed through OEMs, direct sales, distributors, resellers, digital marketplaces, and Microsoft Experience Centers, with cloud, subscription, perpetual-license, and Software Assurance options.

Executive officers listed include Chairman and CEO Satya Nadella, CFO Amy Hood, Chief Commercial Officer Judson Althoff, Chief Marketing Officer Christopher Capossela, Chief Legal Officer Bradford Smith, human-resources executive Kathleen Hogan, and business-development executive Christopher Young.

The report’s risk section emphasizes intense competition, platform and ecosystem competition, differing business models, and execution risks associated with cloud services and IoT adoption. These factors could adversely affect revenue, margins, operations, financial condition, cash flows, and Microsoft’s stock price.

This continuation application describes wafer-level semiconductor packaging methods for multi-die integrated fan-out (InFO) packages and multi-chip modules. It addresses coefficient-of-thermal-expansion mismatch among packaging materials, which can create stress, delamination, via popping, and electrical failures, particularly when copper and low-k dielectrics are used.

The disclosed process fabricates interconnect structures containing substrates, dielectric and metallization layers, through-substrate vias, redistribution layers, protective or passivation layers, and contact pads. The structures may be tested before assembly, allowing only known-good structures to be selected. Tested and singulated structures are bonded to a carrier with adhesive, encapsulated, and thinned to expose contacts and form a reconstructed wafer. Packaged semiconductor devices, including processor dies and memory cubes, are then positioned over individual, adjacent, or shared interconnect structures.

Device contacts may be aligned and bonded by direct Cu-to-Cu bonding at lower temperatures or by solder bonding using reflow. Underfill may be applied by capillary-underfill or moldable-underfill processes. The assembly is subsequently encapsulated, cured, and thinned. The carrier is removed using thermal or laser-assisted debonding after a handling wafer, ring, or tape provides support, and external contacts are formed for connection to devices such as printed circuit boards.

A disclosed embodiment uses a single large universal interconnect structure embedded in encapsulant. Multiple packaged devices share its contacts. Universal redistribution layers are formed over the reconstructed wafer by alternating patterned dielectric layers and conductive layers. A passivation layer, under-bump metallizations, and contact bumps are then added, allowing processor dies and memory cubes to be flip-chip bonded. The resulting structure is underfilled, encapsulated, thinned, debonded from the carrier, and provided with external contacts.

The claimed methods arrange and encapsulate interconnect structures, electrically couple semiconductor dies to them, remove the carrier, and bond external contacts. Other embodiments form redistribution layers over a universal interconnect structure and bond dies through those layers to the interconnect. Claimed package structures include semi-finished substrates in a first encapsulant, electrically connected semiconductor dies, a second encapsulant, optional redistribution layers, and external contacts that may directly connect to a printed circuit board.

The disclosed packages can exceed 70 mm by 70 mm for high-performance computing and AI applications requiring high data rates, bandwidth, and low latency. Component and board-level testing, lower-temperature bonding, and thermal-expansion coefficients selected to approximate those of printed circuit boards are described as reducing stress and improving component- and board-level reliability.

On Nov. 26, 2001, Enron shares fell as much as 20%, touched an all-time low of $3.76 and closed at $4.01, down about 92% for the year. Investors increasingly doubted Dynegy’s proposed acquisition, citing possible invocation of the deal’s “material adverse change” provisions. Dynegy’s board offered no public assessment, while management continued due diligence and sought regulatory approvals. Enron traded at less than one-third of its reported book value, reflecting concern that its earnings and balance-sheet figures were unreliable.

Enron sought between $500 million and $1 billion in additional financing and worked to restructure debt. Banks extended the deadline on a $690 million loan from Nov. 27 to Dec. 14 and were expected to negotiate a further postponement as other loans approached maturity. Enron had less than $2 billion in cash and credit lines, and a downgrade below investment grade could trigger $3.9 billion in debt repayments. Its bonds also fell to distressed levels amid concern that banks might gain priority at the expense of unsecured creditors.

Citigroup had used credit-default swaps and related trusts to transfer $2.384 billion of Enron exposure. If Enron defaulted, Citigroup would receive securities from the trusts in exchange for defaulted Enron obligations, while synthetic-note holders would not be direct Enron creditors.

Three lawsuits sought class-action status for employees who allegedly lost $850 million in Enron stock held through 401(k) plans. The suits alleged that Enron encouraged purchases at artificially inflated prices, sold stock without required prospectuses and temporarily prevented employees from selling shares.

Broader reports said Enron’s trading volumes and profitability were weakening, making its assets less valuable to Dynegy. Rating agencies also warned that combining Dynegy with Enron’s substantial debt could harm Dynegy’s credit standing, and Dynegy’s bonds declined. Petrobras and its pension fund were reportedly close to regulatory approval to buy Enron’s stakes in CEG and CEG Rio, while India’s AV Birla Group denied interest in Enron’s Dabhol Power stake. The energy-trading sector faced increased scrutiny of mark-to-market accounting and earnings quality, with many traders trading at roughly nine times earnings.

Martin Colin Hodder, 45, was jailed for 18 weeks and given a one-year restraining order after admitting two assault charges involving his ex-partner and her daughter. Prosecutors said he drank 1.5 bottles of vodka, retrieved a butter knife, threatened the women and slashed the ex-partner’s arms and the daughter’s wrist. The older victim called the sentence a disgrace; his lawyer said he had not been in trouble for six years.

Coach Julien said an injured player was still being evaluated and had been unable to finish the previous game, with no update expected yet. He praised a limited-experience player’s performance and decision to move him into “Bergy’s” spot despite a lack of chemistry. The team played better in the third period after being too passive earlier, and Julien said both teams needed their players to step up. Chicago must win the next game at home, but he expressed no panic and expected the team to bounce back.

Julien emphasized lineup depth, noting contributions from Shaw and Paille and saying teams cannot rely solely on a few stars. The first four games had been tight, close, and exciting, but he could not predict whether scoring or penalties would continue. He defended Zdeno Chara, calling him one of the league’s best defensemen, and said the criticism of him was unwarranted.

Campbell’s injury had prompted the team to evaluate Daugavins, Soderberg, and other players. Julien was considering switching between Daugavins and Soderberg because of their contrasting styles and was seeking the best fit. He described penalties, bad shifts, and strong periods as causes of momentum swings and said he manages the bench and utilizes players to generate offensive opportunities.

Both coaches were making adjustments and attempting to gain an edge through lineup and matchup changes. Julien said every player must contribute, with no passengers, and prioritized creating the next goal over perfect line matching.

Power futures were largely unchanged, with July reaching $28.75 at COB, $39.75 at PV, $38.25 at Cinergy, and $46.15 at PJM. Other coverage included a natural-gas storage open season at the Southern Pines Energy Center, preparations for future data-center power demand, MISO, PJM, and SPP’s planned unified wholesale electricity market, and gas-storage proposals from Progas. The financial summary reported declines in major stock indexes and March NYMEX crude oil, which fell to $20.88.

University of Michigan researchers developed a clear, durable “omniphobic” coating that repels nearly all known liquids and prevents grime buildup on tables, floors, walls, and phone screens. Inspired by easier cleanup around a child, it is undergoing toxicity testing.

The court granted Waste Away Group, Inc.’s motion for summary judgment on Paula Norrell’s Title VII claims. Norrell, a female employee, had risen from inside sales representative to district sales manager and applied for the newly combined Montgomery–Opelika district sales manager position. Waste Away selected male candidate Terry White, who had previously held that exact position and had greater outside-sales, organizational, leadership, and market experience.

Although Norrell established a prima facie failure-to-promote claim, Waste Away articulated a legitimate, nondiscriminatory reason: White was the most qualified candidate. The court found no genuine dispute that Norrell failed to show this reason was a pretext for gender discrimination. Her evidence concerning comments by supervisors and Johnson, including a request that she train White, consisted of stray or isolated remarks unrelated to the promotion decision; Malphrus was not a decisionmaker, and Johnson and Mitchell independently interviewed and evaluated the candidates. Norrell also was not substantially more qualified than White. Norrell abandoned her disparate-impact claim after discovery. Final judgment was entered for Waste Away, with costs taxed against Norrell.

The Triangle Post is a structured basketball offense created, developed, and refined by Tex Winter. Rather than relying on fixed plays, it uses defensive recognition, sound principles, precise spacing, player movement, and fundamental execution. It comprises three elements: an entry, a sideline triangle, and a weakside two-person game. Every player must understand the options from each position and be proficient in fundamentals and footwork.

Players are spaced 15 to 20 feet apart to spread the defense, discourage help and double-teams, create accurate passing lanes, and open the basket for post play, drives, cuts, and slices. The triangle can form quickly on either side, forcing the defense to cover the full court. Because offensive choices depend on defensive deployment, any pass or dribble can initiate the system, and numerous entries are available, including cuts, dribble clears, post pops, screens, reversals, and dribble weaves.

Once established, the sideline triangle creates post-up, post-split, post-isolation, screen-and-roll, and solo-cut opportunities. The weakside two-person game can begin with a pass or dribble entry and includes drives, jumpers, rolls, fakes, cuts, and lob passes. Counters are based on defensive reads: trailing defenders allow hand-off drives, defenders going behind screens allow pull-up jumpers, switches create post or wing isolation, and aggressive shows invite fake screens or opposite drives.

Defensive overplays also create automatic counters. Fronting the post can lead to an overhead pass, high-post feed, or ball reversal; sagging off can lead to dribble penetration, a drop pass, or a kick-out; doubling the post can produce open shooters or a weakside two-on-one; and denying reversal or backdoor passes can lead to backdoor cuts, lobs, or drop passes.

Installing the offense requires learning every component before full-team use. The recommended progression includes two-player entries, weakside two-game shooting, 3-on-3 sideline triangles, 4-on-4 shell work, 5-on-5 scrimmages, and game situations, alongside individual skill development. Coaches should scout opponents, anticipate their reads, monitor defensive adjustments, and vary entries to prevent predictable defense. The passage also emphasizes learning how to defend the Triangle Post because it is among the game’s most-used offenses.

Bollinger Bands, developed by John Bollinger in the 1980s, analyze asset volatility and potential trend changes using a moving average with standard deviations plotted above and below it. They can help identify movement relative to the average, possible reversals, and trend continuation, but require defined trading rules, parameter testing, and backtesting.

Disadvantages include false signals, reduced effectiveness in low-volatility range-bound markets, delays caused by reliance on historical data, and sensitivity to time-frame and settings. Default settings use a 20-period moving average, while the period, standard deviations, multiplier, and source can be adjusted.

TradingView supports Bollinger Bands and their construction in Pine Script. A breakout strategy seeks to capitalize on band breaches. An H4 test using full capital per trade reportedly produced considerable returns despite uncomfortable drawdown, but further research and optimization are needed. Bollinger Bands can support breakout, mean-reversion, or squeeze strategies as a primary or secondary component.

The speaker accepts the presidential oath as a sacred trust and pledges to promote the welfare of all citizens, placing national interests above party, sectional, and private concerns. He urges renewed devotion to the Constitution, administered in a spirit of amity and mutual concession, with respect for the powers reserved to states and the people. Every voter shares responsibility for public government and should closely scrutinize public officials.

Government officials should limit expenditures, practice economy, and recognize merit and competency rather than partisan service. The nation’s finances should ensure business confidence, steady wages, reduced unnecessary taxation, and avoid surplus Treasury funds that encourage waste. The public domain must be protected, Native Americans treated fairly with education and advancement toward citizenship, polygamy in the territories suppressed, and immigration laws against servile labor enforced. The TPS7H500x-SP family comprises four radiation-hardness-assured, peak-current-mode PWM controllers for space-grade DC-DC converters: TPS7H5001-SP, TPS7H5002-SP, TPS7H5003-SP, and TPS7H5004-SP. They operate from 4 V to 14 V, support switching frequencies from 100 kHz to 2 MHz, and use a 0.613 V internal reference with +0.7%/−1% accuracy. The TPS7H5001-SP is a dual-output device optimized for silicon and GaN converters with programmable dead time, synchronous-rectifier controls, and configurable maximum duty cycle. The TPS7H5002-SP is a single-output device for buck and isolated topologies with programmable dead time and leading-edge blank time. The TPS7H5003-SP is similar but has fixed 50 ns dead time and blank time. The TPS7H5004-SP is a dual-output device for non-synchronous push-pull and full-bridge converters, with configurable blank time and a fixed 50% maximum duty cycle.

Startup requires UVLO, reference, enable, fault, and thermal conditions to be satisfied before soft start begins. VIN requires at least 0.1 µF of bypass capacitance, while the internal 5 V VLDO regulator requires 1 µF. Enable can be tied to VLDO, driven externally, or programmed through a resistor divider for adjustable UVLO. The internal 1.23 V bandgap reference is divided to 0.613 V and requires a 470 nF REFCAP capacitor. Output voltage is programmed with a VSENSE resistor divider, and a soft-start capacitor controls the gradual rise of the output; synchronous-rectifier outputs activate after the SS voltage exceeds 1 V.

Switching frequency can be set with an RT resistor, synchronized to an external clock, or coordinated between two controllers in primary-secondary mode. An external clock must be twice the desired switching frequency and range from 200 kHz to 4 MHz with a 40%–60% duty cycle. Primary outputs have approximately 150 mA peak capability, so external gate drivers are recommended. Pulse skipping is used at high frequencies to maintain output voltage when the required duty cycle falls below the minimum on-time.

Duty-cycle limits are configured through DCL. The TPS7H5002-SP and TPS7H5003-SP support 75% or 100%; the TPS7H5004-SP requires a 50% limit. OUTB and, where supported, SRB are active only with the 50% limit. Dead time is programmable on the TPS7H5001-SP and TPS7H5002-SP and fixed at 50 ns on the TPS7H5003-SP. Leading-edge blank time is programmable except on the TPS7H5003-SP.

Peak-current control compares sensed current with a stepped-down COMP voltage. CS_ILIM also provides overcurrent protection: crossing 1.05 V initiates cycle-by-cycle limiting, followed by hiccup delay and restart sequencing controlled by the HICC capacitor. The FAULT pin can trigger shutdown for external protection logic when its voltage exceeds 0.6 V for the specified pulse width; restart follows a frequency-dependent delay after the fault clears. Programmable slope compensation mitigates subharmonic oscillation, with 1 times the inductor falling-current slope recommended. Type 2A or Type 2B frequency compensation can be used. Thermal shutdown stops switching above 175°C and permits reinitialization below 160°C.

A documented example uses the TPS7H5001-SP in a 500 kHz synchronous GaN push-pull converter with a 5 V output. It selects a 205 kΩ RT resistor, 10 kΩ/1.4 kΩ feedback divider, 20.5 kΩ dead-time resistors, 49.9 kΩ blank-time resistor, 33 nF soft-start capacitor, 2.5 transformer turns ratio, 40 µH primary inductance, 0.47 µH output inductor, at least 1.3 mF output capacitance, and 7.5 Ω current-sense resistor. Type 2A compensation uses 40.2 kΩ, 15 nF, and 47 pF components, while the slope-compensation resistor is 102 kΩ.

Layout guidance emphasizes separating feedback and control traces from switching nodes and power magnetics, minimizing high-di/dt and high-dv/dt loops, connecting analog and power grounds at one point, using short and wide high-current traces, placing bypass and compensation components close to the controller, and filtering the CS_ILIM signal when necessary.

Jane Goodall’s collection of Gombe chimpanzee skeletons, paired with records of each animal’s sex, age, weight and life history, enabled researchers to study how individual development affects skeletal anatomy and offered new perspectives on hominid evolution. Goodall said field researchers should “not waste anything.” Her collection showed that bone size does not reliably indicate body weight and revealed unusual patterns of bone loss and strength associated with aging and childbirth.

The second week of motherhood was especially difficult for the author. As hospital support and pain medication wore off, sleep deprivation, painful breastfeeding, loneliness, and emotional rawness intensified. Her babies gained little weight or, in one case, reacted to proteins in her breast milk, making her feel like a failure. She struggled to understand and soothe crying, fought with her husband, and felt exhausted and reduced to a pacifier when her baby would not sleep. These difficulties harmed her mental health, confidence, and marriage, but eventually improved, and she came to love the fourth trimester.

On June 15, 2017, Amazon.com, Inc. entered into a merger agreement to acquire Whole Foods Market, Inc. through Walnut Merger Sub, Inc. Whole Foods would survive as the subsidiary, and its eligible outstanding shares would be converted into the right to receive $42 per share in cash. Closing required shareholder approval, regulatory clearances, and other customary conditions, and was not conditioned on Amazon obtaining financing. Either party could terminate if the merger had not closed by February 15, 2018, subject to a possible 90-day extension. Whole Foods would owe a $400 million termination fee in specified circumstances, including after a board recommendation change or acceptance of a superior proposal. Amazon expected to finance the transaction with debt and cash on hand and obtained commitments for a bridge facility of up to $13.7 billion. Amazon and Whole Foods jointly announced the agreement on June 16, 2017.

William J. O’Neil developed the follow-through day as a market-timing signal for identifying a shift from a correction or bear market to a new uptrend. It uses only price and volume data from major indexes such as the Dow, Nasdaq, and S&P 500.

A higher-closing session begins a rally attempt. On Days 2 and 3, the index may close higher or lower but must not fall below Day 1’s low. A rally attempt fails if any rally day falls below the previous rally day’s low, requiring the process to restart. From Day 4 onward, a follow-through day occurs when a major index closes significantly higher than the previous day on greater volume. The best window is generally Days 4–7, although later signals can work.

The signal indicates that selling may have ended and a new uptrend has begun, but it does not guarantee the absolute market bottom or justify immediate full investment. Investors should also examine leading stocks and market sentiment. A fall below the original Day 1 low constitutes complete failure and a sell signal. The passage states that no bull market since the early 1900s began without a follow-through day.

An S&P 500 backtest using SPY found weak short-term index results because markets tend to mean-revert and the strategy buys strength rather than weakness. Results improved slightly when the 25-day RSI was below 55, and results for individual stocks may differ. The stated backtest rules require Day 1 to close higher, Days 2 and 3 to avoid lower lows, and Day 4 to gain at least 0.75 of the 25-day average high-low range, with a purchase at the close when conditions are met.

The double top is a bearish reversal pattern consisting of two swing highs at roughly the same level, separated by a swing low. It appears after an uptrend or prolonged pullback in a downtrend and signals a possible downward price reversal. The highs form resistance, while a neckline connecting the two swing lows acts as support. A break below the neckline, preferably with significant volume, confirms a potential short entry; long-term investors may use the pattern as a warning to close long positions.

Suggested rules require an existing uptrend, swing highs within 3% of each other, and a volume-supported neckline break. Profit targets are projected from the pattern’s height down from the neckline. Stops may be placed mid-pattern or above it.

Research cited from Thomas Bulkowski’s study of 500 stocks over five years found that only 39% of double tops reached their targets, compared with 68% for double bottoms. Because patterns were manually identified and shorting is difficult, the authors consider the strategy challenging and dependent on human judgment.

On October 29, 2001, Enron’s shares fell roughly 60% over two weeks to near seven-year lows after the energy company reported its first quarterly loss in more than four years, including a $1.01 billion charge, and disclosed a $1.2 billion reduction in shareholder equity. Investor concerns centered on previously undisclosed off-balance-sheet partnerships managed by former CFO Andrew Fastow. Following an SEC inquiry, Fastow stepped down; CEO Jeffrey Skilling had also resigned and Chairman Ken Lay had resumed the CEO position.

Moody’s cut Enron’s senior unsecured long-term debt rating from Baa1 to Baa2, placed its commercial-paper rating and long-term obligations under review for downgrade, and said write-downs reduced business valuations, increased leverage above 50%, and weakened earnings. Standard & Poor’s maintained a BBB-plus rating with a negative outlook, while Fitch placed the debt on negative watch.

Enron drew about $3 billion from bank credit lines, used approximately $2 billion to repay commercial paper, and sought another $1 billion to $2 billion to restore liquidity and confidence. Analysts and lenders anticipated higher borrowing costs, collateral requirements, and other restrictive terms. Enron’s 6.4% bonds due in 2006 fell from near par value to roughly 80–83 cents per dollar, with yields reported at 12.1%.

Most major U.S. wholesale gas and electricity traders said business with Enron remained at normal levels, though they monitored its credit exposure closely. In Europe, some large energy groups halted or restricted trading and discussed letters of credit; British traders reported no clear effect on market liquidity. Analysts warned that further credit deterioration could reduce Enron’s access to financing and hinder its trading operations.

In the broader credit market, Moody’s and Standard & Poor’s reported worsening corporate credit conditions, a U.S. recession, and more than $100 billion in expected corporate defaults in 2001. The Sept. 11 attacks, weak financing conditions, debt-financed mergers, and buybacks were cited as contributing factors.

Commentary also included an unconfirmed report that Royal Dutch/Shell might consider acquiring Enron; favorable insider buying in other independent power producers Calpine, AES, Mirant, and NRG, contrasted with continued insider selling in Enron; concern that Enron’s decline could undermine broader market confidence; and a defense of Enron’s past contributions to Houston and the electricity market.

Retired Metro Police homicide detective Phil Ramos said the body-camera footage captured officers’ anxiety outside Stephen Paddock’s hotel room. He did not fault the first officer for not activating his camera, called the accidental discharge understandable, and said no firm conclusions could be drawn from the partial, possibly un-timestamped video.

An extreme heat wave was expected to shift west after July 4, bringing dangerous temperatures to Southern California. New York’s heat index reached 106°F, New England had record temperatures, and at least one heat-related death was reported. The NWS urged outdoor visitors to seek shade and drink fluids. A storm was expected to cool the East Coast this weekend.

Education policy has become increasingly polarized by the COVID-19 pandemic, pandemic learning loss, racial reckoning, social media activism, and growing distrust of schools and educators. Partisan divisions have intensified scrutiny of curricula, instruction, and extracurricular activities, potentially distracting from student outcomes and community trust. Despite federal gridlock, however, states are pursuing substantive reforms with support across political lines.

The paper argues that “cross-partisan” support—public backing across differing political philosophies or tangible policy achievement—can produce meaningful education reform. Analysis of state initiatives and discussions with education leaders identifies five common factors: policies and solutions must be easy to communicate and broadly appealing; responsive to local contexts and supported by credible local champions; provided with political cover; structured so both sides can claim victories; and advanced through strategic media use.

Examples include science-based reading policies following the *Sold a Story* podcast, teacher apprenticeship programs and other responses to staffing shortages, interstate teacher licensure reciprocity, locally tailored career and technical education, Virginia’s revised history standards, teacher pay increases, and expanded civics requirements.

Additional recommendations include understanding the political landscape, setting realistic expectations, establishing a shared definition of the problem, assessing urgency and effects on frontline staff, framing proposals as expanding rather than narrowing opportunities, avoiding mission creep, prioritizing objectives, and understanding opponents’ values. Despite significant barriers, the paper concludes that cross-partisan collaboration can advance education policy in ways that serve students, families, and communities.

Microsoft Corporation reported unaudited financial results for the quarter ended September 30, 2021, the first quarter of fiscal 2022. Revenue increased 22% to $45.3 billion, including $16.6 billion from products and $28.7 billion from services and other revenue. Gross margin rose 21% to $31.7 billion, operating income increased 27% to $20.2 billion, and net income increased 48% to $20.5 billion. Diluted earnings per share were $2.71, compared with $1.82. A $3.3 billion tax benefit from transferring intangible properties from a Puerto Rico subsidiary to the United States reduced the effective tax rate to zero. Excluding that benefit, adjusted net income was $17.2 billion and adjusted diluted earnings per share were $2.27.

Microsoft Cloud revenue increased 36% to $20.7 billion. Azure and other cloud services grew 50%, Office 365 Commercial revenue grew 23%, Dynamics 365 revenue grew 48%, and LinkedIn revenue grew 42%, including 61% growth in Marketing Solutions. Microsoft 365 Consumer subscribers increased 19% to 54.1 million. Windows OEM revenue grew 10%, search and news advertising revenue excluding traffic acquisition costs grew 40%, and Surface revenue declined 17%.

Revenue by segment was $15.0 billion for Productivity and Business Processes, $17.0 billion for Intelligent Cloud, and $13.3 billion for More Personal Computing, representing growth of 22%, 31%, and 12%, respectively. Segment operating income grew 33% for Productivity and Business Processes, 39% for Intelligent Cloud, and 7% for More Personal Computing.

At September 30, 2021, Microsoft held $19.2 billion in cash and cash equivalents and $111.5 billion in short-term investments. Total assets were $335.4 billion, total liabilities were $183.4 billion, and stockholders’ equity was $152.0 billion. Operating cash flow was $24.5 billion. Financing activities used $16.3 billion, including $7.7 billion for share repurchases and $4.2 billion for dividends; investing activities used $3.3 billion, including $5.8 billion for property and equipment additions.

Microsoft completed the $8.1 billion acquisition of ZeniMax Media on March 9, 2021. It also entered an agreement on April 11, 2021 to acquire Nuance Communications for $19.7 billion, including net debt, subject to regulatory approvals and other closing conditions. The Board authorized a new $60 billion share repurchase program, and a quarterly dividend of $0.62 per share was declared.

The company remained under IRS audit for tax years 2004 through 2017, primarily concerning transfer pricing. Microsoft also disclosed a Chinese antitrust investigation, cell-phone-related litigation, and other claims, with $333 million in accrued legal liabilities and approximately $500 million in additional reasonably possible aggregate losses.

This systematic review and meta-analysis assessed Chikungunya seroprevalence in Ethiopia following its first documented detection in 2016. Following PRISMA guidelines, 40 records from major databases and Ethiopian repositories were screened, yielding five eligible English-language observational studies published from 2016 through November 2023. Four studies were cross-sectional and one was case-control; four used ELISA and one used RT-qPCR.

Pooled seroprevalence was 12.35%. The highest regional estimate was 43.6% in SNNPR, and the highest district estimate was 51.58% in Debub Ari. The lowest estimates were recorded in Dire Dawa, approximately 12%, and Lare district, 6.25%. Random-effects analysis showed substantial heterogeneity across districts (I²=97.72%) and an overall logit effect size of -1.25 (95% CI -1.87 to -0.63). ELISA studies had significant heterogeneity, whereas RT-qPCR studies showed none. Begg’s and Egger’s tests did not indicate significant small-study or publication bias.

Prevalence varied by occupation, education, age, sex, and location. Farmers generally had higher prevalence, people with formal education had higher rates than those without, and adults often had higher prevalence than children. Findings by sex were inconsistent across studies.

The review’s limitations included the small number of studies, predominance of cross-sectional designs, possible underrepresentation of current prevalence, and insufficient molecular surveillance to determine circulating viral strains. The authors recommended operational readiness, collaboration, public awareness, and prevention strategies tailored to geography and testing methods.
