Their leading first-round targets are edge rusher Bradley Chubb, interior lineman Quenton Nelson, and running back Saquon Barkley. Chubb and Nelson could help protect Andrew Luck, while Barkley would upgrade the offense and relieve pressure on Luck and Jacoby Brissett.

Supplemental code, exercises, and other resources are available at the book’s GitHub repository. Example code may generally be reused without permission, although redistributing substantial portions in product documentation or selling example collections requires permission. Attribution is appreciated but optional. The book also provides publisher contact details, a web page for errata and examples, and information about O’Reilly’s Safari training platform.

Modern applications’ availability, reliability, agility, and rapid-scaling requirements often require distributed systems composed of multiple applications or replicas communicating across machines. Although properly designed distributed systems improve reliability and enable scalable team structures, they are substantially harder to design, build, and debug than single-machine applications. Containers, container images, and orchestrators have made reusable distributed-system patterns and components more accessible, much as earlier advances in algorithms and object-oriented programming established shared development practices.

Patterns are technology-independent blueprints that provide general design guidance rather than prescribing specific products or application stacks. Their value includes allowing developers to learn from others’ mistakes, establishing a shared vocabulary for discussing systems, and identifying components that can be implemented once and reused across applications. Historical precedents include Knuth’s reusable algorithms, interface-based object-oriented design patterns, and open-source communities that collaboratively develop and distribute software.

The book first examines single-node patterns in which tightly coupled containers are co-scheduled on one machine and may share filesystems, networking, process namespaces, or memory. Containers can establish boundaries for resource requirements, team ownership, and separation of concerns. Splitting an application into multiple containers can isolate resource priorities, support focused teams and reusable modules, simplify testing and deployment, and enable independent, smaller-scope rollouts.

The sidecar pattern pairs an application container containing core logic with a sidecar that augments it. Examples include an nginx sidecar that adds HTTPS termination and proxies requests to a legacy HTTP service on localhost; a configuration-management sidecar that synchronizes API-based configuration to a shared filesystem and signals the application to reload; a topz sidecar that shares the process namespace and exposes consistent resource-usage information; and a Git synchronization sidecar that updates a Node.js application, creating a simple platform as a service. Reusable sidecars should be parameterized—preferably through environment variables—define stable APIs for all interactions, and be documented through Dockerfile directives such as EXPOSE, ENV, and LABEL.

The ambassador pattern places an ambassador container between an application and external systems. It can route requests to appropriate shards in a sharded storage service, perform service discovery and broker connections to environment-specific services, or split production and experimental traffic. Examples include a client-side Redis sharding proxy configured with twemproxy and an nginx ambassador that uses IP hashing to send 90% of traffic to production and 10% to an experiment while keeping each user’s assignment consistent. The pattern separates concerns, permits reuse across applications, and can improve implementation consistency and quality.

The adapter pattern modifies or normalizes an application’s interface so it conforms to a predefined common interface. Monitoring adapters can expose metrics in Prometheus-compatible form; logging adapters can redirect logs to standard output and normalize formats through tools such as Fluentd; and health-check adapters can run richer diagnostic queries against databases such as MySQL without modifying the original database image. Adapters avoid maintaining modified third-party images, isolate resource usage, support independent updates, and allow common solutions to be reused across applications.

Multi-node distributed systems are more loosely coupled than single-node container groups and coordinate through network calls, parallelism, and loose synchronization. Microservices divide an application into focused components that communicate through defined APIs, enabling smaller teams, independent release schedules, and component-specific scaling. Their disadvantages include harder debugging and more complex design and coordination, which distributed patterns are intended to address.

A replicated load-balanced service consists of identical servers behind a load balancer and is commonly used for stateless services. Replication provides redundancy, fault tolerance, and horizontal scaling; at least two replicas are presented as necessary for high availability. Readiness probes indicate when initializing instances can accept requests. Session-tracked variants route a user’s requests consistently to one replica through IP-based hashing, cookies, or application-level mechanisms; consistent hashing minimizes user remapping when replica counts change.

Stateless serving can add a separate replicated caching tier. A small number of relatively large cache replicas may preserve more cached content and provide better hit rates than scaling a cache beside every application instance. Because cached traffic obscures client addresses, session tracking at this layer should use cookies or HTTP headers. Caching proxies can also enforce rate limits, return HTTP 429 responses, and report remaining request allowances. SSL termination can be provided by a separate replicated nginx tier, producing a complete flow of nginx for HTTPS termination, Varnish for caching and rate limiting, and the application tier behind it.

Sharded services differ from replicated services because each shard handles only a subset of requests, while a routing root directs traffic to the appropriate shard. Sharding is generally used for stateful data too large for one machine and allows scaling according to state size. The excerpt introduces these concepts through the design of a sharded cache and notes that client-side ambassadors can distribute requests to the sharded service.

The Piotroski F-Score, developed by Stanford finance professor Joseph Piotroski, is a stock-selection method that evaluates financial health across nine binary criteria covering profitability, liquidity, and efficiency. Scores of 8–9 indicate strong fundamentals, while scores of 0–4 suggest weak finances. Investors can use the score to identify potentially undervalued value stocks and growth stocks, conduct further research, diversify a portfolio, and rebalance investments. The strategy also involves analyzing financial ratios, assessing risk and return, and backtesting results using historical data.

Reported backtests indicate that the F-Score may outperform broad-market benchmarks. Alpha Architect tested large NYSE stocks from 1974 through December 2014, finding annual returns of 13.3% for its modified score and 12.6% for the original Piotroski score, versus 11.2% for the S&P 500, with similar standard deviations. Among the cheapest 20% of stocks with Piotroski scores above 6, annual returns were 15.9% for Alpha Architect’s method and 15.2% for the original score, compared with 11.2% for the S&P 500. ValueSignals tested the score on European stocks from 1999 to 2011, while Alexander Eriksen studied Piotroski, contrarian, and combined strategies on Norwegian and Swedish stocks from 1997 through 2011.

The F-Score is not a guarantee of success and should be used alongside other research and analysis.

During Supreme Court oral argument, several justices indicated that trial courts may restrict defense counsel’s overnight discussions with a client who is testifying, barring direct discussion of the testimony while allowing collateral trial-strategy matters. The case arose after David Villarreal’s trial judge prohibited his lawyer from discussing his testimony overnight; Texas courts upheld his murder conviction, and Villarreal argued that the order denied effective assistance of counsel.

Villarreal’s lawyer, Stuart Banner, warned that an unclear boundary would chill necessary legal advice and inhibit witness preparation. Justices Kagan and Gorsuch suggested courts may prohibit coaching or preparation of specific testimony while permitting advice tied to broader strategy. Texas defended a distinction between impermissible “management” of testimony and permissible discussions that only indirectly concern it. The U.S. instead proposed a bright-line rule barring any discussion of the client’s testimony. The justices debated whether advice on presentation issues such as eye contact and mumbling was impermissible. No holding was reported.

Splitting an application into multiple containers on one machine can provide resource isolation, clarify team ownership, and enforce separation of concerns. Separating priority workloads allows each container to have distinct resource requirements and prevents background services from degrading user-facing services. Small, focused containers can also be owned by small teams, reused across environments, tested and deployed independently, and rolled out or rolled back with fewer dependencies.

Single-node patterns tightly couple containers on the same machine, often sharing filesystems, network namespaces, and other resources. In Kubernetes, such a group is called a pod. The sidecar pattern pairs an application container with a sidecar that augments it without changing its core logic. Examples include adding HTTPS termination to a legacy HTTP service, synchronizing configuration from an API, exposing process-resource information through a shared PID namespace, and building a simple PaaS in which a Git-synchronization sidecar triggers application reloads. Reusable sidecars should be parameterized, expose stable and carefully maintained APIs, and be documented through Dockerfile comments, environment-variable defaults, and metadata labels.

The ambassador pattern places a container between an application and the outside world to broker communications. An ambassador can route requests to storage shards while presenting a local endpoint to the application, discover environment-specific services, or split traffic between production and experimental implementations. Client-side ambassadors simplify deployment of sharded services but require deployment alongside each application pod; shared routing services centralize that responsibility but add a network hop and must be scaled independently.

The adapter pattern modifies an application’s interface to conform to a common standard. Monitoring adapters translate incompatible metrics interfaces, such as Redis metrics, into Prometheus format. Logging adapters redirect or transform heterogeneous logs into consistent streams for aggregation. Health-check adapters run richer diagnostic queries without modifying vendor-supplied database containers. These adapters promote reuse, independent updates, and resource isolation while avoiding the cost of maintaining patched application images.

Multi-node patterns are more loosely coupled and communicate through network calls. Microservices divide an application into small services with formal API contracts, enabling focused teams, independent release schedules, and independent scaling. Their disadvantages include greater debugging and architectural complexity, which distributed patterns can mitigate by providing reusable designs and shared operational lessons.

Replicated load-balanced services use identical, stateless replicas behind a load balancer for redundancy and horizontal scaling. At least two replicas support failover and availability, while readiness probes distinguish running containers from those initialized and able to receive requests. Session-tracked variants route each user consistently to one replica, using IP hashing where appropriate or application-level mechanisms such as cookies when clients are behind NAT. Consistent hashing can minimize user remapping when replica counts change.

Caching can be deployed as a separate replicated tier rather than as a sidecar, allowing a few large cache replicas to serve many smaller application replicas and improve hit rates. HTTP proxies can also provide rate limiting, return 429 responses when limits are exceeded, and report remaining quota. A replicated nginx tier can terminate TLS with separate edge and internal certificates before forwarding traffic through a cache to the application.

Sharded services divide state among shards, with a routing node directing each request to the appropriate shard. Sharding increases usable capacity when data is too large for one machine and avoids duplicating cached entries across replicas. It also creates failure and rollout concerns: losing a shard causes misses and slower recomputation for its requests, so cache performance should be tested with and without caching. Replicating each shard improves availability and permits overprovisioned rollouts and independent shard scaling. Sharding functions should be deterministic and uniformly distributed, commonly using `hash(request) % shard_count`. Keys must distinguish requests only when their responses differ, such as combining country and request path for localized content. Consistent hashing limits redistribution during resharding compared with modulo-based routing.

The examples implement these patterns in Kubernetes using components such as Deployments, Services, StatefulSets, ConfigMaps, Secrets, nginx, twemproxy, Prometheus exporters, Fluentd plugins, Varnish, Redis, and Memcached.

The lecture surveys predecessor lower bounds, building on Van Emde Boas tries and fusion tries, and presents Sen’s communication-complexity proof of an almost matching bound. The easier colored predecessor problem reports only whether a predecessor is red or blue; it captures static randomized structures that succeed with probability greater than one-half.

The proof models a query algorithm and static data structure as communicating parties, with each memory read corresponding to a communication round. Round elimination repeatedly removes an effectively useless initial message while increasing error only slightly. Eliminating Alice-to-Bob messages resembles Van Emde Boas tries, while eliminating Bob-to-Alice messages resembles fusion trees.

For any colored-predecessor data structure with space \(s\), word size \(w\), and query-address length \(a=\log s\), the bound is \(\Omega(\min\{\log_a w,\log_w n\})\). With polynomial space, this becomes \(\Omega(\min\{\log w/\log\log n,\log_w n\})\), matching known upper bounds up to a \(\log\log\) factor and implying earlier pure-\(w\) and pure-\(n\) lower bounds. The lecture also surveys later Patrascu–Thorup results giving a tight tradeoff among \(n\), \(w\), and space, including static improvements and a statement that Van Emde Boas and fusion tries are optimal in different parameter regimes.

The passage introduces NVIDIA’s GA10x Ampere GPU architecture, focusing on the GA102 and GA104. GA102 powers the GeForce RTX 3090, RTX 3080, RTX 3070, RTX A6000, and A40, while GA104 powers the RTX 3070. Compared with Turing, Ampere is described as up to 1.7 times faster in raster graphics and twice as fast in ray tracing, with the RTX 3080 offering up to twice the RTX 2080’s performance and the RTX 3070 rivaling the RTX 2080 Ti.

GA102 contains 10,752 CUDA Cores, 84 second-generation RT Cores, and 336 third-generation Tensor Cores. Its SMs provide dual-datapath FP32 processing, doubling FP32 throughput over Turing, along with larger L1/shared-memory capacity and doubled shared-memory bandwidth. Second-generation RT Cores double ray/triangle intersection throughput and enable concurrent ray-tracing and graphics or compute workloads. Third-generation Tensor Cores support structured sparsity, doubling Tensor Core throughput, and TF32 precision, which provides up to fivefold training throughput.

The architecture also supports GDDR6X on GeForce GPUs and 48 GB GDDR6 on the RTX A6000 and A40, third-generation NVLink for 112.5 GB/s bidirectional interconnect between two GPUs, and PCIe Gen 4 with up to 64 GB/s peak bandwidth. GA102 is fabricated on Samsung’s 8nm 8N process and contains 28.3 billion transistors.

The RTX 3090 targets 8K HDR gaming with 10,496 CUDA Cores, 24 GB of GDDR6X, and DLSS 8K mode. The RTX A6000 combines the GPU’s full core configuration with 48 GB GDDR6 for rendering, AI, graphics, and compute, while the A40 targets data-center visual computing, virtual workstations, and server workloads. The architecture also reorganizes ROPs into graphics processing clusters, increasing raster-operation throughput, and is described as up to 1.9 times more power-efficient than Turing at equivalent performance.

This study compared immune responses to second doses of Pfizer BNT162b2 or Moderna mRNA-1273 vaccines in 27 people with rheumatoid arthritis treated with methotrexate (MTX), abatacept, or rituximab and 13 healthy controls. Serum antibodies, pseudovirus neutralization, and SARS-CoV-2-specific T- and B-cell responses were analyzed.

Rituximab-treated participants had almost no detectable spike-specific antibodies because of B-cell depletion, along with reduced vaccine-induced CD4+ T-cell responses. Abatacept-treated participants had significantly lower spike-specific and neutralizing antibody levels than controls. Although their numbers of receptor-binding-domain-specific B cells were similar to controls, abatacept reduced B-cell activation, IgG class switching, and memory-cell differentiation.

MTX treatment significantly reduced the magnitude of spike-specific CD4+ T-cell activation but did not significantly reduce serum antibody levels, neutralization activity, or B-cell numbers, phenotype, or class switching. Both MTX and abatacept reduced co-expression of IL-2, IFNγ, and IL-21 by vaccine-specific T cells. Abatacept also significantly reduced production of IL-2, IFNγ, and IL-21 individually. IL-21 and IFNγ expression correlated with antibody levels in the treated groups, indicating impaired T-cell–B-cell collaboration.

Age and sampling time did not explain the reduced antibody responses associated with abatacept. Overall, the findings associate abatacept treatment with disrupted T-cell help, B-cell differentiation, and humoral immunity, supporting temporary discontinuation when clinically manageable to improve vaccine responses.

Indonesia’s sovereign wealth fund Danantara plans to launch at least eight waste-to-power projects by the end of October, starting with four or five sites in Jakarta before expanding across Java and Bali to 33 municipalities. Each plant is designed to process 1,000 tonnes of waste daily and generate about 15 megawatts of electricity, at a cost of 2–3 trillion rupiah. Danantara will finance and oversee the projects, while PLN will purchase their electricity for the national grid. The initiative targets Indonesia’s 2025–2034 goal of 453 MW in waste-to-energy capacity and seeks to reduce landfill reliance, pollution, and emissions. Its success depends on coordination with local authorities, strong project oversight, and reliable waste conversion.

MTN and four banks—Access Bank, Agricultural Development Bank, Republic Bank and Societe Generale—plan to raise a combined GH¢4.67 billion on the Ghana Stock Exchange between April and September via four rights issues, one IPO and a bond programme, the largest concurrent capital raise in the bourse's nearly three-decade history. MTN is offloading 35% of the firm for GH¢3.48 billion; the banks seek GH¢1.19 billion to meet the Bank of Ghana's requirement to recapitalise to GH¢400 million by December 2018. Foreign inflows could steady the cedi, while dividend repatriation could deepen depreciation. Former GSE Council chairman Dr Sam Mensah says market absorption capacity is limited and the timing is "high risk", urging a "plan B". Pension assets exceeding GH¢21 billion offer a cushion, but Axis Pensions CEO Afriyie Oware says institutional capacity would be nearly exhausted, requiring strong foreign and retail participation. Investment bankers and Association of Shareholders president Sas George said the market can contain the transactions, with retail uptake dependent on the value offered and discounted rights-issue prices.

This study developed and psychometrically evaluated an Arabic version of the 22-item Orthognathic Quality of Life Questionnaire (OQLQ) for Saudi Arabian patients with malocclusions and dentofacial deformities. The Arabic version was produced through independent forward and back translation, expert review, and pilot testing. The prospective longitudinal study recruited 74 adults from a private orthodontic practice in Jeddah; 12 patients completed preoperative and postoperative questionnaires, and 15 completed repeat questionnaires two weeks apart.

The Arabic OQLQ demonstrated excellent internal consistency (Cronbach’s α=0.92). Test-retest correlations ranged from 0.601 for awareness of dentofacial deformity to 0.879 for oral function, with an overall correlation of 0.859. Construct validity was supported by positive correlations between OQLQ scores and treatment satisfaction, particularly for facial aesthetics, and by significantly better quality-of-life scores among patients reporting improved postoperative appearance.

Overall OQLQ scores were lower after surgery, with median scores decreasing from 34 to 10 in the full cohort (p<0.0001). In the smaller paired subgroup, scores decreased from 22 to 11.5 (p=0.09), while facial aesthetics improved significantly (p=0.03). The authors concluded that the Arabic OQLQ is comprehensible, reliable, valid, responsive, and suitable for assessing quality-of-life changes related to orthognathic treatment. Limitations included small test-retest and paired samples, incomplete validity testing against other instruments, no direct comprehension assessment, and recruitment from a single private practice.

The Supreme Court will consider whether restitution under the 1996 Mandatory Victims Restitution Act constitutes a criminal punishment subject to the Constitution’s ex post facto clause. The case involves Holsey Ellingburg’s bank robbery: if the clause applies, he owes no more restitution than required when the crime occurred; otherwise, revised restitution statutes apply. Restitution is imposed as part of his criminal sentence, governed by criminal procedures, and enforceable through incarceration for nonpayment. The government is not defending the lower ruling that restitution is criminal, while a court-appointed amicus argues the evidence is insufficient to reverse it. The author predicts the majority will not uphold the enhancement.
Delta plans to acquire up to another 32% of Grupo Aeroméxico at MXN43.59 per share, subject to Mexican and U.S. approvals. Its pension trust could reach 49% ownership.
United States v. Walker (8th Cir. 1937): appeal dismissed on appellant's motion with appellee's consent, no costs.
Tradeshift raised $250 million in a Series E led by Goldman Sachs and PSP Investments, bringing total funding above $400 million and its claimed valuation above $1.1 billion.

Stephen Pearse, a former CEO, entrepreneur, and angel investor, describes startup formation, fundraising, and leadership. He says roughly one in ten startups may succeed, with success often meaning at least a tenfold investor return, while moderate returns and failures can still provide valuable experience. Startups seeking outside investment generally need an eventual exit through a public offering or acquisition so investors can recover their money. He also notes that large companies may buy startups when smaller teams can use newer components to produce faster, smaller, cheaper, and better products.

Pearse emphasizes fundraising and presentation. A startup must distinguish itself from competing pitches with a strong hook that can engage attention within seconds. The opening should identify a large market, dissatisfaction with current solutions, a distinctive product, and the technology behind it. Founders should rehearse a concise, audience-specific explanation understandable to a nontechnical person, avoid jargon, emphasize customer benefits, and translate the proposed value into increased revenue or reduced costs. In mixed audiences, the pitch should be pitched to the lowest common denominator.

A presentation should generally fit into 20 minutes, use visuals, manage technical tangents, and culminate in a specific offer of investment in exchange for equity. A suggested sequence is the hook, solution and technology, market, business model, sales and distribution, competition, team, financials, development status, timeline, and final request for funding. Pearse contrasts an overloaded pitch that begins with technical jargon and projections with effective examples that quickly explain a recognizable customer problem, such as integrating separate smart-home devices through one application.

Successful presenters should project passion, confidence, and engagement, speak slowly, maintain eye contact, involve the room, practice repeatedly, and prepare for difficult questions. They should know their audience, research attendees, avoid technical distractions, and respond firmly even when an answer requires follow-up.

Pearse advises founders to begin fundraising before money is urgently needed, ideally about six months before depletion. Investor outreach should be coordinated in parallel rather than conducted serially, creating simultaneous interest and competition among potential funders. Attention can be generated through personal introductions, a clear differentiator, or outside coverage. When choosing between offers, investors’ reputation and ability to facilitate future financing may matter as much as equity dilution. Cash flow must be monitored closely, potentially with a CFO.

Startups should embrace customer feedback, prototypes, pivots, and the lean-startup method when circumstances change. For example, one company shifted from an internet-addressable irrigation system to a broader smart-home integration platform. Although intellectual property can be useful, Pearse considers speed and reaching the market first more important than exclusive protection. Founders should maintain a clear mission, stay focused, build a team whose skills and chemistry complement one another, and prepare for difficult personnel decisions. Experienced investors may not contribute much beyond their networks and introductions, while angel investors may be more hands-on.

The central message is that leadership wins: founders must show passion, confidence, and engagement, then make a clear call to action by inviting investors to join and help change the world.

The team has performed well on the road and has depth, with four strong lines, six capable defensemen, solid goaltending and helpful deadline and in-season additions. He credits increased owner commitment for the team’s success. The next game in Anaheim is sold out and expected to be competitive. This systematic review examined how student personality traits relate to satisfaction and success in online higher education, with particular relevance to occupational therapy education. Following Cochrane and PRISMA methods, authors searched seven databases for peer-reviewed English-language studies published from January 2000 through June 2024. Eligible studies involved higher education students, online learning, recognized Big Five or Myers-Briggs personality assessments, and measures of satisfaction and/or success. Risk of bias was assessed with the Mixed Methods Appraisal Tool, and findings were synthesized qualitatively by theme and strength of evidence.

Of 848 records identified, 23 were included. All were level IV evidence, resulting in low-strength findings, and none specifically examined occupational therapy programs. Conscientiousness was consistently associated with greater satisfaction, engagement, and grades. Openness, agreeableness, and emotional stability were also generally linked to better outcomes, whereas neuroticism was usually negatively associated with satisfaction and success, although one study found higher-neuroticism students performed better online. Extraversion had mixed associations with grades and satisfaction and was more closely linked with face-to-face preference and active discussion participation. Personality also influenced class-format choices, assignment preferences, and perceived isolation.

The evidence was limited by the exclusively descriptive studies, nonstandardized satisfaction measures, search restrictions, possible missed studies, and geographic variability. No occupational therapy studies were identified. Future research should use stronger designs and test interventions, particularly in occupational therapy and other health-professions education. Educators are encouraged to use Universal Design for Learning, flexible course and assignment design, synchronous discussion opportunities, and support for self-regulated learning, self-efficacy, and locus of control to accommodate diverse student needs.

In 1977, amid fear of Peter Sutcliffe and wider threats to women, the Leeds Revolutionary Feminist Group organized the UK’s first Reclaim the Night marches, held in 12 towns and cities. Women carried banners and torches to protest harassment and violence. The marches continued for over a decade before fading in the early 1990s and being revived in 2004. Four decades later, Leeds theatre company RashDash drew on the movement’s history for The Darkest Corners, a physical-theatre production with live music staged in a Holbeck car park during Transform 17. Creators Abbi Greenland and Helen Goalen said women still feel vulnerable at night and sought to celebrate women’s solidarity and activism.

Adjunct instructors at Southwestern College held a sparsely attended rally seeking better wages and protections equal to those of full-time faculty. They teach nearly 75% of the college’s classes but receive fewer benefits, work long hours, travel among colleges, and face unstable employment and inadequate insurance. English adjunct Geoffrey Johnson said these pressures undermine education. Math adjunct Mark Freeman described commuting to five colleges, while English adjunct Cody Dolnick highlighted the difficulty of retaining health coverage and being rehired. Other adjuncts discussed financial strain and limited workers’ compensation. President Kindred Murillo and Trustee Roberto Alcantar attended in support, praising adjuncts’ commitment to students and the college. Dolnick and Johnson called for greater support for adjuncts, including paid office hours and disability leave.

NVIDIA’s Turing GPU architecture combines dedicated RT Cores, Tensor Cores, redesigned streaming multiprocessors, and enhanced graphics pipelines to support hybrid rendering, which integrates real-time ray tracing, rasterization, AI-based image enhancement, and simulation.

Turing supports USB Type-C and VirtualLink, an open standard led by NVIDIA, Oculus, Valve, Microsoft, and AMD. VirtualLink uses a USB-C alternate mode to deliver display, power, and data through one connector while supporting four HBR3 DisplayPort lanes and a SuperSpeed USB 3 link for motion tracking. This reduces VR headset cabling and permits VR use on compact devices that can accommodate only a small USB-C connector.

Turing TU102 and TU104 replace MIO and PCIe interfaces for SLI transfers with second-generation NVLink. TU102 has two x8 links and TU104 has one, with each link providing 25 GB/s per direction. Both support two-way SLI but not three- or four-way configurations. The greater bandwidth enables display configurations unavailable with the previous SLI bridge.

Turing introduces hardware-accelerated, real-time ray tracing through an RT Core in every streaming multiprocessor. Each RT Core contains separate units for bounding-box tests and ray-triangle intersections, handling BVH traversal and intersection testing that previously required thousands of shader instructions per ray. RT Cores free the multiprocessor for other graphics and compute work. The passage reports more than 10 Giga Rays per second on Turing, compared with approximately 1.1 Giga Rays per second in software on Pascal, making ray tracing about ten times faster.

Turing supports hybrid rendering, combining rasterization for visibility and primary-ray work with ray tracing for effects such as reflections, refractions, shadows, and indirect lighting. Dedicated RT Cores, BVH acceleration structures, denoising, and advanced acceleration structures allow real-time ray tracing on a single GPU. Compatible technologies include NVIDIA RTX, OptiX, NVIDIA Real-Time Ray Tracing Libraries, Microsoft DirectX Ray Tracing, and the forthcoming Vulkan ray-tracing API. Ray-traced shadows can provide physically correct contact hardening, ray-traced ambient occlusion produces more detailed environmental shading than screen-space techniques, and ray-traced reflections avoid limitations associated with screen-space reflections and cubemap probes.

NVIDIA NGX is a deep-learning technology stack within RTX that uses Turing Tensor Cores for AI-based graphics and application services. NGX exposes pretrained features through an API managed through GeForce Experience or Quadro Experience, with models interfacing with CUDA 10, DirectX, Vulkan, and TensorRT. Deep Learning Super-Sampling, or DLSS, trains a neural network using high-quality 64-times-supersampled reference images. Standard DLSS renders from fewer input samples and infers a target-resolution result, reducing shading work while maintaining quality comparable to temporal anti-aliasing. DLSS 2X renders at target resolution and uses a larger network to produce output approaching 64-times-supersampled quality. Other NGX features include InPainting for replacing image content, AI Slow-Mo for generating interpolated frames, and AI Super Rez for 2x, 4x, or 8x image and video upscaling.

Mesh shading adds task and mesh shader stages that use cooperative thread models. Task shaders process object lists in parallel, launch mesh shaders, select geometry-level-of-detail versions, and can cull or modify geometry. This removes CPU draw-call bottlenecks and enables real-time rendering of hundreds of thousands of objects. The technology also supports dynamic cutaways and other specialized geometry operations.

Variable Rate Shading controls shading rates independently from visibility rates in 16-by-16-pixel regions. Developers can select from several pixel footprints, assign different rates spatially or per primitive, and use multiple rates within one triangle. Example algorithms include Content Adaptive Shading, which lowers rates in spatially or temporally uniform regions; Motion Adaptive Shading, which reduces rates for rapidly moving objects; and Foveated Rendering, which shades peripheral regions less densely and focused regions more densely. Variable Rate Shading can also increase shading above the per-pixel baseline when used with multisample anti-aliasing.

Texture Space Shading stores dynamically computed shading values in texture-space texels rather than directly in screen pixels. It decouples visibility sampling from appearance sampling, allowing different rates, grids, or timing while reusing previously shaded texels across pixels, frames, or stereo views. Its flexibility, stability, and multi-resolution support are particularly useful for VR rendering.

Multi-View Rendering can process up to four hardware views per pass and supports up to 32 views at the API level. It shares geometry and view-independent shader results while computing view-dependent attributes separately. Turing expands Pascal’s Simultaneous Multi-Projection capabilities and applies to stereo and wide-field-of-view VR displays, multiple character instances, shadow-depth buffers, and cascaded shadow maps. Turing also adds bindless constant-buffer and unordered-access views, co-located resource types, and Tier 2 resource-heap support.

The full TU104 contains 48 streaming multiprocessors, 3,072 CUDA Cores, 368 Tensor Cores, 48 RT Cores, a 256-bit memory interface, and one x8 NVLink link. It is used in products such as the GeForce RTX 2080, Tesla T4, and Quadro RTX 5000. The Tesla T4 variant has 40 streaming multiprocessors, 2,560 CUDA Cores, 320 Tensor Cores, and 320 GB/s memory bandwidth. TU106, used in the GeForce RTX 2070, has 36 streaming multiprocessors, 2,304 CUDA Cores, 288 Tensor Cores, and 36 RT Cores but does not support NVLink or SLI.

RTX-OPS is presented as a workload-based performance metric that weights Tensor operations at 20%, CUDA-core operations at 80%, RT-core operations at 40%, and INT32 operations at 28%. For the RTX 2080 Ti, the passage calculates a total of 78 RTX-OPS. The passage also explains ray casting, BVH tree traversal, BVH building and refitting, denoising, and the importance of RT Cores, hybrid rendering, and BVH acceleration in making real-time ray tracing practical.

Sharon Goldman’s “Eye on AI” highlights Pika, a Gen Z-focused AI video company co-founded by 26-year-old Demi Guo and Chenlin Meng. Pika has raised about $135 million at a $470 million valuation and serves 16.4 million users. Its TikTok-like app features Predictive Video, which turns a selfie and a simple request into a complete video with a script, music, dance moves, lighting, effects, and AI-generated surroundings. Pika emphasizes creativity, interaction, and self-expression for Gen Z and Gen Alpha, distinguishing itself from OpenAI’s cinematic Sora, Meta’s Vibes, and mass-produced “slop.”

Other developments include San Francisco rents rising 6% over the past year amid AI-startup growth, with some AI hub neighborhoods seeing 13% increases. TSMC reported a record 39.1% profit increase on AI-chip demand and raised its 2025 revenue-growth forecast to the mid-30% range. Spotify partnered with Sony, Universal, Warner, Merlin, Believe, and others to develop opt-in, responsible generative-AI tools for artists and songwriters. A survey found low American interest and trust in AI mental-health tools: 11% would consider using one, 8% trust them, 40% distrust them, and only 4% have tried one.

The article examines students’ perceptions of and preferences between online learning (OL) and emergency remote education (ERE). OL is an intentionally planned, technology-mediated modality offering flexibility and emphasizing interaction, assessment, autonomy, and self-regulated learning. ERE arose as a temporary response to the COVID-19 crisis, requiring rapid conversion of instruction to remote formats despite limited time, preparation, technological access, and digital literacy.

The study used a case-based approach at a medium-sized private university in Colombia’s Caribbean region. A total of 88 students completed an online survey rating 14 OL and ERE components on a 1–10 scale and answering open-ended questions. Data were examined through descriptive statistics, paired tests, the add-on preferential groups model with permutation testing, and qualitative content analysis.

Students generally viewed both modalities positively, but rated OL more highly across most assessed components. Significant OL advantages included content quality, active and collaborative activities, support for diverse learning styles, time for asynchronous work, educational resources and platforms, assessment strategies, and technical support. More than 57% preferred OL for several individual components. Differences in instructor interaction and feedback were comparatively small, while preferences for student-to-student interaction were nearly equal, although students considered this interaction slightly more effective in ERE.

Open-ended responses identified flexibility, comfort, effective learning, technological development, and instructor contact and feedback as advantages of ERE. Its main weaknesses concerned insufficient instructor preparation and organization, limited use of varied technologies, excessive content, and inadequate interaction or information access. OL was valued for its planning, structure, flexibility, learning effectiveness, interaction, and technological resources. Suggested improvements included stronger instructor-student interaction, more varied activities, fewer assignments and assessments, additional synchronous sessions, and better scheduling.

The findings support ongoing instructor training in digital tools and pedagogy, reduced student workload, authentic and collaborative assessment, and spaces that promote peer interaction. They also indicate that elements of ERE, particularly its synchronous interaction and direct access to instructors, may be valuable in post-pandemic education.

Mark Cuban said President Donald Trump’s planned TrumpRx.gov could reduce prescription-drug prices if it forces pharmacy benefit managers and insurers to change their business practices, adding that Trump would deserve credit if that occurred. The federal website is intended to sell discounted drugs directly to consumers and is scheduled to go live in early 2026. Cuban, who founded Cost Plus Drugs in 2022, gave the platform a “B” because he believes it remains structured to benefit large PBMs, whose rebate practices he and other critics say inflate costs.

The initiative gives participating drugmakers a three-year reprieve from pharmaceutical tariffs and advances Trump’s effort to align U.S. drug prices with those in other countries. Initial participation is limited to Pfizer, though Trump says other manufacturers will join. KFF’s Drew Altman remains skeptical, saying direct-to-consumer platforms function as cash-only pharmacies that cannot accept insurance and therefore mainly benefit uninsured consumers.

The Russell 2000 is a market-weighted index of roughly 2,000 U.S. small-cap stocks and a subset of the Russell 3000. It is reconstituted annually on the fourth Friday of June to add qualifying companies, remove ineligible ones, and adjust constituent weights to reflect market-capitalization changes. Required buying and selling can create temporary market imbalances and have historically contributed to an end-of-June rally.

The proposed strategy buys the Russell 2000 at the close of the first trading day after June 23 and sells at the close of the first trading day of July. Backtesting the cash index (^RUT) from 1988 found an average gain of 1.34% over six trading days, compared with 0.85% for the S&P 500. A strategy equally allocated to a long Russell 2000 position and a short S&P 500 position averaged only 0.23%, with weak performance during its first 12 years and relatively flat results over the following decade.

Motley Fool Money presents several cash-back credit-card offers and discloses that advertiser compensation may affect product placement or coverage, though not product ratings. The Wells Fargo Active Cash Card offers unlimited 2% cash back, no annual fee, a $200 bonus after $500 in purchases within three months, 0% intro APR for 12 months on purchases and qualifying transfers, and cell phone protection. Capital One Quicksilver offers unlimited 1.5% cash back on purchases, 5% on Capital One Travel bookings, no annual or foreign transaction fees, up to $300 in welcome benefits, and 0% intro APR for 15 months on purchases and transfers. A Citi offer provides 2% cash back when purchases are paid in full, 5% on Citi Travel bookings, $200 after $1,500 in purchases within six months, and 18 months of 0% intro APR on balance transfers only. Each lists a recommended credit score of 670–850, but approval is not guaranteed.

Digital leaders coordinate teams through transparent, data-driven objectives aligned with company strategy. Effective goal-setting combines top-down and bottom-up processes, builds employee buy-in, and avoids excessive analysis that undermines intuition. Digital laggards often have priorities weakly connected to strategy, leading employees to deprioritize poorly understood objectives and worsen organizational misalignment.

A strong data culture aligns organizations vertically by connecting individual and team goals to company goals, and horizontally by providing common data models, transparent access, and clear metrics that improve collaboration. At digital leaders, leadership beliefs, stated values, and employee behaviors reinforce one another; at laggards, entrenched habits, skill gaps, and insufficient leadership focus prevent this alignment. Changing mindsets and behaviors remains a major challenge, but successful transformations are possible and mature organizations must continue developing their cultures.

Strong data cultures emphasize learning, risk-taking, transparency, and measurement. Organizations fall into four maturity patterns: data novices, insight-ready firms, tech-enabled firms, and data-reliant firms that may over-rely on data and discourage critical thinking. Each can build on existing strengths through targeted action.

The President returns a House bill appropriating $1,378,450 for more than forty harbor and river improvements, withholding approval on constitutional and fiscal grounds. He argues that Congress has neither express nor incidental authority to construct internal improvements within states or appropriate Treasury funds for them. Although he accepts long-standing federal support for navigation aids, the bill includes many local projects unrelated to foreign commerce or the protection of shipping. Approving it would establish a sweeping internal-improvement system, encourage consolidated federal power, distribute public funds unequally, promote sectional conflict and waste, and increase public debt or taxation. He also considers $1 million to $2 million in nonurgent spending imprudent during a foreign war.

Coach DeBoer said his team made poor reads and decisions that the opponent capitalized on, and that it must improve. He described the team as tentative early before playing better, noting similar successful rallies in the previous two rounds. He said the team did not deserve to win but would have been fortunate to steal the game. DeBoer planned to maintain the team’s routine and preparation rather than make changes, emphasizing patience, traffic, shots, and persistence against strong opponents. He cited the organization’s extensive experience and the community’s excitement over the Stanley Cup Final run. He also discussed his family’s support during a period of unemployment.

The coach said Boston deserved to win after a hard-fought game, crediting strong goaltending, tough scoring around Vancouver’s net, and solid defensive coverage and rebounding. He praised Vancouver’s effort and noted the team had several good scoring chances but could not convert, while rejecting injuries as an excuse. Despite disappointment, he said both teams competed hard and that Boston was the better team. Jeff is expected to play in the seventh game, and the coach believes he has the necessary experience. He said everyone will be nervous but must manage it, enjoy the moment, and focus on the process. Reflecting on his fifth year coaching in Vancouver and his long path back to the NHL, he said he is excited about the opportunity and understands what is at stake.

The statistical analysis plan (SAP) for protocol ZP4207-17086 defines analyses for a phase 3, randomized, double-blind, placebo- and active-controlled trial evaluating a single 0.6 mg dose of dasiglucagon against placebo and GlucaGen® in children with type I diabetes. The study includes screening from Day −30 to Day −3, treatment on Day 0–1, and follow-up on Day 28, with approximately five centers in Europe and the USA.

The primary endpoint is time to plasma glucose recovery, defined as the first increase of at least 20 mg/dL from baseline within 45 minutes without rescue IV glucose. The primary analysis uses the full analysis set (FAS), with Kaplan–Meier estimates and a log-rank test stratified by age group and injection site. Patients receiving rescue glucose or not recovering by 45 minutes are censored at 45 minutes; supportive and sensitivity analyses address alternative censoring approaches, linear interpolation, and Wilcoxon and Cox proportional hazards methods.

Secondary efficacy endpoints include recovery within 10, 15, 20, and 30 minutes and changes from baseline at those times. Recovery rates are analyzed using Cochran–Mantel–Haenszel tests, or non-stratified Fisher’s exact tests if cell counts are insufficient, while glucose changes are analyzed by ANOVA adjusted for age group and injection site. Confirmatory testing of dasiglucagon versus placebo follows a hierarchical order at a two-sided 0.05 significance level; GlucaGen comparisons are not included in the hierarchy. Missing efficacy data are not imputed, and no interim analyses or confirmatory analyses are planned.

Safety analyses use the safety set and cover treatment exposure, hypoglycemia induction, rescue glucose, local tolerability, treatment-emergent adverse events, serious events, laboratory results, vital signs, ECGs, immunogenicity, and pregnancy testing. Pharmacokinetic analyses use non-compartmental methods in Phoenix WinNonlin, while the pharmacodynamic endpoint is baseline-adjusted glucose response area from 0–30 minutes calculated in SAS.

The SAP also specifies safety, per-protocol, and FAS definitions; demographic, baseline, medical-history, medication, protocol-deviation, and disposition summaries; data-handling conventions for missing values and concentrations below quantification limits; and standards for tables, listings, figures, program validation, and quality control. All analyses and tabulations use SAS 9.4 or later, with PK/PD analyses using Phoenix WinNonlin 6.4 or later.

**Summary**

The passage is an NVIDIA technical document describing the GA10x (Ampere) GPU architecture and related technologies.

**GDDR6X memory:** GA10x uses GDDR6X, developed with Micron Technology as the first GPUs to employ it. PAM4 four-level signaling transfers two bits per clock edge, doubling the I/O data rate over PAM2/NRZ, while a new MTA encoding scheme limits signal transitions to improve SNR; new interface training, equalization, and package/PCB signal-integrity work support data rates up to 19.5 Gbps and up to 936 GB/sec peak bandwidth—over 52% more than the TU102 in the RTX 2080 Ti, and up to 64% more bandwidth than prior GPU generations. Pseudo-independent memory channels also assist BVH ray traversal.

**Storage and RTX IO:** As games exceed 200GB and SSDs (up to 7 GB/sec) outpace hard drives (50–100 MB/sec), traditional file systems and CPU decompression become bottlenecks. NVIDIA RTX IO, working with Microsoft's DirectStorage API, performs GPU-based lossless decompression and direct SSD-to-GPU loading, delivering up to 100x I/O performance, 20x lower CPU utilization, near-instant loading, higher frame rates, less object pop-in/stutter, and reduced install sizes. It benefits gamers, artists, and rendering workflows, using Turing/Ampere DMA and copy engines with asynchronous compute.

**NVIDIA A40:** Based on GA10x, the A40 delivers up to 2x FP32, 2x ray-tracing, and 5x (10x with sparsity) throughput versus Quadro RTX 6000, a PCIe Gen4 interface, 48 GB memory scalable to 96 GB via third-generation NVLink, three DP 1.4 outputs, vGPU support, Quadro Sync, and EGX platform compatibility.

**Display and media:** Ampere supports 4K 120Hz and 8K 60Hz, DisplayPort 1.4a with DSC 1.2a (two 8K displays at 60Hz), and HDMI 2.1 at 48 Gbps with dynamic HDR, plus HDCP 2.3/1.x. The fifth-generation NVDEC supports MPEG-2, VC-1, H.264, H.265, VP8, VP9, and AV1; GA10x is the first GPU with hardware AV1 decode (50–55% bitrate savings over H.264), playing 8K60 HDR at ~4% CPU usage versus a CPU decoder's 28 FPS and 85% utilization. Seventh-generation NVENC exceeds x264 Fast quality, matches x264 Medium, and encodes 4K H.264 and 8K HEVC.

**Architecture and GPUs:** GA10x provides up to 2x gains in shading, ray tracing, and AI; second-generation RT Cores double ray/triangle intersection and add motion-blur support plus concurrent ray tracing with shading or compute; third-generation Tensor Cores implement structural sparsity, doubling effective throughput, and DLSS enables 8K HDR rendering. The GeForce RTX 3090 (GA102) has 24 GB GDDR6X, 82 SMs, and 10,496 CUDA cores, 1.5x faster than TITAN RTX; the RTX 3070 (GA104) outperforms the RTX 2080 Ti but uses GDDR6 and lacks NVLink. New Error Detection and Replay (EDR) detects and retries failed GDDR6X transactions, with performance plateauing signaling the memory limit. The RTX A6000 (GA102) offers 10,752 CUDA cores, 48 GB GDDR6 scalable to 96 GB via NVLink, and hardware-accelerated AI denoising. The document closes with NVIDIA's standard specifications disclaimer and 2021 copyright notice.

Apple Inc. filed a Form 8-K dated May 1, 2018. The company issued a press release and related data sheet concerning its financial results for the second fiscal quarter ended March 31, 2018, attached as Exhibits 99.1 and 99.2. The information was not deemed filed under Section 18 of the Exchange Act or incorporated by reference unless expressly incorporated by specific reference. The report was signed by Luca Maestri, Senior Vice President and Chief Financial Officer.

According to reports, Queen Elizabeth II planned to step aside at 95 and would seriously consider passing the throne to Prince Charles if she were still alive. A proposed Regency Act would allow Charles to assume full governing powers while she remained alive; Clarence House declined to comment, though a royal commentator said preparations were advancing. Ascended in 1952, Elizabeth was Britain’s longest-reigning monarch. Charles was first in line, followed by Prince William and Prince George.

Microsoft Corporation filed a Form 8-K dated April 12, 2021, reporting under Item 7.01 (Regulation FD Disclosure) that it had entered a definitive agreement to acquire Nuance Communications, Inc. for $56.00 per share in an all-cash transaction valued at $19.7 billion, inclusive of Nuance's net debt. The press release was attached as Exhibit 99.1 and investor presentation slides as Exhibit 99.2, with Microsoft and Nuance representatives presenting to investors on and after April 12, 2021. Dolliver, Assistant Secretary, and lists Microsoft's registered securities (common stock and 2.125%, 3.125%, and 2.625% notes due 2021, 2028, and 2033) traded on NASDAQ.

During the ongoing federal shutdown, the Office of Management and Budget said layoffs had begun, identifying 4,132 to 4,232 workers for termination. The filing lists 315 Commerce, 1,100–1,200 Health and Human Services, 442 Housing and Urban Development, 176 Homeland Security, and 1,446 Treasury employees. Health and Human Services, Housing and Urban Development, and Education confirmed cuts, while Homeland Security said layoffs would occur within CISA.

Federal employee unions filed a lawsuit and sought a temporary restraining order, arguing that the shutdown was being improperly used to lay off workers. About 658,000 federal and military employees were furloughed without pay, with some facing partial or missed paychecks until the government reopens. Workers across several agencies anticipate further cuts and cited financial insecurity and potential harm to local businesses. Earlier firings, retirements, buyouts, resignations, and deferred resignals had also reduced the federal workforce.

Chennai’s 19-year-old Punith Kumar ranked first in India and third internationally in the ACCA CA final P2 exam. He completed the course in two years and three months while interning, aided by rigorous study and mentor support, and plans to finish remaining papers by September.

The passage reviews international decisions awarding damages for vessels seized or detained by foreign governments. In the Hope On, an arbitral commission held that loss of vessel use was proper damages, measured by the probable catch lost during absence from fishing grounds. In the Col. Lloyd Aspinwall, seized by Spanish agents, the umpire allowed damages for 114 days of interrupted trade. Awards by the Bering Sea Commission likewise applied this rule in cases involving the Favorite, Alfred Adams, Juniata, Pathfinder, Black Diamond, Lily, and Triumph. The Triumph award illustrates the method by calculating the value of the season’s estimated catch remaining at seizure. The passage concludes that a government may not, based on mere suspicion of trespass, forcibly enroll citizens of a friendly nation aboard its vessels without their consent.

The passage explains that, despite momentum working over longer periods, the SPY exhibits short-term mean reversion: it tends to rise after a down day and fall after an up day. Mean reversion captures price bounces and dips as asset prices eventually return toward their long-run averages. A strategy of buying after a red day and selling after a green day was backtested using SPY data adjusted for dividends and splits. Reported results included higher CAGR, better risk-adjusted returns, less time spent in the market, and substantially lower maximum drawdown than the green-day strategy. The backtest supports short-term mean reversion in the S&P 500, while momentum remains effective over longer timeframes.

The Jan. 21 Option Investor Newsletter reported broad market declines amid profit-taking and concerns about Brazil, global currencies, export weakness, and possible devaluation of China or Hong Kong. The Dow fell 71.83 points to 9,264.08, the Nasdaq lost 70.77 points to 2,344.72, and the S&P 500 declined 21.46 points to 1,235.16. Internet and technology stocks sold off sharply, while volatility reached 31.95. Market posture was mostly neutral, with hardware bullish and insurance and oil-and-gas sectors bearish. Pinnacle Capital Advisors described sentiment as bearish and recommended protecting long positions, building hedges, and considering cash if the Dow remained below 9,400 or volatility stayed above 30%.

The newsletter emphasized that strong earnings did not prevent sell-offs when expectations were high. IBM and Lucent declined despite beating estimates, while Sun Microsystems announced a 2-for-1 split and strong results but also fell on profit-taking. It generally advised confirming market direction before initiating trades and warned against holding positions through earnings.

Sun Microsystems fell sharply after announcing its split and earnings beat.

New call plays recommended Vodafone calls expiring February through April, Qwest Communications calls expiring February and March, and diagonal spreads in Citrix Systems, Read-Rite, Level 3 Communications, and Sepracor, with specified strikes, target debits, and projected returns. The newsletter also identified weak put candidates including Avid, Bank of America, Baxter, Campbell’s, DuPont, Eastman Kodak, Electronic Arts, Housey, Lilly, Microchip, Merck, Coca-Cola? RMBS and Walt Disney, generally recommending tighter protective stops.

QCOM, Disney, Yahoo, Check Point, Lucent, and ATI were dropped from the call list because of weak performance, earnings concerns, or changes in their investment profiles. Ofcom has proposed automatic compensation for fixed broadband and landline customers whose service is not promptly fixed, whose new service is not working by the promised date, or whose engineer misses an appointment. Payments would take the form of cash or bill credits and be set by Ofcom. The proposal could benefit up to 2.6 million customers through £185 million in annual compensation. A consultation runs until 5 June, with a decision expected by year-end.

The Sonora High School Athletic Hall of Fame’s 2017 class honors 12 former Wildcats athletes and coaches whose careers span 1950–2008. Inductees include Howard “Socky” Keefe, Dennis Jackson, Don Moore, Cam Fray, Jon Wagner, Mark McCollough, Becky Fray Aguilar, Jodi Gardella Richey, Jessica Peterson McCornack, Lexi Kopf Scoles, and coaches Lloyd Gaspar and Gary Smith. Book censorship is expanding from public schools into higher education, with PEN America reporting 22,810 U.S. school book bans from 2021–2025. Conservative pressure now targets campus libraries, curricula, course assignments, syllabi and academic departments, including at Franciscan University, New College of Florida, the U.S. Naval Academy and Texas A&M. The passage also cites West Point professor Graham Parsons’s resignation over course restrictions and an Israeli official’s demand that Princeton ban *The Right to Maim*. New legislative proposals would require public, searchable syllabus, enabling readings to be challenged. The Trump administration’s proposed “Compact for Academic Excellence” would condition federal funding on colleges abolishing units seen as belittling conservative ideas. Despite these threats, broad public opposition to book banning offers hope, and the passage calls for educators, librarians, professors and students across institutions and ideologies to unite against censorship.

A federal judge upheld FACEA’s religious protections for Falun Gong practitioners, rejecting a Commerce Clause challenge and ruling that places of worship need not be physical temples. The decision will be appealed before a jury trial in the harassment lawsuit.

Under the Carter administration, MONs introduced higher-risk, costlier, or geographically specific covert operations within previously approved objectives, requiring CIA-State and broader interagency coordination. They were later used for significant changes to findings, while entirely new covert actions still required presidential findings. The CIA typically notified Congress within 48 hours. The 1980 Intelligence Oversight Act retained notice requirements but limited briefings to two intelligence committees, clarified that notice did not imply congressional approval, and allowed the president to delay advance notice in extraordinary circumstances, followed by timely notice and an explanation.

Early 1983 archival records show Shultz presenting Reagan a four-part Soviet agenda: human rights, arms control, regional issues, and bilateral relations. Memos and telegrams circulated among officials, and Eagleburger later briefed Clark on Shultz’s meeting with Dobriansky.

In St. Louis & San Francisco Railroad Co. v. Conarty, a widow acting as administratrix sued the railroad after her husband, a switchman, was killed when an engine collided with a coal car missing its drawbar, coupling, and headblock. The jury awarded $10,000, and the railroad appealed.

The court held that the Federal Employers’ Liability Act validly prohibited removal to federal court based on diversity of citizenship. It also held that the 1910 amendment permitted the widow, in one action and with one recovery, to seek compensation for both the decedent’s pain and suffering and the widow and next of kin’s pecuniary losses.

Although the disabled car was being moved for repairs, it remained in use for interstate commerce. The 1910 amendment allowed defective cars to be hauled to repair facilities at the carrier’s risk without exempting the carrier from civil liability for employee injuries. Proper couplers were required, and the missing equipment directly caused the collision and death even though the decedent was not handling the coupler.

The court permitted the widow to testify about the decedent’s financial contributions because that testimony concerned damages and was collateral to the railroad’s liability. The judgment was affirmed.

The RBZ said the official US dollar–bond note exchange rate remains 1:1 and urged the public to use licensed banks, bureaux de change, and money-transfer agencies. Licensed institutions may charge a spread of up to 10% when exchanging either currency for others. The RBZ welcomed arrests of illegal money changers and said it would act against retailers refusing non-cash payments.

The dollar reached a three-week high after New York Fed President William Dudley indicated any pause in rate hikes while shrinking the Fed’s bond portfolio would be brief, supporting Treasury yields. March job growth missed forecasts, but unemployment fell to 4.5%, suggesting labor-market strength remained intact. Speculators cut net long dollar positions to a five-week low. The euro weakened amid uncertainty surrounding France’s tightening presidential election, while geopolitical tensions involving Syria supported the yen as a safe-haven currency.

The passage derives a spectral quantum Cramér–Rao bound for continuous-wave interferometric phase estimation using paired squeezed states with finite squeezing bandwidth. For pure squeezed states without losses, the phase-estimation PSD is bounded by 1/[(ΔΩ/π)n(n+2)], where ΔΩ is the squeezing bandwidth and n is photon flux per frequency mode. At large n, standard deviation scales as 1/√n, yielding Heisenberg scaling. Two output homodyne detectors and a nonlinear estimator can attain the bound. At mid-fringe with quadrature detection, squaring and subtracting the records recovers a sinusoidal signal because the rectified statistic is Rayleigh distributed with a phase-linear mean. Practically, filtered records are processed by an unbiased linearized maximum-likelihood estimator.

This study evaluated the prognostic value of the prognostic nutrition index (PNI), neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR), and platelet-to-lymphocyte ratio (PLR) in patients with chronic hepatitis C-associated cirrhosis complicated by type 2 diabetes, for which evidence was limited. Researchers included 56 patients with both cirrhosis and type 2 diabetes, 85 with cirrhosis alone, and 85 with type 2 diabetes alone at Fuyang Second People’s Hospital from January 2018 to December 2021. After six months of treatment, the combined-disease group was divided into poor-prognosis and good-prognosis subgroups. Serum albumin, liver enzymes, and blood-cell counts were measured, and PNI, NLR, and PLR were calculated using admission data.

The Rubber Band trading strategy is a simple contrarian, mean-reversion approach for stocks that identifies overbought or oversold conditions expected to revert toward the mean. It can use Keltner Channels, Bollinger Bands, momentum oscillators, or similar indicators. With a standard 20-period Keltner Channel and 10-period ATR, a buy signal occurs when price opens and closes below the lower band, while a sell signal occurs above the upper band. Reversal candles can confirm signals, which should be backtested. Profit targets are generally the middle band or just before the opposite band. An XLP out-of-sample backtest produced 328 trades, a 0.45% average gain, 6.1% CAGR, 20% market exposure, a profit factor of 2, and a 16% maximum drawdown. The strategy favors buying amid excessive pessimism and selling amid euphoria, works mainly on stocks, and is considered more difficult to apply to assets such as gold and commodities.

UK university staff are in a fourth week of strikes over changes to defined-benefit pensions, with some exams likely to be affected. Talks between Universities UK and UCU have failed, prompting 14 further strike days likely between April and June. UCU still favours an Acas-negotiated settlement. Edinburgh University was criticised for requesting old lecture recordings for students affected by the strike.

This medRxiv preprint (not peer reviewed) examines whether plasma biomarkers can predict cognitive decline and dementia progression when combined with other non-invasive measures. Background notes that standard Alzheimer's disease (AD) diagnostic markers (amyloid-β, tau, neurodegeneration) require costly, invasive CSF or PET testing, while plasma markers such as Aβ42/40, p-tau181, and neurofilament light (NfL) offer accessible alternatives whose role in predicting cognitive decline remains underexplored.

Data came from the ADNI, forming two cohorts: Cohort 1 with p-tau181 and NfL (larger sample), and Cohort 2 adding Aβ42/40. A two-stage machine learning framework was applied: ridge linear regression derived an MRI score from CAT12 volumetric and cortical thickness measures, which was then combined with demographics, APOE4, baseline composite cognitive scores (ADNI-MEM, -EF, -LAN, -VS), and plasma biomarkers using random forest regression (1,000 trees), with nested stratified 10-fold cross-validation repeated 10 times, evaluated by cross-validated Pearson correlation (R) and mean absolute error (MAE). Four models were compared: basic, plasma, MRI, and combined.

Results: For memory (ADNI-MEM), performance improved significantly from basic (R=0.38) to plasma (0.45) and MRI (0.46) models, with the combined model best (0.50, MAE=0.10); the MRI versus plasma difference was not significant. Other domains showed little improvement over the basic model except ADNI-LAN, where the combined model significantly outperformed basic. Cohort 1 and 2 performed similarly. Feature importance analysis showed the MRI score most important for memory, APOE4 significant only for memory, NfL and p-tau181 important for memory, executive function, and language but not visuospatial, and Aβ42/40 least important overall. Prediction was harder in cognitively unimpaired (CU) than MCI groups across all domains (e.g., ADNI-MEM R=0.17 vs 0.53; ADNI-VS 0.33 vs 0.40, not significant).

For progression, predicted decline rates (ADNI-MEM) were split into tertiles: Kaplan-Meier curves differed significantly across all models (log-rank P<0.001). C-index for CU conversion to MCI/dementia was 0.68 (basic), 0.72 (plasma), 0.69 (MRI), 0.76 (combined); for MCI-to-dementia, 0.76, 0.74, 0.77, and 0.79 respectively. Combined-model highest-tertile individuals had over 33-fold and 29-fold greater risk than the lowest tertile in CU and MCI groups.

Conclusions state that plasma biomarkers, combined with MRI and cognitive scores, support domain-specific decline and dementia progression prediction, but are weaker in non-memory domains; limitations include focus on AD-specific biomarkers and an AD-centric cohort, warranting broader biomarker studies.

A National Academies report says scientists should be allowed to edit heritable human DNA only to prevent serious, strongly heritable diseases when reasonable alternatives are unavailable. Such trials require evidence that the targeted gene causes or strongly predisposes carriers to disease, assessment of risks and benefits, public scrutiny, and long-term follow-up. Editing traits such as strength, intelligence, or beauty should remain prohibited. The panel also called for continued public debate and international oversight and regulation as gene-editing technology advances. CRISPR-Cas9 is already being tested in adult cells, including a Chinese lung cancer trial, without altering the germline.

During a May 21–27 Singapore operation, police arrested eight women for suspected online sexual-service advertising, 14 men for gaming-law offences and one for drink-driving, checking 700 people and seizing S$730 and 10 handphones.

Aiden Markram was named South Africa’s cricket captain after Faf du Plessis was forced out with a finger injury. Markram called the appointment an honour and positive pressure, said he would rely on senior players and du Plessis’s advice, and hopes to bounce back in the second ODI against India, which trails the six-match series 1–0.

Google expanded speech recognition to 30 additional languages and locales, bringing the total to 119, including eight Indian languages, Swahili and Amharic. Initial support covers Gboard for Android, Voice Search and the Cloud Speech API, with Google Translate planned. Google trained the system using native speakers’ recordings and machine learning to improve accuracy.

Saints open their 2017/18 Anglo-Welsh Cup campaign at Exeter Chiefs on November 4, followed by a home match against Dragons on November 11. Their remaining pool games are away to Sale Sharks in January and at home to Harlequins in early February.

The paper introduces TeraAgent, a distributed simulation engine that extends BioDynaMo to scale agent-based models across multiple servers. It addresses BioDynaMo’s single-server limits, poor integration with MPI-based tools, and restricted hardware flexibility. TeraAgent partitions simulation space among MPI ranks, exchanges nearby agents for aura updates, migrates agents across partitions, and dynamically balances loads. It supports MPI-only and MPI/OpenMP hybrid modes and allows models to move from laptops to workstations, clouds, and supercomputers with minimal code changes.

TeraAgent IO serializes agent object trees directly into contiguous buffers and restores objects from received buffers without separate deserialization allocations. It retains mutability, avoids pointer deduplication, endian conversion, and schema evolution, and intercepts deletion to manage buffer memory safely. Delta encoding exploits gradual changes between iterations to reduce transferred data; when combined with LZ4 compression, it further reduces message sizes.

Evaluations using cell clustering, cell proliferation, epidemiology, and oncology simulations produced results matching BioDynaMo and passed 180 automated tests. TeraAgent simulated 501.51 billion agents on 84,096 CPU cores, 250 times more than BioDynaMo. It achieved an eightfold higher agent update rate per core than Biocellion and 39-fold faster in-situ visualization. Median serialization and deserialization speedups were 110× and 37×, respectively, while delta encoding reduced required transfers by up to 3.5×. Compression accelerated distribution operations by up to 11×, although agent reordering overhead limited overall gains on the supercomputer’s low-latency interconnect. Strong scaling was effective to eight nodes before load imbalance dominated, while weak scaling reached a runtime plateau.

The paper proposes a model-based geostatistical (MBG) approach to design cost-efficient soil-transmitted helminth impact assessment surveys. It combines baseline prevalence data, preventive chemotherapy coverage history, school or community locations, and optional environmental and population covariates to map baseline prevalence, project future prevalence through a five-state Markov model and local thinning, and simulate optimized survey designs. The method was applied in Kenya, Zimbabwe, and Sierra Leone, with transition parameters estimated from repeated Kenyan surveys and existing impact surveys used as the evaluation standard. Projected impact prevalence closely matched observed prevalence in Kenya but showed larger discrepancies in Zimbabwe and Sierra Leone, partly because their endemicity levels differed. MBG survey designs matched the accuracy of classical random-sampling surveys while using substantially fewer schools and children, producing an average estimated cost reduction of 80%: 91% in Zimbabwe, 86% in Kenya, and 62% in Sierra Leone. The approach also generates detailed prevalence maps that may identify residual hotspots, and the authors are developing a manual and web application for implementation.

National home prices rose 7.1% year over year and 1.1% month over month in May 2018. CoreLogic cited limited housing supply, especially entry-level homes, and homeowners retaining low-rate mortgages. In the 100 largest metropolitan areas, 40% were overvalued, 26% undervalued and 34% at value. National home prices were forecast to increase 5.1% by May 2019.

The disclosure describes a vehicle vision and driver-monitoring system using exterior and interior cameras, vehicle sensor data, and an electronic control unit to process images, detect objects, display images, and assist or alert the driver.

Driver attention is estimated from a maximum workload, driving workload, and distraction workload. The maximum workload is initialized to a predetermined value and may be adjusted using driver information such as age and experience. Distraction workload may be based on media-system use, steering behavior, gaze direction, and other signs of visual distraction. Driving workload may incorporate vehicle controls, in-cabin observations of visual driving and drowsiness, driver situational awareness, ADAS information, traffic and road complexity, weather, driving duration, and time of day. Weighted driving and distraction workloads are subtracted from the maximum workload to produce an attention value, which may be expressed as a percentage from zero to one hundred. The weights and calibration values can be adjusted during testing, operation, or through machine learning.

Driver-state inputs may include identity, driving behavior and style, posture, facial expressions, voice, biometrics, focus, environmental conditions, climate-control use, audio, and entertainment activity. Passenger behavior may also be monitored to refine driver estimates.

Inputs and outputs can include states, confidence levels, availability values, and adjustable calibration weights or functions. Detected vehicles, pedestrians, or other hazards may be displayed with alerts or overlays. If the driver is not attentive to a detected hazard and its risk exceeds a threshold, the system may autonomously brake or steer to avoid it. The system may also use radar, lidar, ultrasonic sensors, ADAS, and vehicle-to-vehicle or vehicle-to-infrastructure communications. In autonomous or semi-autonomous vehicles, an occupant capable of taking control is treated as the driver.

Alere said its 2013-2015 financial statements should not be relied upon due to revenue-recognition misstatements in South Korea and Japan, without changing transaction revenue totals. It expects additional control weaknesses and may need more time to file its March-quarter Form 10-Q.

Shonda Rhimes and Shondaland have signed a deal to create new shows for Netflix, while “Grey’s Anatomy,” “Scandal” and “How to Get Away With Murder” remain on ABC. Financial terms and the deal’s duration were not disclosed.

The American Academy of Pediatrics says five tests commonly ordered for short, overweight or early-pubertal children may be unnecessary when the child is otherwise healthy and follows an expected growth curve. It urges selective, evidence-based testing for hormone and endocrine disorders, vitamin D deficiency, thyroid problems in obese children, and thyroid abnormalities, with attention to each test’s specific indications.

Several women detained at T. Don Hutto Residential Center in Taylor, Texas, wrote letters describing separation from their children and harsh conditions in immigration holding facilities. An anonymous woman said she and others were confined in chain-link cages she called “la perrera,” slept on floors under aluminum-paper blankets, and went eight days without bathing or brushing their teeth. She was separated from her children and learned their whereabouts 21 days later.

Grassroots Leadership circulated the letters and a petition seeking release and family reunification. Other letters conveyed maternal anguish, including messages from Mirian and a Guatemalan mother to her five-year-old son. Claudia said she was separated from her son at criminal court and described their suffering.
