He rejects geographical sectional parties and argues that abolitionist organizations, though claiming to oppose slavery’s expansion, seek to alter the domestic institutions of existing states through unconstitutional and revolutionary means. He identifies three stages in this sectional conflict: agitation for emancipation in the South, resistance to the Fugitive Slave Act, and disputes over restrictions on slavery in territories and new states. He argues that the Supreme Court had established that Congress could not impose such restrictions and that the repeal of the Missouri Compromise’s slavery line was not a breach of a binding compact. Kansas-Nebraska legislation instead allowed settlers to establish new states under popular sovereignty.

The President attributes Kansas’s disturbances primarily to outside sectional intervention rather than territorial self-government. He reports that revolutionary efforts to create a rival government failed, armed groups were expelled or dispersed, and the use of federal military forces restored order without bloodshed. He maintains that the president has no authority to supervise the legality of territorial elections and urges Congress or Kansas’s legislature to remove any unconstitutional laws and protect citizens’ rights.

Government finances are reported as improving. Customs receipts exceeded $64 million, total receipts reached $73,918,141, and public debt had fallen to $30,963,909, though much could not yet be called because it was not due. The President urges reducing annual customs revenue to approximately $48–50 million, distributing taxation more equally, and strengthening controls over public funds and official records.

The Army remained heavily engaged against hostile Indians but was providing greater frontier security; further organizational reforms, troop redistribution, and increased military armament are recommended. The Navy had improved in personnel, discipline, ordnance, and ships, leading to support for additional frigates and further naval expansion. Public-land sales and surveys are cited as evidence of western development. The Post Office recorded expenditures exceeding receipts by $2,787,046 because of expanded mail service and railroad transportation, prompting recommendations concerning franking, steamship routes, and contracts for carrying mail.

In foreign affairs, the President reports generally amicable relations. Negotiations with Great Britain address Central American transit routes, fisheries, and expanded trade, while efforts to resolve Danish Sound dues continue. Unresolved issues remain with Spain and Cuba. The United States proposed that neutral flags cover enemy goods except contraband and that neutral property aboard belligerent vessels be exempt from capture, and endorsed the Paris Declaration’s effective-blockade rule. It supported abolishing privateering only if amended to exempt belligerent private property at sea from capture; Russia approved the amendment, and favorable responses were reported from France and other maritime powers.

The President also addresses instability in Latin America. He sought redress from Mexico for injuries to American citizens and delayed recognizing competing authorities in Nicaragua because the legitimate government remained uncertain. New Granada’s proposed tonnage and mail taxes violated treaty and contract rights, while a violent attack in Panama killed Americans and destroyed railroad property. He demanded punishment and full indemnity, stationed naval forces at Panama and Aspinwall to protect Americans and transit routes, and began negotiations for lasting security.

The message closes by presenting the United States as peaceful, prosperous, and internationally respected. It characterizes the current generation’s task as maintaining and extending national power, responsibly conducting foreign relations, and managing domestic political tensions before the President transfers the executive office to his successor.

The Texas Rangers and Bruce Bochy mutually agreed to end his three-year tenure after the club finished 81-81, its first .500 season, following a 2023 World Series championship and two consecutive losing seasons. Bochy went 249-237 with Texas and was offered an advisory front-office role. He recently said he still loved managing.

At 70, Bochy was baseball’s winningest active manager, with 2,252 career wins, sixth all-time, and four World Series titles. Former Marlins manager Skip Schumaker was considered a potential replacement, though no search discussions had occurred. The Rangers led MLB in ERA at 3.47 and set a single-season fielding-percentage record, but injuries and a late collapse eliminated them from playoff contention. Elsewhere, San Francisco fired Bob Melvin after a fourth consecutive missed postseason, while Minnesota dismissed Rocco Baldelli after seven seasons that included three AL Central titles but only one playoff appearance in his final five years.

U.S. Treasury yields fell sharply after President Donald Trump said he wanted interest rates to remain low and called the dollar “too strong.” The 10-year yield reached a five-month low of 2.22%, while a flatter yield curve pressured bank stocks. The dollar reversed an early decline to end slightly higher. European equities fell, with banks declining more than 1%, while Asian stocks rose on strong Chinese trade data and Trump’s statement that China was not manipulating its currency. Trump also declined to rule out renominating Federal Reserve Chair Janet Yellen. Oil rose modestly, and gold remained near a five-month high.

Cover 3 uses four underneath droppers and three deep defenders, with the free safety closing the middle in a MOFC shell. It limits vertical routes, allows defensive disguises, and helps defenders add to the run fit, but leaves seams and flats vulnerable. Offenses can attack these areas with quick-game throws, RPOs, four-vertical concepts, and flood concepts. Quick passes and RPOs exploit flat defenders and outside linebackers, while route combinations such as slant/flat and dig/whip target bailing cornerbacks. Flood concepts overload field-side zones. Examples from Ole Miss, Michigan, Oklahoma, and BYU illustrate Dagger, square out-seam, Y-cross, and post-wheel concepts against Cover 3.

The article backtests the NR7 narrow-range volatility strategy on SPY, entering during periods of low daily trading-range volatility. The original strategy produced a 7.8% CAGR, 899 trades, a 0.27% average gain per trade, and a 25% maximum drawdown, which the authors considered inadequate for a multi-day holding period. Adding one undisclosed entry parameter while retaining the exit rule raised the average gain to 0.46%, reduced maximum drawdown to 13%, and significantly reduced the number of trades. Sixty-seven percent of improved trades occurred when the close exceeded the previous day’s close. Because NR7 enters during low volatility rather than buying weakness, it may diversify mean-reversion strategies. The authors also caution against excessive optimization and faulty quote data, and offer AmiBroker and TradeStation EasyLanguage code for the free version.

The case examines the causes of the 2008 financial crisis and proposed responses. The collapse of the U.S. housing market triggered a worldwide economic crisis: falling home values and rising mortgage defaults left smaller lenders and mortgage companies holding risky loans they could no longer sell. As banks failed and credit markets froze, lending to individuals and businesses largely stopped.

The housing boom was fueled by rising prices, relaxed lending standards, subprime mortgages, and heavy household borrowing. Home prices grew rapidly while incomes remained flat, and household debt rose from 50% of GDP in the 1980s to 100% by the mid-2000s. Investors extracted roughly $2 trillion in housing equity through loans, refinancing, and sales. Mortgage-backed securities and credit default swaps spread mortgage risk throughout the financial system.

Several structural developments facilitated the crisis. The repeal of Glass-Steagall in 1999 and the Commodity Futures Modernization Act in 2000 weakened regulation, expanded shadow banking, and allowed complex derivatives to proliferate. Financial institutions became highly leveraged and “too big to fail.” A growing global pool of investment capital, including money from emerging markets, generated intense demand for mortgage-backed securities and contributed to the loosening of mortgage standards. Wall Street’s political contributions and revolving personnel ties with government also gave large financial institutions substantial influence.

Andrew Lo emphasized a human dimension to the crisis. Prosperity encouraged complacency, excessive risk tolerance, and greed; collapse then produced fear and uncertainty. Banks’ reluctance to mark down their assets and widespread liquidity runs intensified the crisis by causing even solvent banks to withhold short-term credit from one another. Simon Johnson instead emphasized the role of a banking “oligarchy,” arguing that politically powerful elites made increasingly large, government-backed gambles. David Beim emphasized decades of overborrowing and rising living standards that households could no longer sustain.

Responsibilities were widely disputed among bank executives and quantitative analysts, regulators, politicians, hedge funds, government-sponsored enterprises, lenders, investors, and homeowners. Regulators faced criticism for permissive leverage rules and insufficient expertise, while Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac were criticized for lowering credit standards.

The Bush and Obama administrations responded with TARP assistance, restrictions on executive compensation, a $500 billion Public Private Investment Program to purchase toxic assets, and stress tests of 19 major banks. Ten banks were ordered to raise $75 billion in capital. Critics, including Johnson, argued that the bank-by-bank approach reflected political influence and did not adequately restore lending. Johnson proposed a systematic government-managed bankruptcy program that would separate toxic assets, divide healthy banks into smaller entities, and eventually return them to private ownership while protecting deposits.

For future crises, Lo recommended greater transparency, confidential regulatory reporting by large hedge funds, a Capital Markets Safety Board to investigate failures and systemic risk, accounting methods that explicitly measure risk, and stronger corporate governance. His proposals included placing quantitative experts on executive and boards, making risk officers independent and responsible for stability rather than profits, reducing corporate political contributions, and expanding finance education and financial-technology research. By spring 2009, the value of toxic assets, effects of consumer debt, effectiveness of government rescues, and likelihood of future crises remained uncertain.

The passage argues that the United States entered the war largely to defend national rights and honor and was initially unprepared mentally and militarily. It frames the conflict as a test of popular government’s capacity for self-defense and a commitment to freedom and international relationships. The decision to fight is final regardless of setbacks involving Russia, Italy, France, or England. The United States must continue until it has secured a safe nation and renewed true American citizenship.

Britain’s SIG Plc appointed Ernst & Young LLP as external auditor amid an FRC investigation into Deloitte’s audits of SIG’s 2015 and 2016 accounts. SIG is reviewing historical accounts after profit-overstating allegations while maintaining full-year underlying profit expectations.

Canada’s S&P/TSX composite index gained 15.03 points, or 0.10%, to 15,801.06, setting a seventh consecutive record high led by financial services after strong Canadian and U.S. data. U.S. indexes opened nearly unchanged as upbeat economic data supported prospects of a rate hike; the Dow was flat while the S&P 500 and Nasdaq edged lower. Fed Chair Janet Yellen said delaying a hike would be unwise but gave no timing. Strong retail sales and inflation figures helped fuel four consecutive record closes on Wall Street. Oil fell below $56 per barrel after API data showed U.S. crude inventories unexpectedly rose 9.9 million barrels, raising concerns about OPEC-led production cuts despite strong overall compliance.

North Wales Police’s summer campaign, launched June 14 alongside the Football World Cup, made 95 arrests in just over two weeks: 55 for drink-driving and 40 for drug-driving. Convicted drivers may receive at least a 12-month disqualification and heavy fines. Police urged residents to report suspected impaired drivers via 101 or Crimestoppers.

Before a must-win game, the speaker says the series has been close and the team is down but staying positive. Scoring is hard despite sustained pressure and blocked shots; they plan shots on net, high rebounds, and applying pressure, expecting breaks as in the Rangers series, won despite two shutouts.

CMB BC defeated March Town 3–2 in the Ivan Henson Memorial Trophy final, winning singles and fours but losing pairs and triples, with overall shots 66–62. In the annual ladies-versus-men match, the ladies won 20–16 (163–157), leading by two entering round six.

The study develops and evaluates 1D non-LTE corrections for neodymium abundances in metal-poor FGK stars, where LTE analyses may bias inferred r-process enrichment. A new Nd I/Nd II model atom was assembled from experimental atomic data, including 268 Nd I levels, 556 Nd II levels, bound–bound transitions, and collisional data. The atom was calibrated against solar Nd abundances, used to model HD222925 and other metal-poor stars, and validated through synthetic spectra generated with MULTI2.3 and TS-NLTE. Tests showed that adding higher-energy theoretical levels and hyperfine/isotopic data had negligible effects on the derived corrections.

Using the model atom with MULTI2.3 and MARCS atmospheres, the authors derived LTE and NLTE abundances for Nd II lines in benchmark stars and constructed a six-dimensional grid of corrections spanning temperature, surface gravity, metallicity, microturbulence, LTE Nd abundance, and wavelength. The grid included 122 previously observed optical and near-infrared lines and 54,450 model calculations. Linear interpolation reproduced directly calculated corrections with a mean difference of 0.001 dex.

Across the grid, NLTE corrections ranged from approximately −0.3 to +0.5 dex and depended strongly on stellar parameters, Nd abundance, excitation potential, and wavelength. Optical-line corrections were generally positive, reaching the largest values for blue, low-excitation lines in cool, metal-poor giants. Typical corrections were about +0.1 dex in main-sequence stars and roughly +0.2 dex in red giants at lower Nd abundances, declining toward zero as Nd abundance increased. Near-infrared H-band corrections were generally negative, reaching about −0.3 dex for some warm giants. Departure coefficients indicate that upper-level overpopulation largely drives the positive optical corrections.

The study recommends applying 1D NLTE rather than LTE abundances, particularly for blue lines in metal-poor giants, and using moderate- or high-excitation lines when possible. It also notes that uncorrected 3D atmospheric effects may contribute to remaining line-by-line trends and calls for further analysis of other neutron-capture elements and expanded stellar parameter ranges.

At his first major rally since becoming Ontario Progressive Conservative leader, Doug Ford told nearly 2,000 supporters he plans to “take back” the province and build a majority government by attracting Liberal and NDP voters through opposition to Premier Kathleen Wynne. He criticized Wynne’s management of provincial finances and the throne speech’s spending promises, proposing tax and hydro-rate cuts, regulatory rollback, a business-friendly climate, manufacturing jobs, and development of northern resources and the Ring of Fire. Supporters praised Ford’s personality and fiscal positions, including opposition to the proposed carbon tax; some also supported his call for reviewing sexual education. The rally featured the three leadership candidates he defeated. The contest followed Patrick Brown’s resignation amid sexual-harassment allegations he denied.

A player credits his longtime NHL coach, whose French background has made communication easier, with valuable guidance and reminders that contributed to his success. He says adding veteran goalie John, previously a frequent opponent and one of the league’s best, reassured the team, and John has handled his backup role well. In the playoffs, he emphasizes staying positive and focused, reviewing tape, and adjusting to opponents’ strategies. Despite an early power-play goal by the opposition, strong penalty-killing helped his team respond. He values special teams, open communication, and his coach’s experience and confidence in him.

The Mets rallied from a 4-1 deficit to beat the Cubs 9-4, taking two of three games. Curtis Granderson’s 300th home run highlighted a five-run eighth inning that included Lucas Duda’s three-run homer and T.J. Rivera’s RBI single. Juan Lagares tied the game with a sixth-inning triple.

Matt Harvey surrendered three homers in four innings and said his arm was not working; he plans to see a doctor. The Mets also lost Neil Walker to a left-leg injury, while the Cubs’ Ben Zobrist remained sidelined with a wrist injury. Anthony Rizzo and Kyle Schwarber homered for Chicago, which dropped six of eight games and continued to play sloppily. New York improved to 30-34 and won five of six overall, earning a standing ovation for Granderson. Upcoming games include the Mets hosting Washington and the Cubs visiting Pittsburgh.

The passage defines the Guest-Hypervisor Communication Block (GHCB) protocol for SEV-ES and SEV-SNP guests. The 4 KB, page-aligned GHCB must be mapped decrypted or shared so the guest and hypervisor can exchange data. Its format mirrors the SEV-ES VMCB save-state area through offset 0x3ff, but only fields required for VMGEXIT processing are included to limit exposed guest state.

Protocol version 2 adds hypervisor feature advertisement through a 52-bit bitmap, enables independent evolution of SEV-ES and SEV-SNP, and includes XSS MSR reporting, restricted APIC emulation, and shared-buffer requirements. Revision 2.01 updates SNP guest-request sequence numbers to 64 bits and documents malformed-GHCB errors. Revision 2.02 adds the VLEK GUID and error reporting through the upper 32 bits of SW_EXITINFO2. Revision 2.03 adds APIC-ID retrieval, multiple VMPL levels, and SEV-ES page-state notifications. Revision 2.04 adds SEV-TIO, Secure AVIC, and another GHCB MSR protocol function.

The guest specifies the GHCB’s guest-physical address through MSR 0xc001_0130; hardware saves and restores it through VMCB offset 0xa0, and hypervisors must not intercept that MSR. The lower 12 bits of the MSR encode protocol requests, including feature support, SEV information, CPUID retrieval, preferred or registered GHCB addresses, page-state changes, VMPL changes, and GHCB unregistration. SNP guests must register a GHCB GPA before first use, and the hypervisor must ensure the page is hypervisor-owned and shared. An example negotiation covers obtaining the protocol-version range and page-table encryption bit, establishing the GHCB, and registering its GPA.

NAE events generate #VC exceptions in SEV-ES guests. Guests inspect the exception, place required state in the GHCB, and execute VMGEXIT; hypervisors process the event and return results in the same structure. Guests and hypervisors must reset and set VALID_BITMAP to identify valid fields. Standard processing requires SW_EXITCODE, SW_EXITINFO1, and SW_EXITINFO2 from the guest, with SW_EXITINFO1 and SW_EXITINFO2 returned by the hypervisor. Nonzero SW_EXITINFO1 indicates an error, including malformed input, invalid VALID_BITMAP data, unregistered SNP GHCB addresses, invalid SW_SCRATCH values, or other invalid event input.

Supported events include IOIO and MSR protection, MMIO reads and writes, page-state changes, SNP guest and extended guest requests, AP creation, #HV doorbell management, #HV IPIs and timers, APIC-ID lists, SNP Run VMPL, SNP TIO guest requests, Secure AVIC backing-page management, and termination requests. SNP guest requests use separate shared request and response pages and pass through firmware. Extended requests can return certificates identified by GUID. Page-state requests describe private, shared, PSMASH, and UNSMASH operations and maintain progress in shared structures so processing can resume after interruption. AP creation can add, update, or remove vCPU state and enables SNP vCPU hotplug. Secure AVIC registers or unregisters a private APIC backing page for each vCPU.

The SNP Secrets Page reserves 96 bytes for guest use, including VMPL-specific 64-bit message-sequence numbers, an AP jump-table address, and guest-defined storage. Firmware can pass Secrets and CPUID pages to the OS through the EFI SEV-SNP Confidential Computing Blob protocol.

SMP boot procedures differ for SEV-ES and SEV-SNP because measured vCPU register state cannot normally be changed. SEV-ES uses AP Reset Hold requests and an encrypted AP jump table, while SEV-SNP can use the AP Creation event to supply VMSA state. NMI delivery requires interception of #DB but not IRET. Hardware debug-register virtualization is supported when enabled; otherwise DR7 accesses are intercepted and cached. SMM and nested virtualization are unsupported.

With Restricted Injection, host notifications use a shared #HV doorbell page containing PendingEvent and NoEoiRequired fields. The host presents interrupt vectors and non-maskable events, emulates APIC ready, acknowledgment, in-service, and EOI behavior, and delivers #HV notifications as required. The guest atomically exchanges PendingEvent with zero before acting on an interrupt and uses atomic exchanges for EOI handling, while validating vectors because a non-cooperative host may corrupt the shared page.

The speaker thanks President Clinton and Vice President Gore, describes America’s peaceful transfer of power and enduring ideals of freedom, democracy, equality, and opportunity, and pledges to build a nation of justice and opportunity. He says these ideals must be enacted through civility, courage, compassion, and personal responsibility, supported by government, schools, religious institutions, charity, and active citizenship. He warns that political disputes have serious consequences for freedom, education, the economy, and the vulnerable. His proposed actions include reforming schools, Social Security, and Medicare; reducing taxes; strengthening defenses; confronting weapons of mass destruction; defending allies and interests; and addressing poverty and hopelessness. He emphasizes that government cannot replace the public spirit of citizens and that service, moral character, and community responsibility are essential. Concluding that the nation’s purpose is renewed through service to others, he calls for a more just and generous country that affirms the dignity of every life.

The release of “Fifty Shades Darker” has boosted interest in bondage lingerie, prompting physical retailers to capitalize while online sites continue to dominate sales. Coco de Mer launched an official collection with E.L. James, Ann Summers promoted bondage-themed products, and Taylor Swift wore lingerie styling in a film-related video. Ann Summers’ online bondage sales rose over 42%, Bondara’s averaged a 30% increase, and overall online sex toy, bondage and lingerie sales grew 62% since 2014.

In July 2020, the NHL and NHLPA negotiated a return-to-play plan for the COVID-19-interrupted 2019–20 season and an extension of their collective bargaining agreement through 2025–26. The 2013 CBA, adopted after a 113-day lockout, set player compensation at 50% of league revenue, with revenue-sharing payments to players if compensation was below that share and salary clawbacks if it exceeded it. Negotiations therefore required agreement on measuring league revenue and player compensation and on the revenue split. Players chose agent Emilie Castonguay as lead negotiator; owners chose Commissioner Gary Bettman. Revenue-sharing considerations included ticket sales, national broadcasting rights, arena concessions, player salaries, signing bonuses, deferred salary, and contract buyouts. Castonguay favored calculations showing higher league revenue or lower player compensation, while Bettman’s interests pointed the opposite way. Both recognized that extreme positions could prompt demands for a split other than 50/50, while the absence of a timely agreement could again cancel games and reduce associated beer sales.

Green Monday laptop deals range from an ultra-budget HP Laptop 14t ($190, $110 off MSRP) to a gaming 14-inch Razer Blade ($1,600, $200 off). Other offers include HP’s $700 Envy x360 convertible ($170 off), a $380 Dell I3567-3964BLK ($140 off), and a $330 Lenovo 14-inch touchscreen 2-in-1 ($70 off). The Envy has a 1080p touchscreen, Core i5, 8GB RAM and 1TB storage; the Razer has a 1080p display, Core i7, 16GB RAM, SSD and GTX 1060; the HP 14t has 4GB RAM and 32GB storage; the Dell has 8GB RAM and 2TB storage; and the Lenovo has 4GB RAM and 500GB storage. The Georgia Supreme Court affirmed James Johnson’s conviction and life sentence for murdering his father, J. A. Johnson, following a retrial after the first conviction was reversed for legal error. The court rejected Johnson’s objection to jurors who had previously been struck or excused because he did not identify the jurors or the grounds for challenge and showed no legal disqualification. It upheld the admission of evidence that Johnson discussed his father’s life insurance and money and sought assistance obtaining the money after the killing, finding that his statements could indicate his impressions and possible motive even though he was not shown to be a beneficiary. The court also upheld the jury instruction addressing Johnson’s concession that his father was killed and the killing was murder, while denying that he was responsible. The evidence supported the verdict, and no other grounds for a new trial showed error.

An NPR/Marist poll finds that 1 in 5 American jobs is held by a worker under contract, with contractors and freelancers projected to make up half the workforce within a decade; 30 percent of Americans hold a second job for pay. Emily Doherty, 28, a full-time museum worker in Virginia, performs as a Colonial-era reenactor at living-history museums and national parks to cover living costs and a $500 monthly student loan payment, working as many as four hours on weeknights and eight on weekends, which costs her time with friends and family. She plans to save for a summer flight to Maine to see her sister perform. Student loan debt totals nearly $1.4 trillion, according to the Federal Reserve Bank of New York. Jon Jacobs, 31, a substance addiction therapist in Milwaukee, left a bartending side job for Lyft driving to spend more time with his young children, accepting lower pay. University of Chicago professor Susan Lambert notes such workers face tough choices between extra jobs and family time.

The Ninth Circuit granted Harnek Singh’s petition in part and remanded to the BIA to consider his credibility challenge and his asylum and withholding claims, which the Government conceded had not been considered. The court did not reach his torture claim. It granted Baljinder Kaur’s petition and remanded, accepting her testimony as credible.

Scientists from Germany, Italy and the Czech Republic created the first hybrid embryos using frozen northern white rhino sperm and southern white rhino eggs. With only two females, Najin and Fatu, remaining and both unable to reproduce, researchers plan to harvest their eggs, combine them with preserved sperm to create pure northern white rhino embryos, and implant them in southern white rhino surrogates. They are also developing a method to turn frozen skin cells into eggs to expand genetic diversity. Researchers hope for a northern white rhino birth within three years and new eggs from skin cells within a decade, though egg harvesting could endanger the females and requires Kenyan approval. Conservationists have criticized the costly, uncertain effort as diverting attention from four other rhino species they consider more threatened.

The team denied fatigue, citing the opponent’s puck management. After the second goal, they grew frustrated, left their system and took penalties before regaining their game in the third. They expect their goaltender to bounce back.

An email chain forwards a Texas Monthly article, “How Enron Blew It” by Mimi Swartz, examining Enron’s rise and abrupt decline.

Under Ken Lay and CEO Jeff Skilling, Enron evolved from a pipeline company into a trading powerhouse after natural-gas deregulation. Skilling’s “Gas Bank” concept allowed Enron to contractually guarantee gas supply and prices, take ownership of trading risks, and profit from transactions. Enron soon dominated gas trading and expanded into electricity, commodities, broadband trading, and online commerce. Revenue rose from $40 billion to $100 billion between 1985 and 2000, while the stock increased 1,700 percent.

Skilling built a knowledge-based culture around exceptionally intelligent, aggressive, and ambitious employees. Enron recruited heavily, offered uncapped performance bonuses and extensive perks, and encouraged extreme productivity. It also created an inward-looking, highly competitive environment marked by forced ranking, surveillance, confidentiality agreements, paranoia, and regular workforce turnover. Employees described Enron as a collection of mercenaries, while Skilling’s intense focus on intellectual capital and results led him to minimize concerns about longer-term consequences.

Enron emphasized rapid profits and short market horizons. It applied mark-to-market accounting on an unprecedented scale, booked long-term profits immediately, and sometimes abandoned projects when expected margins declined. Rebecca Mark, who had overseen Enron International, was moved to run Azurix after conflicts over Enron’s global power-plant projects; Azurix subsequently struggled and was folded back into Enron.

After Skilling became CEO in February 2001, Enron faced mounting problems. It was criticized for its role in California’s electricity crisis, while its Indian power project remained costly. The telecommunications investment collapsed with the technology bubble, analysts questioned its accounting and profits, and executive stock sales further damaged investor confidence. Enron’s stock fell from $80 in January to around $35 by October.

Skilling resigned abruptly after six months as CEO, returning Lay to the position. Lay promised a kinder company focused more closely on its core business and reconsidered practices such as forced employee rankings. The article portrays Enron’s aggressive culture, risk-taking, and pursuit of short-term profits as central to its decline, while ending with Skilling expressing confidence in future technology and commodity trading.

The volume documents the intellectual assumptions and themes underlying the Reagan administration’s foreign policy rather than major decisions or diplomatic exchanges. Drawing on public statements, interviews, testimony, memoranda, correspondence, meeting minutes, and other records from the eight-year administration, it samples documents concerning Reagan, George H.W. Bush, Alexander Haig, George Shultz, national security advisers, Caspar Weinburger, Jeane Kirkpatrick, and influential State Department and National Security Council staff. Themes include resetting U.S. foreign policy, promoting a world order hospitable to U.S. values, pursuing activist bipartisan foreign policy, and developing a restrained, reciprocal U.S.-Soviet relationship. Footnotes identify sources, classification, distribution, drafting details, and whether senior officials read each document; editorial notes provide context and related sources. The index lists document numbers. A 2018–2022 declassification review withheld no documents, made no excisions of a paragraph or more, and made minor excisions in three documents.

This retrospective observational study examined whether serum cardiac troponin T (cTnT) reflects respiratory dysfunction in ALS. It analyzed routine clinical data from a Bonn discovery cohort (297 patients; 96 with pulmonary function tests) and a smaller Essen validation cohort (49 patients), with serum neurofilament light chain (NfL) available in a subset.

cTnT was elevated in 65% of Bonn patients and 47% of Essen patients. Levels correlated negatively with total ALSFRSr and its respiratory domain. They were also inversely associated with FVC, SVC, FEV1, and PEF, with adjusted regression confirming associations for FVC, SVC, and FEV1; the SVC association was reproduced in the validation cohort. ROC analyses showed that cTnT could identify clinically important pulmonary impairment, including SVC or FVC below 80% and PEF below 75%, with proposed cutoffs of 14.0–17.8 ng/L. In contrast, NfL correlated with total ALSFRSr but not with respiratory function or pulmonary parameters.

The authors suggest that elevated cTnT in ALS may reflect degeneration or remodeling of respiratory skeletal muscle and could complement neurofilament testing. However, the observational design, small validation cohort, possible pulmonary test measurement errors, and lack of confirmed significance for every validation result limit causal conclusions. Prospective studies are needed to clarify the mechanism and assess cTnT responses to interventions such as non-invasive ventilation.

In June 2017, Ryshonda Harper Beechem became Pelahatchie, Mississippi’s first Black mayor, winning a no-runoff election by 12 votes. She is also the first Black mayor of the surrounding majority-white county. Since taking office, her relationship with the five-member, racially diverse Board of Aldermen has become publicly hostile. The board has made sudden rule and staffing changes without consulting her and frequently overturned her vetoes. Most notably, it cut her salary by 75% from $12,000 to $250 per month while also halving aldermen’s pay. Beechem, an accountant who maintains that the budget did not require the reduction, vetoed the cut and cited “no confidence” amid a state auditor’s investigation into alleged misuse of town funds. Three clerks resigned in early 2018, contributing to further staffing disputes. Residents debate the conflict online, with some citing financial concerns, others criticizing Beechem, and some alleging racism.

This prospective longitudinal study used NET-QUBIC data to assess whether the COVID-19 pandemic altered health-related quality of life (HRQOL) among head and neck cancer survivors from 24 to 36 months after treatment and whether patient characteristics moderated these effects. The analysis included 318 survivors: 199 whose 36-month questionnaires were completed before March 14, 2020, and 119 completed during the pandemic. Measures covered disease- and tumor-specific HRQOL, physical activity, distress, anxiety, depression, fear of cancer recurrence, and loneliness.

Overall, no statistically significant differences in HRQOL changes were found between the pre-pandemic and pandemic groups. Exploratory analyses identified moderating factors for 31 of 46 outcomes. Key subgroup findings included worsening physical activity among women, worsening appetite loss among survivors receiving multimodality treatment, worsening swallowing among those with moderate or severe comorbidity, and worsening fear of recurrence among survivors with a lifetime major depressive disorder. Survivors living alone reported reduced painkiller use, while those with disease progression reported reduced financial problems. A different emotional-loneliness trajectory was also found among survivors with above-median BMI.

Limitations include that all participants completed primary treatment before the pandemic, some covariates were measured only at baseline, numerous outcomes created a risk of chance findings, and participants’ COVID-19 infection status was unknown. Included survivors also had lower comorbidity and less frequent lifetime major depression than excluded survivors. The authors concluded that the pandemic did not generally affect HRQOL trajectories but did affect specific subgroups, supporting individualized supportive care.

The paper introduces Text2MBL, a framework that converts textual design descriptions into BIM-based modular building layouts through fine-grained, action-level code executed over sequential steps. It addresses modular construction’s constrained, standardized design space, the need to incorporate user preferences, and the difficulty of producing semantically structured BIM models without error-prone image-to-BIM conversion.

Text2MBL formalizes modular layouts using Modules, Units, Rooms, and architectural elements, with adjacency, connectivity, co-location, and hierarchical containment relationships. Its proof-of-concept implementation extends Autodesk Revit through the C# API using object-oriented Module, Unit, Room, and utility classes that encapsulate module creation, splitting and merging, unit initialization, room placement, doors, holes, and geometric operations. The representation reframes text-to-layout design as sequence-to-sequence code generation.

The authors curated 198 real-world modular housing designs, annotating each with executable BIM action code and two independently written descriptions using named or positional coding styles. Qwen2.5-family language models were fine-tuned to map text to modular layouts and evaluated for executable validity, semantic fidelity, and geometric consistency.

The article explains the football route tree, a long-used system for organizing and teaching pass routes. Because teams have more routes than available single-digit labels, each team’s route tree may differ. Although route trees were historically used to call plays, they are now primarily teaching tools.

Several quick routes help quarterbacks throw rapidly to open receivers. The hitch route stops at 5–6 yards, while the slant breaks inward at about 45 degrees, often after a short release. The quick out breaks toward the sideline at roughly five yards, and the stick route attacks the middle against zone coverage or breaks away against man coverage.

Horizontal routes include the flat, whip, drag, and shallow cross. These are generally used within concepts to stretch coverage, create mismatches or rubs, and provide opportunities for receivers to catch the ball in motion.

The option, or choice, route gives receivers multiple paths according to the defense’s reaction. It is difficult to cover but requires extensive practice and precise coordination between quarterback and receiver.

Deep routes include the go route down the sideline and the seam route through the space between linebackers and safeties. The corner and post routes break toward the sideline and goal posts, respectively, while the square out breaks sharply outside at 10–12 yards. The dig route breaks into the middle at 10–15 yards, and the curl turns back toward the quarterback at a similar intermediate depth. The comeback route releases downfield before breaking toward the sideline, demanding exact timing.

The post-corner combines a post and corner, initially appearing to break inward before the receiver redirects outside to exploit an aggressive defender. Overall, the article describes each route’s depth, movement, coverage matchups, timing requirements, and common uses in passing concepts, run-pass options, and team offenses.

Paralyzed Veterans of America thanked Deputy Secretary Tom Bowman for his 30 years in the Marine Corps and subsequent service on Capitol Hill and at the Department of Veterans Affairs, and wished him well in retirement. The organization said it looks forward to continuing its work with the VA under Acting Secretary Peter O'Rourke, noting that implementation of the recently passed VA MISSION Act remains one of its highest priorities, and expressed hope that the revolving door in leadership will not hamper those efforts. Paralyzed Veterans is the only congressionally chartered veterans service organization focused solely on veterans with spinal cord injury or disease; for more than 70 years it has secured veterans' earned benefits, monitored care in VA spinal cord injury units, funded research and education toward a cure, developed training and career services, promoted accessibility, provided sports and recreation programs, and advocated for veterans and people with disabilities. With more than 70 offices and 33 chapters, it serves veterans, families, and caregivers in all 50 states, the District of Columbia, and Puerto Rico.

A Markov state-transition model using Brazilian evidence evaluated one-time Mycobacterium tuberculosis infection screening and tuberculosis preventive treatment (TPT) for formerly incarcerated individuals. TST and IGRA tests were combined with 1HP, 3HP, 4R, or 9H regimens and compared with no screening and passive TB diagnosis. Outcomes included lifetime TB cases, deaths, disability-adjusted life years (DALYs), and costs from a TB program perspective.

All strategies were cost-effective relative to no screening at the study’s $6,300–$9,700 per DALY threshold. TST with 3HP cost $242 per DALY averted and was estimated to prevent 31 TB cases and 4.1 TB deaths per 1,000 people. IGRA with 1HP produced the greatest health gains but higher incremental costs; the preferred strategy remained uncertain. Benefits and cost-effectiveness were greatest among younger individuals, those with longer incarceration histories, and those screened soon after release, although every subgroup examined remained cost-effective. Results were robust to parameter uncertainty and reinfection rates up to 50 times the general-population rate. Limitations included no explicit simulation of reincarceration, uncertainty in model parameters, unmodeled selection and uptake effects, and exclusion of benefits from reduced TB transmission.

This 2018 electronic edition of *Foreign Relations of the United States* contains the full diplomatic-papers series in a portable format with search, bookmarking, note-taking, and offline access. The Office of the Historian sought fidelity to the printed edition but recommends citing persistent document numbers rather than original page numbers; older volumes include corresponding document numbers in brackets. The volume was prepared and technically edited under named State Department officials, following Department of State Regulation 1350 of 1961. FRUS is designated the official record of U.S. foreign policy. Its Historical Office must apply historical objectivity, preserve original text, mark deletions, and retain facts of major importance, while permitting certain omissions for reasons such as security and clearance. From 1950 onward, the companion *American Foreign Policy* series systematically covers major messages, addresses, statements, reports, notes, and treaties; for 1945–1949, this volume offers only brief, noncomprehensive indications of major documents.

The passage describes embodiments for wireless-device access control in mobile communication systems supporting LTE, 5G NR, wireless local area networks, and other technologies, including reduced-capability devices. It presents a core-network/radio-access-network architecture and a 5G system containing a 5G core, NG-RAN, and user equipment, with service-based architecture, network slicing, control/user-plane separation, and NG, Xn, and Uu interfaces.

The NR user-plane protocol stack includes PHY, MAC, RLC, PDCP, and SDAP layers, while the control plane adds RRC and NAS. Their functions, channel mappings, packet processing, coding, modulation, scheduling, and radio-resource handling are described. The passage also covers RRC idle, inactive, and connected states; OFDM numerologies and time-frequency resource grids; bandwidth-part adaptation and switching; carrier aggregation; PUCCH groups; contention-based, contention-free, and two-step random access; synchronization and reference signals; beamforming, beam sweeping, beam management, and quasi-colocation.

Wireless-device and base-station hardware are described with antennas, RF front ends, processing systems, memory, GPS, and peripherals, along with timer handling, multi-cell configuration, and RRC-based configuration of device resources and procedures.

The Supreme Court deferred until January 2026 its decision on the Trump administration’s request to pause a federal order keeping Lisa Cook on the Federal Reserve’s Board of Governors, leaving the order in place and preventing her removal for now. The court will address the stay request rather than the underlying merits and directed the parties to file amicus briefs.

A district judge found Cook was likely to prevail, ruling that Trump lacked statutory “cause” to remove her and likely violated her constitutional rights by failing to provide notice and a hearing. Fed governors serve staggered 14-year terms and may be removed only for cause, though the statute does not define that term. Trump cited mortgage fraud allegations by Cook, who denied them and argued they were unproven.

The Supreme Court also agreed to review a related case involving the Trump administration’s attempt to fire FTC member Rebecca Slaughter and directed the parties to address whether courts may order wrongly removed officials reinstated or retained.

This study used finite element modeling to examine how collagen fiber continuity and tortuosity affect stretch and stress in arterial tissue with wall-thickness variations. A three-dimensional representative volume element (500 × 500 μm) transitioned from 100 to 200 μm thickness and contained discrete collagen fibers embedded in a nearly incompressible neo-Hookean matrix. Two fiber architectures with equal overall collagen volume density (35.5%) were compared: abrupt fiber termination at the thickness gradient and continuous fibers spanning it. Uniaxial tensile loading was simulated using fibers with recruitment stretches of 1.01 or 1.25.

At an applied stretch of 1.5, abrupt terminations produced greater regional differences: the thin region averaged 1.56 stretch and 0.56 MPa stress, compared with 1.30 and 0.34 MPa in the thick region; maximum stress reached 2.49 MPa. With continuous fibers, thin- and thick-region responses were nearly identical, averaging stretches of 1.48 and 1.47 and stresses of 0.45 and 0.44 MPa, while maximum stress was 0.664 MPa. The stretch difference fell from 20% to 0.68%.

Continuous fibers also produced more uniform fiber-level stress and higher local density in the thin region (51.93% versus 26.04% in the thick region), compared with approximately uniform density under abrupt termination. Fiber tortuosity delayed collagen engagement: before recruitment, thickness geometry dominated the response, but after fibers recruited, disparities generally decreased, especially for continuous networks.

The results indicate that collagen architecture is a major determinant of local mechanics and that continuous fibers redistribute load and mitigate geometry-induced stress and stretch differences. For tissues with confirmed fiber continuity, constant-thickness models may provide reasonable predictions, particularly after fiber recruitment. Limitations include the idealized geometry and boundaries, absence of residual stress and multiaxial loading, and lack of experimental validation. Future work should examine complex tissue geometries, mixed fiber architectures, and validation using mechanical testing, digital image correlation, and multiphoton imaging.

The passage defines conservative handling of missing or incomplete adverse-event dates: onset is assumed to occur during study treatment and be considered a TEAE unless partial dates or other information indicate otherwise. It specifies calculations for durations in days, months, and years; conversion of height, weight, and temperature to metric units; BMI; and change from baseline as postbaseline minus baseline value.

SAS quality-control requirements cover program naming, headers, logical structure, comments, documented hard coding, adherence to derivation rules, validated source datasets, and proper program execution. The SAS log must be fully reviewed for errors, warnings, merge notes, and uninitialized variables. Output reviews verify file names, titles, footnotes, headers, formatting, sorting, page breaks, significant digits, population totals, and inappropriate or missing data. Pinnacle 21 validation is required for SDTM, TDM, and ADaM datasets, with errors or warnings corrected or explained.

Programmers and validators must review datasets against the protocol, SAP, and CRF. Validation includes spot-checking at least two patients, confirming all CRF sections or forms are represented, and checking datasets, variables, populations, parameters, tests, visits, time points, units, ranges, percentages, and counts. Derived variables in listings are compared with source data and manual calculations for at least two patients. Figure values are compared with validated tables for at least 25% of plotted points, with manual calculations performed when feasible. QC completion, findings, and resolutions must be documented in the Program Status Document; patient spot-check outputs and the Pinnacle 21 report must be retained in the study folder.

The proposed tables, figures, and listings follow ICH E3 organization and cover patient disposition and demographics, diabetes history, body measurements, medical history, concomitant medications, glucose recovery, plasma glucose, adverse events, ECG, laboratory and urine tests, pregnancy testing, local tolerability, vital signs, immunogenicity, pharmacokinetic and pharmacodynamic results, protocol deviations, and individual listings.

Time to glucose recovery is defined as a plasma-glucose increase of 20 mg/dL within 45 minutes without IV glucose; failure to recover or receipt of IV glucose before 45 minutes is also specified. Cox models include treatment, age, injection site, and baseline plasma glucose. Recovery assessments at 10, 15, 20, and 30 minutes use CMH tests stratified by age group and injection site; inferential glucose-change tests use ANOVA with the same factors. Patients receiving rescue IV glucose before recovery are treated as not recovered, or use the glucose value at rescue for change calculations. Safety tables count each patient once within summation levels and calculate percentages from treatment-group totals. Pre-dose PK results below the LLOQ are set to 0 pmol/L, and PK results are rounded to three significant digits. Listings are sorted by treatment, subject ID, parameter, visit, and time point, and generally display all available data unless otherwise specified.

LG’s SJ9500 Super UHD TV uses Nano Cell quantum-dot film to improve 4K color, contrast, blacks, and viewing angles, retaining 95% of color and contrast off-axis. It supports HDR10, Dolby Vision, Advanced HDR, scene optimization, and simulated HDR for standard content. LG also introduced the SJ8500 and SJ8000; pricing and release dates remain unannounced.

Enerfax Daily No. 949, dated February 26, 2002, compiled North American natural-gas and power prices, futures, volume, option volatility, corporate news, regulatory developments, financial indexes and sponsor advertisements. Henry Hub physical gas was listed at $2.40, while Gulf/Eastern locations ranged from $2.30 to $2.66. SG Resources solicited firm storage-service bids for the Southern Pines Energy Center, a salt-cavern storage facility on the Mississippi-Alabama border, from February 4 through March 4. The facility is planned to connect with nine major pipelines serving the Mid-Atlantic and Southeast.

The contracts were valued at $43 billion, averaged $88/MWh and were described as about three times the spot-market price. Calpine defended its contracts, while FERC Chairman Wood planned an investigation into possible manipulation of California’s power market and long-term contract prices. Asteroid 2025 TF passed over Antarctica on October 1 at 00:47:26 UTC, coming within 428 ± 7 km of Earth’s surface. Measuring 1–3 meters across, it was detected by the Catalina Sky Survey only hours after the flyby and posed no threat. ESA astronomers later used the Las Cumbres Observatory telescope to determine its distance and closest-approach time with exceptional precision. The encounter highlighted how global asteroid-surveillance and planetary-defense networks can track even tiny near-Earth objects, while illustrating that objects of this size typically break up in the atmosphere and cause little damage.

This continuation application claims priority to U.S. Provisional Application No. 62/718,773, filed Aug. 14, 2018, and relates to an apparatus and method for transcutaneous nerve stimulation, particularly non-invasive facial nerve stimulation to artificially elicit eye blinking in people with acute facial paralysis.

The background describes the facial nerve’s anatomy, functions, and role in facial expression, taste, salivation, tear production, and blinking. It explains facial nerve paralysis and Bell’s palsy, including symptoms, causes, diagnosis, prognosis, eye protection, corticosteroids, possible antiviral benefit, and the rarity of surgery. It also reviews spontaneous, reflex, and voluntary blinking, including the muscles and neural pathways involved. Dry eye syndrome is discussed in terms of causes, symptoms, prevalence, diagnostic tests such as Schirmer, tear breakup time, slit-lamp, and tear-protein analysis, and treatments including artificial tears, medications, lacrimal plugs, and environmental measures.

Transcutaneous electrical nerve stimulation is described as applying electrical current through skin electrodes to stimulate nerves, generally for pain relief. Prior-art devices and patents cited cover asymmetric biphasic signals, patient-shock protection, continuity checks, gradual pulse ramp-up, automatic or timed operation, electrode arrays, and microprocessor-controlled stimulation. Electrical muscle stimulation is distinguished from TENS and described as producing muscle contractions for rehabilitation, strength training, and neural or muscular testing.

The passage also reviews conventional skin electrodes, flexible screen-printed dry “electronic skin” electrodes for electromyography, passive, active, dry, and implantable EEG electrodes, and EEG recording, filtering, sampling, and intracranial recording methods. Additional background covers Internet and TCP/IP networking, wireless systems and antennas, ISM bands, Wi-Fi, ZigBee, Z-Wave, Bluetooth and Bluetooth Low Energy, wireless mesh and body-area networks, cellular communications, near-field communication, random-number generation, smartphones, instant and text messaging, SMS, MMS, Facebook Messenger, Twitter, and WhatsApp.

Reports that the Tong Hâk were preparing to march on Seoul and expel foreigners proved to be an unsubstantiated rumor, although officials and foreign representatives showed some unease. The British and German gunboats at Chemulpo declined to remain without evidence of actual danger and subsequently departed.

About forty Tong Hâk, led by Pak Siung-ho, knelt before the palace gate and presented a petition to the king. Although its contents were unknown, it was believed to seek reversal of the founder Ch’e Cheng-woo’s conviction for heresy and permission to practice their religion, as well as possibly protesting foreigners and Christianity. The group’s emergence from severe persecution to bold public demands suggested substantial support in Seoul; large numbers had entered the city for the crown prince’s examinations.

According to Pak, Ch’e Cheng-woo founded the religion in 1859 and received sacred books after a year of prayer. Its teachings emphasized worship of one God, ancestor sacrifice, family and social hierarchy, faithfulness, reverence, and benevolence. Pak denied hostility toward foreigners and the acrobatic or conjuring feats popularly attributed to the group. He described its adherents as scholars and said anyone obeying its precepts could join. Critics, however, suggested that true believers were joined by opportunists, debtors seeking escape from creditors, and people hostile to Roman Catholic priests. The narrator cautioned that such Korean remarks likely contained exaggeration.

The PENTAD Timing Model, created by Nelson Freeburg, uses four stock indices and an advance/decline line to generate weekly buy and sell signals for the US stock market. It combines moving-average envelopes, with upper buy and lower sell zones, and moving-average slopes, which act like oscillators. The model operates by voting: entry requires a unanimous “yes,” while at least two “against” votes trigger an exit. Freeburg is an experienced trader, researcher, and former editor of Formula Research who develops and tests objective trading systems. The passage describes the model’s structure and formulas and outlines a historical backtest covering equity, drawdowns, monthly and annual returns, and performance against the S&P 500 Total Return index.

The Facebook–Cambridge Analytica scandal intensified public concern over data surveillance, prompting privacy checks, permission changes, a “Delete Facebook” movement, and an FTC investigation that led to Facebook’s stock price to fall. Users had authorized Facebook to collect personal data and allow third-party access under terms they formally accepted but rarely understood; Cambridge Analytica’s access exceeded what Facebook and most users had sanctioned.

The passage argues that unauthorized access is serious, but focusing on consent alone misses a deeper problem: formal consent is often artificial, while choice architecture—the design of decision environments—already shapes behavior. Personalized choice architecture combines information from multiple sources into detailed individual profiles and tailors subliminal influence to each person. By targeting intimate traits, it blurs persuasion and coercion and may erode autonomous choice and democratic self-government.

Such techniques can support beneficial interventions, including counter-narratives to ISIS recruitment, but misuse can become manipulation. Cited examples include Jigsaw’s ISIS outreach and Facebook’s alleged targeting of at-risk Australian youth. Because individualized microtargeting creates systemic risks, quitting Facebook alone is insufficient; broad social, economic, technical, legal, and ethical limits are needed to preserve meaningful choice.

The Mortgage Collaborative, an independent mortgage cooperative, announced a partnership with Strategic Compliance Partners (SCP), adding the compliance firm to its preferred partner network. The Aug. 21, 2017 solar eclipse will cross the United States, giving most locations a partial eclipse and a narrow, roughly 70-mile-wide path totality. Totality will reach Oregon at 10:16 a.m. PT and end near the Atlantic coast at 2:49 p.m. ET. During totality, the sky will darken, stars will appear, and temperatures will drop; Baily’s Beads and a diamond-ring effect will precede and follow it. Outside the totality path, the moon will cover 20–99 percent of the sun.

Viewing the sun is dangerous without proper eclipse glasses compliant with ISO 12312-2. Direct viewing is safe only while the sun is completely blocked during totality. NASA offers an interactive map, a four-hour “Eclipse Megacast,” livestreams, and a 3-D simulation. Photography is possible with tips for cameras and smartphones. The next total solar eclipse will occur July 2, 2019, and the next over the United States will be April 8, 2024.

Alabama’s special Senate election pits Republican Roy Moore against Democrat Doug Jones for the seat vacated by Jeff Sessions. Moore, a former chief justice removed twice and accused of decades-old sexual misconduct with teenage girls, has drawn opposition even from some Republicans, including Sen. Richard Shelby. He denies the charges and is supported by conservatives who cite his evangelical, anti-establishment positions and alignment with Trump.

Democrats see the vote as a chance to distance Alabama from its segregationist political history; Republicans view Moore’s victory as an endorsement of conservative values and Trump’s agenda.

Both parties are watching closely: Democrats need strong turnout among young and non-white voters and suburban moderates, while Republicans expect most Alabama conservatives to remain with Moore.

The AMD Geode CS5535 Revision A3 specification update documents multiple device limitations and required workarounds:

- The CS5535 does not meet USB over-voltage protection requirements; external over-voltage protection circuits are required.
- LBAR values of 10000h or higher are illegal on x86 systems and should not be used.
- Automatic Local bus clock gating can prevent an edge-configured PIC input from returning to Idle when its source remains high, causing missed interrupts and possible system hangs.
- ATAC and ACC PRD prefetch settings can read part of the next PRD when tables are not 8-byte aligned. PRD entries should be defined before transfers, and on-the-fly ACC changes should be at least two tables ahead.
- A preceding UDMA read with host termination can corrupt UDMA-write CRC state after device termination, causing invalid CRCs. UDMA I/O blocking via bit 8 of the ATAC Error MSR is recommended.
- ATAC SSMI during DMA does not block IDE I/O as intended; the feature is not operationally required and should not be used.
- GLIU statistics-counter ASMIs may be lost when hardware clock gating is enabled for domain zero.
- Byte access to ACPI PM1_STS and PM1_EN can hang; only WORD or DWORD access is supported. WORD or BYTE writes to PMC registers can also corrupt the same or unrelated registers, so an SMI I/O trap is recommended for ACPI-defined registers.
- KEL emulation cannot distinguish writes to I/O ports 060h and 064h through CmdData, and Snoop mode incorrectly changes HCE register state; trap-level handling or saving and restoring HCE state is required.
- Reading port 060h can incorrectly clear the KEL AuxOutputFull bit; interrupts should be used for USB keyboard and mouse management.
- Back-to-back PCI reads one clock apart within one cache line can fail, although the Geode GX cannot issue such reads in real systems. The 8259 PIC polling mode is unsupported.
- Automatic UART clock gating does not work correctly in CEIR mode and should remain disabled, resulting in slightly higher device power.
- IRDY# and DEVSEL# have a guaranteed 1.5 ns tVAL rather than the specified 2 ns, though no failures are expected; 10–50 pF capacitors can slow the edges if problems occur.
- Simultaneous interrupt and SSMI events may allow the I/O to complete before the SSMI is signaled. The update directs use of the processor for desired SSMI handling.
- UDMA commands sent to a CD-ROM after enabling the bus master fail; the required order is the PIO command followed by bus-master enable. An unexpected IDE interrupt before transfer completion can also reset the bus-master engine.
- GPIO[27:24] wake inputs do not function from ACPI S3; use PWRBTN#, optionally with external circuitry to combine wake events.
- Immediate reads of legacy RTC CMOS RAM after writes through the extended port can return incorrect data.
- Block- and demand-mode legacy DMA prevents reliable LPC I/O; use single-transfer mode instead.
- USB controller clock gating can cause register-read failures and should be disabled.
- ATAC can hang with WORD-aligned PRD addresses; all ATAC drivers should use DWORD alignment.
- The LPC controller can abort transactions after insufficient valid SYNC clocks, causing discarded writes or all-ones reads; a PLD workaround is described.
- SMB NEGACK may be delayed or cleared unexpectedly; clearing it requires two writes, first setting NEGACK and then writing 00h.
- The GLPCI retry limit counts retries from other PCI bus masters, so it may stop retrying early; the limit can be increased or disabled.
- After suspend, atomic GPIO High Bank Feature Bit Register writes clear nonselected bits and must use read-modify-write.
- The SMBus data hold time does not meet the 300 ns SMB 2.0 minimum.
- LOWBAT_FLAG may fail to record a low-battery condition after abnormal standby.
- If PM_SCXD, PM_SCYD, or PM_IN_SLPCTL delay values exceed PM_SED’s delay, SLEEP_X and SLEEP_Y remain asserted and PCI/IDE inputs stay disabled; their delay counters must be programmed below the PM_SED value.

The document also includes AMD copyright, warranty and liability disclaimers, product-use restrictions, and trademark notices.

The study investigates automated question generation, adaptive assessment, simulation, and engagement in the proposed AnveshanaAI platform for AI/ML education. It addresses gaps in existing platforms, which largely offer static question repositories without adaptive generation, difficulty calibration, or peer-driven feedback.

AnveshanaAI’s dataset contains 10,845 problem–answer pairs across 26 AI/ML subject categories and four difficulty levels. Sources included academic material, challenge repositories, research references, and human-authored tasks. Preprocessing included tokenization, chunking, embedding, and vectorized storage. Each entry includes an ID, problem, answer, category, difficulty, tags, and Bloom’s taxonomy level. Difficulty scaling added rephrased, domain-shifted, and edge-case problems, while cross-mode adaptation produced coding, simulation, debugging, and viva-style tasks. Quality assurance included automated LLM self-checks, static validation, sandbox testing, and rubric-based alignment.

The platform serves learners and administrators. Learners receive categorized challenges, progress metrics, streaks, badges, levels, simulations, and oral-style viva interactions. Administrators can create or upload challenges, run augmentation pipelines, analyze performance and engagement, and export data for research or LMS integration. Its modular architecture includes a question-generation pipeline, adaptive delivery engine, multimodal interaction layer, analytics dashboard, fine-tuned LLMs, Docker-based code sandboxes, vector retrieval, and Whisper-based speech recognition. The React/Vite frontend, Node.js/Express backend, and MySQL storage support challenge execution, user management, and analytics. Performance data are used to generate feedback, adjust difficulty, and recommend learning paths.

Dataset analysis showed 64% effective category utilization, 91% utilization across difficulty levels, and 97% utilization across Bloom’s taxonomy levels. Category and difficulty were strongly associated (Cramér’s V = 0.596), while Bloom’s level had weak associations with both. Question–answer semantic similarity generally clustered between 0.6 and 0.8.

The disclosure describes Polkadot, a heterogeneous multi-chain framework centered on a relay chain that hosts parallel chains called parachains. Its objectives are pooled security across heterogeneous blockchains, interoperability, and scalability through parallel execution and separation of transaction execution from consensus.

Parachain collators assemble and execute transactions into candidate blocks and provide state-transition proofs. Validators assigned to each parachain receive, validate, republish, and vote on these candidates, checking both state-transition validity and external-data availability. An asynchronous Byzantine fault-tolerant process seals relay-chain blocks containing valid parachain candidates. Invalid blocks may be detected and reverted, while responsible nodes are punished.

Validators are selected through a nominated proof-of-stake system and bonded for their duties. Nominators provide stake to validators, collators operate full nodes for particular parachains, and “fishermen” submit evidence of validator misconduct for a bounty. Rewards, withheld payments, bond reductions, burning, and confiscation discourage inactivity, invalid voting, double-signing, and fork support. Checkpoints and long bond-liquidation periods protect against long-range attacks.

The relay chain is designed with minimal application functionality and modular components for consensus, validator management, governance, staking, and parachain administration. A parachain registry stores static chain information and dynamic routing data, while governance may add, suspend, or remove parachains through referenda or validator voting.

Parachains produce interchain posts in FIFO egress queues. Relay-chain maintainers transfer these posts into destination parachains’ ingress queues, using Merkle proofs to establish fidelity and saturation rules to limit message flooding. Direct routing is supplemented by multi-phase “hyper-cube” routing to accommodate many chains with lower connectivity at the cost of additional latency.

The framework also addresses data availability through validator attestations, collator challenges, possible separate availability guarantors, delayed availability voting, and secondary data storage. Additional safeguards address overweight blocks, collator selection fairness, collator insurance, and penalties for failing to supply data.

Interoperability with Ethereum is described through validator-signed forwarding, break-in contracts, and logs emitted by break-out contracts, supported by header, state, and confirmation proofs. Bitcoin interoperability may use a validator-controlled break-out address, proof-of-work confirmations, incentivized oracles, and threshold signatures, although Bitcoin’s signature and coordination limitations make secure two-way transfers difficult.

A randomized controlled superiority trial compared radial extracorporeal shock wave therapy plus an eight-week, three-phase rehabilitation program (rESWT+RP) with sham rESWT plus the same rehabilitation program in semi-professional athletes with acute hamstring muscle complex injury type 3b. Forty participants were randomized; retrospective ultrasound review reclassified four as type 3a injuries, leaving 36 in the modified intention-to-treat analysis.

Mean and median times to return to sport were 25.4 and 25.5 days with rESWT+RP, respectively, versus 28.3 and 27.5 days with sham rESWT+RP; the difference was statistically significant (p=0.037). Six-month satisfaction did not differ significantly between groups (mean 9.0 vs. 8.4; p=0.145), nor did re-injury within six months (one case in each group; p>0.999). No intercurrent events associated with rESWT were reported.

The authors concluded that adding rESWT to the rehabilitation program shortened return-to-sport time without increasing re-injury or heterotopic ossification. They noted limitations including the small sample, retrospective exclusion of 10% of participants, ultrasound rather than MRI diagnosis, and inability to blind the treating investigator.
