Czech central bank board member Toms Nidetzky expects one more rate hike this year after three increases since August, though no action is needed yet. The bank forecasts the 0.75% repo rate will rise around late 2018 or early 2019.

FoLix, the first FDA-cleared fractional laser of its kind, is a noninvasive, surgery-free hair loss treatment administered in-office. Unlike red light caps that passively stimulate follicles, it creates microscopic channels in the scalp to trigger a controlled healing response, boost circulation and deliver growth signals to follicles. Sessions take 20–30 minutes, require no anesthesia, need no special aftercare and involve little downtime; topical treatments can be resumed after 24–72 hours. Patients need three to six sessions in the first year, spaced weeks to a month apart, then up to twice yearly for maintenance, costing $750–$1,250 per session. Dermatologists say it suits early-to-moderate hair loss with intact but underperforming follicles, and is not intended for complete baldness or extensive scarring. It may appeal to those avoiding daily finasteride or minoxidil. Mild, temporary side effects include redness, tightness, scalp sensitivity and shedding. Though costly, it is more affordable than surgery, and doctors urge consulting a physician since hair loss can have many causes.

The court rejected defendants’ challenge to reduced damages for an infant who developed Erb’s palsy after shoulder dystocia, finding no material deviation from reasonable compensation and no basis to restore the original future pain-and-suffering award.
Protesters in several cities countered a deadly white supremacist rally in Virginia, with Seattle arrests, Denver and New York marches, and a Charlottesville vigil.

The team expressed confidence in both goaltenders, who performed well in tough situations all year. One goalie was pulled despite battling hard every game since his return; teammates said the team must start helping him rather than leave him "out to dry." Considered underdogs, they believe they can compete but need better execution, persistence, and more physical play.

The study examines how distance education was implemented for visually impaired students receiving professional music education in Turkey, focusing on accessibility, technological tools, course materials, assessment, strengths, weaknesses, and student recommendations. It reviews the development of distance education from correspondence to radio, television, internet, and web-based platforms, noting that COVID-19 prompted its rapid adoption. Earlier applications included letter-based violin instruction in the 1970s, while later developments expanded synchronous and asynchronous music instruction through digital tools, software, audio, and video.

A qualitative case-study design was used. Data were collected through semistructured telephone and online interviews with seven visually impaired undergraduate or graduate music students across Turkey, representing 80% of visually impaired music-department students in the country. Interviews were recorded with consent, transcribed, and analyzed through content analysis. Participants were questioned about course delivery models, equipment, material adequacy, assessment, perceived strengths and weaknesses, and suggestions.

Most courses were delivered synchronously, although some participants also used recorded lessons, PDFs, or post-lesson videos asynchronously. Participants used computers, phones, and tablets independently. Course documents generally did not accommodate special needs and were usable mainly by students able to read large print; some participants required parental assistance, while digital slides were inaccessible to others. Assessment arrangements varied. Some received individual accommodations, such as video-based or homework-format examinations and separate practical examinations, while others faced difficulties with written theoretical examinations and depended on friends for support.

Reported strengths included flexibility in time and place, greater social acceptance, and reduced concern about appearing conspicuous in class; two participants identified no strengths. Major weaknesses involved technical inadequacies affecting music instruction, including poor sound synchronization, inadequate audio transmission, and an inability to sing and play simultaneously. Limited instructor technological knowledge and inefficient institutional systems were also identified.

Students recommended longer lesson durations, accessible document-to-audio conversion, screen magnification and text adjustment, digital music notation archives, Braille resources, technical support, accessible interfaces, rapid system troubleshooting, and more constructive instructor attitudes. The study concludes that distance education was difficult for visually impaired professional music students because systems were largely designed around sighted students. Access often depended on parents, friends, large print, or external training. Screen readers, speech-recognition and dictation software, Braille printers, audio materials, interactive voice- or touch-controlled content, disability-specific preparation, and sustained human support were proposed as necessary improvements.

BIREL ART/PSL achieved a double victory at the Florida Winter Tour’s Palm Beach ROK round. Ryan Norberg won ROK Senior and fastest lap, regaining the championship lead, while Scott Davidson earned his first season win in ROK Shifter Masters. Igor Pushkin finished fifth, Ryan MacDermid 10th, and Justin Aresneu 12th.

A three-judge federal court held that Alabama’s designation under Section 4 of the Voting Rights Act covered Hale County and required Section 5 preclearance for changes in county election procedures. Hale County’s 1965, 1971, and 1973 enactments changing county commissioner elections from district-based to at-large had not been precleared and were therefore unenforceable; past elections under those enactments were unlawful, although previously elected officials could remain in office until lawfully replaced successors.

The court ordered the November 2, 1976, at-large election to proceed, with the elected and incumbent commissioners serving provisionally. Hale County had to submit the challenged enactments and requested information to the Attorney General for expedited review and, if necessary, seek a declaratory judgment in the District of Columbia. Unless the at-large system was approved, a prompt district-based election would be required.

The coach said the team missed scoring chances and must stay positive after a loss, focusing on the important third game. He emphasized avoiding turnovers, breakouts, and lapses by keeping the puck on the outside rather than chipping it into the middle. Despite losses being difficult this late in the season, the team must maintain its will to win, play fearlessly, and prepare to advance.

The author harshly criticizes Hillary Clinton, portraying her as truth-indifferent, ambitious, arrogant, and responsible for numerous political and personal scandals. The passage alleges that she helped reverse George W. Bush’s 2003 policy of leaving Libya alone, contributed to the Arab Spring and renewed slave auctions, and represented her actions as a successful strategy. It also accuses Bill Clinton of arranging a 2016 airport meeting with Attorney General Loretta Lynch, alleges an FBI cover-up and James Comey’s failure to investigate Clinton’s use of a personal email server, and criticizes mainstream media for assisting the Clintons.

The author cites Clinton’s Bosnia sniper-fire claim, Whitewater, Filegate, the Clintons’ use of the IRS, Vince Foster’s death, fundraising, the Clinton Foundation, Benghazi, “ChinaGate,” “TravelGate,” “PardonGate,” and other alleged controversies. Quoting the late Christopher Hitchens, he calls Clinton a liar and “pitifully inadequate” presidential candidate, then asks whether America is “done.”

NVIDIA’s GA10x Ampere architecture builds on Turing with doubled FP32 throughput, second-generation RT Cores, third-generation Tensor Cores, faster memory and storage, and improved GPU-to-GPU and host connectivity. Each GA10x SM partition can execute either 32 FP32 operations or 16 FP32 plus 16 INT32 operations per clock, enabling 128 FP32 operations per clock across an SM. The GeForce RTX 3090 provides over 35 FP32 TFLOPS, more than twice the rate of Turing GPUs.

The full GA102 GPU contains seven Graphics Processing Clusters, 42 Texture Processing Clusters, 84 Streaming Multiprocessors, and 168 FP64 units. Each SM includes 128 CUDA Cores, four third-generation Tensor Cores, one second-generation ray-tracing core, a 256 KB register file, four texture units, and 128 KB of configurable L1 cache/shared memory. Moving ROPs into each GPC raises the full GPU’s ROP count from 96 in TU102 to 112, improving multisample antialiasing, fill rate, and blending. GA10x also doubles shared-memory bandwidth relative to Turing, while the GA102 has 512 KB of L2 cache per memory controller. Ampere GPUs are reported to be up to 1.9 times more power-efficient than Turing GPUs at the same performance level.

Second-generation RT Cores double ray/triangle intersection performance, support BVH traversal, and can execute ray-tracing work concurrently with graphics or compute workloads. The GA10x SM can also run two compute workloads simultaneously, allowing tasks such as compute-based denoising to operate alongside RT Core ray tracing. A new Interpolate Triangle Position unit accelerates ray-traced motion blur for moving and deforming geometry. The architecture supports motion-blur rendering up to eight times faster than Turing, with a reported Blender test showing up to fivefold improvement.

Third-generation Tensor Cores are more powerful than Turing Tensor Cores despite their lower number per SM. They support FP16, BF16, TF32, INT8, INT4, and binary precision, but not FP64 acceleration. Fine-grained structured sparsity uses a 2-out-of-4 nonzero pattern to double matrix-operation throughput and halve weight storage and bandwidth requirements while retaining dense-operation throughput. TF32 provides up to five times the training throughput of the previous generation without code changes and twice the throughput of standard FP32. Tensor Cores accelerate AI denoising, DLSS super-resolution with up to 8K output, NVIDIA Broadcast, and NVIDIA Canvas. The RTX 3080 is listed at 119 peak FP16 Tensor TFLOPS, rising to 238 with sparsity, and 238 INT8 Tensor TOPS, rising to 476 with sparsity.

GDDR6X uses PAM4 signaling and Maximum Transition Avoidance coding to support data rates up to 19.5 Gbps and peak bandwidth of 936 GB/sec on the RTX 3090. It offers more than 52 percent greater bandwidth than the RTX 2080 Ti’s GDDR6 memory and supports pseudo-independent channels for BVH traversal. The RTX A6000 and A40 use 48 GB of GDDR6 memory, expandable to 96 GB by linking two GPUs with third-generation NVLink. Each NVLink connection provides 56.25 GB/sec in each direction, or 112.5 GB/sec total between two GPUs. GA10x also supports PCIe 4.0, offering up to 64 GB/sec peak bandwidth with an x16 slot.

NVIDIA RTX IO works with Microsoft’s DirectStorage API to move compressed assets directly from NVMe storage to the GPU for lossless GPU-based decompression. It can accelerate I/O by up to 100 times versus hard drives and traditional storage APIs while offloading work that may occupy dozens of CPU cores, enabling faster loading, streaming, rendering starts, and reduced object pop-in and stutter.

The GA10x platform supports DisplayPort 1.4a with DSC 1.2a and HDMI 2.1, including 8K at 60 Hz and 4K at 120 Hz. Its fifth-generation NVDEC decoder supports MPEG-2, VC-1, H.264, H.265, VP8, VP9, and AV1. GA10x is the first GPU generation described as providing hardware AV1 decoding, capable of 8K60 HDR playback with about 4 percent CPU usage in the cited test. Seventh-generation NVENC provides hardware encoding up to 4K H.264 and 8K HEVC.

The NVIDIA A40 targets data-center visual computing and supports virtualization, Quadro Sync, and the NVIDIA EGX platform. Compared with the Quadro RTX 6000, it offers up to twice the FP32 and ray-tracing throughput and up to five times the AI training and data-science throughput, or ten times with sparsity. It includes 48 GB of memory, three DisplayPort outputs, and support for 96 GB through dual-GPU NVLink.

The GeForce RTX 3090 uses GA102 with 82 SMs, 10,496 CUDA Cores, and 24 GB of GDDR6X memory. The RTX 3070 uses GA104, lacks NVLink, and uses GDDR6 rather than GDDR6X; the document states that it outperforms the previous RTX 2080 Ti. The RTX A6000 provides 10,752 CUDA Cores and 48 GB of GDDR6, expandable to 96 GB through NVLink. GDDR6X memory interfaces also include Error Detection and Replay, which detects failed transactions and retries them to improve overclocking reliability and identify performance plateaus.

Austria's Anna Gasser won Olympic gold in the debut women's Big Air snowboarding event at Pyeongchang, edging two-time gold medalist Jamie Anderson of the U.S. Anderson, who had won slopestyle gold days earlier, led by 2.75 after scoring 90 and 87.25 on her first two jumps but fell on her final attempt. Gasser's winning run, a double cork 1080, earned a 96 for a total of 185.00. New Zealand's Zoi Sadowski Synnott took bronze with 157.50, the nation's first Winter Olympic medal since 1992. Officials moved the final from Friday to Thursday over wind concerns, and most of the 50 runs were completed in mostly calm conditions.

This continuation application describes electrical interconnects for quantum computing systems, especially flexible cables connecting rigid circuit boards and quantum processor units within dilution refrigerators. Flexible cables may carry parallel striplines, microstrips, or coplanar waveguides between grounding planes, with conductive vias for shielding and fan-out ends for secure mechanical attachment. Rigid boards can host active and passive components and be thermally anchored to isothermal plates. Implementations include integrated filters and attenuators, absorptive regions for noise suppression, and connections using solder or indium bumps, wire bonds, flip-chip assemblies, clamps, and compliant spring contacts. Described materials include copper, superconducting niobium, titanium-niobium, and aluminum, nonsuperconducting metals, and polymer dielectrics. The interconnects are presented as addressing thermal-load, assembly, space, and scalability challenges associated with growing quantum-computer I/O requirements.

A Teagasc survey of 314 male farmers in southeast Ireland found elevated cardiovascular disease and cancer mortality, alongside low doctor consultation and self-reported health risks. Although working identity often takes priority over health, 39% reported ill health in the previous year, mainly back pain, arthritis or anxiety. Smoking, alcohol use and rheumatoid arthritis were also prevalent, with under-45 farmers more likely to smoke and drink weekly and those over-45 more likely to report arthritis.

Former New York Judge Louis L. Nock joined Anderson Kill after resigning from the bench, citing family considerations and mandatory retirement at 70. His move coincided with an agreement under which the New York State Commission on Judicial Conduct dropped ethics charges in exchange for his resignation and a promise never to accept judicial office again. Complaints alleged rude, demeaning conduct toward court staff and retaliatory threats. Nock denied wrongdoing, and no finding was made after the commission denied two dismissal motions. He served as a New York City civil court judge from 2015 and as an acting state supreme court justice from 2018. Anderson Kill said it disclosed the allegations before hiring him and found nothing questioning his conduct or character.

The LIVE-AIR phase 3 trial evaluated lenzilumab, a GM-CSF-neutralizing antibody, in 520 hospitalized adults with COVID-19 pneumonia. In the 479-participant modified intent-to-treat population, lenzilumab improved day-28 survival without invasive mechanical ventilation (SWOV) versus placebo (HR 1.54; 95% CI 1.02–2.32; p=0.0403). Elevated baseline CRP was the strongest predictor of progression to invasive mechanical ventilation or death. Treatment effects were greatest among participants with baseline CRP below 150 mg/L, including improved SWOV (HR 2.54; 95% CI 1.46–4.41; nominal p=0.0009), lower incidence of invasive mechanical ventilation, ECMO, or death, more ventilator-free days, fewer ICU days, and faster recovery. SWOV was similar between treatments among participants with CRP of at least 150 mg/L. Lenzilumab also lowered CRP levels from day 2 and was well tolerated, with no reported treatment-attributable serious adverse events or infusion reactions. Most CRP analyses were exploratory and post hoc, the trial was not powered to demonstrate a mortality benefit, and the findings will be prospectively evaluated in the ACTIV-5/BET-B trial.

The speaker calls the upcoming game the biggest they can play. The team is calm, excited, and ready despite nerves; fans and the city support them, and an injured teammate’s presence would mean a lot.

At sentencing, Donna Adelson, 75, insisted she was an innocent woman and said she would have stopped the murder-for-hire plan had she known of it before Florida State University law professor Dan Markel’s 2014 shooting death. Convicted of murder, conspiracy and solicitation, she was sentenced to life in prison plus 30 years; Judge Stephen Everett said she showed an “utter lack of remorse.”

The White House confirmed plans to withdraw Kathleen Hartnett White’s nomination to chair the Council on Environmental Quality after it stalled in the Senate. The climate-change skeptic drew criticism for questioning mainstream climate science, opposing stricter pollution limits and praising fossil fuels. Her think-tank received fossil-fuel industry funding. Democrats including Sen. Tom Carper welcomed the decision and urged Trump to nominate an environmental and public-health champion.

A five-year study of 35 public pension plans representing about 14.5% of industry assets found wide performance variation from 2008 to 2012: annualized returns ranged from 15% to -4.2%, with more than half performing below the roughly 4.5% balanced-index return. Asset-allocation differences and behavioral gaps explained much of the variation. Performance was associated with institutional knowledge, board stability, professionalism, composition, engagement, staff support, diligence, monthly meetings, and effective delegation and consultation. Investment expenses and required contribution rates were not statistically significant. Plans in the top 20% of Fiduciary Effectiveness Quotient scores nearly outperformed twice as much as those in the bottom 20%; each one-unit FEQ improvement corresponded to a 0.36% increase in five-year investment performance, with the relationship persisting under a one-year lag. The study concludes that asset-owner governance can be measured and materially affects investment results.

Ray tracing realistically simulates scene lighting but is computationally intensive, and until now GPU architectures could not perform it in real time on a single GPU; professional tools such as NVIDIA Iray plugins and the OptiX engine served artists and designers, and Volta GPUs rendered movie-quality scenes but not in real time, so games relied on rasterization instead. NVIDIA achieved real-time ray tracing after nearly 10 years of collaboration among its research, GPU hardware design, and software engineering teams, by introducing hardware-based ray tracing acceleration engines called RT Cores, which enable Turing GPUs to render physically correct reflections, refractions, shadows, and indirect lighting in real time.

A cross-sectional study assessed contraceptive knowledge, attitudes, practices, and predictors among 217 female students at NTA TV College in Jos, Nigeria. Mean age was 21.9 years, and 73.7% had had sexual intercourse. Good knowledge, attitude, and practice were reported by 55.3%, 47.5%, and 50.7%, respectively. Friends and the internet were the main information sources, condoms and oral contraceptive pills were most commonly used, and fear of side effects or health risks was the leading reason for non-use. Multivariable analysis found that being over 19 predicted good knowledge; diploma status, off-campus residence, and good knowledge predicted good attitudes; and being Plateau-indigenous and having had sex predicted good contraceptive practice. The authors concluded that relatively low levels require targeted advocacy, improved education, policy reforms, and youth-friendly sexual and reproductive health services. Limitations include the single-institution setting and possible social-desirability bias.

Hui Ying Financial Holdings Corporation, formerly Sino Fortune Holding Corporation, operates an online platform in China that connects investors with underserved SME and individual borrowers, maintains risk reserves, and provides a secondary market for investors.

For 2017, revenue rose 88.4% to $46.50 million from $24.68 million in 2016, driven by higher loan volumes and a newly launched entrusted-loan business. Origination fees increased 52.7% to $26.70 million, repayment management fees rose 153.3% to $18.21 million, and entrusted-loan financing income reached $1.58 million. Operating income climbed 301.6% to $17.95 million, while net income rose 343.9% to $15.27 million from $3.44 million. Diluted EPS increased to $0.21 from $0.05, and operating margin improved to 38.6% from 18.1%. Operating expenses increased 41.2% to $28.55 million, primarily reflecting higher sales and marketing activity and expenses related to the company’s Nasdaq uplisting.

Loan volume facilitated through the platform increased 59.9% to $1.31 billion, with 23,263 loans, 8,047 borrowers, and 69,232 investors in 2017. Outstanding loans rose to $436.3 million from $246.1 million. Cumulative facilitated loan value reached $2.87 billion since the platform launched in December 2013. The company reported 367,893 registered investors and 24 cooperative guarantor partners at year-end.

At December 31, 2017, cash and equivalents totaled $12.68 million, current assets totaled $55.27 million, and current liabilities totaled $17.47 million, producing a current ratio of 3.16. Operating activities provided $24.07 million of cash, investing activities used $34.02 million, and financing activities provided $13.37 million from convertible-note issuance. Total assets were $59.06 million, total liabilities were $30.66 million, and stockholders’ equity was $28.40 million. Prior-year financial statements were restated.

Chrissy Teigen, 32 and pregnant with her second child, told Refinery29 that she has a family history of stretch marks and previously developed them on her inner thighs. She emphasizes prevention by using Aquaphor, coconut oil, and Lumière de Vie’s Lumière Concentrate on her belly and body. Her nightly 10–15-minute skincare routine is assisted by husband John Legend and daughter Luna. She receives Lumière products through a beauty campaign and applies the concentrate around her belly’s sides. Teigen also said she has never seen a woman without stretch marks and views them as a common bond among models.

Research involving 9,859 UK adolescents aged 10–15 found that girls used social media more than boys and experienced a larger decline in well-being. Girls using social media for an hour or more by age 10 had lower well-being at 15. By age 13, about half of girls used social media for over an hour on school days, compared with one-third of boys. Researchers said the link may have been underestimated because use was self-reported and measured only on school days.

The Jan. 26, 2001 compilation covers California’s electricity crisis and several Enron-related developments. A Times of India editorial blamed rolling blackouts and financial distress among utilities on flawed post-1996 deregulation, including capped retail tariffs, restrictions on long-term power contracts, plant closures and rising demand, while advocating adequate long-term capacity and a careful transition to deregulated markets. A Wall Street Journal report described wind power’s revival as a partial response to California’s shortages, noting that newer projects can generate electricity more cheaply than natural gas, although wind remains intermittent and supplies only about 1.5% of California’s power.

Market coverage said investors favored defensive blue-chip stocks and anticipated Federal Reserve rate cuts, pushing the Dow higher while the Nasdaq and Standard & Poor’s 500 declined. Enron shares rose $2.25 to $82 after the company indicated that 2001 profits would likely exceed analysts’ forecasts.

Business Standard and The Wall Street Journal reported that cash-strapped Maharashtra State Electricity Board was expected to miss a 1.59 billion-rupee payment to Enron’s Dabhol Power, potentially prompting Enron to invoke state and federal guarantees. A Business Standard editorial said U.S. mediation urged Maharashtra Chief Minister Vilasrao Deshmukh to honor the contract and permit regulator-set electricity tariffs despite political opposition.

The Houston Chronicle reported that Enron’s new “rank and yank” system would divide employees into five categories, comparing performance with coworkers and prompting concerns about managerial bargaining and motivation. Other items included David Nyhan’s announcement of a four-month Harvard fellowship and criticism of Enron’s California profits and political contributions, and a report on California Democrats’ anti-Bush activism and proposals for time-of-use electricity pricing.

The coach said the team must absorb Chris Pronger’s one-game suspension by spreading minutes and power-play responsibility among Joe DiPenta, Jackman, Beauchemin, Niedermayer, O’Donnell and Huskins, with specialty teams central to success. Chris Kunitz was a game-time decision after treatment. After a previous loss, the coach said the players had taken too many penalties and become overly emotional, but regrouped through stronger forechecking, penalty killing and goaltending. Huskins, Selanne and Penner were praised for stepping up, particularly Selanne’s setup for Penner. The team must reduce undisciplined penalties, maintain intensity and avoid complacency after taking the lead. Personnel decisions would prioritize winning while protecting player health. With four games left in the series, the team was preparing to match its opponent’s intensity, skill and will.

The President vetoed House bill No. 6242 because its river and harbor appropriations included local projects that did not serve the common defense, general welfare, or interstate commerce and therefore exceeded constitutional limits on federal spending. He also objected to the bill’s excessive total, noting that appropriations had risen from $3,975,900 in 1870 to $18,743,875, potentially exceeding current national needs and encouraging wasteful spending. He recommended appropriating only half the proposed amount for the fiscal year, with the Secretary of War selecting eligible projects and limiting expenditure on any purpose to the amount specified in the bill.

A domestic violence support group for women survivors meets Tuesdays at noon for free. AARP Tax Aide offers no-cost walk-in federal and Oregon tax help at three sites, with exclusions and documentation requirements. Registration is open for a Feb. 24 Chess for Success tournament for K–12 students in four counties. Girls Up is collecting clean, used bras and sports bras in February for local women in need and homeless shelters.

Pakistan Volleyball Federation Chairman Chaudhry Mohammad Yaqoob urged the federal government to build a well-equipped sports complex in Abbottabad, where summer weather is moderate, so national teams could hold camps from May to September and international events could be hosted. He said billions were wasted on the underused Narowal complex and noted that Islamabad’s Liaquat Gymnasium lacks air-conditioning. For the Asian Games, Yaqoob said a four-month camp was needed and requested early preparations. Junior, youth and senior camps were moved to Peshawar but had not begun after the Pakistan Sports Board halted them over financial issues. The board will meet federations and the Olympic Association on June 6, while Iranian coach Hamid Movahedi is expected to join the Peshawar camp.

The TPS7H500x-SP series comprises radiation-hardness-assured, fixed-frequency peak-current-mode PWM controllers for space-grade DC-DC converters. They operate with external gate drivers, support switching frequencies up to 2 MHz, and can be used with buck, flyback, forward, active-clamp forward, push-pull, and full-bridge topologies. The controllers regulate peak current and duty cycle by comparing sensed switch current with a stepped-down COMP voltage and turning off the power switch when the threshold is reached.

In peak-current-mode converters, duty cycles above 50% can cause subharmonic oscillation. The TPS7H500x-SP mitigates this with a voltage ramp subtracted from the divided COMP voltage. Minimum compensation is 0.5 times the inductor’s falling-current slope, although equal to the falling slope is recommended because higher values provide no additional stability benefit. An external resistor from RSC to AVSS sets the compensation.

The devices support Type 2A or Type 2B frequency compensation. Type 2A adds CHF for high-frequency noise attenuation. Component selection begins with the desired crossover frequency and involves calculating RCOMP, CCOMP, and, optionally, CHF based on the power-stage transconductance, dominant pole, and output-capacitor ESR zero. Thermal shutdown stops switching above a typical junction temperature of 175°C and restarts the power-up sequence below 160°C.

A 500-kHz synchronous push-pull design using the TPS7H5001-SP and GaN FETs produces 5 V and includes a 205-kΩ timing resistor; 10-kΩ and 1.4-kΩ output-feedback resistors; approximately 25 ns dead time; a 49.9-kΩ leading-edge-blank-time resistor; and a 33-nF soft-start capacitor providing about 7.5 ms startup. The design targets 35% duty cycle, a transformer turns-ratio value of 2.5, and 40 µH primary inductance. Primary GaN FETs are rated 170 V, while an 80-V synchronous rectifier is used. The output inductor is 0.47 µH. At least 1.3 mF of output capacitance is required, but 2.3 mF is used for radiation-induced single-event-transient mitigation. Cycle-by-cycle limiting begins at roughly 35 A, with a 45% margin over the 24.25-A maximum peak inductor current; a 1:100 current-sense transformer and 7.5-Ω sense resistor are used. Other selected values include a 3.3-nF hiccup capacitor and a 102-kΩ slope-compensation resistor. Type 2A compensation uses a 10-kHz crossover with RCOMP of 40.2 kΩ, CCOMP of 15 nF, and CHF of 47 pF. Testing may require optimization of compensation, blank time, RCD-clamp values, and other parameters.

The controller supply range is 4–14 V and requires at least a 0.1-µF VIN-to-AVSS bypass capacitor, preferably low-ESR ceramic placed close to the device. Layout guidance emphasizes separating feedback and control traces from noisy switching signals, minimizing switch-node area and high-dv/dt/high-di/dt loops, keeping AVSS separate from power ground except at one connection, using short and wide current traces, and placing filtering, compensation, and bypass components near their associated pins. An optional LC output filter can reduce ripple, with damping available for high-frequency peaking.

Application information is provided without warranty, with customers responsible for component suitability, validation, and testing. The document also lists radiation reports, evaluation-module guides, support resources, revision history, and package and orderable information subject to change.

The former Johnson Publishing Company headquarters in Chicago, once home to Ebony and Jet, received landmark status and was sold for $10 million. A developer plans a $20 million conversion into 150 luxury apartments while preserving the magazines’ façade signs.

The Nigerian Federal Government unveiled plans for several development projects in the South-East, including the Assumpta Science Centre in Owerri, Imo State. The Ministry of Science and Technology entered an MoU with the Vatican City’s Pontifical Council for Culture concerning the centre. Minister Ogbonnaya Onu said science, technology and innovation would support economic diversification and national development, while Imo State Governor Rochas Okorocha pledged support for the project’s completion.

Duane Boning welcomed students in Cambridge and Singapore to MIT 2.830J, Control of Manufacturing Processes, co-taught with David Hardt, with Hayden Taylor serving as teaching assistant. Lectures were videotaped and linked between the locations, with seating available for students wishing to opt out. Course materials—including notes, readings, assignments, and weekly problem sets—were distributed through the class website; lecture slides were generally posted a day in advance, but the instructor would not provide printed copies. Classes missed because of holidays in one location would be available online to students in the other.

Students were advised to have substantial experience with at least one manufacturing process, whether through coursework such as manufacturing physics or microfabrication or through industrial experience, and to have basic probability and statistics knowledge. Semiconductor fabrication would receive additional emphasis, although the course would also cover macroscopic processes such as forming, forging, and metalworking.

Two required textbooks were introduced: Gary May and Costas Spanos’s *Semiconductor Process Control* and Douglas Montgomery’s *Introduction to Statistical Quality Control*. The first focused on semiconductor process control, while the second covered statistical quality control, experimental design, and related statistical methods. Both were available on reserve at the MIT library.

Assessment consisted of approximately eight individual weekly problem sets during the first two-thirds of the semester, two quizzes, and a team project replacing weekly problem sets during the final third. No final exam was given. Problem sets accounted for about 40 percent of the grade and quizzes for another 40 percent. Although students could discuss problems, each weekly submission required an independent explanation of the reasoning behind the answer. Teams, typically comprising three students, would complete a substantial project involving process diagnosis, improvement, optimization, robustness, yield modeling, or defect modeling. Projects could draw on shareable work or research data, and required a joint report and presentations during the final two class periods.

The course emphasized understanding, modeling, and controlling manufacturing variation in order to maximize quality and conformance to specifications. Cost, throughput, flexibility, equipment efficiency, setup time, energy use, material consumption, and rework were discussed as secondary considerations and as factors that interact with quality. The instructors stressed that each unit operation must operate effectively because problems cannot simply be corrected through final inspection.

Boning described a manufacturing process as a transformation of a workpiece’s geometry or material properties through equipment and a controlled physical environment. Product characteristics could be represented as outputs determined by controllable settings, fixed process parameters, and disturbances. The planned curriculum moved from statistical process control, used to detect deviations and equipment problems, to empirical process modeling and design of experiments, including response-surface methods, optimization, and robustness. It would then examine feedback control, in which control settings are adjusted in response to observed disturbances.

Examples illustrated why variation becomes increasingly important as dimensions shrink. In semiconductor manufacturing, feature sizes of 90 and 65 nanometers made dimensional control and compensation for variability central concerns. Other examples included microfluidic channels, high-density electrical connectors, and assembled products whose dimensional imperfections accumulate. Hardt noted that automotive production often controls variation more effectively than one-off aircraft assembly because higher volume enables processes to reach a stable state, while manufacturing changes can also introduce new variability. The discussion also covered industry progression from extensive inspection toward process control, rework, and yield improvement, including the example of testing and sorting chips according to maximum operating frequency.

This beginner guide describes CJ Affiliate (Commission Junction), an affiliate network operating since 1998 that connects advertisers with publishers. CJ tracks sales or leads generated by publishers, pays commissions according to program terms, and handles payments and technical issues. It offers thousands of programs across nearly every niche, promotional tools, granular reporting, and account-manager support.

Applicants join for free with a website or social media profile containing relevant content and an audience in the United States or Canada. They must create an account, provide site statistics and a profile description, complete payment and tax information, and await approval. Approved users can search and apply for programs, then promote them through affiliate links in blog posts and track clicks, sales, and commissions via the dashboard.

The guide considers CJ legitimate and long-established, with an easy-to-use interface, no monthly or annual fees, and options including direct deposit, checks, and Payoneer. It notes a learning curve and potentially strict approval process, and emphasizes quality content and possible alternatives if CJ is unsuitable.

The Eagles held Monday morning training camp practice before Thursday’s preseason game against the Buffalo Bills. Cornerback Ronald Darby, acquired in the Jordan Matthews trade, joined the first-team defense; coach Jim Schwartz said Darby was still learning the defensive calls. Updates were also provided on Alshon Jeffery and Carson Wentz.

The excerpt documents terminal functions, configuration, operating conditions, and timing for a TI DaVinci digital media processor. Analog composite/S-Video outputs drive 75-ohm loads in normal mode and require specified feedback or load resistors; bypass-mode connections differ, and unused or powered-down pins remain unconnected. Supply tables define required 1.8-V, 1.8/3.3-V I/O, 3.3-V analog, and variable core rails, including mandatory connections and capacitor or ground requirements.

At reset deassertion, BTMODE[15:0] is latched to select primary and fallback boot sequences, GPMC/XIP options, Ethernet PHY mode, and PCIe addressing. ROM tables identify pins configured for XIP, NAND, I2C, MMC/SD, SPI, EMAC, PCIe, and UART boots. PINCNTL1–270 MUXMODE registers select pin functions, with zero tri-stating outputs. Pullup/pulldown guidance prevents floating inputs and includes typical 1-kΩ and 20-kΩ resistor suggestions.

The device uses L3/L4 switch-fabric interconnects and core-logic, memory, and switchable power domains. SmartReflex/DVFS adjusts domain voltage and frequency, SRAM can enter shutdown with data loss, and specified power sequencing and decoupling are required. POR, warm, watchdog, software, test, and local resets are described with PCIe and EMAC reset isolation, reset pin states, clock sources and PLLs, SYSCLK limits, and ARM/DSP interrupt routing. Timing sections cover transitions and board routing, while peripheral sections describe DCAN, EDMA, AET, trace, JTAG, and a three-port gigabit EMAC switch supporting MII, GMII, RMII, RGMII, and MDIO.

This study translated the Revised Waterloo Footedness Questionnaire (WFQ-R) into modern standard Arabic (WFQ-Ar), adapted it for Saudi culture, and evaluated its measurement properties. Adaptation followed Beaton’s five-stage process: independent forward translations, synthesis, back-translation, expert review, and pilot testing. Convenience sampling recruited 320 Arabic-speaking adults from across Saudi Arabia; 30 participated in pilot testing and 290 completed the final questionnaire twice, one week apart. Minor adaptations included clarifying item 9 and replacing abbreviated response options with full words.

Among the 290 main participants, the mean age was 29.9 years, 54.1% were female, and 90.3% reported a right-foot preference using a ball-kicking question. Pilot interviews and expert review supported the WFQ-Ar’s face and content validity, and no floor or ceiling effects were found. Exploratory factor analysis identified one factor explaining 55.79% of the extracted variance, with item loadings of 0.56–0.82. The questionnaire had high internal consistency (Cronbach’s α=0.93) and test-retest reliability (ICC=0.94; 95% CI 0.93–0.95). The standard error of measurement was 4.5 points, or 10% of the total score. WFQ-Ar scores correlated significantly with the single-item foot-dominance measure (r=0.48, p<0.001), and Bland–Altman analysis showed acceptable agreement between test and retest scores.

The findings indicate that the WFQ-Ar is a valid and reliable measure of footedness for clinical and research use. Because participants were Saudi adults without disabilities and the translation used modern standard Arabic, local validation is recommended before use in other Arabic-speaking countries or populations.

CoreWeave shares rose as much as 8% after the cloud provider introduced tools for individual developers to build AI agents. Its serverless reinforcement learning service automatically adjusts computing capacity; tests showed it could train models faster at 40% lower cost than running Nvidia H100 GPUs locally, without affecting model quality. The launch followed CoreWeave’s $1 billion acquisition of Weights and Biases and complements its GPU-rental business.

Lasting peace requires equality among nations based on rights and common strength, not territorial equality or individual power. Governments derive just authority from the consent of the governed, and peoples cannot be transferred between sovereignties as property. Stability also requires freedom and justice for all, including an independent Poland and safeguards for peoples living under governments hostile to their welfare. Nations should have access to major sea routes through territorial cessions or neutralized rights of way, while the seas must remain legally and practically free for commerce and international intercourse. This requires limits on naval armaments and international cooperation to keep the seas safe, leading to the broader need to limit armies and military preparations. Statesmen must address these issues candidly, make concessions, and accommodate national policies to peace rather than continue building disproportionate armaments. The speaker presents these views as reflecting the position of the U.S. government and the wishes of Americans, liberals, and humanity worldwide.

Seasonal trading exploits recurring price patterns linked to factors such as business cycles, weather, news, and holidays. Silver historically performs best from December through February and from July through August; January and July are positive 69.5% and 63.6% of the time, while June and September are the weakest months. The pattern may reflect industrial users placing annual orders early in the year.

A backtested strategy since 2001 buys silver in December and sells in February, then buys in July and sells in August. Holding silver for five months annually, it earned 3.9 percentage points more per year than buy-and-hold, with a risk-adjusted return of 26.93% versus 7.33% and maximum drawdown of -23.34% versus -71.65%.
Parliament will adjourn early on February 7, 2018, to prepare for President Nana Akufo-Addo’s February 8 State of the Nation Address. Members were urged to arrive by 9:15 a.m. and not bring guests.

A March 30, 2001 email compiled reports on California’s electricity crisis and related federal and international developments. California regulators approved utility rate increases of up to 46%. Gov. Gray Davis sought another $500 million for state purchases of power for Southern California Edison and Pacific Gas & Electric, bringing purchases to $4.7 billion since January. The utilities began repaying the state, including a combined payment of more than $105 million. PG&E estimated that 69% of residential customers would face increases, while SMUD proposed surcharges affecting all 525,000 of its ratepayers.

To reduce shortages and blackouts, California pursued conservation and expedited power-plant development. More than 190 energy bills were introduced, including two proposals allocating about $1 billion for programs that could cut summer demand by as much as 4,000 megawatts. The state also accelerated permits for gas-fired peaking plants, eased certain environmental and discharge requirements, offered incentives, and planned to purchase fuel and guarantee operators a reasonable profit. Environmental and public-health groups opposed these measures, citing pollution risks and reduced oversight. Grid operators forecast a possible 7% June power shortfall, partly because drought had reduced Northwestern imports. California’s controller projected a $7.4 billion shortfall over 18 months and $26.8 billion in power purchases, though the Department of Finance disputed that estimate.

Other measures included proposed reinstatement of penalties that had totaled $200 million under Southern California Edison’s interruptible-power program; advance blackout information for San Francisco and Huntington Beach; and an electronic notification system under consideration. Police had issued no citations under a vague order requiring large businesses to reduce outdoor lighting by 50%. Political disputes continued over access to state power contracts, Davis’s handling of rate increases and conservation, and possible ballot initiatives. Bush called energy a paramount concern, rejected the Kyoto Protocol, supported opening Arctic National Wildlife Refuge to drilling, and faced international and religious criticism. Canada offered increased oil and gas exports, while other reports examined San Jose’s electricity needs and EPRIsolutions’ work on distributed generation, efficiency, cogeneration and microgrids.

The ADS868xW supports an internal or external 4.096-V reference, selected by the INTREF_DIS bit of RANGE_SEL_REG. The internal reference is enabled by default, is factory-trimmed, and is temperature compensated from −40°C to +125°C. When selected, REFIO becomes an output and requires at least 4.7 µF of decoupling; it must not directly drive external loads. Mechanical stress and solder-reflow cycles can shift the reference voltage, with multiple reflows causing additional shifts, so boards with repeated reflow exposure should mount the device in the second pass. In external-reference mode, a 4.096-V source is applied to REFIO and the internal buffer drives REFCAP, requiring at least 10 µF plus a nearby 1 µF for high-frequency decoupling. The external source should be appropriately filtered, and the buffer must not drive external loads. Reference-buffer temperature drift is typically 0.5 ppm/°C and at most 2 ppm/°C.

The 16-bit ADC supports single-ended and differential inputs in bipolar and unipolar ranges and uses straight-binary output. FSR equals PFS minus NFS, and LSB size equals FSR/2^16. Alarm functionality includes programmable input high- and low-threshold alarms with hysteresis and fixed-typical AVDD alarms at 4.7 V and 5.3 V. Active and tripped flags are available in ALARM_REG; active flags clear at the end of each conversion, while tripped flags remain set until the register is read. Alarm status can be accessed through the active-high ALARM pin, the alarm registers, or flags appended to conversion data.

The multiSPI interface combines input and output shift registers, configuration registers, and a protocol unit, presenting a 32-bit input-output shift register to the host. Standard SPI operation uses CONVST/CS, SCLK, SDI, and SDO-0; RST is tied to DVDD and RVS can be monitored. In a daisy chain, devices share CONVST/CS and SCLK, have identical configuration, and connect sequentially through SDO-0 and SDI. An optimal frame contains 32 × N clock edges for N devices, and data returns from device N through device 1. System throughput decreases proportionally as devices are added.

The device operates in RESET, ACQ, and CONV states. The active-low RST pin can trigger either an application reset, which restores configuration-register defaults, or a power-on reset, which also resets the PGA, ADC driver, reference, and other internal circuitry. Reset is exited by holding RST high with CONVST/CS and SCLK low, after which the device enters ACQ and RVS goes high. ACQ acquires the analog input and can use low-power NAP mode. A rising CONVST/CS edge starts conversion; the device ignores further CONVST/CS transitions until conversion ends and then returns to ACQ. Hosts can monitor RVS or wait for the maximum conversion time.

Programming uses nine configuration registers and supports byte and half-word commands, including register read, write, set, and clear operations. A transfer frame begins on the falling edge of CONVST/CS, loads the output shift register, and accepts shifted-in command data; its ending rising edge decodes the command and starts conversion. A 32-clock frame is optimal and required for writes. Shorter frames are invalid for writes but can return requested output bits; in longer frames, the final 32 shifted-in bits form the command. The following output word can contain a register read, the latest conversion result, or a configured fixed pattern. Optional appended data consists, in order, of device address, input range, AVDD alarm flags, input alarm flags, and parity.

Four legacy SPI-compatible clock and phase modes support configuration. Read protocols include single-SDO and dual-SDO legacy modes and source-synchronous operation. Dual-SDO mode launches two bits per clock and therefore transfers the same data in half as many cycles. Source-synchronous mode supplies an output clock on RVS, selectable from the external SCLK or an internal device clock. SDI_MODE selects the applicable legacy protocol for both reads and writes.

The configuration registers provide device identification for daisy-chain addressing; reset, NAP, and power-down control; input and output protocol selection; output flags, parity, and test patterns; reference and input-range selection; alarm flags; and programmable alarm thresholds and hysteresis. Writes to RST_PWRCTL_REG require first writing the protection key 69h to address 05h.

An eight-channel industrial input-module design combines an ADS8681W with a MUX36D08 differential multiplexer. Each channel is software-configurable as voltage or current, supports standard industrial ranges, and uses the ADC’s fast-settling input stage, including settling to 1% accuracy in under 5 µs. An NTC-thermistor example demonstrates how programmable thresholds and hysteresis improve temperature alarms and reject noise near the limits.

The device uses separate AVDD and DVDD supplies, with recommended 10 µF and 1 µF decoupling. PCB layout should separate analog and digital signals, keep bypass and reference capacitors close to their pins with minimal vias, use short ground paths, and avoid placing vias between supply pins and capacitors. NAP mode reduces power between conversions and is exited by pulling CONVST/CS low after the specified wake-up delay. Power-down mode powers down analog blocks while retaining the interface and register contents; the host must clear PWRDN and allow the specified power-up delay before resuming operations.

India’s probable T20I squad for the three-match series against England in January 2017 is likely to differ significantly because several senior players are injured or resting. Shikhar Dhawan and KL Rahul are expected to open, with the third slot contested between Mandeep Singh and Rishabh Pant. Virat Kohli and MS Dhoni are certainties, while Ajinkya Rahane’s fitness is uncertain. Manish Pandey, Karun Nair, and potentially recalled Suresh Raina may fill middle-order roles, with Deepak Hooda likely preferred over Yuvraj Singh. With Ravichandran Ashwin, Ravindra Jadeja, Jayant Yadav, Axar Patel, Mohammed Shami, and Umesh Yadav unavailable or likely rested, the bowling options are Amit Mishra, Kuldeep Yadav, Shahbaz Nadeem, Jasprit Bumrah, Ashish Nehra, and Bhuvneshwar Kumar. The squad will also serve as preparation for the June ICC Champions Trophy.

This continuation patent application describes methods for using a single video bitstream with both standard dynamic range (SDR) and high dynamic range (HDR) systems. An encoder receives an HDR master, a reference SDR master, and, in some embodiments, target SDR display properties. It derives a color-volume transform, such as tone mapping, scaling, or lookup tables, that converts HDR values to SDR values closely matching the reference after simulated SDR display operations. The encoder may also apply color-space, transfer-function, quantization, and chroma-subsampling operations and generate metadata describing how to reverse the conversion. In one embodiment, SDR values are encoded and HDR decoders reconstruct HDR values using the metadata. In another, HDR values are encoded and SDR decoders use metadata to downconvert them. The transform can be selected through candidate testing and distance minimization or derived through scaling relationships.

The city’s four-month LIHI contract paid $75,000 to operate Camp Second Chance and provide case management. It set stay expectations, required continuous gate security, barred residents under 18, and gave campers no veto over LIHI decisions. A second-year renewal was under discussion, while this year’s contract remained unfinalized.

A federal judge temporarily barred the Trump administration from proceeding with federal worker layoffs related to the government shutdown. Judge Susan Illston issued the restraining order after unions filed suit alleging the administration unlawfully used the shutdown to justify staff cuts. The pause covers multiple agencies, including Commerce, Education, Energy, Health and Human Services, Housing and Urban Development, Homeland Security, and Treasury. An OMB filing identified 4,132–4,232 workers marked for layoffs, while OMB chief Russell Vought said total layoffs would reach about 10,000. Treasury and HHS had the largest termination lists, and some CDC workers mistakenly received reduction-in-force notices. Union leaders called the layoffs unlawful. Furloughed workers reported financial hardship, prompting bridge-loan programs, and the administration may appeal.

Model Ella Ravenscroft, 20, underwent surgery to remove four moles after they changed during two years of using sunbeds once or twice weekly. Left with several scars, she is warning others about sunbed risks and urging people to have changed, itchy, bleeding or unusual moles checked promptly.

The article says sunbed use can increase melanoma risk by 16–20%. Almost 500 people are diagnosed with melanoma annually in Greater Manchester, and around one-fifth die. Most moles are harmless, but changes in size, shape, colour or texture, uneven colouring, inflammation, or growths that bleed, ooze, crust or do not heal may require medical attention. Experts advise people to know what their skin normally looks like and show a doctor any unusual changes, as early treatment can prevent melanoma from spreading.

Sprint and The Sprint Foundation launched the five-year 1Million Project, which aims to connect 1 million high school students lacking home internet. Beginning Aug. 15, Sprint will connect 180,000 low-income students in more than 1,300 schools across 32 states this school year. Participants receive a free smartphone, tablet, or hotspot with 3GB of high-speed LTE data monthly for up to four years. Sprint estimates its five-year contribution of services, support, and staff at $2.16 billion.

Gulf stock markets mostly fell on Wednesday in modest volumes, led by profit-taking in Qatar, whose index dropped 2.3 percent to 8,916 points. Qatar Islamic Bank fell 4.7 percent and Qatar National Bank 2.1 percent in heavy volume after both had surged on MSCI's mid-May announcement of higher index weightings; passive fund buying continued while other investors took profits. Dubai fell 0.5 percent to 2,909 points, slipping below its level when the UAE announced long-term visas and higher foreign ownership ceilings, with DAMAC down 2.5 percent; DXB Entertainments rose 4.1 percent. Abu Dhabi fell 0.4 percent as Aldar Properties dropped 1.9 percent. Saudi Arabia edged up 0.1 percent, with Al Tayyar gaining 1.0 percent after repaying a 307 million riyal long-term loan early. Egypt's index dropped 1.4 percent, with Talat Mostafa down 6.3 percent. Kuwait, Bahrain and Oman also declined slightly.

Hexane is an organic, six-carbon hydrocarbon solvent found in plants’ volatile fractions and gasoline. Pure hexane is used in laboratories, while solvent-based hexane is widely used to extract vegetable oils, clean textile, printing, furniture and leather products, and produce glues, gasoline, rubber and cement. It also removes unwanted tastes and odors and is used in cooking-oil production. Excess inhalation can cause weakness, numbness, blurred vision, headache and fatigue; OSHA’s permissible exposure limit is 500 ppm. A sodium hydroxide–methanol alternative for extracting soybean oil has been implemented successfully, though high moisture increases methanol use. China dominates the global hexane market, while North American and European demand is expected to grow with automotive rubber demand.

Josie Goodenow will speak to Laguna Beach Garden Club members about native bees, including the Blue Orchard Mason Bee, and European honeybees on Oct. 13. The event begins with a 9:30 a.m. social, followed by a 10 a.m. general meeting. The public is welcome, and first-time guests attend free.

Pennsylvania parents Nicole Sciortino and Vincent Licciardello, both 30, were charged with child endangerment after leaving their children, ages 10 and 11, unsupervised for three days while Sciortino was in Florida and Licciardello occasionally dropped off food. Police found the home deplorable and the thermostat at 58 degrees. Investigators said the children were not alone for weeks, as alleged. Each parent received $10,000 unsecured bail, and the children are staying with family friends.

A medRxiv preprint evaluated cerebrospinal fluid tumor-derived DNA (CSF-tDNA) analysis in patients with advanced lung adenocarcinoma and suspected leptomeningeal disease (LMD). Using a lung cancer-specific CAPP-Seq targeted sequencing panel, investigators analyzed 81 CSF, blood, and tissue samples from 24 patients. A prospective subset of 12 patients with refractory LMD received osimertinib and underwent serial lumbar punctures before and approximately three weeks after treatment.

CSF-tDNA variant allele fractions were substantially higher than plasma circulating tumor DNA VAFs (median 32.7% versus 1.8%; P<0.0001) and were moderately correlated with plasma VAFs (ρ=0.45; P=0.03). For definitive LMD, CSF-tDNA had 91.7% sensitivity, compared with 81.8% for cytology and 80.0% for MRI. Detectable CSF-tDNA was also present in four of nine cytology-negative samples. CSF-tDNA detection at initial lumbar puncture was associated with poorer overall survival (HR 7.1; P=0.02), as was positivity for both CSF-tDNA and cytology relative to negativity for both (HR 8.4; P=0.015).

In nine EGFR-mutant patients with matched pre- and post-targeted-therapy samples, putative resistance mutations were detected in peripheral blood in seven patients, all of whom had CNS progression, but were much less common in matched CSF. Cases illustrated differences between compartments, including blood-detected KRAS G12A, EGFR T790M, and ERBB2 amplification that were absent from CSF, suggesting spatially distinct resistance mechanisms.

In the prospective osimertinib cohort, patients with CNS progression had elevated follow-up CSF-tDNA VAFs, whereas patients without progression showed a trend toward lower VAFs. Pretreatment CSF-tDNA VAF was not prognostic, but post-osimertinib CSF-tDNA VAF strongly predicted CNS progression (HR 6.2; P=0.009). CSF osimertinib penetration was not significantly correlated with CSF-tDNA concentration or VAF change.

The authors concluded that CSF-tDNA detection is feasible and may improve LMD diagnostic sensitivity, support prognostication and treatment-response monitoring, and help guide strategies that account for differences in resistance mechanisms between CSF and peripheral blood. Limitations included the small cohort, few paired CSF samples collected at resistance, and limited CSF volume. Prospective studies are needed to validate clinical utility.
Greg De Vries is praised as a skilled, physical defenseman, while Jon Klemm is called underrated. Skoula is described as a promising defenseman with speed, strength, size, poise, and a good shot.

In 2016–17, 719 people in Devon, Cornwall and the Isles of Scilly were admitted to hospital with eating disorders, including two children under 10, 13 aged 10–12 and 91 aged 13–15. Admissions reached a record high, more than twice the 298 recorded in 2010–11. Women and girls accounted for 94% of cases; anorexia was the most common diagnosis (45%), followed by bulimia (24%). Young Minds urged early intervention and timely community care. Beat said admissions represent only the most severe cases and may reflect increased awareness, bed availability or insufficient outpatient provision.

NVIDIA Corporation reported an underwriting agreement with Morgan Stanley & Co. LLC, as representative of the underwriters, to issue $5.0 billion of unsecured senior notes: $1.25 billion each of 0.309% notes due June 15, 2023; 0.584% notes due June 14, 2024; 1.550% notes due June 15, 2028; and 2.000% notes due June 15, 2031. Net proceeds were approximately $4.98 billion after underwriting discounts and estimated offering expenses and were intended for general corporate purposes, potentially including repayment of debt.

The notes are governed by a September 2016 base indenture with Wells Fargo Bank, National Association, as trustee, as supplemented by an officers’ certificate dated June 16, 2021. The indenture includes customary covenants and default provisions. NVIDIA may redeem the notes before maturity with 10 to 60 days’ notice, generally at a make-whole price, subject to stated exceptions. A change of control combined with an investment-grade downgrade by Moody’s and S&P triggers a requirement to repurchase the affected notes at 101% of principal plus accrued interest. The notes rank equally with NVIDIA’s unsecured and unsubordinated debt but are structurally subordinated to subsidiary liabilities and effectively subordinated to secured debt.

Poor medication adherence is common among hemodialysis patients, who may take 10–20 tablets daily; reported non-adherence exceeds 50% and contributes to inadequate complication management and increased mortality. Person-centered care (PCC) combines evidence-based treatment with attention to patient preferences, goals, and shared decision-making. Although continuity, needs-driven practice, and coordinated care may improve adherence, empirical evidence is limited. Trust in physicians is theorized to mediate relationships among PCC, physician-patient interactions, and adherence.

This multicenter, cross-sectional study examined Japanese patients at six outpatient hemodialysis facilities. It aimed to assess interrelationships among PCC, trust in physicians, and medication adherence, and to test the mediating role of physician trust. Eligible adults had kidney failure, received hemodialysis or combined hemodialysis and peritoneal dialysis, regularly attended participating facilities, and could complete questionnaires. Patients without regular prescriptions or with severe dementia or complete blindness were excluded. Data were collected from April 2022 to February 2023 using paper questionnaires and informed consent. Medication adherence was measured with the Japanese 12-item ASK-12 scale, covering inconvenience/forgetfulness, treatment beliefs, and behavior; higher scores indicated greater adherence difficulties.

As the Supreme Court prepares for its 2025-26 term, it will consider Victor Tony Jones's request to stay his execution. Sentenced to death in 1993 for the December 1990 murders of Matilda and Jacob Nestor, Jones is scheduled to be executed Tuesday at 6 p.m. EDT. The court has denied every stay request this year despite more than 30 emergency applications. If executed, Jones would be the year's 34th, prompting debate over the execution surge and the Court's role.

Executions fell for a decade, reaching a low of 11 in 2021, amid drug shortages and debate over lethal injection drugs. Biden's 2021 federal moratorium, extended by Garland over pentobarbital concerns, ended with Trump's Jan. 20 order; 33 executions had occurred by Tuesday, with Florida, where Jones would be the 13th, driving the surge. The court also ruled for death row inmates in three 2024-25 cases and will weigh how multiple IQ scores should guide determinations of intellectual disability, a case now set for early December.

Archive360 announced that Archive2Azure was a finalist for Best Cloud Storage Solution and FastCollect for PSTs was a finalist for Best Data Storage Solution in the 2017 DBTA Readers’ Choice Awards. Archive2Azure manages legacy and unstructured data in Microsoft Azure for retention, compliance, and eDiscovery readiness, while FastCollect automates PST discovery, migration, storage, deletion, and auditing. Archive360 has migrated tens of petabytes to the Microsoft Cloud since 2012, and its solutions are available directly and through partners. Winners were scheduled to be featured on the DBTA website and in the August 2017 issue of Database Trends and Applications magazine.

The U.S. passenger-car market was worth about $270 billion at retail in 2016, with sales projected to remain roughly flat through 2021. GM, Ford, and Chrysler held about 46% of 2018 market share but operated with low margins and high exit barriers due to specialized assets and the approximately three million industry jobs. Foreign manufacturers had expanded their U.S. production, while limited brand loyalty created opportunities for new entrants. A fragmented, highly profitable supplier industry was expected to gain value from advanced systems and software as electric vehicles require fewer components.

Customer behavior and transportation trends were changing. Millennials were becoming the fastest-growing buyer segment, researching vehicles extensively online and favoring compact cars and crossovers. Consumers increasingly disliked dealership negotiations, and 75% of respondents in a large Accenture survey would consider online purchasing. Urban residents were also adopting public transit, ride-hailing, bike-sharing, and scooter-sharing, raising questions about whether private ownership would give way to mobility-as-a-service. Meanwhile, declining battery costs, government incentives, and expanding charging infrastructure supported EV adoption; autonomous driving and connected-car services were also being developed by automakers and technology companies.

Tesla was founded in 2003 by engineers without automotive-industry backgrounds and was led by Elon Musk from 2008. Its “Master Plan” called for entering through the luxury market, using early models to establish demand, and then moving rapidly toward higher-volume, lower-priced vehicles. The $100,000 Roadster, the Model S sedan, and the Model X crossover established Tesla in the luxury EV segment, although each faced delays, technical problems, and missed projections. The $35,000 Model 3 marked Tesla’s first mass-market effort.

Model 3 production exposed major operational difficulties. Tesla vertically integrated much of its design and manufacturing, built battery packs at its $5 billion Gigafactory with Panasonic, and expanded its heavily automated Fremont plant. Musk conceded that excessive automation had been a mistake, while skipped beta testing left incomplete systems, manual assembly, component-quality problems, and substantial rework. Tesla eventually reached 5,000 Model 3s per week, but only after missing its original schedule by more than six months. In the second quarter of 2018, Tesla reported a $743 million net loss on $4 billion in revenue, leading some investors to question its viability.

Unlike traditional automakers, Tesla sold directly through salaried company stores, though dealership laws restricted expansion in several states. It operated its own service centers, Supercharger network, and over-the-air software updates. Its “Master Plan, Part Deux” proposed fully autonomous vehicles that owners could share with other drivers, potentially supporting a Tesla ride-hailing service. Musk expected the platform to launch by the end of 2019, subject chiefly to regulatory approval. The case concludes with uncertainty over whether Tesla could overcome its production and financial challenges while transforming an industry increasingly oriented toward EVs, autonomy, connectivity, and alternative mobility.

An email from Ann Schmidt dated July 26, 2001, compiles media coverage focused on Enron and related energy and business issues. Fortune ranked Enron No. 16 on its Global 500 list. BusinessWeek reported a third consecutive quarterly decline in corporate profits: a survey of 90 companies showed net income down 34%, with Enron’s 196% revenue growth accounting for most of an 8% overall sales increase.

Dow Jones Newswires reported that federal electricity price caps and low Western power prices were causing developers to cancel peaking plants, reducing projected Northwest capacity by up to 1,000 megawatts and raising reliability concerns. Some industry participants disputed the caps’ role, citing conservation, lower demand and new generation.

Reuters coverage described the Bonn climate agreement’s emissions-trading and clean-development mechanisms, which were beginning to influence corporate investment strategies. It also reported that Kobe Steel planned to borrow 165 billion yen for a wholesale electricity business, while noting Enron’s interest in Japan’s deregulated market.

Enron canceled its Miami-Dade power-plant option and focused on Deerfield Beach, where a county moratorium had stalled construction. The Washington Post reported that White House adviser Karl Rove delayed divesting stocks and met with officials from six companies, including Intel and Enron, prompting conflict-of-interest concerns and demands for a Justice Department review; Rove sold the holdings in June.

TheStreet.com reported that Enron executives Kenneth Lay and Jeffrey Skilling praised the company’s stock while selling substantial shares, creating mixed signals for investors. Another article said Enron’s broadband business had shifted from $17 million in pretax income to a $109 million loss, prompting scaled-back operations and reduced analyst valuations, while the company’s core wholesale energy business remained solid.

Coach Sutter said his team would maintain its established approach rather than make changes simply because it had advanced deep in the playoffs. He described the opponent as skilled, hard-working, bigger and quicker up front, but said one game did not justify major adjustments. He emphasized forechecking with five players, limiting the defense’s ability to move pucks to quicker centers such as Zajac, Josefson and Henrique, and managing line combinations and ice time as fatigue increases. He also noted that poor ice conditions and snow required players to reinforce their positioning and puck movement.

Sutter said the teams were close and that bad bounces, calls or changes could decide games, while expecting both teams to play hard. He described home ice as an advantage because of the final change and the ability to give a star player extra shifts, but said chasing matchups late causes fatigue and positional problems. He rejected the idea that playing at home or away materially changed his team and said it would have preferred to play the previous day and travel home.

The F-Pace has helped boost Jaguar's sales and may save the company. A 2018 F-Pace SVR is being finalized and filmed at the Nürburgring, likely with a 5.0-liter supercharged V8 producing 500 or 575 HP.

DLSS 4 marks NVIDIA’s first shift from CNN-based models since DLSS 2, introducing transformer-based AI for Super Resolution, Ray Reconstruction and DLAA. Transformers use self-attention to detect longer-range patterns across larger pixel windows and scale to twice as many parameters with greater Tensor Core use. Super Resolution combines lower-resolution samples, motion data and prior-frame feedback to produce higher-resolution images with better temporal stability, less ghosting, more motion detail and improved anti-aliasing. Ray Reconstruction uses a supercomputer-trained network to generate pixels between sampled rays, improving quality in challenging lighting and reducing denoiser artifacts. DLAA applies Super Resolution technology at native resolution to improve stability, motion detail and anti-aliasing.

Blackwell is designed to advance developer-created neural shaders, which train AI models to approximate complex rendering computations and can run on some prior-generation GPUs. The document traces GPU shaders from fixed-function pipelines through programmable vertex, pixel, geometry, tessellation, compute, mesh and ray-tracing stages. A Cooperative Vectors API for DX12 and Vulkan, created with Microsoft and paired with Slang features, allows Tensor Cores to be used from any shader. This enables neural texture compression and technologies including RTX Neural Materials, Neural Radiance Cache, RTX Skin and RTX Neural Faces.

Neural Materials approximates complex multilayer materials for real-time rendering. Neural Texture Compression compresses and decompresses textures more efficiently; a cited demo falls from 1,110 MB to 333 MB while increasing visual quality. Blackwell’s improved point-sampling rate accelerates Stochastic Texture Filtering. Neural Radiance Cache uses live-trained networks to infer many-bounce lighting from path-traced rays, reducing GPU work while improving indirect-light quality and scalability. RTX Skin applies real-time ray-traced subsurface scattering to translucent materials. RTX Neural Faces uses a TensorRT-optimized generative model, trained on many offline face images and conditions, to turn a rasterized face and 3D pose data into a more natural-looking face in real time.

The North Carolina Court of Appeals affirmed the dismissal with prejudice of Lewis Williamson’s appeal from the Town of Surf City’s closing of a 20-foot portion of North Shore Drive.

The Town followed the procedures required by N.C.G.S. § 160A-299, including adopting a resolution of intent, providing notice, conducting a public hearing, and approving a street-closing order. The closed right-of-way vested partly in Williamson and partly in Surf City, which owned adjacent property and sought the closure to construct improvements to its beach-access property.

Williamson argued that the Town’s intended use of the closed land for public facilities made the closure improper and that the statute permits only closure of an entire street. The court found that § 160A-299 does not restrict a town’s authority based on its intent when it follows the statutory procedures. It also held that the statute authorizes closing all or part of a street and distinguished *Wooten v. Town of Topsail Beach*, where the town had not complied with the required procedures and did not acquire an interest in the closed property.

MKM Partners raised Tutor Perini Corporation’s price target from $31 to $34 while retaining a buy rating. Other firms were mixed: FBR reaffirmed outperform with a $35 target, Zacks upgraded sell to hold, Sidoti downgraded buy to neutral and cut its target to $22, and Seaport upgraded accumulate to buy. TPC has a consensus Buy rating and $27.29 price target.

The company reported quarterly EPS of $0.57, below the $0.62 consensus estimate, and revenue of $1.33 billion. Revenue fell 0.6% year over year, while EPS declined from $0.68. Analysts forecast $1.92 EPS for the current year.

COO James A. Frost sold 7,500 shares for $215,925 and retained 439,726 shares. Insiders own 23.4% of TPC, while hedge funds and institutional investors own 82.52%. Tutor Perini provides general contracting, construction management, and design-build services through its Civil and two other segments.

The application discloses a rotating shaft mechanism and a foldable mobile terminal. The mechanism addresses the need for a specialized hinge that supports a flexible display without pulling, squeezing, or arching it, while reducing the folded terminal’s thickness and gaps.

The rotating shaft mechanism includes a main shaft assembly, a swing arm assembly, and a support assembly. Swing arms are connected to opposite housings and rotatably or slidably engage the main shaft. Connecting rods rotate around axes different from the corresponding swing-arm axes and slidably engage the swing arms, causing support plates on either side of the main shaft to rotate. Engaging gears synchronize the connecting rods and housings. A cam-based limiting mechanism, using engaging cams, protrusions, notches, and elastic parts, limits the folded and unfolded positions and may provide damping during folding.

The support plates support the flexible display when unfolded and, when folded, rotate with the main shaft to enclose space accommodating the display’s bent portion. This arrangement allows the non-adhesive display area to form a droplet or semicircular shape without bulging. The folded mechanism’s thickness is approximately equal to that of the two stacked housings.

The mobile terminal includes the rotating shaft mechanism, two housings, and a flexible display connected to the housings. A flexible blocking layer made of elastic steel or plastic may cover notches in the main shaft assembly. Its ends can be inserted into the housings or connected through movable swing rods so that it flexes and rotates with the mechanism, improving the folded terminal’s appearance.

Investing.com highlights seasonal market weakness, reduced liquidity, institutional rebalancing, tax-loss selling, and fading August optimism. Technical analysis suggests TLT could break resistance as yields fall, while a weakening dollar may support commodities; gold, yields, and dollar movements could shift risk sentiment. The page also features stock and cryptocurrency market stories, promotes AI-selected portfolios, and warns of trading risks, data limitations, and third-party content.

The passage introduces a study of COVID-19 forecasting for the USA, India, Brazil, Russia, and the UK, countries identified as among the most intensely affected by the pandemic.
