It describes COVID-19 as originating in Wuhan in December 2019 and notes that the WHO declared it a global pandemic on March 11, 2020. The study aims to forecast daily confirmed and death cases to support health planning, policy-making, and assessment of the pandemic’s scale.

Because single linear or nonlinear forecasting models can produce fluctuations and inaccurate predictions for dynamic COVID-19 time series, the study proposes hybrid models combining ARIMA with machine-learning methods. ARIMA is presented as a traditional approach for linear univariate series, while ANN, ARNN, and WBF are used to capture nonlinear patterns. The proposed models, ARNNS and SVMAR, are intended to improve short-term and long-term out-of-sample forecasts, reduce component-model errors, provide interpretability, and accommodate dynamic, robust, and seasonal behavior.

Daily confirmed and death-case data for the five countries were obtained from the Global Change Data Lab. The datasets have different starting dates but share a terminal date of January 15, 2021, and each contains more than 300 observations. Preliminary analysis indicates that the datasets are not normally distributed, and the epidemic curves had not yet displayed a clearly spiky, declining pattern. The passage also outlines the paper’s sections, covering data and preliminary analysis, model formulation, experimental results, discussion, and conclusions.

The United States supported a Rio Conference resolution urging the Second Hague Peace Conference to consider compulsory collection of public debts and other means of reducing conflicts over financial obligations. Its policy was not to use armed forces to collect ordinary contractual debts, citing respect for national sovereignty and concern that force could enable oppression and warfare, though exceptional cases involving fraud or treaty violations might justify it. The United States preferred international consideration of these distinctions at a conference representing both creditors and debtors.

The passage also described successful joint mediation by the United States and Mexico, which ended a war among Guatemala, Honduras, and Salvador. It argued that coordinated action by American republics could promote peaceful and reasonable handling of international disputes, strengthen international responsibility, and advance global peace.

Royalty North Partners Ltd. announced it granted 35,000 incentive stock options to directors, officers, employees and consultants, exercisable at C$1.47 per share and expiring October 6, 2022. It also awarded 37,500 restricted share rights to certain directors and senior officers, vesting fully over two years.

A Kuwaiti court sentenced Salem Buhan and Amira Hussein to death for torturing and killing their three-year-old daughter. The verdict is subject to appeals and supreme court review; executions are carried out by hanging.
Dr. Ian K. Smith’s *The Clean 20* advocates reducing processed foods without eliminating food groups, with 20 clean foods, a meal plan, 60 recipes and substitutions, and 20-minute workouts.

The River Witham railway bridge at Stamp End was built for the Manchester, Sheffield and Lincolnshire Railway, whose 1848 Lincoln–Grimsby line served Grimsby’s port and distributed fish inland. Engineer John Fowler used innovative iron box-girder technology, possibly making it Britain’s oldest surviving wrought-iron box-girder railway bridge still carrying trains. The bridge originally had a 74-foot central span with two timber side spans. Increasing train weights prompted major alterations: the side spans were replaced with steel plate girders around 1901–03, the central span was reinforced, and cross-girders were strengthened in 1948. A steel deck was added in 1968. Network Rail has since replaced the crossing in a £7m project.

A multicenter cross-sectional study assessed SARS-CoV-2 humoral immunity among 1,411 emergency-department patients at five university hospitals in North Rhine-Westphalia, Germany, from August to September 2022. Spike IgG was detected in 95.6% of participants, while nucleocapsid IgG was detected in 24.0%. Although 94.4% had received at least one vaccine dose, only 67.7% followed German vaccination recommendations, and 45.7% reported prior infection. Spike IgG levels increased with the number of vaccination or infection encounters and were lower in immunosuppressed participants. Nucleocapsid IgG status was the strongest predictor of spike IgG levels.

Pseudovirus testing found detectable neutralization against Wu01, BA.4/5, and BQ.1.1 in 94.4%, 84.9%, and 73.8% of participants, respectively. Neutralization against BQ.1.1 was 23.6-fold lower than against Wu01 and 4.2-fold lower than against BA.4/5. Spike IgG levels were the strongest overall predictor of neutralization, followed by factors such as previous infections, nucleocapsid IgG status, age, and vaccination history. However, low spike IgG levels did not reliably indicate neutralizing activity, particularly against immune-evasive BQ.1.1.

The findings indicate that prior vaccination or infection substantially contributes to humoral immunity, but neither antibody detection nor neutralization assays alone fully capture protection. The authors emphasized improving vaccine uptake and considering immune escape when assessing COVID-19 risk. The emergency-department sample was not representative of the general population, and the study lacked clinical outcomes for prior infections.

Researchers developed kirigami-inspired parachutes made from perforated Mylar disks. They open automatically, realign, and fall straight down regardless of their initial orientation. Concentric slits expand into a latticework vase that creates drag and slows payloads. In laboratory tests, they landed closer to targets than traditional parachutes or uncut disks. A 0.5-meter parachute slowed a 1-kilogram water bottle dropped from 60 meters to about 14 meters per second, versus 34 meters per second without one. Potential uses include humanitarian aid and drone package delivery, though their low drag makes human descent impractical. Researchers are also considering biodegradable materials and designs for imaging during planetary descents.

Intraday trading involves buying and selling financial instruments—such as stocks, futures, or forex—within the same trading day. It includes scalping, which targets small price fluctuations, and day trading, which targets larger daily movements while requiring positions to be closed before market close. The strategy seeks to profit from intraday price movements while limiting exposure to gaps and other risks. It is most common in forex and futures but is also used in stocks. Because intraday strategies are complex, difficult to backtest, and affected by noise, the article states that most traders lose money.

In the US, FINRA defines a pattern day trader as one who executes at least four day trades within five business days when those trades exceed 6% of total account trades. Such traders must maintain at least $25,000 in eligible equity before day trading and generally face a four-times maintenance-margin buying-power limit. Stock CFDs may offer higher leverage for smaller accounts but are prohibited to US traders.

The article recommends developing a personal trading plan and backtesting it for a statistical edge. Other guidance includes studying markets and relevant company fundamentals, setting realistic goals, avoiding crowd-following, selecting a regulated low-fee broker, trading highly liquid stocks, using a quantified or automated system, and reviewing results after groups of trades rather than after each trade.

An example hourly strategy on WTI crude oil futures, entering after consecutive lower lows and lower highs, performed poorly over 2000–2021, with a 47% win rate and an average trade of negative 0.11%. An out-of-sample test produced only 21 trades averaging 0.57%, with performance appearing to improve from July 2021. This illustrates the article’s claim that intraday strategies are less likely than daily strategies to pass out-of-sample testing.

The FAQ identifies high-liquidity, high-volatility markets as preferable and lists scalping, momentum, news-based trading, and trend following among common strategies. It says the first two hours after opening may offer strong liquidity and volatility, while required capital depends on the instruments and should cover trading costs and possible losses. Popular indicators include moving averages, MACD, Bollinger Bands, and RSI, although the authors caution against expecting them to work consistently on intraday data. The article states that stocks may offer the best opportunities and forex the least, and emphasizes that traders without a tested plan should avoid intraday trading.

The North Carolina Court of Appeals reversed the trial court's dismissal of defendant's controlled substance charges on double jeopardy grounds. Defendant was arrested in August 1997, and police seized about 1,300 grams of cocaine and 9,000 grams of marijuana. The Department of Revenue then assessed a drug tax of $456,574.26 under the Controlled Substance Tax Act, docketed it as a judgment in September 1997, and defendant paid part of it before trial. The trial court granted defendant's motion to dismiss the charges in February 1998.

The State argued the dismissal conflicted with State v. Ballenger and State v. Creason, which had upheld assessment and collection of the drug tax against constitutional challenges. Defendant relied on the Fourth Circuit's decision in Lynn v. West, but the court noted that only U.S. Supreme Court decisions bind North Carolina courts; lower federal appellate decisions carry only such persuasiveness as they reasonably command. The court concluded that reexamining Ballenger and Creason in light of Lynn v. West, or amending the tax statute, was beyond its province, and reversed the dismissal.
State v. Montecalvo (1996): the Ohio Supreme Court reversed the court of appeals' judgment, relying on State v. Szefcyk, decided the same day; Cook, J., did not participate.

Netflix fell 0.68% in premarket trading, likely following a Barron’s article about rising debt and content producers leaving for their own services, rather than Rhimes’s deal. Rhimes will move future shows to Netflix while continuing existing ABC programs. Disney plans a 2019 streaming service, and Netflix is acquiring Millarworld.

Container images should be documented so users can understand and reuse them. Recommended Dockerfile practices include documenting exposed ports with `EXPOSE`, defining parameter defaults and documenting environment variables with `ENV`, and adding maintainer, URL, and version metadata through `LABEL`. Standardized Label Schema labels allow multiple tools to consume the same image information. Stable APIs are also important for preserving sidecar compatibility.

The passage describes three tightly coupled, single-node container patterns:

- **Sidecar containers** augment application containers with reusable functionality.
- **Ambassador containers** broker interactions between applications and external services. Examples include routing requests to sharded Redis or Memcached backends, discovering environment-specific services, and splitting traffic between production and experimental implementations. Kubernetes examples use twemproxy for sharding and nginx for consistent, IP-hashed 10% experiments.
- **Adapter containers** translate heterogeneous application interfaces into standard interfaces. Demonstrated uses include adding Prometheus-compatible metrics to Redis, normalizing logs from Redis and Apache Storm with Fluentd, and providing rich MySQL health checks without modifying third-party database images.

These patterns separate concerns, support independent resource allocation, avoid invasive changes to externally supplied containers, and enable reuse and sharing.

At the multi-node level, microservices consist of independently developed components communicating through APIs. This approach supports team autonomy, stable contracts, independent releases, and separate scaling strategies, but it makes debugging and architectural design more difficult. Distributed patterns provide reusable guidance for these systems.

Replicated, load-balanced services use identical stateless replicas behind a load balancer. Replication provides redundancy and horizontal scaling, while readiness probes distinguish running containers from those prepared to serve traffic. Session-tracked variants consistently route a user to one replica using IP hashing, cookies, headers, or consistent hashing. Caching can be added as a separate replicated tier; reverse proxies such as Varnish can also provide rate limiting, return HTTP 429 responses, and expose remaining request limits. A replicated nginx tier can terminate SSL before traffic passes through the cache to the application.

Sharded services divide state or data among shards, with a root routing requests to appropriate shards. Unlike replicas, shards are not interchangeable, and shard failures can reduce cache hit rates and increase latency. Sharding functions should be deterministic and uniform, commonly using a hash modulo the shard count, and keys must distinguish requests with different responses without being unnecessarily specific. Consistent hashing minimizes data remapping when shard counts change. Replicated shards improve availability and permit individual hot shards to scale independently.

Scatter/gather systems distribute each request to multiple leaves in parallel and combine their partial responses at the root. This reduces latency for independent computation and can be combined with data sharding, but additional leaves introduce communication overhead, straggler latency, and compounded availability risk. Replicating each leaf shard mitigates those reliability and upgrade limitations.

Function-as-a-service simplifies deployment, automatically scales and restarts functions, and provides granular, stateless execution units. Its forced independence, network-only communication, and external state requirements also increase architectural and operational complexity.

The Buck Sweep is a misdirection off-tackle run with two lead pullers, primarily used in the Wing-T offense and applicable to other schemes. It can attack from off-tackle to the edge, exploiting defensive indecision, creating space for blockers, and developing vertical creases. Its layered fakes and handoffs make the ballcarrier difficult to identify, while its blocking angles allow undersized linemen to displace defenders horizontally. Its main weaknesses are its reliance on precise timing, spacing, and extensive practice; disrupted coordination can create significant problems, and effective pullers are essential. The passage outlines blocking assignments against 3-4 and 4-3 fronts, including guard pulls, kick-out blocks, fullback trap fakes, tailback handoff reads, and quarterback mesh and boot mechanics. Two variations are described: a shotgun Wing-T version using a mesh instead of layered handoffs, which can create a quarterback-keeper opportunity, and an I-Wing version featuring a tailback counter step with mostly unchanged blocking and quarterback footwork.

Concerns grew that Google might discontinue Inbox, its alternative Gmail interface, as Gmail adopted features such as Smart Reply and native snoozing while Inbox updates slowed. Google denied that the upcoming Gmail announcement affected Inbox, saying it remained a testing ground for innovative email workflows. Quiet development continued through AI-powered Highlights, follow-up suggestions, and unsubscribe recommendations. Inbox also retained distinct message bundling, travel-related organization, in-message details, and exclusive integration with Google reminders.

When Inbox launched in 2014, Google officials said it was initially separate but could eventually replace Gmail for most users. A former product manager reported in October 2016 that Inbox had a non-trivial, growing user base, and its Android app then showed 10 million Google Play installs. Despite reduced promotion and uncertainty about its long-term role, Inbox did not appear unused, abandoned, or close to being sunset.

Freelance writer Oobah Butler created a fictitious TripAdvisor listing for “The Shed at Dulwich,” his garden shed in South London, to test whether the platform’s rankings could be manipulated. Using a burner phone, an emotion-themed website, a vague address, exclusivity claims, and coordinated fake reviews from friends and family, he moved the listing from last place in London to the city’s top-ranked restaurant in November 2017. The hoax prompted calls, free samples, job offers, and worldwide reservation requests, while the listing received 89,000 views in one day. Butler later exposed the prank and briefly opened the restaurant for one night with actors, diners, and an inexpensive meal.

TripAdvisor said it had reviewed and penalized the property, removing reviews and lowering its ranking, but said its fraud controls focus more on manipulating real restaurants’ rankings than fake businesses. The episode highlighted platform verification weaknesses and online disinformation amid broader criticism of TripAdvisor over deleted reviews of dangerous activity.

The global shiitake mushroom market is projected to reach USD 35.4 billion by 2023 at a 15.31% CAGR, with Asia Pacific holding 82.54% share in 2017 and China accounting for 97% of the regional market. Growth is driven by the mushroom's nutritional and medicinal attributes. Dried shiitake is expected to grow fastest (CAGR 14%), fresh shiitake leads in Asia Pacific (15.59%), and pharmaceutical application is the fastest-growing segment. Key players include Bonduelle SA, Mitoku, Agro Dutch Industries, The Mushroom Company, Modern Mushroom Farms, Hirano Mushroom, and Banken Champignons.

Stroke can disrupt motor coordination, causing weakness and difficulty with functional hand tasks. Surface EMG can quantify altered muscle activation, including excessive antagonist co-contraction and changes in muscle synergies, but conventional low-density electrodes cannot adequately measure small hand muscles. This study uses a wearable high-density EMG sleeve to characterize forearm coordination in seven chronic-stroke participants and seven able-bodied participants.

Stroke participants’ affected arms and able-bodied participants’ right arms were recorded while attempting 12 common hand, wrist, and thumb movements; able-bodied participants also completed 25 additional movements and grasps. Participants received visual cues and repeated each movement at least 10–15 times. Stroke participants underwent clinical assessments of gross arm movement, hand coordination, dexterity, and spasticity, with some analyses separating mild and severe impairment groups.

The NeuroLife sleeve contained 59–75 bipolar channels depending on arm size. EMG was sampled at 3,000 Hz, filtered, corrected for movement and electrode artifacts using blind source separation, and converted to RMS features. Data were standardized to a 70-channel right-arm configuration, while synergy decomposition retained the original sleeve resolution before mapping. Channels were assigned to six forearm muscle groups; leave-one-out validation captured 86.9 ± 0.84% of single-agonist movement activity.

The analyses assess co-contraction, muscle coupling, and time-invariant muscle synergies, and test whether combined EMG features can indicate functional movement ability after stroke. The work presents the sleeve as a potential source of motor-related biomarkers for rehabilitation research and clinical care.

Port Gregory lost electricity intermittently for four days, disrupting medical equipment and causing a resident to report about $500 in freezer losses. Western Power said storms stretched response resources, while the network’s location limited backfeeding and salt and dust created maintenance challenges. Customers without power for at least 12 consecutive hours could claim an Extended Outages Payment, capped at $80.

Divergent nationalist aims among the Allies have produced uncoordinated strategy, strained relations with Russia and Italy, and contributed to Italy’s and Rumania’s military disasters. Unity in both coalitions requires pooling national purposes, sharing political power with moderate groups, and placating the left despite opposition from the irreconcilable right. The Western military decision is expected to come through exhausting Germany’s reserves rather than an immediate spectacular victory, requiring moral and administrative economy, broad popular consent, and diplomacy exposing German deception. The Allies are expected to resist any German winter peace offensive until they can force a German retreat behind the Meuse and Scheldt and begin an invasion through Lorraine. The anticipated outcome includes destroying submarine bases, recapturing northern France, and potentially invading Germany, with the deeper decision depending on comparative manpower reserves as the American reserve becomes available.

Sonali Bendre Behl announced her diagnosis of high-grade metastasized cancer and is undergoing treatment in New York, expressing optimism, determination to fight, and gratitude for family and friends' support.

Cryogenic 4D-STEM with a variable-temperature liquid-helium holder and dynamical multislice simulations were used to map polarization in SrTiO3 through asymmetries and center-of-mass shifts of inversion-related Kikuchi bands. The room-temperature cubic phase showed no detectable polarization, whereas below the antiferrodistortive transition near 105 K, SrTiO3 developed locally non-centrosymmetric polar nanodomains.

At 69 K, the nanodomains had a characteristic correlation length of approximately 20 nm and exhibited multiple polarization directions. An additional correlation peak near 25 nm, corresponding to a wavevector of about 0.04 nm⁻¹, indicated periodic spatial organization among the domains rather than random placement. This periodicity reflected correlations between nanodomains, not a true incommensurate atomic modulation.

Cooling initially enlarged the domains and strengthened their periodic ordering down to about 69 K. Below the quantum-paraelectric transition near 40 K, this trend reversed: polar clusters became smaller, more disordered, and more randomly oriented, while periodic order weakened. At 35 K, the correlation length was approximately 14 nm, and cooling to 23 K produced further fragmentation. Quantum paraelectricity therefore involved re-entrant disordering of existing polar nanodomains rather than the complete absence of polarization.

These nanoscale polar textures may underlie SrTiO₃’s anomalous thermal conductivity, glass-like dynamics, and polar-acoustic anomalies. Correlations among preformed nanodomains may also provide a pathway for externally induced long-range ferroelectric order and may connect the fluctuating polar phase to superconductivity in doped SrTiO₃.

Apple plans to use improved access to foreign cash after tax reform to become approximately net cash neutral over time, with equal cash and debt. With a current net cash position of $163 billion, Apple could reduce cash, increase debt, or both, potentially through larger dividends or share repurchases. Its debt extends into 2047, providing decades of flexibility, while specific capital allocation plans are expected with second-quarter results.

U.S. stocks ended mixed Friday as September nonfarm payrolls fell by 33,000—the first monthly decline in seven years—dampening sentiment, though wage growth beat expectations. The S&P 500 slipped 0.11% after six record closes, while the Nasdaq rose 0.07% to a sixth consecutive record close. Walgreens and CVS each fell 4.9% on reports Amazon was nearing a decision to sell prescription drugs; Amazon gained 0.9%. The Dow was nearly unchanged. All three indexes posted weekly gains of 1.2%-1.6%. Other concerns included North Korea’s planned long-range missile test and falling oil prices; Costco dropped 6% after reporting lower gross margins.

The dollar reached a two-month high against the yen and seven-week high against the euro after September wages rose 0.5%, surprising investors despite storm-distorted payroll losses. Improving U.S. data, potential tax cuts and a 93% probability of a December Fed rate hike supported the currency.

Fior Markets’ “Cooking Oil Market 2017 Global Analysis and Forecast to 2022” examines global industry trends, market size, growth, share, revenue, segmentation, leading players, drivers, restraints, challenges, opportunities, technologies, regulation, strategies, and forecasts. It includes product, application, and regional analyses covering the USA, Europe, Japan, China, India, and Southeast Asia.

Protests at PIMS entered a fifth day as employees demanded its separation from SZABMU and blocked Vice Chancellor Prof. Javed Akram from his office. CADD and Law ministries said the PIMS amendment bill would soon be submitted for prime ministerial and parliamentary approval. Despite assurances and political support, staff maintained their strike, citing unmet demands and concern for patient care. Akram offered to resign but warned against disrupting services for up to 20,000 daily patients.

Dinbych had more territory and possession against a tightly organised Wrexham, whose defence frustrated their sustained pressure. Wrexham led 12–10 at half-time through tries by James Price and James Weston. Dinbych then moved ahead with tries from Aidyn Jones and Owain Davies before Jack Ratcliff’s converted try narrowed the deficit. Dinbych held possession to the finish and won narrowly, while Wrexham earned a losing bonus point. Dinbych 2nds also lost 16–10 at Flint, gaining a losing bonus point.

The team says it is accustomed to hostile road arenas and media attention, having started each playoff series on the road, and plans to put media distractions behind it. Facing the New Jersey Devils, the team credits its patience, persistence, and late goals in Detroit and Dallas with keeping it in the series. After a passive, hesitant loss in which it did not skate or work hard enough, the team acknowledged its disappointing effort and the opponent’s difficult system. It intends to maintain its approach while playing harder, generating more shots, getting to Brodeur, and showing that the Devils have not yet seen its best.

Singapore Airlines will resume nonstop Singapore–Newark flights on Oct. 12, restoring a route last flown in 2013. At 9,537 statute miles, it will surpass Qatar Airways’ Doha–Auckland route as the world’s longest flight by distance. The flights will use the Airbus A350-900ULR, configured with 161 seats: 67 business-class and 94 premium-economy seats, with no coach. Service will initially operate three times weekly, with daily flights planned after another ULR enters service. Seven of the airline’s 46 additional A350-900s on order will be ULRs. Newark will become Singapore Airlines’ fifth U.S. airport served.

This manuscript presents an updated mapping review of occupational therapy and occupational therapy assistant (OTA) fieldwork literature in the United States from 1989 through October 2020. The AOTA Academic Fieldwork Coordinators Academic Leadership Council’s Research Promotion committee reviewed research across four bibliographic databases and the Journal of Occupational Therapy Education, mapping included studies by AOTA’s 2018 Occupational Therapy Education Research Agenda categories, education level, and fieldwork level. Of 1,619 screened records, 67 research articles met eligibility criteria.

The literature disproportionately addressed Level II fieldwork for occupational therapy students, instructional methods (23 articles), and learner characteristics and competencies (31 articles). Socialization to the profession (6) and faculty development and resources (3) received limited attention. Four articles could not be mapped to an agenda category. No included studies addressed theory building, signature pedagogies, or diversity, inclusion, and equity. OTA fieldwork and Level I experiences were substantially underrepresented; only one article focused exclusively on OTA fieldwork.

The review confirmed trends identified in 2015 and highlighted persistent gaps, particularly research on OTA programs, Level I fieldwork, theory, signature pedagogies, and understudied agenda categories. Mapping limitations included the lack of article-quality assessment, inconsistent descriptions of fieldwork levels, and difficulty applying categories originally designed for didactic education to fieldwork scholarship. Non-U.S. studies, non-peer-reviewed works, and articles without research questions were excluded, and newer publications may not be represented.

The authors recommend shifting research toward underexplored areas, including active engagement, transformative learning, constructivism, clinical reasoning, and collaborative fieldwork. They call for team-based scholarship involving fieldwork coordinators, faculty, educators, practitioners, students, and consumers, and recommend incorporating fieldwork more explicitly into future revisions of the AOTA Education Research Agenda to support evidence-based integration of classroom and clinical education.

Peruvian police are considering expelling U.S. citizen John Dougherty and Canadian citizen Jennifer Moore, who entered Peru as tourists, for allegedly inciting rural protests against Hudbay Minerals’ Constancia mine. The ministry says their conduct affects public order; Hudbay suspended operations amid protests over promised community projects.

Egypt’s Antiquities Ministry announced that archaeologists discovered a 4,400-year-old tomb near Cairo’s pyramids. It likely belonged to Hetpet, a high-ranking woman from Egypt’s 5th Dynasty who was close to royalty. Paintings depict hunting, fishing, and monkeys reaping fruit and dancing before an orchestra. Excavation of another possible Hetpet tomb is underway.

Jack Hare reviews the collective Thomson-scattering spectrum derived from electron-density fluctuations. The spectral density depends on the Fourier transform of the density, while test-particle theory separates electron and ion responses through species susceptibilities. Scattering always occurs from electrons: the electron component describes electrons repelling other electrons, while the ion component describes electrons responding to ions.

For Maxwellian distributions, the susceptibilities are expressed using the collective parameter \(\alpha=1/(k\lambda_{D,e})\), the species thermal velocities, and the dimensionless phase velocities \(\zeta_j=(\omega/k)/v_{T,j}\). The function \(W(\zeta)\) has real and imaginary components that account for distribution-function coupling and damping. Electron and ion temperatures may differ.

In the limit \(\alpha^2\to0\), corresponding to fluctuations smaller than the electron Debye length, both susceptibilities vanish, no plasma modes appear, and the spectrum reduces to the incoherent electron distribution function. This limit can be selected experimentally through the scattering geometry, detector position, or laser wavelength.

For high-frequency modes, the ion response is negligible. Requiring the real permittivity to vanish yields the electron-plasma-wave dispersion relation
\[
\omega^2=\omega_{pe}^2+\frac{3T_e}{m_e}k^2.
\]
Damping turns the corresponding singularities into peaks. Their positions and widths provide information about plasma density and electron temperature, while full spectral fitting is normally used to infer these parameters.

For low-frequency modes, the electron response is simplified while electron damping is retained. Ion-acoustic resonances are visible when \(zT_e/T_i>3\); below this condition they are damped. The derived dispersion relation approaches the familiar ion-acoustic speed in the strongly collective limit. For \(zT_e/T_i\ll1\), the spectrum resembles the ion distribution because the ion-acoustic feature is strongly damped; near unity it has a hybrid form; and for \(zT_e/T_i\gg1\), strong ion-acoustic resonances dominate.

A frequency-integrated Salpeter approximation, assuming equal electron and ion temperatures, compares the electron and ion contributions. At small \(\alpha\), only the electron feature remains; at intermediate \(\alpha\), electron scattering is coherent while ions may be coherent or incoherent; at large \(\alpha\), the ion feature dominates and the electron feature can become effectively invisible. Because electron-plasma and ion-acoustic frequencies are widely separated, measuring both on one spectrometer is difficult.

Electron-ion drift shifts the electron distribution relative to the ions and makes the two ion-acoustic peaks asymmetric. Only the drift component along the scattering vector is measurable. Fitting the full spectrum yields \(V_d\cdot k\); with the density and ion charge, this gives the local current density \(J\cdot k\). Measurements at multiple positions, combined with symmetry assumptions and Ampère’s law, may then be used to infer a magnetic field. Direct cyclotron modulation of spectral features is much more difficult because it requires nearly perpendicular observation and disappears with even a small angular error.

Ion-acoustic spectra can provide electron temperature, ion temperature, ion bulk velocity, and relative electron-ion drift, but electron density requires the electron-plasma-wave feature. Measuring electron distributions can also reveal fast or runaway electrons and other nonthermal populations.

Collisions damp coherent features and modify the incoherent spectrum through the collision operator in a Vlasov-Fokker-Planck treatment, so they must be included to avoid incorrect parameter estimates. Spatial temperature variations, velocity shear, turbulence, finite observation volumes, and finite collection angles can broaden, blur, or superpose spectral features; velocity gradients can mimic elevated ion temperature. Smaller collection volumes and apertures reduce these effects but sacrifice signal-to-noise, while multiple observation angles can help distinguish gradients but require additional spectrometers. Stronger lasers improve signal but are limited by inverse-bremsstrahlung absorption, instabilities, and cost.

Current research includes accelerating evaluations for arbitrary non-Maxwellian distributions using machine learning and other methods, and multi-angle optical systems that recover higher-dimensional Thomson-scattering distribution functions.

The study examines Turkey’s highly centralized National Education system, in which policies, appointments, and administrative decisions flow from central directorates through a bureaucratic hierarchy. Political considerations often influence appointments, while principles such as accountability, transparency, participation, efficiency, sustainability, and flexibility are insufficiently incorporated. Turkey’s 2018 PISA scores and GDP per capita were below OECD averages.

The study’s purpose is to develop a local education board model for Turkey based on OECD countries’ administrative structures and the views of teachers and education administrators. It used an exploratory sequential mixed-method design. Qualitative data came from literature, OECD and Ministry of National Education reports, and the education systems of Turkey and 15 OECD countries whose PISA and GDP averages exceeded OECD averages. These findings informed a 16-question survey administered to teachers and administrators in Seyhan district, Adana. Of the intended sample of 370, 421 participants responded. Test-retest correlations were 0.961 and 0.960, and Cronbach’s alpha was 0.978. Data were analyzed using SPSS 21 and Excel.

The literature describes good governance and boards as alternatives to centralized administration because they distribute authority, enable stakeholder participation, strengthen accountability and transparency, and bring diverse perspectives into decisions. Although board systems can slow decisions, disperse responsibility, and generate conflict, countries using them have generally recorded stronger educational and economic outcomes. In the survey, 61.5% of respondents preferred local administration, while 38.5% preferred central administration. Forty-one percent favored independent provincial education boards as the main local authority, and 61% supported management through elected boards. Respondents broadly favored including teachers, students, parents, principals, education supervisors, unions, governors, mayors, university representatives, professional organizations, and other stakeholders in provincial, district, vocational, school, inspection, and evaluation boards. They also favored transferring 22 of 27 central responsibilities to local units, while the Ministry should retain broad policy-setting, regulatory, monitoring, evaluation, and auditing functions.

Based on these findings, the study proposes a Local Education Boards model. A National Education Supreme Council would establish national policies and five-year and annual plans, while the Ministry would implement, monitor, evaluate, audit, and support local bodies. A Higher Education Council would oversee higher-education policy. Provincial and district boards would formulate local policies and plans, appoint education directors, and supervise subordinate boards and organizations. Local education organizations would carry out operational duties, including budgets, personnel, curriculum implementation, training, infrastructure, and evaluation. Vocational boards would coordinate regional vocational policy with universities and industry, while school boards would select administrators, plan school activities, manage budgets, and conduct audits. Independent supervisory boards would report directly to governors or mayors. Decisions would generally use majority voting or unanimity, and school-level decisions would conform to provincial board decisions.

The authors recommend pilot programs to test and refine the model, further research on board composition and internal operation, and consideration of the model by Turkish policymakers. The study is limited by its exploratory sequential design, restricted quantitative sample, reliance on PISA and GDP data from only 16 of 36 OECD countries, and the general rather than fully detailed structure of the proposed model.
A federal judge declined to delay an order letting transgender people enlist in the military on January 1, 2018. The Pentagon prepared to comply as Justice reviewed legal options.

Texas HB 8 will replace STAAR with three shorter exams at the beginning, middle and end of the school year when the system launches in 2027-28. Districts may select TEA-approved national assessments for the first two tests, while the agency will develop the end-of-year exam, which will assess curriculum mastery. Results will be released within about two days.

Supporters say shorter tests and a ban on practice and benchmark exams will reduce instructional time spent on testing. Parents, teachers and administrators remain concerned that three exams, restrictive testing-day protocols and the continued heavy weight of the end-of-year test on school accountability ratings could maintain or increase stress.

Lawmakers directed the TEA to develop a student-progress measure and study how the new tests should affect accountability ratings. The progress measure will not be ready at launch, while the accountability report is due in 2029-30 and its findings are not required to be implemented. The law also requires tracking pre-K, extracurricular and workforce participation, but these measures will not count toward school ratings.

Educators will review the new end-of-year exam through a commissioner-appointed committee. Some districts and families favor adaptive MAP testing, which they describe as less stressful and more useful for measuring growth than STAAR.

NVIDIA RTX IO integrates with Microsoft’s upcoming DirectStorage API to accelerate NVMe storage operations in gaming PCs. It enables parallelized game-specific APIs, direct transfer of compressed data from SSDs to GPU memory, and GPU-based lossless decompression, reducing CPU workload and improving I/O performance. NVIDIA claims RTX IO can deliver 100× throughput, 20× lower CPU utilization, and decompression beyond Gen4 SSD limits.

The NVIDIA A40 is a GA10x Ampere data center GPU for visual computing. Compared with the Quadro RTX 6000, it offers up to twice the FP32 and ray-tracing throughput and up to five times the AI and data-science throughput, or ten times with sparsity. It has 48GB of memory, expandable to 96GB through dual NVLink, PCIe Gen4 connectivity, DisplayPort 1.4 outputs, vGPU support, Quadro Sync, and compatibility with the NVIDIA EGX Platform.

Ampere GPUs support 4K at 120Hz and 8K at 60Hz, including two 8K displays. They feature DisplayPort 1.4a with DSC 1.2a and HDMI 2.1 with up to 48 Gbps bandwidth and dynamic HDR support. Their fifth-generation NVDEC decoder accelerates MPEG-2, VC-1, H.264, H.265, VP8, VP9, and AV1 decoding on Windows and Linux. GA10x GPUs provide the first hardware AV1 decode support; in a cited test, they played 8K60 HDR AV1 content with about 4% CPU usage, compared with 28 FPS and more than 85% CPU usage using software decoding. Their seventh-generation NVENC encoder provides hardware-accelerated, low-latency streaming and archiving, including 4K H.264 and 8K HEVC encoding, while offloading work from the CPU and graphics engine.

GA10x Ampere architecture provides up to twice the programmable-shading, ray-tracing, and AI performance of prior-generation architecture. Its second-generation RT Core accelerates ray-triangle intersections and ray-traced motion blur and supports concurrent ray tracing, shading, and compute. Its third-generation Tensor Core supports structural sparsity for increased effective throughput. The architecture also introduces GDDR6X memory, reaching 19.5 Gbps and 936 GB/s in the GeForce RTX 3090, along with enhanced DLSS supporting 8K HDR rendering.

The GeForce RTX 3090 uses the GA102 GPU with 24GB of GDDR6X memory, 82 streaming multiprocessors, and 10,496 CUDA cores; NVIDIA describes it as 1.5× faster than the TITAN RTX. The RTX 3070 uses GA104 and is described as faster than the RTX 2080 Ti, while using GDDR6 rather than GDDR6X and excluding NVLink.

GDDR6X memory interfaces on GA10x GPUs include Error Detection and Replay, which detects transmission errors and retries failed transactions. This allows memory-overclocking limits to be identified through plateauing performance, although continued overclocking can still cause crashes.

The RTX A6000 uses GA102 with 10,752 CUDA cores, 84 second-generation RT Cores, 336 next-generation RT Cores, and 48GB of GDDR6. It supports real-time and final-frame ray tracing, hardware-accelerated motion blur, AI denoising, and large 3D datasets, with two boards providing 96GB combined memory through NVLink. The specification includes comparative workstation rendering, HPC, and deep-learning benchmark results and states that NVIDIA disclaims warranties for accuracy, fitness for particular uses, and product applications.

A vulnerability in Atlassian Jira and Confluence allowed attackers to exploit a proxy for SSRF and XSS attacks, exposing AWS credentials that could enable server takeovers, data theft, or destruction. The flaw received a 6.1/10 NIST severity rating and Atlassian products were patched, but many legacy deployments remain exposed. Researcher Robert Wiggins found more than a dozen major companies running outdated systems. Several organizations fixed or took servers offline after being contacted, while at least three unnamed companies remained vulnerable. Updating Atlassian software is recommended.

England qualified for the 2018 World Cup in Russia but were criticized for a cautious, cautious 4-2-3-1 formation in their 1-0 win over Slovenia. The passage argues that Southgate should adopt three centre-backs with wing-backs, use Dele Alli as No. 10 and keep Raheem Sterling on the wing, while retaining Jordan Henderson and Eric Dier for protection. It also urges Southgate to take risks against Brazil and Germany in upcoming friendlies, warning that continued conservatism could lead to another disappointing tournament exit.

Spotify, Comcast, and Oracle recently announced co-CEO arrangements, adding to a broader adoption of a leadership model that can aid succession planning but risks unclear authority and power struggles. Spotify’s Daniel Ek is being succeeded by Gustav Söderström and Alex Norström, while Comcast promoted President Mike Cavanagh alongside CEO Brian Roberts.

Co-CEO companies remain relatively uncommon, comprising about 1.2% of the Russell 3000. However, companies with two leaders posted average annual shareholder returns of 9.5% from 1996 to 2020, compared with 6.9% for single-leader companies.

Experts emphasized that successful co-leadership requires clearly defined responsibilities, alignment on strategy, effective communication, shared accountability, and equal commitment. Netflix, Sony Interactive Entertainment, Salesforce, Chipotle, Lennar, Warby Parker, and Revolve are among companies that have used the model. Its success depends heavily on the individuals involved, and critics cited ambiguity, compensation costs, and difficulty sharing power.

NVIDIA Corporation’s unaudited Form 10-Q covers the third quarter of fiscal 2016, ended October 25, 2015. Third-quarter revenue was $1.305 billion, up 7% from $1.225 billion, while gross profit rose to $734 million, operating income to $245 million and net income to $246 million. Diluted earnings per share increased to $0.44 from $0.31. For the first nine months, revenue rose 5% to $3.609 billion, but operating income declined to $495 million and net income to $406 million from $437 million; diluted earnings per share fell to $0.72 from $0.77.

GPU revenue increased 12% in the third quarter to $1.110 billion, driven by 40% growth in high-end GeForce gaming products, while operating income rose to $367 million. Tegra Processor revenue fell 23% to $129 million as OEM smartphone and tablet sales declined more than 80%, partly offset by automotive growth, with a $65 million operating loss. “All Other” revenue remained $66 million, primarily from Intel patent licensing.

At October 25, 2015, NVIDIA held $471 million in cash and $4.257 billion in marketable securities, with total assets of $7.174 billion, long-term debt of $1.406 billion and shareholders’ equity of $4.465 billion. Nine-month operating cash flow was $664 million, compared with $463 million a year earlier.

The company wound down its Icera modem operations after finding no viable buyer. Restructuring charges totaled $8 million for the quarter and $97 million for the first nine months; an additional $25 million to $35 million was expected in the fourth quarter, with activities affecting about 5% of the global workforce and expected to be substantially completed by fiscal year-end.

NVIDIA returned $604 million to shareholders during the first nine months through dividends and repurchases. A $400 million accelerated share repurchase acquired 18 million shares at an average $21.63; cumulative repurchases reached 226 million shares for $3.72 billion. The quarterly dividend was subsequently increased to $0.115 per share, and a new $135 million accelerated repurchase began with an initial delivery of three million shares.

Recent initiatives included GRID 2.0 cloud graphics, new GeForce products and GameWorks VR, and expanded automotive deployments, including the Tesla Model X. NVIDIA also recorded a $21 million charge for the SHIELD 8-inch tablet recall.

Patent litigation involving Qualcomm and Samsung remained unresolved, including ITC and court proceedings. NVIDIA had not accrued liabilities because potential losses were considered not probable and could not be reasonably estimated.

This 1902 *Foreign Relations of the United States* appendix contains the English translation of the U.S. memorandum presented to arbitrator T. M. C. Asser under the September 3, 1900 exchange of notes between the United States and Russia. It supports claims by the owners, officers, and crews of the *Cape Horn Pigeon*, *James Hamilton Lewis*, *C. H. White*, and *Kate and Anna* for indemnity arising from their arrest and seizure by Russian agents. Secretary of State John Hay transmitted Herbert H. D. Peirce’s dispatch and translation to Senator H. C. Lodge for printing as a public document. Front matter describes the Department of State’s searchable, portable, offline-accessible 2018 electronic edition and recommends citing document numbers rather than page numbers.

In this New York Court of Claims action, Ralph Hartwell Brubaker, individually and as administrator of Berenice M. Brubaker’s estate, sought compensation for four State appropriations of land for the St. Lawrence River power project. The approximately 365-acre unimproved tract near Massena was divided by Middle Road, with northern land zoned for agriculture and southern land zoned for industry.

Applying *United States v. Miller*, the court held that project-caused increases in value could not be attributed to the State for land within the project’s probable scope at the time of governmental commitment, but enhanced value could be recovered for adjacent land later taken. The 1955 appropriation of roughly 183 acres north of Middle Road was awarded $32,000 without project-related enhancement because the record contained no probative evidence that the land was within the probable condemnation area. No consequential damage to the remainder was found.

The State was awarded $100 for a 0.15-acre flooding easement that lay within an existing drainage easement. For the 1957 appropriation of 25.34 acres south of Middle Road, the court found $88,500 in value before and $48,750 after the taking and awarded $39,750, consisting of $12,675 in direct and $27,075 in consequential western-property damages. For a 55.38-acre electrical transmission-line easement, the court found that the taking destroyed the remaining interest’s market value and awarded $27,700, with no consequential damage to the remaining property. Interest was awarded as specified for each appropriation.

This continuation application describes a display device including a substrate, pixel and opposing electrodes, an emission layer, and an encapsulation portion formed from alternating organic and inorganic thin films. The encapsulation edge tapers toward the substrate. An organic planarization layer covers at least part of this edge and forms a larger angle with the substrate than the encapsulation edge, potentially at least about 70 degrees, to provide a flatter surface. The layer may cover all or part of the encapsulation portion and may have a flat or curved edge.

Touch-sensor patterns, including electrodes and wiring, may be formed on the planarization layer. This configuration increases the available pattern area, reduces bezel and touch-sensing dead space, and lowers parasitic capacitance between the touch pattern and the opposing electrode. Described capacitive touch sensors include alternating first and second electrodes connected to a driver and using mutual- or self-sensing capacitors. The display device also includes thin-film-transistor pixels, display and peripheral areas, barrier and passivation layers, and encapsulation to restrict moisture and oxygen penetration.

NBA defenses can disrupt UCLA’s high-post rub and quick down-screen reversals through three-phase show-and-recover defense. Switching is vulnerable because the screener can post against a smaller defender. Defenders instead show cutters behind the screen, recover into pass-denial positions, pressure the ball, front the post, and pack the weak side. An alternative “All Out SOS” strategy traps the wing on the first pass, exploiting the point guard’s low-post cut and difficulty reversing the ball. Effective play requires coordinated rotations as the pass leaves the passer’s hands, with defenders closing out, denying the high post, and fronting the low post.

During arguments in *Bost v. Illinois State Board of Elections*, Supreme Court justices appeared willing to let congressional candidate Michael Bost challenge Illinois’s 14-day mail-ballot counting rule, but debated the proper standing standard. Paul Clement proposed broad “candidate standing,” while Elena Kagan favored requiring a substantial risk of electoral disadvantage without proving the challenged rule could change the election’s likely outcome. Sonia Sotomayor and Ketanji Brown Jackson appeared more skeptical because Bost said the rule would not threaten his safe seat. Clement also cited added monitoring costs. Illinois Solicitor General Jane Notz said even Kagan’s test would not help Bost on the alleged facts but suggested that election-outcome effects or severe reputational injury could suffice. Brett Kavanaugh and the government’s attorney raised concerns that rejecting standing could force election disputes into post-election litigation and leave only major parties able to litigate.

SEM-based microscale four-point-probe measurements, coupled with XRD, EDS, EBSD, and imaging, were used to separate electrical contributions in heat-treated Al-Mg-Si alloys. Bulk resistivity was measured by the Van der Pauw method, while local measurements resolved grain interiors and individual Si and Mg₂Si precipitates. Grain-interior resistivity was similar across compositions under the same heat treatment but varied with heat treatment, reflecting changes in solid-solution composition and nanoprecipitate state. Bulk resistivity generally increased with Si and Mg content, with treatment at 350 °C for 72 hours producing the lowest values for each composition. Si and Mg₂Si precipitates contributed nearly equally to the effective resistivity, indicating that precipitate volume rather than phase identity governs the increase with solute content. Neglecting vacancies, dislocations, and grain boundaries because of their low density, bulk resistivity was modeled as grain-interior resistivity plus a term proportional to total solute concentration. Linear fits had R² values of 0.954–0.972, with coefficients dependent on annealing conditions.

Y-Cross is a drop-back passing concept used in the Air Raid offense and elsewhere. It is a weak-side flood concept built around a post route, deep crosser, and RB route to the flat, with the TE or a speedy slot receiver serving as the crosser. Backside route combinations can give the quarterback additional progression options. The concept is effective against man coverage and Cover 4, where a post receiver can beat the free safety over the top. Cover 3 is less favorable because the post safety occupies the middle, though the concept remains callable against all defenses. The base quarterback progression is post, deep crosser, then RB check-down or backside dig. Variations include reading a post-wheel combination before the cross and adding a curl-flat route against one-high defenses. Personnel grouping, route coaching, and quarterback scanning are central to successful execution.

Bitcoin reached a six-week high, rising 4.4% to $9,340.88 as reports of growing interest from major financial institutions lifted market sentiment. Total cryptocurrency market capitalization reached $427 billion, and 24-hour trading volume totaled $28 billion. Goldman Sachs reportedly hired a digital asset markets head, Barclays assessed client interest in a crypto trading desk, and one in five surveyed institutions considered crypto trading within a year. Regulatory scrutiny remains a challenge.

Wichita Falls recorded five DWI arrests over St. Patrick’s Day weekend, with year-to-date arrests declining from 39 in 2016 and 38 in 2017 to 25. Sgt. Harold McClure cited increased awareness, ridesharing and sober-driver use, and police presence at celebrations as possible reasons.

The guide explains EUR/USD trading, describing the euro–dollar pair as the world’s most widely traded currency pair because of its high liquidity, tight spreads, extensive market information, and connection to the economic health of Europe and the United States. Its value is influenced by inflation, employment, GDP, interest rates, central-bank policies, political developments, geopolitical events, and market sentiment. EUR/USD is presented as accessible to beginners but difficult to trade profitably, with the authors noting that no forex pair is easy.

The recommended approach combines technical analysis, fundamental analysis, and sentiment analysis. Technical tools include moving averages, Fibonacci retracement levels, support and resistance, pivot points, breakout and narrow-range patterns, and indicators such as ADX, ATR, CCI, and Directional Movement Index. Fundamental analysis focuses on economic releases, monetary-policy divergence, and interest-rate differentials, which are presented as major long-term determinants. Sentiment is described as most useful for short-term trades. Entry methods include waiting for breakouts, pullbacks, or narrow-range patterns, while risk controls include stop-loss orders, position sizing, diversification into uncorrelated pairs, and limiting leverage.

The article strongly emphasizes backtesting strategies with strict rules. One example, using Yahoo Finance’s “EURUSD=X” data and accompanying Python code, reportedly produced 713 trades and a 53% gain per trade, although the one-day holding-period equity curve was smoother than the two-day curve. Backtest results may differ between spot forex and futures. The text warns that a profitable backtest does not guarantee future success.

Trading styles discussed include position trading over weeks or months, swing trading over days or weeks, day trading, and scalping over minutes. Scalping and day trading are portrayed as difficult, with many traders losing money, while position and swing trading require patience. Proposed strategies include carry trades, hedging, correlation analysis, and trading around economic news.

Trading timing is linked to the European session, central-bank announcements, and the European–U.S. overlap. The highest movement and liquidity are generally associated with 12:00–4:00 p.m. GMT in summer and 1:00–5:00 p.m. GMT in winter. The guide also discusses managing volatility by reducing positions or tightening stops, particularly when correlations rise during uncertain markets.

Finally, the passage covers broker selection, including regulation, security, platforms, fees, minimum accounts, and customer support. It recommends practicing on a demo account, reviewing performance, refining strategies continuously, and transitioning to live trading only after gaining confidence. Common mistakes include impulsive trading, inadequate risk controls, excessive leverage, failure to diversify, unclear or untested plans, poor monitoring, and insufficient demo practice.

This study presents a bibliometric analysis of artificial intelligence in STEM education research from 2020 to 2024. It reviews AI’s educational applications, including personalized learning, advanced analytics, instructional automation, adaptive testing, virtual learning environments, assessment, and teacher support, while noting challenges involving ethics, AI literacy, data privacy, learner autonomy, and excessive algorithmic control of learning.

Using the Dimensions database, the researchers searched for “artificial intelligence” AND “stem education,” filtered 101 records to a final dataset of 35 articles, and analyzed them with Microsoft Excel and VOSviewer. The analysis found that cited publications and citations increased sharply in 2024: 15 articles received 234 citations, averaging 15.62 citations per article. The United States led with nine documents and 103 citations, followed by China with five documents but no citations.

Nesra Yannier, Kenneth R. Koedinger, and Scott E. Hudson had the highest citation counts, with one article each cited 55 times. The most cited journals were the International Journal of Artificial Intelligence in Education, the Proceedings of the Interaction Design and Children Conference, and Frontiers in Education. The most cited articles were “Active Learning is About More Than Hands-On: A Mixed-Reality AI System to Support STEM Education” and “Smiley Cluster,” with 55 and 43 citations, respectively. Carnegie Mellon University was the most cited institution.

The findings indicate growing interest in active learning, mixed-reality systems, and inclusive STEM practices. Proposed research directions include long-term intervention studies, cross-cultural comparisons, ethical frameworks, improved AI literacy, and integration with VR/AR. The authors note that the limited timeframe and database coverage and the use of citation counts as an impact measure constrain the analysis.

The Trump administration’s $100,000 fee for new H-1B visas could imperil thousands of U.S. college jobs, though agencies have not clarified whether universities must pay it. As of June 30, colleges and universities employed 16,797 H-1B workers—about 5% of fiscal year 2025 approvals. At least 930 institutions had approved visas, with the top 100 accounting for roughly 70% of university approvals. Universities use the program to recruit specialized academic, research and medical staff, while the administration alleges employers use H-1B visas to avoid hiring Americans. The annual cap is 85,000, but universities, nonprofit research institutions and national labs are exempt. National-interest exemptions are possible. Experts say many colleges could not afford the fee, potentially hampering hiring.

Benjamin Franklin’s fire-prevention maxim is presented as equally applicable to natural disasters: although storms cannot be prevented, preparation and resilient infrastructure can reduce harm before, during, and after them. Hurricanes Maria, Harvey, and Irma exposed prolonged health risks, including power shortages, contaminated floodwater, toxic chemicals, mold, mosquito-borne disease, structural hazards, heat exposure, mental stress, and economic disruption. The author argues that authorities should strengthen disaster preparedness, public education, industrial-site protection, seawalls, tree trimming, electrical grids, and flood monitoring. Despite improvements such as concrete utility poles and substation water gauges, Irma left half of Florida without power, and full restoration took ten days.

At the California Democratic Party convention in San Diego, no candidate for governor or U.S. Senate won the 60% delegate support required for endorsement. In two Orange County House races, Dave Min received the endorsement in the challenge to Rep. Mimi Walters after a floor fight, while Hans Keirstead defeated unified opposition in the race against Rep. Dana Rohrabacher. Min won exactly 60% support from 50 district delegates; opponents gathered 300 signatures to force a full-delegate vote, but the endorsement ultimately stood. Keirstead’s opponents also submitted a challenge but missed the entry deadline.

In three other targeted Southern California Republican districts, preferred candidates failed to reach the threshold: Mike Levin and Bryan Caforio each received 53%, and Jay Chen 47%. For Senate, delegates favored Kevin de Leon over Dianne Feinstein, 54% to 37%. In governor polling, Gavin Newsom led with 37% delegate support, while Antonio Villaraigosa placed fourth with 9%. Endorsements give candidates the Democratic Party designation on sample ballots.

Investing.com’s page combines market headlines with commentary on seasonal weakness, institutional rebalancing, and technical levels. It notes 35 years of seasonal weakness, diminished liquidity, thin trading volume, tax-loss selling, and institutional rebalancing, with earnings momentum and optimism potentially fading in August. TLT analysis identifies resistance near the 80-month moving average at 100 and a bullish divergence, while a dollar break below 98 could lead to lower yields and further TLT strength. Lower yields, a weakening dollar, and rising gold are described as generally risk-off. The commentary also cites key levels at 215, 222, and 81.70 and warns that market leadership may shift. Headlines mention AMD’s OpenAI chip deal, gold above $3,900 per ounce, and an Evercore projection of 9,000 for the S&P 500. The page promotes AI-selected portfolios and includes trading-risk, data-accuracy, copyright, and advertising disclosures.

Five European research institutions are working to establish October 10 as International Coccolithophore Day, highlighting microscopic, single-celled algae that regulate climate and support marine ecosystems. Coccolithophores remove carbon dioxide, produce oxygen, nourish food webs, and form calcium carbonate plates that sink to the seafloor, eventually contributing to chalk and limestone layers that preserve records of past climates. Their production stores carbon in deep-sea sediments, while their fossils help reconstruct ancient oceans.

The initiative, led by institutions in Croatia, the UK, Norway, Portugal, and the International Nannoplankton Association, supports research into how coccolithophores influence ocean carbon storage and respond to warming, acidification, nutrient changes, viruses, grazers, bacteria, and aerosol-driven fertilization. Climate-driven changes threaten these organisms and dependent ecosystems. The campaign seeks greater ocean literacy, policy attention, and public engagement by demonstrating the planetary impact of microscopic life.

Kimberly Jones posted a video of her middle-school son Keaton describing being bullied, drawing more than 18 million views and over $29,000 for his education. Athletes and entertainers including Delanie Walker, Tyler Byrd, Kelsea Ballerini, Dale Earnhardt Jr. and Snoop Dogg offered support.

Gunmen kidnapped 52 mostly Uzbek farmers from three villages in Jowzjan while they worked their land; the motive was unclear. Police blamed Taliban fighters, though a Taliban spokesman could not confirm the report. Elders were seeking their release, and police said they might launch an operation if talks failed.

On June 28, 2021, NVIDIA completed the domestication of a foreign subsidiary, repatriating to the United States the economic rights to certain non-U.S. intellectual property. The move simplified its corporate structure and aligned it more closely with its operating structure in response to OECD base erosion and profit sharing conclusions and changes in U.S. and European tax laws. For the second quarter of fiscal 2022, NVIDIA raised its expected GAAP and non-GAAP tax rates to 13% plus or minus 1%, excluding discrete items, from 10% plus or minus 1%. The domestication is expected to generate a discrete tax benefit of approximately $250 million to $300 million.

A retrospective cross-disorder study used UK primary-care records from THIN to compare prediagnostic clinical features and medication use for Alzheimer’s disease (AD), Parkinson’s disease (PD), and dementia with Lewy bodies (DLB). The cohort included 20,214 AD, 28,222 PD, 4,682 DLB cases, and 20,214 controls; selected medication findings were examined in the UK Biobank.

All three disorders were associated with more health conditions and medication use during the five years before diagnosis. Memory problems were more common before AD, tremor before PD, and confusion, hallucinations, memory problems, and falls before DLB. Constipation, urinary disorders, and hypotension were associated with all three conditions but were stronger for PD and DLB. Treatments for depression, anxiety, and constipation were more frequent before all three diagnoses, while antihypertensive and antidiabetic use was lower. Compared with AD, PD and DLB had more beta-blocker and laxative use; statin use was lower before PD but higher before DLB.

Among PD patients, prescriptions for hypercholesterolemia, constipation, depression, and psychosis were independently associated with dementia developing within five years of PD diagnosis. UK Biobank analyses replicated lower statin use before PD than AD and showed higher antihypertensive and statin use among PD patients who subsequently developed dementia than among those with all-cause dementia.

The findings indicate distinct, prolonged prodromal profiles for AD, PD, and DLB and suggest possible clinical value in primary-care prescribing records. However, observational data cannot establish causality, and diagnoses, disease boundaries, and control matching may have affected the results.

Tesla Motors, Inc. filed an unaudited Form 10-Q for the quarter ended June 30, 2015. For the three months, revenue was $955.0 million, up from $769.3 million in 2014, primarily because of increased Model S deliveries. Automotive revenue was $878.1 million and services and other revenue was $76.9 million. Gross profit was $213.4 million, but gross margin declined to 22.3% from 27.7%, primarily due to product and regional mix, higher manufacturing costs, obsolete inventory and lower regulatory-credit revenue. Operating loss increased to $170.2 million from $28.8 million, and net loss increased to $184.2 million from $61.9 million, or $1.45 per share versus $0.50.

For the six months ended June 30, 2015, revenue was $1.895 billion, up from $1.390 billion; gross profit was $473.4 million; operating loss was $272.6 million; and net loss was $338.4 million, or $2.68 per share. Research and development expense rose to $348.9 million, while selling, general and administrative expense increased to $397.2 million, largely reflecting Model X development and expansion of Tesla’s retail, service and Supercharger infrastructure.

At June 30, 2015, Tesla had $1.151 billion of cash and equivalents, $6.468 billion of total assets, $5.702 billion of liabilities and $715.9 million of stockholders’ equity. Inventory rose to $1.212 billion from $953.7 million at year-end, and net property, plant and equipment increased to $2.646 billion from $1.829 billion. For the first six months, operating activities used $291.3 million, investing activities used $855.2 million, and financing activities provided $404.5 million, reducing cash by $755.0 million.

Tesla had delivered more than 78,000 Model S vehicles by June 30, 2015. Management expected 50,000–55,000 combined Model S and Model X deliveries in 2015, Model X customer deliveries late in the third quarter, Model 3 deliveries in late 2017, and combined weekly production of 1,600–1,800 vehicles in 2016. The company was investing in production capacity, a Gigafactory targeted to begin production in early 2016, new Powerwall and Powerpack products, and an expanded Supercharger network.

The filing identified risks from Model X production and supply-chain complexity, manufacturing inefficiencies, market demand, residual values, expansion in China and Asia, and potential Gigafactory cost overruns or delays. A 2013 securities class action against Tesla and CEO Elon Musk had been dismissed with prejudice, but the plaintiffs’ appeal was pending.

The article explains gold trading and several strategies for profiting from gold-price fluctuations. Gold is traded through futures, options, spot markets, shares, CFDs, and ETFs; most transactions are cash-settled without physical delivery. Traders may buy low and sell high or use gold as a “safe haven” hedge because it can move inversely to stocks and bonds.

The article traces gold’s history from its early use in Egypt to its role in international trade, the Bretton Woods gold standard, and the introduction of gold futures in 1974. It says gold is harder to trade than stocks because it depends heavily on random macroeconomic news, although it has a generally positive overnight bias.

A weekend swing strategy was backtested using GLD from late 2004 through September 2021. Holding from Thursday’s close to Friday’s close averaged a 0.14% gain with a 1.4 profit factor, while holding from Thursday’s close until Monday’s open averaged 0.19% with a 1.3 profit factor. Both were described as weak strategies. Adding one unspecified parameter improved the results to levels considered suitable only for small positions, and different entry and exit times might perform better.

The study reviewed the latest Voluntary National Reviews from 18 Eastern Mediterranean Region countries submitted between 2016 and 2021, assessing reporting on health-related SDG targets, indicators and data availability. All countries had mechanisms to monitor and report SDG progress, 11 reported on all 17 SDGs, and 17 prioritized or adapted targets to national contexts; however, only eight explicitly stated 2030 targets for some indicators.

Reporting varied by indicator type and country income, with higher-income countries generally reporting more comprehensively. Maternal mortality, neonatal mortality and under-five mortality were the most frequently reported SDG3 indicators. On average, reviews provided data for about 11 SDG3 and 6.4 non-SDG3 indicators, while only Qatar reported trends for every SDG3 indicator. Fourteen reviews identified limited data availability as a monitoring challenge, citing insufficient human resources, low data quality, inadequate statistical tools, limited transparency and insufficient disaggregation.

Twenty-nine of 32 SDG3 indicators could be derived from civil registration and vital statistics, national surveys, disease surveillance and routine health information systems. Reporting was higher for indicators based on disease surveillance and civil registration than for those based on routine systems and surveys. Data routinely reported to WHO/EMRO were often omitted from the reviews.

The findings indicate that weak health information systems, limited data availability and insufficient analytical capacity hinder monitoring of health-related SDGs. Strengthening regulatory frameworks, data-collection capacity, civil registration systems and population-based surveys is needed to improve access to quality data and support evidence-based public health action.

An Investing.com article argues that Friday’s gold rally was unusual because gold rose sharply and the U.S. dollar index fell, while silver, platinum, and mining stocks barely moved. It notes that gold remained below a rising resistance line, while the VanEck Junior Gold Miners ETF’s failure to rise reinforced a bearish setup. The article says this divergence suggests precious-metals markets may be in the early stage of a larger decline. It also says the dollar index’s move back to its July high verified an inverse head-and-shoulders pattern, while stocks remained below previous highs and rising support after a sell-off. The author compares the market setup to 2008 and promotes Investing.com’s stock screener. The page also contains unrelated headlines, advertisements, and risk and data disclosures.

Cowboys owner and general manager Jerry Jones was fined $250,000 by the NFL for an “inadvertent” obscene gesture toward fans at MetLife Stadium during the Cowboys’ 37-22 win over the Jets. Jones said he intended to give Cowboys fans a thumbs-up or point toward them after a touchdown. The Cowboys are likely to appeal and must decide by Friday. The article also notes previous NFL fines involving Panthers owner David Tepper and former Texans owner Bud Adams.

A rare white moose filmed in Sweden captivated people worldwide. The BBC reported that about 100 live in Sweden and develop white fur through a genetic mutation, not albinism. The filmed twin calves’ status as albino or piebald remains unknown.
Regrouping before tomorrow’s game in a long series, the team says the schedule may disrupt its rhythm. It controlled the first two periods but let up in the third; the power play must score more.

The ADS868xW is an integrated, fully differential 16-bit successive-approximation data-acquisition device with an analog front end, ADC driver, programmable gain amplifier, and precision reference buffer. It supports bipolar and unipolar single-ended or differential input ranges and uses straight-binary output. The LSB value equals the full-scale range divided by 2¹⁶.

The device can use an internal nominal 4.096 V reference or an external 4.096 V reference, selected through the INTREF_DIS bit of RANGE_SEL_REG. The internal reference requires at least 4.7 µF between REFIO and REFGND and cannot directly drive external loads. Reflow and thermal or mechanical stress can shift its output voltage. In external-reference mode, REFIO is an input, while the internal buffer drives REFCAP; REFCAP requires at least 10 µF to REFGND plus a nearby 1 µF decoupling capacitor.

Alarm features include active-high input and AVDD alarms. Input alarms have independently programmable high and low thresholds with common programmable hysteresis. The AVDD alarm uses fixed typical trip points of 4.7 V and 5.3 V. Active and tripped flags are available through the ALARM/SDO-1/GPO pin, ALARM_REG, or appended output data; active flags clear after each conversion, while tripped flags clear when ALARM_REG is read.

The multiSPI interface supports four SPI-compatible configuration protocols, single- or dual-SDO output, and source-synchronous operation with selectable internal or external clock sources. In daisy-chain configurations, devices use identical register settings, an optimal frame contains 32 × N clock captures, and data are returned in reverse device order. The device operates in RESET, ACQ, and CONV states and supports application reset, power-on reset, NAP mode, and power-down mode.

Programming uses 32-bit commands containing byte or half-word register operations. Frames shorter than 32 clocks cannot write registers, while in longer frames the final 32 shifted bits form the command. Output data can include conversion results, register data, device addresses, input ranges, alarm flags, parity, or test patterns according to DATAOUT_CTL_REG settings.

The illustrated industrial design combines an ADS8681W with an eight-channel differential multiplexer to support standard voltage and current inputs. The device uses separate AVDD and DVDD supplies and requires specified supply, reference, and bypass capacitors. Recommended PCB layout separates analog and digital sections, keeps bypass and reference capacitors close to their pins without intervening vias, and connects grounds through short, low-impedance paths.

Princeton scientists and international collaborators developed Diag2Diag, an AI system that uses data from multiple plasma sensors to generate detailed synthetic readings that other diagnostics cannot capture, particularly at the plasma edge, or pedestal. The approach could improve plasma monitoring and control while reducing hardware, maintenance, cost, and complexity, helping make commercial fusion reactors more compact, reliable, and economical. Diag2Diag may also enhance or recover data in spacecraft, robotic surgery, and other systems where sensors are degraded or limited.

The AI was trained with sensor data from DIII-D National Fusion Facility experiments and detailed previously unobservable changes in the pedestal. Its results provide new evidence for a magnetic-island theory of plasma disruption suppression, showing that resonant magnetic perturbations can flatten both temperature and density at the plasma edge. The researchers plan to extend the technology to additional fusion diagnostics and other fields.
