The article reviews 10 AI content generation and writing tools recommended for 2022, arguing that AI writers are cheaper than hiring humans and perform content tasks at a high level.

- **Jasper:** Adapts to a user's writing style and medium; trusted by 50,000+ marketers for campaigns, ad copy, and blog posts; offers SEO-optimized and long-form articles up to 10,000 words, guarantees original content, and provides monthly word allowances up to over 300,000.
- **Copy.ai:** Over 90 templates for marketing copy, social posts, ads, and product descriptions; 25 languages; Chrome extension; 7-day free trial with 100 runs daily; Pro plan $49/year ($35/month); 7,000 free words via its link.
- **Frase:** SEO research and optimization tool generating content briefs, outlines, intros, FAQs, competitor analysis, and Google Search Console-driven content opportunities; plans from $14.99 to $114.99/month plus $35/month SEO add-ons.
- **Article Forge:** Generates complete articles from a keyword alone, draws on high-ranking websites, integrates with WordAi, RankerX, SEnuke TNG, and SEO Autopilot, supports bulk and automatic generation, and offers a 30-day money-back guarantee; output is not always on point.
- **Rytr:** Free generator for blog posts, school papers, captions, and product/meta descriptions; 30+ languages and tones, built-in plagiarism checker; free plan covers 5,000 characters, with paid plans adding AI image generation.
- **An unnamed free tool:** Creates marketing copy, websites, and blogs with tone, grammar, and plagiarism checkers; free plan includes ten credits, with paid tiers adding templates and short- and long-form writing tools.
- **CopySmith:** Creates documents, blogs, presentations, product descriptions, landing pages, and rewritten unique content, including SEO-friendly Shopify descriptions; free trial without credit card, then 50- or 400-credit plans or custom enterprise pricing.
- **Hypotenuse:** Beginner-friendly tool for videos, articles, and infographics, offering tailored copy, data drawn from social media and websites, and automated product descriptions; free trial only, then 100- or 350-credit monthly plans or custom enterprise pricing.
- **Kafkai:** Produces niche-specific content with personalization, keyword/tag SEO features, and content seeding; long-form quality is weaker; plans range from $29 to $199 monthly for 100–2,500 articles.
- **Peppertype:** Lightweight, beginner-friendly tool offering templates, copywriting frameworks, autocorrect, and engagement tracking; free trial and paid plans with custom enterprise pricing.

The author favors Jasper as one of the best options for high-quality content and notes the article contains affiliate links.

Origin PC announced the Eon15-S gaming laptop, starting at $999. The base model has an Nvidia 1050Ti GPU, Intel Core i3 processor and 120GB SSD. A $100 upgrade adds a Core i5 CPU and double the storage. It also includes an IPS display and 24/7 US-based lifetime support, with a one-year warranty.

The Supreme Court declined to review Ghislaine Maxwell’s challenge to a ruling limiting the scope of her 2007 non-prosecution agreement with Jeffrey Epstein. Maxwell argued that its protection of potential co-conspirators applied nationwide, but the solicitor general said the case-specific issue did not warrant Supreme Court review. Maxwell is serving a 20-year prison sentence for sex trafficking of a minor and other charges.

The 5-Day Low of the Range Strategy goes long at the close when IBS is below 0.25 and the close is below the previous five days’ lowest low, exiting after five days. Since January 1993, it produced 309 winners from 517 trades, averaging 0.46% per trade with a roughly 60% win rate and larger average winners than losers. Profitability peaks at three to seven days; a five-day exit delivered a 10.76% annualized return while invested for 510 days, versus 2,826 days for buy and hold. Performance has weakened recently. A short-selling version uses today’s range—0.75 produces more entries, while 0.9 better matches the long strategy’s fill rate—and has yielded nearly 10%, though short trading is more difficult.

Central-laboratory RT-PCR was the gold standard for COVID-19 testing but could involve delays, nasopharyngeal swab discomfort and collection difficulties, and additional sample handling. The Sal6830 SARS-CoV-2 Saliva Test was developed as a point-of-care alternative using self-collected saliva processed directly in a sealed cartridge, with results in approximately 30 minutes.

A prospective study at two U.S. health clinics evaluated six healthcare workers without laboratory training. In blinded testing of 48 samples at 1.9 times the limit of detection, all 24 negative samples were correctly identified, while 23 of 24 positive samples were detected and one was invalid. In 119 participants suspected of COVID-19, Sal6830 results had 87.2% positive agreement, 97.2% negative agreement, and 93.3% overall agreement with the Cepheid Xpert Xpress CoV-2/Flu/RSV test. Differences were attributed to the platforms’ viral capture methods: the Cepheid test detects viral particles and noninfectious debris, whereas Sal6830 captures intact virions.

A usability questionnaire completed by nine workers found the system easy to use, interpretable, and usable without technical support. All participants were confident using it, and all would recommend it to another non-laboratory healthcare professional. The authors concluded that Sal6830 could be operated accurately and confidently by non-laboratory-trained healthcare workers without additional training or technical backup.

Neural Radiance Cache trains a neural shader on live game data to infer final lighting from one-bounce path-traced rays, reducing GPU demands while improving real-time global illumination, indirect-light quality, scalability, and adaptability.
Washington appealed Nelson’s Spokane County judgment; the court reversed and remanded.

This application, a continuation of U.S. patent application Ser. No. 14/840,619 filed Aug. 31, 2015, describes systems, methods, and devices for a voice-directed inspection system supporting multiple inspectors of business assets.

The system includes a host computer, one or more site computers communicating with the host over a network (wired or wireless, WAN/LAN), and inspection assistance devices—each comprising a portable computer device and headset—positioned at inspection sites near the asset being inspected. Inspection plans, divided into sections containing steps, are created or received by a site computer, which may include an inspection plan editor used to create, modify, and store plans and translate instructions into speech. Inspectors receive audible commands and supply spoken results, which are stored and transmitted back to the host computer, potentially using SSL encryption.

To permit parallel work, a site computer receives assignment requests from inspection assistance devices, determines whether multiple unfinished sections of a plan exist and whether they interfere (for example, pertaining to physically distinct parts of the asset), and distributes sections accordingly—by priority of importance, order of request, inspector qualification, or prior work on those sections. The site computer receives completion updates as individual steps finish or batched, then forwards them to the host computer. Requests may specify a particular section or any unfinished section, and multiple inspector identifiers may be associated with the same plan and asset.

The portable computer device includes a speech module, text-to-speech, speech recognition using speaker-independent, self-adapting voice templates, transcription of free-form audio, optional barcode scanning, and an inspection assistance program handling sign-on, authorization, section skipping, mandatory sections, completion determination, and result review. The disclosure incorporates by reference a lengthy list of patents and patent applications.

The passage argues that criticism of originalism asks the wrong question: judges are legal decision-makers, not historians. In New York State Rifle & Pistol Ass’n v. Bruen, the Supreme Court adopted a two-step test for Second Amendment challenges. Courts first determine whether the challenged conduct is covered by the amendment’s plain text; if so, the government must show that its regulation is consistent with the nation’s historical tradition of firearm regulation. Justice Stephen Breyer and Judge Carlton Reeves objected that this historical inquiry is impractical for judges.

The passage contends that judges’ legal role makes the inquiry manageable. Step one requires determining the original meanings of terms such as “people,” “keep,” “bear,” and “arms.” Step two asks whether evidence establishes a genuine, recurring regulatory tradition rather than an outlier practice. Historical sources may be harder to locate, but they are durable and reliable, while burdens of proof help resolve uncertainty. Replacing historical inquiry with means-ends scrutiny would make judges resemble legislators and, if originalism is correct, would be unnecessary because history reveals the law.

The speaker celebrates winning the Cup and praises Buffalo’s young team, while reflecting on the team’s playoff success after last year’s early exit. He credits resilient teammates, veteran experience, and contributions from injured players, including Hull, describing the grueling journey as worthwhile.

An MIT OpenCourseWare poker lecture emphasizes evaluating decisions by expected value rather than by a single result. Using credit-card roulette and a bus-stop example, the professor illustrates how randomness averages out over time, good decisions can produce bad outcomes, and bad decisions can produce good outcomes. Players should therefore analyze their reasoning independently of the outcome and compare their choices with the best decision available.

The lecture presents three levels of poker reasoning. Level one compares a specific hand against a specific opponent hand and relies heavily on hand-reading. Level two compares one’s hand against an opponent’s range of possible hands and is called exploitative play: opponents’ tendencies are modeled and used to adjust their estimated hand distribution. This can be profitable, but modeling is difficult, assumptions may be wrong, and adaptive opponents can exploit a static model. Level three compares ranges of hands and uses optimal, Nash-equilibrium-style play. Randomization makes opponents indifferent among actions and protects against exploitation, while profits against skilled opponents come from their occasional inconsistencies. Rock-paper-scissors is used to contrast exploitative and optimal strategies.

Blinds and antes create the incentive to participate and compete for forced money. A “Who’s Taller?” game demonstrates why poker without blinds would struggle to remain a game. Effective stack size depends on the chips that can actually be lost to players still capable of acting, while position determines how many players must be beaten to steal the blinds. Equity may describe winning against remaining cards, an opponent’s possible hands, or a specified range; it can be calculated by counting card combinations or with tools such as PokerStove.

The instructor recommends raising rather than calling when folded to in tournaments, usually to about 2.25 big blinds when antes are present. He advises shoving with roughly 12 big blinds or less with antes, or 10 or less without antes, though a raise remains acceptable. Suggested opening ranges widen substantially by position, from about 6% under the gun to roughly 55% on the button. Conservative starting ranges are preferred, including value on suited hands and connectors; suited cards are more useful because a flush is less obvious when the player holds two cards of that suit. Small blind raises cost less but leave the player out of position postflop. Short stacks can justify wider shoving ranges, although larger shoves may induce more opponents to fold.

Finally, the lecture distinguishes bluffing—betting a weak hand to induce folds—from value betting—betting a strong hand to elicit calls. Medium-strength hands are generally checked toward showdown. Poker decisions should account for expected value, ranges, equity, stack size, position, and blinds rather than relying on pocket cards alone.

Many UK ovarian cancer cases are diagnosed late: only one-third are identified at stages 1–2, and nearly half first present as emergencies. The four main symptoms are persistent bloating, difficulty eating or feeling full quickly, changes in urination, and persistent pelvic or tummy pain. Symptoms are often vague or dismissed, while barriers include difficulty obtaining appointments and healthcare providers dismissing concerns.

There is no routine screening test for ovarian cancer. CA-125 may be elevated by non-cancerous conditions and cannot diagnose cancer alone, although doctors may use it during assessment or treatment monitoring. Women are advised to seek medical advice if symptoms are persistent, new or concerning, even without all four main symptoms. Other possible signs include lower-back pain, digestive discomfort, bleeding after menopause and unusual fatigue.

Ovarian Cancer Action provides a free online symptom checker and downloadable symptom diary to help identify patterns and support GP consultations. Early diagnosis is important: the passage cites 95% survival when caught early, compared with 16% at stage four. Most stage-one patients had experienced symptoms, so Jo Stanford rejects the “silent killer” label and urges women and those supporting them to recognise symptoms and seek prompt care.

DryShips raised $14.5 million through a continuous equity offering, issuing 7,912,449 post-reverse-split shares at an average price of $1.79. The April 10–17 issuance diluted shareholders by 16.8%, leaving 54.92 million shares outstanding and an equity market capitalization of $106 million on April 17. Kalani Investors failed to fulfill $5 million and $25 million fixed requests, providing only 48% of the $30 million sought.

Weak demand left $173.4 million still to be issued, equal to 164% of the company’s market value. Issuance represented 8.86% of trading volume, the weakest result in the offering program. At the recent pace, completing the offering would take about 54 trading days and require roughly 105.7 million additional shares at a 15% discount, causing substantial further dilution.

The author attributes weak sales partly to a 56% price decline following DryShips’ 1-for-4 reverse split. The author expects the company eventually to pursue debt financing and resume equity issuance during any resulting price rebound. The recent sales also moved the $75 million F-3 eligibility threshold further away.

On September 20, 2017, Hurricane Maria struck Puerto Rico with 155 mph sustained winds, torrential rain, island-wide flooding, extensive infrastructure and electricity-grid damage, more than $82 billion in damages, and losses of about 80% of crop value. Indirect emergency-related deaths are difficult to count because disrupted transportation can restrict access to medicine and health care, while inconsistent cause-of-death guidelines and training complicate mortality counts. Previous research on Maria examined excess mortality but covered few causes, ended in October 2017, and did not account for population displacement.

The study proposes a generalized additive semiparametric Poisson regression model to estimate cause-specific excess deaths after Maria while controlling for population size, mortality trends across years, and within-year variation. It uses pre- and post-emergency period indicators, cause-of-death indicators, and their interactions. Coefficients are estimated through penalized likelihood, with smoothing parameters selected by restricted maximum likelihood. Population displacement is incorporated. Excess deaths are estimated by contrasting predicted post-emergency mortality with the corresponding pre-emergency estimate, avoiding double-counting displacement.

At the 2017 Molecule ProKart Series finale at Hamilton’s Agrisea Raceway, Dylan Drysdale, Tim Loughran and Garry Cullum won the Wifiplus KZ2, Aarque Group KZ2 Masters and KZ2 Restricted class titles, respectively. Aaron Wilson won the KZ2 Final after Mat Kinsman retired, while Drysdale’s second place secured his championship. Loughran won the Masters Pre-Final and finished second in the Final to take the title; Brett Hollander placed second overall and Enrico van der Griend third. Cullum won all three Restricted heats and both finals, taking the title by 20 points over Regan Hall, with Aaron Wooley third.
NASA’s HAMMER mission could deploy a nuclear device to destroy asteroid Bennu if it threatened Earth. Bennu has a 1-in-2,700 chance of impact on September 21, 2135.

Hendrik Bessembinder’s 2017 study of 26,000 U.S. stocks from 1926–2015 found that only 43% outperformed one-month Treasury bills, while just 86 stocks generated half of all returns. Thirty stocks accounted for 30% of returns, showing that strong market averages were driven by a small number of companies while the median stock performed poorly. A similar Norwegian study covering 1985–2017 found that only 18 companies, 2.7% of IPOs, explained the Oslo Stock Exchange’s 2,000 billion NOK in value creation, with most shares failing to exceed risk-free rates. Because randomly selected stocks are more likely to underperform, the passage recommends passive funds as the simplest option and emphasizes diversification for investors selecting individual stocks.

With no clear attack, either team may kick the ball out when the referee continues play despite an injury, allowing assistance. After treatment, the other team takes the throw-in, generally backward to the opponent’s defender; neither side may exploit the gesture, and a midfielder should pass back. If the referee stops play for an injury, it restarts with a dropped ball, which may similarly be passed backward.

Intelligent predictive maintenance, or e-Maintenance, is presented as a major pillar of e-Manufacturing that supports near-zero downtime through real-time, smart monitoring, degradation prediction, performance assessment, and web-enabled control. Web-enabled agents can integrate maintenance decisions with CRM, ERP, and e-commerce systems, while remote machine assessment requires sensors, reasoning agents, wireless communication, virtual integration, and interface platforms. Research priorities include predictive intelligence, quality–degradation mapping, data mining and knowledge conversion, scalable networking and informatics platforms, security, distributed decision systems, workforce training, and an e-manufacturing-oriented enterprise culture.

Reconfigurable maintenance aligns production-system configurations with customer requirements and changing demand. It considers tolerances, maintenance policies, quality, production costs, and possible failures while enabling cooperation among companies through shared diagnostic knowledge, service activities, productivity information, and lifecycle data.

Modular reconfigurable maintenance uses a distributed architecture, monitoring modules, sensors, radio-signal transmission, and a control center to support remote maintenance, cost reduction, and rapid detection of adverse conditions. Historical data, measurement interpretation, degradation trends, and expert systems help identify faults, assess reliability, select corrective measures, and update the knowledge base. Maintenance policies must adapt as systems are reconfigured.

The conclusion emphasizes that competitive pressures and mass customization require rapid, low-cost responses, making integrated reconfigurable maintenance essential for reducing costs, improving quality, and ensuring production-system reliability.

The author admits to prematurely abandoning the market and presents 21 charts challenging bearish forecasts on U.S. equities and volatility products. They cite signs of underlying strength in market breadth and ask what happens if equities rally instead. Disclosures state the author is long U.S. equities and VIX and is uncompensated except by Seeking Alpha.

Teachers’ Union of Ireland general secretary John MacGabhann advised teachers against Facebook friendships with students, warning that virtual relationships can blur professional boundaries and cause professional or legal harm. He urged members to think before posting, avoid hasty or angry online comments and disputes, and ignore employers’ unreasonable demands for constant availability, including switching off devices when necessary.

- VentureWire’s May 17, 2001 edition highlights Tahoe Networks’ launch with a $38 million first round led by Redpoint Ventures, with Accel Partners participating. Startups.com became Startups, Inc., shifted from company acceleration to market intelligence, and cut 11 of 35 staff. Hermes said BTPS allocated $965 million for private-company and private-equity investments, including up to $50 million in Botts Capital Partners 2 and a stake in Botts & Co. OffRoad Capital reorganized into OffRoad Technologies and OffRoad Capital and reduced its workforce from 60 to 30.
- Other features report that Flatiron Partners was continuing to seek investments, iBase was expanding into the U.S. following a £4.2 million Series B, and DataSynapse expected to close a $15 million Series B within two weeks.
- Funding announcements included $9 million for Alphamosaic, $3.5 million for Comlase, $7 million for Xora, $8 million for e.Intelligence, $9 million for Foundstone, $2 million for Yube, $5 million for Beyond Genomics, $1.1 million for Cpocket, and $3 million for Embark, bringing its Series F total to $8 million. InterWest invested in Algorx; eVentures took a minority stake in White Amber; and Orange agreed to acquire a one-third stake in 3G Infrastructure.
- Eazel ceased operations after failing to secure additional funding, while RoundArch cut 34 employees, or 12% of its North American staff. New products and ventures included Compete, Sightward, Impart Technology, and Wireless Intellect Labs, a research center formed by EdgeMatrix and MobileOne.
- M&A activity included acquisitions by All Bases Covered, Princeton eCom, printCafe, Pitman, Bignose, and eKit.com; printCafe bought the assets of bankrupt Impresse, and Lost Boys merged with MetaDesign following its acquisition of Lab Production.
- The edition also reported new chairmen and executives at Clarity, SmartBargains, Creative Planet, CyLex Systems, Zone Labs, PrivateExpress, and EVLogix. Bezeq and Discount Capital Markets announced a $50 million communications-startup fund, while Encompass Ventures and Atlas Venture added personnel.

The executive pledges zealous service and seeks to administer the Constitution by enforcing federal laws, managing foreign relations and revenue, commanding the armed forces, and promoting national interests within the limits of executive authority. Foreign policy should preserve peace, cultivate fair and honorable friendships, and demonstrate the restraint appropriate to a powerful nation. Reserved state powers will be respected, while strict public economy will reduce the national debt and curb wasteful spending. Tariffs should equitably balance agriculture, commerce, and manufacturing, except for products essential to national independence; internal improvements and the diffusion of knowledge are also important.

Standing armies will not be expanded in peacetime, and the military will remain subordinate to civil power. The Navy, forts, arsenals, dockyards, and military improvements will be maintained, while the national militia is affirmed as the country’s chief defense. Policy toward Indian tribes should be just and liberal, respecting their rights and needs. Administrative reform should correct patronage abuses, restore proper appointment processes, and select diligent, competent, and honest officials. The speaker seeks guidance from predecessors, the other branches of government, and citizens, while relying on divine providence for the country’s continued welfare.

The passage reviews the historical development and political shaping of education in the Turkish Republic of Northern Cyprus (TRNC). Education evolved from Ottoman-era religious schooling through British colonial ethnic divisions and the post-1960 Republic of Cyprus into the post-1974 Northern Cyprus system, marked by close relations with Turkey and Turkish-language instruction. Education Council decisions addressed teacher training, curricula, textbooks, infrastructure, higher education, and quality, while the Ministry of Education, teachers’ unions, and other institutions also shaped policy.

The study focuses on how TRNC presidents’ discourses on history, identity, and education have influenced policy alongside Council decisions. Rauf Denktaş emphasized national identity, history, and integration with Turkey; Mehmet Ali Talat emphasized European harmonization and modernization; Derviş Eroğlu focused on cooperation with Turkey and technical education; Mustafa Akıncı highlighted multiculturalism, peace, and intercommunal dialogue; and Ersin Tatar prioritized national identity and Turkish integration. Other recurring issues include calls for greater English provision, internationalization and foreign-student policies, cooperation with Turkey, and debates over secular and religious education.

History textbooks have largely presented Turkish-Cypriot-centered narratives, particularly following 1974, reinforcing division and portraying Greek Cypriots as aggressors. Reforms since the early 2000s and after the 2004 Annan Plan sought more pluralistic and reconciliatory curricula but encountered political and societal resistance. The passage recommends multi-perspective, scientifically grounded curricula, long-term policies less dependent on political leaders’ ideologies, and teacher training, curriculum reform, and public-awareness initiatives supporting peace while preserving cooperation with Turkey and local educational autonomy.

Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov said India’s SCO accession has increased its political profile and capacity to support stability in Central and South Asia and help resolve the Afghanistan crisis. He aimed for India-Russia trade of $30 billion by 2025 and said deeper defence ties would expand Russian technology transfers to India. Lavrov doubted the US strategy of using force in Afghanistan, citing NATO’s failure to curb extremism, terrorism and drug production. He denied supporting the Taliban, saying contacts sought to protect citizens and press for UN-compliant negotiations. He argued Afghanistan’s settlement required the government, Taliban, neighbours and Central Asian states.

A letter from fired assistant U.S. attorney Michael Ben’Ary alleged that DOJ leadership prioritized punishing perceived President Trump enemies over public safety and national security by removing career officials from U.S. attorney’s offices and the FBI. Ben’Ary said a false social media post led to his abrupt firing during a prosecution related to the 2021 Afghanistan airport bombing and criticized justice depending on DOJ officials’ social media views.
The coach urges a strong start and preparation for an opponent playing at home, noting the team has a chance to end the series. He warns that a poor beginning could make for a difficult night.

New England Patriots wide receiver Malcolm Mitchell received the Promise Hero Award from America’s Promise Alliance for overcoming literacy challenges and promoting reading. After struggling to read in college, Mitchell taught himself using children’s books and practiced until he could read multiple books simultaneously. He later founded Read with Malcolm, which introduces books to children in underserved communities and promotes age-appropriate reading materials in homes and schools.

Mitchell, who grew up in a single-parent household with his mother, brother and sister, credits his family and upbringing with shaping his persistence. The initiative’s goals include inspiring children to read, expanding their access to books and helping them overcome adversity. Mitchell graduated from the University of Georgia in 2015, was drafted by the Patriots and wrote *The Magician’s Hat*. He advises young people facing difficulties to never give up, keep improving and view adversity as an opportunity to achieve something meaningful. He hopes to continue writing, reading and motivating children through literacy while also pursuing football.

Yandex announced it will report second-quarter 2018 financial results on July 26, followed by an 8:00 a.m. ET conference call and webcast. The company develops machine-learning-powered search, transportation, navigation, information, and mobile services.

The article examines the digital accessibility skills gap in computing education and professional training, particularly in India. It defines digital accessibility as inclusive design and development of technologies usable by people with disabilities, describes the WCAG 2.2 POUR principles and three conformance levels, and notes that accessibility is legally mandated in several jurisdictions. Despite these mandates, the 2025 WebAIM report found that only 5.2% of the top one million websites met WCAG Level AA. Inaccessibility also creates economic losses, while surveys identify insufficient accessibility knowledge, tools, organizational support, and training as major barriers. Accessibility education has expanded internationally, but research and cross-sector initiatives remain limited in the Global South, especially India.

The authors designed and delivered a one-day, beginner-friendly workshop for Indian software professionals, computer science educators, and UX designers. It used preparation, execution, and post-workshop reflection phases and covered accessibility basics, universal and inclusive design, accessible software development, testing and reporting, and teaching accessibility. Instruction combined lectures, think-pair-share activities, hands-on use of assistive technologies and testing tools, case studies, lightning talks, and four thematic booths. Pre- and post-workshop surveys assessed participants’ knowledge, attitudes, confidence, and intended application.

Among 73 participants, 33 were software engineers, 28 educators, and 12 UX designers; most had no previous formal accessibility experience, and four self-identified as having disabilities. Participants rated the activities highly, with accessibility-tool demonstrations receiving the most “Exceptional” ratings. Post-workshop, 73 considered the workshop highly engaging, 64 felt very confident, 73 considered it highly effective, and 73 intended to apply their learning. All 100% would recommend it, while 52% reported a significant shift in their perception of accessibility and personal responsibility for advancing it.

Open-ended responses identified interest in advanced inclusive design, AI and emerging technologies, diverse user contexts, organizational policy and commitment, and further practice-based learning. Limitations included technical difficulty for some participants, the educational limitations of disability simulations, insufficient domain-specific examples, and a desire for continuing resources. Recommendations include distributing pre-workshop materials, customizing content by role or domain, adding real-world cases, encouraging peer learning, and providing follow-up opportunities and shared resources. The authors conclude that experiential accessibility training can improve confidence, practical understanding, and inclusive-design mindsets, but sustained follow-up is needed to assess workplace application.

The passage examines whether the Supreme Court will uphold President Donald Trump’s firing of FTC Commissioner Rebecca Kelly Slaughter. It frames the issue through *Humphrey’s Executor*, which rejected Franklin D. Roosevelt’s attempt to remove FTC Commissioner William Humphrey at will and upheld statutory removal protections. Although the author believes Slaughter’s firing will likely be upheld, the Court need not abandon the precedent entirely.

Recent cases focus on an agency’s actual powers. In *Seila Law*, the CFPB failed to qualify for independence because its single director wielded binding rulemaking, adjudicatory, and executive enforcement powers unlike those of the 1935 FTC. The modern FTC retains a bipartisan, multi-member structure, but its expanded regulatory and enforcement authority, reduced adjudicatory role, and increasingly ideological approach make it resemble an executive enforcement agency.

The author expects a “mend it, don’t end it” approach: preserve *Humphrey’s Executor* while narrowing agency independence, potentially harming the FTC but not the distinctively structured Federal Reserve. The Court’s review question separates the constitutionality of Slaughter’s firing from the precedent’s future constitutionality.

In a 14 February 2017 speech responding to President Jacob Zuma’s State of the Nation Address, DA leader Mmusi Maimane condemned the ANC government, alleging that its transformation agenda enriched connected elites rather than ordinary South Africans. He criticised the deaths of 94 patients at Esidimeni, the Marikana 34, the security surrounding Parliament, and what he called the government’s corruption and disregard for vulnerable people.

Maimane described nearly six million mainly black young South Africans unable to find work, about 500,000 children leaving education annually, three million people under 25 not in education, employment or training, and 340,000 additional unemployed youths. He criticised proposed land reform, black economic empowerment, a state mining company, the MPRDA Bill and a trillion-rand nuclear build as benefiting ANC insiders.

The DA’s proposed “Rescue Plan” included improving teacher training and school accountability, expanding student aid, vocational training, apprenticeships and internships, and strengthening universities. It sought private-sector-led employment, reduced business regulation, entrepreneur funding, infrastructure and broadband investment, independent electricity producers, partial privatisation of state enterprises, inclusive black economic empowerment and land ownership reform. It also proposed adding 50,000 police officers, expanding clinics and basic healthcare, and reducing corruption through transparent tenders, spending limits, fewer ministries and reduced government perks. Maimane concluded by presenting the DA’s vision of an inclusive, prosperous South Africa that would work with rather than against its people.

Alexa and Echo can reduce cleaning labor in several ways: the Cleaning Buddy skill sets cleaning tasks on a schedule; Amazon voice purchasing (with a four-digit confirmation code and one-click payment enabled) lets you order supplies by voice; Neato and Roomba vacuums can be started, paused, stopped, scheduled, and queried via voice commands; and the Laundrapp service handles laundry pickup and delivery in about 100 US cities, while Good Housekeeping or Stains Be Gone skills offer stain-removal advice.

The study examines topographic defects introduced by electropolishing highly polished bulk niobium for superconducting radio-frequency cavities. White-light interferometry and atomic force microscopy showed that electropolishing develops sharp intergranular steps, with heights up to 70 nm and local slope angles near 50°. Average and peak-to-valley roughness generally increased with electropolishing removal, while microstructure strongly influenced the step distribution.

Sequential electropolishing showed that each polishing cycle smooths an existing step but forms a new one, with the boundary shifting about 0.6 µm for each micrometer removed. Sequential measurements indicated that relative grain orientation, rather than removal depth, primarily controls step height and slope. Electrolyte exposure without applied voltage caused only minor additional etching, indicating that electropolishing itself is the main source of the steps.

London-theory calculations modeled the steps as parallel surfaces connected by an inclined plane. The models predict magnetic-field enhancement and current crowding at the step bottom, together with suppression of the superheating field. Superheating-field suppression depends on step height, slope angle, and coherence length, while magnetic-field enhancement depends on step height relative to the London penetration depth. These defects can substantially reduce the achievable peak magnetic field, with degradation greater than previously estimated. Alloying reduces magnetic-field enhancement but makes superheating-field suppression more severe.

Fick-law diffusion simulations showed that sharp steps deplete impurities near the step bottom and concentrate them near the top. When step dimensions approach or exceed the impurity diffusion length, substantial spatial nonuniformity develops at the preferred vortex-entry location. Small slope angles and step heights preserve impurity-dose uniformity, relevant to low-temperature baking and nitrogen-infusion treatments. The study concludes that smoother surfaces and microscopic assessment of roughness are necessary for high-field SRF performance. It also notes that power spectral density analysis alone is inadequate because it discards phase information and cannot reliably distinguish performance-relevant defect geometries.

MIT researchers developed an engineered prime-editing system, called vPE, that reduces unwanted DNA mutations by modifying Cas9 proteins and stabilizing the RNA template. Tested in mouse and human cells, the system cut errors to as little as one-sixtieth of the original rate—from roughly 1 in 7 to 1 in 101 edits in one mode, and from 1 in 122 to 1 in 543 in another. The approach adds no delivery steps and could make gene therapies for hundreds of genetic diseases safer and more practical. Researchers are now working to improve editing efficiency and tissue-specific delivery.

British police declared a "major incident" in Amesbury, England, after a man and a woman in their 40s were found unconscious and hospitalized in critical condition following exposure to an unknown substance. Counterterrorism officers are working with Wiltshire Police, who cordoned off locations the pair visited and said it is unclear whether a crime was committed. The town is near Salisbury, where Sergei and Yulia Skripal were poisoned with a nerve agent.

D.A.N. Joint Venture III, L.P. sought to deny Ambrozy Jerry Fasolak’s Chapter 7 discharge under Bankruptcy Code §§ 727(a)(2)–(5), alleging fraudulent transfers, inadequate financial records, false oaths, and failure to explain lost assets. Fasolak, a 72-year-old retired manufacturing businessman, had transferred funds and other assets to his wife and made inaccuracies in his bankruptcy filings and testimony.

The court found that although some transfers occurred and the filings contained errors, the evidence did not establish fraudulent intent, missing records, knowing false oaths, or an unexplained loss of specific substantial assets. Credible testimony indicated that Fasolak had withdrawn from managing his business and finances and relied on his wife, that omitted corporate income reflected limited consulting work, and that the errors resulted from mistake or misunderstanding rather than deception. The court entered final judgment for Fasolak and ordered that his Chapter 7 discharge be granted.

Horse polo originated in Persia more than 2,000 years ago and spread through the Middle East, Central Asia, and the Far East. The modern game developed in India, where the wooden ball was called “polo,” before British travelers carried it to England and the United States. Known as “The Sport of Kings,” polo initially developed a reputation as an elite pastime.

The Milwaukee Polo Club, formed in the Milwaukee area in 1923 and now based in Hartland, presents itself as an accessible, “blue collar” alternative. Its members include nurses, students, retirees, and other ages and occupations. Matches cost $5 for adults, with children free, and spectators can visit the horses and players. Games typically feature six seven-minute chukkas, a halftime horse-and-player visit, and last about two hours.

Play depends on safe field conditions and fair weather, although horse demonstrations continue on off-days. The club emphasizes proper feeding, grooming, workload limits, rest, and balance in caring for polo horses, which are regarded as essential teammates.

A hockey coach emphasizes preparation, focus, puck execution, and making the most of rare opportunities rather than relying on momentum. In a salary-cap environment, he says team depth and player development are essential because injuries are unpredictable and teams cannot depend on one or two players. He praises both finalists’ depth and effort, describing team building as winning together, sacrificing, and supporting teammates.

After a poor previous game, the coaching staff reviewed the forecheck and stressed proper puck handling, positioning, and execution, since turnovers strengthen opponents’ forechecks. He notes that goaltenders have performed better at home and that team play must support them. An injured player reportedly feels good, with no negative reports. Despite strong performances by both teams, he says the final has been close and difficult, with the outcome still uncertain.

After recent ICE arrests, Austin ISD directed staff not to distribute unvetted resources or discuss controversial political issues on district property, citing heightened state scrutiny. At least 51 people were detained, and students reported anxiety about family safety. Board Vice President Paul Saldana criticized the memo as overly conservative and said the board was not briefed. The district posted general immigrant resources, while Education Austin distributed ICE guidance, lawyer referrals, and Know Your Rights materials and urged clearer family communication.

A 13-year-old girl was shot in the thigh in a Guildford, Sydney-west garage on Tuesday night about 9.45pm. She was taken to Westmead Children's Hospital in serious but stable condition; police believe the shooting was not random.

Penny stocks—low-priced equities mostly traded over the counter or on Pink Sheets rather than major exchanges—are presented as highly speculative and generally poor investments. Many represent new, unproven, declining, unprofitable, or bankrupt businesses, and the passage claims nearly all ultimately fail. Companies use OTC markets because they cannot meet, or choose to avoid, the strict and costly listing requirements of exchanges such as the NYSE and Nasdaq.

OTC trading involves less regulation and financial disclosure, limited broker coverage, low liquidity, wide bid-ask spreads, high volatility, and potentially high per-share commissions. These conditions make research and trading expensive and expose investors to fraudulent “guru” offers, pump-and-dump schemes, and other scams. Some highly publicized success stories may therefore reflect manipulation rather than sound investing.

Although profits are possible, the passage rejects penny stocks as a dependable route to wealth and says consistently profitable penny-stock strategies are difficult to find. Investors may overlook opportunity costs and established companies while overestimating their own skill through hindsight. The full loss of an investment is possible, so the passage stresses understanding the risks, conducting due diligence, limiting exposure, and ultimately recommends avoiding penny stocks altogether.

Mark Warner accused Republicans of an unprecedented effort to undermine Robert Mueller’s investigation and FBI integrity through the Nunes memo. He said he and Sen. Richard Burr were denied pre-release access and House Democrats were blocked from releasing their memo. Warner warned that failing to address Russian election interference as a national cyberwarfare threat leaves the country less safe.

The passage studies many-to-one two-sided matching, where participants are assigned to teams and preferences may contain ties. Participant-justified envy-freeness prevents participants from envying participants held by teams they prefer when the envy is justified by those teams’ preferences, but it can leave teams highly unfair. Team envy-freeness up to one participant (team-EF1) addresses this concern, yet prior work cited in the passage shows that team-EF1 and participant-justified envy-freeness can be incompatible in many-to-one matching; deciding whether both hold is NP-hard.

A new criterion, team-justified EF1, accounts for participant preferences when evaluating team envy. Participants who strictly prefer the envied team are removed before comparison, after which one additional participant may be removed to eliminate remaining envy. Its ordinal counterpart, team-justified SD-EF1, uses stochastic dominance and allows ties. Balancedness, meaning team allocations differ in size by at most one, is also considered.

The main algorithm creates balanced team slots and participant-specific eligibility sets. In each iteration, it computes an eligible matching that maximizes team-slot values in round-robin order, breaking ties by lexicographically optimizing participants’ preferences. Eligibility sets are expanded when participants remain unmatched. The resulting allocation satisfies team-justified SD-EF1, participant-justified envy-freeness, balancedness, and Pareto optimality, and therefore is swap stable. The algorithm is polynomial-time implementable. With universally indifferent participants it reduces to round-robin drafting, while under strict preferences it coincides with participant-proposing Gale–Shapley. Earlier approaches either achieve fairness on both sides but can be severely unbalanced, or achieve fairness and balance but not swap stability.

With augmented tie-breaking, the algorithm is group-strategyproof for participants: no group can misreport its preferences so that every member strictly benefits. It is not individually strategyproof for teams. The passage also extends the algorithm to team quotas and preferences for participants or teams to remain unassigned. Using dummy participants and a dummy team, the extension produces partial allocations satisfying stability, Pareto optimality, participant group-strategyproofness, and an extended quota-adjusted form of team-justified SD-EF1. Overall, the work connects fair division and two-sided matching through an algorithm that combines round-robin and Gale–Shapley while addressing indifferences and fairness on both sides.

**Summary**

The passage contrasts digital leaders with "digital laggards" across five cultural dimensions. Digital laggards optimize short-term comfort, offering narrow "as-is" training and transactional, risk-averse cultures often paired with low trust in employees and leadership; even digital leaders find that instilling a learning mindset takes deliberate, sustained effort rather than a "light switch" change, and heavily regulated industries require pockets of controlled experimentation.

On data, digital leaders treat transparency as central: data are shared broadly across teams, are not restricted by role, and data-hoarding is discouraged, though appropriate governance and privacy controls are maintained to build trust (88% of digital leaders have standardized APIs versus 27% of laggards). Laggards keep data close to the vest, hoarding it as power, storing it in silos, and favoring a "culture of genius" and business judgment over data-driven decisions.

On measurement, digital leaders encourage collecting and examining relevant data, use detailed metrics and 360-degree reviews, and give teams flexibility and autonomy; measurement grounds realistic yet ambitious goals. Laggards set aspirational goals ungrounded in data, so employees avoid measurement and default to qualitative, process-adherence practices that stifle innovation.

Two case studies illustrate this: a pharmaceutical company built a localized experimentation environment that automated compliance checks in a quarter of the prior time and spread the tool to other groups, boosting morale and autonomy; a digitally transforming retailer replaced an audited quarterly report with a real-time dashboard, pushing sales data three times daily so leaders could act on inventory, marketing, and supply chain decisions.

Digital leaders also connect data-driven objectives to strategy through transparent methodologies and top-down/bottom-up goal setting, aligning teams vertically and horizontally, though some struggle with analysis overhead that displaces human intuition. Data culture itself is the coordinating mechanism at digital leaders, where espoused values and daily behavior reinforce each other; laggards show misalignment between stated values and behavior, with entrenched habits and weak leadership focus as barriers.

The passage concludes that transformation remains achievable and identifies four maturity patterns—data novice, insight ready, tech enabled, and data reliant—each requiring targeted actions, and notes that changing ingrained mindsets is the hardest part of transformation.

The address reviews a century of U.S. constitutional history, beginning with the Articles of Confederation and the creation of a stronger national union after independence. It credits the Constitution with expanding freedom, strengthening order, preserving the Union through civil war, and enabling national growth. The Supreme Court’s decision to preserve national supremacy is presented as final, while state autonomy and local self-government remain protected.

The speaker identifies the abolition of slavery and extension of citizenship to formerly enslaved people as the era’s most important political change. Despite disturbances in Southern communities, the speaker argues that there was no acceptable alternative to slavery or equal citizenship. He urges full constitutional protection for Black citizens, acknowledges that equal suffrage remains obstructed in some places, and warns that denying voting rights would threaten the government. He calls for universal education to address ignorance and corruption among voters and calls on all sections and races to prepare the next generation for civic responsibility.

Economic policy forms another major focus. The speaker supports preserving public credit, repaying the national debt at a lower interest rate, and maintaining a monetary system based on gold and silver, while calling for international agreement on their relative values. He argues that federal paper notes should be redeemable in coin rather than serve as compulsory legal tender. Government attention is also urged toward agriculture, manufacturing, transportation, harbors, waterways, and eventual development of an interoceanic canal, without granting exclusive commercial privileges to the United States.

The address calls for enforcement of religious freedom while condemning polygamy and any transfer of governmental authority to ecclesiastical organizations. It also advocates statutory civil-service rules governing minor executive offices and removals. Finally, the speaker vows to uphold the Constitution, enforce federal law, reduce government spending, ensure honest administration, respect states’ reserved rights, and rely on Congress, citizens, and patriotic cooperation to govern effectively.

The ATR trailing stop, introduced by J. Welles Wilder, is a volatility-based technical indicator that provides dynamic stop-loss levels based on the average true range (ATR). It helps manage risk, protect profits, minimize losses, identify exit points, and provide entry signals through breakouts or reversals at trailing-stop levels. Traders calculate stop values by multiplying ATR by a multiplier, typically 3.5, then subtracting it from the previous close for long positions or adding it for short positions. ATR bands derived from ATR can identify potential breakouts and gauge volatility intensity. A sustained breach of trailing-stop levels may signal a trend reversal, while the point where price intersects those levels indicates changing market dynamics. ATR trailing stops can be used with stocks and futures and combined with other technical indicators in trading strategies. Because the method primarily reflects current volatility and may not fully account for past performance and price movements, traders should consider trading uncertainty, potential losses, and additional technical and fundamental analysis.

Harvard President Drew Faust announced she will step down on June 30, 2018, after 11 years, coinciding with the conclusion of Harvard’s fundraising campaign, which has raised $8 billion against a $6.5 billion goal. Faust, who plans to take a sabbatical and return to scholarship, is credited with restoring campus trust, fostering collaboration, expanding financial aid, and supporting the arts and sciences, though her tenure also faced criticism and controversies. She will spend her final year advocating against threats to federal research funding, recruiting students and faculty, and advancing inclusion and belonging, while a search committee will be formed to select her successor.

Texas A&M receiver Christian Kirk bypassed his senior season and is the Aggies’ best hope to extend their streak of at least one NFL first-round selection dating to 2011. Projected as a fringe first-round pick, Kirk could become A&M’s 10th first-round choice in eight drafts. Safety Armani Watts projects as a mid-round choice, while receiver Damion Ratley is a possible late-round selection. Texas A&M had five players drafted in 2017, three in 2016 and two in 2015, while all three 2014 selections were first-round picks. Defensive tackle Zaycoven Henderson’s arrest and pending criminal case dropped his projection from a possible mid-round selection to uncertainty. Recent A&M first-rounders include Von Miller, Ryan Tannehill, Luke Joeckel, Jake Matthews, Mike Evans, Johnny Manziel, Cedric Ogbuehi, Germain Ifedi and Myles Garrett. The 2018 draft begins Thursday in Arlington.

Michigan State Superintendent Michael Rice is retiring after leading the state since 2019 and spending decades in education. Dearborn Public Schools Superintendent Glenn Maleyko will succeed him, with Chief Deputy Superintendent Sue Carnell serving temporarily.

Rice urged lawmakers to guarantee students 180 instructional days. Michigan schools can count up to seven teacher professional-development days as instructional time and shift up to 15 days to online instruction, while closures such as snow days can further reduce instruction. Reporting on how often schools use these options is not required.

Rice described slow academic recovery following pandemic disruptions, weak national test performance, chronic absenteeism and increased mental-health concerns. Third graders recorded their lowest reading scores in the 11-year history of Michigan’s M-STEP. Although Michigan has made progress through additional funding for vulnerable students, expanded preschool enrollment and a record 82% high school graduation rate, none of the state’s strategic education goals has been fully achieved.

Rice cited Mississippi’s science-of-reading training, literacy coaches, early-grade class sizes and protection of instructional time as models for improving literacy. More than 5,000 Michigan teachers have completed LETRS training and another 7,000 have started; Rice and the State Board of Education want it required for K-5 teachers.

Teacher shortages are also improving following state investments in stipends, scholarships and “grow your own” programs. The number of people preparing to enter teaching has risen from 9,500 in 2017 to 18,000 annually, though Rice said shortages are not over until every classroom is fully staffed.

Alphabet agreed to pay $24.5 million to settle Donald Trump’s lawsuit over YouTube’s post-January 6 suspension, with $22 million going to Trump and $2.5 million to co-plaintiffs. Trump directed his share toward a White House ballroom project. YouTube suspended his account in January 2021 and restored access in March 2023. Alphabet admitted no liability.

Peter Lynch, born in 1944, managed Fidelity’s Magellan Fund from 1977 to 1990. He increased the fund from $20 million to $14 billion, produced average annual returns of about 29%, and retired at age 43. His first investment, Flying Tiger Airlines, rose from $7 to $32 within two years.

Lynch’s strategy emphasized investing in understandable, undervalued companies and analyzing fundamentals rather than predicting markets or following short-term price movements. He favored simple business models, quality products, sound balance sheets, strong profit margins, and companies overlooked by large investors. He categorized companies as slow-growing, moderately growing, fast-growing, cyclical, emerging from crisis, or possessing undervalued assets. He viewed small, fast-growing companies as potential “ten baggers,” while recognizing their greater risks.

Magellan’s portfolio focused 30–40% on growth stocks, 10–20% each on moderately growing and cyclical stocks, the remainder mainly on turnarounds, and 1% on 500 smaller potential investments. Lynch reviewed holdings quarterly, analyzed earnings and prospects, rebalanced as needed, and remained fully invested. He reduced or sold holdings when prices rose without corresponding fundamental improvement and increased holdings when prices fell while fundamentals remained stable or improved.

Lynch also promoted fundamental research, long-term ownership, and the belief that individual investors could outperform large institutions, while noting that he had access to Fidelity’s extensive analytical resources and direct communication with company management.

George Afriyie has been relieved of his duties as vice president of the Ghana Football Association following a Tuesday Executive Committee meeting, confirming a rift with president Kwesi Nyantakyi. Afriyie had announced his intention to contest the GFA’s 2019 elections, but Nyantakyi never publicly endorsed him. Tensions reportedly grew over financial disagreements and suspicions that Afriyie sided with Nii Lante Vanderpuije, a critic of Nyantakyi.

Afriyie was removed as Black Stars Management Committee head two weeks before the vice-presidential dismissal and replaced by Winfred Osei, who praised Nyantakyi’s experience. His removal strengthens his campaign to replace Nyantakyi, although two former vice presidents, Fred Pappoe and Fred Crentsil, were also removed from office.

Afriyie says three terms on the Executive Committee gave him the experience to succeed Nyantakyi and build on the administration’s achievements. The dispute reflects divisions within the committee amid uncertainty over whether Nyantakyi will seek a fourth term in 2019. His tenure included three World Cup qualifications but also concerns over the Premier League and the FA Cup’s decline and eventual revival.

June 8, 2001 news clippings focused on the dispute over Enron-promoted Dabhol Power Company’s 2,184-MW Maharashtra project. The 740-MW first phase was operating, while the 1,444-MW second phase, 92% complete, had been postponed. MSEB, the plant’s only buyer, stopped purchasing power after disputing DPC’s costs and defaulting on $48 million in payments; Enron had issued a preliminary termination notice.

At a three-day Singapore meeting, Indian and foreign lenders formed an IDBI-led committee to negotiate with MSEB. They engaged Stone & Webster to evaluate suspending or closing the plant for up to a year, including potential losses for DPC, MSEB and lenders, project revenues, additional funding needs, restart costs, and whether completing the power blocks and LNG terminal would improve the project’s value. Foreign lenders favored suspension, while DPC proposed temporary suspension or completion of mechanical work and deferral of the remainder. DPC also indicated willingness to reduce its projected rate of return from 16% to 11% if MSEB guaranteed purchases and reinstated the power purchase agreement.

Prime Minister Atal Bihari Vajpayee expressed optimism that the dispute could be resolved through central government intervention, prompting private power producers to anticipate an early settlement. Lenders, however, wanted more proactive commitments from the government. State electricity boards were also considered unlikely buyers of DPC power because their supply costs made tariffs above roughly Rs 3 per unit unaffordable, making the proposed third-party sales unlikely. The Godbole renegotiation committee said DPC’s return on equity should not exceed 16% even at 90% plant load factor and asked IDFC and Crisil to develop supporting parameters.

DPC appealed to the Bombay High Court for a stay on MERC’s May 29 order, which restrained reactivation of the escrow account and arbitration proceedings. DPC argued that MERC lacked jurisdiction and that the PPA provided for international arbitration. It also objected to public hearings, with a hearing scheduled for June 11. MSEB had alleged failures to supply power on three dates and imposed a penalty of Rs 401.24 crore; MERC’s next hearing was set for June 14. The Godbole panel also accused DPC of maintaining conflicting positions, and another negotiation round was planned for June 30.

Commentary in the clippings favored a negotiated settlement over prolonged litigation, called for honoring contracts and improving state electricity boards’ finances and project assessment, and supported direct third-party sales by independent producers. Narmada Bachao Andolan leader Medha Patkar demanded a judicial inquiry, described Enron supporters as “anti-nationals,” and announced further agitation.

A National Geographic Society–supported assessment found low cheetah population estimates in southern Africa, supporting scientists’ recommendation to list the species as Endangered on the IUCN Red List.

The study assesses whether ovitrap egg records and climate data can forecast invasive Aedes mosquito abundance in the Basque Country, northern Spain, where no autochthonous Aedes-borne disease transmission had been recorded, although imported dengue, chikungunya, and Zika cases had increased and Aedes albopictus and Aedes japonicus were present. Ovitrap data from 2013–2023 across 63 municipalities and meteorological data from 2016–2023 were aggregated biweekly by province. Araba was excluded because sparse, zero-heavy data were insufficient for reliable model fitting.

GLM, SARIMAX, Random Forest, and Conditional Inference Tree models were evaluated with and without lagged egg counts and weather variables, using 2023 as the test year. Temperature had the strongest association with egg counts, while humidity had an intermediate relationship and precipitation a weak negative association. Including lagged variables generally improved performance. Random Forest fitted the training data best but appeared to overfit; GLM generalized best on the test data, with R² values of 0.85 in Gipuzkoa and 0.81 in Bizkaia, followed closely by SARIMAX. Conditional Inference Trees performed worst. Poor Bizkaia test performance was attributed partly to unusually high egg counts in 2023 compared with the training period.

After refitting the best models through 2023, the study forecast lower Aedes abundance for 2024 at provincial and municipal levels. The findings identify egg abundance as an important predictor, emphasize temperature’s role, and support continuous localized surveillance to improve forecasting and vector-control strategies in non-endemic regions. Limitations include provincial microclimates, sparse data, dataset partitioning, and the potential benefits of shorter monitoring intervals.

A hockey coach says his team has been more comfortable, quick, and assertive at home in the playoffs and hopes to carry that advantage into the next Stanley Cup Final game. He describes the series as hard-fought and momentum-driven, praises both teams’ effort and star players, and emphasizes focusing on execution rather than the prize.

He views the Finals as a rare, exciting opportunity and a “one-and-done” event, while noting that Red Wings veterans and Hall of Famers such as Gordie Howe, Steve Yzerman, and Scotty Bowman remain special parts of the organization’s identity. He also discusses learning successful tactics from Igor Larionov and other great players.

The coach expresses confidence in the team and stresses enjoying the moment, while acknowledging the difficult economic conditions facing some Detroit residents. He expects Hossa to perform his usual role without worrying about scoring, says Pittsburgh’s defensemen were excellent, and smiles at the suggestion that his team was outcoached in the previous game.

Eight years after graduating, the author reflects fondly on college, recalling exceptional people, fascinating classes, and returning to campus after breaks. Yet they regret taking opportunities for granted and missing time for adventure. They emphasize that everyone experiences college differently and that their reflections concern only their own experience.

HPBOSE declared Himachal Pradesh Class 12 results for 2018 on April 24 at 14:07. Results were available through hpbose.org, examresults.net, indiaresults.com, and SMS by sending HP12ROLLNUMBER to 56263. The Class 12 exams ran March 6–29.

Seven candidates qualified for the April 18 special election to replace U.S. Rep. Tom Price in the 6th Congressional District, bringing the field to 15. Price was nominated as President Trump’s health secretary. A runoff is scheduled for June 20.

Liverpool’s 2017/18 season opens at Watford on August 12 and ends at home against Brighton on May 13. Fixtures include Everton, Manchester United, Swansea and Chelsea, with dates subject to broadcast changes.

Researchers at Cardiff University and collaborating UK institutions studied whether CT lung cancer screening encourages smoking cessation among high-risk British smokers. Nearly 2.5 million residents aged 50–75 received risk-factor questionnaires; 8,729 high-risk respondents were assessed and invited to screening or given standard cessation information. At two weeks, 10% of the screening group had quit versus 5% of controls; at two years, the figures were 15% and 5%, respectively. The findings suggest screening can prompt cessation without falsely reassuring smokers, although self-selection and distress about smoking may have influenced outcomes.

Geminids peak Wednesday night, best viewed from midnight to 4 a.m. Thursday, with up to 50 meteors possible. Rural, low-light locations improve views; no telescope is needed. A smaller crescent moon should aid visibility.

Caltech and six partners received $4.9 million from USGS for ShakeAlert development; the agency bought about $1 million in sensors. The system is designed to provide seconds of warning for protective action. USGS estimates completion and operation require $38.3 million in capital and $16.1 million annually.

Northwestern’s first NCAA bid is within reach after a 66–59 upset of Wisconsin, but media pressure and games ahead pose risks. The Wildcats face Maryland next without Scottie Lindsey, expected to miss his fourth straight game due to mono.

Valmet’s Board approved a long-term share-based incentive plan for key employees covering 2018–2020. The 2018 reward depends on comparable EBITA margin and stable-business order growth in Services and Automation; part will be paid in shares and part in cash in 2019 to cover taxes. Rewarded shares have a two-year transfer restriction and generally must be returned if employment ends during it. The plan includes about 120 participants, with rewards capped at approximately 586,000 shares.

American Airlines’ November 19, 2001 email to Theresa Staab promoted Net SAAver weekend getaway fares. Domestic travel departed November 30 after 7 p.m. or December 1 and returned December 3 or 4; international travel departed November 29 or 30 and returned December 3 or 4. Tickets had to be purchased by November 23, 11:59 p.m. CT, and listed fares were roundtrip. Domestic fares ranged from $69 to $312, while international fares ranged from $59 to $519. A separate Thanksgiving web-only sale required purchase by November 21. Fares were available through AA.com to AAdvantage members, with some travel possibly on American Eagle. The email also offered AAdvantage Net SAAver Awards for eligible domestic trips starting at 4,000 miles plus $39 and promoted Florida, Fairmont Scottsdale Princess, Starwood, and Hertz vacation packages. Restrictions included excluded taxes and fees, nonrefundable tickets, limited seats, possible fare changes, and a change fee of up to $100.

A survey of 202 Illinois daycare administrators, managers and teachers found nutrition, exercise and tooth-brushing outranked sun safety; fewer than one in five named sun protection a top priority. About half of programs provided sunscreen, but 77% of those barred children from applying it themselves, and half used sprays, often aimed at faces. Most reported no sunburns. Experts said teachers need sun-safety education; parents can help by applying sunscreen and sending hats and long sleeves.

A Denver federal jury found radio host David Mueller liable for assault and battery against Taylor Swift, concluding he groped her during a 2013 backstage photo session before a concert. The eight-person jury reached the verdict on Aug. 14, 2017, after one day of deliberations, and awarded Swift the $1 compensation she had sought. Mueller had sued in 2015 claiming Swift's accusation was false and led radio station KYGO to fire him; Swift countersued. Swift, dropped from Mueller's suit Friday when a judge found insufficient evidence that she fabricated the encounter, was not told of that ruling, and the jury also found that Swift's mother and her manager, Frank Bell, had not interfered with Mueller's contract to get him fired. Swift said she would donate an unspecified amount to organizations that help sexual assault victims defend themselves. In closing arguments, Mueller's lawyer questioned witness credibility and pointed to a photo of the encounter, while Swift's lawyer cited Mueller's testimony that his supervisor said he placed his hands on Swift's bottom and his destruction of a recording of a conversation with his employers about the allegations.

Lawyer Angela B. Ryan recounts how, during three pregnancies totaling 27 months of working as an attorney, colleagues, judges, opposing counsel and others repeatedly touched her pregnant belly without consent in professional settings. She describes the reactions and laughter that normalized the conduct, saying it undermined her autonomy and was treated as workplace spectacle rather than harassment. Although pregnancy-discrimination law recognizes pregnancy-based harassment, Ryan says unwanted belly touching is rarely addressed in practice. She argues that it is also a professionalism and public-health concern, noting research on stress hormones and its effects on mothers and babies. Acknowledging her earlier judgments of pregnant colleagues, Ryan urges legal workplaces to adopt and enforce a clear standard: do not touch a pregnant person without explicit consent. She calls for changes through courthouse training, HR policies, harassment rules, judicial education and professional culture, emphasizing that consent does not end with conception.

The team believes recent games showed improvement in puck management, positioning, and chance creation despite low goal totals. Players express confidence—without becoming cocky—after two straight wins, citing a strong road playoff record and little concern about home-road advantage. They are focused on Thursday’s game, viewed as the most important, and believe the every-other-day schedule keeps them mentally engaged. A ten-day layoff hurt their timing and mood but not their conditioning, while travel and a possible home-crowd advantage should affect both teams similarly.

A goaltender described as outstanding throughout the playoffs has provided a major lift and raised team confidence. Both teams are considered defensively strong and comfortable with their matchups. The speaker expects little trouble from player shadowing and believes either side can score first, overcome a deficit, and succeed in overtime, where his team has felt fortunate and confident.
Pete Hegseth addressed hundreds of generals and admirals summoned worldwide, making the case for shaking up a force he described as soft and “woke.”

This passage is an extract from the SD Physical Layer Simplified Specification (Version 6.00) covering pre-erase, erase operations, write protection, card lock/unlock, and command structures.

**Pre-erase (ACMD23):** Setting a number of write blocks to be pre-erased before a Multiple Block Write (CMD25) makes that write faster. If the write is terminated early, remaining block contents are undefined; if more blocks are sent than declared, the card erases them one by one as data arrives. The count resets to 1 after the write. ACMD23 must be sent immediately before the WRITE command, otherwise it may be cleared by intervening commands. For pipeline-based hosts unable to identify the last successfully written block, the card answers ACMD22 with the number of well-written blocks.

**ERASE (CMD38), DISCARD and FULE:** Erase ranges are set with ERASE_WR_BLK_START (CMD32) and ERASE_WR_BLK_END (CMD33) followed by CMD38; out-of-sequence commands set ERASE_SEQ_ERROR or ERASE_RESET bits, and write-protected sectors are left intact with WP_ERASE_SKIP set. Address fields are byte-based write block addresses, with LSBs below WRITE_BL_LEN ignored. The card signals progress by holding DAT0 low; hosts may issue CMD7 to deselect. Post-erase data is '0' or '1' as defined by SCR bit 55 (DATA_STAT_AFTER_ERASE). DISCARD (CMD38 argument 00000001h) makes discarded content "don't care" and requires DISCARD_SUPPORT (b313); it is supported only on SDHC/SDXC, not SPI, with a 250 ms busy timeout, and pending discards are lost on power cycle. FULE (CMD38 argument 00000002h) logically erases the whole user area, requires FULE_SUPPORT (b312), is likewise SDHC/SDXC only, and has a 1 second busy timeout. If DISCARD or FULE is unsupported, ERASE is executed instead.

**Write protection and lock/unlock:** Three mechanisms exist: a mechanical write-protect switch (host responsibility), optional card-internal write protection (section blank), and password-based card lock. Passwords are stored in 128-bit PWD and 8-bit PWD_LEN registers, with optional 128-bit FEP/FEP_LEN for Card Ownership Protection (COP). Locked cards accept class 0 commands, ACMD41, CMD16 and the lock-card class; CMD42 is issued in transfer state and carries mode, password length and password data (password up to 16 bytes; old plus new password up to 32 bytes).

**COP:** COP prevents reuse of a card without knowing PWD. When FEP is set, Force Erase and Clear PWD are disabled and COP Unlock (CMD42[1Fh]) is required after power-up/reset; until then the card is COP-locked and returns CARD_IS_LOCKED and LOCK_UNLOCK_FAILED. COP Unlock moves the card to CMD42 Ver.2.0 mode, adding FEP management, Force Erase, and Reset PWD inhibit (PWD cannot be reset while FEP is set). Force Erase (CMD42[08h]) erases PWD, PWD_LEN and all memory and is rejected on an unlocked card; FEP Force Erase (CMD42[18h]) requires the correct FEP and leaves FEP intact. The secure area is not erased, lock state is kept during the erase, and write protection is cleared after the user area erase completes. Host guidance is not to issue force erase when Permanent Write Protect is set, to clear Temporary Write Protect afterward, and not to set FEP on a COP card locked with an unknown PWD.

**APP_CMD and switch function:** CMD55 makes the next command an ACMD; the APP_CMD bit indicates whether a defined ACMD was accepted, undefined ACMDs act as regular commands, and illegal commands produce an Illegal Command Error. ACMD41 is an exception, and several ACMD numbers are reserved for proprietary use. CMD6 (SWITCH_FUNCTION) supports six function groups with 16 branches each — Access Mode (bus speed), Command System, Driver Strength, Power Limit and others — with function 0 as default; mode 0 checks supported functions and mode 1 sets them, returning R1 plus a 512-bit status block on DAT with a 100 ms timeout and an 8-clock switching period. The status block carries per-group function selection, support bits and busy status; the Power Limit group defaults to 0.72 W and supports 1.44 W and 1.80 W settings.

**Other topics:** High-Speed mode raises the clock to 50 MHz for 25 MB/sec and allows only one card with 1-to-1 signal connections. CMD8 (Send Interface Condition) is issued in Idle state before ACMD41 to check host voltage support. SDSC cards use byte addressing and CMD16-set block lengths, while SDHC/SDXC use block addressing with a fixed 512-byte length regardless of CMD16, disable partial/misaligned access, and reject CMD28-30. CMD34-37, CMD50 and CMD57 are reserved for the command system. The host may pause or stop the bus clock, providing eight clock cycles after transactions and a clock edge to release the busy signal. CRC7 (x7+x3+1) protects commands, responses except R3, and CID/CSD; CRC16 (CCITT, x16+x12+x5+1) protects block payloads, with CRC16 of 0x7FA1 for 512 bytes of 0xFF. CRC failures and illegal commands leave card state unchanged and set COM_CRC_ERROR or ILLEGAL_COMMAND. Read timeouts are 100 ms or 100× TAAC/NSAC, write timeouts 250 ms (up to 500 ms for SDXC, 1 second for UHS-II data bursts), and erase timeouts come from SD Status parameters when supported. Commands are 48 bits with start bit, direction, 6-bit index, 32-bit argument, CRC and end bit; command classes are advertised via CCC in the CSD, with classes 0, 2, 4, 5 and 8 mandatory and class 7 (except CMD40) mandatory for SDHC/SDXC. Responses comprise R1, R1b, R2 (136-bit CID), and R3 (48-bit, no CRC).

Commander Chris Hadfield celebrated Christmas aboard the International Space Station in 2012, orbiting Earth while his crew slept. Acting as Santa, he hid cards written by astronauts’ families for the others to find. Holidays in orbit, with 16 sunrises every 92 minutes, required adaptations: dense fruitcake was velcroed to a table, while turkey, reconstituted potatoes, processed vegetables, an artificial tree, and personalized stockings were prepared. The American and Russian crew combined traditions from their cultures, treating holiday preparations as essential to mission success and psychological well-being. Hadfield viewed familiar customs as meaningful anchors for reflection on relationships and wellbeing, noting that even in space, customs can ground people.
Compared with V100, A100 offers 1.5x per-SM L1/shared-memory capacity, 40 GB HBM2 at 1555 GB/s, a 40 MB L2 cache with 2.3x read bandwidth, plus residency controls and compute data compression.
Polling began in 69 of Uttarakhand’s 70 assembly seats amid tight security involving nearly 30,000 personnel. Karnaprayag polling was rescheduled to March 9 after a candidate died in an accident.

In McGillivray v. Eramian, the Massachusetts Supreme Judicial Court held that a bowling-alley proprietor was negligent in maintaining an uneven, splintered approach that injured the plaintiff’s finger.
