The evidence did not establish contributory negligence because the plaintiff had not observed the protruding splinter and his hand position was not improper. The court affirmed the jury’s $750 verdict for the plaintiff and the denial of the defendant’s requested instructions.

Samsung announced three cheaper, water- and dust-resistant Galaxy A smartphones—the A3, A5 and A7—set to launch in Russia before expanding elsewhere. In its first unveiling since the Galaxy Note 7, Samsung introduced devices with 16-megapixel cameras, fingerprint sensors and Galaxy S-like designs.

Under regulations issued July 19, 1902, only the Secretary of State could grant and issue U.S. passports. Persons abroad applied to the appropriate U.S. diplomatic representative, consul-general, or consul; residents of U.S. insular possessions applied to the possession’s chief executive. Passports could not be issued to those who did not owe U.S. allegiance, including persons who had only declared their intention to become citizens.

Applicants in the United States submitted a sworn written application stating birth, occupation, permanent residence, and intention to return and perform citizenship duties, along with an oath of allegiance, a physical description, and proof from at least one credible witness. Persons born abroad to native citizens had to prove their fathers’ U.S. birth, residence, and citizenship. Naturalized citizens had to submit their naturalization record and provide emigration, residence, and identity details. Women had to state their marital status; spouses or widows of naturalized citizens had to produce the spouse’s certificate and related facts. Children claiming citizenship through a naturalized parent had to submit the parent’s certificate and details of the parent’s emigration, naturalization, and residence. Loyal residents of insular possessions had to declare U.S. allegiance and provide two credible witnesses supporting their birth, residence, and loyalty.

After the July 4 Kerr County flood killed 25 Camp Mystic campers, two counselors and the camp’s director, parents of the 27 girls who died organized to advocate for stronger camp safety laws. Matthew and Wendie Childress, whose daughter Chloe was a first-year counselor, joined other families, including Blake Bonner, whose 9-year-old daughter Lila attended camp for the first time.

The families met with Gov. Greg Abbott, legislative leaders and lawmakers, shared their stories and testified at hearings. Abbott called a special session focused on camp safety, and the House and Senate passed related bills. Laws signed Sept. 5 require overnight cabins to be moved out of floodplains, camps to use radios and alert systems to follow weather warnings, and staff to receive emergency-plan training, including where to move children to higher ground.

Childress said the advocacy gave him a way to channel his grief and honor his daughter, while Bonner said reforms could help prevent future losses. Lawmakers credited the parents’ emotional advocacy, but the passage of the bills did not end their pain: their daughters still could not return, and they faced a future of continuing to live with and remember them.

The excerpt details L4 Slow Peripheral memory-map regions, including regions decoded internally by the Cortex-A8 that are reserved for other masters. The DDR DMM TILER provides a 4-GB extended addressing range through a 33rd address bit for rotated and mirrored frame-buffer views; only HDVPSS and ISS can access the full range, while other masters can access one view through the base 512-MB TILER region. Terminal-function tables list signal names, multiplexing, pin numbers, types, pull states, supply sources, and functions. Boot-configuration pins are multiplexed between Cortex-A8 boot mode and GPMC functions, with BTMODE bits sampled at reset and the pins subsequently operating as GPMC_D[15:11].

China launched its first talent visa program to attract foreign professionals, especially young workers and graduates in science and technology from top universities, to study and do business in the country. The announcement came as the US imposed a $100,000 fee on H-1B visas, and it immediately triggered xenophobic backlash.

AI, particularly large language models (LLMs), could reshape social-science research by expanding access to web-scale data, synthesizing research datasets, and automating tasks such as stance detection, sentiment analysis, and free-text coding. Role-playing and interview-informed memory mechanisms may help models represent demographic preferences and behaviors, but synthesized data can contain bias, stereotypes, and questionable authenticity. Limited high-quality datasets and the cost of training and deploying models also restrict access. LLMs may generate hypotheses or social theories, although concerns about originality, validity, and falsifiability require human–AI collaboration that combines automated search with human interpretation and oversight.

Generative AI creates legal and ethical challenges, including misinformation, malicious deepfakes, bias, discrimination, and jailbreak-related safety failures. Although governments and technology companies have introduced laws, principles, and internal guidelines, regulation remains fragmented, communication between industry and policymakers is inconsistent, and countries have not reached consensus. The passage calls for forward-looking, human-centered regulation that balances innovation with fundamental rights, transparency, safety, security, and accountability. It recommends top-down cooperation among industry, academia, and policymakers alongside bottom-up participation by developers, researchers, users, and communities. Transparent reporting channels, rapid mechanisms for investigating emerging risks, and social-computing tools for monitoring community needs could help governance adapt as AI systems evolve.

This cross-sectional analysis of the COVID-PCD participatory cohort examined diagnostic testing among 747 people with primary ciliary dyskinesia from 49 countries. Most participants (92%) reported some diagnostic testing, but use varied substantially by country. Among participants aged five or older, 49% reported nasal nitric oxide measurement, while 75% of all participants reported biopsy analysis and 58% reported genetic testing. Of those reporting biopsy, 58% said samples were assessed by high-speed video microscopy and 50% by electron microscopy.

Participants’ recall of testing also varied. Eight percent could not recall whether biopsy occurred, compared with 18% for nasal nitric oxide; 38% and 47%, respectively, were unsure whether biopsy samples underwent high-speed video microscopy or electron microscopy. Recall was poorest in Switzerland.

Among participants aged five or older who underwent testing, 36% reported nasal nitric oxide measurement, biopsy, and genetic testing. These three tests were reported by 59% of German participants, 18% of Swiss participants, and 22% of Australian participants. Among children under five, 72% underwent biopsy and genetic testing.

Testing increased with more recent diagnosis. Compared with diagnoses before 2000, diagnoses after 2010 were associated with nasal nitric oxide measurement, biopsy, and genetic testing. Participants with situs abnormalities reported fewer tests than those with situs solitus. Testing also varied by country, while age at diagnosis was not associated with individual test use.

Self-reported data could not be verified against medical records, and recruitment through support groups may have introduced selection bias. The findings indicate incomplete diagnostic work-up in many countries and support reviewing previous results and considering additional testing, particularly for people diagnosed long ago or with situs abnormalities, to improve characterization for personalized treatment.

Judge Reed O’Connor rejected a challenge to the Biden-era gainful-employment rule and sided with the Education Department. The rule requires for-profit, nondegree programs to show that graduates can afford loan payments and earn more than high school graduates; programs failing for two consecutive years could lose federal aid. Trump officials defended the rule, while both opponents and advocates anticipate a future rulemaking process.

Prava Chatterjee sought to vacate a $87,000 settlement of her deceased son’s admiralty claim after her son-in-law allegedly forged a power of attorney, executed a release in India, and delivered no settlement proceeds to her. The district court excluded testimony from an earlier Calcutta commission, denied Chatterjee’s request for a new commission in India, and ruled that the shipowners had proved the release was valid.

On appeal, the Third Circuit held that federal maritime law governed the release and that the careful-scrutiny standard for seamen’s releases applied to settlements obtained from deceased seamen’s survivors. The shipowners therefore bore the burden of proving that the release was freely executed, without deception or coercion, and with full understanding of its terms, even if the alleged fraud was committed by others.

The court held that the power of attorney was a localized contract-and-agency issue governed by Indian law under Pennsylvania’s conflicts rules. Although Indian and Pennsylvania agency law were substantially similar, their fraud standards differed materially.

Although exclusion of the former commission testimony was permissible under the hearsay and cross-examination requirements, the unexplained denial of a new commission amounted to an abuse of discretion. Together, the evidentiary rulings created a procedural void that prevented Chatterjee from presenting evidence on forgery, authority, fraud, and ratification, depriving her of due process and a fair trial. The court vacated the denial of her petition and remanded the case with instructions to issue a commission under Rule 28(b) to take testimony in India.

Halliburton reported first-quarter net income of $46 million, or 5 cents per share. Adjusted earnings met expectations at 41 cents, while $5.74 billion in revenue missed forecasts; shares were up over 6% year to date.

U.S. international student arrivals in August were 19% lower than in August 2024, aligning with forecasts and institutional reports of reduced enrollment following visa interview freezes and delays. National Travel and Tourism Office data is considered more definitive, though it excludes some students. SEVIS data showed a conflicting 0.8% enrollment increase for September, but experts cited incomplete reporting, visa-status changes and timing issues.

Declines were especially steep among students from Iran, Syria, Haiti, Ghana, Nigeria and India, while arrivals from Europe and Oceania remained relatively flat. Experts said total enrollment declines could exceed 20%, with potential effects on university revenue, college-town economies and the broader economy. Better fall enrollment figures are expected in mid-November from the Institute of International Education’s Fall Snapshot report.

NAFTA has driven sustained economic growth and transformed Canadian manufacturing, making its modernization a federal priority. However, new free-trade agreements alone will not secure prosperity because most exports outside North America have stagnated since existing FTAs were signed. Canada needs a comprehensive five-part strategy: reform its costly and uncompetitive tax and regulatory environment; address non-tariff barriers that disadvantage Canadian exporters; prioritize trade partners with historical, cultural and legal ties; leverage integrated North American supply chains, which generate roughly 85% of Canada’s value-added exports; and consolidate export-support programs to help small and medium-sized manufacturers expand globally. Structural reforms should begin without waiting for NAFTA renegotiations to conclude.

A New Delhi court deferred to July 6 consideration of the ED chargesheet against Karti Chidambaram, Advantage Strategic Consulting and Chess Management Services in the Aircel-Maxis money-laundering case. The ED alleges the firms received payments linked to Maxis’s $800 million investment and that Karti helped secure FIPB clearance in 2006. Karti has interim arrest protection until July 10. Separately, a special court dropped charges against Dayanidhi Maran, Kalanithi Maran and others for lack of concrete evidence.

After returning from the Crimea Conference at Yalta, the speaker reports that the United States, Britain, and Soviet Union reached unanimous agreements on military strategy, Germany’s defeat and occupation, liberated Europe, Poland, and the structure of an international security organization. The conference’s aims were to defeat Germany quickly with minimal Allied losses and to lay foundations for lasting peace.

The Allied chiefs of staff coordinated plans for Germany’s final defeat. As American, British, and Soviet forces approached each other, they established closer tactical cooperation, daily exchanges of information, coordinated use of heavy bombers, and joint distribution of supplies and transportation. The Allies demanded Germany’s unconditional surrender, the destruction of Nazism and German militarism, complete disarmament, punishment of war criminals, and reparations in kind. Germany would be temporarily divided into occupation zones administered by Britain, Russia, France, and the United States, while unconditional surrender would not mean the enslavement or starvation of the German people.

The three powers also accepted joint responsibility for the political and economic problems of liberated territories and former Axis satellite states. They agreed to support representative interim governments, free elections, and reconstruction so those regions could become self-supporting. Poland was to receive a broader-based provisional government and eventually a freely elected government, with the long-term objective of creating a strong, independent, and prosperous nation. Its eastern boundaries were settled as a compromise involving territorial compensation from the west. Yugoslavia was also addressed, and France was invited to join the postwar control of Germany, the international security organization, and joint responsibility for liberated Europe.

The conference also resolved the remaining issue over voting in the Security Council, though the terms were not yet public. A United Nations conference was scheduled for San Francisco on April 25, 1945, to draft a charter for preserving international peace. The speaker sought Senate approval and presented the American delegation as bipartisan, arguing that world peace was not a party issue.

The speaker emphasized that defeating Germany would not end the Pacific war and that Japan’s unconditional surrender and the eradication of Japanese militarism remained essential. Concluding that the Yalta agreements marked a turning point, the speaker urged Congress and the American people to support a universal organization replacing unilateral action, exclusive alliances, spheres of influence, and balances of power, arguing that lasting peace would require continuing cooperation, planning, and sacrifice.

A team representative was unsure whether a player would play the next day, citing no clear fatigue or discouragement factor. He praised the team’s home and road successes, said venue had not greatly affected it, but noted that home distractions may have affected key players early in the previous game.

Pokémon GO's Solstice Event, live for just over a day, offers three times XP for catches and for nice, great and excellent throws, curveballs and first throws; combined with a discounted Lucky Egg, catch-related actions yield six times XP. The throw bonuses make accurate targeting genuinely satisfying, though no extra XP applies to evolving, discouraging mindless Pokédex grinding. The event helps casual and midcore players level up ahead of upcoming gym changes, though Stardust remains scarce, and the winter/summer solstice theme suits the game's worldwide character.

Theresa May faces mounting Conservative pressure over Brexit ahead of Friday’s Chequers cabinet meeting. Andrea Jenkyns warned that failing to deliver Brexit—or accepting a “soft Brexit” that keeps Britain closely aligned with EU rules—would be “catastrophic” for the party, while Jacob Rees-Mogg urged May to stand firm on leaving the single market and customs union. Remain-supporting MPs favor pragmatism to avoid business, port and Northern Ireland border disruption. Michael Gove said May has a clear plan, that ministers would unite behind Brexit, and denied resignations were likely.

After nearly a decade of strong gains, the S&P 500 had nearly quadrupled from its post-crisis lows, but the author argues that changing monetary policy and rising volatility foreshadow a more challenging market environment. Although the index has not suffered a sustained break below its 200-day moving average, it went more than 60 trading days without setting a new high. Meanwhile, the Federal Reserve had begun raising rates and shrinking its balance sheet, unlike its response to earlier post-crisis volatility. Other major central banks were pursuing divergent policies, with China modestly reducing its balance sheet while stimulus continued elsewhere. Strong corporate earnings, aided by tax cuts, were largely being directed toward dividends and buybacks rather than capital expenditures.

Market volatility rose sharply in early 2018, briefly eliminating strategies that profited from persistently low volatility. The VIX quickly retreated from its February spike but remained above 15 and repeatedly reached the high 20s, unlike earlier post-crisis periods when volatility usually subsided quickly. The author compares this pattern with 2006–07, arguing that sustained higher volatility could indicate a market top even if the S&P 500 later reached new highs. He also expects any future bear market to be slow, prolonged, and unforgiving, with policymakers potentially prolonging the correction despite having limited tools to reverse it.

The contrast with 2017 was substantial. In 2017, the market moved more than 1% in either direction on only eight of 251 trading days. By early 2018, it had done so on 31 of 79 days, including eight moves exceeding 2%, seven of them downward. At that pace, 2018 was on track to rank as the seventh-most volatile year since World War II based on 1% moves and the fourth based on 2% moves.

The author also reviews earlier unusually calm periods. The low volatility of 1944 was followed by a market peak and a three-year bear market in which nominal losses exceeded 25% and inflation-adjusted losses reached 42%. Similarly subdued volatility in 1963–65 preceded a nearly two-decade, 62% inflation-adjusted decline beginning in 1966.

Overall, the author expects volatility to persist or intensify through 2018 and 2019 and potentially help form a top in the long-running bull market. He contends that policy-supported markets consistently rising are distorted and vulnerable to severe price corrections. Because bear markets are typically triggered by risks that become visible only after they are underway, strong earnings and economic forecasts—also present before the 2000 and 2007 declines—may offer false reassurance. Investors are advised to identify dangers not yet recognized by the broader market, where the author believes potential opportunities may lie.

The article explains Jack Bogle’s strategy of using low-cost index funds to invest in broad stock and bond markets rather than selecting individual securities. The Bogleheads 3 Fund Portfolio combines U.S. total-stock, international-stock, and U.S. total-bond index funds, while the Bogleheads 4 Fund Portfolio adds an international-bond fund for broader global diversification.

The article allocates 50% to U.S. stocks, 30% to international stocks, and 20% to U.S. bonds for the 3 Fund Portfolio, citing VTI, VEU, and BND as possible funds. Its allocation is 50% U.S. stocks, 30% international stocks, 10% U.S. bonds, and 10% international bonds for the 4 Fund Portfolio, citing VTI, VEU, BND, and IXUS. Both strategies emphasize diversification, low costs, regular contributions, long-term holding, and periodic rebalancing.

Backtests using those allocations produced annual returns of 7.6% for the 3 Fund Portfolio, with reinvested dividends and a 28% maximum drawdown, and 7.8% for the 4 Fund Portfolio with a 31% maximum drawdown. Market volatility can reduce stock values, while rising interest rates can lower bond prices. Portfolio selection should consider goals, time horizon, risk tolerance, allocation, expenses, and historical performance.

Guyana approved hosting the CWWA’s 26th annual conference, scheduled for October 16–20 at the Guyana Marriott Hotel. Focusing on water, wastewater and waste management, the ministerial forum is expected to attract over 250 delegates and 40 exhibitors.

The address launches a nationwide appeal for voluntary unemployment relief as winter approaches, amid deepening economic hardship. A national organization under Walter Gifford will coordinate with state and local agencies and business, labor, welfare, religious, fraternal, and patriotic groups to support community fundraising. Thousands of towns and cities already have relief committees, community chests, or similar organizations. Funds will provide work, direct assistance, and health and character-building services.

Federal, state, and local governments are expanding public works and relief programs, providing livelihoods for nearly 700,000 families through federal public works, while measures to support credit and employment have been adopted and immigration has been stopped. Despite these efforts, voluntary aid remains necessary to prevent hunger and cold.

The appeal emphasizes individual responsibility, neighbor-to-neighbor assistance, and self-help as foundations of democracy. Americans are asked to make November 26 an exceptional Thanksgiving by ensuring that no deserving citizens suffer. It concludes by invoking the nation’s endurance from Valley Forge to Yorktown.

LG introduced the V35 ThinQ, a premium smartphone with a Snapdragon 845 processor, 6GB RAM, 6-inch OLED display, dual 16MP rear cameras, and 8MP front camera. It features AI-assisted photography, Google Lens, far-field Google Assistant, Hi-Fi audio, IP68 resistance, and a headphone jack. Pricing and release details remain unannounced.

**Summary**

Drug repurposing (repositioning/reprofiling) identifies new therapeutic uses for existing drugs, reducing development time and cost; it accounts for roughly one-third of all drug approvals and about 25% of pharmaceutical sector revenue. Cited examples include thalidomide (originally an anti-nausea drug, later used for leprosy and several cancers), sildenafil (developed for angina, later used for pulmonary hypertension and impotence), and rituximab (cancers, under investigation for rare autoimmune diseases). Repurposing is particularly significant for rare diseases, where treatment options are limited and new drug development is difficult due to small patient populations; it can also bypass early development stages such as safety testing. Knowledge graphs represent entities (drugs, genes, diseases) as nodes and relations as edges, and machine-learning embeddings of knowledge graphs are a popular method for predicting new drug–disease connections.

The preprint defines an observation (fact) as a causative, physical-interaction, or correlational relation between biomedical concepts reported by a scientific article; an uncited observation as one supported by a single reference; a statement as a text snippet describing an observation; and an assertion as an NLP-captured statement supporting an observation.

**Methods.** Elsevier's Biology Knowledge Graph (EBKG) is built with proprietary AI NLP from both open access (OA) and controlled access (CA) sources, plus PubMed abstracts (34.5 million OA documents, 14,224 journals), Elsevier full-text articles (5 million), third-party full-text articles (2.2 million), and clinical trials (0.43 million). In 2023 it contained 335,991 objects of 15 concept types and 15,860,468 relations of 17 types (including regulation 6,575,095, functional association 2,529,912, binding 1,172,377). The technology uses named entity recognition, supervised learning, and pre-trained language models over abstracts and full texts, plus entity grounding to external identifiers (NCBI Gene, PubChem); relations are annotated with supporting sentences and article identifiers, and were labeled OA if at least one supporting reference was OA, otherwise CA. For drug repurposing the authors selected all relations for 9,302 rare diseases (1,025,840) and all drug–target relations (68,850 direct, 701,218 indirect).

**Results.** OA and CA contributed roughly equally at the relation level (8,456,366 vs 7,988,632), although 1.5 times more NLP statements were asserted from CA (45,059,137 vs 29,567,668). OA contribution grew significantly after 2006, and more than 50% of relations needed for rare-disease drug repurposing are now in OA. Rare diseases with more than 100 relations tend to have more than 50% of relations in OA; no comparable bias appeared for drug–target relations. Essentially all relations with four or more references are OA, while about 40% of single-reference relations are OA. CA-only facts grew every year but more slowly than OA, so CA's relative fraction declined. There was no difference in citation rate or time to first citation between OA and CA content.

**Uncited relations.** About half of all EBKG relations are supported by a single reference, and these accumulate almost exponentially in both OA and CA corpora; 85% of uncited relations came from peer-reviewed literature. Roughly 10% of NLP relations are false positives, mainly from long sentences listing multiple relations. Other causes are hypothetical statements in discussions or reviews, whose refutation goes unreported, and true findings never followed up. Articles with uncited relations showed higher assertions-to-relations ratios than the graph average, indicating most uncited relations come from original research without follow-up. Of ~27,000 retracted PubMed articles, only 8,562 (31.7%) were OA.

**Discussion and conclusion.** The OA movement emerged around 2000 with non-profit publishers (PLoS, BioMed Central) and the 2001 Budapest Open Access Initiative; Elsevier uses gold and green OA models. The authors propose additional relation-confidence criteria beyond reference counts (epistemic discourse analysis, article citation index, a statistical alignment score with the whole graph, and distinguishing self-citations from independent observations), six credibility tiers from highly cited observations to internet and LLM-generated content, and training LLMs on different literature subsets to assist peer review. Conclusions: citation rates of CA and OA facts do not differ; half of all relations rest on a single reference, equally distributed between CA and OA; and additional confidence scores are needed to estimate relation confidence.

The instructor outlines course plans: a short problem set is due the following Tuesday, while the first quiz, one week from Thursday, will cover statistical basics through statistical process control and control charting. The quiz is closed book, but students may bring one side of a page of notes and a calculator; statistical tables will be provided. Yield modeling will be addressed in the next lecture and excluded from the quiz.

Control charts are presented as repeated hypothesis tests in which each new sample is checked for evidence that the process has shifted from its nominal distribution. Under the null hypothesis, a Gaussian process is assumed. Alpha, the false-alarm probability, determines the upper and lower control limits; for example, three-sigma limits place alpha/2 in each tail. Average run length under the null hypothesis is the reciprocal of the false-alarm probability. When the process has shifted, beta represents the probability of missing the shift, power is \(1-\beta\), and the average run length for detecting a real shift is \(1/(1-\beta)\).

Increasing sample size reduces beta by narrowing the sampling distributions while maintaining the same alpha; the control limits are adjusted accordingly to preserve the false-alarm rate. Operating-characteristic curves relate sample size, shift size, and beta, although determining the required sample size generally requires iterative calculation. Widening control limits reduces false alarms but also sensitivity. Sampling frequency provides another degree of freedom because larger samples or more frequent sampling can delay detection in clock time.

A control-chart alarm alone cannot establish whether it is false or genuine. When an alarm occurs, investigators should verify the measurement equipment, examine historical data for additional patterns or drift, and check the process, equipment, operators, feedstock, and other potential sources of variation. Requiring two consecutive out-of-limit points is one way to demand stronger evidence. Control limits serve statistical detection and should not be confused with specification limits, which define acceptable product characteristics and remain unchanged by sample-size adjustments.

Process capability compares an in-control process’s spread and centering with specification limits. CP is the specification width divided by six process standard deviations, so it measures spread without penalizing an off-target mean. CPK also incorporates the mean’s position by using the smaller distance from the mean to a specification limit divided by three standard deviations. Larger values are generally preferable, though their suitability depends on the process and costs. A centered process with six sigma of spread between specification limits has CP and CPK of 1. The same spread with the mean at one specification limit has CPK 0. Halving the spread produces CP 2; with the mean offset by three sigma, CPK is 1, and recentering raises CPK to 2.

Approximate nonconformance rates illustrate these indices: CPK 1 corresponds to roughly three defects per thousand; CPK 1.33 corresponds to about four sigma and approximately a hundredfold reduction; CPK 1.67 and 2 provide successive hundredfold reductions, with CPK 2 associated with roughly one or two defects per billion. Such capability also provides robustness against shifts; for example, a two-sigma shift under a centered process with CP and CPK 2 was described as producing about 31–32 nonconforming parts per million.

A quadratic quality-loss function penalizes squared deviations from a target. Minimizing expected loss requires centering the process mean and reducing its variance. Expected loss can be decomposed into contributions from variance and mistargeting. Tail probabilities from the process distribution can also estimate nonconforming-part fractions and support comparisons between the benefits of recentering and reducing variation.

With many simultaneous control charts, individual false-alarm rates can create excessive aggregate alarms, requiring wider limits or other adjustments. Multiple process steps may also have dependent deviations, so quality does not necessarily combine additively. Statistical monitoring should emphasize measurements most relevant to product requirements.

The lecture then previews alternatives to conventional \(\bar{x}\) and range charts for using every-part inspection, improving response speed, and detecting subtle changes. These include moving-average charts, exponentially weighted moving averages, and cumulative sum charts for detecting small shifts or drift. Correlation and sampling intervals must be considered when individual observations are temporally dependent.

Managed by Q, founded by Dan Teran and Saman Rahmanian, launched an on-demand office cleaning and maintenance service in New York in April 2014. The founders envisioned a technology-enabled company that would manage customers’ physical-space needs through cleaning, maintenance, and office supplies. They targeted office managers because they had purchasing authority and wanted fewer vendors and less logistical complexity. By late July 2015, Q had raised $15 million in Series A funding, expanded into Chicago and San Francisco, and achieved high customer satisfaction and retention above 90%.

Q served companies occupying 6,000–20,000 square feet in Class B and C buildings. Cleaning operators performed office, kitchen, conference-room, and workstation cleaning, floor care, trash removal, and supply restocking. Helpers and handymen handled maintenance ranging from furniture assembly and light bulbs to painting, carpentry, plumbing, and electrical work. Customers received a wall-mounted iPad with a customized dashboard showing requested tasks, photos, cleaner attendance, completed work, messages, and feedback. The platform also supported maintenance requests, supply orders, and referrals to third-party vendors. The fragmented $51 billion janitorial-services industry, in which 96% of firms had fewer than five employees, presented substantial opportunity.

Q initially subcontracted cleaning workers but shifted to directly employed “operators” after three months because inconsistent subcontractor performance undermined service quality. Unlike many on-demand competitors, Q paid above-standard wages, trained workers, provided benefits and stable schedules, and offered career paths from operator to mentor or supervisor. By late July 2015, it employed 247 field operators across its three cities. Cleaning operators earned $12.50 per hour, while helpers and handymen earned $20 and $40–$45 per hour. Full-time staff received health insurance, vacation, a 401(k), and workers’ compensation, and Q planned performance-based bonuses.

Hiring combined online applications, an information session, a personal interview, and role-specific assessment. Cleaning candidates then completed introductory instruction, two practical cleaning sessions with a mentor, two or three supervised deep cleans, and a policy quiz. Trainees received less than the regular operator wage. Cleaning operators were assigned recurring accounts and used iPads and apps to record tasks, communicate with customers and headquarters, and identify maintenance or supply needs. Maintenance personnel received on-site support from experienced colleagues.

Q emphasized quality, transparency, technology, communication, and community. Customers continuously rated operators and could request additional work, while operators reported problems and suggested improvements. Headquartered employees and managers also performed deep cleans to understand field work. Regular citywide town halls allowed operators to question leadership, seek updates, and recognize top performers. Headquarter functions set companywide compensation, policies, procedures, and customer-acquisition strategies, while city managers handled daily operations. A centralized digital repository called Q Knowledge documented standardized and location-specific processes.

By July 2015, Q served 228 New York accounts, 25 in Chicago, and 28 in San Francisco. Cleaning represented about 70% of typical customer spending, with maintenance and supplies providing the remainder; maintenance had the highest gross margin. Management was weighing geographic expansion, including planned entry into Boston, Atlanta, and Washington, D.C., against deeper growth in existing markets through additional services and a broader third-party vendor platform. Although investors viewed the platform as potentially scalable and high-margin, Teran recognized that expansion would require recruiting and training a substantial workforce. He intended to pursue growth without compromising Q’s employee-centered model, service quality, or culture.

Lawmakers planned to use President Donald Trump’s first State of the Union address to emphasize various issues. Female Democrats were to wear black in support of the #MeToo movement, and Rep. Annie Kuster invited sexual-assault survivor Chessy Prout. Dozens of young immigrants protected under DACA were invited to the House gallery, while Republican Rep. Kevin Cramer invited a border-wall contractor. At least eight Democratic representatives planned to boycott. Bill Nye, invited by NASA nominee Jim Bridenstine, urged Trump to present an ambitious, science-driven space agenda. Rep. Joe Kennedy of Massachusetts was chosen to deliver the Democratic response and was presented as a champion of middle-class policies.
Iraq began bombing Islamic State-held Tal Afar and planned a ground assault after the air campaign, following the recapture of Mosul and the collapse of Islamic State’s self-proclaimed caliphate.

Sarahah is a free Android and iOS app for anonymous messaging. Users create profiles that visitors can message without logging in, while senders may optionally identify themselves. Recipients can flag, delete, reply to, or favorite messages. The app has rapidly gained visibility and popularity in places including Egypt and Saudi Arabia. Its reception is nearly evenly divided between five- and one-star Google Play ratings. Developers say it supports self-development through anonymous feedback, but users report hateful comments and potential bullying. Privacy features include hiding profiles, restricting comments to logged-in users, and blocking senders. Its interface is barebones, and its long-term popularity remains uncertain.

The passage lists telegrams and related records dated January 8 through September 3, 1942, with reference numbers, locations, dispatch times, and often receipt times. Most originate in Washington or Helsinki, with others from Kuibyshev (Moscow), Stockholm, London, and Ankara.

The PGA848 is a monolithic, high-voltage, high-bandwidth programmable-gain instrumentation amplifier with a single-ended output. It combines a high-speed current-feedback input stage, an internally matched gain resistor network, and a differential output stage. Three digital gain-select pins provide eight gain settings from 0.5 V/V to 100 V/V. Its linear input range extends to within 3 V of either supply while maintaining common-mode rejection, and it is intended for factory automation, data acquisition, test and measurement, analog input modules, and semiconductor test.

A typical application drives a 16-bit, 1 MSPS ADS8860 SAR ADC. The PGA848 accepts single-ended or differential inputs and uses ±15 V input-stage and 5.3 V output-stage supplies. A REF6250 supplies the ADC’s 5 V reference, while a precision divider and buffered OPA192 set the PGA848 REF pin to 2.5 V for ADC midscale operation. The reference buffer uses dual feedback and an isolation resistor for stability, providing 86° phase margin.

Three filters suppress EMI/RFI, shape bandwidth, and provide charge kickback compensation for the ADC. A 75 pF feedback capacitor with the PGA’s 6.67 kΩ feedback resistors gives a nominal cutoff of 318 kHz, or 277 kHz at the high resistor-tolerance limit. The circuit maintains −0.1 dB flatness to 41 kHz, and C0G capacitors are used throughout the signal path.

Nominal performance is specified with ±15 V input and output supplies and VICM and VREF at mid-supply. Output-stage supplies must remain within input-stage supply levels, and supplies above ±20 V can permanently damage the device.

Recommended layout practices include symmetric input paths, local low-ESR bypass capacitors, separation of sensitive input traces from supply and output traces, and minimizing leakage, parasitic capacitance, thermal junctions, and thermal-source proximity. PSpice for TI and TINA-TI are presented as simulation resources. Additional sections cover related documentation, support, ESD precautions, revision history, and ordering information.

Pure tungsten oxidation in synthetic air was investigated from 400–1050°C, alongside WO₃ sublimation from 750–1100°C, using thermogravimetric analysis, differential scanning calorimetry, XRD, Raman spectroscopy, SEM, and EBSD. Oxidation initially followed parabolic kinetics, consistent with diffusion control, before transitioning to linear growth. Arrhenius activation energies were 180.4 ± 3.8 kJ/mol for the parabolic regime and 117.5 ± 3.3 kJ/mol for the linear regime. Edge effects were negligible during parabolic growth but became significant during linear oxidation, with oxidation rate increasing with the specimen perimeter-to-area ratio. Above 600°C, the scale developed voids, cracks, delamination, and brittle edge regions that readily spalled, creating potential dust hazards during fusion-device maintenance, accidents, and waste handling.

WO₃ sublimation increased monotonically with temperature, reached a steady rate after approximately one hour, and exhibited zero-order, surface-reaction-controlled kinetics. Its activation energy was 335.8 ± 17 kJ/mol.

Raman and XRD characterization showed a multilayer oxide scale: an inner WO₂ layer approximately 30–50 nm thick, a dense 10–20 µm WO₂.₇₂ layer, and an outer region containing WO₂.₉ and WO₃. XRD could distinguish WO₂ and WO₂.₇₂ but not WO₂.₉ from WO₃, whereas Raman spectroscopy distinguished the outer phases. SEM revealed a cracked, relatively dense outer layer, aligned voids in the middle region, and small cavities near the tungsten–oxide interface. The dense WO₂.₇₂ layer was linked to parabolic diffusion control; later void and crack formation was associated with variability in linear-regime growth.

Cracking was related to oxide expansion, thermal-expansion mismatch, phase and thickness variations, and grain-orientation-dependent oxidation differences. Because WO₂ may act as a tritium-permeation barrier, its formation could contribute to the low detritiation efficiency previously observed in JET tungsten components.

Missouri detective Wissbaum inhaled fentanyl-mixed heroin while reviving an overdose victim with Narcan. He developed a headache, light-headedness, and tingling hands. Both were hospitalized and are okay; police say the combination endangers first responders.

Joseph Nicholson, who stabbed Joey Tanner, 16, three times in the back in June 2007, killing him and nearly killing 17-year-old Jeremy Rodgers, will be eligible for parole earlier after the Ontario Court of Appeal overturned his first-degree murder conviction because of inadequate jury instructions. He will be resentenced for second-degree murder, carrying life imprisonment and 10 to 25 years without parole; Crown attorney Ray Williams seeks 16 years. At the hearing, Tanner’s parents described their continuing grief, while Nicholson apologized and asked to rehabilitate. The attack followed a confrontation outside a Barrie apartment, where teenagers were drinking and using cocaine and expected a fistfight, but Nicholson used a flick knife, causing fatal internal injuries. The Crown cited Nicholson’s violent criminal record and prison misconduct. Justice Guy DiTomaso will impose the sentence Aug. 11.

Katie Albert, a Waterloo High School graduate studying psychology with a studio art minor at Southern Illinois University Edwardsville, describes the second half of her semester studying abroad in Florence, Italy. Italian class is progressing, and she continues to enjoy painting and drawing classes, having completed five paintings and numerous drawings using watercolor, charcoal, graphite, and conte crayon. She also participated in a cooking class and attended school-sponsored day trips to Siena, Pisa, and Lucca. Over spring break she visited seven countries in ten days, touring Copenhagen, Amsterdam, Brussels, Luxembourg, Metz, and Kaiserslautern, where she visited the village of Becherbach, her fourth-great-grandfather Abraham Maurer's birthplace. She finished in Switzerland, spending a day in Adelboden and tandem paragliding between Geneva and the French border. Back in Florence, she found the tourist season beginning, then took a trip to Split, Croatia, for white water rafting and cliff diving, a cruise to Brač, and a visit to Krka National Park, reaching a milestone of 20 countries by age 20. With three weeks left, she faces final exams, apartment inspections, souvenir shopping, and mixed feelings about leaving Florence.

From July 2, Australia’s childcare subsidies will be combined into a single means- and activity-tested payment, replacing the Child Care Rebate and means-tested Child Care Benefit. Of about 1.2 million eligible families, an estimated 489,000 could miss funding unless they update their Centrelink details through myGov with 2018–19 income estimates and both parents’ activity hours. Both parents generally must work, study, volunteer or seek work at least eight hours per fortnight, with subsidised care ranging from 36 to 100 hours per fortnight. Payments vary by income, generally covering 85% of fees for families earning $66,958 or less and tapering to 50% and 20% at higher income levels; families earning over $351,248 receive no subsidy. Households earning under $186,958 have no annual cap, while the cap for higher-income families rises from $7,500 to just over $10,000 per child. Exemptions and additional subsidies apply in certain circumstances. Children must meet immunisation requirements or have a valid recorded exemption. The $1.2 billion package includes a safety net and is estimated to encourage more than 230,000 families to increase workforce involvement.

Jeffing is a 1970s run-walk method created by Olympian Jeff Galloway. It alternates running with planned walking breaks, making exercise more manageable. Dr John Gallucci Jr says it can reduce exhaustion and overuse stress, aid muscle recovery and aerobic endurance, and help beginners build confidence and consistency. Beginners might run and walk for 1–2 minutes each, then gradually lengthen running intervals while keeping recovery breaks and progressing slowly. Experienced runners can use it during long runs and recovery weeks to reduce fatigue and injury risk. It may suit long-distance runners and varied lifestyles, but not sports requiring continuous high-intensity effort. Poor progression or mechanics can still cause injuries.

This survey examines algebraic, geometric, and combinatorial invariants of matroids and complex hyperplane arrangements, emphasizing how these invariants depend on the matroid itself versus its realizability. It begins with matroid fundamentals, including bases, circuits, flats, geometric lattices, the Möbius function, localization, direct sums, and realizability, then introduces weak multinets, multinets, reduced multinets, and nets. Multinets encode partitions of a matroid’s ground set with prescribed multiplicities and rank-two base loci. Nets are linked to Latin squares and, in complex projective planes, to realizations of finite groups. Open questions concern extending a Riemann–Hurwitz-type inequality to nonrealizable matroids and determining whether every 3-net in \(\mathbb{CP}^2\) is algebraic.

The Orlik–Solomon algebra \(A(M)\) is the quotient of an exterior algebra by circuit relations. Its graded ranks are the matroid’s Betti numbers and are determined by the Möbius function of its lattice of flats. For realizable matroids, \(A(M)\) is isomorphic to the integral cohomology ring of the hyperplane-arrangement complement. Its quadraticity and quadratic Gröbner-basis properties are related to supersolvability.

The holonomy Lie algebra \(h(M)\) is defined by quadratic relations dual to multiplication in \(A(M)\). For realizable matroids, its graded ranks correspond to lower-central-series ranks of the complement’s fundamental group, although torsion can occur in positive characteristic. Its metabelian quotient \(h(M)/h(M)''\), called the holonomy Chen Lie algebra, has graded ranks matching the group’s Chen ranks. The Chen-rank conjecture is reformulated in terms of multinets on submatroids.

Resonance varieties are defined as jump loci of Aomoto-complex cohomology and encode dependencies among circuits and flats. In degree one, their components correspond to multinets on submatroids. Koszul modules \(W^q(M,k)\) are homological modules over a symmetric algebra, and their supports are closely related to resonance varieties; in degree one, \(W^1(M,k)\) equals the infinitesimal Alexander invariant and has a Hilbert series determined by the Chen ranks.

The survey also highlights unresolved issues, including the linearity of higher-degree resonance varieties for nonrealizable matroids and whether torsion in holonomy Lie algebras or the structure of Koszul modules can distinguish realizable from nonrealizable matroids.

The last trading day of the month is a weak day for stocks, distinct from the last calendar day when weekends or holidays intervene. From 1993 to July 2021, buying SPY at the close of the second-to-last trading day and selling at month-end close averaged a 0.06% loss per trade and a negative 0.8% annual CAGR, versus the market’s average daily gain of 0.04%. The overnight return from the second-to-last close to the last day’s open averaged 0.04%, but the final day’s open-to-close return averaged negative 0.11%, with a 42% win rate and notable left-tail losses. The passage attributes the weakness speculatively to profit-taking and presents the pattern as a possible seasonal trading opportunity.

Sharon Haliwell, 48, died by suicide at her Wigan home after addiction to sleeping pills and abuse by her husband. Although two mental health assessments found her at risk of suicide, she was not referred for counselling because of an error, and poor communication between North West Boroughs NHS teams was identified. Reforms included improved information-sharing, staff training and updated procedures for contacting relevant clinicians.

The speaker says fatigue is pushed aside during a race to four, with adrenaline taking over, and notes his team has rebounded with strong performances despite not yet winning a game. He credits veteran players, established chemistry, and contributions from newer players. The Sykora-Elias-Arnott line has clicked for over a year, while the team aims to shut down skilled opponents physically. Despite scoring no goals, Joe is playing effectively and dominating the offensive zone.

Anna Ryder Richardson is leaving Manor House Wildlife Park near Tenby for France and divorcing Colin MacDougall after 16 years. She blames the zoo’s financial pressures, workload and loss of privacy for their marriage breakdown. The couple bought the rundown park for £1 million in 2008 and spent seven months renovating it, including investing another £1 million in animal enclosures. They lived in a wooden cabin for four years while their animals occupied heated buildings, and struggled to meet annual costs of about £600,000.

Their wildlife park and family life were featured in Channel 4’s *Chaos at the Zoo*, while Anna had previously presented *Changing Rooms*. She acknowledges that buying the zoo against Colin’s wishes was naive and that constant television exposure affected them and their daughters.

In August 2010, a tree fell in the park, seriously injuring visitor Gruff Davies-Hughes and his mother. The family faced more than £100,000 in fines and costs; the case against Anna was dropped after Colin pleaded guilty. Although the park became a popular conservation attraction, Anna believes the incident further damaged their relationship.

Now 53, Anna plans to renovate a ruined farmhouse on six acres near Bordeaux and live there with daughters Bibi and Dixie. She is learning French and hopes to pursue cooking and gardening. Colin will manage the zoo. Anna is also returning to television as co-presenter of *60 Minute Makeover* with Peter Andre.

Born with a murmur that caused a slow heart rate and low energy, Tiffany Gholston received a pacemaker at 20. She stays active, eats well, and meditates while supporting the American Heart Association’s Go Red For Women campaign and raising funds for research she says saved her life.

Hackers released more unaired HBO episodes, including "Curb Your Enthusiasm," "Insecure," "Ballers" and "The Deuce," but no "Game of Thrones" material. HBO, which acknowledged the summer hack and a multi-million-dollar ransom demand, said it would not engage with the hacker.

The 74 shares education news, commentary, documentaries, youth profiles, and requests for donations and newsletter subscriptions. Coverage includes a west Texas girls’ camp reopening after deadly July floods, teens offering normalcy during Los Angeles fires, and Mississippi teacher Jamal Roberts winning American Idol. Other headlines address NYC school meals, youth vaping, COVID-19 vaccines, school funding and accountability, college access, and integration efforts. Civil-rights retrospectives examine Delaware’s first day of integration and student-led school strikes, while profiles spotlight women in STEM, school innovators, and first-generation students. Additional features cover pandemic recovery, music education, Juneteenth, parenting, and a national spelling bee winner.

Motley Fool Money’s Oct. 15, 2025 credit-card roundup highlights three offers. The Wells Fargo Active Cash Card offers unlimited 2% cash back, a $200 bonus after $500 in purchases within three months, and 12 months of 0% intro APR on purchases and qualifying balance transfers. It has no annual fee, Visa Signature concierge service, and up to $600 in cell-phone protection with a $25 deductible. The Capital One Quicksilver Cash Rewards Credit Card provides unlimited 1.5% cash back, 5% back on travel bookings through Capital One Travel, a $100 travel credit plus a $200 cash bonus, no annual or foreign-transaction fees, and 15 months of 0% intro APR. A Citi offer provides 2% back on purchases when the minimum due is paid on time, 5% back on certain Citi Travel bookings, and $200 back after $1,500 spent in six months; its 18-month 0% rate applies only to balance transfers, which do not earn rewards. Applicants are recommended to have good or excellent credit, though approval is not guaranteed. The passage discloses that compensated partnerships may affect offer placement but do not influence product ratings, and that Motley Fool maintains editorial independence.

Einstein researchers found that appetite-suppressing POMC neurons in the hypothalamus’s arcuate nucleus contain heat- and capsaicin-sensitive TRPV1-like receptors. Activating these receptors reduced food intake in mice, while blocking or silencing them prevented this effect. Exercise raised body and arcuate nucleus temperatures and cut food intake by about 50 percent, but mice lacking the receptors showed no exercise-related reduction.

Per curiam, the Texas Supreme Court denied Anna Black's writ of error in her Health Spa Act surety suit against the Texas Department of Labor and Standards. The Court noted its denial neither approves the appeals court's witnesses/documents distinction nor relieves parties of showing good cause in the record under Rule 215.5.

Researchers from the Harvard-Smithsonian Centre for Astrophysics and Tel Aviv University propose a global network of mobile phones and low-cost radio receivers to detect fast radio bursts originating within the Milky Way. An app could continuously record candidate signals and upload them to a central service for correlation. GPS arrival times could locate a burst, while dispersion measures could estimate its Galactic distance. Researchers estimate a Galactic FRB may occur every 30–1,500 years, though a repeating source like FRB 121102 could emit weekly. FRB 121102, the only repeating FRB detected so far, has produced 16 bursts traced to a galaxy three billion light-years away, but its cause remains unknown.

McLaren says factory work has resolved reliability problems from Barcelona testing, including wheel nut, battery, exhaust and overheating issues. Ahead of the Australian opener, Eric Boullier and Fernando Alonso expressed confidence in the Renault-powered MCL33’s potential while acknowledging further work is needed in a tightly contested midfield.

The patent discloses systems and methods for adaptive radiotherapy that use biological, physiological, or anatomical data extracted from imaging acquired at or during treatment to update treatment plans and radiation delivery. Imaging modalities include PET, MRI, SPECT, X-ray, CT, ultrasound, and magnetic particle imaging. Data may include tracer uptake, SUV, tracer kinetics, metabolism, oxygenation, gene expression, blood flow, vascularity, tumor morphology, and lymphatic activity. A controller evaluates plan deliverability using current imaging data, dose-volume histograms, plan quality indices, dose distributions, and clinician-approved ranges, and may provide pass/fail notifications and adaptation recommendations. Plans may be modified by changing doses, target contours, geometry, fractionation, session number or duration, beam delivery, and motion management. The disclosure further describes online, real-time, and offline adaptive radiotherapy, acceptable biological activity and PQI ranges, and bounded DVH methods for comparing treatment images against calculated limits.

After eight years in the league, the speaker celebrates winning the Stanley Cup with his teammates, praising their leadership and contributions. He thanks Scotty, his family, and his six-year-old daughter, Dasha, describing the championship as a long-held dream and expressing motivation to remain healthy and possibly continue playing. He notes that many top Russian players play abroad, particularly in Europe, and suggests bringing the Cup to Moscow could generate interest, attract investors, and support Russian hockey.

Early National Weather Service forecasts suggest unsettled weather may affect next Monday’s partial solar eclipse in the Philadelphia area, with reliable forecasts expected from Friday. Philadelphia is outside the path of totality; Charleston, South Carolina, will experience totality at 2:48 p.m. ET.

Microsoft Corporation filed a Form 8-K on October 26, 2017, reporting financial results for the fiscal quarter ended September 30, 2017. Exhibit 99.1 contains the company’s press release and is furnished rather than deemed filed under Section 18 of the Exchange Act. The report was signed by Frank H. Brod, Corporate Vice President of Finance and Administration and Chief Accounting Officer.

Huddersfield followed a 12-0 pre-season win over Warrington with a 28-16 Super League XXII victory over Widnes. Ahead of their home clash with Salford, head coach Rick Stone praised the team’s hard work but urged them to build on their positive start.

This compilation bridges the Dumbarton Oaks Proposals and the Charter of the United Nations, focusing on the United States' role in establishing the UN's legal framework and the American Delegation's positions, emphasizing the reasoning and atmosphere of informal agreements among the major Powers rather than the formal Conference proceedings. It lists related English-language publications from the United States, United Kingdom, USSR, Canada, Australia, and New Zealand. U.S. policy recommendations are traced from early 1945 through the May 2 "Changes in the Dumbarton Oaks Proposals" and the May 4 amendments proposed by the United States, United Kingdom, Soviet Union, and China. Substantive work began May 7, and documentation through the Charter's signing on June 26 covers four phases: policy development, negotiation, debates, and drafting. Policy evolution appears in minutes of seventy-nine U.S. Delegation meetings, twelve "Big Four" and twenty-nine "Big Five" meetings, and informal meetings with other American Republics; footnote citations link this unpublished material to published proceedings. Many records are informal notes rather than approved verbatim minutes. Selected documents include Stettinius's daily record, memoranda of conversations, daily reports to the Department, instructions, departmental correspondence, diplomatic notes, policy statements, and Presidential correspondence, with minor deletions noted. Sources include Department of State files, the Library of Congress, the Department of the Interior, the U.S. Mission to the UN, and the Franklin D. Roosevelt Library.

On March 22, 2016, NVIDIA entered an accelerated share repurchase agreement with Barclays, paying $500 million and receiving 12,108,715 NVIDIA shares. The repurchase was part of its plan to return $1 billion to shareholders through dividends and share repurchases. Settlement could require Barclays to deliver additional shares or NVIDIA to deliver shares or make a cash payment, based on NVIDIA’s average daily VWAP.

The coach explains that the team reduces third-period ice time so players reach the bench with energy, noting that fatigue during an energized game can reduce subsequent shifts’ performance. Line combinations remain unsettled: Hogue is in the mix, Hrkac and Plante are being evaluated, and Sydor could provide a different, physically powerful line, pending medical updates. Brett Hull is doubtful for the next game because his soreness does not appear sufficiently resolved, with the team preparing to play without him while avoiding further injury.

Keane and Carbonneau were given the option of taking one pregame skate after heavy workloads. The coach describes using shutdown forwards against leading opponents and adjusting lines according to matchups. Specific injury details are withheld to protect players and the team, but players are told clearly whether they are playing.

With Hull, the compromise is to allow freedom with the puck while requiring physical, aggressive play without it. Hull’s different perspective and strong personality require managing egos and finding common ground. The team also focuses on special-teams pressure, composure against goalies and the ability to exploit weaknesses, noting that few players remain calm in high-pressure situations.

Hogue is expected to take a pregame warmup and continue progressing if his injury remains stable. After an overtime loss in Colorado, players acknowledged insufficient physical and mental sacrifice and intend to improve their effort and shot-blocking. tactically, Hull and Modano retain offensive creativity, but team structure takes priority, including putting the puck behind defenders and limiting dangerous players such as Peca from controlling the game’s tempo or approaching the net.

Intel is in early talks with AMD to manufacture chips through Intel’s foundry business, according to Semafor. A deal would be a significant customer win, support investment in Intel’s manufacturing technology and signal other chipmakers’ confidence in Intel, though the manufacturing volume is unclear. Intel shares rose 7% Wednesday and are up nearly 77% in 2025, while AMD gained over 1%. Intel declined to comment, and AMD said it does not comment on rumors.

California’s $43 billion in long-term electricity contracts face an estimated 15%, or $6.5 billion, decline in value as western power prices fall and electricity consumption drops 9%. A Dow Jones column said exiting more than 40% of the contracts could benefit California, but major sellers were unlikely to exercise their options because prices remained favorable. The state bought June-through-September power at $325 per megawatt-hour, compared with $390 shortly afterward, and avoided blackouts.

Options volatility fell to multi-month lows as investors anticipated range-bound stocks and sold options for upfront income, including through covered-call strategies. Heavy trading occurred in Ericsson calls and Microsoft puts, while longer-dated options were favored because they offered larger premiums and greater downside protection. The VIX closed at 25, while Nasdaq volatility indexes approached eight-month lows. Bullish activity included trades in Cree and Enron; one Enron spread involved buying more than 5,000 June $55 calls and selling roughly 5,000 June $50 puts.

Saudi Arabia awarded eight international companies participation in three natural-gas ventures requiring about $25 billion, marking a major reopening of its energy sector to foreign investment. ExxonMobil, Shell, BP and Phillips were selected for the roughly $15 billion South Ghawar project, though its leader remained undecided. ExxonMobil was named leader of the Red Sea venture, with Enron and Occidental receiving stakes. Shell, TotalFinaElf and Conoco were selected for the Shaybah venture, whose leader was also pending. Saudi Arabia was expected to announce the remaining leaders by June 5 and sign memorandums of understanding by then. Exact ownership stakes, management structures and government participation were unresolved; planned developments include exploration, power generation, desalination, petrochemicals and chemicals, with consortia operating downstream projects and Saudi Aramco expected to oversee and operate upstream segments.

The U.S. government welcomed the participation of American firms as consistent with its energy policy. Analysts said the investments could support Saudi economic growth and job creation while positioning foreign companies for possible future access to Saudi crude reserves, although financial terms remained uncertain and were expected to yield 10%–15% returns. Aramco was expected to hold equity and oversee the projects without bearing their costs.

Steven Kean told James Hughes that Enron’s role concerning proposed Export-Import Bank funding cuts was smaller than a Wall Street Journal article suggested and commensurate with the company’s level of interest. After repeated discussions with John Hardy about the relative importance of OPIC, ExIm and other funding organizations as Enron’s business emphasis changed, Enron reduced headcount and expenditures in its proposed 2001 budget. Hardy also joined Linda Robertson’s Washington, D.C., organization rather than continuing as a standalone effort. Kean nevertheless expected Hardy to retain substantial project-finance responsibilities involving existing and continuing projects and transfer issues related to asset sales, and asked whether Hughes agreed.

Hardy said Enron was not leading the fight against the Office of Management and Budget and had not participated in meetings on Capitol Hill, but needed to demonstrate support for federal agencies’ programs and budgets. Enron was negotiating with ExIm and OPIC over Electrobolt and expected to need their support for problem projects. Rebecca McDonald served on ExIm’s private-sector advisory committee.

Attached reports said major exporters, including Enron, were lobbying Congress to prevent a proposed 25% reduction in ExIm’s $865 million operating budget. The bank had provided $12.6 billion in loans, guarantees and insurance during the prior fiscal year, including $135 million to Enron.

Other reports covered increased competition in the Dutch gas market, where Enron was actively trading; Southern California Edison’s proposed $2.7 billion transmission-line sale to the state, litigation by suppliers including Enron Wind, and California power contracts involving Enron that still required credit details to be resolved. Sierra Pacific’s CEO doubted the SEC would approve its $3.1 billion acquisition of Enron’s Portland General Electric because of financial and regulatory concerns. Additional items noted Enron’s Houston office tower, declining U.S. natural-gas prices, and completion of an outage on Enron’s Transwestern San Juan lateral.

Microsoft Corporation filed a Form 8-K dated July 18, 2019, announcing financial results for the fiscal quarter and year ended June 30, 2019. The press release was furnished as Exhibit 99.1 and not deemed filed for Section 18 liability or incorporated by reference absent specific reference. Frank H. Brod, Corporate Vice President, Finance and Administration, and Chief Accounting Officer, signed the report.

The Stack Offense uses two compact alignments outside the free-throw line, three ball handlers, and two stationary post screeners to reduce turnovers. Ballhandlers dribble, pop off screens for passes, and look for rolling or stepping-out posts when defenders overplay, show, sag, or deny passing lanes. If a handler cannot beat the defender, they pass out and reset the stack. When passing lanes are denied, receivers back cut, with posts setting back screens or stepping out for a return pass. Ballhandlers should drive decisively when the basket is open while avoiding offensive fouls.

A cross-sectional secret-shopper audit evaluated access to electronically prescribed, nameless expedited partner therapy (EPT) at 335 retail pharmacies in New York City. Trained pseudopatents used a standardized telephone script to assess pharmacists’ EPT awareness, willingness to dispense, counseling, insurance use, and reported barriers. Pharmacies were linked to neighborhood socioeconomic vulnerability using the CDC Social Vulnerability Index (SVI).

Only 40% of pharmacists reported awareness of EPT, and willingness to dispense nameless prescriptions was approximately 30%. Awareness was associated with greater willingness (48% versus 18%; p<0.001), while 31% of pharmacists refused or terminated the call. Common refusal reasons were unfamiliarity with EPT and belief that a patient name was legally required. Among potentially fillable prescriptions, only 46% followed New York State EPT guidelines, although insurance could be used for 86%. National-chain pharmacies were more aware of EPT than non-chain pharmacies. Higher neighborhood SVI was associated with greater EPT awareness but not willingness to dispense. Neighborhood chlamydia incidence, borough, and pharmacy type were not significantly associated with willingness.

The findings identify limited awareness, regulatory misconceptions, and inconsistent adherence as barriers to EPT access. The authors recommend pharmacist education, policy interventions, standardized practices, and further evaluation of electronic prescribing and insurance coverage. Limitations include the hypothetical telephone-based scenario, potential variability between secret shoppers, and focus on one metropolitan area.

Keaton Jones, a sixth-grader at Horace Maynard Middle School, posted a viral video describing being bullied at lunch, including having milk poured on him and ham put down his clothes. His mother shared the video, prompting public support under #StandWithKeaton. Principal Greg Clay said the incident was resolved, action was taken with the children involved, and he was unaware of repeated bullying. The school planned a student assembly and an anti-bullying talk. Parents acknowledged that bullying occurs occasionally and urged students to respect others and intervene when bullying is witnessed.

The disclosure describes a machine learning model scaling (MLMS) framework for hardware-aware AI/ML architecture search and model swapping. It addresses resource-intensive neural architecture search and manual, platform-specific optimization by selecting subnets from a supernet that satisfy changing hardware constraints and performance targets while reducing energy use and data-transfer costs.

An MLMS engine includes an interface, subnet selector, model pool, and subnet pool. A performance auditor within an ML model adaptation decision maker monitors inference quality and contextual conditions. A client supplies an ML configuration covering the supernet, application quality metrics, system constraints, auditor settings, datasets, tasks, and target hardware information. The auditor monitors metrics such as accuracy and latency, along with operational mode, system state, physical environment, and networking environment, and triggers a replacement search when configured thresholds indicate a change.

The subnet selector can use modular NAS or multi-objective evolutionary methods to identify candidate subnets, including Pareto-efficient alternatives. It favors replacements with the greatest overlap in pre-trained parameters with the deployed subnet, changing only differing vectorized architecture values to reduce memory writes and transfer energy. A two-stage search-and-swap algorithm first retains candidates whose performance is within a specified margin and that satisfy original and newly changed constraints, then selects the candidate with the lowest transfer cost. Elastic supernets may encode variables such as kernel size, width, and depth to enable model changes without restarting the framework.

The disclosure also identifies model- and platform-based metrics, including error, accuracy, latency, throughput, power, memory footprint, and processor utilization. Example applications include scaling models on drones, remote sensors, IoT image-recognition devices, and edge or federated-learning systems as power, environmental, hardware, and network conditions change. Example compute-node implementations include processors, GPUs, NPUs, FPGAs, ASICs, DSPs, SoCs, accelerators, memory, and storage supporting an inference engine and the MLMS components.

The passage examines how globalization and global issues can be integrated into university English-language education. It describes globalization as an interconnected “global village” affecting migration, culture, language hierarchies, economies, education policy, textbooks, and international communication. English is presented as a major lingua franca and a means for intercultural exchange, while issues such as health, environmental degradation, war, human rights, poverty, trade, and energy are identified as relevant teaching topics.

The study involved 372 non-English-major university students across three Taiwanese institutions over an 18-week semester. Using surveys, group and pair discussions, presentations, news, films, online videos, Wikipedia, and a Facebook group, teachers incorporated topics including global warming, tourism, music, festivals, food, cultures, arts, technology, sports, endangered animals, the Middle East, traditional stories, alternative energy, therapies, architecture, and environmental protection.

Students broadly supported globalization education and considered global issues significant, current, and relevant to their majors. They reported greater intercultural awareness, confidence in international communication, motivation to study English, and interest in incorporating global subjects into formal curricula. The most valued issues included global warming, energy, and environmental protection. Suggested activities included travel, disaster films, historical and current events, international speakers, English-language news, and interaction with exchange students. The passage concludes that global topics can make EFL study more practical and internationally relevant while preparing Taiwanese university students to communicate and participate in the global community.

Skinimalism is a simplified skincare approach using a few high-quality, targeted products instead of lengthy routines with multiple actives. It aims to support the skin barrier, natural texture, hydration, and long-term skin health while potentially reducing irritation, product waste, packaging, and costs. Simplifying a routine may also reduce the pressure created by social media and skincare marketing.

The approach is not suitable in the same way for everyone. Acne, pigmentation, rosacea, sensitive or compromised skin, and menopausal skin may still require specific ingredients such as retinoids, azelaic acid, salicylic acid, niacinamide, or moisturisers, along with SPF. However, these can often be used within a shorter, barrier-friendly routine rather than alongside numerous products. Actives should be introduced cautiously, ideally with professional advice.

For healthy skin, Parkinson recommends tailoring the routine to individual needs, age, lifestyle, and tolerance, eliminating one or two products at a time and allowing 2–4 weeks for the skin to adapt.

A single-case study examined whether smartphone touchscreen interactions could track neurobehavioural changes associated with anti-seizure medication adjustment and seizures. A man in his late twenties with refractory right temporal lobe epilepsy recorded 718,357 interactions over 185 days using the TapCounter app. During a five-day epilepsy monitoring unit admission, lamotrigine and perampanel were tapered and withdrawn, and video-EEG documented multiple focal seizures and one focal-to-bilateral tonic-clonic convulsion.

Daily joint-interval distributions of inter-touch intervals were analysed using kernel density estimation and cluster-based permutation testing. Tapering anti-seizure medication was associated with faster next-interval dynamics, a change that reversed when medication restarted. The day of the convulsion showed slower next-interval dynamics than the preceding three days, likely reflecting predominantly post-ictal changes because the seizure occurred soon after awakening.

The findings indicate that regular smartphone use may provide an unobtrusive way to monitor medication- and seizure-related behavioural fluctuations that cross-sectional assessments may miss. However, the effects of focal seizures were not evaluated, and cohort studies are required to determine generalisability and clinical utility.

The case examines Market Basket, a New England supermarket chain, and the 2014 conflict over the leadership of CEO Arthur T. Demoulas. After Arthur T., his management team, and other longtime executives were fired, employees, customers, and vendors protested for six weeks until he was reinstated with full operational authority.

Founded in Lowell, Massachusetts, by Greek immigrant Athanasios “Arthur” Demoulas and his wife in 1917, the company was later run by his sons Mike and George. A dispute over ownership led to litigation that gave George’s family, led by Arthur S. Demoulas, a 50.5% stake and a $206 million judgment. Mike grew Market Basket from 14 stores in 1971 to 51 in 1994, using profits rather than debt and emphasizing low prices, clean stores, employee benefits, and community involvement. Mike died in 2003, and his son Arthur T. became CEO in 2008.

By 2014, Market Basket operated 71 stores in Massachusetts, New Hampshire, and Maine, employed 25,000 nonunion workers, and generated $4.6 billion in revenue. Arthur T. described its model as resting on three elements: its employees, its low-price and low-cost structure, and its lack of debt. The chain emphasized high sales volume, uniform prices, a broad private-label assortment, company-operated warehouses, experienced category buyers, internal promotion, extensive training, flexible scheduling, profit sharing, bonuses, and low employee turnover. It also provided unusually strong customer service, including stocking stores while customers shopped and requiring employees to greet anyone within ten feet.

The company’s relationships with employees, suppliers, customers, and communities were closely intertwined. Many employees had spent decades working their way up, while many vendors and customers had longstanding personal relationships with the company. Management maintained a decentralized, fast-decision culture in which stores, buyers, and supervisors could adapt products and prices quickly. Local suppliers depended heavily on Market Basket’s business, and employees and customers commonly viewed the chain as part of their community.

All nine shareholders belonged to the Demoulas family. Arthur T. resisted board oversight of spending and related-party transactions, while Arthur S.’s family sought greater control and liquidity.
