In 2013, Arthur S.’s side gained control of the board. It suspended Arthur T.’s authority, approved a $300 million shareholder distribution, and later rejected Arthur T’s attempt to block the payment. Market Basket also reduced prices by an additional 4%, a decision expected to cost $170 million.

On June 23, 2014, the board fired Arthur T. and two senior executives and appointed former Albertsons CFO Felicia Thornton and former Radio Shack president James Gooch as interim co-CEOs. Other longtime executives and managers resigned or were dismissed, including eight managers accused of leading the protest. Employees, vendors, and customers then organized a walkout, picketing, boycotts, fundraising, and public advocacy. The protest effectively halted warehouse support and deliveries while stores remained open. Sales fell by more than 90%, part-time employees were laid off, and vendors and nearby businesses suffered losses while competitors gained customers.

The interim leadership’s return-to-work ultimatums and job fairs did not break the protest. Support came from the United Food and Commercial Workers International Union, local businesses, customers, politicians, and media. On August 27, the board and shareholders agreed to sell 50.5% of the company to Arthur T. and his family for $1.6 billion, restoring him and his management team. Operations resumed within weeks, and employees received $49 million in bonuses. However, the acquisition required $1 billion in mortgage financing and $600 million in syndicated loans, raising questions about whether Market Basket could sustain its low prices, employee compensation and benefits, debt-free model, and growth.

Microsoft Corporation filed a Form 10-Q for the quarter ended September 30, 2018, the first quarter of fiscal 2019. The company reported revenue of $29.084 billion, up 19%; gross margin of $19.179 billion, up 18%; operating income of $9.955 billion, up 29%; net income of $8.824 billion, up 34%; and diluted earnings per share of $1.14, up 36%. Productivity and Business Processes revenue rose 19%, Intelligent Cloud revenue rose 24%, and More Personal Computing revenue rose 15%, with operating income increasing 29%, 37%, and 23%, respectively.

Commercial cloud revenue increased 47% to $8.5 billion. Azure revenue grew 76%, Office 365 commercial revenue 36%, Dynamics 365 revenue 51%, LinkedIn revenue 33%, and gaming revenue 44%. Revenue growth was partly offset by a lower gross-margin percentage in More Personal Computing and increased spending on cloud and artificial-intelligence engineering, LinkedIn, and commercial sales capacity.

At September 30, 2018, Microsoft held $15.137 billion in cash and cash equivalents and $120.743 billion in short-term investments. Total assets were $257.619 billion, total liabilities were $171.652 billion, and stockholders’ equity was $85.967 billion. Operating cash flow was $13.657 billion, while the company used $3.744 billion for share repurchases and $3.220 billion for dividends. Microsoft had agreed to acquire GitHub in a $7.5 billion stock transaction expected to close by the end of October 2018.

The financial statements were prepared under U.S. GAAP, and Deloitte & Touche reported that it was unaware of any material modifications needed for conformity with GAAP. Notes addressed investments, derivatives, leases, unearned revenue, taxes, contingencies, and newly adopted accounting standards. The effective tax rate declined to 14% from 18%, primarily due to the Tax Cuts and Jobs Act. Legal matters included patent claims, Canadian antitrust litigation awaiting settlement approval, a Chinese regulatory investigation, cellular-phone litigation, and an employment-discrimination appeal.

The 2022 NFL Draft set a record with six wide receivers selected in the first 20 picks, reflecting their growing value as offenses increasingly emphasize passing. Wide receivers complete the passing game by running routes, creating separation, and securing accurate throws from quarterbacks, requiring route-running skill, football IQ, coordination, agility, speed, strong hands, and toughness. They also contribute as run blockers by holding perimeter blocks and pursuing defenders downfield.

Wide receivers typically line up away from offensive linemen near the sideline and primarily receive passes, which explains the position’s name. Other names include wideout, split-end, and flanker. Elite receivers create difficult one-on-one matchups and force defenses to adjust their alignments, giving offensive coordinators more options in game planning.

Notable historically great receivers include Jerry Rice, NFL career leader in receptions, receiving yards, and touchdowns; Randy Moss, who set the single-season touchdown-reception record with 23 in 2007; and Steve Largent, a seven-time Pro Bowler whose number was retired by the Seahawks.

The paper introduces PerovSegNet, a YOLOv8x-seg–based framework for automated segmentation of perovskite and lead iodide SEM images. The PerovData dataset contains 10,994 annotated images expanded from 40 manually labeled originals, covering perovskite, lead iodide, and defects. UMAP analysis showed clear separation among the three classes, while annotation statistics revealed substantial variation in object size and a predominance of small objects.

PerovSegNet adds two modules to the backbone and neck. ASDCB combines standard, dilated, depthwise separable, and attention-enhanced convolutions with channel shuffling and ConvFFN processing to improve multi-scale feature fusion and boundary localization. SAD replaces conventional pooling with dual-path depthwise separable convolutions and adaptive pooling, preserving fine textures while capturing large-scale morphology. The resulting backbone, neck, and prediction head generate pixel-level masks for perovskite, lead iodide, and defects.

In comparisons on PerovData, PerovSegNet reached 87.3% mAP@0.5 and 80.0% mAP@0.5:0.95, outperforming Mask R-CNN, Cascade Mask R-CNN, and Cascade InternImage-XL. Ablation results showed that SAD and ASDCB individually improved mAP@0.5 from the 83.17% YOLOv8x-seg baseline to 86.30% and 86.42%, respectively; combining them produced 87.25% mAP@0.5 and 79.96% mAP@0.5:0.95 while reducing parameters and GFLOPs by about 24% and 25%. Defect segmentation accuracy increased from 33% to 64%, while lead iodide and perovskite accuracy each rose from 84% and 82% to 88%.

The framework automatically extracts masks, areas, counts, and shape descriptors across multiple SEM magnifications. An observational analysis of approximately 25 papers from 2022–2025 found that perovskite area correlated positively with PCE (\(r=0.78\)), lead iodide area had a mild positive correlation (\(r=0.23\)), and defect area and count correlated negatively (\(r=-0.27\) and \(r=-0.32\)). These results do not establish causality, and identified limitations include class imbalance, segmentation errors, imaging-condition dependence, limited cross-magnification validation, and insufficient inference speed for in situ or inline deployment.

A University of Connecticut study found that vaping nicotine-based liquid produced DNA damage approximately equivalent to smoking unfiltered cigarettes, with potential damage increasing with the number of puffs. Researchers used a low-cost, 3D-printed “organ-on-a-chip” device containing human metabolic enzymes and DNA. DNA damage can cause cellular mutations that lead to cancer.

The tutorial demonstrates how to backtest a momentum strategy in Python using sector SPDR ETFs. Historical adjusted closing prices are downloaded with yfinance and processed with pandas, numpy, and matplotlib.pyplot. Monthly returns are calculated, and momentum is defined as each ETF’s rolling nine-month performance. Each month, the three ETFs with the strongest momentum are selected and held in an equally weighted portfolio. Portfolio returns since 2005 are calculated and plotted against SPY. The strategy produced a 9.89% CAGR, compared with SPY’s 9.46%, resulting in little alpha and nearly identical performance. The strategy can be customized by changing the selected ETFs or assets.

The Evening Star is a bearish reversal pattern formed by a tall bullish candle, a small candle that gaps above it, and a bearish candle that closes below the first candle’s midpoint. It occurs during an upward price swing and may signal a potential reversal. Reliability increases with a significant gap between the first two candles and a third candle longer than the first. Traders often confirm the pattern with trendlines, support and resistance levels, momentum oscillators, RSI, stochastic oscillator, or Bollinger Bands before opening short positions. Risk management is essential because false signals, volatility, overreliance on technical analysis, lack of diversification, and losses without proper controls are possible. Exits may use profit targets, directional indicator signals, or stop-loss orders. The strategy can be adapted to changing market conditions, and timeframe selection depends on trading style and risk tolerance; some traders use multiple timeframes. Backtesting with defined rules and settings is recommended. In an AAPL example, two Evening Star patterns preceded significant declines, and trades opened after each pattern with stops above the pattern and targets at support would have been profitable.

Anna Mae Blessing, 92, was charged with first-degree murder, aggravated assault and kidnapping after authorities said she shot her 72-year-old son multiple times in their Fountain Hills home. His girlfriend disarmed two pistols. Blessing said she had considered killing him because he planned to place her in assisted living.

The passage argues that U.S. education has adopted business practices that categorize students, standardize performance, and treat teachers as professionals, but these reforms have not broadly improved teacher compensation, student outcomes, or equity. Since Horace Mann’s public education movement, schools have used bureaucratic structures and classifications based on factors such as age, race, sex, grade, and subject. Reports such as *A Nation at Risk* identified inadequate teacher preparation, pay, and working conditions, leading to higher standards and national certification without greater financial security or independence for teachers.

The No Child Left Behind Act introduced competition, financial incentives, accountability, standardized testing, and annual yearly progress requirements. Schools failing to meet requirements faced improvement plans, supplemental services, staff or curriculum changes, extended class time, and potentially closure or conversion to a charter school. Charter schools have produced isolated successes, but research cited in the passage reports mixed outcomes, segregation, budgetary disruptions, disparities, and the selective admission of high-performing students, alongside no broad gains in test scores.

The passage also examines the medical model of learning, which attributes learning differences primarily to innate biological characteristics. It describes this approach as rooted partly in eugenic and slaveholding beliefs and argues that diagnosis can encourage fixed mindsets, stigma, and stereotype threat, contributing to disengagement and weaker academic performance. Alternatives include mindfulness, positive role models, and involving students in understanding their conditions through inquiry, self-discovery, and problem-solving.

Problem-solving is presented as a fundamental learning process extending beyond humans to other organisms and cognitive systems. It involves interaction with the environment, creating predictions, testing theories, explaining outcomes, correcting errors, and refining understanding. Human problem-solving is distinguished by explanation and metacognitive reflection. The scientific method and children’s natural “child scientist” behavior are presented as examples of this recurring process.

Cognitive development is described as recursive. Perception is constructed through heuristics shaped by experience and environmental interaction rather than as a direct recording of reality. Because these heuristics develop through engagement, restricted sensory experience can impair development, and similar mechanisms may contribute to some forms of dyslexia. Across biology and psychology, research is presented as converging on an interactive process in which prior experience shapes predictions that guide action.

For education, the passage emphasizes metacognition, feedback, collaboration, and mentoring. Teachers, parents, mentors, and scientific peer reviewers are described as supporting students’ reflection and problem-solving. Reduced parental time, fewer siblings, budget cuts, costlier support services, and technology that limits environmental interaction are identified as contributing to weaker learning. Recommended reforms replace diagnosis and exclusion with frequent feedback, high expectations, participatory testing, and assistance in applying a scientific-method-style cycle of problem identification, hypothesis, testing, and revision.

At the institutional level, problem-solving should be organized bottom-up. Students should develop self-directed learning; teachers should model visible problem-solving; administrators should address issues that exceed classroom capacity; and institutions should identify their own weaknesses and deploy resources accordingly. Collaboration, self-reflection, one-to-one support, and assessment of individual progress are favored over norm-based comparison, stigma, bureaucratic specialization, and commercialized school models. The conclusion calls for restructuring education around self-regulated learning rather than business-style efficiency, testing, categorization, and treating teachers as information dispensers.

Twelve autism units are planned across Sligo/Leitrim and Donegal in 2018/19, including five primary and seven post-primary ASD classes. Leitrim’s ASD classes have increased from two to five since 2011. Where demand exceeds available places, a fair, non-discriminatory selection process may be required, and parents are advised to apply early.

The author rejects Ambassador Hartman’s advice to trade away INF deployment, arguing that INF has become a test of NATO viability. Without balanced theater arms control, non-deployment could undermine NATO and strengthen European pacifist and anti-American forces. Contrary to Hartman, Mitterrand supports INF, Italy remains firm, and Britain and Germany are likely to honor commitments. The author urges the United States to uphold zero-zero and deploy if the Soviets do not alter their position. If Moscow adopts a balanced posture, asymmetrical reductions might establish theater-nuclear parity, but signaling readiness to abandon zero-zero could embolden opponents, embarrass European governments, and weaken Soviet incentives to compromise.

A separate memorandum records Secretary Shultz’s meeting with Dobrynin. They agreed to regular consultations on arms control and bilateral issues and discussed possible Foreign Ministers’ and summit meetings. Dobrynin favored the Shultz-Gromyko channel because Geneva negotiators lacked flexibility and said Foreign Ministers should resolve major problems before treaty drafting.

The passage examines damages for unjustifiable detention of whaling vessels and recognizes that lost catch may be included when assessing damage. In the Costa Rica Packet, the mate should have taken command while the captain was provisionally detained. In *Potomac*, the U.S. Supreme Court held that owners of an injured vessel are entitled to full compensation for loss of use during repairs, measured by market price when available and otherwise by probable profits. In *Williamson v. Barrett*, the court reaffirmed compensation for repair costs and lost service, including the vessel’s earning capacity or hire value. The English *Gazelle* decision allowed gross freight minus ordinary voyage expenses, though this could be inadequate for prolonged repairs. These principles were applied by the Court of Commissioners of Alabama Claims to four whaling ships captured by the Confederate cruiser *Shenandoah* and forced to abandon their voyages.

Cutting and polishing CZTS semiconductor crystals creates a damaged surface layer that impedes charge collection and causes leakage currents, requiring chemical polishing before use as radiation detectors. This study examined the etching of Cd₁₋xZnxTe₁₋ySey crystals with zinc content x ≈ 0.1 and selenium contents y = 0, 0.022, 0.06, and 0.1 using freshly prepared 5% bromine in methanol at 19°C. Etching trajectories, stagewise and average etching rates, and surface morphology were measured.

A thermodynamic model predicts that CZTS should etch more slowly than selenium-free CZT under identical conditions, with the rate difference related to the excess Gibbs energy of the quaternary solid solution. Average eight-minute etching rates decreased from 24 μm/min for CZT to 18, 15, and 13 μm/min for selenium-containing samples. At y ≈ 0.02, the experimental rate reduction was about 24%, consistent with the predicted 22%. These results provide evidence that selenium hardens and strengthens the crystal lattice and reduces the visibility of growth defects.

Short etching generally reduced surface roughness, whereas prolonged treatment beyond 3–5 minutes could increase roughness and preferentially attack damaged areas, edges, and defects. Stirring increased etching rates by roughly 1.5–2 times. The results support using etching trajectories and average rates to select suitable polishing conditions for CZTS detector elements.

Vanuatu’s Reserve Bank may investigate APMA Financial Investment Centre’s savings and loan scheme. Ambae’s volcano rating was lowered to level 3, with eruptions confined to Lake Voui. Relief supplies were collected for evacuees, teacher salary scales take effect in 2018, and 21 retirees received service medals.

Crystal Palace host Newcastle United at Selhurst Park on Sunday. Newcastle may feature Islam Slimani, while Palace’s Bakary Sako is a sixth long-term absentee with a broken ankle. Newcastle hope to repeat Sunderland’s 4–0 win over Palace.

Professor Claire Massey launched the second edition of The New Zealand Land and Food Annual, featuring 31 experts on sustainable food production. It supports efforts to triple New Zealand’s $33 billion land and food sector by 2025 through nutrition-driven agriculture within planetary boundaries, while current farming and food-processing practices remain unsustainable.

The passage reviews the formation, evolution, composition, and observational signatures of small-body reservoirs that may source exocometary activity, using Solar System populations as analogues and constraints. After gas dispersal, remnants form dynamically distinct reservoirs shaped by planetary resonances and migration. These include asteroid groups, co-orbital and Trojan populations, Centaurs, Jupiter-family comets, several trans-Neptunian populations, and the Oort cloud. Their compositions range from volatile-poor, silicate-rich inner bodies to predominantly icy outer bodies containing water, CO₂, CO, methane, methanol, complex organics, and other volatiles.

Stars form in dense molecular clouds that collapse, rotate, and form protostellar discs, with young stars classified as Class 0, I, II, or III. Discs around Class II stars commonly contain rings and gaps associated with planet formation, while more massive Class 0/I discs may contain sufficient solids for forming planets but generally have fewer distinct substructures. Birth environments influence discs through external photoevaporation and stellar flybys, potentially truncating or destroying them, transporting material, and altering disc chemistry. Photoevaporation dominates in massive, dense, long-lived clusters, whereas flybys are more important in low-mass, short-lived clusters.

Disc temperature and dust opacity control where molecules condense, producing snowlines that divide icy outer planetesimals from largely refractory inner bodies. Stellar luminosity shifts these snowlines outward for more massive stars. Evolving gas and dust can develop elemental abundance anomalies and CO depletion beyond simple snowline explanations, so composition depends on where and when planetesimals form. Stellar mass also affects disc lifetime, dust mass, radius, planet occurrence, and the distribution of snowlines. Although exocomets are most readily detected around A-type stars, planets and potentially debris reservoirs occur around stars across a broad mass range.

Dust initially grows from submicrometre grains through collisional sticking, sedimentation, turbulent collisions, and radial drift. Growth eventually encounters a bouncing barrier, particularly for silicate aggregates, after which fragmentation and mass transfer may permit larger bodies. An increasingly favored pathway involves millimetre-to-decimetre pebbles concentrating in vortices, pressure bumps, or midplane layers. The streaming instability amplifies local dust-to-gas ratios, and sufficiently dense, weakly diffusive pebble clouds can exceed the Hill density and collapse gravitationally into planetesimals. Simulations favor shallow size distributions dominated by large bodies, and Solar System evidence—including roughly 100-km primordial asteroids, Arrokoth, and trans-Neptunian binaries—supports a “born big” formation scenario. Planetesimal mass may scale with stellar mass, while formation location also affects size.

After gas dispersal, surviving solids form debris discs, likely reservoirs for many exocomet populations. Their observed dust masses are far below their inferred total masses because larger bodies continually replenish dust through collisions. Debris discs vary in radius, mass, morphology, and likely composition, and their structures may reflect formation conditions, collisions, or planetary interactions. Collisional grinding progressively depletes them, making younger systems more favorable for detectable exocomet activity.

Solar System orbits constrain early disc evolution and stellar encounters. Surface colors, near-infrared spectra, cometary abundances, isotope ratios, and samples returned by missions such as Hayabusa, Hayabusa2, OSIRIS-REx, Stardust, and Rosetta provide information about formation locations and composition, although subsequent dynamical, physical, and chemical evolution complicates interpretation. JWST observations are already distinguishing compositional groups among trans-Neptunian objects and Centaurs.

The Oort cloud is divided into inner and outer regions. Models indicate that a small fraction of planetesimals ejected from near their parent stars remains bound, with Galactic tides isotropizing and circularizing their orbits. Its formation time and pristine state remain uncertain, and some members may have been captured from other stars. Cluster encounters can strongly alter Oort-like clouds, temporarily increasing the inward comet flux while reducing their long-term reservoir. The existence of exo-Oort clouds remains theoretically possible but observationally unconfirmed.

Overall, small-body reservoirs are expected around most young or main-sequence stars, but their abundance, architecture, composition, and exocomet contribution remain uncertain. Outstanding questions include the effects of birth environment and binary stars, the dominant exocomet reservoir, the roles of planets and non-native objects, debris-disc mass and location, and the extent to which debris discs resemble Kuiper belts. Future observations with JWST, ALMA, Rubin Observatory, SPHEREx, Roman, the Extremely Large Telescope, and the Giant Magellan Telescope are expected to address these issues.

This document is an excerpt of the Statistical Analysis Plan (SAP) for study ZEA-DNK-02170 (protocol ZP4207-17086), describing pharmacokinetic (PK), pharmacodynamic (PD), and safety analyses for dasiglucagon versus placebo, plus appendices covering data presentation, SAS programming QC, and the list of planned tables, figures, and listings.

PK analyses: Summary statistics of plasma dasiglucagon and GlucaGen concentrations will be presented by treatment group and time point, with change from pre-dose also summarized; results are displayed as mean (SD) with pre-dose values below LLOQ set to 0 pmol/mL and results rounded to three significant digits. Figures will show mean concentrations versus nominal time on both original and logarithmic scales (treatment curves combined in one graph with overlay plots) and individual concentration-time curves per treatment group. Placebo samples will not be analyzed by the laboratories analyzing dasiglucagon and GlucaGen.

PD analyses: Plasma glucose is measured pre-dose and at 4, 6, 8, 10, 12, 15, 17, 20, 30, and 45 minutes (plus 60 minutes if body weight ≥21 kg). Actual sampling times must not deviate more than ±30 seconds from nominal through the 20-minute point and ±1 minute thereafter; pre-dose is within 2 minutes prior to dosing. The primary PD endpoint is plasma glucose response as area under the effect curve above baseline from 0 to 30 minutes (AUE0-30min), calculated with SAS. Summary statistics, raw data listings, and mean/individual concentration-time curves will be provided.

Safety analyses (based on the safety set) comprise: extent of exposure (insulin use before the hypoglycemia induction procedure, details and totals of the induction procedure, trial medication administration, and post-treatment rescue glucose infusion, including time to first IV glucose infusion calculated as time of first glucose administration minus study medication administration time, summarized descriptively without censoring and without statistical tests); local tolerability at the injection site assessed at 30, 120, and 300 minutes after dosing, tabulated by time point, symptom and grade (excluding "other types of reactions"); and adverse events, where treatment-emergent AEs (TEAEs) include events occurring after dosing or pre-existing events worsening during the study, with partial onset dates conservatively counted as treatment-emergent unless other data indicate otherwise. Verbatim terms are mapped to MedDRA version 21.0 or higher. Causality uses a 0–3 investigator scale (not related, unlikely, possibly, probably related), with possible/probable grouped as related and missing relationship queried and defaulted to related; severity is mild/moderate/severe and is not imputed when missing. An overview AE table (based on verbatim counts) covers screening AEs, TEAEs, AESIs, other important events, injection site reactions (investigator-assessed and special search category), study drug-related TEAEs, serious TEAEs, serious drug-related TEAEs, and deaths, with frequency tables by system organ class and preferred term (patients counted once per preferred term, ordered by descending incidence in the dasiglucagon group). Special search categories include QT interval prolongation (broad SMQ) and drug-related hepatic disorders (broad SMQ).

Laboratory analyses include continuous results with descriptive statistics, low/high/within-range flags and counts/percentages, categorical results with counts/percentages, and change from baseline (screening V1 to follow-up V3) for continuous parameters, applied to hematology, biochemistry, coagulation (screening only), urinalysis, pregnancy test, and alcohol breath test. Vital signs are summarized at baseline and each postbaseline time point with categorical pulse rate analysis; physical examination appears in listings only. ECG assessments include investigator overall interpretation, descriptive statistics by parameter, and categorical QTcF counts (>450, >480, >500 ms) and changes from baseline (>30, >60 ms). Immunogenicity (ADA) is analyzed descriptively per treatment group, counting treatment-induced ADA (baseline-negative, post-dose positive) and treatment-boosted patients (baseline-positive with ≥5-fold titer increase) among evaluable patients; no statistical tests are planned.

Changes from the protocol: the statistical analysis for the primary efficacy parameter was reworded with additional sensitivity and supportive analyses, and secondary efficacy terminology changed from "…within 30 (20/15/10) min" to "…at 30 (20/15/10) min".

Appendices specify presentation and programming standards (decimal-place rules for means, medians, standard deviations, minima/maxima and percentages; zero-count categories shown; P-values to three decimals; footnotes left justified at page bottom with source and program/data-cutoff/run date statements; SAS date and 24-hour time formats; tables, figures, and listings organization, sorting and legends; unit conversions for height, weight, temperature, BMI, durations, and change from baseline formulas), SAS programming QC requirements (program naming, header, documentation, hard coding, SAP derivation, log review, output review, Pinnacle 21 validation, spot-checks of at least two patients, and retention of QC documentation in BIO-0205-TMP-002), and an ICH E3-based index of planned tables, figures, and listings for sections 14 and 16.2, including time to plasma glucose recovery (summary tables, Kaplan-Meier curves, histogram, linear interpolation, sensitivity analyses), plasma glucose recovery within 10/15/20/30 minutes with 95% CIs and Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel tests stratified by age group and injection site, plasma glucose change from baseline with ANOVA (treatment, age group, injection site), AE tables and listings, ECG, laboratory, vital sign, immunogenicity, PK/PD outputs, and subject disposition listings.

The Department clarified that passport applicants need not state an intention to return within two years; passports remain valid for two years and may be renewed upon a satisfactory application. It also specified that a mission’s first secretary ordinarily serves as chargé d’affaires ad interim in the head’s absence, while use of a second or third secretary in an emergency requires prior consultation with the Department. Finally, an executive order prohibited diplomatic and consular officers from publicly criticizing or charging fellow officers, requiring that such matters be communicated confidentially to the Department of State.

Seminary graduation exercises for 16 Miami Valley seniors were held May 20 in Huber Heights. More than 100 students attended with their families, and graduates received Book of Mormon certificates. Three seniors discussed scripture’s spiritual and practical benefits.

The TPS7H500x-SP push-pull converter design uses a 49.9-kΩ resistor for an initial 50-ns leading-edge blank time and a 33-nF soft-start capacitor producing approximately 7.5 ms of soft start. The transformer design targets a 35% maximum duty cycle, a 2.5 turns ratio, and magnetizing current equal to 6% of output current; its calculated primary inductance of 33 µH was implemented as 40 µH. Primary GaN FETs are rated at 170 V for a 36-V maximum input, while an 80-V synchronous rectifier is selected for an expected 20-V maximum stress. A parallel Schottky diode may reduce soft-start current and reverse-conduction losses. An RCD clamp can limit switch-node voltage, with component values calculated from overshoot, leakage inductance, peak primary current, and capacitor ripple, then optimized through testing.

The output inductor is 0.47 µH with a target ripple current of 40%. Output capacitance calculations require at least 1.3 mF; the design uses 2.3 mF, provided by seven 330-µF polymer tantalum capacitors. An optional inductor-capacitor output filter can further reduce ripple, with damping available if high-frequency peaking occurs. Cycle-by-cycle current limiting begins at approximately 35 A, and a 7.5-Ω sense resistor with a 1:100 current-sense transformer sets the overcurrent level. The hiccup capacitor is 3.3 nF. Type 2A frequency compensation targets a 10-kHz crossover with selected values of 40.2 kΩ for RCOMP, 15 nF for CCOMP, and 47 pF for CHF. A 102-kΩ resistor sets slope compensation.

The controllers require a regulated 4-V to 14-V supply and at least a 0.1-µF ceramic bypass capacitor from VIN to AVSS. Layout guidance emphasizes separating feedback and control traces from power components and switching nodes, minimizing high-dv/dt and high-di/dt loops, separating analog and power grounds at one point, using short and wide current paths, placing filtering and compensation components near their pins, filtering CS_ILIM if required, and connecting the CFP package’s backside metallization to AVSS through multiple vias. The document also includes application curves, PCB layout examples, radiation-related documentation, support resources, revision history, and mechanical and orderable information.

Amazon.com, Inc. filed its Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2019. The company operates through three segments—North America, International, and Amazon Web Services—and serves consumers, sellers, developers, enterprises, content creators, and advertisers. Its operations include online and physical stores, third-party seller programs, Prime, electronic devices such as Kindle, Fire tablets, Fire TV, Echo, and Ring, media content, publishing services, advertising, and AWS cloud offerings. Whole Foods Market has been consolidated since its acquisition on August 28, 2017. Amazon reported approximately 798,000 employees at year-end.

The filing identifies risks including intense competition, expansion into new products and geographies, fluctuating growth, international and regulatory exposure, fulfillment-network and data-center capacity, seasonal inventory risks, acquisitions, foreign exchange, personnel retention, cybersecurity and system interruptions, intellectual property, stock-price volatility, litigation, taxes, supplier dependence, product liability, payments, and seller misconduct. Fourth-quarter revenue represented 31% of annual revenue in 2019.

Net sales increased from $107.0 billion in 2015 to $280.5 billion in 2019, while operating income rose from $2.2 billion to $14.5 billion and net income from $596 million to $11.6 billion. Diluted earnings per share were $23.01 in 2019. Operating cash flow was $38.5 billion, compared with $30.7 billion in 2018, and cash, cash equivalents, and marketable securities totaled $55.0 billion at year-end. Investing activities used $24.3 billion, including $12.7 billion of cash capital expenditures and $2.5 billion of acquisition and investment payments; financing activities used $10.1 billion.

Management emphasized long-term sustainable free cash flow, customer-experience improvements, efficient inventory turnover, and disciplined infrastructure and technology investment. Critical accounting judgments included inventory valuation and income taxes; each additional 1% of inventory valuation allowance as of December 31, 2019 would have increased cost of sales by approximately $230 million.

Anthology Inc., an education-technology company built through acquisitions, is restructuring amid more than $1 billion in debt and an $80 million revenue decline over two years. Oaktree and Nexus Capital Management are providing $50 million so Anthology can focus on its Blackboard learning-management platform and become debt-free early next year. The company is selling its enterprise operations, life-cycle engagement and student-success businesses to Encoura and Ellucian.

Analysts attributed Anthology’s financial strain to costly integration of overlapping products, rising interest rates, slower institutional purchasing and a failed strategy of cross-selling an integrated suite of software. The company was formed in 2020 and acquired Blackboard in 2021. Its breakup reflects a broader higher-education technology shift toward sustainable, interoperable and modular platforms.

Federal Reserve Chair Janet Yellen rejected President Trump’s criticism of Dodd-Frank, citing strong, well-capitalized banks, lending above pre-crisis levels, increased Tier 1 capital, and a resilient financial system. She urged exempting community banks from the Volcker Rule and said U.S. interest rates should rise sooner than expected.

DAWN-plasma is a randomized, open-label, multicenter phase 2 proof-of-concept trial evaluating convalescent plasma’s safety and efficacy in hospitalized adults with COVID-19 by comparing standard care with and without plasma, using a 2:1 allocation and WHO-aligned outcomes.

Germany’s education system reflects its history of unification, Nazi rule, postwar division, and reunification. The country had about 83.2 million residents in 2023, including 10.9 million immigrants, and was 77.5% urban in 2021. Rising student numbers associated with immigration and a modest birth-rate increase may have contributed to a teacher shortage.

After unification in 1871, Bismarck introduced Prussian-influenced, tax-funded compulsory schooling, initially eight years, combining basics with obedience, civic duty, and ethics. Nazi rule standardized secondary education in 1938 to promote obedience, physical fitness, nationalism, and racism rather than critical inquiry.

Postwar West Germany retained three secondary tracks: Hauptschule, Realschule, and Gymnasium, with vocational, intermediate, and university-preparatory functions; Gesamtschule was added in the 1960s. East Germany developed a distinct socialist system. Following reunification, the three-tier model became national, and public education became free. Education is now governed mainly by the states, producing differences in curricula, school choice, and whether Hauptschulen remain separate or are combined with Realschulen.

Special schools, or Hilfsschulen, emerged in the 1920s to provide tailored education for disabled students and prepare them for low-wage vocational work. In 1960, the Kultusministerkonferenz (KMK) established various special-school types and legal frameworks. Inclusion has expanded since the early 1990s, although special and general systems also became more distinct; students with disabilities in special schools have performed worse than comparable peers in inclusive schools.

About 577,000 students attended seven categories of special schools in 2019–2020, across roughly 2,800 schools with 68,500 educators. In 2021–2022, about 93,000 disabled students were enrolled in general elementary schools and 25,000 in general secondary schools. Reported inclusion rates were 33.6% at the elementary level and 14.9% at the secondary level. Around half of disabled students included at secondary level attend Hauptschule. Physical accessibility barriers persist, and admission to Gymnasium is difficult because it is the highest and most advanced tier and has limited specialized services.

Students needing support may be referred by a teacher or parent for comprehensive assessment. Teachers, specialists, parents, and students collaborate on an individualized plan, with procedures varying by state and mobile special education services providing assessment, advice, and coordination. On-campus programs increasingly allow disabled students to remain with same-age peers while receiving specialized instruction. Parents tend to favor inclusion more for physical or sensory disabilities than for behavioral or severe cognitive disabilities, and the appropriate setting depends on individual needs.

Teacher education follows a two-phase model. Phase one generally comprises a six-semester bachelor’s and four-semester master’s at a university, followed by a first state examination. Phase two is a paid, two-year Referendariat with mentor guidance, classroom responsibility, and a final state examination leading to state certification. Teachers have civil-servant status, providing job security and benefits, but professional development and movement between careers or school types are limited. Special educators follow a similar path, usually intern in special schools, specialize in elementary or secondary education, and receive greater preparation in pedagogy, behavior management, behavior analysis, and breaking complex tasks into steps. They are trained primarily for elementary and vocational secondary settings.

Legislation supporting disability rights includes the 2006 General Equal Treatment Act, the 2008 UN Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities, and KMK recommendations on diversity issued in 2015. North Rhine-Westphalia’s 2013 school-law amendment closed or merged many special schools and shifted responsibility to general schools, with former school categories used to identify services. States retain substantial autonomy and fund their schools, while the KMK coordinates national policy.

Remaining challenges include balancing inclusion with specialized environments, securing stable funding for support services, and addressing teacher attitudes. Inclusive settings can produce positive cognitive outcomes but also unfavorable peer comparisons and isolation; full inclusion may not suit every student. Physical placement does not automatically create social inclusion, although positive teacher attitudes are associated with greater social integration. Poor implementation of MTSS/RTI has been viewed negatively. The division between vocational and university-preparatory schools, especially limited services and a rigid culture within Gymnasium, continues to restrict secondary inclusion and employment options.

Federal reduction-in-force layoffs affected Education Department employees, though the department did not specify how many or which offices were involved. OMB Director Russell Vought said the promised cuts had begun. Sources said the latest round would include elementary and secondary education and communications and outreach staff, but not the Office of Federal Student Aid. Earlier layoffs were blocked by lower courts, but the Supreme Court overturned those rulings in July, and affected employees left in August. The department’s employee union vowed to challenge the latest cuts. HHS employees in multiple divisions also received layoff notices, while NIH’s staffing status remained unclear. Democrats opposed the layoffs, called them unconstitutional, and said Vought and President Trump used the shutdown to pressure the Senate.

During a Warsaw visit, Angela Merkel and Mateusz Morawiecki discussed Poland’s rule-of-law dispute, economic cooperation, migration, European unity and the Skripal poisoning in Britain. Merkel welcomed possible progress in talks on Poland’s judicial overhaul, while Morawiecki said agreement required compromise. They also backed strong EU conclusions and a firm response to the nerve-agent attack, holding Russia responsible unless it proves otherwise.

This continuation application describes transistor gates and contacts using cobalt or metal-silicide layers over metal-nitride barriers to reduce resistance and improve adhesion. Doped-polysilicon gates suffer a carrier-depletion effect that increases effective gate-dielectric thickness, while conventional tungsten gates require a highly resistive tungsten nucleation layer that degrades performance as gate dimensions shrink. Cobalt and metal silicides are described as lower-resistivity alternatives with good TiN adhesion, corrosion resistance, and smoother films.

Using FinFETs as the primary example, the fabrication sequence forms fins by recessing STI regions, creates a dummy gate stack and spacers, recesses the fins, and grows or implants source/drain epitaxy regions. ILD and a contact etch-stop layer are then formed and planarized. After removing the dummy gate, a replacement gate dielectric comprising an interfacial oxide and high-k dielectric is formed, followed by diffusion-barrier, work-function, and TiN barrier layers. A metal-containing layer is deposited over the barrier and may be homogeneous cobalt or a metal silicide, or may comprise two layers in either order. One example uses lower cobalt-silicide and upper substantially silicon-free cobalt layers, formed by lowering or gradually reducing the wafer temperature during deposition. The deposited layers are planarized, recessed, and capped with a hard mask.

Source/drain and gate contact plugs are then formed using metal, barrier, and cobalt-containing or metal-silicide layers. Additional ILD and an etch-stop layer receive vias containing barrier and metal-containing material. The disclosed methods and devices apply these materials to the gate electrode, source/drain contact plug, or gate contact plug, with planar transistors also able to use the concepts described.

OpenAI’s invite-only iOS app, powered by Sora 2, lets users create digital avatars and share AI-generated videos of themselves and friends through a TikTok-like feed. The app generates scripts, visuals, and sound, while users control who may use their likeness and can monitor clips featuring them. Testing found many videos convincing but imperfect, with some prompts involving suggestive material, self-harm, public figures, and copyrighted characters blocked while others were permitted. OpenAI says safeguards address deepfake misuse, sexual content, graphic violence, extremism, hate, and self-harm, though restrictions remain inconsistent.

The TMS320DM814x DaVinci device provides 128 hardware spinlocks for synchronizing multiple processes through single-read lock operations, avoiding unsupported read-modify-write bus transfers. Its Mailbox module supports communication among the ARM Cortex-A8, C674x DSP, and Media Controller using interrupt-signaled messages, flexible queue assignment, four-message FIFO queues, and overflow notification.

A unified memory map covers on-chip memories and peripherals. Separate maps describe L3, L4 fast and slow peripheral domains, the C674x DSP’s limited peripheral access, and Cortex-A8-decoded regions. The DDR DMM TILER also provides a 4-GB extended range using a 33rd address bit for rotated and mirrored frame-buffer views; this full range is accessible only to HDVPSS and ISS, while other masters can access one view through the 512-MB base-map region.

Device pin tables describe terminal functions, multiplexing, pin and ball numbers, electrical types, internal or external pull requirements, supply voltages, PINCNTL control registers, de-selected input states, and multimuxed options. Interfaces covered include boot configuration, camera, CAN, DDR2/DDR3, Ethernet, GPIO, GPMC, HDMI, I2C, McASP, PCIe, reset/interrupt/JTAG, SD, SPI, clocks, timers, UART, USB, video input/output, and power supplies.

BTMODE inputs are sampled when reset is released and control the boot sequence and related GPMC, EMAC, XIP, and PCIe options. The ROM configures pins for NAND, I2C, MMC/SD, SPI, EMAC, PCIe, and UART boot modes. PINCNTL1–PINCNTL270 MUXMODE registers control pin multiplexing; the default mode tri-states pins, while some functions permit routing to multiple device pins. Unused inputs should not float, most pins have internal pullup or pulldown resistors, and all supply pins require the correct voltage even when associated interfaces are unused.

Four experiments in the US and India found that parents favored same-gender children when allocating money or prizes: mothers chose daughters and fathers chose sons. The researchers attributed this to identification with same-gender children and suggested gift-giving reinforces parental identity. More than 90% of participants nevertheless claimed not to prefer one child over another.

The application claims priority to U.S. Provisional Application No. 62/474,562, filed March 21, 2017, titled “OFF-ROAD UTILITY VEHICLE,” and incorporates co-filed Application No. 62/474,556, “Cab and Fasteners for Vehicle Cab.” It describes side-by-side recreational off-highway vehicles, noting their multiple seating, automobile-like controls, and ability to traverse harsh terrain, while identifying vehicle geometry, suspension, clearance, wheelbase, center of gravity, and power as factors affecting ride, reliability, maintenance, terrain capability, and cargo capacity.

The disclosed utility vehicle includes a body, frame, ground-engaging members, an optional rear cargo box, two- or four-wheel drive, side-by-side seating, fuel system, receiver hitch, lighting, doors, rollover protection structure, steering, front and rear suspensions, drivetrain, continuously variable transmission, brake pedal assembly, steering and gear-selector column, floorboards, and removable seats. The summarized embodiment specifically provides a longitudinal centerline and a rear suspension whose left A-arm has a pivot axis positioned to the right of that centerline. The description and figures elaborate frame construction, ROPS connections, adjustable seats, anti-roll bars, damping components, steering hardware, vibration-isolated driveline, CVT housing, flywheel sensor, brake-fluid system, steering tilt, gear selection, floorboard drainage, traction features, and seat removal and stowage.

Several universities, including MIT, Columbia, Michigan, and Rochester Institute of Technology, are piloting online MicroMasters courses in fields such as supply chain management, entrepreneurship, UI design, and AI. MIT’s one-year supply chain program normally costs $67,938, while its certification costs $1,350. The certificate is not a degree; students seeking a graduate degree must complete an on-campus semester at full cost. MIT expects to admit only 40 students annually to its blended program and will consider their online-course performance. Participants gain skills valued by employers, and GE, Walmart, IBM, and Volvo recognize or promote the courses. Universities can use performance in the courses to assess applicants more reliably.

A speaker anticipates an exciting game against former Colorado teammates, praises the fans’ support, and values the opportunity to play for them. They recall hoping the players would compete together after the Olympics and say the trade benefited Colorado by adding leadership, raising expectations, and demonstrating the value of hard work and teamwork.

The coaching staff said their loss was not caused by goaltending, noting their goalie had a solid game while Pekka Rinne was excellent. They said Kris Letang will not return for the series. Archie was added to provide energy, speed, and enthusiasm, while Carter Rowney has contributed strong center play, faceoffs, size, penalty killing, and physicality. The staff viewed the previous game as one of the team’s strongest performances in the series despite missed scoring chances. They plan to continue adjusting lines to create balance and secondary scoring, believing that spreading talent among combinations makes the team harder to play against. They acknowledged some preventable goals, considered the game closer than the score, and expected players due for goals to score.

RTX Blackwell builds on NVIDIA’s AI foundations with neural rendering and shading. DLSS Super Resolution, Frame Generation, and Ray Reconstruction boost performance and image quality, while generative AI supports dynamic content, realistic simulations, and multiple 3D design options. The architecture honors mathematician and statistician David H. Blackwell.

Developed and refined by Tom Davis, the Boston zone offense gained national exposure while he coached Boston College. It uses five specialized roles—O1 through O5—without positional interchange; players simply flip sides, allowing greater efficiency in their assigned roles. The offense emphasizes a strong low-post attack, dribble entries, fast tempo, and both overloading and spreading the zone.

O1 is the primary ballhandler, O2 the top-of-circle shooter, O3 the baseline shooter, O4 the weakside rebounder, and O5 the primary post scorer. Sharp, accurate ball movement, including skip passes, post feeds, reversals, and pump-fake passes, creates defensive breakdowns and open shots. Players should avoid forced passes and unnecessary dribbling.

Ball reversals trigger coordinated wing and baseline movement. Give-and-go cuts and flash entries create passing and scoring options. Post feeds exploit how zone defenders position themselves, while baseline runs force difficult matchup decisions. When passes are denied or overplayed, counters include skip passes, cross-court “X” passes, backcuts, drop passes, dribble penetration, and kick-out opportunities. The system includes reads and counters against 2-3, 1-2-2, and 1-3-1 zones.

Hawaiʻi is expanding charter preschools to advance its goal of giving all 3- and 4-year-olds access to preschool by 2032. Charter schools currently operate 33 preschool classrooms, while roughly 6,700 children lack access, requiring about 330 additional classrooms over seven years.

Waikīkī Community Preschool became the state’s first private preschool to convert to a charter. State funding made it tuition-free, improved teacher recruitment and allowed it to reach full capacity, serving 98 children with a waitlist of 10 to 30. Charter preschool teachers are state employees with K-12 salary and benefit levels, but licensing requirements are harder to fill amid staffing shortages.

The charter model provides stable funding, but $171,000 per classroom does not cover staffing, rent and facilities. Waikīkī expects a $150,000 to $200,000 shortfall, while Parkway Village Preschool faces deficits of $50,000 to $60,000 per classroom. Both rely on nonprofit fundraising and support.

Only two private programs applied to become charters, and one application was denied. Conversion may preserve existing seats rather than create new ones. The state is also planning 15 more charter preschool classrooms by fall 2028 and received $20 million for construction, though private-property charter sites generally cannot use those funds.

STAT’s “Up and down the ladder” feature highlights pharmaceutical personnel moves, including enGene’s hiring of Hussein Sweiti as chief medical officer. Sweiti previously led oncology clinical development at Johnson & Johnson. The full article is exclusive to STAT+ subscribers.

PIM Capital is presented as PAN Finance’s Fund Structuring Partner of the Year for Mauritius and South Africa, specializing in alternative investments and cross-border fund structuring and administration across emerging markets. It emphasizes locally attuned, flexible solutions for complex jurisdictions, including grey-listing environments, varied regulations and currency volatility.

The firm’s hands-on approach focuses on upfront planning, selecting appropriate jurisdictions and designing operational structures that support long-term flexibility and reduce costly restructuring. PIM Capital works with family offices, wealth managers, large global asset managers and emerging private wealth firms, offering tailored fund structures through offices in Sub-Saharan Africa, Mauritius and Guernsey. Its teams also provide financial-services expertise in the Global North.

PIM Capital differentiates itself from traditional administrators by accepting unusual opportunities, dedicating time to client-specific “solutioneering” and treating fund managers as partners. It may absorb initial costs or reduce upfront fees to build long-term relationships and prioritizes shared growth over immediate margins. Christopher Erasmus, who leads the Mauritius team, specializes in fund and corporate structuring, global markets, tax strategies and asset protection.

Amazon.com, Inc. filed a Form 8-K (dated June 1, 2018) reporting the results of its Annual Meeting of Shareholders held May 30, 2018. Under Item 5.07, all ten director nominees — Jeffrey P. Bezos, Tom A. Alberg, Jamie S. Gorelick, Daniel P. Huttenlocher, Judith A. McGrath, Jonathan J. Rubinstein, Thomas O. Ryder, Patricia Q. Stonesifer and Wendell P. Weeks — were elected to serve until the next annual meeting or until their successors are elected and qualified. The appointment of Ernst & Young LLP as independent auditors for the fiscal year ending December 31, 2018 was ratified, and the advisory vote on named executive officer compensation was approved. Two shareholder proposals were rejected: one requiring an independent board chair and one addressing vote-counting practices for shareholder proposals. Broker non-votes totaled 77,060,068 on the director, compensation and shareholder proposal votes. The report was signed by David A. Zapolsky, Senior Vice President.

Day trading can be profitable, but the author considers it difficult, risky, and unlikely to succeed without years of preparation, patience, strict discipline, and a willingness to learn from mistakes. Novices should start with swing trading, which allows positions to be held for days or weeks and benefits from longer market trends. The author reports profitable stock trading from 2002 to May 2012, with the best 1% of trading days generating 11% of total profits, although performance deteriorated over time and required research, new strategies, and psychological adaptation to larger drawdowns.

Automated or algorithmic trading has changed market conditions, reducing liquidity, increasing rapid price movements, and making fast execution important. The author explores strategies less affected by algorithms, including automation and mean reversion, despite their longer losing periods. Negatively skewed strategies are warned against because rare large losses can erase many gains.

Court records concerning the failed Tuco Trading firm reportedly showed poor profitability among its traders. According to the author, most day traders fail because the work demands constant discipline, difficult decisions, and psychological resilience; short-term trading is described as roughly zero-sum. Profits should be protected, losses controlled, and exceptional trading days managed carefully.

FPI demand for corporate bond limits exceeded the notified Rs 3,360 crore, with 58 bidders bidding Rs 5,898 crore. Cut-off and highest bids were 15.25 and 25 basis points, respectively, compared with 1.20 and three basis points for G-secs. For G-secs, 37 bidders bid Rs 7,116 crore against Rs 5,481 crore notified. It was the second corporate bond auction this fiscal year.

The article describes Turnaround Tuesday, a strategy based on market reversals from Monday’s close through at least Tuesday’s close. SPY backtests indicate that buying weakness on Mondays—particularly when Monday closes at least 1% below Friday—and selling at Tuesday’s close has been profitable for roughly 30 years. Monday-close entries performed about twice as well as Tuesday-close entries, while buying strength on Mondays was unprofitable. Filters such as Intraday Breadth Strength can improve results. The effect was illustrated by Black Monday on October 19, 1987, followed by Tuesday and Wednesday gains of 5.3% and 9.1%. The strategy has favorable risk and reward but works best on weak Mondays and requires caution amid macro and geopolitical risks.

Allen and Carter negotiated a U.S.–Hawaiian reciprocity treaty, signed January 30, 1875, and effective September 9, 1876 after Congress acted on customs dues. Britain and initially Germany disputed the 1852 treaty’s “parity” or “favored nation” clause; Carter successfully opposed Germany’s claim. Britain’s proposed 10 percent duty on free-schedule imports was rejected, and after debate and a ministry change, Hawaii acknowledged U.S. exclusive privileges and pledged to uphold the treaty. An annexation scare prompted Evarts to deny further U.S. ambitions.

Over the next three years, treaty, customs, fraud, and British-claim disputes were settled diplomatically. A domestic scandal brought ministerial changes and a briefly rescinded recall request, supporting charges of corruption and opposition to extending the treaty. The United States also assisted with liquor restrictions in the Ralik Islands and a Hawaiian-Japanese treaty. In June 1881, Comly reported continued British efforts to invoke parity, citing an 1855 concession that Britain could not claim equal trade advantages under the 1852 treaty.

Femtosecond noise correlation spectroscopy (FemNoC) was used to measure spontaneous magnetization fluctuations in the canted antiferromagnet Sm₀.₇Er₀.₃FeO₃ across its temperature-driven spin reorientation transition (SRT). By correlating Faraday-rotation noise from consecutive probe pulses, the experiment quantified quasi-ferromagnetic (qF) magnon fluctuations and random telegraph noise while also determining the net magnetization angle. Results were compared with atomistic spin-noise and Monte Carlo simulations.

At low fields, magnetization rotates from the crystallographic a-axis toward the c-axis, with experimental critical temperatures near 299 and 321 K. Near the lower transition, the qF mode variance increases and its resonance softens as the free-energy potential broadens; switching between degenerate states produces random telegraph noise. A c-axis magnetic field deflects the magnetization, shifts the SRT onset to lower temperatures, and suppresses the enhanced variance and mode softening, particularly above about 60 mT.

Field scans show hysteretic behavior associated with magnetic domains. Increasing the field systematically reduces qF magnon noise and raises its frequency, consistent with field-induced stiffening of the free-energy potential. Atomistic and Monte Carlo simulations reproduce the principal temperature and field trends, linking fluctuation amplitude to free-energy curvature. The findings demonstrate that FemNoC can map magnetization potentials and enable external control of picosecond spin fluctuations for high-frequency, low-noise spintronic devices.

The invention describes camera-module packaging using molded bases instead of conventional holders. Conventional integral encapsulation presents mass-production problems because square or prismatic light windows and mold blocks create friction, deformation, flashes, and damage during demoulding, while straight inner walls may reflect stray light onto the photosensitive element and degrade image quality.

The invention integrally molds a base onto a circuit board, or onto a circuit board and photosensitive element, with a non-prismatic light window. Sloped or multi-step inner surfaces, inclined outer surfaces, and prescribed acute inclination angles facilitate demoulding, reduce friction and damage, maintain mounting areas for lenses, actuators, and filters, and reduce stray-light interference. The molded base can replace a conventional holder, protect electronic components from dust, and support fixed- or automatic-focus modules.

Manufacturing uses first and second molds containing a light-window forming block and surrounding base-forming guide groove. Liquid molding material is introduced into the groove, solidified, and demolded. The forming block has a trapezoidal or multi-step trapezoidal cross section that widens upward to assist release. The process accommodates individual circuit boards and joint arrays for separated or multi-window camera modules. The modules may be incorporated into phones, computers, televisions, wearables, vehicles, cameras, and monitoring devices.

In this guest lecture for MIT 2.830J (Control of Manufacturing Processes), David Hardt recasts the course's process-control framework from a mechanical engineering perspective. He models a manufacturing process as equipment plus material plus their interaction, described as a directed energy exchange that transforms the material's geometry (and sometimes its properties), with output geometry and properties expressed as a function of process parameters. The energy exchange may be mechanical, electrical, thermal, or chemical, and its location and intensity determine the result: a point source (e.g., a laser) acts locally and is moved around the part, while a shaped tool or mold imposes a distributed field everywhere at once.

Hardt classifies all geometry-changing processes into four modes: removal (machining, etching, oxidation), addition (coating, 3D printing), formation (solidification against a form, as in casting or stereolithography), and deformation (bending, without adding or removing material). Examples discussed include orthogonal turning, where material leaves at the point of maximum shear stress; injection molding, where heat and pressure act against the mold; laser processing with femtosecond lasers; chemical vapor deposition, where the substrate's topology governs where material deposits; and rolling, where the roll gap controls thickness while roll shape and camber control thickness distribution (the Alcoa Tennessee cold rolling mill for beer-can stock must hold roughly 15-micron tolerances, achieved with roll camber plus local heating or cooling).

From the area of the energy interaction relative to the area being changed, Hardt derives a serial versus parallel taxonomy. Serial processes (femtosecond laser machining, CNC machining, robotic work, 3D printing) involve a small interaction area moved along a trajectory; parallel processes (stamping, hot isostatic pressing, molding, lithography) involve simultaneous interaction over the whole area. Rolling is mixed. The distinction determines control strategy: in serial processes the dominant knob is the trajectory of the tool, whereas in parallel processes the knob is the shape of the energy distributor (mold, mask, pattern, heat distribution). Examples of the taxonomy include cutting, grinding, polishing, water-jet and wire EDM (serial mechanical/electrical removal), photolithography with wet etch and CMP (parallel), HIP (parallel addition), and stereolithography, in which UV-curable polymer is solidified by a scanning laser in liquid (serial chemical formation).

Choosing an energy mode matters because processes differ in rate, cost, quality, and flexibility. Mechanical actions are fast and interruptible; thermal and chemical ones are slower and harder to stop. Quality depends on side effects and on diffusion—mechanical stress fields, heat dissipation, and chemical undercutting—which limit achievable feature size and precision—plus repeatability, which depends on interfaces and on tool wear. Serial processes are generally the most flexible, since a CNC machine's trajectory can be reprogrammed with near-zero changeover, whereas parallel processes are locked to expensive tooling. Removal processes are least sensitive to material properties (machining is a nearly pure geometry change), while deformation is highly sensitive to material variation; deposition processes are insensitive to part size, since the substrate rather than the tool determines the geometry.

The lecture closes with sources of variation. Hardt partitions parameters into equipment properties (stiffness, straightness, thermal expansion, machine geometry), equipment states (forces, pressures, temperatures, flows, velocities), material properties, and material states. Equipment states are generally well controlled thanks to CNC, servo, and temperature regulation, while equipment properties are uncertain owing to build quality, degradation, and tool wear. Material properties vary substantially—for example, aluminum from different mills differs by about 10% in yield strength and strain-hardening behavior, which spoils bending control but not machining. Material states are often unknown, as when a polymer is pulled from a 100 °C oven: its temperature at forming is unmeasured, and in injection molding the melt temperature in the mold is known only via embedded sensors, though pressure can also be measured. His conclusion is that the largest sources of variation are material uncertainties and the uncertain coupling at the energy–material interface, whereas what is typically manipulated in practice are equipment states; the remaining lecture notes cover the machining, turning, blending, and molding processes in detail.

The speaker expresses joy at being part of a group where many players returned from the prior year, describing the challenge and reward of attempting to go back-to-back. He praises a competitive team that cares about individual and group play, with everyone willing to do what it takes. The group absorbed the loss of a heavy-minute player without being intimidated, and players stepping into the lineup, including Dales' absence, plus newly acquired veterans performed well. He highlights coach Geno and two goaltenders who "stole" playoff games, including Mur, who kept the team in during the Washington series, and young Guentz's scoring. He also describes passing the cup to a long-time player who had yet to appear in a playoff game, calling it special for both of them.

The lecture explains interactions between neutral atoms through dipole fluctuations and virtual photons. Classically, neutral atoms have no direct Coulomb attraction: after a multipole expansion, the leading dipole interaction scales as \(1/R^3\), but classical fluctuations cost more energy than the interaction provides. Quantum zero-point motion makes \(\langle d^2\rangle\) nonzero, allowing correlated dipole fluctuations and producing a second-order van der Waals potential proportional to \(1/R^6\). First-order perturbation gives a \(C_3/R^3\) interaction when one atom is excited.

A coupled-oscillator model, illustrated with coupled LC circuits, reproduces the \(R^{-6}\) result through shifted normal modes and zero-point energy. Alternatively, quantum electromagnetic vacuum fluctuations can induce correlated dipoles in both atoms; summing over field modes yields a retarded \(1/R^7\) potential, called the Casimir–Polder potential. The transition between short- and long-range behavior occurs when the separation becomes comparable to an atom’s resonant wavelength.

In the QED treatment, neutral atoms have no remaining direct longitudinal Coulomb interaction, so their interaction must arise through the quantized radiation field. Fourth-order diagrams describe virtual-photon exchanges that return both atoms to their ground states. At short range, high-frequency photons dominate and the exchanges are effectively sequential, yielding \(R^{-6}\). At long range, atomic excitation energies dominate and two photons are effectively exchanged nearly simultaneously, adding another inverse-distance factor and producing \(R^{-7}\).

This cross-sectional study examined Kuwait University Faculty of Education staff’s perceptions of AI’s potential and challenges in education. An online survey of 63 randomly selected academic staff and administrators used established measures of AI attitudes, teacher perspectives, student empowerment, challenges, educational scenarios, and applications.

Faculty showed moderate overall acceptance of AI, strong belief that it would benefit humanity, and limited prior teaching experience with AI. Data analysis, machine learning, and natural language processing were identified as important links between education and AI. Respondents also emphasized student abilities to identify AI use cases, assess system intelligence, and recognize technical limitations. Challenges were rated highly, particularly insufficient teaching materials, limited expertise, subject complexity, and lack of practical examples. AI educational scenarios—including personalized intelligent teaching, smart schools, and remote education—received high ratings. Inferential tests found no significant differences by gender, academic degree, or department.

The study concluded that AI presents substantial educational potential but requires reforms, teacher preparation, suitable materials, and technologically aligned pedagogy. Limitations included excluding student perspectives and restricting the sample to one university; future research was recommended across multiple institutions.

Lectures 7 and 8 introduce economics’ expected-utility framework for analyzing risk. Many choices involve uncertainty, including education, housing, farming, business decisions, investments, health decisions, and everyday behaviors. People can reduce risk exposure through insurance, informal assistance, or avoidance. Risk aversion may reflect diminishing marginal utility of wealth, loss aversion, minimum consumption needs, anxiety, regret, disappointment relative to expectations, and the difficulty of contingent planning. People generally accept risk when compensation is high enough, yet some voluntarily engage in negative-expected-return gambling, lotteries, and sports betting.

Expected utility assigns utility to final outcomes and evaluates lotteries as probability-weighted averages of those utilities. Expected monetary value instead weights monetary payoffs. A linear utility function represents risk neutrality, a concave function risk aversion, and a convex function risk lovingness. Risk-averse expected-utility maximizers reject all fair gambles. The model assumes that only final outcomes matter and that probabilities enter linearly, thereby excluding considerations such as expectations, reference points, anxiety, stress, and regret. This can make behavior that seems irrational from the model’s perspective— such as regret-driven rejection of additional lottery tickets—appear inexplicable.

Economists measure risk aversion using absolute and relative coefficients, often represented by the CRRA utility function and its parameter, gamma. Risk aversion can be estimated from certainty equivalents, choices between gambles, or real-world insurance decisions. Constant relative risk aversion also implies a constant allocation of wealth to risky assets.

The lecture highlights a central inconsistency. Large-stakes certainty equivalents suggest a relative risk-aversion parameter around 0–2 and generally below 10. By contrast, rejecting a 50–50 bet to gain $11 and lose $10 implies gamma above 18. Rabin’s result shows that, for any weakly concave expected-utility function, consistently rejecting this small gamble implies extremely rapid declines in marginal utility and implausible aversion to larger gambles. A single risk-aversion parameter therefore cannot reconcile sensible small- and large-scale risk choices. The lecture suggests that reference dependence and loss aversion, which introduce additional parameters, may better explain the pattern.

Finally, the lecture describes Sydnor’s use of roughly 50,000 home-insurance policies. The data record customers’ available premium-deductible menus, selected policies, and subsequent claims, allowing researchers to bound or estimate risk aversion from real choices. Low claim rates and data on both new and long-term customers help address uncertainty about customers’ actual and perceived risks. The analysis of insurance choices will continue in the next lecture.

Sears borrowed $100 million from Eddie Lampert’s ESL Investments, which agreed to lend up to $100 million more. Lampert’s fund has loaned the retailer nearly $2 billion over two years amid declining mall traffic and e-commerce competition.

CSUSB veteran students described military tuition benefits. Active-duty members may receive tuition assistance up to $4,500 annually, though service obligations can interrupt school. The Post-9/11 GI Bill offers eligible members and veterans who served at least 90 days up to four years of benefits for college or certificate programs; after leaving service, benefits must generally be used within 10–15 years. Public-school tuition is paid in full, with payments based on active-duty months and credits. The Montgomery GI Bill provides similar benefits but requires full-time students to pay educational expenses; full-time students receive $1,857, while part-time students receive half.

On January 16, 1945, preparation of background memoranda for President Roosevelt and the American delegation to the Malta and Yalta Conferences was completed, and the resulting “Yalta Briefing Book” was presented shortly afterward. In a subsequent conversation, Leo Pasvolsky discussed Dumbarton Oaks proposals with the Soviet ambassador, who wanted clarification before departing for Moscow. Pasvolsky explained the proposal concerning regional peaceful settlement, while the ambassador sought to understand the arguments supporting the voting formula. The ambassador considered the International Court issue substantively settled. On dependent areas, Pasvolsky outlined alternatives involving trust and colonial areas, international trusteeship, regional commissions, and international accountability, noting the Philippines as a desirable approach. Only international trusteeship was viewed as properly belonging on the United Nations Conference agenda, although colonial issues might be addressed elsewhere or through the future international organization’s General Assembly or Economic and Social Council.

The Texas Court of Criminal Appeals held that Wells’s appeal bond was insufficient because it lacked approval from the trial judge and instead was approved by a special judge. After Wells’s embezzlement conviction and two-year sentence, his appeal was dismissed.

The Indiana Supreme Court affirmed Shircliff’s conviction for conspiring to bribe township trustee Valentine Strange to employ Edward O’Connor as a teacher and retain $50 from his wages. The indictment was sufficient without alleging that a school position was vacant because trustees have a legal duty to employ teachers, and the conspiracy did not need to be consummated. Issues concerning continuance and evidence were not reviewable because the bill of exceptions was untimely filed. O’Connor’s discharge as a State witness could not be challenged for the first time on appeal. The court presumed that the first special judge was unable to preside, validating the second special judge’s appointment and judgment.

House Democratic Leader Hakeem Jeffries rejected a GOP-backed spending proposal and said Democrats will not support it. Democrats insist any agreement to avert a government shutdown at 12:01 a.m. Wednesday must extend enhanced Obamacare tax credits scheduled to expire at the end of 2025. Republicans want negotiations on continuing the credits to occur after the Senate approves a funding resolution. Trump is scheduled to meet with Jeffries, Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer, House Speaker Mike Johnson and Senate Majority Leader John Thune at 3 p.m. At least seven Senate Democrats would need to vote with Republicans for shutdown legislation to pass.

H&M’s March local-currency sales rose 6%, below its preliminary reading, further clouding its 10%–15% full-year growth target after local sales fell in February for the first time in four years. Analysts cited intense competition from Primark and online retailers and questioned rapid store expansion in the crowded value-fashion market. H&M had 4,426 stores at March’s end, up 11% year over year, while expanding e-commerce and higher-priced brands that remain a small share of turnover. It is also investing in a more flexible Asian supply chain.

Microsoft Corporation filed its Form 10-K annual report for the fiscal year ended June 30, 2022. Its common stock and two note series were listed on Nasdaq. As of December 31, 2021, non-affiliates held common stock valued at $2.5 trillion, and 7,457,891,872 shares were outstanding as of July 25, 2022. The filing cautions that forward-looking statements depend on assumptions and are subject to risks and uncertainties.

Microsoft describes its mission as empowering every person and organization to achieve more. Its research and development priorities include reinventing productivity and business processes, building intelligent cloud and edge platforms, and creating more personal computing.
