Its portfolio includes Microsoft 365, Teams, LinkedIn, Dynamics 365, Azure and other cloud services, GitHub, Nuance, Windows, Surface devices, Xbox products and services, and search and news advertising. It completed the Nuance acquisition in March 2022, announced plans to acquire Activision Blizzard in January 2022, and acquired advertising technology company Xandr on June 6, 2022.

The company reports through three operating segments: Productivity and Business Processes, Intelligent Cloud, and More Personal Computing. These segments include Office and collaboration services, LinkedIn and Dynamics; Azure, server products, GitHub, Nuance, and enterprise services; and Windows, devices, gaming, and advertising. A March 9, 1943 draft declaration distinguished mandated or detached territories, proposed placing only those under international trusteeship, suggested regional commissions for colonial areas, and called for progressive self-government and fixed schedules for colonial independence. NVIDIA’s Turing GPU architecture introduces hybrid rendering, combining rasterization, real-time ray tracing, AI, and simulation. RT Cores in each Streaming Multiprocessor handle BVH traversal and ray-triangle intersection testing, freeing the SM for shading and compute work. Combined with BVH acceleration and denoising, they deliver roughly ten times the ray-tracing performance of Pascal, which performed these operations in software on CUDA cores. Ray-traced shadows, ambient occlusion, and reflections can run in real time on a single Quadro RTX 6000 or GeForce RTX 2080 Ti.

Ray tracing casts rays backward from the camera through scene pixels to determine intersections, lighting, reflections, refractions, shadows, and indirect illumination. Bounding Volume Hierarchies reduce intersection tests by organizing geometry within nested bounding boxes, while denoising allows fewer rays and lower sample counts to produce high-quality results. Ray-traced shadows can reproduce physically correct contact hardening, ray-traced ambient occlusion adds realistic environmental definition, and ray-traced reflections avoid artifacts and limitations associated with screen-space reflections and static cubemap probes.

NVIDIA NGX is a Turing-only, deep-learning technology stack that uses Tensor Cores to accelerate client-side graphics, rendering, and AI services. Its Deep Learning Super-Sampling (DLSS) network is trained against 64-times-supersampled references, allowing lower-resolution rendering while producing results similar to Temporal Anti-Aliasing with about half the shading work. Standard DLSS reportedly gives the RTX 2080 Ti twice the performance of the GTX 1080 Ti, while DLSS 2X renders at target resolution and uses a larger network to approximate 64-times-supersampled quality. Other NGX features include AI Inpainting, AI Slow-Mo for interpolated video frames, and AI Super Rez for 2x, 4x, or 8x resolution enhancement.

Mesh Shading adds Task and Mesh Shader stages that cooperatively process object lists and generate triangles. This removes per-object CPU draw calls, enables more than an order of magnitude more objects to be rendered in real time, supports dynamic level-of-detail selection, and permits geometry manipulations such as spherical cutaways in CAD models.

Variable Rate Shading (VRS) allows each 16-by-16-pixel region to use a different shading rate, with developers selecting among seven rate options. It supports content-adaptive shading for spatially or temporally uniform regions, motion-adaptive shading for moving objects, and foveated rendering that shades peripheral areas less heavily. VRS can also increase shading up to the MSAA sample count.

Texture Space Shading stores dynamically computed shading values in texture-space texels, decoupling visibility and appearance sampling from the screen-space pixel grid. Previously shaded texels can be reused within or across frames, improving temporal stability and helping VR applications remain within fixed rendering budgets. In stereo VR, one eye’s completed shading can be reused for the other, with additional shading performed only for previously unseen content.

Multi-View Rendering draws multiple viewpoints or character instances in one pass. Turing supports up to four hardware views per pass and up to 32 views through the API, while sharing independent shader work across views. Applications include single-pass stereo and multi-projection VR, canted high-field-of-view HMD displays, multiple shadow maps, and rendering several poses from one mesh.

Turing also extends DX12 resource access with bindless constant-buffer and unordered-access views, supports mixed resource types within the same heap, and retains Tier 2 resource-heap support. VR features include USB Type-C and VirtualLink connectivity, expanded Multi-View Rendering, foveated shading, and RT Core acceleration of NVIDIA VRWorks Audio ray-traced sound.

RTX-OPS is presented as a workload-based hybrid-rendering metric. A representative Turing frame spends about 20 percent of its time on DLSS and 80 percent on rendering, with ray tracing accounting for roughly half of FP32 shading time. The metric weights tensor operations at 20 percent, FP32 operations at 80 percent, RT operations at 40 percent, and INT32 operations at 28 percent, yielding 78 RTX-OPS for the RTX 2080 Ti under these assumptions.

## Summary

The passage covers container design patterns and distributed system architectures, moving from single-node patterns to multi-node distributed patterns.

**Ambassador pattern:** Introduced as a single-node pattern in which an ambassador container brokers interactions between the application container and the outside world, forming a tightly coupled pair scheduled to one machine. Its value lies in modular, reusable containers and separation of concerns, speeding development and producing more consistent, higher-quality implementations. Three applications are described: (1) *Client-side sharding* — sharding splits a storage layer into disjoint pieces across machines; routing logic can either live in the sharded service with its own stateless load balancer (a distributed ambassador) or in a client-side ambassador proxy, each with deployment trade-offs; with the client-side approach the application connects to what appears to be a single storage backend on localhost, while the proxy routes requests to the appropriate shard. A hands-on example deploys sharded Redis using a Kubernetes StatefulSet (three redis containers), a Kubernetes Service for per-replica DNS names, and twemproxy as the ambassador, configured via a ConfigMap and serving the Redis protocol on localhost:6379. (2) *Service brokering* — portable applications need service discovery, so an ambassador introspects its environment and brokers the appropriate connection (e.g., SaaS MySQL in a public cloud versus a spun-up MySQL in a private cloud) while the application always connects to localhost. (3) *Experimentation/request splitting* — an ambassador proxies requests to both production and experimental implementations, returning only production responses; nginx is configured with IP hashing for user consistency and a weight parameter sending 90% of traffic to production and 10% to the experiment; it can alternatively be deployed as a separate microservice.

**Adapter pattern:** The adapter container modifies the application container's interface so it conforms to a predefined interface, addressing the heterogeneity of real-world applications written in various languages with different conventions. Applications include: *monitoring*, where the adapter transforms the application's monitoring interface into that expected by a general-purpose monitoring system (decoupling, reuse, and dedicated CPU/memory per container) — demonstrated by adding the open source `oliver006/redis_exporter` to a Redis pod so Prometheus can scrape it; *logging*, where the adapter redirects logs to stdout and normalizes formats into one structured representation, preferred over modifying a third-party image (patching/rebasing is expensive and prevents reuse) — demonstrated with fluentd plus the `fluent-plugin-redis-slowlog` plugin to capture Redis SLOWLOG entries and, similarly, `fluent-plugin-storm` for Apache Storm's REST API; and *health checks*, where an adapter container holds a shell script or Go program performing rich diagnostic queries against an off-the-shelf database (e.g., MySQL) and exposes an HTTP health check, leaving the original image unchanged and making the solution shareable by teams without deep database knowledge.

**Microservices and multi-node patterns:** Single-node patterns are building blocks for larger, more loosely coupled multi-node systems whose components communicate over the network with parallel calls and loose synchronization. Microservices (components communicating over defined APIs) contrast with monoliths, offering reliability and agility — smaller "two pizza" teams, formal APIs as stable contracts, independent release schedules, and independent scaling per component — but making debugging and architecture harder. Patterns ease both by codifying design practices and sharing lessons.

**Replicated load-balanced services:** Identical servers behind a load balancer (round-robin or session stickiness) provide stateless services. Replication supplies redundancy and scale; at least two replicas are needed for high availability, and achieving a three-nines SLA with a single instance would require rollouts in under 1.4 minutes (or 3.6 seconds with hourly deployments). Readiness probes signal when an application is initialized and able to serve, distinct from health probes that trigger restarts. A hands-on example deploys a NodeJS dictionary server as a Kubernetes Deployment with a Service acting as the load balancer. *Session tracked services* route a user's requests to one replica (by hashing source/destination IPs), though NAT breaks IP-based tracking externally, so application-level tracking such as cookies is preferred; consistent hashing minimizes remapping during scaling. *Application-layer refinements* include a caching tier (Varnish) — deployed as a separate replicated tier of few large replicas rather than sidecars, because caching every page in many replicas reduces hit rate — which then breaks IP affinity and requires cookie or header-based session tracking. The edge layer also provides rate limiting and DoS defense (throttling by IP and path, lower anonymous limits, login for higher limits, HTTP 429 responses, remaining-calls headers) and SSL termination via nginx, since Varnish cannot terminate SSL, producing a three-layer stack of nginx, Varnish, and the web app deployed as three Kubernetes Deployments with Services.

**Sharded services:** Unlike replicated services, each shard serves only a subset of requests, with a root distributing them; sharding supports stateful services whose data exceeds one machine. A sharded cache stores unique data per shard, raising memory utilization (e.g., 50% of the data set versus 5% in an equivalent replicated deployment) while serving the same request rate. Cache hit rate defines system capacity and latency, so capacity should be rated below maximum and the system load-tested with and without caches. Because a request always maps to one shard, shard failures and upgrades lose capacity; therefore each shard can be a replicated service, enabling failure tolerance, rollouts under load, and "hot sharding" where overloaded shards are scaled or moved (shard A replicated to a second machine while B and C are combined). A hands-on example deploys sharded memcache with a StatefulSet, a Service for DNS names, and a twemproxy ambassador on localhost:11211, or alternatively a shared replicated shard-routing service that reduces complexity but adds an extra network hop and must be scaled. *Sharding functions* map requests to shards using hash plus modulo (`hash(Req) % 10`), requiring determinism and uniformity; key selection matters, since hashing the entire request over-distinguishes, hashing only the path is too general when location matters, and a better compromise is `shard(country(ip), path)`. Re-sharding with modulo remaps nearly all keys, so consistent hashing functions are used to remap only about K/11 keys when going from 10 to 11 shards, implemented via nginx's consistent hash on the full request URI.

**Scatter/gather:** A root simultaneously farms each request out to all leaves, each performing partial work and returning partial results that the root combines — parallelizing computation rather than data, equivalent to an embarrassingly parallel problem (60 seconds of work across 30 cores yields 2 seconds), and extending parallelism across machines so CPU rather than memory, network, or disk is the bottleneck and load can be dynamically shifted away from slow nodes. A document-search example indexes words as hashtable keys, fans "cat" and "dog" out to separate leaves, and intersects the returned document sets at the root. With *leaf sharding*, data too large for one machine is split (e.g., patent ranges), every shard processes the request, and the root computes the union. Choosing the number of leaves is critical: per-request overhead grows with leaf count so gains are asymptotic, and the *straggler problem* dominates latency because the root waits for the slowest leaf — scattering to 5 leaves turns a 99th-percentile request latency into roughly a 95th-percentile system latency, and 100 leaves effectively guarantee the worst-case latency; the same effect applies to availability. The remedy is to replicate each shard so leaf requests are load balanced across healthy replicas, allowing failures and upgrades without user-visible outages.

**Functions and event-driven processing (FaaS):** FaaS is described as serverless and event-driven, with the two concepts distinguished (a container-as-a-service orchestrator is serverless but not event-driven; self-hosted FaaS on owned hardware is event-driven but not serverless). Benefits center on developers: no artifact to build or push, automatic scaling and restart on failure, and fine-grained stateless building blocks that are inherently modular. Challenges arise from forced decoupling — functions communicate only over the network and hold no local state — making it hard to see the whole service, diagnose failures, or detect dependency loops (A→B→C→A) that terminate only on timeout or exhausted budget; rigorous monitoring and alerting are required. FaaS's time-bounded runtime makes it a poor fit for background processing such as video transcoding or log compression; scheduled triggers alone are insufficient, requiring long-running environments and a pay-per-consumption model. A further architectural limitation is the need to hold significant data in memory to serve requests.

Apple Inc.’s Form 10-Q for the fiscal quarter ended December 26, 2015 reported net sales of $75.9 billion, up 2% from $74.6 billion in the prior-year quarter. Growth in Services and Other Products, along with a $548 million Samsung payment recorded in licensing net sales, was partly offset by lower iPad sales and foreign-currency weakness. Gross margin increased to 40.1% from 39.9%, while operating income declined slightly to $24.2 billion. Net income rose to $18.4 billion, and diluted earnings per share increased to $3.28 from $3.06. Operating expenses increased 14%, primarily due to higher research and development and selling, general and administrative expenses. The effective tax rate declined to 25.3% from 26.2%.

iPhone net sales increased 1% to $51.6 billion, with unit sales nearly unchanged and average selling prices flat. iPad net sales fell 21% and unit sales fell 25%, while average selling prices rose 5%. Mac net sales declined 3% and unit sales fell 4%, with average selling prices flat. Services sales rose 26% to $6.1 billion, primarily due to the Samsung payment, App Store and AppleCare sales, while Other Products sales increased 62% to $4.4 billion.

Geographically, net sales increased 14% in Greater China, 4% in Europe and Rest of Asia Pacific. Sales declined 4% in the Americas and 12% in Japan, with lower iPhone sales and currency weakness contributing to the declines. Segment operating income increased to $27.6 billion from $27.3 billion.

At December 26, 2015, Apple held $16.7 billion in cash and cash equivalents and $199.1 billion in marketable securities. Total assets were $293.3 billion, total liabilities were $165.0 billion, and shareholders’ equity was $128.3 billion. Operating activities generated $27.5 billion of cash, while investing and financing activities used $20.5 billion and $11.4 billion, respectively. The company held $7.3 billion of commercial paper and $55.7 billion of term debt. Apple stated that its cash, cash equivalents and marketable securities were sufficient to meet its liquidity requirements for the next 12 months.

The company used $6.9 billion to repurchase common stock and $3.0 billion for dividends during the quarter. Its share-repurchase authorization totaled $140 billion, of which $110 billion had been utilized. First-quarter capital expenditures were $2.3 billion, and Apple anticipated approximately $15 billion of capital expenditures for fiscal 2016.

Apple’s marketable-securities portfolio was primarily highly rated, with no investments considered other-than-temporarily impaired. The company used foreign-exchange and interest-rate derivatives to hedge selected exposures. After collateral and setoff rights, derivative liabilities exceeded derivative assets by $116 million.

As of quarter-end, Apple had $7.4 billion of gross unrecognized tax benefits, of which $2.7 billion could affect its effective tax rate if recognized, plus $1.4 billion of accrued interest and penalties. A European Commission investigation concerning alleged state aid to Apple’s Irish subsidiaries could result in tax recovery covering up to 10 years, but the potential impact was not estimable. Samsung paid Apple $548 million in December 2015; further supplemental damages and interest remain unresolved, and Apple recognized no additional amounts.

Apple disclosed supply concentration, foreign-currency, competition and outsourced-manufacturing risks, noting that many components came from single or limited sources and substantially all hardware production was outsourced primarily in Asia. It had $20.7 billion of manufacturing and component purchase commitments, $7.9 billion of other off-balance-sheet obligations and $6.6 billion of future minimum noncancelable lease payments. Apple also reported that there had been no material changes in its critical accounting estimates or market-risk exposures during the quarter.

AT&T plans to activate nationwide LTE-M service by the end of June for low-power Internet of Things devices. LTE-M uses minimal energy, can last up to 10 years on one charge, penetrates thicker walls, and provides low data speeds suitable for small transmissions. Applications include PepsiCo soda fountains that track flavor preferences, RM2 composite pallets that transmit shipment information, and Capstone Metering water meters that detect leaks, faulty toilet flappers, and potentially handwashing behavior. AT&T says these devices should not impede ordinary network use. Pricing is undecided, but per-bit or per-device fees are under consideration.

Tigers manager A.J. Hinch said Tarik Skubal will not pitch in Game 4 of the ALDS against the Mariners despite Detroit facing elimination, preserving the ace for a potential Game 5. Skubal struck out nine in seven two-run innings in Game 2.

Lego DC Super Villains, announced with a full trailer, lets players create a super villain and work with DC villains in a parallel universe where the heroes are absent. It releases October 16, 2018, for PC, PlayStation 4, Xbox One, and Nintendo Switch, with bonus-character special editions.

A coach praises a right winger as one of the league’s best, while noting that Jordan and Andrew can play either side and are shifted between positions to preserve line combinations. Rhett is described as an experienced young defenseman, and another veteran defenseman is called underrated, disciplined, penalty-free and effective against elite opponents. The coach credits veteran leadership and Jarome’s assumption of the captaincy for Jarome’s improved play, saying Jarome needs support and advice rather than criticism. After an uneven first period, the team adjusted and improved, and the coach says the club will focus on its own weaknesses rather than its talented rivals. He dismisses poor ice and fatigue as excuses, citing the team’s demanding playoff schedule, travel and continued success. He also discusses line adjustments, San Jose’s use of a forward on the point, and an older, respected official known for communicating with players between whistles.

Pakistan halted work on three CPEC road projects after China stopped funding, pending Chinese approval of the financial mechanism. A parliamentary committee insisted the projects were not shelved, while experts linked the crisis to debt-trap concerns and cited Sri Lanka’s Hambantota transfer to China.

The passage advocates a gradual, graduated national inheritance tax on gifts, bequests, and devises, with rates rising sharply for large estates and beneficiaries more remotely related to the deceased. Moderate inheritances should be lightly taxed to encourage thrift and ambition, while swollen fortunes should face increasing burdens. Temporary federal inheritance taxes were enacted in 1797, 1862, and 1898, and the Supreme Court upheld the Civil War and 1898 measures as constitutional. Because the 1894 federal income-tax law was narrowly held unconstitutional, the passage urges efforts to devise valid legislation before resorting to constitutional amendment.

This medRxiv preprint presents a retrospective cohort study of postoperative complications after coronary artery bypass graft (CABG) surgery. CABG relieves the mismatch between myocardial demand and supply in ischemic heart disease and is performed on-pump (with cardiopulmonary bypass, CPB) or off-pump, using grafts from saphenous and brachial veins, internal thoracic arteries and intercostal arteries, approached endoscopically or by thoracotomy, increasingly with robot-assisted techniques. Post-CABG complications (arrhythmia, psychosis, stroke, myocardial infarction, hydrothorax, re-sternotomy, dyspnea, sternal wound infection) occur in all CABG types, with risk factors including diabetes mellitus, hypertension, dyspnea, progressive angina, post-myocardial infarction myocardial sclerosis (PMIMS), advanced age, long CPB and aortic cross-clamp times, and prolonged ICU and total hospitalization. The study aimed to clarify the role of the number of shunts and internal thoracic arteries (ITA) used in complication development.

Methods: Data from Mordovian Republic Hospital (2017–2021); 290 patients aged 41–80 (mean 61.36); 15.86% female, 84.14% male; annual cases 33, 35, 61, 84 and 77 in 2017–2021. Analysis used t-tests, one- and two-way ANOVA, and Pearson correlations (Statistica v10).

Results: 278 (95.86%) on-pump and 12 (4.14%) off-pump; BMI 16.36–45.35 kg/m²; ejection fraction 29–77; CPB 0–431 min; ischemia 0–147 min; ICU stay 1–27 days (mean 2.82); total hospitalization 7–50 days (mean 11.72). Prevalence: diabetes 66/289, dyspnea 55, arrhythmia 69, progressive angina 112, PMIMS 178, preoperative LV aneurysm 9; 7 patients had shunt surgery with LV aneurysm repair; shunts numbered 1–6; one ITA used in 191 and two in 99 patients. Complications: arrhythmia 31 (10.73%), psychosis 14 (4.95%), stroke 4 (1.41%), postoperative MI 2 (0.71%), hydrothorax 34 (12.01%), re-sternotomy 9 (3.18%), superficial sternal infection 1 (0.40%), deep 5 (2.00%), dyspnea 11 (3.89%); 5 deaths (3 intraoperative); one complication in 53 patients, two in 15, three in 3, four and five in one each; most frequent was hydrothorax (28, 11.20%). Women had higher BMI and ejection fraction and later disease onset. Diabetes occurred in older patients with higher BMI and longer ICU/total stays; diabetes complications were linked to obesity and longer stays. Dyspnea prolonged total stay, and preoperative arrhythmia occurred in older patients. PMIMS lowered ejection fraction and lengthened ICU stay; LV aneurysm lowered ejection fraction; shunt plus LV repair prolonged cross-clamp time; post-CABG LV aneurysm had lower ejection fraction and longer CPB and cross-clamp times. Elderly patients had more arrhythmia, psychosis and stroke, and these extended ICU and total stays. Hydrothorax was associated with low BMI, longer CPB and cross-clamp times and longer stays; dyspnea and deep sternal infection extended stays; deceased patients had longer CPB and cross-clamp times. Elderly patients used fewer ITAs, and two-ITA patients had longer cross-clamp and CPB times; cross-clamp and CPB times correlated directly with number of shunts (r=0.826). Progressive angina and PMIMS were associated with more complications; no significant association between number of complications and number of shunts or ITAs, nor with survival status. Age correlated with ICU/total days and complication count; complications correlated with age, CPB time, cross-clamp time, ICU and total days; total days correlated with ejection fraction and ICU days; BMI correlated with ejection fraction.

Conclusions: Elderly CABG patients face higher risks of psychosis, arrhythmia, stroke and prolonged ICU and total hospitalization; hydrothorax occurs with low BMI and long aortic cross-clamp time, which prolongs CPB; progressive angina and PMIMS increase postoperative complication risk, particularly hydrothorax.

Coach Sutter’s team emphasizes preparation, role acceptance, speed, and collective play rather than individual stardom. Players describe Kopy as a tenacious, puck-handling top two-way player whose work, minutes, and playmaking have made him a significant contributor and Selke nominee. They praise Slava, Toffoli, Pearson, and others as reliable role models. Despite its youth, the team is playoff-proven, tightly led, and still developing. Sutter calls every game an elimination game, describes the team as fast, and says its goalie is among the league’s best and prepared to keep playing as the Stanley Cup Final continues.

The Mighty Ducks attributed their success to home-court confidence, toughness, and handling adversity. After losing Bobby Holik and other leaders, the team added players and grew together. John became a key defensive player and stepped up when Joe was injured, earning praise as a major reason for the team’s success and as a deserving Conn Smythe recipient. Despite injuries, fatigue, difficult travel, and a bumpy playoff run, the Ducks won the Stanley Cup. The team intends to build on the title with its young players and strong organization, while avoiding settling for one championship and refraining from calling itself a dynasty yet.

Lewis Roberts sued David B. Prosser and Charles R. King for false imprisonment after they caused his arrest under an execution issued on a judgment against him and another assignee of debtor Robert Mills. The prior action sought an accounting, determination of assets and funds chargeable to the assignees, and distribution among Mills’s creditors. The court held that although assignees hold assigned property in a fiduciary capacity, the prior action was not simply one for money had and received under Code section 179. The statute did not authorize arrest in actions compelling trustees to account for funds subject to duties to multiple beneficiaries. Roberts’s arrest was therefore unauthorized, and the $100 judgment for false imprisonment was affirmed with costs.

America Saves Week, coordinated by America Saves and the American Savings Education Council, promotes good savings behavior. The 2017 event runs February 27–March 4 with daily themes, activities, resources, and participant recognition.

After Erik Brust and his cousin Jonathan Jeffrey devised a natural, creamy fruit pop, Jeffrey died of a drug overdose at 21 before they developed it. Brust founded JonnyPops in his memory and worked with St. Olaf classmate Connor Wray on a recipe of fruit, real cream, cane sugar, and salt. Starting with Twin Cities farmers markets in 2012, the business expanded into food-service distribution, multiple states, and about 50 Minnesota grocery-store partners in 2014. Brust and Wray later joined full-time and were named to Forbes’ 2018 “30 Under 30.”

JonnyPops’ gluten-free, additive- and filler-free pops now have 10,000 U.S. distribution points. Its Delights line added five flavors in 2018. Under Better Pop for a Better World, the company crowdsources messages printed on pop sticks and partners with retailers to support addiction-treatment organizations, including Hazelden and Betty Ford.

Following his reelection, the speaker expresses gratitude for his constituents’ renewed confidence and pledges to justify their approval through continued service. He attributes his election not to personal merit but to powerful, permanent causes demonstrating the strength and stability of the Union. Reviewing the previous administration, he argues that its policies should be corrected when unsound and supported when beneficial.

For national defense, he supports coastal fortifications, a reduced peacetime army, and a stronger navy. These measures, enacted in 1815 and 1816, would enable a smaller defensive force, protect commerce and cities, deter invasion, and offer protection even during other nations’ wars. He presents them as economical and peace-oriented rather than hostile, and reports substantial progress toward completion.

In foreign affairs, the government maintained strict neutrality between Spain and its South American colonies, treating both parties equally in trade, arms sales, port access, and enforcement against illegal provisioning. The speaker endorses continued neutrality while reserving the right to act if honor or national interests require it. He reports decisive action against buccaneering in Florida and neighboring waters, supported by prosecutions, executions, and pardons for offenders who lacked knowledge of their crimes.

He expresses confidence that the ratified treaty with Spain has established permanent friendship, settled western boundaries, and secured Florida. Florida is described as strategically important for western commerce, access to the Gulf of Mexico, naval harbors, protection from Indian attacks, and security of the Mississippi and other waterways. The 1818 convention with Great Britain renewed commercial relations for ten years and resolved several disputes, including fisheries, although restrictions on West Indian trade remained. Negotiations with France continued, while naval forces were maintained near the Mediterranean and Pacific to protect commerce, fisheries, and the suppression of piracy and the slave trade.

The nation’s finances and resources are portrayed as strong. Nearly $67 million of public debt had been paid while defense and internal improvements advanced without direct taxes or excises. Falling prices had reduced revenue, however, prompting loans and renewed consideration of taxation. The speaker favors financing current peacetime needs through current revenue and, when necessary, internal duties, excises, and matching import taxes to provide more stable revenue, promote manufactures, and avoid excessive reliance on foreign commerce.

Regarding Indian tribes within United States territory, he criticizes their treatment as independent nations, arguing that it delayed improvement and contributed to dispossession. He proposes ending tribal sovereignty, securing land rights for individuals and their descendants, granting reasonable equivalents, and using permanent funds to support civil government and education until tribes could sustain themselves.

Although Europe faces renewed instability, the speaker favors peaceful relations, neutrality in foreign wars, and peaceful redress for injuries, while insisting on the right to defend American maritime rights and prepare for danger during peacetime.

Finally, he credits the nation’s progress to a fully elective system in which sovereignty rests with the people and officials remain responsible to them. Despite early imperfections, national and state conflicts have been resolved without serious disorder. Territorial expansion, control of the Mississippi and Louisiana, acquisition of Florida, admission of new states, and rapid population growth have transformed the United States into a stable and powerful nation.

Nvidia will continue sponsoring H-1B visa employees despite President Trump’s new $100,000 fee, potentially costing the company an estimated $147.3 million for workers approved in 2025. The fee applies only to new applicants, not renewals or current visa holders. Jensen Huang called legal immigration essential to U.S. technology and innovation and said Nvidia’s success would be impossible without immigrant workers, while also saying the fee sets the bar too high. A Nvidia spokesperson declined further comment.

For Oct. 6, target increases included AdvanSix ($46), Deckers ($80), New Oriental ($100), Netflix ($215), Plug Power ($4), Constellation Brands ($235 and $226), 2U ($66) and Yum China ($45); declines included Ascena ($2.50) and Rite Aid ($2.25). BNP Paribas set €64 for Covestro (sell), €96 for BASF (buy), and neutral targets for Evonik (€29), Linde (€175), Lanxess (€65) and Wacker Chemie (€110). Other targets were Costco $185, Inovio $13, Eli Lilly $86 and Mallinckrodt $70.

This review protocol assesses the relationship between serial rt-PCR Ct values or other viral-burden measures and the likelihood and duration of replication-competent SARS-CoV-2 in solid organ or hematopoietic stem cell transplant recipients. It will also examine how age, sex, comorbidities, immunosuppression, vaccination, symptoms, and disease course affect viral burden and infectious-virus detection.

LitCovid, medRxiv, Google Scholar, and the WHO COVID-19 database will be searched from November 2019 through December 31, 2021, without language restrictions. Four researchers will screen studies, with duplicate full-text review and third-reviewer arbitration. Eligible primary studies must report serial Ct values or viral-burden measures alongside viral culture results from the same respiratory specimens in pre- or post-transplant patients. Reviews, abstract-only reports, post-mortem-only studies, non-respiratory-sample-only studies, and studies without viral cultures will be excluded.

One researcher will extract data and a second will independently verify it. Study quality will be assessed using five criteria covering case definitions, population reporting, study duration, rt-PCR methods and calibration, and viral culture methods. Results will follow PRISMA reporting standards and be presented in tables and narrative. Because assay and laboratory differences may preclude meaningful pooling or a universal cutoff, the authors plan a summary estimate of the relationship between viral burden and infectious-virus detection, with age and sex analyses where sufficient data exist. The work is supported by the NIHR Evidence Synthesis Working Group and the University of Calgary.

After the President’s assassination, the constitutionally chosen successor assumes executive duties amid national grief, honoring the murdered leader’s courage, achievements, and reform agenda. The address affirms that popular government remains secure despite presidential death, reports prosperity and peaceful foreign relations, sees no need for a special congressional session, and pledges faithful constitutional service with reliance on divine guidance and the American people.

Lincolnshire County Council approved a new care-leavers strategy and supports care leavers beyond age 18, including guidance to 25, council-tax discounts of up to 100%, university and driving-licence costs, and help for those in custody. Its leaving-care budget is about £1.2 million, serving 300 young people, while more than 600 children remain in care.

A fossil of the pregnant, long-necked marine reptile Dinocephalosaurus, found in Yunnan Province, China, contains a developing embryo and indicates that the Triassic-era fish eater gave birth to live young rather than laying eggs. The roughly 13-foot (4-meter) animal was the first known viviparous member of the archosauromorph group, which includes birds, crocodilians, dinosaurs and pterosaurs. Live birth supported its fully marine lifestyle, while its genetic sex determination resembled that of mammals and birds.

The Nebraska Supreme Court affirmed a judgment for Farmers State Bank of Craig on a $3,000 promissory note against Samuel J. Lydick. Lydick alleged that the note and an earlier $5,000 note were given without consideration for shares in Missouri Valley Cattle Loan Company, which bank officer Everett J. Martin and others had fraudulently induced him to purchase.

The jury found that the bank purchased the note for value, in good faith, before maturity, and without notice of a title defect, and that Martin had not made the alleged fraudulent representations. The court properly withdrew a later cross-petition claim because competent evidence did not support it. The evidence sustained the verdict, and the jury instructions correctly stated the issues.

The court rejected Lydick’s contention that a bank named as payee on an unindorsed note could not be a holder in due course. It held that a payee who receives a negotiable instrument in good faith, for value, before maturity, and without notice of an infirmity from a holder other than the maker or drawer is a holder in due course, precluding defenses such as fraud and failure of consideration.

PenFed Credit Union CEO James Schenck received the Large Business Philanthropist of the Year award at the 20th annual Volunteer Alexandria Business Philanthropy Summit for his community service and support of military members and veterans. PenFed and its foundation have donated to organizations assisting wounded warriors, military families, veterans, and veteran entrepreneurs, including support for accessible homes and the Veteran Entrepreneur Investment Program. Since 2001, the foundation has provided more than $30 million in financial support. PenFed, established in 1935, serves 1.6 million members worldwide and holds $23 billion in assets.

Amazon’s Prime Day 2 is scheduled for October 7–8, with early deals underway. WIRED independently selects its featured products but may receive compensation from retailers or linked purchases. Its hand-tested deal guide, updated September 30, 2025, includes the 2025 A16 iPad at $299, Anker MagGo 10K power bank at $70, 2025 M4 MacBook Air at $799, Arlo Pro 5S security camera at $100, and 2024 Kindle Scribe at $300. Additional promotions cover audio gear, chargers, smart-home devices, fitness trackers, and accessories, with feature details, limitations, and price histories. WIRED plans more stories and a liveblog when the sale begins.

China has modernized the PLA over two decades to match its global power, defend regional interests and sea lanes, support China-led infrastructure and Indian Ocean access, and counter U.S. influence. The transformed force has enabled a more assertive China, while the ultimate outcome and future use of its military power remain uncertain.

North Korea’s roughly $1 billion in syndicated loans have defaulted since the 1980s and have never been restructured. Repackaged by BNP in 1997 into transferable NK Debt Corporation securities, they rose to 14–18 cents on the dollar after Kim Jong-il’s 2011 death, on hopes of reform under Kim Jong-un. Trading largely froze after sanctions in early 2013, with no trades seen in three to four years. New U.N. sanctions amid U.S.-North Korean tensions could cut export revenue by one-third and further discourage trading. Total debt was estimated at $3 billion in 2013, while interest arrears are estimated at four to five times the $1 billion principal. Franklin’s Emerging Markets Debt Opportunities Fund held $15.5 million in NK Debt Corporation zero-coupon bonds due in March 2020 but assigned them no value in 2016. Experts expect the debt to remain inactive for a long time, resembling Cuba’s legacy debt.

Latin American stocks rebounded Monday as easing U.S.-North Korea tensions renewed appetite for risky assets, partly reversing a nearly $1 trillion global equity selloff last week. Mexico’s IPC rose 1.1%, while Brazil’s Bovespa touched its highest level since May; all listed regional indexes gained. Currency trading was subdued as the Mexican peso strengthened ahead of NAFTA negotiations and the Brazilian real fluctuated before an expected widening of the fiscal deficit. Scotiabank cautioned that renewed North Korean missile testing could revive geopolitical risks.

The study develops a modular framework at NSLS-II for collaborative human–AI control of multimodal synchrotron experiments. AI agents process and analyze XRD and XAFS data and can recommend measurements through Bayesian optimization. K-means clustering reduces high-dimensional data to labels, a scientific-value function and Gaussian-process surrogate estimate the value of unmeasured locations, and an acquisition function selects measurements. Requests pass through human-controlled adjudicators and a secure queue server, while agents cannot access safety interlocks. Bluesky, Bluesky Adaptive, queue-server, and Tiled support secure data streaming, distributed deployment, visualization, and operating modes ranging from manual to autonomous.

Live synchronous XRD and XAFS mapping was performed on identical sputtered Al–Ni–Pt combinatorial libraries at the PDF and BMM beamlines. Because XRD measurements took about 10 seconds and XAFS measurements about 10 minutes, only XRD agents actively queued measurements, while XAFS agents reported suggestions. The experiment demonstrated inter-beamline communication, inter-agent coordination, and real-time processing, but early agent configurations favored exploitation too strongly, producing dense sampling near wafer edges and sparse coverage elsewhere.

XAFS modeling mapped composition, with each element most abundant near its deposition site; measured ranges were 18.2–44.3% Al, 21.8–50.9% Ni, and 21.8–53.6% Pt. XRD identified FCC and FCT phases and composition-dependent lattice variations, although overlapping peaks, phase-specific texture, and anisotropic broadening prevented determination of exact phase compositions and relative amounts.

A digital twin based on a simulated Al–Li–Fe oxide library compared AI-driven mapping with geometric grids and random sampling. Across 10 campaigns, AI-driven mapping achieved higher model accuracy after one post-seeding measurement; at 5% data collection, accuracies were 98.9%, 95.9%, and 96.6% for AI-driven, geometric-series, and random strategies, respectively. AI-driven mapping better resolved phase-region boundaries and localized minor phase combinations while prioritizing uncertain or rapidly changing areas. The framework is presented as a safe, extensible, interoperable basis for collaborative multimodal experiments with continued human oversight.

Let’s Grow Kids, a Vermont child care advocacy organization founded by Rick Davis in 2015, officially ended its operations on Oct. 3, 2025, after raising more than $70 million in private philanthropy and growing to 40 staff members. The group helped pass Act 76, signed into law in 2023 to create a near-universal child care program. Since then, more than 100 child care programs have opened, creating over 1,000 spaces and 230 early childhood educator jobs, while an additional 4,000 children have qualified for tuition assistance.

Leaders Aly Richards and Davis said the organization’s planned sunset sharpened its focus, encouraged large one-time gifts, attracted talent and prompted early transition planning. Permanent organizations now handle child care financing, workforce, data and advocacy, while remaining staff joined the Let’s Grow Kids Action Network to protect Act 76’s funding. Despite progress, First Children’s Finance estimated that only 80% to 90% of participating families qualify for subsidies, leaving gaps in access. Other states have contacted Richards about Vermont’s approach, particularly its sunset strategy.

According to court documents, Joshua Bowen shot Jennifer Bartell several times on March 14 following a Facebook argument involving Bartell's daughter. Bowen, Albany Pierce, Shaunicka Cooley and Shyrayno Jackson were arrested; three face accessory-after-the-fact charges. Neighbors said the shooting stemmed from an ongoing dispute, not a random drive-by.

A federal judge ruled that Nirvana’s 1991 *Nevermind* album cover, depicting a naked baby floating underwater toward a dollar bill, is not child pornography and dismissed Spencer Elden’s 2021 lawsuit. U.S. District Judge Fernando Olguin found the image insufficiently lascivious, noting that Elden’s nudity was the only relevant statutory factor present.

Florida Museum researchers found that vitamin-producing bacterial symbionts in blood-sucking lice have continuously hosted by primate-parasitizing lice for at least 20–25 million years, tracking primate evolution rather than being repeatedly replaced. Genome comparisons from lice of humans, chimpanzees, gorillas and red colobus monkeys showed tiny, extensively reorganized bacterial genomes, with retained genes clustered near one another and much of the remaining DNA devoted to synthesizing essential B vitamins. The findings make lice–bacteria symbioses a useful system for studying mutualism, genome reduction and primate evolutionary history.

Researchers led by Dr. Valentin Bickel used deep learning to identify Martian dust devils in more than 50,000 satellite images from ESA’s CaSSIS and Mars Express HRSC cameras. Stereo images of about 300 dust devils revealed that the winds and dust devils can reach 44 m/s (160 km/h) across Mars, exceeding previous surface measurements. These strong winds likely lift substantial dust into the atmosphere, influencing Mars’ weather, climate, dune formation, and slope streaks. The study provides the first global, two-decade assessment of when and where winds are strong enough to raise dust. Researchers said improved wind models can help assess risks, adapt technical systems, and plan future landed Mars missions more efficiently.

The study examined whether resting-state functional connectivity of the nucleus accumbens (NAc) is associated with the course of ADHD symptoms and response to stimulant medication in newly diagnosed adults. Fifty-four physically healthy adults received baseline fMRI and clinical assessments, including the Wender-Reimherr Interview (WRI), and were followed for approximately three years. All participants were prescribed methylphenidate; 20 discontinued treatment after an average of six months, while 34 continued at follow-up.

Baseline symptom severity was inversely associated with connectivity between the NAc and the right paracingulate gyrus. Across all participants, greater symptom improvement over time was associated with lower NAc connectivity with the right anterior insular cortex. When analyses were stratified by medication status, higher NAc connectivity with the right posterior insula was associated with improvement among treated patients but with poorer outcomes among non-responders. Head-motion measures did not differ significantly between groups.

The authors interpret these findings as links between reward-circuit connectivity and the default-mode and salience networks, suggesting that NAc connectivity may have potential as a prognostic or medication-response biomarker. They identify limitations including the small sample, the limited ability of resting-state fMRI to delineate brain nuclei or directly measure behavior, and call for larger studies, task-based assessments, younger participants, and longer follow-up.

A Utah audit found seven products with incorrect markup entries caused a $186 departmental loss and overcharged 28 business customers by $1,161. The agency plans refunds and added automated pricing checks. Auditors also found a $4.6 million revenue-transfer failure that was corrected.

Philadelphia experienced a devastating yellow fever epidemic in August–November 1793, fueled by hot, dry conditions, abundant mosquitoes, and refugees arriving from the Caribbean. About 5,000 people—more than 10% of the population—died, prompting many residents and national leaders to flee. Physicians, including Benjamin Rush and Philip Syng Physick, failed to identify the cause through bloodletting, smoke, or quarantine. More than a century later, mosquitoes were recognized as the disease’s vector.

After the last reported North American outbreak in New Orleans in 1905, Brazil has faced a severe yellow fever resurgence since December 2016, with at least 326 confirmed cases and 220 deaths. Recommended responses include reducing standing water, improving sanitation and drainage, and vaccination. The yellow fever vaccine is 99% effective and generally requires one dose. Penn researchers are also developing DNA- and mRNA-based Zika vaccine candidates.

Rachael Caplan, 29, lives with severe Complex Regional Pain Syndrome (CRPS), which leaves her bedridden in her parents’ Thornhill home, largely unable to use a computer or go outside. Before her symptoms began during law school, she was athletic, had a law degree and planned to practice family law. Following acupuncture for a hip injury in 2012, her pain intensified and spread, and she was not diagnosed until June 2013, on her 26th birthday.

CRPS can progress from an autoimmune-like condition to a neurological disease causing intense, constant pain, swelling, temperature and colour changes, and other physical effects. Early diagnosis is considered crucial; PARC reports an 80 to 90 percent treatment-success rate within the disease’s first three months, while specialists say reversal after six months is unlikely. Most severe patients become disabled, although the course varies.

Caplan’s treatments, including physiotherapy and opioids, have failed or worsened her condition. She has consulted about 60 healthcare providers and tried therapies in Canada and the United States. Green LED light therapy recently reduced her head pain and improved her sleep.

Supported by friends and family, Caplan is raising CRPS awareness through a Facebook page and an ice-water challenge using the hashtag #AceThisFire, which received more than 20,000 views. She hopes greater awareness will lead to earlier diagnoses, additional treatments and possibly a cure or remission.

Gulf Island Fabrication trades at a significant discount to book value, with potential asset sales near book value approaching its roughly $120 million market capitalization. The investment thesis is based on valuation rather than a turnaround, although the company operates in a troubled segment with weak offshore markets, operating problems, and a challenging near-term outlook.

Gulf Island builds offshore platforms, support vessels, wind turbine pedestals, and other steel structures through Fabrication, Shipyards, and Services divisions. Severe oversupply in Gulf of Mexico offshore support vessels and muted prospects for new offshore platforms are limiting new contracts. Two multipurpose support vessels for Hornbeck Offshore had technical problems, delaying delivery to 2019 and contributing to a $23.9 million loss; Gulf Island reported a $24.3 million quarterly loss on $37.3 million of revenue.

Positives include effectively no debt and a backlog concentrated in shipyards. Gulf Island was selected as prime contractor for SeaOne’s Caribbean Fuels Supply Project, received an offshore wind memorandum of understanding from EEW, and may seek equity financing for growth. It is selling Texas facilities carried at about $100 million, including a $55 million South Yard agreement, potentially valuing the remaining businesses at about $30 million. The author considers shares attractive if asset values are realized, while noting equity-raising, margin, execution, and short-term price risks.

The paper introduces QoCGM, an open-source MATLAB tool for comprehensive continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) data analysis. Tested with MATLAB R2021b, QoCGM processes preprocessed CSV files containing timestamps and glucose values in mg/dL or mmol/L. Users specify sampling frequency and tolerance, the end of the nocturnal period, unit conversion and plotting options, and whether missing data should be interpolated or removed. The tool removes duplicate timestamps, identifies gaps using sampling intervals and tolerance thresholds, and can reconstruct missing values using piecewise cubic Hermite interpolation. It exports derived metrics as CSV files for statistical analysis.

QoCGM calculates descriptive statistics, time-in-range, glycemic risk, variability, glycemic control, and entropy/complexity metrics. Descriptive and time-in-range measures are reported for full days and separately for daytime and nighttime, with day-to-day variability also assessed. Metrics include GRI, LBGI/HBGI, GRADE, CONGA, MAGE, mobility, distance traveled per minute, fasting glucose proxy, GMI, hypoglycemia-event counts, and multiscale entropy. QoCGM averages summary variables across days for each participant; individual-day results can be obtained by splitting signals into separate files.

A case study used the first seven days of CGM data from the DiaMonT trial’s insulin-treated type 2 diabetes population. Data were available for 324 of 331 participants. Median glucose was 162 mg/dL, median TIR was 65%, and median CV was 24%. Coefficient-of-determination analysis showed substantial overlap among many metrics, while day-to-day TIR SD, mean continuous improvement, mobility, and distance traveled per minute had low R² values with other metrics. Daytime and nighttime TIR measures also differed notably, supporting their separate analysis. The authors conclude that QoCGM can support CGM research and clinical practice, while further work is needed to establish clinical implications.

European statesmen are expected to prioritize economic recuperation after the war. Slow demobilization could fuel insurrection, while rapid demobilization could cause an economic crisis unless raw materials, transportation, markets, and credit were restored. Competition to control these resources, especially sea-borne supplies from the Baltic–Balkans–Persian Gulf region, would therefore be a major instrument of negotiation.

German imperial policy depended on dominating eastern Europe while obtaining supplies from the outer world and regaining lost foreign markets. Two schools differed over how to achieve this: the Kühlmann–Helfferich group favored accommodation with the Western powers, while the Fatherland Party advocated military and naval power and the constant threat of force. German Socialists supported the moderate school because it promised quicker results and reduced military expenditures.

Belgium became the pivot of this contest. Its control would provide commercial advantages, prevent England from landing another army in France, and leave France at Germany’s mercy. Bethmann also considered an administrative division of Belgium, with Flemish control of the Flanders coast.

Dunkin’ Donuts will launch fall flavors on Aug. 28, returning pumpkin spice offerings and adding maple-pecan coffees and lattes, pumpkin cream cheese, and a maple-sugar bacon breakfast sandwich. The limited-time rollout could provide a sales edge, while new products have helped drive strong earnings.

Sarasota County petitioned the Department of Administration for a declaratory statement concerning whether a proposed crude oil splitter in Manatee County qualified as a development of regional impact under Chapter 380. The Department stated that only projects listed as presumed regional developments under Florida Administrative Code Rule 22F-2 were covered and denied the County’s request without a hearing.

The majority held that Sarasota County lacked standing to seek judicial review because it was neither a developer nor an entity authorized to initiate the regional-impact process; an unfavorable declaratory statement alone did not confer standing. The court therefore denied certiorari without reaching the merits. Judge Boardman concurred, noting that the County could pursue relief through its regional planning agency or under the Florida Environmental Protection Act.

Judge Scheb dissented, viewing the statement as final agency action subject to review and arguing that Rule 22F-2 created presumptions rather than an exhaustive list, leaving the state land planning agency authority to determine whether an unlisted project was a regional development.

A coach said one player was given a day off and stressed that every shift must count. After strong first periods in Boston, the team lost control in the second. He praised two opponents as playing better than their point totals suggest, while crediting their goaltender and defensemen, and expects their scoring to turn soon. The team will focus on one game at a time and execute its plan.

ICICI Bank said its mortgage portfolio exceeded Rs 1.5 trillion, making it the largest private-sector mortgage lender and half of its roughly Rs 3 trillion retail loan book. It targets Rs 2 trillion by FY20, with about 15% annual growth driven by smaller cities and the Awas Yojana. SARS-CoV-2 vaccines substantially reduced COVID-19 cases, hospitalisations and deaths, but emerging variants and waning immunity reduced protection against infection, especially with Omicron, while protection against severe outcomes was more durable. This study inferred immune waning and boosting by fitting a mechanistic model to English vaccine-effectiveness data for AZD1222, BNT162b2 and mRNA-1273 against Delta and Omicron BA.1/BA.2, covering mild disease, hospitalisation and death. The model represented immunity as biphasic exponential decay linked logarithmically to protection and estimated a 6.5-fold reduction in immunity against Omicron relative to Delta. It fitted the observed data well and estimated rapid and slow immunity half-lives of 33 and 580 days, respectively. At 180 days after boosting, estimated protection against Omicron hospitalisation was 49.5% for AZD1222, 63.7% for BNT162b2 and 69.8% for mRNA-1273; after one year, it declined to 38.9%, 53.3% and 60.0%, respectively.

The Moderna bivalent mRNA-1273.214 vaccine produced 1.61-fold higher neutralising antibody titres against BA.1 than the original vaccine. Its additional early protection against hospitalisation and death was initially small relative to any booster’s benefit, but it was predicted to last longer: one year after a fourth dose, protection against hospitalisation was 60.0% with the original vaccine and 77.9% with the bivalent vaccine. Over one year, slightly more than half the additional protection was attributed to receiving a fourth dose and the remainder to switching to the bivalent vaccine; nearly twice as many severe-disease episodes were projected to be prevented compared with original-vaccine boosting.

The framework was presented as a way to guide booster strategies using population effectiveness and immunogenicity data. Limitations included inability to separate infection-induced from vaccine-induced immunity, lack of direct immunological measurements, uncertainty in long-term model projections, and inability to distinguish COVID-19-related hospitalisations or deaths from other causes among people testing positive.

A Tweak Mattress survey of 2,000 British adults found the average respondent wakes three times nightly, while one in ten wakes seven to ten times. Reported causes include needing the toilet (47%), snoring (41%), losing bed space (25%), discomfort (19%), nightmares (11%), tossing and turning (10.5%), sleep-related talking or noises and phone light (10% each), anxiety (6%), and a partner using a TV or book (4.6%). Psychologist Robert Stewart said sleep quality depends on sleep hygiene and sleep cycles; consistent pre-bed routines can aid sleep, while noise, snoring, and discomfort may cause people to wake or struggle to return to sleep.

Larry Connors’ R3 mean-reversion strategy, presented in *High Probability ETF Trading* (2009), was backtested on 25 liquid ETFs from 2000 through December 2020 without commissions or slippage. Entry requires a close above the 200-day moving average, three consecutive declines in two-day RSI beginning below 60, and RSI below 10; positions exit when RSI exceeds 70. The all-ETF portfolio recorded 992 trades, a 75% win rate, 0.68% average gain per trade, a 2.08 profit factor, 6.47% CAGR, and a maximum drawdown of 16% in August 2011. SPY’s win rate was 90% across 79 trades since 1993. A 50/50 QQQ/SPY portfolio had a 3.37 profit factor and 2.69% CAGR, with only 4.5% market exposure. The authors could not fully replicate Connors’ results because they obtained fewer fills. They concluded that R3 remained effective after 12 years, particularly in equity markets, but did not suit every market.

Six Texas public university systems ordered or began reviews of courses, syllabi and programs after conservative politicians targeted institutions and faculty over teaching gender identity and transgender topics. Texas A&M initiated a systemwide audit following controversy over a children’s literature lesson not described in its catalog; the University of Texas is reviewing gender-identity courses, while North Texas ordered expedited reviews due January 1. University of Houston and Texas Woman’s University are also reviewing curricula. No current state or federal law prohibits public-university professors from teaching about transgender identity, but written and unwritten policies have restricted such instruction. It remains unclear whether courses will be censored or removed.

Professors have also been identified through publicly available syllabi. More than 500 colleges and universities use the Simple Syllabus platform, which can make course information searchable, although institutions can restrict access and faculty can hide some content. Texas law requires public institutions to publish syllabi with assignments, readings and topic descriptions, but not class times or locations. Lecturer Andrew Joseph Pegoda was targeted by a conservative news site after it found his queer-theory courses through Simple Syllabus. He now faces tension between omitting details to protect himself and including enough detail to protect himself from complaints or termination.

This medRxiv preprint reports a nonrandomized, unblinded study examining whether BNT162b2 COVID-19 boosters affect glucose control and insulin sensitivity. In a longitudinal cohort of 155 healthy, prediabetic, and diabetic adults assessed before and two weeks after a booster, SARS-CoV-2 spike protein, spike IgG, and neutralizing activity increased similarly across groups. Among prediabetic and diabetic participants, HbA1c, HOMA-IR, triglycerides, and the triglyceride-glucose index increased significantly, while fasting glucose and insulin did not change. HOMA-IR also correlated positively with post-vaccination immune markers.

Repeated BNT162b2 vaccination in mice impaired glucose and insulin tolerance, increased triglycerides, and reduced insulin-stimulated Akt phosphorylation in insulin-sensitive tissues, without changing fasting glucose, insulin, or body weight. The authors interpreted these findings as impaired insulin sensitivity rather than reduced insulin secretion. Metformin improved glucose tolerance, insulin tolerance, and insulin signaling in vaccinated mice without altering vaccine-associated spike protein, IgG, or neutralization measurements.

The authors proposed that persistent spike protein and immune responses may disrupt insulin signaling through pathways involving TLR4 and estrogen receptors. They recommended closer glucose monitoring after vaccination for people with prediabetes or diabetes and called for further clinical and mechanistic research.

Love in the Time of Chasmosaurs is an offbeat, educational website for dinosaur enthusiasts, featuring scientific reports, links to research and magazine articles, and varied paleoart recreations of dinosaurs and other prehistoric animals. Museum-visit reports and photos from dinosaur exhibits worldwide accompany readers on the trips. Active since 2009, the site posts nearly weekly and offers monthly dinosaur-news roundups and an extensive archive. Its title parodies Gabriel García Márquez’s *Love in the Time of Cholera*, and its homepage features a chasmosaur mascot.

He describes the victory as a dream come true and reflects on the sacrifices of parents, coaches, teammates and veteran players such as Billy Guerin and Gonch. This prospective study compared 101 patients with cardiomyopathy—43 with dilated cardiomyopathy and 58 with other cardiomyopathies—with 101 healthy controls. Blood samples were analyzed for inflammatory markers (CRP, TNF-α, and IL-6), oxidative-stress markers (malondialdehyde [MDA] and glutathione peroxidase [GPX] activity), and NT-proBNP. Cardiomyopathy patients had significantly higher CRP and TNF-α concentrations than controls, along with elevated MDA and GPX activity. Within the cardiomyopathy group, TNF-α correlated positively with GPX and MDA, while NT-proBNP correlated positively with both MDA and GPX. IL-6 and GPX were not significantly correlated. The findings indicate that inflammation and oxidative stress are associated with cardiomyopathy and that their relationship is linked to disease severity as reflected by NT-proBNP. The authors reported no conflicts of interest.

Cardiac surgery at Huntington University Hospital required frequent blood transfusions, despite a cited 2006 study associating transfusions after aortic valve replacement or coronary artery bypass grafting with substantially lower survival. From 2011–2013, about 71% of HUH’s 500 annual AVR or CABG patients received transfusions, compared with a U.S. average of 48.9%.

In 2014, cardiac surgeon Dr. Frank Young led a Blood Conservation Project intended to reduce blood-product use by two-thirds within one year, lower transfusion rates to the national average, save $2.5 million annually, and prevent an estimated 125 deaths over 10 years. The project faced organizational and cultural obstacles: cardiac teams included physicians and hospital staff with separate reporting structures, surgeons had no formal authority over nursing staff, and transfusion decisions could occur without notifying the surgeon. Veteran surgeons were also reluctant to change established routines.

A review by the Center for Cardiac Medicine’s Committee for Operational Excellence found that 51% of cardiac patients experienced bleeding-related complications. Cardiac surgery generated nearly $8 million in direct costs for bleeding complications in 2013, and HUH spent several million dollars more on blood products than similar academic hospitals. Potential conservation methods included ensuring no bleeding before chest closure, autologous blood harvest, and retrograde autologous priming.

The project drew support from anesthesiologist Anil Gupta, administrators, nurses, perfusion staff, cardiologists, and some surgical colleagues. Gupta noted that about 40% of transfusions occurred in the ICU and that staff welcomed improved blood-product use. Skeptics included veteran surgeons who preferred familiar routines and had little incentive to consider costs. Young’s remaining challenge was to demonstrate the need for change, convert skeptics into supporters, involve the appropriate teams, and make the changes sustainable.

**Summary**

This is the Statistical Analysis Plan (SAP, version 1.0, 16AUG2019) for study ZEA-DNK-02170/ZP4207-17086, a multicenter (~5 centers) pediatric trial (ages 6–11 and 12–17 years) comparing dasiglucagon 0.6 mg with placebo, with GlucaGen® as a reference arm.

**Sample size:** Based on phase 2 medians of ~10 minutes to a ≥20 mg/dL glucose rise for dasiglucagon 0.6 mg and >50 minutes for placebo, assuming an exponential time-to-recovery distribution, a 2-sided log-rank test has 90% power with 45-minute follow-up at the 5% level with 20 dasiglucagon and 10 placebo patients; 10 GlucaGen® patients are expected to suffice.

**General considerations:** Results are presented as summary tables, listings and figures using ICH numbering; tests are 2-sided at 0.05 (significant if P ≤ 0.05). Continuous data are summarized by mean, SD, median, min, max and valid cases (geometric mean and geometric %CV for PK except Tmax); categorical data by counts and percentages, with missing percentages omitted. Tables are presented by treatment group with a total column. Analyses defined before unblinding are a priori; later ones are post hoc/exploratory. SAS version 9.4 or higher and Phoenix WinNonlin version 6.4 or higher are used; outputs in ASCII or RTF.

**Analysis sets:** Safety set (randomized and dosed, by treatment received); FAS (safety set, by randomized treatment and planned injection site); PPS (FAS without relevant protocol deviations, relevance decided case-by-case before unblinding). Primary endpoint analysis uses FAS; a secondary primary-endpoint analysis uses PPS; safety analyses use the safety set.

**Baseline/demographics:** Disposition, screening, randomized and per-set counts by treatment and country/center (US vs non-US); demographics (age, age group, sex, childbearing potential, ethnicity, race), diabetes history, medical history (MedDRA 22.0), body measurements and BMI categories, plus screening assessments (physical exam, vital signs, 12-lead ECG, central safety labs, immunogenicity sample). Concomitant medications and current diabetes treatment are coded to WHODrug Global (March 2018), summarized by ATC level 2 and preferred name, with rules distinguishing prior from concomitant medication.

**Efficacy:** Primary endpoint is time to plasma glucose recovery (first ≥20 mg/dL increase from baseline during the hypoglycemic clamp without rescue IV glucose, within 45 minutes). Secondary endpoints are recovery within/at 10, 15, 20 and 30 minutes and glucose changes from baseline at those times. Baseline is the last non-missing pre-dose value; no imputation is used; no interim analyses are planned. Covariates are age group and injection site. A hierarchical test order (primary, then recovery at 30/20/15/10 min, then glucose changes at 30/20/15/10 min) controls multiplicity at 0.05; GlucaGen® comparisons are excluded from the hierarchy. The primary endpoint is summarized with Kaplan-Meier and analyzed by log-rank test stratified by age group and injection site (PROC LIFETEST), with patients receiving rescue IV glucose censored/set "not recovered" at 45 minutes; sensitivity analyses with and without censoring at rescue, a stratified Wilcoxon test, a recovery histogram, and a discrete-time Cox proportional hazards model (ties=discrete) with hazard ratios and 95% CIs plus homogeneity models (sex, BMI class, ethnicity, race, US/non-US); linear interpolation of recovery times is a supportive analysis (ties=exact). Recovery rates at 10/15/20/30 minutes are compared by Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel test stratified by age group and injection site (non-stratified Fisher exact if cells are too small), and glucose changes by ANOVA with treatment, age group and injection site, reporting least-square means with 95% CIs.

**PK/PD:** Plasma dasiglucagon/glucagon are sampled pre-dose and at 10, 20, 30, 40, 60, 90, 140, 220 and 300 minutes, with windows and LLOQ handling rules; NCA metrics via Phoenix, determined by Synteract using data transferred from York Bioanalytical Solutions/MLM laboratories. Glucose is sampled pre-dose and at 4, 6, 8, 10, 12, 15, 17, 20, 30 and 45 minutes (plus 60 minutes if weight ≥21 kg); the PD endpoint is AUE0–30 min computed in SAS. Concentration summaries, listings and mean/individual curves are produced.

**Safety:** Based on the safety set: insulin administration prior to and details of the hypoglycemia induction procedure, trial medication administration, and post-treatment rescue glucose infusion (time to first IV glucose summarized descriptively without censoring); local tolerability at 30, 120 and 300 minutes; TEAEs summarized by MedDRA (21.0 or higher) system organ class and preferred term with causality (0–3, probable/possible = related) and severity (missing severity not imputed), including AESIs, other important events, injection-site reactions, related TEAEs, SAEs, deaths, and special search categories (e.g., QT prolongation, drug-related hepatic disorders). Laboratory, vital-sign, ECG (including QTcF categories >450/480/500 ms and change >30/>60 ms), pregnancy test, alcohol breath test and immunogenicity (ADA treatment-induced and treatment-boosted, ≥5-fold) analyses are described.

**Protocol changes:** The primary efficacy analysis was reworded with added sensitivity and supportive analyses, and secondary efficacy terminology changed from "within" to "at" the specified minutes.

**Appendices:** Presentation/programming specifications (decimal places, percentages to tenths, P-values to 3 decimals, footnotes, listing sort orders, date/time formats, derived-variable formulas for durations, unit conversions, BMI and change from baseline, conservative handling of partial dates), SAS programming QC requirements (program naming, header, comments, log and output review, Pinnacle 21 validation, spot-checks of at least two patients, documentation), and the planned index of tables, figures and listings per ICH E3 with mock shells and programmer notes.

Meb Faber’s three-way momentum/trend-following strategy allocates capital equally among stocks, bonds, and gold when each asset’s monthly 3-bar moving average exceeds its 10-bar moving average; otherwise, it holds no position in that asset. Using GLD, SPY, and TLT, the authors’ backtest from 2006 grew $100,000 to $422,000, with an 8.9% CAGR, 57% win rate, 1.6 profit factor, and 18% maximum drawdown. Nearby moving-average settings produced similar results, suggesting the approach was not curve-fitted. The article characterizes it as simple, defensive during major downturns, and best evaluated over long periods.

Passing-direction terminology describes the path a ball is expected to travel from a passer to a potential receiver, regardless of the player’s facing direction. General directions, clockwise from forward, are angled right, right, back and right, back, back and left, left, and angled left.

Terms are grouped into forward, angled right, back and right, back, back and left, angled left, and other categories. Forward terms include ahead, deep, downfield, down the line, forward/front, long, parallel, short, straight, and upfield. Right- and left-side terms include angled, corner, diagonal, line, post, centering, flat, lateral, square, and wide. “Back” terms refer to the goal being defended, while reverse passes simulate a forward action before passing more than 90 degrees to a trailing teammate.

Additional terms describe a pass’s angle, back heel, center, far and near posts, field axes, interface, outlet, parallel play, passing angle, possession, reverse field, straight lines, and switching fields. Definitions cover distances, locations, orientations, and purposes such as retaining possession, starting counterattacks, and moving the ball across the field.

NVIDIA’s GA10x Ampere architecture introduces major improvements across graphics, ray tracing, AI, memory, storage, and data-center workloads.

- **Graphics architecture:** ROPs move from the memory controller and L2 cache into each GPC, reducing frontend/backend throughput mismatches. GA102 has 112 ROPs versus TU102’s 96, improving multisample anti-aliasing, pixel fill rate, and blending.
- **SM and cache design:** Each GA10x SM has four partitions with a shared 128 KB L1 data-cache/shared-memory subsystem. Both datapaths now process FP32, enabling 128 FP32 operations per clock per SM, or 64 FP32 and 64 INT32 operations. Compared with Turing, L1 capacity is 33% larger, shared-memory bandwidth doubles to 128 bytes per clock, and GA102 provides 10,752 KB of L1 cache versus TU102’s 6,912 KB.
- **Tensor Cores:** Third-generation Tensor Cores are fewer per SM than Turing’s but individually more powerful. They add TF32 and BF16 support, structured sparsity, and up to twice the matrix-multiplication throughput. The RTX 3080 reaches 238 peak FP16 Tensor TFLOPS with sparsity, 2.7 times the RTX 2080 Super’s dense peak. Fine-grained 2:4 sparsity compresses neural-network weights and doubles math throughput while producing virtually no loss in inference accuracy.
- **Ray tracing:** Second-generation RT Cores double ray/triangle intersection throughput, support concurrent RT with graphics or compute, and can execute two compute workloads simultaneously. A new Interpolate Triangle Position unit accelerates ray-traced motion blur involving moving or deforming geometry, enabling motion-blur rendering up to eight times faster than on Turing; NVIDIA measured up to five times faster on an RTX 3080 than an RTX 2080 Super.
- **DLSS:** Enhanced DLSS uses third-generation Tensor Cores and a new 9× scaling factor, enabling 60 fps 8K ray-traced gaming on the GeForce RTX 3090.
- **Memory:** GA10x supports GDDR6X with PAM4 signaling and the Maximum Transition Avoidance encoding scheme. It supports data rates up to 19.5 Gbps and peak bandwidth of 936 GB/sec, over 52% more than TU102 and up to 64% more than preceding GPU generations.
- **Storage:** NVIDIA RTX IO works with Microsoft DirectStorage to move compressed assets directly to the GPU for GPU-based lossless decompression. It can accelerate I/O by up to 100 times versus hard drives and traditional storage APIs while offloading work that could otherwise consume dozens of CPU cores.
- **Efficiency:** NVIDIA states that Ampere GPUs are up to 1.9 times more power efficient than Turing GPUs at the same performance level.
- **Data-center products:** The GA10x-based NVIDIA A40 provides up to twice the FP32 and ray-tracing throughput of Quadro RTX 6000, along with up to five times the AI throughput, or ten times with sparsity. It has 48 GB of memory, PCIe Gen4, and can scale to 96 GB through two A40s connected with NVLink. The RTX A6000 also provides 48 GB of GDDR6 memory and can combine two cards for 96 GB.
- **Display and media:** Ampere supports 4K at 120 Hz and 8K at 60 Hz through DisplayPort 1.4a and HDMI 2.1 with Display Stream Compression. Fifth-generation NVDEC adds hardware decoding for MPEG-2, VC-1, H.264, H.265, VP8, VP9, and AV1, while seventh-generation NVENC supports H.264 up to 4K and HEVC up to 8K.
- **Products and reliability:** The RTX 3090 has 82 SMs, 10,496 CUDA Cores, and 24 GB of GDDR6X; the RTX 3070 uses GA104 with GDDR6 and is described as faster than the RTX 2080 Ti. GDDR6X memory includes Error Detection and Replay, which detects failed transmissions and retries them until the transaction succeeds.
