From November 1961 to October 1962, an augmented Special Group oversaw Operation Mongoose, with Edward G. Lansdale coordinating CIA, State Department, and Defense Department activities. CIA units in Washington and Miami implemented military, sabotage, and political-propaganda programs. In 1962, Kennedy created a separate Special Group (Counter-Insurgency) to formulate broad counterinsurgency policies; in 1966, Johnson assigned overseas coordination to the Secretary of State.

In June 1964, “Special Group 5412” became the 303 Committee, retaining its composition and functions. It approved 163 covert actions under Kennedy and 142 under Johnson through February 1967, although the Church Committee estimated that only 14 percent of CIA projects received case-by-case review. The committee could amend or reject CIA proposals, while State Department objections could modify or nullify them.

Nixon’s 1970 NSDM 40 renamed it the 40 Committee, added the Attorney General, required annual reviews, and retained DCI responsibility subject to committee approval of major or politically sensitive operations. Formal meetings later declined, and the committee reviewed about 25 percent of CIA covert-action projects. Nixon directed the DCI to promote a coup against Salvador Allende without committee coordination or approval.

The 1974 Hughes-Ryan amendment required a presidential finding and congressional notification for each covert action.

The lecture examines the economics of spam and security, distinguishing attacks motivated by ideology or state interests from financially motivated cybercrime. The latter may be deterred through financial pressure because attackers must invest in infrastructure. Spam remains profitable because sending is extremely cheap, while click and purchase rates are extremely low. One cited study found 10,000 clicks from 350 million messages and only 28 purchase attempts; sending a million messages could cost about $60.

A Chinese case study describes vehicles equipped with antennas that collect mobile-phone numbers and send text spam, potentially up to 200,000 messages daily. Equipment costs roughly $1,600, comparable to estimated daily profits, while low labor costs, infrequent arrests, and fines below $5,000 weaken financial disincentives. Chinese carriers reportedly earned revenue from spam messages and provided 106-prefix numbers, originally intended for legitimate bulk messaging, that spammers could exploit.

The lecture also describes markets for cyber arms, including firms selling malware, zero-day exploits, and information about unpatched machines. Government agencies and companies are customers. Some companies conduct “hackbacks” against attackers because the legal system often lags behind practice, although the legality of such actions is uncertain and unresolved in many cases.

The spam ecosystem has three components. “Advertising” obtains clicks through email, text messages, social networks, or targeted phishing. “Click support” requires domains, DNS infrastructure, web servers, redirects, or botnet hosts to deliver the advertised site. “Realization” handles purchases, payment processing, and delivery. Affiliate programs commonly perform backend payment work for spammers, which receive commissions of roughly 30–50% per sale.

Potential defenses include IP blacklists, email micropayments, proof-of-work requirements, and CAPTCHAs. However, adoption by all providers, legitimate bulk-mail use, compromised devices, and user friction complicate implementation. Attackers evade these measures through botnets, compromised webmail accounts, and BGP address hijacking. Botnets can contain millions of infected machines, with malware installation reportedly costing about $0.10 per U.S. host and $0.01 per host in Asia. Their command infrastructure may be centralized on “bulletproof” hosting or distributed peer-to-peer, while fast-flux DNS techniques rotate addresses to avoid detection.

CAPTCHAs provide limited barriers because attackers can obtain automated or human solutions for roughly $0.001 each, including through low-cost labor, Mechanical Turk, reuse of CAPTCHAs from legitimate sites, and majority voting among solvers. More frequent CAPTCHAs and stronger authentication protect systems but can irritate legitimate users, illustrating the tradeoff between desired and tolerated friction.

Spam infrastructure is decentralized. Affiliate providers, registrars, web servers, and DNS systems are distributed, preventing a single takedown from collapsing the ecosystem. International intellectual-property differences and the need to establish links between spam messages and financial transactions further complicate enforcement.

The realization stage uses a chain involving customers, merchants, payment processors, acquiring banks, card networks such as Visa or Mastercard, and issuing banks. A single affiliate has reportedly processed more than $10 million through this system. Spammers often classify transactions accurately and deliver purchased goods because misclassification, nondelivery, and excessive chargebacks can produce significant fines and jeopardize access to a limited group of acquiring banks. Yet some spam activity remains legally ambiguous when the advertised product itself is not illegal, while pirated software presents clearer violations.

Following research that exposed these financial channels, Visa classified pharmaceutical sales as high risk, imposed stricter merchant-bank requirements and audits, and explicitly prohibited illegal drug and trademark-infringing sales. Some spammers began requiring identification to prevent researchers’ test purchases, though this discouraged customers. The lecture also emphasizes ethical review for research involving purchases from illicit markets and destruction or nonuse of acquired counterfeit or pirated goods.

Finally, the lecture describes private-sector hackbacks against botnets and criminals, citing a 2013 coalition operation in which participating companies took control of a botnet’s command infrastructure. Microsoft relied on trademark-violation arguments, and the lecture states that courts allowed the action. Such cases illustrate the growing shift of some offensive cybersecurity responsibilities from governments to private institutions, alongside continuing legal uncertainty.

A self-driving Uber Volvo SUV struck and killed 49-year-old Elaine Herzberg in Tempe, Arizona, as she walked a bicycle outside a crosswalk. Police said the vehicle was traveling about 40 mph in autonomous mode with a human backup driver; neither showed signs of impairment, and authorities had not determined fault. It was the first death involving a fully autonomous test vehicle. Uber suspended testing in Phoenix, Pittsburgh, San Francisco and Toronto as federal and local authorities investigated. The crash could damage public confidence in autonomous vehicles and prompt tighter state or federal regulation. Arizona’s testing rules require no incident reports, while safety advocates called for greater federal oversight. Earlier crashes involved an Uber test vehicle and a Tesla operating on Autopilot.

NVIDIA Corporation’s unaudited Form 10-Q for the second quarter of fiscal 2023, ended July 31, 2022, reported revenue of $6.704 billion, up 3% year over year but down 19% sequentially. Gross margin fell to 43.5% from 64.8%, operating income declined to $499 million from $2.444 billion, and net income fell to $656 million from $2.374 billion. Diluted earnings per share were $0.26 versus $0.94. A $181 million tax benefit contributed to net income exceeding pretax income.

The gross-margin decline primarily reflected a $1.34 billion charge comprising $1.22 billion of inventory and related reserves and $122 million of warranty reserves. The inventory charge included approximately $570 million for inventory on hand and $650 million for excess purchase obligations and related penalties, primarily relating to Gaming and Data Center demand. The warranty reserve related to a defect in a third-party component embedded in certain Data Center products.

Graphics revenue was $2.797 billion, down 28%, while Compute & Networking revenue was $3.907 billion, up 50%. By market, Gaming revenue was $2.042 billion, down 33% year over year; Data Center revenue was $3.806 billion, up 61%; Professional Visualization revenue was $496 million, down 4%; Automotive revenue was $220 million, up 45%; and OEM and Other revenue was $140 million, down 66%. Revenue billed to the United States was $1.988 billion, China including Hong Kong $1.602 billion, Taiwan $1.204 billion, and other countries $1.910 billion. No customer represented at least 10% of revenue, while two customers represented 21% of accounts receivable.

For the first six months, revenue rose 23% to $14.992 billion, while gross margin declined to 55.7% from 64.5%. Operating income fell to $2.367 billion from $4.400 billion, and net income declined to $2.274 billion from $4.285 billion. First-half operating expenses included a $1.353 billion charge for terminating NVIDIA’s planned acquisition of Arm because of regulatory challenges.

At July 31, 2022, NVIDIA reported $43.476 billion of assets, $19.625 billion of liabilities, and $23.851 billion of shareholders’ equity. Cash, cash equivalents, and marketable securities totaled $17.037 billion, down from $21.208 billion at fiscal year-end. Six-month operating cash flow was $3.001 billion, investing cash flow was $4.230 billion, and financing cash flow used $6.208 billion. NVIDIA repurchased 19 million shares for $3.35 billion in the quarter and 28 million shares for $5.34 billion in the first half, paid $100 million and $200 million of dividends, respectively, and retained $11.93 billion of repurchase authorization through December 2023.

Management cited lower channel-partner sales, macroeconomic weakness, high inflation, weakened consumer purchasing power, COVID-19 lockdowns in China, and the war in Ukraine as factors affecting demand and supply. On August 26, 2022, the U.S. government imposed export license requirements on future shipments of A100 and forthcoming H100 chips and related systems to China, including Hong Kong, and Russia. NVIDIA stated that approximately $400 million in potential third-quarter China sales included in its outlook might be affected and that exemptions or licenses might be required.

Stock-based compensation was $649 million for the quarter and $1.227 billion for the first half. NVIDIA also disclosed $9.22 billion of inventory purchase and long-term supply obligations, a $575 million commercial paper program with no paper issued, and a $5.5 million SEC settlement concerning prior cryptocurrency-related disclosures. Securities and derivative lawsuits remained pending or stayed, and no loss accrual was recorded because potential liabilities were not considered probable.

The court denied Willie Tyler’s motions to dismiss the indictment and permitted a retrial on two obstruction-of-justice counts arising from the murder of Doreen Proctor, a planned witness in his brother’s state drug trial. Tyler had been convicted of obstruction through murder and through intimidation and threats, and the convictions had been affirmed and repeatedly challenged through postconviction proceedings. Following a Third Circuit remand, the court found that Tyler had shown actual innocence under the statutory “official proceeding” provision but not the “investigation-related communications” provision. It therefore vacated both convictions and ordered a new trial under the latter provision.

Tyler argued that retrial would violate the Confrontation Clause because the government’s proof relied on testimony from narcotics detective David Fones recounting Proctor’s statements about his brother. The court held that the statements would not be used to prove their truth, but only to show that Proctor would have communicated with a federal law-enforcement officer, as required by the statute. Because the statements were admissible for that nontruth purpose, their admission would not violate the Confrontation Clause, and Tyler could object if the government sought to use them improperly at trial.

The court also rejected Tyler’s Double Jeopardy claim. His earlier state prosecution was permissible under the dual-sovereignty principle. Although he relied on *Burks* and *Sanabria*, the court distinguished those cases because Tyler’s convictions were vacated for legal errors under *Arthur Andersen* and *Fowler*, not for insufficient evidence. A retrial following the successful reversal of convictions based on legal error is therefore permitted.

Finally, the court rejected Tyler’s due-process claim that prosecutorial misconduct required dismissal. The record did not support his contention that the government fabricated federal-officer status for investigator Ronald Diller. Although the government failed to disclose Mark Spotz’s 1997 statement until 2016, Tyler did not establish prejudice or a reasonable probability of a different result. The court also found no intentional misconduct warranting the extraordinary remedy of barring prosecution. An appropriate order would issue.

A year after Hurricane Helene flooded four western North Carolina school buildings in September 2024, EdNC asked district superintendents about the recovery. Some schools have reopened; others still await permanent homes.

In Henderson County, Perry Creek split Atkinson Elementary, which took on two inches of water. Atkinson operated at the Boys & Girls Club until new, more durable flooring was completed and students returned before Christmas 2024. The school plans vegetation and drainage improvements, and the club now places five mentors in district elementary schools and transports Atkinson students for after-school programming. Superintendent Mark Garrett stressed the value of prearranged community partnerships.

In McDowell County, Old Fort Elementary flooded and closed for repairs until the 2025-26 school year, while its students merged with a nearby school. Old Fort received new flooring, doors, paint and higher-mounted HVAC units; the host school got new flooring, paint and a resurfaced parking lot. Students returned on Aug. 25.

In Watauga County, roughly 70% of Valle Crucis School flooded. It stayed closed through 2024-25 with students housed at a university, Holy Cross Episcopal Church and Caldwell Community College and Technical Institute, which offered graduating middle schoolers the option to enroll there. A new building was delayed by construction workforce shortages, and the district continues seeking FEMA and insurance funding to preserve the original rock facade, which stayed dry.

In Yancey County, Micaville Elementary flooded and closed permanently, displacing 48 students. Expansions added 14 classrooms at Burnsville Elementary and 12 at Blue Ridge Elementary, with Blue Ridge expected in December. After cell service failed, the district issued weekly updates on a local radio station; campuses now have Starlink but retain bus-radio closure plans. Slope failures, drainage, mold and gutter repairs remain concerns, and all campuses need funding. The county's only high school served as an emergency command center housing 300 people.

Children’s mobile-device ownership varies widely by country and age. Sara Zaske said her daughter had little interest in a phone while living in Germany, where few third graders owned smartphones, but wanted one after moving to the San Francisco Bay Area. Her family planned to give her a flip phone in fourth grade and delay a smartphone until high school.

A 2015 European study of about 3,500 children found that 46% owned smartphones and 33% owned other mobile phones, though school restrictions and cost-saving practices differed by country. In the US, about 45% of children ages 10 to 12 had smartphones with service plans, while 42% of children age 8 or younger had their own tablets.

Ownership also varied elsewhere: 72% of South Korean children had smartphones by ages 11 to 12, while rates in Turkey largely favored giving phones to children ages 12 to 17. Mobile-phone access among African children ranged from low ownership in Malawi and Ghana to 81% among South African secondary students, with substantial growth from 2007 to 2014. In Australia, parents reported a median first-phone age of 8.

The American Academy of Pediatrics says there is no “right” age for a child to receive a phone but recommends limiting media use for young children, monitoring content, avoiding screens before bed and during meals, and not using media as the sole way to calm children.

Anglogold Ashanti shares fell 0.35% in the latest session, closing at $11.24. Analysts’ mean 52-week target is $13.89, based on four opinions, with a range of $11.50–$16.91. The coach said his staff had adjusted lines in the playoffs to create favorable matchups but had not won them. After two losses, he said the team needed to respond, improve the coaching staff’s work, and channel its emotion into confident play. In the latest game, the team skated better, managed the puck effectively, won faceoffs, and played its best game of the series. He praised a star player’s defense and shooting and the Krog line’s performance, particularly Stumpy’s. A second-period goal followed a line change when the team failed to move down the ice, but it generally slowed New Jersey and controlled its emotions better than in the first two games. The coach said the strategy had not changed, acknowledged New Jersey’s strong defense, and believed the series now had a chance to continue, while emphasizing that one victory did not yet constitute a series.

Chongqing’s online tax system, launched in 2016 and expanded with an integrated payment platform on Aug. 1, has streamlined property transactions and business tax filing. Yin Dinghan completed a home purchase’s tax procedures in 30 minutes, while agent Lyu Yan now finishes company filings online in minutes rather than spending at least a day at tax offices. Nearly 90% of businesses in nine city districts use the payment system, average waits fell from 83 to 15 minutes, and almost 95% of bureau transactions can be completed online. Mobile tax services have attracted more than 1.2 million users this year.

Professor Hong introduces a graduate quantum field theory course, the first of a three-semester sequence. The course will develop the concepts, formalism, and techniques needed to describe quantum dynamics of fields, with the goal of understanding quantum electrodynamics. Quantum field theory describes three fundamental interactions, offers partial tools for quantum gravity, and has become a common language across theoretical physics. Hong emphasizes mastering its fundamentals through problems, examples, and physical intuition rather than calculation alone. He recommends connecting difficulties to quantum mechanics, understanding the physical problems motivating formalisms, and reviewing examples to build intuition. Problem sets are central to learning, and lecture notation may differ from the recommended texts by Peskin and Weinberg.

The lecture begins with the principle of locality: physical effects propagate between neighboring points rather than occurring instantaneously across a distance. Fields implement locality by assigning dynamical variables to every spatial point. Maxwell’s equations and Einstein’s general relativity provide local examples; when expressed in field variables, their equations depend on quantities at the same point and their derivatives. Field types include scalar, vector, tensor, and spinor fields. The lecturer uses relativistic notation with \(c=\hbar=1\).

Classical field theory is developed by generalizing the action principle from classical mechanics. A local field action has the form
\[
S=\int dt\,d^3x\,\mathcal L,
\]
where the Lagrangian density \(\mathcal L\) depends only on fields and their derivatives at the same point. Locality excludes terms coupling different points. Only first time derivatives are included, while higher spatial derivatives are possible; Lorentz invariance generally restricts spatial derivatives to first order as well.

Canonical momentum density and Hamiltonian density are defined by generalizing ordinary mechanics to infinitely many degrees of freedom. Varying the action and integrating by parts yields the local field equation
\[
\frac{\partial\mathcal L}{\partial\phi_a}
-\partial_\mu\left(\frac{\partial\mathcal L}{\partial(\partial_\mu\phi_a)}\right)=0.
\]

The discussion assumes translation and Lorentz invariance and gives Maxwell theory and Einstein gravity as classical field examples. The simplest case is a real scalar field with action
\[
S=\int d^4x\left[\frac12\partial_\mu\phi\,\partial^\mu\phi-V(\phi)\right],
\]
where \(V(\phi)\) may be a polynomial. The Higgs field and pion excitations are presented as examples of real scalar fields. A linear potential acts as an external source, while the quadratic potential \(V(\phi)=\tfrac12m^2\phi^2\) gives the Klein–Gordon equation,
\[
(\partial^2-m^2)\phi=0.
\]

U.S. stocks rose modestly as investors remained cautious during the prolonged federal shutdown. Technology and growth sectors led gains, while uncertainty over fiscal negotiations, delayed economic data, liquidity, interest rates, and the broader economy could increase volatility if the shutdown continues.

The article presents Kinder Morgan (KMI) as a North American midstream oil and natural gas company positioned to resume dividend growth after difficulties following the 2015 oil crash. Its assets include 70,000 miles of natural gas pipelines, daily transportation of 2.1 million barrels of oil, 152 million barrels of terminal capacity, and the TransCanada pipeline. The company says its predominantly fee-based assets limit commodity-price risk and provide stable cash flow.

Kinder Morgan shifted from costly acquisitions toward expansion projects, reduced net debt by $5.8 billion over two years, and saved roughly $500 million annually in interest expense. Its 2017 budget projected $4.46 billion of distributable cash flow against $1.1 billion in dividend costs, allowing growth capital to be funded internally. Planned dividend increases include 60% in 2018 and 25% in each of 2019 and 2020, reaching $1.25 per share in 2020.

The company has a $12 billion fee-based project backlog, including $8.8 billion of growth capital for the following four years, plus $1.8 billion of carbon-dioxide projects. The article expects these projects to generate additional cash flow, lower the risk of further dividend cuts, and support further debt reduction, while identifying execution on growth plans and promised dividend increases as key items for investors to monitor.

President Donald Trump said the U.S. will impose an additional 100% tariff on China and export controls on all critical software starting Nov. 1, 2025, bringing total tariffs on Chinese goods to 130%. The announcement followed China’s restrictions on rare-earth exports, which it licenses for foreign products containing more than 0.1% rare earths or made with Chinese production technology beginning Dec. 1. China produces more than 90% of processed rare earths and magnets. Stocks and bond yields fell, with the S&P 500 dropping 2.7%, while grain prices declined after Trump said he would not meet Chinese President Xi Jinping at a South Korean summit. U.S.-China trade talks had recently been progressing, but rare-earth controls and semiconductor-related export restrictions remained sources of tension.

The paper introduces a quantum algorithmic framework for sparsifying generalized linear models (GLMs), covering linear, multiple, ridge, Lasso, Huber, \(\ell_p\), and \(\gamma_p\) regression. A GLM loss is defined as \(F(x)=\sum_i f_i(\langle a_i,x\rangle-b_i)\), with loss families required to satisfy \(L\)-auto-Lipschitz and lower \(\theta\)-homogeneous conditions. A sparsifier replaces the full dataset with a small weighted subset whose loss approximates the original objective across a specified range.

Given quantum query access to the data and loss functions, the algorithm constructs an \(\varepsilon\)-approximate sparsifier with \(O(\log(s_{\max}/s_{\min})\,n/\varepsilon^2)\) nonzero weights in time
\[
\widetilde O\!\left(\left(\sqrt{mn}/\varepsilon+n^\omega+nr^2\right)\log(s_{\max}/s_{\min})\right).
\]
For constant approximation error, this provides quadratic speedups in the number of data points relative to the fastest classical sparsification methods while retaining their approximation guarantees.

The framework computes multiscale leverage score overestimates using quantum leverage-score approximation, recursive weight refinement, and quantum binary-search-based initialization. It then performs importance sampling through multiple quantum-state preparation and quantum sum estimation, enabling efficient sampling and reweighting. The resulting sparsifiers yield approximate empirical-risk minimizers for linear, multiple, ridge, Lasso, Huber, \(\ell_p\), and \(\gamma_p\) regression, and subsume prior quantum algorithms for the first three tasks. The work addresses computational optimization rather than statistical model estimation from random samples.

Digital Foundry found Monster Hunter World visually appealing in many respects, with detailed monsters, environments, shadows and character animations, but technically disappointing across all four tested consoles. Common issues include reduced contrast, washed-out lighting, barely noticeable HDR, clipping, missing collision detection, motion blur, uneven frame times and inconsistent controller response.

The base PS4 runs at 1080p with mostly low frame rates, while the Xbox One’s 864p output and performance are worse. In Resolution mode, the PS4 Pro uses checkerboard 1800p rendering, while the Xbox One X renders at 1728p with smoother edges; the Pro offers sharper detail and better performance, but some distant assets are missing on the One X. In Frame-rate mode, both consoles output at 1080p, with the One X generally performing faster. Graphics mode extends levels of detail, restores the missing assets and shows the One X running 6–10 fps faster than the Pro. Overall, Digital Foundry concluded that Monster Hunter World was poorly optimized, particularly for the Xbox One X, despite being enjoyable to play.

The Flex offense is a screening-based system built around continuous “Pick the Picker” actions, combining baseline and down screens to create open shots and maintain two weak-side rebounders. It supports post-up, back-cut, back-door, lob, shuffle-cut, high-post rub, and dribble-clear actions. A weak-side double screen gives receivers options to cut low, high, or pop out. Because shooters often face away from the basket, offensive rebounding requires anticipation, hustle, determination, and second and third efforts.

Tesla Motors, Inc. filed a Form 8-K dated August 3, 2016, reporting its financial results for the quarter ended June 30, 2016. The Second Quarter 2016 Shareholder Letter was posted online and attached as Exhibit 99.1. The information was furnished, not deemed filed, for specified securities-law purposes. CFO Jason Wheeler signed the report.

Snowy plover nests were spotted at Clatsop Spit for the first time in decades, linking western Washington and northern Oregon populations. The sighting followed Fort Steven State Park’s designation of a half-mile beach section for the species, which has been threatened since 1993.

Early benchmarks of Qualcomm’s Snapdragon X2 Elite Extreme showed strong multicore performance, including a Cinebench 2024 score of 1,974—62% above Apple’s base M4 and 15% above the M4 Pro. Its single-core score of 161 confirmed Qualcomm’s claimed 39% generational improvement, though it remained behind Apple’s M4.

Integrated graphics improved substantially through a new architecture. The Extreme scored 5,628 in 3DMark Steel Nomad Light, 53% above Intel’s Lunar Lake chips, and was 30% faster than the M4 in Solar Bay. It still delivered roughly half the performance of a discrete Nvidia RTX 5050, and game compatibility remains an issue. Qualcomm also claimed gains of 28% in Photoshop, 43% in Lightroom, and 47% in Premiere Pro over the prior Snapdragon X Elite.

Testing covered only the Extreme configuration in a large 16-inch reference laptop; results for the standard X2 Elite and smaller systems remain unknown. The Extreme uses an 18-core X2E-96-100 chip with dual-core 5-GHz boost and 12-channel memory reaching 228 GB/s. Two standard X2 Elite variants have 18 or 12 cores and 8-channel memory, potentially limiting AI workloads despite all three chips’ 80-TOPS NPUs. Qualcomm aims to make its chips a major Windows PC competitor and reach 50% market share within five years.

The Ravens ruled out quarterback Lamar Jackson for Sunday’s game against the Texans with a hamstring injury, his first missed game due to injury since a January 2023 wild-card loss. Baltimore (1-3) will start a backup whom coach John Harbaugh says is ready to operate within the offense. Jackson has thrown 10 touchdowns and one interception this season and ranks fifth in Total QBR. The Ravens are 4-10 without him since 2018 and have lost four straight games played without him. Six players are ruled out, including four Pro Bowlers from last year, and four more are questionable. Harbaugh said the team remains positive and determined, while the Texans seek their first win over Baltimore since 2014.

DSS Consulting, founded in 1997 by three retired school administrators, provides specialized administrative support to small school districts. Founder involvement declined, client needs became more diverse, and revenue growth stalled, prompting a reorganization under COO Meg Cooke. DSS shifted from functional practice groups to cross-functional regional teams supported by smaller specialist groups, with the goals of developing new services, serving larger districts, and reducing functional silos.

Chris Peterson, a former teacher and technology specialist who joined DSS in 2001, led the Southwest Region team. She assembled seven experienced consultants who already knew one another, and the team quickly became cohesive despite uncertainty about the reorganization. Drawing on shared experiences, the team identified a lack of affordable integrated planning and budgeting systems in small districts and developed a scaled-down product.

District feedback was generally positive but raised questions about customization and pricing. As the team revised its specifications, disagreements slowed progress, but a team offsite helped restore focus and finalize the design. The project included a third-party database, an outside firm’s data-entry program, district forms, and consultant instructions. Because practice-group specialists provided limited support, Peterson escalated the issue to Cooke, but Cooke did not take direct action. The team filled knowledge gaps independently and completed a beta-ready product within ten days, with a test district scheduled.

At a Friday meeting, Peterson reported the project’s progress, praised her team’s cohesion and initiative, and noted that larger districts might be interested in an expanded version. On Monday, however, Cooke canceled the project, citing limited capacity for new products, lack of reported demand from other regions, and concern that large districts would not be interested. Peterson objected because other teams had not fully assessed the system, but Cooke said the decision was final. Cooke also announced that the Southwest team would shift to marketing only, undergo personnel changes, and either adopt a new direction under Peterson or return Peterson to the IT practice group.

President Donald Trump urged Gen Z TikTok users to thank him, saying, “I saved TikTok, so you owe me big,” during an Oval Office message. The remark followed his reversal on a proposed TikTok ban, which he first floated during his first presidency and which became a 2024 law requiring the app to sell its U.S. operations or face prohibition. Trump recently signed an executive order allowing a consortium of Trump-aligned billionaires, including Larry Ellison, Rupert Murdoch and Michael Dell, to purchase and restructure TikTok’s U.S. operations. The pending deal, negotiated amid talks with Chinese President Xi Jinping, is believed to be worth about $14 billion. His outreach to TikTok’s largely under-30 audience reflects the platform’s growing influence over youth opinion and political discourse.

Actor Cynthia Nixon announced her candidacy for New York governor on Twitter, promising a people-powered campaign without corporate contributions. The 51-year-old LGBT advocate will challenge Democratic incumbent Andrew Cuomo.

Florida’s First District Court of Appeal granted Denny Jenkins a belated appeal from the October 5, 2015 judgment and sentence in Suwannee County Circuit Court case 14-532-CF. The opinion will serve as the notice of appeal once the mandate issues, and the trial court must appoint counsel if Jenkins qualifies.

A December 2000 McKinsey memorandum provides a periodic update on international electric-power privatization and restructuring from June through November 2000. Governments facing rising electricity demand and insufficient funding are increasingly opening generation markets to foreign investors, even where full privatization is not planned. State-owned utilities are unbundling, while wholesale and retail competition is being introduced. Some international companies have reduced overseas exposure or shifted investments toward less risky markets such as the United States and Europe. European reform was driven by the EU Directive; Asian governments were resuming restructuring as economies recovered; and Latin American privatizations restarted more slowly following currency devaluations.

In Western Europe, EU rules opened customer choice to large users in February 1999, covering about one-quarter of demand, while phased gas deregulation began in August 2000. Consolidation, mergers, alliances, cross-border investment, and new trading operations became prominent. Austria’s unbundling remained incomplete and lacked an independent system operator; Denmark planned full retail access by 2003 and had consolidated generation into two major firms; Finland had permitted choice since 1998, though switching remained low; France accelerated opening to 34% of its market by year-end 2000; and Germany continued major utility mergers despite regulatory and grid-access obstacles. Greece was preparing state utility PPC for partial privatization and possible separation, while Ireland phased in supply competition and planned generation auctions. Italy required ENEL to sell substantial capacity, reduced permissible market-control levels, separated generation, transmission, and distribution entities, and created a state transmission operator. The Netherlands expanded retail choice, developed the APX online exchange, and arranged state purchase of the TenneT grid. Norway and Sweden relied heavily on NordPool; Portugal maintained separate public and independent supply systems; Spain planned asset divestitures following Endesa’s proposed merger with Iberdrola; Switzerland legislated phased market opening; and the United Kingdom, already fully open since 1999, was consolidating supply and postponing new wholesale trading arrangements.

Central and Eastern European countries continued restructuring to attract capital and prepare for possible EU membership, often under IMF pressure. Bulgaria planned to separate NEK’s generation, transmission, and distribution functions and privatize or upgrade generation by 2001–2005. The Czech Republic announced strategic sales in CEZ and regional distributors and prepared for market opening between 2002 and 2006. Hungary had already sold majority stakes in regional distributors and generators but faced price-control and contractual disputes. Moldova scheduled distribution and generator privatizations; Romania separated Conel into generation, transmission, and distribution units before staged privatization and market opening; Russia sought renewed reform momentum and greater foreign ownership; and Slovakia approved a plan to restructure and partially privatize its energy sector. Turkey proposed unbundling TEAS and expanding private generation, while Ukraine attempted distribution sales amid payment problems, employee arrears, and corruption.

Across Asia-Pacific, economic recovery and returning electricity demand prompted renewed unbundling plans, although IPPs continued to face problematic PPAs and weak government guarantees. Australia targeted full customer choice by 2003 and was expanding its national electricity market. China pursued nationwide interconnection and rural-grid upgrades while limiting project returns and lacking guarantees. India’s proposed Electricity Bill would establish state regulators, unbundle utilities, and facilitate transmission access, but only five states had made significant reforms and state electricity boards were financially weak. Indonesia’s IPP program was severely affected by PLN’s inability to pay operators, while Japan opened 30% of its market despite high grid-access charges. Malaysia continued separating TNB’s businesses; New Zealand split ECNZ into three state-owned generators and separated competitive and noncompetitive activities. Pakistan and the Philippines faced payment, guarantee, and legislative obstacles; Singapore lagged in retail competition; South Korea was breaking KEPCO into six generation companies; Taiwan was considering market-opening legislation; Thailand was preparing a wholesale pool; and Vietnam was beginning limited regulatory reform and grid expansion.

In Latin America, inflation, currency instability, ownership limits, and drought-related hydro shortages had delayed investment and further privatizations. The Inter-American Development Bank estimated that distribution and generation had been privatized in all major regional economies except Venezuela and Mexico, although 75 million rural residents in poorer countries still lacked grid access. Transmission concessions and privatizations were increasing. Argentina auctioned a stake in Transener and offered transmission lines for private operation. Brazil launched its wholesale market and internet-based trading initiative, while analysts warned that its hydro-dependent system could face shortages in 2001; the state also arranged the privatization of CESP Paraná. Chile, where privatization was largely complete, proposed distribution and transmission reforms and a Transelec sale. Colombia postponed further asset sales because of strikes and attacks on transmission facilities, while its ISA share offering proceeded. Mexico’s government sought market opening without privatization amid major investment and regulatory needs. Nicaragua, Panama, Peru, Venezuela, and several Caribbean and Central American countries pursued varying combinations of asset sales, transmission projects, partial liberalization, and stalled privatizations.

African and Middle Eastern governments were opening their sectors to foreign investment, although most still relied chiefly on IPPs rather than broad privatization. Côte d’Ivoire, Gabon, Guinea, Mali, and Senegal had privatized their power systems. Regional transmission initiatives included the Mozambique Transmission Company, a West African Power Pool covering 16 countries, and a six-country link among Egypt, Jordan, Iraq, Syria, Turkey, and potentially Lebanon. Algeria proposed unbundling Sonelgaz and permitting BOT projects; Ghana planned regional distribution privatization and diversification away from hydropower; Nigeria sought IMF-backed reform and NEPA’s restructuring; and South Africa was considering separating Eskom’s functions and possibly privatizing some stations. Egypt sought private stakes in regional utilities and used BOOT procurement, Israel made little restructuring progress, and Jordan, Kuwait, Lebanon, Palestine, Qatar, Saudi Arabia, Tunisia, and the UAE focused mainly on IPPs, market preparation, regional interconnections, or partial state-utility reform.

The memorandum also included maps, a “slippery slope” analysis, and timelines for market openings, and invited local amendments, updates, and additional country information.

VentureWire’s October 12, 2000 issue reported private-company financing, acquisitions, leadership changes, and venture-fund news.

Top stories included Weiss Peck & Greer Venture Partners’ spin-off as Lightspeed Venture Partners, which closed a $1 billion fund focused on early-stage communications, Internet, and software companies; the formation of MobileAria by Mayfield Fund, Palm, and Delphi Automotive Systems to develop a hands-free wireless Internet platform for automobiles; and Nth Power Technologies’ completion of a $120.5 million energy fund. B2B e-commerce provider ThoughtWorks raised a $28 million first round led by Schroder Ventures US Fund. Kozmo.com and Urbanfetch.com ended merger negotiations, citing financial disclosure differences and conflicts over business-to-consumer strategy. Children’s Internet media company MaMaMedia laid off about 40% of its 110 employees while seeking additional financing.

Other reported financing rounds included VelQuest, $9.2 million; Invertica, $2 million; CheckSpace, $11 million; Kenamea, $8 million; Kamoon, $23 million; Onex Communications, $20 million; KnowledgeLINK, $11 million; Maximiles.com, $7.8 million; Context Media, $20 million; Anystream, $13 million; Riot Entertainment, $15 million; mDiversity, more than $18 million; WorldPreferred.com, $3.7 million; Keen.com, $42 million; Mascot Network, $12 million; Expand Networks, $25 million; Iridian Technologies, $33.3 million; TurboLinux, $30 million; and KnowledgeTrack, $6 million. Miva received undisclosed first outside funding, while M-Systems invested $10 million in Saifun Semiconductors as part of a $40 million round. Wellogix and AccessBroker.com also raised undisclosed amounts, and Millemercis.com raised $662,000. PerkinElmer increased its stake in Bragg Photonics to 26%, and Texaco acquired a minority stake in Red Sky.

New-deal developments included Boxman.com seeking voluntary liquidation after failing to secure funding and Benchmark Tape renaming itself Benchmark Storage Innovations.

Reported acquisitions included BET.com buying 360HipHop.com; Need2Buy buying Unimate Electronics; CyberSight buying Nine Dots; Hire.com buying Advanced Recruiting Technologies; Newtek Capital taking a 50% stake in AIDA; PowerSchool buying Nordex International; and Away.com buying Adventuroustraveler.com. Financial terms were generally undisclosed.

Four board appointments were announced at CaritaSoft, OpenAvenue, Torrent Systems, and MeetU. Leadership changes included new executives at RedCelsius, MediaOcean, GemKey, MeasureCast, Ocentrix, Zeus Wireless, and eRisks. Cardinal Venture Capital created a $75 million wireless fund, while Infinity Capital named John Hershey as managing director and Dan Eitingon as a venture advisor.

The passage surveys America’s post–Great War condition, noting serious remaining burdens but restored confidence, revived business, and growing prosperity. It argues that continued success requires learning from national history, preserving American independence, and acting comprehensively rather than relying on slogans. America should maintain a balanced military force for defense while promoting peace through goodwill, international conferences, arbitration, and the rule of law.

Although the United States should avoid involvement in Old World political controversies, it must help relieve suffering and support distressed nations using its resources and influence. The speaker sees the Washington conference and similar consultations as useful, urges adherence to the Permanent Court of International Justice, and advocates reducing economic pressures that breed conflict. Permanent peace ultimately requires the cultivation of human brotherhood, religious conviction, and justice under law.

At home, political parties must exercise responsible, coherent government and honor their commitments once entrusted with power. The administration is described as having a mandate to uphold constitutional guarantees, respect private property, reduce public spending, and reform taxation. Economy is presented as a practical moral principle: unnecessary taxation burdens workers, while excessively high rates obstruct business and harm the poor. The goal is prosperity that creates broader opportunity rather than destroys existing success.

The passage credits restrictive immigration and a protective tariff with favorable labor conditions and notes recovery in transportation and prospects for agriculture. It also stresses preserving the Constitution, divided federal and state authority, obedience to law, representative government, religious tolerance, education, and moral order. America’s mission, it concludes, is not territorial empire but leadership toward peace, justice, prosperity, and the welfare of humanity.

This medRxiv preprint (posted January 3, 2023; not peer reviewed) examines soft-tissue sarcomas (STS) in the United States. Background: STS are rare, heterogeneous malignant tumors of connective and mesenchymal tissues with more than 35 histologic subtypes; lifetime diagnosis probability is about 0.4%, incidence is rising annually, and STS account for roughly 1% of incident US cancers (an estimated 13,040 new cases in 2018). Incidence is higher in patients 65 and older (11.3 vs. 2.3 per 100,000), and survival is poor because tumors are typically high-grade and diagnosed at advanced stage. Treatment options include surgery, radiation, and chemotherapy, with little prior information on how histology and stage affect outcomes, especially in elderly patients. The study aimed to determine mortality rates and predict overall survival for different treatments and sarcoma types among STS patients, including heart cancer.

Methods: SEER Research Plus data (2000–2018, 18 registries; 7.75 million cancer cases screened; 55,261 soft-tissue cancer cases) were analyzed with R and Stata. Sarcoma subtypes studied were liposarcoma (LiS, n=9,098), leiomyosarcoma (LeS, 6,168), giant cell sarcoma (GcS, 3,042), myxofibrosarcoma (MyS, 2,405), synovial sarcoma (SyS, 2,256), and spindle cell sarcoma (ScS, 1,880). Methods included Pearson chi-square, Kaplan-Meier, log-rank tests, multivariable Cox proportional hazards models (HRs, 95% CIs), and all-cause mortality nomograms (p<0.05).

Results: 24,849 patients were included; mean age 59, 56% male, 82% white. Median survival was shortest for GcS (42 months) and longest for LiS (76 months). At diagnosis, 12% had distant-stage disease and 73% had one primary-site tumor. Treatment use: surgery 82%, radiotherapy 42%, chemotherapy 19%, primary systemic therapy 14%. Survival differed significantly by subtype (MyS 75% vs. ScS 37%). Surgery, radiotherapy, and chemotherapy significantly reduced mortality, while primary systemic therapy had contradictory effects. Factors associated with worse survival were increasing age, male sex, non-white race, higher grade, and advanced stage; distant-stage patients had a 3.66-fold higher hazard of death (95% CI 3.34–4.00). Each additional year of age raised mortality risk (HR 1.02–1.06 by subtype); surgery reduced mortality across all subtypes (e.g., MyS HR 0.29, 95% CI 0.19–0.43). Nomograms estimated 5- and 10-year survival: patients receiving chemotherapy had survival above 80% versus 55% and 46% without it; surgery-only patients had survival above 90% versus 45% and 25% without surgery; radiation alone did not significantly improve survival. MyS patients showed an 85% survival improvement with treatment, while GcS five-year rates were low (18% chemotherapy, 10% radiation, 25% surgery). Calibration closely matched observed and predicted event probabilities.

Discussion: The authors describe this as the first study to evaluate cancer treatments across sarcoma types with tumor histology and stage, and report that surgery reduced mortality by 74%, chemotherapy by 33%, and radiation by 24%.

Limitations: SEER lacks data on surgical margins, perineural invasion, p53 positivity, histologic subtypes, recurrence, radiation dose/fractionation/beam energy, and some confounders (tumor depth, performance status); follow-up was short, and external validation is still required.

Conclusions: Increasing age, male sex, non-white race, and advanced stage negatively affected survival. MyS was associated with higher and ScS with worse survival. Surgery, radiation, and chemotherapy were linked to better outcomes, whereas primary systemic therapy gave conflicting results. An all-cause mortality nomogram predicting overall survival probability was developed. No grant funding was received; the authors thank NCI for open access to SEER.

MIT 14.271 is an introductory industrial organization course co-taught by Glenn Ellison, Tobias, and Jean Tirole. Ellison will deliver most lectures, which are intended to teach basic IO theory, empirical approaches, and the relationship between models and evidence. The course covers roughly 12 topics, generally with theory on Wednesdays and empirical work on Mondays.

The lecture begins with single-product monopoly pricing. A monopolist chooses quantity to maximize revenue minus cost, producing the familiar condition that marginal revenue equals marginal cost. Rewriting this condition yields the Lerner index: \((p-MC)/p=-1/\epsilon\), so the markup depends on demand elasticity rather than the level of demand. Monopoly creates consumer surplus, profit, and deadweight loss by restricting output. Potential additional problems include productive inefficiency, quality distortions, rent seeking, and the transfer of surplus from consumers to shareholders. IO models generally assume quasi-linear preferences and therefore set aside income-distribution effects within standard models.

For multiproduct monopolists, cross-price effects create diversion ratios. Raising one product’s price can reduce its sales but increase or decrease sales of another product. With substitutes, margins generally exceed the single-product Lerner formula; with complements, the seller may price one product below cost or even at a negative price to encourage sales of a profitable complementary product. Examples include printers below cost with profitable ink, newspapers below cost supported by advertising, and devices used to sell accessories. Multiproduct prices must therefore be analyzed jointly rather than independently.

The lecture then examines product quality with heterogeneous consumers. A monopolist equates the marginal consumer’s valuation of a quality improvement with its effect on unit cost. A social planner instead uses the average consumer’s valuation and generally serves more consumers. These differences can push monopoly quality below the socially preferred level, although they can also work in opposite directions. With homogeneous consumers, marginal and average consumers coincide, yielding an optimal-quality result.

Durable goods introduce commitment problems because forward-looking consumers anticipate later price cuts. With commitment, the optimal policy is to charge the monopoly price and make no later sales rather than walk down the demand curve. Without commitment, prices decline and profits are lower. Observed price reductions may reflect preferences for being an early adopter, falling production costs, or weak commitment. The Coase conjecture predicts that sufficiently frequent repricing can drive durable-goods prices and profits toward zero, but the lecture notes practical and strategic reasons this extreme result may not occur, including adjustment costs, new high-value customers, imperfect consumers, rental arrangements, most-favored-customer guarantees, and capacity constraints. This skepticism may also apply to dynamic structural models that assume period-by-period optimization.

The final topic introduces information design. Information varies widely across products: laptops provide detailed specifications, mattresses provide little comparable information, and wholesale used-car auctions deliberately reveal very little. Monopolists may benefit from concealing product information, while intermediaries such as Yelp and Amazon must balance consumer information against producers’ ability to extract surplus. In a sandwich example, full disclosure leads to a $12 price and $2 profit; concealing information raises expected willingness to pay to $9 for all consumers and profit to $3, but creates inefficient sales and eliminates consumer surplus. A partial-information policy that identifies consumers as low-, medium-, or high-value can produce a $10 price, selling to the medium- and high-value groups and yielding higher consumer surplus and profit than under full information.

Information design will continue in the next lecture. The following Monday will cover the empirical papers by Chevalier and Goolsbee and by Gentzkow and Shapiro; students without substantial econometrics training are advised to skim initially demanding demand-estimation papers.

A lecture examines how natural structures achieve lightweight mechanical efficiency. Iris leaves have stiff fiber-reinforced surfaces separated by a foam-like parenchyma core, making them behave like sandwich beams. Four cut leaf beams were tested as cantilevers under weights; calculations using measured geometry and estimated material properties predicted stiffness within the same order of magnitude as measurements, supporting the sandwich approximation despite the leaf’s curved cross-section.

Other natural sandwich structures include cat-tail leaves with internal webs resembling I-beams, grasses with dense outer fibers, seakelp fronds with buoyant honeycomb cores, bird skulls with outer and inner plates joined by foam or trabecular ribs, cuttlefish shells with chambers that control buoyancy, horseshoe crab shells, and Galapagos tortoise shells. Such designs reduce weight and material use while supporting multiple functions, including photosynthesis and buoyancy. The lecture also describes asymmetric ear placement in owls and head movements in foxes as adaptations for locating prey.

The second main topic is weight-efficient palm stems. As palms grow taller without greatly increasing diameter, they add layers to cell walls, creating a radial density gradient with dense tissue at the periphery and lighter tissue inside. This places stronger material where bending stresses are greatest. Measurements showed that Young’s modulus varied with density to the 2.5 power and strength with density squared. A density-gradient stem was calculated to have 2.5 times the flexural rigidity of an equal-mass uniform stem, while its strength distribution closely matched the radial bending-stress distribution. Bamboo was noted as having a similar density gradient.

Rep. Trey Gowdy, a Trump ally and House Oversight Committee chairman, said after being briefed by the FBI and Justice Department that there is no evidence the agency planted a “spy” on Trump’s 2016 campaign. He said using a government informant was routine law-enforcement practice unrelated to Trump. His comments contradicted Trump’s “spygate” claims. Trump’s lawyers have sought classified information about the FBI investigation’s origins ahead of Robert Mueller’s interview of the president.

The study evaluates post-hoc Temperature Scaling (TS) for a lightweight CNN classifying brain tumors versus normal cases in T1-weighted MRI images. The composite dataset was drawn from Figshare, SARTAJ, and Br35H, preprocessed to 256×256×3 resolution, and split with stratified sampling. The CNN used four convolutional layers, two fully connected layers, and dropout. TS divided the model’s logits by a scalar temperature optimized on a validation set by minimizing Negative Log-Likelihood (NLL).

The model was evaluated before and after TS on clean data and test data corrupted with Gaussian, Poisson, salt-and-pepper, speckle, and uniform noise. Performance was assessed using accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, NLL, and Expected Calibration Error (ECE). On clean data, TS produced minimal changes and slightly reduced some classification metrics. Across noisy conditions, it consistently lowered or maintained NLL and ECE while largely preserving classification performance. Tests with ResNet50 further showed reduced NLL, ECE, false positives, and false negatives, with unchanged or improved accuracy. The authors propose evaluating TS and other adaptive or sample-dependent calibration methods on larger datasets, additional architectures, changing noise levels, and distribution shifts.

The lecture finishes Cantor’s theorem that every set \(A\) has strictly smaller cardinality than its power set. An injection from \(A\) to \(\mathcal P(A)\) maps each element to its singleton, and a contradiction argument rules out a bijection by constructing a subset \(B\) of elements not contained in their own images. This establishes infinitely many distinct infinite cardinalities.

The lecture then introduces the real numbers as the unique ordered field containing \(\mathbb Q\) with the least upper bound property. Ordered sets are defined by comparability and transitivity, with examples including the natural numbers, integers, rationals, and dictionary order on \(\mathbb Q \times \mathbb Q\). Upper and lower bounds, suprema, and infima are defined, along with the least upper bound property. Examples of sets possessing this property include finite ordered sets, the negative integers, and the integers; \(\mathbb Q\) does not possess it.

Finally, the lecturer considers the positive rationals whose squares are less than \(2\). If a rational supremum \(x\) existed, it would satisfy \(x\geq1\) and \(x^2=2\). A contradiction argument rules out \(x^2<2\) by finding a larger element of the set; the case \(x^2>2\) is deferred to the next lecture.

Schools often maintain monolingual norms, although translanguaging can validate multilingual learners’ identities, linguistic capital, and sense of belonging. Unlike code-switching, translanguaging treats multilingual repertoires as integrated resources that learners draw on to communicate and make meaning. When encouraged, it can deepen content learning, support weaker-language development, strengthen home-school connections, and affirm bilingual identities. However, many educators lack sufficient training, and middle grades educators face particular challenges because multilingual learners often receive instruction in English-dominant settings with increasing academic-language demands.

This case study examined how two middle grades teacher candidates viewed, experienced, and used translanguaging during a year-long Professional Development School experience and how their ESL-focused coursework prepared them for multilingual learners. The participants, Patricia and Ruby, were among the first middle grades candidates to pursue an ESL endorsement. Patricia was a bilingual Polish-American immigrant studying mathematics and ESL; Ruby was an English-monolingual student of Hispanic heritage studying mathematics, English language arts, and ESL. They completed the program in two neighboring school districts: Central Middle School, which had a transitional ESL program, and Spring Valley Middle School, which offered transitional ESL and a one-way Spanish-English dual-language program. Patricia primarily student-taught mathematics, while Ruby primarily taught English language arts with limited placement in bilingual intervention or science instruction.

Data included coursework observations, four rounds of interviews per participant, classroom visits, supervision notes, and conversations with cooperating teachers. Analysis used open and axial coding, NVivo, and contrastive comparison, with findings focused on teacher-candidate preparedness and implementation challenges.

Both candidates held positive, asset-based views of translanguaging, valued students’ home languages, and reported that coursework taught them strategies for scaffolding learning. They also said they had tools for supporting multilingual learners. Their classroom implementation, however, was limited. Patricia independently used translation technology, peer grouping, and translated assessments, while also seeking outside resources. Ruby remained highly uncomfortable using languages other than English, made only limited attempts to incorporate Spanish, and said she did not know how to adapt instruction to individual students. Cooperating teachers also expressed positive views but rarely modeled native-language use; one bilingual teacher primarily translated English curriculum into Spanish.

Despite more than 100 clinical hours with multilingual learners and completion of an ESL endorsement, both candidates felt unprepared to meet learners’ needs fully. The study identified a theory-practice gap: possessing inclusive attitudes and instructional strategies did not ensure that translanguaging became part of everyday teaching. The authors recommend professional development for cooperating teachers, particularly before or alongside teacher-candidate placements; intentional co-teaching that builds teachers’ translanguaging toolkits; measurable, recurring classroom practices that draw on students’ linguistic resources and backgrounds; and additional research and training focused on translanguaging in middle grades.

Australian business investment rose 0.4% in the first quarter, below expectations. Construction fell 1.3%, with new factory construction down 16%, while machinery investment rose 2.5%. Next year’s capex estimate was $87.7 billion, still below forecasts.

The team feels more prepared than last year, benefiting from an extra family day and strong practice. Despite early-season struggles with focus, they found the intensity needed to win and believe it will continue in the playoffs.

Ford Model e’s first separately reported full-year results showed a 2023 loss before interest and taxes of $4.7 billion, up from $0.9 billion in 2021 and $2.1 billion in 2022, contrasting with profits from Ford’s conventional vehicle sales. Although Henry Ford developed early EV prototypes, Ford repeatedly discontinued EV projects before committing to major investments. Planned EV spending rose from $4.5 billion in 2016–2020 to $50 billion through 2026, targeting 50% of global production by 2030. Ford introduced the Mustang Mach-E, F-150 Lightning, and E-Transit in 2021, reached 275,000 EV orders or reservations, and became the second-largest U.S. EV seller. Momentum faded amid weak demand and pricing pressure, leading Ford in October 2023 to delay $12 billion in planned EV investment.

Under U.S. GAAP, research and development costs are expensed as incurred. Under IFRS, research costs are expensed, while qualifying development costs may be capitalized after technical and commercial feasibility is established, delaying expense recognition through intangible-asset amortization. Before presenting 2023 results, CFO John Lawler noted Ford’s $8.2 billion R&D expense exceeded its $5.5 billion consolidated profit before interest and taxes by 50%, while an increasing share supported EVs. International competitors reported some capitalized development costs.

NVIDIA Corporation’s unaudited Form 10-Q for the quarter ended October 25, 2020 reported third-quarter revenue of $4.726 billion, up 57% year over year, gross margin of 62.6%, operating income of $1.398 billion, net income of $1.336 billion, and diluted EPS of $2.12. For the first nine months, revenue was $11.672 billion and net income was $2.875 billion, compared with $7.813 billion and $1.845 billion in the prior-year period. Total assets were $26.881 billion, shareholders’ equity was $15.334 billion, and cash, cash equivalents, and marketable securities totaled $10.14 billion.

Graphics revenue increased 25% to $2.787 billion, while Compute & Networking revenue rose 146% to $1.939 billion. Gaming revenue increased 37% to $2.271 billion and Data Center revenue rose 162% to $1.900 billion; Professional Visualization and Automotive revenue declined 27% and 23%, respectively.

COVID-19 increased demand for Gaming and Data Center but constrained component availability and logistics. Pending securities and derivative lawsuits were disclosed, with no loss accrual because liabilities were not considered probable.

RDRAND and RDSEED are slow MMIO operations. For latency-sensitive uses, seeding a software PRNG with hardware randomness may improve security and performance. AMD’s RNG library for Zen processors provides a high-level API for cryptographic applications.

Billionaire investor Jeff Greene warned that higher interest rates and renewed U.S. fiscal action could end the stock market’s nine-year rally. Divergence trading identifies potential momentum shifts or reversals by comparing price swings with an oscillator. Bullish divergence occurs when price makes a lower low while the oscillator makes a higher low; bearish divergence occurs when price makes a higher high while the oscillator makes a lower high. Classical divergence generally forms against the prevailing trend, while hidden divergence typically accompanies a pullback and may indicate trend continuation. Traders commonly use RSI, MACD, the Stochastic Oscillator, and CCI, often seeking confirmation from trendline breaks, candlestick patterns, volume, or other analysis.

The passage presents a simple backtest of a divergence strategy on SPY. Results were generally strong when using approximately 2 to 20 days, with profit factors above the preferred 1.75 and strong Sharpe ratios. The equity curve showed low drawdowns and only one losing year, 2012, but the authors caution that the curve may reflect curve fitting and that relatively few trades occurred.

Chart examples include a classical bullish divergence on the Nasdaq 100 in March 2020, followed by a hammer candlestick and a strong rally; a hidden bullish divergence on TSLA during the pandemic crash, followed by bullish engulfing; a classical bearish divergence on the S&P 500 before the pandemic announcement, followed by a harami and market decline; and a hidden bearish divergence on the Nasdaq 100 in December 2018, also followed by a harami and downswing.

The strategy can provide structured entry and exit signals and is applicable across markets and time frames. Volume may confirm or weaken signals, while key mistakes include misunderstanding divergence, trading signals without market context, overtrading, neglecting position sizing and stop losses, and making emotional decisions. The passage stresses backtesting, confirmation, risk management, and disciplined trading rules before risking capital.

The UAE delayed startup of Barakah’s first reactor to late 2019 or early 2020. The first of four reactors is complete, with the others 72–93% done; the plant is expected to supply 25% of UAE electricity.

The passage provides PCB layout guidance for the UC1825B: keep high-current traces short, direct, and thick, with a recommended minimum of 15 mils per ampere; place inductors, capacitors, and diodes close together; use ground planes on both PCB sides; separate power and signal planes in multilayer designs; provide about one via per 200 mA for significant interplane current; and arrange switching loops to maintain the same direction. A dedicated power-ground section should connect PGND, MOSFET sources, input returns, and the bulk input capacitor, while VCC and VREF require high-frequency ceramic bypass capacitors, analog circuitry connects to signal ground, and the output requires a high-current Schottky clamp to VCC and PGND. It also covers documentation updates, TI support resources, ESD precautions, mechanical and orderable information, package-drawing notes, and TI resource and liability disclaimers.

President Andrew Johnson appointed William W. Holden provisional governor of North Carolina on May 29, 1865, and directed federal officials to restore the state to its constitutional status. Loyal voters subject to amnesty and pre-secession qualifications were to elect a convention to establish a republican government. The proclamation also ordered enforcement of federal laws, restoration of postal and revenue operations, federal court proceedings, and implementation of naval and Interior Department laws in North Carolina.

Charles A. Meeker and his four minor daughters brought a § 1983 action alleging that defendants’ conduct during a child-abuse investigation and transfer of the daughters’ custody violated their Fourteenth Amendment family rights. The district court dismissed all claims, citing defective service, res judicata from two prior actions, and, as to guardian ad litem Deborah Grout, failure to state a claim because she was not acting under color of state law. The Tenth Circuit affirmed. It addressed only Meeker’s appeal because he could not represent his daughters without an attorney. Applying the reasoning of Polk County v. Dodson, the court held that a guardian ad litem, like a public defender, owes undivided loyalty to the minor and exercises independent professional judgment rather than acting under color of state law, even when advocating goals consistent with the state’s objectives. All defendants’ motions to affirm were granted.

The Missouri Court of Appeals affirmed summary judgment for Bank of St. Louis and two employee defendants in Harvey F. Euge’s malicious-prosecution action. Euge’s conviction for obtaining money with a bogus check had been reversed because the check was drawn by a fictitious person on an existing, funded account and therefore did not meet the statutory definition of a bogus check. The court held that a conviction creates a presumption of probable cause even if later reversed, unless the plaintiff proves false or fraudulent testimony, other improper means, or that defendants did not believe the alleged facts. Because Euge accepted the underlying facts and argued only that they did not legally constitute the charged offense, probable cause was a question for the court rather than the jury. The undisputed facts established probable cause as a matter of law, so summary judgment was proper.

The paper introduces video object segmentation-aware audio generation, a task designed to give users fine-grained control over Foley synthesis by generating sound for a selected object in a video rather than for the entire scene. The proposed Segmentation-Aware Generative Audio Network (SAGANet) extends the pretrained MMAudio model with text, video, and binary object-mask conditioning. Its control module processes global frames and a focal crop around the target object, then combines localized and global features through shared Synchformer weights and gated cross-attention. The control module can be trained without full model fine-tuning, while optional LoRA tuning further adapts relevant DiT layers.

The authors also present Segmented Music Solos, a benchmark of five-second musical-instrument clips with frame-aligned segmentation masks and object labels. It contains 5,395 training, 665 validation, and 745 test samples covering more than 25 instruments, built from MUSIC21, AVSBench, and Solos, with URMP used for multi-instrument testing. The pipeline verifies objects visually and audibly, selects clips, and generates training masks with Florence-2 and GroundedSAM2.

Experiments show that SAGANet outperforms MMAudio across distribution matching, audio quality, semantic alignment, and temporal synchronization metrics, with especially large gains in temporal alignment. LoRA-tuned SAGANet reduces DeSync from 0.95 for MMAudio to 0.31 and raises the ImageBind score from 35.94 to 40.87. Ablations show that both global context and localized information are necessary: global cues favor overall quality, while focal cues improve synchronization, and their fusion provides the strongest semantic and temporal performance. Despite training on single-source clips, the model generalizes to multi-instrument scenes.

Britain’s FTSE 100 rose 0.6% from a three-month low as banks and miners recovered, while mid caps gained 0.8%. TUI reached a record high after an upgrade, but Experian and G4S fell following downgrades; energy stocks lagged as oil prices declined.

Iran's President Hassan Rouhani threatened in Vienna on July 4 to disrupt neighboring countries' oil shipments if Washington proceeds with its goal of halting purchases of Iranian oil. Revolutionary Guards Quds Force commander Qassem Soleimani praised the remarks and said he was ready to implement such a policy. The US withdrew from the 2015 nuclear deal in May and told countries to stop importing Iranian oil by Nov. 4 or face sanctions. Iran's Opec governor said Trump's policy would raise global oil prices and hurt the US economy. The EU vowed to keep the deal alive, and foreign ministers from China, France, Germany, Britain and Russia will meet Iranian officials in Vienna Friday.

Tom Petty, 66, died at UCLA Hospital after a cardiac arrest, with further tests needed to determine his cause of death. His family switched off life support after he showed no brain activity. Tributes poured in from musicians and fans, and he was known for the Heartbreakers and Traveling Wilburys.

The Gretna Trust & Savings Bank, as dative testamentary executor of Priscilla Lewis’s estate, sued David Lewis for $505.58 withdrawn after her death and for unpaid rent. Lewis admitted the withdrawals but claimed he was reclaiming loans to his mother and denied owing rent. The court held that the funds belonged to his mother’s estate and that Lewis, as a creditor, could not satisfy his claim by taking estate assets; any claim must be presented when the estate account is filed. Because the rent claim was not proven, the court reversed the judgment and awarded the bank $505.58 with legal interest and costs.

The paper develops an ontology-based method for robots to compare competing valid plans, determine which plan is preferable, and explain the differences to humans or other agents. It addresses two questions: how to model and reason about plan properties, and how to use that model to construct contrastive explanations.

The proposed ontology extends OCRA and inherits the DUL foundational ontology. It formalizes three plan qualities: execution cost, expected makespan, and number of tasks. It adds relations for comparing qualities as better, worse, or equivalent and for relating plans as cheaper, faster, shorter, more expensive, slower, longer, or equivalent, including relations for equal costs, makespans, and task counts. The model was formalized in OWL 2 DL and validated through competency questions and examples. Plan task sequences are represented using existing DUL concepts.

A knowledge-based framework, know-plan, integrates ROSPlan-generated plans with Knowrob and Prolog reasoning. Logical rules compare numerical quality values, treating lower values as preferable, and infer overall plan relations. Under the proposed criterion, a plan is better when all corresponding qualities are better; conflicting comparisons produce no conclusion, and users may define different criteria. In a drink-delivery example, the tea plan has six tasks with cost and makespan of 27, while the cola plan has eight tasks with values of 59, so the tea plan is inferred to be better.

The paper also introduces ACXON, an algorithm extending the XONCRA/AXON methodology to generate textual contrastive narratives from a time-indexed knowledge graph. At three specificity levels, ACXON retrieves progressively deeper relationships, removes non-divergent and repeated knowledge, and applies casting, clustering, ordering, and grouping to produce contrasting sentences. It is designed to remain independent of particular ontologies and can potentially compare entities other than plans.

Evaluation used 30 plan pairs from the IPC Rovers, Crew planning, and Match cellar domains. Against AXON applied separately to each plan, ACXON significantly reduced construction times and, at specificity levels two and three, reduced the number of knowledge tuples by more than 40% and 70%, respectively. Estimated auditory and visual interaction times fell by approximately 40% and 70% at those levels. At specificity level one, ACXON produced longer but more informative narratives. Readability was broadly similar around an average ninth-grade level, although AXON scored better at level three because its short sentences contrasted with ACXON’s more complex subordinate clauses.

A proposed refinement restricts retrieval to selected object classes, such as plan qualities, to shorten explanations and support personalization. This creates a trade-off between brevity and informativeness. Future work includes user studies, more accessible language, and investigation of when and in what contexts robots should provide explanations.

The report examines how U.S. Treasury liquidity may relate to recurring stock-market gains and the saying “Sell in May and come back in November.” Treasury cash-balance data from 2006–2017 show recurring January, May, and November peaks. January coincides with Federal Reserve reverse-repurchase operations. May tax refunds, which the report says disproportionately benefit wealthy taxpayers who are more likely to save and invest, may increase liquidity and support a stock-market rise. In November, Treasury buybacks and funds from maturing bondholders may produce another influx of investment.

The author identifies May as the most consistent liquidity spike, concluding that the saying is driven more by fiscal and Federal Reserve operations than by seasons, holidays, or horse races. Recent tax-law changes could strengthen the May effect in 2018 and 2019, while changes in the federal funds rate may also affect liquidity. Further research is needed to identify strong years and assess the February and November patterns. The author discloses holding no positions in the stocks mentioned and receiving only Seeking Alpha compensation.

Researchers at Karolinska Institutet analyzed MRI scans from 27,500 middle-aged and older UK Biobank participants, using machine learning to estimate brain age from more than 1,000 MRI features. After scoring self-reported chronotype, sleep duration, insomnia, snoring, and daytime sleepiness, they found that brain age increasingly exceeded chronological age as sleep health worsened. The gap widened by about six months for each one-point decrease in the sleep score; participants with poor sleep had brains that appeared an average of one year older than their actual age. Low-grade inflammation explained just over 10% of this association. The researchers said healthier sleep may help prevent accelerated brain aging and cognitive decline, while impaired waste clearance and cardiovascular effects are other possible mechanisms. Limitations include the UK Biobank participants being healthier than the general UK population and sleep data being self-reported.
