Recent cosmic shear surveys measure the structure-growth parameter \(S_8\) at percent precision, but intrinsic galaxy alignment (IA) can bias inferred cosmological parameters by \(4–5\sigma\), while baryonic feedback is another major limitation. Existing IA prescriptions include NLA, extended NLA, tidal torque, TATT, halo, and effective-field-theory models. Observations indicate strong color dependence, with bright red galaxies generally showing alignment while blue galaxies are often consistent with no alignment.

The paper introduces a pipeline that applies NLA, extended NLA, and tidal torque models to the same SkySim5000 N-body simulation. It also presents an extended tidal torque model and couples simulated tidal fields to HOD galaxies to include realistic nonlinear galaxy bias. The resulting catalogues can support validation of IA models, analysis of beyond-two-point lensing statistics, testing IA-mitigation methods, and studying source-clustering effects.

For validation, tomographic shear two-point correlation functions are computed using Limber-approximation predictions, a Halofit matter power spectrum, and CosmoSIS. Simulations use an LSST Year-1-like redshift distribution with \(z_0=0.13\), \(\alpha=0.78\), and 3 galaxies per square arcminute, divided into five tomographic bins and smoothed with \(\sigma=0.05(1+z)\). Correlations are measured with Treecorr over 20 logarithmically spaced angular bins from 0.5 to 475.5 arcminutes, with unit galaxy weights and no shape noise in most measurements. The simulations also produce galaxy-shear catalogues, aperture mass maps, and convergence maps derived through Kaiser–Squires inversion.

**Restoration Affiliates (Case 13-150, prepared by Cate Reavis under Professor Ezra Zuckerman, MIT Sloan, August 6, 2014)**

Rich Piltch, founder and president of ARS (Always Ready to Serve), a 150-employee, $25 million New England restoration and reconstruction firm, embraced the "Go-Giver" philosophy of The Go-Giver (Bob Burg and John David Mann) — giving without expecting return — as a business principle. Acting on it, Piltch joined with Damon Gersh (Maxons Restoration), Ras Fenger (Disaster One), and Andy Goldberg (RestoreCore) to form Restoration Affiliates (RA) in 2011, a collaborative partnership of smaller regional firms designed to give them national coverage and the capacity to compete with national players such as Belfor. By fall 2013, RA had 21 member organizations with combined revenue of $300 million.

**Industry.** Restoration contractors restore property to its prior condition after disasters (water mitigation, mold remediation, fire cleanup, reconstruction), unlike remodelers who make planned changes. Restoration work usually involves multiple parties — insurer, property manager, and renter. Historically contractors depended on insurers and preferred-vendor programs, but insurers constrained them, controlled costs, and made final decisions. From the early 2000s, firms including ARS shifted toward property management companies and institutions (colleges, schools, hotels, assisted living), offering 24/7 live phone response, training, daily communication, and disaster planning services (gaining traction after Superstorm Sandy in October 2012). The industry remained highly fragmented with few national firms; large insurers and property managers wanted providers with national reach. Belfor was the top national provider ($1.3 billion revenue, 300 offices in 29 countries; U.S. subsidiary with 80 offices and 3,800 employees), growing by acquisition while keeping power centralized; American Technologies, the next-largest non-franchise firm, had 15 branches and ~$111 million revenue. Franchisors SERVPRO (1,500 franchises) and ServiceMaster Clean (3,000 franchises, $140 million revenue) had geographically restricted territories and autonomous operators, with limited quality consistency, relationship cultivation, or referral incentives. Third-party administrators (Contractor Connection, Alacrity) matched contractors to insurers' preferred-vendor programs for a percentage of each loss, simultaneously acting as competitors and as customers who could raise fees unilaterally and impose strict demands.

**ARS.** Founded in 1987 in his brother's basement in Brookline, Massachusetts, ARS progressed from painting/cleaning to remodeling and construction, then by the late 1990s became a full-service restoration and reconstruction company — a deliberate choice because restoration was recession-proof and offered better margins, since equipment generates revenue while few costs accrue. ARS grew by building networks and relationships (boards of RHA, NEAHMA, IREM), giving free training to priority service agreement (PSA) customers (others paid $200 per person), and diversifying away from insurers, who fell from 90% of business in 2005 to 35% in 2013, while up to 60% of customers were property management firms with PSAs. A live person answered phones 24/7/365, calls were qualified, small crews handled minor losses and larger jobs drew on seven other offices, project managers wrote insurance estimates under prearranged unit pricing, and ARS sent all interested parties daily updates on work, equipment, and next steps, which reduced customer fear.

**RA's formation and structure.** The four founders had met through Business Networks, founded by Les Cunningham in 1986, a peer-network organization Piltch credited as "the number-one reason ARS has been successful." Earlier collaborative attempts had failed through overpromising, underdelivering, and lack of trust ("a shark tank," per Gersh). The 2011 kickoff was a National Restoration Summit hosted by ARS on March 24, which Piltch organized at no charge as a Go-Giver gesture. Catalysts included ARS's 2010 loss of Archstone (50,000 units) to a Belfor national contract and the capacity demands of catastrophes such as Sandy. RA was structured as an LLC with equal shareholder responsibility, a bylaws mission of collaborating to serve regional and national accounts with high workmanship, communication, and ethical standards, and a nine-person board with standing and ad hoc committees (including Service Area, Service Standards, and Membership). Members must be privately owned, independent, commercially focused regional firms with at least $5 million revenue and a dedicated marketing person, submitting an application with five commercial references; they paid $5,000 dues plus $12,000 for marketing, and referred projects generated 10% (mitigation/restoration/remediation) and 5% (repairs/reconstruction) fees, while associate members ($1 million revenue) paid 15% and 10%. Bylaws required affiliates to be active "Go-Givers," treat referred projects and client relationships as top priorities, and accept competitors; the board could terminate, penalize, or suspend members by supermajority vote.

**Technology and contracts.** In September 2013, RA hired a St. Louis association management company, and its first tasks included building a communication system, since job tracking was limited to Excel spreadsheets and Dropbox. RA marketed disaster-planning software, with two member-developed options — faciliSmart (Dean Mitchell) and SecureCore (RestoreCore) — and an undecided choice of which to market and how to compensate developers. Impressed by RA's national coverage and software (which Belfor lacked), Forest City Enterprises, the nation's fourth-largest property management company, invited ARS, Maxons, Dean Mitchell, and Carrera to its Cleveland headquarters and awarded a three-year nationwide contract, with referral fees split between ARS and RA.

**Open strategic questions.** These included the administrator's authority versus the board's, member transparency and information sharing, customer-facing contact strategy, consistent service standards (adopting S500/S520 standards versus creating RA's own), pricing on referred jobs, whether referral fees undermine the collaborative spirit, what defines a customer, and internal competition over overlapping territories (resolved by "primary" and "secondary" designations, territorial splits, or client choice). RA also debated how to market itself as 21 separate businesses. Piltch viewed RA as a low-risk growth strategy and wanted to resolve these issues so other members could assume more leadership responsibility.

The passage presents a general framework for constructing codensity presentations of monads, summarized by the principle “Codensity Monads = Density + Duality.” A codensity setting consists of a dual adjunction, a dense functor, an equivalence, and a functor decomposed as \(F \cong RG^{op}E\). The main theorem shows that the monad induced by this adjunction is the pointwise codensity monad of \(F\). This reduces codensity questions to generally better-understood questions about density and duality.

The method yields short, uniform presentations for ultrafilter monads on sets and topological spaces; filter monads on sets and topological spaces; neighbourhood and other double-dualization monads; and Isbell duality. It also covers Vietoris monads on Stone spaces, the lower Vietoris monad on topological spaces, and the sobrification monad.

For probability theory, the framework provides codensity presentations of the expectation, Giry, Radon, and Kantorovich monads, as well as an \(S\)-valued measure monad on Stone spaces. Integral representation theorems are identified as the main nontrivial ingredient for these examples. The passage concludes by proposing extensions to monads in 2-categories, monad extensions or pushforward monads, and additional Vietoris-type monads.

This passage presents an extended memorial tribute to Henry Clay, portraying him as a nationally prominent statesman whose life paralleled the rise of the United States. Born in Hanover County, Virginia, on April 12, 1777, Clay practiced law in Kentucky before serving nearly five decades in public office. He served repeatedly in Congress as Speaker, briefly as Secretary of State, and several terms in the Senate. He helped bring Congress toward war with Great Britain in 1812, participated in negotiating peace, and played leading roles in resolving the Missouri admission crisis, Nullification, and conflicts over slavery in newly acquired territories. He also unsuccessfully sought the presidency three times.

The tribute emphasizes Clay’s eloquence, judgment, determination, devotion to liberty, and concern for national unity. It credits him with supporting South American and Greek independence and describes him as a trusted crisis statesman. On slavery, it says he opposed it in principle, supported gradual emancipation in Kentucky, owned slaves, and believed immediate abolition would endanger both liberty and the Union. He was an early member and longtime president of the American Colonization Society, which he viewed as a gradual means of emancipation and African advancement. The passage concludes by mourning Clay as a champion of freedom whose national service was said to have contributed to his country’s prosperity and stability.

The disclosure describes a messaging system incorporating virtual object machine learning to classify dynamic subjects such as animals and human hands. Synthetic training data is generated from rigged 3D models whose poses, textures, backgrounds, lighting, and camera viewpoints can be varied programmatically. Marker metadata identifies joints and other regions of interest, enabling creation of large, labeled image sets without manually positioning subjects or tagging every image.

The virtual object machine learning system includes interface, model, gesture, model-texture, environment, machine-learning, and render engines. The render engine produces training images from combinations of 3D models, poses, textures, environment settings, and virtual cameras. The machine-learning engine trains classifiers using schemes such as support vector machines, logistic regression, k-nearest neighbors, and neural networks, as well as unsupervised methods. Classifiers can identify an object’s type, pose, or gesture, detect key points, and generate pixel-mask data. Training may occur on a server, with the resulting model transferred to client devices for image classification.

The messaging environment includes messaging client applications, an API server, an application server, and a database server. The application server hosts messaging, image-processing, and social-network systems, while client and server systems also provide ephemeral timers, collection management, annotations, and virtual object machine learning. Collections can include personal, live, and location-based stories. The annotation system can provide geolocation-, user-, or merchant-based media overlays containing text, images, logos, animations, sound effects, and visual effects.

Database structures store messages, entities and relationships, annotations, images, videos, and story collections. Messages can contain text, image, video, and audio payloads; annotations; duration and geolocation parameters; story identifiers; tags; and sender and receiver identifiers. Ephemeral timer systems separately control message display, participation within a story, and the overall story duration, removing expired messages and related interface indicators.

In one example, a client device captures an image of a Labrador retriever, a trained model identifies the dog as playful, and the annotation system overlays corresponding text before the image is published. The disclosure also describes representative layered software and hardware architectures in which the described methods may execute using processors, memory, storage, and input/output components.

The paper introduces AI-Noether, a formal abductive-reasoning system for reconciling data-derived polynomial hypotheses with canonical scientific theory. Given known polynomial axioms that do not imply a target hypothesis, AI-Noether searches for the smallest additional axioms that would make the hypothesis derivable. It requires neither data for the missing axioms nor prior knowledge of the variables they involve, and can report that no single missing axiom suffices.

The method has three stages: encoding the axioms and hypothesis as an ideal and its geometric variety; decomposing the variety into irreducible components that expose residual constraints; and testing component generators using Gröbner bases, variable elimination, and projection onto the hypothesis variables. Candidates are retained when their addition allows the target hypothesis to be derived.

The system is presented as distinct from conventional explainability tools such as LIME and SHAP because it seeks missing scientific axioms rather than merely explaining a model’s local predictions.

Tests covered physical systems including Kepler’s third law, Compton scattering, Einstein’s equations, escape velocity, light damping, Hagen–Poiseuille flow, neutrino decay, Hall effect, and the carrier-resolved photo-Hall effect. The reported experiments recovered every single removed axiom in the listed systems. When pairs or triples of axioms were removed, recovery rates across six benchmarks ranged from 25% to 60%, with most failures involving three missing axioms. The paper also provides a sufficient recoverability criterion based on ideal height and associated primes.

The approach is limited to laws expressible as real polynomials; future work is proposed for ordinary and partial differential equations and for reconciling new data-driven discoveries with prior literature.

Nanyang Polytechnic researchers developed a process to convert coffee waste into biodegradable plastic. After adding water and Cupriavidus necator bacteria, the mixture is left for seven to 10 days, allowing the bacteria to consume the waste and produce the biopolymer PHA for extraction. The butter and sugar in Nanyang coffee naturally support bacterial growth. The team replaced heavy solvents with acetone and an alkaline solvent, reducing waste and costs by about 50%, then genetically modified the bacteria to raise PHA purity above 50%, yielding roughly 1–3 grams per 100 grams of coffee waste. PHA decomposes faster and releases fewer toxic compounds than PVC. After laboratory experiments began in 2013, the team is seeking industrial partners and aims to commercialise the process within three to five years.

The Iowa Supreme Court reversed and remanded a district court decision that had allowed Gary G. Kehde to receive unemployment benefits. Kehde was discharged from Dubuque Packing Company after a supervisor found him holding a lit marijuana cigarette on company premises during a work break. Administrative proceedings found that the conduct violated a known company rule and constituted misconduct, disqualifying him from benefits. Kehde maintained that he did not know of the rule, was not intoxicated, and initially claimed the cigarette belonged to another employee, but later conceded possession.

Dubuque Pack sought to withdraw its protest after Kehde’s union obtained an arbitration decision. The appeal board declined to allow the withdrawal, and Kehde sought judicial review without requesting rehearing. The court held that a rehearing application was not a prerequisite to judicial review, so the district court had jurisdiction. It also held that, because eligibility is determined from the facts—not merely whether an employer protests a claim—withdrawal of the protest did not affect the decision, making any error harmless. Finally, the court found substantial evidence of misconduct: possession of marijuana on company premises was deliberate, unlawful, and violated legitimate employer safety expectations. Kehde therefore remained disqualified from unemployment benefits.

A regulation American football field is 120 yards long and 53.3 yards wide, covering approximately 1.32 acres, with 100 yards between the end zones. Each end zone is 10 yards deep. Goal lines are 100 yards apart, and breaking either goal line with any part of the ball scores a touchdown. Short white lines mark each yard, solid lines appear every five yards, and numbers generally mark every 10 yards. Hash marks guide ball placement and vary by level: 18 feet 6 inches apart in the NFL, 40 feet in college, and 53 feet 4 inches in high school. Sideline numbers help coaches align players and are typically 12 yards from the sideline in the NFL, 9 yards in college, and 6 yards in high school. Six-foot-wide sidelines define the field’s boundaries, and coaches commonly must remain between the 25-yard lines.

Industry-sponsored trials are becoming increasingly complex, increasing participant and staff burdens and costs despite ICH guidance recommending reductions in irrelevant data collection. Merck’s “Lean Design” project rebuilds schedules of assessment (SoAs) from “Ground Zero,” requiring biological justification, justified timing and frequency, appropriate subsampling, and exclusion of irrelevant routine-care data. The Faro Smart Design Tool estimates participant burden, visit and staff time, resource needs, costs, blood volume, and operational complexity in real time.

Merck applied Lean Design workshops to six late-stage protocols across cardiovascular disease, psychiatry, cancer, and other conditions. Teams retained primary endpoints, adverse-event collection, and essential administration while reviewing proposed assessments individually. Some examinations and laboratory panels were omitted or reduced, and selected assessments were limited to smaller participant subsets. Comparing original, recommended, and adopted SoAs showed substantial potential savings, including 4–47 participant hours per participant per trial. For one cardiovascular trial, a $9,000 per-participant reduction would save nearly $120 million. Teams adopted some, but not all, recommendations because protocols were late in development, teams were uncomfortable with uncertainty, and they worried about regulatory expectations.

The authors concluded that rebuilding SoAs from first principles with quantitative feedback can substantially reduce inessential assessments, burdens, costs, and complexity. Reported estimates excluded downstream data collection, monitoring, cleaning, reconciliation, analysis, and reporting costs, and results may differ outside Merck. Merck subsequently launched company-wide implementation and training in Lean Design principles.

**Summary**

This patent application (a continuation of U.S. Ser. No. 15/276,590, claiming Provisional No. 62/233,025) concerns an improved non-occluding intravascular blood pump designed to reduce hemolysis and blood clotting caused by high shear stresses at component "hotspots."

**Structure:** The pump includes a cylindrical shroud with an inlet and outlet, an impeller sharing the shroud's central axis, a centrally disposed motor that rotates the impeller to draw blood through the inlet and expel it through the outlet, and pillars coupling the motor to the shroud to hold it close to the impeller. Blood flows freely around the device, making it non-occlusive. Embodiments may be ventricular assist devices, axial flow pumps, or catheter-based circulatory heart pumps suited to NYHA Class III–IVa heart failure patients.

**Hemolysis-reduction design features:** a trumpeted shroud with a larger inlet than outlet; a smooth inlet transition; an inlet length of at least 1.5 times (up to 0.5–1.5 times) the shroud inner diameter, or about 9 mm or more in the explored embodiment, to prevent flow detachment; a bare hub length of 0.2–0.3 times the shroud inner diameter; raked-back impeller leading edges (60–90°, with 75–85° and 60–75° ranges specified); a wrap angle of 100±10°; shroud-to-blade clearance of 200–300 microns (at least 250±50 microns) to keep shear rates below a critical 10,000–50,000 s⁻¹; matching stator and impeller flare angles and hub/tip diameters; pillar angles matched to the outlet blade angle within 5–10° with rounded edges; and mismatched pillar counts and alignment relative to impeller blades. The shroud may be formed by laser-patterning nitinol and rolling it cylindrical, with hook-shaped strut tips.

**Analysis approach:** Development proceeded in three phases, addressing hydraulic design (about 6 mm diameter pump, descending aorta placement, series operation with the left ventricle), then minimum hemolysis with wide operating range. Transient CFD simulations and hotspot analysis identified major shear concentrations at the impeller, inflow shroud, and pillars, with detached turbulent flow reaching the impeller leading edge and producing asymmetrical shear. Blood damage was estimated by Lagrangian particle tracking over 3000 path lines using Heuser constants (C = 1.8×10⁻⁶, α = 1.991, β = 0.765) and Bludszuweit cumulative damage with Von Mises stress, yielding comparative rather than absolute values.

**Results:** Impeller maximum shear stress fell by 150–200 Pa, mean impeller shear dropped below 400 Pa up to 30,000 rpm, and experimental NIH improved 78% at 20 k rpm to a level comparable to the BP80 reference pump. Flow loop testing confirmed maintained flow rate and pressure generation, with a small hydraulic output increase and reduced shaft power. Fifteen impeller prototypes were tested over 18–25 k rpm; the best combination was impeller P_31 (extended hub, revised blade angles, wrap angle, and rounded leading edge), 30°-oriented pillars, and an extended inlet shroud, yielding lower predicted hemolytic potential, greater efficiency, and improved flow guidance.

Asteroid 2025 TF, estimated at 1–3 meters across, passed over Antarctica on October 1 at 00:47:26 UTC, coming within 428 ± 7 km of Earth’s surface. The Catalina Sky Survey detected it only hours after the flyby, and ESA astronomers used Las Cumbres Observatory observations at Siding Spring to determine its trajectory with exceptional precision. Objects this small generally pose no serious threat, though they may create fireballs or leave small meteorites. The report contrasts them with roughly 20-meter asteroids, which can cause damaging airbursts, and much larger objects, which may have regional or global consequences. Survey and follow-up networks support planetary defense by cataloging near-Earth objects, refining their orbits and improving impact predictions.

Molecular dynamics simulations compared SNAP, EAM, FS-1, and FS-2 interatomic potentials for primary radiation damage in pure niobium at 300 K and PKA energies of 1–75 keV. All potentials reproduced rapid Frenkel-pair production, partial recombination, and stabilization of residual defects. Surviving Frenkel pairs increased with energy under a two-regime power law, with a transition near 20 keV corresponding to the onset of subcascade formation. Potential choice strongly affected defect production, clustering, and morphology.

EAM generated the strongest short-range repulsion and a balanced mixture of C15-like rings and 1/2⟨111⟩ loops, with rare ⟨100⟩ clusters. FS-2 produced predominantly large 1/2⟨111⟩ dislocation loops, accounting for over 70% of its defects. FS-1 and SNAP favored compact, disordered, and C15-like clusters; SNAP generated C15 rings up to nine atoms, which may evolve into 1/2⟨111⟩ or ⟨100⟩ loops. Vacancy clustering exceeded interstitial clustering for every potential, and maximum cluster sizes generally increased with energy. SNAP and FS-2 also reproduced the DFT-supported ⟨111⟩ self-interstitial dumbbell, unlike EAM and FS-1, which generally favored ⟨110⟩ configurations. Overall, the results show that potential selection strongly influences niobium’s predicted radiation-damage structures.

The study examines machine-learning-assisted genome-wide association studies (GWAS), in which machine learning imputes missing phenotypes before association testing. Conventional methods often treat imputed values as observed, ignore imputation uncertainty, and target an estimand different from SNP effects on the true phenotype unless effects are identical across all SNPs. This can produce false-positive associations despite high imputation accuracy or genome-wide genetic correlation.

In a UK Biobank type 2 diabetes benchmark, GWAS on imputed liability had an 81% replication-failure rate against ground-truth UK Biobank associations and 48% against the DIAMENTE study. Several false positives reflected variants influencing HbA1c through erythrocytic rather than glycemic pathways. Theoretical analysis showed that existing approaches are weighted combinations of observed- and imputed-phenotype GWAS and therefore depend on strong, generally unrealistic conditions for validity.

The authors introduce Post-prediction GWAS (POP-GWAS), which combines summary statistics from three GWAS: observed phenotypes in labeled samples, imputed phenotypes in labeled samples, and imputed phenotypes in unlabeled samples. The difference between observed and imputed effects in labeled samples is used to debias each SNP’s imputed-outcome estimate. The method requires no assumptions about the imputation algorithm, predictors, or imputation quality; provides unbiased estimates and calibrated error rates; is never less powerful than GWAS using only observed phenotypes; supports binary traits, relatedness, overlapping samples, and selection bias; and requires only summary statistics.

Simulations confirmed POP-GWAS’s validity and power advantages. In the type 2 diabetes application, all identified loci replicated, no false-positive erythrocyte variants remained significant, and POP-GWAS identified 13 loci versus six from conventional GWAS. POP-GWAS was also shown to be the best linear unbiased estimator and to have a finite effective-sample-size bound for fixed imputation accuracy.

Applied to DXA-derived bone mineral density across 14 UK Biobank skeletal sites, POP-GWAS increased effective sample size by 9.7%–50.7% and identified 188 loci, 39% more than conventional GWAS. Meta-analysis brought the total to 303 loci, including 89 novel loci. The analyses revealed site-specific genetic architecture, enrichment in bone-related pathways and regulatory regions, osteoclast colocalization at 18 genes, and evidence that WWOX upregulation may causally increase bone mineral density. A head-specific association was identified at LGR5. The study notes that the bone-density analysis was largely limited to participants of European ancestry and provides public software, summary statistics, and a power calculator.

The paper studies algebraic generalizations of computational problems using semirings, noting applications in algorithms, automata, optimization, machine learning, database provenance, and logic. It defines semiring semantics for propositional logic, first-order logic, and existential second-order logic, including constants from the semiring, formula inequalities, weighted interpretations, and Boolean-style existential relation quantification. It also introduces a semiring version of BSS machines and defines the non-deterministic polynomial-time class \(NP_K\), its reductions, and completeness. For positive, commutative, nontrivial semirings, the paper proves \(ESO_K = NP_K\), an analogue of Fagin’s theorem, by existentially encoding machine computations with relations. It also generalizes the connection between the Boolean part of \(NPR\) and \(\exists\mathbb R\) to positive commutative semirings. Further results include a Cook-theorem analogue and completeness of the true existential theory of \(K\) for the Boolean part of \(NP_K\), using a non-arithmetic reduction.

The study develops a framework for designing dilute Boger fluids with prescribed shear modulus \(G_0\), relaxation time \(\tau\), and first normal-stress difference coefficient \(\psi_1\) by adjusting polymer concentration \(c\), molecular weight \(M\), and solvent viscosity \(\eta_s\). Model fluids used polyisobutylene in a polybutene–mineral-oil solvent and were characterized using oscillatory and rotational rheometry.

Polybutene–mineral-oil solvent viscosity followed \(\eta_s \approx 0.022\exp(10.3\phi_{PB})\) Pa·s. Polymer concentrations below the overlap concentration, generally under 0.6 wt%, produced dilute fluids; above it, polymer shear thinning became significant. A single-mode Zimm model adequately described the dynamic moduli. The polymer–solvent parameter \(\chi\), obtained from high-frequency modulus ratios, averaged \(0.30 \pm 0.023\), while \(G_0\) and \(\tau\) were fitted at intermediate frequencies. Rotational measurements showed that the standard Zimm/Oldroyd-B estimate \(\psi_1=2\chi G_0\tau^2\) overpredicts measured stress; the corrected relation was \(\psi_1=2\delta\chi G_0\tau^2\), with \(\delta\) typically 0.2–0.4.

Measured scalings were \(G_0\propto c^{1.00}M^{-0.93}\eta_s^{0.01}\), \(\tau\propto c^{0.10}M^{1.54}\eta_s^{0.84}\), and \(\psi_1\propto c^{1.41}M^{1.86}\eta_s^{1.61}\), with corresponding concentration, molecular-weight, and solvent-viscosity dependence for \(\delta\chi\). These empirical relationships formed an invertible matrix that enabled unique design recipes for the model system. Five fluids demonstrated independent control of \(G_0\) and \(\tau\), while three fluids maintained nearly constant \(\psi_1\) despite substantially different viscosities. The framework can potentially be adapted to other flexible-polymer Boger fluids, estimate properties beyond rheometer torque limits, and infer polymer degradation or scission, although fitting reliability, commercial-polymer polydispersity, and the high-shear decline of \(\psi_1\) remain limitations.

The forwarded Texas Monthly article traces Enron’s transformation from a debt-burdened pipeline company into an energy-trading powerhouse and examines the culture and business decisions behind its 2001 collapse.

After Ken Lay helped engineer Houston Natural Gas’s 1985 sale and established Enron, he hired consultant Jeff Skilling. Skilling proposed the “Gas Bank,” which allowed Enron to contractually guarantee gas supply and prices, buy and sell gas directly, and assume trading risk. Initially rejected by executives, the idea was supported by Lay and quickly generated major profits. Enron subsequently dominated natural-gas trading and expanded into electricity, bandwidth, broadband, water, and other markets.

Enron recruited highly educated, aggressive employees and rewarded rapid results with high salaries, uncapped bonuses, prominent titles, and extensive perks. This created a demanding culture centered on immediate profits and intellectual capital. Internal competition intensified through the Performance Review Committee, a forced-ranking system nicknamed “rank and yank” that regularly removed employees considered weak performers. Workaholism, monitoring, restrictive confidentiality agreements, and weakened teamwork became common. Under Skilling, Enron increasingly abandoned long-term assets and projects in favor of short-term returns, subjective mark-to-market accounting, and the practice of recognizing profits upfront.

Skilling rose to president and chief operating officer in 1997 and became CEO in February 2001. During his tenure, Enron traded a widening range of commodities, launched the successful EnronOnline platform, entered broadband and bandwidth trading, and arranged a Blockbuster movie-on-demand deal. The company also sought to shed physical infrastructure, including pipelines and power plants. Rebecca Mark, who had built Enron International, was removed from a central role and made head of Azurix, a water company created through a multibillion-dollar acquisition. Azurix struggled, its stock fell from $19 to $5, and it was folded back into Enron after Mark resigned.

Enron’s troubles intensified in 2001. Its role in California’s electricity crisis made it a target for criticism concerning deregulation and political influence, while Skilling’s responses drew further criticism. The telecommunications market collapsed, the Blockbuster venture faltered, and analysts questioned Enron’s accounting, profits, asset sales, and executive stock-option transactions. The stock declined from $80 in January to roughly $35 by early November. The economic downturn contributed to the decline, but the article emphasizes Enron’s aggressive culture, internal competition, and emphasis on short-term profits.

Skilling resigned abruptly after six months as CEO, saying Enron had consumed his family life and financial well-being. Lay returned as CEO, promised to limit innovation to Enron’s core business, reduce broad trading, and reconsider the Performance Review Committee’s effect on morale. Skilling, whose net worth remained heavily tied to Enron, defended his decisions and later expressed interest in Houston’s future as a center for commodity trading.

The study conducted a multi-ancestry transcriptome-wide association study (TWAS) of general cognitive function, white matter hyperintensities (WMH), and Alzheimer’s disease (AD), using genotype and gene-expression data from 1,032 African-ancestry (AA) and 801 European-ancestry (EA) participants in GENOA and summary statistics from published GWAS. The METRO method jointly modeled gene expression across ancestries while accounting for linkage disequilibrium differences and effect-size heterogeneity. FOCUS fine-mapping then identified 90% credible sets of potentially causal genes, and functional enrichment characterized associated pathways.

Before fine-mapping, METRO identified 602 genes associated with general cognitive function, 45 with WMH, 231 with AD using an EA GWAS, and nine with AD using an AA GWAS at a Bonferroni-corrected threshold of \(P<2.90\times10^{-6}\). Fine-mapping reduced these sets to 266 genes across 172 regions for cognitive function, 23 across 15 regions for WMH, 69 across 56 regions for EA AD, and two genes in the AA AD analysis. Eighty-two, 12, and 45 fine-mapped genes for cognitive function, WMH, and EA AD, respectively, had not been identified in the corresponding original SNP-based or gene-based analyses. The AA AD analysis identified APOE and PVRL2 in the APOE region, while TOMM40 was reported as the sole overlap between the EA and AA AD analyses.

Fine-mapped cognitive-function genes were enriched for protein binding, developmental cell growth, protein metabolism, neuron-to-neuron synapses, and neuron projection. WMH genes were enriched for zinc-finger motifs, miRNA has-212-5p, and retinal inner plexiform layer, with newly identified genes enriched for ZNF690 and the ClpX protein-degradation complex. EA AD genes were enriched for amyloid-fibril formation, amyloid-beta clearance, microglial activation, amyloid-beta metabolism, and neurofibrillary tangles; newly identified genes were associated with hematopoietic cell lineage and neurofibrillary tangles. The two AA AD genes were enriched for coreceptor-mediated virion attachment to host. Overall, the findings implicated innate immunity, vascular dysfunction, and neuroinflammation.

ICA1L was the only gene remaining in overlapping credible sets for WMH and EA AD. Lower ICA1L expression was associated with greater AD risk and more WMH, linking overlapping AD and vascular-dementia neuropathology, although potential adverse effects limit its current prioritization as a drug target. TOMM40 also appeared in both EA and AA AD analyses, and genes previously linked to AD, strokes, immune disorders, and neurodegeneration were among the EA AD findings.

For WMH, 65.2% of genes received stronger contribution from EA than AA expression models. Contributions were more similar between ancestries for cognitive function and both AD analyses, which may have improved the detection of genes relevant to AA populations.

Major limitations were the use of gene expression from immortalized B-lymphoblastoid cell lines rather than brain or other disease-relevant tissues, correlated TWAS tests for nearby genes, reliance on predominantly EA GWAS summary statistics, and insufficient power in the smaller AA AD GWAS. The authors concluded that integrating expression data across ancestries can improve the identification and interpretation of gene-trait associations and may facilitate generalization beyond EA populations and the development of dementia treatments or preventive targets.

This June 7, 2001 compilation of news clippings centers largely on Enron's business activities and troubles.

**Chicago electricity deal.** Enron Corp. and Exelon unit Commonwealth Edison Co. signed an agreement to supply power to Chicago and 47 suburban communities — the largest such deal since Illinois deregulated in 1997. Enron will provide 60% of the 400 megawatts contracted annually, with ComEd supplying the rest; contract terms were undisclosed. Separately, Mayor Richard Daley proposed the city buy 60% of its municipal electricity needs from Enron in an eight-year deal, cutting the city's $50 million annual electric bill by about $3 million, with ComEd providing the remainder. Environment Commissioner William Abolt acknowledged the California implications of Enron's involvement, while Enron said it stands by customer contracts at agreed rates.

**Dabhol Power (Enron's Indian unit).** A three-day meeting of Indian and foreign lenders in Singapore ended "positively," with no further Singapore meetings planned. The $3 billion, 2,184-megawatt project is in dispute with its sole customer, the Maharashtra State Electricity Board (MSEB), which stopped buying power after failing to pay about $48 million in December and January bills and objecting to Dabhol's high tariffs (INR7.1/kWh versus INR1.5 from others). Enron owns 65%, MSEB 15%, GE 10% and Bechtel 10%. Phase one (740 MW) is operational; Phase two (1,444 MW, more than 90% complete) is in doubt, with one source saying completion would require $500 million and roughly $30-40 million owed to contractors led by Bechtel, and no loan disbursements in three months. IDBI Executive Director R.S. Agarwal denied lenders proposed mothballing Phase two, saying that was Dabhol's own proposal to suspend construction about a year, forwarded to lenders' engineer Stone & Webster for a commercial assessment. Dabhol had set an informal mid-June deadline on continuing construction, and lenders are trying to steer the government toward finding additional buyers. Indian lenders have extended about $1.4 billion in unsecured loans, versus about $600 million in government guarantees received by foreign lenders (ABN Amro, Citibank, Bank of America, Credit Suisse First Boston), which had approved Dabhol's termination notice in April. Indian Prime Minister Atal Behari Vajpayee expressed confidence of a resolution; the government directed the Central Electricity Authority to scout for buyers, while private power producers welcomed the high-level attention. Dabhol also plans to court challenge a Maharashtra regulator order barring it from seeking international arbitration until June 14. Business Standard reported DPC claims the power purchase agreement remains in force and that it will bill MSEB for Phase two power, and that the plant load factor (DPC wants 90%) is the key dispute with the Godbole panel.

**Other Enron items.** Enron Broadband took part in a $30 million venture investment in AP Engines, led by Thomas Weisel Capital Partners; AP Engines develops software letting broadband providers carry data, voice, video-on-demand and video conferencing. A subsidiary pre-let an additional 1,170 sq m at 21 Grosvenor Place, London, to Enron Power Operations at £0.7 million annually, with a lease expiring in 2014 and refurbishment costing an additional £1 million.

**India reform commentary.** The Daily Deal reported that while Finance Minister Yashwant Sinha touts foreign investment liberalization, key privatizations — Air-India, Maruti Udyog and Videsh Sanchar Nigam — remain unsold, jeopardizing a $2.3 billion sales target; only $12 billion of $55.1 billion in approved FDI was actually invested between 1991 and 1998, and GDP growth fell from 6.6% to about 6%.

**Steel trade dispute.** GM, Stripmatic Products and other steel-consuming companies criticized Bush's order for an International Trade Commission investigation of steel imports, fearing tariffs would raise prices and cost jobs. About 8 million Americans work in steel-consuming industries versus roughly 160,000 steel producers; a coalition study (including Enron) estimated tariffs would cost 19,000-32,000 jobs while protecting about 3,700 steelworker jobs.

**Pacific Hydro.** Australia's best-performing index stock plans 114 wind turbines in Victoria, could build 1,000 turbines, and is expanding hydro in the Philippines and possibly Nepal; shares rose 8.8% to A$4.32 after a 15% weekly slump, though at 72 times earnings analysts questioned valuation.

**Chicago ward remap.** The City Council approved a blueprint 44-3 that avoids retrogression in minority voting strength, so Hispanic ward growth likely comes from the 23 white-majority wards; Ald. Dorothy Tillman voted against, disputing her chosen attorney, and Alds. Moore and Wojcik objected to procedural tactics. The Council also unanimously prohibited racial profiling by police.

**California power politics.** California regulators appear ready to vote on suspending direct access for large electricity users, a blow to the Keeley plan (backed by Gov. Davis's $2.76 billion deal to buy Southern California Edison's grid) that Enron has lobbied to preserve; the state Department of Water Resources risks a power surplus if large users leave, and utility users' group Utility Resource Management Group warned of rate increases. A Tribune editorial criticized California Attorney General Bill Lockyer's joking remark that he would like to escort Enron chairman Kenneth Lay to a prison cell, arguing Lockyer treats prison rape as acceptable.

A medRxiv preprint from Oregon Health & Science University examined hybrid immunity from combined SARS-CoV-2 vaccination and natural infection using two cohorts. The longitudinal cohort included 10 previously infected recipients of two-dose BNT162b2 and 20 matched participants without prior infection. The cross-sectional cohort included 20 vaccine-only participants and 46 with hybrid immunity—23 infected before vaccination and 23 with vaccine-breakthrough infections—whose exposure intervals ranged from 35 to 404 days. ELISA and live-virus neutralization assays measured antibodies against ancestral WA1 and the Alpha, Beta, Gamma, Delta, Omicron BA.1, and Omicron BA.2 strains.

Compared with vaccination alone, hybrid immunity produced significantly higher antibody levels and neutralizing titers against all tested strains. RBD-specific total antibodies increased 3.6-fold, primarily through higher IgG and IgA, while full-length spike-specific total antibodies increased 3.1-fold. Neutralizing titers increased 8.4-fold against WA1, 12.5-fold against Alpha, 22.7-fold against Beta, 9.6-fold against Delta, 19.0-fold against Omicron BA.1, and 13.3-fold against Omicron BA.2. Hybrid immunity also improved antibody potency and cross-neutralization of most variants.

Antibody levels and neutralizing titers increased with the time between vaccination and infection, with significant trends persisting in both infection-before-vaccination and breakthrough-infection groups. By day 400, modeled neutralizing increases ranged from 4.8-fold against Alpha to 17.6-fold against Omicron BA.1. Longer intervals also improved cross-neutralization of more vaccine-resistant variants, although neutralizing potency per antibody did not increase over time. Age and sex had weaker associations, while collection interval was not significantly associated with antibody measures.

The findings suggest that immune responses continue developing for more than a year after initial antigen exposure and that later vaccination or infection can substantially improve antibody quantity and breadth. The authors concluded that delayed vaccination may still provide substantial benefits and supported expanded vaccine access, while stating that intentional COVID-19 infection is not a reasonable public-health strategy.

Chiefs defensive lineman Chris Jones acknowledged that he did not pursue Trevor Lawrence on the Jaguars’ game-winning touchdown, saying he mistakenly believed Lawrence was down. Jones called the lapse a “teaching point,” promised it would not happen again and said he had already shifted his focus to the Chiefs’ upcoming game against Detroit’s top-scoring offense. He also said his X and Instagram accounts were deactivated before the game, not afterward to avoid criticism, and emphasized that he accepts constructive criticism.

DPI (UK), a Castle Donington-based maker of aluminium frames and lightboxes, received a grant of over £12,200 from Collaborate, an ERDF-funded project overseen by Leicester City Council. The money funds an automated saw enabling larger aluminium panels and bigger structures to be produced in the UK rather than imported, shortening contract times and eventually creating jobs. Launched three years ago by directors Sandra Wiggins and Paul Tomlinson, the company grew 37% last year. Collaborate grants of £5,000–£25,000 cover a third of capital costs.

Andrew W. Lo introduces MIT’s 15.401 Finance Theory, a 13-week course aimed primarily at first-year MBA students. He presents finance as a rigorous and practical field essential to business management, defining it as mathematics plus money and emphasizing that advanced quantitative preparation is not required. Examples of James Simons, Warren Buffett, and Jack Welch illustrate the range of mathematical and analytical skills used in finance.

Lo identifies two fundamental challenges in financial analysis: valuing assets and managing them. A classroom auction demonstrates price discovery under limited information: participants paid $45 for an undisclosed package containing an iPod Nano with a stated retail value of $149. He then introduces accounting as finance’s foundation, distinguishing stocks from flows and relating them to balance sheets and income statements. Corporate decisions are framed around cash raised, real investment, operating cash flow, reinvestment, and distributions, with the objective of maximizing shareholder wealth. He applies the same framework to personal household finance.

Time and risk are presented as the factors that make finance distinct from ordinary economic analysis. Lo introduces six basic principles, elaborating on the absence of systematic free lunches, preferences for more money, earlier money, and less risk, and self-interested behavior. The final lecture will examine limitations in these approximations and the role of market imperfections.

The course covers introductory concepts, valuation and discounting, asset pricing, risk, and corporate finance. Required work includes readings, participation, a case study, a midterm, and a final; grades are weighted 10% for the case study, 10% for attendance and participation, 25% for the midterm, and 55% for the final. Lo emphasizes active participation, practice problems, recitations, reviewing lecture notes, and applying course concepts to personal financial decisions.

President Trump’s description of the House-passed health care bill as “mean” has angered or confused some Republican conservatives he had pressed to support it, despite his earlier praise as “a great plan.” The remark came as Senate GOP efforts to create their own health care package were slowed by disputes over Medicaid expansion, coverage requirements and subsidies. Trump wants a “more generous” Senate version. GOP leaders target Senate passage by the July 4 recess, though Sen. John Cornyn suggested the end of July may be needed.

ARDD’s report, presented at Yarmouk University, praised Jordan’s government and UNHCR for rapidly establishing legal services and coordination mechanisms for Syrian refugees, including camp legal sections, free protection, documentation, awareness programs, and provider training. It said these services protect human rights and facilitate education and healthcare. Challenges remain, including changing needs, labour-market access, limited funding, and pressure on legal aid. A registration campaign registered 25,000 additional refugees.

The patent describes a hardware database privacy system that executes differentially private versions of analytical queries against private databases without exposing record-level information. Clients submit queries with specified privacy parameters; account management verifies the requests and updates privacy budgets, while query-handling and data-integration modules retrieve and merge required data. The privacy system modifies query operations according to client parameters and entity-imposed limits, then returns differentially private results for display.

The system defines differential privacy and global, local, and smooth sensitivity. Its engines support counts, means, medians, variances, interquartile ranges, batch- and stochastic-gradient models, random forests, histograms, model testing, synthetic databases, and validation. Outputs or computations are perturbed using Gaussian, Laplacian, or Cauchy noise and smooth-sensitivity bounds. Mean and variance queries use differentially private medians of aggregated sublists; random forests perturb leaf-label proportions; and histograms perturb bin counts directly or through private wavelet decomposition. Model testing generates differentially private thresholds and confusion matrices. The synthetic-database engine projects data into fewer dimensions while approximately preserving pairwise spatial relationships, allowing further analysis of the synthetic data. A validation engine tests queries on neighboring datasets and may reject those that fail the specified privacy definition.

Moody’s said India may meet its 3.3% fiscal deficit target for the year ending March 2019 by curbing capital spending. A Moody’s-ICRA poll found most respondents in Singapore and Mumbai expected slippage, citing rising oil prices and inadequate bank recapitalisation.
Sensors reveal greater noctule bats snatch birds from the sky at midnight.

The MSPM0C1105 and MSPM0C1106 datasheet, revised in September 2025, warns that electrostatic discharge can degrade or destroy integrated circuits and recommends proper handling precautions. Revision A updated power modes, package information, device specifications, CPU features, ADC ENOB with an external reference, DEVICEID and USERID tables, and added a DEGUGSS section while removing DGS32 data. The document provides mechanical, packaging, and orderable information, including package drawings, thermal-pad and solder-stencil guidance, tape dimensions, product-status, RoHS, moisture-sensitivity, and part-marking notes. It also includes Texas Instruments’ disclaimers regarding information accuracy, liability, technical resources, warranties, and applicable sales terms.

TyreWatch, a predictive tyre-management service launched on 16 May at Harwell Innovation and Science Campus, monitors fleet tyre pressure and temperature using wheel-rim sensors. Data is transmitted via cellular and satellite connectivity to a central server, where real-time information is analysed against vehicle-specific baselines and published through a secure web portal and push notifications. Drivers receive dash-mounted warnings, while AI recommends corrective action for escalating trends: maintenance alerts for gradual pressure loss and critical alerts for rapid changes. Monitoring continues after vehicles return to base, allowing punctures to be detected and potentially repaired before the next working day.

The open, white-label architecture can integrate with manufacturer-installed sensors, warning lights, load data and third-party telematics providers; complete retrofit hardware is also available. Audits reportedly found average fleet pressures 10% below manufacturer specifications, associated with 1% higher fuel consumption and 10% greater tyre wear. Testing reportedly prevented 95% of tyre-related breakdowns. The product was developed by the Pathway to Autonomous Commercial Vehicles consortium with £1.2 million in Innovate UK funding.

Against a Box & One “Chaser” defense, a ball-handling star can use double mid screens to drive in either direction, pass to a rolling screener or corner shooter, or use a drop pass when post help arrives. A screen-and-pop variation has one screener pop while the other rolls. If no shot is available, a reversal pass can initiate single/double continuity. Execution requires coordination, communication, timing, defensive recognition, and experience. Coaches should scout opponents, anticipate defensive reads, vary alignments and entries, and attack weaker defenders. In Box & One, four defenders cover areas in a box zone while one chaser exclusively denies the ball and rebounds.

Japanese government bonds firmed after a two-year auction drew bids 5.51 times the 2.2 trillion yen offered, well above the previous 3.82 times. The 10-year JGB yield was steady at 0.015%, while most other benchmark yields fell. The BOJ kept policy unchanged, maintained its 80-trillion-yen purchase guidance, and said less bond buying could still achieve its rate targets without disrupting markets.

The address offers gratitude for abundant harvests, continued peace, and civil and religious liberty, while urging citizens to use these blessings responsibly and devote their abilities to God and their own welfare.

Foreign relations are generally peaceful. The Russo-Ottoman War had not drawn France, Prussia, or Great Britain into participation, and hopes were expressed for a moderate settlement and renewed aid to the Greeks. Commerce with France continued to expand, although claims for losses suffered under the revolutionary governments remained unresolved. A likely favorable French response was anticipated. The northeastern boundary dispute with Great Britain was referred to the king of the Netherlands as umpire under the Treaty of Ghent and the 1827 convention. Congress was urged to consider British restrictions on direct colonial trade, which redirected commerce through other channels without reducing American exports, revenue, or navigation. A treaty of amity, navigation, and commerce with Austria was prepared for signature based on liberal intercourse and reciprocal fairness.

The address describes free trade and commercial reciprocity as longstanding American policies, supported by treaties with numerous European and American nations and by the abolition of discriminatory duties. The principal exception was renewed British colonial exclusion affecting the United States, prompting criticism of the commercial convention, which either government could terminate on twelve months’ notice. Danish indemnity claims were being resolved, with some settlements already completed. Relations with neighboring American countries remained friendly but unsettled: treaties with Mexico were pending, civil conflict obstructed commerce with Central America, and political upheavals affected Colombia and Peru, while peace between Buenos Aires and Brazil and partial compensation for American losses were welcomed.

Revenue and public finances were favorable. The projected 1829 Treasury balance was about $5.1 million, more than $12 million had been applied during the year to reducing public debt, and further exports of grain were expected to raise revenue sufficiently to extinguish another $10 million in principal in 1829. The recent tariff was defended as protection for domestic manufacturing and as a response to restrictive British laws, but Congress was advised to revise any provision that benefited one section of the country at another section’s expense. Its effect on revenue remained uncertain, although no decline in receipts was yet visible.

The address also discusses the constitutional balance between federal and state authority, warning that sustained conflict between national and state laws would harm the country. Army discipline was generally satisfactory. Federal policy toward Indian tribes had combined recognition as independent powers and landholders with efforts at conversion and civilization; greater success in acquiring land than in achieving those aims had created subsistence obligations and conflicts over sovereignty, requiring a remedy. Congress was also advised to consider the Secretary of War’s proposed plan.

Public works included coastal fortifications, roads, canals, river and harbor improvements, lighthouses, and other infrastructure, supported by roughly $2 million in annual expenditures and additional appropriations. West Point was presented as an essential national institution whose improvements would benefit the Army and society.

Navy reports described effective suppression of piracy, protection of neutral commerce, and the need to maintain forces near the Mediterranean. A coastal survey expedition for the Pacific and South Seas was nearing departure, and measures for naval improvement included ship-timber preservation, two new dry docks, and plans for navy-yard development. Postal administration had expanded from fewer than 200 offices to nearly 8,000, with substantial growth in revenue and routes, although expenses exceeded receipts by about $25,000. Congress was also asked to complete the District penitentiary, extend land-debt repayment terms, and authorize an improved fifth census, preferably beginning in spring, with broader age categories, better manufacturing returns, and greater compensation for enumerators.

Jammu and Kashmir Deputy Chief Minister Nirmal Singh said the government is considering vocational skill courses and optional curriculum papers. Visiting women’s colleges in Srinagar, he praised student projects involving mushroom cultivation, floristry, chocolate making and papier-mâché.

A fired Washington State Walmart employee returned to retrieve a safe he allegedly left there, which contained heroin and Xanax. He was arrested and booked for unlawful possession of a controlled substance.

A retrospective histopathologic study reviewed 30 adrenalectomy specimens from 2018 through September 2022 and examined adrenal vessels using H&E staining and immunohistochemistry. Normal adult adrenal veins consistently showed age-associated asymmetrical longitudinal smooth-muscle bundles, diminished or disorganized elastic tissue, and arterial-wall changes morphologically indistinguishable from fibromuscular dysplasia (FMD). Segmental arterial mediolysis (SAM) was commonly found in adrenal cortical adenomas and pheochromocytomas, with arterial hyalinization, macrophage accumulation, myxoid or fibrinoid medial degeneration, and intimal fibroplasia. Pheochromocytoma vessels were often thin-walled, with blood lakes lacking discernible endothelial lining.

No FMD or FMD-like lesions were identified in arteries outside the adrenal glands. Fetal adrenal vessels also lacked these abnormalities. Hemorrhage and vascular thrombosis were the most frequent complications. The findings suggest that FMD and SAM may represent a spectrum of vascular injury influenced by the local adrenal tissue environment, adrenal hormones, or hormone-receptor function, while providing a basis for further investigation of FMD at other sites.

Donna Adelson was sentenced to life in prison for orchestrating the 2014 murder-for-hire of her former son-in-law, Florida State University law professor Dan Markel, plus 30 years for conspiracy and solicitation to commit murder. Adelson maintained her innocence and claimed she would have stopped the plot had she known of it. Judge Stephen Everett said he could consider her “utter lack of remorse,” while her husband Harvey defended her account of events.

Microsoft Corporation’s Form 8-K dated October 26, 2021 reported its financial results for the fiscal quarter ended September 30, 2021. The press release was furnished as Exhibit 99.1 and deemed not “filed” for purposes of Section 18 of the Exchange Act.

IDC finds that public-cloud HPC is expected to become the leading architecture among industrial enterprises using or planning HPC, followed by hybrid-cloud systems and prebuilt systems. Cloud HPCaaS can offer scalability, flexibility, faster access to modern hardware and analysis methods, and cost advantages by shifting expenditure from CAPEX to OPEX. In-house clusters have expansion, maintenance, downtime, and agility limitations, although they may remain necessary for sensitive data. Hybrid architectures can keep sensitive analysis on-premises while using public-cloud capacity for peak loads or noncritical workloads.

Industrial HPC users consider HPC important for performance, innovation, security, resilience, collaboration, and new data-based products and business models. More than half see HPC optimization as important for developing new solutions, over 80% value security and resilience, and 81% of current HPC users intend to implement HPC-based business models. However, cloud HPC still requires trained IT and analysis personnel to configure clusters, run calculations, and interpret results.

IDC recommends virtual product and manufacturing development, lifecycle transparency, a holistic data strategy with a common database, and careful evaluation of on-premises, HPCaaS, or hybrid operating models. It also advises considering scalability, security, energy efficiency, and external expertise when selecting solutions.

The findings are based on a December 2021 telephone survey of 200 technology decision-makers at industrial enterprises with more than 500 employees in Germany, Austria, and Switzerland.
Two pieces of ammunition were found in a Litchfield High School bathroom Wednesday, prompting a lockdown. Police searched the school; students were dismissed to parents around 10 a.m.

The passage examines baseball’s growing emphasis on bullpens and relievers over starting pitching, a trend the Yankees have helped advance. New York has reinforced its bullpen with players such as Dellin Betances and five-year closer Aroldis Chapman, while managers increasingly remove starters after about five innings. Starting pitchers averaged 87 pitches per start in 2015, and quality starts became less common in 2016. Hall of Famer John Smoltz advocates longer starter appearances, arguing continued bullpen overuse slows games and creates “dead time.” MLB’s commissioner has considered reliever-use limits, with player association approval required.

A Boeing-funded study examined cold and flu transmission on 10 U.S. flights by testing cabin surfaces and air, observing passenger movement, and modeling contact with a hypothetical infectious aisle passenger. About 38% of passengers never left their seats, while aisle passengers moved most often and window-seat passengers least. The 11 passengers nearest an infected person had the highest risk, and modeling suggested that an average of one person among roughly 150 passengers would be infected. Researchers recommended that passengers seeking to limit exposure stay in window seats, though outside experts said the small study—which detected no viruses and observed only one coughing passenger—could not support broad conclusions about airline infection risks.

The passage reviews the SuperTrend indicator, a trend-following tool created by trader Oliver Seban that signals trend direction, continuation, and reversals by plotting a line above or below price (green above, red below) and flipping direction when a candle's close crosses the prior period's SuperTrend value. The indicator is built from a candle's median price ((H+L)/2) combined with Welles Wilder's Average True Range: Upper Band = Median Price + Multiplier × ATR, Lower Band = Median Price − Multiplier × ATR. The displayed line alternates between the bands, with the lower band unable to decrease and the upper band unable to increase. Seban's recommended inputs are an ATR period of 10 and a multiplier of 3, though common alternatives include lengths of 7, 10, 14, or 20 and multipliers of 1–3.

A long backtest of the S&P 500 index over 60 years on weekly bars, using default parameters, reinvesting capital without commissions, slippage, or dividends, and trading long only, produced 38 trades, a 65.79% probability of a winning trade, an accuracy/success rate near 67%, and a maximum drawdown of 24.6% versus 56.24% for buy-and-hold. The win rate is said to vary with market conditions, asset class, timeframe, and parameters, and thorough backtesting across conditions is advised. One example trade under the stated rules was a buy on 05/29/2020 at 3044.31 and a sell on 01/21/2022 at 4397.94, a gain of 1353.63 points or 44.46%. The authors judge the strategy highly accurate for capturing upswings while avoiding downswings, and note the indicator dates from the 1990s, giving roughly 40 years of out-of-sample performance.

The weekly timeframe is described as best, though intraday and daily use is possible, and suitable timeframes should be determined by backtesting. The indicator is characterized as lagging, since it derives signals from historical price data. Its benefits include clear trend direction, straightforward entry and exit signals, and filtering market noise; it also aids in setting stop-loss and trailing stop levels. It differs from moving averages, MACD, and RSI by combining price action with volatility, and it can be used alongside moving averages, RSI, and Bollinger Bands for added confirmation. It adapts to volatility by widening in volatile conditions and tightening when volatility is low, can be applied in ranging markets (identifying reversals and range boundaries, with parameters adjusted or confirmed by oscillators such as RSI or Stochastic), and is suitable for intraday trading when combined with other tools and risk management. Limitations noted include false signals and whipsaws in choppy or high-volatility markets, and its accuracy depends on instruments that tend to maintain directional trends.

Encode general counsel Nathan Calvin accused OpenAI of using subpoenas issued in its lawsuit against Elon Musk to intimidate nonprofit critics of California’s SB 53, implying Encode was secretly Musk-funded. Encode denies Musk funding and refused to provide documents. Calvin said OpenAI sought to weaken SB 53, which requires frontier-model developers to publish transparency frameworks and reports, report critical safety incidents, and share catastrophic-risk assessments under state oversight. OpenAI chief strategy officer Jason Kwon said subpoenas are standard in litigation and Encode’s funding and support for Musk raised legitimate questions. The allegations drew concern from OpenAI personnel, former employees, AI researchers, and watchdog founder Tyler Johnston, who also received a subpoena. Calvin praised OpenAI’s safety research but said its tactics threatened critical policy work.

The message reports that the country is at peace, national defense and public health are strong, industrial conflict has declined, and education and science continue to advance. Mortality and sickness rates have fallen, while private organizations, local authorities, states, and federal agencies are cooperating to provide relief during the economic depression. Federal loans through the Reconstruction Finance Corporation are intended to prevent hunger and exposure.

The worldwide depression continued, worsening after the European economic collapse and producing acute financial crises. Emergency policies are credited with averting economic disaster, and business indicators showed improvement after mid-1932. Federal credit expansion and RFC lending supported banks, agriculture, railways, industry, and individuals, but recovery also requires restored confidence. The message identifies three immediate priorities: reducing government expenditures and balancing the federal budget, reorganizing the banking system, and cooperating internationally to strengthen commodity prices and economic stability.

The proposed budget reduces appropriations by more than $830 million, partly offset by roughly $250 million in uncontrollable costs. Federal public-works activity would be limited largely to existing commitments and self-liquidating projects, with proposed next-year spending of $442.769 million, compared with $717.262 million for the current year. The furlough system would continue, supplemented by a temporary 11 percent salary reduction on earnings above $1,000. Certain veterans’ payments would be eliminated without reducing benefits for specified war-disabled or needy veterans. Revenue measures include replacing selected manufacturers’ excise taxes with a broadly applied uniform rate, while more than fifty executive and administrative agencies would be consolidated.

The banking system is criticized for amplifying the depression by impairing credit and contributing to failures, hoarding, and the loss of savings, homes, farms, and businesses. Since January 1930, 4,665 banks had suspended with $3.3 billion in deposits, and currency hoarding exceeded $1.6 billion at the crisis peak. RFC and Federal Reserve measures provided temporary relief but were not permanent solutions. The message calls for banking reorganization, stronger regulation and enforcement of safe practices, and changes to federal farm-loan and joint-stock land-bank systems, while rejecting currency inflation and direct government banking.

International economic cooperation is presented as essential to recovery. Proposed efforts include world disarmament, a world economic conference, stable currency and exchange rates, expanded trade, and cooperation on world peace and recovery. The United States rejected suspending European war-debt payments due December 15 but proposed addressing temporary exchange difficulties.

Additional legislative priorities include transportation and power regulation, antitrust reform, western range conservation, federal aid for child health, World Court membership, ratification of the Great Lakes–St. Lawrence Seaway Treaty, and revisions to bankruptcy laws and federal court procedure.

The message concludes that government action must preserve ordered liberty, individual and community responsibility, equality of opportunity, and private initiative. The federal government should regulate rather than compete in economic life except during emergencies, while encouraging voluntary cooperation. Social and economic policies, it argues, must conform to the nation’s historical traditions and spiritual foundations.

A Case Western Reserve University study estimates that the federal government spends $55 billion annually addressing the effects of childhood exposure to domestic violence. The study, published in The Journal of Family Violence, linked such exposure to increased health-care use, violent crime, and lost productivity from lower educational attainment. About 15.5 million U.S. children are exposed to intimate partner violence annually, and more than 25% experience it during their lifetimes. By age 64, an exposed child’s average lifetime cost to the national economy is nearly $50,000. Researchers said the findings can help policymakers support more effective prevention and treatment efforts.

The court denied plaintiffs’ request to enjoin NASD Regulation’s Rule 8210 demands requiring on-the-record interviews. Plaintiffs, including D.L. Cromwell Investments and four Cromwell employees, argued that Regulation was acting as the government’s agent, that the demands coerced them into violating their Fifth Amendment rights by asserting self-incrimination, and that Regulation had improperly used grand jury materials.

The court found no direct evidence that the U.S. Attorney’s office or another government agency encouraged or coerced Regulation’s Division of Enforcement. Although Regulation’s Criminal Assistance Prosecution Unit assisted federal investigators and shared facilities and systems with the Division of Enforcement, the court credited evidence that the Division’s investigation was independent. Contacts between government and Regulation personnel had legitimate explanations, so the interviews did not constitute governmental action.

The court also found no credible evidence of an unauthorized disclosure of grand jury materials. Although two documents shown to a Cromwell employee likely came from a warrant search, plaintiffs did not establish that those documents were matters occurring before a grand jury and were therefore protected by Rule 6(e). The court rejected plaintiffs’ analogy to the former-client confidentiality doctrine because the inquiry did not require disclosure of protected confidences. It suggested, however, that Regulation should strengthen controls separating its enforcement and criminal-assistance operations.

The passage criticizes We Energies’ high rates, executive pay, and rate increases, attributing them to its monopoly status, power-plant overbuilding, shareholder returns, and a Public Service Commission that largely approved utility requests. It says rates were once among the nation’s lowest under CEO Charlie McNeer, who prioritized affordability to retain businesses and jobs, but rose rapidly after his retirement. The passage compares We Energies with municipal utilities, which it says often charge less and are accountable to customers. While We Energies has proposed a rate freeze through 2019, the Citizens Utility Board and Initiative for Competitive Energy advocate a rate rollback, and broader business support for the freeze is growing.

Canadian Blood Services will open Canada’s largest blood donation clinic at Eau Claire Market on July 10, featuring 20 beds and replacing the 18-bed 13th Avenue S.W. clinic. With O-negative blood critically low, the organization needs 50,000 more donations by the end of June to reach its goal of 150,000 by July 1. Calgary is also building a blood operations facility scheduled to open in 2020.

F2 Logistics faces Generika-Ayala at 7 p.m. seeking a fourth straight win and the No. 2 seed in the 2018 Chooks to Go-PSL Grand Prix. Generika-Ayala earned its first victory by defeating Smart 4–1 after four losses. Sta. Lucia (2–3) plays winless Smart at 4:15 p.m., while F2 is favored but coach Arnold Laniog urged caution.

Members adopting the proposed specification must obtain licenses from SD-3C, LLC for any incorporated portions of SD Specifications versions 1.0 or 1.01. Host-device implementations require a SD Host Ancillary License Agreement, while memory-capable SD Cards require a SD Memory Card License Agreement. The Physical Layer Simplified Specification/Addendum is a non-confidential subset of the SD Card Association’s complete specification and is provided “AS-IS” without warranties. It disclaims responsibility for resulting damages or patent and other rights violations, grants no implied licenses, and creates no obligation to disclose confidential information.

The specification defines the physical interface and command protocol for SD Memory Cards, their operating environment, handling, registers, electrical characteristics, and related system behavior. SD Memory Cards are designed for security, capacity, performance, and environmental requirements in consumer electronics. Their content-protection system uses mutual authentication and a new cipher algorithm while permitting non-secure access to users’ content. An optional secondary security system based on standards such as ISO-7816 supports public-network, mobile-commerce, and digital-signature applications. The separate SDIO specification covers compatible cards providing high-speed, low-power I/O and optional memory storage.

Three memory-card capacities are defined: SDSC up to 2 GB, SDHC above 2 GB through 32 GB, and SDXC above 32 GB through 2 TB. Hosts supporting higher capacities must also support lower-capacity cards. Cards may be read/write, including flash, OTP, or MTP media, or read-only ROM cards with fixed content. They have a main User Area and a Protected Area whose total constitutes card capacity. Operating voltage is 2.7–3.6 V, while UHS-II cards also use VDD2 at 1.70–1.95 V.

The SD bus uses serial command, response, and data transfers. Commands contain address or parameter information protected by CRC, and data is transferred in single or multiple blocks. Cards receive session addresses during initialization. The interface supports standard and wide buses, SPI mode, and UHS-I and UHS-II operation. Defined speed classes range from unspecified Class 0 performance to minimum rates of 2, 4, 6, and 10 MB/sec. UHS-I provides up to 104 MB/sec over a four-bit bus for SDHC and SDXC cards through 3.3 V and 1.8 V signaling, with bus mode, driver strength, power limit, voltage switching, and sampling-point tuning commands. UHS-II adds high-speed differential lanes, including FD624 operation up to 624 MB/sec.

Cards contain identification, relative-address, capacity, configuration, status, and optional driver-stage registers. Reset can occur through power cycling or CMD0. UHS-II initialization includes PHY, device, enumeration, configuration, and SD-TRAN stages, while UHS-II hosts support both legacy SD and UHS-II interfaces.

The host controls all communication using broadcast or addressed commands. Card identification mode covers reset, voltage validation, initialization, CID retrieval, and RCA assignment; data transfer mode uses point-to-point commands with selected cards. Initialization includes CMD0, CMD8 for operating-condition verification, ACMD41 for voltage and capacity negotiation, CMD2 for CID, and CMD3 for RCA. Reads and writes can use single- or multiple-block transfers, with CRC protection, stop commands, and DAT0 busy signaling.
