Additional features include cache, self-maintenance, command queuing, low-voltage initialization, content protection, password locking, permanent and temporary write protection, and mechanical write-protect switches. Application Performance Classes specify minimum random and sustained sequential performance, with enhanced figures available when cache and command queuing are used. Reserved fields must generally be set to zero unless otherwise specified, and hosts and cards need not check them. The document also contains extensive chapters, diagrams, tables, references, terminology, host-design guides, SPI procedures, and mechanical drawings for SD and microSD form factors.

Prince’s music reached Spotify despite his lifetime opposition, prompting fans to view it as betrayal. Taylor Swift’s label withdrew her 2014 album from Spotify, citing music’s value; Garth Brooks has avoided Spotify and iTunes and plans to release his next album on his own website. Thom Yorke criticized Spotify despite Radiohead’s presence there. Beyoncé’s Lemonade remains exclusive to Jay Z’s Tidal, while Joanna Newsom denounced Spotify as a “villainous cabal of major labels.”

Market Research Future published a global Blowout Preventer market report, segmented by annular and RAM type, land and offshore wells, and region, with forecasts through 2021. Growth is linked to rising oil and gas demand, greater unconventional-resource and offshore exploration, and stricter safety standards. The report covers market structure, pricing, supply chains, Porter’s Five Forces, historical and forecast revenues, country-level analysis, and competitors. The Middle East is expected to dominate due to increased onshore drilling, while Asia-Pacific is projected for high growth because of its hydrocarbon potential.

Lake Lugano, in Switzerland's Italian-speaking canton of Ticino, is a quieter, less-visited alternative to crowded Lake Como. Lugano, the lake's largest city, offers a palm-lined waterfront promenade, café-filled piazzas, open-air markets, and a mild climate called the "Sunroom of Switzerland." Nearby hillside villages such as Gandria, Morcote, and Monte Bré see far fewer tourists, and guides recommend local ferries and funiculars instead of private transfers.

Attractions include small art museums such as the Museum of Art of Italian Switzerland, Monte San Salvatore's funicular and summit views, Monte Generoso's hiking trails, summit restaurant, and botanical gardens, and lakeside parks like Parco Ciano, Parco San Grato, and Parco Scherrer. The Olive Grove Trail links Gandria and Castagnola, and Gandria is reachable only by boat or on foot. Dining recommendations include Ticino merlot wine tasting, rustic food at Grotto Morchino, Locanda Gandriese, and the boat-accessible Grotto dei Pescatori Caprino, while the five-star Grand Hotel Villa Castagnola occupies a 19th-century lakeside villa. Both experts describe the region as ideal for couples, families, and older travelers wanting culture and nature without crowds.

Prime Minister Justin Trudeau and Public Safety Minister Ralph Goodale expressed sorrow but said there was no apparent terrorism or national-security link after a Toronto man allegedly drove a van into pedestrians on Yonge Street, killing 10 and injuring 15. Police arrested 25-year-old Alek Minassian as a large homicide investigation continued. Both ministers praised first responders and welcomed international condolences and offers of assistance.

European stocks opened slightly higher, led by energy shares as Brent crude reached a 30-month high following the shutdown of the leaking Forties pipeline. The FTSE 100 rose 0.2%, while the CAC 40 and DAX 30 gained 0.1%, ahead of decisions by US, British and eurozone central banks.

Outgoing Federal Reserve Chair Janet Yellen said she did not view recent Wall Street gains as a bubble, but warned that asset valuations were elevated and advised diversification. She described the U.S. economy and job market as strong, expressed disappointment at not serving a second term, and was succeeded by Jerome Powell.

Founded in 2016 and based in Madrid, Dunas Capital is an independent Spanish asset manager serving local and international institutions with traditional and alternative financial and real-estate investments. It reported approximately €4.5 billion in assets under management as of July 2025, more than 80 professionals, and supervision from Spain’s CNMV and DGSFP. Its philosophy prioritizes capital preservation, risk management, value investing, transparency, innovation, flexibility, experience, and sustainability.

Dunas manages portfolios through a risk-first, absolute-return approach. It uses estimated volatility to set risk budgets, invests flexibly across asset classes without sector, country, rating, or asset-type restrictions, applies value-investing techniques, and uses options and futures to limit tail risk.

Four non-indexed, conviction-driven mutual funds share the same management team and philosophy but offer different return and volatility targets. Dunas Valor Prudente, with nearly €1.5 billion in assets, targets 12-month Euribor plus 100 basis points with maximum volatility of 3%; Equilibrado targets Euribor plus 200 basis points and 6% volatility; Flexible targets Euribor plus 400 basis points and 10% volatility; and Audaz targets Euribor plus 600 basis points and 15% volatility. Its alternative investments cover infrastructure, renewable energy, transportation, and agriculture with sustainable and social-impact objectives.

The Pennsylvania Supreme Court held that the testator’s unqualified gift to his “grandchildren” included all grandchildren, including the children of his three afterborn children. The majority emphasized that clear testamentary language controls, disinheritance requires express words or necessary implication, and “per stirpes” determines shares without excluding any ancestral line. It dismissed the exceptions and confirmed the auditing judge’s account absolutely.

Stearne, J., joined by Sinkler, J., dissented. The dissent argued that the will’s overall scheme and surrounding circumstances showed that the testator intended “grandchildren” to mean only the issue of the four children named in the will. Because the afterborn children had already received shares by operation of law and their descendants had also been included in the trust, the majority’s construction would produce an unjust distribution. The dissent would have sustained the exceptions.

AMD’s SEV-ES Guest-Hypervisor Communication Block Specification Agreement permits recipients to review the specification only to design compatible products or provide feedback. It prohibits duplication, removal of notices, and transfer of rights; retains all AMD intellectual property; disclaims warranties and liability; permits unrestricted use of voluntarily submitted feedback; imposes export-law and U.S. government restricted-rights obligations; and specifies California law and venue in Santa Clara County.

The technical specification defines communication between SEV-ES or SEV-SNP guests and hypervisors. These technologies encrypt guest register state during world switches, preventing direct hypervisor access. VM exits are classified as automatic exits, which expose no guest register state, or non-automatic exits, where the guest controls which state is shared through the Guest-Hypervisor Communication Block (GHCB). The standard requires a 4 KB, page-aligned, decrypted/shared GHCB, standardizes required non-automatic exit events and minimum exchanged state, and defines VMGEXIT processing, VALID_BITMAP handling, error reporting, protocol negotiation, CPUID exchange, and SEV-SNP GHCB registration.

Version 2 adds a hypervisor feature bitmap and initial SEV-SNP support. Later revisions add 64-bit guest-request sequence numbers, malformed-input error codes, VLEK identification, APIC ID retrieval, multiple VMPL levels, page-state changes, the SEV-SNP Confidential Computing Blob EFI protocol, SEV-TIO, and Secure AVIC.

Specified events include IOIO and MSR protection, VMMCALL, MMIO page faults, SNP guest and extended guest requests, AP creation, restricted-injection doorbells, IPIs and timers, APIC ID lists, VMPL changes, SEV-TIO requests, Secure AVIC backing-page management, guest termination, and unsupported exits. The document also defines SNP secrets-page fields, firmware-to-OS page exchange, SMP AP-booting methods, AP jump tables, NMI handling, and hardware debug-register behavior. SMM and nested virtualization are not supported.

Tax authorities are likely to use net asset value, rather than discounted cash flow, to calculate the fair market value of unlisted shares for capital-gains tax. The proposal treats the higher of the sale price or prescribed FMV as consideration, potentially affecting start-ups and private-market investors.

The Dogs of the Dow (DOD) strategy selects the 10 highest dividend-yielding stocks among the 30 components of the Dow Jones Industrial Average. Investors allocate equal dollar amounts to those stocks and rebalance annually at the beginning of each calendar year. The strategy was popularized by Michael B. O’Higgins in his 1991 book *Beeding the Dow*, though related ideas appeared in 1951 and in *The Wall Street Journal* in the early 1980s.

Investors can implement DOD through individual stocks, ETFs, or mutual funds. ETFs may offer lower costs than buying stocks individually, and the listed funds are described as reasonably liquid.

The passage’s backtests show substantial underperformance versus the S&P 500. From August 1998, a $10,000 investment with dividends reinvested grew to about $60,000 in SPY, compared with $32,000 under DOD; the respective CAGRs were 7.7% and 5%. A second test starting in April 2014 produced values of $19,000 for SDOG, $11,600 for IDOG, $11,200 for EDOG, and $23,300 for SPY. Although SDOG performed best among the DOD ETFs, all underperformed the broader market. Because of DOD’s poor diversification and long-term results, the passage recommends using it only for a small portion of a portfolio.

Ibrahim Shehu Shema, former Katsina State governor, was remanded in Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC) custody on Tuesday over alleged money laundering of N5.7 billion SURE-P funds. Justice Babagana Ashigar of the Federal High Court in Katsina ordered his detention until 27 April 2018, when the court will hear the written bail application filed on 18 April. Shema pleaded not guilty to 26 charges, while lead counsel Emmanuel Ukala SAN sought bail, which the prosecution counsel, Sam Ologunorisa, opposed, arguing the offence warrants at least seven years' imprisonment without option of fine. Ashigar overruled the defendants' oral bail application and adjourned the matter.

FULE logically erases the full user area using CMD32 (0), CMD33 (user-area end), then CMD38 (00000002h). Hosts must check FULE_SUPPORT; unsupported cards perform ERASE. Incorrect sequencing sets ERASE_SEQ_ERROR, while other out-of-sequence commands set ERASE_RESET. Incomplete ranges trigger ERASE. FULE supports SDHC/SDXC, not SPI, and holds DAT0 low while active.

June 26, 2001 news clippings focused on California’s electricity crisis and related energy policies. FERC opened confidential settlement talks in Washington, D.C., led by administrative law judge Curtis Wagner, with roughly 140–150 representatives from California, other Western states, utilities, and generators. California demanded $8.9 billion in refunds for alleged overcharges since May 2000, while other states sought up to $6 billion. Generators denied overcharging, cited natural-gas shortages and market conditions, and said utilities owed them billions. Wagner urged compromise, estimated refunds might total roughly $2–$2.5 billion, and said he would recommend a solution to FERC if no settlement was reached. Issues included refund eligibility, long-term contracts, creditworthiness, PG&E’s bankruptcy, natural-gas prices, pipeline capacity, and legal immunity for suppliers.

New FERC commissioners Pat Wood and Nora Brownell met Gov. Gray Davis and California officials, promising cooperation, competition in the natural-gas market, greater inspections of idle plants, and consideration of refunds and gas prices. Three former Duke Energy employees alleged that Duke reduced output and discarded parts during shortages to inflate prices. Duke and the Independent System Operator said output changes followed grid orders for balancing reserves and disputed the allegations.

Other reports said state officials sought to suspend direct-access electricity enrollment because customers leaving traditional utilities could raise costs and endanger financing tied to roughly $50 billion in state power purchases; proposed legislation included exit fees. Additional coverage described growing solar subdivisions in San Diego, supported by falling panel costs and subsidies but constrained by manufacturing capacity, buyer interest, net-metering rules, and policy uncertainty, and questioned 42 pending power plants because of uncertain completion, pricing, and ownership.

COVIDFast is a laboratory-developed, extraction-free RT-qPCR assay for rapid, high-throughput SARS-CoV-2 detection. It offers two sample options: SwabFAST for anterior nares swabs and SalivaFAST for saliva. Sample-specific buffers and proteinase K replace conventional RNA extraction, which the authors identify as a laborious, costly, contamination-prone bottleneck. SwabFAST uses a TBE-based viral transport buffer that also transports swabs; SalivaFAST uses a TCEP-based preparation buffer to improve proteinase K activity.

The workflow uses standardized 2 mL barcoded cryovials, automated decappering, and electronic pipetting to support high-throughput processing. Viral transport buffer stability testing showed consistent detection across tested storage temperatures and durations. Analytically, extraction-free testing produced the same qualitative and similar quantitative results as extraction-based RT-qPCR for both specimen types. The limit of detection was 4 copies/µL, with 20/20 replicates positive for both swabs and saliva.

In comparisons of extraction-free testing with the CDC extraction-based protocol, swab testing had 100% positive and negative percent agreement, while saliva testing had 98.8% positive and 99.4% negative agreement. Compared with SalivaDirect, SwabFAST had 83.3% positive and 99.4% negative agreement in 179 paired clinical samples; SalivaFAST had 95% positive and 100% negative agreement in 40 saliva samples.

By December 23, 2021, COVIDFast had performed 409,883 tests, including 342,734 SwabFAST tests and 67,149 SalivaFAST tests. The overall positive rate was 8.10%, with rates of 7.71% for SwabFAST and 10.09% for SalivaFAST. The system produced results within 24 hours of sample receipt at volumes exceeding 5,000 tests per day and was described as reducing material, labor, and automation costs. The authors propose extending the extraction-free platform to other viruses and potentially bacteria and fungi.

U.S. home prices rose across all measured markets in February 2018. The Case-Shiller National Index gained 6.3% year over year, while the 10-City and 20-City Composites rose 6.5% and 6.8%. Seattle led annual gains at 12.7%, followed by Las Vegas at 11.6% and San Francisco at 10.1%. All 20 cities posted monthly increases; the National Index rose 0.4% unadjusted and 0.5% seasonally adjusted, while both composites rose 0.7% and 0.8%, respectively. National prices had increased for 70 consecutive months, averaging 6% annually. David Blitzer said employment gains supported rising prices and, with expected economic and employment growth, the streak was likely to continue. Seattle ranked highest in both employment and price growth; California home prices outpaced what employment trends would suggest, while Miami prices rose less despite better-than-average employment growth. The indices track typical single-family homes using matched arms-length sales pairs and are revised for the prior 24 months.

Coach Quenneville said his resilient team remains focused on improving after a difficult playoff stretch that included a seventh-game conference-final overtime loss and a tough series against Anaheim. He praised the consistent preparation, accountability and leadership of the veteran core, while crediting roster changes, deadline acquisitions and organizational depth. Hossa was highlighted as a consistent, two-way player who controls space, applies pressure and brings speed, while Kimmo provided reliability on defense. The team emphasizes the same preparation, taking each shift one at a time, avoiding complacency and putting the group first. Veteran players have risen in important games, and depth has been crucial when players missed games. The coach also identified puck movement, quickness and pace as areas the team must maintain against forechecking opponents.

Betteys’s wife sued Ætna Life Insurance Company under her husband’s accident policy for death benefits and weekly disability indemnity. After Dr. Betteys’s death, Ætna denied that his death resulted from an accident, recalled proof-of-death forms, and later rejected the delayed proof submitted. The court held the denial of liability excused compliance with the policy’s 60-day proof-of-death requirement, and letters from the insurer and its agents were admissible on the issue of waiver.

However, waiver of the proof requirement did not waive or estop enforcement of the separate contractual deadline for bringing suit. Ætna’s denial did not lull the plaintiff into delay; she waited until after the death-benefit action was barred and therefore could not recover the death benefit. The court reversed the judgment, directed a verdict for Ætna on that claim, and ordered a new trial concerning weekly disability indemnity.

Austria’s Financial Market Authority raised its forecast for Heta Asset Resolution’s wind-down proceeds to €8.6 billion, up €2.6 billion, citing stronger asset sales. An initial payment of about €4 billion to creditors is expected this summer.

A preliminary inquiry continued into the alleged robbery-related murders of Phyllis Caesar and Constance Fraser, found bound and gagged in their South Road, Georgetown home. Imran “Christopher” Khan, Steven Andrews and Phillip Suffrien are charged. Police witnesses testified, and the inquiry resumes Monday.

The passage specifies SD Memory Card tuning, initialization, data transfer, erase, security, function-switching, bus, and error-handling behavior.

CMD19 sends a fixed-length tuning block without requiring CMD16. It is mandatory for HOST-SDR-VD, optional for HOST-SDR-FD, and is legal only in Transfer State with 1.8 V signaling while the card is unlocked. A tuning sequence consists of consecutive CMD19 executions; the card must complete 40 executions within 150 ms, excluding host processing time.

During card identification, the host remains at fOD frequency, then may use fPP in Data Transfer Mode. CMD9 retrieves the CSD, optional CMD4 configures driver strength and may switch the clock to fPP, and CMD7 selects one card for Transfer State. Selecting another card or issuing CMD7 with RCA 0x0000 deselects the previous card. Data communication is point-to-point with the selected card. CMD12 can abort reads or writes, and writes must be stopped before deselection. During programming, parameter-set and read commands are rejected; other cards may be accessed through separate CMD and DAT lines. Resetting a card terminates pending programming and may destroy its data.

ACMD6 selects or deselects 4-bit bus operation, while the default is 1-bit; locked cards reject ACMD6. Blocks are normally limited to 512 bytes, with CRC protection. CMD17 reads one block and CMD18 reads consecutive blocks until CMD12. Misaligned partial-block accesses are detected and may produce ADDRESS_ERROR. Block writes use CRC-checked data, reject address, length, and write-protection errors, may buffer subsequent blocks, and expose busy status through DAT0 and CMD13. ACMD23 can pre-erase blocks, and ACMD22 reports the number of successfully written blocks.

Erase uses CMD32, CMD33, and CMD38 in sequence. Protected sectors remain intact, and DAT0 indicates an ongoing erase. DISCARD is optional for SDHC and SDXC cards, is unavailable through SPI, requires the DISCARD_SUPPORT status bit, and has a 250 ms busy timeout; discarded contents become “don’t care.” FULE logically erases the full user area, requires FULE_SUPPORT, and has a one-second timeout. Out-of-sequence or invalid commands reset the sequence and set error bits. Cards without DISCARD or FULE execute ERASE instead.

Write protection can be mechanical, internal, or password-based. Passwords are stored in nonvolatile PWD and PWD_LEN registers, with optional FEP and FEP_LEN registers for Card Ownership Protection (COP). CMD42 sets, clears, replaces, locks, or unlocks passwords and can force-erase card contents. FEP protects against force erase and password reset; COP Unlock is required after reset when FEP is set. Force erase removes user-area data and the password but not the secure area. Incorrect passwords and invalid command parameters set LOCK_UNLOCK_FAILED, and failed operations can leave the card locked.

CMD55 causes the next command to be interpreted as an application-specific command. A defined, legal ACMD returns APP_CMD set; an undefined but legal command is treated as a regular command and returns APP_CMD clear; an illegal command returns an illegal-command error. ACMD41 is an exception because its response does not carry APP_CMD status.

CMD6 switches or queries card functions, including bus access mode, command-system extension, driver strength, and power limit. Mode 0 reports supported functions, selected results, and maximum power consumption; Mode 1 changes functions. Function 0 is the default, and defaults return after CMD0 or a power cycle. CMD6 returns a fixed 512-bit status block, has a 100 ms timeout, and requires eight clocks before changed bus behavior is used. The default power limit is 0.72 W; removable cards are limited to 1.80 W, while UHS-I cards are limited to 1.44 W. Function status reports busy functions, which cannot be changed.

High-Speed mode uses a 50 MHz clock for 25 MB/s operation. It is optional, and only one card may be driven when cards could use different timing modes. CMD34–37, CMD50, and CMD57 are reserved for selectable command-system extensions.

CMD8 is issued while the card is in Idle State to verify the host’s supply voltage. The card returns R7 with the voltage range and check pattern if it accepts the voltage; otherwise it does not respond and remains idle.

SDSC cards use byte addresses and CMD16-defined block lengths. SDHC and SDXC cards use 32-bit block addresses, fixed 512-byte memory-access blocks, and do not permit partial or misaligned access. CMD42 remains governed by CMD16. SDHC and SDXC cards do not support write-protected groups.

The host may vary or stop the bus clock, subject to frequency limits, but must provide eight clocks after specified command, response, and data transactions. CRC7 protects commands and most responses, while CRC16 protects each transferred data block. A failed command CRC prevents execution and sets COM_CRC_ERROR; an illegal command also leaves card state unchanged and sets ILLEGAL_COMMAND.

Read commands must respond within 100 ms or the applicable earlier calculated timeout. Write operations must respond within 250 ms or the applicable earlier calculated timeout; high-capacity cards have a maximum busy duration of 250 ms for writes.

The paper proposes DNN-Transformer-AE, a hybrid deep-learning framework for corporate tax-risk supervision and risk-level assessment. It combines a DNN for static enterprise attributes, a Transformer with positional encoding and self-attention for financial and tax time series, and an autoencoder that flags anomalies through reconstruction errors. The resulting representations are fused to generate risk scores and classify enterprises as high, medium, or low risk.

Using real tax and financial records from approximately 12,000 enterprises across manufacturing, retail, and internet services, the model achieved 0.91 accuracy, 0.86 recall, and 0.88 F1 on the test set, outperforming logistic regression, random forest, XGBoost, and DNN-LSTM. Training and validation losses converged near 40 epochs at approximately 0.05.

The framework is intended to improve risk detection, supervision, resource allocation, and enterprise self-remediation. Limitations include the absence of macroeconomic and inter-firm data and potentially high computational complexity; future research could incorporate broader data and develop interpretable, lightweight models.

The study develops a quantum-geometric framework for the orbital degree of freedom in magnon–phonon-coupled systems. It identifies global lattice rotation and the self-rotation of Bloch wavepackets as distinct sources of orbital angular momentum (OAM), with the latter linked to the quasi–quantum geometric tensor. In a two-dimensional Néel-ordered honeycomb antiferromagnet, magnetoelastic coupling hybridizes magnons with out-of-plane phonons, breaks required symmetries, and enables transfer of intra- and inter-band OAM between them. Consequently, linearly polarized phonon modes acquire finite OAM and a magnetic moment.

The transferred moment and OAM generate electric polarization and a transverse voltage under temperature or strain gradients, with contributions from both spin Berry curvature and OAM. At low magnetic fields in MnPS₃, the OAM contribution dominates, producing microvolt-scale voltages and net polarization five to six orders of magnitude larger than in the DMI-only case. The response increases with temperature and coupling strength, persists at zero temperature, and vanishes without magnon–phonon interaction. The framework is presented as applicable generally to periodic fermionic and bosonic systems and as a foundation for phonon orbitronics.

The IMF advised Saudi Arabia to phase in fiscal reforms gradually, warning that rapid spending cuts and price increases could damage growth amid low oil revenues. The IMF projected a 2017 budget deficit of 9% of GDP. Saudi Arabia’s Vision 2030 aims to reduce oil dependence, restore budget balance by 2019, introduce a 5% VAT in 2018 and achieve a deficit-free budget by 2022, alongside tax, fee and energy-price increases.

Value area trading uses volume profiles to identify the price range containing 70% of trading volume during a given period. These areas can mark potential support, resistance, and buying or selling opportunities. The strategy is common in futures but can also apply to stocks, forex, and intraday through monthly timeframes, depending on the trader and market. Signals may involve breakouts above or below the value area, rejection or reversal patterns, and bullish or bearish divergence. Value areas can also help set stops and profit targets or confirm signals from other strategies. Traders should use position sizing, stop-loss orders, diversification, and discipline to manage risk. Limitations include false signals, changing value areas, and the need for additional factors. Backtesting requires clearly defined trading rules and settings.

The study computes finite-temperature equilibrium vacancy concentrations in a nine-component refractory multi-principal element alloy containing group 4, 5, and 6 elements on a body-centered-cubic structure. A DFT-parameterized embedded cluster expansion (eCE) model reproduces the formation energetics of the elements and vacancies with an overall test RMSE of 7.72 meV/site. Canonical Monte Carlo simulations, combined with free-energy integration and Widom particle exchange, provide chemical potentials for a canonical coarse-graining formalism that calculates equilibrium vacancy concentrations and local compositions around vacancies at dilute vacancy concentrations.

Calculations for four alloys show that group 4/5/6-only alloys have extremely low vacancy concentrations, whereas adding group 4 elements increases them by roughly 10–100 times. Vacancy concentrations show Arrhenius-like temperature dependence and strong sensitivity to short-range order and bonding energies. Zr and Hf preferentially occupy the first-neighbor shell around vacancies, while Mo is enriched in the second-neighbor shell. The coarse-graining predictions closely match semi-grand canonical Monte Carlo results for HfNbTaTiZr while requiring far fewer samples. Some calculated temperatures correspond to phase-separated mixtures and are identified as uncertain.

Binary-alloy calculations show that favorable element bonds lower vacancy concentrations, whereas unfavorable bonds raise them by making vacancy formation energetically preferable. Trends from dilute solute–vacancy binding persist in concentrated alloys. Increasing the group 4 fraction lowers vacancy formation free energy; roughly 50–60% group 4 content is calculated to produce vacancy concentrations of about \(10^{-4}\)–\(10^{-5}\) at 1500°C, although excessive group 4 content may degrade high-temperature properties, increase interstitial uptake, or promote martensitic transformations.

The study also finds that single special quasi-random structures can misrepresent vacancy formation free energies in non-ideal alloys, underestimating equilibrium vacancy concentrations by factors of about three and seven for Cr–Ti and HfNbTaTiZr, respectively. Differences in sampled short-range order and chemical potentials contribute to these discrepancies. The framework neglects vibrational free-energy contributions, divacancies, larger vacancy clusters, and non-dilute vacancy behavior.

Scientists are preparing for the first total solar eclipse visible in the U.S. in nearly a century, with the moon’s shadow crossing from Oregon to South Carolina. Researchers and citizen-scientists will study the sun’s corona, Earth’s weather, space weather, and the effects of darkness on animals and plants using telescopes, cameras, satellites, aircraft, high-altitude balloons, and volunteer observations. Federal agencies are spending about $7.7 million on projects, including the Citizen CATE initiative, iNaturalist observations, and the University of California, Berkeley’s Eclipse Megamovie 2017.

Eclipses remain uniquely valuable because the sun’s brightness prevents direct observation of its outer atmosphere, where temperatures exceed one million degrees. Scientists also note that eclipse observations helped discover helium in 1868 and provided the evidence used to confirm Einstein’s theory of relativity in 1919.

A news roundup led by the arrest of Iowa’s largest school district superintendent by Immigration and Customs Enforcement. Other headlines cover school integration, education policy, funding, college access, student and teacher achievements, COVID-19 learning impacts, and youth issues, along with brief coverage of politics, science, entertainment, sports, and community news.

A conveyance by extent is subject to the same construction rules as a conveyance by deed. An execution on a debtor’s land conveys all buildings standing on it, whether or not their foundations extend below the surface. In this trespass action involving a barn and blacksmith’s shop, the court held that the buildings passed with the land under the execution and the plaintiff’s subsequent deed. Parol evidence could not show that the buildings had been excluded or reserved, because the execution returns contained no such exception and could not be varied by oral testimony. The evidence offered by the defendants was properly rejected, and judgment was entered for the plaintiff on the verdict.

A long-term Danish study found that children born to mothers with rheumatoid arthritis had nearly triple the risk of the disease, 2.2 times the risk of thyroid disease and 1.6 times the risk of epilepsy compared with other children.

Microsoft Corporation’s Form 10-Q for the quarter ended March 31, 2020 presented unaudited GAAP financial statements. Third-quarter revenue was $35.021 billion, up from $30.571 billion a year earlier; operating income was $12.975 billion, net income was $10.752 billion, and diluted EPS was $1.40. For the first nine months, revenue was $104.982 billion, net income was $33.079 billion, and diluted EPS was $4.30, compared with $92.126 billion, $26.053 billion, and $3.36 in the prior-year periods.

Commercial cloud revenue for the quarter was $13.3 billion, up 39%. Office Commercial revenue rose 13%, Office 365 Commercial grew 25%, LinkedIn revenue rose 21%, Dynamics grew 17%, Dynamics 365 grew 47%, server products and cloud services grew 30%, Azure grew 59%, and Windows Commercial grew 17%. Third-quarter revenue was $11.743 billion for Productivity and Business Processes, $12.281 billion for Intelligent Cloud, and $10.997 billion for More Personal Computing.

At March 31, 2020, total assets were $285.449 billion, including $137.626 billion of cash, cash equivalents, and short-term investments; total liabilities were $170.948 billion, and stockholders’ equity was $114.501 billion. Nine-month operating cash flow was $42.002 billion, financing used $33.769 billion, and investing used $7.761 billion. The filing disclosed $17.177 billion of stock repurchases and $11.272 billion of dividends paid during the nine-month period.

Management reported that COVID-19 had a minimal net revenue impact in the third quarter. Cloud usage increased, while transactional licensing slowed, LinkedIn advertising declined, Windows OEM and Surface demand rose, gaming engagement increased, and search advertising weakened. The notes addressed investments, derivatives, debt, taxes, leases, unearned revenue, contingencies, and share repurchases. Deloitte reviewed the interim information and reported that no material modifications were necessary; the review did not constitute an audit opinion.

This continuation application incorporates by reference earlier disclosures concerning video coding using directional modes and non-separable transforms. It describes video encoding and decoding based on intra and inter prediction, motion compensation, transforms, quantization, entropy coding, and loop filtering, with applications including streaming, videoconferencing, television, and compressed-media storage.

The disclosure proposes reconstructing a coded block by deriving its intra prediction mode and applying an associated non-separable transform. For a directional mode, coding information specifies a nominal mode and an angular offset. The prediction angle is the nominal angle plus the offset, which may be calculated from a signaled offset integer and a step size. The nominal mode also identifies a transform-set mode, independently of the angular offset, to select a set containing one or more non-separable transforms. A signaled transform index identifies a particular transform within that set, and the block is reconstructed using the directional prediction and selected transform.

Non-directional modes include DC, PAETH, SMOOTH, SMOOTH_V, SMOOTH_H, recursive-filtering, and chroma-from-luma modes. Transform sets may also be associated with non-directional modes or nominal modes. The disclosed non-separable transform may be a secondary transform, including a low-frequency non-separable secondary transform or reduced secondary transform. Such transforms can be restricted to selected leading coefficients, excluded for PAETH or recursive-filtering modes, and omitted for transform-skip blocks or blocks with few nonzero coefficients.

The passage describes extending eight nominal angular modes into 56 finer directional modes using angular offsets, as well as smooth predictors based on neighboring samples, recursive-filtering predictors using seven-tap filters, chroma-from-luma prediction, and multi-line intra prediction. It also describes reduced non-separable secondary transforms that map fewer coefficients to reduce transform-matrix storage and computational complexity. Transform sets may contain multiple transform kernels, with their selection signaled by an index, context coding, and restrictions based on the last significant coefficient. The secondary transform may be separately signaled for luma and chroma, disabled for intra subpartition or matrix-based intra prediction, and limited to DCT2-based blocks up to 64×64.

Additional embodiments describe line graph transforms derived through eigen-decomposition of generalized graph Laplacian matrices. These transforms can include forms of discrete cosine and sine transforms and may serve as primary transforms for modeling row- and column-wise residual statistics. Encoder and decoder embodiments are presented as functional pipelines for prediction, residual transformation, quantization, entropy coding or parsing, reconstruction, reference-picture management, and in-loop filtering.

A University of Maryland study of 1,099 college students found that continued energy drink consumption between ages 21 and 24 was associated with increased later use of cocaine or prescription stimulants for nonmedical purposes. Occasional consumption also correlated with greater risk, while those who stopped consuming energy drinks were less likely to develop substance-abuse issues. Researchers said the reason for the association remains unknown and needs further investigation.

The study examines the characteristics, employment conditions, and career prospects of Hungarian higher-education lecturers using national and international statistics, comparative charts and tables, and documentary analysis of Hungarian legislation. It reviews post-1990 higher-education development, international enrollment and staffing comparisons, legal rules for academic appointments, academic career structures and earnings, and the supply of future faculty through doctoral enrollment.

Hungarian higher-education participation expanded rapidly after 1990, rising from 986.9 students per 100,000 inhabitants in 1990 to a peak of 3,952.2 in 2005–06, before declining to 2,825.4 in 2022–23. Institutional consolidation, demographic change, tuition policies, the Bologna reform, reduced public funding, and admission restrictions shaped enrollment. Post-2010 policies favored recruitment restriction and elitism, reduced opportunities for several demographic groups, and left the proportion of young graduates well below the EU’s 40% target. By 2020, nearly one-third of academic staff worked in non-state institutions, while staffing in foundation institutions represented 62% of the sector.

Lecturer numbers broadly followed enrollment until 2004 but diverged afterward. The student-teacher ratio increased from 5.9 in 1990 to 17.9 in 2006, then declined to 10.4 in 2022. Teaching loads tripled by 2006 and remained about twice their 1990 level in 2022. Lecturers were older than the developed-country average, although Hungary ranked in the middle internationally by age distribution. Women’s representation increased with enrollment, reaching 41.5% in 2020, but remained comparatively low.

Legislation from 1993 onward defined academic qualifications and positions, including professors, associate professors, assistant professors, and assistant lecturers. Later amendments imposed stricter qualification, research, international-recognition, and foreign-language publication requirements, expanded public competition, and limited the renewal of fixed-term appointments. The 2011 Act separated the professorial title from employment, strengthened institutional appointment criteria, and reduced university autonomy through centrally appointed chancellors and changes to accreditation and personnel procedures. It also established minimum teaching and research-time requirements. In 2020, 22 public universities were reorganized as public foundations with government-appointed governing boards; employees lost civil-service protections, although salaries increased and became linked to performance evaluation.

Although total academic employment largely stagnated after 2005, the number of university and college professors fell by two-thirds between 2005 and 2020, while other categories grew. Retirements, funding constraints, stricter requirements, and low pay contributed to the decline. Professor salary bases remained at 554,400 HUF per month from 2018 through 2023 despite inflation exceeding 30% between 2018 and 2022, while junior academic salaries were below comparable non-university labor-market earnings. Reorganized universities delivered raises of roughly 70–80%.

Academic earnings generally peak late in careers, while doctoral graduates working in teaching and research have comparatively low monthly and lifetime earnings. Their lifetime earnings fall below those of university graduates overall and only slightly exceed those of public-sector graduates; obtaining a doctorate appears financially advantageous mainly relative to employment in the public sector rather than business. The study concludes that lost doctoral-study earnings, modest starting salaries, hierarchical institutions, insecure employment, and limited opportunities may impede the recruitment and retention of academics.

Globally, doctoral enrollment rose from 2.9 million in 2015 to a projected 3.3 million in 2020. Hungary ranked 53rd by global share and 47th per 100,000 inhabitants in 2015, falling to 49th and 42nd respectively in 2020. Because doctoral-student numbers correlate strongly with international publications, the country’s weak position may threaten its future supply of higher-education teachers and researchers.

The 2018 Scottish Accountancy & Finance Awards recognize accountants’ contributions to private and public-sector organizations. Hosted by Sarah Heaney with entertainment by DNA, the event includes a champagne reception, three-course dinner, and awards ceremony. Categories include large and small accountancy firms, finance directors, emerging finance directors, young accountants, tax teams, and corporate finance teams. Tickets cost £132 plus VAT individually, £1,200 plus VAT for a table of 10, or £1,440 plus VAT for a table of 12.

The speaker reflects on Detroit as his first hockey team, calling it a great city that treated him well; the team reached the semi-finals in two consecutive years. He describes being traded to Washington as a shock, says the trade didn't work out, and credits summer changes and a strong crop of players for the team's success. He is excited to return, having enjoyed playing in Detroit with Steve and Kocur.

Azerbaijan sold six tonnes of organic honey last year at $8,000–$8,500 per tonne. Agriculture Minister Heydar Asadov said the country aims to expand exports as global demand is projected to rise sharply in 2020–2022. The ministry plans to seek greater state support for beekeeping.

The Texas Education Agency is investigating hundreds of teachers’ social media posts about Charlie Kirk’s killing after Education Commissioner Mike Morath called the remarks “reprehensible and inappropriate” and promised referrals that could lead to suspended teaching licenses. Gov. Greg Abbott supports the probe, arguing that celebrating Kirk’s assassination is unacceptable and that some posts called for violence.

Legal experts and public education advocates contend that the investigation is an attack on teachers’ First Amendment rights and part of a politically driven “witch hunt.” They say teachers do not surrender their free-speech rights when employed and that discipline for personal speech requires evidence of significant workplace disruption; widespread outrage alone may not suffice. State ethics rules and disciplinary procedures allow boards to suspend or fire educators and the agency to place warnings on teaching certificates or revoke licenses. The agency did not answer questions about how it would consider First Amendment protections.

Marc Ó Sé says an injury-free James O'Donoghue could be a 'huge' boost for Kerry this summer. The 2014 Footballer of the Year scored nine points on his return against Clare, and Ó Sé expects him to improve each game, giving Kerry a second scoring threat alongside Paul Geaney.

The article defines a bond as an issuer borrowing investors’ capital in exchange for scheduled interest payments and repayment of principal at maturity. It focuses on Treasury bonds, primarily through the TLT ETF, rather than over-the-counter corporate bonds. Bond prices generally move inversely to interest rates, creating interest-rate risk: an investment worth $1 million could fall to $800,000 when rates rose.

Bond trading strategies are systematic plans designed for objectives such as income, capital preservation, or appreciation. Examples include yield curve, duration, credit spread, tactical asset allocation, scalping, fundamental, seasonal, and price-action strategies. Strategies vary with market conditions, investment goals, time horizons, and risk tolerance. Common mistakes include insufficient market knowledge, excessive reliance on historical results, poor risk management, chasing yield without assessing credit and liquidity risks, inadequate diversification, inflexibility, and emotional bias. For beginners, dollar-cost averaging is suggested.

Day trading bonds involves buying and selling within the same day and requires understanding pricing, liquidity, and interest-rate factors. It can be automated using algorithms based on market, economic, rate, and issuer data, though human oversight remains important.

Several backtested TLT strategies showed strong historical performance, but their continuation is not guaranteed. Because SPY and TLT correlations were often near zero, bonds were presented as complementary to stocks. Combining the bond strategies with an S&P 500 strategy reportedly increased annual returns from 11.5% to 18.6% while reducing drawdowns, illustrating the value of diversification rather than searching for a single perfect strategy.

Enron was in advanced but delicate talks to sell its Portland General Electric unit to Northwest Natural for about $1.8 billion in cash and stock, with Northwest Natural expected to assume roughly $1 billion of debt and give Enron a minority stake. Financing and board approval remained uncertain, though an agreement could have been announced within days. Northwest Natural confirmed the discussions; Bloomberg described the total transaction value as $2.8 billion including assumed debt. The sale followed the collapse of Enron’s $3.1 billion agreement with Sierra Pacific Resources amid California’s power crisis.

Enron also planned to eliminate about 500 jobs, up to 10% of its European workforce, primarily through voluntary severance.

BG Group’s $388 million purchase of Enron’s 30% interest in India’s Panna-Mukti and Tapti offshore fields was threatened because ONGC and Reliance opposed BG obtaining operatorship; BG required full operatorship, with a decision expected by the end of October.

Tata Power was preparing a bid for Enron’s 65% stake in the stalled $2.9 billion Dabhol Power project, while Indian lenders formulated a revival package and sought concessions, discounted payments and tariff restructuring. BSES declined to bid, citing uneconomic project parameters. Dabhol remained shut after its sole customer stopped purchasing power and defaulted on payments.

Northwest Natural also raised its quarterly common dividend from 31 cents to 31.5 cents per share.

Microsoft announced that Chief Accounting Officer Frank H. Brod will retire effective July 31, 2020, and remain through September 30 to assist with the transition. Alice L. Jolla will succeed him. Her appointment includes a $1.5 million stock award vesting quarterly at 6.25% per quarter, contingent on continued employment.

Bitcoin fell as much as 16% to US$7,643 before recovering to US$8,715, down 21% for the week and over half from its December 18 record of US$19,511. Setbacks include regulatory threats, the US$500 million Coincheck heist, manipulation fears and Facebook's ad ban. Ripple, Ether and Litecoin fell at least 18%. Roubini called bitcoin the "mother of all bubbles," now bursting.

After ABC canceled the *Roseanne* reboot over Roseanne Barr’s racist tweet about Valerie Jarrett, President Trump criticized the network and Disney CEO Bob Iger for apologizing to Jarrett but not him. Iger said ABC had “zero tolerance” for racist, bigoted comments; Jarrett confirmed he called to apologize and announced the cancellation. Democratic lawmakers defended Jarrett and questioned Trump’s response. Jarrett said the country’s tone begins with its president but citizens must also push back.

Best Hope Services plans to launch Nigeria’s first online trade exhibition on May 1, enabling local inventors, scholars and entrepreneurs to showcase products worldwide without physical venues. The e-fair will feature expos, connections, trade and events across technology, automobiles, electronics and other sectors.

Microsoft is reportedly developing Polaris, a modular Windows 10 edition built on Windows Core OS for desktops, laptops and 2-in-1 devices. It would rely on Microsoft Store UWP apps and feature a new CShell interface, making the OS lighter, faster, more secure and potentially more battery-efficient. Legacy desktop applications would not work directly, and users reportedly could not upgrade to Windows 10 Pro, though remote virtualization might enable older programs. Polaris was expected in 2019.

U.S. and Chinese interests converge in preserving peace, expanding trade—about $3.5 billion annually—and addressing the Soviet military buildup; China’s modernization also depends substantially on Western and U.S. technology. Despite disagreements over Taiwan, Chinese leaders reportedly favor a strong U.S. role in defending regional peace.

A Reagan-Bush administration would pursue a global, strategic partnership with China, extend friendship broadly, and expand trade, scientific, and cultural ties. It would work with China, Japan, South Korea, and Taiwan to promote Western Pacific peace, stability, and economic growth while opposing aggression and hegemony. U.S. relations with Taiwan would follow the Taiwan Relations Act, which treats nonpeaceful attempts to determine Taiwan’s future as a grave threat, provides defensive weapons, mandates resistance to coercion, and establishes safeguards through the American Institute in Taiwan. The passage criticizes President Carter’s normalization concessions, argues that a Taiwan liaison office could have been retained, and notes congressional funding and oversight of Taiwan relations.

Researchers examined how polypropylene’s molecular regularity, or isotacticity, and thermal treatment affect its mechanical properties. Samples with isotacticity ranging from 25% to over 95% were formed into films by rapid quenching or slow cooling, then mechanically tested. Stress-strain results showed that material behavior depended on both isotacticity and cooling history, with elastic modulus closely related to crystallinity. Greater isotacticity favors ordered crystalline regions and stronger materials, while quenched and slowly cooled samples developed different crystallite structures. The findings demonstrate that controlling chain structure and preparation conditions enables polypropylene to be produced with predetermined properties, such as elasticity or hardness. The study was published in Polymer in 2017.

Up to 200 participants will be selected for two nine-day JACL Kakehashi trips to Japan, promoting Japan-U.S. relations through educational visits, cultural activities, and a homestay. Applicants must be 18–25, students or young professionals of Japanese American or Asian American heritage; Japanese nationals and passport holders cannot apply. JACL membership is not required.

Walmart’s reported bid for online clothing retailer Bonobos is part of its effort to expand in online fashion, attract younger millennial shoppers and regain share from Amazon. The deal would be Walmart’s fourth small online apparel acquisition since 2017, following ShoeBuy, Moosejaw and ModCloth, and reflects Marc Lore’s acquisition-led e-commerce strategy. Walmart has struggled online: online sales are about 3% of total sales, and the company has struggled to attract affluent young consumers and prominent brands. Analysts questioned whether acquisitions could materially help, while Amazon dominates U.S. online clothing and footwear. Walmart has spent $3.1 billion on e-commerce and digital projects over four fiscal years and paid $3.3 billion for Jet.com, where Lore came from.

Materials modeling for disordered systems requires atomistic structures that reproduce experimental structural statistics, yet standard Monte Carlo and molecular dynamics approaches do not guarantee experimental agreement. Reverse and hybrid reverse Monte Carlo can improve agreement with observables such as XRD, neutron diffraction, and pair distribution functions, but may produce unphysical artifacts, require material-specific constraints, and suffer from low computational efficiency. Earlier molecular-dynamics-based inverse methods had poor scaling, inaccurate gradients, and inadequate treatment of thermal effects.

The article develops molecular augmented dynamics (MAD), an O(N) modified molecular-dynamics method that jointly optimizes physical and experimental constraints. Its Hamiltonian combines kinetic energy, an interatomic potential that penalizes unphysical high-energy configurations, and an experimental potential measuring disagreement between predicted observables and experimental data. Analytical, linearly scaling forces are derived for XRD, neutron diffraction, pair distribution functions, and XPS predictions, including thermal broadening and smooth gradients. The XPS derivation indicates that any observable depending on local, position-differentiable descriptors can be treated this way. Simulation parameters and CPU/GPU scaling within TurboGAP are also presented.

Intel released 14nm Coffee Lake desktop chips and Z370 chipsets, with major vendors selling boards worldwide. Its roadmap includes additional Coffee Lake products, Gemini Lake, notebook and vPro models, 10nm Cannon Lake in mid-2018, and Ice Lake in 2019.

A roundup of making tips covers adding rare-earth magnets to alligator-clip tester wires, repurposing an old motor as a rotating display for filming, and adding a hobby knife to a compass for interchangeable pens or markers. It advises marking unreliable material edges with a squiggly line, converting a drill press into a drum sander, and using a $10 IKEA flexi-neck LED lamp for directed workbench lighting.

In 1976, Kent Howerton won the 500cc National Motocross opener at Moto-Masters, followed by Bob Hannah and Tony DiStefano. At the 1982 High Point National, Ricky Johnson won the 250 class, while Honda swept the 500 class. Yamaha budget cuts accompanied coach Gary Bailey’s departure and Mike Bell and Rick Johnson skipping the Trans-USA. Ross Pederson won the 1987 Montreal Supercross.

The “Drive & Kick” offense uses a three-player weave from a 3–2 spread. The handler drives for a layup, then passes outside and replaces the next player when denied. Baseline zone help enables kick-outs, while sagging help creates back-cut drop-pass opportunities.

The passage introduces NVIDIA’s A100 Tensor Core GPU, an eighth-generation data-center accelerator built on the Ampere-based GA100 and designed for AI, HPC, and data-analytics workloads. It uses third-generation Tensor Cores supporting FP16, BF16, TF32, FP64, INT8, INT4, and binary data, plus 2:4 fine-grained structured sparsity that can double Tensor Core throughput. Reported gains over V100 include up to 10× for TF32, 2.5× for FP16 mixed precision and FP64, and 20× for sparse INT8.

A100 includes 108 streaming multiprocessors, 40 GB of HBM2 memory with 1,555 GB/s bandwidth, and a 40 MB L2 cache with residency controls and data compression. Third-generation NVLink provides 600 GB/s total GPU-to-GPU bandwidth, while PCIe Gen 4 supports SR-IOV.

Multi-Instance GPU (MIG) can partition an A100 into as many as seven isolated GPU Instances, with further compute-instance subdivisions, predictable QoS, fault isolation, and support for simultaneous workloads. CUDA 11 adds hardware-aware task graphs, asynchronous global-to-shared-memory copies, asynchronous barriers, L2 persistence controls, and expanded Cooperative Groups functionality. Other hardware additions include NVJPG decoding, optical-flow acceleration, improved atomics, and five NVDEC units.

DGX A100 combines eight A100 GPUs with NVSwitch, delivering up to 5 PFLOPS in a 6U system and up to 56 isolated MIG accelerators. It also supports large-scale deployment through InfiniBand, Ethernet, NVIDIA GPU Cloud, Kubernetes, and NVIDIA DeepOps.

Santa Barbara’s Housing Authority received a Gold Nugget Award for Best Affordable Project for Bradley Studios, a 54-unit infill development serving vulnerable, low- and extremely low-income residents with special needs. Built in 2012, its interconnected buildings resemble small Craftsman homes and include community and recreation rooms and social-service offices. McGillivray Construction built the project, while Peikert Group Architects LLP designed it.

Spatial transcriptomics and immunohistochemistry of cutaneous leishmaniasis lesions from Sri Lanka, Brazil, and India identified myeloid-cell-rich niches expressing IDO1 and CD274 (PD-L1). These niches contained mature dendritic cells and CCL18+ macrophages and were consistently associated with nearby CD8+ memory T cells, regulatory T cells, and IL-32 expression. IL32, LYZ, GBP1, IFI30, and FTH1 formed a shared molecular signature associated with IDO1/CD274 expression across the three disease forms. The authors proposed that CCL18+ macrophages recruit IL-32-producing T cells, which induce immune-checkpoint expression, while IFNγ and TNF further activate these myeloid cells.

In Sri Lankan patients treated with sodium stibogluconate, high IL-32 levels and especially high numbers of IL-32+CD8+ T cells were associated with delayed cure; low numbers of IL-32+CD8+ cells predicted earlier healing. IL-32+ regulatory T-cell abundance showed only a nonsignificant trend toward slower healing. The study was limited by small biopsy cohorts, inability to analyze resolved lesions or isolate cells for functional testing, and reliance on unmatched single-cell reference data.

Acting CDC director Jim O’Neill called for manufacturers to replace the combined MMR vaccine with separate monovalent shots, echoing President Trump’s proposal. No evidence shows that splitting MMR improves safety or effectiveness, and monovalent vaccines are unavailable in the U.S.; developing them would likely require years of clinical trials, manufacturing changes, and FDA approval. A 2017 study found that 69% of children completed the recommended series with combination vaccines, compared with 50% using single-antigen vaccines. MMR is highly effective with minimal side effects, though the CDC cites roughly one additional febrile seizure per 3,000–4,000 vaccinations. Experts warn that officials’ rhetoric could reduce vaccination rates and increase preventable disease and deaths.

This datasheet section (TI SLASFJ6A, Rev. September 2025) details the components of the MSPM0C1105/6 microcontrollers. The devices are ultra-low-power 32-bit MCUs built on the Arm Cortex-M0+ core running up to 32 MHz, offering extended temperature range (-40°C to 125°C), 1.62 V–3.6 V supply, up to 64 KB flash and 8 KB SRAM, and a trimmed on-chip high-speed oscillator (-2.1% to +1.6%) that removes the need for an external crystal. Analog/digital peripherals include a 3-channel DMA, CRC-16 accelerator, 12-bit 1.6-Msps ADC, comparator with 8-bit reference DAC, temperature sensor, one 16-bit advanced timer with deadband, four 16-bit general-purpose timers, windowed watchdog, three UARTs, one SPI, and two I²C supporting LIN, IrDA, DALI, Manchester, smart card, SMBus and PMBus.

The CPU subsystem adds prefetch logic, an I-cache with two 64-bit lines, a 24-bit SysTick down counter, and an NVIC with four priority levels and tail-chaining. Five power modes are described (RUN, SLEEP, STOP, STANDBY, SHUTDOWN) with two power domains, PD1 and PD0; SHUTDOWN disables both domains and is exited only via NRST, SWD, or an IO logic-level match. Tables enumerate per-mode functionality (EN/DIS/OPT/NS/OFF), noting that SYSOSC/ULPCLK states persist on entry to STOP0 and that STANDBY1 clocks only TIMG14, TIMG8, IWDT and RTC.

The PMU provides a brown-out reset monitor with three thresholds, a core regulator, and parity-protected trim for POR. The clock module supplies LFOSC, trimmed SYSOSC, external LFXT/LFCKIN and HFXT/HFCKIN sources, and distributes MCLK, CPUCLK, ULPCLK, MFCLK, LFCLK, ADCCLK, CLK_OUT, HFCLK and HSCLK. DMA_B has two full-feature channels plus one basic channel, supports ADC/UART/SPI/timer triggers, byte/short-word/word transfers, up to 64k transfers, ping-pong early interrupts, cascading, stride and gather modes. An event manager moves events via static (IRQ), DMA trigger and generic routes (1:1 or 1:2 splitters).

Flash provides in-circuit program/erase with 1 KB sectors and up to 100,000 cycles on 32 sectors. SRAM is zero-wait-state, retained through STANDBY, lost in SHUTDOWN, and supports 1 KB write protection. GPIO supports up to 45 pins with set/clear/toggle, "Standard with Wake" and "FastWake"; IOMUX provides drive strength, pullup/down, and pin muxing via PINCM.

The ADC converts at up to 1.6 Msps (10.6-bit ENOB with external reference), includes internal temperature/supply/analog-chain channels, and offers a 1.4 V or 2.5 V internal VREF or external VREF+/− with a decoupling capacitor. The temperature sensor has a factory single-point calibration value in the factory constants region. The LFSS holds the RTC (with prescaler extension, timestamp capture, calendar/alarm/periodic interrupts, ±240 ppm calibration, clock output) and the asynchronous IWDT (25-bit counter, LFOSC-based, eight selectable periods). VREF offers a shared 1.4 V/2.5 V reference supporting ADC operation up to 515 ksps, plus external reference input. The comparator provides six TIMx blanking sources, wake from all low power modes, output tied to advanced timer fault handling, selectable inputs, and an 8-bit reference DAC. Security includes flexible firewalls and CRC-16 with custom polynomial; the CRC module supports CRC16-CCITT and bit reversal.

Peripherals include three UARTs (LIN mode, parity options, programmable baud, TX/RX FIFOs for DMA, loopback), I²C (7- and 10-bit addressing, multi-controller, up to 100 kbps/400 kbps/1 Mbps, SMBus 3.0, address-match wakeup, glitch filters), SPI (up to 16 Mbit/s via ULPCLK/2, controller or peripheral, 4–16-bit frames, TI/Motorola/National Microwire formats), the WWDT (eight periods, auto-stop in sleep, interval mode), and TIMx timers (TIMG with QEI and cross-trigger; TIMA with clock doubler, repeat counter, shadow/CC registers, asymmetric PWM with deadband and fault handling). A two-wire SWD port and DEBUGSS provide on-chip pull resistors, SWD disable for GPIO use, peripheral control during debug, a DSSM mailbox, and SWD lockout with password-authenticated debugging. A memory-mapped FACTORY region holds DEVICEID (0x41C4.0004) and USERID (0x41C4.0008) data plus trim information.

For layout, TI recommends 10 µF and 0.1 µF low-ESR decoupling on VDD/VSS placed close to the pins, a 47 kΩ pullup with 1000 pF pulldown on NRST, crystal bypass capacitors, and pullups on 5V-tolerant open-drain IOs used for I²C/UART. The document also lists TI development tools (LaunchPad, TI Resource Explorer, SysConfig, MSP Academy, GUI Composer, TI Arm-Clang), X versus MSP device prefixes, support resources, ESD cautions, the July-to-September 2025 revision history, and mechanical, packaging and orderable information.

The study examined the empathic profiles of 206 university teachers in three Education faculties at a Spanish university. Participants completed the Spanish adaptation of the Interpersonal Reactivity Index, measuring perspective taking, fantasy, empathic concern, and personal distress. Teachers reported high overall empathy, with above-midpoint scores in perspective taking, fantasy, and empathic concern and moderate personal distress. Female participants scored significantly higher than male participants on the total scale and every dimension. Empathy did not differ significantly by degree programme, campus, contractual status, or university teaching experience. However, teachers with prior non-university experience scored higher in perspective taking, fantasy, and empathic concern, while those with only university experience scored higher in personal distress. The findings indicate generally high empathy among education faculty, supporting the importance of developing educators’ socioemotional competencies and their role as empathetic models. Limited generalizability due to sample size and potential social desirability bias was noted.

The Department considered regional decentralization premature and potentially harmful, advising that discussion wait until the international organization was firmly established, though regional assembly committees might serve limited purposes. The February 21 Mexico City Conference was expected to address the Argentine problem, permit full discussion of the Dumbarton Oaks proposals, and secure support for U.S. plans without making inconsistent commitments. Similar discussions with Latin American ambassadors sought their views and backing.

Dumbarton Oaks proposed an International Court of Justice as the Organization’s principal judicial organ, with a statute annexed to the Charter, all members automatically parties, and nonmembers able to join under General Assembly conditions following Security Council recommendation. Its statute would either revise or replace the Permanent Court of International Justice’s statute. No agreement was reached on a preliminary meeting of jurists, its timing, composition, or terms, although the U.S. delegation circulated a tentative revised draft. The recommended procedure was to convene about fifteen technically qualified jurists when United Nations Conference invitations were issued, charged with preparing the statute and alternative procedures for putting it into effect.

UNC Chapel Hill placed Associate Professor Dwayne Dixon on leave while investigating his alleged advocacy of politically motivated violence, warning that disciplinary action could include dismissal. The inquiry followed attention to a Georgetown University flyer promoting the John Brown Gun Club, which Turning Point USA spokesperson Andrew Kolvet connected to Dixon through an old, removed post about Redneck Revolt. Dixon previously led the now-inactive Silver Valley chapter of Redneck Revolt, supported gun rights and described himself as an anarchist, but said he left the chapter in 2018. A petition for his reinstatement exceeded 900 signatures, while UNC’s AAUP chapter condemned his removal and argued that right-wing activists baselessly linked him to flyers posted by another group on another campus.

Three Illinois men were shot at point-blank range during Larry’s Fun Fest at Great Lakes Dragaway near Union Grove, Wisconsin, on Aug. 13, 2017. The victims, identified as gang members, were David L. Watson, 30; Khalid R. Howard, 30; and Derek K. Edwards, 26. Howard and Edwards died at the scene, while Watson died en route to a hospital. Sheriff David Beth said authorities suspected the killings were gang-related, but the motive and reason for choosing the venue were unknown. The shooter remained at large; he was described as a thin, athletic Black man aged 20–30, and the pistol was not recovered. The event drew 15,000 people and had no spectator weapon screening. Deputies preserved evidence overnight while authorities investigated, though family members were reportedly uncooperative.

Stan Bowman and Joel Quenneville attribute the Blackhawks’ success to team continuity, strong coaching and scouting, and player development rather than any one individual. They praise Corey Crawford’s consistent goaltending, the maturity of the core, the growth of younger players, and contributions from internally developed players such as Bickell, Andrew Shaw, Brandon Saad and Nick Leddy.

Quenneville says the team plans to play to its strengths against a strong, unpredictable opponent, while acknowledging how narrow the margin between winning and losing can be. Crawford is described as large, quick, patient and relentless. Bowman expresses pride in Bickell’s development and his important role in the team’s success. Quenneville also reflects on his early career with the Windsor Spitfires and praises the franchise and Claude’s career.

The Bearish Engulfing candlestick is a technical-analysis tool that signals strong bearish sentiment and a potential reversal from an uptrend to a downtrend, though it does not guarantee a reversal. It typically appears after an uptrend and consists of a bullish candle followed by a larger bearish candle whose body completely engulfs the first candle’s body, opening above its high and closing below its low. Traders may use it to close long positions, enter short positions, adjust stops, or identify potential entry and exit points.

Validity can be strengthened by confirming the pattern with other technical indicators, changes in momentum or price action, and trend context. Suggested risk controls include stop-loss orders, position sizing, risk/reward ratios, diversification, hedging, and a defined risk-management plan. Major risks include false signals, changing market conditions, volatility, and leveraged losses. A stop-loss for a short trade is placed above the high of the first candle, with a profit target potentially set at support below the current price.

The passage reports a 55–65% success or win rate in the stock market, subject to market, volatility, and strategy conditions, and recommends backtesting. In one cited S&P 500 backtest, adding a five-day RSI filter above 60 reduced trades from 258 to 58 while raising average gain per trade from 0.73% to 0.88%. The passage also reports 311 S&P 500 occurrences since 1993, ranking it third in frequency among 75 tested candlestick patterns. Related bearish reversal patterns include dark cloud cover, evening star, and bearish harami, all of which indicate weaker bearish formations than Bearish Engulfing.

The 50 EMA strategy is a popular trend-following approach that uses the 50-day exponential moving average to identify medium-term trends and generate buy and sell signals. Price above a rising 50 EMA indicates an uptrend and can prompt a long position; price below a falling EMA indicates a downtrend and can prompt a short position. Opposite crossovers signal exits. Traders often confirm signals with RSI, MACD, or other indicators and commonly test the strategy on four-hour or daily charts.

The passage recommends backtesting across timeframes and assets, maintaining a favorable risk-reward ratio, diversifying, and considering stop-loss and take-profit orders, although it notes that stop-losses rarely improved its tested strategies. A basic moving-average crossover performed poorly across several asset classes. On the S&P 500, it returned 6.8% versus 7.3% for buy-and-hold, with a 32% rather than 56% maximum drawdown. Using the 50 EMA as a filter with a second indicator produced stronger stock results: QQQ returned 11.5% annually with a 22% drawdown, while SPY returned 8.9% with a 16% drawdown. Overall, the strategy is simple and best used with confirmation tools and thorough testing.

The AMD Secure RNG Library provides an easy-to-use API for accessing random values generated by AMD hardware through the x86 RDRAND and RDSEED instructions. RDRAND returns 16-, 32-, or 64-bit random values, while RDSEED returns conditioned values of those sizes. The library supports single values, arrays, and streams of random bytes, abstracts low-level instruction handling, detects hardware failures, and allows configurable retries. Applications should use the CPUID-based `is_RDRAND_supported` and `is_RDSEED_supported` functions to verify hardware support before generating random values. Because each instruction performs a relatively slow memory-mapped I/O operation, latency-sensitive applications may seed a software PRNG with hardware-generated randomness. The library benefits applications requiring secure random values, including cryptographic key generation, communications, authentication, simulations, and gaming.

The First Circuit granted the Education Department’s request to stay an injunction, allowing it to fire half of the 550 employees in the Office for Civil Rights. The ruling followed a July Supreme Court decision in New York v. McMahon permitting similar reductions. A Massachusetts district court had blocked OCR layoffs, finding the staff reduction imperiled the office’s civil-rights mandate, but the appeals court found the cases sufficiently similar at the preliminary stage.

Following Charlie Kirk’s murder, the Trump administration intensified its targeting of nonprofits, with President Trump designating “antifa” a terrorist organization and promising to investigate those funding it. This study evaluated the effect of enforcing Kenya’s 2014 national referral guidelines on orthopaedic and trauma facility referrals to Kenyatta National Hospital (KNH), a tier-six national teaching and referral hospital. A retrospective pre-post study compared five months before and five months after enforcement on 1 July 2021, using 468 patient records from KNH’s emergency department, orthopaedic outpatient clinic and corporate outpatient care. Enforcement required sequential referrals, KNH referral-office concurrence and written referral letters.

Most referrals came from Nairobi and neighboring counties and from government facilities. Referral numbers increased after enforcement, but the overall increase and differences between government and private facilities were not statistically significant. Referral patterns differed significantly by tier: direct referrals from tiers II and III decreased, while referrals from tiers IV, V and VI increased. Forty-three facilities stopped referring directly to KNH; 67.4% were private facilities and 81.4% were in tiers II–IV. Associated factors included human-resource capacity, infrastructure, availability of equipment and implants, finances, and patient preference. Staffing and resource constraints were prominent in both government and private facilities, while patient preference was more strongly associated with private-facility referrals.

The findings indicate that enforcement reduced direct referrals from lower-tier facilities and increased referrals from higher tiers, although the retrospective design and effects of COVID-19 limited causal conclusions. Recommendations included sensitizing facilities to the guidelines, strengthening staffing and infrastructure, developing and training staff on standard referral procedures, ensuring adherence, and clarifying that KNH should manage complex referrals rather than be the first point of contact for orthopaedic care.

The 1-2-2 zone is presented as a strong defense against outside shooting and fast breaks and as a late-game option for protecting a lead. The point defends out front and the high post, wings work opposite and handle weak-side rebounding, and baseline defenders move in unison. Defenders shift with every pass and collapse when the ball enters the middle. Corner options include pass denial, dropping to help against a dominant post, or trapping the ball handler. The zone can also switch to a 2-1-2 on the first pass, placing an athletic defender in the middle while maintaining weak-side rebounding, and can extend easily into half- or full-court presses.

Research suggests that the probiotic Lactobacillus rhamnosus GG (LGG) may protect the liver from oxidative damage. Emory University researchers fed mice an LGG-rich or normal diet before giving them high doses of acetaminophen. Mice receiving LGG showed improved liver antioxidant responses and protection from oxidative injury. The protein Nrf2, which regulates genes involved in combating free radicals, played a pivotal role. Because the study used mice, further research is needed to determine whether the findings apply to humans. Probiotics are not a substitute for medicine, and consulting a doctor before adding supplements is advised.
