At the first triple-header T20 Cayley Cup Finals Day at North Marine Road, Ganton won Division Two by nine wickets (103-1 to 97-8), with Ian Cousins unbeaten on 40. Mulgrave won Division One by 28 runs, scoring 165-5 against Sherburn’s 137 all out; Chris Knight made 43 and Alfie Jacobs 36, while Dan Simpson led Sherburn with 50. Ebberston won the Premier Division by six wickets, reaching 89-4 against Filey’s 86 all out. The ground, umpires and scorers were thanked.

After a first panic attack at 19, the writer was diagnosed with panic disorder and has treated it with therapy and medication, though occasional attacks continue. Experts distinguish panic attacks from “anxiety attacks,” describing the former as intense bursts of fear that typically last under 30 minutes and may lack an obvious trigger when associated with panic disorder. Recognizing symptoms—including palpitations, sweating, shaking, breathlessness, choking sensations, chest discomfort, nausea, dizziness, tingling, detachment, and fear of losing control or dying—is recommended, along with a physical exam to rule out other problems. Coping strategies include keeping reassuring facts and positive mantras on a phone or index card, visualizing panic as waves that rise and recede, distracting oneself with games, word puzzles, relaxing music, or guided relaxation, and practicing slow, deep full-body breathing daily. Deep breathing during an attack may slow heart rate and calm the body. Professional guidance is emphasized.

The study used the 2019 National Survey of Early Care and Education to examine how families searched for child care and early education for children under age 6. The analytic sample included 1,190 households that searched within the previous 24 months and considered more than one provider. Latent class analysis identified five search types based on the first two information sources families reported: CCR&R/local organizations or friends and family; internet search or social media; known providers or friends and family; social media or friends and family; and friends and family or internet search. Friends and family was the most common source, followed by internet searches. Half of families reported one source and half reported two.

Regression analyses found that search types varied by whether families sought information about types of care, whether the child had a condition affecting how care is provided, and geographic region. Families using CCR&R/local organizations or friends and family and those using known providers or friends and family were more likely to search for children with conditions affecting care. Search types also differed between the Northeast and West. No significant relationships were found for the other information sought or most family and child characteristics.

The findings are limited by the reliance on only the first two sources reported, the exploratory and correlational design, and the selected sample’s higher incomes, greater likelihood of having two working parents, and greater likelihood of speaking only English.

The NVIDIA A100 Tensor Core GPU uses the Ampere architecture for AI and HPC workloads. It has 108 streaming multiprocessors versus V100’s 80, third-generation Tensor Cores, and up to 16 times the peak mixed-precision performance of standard FP32 FMA operations. Its Tensor Cores share data across all 32 threads in a warp rather than eight, issue eight times fewer matrix-multiplication instructions, and perform 2.9 times fewer register-file accesses than V100.

A100 includes 40 GB of HBM2 memory across five active stacks, delivering 1,555 GB/s bandwidth. SECDED ECC protects HBM2, L2 cache, L1 caches, and register files. Its 40 MB L2 cache is 6.7 times larger than V100’s, with two partitions, 40 slices, and 2.3 times the L2 read bandwidth. Compute Data Compression can improve DRAM bandwidth and L2 read bandwidth by up to fourfold and L2 capacity by twofold. L2 residency controls let applications reserve cache space for frequently reused data.

Efficient data delivery is supported by an asynchronous global-to-shared-memory copy instruction that bypasses L1 and the register file. A100 also introduces asynchronous barriers and increases maximum shared-memory allocation per SM from 96 KB to 164 KB.

MIG can divide an A100 into as many as seven isolated GPU Instances with dedicated compute, cache, and memory resources. These instances provide predictable performance, quality of service, fault isolation, and error containment. GPU Instances can contain multiple Compute Instances, which support simultaneous contexts and Volta-style MPS. MIG configurations also permit vGPU migration between instances and GPUs, helping reduce fragmentation and conserve resources.

Third-generation NVLink provides twelve links and 600 GB/s total bandwidth, compared with six links and 300 GB/s on V100. A100 also supports PCIe Gen 4 at 31.5 GB/s per direction for x16 connections and SR-IOV GPU sharing. Enhanced error attribution, isolation, containment, remote fault reporting, and link recovery improve resilience in multi-GPU and multi-tenant environments.

Additional hardware includes a five-core NVJPEG decoder, an optical-flow accelerator supporting optical flow and stereo disparity, improved FP16 and FP32 atomic throughput, and five NVDEC units for H.264, HEVC, and VP9 decoding. A100 has no display connectors, ray-tracing RT Cores, or NVENC encoder.

CUDA 11 adds support for Tensor Cores, sparsity, CUDA Graphs, MIG, and L2 residency controls. Task graphs reduce launch overhead and optimize complex dependencies. CUDA also exposes asynchronous copying, asynchronous per-thread barriers, persistent L2 allocation in 2.5 MB increments, and hardware-accelerated reductions. L2 set-aside is unavailable in MIG mode.

DGX A100 combines eight A100 GPUs with six NVSwitches, providing 4.8 TB/s total bidirectional bandwidth and up to 5 PFLOPS in a 6U system. MIG can create up to 56 isolated accelerators per system. Its software stack includes CUDA 11, the NVIDIA Container Toolkit, GPU-accelerated containers, and the NGC Private Registry for optimized AI/HPC software, models, and deployment assets.

The appendix describes neural-network pruning and two sparsity approaches: fine-grained sparsity, which removes individual weights, and coarse-grained sparsity, which removes larger network sections. A100 supports fine-grained structured 2:4 sparsity, which balances workloads while retaining nearly all evaluated model accuracy and can improve compute and memory efficiency.

The lecture demonstrates common web-security vulnerabilities using simplified Python CGI servers. A Shellshock example shows how CGI servers may convert attacker-controlled HTTP headers into Bash environment variables, allowing malformed shell syntax to execute commands. A cross-site scripting example embeds attacker-supplied content directly into HTML; a straightforward script was blocked by browser filtering, while malformed image syntax bypassed the filter, demonstrating inconsistencies among HTML, CSS, and JavaScript parsers.

Browser XSS filters use heuristics and are not complete, particularly for persistent XSS stored in comments or profiles. Other defenses include HTTP-only cookies, which restrict client-side cookie access but do not prevent CSRF; hosting untrusted content on a separate domain; server-side sanitization and encoding, as performed by Django templates; constrained markup languages such as Markdown; Content Security Policy (CSP), which restricts content sources and can block inline script and dynamic code mechanisms; and `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`, which prevents MIME-type sniffing.

The lecture also covers SQL injection and path traversal. Untrusted values concatenated into SQL queries can introduce additional commands, while simple quoting defenses can be bypassed. Secure applications should rigorously encode data, use parameterized or framework-provided database interfaces, and validate or escape user-supplied path components. Raw SQL queries remain a risk because developers sometimes bypass frameworks for performance.

For session management, cookies commonly contain session identifiers that are valuable to steal. Risks increase when trusted and untrusted parties share domains or subdomains because cookie access can cross those boundaries. Stateless authentication can replace persistent cookies by signing each request with a shared secret key using a message authentication code; the server verifies the signature and can reject revoked keys or expired requests. Replay remains possible within an expiration window. DOM storage and client-side certificates are alternatives, but require custom authentication logic or introduce key-management, revocation, installation, and usability difficulties.

Protocol-parsing inconsistencies can also create vulnerabilities when components disagree about a URL’s origin. The GIFAR attack combines an image with an embedded JAR file: it passes image validation, then executes as a Java applet in the target origin when combined with XSS. Proper resource-length validation can prevent such embedding.

Finally, the lecture describes covert-channel attacks that infer browsing history through observable timing. Attackers can test link colors, cached-resource response times, DNS resolution times, and iframe-rendering behavior. Browsers can block JavaScript access to visited-link colors, but timing attacks may still reveal whether candidate sites were accessed, including through geographic map tiles.

Eagles receiver A.J. Brown expressed frustration over his low target volume and production, saying he wants the ball when the offense struggles and the game is on the line. Despite one six-catch, 109-yard touchdown performance, he and DeVonta Smith have posted disappointing statistics. Philadelphia is 4-0, but coordinator Kevin Patullo must involve both receivers as the team seeks to repeat as Super Bowl champions.

A Royal Holloway University of London study found that bumblebee queens exposed to thiamethoxam, a neonicotinoid pesticide, were 26% less likely to lay eggs than unexposed queens. Researchers said reduced reproduction could drive wild bumblebee populations toward decline, but field effects remain uncertain and other pressures, including limited forage and parasites, may also matter. The findings may strengthen calls for further restrictions amid EU debate over a temporary moratorium on neonicotinoids.

Swarthmore students stress about grades, internships, and presenting themselves as capable, but they should remember that mistakes are acceptable in college and can often be laughed at. Although campus expectations are high, errors are not life-changing and can teach more than successes. Students should give themselves and others a break, forgive mistakes, assume good intent, and seek clarification before reacting to offensive-sounding remarks. While laughter cannot solve everything, it can help people cope with discomfort and feel better.

The lecture reviews Problem Set 8: Exercise 8.2 is considered inadequately supported by prior background, Exercise 8.3 uses BCJR decoding and is deferred because the algorithm was not covered, and \(\sigma^2=1\) is suggested for the noise variance. Only Exercise 8.1 is assigned for Wednesday.

Chapter 11 concludes with Hadamard-transform graphical realizations of Reed–Muller codes. The binary Hadamard matrix \(U_m\) is constructed from tensor powers of a \(2\times2\) matrix, is self-inverse, and provides generators for Reed–Muller codes; row weights correspond to the Hamming weights of binary indices. Fixing selected coefficients to zero yields codes such as the \((8,4,4)\) and \((8,7,2)\) Reed–Muller codes. Recursive controlled-NOT-like gate networks implement the transform in a butterfly structure similar to fast Fourier transform networks. The resulting \((8,4,4)\) realization can be reduced to 12 simple constraints with binary variables. This realization contains cycles and is relatively simple, but cyclic graphs sacrifice exact decoding performance. Agglomerating cycles produces a more complicated, cycle-free two-section trellis realization with higher branch complexity. In general, agglomerated Hadamard-transform realizations provide four-section, cycle-free Reed–Muller representations whose state dimensions meet the cut-set bound and attain minimal trellis complexity.

The lecture also distinguishes factor graphs, Markov graphs, and directed Bayesian networks. Chapter 12 then introduces a posteriori probability (APP) decoding and the sum-product algorithm. On cycle-free graphs, APP decoding is exact and terminates in time proportional to the graph’s diameter; on a trellis it corresponds to the BCJR algorithm, which computes posterior probabilities but is more complex than Viterbi decoding. On graphs with cycles, sum-product decoding becomes iterative and approximate, with performance degraded by short cycles; large-girth graphs are therefore preferred. APP decoding computes posterior probabilities for every external and internal variable. For a memoryless channel, Bayes’ rule expresses these probabilities as sums of products, divided into intrinsic and extrinsic information. The lecture introduces the sum-product algorithm’s past–future decomposition, based on the cut-set property of cycle-free graphs and the Cartesian-product factorization of compatible code portions. The update rule and schedule remain to be completed in the next lecture.

A Spring Valley woman is San Diego County’s first confirmed West Nile virus case this year. In 2016, the county reported 22 cases and two deaths. Symptoms can appear 2–14 days after an infected mosquito bite and include headache, fever, nausea, rash, fatigue and swollen glands; many infected people have no symptoms, but rare cases can be severe or fatal. California has recorded 231 illnesses and 12 deaths this year, while San Diego County has reported 32 infected dead birds, eight positive mosquito batches and one infected horse. Residents are urged to use insect repellent, wear long sleeves outdoors, eliminate standing water and report mosquito activity, dead birds or breeding sources to Vector Control.

Asian equities turned cautious after the Federal Reserve raised interest rates by 25 basis points for the second time this year, as expected, and detailed plans to shrink its balance sheet. The Nikkei fell 0.6%, Kospi 0.75%, ASX 200 1.13%, and Hang Seng 0.91%, while Shanghai and Shenzhen edged up. Markets viewed the hike as dovish and doubted the Fed’s forecast of three increases this year; former Fed Governor Robert Heller expected one more. Oil reached a seven-month low on rising U.S. gasoline inventories. Australian jobs data beat forecasts, lifting the currency, while New Zealand GDP missed expectations and the kiwi weakened. Toshiba shares fell amid a dispute with Western Digital and concerns it would miss its financial filing deadline. The dollar index remained below 97, while the Dow closed up 0.22%.

This retrospective multicentric study used T1-weighted MRI from 4,392 patients with multiple sclerosis or clinically isolated syndrome at 15 European centres to model healthy brain ageing, disease duration, and multiple-sclerosis-specific ageing. A longitudinal early-disease cohort included 252 patients and 749 sessions.

Using DeepBrainNet, multiple-sclerosis brains appeared 7.81 ± 9.35 years older than predicted. A 3D DenseNet264 disease-duration model achieved a test-set mean absolute error of 5.63 years and R² of 0.34, explaining more variance than total lesion or thalamic volume. The multiple-sclerosis-age model was more accurate, with mean absolute error of 3.78 years and R² of 0.80. Disease-duration gap was nearly uncorrelated with conventional brain-age gap, whereas multiple-sclerosis-age gap remained moderately correlated with it. All measures reflected distributed brain-volume changes, and disease-duration predictions were sensitive to lesion filling.

Brain-age gap, disease-duration gap, and multiple-sclerosis-age gap were each associated with EDSS disability. Disease-duration gap significantly improved explanation of EDSS beyond brain-age gap cross-sectionally and longitudinally; multiple-sclerosis-age gap did not. Annual EDSS worsening correlated with increases in brain-age gap and disease-duration gap.

The authors concluded that brain-predicted disease-duration gap is a clinically meaningful marker of multiple-sclerosis-specific brain damage that complements healthy brain-age models. Limitations included noisy retrospective disease-onset estimates, possible treatment confounding, disease-duration-dependent bias, and the need for further validation in longer and more diverse cohorts.

The paper applies non-Markovian Situation Calculus to a taxonomy of obligations. It reviews Reiter’s successor-state solution to the frame problem, Gabaldon’s extension allowing action preconditions and effects to depend on past situations, and prior work on knowledge-producing actions. It motivates the approach through smart contracts, whose obligations require explicit formal representation.

The sequential and temporal Situation Calculus is presented as a many-sorted second-order logic covering actions, situations, time, and other objects. Actions generate situations through `do(a,s)`, while predicate and functional fluents represent changing properties. Basic action theories include action precondition axioms, successor-state axioms, unique-name axioms, initial-state axioms, and foundational axioms governing situations and reachability.

Non-Markovian theories allow preconditions and effects to reference bounded past situations. The paper summarizes the bounded-formula definitions and notes that regression can compile certain non-Markovian sentences into equivalent sentences involving only the initial situation, although reasoning is outside its scope.

A running door-opening example specifies actions for unlocking, locking, moving, pressing a button, and notifying a manager, together with fluents describing the door’s state, the agent’s location, and notification status. It provides explicit precondition and successor-state axioms for these elements.

Finally, the paper summarizes a deontic embedding of obligations into Situation Calculus. A fluent `O(s′,s)` represents deontic accessibility between situations, and `Oblg(ϕ,s)` expresses that ϕ must hold in every situation accessible from s. This approach combines deontic modalities with time, permits actions that create obligations, and extends Reiter’s frame-problem solution to obligation-changing actions.

After Richard III’s remains were confirmed beneath a Leicester car park, the discovery affected several people connected to the story. Dominic Smee, who had scoliosis resembling the king’s curved spine, researched Richard’s fighting techniques and underwent 32 hours of foot combat training and 40 hours of riding training. He portrayed Richard’s final moments in the documentary *Richard III: The New Evidence* without a stunt double and later became more confident about his condition, giving lectures about his experiences.

Michael Ibsen, a cabinet-maker and descendant of Richard’s sister Anne, supplied a DNA sample that helped confirm the remains beyond reasonable doubt. He was asked to make Richard’s coffin and experienced public attention and autograph requests after the reburial.

Mike Mistry, the car park attendant for more than 15 years, witnessed the excavation and unknowingly contributed to its mythology by painting the “R” marking the space above Richard’s grave. The car park became a major tourist attraction, but Mistry was made redundant in 2016.

Musician Ian Churchward turned the discovery into an inspiration for his folk-rock band, The Legendary Ten Seconds. The discovery prompted his first Ricardian song, “The House of York,” and led to five Richard III albums, a sixth in progress, festival performances, and a concept album, *Tant Le Desiree*.

- Duty-cycle programming uses the DCL pin. TPS7H5001-SP, TPS7H5002-SP, and TPS7H5003-SP can select a 100% limit by connecting DCL to VLDO or a 75% limit by leaving DCL floating. A 50% limit uses DCL tied to AVSS and is supported by the TPS7H5001-SP and TPS7H5004-SP; OUTB/SRB are active in this configuration. TPS7H5004-SP supports only the 50% limit. In external synchronization, a 50%-duty-cycle system clock provides the most precise limiting.

- CS_ILIM senses transformer primary current for peak-current-mode PWM and overcurrent protection. OUTA/OUTB turn on with the internal clock and turn off when the sensed peak reaches a COMP/2 reference with a 150-mV offset. A sense resistor connected to AVSS is required, and the nominal current-sense threshold is 1.05 V. Its value depends on converter topology, transformer turns ratios, and the intended overcurrent level, with margin required between normal peak current and the trip point.

- Overcurrent triggers cycle-by-cycle limiting while CHICC is charged by an 80-µA pulsed current until reaching 0.6 V. Switching then stops, the soft-start pin is discharged, and the hiccup restart sequence begins. Restart occurs after the HICC voltage falls from 1 V to 0.3 V. CHICC controls both the cycle-by-cycle limiting delay and the non-switching restart interval; 3.3 nF is the minimum recommended value.

- The FAULT pin supports external overcurrent, overvoltage, or other protection logic. A qualifying voltage above the typical 0.6-V rising threshold causes shutdown and soft-start discharge. When FAULT falls below the typical 0.5-V falling threshold, the controller waits approximately 15 switching cycles plus an internal delay before restarting soft start. A renewed threshold violation restarts the delay.

- Slope compensation mitigates subharmonic oscillation above 50% duty cycle. The minimum compensation is 0.5 times the inductor’s falling-current slope, while the recommended value is one times that slope; a resistor from RSC to AVSS sets the level. Type 2A or Type 2B frequency compensation is supported. Type 2A adds CHF for high-frequency attenuation. Compensation selection begins with the desired crossover frequency, followed by calculation of RCOMP, CCOMP, optional ESR-zero compensation, and power-stage transconductance. Thermal shutdown stops switching above a typical junction temperature of 175°C and permits reinitialization below 160°C.

- The controllers use fixed-frequency, peak-current-mode control. Their internal oscillator starts the primary output, and switching stops when the external power-switch current reaches the stepped-down COMP reference. The TPS7H500x-SP family is intended for radiation-hardness-assured space-grade DC-DC converters, supports switching frequencies up to 2 MHz, requires external gate drivers, and can be used with buck, flyback, forward, active-clamp forward, push-pull, and full-bridge topologies.

- A 500-kHz synchronous push-pull design using GaN devices and the TPS7H5001-SP uses a 205-kΩ RT resistor, 10-kΩ/1.4-kΩ VSENSE divider for 5 V output, approximately 25-ns dead time with 20.5-kΩ PS and SP resistors, and a 49.9-kΩ leading-edge blank-time resistor. A 33-nF soft-start capacitor provides about 7.5 ms. DCL is tied to AVSS for a 50% controller limit while the design targets approximately 35% duty cycle. The transformer uses a 2.5 turns ratio and 40 µH primary inductance. Primary GaN FETs are rated at 170 V, while 80-V synchronous rectifiers are used with optional parallel Schottky diodes.

- The example selects a 0.47-µH output inductor with a target 40% ripple current. At least 1.3 mF of output capacitance is required for ripple and transient response, while 2.3 mF is used for additional single-event-transient mitigation. Cycle-by-cycle limiting begins at roughly 35 A, providing about 45% margin over the 24.25-A maximum peak inductor current. A 1:100 current-sense transformer and 7.5-Ω sense resistor are used. The design also uses a 3.3-nF hiccup capacitor, Type 2A compensation targeting 10 kHz with 40.2-kΩ RCOMP, 15-nF CCOMP and 47-pF CHF components, and a 102-kΩ RSC resistor.

- Controller supply voltage must be regulated and within 4 V to 14 V. At least 0.1 µF of ceramic bypass capacitance is required from VIN to AVSS, with additional local or bulk capacitance as needed. Layout guidance emphasizes separating feedback and control traces from switching signals, minimizing switch-node copper and high-di/dt loops, using short and wide current paths, separating analog and power grounds except at one connection point, placing filtering and compensation components near their pins, and connecting CFP backside metallization to AVSS through multiple vias. TI states that application information is not part of the component specification and that users must validate and test final designs.

A Fox News “Halftime Report” leads with an argument that declining party affiliation and California’s nonpartisan top-two primary system have failed to reduce partisanship. Citing preliminary data that California registered independents now outnumber registered Republicans, the article says national media has sorted voters into ideologically homogeneous blocs, increasing alienation and incentives for extremism. It warns that further party decline could produce numerous narrow-interest factions rather than a moderate third party and argues that parties need strengthening, not additional weakening.

Other reports cover Trump’s 40.8% average job approval, Democrats’ six-point average advantage in House polling, and a Quinnipiac survey showing Ted Cruz leading Beto O’Rourke 50%–39% in Texas. Republicans are emphasizing immigration, while Democrats promote health-care protections. Trump plans to address a high-dollar America First Action fundraiser despite limits on direct donations. Phoenix Mayor Greg Stanton resigned to run for Congress, while Trump continued questioning the FBI’s Russia investigation after Rep. Trey Gowdy defended its use of a confidential source; reporting also described Trump’s pressure on Jeff Sessions to reverse his recusal.

Additional features recount Andrew Jackson’s fatal 1806 duel with Charles Dickinson, include reader commentary on political tribalism and manual transmissions, and report that Long Island Rail Road passengers united in singing Billy Joel’s “Piano Man.”

Junior County, a 6-foot-4 combo guard from Wasatch Academy in Utah, committed to UConn as the first 2026 recruiting commitment for coach Dan Hurley. The No. 43 prospect in ESPN’s SC Next 100 and a top-five shooting guard chose the Huskies after visiting his other finalists. County cited the practice atmosphere, his relationship with Hurley and the campus, and expects to develop and make winning plays on both ends of the floor. He averaged 13.6 points, 4.8 rebounds and 3.4 assists for the Utah Prospects last spring and summer. UConn’s recent classes include a top-five group in 2025 and consecutive top-10 classes in 2024 and 2023, with back-to-back national championships in between.

VentureWire’s November 14, 2000 issue reports private-company business and technology news. Top stories cover Apax Partners’ planned merger of its Israeli and European units and $600 million commitment to Israeli companies; New Edge Networks’ elimination of 135 jobs and office consolidation; KSolutions’ $50 million first funding round; and Cisco’s $295 million stock acquisition of wireless-chip maker Radiata.

The “Bad News” section reports four senior Buzz MSP executives’ departures, eSociety’s closure, and iExplore restructuring layoffs. New product developments include Venture Studio’s launch of EstimatesOnline and name changes for Wapmagic, Radix Wireless, and NetEx.

The issue also reports numerous board and executive appointments, Murphree Venture Partners’ first close of a fund targeting $150 million–$200 million, venture-capital personnel changes, and corrections to prior coverage.

Beijing ordered 15 online property portals to remove false ads, rumors, feng shui and financing advice, and stop promising investment returns or helping with hukou and school enrollment. The curbs accompany higher down payments, a 25-year mortgage limit, and an existing ban on third-home purchases.

Researchers led by the Okinawa Institute of Science and Technology combined fungal fossils with 17 horizontal gene transfers to refine the evolutionary timeline of fungi. Because fungi rarely fossilize well and evolved complex multicellularity multiple times, these transfers provided “older-than/younger-than” constraints that helped calibrate molecular-clock estimates. The analysis dates a common ancestor of living fungi to roughly 1.4–0.9 billion years ago, hundreds of millions before land plants. The findings support a prolonged period of fungi-algae interactions in which fungi recycled nutrients, broke down rock, and helped form primitive soils. Researchers suggest these ecosystem-engineering fungi prepared terrestrial environments for the later colonization of land by plants.

The passage argues that U.S. strategic superiority and resolve contributed to avoiding war during the 1962 Cuban missile crisis, but that subsequent complacency allowed Soviet military growth and declining American credibility. It criticizes the Carter administration’s defense cuts, inconsistent responses to Soviet actions in Cuba and Afghanistan, and weak Middle East policy as evidence of an approach that invited aggression and isolated the United States. Drawing on the lessons of World War II, it contends that weakness can be provocative and that peace requires a strong defense. It calls for restoring U.S. military superiority in conventional and strategic forces, firmly combating terrorism, maintaining deterrence, and consulting allies to strengthen alliance unity. It concludes that reaffirming American principles and rebuilding confidence and cohesion among allies offers the best hope for world peace.

- Internal LJM2 documents showed that the Enron partnership led by CFO Andrew Fastow and several associates earned more than $7 million in management fees and about $4 million in capital increases on roughly $3 million invested. Some transactions improved after terms were renegotiated; LJM2 received its $30 million investment plus $10.5 million from an early settlement of the Raptor III deal. The arrangement raised conflict-of-interest concerns. Enron reported a $618 million third-quarter loss after a $1.01 billion write-down, including about $35 million from ending LJM2 transactions, while a $1.2 billion shareholder-equity reduction followed the repurchase of 55 million shares involved in LJM2 deals. Enron said its dealings were proper, Fastow ended his association with LJM2 in July, and a shareholder sued alleging that Fastow’s management of partnerships cost Enron at least $35 million.

- TheStreet.com highlighted Bayer’s limited anthrax-related Cipro upside, i2 Technologies’ $5.5 billion quarterly loss under GAAP, Microsoft’s fake cereal-box campaign targeting Novell, AMD CEO Jerry Sanders’ defiant remarks amid AMD’s downturn, and Enron’s disputed accounting and shrinking shareholder equity.

- New Power revised its netting agreement with three Enron subsidiaries through January 4, 2002, reducing required cash collateral. The first $70 million must remain cash, while collateral above that may include eligible receivables and inventory under specified limits. New Power said the change and cost reductions should provide sufficient resources while it seeks asset-backed financing, though no arrangement had been secured. It maintained its previous third-quarter loss estimate but forecast slightly lower customers and revenue.

- National Journal reported that Cassidy & Associates led Washington lobbying firms with $16.68 million in first-half fees. Greenberg Traurig rose to fifth after hiring Jack Abramoff and earning $4 million from a Cuba-related case; Van Scoyoc ranked sixth and Quinn Gillespie seventh. Patton Boggs, Akin Gump, and Verner Liipfert ranked second through fourth, while Williams & Jensen, Washington Council Ernst & Young, and Barbour Griffith & Rogers completed the top ten.

- The Texas Business Hall of Fame honored Stanford Alexander, Compaq founder Rod Canion, former Reliant Energy chairman Don Jordan, and Dynegy chairman Chuck Watson for their business and civic contributions.

- London Metal Exchange Week was expected to attract fewer delegates because of recession concerns, budget cuts, and travel fears. Metals demand and prices were falling, producers faced pressure to cut output, and several firms were leaving or reducing their involvement in the industry.

- The Bombay High Court scheduled hearings for December 11 on Dhabol Power Company’s challenge to the Maharashtra Electricity Regulatory Commission’s jurisdiction over its dispute with the Maharashtra State Electricity Board. The case also involved allegations of bias by an MERC member and requests from the U.S. Exim Bank and DPC’s offshore lenders to intervene.

During its earnings call, United Airlines positioned itself as a premium carrier with subtly pointed comparisons to Delta Air Lines and American Airlines. United emphasized uncrowded airport lounges, contrasting its approach with long lines at Delta’s Sky Clubs, and highlighted seatback entertainment installed on more than 146,000 seats across 765 aircraft. United also said 64% of its fleet has seatback screens, representing more than $1.6 billion in investment.

United’s premium cabin revenue rose about 6% year over year in the third quarter, compared with Delta’s 9%. Delta has addressed crowded lounges by changing access and fees and introducing higher-end Delta Reserve lounges. American, meanwhile, largely avoids seatback screens on domestic aircraft, favoring tablet holders and connectivity while arguing that more than 90% of customers use their own devices.

United’s stock fell more than 7% after mixed quarterly results but remained up over 34% year over year.

China’s top official in Hong Kong warned that no activity harming national sovereignty and security, challenging central government authority or Hong Kong’s Basic Law, or undermining mainland stability would be tolerated. The warning reflects growing concern over pro-independence politicians, tightening Beijing control, and erosion of the city’s autonomy, freedoms, rule of law, and distinct identity.

MusConv is paid software that transfers playlists from Spotify to Amazon Music. Its Basic, Professional, and Ultimate subscriptions include features such as unlimited transfers, CSV exports, batch importing, free updates, Apple Music support, priority assistance, and duplicate-track deletion.

The speaker describes his pregame routine of wearing a hoodie and headphones, clearing his mind, and eliminating distractions. He says the team played well, values winning regardless of how goals are scored, and is focused on an upcoming Monday night opportunity after a difficult Chicago series. Motivated by his desire to win the Stanley Cup and support from teammates, family, and friends, he blocks out outside pressures. He credits his teammates’ first-period shot blocking and prevention of second and third chances for creating momentum and helping him perform.

The Competition and Markets Authority said some care homes may be breaking consumer law through practices including charging deceased residents, billing before admission, threatening eviction, failing to advertise prices and hindering complaints. These abuses particularly affected self-funding residents, whose weekly fees often exceeded £600 and led some to sell their homes. The CMA is considering tighter billing rules and is bringing a test case, while stating sector returns cover operating costs. Citizens Advice said gaps in consumer protection cause distress and financial pressure.

Amazon.com, Inc. filed a Form 8-K dated July 23, 2015, announcing its second-quarter 2015 financial results. The filing includes a results press release and information regarding non-GAAP financial measures, both incorporated by reference. It was signed by Chief Financial Officer Brian T. Olsavsky.

During National Health Center Week, Caring Health Center highlighted care for over 20,000 Springfield residents, held an Elected Officials Day with community leaders, and honored healthcare contributors.

Education regulators are reviewing a former technology employee’s allegation that Ohio’s Electronic Classroom of Tomorrow (ECOT) ordered staff to manipulate student data with ActivTrak software to inflate attendance and secure state funding. The employee reported the concerns to the Education Department and Auditor Dave Yost, whose office included them in an unreleased financial audit. The state had previously found that ECOT overreported full-time-equivalent students, owed $60 million for 2015–16, and faced a $19 million penalty for 2016–17. The whistleblower said an initial ActivTrak run showed students had only slightly more than half the required hours to justify ECOT’s enrollment, and that officials adjusted data to meet desired outcomes. ECOT’s spokesman denied the allegations, while its superintendent alleged a state conspiracy. The Education Department said it had questioned ECOT extensively and would consider the information in its next attendance review. State officials called for a criminal investigation, but the county prosecutor said he had received no referral.

In his final Oval Office address, the president thanks Vice President Gore, his Cabinet, staff, and Americans, citing eight years of economic, social, and environmental progress. He says the nation created 22 million jobs, reached its lowest unemployment in 30 years and highest homeownership, expanded family leave, college aid, health insurance, education, and land preservation, reduced crime and poverty, and improved incomes, air, water, and food safety.

He identifies three priorities. First, America should maintain fiscal responsibility, noting that recent budgets converted deficits into surpluses and reduced national debt by $600 billion. Continuing that course could lower interest rates, support prosperity, prepare for retiring baby boomers, invest in the future, and provide tax relief. Second, globalization makes America more interconnected and exposed to terrorism, organized crime, narcotics, weapons, disease, and environmental degradation, so the United States must lead through alliances and global engagement. He argues that global inequality requires action and that trade should benefit people worldwide. Third, America must unite amid increasing diversity by respecting common values, overcoming differences, and treating everyone fairly and with dignity regardless of race, religion, gender, sexual orientation, or arrival date.

He wishes George W. Bush and his family well, expresses confidence in America’s future, and says he will remain in service as a citizen.

Blockchain is being adopted across enterprises for security, transparency, efficiency, sustainability, and traceability, but implementation requires coordinated management, finance, supply chain, IT, legal, procurement, and sales expertise. Successful integration depends on technical capabilities alongside social, methodological, and personal competences, including leadership, communication, creativity, problem-solving, adaptability, and willingness to learn.

The study examined blockchain curricula at US universities with AACSB-accredited business schools. A March 2024 search identified 533 institutions, 151 of which offered at least one blockchain course, yielding 361 courses. Courses were classified by topic and academic field, analyzed for connections with AI, IoT, and cybersecurity, and independently categorized and peer-reviewed by multiple authors.

Computer science and information systems hosted the most courses, followed by finance, business and strategy, and law. Business was the largest academic field with 216 offerings, compared with 85 in computer science and 31 in law; courses also appeared in areas such as biology, literature, and political science. Seventy-two percent of courses were undergraduate-level, 23% graduate-level, and 5% available at both levels. Private universities were more likely than public universities to offer blockchain courses, and offerings generally increased with undergraduate enrollment.

The largest course category was blockchain fundamentals and overviews, followed by digital assets and cryptocurrencies and technical development. Business implications, law and compliance, supply chain and governance, and interactions with other technologies were less frequently covered. AI and machine learning were referenced most often among related technologies, followed by IoT and non-fungible tokens.

The findings support holistic workforce preparation and curricula aligned with industry needs. Future research should assess competency requirements by job level, identify which disciplines address them, examine evolving course content, and repeat the study after five years.

After his grandfather died of heart disease, seven-year-old Joseph Nyberg created “Heart Cents,” collecting pennies and dollars in Savannah and Richmond Hill for a month. He raised more than $200 for St. Joseph’s heart patients; matching and anonymous donations brought the total to $672 and 14 Heart Cents. The funds will help with transportation and co-pays, and Joseph plans to continue fundraising in his grandfather’s honor.

The device supports single-SDO, dual-SDO, and source-synchronous read protocols. It defaults to SPI-00-S after power-up or asynchronous reset; another SPI protocol can be selected through SDI_MODE[1:0], with SDO_MODE[1:0] set to 00b for reads. RVS remains low during SPI transfers. Short frames can read only required MSBs, while long frames with SDO_CNTL_REG[7:0] = 00h support daisy chaining. Optional dual-SDO mode is enabled by setting SDO1_CONFIG[1:0] to 11b, using the ALARM/SDO-1/GPO pin as SDO-1 and launching two data bits per SCLK edge. A valid write requires at least 32 SCLKs per transfer frame.

The disclosure describes noninvasive physiological monitoring systems and methods that combine optical sensor data from multiple patient measurement sites to generate a single physiological-parameter measurement. Light of one or more wavelengths is transmitted through tissue, and photodetector signals, raw or minimally processed, are combined by a signal processor. Measurements may include oxygen saturation, pulse rate, plethysmograph waveform, perfusion index, pleth variability index, methemoglobin, carboxyhemoglobin, total hemoglobin, glucose, and other patient characteristics. The processor may also generate separate measurements for each site and compare or average them.

Additional embodiments employ multiple light emitters and photodetectors distributed in three-dimensional configurations conforming to a measurement site’s anatomy, including clip and adhesive-tape sensors. These arrangements provide varied light paths, improve measurement robustness, and supply topology information that can indicate whether a sensor is correctly positioned. The disclosure covers suitable monitors, sensor interfaces, signal processors, sensors, and associated methods for measurement sites such as the nose, earlobe, finger, hand, foot, or other body locations.

The patent concerns a compact, lightweight surgical robot arm and wrist designed to balance mobility, positioning accuracy, compactness, and force measurement. The wrist includes a proximal roll joint, a universal joint formed by crossed-axis pitch joints, and a terminal roll joint that can align with the surgical instrument shaft. This arrangement allows the end effector to occupy a hemispherical workspace without requiring fast motion near a singular joint configuration and helps multiple robot arms operate closely together.

Torque sensors associated with the wrist joints measure applied torque, including forces on an instrument in multiple directions. Their outputs are supplied to a processor, which distinguishes externally applied loads from motor-generated torque and can provide force feedback to the surgeon through haptic input devices. Suitable sensors include resistance-based strain gauges, piezoelectric strain gauges, and non-contact magnetostrictive gauges.

The arm uses alternating roll and pitch joints, including an RPRP sequence, with alternative sequences and lateral offsets to improve mobility, reduce kinematic singularities, and avoid enlarging the swept volume near the instrument tip. The wrist may be located at the end of the robot arm or within the surgical instrument. In either configuration, it supports surgical tools such as grippers, shears, cameras, lasers, or knives. The design aims to facilitate precise positioning, human-like wrist motion, compact multi-arm access, and safer movement of instruments through incisions without enlarging the wound channel.
Nobel Prizes honor discoveries but leave much science unseen; Karikó joined few women winning medicine’s 2023 prize.

CoreLogic reported year-over-year home-price growth of 8.3% in Los Angeles County, 8.2% in Riverside and San Bernardino counties, and 6.2% in Orange County in May. The book aims to establish common patterns and practices for distributed systems, regularizing their design in the way patterns have improved algorithmic and object-oriented development. It defines distributed systems as applications composed of components running across multiple machines, while beginning with single-node container patterns that form the building blocks of distributed-system patterns.

Containers establish boundaries for resources, team ownership, and separation of concerns. Separating application components into containers enables resource isolation, tailored requirements and priorities, modular reuse, focused team ownership, easier testing and updates, and independent, smaller, more reliable deployments and rollbacks. The single-node patterns assume tightly coupled containers can be reliably scheduled on one machine and may share volumes, filesystems, network namespaces, and memory; Kubernetes calls such a grouping a pod.

The Combo defense counters Four Corner and other spread offenses by combining perimeter person-to-person pressure with baseline zone support. Three outside defenders deny passes, force the dribbler toward the sideline, and stop return passes. Rotations trap penetration or picks, creating forced passes and interception opportunities. If X4 and X5 handle and shoot well, switch to a 1-3-1 trap.

Mikel Obi pledged that Nigeria’s Super Eagles would give their best against England in a friendly at Wembley on June 2, 2018. Nigeria will also face the Czech Republic before competing in World Cup Group D against Croatia, Iceland and Argentina.

The passage documents AGESA host-environment services and boot procedures for x86-64 and AArch64 platforms. Stackless assembler routines create a per-core pre-memory stack, map it into global address space, configure MTRRs, establish SS:ESP, and create a UEFI PEI hand-off. Protected-mode callers must provide a zero-base GDT stack-segment descriptor. A corresponding routine removes the pre-memory stack after main memory becomes available, flushes caches, and disables CAR mode without modifying MTRRs. AArch64 systems with a PSP do not use these stack and early-boot mechanisms.

AmdCreateStruct allocates and default-initializes AGESA parameter structures using the pre-memory heap, post-memory DRAM, or host-provided storage; AmdReleaseStruct releases them. Other services return DIMM data-eye bitmaps, APIC addresses, available pre-memory execution-cache size, processor-die PCI addresses, the current socket/die/core identity, and FRU DIMM locations for a memory address. They also merge requested MMIO ranges and read event-log entries from a circular buffer.

AmdInitReset performs minimal reset-time processor initialization on all cores, separates BSP and AP tasks, configures FCH features, and allocates up to three flash-based execution-cache regions under address, size, alignment, and boundary rules. AmdInitEarly establishes the boot environment from platform, VRM, power-management, C-state, frequency, table-generation, display, and PCIe settings; it initializes links and power management and may request a warm reset. The post-memory sequence initializes and enables main memory, handles HOB or artifact data, disables the pre-memory stack, configures graphics hardware, and leaves the BSP and APs in defined cache and MTRR states. Later boot stages generate ACPI, DMI, PState, WHEA, CRAT, and CDIT information for operating-system handoff and prepare final processor state. Separate procedures save silicon context for suspend and restore or reinitialize it during resume.

Required host call-outs cover buffer allocation, deallocation, and lookup; system reset initiation; SPD reads; execution of routines on application processors; AP task waiting and idling; and related coordination. Optional call-outs support heap rebasing, IDS data retrieval, memory timing, training, voltage, external Vref, and self-refresh hooks, video BIOS repost, FCH customization, memory-test voltage adjustment, PCIe clock requests, and platform-specific controls. Most interfaces require an established stack, coherent processor links where topology data is queried, correct MTRR and cache handling, and host-provided memory allocation or preservation across the pre- to post-memory transition. Published entry functions reside in a protected flash boot block, and host customization is supported through build-configuration settings and user-defined register tables.

United Distributors sued Air-eo Appliance & Hardware, Inc., Henry R. Burke, and Alfred R. Willis for an unpaid $3,107.82 note. Willis had signed a personal guarantee when contemplating becoming a 50% shareholder in Air-eo. Before acquiring stock, however, he decided not to join the venture. Although the plaintiff’s salesman returned Willis’s other documents, he unintentionally retained the signed guarantee.

Air-eo later purchased air-conditioning units from the plaintiff, and Burke continued operating the business without Willis’s participation. Willis argued that the guarantee failed for lack of consideration because he never became a shareholder, and alternatively asserted revocation and estoppel. The Louisiana Supreme Court affirmed the dismissal of the suit against Willis, holding that his contemplated stock ownership and association with Air-eo were the sole consideration for the guarantee. Because those plans failed and the plaintiff was informed that Willis would not participate, the guarantee became ineffective under Revised Civil Code Articles 1825–1827.

The VIX, created by the CBOE in 1993, measures expected U.S. equity-market volatility over the following 30 days and is widely used as a market-sentiment indicator. Introduced in 2004, VIX futures are contracts based on the VIX Index that trade on Cboe Futures Exchange. They allow investors to hedge equity risk, diversify portfolios, arbitrage, or speculate on volatility. Although generally negatively correlated with equities, futures do not precisely track spot VIX; the S&P 500 VIX Short-Term Futures Index captures only about half of spot movements, and rolling contracts can make it costly as a long-term hedge.

A VIX futures strategy may use technical or fundamental analysis to determine entry and exit points, combined with risk management and position sizing. The authors’ backtests of futures did not produce a strategy they considered valuable, so they instead tested buying stocks when spot VIX was high. That strategy was invested 13.11% of the time, averaged a 0.64% gain per trade, returned 5.78%, had a 23% maximum drawdown versus 55% for buy-and-hold, and had only two down years, 2008 and 2022.

VIX prices are primarily influenced by bull and bear market cycles: they generally decline during bull markets and rise during bear markets. Futures pricing also reflects mean reversion through contango, when spot VIX is low, and backwardation, when it is extremely high. The VIX index has historically performed better in summer and fall, stagnated in winter, and declined in spring.

Full and mini contracts are quoted to three decimal places. Their multipliers are $1,000 and $100 per index point, respectively. The minimum price fluctuation is 0.05, representing a $50 tick for the full contract. Monthly contracts expire on the Wednesday 30 days before the third Friday of the following month, with trading ending at 8:00 a.m. CT and final financial settlement based on the VIX Special Opening Quotation.

Traders access futures through a funded brokerage account; leverage can magnify losses substantially. CFDs are broker-specific contracts without expiry dates. The futures symbol is VX, while the index symbol is VIX. VX reached 80.850 in March 2020; the spot index’s record high was 89.53 in October 2008, and its low was 8.56 in November 2017.

The study developed simultaneous ADF-EDS-EELS tomography to map three-dimensional structure, chemical composition, and transition-metal valence states in a single low-dose STEM acquisition. This reduced cumulative electron exposure and beam damage while maintaining precise alignment among imaging, compositional, and spectroscopic channels without post-registration.

Applied to NCM111 cathodes at pristine, 50-, 100-, and 200-cycle states, the method showed progressive capacity loss of 34.3% after 50 cycles and 52.2% after 100 cycles, with complete failure by 200 cycles. The layered Li(TM)O₂ structure became spinel-like after 100 cycles and rock-salt-like by 200 cycles.

Chemical composition remained largely uniform throughout the particle and was nearly unchanged through 100 cycles. At 200 cycles, average oxygen content fell from about 66–67% to 61%, and approximately 33.7% of particle volume was estimated to have a rock-salt composition. In contrast, transition-metal segregation was concentrated near particle surfaces and was strongest for Co, followed by Ni and Mn.

Mn and Co valence states showed pronounced depth dependence. Between 100 and 200 cycles, Mn4+ decreased from 80.7% to 53.4% and Mn2+ increased from 12.1% to 42.0%; Co3+ decreased from 77.5% to 11.0% while Co2+ increased from 22.5% to 89.0%. Surface-localized transition-metal clustering was present even in pristine particles and was identified as the remaining explanation for lower near-surface valence states after oxygen gradients, excess lithium, and secondary phases were ruled out.

Overall, degradation was attributed to interacting structural phase transitions, transition-metal migration, and dissolution-driven segregation. These processes produced non-monotonic changes in chemical inhomogeneity and valence states during cycling. The simultaneous tomography framework was presented as a broadly applicable method for correlating structural, chemical, and electronic behavior in complex materials.

Brayan Rocchio’s eighth-inning solo homer ignited a five-run rally as the Guardians beat the Tigers in Game 2 of the AL Wild Card Series, forcing a decisive Game 3. Rocchio connected with Troy Melton’s 99.9-mph fastball despite strong winds and difficult shadows, then Cleveland broke a 1-1 tie after managing only two hits through seven innings. Detroit stranded a team playoff-record 15 baserunners. The comeback extended Cleveland’s season after Rocchio spent six weeks in Triple-A and the club overcame a 15½-game division deficit. Both teams now face elimination, with the Guardians carrying momentum after repeatedly overcoming adversity.

The Indiana Court of Appeals affirmed the trial court’s determination that Mumma Brothers Drilling Co. owed sales or use taxes on certain drilling-equipment purchases. Although Mumma was a contractor covered by Indiana Code 6-2-1-38(k), it could avoid tax if the ultimate purchaser or user had an exemption. Mumma relied on the exemption for manufacturing machinery and equipment directly used to extract tangible personal property. The court held that extracting water for personal, business, farm, or livestock use, without resale, did not qualify because “manufacturing” contemplated resale of the extracted property. Mumma therefore failed to establish an exemption, and the judgment was affirmed.

Elliott Wave theory is a technical-analysis principle developed by Ralph Nelson Elliott from 75 years of stock data, asserting that asset prices move in recognizable wave patterns. It has two main wave types: five-part impulse waves that move with the market trend and three-part corrective waves that move against it. Each wave contains smaller sub-waves and follows specific identification rules, including that wave 2 cannot fully retrace wave 1 and wave 3 cannot be the shortest motive sub-wave. Traders use the theory to identify possible price directions and trading opportunities across stock, forex, and commodity markets. It is mainly used by technical traders, including day traders, swing traders, and long-term investors, often alongside trend lines, moving averages, RSI, and stochastic oscillators. No single timeframe is best; it depends on the trader’s style and personality. Because wave interpretation, entries, and exits are highly subjective, the theory offers no certainty and is extremely difficult to backtest, even with AI and machine learning, while also creating risks of curve fitting.

In a Supreme Court hearing on Holsey Ellingburg’s sentence, the government agreed that the Mandatory Victims Restitution Act cannot increase his punishment because it was enacted after his offense. Justices debated whether required restitution is criminal, civil, or both, and therefore whether the Ex Post Facto Clause bars applying it. Justice Alito emphasized the statute’s victim-remedy features, while Justices Kagan and Jackson stressed its integration into criminal sentencing. After arguments that Ellingburg should prevail, an attorney appointed by the justices defended his sentence. The author predicted the Court would reject applying the statute to Ellingburg early in the year, without lengthy separate opinions, though some justices might disagree.

This preprint examines how microtubule dynamics influence androgen-receptor signaling, taxane response, and drug resistance in advanced prostate cancer. Approximately one-third of metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancers are primarily refractory to systemic therapy, and tumors refractory to tubulin inhibitors are uniformly fatal within 12–18 months. Docetaxel and cabazitaxel are the only approved chemotherapy options, but reliable molecular markers for selecting effective taxanes or other tubulin inhibitors are lacking.

Wild-type androgen receptor and splice variants associate differently with microtubules. ARv567 is predominantly microtubule-bound, and its nuclear accumulation is inhibited by paclitaxel; ARv7 shows less microtubule association, is unaffected by paclitaxel in the same assay, and is associated with docetaxel resistance in xenografts. In isogenic prostate cancer cells, wild-type AR slightly reduced microtubule growth speed and caused microtubules to slow near the cell edge. ARv7 was predominantly nuclear, increased microtubule growth speed by more than 40%, eliminated edge-associated slowing, and produced tracks that rarely overlapped nuclear regions.

A computational imaging method was used to quantify microtubule dynamics by tracking fluorescent EB1 or EB3 comets in live-cell confocal images. The pipeline detects comets with band-pass filtering, tracks them using Mahalanobis distance and a Kalman filter, and links growth tracks through a Hungarian algorithm with temporal and directional search constraints to identify pauses, shortening, rescue, and catastrophe events.

Patient-derived prostate organoids were established from primary, lymph-node, and distant-metastatic tumors from 16 patients. Reducing the ROCK inhibitor Y-27632 fourfold relative to benign-organoid conditions temporarily selected for resilient high-grade tumor cells. Low-grade tumor cells converted to normal epithelium ex vivo, whereas high-grade primary tumor cells failed to propagate and were overgrown by normal epithelial cells. In mCRPC, androgen-independent circulating tumor cells could be only 6.2–7.0 µm in diameter and detectable by PSMA despite absent AR expression, indicating that size-based circulating-cell enrichment could miss disseminated disease.

Additional findings linked altered cytoskeletal dynamics to resistance. Op18 upregulation in androgen-independent organoids was associated with reduced microtubule polymerization, smaller spindles, and smaller, more resilient cells. ERG-positive circulating tumor cells showed no taxane-induced microtubule bundling, unlike ERG-negative cells. Paclitaxel suppressed fast microtubule growth in breast cancer cells, and higher EB1 density, smaller cell size, and altered turnover were associated with resistance. Both abnormally fast and abnormally slow microtubule turnover were identified as resistance-associated features.

The tumor suppressor pVHL was shown to stabilize microtubules and reduce turnover, whereas pVHL loss increased turnover and reduced drug susceptibility. Serum starvation induced quiescence-associated turnover through GSK3β-mediated phosphorylation and inactivation of pVHL; GSK3 inhibition restored baseline dynamics. pVHL and GSK3β cooperatively maintained primary cilia. Specific VHL mutation domains were associated with different microtubule abnormalities, suggesting that destabilizing or stabilizing tubulin drugs could be matched to particular mutation classes.

Circular Hough transform was used to detect taxane-induced circular microtubule bundles. After paclitaxel exposure, 83% of parental A549 cells formed rings, compared with 27% of BRCA1-knockdown cells, and ring intensity was substantially higher in the susceptible cells, providing a potential image-based resistance assay. The proposed validation strategy includes correlating organoid microtubule dynamics with expression of 70 microtubule-regulating genes and clinical outcomes, testing regulator knockdowns in patient-derived xenografts, evaluating treated tissue slices through three-dimensional imaging, performing transcriptomic analyses, and screening expanded tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes with patient-derived organoids.

Overall, the work proposes computational microtubule-dynamics measurements as ex vivo tools for anticipating drug resistance, matching tumors to tubulin inhibitors, and identifying sensitizing targets. It also emphasizes that microtubulin-inhibitor effects are dose-dependent and nonlinear, reinforcing the need for reliable biomarkers and individualized regimen and dose selection.

The document describes NVIDIA RTX IO, the GA10x Ampere architecture, and the A40, A6000, and GeForce RTX 30-series GPUs. RTX IO addresses bottlenecks in traditional storage APIs by using Microsoft DirectStorage and GPU-based lossless decompression to transfer compressed assets directly from NVMe SSDs to the GPU. NVIDIA claims up to 100× I/O performance and substantially lower CPU utilization, enabling faster game and asset loading, smoother frame rates, reduced pop-in and stutter, and high-rate texture streaming.

The Ampere-based NVIDIA A40 targets data-center visual computing, AI, and scientific workloads. It offers increased FP32 and ray-tracing throughput, higher AI throughput with sparsity, PCIe Gen4 bandwidth, 48 GB of memory expandable to 96 GB through NVLink, virtual GPU support, and compatibility with the NVIDIA EGX Platform. The GA10x architecture also supports advanced displays, including 4K at 120 Hz and 8K at 60 Hz through DisplayPort 1.4a and HDMI 2.1.

Fifth-generation NVDEC provides hardware decoding for MPEG-2, VC-1, H.264, H.265, VP8, VP9, and AV1. GA10x GPUs add hardware AV1 decoding capable of 8K60 HDR playback with low CPU usage. Seventh-generation NVENC provides hardware encoding for gaming, streaming, and archiving, including H.264 up to 4K and HEVC up to 8K.

GA10x provides up to twice the performance of the prior architecture in programmable shading, ray tracing, and AI. Its second-generation RT Core adds motion-blur acceleration and concurrent ray tracing with shading or compute, while its third-generation Tensor Core supports structural sparsity. The RTX 3090 includes 24 GB of memory and exceeds the TITAN RTX in performance, while the RTX 3070 uses GDDR6 and is described as faster than the RTX 2080 Ti.

The RTX A6000 provides 48 GB of GDDR6 memory, second-generation RT Cores, third-generation Tensor Cores, hardware-accelerated ray tracing, AI denoising, and support for combined 96 GB memory configurations through NVLink. New Error Detection and Replay technology detects and retries faulty GDDR6X memory transactions during overclocking, helping identify performance limits and reduce memory errors. The document also notes that specifications may change and includes NVIDIA’s warranty, liability, licensing, and suitability disclaimers.

The Eleventh Circuit affirmed Alexis Perez’s 51-month sentence for conspiracy to commit mail fraud. It rejected a three-level reduction for an incomplete conspiracy because Perez and his co-conspirators had developed a detailed plan, possessed the means to execute it, and were on the verge of doing so when law enforcement intervened. The court also rejected a minor-role reduction because Perez was involved in planning and preparation, understood the fraudulent scheme, was paid for his services, and was not shown to be less culpable than most participants. The court declined to enforce his sentence appeal waiver.

Price action trading is a form of technical analysis that uses patterns in an asset’s historical price movements to identify entry and exit opportunities. It examines price swings, broader trends and ranges, chart patterns, candlestick patterns, support and resistance, and market sentiment. Pure price action traders generally rely on these price-based features rather than indicators, though some combine them with moving averages, the VIX, or the RSI.

For day trading, price action is analyzed on intraday charts, where sufficient volatility is important. Common approaches include trend following, breakouts, reversal trades, and scalping. Backtesting is recommended to evaluate each strategy objectively, but price action strategies can be difficult to code and manual testing may be affected by cognitive bias. No strategy is universally best, and results may differ across markets, making out-of-sample testing, strategy optimization, and diversification important.

An example based on lower highs and lower lows showed poor long-side performance from 2000 to 2021, while a limited out-of-sample test of 21 trades produced a positive average return beginning in 2021. The article cautions that apparently convincing chart patterns may reflect randomness and that anecdotal evidence alone cannot establish a strategy’s long-term expectancy.

Ways to pay off debt include reducing credit card use, creating a spending plan and emergency fund, paying as much as possible each month, using extra income such as overtime, and cutting discretionary expenses. The passage recommends tackling high-interest debts first, redirecting payments from paid-off cards to remaining balances, and making gradual lifestyle changes to avoid becoming overwhelmed.

Spanish police dismantled a prostitution network recruiting Venezuelan transsexuals through fake “Miss Trans” competitions, freeing over 20 victims and arresting 14 suspected managers. Police said it earned up to €1 million over five years.

Google Doodle honored what would have been German physicist Max Born’s 135th birthday with a colorful homepage illustration. Born, a physicist and mathematician born in Breslau, Germany, made foundational contributions to quantum mechanics and received the 1954 Nobel Prize for the Born Rule, which uses mathematical probability to predict measurement outcomes and underpins nearly all quantum-physics predictions. He spent 12 years as a professor of theoretical physics at the University of Göttingen, where notable scientists including Werner Heisenberg, Enrico Fermi, J. Robert Oppenheimer and Maria Goeppert-Mayer joined the institution. Born and Albert Einstein maintained a close friendship for more than 40 years despite differing scientific views. After Hitler came to power, Jewish academics including Born were prohibited from working at universities, and Born emigrated to England in 1933. He also worked with future Nobel laureate Otto Stern in Frankfurt. Born died on Jan. 5, 1970, aged 87, from a heart ailment complicated by arterial thrombosis.

The bill allows district and charter schools to develop innovative education plans and seek waivers of state board rules. LEAs may use restricted state funds and accept private support for such programs. Plans must be submitted to the State Board, which may terminate plans, grant waivers, and report annually by November 30. As no applications or approved plans have been reported, the Board should publicize the program, provide information and optional application forms, and support local applicants.

UK employment rose by 109,000 in the three months to April, lifting the rate to a joint-record 74.8%, with hiring continuing into May. However, annual regular pay growth fell to 1.7% while inflation reached 2.9%, reducing real pay and pressuring household spending. Post-election uncertainty may weaken business confidence and domestic growth, leaving growth more reliant on exports, corporate services and investment. Moderating input-cost inflation suggests consumer inflation may peak, but little improvement in wages is expected. With Brexit discussions beginning and the outlook unclear, the Bank of England is likely to keep interest rates on hold.

The passage describes host-environment integration with AGESA/AGESATM software through a binary-module interface. Host BIOS bridge code calls the AGESA dispatcher with function parameters, receives a status code, and provides reverse call-outs through a host-resident router. The host must establish a valid stack, populate the standard header, provide configuration data, and use published entry-point identifiers from AMD.H.

UEFI support spans SEC, PEI, DXE, and runtime phases, with libraries and tools for 16-bit, 32-bit, and 64-bit development. Platform-specific build options are supplied through files such as `<plat>Options.c`, and builds require environment variables identifying the AGESA root, options directory, and target platform. Core code can be supplied as a binary module or integrated as source; customization proceeds from platform solution to build method to individual configuration elements.

Assembly routines create and remove the pre-memory x86-64 stack, initialize processor cache and MTRRs, establish the SEC-to-PEI handoff frame, and later disable Cache-as-RAM after memory becomes available. These routines use stackless register-passing conventions and have documented register, status, alignment, and cache-control requirements.

Host services include creating and releasing AGESA parameter structures, reading DIMM data-eye results, obtaining APIC and PCI addresses, identifying the current socket, die, and core, mapping a memory address to a DIMM and its chip-select, bank, row, and column, merging MMIO ranges, and reading circular event-log entries.

The published initialization sequence covers reset, early configuration, memory initialization, environment setup, late initialization, and runtime preparation. These stages configure execution-cache regions, processor power management, memory and VRM settings, PCIe and graphics features, ACPI/DMI tables, and suspend or resume state. Processor and memory PEIMs coordinate initialization and publish PPIs and HOBs, while the DXE driver generates tables and publishes the AGESA DXE protocol. The host must provide required call-outs, including permanent buffer allocation, preserve specified cache controls and processor state, and maintain required memory regions across pre-memory and post-memory transitions.

Minister Schoenfeld met Finnish Foreign Minister Witting to clarify that American public and press opinion of Finland was less favorable than Witting believed and that the United States had not changed its earlier position. Witting defended Finland’s strategic aims, including control of the Karelian and Onega isthmuses, and described Finnish realism as rooted in long experience with Russia. He acknowledged Germany and Britain made similar claims regarding small nations and appeared uncertain how Finland could act amid forces beyond its control. He also relayed Procopé’s private view that small European nations might come under Anglo-Russian control after the war and Germany’s war industries should be dismantled. Separately, the Secretary of State advised Procopé that American citizen personnel of the Finnish Legation and consulates fell under Finnish ministerial jurisdiction and must comply with U.S. requests or sever official ties. Finnish consular personnel in the United States were also required to make certain inquiries before leaving the cities where their offices were located.

Mentoring relationships with adults and peers—including teachers, counselors, coaches, school staff, volunteers, extended family, friends, and community leaders—can support students’ academic achievement and educational engagement. School-based, after-school, community-based, and naturally developing mentoring relationships all show evidence of positive effects, including improved attendance, grades, test scores, classroom behavior, school connectedness, motivation, graduation, and postsecondary enrollment.

The COVID-19 pandemic intensified educational challenges, particularly for low-income students, students of color, students with learning disabilities, and other marginalized youth. By the end of the 2020–21 school year, the average student was reported to be five months behind in mathematics and four months behind in reading. Only 39% of students felt school adults were available to talk with them, and 49% identified depression and anxiety as obstacles to learning.

Meta-analyses from 2002, 2011, and 2019 found that mentoring programs generally improve academic and educational outcomes, including attendance, grades, test scores, classroom behavior, truancy, school engagement, and peer support. Research syntheses from the National Mentoring Resource Center similarly concluded that evidence-based mentoring programs often produce moderate-to-large effects. Mentoring can be especially effective when it addresses cultural, environmental, and social barriers and uses practices such as academic goal-setting and stress management. Cross-age peer mentoring improves school belonging and connectedness and may benefit both younger students and older mentors through gains in leadership and academic engagement.

Representative studies found that school-based programs such as Big Brothers Big Sisters, Gear Up, AMPED, Project Arrive, Success Mentors, and Check and Connect improved academic performance, assignment completion, attendance, credits earned, instructional time, school engagement, and graduation outcomes. After-school programs including Quantum Opportunities, the Village Model of Care, and Canada’s Pathways to Education were associated with higher GPAs, graduation rates, college acceptance or enrollment, and other positive outcomes.

Naturally developing relationships with teachers and other caring adults are also linked to stronger school attachment, motivation, attendance, educational attainment, graduation, and college attendance. Teacher mentoring can support students’ relationships with teachers and parents, reduce disciplinary problems and negative school behavior, and benefit students of color by strengthening racial regard, reducing stereotype threat, and helping address systemic barriers.

Mentoring relationships remain inequitably distributed. Youth of color, low-income youth, and youth whose parents have limited education report fewer mentoring relationships and less natural support from school personnel. Expanding access requires private, public, local, state, and federal investment, along with policies that increase both the quantity and quality of mentoring available to students.

A CDC-led longitudinal evaluation followed 11 SARS-CoV-2-positive nursing home residents in Georgia from October 2020 through April 2021. Participants underwent repeated nasal antigen and RT-PCR testing, viral culture, serology, and clinical assessments. Ten received the Pfizer-BioNTech vaccine, while one declined it.

Among 10 participants with post-infection samples, nine developed detectable Pan-Ig, IgG, and IgA antibodies, and eight developed IgM. Antibodies were first detected within 30 days of diagnosis. When antibodies first appeared, six of nine tested participants remained RT-PCR-positive, but none had culturable virus. Pan-Ig and IgG levels remained elevated, while IgM and IgA began declining around 31–60 days; some participants experienced IgM or IgA seroreversion before vaccination. One unvaccinated participant retained detectable Pan-Ig, IgG, and IgA antibodies for at least 150 days.

After vaccination, all 10 vaccinated participants had detectable Pan-Ig, IgG, and IgA, and six had detectable IgM. Post-vaccination Pan-Ig, IgG, and IgA geometric mean titers exceeded post-infection titers, with maximum ratios of 142.3, 200.5, and 4.4, respectively. Pan-Ig, IgG, and IgA titers began decreasing during 61–90 days after vaccination.

The findings indicate that nursing home residents mounted persistent antibody responses after infection and that vaccination augmented Pan-Ig, IgG, and IgA responses. Limitations included the small sample, exclusive use of the Pfizer-BioNTech vaccine, infrequent sampling, difficulty classifying illness severity, and evaluation before the Delta and Omicron variants emerged in the United States.
