The court affirmed the dismissal of Lever Brothers’ opposition to Thrift-D-Lux Cleaners’ service-mark application for “Thrift-D-Lux Cleaners,” bearing the slogans “Thrifty In Price” and “De Luxe In Quality.” Lever Brothers had extensively used and registered “Lux” for soap products and operated about 600 affiliated “Lux Laundries,” roughly 470 of which offered dry cleaning. It argued that “Lux” was the dominant portion of “Thrift-D-Lux” and likely to cause confusion.

The court held that “Thrift-D-Lux” conveys thrift combined with de luxe, rather than “Thrifty Lux.” Because “de luxe” is commonly used and no evidence supported likely confusion between “Lux Laundries” and “Thrift-D-Lux” stores, Lever Brothers had not shown it would be damaged by registration. The cited “Knit-Kins” case was distinguishable because the shared suffix was identical, while “D-Lux” and “Lux” differ. The “Sit-Ru-Lux” case was not controlling because it concerned related goods in the same commercial class rather than services.

An outside day is a two-bar price pattern in which the second bar has a higher high and lower low than the first and its open and close extend beyond the first bar’s range. It signals rising volatility and can reflect either buyer or seller conviction. The pattern has four configurations based on whether each bar is up or down; configurations with bars moving in opposite directions are outside reversals.

Outside bars may indicate trend continuation or reversal depending on the surrounding price action. A bullish outside day has a bullish second bar regardless of the first bar’s direction, while a bearish outside day has a bearish second bar. An outside reversal closes opposite to both the previous bar and the prevailing price swing, producing a bearish reversal in an upswing and a bullish reversal in a downswing.

Although popular, outside-bar strategies are subjective and context-dependent. The pattern should not be traded alone, but combined with trend, support and resistance, pivot, and Fibonacci analysis, and any strategy should be backtested.

SPY backtests found an average open-to-close gain of zero after an outside day, compared with roughly 0.04% for a random day; other ETF results also appeared random. One modified rule returned negative 0.07%, while the inverse rule gained 0.06% but was described as not tradable. Overall, extensive testing found little usefulness for outside days in day trading.

In his inaugural address, the incoming president thanks President Reagan and invokes George Washington’s example, presenting the inauguration as both a bicentennial celebration and evidence of the nation’s 200-year continuity. His first act is a prayer asking that power be used to help people rather than serve personal interests.

He declares that freedom works and is right, citing free markets, free speech, free elections, and individual liberty as foundations of a just, prosperous life. He urges unity on crucial issues, diversity on important ones, and generosity in all things. Despite America’s freedom and prosperity, he says the nation must avoid defining success solely through material wealth and should instead pursue greater kindness, civic responsibility, and moral purpose.

The president identifies homelessness, child neglect, addiction, crime, and unprepared young mothers as pressing problems. He argues that public spending alone cannot solve them, calls for reducing the federal deficit and allocating limited funds according to need, and emphasizes the resource of American goodness and courage. He encourages hands-on activism through community organizations, calling them “a Thousand Points of Light,” and urges cooperation between generations.

He also calls for renewed cooperation between the executive and legislative branches, a balanced federal budget, and an end to partisan division. Addressing national security and foreign affairs, he promises to maintain alliances, protect peace, honor commitments, continue developing closer relations with the Soviet Union, and promote good faith among nations.

He identifies drugs as a problem requiring a unified societal response and closes by expressing confidence in the American people, describing the nation’s future as a shared story of unity, diversity, and generosity.

The Pennsylvania Supreme Court affirmed judgment for assignees of a Pennsylvania judgment previously assigned by the Thompson Oil Company. The assignment was made for value and in good faith while the assignor, assignees, and judgment were all in Pennsylvania, making it valid everywhere and leaving the Thompson Oil Company with no attachable interest. A later New York foreign attachment against the judgment debtors therefore could not displace the assignees’ rights, even though the garnishees initially lacked notice of the assignment. The New York court’s contrary judgment did not bind the assignees, who were neither parties nor privies, and was void insofar as it affected them because New York lacked jurisdiction over the assignees and the assigned property. Full faith and credit did not prevent inquiry into the New York court’s jurisdiction. The garnishees’ payment was not a bar to recovery by the assignees. Any error in ordering production of the New York record was waived because no exception was taken and the parties later filed the record.

Aziz Ansari says he has used a flip phone without email for about a decade and relies on assistants, asks directions, calls his wife, and hails taxis rather than using smartphone apps. He credits this low-tech lifestyle with providing more space to think and helping him write, while acknowledging that such offline living is unrealistic and privileged for many. Ansari believes ChatGPT can make mistakes, reinforce existing beliefs, homogenize opinions, and outsource critical thinking; he prefers human interaction and says AI can diminish humanity. The article also notes other celebrities and noncelebrities choosing analog alternatives, including Chris Nolan, Dolly Parton, and people replacing smartphones with flip phones or wall-mounted landlines to reduce screen and social-media use.

The appellate court affirmed the dismissal of a plastic surgeon’s action against the New York State Department of Health. The court held that the suit, although framed as a disability-discrimination claim under Executive Law § 296, was actually a time-barried CPLR article 78 challenge to the revocation of his medical license by the Administrative Review Board for Professional Medical Conduct. It rejected the argument that the statute’s permissive “may review” language allowed an independent action, as that would undermine administrative-review law and risk inconsistent decisions.

Northern Ireland’s health service, the only UK health service not led by a minister, faces ageing and complex-care pressures, GP staffing difficulties, rising drug costs and prolonged hospital waits. An extra £30 million was allocated in March, when 83,392 people had waited over a year for a first hospital appointment. A neurology recall and poor care at Dunmurry Manor drew criticism of the RQIA, while 2016 reform recommendations stalled after Stormont’s collapse.
