SEV-ES defines special HLT behavior because #HV delivery ignores interrupt shadows. A guest should execute HLT with interrupts disabled without checking pending interrupts. If the host intercepts HLT while interrupts or non-maskable events are pending, it should immediately re-enter the guest. Upon resumption, the guest should inspect interrupt state as though it had just received #HV.

The #HV doorbell page is configured through VMGEXIT SW_EXITCODE 0x8000_0014 using SET and QUERY actions. SET is required when Restricted Injection is enabled, while QUERY determines whether a page is already assigned. The mapped page must be accessed with C=0, and guests should PVALIDATE it before handing it to the host. The host may clear its RMP assignment after mapping, and reuse of a former guest physical address requires a new page assignment.

The host must faithfully emulate APIC interrupt presentation, acknowledgment, in-service, and EOI semantics. It presents the highest-priority ready vector through PendingEvent.Vector, uses NoFurtherSignal to prevent duplicate #HV notifications, tracks acknowledgment and EOI state, and represents non-maskable events through PendingEvent flags.

The guest must atomically exchange PendingEvent with zero before acting on a vector. EOI handling requires exchanging NoEoiRequired with zero and, when its previous value was zero, writing the X2APIC MSR via VMGEXIT. Guests must handle non-maskable events even when EFLAGS.IF is zero and validate all observed vectors. Non-cooperative behavior may cause denial of service but must not compromise host integrity.

Existing national and industry measures remain limited by poor government–industry communication, divergent international regulations, and risks that emerge only during real-world use. ASTROCO is a conformer-style encoder for self-supervised representation learning of irregular astronomical light curves. It combines multi-head self-attention for long-range dependencies, depthwise convolutions with gated linear units for local features, and a gated feed-forward network, connected through residual connections, dropout, and layer normalization. Magnitudes and uncertainties are projected and concatenated with sinusoidal time embeddings, then fused via a linear layer, GeLU, and LayerNorm.

Training uses masked reconstruction: 50% of positions are targeted, with masked values, random replacements, and unchanged observations included in the loss. Trainable softmax weights mix features from all encoder layers before masked mean pooling produces compact embeddings.

On the MACHO R-band dataset, ASTROCO-S (5.9M parameters) and ASTROCO-L (15.2M parameters) achieve lower reconstruction error and higher macro-F1 scores than Astromer v1/v2. ASTROCO-S surpasses the baselines despite using fewer training resources, while ASTROCO-L achieves the strongest overall benchmark. The results indicate benefits from locality-aware convolutions, gating, and soft cross-layer feature mixing.

The Triangle Offense creates unique defensive problems because its options depend on defensive positioning. Traditional NBA defenses pack the paint, deny interior access, and force perimeter shots, often using “show and recover” against cuts and screens. The described phases cover denying the corner cut, defending the post feed, handling corner screen-and-roll action, and disrupting weakside two-man play.

SOS strategies aggressively disrupt the offense’s initial flow. They can extend full court to lengthen passing lanes and pull players away from their normal positions. Additional concepts address wing entries, post splits, and ball reversals.

“All Out” disruption begins with pressure on the first pass and a wing trap, forcing offensive players into unplanned situations. Defenders rotate into designated help positions, front the post, close out to open players, and use additional trap rotations after passes out of the trap. Optional trapping can continue on corner passes.

The paper reviews twelve shared tasks organized by NFDI4DS, a German consortium supporting FAIR, transparent, interoperable, and reproducible research data infrastructure. The tasks address scholarly information processing through community collaboration, standardized datasets and metrics, open resources, and shared methodological development.

Seven tasks are completed. SOMD 2025 evaluated joint software-mention and attribute extraction with relation classification, with the best system achieving F1 scores of 0.89 and 0.63 across two phases. SciVQA developed question-answering systems for scientific figures, using 3,000 images and 21,000 question-answer pairs to assess visual and non-visual reasoning. ClimateCheck linked social-media climate claims to scholarly articles, evaluating both abstract retrieval and claim–abstract relation classification. FoRC 2025 classified research papers by multiple contribution topics using a hybrid retrieval and zero-shot prompting approach. LLMs4Subjects, held as SemEval-2025 Task 5, evaluated bilingual subject tagging for 123,589 open-access technical-library records, with 14 teams using methods including LLM augmentation, few-shot ensembles, and retrieval-augmented generation. LLMs4OL-2024 benchmarked LLMs for ontology learning across three tasks and 21 subtasks, highlighting hybrid and domain-adapted methods. Scholarly QALD developed natural-language interfaces over scholarly knowledge graphs, including single-source, multi-source, and comparative question-answering tasks.

CheckThat!Lab Task 4 is ongoing at CLEF 2025. It includes detection of scientific claims, references, contexts, and entities in tweets, plus retrieval of source papers for claims with implicit references.

Four tasks are under development. Dataset and Machine Learning Model Mention Detection will use gold-standard corpora to support fine-grained extraction of ML models and datasets from scholarly articles. ReadMe2KG will extract named entities from GitHub README files and link them to the NFDI4DS knowledge graph. CURED, planned for 2026, will evaluate clinical prognosis models that provide calibrated uncertainty estimates to support collaborative decision-making. Algorithm2Domain is developing a meta-benchmarking platform and knowledge base for evaluating algorithm generalizability, domain adaptation, modular benchmarking, and FAIR benchmarking practices.

Together, the twelve tasks demonstrate NFDI4DS’s community-based approach to advancing tools, datasets, standards, and reusable research outputs.

NVIDIA’s Ampere-based A100 Tensor Core GPU is designed for HPC, AI, analytics, genomics, and related data-center workloads. Its 108 streaming multiprocessors and third-generation Tensor Cores accelerate IEEE-compliant FP64 computation, delivering up to 2.5× the FP64 performance of Tesla V100. A new double-precision matrix multiply-add instruction replaces eight V100 DFMA instructions, reducing instruction fetches, scheduling overhead, register reads, power use, and shared-memory bandwidth. Each A100 SM performs 64 FP64 FMA operations per clock, equivalent to 128 FP64 operations, and the GPU reaches peak FP64 throughput of 19.5 TFLOPS.

A100 also supports mixed-precision formats including FP16, BF16, and TF32. NVIDIA’s Tensor Core Accelerated Iterative Refinement Solver automates mixed precision for linear systems. Across 37 SuiteSparse tests, TF32 produced the fastest and most robust results, with geometric-mean speedups of 2.0× over the FP64 solver, compared with 1.9× for FP16 and 1.8× for BF16; speedups reached 4× for roughly 40,000-element complex matrices.

Fine-Grained Structured Sparsity uses a 2:4 pattern requiring two nonzero values in every four-entry vector. Sparse matrix multiply-accumulate instructions skip zero entries, doubling Tensor Core math throughput, while compression halves weight storage and bandwidth requirements. NVIDIA’s pruning recipe—dense training, structured pruning, and fine-tuning—produced virtually no inference-accuracy loss across evaluated vision, detection, segmentation, language-modeling, and translation networks. Sparsity-based training acceleration without accuracy loss remains an active research area.

A100 combines 192 KB of L1 cache and shared memory per SM, versus 128 KB on V100, and includes separate FP32 and INT32 cores that can execute simultaneously at full throughput. Its 40 GB HBM2 subsystem provides 1,555 GB/s of bandwidth, more than 1.7× that of V100. The 40 MB L2 cache is 6.7× larger than V100’s and provides 2.3× higher bandwidth. ECC protects HBM2, L2, L1 caches, and register files, while Compute Data Compression can improve DRAM bandwidth, L2 bandwidth, and effective L2 capacity by as much as twofold to fourfold.

Deep-learning optimizations include greater warp-level data sharing, larger Tensor Core operations, fewer issued instructions and register accesses, asynchronous global-to-shared memory copies, hardware asynchronous barriers, and programmable L2 residency controls. These features reduce register and shared-memory traffic, hide memory latency, improve cache reuse, and support strong scaling. CUDA 11 adds support for third-generation Tensor Cores, sparsity, CUDA Graphs, MIG, and L2 persistence. CUDA Graphs define workflows separately from execution, reducing repeated launch overhead and enabling graph-wide dependency optimizations. Cooperative Groups adds asynchronous-copy pipelines, hardware-accelerated reductions, and lower grid-synchronization overhead.

MIG can partition an A100 into as many as seven isolated GPU Instances with dedicated compute, cache, memory-controller, and DRAM paths. GPU Instances can contain multiple Compute Instances, each with its own scheduling pipe and independently switched GPCs, while supporting Volta-style MPS. This provides quality-of-service guarantees and fault isolation for concurrent virtual machines, containers, and processes. MIG configurations can be migrated between matching GPU Instances or GPUs, allowing workloads to be consolidated and physical GPUs to be serviced without terminating jobs.

Third-generation NVLink provides 12 links per A100, 50 Gbit/s per signal pair, and 600 GB/s total GPU-to-GPU bandwidth, compared with 300 GB/s on V100. PCIe Gen 4 provides 31.5 GB/s per direction on x16 connections, while SR-IOV enables PCIe GPU sharing and virtualization. A100 adds improved error attribution, isolation, containment, remote fault reporting, and NVLink recovery mechanisms for multi-GPU and multi-tenant environments.

Additional hardware includes a five-core NVJPG JPEG decoder, a GA100 Optical Flow Accelerator for optical-flow and stereo-disparity estimation, improved FP16 and FP32 atomic throughput, and five NVDEC units for H.264, HEVC, and VP9 decoding. A100 supports compute capability 8.0 and does not include display connectors, RT Cores, or an NVENC encoder.

DGX A100 combines eight A100 GPUs with six NVSwitches, providing 4.8 TB/s of bidirectional interconnect bandwidth and up to 5 PFLOPS of AI performance. Its eight ConnectX-6 HDR InfiniBand adapters each operate at 200 Gb/s. MIG can expose up to 56 isolated accelerators within the system, allowing training and inference jobs to run concurrently. NVIDIA reports up to six times the AI-training performance of V100-based DGX-1 systems. The DGX software stack includes CUDA 11, the NVIDIA Container Toolkit, and GPU-optimized containers for frameworks such as PyTorch, TensorFlow, TensorRT, RAPIDS, and CUDA-X HPC.

U.S. stocks reversed early gains Thursday as rising Treasury yields and technology weakness offset strong earnings ahead of major tech reports. The S&P 500 was headed for its first weekly decline in five after the Fed held rates steady and signaled concern about inflation; employment claims, factory prices and labor costs reinforced those concerns. The Dow rose 0.14%, while the S&P 500 fell 0.06% and the Nasdaq dropped 0.35%. Fourth-quarter S&P 500 earnings growth was estimated at 14.9%, with 79.7% of 227 reporters beating estimates. After hours, Amazon gained over 6%, Alphabet fell nearly 3% and Apple about 1%.

This study examines the global rankings of higher education institutions (HEIs) in ten Asian countries from 2015 to 2025, using the Times Higher Education World University Rankings (THE WUR), and considers the higher education policies that could improve those positions.

The literature review notes that while Asian HEIs make strong efforts to raise their global standings, they remain less competitive than American institutions; earlier studies covered single countries or case sets, and UNESCO/NGO reports highlighted internationalization, funding, quality, inequality, workforce-relevance and research/innovation weaknesses in Asian higher education, noting low international student hosting in South/West and Central Asia (1.2% each) and leading gross enrollment rates in East and South-East Asia (2000–2020). This gap motivates a longitudinal, ten-country study.

Methodologically, the research is a qualitative multiple case study. The study group comprises the top five HEIs per country from the 2024 THE Asia University Rankings for Bangladesh, China, India, Indonesia, Japan, Pakistan, the Philippines, Thailand and Vietnam, plus the top five Russian HEIs from the 2025 THE WUR (Russian HEIs are absent from the Asia ranking), with countries selected using CIA World Factbook population data. Data were drawn from open THE WUR datasets (2015–2025) and analyzed by document analysis, using year-by-year tables per institution; "successful momentum" denotes two-year-period improvements with an overall positive ten-year trend, and the reverse defines unsuccessful momentum. Validity was supported by analyst triangulation with two external evaluators; no ethics approval was required.

Results by country: Chinese HEIs showed the strongest gains (Tsinghua 49th to 12th; Peking 48th to 13th; Fudan 193rd to 36th; Zhejiang 301–350 to 47th; Shanghai Jiao Tong 276–300 to 52nd, slipping from the top 50). Japanese institutions ranked consistently, with Tokyo (23rd to 28th) and Kyoto (54th in 2021, 55th in 2024–2025) in the top 100, while Tohoku, Osaka and Tokyo Tech fluctuated until recovering into the top 200 by 2024. Russian HEIs performed stably: Lomonosov Moscow State University stayed in the top 200 (107th in 2025), MIPT reached 251–300, HSE and MEPhI remained near the top 500, and Bauman was least successful but fluctuating (351–400 in 2025). Indian HEIs trended positively, with the Indian Institute of Science consistently listed (mostly 251–300) and Anna University, Mahatma Gandhi University and Jamia Millia Islamia rising, while Shoolini fluctuated. Indonesian HEIs entered the index late and declined (ITB, BINUS, Sebelas Maret, Gadjah Mada reaching 1201–1500); Pakistani HEIs showed inconsistent patterns with Quaid-i-Azam best (401–500 in 2025); Bangladeshi HEIs were newcomers with mostly neutral trends; Vietnamese HEIs showed the steepest decline (Duy Tan and Ton Duc Thang falling from 401–500 to 601–800, HanoiUST and VNU Hanoi declining, Hue steady at 1501+); Philippine HEIs were mixed (University of the Philippines rose to 401–500 then declined; Ateneo, De La Salle declined; Mapúa and Santo Tomas stable at 1501+); Thai HEIs mostly declined slightly, with Chulalongkorn the most consistent.

The discussion concludes that, except for China, Japan and Russia, Asian HEIs lag behind international counterparts with unstable ranking profiles; India outperformed other Asian countries and Vietnam declined most sharply. Limitations are the restricted sample (top five HEIs in the ten most populous Asian countries) and the absence of QS or Webometrics data. Policy recommendations include diversifying global research/teaching networks, using global marketing and public relations, expanding funding opportunities, and opening overseas offices with supportive government regulations. The work was unfunded, single-authored, and free of conflicts of interest; the author, Dr. Can Sakar, holds a PhD from the University of Kansas and lectures at the Gendarmerie and Coast Guard Academy in Türkiye.

Odell Beckham Jr. accepted a six-game NFL suspension for violating the league’s performance-enhancing drug policy. The three-time Pro Bowler said he did not knowingly take banned substances and was told his testosterone levels were too high. The suspension began Tuesday, making him ineligible until Week 12. The 33-year-old free agent wants to return this season and identified four teams he would join. Beckham was released by the Dolphins last December after recording nine catches for 55 yards in nine games.

The lecture reviews renormalization and logarithmic resummation in SCET using the heavy-to-light \(b\to s\gamma\) current. The one-loop result separates into a piece matching the infrared behavior of QCD, ultraviolet divergences canceled by effective-theory counterterms, and a remainder whose difference from the full theory determines matching. The required Wilson-coefficient counterterm contains both \(1/\epsilon^2\) and logarithmic terms. Here the operator momentum label \(\omega\) is fixed by external kinematics to \(m_b\).

In general, an operator’s delta function fixes the total momentum of its quark fields and Wilson line. The relevant momentum labels are external when they do not enter loop integrals and fixed when external kinematics determine them. For \(b\to s\gamma\), massless-photon kinematics gives \(\omega=m_b\). More complicated operators can retain loop-momentum dependence, causing their anomalous dimensions to contain integrals rather than a simple product.

The renormalization-group equation for the Wilson coefficient yields both a regular anomalous dimension and a cusp anomalous dimension multiplying \(\log(\mu/\omega)\). Solving the leading-log equation produces a Sudakov exponential. With a fixed QED-like coupling, this gives double logarithms of the form \(\alpha\log^2\); with the running QCD coupling, it instead depends on ratios of coupling scales. Expanding the exponential gives a series \(\alpha_s^k\log^{k+1}\) at leading log, with higher anomalous-dimension orders supplying next-to-leading and next-to-next-to-leading logarithms. Tree-level matching and anomalous dimensions through increasing loop order are required at each accuracy.

The cusp arises when ultrasoft effects are encoded in Wilson lines: a lightlike Wilson line contains a kink, producing a single logarithm in the anomalous dimension at all perturbative orders. Wilson lines ending on quark fields in collinear interactions have an analogous structure and also account for double poles in dimensional regularization.

The lecture then generalizes these results to operators involving multiple collinear directions. When each direction has only one building block, momentum labels remain external and fixed, and the anomalous dimension factorizes into products. When multiple fields lie in the same collinear sector, a momentum combination enters loop integrals, yielding integral anomalous dimensions. Such operators reproduce familiar equations such as the Altarelli-Parisi/DGLAP evolution equation.

Finally, the lecture begins the application to deep-inelastic scattering, \(ep\to eX\). It distinguishes inclusive, endpoint, and resonance or exclusive regions, focusing on generic inclusive kinematics in the Breit frame. Hard and collinear modes are separated, and the lowest-order effective-theory operators are quark or gluon bilinears containing Wilson lines. Their proton matrix elements define quark and antiquark parton distributions. A forward-matrix-element constraint fixes the difference of the two momentum labels, while their sum remains bounded by the proton’s momentum and is identified with a parton momentum fraction. This prepares for a factorization theorem relating deep-inelastic scattering to PDFs and a perturbatively calculable hard coefficient.

The passage describes how open source communities advanced container technology and demonstrated that software development is a community endeavor. It presents design patterns as general, technology-neutral blueprints for organizing distributed systems and guiding design decisions. Patterns help developers learn from others’ mistakes, establish a shared vocabulary, and identify reusable components whose shared use improves their quality and consistency.

Single-node container patterns begin with dividing an application into tightly coupled containers, often grouped as a Kubernetes pod. This division provides resource isolation, team ownership, separation of concerns, modular reuse, easier testing, and more reliable deployments. The sidecar pattern pairs an application container with a companion container that augments it. Examples include adding HTTPS to a legacy service, synchronizing dynamic configuration, exposing process resource usage, and synchronizing source code for an automated deployment platform. Reusable sidecars require parameterization, typically through environment variables; a stable API that avoids breaking changes; and documentation through Dockerfile directives such as `EXPOSE`, `ENV`, and `LABEL`.

The ambassador pattern places a companion container between an application and the outside world to broker communication. It can route requests to storage shards, discover and connect to environment-specific services, and split traffic between production and experimental implementations. A client-side ambassador keeps the application connected to a local proxy, while a shared routing service offers simpler deployment at the cost of scaling and an additional network hop.

The adapter pattern modifies an application’s interface to conform to a predefined standard without changing the application container itself. Applications can use adapters to expose consistent monitoring interfaces, normalize heterogeneous log formats, and provide richer health checks. Prometheus exporters, Fluentd plugins, and database health-check containers illustrate how reusable adapters integrate heterogeneous or third-party software while isolating resources and reducing maintenance.

The passage then introduces microservices, which divide an application into focused components communicating through defined APIs. This architecture supports independent development, release scheduling, and scaling, but makes system design and failure debugging more difficult. Distributed patterns can standardize recurring design practices and make lessons reusable across systems.

A replicated load-balanced service uses identical stateless replicas behind a load balancer. Replication provides redundancy and horizontal scaling, and readiness probes prevent unfinished instances from receiving traffic. Session tracking can route a user consistently to one replica, using consistent hashing or application-level mechanisms. A separate replicated caching tier can improve latency and capacity, with relatively few large cache replicas rather than one cache per application instance. Reverse proxies in this layer can also provide rate limiting, while a replicated nginx tier can terminate SSL before forwarding traffic to the cache.

A sharded service instead divides requests or state among multiple shards, with a routing node selecting the appropriate shard. Sharding is generally used for stateful systems whose data exceeds one machine’s capacity and enables scaling by data volume. Sharded caching uses memory more efficiently because each key resides on one shard, but a failed shard affects the requests mapped to it. Combining sharding with replication makes each shard resilient and permits independent shard scaling and safer rollouts. The passage presents Kubernetes implementations of these patterns while noting trade-offs between per-application ambassadors and shared shard-routing services.

The study examined whether increased physical education (PE) hours and cognitively engaging activities improve attention among 75 sixth- and seventh-grade students. Class-level randomization assigned students to experimental or control conditions; Class 6 received four PE hours weekly, while Class 7 received two. Activities included agility drills, coordination circuits, and strategic team games.

Participants completed the Bells Test in October and December, assessing initial visual-search speed, sustained attention, and errors. Experimental groups improved significantly in bells detected during the first 30 seconds in both classes (p < 0.001). Sustained attention over 120 seconds improved significantly only in Class 6 (p = 0.012), while control groups showed no significant changes.

The findings suggest that more PE hours, particularly when activities are strategically designed, may improve short-term attention speed, while benefits for prolonged attention and accuracy are less consistent. The authors note limitations including class schedules, fatigue, extracurricular activities, limited generalizability, and the inability to separate effects of specific activity types. Further research is needed on long-term effects, activity content, and optimal scheduling.

The UK’s Competition and Markets Authority has designated Google Search with Strategic Market Status after a 10-month investigation, marking the first use of powers under the Digital Markets, Competition and Consumers Act to target a major technology company.

Potential measures include allowing users to choose rival search engines, introducing fair-ranking principles, increasing data portability, and requiring Google to seek permission to use publishers’ content in AI Overviews without affecting their search visibility. The CMA says Google handles more than 90% of UK general search queries and that UK firms spent over £10 billion on its search advertising in 2024.

The rules would affect Google Search’s News tab, Top Stories carousel and Discover, but not standalone Google News or Gemini. Google warned that interventions could inhibit innovation, slow product launches and raise prices, while consumer watchdog Which? said the designation could promote competition as generative AI changes search.

The disclosure describes methods, systems, and hardware for implementing deep neural networks, particularly convolutional neural networks, with configurable activation modules. Following DNN optimization, calibration data are processed by the hardware or a simulation while inputs to each activation module are monitored to determine their likely range, using extrema, histograms, or probability thresholds. Lookup data approximating each activation function over that range are generated and loaded into programmable lookup tables, allowing entries to be used efficiently and activation functions to change at runtime. Ranges may be determined separately for each function, processing point, or activation module.

Activation implementations may store gradient and offset values, adjacent output samples for linear interpolation, or additional samples for quadratic interpolation. Address bits select table entries, while remaining bits support interpolation. Dual even/odd data stores permit simultaneous retrieval of adjacent entries, and double buffering allows one function’s data to be loaded while another is used. Offsets can center input values, while out-of-range inputs may be clamped or extrapolated. A dedicated ReLU path can bypass and deactivate the lookup-table path to reduce power.

The CNN hardware includes memory and input interfaces, buffers, a command decoder, convolution engines, accumulators, and activation, normalization, pooling, and shared-buffer modules. Lookup-table implementations can reduce chip area and power compared with programmable activation-function logic, with table size balanced against accuracy. The methods may be implemented in software, firmware, fixed or programmable hardware, or integrated circuits, including systems for processing hardware definitions and manufacturing the circuits.

Rockwood School District in Missouri keeps students in grade-level classrooms for whole-class literacy instruction rather than grouping them across grades by reading ability. After daily phonics and comprehension lessons, students join flexible, needs-based small groups for reteaching or enrichment based on real-time data and observations. They also participate in independent and partner reading and can receive targeted specialist intervention. Teachers use scaffolded, multimodal lessons and movement, such as gestures for phonemes, tapping for spelling, and jumping to count syllables.

The author cites research involving nearly 12,000 students indicating that students placed in the lowest kindergarten reading groups rarely caught up with peers. Lower-track assignments can limit exposure to complex vocabulary and comprehension strategies and are difficult to change. Rockwood’s 2024–25 data showed kindergartners exceeding national proficiency averages in every skill group, sometimes by more than 17 percentage points, while first and second graders surpassed national averages in nearly every domain. The author does not claim the model solves the literacy crisis or suits every district, but argues that strong, inclusive, grade-level instruction with strategic support can help all students develop literacy, confidence, stamina, and joy.

A study of 198 honey samples from every continent except Antarctica found neonicotinoids in 75%; 45% contained multiple compounds. Detection rates were highest in North America (86%), Asia (80%), and Europe (79%).

China announced it will close its domestic ivory market by the end of 2017, a move conservationists say could sharply reduce demand and help elephant populations recover. The 1989 international ban failed to stop poaching because it excluded older ivory. China’s plan includes redirecting ivory carvers and educating the public; similar bans may encourage other countries to act.

The review synthesizes 41 publications on emerging models, technologies, and quality in higher education, particularly during the COVID-19 transition to online learning. Studies examine online teaching service quality, leadership spirituality, resistance to change, students’ e-learning experiences, quality assurance and management, gender differences, and higher education leaders’ pandemic responses. Recurring quality factors include technological infrastructure and digital literacy, instructional design, instructor competence, timely feedback and student support, institutional resources, effective leadership, stakeholder collaboration, organizational resilience, and strategic planning.

Additional topics include interoperability in e-learning, service quality and student loyalty, e-learning acceptance, alignment of student and faculty expectations, and the relationship between rankings and academic quality. The review also addresses rankings’ benefits and limitations, their use in accreditation and identifying diploma mills, the value of online learning, equity and inclusion indicators, advanced technologies, sustainable development goals, ISO 21001, universities’ societal roles, career development, virtual universities, ICT-based governance, entrepreneurship, artificial intelligence, big data, recognition of informal learning, academic freedom, faculty development, Curriculum 4.0, internationalization, co-creation, demonstration-based teaching, and institutional support for online teaching.

Methods include mixed-methods surveys and interviews, quantitative group comparisons, qualitative interviews and focus groups, literature reviews, case studies, and statistical or thematic analysis. Overall, the review favors evidence-based, equitable, inclusive, collaborative, and adaptable approaches, supported by investment in technology, faculty development, institutional support, continuous improvement, and critical engagement with quality frameworks and rankings. Open access and collaborative digital platforms are identified as expanding access and agility while creating challenges that require strategic adaptation to improve higher education and advance knowledge.

Platinum is a rare, silver-white platinum-group metal used in jewelry, automotive catalytic converters, and other industrial applications. Its high demand, scarcity, and potential price volatility make platinum futures attractive for speculation, diversification, and hedging.

Platinum futures are standardized, legally binding contracts traded on CME Globex. One contract represents 50 troy ounces, quoted in U.S. dollars per ounce, with a minimum price fluctuation of $0.10 and a $5 tick value. Contracts cover three consecutive months plus January, April, July, and October within the nearest 15 months. They are physically settled, and trading ends on the third-to-last business day of the contract month. As of December 14, 2022, platinum traded at $1,036.90, making one contract worth $51,845.

A platinum futures strategy may combine technical and fundamental analysis with defined entry and exit rules, position sizing, risk management, and backtesting. The article presents two backtests: a monthly long-and-short strategy produced 473 trades, a 64% win rate, a 0.57% average gain, and a 1.7 profit factor; a seasonal strategy with a volume requirement produced 60 trades, a 75% win rate, a 0.66% average gain, and a 2.3 profit factor. The reported results were uncorrelated with the stock market. Platinum futures have historically performed better in winter and spring than in summer and fall.

Platinum prices are influenced by supply and demand, production costs, macroeconomic and political events, and demand from the automotive, jewelry, and medical sectors. South Africa supplies about 80% of global production and holds 90% of proven reserves. TradingView records an all-time high of $2,308.80 in March 2008 and an all-time low of $267.10 in July 1985.

Traders can access futures through a broker and initial margin, or trade platinum CFDs without facing expiry or physical delivery. ETFs, options, futures, stocks, and physical coins or bars are other investment options. Major risks include leverage, potentially large losses, market volatility, and futures settlement through physical delivery. The article recommends quantified backtesting, strict trading rules, and consideration of costs, risk tolerance, goals, and experience before trading commodities.

Teach For America’s Ignite Fellowship provides high-dosage virtual tutoring designed to improve student learning, support current teachers, and encourage future educators. Its first year reached more than 40 communities, trained over 5,500 virtual tutors, and delivered nearly 200,000 hours of customized learning; middle-school math scores grew at up to 2.5 times the expected rate, while elementary readers progressed up to three times faster than average.

The passage identifies three key practices: structured training and ongoing coaching are essential; technology should expand human relationships rather than replace them; and tutoring can strengthen the teaching pipeline. Research found that Ignite tutors were nearly three times as likely to apply to Teach For America’s teaching program, with the strongest effects among men, people of color, and students who did not major in education. Since launch, 550 fellows have joined the teaching corps, including 280 in the latest year. The author argues that tutoring should be funded as a long-term instructional strategy rather than treated only as pandemic recovery.

House bill 7864 would exclude immigrants over 16 who cannot read and write English or another language, requiring them to write 20 to 25 words from the Constitution, with limited exemptions for certain relatives. It would also prohibit aliens from working on public works and make it a crime for them to enter habitually for wage labor. The President rejected the bill as harsh, oppressive, and ambiguously drafted, arguing that literacy is an unreliable measure of character or citizenship, unemployment is chiefly tied to economic depression, and the labor restrictions could harm border communities and prompt retaliation. He also found the family exemptions incomplete, burdensome, and potentially exploitative.

The study introduces the NL2GeoSQL task to evaluate large language models generating PostGIS queries from natural language. It addresses the greater complexity of GeoSQL, including spatial functions, parameter and argument constraints, geometry construction, schema linkage, SRIDs, dimensionality, and environment-dependent behavior. Existing NL2SQL and geospatial code benchmarks do not comprehensively evaluate PostGIS query generation across conceptual understanding, syntax, semantic alignment, execution, and robustness.

Two main resources are developed. GeoSQL-Bench contains 14,178 questions in three categories: 2,380 multiple-choice and true/false questions; 7,488 syntax-level SQL generation questions divided into explicit and underspecified prompts; and 4,310 table-schema retrieval questions, also divided into explicit and underspecified prompts. Sources include all 340 functions and 756 examples in the PostGIS 3.5 manual, plus 82 databases spanning eight geospatial themes derived from UN-GGIM and ISO 19115. GPT-4o assists with linguistic organization and formatting, while three experts use dual review and final adjudication to verify content, executability, and schema consistency.

GeoSQL-Eval provides an automated end-to-end framework organized around four cognitive dimensions, five capability levels, and 20 task categories. It evaluates conceptual knowledge, syntactic and executable SQL generation, semantic alignment and function invocation, result accuracy, robustness, generalization, resource consumption, and error distributions. Generated queries are parsed into abstract syntax trees, executed in PostGIS, and evaluated using exact-answer matching, execution pass rate, syntax accuracy, table and field hit rates, function-name hit rate, argument matching, geometry and value comparison, pass@n, coefficient of variation, stability-adjusted accuracy, and entropy-weighted rankings. Each task is run five times to assess consistency and hallucinations.

The study evaluates 24 models across six categories: general non-reasoning, general reasoning-enhanced, general code-generation, geospatial code-generation, general SQL-generation, and GeoSQL generation strategies. Results show that general reasoning-enhanced and non-reasoning models generally lead. GPT-5, o4-mini, and DeepSeek-R1-0528 perform strongly across complex tasks, with o4-mini ranking highest overall and for table-schema retrieval. SpatialSQL performs competitively in schema retrieval. Conceptual multiple-choice and true/false accuracy is relatively high, but function-rule compliance, argument matching, execution reliability, and schema retrieval remain major weaknesses. Syntax-level tasks produce nearly valid SQL more often than executable SQL, while table-schema retrieval is consistently harder. PostGIS function errors and SQL syntax errors dominate both task types, jointly accounting for about 70% of errors; geometry parsing and SRID or dimension mismatches are less frequent but persistent. Reasoning-enhanced models often improve with additional attempts, though all model categories decline on underspecified prompts. Non-reasoning models are generally most efficient, whereas reasoning models vary substantially in token use and generation time.

The work also publicly releases a GeoSQL-Eval leaderboard for model submission, metric review, rankings, and ongoing updates. Limitations include incomplete coverage of PostGIS raster, network-analysis, and advanced spatial functions, focus on PostGIS rather than other spatial databases or extensions, limited model coverage, and no unified cross-platform evaluation mechanism. Future work is proposed to broaden function, model, extension, modality, and platform coverage while supporting continuous community evaluation.

On October 7, 1944, the United States, Great Britain, and China informally discussed the League of Nations’ dissolution and transition to the United Nations at Dumbarton Oaks. They agreed to exchange papers but set no date. The League’s Supervisory Committee later appointed Hambro, Bruce, and Castillo Nájera to select a Conciliation Committee to confer with a group designated by the United Nations Conference. The United States made no commitment regarding an expert, and the meeting could not be planned until the conference was scheduled. The Supervisory Committee was expected to discuss liquidation and further preparations on January 19, 1945. It was recommended that the United States take no initiative unless the United Kingdom or China did so. At a January 31 meeting with diplomats from American republics, officials urged progress on the Dumbarton Proposals before the Mexico City Conference and addressed corrections to the December 29 minutes concerning “assuring respect for international treaties.”

Kyle Busch won his third straight NASCAR Cup race at Richmond, joining Kevin Harvick, but hopes his momentum is not peaking too early in the 2018 regular season. He credits short tracks and his late-model teams for an edge, while acknowledging that a fourth consecutive victory at Talladega would be difficult.

Researchers tested software patches designed to strengthen biosecurity screening of synthetic DNA orders for AI-generated harmful proteins. In computer simulations, the team generated about 76,000 blueprints for 72 harmful proteins. Although screens flagged nearly all original forms, many AI-modified versions bypassed them; patches improved detection, including of fragmented genes, but about 3% of variants still went unflagged. No physical proteins were produced, and it remains unclear whether the variants retained their function. Experts noted that malicious attempts to produce such proteins remain exceedingly rare, while emphasizing continued vigilance and risk management.

New Orleans is adapting to increasingly extreme weather after Hurricane Katrina devastated the Lower Ninth Ward and disrupted housing, rebuilding, and community life. Residents have built evacuation centers, raised homes, installed solar panels, created rain gardens, and learned to grow food in raised troughs because soil remains contaminated.

The Greater New Orleans Urban Water Plan seeks to manage heavy rainfall and land subsidence through green infrastructure, including parks, trees, ponds, and the planned Mirabeau Water Garden. Architects argue the city must replace outdated pumping practices and learn to accommodate water.

Louisiana’s 2017 Coastal Master Plan identifies $50 billion in projects, including rebuilding wetlands and barrier islands, constructing levees and flood gates, raising homes, and relocating some residents. Coastal wetlands are disappearing at a rate of about one football field per hour.

Oil and gas extraction contributes to subsidence, while rising seas pose a growing threat. Louisiana is projected to experience average sea-level increases of about 1 centimeter annually by 2050, prompting experts to study the state’s adaptation measures as potential models for elsewhere.

The cup and handle is a bullish continuation chart pattern consisting of a rounded, U-shaped cup and a smaller trading-range handle on its right. The cup forms after a rally and represents consolidation; the handle generally forms as a slight downward drift. A breakout above the handle’s resistance completes the pattern and is expected to resume the prior uptrend. Qualification criteria include an existing trend, a U-shaped cup with a 30–50% retracement, a handle, and an upside breakout. The inverted version forms in a downtrend and signals bearish continuation.

Volume generally declines as the cup forms, increases during recovery, decreases during the handle, and rises significantly on the breakout. Traders may enter with a stop-buy order slightly above the handle’s upper trendline or wait for price to exceed the cup’s swing high. Profit targets are often calculated by adding the cup’s depth to the breakout price. Stop-loss orders may be placed below the handle’s low or the cup’s bottom. Common errors include entering before full confirmation, ignoring volume, setting targets or stops poorly, neglecting broader market conditions, and relying solely on the pattern without other analysis.

The pattern reflects a psychological shift from fear and pessimism toward optimism and renewed buying. The handle represents a final test of investor conviction, often involving profit-taking or hesitation before a possible advance. High volatility can make the formation erratic, produce false signals, or cause failure, while low-to-moderate volatility generally makes it clearer and more reliable.

The pattern is most useful within an existing uptrend and should be supplemented with volume, moving averages, RSI or MACD, fundamental analysis, and market context. It may offer a framework for identifying potential long-term bullish trends but cannot guarantee future movements.

Historical backtests cited are limited and use differing rules. An S&P 500 test covering 2016–2018 reportedly underperformed the index but showed favorable trading metrics with low market exposure. Thomas Bulkowski’s broader study found a 26% failure rate, falling to 10% when trades waited for an upside breakout, and a 38% average gain. CANSLIM outperformed the broader market in backtests but has lagged recently, and does not establish the cup and handle strategy’s profitability independently.

NVIDIA Corporation filed a Form 8-K on May 10, 2018, announcing financial results for the first quarter of fiscal 2019, ended April 29, 2018. The filing attached a press release as Exhibit 99.1 and CFO Commentary from Colette M. Kress as Exhibit 99.2. The materials were furnished rather than filed and were not to be incorporated by reference in subsequent SEC filings. Kress signed the report as Executive Vice President and Chief Financial Officer.

The lecture presents the induced graph removal lemma: for every graph \(H\) and \(\varepsilon>0\), there is \(\delta>0\) such that any \(N\)-vertex graph with fewer than \(\delta N^{|H|}\) induced copies of \(H\) can be made induced-\(H\)-free by adding or deleting fewer than \(\varepsilon N^2\) edges. Unlike the ordinary removal lemma, which permits only edge deletion, the induced version may require both adding and deleting edges. It also has a multicolored formulation, where edge patterns are eliminated by recoloring few edges.

The standard triangle-removal proof relies on regularity partitions, cleaning, and counting. For the induced version, low- and high-density part pairs can be cleaned, but irregular pairs pose a major obstacle: they cannot simply be discarded without losing control of induced copies. Ordinary regularity cannot eliminate all irregular pairs, as demonstrated by the half graph.

To overcome this, the lecture introduces a strong regularity lemma. Given a sequence of positive error parameters, it produces a bounded pair of nested partitions \(P,Q\), where \(P\) is regular, \(Q\) is an extremely regular refinement, and their energies differ by little. The proof repeatedly applies Szemerédi’s regularity lemma; since energy is bounded between 0 and 1, the sequence must eventually have a sufficiently small energy increment.

A corollary yields an equitable partition \(V_1,\ldots,V_k\) and large subsets \(W_i\subseteq V_i\) such that every \(W_i,W_j\) pair, including \(i=j\), is regular, while densities between the \(V_i\)'s and corresponding \(W_i\)'s are similar for all but a small number of pairs. This enables the induced removal proof: partition the graph using the corollary, delete or add edges between relevant part pairs according to their densities, and change fewer than \(\varepsilon N^2\) edges. If an induced \(H\) remained, the counting lemma applied to the regular \(W_i\)'s would produce many induced copies in the original graph, contradicting the hypothesis.

The lecture also states an infinite removal lemma for a possibly infinite family of finite forbidden patterns, requiring \(k\)-dependent regularity. Finally, it connects these results to property testing. A randomized triangle tester samples vertex triples and distinguishes triangle-free graphs from graphs that are \(\varepsilon\)-far from triangle-free. More generally, the infinite removal lemma implies that every hereditary graph property has an oblivious, one-sided-error property tester.

A higher-order self-energy correction contains an integral that diverges logarithmically at infinite momentum, producing unphysical infinite scattering amplitudes. Introducing a cutoff restores sensible, Lorentz-invariant calculations, though divergent corrections remain. Renormalization defines physical masses and couplings as bare parameters plus corrections, allowing predictions at experimentally relevant scales. The electromagnetic, weak, and strong couplings vary logarithmically with energy, with their running affected by new particles and their behavior not converging at very high scales. Introducing new particles could potentially unify the interactions, while observed masses and couplings are understood to be scale-dependent.

Boston has been the world’s undisputed life sciences capital for over a decade, fueled by abundant lab space and billions in venture capital and federal research funding, but funding cuts and threats to higher education are challenging its competitive edge.
Roma are reportedly interested in Manchester United winger Adnan Januzaj, who is out of favour and expected to be sold, as a low-cost replacement for Mohamed Salah.

An O’Reilly copyright page for Brendan Burns’s 2018 book provides purchasing information, an errata link, trademark notices, and disclaimers concerning errors, damages, and compliance with licenses and intellectual property rights.

The passage compares dollar-cost averaging with lump sum investing. It backtests a lump sum buy-and-hold strategy using an equally weighted portfolio of five diversified, liquid ETFs and examines equity curves, drawdowns, monthly and annual returns, and performance statistics before, during, and after financial crises. Lump sum investing places money into the market at once, providing immediate exposure to gains and more time for returns. Dollar-cost averaging invests fixed amounts regularly regardless of market conditions, buying more shares at lower prices and fewer at higher prices while reducing timing pressure. Historically, lump sum investing and remaining invested over long periods—preferably at least ten years—provided a higher probability of success. Earlier investment generally produced greater average earnings, while crisis effects diminished over long horizons. Lump sum investing may offer higher long-term returns, whereas dollar-cost averaging provides greater stability; the choice depends on personal preferences and risk tolerance.

An email sent by Ann Schmidt on June 5, 2001 compiled press clippings centered on Enron and California’s energy crisis.

The New York Times reported that Southern California wholesale gas prices exceeded $11 per thousand cubic feet, compared with about $4 in New York. Pipeline shortages, dependence on gas-fired power, reduced hydroelectric imports, drought, strong demand and plant outages contributed to the crisis. Critics alleged that market rules, financial trading and storage practices by El Paso and Southern California Gas had inflated prices; both utilities denied wrongdoing, and Enron said it had hedged and resold pipeline capacity without profiting substantially from California’s price increase. Federal regulators considered requiring transaction disclosures, reinstating short-term pipeline price caps and scrutinizing bundled gas-and-capacity sales.

The Wall Street Journal described FERC’s new California electricity price plan, which uses production costs as a benchmark during tight supply and allows regulators to seek refunds. It also requires generators to offer capacity continuously and state officials to report bids and outages. Critics said the plan retained loopholes, particularly through out-of-state “megawatt laundering,” while FERC had tentatively ordered more than $100 million in refunds.

PBS’s “Frontline” and The New York Times jointly presented the documentary “Blackout,” which examined deregulation, shortages, alleged price manipulation and the role of Enron and other traders. Reviews described it as comprehensive but contentious, and it warned that California’s problems had national implications and could contribute to summer blackouts.

California’s Senate Rules Committee approved subpoenas for pricing, bidding and sales records from Reliant Energy, Dynegy, Williams Energy, Enron, NRG Energy, Duke Energy, Mirant and AES. A state inquiry was examining whether out-of-state generators illegally profited from the crisis. The committee also considered records from the Los Angeles Department of Water and Power and state Water Resources Department. PG&E and Edison said high wholesale prices had caused nearly $14 billion in losses, while California was buying power for utilities serving nearly nine million customers.

Enron-related coverage said Indian and foreign lenders were meeting in Singapore to try to preserve Enron’s $2.9 billion Dabhol power project in Maharashtra. The project was disputed over tariffs and unpaid bills; Enron denied renegotiating its contract and had issued a pre-termination notice. Separately, Marathon replaced Enron’s 20% stake in part of a $25 billion Saudi Arabian natural-gas venture as Enron focused more heavily on commodity trading. Enron also proposed using $125 million from Connecticut’s conservation fund for a fuel-cell project, drawing criticism that it diverted money from proven conservation programs.

Other clippings covered Domtar’s $1.65 billion purchase of four Georgia-Pacific paper mills, declining newsprint prices amid weak demand and excess inventories, disputes over delays in Karl Rove’s stock divestiture, new securities offerings, and rapid growth in India’s mobile-phone market.

NeoWorld is a deep-learning framework for constructing an interactive, continuously expanding virtual world from a single image, inspired by the on-demand rendering concept in *Simulacron-3*. It uses a hybrid representation: backgrounds remain lightweight object-centric 2.5D Gaussian layers, while foreground or user-selected objects are progressively reconstructed as full 3D models. This balances rendering efficiency, immersive 3D exploration, and object-level interaction.

The framework begins by decomposing an image into foreground and background layers using depth edges and panoptic segmentation. Compact codebook embeddings encode instance-level semantics efficiently, while reconstruction, segmentation, and KNN-smoothing losses improve appearance, mask accuracy, and geometric consistency. Labels are propagated across viewpoints to preserve object identity as the scene expands. New views are generated through rendering and inpainting, allowing the world to unfold along user exploration paths.

Relevant objects are reconstructed with an image-to-3D module and aligned to the existing scene through learned coarse pose estimation followed by differentiable fine alignment. Reconstructions whose fidelity falls below a threshold are returned to 2.5D. An LLM interprets natural-language instructions, identifies target objects, and determines manipulations such as translation, rotation, animation, or physics parameters.

Experiments used 28 curated images to generate 112 scenes and compared NeoWorld with world-generation, video-generation, and object-segmentation baselines. NeoWorld surpassed WonderJourney and WonderWorld in reported perceptual quality, 3D consistency, scene quality, and long-term consistency, while offering a favorable balance of rendering speed and realism. Its object-centric representation reached an IoU of 70.53, exceeding the tested segmentation baselines and ablation variants. In dynamic interactions, NeoWorld achieved higher reported prompt-alignment and VideoCLIP scores than the compared video models; prior 3D world-generation methods supported navigation but not text-guided object control. Ablations found that the codebook provided a strong efficiency–accuracy balance, while both coarse and fine alignment improved output quality.

The authors identify limitations arising from its reliance on separate pretrained modules, including propagated upstream errors, object-alignment failures, LLM misinterpretation of ambiguous prompts, image-to-3D errors under occlusion or difficult textures, and segmentation errors.

Senator Sherwin Gatchalian urged the Department of Education to address delayed performance-based bonuses for public school teachers, calling delays since 2012-2013 unacceptable. As bonuses for 2016-2017 remained unpaid, he urged streamlined clearances; DepEd blamed failed bids and clearance backlogs.

Robert Mugabe returned to Zimbabwe from Dubai after receiving medical treatment in Singapore, amid allegations that his G40 allies were responsible for the June 24 White City Stadium bombing in Bulawayo. The attack killed two and injured more than 40, including senior officials. The government claimed it was an assassination attempt on President Emmerson Mnangagwa, who said he suspected G40 based on a hunch and that he could not trust Grace Mugabe. Mugabe has called the post-intervention government illegitimate, demanded constitutionalism and was expected to support the MDC Alliance before the July 30 elections. Patrick Zhuwao warned British Prime Minister Theresa May that Mnangagwa might use the attack to target perceived enemies, while Jonathan Moyo alleged the government had cancelled rallies in Matabeleland. Police continued investigating.

The ADS9803 is an eight-channel, 20-bit, 2 MSPS data-acquisition system with a programmable PGA on every analog input. Each input supports single-ended or differential bipolar operation, independently selectable ranges, and low-pass filtering. Inputs can swing to ±18 V through internal clamp protection; above this threshold, current must remain within ±10 mA, which can be limited with a series resistor. Matching source impedance between AINxP and AINxM minimizes additional offset error. The PGA provides low-noise and wide-bandwidth modes, with bandwidth selected through ANA_BW[7:0]. A common-mode rejection circuit supports voltages up to ±12 V, with configurable settings for differential and single-ended inputs.

The ADC outputs 20-bit conversion data in straight-binary or binary-two’s-complement format, with LSB size determined by the selected input range. It accepts differential or single-ended sampling clocks; single-ended operation consumes less power. Normal operation requires a free-running sampling clock, and output data and clocks are invalid while it is stopped. SMPL_SYNC can synchronize simultaneous sampling across multiple ADS9803 devices, align channel sequencing, and align FCLKOUT. It is required after startup, clock restart, or reset.

An internal low-drift voltage reference is provided, with reference noise filtered by connecting a 10 µF ceramic capacitor to REFIO. An external reference can also use REFIO, but the internal reference must then be disabled. The source-synchronous interface supports two- or four-lane SDR and DDR modes. It outputs data, DCLKOUT, and FCLKOUT; each 20-bit result is transmitted MSB first in a 24-bit packet with six trailing zeros. The frame-clock frequency is one-fourth the sampling-clock frequency.

An optional output randomizer XORs conversion data with either the result’s LSB or a PRBS bit, reducing correlation between ground bounce and analog input voltage. Simple averaging improves SNR while halving output data rate, whereas moving averaging does not change the output rate. Fixed, digital-ramp, and alternating test patterns can replace data for channel groups 1–4 and 5–8 for interface debugging.

The device can be reset through the RESET pin or register field and powered down through the PWDN pin or PD_CH field. Initialization after power-up or reset requires a free-running sampling clock and a defined register-write sequence, followed by configuration of input ranges, bandwidth, common-mode range, and data interface. Speed-boost mode converts one selected channel pair at up to 8 MSPS while the other six channels remain idle.

Configuration registers are 16 bits, organized into three banks with 8-bit addresses. Bank 0 is always accessible, while banks 1 and 2 are selected through REG_BANK_SEL. Normal register writes use 24-bit SPI frames. Register reads require SPI_RD_EN and SPI_MODE to be enabled and require separate frames for bank selection, read enable, address transmission, and read disable.

Multiple ADS9803 devices can be daisy-chained for configuration through shared CS and SCLK signals and chained SDI/SDO connections. Daisy-chain mode must be enabled after power-up or reset, and DAISY_CHAIN_LEN specifies the number of devices excluding the first. A write to N devices requires N × 24 SCLK cycles in one SPI frame. Register maps cover SPI and daisy-chain controls, data formatting, averaging, XOR randomization, test patterns, speed boost, gain-error correction, bandwidth, reference selection, output lanes, PGA ranges, and common-mode settings.

In an ATE application, the ADS9803 supports direct channel connection or multiplexed PMU signals. Its post-calibration total unadjusted error is stated as 0.0015% at 25°C ±5°C. Wide-bandwidth operation supports multiplexing and settles to 99.95% of full scale in 7.5 µs; the documented bandwidth modes extend to 22.7 kHz for low noise and 700 kHz for wide bandwidth. The device uses AVDD_5V, VDD_1V8, and IOVDD supplies without a required power-up sequence. Recommended layout includes separate 0.1 µF bypass capacitors near each supply, reference decoupling near REFIO and REFM, short ground-plane connections, and separation of analog and reference paths from digital signals and noise sources.

Additional sections describe development tools, documentation notifications, TI E2E support, trademarks, ESD handling precautions, revision history, and mechanical, packaging, and orderable information, along with applicable disclaimers.

Apple Inc.’s Form 8-K reports that on February 2, 2015, it entered an underwriting agreement with Goldman, Sachs & Co. and Deutsche Bank Securities Inc. for five note series: $500 million of floating-rate notes due 2020; $1.25 billion of 1.55% notes due 2020; $1.25 billion of 2.15% notes due 2022; $1.5 billion of 2.50% notes due 2025; and $2 billion of 3.45% notes due 2045. Floating-rate interest is payable quarterly, while fixed-rate interest is payable semiannually. The notes will be issued under Apple’s 2013 Form S-3 registration statement and an indenture with The Bank of New York Mellon Trust Company, N.A., as trustee. They will constitute senior unsecured obligations ranking equally with Apple’s other unsecured and unsubordinated debt. The filing includes the underwriting agreement, officer’s certificate, forms of the global notes, legal opinion, earnings-to-fixed-charges calculation, and related consent.

Tuberculosis (TB), caused by Mycobacterium tuberculosis, remains a major infectious disease despite global control efforts being disrupted by COVID-19. Pulmonary TB is treated with rifampicin, isoniazid, pyrazinamide, and ethambutol, but antimicrobial resistance can develop. Extrapulmonary TB (EPTB) accounts for about 16% of reported cases, with lymph-node TB most common and pleural TB second, yet its treatment is less studied and often overlooked.

This study developed a whole-body human physiologically based pharmacokinetic (PBPK) model to simulate the time-dependent concentrations of all four first-line anti-TB drugs at extrapulmonary sites. The model extends a previous framework with a consolidated lymph-node compartment and a pleural-fluid subcompartment, using 17 perfusion-limited tissue compartments described by 18 ordinary differential equations. Physiological and tissue-partition parameters were obtained from literature and calculated using the Rodgers and Rowland method. Pharmacokinetic parameters were calibrated against plasma data and limited lung-concentration data, then independently validated with separate datasets. Simulations used standard oral doses and included both slow- and fast-acetylator isoniazid cases.

Predictions were generally consistent with available experimental data, although pleural rifampicin concentrations were overestimated. Rifampicin and isoniazid exceeded their critical concentrations in the pleura, while pyrazinamide and ethambutol did not. In lung tissue, rifampicin and isoniazid remained above critical concentrations for much of the dosing interval; ethambutol was below its threshold for a substantial period, and pyrazinamide was consistently below it. At extrapulmonary sites, rifampicin peaks exceeded its critical concentration, whereas ethambutol failed to reach it in the brain, kidney, bone, and skin. Isoniazid produced higher peaks and longer periods above threshold in slow acetylators than in rapid acetylators. Pyrazinamide did not reach its critical concentration in any simulated organ.

Limitations included limited tissue-validation data, a single lymph-node compartment, omission of rifampicin autoinduction, age effects, drug interactions and synergy, and host immune activity. Brain concentrations may also be overpredicted because meningeal inflammation and cerebrospinal-fluid penetration were not modeled. The model was presented as an initial tool for evaluating EPTB regimens and supporting further tissue-concentration studies and quantitative systems pharmacology models.

Microsoft Corporation’s unaudited Form 10-Q for the quarter ended September 30, 2017 reported revenue of $24.538 billion, up from $21.928 billion a year earlier. Product revenue declined to $14.298 billion from $14.968 billion, while service and other revenue rose to $10.240 billion from $6.960 billion. Gross margin increased to $16.260 billion, operating income to $7.708 billion, net income to $6.576 billion, and diluted earnings per share to $0.84 from $0.72. Operating cash flow was $12.440 billion; investing activities used $6.904 billion and financing activities used $6.341 billion. At September 30, cash and cash equivalents totaled $6.884 billion, short-term investments totaled $131.587 billion, total assets were $249.097 billion, total liabilities were $159.450 billion, and stockholders’ equity was $89.647 billion.

Revenue by segment was $8.238 billion for Productivity and Business Processes, $6.922 billion for Intelligent Cloud, and $9.378 billion for More Personal Computing; corresponding operating income was $3.006 billion, $2.137 billion, and $2.565 billion. Commercial cloud revenue was $5.0 billion, compared with $3.2 billion in the prior-year quarter. LinkedIn contributed $1.148 billion of revenue after its $27.0 billion acquisition in December 2016.

Microsoft adopted the new revenue recognition standard on July 1, 2017 using the full retrospective method and the lease standard using a modified retrospective method. Revenue recognition for Windows 10 and certain multi-year commercial software subscriptions changed primarily from ratable recognition to upfront recognition. The retrospective adjustments increased 2016 quarterly revenue by $1.475 billion, net income by $977 million, and diluted earnings per share by $0.12. Lease adoption materially changed the balance sheet by recognizing operating lease right-of-use assets and liabilities but did not affect the income statement. New guidance not yet adopted addresses hedging, intra-entity asset transfers, credit losses, and financial instruments.

The filing also disclosed investments and derivatives used to manage foreign-currency, equity-price, interest-rate, and credit risks. Commercial paper outstanding was $8.2 billion, while long-term debt had a carrying value of $77.3 billion and an estimated fair value of $81.3 billion. The effective tax rate was 18%. Microsoft repurchased 22 million shares for $1.6 billion during the quarter, had $35.2 billion remaining under its repurchase authorization, and declared a quarterly dividend of $0.42 per share.

Pending matters included IPCom patent litigation, 40 other patent cases, antitrust litigation in Canada, a Chinese regulatory investigation, and cell-phone-related claims. Aggregate legal liabilities were accrued at $371 million, and potentially adverse outcomes beyond recorded amounts were estimated at up to approximately $1.1 billion. Deloitte & Touche reviewed the interim statements and reported no material modifications; it also concluded that the retrospective adjustments were appropriate and properly applied.

The Federal Reserve raised its federal funds target range by 0.25 percentage points to 1–1.25%, its third hike since ending the post-crisis flatline policy. The rate had fallen from 5.25% in 2007 to 0.25% in 2008.

The study established the K-T collaborative EVT registry by harmonizing patient-level data from South Korea’s CRCS-K and Taiwan’s TREAT-AIS. It included 7,835 EVT-treated patients from Korea and 2,106 from Taiwan, yielding 9,941 cases with approximately 200 shared fields. Collected variables covered demographics, pre-stroke function, vascular risk factors, stroke characteristics, treatment and timing metrics, laboratory measures, and outcomes. Primary EVT outcomes were successful recanalization, symptomatic intracerebral hemorrhage, 90-day modified Rankin Scale scores, and 90-day mortality.

Compared with Korean patients, Taiwanese patients were older, had more vascular risk factors, lower kidney function, more severe strokes, and lower pre-stroke functional independence. They also had lower intravenous thrombolysis rates and longer arrival-to-groin puncture times. Successful recanalization and symptomatic hemorrhagic transformation rates were similar between countries, while functional independence at 90 days was lower in Taiwan (34.7% versus 41.1%) and mortality was higher in Korea (14.2% versus 6.2%).

Patients’ mean age was 70.1 years; 24.9% were at least 80 and 3.0% were at least 90. Older patients had lower favorable functional outcomes, higher mortality, and lower recanalization success, but comparable symptomatic hemorrhage rates. Age’s relationship with functional recovery and mortality was nonlinear and most pronounced between ages 75 and 85. Pre-stroke functional independence, baseline NIHSS, bridging thrombolysis, and other clinical factors influenced outcomes.

The authors concluded that advanced age was associated with poorer EVT outcomes but did not support age-based exclusion, emphasizing individualized patient selection. Limitations included differences between registry methods, varying inclusion periods, unavailable detailed imaging and post-discharge data, and the retrospective analysis.
Dr. Maria Pane, a GBMC neonatologist, cares for very sick, tiny patients, includes parents in rounds, and values team collaboration. The Father’s Day 5K supports the neonatal intensive care unit.

Amazon.com, Inc.’s unaudited Form 10-Q for the quarter ended June 30, 2022 reported Q2 net sales of $121.234 billion, up 7% from $113.080 billion a year earlier, as service sales rose to $64.659 billion while product sales declined to $56.575 billion. Operating expenses increased to $117.917 billion from $105.378 billion, reducing operating income to $3.317 billion from $7.702 billion. Other expense of $5.545 billion produced a net loss of $2.028 billion, or $0.20 per diluted share, versus net income of $7.778 billion, or $0.76 per diluted share, in Q2 2021. For the first six months, sales were $237.678 billion, operating income was $6.986 billion, and the net loss was $5.872 billion, or $0.58 per diluted share.

Segment results showed North America sales increasing 10% to $74.430 billion but an operating loss of $627 million; International sales falling 12% to $27.065 billion with a $1.771 billion operating loss; and AWS sales increasing 33% to $19.739 billion with operating income rising to $5.715 billion. Management attributed the consolidated sales and cost pressures to inflation, supply-chain constraints, labor-market issues, fulfillment inefficiencies, higher transportation and wage costs, and a return toward pre-pandemic demand patterns.
