As of June 30, 2022, Amazon held $37.478 billion of cash and cash equivalents and $23.232 billion of marketable securities, with total assets of $419.728 billion, long-term debt of $58.053 billion, and stockholders’ equity of $131.402 billion. Six-month operating cash flow was $6.175 billion, investing cash flow used $11.172 billion, and financing activities provided $6.616 billion. The company held $62.5 billion of unsecured senior notes, had $8.2 billion of commercial paper and $935 million of credit-facility borrowings outstanding, and had no borrowings under its $10 billion unsecured revolving credit facility.

Amazon completed its 20-for-1 common-stock split on May 27, 2022. It also changed estimated useful lives for servers from four to five years and networking equipment from five to six years, reducing Q2 depreciation and amortization by $928 million and benefiting the net loss by $728 million.

The company acquired MGM Holdings for approximately $6.1 billion net of cash acquired, assumed and immediately repaid $2.5 billion of debt, and recognized $3.4 billion of video content and $4.9 billion of goodwill. In July 2022, it agreed to acquire 1Life Healthcare for approximately $3.9 billion, subject to closing conditions.

The Rivian investment generated a marketable-equity valuation loss of $3.9 billion in Q2 and $11.5 billion for the first six months; its fair value declined to $4.1 billion from $15.6 billion at year-end. Amazon also reported $278.734 billion of contractual commitments and several patent disputes, including matters involving Eolas Technologies, BroadbandiTV, and Acceleration Bay. It was also paying a €1.13 billion Italian Competition Authority fine while pursuing recovery through appeals.

The lecture introduces probabilistically checkable proofs (PCPs) and presents a construction based on the GKR protocol. A PCP is a proof string that an efficient probabilistic verifier checks using randomly selected oracle queries rather than reading the entire proof. Completeness requires an accepting verifier for every yes-instance with an appropriate proof; soundness requires rejection of any proof for a no-instance. Verifiers typically choose their query locations nonadaptively, and although they read the full input, related notions called PCPs of proximity can reduce input reading.

The stated goal is to construct, for every NP language, a PCP with completeness 1, soundness 1/2, and polylogarithmic randomness and query complexity, while allowing efficient proof generation. Known PCPs can use only three proof queries and logarithmic randomness, but the lecture focuses on a polylogarithmic-query construction.

For the construction, 3SAT is reduced to a shallow, logspace-uniform verification circuit with efficiently computable addition and multiplication gates. The prover extends the witness and every circuit layer into low-degree polynomials over a carefully chosen field. The proof contains these extensions and possible sumcheck transcripts for every random branch. GKR’s “forgetting” property avoids storing the full exponentially branching transcript tree, keeping the proof polynomially sized. The verifier emulates GKR using the oracle, checks the output and sumcheck relations, and performs a low-degree test on the supplied witness extension.

Parameters are chosen so the field and transcript trees remain polynomial in the circuit size. Each of the \(2d\) sumchecks has soundness \(3mH/F\), and a union bound over them gives total soundness \(2d\cdot3mH/F\). Choosing \(F\) sufficiently large but still polylogarithmic yields soundness at most 1/2 and overall polylogarithmic randomness and queries. Reusing randomness across sumchecks is unsafe because a prover could exploit the known correlation. The lecture also previews low-degree testing and a transition to cryptography, computational soundness, and succinct arguments.

This study evaluated how pupil dilation affects portable-camera retinal image gradability and AI-based diabetic retinopathy screening. Among 327 patients, mydriatic images were more often gradable than non-mydriatic images (82.1% vs. 55.6%; P<0.001). Non-mydriatic image quality was associated with systemic hypertension, older age, longer diabetes duration, male sex, and Indigenous race. An AI model performed better with mydriatic images for accuracy, F1 score, and AUC (82.91%, 0.83, and 0.94) than with non-mydriatic images (79.23%, 0.79, and 0.93), and mydriasis reduced false positives while false-negative rates were similar. The between-group performance difference was not statistically significant (P=0.3279). Limitations included selection bias, one dataset and camera model, and restricted generalizability.

A Georgia jury convicted Robert Pearl Bryson of two counts of aggravated sodomy, four counts of aggravated child molestation, one count of child molestation, and two counts of failure to register as a sex offender. The court affirmed the convictions, finding no error.

Victims’ statements, videotaped interviews, and trial testimony showed that Bryson befriended boys aged eight and ten and engaged in oral and anal sexual contact with them. The evidence was sufficient to prove aggravated sodomy because contact, not penetration, was required. It also sufficiently supported the child-molestation conviction, given Bryson’s kiss of the ten-year-old boy and the surrounding circumstances.

For failure to register, the evidence established Bryson’s prior North Carolina sex-offender conviction, his 2003 registration in Stephens County, and his subsequent departure from Georgia for more than a year without notifying county authorities of his changed residence address. His exact new residence was not required to prove the offense.

The court rejected Bryson’s remaining arguments because his challenges to the indictment were untimely or waived, the grand jury was not illegally constituted, withdrawal of counsel shortly before trial would delay proceedings and was not required, the connected offenses did not require severance, and the no-contest plea was admissible to establish a conviction for registration purposes. Bryson also waived his ineffective-assistance claim by failing to pursue it at his first opportunity despite the trial court’s warning.

Image registration aligns a moving image with a fixed image by optimizing a coordinate transform using an image dissimilarity term and regularization. While affine, deformable, and composite transforms are widely used, modern imaging resolutions create substantial compute and memory demands; deep-learning pipelines are especially limited by activation memory.

The paper proposes Flash Fused Distributed Primitives (FFDP), combining single-GPU fused kernels with distributed execution. A composite implicit grid sampler avoids materializing transformed grids, implicit Parzen windowing computes mutual-information histograms without large intermediate tensors, and fused LNCC reduces memory-intensive intermediate calculations. For multi-GPU registration, Grid Parallel provides boundary synchronization for images, warps, and optimizer states, while a distributed ring sampler interpolates sharded moving images without an allgather. Distributed MSE, LNCC, and MI losses aggregate results correctly across GPUs.

The kernels reduce additional high-bandwidth-memory overhead from O(N) to O(1) for grid sampling and mutual information and substantially reduce LNCC overhead. FFDP accelerates traditional registration by up to 7.48× with up to 59% less memory and deep-learning pipelines by up to 6.14× with up to 24% less memory. It supports problems up to 64× larger on one GPU and scales across multiple GPUs with memory use largely independent of GPU count.

A 250-micrometer in-vivo MRI was registered to a 100-micrometer ex-vivo human brain volume containing more than 11 billion transform parameters in about one minute using eight A6000 GPUs. On a simulated 250-micrometer brain dataset, the method achieved Dice, inverse Dice, and AvgHD90 scores of 0.895, 0.597, and 0.216, respectively, improving accuracy while requiring up to 500× fewer GPU-hours than alternatives.

This paper by Sergey A. Yablonsky (Technology Innovation Management Review, 2019) develops a multidimensional, data-driven AI innovation framework linking Artificial Intelligence (AI), Big Data (BD), and Advanced Analytics (AA). It argues that although enterprises are rapidly adopting digital technologies and AI is only now becoming commercially viable, most research on AI innovation examines technical, architectural, or information-system perspectives rather than managerial ones. The study aims to clarify why and how BD and AA engage AI and to build a strategic conceptual framework and taxonomy of AI/BD/AA maturity and value chains.

Methodologically, the conceptual study follows Nickerson et al.'s (2012) iterative conceptual-to-empirical and empirical-to-conceptual taxonomy development approach, drawing on Moyer (2016) for the four-part digital-transformation framing (concepts, capabilities, assets, research). Data came from a literature review of information resources from 2010 to 2019 and semi-structured expert interviews with members of technology groups, founders, and CTOs of the Russian National Technology Initiative (one interview per market, averaging 50 minutes), all recorded, transcribed, and analyzed thematically. The resulting taxonomy contains over 100 features, seven dimensions, and twenty characteristics.

The paper reviews definitions of AI, BD, and analytics (descriptive, diagnostic, predictive, prescriptive, and augmented), outlines seven overlapping technology platform areas (Information Systems, Customer Experience, Data and Analytics, IoT, Ecosystems, Trust/blockchain, and Integration), and specifies an AI/BD/AA micro-level value chain comprising AI awareness/BD acquisition, measurement of BD curation, AI reporting and interpretation/BD storage, and AI decision-making/BD usage.

Adopted in part from Vesset et al. (2018), the resulting framework combines these value chains with five AI maturity levels: Human-Led/Initial Analytics; Human-Led, Machine-Supported/Advanced Analytics I; Machine-Led, Human-Supported/Advanced Analytics II; Machine-Led, Human-Governed/Advanced Analytics III; and Machine-Controlled/Advanced Analytics IV, each mapped to corresponding value-chain levels. The framework is presented as a practical tool for identifying industry and functional use cases where AI can automate tasks, activities, and processes, communicating AI capability value, and guiding transformation under human-driven ethical norms alongside legal and societal considerations.

The March 2006 AMD Geode CS5535 Companion Device Silicon Revision A3 specification update documents these behavior changes and workarounds:

- An IRQ coinciding with an SSMI event may allow the trapped I/O to finish before the SSMI is signaled, making CS5535-generated SSMIs unreliable; the stated resolution is to use the Geode GX processor.
- UDMA fails when the IDE bus master is enabled before a PIO command packet; send PIO first, then enable bus mastering.
- From ACPI S3, wake transitions on GPIO[27:24] (SLP_BUT#, THRM_ALRM#, and LOW_BAT#) are not recognized. Use PWRBTN#, or external OR circuitry powered by VIO_STB and VMEM while retaining individual connections for source identification.
- An immediate extended-port write followed by a legacy-port read can return incorrect RTC CMOS RAM data; an intervening address-port write prevents this. No resolution is given.
- Block- and demand-mode legacy DMA can block LPC I/O and return invalid data; use single-transfer mode, optionally converting modes in SMM.
- USB clock gating causes some controller register reads to fail while idle; disable clock gating.
- An IDE interrupt after bus mastering starts resets the CS5535 bus-master engine and stops the transfer. Only one CD-ROM firmware exhibited the problem, which its manufacturer later revised.
- A Port 60h read incorrectly clears the KEL AuxOutputFull bit, potentially corrupting USB PS/2 mouse and keyboard emulation; use interrupts.
- tACK does not change UDMA setup-to-IDE_DACK timing, which is fixed at 30 ns; no action is required.
- WORD-aligned ATAC PRDs can hang; make all ATAC drivers use DWORD alignment.
- LPC may abort transactions after only two clocks without a valid SYNC pattern following turnaround, discarding writes or returning all ones for reads; use a suitably programmed PLD connected to the LPC bus.
- The SMB NEGACK bit may be set late or cleared unexpectedly by a register read. Clear it by writing 1 to SMB_STS[4], then writing 0x00 to SMB_STS.
- The GLPCI retry counter counts other PCI-bus retries, so a master may stop retrying early.
- After suspend, atomic writes to GPIO High Bank Feature Bit Registers clear unselected bits; use a full-register read-modify-write transaction.
- CS5535 SMBus data hold time is below the SMB Specification 2.0 minimum of 300 ns.
- LOWBAT_FLAG may fail to set after a low-battery event in Normal or Restart Standby, preventing later detection.
- If its delay exceeds PM_SED, Sleep exit can leave SLEEP_X and SLEEP_Y asserted and PCI/IDE inputs disabled; program the relevant delay counters below PM_SED.

The Mississippi Supreme Court affirmed Ulysses S. Gandy’s second conviction of manslaughter and ten-year sentence. Gandy was convicted after a jury found that he drove while intoxicated into the wrong lane on a straight, unobstructed stretch of Mississippi State Highway 25, causing a collision that killed Daniel Palmer and two passengers. Conflicting testimony addressed the vehicles’ positions after impact and Gandy’s intoxication, including evidence from witnesses, medical personnel, and his own statements that he had consumed alcohol.

The court held that competent evidence supported the verdict and that conflicting evidence was for the jury to resolve. Although intoxicated driving is not itself manslaughter, the evidence supported the jury’s finding that Gandy’s intoxication causally contributed to his culpable negligence.

The court also rejected Gandy’s other claims. It found no reversible error in refusing his requested intoxication instruction because other instructions adequately presented the issue. State Exhibits 1, 5, and 7 were properly admitted because they illustrated post-collision observations by their sponsoring witnesses rather than speculatively reconstructing the vehicles’ positions at impact. Finally, the court found no reversible error in denying the jury a food or refreshment recess, noting that jurors could have requested one and Gandy cited no supporting authority.

The study developed an age-structured, regional SIR metapopulation model linking SARS-CoV-2 transmission to four Google Community Mobility Report (GCMR) settings: grocery and pharmacy, retail and recreation, transit stations, and workplaces. Mobility effects were modeled additively, while temperature as a seasonality proxy and Alpha and Delta variant prevalence were modeled as multiplicative effects on infection risk. Region- and week-specific random effects captured transmission outside the selected settings. The model was fitted in a Bayesian framework to weekly hospitalization data.

For Norway and Sweden, the model covered all 11 and 21 regions, respectively, from February 2020 through July 2021, accounting for age-prioritized vaccination and emerging variants. It was also applied to Bavaria and Berlin from February through December 2020. Model fits reproduced regional hospitalization trends well. The four GCMR settings accounted for an estimated 60.0% of infections in Sweden, 38.7% in Norway, and 65.2% across Bavaria and Berlin, with substantial variation among regions.

At pre-pandemic activity levels, transit and workplaces contributed most to infections in Norway and Sweden, followed by retail and recreation and grocery and pharmacy. In the German regions, retail and recreation had the greatest contribution, especially in Berlin. A 20°C increase in temperature reduced estimated transmissibility by about 40% in Norway and Sweden and by approximately half in Germany. Delta was estimated to roughly double transmissibility, though with substantial uncertainty; evidence of increased Alpha transmissibility appeared in Norway but not clearly in Sweden.

The authors found a clear association between GCMR data and infection dynamics, while noting limitations including linear and time-constant mobility-contact assumptions, simplified vaccination and variant effects, reliance on literature-based assumptions, and possible measurement error in GCMR data. The paper was posted as a non-peer-reviewed medRxiv preprint.

The speaker accepts the Democratic nomination for president, thanks Texas and Dallas, and frames the election as a choice between two visions of government: hope, confidence, growth, and individual opportunity versus pessimism, fear, and expanded government. He credits his administration with reducing the growth of federal spending, inflation, and taxes; creating millions of jobs; strengthening the military; repairing alliances; and restoring public confidence, while blaming opponents for inflation, high interest rates, tax increases, deficits, poverty, crime, weak defense, and concessions to the Soviet Union.

He advocates a balanced-budget amendment, presidential line-item veto power, voluntary school prayer, stronger anticrime legislation, tuition tax credits, enterprise zones, and simpler, lower taxes. He also supports continued aid to Israel and free Latin American allies, stronger U.S. defenses, and nuclear arms reductions through negotiations with the Soviet Union. Defending the Grenada rescue mission, he contrasts it with the Soviet invasion of Afghanistan and emphasizes that the operation was invited and saved American students.

Rejecting a simple left-versus-right choice, he advocates limited but necessary government, individual dignity and liberty, equality, family, religious tolerance, and opposition to totalitarianism. He describes his departure from the Democratic Party as reflecting its leaders’ abandonment of original principles and welcomes other Democrats who share his views. Concluding with the 1984 Olympic torch relay and the Statue of Liberty, he presents America as unified, hopeful, and prepared for continued prosperity, peace, and renewed opportunity.
EUR/USD rose for a fourth straight session toward 1.1840 on dollar weakness, as ECB and FOMC minutes approached, with QE tapering and balance-sheet reduction in focus.

ESD can damage integrated circuits, causing performance degradation or complete failure; proper handling precautions are required, especially for precision devices. Revision A updates the ADS8685W and ADS8689W document status from Advance Information to Production Data. Mechanical, packaging, and orderable information is provided but may change without notice. Notes define product status, preproduction material limitations, RoHS classifications, lead or ball finishes, moisture sensitivity and peak reflow ratings, and part markings. Carrier-tape dimensions and a representative pin 1 orientation diagram are included, though actual packages may vary. TI disclaims warranties for information and resources, states that liability for page information cannot exceed the annual purchase price of affected parts, and places responsibility for product selection, design, validation, testing, and compliance on developers. Resource use is limited to developing applications with the described TI products; reproduction and display are prohibited. TI products remain subject to applicable sales terms, and TI rejects additional or differing terms.

A July 9–10, 2001 collection of news reports focused on Enron, California’s electricity crisis, and India’s Dabhol power project.

California records showed that high power prices involved numerous public and private suppliers, not only the Texas companies criticized by Gov. Gray Davis. During the first quarter, some public entities charged more than major private generators; Enron averaged $181 per megawatt-hour, while Mirant averaged $225. California spent nearly $8 billion buying power in the first five months, although average prices declined from $316 per megawatt-hour in January to $243 in May. Purchases later fell below projections as prices decreased.

A California Senate committee investigating alleged price gouging disputed Duke Energy’s refusal to authorize public release of confidential bidding data from its Chula Vista plant. Former employees alleged the plant’s output was manipulated during a January emergency, while Duke said it followed grid operator instructions. Six generators, including Duke, said they would comply with document requests; Enron and Mirant had been cited for contempt.

FERC-mediated refund negotiations between California and major generators ended without agreement. The presiding judge planned to recommend refunds of “hundreds of millions, and maybe $1 billion,” compared with California’s $8.9 billion demand; generators had offered $716.1 million. California officials maintained that multiple billions were owed and raised the possibility of further litigation. Separately, a judge allowed California’s attorney general to share subpoenaed documents from Reliant, Mirant and Dynegy with Oregon and Washington for investigations into possible manipulation of Western electricity markets.

In India, Dabhol Power president and CEO Neil McGregor left after his contract expired, and Enron India managing director K. Wade Cline assumed additional operational responsibility. Dabhol’s dispute with the Maharashtra State Electricity Board over unpaid bills and high tariffs continued, halting second-phase construction and additional financing. Kenneth Lay said Enron had no immediate plan to leave India but that further discussions with Indian officials and lenders were required. Options discussed included a central-government buyout, third-party sales, lower tariffs, reduced returns and sale of Enron’s stake. Indian lenders were considering replacing the project’s engineering consultant, and Maharashtra’s government was considering a judicial inquiry.

Enron Broadband and Anschutz Investment were identified as key investors in Tropic Networks’ $60 million financing. Separately, analysts rated Enron a “buy” despite its California scrutiny, Dabhol problems and other setbacks, citing expectations for continued growth in its core electricity and natural-gas businesses. Power producers were generally expected to meet second-quarter earnings targets as stronger April and May prices and increased output offset lower June prices.

Grief is a highly personal emotional response to losing someone or something important and may also follow major life changes. Its effects, duration, and coping mechanisms vary according to personal circumstances, with no right or wrong way to grieve and no fixed sequence of stages.

Anticipatory grief may occur before an impending loss, such as a terminal illness, allowing time to prepare and say goodbye. Grief can also accompany leaving a long-term home because of health, finances, downsizing, or sheltered care. If possible, major decisions about moving should be deferred for several months after bereavement, and relocation may increase loneliness or disrupt support networks.

After a death, people may experience numbness, denial, acceptance or relief, intense yearning, repeated recollection of events, restlessness, disturbed sleep, loss of confidence, guilt, anger, and profound sadness or depression. These reactions can vary and recur. Support from friends and family is important, while depression or a need for additional help should be discussed with a GP or specialist organisation.

There is no simple answer to how long grief lasts. Time alone does not heal, but most people eventually experience more good than bad days and may begin looking forward. The intense period of grief may last longer than expected but does not continue forever in the same intensity.

The ADS9803 is an eight-channel, 20-bit, 2 MSPS data-acquisition system with a built-in analog front end. It supports simple averaging, which halves the output data rate, and moving averaging, which preserves the output rate. Debug test patterns for channel groups CH[4:1] and CH[8:5] include fixed, digital-ramp, and alternating patterns.

The device can be reset via the RESET pin or register field and powered down via the PWDN pin or a register field; initialization requires a free-running sampling clock and a sequence of register writes. User-configurable settings include analog ranges, bandwidth, common-mode voltage, output-lane count, and internal reference selection. Speed-boost mode converts only a selected analog input pair at up to 8 MSPS while leaving the other six channels idle.

Configuration registers are organized into three banks, with bank 0 always accessible. SPI register writes require bank selection before accessing banks 1 or 2; register reads require enabling read mode and use two 24-bit frames for a single device. Multiple ADCs can be daisy-chained using shared CS and SCLK connections and chained SDI/SDO signals, with register writes requiring 24 SCLKs per device.

Application information covers ATE and pin-electronics use, post-calibration accuracy of 0.0015% at 25°C ±5°C, low-noise and wide-bandwidth modes, multiplexed-signal settling, three power supplies, reference and bypass-capacitor placement, and analog/digital layout guidance. The document also lists development tools, support resources, ESD precautions, revision information, ordering details, and legal disclaimers.

The Patriots struggled offensively against Miami but stayed close until the final minute. Stephen Gostkowski’s bizarre onside-kick attempt was recovered by the Dolphins, who won despite New England’s late chance to force overtime.

Researchers led by Joshua Caldwell developed higher-quality hexagonal boron nitride (hBN) hyperlenses by using isotopically purified boron. Natural boron’s mixed isotopes degrade the crystal’s optical properties, while 99 percent purified hBN reduces optical losses, triples polariton lifetime and travel distance, and improves imaging resolution by roughly tenfold. The crystals could, in principle, capture images of objects as small as 30 nanometers, potentially allowing observation of viruses and cellular processes in living cells. Unlike electron and atomic-force microscopes, hyperlenses may image samples in natural, solution-based environments without high vacuum, harmful radiation, or lethal preparation. Infrared hyperlensing could also provide spectroscopic “fingerprints” and may benefit biological and medical research, communications, and nanoscale optical components. Researchers suggested further gains from larger purified crystals and theoretical improvements of another tenfold.

Attackers can beat an offside trap by recognizing when defenders move up instead of retreating, timing runs so the ball is played while they remain onside, and avoiding interference if forced offside. Tactics include faking a pass or self-passing to draw defenders into the trap, dribbling into open space, making properly timed through passes, using horizontal, lateral, checking, deep-lying, bending, delayed, and short runs or passes, and employing a designated “non-runner,” particularly on free kicks. Attackers should also exploit any failure by defenders to execute the trap, potentially gaining a one-on-one opportunity with the goalkeeper. Effective scouting, coaching, patience, and practiced execution are essential during both open play and set pieces.

Periwinkle sea snails exposed to ocean conditions predicted for 2100 adapted despite declining metabolism, accelerating shell production and forming less-dense, less-soluble shells. Researchers suggest this may help other calcifying organisms adapt to acidifying oceans.
Following People v. Soldán, the court reversed the judgment and acquitted the defendant because the cases were identical except for the loan amount.

China’s Ministry of Commerce added Canadian research firm TechInsights and nine subsidiaries to its “unreliable entity list,” effectively barring them from business with Chinese organizations. The blacklist followed TechInsights’ analysis of Huawei’s advanced AI chips, which found components sourced from international foundries and raised questions about Western export controls. Chinese authorities said the firm exposed sensitive information and violated national interests. The restrictions prohibit cooperation, data provision, and access to Chinese clients, with analysts viewing the move as tighter technology controls amid semiconductor tensions.

Barron’s writer Jack Hough argues that Netflix stock could lose more than half its value, citing Disney and Facebook’s video plans, Amazon Prime, Netflix’s cash burn, unconventional accounting, and canceled-show write-offs. The passage counters that competition fears are overstated, noting Netflix’s subscriber base has more than quadrupled since Prime Video launched. It also highlights Netflix’s pricing power, with two U.S. increases since early 2014 and further increases in Australia and Canada. Finally, it emphasizes Netflix’s competitive moat: 104 million streaming accounts, millions of quarterly additions, a broad customer base that spreads costs, and market dominance that attracts content creators. Despite acknowledging that Netflix stock is expensive and will eventually correct, the passage characterizes the bearish case as flawed and betting against Netflix as risky. The Motley Fool disclosed holdings in Netflix, Disney, Amazon, and Facebook.

A study of two national injury databases found that nearly 17,000 children under six were treated in emergency rooms for window-blind injuries from 1990 to 2015. Most injuries were minor, but cord entanglement accounted for 11.9% of cases, nearly 80% of 726 hospitalizations, and more than 94% of 271 deaths. Entanglements mostly occurred at home while children were unsupervised and involved window-blind cords.

Researchers recommended mandatory cordless or inaccessible-cord coverings because voluntary standards, supervision, cord tying, and safety kits had not adequately prevented injuries. In 2014, the Consumer Product Safety Commission began considering a mandatory cord-accessibility rule. A 2017 proposal would require stock window coverings—over 80% of the U.S. market—to be cordless or have inaccessible cords, while allowing corded custom products.

The commission recommends cordless or inaccessible-cord coverings for homes with children and advises consumers to look for the “Best for Kids” certification label.

Ryan Kerr, 26, of Evercreech, admitted three assaults on December 7, December 27 and May 28 — including punching a woman's face and attacking a man in a pub toilet, where witnesses said he punched and stamped on him. With prior battery and assault convictions and no remorse shown, Judge David Ticehurst remanded Kerr in custody pending sentencing on October 13.

Peterborough City Council has brought 179 of 574 long-empty private homes back into use in the past year and 663 over five years, generating more than £3 million through the government’s New Homes Bonus. Its Phase Two budget proposals are open for consultation amid an 80% fall in grants, from £55 million to £10 million over eight years. The council is campaigning for fairer funding to protect vital services. Two Public Space Protection Orders introduced six months ago are associated with fewer littering fines and reduced unauthorised cycling. The new CHUMS service will support children and young people with anxiety, depression, self-harm and other mild-to-moderate mental health needs.

Chef and cookbook author Shannon Bard announced that her Portland restaurant, Zapoteca, has closed permanently. The Bards cited their desire to spend more time with their five children. They retain Toroso in Kennebunk, Salud in Portland, and Salud’s cooking school and catering company. Bard’s 2015 cookbook celebrated Zapoteca’s Mexican cuisine; she also appeared on Food Network shows and cooked at the James Beard House in 2014.

The study followed the Declaration of Helsinki and ICH Good Clinical Practice guidelines. ethics committees approved protocol amendments and informed consent documentation before study initiation, and investigators were required to report serious or unexpected adverse events. Participants received study explanations, time to ask questions, and signed informed consent before enrollment. The study hypothesized that administering high-volume convalescent plasma with high neutralizing-antibody titers early during hospitalization would reduce the need for mechanical ventilation. Its primary objective was to evaluate the efficacy and safety of best supportive care plus convalescent plasma versus best supportive care alone. The secondary objective was to compare convalescent plasma with standard care regarding clinical severity, oxygenation, ventilation, and hospitalization.

The NAAIM Exposure Index, compiled by the National Association of Active Investment Managers, measures members’ average exposure to U.S. equity markets. Members report their firms’ exposure weekly as of Wednesday, and responses are averaged and plotted as a two-week moving average. High readings indicate bullish sentiment and low readings bearish sentiment, potentially signaling market tops or bottoms. However, the index is not predictive, and backtests found tested contrarian strategies performed poorly; other indicators, such as the VIX, were more effective.

Lubrizol will invest US$80 million to expand TPU capacity across North America, Europe and Asia. North American upgrades include production, storage and logistics improvements; capacity is expected in 2018, with further Asian and European expansions planned for 2019.

Unbeaten Jeff Horn defends his WBO welterweight title against Gary Corcoran in Brisbane on Wednesday, hoping to dispel doubts about his controversial unanimous decision over Manny Pacquiao last July. A victory could lead to a mandatory bout with Terence Crawford, while promoter Bob Arum also floated a possible Pacquiao return and major 2018 fights; defeat could send Horn back into obscurity. Corcoran, 17-1 and ranked 10th by the WBO, is the underdog seeking his first world title in his first fight outside Britain and Ireland. Accusations of head-butting and biting have added intrigue, with both camps mocking the claims, but both fighters expect an aggressive contest.

The Pharmalittle newsletter highlights Trump’s drug-pricing plans, including Pfizer’s agreement to lower prices for Medicaid and direct patients, price new medicines at parity with other countries, and avoid certain drug tariffs if it continues U.S. manufacturing. Trump said similar deals with other pharmaceutical companies were forthcoming. Experts remain skeptical about affordability gains, noting Medicaid enrollees already pay little or nothing, existing pricing and rebate rules may limit effects, and Medicaid budget impacts are unclear. The newsletter also notes a European Commission investigation into Sanofi.

Manchester City host Burnley at the Etihad on Jan. 2, with City seeking another win in their 2017 title push and Burnley seeking points to avoid relegation. Pep Guardiola’s side must win midfield, defend set pieces and score early, while Sergio Agüero returns. Burnley, who have struggled away, rely on Andre Gray and Sam Vokes.

This non-peer-reviewed preprint examined whether Tourette syndrome (TS) is associated with increased sensorimotor neural noise. Nineteen adults with TS and 19 age- and sex-matched healthy controls underwent EEG recording while receiving 75 single-pulse median nerve electrical stimulations. Neural noise was operationalized as trial-by-trial variability in the magnitude or timing of evoked responses.

Compared with controls, the TS group showed greater trial-by-trial variability in somatosensory evoked potential (SEP) amplitude throughout the analyzed epoch, but not greater variability in component timing. Stimulation reduced variability in both groups at comparable rates, suggesting that abnormal variability at rest may normalize with stimulation. Most SEP amplitudes, timings, and spatial topographies did not differ between groups. The P2/P100 component was larger in the TS group, and its magnitude correlated with greater tic impairment. The TS group also had elevated power spectral density and flatter 1/f slopes at high-beta and gamma frequencies, consistent with increased neural noise.

Inter-trial phase coherence increased after stimulation in both groups across alpha, beta, and low-gamma frequencies. Its early rise was generally slower in the TS group, while alpha coherence remained elevated for less time; beta coherence was briefly greater in the TS group around the P100 response. Greater premonitory urges were associated with smaller gamma-coherence increases and larger reductions in coefficient of variation, while motor-tic severity was associated with greater alpha-coherence increases. EEG variability and high-frequency spectral power were negatively associated with IQ scores. Overall, the authors concluded that sensorimotor neural populations may be less stable at rest in TS but show comparable stabilization following stimulation.

Facebook released an expanded, roughly 8,000-word rule book detailing permitted content on topics including drugs, sex work, bullying, hate speech and violence, aiming to clarify its moderation practices and criticism over content removals. The standards permit some graphic imagery with warnings, restrict certain speech and hacked material, and introduce appeals for removed individual posts and explanations for more takedown decisions. Facebook uses automated software and 7,500 moderators, reviews standards every two weeks with outside feedback, and plans public forums. Government requests require formal legal review and may trigger country-specific blocks; false information and personal-data use are not covered by the standards.

Apple Inc. reported that on June 20, 2017, it completed the issuance and sale of $1 billion aggregate principal amount of 3.000% senior unsecured notes due June 20, 2027. Interest is payable semiannually in arrears on June 20 and December 20, beginning December 20, 2017. The notes rank equally with Apple’s other unsecured and unsubordinated debt. The issuance was conducted under a June 13, 2017 underwriting agreement with Goldman Sachs & Co. LLC, J.P. Morgan Securities LLC, and Merrill Lynch, Pierce, Fenner & Smith Incorporated, and pursuant to an indenture with The Bank of New York Mellon Trust Company, N.A., as trustee. Apple furnished the underwriting agreement, officer’s certificate, form of global note, and legal opinion and related consent as exhibits.

A federal jury cleared retired Little Rock police lieutenant David Hudson of excessive-force charges arising from his 2011 arrest of Jon “Chris” Erwin. Video showed Hudson punching Erwin seven times outside Ferneau and taking him to the ground, sparking national debate about police use of force. After two days of testimony, the jury unanimously found that Hudson’s actions were reasonable from his perspective.

Hudson testified that he was asked to remove an unruly private-party group and that Erwin repeatedly questioned him, resisted arrest, and placed his hands on the officer. He said he punched Erwin to gain compliance before taking him down when Erwin continued resisting. Testimony indicated that partygoers appeared intoxicated, while witnesses disagreed about whether Erwin was under attack. Hudson’s attorneys argued that Erwin’s conduct was omitted from the five-second video, while Erwin’s attorney said the incident reflected excessive force.

Erwin, who reported facial injuries, said he never resisted and that his misdemeanor arrest charges were dismissed, though the judge barred testimony about the dismissal. The city and restaurant owner settled Erwin’s claims, potentially leaving Hudson responsible for any damages. After the verdict, Hudson said he felt vindicated, while Erwin maintained that he had been wronged and said his goal was to expose what he called bad police officers.

U.S. statements on the war drew little attention in Finland, where resentment grew toward German troops and German influence over the press. Finland depended on Germany for military supplies and increasingly food, while Nazi censorship and Social Democratic unease reflected mounting war weariness. A January 3 trade-union memorial warned that continued war would worsen conditions, especially for workers and food distribution; growing divisions between socialists and conservatives concerned Berlin because of the possibility of a socialist peace movement. Despite calls to resist, ordinary Finns and soldiers increasingly questioned the conquest of Soviet Karelia, as prolonged resistance strained the population and economy.

Soviet official Vyshinski told U.S. chargé Thurston he knew nothing of reported Soviet-Finnish talks. Separately, Finnish official Toivola accepted U.S. concerns that press attacks and legation telephone censorship harmed relations with the United States and could endanger Finland’s support in Britain and the United States. Toivola promised to urge restraint but said Finnish commentary could not directly criticize Germany because of Finland’s dependence on German food supplies; he also accepted that German diplomats might have inspired attacks on the U.S.

Texas Monthly’s November 2001 article traces Enron’s transformation from a debt-burdened pipeline company into an energy-trading powerhouse under Ken Lay and Jeff Skilling. After joining Enron as a consultant in 1985, Skilling proposed the “Gas Bank,” which allowed Enron to buy, sell and assume risk in natural gas. By creating and dominating new markets, Enron expanded into electricity, online commodity trading, bandwidth, weather derivatives and water services. Its stock rose sharply as revenue and market share grew, and Skilling became CEO in February 2001.

Enron’s success depended on an aggressive, elite culture that rewarded risk, speed and individual performance. It recruited highly educated, ambitious employees, offered perks and potentially unlimited bonuses, and promoted a knowledge-based business model. The company increasingly treated workers as replaceable commodities through forced rankings and constant turnover, while internal competition, excessive workloads, surveillance and paranoia weakened morale.

Enron also relied on mark-to-market accounting at an unprecedented scale, recognizing projected deal profits up front and retaining control over markets it created, dominated and sometimes quickly abandoned. Under pressure to maximize near-term returns, it shifted away from long-term assets and toward trading intangible products. Rebecca Mark was sidelined through the creation of Azurix, but its water business failed, and costly projects such as the Dabhol power plant in India weighed on performance.

By 2001, Enron faced public criticism during California’s electricity crisis, questions about its accounting and financial reporting, the collapse of its telecommunications investments and broader economic weakness. Its stock fell from $80 in January to around $35. Skilling resigned after six months as CEO, and Lay returned to lead the company, promising to narrow its focus, reduce reliance on broad trading and reconsider the Performance Review Committee. The article attributes Enron’s decline not only to external crises and the economic downturn but also to the aggressive culture, internal practices and pursuit of rapid profits that had defined its rise.

Amazon.com, Inc.’s unaudited Form 10-Q for the quarter ended March 31, 2018 reported net sales of $51.042 billion, up 43% from $35.714 billion, operating income of $1.927 billion, and net income of $1.629 billion. Diluted earnings per share were $3.27. Results included Whole Foods Market from its August 2017 acquisition.

North America generated $30.725 billion in sales and $1.149 billion in operating income; International generated $14.875 billion in sales and a $622 million operating loss; AWS generated $5.442 billion in sales and $1.400 billion in operating income. Sales growth reflected higher unit sales, third-party seller activity, advertising sales, increased AWS usage, and Whole Foods in North America.

Cash, cash equivalents, and marketable securities had a fair value of $25.0 billion at March 31, 2018, while trailing-12-month operating cash flow was $18.194 billion. Q1 operating cash flow was negative $1.791 billion. Amazon had $24.3 billion of unsecured senior notes outstanding, and total contractual commitments were $119.214 billion.

Amazon adopted new revenue-recognition guidance on January 1, 2018, increasing retained earnings by approximately $650 million and changing the presentation of Prime membership and advertising revenue. Restricted-cash guidance was applied retrospectively, and new lease guidance was planned for adoption in Q1 2019.

Disclosed contingencies included $2.6 billion of tax contingencies, an IRS transfer-pricing claim seeking approximately $1.5 billion of additional federal tax, and an approximately €250 million Luxembourg tax recovery under appeal. Amazon also disclosed patent litigation and sanctions-related reviews. On April 12, 2018, after quarter-end, Amazon acquired Ring Inc. for approximately $900 million, net of acquired cash.

The coach said Colorado and Detroit have played similarly, though the series has shifted toward tighter play. Frequent penalties have made it difficult to assess the series’ flow, momentum, or tactical style. After two games, the team has narrowed its approach to one or two methods, emphasizing quicker puck movement through the neutral zone, faster defensive positioning, and shooting when favorable opportunities arise. Colorado has done well taking away the back end, while Detroit’s power play has generated little and is unlikely to change dramatically because of one adjustment.

Colorado’s penalty kill benefits from skilled, intelligent players who read plays and move the puck quickly. The coach compared this approach to Ron Francis’s penalty-killing ability and noted that his line has scored well, particularly on the road.

An earlier attempt to use Sandis as an offensive driver from the defense was viewed as unrealistic and produced inconsistencies. The addition of Hedican and Adams allowed the defense to be reorganized around players’ strengths, giving each pairing speed and physical presence and improving the team’s overall defensive structure.

The coach said officials have been consistent but have made many calls, complicating evaluation of the games. He believes legitimate power plays can improve the flow of hockey but dislikes post-whistle pushing and shoving when little is at stake. Communication during games is also difficult because arenas are loud.

Coaching Arturs involves learning his personality and consistent emotional state. The coach generally avoids criticizing or advising goalies, explains decisions when removing them, and notes that Barrasso’s situation was different because he knew he would play every night.

For the remainder of the series, the team plans to use two defensive pairings against particular lines while rotating two forward lines by style. The coach hopes to give the fourth line more ice time, which will require fewer defensive-zone faceoffs. Matchups will matter less if the team is playing at its best. He also said Sami Kapanen will take power-play point duties and appeared tentative, but changes must account for the consequences of rotating an entire unit.

The coach said he has no single coaching philosophy and adapts to his surroundings, including abandoning the speed-based approach used in junior hockey. He relies heavily on Kevin McCarthy and Randy Ladouceur and is comfortable delegating. He described himself as a quiet coach who values honesty with the media, loves hockey and watching it, enjoys the pressure and uncertainty of coaching, and continues to speed while traveling.

The study surveys ontologies and ontology design patterns (ODPs) for scientific workflow and process modeling in Materials Science and Engineering (MSE), where processing routes shape material structure, properties, and performance. It defines three domain-specific requirements: modeling process structure and execution order; representing data, inputs, outputs, and experimental resources; and capturing project goals, participants, and roles. Nine domain experts reviewed the requirements and extracted patterns.

Ontologies examined include P-PLAN, Metadata4Ing, OPMW, WILD, the General Process Ontology, and PMDcore. Manual analysis produced Process, Resource, and Project ODPs. P-PLAN strongly supports process and resource modeling; Metadata4Ing supports resource and project constructs; OPMW supports process and resource modeling but lacks project context; WILD focuses on process structure; GPO supports processes and resources but not organizational roles; and PMDcore supports all three categories.

A baseline automated method embeds requirement sentences and ontology terms extracted from labels, definitions, comments, and annotation properties using sentence-transformer models. Cosine similarity identifies candidate terms, which are evaluated against curated mappings with precision, recall, and F1-score. Candidate modules are generated with ROBOT extraction methods; STAR with no intermediate classes is selected as the default because it produces compact, logically coherent modules.

Evaluation found that P-PLAN achieved the highest F1 scores for Process (0.59) and Resource (0.53) ODPs. PMDcore supported all three categories, scoring 0.36, 0.21, and 0.25 respectively, with strong Project recall. Metadata4I performed moderately on Resource and Project ODPs but poorly on Process, while WILD produced no evaluated matches.

Limitations include bias toward richly annotated terms, sensitivity to requirement wording, independent processing of each ontology, and reliance on modularization as the main reuse strategy. Proposed future work includes additional MSE subdomains, ontology mappings for cross-ontology pattern detection, controlled vocabularies, multi-expert validation, and a platform for publishing patterns and gathering community feedback.

Public Health Wales investigated a July 2021 Salmonella Typhimurium outbreak linked to an Eid al-Adha barbecue and lunch in Cardiff. The investigation used case finding, a cohort study, nested case-control analysis with Firth logistic regression, and whole-genome sequencing of human, food, and environmental samples. Twenty-two symptomatic cases were identified within a social network of 43 people, with 12 seeking emergency care, six admitted overnight, and one requiring intensive care. Sequencing found five cultured Salmonella Typhimurium cases and three cases with additional pathogens were genetically indistinguishable from cases.

Consumption of “marara,” a traditional dish made from raw sheep liver, was the most likely transmission vehicle. All nine raw-liver consumers in the barbecue cohort became ill, and raw liver remained strongly associated with illness after adjustment (aOR 49.99; 95% CI 1.71–1461.54). Lamb and spicy sauce were not independent risk factors. All 11 leftover raw-lamb samples tested had sequences identical to human isolates, with matching sequences also found at two local butchers and the supplying abattoir, indicating widespread sheep-meat contamination and opportunities for cross-contamination. The precise point of contamination was not established.

Culturally sensitive community engagement included an educational session and multilingual food-safety materials and Eid al-Adha infographics. The authors identified traditional raw offal as a new outbreak vehicle and recommended that investigations consider culturally relevant dishes omitted from routine questionnaires, alongside proactive messaging about raw and undercooked meat and offal.

An appeals court ruled that the federal government lacked authority under the Lacey Act to restrict interstate trade of Burmese pythons and other giant exotic snakes within the contiguous United States. The ruling does not alter bans on importing injurious species or state laws, including Florida’s pet ban. The U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service is reviewing the decision, and owners are cautioned not to move their snakes because other challenges may remain.

The coach said New Jersey remained disciplined and strong throughout the series, while his team had spent much of the series chasing them without controlling key areas. He described the latest game as the first time his team had consistently “gone after it,” after spending four games as the “nail” to New Jersey’s “hammer.” The team had no injuries, used three centers including Nieuwendyk and Modano, and planned to alter its forward lineup. Morgan “Dr. Noc” McSweeney, a biotech scientist and science-focused social media creator, calls his approach “edutainment”: translating academic research, public health and current events into engaging, digestible and actionable content. Common formats include reacting to incorrect health claims, explaining research such as diet and microbiome effects, and turning study findings into practical health advice.

He says charged, confrontational content tends to reinforce existing supporters rather than inform undecided people, while nuance may reduce reach. He therefore focuses on viewers confused about public health, avoids prolonged engagement with committed anti-science audiences and emphasizes nonpolarizing content that can introduce people to broader views. He has found that audiences want evidence and explanation, not simply directives such as “you’re wrong.” Different viewers also require different levels and framings of information, making diversity among science communicators important so audiences can find trustworthy sources with whom they relate.

His process is informal. While working full time in biotech, he usually spends one or two hours at night selecting topics from comments, emails, direct messages and news, outlining scripts and recording. For major breaking stories, he waits to identify common questions and gaps in existing coverage. Although he has made thousands of videos, he estimates only about one in 30 becomes especially successful, while an average video currently receives roughly 500,000 to one million views.

McSweeney argues that institutions such as the CDC, NIH, FDA and WHO lag in effective social media communication because of insufficient resources, legacy media structures, lengthy review processes and the difficulty of producing hundreds of videos while learning. He says institutions should invest in influencer-style communication and permit experts and health care providers to create evidence-based content without fear of punishment.

He keeps his social media work separate from his job and generally does not discuss his specific projects, though his biotech experience adds credibility and informs his presentation. His work involves monoclonal-antibody therapeutics for respiratory infectious diseases, and he remains personally invested in seeing it through at least the Phase 2 stage. He also weighs eventually becoming a full-time science communicator.

McSweeney says briefly sharing personal details can build trust. He recounts that mentioning he had to leave a livestream to cook dinner for his wife helped a viewer see him as a genuine person rather than an industry representative. He now believes institutions and communicators should incorporate more personal elements and says occasional personal or entertaining posts can strengthen relationships with audiences. He handles hostile comments by hiding, blocking or deleting them rather than responding, noting that replies increase their visibility and rarely change minds.

The Coppock Curve is a long-term momentum strategy devised by economist E.S.C. Coppock in 1965 under an Episcopal Church mandate. It uses a 10-month weighted moving average of the sum of 11-month and 14-month price rate-of-change indicators to capture market uptrends while filtering corrections. On a monthly timeframe, it signals a long entry when the curve crosses above zero and an exit when it crosses below zero from above.

The strategy is primarily intended for stocks and stock indices and has generated relatively few trades because of its monthly timeframe. A backtest using monthly S&P 500 data from 1960 recorded 12 trades over 63 years, all profitable. Two examples lasted more than six years and returned approximately 80% and 65%. The backtest showed substantially reduced drawdowns, about one-quarter less time invested in the market, and a risk-adjusted return exceeding buy and hold, although the small number of trades limits the significance of the results. The article also notes that the strategy may be applied to shorter timeframes if validated through separate backtesting.

Backup Nick Foles leads the Philadelphia Eagles against the New England Patriots in Super Bowl LII, seeking the franchise’s first Super Bowl victory. A win could cement his legacy but might be his final game as starting quarterback because Carson Wentz, who tore his ACL, is expected to return in 2018. Although Philadelphia is committed to Wentz, Foles’ postseason performance has increased his trade value and interest from other teams. His two-year contract allows him to test free agency after 2018, and the central question is whether the Eagles should retain him as Wentz’s dependable backup or sell him at peak value.

He calls for passage of a defense budget and rejects further reductions in defense and foreign assistance.

He accepts responsibility for the failed Iran initiative, acknowledges serious mistakes, and vows corrective action while warning against letting setbacks deter future efforts to advance peace and freedom. He demands continued support for U.S. interests and allies in the Middle East and resistance to terrorist blackmail.

On Soviet policy, he calls for political settlement and Soviet troop withdrawal in Afghanistan, continued support for Nicaraguan freedom fighters, and adherence to the Monroe Doctrine. He also urges expanded trade negotiations, fair international commerce, progress on human rights and arms reduction, and continuation of the Strategic Defense Initiative, promising to veto measures that weaken national security or negotiating leverage.

Domestically, he advocates a constitutional balanced-budget amendment, a presidential line-item veto, adherence to deficit-reduction commitments, and opposition to higher taxes. He proposes state-based welfare reform, protection against catastrophic medical costs, increased competitiveness, stronger education, voluntary school prayer, drug-free schools, worker retraining, and assistance to farmers.

The president concludes that the Constitution’s distinguishing principle is “We the people”: Americans, not government, are sovereign. Using Benjamin Franklin’s image of a rising sun, he declares that the nation is unfinished and capable of continued progress.

The excerpt documents L4 peripheral memory mapping and boot-configuration pin multiplexing for the TMS320DM814x device. L4 Fast and Slow memory-map details appear in Tables 3-5 and 3-6. Cortex-A8-decoded regions shown for reference are not physically part of L4 Slow and are reserved to other masters. The DDR DMM TILER provides an additional 4-GB addressing range, enabled by a 33rd address bit, for rotated and mirrored frame-buffer views. Only HDVPSS and ISS can access the full range; other masters can access one view through the 512-MB TILER region in the base 4-GB map.

Device-pin tables list signal names, multiplexed functions, ball and package identifiers, pin types, internal pull states, supply voltage, PINCNTLx controls, deselected-input states, and multi-mux options. Boot-configuration pins are multiplexed between ARM Cortex-A8 boot mode and GPMC. At reset, BTMODE bits are sampled to determine GPMC CS0, reset-output, XIP, Ethernet PHY, reserved-boot, and ARM boot-mode configurations; afterward, the pins serve as GPMC multiplexed data/address signals.

The lecture frames sustainable real estate finance around three topics: sustainable finance broadly, mortgage and debt markets, and private equity. It explains how tenant demand for green, healthy, and climate-resilient buildings can generate rental premiums, higher property values, and incentives for developers. Within sustainable finance, climate risk is treated as a financial risk that asset managers have a fiduciary duty to manage. Portfolio theory is used to compare bonds, stocks, conventional real estate, and green real estate. True green buildings can offer lower risk and higher returns because of regulation, tenant preferences, and investor expectations, while brown buildings face penalties, tenant departures, and risk premiums. These differences shift the efficient frontier and redirect capital toward sustainable assets.

The mortgage section examines how flooding, wildfire, and other hazards can reduce property values and increase delinquency and default risk. Government-backed mortgage and flood-insurance programs face particular difficulties in assessing climate risk and protecting lower-income households, creating social and political concerns about more accurate risk pricing. Work with Fannie Mae aims to incorporate climate risk into mortgage appraisals.

Green mortgages are presented as a way to reward energy efficiency. Evidence cited indicates that energy-efficient homes are less likely to default, partly because lower energy bills improve repayment capacity; their higher values can also support larger loans. Banks may therefore offer better loan-to-value terms to households presenting an energy-efficiency rating. A renovation-financing model would also allow banks to lend against expected post-renovation appreciation, with the additional funds used for green improvements.

The lecture concludes with private equity, including commingled funds structured around general and limited partners. ESG considerations are increasingly incorporated into investment memoranda, due diligence, and asset-management plans because sustainable properties are viewed as potentially improving business value and reducing physical and transition risks.

Gold surged above $4,000 per ounce as weak U.S. retail and manufacturing data increased expectations that the Federal Reserve will ease monetary policy, potentially by early 2026. Falling yields, a softer dollar, broader market uncertainty and central-bank buying strengthened demand for gold as a safe-haven asset. Geopolitical tensions, fiscal pressures and concerns about debt sustainability and corporate earnings further supported the rally, while emerging-market central banks continued accumulating holdings. Analysts warned that hawkish Federal Reserve signals or stronger U.S. growth could cause short-term corrections, but said sustained prices above $4,000 could attract more institutional capital into precious metals and reshape 2025 asset allocation.

On 3 July 2018, Spanish- and Italian-language Wikipedias blocked all articles to protest proposed EU copyright rules ahead of the European Parliament’s 5 July vote. The directive, backed by the European Committee on Legal Affairs, would update EU copyright law for the first time since 2001. Articles 11 and 13 mandate website content filters and introduce a “link tax” intended to send traffic to news sites. Critics said vague rules and national variations could restrict sharing and search, threaten online freedom and endanger Wikipedia despite a proposed exception for such platforms. English Wikipedia displayed a banner rather than blocking access. Jimmy Wales said local communities decide their own protests and accused the European Commission of misleading the public. Supporters argued Article 13 would correct an “extreme imbalance” in copyright law.

Twin Rivers Council is enrolling girls in grades kindergarten through third grade in Cub Scouts, with a goal of 125 new members. Registration through March 31 via the BSA’s “Be a Scout” website or the council office allows families to prepare for summer camping and other programs.

Earth Day, observed annually on April 22 since 1970, has grown from early-1990s roadside cleanups into what the author calls a spring ritual deifying nature. Writing from Windham, the former Sun Media Group managing editor, he argues "Big Environment" has become a powerful political force comparable to Big Oil, sometimes prioritizing environmental concerns over population and commercial growth. He cites Protect South Portland's Clear Skies Ordinance, which bans Canadian oil sands within city limits, as an example: it is decimating the local oil industry, costing taxpayers millions in court defense, and prompting firms to seek tax abatements. He also faults wind power for marring Maine's landscape, endangering birds, and failing to meet energy needs, estimating 47 Mars Hill-sized farms per county would be needed to power just Maine homes. Accusing environmental groups of manufacturing fears to solicit donations, he calls anti-tar-sands campaigning "hysteria." Suggesting nature works like clockwork, he recommends spending Earth Day outdoors for enjoyment rather than fear.

A football blitz sends five or more defenders directly at the quarterback, rather than the usual four pass rushers, to pressure him, disrupt his pass, or sack him. Because blitzing leaves fewer defenders to cover receivers and other areas, it carries risk, but a well-timed blitz can significantly disrupt an offense. Defensive coordinators call variations to outsmart offensive playmakers and help the defense gain possession quickly.

Common blitz types include conventional, zone, safety, cornerback, zero, and run blitzes. Zone blitzes substitute a linebacker for a defensive lineman or edge rusher who drops into coverage, while safety and cornerback blitzes create surprise at the cost of leaving an opponent uncovered. Zero blitzes provide no deep safety and are generally used when a run is expected. Run blitzes aim to stop the ball carrier quickly.

Offenses can counter blitzes with quick passes, often targeting running backs on short routes; mobile quarterbacks who evade the rush; and max-protection schemes that keep extra blockers in to slow the blitz. Quarterbacks can also identify and exploit coverage gaps before or immediately after the snap.

NVIDIA Corporation reported unaudited results for the third quarter of fiscal 2017, ended October 30, 2016. Quarterly revenue was $2.004 billion, up 54% year over year and 40% sequentially. Gross profit was $1.183 billion, with a 59.0% gross margin versus 56.3% a year earlier. Operating income rose to $639 million from $245 million, net income increased to $542 million from $246 million, and diluted earnings per share were $0.83 versus $0.44. For the first nine months, revenue was $4.737 billion, up 31%; operating income was $1.201 billion, net income was $1.012 billion, and diluted earnings per share were $1.59.

GPU revenue was $1.697 billion, up 53% year over year, with operating income of $678 million. Growth reflected high-end GeForce GPU sales, Pascal-based products, strong deep-learning demand, cloud and virtualized-computing products, and initial DGX-1 sales. Tegra Processor revenue was $241 million, up 87%, and operating income was $17 million, compared with a $65 million loss a year earlier; automotive revenue rose 61%. The All Other category reported $66 million of revenue and a $56 million operating loss. Third-quarter market revenue was $1.244 billion for gaming, $240 million for datacenter, $207 million for professional visualization, $127 million for automotive, and $186 million for OEM and IP.

As of October 30, cash and cash equivalents were $1.940 billion and marketable securities were $4.731 billion. Total assets were $9.612 billion, total liabilities were $4.243 billion, and shareholders’ equity was $5.324 billion. Nine-month operating cash flow was $951 million, investing activities used $420 million, and financing activities provided $813 million.

NVIDIA early adopted a stock-based compensation accounting standard in the third quarter. The adoption increased retained earnings and deferred tax assets by $353 million, included a $42 million tax benefit in quarterly tax expense and $62 million for the nine months, and required adjustments to previously reported 2017 quarterly results. Stock-based compensation expense was $176 million for nine months, compared with $145 million a year earlier. Quarterly and nine-month effective tax rates were 12.8% and 14.2%, respectively. NVIDIA expected recently issued standards on intra-entity asset transfers and cash-flow classification not to have a material impact, while it continued evaluating the lease and revenue-recognition standards.

In September 2016, NVIDIA issued $1.0 billion of 2.20% notes due 2021 and $1.0 billion of 3.20% notes due 2026, generating net proceeds of $1.99 billion for convertible-note repayment and general corporate purposes. The company also had a $575 million revolving credit facility with no borrowings outstanding. During the nine months, NVIDIA settled $444 million principal of its 1% convertible notes, issued 15 million shares for the excess conversion value, recognized a $15 million loss, and received notices for an additional $229 million principal amount.

NVIDIA returned $694 million to shareholders during the first nine months through $509 million of share repurchases and $185 million of dividends. Its board added $2.0 billion to the repurchase authorization, leaving $2.96 billion available through December 2020. The quarterly dividend was increased to $0.14 per share from $0.115, and the company stated that it intended to return $1.25 billion to shareholders in fiscal 2018.

The report also disclosed inventory purchase obligations of $908 million, a build-to-suit headquarters lease financing arrangement under which banks could fund up to $380 million, and NVIDIA’s associated lease guarantee. Intellectual-property disputes with Samsung and Qualcomm were resolved through dismissals and limited patent licenses, while litigation with Advanced Silicon Technologies was resolved through a license agreement and a $10 million charge to cost of revenue. During the quarter, NVIDIA expanded Pascal GPU offerings, launched Tesla P40 and P4 products and TensorRT, began shipping DGX-1, announced NVIDIA technology for the Nintendo Switch, and announced that DRIVE PX 2 would power Tesla vehicles’ AutoPilot systems.

Market sentiment measures the aggregate mood of investors and traders as bullish, neutral, or bearish. Sentiment indicators track this mood and may identify potential market turning points when readings become extreme. The AAII sentiment index, published weekly since the 1980s by the American Association of Individual Investors, surveys members about the stock market’s expected direction over the next six months.

AAII sentiment may work contrarian: extreme bullishness can mean most participants are already positioned for rising prices, while extreme bearishness may leave few sellers and allow even slightly positive news to trigger buying.

Spreadsheet backtests using weekly AAII data since 1987 measured four-week S&P 500 returns. After bearish signals, such as a bull-bear spread below -20, average gains were 1.03% per trade, though drawdowns—including during the 2008–09 crisis—remained substantial. Bullish spreads above 20 averaged 0.52% per trade, while spreads above 40 averaged a negative 0.33%, with relatively few trades.

Overall, very bullish readings were followed by mediocre or lower returns, whereas very bearish readings were followed by above-average returns. The passage concludes that AAII sentiment can inform trading strategies, but other indicators may be better suited to short-term trading.
Antarctic krill eject compact masses of leftover food that sink to the seafloor, and they eject more food when contaminated with plastic, though the effects on the global carbon cycle remain unclear.

The passage examines professional education and lifelong learning for librarians in Romania in response to rapid technological, informational, and social change. Romania’s library system includes the National Library, public libraries, educational libraries, and specialised libraries, administered by central ministries and local authorities and represented by two professional associations. Academic LIS education developed after 1999, but low salaries, limited educational investment, and the low prestige of librarianship reduce its attractiveness to young people.

Three training routes are identified: a bachelor’s degree in LIS; a bachelor’s degree in another field followed by postgraduate LIS training; and professional competence acquired outside formal education and assessed against occupational standards. The second route is preferred by many school and academic librarians and brings multidisciplinary expertise into the profession, although it is classified as lifelong education despite functioning as initial education. The third route, supported historically by public libraries, presents difficulties in certifying competence and risks admitting inadequately prepared entrants. Non-formal training—including library visits, conferences, professional events, and mentoring—has received positive feedback, but institutional financial support is limited despite legal requirements to allocate at least 5% of personnel expenditure to training.

The National Library of Romania led development of the Occupational Standard “Librarian (Higher Education),” recognised by the National Authority for Qualifications. It defines transversal, organisational, legal, environmental, ICT, and library-management competences, together with academic knowledge, professional activities, responsibilities, and promotion requirements. The standard provides a national framework for professional assessment, employment, and promotion. The passage proposes adding competences related to internationalisation and multicultural adaptation, public education in information literacy, and the promotion of reading through stronger psycho-pedagogical skills for librarians working with children. It concludes that LIS institutions and methodological libraries should update their programmes and strategies in response to new professional requirements and the negative public image of librarianship.

The paper develops a theoretical and empirical framework for information design that combines Bayesian persuasion with behavioral framing. A sender observes the state of the world, while a receiver has a prior belief and chooses among actions based on expected utility. In addition to a signaling or recommendation scheme, the sender may choose a framing: natural-language text or other presentation cues that induces an initial receiver belief. This framing-to-belief relationship is represented by a potentially noisy belief oracle and may be Bayesian or non-Bayesian.

The model yields three optimization settings: recommendation-only, framing-only with a fixed recommendation scheme, and joint optimization of framing and recommendations. The paper focuses on the latter two. Framing-only optimization is generally computationally intractable, including for approximation, and sender utility is discontinuous in the induced belief, making errors in the belief oracle consequential. Joint optimization is more tractable: sender utility is continuous in the framing-induced belief, making the problem robust to oracle errors, and the authors provide a quasi-polynomial-time approximation scheme.

For practical joint optimization, the paper proposes a hill-climbing method in which LLMs generate framings and approximate the belief oracle, while analytical methods optimize recommendations. Case studies examine a realtor choosing both self-presentation and property recommendations and a clothing brand choosing advertising text alongside discount strategies. The method performs strongly under LLM-based evaluation. Human evaluations show weaker and more variable responses, but broadly confirm the predicted direction and approximate magnitude of the effects.

The work positions LLMs as scalable tools for systematic persuasive design while distinguishing the greater promise of joint optimization from the severe difficulties of optimizing framing alone.
