The adapter pattern adds a separate container that modifies an application’s interface to conform to a predefined standard. It is used to normalize monitoring interfaces, redirect or transform logs, and implement richer health checks without changing vendor-supplied application images. Examples include a Prometheus exporter for Redis, Fluentd adapters for Redis slow-query logs and Apache Storm, and a MySQL health-check adapter. Separating these functions into adapter containers promotes modularity, independent updates and resource isolation, and reuse across applications.

Microservices divide an application into independently developed components that communicate through defined APIs. This approach can improve team focus, release independence, and service-specific scaling, but it makes system-wide debugging and architectural design more difficult. Distributed patterns can help manage these complexities.

Replicated load-balanced services use identical instances behind a load balancer. Replication provides redundancy, fault tolerance, and horizontal scaling, while readiness probes prevent traffic from reaching instances that are still initializing. Session-tracked variants route a user’s requests to the same replica, commonly through consistent hashing or application-level tracking such as cookies. A complete stateless serving architecture can add a replicated caching tier, rate limiting through a reverse proxy, and replicated nginx servers for SSL termination.

Sharded services divide requests or data among shards, with a root or router selecting the appropriate shard. They are primarily used when state is too large for one machine. Sharding improves memory utilization compared with replicated caches, although a failed shard can reduce cache hit rates and increase latency. Replicating individual shards improves availability, enables safe upgrades, and allows overloaded shards to scale independently. A sharding function must be deterministic and uniform; hash functions combined with modulo are commonly used, and selecting an appropriate key is essential. Consistent hashing minimizes key remapping when the number of shards changes. Routing may use per-pod ambassadors or a shared, replicated routing service, trading deployment simplicity for additional network latency and scaling requirements.

The scatter/gather pattern distributes each request simultaneously to multiple leaves, which perform portions of the computation and return partial results for the root to combine. It reduces latency through parallel processing and can be combined with data sharding. However, communication overhead and slow “straggler” leaves can limit gains, while the requirement to query every leaf reduces availability. Replicating each leaf shard mitigates these reliability and upgrade concerns.

Functions as a service (FaaS) provides event-triggered, automatically managed, stateless execution. It simplifies deployment, scaling, and recovery but creates operational and debugging difficulties because dependencies are not directly represented. FaaS is generally poorly suited to long-running background work, workloads requiring large in-memory datasets, or sustained high request volumes with unfavorable per-request economics. Suitable patterns include stateless request or response decorators, such as adding defaults before an API call, and asynchronous event handlers, such as sending two-factor authentication codes. Event-based systems can also be organized as directed pipelines of decoupled event-processing stages.

The lecture extends numerical wave-equation methods from the one-way, first-order equation to the two-way, second-order equation \(u_{tt}=c^2u_{xx}\). Written as a first-order system, the symmetric matrix has eigenvalues \(c\) and \(-c\), corresponding to waves traveling in opposite directions. The continuous solution consists of functions of \(x-ct\) and \(x+ct\); initial displacement and velocity determine how these waves divide, with initial-velocity effects confined to the region between the characteristic lines.

Spatial discretization is analyzed with the method of lines. Substitution of a Fourier exponential shows that centered second differences replace \(k^2\) with
\[
\frac{2-2\cos(k\Delta x)}{\Delta x^2}
=\frac{4\sin^2(k\Delta x/2)}{\Delta x^2},
\]
introducing a frequency-dependent wave speed and hence dispersion, although the scheme remains second-order accurate.

A fully discrete, centered time-and-space scheme is then examined. Its two amplification factors must have magnitude at most one for stability. This yields the Courant–Friedrichs–Lewy condition
\[
r=\frac{c\Delta t}{\Delta x}\leq 1.
\]
Larger values of \(r\) produce unstable amplification factors.

The lecture also identifies variable coefficients, forcing terms, high-frequency oscillations, finite boundaries, and second-difference matrices as features of more realistic wave problems. High-frequency problems require sufficiently small spatial steps. The next lecture will introduce staggered-grid methods.

The study demonstrates controlled defect engineering of CVD-grown monolayer MoS₂ using 1 MeV electron irradiation at approximately 3 × 10⁶ electrons/s for 30, 60, and 120 s. Raman and PL measurements showed irradiation-induced chalcogen vacancies and disorder, Raman-mode shifts, excitonic blueshifts, and reduced photoluminescence intensity. XPS identified increased Mo–O bonding and progressive Mo oxidation from Mo⁴⁺ to Mo⁵⁺ and Mo⁶⁺, while sulfur remained largely unaffected. KPFM measurements showed the work function increasing from 4.8 to 5.24 eV after 120 s, indicating irradiation-induced p-type behavior.

Low-temperature PL revealed a broad defect-bound emission 200–300 meV below the A exciton that intensified with irradiation. Longer exposures produced deeper and shallower defect emissions near 1.64 and 1.73 eV, respectively, attributed to oxygen interacting with sulfur vacancies. Temperature- and excitation-power-dependent measurements indicated strong carrier localization, increased nonradiative recombination, trap saturation, and stronger phonon coupling for defect-bound excitons than for free excitons.

Circular-polarization-resolved PL showed that defect emission was unpolarized and that the A-exciton valley polarization decreased from 62% in as-grown MoS₂ to 38% after 120 s of irradiation, consistent with defect-mediated intervalley scattering and carrier trapping. First-principles calculations showed that sulfur vacancies introduce donor-like states, whereas oxygen-related configurations create more readily ionized acceptor-like states near the valence band, producing net p-type doping and the observed defect emission. Overall, the results establish electron-beam exposure time as a controllable means of tuning defects, oxidation, excitonic behavior, and valley polarization in monolayer MoS₂, with possible application to other TMDs after parameter optimization.

The article examines gold’s price drivers and all-time-high frequency before introducing and backtesting a strategy for trading near record prices. Gold is influenced by supply and demand, the US dollar, investor risk appetite, central-bank reserve purchases, and jewelry demand; it is also used as an inflation hedge. From 1955–2022, gold reached 80 monthly all-time highs—about 1.25 annually and 10% of months—though it went 14 years without a new high from 1981–2005. The strategy uses monthly closing prices from the World Bank’s Commodities Markets Database. It spends only about one-third of the time in the market, yielding lower returns while reducing maximum drawdown to almost half and performing similarly to an inflation-focused strategy.

The Wing-T is a football offense developed by Harold “Tubby” Raymond at the University of Delaware. It uses misdirection, unusual formations, and a varied run game to make plays look alike, slow aggressive defenses, and force them to react. It requires at least two capable running backs, including a strong fullback, and an athletic quarterback; smaller, quick linemen skilled at pulling and trapping can be advantageous.

The offense’s strengths include deception, play action, quick motions, unusual formations, and experienced coaches’ ability to adjust. Its main weakness is the lack of a traditional dropback passing game. Common formations include Wing, Wing-Slot, and unbalanced alignments. Common running plays include Buck Sweep, Down/Belly G, and Trap, while passing concepts include Waggle, Single Receiver Option Route, and Play Action Vertical Pass.

The traditional Wing-T is largely extinct in major college football but remains common in high school. Its principles have also influenced spread offenses, including those used by Gus Malzahn at Auburn and UCF.

The ADS868xW devices operate in acquisition (ACQ), conversion (CONV), and reset states. They enter ACQ at power-up, after asynchronous reset, and after each conversion. A falling RST edge causes a reset, while a rising CONVST/CS edge initiates conversion. Conversions use an internal clock, ignore further CONVST/CS transitions until completion, and return the device to ACQ. The host can detect completion through an RVS transition or wait for the specified maximum conversion time. A low-power NAP mode is available during acquisition.

Programming supports data reads and writes through nine configuration registers. A transfer frame begins when the host pulls CONVST/CS low, causing RVS to go low, loading the output word into a 32-bit shift register, and resetting the command state to NOP. SCLK edges shift input data in and output data out. Pulling CONVST/CS high transfers the input register to the command processor. A 32-clock frame is optimal and permits a valid command; shorter frames invalidate writes and are treated as NOPs, although transferred output data remains valid; longer frames use the final 32 input bits as the command.

Input commands support byte and half-word operations, including register reads, writes, bit setting, and bit clearing. Half-word commands ignore the least significant address bit. Register commands are 32 bits long and execute on the rising CONVST/CS edge. Output data can contain a fixed test pattern, 8- or 16-bit register data, or the latest 16-bit conversion result. Optional appended fields include the device address, input-range flags, AVDD alarm flags, input alarm flags, and parity bits.

The multiSPI interface supports four legacy SPI-compatible configuration protocols and, for reads, single-SDO, dual-SDO, and source-synchronous protocols. SPI-00-S is used after power-up or reset, and other SPI modes are selected through SDI_CTL_REG. The SDO control register selects output behavior, clock source, and bus width. Dual-SDO mode uses SDO-0 and SDO-1 and requires half as many clock cycles as single-SDO mode. Source-synchronous modes provide a synchronous output clock on RVS and support internal or external clock sources.

The register map includes device identification for daisy-chain systems, reset and power control, SPI input and output control, output-data control, reference and input-range selection, alarm status, and programmable high and low alarm thresholds. Reset/power-control writes are protected by writing 69h to address 05h. Output-control registers can append status flags and parity or select fixed data patterns. Alarm registers report active and tripped input and AVDD conditions.

The ADS868xW is a 16-bit successive-approximation ADC with a fully differential input, integrated analog front end, and buffered precision reference. An eight-channel industrial input-module design combines an ADS8681W with an MUX36D08 differential multiplexer and supports software-configured voltage or current channels for PLC, DCS, and data-acquisition systems. The design covers bipolar, unipolar, and current inputs up to the listed industrial ranges, settles to 1% accuracy in under 5 µs, and uses the ADC’s high-bandwidth input, programmable gain, integrated driver, and reference. Device protections include overvoltage detection, an input alarm, and an AVDD alarm.

Input-alarm thresholds and hysteresis are programmable for applications such as NTC thermistor sensing, where hysteresis helps prevent noise-induced false alarms near threshold crossings.

The device uses separate AVDD analog and DVDD digital supplies. TI recommends close-placement supply-decoupling capacitors, including 1 µF and 10 µF capacitors, at least 4.7 µF at REFIO when using the internal reference, and specified 1 µF and 10 µF capacitors at REFCAP. PCB layout should separate analog and digital routing, keep supplies clean, avoid vias between supply pins and bypass capacitors, and connect grounds through short, low-impedance paths.

NAP mode reduces consumption between conversions and is enabled through the protected reset/power-control register; the device enters NAP after conversion while CONVST/CS remains high and requires the specified wake-up delay before another conversion. Power-down mode shuts down analog blocks while retaining the interface and register contents; exit is initiated by clearing the power-down bit and requires the specified power-up delay.

Figure 8-5 provides ADS9803 PCB-layout guidance: keep digital lines away from analog signal paths and noise sources; place 0.1 µF ceramic bypass capacitors near AVDD_5V, VDD_1V8, and IOVDD; avoid vias between power pins and capacitors; place reference decoupling near REFIO and REFM; avoid vias between REFIO and capacitors; and connect GND and REFM to a ground plane using short connections.

In early February 2008, Charlie Devins visited Corning to study its centrally managed innovation system, particularly the Growth and Strategy Council (GSC). He questioned whether the structure created political tensions, slowed innovation, could scale as Corning accelerated growth, or could be replicated elsewhere.

Founded in 1851, Corning repeatedly commercialized innovations in glass, ceramics, fiber optics, television bulbs, cookware, automotive emissions systems, and life-science products. Its 2000 prosperity depended heavily on telecommunications: revenue reached $7.1 billion, the company held about 40% of the global optical-fiber market, and it spent more than $9.9 billion on acquisitions. The telecommunications crash then reduced revenue from $6.3 billion in 2001 to $3.1 billion in 2002, drove the stock from $100 to $1.50, produced a $5.4 billion loss, and resulted in layoffs of more than 12,000 people. Corning maintained its research spending and core identity, returned many former employees, and by 2008 had recovered to $5.86 billion in revenue and $23 in stock. Its four segments were Display Technologies, Telecommunications, Environmental Technologies, and Life Sciences.

Corning combined business units led by general managers with centralized research at Sullivan Park. Shared expertise in glass and ceramics, personnel transfers, and co-located research enabled synergies among businesses. Its governance structure included a Technology Council (CTC) for early-stage projects and the GSC for high-potential projects in later stages. The CTC evaluated opportunities, market size, strategic fit, differentiation, and resource requirements. The GSC, led by CEO Wendell Weeks, COO Peter Volanakis, and CTO Joe Miller, advised and supported the four business segments while controlling significant portions of innovation investment and resource allocation.

Corning followed a stage-gate innovation process centered on customer problems, specialized technology, and “keystone components.” Its culture emphasized generating many ideas, applying capabilities from failed ideas elsewhere, and making sustained long-term investments, or “patient money.” Display technologies took 14 years to become profitable, while optical fiber took 20 years despite substantial investment. Corning spent 10% of revenue on research, development, and engineering; in 2007, 64% of its $565 million budget supported existing businesses, while corporate funding covered research, exploratory work, and new business development.

The GSC began in 2001 and became the principal forum for balancing innovation across existing and developing businesses. It paced programs, allocated resources, advised on pricing and product decisions, and provided expertise and rigor. It met several times monthly, typically with 18–20 attendees and three extensively prepared topics. Presenters received written feedback afterward, while an annual September portfolio review used project-level zero-based budgeting. Although some managers found large meetings intimidating, the council was generally valued for objective, frank discussion and for challenging assumptions.

The GSC enabled major commitments in diesel filters and fiber-to-the-home. In 2005 it approved a production line after Volkswagen requested urgently developed diesel filters, despite the program’s substantial losses. In 2003 it supported Corning’s response to Verizon’s fiber-to-the-home initiative, helping the company introduce products rapidly and later develop lower-installation-cost solutions with Verizon.

As Corning sought to double its pace of creating businesses, the GSC faced risks that meetings would become less strategic, that it could not evaluate rising numbers of opportunities, and that it would struggle with unfamiliar business models. Its challenge was to preserve candid strategic dialogue, prioritize effectively, and ensure balanced, honest presentations from program managers.

The article presents a long-only trading strategy for the Global X Robotics and Artificial Intelligence ETF (BOTZ), using short-term Donchian Channels with an Exponential Moving Average (EMA) filter. Donchian Channel length 3 and EMA 200 were selected for testing, though they were not the optimal settings; this approach was intended to reduce curve fitting and improve realism. The strategy generated 87 daily trades in a backtest beginning September 13, 2016, outperformed buy-and-hold with less volatility, and showed promising results on a two-hour timeframe. The EMA filter improved results across nearly all tested settings.

The authors emphasize that optimization should test a strategy’s robustness across varied inputs rather than identify perfect values. Because BOTZ has a short trading history and the strategy has relatively few trades, its equity curve is not yet statistically reliable and may be curve fitted. Out-of-sample backtesting and an incubation period are strongly recommended before live trading.
The team started well but faltered in the third. They cited turnovers and too-simple puck play, vowing to improve and win next.

Judge Steven Sword sentenced three defendants in the 2015 killing of 15-year-old football player Zaevion Dobson: Christopher Drone Bassett received life plus 35 years, Richard Gregory Williams III 143 years, and Kipling Deshawn Colbert 109 years. Portions of the latter terms covered unrelated charges. Bassett was convicted of first-degree murder; the others of facilitating it.

The passage describes the US S&P 500 Financial Services sector (GICS classification), which includes traditional banks, investment houses, insurers and fintech firms, and whose capitalization-weighted index is tracked by Vanguard Financials ETF (VFH) and Financial Select Sector SPDR Fund (XLF). Following the 2008/09 crisis and tighter regulations, the sector has shown stable, steady growth, though it fell 85% from its 2007 peak and XLF still trades near 2007 levels excluding dividends. The five largest stocks by market cap as of July 21, 2022 are Berkshire Hathaway ($631.802B), JP Morgan Chase ($336.74B / $343.162B), Bank of America ($253.827B), Citigroup ($146.347B) and Goldman Sachs ($110.401B). A backtested XLF trading strategy based on monthly edges and volatility yields 198 trades, 1.05% average gain, 73% win rate, 21% max drawdown and a 2.25 profit factor; it works on most stock indices but not commodities. The sector's high volatility makes it a good trading vehicle, but its high correlation to the overall market (S&P 500, Nasdaq 100) should be considered alongside non-correlated strategies.

The work presents a simple, robust, and scalable method for fabricating visible-light Fabry–Perot microcavities using buckled dielectric membrane mirrors. The method begins with double-sided polished silicon, whose RMS roughness is reduced from about 0.3 nm to 33–50 pm through repeated wet oxidation and hydrofluoric-acid removal. A roughly 5 μm stack of 21 quarter-wave SiO₂/Ta₂O₅ pairs, with a SiO₂ capping layer, is deposited by ion-beam sputtering. Photolithography and a Bosch backside etch suspend the dielectric stack, causing its compressive strain to buckle it into a concave micromirror.

Arrays of 600 μm mirrors can be fabricated with high yield and uniformity. Reliable radii of curvature from 0.9 to 21 mm are obtained, and a COMSOL model assuming 0.3% compressive strain matches the measured shape with an R² of 99.98%. Orthogonal profile measurements show perfect rotational symmetry, with an R² of 100%.

Two aligned mirrors were characterized by swept ring-down near 780.24 nm using a piezoelectric transducer. The highest measured finesse is \(0.89\times10^6\), and the highest quality factor is \(2.3\times10^9\), corresponding to a linewidth of \((2\pi)124\pm0.5\) kHz. Finesse decreases with cavity length because of diffractive and other imperfections, while Q initially increases and later plateaus or declines. The measured finesse bounds combined scattering and absorption losses at 2.20 ppm; assuming no absorption gives a surface-roughness upper bound of 90 pm. The vendor-estimated absorption of 1.5–2 ppm indicates that scattering is comparable to or below state-of-the-art visible dielectric-coating losses. Extrapolation to telecom wavelengths yields a finesse of \(3.5\times10^6\).

The mirrors can also be integrated into compact fiber- or chip-compatible assemblies. Manually glued 1.7 mm mirror chips form 45 μm or 1 mm cavities with total stack lengths of 1 or 2 mm. The 45 μm cavity reaches \(F=0.616\times10^6\), \(Q=7.45\times10^7\), a 5.16 MHz linewidth, and a 3.18 THz free spectral range; the 1 mm cavity reaches \(F=0.263\times10^6\) and \(Q=6.74\times10^8\).

Compared with other resonator types, traditional polished cavities retain higher finesse and Q but are large and difficult to scale, while ring resonators and microdisks involve lower performance or more complex coupling. The demonstrated microcavities combine high finesse, small mode volume, short length, and modest radii of curvature, supporting potential uses in visible lasers, sensing, quantum networking, compact filters, external-cavity lasers, transfer cavities, and neutral-atom or trapped-ion optical interfaces.

Amazon is developing a home robot codenamed “Vesta,” overseen by Lab126 head Gregg Zehr. The project has accelerated hiring and reportedly targets employee trials by year-end and consumer releases as early as 2019. The robot may operate as a mobile Alexa, using advanced cameras, computer vision, and navigation, though its tasks remain unclear. The effort is separate from Amazon Robotics’ warehouse systems. Recent advances make consumer robotics more feasible, while Amazon may subsidize costs for Prime subscribers. The consumer robot market is projected to grow from about $5.4 billion this year to $15 billion annually by 2023.

SAN MIGUEL Pure Foods moved a planned P100–150 billion follow-on offering to the third or fourth quarter, citing market volatility and the need to let investors absorb other bank stock-rights offerings. The sale is needed to meet the 15% minimum public ownership requirement after consolidation and renaming as San Miguel Food and Beverage.

The disclosure describes computer-implemented methods, systems, and computer program products for simulating physical-asset digital twins with selectively bypassed inputs. A digital twin mirrors an asset and is updated over its lifecycle using real-time data from sensors, IoT devices, and recording systems. A processor creates and stores multiple timestamped versions, with version management recording changes detected from performance data or reported by users.

A user can select a current, previous, or base version for simulation, replace components, or construct a hybrid model from portions of two or more versions. The simulation engine can bypass selected components, substitute alternatives across repeated runs, limit simulation to selected portions, and use user-supplied overriding values as outputs for non-simulated upstream components. It may also combine intermediate results from successive sections, with optional augmented-reality tools for selecting and mapping components.

The digital twin module includes creation, data collection, version management, simulation, and reporting engines. The reporting engine transmits, displays, archives, and may expose shared simulation results. Implementations may operate across networked host, client, repository, sensor, and IoT systems, including cloud or containerized environments that run multiple digital-twin instances. The workflow collects and analyzes operational data, creates updated versions when changes are identified, configures and runs simulations, and reports results for review or reruns with revised parameters.

Nigeria is experiencing growth in large shopping malls, driven by demand for convenient, one-stop shopping, growing brand consciousness and the needs of consumers who shop after work. More than five upscale malls have opened, while retailers such as Shoprite and Spar are expanding. The expansion signals investor confidence, creates jobs, boosts tax revenues and reflects changing lifestyles that favor purchasing all needs under one roof.

Exeter City manager Paul Tisdale said his side could be proud of their performance despite a 1-0 defeat to Luton Town, who deserved to win. With six players missing, Exeter gave 20-year-old Jordan Storey his first league start and defended solidly. Liam McAlinden’s late equaliser was ruled out for a foul by Robbie Simpson, which Tisdale disputed. Tisdale praised Storey’s development and the work of Matt Taylor and Andy Tillson. Before hosting promotion rivals Wycombe Wanderers, he said Exeter’s good form showed no decline despite the defeat.

BTMODE states sampled at reset deassertion are latched into CONTROL_STATUS. BTMODE[15:11] configures GPMC bus width, wait enable, and multiplexing; BTMODE[4:0] defines a boot sequence attempted in order. BTMODE[7:5] are reserved and pulled down. For EMAC and XIP modes, BTMODE[9:8] and [10] select PHY mode and GPMC muxing.

Chat interfaces will remain stable as messaging apps build wider ecosystems of services: WeChat already offers meals, cabs, games and dating, while India's WhatsApp (about 94% reach) is adding voice/video calls and payments. Engagement is the battleground, with cheap Jio data driving content consumption; the author favors professionally produced content over Instagram-style stories, urges Hike to bundle payments with Airtel TV and Wynk, and cites the Gamepind gaming JV, even as India's internet coalesces into an oligopoly of global giants.

The passage describes a network security appliance that filters, forwards, blocks, buffers, or modifies packets based on addresses, ports, protocols, payloads, QoS, metadata, and other conditions. It incorporates a local touch screen or similar interface so administrators can maintain and control the appliance when remote access is unavailable or disrupted by denial-of-service attacks. Local controls receive priority processing resources and may reserve memory, throttle packet processing, pause selected traffic, close ports, blacklist sources, modify filters, or elevate attack-related rules to improve response times and avoid manual rebooting or disconnection.

Packet-filter rules may be implemented through geoprocessing. IP ranges and other filter parameters are mapped to multidimensional regions or minimum bounding rectangles and searched with spatial algorithms and R-tree indexes, enabling multiple conditions to be evaluated simultaneously and reducing rule-matching latency.

A management server maintains a rules database containing rules for mandatory and potential threats. Known or active attack rules may be distributed to all appliances, while potential or inactive rules are selected for subsets according to scores, weights, distribution percentages, random selection, or device-based hashing. Appliances report matching attack attempts, allowing relevant rules to be promoted for broader distribution, while unused low-priority rules may be removed. This approach reduces appliance memory, processor, bandwidth, and battery requirements while providing early warnings of emerging attacks.

The appliance also supports local workflows for detecting attack packets, issuing visible or audible alerts, logging events, authenticating administrative requests, and applying emergency rule changes. Packets from unrecognized devices may be buffered, quarantined, forwarded, or modified only after local authorization; absent interaction within a set period, buffered packets may be discarded. Rules can include actions, conditions, parameters, identifiers, mandatory flags, distribution scores, and logs, and refreshed rule sets may be sent as deltas to reduce update bandwidth.

Apple Inc.’s Form 8-K reported shareholder voting results from its March 10, 2015 Annual Meeting. Tim Cook, Al Gore, Bob Iger, Andrea Jung, Art Levinson, Ron Sugar, and Sue Wagner were elected as directors. Shareholders approved the appointment of Ernst & Young LLP as Apple’s independent registered public accounting firm for 2015, an advisory resolution on executive compensation, and an amendment adding 50 million shares to the Employee Stock Purchase Plan. Shareholder proposals titled “Risk Report” and “Proxy Access for Shareholders” were not approved. The amended and restated Employee Stock Purchase Plan was filed as Exhibit 10.1.

Environment Canada said reviewed phthalates pose no human-health risks, though one requires further environmental study. Environmental Defence criticized weaker Canadian protections, noting the EU found at least four phthalates risky and requires manufacturers to prove product safety. The government is considering Canadian committee recommendations and plans a regulatory modernization proposal by June 2018.

The passage argues that standardized-testing monopolies constrain educational freedom by prompting schools to tailor curricula and instruction to single exams. Some states extend public-school testing mandates to private schools through school-choice programs, requiring assessments based on public standards or specific tests such as the ACT or SAT. It also cites declining test rigor, including shorter SAT reading passages, a 240% spike in top AP Literature grades despite falling national reading scores, and a 71-point decline in SAT math rigor from 2008 to 2023.

Rather than banning standardized testing, the author advocates allowing schools or students to choose among assessments. The Classic Learning Test is presented as an alternative grounded in classic literature, philosophy, and history, while a cited study found a 0.89 correlation between CLT and SAT scores. The passage recommends that states provide multiple assessment options for school-choice programs and accept all admissions tests for public-college admission and scholarships. Arkansas and Florida are cited as states already implementing parts of this approach.

The Supreme Court will hear arguments on whether Colorado’s 2019 ban on providing conversion therapy to minors violates free speech. The law exempts religious ministry but bars licensed mental health professionals from treating clients under 18. Therapist Kaley Chiles, a practicing Christian, challenges the law as a content-based “gag order” on counselors who use only speech. She argues that strict scrutiny applies and that Colorado has not shown a compelling interest or narrowly tailored the ban.

Colorado maintains that the law regulates healthcare treatment rather than speech, so rational-basis review applies. It also argues that conversion therapy is unsafe and ineffective and that the ban is narrowly tailored to protect minors. The federal government supports Chiles’s claim that her case involves speech, while agreeing that the case should be remanded and noting Colorado would likely fail strict scrutiny. The 10th Circuit upheld the law under rational-basis review, despite a dissent warning that the majority improperly treated speech as conduct.

A Canadian Society of Palliative Care Physicians analysis concluded that palliative and hospice care can improve care while reducing costs. Hospital-based care saved an estimated $7,000–$8,000 per patient compared with usual acute care, while expanded services at Johns Hopkins were projected to save more than US$19 million over five years. Outpatient care produced about 30% direct health-care savings and improved satisfaction, symptom control, and quality of life. Expanding home-based care in Ontario could avoid $191 million–$385 million in costs, and shifting patients from acute care to residential hospices saves about $600 daily. The Society recommends combining these programs and strengthening government action to improve, monitor, and evaluate palliative care access and quality across Canada.

AMP chairman David Murray blamed prescriptive ASX governance rules for inhibiting new models and creating a financial-sector “trust deficit.” He urged stronger governance mechanisms, arguing that “one-size-fits-all” rules encourage conformity through the path of least resistance.

Gardaí appealed for information about 18-year-old Cameron Reilly’s murder in Dunleer, seeking his missing iPhone for possible messages from his attackers. Separately, a west Dublin operation aimed at preventing a gangland attack resulted in two arrests and the seizure of a semi-automatic shotgun, €1 million in drugs and cash.

The seventh Johnston Press South Business Awards, presented by Nick Wallis at Brighton’s Grand Hotel, recognized businesses from across the south coast. Guardian Angel Carers of Chichester won Overall Business of the Year and Large Business of the Year. Olive and Vine in Midhurst received the Place to Eat or Drink award, Brandon Relph of Go Creative won Young Achiever, Southsea Bathing Hut was named Retailer of the Year, and Talks at Six won Outstanding Contribution to the Community. Guardian Angel Carers’ Christina Bassadone said the awards boosted and recognized her team, while Olive and Vine’s Dean Brown-fuller planned to expand outdoor catering.

The court held that the jury instructions were not erroneous. The charge sufficiently presented the plaintiff’s allegation that the defendants failed to sound their horn or give warning. Instructions concerning right-of-way and reducing speed were unnecessary because those specific allegations were not pleaded and no special requests were made. The statutory-negligence charge did not prevent consideration of other negligence theories, and comparative-negligence instructions were proper because the evidence supported finding both parties negligent. Any error concerning damages was harmless. Because the evidence was conflicting, the jury’s verdict for the defendants was authorized, and the judgment was affirmed.
CBN introduced Form X to ease SME forex documentation, requiring a letter, beneficiary invoice, and wire transfer for visible or invisible needs of $10,000 or less.

The disclosure describes enhanced trick-play modes for streamed video, including fast-forwarding, rewinding, and fixed-duration skipping. A streaming client and video player maintain a normal buffer window for continuous playback and a trick-play window containing sparsely sampled frames—often key frames—outside the normal window, without downloading intervening frame ranges. During trick playback, the player uses only the buffered subset and may adjust frame display timing to approximate the requested speed.

A trick-play optimizer uses frame indexes, metadata, jump points, playback rates, and network-performance metrics to select which frames to request, their spacing, and which bitrate stream to use. The optimizer may extend the trick-play buffer as playback advances, switch among differently encoded streams, and later request missing intervening frames to restore continuous playback. Streaming clients also support adaptive bitrate selection and may combine content from multiple streams.

The described system includes a video repository, streaming server, optional proxy server, streaming client, video player, and performance monitor. Indexes can address key frames, other frame types, audio data, and multiple trick-play rates. A proxy server can generate or map metadata, streams, and frame indexes for conventional streaming servers, including HLS-compatible servers, and relay content requests.

Breast cancer is the UK’s most common cancer, with about 56,000 new cases annually. Regular self-examination helps identify changes from what feels normal. Lumps may be pea-sized or hard and irregular, and can occur anywhere in the breast or armpit. Other warning signs include swelling, skin dimpling or puckering, changes in breast shape or size, unexplained dryness, redness or rashes, nipple discharge or rash, and newly inverted nipples.

To check, inspect your breasts in a mirror, then lie down and use slight pressure while moving your palm in a circular spiral across the entire breast, including underneath. Repeat while sitting and examine both armpits, noting unfamiliar lumps or swellings. Checks should be thorough and repeated every two weeks to monthly, ideally on the same day each month. Moist skin during bathing may make lumps easier to feel.

A doctor should assess concerning lumps or changes. Doctors may review medical and family history, medicines, smoking and alcohol use, perform an examination, and arrange a referral if needed.

Risk factors include BRCA1 and BRCA2 mutations, early menstruation, later menopause, never giving birth, and certain hormone replacement therapy use, particularly combined HRT for more than five years. An active lifestyle and prolonged breastfeeding may reduce risk. Although more common in women, breast cancer can also develop in men, usually between ages 60 and 70, and may cause a lump or nipple changes.

Early diagnosis improves the likelihood that treatment will be effective. More than three in four women diagnosed with breast cancer remain alive after ten years.

NVIDIA appointed Donald F. Robertson Jr. as Vice President, Chief Accounting Officer and Principal Accounting Officer effective June 17, 2019, reporting to Executive Vice President and Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress. He succeeded Michael Byron, who became Vice President, Finance, Merger & Acquisition Integration and Financial Systems.

Previously, Robertson served as Western Digital’s Vice President of Finance and Chief Accounting Officer and held accounting leadership roles at SanDisk. He is a certified public accountant with degrees from UC San Diego and San Jose State University.

Robertson’s at-will offer letter provides a $650,000 annual base salary, a $600,000 sign-on bonus subject to repayment if he leaves during his first year, and 15,000 restricted stock units vesting over four years. He is also eligible for NVIDIA’s employee stock purchase plan and comprehensive benefits and entered into the company’s standard indemnity agreement. The offer letter is filed as Exhibit 10.1.

Travis Haydon, 20, was jailed for 18 months in a young offender institution for stabbing Liam Brown in the abdomen with a flick knife outside the Newmarket Tavern in Plymouth, following an argument over a spilt drink. He pleaded guilty to actual bodily harm, carrying an offensive weapon, possession of cannabis and breaching a suspended prison sentence for affray. The judge cited his "appalling record" for violence and said the offence was aggravated by alcohol and drugs, noting the facts suggested malicious wounding. Brown was treated for a two-centimetre puncture wound and kept overnight in hospital, with no lasting damage.

SPYR announced that shareholders of record on May 19, 2017, would receive a one-for-one stock dividend in a new publicly traded spin-off company separating its restaurant division. The spin-off plans to license or franchise the Eat at Joe’s concept, manufacture and distribute branded foods, and possibly acquire food-related companies. It will seek SEC registration and a separate trading symbol. The article estimated potential spin-off share values using Eat at Joe’s former $0.20–$0.50 trading range, while noting that low trading float could affect prices. Stock Market Media Group disclosed that it publishes SPYR content under a one-year contract for $5,000 per month plus 250,000 restricted SPYR shares, subject to securities-law and volume limits.

A nearly complete 167-million-year-old fossil from Scotland’s Isle of Skye revealed a newly named lizard, *Breugnathair elgolensis*, with a unusual combination of primitive and specialized traits. It had a short, fully limbed body alongside snake-like jaws and hook-shaped teeth resembling those of pythons. CT scans and high-powered X-rays confirmed that the fossil belonged to one animal rather than combining separate snake-like and gecko-like specimens. Researchers placed it in a new squamate group, Parviraptoridae, previously known only from fragmentary fossils. The discovery may indicate that early snake ancestors differed from current expectations, or that snake-like features evolved independently in an extinct squamate lineage; the fossil did not resolve which explanation is correct. The specimen was found in 2016 and studied for nearly a decade.

The A100’s 40 MB shared L2 cache is 6.7 times larger than V100’s, benefiting HPC and AI workloads that repeatedly access data. Two partitions deliver 2.3 times V100’s L2 bandwidth, with reads of 5120 bytes/clock versus 2048. Ampere adds cache-residency controls and L2 compression, providing up to fourfold improvements in DRAM read/write and L2 read bandwidth.

- **RTC_B:** Operates from a 32 kHz clock source and provides timekeeping, calendar counters, configurable calendar alarms, minute/hour/midnight/noon interval alarms, and periodic interrupts from 4096 Hz down to 0.5 Hz. It supports binary or BCD format, leap-year correction for 1901–2099, standby interrupt support, and calibration for crystal offset and temperature drift up to ±240 ppm total. GPIO clock output for calibration is supported, while TIO output and several other listed features are not.

- **Watchdog timers:** The independent **IWDT_B** uses the fixed 32 kHz LFOSC path with a programmable divider, offers eight periods from 2 ms to 2 hours, and generates a power-on reset if not serviced. The windowed **WWDT** can reset or interrupt the device when not serviced within a specified window; it provides eight selectable periods, automatic stopping during sleep, and an interval-timer mode.

- **TIMx timers:** **TIMGx** general-purpose timers support 16- or 32-bit counting modes, an 8-bit prescaler, repeat reload, and selected shadow registers. TIMG8 and TIMG9 also support QEI and Hall-sensor inputs. **TIMAx** advanced timers provide 16-bit counting, repeat counters, complementary PWM with programmable dead time, and configurable fault handling, including fast responses under 40 ns and safe-state outputs. Both types support synchronization, cross-triggering, interrupts, DMA triggers, and peripheral triggers such as ADC.

- **Analog and I/O:** DAC_OUT connects to PA15, so PA15 is not recommended for an external signal when DAC_OUT is used. The IOMUX selects digital peripheral functions and controls output drivers, input paths, and SHUTDOWN wake-up logic. Pin support for analog functions, wake-up, drive strength, and pull resistors varies by pin.

- **Debug and boot:** A two-wire ARM-compatible serial wire debug interface provides access to device debugging functions. The boot strap loader supports UART or I2C programming and configuration, uses a user-defined 256-bit password, and can be disabled, though it is enabled by default for production programming. It can be invoked through the BSL_invoke pin, automatically on devices with unprogrammed reset vectors and stack pointers, or from application software using a SYSRST command.

- **Factory data:** Devices contain a memory-mapped, read-only FACTORY region describing capabilities and providing factory trim data. DEVICEID and USERID fields include part, manufacturer, device, and variant information. Hardware revision and identification data also appear in package markings.

- **Typical schematic recommendations:** Use a 10 µF bulk and 0.1 µF ceramic decoupling capacitor near VDD/VSS. The NRST circuit typically uses a 47 kΩ pull-up and 10 nF pull-down. When SYSOSC frequency correction is used, place a 100 kΩ, 0.1%-tolerance resistor with a TCR of 25 ppm/°C or better between ROSC and VSS. VCORE requires a nearby 0.47 µF capacitor and no other connections. Open-drain I/O requires pull-up resistors for high-level output. This application guidance is not part of TI’s component specification or accuracy warranty.

- **Development and documentation:** TI provides the MSPM0 SDK, SysConfig, CCS, TI Resource Explorer, MSP Academy, GUI Composer, IAR Embedded Workbench, Keil MDK, TI Arm-Clang, and GNU Arm Embedded Toolchain support. MSP-prefixed devices are qualified production parts, while X-prefixed devices are experimental and not recommended for production. Documentation should be supplemented with device-specific data sheets because peripheral implementations and pin functions vary. TI also notes ESD handling precautions.

- **Revision and ordering information:** The April 2025 revision updates device comparisons, electrical and timing specifications, memory and operating-mode details, DMA, ADC, security, UART, SPI, LFSS, and timer information, and adds package variants and detailed documentation. Mechanical, packaging, RoHS, moisture-sensitivity, marking, and orderable information are provided, along with automotive-qualified MSPM0G3518-Q1 and MSPM0G3519-Q1 versions.

Chicago is preparing for an enormous security challenge as crowds gather for Sunday’s Bank of America Chicago Marathon, with as many as 1.7 million spectators along its 26.2-mile route, followed by Monday’s Cubs playoff game and Bears football game. Concern has intensified after the Las Vegas concert shooting and reports that a gunman had booked rooms overlooking Lollapalooza in Grant Park, raising fears of attacks from high-rises.

Police will deploy 1,000 more officers than usual Sunday and increase undercover presence around the marathon. Measures include bag checks, random spectator bag searches, restrictions on unattended items and access to start and finish lines. City officials and security experts emphasized layered defenses, coordination with high-rise personnel and public vigilance. Mayor Rahm Emanuel said he was “100 percent” confident the events were secure.

Experts said copycat attacks are rare because they require extensive planning and heightened alert. Some runners expressed concern but continued with their races.
AI models generated multiple bacteriophage genomes; some outperformed a well-studied strain in lab tests.

Saudi Aramco plans to change the pricing formula for its long-term Asian crude sales in October, marking the first change to official selling price benchmarks since the mid-1980s, according to trade sources. The new formula will use average monthly prices for DME Oman futures and Platts-assessed Dubai crude, replacing the previous Oman-Dubai average. The change is expected to boost Oman futures liquidity and may influence pricing by other regional producers.

WIRED’s “Uncanny Valley” examines renewed interest in autonomous delivery robots through DoorDash’s unveiling of Dot, a nearly five-foot-tall robot equipped with cameras and sensors. DoorDash Labs created Dot as part of a hybrid delivery model combining human couriers with drones and autonomous vehicles. The robot is designed to travel on sidewalks, roads, and bike lanes, presenting technical and regulatory challenges.

DoorDash is also partnering with Los Angeles-based Coco Robotics, whose smaller sidewalk robots still rely partly on remote operators. Although autonomy has improved, the technology remains less advanced and less expensive to develop than systems such as Waymo. Earlier investment in delivery robots, including projects by Amazon and FedEx, slowed because robots must handle crowded, unpredictable sidewalks and varied obstacles. Starship Technologies has focused on controlled environments such as university campuses, where wide, paved paths and pedestrian-only areas simplify navigation.

The discussion raises concerns about robots competing with cyclists for limited bike-lane space and creating uneven local regulations. It also questions whether robots would reduce labor demand. Human couriers can perform tasks robots struggle with, such as navigating stairs, gates, and codes, while robots may shift cleaning, loading, and curbside pickup work to other people. Overall, delivery robots remain promising but costly, technically difficult, and likely to complement rather than replace human delivery workers for now.

The speaker welcomes the visiting chiefs, assuring them of friendship, peace, and good neighborliness. He pledges to respect boundaries established by mutual consent, protect Native lands, and punish Americans who encroach. The government is willing to purchase available land along the Mississippi for boat rest stops, supplies, and care for sick travelers; knowledgeable officials will negotiate the boundaries and price. Earlier lands sold to the English were paid for at the time and therefore are not owed by the government. He urges the visitors to adopt farming, livestock raising, and textile production as more efficient ways to support their families than hunting, and promises assistance. He clarifies that previously sent clothing and necessaries were gifts, while the trading store was provided at the visitors’ request and would not transfer ownership of their land. The Secretary at War will address remaining matters, and the visitors will receive transportation, care, and a safe return home.

The Florida Second District Court of Appeal reversed the Unemployment Appeals Commission’s denial of benefits to Genel Altimeaux. After a pay dispute involving Haitian workers, Altimeaux was told he was no longer employed and initially received unemployment benefits. The referee then found that he voluntarily quit. On remand, after a second hearing, the referee again relied on testimony from the first hearing, which Altimeaux had not been able to cross-examine. The court found no competent, substantial evidence that Altimeaux personally quit; testimony at the second hearing indicated that only the group’s spokesman discussed quitting, while Altimeaux denied quitting. The court therefore directed reinstatement of Altimeaux’s unemployment award.

Parents are questioning Township High School District 113’s transparency in selecting a Highland Park High School principal, particularly why only two parents joined the stakeholder committee. Superintendent Christopher Dignam said the same process used at Deerfield is underway, with Ray and Associates screening candidates before an 18-member committee interviews two or three finalists, aiming to select a principal by April 25.

Pin and Pull is a perimeter run concept that creates favorable down-block angles and uses lead blockers in space. Its strengths include extra blockers at the point of attack, flexible down-block and pull assignments based on pre-snap alignments, and a tailback who can run from the C-gap to the sideline. It requires at least two guards capable of effective pulling, and it is best suited to speed backs who can stress defenses horizontally and gain depth quickly, although power backs may have some success. Unlike a traditional Buck Sweep, which uses an inside run to hold defenders, Pin and Pull is a true perimeter run. The passage details assignments against 3-4 odd and 4-3 even fronts, plus toss variations using motion or a tight end-wing formation.

Tracking greater noctule bats with biologgers showed that Europe’s largest bat captures migrating songbirds in flight. The bats ascend above 1,200 meters, dive vertically for several minutes, and use high-frequency feeding buzzes to pursue prey. One escaped near the ground; another was eaten during a 23-minute flight. Sound and field evidence indicate that the bats dismember birds while airborne.

The article argues that gold’s strong Friday rally lacked confirmation from silver, platinum, and mining stocks. The VanEck Junior Gold Miners ETF failed to rise meaningfully and closed below its April high for a third consecutive day, which the author sees as bearish after its late-July decline. The dollar index is said to have confirmed an inverse head-and-shoulders breakout and could rally to at least 101.3, while stocks remain below rising support despite a brief pause. The author compares the setup to 2008 and maintains the “Peak Chaos” thesis. A reader disputes the technical-analysis methods, and the page includes market-risk and data disclaimers.

Verizon and AST SpaceMobile announced a commercial agreement to provide space-based cellular broadband across the continental U.S. The author rates Verizon a “strong buy,” citing improved growth prospects and competitive positioning, while rating AST SpaceMobile a “sell” because of dilution, minimal revenue, high valuation, and speculative risk. Verizon’s outlook is described as strong.

Former Nepali prime minister K.P. Oli appeared set to return to power after winning his parliamentary seat, with his Communist UML party and Maoist allies on course for a majority. His agenda includes expanding Chinese railways, developing infrastructure and hydropower projects, creating jobs, and serving a full five-year term while balancing ties with China and India.

Brock University researchers found that rosemary extract inhibited survival and proliferation of lab-grown A549 human lung cancer cells by blocking the Akt/mTOR/p70S6K pathway and enhancing apoptosis. The study, published in *Biomedicine & Pharmacotherapy*, suggests potential anti-tumour and chemoprevention properties, but researchers say it is too early to recommend increased rosemary consumption. Further studies will examine whether carnosic acid, rosmarinic acid, or other components cause the effects.

Plans will widen the 32-mile M4 stretch between junctions 3 and 12 to four lanes in both directions and add variable speed-limit technology. The £862.4 million project starts in September and targets completion by March 2022.

A compilation of January 16–17, 2002 reports examines Enron’s collapse, its off-balance-sheet partnerships, and related scrutiny of auditors, consultants, directors, and government officials.

Enron’s planned 2000 Blockbuster venture to deliver movies over telephone lines was short-lived and had reached only a small pilot stage when the companies split. Separately, Enron created Project Braveheart, valued at $124.8 million, and recorded $110.9 million in profits from it in two quarters despite the venture generating no profit. To qualify for off-balance-sheet accounting, Enron used investments from nCube and its majority-owned SE Thunderbird partnership to create a nominal 3% outside interest. CIBC invested $115.2 million in return for 93% of Braveheart’s cash flow for ten years and a repayment guarantee. Arthur Andersen approved the structure and valuation. After the Blockbuster venture ended, Enron reversed the Braveheart gains and reported a $618 million third-quarter loss. Other partnerships were used to shift debt from Enron’s books, raise cash, and support reported earnings.

Pricewaterhouse advised on asset transfers involving the LJM partnerships, while KPMG issued independent reports on them. Three Canadian institutional investors sued investment banks and Andersen, while Deloitte’s peer review found minor shortcomings in Andersen but recommended no action. McKinsey had advised Enron for years and helped shape its diversification strategy; the firm said it was not hired to address financial reporting or off-balance-sheet financing and had not been contacted by investigators.

Enron’s board twice waived ethics rules in 1999 so CFO Andrew Fastow could manage LJM partnerships from which he earned more than $30 million. Those waivers, a $586 million earnings restatement, and 50 shareholder suits raised questions about director liability and potential cancellation of insurance coverage.

Investigators learned that whistleblower Sherron Watkins warned Kenneth Lay in August 2001 of impending accounting scandals and communicated similar concerns to Andersen. Andersen documents showed that its executives discussed Enron’s LJM transactions, conflicts of interest, aggressive structuring, and “intelligent gambling” before retaining Enron as a client. The firm also knew of Watkins’s concerns. Andersen partner David Duncan was fired for ordering the destruction of Enron-related emails and documents; he said he acted on advice from an Andersen lawyer. Congressional, Justice Department, SEC, Texas, and California inquiries examined the destruction, Enron’s accounting, and Andersen’s conduct.

SEC Chairman Harvey Pitt’s former representation of Andersen and major accounting firms prompted demands that he recuse himself, although he said he was not managing the investigation. Critics also scrutinized Enron’s political relationships with the Bush administration and Vice President Dick Cheney. White House economic advisers monitored Enron’s collapse without informing President Bush, stating that financial markets stabilized and a bailout was unnecessary.

A federal task force began examining retirement-plan security after many Enron employees lost substantial 401(k) savings. Enron Europe entered administration, and its former vice president attributed the collapse to lost confidence, counterparties, and financing while describing the core European trading business as sound. IntercontinentalExchange reported increased trading and planned clearing services to reduce counterparty risk. American Electric Power acquired Enron Nordic Energy, adding a Nordic power-trading team representing about 20% of regional trading volume.

GA10x GPUs support GDDR6X memory with data rates up to 19.5 Gbps and peak bandwidth of 936 GB/s, more than 52% above the TU102 in the GeForce RTX 2080 Ti. Its pseudo-independent memory channels support BVH ray traversal in RT Cores.

As games and creative assets exceed 200 GB and SSDs reach multi-gigabyte-per-second speeds, traditional file systems and storage APIs can leave CPUs struggling with decompression. NVIDIA RTX IO uses Microsoft DirectStorage to move compressed data directly from NVMe SSDs to the GPU, where lossless decompression offloads work that may otherwise consume dozens of CPU cores. The technology can accelerate I/O by up to 100 times versus hard drives and traditional APIs, improve frame rates and texture streaming, reduce object pop-in and stutter, and enable near-instantaneous loading. It also supports professional workflows involving large CAD, rendering, scientific, and virtual-reality datasets.

The GA10x-based NVIDIA A40 is designed for data-center visual computing. Compared with the Quadro RTX 6000, it provides up to twice the FP32 and ray-tracing throughput, up to five times the AI-training and data-science throughput, or ten times with sparsity, and twice the PCIe Gen4 bandwidth. It includes 48 GB of memory, expandable to 96 GB by linking two A40s with NVLink, three DisplayPort 1.4 outputs, vGPU support, and compatibility with NVIDIA EGX and Quadro Sync.

Ampere GPUs support 4K at 120 Hz and 8K at 60 Hz, including two 8K displays through DisplayPort 1.4a with DSC 1.2a. They are the first discrete GPUs supporting HDMI 2.1, which provides up to 48 Gbps of bandwidth and supports 8K60, 4K120, and dynamic HDR. GA10x also includes HDCP 2.3 and 1.x.

Fifth-generation NVDEC provides hardware-accelerated decoding for MPEG-2, VC-1, H.264, H.265, VP8, VP9, and AV1. GA10x GPUs were the first to offer AV1 hardware decoding; the passage reports 50–55% bitrate savings over H.264 and playback of 8K60 HDR AV1 with roughly 4% CPU usage in the cited test. Seventh-generation NVENC offloads encoding, reducing CPU usage and supporting H.264 up to 4K and HEVC up to 8K. Its quality exceeds software x264 at the Fast preset and is comparable to x264 Medium in the described streaming tests.

The GA10x Ampere architecture provides up to twice the performance of the preceding architecture in programmable shading, ray tracing, and AI. Its second-generation RT Core doubles ray-triangle intersection performance and supports motion blur and concurrent ray tracing with shading or compute. Third-generation Tensor Cores implement structural sparsity, doubling effective throughput. The GeForce RTX 3090 uses GA102 with 24 GB of GDDR6X, 10,496 CUDA cores, and 82 SMs and is described as 1.5 times faster than TITAN RTX. The GA104-based RTX 3070 exceeds the previous RTX 2080 Ti but lacks NVLink and uses GDDR6 rather than GDDR6X.

Error Detection and Replay on GA10x GDDR6X interfaces detects failed memory transmissions and retries them until successful. Repeated errors reduce useful bandwidth and create a performance plateau that indicates the memory overclock limit, although EDR cannot prevent every crash.

The RTX A6000 uses GA102 with 10,752 CUDA cores and 48 GB of GDDR6, expandable to 96 GB through NVLink. It supports hardware-accelerated motion blur and AI denoising and is positioned for large 3D scenes, rendering, engineering, and other professional workloads.

The NVIDIA publication states that the listed information is believed accurate as of its stated date, reserves the right to change specifications, disclaims warranties, and places responsibility on customers to verify product suitability for their applications.

The passage introduces COTUTOR, a generative AI educational model combining real-time signal processing, Bayesian knowledge tracing, and convex optimization to personalize instruction. Unlike LLM-based educational tools that lack an explicit model of student progress, COTUTOR continuously estimates learning states using submission and grading data, participation logs, and student queries and feedback. Its iterative process processes these signals, updates skill-mastery probabilities, predicts subsequent needs, and selects educational resources, activities, and educator interventions.

COTUTOR applies knowledge tracing to Online Judge data, using timestamps, attempts, scores, errors, resource usage, difficulty, and correctness. Exponential smoothing captures recent interaction trends, while BKT updates mastery probabilities using learning, slip, and guess rates. The model can recommend challenging tasks, review sessions, or targeted support based on current mastery.

Implemented as a copilot in My Code Weapon and Nemobot, COTUTOR provides deadline reminders, query handling, linked learning materials, and exercises tailored to mastery levels. It maintains persistent student trajectories, standardizes responses where possible, and logs outputs for instructor review to improve transparency and mitigate hallucinations.

The passage also formulates educational resource allocation as convex optimization. Across sequenced sessions, normalized allocations, budget and priority constraints, and a dependency requiring sufficient theory before application can maximize students’ terminal sentiment. COTUTOR evaluates individual and collective allocation under alternative influence functions, including linear and power models. The proposed convex formulation is presented as interpretable, globally optimal, and less computationally intensive during inference than autoregressive LLMs. Evaluation plans include educational-dataset benchmarks and a controlled classroom study; the passage reports that COTUTOR outperforms prior methods and improves real-world learning effectiveness.

News reports from November 26, 2001 focused on Enron’s financial crisis and its proposed acquisition by Dynegy. Dynegy’s all-stock offer initially valued Enron at about $9.2 billion, or $10.85 per share, while the companies continued to review Enron’s finances and pursue a merger expected to take six to nine months. ChevronTexaco, which owned 26% of Dynegy, supplied Enron with an immediate $1.5 billion cash infusion and retained rights to acquire the Northern Natural Gas pipeline if the merger failed.

Enron’s shares fell to about $4.71, prompting speculation that Dynegy might renegotiate or withdraw. The agreement included material-adverse-change provisions and litigation triggers: Dynegy could alter the transaction if Enron faced reasonably likely litigation costs of $2 billion, while costs reaching $3.5 billion would be deemed a material event allowing termination. Enron could accept a superior offer by paying a $350 million fee. Deal experts said Enron’s stock decline alone would probably not permit cancellation, and shareholder approval was still required.

Enron sought $500 million to $1 billion from outside investors, while J.P. Morgan Chase and Citigroup were expected to provide $500 million to $1 billion if an informal arrangement among Enron, Dynegy, lenders, and rating agencies remained intact. A collapse of the Dynegy deal could have triggered debt downgrades and repayments linked to Enron’s partnerships and off-balance-sheet entities.

Enron had disclosed a $1.2 billion equity charge, revised earnings dating from 1997 downward by roughly $600 million, and faced an SEC investigation into affiliated partnerships and off-balance-sheet transactions. BusinessWeek said Enron’s disclosures illustrated broader confusion surrounding corporate earnings, record write-offs, and inconsistent “pro forma,” “operating,” or “core” earnings measures. It described efforts by S&P, the SEC, the FASB, and international accounting standard setters to establish clearer rules linking standardized operating earnings to audited net income.

ChevronTexaco’s stake positioned it to become a major energy trader if the merger succeeded; it planned to invest as much as $2.5 billion to maintain its 26% ownership, and trading could exceed 10% of its earnings. California’s attorney general was examining the acquisition for antitrust issues, while state grid officials sought restrictions on market-rate electricity sales by major power sellers.

Options markets were calm after Thanksgiving, with the VIX falling to 24.79, though Enron call options traded heavily and Eli Lilly puts also attracted interest. Charles Schwab advised investors to diversify, avoid emotional decisions, and remain invested despite post-September 11 uncertainty. Other reports covered former Enron executive Rebecca Mark’s post-Enron activities, India’s Aditya Birla Group denying interest in Enron’s 65% stake in the Dabhol power project, and commentary attributing Enron’s collapse to opaque accounting, aggressive dealmaking, and insufficient scrutiny of its finances.

Jamie Dimon said AI is real, transformative and worth using, while some AI-related asset prices may be in “bubble territory.” Comparing it with the internet, he argued that the technology will probably pay off overall. Dimon warned that AI will eliminate jobs and that technological change is happening too quickly. He urged governments, businesses and society to prepare through retraining, new income models, early retirement and safety nets rather than ignore displacement. Under Dimon, JPMorgan has invested billions in AI since 2012 and has more than 2,000 AI staff. He advocated ongoing training and adaptation, thoughtful regulation and deliberate planning, while also estimating a 30% chance of a stock-market correction.

Jane Goodall, who died October 1 at 91, left a scientific legacy beyond her observations of chimpanzees at Gombe National Park. Her team collected chimps’ bodies after death, used insects to clean the remains, and preserved skeletons whose sex, age, weight, and life histories were known. This collection enables researchers to study how development and experience shape skeletal anatomy and may provide new perspectives on ancient hominid fossils. Goodall said she collected skeletons because “When you’re working in the field, you shouldn’t waste anything.” The matriarch Flo’s unusually large but light skeleton demonstrated the difficulty of estimating body weight from bone size, while her bone-loss pattern, recent motherhood, and longevity illustrated skeletal changes in aging female chimpanzees.

The patent describes multi-camera imaging systems for detecting faint objects in space or other low-light, low-contrast environments where individual cameras have insufficient signal-to-noise ratio (SNR). It is a U.S. continuation of U.S. Patent No. 11,108,941, with priority to PCT/US17/52105 and U.S. Provisional Application No. 62/396,780; the invention was made partly with government support.

Three array configurations are disclosed. A common field array positions multiple cameras so their fields of view share a region. A computing system co-registers and combines their images, increasing SNR by approximately the square root of the number of images combined. A hybrid field array uses multiple such camera arrays with partially overlapping common fields; their combined images are stitched into a composite image covering a wider field of view. An adaptive field array initially provides a broad composite field for target detection, then automatically repositions or reorients the cameras to share a field containing the detected target before co-registering and combining images.

The systems may use commodity, low-performance cameras, including raw, uncompressed image data, and can be co-located, geographically dispersed, hierarchically expanded, or divided into independently steerable sub-arrays. They offer lower camera, operating, maintenance, and environmental costs, increased effective bit depth of approximately Log₂(M) bits for M cameras, improved data for deconvolution, and reduced cosmic-ray artifacts.

Calibration includes dark-frame, flat-frame, bias-frame, barrel-distortion, and sky-field procedures. Data processing uses star matching and right-ascension/declination mapping to register images, sums registered pixel values to improve SNR, and aggregates successive images to detect streaks with methods such as the Hough transform. Streak timing and coordinates support initial orbit determination, catalog matching, and identification of uncorrelated targets. Potential uses include astrophotography, deep-space searches, satellite detection and tracking, tactical sensing, and night vision.

Researchers from the University of Washington and several companies conducted the first large-scale field test of poplar trees fortified with a naturally occurring bacterium at NASA Ames’ Middlefield-Ellis-Whisman Superfund research area. Inoculated and untreated trees were planted above TCE-contaminated groundwater. Inoculated trees grew larger and healthier within one year, remained more robust after three years, and contained greatly reduced TCE. Downstream groundwater also had lower toxin levels, while soil near the roots showed increased chloride, a byproduct of TCE degradation. The bacterium was selected from microbes isolated from poplars growing in contaminated soil because it eliminated nearly all TCE in laboratory flasks. Researchers said the approach improves phytoremediation, protects tree health and could enable faster, lower-cost cleanup of contaminated sites.
