A three-year study of 195 Ugandan health facilities found that smaller, rural, and for-profit facilities struggled to sustain HIV treatment, while funding systems favored larger, established hospitals. Key constraints included shortages and turnover of ART-skilled staff, difficulty meeting donor reporting requirements, and irregular or inadequate antiretroviral supplies; some facilities discontinued services despite outside support. Patients also favored larger hospitals, which offered more services and staff, shorter waits, and fewer stock-outs. Donor-supported treatment in some for-profit facilities attracted broader patient populations, conflicting with providers’ commercial goals. Without intervention, treatment coverage is unlikely to expand beyond established hospitals. Proposed measures include hospital–facility mentoring, government service-purchase agreements, targeted salary support, greater government financing, and expanded fiscal space to reduce unsustainable reliance on major donors.

The socket cover uses a latch and support tabs to hold the actuation lever closed after mating. Actuation/de-actuation force must be below 3.6 kgf, and package-pin displacement must remain below 1.0 mm. The socket must retain electrical and mechanical integrity after 50 actuations. Inspection criteria address solder balls, contacts, gold plating, cover/base condition, securing tabs, fit, latch, and lever integrity.

Electrical requirements include a 1.5 A per-contact rating with less than 30°C temperature rise across at least six energized rows. Initial and final LLCR must not exceed 25 mΩ per contact with Kovar pins, based on 200 daisy-chained pairs. Mated inductance must be below 4 nH for a single pin and 3 nH ±10% for two- or three-pin configurations; capacitance must be below 1 pF. Differential impedance must be 100 Ω ±10%, single-ended delay skew below 10 ps plus 3 ps measurement error, dielectric withstand at least 650 Vac, and insulation resistance at least 1000 MΩ.

Corn, also known as maize, is a heavily traded agricultural commodity. Corn futures are standardized contracts traded on CME Globex in which the seller delivers a specified quantity and quality of corn at a pre-agreed price on a future date. Settlement occurs through physical delivery, and trading terminates on the business day before the 15th of the contract month. Speculators can close or roll positions before expiry, and retail brokers commonly close positions automatically. Futures also allow farmers and other industry participants to hedge price risk.

A corn futures strategy uses technical and fundamental analysis, entry and exit signals, position sizing, and risk management. The passage cites WASDE corn-yield forecasts as an input for yield-based models and identifies seasonal patterns as a potentially promising commodity strategy. Historical data indicates that corn tends to perform better in January, February, April, May, October, November, and December than in July, August, and September. One seasonal backtest, without leverage, suffered a 70% maximum drawdown, largely because of a 2012 short position. A second seasonal strategy with a momentum filter reported an average unleveraged return of 1.13% per trade across 175 trades, a six-day average holding period, 13% market exposure, low correlation with stocks, and a worst-year loss of 7.9%. The authors note that long-lasting, consistently performing commodity strategies have been difficult to find.

Corn prices are influenced by weather in major growing regions, WASDE and other USDA production and supply reports, Chinese demand, and broader macroeconomic data. Futures are available in full and mini sizes of 5,000 and 1,000 bushels, respectively, and are quoted in U.S. cents per bushel. Minimum fluctuations are $12.50 for a full contract and $1.25 for a mini contract. Globex trading runs Sunday through Friday from 5:00 p.m. to 4:00 p.m. CT, with a daily maintenance break. CME ClearPort and Trading at Settlement have separate schedules.

The passage reports a November 24, 2022 price of 663.2 cents per bushel, equal to $33,160 for a full contract and $6,632 for a mini contract. Based on 62 years of MacroTrends data, the reported all-time high was $8.3125 in 2012 and the low was $1.007 in 1960.

Leverage is the principal cited risk: a 5% adverse move at 20x leverage could wipe out an account. The Teucrium Corn Fund (CORN) provides ETF exposure across multiple maturities. CFDs offer another way to speculate on corn prices without physical delivery or expiry, but the passage warns that most CFD traders lose money.

The Supreme Court will hear arguments Oct. 6 on whether Delaware’s “affidavit of merit” statute applies in federal court. The statute requires medical malpractice plaintiffs to establish obvious negligence or submit an affidavit from a medical professional attesting to a defendant’s negligence. Harold Berk’s Florida residency gave him federal jurisdiction over claims involving Delaware defendants, and the lower courts dismissed his case without the required affidavit, treating the statute as substantive under the Erie doctrine.

Choy and Beebe argue that the statute does not conflict with federal pleading rules, which permit statutes to impose additional verification requirements, and that applying it would serve states’ efforts to reduce malpractice litigation costs. A professors’ amicus brief contends that state statutes altering malpractice pleading requirements should not govern federal procedure. The author expects a closely contested argument.

The President reports an emergency arising from South Carolina’s November 1832 ordinance, which declared federal tariff acts of 1828 and 1832 and other revenue laws unconstitutional and void within the state, prohibited their enforcement after February 1, and threatened separation from the Union if the federal government used military or naval force.

South Carolina’s legislature adopted measures to enforce the ordinance through state courts and penalties, required officials and jurors to swear allegiance to it, and empowered the governor to resist federal coercion. The governor sought authorization for thousands of volunteers and militia forces, while proclamations and military preparations signaled an organized effort to obstruct federal customs officers. The President maintained that South Carolina had not exhausted constitutional remedies through courts, public opinion, or amendments and had no justification for revolutionary separation from the Union.

The President reported that existing federal enforcement measures were inadequate. Treasury officials had instructed customs collectors to perform their duties, and the Charleston customhouse had been moved to Castle Pinckney, but other ports remained vulnerable. South Carolina’s replevin and distress procedures, supported by the posse comitatus, could overpower federal officers and potentially cause violence, making collection through ordinary courts impracticable.

The President recommended that Congress authorize the President to relocate or abolish obstructed ports of entry, establish secure customhouses, detain vessels and cargoes until duties were paid or secured, and use land and naval forces and militia when necessary. He also recommended restoring procedures allowing removal of federal-law cases from state courts, providing federal remedies for injuries to federal officers and citizens, protecting federal prisoners, and modifying existing law to permit military enforcement where federal laws were openly obstructed. The message urged Congress to act while preserving the Constitution, the supremacy of federal law, and the Union.

The study evaluated the Karius Test, an unbiased plasma microbial cell-free DNA sequencing assay, in a commercial laboratory cohort across 39 U.S. states and the District of Columbia from April 2018 through September 2021. Among 19,739 eligible samples from 16,172 hospitalized patients, median turnaround was 26 hours and 96% produced valid results. The assay uses proprietary enrichment and analytical methods to detect and quantify bacteria, DNA viruses, fungi, and parasites, reporting concentrations as molecules per microliter (MPM). Most orders came from infectious-disease and hematology/oncology providers.

Among analyzed reports, 42% identified no pathogens and 58% identified at least one. Positive reports represented 8,849 patients and included 22,792 detections across 701 taxa: 526 bacterial, 103 fungal, 47 viral, and 24 parasitic taxa. The top 50 taxa, which accounted for 69% of detections, included both common commensal/environmental organisms and clinically important viruses and fungi. Quality-control metrics for quantification were met in 90% of positive samples. The test also detected uncommon or diagnostically challenging organisms, including Legionella, Nocardia, Mycobacterium, systemic dimorphic fungi, zoonotic bacteria, and protozoan and helminthic parasites. Species-level analyses documented multiple detections within several bacterial genera and occasional co-detections at similar MPM levels.

The authors concluded that the test’s performance was consistent with its initial validation and that it could operate reliably at scale. However, the 58% positivity rate was below rates reported in selected clinical populations, reinforcing the need for diagnostic stewardship and population-specific interpretation. MPM values are influenced by microbial and patient factors, and thresholds for definite infection have not been established. Study limitations included unavailable orthogonal testing and treatment data, clinical context for only 29% of patients, and insufficient data structure to analyze repeated testing or changes in the bioinformatics pipeline. The study was supported by Karius, with two authors serving as uncompensated consultants.

Coach Julien said his team forced overtime but lost after an average performance. He cited poor decision-making, inadequate puck movement, weak defensive coverage, unaggressive play through the neutral zone, and a game plan opened too much in an effort to score. Although the team rallied, it also conceded too many opportunities, including the game-winning goal. Players became frustrated and focused on officiating rather than their game, and Julien assessed the entire team as average.

He praised the team’s effort, including strong performances from Patrice Bergeron and Jaromir Jagr, whose line develops chemistry through consistent play together. He also praised Johnny for his offensive production, tying goal, shot, and overall playoff performance. Despite the loss, Julien viewed the series as tight and said the team must improve and move on immediately.

The coach emphasized focusing only on the next game rather than momentum, previous results, or future opponents. He said roster and line-up decisions should serve that immediate goal, even if players must be rested or moved. He also described the importance of honest communication between coaches and players and praised a veteran player’s conditioning habits and willingness to put in extra work.

Chicago’s strong forechecking and positioning in shooting lanes were identified as reasons his team needed smarter puck decisions. Julien said scoring chances were present for both sides and did not place excessive emphasis on shot totals.

He praised players’ ability and willingness to perform different roles, including penalty killing, power play work, faceoffs, and replacing an injured Greg Campbell. Role players’ pride, versatility, vision, and ability to create power-play opportunities were described as important assets for the club.

NVIDIA filed an unaudited Form 10-Q for the first quarter of fiscal 2020, ended April 28, 2019. Revenue was $2.22 billion, down 31% year over year, with gross margin declining to 58.4% from 64.5%. Operating expenses rose 21% to $938 million, operating income fell 72% to $358 million, and net income declined 68% to $394 million. Diluted earnings per share were $0.64, compared with $1.98.

GPU revenue decreased 27% to $2.02 billion, while Tegra Processor revenue fell 55% to $198 million. Gaming revenue declined 39% to $1.05 billion, data center revenue fell 10% to $634 million, and OEM and other revenue dropped 74% to $99 million. Professional visualization revenue increased 6% to $266 million, and automotive revenue rose 14% to $166 million.

Cash, cash equivalents, and marketable securities totaled $7.80 billion, up from $7.42 billion at fiscal year-end. NVIDIA paid $97 million in dividends, made no first-quarter share repurchases, and intended to return the remaining $2.20 billion of its planned $3 billion fiscal 2020 shareholder return through repurchases and dividends.

NVIDIA agreed to acquire Mellanox Technologies for $125 per share in cash, representing an enterprise value of approximately $6.9 billion. The transaction required shareholder and regulatory approvals and could trigger a $350 million termination fee under specified circumstances.

The company adopted a new lease accounting standard, recognizing $470 million of lease assets and $500 million of lease liabilities. It also disclosed stock-based compensation of $178 million, $2.27 billion of unearned compensation, securities and derivative litigation, and risks associated with completing and integrating the Mellanox acquisition. Management concluded disclosure controls were effective, with no material changes in internal financial reporting controls.

This pilot study investigated whether a convolutional neural network (CNN) can identify benign or malignant thyroid nodules from ultrasound images, potentially supporting radiologists and reducing reliance on invasive fine-needle aspiration and time-consuming expert interpretation. The study used the 2015 Thyroid Digital Image Database from Universidad Nacional de Colombia. TI-RADS categories TR2–TR3 were treated as benign and TR4–TR5 as malignant.

Images were normalized, divided into training, testing, and validation sets, and expanded through rotation, shifting, and flipping; noise and blur augmentation were excluded. Early stopping and learning-rate reductions were used to limit overfitting. Because malignant images were approximately four times more numerous, class weights favored benign cases fourfold. The binary classifier combined pretrained VGG16 and Inception v3 networks and used binary cross-entropy with sigmoid output. It was trained for 10 epochs with a batch size of 8.

The hybrid model achieved 87.5% accuracy and an AUROC of 0.929. The authors attributed its performance to the combined image-analysis capabilities of VGG16 and Inception v3, pretrained weights, and measures addressing class imbalance. They identified the small, skewed dataset as the main limitation, noting that the model could still favor the majority class. A larger clinical dataset and the inclusion of normal thyroid images were recommended to improve reliability.

India’s Congress Party elected Rahul Gandhi unopposed as president, succeeding his mother, Sonia Gandhi, who has led since 1998. The 47-year-old great-grandson of Jawaharlal Nehru aims to revive Congress after its 2014 election defeat and weak local results while challenging Prime Minister Narendra Modi. His appointment coincided with Gujarat state polls, seen as a test for Modi amid criticism of economic growth and sales-tax implementation. Despite Congress’s hopes, a Pew survey found Modi remained highly popular, with a favorability rating 30 points above Gandhi’s.

Hiscox’s 2016 survey of over 4,000 small and medium-sized businesses found U.S. entrepreneurs most motivated by flexible hours, greater control and remote work—not higher income. Despite taking few vacations, 70% reported revenue growth, 68% profit growth and 73% growth in new customers. U.S. owners showed strong hiring optimism, though 61% lacked succession plans. Funding remained a growing challenge, prompting some businesses to use personal credit, venture capital and peer-to-peer lending. Oregon offers state-backed loan, guarantee and capital-access programs for businesses unable to obtain traditional financing. Only 34% of U.S. owners believed government policies supported entrepreneurs, while 31% cited political instability as harmful. Forbes ranked Bend first among small business climates and highlighted its leading U.S. job-growth rate. Overall, American entrepreneurship reflected cautious optimism, with Oregon experiencing strong job gains, rising wages and near-full employment, though funding, policy and political risks remained.

Interest rates and stocks are generally viewed as inversely related, and the S&P 500 often reacts before rate changes affect the broader economy. Yet their correlation has grown more positive since the 2000s, so rising rates do not always mean falling share prices. A dividend-unadjusted S&P 500 backtest based on an SMA versus the 10-year yield yielded poor compounded returns when holding stocks as rates rose. Holding stocks while rates fell dramatically improved CAGR, slightly reduced market exposure, and left drawdown largely unchanged. The strategy performed better before the 1990s than in the 2000s and 2010s, when quantitative easing occurred.

President Barack Obama will deliver a Jan. 10 farewell address in Chicago, thanking supporters, reflecting on his eight years in office and offering thoughts on the country’s future. Donald Trump will be sworn in Jan. 20; despite major policy differences, Obama has sought a smooth transition of power.

Apple Watch Series 3’s LTE model continues a sluggish international rollout while helping Apple consolidate its dominance in the stagnant wearable market. May 4 pre-orders are planned for Denmark, Sweden and India, with deliveries a week later; pricing remains unannounced.

IFC Films promoted Mark Boxer to executive vice president of sales and distribution and Lauren Schwartz to senior vice president of publicity and promotions. Boxer oversees theatrical, non-theatrical and Canadian distribution, while Schwartz leads campaigns for films including “45 Years” and “Finding Vivian Maier.”

Nearly nine months after the Palisades fire, Marquez Charter Elementary reopened on a temporary campus, becoming the first public school to return to a campus destroyed by the Palisades and Eaton fires. The site has 19 classrooms, a kitchen, library and play areas. Enrollment has fallen about 58%, from 310 to 130 students, and LAUSD estimates three-quarters no longer live in the Palisades.

LAUSD cited parent surveys and town halls in deciding to reopen Marquez before other affected campuses. Transportation, student relocation timing, environmental concerns and commutes influenced families’ preferences. The district estimates Marquez’s temporary campus and rebuild will cost $202.6 million and be completed by 2028, while rebuilding three damaged Los Angeles campuses will cost about $600 million.

Pasadena Unified, the hardest-hit district, installed portable classrooms at five campuses but has no timeline for rebuilding them.

The MMA Manifesto’s middleweight rankings, voted by Jeff Fox, Ryan MacDonald, Ricky Leone, and Daniel Vreeland, exclude suspended fighters and those inactive for at least 12 months without a scheduled fight. Michael Bisping leads as UFC middleweight champion with 39 points, followed by Luke Rockhold (35), Yoel Romero (34), Chris Weidman and Ronaldo “Jacare” Souza (25 each), Gegard Mousasi (20), Robert Whittaker (13), Anderson Silva (12), Vitor Belfort (9), and Kelvin Gastelum (5). Belfort and Gastelum are scheduled to fight March 11.

This study examines the scholarly landscape of open education and its implications for equitable access. Open education includes open educational resources (OER), massive open online courses (MOOCs), open textbooks, open-access journals, and open educational practices (OEP), with the aim of making education accessible, affordable, inclusive, and collaborative. Although the field is expanding rapidly, research remains fragmented across individual components. Persistent barriers include digital and infrastructure inequalities, inadequate accessibility standards, limited awareness, faculty resistance, insufficient training, weak institutional support, and challenges of scalability and sustainability.

The study asks which trends and emerging areas characterize open education and how findings can inform policy and practice. After reviewing research on pedagogical innovation, learner engagement, quality assurance, sustainability, social justice, localization, and global access, it applies bibliometric analysis to the broader field. In September 2023, the authors searched Web of Science using “Open Education” in the topic field across all research areas and document types. After multiple-reviewer screening and a pilot analysis, they retained 402 English-language, peer-reviewed or formally reviewed publications and analyzed them with VOSviewer 1.6.18.

The 402 publications received 3,041 citations, including 329 self-citations, with 7.56 citations per article and an H-index of 27. No eligible publications appeared before 2015; output grew from 2016, reaching 82 publications in 2020 before falling to 56 in 2021.

Co-citation analysis identified five thematic clusters: Evolving Open Education (17 publications), OER’s Role in Education (16), Adoption of Open Education (9), Educational Paradigms of MOOCs (8), and Implementation of OEP (7). Collectively, these clusters trace a shift from providing access toward pedagogy, technology, and social justice, while identifying limited empirical implementation, institutional and cultural barriers, weak scalability and sustainability, MOOC dropout and engagement problems, and insufficient evidence of long-term outcomes.

Co-word analysis found 49 keywords and five clusters: blended learning in open education, openness during the COVID-19 era, challenges of OER adoption, inclusive digital pedagogy, and collaborative online academia. Emerging research directions include scalable and quality-assured blended and MOOC models, sustaining post-pandemic openness, funding and incentives for OER adoption, equitable digital pedagogy, and ICT-supported collaboration despite infrastructure constraints.

The findings portray open education as dynamic and dependent on integrating pedagogy, technology, and social justice. OER can reduce costs, expand flexible and personalized learning, and improve participation and outcomes, but successful adoption requires faculty development, institutional incentives, supportive policies, and adaptation to local contexts. Limitations include reliance on Web of Science, subjective cluster interpretation and thresholds, and incomplete representation of regional and institutional variation. Future research should incorporate additional databases, combine bibliometric analysis with qualitative perspectives, examine contextual differences in adoption, and investigate open education’s potential challenges and drawbacks.

The OHL strategy is an intraday trading approach that uses the opening, high, and low prices from the first few minutes of a session to identify trade entries. A buy signal occurs when the open equals the low, suggesting bullish sentiment, while a sell signal occurs when the open equals the high, suggesting bearish sentiment. It is best suited to low timeframes such as 1-, 5-, or at most 15-minute charts. Some traders modify the strategy by requiring OHL buy signals above central pivot range levels and sell signals below them.

Backtests on the S&P 500 and ES futures produced 1,401 trades with an average gain of 0.04%. The average rose to 0.06% when the day opened above the previous close and fell to 0.01% when it opened below. A WTI crude oil test under specified conditions produced an average gain of 0.12%. Reversed trading rules averaged 0.00% for SPY and WTI, though results varied by the opening price relative to the previous close. The article concludes that the first minutes may have some predictive value, but the tests were simple, the S&P results were not considered tradable, and further development and backtesting were needed.

The paper introduces a neural solver combining physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) with isogeometric analysis (IGA) to address PINN difficulties on complex, multi-patch computer-aided design (CAD) geometries. Its three main targets are maintaining solution continuity across patch interfaces, strongly imposing Dirichlet boundary conditions, and normalizing neural-network inputs despite large variations in physical geometry.

For elliptic boundary-value problems, the method uses a variational PINN framework in which feedforward neural networks approximate the solution by minimizing a discretized energy functional through gradient-based optimization. Multi-patch geometry is represented by NURBS mappings from common reference domains to physical subdomains. Patch-specific neural ansatz functions operate in these reference domains, and their solutions are pushforwarded to the physical geometry.

Each patch ansatz combines an interior term with interface-conforming terms. The interior term uses a neural-network output multiplied by polynomials that vanish on Dirichlet boundaries and patch interfaces, together with a term that imposes prescribed boundary data. A custom output layer with a residual connection strongly enforces Dirichlet conditions. Interface-specific neural networks connect neighboring patch solutions, while multi-indices accommodate intersections involving surfaces, curves, points, and three or more patches. These constructions ensure differentiability within patches, \(C^0\) continuity across interfaces, and natural input normalization on reference domains.

The approach draws on finite-element tearing and interconnecting methods, their IGA extension, and mortaring methods. It is demonstrated on a two-dimensional magnetostatics model of a quadrupole magnet and a three-dimensional nonlinear solid-mechanics model of a mechanical holder with hyperelastic behavior, contact conditions, and parametric dependencies. Prior combinations of PINNs, neural networks, and IGA largely address single-patch geometries or weakly impose interface and boundary conditions, whereas the presented solver uses interface-specific networks and strong boundary enforcement for multi-patch CAD domains.

Owen Sound Foodland is among 87 new stores approved to sell beer and cider beginning in April. Its 34,000-square-foot replacement store, tentatively opening March 22, will feature fresh foods, expanded services and a seating area while retaining traditional departments. Employment will increase from 100 to about 160.

Machine-learning force fields provide a faster alternative to costly first-principles calculations, but graph-based architectures face challenges for point defects, including oversmoothing, limited treatment of non-local interactions, high computational demands, and substantial data requirements. The passage introduces ADAPT, a coordinate-based Transformer that applies attention over all possible atomic interactions to predict per-atom forces and structure energies from Cartesian coordinates and atomic features. ADAPT uses separate force and energy networks, represents each atom as a token with 12 descriptors, and avoids graph-based inductive biases. Trained on DFT data for primarily complex silicon defects, it reports state-of-the-art energy and force performance, outperforming MACE and MatterSim, with training costs two orders of magnitude below message-passing architectures.

Nearly 88% of Irish quoted companies met or beat earnings expectations, while a review of 33 companies found average EPS growth of 8%. Aryzta, Ryanair, Tullow Oil and IFG Group missed forecasts. The Iseq reached a 15-month high, 6% above its pre-Brexit level, despite investor concerns. Irish Continental led the Iseq 10, while Aryzta fell furthest.

This descriptive survey examined Turkish parents’ experiences, criticisms, and suggestions regarding compulsory emergency distance education during the COVID-19 pandemic. Data were collected from 2,371 parents across 12 regions using a 16-question survey and analyzed with descriptive statistics and content analysis.

While 57.7% of parents expressed positive views of distance education, 42.3% were negative. Positive aspects included maintaining education, protecting health, and enabling flexible learning, while criticisms concerned inadequate content, difficult adaptation and learning, short lesson durations, lack of interaction, technical problems, and unequal access. Most parents rejected fully replacing face-to-face education with distance learning, although they supported its continued use alongside classroom instruction.

Major reported concerns included students’ adaptation, motivation, time management, self-discipline, limited technological access, infrastructure and internet problems, insufficient educational content, and inadequate psychological and technical support. WhatsApp was the leading parent-teacher communication channel. Parents suggested distance examinations, continued distance-learning support, richer materials, and longer courses. Recommendations included improving affordable internet and device access, reducing the digital divide, expanding open educational resources, and strengthening digital literacy for families, teachers, and students.

The Tigers’ closer-by-committee approach has not worked well, and they could pursue two-time All-Star closer Raisel Iglesias in free agency if he opts out. Iglesias posted a 2.97 ERA, 75 strikeouts, a 0.904 WHIP and 40 saves in 70 appearances and could provide Detroit a dedicated closer following Tarik Skubal.

Taiwan’s Executive Yuan plans to merge the Mongolian and Tibetan Affairs Commission with the Ministry of Culture and the Mainland Affairs Council by year-end, closing the century-old agency. Six of its 49 employees will transfer to the council; others will continue Mongolian and Tibetan affairs under the ministry. The Executive Yuan will seek repeal of the commission’s authorizing act next session but may close it first. Pan-green lawmakers largely welcomed the decision, though Tsai Yi-yu opposed absorbing part of the commission into the council.

The speaker reflects on a team’s growth, collective responsibility, and pride in playing tough, disciplined hockey despite losing. The game was decided by small margins, including a near goal and accidental contact that could have changed the outcome.

Manchester United midfielder Marouane Fellaini has been urged by Jose Mourinho to sign a new contract while a knee injury could keep him out for up to two months. He will miss Huddersfield, undergo further tests, and risks missing both Champions League matches against Sevilla. He has missed 20 games this season.

Renewable energy fluctuations create grid-balancing challenges because excess generation must be consumed immediately, while backup plants remain available for shortages and surpluses. Prof. Mahesh Bandi combined turbulence theory with wind-plant data to show that wind-power fluctuations follow the same spectral pattern as wind-speed fluctuations for a different reason than the power-speed cubed relationship. Spatial and temporal measurements of turbulence are fundamentally different, and turbines within the same large-scale eddies exhibit correlated power output. Geographic smoothing averages fluctuations only at high frequencies; at low frequencies, dispersed plants can generate simultaneous surges that cannot be averaged out. Data from Texas and Ireland confirmed this natural limit, which has implications for estimating backup capacity, reducing reserve-related emissions and costs, and selecting optimal regional combinations of renewable sources.

Merger arbitrage seeks profits from the spread between a target company’s share price and an acquisition offer. Investors typically buy the target and hold until the deal closes, when the price is expected to converge with the offer, but risk substantial losses if the deal fails. Effective execution requires assessing completion odds, regulatory hurdles, deal terms, market conditions, liquidity, and continuously monitoring developments.

Backtests showed lower volatility than the S&P 500 but substantially lower returns. The IQ Merger Arbitrage ETF returned a 2.73% CAGR versus 18.52% for the S&P 500, with volatility of 7.83 versus 17.27. The Merger Fund returned 4.46% versus 17.37%, with volatility of 3.81 versus 17.29.

Verdad Research studied 835 deals from 2000–2020 by buying targets five days after announcement and, for stock-financed deals, shorting acquirers. Eighty-nine percent closed successfully. Successful deals averaged 2.0% returns, canceled deals lost 2.8%, and the blended return was 1.5%. Long-target positions drove completed-deal returns, while acquirer shorts reduced returns but mitigated losses in failed deals. Disciplined merger arbitrage may offer uncorrelated returns, but requires extensive research and is difficult to execute qualitatively.

Oxygen-containing rare-earth hydride (REHO) films exhibit color-neutral photochromism, remaining largely transparent in the visible and near-infrared while losing almost 50% of their transmittance without a pronounced absorption band. This makes them promising for smart-window applications. REHO films are commonly fabricated by magnetron sputtering, and their microstructure, composition, and optical properties depend on deposition conditions. Photchromism is stronger in thicker films and occurs under varied environments and illumination conditions.

Although REHO has been described as a single-phase oxyhydride, studies indicate a multiphase structure containing O-rich and H-rich regions, with hydrogen migration implicated in photochromism. During blue-light illumination of YHO, optical transmittance changes rapidly during the first 2–3 minutes, with approximately 30% of the change occurring in this period, followed by slower darkening. Standard zero-, first-, and second-order reaction models do not adequately describe this behavior.

Electron energy-loss spectroscopy found plasmon peaks at 14.4 eV for photochromic YHO and 15.9 eV for opaque, inherently non-photochromic YHO, suggesting that photochromic films contain more free or potentially mobile hydrogen. Such hydrogen may reside at grain boundaries and micropores and facilitate light-induced migration.

A two-phase exponential model incorporating hydrogen transfer and a constant fraction of photo-inactive material fits the observations substantially better than a single-phase model. The fast component, with a rate constant of 0.016 s⁻¹, is associated with a local light-driven process and possibly rapid loss of loosely bound hydrogen. The slow component, with a rate constant of 0.001 s⁻¹, is attributed to hydrogen migration or diffusion between domains, accompanied by gradual lattice contraction that continued for at least 2–3 hours. Microstructural tuning may therefore enable control of the two processes and optimization of photochromic performance.

YHO films were prepared by reactive magnetron sputtering and oxidized in air. Transmittance was measured from 500–900 nm under illumination from a 405 nm LED. The exact origins of the two processes remain unresolved, but the model describes the experimental data well.

On January 26, 2022, Tesla, Inc. reported releasing its financial results for the fiscal quarter and year ended December 31, 2021, through its Fourth Quarter and Full Year 2021 Update posted on its website. The update was attached as Exhibit 99.1 and furnished, rather than filed, under Item 2.02. The report was signed by Chief Financial Officer Zachary J. Kirkhorn.

Congress failed to avert a federal government shutdown after a temporary funding measure expired, pausing operations from midnight Wednesday. Most schools face little immediate disruption, and the Education Department said Title I and special education funding would continue as expected. However, about 1,100 districts serving roughly eight million students, particularly those near military installations or national parks, could face cash-flow problems. A prolonged shutdown could disrupt Head Start, school nutrition, WIC, and other programs. Six Head Start grantees serving about 6,500 children expected new funding, while more could be affected after Nov. 1. USDA funds were available for September and October school meals, and SNAP was expected to continue if the shutdown lasted no more than a week. Essential Education Department staff would remain, but civil-rights investigations, regulatory work, and grant assistance would pause. Trump said more government programs could be eliminated during the shutdown, while the Office of Management and Budget asked agencies to consider additional mass layoffs, prompting a union lawsuit.

Chicago wheat rose 0.9% to $4.54-3/4 a bushel, recovering part of its biggest three-session decline since April 2013 (down 7.8% over three days), after a winter storm brought about an inch of moisture to drought-hit southern Plains hard red winter wheat in Kansas, Nebraska and northern Colorado. Corn edged up 0.1% at $3.75-1/2, ending a four-session losing streak, and soybeans gained 0.2% to $10.25. The USDA rated 11% of Kansas winter wheat good-to-excellent, down from 12%, with Texas also declining. Ukrainian winter grain was mostly good or satisfactory as of March 18; Argentine rains pressured corn; and Australian wheat was offered at $306 a tonne in Iraq's tender. CME's new cash-settled Black Sea grain futures drew active trading. Oil and Asian shares fell amid tech stock concerns over Facebook data.

Arkansas Gov. Asa Hutchinson’s son, William Asa Hutchinson III, was arrested on DWI, speeding and implied-consent charges and released on bond. A prior DWI conviction was dismissed over citation errors.

U.S. billionaire Paul Kazarian, whose firm Japonica Partners became a major Greek bondholder, opened his first European office in Lisbon and is seeking Portuguese investments in real estate and technology. He praised the recovery policies of Portugal and Greece’s Socialist-led governments, highlighting Portugal’s strong growth and exit from its bailout. Kazarian sees opportunities in Portuguese companies that can expand beyond former Portuguese colonies into global markets.

This study examines degradation of commercial NMC/graphite 3032 coin cells (200 mAh nominal) under high C-rate cycling, using X-ray diffraction (XRD), scanning electron microscopy (SEM) with energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDS), and lithium Nuclear Reaction Analysis (Li-NRA), a mostly non-destructive method for direct lithium quantification via the ⁷Li(p,γ)⁸Be reaction.

Cells were cycled 278 times between 2.7 and 4.3 V at 25 °C: 11 cycles at 1C (200 mA), 67 at 2C (400 mA), and 200 at 3C (600 mA). At 1C the cell charged to 206.50 mAh and retained 207.06 mAh (~100.3% retention). At 2C, capacity fell from 148.97 mAh to 132.84 mAh (0.24 mAh/cycle, 89.2% retention). At 3C, capacity declined from 82.16 mAh to 42.67 mAh (0.19 mAh/cycle, 51.9% retention), with roughly 60.19% loss. Average coulombic efficiency remained near 99.8–99.9% across rates, while internal resistance was ~0.32 Ω at 1C, dropped to 0.22 Ω at 2C, and rose from 0.23 Ω to ~0.34 Ω over the 3C stage, indicating progressive interfacial degradation.

XRD showed the NMC cathode (rhombohedral, R-3m) c-lattice parameter contracting from 14.27878 Å to 14.27442 Å, a (003) peak shift to lower 2θ, and reduced peak intensities suggesting structural degradation and possible lattice collapse. Graphite (hcp, 194:P63/mmc) showed c-parameter expansion from 6.71906 Å to 6.72132 Å, a strengthened 43.3° peak attributed to Cu (111) or metallic lithium, and peak splitting near 74.3°.

SEM revealed surface decomposition products and micro-cavities on the cycled cathode (with ~2.7 at.% oxygen increase) and a rougher, cracked, exfoliated graphite surface with SEI formation. EDS gave cathode density decreasing from 4.624 to 4.20 g/cm³ and anode density rising from 1.99 to 2.03 g/cm³, consistent with surface layer growth and lithium accumulation.

Li-NRA quantified a cathode bulk lithium loss of 1.86×10²² atoms/cm³ and a corresponding anode gain of 1.38×10²² atoms/cm³ (~19.7% loss and 115.96% gain), with reduced lithium penetration depth in the dense anode and deeper penetration in the cathode. The authors conclude that high C-rate cycling accelerates Ni-rich NMC degradation, that lithium plating on graphite is the main anode aging mechanism, and that Li-NRA enables quantitative lithium depth profiling to diagnose degradation pathways. Future work will compare charged and discharged states at different C-rates. Funding was provided by the NYS Center for Advanced Technology in Nanomaterials and Nanoelectronics (CATN2); ChatGPT was used for grammar and readability improvements.

The Education Department will convene special committees to rewrite the Obama-era Borrower Defense to Repayment and Gainful Employment regulations, with hearings set for July, following Education Secretary Betsy DeVos's claim that the rules are "overly burdensome and confusing." DeVos said nearly 16,000 pending defense claims will be fulfilled. Eight states and the District of Columbia filed a federal court motion seeking to retain the rules, arguing they protect borrowers from misleading and predatory practices by postsecondary institutions. Consumer advocates Rohit Chopra and Betsy Mayotte criticized the change as leaving students with unaffordable debt and costs shifted to taxpayers, while Career Education Colleges and Universities CEO Steve Gunderson said the changes would protect students from fraud and shield schools from ideologically driven efforts against career education.

T-bills traded slightly bullish, with shorter maturities favored as N300bn bond-maturity inflows boosted liquidity. The CBN’s N49.60bn PMA attracted N103.40bn in bids. OBB and OVN rates fell to 1.75% and 2.50%, while interbank rates stayed at N305.95/$. The naira weakened amid dollar shortages and CBN intervention, while long-dated sovereign bonds declined.

The Panthers gave Kawann Short a five-year, $80 million extension, avoiding the franchise tag after a yearlong negotiation. The deal supports general manager Dave Gettleman’s win-now roster approach, alongside the return of Julius Peppers and additions of Mike Adams and Captain Munnerlyn; the projected base defense averages 29.45 years old. Quarterback Cam Newton remains a major concern following shoulder surgery and previous injuries, while Carolina has replaced Ted Ginn Jr. and Philly Brown and signed Matt Kalil to a five-year, $55 million deal. With Short secured, the Panthers’ next major move is expected to be selecting an offensive playmaker with the No. 8 pick, with Leonard Fournette, Christian McCaffrey and O.J. Howard atop their board.

The University of Calgary Chess Club will host the annual Battle of Alberta tournament Feb. 18–19, with 30–40 provincial players competing under World Chess Federation rules. The event is open to students and independents, with fees of $10 and $15, respectively.

The disclosure, a continuation of U.S. patent application Ser. No. 17/809,484 with priority to Provisional Patent Application No. 63/223,045, describes methods, systems, and hardware for a cache-coherent switch-on-chip using the Compute Express Link (CXL) protocol. The switch connects processors, accelerators, memory, persistent memory, storage, network interfaces, ASICs, and other resources through PCI/CXL ports, switched fabric, processing cores, and virtual hierarchies. It provides low-latency coherent caching and memory access, routes component traffic without CPU mediation, and supports multi-host resource sharing, disaggregated and composable servers, and on-demand allocation of pooled resources. Cache hierarchies can prioritize component caches, while SR2MR and SLD2MLD bridges support legacy devices and resource isolation.

Fabric managers detect connected devices, assign them to virtual hierarchies and ports, manage hot-plug operations, inventories, traffic routing, and resource allocation. Embodiments provide memory expansion beyond CPU socket limits, use local DRAM as a buffer for remote persistent memory, and employ AI/ML prefetching to predict future memory accesses. CXL traffic can be tunneled over Ethernet between servers, racks, or data centers, enabling shared memory and accelerators and direct transfers between network interfaces and accelerator memory. Coherency may be resolved by a CPU, home agent, or the switch’s processing core. One method exchanges bias-change and line-resolved messages among the switch, accelerator, CPU, and network interface so coherent data can be written into accelerator cache memory.

Additional embodiments integrate compression, decompression, encryption, erasure coding for redundant storage, computational storage services, chiplets, and a CXL-to-Ethernet bridge. The disclosure also describes CXL packet and frame formats and software stacks involving Ethernet, RoCE, MPLS, IPsec, TCP, UDP, and SSL.

Sugar futures are legally binding contracts to receive or deliver a specified quantity of sugar at a future date and pre-agreed price. They trade on ICE Futures US as Sugar No. 11 (SB) and CME Globex as YO, with 112,000 pounds per contract, a $11.20 tick, and March, May, July, and October contracts. ICE contracts are physically settled, while CME contracts are financially settled. Traders can speculate, diversify into soft commodities, or hedge price exposure through futures or CFDs.

Successful trading requires a backtested strategy incorporating technical and fundamental analysis, entry and exit rules, position sizing, and risk management. An ATR channel-breakout strategy based on the Turtle trading system showed a low win rate but positive, trend-following results in an unleveraged sugar backtest, with small gains offset by a few large winners. Sugar futures have historically performed better in February, June, July, November, and December.

Key price drivers include supply and inventories, government subsidies and tariffs, ethanol demand and oil prices, Brazil’s currency, weather, the US dollar, geopolitics, and regulations. The greatest trading risk is leveraged adverse price movement, which can rapidly produce losses exceeding the posted margin.

On December 14, 2022, SB traded at 19.69 US cents per pound and YO at $0.1976 per pound, making one contract worth about $22,131.20. The reported all-time high was 66 cents in November 1974, and the low was 2.63 cents in June 1985.

Prime Day offers at least $200 off all current MacBooks, making the $800 13-inch M4 MacBook Air the best percentage deal. With 16 GB of RAM, 256 GB of storage, strong performance, and long battery life, it is recommended for most buyers. The $600 M1 MacBook Air remains a budget option, though a rumored replacement may improve its design and ports. MacBook Pro discounts are smaller, around 10–13 percent, and an M5 Pro model may launch soon. The M4 Pro and M4 Max are praised as powerful, but buyers seeking maximum performance may prefer to wait for the M5 generation.

The Supreme Court appeared ready to allow police broader discretion to enter a home without a warrant when responding to an emergency. In William Case’s challenge to his 2021 shooting by Montana officers, police entered his Anaconda home after his former girlfriend reported threats of suicide and harm against officers. Officers saw what they believed was a suicide note and an empty holster, then entered about 40 minutes later. One officer saw an object at Case’s waist that he believed was a gun and shot Case in the abdomen.

Case sought to suppress evidence from the warrantless entry, arguing police needed probable cause to believe someone inside was seriously injured or imminently threatened. Montana and the federal government argued that an “objectively reasonable” belief that emergency aid was needed was sufficient.

Several justices expressed concern that probable cause, a standard tied to criminal investigations, was inappropriate for emergency-aid decisions and warned that a stricter rule could discourage officers from helping people in crisis. The justices broadly favored greater latitude for police, but debated whether to apply the objectively reasonable standard on remand or establish the governing test. A decision was expected by late June or early July 2025.

Thomas Jefferson issued a proclamation on November 27, 1806, reporting a conspiracy by U.S. citizens and residents to prepare a military expedition against Spain’s dominions. He warned deceived citizens to withdraw, ordered participants to cease, directed officials to investigate and punish offenders, and urged citizens to assist authorities.

Microsoft Corporation’s Form 10-Q for the quarter ended September 30, 2019 presents unaudited interim financial statements prepared under U.S. GAAP. Microsoft was a large accelerated filer and reported 7,628,805,618 common shares outstanding as of October 18, 2019. Deloitte reviewed the interim information and noted no material modifications.

For the first quarter of fiscal 2020, revenue was $33.055 billion, up 14% from $29.084 billion a year earlier. Product revenue declined to $15.768 billion, while service and other revenue rose to $17.287 billion. Gross margin increased 18% to $22.649 billion, operating income increased 27% to $12.686 billion, and net income increased 21% to $10.678 billion. Diluted earnings per share were $1.38, compared with $1.14. Operating cash flow was $13.818 billion, investing activities used $1.776 billion, and financing activities used $10.209 billion.

As of September 30, 2019, cash, cash equivalents, and short-term investments totaled $136.636 billion. Total assets were $278.955 billion, total liabilities were $172.894 billion, and stockholders’ equity was $106.061 billion. During the quarter, Microsoft used $4.912 billion for common-stock repurchases, paid $3.510 billion in dividends, and repaid $2.5 billion of debt.

The notes described $131.911 billion of debt investments, $2.684 billion of equity investments, derivative activities for foreign-exchange, interest-rate, equity, and credit risks, and total debt of $69.495 billion. Kano Pillars drew 1–1 with Niger Tornadoes in a rescheduled Week 12 Nigeria Professional Football League match, with Andrew Ikefe and Junior Lokosa scoring for the visitors and hosts, respectively.

Market structure trading analyzes swing highs and lows, support and resistance, trendlines, and channels to interpret price movements and identify potential entry and exit levels. The three main market structures are trending, ranging, and consolidating. Trending markets have sustained upward or downward movement, ranging markets oscillate between defined boundaries, and consolidating markets show indecision, narrower ranges, and reduced volatility.

Candlestick patterns such as doji and engulfing formations may signal shifts in market structure, while volume can help validate breakouts or breakdowns. Fibonacci retracement levels can identify potential support, resistance, or trend-resumption points during pullbacks. Breakout trading seeks entries when prices move beyond key support or resistance, while pullback trading enters during retracements within established trends.

Risk management includes placing stop-loss orders near key levels and adjusting position size according to the strength and certainty of the identified structure. Multiple-time-frame analysis can confirm important levels by comparing intraday, daily, and weekly charts. Harmonic patterns such as Gartley and Butterfly may indicate reversals or continuations, but Fibonacci, multiple-time-frame, and harmonic strategies are difficult to backtest. The article recommends backtesting these techniques to validate their usefulness.

The message transmits U.S. envoy Mr. Wise’s dispatches describing a systematic scheme to evade laws against the slave trade. American vessels are nominally chartered but effectively sold to Brazilian dealers, with British brokers and capitalists, then routed through Great Britain and Brazil to Africa. There, cargo is exchanged for enslaved people, the vessels’ identities and papers are concealed or destroyed, and new crews return the captives to Brazil. Unknowing American crews reportedly bear the legal penalties while principal participants escape. British factors and agents are also implicated in abusing the American flag. Wise suggests stronger Anglo-American suppression measures and criticizes Britain’s practice of transferring captured Africans to West Indies rather than restoring them to Africa, arguing that this perpetuates the trade in another form.

DS introduced the 225hp PureTech 225 petrol engine for the UK DS7 Crossback, featuring turbocharging, variable valve timing, 200-bar injection and Stop&Start. The engine reduces fuel consumption by 6%, while the EAT8 adds efficiency. Launch-year options include two petrol and two Euro 6.2-compliant diesel engines, priced from £34,990.

The address portrays an unprecedented era of domestic prosperity and international peace, attributing these conditions to the character of the American people, cooperation between management and workers, constructive economic conservation, and effective federal administration. Tax reductions increased national income by nearly 50 percent to an estimated $90 billion, while debt repayment, refinancing, and reduced interest costs enabled further tax cuts. A projected surplus of about $37 million was considered too small to support new spending; Congress was urged to avoid immediate appropriations or finance them with new revenue to preserve a balanced budget. Government savings did not prevent expanded veterans’ compensation, civil-service retirement payments, flood control, public buildings, and war-claims adjustments.

Foreign relations were described as peaceful and cooperative. The Sixth International Conference of American States produced eleven conventions and 71 resolutions, and another conference on conciliation and arbitration was scheduled in Washington. Eleven arbitration treaties were signed and 22 more were under negotiation.

In Nicaragua, U.S. Marines protected American lives and interests during a violent revolution. Col. Henry L. Stimson mediated an agreement for ceasefire, elections, and restored peace. A free and fair election produced cooperation from both parties and advanced Nicaragua toward peaceful self-government and renewed prosperity. Chile and Peru resumed diplomatic relations and continued negotiations over their territorial dispute. Relations with Mexico improved substantially, with frank negotiations, growing confidence, and respect for mutual sovereignty. In China, the United States recognized the Nationalist Government, concluded a treaty restoring tariff autonomy and protecting American citizens against discrimination, increased trade, and reduced its military presence. The address also recommended settlements of the comparatively small Greek and Austrian debts.

A peace treaty signed by 15 nations, with 44 others intending to adhere, renounced war as national policy and committed nations to peaceful dispute resolution while preserving the United States’ sovereign right to national defense.

National defense remained essential to preserving order. The Army was not to be increased, while housing, repairs, and a six-year aviation program were underway. The Navy required cruiser replacements, and the pending legislation was endorsed. Defense costs had risen by $118 million over four years and were estimated at $668 million for 1930, but no expansion of Army or Navy personnel was considered necessary. The address rejected the characterization of the country as militaristic or imperialistic and emphasized support for American interests abroad and respect for other nations’ sovereignty.

Veterans’ relief included pensions, compensation, rehabilitation, hospitalization, and insurance. Annual expenditures of approximately $765 million were increasing, so additional legislation required especially careful scrutiny. Congress was encouraged to study consolidating veterans’ services into one department.

Agriculture had improved but remained uneven. Livestock and dairy returns were strong, cotton production increased despite lower prices, and several other crops returned less, although total farm income was expected to exceed that of the previous crop year. The Department of Agriculture had expanded research, regulation, cooperative marketing assistance, and extension work. Government action against surpluses caused by overextended acreage was opposed, as were general subsidies, price fixing, and direct government business. For surpluses arising from weather and seasonal conditions, the address proposed a Federal farm board and revolving loan fund to assist producers’ marketing organizations. Federal tax reductions had shifted part of the agricultural tax burden to state and local governments, which the states were expected to address.

Federal support for commerce was to continue, including efforts to reduce distribution waste and maintain international trade of about $9 billion annually. Civil aviation had developed a national airway system serving three-quarters of the population, largely without subsidies. Recommendations were also made for a permanent Cuban parcel-post agreement, a permanent site for the gifted “Maine” memorial, railroad consolidation and interstate-commerce reforms, and continued development of the merchant marine through private operation, mail contracts, and temporary government operation of strategic routes.

Further proposals included American engineering assistance and private financing for an inter-American highway, expanded air-mail routes around the Caribbean and South America, and river and harbor improvements with coordinated railroad rates. No additional major waterway legislation was recommended while outstanding projects remained incomplete. Federal irrigation projects had brought extensive benefits despite some failures, and new projects required consideration of settlers’ repayment capacity. A Colorado River dam was recommended for flood control, irrigation, and domestic water, with safeguards for the states and electric power generation left to private enterprise. At Muscle Shoals, the nitrate facilities were considered useful for national defense and fertilizer, and leasing the power and nitrate plants was favored over further government construction or retail operations.

Conservation was presented as developing resources without waste. Federal attention to oil supplies, Osage Indian oil lands, minerals, water power, grazing, erosion, and reforestation was emphasized. Restrictive immigration policy was to continue, with preference for essential experts, expedited family reunification, and codification of immigration and naturalization laws.

The address rejected the idea of a fixed limit on wages and profits, maintaining instead that production was the determining factor. Wages had risen substantially since 1922, and government and business were urged to reduce industrial accidents. Federal support for women workers, public health, and infant mortality was also emphasized.

Civil-service salaries had risen nearly 63 percent since 1921, accompanied by generous leave and retirement benefits. The Bureau of Education had surveyed Black colleges and universities, begun surveying agricultural colleges, and proposed surveying secondary schools. A large public-building program was underway. Federal Indian administration required improved health, education, and economic opportunities, greater state participation, and eventual safe termination of federal supervision. The address noted educational, professional, economic, and artistic progress among Black Americans, called for stronger protection against lynching, and urged the Philippines to receive relief from double taxation. Following a destructive Puerto Rican storm, assistance to coffee growers was recommended on a strictly business basis.

All federal legal activities should be consolidated under the Attorney General. The special counsel pursuing oil cases had recovered leased lands and substantial cash and property, and an exemption from restrictions on accepting other government-related cases was recommended. Prohibition remained binding, with continued federal enforcement and state cooperation required.

The conclusion warned that prosperity and peace could be lost without continued effort and public confidence. The government should act with generosity, moderation, patience, justice, and humility, preserving opportunities for a more abundant intellectual, moral, and spiritual life.

The author reports that a majority of Hawaiians, Creoles, and naturalized foreigners favor annexation to the United States and that the sovereign’s expected death without an heir could create a political opening for peaceful annexation approved by the U.S. government. American missionary education, New England influence, and the Fifteenth Amendment have increased support for annexation. Native Hawaiians are estimated at 45,000, down 15,000 since 1866, while 5,000–6,000 foreigners, two-thirds from the United States, hold major government offices and much foreign capital. Hawaii is presented as a strategically located North Pacific naval, coaling, and commercial base with growing trade involving China, Japan, and Australia. Its tropical products could support mutually beneficial trade with western U.S. states, while control by a European power in wartime could harm American commerce. The author suggests U.S. sovereignty might be obtained without payment beyond possible purchases of crown and public lands and annuities to several high chiefs. The unmarried sovereign, believed unlikely to name a successor, is said to face sudden death from obesity-related congestion.

A mother urged parents to keep sick children home after her 3-year-old developed RSV following Christmas dinner with a cousin who had a lung infection. The asthmatic toddler was hospitalized, given antibiotics, and placed on a breathing machine; the original Imgur post was removed.

On June 14, 2017, Flag Day marked the start of construction to convert Verona’s former Annin Flag manufacturing plant into Annin Lofts. The 1919 plant closed in 2013 and will become 112 rental units: 52 loft-style apartments in the four-story main building, which will gain a penthouse floor, and 60 studio, one-bedroom and two-bedroom units in a new building. Developer Ed Russo said the project aims to preserve the property’s historic character. Architect Kurt Vierheilig expected completion within 12 to 14 months. The ceremony featured a flag raising by the Verona Fire Department Honor Guard and recollections of the factory’s history.

He praises Hull’s hard work and emotional Stanley Cup Final goal while noting the opponent remains dangerous and the series resets for the next game.

Apple Inc.’s Form 10-Q for the fiscal quarter ended March 26, 2016 reported second-quarter net sales of $50.557 billion, down 13% from $58.010 billion a year earlier, primarily due to lower iPhone sales and weaker foreign currencies. Net income was $10.516 billion, or $1.90 per diluted share, compared with $13.569 billion, or $2.33 per diluted share. For the first six months, net sales fell 5% to $126.429 billion, while net income declined to $28.877 billion and diluted earnings per share to $5.19. Gross margin was 39.4% for the quarter and 39.8% for the six months, below prior-year levels because of currency weakness and unfavorable fixed-cost leverage.

Second-quarter product sales declined for iPhone, iPad and Mac by 18%, 19% and 9%, respectively, while Services sales increased 20% and Other Products sales increased 30%. Japan was the only geographic segment with quarterly sales growth, rising 24%; Americas, Europe, Greater China and Rest of Asia Pacific sales declined.

At March 26, 2016, Apple held $232.928 billion in cash, cash equivalents and marketable securities, with total assets of $305.277 billion and shareholders’ equity of $130.457 billion. Six-month operating cash flow was $39.064 billion. The company repurchased $13.530 billion of stock, paid $5.871 billion in dividends and dividend equivalents, and issued $15.5 billion of long-term debt during the quarter.

The filing also described risks from concentrated suppliers, outsourced manufacturing, foreign-exchange movements and competition. It disclosed $7.5 billion of unrecognized tax benefits and an unquantifiable potential exposure related to the European Commission’s investigation of alleged state aid to Apple. Apple received $548 million from Samsung in the patent dispute, while the U.S. Supreme Court agreed to hear Samsung’s appeal. The company also described accounting standards scheduled for future adoption covering stock compensation, leases, financial instruments and revenue recognition.

The Foreign Office described discussions with Belgian officials over renewal of the expired Anglo-Belgian Congo “purchase agreement” as informal and focused on specific issues. A memorandum said Far East developments had increased the wartime importance of West African raw materials, leading Britain to press Belgium to expand production of wolfram, tin, copper, palm oil, and rubber. Belgium faced difficulty enforcing production targets amid competing Allied offers; notably, U.S. prices for palm oil and rubber exceeded British offers. Belgium also lacked coordinated orders and programs for estimating machinery, steel, and other needs, and Britain sought a comprehensive 12-month requirements program.

The Secretary of State proposed a joint UK-US arrangement with the Congo covering Belgian requirements and British and American purchases. This required U.S. assurances that it would negotiate jointly and consider Belgian requests for goods supplied by the United States. Washington meetings involving the Department, Board of Economic Warfare, Combined Raw Materials Board, and British Embassy unanimously endorsed the proposal as a constructive way to coordinate Congo exports and imports.

The rescue helicopter responded to three incidents: suspected spinal injury, a fractured leg after a motorbike crash, and a back injury after a trampoline fall. PSRT’s Central North Island helicopters rely on sponsors and donations.

This article, published in the European Journal of Education (Vol. 7, Issue 2, 2024), examines the (re)construction of professional identities of preservice language teachers in initial formation. It opens from Palmer's (1998) claim, cited via Alsup (2006), that educational reform will never succeed if it demeans and disheartens teachers, and from the author's own experience teaching in public elementary schools, where colleagues and superiors advised that the system "swallows" those who do not adapt to it.

The study is grounded in Alsup's (2006) concept of "Borderland Discourse," defined as discourse evidencing integration or negotiation of personal and professional selves, allowing preservice teachers to move from student to teacher without sacrificing personal priorities and passions. The author notes the risks of such naming (it may suggest something stable and easily identifiable) and emphasizes that such discourse is complex, rich, and dependent on social, cultural, and historical context, with cognitive, emotional, and psychological aspects foregrounded over strictly linguistic ones. Identity is treated as multiple, transitory, and transformational, involving claimed versus assigned identities and negotiation through discourse, language, and social practices (Wenger, 2008). The literature notes that first-year teaching remains extremely difficult (Rogers & Babinsky, 2002) and that half of novice teachers leave within five years (Gordon, 1991; Huling-Austin et al., 1989).

Data come from internship reports written over four semesters (2010–2011) by two participants, Laura and Richard, in a Letras course, analyzed alongside their virtual exchanges in a Moodle platform and a practice community (CdP). Laura reports a "breach" between university theory and school practice, later theorizes her own pedagogy (mixing tradition and innovation, prioritizing students' interests), and asserts the teacher as the leading figure in the classroom who must adapt classes to context and diversity. Richard negotiates the shift from student/researcher to intern teacher under multiple evaluators, criticizes trainers for positivist, content-centered methods disconnected from real school conditions, adopts a paternalistic model of care for students, and ultimately rejects teaching English, identifying instead as a mother-tongue teacher.

Concluding inferences stress that the period of institutional change made these contexts arenas for identity negotiation; that the identities of student/apprentice, intern teacher, foreign language teacher, and sociocultural actor follow no chronological order but a back-and-forth movement; that the Supervised Internship discipline is crucial for rebuilding identity and cultural capital; and that Moodle exchanges function as emotional scaffolding, making narratives in virtual and presential settings privileged sites for understanding how language constructs who we are.

New CFPB rules would require payday and auto-title lenders to assess borrowers’ ability to repay within 30 days and limit repeated account debits without reauthorization. Supporters say this would curb rollovers, excessive fees, and debt traps; a 2014 CFPB study found over 80% of payday loans were rolled over or followed by another loan within two weeks. A trade group says the rules could devastate a $39 billion industry serving 30 million–40 million customers annually, while CFPB estimates loan volume could fall by half and many of 16,000 stores could close. The rule faces strong Republican opposition, could be rolled back, and would not take effect until 2019. Meanwhile, the OCC lifted restrictions on banks making small-dollar loans.

Ariel Miranda earned his first win of the season by pitching seven shutout innings in the Mariners’ 6-1 victory over the Marlins at Safeco Field. He allowed four hits, struck out five, walked none, and threw 97 pitches, including 63 fastballs. Miranda attacked hitters aggressively with a fastball around 94 mph and used his changeup to keep them off balance. He began the season as a Seattle starter after Drew Smyly was injured in spring training, having long preferred a rotation role. Robinson Cano ended a recent slump with a 441-foot homer, and Nelson Cruz followed with a 410-foot shot. It was the sixth time a Mariners starter threw seven shutout innings that season.

Oil prices declined as easing Middle East geopolitical tensions eroded the risk premium supporting crude markets. Brent crude fell about 1.4% to $65.07 per barrel while West Texas Intermediate dropped to $61.55, extending earlier losses, aided by rising U.S. crude inventories and slowing demand in transport and manufacturing. Reports of progress toward a Gaza ceasefire plan and renewed diplomatic activity suggested supply and Red Sea shipping risks were diminishing. Expectations that the Federal Reserve could cut rates next year supported risk assets but tempered oil demand forecasts. Analysts said focus is returning to fundamentals, including rising non-OPEC output from the U.S. and Brazil and subdued demand in Europe and parts of Asia, keeping prices under pressure in the short term, with relative stability forecast unless tensions reignite.
