The lecture reviews coherent states of light as eigenstates of the annihilation operator with a complex eigenvalue \(\alpha\). Unlike creation-operator eigenstates, they are normalizable, and \(\alpha\) corresponds directly to the amplitude and phase of a classical electric field. Under time evolution, \(\alpha\) rotates clockwise like a phasor. Coherent states are minimum-uncertainty states, satisfying the Heisenberg bound, and their photon-number fluctuations are Poissonian.

Quantum states can be represented in phase space using \(Q\), \(P\), or Wigner distributions, which differ by operator-ordering conventions. The \(Q\) distribution is always positive but gives finite-width Gaussians for coherent states and rings for photon-number states. The \(P\) representation gives a delta function for a coherent state and a derivative of a delta function for a number state. The Wigner distribution gives exact position and momentum projections and is closest to a classical phase-space distribution, but it can contain negative values.

Photon-number fluctuations can also be characterized by the second-order correlation function \(g^{(2)}\) and the Fano factor. Classical \(g^{(2)}\) is at least 1, whereas quantum states can violate this bound. Coherent states have \(g^{(2)}=1\), Poissonian photon statistics, and a Fano factor of 0. Thermal states have \(g^{(2)}=2\) and a Fano factor equal to the mean occupation. Fock states have zero number variance, a Fano factor of \(-1\), and sub-Poissonian \(g^{(2)}\); a single-photon state has zero simultaneous two-photon detection probability.

Attenuating a coherent state does not produce a single-photon Fock state because attenuation preserves its Poissonian statistics and still permits multiphoton outcomes. Single photons may instead be generated using a single excited atom or ion in a high-finessity cavity. Another approach uses many atoms and heralding: detecting a Raman-transition photon prepares one atom in a known state, which can then be pumped to emit a second photon. Such sources can have high fidelity but retain preparation uncertainties.

Finally, the lecture describes the Hanbury Brown and Twiss experiment, which measures intensity correlations using a beam splitter, two detectors, and coincidence counting. Coherent light gives \(g^{(2)}=1\), while thermal light gives \(g^{(2)}=2\). An isolated single photon can produce no detector coincidence because it reaches only one detector, although correlations at longer delays can reflect the source’s repetition rate. A complete quantum treatment must also include the vacuum state entering the unused beam-splitter port.

Researchers used more than a decade of Gulf of Alaska data from robotic floats and ship-based plankton surveys to examine two marine heatwaves, in 2013–2015 and 2019–2020. Both altered plankton communities and disrupted the biological carbon pump, which normally transports carbon from the ocean surface to the deep sea. Carbon accumulated near the surface or in the upper twilight zone rather than sinking to depths where it could remain stored for millennia. The heatwaves produced different food-web and carbon-transport changes because phytoplankton populations shifted and small grazers increased. These disruptions may allow more carbon to return to the atmosphere and reduce the ocean’s ability to buffer climate change. The findings support sustained, coordinated monitoring of ocean biological and chemical conditions before, during, and after marine heatwaves.

Yen Bai plans to expand agro-forestry processing, develop local brands and markets, and attract investment in high-tech facilities for timber, tea, cinnamon, cassava, camellia, bamboo shoots and livestock. Its 430,000 hectares of forests support wood processing, but most of the province’s 104 plants use low-tech lines. The province targets VND 850 billion in wood-sector revenue by 2020 and double that by 2025. It also plans camellia and bamboo-shoot products worth VND 50 billion by 2020 and VND 200 billion by 2025, plus cattle-meat facilities with annual capacity exceeding 3,000 tonnes.

The court held that former Lincoln County Attorney Bill Vassar’s action abated because successor Frank McVey did not revive or continue it within the six-month period required by Federal Rule of Civil Procedure 25(d) and 28 U.S.C. § 780. The rule requires a showing of substantial need for continuing the action. The court rejected Vassar’s argument that Oklahoma was the real party in interest and dismissed the action without prejudice. Similar orders were entered in the seven related cases, with exceptions allowed for appropriate judgments.

Austria-Hungary informed the U.S. ambassador that it and its allies had offered peace negotiations through the United States, but the enemy governments rejected the proposal without a counteroffer, making a reply impossible. In a note circulated after being given to the press and broadcast, the government defended the proposal as sincere and said its terms would be revealed when negotiations began. It accused the enemy governments of avoiding discussion of how to end the war and instead emphasizing prewar events, military strength, and the alleged motives for the proposal. Asserting that responsibility for the war had already been established, it cited Serbia’s alleged aggression and the Sarajevo assassination, rejected renewed discussion of the war’s origins, and said military advantage should be left to world opinion. It described Austria-Hungary and its allies as acting defensively while alleging enemy territorial ambitions. The government also invoked Ireland, Finland, the Boer Republics, North Africa, and Greece in response to demands concerning national rights and restored liberties. It declared readiness for an oral exchange of views with the enemy governments and said peace depended on their acceptance, while disclaiming responsibility for continued war and committing to fight for a peace preserving its peoples’ existence, honor, and free development.

Mario Batali surrendered oversight of his restaurant empire after reports of sexual misconduct involving at least four women, three of whom worked for him. Batali said the complaints matched his past behavior, accepted responsibility and apologized. ABC asked him to leave “The Chew” during a review, while Food Network paused plans to relaunch “Molto Mario.” His company said an employee made the first formal complaint in October; Batali was reprimanded and required to attend training. The reports emerged amid the #MeToo movement.

Starbucks shares have been largely flat since late 2015, disappointing investors who expected growth. Recent U.S. comparable-store sales have fallen below the company’s previous 5% benchmark, partly due to Mobile Order congestion, though comparable sales are recovering. The Unicorn drink and Frappuccino Happy Hour could support sales. Starbucks has also delivered more than 26% compound annual dividend growth since its first dividend. In China, it is opening 500 stores annually, expects that pace to continue for decades, and reported 7% regional comparable-store sales growth last quarter.

The study developed the Grocery Basket Score (GBS), a mortality-based model for automatically rating the nutritional quality of entire shopping baskets and complementing product-level systems such as Nutri-Score. Using NHANES dietary recalls from 2001–2018 linked to 2019 mortality data, researchers tested nutrient-density and nutrient-deficiency signals in Cox proportional hazards models. The final GBS combined separate food and beverage models as a calorie-weighted average. It penalized high saturated-fat, sugar, sodium, and beverage calorie density; protein, vitamin C, and iron deficiencies; and rewarded fiber.

Validation of 913,298 Open Food Facts products found a Pearson correlation of 0.60 between the GBS and Nutri-Score, with cluster correlations ranging from 0.25 to 0.75. Among 4,382 NHANES 2017–2018 participants, GBS correlations with the AHEI were −0.62 without and −0.60 with the protective effect of moderate alcohol, compared with −0.48 and −0.47 for calorie-weighted Nutri-Scores.

The authors described the GBS as a density-based, automated assessment requiring neither manual food annotation nor household-size information and potentially suitable for deployment through retailer loyalty or digital shopping programs. Limitations include reliance on self-reported U.S. dietary data, exclusion of products with missing nutritional information, use of Nutri-Score 2017 in AHEI validation, limited generalizability beyond the United States, and failure to model alcohol-related harms beyond calorie density. The included signals may also act as proxies, so the model does not establish causal effects or prove that supplementing particular nutrients would reduce mortality.

Carolina Panthers quarterback Cam Newton apologized for sexist comments about a female reporter’s questions amid backlash that included losing an Oikos sponsorship. In an October 5 video, he called his wording degrading and disrespectful, acknowledged losing sponsors and fans, and asked for forgiveness.

The Fifth Circuit held that above-median-income debtors may claim the IRS Local Standard vehicle ownership deduction under the Chapter 7 means test even when their vehicles have no loan or lease payments. Troy and Elaine Tate’s claimed deductions for two vehicles reduced their monthly disposable income below the $166.67 abuse threshold; without the deductions, their filing was presumptively abusive.

The court adopted the “plain language” approach, interpreting “applicable monthly expense amounts” to refer to the local-standard deduction based on the debtor’s geographic area and number of vehicles, rather than requiring an actual ownership expense. It rejected the IRM approach, which barred the deduction when no debt payment existed, because the statute does not incorporate the IRS methodology, distinguishes actual expenses in other categories, excludes debt payments, and favors a uniform, straightforward means test. The court reversed the judgment affirming dismissal of the Tates’ Chapter 7 case and remanded for further proceedings.

The Tiered Memory Page Migration (TMPM) engine supports optional SEV and SNP extensions for migrating memory pages while maintaining the same guest physical address. Availability is determined through the ENGINE_READY bit, and IOMMU enablement is required. TMPM coordinates with IOMMU page tables to safely migrate pages undergoing concurrent DMA and can migrate SNP-protected guest pages inaccessible to the hypervisor or operating system.

PM_PAGE_MOVE_IO migrates DMA-mapped pages using a specified IOMMU host page table entry. PM_PAGE_MOVE_GUEST migrates SNP guest pages: source pages must be Guest-Valid or Guest-Invalid, and destination pages must be in the new Pre-Migration state. Pre-Migration pages contain a platform-specific ASID, cannot be validated by a guest, and must be converted back to Hypervisor state using RMPUpdate.

Commands can migrate groups of up to 128 pages in a Page Migration List. Entries need not be adjacent, may reference multiple guests, and have no order dependence. Per-page statuses are provided when a command returns partial success; PM_RMP_NOTEXCLUSIVE indicates a migration may be retried after a concurrent RMPUPDATE conflict. PM_SUCCESS means all pages migrated, while other return codes indicate no migrations occurred.

Several IOMMU structures and TMPM buffers cannot be migrated. Host software must avoid concurrent modification of referenced IOMMU host page table entries because TMPM may update them non-atomically.

AMD testing found that commands moving at least 16 pages have higher bandwidth, with maximum performance at 128 pages. Rapid command submission, reduced interrupt frequency, and low-water-mark interrupts help keep TMPM busy.

Firmware reload requires pausing operations and tearing down the ring buffer; reload is rejected if the buffer remains initialized, and the replacement firmware must be the same or a newer version. Software must check ENGINE_READY before communicating with TMPM. PM_GET_CAPABILITIES and its FW_VER_Major field identify the reload path; Family 19h is represented by the decimal value 71.
Liberty Island was evacuated after a person climbed the Statue of Liberty’s base. At least six people were arrested for hanging an “Abolish I.C.E.” banner from the pedestal.

The paper introduces FoodSEM, a fine-tuned open-source Llama 3 8B model for food named-entity recognition and linking to the FoodOn, SNOMED-CT, and Hansard taxonomies. It addresses the limited semantic resources and low performance of unadapted language models in the food domain.

FoodSEM’s training data was created from the CafeteriaFCD recipe corpus and CafeteriaSA scientific-abstract corpus in BioC format, converting annotations into instruction-response sequences. Artificial examples were added to address underrepresented ontology entities, producing 21,027 fine-tuning instances. The model was trained with supervised fine-tuning and Low-Rank Adaptation.

Five-fold cross-validation showed that FoodSEM substantially outperformed non-fine-tuned 0-, 1-, and 5-shot prompting baselines. Its macro-weighted F1 scores on artificial data were 0.942 for FoodOn, 0.974 for SNOMED-CT, and 0.937 for Hansard. Scores reached 0.827, 0.863, and 0.843 on CafeteriaFCD and 0.654, 0.713, and 0.730 on CafeteriaSA, respectively. Precision remained high, while lower recall on scientific abstracts was attributed partly to errors in preceding entity-recognition steps.

The paper releases the corpora, model, code, and datasets publicly and identifies scientific-data expansion and retrieval-augmented generation for unseen ontology entities as future work.

A 2024 MIT case study examines Checkr, a technology-based consumer reporting company founded in 2014 by French software engineers Daniel Yanisse and Jonathan Perichon. After experiencing inefficient, manual background-check processes at an on-demand delivery company, they developed AI-powered software and an API that integrate background screening into customer systems. Checkr processes court, credit, and employment data while addressing accuracy and regulatory requirements. By 2024, it had 1,200 employees, more than 100,000 customers, and 30 million annual background checks; 84% of checks were completed within 15 minutes and 92% within four hours.

Yanisse and Perichon noticed that candidates with conviction records—disproportionately Black and Hispanic candidates—were frequently rejected. This prompted Checkr to pursue “fair chance hiring,” which gives people with records fair access to jobs for which they are qualified without lowering safety or hiring standards. Yanisse’s 2015 teaching experience with incarcerated people through Defy Ventures helped shape this mission. Checkr began hiring justice-impacted employees and advocated that businesses expand their talent pools, avoid treating records as automatic disqualifications, and provide fair opportunities.

The case study describes the scale of employment barriers facing the justice-impacted. About 80 million Americans had arrest or conviction records in 2024, more than one-third of the workforce. Formerly incarcerated people faced unemployment rates above 27%, while more than 60% remained jobless within four years of release. At the same time, the U.S. labor market had 9.5 million openings and 6.5 million unemployed workers in early 2024. Research cited in the case found that fair chance hires often stayed longer, performed similarly or better, enhanced workplace diversity, and could reduce recidivism when paired with stable, livable-wage employment.

Checkr embedded its mission in products including Candidate Stories, which allowed applicants to provide context before being rejected, and Assess, which filtered records by age or type of conviction. Since their respective launches, nearly 45,000 candidates had submitted stories and been approved for roles, while Assess had filtered records for more than two million people. Other services included a fair chance hiring dashboard and an Expungement tool. The company also maintained its own fair chance workforce, nonprofit partnerships, employee volunteering, and a 12-month apprenticeship launched in July 2023.

To support its mission externally, Checkr signed the Pledge 1% in 2021, committing 1% of employee time, products, equity, and profits annually. Its CSR division, led by former prisoner Ken Oliver, trained customers and coordinated volunteering, while Checkr.org pursued advocacy, fundraising, and grants. The case study concludes that Yanisse wanted more large companies to adopt fair chance hiring and argued that its long-term success required aligning Checkr’s social mission with customer value, growth, profitability, and shareholder support, particularly as a potential IPO approached.

The DAWn-plasma trial was a prospective, multicenter, randomized, open-label study comparing best supportive care plus four units of high-titer convalescent plasma with supportive care alone in hospitalized patients with COVID-19. Of 483 randomized patients, 320 received plasma plus supportive care and 163 received supportive care alone.

The intervention did not affect the primary endpoint—the proportion alive and free of mechanical ventilation at day 15. No differences were detected in mortality, survival without mechanical ventilation at day 30, or other secondary endpoints. Estimated treatment effects were close to null, with similar results in the per-protocol population.

Safety outcomes were comparable between groups. Patients with adverse events numbered 90 in the plasma group and 49 in the control group. There were 55 fatal adverse events among 49 patients and 118 serious adverse events among 100 patients, without significant between-group differences. Five adverse events led to treatment discontinuation, all in the plasma group; two led to study discontinuation, one in each group. The plasma group had 14 treatment-related adverse events in 12 patients and seven treatment-related serious adverse events in seven patients. CRP, ferritin, D-dimer, and body temperature showed no clinically meaningful between-group differences. Transfusion-related side effects occurred in 19 of 320 plasma-treated patients, and no TRALI cases were reported.

Neutralizing-antibody titers increased from baseline to day 6, but the increase was not influenced by treatment. Better outcomes correlated with higher titers at baseline and day 6, but not with the magnitude of their increase.

Adverse events were graded using NCI CTCAE version 5.0, with an alternative five-grade scale for unlisted events. Investigators assessed events as suspected or not suspected in relation to study treatment. Second primary malignancies were designated events of interest and were reportable as serious adverse events.

Operational guidance covered collection, processing, storage, and transport of baseline and day-6 serum and EDTA samples, optional local PBMC isolation, and retention of screening and day-6 nasopharyngeal swabs for later quantitative PCR analysis.

The TLV321x comparators include internal ESD protection that limits input voltages to 0.2 V beyond the supply rails. For low-impedance input sources, TI recommends a series current-limiting resistor that keeps clamp current at 10 mA or less. An internal power-on reset holds the output low for up to 32 µs after the 1.65 V POR threshold is crossed, after which the output reflects the differential input state.

A comparator compares VIN with VREF, producing a low output when VIN is below VREF and a high output when VIN is above VREF; swapping the inputs reverses this relationship. Propagation delay can differ for rising and falling input transitions and increases with smaller overdrive, particularly below 100 mV. Output rise and fall times are measured between the waveform’s 20% and 80% points.

The devices have 1.8 mV of internal hysteresis. External positive feedback can reduce output chatter caused by slow signals near the switching threshold. Hysteresis behavior depends on the threshold voltage, internal offset, and hysteresis window. Inverting configurations use a three-resistor network referenced to VCC, while non-inverting configurations use two resistors and a voltage reference to define upper and lower switching thresholds.

A low-side current-sensing application uses an amplifier to amplify a shunt-resistor voltage drop, with the comparator changing state at a 1.1 V threshold. Layout guidance includes placing a low-ESR 0.1 µF bypass capacitor at the supply pin, using a solid ground plane, minimizing input-output coupling, and optionally adding an output resistor below 100 Ω to damp ringing or reflections. The devices support split or single supplies, and accurate comparator operation requires a stable, low-noise supply.

The passage also identifies documentation resources, TI E2E support, ESD-handling cautions, revision and mechanical information, and associated legal disclaimers.

The president describes Iraq’s election, with more than 10 million citizens voting, as a landmark for constitutional democracy and a potential ally in the fight against terrorism, while acknowledging that violence will continue. He defends the Iraq intervention, accepts responsibility despite acknowledging that intelligence concerning weapons of mass destruction was partly wrong, and argues that removing Saddam Hussein was justified.

He portrays the conflict as part of a global war on terrorism, rejecting the idea that terrorists would become peaceful if left alone. He cites the September 11 attacks as evidence that terrorists strike regardless of American provocation and supports confronting them abroad, removing safe havens, and strengthening partners such as Iraq and Afghanistan.

He outlines a three-part strategy: maintain offensive operations while transferring responsibility and territory to Iraqi forces; establish an inclusive, unified democratic government; and revive Iraq’s economy and infrastructure. He cites more than 125 Iraqi combat battalions, including more than 50 leading missions, along with public optimism about Iraq’s future. Although he recognizes reconstruction and security challenges, he rejects defeatism and argues the coalition is winning.

He warns that premature withdrawal would abandon Iraqi allies, undermine American troops, encourage regional tyrants, and embolden terrorists. He expects continued sacrifice but says Iraqi forces will grow stronger, potentially requiring fewer American troops; future troop levels will depend on conditions on the ground and military advice rather than political timetables. He asks Congress for continued support and urges Americans to reject despair, honor the sacrifices of service members and their families, and pursue victory.

Southeast Asian stocks rebounded Wednesday as investors sought bargains after losses driven by trade-war fears. Indonesia reversed an earlier decline to a 15-month low and closed 1.8 percent higher, while the government plans to review capital-goods imports for major projects to address its current-account deficit. Philippine shares closed 1.1 percent higher for a fourth consecutive session, led by real estate and industrial stocks, as foreign investors bought 449.8 million pesos of equities. Investors awaited inflation data expected to show a sixth monthly acceleration, raising the prospect of a third interest-rate hike. Singapore, Vietnam and Thailand also posted gains, while Singapore’s central bank chief warned of increased global growth risks from trade tensions and accelerating inflation.

Michael Daniels, 40, of Ashford, was sentenced to five years and three months in prison for conspiracy to steal motor vehicles. As head of sales at BMW Berry in Chiswick, he supplied Alex Tingle with spare keys and customer addresses, enabling Tingle and Vincent Murphy to steal nine luxury cars worth £210,000 between December 2015 and February 2016. The cars were given fake number plates and left with a figure known as “Ali” in Alperton. Tingle received two years in prison, with two concurrent months for possession of Class A drugs, but was due for immediate release after 13 months in custody. Murphy had earlier received 16 months for aggravated vehicle taking. Police identified Tingle from CCTV, leading to his confession that Daniels had orchestrated the thefts. The judge described the case as a “horrendous breach of trust,” and victims described disruption and significant losses.

Edgar Wright’s “Baby Driver” earned $100 million domestically after seven weeks and $67 million overseas, exceeding its $34 million budget and $39 million first-week gross. The June 28 release earned a 94% Rotten Tomatoes score and sent its soundtrack to No. 1 on iTunes. Shot around Atlanta, the film stars Ansel Elgort, Kevin Spacey, Lily James, Jamie Foxx, Jon Bernthal, and Jon Hamm.

After a mistrial, jury selection resumed in Isaiah Hagan’s murder case over Halee Rathgeber’s death. Ten of 14 jurors have been chosen; selection continues Thursday and opening statements begin Monday.

Exchange-traded funds (ETFs) are baskets of securities bought and sold as single instruments on stock exchanges, much like stocks. They can provide exposure to stocks, bonds, commodities, currencies, indices, sectors, or strategies. Unlike mutual funds, whose prices are generally set after market close, ETFs trade continuously during exchange hours, allowing investors to use limit orders, margin, short selling, and long-term holding. Their shares are continuously created and redeemed to keep market prices aligned with underlying assets.

The first recognized U.S. ETF, SPY, launched in 1993 and tracks the S&P 500. ETF adoption grew substantially after the 2008–09 financial crisis. Prominent examples include SPY, VTI for the total U.S. stock market, and IEFA for developed markets outside North America.

ETFs offer diversification, liquidity, intraday trading flexibility, broad asset exposure, and generally lower costs than mutual funds. Potential drawbacks include market losses, volatility, bid-ask spreads, expense ratios, tracking errors, and the risks of specialized, leveraged, or inverse funds. Higher liquidity generally means tighter spreads and easier execution.

The passage describes numerous ETF strategies, including trend following, mean reversion, momentum, sector rotation, arbitrage, quantitative trading, options, volatility trading, pair and market-neutral trading, global macro, smart beta, currency hedging, fixed income, and commodities. Some approaches, particularly arbitrage, high-frequency trading, and statistical arbitrage, are described as more suitable for institutions. It recommends backtesting strategies, considering historical tracking error and costs, avoiding excessive trading, and testing in a demo account before using live capital. It favors diversified strategies and asset classes, considers swing trading easier than day trading or scalping, and states that no single ETF or strategy is best for everyone.

- The guide defines optional extensions to SEV and SNP that facilitate page migration—copying page contents and updating virtual-to-physical mappings—using AMD’s trusted Tiered Memory Page Migration (TMPM) engine. Support can be checked through the `ENGINE_READY` bit in `PM_Status`, and TMPM requires enabled IOMMUs.

- In tiered-memory systems, software can move frequently accessed data to faster memory and less frequently accessed data to slower memory. TMPM provides two principal capabilities: migrating pages undergoing concurrent DMA and migrating SNP-protected guest pages that the hypervisor or operating system cannot directly access.

- `PM_PAGE_MOVE_IO` moves up to 128 pages that may be active DMA targets and directly updates IOMMU host page table entries. It requires the relevant IOMMU host page table entry, coordinated IOMMU flushing and mapping updates, and prevention of CPU access during migration. In SNP systems, it operates on Hypervisor-state pages. Direct migration of 2M pages is unsupported and requires splitting into 4K pages.

- `PM_PAGE_MOVE_GUEST` moves up to 128 SNP guest pages. Source pages must be Guest-Valid or Guest-Invalid, while destination pages must be in the new Pre-Migration state; after migration, destination pages receive the source state and source pages become Pre-Migration. A Pre-Migration page contains a platform-specific ASID, is never associated with a guest, and cannot be PVALIDATEd. `RMPUpdate` is used to restore it to Hypervisor state. Concurrent DMA is unsupported and may be aborted. A 2M request must be aligned and physically contiguous or be split into 4K pages.

- Multi-page migration lists may contain up to 128 entries, need not reference adjacent pages, may span multiple guests, and must have no ordering dependencies between entries or commands. Each entry reports individual status. `PM_SUCCESS` means all pages migrated; `PM_PARTIAL_SUCCESS` requires checking per-page statuses; other return codes indicate that no migrations were performed. `PM_RMP_NOTEXCLUSIVE` identifies a retryable conflict. The list must begin at a 4K-aligned physical address.

- TMPM commands are submitted through an OS-visible driver and a ring buffer separate from the SEV/SNP ring buffer. The buffer contains 1–255 physically contiguous 4K pages and can hold 256 16-byte commands per page. Firmware controls the read pointer, software controls the write pointer, and parallel execution means command completion order is not guaranteed. Initialization requires a ready engine, valid buffer address and configuration, driver initialization, and confirmation of `DRIVER_INIT_COMPLETE`. Shutdown requires pausing or draining the buffer before clearing initialization. Six interrupt sources share one x86 interrupt, including completion, error, empty-buffer, low-water, write-pointer-error, and ring-memory-error conditions.

- AMD testing found that commands moving at least 16 pages have substantially greater bandwidth than smaller commands, with maximum performance at 128 pages. Keeping the input queue populated, using low-water interrupts, and avoiding an interrupt for every command can improve throughput. IOMMU structures, vIOMMU page tables and pinned buffers, and the TMPM ring buffer and argument pages are not migratable. Host software must avoid concurrent modification of IOMMU host page table entries referenced by TMPM operations.

- TMPM firmware can be reloaded only after operations are paused and the ring buffer is torn down. The reload uses the documented BIOS-to-PSP mailbox protocol, should occur with IOMMU `PAGEMIGRATION_EN` bits disabled, and requires firmware of the same or a newer version. The driver must verify `ENGINE_READY` before communicating with the firmware. `PM_GET_CAPABILITIES` supplies the major version used to select the reload procedure; EPYC Family 19h is represented by `FW_VER_Major` value 71.

- The command set comprises `PM_GET_CAPABILITIES`, `PM_PAGE_MOVE_IO`, `PM_PAGE_MOVE_GUEST`, and `PM_NOOP`. Commands and migration entries return overall status and sub-status values for invalid addresses, page states, page sizes, guest context, RMP exclusivity, partial completion, and other failures. Ring-buffer errors are reported through `PM_STATUS`, while hardware faults may be reported through command status and Machine Check Architecture.

- TMPM moves data between 4K-aligned pages, so ordinary system physical addresses must be 4K aligned; host page-table-entry addresses may instead be 8-byte aligned. A 2M address must be 2M aligned. SPA encoding supports 46- or 52-bit addresses, with encryption information encoded when SMEE or SME-MK is enabled.

A Bihar girl diagnosed with drug-resistant TB in 2012 was treated at Delhi’s Lala Ram Swarup TB Hospital but was not given Bedaquiline, which was available only in select cities. Brought to Mumbai in 2016, severely ill and weighing 25 kg, she was treated by Dr Zarir Udvadia, who recommended the drug but could not obtain permission to administer it under government restrictions. Her father petitioned the Delhi High Court, which ordered that Bedaquiline be administered.

Udvadia, who had published a study on the drug in 2012, said thousands more patients urgently need access. He reported a 70% success rate among 30 patients under his care. The passage raises concerns about the drug’s side effects but criticizes inflexible rules that force patients to seek legal redress. It also warns of TB’s resurgence, its highly demanding 18-month treatment, the absence of a preventive vaccine for drug-resistant TB, and the need to prevent further spread.

The discussion focuses largely on Duncan Keith, who is praised for his hard work, maturity, composure, and influence as a demanding but fair coach. The speakers also discuss Rask’s strong performance and the need to score against accomplished goaltenders. Keith is described as a good player and teammate who has occasionally been misunderstood, while his long friendship with one speaker is said to support their on-ice chemistry. The conversation also notes the players’ maturation, changing social habits, and lessons learned from back-to-back first-round exits.

Apple Inc.’s Form 10-Q for the fiscal quarter ended June 27, 2020 reported third-quarter net sales of $59.685 billion, up 11% from $53.809 billion a year earlier, driven mainly by Services, iPad and Mac. Net income was $11.253 billion, diluted earnings per share were $2.58, gross margin was $22.680 billion and operating income was $13.091 billion. Third-quarter sales increased across all product categories and geographic segments: iPhone rose 2%, Mac 22%, iPad 31%, Wearables, Home and Accessories 17%, and Services 15%. Nine-month net sales were $209.817 billion, up 7%, with net income of $44.738 billion and diluted earnings per share of $10.16.

At June 27, 2020, Apple reported total assets of $317.344 billion, total liabilities of $245.062 billion and shareholders’ equity of $72.282 billion. Cash and cash equivalents totaled $33.383 billion, while current and non-current marketable securities totaled $160.234 billion. Nine-month operating cash flow was $60.098 billion, investing activities used $9.820 billion and financing activities used $65.463 billion. Apple repurchased $54.5 billion of stock and paid $10.6 billion in dividends and dividend equivalents during the period. Its $225 billion repurchase authorization had $150.6 billion remaining available.

Apple adopted new lease and hedging accounting standards at the beginning of fiscal 2020. Lease adoption initially recorded $7.5 billion of right-of-use assets and $8.1 billion of lease liabilities. Hedging adoption increased accumulated other comprehensive income by $136 million with an offsetting reduction in retained earnings. Product revenue generally was recognized upon shipment, while service revenue was recognized over time; revenue for bundled services and unspecified software upgrades was deferred. Total deferred revenue was $9.8 billion.

The filing reported adverse third-quarter effects from the COVID-19 pandemic, including temporary store closures, widespread remote work and reduced demand, most pronounced in April and improving during May and June. Legal and regulatory matters included the July 15 annulment of the European Commission State Aid Decision, subject to appeal, with €12.9 billion excluding interest held in escrow; a $503 million VirnetX verdict scheduled for retrial; an iPhone performance-management settlement requiring at least $310 million and up to $500 million; and an appealed €1.1 billion French competition fine. On July 30, Apple announced a four-for-one common-stock split, with split-adjusted trading scheduled to begin August 31, 2020.

Count Tisza privately asked the U.S. ambassador to communicate to American statesmen and the public that the Allied peace terms would mutilate and humiliate Germany, dismember Austria-Hungary and Turkey, and contradict Wilson’s stated peace aims. He argued that national development requires homogeneous states and that the Austro-Hungarian dual monarchy best served this ideal in southeastern Europe.

Germany’s ambassador, Bernstorff, conveyed the Imperial Government’s confidence in Wilson and acceptance of his offer to help organize a peace conference. The Government would not publicly disclose its terms while the Entente had published terms aimed at destroying Germany and its allies, but privately authorized Bernstorff to outline the terms Germany would have accepted on December 12. It also agreed to participate in a postwar international conference based on Wilson’s Senate message.

Bernstorff explained that preparations made postponement of the submarine blockade impossible, but said it would soon end the war, safeguard American interests, and cease once Wilson’s efforts produced a peace acceptable to Germany. He justified unrestricted submarine warfare by alleging that the Entente rejected equal rights, violated international law through restrictions on neutral trade, and sought the destruction of the Central Powers.

The passage details NVIDIA’s GA10x Ampere architecture and its GeForce RTX 30-series, NVIDIA A40, and NVIDIA RTX A6000 GPUs. GA10x includes second-generation RT Cores, third-generation Tensor Cores, GDDR6X support, improved unified L1 cache and shared memory, concurrent ray-tracing and compute capabilities, and PCIe Gen 4. The full GA102 GPU has seven GPCs, 42 TPCs, 84 SMs, 112 ROPs, a 384-bit memory interface, and 6 MB of L2 cache. Moving ROPs from the memory subsystem into each GPC increases raster throughput and improves multisample antialiasing, fill rate, and blending.

Each GA10x SM has 128 CUDA Cores, four third-generation Tensor Cores, a 256 KB register file, four texture units, one second-generation ray-tracing core, and 128 KB of configurable L1 cache/shared memory. Both datapaths in each SM partition can execute FP32 operations, doubling Turing’s peak FP32 rate. GA10x also doubles shared-memory bandwidth, increases unified L1/shared-memory capacity by 33%, and adds TF32 and BF16 Tensor Core support.

Second-generation RT Cores double ray/triangle intersection testing compared with Turing and add an Interpolate Triangle Position unit for hardware-accelerated ray-traced motion blur. Motion-blur rendering can be up to eight times faster, while a measured RTX 3080 Blender Cycles demonstration was up to five times faster than an RTX 2080 Super. GA10x supports concurrent graphics and compute, ray tracing with graphics or compute, and two simultaneous compute workloads. The RTX 3080 renders one cited Wolfenstein frame in 6.7 ms, or 150 FPS, using CUDA, RT, and Tensor Cores.

Third-generation Tensor Cores support structural sparsity and provide up to twice the matrix-multiplication throughput of Turing Tensor Cores. With sparsity enabled, the RTX 3080 delivers 2.7 times the peak FP16 Tensor throughput of a dense RTX 2080 Super configuration. Fine-grained structured sparsity uses a two-out-of-four nonzero pattern, reducing weight storage and bandwidth by half while skipping zero-valued elements. DLSS gains support for a 9x scaling factor, enabling the RTX 3090 to run selected ray-traced games at 8K/60 FPS.

GDDR6X uses PAM4 signaling and Maximum Transition Avoidance encoding. It supports data rates up to 19.5 Gbps and peak bandwidth up to 936 GB/s in the RTX 3090. The RTX 3080 uses a 320-bit GDDR6X interface and provides 1.5 times the memory bandwidth of the RTX 2080 Super. GDDR6X also uses pseudo-independent memory channels to assist BVH traversal.

Third-generation NVLink provides four x4 links, with each link providing 14.0625 GB/s in each direction. Four links provide 56.25 GB/s per direction and 112.5 GB/s total between two GPUs. Two A40 or RTX A6000 GPUs can combine their 48 GB memory pools into 96 GB. Two RTX 3090 GPUs support two-way NVLink SLI, but three- and four-way SLI are unsupported. PCIe Gen 4 doubles PCIe 3.0 bandwidth, with a x16 slot reaching 64 GB/s peak bandwidth.

NVIDIA RTX IO uses GPU-based lossless decompression and Microsoft DirectStorage to move compressed assets directly from storage to GPU memory. The passage reports up to 100 times better I/O performance than hard drives and traditional storage APIs, lower CPU utilization, faster loading and streaming, reduced object pop-in and stutter, and reduced download and installation sizes through compression.

The GeForce RTX 3090 includes 24 GB of GDDR6X, 82 SMs, and 10,496 CUDA Cores and is stated to be 1.5 times faster than TITAN RTX. The RTX 3070 uses the GA104 GPU, lacks NVLink, and uses GDDR6 rather than GDDR6X. The A40 provides 48 GB of GDDR6, third-generation NVLink scaling to 96 GB, PCIe Gen 4, and higher FP32, ray-tracing, and AI throughput than the Quadro RTX 6000. It also supports virtual GPU software and Quadro Sync. The RTX A6000 provides 10,752 CUDA Cores, 48 GB of GDDR6, hardware-accelerated motion blur, AI denoising, and NVLink scaling to 96 GB.

Ampere GPUs support 4K at 120 Hz and 8K at 60 Hz. DisplayPort 1.4a can drive two 8K displays with one cable each, while HDMI 2.1 raises maximum bandwidth to 48 Gbps and supports 8K60 and 4K120 output. Following President William Henry Harrison’s death, the speaker assumes the presidency and vows to preserve the Constitution, relying on the people’s intelligence and patriotism. He outlines policies of peace and justice toward foreign nations, national honor, and improved military readiness.

Seeking to prevent the concentration of power, he calls for separating military authority from control of public funds, limiting presidential patronage, and removing officials who misuse their influence in partisan elections. Faithful officials will remain in office, and the same standards will apply to the speaker’s own appointments.

He advocates rigid economy, avoidance of public debt during peace, abolition of unnecessary offices, limited discretion in spending, and strict punishment for embezzlement. He also supports a sound circulating currency through constitutional measures.

Finally, he urges administrators not to expand federal authority beyond the Constitution, emphasizing the balance between the federal government and the states, the preservation of the Union, and the protection of republican institutions for future generations.

The speaker argues that détente requires reciprocal efforts and that negotiations with the Soviet Union are essential, but one-sided arms-control talks are dangerous during a major Soviet military buildup. The United States should maintain its defensive strength and restore a margin of safety while pursuing honest, verifiable, mutual nuclear reductions; for this reason, he opposes SALT II. Merck halted a late-stage trial of verubecestat after an independent study found it had “virtually no chance” of working, following Eli Lilly’s earlier decision to end the solanezumab trial. The failures, which showed no benefit over placebo, are a major setback for Alzheimer’s research and have intensified doubts about the beta amyloid theory, although experts say the theory is not yet disproven. Merck will continue studying verubecestat in patients with less advanced disease, with results expected in February 2019, while Biogen’s aducanumab trial has shown encouraging signs. No treatment has yet been proven to slow Alzheimer’s disease, and successes in animal studies have not been replicated in humans. Edward C. Turner was arrested for driving while under the influence and refused a breath or blood alcohol test. Oklahoma’s Commissioner of Public Safety revoked his driving privileges for six months, and an administrative hearing sustained the order. The district court modified the revocation to three months, finding six months excessive after considering Turner’s driving record.

The majority reversed the modification, citing State ex rel. Oklahoma Department of Public Safety v. Kopczynski, which held that district courts lacked authority to reduce the mandatory six-month suspension. It concluded that a 1975 amendment to Section 755 created a specific, limited exception for extreme and unusual hardship involving travel to or from employment.

The dissent argued that Kopczynski should be distinguished because it addressed hardship-based modification before the 1975 amendment. It asserted that Section 6-211(e) authorized courts to modify an otherwise justified revocation when the driving record showed the suspension was excessive, and that the amendment did not eliminate that authority. The dissent would have affirmed the three-month suspension.

The case concerns Vermont City Electric (VCE), a municipal utility formed in 1905 to reduce the cost of providing electricity to Vermont City. In 2008, VCE served about 16,000 residential accounts, 2,845 small commercial customers, and 784 large commercial customers. Following the economic downturn, VCE’s Finance Committee capped 2009 direct spending on demand-side management (DSM) programs at $800,000. The Citizen’s Oversight Board, including MBA graduate and wind-energy startup employee Daniela Shazar, therefore seeks an independent assessment of which DSM programs VCE should retain, postpone, or eliminate and what their carbon impact would be.

DSM reduces overall electricity use or shifts consumption away from peak-demand periods. Since 2000, VCE had invested heavily in DSM, but power demand is expected to grow as population rises by an estimated 0.52% annually and per-capita electricity use rises by 0.22%. Residential demand has also shifted from heating and water heating toward cooling, appliances, and electronics.

The case distinguishes power, measured in MW, from energy, measured in MWh. Electricity use varies by hour and season, and load-duration curves summarize how many hours the system must operate at each power level. VCE’s annual curve is approximated with five blocks: 365 hours averaging 60.1 MW, 830 hours averaging 49.4 MW, 4,125 hours averaging 42.0 MW, 2,960 hours averaging 32.8 MW, and 480 hours averaging 27.1 MW.

VCE’s supply sources include the 26.5-MW wood-fired McNeil Generating Station at $50.90 per MWh; 14.9 MW of medium-term hydroelectric and wood contracts at $60 per MWh; the 18-MW fuel-oil VCE Gas Turbine at $150 per MWh, used primarily for peak loads; and up to 50 MW purchased from ISO-NE’s wholesale market at block-dependent prices ranging from $15 to $300 per MWh. A 5.2-MW VCE wind facility was expected to begin operating in 2012 at $76.80 per MWh. McNeil costs were projected to rise 3% annually through 2014, other source costs 4%, and wind costs to remain flat. Discount factors are provided for calculating net present value from 2009 through 2014.

VCE operates nine DSM programs covering new and existing commercial and residential construction, retail energy-efficient products, commercial smart lighting, commercial heating and air conditioning, outdoor lighting, and LED streetlights. Their combined 2009 direct cost is $1,035,027, with block-specific demand reductions projected to continue for six years.

The modeling assignment asks students to construct a mixed-integer optimization model that determines VCE’s least-cost supply plan for 2009 and then 2009–2014, both without and with DSM. The model must separately represent demand in each load block, calculate annual carbon emissions, minimize net present cost using the supplied discount factors, add wind capacity in 2012, and incorporate binary decisions for the nine DSM programs, their six-year demand effects, and the $800,000 2009 spending limit. Students must then evaluate which programs the model selects, prepare a memorandum to the Oversight Board analyzing costs and carbon impacts, assess whether the budget cap affects the optimal program mix, and consider how a carbon tax effective January 1, 2014, might alter the 2014 supply plan.

Excerpts from the TMS320DM814x DaVinci Digital Media Processors data manual (Texas Instruments, 2012–2014) covering subsystem overviews, memory maps, device pin tables, and boot/device configuration.

**Subsystems**
- **System MMU:** All C674x MDMA port accesses pass through the system MMU and are remapped to physical system addresses, protecting ARM Cortex-A8 memory regions from accidental corruption and allowing direct user-space buffer allocation without ARM/DSP translation. EDMA TC0 and TC1 may optionally be routed through the MMU, letting EDMA Channels 0 and 1 transfer using only known virtual buffer addresses; the Control Module's MMU_CFG register enables/disables this for the EDMA TCs.
- **Media Controller:** Manages the HDVPSS and ISS modules.
- **HDVICP2:** A video encoder/decoder accelerator supporting encode, decode, and transcode for MPEG1/2/4 ASP/SP, H.264 BL/MP/HP, VC-1 SP/MP/AP, RV9/10, AVS-1.0, and ON2 VP6.2/VP7, composed of a sequencer with its memories and an interrupt controller.
- **Face Detection (FD):** Performs face detection and tracking on a picture in memory (used for video encoding, face-based priority auto-focusing, red-eye removal). It supports QVGA (320 × 240) 8-bit luma inputs in DRR memory, uses 51.25 KB of DDR working memory, supports minimum face sizes of 20, 25, 32, or 40 pixels, and reports size, position, angle, and confidence level per face.
- **Spinlock:** Provides hardware synchronization for processes on multiple cores through 128 spinlocks (hardware semaphores) whose lock operation needs only a single read access instead of a read-modify-write transfer.
- **Mailbox:** Facilitates communication between the ARM Cortex-A8, the C674x DSP, and between the two processors, with messages written to mailbox registers and interrupts signaling queued messages or overflow. Features include flexible mailbox-to-processor assignment, four-message FIFO depth per queue, reception/queue-not-full notification via interrupts, and four interrupts (one to Cortex-A8, one to C674x, two to Media Controller).

**Memory:** The device has multiple on-chip memories and uses a unified memory map so all bus masters see resources consistently. Tables provide the L3 map for all masters (including Cortex-A8), the C674x map (C674x access limited to McASPx, McBSP, UARTx, I2Cx, SPIx, EDMA, GPIO/INT, GPMC, DDRx, EMAC, PCIe, Timers, USB), the L4 fast and slow peripheral domains, and the DDR DMM TILER Extended Addressing Map, where a 33rd address bit adds a 4-GB range for rotated/mirrored frame-buffer views accessible only to HDVPSS and ISS (other masters access one view via the 512-MB TILER region of the base 4-GB map). C674x addresses 0x1000_0000–0x10FF_FFFF map to internal 0x0000_0000–0x00FF_FFFF.

**Device pins:** Eight package pin maps (A–H) are shown. Terminal functions tables list signal names, multiplexing, ball numbers, package designator, pin type (I, O, Z, S, A, GND), internal pull state (IPU/IPD/DIS), supply voltage source, and pin functions. The MUXED column shows multiplexed functions, the controlling PINCNTLx register, the de-selected input state (DSIS), and the Multi-Muxed (MM) option. Tables cover boot configuration, camera I/F, DCAN, DDR2/DDR3 controllers 0 and 1, EMAC0/EMAC1 (MII/GMII, RMII, RGMII), GP0–GP3, GPMC, HDMI, I2C, McASP0–5, PCIe, RESET/interrupts/JTAG, SD0–SD2, SPI, oscillator/PLL and clock generator, timers, UART0–UART5, USB0/USB1, video input/output 0 and 1, analog TV output, and supply voltages.

**Boot configuration:** Post-boot device state is set by sampling BTMODE[15:0] when reset is de-asserted; values are latched into the Control Module's CONTROL_STATUS register. BTMODE[15:11] set GPMC CS0 default data bus width, wait enable, and address/data multiplexing; BTMODE[4:0] select boot mode order, with the first mode primary and later modes tried if it fails; BTMODE[7:5] are reserved and pulled down; BTMODE[9:8] select Ethernet PHY mode in EMAC boot; BTMODE[10] selects GPMC muxing Option A/B for XIP modes (Option B reconfigures select-pin pulls to IPD, staying IPD after boot); BTMODE[15:12] determine PCIe addressing options. Tables list ROM-configured pins for NAND flash, NAND I2C (EEPROM), MMC/SD, SPI, EMAC, PCIe, and UART boot modes.

**Pin multiplexing:** Controlled per pin by MUXMODE bits of PINCNTL1–PINCNTL270. The default MUXMODE = 0x0 3-states the pin's I/O buffer; inputs are usually routed to all sharing peripherals, though some pins feed a constant 0 or 1 to the associated peripheral when its function is not selected (DSIS). Some functions are Multimuxed (MM) across multiple pins with differing switching characteristics and timing requirements per option.

The lecture introduces MIT’s course on effective field theory (EFT), which requires quantum field theory II, assigns selected quantum field theory III material as background, and uses five problem sets and a final student presentation instead of exams. The first half of the course covers general EFT concepts, while the second focuses on soft-collinear effective theory and its applications to LHC jet physics.

EFT reverses the traditional bottom-up progression of physics by focusing on a particular scale and constructing the simplest theory that captures the relevant physics. It retains higher-order terms in an expansion, allowing systematic corrections and, in principle, arbitrary precision. Examples include nonrelativistic quantum mechanics as a limit of quantum field theory and Newtonian gravity as a limit of general relativity.

Constructing an EFT requires identifying the relevant degrees of freedom, determining the symmetries, establishing the expansion parameter and power counting, and writing the leading-order Lagrangian. Power counting is fundamental to the consistency of the theory and is as important as gauge symmetry. The general guiding principle is decoupling: physics at scales distant from the process under study need not be explicitly retained. Although mass-scale ratios are the classic example, EFT expansions can also use quantities such as velocity, as in nonrelativistic QED.

Hydrogen illustrates several EFT expansions. Heavy quarks and the internal quark structure of the proton can be neglected at low momentum transfer, while nonrelativistic expansions describe the electron and proton dynamics. Integrating out heavy fields may generate higher-order operators and can also change the definition or value of leading-order couplings. Such conclusions remain valid after ultraviolet divergences are regulated.

EFTs are used in two ways. In a top-down approach, a known high-energy theory is expanded by removing irrelevant degrees of freedom and matching it onto a lower-energy theory. The theories agree in infrared observables but may differ in ultraviolet behavior. Matching determines allowed operators and low-energy constants, and the expansion is truncated according to the required precision. Heavy-quark EFT, nonrelativistic QED and QCD, and soft-collinear EFT are presented as examples.

In a bottom-up approach, the high-energy theory may be unknown or too difficult to use for explicit matching. The low-energy theory is instead constructed from its degrees of freedom, symmetries, and power counting by writing the most general consistent operators. Its unknown higher-dimensional couplings can be fitted to experimental data. Chiral perturbation theory, the Standard Model, and quantum gravity are given as examples.

EFT power counting and renormalization also organize logarithmic divergences and can allow infinite logarithmic series to be summed. One example discussed is a disputed higher-order correction to hydrogen energy levels, whose ambiguity was resolved through consistency within an EFT description.

The lecture then applies these ideas to the Standard Model as an EFT. Its leading-order theory contains the gauge, fermion, and Higgs sectors, while omitted higher-energy physics—such as possible grand-unification, supersymmetry, or Planck-scale effects—sets the expansion. Corrections are expressed through higher-dimensional operators built from Standard Model fields. In EFT, renormalizability means that ultraviolet divergences can be absorbed into a finite number of parameters at each order in the expansion, even though the full theory may contain infinitely many operators. Traditional renormalizability is presented as a special case, while theories such as chiral perturbation theory require higher-dimensional operators to remain consistent.

During a 10-day family road trip through Badlands, Glacier, Yellowstone, and Devil’s Tower, the author reflects on weather, risk, and climate change. The passage explains the Draw play, a run play designed to look like a pass play briefly before a late handoff, intended to exploit a defense's commitment to passing and get defenders spread out. It is most effective in pass-heavy offenses and obvious passing situations, where defenses may play three defensive linemen with linebackers 10 yards off the ball. Its biggest weakness is against blitzes, because linemen are locked in one-on-one blocks with no one left to block an unaccounted-for interior rusher; offenses therefore tag an RPO to the draw. Detailed assignments are given for the Draw play against a 3-4 odd front (with the left guard climbing and the center driving the nose tackle) and against a 4-3 even front (with double teams on the nose tackle by the center and a guard). Two variations are described: QB Draw, for an athletic quarterback, often tagged with a perimeter RPO, and Lead Draw, run from 12-personnel Strong-I with different release, double-team, and insert assignments, which requires the offense to show it routinely passes from that set.

Lamtara and Bouziane examined teachers’ perspectives on the barriers to sustaining ICT use in Moroccan compulsory education after COVID-19. A 2023 survey included 297 primary and secondary teachers, focusing on the 130 who had stopped using technology after classes resumed. Findings identified limited access to devices, reliable internet, digital resources and training, as well as insufficient technology and techno-pedagogical knowledge, weak institutional support and a lack of incentives. Geographic, urban-rural and public-private disparities also affected access to ICT.

The study evaluates educational leadership against five ISTE standards: equity and digital citizenship, visionary planning, teacher and student empowerment, systems design, and continuous professional learning. This first-principles study examines how stacking geometry governs magnetic energy scales in chromium diiodide (CrI2) bilayers, a van der Waals magnet whose bulk phase is ferromagnetic while its monolayer is antiferromagnetic. Density functional theory was performed with Quantum ESPRESSO (PBEsol pseudopotentials, DFT-D3(BJ) dispersion, DFT+U with U = 3.1 eV and J = 0.1 eV); exchange tensors were obtained with OpenMX and TB2J via the magnetic force theorem, with and without spin–orbit coupling.

The CrI2 monolayer adopts the 1T structure with edge-sharing CrI6 octahedra. Among four collinear orders (FM, AFx, AFy, AFz), the stripe antiferromagnet AFx is the ground state (AFz +4.85, AFy +5.49, FM +7.14 meV/Cr), stable for U < 6 eV, with moments of ~4.2 µB/Cr, and it is a narrow-gap semiconductor (Eg ≈ 1.12 eV) with anisotropic dispersion and hybridized Cr-d/I-p band edges.

For bilayers, direct (AA, AB, BA) and indirect (AA′, AB′, BA′) stackings were compared across four interlayer magnetic alignments. The indirect BA′ stacking with antiparallel interlayer coupling (↑↓/↓↑) is the global energy minimum; AB′ follows closely, while direct and high-symmetry registries lie 25–50 meV/f.u. higher. Inversion-plus-lateral displacement in prime stackings reduces iodine–iodine repulsion. Average in-plane lattice constants are 7.24 and 3.89 Å with an average interlayer distance of 3.42 Å (σ = 0.29 Å). Bilayer band gaps (0.99–1.07 eV) are reduced relative to the monolayer by interlayer I-pz/Cr-d hybridization, with a non-monotonic dependence on separation. Broken inversion in BA′ yields avoided crossings and spin splittings driven by exchange in a polar structure (8.3/11.6 meV at Γ for parallel alignment versus 5.0/3.2 meV for antiparallel).

Controlled lateral sliding maps corrugated potential energy surfaces connecting all high-symmetry registries with barriers of ~25–50 meV/f.u.; sliding thus toggles inversion symmetry and with it DMI and ferroelectricity, and interlayer separation follows the registry.

Exchange parameters show that intralayer interactions dominate: the antiferromagnetic inter-chain A–B coupling strengthens from −3.66 meV (monolayer) to −3.95 ± 0.06 meV averaged over bilayers (~8–10%), and the ferromagnetic intra-chain A–A/B–B coupling rises from 2.56 to 2.72 ± 0.04 meV (~6%), with Cr–Cr distances nearly unchanged (4.10–4.11 Å), implicating orbital hybridization rather than bond-length changes. Symmetric in-plane anisotropy is nearly registry-independent (ΔJxy ≈ 1.48 meV for A–B, ≈ 1.03 meV for A–A/B–B), whereas DMI is symmetry-forbidden in the centrosymmetric monolayer and appears (0.01–0.02 meV in-plane) only in inversion-breaking stackings. Interlayer exchange is an order of magnitude weaker, with |Jiso| ≈ 0.03–0.07 meV, a sign that depends on both registry and interlayer spin texture, and small but registry-dependent DMI and anisotropy (up to 0.08 meV and 0.36 meV in AA′); second-neighbour interlayer couplings stay below 0.2 meV.

Spin-resolved band centers indicate a spin-selective superexchange pathway: majority Cr-d↑ (−2.42 eV) nearly matches I-p (−2.56 eV), while minority Cr-d↓ lies at 3.32 eV (mismatch ~5.94 eV), reproducing this pattern in BA′ bilayers, consistent with an Anderson–Goodenough–Kanamori picture for high-spin Cr²⁺ (d⁴).

Symmetry analysis shows indirect stackings permit an in-plane polarization Px (Berry-phase values of a few µC/cm², up to ~10 µC/cm², reduced by spin–orbit coupling) alongside finite DMI, offering a stacking fingerprint detectable by second-harmonic generation or photocurrent spectroscopy. Overall, intralayer exchange sets the primary energy scale, stacking symmetry selects the anisotropic and chiral terms, and weak interlayer exchange provides secondary tunability, suggesting applications in stacking-controlled nonvolatile memory, registry-sensitive optical detectors, and mechanically reconfigurable spintronic and multiferroic devices.

This fictional case by Evan Mulbry and Andrew Sutherland (April 3, 2024) concerns RiseEngineer Corporation, a NYSE-listed green design and construction firm. Marsha Jackson, newly promoted to Head of Internal Audit, oversees financial controls and FCPA compliance, including RiseEngineer Elysium, the local subsidiary of the U.S. parent in a country ranking low on Transparency International's Corruption Perceptions Index.

A whistleblower hotline message alleges misconduct in RiseEngineer's Elysium contract win. Investigation found RiseEngineer's $1.2 billion bid was accepted among five bidders (range $800 million–$1.25 billion); the contract spans 12 months. Findings included dinners and small gifts exchanged with officials, a Boston facility tour attended by officials' families, monthly $100 million government wire payments of which $90 million was transferred to headquarters, a $3 million wire to an offshore consultant (TGH Consulting) hired before the bid, $5 million in largely undocumented cash withdrawals, and a sales email expressing discomfort. The subsidiary was also its auditor's only client; two employees suggested a disgruntled former employee filed the claim falsely.

An internal controls report showed subsidiary head Sarah Smith prioritizing profitability, with five salespeople earning $100,000 uncapped commissions, autonomy in customer relationships, pricing, and consultant hiring, and deference to sales over other departments. The finance manager handled all accounting entries and most transactions, permitted undocumented withdrawals and transfers without separate approval, and estimated accounting for uncertain transactions.

Exhibits describe COSO's five internal control elements and the FCPA, which prohibits bribing foreign officials worldwide, treats non-monetary benefits as bribes, requires books-and-records and internal controls for public companies and subsidiaries, and is enforced by the SEC and DOJ with civil and criminal penalties. Discussion questions address the whistleblower's credibility, problematic transactions, control changes for international bids, and the roles of auditors, the board, regulators, and company personnel.

Soccer players specialize by position within a formation but should learn all positions, especially at youth level, to understand their requirements and avoid being type-cast. Coaches must select a suitable formation, assign position names, and use them consistently. For an 11-player team, the general positions are goalkeeper, defenders, midfielders, and forwards.

The goalkeeper is the only position named in the IFAB Laws of the Game, has the privilege of handling the ball within his own penalty area, and must wear a jersey contrasting with other players and the referee. Defenders protect the goal, cover opponents, win the ball, and block shots. Midfielders defend, link defenders and forwards, support attacks, and require broad skills and fitness. Forwards create and convert scoring opportunities through runs, passes, possession, and shooting.

Specific position names reflect formations and numbers of players. Defenders include fullbacks, center backs, stoppers, sweepers, and liberos. Midfielders include central midfielders, attacking or defensive midfielders, holding or passing midfielders, outside midfielders, wing backs, and wide midfielders. Forward roles include center forwards, inside forwards, wingers, strikers, withdrawn forwards, secondary or supporting strikers, and wide strikers. Acronyms are often used in coaching, though “ST” may mean either stopper or striker.

Monitoring systems can apply the adapter pattern to unify varied application monitoring interfaces. A separate adapter container transforms each application’s format into the monitoring system’s expected interface. This decoupling simplifies maintenance, permits independent application and adapter updates, allows adapter reuse, and provides dedicated CPU and memory for each adapter.

The article demonstrates backtesting a Bollinger Band strategy in Python using historical Microsoft data from yfinance. It calculates 20-day simple moving averages and standard deviations with pandas to form upper and lower bands set two standard deviations from the average. Using NumPy, it generates buy and sell positions based on adjusted closes crossing below the lower band or above the upper band, calculates daily strategy returns from lagged positions, and plots cumulative returns as an equity curve. The tested strategy compounded money at 2.65% annually while invested 10.6% of the time and is presented for informational purposes.

Skoltech researchers developed a mathematical model of memory engrams—conceptual representations formed from sensory features. They found that memory capacity in a steady-state conceptual space is maximized at seven dimensions, leading them to propose that seven senses may be optimal. The result was robust across model details, but its implications for actual human senses remain speculative. The model may advance understanding of learning, forgetting, and memory while informing robotics and artificial-intelligence research.

Larry Williams introduced the Williams Vix Fix in 2007 as a synthetic volatility indicator for instruments beyond major stock indexes. It measures trailing 22-day price volatility using the highest close and current low, making it a lagging indicator. Its levels, swings, magnitude, and timing closely resemble the VIX, which measures one-month implied volatility and reflects market fear or complacency.

The passage reports several strategy tests. One S&P 500 strategy generated 322 trades since 1993, averaged 0.5% per trade, had a 2.0 profit factor, and a 23% maximum drawdown. PercentRank-based versions also produced positive results. An improved QQQ strategy traded 352 times since 1999, averaged nearly 1% per trade, had a 75% win rate and 20% maximum drawdown, and returned 12.7% versus 9.2% for buy-and-hold while invested only 20% of the time. Williams did not publish specific strategies, leaving room for experimentation. Overall, the indicator appeared effective for stock indexes, including on the short side, but it was not tested on other asset classes.

Melania Trump is hosting technology executives to discuss cyberbullying and internet safety, her first public event on the issue since identifying it as a first-lady priority. Amazon, Snap, Facebook, Google, Twitter and the Internet Association are expected to attend. Major platforms have anti-harassment policies and educational tools but largely depend on users to report abuse. Persistent bullying includes cruel posts, embarrassing images and circulated private messages, affecting adults and teenagers. Twitter introduced protections for women whose nude images were shared without consent, while Yik Yak shut down partly after complaints and school bans. The scale of online content complicates moderation, and companies struggle to curb harassment while protecting free expression; Twitter has declined calls to suspend President Trump despite complaints about his tweets. No federal bullying law exists, and state requirements vary. Cyberbullying Research Center co-director Sameer Hinduja said federal funding and tools for school programs would help. Trump has also emphasized child well-being, limiting children’s online time, kindness and compassion.

The passage compiles global finance, technology and business headlines, with its main article focused on Opera’s launch of Neon, an AI-powered browser designed to complete tasks such as filling forms, comparing information across sites and writing code. Neon can navigate pages autonomously while operating locally, alongside workflow-management features and reusable prompts for recurring actions. Opera is offering immediate early access, plans broader availability and is positioning the subscription product for power users in the “agentic browsing” market alongside Comet and Dia. The article notes that adoption will require reliability, compliance, safety, transparency and regulatory oversight. Other headlines address JPMorgan Chase’s AI integration, the Bank of England’s six-month repo allocation, instant-payment systems, a BRICS rupee bond, stock markets, U.S. chip policy, OpenAI parental controls, Singapore’s scrutiny of Meta, energy and infrastructure investments, and financial-market developments. The passage also describes Pan Finance and related global financial publications.

Tennessee middle schooler Keaton Jones gained national attention after his mother posted a Facebook video of him tearfully describing school bullying, including name-calling, insults, and having milk poured on him. He asked why people bully others, encouraged victims to stay strong, and said conditions may improve. His sister Lakyn Jones served as his representative as thousands of support offers arrived.

College and professional athletes, celebrities, sports figures, and Tennessee senators encouraged Keaton and promoted awareness of bullying. Among those reaching out were Jarrett Guarantano, LeBron James, Gal Gadot, Chris Evans, Mark Ruffalo, Millie Bobby Brown, and ESPN’s Jemele Hill. Invitations, tickets, friendship offers, and other assistance were extended to Keaton and his family.

The attention also prompted criticism after reports that Keaton’s mother, Kimberly Jones, had posted images of Confederate flags. Lakyn defended her family and said their faith could not be shaken. A GoFundMe campaign started for Keaton and his mother raised more than $58,000 before its creator, Joseph Lam, paused donations and comments. Lam said the campaign was not about his mother and that judging her before knowing her was itself a form of bullying. He hoped the funds would support Keaton’s education. Hill maintained her invitation to Keaton while criticizing what she called “selective empathy.”

Warby Parker is presented as an attractive investment as it expands retail presence and customers, benefits from rising selling prices and new products, and maintains high margins despite tariffs. FY25 guidance calls for 14%–15% revenue growth and nearly two points of margin expansion, with continued double-digit growth expected in FY26. The author reiterates a Buy rating, citing Warby Parker’s brand, margin expansion, and growth runway despite a premium valuation, and discloses a long position in WRBY.

Karuna Nundy, 42, is a lawyer and Supreme Court advocate featured in Verve's 2018 (Em)Power List. A drafter of the Womanifesto, a bill of rights intended to change laws on crimes against women, she campaigns for anti-rape and workplace sexual harassment laws, represents rape survivors, and sought justice for victims of the Bhopal gas tragedy.

The disclosure describes footwear sole structures incorporating traction elements. An outsole includes a plantar surface, a surrounding peripheral surface, an annular cleat set arranged about a central axis, and one or more radial cleat sets extending along intersecting radial axes. The cleats may include major, minor, and peripheral elements with varying heights, tapered widths, reinforcing ribs, and arrangements in the forefoot, toe, and heel regions. The outsole may use separate forefoot and heel plates, including modular shells, skeletons, and inserts. A sole structure combines the outsole with a cushioned midsole, a rigid shank, and a cradle, with the midsole optionally comprising a casing and core. The disclosed configurations provide traction in lateral and longitudinal directions, permit rotation about the central axis, and allow different material properties to be used throughout the sole structure.

Founded in 1977, The Motz Corporation serves the natural and synthetic turf markets and operates The Motz Group and USGreentech. The company recently became employee-owned through an ESOP, allowing employees to share beneficial ownership while retaining its existing management structure, with Joe Motz as CEO and Zach Burns, Valerie Webster, and Kevin McDonnell in their current leadership roles. The Motz Group designs, constructs, and manages natural and synthetic sports fields, while USGreentech develops infill products for sports fields, putting greens, and residential and commercial lawns.

Coach Julien says his team has performed well throughout the playoffs but wants to improve over full games. He credits better puck movement, confidence and power-play execution, while describing the team as calm, confident on the road and resistant to panic when facing deficits. Julien says players should remain comfortable in themselves, while coaches balance respect with authority, make lineup decisions and adapt as players seek more input. He emphasizes choosing the better line matchup, regardless of deployment concerns, and praises Dennis Seidenberg’s hard play, size, strength and battle, saying those qualities fit the team.

This edition publishes documents chiefly from the Department of State and American Commission to Negotiate Peace files, supplemented by records from Wilson, Lansing, Bliss, White, Long, Miller, and House held by the Library of Congress and Yale University. The series generally ends with the commission’s departure from Paris on December 9, 1919, and follows selection guidelines approved by Secretary of State Frank B. Kellogg for earlier *Foreign Relations* volumes. Important records will appear substantially complete, while secondary material will be omitted. The project was undertaken under Cyril Wynne and is directed by Ernest R. Perkins, with James S. Beddie, Morrison B. Giffen, and John W. Foley Jr. compiling the volumes and Matilda F. Axton directing editorial work. The text lists principal treaties and persons and outlines sections on the armistice, American preparations, national representation, U.S. and Allied policies, League of Nations proposals, and other conference agenda items.
