Lewis Williams will seek two wins for the 91kg Three Nations title in Rotherham, potentially becoming Britain’s number two. Josh Finch will also face Cameron Hatton on June 8.

Weybridge Orthodontics offers Invisalign for mild-to-moderate tooth misalignment using custom-made transparent aligners created from 3D scans. Patients wear each pair for 7–10 days, with treatment typically lasting 12–18 months. Removable aligners allow eating and brushing, while simulations preview expected improvements in alignment, appearance, cleaning and jaw strain.

Several research teams have used compact, laser-driven accelerators to generate artificial muon beams, potentially enabling fast, portable scanners for shipping containers and other dense materials. Berkeley Lab researchers accelerated electrons to as much as 10 billion electron volts and produced multi-billion-electron-volt muons in a setup about a bowling-pin length long, far shorter than a conventional accelerator. Teams at ELI-NP in Romania and Shanghai’s Superintense Ultrafast Laser Facility also reported laser-produced muons at energies up to roughly one billion electron volts.

Muons penetrate dense materials and can reveal their contents by measuring absorption or scattering. Natural atmospheric muons are too scarce for rapid scanning. Colorado State University researchers demonstrated an image of a lead object using a laser-produced muon beam and detector inside a truck. Researchers said further advances in laser technology could eventually make muon sources portable.

South32 abandoned its US$200 million purchase of Peabody Energy’s Metropolitan coking coal mine after anticipated concessions to local steelmakers raised competition concerns. The deal would have made South32 the only large coking coal supplier in eastern Illawarra. Peabody will retain the mine and its 16.67% stake in the Port Kembla coal terminal and resume shipments after moving to a new coal panel.

President Donald Trump has met with Jared Isaacman to discuss another nomination to lead NASA after withdrawing his original nomination. Trump cited Isaacman’s Democratic affiliation and close ties to SpaceX CEO Elon Musk as concerns, though relations between Trump and Musk have since cooled. Isaacman, who leads Polaris Dawn and founded Shift4, led private SpaceX spaceflights in 2021 and 2024.

The paper develops mean-field pseudospin models for the long-range polarization ordering and electric-field switching of two phenyltetrazole crystals, APHTZ and MPHTZ. Proton positions, switchable tetrazole π-bonds, and ionic displacements define effective dipoles represented by Ising pseudospins.

APHTZ is modeled as two alternating chain sublattices. Its ground state, FE-I, is ferroelectric along the a axis and antiferroelectric along the b axis; a transverse field along b is predicted to switch it to FE-II, producing a 90° rotation of net polarization. Preliminary mean-field parameters give a transition near 425 K and a tricritical point near 409 K. The predicted transverse switching is first order below the tricritical point and second order above it, with a double hysteresis loop.

MPHTZ is modeled using four chain sublattices that reduce to a two-sublattice checkerboard antiferroelectric arrangement. Parameters fitted to available 300 K polarization data predict an antiferroelectric-to-ferroelectric transition near 421 K and a tricritical point near 413 K. Field-induced switching is first order at low temperatures and second order above the tricritical point, with switching-field behavior closely matching the available measurements.

The models reproduce standard mean-field Ising critical behavior, including square-root order-parameter scaling, Curie-Weiss permittivity laws, and field–temperature phase diagrams with tricritical points. Agreement with available measurements is encouraging, but the scarcity of experimental data leaves the parameters and especially the APHTZ predictions partly qualitative. Further polarization, permittivity, switching, and transition measurements are needed. Proposed extensions include combined longitudinal and transverse fields, improved intrachain-correlation treatments, electrocaloric studies, and more detailed modeling of the parent PHTZ phase mixture.

This study examined whether genetic variants in vitamin B12 metabolism contribute to Parkinson’s disease (PD) risk, age at onset, or progression. Analyses of common variants, two pathway-specific polygenic risk scores, rare variants from UK Biobank and AMP-PD, Mendelian randomization, and genetic correlation found no robust associations. Two polygenic scores showed nominal significance but did not withstand multiple-testing correction. A rare CUBN variant signal was not replicated across cohorts or significant in meta-analysis. Mendelian randomization detected no causal relationship between B12 levels and PD risk, onset, or progression, and no genetic correlation was found. Limitations included restriction to European-ancestry participants, insufficient power for progression analyses, and unavailable LRRK2-related PD data. The authors suggested that gastrointestinal dysfunction, reduced intake, and gut microbiota alterations may contribute to lower B12 levels in PD and that addressing deficiency remains important.

Lorna Gibson concludes a lecture on energy absorption in foams by explaining how compressive stress–strain curves can be converted into log–log energy-absorption diagrams. Tests at fixed strain rate and temperature are performed on foams of different relative densities, and both absorbed energy and peak stress are normalized by the solid modulus. The linear-elastic, plateau, and densification regions correspond to distinct parts of each diagram. The “shoulder point,” where maximum energy is absorbed without increasing peak stress beyond the plateau, represents optimal foam use. Connecting shoulder points across densities, strain rates, and temperatures produces a compact design diagram.

For elastomeric foams, normalization by the solid modulus allows one diagram to represent all such foams because both their Young’s modulus and plateau stress scale with that modulus. For foams with plastic collapse, the diagram is valid only for materials having the same ratio of solid yield strength to solid modulus. Model-based diagrams can be generated by dividing behavior into elastic, plateau, and densification stages. For open-cell elastomeric foams, the lecture uses \(E=E_s\rho_r^2\), plateau stress \(0.05E_s\rho_r^2\), and densification strain \(1-1.4\rho_r\); the resulting shoulder-point line is \(W/E_s=(\sigma_p/E_s)[1-6.26(\sigma_p/E_s)^{1/2}]\). At full densification, the curve approaches the solid-material limit \(W/E_s=\tfrac12(\sigma_p/E_s)^2\), with foams greatly outperforming the solid. Variants account for closed-cell gas contributions and plastic collapse.

The diagrams are applied to impact protection by using mass, contact area, drop height, deceleration limit, material modulus, foam density, and thickness to estimate impact energy, allowable peak stress, and strain rate. One iterative example for a 0.5-kilogram package converges to roughly 0.15-meter-thick polyurethane foam with relative density near 0.01. A second example, with 20-millimeter thickness specified, yields an estimated solid modulus of 28 megapascals and relative density near 0.1. A bicycle-helmet example selects 5%-dense expanded polystyrene and estimates a maximum impact speed of about 22 miles per hour.

The lecture then turns to woodpeckers. Despite claims that they possess special protective material, studies have found no such material. High-speed measurements from 1979 recorded impacts near 15 miles per hour, decelerations up to about 1,500 times gravity, and stopping times around \(1/500\) to \(1/1000\) second. A scaling analysis attributes their tolerance partly to smaller brain size, brain orientation, and shorter impact duration, while anatomical adaptations include a tongue-supporting hyoid apparatus, stiff tail feathers, and zygodactyl feet. The next lecture will cover engineered and natural sandwich panels, including bird skulls.

Niantic announced that Pokémon GO’s Generation II update would arrive later in the week, adding more than 80 Johto Pokémon that would be discoverable “in the wild” as soon as the update went live. The update would also introduce evolution items obtained from PokéStops, Nanab Berries that make Pokémon slower and easier to hit, Pinap Berries that double candy from a successful catch, new avatar clothing, and unspecified “encounter gameplay.” A trailer showed a berry shortcut, a Pokéball drawer, and a relocated camera button, along with Pokémon in less populated outdoor locations.

Niantic did not specify an exact release date or clarify the remaining Generation II Pokémon not included in the “over 80” count. Tracking improvements, trading, and player-versus-player battling were also absent from the announced update. Screenshots additionally suggested Pokémon genders and an Evolve button that previews evolution choices, though these details were not fully confirmed. The release was described as the game’s largest addition of Pokémon since launch and was expected to bring back players who had stopped playing.
Charleston’s council is expected Monday to consider revised carriage horse heat rules; one tour company uses body cameras to document heckling or abuse.

Collected material was to be filed and digested under Dr. Mezes, edited by Mezes and Lippmann, and made readily accessible through the librarian, Andrew Keogh, and cataloguer Miss Wilson. The Inquiry had functioning administrative machinery and drew personnel from institutions across the United States and abroad.

By February 15, researchers were to assemble reliable secondary-source material on the Baltic-to-Persian Gulf region, Central African colonial issues, Central Powers’ immediate economic needs, and freedom of the seas. The loan carries 13% annual interest, a 1% renewal fee, and a 1% extension fee. The Oct. 5, 2000 “Inside UT Football” column by Dallas Morning News Texas writer Chip Brown answered subscriber questions about the Longhorns ahead of their matchup with Oklahoma. Oklahoma coach Bob Stoops said his 4-0 team was more mature, confident, physically stronger and more confident in its running game, while citing turnovers and Texas’s failure to protect a 17-0 lead in the previous year’s 38-28 loss as reasons for Oklahoma’s three-game losing streak against Texas.

Brown viewed the offenses as evenly matched but favored Texas’s defense, predicting a 24-20 Longhorns win and noting that turnovers could change the game’s complexion. Major Applewhite was expected to start against Oklahoma and play most or all of the game, while Chris Simms could return during the rotation against Missouri. Brown said Applewhite might have been a Heisman Trophy candidate had he been the unquestioned starter. The matchup between Oklahoma’s receivers and Texas’s young secondary was identified as a key contest. Sean Rogers was doubtful because of a sprained ankle.

Texas’s offense showed improvement against Oklahoma State through a gap-blocking scheme, but the offensive line, punt protection and special teams remained concerns. Freshman defensive end Adam Doiron was considered for a redshirt or a role at defensive tackle. Brown also discussed Royal-Memorial Stadium’s potential expansion, Texas’s Big 12-record scoring streak of 231 consecutive games, next year’s schedule, and the possibility of using the shotgun more frequently.

Brown argued that Texas needed experience, chemistry and leadership to become a consistent top program, but that its recruiting and depth could make it a powerhouse within two or three years. He defended Mack Brown against mounting criticism and urged patience with offensive-line coach Tim Nunez. Other topics included possible freshman punt returns, David Aaron leaving football for track, the drought-damaged field, the planned move of the Houston game to Robertson Stadium, and the October 14 Colorado game, scheduled for 2:30 p.m. Central time and not televised.

The coach expects a power play during the series and says an absent player remains valuable for his physical presence, net-front positioning, and potential power-play impact. He praises the opponent’s efficiency and says his team must apply pressure, finish checks, and force defense without losing position. The latest game was fast and competitive, with timely goals, a powerful shot from Benny, and strong contributions from the goalie and Antti. However, the coach says his team spent too much time in its own end, allowed too much quality, and needs greater puck possession in the offensive zone. A low-ice-time line provided energy, speed, hitting, forechecking, and offensive-zone pressure. For the next road game, the team must improve and prepare for a difficult match in a loud building.

Deep neural networks divide matrix-multiplication outputs into tiles distributed across GPU SMs. NVIDIA’s A100 has 108 SMs versus V100’s 80 and third-generation Tensor Cores delivering mixed-precision performance 16 times standard FP32 FMA operations, compared with Volta’s 8x speedup. Ampere optimizations improve Tensor Core utilization and programmability while reducing software complexity, memory bandwidth use, latency, and overhead, supporting fixed-workload strong scaling as Tensor Cores consume data 2.5x faster than V100.

After the loss, the coach said the team regrouped with a good practice, emphasizing simplicity, getting the puck deep, fore-checking, and basic execution. He blamed poor puck support, neutral-zone play, and a lack of skating speed, noting opponents improved each round but the system and expectations have not changed and no excuses are accepted. He said pulling out Game 2 leaves them in the same position as against the Rangers and they must win Game 1. Comparing Detroit's trap to New Jersey's and Buffalo's less effective versions, he stressed filling lines and fore-checking. He acknowledged a bad line change and lost puck on Yzerman's power-play goal, and said the power play made mistakes while praising Ron's play without calling him the reason for the loss. He also said overthinking matchups may be a mistake and that playing simple hockey, as they have on the road, could work.

Federal courts plan to continue most operations and pay staff through Oct. 17 during the government shutdown using funds not tied to new appropriations. Judges’ salaries are constitutionally protected, and most deadlines remain unchanged, though hearings and filings may be rescheduled because executive-branch attorneys are unavailable. If funds run out, courts must follow the Antideficiency Act, potentially requiring staff to work unpaid or be furloughed.

Andrew Lo reviews Lehman Brothers at the end of 2007, when it reported $19 billion in net revenue, $4 billion in net income, $145 billion in long-term capital, $282 billion in assets under management, and 28,500 employees. He uses mortgages to illustrate leverage: buying a $500,000 home with 20% down creates 5-to-1 leverage, while 5% down creates 20-to-1 leverage. A 10% decline in home prices would erase half the equity in the first case and wipe out all the investor’s capital in the second. Lehman’s 16-to-1 leverage therefore allowed relatively small asset declines to rapidly exhaust its capital.

Lo attributes the mortgage crisis partly to low housing-price volatility, which encouraged high leverage, followed by sharply increased volatility. Subprime mortgages, adjustable teaser rates, financial engineering, and expanded derivatives helped enlarge the housing market but worsened losses when prices fell. Most mortgages were nonrecourse, allowing banks to seize homes but not pursue other assets; borrowers facing unaffordable payments often surrendered the properties, damaging their credit but potentially borrowing again later. Rising defaults also made subprime credit harder to obtain. The Federal Reserve’s expected rate cut was intended to reduce defaults and pressure but carried an inflation risk.

After the Fed declined to guarantee Lehman’s acquisition and Barclays declined to proceed without a backstop, Lehman filed for Chapter 11. The extent of losses and creditors’ recoveries remained uncertain, while shareholders’ stock fell from $62 at year-end 2007 to zero. Lo argued that concerns about Lehman’s viability destroyed its franchise value even though its employees remained capable. He compared the collapse with Bear Stearns, noting Lehman’s larger exposure, and expected short-term hiring chaos followed by stronger employment opportunities.

Lo then distinguishes inflation from the time value of money. Inflation measures changes in purchasing power through a consumption-price index. Nominal returns reflect changes in dollar wealth, while real returns account for changes in the cost of living. The real return is approximately the nominal return minus inflation, and nominal cash flows must be discounted with nominal rates while real cash flows use real rates.

The lecture transitions to fixed-income securities, which provide known contractual payoffs and include Treasury, federal-agency, corporate, municipal, mortgage-backed, asset-backed, collateralized, and swap-related instruments. At the end of 2006, U.S. mortgage-related securities alone totaled $6.4 trillion, illustrating that bond markets greatly exceeded equity markets in size. Fixed-income markets were less liquid because many securities traded infrequently, especially complex instruments. Participants included issuers, investors, and intermediaries such as dealers, investment banks, rating agencies, insurers, and liquidity providers. Lo used the 1987 crash to show how leveraged dealers acting as market makers could be forced to buy during a collapse and rapidly lose their capital.

For valuation, Lo explains that a three-year, 5% coupon bond with a $1,000 face value can be priced by discounting its $50 annual coupons and $1,050 maturity payment. Market prices determine the discount rates, so prices also convey collective expectations about future rates. Pure discount bonds pay only at maturity and are valued by discounting face value; Treasury STRIPS separate coupon and principal payments from underlying coupon bonds. Lo identifies inflation, credit, timing, liquidity, and currency risks, initially focusing on default-free U.S. Treasury securities. At the lecture’s end, he predicts with 99.5% confidence, based on market prices, that the Federal Reserve will cut interest rates the next day.

The U.S. Supreme Court preliminarily allowed the Trump administration to withhold $4 billion in foreign aid funds while Congress considers the administration’s request to rescind the appropriation. The court said the government had made a sufficient early-stage showing that plaintiffs could not sue or obtain mandamus relief, and that harms to foreign affairs outweighed potential harm to the plaintiffs. The ruling was not a final decision on the merits. Justice Elena Kagan, joined by Justices Sonia Sotomayor and Ketanji Brown Jackson, dissented, arguing that the Court should not have acted on an emergency application involving unsettled legal issues and high stakes.

More than 200 schools across North Wales closed because of snow and ice, with councils citing health and safety concerns and travel disruption for staff and pupils. Overnight temperatures fell to -8C, and a yellow ice warning remained in place until 11am. The Met Office said lying snow and icy roads, pavements and cycle paths could cause injuries and hazardous journeys.

Flintshire closed 78 schools, Wrexham 48 and Denbighshire 47. Eleven schools closed in Conwy, while multiple schools also shut in Gwynedd. Anglesey had no closures listed.

Ysgol Plas Cefndy in Denbighshire was partially open only to pupils living north of the A55, with one exception. Ysgol Ardudwy in Gwynedd was open to staff and Years 10 and 11, while Years 7–9 pupils were told to stay home because of a staff shortage.

At NVIDIA Corporation’s June 3, 2021 annual meeting, stockholders approved increasing authorized common shares from 2 billion to 4 billion, elected 13 directors to one-year terms, approved advisory executive compensation, and ratified PricewaterhouseCoopers LLP as independent auditor for the fiscal year ending January 30, 2022. The amendment was filed in Delaware on June 4, 2021, as Exhibit 3.1 to the Form 8-K.

Boston University Summer Term offers open-enrollment undergraduate and graduate courses through day, evening, or online six-week sessions, plus pre-college programs for high school students. Summer sessions run May 23–August 11.

President Donald Trump welcomed French President Emmanuel Macron to the White House for the first state visit of his presidency, a three-day, pageantry-filled visit praising America’s oldest alliance. Trump thanked France for its “steadfast partnership” during the recent missile strike responding to a chemical attack in Syria. The leaders’ agenda includes the Iran nuclear deal, Syria, security and trade, and Macron said the two countries would fight terrorism and curb weapons of mass destruction in North Korea and Iran.

On Monday, the couples planted a young oak — grown at the World War I Battle of Belleau Wood site and gifted by Macron — then flew by Marine One to Mount Vernon for a private dinner and tour. Tuesday’s events include an arrival ceremony with nearly 500 military members and a 21-gun salute, an Oval Office meeting, a joint news conference, a State Department lunch hosted by Vice President Mike Pence, and a state dinner for about 150 guests featuring rack of lamb, nectarine tart and Washington National Opera performances, with décor arranged by Melania Trump. Trump, skeptical of the nuclear deal’s effectiveness, has been eager to withdraw before a May 12 deadline, while Macron, calling it imperfect, urges the U.S. to stay because there is no “Plan B.” Trump invited no Democrats or journalists, though Louisiana Gov. John Bel Edwards will attend.

Tesla Motors’ unaudited Form 10-Q for the quarter ended March 31, 2015 reported revenue of $939.9 million, up from $620.5 million in the prior-year quarter, driven mainly by increased Model S deliveries. Gross profit rose to $260.1 million from $155.1 million, and gross margin improved to 27.7% from 25.0% due to manufacturing efficiencies, lower vehicle costs, favorable product mix, and higher regulatory-credit sales. Operating loss increased to $102.4 million from $44.0 million, while net loss rose to $154.2 million from $49.8 million; diluted loss per share was $1.22, compared with $0.40.

Research and development expense increased to $167.2 million from $81.5 million, largely reflecting Model X development, Autopilot, and Model S improvements. Selling, general, and administrative expense rose to $195.4 million from $117.6 million due to expanded retail, service, Supercharger, personnel, and corporate infrastructure.

At March 31, 2015, Tesla reported $6.12 billion in assets, including $1.51 billion in cash and cash equivalents and $1.05 billion in inventory. A historical account described Enron’s transformation from a natural-gas pipeline company into a broad commodities trader after gaining exemption from power-market oversight. It grew rapidly, raised its share price above $80 and became a major political donor before using partnerships to conceal debt and inflate earnings. Sherron Watkins warned Lay in August 2001 that Enron could “implode in a wave of accounting scandals.” Enron disclosed major losses and reduced equity in October, acknowledged nearly $600 million in overstated earnings in November, and filed the largest corporate bankruptcy in U.S. history on December 2.

House committee records detailed Arthur Andersen’s concerns about Enron’s off-balance-sheet transactions, conflicts involving CFO Andrew Fastow and document-retention policies. Andersen later acknowledged destroying significant records, fired Duncan and initially attributed responsibility to him; Duncan invoked his Fifth Amendment right when subpoenaed. A federal judge barred further shredding, and Congress subpoenaed records concerning contacts with the White House and federal agencies. Committees also considered barring auditors from lucrative consulting contracts with audit clients.

Other developments included a recommendation to liquidate Enron Australia amid sharply reduced creditor recoveries, several publishing contracts for books about Enron, and preparations by charities to replace lost Enron funding. A $1 million private donation kept a Houston Boys and Girls Club operating. Two editorials blamed Enron’s collapse on greed, weak regulation and a lack of financial transparency.

The passage reviews light-field imaging as a snapshot alternative to sequential 3D biomedical imaging. Conventional confocal, multiphoton, and light-sheet microscopy scan point by point or plane by plane, creating trade-offs among acquisition speed, signal-to-noise ratio, and photodamage. Light-field imaging instead records the spatial and directional distribution of light in one exposure, enabling computational refocusing, synthetic-aperture imaging, multi-view visualization, and volumetric reconstruction without physical scanning.

Its theoretical basis is the seven-dimensional plenoptic function, which is commonly reduced to a four-dimensional light field for static, monochromatic or narrow-band applications. A practical two-plane parameterization represents each ray by its position and direction. Under geometric optics, microlens or pinhole arrays divide incoming rays into subimages that encode angular information, enabling reconstruction at different focal depths. Wave-optics models additionally account for diffraction, interference, aberrations, and the point spread function, providing greater accuracy for high-resolution microscopy and scattering samples at the cost of increased computational complexity.

In biomedical applications, light-field microscopy captures spatial and angular fluorescence data in a single exposure and reconstructs 3D volumes through inverse imaging methods such as Richardson–Lucy deconvolution. This increases volumetric acquisition speed, reduces photobleaching and phototoxicity, and has enabled cellular, subcellular, and functional brain imaging in organisms including C. elegans, zebrafish, Drosophila, and mice. Fourier and extended light-field microscopy address the nonuniform sampling and reconstruction artifacts of conventional microlens systems by sampling spatial frequencies.

Light-field mesoscopy extends imaging to millimeter-to-centimeter scales while retaining cellular resolution. Implementations include MesoLF for high-speed functional imaging of large mouse cortical areas, the compact CM2 and CM2 V2 systems for miniature fluorescence imaging, and RUSH3D, which combines scanning light-field imaging with digital adaptive optics to reduce aberrations in turbid tissue. Miniaturization and improved reconstructions are expanding mesoscopy toward portable and freely moving-animal applications.

In endoscopy, light-field modules can be placed downstream of conventional optics or integrated distally using microlens, liquid-crystal, electro-wetting, or gradient-index lens arrays. Demonstrated systems include light-field otoscopes, laryngoscopes, and endoscopes for tympanic membranes, vocal folds, gastrointestinal tissue, and other targets. These approaches provide real-time 3D imaging, digital refocusing, quantitative depth, compact integration, and reduced operator dependence. Fiber-bundle endoscopies remain challenging because flexible fibers can scramble angular information; proposed solutions transmit perspective images or infer depth from angle-dependent modal patterns, but face resolution, working-distance, sample-sparsity, and pixel-count limitations.

Major technical trade-offs involve data volume, speed, field of view, depth of field, and resolution. Complete 4D sampling is limited by camera readout and produces large datasets. Event cameras and squeezed light-field microscopy increase speed through temporal or spatial compression, but compression can reduce resolution or impair disparity and depth estimation when samples are not sufficiently sparse or disparity information is not preserved. Light-field systems also redistribute a fixed space-bandwidth product from lateral resolution into depth resolution. Reducing lenslet counts, using multiple focal lengths, or reintroducing scanning can improve lateral resolution but sacrifice angular sampling, depth range, or speed. Physics-guided virtual scanning can recover near-diffraction-limited resolution and hundreds of volumes per second, although its dependence on training data limits generalizability.

Meta-optics using engineered metasurfaces may improve these trade-offs by controlling phase, amplitude, spectrum, and polarization. Demonstrated concepts include virtual-moving metalens arrays, interleaved metalenses, polarization-multiplexed dual-focus systems, and compact full-color achromatic light-field cameras. Current limitations include optical crosstalk, aberrations, restricted transmission configurations, and lower performance than compound lenses over large fields of view.

Deep learning is also being used to reconstruct light fields more quickly and robustly. Fully learned systems directly convert raw data into 3D volumes, while hybrid systems combine numerical inversion with neural refinement. View-Channel-Depth architectures reorganize angular views into channels to exploit spatial-angular relationships, and hybrid light-sheet systems can validate or fine-tune reconstructions during long experiments. Remaining concerns include limited generalization, dependence on representative training data, computational demands, interpretability, overfitting, and the possibility of hallucinated or misleading outputs.

The City of Bisbee sought mandamus to recover $2,730.86 in penalties, fees, and costs collected by Cochise County treasurers on delinquent city taxes between 1918 and 1931, along with an accounting. The court held that the 1917 tax-collection statute required the county treasurer to pay such additional charges to the city with delinquent taxes and interest. Because the money was city property held in trust by the treasurer, the county and its supervisors had no authority over it, and a prior demand and supervisors’ approval were unnecessary. Mandamus was therefore an appropriate remedy against the treasurer. The statute of limitations did not bar the claim because express trusts are generally exempt from limitation, and the suit was filed within a year of the treasurer’s refusal to remit the funds. Bisbee was entitled to an accounting for amounts collected through June 13, 1931. However, a 1931 statute directed all interest, penalties, charges, and fees collected on delinquent taxes to the county’s general fund, so Bisbee had no claim to amounts collected after June 12, 1931. The court reversed the judgment and remanded the case with instructions to overrule the demurrer as to Treasurer Daniel S. Kitchel.

The passage outlines defensive fundamentals for side-screen offenses in which a larger screener sets for a smaller ballhandler. Switching can allow the screener to post up, making “Show & Recover” the preferred NBA approach, though tactics vary. Defenders show the ballhandler wide, chase over the screen, sag in help, recover to the screener, and close out on passes. Some teams instead slide through the screen or “Jam.”

SOS disruption uses three scenarios. Above the extended free-throw line, defenders execute an aggressive contact switch, deny penetration and jump shots, smother the ballhandler, and front the screener. Below the line, they trap near the baseline or corner, protect the post through a Triangle I, and close out after a pass. An all-out disruption attacks the point guard before the screen, applies a double team, and uses help-side rotations and pass denial. A secondary post trap is also used if the ballhandler passes to the screener on a base roll. Rotations occur as the ball leaves the passer’s hands.

The study developed a field-oriented metagenomic next-generation sequencing protocol for SARS-CoV-2 detection in clinical swabs. It combined a 15-minute DNase I treatment with 0.22-µm filtration, nucleic acid extraction, whole-transcriptome random amplification, rapid library preparation, and 20-hour Oxford Nanopore sequencing. Offline BLAST analysis, read mapping, and consensus generation enabled viral identification and lineage typing without thermal cyclers, centrifuges, extraction robots, or specialized sequencing infrastructure.

In 16 pooled positive samples, pretreatment markedly increased SARS-CoV-2 detection. After 20 hours, untreated samples had 7.5% reference-genome coverage, compared with 32.8% after filtration, 94.1% after DNase I, and 99.3% after combined DNase I and filtration. Combined pretreatment also produced a 525-fold increase in mean viral reads and reached more than 50% genome coverage after 10 minutes of sequencing. Apparent Orthohepevirus A matches from single pretreatments were identified as false positives after read mapping.

Among individual clinical samples, those with CT values at or below 30 achieved 85.8–100% genome coverage after 20 hours. All 14 positive samples were classified as clade 21J (Delta), while Pangolin assigned sub-lineages to samples with CT values below 33. Viral reads also appeared in a negative swab and water control, although duplicate SARS-CoV-2-specific qPCR assays detected no contamination in either control.

The results indicate that the pretreatment substantially improves the probability of detecting SARS-CoV-2, particularly in samples with CT values below 33, and can support simple field identification. Limitations include lower sensitivity at higher CT values, possible false-positive or false-negative results, the need for empirically defined negative thresholds, and testing limited to SARS-CoV-2. Further evaluation of other viruses, sample types, bioinformatics, and simplified workflows is needed.

The text also recommends agreed fake names for offside traps, nonverbal alternatives for loud crowds, decoy calling, listening for opponents’ calls, and surnames or nicknames for players with identical names.

Consumer Reports testing of 23 popular U.S. protein powders and shakes found that more than two-thirds exceeded its safe daily lead limit in a single serving; some contained up to 10 times that amount. Plant-based powders were the most contaminated, averaging about nine times the lead found in dairy proteins such as whey. Contamination also worsened since Consumer Reports’ 2010 testing, when the worst product contained half the lead of the worst current result. Because many consumers use these products daily, the report said this poses a particular risk. The protein supplement industry has limited oversight: supplements are not FDA-approved before sale, there is no federal lead limit for protein powders, and many companies do not disclose testing. NSF permits substantially more lead than Consumer Reports considers safe. The report advised against daily use of most protein powders because they are unnecessary for meeting protein goals. For most people, 0.8 grams of protein per kilogram of body weight per day—about 53 grams for a 140-pound adult—is sufficient and can easily be obtained through whole foods.

After hundreds of current and former Big Five employees alleged unethical tactics used to meet sales goals, the passage argues that production-based incentives pressure advisers against clients’ interests. It recommends tying bonuses to client satisfaction, compensating advisers for advising against purchases, and establishing minimum education requirements. These changes could reduce complaints, improve asset retention and adviser morale, and enhance the industry’s reputation amid public and regulatory scrutiny.

A July 18, 2001 IEP News email compiled coverage of California’s electricity crisis. An included NPR report said expedited permitting had brought 450 megawatts of generation online in 21 days, but only 2,500 of Gov. Gray Davis’s 5,000-megawatt July target was expected, making summer blackouts nearly certain. PG&E sued California for compensation over forward electricity contracts seized in January, arguing they provided below-market power; PG&E was also seeking bankruptcy protection.

PG&E’s 20/20 conservation rebate program had produced $7.6 million in savings, with 394,000 of 1.3 million processed customers qualifying by reducing summer consumption by 20 percent, exceeding officials’ expectations. Duke Energy reported a 27 percent second-quarter profit increase, driven by trading and wholesale power, while analysts noted risks tied to California operations and long-term contracts.

Politically, Davis was using campaign-style communications and consulting to emphasize energy and environmental issues and position himself as a national Democratic leader, despite criticism that he had failed to anticipate the crisis. Lawmakers considered competing plans to prevent Southern California Edison’s bankruptcy, including state acquisition of transmission lines, bond financing repaid by ratepayers, and direct electricity purchases; consumer groups warned of long-term costs, while business groups favored direct access. A Chicago Tribune editorial criticized the Bush administration’s handling of energy policy, citing reduced investment, market responses to higher prices, and costs from government intervention while supporting conservation, streamlined permitting, environmental protection, and improved transmission.

The coach said Calgary played effectively and aggressively, while his team lacked execution and was too nonchalant. He emphasized that the main adjustment needed is mental: respect the opponent, respond immediately, remain tenacious, and avoid dwelling on the loss or making knee-jerk tactical changes. He praised the team’s workout and confidence but rejected a “must-win” approach, saying every game is one the team wants to win. He expects Nikolai Khabibulin to be his best player and lead the response in the next game. He also said an incident involving Danny caused no injuries and that insurance or Danny’s own money would cover the damage.

Intermediate attacking runs build on basic individual runs by emphasizing timing, deception, and creating opportunities for teammates. Individual runs include back-door, drifting, doubling back, holding, recycled, setting up a defender, and drawing an opponent away. Runs that trigger teammate movements include decoy runs, drawing or dragging an opponent, dropping or leaving the ball, and dummy runs. Teammates may also exchange positions through called or natural offensive switches, including basic diagonal “X” switches, vertical switches, and cross-over exchanges; cross-over receivers should use the same foot as the passer. Players should prepare for a pass, anticipate their next action after receiving, and move toward the ball to prevent interceptions.

The coach praised Arvi’s scoring and key saves, crediting the team’s speed and solid third-period play in his birthday victory. He highlighted contributions from several players, said success depends on collective effort, and emphasized improving as the series becomes more difficult.

U.S. workers’ wages and benefits rose 2.6% in 2017, their fastest 12-month growth since 2015, despite fourth-quarter growth slowing to 0.6% from 0.7%. Wages and benefits each rose 2.5%, while hourly wages increased 2.5%, down from 2.9% in 2016. Trump credited the rise, but economists said gains should be faster given 4.1% unemployment.

The passage reviews AI tools that automate repetitive tasks, improve workflows, and increase productivity across writing, coding, visual content, SEO, and web automation. ChatGPT generates human-like text for translation, question answering, and completion, but may produce biased, offensive, inaccurate, or incoherent content. DALL-E creates high-resolution images from text prompts for commercial, gaming, and creative uses, though image quality and originality can vary. Lumen5 produces videos, social posts, scripts, and other content from source material, but output may require editing. Grammarly checks grammar, spelling, punctuation, clarity, concision, and readability, though suggestions may not always be appropriate. OpenAI Codex generates code in multiple programming languages from natural-language descriptions, while Tabnine predicts context-based code snippets; their suggestions may be inaccurate, inefficient, or unsuitable for complex tasks. Jasper AI supports content generation, and Canva is also listed among task-specific tools. Surfer SEO provides site audits, page optimization suggestions, keyword research, ranking analysis, and backlink analysis, but does not guarantee improved rankings. Zapier automates tasks by connecting web applications, while Compose AI generates written or spoken content from structured data. The passage cautions that generated content and code should be reviewed, tested where relevant, and used as aids rather than replacements for developer or data knowledge.

STAT’s Pharmalittle highlights the FDA’s approval of another generic mifepristone abortion pill, allowing three U.S. companies to produce it. The move drew opposition from anti-abortion groups and Trump-aligned politicians who have urged restrictions on abortion-pill access. It is unlikely to change access: mifepristone is typically combined with misoprostol, and the regimen accounts for about two-thirds of U.S. abortions. Amgen also reported that a 12,000-patient trial found Repatha prevented a composite of cardiovascular death, heart attack and the most common stroke. Amgen withheld full results but said both primary goals were met; analysts said the finding could broaden the drug’s market. Repatha generated $2.2 billion in global sales in 2024, up 36% from 2023. The newsletter also previews coverage of pharma layoffs, Medicare price negotiations, tariffs, AI and other industry issues.

A semi-annual ISM survey released Dec 11 found US manufacturing and services firms expect stronger growth and rising revenue into 2018. Manufacturing revenue is projected up 7.8% (70% of firms see higher earnings) and services up 6% (59% expect improvement). Over 60% of firms in both sectors report difficulty filling jobs, prompting wage increases; employment, labor costs and capital spending are also expected to rise, while material cost increases stay below 2017 levels.

The author criticizes Jerry Coyne’s reliance on a YouTube video claiming the CMB and inflation support a multiverse. They say the cited inflation models do not yield the varied physical laws needed to counter theological fine-tuning, warning against confirmation bias and unreliable social-media sources. They also praise David Gross’s defense of science through rigorous, honest, experimentally testable methods.

Apple Inc. filed a Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended September 30, 2017. The company is a California corporation founded in 1977 and headquartered in Cupertino, California. As of October 20, 2017, 5.134 billion common shares were outstanding, and the non-affiliate market value of its stock was approximately $747.5 billion as of March 31, 2017. Portions of Apple’s 2018 proxy statement were incorporated by reference into Part III of the filing.

Apple designs, manufactures and markets mobile communication and media devices, personal computers, software, services, accessories, networking solutions, and digital content and applications. Its principal products include iPhone, iPad, Mac, Apple Watch and Apple TV, supported by the iOS, macOS, watchOS and tvOS operating systems and services such as iCloud, Apple Pay, Apple Music, AppleCare and its digital content stores. Product developments disclosed for 2017 included iPhone 8 and 8 Plus, the announced iPhone X, updated iPad Pro models, the announced iMac Pro, iOS 11, macOS High Sierra, watchOS 4, Apple TV 4K and Apple Watch Series 3.

Apple’s strategy emphasizes integrated hardware, software and services, continued investment in digital content, direct retail and online distribution, and research and development. Its reportable geographic segments are the Americas, Europe, Greater China, Japan and Rest of Asia Pacific. Products are sold directly and through carriers, wholesalers, retailers and value-added resellers. In 2017, direct and indirect channels represented 28% and 72% of net sales, while domestic and international sales represented 37% and 63%, respectively. No individual customer exceeded 10% of net sales during 2017, 2016 or 2015.

Apple identified intense competition, rapid technological change, product-transition risks, dependence on third-party developers, retailers and content providers, inventory and purchase-commitment exposure, quality problems, intellectual-property licensing and litigation, regulatory and international risks, retail-store commitments, acquisitions, information-technology disruptions, data-security and privacy concerns, key-personnel dependence, natural disasters, foreign-exchange movements, credit and investment risks, and potential tax changes as material risk factors. It cautioned that historical results and seasonal or product-launch patterns are not reliable indicators of future performance.

Most hardware manufacturing is outsourced, primarily to partners in Asia, although some Mac computers are manufactured in the United States and Ireland. The company relies on single or limited sources for certain components and faces shortages, capacity constraints and price fluctuations. Apple spent $11.6 billion, $10.0 billion and $8.1 billion on research and development in 2017, 2016 and 2015, respectively, and maintains a broad portfolio of patents, copyrights, trademarks and other intellectual-property rights.

Apple reported that it owned 13.4 million square feet and leased 23.0 million square feet of building space, primarily in the United States, and owned 4,928 acres of land. It had approximately 123,000 full-time equivalent employees as of September 30, 2017. Net sales are typically highest in the first fiscal quarter because of holiday demand. Hardware generally carries a one-year limited warranty and repair service parts a 90-day limited warranty. Management stated that unresolved legal matters were unlikely to produce a material loss beyond recorded accruals, although outcomes remained uncertain; certain fourth-quarter settlements did not materially affect financial results.

Apple’s common stock trades on Nasdaq under the symbol AAPL. The company paid $12.6 billion in dividends in 2017 and $12.0 billion in 2016, expected quarterly dividends of $0.63 per share subject to board declaration, and planned annual dividend increases subject to the same approval. In May 2017, the board expanded the share-repurchase authorization to $210 billion; $166 billion had been used by September 30, leaving $44 billion available. A $3 billion accelerated share repurchase in May ultimately delivered 20.1 million shares at an average price of $149.20, and another $3 billion accelerated repurchase was initiated in August. A five-year indexed investment, including reinvested dividends, was worth $179 at September 30, 2017, compared with $194 for the S&P 500, $223 for the S&P Information Technology Index and $214 for the Dow Jones U.S. Technology Supersector Index.

The coach said a disputed kick call went against his team and that Ottawa outworked it. He criticized his team’s penalties, discipline, compete level and movement, though he noted the game remained winnable. Chris Kunitz had a lower-body injury unrelated to his previous injury, was medically cleared and had worked off the ice, but the coaching staff had not decided whether he would play or what position would suit him. All other players were available. The coach praised Ottawa’s depth and several of his own previously less prominent players, particularly Samuel Pahlsson, for stepping up in the playoffs. He said the team needed to regroup, refocus and play its best game of the year against the Senators.
Gatwick Airport recorded its busiest July, with 4.7 million passengers, up 2.4% year on year. Long-haul traffic rose 10.7%, cargo 20.4%, and new transatlantic and Asian routes were announced.

James Walker Morales escaped the Wyatt Detention Center by climbing a basketball hoop, cutting fencing, crossing razor wire on the roof, and descending the building. He was noticed missing 3½ hours later; the facility was locked down, two officers placed on leave, and authorities searched for him.

An Ombudsman Services study found one in five British rail passengers is resigned to poor service, with complaints up 31% to two million, mainly over punctuality, customer service and overcrowding. Campaigners called the situation unacceptable and urged regulators to require meaningful action. A proposed rail ombudsman would simplify complaints and penalize operators, while the DfT said £40 billion is being invested and train companies face penalties for poor performance. Operators acknowledged service shortfalls, particularly in London and the South East, despite a longer-term fall in complaints.

Rockefeller researchers led by Shai Shaham described an unusual “compartmentalized” cell-death process in C. elegans. In tail-spike cells, the core separates from the long extension, rounds into a ball and disintegrates; the extension then breaks into bead-like fragments near the cell body while its distal end retracts into a ball and is removed by a neighboring cell. The same pattern occurred in a worm neuron, suggesting comparable deaths may occur in other animals and human disease. The researchers also found that the protein EFF-1 helps phagocytes seal their arm-like extensions around dead-cell remnants, providing insight into cellular cleanup.

Second-quarter filings showed Third Point raised stakes in Alphabet and Facebook, while Omega Advisors reduced holdings in Facebook, Netflix and Amazon and kept Alphabet unchanged. Jana Partners held no FAANG stocks but later earned a hefty profit by selling Whole Foods after Amazon’s $13.7 billion acquisition agreement.

The U.S. government was on track to shut down after midnight amid congressional deadlock over a short-term funding bill. The CBO estimated that furloughs would affect about 750,000 federal employees, costing roughly $400 million daily, with the number varying by agency and shutdown duration. Speaker Mike Johnson accused Democrats of demanding enhanced Affordable Care Act tax credits, while Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries said Democrats would not support funding legislation without health-care protections. Jeffries denied any proposal would provide taxpayer-funded medical coverage for undocumented immigrants. Senate Majority Leader John Thune called Democrats’ concern about expiring ACA credits a “made-up problem.”

This continuation application discloses a heterogeneous computing architecture centered on coarse-grained, dynamically reconfigurable computing circuits (“tiles”). It addresses performance, energy use, and heat limits in existing systems and targets compute-intensive workloads including FFTs, FIR filters, synthetic aperture radar, 5G applications, spectral graph clustering, machine learning, and stencil codes.

A configurable tile includes configurable arithmetic, logical, bit, multiply, and shift circuitry; instruction and spoke memories; tile memory; control circuitry; synchronous network inputs and outputs; and asynchronous packet-network queues. The instruction memory configures data paths, while spoke memory selects master synchronous inputs, current and next instructions, output routing, and other independently configurable portions of a tile. Conditional logic can modify next instructions for branching.

The control circuitry supports self-scheduling, ordered thread and loop execution, conditional branching, backpressure, and threads that begin automatically when dependencies or ordering requirements are satisfied. Completion and loop tables track dependencies, iterations, thread ordering, and nested-loop levels. Continuation, reenter, priority, and run queues manage eligible threads, while thread identifiers and stacks provide access to loop-private variables. Flow control can stop packet output and halt computation after an active instruction when an output queue reaches a threshold.

At the system level, configurable circuits form arrays and clusters connected through a synchronous mesh network and an asynchronous packet network. Synchronous domains pipeline data through tiles, while asynchronous packets carry control, completion, continuation, branching, looping, and memory-related signaling between domains. Cluster components include dispatch and memory interfaces and optional network interfaces for work distribution and system-memory access. The dispatch interface receives work-descriptor packets, distributes configuration and arguments, tracks thread and transfer identifiers, gathers results, and returns completion data. Memory interfaces support loads, stores, and atomic operations.

The broader architecture may include a multithreaded RISC-V-based processor, host processors, host and communication interfaces, memory controllers, and a packet-based hierarchical interconnection network using folded-Clos crossbars and mesh connections. Representative tiles provide integer, floating-point, logical, comparison, conversion, multiply, shift, bit-reversal, and permutation operations. The disclosure also describes corresponding circuit architectures and methods for configuring tiles, controlling thread and loop execution, managing dependencies, scheduling work, and coordinating synchronous and asynchronous networks.

A Lewisville mother earns extra income as a mystery shopper. Consumer Reports found FDA-approved Contrave produces modest weight loss—five to nine pounds more than placebo over 56 weeks—and may cause anxiety, insomnia, headaches, liver damage, seizures, high blood pressure and heart risks. Experts advise consulting a doctor about safer options, including diet, exercise and intensive behavioral programs.

The passage describes MSPM0G3518, MSPM0G3519, MSPM0G1518, and MSPM0G1519 I/O, debugging, boot, identification, application, support, revision, and packaging information. IOMUX selects peripheral functions and controls output drivers, input paths, and shutdown wake-up logic; available pin features vary by device. The 5V-tolerant open-drain IO lacks an output-high PMOS, pull-up, and clamping diode.

An ARM-compatible two-wire SWD interface provides debug access. The boot strap loader supports configuration and memory programming through UART or I²C, is protected by a 256-bit user-defined password, can be disabled, and is enabled by default for production programming. It can be invoked through the BSL_invoke pin, an external reset, an unprogrammed reset vector and stack pointer, or a runtime SYSRST command.

A memory-mapped, read-only FACTORY region contains device capabilities, factory trim data, and identification values. DEVICEID is at 0x41C4.0004 and USERID at 0x41C4.0008. Revision and identification information also appears in package markings.

Recommended schematic practices include placing 10µF and 0.1µF low-ESR ceramic capacitors across VDD and VSS, pulling NRST up to VDD with a typical 47kΩ pull-up and 10nF pull-down, and using a 100kΩ, 0.1% resistor with a TCR of 25ppm/°C or better between ROSC and VSS when SYSOSC frequency correction is enabled. VCORE requires a nearby 0.47µF capacitor and no other circuits. Open-drain I/O requires an external pull-up to output high.

TI provides development software and tools, including CCS, SysConfig, TI Resource Explorer, MSP Academy, GUI Composer, IAR Embedded Workbench, Keil MDK, TI Arm-Clang, and GNU Arm Embedded Toolchain. The “X” prefix denotes experimental devices, while “MSP” denotes fully qualified production devices. Documentation, E2E support, ESD cautions, revision updates, package drawings, orderable information, and automotive-qualified Q1 variants are also covered.

Penn State and USC meet for the 10th time overall, the third time in the Rose Bowl and fourth time in a bowl, with USC holding a 5-4 advantage. Their 1923 Rose Bowl, won 14-3 by USC, was the first game at the current stadium and first officially called the Rose Bowl Game. The article notes the Pac-12’s historical advantage over the Big Ten in Rose Bowl games and highlights quarterbacks, players, coaches, rushing and broadcasting records. Penn State’s three Rose Bowls featured the two highest passing performances in the game’s history, by Oregon’s Danny O’Neill (456 yards) and USC’s Mark Sanchez (413). USC has appeared under every U.S. president from Herbert Hoover through Barack Obama. Penn State’s appearance will tie Pittsburgh for the most Rose Bowls among Pennsylvania teams. Penn State is 14-11 against California schools overall but 3-5 in California.

Facebook publicly released detailed Community Guidelines describing content it removes when users report it. Organized around “safety,” “voice,” and “equity,” the document serves as a manual for human adjudicators, ranging from broad principles to precise rules on harassment, crisis actors, and child abuse. Moderator Rochelle LaPlante praised its transparency and detail while noting that similar policies are common. The guidelines reflect difficult, event-driven compromises. Internally, cross-functional teams meet regularly in what Facebook policy executive Monika Bickert called a “mini legislative session” to decide what the guidelines include.

Point72 Europe London purchased 10,000 Hershey shares worth about $1.07 million in the second quarter. Other funds also increased or initiated positions, while hedge funds and institutional investors collectively own 51.39% of the stock. Analysts have mixed ratings—three sell, eight hold and five buy—with a consensus “Hold” and a $111.55 price target.

Insiders Michele Buck and SVP D. Michael Wege sold 400 and 1,100 shares, respectively. Insiders sold 4.5 million shares worth $477.5 million over 90 days and own 0.92%.

HSY traded at $108.83, down 0.08%, with a $23.12 billion market cap and a 52-week range of $94.03 to $116.49. Quarterly EPS was $1.09 versus $0.90 expected, and revenue was $1.66 billion versus $1.65 billion expected. Hershey announced a $0.656 quarterly dividend, equivalent to $2.62 annualized, with a 2.41% yield.

Single crystals of off-stoichiometric YbCu₁.₁₄Se₂ were grown by self-flux and characterized structurally and magnetically. SC-XRD shows a well-ordered triangular Yb lattice, while disordered Cu vacancies give 56.6 ± 0.7% Cu occupancy rather than the ideal 50%. Susceptibility indicates a Yb³⁺ Kramers-doublet ground state, crystal-field effects, and antiferromagnetic exchange, with a low-temperature Weiss temperature of −17.2(5) K. No magnetic-ordering anomaly appears in specific heat; instead, it is sublinear, follows C ∝ T⁰.⁹⁵ up to 1 K, and yields about 85% R ln 2 entropy between 100 mK and 10 K. AC susceptibility shows frequency-dependent freezing near 0.1 K, while no 1/3 magnetization plateau is detected. The resulting spin-disordered state resembles YbMgGaO₄ and simulations of disordered triangular magnets, suggesting possible universal behavior in exchange-disordered frustrated systems.

Anna Mae Blessing, 92, was arrested in Arizona on suspicion of murdering her 72-year-old son, who planned to place her in assisted living. Police said she concealed two handguns in her robe and shot him, while his girlfriend wrestled away the weapons. Blessing said she intended to kill herself.

At an NHL awards event, Robert “Knobby” Knudsen’s family was honored with the Bridgestone Mark Messier Youth Leadership Award for his advocacy and foundation for children. The 2012 finalists were Dustin Brown of the Los Angeles Kings, Shane Doan of the Phoenix Coyotes, and Ryan Callahan of the New York Rangers. Mark Messier discussed the demands of deep playoff runs, the importance of organizational depth and sustained effort, and the Rangers’ roster strength.

Washington's inaugural address thanks his fellow-citizens for electing him and expresses humility about the magnitude of the office, while taking comfort in the support of fellow-citizens and the constitutional authorities around him. He urges unity after the "contest of opinion" of the recent election, insisting that all will submit to the law and unite for the common good. He invokes the principle that majority rule must be reasonable, that minorities have equal rights protected by equal law, and that differences of opinion are not differences of principle—all Americans being Republicans and Federalists alike. He warns against political intolerance as despotic and bloody as religious intolerance, rejects dissolving the Union or changing its republican form, and defends republican government as the strongest on earth, founded on a compact with the people for the right of self-government.

He cites the nation's blessings—its separation from foreign conflict, chosen land, equality of rights, industry, religion, and belief in an overruling Providence—and says only one thing more is needed: a wise and frugal government that restrains wrongdoing, leaves men free to pursue their own interests, and does not take the bread earned by labor.

He then lists the essential principles of government: equal justice; peace, commerce, and honest friendship with all nations without entangling alliances; support of state governments; preservation of the general government; protection of the right of election; acquiescence in majority decisions; a well-disciplined militia; civil authority over military; economy; payment of debts and preservation of public faith; encouragement of agriculture and commerce; diffusion of information and exposure of abuses; freedom of religion, press, and person under habeas corpus; and impartial jury trials.

Finally, he acknowledges his inexperience and likely errors, asks for indulgence for his own mistakes and support against others', pledges to work for the happiness and freedom of all, and commits himself to retire whenever a better choice can be made, trusting divine Providence to guide the councils of the nation.

Christian Bushman survived a May 2014 cardiac arrest at home after an object struck her chest. Her CPR-trained sister-in-law called 911 and performed CPR until help arrived. Bushman credits CPR with saving her life and has taught it, urging others not to stand by. The passage says 70% of out-of-hospital cardiac arrests occur in homes, while women are less likely to receive bystander CPR and more likely to die.

Torsten Sløk says the U.S. economy is accelerating rather than weakening, criticizing economists for repeatedly forecasting a slowdown that did not materialize. Resilient consumer spending, stronger business investment, stable housing and potential third-quarter GDP growth of 3.9% support his view, while slowing job growth reflects reduced immigration. He expects a 50,000-job September payroll report to exceed consensus and warns that strong growth combined with continued Federal Reserve rate cuts could revive inflation.

Morgan Stanley’s Mike Wilson offers a different interpretation, describing the economy as moving from a “rolling recession” to a “rolling recovery.” Although he sees signs of an early-cycle bull market, weak employment data, including downward revisions and ADP job losses, indicate that the recovery has not reached the labor market. The government shutdown is delaying official jobs data.

Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell also described the environment as “low-hire, low-fire.” Sløk’s diagnosis suggests markets may face higher inflation risks even as the Fed continues cutting rates.

The paper proposes bivariate zero-inflated Poisson models for correlated count data. A common Bernoulli inflation factor generates excess zeros, while comonotonic or counter-monotonic shock models create positive or negative dependence between the latent Poisson counts. The model includes formulas for joint probability mass and distribution functions, probability-generating functions, covariance, correlation, and positive-quadrant dependence ordering.

Estimation approaches include method of moments, one- and two-step maximum likelihood, and an EM algorithm. Simulations across varying sample sizes, Poisson rates, inflation levels, and dependence strengths show that likelihood-based estimators generally outperform moment estimators, although small samples, low rates, and high inflation create numerical difficulties and reduced estimation precision.

The model is applied to monthly Australian disaster counts from 1967–2014. Fits to flood–storm and flood–bushfire occurrences indicate substantial zero inflation and significant dependence, supporting the proposed model over standard Poisson shock models and the independent zero-inflated Poisson model of Liu and Tian (2015). Extensions to higher-dimensional positively dependent models based on multivariate comonotonic shocks are also introduced.

National Literacy Month is framed as a call for sustained investment in literacy in South Los Angeles, where Black children face systemic inequities. The article argues that literacy supports resilience, civic participation and community development, and that culturally responsive books, role models and enrichment programs can help children become leaders. Partnership for Growth LA’s after-school and summer program is cited as evidence: in a 2023–24 pilot, students gained 14.5 points in English Language Arts proficiency, chronic absenteeism fell from 47% to 5%, and 88% of families reported gains in confidence, motivation and social-emotional growth. Anastacia Nwosu’s path from participant to “Kid Mayor,” mentor and field deputy to a California Assemblymember illustrates the program’s civic impact.

The authors warn that funding cuts and federal uncertainty threaten tutors, summer programs and advisers. Read Lead Freedom Schools and similar programs combine literacy instruction with civic action. The article calls for stable funding for evidence-based instruction, sustained local literacy infrastructure and tools that make reading a daily family practice.

The address reports that government offices, records, and property were transferred to the permanent seat of Congress after its last Philadelphia session, where Congress assembled for the first time. Congress is urged to invoke divine blessing and to consider exercising constitutional authority over the District of Columbia in anticipation of the capital’s growth. The temporary army has been discharged, the federal judiciary should be improved to make justice more accessible, and a treaty with Prussia has been ratified and proclaimed. Negotiations with Britain over the suspended sixth article of their treaty and with France over accommodation were continuing, with hopes for amicable settlement. The address recommends maintaining defensive preparations, including a strong navy, completing fortifications at major ports and harbors, and encouraging domestic arms manufacture. Congress is asked to review appropriations, public revenue, and expenditures; current revenue reportedly exceeded that of any previous comparable period. The address closes by emphasizing national prosperity, legal institutions, international harmony, and Congress’s duty to protect public interests and promote general happiness.

Beatrice Fihn warned that panic, carelessness, misconstrued comments or bruised egos could trigger nuclear weapons use and mass civilian deaths. Speaking amid escalating rhetoric between U.S. President Donald Trump and North Korean leader Kim Jong Un, including personal insults and mutual nuclear threats, Fihn said the risk now exceeds that at the end of the Cold War because of more nuclear-armed states, terrorism and cyber warfare. She leads the International Campaign to Abolish Nuclear Weapons, a coalition seeking a treaty banning nuclear weapons.

US$INR January futures on the NSE were viewed bearish, with a sell range of 68.20–68.30, targets at 67.95/67.75, and stop-loss at 68.40. The rupee posted a sixth straight annual loss amid expected Fed rate increases and emerging-market outflows.

The ADS7828 can operate with an internal 2.5V or external reference. LSB size is reference voltage divided by 4096; lower references increase apparent offset, gain, and noise errors, with internal noise contributing 0.32 LSB at 2.5V versus 16 LSBs at 50mV.

The Health Ministry estimates 44,586 sex workers aged 15–49, about 7,000 in Bulawayo, with HIV prevalence averaging 55% versus a 13% national average. Its Estimates report, launched by Dr Mugurungi to guide funding and treatment planning, recorded 25,900 AIDS deaths in 2016 (71 daily, down from 278 in 2005) and 14% of the population HIV positive. Dr Ruth Labode warns that ignoring key populations—sex workers, prisoners, LGBTI, drug users and women—could reverse progress toward ending HIV by 2030.

Montgomery’s average gasoline price rose from about $2.14 to $2.18 in a week, while the nationwide average reached $2.40, GasBuddy’s highest since September 2015. Analysts cited lower oil inventories and geopolitical tensions; AAA predicted higher prices through September amid rising summer demand and a possible OPEC production-cut extension.

GoSun introduced the Fusion, a portable solar-electric oven designed to steam, bake, and roast without fuel indoors or outdoors, day or night. It combines a vacuum-insulated solar oven with a 150-watt electric heater powered by a compact lithium-ion battery. The 10-pound, 3.2-liter unit reaches 350°F, feeds five, remains cool to touch, and is weatherproof, rugged, and shock tolerant. Its solar function operates through clouds and freezing temperatures, while its electric heater is claimed to be five times more efficient than a typical oven. GoSun launched a Kickstarter campaign offering exclusive deals to early backers. The company has sold more than 25,000 solar stoves in over 80 countries.

The lecture extends temporal difference learning from tabular, discretized Markov chains to continuous state spaces using function approximation. After reviewing policy evaluation, TD(λ), eligibility traces, and convergence assumptions for ergodic Markov chains, the lecture identifies state discretization as a major limitation for high-dimensional systems such as the acrobot.

A crash course in least-squares function approximation covers estimating an unknown function from input-output samples. Linear function approximators, which combine nonlinear basis functions with parameters that enter linearly, allow an exact least-squares solution without gradient descent. Example basis functions include radial basis functions, barycentric interpolators, Fourier features, and polynomials. Although neural networks are richer, their parameters are embedded within nonlinearities, making least-squares optimization less convenient.

The lecture applies this method to nonlinear system identification. Although robot dynamics can be highly nonlinear in their states, their equations are often linear in groups of physical parameters. A pendulum simulation uses basis functions such as acceleration, velocity, and the sine of the angle to estimate inertia, damping, and gravitational parameters from random torque excitation. This approach can accurately recover noisy parameters, although insufficient excitation, unmodeled nonlinearities, hidden states, and aerodynamic dynamics can reduce performance. Additional basis functions can capture unmodeled effects.

Temporal difference learning is then extended to linear function approximators by replacing state-based eligibility traces with parameter-based traces. Each parameter receives credit according to its gradient, which for a linear approximator is the corresponding basis-function vector. The λ parameter continues to trade off one-step bootstrapping against long-term Monte Carlo evaluation. For λ=1, the update can be interpreted as gradient descent on Monte Carlo error; for other values, it is not a standard steepest-descent method. The lecture cites convergence results for linear function approximators and arbitrary λ between zero and one.

Although this removes explicit state-space discretization and permits higher-dimensional systems, ordinary TD updates use data inefficiently because each observation produces only a small incremental update. Most Southeast Asian stocks fell or edged lower Monday as investors awaited the U.S. Fed’s two-day policy meeting, with a 25-basis-point rate hike expected and attention focused on whether officials project four 2018 hikes rather than three. The Philippines recovered from early losses to close marginally lower, and Malaysia edged up. Vietnam rose for a sixth straight session, reaching its highest close since March 2007.

The Trap is a quick-hitting, downhill run scheme that kicks out an interior defensive lineman. It can be effective with a powerful fullback or a smaller, dynamic tailback in spread offenses, while Wing-T deception can enhance its operation. Its main strengths are its speed, which gives defenders little time to identify the ball carrier, and its angle-blocking rules, which are forgiving of offensive-line personnel and allow smaller linemen to use defenders’ alignment. Its primary weakness is defenses that squeeze interior gaps, such as a Bear or even front, limiting the offensive line’s ability to climb to linebackers. The passage provides blocking assignments against 3-4 odd and 4-3 even fronts. Two variations are described: a gun Trey same-side trap RPO with a quarterback bubble or slant option, though the backside inside linebacker is unblocked, and a Wing-T trap used as a sister play to Buck Sweep, with identical backfield action but a different ball carrier.

The President reviews U.S. foreign policy, stressing congressional cooperation, national unity, strong alliances, defense readiness, and continued American leadership amid global political and economic uncertainty. He cites improved relations with Europe and Japan, a more stable but competitive relationship with the Soviet Union, an opening with the People’s Republic of China, and diplomatic progress in the Middle East, Latin America, and Africa.

Indochina is the principal urgent issue. The President says violations of the 1973 Paris accords and reduced U.S. support contributed to South Vietnam’s crisis. After General Weyand reported that South Vietnam remained defensible but urgently needed $722 million in specific military supplies, he requested $722 million for emergency military assistance and an initial $250 million for economic and humanitarian aid. He also sought authority to use U.S. forces for limited evacuation purposes, revision of legal restrictions affecting endangered Vietnamese, and congressional action by April 19. He urged North Vietnam to halt military operations and cease violating the accords, called on other Paris signatories to help enforce them, and pledged a maximum humanitarian effort for refugees. In Cambodia, he urged Congress to provide urgently needed food, ammunition, and weapons to the Khmer Republic.

The President also called for standing firm with U.S. allies, strengthening relations with Asian and European partners, lifting the arms embargo on Turkey to advance a Cyprus settlement, and granting trade preference waivers to certain OPEC countries. He pledged continued U.S. peacemaking efforts in the Middle East, progress in strategic arms negotiations with the Soviet Union, reconsideration of sanctions tied to Soviet emigration policies, and further constructive engagement with China.

He identified additional challenges involving hunger, world trade and raw materials, oceans, technology, the environment, energy security, intelligence, and defense. He urged Congress to support international energy cooperation and domestic energy independence, oversee intelligence discreetly, and maintain adequate defense spending. He concluded that the executive and Congress must act as one government, presenting a united foreign policy and honoring American commitments.

Hillview’s April 27, 7:30 p.m. outdoor movie features PG-rated “Sing.” One adult per eight children must stay with the group. A Mexican food truck offers concessions; proceeds support LLS and JDRF. RSVP requested.

The passage documents the AGESA/AGESATM host-BIOS interface, UEFI porting and build process, initialization sequence, and supporting services. The binary module uses 32-bit protected mode with flat addressing; 16-bit real-mode support is deprecated. Host BIOS code calls AGESA through a bridge and dispatcher, while AGESA calls host services through a call-out port and router. Function numbers select published AGESA or host routines. The host must establish a valid stack before calls and populate the standard header. The event log is a circular buffer retaining the 16 most recent events, which are read oldest-first through `AmdReadEventLog`.

Two build methods are described: binary modules, where calls pass through a common entry point, and source integration, where the host incorporates AGESA source and uses its own toolchain. UEFI support spans SEC, PEI, DXE, and runtime phases, with platform-specific option files, environment variables, reference addendum files, and required build libraries. During Cache-as-RAM operation, the host must not modify `SS`, `ESP`, or cache controls.

The UEFI PEI implementation uses separate processor, memory, and reset-coordination PEIMs. These initialize processor components, perform memory initialization, publish coordination PPIs and memory information, and manage warm-reset requests. The DXE driver performs late initialization, generates system data tables, and publishes the `AgesaDxeProtocol`. A separate driver controls iGPU VGA decoding through the `PciIo` protocol.

Native assembly stack procedures establish and remove the pre-memory execution-cache stack, map stack regions, configure MTRRs, and create the SEC-to-PEI handoff frame. The host is required to establish this stack environment and may use `AMD_ENABLE_UEFI_STACK` for UEFI implementations.

Published initialization entry points provide minimal reset initialization, full processor setup, memory initialization, artifact transfer, late display configuration and table generation, and suspend-state saving. Resume entry points restore processors, memory, critical registers, and silicon state before operating-system handoff. The bootstrap processor performs most work, while application processors follow specified coordinated tasks.

Supporting services allocate and release parameter structures using pre-memory, post-memory, or host-provided allocation; retrieve DIMM data-eye results, APIC and PCI addresses, processor identity, and memory-device locations; update MMIO ranges; and read event-log entries.
