North American markets declined as technology sell-offs, higher interest rates and lower oil prices weighed on trading. The TSX lost 75 points and the Dow 424. Tim Hortons first-quarter sales fell 0.3%; Restaurant Brands plans $700 million in renovations.
Vanguard prioritized climate risk in company talks, urging disclosure of environmental business risks. Walden withdrew a proposal seeking review of Vanguard’s proxy voting.

Following President Tyler’s recommendation, Congress funded a diplomatic officer to the Sandwich Islands, and George Brown was appointed commissioner on March 3, 1843. Brown sought impartial treatment for U.S. citizens without exclusive privileges, and the King promised them equal privileges with those of the most favored nation. By August 1844, disputes arose over the denial of a jury trial to American John Wiley and discriminatory treaty provisions favoring Britain. With no U.S. treaty in place, the King requested Brown’s recall, although his conduct was approved by the U.S. government.

Calhoun confirmed U.S. recognition of Hawaiian independence in 1844. In 1846, France and Britain concluded identical conventions modifying jury provisions and liquor restrictions, though they did not appear to fully recognize Hawaiian independence. A Danish treaty that October included a favored-nation clause and appears to have been the first to fully acknowledge Hawaiian independence.

Ten Eyck replaced Brown but continued urging inclusion of a jury clause that Buchanan considered objectionable. Negotiations failed amid disputes over American residents’ rights and increasingly unfavorable foreign treaties. After sharp criticism from Buchanan, Ten Eyck resigned in September 1848, and Charles Fames was appointed on January 12, 1849.

Kearny Financial, parent of New Jersey-based Kearny Bank, trades at 0.68x tangible book value despite declining revenues and a significant goodwill hit. Asset quality is a strength, with FY 2025 new net charge-offs below 0.05%. The author rates KRNY a Hold, citing improved performance and potential as an attractive takeover target amid renewed banking merger activity. The author discloses no positions or business relationships and no compensation beyond Seeking Alpha.

Bernard Tomic was beaten 6-3, 7-5 by David Ferrer in the Brisbane International’s first round, despite saving two match points, as serve problems and unforced errors undermined his game. Tomic blamed inaccurate first serves and heavy offseason training, denied injury and said Ferrer’s consistency was decisive. Nicolas Mahut also advanced, while Samantha Stosur lost to Garbine Muguruza in three sets despite leading a break in the third.

The passage details NVIDIA’s Ampere-based A100 Tensor Core GPU, an eighth-generation data center accelerator built on the 7nm GA100 with 108 streaming multiprocessors and 432 third-generation Tensor Cores. Tensor Cores support FP16, BF16, TF32, FP64, INT8, INT4, and binary operations, while 2:4 fine-grained structured sparsity can double Tensor Core throughput. Compared with V100, the document reports up to 10x faster TF32, 2.5x faster FP16/FP32 and FP64 processing, and up to 20x faster sparse INT8 performance.

A100 includes 40GB of HBM2 memory with 1555GB/s bandwidth, a 40MB L2 cache with 2.3x V100’s read bandwidth, larger L1/shared memory, cache-residency controls, and Compute Data Compression. Its Multi-Instance GPU feature securely partitions each GPU into as many as seven isolated GPU Instances, providing dedicated compute and memory resources, quality-of-service guarantees, fault isolation, simultaneous context execution, and workload migration. Third-generation NVLink provides 600GB/s aggregate GPU-to-GPU bandwidth and supports large multi-GPU systems using NVSwitch and InfiniBand or Ethernet networking. A100 also adds PCIe Gen 4, SR-IOV, NVJPG JPEG decoding, an optical-flow accelerator, improved atomics, and five NVDEC units.

CUDA 11 adds support for Tensor Cores, sparsity, asynchronous copies and barriers, task graphs, L2 residency controls, and Cooperative Groups. DGX A100 combines eight A100 GPUs, six NVSwitches, and 4.8TB/s bidirectional interconnect bandwidth, delivering up to 5 PFLOPS and supporting as many as 56 isolated MIG accelerators.
The team must stay focused, stick to the plan, and avoid relaxing at home despite two hard-fought games; the Finals are not over until four wins.

In a personal-injury action against Samaritan Hospital of Suffern and others, the Appellate Division reversed the grant of summary judgment because the defendants failed to establish their prima facie entitlement to judgment as a matter of law. Costs were awarded, and the sufficiency of the plaintiffs’ opposition papers was not considered.

The paper examines whether a community oral history project can strengthen elementary preservice teachers’ (PSTs) understanding and teaching of citizenship. It reviews concerns that citizenship instruction has declined, controversial topics are avoided, and PSTs may misunderstand citizenship or lack questioning, inquiry, historical-thinking, and culturally responsive teaching skills. Oral histories are presented as a way to learn through community members’ lived experiences, develop open-ended questioning and inquiry, connect disciplines, address emotions and diverse perspectives, and engage students in dialogue and civic action.

A qualitative case study involved 38 elementary PSTs in four social studies methods courses at a South Florida university. Participants selected citizenship topics, interviewed anonymous community members using ten sequential open-ended questions, transcribed interviews using technology, and completed post-project reflection surveys. The most common interview topics were immigration, military service, entrepreneurship, and poverty.

PSTs reported that first-hand accounts expanded their content knowledge, challenged assumptions, and revealed differences among people’s experiences of the same event or issue. The interviews also affected them personally by increasing empathy, appreciation for citizenship and elders, awareness of social and political realities, and motivation toward civic action. Participants became more confident about teaching controversial subjects and planned to incorporate oral histories, community guest speakers, and real-world perspectives into future citizenship instruction. Challenges included securing interviewees, preparing questions, and discomfort with personal questions.

The study concludes that oral histories can provide authentic, humanistic understanding of citizenship’s relationship to democracy and help PSTs prepare future students to engage with community histories and perspectives. Limitations included the absence of a pre-survey and involvement of only one university. Proposed research includes presurveys, professional-development workshops, and follow-up studies of PSTs’ classroom implementation and student impacts.

On January 27, 2017, NVIDIA Land Development, LLC amended its 2015 Participation Agreement for the construction and lease of NVIDIA’s new Santa Clara headquarters to align certain terms with its October 2016 Credit Agreement. The amendment increased the maximum total leverage ratio from 3.0:1.0 to 3.5:1.0 and removed the 3.5:1.0 minimum interest coverage ratio.

PITB’s Plan9 Technology Incubator is accepting applications for its 10th Launchpad until June 20. The Lahore event begins July 17 with a two-day Makeathon, followed by startup training and a pitch competition from July 19–23. Applicants must be Pakistani citizens aged 18 or older with a product-based technology idea; each startup may submit one idea. Selected founders or team members living outside Lahore must relocate there for six months. Selection involves online application review, shortlisting, Launchpad participation, judging, and incubation of top-scoring teams. Since its inception, Plan9 has graduated more than 130 startups with over $70 million in valuation, $2.5 million in investment, and more than 1,000 jobs created.

Dr Malcolm Tunnicliff, who treated 12 Grenfell Tower casualties at King's College Hospital, said staff prepared cyanide antidote kits in advance because foam in older, untreated furniture can release hydrogen cyanide when burned, burning at over 760°C and producing toxic gases that can incapacitate victims in a single breath. Around 60 people were taken to six London hospitals and scores remain missing. The cause of the fire is unknown, though fire chiefs called its rapid spread "unprecedented." Crews reached the tower's top, searching flats with drones over structural concerns, and no more survivors are expected. The 1974 tower was refurbished for £8.6 million before the blaze; Mayor Sadiq Khan and borough leader Nick Paget-Brown promised investigations into its cause.

The speech outlines the planned drawdown of U.S. forces from Afghanistan. Beginning the following month, 10,000 troops will leave by year’s end, returning a total of 33,000 by the next summer and fully reversing the troop surge. The mission will shift from combat to support, with the transition to Afghan security forces expected to be complete by 2014. The speaker credits coalition and Afghan forces with pressuring al Qaeda, killing Osama bin Laden, weakening the Taliban, and expanding Afghan security forces by more than 100,000 personnel.

The speech says political reconciliation is necessary for peace. Talks must be led by the Afghan government, and participants must break from al Qaeda, reject violence, and follow the Afghan constitution. The United States will also continue pressing Pakistan to prevent terrorist safe havens and support efforts against violent extremism.

Reflecting on the wars in Iraq and Afghanistan, the speaker emphasizes their human and financial costs, including nearly 4,500 American deaths in Iraq and more than 1,500 in Afghanistan. He advocates a pragmatic foreign policy that uses force when necessary, targets threats, and relies on international partners when large deployments are unnecessary. He also cites support for Libyan allies without U.S. ground troops as an example.

Domestically, the speech calls for shifting attention from war spending toward jobs, innovation, infrastructure, clean energy, and national unity. It commits to caring for veterans and their families while responsibly ending the wars, strengthening American ideals of freedom, rule of law, and self-determination, and restoring the promise of the American Dream.

Tom Barrett is a corporate growth and change agent with more than 30 years in the landscape industry. For 20 years, he has been principal of Green Water Infrastructure, a Cincinnati-based consulting company integrating water resources into sustainable site development. His collaborative, team-based, strategic leadership emphasizes relationships, identifies patterns amid complexity, and helps organizations overcome stagnation and drive results. He also coaches CEOs, owners, and executives and has held senior sales and marketing roles at Kenney Corp, Ewing Irrigation Products, and Rain Bird. Barrett cites Warren Buffett as his leading role model, reads Seth Godin, Chris Brogan, and Jay Baer, and believes the web is transforming relationships while individuals with passion and vision remain essential to change. He stresses integrity, continuous learning, and rejects the unsustainable “winner take all” mentality of American business.

House Republicans are meeting to discuss an unfinished government funding bill ahead of a Friday midnight deadline, with disputes over an Affordable Care Act stabilization package, abortion restrictions, and other policy riders. Trump supports the health-care plan, while Democrats oppose the abortion provisions and some conservatives oppose ACA funding. Negotiations also stalled over protecting DACA recipients, and congressional harassment-reporting reforms may be excluded. Republicans are seeking to correct tax-bill errors, while controversial riders may be dropped to avoid a shutdown.

NerdWallet ranked home affordability in 172 U.S. metropolitan areas for the first quarter of 2018, comparing median household income with principal-and-interest payments on median-priced single-family homes. Calculations assumed a 20% down payment, a 4.45% interest rate and a 30-year fixed mortgage, excluding insurance, property taxes and homeowners association dues.

Decatur, Illinois, was the most affordable market: the median home price was $73,000, and the monthly payment equaled 7.6% of median monthly income. The other most-affordable markets were Cumberland, Maryland-West Virginia; Elmira, New York; Binghamton, New York; and Peoria, Illinois.

San Jose-Sunnyvale-Santa Clara, California, was the least affordable, with a $1.37 million median home price and a monthly payment equal to 60.3% of median monthly income. The other least-affordable markets were Honolulu; San Francisco-Oakland-Hayward; San Diego-Carlsbad; and Los Angeles-Long Beach. California had four of the five least-affordable markets.

The British Embassy reported that the Department and other agencies supported the proposed objectives and would sympathetically consider requests from the Belgian Congo, subject to reasonableness and British supply conditions. Belgium was to submit consolidated lists of available materials and total British and American requirements for review in London and Washington with technical experts. The United States planned to send Dean Frasché as a tin adviser, a mining specialist, and a representative to assess Belgian needs, while Britain was urged to send corresponding experts and prepare joint reports. The Department called for immediate consultation with Harriman and the Minister of Supply to initiate negotiations with the Belgian government. Belgium’s colonial minister postponed his planned Washington trip. A tripartite Anglo-American-Belgian supply agreement was proposed, tentatively effective September 1, 1942, while an unsigned second Anglo-Belgian purchasing agreement was still expected to be concluded.

Professor David Nutt and his team have developed “alcosynth,” a synthetic alcohol designed to mimic alcohol’s effects without causing the acetaldehyde buildup associated with hangovers. After testing about 80 compounds, they narrowed the options to five and plan to submit one to Britain’s Food Standards Agency as a novel food ingredient. The team is seeking $11.8 million for final safety checks before public sale, with the goal of replacing regular alcohol by 2050.

A May 3, 2001 news digest covered Enron-related developments in energy, finance and corporate strategy. In Pompano Beach, Florida, residents were to discuss Enron’s proposed power plant before the City Commission’s vote on a zoning variance. An Associated Press article examined California lawmakers’ proposal to refuse electricity purchases above specified prices and accept additional blackouts. The state had spent $5.7 billion on power in three and a half months, but economists cited potentially greater economic losses from prolonged outages and questioned the proposal’s viability.

Indian lenders asked the government to help resolve the dispute between Enron’s 65%-owned Dabhol Power Co. and the Maharashtra State Electricity Board over high prices and unpaid bills. About $48.2 million remained overdue, and Dabhol had authorized management to halt power sales if no resolution was reached. A government panel was formed to renegotiate the project’s $2.9 billion contract; its first meeting with Dabhol was postponed to May 11. Lenders warned that Enron could withdraw and that a new buyer might be sought.

The Democratic National Committee criticized the Bush administration’s energy policy as favoring oil and gas interests through campaign contributions, regulatory rollbacks, proposed Arctic drilling and reduced conservation funding. It also cited Enron’s record first-quarter operating income and the high proportion of energy-industry personnel on Bush’s energy transition team.

British utility Innogy began wholesale electricity trading on the France-Italy border, was nearing entry into Germany and planned to expand its European trading team and gas activities. Its strategy emphasized trading services rather than acquiring physical assets, with France expected to be a key market.

Mosaic Group reported first-quarter revenue of $171.8 million, up 89%, and 29% growth in diluted cash earnings per share, marking its 18th consecutive quarter of year-over-year revenue growth. Its Paradigm unit secured $20 million to $25 million in annual new business and expanded its customer-acquisition contract with Enron-created New Power.

European telephone-company debt prospects improved as British Telecom, Deutsche Telekom and Royal KPN announced asset sales and debt-reduction plans, prompting investors to become more favorable toward their bonds and bankruptcy swaps. Separately, European corporations were increasingly using credit derivatives to hedge receivables and counterparty risk, though the market remained small and the instruments complex and costly.

Allegheny Energy completed its purchase of three Enron natural-gas plants in Tennessee, Indiana and Illinois, adding 1,710 megawatts and planning to control more than 14,000 megawatts by 2005. Salomon Smith Barney sharply reduced its forecast for U.S. power-generation profitability from 2002 because electricity prices were expected to fall faster than natural-gas prices. Fitch affirmed Northern Border Partners’ BBB+ rating and its pipeline affiliate’s A- rating, changing both outlooks to stable.

EnergieKontor signed a framework agreement with Enron Wind for 200 megawatts of turbines in Germany and Spain and was negotiating for as much as 700 megawatts of additional wind projects in Spain’s Castilla-La Mancha region. Scottish Power, meanwhile, reported lower fiscal-year profits and adjusted earnings and was restructuring into three divisions, considering the sale of Southern Water and emphasizing U.S. cost reductions and acquisitions.

The passage contrasts the Duchess of Cambridge’s $8,900, 24-hour stay at the Lindo Wing with the high cost and poorer outcomes of U.S. maternity care. Average American delivery costs are cited at $12,290, with cesarean sections averaging $16,907, emergency bills potentially exceeding $30,000, and premature-triplet costs exceeding $870,000.

The United States also has comparatively high infant and maternal mortality, lower life expectancy than the rest of the OECD, and high health spending: $3.3 trillion, nearly 18% of GDP, in 2016. Americans reportedly use health services at rates similar to Europeans but pay substantially more, while higher costs increase insurance premiums, deductibles, copays, and employer expenses.

Despite gains in coverage under the Affordable Care Act, many patients remain underinsured or face large uncovered expenses, prompting tens of thousands to use medical crowdfunding. U.S. first-child costs are described as 13 times those of comparable British couples, whose National Health Service covers most vaginal childbirth costs. The passage concludes that every mother should have access to safe, clean, comfortable maternity care and competent caregivers without parents having to fear the cost of their newborn’s medical bills.

The passage examines innovations in curriculum and teacher education, including technology integration, continuous professional development, innovative teaching methods, cross-cultural perspectives, and inclusive curriculum design. It argues that combining these approaches requires teacher education programs to evolve and helps create flexible, equitable learning environments that prepare all students for a globalized future.

Michael James Costa, 38, absconded from supervised release in Rochester, Minnesota, in April 2017 and remains a fugitive. Authorities warn against confronting him and request information by calling 911 or the assigned DOC investigator.

Apple Inc.’s Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended September 30, 2023 describes its business, principal risks, legal proceedings and share repurchase activity. The company designs, manufactures and markets iPhone, Mac, iPad, wearables, accessories and related services, including advertising, AppleCare, cloud services, digital content and payment services. Its reportable segments are the Americas, Europe, Greater China, Japan and Rest of Asia Pacific. During 2023, direct channels accounted for 37% of net sales and indirect channels for 63%. Apple had approximately 161,000 full-time equivalent employees as of September 30, 2023.

The company operates in highly competitive markets and depends on continued innovation, research and development, intellectual property, third-party developers and content providers, and complex global manufacturing and logistics networks. Significant risks include adverse macroeconomic and trade conditions, geopolitical events, natural disasters, public health issues, component shortages, product transitions and defects, inventory impairments, cybersecurity and data-protection failures, dependence on suppliers and resellers, acquisitions, legal and regulatory compliance, tax changes, foreign exchange movements, credit and investment losses, and stock-price volatility. The filing cautions that forward-looking statements are not guarantees and actual results may differ materially.

Legal proceedings include Epic Games’ antitrust lawsuit concerning the App Store. A district court injunction permits certain external purchase links, the Ninth Circuit affirmed the ruling, and enforcement was stayed pending Apple’s Supreme Court appeal. The International Trade Commission also entered a limited exclusion order covering certain Apple Watches with blood oxygen functionality; Apple intends to appeal.

Common stock trades on Nasdaq under “AAPL.” Apple had 23,763 shareholders of record and 15,552,752,000 shares outstanding as of October 20, 2023. During the fourth quarter, Apple repurchased 106.595 million shares for $74.069 billion. It had used $15.9 billion of a newly authorized $90 billion repurchase program and completed the remaining $4.6 billion of its prior program during the quarter.

Students were honored at district Student of the Year celebrations for overcoming adversity and planning college and careers. Hemet High’s Cassi Tichy, who battled cancer, will attend Cal State Fullerton for arts and entertainment. Beaumont’s Ana Aguirre, who adapted to four foster families, was accepted to UCLA as a biology major and aims to become an anesthesiologist. Other honorees received scholarships of $500–$2,000 and $100 Walmart gift cards.

This continuation of the “MULTI-MODAL INTERFACES” patent application describes digital-assistant systems supporting multiple user-input modalities on electronic devices. A digital assistant accepts spoken or textual requests, infers user intent, identifies and executes task flows, and provides audible or visual responses. Implementations may use a device-side client and server, connect to external services, operate standalone, or use another device as a proxy.

Disclosed methods allow words entered in one input mode to be displayed, selected through another mode, and modified by further input. Other methods use device context to disable outputs when specified criteria are met, identify alternative input modes for performing tasks, and request additional input in a selected modality when needed to complete a task. Equivalent computer-readable media and electronic-device implementations are also described.

The detailed description covers portable and nonportable multifunction devices with touch-sensitive displays, processors, memory, networking, audio, optical, proximity, motion, and contact-intensity sensors, tactile outputs, digital-assistant software, application modules, and event handling for touch, gesture, mouse, stylus, voice, eye, and biometric inputs. The described techniques aim to make interactions more intuitive and efficient, avoid unnecessary outputs, reduce power use, and improve battery life.

In his final State of the Union address, the President reports that the Union is good but still needs improvement and celebrates an orderly transition to President-elect Carter. He recalls beginning his presidency amid national division, resignations, the aftermath of the Vietnam War, recession, inflation, congressional conflict, and doubts about the country’s institutions and international leadership.

He credits policies of shared governmental responsibility, restrained spending and inflation, tax reductions, local control, and energy development for economic recovery. Inflation fell from 12.2 percent to 5 percent, employment exceeded 88 million, and four million jobs were added since spring 1975, though unemployment remained a major concern. He urges Congress to enact a permanent $10 billion tax cut, raise personal exemptions, encourage investment, lower the corporate tax rate, and end double taxation of dividends. Federal aid to state and local governments reached $70 billion, while annual crime growth fell from 18 percent to 2 percent but remained a serious problem.

The administration made inadequate progress toward energy independence, leaving the country more dependent on foreign oil. It enacted initial conservation, resource-development, stockpiling, and emergency measures, but the President proposed further action on domestic oil and gas production, coal, nuclear power, and an energy independence authority.

Foreign policy achievements include stronger alliances with Western European, Japanese, and Canadian partners; the Vladivostok Accord on strategic weapons; progress toward Middle East peace; expanding dialogue with China; closer ties in Asia; increased cooperation between developed and developing nations; and initiatives addressing nuclear proliferation and ocean use. In Africa, the United States supported peace, majority rule, minority rights, and self-determination. The President urged bipartisan congressional support for the new administration while defending presidential responsibility in foreign affairs and Congress’s constitutional war, consent, and appropriations powers.

He also reports reversing the decline in real defense spending and advocates continued strategic programs, including Trident, the B-1 bomber, and a new intercontinental ballistic missile, alongside strong conventional, naval, and NATO capabilities. Internationally, he urges attention to federal judicial vacancies, excessive regulation, and rising congressional and federal spending. He closes by emphasizing constitutional checks and balances, individual liberty, public service, and the need for continued national improvement.
Judgment reduced by $914.36, plus interest; affirmed without costs.

The study evaluates whether multimodal large language models and vision-language models possess the specialized knowledge needed for marine species recognition and introduces FishNet++, a multimodal benchmark derived from FishNet. FishNet++ contains 99,556 images covering 17,393 fish species, 35,133 textual descriptions, 706,426 key-point annotations, and 119,399 bounding boxes. Descriptions were generated from reliable marine sources using GPT-4o and validated by experts and a user study; taxonomic corrections and additional images improved coverage and representation.

Zero-shot recognition remains poor: Qwen2.5-VL, the best-performing open-source model, achieves 6.2% accuracy on frequent species and 0.2% on rare species, while GPT-4o reaches 17.9% and 1.2%. Diagnostic experiments identify both deficient taxonomic knowledge and weak fine-grained visual perception. Qwen2.5-VL translates between common and scientific names with only 3.6% accuracy, performs below chance when verifying visually similar species, localizes fish reasonably well, but performs poorly on precise key-part localization.

Fine-tuning Qwen2.5-VL on FishNet++ raises frequent-species accuracy from 6.2% to 37.0% and improves genus- and family-level accuracy. Explainable fine-tuning maintains strong performance while generating human-readable justifications for predictions. Ensemble retrieval-augmented generation also improves zero-shot results, though less substantially than supervised fine-tuning. Overall, the work concludes that domain-specific benchmarks and training substantially mitigate, but do not eliminate, the challenges of fine-grained marine species recognition.

James announced a “Second Decision” for Oct. 7 at noon EST, shifting attention from the Lakers’ championship hopes as Luka Dončić awaited news. The 40-year-old forward’s retirement is considered unlikely; the announcement may instead concern a strategic partnership or business move.

Bougainville lifted its 40-year ban on new mining and exploration, permitting applications in the iron-rich Tore, Isina and Jaba areas. Panguna remains excluded, while officials say genuine investment could support economic development.

SRAM in switchable power domains enters SHUTDOWN when its domain is turned OFF, losing all stored data, and returns to ACTIVE when the domain is turned ON. Selected ALWAYS_ON SRAM can be shut down independently through x_MEM_PWRDN registers. Some I/O groups support independently selectable 1.8-V or 3.3-V supplies, while each DDR interface supports 1.5 V or 1.8 V. PHYs must be placed in power-down mode before their domains are turned OFF. Low-Power Standby requires all switchable domains OFF, the Cortex-A8 executing an IDLE loop at its lowest frequency, and unnecessary functional blocks clock-gated.

Supplies are divided into four sequencing groups and require specified power-up and power-down orders. The 3.3-V supplies must not exceed the 1.8-V supplies by more than 2 V. PLL and analog supplies require filtering, preferably a ferrite bead with nearby capacitors. Recommended decoupling uses 0.1-µF capacitors no larger than 0402, at least one per two power pins, plus an approximately 10-µF bulk capacitor per ten power pins. Excess capacitance must not disrupt startup sequencing, and reset should remain asserted until supplies are stable.

System resets include power-on, external warm, emulation warm, watchdog, software global cold and warm, test, and peripheral-local resets. POR resets the entire chip, including Test and Emulation logic and the EMAC Switch; warm resets generally preserve those blocks. POR requires stable supplies and input clocks, keeps most pins in Hi-Z, latches BTMODE, and releases the Cortex-A8 to execute from Boot ROM. PCIe and EMAC Switch reset-isolation features permit selective resets under specified conditions. Simultaneous reset requests are handled according to priority. RSTOUT_WD_OUT behavior depends on reset type and the latched BTMODE[11] value, while power-domain transitions trigger domain-specific cold or warm resets.

The device accepts DEV and AUX clocks from crystals with internal oscillators or 1.8-V LVCMOS sources. DEV clocks are generally 20 MHz but may range from 20–30 MHz under specified conditions; AUX clocks are optional and support precise audio or video timing. A low-jitter differential SERDES clock is required for PCIe, and optional external clocks are available for audio functions and a 32.768-kHz reference. The device contains 12 top-level and four embedded PLLs, which start in bypass mode after reset and must satisfy reference, internal-output, output, and module-frequency limits. The ARM interrupt controller handles up to 128 requests, while the C674x controller combines 128 events into 12 prioritized interrupts.

Peripheral sections cover DCAN, EDMA, debug and trace, JTAG, Ethernet switching, GPIO, external-memory control, HDMI, and video processing. Two DCAN interfaces support CAN 2.0, masking, FIFO and loopback modes, and interrupts. EDMA supports up to 64 channels and remapping to 512 parameter entries. Advanced Event Triggering provides program breakpoints, data watchpoints, counters, and state sequencing; Cortex-A8 and system trace record execution in real time. JTAG supports testing and emulation and includes a defined device ID. The EMAC Switch is a three-port Gigabit switch with one internal and two external ports, supports MII/GMII/RMII/RGMII, and requires 3.3-V PHY interfaces; MDIO manages PHY configuration and status. Four 32-channel GPIO modules support configurable inputs, outputs, interrupts, and wired logic. The GPMC provides a glueless interface to NOR, NAND, SRAM, and similar memories with up to 512 MB addressing across eight chip selects, while the ELM locates NAND errors using BCH algorithms.

The HDMI 1.3a transmitter supports digital video, multichannel audio, CEC, and DDC, with defined high-speed TMDS impedance, routing, ESD-protection, and pullup requirements. The HDVPSS provides video capture and display pipelines, scaling, de-interlacing, alpha blending, color conversion, compositing, graphics layers, and HDMI output.

Aaron Rodgers threw for 300 yards and four touchdowns as Green Bay beat Detroit 31-24, finishing the regular season on a six-game winning streak and claiming the NFC North title by one game. Rodgers ended the season with 4,428 passing yards, 40 touchdowns and seven interceptions despite a sore right calf. Detroit, which lost its final three games, will face Seattle as the NFC’s lowest-seeded playoff team, while Green Bay hosts the New York Giants. The Packers totaled 448 yards, 28 first downs and 153 rushing yards; Detroit’s Zach Zenner ran for 69 yards and a touchdown. Green Bay cornerback Quinten Rollins was carted off with a neck injury and evaluated at the hospital.

NVIDIA’s GA10x-class Ampere architecture builds on Turing with second-generation RT Cores and third-generation Tensor Cores, delivering up to twice the performance in programmable shading, ray tracing, FP32 processing, and AI, with structural sparsity doubling Tensor Core throughput.

The NVIDIA A40 targets data-center visual computing, offering up to 2× FP32 and ray-tracing throughput and up to 5× AI/data-science throughput, or 10× with sparsity, versus the Quadro RTX 6000. Its PCIe Gen4 interface provides up to 2× higher bandwidth, while 48GB of memory can scale to 96GB by linking two GPUs with NVLink. It supports vGPU software, Quadro Sync, three DisplayPort 1.4 outputs, and the NVIDIA EGX Platform. Virtualization is enabled by default with display outputs disabled.

Ampere GPUs support 4K120 and 8K60 displays, including two 8K60 displays with one cable each. DisplayPort 1.4a with DSC 1.2a and HDMI 2.1 with up to 48 Gbps bandwidth add support for high resolutions, refresh rates, and dynamic HDR. The architecture also supports HDCP 2.3 and HDCP 1.x.

Fifth-generation NVDEC provides hardware-accelerated decoding for MPEG-2, VC-1, H.264, H.265, VP8, VP9, and AV1 on Windows and Linux. GA10x GPUs are the first to provide AV1 hardware decode; in the cited test, NVDEC played 8K60 HDR AV1 using about 4% CPU compared with 28 FPS and over 85% CPU utilization for software decoding. AV1 is described as providing roughly 50–55% bitrate savings over H.264.

Seventh-generation NVENC offloads encoding from the CPU, supports high-quality low-latency streaming, and can handle 4K H.264 and 8K HEVC encoding. Its quality reportedly exceeds software x264 with the Fast preset and approaches x264 Medium.

GeForce GA10x GPUs also add accelerated ray-traced motion blur, concurrent ray tracing and shading or compute, RTX IO for direct SSD-to-GPU loading and decompression through DirectStorage, and the first GPU support for GDDR6X memory. The RTX 3090 uses GA102, has 24GB of memory, 10,496 CUDA cores, and up to 936 GB/s peak bandwidth, and supports 8K HDR rendering with DLSS. The RTX 3070 uses GA104 and GDDR6, excludes NVLink, and is described as faster than the RTX 2080 Ti.

GA10x GDDR6X memory includes Error Detection and Replay, which detects faulty transmissions and retries them until successful, helping identify memory-overclocking limits without immediately crashing.

The RTX A6000 workstation GPU has 48GB of GDDR6 memory, expandable to 96GB through NVLink, and supports real-time and final-frame ray tracing, hardware-accelerated motion blur, and AI denoising. Comparative graphics, rendering, HPC, and deep-learning benchmarks are presented against the RTX 6000. NVIDIA provides the specifications and materials as-is, disclaims warranties, and states that its products are not authorized for medical, military, aircraft, space, life-support, or other safety-critical applications.

This lecture reviews relativistic kinematics for particle and nuclear physics. It defines \(\beta=v/c\) and \(\gamma=1/\sqrt{1-\beta^2}\), along with a particle’s total energy \(E=\gamma mc^2\), momentum \(p=\gamma mv\), and the relation \(E^2=p^2c^2+m^2c^4\). For massless particles, \(E=pc\); at rest, \(E=mc^2\). Energy and momentum transform under Lorentz boosts like time and space.

Lorentz transformations preserve the invariant quantity \(m^2s^2\), whereas total energy and momentum are conserved in reactions without being Lorentz invariant. In a particle decay, the invariant mass calculated from the summed energies and momenta of the daughter particles equals the parent’s mass. This principle allows particles such as the Higgs boson to be identified from their decay products.

The lecture contrasts collider and fixed-target experiments and uses Z-boson production as an example. It also assigns exercises involving the Lorentz factor of 100 GeV electrons and positrons, deuteron binding energy, photon reabsorption, antiproton production thresholds, pion decay speeds, proton–neutron–pion production, and photon wavelength shifts in Compton scattering. These calculations apply relativistic kinematics without requiring knowledge of the underlying dynamics or forces.

A July 26, 2001 email compilation titled “Enron Mentions” noted that Fortune ranked Enron 16th on its Global 500 list and summarized several business and policy developments:

- Corporate earnings were falling sharply. BusinessWeek reported that profits at 90 bellwether companies had declined for three consecutive quarters. Second-quarter net income fell 34%, while sales rose 8%, largely because of Enron’s 196% revenue increase; excluding Enron, sales were flat. First Call projected an 8% third-quarter earnings decline, and 811 companies had warned of lower second-quarter earnings. Intel’s net income fell 94%, Motorola lost $759 million, General Motors’ profit fell 73%, and United Airlines lost $292 million. Citigroup, General Electric, Pfizer and Johnson & Johnson reported gains.

- Western electricity prices and federal price controls were causing power developers to cancel projects, potentially reducing projected Northwest generating capacity by as much as 1,000 megawatts, or 3% of peak demand. Portland General Electric halted installation of a 45-megawatt peaking turbine, and utilities abandoned negotiations with NRG Energy that would have supported 300 megawatts of new capacity. Some industry participants attributed cancellations to federal price controls, while others cited weak demand, conservation and new generation already under construction. Utilities raised concerns about winter reliability, while some developers continued projects with advance supply contracts.

- The Bonn climate agreement created mechanisms for international greenhouse-gas emissions trading and Clean Development Mechanism projects as governments worked to implement the Kyoto Protocol and meet emissions limits by 2012. The measures were encouraging investment in lower-emission projects and giving carbon costs a role in corporate investment decisions. Royal Dutch/Shell projected a carbon price of $5 per tonne in 2005 and $20 per tonne by 2012. Green investment funds and established energy, oil, automobile, utility and independent power companies were among those expected to benefit or adapt, while the article identified Enron’s trading capabilities as potentially useful in emissions trading.

- Kobe Steel announced plans to borrow 165 billion yen, or $1.34 billion, to enter Japan’s wholesale electricity market. It was building two coal-fired generators with capacity of 700,000 kilowatts each and planned to begin supplying power in April 2002. Japan had opened roughly 30% of its electricity market to large consumers, and Enron was among the foreign companies interested in participating.

- Enron canceled its Miami-Dade County power-plant option and concentrated on a stalled Deerfield Beach project. The Deerfield plan was placed on hold by Broward County’s moratorium on new power-plant construction, which was enforced through air-quality permit denials and scheduled to end May 1. Enron was considering legal action, while the cancellation allowed Miami-Dade to proceed with closing a construction landfill on the former site. Enron did not rule out developing another Miami-Dade location.

- The Washington Post reported that presidential adviser Karl Rove took five months to divest government-related stocks, meeting officials from six companies—including Intel and Enron—while still holding interests in them. The Intel meeting and Rove’s discussions with Enron CEO Kenneth Lay about energy policy, global warming and a possible FERC appointment drew criticism as possible conflicts of interest. The White House defended the contacts as inconsequential or broad policy discussions, while Rep. Henry Waxman sought a Justice Department review. Rove received divestiture orders on June 6 and sold his holdings June 7.

- TheStreet.com reported that Enron Chairman Kenneth Lay and CEO Jeffrey Skilling were publicly describing Enron’s stock as undervalued while selling substantial holdings. Lay sold nearly 400,000 shares during 2001, while Skilling sold shares between $52.95 and $80.57 and registered additional shares for sale. Enron said the transactions were routine program sales connected to expiring options, taxes and equity-based compensation, but analysts said the sales sent a mixed message about management’s public comments.

- Enron’s broadband business was losing value as investors rejected earlier projections that it would account for billions of dollars. Enron reported a $109 million broadband loss, compared with $17 million in pre-tax income a year earlier, and said recovery would be delayed by at least a year. Analysts reduced Enron’s target prices and assumed no value for broadband, although its wholesale energy business remained strong. Enron planned to reduce spending sharply while retaining some broadband services and considering whether to sell or lease the network.

Repeated North Atlantic low-pressure systems have brought blustery, showery weather through much of July and August, but forecasters say high pressure may build by the weekend and bring warmer, sunnier conditions to much of Britain. Temperatures could reach the low 20s C on Saturday and about 25C in southeast England from Sunday to Monday, though Tropical Storm Gert could disrupt the outlook. The Met Office sees only a small chance of settled weather, mainly in southern Britain. Gert is expected to remain offshore, strengthen briefly, then move northeast and weaken before reaching the UK.

U.S. colleges celebrated Valentine’s Day with treats, serenades, rallies, date-night guides, e-cards, relationship stories, and campus surprises. Arizona State students shared customs from their home countries, Cal’s gymnastics team distributed valentines, Marshall received a tuba serenade, and Montclair held a rally celebrating love. Duquesne offered an on-campus date guide, Clemson staged a surprise, and Lehigh teased rival Lafayette. Boston University promoted e-valentines and shared stories from an estimated 9,030 couples who met on Commonwealth Avenue.

President Hayes returned Senate Bill 71 to the Senate, objecting that its 20-year suspension of Chinese laborers’ entry and residence violated the 1880 treaty with China and the nation’s good faith. The treaty allowed Congress to regulate, limit, or suspend such immigration, but not absolutely prohibit it, and required reasonable limits confined to laborers. Negotiators’ records indicated that neither government contemplated a ban lasting nearly a generation.

Hayes supported legislation addressing Chinese immigration but urged Congress to shorten the suspension, reconsider discriminatory registration and passport requirements, and provide for transit. He warned that a permanent restrictive policy could drive Asian trade elsewhere. Although concerned about labor competition and public order, he noted that Chinese labor had benefited U.S. railways, agriculture, mining, and commerce, and recommended a shorter experimental period whose successful provisions could later be retained. He enclosed treaty papers and a memorandum from the Chinese minister.

A fishing group including former NHLer Willie Mitchell encountered an eight- to nine-foot salmon shark about 120 kilometres off Tofino, initially mistaking it for a great white and filming it underwater. Biologists said the shy species primarily eats Pacific salmon, belongs to the great-white family, and can reach three metres. The rare sighting was viewed as a sign of a healthy ecosystem, while climate change could push southern shark species northward.

Sean Combs was sentenced Friday to 50 months in prison for two offenses, closing his criminal case after a July verdict seen as a partial win for the defense. He has denied accusations of sexual assault and still faces dozens of civil suits, with an attorney predicting more lawsuits. Combs said his conduct cost him his businesses, career and reputation. His once nearly $1 billion empire spanning music, fashion, alcohol and media has contracted: Diageo ended its Cîroc relationship, Sean John was pulled from Macy’s, and he stepped down from Revolt and sold his stake. The civil cases could bring settlements, legal fees and further reputational damage, though Combs retains mansions and a private jet for sale. A reputation strategist said he is unlikely to regain his former status, while his former girlfriend’s lawyers said the sentence recognizes the impact of his conduct.

German MP Norbert Röttgen, a close Merkel ally, said Germany should formally suspend EU membership talks with Turkey as long as Erdoğan consolidates authoritarian power, adding "Erdoğan is not Turkey." Erdoğan told a rally in Ankara that threatened freezing talks "is not that important for us anyway," and accused German and Dutch leaders of "Nazi practices" over cancelled rallies in Europe.

Academics in Zimbabwe and South Africa said Grace Mugabe’s 2014 sociology doctorate from the University of Zimbabwe fell below PhD standards. They called the thesis plagiarized, lacking original ideas and citing works published after her graduation. The thesis was uploaded four years late, prompting ridicule and a petition to Zimbabwe’s anti-corruption commission; officials said no investigation was underway. Rhodes University’s Kirk Helliker said its theory was extremely shallow.

U.S. stocks closed higher Monday, led by technology and energy as oil prices rose and investors awaited an expected Federal Reserve rate increase. The Dow gained 0.23%, the S&P 500 0.32%, and the Nasdaq 0.51%. Futures pricing implied an 85% chance of a 25-basis-point hike and a 15% chance of 50 points. Bluebird Bio surged on positive trial data, while bitcoin-related stocks rose sharply. Markets largely ignored an attempted bombing at a New York commuter hub.

The court held that Eugene A. Causey acquired fee-simple title to the section 16 lands through a prior chancery decree quieting title based on Isaac Adair’s promise to give him the land, Causey’s possession, and his valuable improvements. An absolute promise to convey land represents the grantor’s entire estate, and “title” means a fee. The decree binding Causey’s heirs, including those unborn when it was rendered, also bound appellants and his conveyance to T. F. Tiller.

The section 15 lands were not involved in that decree. Adair’s will gave Causey only a life estate, with the fee in remainder to his children, and Tiller acquired no greater interest. A life tenant may cut timber only as reasonably necessary for proper enjoyment and good husbandry and may not materially diminish the remaindermen’s inheritance. All merchantable timber had been removed from the 160 wooded acres, with an actual value of $619.38. Because good husbandry required one-fourth of the standing timber to remain, damages were limited to one-fourth of that value. The chancery court’s award of $154.84 was therefore proper, and the decree was affirmed.

MIT CSAIL researchers developed Pensieve, a neural-network-based system that selects video-streaming algorithms according to network conditions to reduce buffering and improve playback quality. Tests showed 10–30% less rebuffering and 10–25% better quality; users could prioritize quality, speed, or data use. The team plans to open-source it and test it for VR video.

The passage examines how female sex scandals are judged differently from male scandals, using renewed rumors about Nikki Haley’s affair and Megan Barry’s admitted affair with Nashville police Sgt. Robert Forrest Jr. Barry apologized, emphasized the affair’s consensual nature, invoked faith, avoided details, and resisted scrutiny of other alleged affairs.

The author argues that Barry’s response created a “female sex scandal playbook”: public disclosure, embarrassment, shame, minimal detail, and distinctions from abuses of power by men. Supporters minimized her conduct, while media figures defended Haley and criticized author Michael Wolff, himself a former participant in a workplace sex scandal.

Earlier commentary asked why powerful women rarely face sex scandals and invoked feminism’s “emotional labor,” portraying female politicians as too burdened by work and caregiving for such behavior. The passage says women involved in scandals are also expected to deny pleasure and center shame or forgiveness rather than acknowledge enjoyment.

Predicting Barry’s continued political survival, the author suggests she may be insulated by #MeToo-era attitudes and a broader cultural preference for celebrating strong women, marking a shift away from the traditional scarlet-A treatment of female adultery.

Two years after being traded from Toronto to Pittsburgh, two-time Stanley Cup champion Phil Kessel celebrated his Cup day by golfing and filling the trophy with hot dogs, captioning a photo "Hotdogs taste better out of The Cup! #twotime" — a jab at a Toronto Sun column by Steve Simmons.

Aligned single-crystal graphene flakes were grown by ambient-pressure CVD on atomically smooth Cu(111)/sapphire. SEM, AFM, contact-potential imaging, Raman spectroscopy, and STM showed that some coalescing flakes formed seamless stitches, while others contained merging lines with nanoscale structural defects. Wet oxidation in 90 °C water produced Cu₂O beneath 55 of 122 examined merging regions, indicating water-permeable pathways through the graphene; the remaining 67 regions showed no such oxidation and were considered likely seamless. STM revealed that many defective merging lines were vertical overlapped junctions, with one graphene flake overgrowing another at a copper step, including between crystallographically aligned flakes. Tip manipulation tore and folded the upper graphene layer, confirming the overlap structure. The study classifies graphene merging as seamless stitching, defective stitching involving structural defects or grain boundaries, and overlapped junctions. Approximately 55% of merging regions appeared seamless, while 45% were defective. These findings challenge the assumption that aligned stitched graphene is uniformly impermeable and suggest potential uses in nanofiltration, desalination, and molecular sieving.

The PGA Tour is coordinating with law enforcement to protect players and fans at Wednesday’s Dell Technologies Match Play in Austin amid a bombing investigation that has killed two people and injured four.

The NCLT directed Bhushan Steel’s Committee of Creditors to consider employees’ objections to Tata Steel’s bid and report its decision, rejecting Tata Steel’s challenge to the employees’ standing. Employees argue Tata is an “undischarged insolvent” under IBC Section 29A.

The U.S. Department of State’s Office of the Historian released the 1902 Foreign Relations of the United States as an ebook on May 26, 2018. It preserves the printed edition’s full content while adding search, bookmarking, note-taking, and offline access; document numbers are recommended for citation. The volume includes President Theodore Roosevelt’s message to Congress, which credits laws, long-term economic forces, and citizens’ enterprise for national prosperity, acknowledges harms accompanying industrial growth, and calls for patient, practical regulation that preserves greater benefits while addressing lesser evils.

Singer Meghan Linsey was bitten by a brown recluse spider while sleeping, causing worsening facial pain, swelling, muscle spasms, a full-body rash, and a necrotic wound. There is no antidote; treatment focuses on symptoms and wound care, and recovery can take weeks or months. Linsey underwent hyperbaric oxygen therapy, and two months later her wound was healing well with an almost unnoticeable scar. She has resumed performing and hopes sharing her experience raises awareness of brown recluse spiders, whose bites are rare but can cause serious tissue damage.

Vision-language models support captioning, visual question answering, dialogue, and embodied tasks such as autonomous driving, but long visual token sequences create memory and latency bottlenecks. Existing training-free pruning methods generally use fixed schedules or handcrafted layer-specific rules, which cannot adapt to sample, query, or layer-dependent token importance while reliably respecting computational budgets.

The paper proposes Complexity-Adaptive Pruning (AutoPrune), a training-free framework that assigns each input a customized pruning policy. It estimates sample complexity through mutual information between early-layer visual and textual tokens: high values indicate simpler inputs, while low values indicate complex inputs requiring broader exploration. This estimate modulates logistic token-retention curves modeled on the human explore–commit–stabilize pattern, producing aggressive early pruning for simple inputs and conservative, delayed pruning for complex ones. Each curve is rescaled so its area meets a specified token or FLOPs budget.

AutoPrune can be integrated into models including LLaVA-1.5, LLaVA-NeXT, and Senna. Experiments across vision-language benchmarks and autonomous-driving tasks report consistent improvements over existing training-free methods across pruning ratios. On LLaVA-1.5-7B, AutoPrune prunes 89% of visual tokens and reduces inference FLOPs by 76.8% while retaining 96.7% of original average accuracy, a 9.1% gain over PDrop. The pruning problem is further formulated as jointly optimizing token allocation, selection, and revival under a global computation constraint.

A Nature Climate Change study finds human-caused climate change could become the leading driver of extreme U.S. summer heat waves in the 2020s. California, Nevada, and arid Oregon, Utah, Arizona, and Idaho may cross that threshold within years; the Great Lakes in the 2030s and the Great Plains in 30–50 years. Without human influence, half of projected extreme heat waves would not occur.

The 1-4 “Slice” zone offense uses a high alignment, strong inside posting, and spot-up outside shooting. It allows entry passes and quick pressure releases to four receivers, while rapid reversals and rotations force zone defenses to shift. The system is easy to teach but difficult to defend and requires strong fundamentals, zone-reading, player development, and an inside game.

Basic actions include O1 entry passes, O5 slice cuts, and post-ups when cuts are denied. O4 can feed from high/low action, shoot, or drive. Options also include wing baseline feeds, cross-court skip passes, weakside give-and-go rotations, and ball reversals through O4. Overplayed posts can be released via pump fake-and-lob or passed to a wing, while overplayed wings can receive back-cut feeds directly or through O4. The offense maintains continuity through weakside skips, high-post passes, give-and-go actions, and spot-ups.

- **Interrupts:** The ARM Cortex-A8 Interrupt Controller prioritizes requests from system peripherals, handles up to 128 inputs with programmable priorities, and generates IRQs or FIQs; general-purpose devices do not support FIQ generation. The C674x interrupt controller combines up to 128 device events into 12 prioritized CPU interrupts. Events 15–95 can be selected from 24 multiplexed sources through `DSP_INTMUX_x` registers. The DSP controller also generates CPU exceptions, NMI, and emulation interrupts.

- **Timing and board routing:** Datasheet timing values are specified at device pins and exclude board-routing delays, which must be included in system analysis. IBIS models are recommended for accurate I/O timing analysis, while DDR2 timing is addressed through PCB routing rules. For 3.3-V signals, Vref is 1.5 V, and timing tests use a 4-V/ns input edge rate. A 2-ns transmission line may represent tester load effects, but its delay is not added to or subtracted from datasheet timings.

- **DCAN:** Two DCAN interfaces support distributed real-time control and CAN protocol version 2.0. Features include per-message identifier masks, programmable FIFO and loop-back modes, automatic bus-on recovery using a programmable 32-bit timer, test-mode access to message RAM, configurable CAN Rx/Tx pins, and interrupt lines including parity-error support.

- **EDMA:** The EDMA controller transfers data between memories and slave peripherals for cache servicing, non-cacheable accesses, user-programmed transfers, and host accesses. It supports up to 64 channels. Each synchronization event defaults to its matching parameter entry but can be remapped to any of 512 parameter-table entries.

- **Debug and test:** Advanced Event Triggering provides hardware program breakpoints, data watchpoints, event or cycle counters, and state sequencing. Cortex-A8 and system-level trace collects and exports real-time execution, timing, and data-access information without affecting system execution; destinations include the ETB and the 5-pin system trace interface. IEEE 1149.1 JTAG supports BSDL testing and emulation. TRST has an internal pulldown and may require external handling with third-party controllers. The read-only JTAG ID register is at `0x4814 0600`, with device value `0x0B8F 202F`.

- **Ethernet:** The EMAC switch contains three gigabit ports, one internal and two external. External ports support 10Base-T, 100BaseTX, and full-duplex 1000BaseT through MII, GMII, RMII, and RGMII modes. Its I/Os are 3.3 V and are not compatible with 2.5-V signaling. Rather than driving `MTXER` on transmit underflow, the switch deliberately corrupts the frame CRC so the network detects an error. CPPI provides 2,048 words of 32-bit buffer-descriptor memory for up to 512 descriptors. The MDIO module polls all 32 addresses on a shared two-wire bus, enumerates PHYs, and supports autonegotiation configuration, result retrieval, and EMAC parameter setup.

- **GPIO:** Four 32-channel GPIO modules provide up to 128 configurable 1.8-V/3.3-V pins, subject to device configuration. Channels can operate as inputs or outputs, generate edge- or level-based interrupts for the ARM or Media Controller, and include keyboard-interface debouncing. Atomic set/clear operations permit multiple software processes to control outputs without disabling interrupts.

- **GPMC and ELM:** The GPMC provides a glueless interface to NOR and NAND flash, SRAM, pseudo-SRAM, and custom asynchronous devices. It supports 8- or 16-bit multiplexed address/data buses, up to eight chip selects, 512 MB of addressing, and prefetch/write-posting functions for NAND. The ELM locates BCH errors for 512-byte NAND blocks using 4-, 8-, or 16-bit error-location algorithms and generates completion interrupts.

- **HDMI:** The device includes an HDMI 1.3a transmitter with TMDS encoding, CEC, DDC/I2C, DVI RGB compatibility, uncompressed multichannel L-PCM audio, and TMDS clock rates up to 185.625 MHz. Supported video includes 1920×1080p at 75 Hz with 8-bit color, 1600×1200 at 60 Hz, and higher color depths at reduced resolutions. TMDS pairs require 100 Ω ±10% differential and 60 Ω ±10% single-ended impedances, paired vias, and careful differential routing. HDMI inputs require ESD protection with no more than 5 pF capacitance; DDC pullups are required unless integrated in the ESD device.

- **Video processing and output:** The HDVPSS provides external video capture and display outputs, HD/SD encoders, HDMI, two processing pipelines, de-interlacing, scaling, alpha blending, chroma keying, color-space and pixel-format conversion, picture-in-picture composition, and three graphics layers. It supports format conversions up to 1080p at 60 Hz, digital outputs up to 30 bits at 165 MHz, and an external capture port up to 165 MHz. Analog video DAC outputs operate in normal or bypass mode; board layouts should use short, isolated traces and 75 Ω-impedance routing, with bypass and reconstruction-filter placement specified for each mode.

- **I2C and imaging:** Four I2C modules implement the version 2.1 two-wire bus at 10–400 Kbps, with seven- and ten-bit addressing, multimaster operation, a noise filter of 50 ns or less, and a 32-byte FIFO. They do not support CBUS-compatible devices or fail-safe I/O buffers. The Imaging Subsystem accepts parallel or serial camera data, processes it through the Image Signal Processor, and provides flash-strobe and mechanical-shutter timing. It supports Bayer and YCbCr input, up to four camera data lanes, protocol error correction, cropping and compression, sensor linearization, lens-shading and defect correction, color correction, 3A data collection, and 8-, 12-, or 16-bit output.

- **DDR2/DDR3 memory:** Dedicated memory interfaces support 16- or 32-bit DDR2/DDR3 paths, device densities from 64 Mb through 4 Gb, two chip selects, independent page tracking, associated PHYs, and interleaving across two DDR interfaces. DDR2 designs generally support x16 DDR2-800 or faster compatible devices and require a minimum six-layer stackup, isolated routing regions, high-speed bypass capacitors, specified termination, and a resistively divided VREF. DDR3 designs support x8 or x16 devices through DDR3-1600, require at least four layers, need separate keepout regions for multiple controllers, and require uninterrupted reference planes and extensive high-speed decoupling. Return-current paths should be kept short, with transitions between reference planes supported by bypass capacitors or vias as specified.

The lecture frames policy as a “game changer” for sustainable real estate by balancing three bottom lines: environmental benefits, social benefits, and private profit. Because markets may fail to balance these goals, policy must address information asymmetry through certifications such as LEED and Well, split landlord-tenant incentives through green leases, and externalities by converting social benefits and costs into private financial incentives.

Positive externalities arise when green buildings generate societal benefits, such as lower carbon emissions, that developers cannot fully monetize, producing an undersupply of sustainable buildings. “Carrots,” including subsidies, tax rebates, grants, density bonuses, and matching funds, can make these benefits financially rewarding and turn negative project NPVs positive. Negative externalities from brown buildings and pollution can be addressed through “sticks,” such as carbon taxes, penalties, disclosure requirements, energy-performance mandates, and building codes. Policy calibration is difficult: incentives must be large enough to change behavior but not impose excessive social costs, and policymakers face modeling uncertainty, unintended consequences, affordability concerns, and behavioral responses.

Examples of carrots include the EU’s building-renovation funding, Massachusetts Mass Save services and heat-pump subsidies, and Arlington, Virginia’s increased floor-area ratios for LEED-certified buildings. Density bonuses reward greener development without direct payments but can increase embodied and operational carbon, energy use, traffic, and infrastructure demands. MIT research on the balance between sustainability and housing affordability examines how Massachusetts net-zero requirements, including stricter HERS energy scores, may raise building costs that developers pass to renters and buyers, potentially worsening affordability, especially for lower-income households. The lecture recommends pairing mandates with subsidies.

Examples of sticks include New York City’s building energy-score disclosure, Boston’s BERDO emissions limits, Cambridge’s proposed BEUDO, and UK rules preventing poorly rated properties from being leased. Boston and Cambridge use different approaches: Boston uses absolute emissions limits with a 2050 net-zero goal, while Cambridge uses each building’s 2018–2019 baseline and a proposed 2035 net-zero target. This baseline method can create unequal burdens depending on when buildings were renovated. MIT faces potential BEUDO penalties and plans to reach net zero by 2026 through carbon offsets, with actual campus-wide net zero targeted by 2050, although the lecturer notes uncertainty and credibility problems in the carbon-offset market. The lecture also observes that governments tend to use stronger enforcement against large commercial owners and incentives for households.

Energy codes can support both mitigation, by reducing emissions, and adaptation, such as requiring elevated ground floors in flood zones. Their stringency varies by jurisdiction, potentially encouraging developers to move toward less restrictive states.

The lecture then examines climate-resilience investment in coastal areas despite continued migration into high-risk zones and development that is often rebuilt larger after disasters. Resilience measures are costly and can involve elevating land, flood barriers, permeable surfaces, and preserving natural space. Miami illustrates a positive feedback loop in which public investment protects its economic base, attracts residents and businesses, expands the tax base, and supports further investment. Poor communities such as Fair Bluff, North Carolina, face a negative loop in which repeated disasters, depopulation, business closures, and limited tax revenue prevent resilience investment. The federal allocation of $47 billion for climate resilience raises moral-hazard and distributional concerns, especially because local matching requirements disadvantage poorer towns. Whether to continue protecting vulnerable communities or pursue organized “managed retreat” remains an unresolved and controversial policy question.

Mayor Bill de Blasio urged Albany to expand the city's expiring School Zone Speed Camera program and announced a redesign of Ninth Street in Park Slope, where two children were killed in March by a driver running a red light. The redesign, spanning Prospect Park West to Third Avenue, adds protected bike lanes, expanded pedestrian and cyclist access, and changed loading regulations. The DOT proposal will be released at a community workshop, presented to Community Board 6 next month, and installed this summer. The city seeks cameras at 150 additional school zones, a broadened definition of school zones, and program extension to 2022.

The NBA has no clear successor to LeBron James and Stephen Curry, who remain dominant in jersey sales, social-media engagement, ratings and narrative influence despite their ages. Victor Wembanyama is presented as the leading candidate to become the league’s next face, supported by his exceptional skills, international profile and predictions from 16 of 20 coaches, scouts and executives that he will be the NBA’s best player in 2030. Anthony Edwards is the strongest candidate to follow a Jordan-like path as a charismatic, elite scoring guard. Luka Dončić could become the next face through the Lakers’ visibility and a potential championship, while Cooper Flagg, Shai Gilgeous-Alexander and Jalen Williams are additional possibilities. Zion Williamson and LaMelo Ball offer less conventional routes modeled on Curry’s late emergence. Because “face of the NBA” has no formal criteria, talent and accomplishments must combine with market visibility, social-media reach, storytelling and compelling rivalries. Future clashes among Wembanyama, Flagg, Dončić, Edwards and Gilgeous-Alexander could help create the league’s next central star or rivalry.

This continuation patent application describes electronic devices with transparent glass enclosures defining multiple sides, including major sides, peripheral sides, and corner regions. Enclosures may be monolithic or formed from multiple glass members with varying wall thicknesses, curved or tapered edges, overlapping joints, textured input regions, and force-sensitive areas. Display assemblies positioned within the enclosure may extend through multiple sides, using one folded or flexible display or multiple coordinated panels. Touch and force sensors, haptics, speakers, microphones, cameras, and other sensors may support interaction through the exterior surfaces.

Display regions may correspond to distinct physical surfaces or be dynamically combined into a unified, continuously scrollable interface spanning several sides. Either major side may be selected as the primary interface based on orientation, user interaction, biometrics, time, application state, or user preference. Symmetrically arranged speakers, microphones, cameras, and sensors can provide similar functionality regardless of orientation.

Disclosed enclosure shapes include cuboid, cylindrical, elliptic cylindrical, and octagonal forms. Glass components may be joined using glass frit, adhesive, epoxy, fusion or ultrasonic welding, mechanical interlocks, or additive manufacturing. Joints and seams can be positioned near corners or outside viewing areas to preserve transparency and display continuity. Openings and removable or fixed caps may accommodate assembly, charging, communication, audio, or optical components. Internal components may include processors, memory, circuit boards, batteries, cameras, sensors, wireless charging components, wiring, and structural supports, while touchscreens may detect input across most or all exterior surfaces.

Russia has agreed to April 24 talks in Geneva with the US and UN to restart peace efforts in Syria, subject to US confirmation. The meeting would be the first such contact since Donald Trump became president. It follows a US strike on a Syrian air base in response to a deadly nerve-gas attack attributed to Bashar al-Assad’s regime. Russia and Iran warned that further attacks would prompt military retaliation.

The article argues that the paradox of moral education arises from philosophy of education’s tacit reliance on libertarian free will, which understands autonomy and responsibility through alternative choices and self-initiated action. The dilemma of determinism challenges this view: determinism appears to eliminate freedom and responsibility, while indeterminism provides no adequate control over choices.

Drawing on Harry Frankfurt’s thought experiment and hierarchical theory of the will, the article proposes that alternative possibilities are unnecessary for moral responsibility. The relevant basis is volitional control: people form second-order desires, assess their own wills, and identify with or reject particular first-order desires. People may therefore act authentically and responsibly when acting from a will they genuinely want, even if they cannot act differently or do not control the conditions determining their actions. Rationality, the moral status of reasons, and control over external alternatives are not required criteria.

For moral education, responsibility should be assessed through what people actually do and how they identify with their wills rather than through hypothetical alternatives. Educators should help young people accept responsibility for actions, omissions, and consequences, including conduct they believe is forced, because their attitudes toward inevitability reveal preferences, values, and character. This hierarchical interpretation makes questions about determinism or indeterminism irrelevant to responsibility and resolves the paradox of moral education.

About 666 pilot whales stranded in two pods at Farewell Spit in New Zealand, authorities began removing more than 300 carcasses from the beach. Workers punctured the decomposing whales to prevent gas buildup and explosions before trucking them elsewhere. Three-quarters of the first 416-strong pod died; survivors and a second pod of about 250 were refloated. No new strandings were reported Tuesday, but officers remained alert.
