The lecture reviews stopping trials and Wald’s equality: if \(J\) is a stopping trial for IID random variables \(X_n\) with mean \(\bar X\) and finite \(E[J]\), then \(E[S_J]=\bar X E[J]\). Possibly defective stopping trials are introduced because a proposed rule may never stop. The elementary renewal theorem is then derived: for renewal interarrival times with mean \(\bar X\), \(\lim_{t\to\infty}E[N(t)]/t=1/\bar X\). Its proof requires truncating the interarrival distribution and carefully passing to limits.

Generalized stopping trials extend the framework to paired input and auxiliary variables, such as arrivals and service times. In a G/G/1 queue, the first arrival to an empty system defines a stopping point. Future arrivals and service times are independent of the preceding history, so successive busy-period beginnings form an embedded renewal process.

The lecture also presents Little’s theorem as an accounting identity: the long-run time-average number of customers in the system equals the arrival rate \(\lambda\) times the mean customer delay. Finally, for an M/G/1 queue with Poisson arrivals, IID service times \(V\) of finite first and second moments, and traffic intensity \(\rho=\lambda E[V]<1\), the Pollaczek–Khinchin formula gives the mean queueing delay as
\[
E[W_q]=\frac{\lambda E[V^2]}{2(1-\rho)}.
\]
The discussion emphasizes that unstable queues or infinite service-time second moments can produce extreme or infinite waiting times.

E. B. Woolf & Co. sued Alfred Hamburger on quantum meruit for brokers’ commissions arising from his sale of a printing plant. The court held that the evidence supported a finding that the plaintiffs were employed as brokers and procured the purchaser, making them the efficient procuring cause of the sale despite earlier failed negotiations and the purchaser’s intent to resell. Refusal to give inapplicable legal propositions was proper. The court found error in fixing damages below every customary commission rate testified to: damages had to be assessed from the record, at 2.5% or 5% of the property’s value or an amount between those rates. Plaintiffs’ unpreserved cross-errors could not be heard, but this did not prevent entry of a proper judgment. The lower judgment was reversed and a $750 judgment entered.

Suicide is a major global public health concern and a leading cause of death among people aged 10–24. Although China’s overall suicide rate has declined, adolescent risk remains substantial: studies report high rates of suicidal thoughts, planning, attempts, and ideation. China’s Ministry of Education has promoted mental health services and collaboration among schools, families, and mental health providers.

School-based gatekeeper training is widely used to help teachers, parents, and peers recognize suicide warning signs, communicate with at-risk students, and refer them for professional support. Existing programs can reduce stigma and improve knowledge and self-efficacy, but evidence for reducing suicide behavior or consistently changing gatekeeper behavior is inconclusive. In China, rigorous, culturally localized studies among secondary-school teachers and parents are lacking, while factors such as rural left-behind children and shortages of qualified school counselors complicate implementation.

This study therefore uses a two-round Delphi process to develop a localized school-based suicide-prevention gatekeeper training program for Chinese teachers and parents. Initial content was based on literature, school counselors, and suicide-prevention experts, then organized into eight areas covering suicide understanding, risk factors and warning signs, communication, risk assessment, safety planning, teacher–parent collaboration, support and referral, and barriers to seeking or providing help. Chinese experts rated statements for importance, feasibility, and appropriateness using a five-point scale, received feedback, and rerated them. Statements with substantial consensus were retained, while those with low or conflicting ratings were discarded.

The study reports a solid-state method for generating and detecting magnetic monopole fields on three-dimensional topological insulator surfaces using scanning tunneling microscopy and spectroscopy. A radially distributed electric field from an STM tip induces Hall surface currents at the interfaces of a topological-insulator layer, producing fields equivalent to paired magnetic monopoles. The orbital magnetic moments of image potential states couple to these fields, causing Zeeman splitting of their energy levels.

Bismuth films grown on Si(111) exhibited progressively more topological structures: topologically trivial √3-Bi, two-dimensional topological-insulator Bi(110), and three-dimensional higher-order topological-insulator Bi(111). Image potential states on √3-Bi and Bi(110) showed six Gaussian-like peaks whose linewidths decreased with increasing quantum number. In contrast, Bi(111) states with quantum numbers above one were asymmetric and split, with two sub-peaks clearly resolved for \(n=2\) and overlapping sub-peaks at higher levels. The measured \(n=2\) splitting was about 400 meV, comparable to a theoretical estimate of 204 meV, and its scaling followed the proposed model.

Possible explanations involving symmetric and antisymmetric states, quantum-well confinement, and quantum-dot confinement were examined and ruled out based on energy-level behavior, thickness independence, and terrace size. The splitting also varied systematically with tunneling current and therefore tip electric field, as predicted for field-induced magnetic monopoles. Overall, the observations and modeling support the interpretation that magnetic monopoles were generated, detected, and electrically modulated on a three-dimensional topological-insulator surface.

The ninth-generation NVENC encoder improves AV1 and HEVC quality by 5% BD-BR PSNR and adds 4:2:2 encoding; its AV1 Ultra High Quality mode adds another 5% improvement, with combined gains of up to 15% BD-BR PSNR. The RTX 5090 supports up to three encoders and two decoders, boosting export speeds by more than 50% generation over generation and fourfold over a single encoder in the RTX 3090. The sixth-generation NVDEC decoder doubles H.264 decoding speed, matches HEVC and AV1 speeds, and supports 4:2:2 H.264 and HEVC.

Blackwell supports DisplayPort 2.1b with up to 80 Gbps using UHBR 20. With DSC, it can drive 8K at 165 Hz or 4K at 480 Hz, though the highest link rates require a DP80LL-certified cable.

DLSS 4 adds Multi Frame Generation, which can create up to three additional frames for each traditionally rendered frame. Its AI model is 40% faster and uses 30% less VRAM than the prior method, while enhanced Flip Metering moves pacing to the display engine and doubles pixel-processing capability. DLSS 4 also replaces convolutional models with transformer-based models for Super Resolution, Ray Reconstruction, and Deep Learning Anti-Aliasing. These models use twice as many parameters and improve temporal stability, motion detail, lighting, anti-aliasing, and ray-traced image quality.

Blackwell advances neural shaders through Cooperative Vectors for DX12 and Vulkan and differentiable shading features in Slang. The Blackwell GPU family includes GB202 for the RTX 5090, with 92.2 billion transistors, 192 streaming multiprocessors, 24,576 CUDA cores, 192 RT cores, 768 Tensor cores, and a 512-bit memory interface; GB203 for the RTX 5080 and 5070 Ti, with 45.6 billion transistors, 84 multiprocessors, 10,752 CUDA cores, 84 RT cores, 336 Tensor cores, and a 256-bit interface; and GB205 for the RTX 5070, with 31 billion transistors, 50 multiprocessors, 6,400 CUDA cores, 50 RT cores, 200 Tensor cores, and a 192-bit interface. The patent describes image encoding and decoding using motion-vector refinement to improve inter-prediction compression efficiency and reduce computational complexity. An initial L0 or L1 motion vector for a current block is derived, refined, and used for motion compensation through either merge-mode-based or prediction-block-based refinement. Merge-mode refinement uses signaled vector magnitude, direction, and integer- or subpixel-unit information, with search-area offsets added, mirrored, or scaled according to POC differences between L0/L1 reference pictures and the target picture. Prediction-block refinement searches within predetermined areas around the initial vector positions and evaluates candidate prediction blocks using distortion measures such as SAD, SATD, SSE, or MSE. It is conditionally performed based on bidirectional merge prediction, POC differences, and block dimensions; blocks exceeding 16 pixels may be divided into 16×16 subblocks.

The passage also describes encoder and decoder architectures, quad-, binary-, and ternary-tree coding-unit partitioning, AMVP, merge, skip, and current-picture-reference inter-prediction modes, reference-picture and merge-candidate construction, and related coding terminology. It is a continuation of PCT application PCT/KR2019/003642 and related Korean and U.S. applications, whose contents are incorporated by reference.

Tesla, Inc.’s unaudited Form 10-Q for the quarter ended June 30, 2017 covers its automotive and energy generation and storage segments. The company also maintained resale-value guarantee programs, a $343.3 million accrued warranty reserve, and variable-interest-entity arrangements for which it is the primary beneficiary and consolidates the related funds.

Commitments include a 10-year build-to-suit lease for Gigafactory 2, approximately $5.0 billion of required New York spending, and potential annual program payments of $41.2 million for failure to meet investment or job-creation requirements.
