Developmental research suggests children’s fantastical beliefs, including belief in Santa, are not harmful and may support counterfactual reasoning and emotional development. Most children eventually abandon the idea that Santa is physically real by about age eight, a normal stage of cognitive development. Parents can extend belief through plausible explanations, let children develop their own explanations, or provide evidence that Santa is a beloved fantasy. Studies indicate children generally react positively to learning the truth, and a single well-intentioned lie is unlikely to cause lasting harm. Families can maintain a positive Santa tradition after belief ends through creative activities and modest gifts from Santa.

Jacques Dubochet, Joachim Frank and Richard Henderson won the Nobel Prize in Chemistry for developing cryo-electron microscopy, which freezes biomolecules to produce detailed, atomic-scale images and reveal previously unseen molecular processes. Dubochet vitrified samples, Frank sharpened images mathematically, and Henderson produced a 3D protein image at atom-level resolution in 1990. The 9-million-kronor prize recognizes the method’s importance to understanding life’s chemistry and developing pharmaceuticals.

Ten days before his death, Stephen Hawking and Thomas Hertog submitted a paper proposing an alternative multiverse model with infinitely many parallel universes. The paper also suggests that our universe will eventually die as stars lose their energy. Hawking died at 76, and Hertog said he should have won a Nobel Prize, which is not awarded posthumously.

The document specifies version 2 of the Guest-Hypervisor Communication Block (GHCB) protocol for SEV-ES and SEV-SNP guests. It defines a 4 KB, page-aligned, decrypted GHCB whose layout mirrors the SEV-ES VMCB save area, with protocol-version negotiation, hypervisor feature advertisement, CPUID requests, SEV encryption-bit discovery, and GHCB address registration managed through MSR 0xc001_0130. Non-Automatic Exits use a standardized #VC and VMGEXIT sequence, with required guest state, VALID_BITMAP handling, error reporting, and reserved shared-buffer procedures. Supported operations include IO, MSR, MMIO, VMMCALL, page-state changes, SNP guest requests, extended guest requests, AP creation, APIC ID discovery, multi-VMPL execution, trusted I/O, Secure AVIC backing-page management, termination, and restricted-injection doorbell, IPI, and timer services. The specification also covers SNP secrets-page sequence-number extensions, EFI delivery of SNP pages, VCEK and VLEK certificate returns, AP booting and jump tables, NMI handling, and hardware debug-register virtualization. Host notifications use an #HV doorbell page with PendingEvent and NoEoiRequired fields, while the host emulates APIC presentation and end-of-interrupt behavior. SMM and nested virtualization are not supported.

The passage describes a continuation patent application concerning pin-trap mechanisms for surgical linear cutters. A linear surgical stapler has a cartridge half supporting a staple cartridge and an anvil half supporting an anvil surface with staple-forming pockets. The halves pivot toward one another to clamp tissue, after which a firing assembly simultaneously drives staples through the tissue and cuts it with a knife. The stapler also includes a pivoting clamp lever, a firing assembly operated by one of two actuators, a retaining assembly, and various pins, notches, slides, springs, latches, and camming surfaces that control clamping, firing, and separation.

An exemplary stapler includes a cartridge channel, an anvil channel, a staple cartridge with a tissue-gap post, and a firing assembly with a slide block, cam ramps, beams, and an angled knife. During use, the proximal ends of the stapler halves are coupled by capturing a proximal anvil pin, the distal latch pin enters slots in the cartridge half, and closing the clamp lever clamps tissue between the staple cartridge and anvil plate. Moving an actuator distally fires the staples and knife simultaneously. The firing assembly is then returned, the clamp lever is released, and the proximal anvil pin is released so the stapler halves can separate.

The detailed description presents numerous pin-trap embodiments that retain the stapler halves together at their proximal ends while permitting a defined open angle, supporting one-handed manipulation while reducing unintended separation. These embodiments include a longitudinally translatable slide with an aperture that captures the proximal pin; a spring-biased retention pin interacting with camming surfaces; distally and proximally biased locking slides; slides with J-shaped hooks, buttons, and compression or torsion springs; and C-clips released by either a pivotable ejector lever or a slidable ejector slide. Other embodiments use stepped notches with insertion and separation camming surfaces, opposing spring-biased slides, or a rotatable latch with a torque arm that releases the proximal pin when the anvil half is opened farther.

Additional examples describe surgical staplers having an anvil surface, a staple-deploying half, a lateral proximal pivot projection, and a locking member that translates between locked and unlocked states. The locking members may include closed-end notches, hooks, buttons, springs, and camming surfaces that either assist separation or permit pivotable capture of the projection during movement between open and clamped states. The passage states that the described features may be combined in various ways and that the disclosed embodiments and combinations are illustrative rather than limiting.

The team has become more relaxed as the playoffs progressed, though players still feel nervous before games. RSI readings above 70 indicate overbought conditions, while readings below 30 indicate oversold conditions. The strategy buys when RSI is below 30 and the closing price is above the SMA, and sells when RSI is above 70 and the closing price is below the SMA.

The Stochastic Indicator Strategy is a momentum-based technical analysis method that compares an asset’s closing price with its high-low range over a specified period, typically 14 periods. It generates two lines: %K, representing the closing price’s position within that range, and %D, a moving average of %K, typically over three periods. Readings above 80 generally indicate overbought conditions, while readings below 20 indicate oversold conditions. Crossovers between %K and %D are interpreted as shifts in bullish or bearish momentum. Traders may also examine divergence between price and the indicator as a possible reversal signal.

The strategy is used to identify potential trend reversals, overbought and oversold conditions, and entry or exit points. It can be applied to stocks, forex, commodities, cryptocurrencies, and other markets across intraday, swing, and longer-term timeframes. Traders commonly combine it with moving averages, RSI, MACD, support and resistance, chart patterns, and broader market analysis.

Sensitivity can be adjusted by changing the lookback and moving-average periods, smoothing settings, and overbought/oversold thresholds. Longer periods and higher thresholds generally produce fewer, less responsive signals, while shorter periods and lower thresholds produce more frequent signals.

The passage reports an Amibroker backtest using SPY to represent the S&P 500, testing short-term mean-reversion and %K/%D crossover styles. From 1993, the tested rules produced 556 trades, an average return of 0.57% per trade, a 2.2 profit factor, and a 19.8% maximum drawdown. The oversold/overbought approach substantially outperformed the tested crossovers, and short lookback periods performed best.

The strategy may generate false signals in sideways or low-volatility markets, lag in strong trends, and become unreliable during erratic volatility or sudden price movements. Recommended risk practices include setting maximum trade risk and stop-loss orders, diversifying, sizing positions appropriately, and monitoring and adjusting exposure as conditions change.

This observational TriNetX study evaluated the cardiovascular effects of adding GLP-1 receptor agonists to guideline-directed therapy in adults with cancer therapy-related cardiac dysfunction after cardiotoxic antineoplastic treatment. Patients with prior acute coronary syndromes, CABG, or PCI were excluded. Following 1:1 propensity-score matching, 2,446 patients were followed for one year, with 1,223 receiving GLP-1 receptor agonists and 1,223 not receiving them.

The composite outcome of heart failure exacerbation, death, or hospital/emergency department admission occurred in 55.7% of the GLP-1 group versus 68.9% of the control group (OR 0.566, p<0.001). GLP-1 receptor agonists were also associated with significantly lower mortality, heart failure exacerbations, and all-cause hospital admissions, while survival analyses confirmed reduced cardiovascular adverse outcomes. Differences in atrial fibrillation/flutter and ventricular tachycardia were not statistically significant, and gastroenteritis incidence was similar between groups.

The findings suggest GLP-1 receptor agonists may offer cardioprotective benefits in patients with cardiac dysfunction after cancer therapy. However, the observational design prevents causal conclusions, and residual confounding, reliance on electronic health records, unavailable chemotherapy-regimen data, limited demographic representation, and the short follow-up period were acknowledged limitations. Randomized controlled trials were recommended for validation.

The disclosure describes a respiratory assistance system that heats and humidifies respiratory gases delivered through a humidification chamber, inspiratory conduit, and patient interface. The system aims to provide comfortable care, maintain appropriate humidity, and reduce heat loss and condensation. It supports invasive ventilation, non-invasive ventilation, high-flow therapy, and positive airway pressure therapy.

A controller analyzes respiratory-gas characteristics to determine whether the gas source is a room-air-entraining ventilator, such as a blower or turbine, or a non-entraining source supplying dry gas from a wall supply, tank, or bottle. Detection may use mean and bias flow rates, breathing patterns, flow direction, inlet temperature, inlet and outlet sensor measurements, rebreathing patterns, and the presence of an expiratory conduit or heater-wire adapter. Hardware detection can use voltage or resistance measurements and may identify the conduit type, including adult or infant tubing.

Rebreathing can be detected by comparing inlet and outlet flow profiles, correlating sensor signals, identifying double peaks, distinguishing inspiratory and expiratory phases, or comparing phase durations. Bias flow is calculated from raw flow measurements using rate-of-change and average-flow checks, with an additional zero-crossing check for rapidly changing signals. Sensor readings may also be weighted, compared across locations, or used to infer the therapy type and system configuration.

Once the gas source and relevant operating conditions are identified, the controller adjusts chamber-heater temperature set points and power or duty cycle to account for incoming gas humidity and minimize condensation. In one embodiment, the set point is reduced for room-air-entraining systems and maintained for non-entraining systems. The controller may also adjust conduit heating and use outlet temperature as a proxy for humidity when direct humidity measurement is unavailable. It can estimate heat loss through unheated components, use a predetermined default or safety mode before source confirmation, and control heater-plate temperature from outlet-temperature measurements.

The system may also automatically identify connected optional components and validate user-selected gas-source or operating configurations against sensor-derived data. User interfaces can request or display gas-source selections, present detected set points, allow users to accept or reject automatic detections, and issue audible or visual alerts when user input conflicts with measured operating conditions.

A Nigerian cross-sectional study evaluated whether HIV infection and occupational chemical exposure were associated with markers of oxidative stress, apoptosis regulation, immune status, and cancer risk. The study included 248 adults: 128 HIV-positive and 120 HIV-negative participants divided into HIV-positive exposed (n=62), HIV-positive unexposed (n=66), HIV-negative exposed (n=60), and HIV-negative unexposed (n=60) groups. Participants’ serum p53, bcl2, SOD, 8OHdG, and MDA levels and CD4 counts were measured.

HIV-positive exposed participants had lower p53 and bcl2 levels than the other groups, although differences were significant only compared with HIV-negative unexposed participants. They also had significantly higher MDA than HIV-negative exposed and unexposed participants; differences in 8OHdG and SOD were not significant. P53 and bcl2 correlated positively with 8OHdG and SOD but not significantly with MDA. HIV-positive participants had lower CD4 counts regardless of occupational exposure, and CD4 counts were negatively correlated with MDA. After adjustment for sex, age, BMI, and smoking, HIV status and SOD activity were significantly associated with p53 and bcl2, while occupational exposure, CD4, 8OHdG, and MDA were not.

The authors interpreted the findings as suggesting that combined HIV infection and occupational chemical exposure may be associated with oxidative stress, impaired apoptotic regulation, and increased cancer susceptibility. The cross-sectional design prevented causal conclusions, and specific cancers and long-term outcomes were not assessed; longitudinal studies were recommended.

Researchers have proposed installing roughly 10 million wind-powered pumps across the Arctic to spray seawater onto sea ice, potentially adding a one-meter layer each winter. In Dougherty v. A. M. Uhrik, Inc. (No. 11410), the Third Circuit, sitting per curiam (Maris, Goodrich, and Staley, Circuit Judges), affirmed the district court's judgment. A genomic surveillance study in Connecticut from January 2022 to January 2023 combined whole-genome sequencing, epidemiological modeling, RT-qPCR viral-load measurements, and patient and vaccination metadata to examine successive Omicron lineage replacements. Sequencing covered approximately 5–10% of reported cases statewide. BA.1 emerged first and rapidly displaced Delta, followed by BA.2 in March 2022, co-circulating BA.4 and BA.5 from May through December, and XBB-based lineages late in 2022. Modeled estimates attributed about 1.5 million infections to BA.1, more than 2.1 million combined infections to BA.2, BA.4, and BA.5 within nine months, and about 0.4 million infections to XBB descendants through January 2023.

BA.1 had the fastest initial growth, rising from 5% to 50% of cases in 10 days, while later replacements took 20–59 days. Comparative reproduction-number ratios indicated that BA.1 was 78.4% more transmissible than Delta, BA.2 was 76% more transmissible than BA.1, BA.4 and BA.5 had smaller advantages over BA.2, and XBB had a 28.5% advantage over late-stage BA.5. Viral copy numbers varied over time and did not consistently explain replacement: early BA.2 had higher viral copy numbers than late BA.1, but incoming BA.4 and BA.5 had lower values than contemporaneous BA.2.

Vaccine-breakthrough analyses showed that immune escape contributed to BA.1’s emergence, with increased odds of BA.1 infection among people with at least two vaccine doses more than five months after vaccination. BA.2 showed no significant overrepresentation among breakthrough infections. BA.5 showed a nonsignificant tendency toward breakthrough infection, while XBB showed a nonsignificant tendency toward lower odds among those vaccinated more than five months earlier.

The authors proposed an SIR-based conceptual model in which lineage fitness depended on a changing combination of intrinsic transmissibility, antigenic distance, and immune escape as population immunity evolved. BA.2 combined greater transmissibility with access to Omicron-naive hosts; BA.4 and BA.5 succeeded by escaping immunity from earlier pre-Omicron and BA.1/BA.2 exposures; and XBB combined immune escape with higher transmissibility. The study concluded that integrated genomic, clinical, and epidemiological surveillance can help assess pathogen fitness and support variant monitoring, though results may not generalize to populations with different immunity, vaccination, or public-health conditions, and Ct-based viral-load estimates have methodological limitations.

Tesla introduced lower-priced Model Y and Model 3 Standard versions at $39,990 and $36,990, respectively—about $5,000 below Premium variants but still above the canceled $7,500 EV tax credit’s former impact. The models reduce costs through smaller wheels, fewer luxury features, no rear touchscreen, and less powerful powertrains; the Model Y Standard has an estimated 321-mile range versus 363 miles for the Premium. Analysts doubt the roughly 10% price cut will attract many buyers, saying an EV near $30,000 would be more compelling. Supervised Full Self-Driving remains an extra $8,000. Meanwhile, Tesla’s global sales are down 6%, and Musk is prioritizing autonomy and robotics over new affordable models.

Japan’s high life expectancy, ageing population, declining natality, and pension reforms heighten the importance of understanding subjective survival probabilities (SSP), or self-rated life expectancy. SSP differs from self-rated health, is strongly associated with mortality, and may be influenced by socioeconomic position, family longevity, life circumstances, and perceived control. However, little research has examined how employment status and working conditions relate to SSP among older adults in Japan, where long working hours and distinctive late-career employment arrangements are common.

The study examines four questions: whether SSP differs by employment status among people aged 50 and over; whether job satisfaction and working time relate to SSP among employed and self-employed people; how job satisfaction interacts with employment category; and whether demographic, socioeconomic, and health-related adjustments alter these relationships. It distinguishes employment status from the nature of work and reviews Japanese policies governing pension eligibility, mandatory retirement, reemployment, job satisfaction, working time, age discrimination, workplace support, and earnings.

The analysis uses four waves of the Japanese Study of Aging and Retirement (JSTAR), collected in 2007, 2009, 2011, and 2013 across ten cities. The full sample comprises 16,932 observations from 7,082 respondents, aged 50–75 at baseline. SSP is measured through repeated questions asking respondents the probability they will live to specified ages from 75 to 110, although responses are sparse and not normally distributed for certain age thresholds.

The lecture examines industrial organization models in which the number of firms is endogenous. In a two-stage entry model, potential entrants pay a fixed cost \(K\), then compete through Bertrand, Cournot, price competition with search, or another market game. Backward induction determines equilibrium profits for each number of firms and then the number of entrants. Pure-strategy equilibria can involve discrete entry, while mixed-strategy equilibria with many potential entrants generate expected profits equal to \(K\). Lower entry costs generally increase entry, although equilibria may remain finite when profits quickly reach zero or when all consumers optimally purchase one product. In Cournot and Hotelling examples, equilibrium firm size and the number of firms rise approximately with the square root of market size.

For homogeneous goods, the first-best outcome is one firm pricing at marginal cost, but this is generally infeasible without price regulation. The socially optimal number of firms is therefore determined by comparing consumer surplus, production costs, and fixed entry costs. Under the lecture’s assumptions, entry is generally excessive: firms internalize their own variable profits but not the business-stealing effect on incumbent firms, so private entry incentives exceed the social benefit of additional output. Bertrand can produce the limited exception of one fewer firm than the second-best benchmark. Numerical examples can show substantially more firms than socially desirable.

With heterogeneous goods, entry may be either excessive or insufficient. Entry is insufficient when an additional variety raises consumer surplus enough to outweigh losses imposed on incumbent firms. This can occur when consumers obtain better matches between products and tastes rather than benefiting only from lower prices. Nevertheless, many standard models still generate excessive entry. In a Hotelling-circle example with evenly located firms, equilibrium entry equals twice the socially optimal number because business stealing dominates, despite improved matching.

Vertical differentiation produces two cases. Under the “natural oligopoly” case, all consumers optimally want the highest-quality product, so only finitely many firms can remain viable even as fixed costs approach zero. Under the “specialization” case, different consumers optimally choose different qualities, allowing infinitely many firms as entry costs fall and prices approach marginal cost.

The lecture also reviews data from the U.S. Census of Manufacturers, including information on firm entry, exit, growth, employment, sales, plants, and equipment. Census evidence shows substantial entry and exit across narrowly defined industries. Dunne, Roberts, and Samuelson documented these patterns, and Jovanovic developed a framework in which firms learn their unknown productivity or cost types through repeated signals. Under Bayesian learning, uncertain small firms may grow rapidly if they receive favorable information but also exit more frequently. Larger, established firms have better information, higher profits, and lower costs. Industry concentration is consequently correlated with profit levels and profit dispersion because of heterogeneity in firm costs, rather than solely because competition affects markups.

Vellodi extends Jovanovic’s framework to rating intermediaries such as Amazon, Yelp, and TripAdvisor. Firms have binary quality, consumers learn from Poisson-arriving reviews, and uncertain firms may price below cost to attract customers and information. Free entry requires the expected discounted value of a new firm to equal its entry cost, while firms exit when learning makes continued operation unprofitable. A consumer-optimal platform design would partially reveal information: reviews for sufficiently high-quality firms should cease, weakening the payoff to proven high quality and encouraging new firms to invest more in becoming known as moderately high quality. The lecture concludes by previewing empirical work on entry, including Bresnahan and Reiss and more recent research.

MIT 14.13 introduces psychology and economics, or behavioral economics, as a field studying how psychological and economic factors jointly influence behavior. Drawing on psychology and related disciplines, it seeks to make economic models more realistic, predictive, and useful for policy without replacing standard economics.

The lecture reviews standard economic assumptions: stable and well-defined preferences, rational utility maximization, narrow self-interest, self-control, time discounting, risk aversion, optimal Bayesian information processing, preferences for final outcomes, and no utility from beliefs themselves. It then presents evidence that real behavior often departs from these assumptions. Examples include motivated beliefs, inconsistent preferences, context-dependent choices, limited attention and memory, reference-dependent preferences, commitment devices, imperfect belief updating, limited self-control, social preferences, peer effects, and overconfidence about multitasking.

Illustrations include the effects of opt-in versus opt-out organ-donation policies, reminders for medication adherence, charitable giving, selective-attention experiments, and individuals who avoid information because it could worsen their well-being. The discussion emphasizes that behavioral economics does not simply add every possible psychological complication. Good models should remain simple, tractable, conceptually insightful, generalizable, falsifiable, empirically consistent, and capable of good predictions. Mainstream principles such as incentives, market allocation, mathematical modeling, and empirical testing remain important. An experiment on energy use illustrates that financial incentives can have larger and more persistent effects than moral suasion.

The lecture applies these ideas to laptops in classrooms. Standard economic considerations include note-taking benefits, personal choice, and externalities. Psychological considerations include temptation, limited self-control, the cognitive effort required to resist distraction, mistaken beliefs about multitasking, and resistance to paternalistic rules. Evidence cited from a randomized trial found that allowing laptops reduced test scores by 0.18 standard deviations, prompting an opt-in laptop-section policy.

Planned topics include preferences, time and risk preferences, social preferences, emotions, depression, limited attention, belief updating, demand for information, mental accounting, preference malleability, happiness and mental health, discrimination, policy and paternalism, and poverty. Students are asked to read sections one and two of Matthew Rabin’s paper on psychology and economics.

The Government Accountability Office examined federal school-improvement activities under Title I, Part A of the Elementary and Secondary Education Act, focusing on comprehensive support and improvement (CSI) schools, their improvement plans, and Department of Education monitoring of state compliance.

In 2019–20, about 5,200 CSI schools served 2.5 million students, or 5% of all public-school students. Nearly 90% were Title I schools. Compared with other public schools, CSI schools had higher concentrations of low-income and Black students, were more often located in urban areas, had slightly higher student-teacher ratios, and had much lower math and reading proficiency rates.

GAO reviewed a nationally generalizable sample of 90 CSI plans. An estimated 42% appeared to address all three selected requirements: a school-level needs assessment, identification of resource inequities, and evidence-based interventions. Another 30% addressed two elements, while 28% addressed one or none. Estimated rates were 73% for needs assessments, 52% for resource inequities, and 86% for including an intervention. Fifty-eight percent included an intervention supported by a high-quality study reviewed by What Works Clearinghouse, while 18% included interventions shown to be ineffective. GAO did not independently determine whether plans legally complied with ESEA requirements or whether interventions met the statutory evidence-based standard.

School and district officials reported difficulty developing needs assessments, identifying resource inequities, and selecting evidence-based interventions.

Education’s routine and targeted monitoring identified compliance deficiencies, including states’ failures to ensure districts addressed resource inequities. Because monitored states and districts selected the CSI plans reviewed, GAO recommended that Education independently select those plans. Education agreed and said it would begin doing so in spring 2024.

This study examined sodium homeostasis in structural connectivity hubs and non-hub regions in drug-resistant focal epilepsy using 7T anatomical, diffusion, and sodium MRI. The analyzed cohort included 23 patients and 21 age- and sex-matched controls; SEEG classified brain regions as epileptogenic, propagation, non-involved, or unexplored, while diffusion tractography and graph metrics identified structural hubs.

Patients had higher total sodium concentration (TSC) than controls across the brain, with increases in both epileptogenic and non-epileptogenic regions. Patient TSC also correlated positively with the extent of the epileptogenic network. The sodium signal fraction, f, was increased in the epileptogenic zone but decreased in propagation, non-involved, and unexplored regions relative to corresponding controls.

Structural hubs had higher TSC than non-hubs in both patients and controls, whereas f did not differ by hub status. Epilepsy-associated increases in TSC and decreases in f occurred regardless of whether regions were hubs, contradicting the hypothesis that hubs would show a distinct epilepsy-related ionic profile. These changes were more pronounced in patients without epileptogenic-zone overlap with hubs, although the between-group difference in f was not statistically significant.

The authors concluded that elevated TSC in hubs likely reflects microstructural differences and nonspecific tissue-integrity changes rather than an epilepsy-specific hub effect. In contrast, increased f in the epileptogenic zone may indicate regional susceptibility to homeostatic failure and the generation of abnormal rhythms. Canonical hubs were rarely part of the epileptogenic network, and hub overlap showed only a nonsignificant trend toward postoperative seizure recurrence.

The coach said the team started strongly with players in the right roles before a catastrophic injury was expected to keep one player out for up to six months. The absence helped him evaluate the organization’s depth, test young players—including Hertl at center and Tierney—and identify roster needs before the trade deadline, leading to useful acquisitions. He praised the veteran group’s work ethic and DeBoer’s inclusive leadership, noting that the team moved past internal drama to focus on hockey. On special teams, he said the unit struggled to find its rhythm after long gaps between opportunities but could improve by drawing penalties and attacking more holes. He described Melker as a high-IQ, competitive and honest player who gained more offensive responsibility because of injuries. He also rejected claims that the team lacked character or leadership, praised its resilience on the road, and called DeBoer an exceptional leader who combined professionalism, work ethic and a relaxed approach.

Telltale Games confirmed an original new IP is in development but is not an immediate release, with details about its genre and story still unknown. The studio is also exploring VR, streaming services, set-top boxes and potentially Netflix as new platforms for its games, with more information planned for summer. Telltale, which has up to 400 employees, can work on four projects simultaneously and is producing more Game of Thrones, Minecraft and Guardians of the Galaxy episodes. Additional announcements are expected this summer.

Periyar University published its 2017 UG and PG examination results on its official website, where students enter their registration number and date of birth to view and save them; results are also available from their colleges. The website was slow due to heavy traffic. Within 10 days of publication, students may request re-totalling for Rs 200, revaluation for Rs 250, or an answer-sheet copy for Rs 250, with further instructions expected from the Controller of Examinations and assistance available from college principals or department heads.

A declaration condemns Japanese and foreign rebels for bringing anarchy to Korea, invokes patriotism, loyalty, filial duty, and national unity, and vows to drive them out with support from loyal gentry. A Japanese consul reports that the Tong Hâk are moving toward Seoul and advises Japanese subjects to prepare to evacuate their women and children at short notice. An open letter to Japanese merchants praises Chinese civilization and sage benevolence, condemns Japanese interference and the 1592 invasion of Korea, declares lasting enmity, and warns Japan to choose between danger and peace.

IDT Corporation held its Q4 and full fiscal year 2025 earnings call on September 29, 2025. CEO Shmuel Jonas and CFO Marcelo Fischer discussed financial and operational results for the three- and twelve-month periods ended July 31, 2025, followed by questions. Management cautioned that forward-looking statements are subject to risks and uncertainties and noted that non-GAAP measures would be reconciled with GAAP measures in the earnings release.

Britain’s first carbon-neutral new-build church, the Church of the Annunciation in Walsingham, opened in 2006. Designed by Anthony Rossi, it features solar panels and a deep-bore heating system. A planned PassivHaus church in Sheffield was shelved over funding; one exists in the US, and two Canadian projects are under construction.

Canon’s EOS 77D offers features resembling the T7i and 80D, including a 24.2-megapixel Dual Pixel CMOS sensor, 45-point autofocus and an optional beginner-focused interface, but its build quality and lack of weather sealing leave it awkwardly positioned between the two models. Low-energy Bluetooth improves Wi-Fi connectivity, and the new compact EF-S 18-55mm f/4-5.6 IS STM kit lens supports Canon’s PZ-E1 power-zoom adapter. The 77D was scheduled for April 2017 at $900 body-only, $1,050 with the new lens and $1,500 with the 18-135mm lens.

Via Browser is presented as a lightweight, fast, customizable, and stable Android browser with features comparable to full-sized alternatives. It installs from Google Play by searching for “Via Browser” by Lakor and approving Storage and Location permissions. It supports searches and direct URLs, selectable search engines, an optional pull-to-refresh gesture, Do Not Track, ad blocking, disabled location access, incognito mode, and a tab popup for quickly accessing or closing tabs. The author considers Via an excellent combination of speed, options, simplicity, and low resource use for mobile use.

At High Prairie Elementary School, students learned to use OverDrive to access e-books, and Grade 6M elected Shayla Grey as class prime minister. Grade 4W will grow vegetables and flowers; Grade 4D is working on reading sequences, simple machines and seeds; and Grade 5C is creating biographies, researching Alberta’s Famous Five and preparing to interview older relatives. Grade 5’s book sale sold out. Kindergarten students are preparing for a Christmas concert and exchanging postcards worldwide, while Grade 1 students are rehearsing and testing colour and transparency. Students also supported Remembrance Day and Christmas Shoeboxes, completed holiday anti-drunk-driving bags, and began a “Lighting Up Our School with Kindness” campaign.

The DD automatically gates off its Local bus clock when idle. A PIC edge input staying high while the clock is off prevents return to Idle; edges go unrecognized, the clock never restarts, and the system may hang. Idle requires clock on and input low.

The Supreme Court denied Google’s request to temporarily pause an injunction requiring changes to Google Play policies, citing security concerns. The order arose from Epic Games’ antitrust dispute with Google over Android app-store and in-app purchasing rules. A 2023 jury found Google’s policies unlawfully maintained an app-store monopoly, and the 9th Circuit affirmed the verdict and injunction. Developers must be allowed to use their own payment systems, while broader changes allowing more app stores are due by July 2026. Epic argued that a pause was unnecessary.

Traditional Russian sunburn remedies include sour cream, yogurt, or kefir for redness; egg whites, nettle decoction, or watermelon juice for pain; sea buckthorn oil for peeling and chafing; potatoes, carrots, and pumpkins for itching; and sauerkraut in a gauze sack for swelling. Other suggested treatments are a baking-soda-and-water bandage applied six times over three days, warm-water oatmeal used as a cream for up to two days, and a sour-cream mask with ten drops of lemon juice left on for ten minutes. Vitamin-rich fruit is suggested afterward.

Academic code violations remain high at Brown, with over half occurring in the computer science department, according to Thomas Doeppner, co-chair of the standing committee on the Academic Code. In 2015-16, 49 undergraduates and seven graduate students were charged, receiving sanctions ranging from reprimands and loss of credit to No Credit, transcript notations, suspension and dismissal. The committee is seeking to expand from five to nine faculty members due to heavy caseloads. Preventative efforts include a required online academic code tutorial, syllabi-based integrity standards, and signed collaboration policies tested in the computer science department, which uses MOSS software to detect plagiarism. Common violations include unauthorized collaboration and "furnishing" answers, which penalizes both students. International and first-year students are slightly overrepresented, and orientation was revised two years ago to address these expectations. Proposals under discussion include a student integrity panel or week and a student-based honor code, alongside the stated aim of helping students succeed.

NVIDIA Corporation’s Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended January 27, 2019 describes a GPU- and CUDA-based computing platform spanning gaming, professional visualization, data centers, and automotive markets. NVIDIA reports two segments, GPU and Tegra Processor, with brands including GeForce, Quadro, Tesla, DGX, GRID, DRIVE, Clara, SHIELD, and Jetson. The company invented the GPU in 1999, introduced CUDA in 2006, and had invested more than $17 billion in research and development.

The document details NVIDIA’s strategies of advancing GPU computing, extending its platform leadership in AI and visual computing, developing autonomous-vehicle systems, and leveraging intellectual property. Its platform supports GPU-accelerated gaming, professional design and visualization, deep learning and scientific computing, cloud graphics, and self-driving applications. NVIDIA works with server manufacturers, cloud providers, software developers, automotive companies, and other partners and reported more than 1.2 million CUDA and software-tool developers.

Manufacturing is outsourced under a fabless model, with third parties producing wafers, packaging, testing, and assembling products. NVIDIA maintains substantial inventory to support short lead times and manages demand through customer forecasts, channel partners, and manufacturing orders. Competition includes AMD, Intel, Xilinx, Broadcom, Qualcomm, Ambarella, Renesas, Samsung, and Texas Instruments, among others. NVIDIA protects its technology primarily through patents, trademarks, trade secrets, nondisclosure agreements, and licensing arrangements. As of January 27, 2019, it had 13,277 employees, including 9,486 in research and development.

Risk factors include rapidly changing markets and technology, intensifying competition, cybersecurity and data-protection incidents, product defects, reliance on third-party manufacturers and development tools, business and supply-chain disruptions, inaccurate demand forecasts, international operating and trade risks, difficulty retaining personnel, acquisition integration, intellectual-property disputes, privacy and data-protection requirements, tax liabilities, litigation and regulatory proceedings, and provisions that may impede a change in control. International sales represented 87% of revenue in fiscal years 2017–2019, and China, including Hong Kong, accounted for 24% of fiscal 2019 revenue.

NVIDIA’s headquarters are in Santa Clara, California, with owned and leased facilities there and in other U.S. and international locations; it also leases data-center space globally. Its common stock trades on the Nasdaq Global Select Market under “NVDA.” Since beginning its repurchase program in 2004, NVIDIA had repurchased 260 million shares for $7.08 billion through January 27, 2019. It then had authorization to repurchase up to $7.24 billion and intended to return $3 billion to shareholders by the end of fiscal 2020. During fiscal 2019, it repurchased 5.204 million shares in the fourth quarter and withheld approximately 4 million shares for tax obligations tied to restricted stock unit vesting.

NVIDIA reported that Mellanox Technologies and NVIDIA International Holdings received Chinese antitrust approval for NVIDIA’s proposed acquisition of Mellanox. The deal also received approval from the European Commission and Mexico, and the U.S. Hart-Scott-Rodino waiting period expired May 23, 2019. Closing was expected on or about April 27, 2020, subject to customary closing conditions.

The Executive addresses Congress on the suspension of federal authority in South Carolina, Georgia, Alabama, Mississippi, Louisiana, and Florida. Federal forts, arsenals, dockyards, customhouses, weapons, and public revenue had been seized, while forces opposed to the Union had built or strengthened fortifications and besieged remaining federal positions. Secession ordinances had been adopted in all six states, and an organization claiming to be the Confederate States sought foreign recognition and assistance.

The incoming administration initially pursued peaceful measures: retaining federal property, collecting revenue, continuing postal service, protecting residents’ rights, and relying on time, debate, and elections. After Major Anderson and Lieutenant General Scott concluded that Fort Sumter could not be timely reinforced or resupplied, the administration attempted to reinforce Fort Pickens and prepared to provision Fort Sumter without reinforcing it unless attacked. The fort was nevertheless bombarded and surrendered before the provisioning expedition arrived. The Executive characterized the attack as an aggressive act intended to force the Union’s immediate dissolution, leaving the government to resist armed rebellion with force.

Popular and state responses were uneven. Most Union states provided troops, but the seceded states generally did not, and support in the border states varied. Virginia’s convention and legislature quickly adopted secession, seized federal military facilities, accepted Confederate troops, entered an alliance with the Confederate States, and transferred the Confederate government to Richmond. The Executive also opposed proposed “armed neutrality,” arguing that it would aid secession by blocking Union forces while allowing supplies to reach insurgents.

The government called for 75,000 militia, instituted a blockade, sought volunteers and additional regular troops and sailors, and temporarily authorized the suspension of habeas corpus in limited circumstances. The Executive argued that rebellion and public safety justified the suspension, maintained that the Constitution did not specify who could exercise the power, and submitted the matter to Congress.

Although foreign governments had initially appeared to expect the Union’s destruction, the Executive reported that its sovereignty and rights were now generally respected and that foreign sympathy for the United States had increased. He recommended that Congress authorize at least 400,000 men and $400 million for the conflict.

The Executive rejected the constitutional claim that states could lawfully secede. He argued that states possessed only powers reserved by the Constitution, had never existed outside the Union, and could not claim a right to destroy the federal government or evade national obligations and debts. He questioned whether disunion commands popular support in the seceded states and described elections held under military pressure as insufficient evidence of public sentiment. He characterized the struggle as a defense of representative government and the rights of ordinary people, noting the broad public response and the loyalty of common soldiers and sailors despite resignations by many officers.

After suppressing the rebellion, the Executive pledged to follow the Constitution and laws, preserve federal government for all citizens, and protect the constitutional guarantee of republican government. He concluded by asking Congress to perform its duty and assuring loyal citizens of speedy restoration under the Constitution and laws.

Rancho Bernardo Kiwanis Club celebrated 50 years of community service at a StoneRidge Country Club dinner. Founded in 1967, the club established a nonprofit foundation with a $160,000 donation from Franklin Lenfesty. Its annual pancake breakfast typically earns $20,000. The club sponsors youth groups and Boy Scouts, supports a community tot lot, donates to Rady Children’s Hospital and Romanian transitional homes, serves meals at Ronald McDonald House, and installs holiday decorations. President John O’Rourke said it has helped over 800,000 children.

A retrospective, single-center CMR study of 15 adults with excessive left ventricular trabeculation (ET) investigated whether trabecular tissue and intertrabecular recesses affect ventricular volume and ejection fraction measurements. Threshold-based segmentation separated the compact wall, trabeculations, central cavity, and intertrabecular recesses in end-diastole and end-systole.

The intertrabecular recesses had substantially greater fractional volume change and ejection fraction than the central cavity (61±17% vs. 44±16%, P<0.001). A four-chamber analysis, expanded to 30 cases with publicly available images, showed the same pattern in area measurements. Contoured total ventricular ejection fraction correlated positively with global longitudinal shortening and mitral annular plane systolic excursion.

Including trabeculations in the blood pool, as recommended by guidelines, increased end-diastolic and end-systolic volumes and reduced measured ejection fraction. Excluding intertrabecular recesses, as in the Jacquier criterion, reduced measured volumes, stroke volume, and ejection fraction. Contouring trabeculations halved the number of patients classified with severely reduced ejection fraction and doubled the number above 50%; total ejection fraction was not significantly correlated with trabeculation extent. Theoretical calculations confirmed that trabecular amount, compliance, and labeling differences can materially alter measured ventricular volumes and ejection fraction.

Limitations included manual labeling, threshold-based separation, a small single-center sample, absence of clinical data, and the need for validation in larger prospective studies. The authors concluded that contouring trabeculations provides more accurate ventricular volume and ejection fraction assessment and may prevent inappropriate diagnosis or treatment in ET.

Lois Riess, 56, is in Texas custody awaiting transfer to Florida or Minnesota for trial on charges related to the killings of her husband, David Riess, and Pamela Hutchinson. Authorities allege that Riess shot David in their Minnesota home, forged checks to take $11,000 from his account, then targeted Hutchinson in Florida because they resembled each other, intending to steal her identity. She was arrested after a national manhunt.

Florida charges include second-degree murder, grand theft, vehicle theft and identity-related offenses; Minnesota charges include felony theft, with a second-degree murder charge reportedly pending. Florida prosecutors could seek a first-degree murder indictment, allowing them to consider the death penalty after evaluating aggravating and mitigating factors. The state that receives her first may affect prosecution strategy.

Riess also has a history of theft and gambling, including taking guardianship funds from her disabled sister and winning a $1,500 casino jackpot while a fugitive.

Netgear’s three-camera Arlo security system is reduced from £409.99 to £249.99 for 19 March. It includes smartphone/browser control, motion alerts, night vision, live feeds, waterproof battery-powered cameras, one week of free online storage, and Alexa compatibility.

In a televised address, the President reviewed U.S. progress against COVID-19 and announced a six-part plan. He said fully vaccinated Americans rose from about 2 million when he took office to over 175 million; deaths in the week of January 20 exceeded 25,000 and were down 70 percent in the following week; and job creation rose from about 50,000 to 700,000 per month. He nonetheless described the current period as difficult, citing the highly contagious Delta variant and nearly 80 million unvaccinated Americans (about a quarter of eligible adults), whom he said were overcrowding hospitals. He called COVID-19 "a pandemic of the unvaccinated," criticized elected officials undermining mitigation efforts, and stressed vaccine protection, citing roughly one hospitalization per 160,000 fully vaccinated Americans per day and one confirmed positive case per 5,000 fully vaccinated per day.

The six parts of his plan:
1. Vaccination requirements: a Department of Labor emergency rule requiring employers with 100+ employees (80+ million workers) to be fully vaccinated or show weekly negative tests; extending healthcare mandates to 17 million workers; executive orders covering federal employees and contractors; paid time off for vaccination; appeals to large venues and to physicians to contact unvaccinated patients. Together, these affect about 100 million Americans, two-thirds of workers.
2. Boosters: doses purchased and distribution ready, with eligibility and timing left to the FDA and CDC.
3. Children and schools: vaccinating children 12 and older; vaccinating households to protect children under 12 pending independent FDA review; school safety measures including testing, masking, ventilation, distancing and vaccination; requiring vaccination for roughly 300,000 Head Start educators; calling on governors to require teacher vaccination; Education Department legal action and restoring withheld pay for school officials.
4. Testing and masking: using the Defense Production Act to expand rapid test production; retailers selling at-home kits at cost; free testing at 10,000 pharmacies; $2 billion for nearly 300 million rapid tests; doubling TSA mask fines.
5. Economic recovery: expanding COVID-19 Economic Injury Disaster Loans to $2 million from $500,000, with no repayment for two years.
6. COVID-19 care: deploying nearly 1,000 federal personnel to 18 states, doubling military health teams, and increasing monoclonal antibody shipments by 50 percent after 1.4 million courses were distributed; he said these treatments reduce hospitalization risk by up to 70 percent.

He also emphasized equity in the response, noted nearly 140 million vaccine doses donated to over 90 countries plus another 500 million Pfizer doses purchased for 100 lower-income countries, and said a pandemic preparedness plan would be released next month, closing by urging Americans to get vaccinated.

The paper examines how blockchain companies create and capture value through digital business models. Blockchain is presented as a distributed, consensus-based ledger that provides immutable, transparent, and verifiable transaction records through cryptography and smart contracts, potentially reducing reliance on trusted intermediaries. The study focuses on value creation and value capture, drawing on digital business model and value configuration frameworks, because blockchain companies share a common value delivery architecture and broadly similar stakeholder roles.

An exploratory multiple-case study examines five Chinese blockchain companies selected with recommendations from the People’s Bank of China and the China Academy of Information and Communications Technology. All five use permissioned consortium blockchains without issuing tokens. Data came from 43 interviews with 31 informants, totaling 1,963 minutes, and company archives. Interview transcripts underwent thematic and cross-case analysis.

The cases produce five blockchain-inspired business models. ChainArchitect represents the platformer model, creating value through a proprietary, tree-based ledger architecture and an open platform for third-party applications while seeking to become an industry standard; its main challenge is compatibility with existing infrastructure. ChainFinance is a disintermediator, using blockchain for RMB interbank transfers to replace conventional clearing roles and reduce costs; incumbent resistance and organizational inertia impede adoption. ChainNova is a transformer, creating tailored applications such as agricultural traceability systems and attempting to transfer lessons across sectors; differences among industries limit replication. ChainSecurity is a mediator, applying blockchain to asset-backed securities to improve transaction tracking, risk assessment, pricing, and documentation; obtaining participant buy-in while addressing confidentiality and authority remains difficult. ChainDraft is a co-innovator, developing proprietary blockchain-based applications such as an electronic draft system with a bank and capturing value through licensing; low customer awareness, small-scale pilots, development costs, and limited market penetration constrain returns.

The findings show that blockchain can support value creation at ecosystem, conventional value-chain, and individual-organization levels. Its business impact may resolve incumbent inefficiencies rather than simply disrupt established models. The typology is not definitive or exhaustive because it is based on five companies in mainland China, and further research—including cases outside China and firms that differ in value delivery architecture or stakeholder networks—is needed.

After the Trump administration fired most members of the 26-member National Council on the Humanities, four remained, all Trump appointees. The council advises the NEH on grants, policy and funding. Karen Stout, a dismissed member who began serving in 2022, expressed disappointment.

Harvey Ulfers received 2 years, 9 months for wire fraud and money laundering involving at least $250,000 in Deere losses. Co-conspirator Patrick Williams received 27 months; both must pay restitution.

This cohort study (English primary care data via TPP SystmOne) extended previous estimates of COVID-19 vaccine effectiveness (VE) for BNT162b2 and ChAdOx1 beyond 26 weeks after a second dose and into the omicron era, with follow-up to the earlier of 50 weeks post-second-dose or 31 March 2022. Eligible individuals were adults ≥18 years on 1 July 2020, registered at an English practice for ≥1 year, not in a care home or medically housebound, with complete demographics and no prior SARS-CoV-2 infection. VE was estimated over 12 consecutive 4-week periods in subgroups aged 65+, 18-64 clinically vulnerable (CV), 40-64 and 18-39; both vaccines were evaluated in the 65+ and 18-64 CV subgroups, only ChAdOx1 in 40-64, and only BNT162b2 in 18-39. Unvaccinated individuals remained eligible throughout, and third doses were offered progressively from the later of September 2021 and six months after dose two, becoming available to all adults in mid-December 2021 with a three-month interval.

Eligible numbers were 1,990,562 (BNT162b2), 3,281,054 (ChAdOx1) and 1,227,170 (unvaccinated); follow-up lasted up to 50 weeks in the 65+ and 18-64 CV groups and 47 and 38 weeks in the 40-64 and 18-39 groups. Third-dose uptake reached ≥90% in the 65+, 18-64 CV and 40-64 subgroups and a maximum 73% in 18-39.

In the 65+ subgroup, HRs for non-COVID-19 death (two doses vs no vaccine) rose from 0.61 (95% CI 0.51-0.73) to 2.40 (2.02-2.85) between weeks 27-30 and 35-38, with similar trends for ChAdOx1 and the 18-64 CV and 40-64 groups, indicating selection bias from vaccination deferred after recent infection, illness or frailty. VE for COVID-19-related outcomes in these subgroups was therefore not interpreted beyond 26 weeks, and omicron's effect could not be separated from depletion of the two-dose group.

In the 18-39 group, non-COVID-19 death HRs did not change markedly during third-dose rollout. HRs for COVID-19 hospitalisation waned approximately log-linearly, from 0.04 (0.03-0.07) at weeks 3-6 to 1.48 (0.69-3.17) by weeks 35-38, with VE negligible by then. HRs for positive SARS-CoV-2 test rose from 0.25 at weeks 3-6, exceeded 1 by weeks 5-18, and reached 1.97 (1.91-2.02) at weeks 23-26, close to the HR for any test (2.16); any-test HRs stayed near 2 throughout. The authors caution this may reflect differential testing and testing-policy changes in January 2022, and found no evident omicron effect on waning in this subgroup.

They conclude that estimating long-term effectiveness of two doses is difficult where third-dose uptake is high, and recommend future studies address these factors, consider reasons eligible individuals missed further doses, and report non-COVID-19 outcomes to reveal bias. The study was approved by the Health Research Authority (22/PR/0095) and the University of Bristol Faculty of Health Sciences Ethics Committee (117269), and funded by UKRI, NIHR, Asthma UK and others.

Halimat Oniru, founder of Haleem Group, is praised as a successful Nigerian entrepreneur and role model for women. The company, headquartered in Abuja and operating in Lagos, Delta, Bayelsa, and Cross River, is described as a major road-construction business and one of West Africa’s top dredging companies, providing tens of thousands of jobs.

Amazon.com, Inc.’s unaudited Form 10-Q for the quarter ended June 30, 2021 reported Q2 net sales of $113.1 billion, up 27% from $88.9 billion, and operating income of $7.7 billion versus $5.8 billion. Net income was $7.8 billion, or $15.12 diluted EPS, compared with $5.2 billion and $10.30. For the first six months, net sales rose 35% to $221.6 billion, operating income increased to $16.6 billion from $9.8 billion, and net income doubled to $15.9 billion from $7.8 billion.

Q2 segment sales and operating income were $67.6 billion and $3.1 billion for North America, $30.7 billion and $362 million for International, and $14.8 billion and $4.2 billion for AWS. Management attributed sales growth primarily to higher unit sales, including third-party seller sales, advertising, and increased AWS usage, while fulfillment, shipping, technology infrastructure, payroll, and other costs also increased.

Operating cash flow was $12.7 billion for Q2 and $16.9 billion for the first six months, below prior-year periods, as property and equipment purchases reached $14.3 billion and $26.4 billion, respectively. Amazon ended June with $40.7 billion of cash, cash equivalents, and restricted cash; total assets were $360.3 billion and stockholders’ equity was $114.8 billion. Trailing-twelve-month free cash flow was $12.1 billion, compared with $31.9 billion a year earlier.

The company issued $18.5 billion of senior notes in May 2021 and reported $50.7 billion of unsecured senior notes outstanding at June 30. It had $255.6 billion of contractual commitments and agreed to acquire MGM Holdings for approximately $8.5 billion, to be funded with cash on hand. Q2 included approximately $1.5 billion of COVID-19-related costs; management expected sales growth to decelerate in Q3 and pandemic-related costs and supply constraints to continue into part of the quarter.

Disclosures also covered a €746 million Luxembourg data-protection fine, which Amazon disputed, numerous antitrust and consumer-protection cases, approximately $2.8 billion of tax contingencies, operating and finance leases, marketable securities, stock-based compensation, and unearned revenue.

The passage describes a ClimaCell patent application covering systems, software, and methods for collecting and processing weather data to determine current conditions and rapidly forecast precipitation, atmospheric water vapor, liquid water content, fog, and visibility. It identifies related continuation patents and applications, all incorporated by reference, and includes a 2018 ClimaCell copyright notice.

The background explains that fog can disrupt aviation, road transportation, and shipping by reducing visibility. Existing fog-detection methods depend largely on direct observation and instruments, limiting their geographic reach. Microwave-attenuation methods can also mistake attenuation caused by rain, dense atmospheric water, or other hydrometeors for fog. Prior systems do not effectively support satellite microwave links, integrate real-time fog inference with machine-learning prediction, or process high-frequency sensor readings at the scale and speed required for rapidly changing weather. Existing forecasting is further limited by computational load, data latency, reliance on fixed or inaccurate sources, and reliance on hindcast methods.

The disclosed technology uses asynchronous, parallel processing to shorten cadence intervals to as little as one minute. It preprocesses weather and non-weather data—including terrestrial and satellite microwave attenuation, vehicle sensor reports, radar, numerical weather prediction data, and other sources—into precipitation, water-vapor, liquid-water-content, and fog estimates. The document states that combining processed measurements can improve forecast accuracy by 30–70% and forecast speed by up to 50%.

An illustrative architecture contains four logical components: an information collection and normalization server; an offline/background processing server; a modeling and prediction server; and an information distribution and alerting server. The first asynchronously gathers, cleans, filters, normalizes, and tags data. The second develops filters, transforms, machine-learning models, predictive models, and fog-inference rules and performs non-time-critical processing. The third manages cadence cycles and runs parallel forecast calculations, blending, weather inference, precipitation forecasting, fog forecasting, and runway visual range calculations. The fourth combines forecasts with maps and templates to produce maps, reports, alerts, dashboards, and API or web-interface outputs tailored to requested locations, forecast types, and time periods.

A system database stores radar, weather-sensor, microwave-link, NWP, precipitation, storm, wind, CAPE, fog, RVR, map, location, forecast-skill, and related data. Cadence instances act as control records for repeating processing cycles. Their data is organized into sparse tile layers and tile stacks for collection, forecasting, and post-processing. Cadence instances can reuse prior data, reference unchanged tile layers, compare duplicate structures, and later update forecasts as new observations arrive. Short cadences support near-real-time forecasting, while longer cadences support multi-day forecasts.

Processing proceeds through collection, collection post-processing, forecast preprocessing, iterative forecast generation, and post-forecast processing. Forecast outputs include precipitation, wind, CAPE, fog, accumulated precipitation, and RVR. A cadence manager determines whether to recalculate an entire instance or incrementally update only changed and dependent tiles. It compares current observations with prior forecasts using thresholds and confidence measures, propagates verified or changed data through dependent tile layers, and selectively recalculates specialty forecasts such as fog and RVR when inputs change. The passage concludes with an example of propagating collected data from one cadence instance and merging it with a previous forecast to create new forecast tile layers.

Two Oceans Restaurant in Table Mountain National Park has stopped selling West Coast Rock Lobster after SASSI red-listed the unsustainable species, with less than 2% remaining. SANParks TMNP supports SASSI’s sustainable seafood initiative.

The MSPM0G3519, MSPM0G3518, MSPM0G1519, and MSPM0G1518 devices include an independent watchdog timer with eight periods from 2 ms to 2 hours that triggers a POR reset if not serviced, and a windowed watchdog timer that can generate a reset or interrupt, stop during sleep, or operate as an interval timer. TIMGx general-purpose timers are software-compatible subsets of TIMAx advanced timers. TIMGx supports multiple counting modes, prescaling, repeat-reload operation, QEI and Hall-sensor inputs on selected instances, synchronization, cross-triggering, and interrupt/DMA or ADC trigger generation. TIMAx adds complementary PWM outputs with programmable dead bands, configurable fault handling, repeat counters, and additional capture/compare channels.

DAC_OUT connects to PA15, which should not carry external signals while DAC output is enabled. IOMUX selects digital IO functions and controls output drivers, input paths, and shutdown wake-up logic. The devices provide a two-wire ARM-compatible SWD interface. A UART- or I2C-compatible boot strap loader supports configuration and memory programming, is protected by a 256-bit user-defined password, can be disabled, and is enabled by default. It can be invoked through BSL_invoke, on blank devices with unprogrammed reset vector and stack pointer, or by application software.

A memory-mapped FACTORY region provides read-only capability descriptions, factory trim data, hardware revision information, and device identifiers. Typical implementation guidance includes using 10 µF and 0.1 µF VDD/VSS decoupling capacitors, a 47 kΩ NRST pullup with a 10 nF pulldown, an optional 100 kΩ SYSOSC FCL resistor, and a 0.47 µF VCORE capacitor. Open-drain I/O requires an external pullup.

TI documents development tools, MSP/X device nomenclature, documentation support, ESD precautions, revision changes, mechanical and packaging data, orderable information, and resource and liability disclaimers.

Linda Ronstadt, diagnosed with Parkinson’s disease in 2013, described the daily challenges of speaking, traveling and performing basic tasks while continuing to exercise and selectively maintain her public life. Her “A Conversation With Linda” events combine archival photos, videos and music from her career with an audience question-and-answer session.

Ronstadt’s 1977 album *Simple Dreams* earned a 40th-anniversary expanded edition featuring three live 1980 recordings. The album spent five weeks at No. 1, became her fifth consecutive million-selling platinum album, and sold more than 3.5 million copies in its first year—a record for a female artist. Its hits included “Blue Bayou,” “It’s So Easy” and “Poor Poor Pitiful Me,” while “I Never Will Marry,” recorded with Dolly Parton, became a Top 10 country hit. The album won the Grammy for Best Recording Package, and Ronstadt was inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame in 2014.

The application describes blockchain-based digital certificate management methods, apparatuses, and systems to reduce risks from hacked or malicious certificate authorities. A certificate authority issues a digital certificate and requests that it be written to the blockchain, but the certificate remains invalid until blockchain nodes perform consensus verification and approve or reject the request using defined criteria, thresholds, or proportions. The blockchain likewise consensus-verifies certificate revocation lists, revocation records, and updates, while nodes construct and maintain local revocation lists to check transaction participants’ certificates under predetermined rules. Corresponding method, processor, apparatus, storage-medium, and system implementations are disclosed. By decentralizing certificate storage, chaining, and revocation-list maintenance while limiting the certificate authority’s role, the disclosed system aims to reduce verification costs, improve transaction efficiency, and protect blockchain security when the authority is faulty or malicious.

Kyle Busch won the Overton’s 400 for Joe Gibbs Racing in a Toyota, overcoming a car that initially handled too tightly and later became too loose. Aric Almirola won Stage 1, while Kevin Harvick won Stage 2. Busch started 16th, finished the first two stages in 12th and 11th, and entered the final stage in 10th.

After a caution for teammate Denny Hamlin, Busch’s crew delivered a fast pit stop, moving him from ninth to sixth. He quickly advanced into the top five and reached second by lap 193. Another fast stop for four tires and fuel on lap 207 gave him the lead on lap 210. Busch held off Kyle Larson on the final lap to win by 1.162 seconds after leading 59 laps.

The victory was Busch’s 48th Monster Energy NASCAR Cup Series win in 479 races, fifth of the season, and second at Chicago. He now has 190 career victories across NASCAR’s top three divisions. Busch credited his crew’s persistence, pit stops, and track position with the victory. The next Cup Series race is the Coke Zero Sugar 400 at Daytona International Speedway on July 7.

This medRxiv preprint reports a prospective psychometric validation of the 17-item COVID-19 Yorkshire Rehabilitation Scale–Modified (C19-YRSm), a patient-reported measure of Long Covid symptoms, functional disability, and overall health. Data came from the UK LOCOMOTION study across 10 Long Covid services. Of 1,314 patients completing the C19-YRSm at least once, 263 repeated it after about 30 days; 193 completed FACIT-Fatigue and 98 completed both C19-YRSm and EQ-5D-5L at both time points.

The C19-YRSm showed good item and scale characteristics, low missingness, strong internal and test-retest reliability, and expected convergent correlations with FACIT-Fatigue. Symptom Severity and Functional Disability scores were strongly associated, while Overall Health correlated inversely with poorer outcomes. Scores also distinguished patients by symptom burden and by previous COVID-19 hospitalisation or ICU admission. All three subscales detected change over 30 days, with standardized response sizes of 0.22–0.50, compared with 0.14 for the EQ-5D-5L Index and 0.18 for its visual analogue scale.

Initial minimally important differences were two points for Symptom Severity and Functional Disability and one point for Overall Health; clinically important differences based on the standard error of measurement were four points for Symptom Severity and Functional Disability. Confirmatory factor analysis provided some support for separate Symptom Severity and Functional Disability factors, although fit statistics did not individually meet all predefined thresholds.

The authors conclude that the C19-YRSm is a valid, reliable, responsive, brief, and easy-to-administer condition-specific measure that can capture Long Covid trajectories and intervention effects and may inform clinical practice, policy, and trial design. The importance thresholds require confirmation through anchor-based methods, and further psychometric research is needed.

President Donald Trump said Monday’s underground explosion in Manhattan highlighted the need for Congress to enact immigration reforms, including ending “chain migration” and strengthening security. Police identified the suspect as Akayed Ullah, a 27-year-old permanent resident of Bangladeshi descent who entered the U.S. on an F43 family immigrant visa in 2011; DHS said he benefited from family chain migration. Trump urged Congress to increase ICE staffing, expand immigration officers’ arrest and detention powers, address fraud and abuse, and impose the strongest penalties for terrorism, including death where appropriate. He had similarly focused on immigration after the Halloween attack in Tribeca. Separately, a federal appeals court heard arguments over whether children can sue Trump’s administration over its environmental policy.

The TPS7H500x-SP push-pull converter design targets a maximum duty cycle of 35%, providing margin below the controller’s 50% limit for efficiency and load-transient effects. The transformer turns ratio is 2.5. Magnetizing current is targeted at 6% of output current, yielding a calculated primary inductance of 33 μH; 40 μH is used in the actual design. Primary GaN FETs are rated at 170 V for a 36-V maximum input to accommodate voltage doubling and transients. Secondary synchronous-rectifier GaN FETs are rated at 80 V for an expected maximum stress of approximately 20 V; an optional parallel Schottky diode can reduce soft-start current and reverse-conduction losses. An RCD clamp limits switch-node voltage, with initial resistor and capacitor values determined from allowable overshoot, leakage inductance, and peak primary current before testing-based optimization.

A 40% output-current ripple target results in selection of a 0.47-μH output inductor. Output-capacitance calculations for load transients and voltage ripple require at least 1.3 mF. Approximately 2.3 mF is used to provide additional single-event-transient mitigation, implemented with seven 330-μF polymer tantalum capacitors. An optional LC output filter can further reduce ripple, with a resistor available for damping high-frequency peaking.

Cycle-by-cycle current limiting begins at approximately 35 A, about 45% above the 24.25-A peak inductor current at maximum load. Primary current is sensed through a 1:100 current-sense transformer, and a 7.5-Ω RCS resistor is selected. The hiccup capacitor is 3.3 nF. Type 2A frequency compensation uses a 10-kHz crossover and a calculated power-stage transconductance of 16.2 A/V; RCOMP, CCOMP, and CHF are set to 40.2 kΩ, 15 nF, and 47 pF, respectively, with final tuning expected during testing. A 102-kΩ resistor from RSC to AVSS provides slope compensation matched to the output-inductor falling slope.

The controllers require a regulated 4-V to 14-V input supply and at least a 0.1-μF bypass capacitor from VIN to AVSS. X5R-or-better ceramic capacitors should be placed close to the controller with low-impedance paths to AVSS; bulk input capacitance is recommended when the supply is remote.

Layout guidance includes routing feedback away from magnetics and switch nodes, minimizing switch-node copper and high-d/dt/dv/dt loops, connecting analog and power grounds at one point, using short, wide high-current traces of at least 15 mils per ampere, placing filtering, bypass, compensation, and VSENSE components close to their associated pins, separating high-dv/dt gate-drive traces from sensitive signals, filtering CS_ILIM where necessary, isolating SYNC from sensitive circuitry, and connecting CFP backside metallization to AVSS through multiple vias. Application curves cover 10-A output soft-start and a 5-A load step. The document also lists related evaluation-module and radiation reports, update-notification and support resources, ESD handling cautions, revision details, and mechanical, packaging, and orderable information.

The Department of Transport warned that commercial State companies believe government-set 2011 salary rates are too low to attract suitable CEOs or retain senior staff. Edmonton police seized a record $3.2 million in carfentanil after firefighters found suspicious powders in a vacant southwest basement suite during a Jan. 28 fire call. Testing confirmed carfentanil in blue and pink powders, while white powder was believed to be caffeine used as a cutting agent. Police said the drug was likely intended for street-level distribution and the black market.
