NVIDIA Corporation’s Form 10-K covers the fiscal year ended January 31, 2016, a 53-week year. The company describes itself as a visual-computing platform company that evolved from a PC graphics-chip manufacturer and targets four markets: Gaming, Professional Visualization, Datacenter, and Automotive. Its two reportable segments, GPU and Tegra Processor, share a common architecture and combine hardware, system software, algorithms, systems, and services.

GPU brands include GeForce for gaming, Quadro for professional design, Tesla for deep learning and accelerated computing, and GRID for cloud visualization. Tegra processors support the DRIVE automotive platform and SHIELD devices and are also sold to OEMs. Other technologies include CUDA, virtualized GPUs, Iray, DesignWorks, DIGITS, DRIVE PX, and GameWorks. GeForce Experience had more than 70 million downloads. NVIDIA reported $12 billion invested in research and development since inception and approximately 7,300 patent assets.

Sales and marketing focus on OEMs, ODMs, system builders, motherboard and add-in-board manufacturers, distributors, retailers, and software developers. ASUSTeK represented 11% of fiscal 2016 revenue. Most sales are made under standard purchase orders, and only a small, insignificant portion of backlog is noncancelable. Revenue is primarily consumer-focused and has historically been stronger in the second half of the fiscal year.

NVIDIA uses a fabless manufacturing model. Foundries including TSMC and Samsung manufacture wafers, while independent subcontractors perform assembly, testing, and packaging. The company manages inventories through demand forecasts and maintains substantial semi-finished inventories because of short semiconductor lead times. Cash and marketable securities rose 9% to $5.04 billion at fiscal year-end, and management said available balances and operating cash flows should meet operating, acquisition, capital-expenditure, and shareholder-return needs for at least 12 months.

As of January 31, 2016, NVIDIA had 9,227 employees, including 6,566 in research and development. R&D expense was $1.33 billion in fiscal 2016, $1.36 billion in 2015, and $1.34 billion in 2014. The company faces intense competition from GPU and system-on-chip suppliers, including AMD and Intel, and graphics-technology licensors. It protects its intellectual property through patents, trademarks, trade secrets, nondisclosure agreements, and licenses; issued patents expire between April 2016 and December 2034.

Fiscal 2016 revenue was $5.010 billion, compared with $4.682 billion in 2015. Operating income was $747 million, net income was $614 million, and diluted earnings per share were $1.08. Cash and marketable securities totaled $5.037 billion, total assets were $7.370 billion, and shareholders’ equity was $4.469 billion. Fiscal 2016 results included $131 million of restructuring and other operating charges and $86 million of after-tax restructuring charges related to winding down or selling the Icera modem business.

Principal risks include intensifying competition, declining Intel licensing revenue, manufacturing-yield problems, product defects and recalls, cybersecurity breaches, dependence on third-party foundries and subcontractors, failure to secure design wins, natural disasters and geographic concentration, customer concentration, demand-forecasting errors, margin pressure, international operations, acquisition integration, intellectual-property disputes, privacy concerns, headquarters construction financing, indebtedness, and anti-takeover provisions. Revenue from customers outside the United States and Other Americas represented 79% of fiscal 2016 revenue. NVIDIA also had $1.5 billion of 1% convertible senior notes due 2018, with possible shareholder dilution from associated warrants.

NVDA common stock trades on the NASDAQ Global Select Market. The quarterly dividend was increased to $0.115 per share in November 2015, equivalent to $0.46 annually, and NVIDIA paid $213 million in cash dividends in fiscal 2016. It had repurchased 231 million shares for $3.85 billion and retained authorization to repurchase $1.47 billion through December 2018, intending to return approximately $1 billion to shareholders in fiscal 2017 through repurchases and dividends. An indexed $100 investment in NVIDIA stock ended at $127.99 over five years and $197.25 over ten years, versus $167.81 and $187.41 for the S&P 500 and $139.35 and $129.50 for the S&P Semiconductors Index.

Dwight Eisenhower, addressing the Republican National Convention on its hundredth anniversary, accepts the party's nomination for the Presidency for a second time. He thanks the delegates, alternates, and guests for their welcome and for retaining the team chosen in 1952, and briefly endorses Richard Nixon's dedication and ability. Invoking Abraham Lincoln's two-sentence reply upon his 1860 nomination, Eisenhower says the dominant question before the convention is the future, arguing that the Republican Party is "the Party of the Future" because its policies are designed to stand the test of tomorrow. His victory prediction in November rests, he says, on the assumption that Republicans, independents, and like-minded Democrats will register and vote everywhere, noting that registration is running far below previous years and urging all organizations, including Youth for Eisenhower, to help.

He gives five reasons for the party's claim to be the Party of the Future. First, it stands on long-range principle rather than short-term expediency, illustrated by the farm program (Soil Bank, Great Plains program, restoring farm prices and income), adherence to free collective bargaining without government interference (credited for a complete steel contract and a period of labor peace), and resistance to concentrating power in Washington in favor of building up state activities, finances, and prestige. Second, the party concentrates on present and future issues rather than depression-era debates: water supply, highways, health, housing, power development, peaceful uses of atomic energy, urban organization and redevelopment, and first-class education for a growing school-age population. Third, it draws people together rather than pitting groups against each other, embracing the motto "E pluribus unum" and appealing to working people, small farmers, small businessmen, minority groups, and reformers of many kinds. Fourth, it accomplishes needed work by enlisting free, creative individuals and private organizations, citing progress on equal justice and opportunity, the elimination of discrimination in the armed services, the District of Columbia, and among government contractors, a 14-point program for small businessmen, and remaining needs of older citizens, migrant farm laborers, handicapped workers, American Indians, low-income farmers, and women. Fifth, the party must be dedicated to peace, for without peace there is no future.

Eisenhower states three imperatives of peace: maintaining national moral, economic, and military strength; collective security built on helping free nations realize their own political, economic, and military potentialities through voluntary association rather than monolithic power; and, without relaxing defenses, bridging the chasm separating Americans from peoples under communist rule, using growing exchanges of ideas, books, students, tourists, artists, radio programs, and officials to replace mistrust with understanding. He also cites the Atoms for Peace Plan, agreements with more than thirty nations for research reactors and seven for power reactors, and twenty thousand kilograms of nuclear fuel set aside for foreign programs, alongside continued disarmament efforts.

Concluding that this future will be achieved not by revolution but by the combined efforts of 168 million free Americans and friends abroad, he echoes Lincoln's hope that a divided house will "cease to be divided," invokes faith over anxiety as the handle on tomorrow, and accepts the nomination "humbly but confidently."

The paper examines Bell’s statistical independence assumption (SI), arguing that it is best understood through relative frequencies: an apparently random sample should have approximately the same distribution of states as the population from which it was drawn. On this interpretation, violating SI means that random selection systematically fails to produce representative samples, regardless of whether nature is deterministic.

Bell’s theorem establishes nonlocality only if SI and other assumptions hold. Superdeterministic theories reject SI instead of local causality, allowing Bell experiments to be explained by local models. Although superdeterminism is commonly restricted to deterministic theories with fine-tuned initial conditions, the paper argues that this restriction is unnecessary and identifies three forms: deterministic theories with fine-tuned initial conditions, statistical flukes in deterministic or indeterministic theories, and nomic exclusion in either kind of theory.

The paper reviews Leibnizian Quantum Mechanics, which reproduces quantum predictions using infinitely many internal Bohmian universes with homogeneous, atypical initial conditions. Although its initial conditions are not highly complex, the authors question whether its statistical-independence violation can be explained under the frequency interpretation.

Statistical-fluke theories use improbable distributions of events rather than special initial conditions. Examples include repeated heads in fair-coin experiments, a million consecutive observations of quantum entanglement correlations, and observers inhabiting atypical Everett branches. In each case, observed results fail to represent the distribution stipulated by the theory.

Nomic exclusion models make combinations of measurement settings and ontic states physically impossible, preventing experiments from revealing local hidden-variable assignments inconsistent with quantum predictions. Toy “goblin” models illustrate three causal structures: hidden variables influencing goblins that influence settings; goblins independently determining hidden variables and settings; or settings influencing goblins that determine hidden variables. Such mechanisms need neither fine-tuned initial conditions nor statistical flukes. Existing models by Donadi and Hossenfelder, Hance and Hossenfelder, Hance, and Ciepielewski, Okon, and Sudarsky are discussed as variants of this category.

The authors also argue that properly understood retrocausal theories need not violate SI. Under a causal-order interpretation, ontic states differ from those in the standard temporal-order interpretation, so apparent violations can disappear. A local retrocausal Zig-Zag model is presented, while invariant set theories are likewise argued not necessarily to be superdeterministic.

Finally, the paper outlines philosophical implications: some compatibilist accounts of free will would make superdeterminism restrictive of freedom; superdeterministic theories have a conspiratorial element; and while they need not undermine the scientific method, the authors characterize superdeterminism as pre-scientific rather than itself scientific.

Regina father Marshall Pelletier posted a photo of his infant son, splashed with road slush by a car hitting a puddle while his wife pulled the child in a sled on the sidewalk. Regina and Saskatoon bylaws prohibit splashing pedestrians, but police say the offence is difficult to pursue without driver, vehicle and licence plate details. Will Ma explains independent chip mode (ICM), which assigns nonlinear monetary value to tournament chips because players want to survive and reach escalating payouts. Maximizing chip EV remains a useful approximation of maximizing expected money, but ICM creates important differences near the payout bubble and final table. ICM is a tournament-risk adjustment, not a mandate to avoid all positive-EV gambling. Professional players who frequently reach bubble situations may prefer smaller tournaments, while recreational players may reasonably prioritize cashing.

Basic ICM assumes a player’s chance of winning is proportional to their share of total chips, though it may omit positional advantages. In an example with three players, payouts and stacks of 5, 3, and 2, the smallest-stack player has a 20% chance to win, roughly a 29% chance to finish second, and an equity of 2.89 rather than 2. The calculation becomes recursive with more players and is normally performed with an ICM calculator. ICM does not apply in cash games, winner-take-all tournaments, or heads-up play. It is most relevant where payouts rise sharply, particularly on the bubble and final table. Large stacks generally have lower money EV than chip EV, while small stacks have higher money EV and often positive chip EV.

Ma then plays through a tournament’s final table while applying these concepts. As the second-largest stack, he wants to avoid large confrontations with the chip leader and benefits when shorter stacks bust. He explains that extreme shoves can be justified by ICM, that calls to shoves should be tightened at the final table, and that a large stack can shove more aggressively because opponents are highly motivated to fold. As eliminations change the stacks and payouts, he continually recalculates which risks are acceptable.

One hand illustrates the calculation. Ma bluffs with jack-ten offsuit and faces an all-in. Chip EV requires about 33% equity to call, but ICM raises the threshold to approximately 39.6%; estimated equity against plausible ranges is only about 34–37%. He therefore folds, though he later questions whether the initial bluff was wise.

With three players remaining, Ma again uses ICM to justify broad shoving and selective folding. When one player has only one big blind, extreme ICM pressure makes any two cards a strong shove. That player eventually calls with ace-queen and doubles, and Ma discusses how players might collude to eliminate the short stack, although selfish incentives undermine such cooperation.

In heads-up play, ICM no longer matters. Ma notes that the small blind has position, demonstrates preflop adjustments, and discusses exploiting opponents who either fold excessively or aggressively reraise. His opponent mounts a comeback, but Ma ultimately wins after calling with pocket sixes and making a straight. He cautions that the selected tournament contains selection bias because it was chosen for successful outcomes. The lecture concludes by previewing the final theory class, deeper cash-game strategy, and a guest lecture from Bill Chen.

The World Bank raised China’s 2025 GDP growth forecast to 4.8% from 4.5%, citing government stimulus, stronger exports, increased domestic investment, infrastructure spending and improving consumer sentiment. It expects growth to slow in 2026 due to fiscal constraints, global trade uncertainty and weaker demand. Local government debt, demographic pressures, declining productivity, property weakness and subdued private consumption remain structural risks. The Bank anticipates a gradual shift toward consumption-driven growth supported by green industries and digital innovation, alongside productivity and services-sector reforms.

Researchers led by the University of South Florida’s Dr. Davide Tanasi chemically analyzed organic residue in pottery found at the Early Bronze Age site of Castelluccio in Sicily. The fragments formed a 3.5-foot storage container found with a terracotta plate and pottery cooking equipment. Nuclear Magnetic Resonance, Gas Chromatography and Mass Spectrometry identified oleic and linoleic acids, confirming the residue as olive oil. Dated to the late 3rd or early 2nd century BC, it is the oldest olive oil recovered in Italy and provides evidence that systematic olive-oil production began at least 700 years earlier than previously thought. The study appeared in Analytical Methods.

Jim Cramer reversed his positive view of Snap after its controversial app redesign, saying the stock remains too risky and overpriced but could become attractive at a lower price. He cited concerns that redesign backlash and celebrity complaints could reduce user engagement and drive advertisers away.

The running back is a key offensive football position primarily responsible for taking handoffs, gaining positive yardage, and protecting the ball. Running backs must also pass block and catch passes, making versatility especially valuable. The position is sometimes called tailback or halfback because players line up behind the offensive line. Elite running backs generally combine an athletic build with speed, agility, vision, toughness, strength, and receiving ability. Teams may use short-yardage backs to gain tough yards and all-purpose backs as receiving threats. The passage profiles Barry Sanders, Emmitt Smith, Walter Payton, Jim Brown, and Ladanian Tomlinson, highlighting their notable rushing, receiving, scoring, and MVP achievements. Breaking tackles, evading defenders, and turning negative plays into big gains separate successful running backs, making a reliable player who can run, block, and catch a major asset to any offense.

During puberty, children's self-concept is still forming, peers gain influence over parents, and normal physical and emotional changes can leave them insecure or isolated, sometimes triggering depression. Parents should listen supportively without judgment, continue offering positive reassurance, and seek professional help—such as from a school counselor—when signs of depression appear.

Unwanted holiday gifts can be sold or traded online. Kijiji reports Canadians averaged $1,037 from second-hand goods; collectibles suit eBay or auctions, low-value household goods garage sales, and heavy items Kijiji because buyers can collect them. Kijiji searches favor electronics, while Bunz enables noncash trades for clothing, perfume, makeup, furniture and decor.

Sellers should use clear, well-lit, multi-angle photos, condition labels such as BNIB, BNWT and EUC, and engaging descriptions. Prices can be benchmarked against eBay sold listings, adjusted for condition and declining value. Kijiji searches rise about 10% in January, with Jan. 8 most popular and Sundays leading; furniture and decor sell well in August and September.

Gift cards sell on Bunz, Kijiji and Craigslist, or can be exchanged through businesses such as CardSwap for less than face value. Regifting is appropriate only when an item is brand new, originally packaged and desired by the recipient; handmade, personalized or carefully selected gifts should not be regifted.

David Luiz is holidaying in Dubai, where he flyboarded and posed by the Burj Khalifa. After an injury-hit season, the Brazilian lost his place at Chelsea and was dropped by Brazil; Chelsea finished fifth but won the FA Cup.

Antonio Conte says the media applies greater pressure to him after defeats than to rival Premier League managers. His first Chelsea season ended with the league title and an FA Cup final appearance, but this campaign has been difficult, prompting exit rumours despite his desire to stay for at least the remaining 18 months of his contract. Chelsea are 18 points behind Manchester City and seek a top-four finish. Conte contrasted his scrutiny with that faced by Pep Guardiola, Jose Mourinho, Jurgen Klopp, Mauricio Pochettino and Arsene Wenger, arguing that critics overlook Chelsea’s title win as underdogs.

The paper addresses PDE-constrained inverse problems on irregular or complex geometries, where unknown physical fields must be reconstructed from sparse, noisy observations and classical PDE-constrained optimization is computationally costly. Although neural operator learning and diffusion models have shown promise in scientific computing, most related methods assume regular grids, while irregular-geometry research has focused mainly on forward tasks.

The authors introduce GeoFunFlow, a geometry-aware diffusion framework combining operator learning and generative modeling. Its geometric function autoencoder (GeoFAE), built around a Perceiver module, handles unstructured meshes of varying sizes and supports continuous reconstruction of solution fields. GeoFAE is coupled with a latent diffusion model for posterior sampling conditioned on sparse, noisy sensor data. The framework uses conditional rectified flow, learning a velocity field integrated as a deterministic ODE from noise to data, enabling posterior generation without explicit likelihood evaluation or MCMC. Given well-trained models, theoretical guarantees are provided for accurate posterior approximations. The authors report state-of-the-art accuracy and efficient inference on complex-geometry benchmarks.

Formally, conditioning combines the geometry \(\Omega\), sensor locations \(X\), and noisy measurements \(y=S_{\Omega,X}[u]+\epsilon\), with the goal of learning posterior distributions over unknown fields \(u\).

NASA launched Voyagers 1 and 2 in 1977 to study Jupiter and Saturn; both remain functional after more than 40 years. Voyager 2 used a planetary alignment occurring every 176 years to fly by Uranus and Neptune, making it the only spacecraft to fly by all four giant planets. The probes carry Golden Records about Earth and humanity. Voyager 1 entered interstellar space in 2012, and both continue outward.

Researchers from Karolinska Institutet and Finnish collaborators developed the CORE model to predict a person’s 10-year risk of severe liver disease using age, sex, and three routine liver enzyme tests (AST, ALT and GGT). The model uses data from more than 480,000 Stockholm health-check participants followed for up to 30 years and correctly distinguished those who developed severe liver disease in 88% of cases, outperforming the FIB-4 method. It also showed high accuracy in population groups in Finland and the UK. A web-based calculator is available for primary-care clinicians, and the model may enable earlier detection of cirrhosis and liver cancer. Researchers said further testing is needed in high-risk groups, including people with type 2 diabetes or obesity, and integration with medical-record systems is required.

The Option Investor Newsletter reported gains for the Dow and a record close for the Nasdaq, led by Internet and technology stocks. @Home agreed to acquire XCIT for $7 billion, while rumors of a major Compaq Internet purchase added to sector enthusiasm. Microsoft and QCOM exceeded earnings estimates, and several technology stocks rallied. However, the put/call ratio was 0.42, and gains in T, IBM and GM accounted for more than 60 Dow points, indicating weak broader market internals. Futures rose ahead of President Clinton’s State of the Union address, which was expected to include support for investing Social Security funds in retirement accounts, and Alan Greenspan’s testimony.

Market posture became bullish for the Nasdaq-100, hardware and software, while most broad indexes and sectors remained neutral and oil and gas was bearish. Pinnacle Capital reported excessive bullish sentiment—60% bullish versus 30% bearish—while noting bearish short-term indicators and advising subscribers to protect long positions.

The newsletter reviewed numerous call and put picks, citing earnings, possible stock splits, technical levels and company developments. It dropped XCIT and BMCS put plays. Ford was listed under new call plays, with February and March call spreads, while no new conventional put plays were offered. Four speculative debit-spread plays were proposed in PTEK, OMPT, SCUR and RHD. Portfolio updates covered exits from ATI, LU, FTL and LUV positions and adjustments to OXHP and WCOM. The publication included subscription information and a disclaimer stating that its content was educational, was not an offer or recommendation, and should not replace advice from a qualified professional.
Chicago hotels must provide panic buttons that alert supervisors and HR to workers’ locations; a survey found 58% experienced guest sexual harassment.

The case examines DeBeers’s response to growing competition from laboratory-grown diamonds. In 2007, Lee Mandell considers buying his fiancée an engagement diamond after reading about synthetic diamonds and viewing *Blood Diamond*. Although chemically identical to mined diamonds and producible flawlessly within days, synthetics cost 15–40% less, avoid mining-related environmental damage and the possibility of purchasing conflict diamonds, and appeal to consumers concerned about diamond provenance. A jeweler nevertheless rejects the idea of giving a girlfriend a synthetic diamond, emphasizing the age, rarity and romance of natural stones.

The global diamond industry produced an estimated $13 billion in rough stones and $62 billion in jewelry annually in 2005–2006. Production and value increased between 2000 and 2005. Seven countries accounted for most output, while India dominated low-cost cutting and polishing and was processing more than half the world’s diamonds by value. Industry integration was increasing as mining companies entered retail and retailers invested in mines. Southern African governments sought greater participation in cutting, polishing and marketing to retain more value from their resources. The United States represented 46% of demand, followed by the Middle East and Japan, while India and China were the fastest-growing markets.

DeBeers had historically controlled the industry by producing 45% of global rough supply and selling 80%, determining buyers, quantities and prices. Its dominance weakened after the Soviet Union’s collapse, Russia’s emergence through Alrosa, Argyle’s withdrawal in Australia and the development of Canadian production. DeBeers bought excess supply to support prices, causing its stockpile and market-control costs to rise. Antitrust enforcement, price-fixing charges and publicity surrounding its purchase of conflict diamonds also damaged the company.

In 1998, DeBeers abandoned its role as buyer of last resort and shifted toward a demand-driven, brand-focused strategy. It stopped stockpiling and purchasing on the open market, sold only stones from its own operations, promised conflict-free supply, reduced and reorganized its sightholder network, and introduced the Supplier of Choice program. The Forevermark program guaranteed that participating natural diamonds were natural, ethically traded and untreated. DeBeers launched branding and advertising campaigns, expanded retail stores and rebranded its Central Selling Organization as the Diamond Trading Company. After privatization, it settled U.S. price-fixing and consumer antitrust claims. Joint ventures with Botswana and Namibia also moved sorting, aggregation, sales and marketing activities closer to producing countries.

The synthetic-diamond market was expanding rapidly. Annual sales were nearly $50 million, and analysts projected growth at a 45% compound annual rate to more than $2 billion by 2015. U.S. production reached 400,000 carats in 2006, while prices rose 20%. Producers used high-pressure, high-temperature methods and chemical vapor deposition, which could create flawless and colored stones. Most synthetic jewelry diamonds were still limited to one carat, and producing colorless stones was expensive.

Synthetic diamonds competed on price, environmental effects and political concerns. The Kimberley Process had reduced conflict diamonds to roughly 1% of the trade by 2006, although enforcement remained difficult, and some consumers argued that natural diamonds supported African communities while synthetics did not. The GIA began grading lab-grown diamonds using the same four Cs applied to natural stones and requiring disclosure of their laboratory origin. Synthetics also had growing industrial applications in semiconductors, heat management, optics, data storage and biomedical products; they already represented 90% of the industrial diamond market.

DeBeers responded through detection technology, including free laboratory equipment and $17 million in research, and through consumer education about natural diamonds’ age, uniqueness and benefits to mining communities. It largely maintained that synthetics and natural diamonds were different products and sought additional natural-diamond supplies through new deposits and marketing agreements. The passage ends with Lee still weighing the jeweler’s rejection of synthetics against their financial, environmental and conflict-free advantages, leaving DeBeers’s ultimate response unresolved.

In his final address to the United Nations, the U.S. president reflected on his career since entering the Senate in 1972 and on historical progress through the Cold War, the Vietnam War, apartheid, international war-crimes accountability, and efforts to combat violence against women. He argued that, despite conflicts over Ukraine, Gaza, Sudan, climate change, hunger, terrorism, displacement, and democratic decline, the “center has held” and international cooperation remains essential.

He urged continued support for Ukraine until it achieves a just and durable peace based on the U.N. Charter, responsible management of competition with China, and stronger alliances and partnerships in the Indo-Pacific. In the Middle East, he condemned the October 7 attacks, supported a U.N.-endorsed ceasefire and hostage agreement, advocated a two-state solution, and called for efforts to prevent a wider regional war and prevent Iran from obtaining a nuclear weapon. He also called for an end to Sudan’s civil war and unrestricted humanitarian aid.

Highlighting investments in food security, global health, climate action, renewable energy, and infrastructure, he urged continued international action on climate change, hunger, disease, and mpox. He supported reform and expansion of the U.N. Security Council and called for the United Nations to resume its central peacekeeping role.

Addressing artificial intelligence, he said its benefits and risks require global rules, safety standards, equitable access, and safeguards for human dignity and democratic values. He closed by emphasizing public service, democracy, and the need for international cooperation, announcing that after 50 years in public service he would yield to a new generation of leadership while expressing confidence that collective action could overcome seemingly impossible challenges.

An email circulated May 10, 2001, compiled reports on California’s electricity emergency. Rolling blackouts began earlier than expected amid hot weather, power-plant maintenance, scarce supply from other states, reduced Northwest hydroelectric output and transmission bottlenecks. Grid operators avoided further blackouts as temperatures fell, but forecasts indicated at least 30 more blackout days could occur during the summer. PG&E filed for bankruptcy protection in April, while Southern California Edison also faced insolvency.

The Public Utilities Commission had approved increases of as much as 46 percent in March. A pending proposal would exempt residential customers using no more than 130 percent of baseline usage—about half of PG&E and Edison’s residential customers—while heavier users, businesses and farms would face larger increases. The rate structure was projected to generate $5 billion annually and was intended to encourage conservation, but consumer advocates, manufacturers and other groups criticized how the burden would be distributed. A bankruptcy judge allowed PG&E to continue paying natural-gas suppliers while other creditors awaited repayment.

Gov. Gray Davis asked power generators to accept 70 cents on the dollar for roughly $1.1 billion to $1.2 billion owed by Edison. Davis linked the proposed 30 percent reduction to the state’s planned $2.76 billion purchase of Edison’s transmission system. Some generators were willing to discuss reductions, while Reliant Energy rejected the proposal. Davis sought additional summer power supplies, raised the possibility of a windfall-profit tax and continued investigations into alleged price manipulation.

California spent more than $6 billion buying power for utilities after high wholesale costs and frozen retail rates left PG&E and Edison unable to purchase electricity themselves. The Legislature approved $13.4 billion in revenue bonds, but the measure would not take effect for 90 days. Meanwhile, a legislative analyst said the state’s budget surplus had fallen by $3.4 billion because of reduced technology-related tax revenue, raising the prospect of spending cuts if the energy costs and delayed bond repayment placed additional pressure on the general fund.

Federal policy was also under scrutiny. The Bush administration was preparing a long-term national energy strategy centered on transmission improvements and conservation, while some congressional Republicans pressed for immediate assistance and worried that inadequate action could hurt the party in the 2002 elections. A House emergency bill included limited aid for California and possible temporary waivers of certain power-plant emission standards, but proposals for wholesale price controls and additional assistance faced opposition. Environmental groups criticized the administration’s plan for insufficient emphasis on efficiency and renewable fuels.

Only eight of PG&E’s 300 small power plants remained shut down for payment reasons, providing 109 megawatts; statewide, about 1,400 megawatts were offline. Operators said new payment and pricing rules could force many plants to operate only during peak-demand periods. Western officials also reported that the regional transmission system was fragmented and overworked, with no immediate solution or established funding method for upgrades.

Bernstorff relayed Wilson’s confidential offer of mediation, coupled with requests that Germany disclose its moderate peace terms, accept his Senate-message basis, and publish them. Bernstorff urged postponing unrestricted U-boat warfare, arguing that diplomatic delay could improve Germany’s position, avert U.S. entry, and produce a better peace through conferences, while immediate war risked prolonged conflict. He sought prompt wireless guidance on a February 1 dispatch. In France, 80–90 Socialist deputies endorsed Wilson’s Senate address as promoting peace based on popular will, urged government and belligerent support for a peace conference, and called for resistance to imperialist ambitions. Officials and much of the press approved the message, though many French writers held that peace should follow an Allied victory.

Amanda Nunes retained her UFC title by decisively defeating Ronda Rousey at UFC 207, handing Rousey a second consecutive loss. Nunes blamed Rousey’s head coach, Edmond Tarverdyan, for emphasizing boxing over her successful judo and contributing to her career decline. The loss again exposed the vulnerability Holly Holm had revealed the previous year. Although Nunes had offered Rousey a rematch, the decisive result cast doubt on that possibility. Rousey said she needed time to assess her future amid calls to retire, while Sportskeeda suggested she consider changing fight camps.

The study developed a physician- and medical-biller-labeled dataset of 663 ophthalmologists to address limitations of the LEIE fraud database, including severe class imbalance, focus on overt fraud, and lack of procedure-level detail. Using 2015 CMS Medicare Provider Utilization and Payment Data, each provider was represented by 1,028 features derived from 513 ophthalmology HCPCS codes, service and beneficiary counts, payments, and utilization ratios. The labeled set included 200 overutilizers and 463 non-fraudulent providers.

Five models—KNN, logistic regression, SVM, XGB, and multilayer perceptron—were compared with a stacking ensemble using repeated nested cross-validation. Stacking performed best, with an AUROC of 0.907 and Brier score of 0.109; XGB had an AUROC of 0.898 but poorer calibration. Applied to 2021 billing data for 17,013 ophthalmologists, the model predicted 1,457 overutilizers, an 8.6% rate. Estimated potential 2021 Medicare losses in ophthalmology were $437.1 million. Extrapolation to all of Medicare estimated $49.1 billion in annual losses, or 5.5% of its 2021 budget. Predicted rates varied geographically: jurisdiction JE had the highest rate at 14.01%, while JN had the highest estimated losses at $63.6 million.

SHAP analysis identified Medicare payment per patient as the strongest feature, with higher ratios increasing overutilization predictions; excessive use of specific HCPCS codes was also influential, although high use alone does not establish fraud. Limitations include the small labeled dataset, reliance on model-based estimates requiring audit validation, difficulty distinguishing overutilization from intentional fraud without medical records, and the labor-intensive need for specialty-specific labeled data. The report is a medRxiv preprint that has not been peer reviewed.

The statistical analysis plan specifies demographic and baseline summaries by treatment group for the safety analysis set and full analysis set (FAS). Variables include age, age group, sex, childbearing potential, ethnicity, race, diabetes history, medical history, height, weight, and BMI. BMI will also be summarized by BMI class and country, including US versus non-US countries. Time since diabetes diagnosis will be calculated under specified rules for incomplete dates. Medical history terms will be coded using MedDRA version 22.0 and summarized by system organ class and preferred term.

Concomitant medications and current diabetes treatments will be coded using WHODrug Global, version March 2018, with summaries by WHO ATC level 2 and preferred name. Listings will include documented and coding drug names, preferred terms, ATC codes, and ATC terms. Prior medications will be listed and flagged; medications with unclear dates will be treated as concomitant.

The primary efficacy analysis will use the FAS, with supportive analyses in the per-protocol set. The primary endpoint is time to plasma glucose recovery, defined as the first increase of at least 20 mg/dL from baseline within 45 minutes after dosing without rescue IV glucose. Secondary endpoints include recovery within 30, 20, 15, and 10 minutes and changes from baseline at those times. Baseline is the last non-missing pre-dose value, including unscheduled visits when applicable. Models will adjust for age group and injection site, and only observed, non-missing data will be analyzed without imputation. No interim analyses are planned.

Confirmatory comparisons of dasiglucagon 0.6 mg versus placebo will use a hierarchical two-sided 0.05 testing sequence covering the primary endpoint followed by the secondary endpoints. GlucaGen® comparisons will not be included in this hierarchy. Approximately five centers will participate, but center will not be included in the primary model. Time to recovery will be analyzed with Kaplan-Meier methods and a log-rank test stratified by age group and injection site. Subjects receiving rescue IV glucose and those not recovering by 45 minutes will be censored at 45 minutes in the primary analysis. Sensitivity analyses will either leave rescue recipients uncensored or censor them at rescue administration, and a stratified Wilcoxon test will provide supportive evidence. A descriptive discrete-time Cox model may be used if proportional-hazards conditions and censoring limits are met, with additional models for sex, BMI class, ethnicity, race, and US/non-US status. Linear interpolation will provide a supportive estimate of recovery time.

Recovery rates at 10, 15, 20, and 30 minutes will be compared using a Cochran–Mantel–Haenszel test stratified by age group and injection site, with response rates and 95% confidence intervals. Plasma glucose changes will be analyzed by ANOVA using treatment, age group, and injection site, including adjusted means and treatment-difference confidence intervals.

Plasma dasiglucagon and glucagon concentrations will undergo noncompartmental analysis using Phoenix WinNonlin version 6.4, with concentration summaries and time-course figures. Pharmacodynamic sampling will include plasma glucose at specified post-dose time points, with 60-minute sampling for participants weighing at least 21 kg. The pharmacodynamic endpoint is baseline-adjusted glucose area under the effect curve from 0 to 30 minutes, calculated with SAS.

Safety analyses will use the safety set. Outputs will cover insulin and trial-drug administration, hypoglycemia induction, rescue glucose, local tolerability, adverse events, laboratory results, vital signs, ECG findings, and immunogenicity. Treatment-emergent adverse events will be summarized by MedDRA system organ class and preferred term, with separate summaries for special-interest events, injection-site reactions, related events, serious events, severity, causality, and deaths. Missing causal relationships will be set as related after unsuccessful querying, while missing severity will remain missing.

Laboratory data will be listed individually and summarized descriptively by treatment and time point, with reference-range classifications, categorical counts, and screening-to-follow-up changes. ECG outputs will include investigator assessments, descriptive parameters, QTcF categories above 450, 480, and 500 ms, and changes above 30 and 60 ms. Antidrug antibody incidence will be described without statistical testing, combining treatment-induced and treatment-boosted cases.

The appendices define table, figure, and listing formats, calculation conventions, conservative handling of incomplete dates and medications, unit conversions, BMI and change-from-baseline formulas, and SAS programming quality-control requirements, including validation, log and output review, source-data spot checks, and Pinnacle 21 assessment. Changes from the protocol include expanded primary-endpoint analyses and terminology changes from “within” to “at” specified post-dose time points.

Tesla, Inc. filed an unaudited Form 10-Q for the quarter ended March 31, 2019. It reported 173,720,801 common shares outstanding as of April 22, 2019 and identified itself as a large accelerated filer.

For the three months ended March 31, 2019, total revenue was $4.54 billion, including $3.72 billion from automotive operations, $324.7 million from energy generation and storage, and $492.9 million from services and other activities. Gross profit was $565.7 million, operating loss was $521.8 million, and net loss attributable to common stockholders was $702.1 million, or $4.10 per share. Vehicle pricing adjustments increased the sales-return reserve and reduced automotive revenue by $500.5 million, with a corresponding $408.8 million reduction in automotive cost of sales and a $91.7 million reduction in gross profit.

At March 31, 2019, Tesla reported $28.91 billion of assets, including $2.20 billion of cash and cash equivalents, $3.84 billion of inventory, $6.24 billion of solar energy systems, and $9.85 billion of property, plant and equipment. Total liabilities were $22.87 billion, and total stockholders’ equity was $4.61 billion. Net cash used in operating, investing and financing activities was $639.6 million, $305.8 million and $653.0 million, respectively, leaving $2.68 billion of cash, cash equivalents and restricted cash at quarter-end.

Tesla adopted ASC 842 on January 1, 2019 using a cumulative-effect adjustment. The adoption recognized $1.29 billion of operating lease right-of-use assets and $1.24 billion of related liabilities, while derecognizing build-to-suit lease assets and liabilities of $1.62 billion and $1.74 billion. It also reclassified certain post-January 2019 solar arrangements from lease accounting to revenue recognition under ASC 606.

The filing also disclosed inventory write-downs, an ending accrued warranty reserve of $843.9 million, debt and lease obligations, equity incentive awards, and a planned $47.0 million impairment of acquired in-process research and development in the next quarter. Legal proceedings included the SolarCity acquisition litigation, Model 3 production-related securities litigation, litigation concerning the 2018 CEO Performance Award, and nine stockholder actions arising from Tesla’s potential going-private transaction.

The filing cautioned that forward-looking statements reflect current expectations, involve risks and uncertainties, and may differ materially from actual results.

BSEB declared BETET/BSITET 2011 results for the 2016 special examinations across Classes 1–12. Candidates can check results with a 10-digit roll number, print them, and download official answer keys for both papers.

North Carolina child care academies operate in at least 11 counties, providing customized, low- or no-cost routes into early childhood education. Programs last two to six weeks, require 20 to 64 hours of training, and are designed to address staffing shortages; 60% of licensed child care providers reportedly experienced shortages. A $1.476 million state-funded expansion pilot passed the North Carolina House but was omitted from the final General Assembly budget. DCDEE separately offers grants of up to $50,000 to as many as 10 UNC institutions to run academies through July 31, 2026.

Two models have developed. The classroom-ready model requires at least 20 hours of instruction, including CPR, first aid, infant safety training and background checks, and qualifies graduates to work in licensed child care facilities. The teaching credential model adds training equivalent to the semester-long EDU 119 course. Graduates earn transferable EDU 3119 credit at North Carolina’s 58 community colleges, qualify as licensed lead teachers or elementary teaching assistants, and can continue toward an associate degree.

Programs are typically collaborations among community colleges, Smart Start partnerships and child care resource and referral organizations. Examples include:

- Wayne and Johnston counties: Camber Foundation funding supports 60-hour, two- to three-week programs. Combined academies graduated 63 students, more than half of whom entered child care or higher education. Johnston’s program cost about $430 per student.
- Stanly County: Two classroom-ready academies graduated 13 students, with five to 10 obtaining jobs. Funding constraints have prevented adoption of the teaching credential model.
- McDowell County: A two-week teaching credential academy graduated six students; four entered child care and two pursued higher education. A Dogwood Health Trust grant covered training and associate-degree tuition.
- Durham County: A bilingual, six-week teaching credential program cost an average of $1,264 per student and drew 140 applicants for 20 slots.

The state task force has described academies as scalable local solutions, while interest is growing among additional community colleges.

Ontario Thrive says the first two debates neglected gender equity and sexual violence, despite approximately 19 women reportedly being murdered since January. It cites Elisabeth Salm’s fatal workplace assault and the Gagnon family killings. The group criticizes the prospective premier for focusing on memes, making dismissive comments about women, and failing to answer questions on sexual violence. It calls for safe workplaces, affordable child care, safe transit, a livable minimum wage, and education on consent and gender-based violence.

Sheffield residents and campaigners oppose Amey’s tree-felling plans, with 31 trees along Rivelin Valley Road threatened. Its 700 lime trees are described as the UK’s second-longest avenue. Residents question claims that damaged roots justify removal during resurfacing and say felling would harm the avenue. The dispute stems from a 25-year, £2bn private finance initiative signed with Amey in 2009, and an independent panel’s report is awaited.

Investing.com’s financial markets page lists headlines on the S&P 500 ending its winning streak amid an Oracle-led tech selloff, IBM’s Anthropic partnership, Goldman Sachs’ $4,900 end-2026 gold target, Bitcoin above $126,000, Disney, EUR/USD, and the U.S. dollar. Market commentary cites 35 years of seasonal weakness, thin liquidity, institutional tax-loss selling and rebalancing, and fading earnings optimism in August. Technical analysis of TLT and market indicators discusses possible further yield declines, bullish divergence, resistance levels, and risks to a continued rally. A weaker dollar is described as bullish for commodities, energy, and raw materials, while gold resistance is identified at $38.50 and $40. The page also promotes a stock screener and includes trading-risk, data-accuracy, advertising, copyright, and cookie notices.

This SCET lecture applies effective field theory to dijets produced in \(e^+e^-\) collisions through a virtual photon or \(Z\). The final state is organized into hard, collinear jet, and isotropic ultrasoft modes, with characteristic scales \(q^2\), \(\mu_j\sim m\), \(\mu_s\sim m^2/q\), and \(\Lambda_{\mathrm{QCD}}\). Measuring small hemisphere invariant masses \(m^2,\bar m^2\ll q^2\) selects a two-jet configuration; the power-counting parameter is \(m/q\).

Two regimes are distinguished: the peak region, where \(\mu_s\sim\Lambda_{\mathrm{QCD}}\) and nonperturbative effects must be retained, and the tail region, where \(\mu_s\gg\Lambda_{\mathrm{QCD}}\), ultrasoft physics is perturbative, and power corrections scale as \((\Lambda_{\mathrm{QCD}}/\mu_s)^n\). Matching the QCD current to SCET, making a field redefinition, and factoring the constrained cross section yields a factorization theorem containing a hard function (the squared Wilson coefficient), two jet functions, and a soft function. These functions naturally use the hard, jet, and soft scales, with renormalization-group evolution resumming logarithms such as \(\ln(m^2/q^2)\). The soft function encodes nonperturbative physics and may be separated through a soft-function OPE into a perturbative power-law tail and a nonperturbative exponential contribution. Higher power corrections do not introduce new degrees of freedom.

The lecture also treats thrust. In the dijet limit, the thrust axis aligns with the jet axis, and \(\tau=1-T\) is related to the sum of the two hemisphere masses. Projecting the factorization formula onto this symmetric combination gives a one-variable result with analogous peak and tail regions; outside the dijet regime, additional jet degrees of freedom are required.

Perturbatively, one-loop matching provides the hard function, while cut quark and Wilson-line diagrams determine the jet and soft functions. The hard coefficient renormalizes multiplicatively, whereas the jet and soft functions have convolution-type renormalization-group evolution.

Former Infosys CFO V. Balakrishnan said SEBI should decide Infosys’s consent plea in the Rajiv Bansal severance case on legal merits, not the whistleblower’s emotions. The whistleblower alleged governance and disclosure lapses, called the settlement a “backdoor agreement” and urged prosecution of Infosys’s board and management. The MAGIC stereo telescope and CTAO LST-1 are Imaging Atmospheric Cherenkov Telescopes at the Roque de los Muchachos Observatory on La Palma. Their on-site analysis (OSA) pipelines have operated since 2012 for MAGIC and 2021 for LST-1, providing rapid access to processed data for daily quality checks, science alerts, scheduling, and transient follow-up. MAGIC produces up to 2 TB of raw data daily, while LST-1 produces up to 30 TB.

Both pipelines use a common analysis sequence: digitised signals and metadata form DL0 data; calibration yields pixel charge and arrival times at DL1; image and particle-parameter reconstruction produce DL2; photon-candidate lists and instrument response functions form DL3. LST-1’s pipeline evolved from MAGIC’s design but was largely rewritten, with MAGIC using Mars and LST-1 using lstchain. Both are primarily Python systems launched through cron jobs and managed through key files and job dependencies.

Daily processing begins with DAQ and slow-control information and an observation summary. Data are divided into time-based file sets and processed in parallel using Torque for MAGIC and SLURM for LST-1. OSA monitors jobs, flags problems, merges output files, transfers results off-site, and cleans temporary directories. Web pages display analysis status, while email alerts report unrecoverable failures. Failed processes are retried and may be vetoed; detailed recovery procedures currently exist only for MAGIC but are planned for LST-1.

MAGIC additionally generates significance plots, sky maps, spectra, and light curves, while equivalent high-level steps are being added to LST-1. The stated lessons are that next-day analysis is essential, must be coordinated with observatory databases and simulation tools, and should combine automation with human oversight and robust error detection and recovery. The systems are presented as effective prototypes for future CTAO on-site pipelines.

An informal meeting discussed a draft agreement among the United Kingdom, United States, and Belgian governments regulating Congo commodity purchases and supplies to the Congo. Belgian representatives proposed allowing earlier revision if Belgian territory was liberated, enabling the government to direct Congo products to Belgian needs. They requested clarification of Article 3’s pricing procedure; the discussion indicated that existing special price arrangements should remain undisturbed, detailed prices might take time to establish, and actual prices should be set through subsidiary arrangements rather than included in the agreement. Belgian concerns also included dollar exchange for exports to the United States and a specific shipping guarantee. British representatives noted the January 1941 finance agreement’s foreign-exchange undertaking and considered shipping adequately covered by Schedule 2 and Article 6, while referral to the Ministry of War Transport or discussion with the American shipping representative was suggested. Participants also considered avoiding overlap between the current bilateral agreement and the new three-party agreement, with uncompleted transactions potentially lapsing. Article 1 provides that, from September 1, 1942, through December 31, 1943, Belgium would make scheduled Congo exports available to British and American buyers.

OpenAI announced new ChatGPT parental controls after a lawsuit following a California teenager’s death, which alleged the chatbot provided harmful advice and helped draft a suicide note. Through mutually agreed account linking, parents can restrict sensitive content, disable voice or image functions, set quiet hours, control conversation storage, and receive acute-risk alerts without access to transcripts. OpenAI is also developing age prediction to flag users under 18 and apply stricter safety settings amid scrutiny of AI’s impact on minors.

Plymouth Studio School is expected to close in September 2018 after a decision in principle was made following discussions with the Regional Schools Commissioner’s office and Department for Education. A final decision was due from the Minister for Schools in July 2018. The £4.2 million school, which opened in 2015 to provide specialist education for students aged 14–19 with an emphasis on sports, faced financial viability concerns and an Ofsted inspection that rated it “inadequate.”

Headteacher Mark Cahill said staff would support pupils’ transition to secondary schools, with the local authority confirming sufficient places. Parents were notified and offered briefings, while the RSC planned a listening period. The council, school and Careers South West arranged guidance sessions for families, and HR specialists liaised with staff about future options.

The school moved into a purpose-built facility at the University of St Mark and St John’s campus in November 2016 and planned to enrol 300 pupils. It offered GCSE, A-level and BTEC qualifications, sports coaching and high-performance facilities. Its closure would make it the 19th studio school to close since the model began.

The HHLL strategy is a price-action reversal system based on price swings and broken trend structures. It seeks long opportunities when a downtrend forms a lower low followed by a higher high, and short opportunities when an uptrend forms a higher high followed by a lower low, with entries on the subsequent pullback.

Strict backtesting is difficult because identifying swing tops and bottoms requires discretion. ZigZag was considered unsuitable because it uses forward-looking elements and lags. A simplified backtest uses an outside day, when the current day’s high and low exceed the previous day’s, as a trade criterion.

On Philip Morris, the backtest recorded 118 trades, a 9.8% CAGR, a 1.26% average gain per trade, and a profit factor of 2.2. AmiBroker and plain-English versions of the code are offered for purchase.

Designs in Mind has taken a permanent lease on a former Chrissie’s shop in Cross Street, Oswestry, following a successful pop-up trial. The shop, Jolt, sells brightly coloured homeware and prints, many designed by members referred through a mental health scheme, and offers screen-printing and lino-printing workshops. H. Under NSC 10/2, CIA covert activities included propaganda, economic warfare, sabotage, support for resistance and anti-Communist groups, but excluded armed conflict by recognized forces, espionage, counterespionage, and military deception. The newly created Office of Policy Coordination organized and managed covert action, initially receiving guidance from State in peacetime and the military in wartime; in 1950, guidance was routed through the DCI. During Korea, covert action became the CIA’s costliest and most bureaucratically prominent activity. Truman’s 1951 response created the Psychological Strategy Board, while NSC 10/5 reaffirmed and expanded the CIA’s mandate, including guerrilla warfare. By the end of Truman’s term, only the DCI and President could authorize, manage, or curtail operations.

Eisenhower narrowed CIA autonomy beginning in 1954. NSC 5412 and later directives required coordination with State and Defense, while senior officials approved major programs. The body created by NSC 5412/2 became the “Special Group,” which reviewed and approved CIA initiatives. After the Bay of Pigs, the Taylor Report led it to assume greater planning and review responsibility. In 1963, the Special Group adopted informal criteria—including risk, exposure, political sensitivity, success prospects, and cost—for deciding which projects to review.

Fullbacks primarily serve as extra blockers in pro-style offenses, lining up beside or behind the quarterback in two-back formations and sealing blocks at the second level to help running plays succeed. Although generally less athletic than running backs, they compensate with toughness, tenacity, and strong run- and pass-blocking ability. They occasionally carry the ball on fullback dives or receive short passes. Traditionally larger than running backs, fullbacks typically stand 5-foot-11 to 6-foot-1 and weigh 235–250 pounds. Their use has declined with the spread offense’s popularity, but they remain important to traditional running schemes. Notable fullbacks include six-time Pro Bowl selection Mike Alstott, who scored 58 career touchdowns, and Larry Csonka, who nearly rushed for 7,000 yards with the Miami Dolphins.

In 2012, the author helped organize a May Day strike in Brooklyn, but insufficient participation failed to disrupt business. Following the Trump administration’s actions, new strikes were planned for February 17 and March 8, with May 1 also under consideration. Francine Prose and David Simon promoted the February action, while women activists, including Angela Davis, organized the March strike to advance “a feminism for the 99 percent” and build on the Women’s March.

The article cites European strikes as effective political tools: 63 general strikes from 2000 to 2016 led governments to change or withdraw policies 42 percent of the time, including after a Polish women’s strike helped defeat an anti-abortion bill. ## Summary

**UHS-II initialization and card selection:** The broadcast SET_DSR command (CMD4) configures driver stages of all identified cards, programming DSR registers per bus layout, card count and data transfer frequency, and switching the clock rate from fOD to fPP. CMD7 selects one card into the Transfer State; a previously selected card returns to Stand-by, and issuing CMD7 with reserved RCA 0x0000 returns all cards to Stand-by. This may be used before identifying new cards without resetting registered cards; cards with an RCA do not respond to ACMD41 or CMD2. CMD48, CMD49, CMD58 and CMD59 are available in UHS-II mode.

**Data transfer mode:** All data communication is point-to-point between host and selected card. Read and write commands can be aborted with CMD12; write commands must be stopped before deselection by CMD7. After a transfer, the card moves to Programming State (success) or Transfer State (failure). Write buffering permits the next block while the previous is programmed, with DAT0 held low (BUSY) when buffers are full; there is no buffering for write CSD, write protection or erase. Parameter set commands (CMD16, CMD32, CMD33) and read commands are not allowed while programming. Selecting another card moves the busy card to Disconnect State and releases the DAT line; it can be reselected via CMD7 to reactivate busy. CMD0 or CMD15 terminates pending programming and may destroy data. CMD34-37, CMD50 and CMD57 are reserved for command system expansion.

**Bus width and capacity:** 4-bit wide bus is selected/deselected with ACMD6; default after power-up or CMD0 is 1-bit, and a locked card rejects ACMD6 as illegal. For 2 GByte cards, READ_BL_LEN/WRITE_BL_LEN is 1024 bytes while CMD16 block length stays ≤512 bytes.

**Data read:** Blocks are transmitted synchronously with start bits, payload (with optional ECC), end bits and 1- or 4-bit CRC; reads are aborted safely by power-off, and data is preserved except during host write/erase. Read commands are rejected on BLOCK_LEN_ERROR or ADDRESS_ERROR. The basic transfer unit is a block of at most 512 bytes; CMD16 block length up to 512 bytes. CMD17 reads one block and returns to Transfer State; CMD18 reads consecutive blocks until CMD12, with OUT_OF_RANGE to be ignored at the last user-area block. Block misalignment sets ADDRESS_ERROR, aborts transmission and requires CMD12 to recover.

**Data write:** Each received block carries a 1- or 4-bit CRC checked before writing, preventing corrupted data. Writes are rejected on BLOCK_LEN_ERROR or ADDRESS_ERROR; CMD16 block length must be 512 bytes for block write regardless of WRITE_BL_LEN. Partial blocks are allowed when WRITE_BL_PARTIAL=1; CRC failure discards data. Multiple block write is preferred for speed; misalignment aborts programming before the first misaligned block; writing to protected areas sets WP_VIOLATION. CSD programming needs no prior block length, is CRC protected, and fails if the ROM portion does not match. During programming DAT0 stays low, status is polled with CMD13 (READY_FOR_DATA), CMD7 deselects without interrupting the write, and interleaved writes to several cards are possible. ACMD23 pre-sets the number of pre-erased blocks (reset to 1 afterwards, best sent immediately before the write); ACMD22 returns the number of successfully written blocks.

**Erase, Discard and FULE:** Erasing uses CMD32, CMD33, CMD38 in sequence. Out-of-sequence commands set ERASE_SEQ_ERROR or ERASE_RESET; write-protected sectors stay intact with WP_ERASE_SKIP set. Address fields are write-block addresses in byte units with LSBs below WRITE_BL_LEN ignored, and DAT0 low indicates progress. Post-erase data is '0' or '1' per DATA_STAT_AFTER_ERASE (bit 55). DISCARD (CMD38 argument 00000001h) is similar to erase with contents treated as "don't care", requires the DISCARD_SUPPORT bit (b313), applies to SDHC/SDXC only, has a 250 ms busy timeout and is forgotten on power cycle. FULE (CMD38 argument 00000002h, with CMD32 = 0 and CMD33 = end of user area) logically erases the entire user area, requires FULE_SUPPORT (b312), falls back to ERASE if the full area is not specified, and has a 1 second busy timeout.

**Write protection and lock/unlock:** Three methods exist: mechanical switch (host responsibility), card internal write protection (section blank), and password protection. The mechanical sliding tablet's position is unknown to card circuitry. Passwords are held in 128-bit PWD and 8-bit PWD_LEN registers, with optional FEP/FEP_LEN for Card Ownership Protection (COP); these are non-volatile. Locked cards execute class 0, ACMD41, CMD16 and "lock card" commands only, and lock automatically after power-up when PWD_LEN is non-zero. Lock/unlock (CMD42) works only in Transfer State and uses a single-block-write structure; it carries mode, password length (≤16 bytes; old+new ≤32 bytes) and password data, with block length at least equal to the data structure and even in DDR50. COP prevents card reuse without PWD; CMD42[1Fh] (COP Unlock) is required after power-up or reset when FEP is set, and CMD42[1Fh] alone unlocks a COP-locked card. COP cards operate in CMD42 Ver.1.0 compatible mode, or Ver.2.0 mode after COP Unlock, adding FEP management (Reset/Set/Replace FEP), Force Erase versus FEP Force Erase (CMD42[08h]/CMD42[18h]) and Reset PWD inhibit. Errors set LOCK_UNLOCK_FAILED (bit 24), and CARD_IS_LOCKED (bit 25) reflects state changes. Locking, unlocking, setting, changing and clearing passwords follow defined CMD7/CMD16/CMD42 sequences. ACMD6 is rejected while locked, and locked cards accept only listed commands. Card types 1, 2 and 3 (COP) differ as tabulated; hosts should avoid error-producing parameters, avoid force erase when permanent write protect is set, clear temporary write protect after force erase, and not set FEP on a COP card locked with unknown PWD. Force erase clears all content including PWD and leaves the secure area intact, keeping the card locked during the erase; FEP force erase requires a matching FEP and leaves FEP unchanged.

**Application and general commands:** CMD55 (APP_CMD) makes the next command an ACMD; undefined ACMDs are treated as regular commands, the APP_CMD bit signals acceptance, illegal ACMDs raise an illegal command error, and ACMD41 is an exception. ACMD6, ACMD13, ACMD17-26, ACMD38-49 and ACMD51 are reserved for proprietary use. The GEN_CMD (CMD56) section is blank.

**Switch function (CMD6):** CMD6 selects or expands card functions across function groups covering Access Mode, Command System, Driver Strength and Power Limit; support is checked via the SCR "SD_SPEC" field or CSD CCC bit10, and is mandatory from Version 1.10. It is valid in Transfer State, returns an R1 response on CMD plus 512 bits of status on DAT (100 ms timeout), and applies changes within 8 clocks; functions revert to default after power cycle, CMD6 with function 0, or CMD0. Six function groups each support sixteen branches, one active function per group, with function 0 as default. Mode 0 checks supported functions and maximum current/power consumption; mode 1 sets functions and returns supported functions, resulting functions and consumption, ignoring invalid selections and reporting 0xF. Power Limit defaults to 0.72 W, removable cards are limited to 1.80 W, and in UHS-II only function group 4 support is mandatory. The status block includes function selection and support bits per group, maximum consumption and busy status bits, with a data structure version indicating whether busy status is effective.

**Other modes and commands:** High-Speed mode (25 MB/sec) is reached via CMD6 access mode function with a 50 MHz clock, is optional, and requires the host to drive only one card with 1-to-1 CLK/CMD/DAT connections. The Command System group switches interpretation of CMD34-37, CMD50 and CMD57 among standard (illegal), vendor-specific and mobile e-commerce sets. CMD8 (Send Interface Condition) is issued in Idle state before ACMD41, checks host supply voltage, returns R7 echoing voltage and check pattern, or leaves the card in Idle if unsupported. CCS in the ACMD41 response indicates capacity type (0 = SDSC, 1 = SDHC/SDXC); SDHC/SDXC use 32-bit block addressing, fixed 512-byte blocks, and disable partial and misaligned access, and they do not support write-protected groups (CMD28-30). CMD42 is not a memory access command and its block length may be set up to 512 bytes.

**Clock control and CRC:** The host may lower or stop the clock, with ACMD41 requiring 100-400 kHz continuous clock or polling under 50 ms; eight clock cycles must be provided after each transaction type, and stopping the clock of a busy card needs a clock edge to release DAT0. CRC7 (x7+x3+1) protects commands, responses except R3, and CSD/CID (40 and 120 bits respectively); CRC16 (x16+x12+x5+1) protects block payloads, with per-line computation in wide bus and 0x7FA1 for 512 bytes of 0xFF data. A CRC failure yields no response, no state change and COM_CRC_ERROR; illegal commands likewise give no response or state change with ILLEGAL_COMMAND set.

**Timeouts:** Read timeout is the lower of 100 times the typical access time (TAAC+NSAC) or 100 ms; write timeout is the lower of 100 times the typical program time (R2W_FACTOR based) or 250 ms. SDHC/SDXC indicate fixed values; SDXC busy may extend to 500 ms, speed class writes keep 250 ms, and hosts are advised to use fixed timeouts above 500 ms. In UHS-II, busy is signalled after each Data Burst with a maximum of 1 second.

A report to Congress recommends reciprocal commercial treaties between the United States and other Western Hemisphere republics. Although over 87 percent of Latin American products already enter U.S. ports free, existing concessions complicate negotiations; improved steam and financial services and rebates on imported raw materials could help U.S. merchants compete and enlarge trade.

Microsoft Corporation’s Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended June 30, 2018 describes its strategy around intelligent cloud, intelligent edge, artificial intelligence, and increasingly natural interactions across devices. Its three ambitions are to reinvent productivity and business processes through Microsoft 365, Office, Dynamics, LinkedIn, and Teams; build an intelligent cloud platform through Azure, Azure Stack, and AI tools; and expand personal computing through Windows, Surface devices, Xbox, and related services.

Microsoft reports three operating segments. Productivity and Business Processes includes Office Commercial and Consumer, LinkedIn, and Dynamics. Intelligent Cloud includes server products, Azure, and Enterprise Services. More Personal Computing includes Windows, Surface and other devices, gaming and Xbox Live, and Bing search. Microsoft also announced a $7.5 billion agreement in June 2018 to acquire GitHub, expected to close by year-end, following its $27.0 billion acquisition of LinkedIn in 2016.

The company sells through OEMs, direct channels, distributors, resellers, and partner programs, offering volume-licensing and cloud-subscription options for organizations of varying sizes. Its customers include consumers, businesses, public-sector organizations, developers, internet service providers, and OEMs; no individual customer represented more than 10% of revenue in fiscal 2016–2018. Research and development expense was $14.7 billion in fiscal 2018, or 13% of revenue, and Microsoft reported more than 53,000 issued U.S. and international patents and over 29,000 pending patents. As of June 30, 2018, it employed approximately 131,000 people.

Risk factors include intense competition across platforms and business models; cloud-service execution and infrastructure costs; uncertain returns on new products and acquisitions; impairment of acquired assets; intellectual-property protection, licensing, and infringement claims; source-code leakage; cyberattacks, security vulnerabilities, outages, and misuse of personal data; antitrust and other regulatory compliance; global data-transfer and privacy requirements, including GDPR; employee recruitment and retention; and litigation. The filing cautions that forward-looking statements depend on assumptions subject to risks and uncertainties and that actual results may differ materially.

A collection of May 24–25, 2001 news reports and commentary focuses on Enron’s political influence, its troubled Dabhol power project in India, and the U.S. energy crisis.

The New York Times reported that FERC Chairman Curtis Hebert Jr. and Enron Chairman Kenneth Lay gave different accounts of a telephone call in which Hebert said Lay offered continued support if he changed his views on electricity deregulation and grid access. Lay denied making support conditional on policy. The article also noted that Lay supplied preferred FERC candidates, Enron and its executives gave $2.4 million to federal candidates in 2000—72% to Republicans—and Pat Wood was widely expected to replace Hebert after Senate approval of other nominees.

In Maharashtra, the State Electricity Board notified Enron’s Dabhol Power Co. that it was rescinding the seven-year power-purchase agreement, citing performance failures and alleged misrepresentation. Dabhol said the board lacked the right to cancel and had separately initiated termination over unpaid December and January bills. Reports cited claims ranging from $48 million to $64 million in unpaid bills and $85.31 million in penalties. Indian mediators said committee recommendations were nonbinding and that government liabilities could reach 170 billion rupees, or $3.6 billion, if the project ended. Negotiations continued as the government discussed an NTPC takeover or sale of Enron’s 65% stake. Bechtel stopped work and threatened to withdraw unless overdue dues were paid by May 31, while lenders withheld about $250 million. MSEB was expected to pay April’s bill under protest; the first phase was operating at roughly 37% capacity, and the second phase remained uncertain.

Other coverage addressed California’s electricity shortages and price crisis. A Los Angeles Times editorial urged Gov. Gray Davis and the Bush administration to cooperate, impose temporary federal wholesale price controls, and replace political threats with practical action. Davis’s job rating had fallen 18 points since January, although other potential gubernatorial candidates also polled poorly. Attorney General Bill Lockyer threatened legal action against energy generators, including Enron.

The Dow rose 0.2%, the Nasdaq 1.7%, and the S&P 500 0.3% as investors weighed weak economic data, Alan Greenspan’s speech, and Sen. James Jeffords’s departure from the Republican Party; Enron stock fell $1.19 to $54.16. Portland General Electric reported record quarterly revenue and earnings from wholesale power sales but also sharply higher electricity and fuel costs.

Additional articles said deregulation and the crisis were drawing MBAs and executives into energy careers; argued that the internet is transforming corporations from vertically integrated firms toward partner-based business networks; reported an India-Australia cooperation pact in mining, power, coal and other energy, with potential Australian investments of about $3 billion in India; and covered a FERC hearing in which El Paso’s chairman agreed to testify about allegations that the company withheld pipeline capacity to raise California gas prices.

The May 21, 2001 VentureWire People newsletter reports numerous high-tech executive appointments. Wellogix named president Zeke Zeringue CEO after Jeff Livesay stepped down; Livesay remains vice chairman, while director Fred Weber became chairman. EXP Systems appointed Mark Wright president and CEO, with founder Mark Benning continuing as chairman.

SBI’s Ecowrap report expects the RBI’s 4–4.5% inflation forecast to be materially undershot, with CPI inflation below 4% until July. It projects 2017–18 average CPI inflation at 4.8%, citing lower fuel prices and a stronger rupee. Wholesale inflation eased to 5.7% in March, and WPI is expected to exceed CPI through the fiscal year’s fourth quarter.

The passage outlines a U.S. claim against Russia arising from the seizure of the American whaling ship *Cape Horn Pigeon* and the impressment of 31 crew members into Russian service. It seeks $45,000 for the vessel claim, $31,000 for the impressment at $1,000 per man, and compensation for compulsory labor in navigating the Russian schooner at $10 daily for officers and $5 for men. The claimant argues that international law holds Russia responsible for its subjects’ actions and supports full restitution.
