Seattle officer Michl convinced an Uber driver to return a woman’s purse after he demanded extra money, warning of arrest and impoundment and sending a selfie.

The Philadelphia Flyers’ coach praised his team’s resilience, competitive effort, and growth through adversity despite a painful Stanley Cup Final loss. He congratulated the Chicago Blackhawks, describing them as a fast, strong, offensive team with a tight defense, and credited their goalie’s outstanding playoff performance.

The coach said Philadelphia generated promising opportunities late in regulation and overtime but failed to convert them. He also praised Scott Hartnell’s line with Danny Briere and Jiri Leino as the team’s most dangerous and productive unit, while noting Hartnell’s scoring and physical play.

Facing elimination for the sixth time, the Flyers must win at home and then take another game to reach the next round. The coach emphasized the importance of preparation, home energy, and focusing on the immediate objective of beating Chicago once. He expressed confidence in the team’s ability to win a game, citing its experience at home and the calming influence of veteran leaders.

The Supreme Court’s October 2025 term includes major disputes over presidential power, civil rights, social policy and criminal procedure. After a summer of mostly 6–3 emergency rulings allowing Trump administration actions, the court will consider whether the International Emergency Economic Powers Act authorizes tariffs, whether Congress may limit the president’s power to remove agency heads, and whether an executive order restricting birthright citizenship is constitutional.

The court will also rehear a Louisiana redistricting case concerning two majority-Black congressional districts and Section 2 of the Voting Rights Act, which permits liability based on racial disparate impact without proof of discriminatory intent. The issue could affect other federal statutes imposing disparate-impact liability, including Title VII and the Fair Housing Act.

Other arguments address Colorado’s ban on conversion therapy, claims by a Christian counselor that the law violates free speech, free exercise and counseling rights, and state laws restricting transgender athletes from teams corresponding with their gender identities. The term also features a Fourth Amendment case asking whether police entering a home under the emergency-aid exception need probable cause of an emergency. Chemerinsky expects the term’s blockbuster rulings to significantly influence law and American society.

The passage describes a continuation patent application concerning waveguide devices with uniform output illumination, building on related “Waveguide Device with Uniform Output Illumination” applications and other incorporated references. Waveguide optics are presented for display and sensor applications, including AR/VR near-eye displays, aviation and automotive HUDs, biometric sensors, and LIDAR, with emphasis on thin, transparent, lightweight substrates and wide fields of view obtained through multiple recorded holograms.

A disclosed waveguide device includes an optical substrate, light source, light coupler, light extractor, and a debanding optic. The coupler directs incident light into total internal reflection (TIR), with each incidence angle defining a unique TIR angle, while the extractor removes light from the substrate to produce output illumination. Banding occurs when successive light extractions contain gaps or overlaps, creating output ripples that depend on field angle, waveguide thickness, and aperture thickness. The debanding optic shifts or otherwise varies the pupil so that successive extraction profiles integrate into a substantially flat illumination profile. Desired spatial non-uniformity is below 20% and preferably below 10%, although reducing non-uniformity can reduce image brightness.

Proposed debanding optics include an effective input aperture varied according to TIR angle; spatially varying diffraction efficiency, transmission, polarization, or birefringence; multiple, stacked, passive, multiplexed, or electrically switchable input and output gratings; switchable grating arrays providing horizontal and vertical pupil shifts; gratings with rolled K-vectors; and refractive-index layers, including gradient-index media. Other embodiments use partially reflecting or polarization-modifying layers to create separate transmitted and reflected paths, crossed-slant gratings with fold-grating pupil expanders, spatially variable numerical apertures in microdisplays or MEMS arrays, tilted microdisplays, coupling prisms, and light-absorbing films at substrate edges. The document also states a zero-banding condition relating an effective input aperture, substrate thickness D, and TIR angle U through 2D tan(U).

A color waveguide embodiment stacks multiple optical substrates and uses input stops in different substrates and planes. Each stop includes an outer dichroic portion for pupil shifting and color-banding reduction and may include an inner phase-compensation coating. A corresponding method produces incident light, couples it into a substrate for TIR, extracts it through a light extractor, and passes it through a debanding optic to mitigate output banding.

The detailed description discusses input image generators containing light sources, microdisplay panels, collimation optics, beamsplitters, filters, and despecklers; laser, LED, LCD, LCoS, reflective, transmissive, and emissive sources; Bragg, volume, surface-relief, passive, and switchable gratings; and HPDLC-based switchable Bragg gratings. Color systems may use separate wavelength layers, multiplexed gratings, and dichroic filters, while fold gratings can provide dual-axis pupil expansion. Numerous drawings illustrate waveguide configurations, switching arrangements, pupil shifts, variable numerical apertures, tilted image generators, absorbing substrates, and color-registration coatings.

The center occupies the middle of the offensive line and acts as its “quarterback,” directing traffic, calling protections, identifying defenders, and adjusting assignments to the defense’s look. Film study, football IQ, leadership, and quick decision-making are central to the role. Physically, centers snap the ball, block in the trenches, reach linebackers, pull, and pick up blitzes, requiring strength, agility, toughness, and stamina. They are generally thick, compact, and somewhat undersized, estimated at 6'1"–6'4" and 310–325 pounds, with skills in run blocking, pass blocking, and snapping from shotgun or under center. Their leadership and trust with the quarterback help protect the quarterback and support the run game. Notable centers include Hall of Famer Jim Otto and four-time Super Bowl champion Mike Webster.

Amazon.com, Inc. filed a Form 8-K dated October 27, 2016, announcing its third-quarter 2016 financial results. Exhibit 99.1 contains the results press release, while Exhibit 99.2 provides information about non-GAAP financial measures included in Amazon’s public disclosures. The filing was signed by Senior Vice President and Chief Financial Officer Brian T. Olsavsky.

The passage outlines clocking, interrupt, electrical timing, peripheral, and PCB-layout requirements for a DaVinci digital media processor. The PCIe PHY requires a low-jitter differential SERDES clock that complies with the PCI Express REFCLK specification and is AC-coupled with small, equal-sized capacitors placed close to the processor. Optional clock inputs include three AUD_CLK inputs with a maximum frequency of 50 MHz and a 32,768-Hz CLKIN32 reference. CLKOUT0 and CLKOUT1 can select DEVOSC, USBPLL, VIDEO0 PLL, or RTC-divider sources.

The clock system contains 12 top-level and four embedded PLLs. Most use the DEV input clock, while selected PLLs can use AUX; all enter bypass mode after reset. PLL supplies require external filtering, and programming must satisfy REFCLK, CLKDCO, CLKOUT, multiplier, divider, SYSCLK, and module-frequency limits. PLL_USB must be fixed at 960 MHz. PRCM-generated SYSCLKs and module clocks are also constrained by device and peripheral limits.

The ARM Cortex-A8 interrupt controller prioritizes up to 128 requests and generates IRQs or FIQs, while general-purpose devices do not support FIQs. The C674x controller maps up to 128 events to 12 prioritized interrupts, supports multiplexed events, and controls CPU exceptions, NMI, and emulation interrupts.

AC timing is specified at device pins, with input testing at a slew rate below 4 V/ns and a 1.5-V reference for 3.3-V signals. Board-routing delays must be considered, and IBIS models are recommended for system timing analysis.

Peripheral sections describe two DCAN controllers, a 64-channel EDMA controller with 512 mappable parameter entries, Advanced Event Triggering, Cortex-A8 and system trace, JTAG emulation and boundary scan, a three-port gigabit Ethernet switch with MII/GMII/RMII/RGMII and MDIO support, 128 GPIO channels, and the GPMC/ELM for external NOR, NAND, SRAM, and custom devices. Additional sections cover HDMI 1.3a, HDVPSS, video DAC outputs, four I2C modules, the camera/imaging subsystem, and DDR2/DDR3 controllers.

PCB guidance includes HDMI TMDS impedance and ESD-protection requirements, 75-ohm video-output routing, and detailed DDR2/DDR3 stackup, placement, keepout, bypass-capacitor, reference-voltage, termination, and signal-routing rules.

Palestine police arrested two suspects after about 30 cars were broken into. Police say thieves targeted unlocked vehicles without forced entry and urge drivers to report rummaging, even when nothing was taken, and lock their doors.

Enterprises in discrete manufacturing and process industries can benefit from HPC, which processes work orders in parallel across connected systems. Four in five surveyed decision makers view HPC as a game changer for product and process innovation. HPC enables complex simulations, modeling, optimization, and analysis; accelerates iterations; unlocks new industrial and tailored applications; and supports faster development and production. Over 25% already use professional HPC infrastructure, 39% are piloting deployment, and 15% are not engaging because of high investment costs.

Coach DeBoer said Travis, a key player he had coached internationally, missed most of the year with an Achilles injury. After a difficult comeback and setback, Travis insisted he was ready; DeBoer returned him to the lineup because of his veteran quality and the boost he provided, despite some risk.

DeBoer defended the power play despite poor results, saying it had generated quality chances and would not be abandoned. He praised Henrik Lundqvist’s composure, puck handling and calming influence on an inexperienced defense, and said his consistency and leadership were important during the Finals. DeBoer also explained that Lundqvist was temporarily removed because a healthy, younger and fresher Josefson changed the matchup against the Rangers, but Lundqvist stayed ready and was rewarded.

The team adjusted throughout the playoffs, maintained focus and believed it could win three or four straight, though late-season pressure and frustration remained. DeBoer identified scoring and putting more pucks around the net as areas needing improvement. He described Clarky as a hard-working, undrafted player who earned his opportunity and said coaching overseas had made Paul a better coach. He concluded that missed shots and defensive breakdowns had caused losses, making execution the deciding factor.

On November 27, 2001, Dynegy confirmed negotiations to restructure its all-stock acquisition of Enron after Enron’s stock collapse and credit concerns sharply reduced its trading activity. Reports indicated the proposed value could fall by more than 40%, from roughly $9 billion to about $5 billion, with the exchange ratio reduced from 0.2685 to below 0.15 Dynegy shares per Enron share. The talks also covered $500 million to $1 billion in additional funding and extending or refinancing Enron’s debt. No revised agreement was finalized, and litigation or Enron’s deteriorating finances could allow Dynegy to invoke a material-adverse-change clause.

Enron’s trading business remained severely constrained. Many energy companies would buy Enron’s spot gas and power but refused to sell to it because of payment risks; others traded freely or only reduced old exposures. A broker estimated over-the-counter volume at about 25% of its level a month earlier, while Enron disputed that estimate and cited $2.8 billion in 30-day rolling transaction value. Enron’s equity trading unit was reportedly being closed, with roughly 60 employees laid off.

Moody’s kept Enron at Baa3, the lowest investment-grade rating, while S&P maintained a negative credit watch and Fitch described the rating as “evolving.” Bankers seeking as much as $2 billion in financing received rejections from investors including Prince Alwaleed Bin Talal, Carlyle, and Blackstone, while J.P. Morgan and Citigroup planned to provide $250 million each. Enron shares closed at $4.14, and its bonds rebounded from 48 to about 55 cents on the dollar. Investors and arbitrageurs remained skeptical that the merger could be completed, citing liquidity risks, litigation, Enron’s trading losses, and the possibility of bankruptcy.

DLAA provides AI-based anti-aliasing using the Super Resolution technology developed for DLSS, producing higher-quality native-resolution images with greater temporal stability and detail in motion.

Blackwell was optimized for neural shaders, GPU programs that control graphics rendering. GPU shading evolved from fixed-function pipelines to programmable vertex and pixel shaders, unified and geometry shaders, tessellation and compute shaders, primitive and mesh shaders, and real-time ray tracing with dedicated RT cores. Blackwell introduces unified AI and traditional shaders, with enhanced Tensor Cores and Shader Execution Reordering 2.0 enabling concurrent neural filtering, generative AI, and other graphics models. Developer-created neural shaders may also run on prior-generation GPUs.

Neural shaders train AI models to approximate complex rendering calculations, decompress textures, predict indirect lighting, and approximate subsurface light scattering. NVIDIA and Microsoft created the Cooperative Vectors API for DX12 and Vulkan, allowing graphics shaders to access Tensor Cores. Combined with Slang, it supports neural texture compression and features such as RTX Neural Materials, Neural Radiance Cache, RTX Skin, and RTX Neural Faces.

RTX Neural Materials replaces complex mathematical material models with neural approximations, enabling layered, film-quality assets to render at game frame rates. Neural Texture Compression reduces texture storage and bandwidth requirements; one cited demo fell from 1,110 MB to 333 MB while improving visual quality. Stochastic Texture Filtering reduces aliasing and moiré patterns and supports higher-order filtering, with improved point-sampling performance on Blackwell.

Neural Radiance Cache uses small neural networks trained on live game data to infer final lighting for many ray-traced bounces after only one bounce, improving performance and indirect-lighting quality while adapting to each scene. RTX Skin applies ray-traced subsurface scattering to translucent materials. RTX Neural Faces uses a TensorRT-optimized generative AI model to transform a rasterized face and 3D pose data into a more natural face, with training based on thousands of offline images covering angles, lighting, emotion, and occlusion.

Blackwell includes three described GPU configurations. GB202 has 92.2 billion transistors, 192 streaming multiprocessors, 24,576 CUDA Cores, 192 RT Cores, and 768 Tensor Cores with a 512-bit memory interface; it powers the GeForce RTX 5090. GB203 retains key Blackwell features, including fourth-generation RT Cores, fifth-generation Tensor Cores, and DLSS 4; it has 45.6 billion transistors, 84 streaming multiprocessors, 10,752 CUDA Cores, 84 RT Cores, and 336 Tensor Cores with a 256-bit interface, and powers the RTX 5080 and RTX 5070 Ti. GB205 has 31 billion transistors, 50 streaming multiprocessors, 6,400 CUDA Cores, 50 RT Cores, and 200 Tensor Cores with a 192-bit interface, and powers the RTX 5070.

Matrimonial websites have transformed the traditional Indian arranged-marriage process by replacing brokers and personal networks with online matchmaking. They offer free dating services, extensive databases, detailed profiles, and filters for criteria such as religion, occupation, and location. Accessible through websites and mobile apps, they can save time and money while enabling direct text or video communication. Many also provide counseling, privacy options, verified profiles, and membership screening to reduce fake accounts. Users can compare diverse candidates, including non-resident Indians and people seeking second marriages, before deciding whom to meet.

Larry Connors’ %b strategy, presented in Chapter 5 of his 2009 book *High Probability Trading*, is a mean-reversion approach to trading ETFs. “%b” refers to the percentage of the Bollinger Band range; it generally fluctuates between 0 and 1 but can move outside those bounds. A buy occurs when the close is above the 200-day moving average and %b remains below 0.2 for three consecutive days. The exit signal occurs when %b closes above 0.8. Because Connors omitted the lookback and standard-deviation parameters, the tests use five days and two standard deviations.

The authors could not exactly replicate Connors’ results but found promising performance in QQQ and SPY, with relatively few trades. A 25-ETF portfolio simulation from 2000 through December 2020 recorded 677 trades, a 75% win rate, 0.76% average gain per trade, 1.9 profit factor, 4.84% CAGR, and 16% maximum drawdown. Using a 10-day lookback raised CAGR to 8.2% but increased drawdown to 24%. The strategy had not yet been tested in combination with Connors’ other strategies or optimized.

A coarse-grained rod–sphere model represents a nanosphere grafted with a crystallized polymer bundle as a spherical head tethered to a rigid five-bead rod. Three interaction schemes are studied: lock-and-key, symmetric, and unspecific. Molecular dynamics simulations vary the sphere-to-rod radius ratio \(R/r\), temperature, and interaction type to determine self-assembled mesostructures.

Mesostructures are classified using a dimensionality parameter derived from cluster gyration tensors and a degree-of-order parameter based on rod alignment. The simulations produce bulk, gel, monolayer, bilayer, ribbon, fiber, worm, star, spherical, liquid, and dispersed structures spanning zero to three dimensions. Increasing sphere size generally lowers dimensionality by geometrically frustrating growth, while temperature and interaction type influence the resulting phase. Assembly proceeds through aggregation, growth, and consolidation stages, tracked by changes in dimensionality and order.

Lock-and-key rods form bulk assemblies, bilayers, ribbons, and stars; symmetric rods can additionally form fibers and spherical clusters; unspecific rods produce structures at higher temperatures, including monolayers and worms. Straight ribbons spontaneously twist into double helices with equal left- and right-handed probability, and increasing sphere radius reduces the helix pitch. The model reproduces experimentally observed fibers and spherical clusters formed by PiPrOx-grafted silica nanoparticles and offers guidance for designing nanobuilding blocks, although it simplifies polymer crystallization, uses a higher volume fraction and longer accessible timescale than experiments, and represents only one rod per sphere.

This non-peer-reviewed preprint reports the first whole-blood transcriptome-wide comparison of 194 virally suppressed people living with HIV receiving ART and 361 HIV-1-seronegative participants. Of 20,211 genes tested, 566 were differentially expressed in the HIV group, with enrichment in immune functions and cancer-related pathways, including Wnt/β-catenin, PI3K/AKT, MAPK/ERK, p53, and TGF-β signaling. Estimated cell proportions differed by HIV status, including higher CD8+ and follicular helper T-cell proportions and lower naïve CD4+, resting CD4+ memory T-cell, and resting mast-cell proportions; dysregulation occurred across multiple innate and adaptive immune cell types.

Comparison with a pre/post-ART study classified 234 differentially expressed genes as ART-affected and 332 as ART-unaffected. Their largely opposite expression directions suggest ART shifts regulation toward the HIV-negative state without fully restoring it; dysregulation in enriched pathways could not be attributed solely to ART.

Heritability analyses found enrichment for blood-cell counts and several inflammatory diseases, but little or no enrichment for cancer or HIV-acquisition traits. eQTL mapping identified 22,475 associations involving 258 genes, with limited colocalization, although signals were observed for pancreatic cancer and lymphocytic leukemia. Drug-target searches found 111 differentially expressed genes targeted by approved or investigational compounds, including 42 targeted by approved drugs and 11 cancer-pathway genes. The findings identify possible treatment targets but require functional, cell-specific, and longitudinal validation because chronic HIV and ART effects cannot be fully separated.

Tesla, Inc.’s unaudited Form 10-Q for the quarter ended September 30, 2017 covers two operating segments: automotive and energy generation and storage. Third-quarter revenue was $2.985 billion, including $2.363 billion from automotive and $317.5 million from energy generation and storage. Gross profit was $449.1 million, compared with $636.7 million in 2016. The company reported an operating loss of $535.5 million and a net loss attributable to common stockholders of $619.4 million, versus net income of $21.9 million in the prior-year quarter. For the first nine months, revenue was $8.471 billion, compared with $4.716 billion in 2016, while the net loss attributable to common stockholders was $1.286 billion, or $7.80 per diluted share.

At September 30, 2017, Tesla reported $28.107 billion of assets, $21.929 billion of liabilities and $4.711 billion of stockholders’ equity. Cash and cash equivalents were $3.530 billion, inventory was $2.471 billion, and net property, plant and equipment was $9.394 billion. During the first nine months, operating activities used $570.5 million of cash, investing activities used $3.457 billion, and financing activities provided $4.129 billion. Purchases of property and equipment, net of sales, totaled $2.628 billion.

Tesla completed the $109.5 million cash acquisition of Grohmann, which develops automated manufacturing systems, and recorded $40.1 million of goodwill. Measurement-period adjustments were recorded for the $2.1 billion stock acquisition of SolarCity. Energy storage revenue and costs were reclassified from services and other to energy generation and storage to align with reportable segments.

Total debt principal increased to $9.992 billion, with a carrying value of $9.050 billion. During 2017, Tesla issued $977.5 million of 2.375% convertible senior notes due 2022, accompanied by note hedges and warrants, and $1.8 billion of 5.30% senior notes due 2025. The company also exchanged or converted portions of its 2018 notes and repaid or terminated several credit facilities. It reported compliance with all financial debt covenants.

Resale value guarantee vehicle sales to customers are accounted for as operating leases, while certain sales to leasing partners are treated as collateralized borrowings. The related resale value guarantee liability totaled $2.954 billion at September 30, 2017. Tesla’s maximum potential repurchase obligation under the leasing-partner program was $1.18 billion, including $263.5 million exercisable within 12 months.

The company expected to adopt the new revenue recognition standard on January 1, 2018 and estimated an equity increase of $550 million to $750 million. It planned to adopt the lease standard on January 1, 2019, recognizing right-of-use assets and liabilities for substantially all leases. Its accrued warranty reserve was $368.7 million, and gross unrecognized tax benefits were $300.0 million.

The Buffalo build-to-suit lease arrangement required approximately $5.0 billion of capital, operating and other spending in New York over ten years, specified employment and investment milestones, and potential annual program payments of $41.2 million for failure to meet those requirements. Legal proceedings included securities litigation involving SolarCity and Tesla, shareholder challenges to the SolarCity acquisition, and a suit concerning Model 3 production statements. SolarCity also reached a settlement with the United States Treasury under which it returned approximately $29.5 million, or about 5% of certain grants, without admitting wrongdoing. Tesla said it could not estimate possible losses from the pending litigation. The filing cautioned that forward-looking statements were subject to risks and uncertainties and that actual results could differ materially.

This medRxiv preprint reports a case-control study of 108 Thai-speaking Chulalongkorn University students, including 64 with simple dysmood disorder (SDMD) and 44 healthy controls; three participants were excluded after enrollment. The depressed group met DSM-5 criteria for a major depressive episode and had HAM-D scores of 7 to below 22; 47 had first-episode SDMD (FE-SDMD). Participants with metabolic syndrome, elevated suicide risk, relevant immune or neurological disorders, and pregnant or lactating women were excluded. Depression, suicidal behavior, brooding, and a composite depression phenome were assessed using HAM-D, BDI-II, C-SSRS, and the Ruminative Response Scale. Serum lipids, apolipoproteins, and derived atherogenicity and reverse-cholesterol-transport indices were measured.

Compared with controls, SDMD and FE-SDMD participants had significantly higher free cholesterol and ApoE and lower LCAT activity. HDL cholesterol, ApoA1, reverse cholesterol transport, ApoB, and triglycerides showed no substantial changes, although derived atherogenicity, Athero/LCAT, and Athero/RCT indices were higher. These abnormalities persisted among participants without subclinical metabolic syndrome. With increasing subclinical metabolic syndrome stages, HDL cholesterol, ApoA1, and reverse cholesterol transport declined, while triglycerides, ApoE, ApoB/ApoA, and Athero/RCT generally increased. Diagnosis and subclinical metabolic syndrome interacted significantly for several lipid measures.

Free cholesterol was positively associated with depression, suicidal behavior, brooding, and phenome severity, whereas LCAT was inversely associated with these outcomes. Atherogenic indices correlated with all major clinical measures. Regression models explained 19.7% of HAM-D variance using free cholesterol and LCAT and 63.3% of phenome variance using brooding, free cholesterol, and age. Partial least-squares analysis indicated that LCAT’s association with the depression phenome was indirect, operating through free cholesterol and brooding; reanalysis of recurrent-depression data indicated mediation through atherogenicity.

The authors interpret reduced LCAT and elevated free cholesterol as indicating that FE-SDMD and SDMD may be pre-proatherogenic states distinct from subclinical metabolic syndrome. They propose that impaired LCAT activity could contribute to oxidative stress, inflammation, LDL oxidation, and possible central neurodegenerative effects, and recommend lipid screening for people with FE-SDMD. Limitations include the absence of oxysterol, omega-3 fatty acid, and vitamin E measurements; LCAT polymorphisms were not assessed, and prospective studies of lipid changes across depression episodes are needed.

The speaker accepts the responsibilities of office with humility, relying on public cooperation, popular patriotism, and divine providence. He reviews the nation’s development since the Revolution, arguing that the Constitution’s compromises and balance between federal and state authority have preserved civil and religious liberty, expanded prosperity, enabled effective self-government, and survived taxation, factional conflict, war, territorial expansion, and other predicted dangers. He credits adherence to constitutional principles for the Republic’s strength and expresses confidence that citizens can preserve its institutions if they continue to uphold the Constitution and maintain the spirit of union.

On domestic slavery, he maintains that congressional abolition in the District of Columbia against the wishes of slaveholding states and interference with slavery where it exists must be resisted. He argues that the framers’ forbearance preserved national tranquility, acknowledges agitation and local violence, and urges citizens to reject efforts that might endanger the Union.

He pledges to preserve, protect, and defend the Constitution, exercise federal authority only within its limits, and carry out previously stated domestic policies. In foreign affairs, he favors friendship, equal commercial relations, openness, neutrality, and noninterference while resisting aggression against American rights. Concluding with gratitude and humility, he vows faithfully to serve the country and prays for its continued honor, prosperity, and peace.

More than 250 small earthquakes struck near the California-Mexico border since New Year’s Eve, centered beneath Brawley in the southern Brawley Seismic Zone. The strongest measured magnitude 3.9. Scientists monitored the swarm because it could trigger a magnitude-5 or larger quake, though that possibility had largely receded by Sunday night. The roughly 30-mile zone connects the San Andreas and Imperial faults, which have caused destructive earthquakes. The shaking unsettled Brawley’s 26,000 residents and reportedly frightened some dogs away.

The SEC began an informal, voluntary inquiry into Enron’s related-party transactions with partnerships managed by CFO Andrew Fastow. The request covered the LJM Cayman and LJM2 Co-Investment partnerships, which entered complex financing and hedging arrangements with Enron and generated significant profits and fees. Fastow resigned from the partnerships amid conflict-of-interest concerns. Enron said its board approved the arrangements, that auditors and attorneys reviewed them, and that they were properly disclosed; it also said related transactions were intended to hedge investments. The SEC declined to comment, and no formal investigation or allegations of wrongdoing had been announced.

Enron disclosed a $1.01 billion third-quarter write-off, producing a $618 million loss, and a separate $1.2 billion reduction in shareholder equity from repurchasing 55 million partnership-held shares. Critics said the equity reduction was inadequately disclosed in the earnings release and raised questions about asset valuations, accounting treatment, and Enron’s credibility. Analysts also warned that other off-balance-sheet financing vehicles, including the $1 billion Marlin Water Trust II and $2.4 billion Whitewing trust, could require asset sales or new Enron stock for repayment, potentially diluting shareholders if credit ratings and stock prices triggered repayment provisions.

After Enron disclosed the SEC request, its shares fell about 21% to $20.65, losing roughly $4 billion in market value and reaching a 52-week low. Investors continued to question related-party structures, possible undisclosed liabilities, and the departure of CEO Jeffrey Skilling. Moody’s placed Enron’s debt under review for a possible downgrade, although it remained investment grade.

Shareholder lawsuits alleged that Enron and its directors misrepresented its financial condition and that delayed write-downs inflated its stock. Milberg Weiss announced a class action covering purchases between January 2000 and October 2001. Enron scheduled an investor conference call and pledged to cooperate fully with the SEC.

Meanwhile, U.S. stocks rallied late in trading as bargain hunting offset weak corporate earnings and anthrax concerns. The Dow rose 1.88% to 9,377.03, and the Nasdaq gained 2.2% to about 1,708. Enron was a major exception, while semiconductor and industrial shares generally advanced. Janus Capital remained Enron’s largest institutional shareholder with 42.8 million shares, or 5.71%.

Real Madrid drew 1–1 with relegation-threatened Levante at the Bernabéu. Isco’s goal put Madrid ahead after Emmanuel Boateng equalised Sergio Ramos’ opener, but Giampaolo Pazzini scored an 89th-minute equaliser on his debut. The result left Madrid fourth, 18 points behind Barcelona, with their sixth league draw of the season.

Medium- and longer-term trends remain healthy, but short-term technicals are weakening amid a seasonal rise in volatility and credit spreads, bearish breadth divergence, and growing tech concentration. July was broadly risk-on, with equities rising, bonds falling, and frontier markets leading returns; US electricity demand also reached a record high. The page features headlines about UBS raising gold and silver forecasts, the government shutdown and delayed jobs report, AI-selected stock portfolios, and other investment articles, along with trading risk and data disclaimers.

A lecturer demonstrates three standard social-preference games with students, using candy, chocolates, apples, and small cash payments. Unlike typical private experiments, some randomly selected choices are publicly implemented, though participants are asked to choose as they ordinarily would.

In the dictator game, one participant allocates an endowment between themselves and a randomly selected receiver. The lecturer varies the stakes, communication, and publicity, including a nearly private version in which only matched participants know the outcome. Students’ allocations vary, and communication sometimes prompts greater sharing.

The ultimatum game adds strategic interaction: a proposer offers a division, and a responder accepts or rejects it; rejection means neither player receives the allocation. Students play in rotated roles, sometimes with communication, and observe how proposals and responses vary under public and private conditions.

The lecturer also explains the strategy method. Instead of implementing every game separately, students provide contingent plans specifying what they would offer as proposers and the smallest offer they would accept as responders. One selected contingency is implemented, but this approach elicits information about both roles and many possible situations while requiring only one payout.

Finally, students play the trust game. An investor sends some resources to a responder; the amount received is multiplied, and the responder returns some of it. A communication version demonstrates that expectations about the return can influence the initial investment. The lecturer closes by noting that a later class will examine the games’ interpretation, experimental rigor, and relevance to real-world behavior, and invites students to share anonymous observations or anecdotes through the class forum.

The flea flicker is a football trick play that resembles a running play. The quarterback hands the ball to a running back, who tosses it back so the quarterback can throw downfield. As defenders commit to stopping the run, receivers and tight ends release from their blocking assignments and run routes, potentially leaving an open receiver.

Illinois coach Bob Zuppke is credited with developing the play, which he said he first called in 1910 at Oak Park High School and later used against Penn in 1925 on a fake field goal. Its name comes from Zuppke’s description of “the quick flicking action of a dog getting rid of fleas,” with defenders representing the fleas. A quarterback who receives the ball back cannot intentionally ground it because he previously relinquished possession; he must throw toward an eligible receiver.

Examples include Michigan’s 2022 playoff touchdown against TCU, an Oklahoma reverse flea flicker that fooled defenders and produced an opening touchdown, and a fake flea flicker in which the running back continues up the middle after defenders expect a return pass to the quarterback.

The ADS868xW is a fully integrated, 16-bit SAR ADC data-acquisition device with a differential analog front end, programmable gain amplifier (PGA), ADC driver, precision reference buffer, internal overvoltage protection, and alarm functions. It supports single-ended and differential bipolar or unipolar inputs and straight-binary output.

Each analog input includes an internal overvoltage-protection circuit. Input resistors and gain-setting resistors limit input current, while antiparallel diodes protect internal circuitry and establish protection limits. External protection is still required for surges, ESD, and EFT. With AVDD at 5 V, the input protection limit is approximately ±20 V; with AVDD floating, the limit is approximately ±15 V. Higher source impedance reduces protection-diode current but can increase gain error and system noise. Extended operation outside rated conditions may saturate ADC outputs or damage the device.

The PGA converts input signals to drive the internal ADC, adjusts their common-mode level to maximize ADC dynamic range, and selects one of nine input ranges through RANGE_SEL[3:0]. Its default range is ±3 V × VREF. A trimmed resistor network maintains low gain error. A second-order antialiasing low-pass filter at the PGA output has a typical 500 kHz cutoff, and an integrated high-bandwidth, low-noise ADC driver supports rapid settling.

The device can use its nominal 4.096 V internal reference or a filtered external 4.096 V reference, selected with INTREF_DIS. With the internal reference, REFIO is an output and requires at least 4.7 µF of decoupling; it cannot directly drive external loads. The internal reference is factory-trimmed but can shift after soldering or repeated reflow, so the ADS868xW should be soldered during the second PCB assembly pass to reduce thermal stress. It is temperature compensated from −40°C to +125°C. In external-reference mode, REFIO is an input, the internal buffer drives REFCAP, and REFCAP requires at least 10 µF plus a nearby 1 µF decoupling capacitor. The buffer’s specified temperature drift is 0.5 ppm/°C typical and 2 ppm/°C maximum.

The full-scale range equals positive full-scale voltage minus negative full-scale voltage, and LSB size equals FSR/2^16. An active-high alarm output can monitor input voltage against programmable high and low thresholds with programmable hysteresis. A separate AVDD alarm trips below the typical 4.7 V low threshold or above the 5.3 V high threshold. Active alarm flags clear after each conversion, while tripped flags remain set until ALARM_REG is read. Alarm status can be accessed through the ALARM pin, ALARM_REG, or output data flags.

The multiSPI interface uses shift registers, configuration registers, and a protocol unit. It supports four legacy SPI-compatible modes, single- or dual-SDO output, and source-synchronous operation using an external or internal clock, with RVS providing the synchronous output clock. A standard-SPI connection uses CONVST/CS, SCLK, SDI, and SDO-0. In a daisy chain, devices share CONVST/CS and SCLK and are linked through SDO-0 and SDI; an optimal frame requires 32 × N SCLK capture edges for N devices, and data return in reverse device order.

The device operates in RESET, ACQ, and CONV states. The active-low RST input can initiate either an application reset of configuration registers or a power-on reset of all internal circuitry. After reset, the device enters ACQ. A rising CONVST/CS edge starts conversion, during which further transitions are ignored until conversion completes and the device returns to ACQ. The host can detect completion through RVS or by waiting the specified maximum conversion time.

Programming uses nine configuration registers and supports read and write operations. A transfer frame begins when CONVST/CS falls, loads the output shift register, and shifts data on SCLK; the command is decoded when CONVST/CS rises. Exactly 32 clocks provide a standard valid command frame, short frames permit partial output reads but invalidate writes, and in long frames the final 32 shifted bits form the command. Output data can contain a fixed test pattern, register-read data, the latest 16-bit conversion result, and optional device-address, input-range, AVDD-alarm, input-alarm, and parity flags. The registers include DEVICE_ID_REG at 00h, RST_PWRCTL_REG at 04h, SDI_CTL_REG at 08h, SDO_CTL_REG at 0Ch, DATAOUT_CTL_REG at 10h, RANGE_SEL_REG at 14h, ALARM_REG at 20h, ALARM_H_TH_REG at 24h, and ALARM_L_TH_REG at 28h. Writes to protected RST_PWRCTL_REG fields require first writing 69h to address 05h.

An eight-channel industrial input-module design combines the ADS8681W with the MUX36D08 differential multiplexer. It supports configurable voltage or current channels for bipolar and unipolar industrial ranges, including ±2.5 V, ±5 V, ±10 V, 0–5 V, 0–10 V, 4–20 mA, and 0–20 mA. The ADS8681W settles to 1% accuracy in under 5 µs and supports an NTC-thermistor temperature-measurement example using programmable alarm thresholds and hysteresis to avoid false triggering.

AVDD and DVDD are separate analog and digital supplies. Supply decoupling, analog/digital PCB partitioning, short ground paths, and placement of bypass capacitors without intervening vias are recommended. NAP mode reduces power while awaiting conversion, and power-down mode disables analog blocks while retaining register contents and keeping the interface active. Internal-reference layouts require at least 4.7 µF at REFIO; external-reference layouts require 1 µF and 10 µF capacitors at REFCAP, with the 10 µF capacitor having ESR below 0.2 Ω.

The lecture examines elimination for sparse systems \(Ax=b\), focusing on how pivot and unknown orderings affect fill-in—the creation of nonzero entries from initially zero positions. Compatible permutations of equations and unknowns can produce substantially different amounts of fill-in.

The nonzero structure can be represented as an undirected graph whose nodes correspond to matrix rows and whose edges correspond to nonzero entries. Eliminating a pivot removes its incident edges and creates edges between pairs of previously connected nodes, so choosing an effective elimination order is central to controlling fill-in. Bandwidth alone is not always a reliable criterion: a large-bandwidth, well-separated block ordering can avoid fill-in, while a smaller-bandwidth ordering may create it. Red-black, or checkerboard, ordering is introduced as a straightforward heuristic.

Minimum degree ordering is a greedy method that selects the lowest-degree node as the next pivot. Approximate minimum degree (AMD) is widely used and, according to the lecture, is often superior to perfect minimum degree. The graph is used only to determine the ordering; a subsequent numerical pass computes elimination multipliers and the \(L\) and \(U\) factors. For symmetric positive-definite matrices, Cholesky factorization can be used. MATLAB’s `nnz` command can count nonzeros in the factors to measure fill-in.

Graph separators divide a graph into two otherwise unconnected groups. Ordering separator nodes last preserves large zero blocks, although the separator block becomes relatively dense and dominates the work. Recursively applying this process produces nested dissection. Separator algorithms seek small, nearly balanced divisions; the approach may be particularly useful for three-dimensional or very large problems, while AMD is effective for many two-dimensional sparse matrices. Their performance can be compared by asymptotic growth in fill-in and operation counts.

The D.C. Circuit held that the Federal Mine Safety and Health Review Commission had jurisdiction to review an Administrative Law Judge’s Equal Access to Justice Act award but erred in finding the Secretary of Labor’s position substantially justified. CSG had prevailed over Mine Safety and Health Administration citations alleging improper electrical grounding at its crushing plant. The governing regulation required grounding but did not prohibit using equipment frames as grounding conductors or require “fourth-wire” grounding. MSHA conducted no compliance testing, and the Secretary presented no evidence that CSG’s motors were not grounded or otherwise violated the regulation. The court concluded that safety concerns could not justify enforcing requirements absent from the regulations and that the Secretary should seek rulemaking if it wished to prohibit frame grounding. It reversed the Commission, restored the ALJ’s award, and remanded to determine appellate costs.

Starting early gives investments more time to grow and helps establish lifelong saving habits. Investing €50 monthly from age 20 at 5% annual returns could accumulate €75,000 by 60, whereas starting at 40 would require €185 monthly for the same result. The essay examines why philosophy of education is often treated as peripheral to educational research. Standard research texts foreground empirical quantitative and qualitative methods while separating theoretical, ethical, and normative concerns from research itself. Students may therefore question philosophy’s status as research, while colleagues may mistakenly equate it with qualitative research. Economic insecurity, scarce academic positions, publication metrics, grants, and funding criteria further make philosophy appear inessential, impractical, or lacking demonstrable impact. Scientistic accounts also privilege large-scale quantitative evidence as generalizable and predictive, overlooking the limits of experimental generalization, local educational concerns, and ethical questions about what “working” interventions should mean.

Proposed responses include teaching students to critically examine evidence, generalizability, and impact; appealing to their values; defending philosophy against empirical research; and recognizing its intellectual and community value. Yet the field remains internally contested over its identity, traditions, origins, methods, relevance, and future, including whether students should pursue it when employment prospects are limited. Historically, philosophy of education has repeatedly faced criticism as irrelevant, low-quality, or impractical amid changing social and political-economic conditions.

The author proposes an external, long-term historical perspective and rejects both nostalgic accounts of the field’s “golden years” and portrayals of today’s precarity as uniquely exceptional, describing them as partial and self-serving. Instead, philosophy of education should be understood as a site of philosophical, theoretical, and conceptual pluralism and community-based deliberation. Its internal disagreements can foster reflexivity, responsiveness, self-scrutiny, and criticality, supporting more creative and critical collaboration with students and colleagues. A starting point is challenging the assumption that educational research must be empirical.

Researchers at ETH Zurich found that cancer cells transfer mitochondria through threadlike nanotubes into neighboring fibroblasts. Within 24 hours, the fibroblasts grew faster and increased cancer-related gene activity; when injected with cancer cells into mouse ears, they promoted tumor formation. The protein MIRO2 was required for this transfer. The findings indicate that tumors can reprogram surrounding cells to support cancer, though the driving forces, triggers, and mechanisms remain unknown. Researchers identified MIRO2 as a possible therapeutic target while noting that the work is still early.

The president describes the public inauguration as a mutual covenant in which the people pledge support for the Constitution, the Union, the laws, and equal civil and political rights. He invokes divine favor and marks the Constitution’s centennial, contrasting the nation’s present strength and prosperity with its weak beginnings under Washington and his associates.

He attributes national growth to territorial expansion, population and wealth, improved material conditions, broader public education, and strengthened religious, charitable, and temperance influences. He acknowledges that prosperity remains uneven and that many citizens are neither prosperous nor law-abiding.

Calling protective tariffs a revival of earlier support for national independence, he argues that domestic manufacturing, mining, and commerce should promote a more perfect union. Slavery had made tariff policy sectional by preventing Southern cotton and mineral interests from developing alongside Northern industries; its abolition has removed that obstacle. He urges Southern industrial and political leaders to cooperate with Black workers and defend free elections, while rejecting special executive policies for any section. Federal laws must be administered uniformly and obeyed equally, and corporations and communities must respect legal limits.

He calls for stricter naturalization examinations to ensure that applicants possess good character and understand their civic duties, while maintaining hospitality to immigration. In foreign affairs, he supports peaceful arbitration, friendly relations with European powers, and noncoercive protection of American citizens and commercial rights abroad. He opposes European control of a canal linking the Atlantic and Pacific coasts and rejects European colonial dependencies in the independent American states.

On appointments, he urges careful, responsible advice, efficient public service, full enforcement of civil-service laws, and reform toward a less partisan civil service. He identifies Treasury surpluses as wasteful, calls for economy and sufficient revenue, and supports applying small surpluses to the public debt without weakening the protective tariff. He also urges modern warships, American steamship lines, more adequate pensions for Union veterans and their families, and the admission of Dakota, Montana, and Washington as states with prompt land-title confirmation.

Finally, he supports stronger, impartial election safeguards to protect the ballot, responding to electoral ignorance with lawful education rather than repression. He calls for patriotism, fraternity, justice, and respectful acceptance of electoral outcomes, expressing confidence in the nation’s future while insisting that power be guided by justice and mercy and that opportunity remain open to all citizens.

The paper proposes a global, regulator-reported database for significant AI-related incidents in financial markets, addressing gaps in current oversight as AI adoption, algorithmic opacity, market manipulation, and systemic risks increase. Existing databases rely largely on crowdsourcing and news scraping and omit confidential incidents; a search since 2010 identified 20 AI-driven algorithmic-trading cases on regulatory websites that were absent from four major incident databases. Confidential reporting, withholding for market stability and intellectual-property protection, and finance-specific data requirements create structural information gaps.

Drawing on healthcare and aviation reporting practices, the framework combines confidential incident submission, standardized documentation, “black box” style retrospective analysis, and reporting of near misses. Adapted from MiFID II, it includes 15 mandatory fields covering market context, percentage-based volume and price metrics, AI system types, incident patterns, human oversight, and safety mechanisms. It reports AI-driven trades causing more than a 5% price deviation or a 20% volume anomaly against the 30-day average. Timestamps and execution dates are deliberately omitted to protect proprietary information and prevent firm identification while supporting cross-border analysis.

Using 2,999 synthetic records generated from the 20 identified incidents, the paper tests the framework for systemic-risk monitoring and manipulation detection. An ANOVA analysis found AI system type more influential than geography and little regional variation, while the model identified systematic risk patterns with 92% precision. K-means clustering and PCA identified five trading zones associated with stable, anomalous, transitional, irregular, and strategic trading, capturing 68% of variance and supporting detection of spoofing, momentum ignition, layering, and cross-market manipulation.

The paper acknowledges inconsistent institutional reporting, the limited realism of synthetic data, reliance on English-language sources, and the effect of omitting temporal data on Granger causality analysis. It calls for an intergovernmental database and coordinated global oversight to improve transparency, accountability, market stability, and public trust.

## Summary

This passage is an excerpt from the SEV-ES Guest-Hypervisor Communication Block (GHCB) specification, documenting Version 2 changes, protocol definitions, non-automatic exit (NAE) events, and host-notification design.

**Version 2 changes:** Version 2 adds enhancements and additions to SEV-ES support plus initial SEV-SNP support, and introduces hypervisor feature advertisement, allowing a hypervisor to advertise SEV-ES/SEV-SNP support so future enhancements can be supported without all prior features (a minimum feature set remains mandatory). It also adds the XSS MSR value when CPUID 0xd is requested, requires the GHCB SW_SCRATCH shared area to reside in the GHCB, and adds restricted APIC emulation (IPI and timer support).

**Revisions:** 2.01 updates the Secrets Page Guest Reserved Area for 32-bit→64-bit guest request message sequence numbers. 2.02 adds the VLEK GUID, documents a VMGEXIT error code for invalid/malformed GHCB input, and expands SNP Guest Request/Extended Guest Request to return error codes in the upper 32 bits of SW_EXITINFO2. 2.03 adds guest APIC ID list retrieval, multiple VMPL levels, a new GHCB MSR protocol function, two new GHCB NAE events, SEV-ES page state change notification, and the Confidential Computing Blob EFI protocol. 2.04 adds SEV-TIO (trusted PCIe passthrough with TDISP), Secure AVIC (initial support for the vCPU Secure AVIC backing page), another GHCB MSR protocol function, and documentation changes for debug support, unsupported GHCB function behavior, and GUID formats.

**Feature advertisement:** Support is mandatory unless identified as optional via a FEATURES bitmap, limited to 52 bits and requestable by the guest. Bits cover base SNP support, SNP guest AP VMSA creation, restricted injection (and timer), APIC ID list retrieval, running vCPUs at different VMPL levels, SEV-ES page state change, SNP trusted IO, and unregistering a GHCB GPA. Some features have dependencies.

**GHCB mechanics:** The guest specifies the GHCB location; the hypervisor learns it via decrypted/shared mapping, with hardware saving/restoring the GPA in VMCB offset 0xa0. The guest accesses it via MSR 0xc001_0130, which the hypervisor must not intercept; the GHCB must be 4K-aligned, and the lower 12 bits carry GHCBInfo requests/responses (SEV Information 0x001, CPUID request 0x004, preferred GHCB GPA 0x010, register GHCB GPA 0x012, unregister 0x018, termination). Documented fields include maximum/minimum GHCB protocol version and the SEV page table encryption bit number (obtainable from CPUID 0x8000001f EBX[5:0]). GHCB GPA registration is required for SNP guests, with get-preferred/register actions, automatic unregistering of prior registrations, guest termination on GPA mismatch, and per-VMPL registration under Multi-VMPL. Negotiation examples are given for both SEV-ES and SEV-SNP guests.

**Secrets page and EFI:** The Secrets Page Guest Reserved Area holds VMPL0–3 current guest message sequence numbers (low and high 32 bits), the AP jump table physical address, and a guest usage area; the EFI SEV-SNP Confidential Computing Blob configuration table GUID and format are documented.

**NAE events:** All non-AE exits raise #VC with error code equal to the VMEXIT code; the guest copies register state into the GHCB and issues VMGEXIT. Both sides manage the VALID_BITMAP (guest sets at least SW_EXITCODE, SW_EXITINFO1, SW_EXITINFO2; hypervisor sets SW_EXITINFO1/2), with bit positions computed from field offsets. Non-zero SW_EXITINFO1[31:0] signals an error, including hypervisor-requested exception injection (EVENTINJ) and codes for malformed input, unregistered GHCB, invalid SW_SCRATCH, unmarked required inputs, and invalid NAE input. Events described include IOIO_PROT, MSR_PROT, VMMCALL, #NPF/MMIO (using the RESERVED buffer at offset 0x800 with SW_SCRATCH), Page State Change (PSMASH/UNSMASH hints, resumable via cur_entry, defined reason codes), SNP Guest Request (rate limiting, RMPUPDATE/reclaim of response page), SNP Extended Guest Request (certificates by GUID, VCEK and VLEK), AP Creation (RMPADJUST/VMSA create or destroy), #HV doorbell page (GET_PREFERRED, SET, QUERY, CLEAR), #HV Send IPI, #HV Timer (SET/GET), APIC ID List, SNP Run VMPL, SNP TIO Guest Request (guest PCI ID, MMIO range, TDISP status, measurements nonce), Secure AVIC backing page registration/unregistration, Termination Request, and an Unsupported Event exit code for out-of-version NAEs.

**Guest identification and AP booting:** SEV-ES guests are identified via hypervisor-provided CPUID properties (ECX[31], EAX[1], EBX[5:0] encryption bit, EBX[11:6] address-space reduction). Because measured/encrypted registers cannot be updated, AP booting requires new mechanisms: the AP Reset Hold NAE/MSR protocol, an AP jump table (4K, encrypted, aligned, one only, with SET/GET actions and serialization), and the SNP AP Creation feature; hotplug is unsupported without AP creation but supported with it.

**Other:** For NMIs the hypervisor must not intercept IRET but must intercept #DB, with the guest sending an "NMI Complete" message. Hardware debug register virtualization is enabled by the "DebugVirtualization" bit in SEV_FEATURES, otherwise DR7 reads/writes are intercepted and cached. SMM and nested virtualization are not supported.

**#HV host notification (Restricted Injection):** The doorbell page is host-owned (not RMPUPDATE) and accessed with C=0; it defines PendingEvent (bytes 0–1) and NoEoiRequired (byte 2), with bytes 3–63 reserved. PendingEvent bits cover NoFurtherSignal, reserved bits, #MC, NMI, and an 8-bit interrupt vector. Because #HV ignores interrupt shadows, a convention is defined: guests execute HLT with interrupts disabled without checking pending state, the host re-enters the guest if events are pending, and the guest checks interrupt state on resume. The host must emulate APIC ready/acknowledge/in-service/EOI semantics, present the highest-priority ready interrupt, record the last presented vector, and manage NoEoiRequired. The guest must atomically exchange PendingEvent with zero before acting on a vector, validate observed vectors, and complete EOI either by clearing NoEoiRequired atomically or writing the x2APIC EOI MSR via VMGEXIT; it must also handle non-maskable events when EFLAGS.IF=0 and treat an unexpected #HV as grounds for a panic. Pseudocode for host and guest behavior is included.

Sweden’s unemployment rate remained 7.3% in July 2017, but unemployment was 21.8% among foreign-born job seekers versus 3.9% among those born in Sweden. Derivative trading involves buying and selling contracts whose value derives from an underlying asset, such as a commodity, stock, currency, index, or interest rate. Major types include futures, forwards, options, swaps, and CFDs. Futures are standardized exchange-traded contracts obligating parties to buy or sell an asset at a predetermined future price, while forwards are privately agreed contracts settled on a specified date. Options give holders the right, but not the obligation, to buy or sell an asset at a set strike price before expiration. Swaps exchange cash flows, while CFDs pay the difference between an asset’s opening and closing prices.

Derivatives can hedge against price movements, enable speculation, provide access to otherwise difficult markets, and transfer risk from risk-averse parties to risk seekers. For example, farmers can use wheat futures to secure a sale price, and investors can use index put options to protect portfolios from declines. Retail and some institutional traders also use derivatives to seek profits.

Trading carries substantial risks, including leverage, market and cognitive biases, poorly structured products, and greater risk in over-the-counter markets. Consistent profitability is considered unlikely, and derivatives trading is described as zero-sum.

The passage discusses futures-, options-, and general-market strategies. Options strategies may involve trading multiple contracts, including spreads and buying calls based on expected price increases. It emphasizes using a specific, backtested plan, conservative leverage, a margin of safety, and understanding the instruments before trading. A put-selling backtest is cited as producing slightly higher returns and lower volatility than the S&P 500, though historical results do not guarantee future performance.

The study addresses standardizing high-volume, noisy point-of-sale transactions by matching transaction text and zipcodes to merchant IDs and enriching records with merchant details. Existing regex rules cover about 1,000 merchants, while Enhanced String Distance handles fewer than 20% of transactions, leaving many transactions unprocessed and generating substantial inquiry costs.

JPMorgan compared pretrained Llama3-8B, Flan-T5, and SentenceBERT with small proprietary encoder-only, decoder-only, and encoder-decoder Transformer models. Out-of-the-box pretrained models performed poorly on the specialized task. Fine-tuning improved Llama3 by 9% and Flan-T5 by 13%, while SentenceBERT declined by 4%. Proprietary models achieved comparable or better accuracy with far fewer parameters: the 1.7-million-parameter decoder-only model achieved 72.07% accuracy versus Llama3’s 72.89%, while proprietary encoder-decoder and encoder-only models outperformed Flan-T5 and SentenceBERT, respectively.

The experiments showed that larger models and vocabularies were not always better. Performance depended on architecture, tokenizer, vocabulary size, embedding width, and depth. Decoder-only and encoder-decoder models generally outperformed encoder-only models; the decoder-only model provided the best overall accuracy, while the encoder-decoder model offered faster inference. Proprietary models also trained and ran more quickly and at lower cost than the pretrained LLMs.

For deployment, the proprietary decoder-only model was added to process previously unmanageable raw transactions after rule-based and string-distance matching. It generated merchant names and confidence scores for Lucene matching, with filters and monthly manual review used to limit incorrect predictions. The model accurately processed 72% of previously unhandled transactions, increasing overall transaction coverage from 80% to 94% and producing estimated annual savings of approximately $13.2 million.

The Federal Reserve raised its benchmark interest rate by a quarter point to 1%–1.25%, its third increase in six months, citing a slow-growing but durable economy. It also plans to gradually shrink its $4.5 trillion bond portfolio by allowing some securities to mature without replacement, potentially raising long-term rates. This literature review examines chess—described as a strategy game that first appeared in India roughly 1,500 years ago, possibly invented at a king's request to sharpen children's thinking and battlefield skills—and its relationship to education. Researchers variously call it the "king of board games" and the "game of kings," stressing tactical skill, decision-making, creativity, logic, and knowledge of how to finish a game. Some liken chess to life itself (rules must be kept as promises) or to *Drosophila*, because both permit fast, inexpensive research with large samples.

**Advantages cited.** Chess is said to prevent bad habits, build critical thinking and planning skills through plan–test–evaluate cycles, strengthen concentration and self-control, foster analytical and mathematical reasoning, reveal individual differences in cognitive processing, build self-confidence and character, teach persistence and sportsmanship, encourage research rather than rote memorization, develop latent skills unavailable through traditional teaching, and support socialisation and friendship across ages, races, and genders. It also develops observation, awareness, patience, creativity, perseverance, and respect for others.

**Why it may aid education.** Chess trains students to see alternatives, weigh consequences, and use many intellectual skills simultaneously while receiving immediate feedback on each move, which enriches learning and expands thinking beyond habitual patterns. Because mental schemas change more readily in childhood, early chess training appears more effective than later training. Transfer of chess-based problem-solving and reasoning to academic work is described as limited and in need of study. Chess-playing students reportedly adapt better to school, show more optimistic attitudes, greater confidence, and better academic achievement than peers drawn to sports.

**Expertise and learning.** Horgan and Morgan's stages run from novice (recognising facts) through advanced beginner, competence, proficiency, and expertise (automatic operation), with mastery requiring accumulated knowledge, experience, analytical thinking, and constant practice. Sources disagree on whether long practice alone explains expertise, since experience alone does not determine ability. Children reportedly learn chess more easily than adults because their schemas adapt faster, they tolerate mistakes thanks to immediate feedback, and they calibrate self-evaluation more easily; entertainment and motivation also matter. Because most players are children who often quit after early failures, research samples are narrowed.

**Mathematics and reading.** Chess success correlates with mathematical achievement, numerical pattern recognition, and calculation, since both require anticipating steps, questioning decisions, and evaluating alternatives; chess training has been shown to substitute for mathematics instruction hours for special-education students. Chess also improves reading through visualisation, though this link is partly speculative. It benefits gifted students and those with learning disabilities or hyperactivity.

**Caveats and objections.** Some studies find no relationship between chess and academic achievement, and the Pygmalion effect—results reflecting special teacher attention rather than chess itself—may explain reported gains. Intelligence and chess show no strong correlation, and one study found intelligence to have a nearly negative impact; effects depend on multiple interacting factors that are hard to measure. Some argue chess may limit students' time for other activities and that compulsory training harms motivation.

**Research gaps.** A meta-analysis of 24 studies (Sala & Gobet, 2016) found chess improves mathematics, reading, and cognitive skills, with stronger effects in mathematics, but the average effect size of .338 falls short of expectations, most studies lacked active control groups, and none used fully random assignment or ideal pre/post-test designs. Researchers recommend more rigorous, longitudinal, and mixed-method studies, structural equation modelling, attention to the Pygmalion effect, and investigation of meta-cognitive, motivational, and practice-related factors. Meanwhile, classroom implementation is recommended, beginning around ages four to five, with chess offered as an extracurricular activity, optional course alongside mathematics and geometry, competitive tournament, and rehabilitation tool.

The Horns offense uses a 1-4 high alignment with two high-post screeners to expand basic mid-screen and roll action. It gives the ballhandler screens in both directions, limits baseline help, creates kick-out opportunities, and is designed to work against pressure defenses. The primary ballhandler can turn the corner, pull up, return the ball to a cutting screener, or kick out to a spot-up shooter. If the initial action does not produce a shot, the offense reverses the ball through a side screen and looks to feed the low post.

Execution and coordination are central to the offense. Ballhandlers and screeners must use proper footwork, timing, and nonverbal communication while recognizing defensive responses. Counters include driving when a defender chases over, kicking out against help, pulling up when the defense goes under, and feeding the screener after a switch. Additional responses include slipping against anticipated switches, stringing out show-and-recover defenders for rolls or pops, driving opposite an early cheat, back-cutting for a lob when a post is overplayed, and spreading a trap with a dribble or sharp passes.

Variations adapt the Horns concept to different personnel through actions such as Loop, Base Split, Picked Fence, Twin Sides, High Post Rub, Flex, Motion, and Hand Back Lob. Installation emphasizes whole-part-whole teaching, two-player entries, 3-on-3 double-high-post drills, half- and full-court scrimmages, and individual skill development.

Game strategy includes scouting opponents, understanding their expected reads and counters, observing defensive adjustments, varying alignments and entries, moving players against weaker defenders, and avoiding reliance on a single set. The passage also emphasizes preparing to defend the Horns offense because of its widespread use.

The passage describes NVIDIA's Blackwell GPU architecture and related technologies, concluding with specifications and legal disclaimers.

**Power efficiency:** Accelerated frequency switching lets the GPU reach full performance within a given power budget and save power during idle gaps between work chunks, freeing it to burst to higher clocks. Blackwell's low-latency sleep states enter faster, allowing more time power gated and progressive power gating; the deepest sleep state is 10x faster to enter than Ada. Combining Blackwell performance, lower transitional power states, and faster sleep yields up to 50% power savings in a real-life example running inference on small language models.

**DLSS 4:** A suite of neural rendering technologies using AI to boost FPS, reduce latency, and improve image quality, powered by GeForce RTX 50 Series GPUs, fifth-generation Tensor Cores, and an NVIDIA cloud AI supercomputer. Multi Frame Generation (MFG), new in DLSS 4, generates up to three additional frames per traditionally rendered frame; the new frame generation AI model is 40% faster than the prior method, uses 30% less VRAM, and runs once per rendered frame, with AI replacing hardware optical flow. Frame pacing shifts from CPU-based (DLSS 3) to enhanced Flip Metering in the Blackwell display engine, which has twice the pixel processing capability for higher resolutions and refresh rates.

**Transformer models:** For the first time since DLSS 2, DLSS moves to a transformer-based neural network architecture instead of CNNs, using self-attention to identify long-range patterns and ingesting 2x more parameters. This improves Super Resolution (temporal stability, less ghosting, more detail in motion, better anti-aliasing), Ray Reconstruction (larger quality uplift, especially in challenging lighting; fewer denoiser artifacts), and DLAA (higher quality at native resolution).

**Neural shaders:** Blackwell is positioned for developer-created neural shaders, where developers train AI models to approximate shader computations. NVIDIA's new Cooperative Vectors API for DX12 and Vulkan (built with Microsoft) plus Slang lets any shader type access Tensor Cores, enabling neural texture compression (up to 7:1 VRAM compression; a demo dropped from 1110 MB to 333 MB), RTX Neural Materials, Neural Radiance Cache (neural shader inferring lighting bounces from path-traced rays, trained on live game data), RTX Skin (first ray-traced subsurface scattering in games), and RTX Neural Faces (real-time generative AI inferring faces from a rasterized face and 3D pose data, TensorRT optimized). The passage also reviews the evolution of shaders from fixed-function pipelines through programmable vertex/fragment/geometry, tessellation, compute, primitive/mesh shaders, and RTX to Blackwell neural shaders.

**GPU families:** GB202 (flagship) has 92.2 billion transistors, 12 GPCs, 192 SMs, 24,576 CUDA Cores, 192 RT Cores, 768 Tensor Cores, 768 Texture Units, 192 ROPS, 512-bit memory; GB203 (high-end) has 45.6 billion transistors, 84 SMs, 10,752 CUDA Cores, 84 RT Cores, 336 Tensor Cores, 336 Texture Units, 112 ROPS, 256-bit memory; GB205 (entry) has 31 billion transistors, 50 SMs, 6,400 CUDA Cores, 50 RT Cores, 200 Tensor Cores, 200 Texture Units, 80 ROPS, 192-bit memory. Launch products include the GeForce RTX 5090 (GB202), RTX 5080 and RTX 5070 Ti (GB203), and RTX 5070 (GB205), with comparisons to prior-generation cards.

The passage closes with NVIDIA's standard specification disclaimer (no warranties, liability limits, suitability exclusions for medical/military/aerospace/life-support use, customer responsibility for testing and product design, and no patent or IP licenses granted) and trademark/copyright notices (© 2025 NVIDIA Corporation).

California’s 2016 Gun Violence Restraining Order law allows law enforcement, relatives, or household members to ask a judge to temporarily remove a dangerous person’s weapons after other measures have failed. AMD’s Seamless Firmware Servicing (SFS) provides secure, nonpersistent runtime updates to selected AMD firmware components without reflashing the BIOS or resetting the system. It targets high-priority runtime concerns and can improve stability, mitigate selected security issues, and reduce unplanned maintenance. SFS excludes x86 components such as SMM, AGESA, and UEFI, as well as run-once code such as the AGESA boot loader. Updates are lost after reboot and are intended as interim fixes between BIOS releases.

SFS packages target a specific PI release, base patch level, firmware level, and operational state. They use monotonically increasing SFS Patch Levels, component-specific firmware and Security Patch Levels, and a System Patch Level tracking run-once code executed since the last reboot. The host OS can query these version levels. Customers are responsible for testing patches and operating an SFS Deployment Agent that communicates with AMD’s PSP/ASP to apply and track updates.

AMD cryptographically signs every package, and customers may optionally co-sign packages to retain update authority. The ASP verifies required AMD and customer signatures before loading and executing a patch. Co-signing requires an RSA public key supplied during early boot, before SMM setup is finalized. BIOS support is disabled by default and must be explicitly enabled, with co-signing separately configurable.

Runtime updates may be applied during OS boot or system operation, must be reapplied after reboots, and are installed sequentially. In multi-socket systems, patches are applied to the local socket and, when required, additional sockets. Packages validate dependencies before execution and should not apply if any portion fails. The ASP protects the update memory, verifies signatures, executes the patch, updates version information, and returns status. SFS supports querying firmware versions and applying packages through aligned command buffers and the PSP/ASP interface. Package design aims to minimize performance impact, though some SEV updates require affected virtual machines to stop and restart.
