The study documents a systematic “Voice Reasoning Gap” (VRG): current voice-interactive models perform substantially worse than text models on the same reasoning tasks, with degradation increasing as tasks require more complex, multi-step reasoning. For example, GPT-realtime scores 6.1% on VERA math questions versus 74.8% for GPT-5. The authors hypothesize that the gap arises from a conflict between irreversible, low-latency audio generation and the iterative, revisable computation required for complex reasoning, rather than from poor audio perception alone.

The paper introduces VERA, a benchmark combining multi-step general-purpose reasoning, explicit real-time constraints, and direct text-versus-voice comparisons on identical tasks. VERA contains 2,931 voice-optimized episodes across five tracks: 115 competition math problems from AIME, 1,107 web-research questions from BrowseComp, 161 graduate science questions from GPQA Diamond, 548 long-context tasks from MRCR, and 1,000 factual questions from SimpleQA. A reproducible adaptation pipeline filters, rewrites, validates, and synthesizes these episodes with varied speech timbre, tone, and emotion. Outputs are graded by a majority vote from three GPT-4o judgments over normalized ASR transcripts; human evaluation showed 97.8% agreement with GPT-4o.

Across the evaluated voice systems, average accuracy was 40.4 percentage points below the GPT-5 low-effort text baseline. The gap was moderate for retrieval and short-answer tasks but severe for multistep reasoning: GPT-realtime scored 27.4% on factual questions but 6.1% on math, while several voice models scored near zero on math despite achieving much higher context or retrieval accuracy. Architectural diversity produced only marginal differences relative to the much larger modality gap.

Diagnostic experiments indicate that neither additional thinking time, higher speech fidelity, nor simple architectural decoupling eliminates the VRG. Models responding within 1.5 seconds plateaued around 10% accuracy, while approaching text-level accuracy required sacrificing real-time interaction. Audio Flamingo 3’s thinking mode increased latency by 530% while slightly reducing accuracy. The GPT-5-based LiveAnswer cascade improved average accuracy but retained a 15.7-point math gap, achieved only 0.2% on context tasks, and averaged 10.5 seconds to first response; narration introduced grounding and consistency errors. Across a wide range of word error rates, reasoning remained uniformly poor, suggesting speech clarity was not the primary bottleneck.

Failure patterns also differed by architecture. Native streaming systems tended to produce fluent but incorrect continuations, cascades showed unsupported facts, off-target responses, and logical contradictions, and end-to-end systems ranged from strong completion bias to task abandonment. Because the study evaluates heterogeneous systems rather than isolating modality in a controlled experiment, it presents the VRG as a recurring architectural pattern rather than proof of causation. The authors conclude that closing the gap likely requires architectures that separate reasoning from speech through editable internal states, asynchronous or parallel processing, and selective verbalization while preserving consistency across reasoning and narration stages.

Reuters interviews with ARSA fighters and Rohingya refugees portray the group as a loosely organized, poorly equipped insurgency. Following attacks on dozens of Myanmar police posts on August 25, 2017, fighters said they received little training, had limited contact with commanders, and were promised AK-47 rifles but often fought with knives, sticks, and ineffective homemade explosives. Recruitment and coordination relied heavily on WhatsApp groups, including some administered overseas.

ARSA says it is fighting for Rohingya rights, while Myanmar characterizes it as an Islamist movement seeking an Islamic republic. Myanmar also alleges that ARSA killed Muslims who cooperated with authorities and that religious scholars helped recruit members; ARSA denies killing civilians.

More than half a million Rohingya fled to Bangladesh during a Myanmar military counteroffensive that the UN labeled ethnic cleansing. Fighters expressed continued determination to resist despite heavy losses and the dispersal of their ranks. Refugee opinion was divided: some supported ARSA and raised funds for it, arguing Myanmar planned further violence, while others condemned the attacks and said they had already lost everything.

Analysts said the community’s desperation could fuel further militancy and attract transnational Islamist groups, which could exploit conditions in refugee camps to radicalize residents. Al Qaeda also called for support for the Rohingya.

Seattle beat San Francisco 25-23 in the regular-season finale, rallying from an 11-point deficit after coach Pete Carroll pulled quarterback Russell Wilson and other key players in the fourth quarter. Wilson threw for 258 yards and a touchdown, while Trevone Boykin helped seal the win. The loss left the 49ers 2-14 and matched their franchise record for losses in a season. Afterward, San Francisco fired coach Chip Kelly and general manager Trent Baalke. The 10-5-1 Seahawks finished as the NFC’s third seed and will host Detroit in the playoffs.

An October 25, 2001 email forwarded a compilation of news coverage about Enron. Most reports said Enron replaced CFO Andrew Fastow with Jeff McMahon, the head of its Industrial Markets group and a former treasurer, and placed Fastow on leave. Chairman and CEO Kenneth Lay said the change was necessary to restore investor confidence after an unsuccessful analyst conference call and a sharp decline in Enron’s shares.

The move followed an informal SEC inquiry into transactions involving the LJM Cayman and LJM2 partnerships, which Fastow had managed and from which he had severed ties amid conflict-of-interest concerns. Enron had ended its relationships with the partnerships, recorded a $35 million loss and a $1.2 billion reduction in shareholder equity, and reported a $618 million third-quarter loss after $1.01 billion in write-offs. Analysts questioned Enron’s disclosure of complex off-balance-sheet arrangements and raised concerns about possible additional liabilities, asset sales, equity dilution and credit downgrades. Enron denied wrongdoing.

Enron shares closed at $16.41, down $3.38 or 17 percent on the day, traded as low as $15.51, and had lost roughly half their value since October 16. Other energy traders also fell. Analysts issued downgrades and a sell recommendation, though some viewed Fastow’s removal as a positive step that might not resolve concerns about transparency. Shareholder lawsuits alleged overvalued assets, concealed related-party dealings and insider trading, while Moody’s placed Enron’s long-term debt on watch for a possible downgrade. The compilation also included brief coverage of small-cap stocks, proposed corporate-director ratings, European and U.S. markets, and utility earnings.

President Donald Trump’s nomination of White House physician Ronny Jackson to lead the Department of Veterans Affairs was put on hold amid allegations that Jackson created a hostile work environment, improperly dispensed the sleep aid Ambien and was repeatedly drunk on duty. The latter claim was made without evidence by the committee’s top Democrat. Jackson said he wanted to reschedule his hearing and answer questions. Trump met with Jackson, defended him, blamed partisan politics and said he would stand behind him. The White House said Jackson had no plans to withdraw, while some Republicans sought more time to review the nomination and critics questioned the vetting process.

Delta College President Gavin will resign in January to lead a national coalition defending equity in higher education. A leading advocate for community-college DEI programs, Gavin has led Delta since 2021. Trustees will begin the process of appointing his successor in the coming weeks.

The document introduces NVIDIA’s GA10x Ampere architecture, including the GA102 and GA104 GPUs, which build on Turing. NVIDIA reports up to 1.7 times higher traditional raster performance, twice the ray-tracing performance, and up to 1.9 times greater power efficiency than Turing. GA102 is manufactured on Samsung’s 8nm process with 28.3 billion transistors and a 628.4 mm² die. A full GA102 contains 10,752 CUDA cores, 84 second-generation RT cores, 336 third-generation Tensor cores, 112 ROPs, seven GPCs, 42 TPCs, and 84 SMs.

GA10x Streaming Multiprocessors support FP32 operations on both datapaths, doubling FP32 throughput to 128 operations per clock per SM. Each SM includes 128 CUDA cores, four Tensor cores, one RT core, four texture units, a 256 KB register file, and 128 KB of configurable unified L1 cache and shared memory. Shared-memory bandwidth is twice that of Turing.

Second-generation RT cores double ray/triangle intersection throughput and support concurrent ray tracing with graphics or compute workloads. They also add an Interpolate Triangle Position unit for accelerated ray-traced motion blur, reported as up to eight times faster than Turing, with one measured RTX 3080 benchmark showing up to five times faster rendering. Third-generation Tensor cores support structured sparsity, which doubles effective matrix-operation throughput, along with TF32, BF16, FP16, INT8, and INT4 data types. TF32 provides up to five times the prior-generation training throughput without code changes.

GA10x supports GDDR6X memory using PAM4 signaling and Maximum Transition Avoidance encoding, reaching 19.5 Gbps and up to 936 GB/s of peak bandwidth. The RTX A6000 and A40 each provide 48 GB of GDDR6 memory, expandable to 96 GB by connecting two GPUs with third-generation NVLink. GA10x also supports PCIe 4.0, providing up to 64 GB/s over an x16 slot.

GA102 powers the GeForce RTX 3090 and 3080, RTX A6000, and A40, while GA104 powers the RTX 3070. The RTX 3090 has 10,496 CUDA cores, 24 GB of GDDR6X, and supports DLSS 8K mode for 8K HDR gaming. The RTX 3080 provides up to twice the RTX 2080’s performance, while the RTX 3070 rivals the previous-generation RTX 2080 Ti. The RTX A6000 combines 84 RT cores, 336 Tensor cores, 10,752 CUDA cores, and 48 GB of GDDR6 for professional rendering, AI, and compute workloads. The A40 targets data-center visual computing and virtual workstations, offering up to twice the FP32 and ray-tracing throughput and up to five times the AI-training throughput of the Quadro RTX 6000, or ten times with sparsity.

Additional platform features include RTX IO for GPU-based asset decompression with Microsoft DirectStorage, HDMI 2.1 and DisplayPort 1.4a support for high-resolution displays, fifth-generation NVDEC with AV1 hardware decoding, seventh-generation NVENC encoding, and GDDR6X Error Detection and Replay for detecting and retrying faulty memory transmissions.

President Donald Trump’s attendance at the opening of the Mississippi Civil Rights Museum prompted controversy because he had refused to condemn white supremacists in Charlottesville and endorsed Roy Moore after Moore appeared to justify slavery. Civil rights leaders, including John Lewis, threatened to boycott the event. Trump ultimately spoke to a small crowd, largely reading from a script, and did not attend the main event.

Jackson mayor Chokwe Antar Lumumba called the museum opening an important recognition of historical struggle, while arguing that recognizing struggle must also consider what comes next. He aims to make Jackson the “most radical city” through people’s assemblies that promote access, Black self-determination and participatory democracy.

The movement grew from Black activist groups formed after Hurricane Katrina and became central to Jackson politics after Lumumba’s father became mayor in 2012. Lumumba became mayor in 2017 and presented the assemblies as an alternative to “Trumpian authoritarianism,” arguing that radical change requires challenging existing conditions.

The SPLC’s campus guide advises students to counter alt-right speakers without direct confrontation or violence. It encourages educating classmates, creating videos or pamphlets, enlisting campus support, and holding peaceful protests to deny speakers a spectacle. Distributed to over 2,000 schools, the guide identifies leading alt-right figures and explains that labels such as “alt-right,” “identarian,” and “race realist” rebrand white nationalism amid rising campus tensions.

The TLV32xx comparators accept differential input voltages from 200 mV below V− to 200 mV above V+ without output phase inversion within that range. Inputs include ESD clamps and must not exceed the supply rails by more than 200 mV; input current should remain at or below 10 mA, with series resistance recommended to limit transient current. Unused inputs must not be tied together; they should be connected to voltages within the input range with at least 50 mV differential voltage to prevent noise-induced chatter.

The family provides 1.8 mV of internal hysteresis and is available with push-pull or open-drain outputs. Push-pull outputs can source and sink current but must not be connected to other outputs; unused outputs must remain floating. Open-drain outputs support pull-ups from 0 to 5.5 V independent of the supply, logical ORing, and logic-level translation; recommended pull-up current is 100 µA to 1 mA. Unused open-drain outputs may float or connect to V−. Outputs require high-speed PCB layout, and series current limiting is recommended where shorts are possible.

Inputs and outputs have internal ESD protection. TLV321x devices include a power-on reset that holds the output low for up to 32 µs after the 1.65 V reset threshold is crossed, then reflects the differential input once operating conditions are met.

In a basic comparator configuration, an input below the reference produces a low output, while an input above it produces a high output; swapping inputs reverses the logic. Propagation delay depends on transition direction and overdrive, with delays increasing at low overdrive, particularly below 100 mV. External positive-feedback hysteresis can reduce chatter: an inverting configuration uses a three-resistor network, while a non-inverting configuration uses two resistors and a voltage reference.

A low-side current-sensing example amplifies a shunt-resistor voltage drop and switches the comparator at a threshold, with a specified high output above 1.1 V. Layout guidance calls for a 0.1 µF low-ESR ceramic bypass capacitor at each device, minimized input/output coupling, close placement of input series resistors, and optional output resistance below 100 Ω to damp ringing. Both split and single supplies are supported. The document also provides support resources, ESD-handling cautions, revision information, and packaging data.

During Larry Nassar’s final sentencing hearing, Randall Margraves rushed toward the former sports doctor after Judge Janice Cunningham denied his request to confront him privately. Margraves, whose daughters were abused by Nassar, was stopped by deputies, later apologized and said he had lost control; the judge said she would not fine or jail him for contempt. Nassar admitted sexually assaulting girls under the guise of medical treatment and was sentenced to 40–175 years for assaults at Michigan State University and his home. More than 200 accusers have spoken or submitted statements in two Michigan counties.

In Supreme Court arguments in Michael Bowe’s successive habeas case, the justices considered two procedural issues. First, whether 28 U.S.C. § 2244(b)(3)(E), which bars Supreme Court review of a court of appeals’ grant or denial of permission to file a successive habeas petition, permits review of Bowe’s challenge. Bowe’s lawyer, Andrew Adler, argued that it does not because the court of appeals dismissed Bowe’s request under § 2244(b)(1), rather than denying authorization after finding he failed the required preliminary showing. The federal government argued that dismissal constitutes denial and that the statutory structure clearly bars review.

Second, the parties disputed whether § 2244(b)(1), which bars claims presented in earlier habeas applications, applies to federal inmates. Bowe and the government noted that it expressly refers to § 2254 petitions, which govern state inmates. Amicus Kasdin Mitchell argued that § 2244’s cross-reference makes relevant provisions applicable to federal prisoners.

The justices questioned counsel about the jurisdictional bar’s clarity, the resulting review process, and the statutory structure. They gave little indication of their view on jurisdiction, and fewer than five votes appeared to support applying § 2244(b)(1) to federal inmates if that issue were reached.

The lecture introduces data structures for multilevel memory, beginning with the external memory model. This model treats disk as infinite and slow, cache as infinitely fast, computation and cache access as free, and block transfers between disk and cache as the cost. Disk and cache are divided into blocks of size \(B\), with total cache size \(M\). Basic results include scanning an \(N\)-element array in \(\lceil N/B\rceil\) transfers; searching with B-trees in an optimal \(\log_{B+1}N\) transfers in the comparison model; and sorting in \((N/B)\log_{M/B}(N/B)\) transfers. Permuting can be done in the minimum of \(N\) transfers and the sorting bound. Buffer trees achieve optimal amortized update costs and support delayed queries, batch updates, flushing, and priority queues.

The cache-oblivious model assumes algorithms do not know the block size or cache size and cannot control cache replacement; blocks are fetched and evicted automatically. Analysis assumes optimal replacement, though LRU and FIFO are constant-competitive with it using a cache of twice the size. Cache-oblivious algorithms perform well simultaneously for all \(B\) and \(M\), including across multilevel caches. Known results include \(O(N/B)\) scans, \(O(\log_{B+1}N)\) search, insertion, and deletion, and the same sorting bound as the external-memory model. Cache-oblivious priority queues attain the optimal bound under a “tall cache” assumption. Unlike external memory, cache-oblivious permutation cannot achieve the minimum of the sorting and linear bounds up to constant factors. The best constant factor for cache-oblivious search is \(\log_2 e\), although the lecture’s construction achieves a factor of 4.

For static cache-oblivious search, the lecture uses a perfect balanced binary search tree stored in van Emde Boas order. Recursively dividing the tree into smaller subtrees and concatenating their layouts ensures that any root-to-leaf path visits \(O(\log_{B+1}N)\) blocks for every block size.

For dynamic structures, a cache-oblivious B-tree combines this static layout with ordered file maintenance and indirection. Ordered file maintenance stores sorted elements in an array with gaps, supporting insertions and deletions with \(O(\log^2N)\) amortized time. The static tree stores subtree maxima and is updated in postorder. Initially, this yields \(O(\log_{B+1}N+\log^2N/B)\) updates and \(O(\log_{B+1}N)\) searches. A final indirection layer groups items into \(O(\log N)\)-sized buckets, using splits and merges as in B-trees. This removes the extra \(\log^2N/B\) term, producing \(O(\log_{B+1}N)\) updates while preserving the search bound.

Python is an open-source, high-level, dynamically typed programming language widely used in algorithmic trading because of its readability, ease of learning, extensive libraries, and free commercial-use packages. Traders use it for market-data analysis, statistical modeling, trade execution, risk and order management, backtesting, optimization, and live strategy implementation. Scientific libraries such as Pandas, NumPy, scikit-learn, and Zipline support quantitative research, while Python’s large developer community makes code sharing and collaboration easier. Python-based strategies include trend following, momentum, RSI, and moving-average approaches.

A trading algorithm analyzes markets, identifies opportunities, executes trades, and manages positions according to predefined instructions or criteria such as timing, price, and quantity. Algorithmic trading can process data and execute trades faster than manual trading, but the passage argues that coding alone does not ensure profitability; market interpretation and strategy quality remain essential.

Backtesting applies a coded strategy to historical price data under fixed rules for buying and exiting. It can reveal past performance and algorithmic bugs, but it is only a simulation and cannot guarantee future results. Backtests should also account for trading fees and other live costs. A typical workflow involves importing libraries, obtaining OHLCV data, separating in-sample and out-of-sample data, running and optimizing the strategy, and evaluating results.

Common Python backtesting frameworks include PyAlgoTrade, Bt, Backtrader, Fastquant, LEAN, and Zipline. PyAlgoTrade offers documentation, live and paper trading, multiple data sources, several order types, and cryptocurrency and social-media support. Bt focuses on reusable strategy components and portfolio strategies. Fastquant enables backtesting with as little as three lines of code. LEAN provides relatively fast, multi-language strategy support, although its C# core may challenge non-C# users. Zipline supports research, backtesting, and live or paper trading, with historical US stock data and notebook-based use. Backtrader is beginner-friendly, well documented, supports backtesting and live trading, and includes performance analyzers, but may struggle with very large datasets. The best framework depends on the trader’s needs, though Backtrader and QuantConnect are highlighted as popular options.

Python’s stated advantages for trading outweigh its drawbacks, including concerns about execution speed. The passage also presents stand-alone platforms as potentially more economical than building custom Python systems, particularly for traders who lack coding expertise.

The coach was pleased with a close victory and emphasized that the next game is crucial to determining the series. He praised the team’s composure, goaltending, defensive play, and contributions from multiple scorers. A newly acquired player was described as positive, intense, physically strong, and a natural scoring winger who should fit in the room.

The coach said the team remained composed under sustained pressure but lost momentum after consecutive penalties led to Philadelphia goals. Improving discipline and penalty killing was identified as important, while Philadelphia’s puck-moving defense, Lindros line, and Brind’Amour remained concerns. The tying goal was attributed largely to coincidence rather than a planned matchup. The team was advised to avoid risky play at home, remain disciplined, and prepare for Philadelphia’s expected strong response in Game 3. Experience from recent playoff runs was credited for the team’s comfort and composure.

The Kentucky Supreme Court affirmed the Workers’ Compensation Board’s allocation of liability for David Eugene Bunch’s April 1977 workplace injury. Bunch had suffered prior back injuries and surgeries, and the Board found that he had a 55% preexisting occupational disability before the workplace injury. The Board excluded that disability from compensation, assigned 15% of the resulting disability to the employer, and assigned 30% to the Special Fund because the injury had awakened a previously dormant condition.

The Court rejected the Court of Appeals’ conclusion that the preexisting disability should be charged to the Special Fund. It held that the controlling test is not whether the employee was able to work, but whether occupational disability existed immediately before the subsequent injury. Ability to hold a job does not establish the absence of “active” occupational disability. The Court therefore overruled contrary language in the cited Yocum decisions, reversed the Court of Appeals, and affirmed the trial court’s judgment.

Electronic Arts will go private in a $55 billion all-cash deal backed by Saudi Arabia’s sovereign wealth fund, Silver Lake, and Affinity Partners—the largest leveraged buyout in history. Shareholders will receive about a 25% premium, and Andrew Wilson will remain CEO. The deal reduces pressure from shareholders but may bring demands from EA’s new owners. Wilson could pursue generative AI and expand EA’s esports presence in Saudi Arabia, though the company faces competition for “Battlefield 6,” dependence on established franchises such as “The Sims” and “Madden NFL,” and continued struggles in mobile gaming.

Colorado Boy Scout Troop 1532, formed in 2014 by Dr. P.J. Parmar and the Denver-area refugee clinic he runs, is composed almost entirely of refugees from countries including Burma, Rwanda and Nepal. The troop organizes camping trips where scouts cook familiar foods, hike, fish, play soccer, learn outdoor skills and interact in multiple languages. Its leaders say the group helps children adjust to American culture while providing a safe place to be themselves.

Brothers Jean Tuyishime, 15, and Moise Tuyikunde, 12, joined after their family relocated from Rwanda’s Gihembe refugee camp to the Denver area in 2014. Jean wants to become a leader like Parmar and troop leader Justin Wilson and help other children.

The troop faces challenges uncommon to more homogeneous groups, including transportation and scheduling difficulties, difficulty retaining adult leaders and maintaining memberships, and limited focus on merit badges and rank advancement. Scouts also face greater scrutiny and disciplinary issues, including alleged theft, smoking and marijuana use. Leaders emphasize discipline and respect, while Wilson said the boys often do not receive the benefit of the doubt afforded to other children. A Boy Scouts of America spokeswoman said scouting can help refugee children learn American culture, build resilience and develop citizenship, and the troop is viewed as a model for attracting future refugees to the organization.

The Swiss National Bank and European Central Bank are assessing a link between Switzerland’s SIC instant-payment network and the Eurosystem’s TIPS platform. An exploratory phase through 2026 will examine technical and economic feasibility, including legal, compliance, operational, liquidity, cybersecurity and settlement-risk issues. If implemented, the connection could enable transfers between the Swiss and euro currency areas in seconds, reduce reliance on slower, costlier correspondent banking and strengthen Swiss-EU payment integration without adopting the euro. The initiative aligns with the ECB’s interoperability strategy and G20 payment-efficiency goals, but must address differing monetary systems, cyber risks and regulatory requirements.

A November 17, 2001 Commissioner.COM/SportsLine fantasy football report for Paul Lucci’s “Get Bad with Yourself” league contains promotions, the “Luccis Losers” roster, injury notes and Week 10 player updates. Advertisements promote fantasy football guides priced at $9.99, a Norton 2001 software suite for $19.99, discounts, giveaways and a Friday SportsLine Radio fantasy show.

The Luccis Losers roster lists eight active and seven reserve players, including quarterbacks Kurt Warner and Rob Johnson, running backs Duce Staley, Charlie Garner and Mike Alstott, and receivers Cris Carter, Ike Hilliard, Marty Booker and Az-Zahir Hakim. Injury notes say Cameron Cleeland is expected to miss Indianapolis, Johnson will be out at least four weeks, and Warner is expected to start at New England.

Major player news includes suspensions for Correll Buckhalter and Jamal Lewis, who is also rehabbing a torn ACL, and a season-ending torn ACL for Edgerrin James, with Dominic Rhodes expected to start. Emmitt Smith is expected to return against Philadelphia, while Michael Bennett is expected to return for Minnesota. Steve McNair, Fred Taylor, James Jackson, Frank Wycheck and Jerome Pathon were listed as questionable or doubtful; Tyrone Wheatley’s status changed from out to probable.

Start recommendations include Brett Favre, Marshall Faulk, Donovan McNabb, Daunte Culpepper, Ricky Williams, Aaron Brooks, Willie Jackson, Torry Holt, Isaac Bruce, Cris Carter, Randy Moss and Ike Hilliard, often citing favorable matchups. The report advises avoiding or benching several players, including McNair, Az-Zahir Hakim, Donald Hayes, Richard Huntley and Detroit’s low-value running backs.

The team believes its collective play can improve in the remaining games against Boston. With home-ice advantage, strong fan support, and one of the last two teams still playing for the Stanley Cup, the players are focused on earning another chance to win the trophy. Coaches respect Boston’s strength and note that their top players must continue meeting their standards.

Boston’s aggressive goaltender has prompted plans to generate more pucks, traffic, and net preference, along with other tactical adjustments. The coach emphasizes that weak offense is a team-wide execution issue, not solely a goaltending problem. Leadership, accountability, and the core group’s preparation are praised, with confidence that players will seize the opportunity.

The coach also defends a previous lineup decision, expresses trust in goalie Roberto, acknowledges emotional incidents in both Boston games, and believes the previously strong power play will remain effective.

ChatGPT is a conversational AI system from OpenAI that can support trading by analyzing market data, brainstorming strategies, and generating Python backtests, though its answers may be incorrect. The article trained it with trading context, requested a Bollinger Band mean-reversion strategy, and had it produce code using pandas, numpy, yfinance, and matplotlib. The unmodified code was tested on SPY data since inception, adjusted for dividends and splits. Reported results were a 3.20% CAGR, 326 trades, and 45.63% time in the market. The article concludes that ChatGPT is useful as a starting point for developing and refining strategies, but it is not a trading platform, does not provide financial advice or make investment decisions, and cannot guarantee profitable strategies.

Leeds United lost 1-0 to Wolverhampton Wanderers at Elland Road, dropping to seventh and out of the play-off places. Leeds’ poor first-half passing and defensive errors allowed Nouha Dicko to score in the 39th minute, despite two saves by Rob Green. United improved after the break but failed to equalize, leaving Wolves to protect their lead. Leeds may now need to win all three remaining matches to secure a play-off place.

The coach said the team must move on from its loss and focus on winning in St. Louis. Despite playing well and creating chances, the team lacked desired rebounds and a penalty call. He credited familiarity, mixed lines, and a shared system for the team’s chemistry and chances going forward.

Gold climbed above $4,000 per ounce as disappointing U.S. retail and manufacturing data fueled expectations of Federal Reserve easing, with traders anticipating possible rate cuts by early 2026. Weakening yields, a softer dollar, slower global growth and safe-haven demand supported the rally. Central-bank buying, geopolitical tensions and fiscal pressures further strengthened gold’s appeal. Analysts cautioned that hawkish Fed signals or stronger U.S. growth could trigger corrections, while sustained prices could draw more institutional capital into precious metals in 2025.

Michael Bowe, sentenced to 24 years for an attempted armored-car robbery and a Section 924(c) firearm offense, is asking the Supreme Court to allow successive federal habeas petitions. He argues that Supreme Court rulings holding that conspiracy to commit Hobbs Act robbery is unconstitutionally vague and that attempted Hobbs Act robbery is not a “crime of violence” invalidate his Section 924(c) conviction.

The government says Section 2255(h) limits successive petitions to new evidence of innocence or new retroactive constitutional claims. Bowe’s first obstacle is Section 2244(b)(3)(E), which bars Supreme Court review of rulings authorizing or denying successive petitions. Bowe says it applies only to state inmates, while the government says Section 2255(h) incorporates all of Section 2244(b)(3). Bowe also raises an Exceptions Clause challenge. The second issue is whether Section 2244(b)(1), which bars repetitive claims, applies to federal inmates. The government concedes that it does not but suggests that the abuse-of-the-writ doctrine could limit repetitive federal filings. The court appointed former Justice Thomas clerk Kasdin Mitchell to defend the Eleventh Circuit’s contrary position.

After the Joe Flacco trade, Browns coach Kevin Stefanski is weighing Dillon Gabriel and Shedeur Sanders as Cleveland’s No. 2 quarterback but has not committed to a decision. Sanders began training camp as the team’s fourth-ranked quarterback, spent the first five games as the inactive emergency QB, and split scout-team reps with Gabriel and Zappe. Sanders said he is thankful for whatever role he receives, confident he is ready, and committed to preparing to play at any time. Offensive coordinator Tommy Rees praised Sanders’ preparation, growth, and understanding of the offense. Responding to criticism from ESPN analyst Rex Ryan, Sanders avoided negativity while acknowledging that he is mindful of how his playful personality may be interpreted.

Coach Dean Smith's "Four Corner" offense, a UNC trademark and among the most recognizable spread offenses, requires a player with special ballhandling and one-on-one skills. Spreading the floor with a player in each corner creates isolation for O1, allows one player to control the game, minimizes ballhandling errors and turnovers, and reduces opponents' offensive possessions. When defender X1 cuts off O1's dribble penetration, O1 passes to a corner player, leads for a return pass, then drives or kicks out to O3 or stepping-out baseline corners (O2, O4). If the passing lane is denied, O5 back cuts for a drop pass and the baseline corner player can pass to the opposite corner cutting to the basket. If X1 overplays and denies the return pass to O1, O2 exchanges positions with O1 and dribbles, and O3 initiates penetration if that return pass is also denied.

This continuation application describes near-eye waveguide displays for virtual, augmented, and mixed reality systems. A display assembly generates image light using a source assembly and directs it through an output waveguide to the user’s eye. The source assembly may include MicroLEDs or other light sources, optics that expand and collimate the light, and scanning mirrors that scan it in one or two dimensions. Coupling and decoupling elements, such as diffraction or holographic gratings, transfer the image light into and out of the output waveguide. A controller divides display content into sections and coordinates illumination and scanning so the user perceives a complete image. Some embodiments add a narrow source waveguide that expands the light in one dimension and uses an actuator to rotate and scan it in another.

Source elements may be arranged in flat or curved linear arrays, stacked arrays, nonadjacent arrays, or sparse two-dimensional arrays. They may emit the same or different colors, including infrared, and optical isolators may surround elements to reduce interference and crosstalk. Scanning may use raster or interlaced patterns. MicroLEDs offer wide spectra and high brightness, but their small array size limits simple two-dimensional resolution to about 640×480, while large pixel pitch and low fill factor increase display size. Linear, sparse, and MicroLED configurations can also ease scanning-angle and resonance-frequency constraints.

Air Canada apologized and offered compensation after bumping 10-year-old Brett Doyle from an oversold flight, his father said. The family was told no seat was available, then drove to Moncton after their replacement flight was canceled. They eventually reached Montreal and continued to Costa Rica. Air Canada offered a C$2,500 travel voucher while investigating what happened. The case drew attention amid criticism of airline overbooking after United forcibly removed a passenger in Chicago.

The passage praises the Army’s and civil authorities’ constructive statesmanship in the Philippine Islands and Filipino cooperation with U.S. representatives. It argues that the small Army should remain highly efficient, conduct regular maneuvers, and train officers and enlisted men individually and collectively, especially in marksmanship and independent responsibility. It urges a general staff, reorganization of supply departments, prompt militia reform, clearer National Guard relationships, humane disposal or light work for worn horses, and continued development of young officers. It also calls for expanded naval maneuvers, improved gunnery, adequate practice ammunition and incentives, yearly additions to the fighting fleet, and sufficiently trained crews and ship personnel. Because U.S. foreign policies require a first-class navy, an inadequate force would leave the isthmian canal vulnerable and the Monroe Doctrine unsupported. A strong navy is presented as a guarantor of peace, and neither ships nor crews can be improvised once war begins.

Youth soccer position placement should reflect the chosen formation, players’ abilities and temperaments, and program goals. Basic roles include goalkeepers, defenders, midfielders, and forwards, each requiring particular skills and dispositions: goalkeepers need hand skills and a desire to play; defenders must mark opponents, stay goal-side, and tackle; midfielders contribute on offense and defense and should enjoy running; forwards need scoring ability and an attacking mindset.

Coaches can evaluate players through observation, drills, experimentation, player preferences, outside reviews, scrimmages, and monitoring achievement and enjoyment. After selecting a formation and naming positions, coaches should diagram the formation with attack direction and defended goal, teach relative field locations, assign players, and practice moving the team between attack and defense. Functional training should demonstrate position-specific expectations.

Coaches should avoid type-casting young players and expose everyone to all positions because abilities may develop over time. Equal playing time, position exposure, skill development, and small-sided games should guide placement decisions alongside competitiveness. Rotating goalkeepers and using playing-time charts can help promote equality.

Rush Bowls, a Colorado chain that opened its first St. Louis-area location in the Central West End, serves smoothies and blended-fruit bowls in a quick-service format. Customers order at the counter, and the shop can be very noisy because of the blenders and hard surfaces.

The menu includes 17 basic smoothies for $6.50 and four bowl categories priced at $7.95: Enlightened Bowls, acai bowls, seasonal bowls, and Comfort Bowls. Bowls use fruit blended with options such as fat-free milk, fat-free frozen yogurt, or vanilla soy, with toppings including granola, honey, acai, chai, peanut butter, and house-made jelly. Comfort Bowls feature flavors such as peanut butter and jelly, chocolate-covered strawberry, peach cobbler, and apple pie à la mode.

The restaurant also offers a few stools for dine-in customers. It is primarily aimed at people seeking a quick meal before or after exercise, making its location near Forest Park, Steel Wheels, and LimeBike convenient for active customers.

EUR/USD extended its monthly decline toward 1.0500 after disappointing eurozone GDP, German ZEW sentiment and industrial production data. Fed Chair Janet Yellen’s unexpectedly hawkish testimony, suggesting interest-rate increases may be appropriate and balance-sheet reduction would accompany normalization, boosted the dollar. Technical indicators point toward 1.0500, then 1.0350 if the bearish trend extends.

The study examines the digitalization of higher education in Ethiopia within the context of national development plans, African Union strategies, and the global digital divide. It identifies policies, initiatives, current practices, and barriers affecting digital transformation using a qualitative document and thematic analysis of continental, national, and institutional policies, publicly available reports, and the author’s professional experience.

Ethiopia has prioritized ICT infrastructure, digital education, and innovation through the Growth and Transformation Plan II, the Homegrown Economic Reform Agenda, the Ten-Year Development Plan, Digital Ethiopia 2025, and national ICT policies. MoSHE introduced a National ICT Policy and Strategy for Higher Education and TVET, a Digital Skills Country Action Plan for 2021–2030, and an institutional ICT policy allowing universities to tailor policies to their needs. These instruments aim to improve access, equity, quality, research, administration, digital skills, infrastructure, and institutional connectivity.

Major initiatives include the Ethiopian Education and Research Network (EthERNet), the National Academic Digital Repository of Ethiopia (NADRE), and the National Academic Digital Library of Ethiopia (NADLE). Their reach and resources remain limited: EthERNet connected only a minority of universities and TVET institutions, while NADRE lacks visibility and academic content and NADLE hosts a relatively small collection of learning resources.

Digitalization practices in Ethiopian higher education remain largely administrative, including digitizing records, student information systems, and routine services, rather than transforming teaching, learning, and research. The COVID-19 university closures exposed inadequate infrastructure, curriculum, and digital preparedness. Although fully online degree programs were later authorized and initiatives involving learning management systems, higher-education management information systems, and emerging technologies were introduced, limited teacher and student skills, restricted training opportunities, and weak connectivity constrained their effectiveness.

Major barriers include unreliable and unaffordable internet, insufficient campus bandwidth, unreliable electricity, weak ICT infrastructure, shortages of skilled ICT personnel, limited digital literacy, and resistance to poorly contextualized institutional changes. The findings conclude that policies alone are insufficient: effective digital transformation requires dependable infrastructure, affordable internet, capable personnel, sound leadership and governance, and effective policy implementation. Ethiopia should shift attention from expanding higher education toward ensuring its quality and relevance through digitalization, while future research incorporate primary data from different institutions and examine effects on universities’ core missions.

WTI crude futures fell 46 cents to $52.72 a barrel after a third consecutive weekly gain. Rising U.S. shale output, with oil rigs added for a 13th straight week, pressured an oversupplied market and efforts to curb output. Easing Libyan and geopolitical tensions weighed on prices, while stronger Chinese data and hopes of extended OPEC production cuts provided support.

Bergdorf Goodman hosted Dita Von Teese’s unveiling of her Scandalwood fragrance. Other headlines covered scalp facials, holiday windows, luxury retailers’ sales and holiday prospects, Linda Fargo, retailer responses to Ivanka Trump, an $11 million lawsuit involving Saks and John Barrett, and Barbara Taylor Bradford.

Wisdomtree Investments shares rose 2.43% in the latest session, closing at $9.68. Nine analysts have a mean 52-week price target of $10.75, with targets ranging from $8 to $13.50. The average brokerage recommendation is 2.55 from 11 recommendations, ranking the stock out of 265 in its industry. Ratings include three Buys, two Outperforms, five Holds, two Underperforms, and one Sell. Its ATR-14 is 0.34, weekly volatility is 3.42%, monthly volatility is 3.62%, and RSI is 57.35. The company has a $1.36 billion market capitalization and 140.94 million shares outstanding. Trading volume was 2.16 million shares versus an average of nearly 1.6 million.

A jury must decide whether Tomas Gajowniczek is not guilty by reason of insanity for allegedly attempting to murder his partner, Alicja Kalinowska, by pinning her down, stuffing underwear in her mouth, pinching her nose and beating her with a hammer. He also denies intentionally or recklessly causing her serious harm.

Prosecution barrister Paul Burns SC said Gajowniczek was acutely intoxicated by cannabis, which does not qualify as a mental disorder under the Criminal Law (Insanity) Act 2006. He argued that his jealousy over Kalinowska’s infidelity was genuine and that the deliberate attack showed an intent to kill.

Defence barrister Ronan Munro SC argued that Gajowniczek had psychosis and was unable to control his actions, citing his paranoia and distress over family, financial and tax concerns. He disputed evidence that Gajowniczek was intoxicated and urged the jury to find him not guilty by reason of insanity. Justice Patrick McCarthy will complete his jury directions.

MCW Pro Wrestling presents “Spring Fever” on April 22 at MCW Arena in Joppa, Maryland, headlined by Rey Mysterio, with a meet-and-greet at 4 p.m. and live action at 7:30 p.m. The card includes vacant tag-title and number-one contender matches, title defenses, a scramble-rules match, Lio Rush vs. Travis “Flip” Gordon, Napalm vs. Marcellus Prime, and Winner Circle vs. The Hell Cats. Tickets are available through MissionTix, by phone, and at the door.

In 1850, Hawaiian commissioners Prince Alexander and Lott Kamehameha received Lord Palmerston’s advice that Hawaii should maintain effective government and preserve independence, or accept a U.S. protectorate or annexation given its economic ties and demographic changes. Britain temporarily seized the islands in 1843 before restoring them, and Britain and France recognized Hawaiian independence in a joint convention. French pressure in 1849–1851 prompted Kamehameha III to cede the islands to the United States, although Secretary of State Daniel Webster later ordered the deed returned. Subsequent annexation and reciprocity proposals failed. The dispatch enclosed a 1870 review of Hawaiian agriculture and commerce and a map showing the islands’ relative location and steamship connections.

Short interest represents the percentage of a company’s outstanding shares sold short, while the short-interest ratio measures the average days required to cover those positions. Broker-dealers report short positions to FINRA twice monthly, and the data is readily available through sources such as Seeking Alpha and NYSE files. High short interest may indicate investor pessimism, but empirical research cited from Nasdaq and CFA Institute studies associates it with weaker future returns. The evidence concludes that buying stocks with persistently high short interest is generally unfavorable over the long term.

A short squeeze occurs when short sellers must repurchase shares as prices rise, often because of limited supply, margin calls, or other covering demand. Gamestop’s 2021 squeeze illustrates the strategy’s volatility and the potentially unlimited risk of short selling. Although traders can earn substantial profits from squeezes, they are rare and difficult to predict, even when short interest is high. Short selling is therefore considered difficult and generally ineffective as a standalone long-term strategy, though it may still support approaches such as pairs trading and portfolio risk mitigation.

The paper argues that conventional multi-agent reinforcement learning is limited by its assumption that each agent has one scalar reward, despite practical agents facing diverse, conflicting objectives. In multi-agent settings, objective trade-offs depend on other agents’ strategies, making independent single-agent multi-objective solutions inadequate. The paper introduces the Multi-Objective Markov Game (MOMG) and Pareto-Nash Equilibrium (PNE), combining Nash stability with Pareto optimality, and proves every finite MOMG admits a PNE. It also establishes equivalence between an MOMG’s PNE set and the union of Nash equilibria from its linearly scalarized games, enabling existing single-objective Markov-game solvers to be reused. Building on this result, the authors develop online learning methods for computationally demanding equilibrium computation. They analyze weaker concepts, including Weak Pareto-Nash Equilibrium and Pareto Correlated Equilibrium, and propose a decentralized online algorithm that provably converges to a PCE.

The speaker calls Ottawa a tough win and says being removed from the lineup was disappointing, though Lindy’s change was best for the team. They will focus on solid all-around play and defense, prepare for a disciplined, hard-working opponent, and note that everyone has contributed during the Stanley Cup playoffs.

Despite poor ice and passing, the team remained aggressive and sought to build on its Colorado series. It rejected calling a late chance blown but admitted failing to adapt to aggressive forechecking and counterattacks.

Indian shares rose Monday, ending a five-day losing streak, as weak U.S. inflation data eased rate-hike concerns and global markets recovered. The NSE index gained 0.83%, BSE 0.82%, and Nifty Bank 0.74%. DLF surged up to 13.7%, while Sun Pharma and BPCL fell after disappointing quarterly results.

Concerns center on the Cavaliers’ late-season decline and 22nd-ranked defense, along with questions about team chemistry, Kyrie Irving’s production, Kevin Love’s fit, and Tyronn Lue’s leadership. Cleveland fell from 30-11 on January 20 to 21-20 afterward. However, LeBron James has reached the NBA Finals in six consecutive seasons, won 18 straight first-round playoff games, and carried weaker teams to the Finals. With Cleveland unusually healthy, Keidel argues the Cavaliers remain unlikely to fail before the Finals, where they would likely face the Warriors.

Tesla’s stock has risen more than 1,000% in five years as the company advances toward making electric vehicles and solar energy affordable to consumers. Model 3 demand is strong, with more than 400,000 preorders and production plans of 20,000 vehicles monthly by December. Revenue and automotive revenue rose sharply, losses narrowed, and Tesla reported $3 billion in cash. It is expanding battery production through Gigafactory 1, plans to unveil an electric semi-truck, and expects annual vehicle production to increase from about 100,000 in 2017 to 500,000 in 2018.

However, Tesla remains unprofitable, pays no dividend, and carries roughly $9 billion in long-term debt. Its $56.9 billion market capitalization and $7 billion in revenue appear excessive compared with Ford, GM, and BMW, which have greater resources and are also developing electric vehicles.

The passage argues that Tesla should be evaluated as a renewable-energy technology company rather than solely against automakers, but execution risks remain, including delays, competition, and possible valuation pullbacks. The author is cautiously optimistic about Musk and Tesla’s management while calling the investment risky and less attractive than a year earlier.

German inflation unexpectedly rose 2.2% year over year in May, above the 1.9% forecast, led by energy prices and the oil surge. Food, energy, and services prices rose 3.5%, 5.2%, and 1.9%, respectively, while core inflation remained subdued. Political uncertainty in Italy may weigh on the ECB, whose asset-purchasing program is likely to be extended through year-end.

The speaker accepts the presidency with humility and gratitude, relying on divine guidance and vowing to preserve, protect, and defend the Constitution. He declares that the Constitution and its compromises will guide his administration, that federal power is limited and delegated, and that both the national government and the states must remain within their constitutional spheres. He vows to protect minority rights, use the presidential veto judiciously, preserve the Union, discourage sectional hostility, and enact just laws that do not favor monopolies or particular sections or classes.

He describes the federal Union as a source of liberty, equality, prosperity, religious freedom, and peaceful government, and warns that destroying it would mean anarchy or despotism. He rejects unnecessary national banks and other institutions that might strengthen the government against popular will, supports strict economy in public spending, and calls for repayment of national and state debts. He favors tariffs primarily for revenue, with incidental protection for domestic industry, while insisting that taxes be distributed fairly and not used to enrich one interest at another’s expense.

The speaker supports the annexation of Texas as a peaceful expansion of the Union that would strengthen both countries, increase trade, and reduce the danger of conflict. He also asserts the United States’ claim to Oregon and calls for extending republican institutions and protection to its citizens there. In foreign relations, he promises respect for other nations, exact justice, avoidance of harmful alliances, and cultivation of commerce and friendly relations. He requires strict accountability from public officers and pledges to govern impartially for the whole country, including those who opposed him.

Star Bulk Carriers (SBLK) is a dry bulk shipping company heavily exposed to Capesize vessels, whose rates rebounded sharply after weakness caused by Brazilian flooding and slower iron ore exports. SBLK announced the acquisition of 16 vessels built between 2010 and 2017, assuming $310 million of debt and issuing 10.5 million shares. The effective purchase price was $433 million, compared with VesselsValue’s estimated $441 million value. The transaction diluted equity by 14% while expanding the fleet from 74 to 90 ships, increasing cargo capacity by 24% and reducing average fleet age from eight years to seven. Estimated NAV was $12.60 per share, potentially rising to $15.40 if fleet values increased 10%. Value Investor’s Edge, a major SBLK holder, set a $15 per-share fair-value target, representing 24% upside, and viewed the acquisition as accretive and supportive of further industry consolidation.

The lecture introduces batch arguments (BARGs), also called SNARGs for Batch NP. A BARG consists of generator, prover, and verifier algorithms. The generator produces a common reference string for the prover and verifier. For an NP relation \(L\), the prover uses witnesses \(w_1,\ldots,w_k\) to prove that instances \(x_1,\ldots,x_k\) all belong to \(L\) with one proof. A BARG is succinct when its proof is smaller than the combined witness length, and it must provide completeness and soundness against nonuniform probabilistic cheating provers.

BARGs are presented as analogues of aggregated signatures and batch interactive proofs, and as building blocks for SNARGs for all of P. A Gentry–Wichs result, under falsifiable assumptions, rules out SNARGs for \(T\)-hard languages with proof length significantly below \(\log T\), roughly the witness length for general NP; this does not preclude succinct BARGs.

The main theorem states that BARGs can be constructed from learning with errors, with proof size governed by the relation-circuit size and verification time linear in the total instance length plus terms depending on \(\log k\), circuit size, and security parameter. Verification is divided into preprocessing that produces a small state and an online phase independent of \(k\).

The construction begins with a simplified Kilian protocol. Separate PCPs for the \(k\) instances form a matrix; each column is hashed, the verifier issues one common PCP query, and the prover opens the queried columns across all rows. The verifier checks the openings and each PCP. Since ordinary compressing hashes may have multiple PCP preimages with different accepting queries, the resulting relation may not be sparse enough for a correlation-intractable hash.

To address this, the protocol uses a correlation-intractable hash, with its key in the common reference string, and a statistically binding hash. The latter is built from FHE: its key encrypts an index, hashing homomorphically selects the indexed coordinate, and the hash is a ciphertext. It provides key indistinguishability, statistical binding, and trapdoor-based extraction. In the nonuniform soundness proof, an invalid instance \(x_{i^*}\) is fixed, the common reference string is switched to an SSB key for \(i^*\), and the relevant PCP row is extracted from the column hashes. An accepted cheating proof would produce a valid pair violating the correlation-intractable hash’s security.

AAPL is Apple Inc.’s ticker symbol on the Nasdaq exchange. Apple, founded in 1976 by Steve Jobs, Steve Wozniak, and Ronald Wayne, designs and sells consumer electronics, software, and online services, including the iPhone, iPad, Mac, Apple Watch, AirPods, HomePod, and Apple TV. It is a Dow Jones Industrial Average component and began trading on Nasdaq on December 12, 1980.

AAPL shares can be purchased through online or full-service brokers. Regular trading hours are typically 9:30 a.m. to 4:00 p.m. ET, although substantial trading also occurs before and after those hours; the stock is not tradable 24 hours a day. Shares do not expire and may be held indefinitely. The passage lists an all-time high of $233.47, reached October 3, 2018, and an average five-year return of approximately 16.1%. Apple pays an annual dividend of $0.82 per share, subject to change by its board.

AAPL’s popularity is attributed to its strong fundamentals, widely recognized products, long record of shareholder returns, and historical upward performance. Prices are influenced by company performance, market conditions, news, and investor sentiment. Selling decisions should consider financial goals, valuation, diversification, company fundamentals, market conditions, tax implications, personal circumstances, psychology, stock performance, and risk tolerance.

Trading AAPL requires market knowledge, rapid analysis, awareness of news and economic or political developments, a trading plan, disciplined risk management, and backtesting. There is no universally best indicator or time frame; day traders may use five- or 15-minute charts, while swing traders may use hourly or daily charts. Swing positions are generally held for days or weeks, while scalping targets minute- or second-level movements, though the passage advises against scalping. A successful strategy should account for fundamentals, technical characteristics, entry and exit plans, and the trader’s risk tolerance.

Becoming a millionaire through AAPL is possible but difficult and unlikely; most traders fail. Successful traders are described as systematic, patient, rational, meticulous, and willing to make decisions.

Options on AAPL allow trading at predetermined prices and can hedge or speculate, but the market is described as zero-sum, competitive, and difficult. The VIX measures market volatility through a basket of stocks; its AAPL-related ticker is VXAPL.

For people who have achieved FIRE and want to preserve wealth, the passage argues that a wealth-building portfolio may be unsuitable for maintaining it. Traditionally safe Treasury bills can also experience drawdowns, may not protect against inflation, and had the lowest return-to-maximum-drawdown ratio among the asset classes examined from 1926–2019. US and foreign equities ranked highest on long-term reward/risk, while global asset-class diversification reduced drawdowns only modestly. The proposed moderately conservative Stay Rich Portfolio combines domestic and foreign equities, TIPS, and corporate bonds through liquid, diversified ETFs. Foreign holdings are included despite weaker ratios to improve diversification. The portfolio is approximately 75% US and 25% foreign, although US companies’ international operations create additional foreign exposure. A backtest covering equity, drawdown, and periodic returns is described.

The lecture reviews transport operations on curved manifolds. Requiring a transported derivative to annihilate the metric produces the covariant derivative, while transport induced by sliding vectors along a vector field produces the Lie derivative. The Lie derivative can be written using partial derivatives yet remains tensorial because connection terms cancel. A vector field \(C\) for which the metric is Lie transported unchanged is a Killing vector, satisfying Killing’s equation. Such vectors correspond to spacetime symmetries, such as independence from a coordinate, and are associated with conserved quantities.

The lecture also examines tensor densities. The Levi-Civita symbol is a density of weight \(1\), while the determinant of the metric is a density of weight \(-2\). Combining densities allows tensor densities to be converted into proper tensors. In particular, multiplying the Levi-Civita symbol by the square root of the absolute metric determinant produces a proper volume element. Examples include four-dimensional volume elements and the volume element in three-dimensional spherical coordinates.

A determinant-based identity provides a shortcut for certain Christoffel symbols and for the covariant divergence of a vector field. The divergence can be rewritten using a derivative of the metric determinant, simplifying calculations and providing a curved-manifold version of Gauss’s theorem. This shortcut generally does not extend to tensor divergences, although antisymmetric tensors are an exception. The stress-energy tensor illustrates why local conservation of energy and momentum does not generally imply a global conserved quantity: transporting vector fields over extended regions introduces path dependence and curvature-dependent ambiguities.

The lecture then turns to the kinematics of bodies in curved spacetime. A neutral, structureless test body in a freely falling frame follows an inertial path, which geometrically means that its tangent vector is parallel transported. This condition yields the geodesic equation, whose solutions are geodesics and whose Christoffel symbols are commonly used in general-relativistic calculations. Charged, extended, or spinning bodies require additional force and curvature-coupling terms beyond this leading test-body description.

The geodesic parameter must be affine for parallel transport to take its standard form. Proper time is an affine parameter for timelike trajectories, and affine reparameterizations are linear. A second derivation varies the proper time between two events and requires the associated action to be stationary. This again produces the geodesic equation and shows that a geodesic is the timelike path between two events along which an observer accumulates maximal proper time. Future discussion will address null trajectories for light and the derivation of conserved quantities by combining Killing’s equation with the geodesic equation.

The article evaluates Larry Connors’ and Cesar Alvarez’s Double Seven mean-reversion strategy, introduced in their 2010 book, across liquid ETFs using backtests from 2000 or ETF inception. The rules require a close above the 200-day moving average, buying at a seven-day low, and selling at a seven-day high, with no stop loss.

On SPY, since 1993, the strategy generated 154 trades, an average gain of 1.18%, an 82.5% win rate, a 2.58 profit factor, and a 1.4 Sharpe ratio. Maximum drawdown was 33%, versus 55% for buy-and-hold. Exposure averaged about 26%, and CAGR was 6.3%, compared with 10.1% for reinvested-dividend buy-and-hold.

Across the tested ETFs as a portfolio, capped at five 20% positions, it recorded 1,189 trades, a 0.63% average gain before slippage and commissions, and 6.3% CAGR, with nearly all gains occurring before 2010. An SPY/QQQ portfolio did not work because of overlapping trades. Performance was reasonable for lookbacks from two to 15 days, while the short version performed poorly. Overall, Double Seven still appeared effective on major stock indices, but other mean-reversion strategies performed better.

Until card identification ends, the host remains at fOD frequency because cards may impose identification-mode frequency restrictions. In Data Transfer Mode, the host may use the fPP range. CMD9 retrieves the CSD, while optional CMD4 configures identified cards’ driver stages, bus layout, card count, and transfer frequency, switching the clock from fOD to fPP. CMD7 selects one card for the Transfer State; selecting another card releases the previous card to Stand-by. CMD7 with reserved RCA 0x0000 returns all cards to Stand-by. Data communication in this mode is point-to-point between the host and the selected card.

Reads and writes may be stopped with CMD12, and writes must be stopped before deselection. Block transfers use CRC protection. CMD17 reads one block and CMD18 reads consecutive blocks until CMD12. The standard block-transfer unit is 512 bytes, and CMD16 may set block lengths up to 512 bytes. Misaligned access is detected, reported through ADDRESS_ERROR, and aborted according to partial-access rules. CMD24 and CMD25 write one or multiple blocks. Write buffering may allow the next block to be sent while the previous block is programmed, with DAT0 held low when the card is busy. No buffering is available for CSD writes, write protection, or erase. Parameter-setting and read commands are prohibited during programming. Selecting another card moves a programming card to Disconnect State without terminating its operation, allowing it to be reselected. CMD0 or CMD15 terminates pending programming and may destroy data.

ACMD23 can pre-erase blocks to accelerate a following multiple-block write; terminated writes leave remaining block contents undefined, and ACMD22 reports the number of successfully written blocks. Erase and discard ranges are identified with CMD32 and CMD33, followed by CMD38. Out-of-sequence operations reset the sequence and set error status. Write-protected sectors remain intact during erase. DISCARD treats discarded contents as “don’t care,” is supported only by SDHC and SDXC cards over the SD interface, and has a 250 ms busy timeout. FULE logically erases the entire user area, uses CMD38 argument 00000002h, and has a one-second timeout. Cards signal busy operations by holding DAT0 low.

Three write-protection methods are described: a mechanical switch, optional internal card protection, and password protection. Password and length are stored in PWD and PWD_LEN registers, which are nonvolatile. Locked cards accept only specified basic commands, ACMD41, CMD16, and lock/unlock commands; data access is prohibited. CMD42 operates in Transfer State and carries its mode and password data in a CRC-protected block.

Card Ownership Protection (COP) adds Force Erase Password (FEP) registers and COP-specific CMD42 functions. COP Unlock, CMD42[1Fh], is required after reset when FEP is set. While FEP is set, Force Erase and PWD reset are disabled, FEP Force Erase requires the correct FEP, and PWD cannot be reset. COP Unlock enables FEP management and the extended command set. Standard Force Erase clears all user-area content and the PWD when FEP is unset; FEP Force Erase performs the same erasure using the correct FEP while retaining the FEP registers. Force Erase does not erase the secure area, preserves the card’s locked state during erasure, and clears temporary and group write protection afterward. CMD42 errors set LOCK_UNLOCK_FAILED, and card-lock state is reported through CARD_IS_LOCKED. Locked cards reject ACMD6, so bus width cannot be changed until the card is unlocked.

CMD55 makes the following command an application-specific command. Defined and legal ACMDs are identified by the APP_CMD status bit; undefined legal commands are treated as regular commands, while illegal commands produce an Illegal Command error.

CMD6 switches or queries card functions. It returns an R1 response and a 512-bit status block, and is valid in Transfer State. Mode 0 queries supported functions, selected functions, and maximum power; Mode 1 changes functions. Invalid selections cancel all requested changes, and busy functions cannot be changed. Function groups cover access mode, command-system extensions, driver strength, and power limit. Default power limit is 0.72 W; removable cards are limited to 1.80 W, and UHS-II power is the combined VDD1 and VDD2 consumption. In UHS-II mode, the power-limit group is mandatory, the command-system group is optional, and the access-mode and driver-strength groups are unused. Selected functions revert to defaults after CMD0, a power cycle, or selection of Function 0. High-Speed mode provides 25 MB/s using a 50 MHz clock and requires one-to-one host-to-card signal connections.

CMD8 is issued while the card is Idle to verify the host’s supply voltage before ACMD41. ACMD41’s response CCS value identifies SDSC when 0 and SDHC or SDXC when 1. SDSC uses byte addresses and command-defined block lengths, whereas SDHC and SDXC use block addresses, fixed 512-byte blocks, and disable partial and misaligned access. SDHC and SDXC also do not support write-protected groups.

The host may lower or stop the bus clock to manage power or data flow, except during ACMD41, when the clock must run at 100–400 kHz or be polled at intervals below 50 ms. Eight clock cycles are required after listed bus transactions, and a clock edge is needed to release a busy card’s DAT signal. CRC7 protects commands, most responses, CID, and CSD; CRC16 protects transferred data and is calculated separately on each line in wide-bus mode. A CRC failure prevents command execution and response while setting COM_CRC_ERROR.

Read timeouts are at least 100 ms for high- and extended-capacity cards; standard-capacity cards use the lower of 100 ms or 100 times the typical access time. Standard-capacity write timeouts use the lower of 250 ms or 100 times the typical program time. High-capacity cards generally limit busy duration to 250 ms, while specified SDXC conditions permit up to 500 ms. UHS-II busy is signaled after each Data Burst and may last up to one second.

Biogetica partnered with Research Needs to conduct clinical trials and research using an evidence-based, system-agnostic approach to natural medicine. A medRxiv preprint analyzes 13,152 genomes from Tennessee’s Biorepository and Integrative Genomics (BIG) Initiative, which links genomic data with electronic health records and environmental information. The predominantly pediatric cohort has more than 42,000 consented participants, 87% of them under age 18, and substantial ancestral diversity: 50% of sequenced participants had non-European or admixed ancestry, including 20% resembling African reference populations and 30% showing admixture. African ancestry was more common in urban areas, while European ancestry predominated in suburban areas, indicating geographic stratification that could confound association studies.

The analysis identified 771,717 novel single-nucleotide variants, comprising 11.2% of observed variants; many were rare, ancestry-specific, and predicted to have functional or clinical consequences. African and African-admixed participants averaged approximately 85,000 more variable sites than other groups, highlighting limitations of a single reference genome. Rare deleterious-to-synonymous variant ratios also differed by ancestry.

Electronic health record analyses found elevated odds of asthma and obesity among participants identifying as non-White, with especially high asthma prevalence in some suburban Memphis areas. Self-reported race did not consistently align with inferred genetic ancestry, and genetically related individuals sometimes reported different racial identities.

BIG combines research with community advisory boards and the Memphis Genomics Educational Network, which provides hands-on genomics education in public schools. The authors present BIG as a community-centered model for inclusive genomics and precision medicine, with future priorities including broader adult enrollment, community education, and pangenomic analyses.
