## Summary

This paper is a PRISMA-guided systematic review of empirically documented uses of large language models (LLMs) in education and the risks they carry, adopting a deliberately critical stance against techno-optimistic framings of AI in teaching. It asks four research questions: which educational LLM applications have been most empirically studied, what methods assess them, what risks arise, and which mitigation strategies have been proposed.

**Background.** The review explains that LLMs are trained on massive corpora and use transformer architectures to predict the next token, producing fluent output; students use tools such as ChatGPT, Gemini, Claude, Copilot, and DeepSeek for clarification, paraphrasing, brainstorming, problem-solving, and even generating full assignments. It organizes risks into three domains — inherent technical, pedagogical, and societal — with a Venn diagram showing overlaps. Technical risks include toxic content (training data includes toxic, biased and noisy material; models remain vulnerable to adversarial prompting and jail-breaking), misinformation (fluent outputs mistaken for reliable, "stochastic parrot" repetition), amplification of bias (explicit and implicit associations, persona conditioning, prompt framing effects; larger effects for younger and marginalized learners), hallucinations (categorized as intrinsic, extrinsic, amalgamated, and non-factual), and privacy violations from memorization and reproduction of identifiable data. Pedagogical risks are framed through Cognitive Load Theory (intrinsic, extraneous, germane load) and metacognitive theory, covering reduced cognitive engagement, over-reliance, diminished critical thinking, loss of student agency, memory erosion (users struggle to quote their own essays), and academic integrity problems tied to Self-Determination Theory's autonomy, competence, and relatedness needs. Societal risks comprise the AI divide (access, effective use, and outcome inequalities, concentrated in wealthy countries), data colonialism (unequal value exchange, e.g., Kenyan content-labour workers, student data used to train models aligned to Global North norms), environmental harm across the model life cycle (mining, manufacturing, data-centre energy, e-waste; GPT-3 training cited at ~1287 MWh and over 550 tons of CO₂), and absent sector-specific regulation.

**Methodology.** Searches spanned ACM DL, IEEE Xplore, Web of Science, ScienceDirect, and ERIC using queries across LLM/GenAI, education, and risk dimensions for 2015–2025 (search date 20 May 2025). Inclusion required peer-reviewed, empirical studies of LLM-based educational tools reporting risks; perception-only studies, model comparisons, and secondary/theoretical work were excluded. Rayyan was used for deduplication and screening by three independent reviewers with consensus resolution: 3,453 records screened, 3,068 excluded, 222 assessed, yielding 69 included studies (all 2023–2025) plus one added via forward references, for 70 papers. Studies were coded by authorship, method, model, educational context, risk types, and outcomes, then grouped into three application areas — operational effectiveness, personalized applications, and interactive learning tools — with subject-area breakdowns. Most studies used GPT-3.5 and, to a lesser extent, GPT-4.

**Operational effectiveness findings.** Comparative evaluations (same rubric and assignment given to LLMs and human educators, evaluated with Pearson correlation, Mann–Whitney U, t-tests, Wilcoxon, thematic analysis) found teacher feedback carries logical rigor, balance of direct corrections and indirect cues, contextual sensitivity, and pedagogical intentionality, whereas ChatGPT feedback rarely uses indirect strategies, repeats corrections, overcorrects, and shows superficial understanding of subjective or creative work; one study reported a moderate human–ChatGPT score correlation of r = 0.46 with ChatGPT more conservative and variable. In data processing, ChatGPT integration with Power BI raised privacy, outdated-training-data, API-responsiveness, and output-quality concerns, and curriculum tagging aligned strongly with US Common Core standards but not with English, Irish, South Korean, or Maharashtra standards, underscoring US-centricity. Domain knowledge studies found LLMs pass professional exams and complete university-level tasks at or above average student performance, while hallucinating, using outdated data, fabricating citations, and producing outputs often indistinguishable from human writing — with pre-service teachers consistently failing to identify AI authorship and being overconfident. Teaching-capability studies found elevated deceptive behaviour and dark-triad traits, and Anglocentric bias in evaluative language.

**Personalized applications findings.** ChatGPT altered scores for identical writing samples based on race, socioeconomic status, and school type, and prompt sequence influenced scoring; institutional data was the main source of bias in progress-monitoring algorithms. Content generation varied subtly with racial/ethnic, income, and disability labels (income and disability showing the largest disparities, gender and race the smallest), image generation portrayed chemists and medical students as male, and Confucian-ethical EFL narratives embedded WEIRD assumptions, gender bias, and problematic authority representations; ChatGPT also fabricated sources and could be manipulated into generating malicious macro code. In dropout prediction, decision tree, KNN, and MLP models trained on 52,000+ learners showed bias across fairness metrics, with oversampling and separate-group models failing to reduce and sometimes exacerbating bias. GPT-3.5 Turbo recommended STEM less often for LGBTQ and Hispanic users, with Asian students three times more likely to be directed to STEM than African-American students and higher-socioeconomic students 30% more likely. Bard, GPT-3.5, and PaLM detected only about half of biased content, while student studies showed transparency strongly shapes perceived fairness.

**Interactive learning tools findings.** Students showed "verification drift" and anchoring effects, spent significantly less time revising texts labelled AI-generated, became less engaged in later sessions, and produced better grammatical accuracy but weaker engagement, analysis, and research quality; feedback interaction was cognitively active but metacognitively limited ("metacognitive laziness"). An EEG study of 54 students writing SAT-style essays found systematic decreases in brain connectivity as external support increased, with LLM use associated with bypassed memory encoding. LLM exposure also shifted religious perceptions (favourable shifts for Christianity and Judaism, decline for Islam). Performance studies reported higher submission rates and assignment scores but lower creativity and post-test knowledge in an eleven-week secondary-school intervention; MATLAB benefits alongside 30.99% reporting incorrect outputs and 80.28% unmet expectations; and ChatGPT-improved writing accompanied significantly lower Ideal L2 Self scores, echoing "AI enfeeblement."

**Risks and mitigation.** Risk frequency tables identify superficial understanding (8) as the leading operational-effectiveness risk, bias (8) for personalized applications, and cognitive/metacognitive risks (9) plus behavioural risks (7) for interactive tools. Mitigation is organized by stakeholder: educators (human monitoring rather than sole grading, teacher training, data privacy, student guidance, transparency, revised learning objectives, LLM literacy); developers (robust training and evaluation, improved detection tools, bias diagnosis at data/training/inference stages, inclusion-focused participatory design, model legibility, human-in-the-loop governance, learner-centred design, explainability); students (verification, responsible use, AI literacy); and governments (data governance, stakeholder collaboration).

**LLM-Risk Adapted Learning Model.** Adapted from Self-Regulated Learning theory, the model reconceptualizes the learning cycle into Interaction, Monitoring, and Outcome stages, tracing how risks accumulate and compound rather than proceeding linearly. Interaction risks (superficial understanding, hallucinations, anthropomorphic characteristics, limited robustness) weaken interpretation during Monitoring (bias, passive processing, weak memory integration), surfacing at Outcome as reduced creativity, over-reliance, and limited motivation, which in turn reshape the next interaction cycle. Intervention points include prompt design and exposing model limitations at Interaction, source transparency and verification prompts at Monitoring, and self-reflection plus usage dashboards at Outcome.

**Conclusion and limitations.** The review consolidates empirical risk evidence across computer science, education, and cognitive psychology, maps applications, methods, and metrics, and calls for human-centred design supporting autonomy, competence, and relatedness. Limitations include a possibly dated search strategy, English-only coverage, and reliance on mostly short-term interventions. Future directions include refining measures of metacognition, collaboration, and trust, testing robustness with newer models, longitudinal studies, cross-cultural comparison, and design-oriented work embedding mitigations in everyday use, with concerns raised about how metacognitive and behavioural patterns may intensify with more powerful systems.

A commodity trading advisor (CTA) is an individual or organization that advises on or manages trading in futures, commodity options, currency swaps, and other derivatives. Most CTAs use systematic, model- and algorithm-based strategies, often emphasizing trend following or momentum across equities, bonds, currencies, commodities, and other global markets. Purely systematic CTAs rely on algorithmic signals without intervention, reducing the influence of human emotions, while some managers trade discretionarily. CTA funds generally operate as managed-futures hedge funds and are registered with the CFTC and members of the NFA. Compensation typically includes management fees and incentive fees tied to profits above a specified hurdle or high-water mark.

Trend-following strategies seek medium- to long-term trends through signal generation and exposure sizing. One example goes long the S&P 500 above its 200-day moving average and stays out below it; its backtest produced a 28% maximum drawdown and 6.73% CAGR, versus 7.16% for buy-and-hold without dividend adjustments. The article presents this as a simple starting point rather than a professional strategy.

The central principle is combining multiple strategies with low correlation, even when individual returns are modest, to reduce volatility and improve portfolio consistency. CTA strategies can provide systematic execution and risk management, but may require capital, market knowledge, and advanced trading expertise. Risks include trading losses, volatility, and unreliable data. Complexity alone may not add value.

The passage argues that Andropov had internal incentives to pursue an arms-control agreement: retaining military support while constraining U.S. defense programs, reducing economic pressure to increase military spending, and politically outflanking rivals. Since little appeared to be lost by negotiating, it recommends prioritizing INF talks, which offered leverage and urgency, while postponing START. A private diplomatic channel was preferable because Andropov favored secrecy and it would limit bureaucratic resistance and leaks from U.S. officials opposed to arms control. Rather than presenting a full proposal initially, the United States should send a short, serious letter acknowledging deteriorating U.S.-Soviet relations and continuing disagreements while emphasizing peace, problem resolution, and reducing nuclear arms, and invite Andropov to respond through the same channel.

The paper proposes a meta-learning framework that trains Fourier Neural Operators (FNOs) to approximate the inverse Hessian operator in 4D-Var data assimilation. The FNO maps the adjoint-derived vector \(f\) to an initial-state estimate, with sparse observations implicitly embedded in \(f\). This estimate initializes conjugate gradient (CG), forming FNO-CG, which is also applicable to incremental 4D-Var for nonlinear PDEs.

Experiments use a linear periodic advection equation with varied background states, error covariances, and observation configurations. Each training and test set contains 5,400 samples. Standalone FNO predictions are generally less accurate than standard CG but provide useful structural information for initialization. FNO-CG reduces the average relative error from \(4.26\times10^{-2}\) to \(1.61\times10^{-2}\) and average iterations from 127 to 105, corresponding to reported reductions of 62% and 17%. Improvements are especially pronounced for poorly conditioned problems. Future work will extend the approach to nonlinear PDEs, including chaotic systems such as the Kuramoto–Sivashinsky equation.

Collected reports from October 25, 2001, detailed Enron’s financial, credit and trading difficulties. Enron reported a $1.01 billion after-tax charge covering its broadband and water-trading ventures and the unraveling of two partnerships overseen by CFO Andrew Fastow. The charge contributed to a third-quarter loss of $618 million, compared with a $292 million profit a year earlier; without the charge, Enron would have earned $393 million.

Enron placed Fastow on leave and named Jeff McMahon as CFO to restore investor confidence. The change followed an SEC inquiry into related-party partnerships Fastow managed, broader questions about Enron’s accounting and off-balance-sheet transactions, and shareholder lawsuits. CEO Kenneth Lay also resigned from i2 Technologies’ board because of his Enron responsibilities.

Standard & Poor’s affirmed Enron’s ratings but revised its outlook to negative, citing the company’s market-value decline, reduced financial flexibility and difficulties rebuilding its balance sheet. Enron planned to use asset-sale proceeds and potentially new equity to reduce debt. S&P said trading volumes, counterparties, risk management and trading discipline remained sound and did not see an immediate liquidity threat, but warned that a downgrade could follow if asset sales or equity issuance fell short. Fitch placed Enron’s securities on negative watch, while Moody’s was reviewing the company for a possible downgrade.

Energy trading partners reported little change in their dealings with Enron, though several were monitoring its exposure and credit. Enron remained a major market maker, with its EnronOnline platform central to U.S. power and gas trading and Enron serving as counterparty to each platform trade. Some traders limited credit, increased caution or shifted business elsewhere, while others said activity remained normal. Analysts warned that reduced EnronOnline volume could create liquidity problems and volatility across energy markets.

Enron said it had roughly $3.35 billion-$3.4 billion in bank credit lines, could raise cash through asset sales and had asked Citicorp to arrange a $750 million loan. It had about $1.85 billion in commercial paper outstanding and was offering two-week paper at a 3 percent yield. Fitch also questioned whether assets backing $3.2 billion of debt at Marlin Water Trust II and Osprey were worth enough to repay it; Enron said asset-sale proceeds would be used to pay that debt.

Enron shares closed at $16.35, down 6 cents and declining for a seventh consecutive session, after falling 49 percent that week and 80 percent year to date. Analysts welcomed the CFO change as a step toward rebuilding credibility but continued to question Enron’s partnership disclosures, debt obligations, diversification and transparency. CNN coverage also cited broadband losses, approximately $3.3 billion in notes due within 20 months, lower energy prices and possible costs from other partnership dissolutions.

Additional coverage included an AP report that selective technology and energy buying reversed an early market decline, and a RealMoney column asking how average investors could obtain timely bond information without institutional data tools.

Soccer coaches should use contingency planning and “what if” questions to avoid improvising when problems arise. Applicable responses should be developed collaboratively with coaches, players, and/or parents, documented, and communicated to everyone. Areas include communications (normal and emergency contact, electronic backups, cancellations, location changes, absences, and backup coaches); player and practice issues (medical needs, injuries, leadership, eligibility, fees, disruptive behavior, team dynamics, and varied field conditions); pregame preparations (equipment, documents, officials, linespersons, player passes, kits, field issues, weather, and transport); in-game contingencies (injuries and emergency care, ejections, cards, suspension, lightning, fighting, referee problems, unexpected lineups, equipment failure, and multiple-player illness); postgame plans (uncollected players and vehicle breakdowns); and extended absences (illness, travel, departure, and succession). Coaches are advised to create checklists, delegate, identify available help, and prepare assistants, players, and parents for contingencies while recognizing that not every possibility can be anticipated.

Darren McGregor praised Hibs’ 3–2 comeback win at Rangers as “character-building” after they conceded early and faced an intense Ibrox atmosphere. Simon Murray equalised, Ryan Jack was sent off, James Tavernier scored an own goal and Vykantas Slivka completed the comeback before Tavernier’s late consolation. McGregor supported Jack’s dismissal and reserved particular praise for Murray, who reached ten goals in seven competitive matches.

Professors and support staff at Nova Scotia Community College ratified six-year 2014–2020 agreements, with 55% of faculty and 64% of support staff voting in favor. They include 7% wage increases and retirement service-award payout options.

- Technologic Partners named its Internet Outlook Investors’ Choice winners: **Bluelight.com, DoDots, Firedrop, Google, GuruNet, iSyndicate, Octopus, Responsys.com, Vitessa, and Vividence**.

Other financing announcements included **Pax Clearing ($67.5 million), Circadence ($51 million), Epoch Internet ($27 million), i2i ($16 million), OnePage ($12.5 million), Prefer Network ($12 million), iMedica ($12 million), Allrecipes.com ($6.5 million), Optranet ($6.7 million), FoodMarketplace.com ($6.1 million), Chevin Software Engineering ($4.2 million), Lost Wax ($3.5 million), Linbox ($2.1 million), Replicon ($2 million), SiteBurst ($2 million), b4bpartner ($1.8 million), and CraniaMania ($1 million)**. Motorola, Intel Capital, Andersen Consulting, and eHatchery made undisclosed investments in SecureOps, MontaVista Software, Everypath, and Primitive Root, respectively.

New companies and ventures included wireless-network technology provider **mDiversity**, interactive digital-television company **Cinema Entertainment Group**, and venture research and advisory group **Daedalus Venture Group**.

Governance and leadership changes included new board appointments at **Fenix Enterprises, Definity Health, and Troika Networks**; HealtheCare’s renaming as **Definity Health**; and new chief executives at **eRIDE, I-Impact, and PetroWEB.com**. **MediaPrise** appointed co-founders as CEO, COO, and CTO. **Vestar Capital Partners** opened its first European office in Paris and planned additional offices in Milan and Frankfurt.

The ADS9803 is an eight-channel, 20-bit, 2 MSPS data-acquisition system with a built-in analog front end. It supports 2- and 4-lane source-synchronous data interfaces using SDR or DDR, producing data on D[3:0] plus DCLKOUT and FCLKOUT. Conversion results are transmitted MSB first in 24-bit packets, with the final six bits zero. The interface also provides XOR-based output randomization, simple averaging that halves the output rate, moving averaging that preserves the output rate, and fixed, ramp, and alternating test patterns for two channel groups.

The device requires a free-running sampling clock and register initialization after power-up or reset. Users can configure analog ranges, bandwidth, common-mode settings, data-interface format, and other options. Speed-boost mode supports up to 8 MSPS while continuously converting a selected channel pair and leaving the other six channels idle.

Configuration registers are organized into three banks. SPI writes select a bank before accessing it, while reads require enabling read mode. Daisy-chain configurations support multiple ADCs using 24 SCLKs per device for register operations.

For ATE applications, the ADS9803 can receive PMU signals directly or through multiplexers. It provides low-noise and wide-bandwidth modes, with wide-bandwidth settling to 99.95% full scale in 7.5 µs. Its post-calibration total unadjusted error is 0.0015% at 25°C ±5°C. The datasheet also documents power supplies, bypass-capacitor placement, PCB layout guidance, register definitions, development resources, and handling precautions.

Low-volatility investing targets stocks or sectors with relatively stable prices and market-relative volatility below 1. It aims to reduce portfolio volatility, limit large declines, and provide more consistent returns, making it potentially suitable for risk-averse or retirement-focused investors. Implementation can involve low-volatility ETFs or mutual funds such as SPLV, or selecting companies with stable earnings, consistent dividends, predictable businesses, low debt, and low beta. Portfolios should be diversified across sectors, reviewed regularly, and rebalanced annually or less. The strategy generally requires a long horizon of years or decades.

Potential drawbacks include lower returns in some periods, prolonged underperformance, and suitability risks for day or swing traders. Historical research cited in the passage found that low-volatility stocks outperformed the most volatile stocks over long periods. Kenneth French’s 1964–2015 analysis found that the three lowest-volatility deciles had not produced negative returns in any ten-year period since 1974, while the most volatile stocks performed particularly poorly during major market declines. The low-volatility effect was also documented across 21 developed-market and 12 emerging-market exchanges. Research on Berkshire Hathaway associated Buffett’s performance with leverage and investments in cheap, safe, high-quality stocks, although its Sharpe ratio was still modest. Backtesting can estimate historical performance, but it does not reliably predict future results.

The speaker mourns a retiring Swedish hockey star, calling him one of the best Swedish players, a role model, and an underrated professional. He praises Adam Larsson’s influence on young Swedes and Henrik Tallinder’s two-decade career, four Stanley Cups, and seven Norris Trophies. He says he feels physically fit after practicing for two to three weeks and would welcome the chance to play in the league. Although comparing European greats is difficult, he considers Jaromir Jagr among the elite for his consistency, longevity, and contribution to four Stanley Cups.

A TeamLease survey found Delhi had the highest job-loss risk among nine cities, followed by Bengaluru and Hyderabad, while Pune had the lowest. Industrial manufacturing and allied sectors faced the highest risk; healthcare and telecom had the lowest.

Lord Williams’s School headteacher David Wybron has asked the Government to address what he calls “The Perfect Storm” in state education. He argues that new, content-heavy GCSE exams place greater pressure on state-school pupils than independent-school peers, who may use coursework and less memory-based assessments. He urges a review of GCSE content and structure, school choice between GCSEs and IGCSEs, and no league-table penalty for choosing IGCSEs, citing concern that exam pressure is discouraging further study and that prescribed content does not build needed skills.

He also highlights a teacher-recruitment crisis, reporting that initial teacher-training recruitment targets have been missed for five years. He asks for all teaching disciplines to be added to the shortage occupation list and for education visa treatment comparable to health care.

Finally, he cites inflation, rising staffing costs, a heating-system replacement and projected funding losses of over £1,000 per pupil caused by the funding formula’s 3% cap, calling for greater fairness and Government attention to school finance.

The Triple RSI strategy modifies standard RSI with four variables—three tied to RSI—and uses mean-reversion rules based on RSI readings, the 200-day moving average, and entry/exit signals. Inspired by Larry Connors’ R3 strategy, it was backtested on SPY in AmiBroker. Since 1993, it produced 83 trades, an average gain of 1.4% per trade, a reported win rate of about 90%, and a profit factor of 5. The article suggests it may complement a long-term buy-and-hold portfolio, with cautious use of leverage.

At E3 2017, Uncharted: The Lost Legacy featured Chloe Frazer and mercenary Nadine Ross battling well-equipped enemies through ancient structures. Naughty Dog started it weeks after Uncharted 4 wrapped.

The AMD Geode CS5535 Rev A3 specification update documents silicon deviations, their implications, and available workarounds; issue numbers are nonsequential because resolved issues are omitted.

- **Interrupt, timer, and DMA behavior:** PIT latch and count-mode operations differ from expected behavior; XPIC AEOI can generate duplicate interrupts; DMA rotating priority does not rotate transfer order; PIC polling is unsupported, and edge-configured PIC inputs can miss interrupts after clock gating. UART and LPC I/O accesses are unreliable during legacy DMA, and USB/UART clock gating has operational limitations.
- **Storage and DMA controllers:** ATAC and ACC PRD tables require proper alignment and initialization; ATAC can hang with non-DWORD-aligned PRDs. A preceding host-terminated UDMA read can cause CRC corruption during a later UDMA write. SSMI does not reliably block IDE I/O, reverse-order UDMA setup fails, and certain early ATAPI interrupts reset the bus-master engine.
- **ACPI, power management, and KEL:** Byte access to PM1_EN or PM1_STS hangs; improperly sized PMC writes can corrupt other registers; thermal alarms, low-battery flags, S3 wake inputs, Sleep Clock controls, and Sleep_X/Sleep_Y timing have documented defects. KEL emulation fails to distinguish writes to I/O ports 060h and 064h, while Snoop mode and AuxOutputFull also behave incorrectly.
- **Other defects:** The GLIU debug port can hang, debug detection and error flags are unreliable, USB electrical protection is insufficient, certain PCI accesses or back-to-back reads fail, RTC CMOS RAM reads can return incorrect data, SMB NEGACK and hold-time behavior is incorrect, GLPCI retry counts include unrelated retries, and GPIO atomic writes after suspend clear nonselected bits.

Recommended mitigations include following specified command sequences, aligning PRD tables to DWORD boundaries, avoiding unsupported clock-gating, polling, DMA, and debug features, using single-transfer DMA, adding USB over-voltage protection, performing GPIO read-modify-writes after suspend, configuring sleep delays, using PWRBTN# for S3 wake, restoring KEL state in software, and applying a PLD workaround for LPC synchronization failures.

Defensive tackles are interior defensive linemen focused on stopping the run and pressuring quarterbacks. They stop ball carriers through quick backfield penetration, shed blocks, chase runners, absorb double teams, and disrupt passing plays, often without receiving flashy statistics. Their size and physical style suit trench play, and their pass-rushing helps occupy blockers, free edge rushers, disrupt quarterbacks, and allow linebackers and defensive backs to remain in coverage. The position developed from the nose guard and may also be called a nose tackle or nose guard. Defensive tackles are generally strong, agile, tough, compact, and sturdy, typically measuring 6'2"–6'4" and weighing 300–335 pounds. Aaron Donald and “Mean” Joe Greene are highlighted among the position’s best players.

The paper introduces PRDNet, a multimodal crystal-representation framework for property prediction. Existing machine-learning force fields and graph-based encodings use finite local neighborhoods, which can miss long-range interactions and map distinct crystal structures to identical representations. Diffraction provides a unique reciprocal-space encoding of periodic atomic arrangements, but conventional X-ray, electron, and neutron probes have limited sensitivity to atoms in different local environments because of fixed or weakly contrasting form factors. PRDNet therefore introduces a learned pseudo-particle that generates symmetry-invariant synthetic diffraction patterns and combines this reciprocal-space information with graph embeddings. The model is designed to remain invariant to crystal rotations, reflections, and translations. Crystal structures are represented by atomic types, coordinates, and a periodic lattice, while diffraction is expressed through structure factors. Evaluations on Materials Project, JARVIS-DFT, and MatBench reportedly achieve state-of-the-art performance across common crystal property prediction tasks.

NVIDIA’s GA10x Ampere architecture supports gaming, data-center, and professional-workstation workloads. DLSS uses Tensor Cores and a deep neural network to combine details from multiple frames into high-quality images with improved performance; Ampere supports 9x super-resolution scaling, enabling 8K ray-traced gaming at 60 fps on the GeForce RTX 3090.

Developed with Micron, GDDR6X uses PAM4 signaling to transfer two bits per clock edge, while MTA encoding and new training, adaptation, and equalization schemes address signal noise. GA10x GPUs support data rates up to 19.5 Gbps and peak bandwidth of 936 GB/s, more than 52% above the TU102. Pseudo-independent memory channels assist BVH ray traversal, while Error Detection and Replay detects and retries faulty GDDR6X transmissions.

NVIDIA RTX IO uses Microsoft DirectStorage to send compressed assets directly from storage to the GPU for lossless decompression, reducing CPU workloads and improving loading, streaming, frame rates, object pop-in, and stutter. The document claims performance gains of up to 100x over hard drives and traditional storage APIs and identifies applications for large game and creative datasets.

The GA10x-based NVIDIA A40 data-center GPU provides increased FP32, ray-tracing, AI, and PCIe Gen4 performance compared with the Quadro RTX 6000. It includes 48 GB of memory, scalable to 96 GB through NVLink, virtualization support, Quadro Sync, and compatibility with the NVIDIA EGX Platform.

Ampere GPUs support 4K at 120 Hz and 8K at 60 Hz through DisplayPort 1.4a and HDMI 2.1 with display-stream compression. Fifth-generation NVDEC provides hardware decoding for MPEG-2, VC-1, H.264, H.265, VP8, VP9, and AV1, including 8K60 HDR AV1 playback with low CPU usage. Seventh-generation NVENC provides hardware encoding for high-quality, low-latency streaming, including 4K H.264 and 8K HEVC.

The architecture’s second-generation RT Cores double ray/triangle-intersection performance and add motion-blur acceleration and concurrent ray tracing with shading or compute. Third-generation Tensor Cores support structural sparsity, while the overall architecture provides up to twice the programmable-shading, ray-tracing, and AI performance of Turing.

The GeForce RTX 3090 uses GA102, 82 streaming multiprocessors, 10,496 CUDA cores, and 24 GB of GDDR6X. The RTX 3070 uses GA104 and GDDR6, lacks NVLink, and is described as faster than the RTX 2080 Ti. The RTX A6000 provides 10,752 CUDA cores, 48 GB of GDDR6 scalable to 96 GB via NVLink, accelerated motion blur and AI denoising, and professional rendering, simulation, virtual-production, and deep-learning capabilities. The document also provides benchmark conditions and legal disclaimers regarding specification accuracy, warranties, and intended uses.

The passage excerpts the Physical Layer Simplified Specification Version 6.00 for SD memory cards. It defines legal and undefined commands, including the special APP_CMD-status behavior of ACMD41. CMD6 switches or expands card functions through access-mode, command-system, driver-strength, and power-limit groups. Mode 0 queries supported functions and maximum power, while Mode 1 sets functions; busy functions cannot be changed, and invalid selections are ignored. CMD6 returns an R1 response and 512-bit status, has a 100 ms timeout, and resets selected functions after CMD0, CMD6 with Function 0, or a power cycle. The default power limit is 0.72 W.

The specification also describes optional 25 MB/s High-Speed mode, the command-system functions assigned to CMD34–37, CMD50, and CMD57, and CMD8 voltage checking before ACMD41. SDSC cards use byte addressing and CMD16-defined block lengths, whereas SDHC and SDXC cards use block addressing and fixed 512-byte blocks.

Bus-clock control, CRC7 and CRC16 error detection, illegal-command handling, and read, write, and erase timeouts are specified. Commands use a 48-bit format and are organized into command classes and state transitions, with modified behavior in UHS-II mode. Responses include R1, R2, R3, R6, and R7, while Card Status, SD Status, and Task Status convey different operational information.

Speed-class methods are optional in this version. Speed Class performance covers Classes 2, 4, 6, and 10 through allocation and recording units, fragmented-write calculations, FAT-update timing, and performance requirements. SDXC requires sequential writes to entirely free allocation units, does not support move performance, and uses exFAT-related FAT, bitmap, directory, and continuous-information updates. CMD20 controls Speed Class recording and identifies directory and CI writes; it is mandatory for SDXC and optional for SDHC. UHS Speed Grades 0, 1, and 3 represent performance below 10 MB/s, at least 10 MB/s, and at least 30 MB/s, respectively.

China’s official manufacturing PMI rose to 51.9 in May from 51.4, exceeding forecasts and marking the fastest expansion in eight months. Production, new orders, exports and industrial profits strengthened, but economists said gains may reflect pollution-control easing and shipment front-loading amid trade tensions rather than stronger demand. Small-firm activity contracted, funding concerns increased and cost pressures persisted. China advanced planned U.S. tariffs on up to $50 billion in Chinese imports. The non-manufacturing PMI edged up to 54.9, construction activity eased, and the composite PMI rose to 54.6. Economists expect growth to slow to 6.5% this year from 6.9% in 2017 amid debt controls, higher borrowing costs and weak investment.

Intel shares climbed 3%, taking the monthly gain above 50% and the stock above $37. The surge increased the value of the Trump administration’s 10% stake to roughly $16 billion, following its $8.9 billion investment in August.

In his farewell address, President Truman reflects on nearly eight years in office, the demands of the presidency, and the orderly transfer of power to President Eisenhower. He defends his administration’s Cold War policies, including aid to Greece and Turkey, the Marshall Plan, the Berlin Airlift, NATO, defense pacts, and military action in Korea, while arguing that firm resistance to communism could preserve peace and eventually produce change. He also cites American prosperity, expanding civil rights, and the public’s essential support. Concluding that he and his wife have no regrets and did their best, Truman thanks the American people and bids them farewell.

The paper introduces Truthful Text Summarization (TTS), an incentive-aligned pipeline for filtering unreliable sources before LLM summarization. TTS generates atomic claims from each source’s peers using a leave-one-out construction, extracts each source’s support, contradiction, or abstention stance, and scores sources by informative peer agreement rather than simple consensus. Low-scoring sources are filtered out before the final summary is generated, without requiring payments to sources.

The scoring rule is designed so truthful, careful reporting maximizes expected inclusion and visibility. Theoretical analysis establishes asymptotic informed truthfulness, strong truthfulness against significant reporting deviations under a hard-threshold design, and finite-sample bounds for approximately informed truthfulness. The framework also remains strategically equivalent when sources implement reporting policies through prose.

Experiments on 300-query subsets of Natural Questions and ClashEval used four reliable and two unreliable sources per query. TTS achieved 70.7% answer accuracy on Natural Questions and 74.3% on ClashEval, compared with 34.0% and 14.0% for the strongest tested baselines. It separated reliable sources from deceptive and prompt-injection sources without ground-truth labels, and truthful scores decreased as sources deviated from accurate reporting. Unlike majority-based scoring, TTS resisted four coordinated uninformative sources while preserving the ranking of reliable documents. Proposed future extensions include reputation priors, tighter retrieval integration, and multilingual or streaming adaptations.

Lilly Nguyen and Phil De Carlos married in Texas Children’s Hospital chapel on New Year’s Day so their premature son, Lucas, could be part of the wedding. After proposing in Lucas’s NICU room, the couple and Lilly’s other children visited the infant following the ceremony.

The Opportunity Project (TOP), a Wichita nonprofit serving children ages 1–5 in three high-poverty Wichita and Derby centers, uses Reggio Emilia–inspired classrooms where children choose activities and teachers guide learning. A study found TOP graduates outperformed similar nonparticipants in academics, social skills and attendance; by third grade they were 19% more likely, and by eighth grade 107% more likely, to read at grade level. TOP also provides scholarships, family counseling and education assistance. Parent Café workshops offer families research, resources and support. William Eckels said the program taught both him and his son about child development, inspiring him to become a preschool or elementary teacher.

MIT and the Carnegie Institution of Science released a public dataset, open-source software, and tutorial based on 20 years of W.M. Keck Observatory observations to support exoplanet research. The dataset contains nearly 61,000 measurements of more than 1,600 nearby stars and has yielded over 100 potential planets. Regularly updated records include observation dates, measured stellar velocities and errors, and indicators of stellar activity.

NVIDIA’s Turing GPU architecture combines rasterization, real-time ray tracing, AI, and simulation. Its NVENC supports H.265/HEVC 8K encoding at 30 fps and provides up to 25% HEVC and 15% H.264 bitrate savings; NVDEC adds HEVC 4:4:4 8-, 10-, and 12-bit decoding and VP9 10/12-bit HDR support.

Turing supports USB Type-C and VirtualLink, an open standard that delivers power, display, and data to VR headsets through one connector while supporting four HBR3 DisplayPort lanes and a SuperSpeed USB 3 link. NVLink replaces MIO and PCIe for SLI transfers: TU102 has two x8 links and TU104 one, providing 25 GB/s per direction per link and supporting two-way SLI while enabling new display topologies.

RT Cores in TU102, TU104, and TU106 accelerate BVH traversal and ray-triangle intersection testing. Combined with hybrid rendering, denoising, and APIs including NVIDIA RTX, OptiX, Microsoft DXR, and Vulkan, they enable real-time ray tracing at more than 10 Giga Rays per second and roughly ten times Pascal’s software-based performance. Hybrid rendering uses rasterization where effective and ray tracing for reflections, refractions, shadows, and other effects. The RTX-OPS metric weights workload use of Tensor, FP32, RT, and INT32 pipelines; one RTX 2080 Ti example totals 78 RTX-OPS.

NVIDIA NGX applies deep neural networks through Turing Tensor Cores. DLSS produces quality similar to temporal anti-aliasing with roughly half the shading work, while DLSS 2X approaches 64-times-supersampled quality. NGX also provides content-aware inpainting, AI-generated slow-motion frames, and AI Super Rez for 2x, 4x, or 8x upscaling.

Turing adds mesh shading with task and mesh shaders to reduce per-object CPU draw calls and support very large object counts, level-of-detail selection, and dynamic geometry manipulation. Variable Rate Shading controls shading independently per 16×16 region and supports content-adaptive, motion-adaptive, and foveated rendering. Texture Space Shading decouples visibility and appearance sampling, reuses shaded texels, and improves temporal stability and stereo VR efficiency. Multi-View Rendering processes up to four views per hardware pass and up to 32 at the API level, enabling efficient stereo, multi-projector, shadow-map, and multi-instance rendering. Turing also supports Tier 2 resource heaps and Tier 3 bindless constant-buffer and unordered-access views.

The full TU104 contains six GPCs, 48 streaming multiprocessors, 3,072 CUDA Cores, 368 Tensor Cores, 48 RT Cores, 13.6 billion transistors, a 256-bit memory interface, and one x8 NVLink link. Tesla T4 uses a reduced TU104 configuration with 40 SMs, 2,560 CUDA Cores, 320 Tensor Cores, and 320 GB/s memory bandwidth for inference workloads. TU106, used in the GeForce RTX 2070, contains 36 SMs, 2,304 CUDA Cores, 288 Tensor Cores, 36 RT Cores, and 10.8 billion transistors, but has no NVLink or SLI support.

The passage also explains ray casting, BVH construction and refitting, denoising, and ray-traced shadows, ambient occlusion, and reflections, including examples from Battlefield V and Shadow of the Tomb Raider. It concludes with NVIDIA warranty, liability, licensing, trademark, and copyright notices.

On the 10th day of the U.S. government shutdown, the Trump administration began permanent reductions in force across federal agencies, with layoffs reportedly affecting Treasury, Health and Human Services, Commerce, Education, Energy, EPA, Homeland Security, Housing and Urban Development, and Interior. Union groups filed or promised lawsuits, while Democratic senators and Republican Sen. Susan Collins criticized the cuts. The administration also froze or cut billions in funding for projects in Democratic-controlled states and cities. Funding bills failed for a seventh time in the Senate, with Democrats demanding extended Affordable Care Act tax credits in any deal to reopen the government.

Amazon.com, Inc.’s unaudited Form 10-Q for the quarter ended June 30, 2018 reported Q2 net sales of $52.9 billion, up 39% from $38.0 billion, and six-month sales of $103.9 billion, up 41% from $73.7 billion. Q2 operating income rose to $3.0 billion from $628 million, net income increased to $2.5 billion from $197 million, and diluted EPS was $5.07 versus $0.40. For the first six months, net income was $4.2 billion and diluted EPS was $8.34.

Q2 segment sales and operating results were $32.2 billion and $1.8 billion for North America, $14.6 billion and a $494 million loss for International, and $6.1 billion and $1.6 billion for AWS. Sales growth primarily reflected increased unit sales, third-party seller activity, Whole Foods Market, and AWS customer usage. Operating cash flow was $7.4 billion for Q2 and $5.7 billion for the first six months, compared with $3.9 billion and $2.2 billion in the prior-year periods. At June 30, 2018, cash and cash equivalents totaled $19.8 billion, marketable securities $7.2 billion, total assets $134.1 billion, and stockholders’ equity $35.0 billion.

Amazon adopted new revenue-recognition guidance in 2018, increasing retained earnings by approximately $650 million and reclassifying Prime fees and certain advertising revenue from product sales to service sales. It also adopted guidance on income taxes and restricted cash. Amazon planned to adopt new lease accounting in the first quarter of 2019 and expected a material impact on its balance sheet and related disclosures.

Amazon acquired Ring on April 12, 2018 for approximately $853 million net of cash acquired and made other acquisitions totaling $39 million. Combined consideration of $892 million was allocated primarily to $607 million of goodwill and $446 million of intangible assets.

The company had approximately $24.3 billion of unsecured senior notes outstanding. It established a $7 billion commercial paper program and a $7 billion revolving credit agreement in April 2018; no amounts were outstanding under either as of June 30, 2018. Total contractual commitments were $122.3 billion. Amazon reported $27.1 billion of cash, cash equivalents, and marketable securities and stated that operating cash flow, available balances, and borrowing arrangements should meet anticipated operating cash needs for at least 12 months.

Disclosed contingencies included sanctions-related voluntary reporting to U.S. agencies, indirect-tax claims, patent litigation, IRS transfer-pricing proceedings, and an approximately €250 million European Commission state-aid recovery. Tax contingencies totaled approximately $3.3 billion at June 30, 2018, and no common stock repurchases were made during the first six months of 2018.

Vladimir Guerrero Jr. was born in Montreal in 1999 to Hall of Fame outfielder and designated hitter Vladimir Guerrero Sr. and Riquelma Ramos. After his parents separated, he moved with his mother and grandparents to the Dominican Republic while spending summers in the United States with his father. Guerrero Sr., raised in the Dominican Republic, recorded 2,590 MLB hits, won the 2004 AL MVP award, made nine All-Star teams and earned eight Silver Slugger awards before his 2018 Hall of Fame induction. He and Guerrero Jr. have established several father-son records, and the younger Guerrero said matching his father’s nine All-Star selections is a goal.

Guerrero Jr. married Nathalie Guerrero in March 2023. They have two daughters: Vlaimel, born in August 2017, and Vlaishel, born in August 2018.

His younger brother Pablo Guerrero is a Texas Rangers prospect. His half-brother Vladi Miguel Guerrero signed with the New York Mets in 2024. Another uncle, Wilton Guerrero, played in MLB from 1996 through 2004 and taught Guerrero Jr. how to play and practice baseball. Uncle Julio Guerrero spent four seasons in the Boston Red Sox minor-league system. His godfather is Hall of Fame pitcher Pedro Martinez, who was teammates with Guerrero Sr. and has publicly praised Guerrero Jr.

Two cousins also played professionally: Gabriel Guerrero appeared for the Cincinnati Reds before retiring in 2022, and Gregory Guerrero spent five seasons in the New York Mets organization. Guerrero Jr.’s mother has primarily remained outside the spotlight, though she was seriously ill in 2023 while Guerrero played in games honoring her.

Unico Properties is modernizing Smith Tower’s manually operated elevators to improve safety, reliability, accessibility and service while preserving the 103-year-old building’s historic character. The work, begun in June after landmark approval, includes changes to call buttons, cab doors and operating panels. At least one elevator operator will remain, though other operator positions will end by mid-2018.

Hamilton Beale, an operator since 1999, plans to leave Seattle for Norfolk, Virginia, partly because of the automation. The building opened in 1914 with eight original elevators and was once the tallest west of the Mississippi River. It now houses businesses including Pixar, Rubicon, Cozi and Portent. Renovations include a Prohibition-inspired café and general store, while the 35th-floor Observatory and bar offer historic character and city views. Worker Hal Mueller said the sounds, mechanics and personal interaction of the traditional elevator rides made the building especially appealing during his job interview.

Diedrick Grafing, since deceased, deposited $2,000 with the East River Savings Institution and $3,000 with the Metropolitan Savings Bank in passbooks reading "in trust for Catharine Heilmann," and regularly drew the interest for his support until his death in August 1894. His executrices sued Heilmann, who had been interpleaded as defendant in place of the banks, alleging the deposits were intended to remain his property during life and pass to her at his death for distribution among certain relatives per a letter found among his papers. Heilmann denied consent to those terms and claimed the funds plus interest were hers.

The court held the deposits created a valid trust, not a gift: retention of the passbooks and the drawing of interest were not inconsistent with an intent to create a trust (citing Martin v. Funk, Willis v. Smyth, Mabie v. Bailey), and Cunningham v. Davenport did not apply because the beneficiary survived the depositor. Grafing's letter directing her disposition of the funds, and her receipt in July 1894 of $2,000 drawn from one account, confirmed his intention; the payment was presumed given in satisfaction of an antecedent debt rather than as a loan. Even if the money was payable to Heilmann only on the depositor's death, that would not make the transaction testamentary, since her interest vested at the time of deposit (Van Cott v. Prentice). Any promise by her to pay others leaves those parties to their own remedies and does not affect her rights in the fund. Judgment was affirmed with costs, all concurring except Brown, P. J., who was not sitting.

House Democrats Nancy Pelosi and Elijah Cummings cited a fake Michael Flynn Twitter account while criticizing Congress’s investigation of Flynn’s discussions with Russian officials. Both later acknowledged the mistake, and The New York Times also removed references to the false tweets and corrected its story.

The 123 reversal strategy is a three-swing technical-analysis formation that signals a potential trend reversal. A bearish 123 top forms when an uptrend fails to make a higher high and then breaks below the previous low; a bullish 123 bottom forms when a downtrend fails to make a lower low and then breaks above the previous high. It resembles a double top or bottom, but the second swing does not reach the prior extreme.

Entries occur at the close of the breakout through point 2 or the next bar’s open, with a possible retest before entry. Stop-loss orders are placed beyond point 3—or point 1 in volatile markets—and profit targets are projected by measuring the pattern. Partial profits and trailing stops may also be used.

The strategy applies to stocks, forex, commodities, and Bitcoin, although the article advises against stock shorting based solely on technical analysis and favors bullish setups. Backtests using GLD produced promising bullish results, including a 2.22 profit factor with a 20-day exit, while bearish performance was weaker. The article notes that the strategy’s subjective rules may allow further improvement.

The disclosure describes cooperative monitoring networks that combine existing security and automation systems to detect, assess, and respond to events at local or neighborhood scale. A system may include monitoring control units, sensors, cameras, lighting and household-device controls, user devices, a monitoring application server, and a central alarm station server with operator terminals. These components communicate through wired or wireless networks.

When an alarm or other event is detected, the system evaluates it against rules and user preferences to determine whether a cooperative monitoring network should be activated. With participant consent, nearby monitoring systems may be selected based on proximity, occupancy, preferences, or mobile-device location. The systems then share alerts and sensor, image, and camera data to coordinate tracking, activate lights, control cameras, identify entities of interest, and notify users. Networks may expand or contract as events move, and cascading notifications may continue until someone handles the incident.

Described applications include tracking an intruder through neighboring cameras, responding to unaddressed medical emergencies, providing assistance through a mobile panic application, and assessing neighborhood-wide malfunctions. Comparing data across systems can distinguish isolated property failures from shared problems such as power loss, radio-frequency jamming, or abnormal solar-panel readings. User interfaces allow configuration of property-specific and cooperative events.

Hajime is a rival IoT malware that researchers describe as more tenacious and resilient than Mirai. It scans for poorly secured cameras, DVRs, and routers, tries common credentials, and installs malicious software. Since its discovery, Hajime has spread unabated, with an estimated 100,000 infected devices globally. Unlike Mirai, Hajime uses a decentralized peer-to-peer network based on BitTorrent protocols, allowing infected devices to relay instructions and making botnet-wide blocking more difficult. Researchers have not observed Hajime launching DDoS attacks, and its operators and ultimate purpose remain unknown, though cybercrime is one possible use. Hajime appears more widespread than Mirai but has infected a different, smaller pool of devices, including those using ARM architecture, limiting their overlap. Researchers say both malware strains are likely to persist because patching vulnerable IoT devices is slow or sometimes impossible, and many vendors have not released security updates.

OpenAI reached a $500 billion valuation in a secondary share sale that authorized up to $10 billion in stock transactions, with current and former employees selling about $6.6 billion. Major investors included SoftBank, Thrive Capital, Dragoneer, MGX, and T. Rowe Price. The valuation rose from roughly $300 billion earlier in 2025, reflecting strong revenue and investor confidence. OpenAI generated $4.3 billion in first-half 2025 revenue, exceeding its full-year 2024 revenue by over 15%. The milestone strengthens OpenAI’s position amid intense AI competition but raises scrutiny over profitability, governance, regulation, market concentration, and whether growth can justify investor expectations.

The UCLA High Post Rub Offense combines inside and outside attacks through precise spacing, quick ball reversals, down screens, and high-post screens. It favors a flexible 1–4 alignment and can begin from either side. Typically, the point guard enters the ball to a wing, uses the high-post screen, and looks for a basket cut or post-up; if that fails, the wing reverses the ball to the high post.

Counters address specific defensive reads. Trailing defenders allow basket cuts, outside denial produces inside cuts, defenders going behind screens create open jump-shot opportunities, and show-and-recover defenses allow the screener to slip toward the basket. Switches can be answered with high-post rolls, corner isolation, or back screens for post isolation and lob opportunities.

Post players counter defensive positioning with a power layup, baby hook, face-up triple-threat move, or post lob. Ball reversal, corner feeds, point feeds, and post splits can create better passing angles, while pressure releases counter double-teams. Down screens include curls, fades, back cuts, rolls, slip screens, post isolation, wing isolation, and weakside post splits. Defensive overplays create automatic counters such as dribble clears, high-post feeds, lobs, weakside entries, back cuts, and screens.

Success depends on coordination, footwork, timing, communication, and understanding defensive reads. Practice should include breakdowns, combination drills, scrimmages, and individual skill development. Coaches should scout opponents, anticipate defensive adjustments, vary alignments and entries, and exploit weaker defenders.

The article says gold’s strong Friday rally was not matched by silver, mining stocks, or platinum, while the VanEck Junior Gold Miners ETF remained below its April closing high for a third session. It interprets this divergence as bearish and notes that gold remains below a rising resistance line. The USD Index returned to its July high and the neckline of an inverse head-and-shoulders pattern, which the author considers verified, with a possible rally to at least 101.3. Assuming the presidency under extraordinary circumstances, the speaker pledges to serve all Americans, notes that he neither campaigned nor subscribed to a partisan platform, and asks the public to confirm him through its prayers. He vows to consult Congress and the public on national priorities, stresses that the country must move forward together, and pledges an uninterrupted search for peace. He promises openness, candor, and honesty, affirms that the Constitution and rule of law remain intact, and calls for healing Watergate’s wounds through the golden rule, brotherly love, mercy, and faith in a higher Power. He asks Americans to pray for Richard Nixon and his family and reaffirms his commitment to uphold the Constitution, do what is right, and serve America to the best of his ability.

Andrew Lo concludes his course on capital budgeting by recommending net present value (NPV) as the primary decision rule: accept independent projects with positive NPV and, among mutually exclusive projects, choose the one with the highest NPV. For advanced applications, adjusted present value (APV) extends NPV by accounting for taxes, project interactions, strategic alternatives, and optionality. NPV calculations should use after-tax cash flows, evaluate project interactions separately, and use CAPM-adjusted discount rates that reflect the risk of each period.

The lecture reviews three alternatives to NPV. Payback period measures how long an investment takes to recover its initial cost. It is short-sighted because it ignores project scale, risks beyond nonpayment, and cash flows after payback; discounted payback corrects the units but still ignores later cash flows. Its practical appeal reflects career risk, liquidity needs, and uncertainty about distant cash flows, although these concerns are better addressed explicitly through discount rates, borrowing costs, and valuation methods.

The profitability index is gross present value divided by initial investment. Like NPV, it distinguishes positive- from negative-NPV projects, but it does not measure the dollars of value created. Consequently, it can lead to poor rankings when mutually exclusive projects differ in scale. IRR is the discount rate at which a project's NPV equals zero, analogous to a bond’s yield to maturity. It generally agrees with NPV when there is one initial outflow, subsequent cash flows are nonnegative, and projects are compared at the same opportunity cost of capital. However, unconventional cash flows can produce no real IRR or multiple IRRs, loans can create reversed rankings, and IRR ignores scale. IRR is nevertheless common in bonds and private equity, where standardized cash-flow structures and cultural practices support its use.

Scale is especially important in corporate capital budgeting because larger investments can reduce returns, so NPV’s dollar-based measure is preferable to rates of return. Economically, investment should continue until marginal benefit equals marginal cost, though doing this accurately requires advanced techniques. Practices surveyed at the time of the lecture showed payback used by more than 80% of large U.S. firms, IRR by 65%, and NPV gaining popularity; IRR remained more prevalent among multinational firms.

More realistic capital budgeting must also address competitive responses, multiperiod capital rationing, changing risks, and noisy data. Beyond financial measures, decisions involve political, social, cultural, and implementation considerations that must be integrated by managers.

The final section introduces efficient markets, which justify reliance on market prices, CAPM, and cost of capital under assumptions of rational behavior. Market efficiency implies no arbitrage, prices reflecting available information, and no added value from active management, although finance remains important as a language for business analysis. Lo plans to contrast this theory with behavioral and cognitive-neuroscience evidence in the next lecture. He illustrates the “wisdom of crowds” with the 1986 Challenger explosion: within minutes, Morton Thiokol’s stock fell much more than the other shuttle contractors’ stocks and was the only one significantly lower at the close, although the commission did not identify its faulty O-ring responsible for the disaster until six months later.

Remote Indian schools are important, but further work is needed on reservations, especially among young people. Education should teach Indians to earn a living, allow careers suited to individual aptitudes, and support tribal industries such as basketry, canoe building, smithing, and blanket making. Boys and girls should master colloquial English and be prepared to meet the conditions of their own communities. Government officials serving Indians should receive adequate pay, maintain exemplary conduct, and receive exemplary punishment for proven misconduct.

Scientific assistance has improved farming through plague control, new crops, low-rainfall wheat production, expanded rice cultivation, range regrassing, new forage crops, and profitable fruit exports. The Smithsonian’s plans should be supported to preserve records of vanishing peoples and endangered animals.

Washington should set high sanitation standards, prevent slums, and model charity, corrections, and labor regulation. Employer-liability and railroad safety measures are needed, along with legislation strengthening the 1893 railway safety law, which has prevented thousands of casualties.

The speaker says the team must recover from a loss, correct mistakes, and return to the details that produced a strong first-game win over Dallas. Dallas is described as a transitional, good rush team with large defensemen that is less effective when the puck is cycled deep in its zone. After dominant performances, the team often becomes less consistent with “dirty work,” including puck entry, cycling, finishing checks, winning board battles, and executing through the neutral zone, which can negate its speed and enable Dallas transitions. The speaker credits the team’s road success to relaxed play, attention to small details, and slowing games when needed. Despite having chances in the second game, the team did not perform as well as in the opener. The focus is on regaining consistency, puck depth, traffic navigation, and simple execution.

This study examined whether the maternal, infant, and child gut microbiomes are associated with neurodevelopment in the first three years of life. Using multi-omics data (16S rRNA metagenomic sequencing, untargeted metabolomics, and short-chain fatty acid measurements) from 116 mother-child pairs in the Vitamin D Antenatal Asthma Reduction Trial (VDAART), the authors tested how well gut microbial and metabolite profiles predicted neurodevelopment scored by the Ages and Stages Questionnaire, third edition (ASQ-Y1, ASQ-Y2, ASQ-Y3). Analyses used multinomial regression with reference frames and a null model to produce Q2 predictive-accuracy scores, with relevant clinical covariates included.

The maternal gut microbiome was the strongest predictor of first-year neurodevelopment (average Q2 ~0.21 at the class level), exceeding the infant microbiome at 3–6 months (~0.096) and the year-one child microbiome, which showed no predictive power for ASQ-Y1. Maternal and infant predictive power declined for year-two outcomes, and neither maternal nor child microbiomes predicted year-three outcomes. Maternal microbiota and metabolites were significantly associated with all five ASQ-Y1 domains.

Because Bray-Curtis dissimilarity between mothers and their children decreased with child age, the infant microbiome's relevance was not attributed to similarity with the maternal microbiome, suggesting distinct prenatal and postnatal roles. Some taxa shared between maternal and infant microbiomes (e.g., Fusobacteriia and Fusobacteriota) showed opposite associations with ASQ-Y1 domain scores.

Limitations include the small sample size, only one prenatal sampling time point, and the very low abundance of Fusobacteriia, warranting validation in larger populations.

A long chain email titled “cancer: don’t u dare delete” circulated among many recipients from August through November 2000, eventually forwarded by Jennifer Cutaia to Judy Hernandez, Crystal Reyna, and Etelvina Guerra. The chain contains mostly forwarding notices, recipient lists, requests to read and forward it, and signatures. A purported appeal from seven-year-old Amy Bruce says she has severe lung cancer from secondhand smoke and a brain tumor from repeated beatings, will die soon without help, and that her family cannot pay her medical bills. It asks recipients to forward the message, stating that the Make A Wish Foundation will donate seven cents for every name added.

Troll Cakes, a New York City bakery and detective agency, bakes chocolate chip brownie cakes featuring internet insults and can anonymously deliver them to trolls. Shipping costs $35, with address tracking adding $25, while a $30 option sends a chosen Trump tweet to the White House.

The goalie plays low, rebounds quickly, and handles the puck well, so the team plans to generate more traffic and shots. After missing a late bounce, the team emphasizes belief, confidence from prior series wins, and earning a win in the next game.

The goalie calls his late Stanley Cup final entry a learning experience. He and Jussi prepared; despite mistakenly holding the puck too long, he believes staying ready and making the right plays can help the team.

Observations of 14 of Centaurus A’s 16 dwarf satellite galaxies show that they orbit in a common plane, conflicting with the lambda cold dark matter model’s prediction of randomly oriented, roughly spherical distributions. This is the first such case beyond the Local Group and may reveal missing physics or flaws in existing simulations. However, some astrophysicists consider the alignment a statistical fluke or an effect of large-scale dark-matter filaments, and further observations are needed.

The passage describes offensive soccer corner-kick options for coaches to select according to players’ abilities. An effective corner kick includes a designed set play, a designated target area or receiver, and a proper service, while other players may create misdirection. Options include:

- **Far post:** A deep, lofted service aimed toward the best header, with inswing or outswing variants.
- **Near post:** A straight, accurate airborne ball exploited when the near-post defense is weak; the receiver may volley, head, glance, or redirect it.
- **Medium:** Corners aimed at the 6-, 12-, or 18-yard areas to challenge central defenders or the goalkeeper.
- **Top of the arc:** A brisk, accurate ground service into space often left weakly defended.
- **Short:** A close pass, particularly for young players, used to draw defenders away before a cross.
- **Skip header:** A flat service near the post that the receiver flicks toward the back post.
- **Direct score:** A rare, curling inswinger intended to enter the goal without a receiver.

Coaches should select kickers based on service needs and receivers based on aggression and heading ability, teach all roles progressively, and practice game-like situations, clearances, rebounds, deflections, and counterattacks. They should also account for wind, goalkeeper strength, timing, signals, offside, and the kicker’s restriction on retouching the ball. A floated corner may test a goalkeeper willing to come out and catch high balls, but can waste the restart if the goalkeeper reliably claims them.

Osteoarthritis involves cartilage degradation, low-grade inflammation, and diagnostic methods that do not yet include approved molecular biomarkers. Lubricin, a heavily O-glycosylated protein important for joint lubrication and cartilage integrity, may provide OA-related glycoform biomarkers. This study developed and validated a Fluorescent Immuno-Lectin Assay (FILA) using five lectins to measure Tn antigen, core-1, core-2, and sialylated glycoepitopes on lubricin. FILA showed acceptable recovery, dilution linearity, and intra- and inter-plate precision, and generally agreed with LC-SRM mass spectrometry.

In matched samples from 19 OA patients, lubricin glycoform levels were one to three orders of magnitude higher in synovial fluid than in plasma. Synovial-fluid lubricin was relatively enriched in truncated Tn antigen, whereas plasma lubricin had greater relative sialylation and core-1/core-2 structures, suggesting different glycosylation and possibly different tissue origins.

In a plasma cohort of 183 OA patients and 41 controls, most lectin-binding glycoforms did not differ significantly between groups. However, SNA-detected glycoforms were decreased in OA (p=0.0023), and the SNA-to-MGL ratio also differed (p=0.0178). Higher BMI correlated positively with MAA, SNA, and Gal-3 binding, while age correlated negatively with MAA and SNA and positively with MGL. The findings indicate that plasma lubricin glycosylation is influenced by OA, BMI, and age; SNA glycoforms alone would not be sufficient as an OA biomarker, and further investigation is required.

A longitudinal study conducted over two autumn/winter seasons enrolled 121 community-dwelling adults aged 60–86 from 61 households. Saliva was collected every two weeks and tested by qPCR for pneumococcus and other respiratory viruses. Among 1,088 tested samples, 4.8% were pneumococcal-positive, and 22.3% of individuals were colonized at least once. Both household members carried pneumococcus in 4.2% of season-one and 6.8% of season-two households, but sometimes at different times.

Carriage was more frequent among participants reporting contact with children. Samples from those with any child contact were positive 10.4% of the time, compared with 2.4% among those without such contact. Daily or every-few-days contact was associated with greater acquisition, while contact with children under 10 increased the acquisition hazard ratio to 3.0. Mean detectable colonization duration was 17.7 days.

Although some household pairs were simultaneously or sequentially positive, the study found no clear evidence of adult-to-adult transmission. Carriage was primarily associated with contact with preschool and young school-aged children, suggesting that adult vaccination may mainly directly protect exposed adults rather than reduce transmission between adults. Adult-to-child transmission was not evaluated. Several serotyping assays showed substantial nonspecificity, some serotypes could not be resolved, and the largely White, highly educated sample may not represent the broader community.

On June 10, 2015, Tesla Motors, Inc. and Tesla Motors Netherlands B.V. entered a senior secured asset-based revolving credit agreement with seven banks. The facility provides up to $500 million, with an option to add $250 million, plus a $100 million letter-of-credit subfacility and a $40 million swingline loan subfacility. Loans may fund working capital and general corporate purposes. The facility matures June 10, 2020, with no amounts outstanding at closing. Availability is based on a borrowing base covering inventory, receivables, and equipment, subject to reserves. Borrowings bear floating interest plus applicable margins, and an unused-commitment fee applies. The borrowers provided guarantees and security interests in specified assets. The agreement includes reporting and financial covenants, debt and dividend restrictions, a conditional fixed-charge coverage requirement, and customary default provisions permitting lenders to demand repayment and foreclose on collateral.

Michael Barnard argues that hurricanes, wildfires, migration, and future climate impacts will increase acceptance of human-caused global warming and shift voters from Republicans toward Democrats. He says population shifts may make formerly safe Republican seats competitive, while gerrymandering and the electoral college cannot offset the trend. He predicts Republicans will eventually be voted out unless they change.

Europe plans to launch Sentinel-3B on Wednesday to monitor pollution and human damage to oceans. The seventh Copernicus satellite since April 2014, it will orbit opposite Sentinel-3A and provide data within three hours, continuously tracking sea level, surface temperature, pollution, sea ice, coastal vegetation, river and lake heights, and wildfires. The EU-ESA Copernicus programme offers free environmental data, maps disaster-stricken areas, and monitors the atmosphere, forests, land and water pollution. Britain’s post-Brexit participation remains uncertain, though it seeks to remain in ESA.

Workers began removing Gainesville’s “Old Joe” Confederate statue Monday and returning it to the United Daughters of the Confederacy, which erected it in 1904. In Tampa, red paint and derogatory graffiti were found at a Confederate memorial and later cleaned. Officials were also discussing relocating another Tampa monument amid broader debates over Confederate memorials.
