The Triangle & Two “Double Stack” offense aligns two posts in the mid-post with shooters behind them to limit outstanding shooters’ touches and create open baseline shots. Options include popping out for a jump shot, curling late, fading to the corner, backcutting, feeding the screener against a switch, crossing under the basket, faking crosses, and using single or double screens. The formation can also flow into base or side screens. Success requires coordination, defensive recognition, communication, timing, experience, and structured drills and scrimmages. Teams should scout opponents when possible, anticipate defensive reads, monitor adjustments, vary alignments and entries, and attack weaker defenders. In the corresponding defense, three players cover a triangle zone while two “chasers” focus on aggressive pass denial.

The passage describes the SEV-ES Guest-Hypervisor Communication Block (GHCB) protocol and related SEV-SNP mechanisms. An SEV-ES guest handles non-automatic exit (NAE) events by catching a #VC exception, disabling interrupts and preemption, establishing the GHCB’s guest physical address in MSR 0xc001_0130, clearing prior invocation data, populating the required GHCB fields and VALID_BITMAP, and invoking VMGEXIT. The hypervisor translates the GHCB address, processes the request according to SW_EXITCODE, returns required state in the GHCB, and resumes the guest after the VMGEXIT instruction. Hypervisor errors are reported through SW_EXITINFO1 and SW_EXITINFO2, with a nonzero SW_EXITINFO1[31:0] indicating an error.

Guests identify SEV-ES support and determine the encryption-bit position through CPUID, including intercepted CPUID exchanges handled through #VC. Guests must avoid unintended encrypted-memory accesses before entering long mode or 32-bit PAE because the hypervisor could not communicate through an encrypted GHCB.

The protocol defines guest and hypervisor handling for NAE events including IOIO protection, MSR protection, hypercalls, MMIO accesses, page-state changes, SNP guest requests and extended guest requests, AP creation, #HV doorbell management, IPI delivery, timers, APIC ID discovery, VMPL changes, SEV-TIO requests, Secure AVIC backing pages, termination requests, and unsupported events. IOIO and MMIO handling may use the GHCB reserved shared buffer for decrypted data, with multiple VMGEXIT calls permitted to transfer data. Page-state requests support private/shared transitions and SNP PSMASH/UNSMASH hints; progress is recorded in shared memory so requests can be resumed.

SNP guest requests require separate shared request and response pages and use the SNP_GUEST_REQUEST firmware API. The hypervisor returns the firmware result in SW_EXITINFO2, while rate limiting is recommended to prevent firmware denial of service. Extended requests can return certificates identified by GUIDs and accompanied by an attestation report. SEV-TIO requests similarly use shared data pages to return measurements, certificates, and a TDISP attestation report.

SEV-SNP launch includes providing a secrets page and CPUID page. Firmware can communicate these pages to the OS through the EFI SEV-SNP Confidential Computing Blob configuration table. The secrets page’s guest-reserved area stores per-VMPL guest message sequence numbers and may communicate the AP jump table address. SNP AP Creation allows a guest to create, update, or remove a vCPU’s VMSA and supports vCPU hotplug.

SMP booting under SEV-ES and SEV-SNP requires special handling because measured register state cannot be modified after launch. Initial AP resets use predetermined values, while subsequent parking uses AP Reset Hold requests. UEFI can transfer AP reset-vector information to the OS through a 4 KiB, page-aligned, encrypted AP jump table. Under Restricted Injection, SNP AP Creation is required because AP Reset Hold and conventional INIT-SIPI behavior are unavailable.

For NMI handling, the hypervisor must not intercept IRET but must intercept #DB, allowing the guest to issue an “NMI Complete” message when another NMI can safely be injected. Hardware debug-register virtualization is supported when indicated by SEV_FEATURES; otherwise, the hypervisor intercepts DR7 accesses and the guest caches and returns the value through the #VC handler. SMM and nested virtualization are unsupported.

The Restricted Injection #HV doorbell mechanism uses a shared, host-owned page containing a PendingEvent field and a NoEoiRequired flag. The host emulates APIC interrupt presentation, acknowledgment, in-service, and EOI semantics through this page. Guests atomically exchange pending-event data, validate observed interrupt vectors, and follow a defined HLT convention so pending maskable and non-maskable events are not missed.

The AEGEAN study randomized 1,162 subjects initiating apixaban for atrial fibrillation to Primary SOC (583) or an Additional Educational Program (579); 1,160 received study drug, and all were included in the Part 1 primary efficacy set. The evaluable set included 1,098 subjects, 1,054 completed Week 24, and 108 (9.3%) discontinued by or at Week 24. In Part 2, 524 subjects were randomized to Secondary SOC (263) or Continued Additional Education (261); 1,003 completed Week 48, and 50 (4.5%) discontinued after Week 24.

Baseline characteristics were comparable between groups. The median age was 74 years, 59.9% were male, mean BMI was 28.7 kg/m², and mean MMSE was 28.3. Common cardiovascular risk factors included hypertension, diabetes, coronary or peripheral vascular disease, prior stroke or TIA, and heart failure. Drug exposure, interruption, dosing, and compliance were similar across groups, with mean compliance above 95% through Week 24 and above 94% at Week 48.

Mean adherence at Week 24 was 91.64% with Primary SOC and 91.88% with Additional Education, with no significant difference; adherence was also comparable at Weeks 4 and 12. At Week 48, adherence remained comparable among Primary SOC, Secondary SOC, and Continued Additional Education groups. Persistence was similar at Week 24 (91.7% versus 91.3%) and Week 48 (85.2%, 87.8%, and 86.1%). The proportion fully adherent over time was 28.1% versus 26.5% at Week 24 and approximately 15% across all groups at Week 48, without significant group differences. Adherence declined significantly in later versus earlier periods in both initial groups. At Week 24, Primary SOC non-adherence was associated with alcohol consumption, technical occupations, permanent atrial fibrillation, and lower MMSE; no variables significantly predicted non-adherence in the Additional Education group.

Safety outcomes were similar between groups. Before Week 24, adverse events occurred in 51.2% and 52.0%, bleeding in 6.5% and 9.0%, and major bleeding in 0.7% and 1.1% of Primary SOC and Additional Education subjects, respectively. After Week 24, adverse events occurred in 33.8%, 40.8%, and 38.6% across the three groups, with bleeding in 4.1%, 4.0%, and 3.2%. There were 24 deaths, no pregnancies, and no clinically concerning hepatic or renal laboratory signal. Overall, adherence and persistence were high and sustained, and the proactive educational program provided no additional benefit.

A phase 2 trial found that adding abatacept to standard graft-versus-host disease (GvHD) prophylaxis nearly eliminated severe acute GvHD in 43 pediatric and adult patients receiving mismatched unrelated-donor stem cell transplants. At 100 days, grade III-IV GvHD occurred in 3% of abatacept recipients, compared with 32% receiving a calcineurin inhibitor plus methotrexate and 22% receiving those drugs plus anti-thymocyte globulin. Abatacept recipients also had better one-year overall survival (85% versus 57% and 68%) and disease-free survival (79% versus 50% and 63%), with reduced transplant-related mortality, intact immune reconstitution, no major uncontrolled infections, and no increased relapse. The study also included a randomized, double-blind cohort of 140 patients receiving human leukocyte antigen-matched unrelated-donor transplants; results were expected within six months of enrollment closing in November 2017.
Stoke City face relegation-threatened Hull City Saturday, aiming to end a five-game winless streak. Defender Geoff Cameron says Stoke must win.

Amazon.com, Inc. filed an unaudited Form 10-Q for the quarter ended September 30, 2015. Q3 net sales were $25.358 billion, up 23% from $20.579 billion a year earlier, comprising $18.463 billion of product sales and $6.895 billion of service sales. Operating income was $406 million versus a $544 million loss, and net income was $79 million versus a $437 million loss. Diluted EPS was $0.17, compared with a loss of $0.95. For the first nine months, net sales rose 19% to $71.259 billion, operating income was $1.124 billion, net income was $114 million, and diluted EPS was $0.24.

Q3 segment results were: North America sales of $15.006 billion and operating income of $528 million; International sales of $8.267 billion and an operating loss of $56 million; and AWS sales of $2.085 billion and operating income of $521 million. Nine-month operating results were $1.747 billion for North America, a $151 million loss for International, and $1.177 billion for AWS. AWS sales increased 78% in Q3 and 70% for the nine months. The company attributed sales growth primarily to higher unit sales, marketplace activity, increased inventory availability, product selection, price reductions and greater AWS usage.

Q3 operating cash flow was $2.610 billion, and nine-month operating cash flow was $3.108 billion. Investing activities used $1.377 billion in Q3 and $4.600 billion over nine months, primarily reflecting capital expenditures and marketable securities activity. Financing activities used $730 million in Q3 and $2.073 billion over nine months, principally for lease and debt repayments. Trailing-twelve-month free cash flow increased to $5.4 billion from $1.1 billion. At September 30, the company held $10.709 billion of cash and cash equivalents, $3.719 billion of marketable securities, total assets of $56.230 billion and stockholders’ equity of $12.430 billion. Total debt had a face value of $9.451 billion, including $1.117 billion due within one year; $750 million of notes matured November 27, 2015. The company also had an unused $2.0 billion revolving credit facility.

During the first nine months, Amazon acquired companies for $393 million, primarily for technology and know-how. On October 19, it acquired Elemental Technologies for approximately $296 million. Total contractual commitments were $33.871 billion, while purchase obligations and open purchase orders totaled $7.8 billion.

The filing disclosed copyright-tariff and patent litigation, several matters on appeal, and $895 million of tax contingencies. The IRS was seeking approximately $1.5 billion of additional federal tax related to 2005 and 2006 transfer pricing, which Amazon was contesting in U.S. Tax Court, while Amazon was also contesting a French assessment of €196 million. Critical accounting estimates involved inventory valuation, goodwill, stock-based compensation and income taxes; no goodwill impairment was identified. Cash, cash equivalents and marketable securities were measured at fair value, with no Level 3 assets reported.

The president addressed the Syrian civil war, noting that it had killed more than 100,000 people and displaced millions. He said the Assad regime was responsible for the August 21 chemical attack that killed over 1,000 people, including hundreds of children, and argued that failing to respond could encourage wider use of chemical weapons, threaten U.S. security, and embolden other dictators.

He proposed a targeted military strike—not ground troops, regime change, or an open-ended campaign—to deter future chemical attacks and degrade Assad’s capabilities. He rejected concerns that the strike would trigger escalation, noting Israel’s ability to defend itself and Assad’s limited ability to threaten the U.S. military.

The president also pursued a diplomatic alternative after Russia indicated willingness to join efforts to secure Syria’s chemical weapons and Assad’s regime admitted possessing them and pledged to join the Chemical Weapons Convention. He asked Congress to postpone authorizing force while diplomacy continued, sending Secretary of State John Kerry to meet his Russian counterpart and seeking a UN Security Council resolution with France, the United Kingdom, Russia, and China. He ordered the military to remain prepared to respond if diplomacy failed.

President Donald Trump addressed senior U.S. military leaders at the White House, praising Pete Hegseth and Gen. Dan “Raising” Caine, thanking them for their service, and emphasizing unity within the armed forces. He criticized the previous administration’s military, immigration, and foreign-policy records.

Trump described the renaming of the Department of Defense as the Department of War as a restoration of the military’s identity and purpose, while arguing that strength would deter enemies and help prevent wars. He also defended the renaming of the Gulf of Mexico to the Gulf of America, noting that the change faced resistance and was upheld in court after a legal challenge by the Associated Press.

He claimed his administration had settled seven conflicts in roughly nine months, including disputes involving India and Pakistan, Azerbaijan and Armenia, and Rwanda and the Congo. He proposed a “Board of Peace” to oversee Gaza after announcing a peace plan, while acknowledging that implementation would require difficult negotiations, including with Hamas. He said the unresolved war between Russia and Ukraine remained his most difficult effort and required bringing President Vladimir Putin and President Volodymyr Zelensky together through demonstrated strength.

The speech emphasized rebuilding and expanding U.S. military capabilities. Trump committed to spending more than $1 trillion on the military in 2026, adding at least 19 Navy ships, modernizing nuclear deterrence, developing the F-47 sixth-generation fighter, constructing the Golden Dome missile-defense system, ordering additional B-2 bombers, and considering new battleships. He claimed the U.S. submarine fleet was undetectable and decades ahead of rivals and said nuclear weapons should never need to be used.

Trump also cited improved recruiting and retention, saying several services had met or exceeded their goals early, the Space Force had exceeded its annual target, and the Marine Corps was on track to meet retention goals unusually early. He announced a 3.8% pay raise for service members and linked stronger recruiting to merit-based personnel policies and increased opportunities for qualified applicants.

Domestic security was another major theme. Trump praised National Guard operations in Washington, D.C., discussed possible military support for cities including Chicago and Portland, and signed an order creating a quick-reaction force for civil disturbances. He described border enforcement as a top priority, claimed unauthorized entries had fallen to zero, and said the administration was targeting gangs, drug trafficking, and cartel activity. He said some cartels had been designated as terrorist organizations and reported destroying four boats carrying substantial quantities of narcotics.

On alliances and arms sales, Trump said NATO members had committed to spending 5% of GDP on defense, enabling more American weapons purchases and reducing the need for U.S. funding to Ukraine. He also announced planned reforms to accelerate military acquisitions and foreign sales, directing defense manufacturers to increase production of aircraft, ammunition, and other equipment.

Trump closed by praising the armed forces’ equipment, leadership, recruiting, and warrior culture. He described military power as the foundation of national security, said the United States should fight as little as necessary while being prepared to fight and win, and thanked the assembled leaders and service members before blessing the military and the United States.

On New Year’s Eve, Melissa was watching television in her east-side Milwaukee home when she heard a loud crash and found her front door kicked or punched in. The alarm scared the suspected intruders away, police received similar calls that night on her street, and the damaged door required boarding. Melissa believes they may have been injured and plans improved home security.

Biogen fell after its CFO left for Alexion; H&R Block beat expectations. Banks declined as bond yields fell. GameStop, Synchronoss and Anadarko fell on weak retail sales, revenue errors and lower oil prices; Brookdale rose amid sale talks.

Childs Farm Baby Moisturiser, priced at £3.99 and sold at shops including Boots and Asda, has drawn online praise from users who claim it relieved or cleared eczema and psoriasis. Laura Gray said her psoriasis disappeared after 24 hours, while Paige Sweeney reported that the cream improved her daughter Evie-Rae’s eczema within days despite previous treatments failing. Joanne said one-year-old Kelisha’s severe eczema cleared after four weeks of regular use. Paige’s before-and-after post was shared more than 40,000 times. Company dermatologist Dr Jennifer Crawley said regular use of a gentle moisturiser can soothe, hydrate and help painful, cracked skin heal.

This study compared the race-adjusted 2009 CKD-EPI creatinine GFR equation with the race-free 2021 equation using linked Truveta electronic health records from more than 8 million adults with repeated serum creatinine tests. Among 1,239,185 patients classified with CKD stages 3a–5 by either equation, the 2021 equation identified CKD earlier for 24% of Black patients versus 0.7% of non-Black patients. It also produced substantial staging differences, particularly among Black patients: nearly 50% of those classified as stage 3a in 2021 did not meet CKD criteria in 2009, 50% of those classified as stage 3b in 2021 were classified as stage 3a in 2009, and about 40% of stage 4 classifications were discordant. By comparison, 99% of non-Black patients classified as stage 4 in 2021 remained stage 4 in 2009. Multivariable analysis found that Black patients had substantially greater odds of increased CKD staging under the 2021 equation. Included social determinants of health were not significantly associated with staging increases. Limitations included incomplete capture of care outside participating health systems and potential inaccuracies in the unvalidated Elixhauser comorbidity index. Overall, the findings indicate that removing race from GFR estimation changes CKD detection and staging, particularly for Black patients, and support further evaluation of its clinical effects.

Apple Inc. filed a Form 8-K on April 28, 2021, reporting its financial results for the second fiscal quarter ended March 27, 2021. The related press release was included as Exhibit 99.1; the information was not deemed filed under Section 18 of the Exchange Act or incorporated by reference except by specific reference. The report was signed by Senior Vice President and Chief Financial Officer Luca Maestri.

The speaker says the team is down to its potential final game of the year and must focus on its next opportunity, noting it has repeatedly bounced back during the year. He doubts home-ice advantage will matter much and says the players know what must be done. He describes the situation as emotionally and mentally draining, with frustration, penalties, and tense bench behavior contributing. After a long flight, the team plans rest, food, and a morning skate. He says the growing hostility between the teams is normal in a long series and creates strong competition.

Legal experts criticised the Communications (Retention of Data) Bill 2017 for omitting two key Murray Report recommendations: High Court authorisation and restrictions on accessing journalists’ source data, and oversight by an independent, resourced monitoring body. The bill would replace the 2011 Act and require district court judges to authorise requests for communication data. Experts also criticised retrospective reviews as insufficient, while noting that the bill expands prior judicial authorisation and calls for more robust reviews to protect privacy rights.
Oral GLP-1 trials showed weight loss in people with obesity.

St. Louis patient Deanna Conley, 77, suffered chronic back pain after nearly 40 years of imaging and five spinal fusion surgeries. Washington University Pain Management Center doctor Michael Bottros recommended a spinal cord stimulator, which uses electrode impulses to block pain signals. After a one-week trial showed improvement, Conley received a permanent implant. She later walked into the clinic without her walker or wheelchair, regained daily activities, and called the result a miracle. The implant requires 15–20 minutes of charging and a wireless controller for adjustments. Bottros described the procedure as relatively low risk and reported remarkable results among nearly all 40–50 patients treated in the past year.

Nineteen-year-old Rory McKelvie was found dead in his sleep at his home in Biggar, Lanarkshire; his death is not being treated as suspicious. He had publicly described receiving little support for his mental health and said his doctor told him to return only when he reached a “breaking point.” He also revealed that someone stopped him from committing suicide in November before urging others to seek help from friends and family. His mother shared the news, his girlfriend Caitlin Brigham paid tribute, and NHS Lanarkshire was contacted for comment.

President Donald Trump faced widespread criticism after defending his writing and capitalization in a tweet containing misspellings, including “poured” instead of “pored” and “bestselling” as one word. Tony Schwartz, ghostwriter of The Art of the Deal, responded that Trump could not read well, much less write, and had contributed little to the book. J.K. Rowling also mocked the tweet. Separately, Trump was criticized for denying Annapolis’s request to lower flags after a deadly newsroom shooting, despite ordering flag lowerings after other mass shootings; he later declared that flags should be lowered.

Clinton County ranked among Site Selection magazine’s “Top 100 Micropolitans,” tying for 64th, after four projects submitted by the Clinton County Port Authority were vetted by JobsOhio and the publication. The submissions represent $70 million in potential investment, 150 jobs to be created, and 400 retained. One project is the Bright Farms facility under construction on Davids Drive. Ohio led the 2017 ranking with 16 Top 100 micropolitans. Micropolitan areas have urban populations of 10,000 to 49,999.

News reports dated Nov. 30, 2001 described Enron Corp. as nearing bankruptcy after Dynegy abandoned a $9 billion takeover and Enron’s credit rating fell to junk status. Enron was widely expected to seek Chapter 11 protection, with more than $15 billion in debt and less than $2 billion in cash. Federal prosecutors in Texas and New York sought to monitor the SEC’s investigation into Enron’s accounting practices as a possible precursor to a criminal inquiry. SEC Chairman Harvey Pitt promised a swift investigation into possible wrongdoing and whether accounting principles were properly applied.

Bloomberg reported that an Enron-affiliated partnership, Joint Energy Development Investments Limited Partnership, invested $50 million in Costilla Energy Inc., which later went bankrupt. Enron wrote off the loss. Legal and accounting experts said the investment was a related-party transaction that should have been disclosed in SEC filings, though Enron said it had included the loss in other results. Enron used more than 30 partnerships to hedge risks and move assets and liabilities off its books; partnership losses contributed to its downfall after the company reported inflating profits by $586 million over five years. Enron reduced shareholders’ equity by $1.2 billion in the third quarter and was responsible for $3.9 billion in partnership debts.

Enron’s European withdrawal disrupted power trading and raised questions about contracts, liquidity and job losses. Enron had employed 6,800 people in Europe and previously held about one-fifth of Europe’s $100 billion annual electricity-trading market. Nord Pool cleared all outstanding Enron trades without losses, while the U.K. Power Exchange, Amsterdam Power Exchange and European Energy Exchange variously suspended or excluded Enron, citing concerns including its inability to post required margins. Power prices in the U.K., Scandinavia and Germany fluctuated sharply as traders unwound positions. Most European utilities reported exposure below $50 million, although banks and insurers also faced losses and credit concerns. Rival traders were positioned to gain customers, while possible buyers examined Enron’s metals business, generation assets and water utility.

Enron’s European trading operation entered administration after Houston cut off funding. The Teesside power station, Enron Direct retail business and other operations with their own revenue remained outside administration. Enron said the 1,875-megawatt Teesside station was operating normally, and Innogy expressed interest in buying Enron’s share of the station and Enron Direct if the price was right. Other potential buyers were identified for Enron assets, including Wessex Water, whose sale to Royal Bank of Scotland and others was being considered.

Dynegy said it planned to take over Enron’s 16,500-mile Northern Natural Gas pipeline on Dec. 12. Under the abandoned merger agreement, Dynegy had acquired $1.5 billion of preferred stock and an option to purchase the pipeline’s common equity for about $23 million. Dynegy said Northern Natural Gas could not take actions such as seek bankruptcy-court protection without its consent as preferred shareholder. Enron could seek to dispute the transaction and had 180 days to repurchase the pipeline for $1.5 billion plus interest. Fitch kept Dynegy on negative rating watch, citing likely litigation over the pipeline option and the aborted merger.

Enron’s overseas operations also remained unsettled. Assets, investments and operations outside the United States generated about 25 percent of revenue. The status of Enron’s controlling stake in Brazil’s Elektro was uncertain; lenders to the $2.9 billion Dabhol Power venture in India threatened to seize the plant over unpaid bills and contract terms; and the European administrator was close to selling Enron’s metals-trading unit.

Market and operational disruptions continued. Enron failed to deliver natural gas to German utilities, while its U.K. balancing panel discussed the company’s market obligations. Enron traders made no new deals but worked to honor existing commitments, with many employees expecting control to pass to a bankruptcy court and creditors. Enron’s Japanese unit planned to decide by year-end whether to continue power projects in Rokkasho, Ube, Matsuyama and Omuta. U.S. Senate and House energy committees planned hearings or investigations concerning Enron and market oversight.

Analysts estimated Enron could cause more than $2 billion in losses for bond and property-casualty insurers and another $1 billion for life insurers. John Hancock’s reported Enron debt exposure was $320 million, followed by Principal Financial at $172 million, Lincoln National at $95 million and MetLife at $62.6 million. MBIA and Ambac said they had no direct exposure, though Ambac had indirect exposure to bonds issued by an Enron-owned Oregon utility.

Enron’s derivatives portfolio was expected to test bankruptcy-law safe harbors. Reports described thousands of counterparties, about $62 billion in assets and roughly $20 billion in derivative contracts owed by Enron as of December 2000. Counterparties sought to unwind and net their trades, but uncertainty over collateral and Enron’s asset values could leave many unsecured creditors with little recovery. Despite the turmoil, major stock indexes were slightly higher, and a Dow Jones column argued that investors were not panicking and that the broader market damage appeared contained, while acknowledging potential losses to shareholders, creditors, banks and derivative counterparties.

Arsene Wenger hopes to field Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang, Henrikh Mkhitaryan, Mesut Ozil and Alexandre Lacazette while improving Arsenal’s defensive record. The £56 million signing Aubameyang joined Arsenal alongside Mkhitaryan and Lacazette, while Ozil accepted a three-year, £350,000-a-week contract. Wenger said retaining Ozil was cheaper than finding a replacement but insisted Arsenal must not live on credit. He declined to guarantee Lacazette a place, with the forward doubtful against Everton because of illness.

Edmonton police charged 62-year-old blogger Barry Kent Winters on June 1 with wilfully promoting hatred against an identifiable group under the Criminal Code—a provision police said they had never previously used and that had generated only three charges in Alberta over six years. The charge followed complaints and a 13-month investigation into his blogs, which contained racist, homophobic, transphobic and other derogatory language, attacked numerous groups and public figures, fantasized about violent deaths, threatened to publish nude images of assault victim Rehteah Parsons and accused her father of molesting her. The blogs had thousands of readers, and Winters was required to remove them as a condition of pre-trial release.

The article raises concerns that prosecuting offensive speech could erode free-speech rights, increase Winters’s notoriety and provide a platform for others, while also arguing that his blogs encouraged hatred and violence and that some criminal sanctions are reasonable, provided the threshold for prosecution is high.

The $7 billion Strategic National Stockpile is a government repository of medicines and emergency supplies managed by the CDC and stored in at least six secret warehouses nationwide. It contains antibiotics, vaccines, antitoxins and nearly 2,000 separately maintained caches of nerve-agent antidotes. The stockpile can rapidly deploy “12-hour push packages” containing antibiotics, syringes and oxygen tubing. Created in 1999 for terrorist attacks, its mission has expanded to natural disasters and infectious disease outbreaks; it deployed supplies after Hurricanes Harvey and Maria, during the swine flu pandemic, and for severe botulism cases.

Under a Trump administration plan, oversight of the $575 million program will shift in October from the CDC to the Assistant Secretary for Preparedness and Response within HHS. ASPR would select and purchase stockpile products, while the CDC has handled replenishment and maintenance. Supporters say the change will streamline decisions and improve coordination. Critics, including bipartisan lawmakers and public health officials, worry it could disrupt state and local distribution relationships, politicize purchasing decisions, favor costly specialized drugs over broadly useful medicines and weaken the CDC’s scientific expertise. Congress gave the program a slight budget increase but urged HHS to maintain a strong CDC role. ASPR chief Robert Kadlec says the reorganization is intended to create efficiencies and improve the stockpile’s visibility and funding, while CDC director Greg Burel says emergency response procedures will not change.

The Missouri Court of Appeals held that sovereign immunity was waived as to the Larisons’ claim that a water district employee negligently created a dangerous condition involving their water meter lid. Although there was no direct evidence explaining how the lid became displaced, the operator’s routine and the circumstances surrounding the accident supported competing inferences of negligent replacement or later tampering. Whether his testimony was credible was a jury question, so summary judgment on the operator-negligence claim was reversed.

The court affirmed summary judgment on the Larisons’ claim that the Water District knew or should have known of the dangerous condition. The only evidence concerned the theoretical possibility that a push mower could dislodge a meter lid, but there was no evidence that Mrs. Larison’s mower rolled over the lid before she stepped backward onto it and fell into the open meter well. The asserted causal connection was therefore speculative.

The court also affirmed summary judgment on the Larisons’ alternative res ipsa loquitur claim. The meter lid was not under the Water District’s exclusive control because it was located in the Larisons’ unfenced yard, accessible to outside interference, and the District inspected it only monthly. Accordingly, the elements required for res ipsa loquitur were not established.

The study assessed whether COVID-19 vaccination was associated with hearing loss, tinnitus, or vertigo using Victoria’s SAEFVIC spontaneous reporting system and a self-controlled case series analysis of more than 4.9 million general-practice presentations from Victoria and New South Wales between January 2021 and March 2023. The vaccination risk window was days 1–42.

Among adults aged 18–64, 678 audiovestibular events were reported after adenovirus vector or mRNA vaccines. SAEFVIC reporting rates were higher for adenovirus vector vaccines than mRNA vaccines (rate ratio 1.94), including for vertigo and tinnitus. Adenovirus vector reporting rates were also higher after dose 1 than dose 2, while overall mRNA rates did not differ by dose.

In the general-practice analysis, relative incidence of audiovestibular conditions increased within 42 days of both vaccine types. Vertigo presentations increased after mRNA vaccination (relative incidence 1.40) but not after adenovirus vector vaccination, while tinnitus presentations increased after both mRNA (1.53) and adenovirus vector vaccines (2.25). No increased relative incidence of hearing loss was identified after either vaccine type.

Spontaneous reports were more frequent among females, but the general-practice analysis found no meaningful sex difference. The authors noted that prior COVID-19 infection was a potential confounder, spontaneous reports were susceptible to reporting bias, and incomplete capture of vaccinations given outside participating practices could have underestimated risk. They concluded that the findings indicate increased vertigo presentations after mRNA vaccination and increased tinnitus presentations after both vaccine types, but no increase in hearing loss, while causality could not be established.

MIT OCW Lecture 8.701 explains how spontaneous symmetry breaking generates gauge-boson masses. A massive spin-1 gauge field would ordinarily violate local gauge invariance, but coupling it to a complex scalar field whose potential has a negative mass-squared term produces a nonzero vacuum expectation value and breaks the symmetry. In a simplified U(1) toy model, this generates a gauge-field mass term, while the massless Goldstone boson is absorbed into the gauge boson’s longitudinal polarization, leaving a physical massive scalar.

The lecture then generalizes the mechanism to the Standard Model’s SU(2) × U(1) symmetry using a complex SU(2) doublet. Its vacuum expectation value generates masses for the W and Z bosons, while the photon remains massless. The three associated Goldstone bosons are absorbed into the W and Z bosons, and a physical Higgs scalar remains. The mechanism was proposed in the 1960s, while the Higgs boson was discovered by the LHC experiment in 2012.

DAVV BCom (Hons) third-semester students were mistakenly given Corporate Accounts papers instead of Corporate Law papers, delaying the exam by about 30 minutes. The university replaced the bundles and denied a leak, though the earlier paper was allegedly served a week before its scheduled exam, and said it could change the paper set if needed. DAVV also rejected colleges’ demand to shift BCom (Hons) back to the semester system, noting no DHE instruction to do so.

Gold steadied below $1,250 an ounce after its biggest weekly drop in more than six months, as markets awaited an expected Federal Reserve rate hike and closely watched policy signals. Spot gold was $1,247.48, down 2.5% last week. Hedge funds and money managers sharply reduced net long COMEX gold and silver positions; silver’s net long position fell by a record 34,915 contracts. Silver was $15.77, platinum $886.40, and palladium $1,004.10. World stocks rose, equity volatility neared a record low, and bitcoin futures exceeded $18,000.

China’s uneven basic education and the “siphon” effect, in which students and teachers move from disadvantaged areas to schools with superior resources, have encouraged the formation of education groups linking prestigious “core schools” with ordinary branch schools. Core schools provide administrators, anchor teachers, guidance, training, curriculum collaboration, and teacher exchanges to improve member schools and expand access to quality education.

Education groups share high-quality resources, management skills, instructional research, and curriculum development, helping reduce gaps between schools and balance regional education quality. They also strengthen teachers’ professional competence, identity, and collaboration; a study of 175 teachers in Shanghai found that more than 90% believed their teaching and research abilities had improved. Group programs broaden students’ access to courses, learning modes, extracurricular activities, and higher-order thinking while fostering a shared educational culture. In Hangzhou’s Xiacheng District, groups made prestigious education accessible to 90% of students and reduced the gap between demand and supply.

Challenges include mechanically imposing core-school culture on branch schools, erasing their distinctive identities and homogenizing the group. Core-school teaching approaches may also fail when transferred without considering differences in teacher ability, student competence, and local needs. Management problems include dispersed resources, substantial demands on core schools, and government assessments based primarily on core-school performance.

Recommended reforms include establishing equal, democratic relationships and a standing committee of member-school leaders; strengthening teacher rotations, training, incentives, teamwork, and online resource sharing; and securing greater government funding, policy support, and recognition for educators serving disadvantaged schools. Education groups offer deeper cooperation than earlier school partnerships, but their continued success requires preserving individual schools’ characteristics and sustaining institutional commitment.

Statewide fire departments hold October Fire Prevention Month sessions, themed “Every Second Counts—Know Two Ways Out.” Officials urge families to maintain multiple exits and usable windows, stay outside during alarms, and rehearse home fire drills.

The passage presents excerpts from the SEV-ES Guest-Hypervisor Communication Block specification covering GHCB negotiation, VMGEXIT handling, and related guest–hypervisor interfaces.

**GHCB negotiation.** The guest ultimately provides the GPA of the GHCB page via the GHCB MSR, which the hypervisor obtains by reading VMCB offset 0x00a0; initially the hypervisor can set the GHCB MSR to allow negotiation. Two examples are given. For an SEV-ES guest, the hypervisor sets VMCB offset 0x00a0 before the first vCPU launch, using GHCBInfo value 0x001; the guest, after a #VC exception from intercepted CPUID, reads MSR 0xc001_0130, extracts the maximum and minimum GHCB protocol versions from GHCBData[63:48] and [47:32], and the encryption bit number from GHCBData[31:24], then continues initialization (establishing 64-bit long mode, configuring page tables with the encryption bit, allocating and marking the GHCB page shared by writing its GPA to MSR 0xc001_0130 with GHCBInfo == 0x000). The SEV-SNP variant follows the same pattern, except the guest verifies CPUID leaf 0x80000000/0x8000001f, reads the non-interceptable SEV Status MSR 0xc001_0131 to confirm it is an SEV-SNP guest, extracts the encryption bit from EBX[5:0], and may use the MSR protocol for SEV Information and Register GHCB GPA requests. The document notes the hypervisor may supply the encryption bit position, but the guest should use the CPUID page value, which the SEV firmware has validated.

**GHCB/VMGEXIT example.** For a version 1 protocol, the guest #VC handler disables preemption and interrupts, ensures the GHCB physical address is in MSR 0xc001_0130, clears prior GHCB field data, and sets required GHCB fields. The hypervisor resumes with VMEXIT_VMGEXIT, reads VMCB offset 0x00a0 for the guest physical address, translates it to a hypervisor virtual address, handles the exit based on GHCB SW_EXITCODE, updates the save state area, and resumes the guest; it may instead recreate the GHCB versioning value or a CPUID response, or terminate the guest if the VMGEXIT cannot be processed.

**Secrets page and EFI protocol.** The hypervisor should supply an SEV-SNP guest with a secrets page, whose 96-byte area from offset 0x00a0 to 0x00ff is reserved for the guest and defined in Table 4 (per-VMPL current guest request message sequence numbers, AP jump table physical address, and a guest usage area). Because a version 2.00 API change widened the guest request message sequence number to 64 bits, 18 of the 40 reserved bytes hold the upper 32 bits plus a 16-bit version number. Firmware can pass the secrets page and CPUID page to the OS via the EFI SEV-SNP Confidential Computing Blob configuration table (GUID 0x067b1f5f-0xcf26-0x44c5-0x8554-0x93d7-0x7791-0x2d42).

**NAE events.** NAE events are all exit events that are not AE events; the hardware always throws #VC for them when an SEV-ES guest is running, with the #VC error code equal to the VMEXIT code. The guest inspects the error code, copies the needed register state to the GHCB, invokes VMGEXIT, and after VMRUN resumes following the VMGEXIT instruction, copying results from the GHCB back into its state; the #VC handler exits with IRET, which should not be intercepted except for NMI. The document defines the supported NAE event list with version associations and minimum state; the hypervisor need not intercept the generating instructions but must handle VMGEXIT for listed events, and the guest must handle #VC for all of them. Each guest- and hypervisor-set GHCB field must have its bit set in the VALID_BITMAP field, with the guest setting at least SW_EXITCODE, SW_EXITINFO1, and SW_EXITINFO2, and the hypervisor setting at least SW_EXITINFO1 and SW_EXITINFO2; both sides reset the bitmap before use. The bitmap bit position is derived from the field offset divided by 8 (e.g., RAX at 0x01f8 gives qword offset 63, byte offset 7, bit position 7). SW_EXITINFO1[31:0] carries error/action codes, including a request to inject an exception with the EVENTINJ value in SW_EXITINFO2, and specific codes for malformed VMGEXIT input, an unregistered GHCB address (SEV-SNP), invalid SW_SCRATCH, required input fields not marked valid, invalid NAE input, and hypervisor-specific reasons.

Specific event handling sections cover: IOIO_PROT, where the guest parses the faulting IN/OUT instruction or para-virtualizes it, builds SW_EXITINFO1, and uses the RESERVED shared buffer at offset 0x800 (address placed in SW_SCRATCH) as a decrypted string buffer, possibly over multiple VMGEXIT calls; MSR_PROT, where the guest parses the faulting RDMSR/WRMSR or para-virtualizes it and uses the NAE table entry; VMMCALL, where registers are hypervisor-specific; #NPF/MMIO access, where nested page table reserved bits (51:n) cause an #NPF with the RSV bit set, and the guest uses NPF/MMIO_READ or NPF/MMIO_WRITE with SW_EXITINFO1 as the MMIO source/destination GPA, SW_EXITINFO2 as byte count, and SW_SCRATCH pointing to a decrypted buffer, with repeated VMGEXIT calls when data exceeds the buffer.

**Page state change.** Available to SEV-ES guests (with the Page State Change Support feature bit) and SEV-SNP guests, this NAE requires SW_SCRATCH to point to a Page State Change structure in the GHCB shared buffer, which can hold up to 253 entries. Each entry carries a GFN to operate on and a current page field (offset in 4K increments; for 4K pages it must be 0, for 2M pages a value of 512 means all pages processed). Operation codes include making a page private (for SEV-SNP also updating the RMP table to guest-owned), making a page shared (RMP to hypervisor-owned), and PSMASH and UNSMASH hints for splitting a 2M page into 512 4K pages or combining them. Because updates occur incrementally, the hypervisor must increment cur_entry and, for 2M pages, cur_page, so the guest can resume an interrupted request; SW_EXITINFO2 carries reason codes such as interrupted request (0x00000000, retry), invalid header or entry structures, an SNP_PAGE_UNSMASH firmware error code, page already in the requested state, 4K/2M RMP overlap, or other errors.

**SNP guest requests.** The SNP Guest Request NAE event lets an SEV-SNP guest reach SEV-SNP firmware via SNP_GUEST_REQUEST using separate shared request and response pages, whose GPAs are translated to SPAs to verify the pages are hypervisor-owned. The response page is assigned to firmware with RMPUPDATE before the API call, then reclaimed with SNP_PAGE_RECLAIM and reassigned to the hypervisor afterward. The hypervisor should validate the response page GPA to avoid message sequence number desynchronization, and must save the return code in SW_EXITINFO2[31:0]; a value of 0 indicates success. Rate limiting is recommended against firmware denial of service, with SW_EXITINFO2 set to 0x0000000200000000 telling the guest to retry, and the guest must retry before another request so the AES-GCM IV is not reused.

**SNP Extended Guest Request.** Similar to the guest request but returns certificate data (VCEK and VLEK certificate GUIDs) in guest-contiguous shared data pages. A table at offset 0x0 of the DATA GPA lists entries of a 16-byte GUID, 4-byte offset, and 4-byte length, terminated by an all-zero entry. If too few pages are supplied, the hypervisor returns the required page count in RBX and sets SW_EXITINFO2 to 0x0000000100000000; this allows attestation reports and their verification certificates to be returned together.

**AP creation and other SNP events.** The AP Creation NAE event (SW_EXITCODE 0x8000_0013) lets an SEV-SNP guest create, add, update, or destroy an AP's vCPU state at a specified VMPL level, providing an alternative to INIT/SIPI booting; the guest must RMPADJUST the page to mark it a VMSA page, and either defer its use until INIT-SIPI or install it immediately. VMPL specification is only valid if the hypervisor advertises SEV-SNP Multi-VMPL. The #HV doorbell page event (SW_EXITCODE 0x8000_0014) registers a doorbell page for #HV injection under Restricted Injection, with GET_PREFERRED, SET, QUERY, and clear actions; a SET request must supply a page-aligned GPA, and the hypervisor must make the page hypervisor-owned. The #HV Send IPI event sends an IPI to guest vCPUs using an x2APIC Interrupt Command Register format. The #HV Timer event requests emulated APIC timer support with SET and GET actions over timer LVT, divide configuration, and initial count registers. The APIC ID List event returns the guest's APIC IDs (a 4-byte count followed by 4-byte entries) in guest-contiguous shared pages, with the required page count returned in RAX if too few pages are supplied, enabling SNP AP-based booting from the start. The SNP Run VMPL event runs the current vCPU at a different VMPL level by associating a unique VMSA (and optionally GHCB) per level; requesting a level without a VMSA must return an error. The SEV-TIO extension binds guests to trusted devices; the SNP TIO Guest Request passes guest PCI ID, MMIO range, and TDISP status, may accept a 32-byte measurements nonce in the data pages, and returns a table of GUID/offset/length data entries, with required page count in RBX and SW_EXITINFO2 set to 0x0000_0001_0000_0000 when insufficient pages are supplied. Secure AVIC manages guest-owned APIC state through a private backing page per vCPU, with REGISTER_BACKING_PAGE and UNREGISTER_BACKING_PAGE actions identified by APIC ID (0xffff_ffff_ffff_ffff meaning the calling vCPU); no feature bit is needed since Secure AVIC in SEV_FEATURES implies support. The termination request event lets a guest request termination, recommending an HLT loop or SHUTDOWN afterwards, with the reason code in SW_EXITINFO1[3:0]/[11:4] and 64 bits of termination information in SW_EXITINFO2; reason code set 0x0 includes 0x01 meaning the SEV-ES/GHCB protocol range is unsupported, with the unsupported feature mask in SW_EXITINFO2. If #VC is invoked for a NAE outside the negotiated version, the guest should VMGEXIT with the "Unsupported Event" exit code.

**Guest identification, AP booting, and other topics.** An SEV-ES guest must determine it is running under a hypervisor via additional CPUID properties: ECX[31] set, EAX[1] set for SEV support, EBX[5:0] the encryption bit position, and EBX[11:6] the reduction in physical address space bits. Because measured/encrypted vCPU registers cannot be updated, SMP booting under SEV-ES (and under SEV-SNP without the AP Creation event) requires a new mechanism: the hypervisor runs the AP with its initial register values on first reset and does not update registers on subsequent resets, with the AP using an AP Reset Hold request so the hypervisor treats it as halted and completes the hold on a SIPI request; the AP then enters real mode at the supplied reset vector with registers set to the Initial Processor State. With Restricted Injection, AP Reset Hold is unavailable and the SEV-SNP AP Creation event is required. Control transfer between environments (e.g., UEFI to OS) requires an AP jump table, a 4K-aligned encrypted page communicated to the OS by UEFI (via the AP Jump Table SET/GET software NAE events or the SEV-SNP secrets page), with serialization required if different reset vectors are used; vCPU hotplug is not supported under SEV-ES. For NMI handling, the hypervisor must not intercept IRET but must intercept #DB, using the guest's "NMI Complete" message as the indicator for injecting another NMI, which frees guest software from a prescribed sequence. Debug register virtualization is supported via the VMSA "DebugVirtualization" feature, in which case the hypervisor should clear intercepts for debug registers; otherwise DR7 read/write must be intercepted and the #VC handler must cache DR7 values rather than update the register. SMM and nested virtualization are not supported.

**#HV doorbell data format.** The doorbell page defines a 16-bit PendingEvent field (bytes 0–1) and NoEoiRequired (byte 2), with bytes 3–63 reserved; the backing page must be host-owned (not assigned via RMPUPDATE) and guest accesses must use C=0. PendingEvent[15] is NoFurtherSignal, [14:10] reserved, [9] indicates a virtual #MC, [8] an NMI, and [7:0] an interrupt vector. Because #HV is delivered regardless of interrupt shadows, a guest ready to halt should not examine pending interrupt state or enable interrupts before executing HLT with interrupts disabled, and on resumption should treat it as having just received #HV.

Under host behavior, the host emulates APIC semantics for presentation, acknowledgment, in-service, and EOI. When an interrupt source is ready and higher priority than anything in service, the host writes its vector into PendingEvent.Vector while the guest is not running; a non-zero vector may be overwritten by a higher-priority vector without another #HV, in which case the host sets NoFurtherSignal. NoEoiRequired is set when no other interrupts are ready and cleared when multiple are. For non-maskable events the host sets the appropriate bit and NoFurtherSignal, delivering #HV only if NoFurtherSignal was previously zero. The host marks an interrupt in service when it observes PendingEvent.Vector zero after presenting a non-zero vector, performs an EOI cycle when NoEoiRequired goes zero after having been set, and re-sets NoEoiRequired when interrupts remain in service with none pending; explicit APIC register writes and NoEoiRequired clearing are treated identically. A non-cooperative guest writing bogus values may lose a #HV notification but cannot corrupt host integrity.

Under guest behavior, on receiving #HV the guest may acknowledge immediately or defer until EFLAGS.IF permits; acknowledgment requires an atomic exchange to retrieve pending event information and zero PendingEvent, since a vector must not be acted on unless atomically exchanged with zero. After acknowledgment the guest assumes standard APIC semantics. For EOI the guest atomically exchanges zero with NoEoiRequired; if the previous value was non-zero, clearing it suffices, otherwise the guest must perform an APIC register write via VMGEXIT to the X2APIC EOI MSR. Even with EFLAGS.IF=0 the guest must be prepared to dispatch non-maskable events, clearing the non-maskable flags and NoFurtherSignal via atomic exchange without changing PendingEvent.Vector. Because a non-cooperative host may write random numbers, the guest must validate each observed vector, and receipt of #HV at any other time than when NoFurtherSignal is zero is grounds for a system panic. The passage also gives pseudocode for host APIC evaluation and guest dispatch, including atomic exchanges of PendingEvent[15..8] and the full PendingEvent field, and of NoEoiRequired.

A February 16, 2001 returned-mail notice reported that delivery to hgovenar@mail.acom2.com failed because the recipient was unknown. The returned email, from Jeff Dasovich to multiple Enron colleagues, was titled “Ken Lay’s email to Sen. Brulte” and included confidential materials intended for delivery to the senator’s office and simultaneous wider circulation.

The materials addressed barriers to distributed generation, Department of Water Resources credit risks under AB1X, and California’s projected summer 2001 electricity shortfall, estimated at about 5,000 MW. Enron’s proposed legislative package sought to increase supply through SB28X, reduce demand through AB31X, establish a competitive retail market through SB27X, and restore investor-owned utilities to solvency through AB18X. Enron preferred clarifying AB1X by amendment but also considered a CPUC order and alternative credit instruments. Dasovich also requested assistance with public relations, coalition-building, legislative messaging, and circulation in Sacramento. This cross-sectional study examined MRI-visible perivascular spaces (PVS), a component of the brain’s glymphatic system, in 467 people with epilepsy—temporal lobe epilepsy with hippocampal sclerosis (TLE-HS), temporal lobe epilepsy without MRI-visible lesions, extratemporal focal epilepsy, and idiopathic generalized epilepsy—and 473 healthy controls. Participants underwent 3T T1-weighted MRI, and PVS were segmented using PINGU and analyzed by region while accounting for age and sex.

All epilepsy groups had significantly greater PVS volume fractions and numbers in the basal ganglia than controls, with volume fractions 101–140% higher and standardized effect sizes of 0.95–1.37. This enlargement remained significant when the thalami were excluded. Thalamic enlargement was observed only in TLE-HS before covariate adjustment. After age and sex adjustment, no epilepsy group differed from controls in total white-matter PVS burden, and most subregional differences were not significant.

TLE-HS showed greater PVS on the contralateral side in whole white matter, most prominently in the temporal lobe, but controls also showed temporal asymmetry and between-group differences were generally absent. No PVS measure was associated with illness duration.

The findings indicate basal-ganglia PVS enlargement across all examined epilepsy subtypes. However, the cross-sectional design cannot determine whether PVS enlargement precedes seizures or results from them; longitudinal studies are needed to clarify this relationship and whether impaired glymphatic function contributes to epilepsy.

NVIDIA reported that David M. Shannon, 60, will retire at the end of 2016 as Executive Vice President, Chief Administrative Officer and Secretary. He joined NVIDIA in 2002 and oversaw its legal and human resources functions. Brian E. Cabrera will lead the legal team upon Shannon’s retirement, while NVIDIA will recruit a human resources leader.

The paper presents a correct-by-construction fault-tolerant voter for synchronous N-modular redundant measurement systems used in avionics control applications. The voter selects a reliable measurement from multiple input units, rejects transient errors, isolates persistently faulty units, limits prime-unit switching, and reports the output’s age and validity to the controller. Its fault model covers self-reported bad health and deviations exceeding the noise threshold δ. Faults persisting for at least the configured persistence limit are permanent, while at most a configured number of units may newly fault in one cycle.

Sixteen formal requirements address fault identification, permanent-fault isolation, output generation, validity status, and output age. The identification algorithm achieves sound and complete classification when enough healthy units remain, and provides partial, sound classification in other cases to delay unnecessary isolation. The voter always supplies healthy data when possible, retains the previous output during transient faults, and reports valid, unidentifiable, or invalid status according to system conditions.

The voter is implemented as a five-state transition system with configurable numbers of units, noise thresholds, persistence limits, and simultaneous-fault bounds. State definitions and transitions carry embedded Rocq proof terms establishing the requirements as invariants. Rocq verification of R1–R16 takes about 23 seconds; extraction produces 362 lines of OCaml code, with a single-cycle transition taking roughly 3 milliseconds. The code can be extracted to OCaml, Haskell, or Scheme. Future work includes hierarchical redundancy management and fault handling for asynchronous voting systems.

Dr. Thomas Wilson Ikubese, a 2019 presidential aspirant, joined the Alliance for New Nigeria (ANN) on May 29, 2018, after the Nigerian Intervention Movement adopted it as its party. He had left the National Conscience Party two weeks earlier, citing over-taxation. The guide defines optional SEV/SNP extensions for page migration and describes AMD’s Tiered Memory Page Migration (TMPM) engine. TMPM copies page contents between physical memory tiers while updating virtual-to-physical mappings. It requires IOMMU enablement and can be detected through the PM_Status ENGINE_READY bit. TMPM safely handles pages concurrently targeted by DMA and can migrate SNP-protected guest pages inaccessible to the hypervisor.

Software monitors access patterns, selects pages to move between memory tiers, and invokes TMPM to copy data and update IOMMU mappings. The PM_PAGE_MOVE_IO command migrates DMA-mapped pages and directly updates associated IOMMU host page table entries. In SNP systems, it applies to Hypervisor-owned pages. PM_PAGE_MOVE_GUEST migrates SNP guest pages whose sources are Guest-Valid or Guest-Invalid and whose destinations are Pre-Migration; afterward, sources remain Pre-Migration and destinations inherit the original source states. Guest migration does not support concurrent DMA, which may be aborted. The new Pre-Migration state uses a platform-specific ASID and must be converted back to Hypervisor state through RMPUpdate.

Commands include PM_GET_CAPABILITIES, PM_PAGE_MOVE_IO, PM_PAGE_MOVE_GUEST, and PM_NOOP. A command can contain 1–128 migration entries in a 4 KB parameter page, with no required adjacency or ordering between pages or commands. PM_SUCCESS means all pages migrated, PM_PARTIAL_SUCCESS requires checking per-page statuses, and PM_RMP_NOTEXCLUSIVE indicates a retry may be possible after an RMP conflict.

AMD testing found that commands moving 16 or more pages have significantly higher bandwidth than smaller batches, with maximum performance at 128 pages. Keeping the command ring buffer supplied, batching interrupt requests, and using a low-water interrupt can improve performance. Certain structures cannot be migrated, including SPA-accessed IOMMU structures, vIOMMU page tables and pinned buffers, the ring buffer, and argument pages.

TMPM uses a separate ring buffer containing 16-byte commands; one 4 KB page holds 256 commands. The driver controls the write pointer, while firmware controls the read pointer, and parallel execution means command ordering is not guaranteed. Device initialization validates engine readiness, ring-buffer address and configuration, and driver initialization state. The queue supports pause/resume, completion, error, empty, threshold, and ring-buffer error interrupts sharing one x86 interrupt signal.

Firmware reload requires pausing operations, draining and tearing down the ring buffer, disabling IOMMU PAGEMIGRATION_EN bits, and issuing a reload through the BIOS-to-PSP mailbox protocol. The replacement firmware must be the same or a newer version, and ENGINE_READY must be checked afterward. PM_GET_CAPABILITIES identifies supported families through FW_VER_Major; EPYC Family 19h uses value 71.

TMPM normally moves data between 4 KB-aligned pages. PM_PAGE_MOVE_IO requires 2 MB pages to be split into 4 KB pages, while PM_PAGE_MOVE_GUEST can accept aligned, physically contiguous 2 MB pages. IOMMU host page table entries have separate alignment rules, and software must avoid conflicting host-PTE modifications during TMPM operations. SPAs may be 46 or 52 bits and include encryption-state encoding.

Command-format errors cause rejection, migration-list errors may produce partial success, ring-buffer errors are reported through PM_Status, and hardware failures may be reported through command status and Machine Check Architecture. A failed batch of up to 128 pages may leave all affected pages unrecoverable, requiring software to preserve system state before reboot.

Doctors warned that eye cancer in India is often detected late, complicating treatment, and urged greater awareness of its types and symptoms. Retinoblastoma, the most common form in children under five, occurs in about one in 20,000 cases; early detection can preserve sight and life. Specialized facilities and trained ocular oncologists remain scarce.

**Summary**

This study examines online informal education and personalized learning in design education, published in the Turkish Online Journal of Distance Education (April 2024, Vol. 25, No. 2).

The introduction distinguishes formal education (structured curricula of compulsory and elective courses), non-formal education (workshops and courses for personal development), and informal education (observational and experiential learning through experts or everyday life). It contrasts conventional face-to-face, teacher-led, passive education with online education, which is virtual, multimedia-based, collaborative, active and student-centered, and notes that digitization since World War II has produced online repositories, virtual environments, hybrid and distance learning, and "ambient learning." The Internet enabled online education regardless of time and place, accelerating during the Covid-19 pandemic.

In design education specifically, sketching, computer-aided design, algorithms, computational and parametric design, and CNC machines have become indispensable tools. The article's primary research question asks how personalized education developed through diversified informal online learning platforms contributes to formal design education. A secondary quantitative method—literature review and case studies—assesses two synchronous examples: Driven by Volumes' five-day "Introduction to Computational Design" workshop (four hours daily, at least 10 participants, teaching Rhino and Grasshopper) and Rethinking the Future's 21-day "Sustainability through Computational Design" course (two hours daily, maximum 25 participants, integrating climate data, environmental analysis and LEED/GRIHA certification considerations with a capstone project and jury presentation). A table lists platforms offering design courses (Udemy, edX/Stanford, Coursera, MODE Lab, Rat-Lab, Black Spectacles, Archistar, Think Parametric).

Findings indicate that workshops and courses provide active, person-centric, collaborative learning, accelerate acquisition of design software skills, and encourage discussion and critical thinking; advantages include applied-based short-term training, open access and virtual accessibility. Limitations include unequal certificates, resource accessibility, restricted involvement in formal education, absence of personal interaction, financial barriers, isolation of participants, and exclusion of certificates from transcripts. The conclusion states that digitalization has brought personalization to teaching, that informal programs are progressively integrating into conventional education, and that certified informal training would strengthen its contribution to formal design education. The study notes its limitation: assessment was theoretical, and variability among organizations and trainers bounds objectivity, so quantitative results are needed.

The author, Zehra Tuğba Güzel, is a Research Assistant in the Department of Landscape Architecture at İskenderun Technical University, pursuing a PhD in design education at Istanbul Technical University.

The study develops and evaluates an integrated environmental education model based on multiple intelligences for students in expanded educational opportunity schools in Nakhon Pathom Primary Education Area 2, Thailand. These schools extend primary education through junior high school to improve opportunities for rural and remote students and support inclusive, sustainable education aligned with SDG 4.

The research followed three phases: assessing environmental education needs and community conditions through questionnaires and interviews; conducting a SWOT analysis and developing an integrated model; and implementing and evaluating the model with students. The main participants were 364 junior high school students, 44 teachers, and three school directors, while 30 students from three schools participated in the effectiveness evaluation. The model addresses nine intelligences and integrates environmental content with subjects through practical, collaborative, learner-centered activities.

Survey results identified agricultural chemical residues, wastewater discharge, chemical air pollution, indiscriminate waste disposal, and technological change as major community concerns. Students showed their lowest levels in environmental awareness, participation, skills, and evaluation ability, with an overall environmental-education mean of 3.95; teachers scored higher overall at 4.48.

The developed model met the specified effectiveness criterion, with E1/E2 values of 81.51/82.11. It also received high content validity (mean 4.60) and construct validity (mean 3.97). Students’ achievement increased significantly after instruction, and their overall satisfaction with the model’s content, activities, and benefits was high (mean 3.83). The findings indicate that the integrated, multiple-intelligences approach improved environmental knowledge, awareness, practical abilities, and engagement. Recommendations include extending environmental education to all educational institutions, using real-world cases and activities, strengthening systematic instruction, and developing standards and curricula for sustainable environmental management.

A seven-judge Constitution Bench of the Supreme Court, headed by Chief Justice T.S. Thakur, held that re-promulgation of ordinances is a fraud on the Constitution and subversion of democratic legislative processes, and that presidential or gubernatorial satisfaction under Articles 123 and 213 is subject to judicial review. Placing an ordinance before the legislature is a mandatory constitutional obligation; failure to do so is a serious constitutional infraction. An ordinance must be laid before the legislature and ceases to operate six weeks after reassembly or earlier upon disapproval. Justice Madan B. Lokur left the mandatory-laying question open. In the Bihar teacher-appointment cases, the Court held that salaries already paid should not be recovered.

A University of Surrey study finds solar photovoltaic power now costs as little as £0.02 per unit in the sunniest countries and is the cheapest option for large-scale generation even in the UK. Global installed solar capacity exceeded 1.5 terawatts in 2024, double its 2020 level. Lithium-ion battery prices have fallen 89% since 2010, making solar-plus-storage systems as cost-effective as gas plants and enabling stored solar power to balance grid demand.

Grid congestion remains a major challenge, with excess solar generation causing wasted energy in California and China. Researchers recommend smart grids, AI-based forecasting, stronger regional connections and continued storage development. Innovations such as perovskite cells could raise output by up to 50% without expanding land use. Long-term policy support, including the US Inflation Reduction Act, the EU’s REPowerEU plan and India’s Production Linked Incentive scheme, along with international collaboration, is considered essential to accelerating a reliable, low-carbon energy transition.

It accuses them of misleading aristocratic children, diverting school funds, and using preaching trips to sell books. Their opponents demand their departure and threaten an attack if they refuse.

Mr. Heard later reported to Mr. Gresham that Seoul’s Confucian followers had petitioned the king to force Tong Hâk adherents to reform or be exterminated. The king replied that the government would handle the matter and admonished the petitioners to study their professed principles.
A non-inverting comparator with hysteresis uses two resistors and VREF. Its output switches from low to high above VIN1 and from high to low below VIN2; hysteresis equals VIN1 minus VIN2.

The strategy sells the S&P 500 after a 20% decline from its all-time high and buys after 18 consecutive closes above the 200-day SMA during a bear market, holding until the next bear market. A backtest from 1927 to the present produced 12 signals, a 7.24% CAGR, 15.26 standard deviation, 0.24 Sharpe ratio, 60% maximum drawdown, and 87.38% market exposure. Excluding the 1929 crash, maximum drawdown was about 25%. Average gains after the signal were 9.54% at six months and 21.84% at one year. Compared with the golden cross, the strategy performed better on a non-risk-adjusted basis, invested 30% more time in the market, and generated fewer signals—12 versus 49. The latest signal occurred on February 15, 2023.
