The Stack Zone Offense is an overload-based system designed to create immediate matchup and adjustment problems for zone defenses. It emphasizes precise spacing, movement, continuity, defined player roles, and offensive rebounding. Its multiple entries and late-clock specials allow the offense to shift sides and attack a zone’s weak side. Missed shots are intended to become effective passes to teammates for put-backs.

The five positions have distinct duties. Point guard O1 directs the offense, reads defenses, attacks from the top, and can shoot from above the circle. Shooting guard O2 is the best outside shooter. Small forward O3 is an active front-line player, baseline shooter, and offensive rebounder. Power forward O4 operates from high or low post, can shoot and pass, and rebounds. Center O5 similarly operates from both post areas, posts on the strong-side block, and can pass or shoot. Several positions are interchangeable.

The offense progresses through four phases. Phase 1 uses basic overload reads, with O1 attacking and teammates spotting up, posting, screening, cutting, and rebounding. Phase 2 adds pass-and-cut action, high-post rolls, side-post feeds, weak-side post reads, and skip passes. Phase 3, labeled “High Post Roll,” develops the post entry and counter options. Phase 4 reverses the ball when O3 cannot feed O2 or O5, with O1 attacking the opposite side.

Continuity can repeat the pass-and-cut sequence. Optional entries include flop and exchange actions, triple-stack alignments, dribble entries, weak-side flop attacks, and post rolls. The triple-stack alignment, contributed by Tom Newell, disrupts defensive assignments by having O3 move opposite O2.

“Crunch Time” specials can be used as the shot or game clock expires. “Vegas” uses a weak-side double screen and skip pass. “Back” creates a weak-side lob through position exchanges and back screens. “Cat” immediately shifts into a 2-1-2 alignment against traps or double teams, using quick passes rather than dribbling. The system also specifies post-roll and back-cut rules depending on whether the ball enters a corner or the middle. Mike Frink is credited with introducing the particular stack continuity.

The passage explains offensive set pieces from free kicks in soccer, including their rules, strategic design, execution, and training.

Free kicks restart play after fouls or procedural violations. The non-offending team receives the ball, opponents must remain at least 10 yards away, and the kicker cannot immediately touch it again. Direct free kicks may result in a goal without another player touching the ball; indirect free kicks require another player to touch it first. The referee verifies placement, player distance, and readiness before play resumes.

Free kicks in the defensive half are generally short passes that retain possession, while those in the offensive third provide planned scoring opportunities. Effective designs account for distance and angle to goal, whether the kick is direct or indirect, and players’ abilities. They aim to overcome the defensive wall with minimal complexity and produce an effective shot. Set pieces are organized by location, with wall size and typical options ranging from crosses around two-player walls to direct shots or passes around four- or five-player walls.

Possible features include direct shots, simple touches, crosses, stepovers, misdirection, screening, committee formations, one- or two-pass plays, chips, decoy runs, ghosting runs, crashing runs, and rebound attempts. Indirect-kick designs must deliberately incorporate the required touch.

Execution depends on capable, responsible players who understand their assigned positions, know whether the kick is direct or indirect, and wait until the referee signals readiness. Coaches may use specialists, request enforcement of the 10-yard distance, and prepare for player absences or defensive tricks such as offside traps. A ceremonial free kick delays the restart while players organize, whereas a quick free kick takes the kick immediately, usually on a direct free kick, to exploit defensive disorganization.

In the rare case of an indirect free kick inside 10 yards of goal, defenders must position their wall on the goal line until the offense touches the ball. A quick simple-touch play may be used.

Practice should progress from running plays without defenders to using mannequins, stationary defenders, active defenders, and officiated scrimmages. Coaches should enforce rules, correct errors, rotate players, prepare contingencies, scout opponents, preserve player creativity, and avoid unnecessary complexity.

The document defines the user-level host interface for AMD AGESA software, aimed at host-environment wrapper implementers. It covers terminology, code and specification versioning, package organization, source-file headers, documentation, and public naming conventions: “Amd” for calls into AGESA and “Agesa” for call-outs. AGESA supplies default configuration values, while hosts provide required parameters through initialized configuration structures. Calls return status codes and may produce detailed event logs; only published entry points, which correspond to boot-sequence points, should be used.

The build design uses platform-specific `<Plat>Options.c` files and separately compiled defaults tables to select supported features and procedures. AGESA can be integrated as source or built as a standalone binary module. Binary images contain aligned `$AMD` and `$MOD` headers and use a bridge, dispatcher, and call-out router architecture. Calls require a valid stack, 32-bit protected flat-address mode, identity-mapped pages when paging is enabled, and a properly populated standard header.

Reported conditions range from success and unsupported operations to warnings, errors, critical errors, and fatal errors, with corresponding host responsibilities for logging, notification, POST continuation, or shutdown. The 16 most recent events can be retrieved through `AmdReadEventLog`.

UEFI support covers SEC, PEI, DXE, and runtime phases, with PEIM modules for processor, memory, and reset coordination and DXE components for table publication and GPU decoding. Integration requires specified build files, environment variables, and cache-as-RAM safeguards. Supporting procedures address structure allocation and release, event-log access, DIMM data-eye results, APIC and PCI identification, core and memory-address lookup, MMIO range merging, and pre-memory stack setup and teardown. Core initialization entry points include `AmdInitReset`, `AmdInitEarly`, and `AmdInitPost`, with extensive platform settings for caches, power management, PCIe, graphics, and memory.

The court affirmed a decree for specific performance of an oral land-sale contract to Thompson, whose assignee was Bales. Moore appointed an agent to sell his land, and Thompson reached a verbal agreement with the agent before Moore later agreed to sell the land to Matthew Hunter, who knew of Thompson’s title bond. Because the trial court had evidence supporting both parties’ theories, the appellate court adopted the theory sustaining its finding that Thompson had the prior equity and could enforce performance.

The court held that, in equity, a valid land-sale contract makes the vendee the owner and the vendor a trustee holding the land subject to a lien for the purchase money; a conforming conveyance relates back to the contract. However, a vendor may elect to treat an earlier oral contract as void by making a later valid sale, which also protects the later purchaser under the statute of frauds unless the purchase money is paid without notice. Thompson’s offer to bring the purchase money into court when liquidated and ready for performance was sufficient. After he tendered the purchase money and accrued interest and demanded a deed, the vendor had to prove use of the funds before interest could be charged.

The study compared a syndromic multiplex PCR panel with targeted hybridization capture-based metagenomic next-generation sequencing (mNGS) for 29 nasopharyngeal specimens from people suspected of acute upper respiratory infection. Detected organisms were assigned to phenotypic groups representing normal flora or contaminants, frequent disease association, and pathogenicity. PCR detected 15 organisms in 28 of 29 samples, while mNGS identified 44 organisms—27 bacteria, 15 viruses, and two fungi—and identified coinfection in 26 samples. For 33 shared targets, positive and negative agreement were 98.33% and 100%, respectively. mNGS additionally detected 29 organisms outside the PCR panel, including 12 of 15 organisms in the frequently disease-associated group and three pathogenic viruses: Coxsackievirus A, rhinovirus C, and SARS-CoV-2; both SARS-CoV-2 results were confirmed by specific PCR. The authors concluded that targeted hybridization capture-based mNGS can broaden respiratory pathogen detection and provide information relevant to possible lower-respiratory trafficking. They also noted interpretive challenges, a need for further study of clinical relevance and trafficking potential, and extensive validation requirements because no FDA-approved infectious-disease sequencing device or kit was available.

The paper addresses the inefficient exchange of technical information among industrial enterprises, focusing on the lifecycle management of process plants. Although standards exist for business documents, manufacturing integration, and some equipment data, none provides a scalable medium for digitally processing heterogeneous technical information. Current exchanges therefore rely on labor-intensive, error-prone methods such as spreadsheets, email, physical media, manual mapping, and repeated data entry.

Industrial information management spans value-chain, enterprise, and lifecycle domains. The lifecycle domain includes engineering, procurement, installation, operation, maintenance, and renewal, with each phase generating information needed for safe and reliable plant performance. Its complexity is increased by large and varied equipment bases, subcontracted services, proprietary back-end systems, inconsistent data structures, and technical records containing hierarchical product, device, design, and attachment data.

The proposed architecture combines an open consortium with a network of mediators. The consortium creates and maintains common business practices, information structures, and APIs, while remaining independent of particular implementation technologies. Mediators route information among parties, coordinate collaborative processes such as quotation, ordering, and delivery, and can provide matchmaking services. Each business party connects to a mediator through an adapter that maps its back-end systems to the agreed formats, allowing it to reach other parties without numerous point-to-point integrations.

A prototype was implemented as a .NET web application with configurable spreadsheet import and export, XML-based mappings, dedicated storage areas, task synchronization, and document storage. Experiments involving two equipment suppliers and two plant operators successfully transferred equipment information for maintenance and production-unit renewal cases, including product data, individual-device data, manuals, and certificates. Configured mappings avoided manual conversion during execution, while storage areas allowed recipients to review and approve incoming data.

The prototype demonstrated practical value but remains limited by the absence of an open consortium, agreed APIs, production adapters, and a mediator network. It supports only a single mediator, limited business workflows, and primarily technical rather than engineering-design information. Future work includes establishing consortium governance, expanding the mediator network and adapters, adding information types and workflows, and extending the approach to financing, logistics, manufacturing, and marine industries. The paper concludes that existing ICT technologies are sufficient, but effective digital exchange depends primarily on coordinating the ecosystem.

In Asa B. Meech v. City of Buffalo, plaintiffs challenged an additional assessment of $588.13 for a sewer improvement in Mariner Street. The city initially estimated and assessed $1,058.63 and contracted with Robert J. Randolph to construct the sewer for that amount. During construction, Randolph encountered an extensive, unforeseen body of quicksand that made completion at the contracted price impossible, and he stopped work.

Randolph petitioned the common council for additional compensation. The council granted $588.13 to secure completion of the sewer and directed assessors to charge that amount to benefited property. Plaintiffs sought to restrain collection, and the special court held the assessment illegal. The general term reversed that judgment.

The appellate court held that Buffalo’s charter authorized a further assessment when the original assessment proved insufficient to cover the improvement’s actual expense. The unforeseen quicksand created such a deficiency, and the city could modify or replace the original contract and agree to additional compensation. The modified agreement also supplied sufficient consideration because Randolph resumed and completed the work. The additional assessment was therefore authorized and valid, and the court affirmed the general term’s order and rendered judgment against the plaintiffs.

This case study examined how physical education teacher education (PETE) students gained 21st-century skills through peer mentoring in a movement education course. It was designed as a qualitative case study using a single-case holistic design, conducted in a 14-week first-year course at a university in Türkiye, involving three peer mentors (one final-year, two third-year students), 25 first-year peer learners, and the course lecturer. Data came from weekly field and reflection notes, meetings with the lecturer, audio recordings, social media messages, short films, peer feedback, and end-of-lesson online reflections, and were analyzed through inductive continuous comparison.

The course design combined storytelling and gamification with basic movement skills. Peer mentors created narratives using well-known series, cartoons, or digital game stories, shared weekly "invitation to the lesson," pre-lesson reminders, and task cards via Instagram and Discord channels, monitored task completion, and held weekly post-lesson evaluations with the lecturer. In the final four weeks, peer learner groups applied their own storytelling teaching designs to peers with mentor feedback.

Three themes emerged: (1) peer learners excluded group members who did not contribute, while peer mentors maintained accountability, divided responsibilities, and used adaptability, rotating leadership, and flexibility to complete tasks; (2) both roles produced storytelling course content, making learning more permanent and increasing awareness of being a teacher, with mentors gaining accountability competence and experiencing the teacher role; (3) narrative content linked to real life helped students connect learned movement skills with daily routines, remember information longer, increase interest, and develop self-evaluation, creativity, and problem-solving awareness.

The discussion and conclusion state that peer mentoring provides teacher candidates with realistic field experience during undergraduate study, supports 21st-century skills such as group work, communication, cooperation, and leadership, and can bridge students and teaching staff; storytelling-based, gamified learning outside traditional classrooms increases the permanence of knowledge and links content to everyday life. Recommendations are to integrate peer mentoring and storytelling into undergraduate teacher education programs at all grade levels, make them sustainable, and conduct long-term studies with prospective teachers.

The Korean diet is based on traditional Korean eating habits and emphasizes whole, unprocessed, plant-rich foods, including seasonal fruits and vegetables, whole grains, lean proteins, healthy fats, fermented foods, and broth-based dishes. Portion control and dietary adjustments are important, and vegan, low-carb, and gluten-free adaptations are possible.

Version 2 of the SEV-ES Guest-Hypervisor Communication Block (GHCB) specification adds a 52-bit FEATURES bitmap through which guests query supported hypervisor features. Features are mandatory unless identified as optional through this advertisement, and some features may depend on others.

The guest selects the GHCB’s guest physical address, which is exposed through MSR 0xc001_0130 and saved in VMCB offset 0xa0. The page must be 4K-aligned and mapped as decrypted or shared for hypervisor access; the hypervisor must not intercept the MSR. The lower 12 bits carry requests and responses. Documented exchanges include feature queries, SEV information for protocol-version and encryption-bit negotiation, CPUID register requests, AP reset hold, preferred or registered GHCB addresses, and termination. SEV-SNP guests must register a shared GHCB GPA before first use and may register separate addresses for each VMPL level.

The specification defines non-automatic exit handling for SEV-ES guests. A guest receives a #VC exception, populates the GHCB, invokes VMGEXIT, and processes the hypervisor’s response after resumption. The VALID_BITMAP identifies supplied fields; SW_EXITINFO1 and SW_EXITINFO2 report results and errors. Interrupts and preemption should be disabled while updating or reading GHCB state.

Supported events address I/O and MSR protection, VMMCALL, MMIO reads and writes, page-state changes, SNP guest and extended guest requests, AP creation, #HV doorbell, IPI, and timer operations, APIC ID lists, VMPL changes, SNP trusted I/O, Secure AVIC backing pages, and termination. Page-state requests use a shared buffer supporting up to 253 entries and can make pages private or shared, with optional SNP PSMASH and UNSMASH hints. SNP guest requests use separate shared request and response pages, preserve firmware message sequence numbers, and require retries before subsequent requests. Extended requests can return VCEK and VLEK certificates. AP creation manages VMSAs at specified VMPL levels and permits vCPU hotplug.

SNP launch processes provide secrets and CPUID pages to the guest, including reserved secrets-page fields for per-VMPL message sequence numbers, and firmware can publish the pages through an EFI configuration table. SEV-ES guests identify their environment through CPUID. SEV-ES application-processor startup uses reset-hold requests and an AP jump table, while SEV-SNP uses the AP Creation event, which is required with Restricted Injection.

Restricted Injection uses a shared #HV doorbell page containing PendingEvent and NoEoiRequired fields. The host emulates APIC presentation, acknowledgment, in-service, and EOI behavior; the guest atomically exchanges pending-event state, validates vectors, and follows defined HLT, EOI, and non-maskable-event procedures.

NMI handling requires an “NMI Complete” message before another NMI is injected. Hardware debug-register virtualization is supported when indicated, with specified DR7 emulation otherwise. SMM and nested virtualization are not supported.

Pumpkin is a nutrient-rich fruit in the Cucurbitaceae family, alongside cucumbers, melons, squash, and gourds. It can be incorporated into salads, soups, desserts, preserves, and baked goods. One cup of cooked pumpkin provides 52 calories, 3 grams of fiber, 13 grams of carbohydrate, iron, potassium, and carotenoids, including alpha- and beta-carotene, lutein, zeaxanthin, and vitamin E. The passage highlights potential benefits for cardiovascular health, immunity, eye health, dementia and cognition, and blood pressure. It emphasizes potassium and the potassium-to-sodium ratio for blood-pressure control, while describing carotenoids as having anti-cancer and anti-inflammatory properties. Lutein may reduce the risk of age-related macular degeneration, and beta-carotene may protect the eye lens from oxidation. The author, Doug Cook, is a registered dietitian and integrative and functional nutritionist.

The paper examines large language models (LLMs) as social artifacts whose significance emerges through engineering design and social embedding. It asks which themes organize the social science of LLMs, whether unsupervised clustering can recover a stable taxonomy, and how machine-derived categories align with expert classifications.

A PRISMA-compliant search of seven databases, refreshed on September 19, 2025, identified 64,717 records and retained 270 studies after deduplication, screening, and full-text assessment. The corpus comprised 142 journal articles, 65 preprints, and 63 conference papers, with most studies published from 2023 through 2025 and distributed across computer science, psychology, sociology, HCI, education, engineering, economics, and general-science venues.

Study 1 encoded titles and abstracts with SBERT sentence embeddings, visualized them with UMAP, and applied K-means clustering. Internal validation metrics and resampling stability analyses supported a three-cluster solution. LDA topic modeling identified two coherent themes per cluster: LLM as Social Minds (111 studies), LLM Societies (99), and LLM–Human Interactions (60). Documents with low or negative silhouette scores were concentrated near conceptual boundaries.

Study 2 had two experts independently classify the corpus using the same three categories. Expert labels were highly predictable from document semantics (Macro-F1 = 0.954 ± 0.018) and strongly aligned with the unsupervised partition (NMI = 0.811; ARI = 0.867). Most machine–expert differences involved low-silhouette boundary studies and highlighted unresolved distinctions among individual cognition, multi-agent interaction, and facilitated group decision-making.

The Social Minds literature examines mind-like capacities, moral and social reasoning, bias, self-regulation, ideological consistency, deception, and trust. Apparent theory-of-mind performance often weakens when prompts are altered or superficial cues are removed, while moral judgments and biases can be replicable yet sensitive to framing. Strategic incentives can also produce misleading outputs that alter users’ confidence and beliefs.

The LLM Societies literature covers interacting agents, generative simulations, cooperation and games, collective learning and polarization, institutional design, and committee- or jury-like decisions. Memory, planning, roles, reputation, rules, and sanctions can generate population-level regularities without hand-engineered rules, although cooperation varies with institutional scaffolds. Multi-agent dialogue also creates risks of deception and strategic misreporting that affect stability and epistemic quality.

The LLM–Human Interactions literature centers on perception, anthropomorphism, trust, reliance, affect, communication, collaboration, creativity, education, work, productivity, inequality, and safety. Interactions jointly shape human and model behavior: mental-state attributions influence trust, repeated outputs can create feedback loops, and LLM support can improve drafting and learning while also producing homogenization, deskilling, unequal benefits, and social-engineering risks.

The three categories are presented as complementary levels of analysis rather than mutually exclusive camps. The resulting framework offers a reproducible, testable map while recommending anti-shortcut tests, mechanism checks for multi-agent simulations, stronger trust calibration, and shared measurement standards. Limitations include an English-only corpus, the September 2025 cutoff, sensitivity to embedding and clustering choices, and the use of narrative synthesis rather than pooled effect sizes. The authors conclude that evaluation should prioritize situated performance and institutional adequacy over claims that LLMs are merely person-like.

Lincoln County defeated Laughlin 3–2 in its Homecoming volleyball match after leading 2–0. Coach Chantel Holt said the Lady Lynx lost focus when they could have finished in four sets, allowing Laughlin’s serving runs to narrow the match. Lincoln regrouped to win the final set and used substitutions to build camaraderie and give players opportunities to contribute. The Lady Lynx are scheduled to host Calvary at 3 and 4 p.m.

WiseGuyReports added its 2017 “Smart Service Robots Market” report to its research database. The report uses SWOT analysis and examines major manufacturers’ profiles, products, production capacity, prices, revenue, market share, and financial health. It analyzes the global market from 2012 to 2022 by region—North America, Europe, China, Japan, Southeast Asia, and India—by personal and professional robot types, and by commercial and home applications. Featured manufacturers include SoftBank, Kawada, Honda, Hajime Research Institute, PROTRYLY VISION GROUP, Ubtech Robotics, Suzhou Pangolin Robot, SIASUN Robot, ROBOTIS, Hanson Robotics, Dongbu Robot, Engineered Arts, Willow Garage, and QIHAN Technology/Sanbot.

The Tiered Memory Page Migration Operations Guide describes optional SEV and SNP extensions that add the Tiered Memory Page Migration (TMPM) engine for copying page contents and updating virtual-to-physical mappings while retaining the same guest physical address (GPA). Support is determined through the ENGINE_READY bit in the PM_Status register, and TMPM requires IOMMU enablement.

In tiered-memory systems, software can move frequently accessed data to faster memory and less frequently accessed data to slower memory. TMPM offloads these migrations, can pause DMA traffic while a page and its IOMMU mapping are updated, and can migrate guest pages protected by SEV Secure Nested Paging that the hypervisor or operating system cannot directly access.

PM_PAGE_MOVE_IO migrates pages that may concurrently be DMA targets and requires the relevant IOMMU host page table entry. Migrated source pages must be DMA-mapped through a single IOMMU host page table. In SNP systems, hypervisor-state pages can be migrated, with both source and destination returned to the Hypervisor state. PM_PAGE_MOVE_GUEST migrates SNP guest pages whose source pages are Guest-Valid or Guest-Invalid and whose destination pages are Pre-Migration. Afterward, source pages return to Pre-Migration and destination pages assume the original source states.

The new Pre-Migration state resembles Guest-Invalid but contains a platform-specific ASID, ignores the GPA, is not associated with a guest, and cannot be validated by a guest. The hypervisor or operating system can use RMPUpdate to return such a page to the Hypervisor state.

A command can migrate as many as 128 pages described in a Page Migration List. Pages need not be contiguous, a list may reference multiple guests, and entries and commands must have no order dependencies. Each entry receives a per-page status. PM_SUCCESS means all migrations succeeded; PM_PARTIAL_SUCCESS requires examining individual statuses; other statuses mean no migrations executed. PM_RMP_NOTEXCLUSIVE indicates a possible retry after a concurrent RMP update conflict.

AMD testing found that commands moving at least 16 pages have significantly higher bandwidth than smaller commands, with maximum performance at 128 pages. Best practices include keeping the command ring buffer full, requesting interrupts after command sequences through NOP or an interrupt-on-complete option, and using the ring-buffer low-water interrupt to refill the queue.

Migration is unsupported for IOMMU structures accessed by SPA, IOMMU page tables for the vIOMMU private address space, vIOMMU pinned backing storage, the ring buffer, and argument pages. TMPM may modify referenced IOMMU host page-table entries non-atomically and set their accessed and dirty bits, so software must avoid concurrent modifications.

Page Migration firmware can be reloaded only when no operations are in flight. The hypervisor or operating system is expected to pause operations, tear down the ring buffer, and use the BIOS-to-PSP mailbox protocol; IOMMU PAGEMIGRATION_EN bits should be disabled during reload. An initialized ring buffer causes PM_MX_INVALID_RELOAD_REQUEST, and reload firmware must be the same version or newer. ENGINE_READY must always be checked before communication. PM_GET_CAPABILITIES identifies capabilities and the EPYC family through FW_VER_Major; Family 19h uses value 71. The Family 19h reload procedure uses a 20-byte reload header, an ASP PCI register sequence, and command ID 0x70.

Because TMPM processes commands asynchronously, software testing individual migrations should keep the ring-buffer tail no more than one command entry ahead of the head. TMPM hardware moves data only between 4 KB-aligned pages, so all source and destination SPAs must be 4 KB aligned.

Amazon.com, Inc.’s unaudited Form 10-Q for the quarter ended September 30, 2016 reported Q3 net sales of $32.714 billion, up 29% from $25.358 billion a year earlier. Operating income rose to $575 million from $406 million, net income increased to $252 million from $79 million, and diluted earnings per share were $0.52 versus $0.17. For the first nine months, net sales were $92.246 billion, operating income was $2.931 billion, net income was $1.622 billion, and diluted earnings per share were $3.36.

Q3 net sales increased 26% in North America, 28% internationally, and 55% for AWS. Segment operating results were $255 million of income in North America, a $541 million international loss, and $861 million of AWS operating income. Operating cash flow was $4.486 billion for Q3, while capital expenditures were $1.841 billion, primarily supporting AWS infrastructure and fulfillment capacity. At September 30, cash, cash equivalents, and marketable securities totaled $18.3 billion at fair value.

The company had no borrowings under its $3 billion revolving credit agreement and entered a separate $500 million secured revolving facility in October. Total contractual commitments were $39.861 billion. A $5 billion stock-repurchase authorization was approved in February 2016, but no shares were repurchased in Q3.

The filing disclosed tax contingencies of $1.7 billion, including an IRS transfer-pricing dispute seeking approximately $1.5 billion in additional federal tax, a French assessment of €196 million, and a European Commission state-aid investigation. It also described patent litigation involving Amazon devices and AWS services, which Amazon disputes, and an ongoing review of orders involving sanctioned individuals and entities, voluntarily reported to U.S. authorities. Critical accounting areas included inventory valuation, goodwill impairment, stock-based compensation, and income taxes.

The 49ers ruled out quarterback Brock Purdy and receivers Ricky Pearsall and Jauan Jennings for Thursday’s game against the Rams, with Mac Jones set to start his third game in the first five weeks. Purdy cited toe soreness and the short turnaround, while Pearsall and Jennings are dealing with knee and rib injuries. Jones is back to full strength after a sprained knee but faces a Rams defense he called the NFL’s best. San Francisco has few healthy receivers and additional injury absences. The surrounding ESPN roundup covers NFL injuries, quarterback situations, rankings, playoff and draft projections, trades, betting and player stories.

A year-long knowledge-exchange project in England brought together UCL’s Institute of Education Citizenship PGCE course and LGBTQ+ anti-bullying charity Diversity Role Models. Through three workshops and placements from October 2023 to June 2024, student teachers explored integrating trans inclusion, rights, identities and personal stories into Citizenship classrooms.

The project occurred amid increased media hostility toward transgender people and proposed Department for Education guidance that could restrict discussion of gender identity. Existing statutory guidance still required teaching the facts and law concerning sexual orientation and gender identity, while the Equality Act 2010 protected transgender students. Teachers reported that classroom “actualizing” largely addressed sexual orientation rather than transgender identities, reflecting limited confidence to teach gender identity and a need for specialist training.

Teachers used equality and human rights frameworks to present LGBTQ+ people as rights holders and encourage empathy and allyship. Personal stories, case studies and role models helped make abstract issues concrete, challenge discriminatory narratives and potentially reduce transphobic bullying. Lessons addressed activism, HIV/AIDS, prejudice, safety, digital resilience and bullying.

Recommendations included extending inclusive practice beyond Citizenship through positive transgender visibility, restorative and consistently enforced anti-bullying approaches, student upstander training and Pride groups. International frameworks cited included the UNCRC, Yogyakarta Principles+10, UNESCO and Plan International, supporting inclusive curricula, comprehensive sexuality education and teacher development. The project highlighted the value of partnerships with specialist civil-society organisations to strengthen teachers’ confidence and capacity.

King Salman and Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan met in Riyadh to review bilateral ties, regional and international developments, and efforts toward peace, security, and combating terrorism. Senior Saudi and Turkish officials attended.

The President urges Congress to substantially reduce tariff duties on Cuban imports, arguing that reciprocity would advance Cuba’s economic recovery, strengthen U.S.-Cuban relations, and benefit American industries without undermining the protective tariff system. He cites Cuba’s urgent financial need, past U.S. assistance, and the strategic importance of Cuba following the Spanish-American War and the anticipated Isthmian Canal.

The passage summarizes medical problems reported after BNT162b2 boosters. Serious problems were defined as life-threatening, requiring hospital care, or causing lasting effects. In Phase 1, one of 24 participants in each of the 20-µg and 30-µg groups had a serious problem: inflamed appendix and inflamed nerves, respectively.
Taiwan health authorities advise avoiding raw or undercooked eggs, heating eggs to 70°C, washing hands after handling shells, thoroughly cooking poultry, wearing masks, and seeking care for fever.

Malaysia’s central bank will allow all resident entities to short-sell Malaysian government securities from May 2, expanding access beyond licensed banks and investment banks. It also permits non-banks net forward hedging positions up to 100% of underlying assets and 25% additional foreign-exchange exposure. BNM is considering short-selling Shariah-compliant government bonds, adding documentation-free currency hedging options and replacing its financial-markets code of conduct.

The New York Supreme Court, General Term, Fifth Department, reversed a $16,369.69 jury verdict for Charles Jones against Orin S. Bacon, executor of James McKechnie, and granted a new trial. Jones alleged that McKechnie promised to protect and save him harmless from liability on notes for Sherman Kingsbury, Jones’s son-in-law, whom Jones had endorsed at McKechnie’s request. If such an agreement was proven, McKechnie’s estate would be bound to perform it.

The court noted that Kingsbury was an interested witness, corroborating testimony was weak, and Jones’s delayed acceptance of mortgages after the alleged agreement required satisfactory proof. The decisive error was the admission of evidence that McKechnie, Denbow, and Kingsbury speculated in hops and that McKechnie refused a profitable sale that could have paid Kingsbury’s debts. Because the timing of the offer was uncertain and Jones was not connected with the hop transaction, the evidence was foreign to the issues, likely to evoke jury sympathy and prejudice, and a basis for speculation. Costs were to abide the event.

Kinlochleven first responders received three defibrillators, cabinets and training through local fundraising and donations. The devices will be placed outside the Co-op and GP surgery, and the group has raised £2,900 toward its £3,500 target.

Magda Enriquez, a Nicaraguan Council of State member representing the Sandinista Women’s Association AMNLAE, recounts leaving an affluent upbringing and American education to become a Sandinista organizer and trained soldier. After returning to Nicaragua in 1970, she founded a school for mentally retarded children; seeing that many were affected by malnutrition drove her into Managua’s slums and toward anti-injustice work informed by Catholic liberation theology. She joined the Sandinistas secretly in 1976 and helped found their women’s association the following year.

During a 1978 peasant land sit-in, police repression and pesticide poisoning left 150 children ill and ten dead before treatment. The incident prompted Enriquez to seek military training. Her eldest son later joined the militia, which she supported despite his age.

Enriquez says the Revolution created opportunities to address women’s problems without immediately resolving them. She has represented the women’s association internationally and helped lay groundwork for Nicaragua’s election procedures. Divorced and raising six children, she credits communal and party support for enabling her extensive political work while remaining closely involved with her family.

England captain Harry Kane scored a penalty and converted in the shootout as England defeated Colombia 4-3 on penalties, with Eric Dier netting the winner and Kieran Trippier also scoring. After Yerry Mina’s late equalizer, England advanced to face Sweden in the World Cup quarter-final on Saturday, with Kane emphasizing the team’s focus. Kane, England’s leading scorer with six goals, praised the squad’s spirit. Radamel Falcao accused the referee of favoring England, while Diego Maradona called the result a “monumental theft” and said the Colombian players were not to blame.

Between weeks 24 and 48, any-AE rates ranged from 33.8% to 40.8% and major bleeding rates from 0.3% to 0.7% across the three groups; two fatal bleeds occurred. Twenty-four deaths and no pregnancies were reported, with no concerning hepatic or renal signal. AEGEAN showed sustained apixaban adherence and persistence through 48 weeks; education provided no additional benefit.

Hinsdale South High School seniors were named Illinois State Scholars for ranking in the top 10 percent of the state’s graduating seniors. Selection combines ACT and SAT scores, unweighted GPA, and junior-year class size; more than 90 students were recognized.

The article examines the risk of running out of money in retirement, especially for Financial Independence, Retire Early (FIRE) individuals. It argues that retirees are vulnerable to adverse return sequences, excessive withdrawals, poor diversification, prolonged bear markets, and unexpected losses. An example follows a couple who retired in 2000 with $1 million and inflation-adjusted withdrawals of $50,000 annually; unfavorable returns and continued withdrawals left them penniless by 2017 and forced them back to work.

Sequence risk is the impact that the ordering of returns has on compounding. A simulation reshuffled 120 years of S&P 500 returns into 10,000 possible 25-year sequences. The average simulated annual return was about 11%, the median 9.5%, and 10% of simulations produced returns below roughly 3%.

William Bengen’s 4% rule is presented as a retirement withdrawal benchmark, but the article says it may be insufficient for FIRE portfolios because their longer horizons increase exposure to adverse sequences. In the example, reducing withdrawals from $50,000 to $40,000 improved outcomes, while a 3% rate allowed eventual recovery. Edward Thorp’s cited guidance recommends limiting perpetual inflation-adjusted spending to 2% of the original capital because early losses can permanently impair a portfolio.

The article concludes that retirees need a substantial margin of safety, conservative withdrawal rates, moderate spending, and diversification across markets and asset classes. It cautions that diversification can improve resilience but cannot eliminate risk because future market behavior may differ from the past.

Andrea and Luke Benrud gained national attention after Luke used CPR to save Andrea from collapsing due to a rare, undetected heart defect causing an irregular heartbeat. Their story was featured by People Magazine, and the CPR-trained family hopes sharing it will encourage others to learn CPR.

Body-camera footage showed Grand Rapids police Officer Kevin Penn pressing an AR-15 muzzle against a suspect’s head and using it to force his head down during an August 19 arrest. The drunk suspect was initially uncooperative and was Tasered by Sgt. Neil Gomez after officers responded to an armed-robbery call; the arrest involved the wrong man. Internal Affairs reported that another officer intervened after the suspect said the barrel hurt him. Penn resigned without charges. Kent County Prosecutor Chris Becker said Penn’s behavior violated police policy and was not something officers are trained to do, but he would not be charged because of the specific facts. The suspect was arrested for resisting arrest and released on his own recognizance.

Analysts expect the ECB to keep interest rates at historic lows and maintain its €30 billion monthly quantitative easing programme through September, tempering hopes of a rapid exit amid weak inflation, slowing growth and global trade uncertainty. Eurozone inflation was 1.3% in March and is forecast at 1.7% by 2020, while business activity remains expansionary but has lost momentum. ECB and IMF forecasts put 2018 growth at 2.4%. Policymakers may emphasize downside risks following U.S. tariff threats, while gradual, persistent normalization remains likely if risks do not materialize.

Police charged a Manheim Township man with drug manufacturing and possession, drug paraphernalia and endangering children after a warrant found marijuana plants and controlled substances in his home. Separate cases involved indecent assault charges against a 75-year-old man, corruption of minors against a 38-year-old man, and burglary, assault and terroristic threats against a 50-year-old man.

Companies hire experienced hosts, trade-show models, registration staff, and moderators to enhance their brand image and engage clients at events. Professionate provides an online staffing portal where companies can search candidate profiles, ratings, and reviews, while recruitment agencies and temporary workers can post profiles or browse vacancies.

Among 100 adults (56 males and 44 females) who completed both the self-reported PCL-5 and clinician-administered CAPS-5, scores were strongly correlated overall (ρ = 0.815). CAPS-5 severity did not differ significantly by sex or trauma type. Correlation was stronger for females (ρ = 0.907) than males (ρ = 0.655), and PCL-5’s odds ratio for predicting CAPS-5 was higher among females (144.6) than males (11.8). Males significantly deviated from the ideal regression based on diagnostic thresholds, with a mean difference of 12.5, whereas females showed no significant deviation. PCL-5 alone misclassified PTSD status for 26.8% of males versus 11.4% of females, primarily by classifying participants as PTSD-positive when CAPS-5 did not.

Correlation also differed by trauma type: civilian-trauma participants had stronger PCL-5/CAPS-5 agreement (ρ = 0.885) than military-trauma participants (ρ = 0.523), with the same pattern within each sex, although the female military subgroup was very small. The findings indicate that PCL-5 may be less reliable for assessing PTSD severity, particularly among males and military populations, and that sex and trauma type should be considered when interpreting self-reported results. Limitations include the small, geographically limited sample and few female participants with military trauma.

The U.N. warned that Yemen’s two-year war and unpaid salaries for over 73% of teachers could prevent up to 4.5 million children from finishing school, increasing risks of child marriage and recruitment as soldiers. The crisis followed the government’s relocation of Yemen’s central bank from Houthi-controlled Sanaa.

Channel 4’s documentary *The Super Orgasm* follows five women who report experiencing as many as 100 orgasms in one encounter. Tests measured arousal, brain-wave activity, and blood flow, finding that participants were easily aroused, showed sustained alpha-wave activity during multiple orgasms, and had increased blood flow in more than 30 brain areas. The documentary’s research was not scientific, however, because its sample was small and lacked a control group. Experts said “super orgasm” is not a meaningful scientific category and differs little from multiple orgasms, which are uncommon but can occur in different patterns and vary greatly among women. They accepted that the featured women may have unusually high numbers of orgasms but described them as outliers. The documentary did not address orgasm quality, and experts warned that suggesting all women could achieve 100 orgasms could create an unrealistic standard or imply that others are deficient.

The lecture proves that for a function \(f:S\subseteq\mathbb R\to\mathbb R\) at \(c\in S\), every function is continuous at \(c\) when \(c\) is not a cluster point of \(S\). If \(c\) is a cluster point, \(f\) is continuous at \(c\) if and only if \(\lim_{x\to c}f(x)=f(c)\), equivalently, if \(f(x_n)\to f(c)\) for every sequence \(x_n\in S\) converging to \(c\). The converse is proved by contradiction using points within \(1/n\) of \(c\).

Elementary trigonometric identities and bounds are used to prove directly that sine is continuous; the sequence characterization then establishes that cosine is continuous. The Dirichlet function, defined as 1 on rationals and 0 on irrationals, is shown to be discontinuous at every real number using rational and irrational sequences.

The lecture also proves that sums, products, and quotients of functions continuous at a point are continuous when the quotient’s denominator is nonzero. Composition preserves continuity when the outer function is continuous at the inner function’s value. As consequences, powers, polynomials, and functions such as \(1/(3+\sin^4x)\) are continuous. The lecture concludes by previewing the extreme value and intermediate value theorems.

A biotech newsletter highlights FDA approval of a second generic mifepristone and Amgen’s 12,000-patient Repatha trial, which found reduced combined risk of heart-disease death, heart attacks, and strokes. It also mentions a new NIH office focused on reducing animal testing and links to coverage of drug pricing, biotech stocks, women’s health, dementia, and tariffs.

Cover 3 is a common zone defense using four underneath defenders and three deep defenders. The two cornerbacks cover the outside thirds, while the free safety covers the deep middle. Defenders stay deeper than the deepest receiver, avoid deep passes, and traditionally do not press. The four underneath zones are the hook, curl, and flat areas on each side, typically handled by three linebackers and the strong safety.

The formation adds a defensive back to the deep field while allowing an extra safety near the line of scrimmage, potentially creating a numbers advantage against the run. It provides balanced coverage against both passing and rushing attacks and is especially common in high school and college football.

Its main weaknesses are the flats, where bailing cornerbacks can leave receivers open for short hitch, out, or arrow routes. Seam routes and four-vertical concepts can also challenge the three deep defenders, particularly when tight ends or slot receivers create difficult matchups. Perimeter runs may succeed because a bailing corner and a rolling safety can leave the edge vulnerable, while outside linebackers must balance run leverage and coverage responsibilities.

Variations include flipping the safeties’ assignments, using a fire zone to create pressure, and Cover 3 Buzz, in which a safety plays the hook-to-curl area over the middle. Coaches may also use pattern-reading coverage such as Rip/Liz to combine zone principles with route-specific coverage.

This message transmits to the House of Representatives a report from the Secretary of State with documents and correspondence relating to the Treaty of Guadalupe Hidalgo (February 2, 1848) and the Senate's amendments, including the commissioners' instructions of March 18, 1848, which the President had earlier declined to make public as prejudicial to the public interest but which the House had again requested.

The instructions confined the U.S. commissioners to procuring Mexico's ratification of the treaty as amended by the Senate, without negotiating any new treaty or altering the ratified terms; they were to explain the Senate's amendments to Mexican officials through personal conferences rather than diplomatic notes, and, if Mexico proposed amendments, to ask Mexico to send a commissioner to Washington to exchange ratifications should the U.S. Senate adopt them. The Secretary of State's letter of March 18, 1848 to the Mexican minister for foreign affairs explained the amendments; this dispatch was transmitted by the commissioners to the Mexican government at Queretaro on April 17 and acknowledged April 19, and it alone was before the Mexican Congress. On May 8, 1848 the Mexican President submitted the amended treaty to Congress, which approved it without modification on May 25, the Senate voting 33 to 5, before the U.S. commissioners were officially received. The commissioners presented their credentials to the Mexican President on May 26, held conferences with Rosa, Cuevas, and Conto, and effected the exchange of ratifications on May 30, enclosing a protocol summarizing the conversations. The amended treaty reached Washington on July 4, 1848 and was proclaimed the supreme law of the land; it was communicated to Congress on July 6 with such papers as were deemed material.

By the time the remaining papers arrived, peace was restored, the first installment of three millions paid, blockades raised, Mexico City evacuated, and troops returning home; the treaty was binding and largely executed, and only a solemn declaration of war could annul it. The protocol therefore could have no binding effect: it was exchanged after the Mexican Congress acted, and neither the commissioners nor the Mexican government regarded it as a new negotiation or a modification.

The protocol contained three explanations, all consistent with the treaty: that suppressing the ninth article and substituting the Louisiana treaty's third article did not diminish the guaranties to inhabitants of the ceded territories, the Senate's amended article being more comprehensive and securing their incorporation into the Union, protection of liberty and property, and free exercise of religion "without restriction"; that suppressing the tenth article did not annul Mexican land grants, which preserve their legal value, with legitimate titles being those valid under Mexican law in California and New Mexico up to May 13, 1846, and in Texas up to March 2, 1836—the objection having been that the article revived extinct grants, and the Senate having rejected it while ratifying the eighth article's final paragraph protecting Mexican property; and that suppressing the concluding paragraph of the twelfth article did not deprive Mexico of the faculty to assign its $12,000,000 payment obligation, the amendment merely prohibiting issuance of transferable government certificates. Believing the protocol consistent with the ratified treaty, the President took no action on it, noting that had it varied from the treaty's terms, though still a nullity, he would have notified the Mexican government.

A jury found John Jacob Beechwood insolvent and guilty of two acts of bankruptcy in an involuntary proceeding brought by American Surety Company. The remaining issue was whether Beechwood was a farmer exempt from involuntary bankruptcy under the Bankruptcy Act, which required personal engagement in farming and that farming provide the principal part of one’s income, measured at the time the act of bankruptcy occurred.

Beechwood lived on a New Jersey farm but worked full time for 15 years as a lawyer and Fidelity and Casualty Company employee, earning most of his income from his profession. A hired practical farmer managed the farm, while Beechwood worked there during weekends and leisure time. On the dates of the two transfers found to be acts of bankruptcy—September 20 and October 10, 1940—he was occupied with efforts to address the consequences of his actions, not earning his livelihood from farming. Although he later devoted his full time to the farm, his status on the relevant dates did not qualify him as a farmer.

The court distinguished the cited cases because the debtors there personally pursued farming as their principal occupation. Beechwood’s farmer defense failed, and the court held that an order adjudicating him bankrupt should be entered.

The Times reported that Paul Manafort, Trump's campaign chairman who consulted in Russia and Ukraine, was among the advisers picked up on calls with Russians; no others were named. Manafort called it "absurd" and denied knowingly speaking to Russian intelligence officers. A January U.S. report said Russia sought to help Trump win; Russia denies involvement. Cummings called the report "very alarming." It followed Michael Flynn's resignation over calls with Russia's ambassador, while Spicer said Trump had not changed his January denial of campaign contacts with Russians.

S. E. Mezes reported good progress at Thursday’s meeting, expressed confidence that The Inquiry would continue satisfactorily, and said he was sending memorandum copies to other attendees. The memorandum identifies materials for peace conferences, including information on nations, national aspirations, international governmental arrangements, world organization, laws of war, reparations, trade routes, business, diplomacy, and concurrent or later action by subcommittees and commissions. Inquiry Document No. 893 surveys conference tasks: establishing boundaries and governments, assessing doubtful states, arranging economic matters, protecting minorities and weak peoples, ensuring equal economic opportunity, revising international law, and considering diplomatic history. It applies these tasks to numerous regions, including Russia, Poland, Belgium, Luxembourg, Alsace-Lorraine, Trentino, Trieste, Austria-Hungary, the Balkans, Turkey, Africa, the Far East, Pacific Islands, Latin America, Persia, Afghanistan, and Spitsbergen. Boundaries will have to be established in several regions, while governments will have to be established for Poland and Austria-Hungary.

Amazon is preparing to cut as much as 15% of its human resources staff, with additional layoffs likely in consumer and other divisions, according to sources. The total number affected and timing are unknown. Its PXT human resources division has more than 10,000 employees worldwide. Amazon made smaller layoffs earlier this year in consumer devices, Wondery and AWS. The cuts come as Amazon reduces costs while investing heavily in AI and plans capital expenditures exceeding $100 billion this year. CEO Andy Jassy has said AI efficiency gains will reduce Amazon’s total corporate workforce. Amazon previously cut at least 27,000 corporate jobs in 2022-2023. Despite the planned corporate cuts, the company plans to hire 250,000 seasonal warehouse and logistics workers.

Vice President Biden’s inaugural address affirmed the Constitution’s promise of equality, liberty, and an unalienable right to the pursuit of happiness. He argued that preserving these principles requires collective action, government innovation, a rising middle class, education, infrastructure, and support for those facing unemployment, illness, disability, or poverty. He called for health-care and tax reforms, social insurance programs, action against climate change, and leadership in developing sustainable energy. On foreign policy, he advocated strong alliances, democratic support, peaceful engagement, and defense through military strength and the rule of law. He also emphasized equal opportunity for women, gay and lesbian citizens, immigrants, voters, and children, while urging citizens to shape public debate and government action without partisan obstruction, recognizing that progress would be ongoing and imperfect.

A Brazilian mouse study in the *Journal of Hematology & Thromboembolic Diseases* examined Bt/Cry toxins used in many genetically modified food crops. It reportedly found that multiple toxin combinations and doses damaged red-blood-cell lineages, caused anemia, suppressed bone-marrow proliferation, and produced lymphocyte patterns associated with leukemia. Certain toxins caused effects in distilled water, challenging the belief that mammalian digestion prevents their activation, and effects became more pronounced after 72 hours. Cry1Ab at 27 mg/kg induced hypochromic anemia, while high doses caused changes indicating bone-marrow damage. The authors concluded that Bt spore-crystals expressing Cry1Aa, Cry1Ab, Cry1Ac, or Cry2A may pose hematological risks to vertebrates and called for further research before concluding they are safe for mammals. The passage also cites a French rat study linking GM corn and Roundup to cancer, raises concerns about combined Cry-toxin and glyphosate exposure, criticizes alleged industry influence on GMO research, and advocates stronger labeling or restrictions pending further evidence.

CarsDirect's December holiday deals on fuel-efficient vehicles include leases as low as $159/month and discounts up to $18,100. For hybrids, the 2017 Kia Optima offers a $5,000 factory discount in Western states ($4,000 elsewhere) or 0-percent APR financing over 60 months, which forfeits $3,000 in bonus cash. The 2017 Kia Optima Plug-In leases for $249/month over 36 months with $1,999 down, plus a $4,919 federal tax credit and California's $1,500 rebate; the 2017 Hyundai Sonata Plug-In runs $289/month, and the 2017 Chevrolet Volt $273/month with a $7,500 credit. For electrics, the 2017 Kia Soul EV offers $18,100 off the EV+ version or a $159/month lease—the cheapest on the market—while the Bolt EV lease runs $303/month ($329 elsewhere). Nationwide, the 2018 Chevrolet Equinox diesel gets $4,000 off with 39 mpg highway. The 2017 Toyota Yaris iA is $2,000 off in Southern California only.

Founded by Herbert Henry Martyn in Cheltenham in 1888, H H Martyn & Co. became a diversified craft and engineering firm employing 1,000 people by 1910. At its Sunningend works, it produced Marble Arch’s iron gates, royal interior work, prestigious architectural commissions, and fittings for more than 100 ocean liners, including the Titanic, Lusitania, Queen Mary and QE2. During the First World War it began manufacturing military aircraft, leading to the birth of Gloster Aircraft Company. Martyn’s also contributed to Sir Henry Segrave’s Golden Arrow car, made Wolseley cars and designed the Unibus scooter. Between 1920 and 1937, it supplied 75% of Britain’s ordered art metalwork and later produced sculptures by Henry Moore and statues of Winston Churchill and Robert the Bruce. Acquired by Maples in the mid-1930s, the firm received further wartime contracts. Britain’s declining shipbuilding industry led Maples to sell its assets and close Martyn’s in 1971.

Index Markets Research’s global Meat Starter Culture Market report examines historical, current, and projected market data, including status, growth, trends, revenues, demand, pricing, capacity, production, supply, and forecasts. It analyzes market drivers, constraints, risks, opportunities, PEST and Porter’s Five Forces, applications, regional markets, and competition, with SWOT, investment feasibility, and return analyses. Coverage includes maturation and surface starters; meat, poultry, seafood, and other applications; and the United States, China, Europe, Japan, Southeast Asia, India, and Rest of the World for 2018–2025. The report also discusses key manufacturers and provides sales contact information for sample and purchase inquiries.

In 1826, Capt. Thomas ap Catesby Jones visited Honolulu to address deserters and American residents’ claims. He negotiated Hawaii’s first treaty with a foreign power, covering friendship, commerce, and navigation. Although the U.S. government did not ratify it, both parties considered its friendly provisions morally binding. In 1829, Commodore Finch carried a presidential letter urging peace, kindness, and justice between Hawaiian authorities and visiting Americans. U.S. naval vessels later intervened in Hawaiian affairs, including Commodore Downs’s protection of persecuted Catholic converts.

French and British pressure increased. In 1839, Laplace secured a Hawaiian commerce treaty with protections for Catholics and avoided hostilities; its terms also introduced intoxicating liquors. Britain had compelled a treaty in 1836, and in 1843 Lord George Paulet seized the islands, forced Kamehameha III to cede them, and established a commission to govern in the king’s absence. After U.S. Commodore Kearney protested the cession and harm to Americans, Rear-Admiral Thomas conferred with the king. The Hawaiian flag was restored on July 31, 1843, and Paulet’s seizure was disavowed.

On September 9, 2020, Amazon.com, Inc.’s Board elected retired General Keith B. Alexander as a director and appointed him to its Audit Committee. Alexander is Co-Chief Executive Officer, President, and Chairman of IronNet Cybersecurity, which he founded in 2014. He previously commanded U.S. Cyber Command and served as Director of the National Security Agency and Chief of the Central Security Service. Upon his election, Alexander received an award of 288 restricted stock units vesting in three equal annual installments beginning November 15, 2021, subject to continued service, and entered into an indemnification agreement with Amazon.

The paper proposes a Bayesian, tree-structured recursive bipartitioning framework for community detection that does not require prespecifying the number of communities. Networks are repeatedly divided into two subnetworks using model-specific MCMC, with recursion governed by a Bayes-factor stopping rule that compares models with and without community structure. This approach can reveal hierarchical community structures and accommodate network properties through likelihood functions.

The framework is developed for three model classes: stochastic block models with block-specific connection probabilities, directed edge-exchangeable models using block-specific GEM distributions and interaction propensities, and latent-space models where connection probabilities depend on latent Euclidean distances and observed dyadic attributes, with communities represented by a Gaussian mixture.

For stochastic block models, the paper defines strong and weak consistency relative to Erdős–Rényi modularity. It proves that a suitable bipartition exists and that recursive bipartitioning is strongly consistent when expected degree divided by the logarithm of subnetwork size diverges, and weakly consistent when expected degree diverges. No theoretical consistency guarantees are provided for the other two model classes. Gibbs-sampling algorithms are developed for the models, and the method is evaluated through simulations and application to stroke patient transfer data, where detected communities can reveal regional hospital connection patterns relevant to healthcare-access disparities.
