Two boards can be linked with NVLink for 96 GB of combined memory. The document provides comparative workstation, rendering, HPC, and deep-learning results against the RTX 6000.

- Overall, the document presents GA10x as delivering up to twice the programmable-shading, ray-tracing, and AI performance of Turing, while adding concurrency, motion-blur acceleration, sparsity, DLSS, faster storage, GDDR6X, modern display support, and improved video encode and decode capabilities.

Welles Wilder introduced the ADX/DMI indicator in his 1978 book *New Concepts in Technical Trading Systems*. ADX measures trend strength, while rising or falling DI+ and DI- indicate bullish or bearish direction. It is a lagging indicator ranging from 0 to 100; readings below 15 indicate a non-trending market, while readings above 20 indicate a trend. Backtests showed that standalone ADX strategies performed modestly. A 10-day DI crossover on SPY produced a 5.4% CAGR and 1.71 profit factor, while an optimized 35-day DI/15-day ADX breakout yielded a 3.03% CAGR and 13.76% drawdown, underperforming buy-and-hold’s 9.9% CAGR. However, adding an ADX filter improved a separate mean-reversion strategy, producing a 7.3% CAGR on SPY and 12.5% on QQQ. The article concludes that ADX is reasonably useful alone but more valuable alongside other indicators and recommends independent backtesting.

The speaker emphasizes disciplined power play and penalty kill execution, puck support, quick changes, and attention to detail against an opponent with elite puck-moving personnel. Despite losing key players, he expresses confidence in the team’s depth and strong community support.

A Stanford, Harvard and Census Bureau study using de-identified data on 20 million U.S. children found persistent racial income gaps even among children from similarly situated families. In 99% of neighborhoods, Black boys earned less as adults than white boys with comparable socioeconomic backgrounds. Black children of top-1% earners had incomes 12.4% below white children from similarly incomeed households. Upward mobility from the bottom income quintile was about 11% for white children and 2.5% for Black children; Black and Native American children had the lowest mobility rates. The earnings gap was largely driven by Black and white men, while Black women earned slightly more than white women after accounting for parental income. Neighborhood conditions remained influential, with larger gaps in affluent areas, though some Washington-area suburbs showed greater parity and were associated with less racial bias and higher community rates of Black fathers. Researchers suggested that historical experiences may help explain persistent disparities.

On October 7, 2016, NVIDIA entered into a five-year unsecured senior revolving credit agreement with Wells Fargo Bank as administrative agent and other lenders. The facility permits borrowings, repayments, and reborrowings of up to $575 million for working capital and general corporate purposes, with outstanding obligations due October 7, 2021. It also allows up to $425 million in additional revolving commitments and/or letters of credit, subject to conditions. Loans may bear interest at NVIDIA’s election at the Adjusted LIBO Rate or Alternate Base Rate plus an applicable rate. The agreement includes customary covenants, events of default, restrictions on subsidiary debt, liens, and fundamental changes, and a debt-to-adjusted-EBITDA maintenance covenant. The obligations rank equally with NVIDIA’s other unsecured and unsubordinated indebtedness.

Future Electronics and NXP will host a free July 4, 2018 seminar in San Sebastian, Spain, introducing the i.MX RT Series crossover processor and offering hands-on feature exercises. The RT105x processors use an Arm Cortex-M7 core for high real-time performance and omit flash memory, allowing flexible, cost-effective implementation. Registration: https://tinyurl.com/NXPRoadshow.

Berliners are honored for their courage in resisting division and tearing down the Berlin Wall. The speaker pledges continued American support, including a new U.S. embassy in Berlin and forces remaining in Europe, and calls on Berliners to apply the same courage to building an independent, democratic, prosperous Europe based on open borders, peace, and cooperation rather than division. The speaker rejects racial, ethnic, and religious hostility, urges young Germans to live peacefully with others, and cites expanding democracy, economic growth, reform, and NATO’s Partnership for Peace as reasons for hope. Walking through the Brandenburg Gate with Chancellor Kohl, the speaker envisions a united Europe free from walls and declares that America stands with Berlin now and forever.

President Donald Trump announced an agreement with Pfizer to lower U.S. drug prices. Pfizer will offer existing drugs to Medicaid patients at the lowest prices paid in developed nations and extend most-favored-nation pricing to new drugs for Medicare, Medicaid and commercial payers. The company will offer selected treatments through TrumpRx.gov at discounts averaging 50% and up to 85%.

Pfizer also received a three-year exemption from pharmaceutical-specific tariffs, conditional on continued U.S. manufacturing investment. The company plans to invest $70 billion in domestic drug manufacturing and research facilities. The deal preceded Trump’s threatened 100% tariff on imported branded or patented pharmaceuticals, though companies building U.S. plants would be exempt. Pfizer shares rose more than 4% after the announcement.

Trump said he was seeking similar agreements with other drugmakers, and the White House confirmed that Eli Lilly was in negotiations.

NVIDIA appointed Tim Teter as senior vice president, general counsel and secretary, effective when his employment begins, expected January 23, 2017. Teter will lead the legal department while David M. Shannon continues to lead human resources and assist with legal matters until his retirement. Teter previously spent more than two decades as a Cooley LLP partner focusing on patent and technology litigation and formerly worked as an engineer at Lockheed Missiles and Space Company.

Teter’s at-will offer includes an $850,000 annual base salary, a fiscal 2018 target annual incentive of $250,000, and a $450,000 first-anniversary bonus subject to repayment if he leaves before his second anniversary. He will also receive restricted stock units targeted at $5.8 million, vesting over four years subject to continued employment, and may participate in NVIDIA’s employee stock purchase plan and comprehensive benefits. NVIDIA also expects him to enter its standard officer indemnity agreement.

The author’s retirement dividend portfolio, held in Roth IRAs, workplace 403(b)s and share-builder accounts, outperformed the S&P 500 every month in 2016. It returned 15% from dividends and capital gains, excluding new contributions, compared with 11.66% for the S&P 500 including dividends. The portfolio returned 5.39% in 2015, while the index was nearly flat, and the author targets annual returns of 6–8% without expecting to repeat 2016’s results.

Of 27 holdings at year’s start, only five declined. Chevron led with a 30.84% gain, followed by JPMorgan at 30.68% and AT&T at 23.60%. Aflac and 3M completed the top five. Gilead Sciences fell 29.23%, CVS Health fell 19.29%, and Starbucks declined 7.51%; Coca-Cola and Target also posted small losses.

The author bought eight new companies, including Visa, Cisco, Pepsi, Cummins, Honeywell, Qualcomm, Disney and V.F. Corp., sold Baxalta for Visa, and ended the year with 35 holdings. Boeing, Cisco and Microsoft performed particularly well among the purchases, while both CVS Health purchases remained at a loss. The author plans to continue buying companies that regularly pay and raise dividends when shares appear under fair value.

The passage reviews the benefits and challenges of virtual education and reports a mixed-method study of Indiana public school districts during the 2020–21 school year. Surveys were sent to all Indiana superintendents and virtual program administrators, with follow-up interviews conducted with 11 volunteers. The survey instrument was based on a 2014 Kansas study. Survey responses, interviews, and prior research were used to identify common themes.

Virtual education can provide flexible scheduling, individualized instruction and pacing, expanded course access, credit recovery, and opportunities to retake courses or improve grades. It may accommodate students with health, physical, behavioral, or other special needs, increase parental engagement, and offer students experiences resembling postsecondary learning. Challenges include unreliable internet access, technology requirements, difficulty providing accommodations, delayed feedback, weaker teacher interaction, isolation, limited community, reduced motivation, and the need for greater independence and time-management skills.

Pandemic-related concerns were the leading factor in adopting or maintaining virtual programs. COVID-19 concerns were rated “very important” by 79.2% of responding superintendents, while 84.8% of program administrators agreed or strongly agreed that they motivated districts to maintain virtual programs. Credit recovery was also highly important. The most frequently identified benefits were maintaining enrollment during the pandemic, reported by 90.1% of superintendents and 88.6% of program administrators; credit recovery; and learner convenience and flexibility.

Student engagement was the leading reported challenge, identified by 80.5% of superintendents and 97.1% of program administrators. Ensuring curriculum and instructional quality ranked second, at 79.2% and 85.3%, respectively. About half identified staffing virtual classes as a challenge, while roughly 47% cited professional development needs.

Interviews identified three pandemic-related themes. Districts faced enrollment and revenue pressures, expanded virtual options, and accelerated technology plans, while viewing virtual education as a way to provide school choice and flexibility. Teachers experienced stress and inadequate platform training but also developed greater technology skills. Students and families faced social-emotional difficulties, weaker peer and teacher relationships, attendance and engagement problems, insufficient self-direction and time management, and a strong dependence on parental support. Some students nevertheless succeeded better virtually than in person.

The findings indicate that districts should account for pandemic-related demand, credit recovery, flexibility, parental support, engagement, instructional quality, staffing, and teacher professional development when designing virtual programs. Future research should examine post-pandemic program changes, characteristics of successful virtual students and educators, and ways to improve program effectiveness. The study represents a snapshot of virtual education in Indiana during 2020–21 and concludes that the pandemic accelerated its growth while highlighting benefits and challenges that had already existed in virtual schooling.

The paper studies decentralized strategy convergence in multi-agent reinforcement learning using game theory. It focuses on “win-stay, lose-shift” satisficing dynamics, where a player whose strategy is a best response keeps that strategy while others may switch. The central question asks when every initial joint strategy admits a finite-length satisficing path ending at an equilibrium.

The paper formalizes finite-player pure-strategy games, best responses, equilibria, mixed games, and a new grouped satisficing path, in which all members of a player group retain their strategies when every member is a best response. This concept generalizes the classical satisficing path. Topological analysis examines the number of best-response groups and establishes that, under convex compact strategy sets and continuous, partially analytic payoffs, best-response groups at local minima persist across admissible successor strategies, allowing games to be reduced to subgames.

The main theorem states that if each strategy set is convex and compact, each payoff function is continuous and partially analytic, and every subgame has an equilibrium, then every initial joint strategy admits a finite-length grouped satisficing path ending at an equilibrium. Corollaries apply this result to continuous games with quasi-convex payoffs, finite-strategy N-player games, and stationary and finite-step finite-state mixed Markov games. The results indicate that stochastic learning can begin from arbitrary strategies and reach equilibrium without requiring best-responding players to change, without restrictions on update functions. Open problems include finding necessary and sufficient conditions, extending the results to positive error tolerance, and restricting how non-best-responding players may change strategies.

This lecture covers two topics: the HP model of protein folding and interlocked 3D chains.

**Protein folding.** Real folding uses energy functions combining torsion potentials, van der Waals forces, hydrogen bonds, hydrophobicity, secondary-structure propensity, and specific interactions, matched against 3D structures from the Protein Data Bank; the correct objective is unknown. The lecture instead studies a simplified model capturing only hydrophobicity: chains of H (hydrophobic) and P (hydrophilic/polar) nodes folded on a square lattice, scored by the number of adjacent H–H bonds, which is maximized. Because each H node has at most two bond neighbors, the optimum is at most twice the smaller of the even-parity and odd-parity H counts. Finding the optimal folding is NP-hard (Berger and Leighton in the 3D cubic lattice; later work in 2D), suggesting nature may reach local optima or that evolved proteins make local optima globally optimal. The best known approximation is a 1/3 factor, achieved by a staged construction using long side branches that match even H's on one side with odd H's on the other, obtaining two bonds per three usable H nodes. A separate theorem (Aicholzer, Bremner, Demaine, Meijer, Sacristan, Soss) shows HP chains with unique optimal foldings exist for all even-length closed chains and all doubly-even-length open chains; singly-even open chains are nearly unique, odd lengths remain open, and extension to the triangular lattice is open. Open questions include protein design (designing chains that fold into a target shape, e.g., a letter "M", with unique optimum) and behavior when H and P counts are imbalanced; the speaker conjectures the counts differ by a constant factor and that a constant number of H nodes makes the problem polynomial-time solvable.

**Interlocked 3D chains.** Chains are separable if they can move apart indefinitely. Results: hairpins (2-chains) never interlock each other (de Bruijn 1954, generalized by Dawson 1984, using star-shaped scaling arguments); two 3-chains separate via non-uniform scaling that preserves the middle bars' lengths; a 4-chain with a 2-chain separates by scaling perpendicular to the shared plane. Three 3-chains interlock, as do a 3-chain with a 4-chain (the smallest pairwise case), an 11-chain with a 2-chain (conjectured optimal), and closed chains — a triangle with an open 4-chain, and a quadrilateral with an open 3-chain — proved topologically. Lubiw's problem asks how many cuts are needed to unlock a 3D chain of n bars; the bounds are between (n−1)/4 and (n−3)/2, i.e., Θ(n), and it remains open whether a clever cutting scheme achieves the lower bound. Finally, interlocked chains have been used to build rigid frameworks inside PSPACE-completeness proofs of motion planning for 3D chains and 2D locked trees; whether a straight chain can be unfolded remains open.

E-minis are electronically traded futures contracts worth a fraction of standard futures contracts. The CME introduced them in 1997, beginning with the S&P 500, to give individual investors access to markets with lower capital requirements. They are traded mainly through Globex across stock indexes, commodities, currencies, and individual stocks, with the S&P 500 e-mini remaining the most active. They can be used to speculate or hedge and generally provide high liquidity, extensive trading hours, and leverage, although leverage can magnify losses.

Traders open an account with a futures broker and buy or sell contracts to establish or close positions. Profits and losses depend on the difference between trading prices. Required capital depends on contract value, exchange margin, and broker rules. For example, the S&P 500 e-mini has a value of $50 times the index, making one contract worth $200,000 at 4,000 points. The article cites a $10,000 CME margin requirement and suggests budgeting roughly $13,000–$15,000. It separately gives a general margin range of $400–$900 and recommends holding more than the minimum to cover losses. Trading costs generally range from $0.50 to $2.50 per contract, plus exchange, broker, and clearing fees.

A backtested @ES strategy used a 9:30 a.m.–4:00 p.m. session, entering and exiting at the close. It produced 163 trades from 2000 through 2021, an average gain of 0.89%, a 79% win rate, and a profit factor of 2. In 2022, its 13 trades averaged 0.18%, compared with the S&P 500’s 15% decline. The article describes these results as decent but not spectacular.

Strategies should be tested and adapted to the asset being traded. The article discourages scalping because of strong competition, commissions, and slippage. It emphasizes written plans, disciplined recordkeeping, and backtesting because most traders fail. Learning resources include books, online courses, videos, and broker tutorials. There is no legal daily limit on e-mini day trades, but brokers may impose pattern-day-trader restrictions, higher margins, minimum balances, or closer monitoring. Open positions must be settled or offset when contracts expire.

WIRED compiled editor-selected Amazon Big Deal Days discounts for Prime members, running October 7–8, on tested products priced under $100. The list covers streaming devices, earbuds, speakers, routers, wireless chargers, gaming gear, smart-home and security products, cameras, pet-care devices, fitness trackers, workout headphones, kitchen appliances, cleaning products, bedding, white-noise machines, personal-care devices, and children’s toys. Each listing includes a sale price and discount. WIRED notes that editors independently select the products but may receive compensation from retailers or purchases.

The passage presents a bibliometric analysis of literature on preparing leaders for digital transformation in education, particularly in Thailand’s Digital Thailand 4.0 and Education 4.0 contexts. Eligible studies were open-access, full conference papers published since 2019 during the COVID-19 pandemic and related to digital disruption, digital literacy, Education 4.0, or digital education leadership.

The analysis identifies five competencies for digital transformation leaders:

- **Digital Literacy/Competency:** Accessing and using technologies, cybersecurity, digital media, office applications, and online collaboration as foundations for transformation.
- **Digital Readiness:** Developing a shared vision, strategy, mindset, skills, infrastructure, and digital systems so people and organizations can adapt to technology-driven change.
- **Digital Culture:** Building an organizational culture that embraces technology, collaboration, hybrid learning, digital data, automated analysis, data security, and decentralized use of information.
- **Digital Mindset:** Using design thinking, accepting inevitable change, encouraging innovation, and moving beyond traditional educational practices.
- **Digital Leadership:** Communicating effectively, rethinking and reinventing roles, adapting to technological change, developing others, forming collaborative digital teams, and preparing educators through knowledge, skills, and abilities.

The analysis emphasizes that digital disruption and COVID-19 accelerated shifts toward online, remote, project-based, and hybrid education, making traditional approaches insufficient. It concludes that successful transformation requires leadership vision, continuous learning, cooperation, and customization rather than a one-size-fits-all approach. Technology cannot replace teachers; educators must adapt and shape digital change to benefit students, educational institutions, and society.

The study uses documentary and field research, including literature, historical records, interviews, observations, and audio-visual materials, to examine Songyang Academy’s history, educational philosophy, and relationship to general education. Songyang Academy originated as a Buddhist temple in 484, evolved into a site for Confucian lectures, and was established as Taiyi School in 955. It flourished during the Northern Song through imperial support, donations, lectures by prominent Neo-Confucian scholars, and an emphasis on self-study and examinations. It later declined during periods of political unrest, briefly revived, and collapsed in the late Qing after the abolition of the imperial examination system.

General education is presented as promoting comprehensive development of morality, intellect, physical fitness, and literacy rather than narrow professional or vocational skills. Drawing on Aristotelian liberal education and Chinese Confucian traditions, Songyang Academy’s philosophy emphasizes moral education, personality cultivation, accessible learning, the unity of knowledge and action, and practical application. Its student-centered teaching emphasizes independent reading, inquiry, questioning, discussion, and debate, with teachers acting as guides. Its management structure combined academic leadership with administrative duties and allowed students to participate in management.

The article concludes that Songyang Academy is an important part of Confucian education, pedagogy, traditional Chinese culture, and world cultural heritage. Its educational principles offer valuable experience for modern general education, while the academy’s educational culture should be preserved and adapted through improved methods, international perspectives, practical applications, interdisciplinary integration, and personalized education to cultivate well-rounded modern talent.

The passage combines support, trademark, ESD, revision-history, and mechanical, packaging, and orderable information for the MSPM0G3519, MSPM0G3518, MSPM0G1519, and MSPM0G1518. TI E2E forums provide verified answers and design help, although linked contributions are provided “AS IS” and may not reflect TI’s views. TI warns that ESD can range from performance degradation to complete device failure and recommends appropriate handling precautions.

The April 2025 revision added a PSA-L1 certification target, corrected low-power timer, UART, SPI, ADC, SRAM, and operating-mode details, added preview package variants, expanded DMA and security information, and revised specifications for power, thermal conditions, POR/BOR, flash endurance, timing, oscillators, digital I/O, ADC, temperature sensing, VREF, comparators, SPI, UART, LFSS, and timers.

Mechanical drawings use millimeters and are subject to change. Package thermal pads must be soldered to the PCB for thermal and mechanical performance; optional via and stencil-design guidance is also provided. Orderable notes describe product status, preproduction terms, RoHS values, lead or ball materials, moisture-sensitivity and reflow ratings, and part markings. Automotive versions MSPM0G3518-Q1 and MSPM0G3519-Q1 are identified as Q100-qualified for high-reliability automotive applications.

TI provides technical and design resources without warranties and states that developers are responsible for product selection, design, validation, testing, and compliance with applicable requirements.

Kobe University researchers found that four model orchid species germinated only near decaying logs, with seedlings almost exclusively associating with wood-decaying fungi. Because orchid seeds are dust-sized and lack nutrients needed for growth, these fungi supply carbon needed for establishment. The fungal partners closely matched those in adults of the same species with coral-shaped rhizomes. Species lacking these rhizomes may switch fungal partners as their nutritional needs change and carbon from rotting wood declines.

The findings reveal a pathway by which carbon moves from forest deadwood to green plants and may help explain the evolution of fully mycoheterotrophic orchids, which obtain nutrients from fungi throughout life and do not photosynthesize. They also indicate that conserving wild orchids requires protecting deadwood and its fungi, especially in warm, humid habitats where woody debris is a major carbon source.

The study examined elementary teachers’ attitudes toward inclusive education for learners with special education needs (LSENs) in Liloan District, Cebu, Philippines. It aimed to identify factors affecting those attitudes and translate the findings into an evidence-based Teacher Inclusion Support Plan. Guided by the Theory of Planned Behavior, Bronfenbrenner’s Ecological Systems Theory, Bandura’s Social Learning Theory, and Philippine inclusive-education laws and policies, the research used an Input-Process-Output model.

A descriptive-correlational design was applied to 30 purposively selected inclusion teachers from four public schools. Data were collected through a demographic questionnaire and a Modified STATIC survey measuring perceived advantages and disadvantages, professional issues, philosophical issues, and logistical concerns. Descriptive statistics, Pearson correlation, and ANOVA were used to examine teacher characteristics and their relationships with attitudes.

Most respondents were women (93.33%), married (83.33%), aged 34–43 (53.33%), and had completed master’s-level units (76.67%). While 26.67% had more than 16 years of overall teaching experience, 90% had only one to five years of experience teaching LSENs, and 80% had attended only one or two inclusive-education trainings. Half of the teachers handled zero or one learner with special needs, while 30% handled more than three. Reported learner needs included learning disabilities, intellectual and developmental disabilities, visual impairment, physical or health impairments, and deafness or hard of hearing.

Teachers’ overall attitudes were positive, with an overall mean of 3.71. Mean scores were 3.50 for advantages and disadvantages, 4.08 for professional issues, 4.03 for philosophical issues, and 3.23 for logistical concerns. Teachers recognized inclusion’s social and philosophical benefits and supported equal access, differentiated instruction, high expectations, specialist assistance, co-teaching, and ongoing professional development. However, they expressed uncertainty about academic outcomes and concerns about large classes, preparation time, behavior management, schedules, instructional materials, specialist access, assistive technology, and adequate budgets. Burnout was reported as low.

No statistically significant relationships were found between teacher demographics and attitudes toward inclusion at p<.05. The authors concluded that teachers shared generally positive philosophical foundations regardless of age, marital status, educational attainment, experience, or learner profiles. They recommended sustained and practical professional development, classroom experience, mentoring, smaller classes, additional qualified personnel, learning materials, assistive technologies, specialist and parental collaboration, schoolwide planning, and continuous monitoring to translate positive attitudes into sustainable inclusive practices and reduce burnout.

Classes resumed at Marjory Stoneman Douglas High School two weeks after 17 students and teachers were killed, with about 50 officers, a security cordon, grief counselors, therapy animals and numerous media vehicles present. Backpacks were prohibited, the freshman building remained cordoned off, and classes began with fourth period so students could reunite with those present during the shooting. Returning students described feelings of nervousness and emotional trauma, while school support and their gun-control activism offered encouragement.

Victims’ relatives testified before Florida lawmakers as the House Appropriations Committee advanced a bill raising the long-gun purchase age from 18 to 21 and allowing trained, deputized teachers to carry concealed weapons. Superintendent Robert Runcie and student activist David Hogg opposed arming teachers, while Gov. Rick Scott declined to say whether he would veto the broader package. An NRA lobbyist supported tighter school security but opposed gun-ownership restrictions. The Senate also advanced its version of the school-safety bill.

Meanwhile, Dick’s Sporting Goods announced it would stop selling assault-style rifles and would not sell guns to anyone under 21. Students were also preparing for a national school walkout against gun violence.

The speaker valued the honor despite missing rookie nomination. He declined the Flyers’ offer, stayed in Europe another year to prepare, and trained hard. Motivated by veterans’ work ethic, he recovered from a poor five-game start as his confidence rose.

The MSPM0G3519, MSPM0G3518, MSPM0G1519, and MSPM0G1518 MCUs include zero-wait-state SRAM, extensive GPIO and pin-muxing capabilities, dual 12-bit ADCs, and multiple analog, security, communications, timing, and debugging peripherals.

- **Memory and storage:** Up to 128 KB of SRAM is divided into two 64 KB banks. Bank 0 provides ECC or parity protection and remains available in run, sleep, stop, and standby modes. Bank 1 lacks ECC/parity, can be disabled or powered down in stop mode, and loses contents in shutdown. Configurable SRAM boundaries partition memory into two read-write sections and a central read-execute section, supporting code protection, zero-wait-state execution, and prevention of self-modifying code.
- **GPIO and IOMUX:** Up to 93 GPIO pins are supported across Ports A, B, and C. Features include multi-bit set, clear, and toggle operations, wake-up functions, and FastWake from stop and standby. IOMUX provides configurable drive strength, speed, pullup/down, digital peripheral routing, and user pin configuration through PINCM.
- **Analog peripherals:** ADC0 and ADC1 support simultaneous, single-ended sampling, 12-bit resolution at 4 Msps with greater than 11 ENOB, hardware averaging for 14-bit effective resolution at 250 ksps, result registers, internal temperature and supply channels, and selectable 1.4 V or 2.5 V references. The temperature sensor produces a temperature-proportional voltage and includes a factory single-point calibration value. VREF supports internal or external references. The comparator compares two input voltages, supports multiple blanking sources and low-power wake-up, and connects to timer fault handling. The 12-bit DAC supports 8- or 12-bit buffered output, self-calibration, multiple data formats, FIFO/DMA operation, and event-fabric triggering. Enabling DAC_OUT occupies PA15.
- **Security:** Features include an AES-128/256 accelerator, flexible code and data firewalls, secure storage for up to four AES keys, CRC-16 and CRC-32, a 32-bit true random number generator, the AESADV block-cipher accelerator, and a keystore designed to protect keys against leakage and partial modification attacks.
- **Communications and processing:** UART peripherals support configurable framing, parity, baud rates, LIN mode, DMA, and loopback. I2C supports 7- and 10-bit addressing, controller and target operation, clock stretching, Standard, Fast, and Fast-mode Plus rates, SMBus 3.0, DMA, glitch filtering, and address-match wake-up. SPI supports controller and peripheral modes, programmable frame sizes, DMA FIFOs, multiple frame formats, and up to 32 Mbit/s on HSIO signals. CAN-FD supports CAN 2.0 and CAN-FD communication up to 5 Mbit/s with extensive transmit and receive buffering. MATHACL offloads selected 32-bit mathematical operations.
- **Low-frequency and timer peripherals:** LFSS_B uses a typical 32 kHz low-frequency clock and includes RTC_B and an independent watchdog. RTC_B provides calendar counters, configurable alarms, periodic wake-ups, calibration and temperature-drift compensation, and clock output. IWDT_B uses an independent 32 kHz source and generates a power-on reset if not serviced; WWDT can reset or interrupt the device and supports sleep-mode stopping and interval-timer operation. TIMG general-purpose timers and TIMA advanced timers provide programmable counting, prescaling, capture/compare, synchronization, interrupts, DMA triggers, and peripheral triggering. TIMA also includes complementary PWM, programmable dead time, and configurable fault handling.
- **Debug and programming:** A two-wire ARM-compatible serial wire debug interface provides debug access. The boot strap loader supports programming and configuration through UART or I2C, is protected by a 256-bit user-defined password, can be disabled, and may be invoked through hardware, an unprogrammed reset vector and stack pointer, or a runtime command.
- **Device information and application guidance:** Factory constants provide read-only capability, identification, revision, and trim information. Typical layouts use specified VDD/VSS decoupling, an NRST pullup and pulldown network, an optional SYSOSC frequency-correction resistor, a required VCORE capacitor, and pullups for 5 V-tolerant open-drain I/O.
- **Support and documentation:** TI provides LaunchPad and BoosterPack resources, SDKs, SysConfig, TI Resource Explorer, CCS, IAR, Keil MDK, Arm-Clang, and GNU Arm Embedded Toolchain support. Device nomenclature distinguishes experimental X-prefixed parts from fully qualified MSP production parts. The document also provides revision history, mechanical and packaging data, orderable information, notes, and package-specific soldering and thermal-pad guidance.

The author calls his 21-year-old college senior daughter “The Girl” (TG) to protect her privacy. Her abilities suggest she could become a literature professor, but the author rejects recommending academia because full-time faculty positions are exceptionally scarce and the field faces untenable costs, a demographic cliff, generative AI, and political hostility. Journalism, publishing, and midlist careers have also weakened, while online publications have suffered layoffs. TG is interested in librarianship, which the author encourages because information-science skills are increasingly flexible and libraries may fare better. The author asks readers for advice for talented young people suited to professorships and says they are rooting for TG.

A hypothetical analysis estimated that a 40% smaller NIH budget could have reduced medical innovation by leaving more than half of drugs approved in the 21st century without crucial funding. Researchers examined at-risk grants from 1980–2007 and FDA approvals of drugs with new active ingredients from 2000–2023. Of 557 approvals, 40 had patents directly acknowledging NIH funding, including 14 citing at-risk grants; 59% cited NIH-supported research, and 65 had patents with more than 25% of references to NIH-funded work. Drugs linked to at-risk research more often received FDA priority review (60% versus 41%) and had higher average market value. Researchers said alternate outcomes cannot be certain and called their estimate conservative because it captured only direct paths from grants to drugs.

The Bronx County Supreme Court affirmed dismissal of Brian O’Loughlin’s defamation complaint against Patrolmen’s Benevolent Association president Phil Caruso. Caruso had called O’Loughlin and eight other officers who sought refunds of a $20 memorial contribution people with “no feelings” and a “disgrace” to the police service. The court held that these vague, subjective statements constituted nonactionable opinion, not provably false facts, and were not actionable as mixed opinion because they merely criticized the officers’ refusal to support the contribution.

Vertical farming grows crops in controlled environments without soil, with plants stacked in layers using methods such as hydroponics and aeroponics. Market growth is driven by demand for quality food, population growth, reduced reliance on water and soil, new technologies, and limited pesticide and fertilizer use. High initial costs, artificial lighting energy consumption, and production of high-value crops hinder growth. North America holds the largest market share, while Asia-Pacific is expected to grow rapidly during 2016–2022. The global market is projected to reach approximately USD 6 billion by 2022 at a 21% CAGR, with major players including AeroFarms, Hort Americas, Philips, Everlight, Sky Greens, and Agrilution.

Growing population and food consumption are increasing cereal production and demand for crop-protection products, especially herbicides. The market is segmented into insecticides, herbicides, and fungicides, with herbicides expected to remain dominant due to low costs, R&D investment, and new active ingredients. North America leads geographically, followed by Asia Pacific and Europe, while Asia Pacific is forecast for rapid near-term expansion. Crop rotation supports soil fertility, reduces erosion and pest attacks, and improves yields, but crop-protection chemicals can harm the environment and human health and reduce soil productivity through overuse.

It describes how UPS systems automatically support data center infrastructure during outages and protect it from power sags and surges, and explains the roles of rectifiers, inverters, batteries, and flywheels. The state’s Board of Regents unanimously approved an emergency policy allowing special-education students who struggle with state exams to earn local high-school diplomas through occupational coursework or work-readiness assessments, without meeting minimum Regents English and math scores. The route applies to students graduating as early as January and requires district superintendent approval of academic proficiency, with limited flexibility for students nearing graduation in 2017–18 or 2018–19. Turkey has secured a €974 million loan from a consortium of international lenders, backed by European development institutions and multilateral lenders, to finance a major highway in central Anatolia. The Florida First District Court of Appeal affirmed AHCA’s dismissal of Glenwood Nursing Center’s request for an administrative hearing as untimely. Glenwood missed the June 14, 2010 deadline, filed on June 15, and argued that AHCA counsel’s post-deadline assurance that a late filing would be accepted equitably tolled the deadline. The court found no equitable tolling because Glenwood knew the deadline, received no extension before it expired, and ignored clear written filing instructions.

The court also rejected Glenwood’s argument that its June 15 request related back to an April 16 letter sent to CMS. That letter sought a CMS hearing, merely referenced disputed state deficiencies, was not identified as an AHCA hearing request, and was not filed with the AHCA agency clerk as required by Florida law. The court therefore upheld the final order dismissing the hearing request with prejudice, which also revoked Glenwood’s nursing home license and imposed a $25,000 administrative fine.

The article presents 10 backtested swing-trading strategies: Monday reversal in the S&P 500, overnight S&P 500 trading, buying new S&P 500 intraday highs, Monday/Tuesday Nasdaq trading, SPY/TLT rotation, SPY/GLD/TLT rotation, XLP mean reversion, the MACD histogram in the S&P 500, turn-of-the-month trading in the S&P 500 and Nasdaq, and trend-following with the 200-day and 12-month moving averages. Strategies were tested in AmiBroker and date back to 2012; code is primarily available to subscribers, with some strategies offered in plain English.

Swing trading involves holding positions for several days to months, generally shorter than position trading but longer than day trading. The article contrasts it with buy-and-hold, which returned about 10% annualized over the last 100 years, and recommends mutual funds and ETFs as a savings cornerstone. Systematic, backtested swing trading may complement buy-and-hold and provide risk-adjusted returns, but it requires discipline, mechanical execution, and careful risk management.

The 200-day moving average is presented as an effective defense against major drawdowns, although it can cause whipsaw losses. The turn-of-the-month strategy spent about 33% of its time invested and, for QQQ, produced a 51% drawdown versus the index’s 83% and a 7.2% annualized return since inception.

The article states that realistic swing-trading returns are generally 5%–20%, with performance judged alongside drawdowns. It warns that most swing traders are unsuccessful and attributes successful trading to quantified strategies that are backtested and tested out of sample. It advises starting small, risking only manageable money, independently verifying strategies, and avoiding unrealistic expectations of sustained triple-digit returns.

This continuation application discloses wood-type golf club heads, particularly drivers, fairway woods, and utility or hybrid clubs. Embodiments include a body with one or more raised sole portions having greater curvature than a conventional sole, which can reduce sole mass and area, increase rigidity, improve acoustics, and potentially eliminate or reduce the need for reinforcing ribs. The soles may be bi-level, extend across most of the sole, or include separate toe-side and heel-side raised portions with a weight track between them. Sloped transitions, stiffening features, thick and thin regions, and internal ribs may further control rigidity and acoustic properties.

Cantilevered peripheral ledges extend below the raised sole portions, while front and rear sit pads or other ground-contact surfaces support the head. Optional crown and sole inserts cover body openings and may use lighter composite, polymeric, graphite, or carbon-fiber materials to reduce mass and free discretionary weight for ribs, weighting, or center-of-gravity adjustment. Seats and ledges secure and align the inserts.

Some embodiments include front and rear weight tracks with sliding, interchangeable weight assemblies for adjusting center of gravity and moment of inertia, influencing club distance, ball flight, spin, draw, and fade characteristics. Adjustable head-shaft connections are also described. A front channel can improve coefficient of restitution across the striking face and forgiveness on off-center strikes.

The passage discusses curvature comparisons, dimensional ranges for volumes, masses, tracks, and inserts, and performance measures including CG location, projected CG, Delta 1, Delta 2, moments of inertia, Zup, and a forgiveness ratio. Metallic faces are used for acoustic response, consistency in wet conditions, and easier removal of ball markings. Manufacturing options include metal frames formed by casting or stamping and composite or polymer inserts made with compatible thermosetting or thermoplastic materials. Stated benefits include greater distance, accuracy, ball-flight control, off-center-strike forgiveness, improved acoustics, durability, and customizability.

- **Hiccup operation:** When CS_ILIM exceeds 1.05 V, the controller performs cycle-by-cycle current limiting. CHICC is charged by an 80 µA pulsed current during each overcurrent cycle. At 0.6 V, switching stops and SS is discharged; HICC is pulled to 1 V, then discharged by a 1 µA restart current until 0.3 V, after which soft start resumes if the overcurrent has cleared. CHICC determines both the limiting-delay and restart intervals, with 3.3 nF recommended; calculated timing is approximate.

- **External fault protection:** A FAULT-pin voltage above the typical 0.6 V threshold for the specified 0.4–1.4 µs minimum pulse width triggers shutdown and discharges SS. Switching remains stopped until FAULT falls below the typical 0.5 V falling threshold. After a delay of approximately 15 switching cycles plus internal logic delay, soft start resumes; a fault during the delay restarts the sequence.

- **Slope and frequency compensation:** Slope compensation uses a voltage ramp to mitigate subharmonic oscillation above 50% duty cycle. Minimum compensation is 0.5 times the inductor’s falling-current slope, while the recommended value is one times that slope. A resistor from RSC to AVSS sets the compensation. Either Type 2A or Type 2B frequency compensation is supported; Type 2A adds CHF in parallel with RCOMP and CCOMP for high-frequency noise attenuation. Component selection begins with crossover frequency, RCOMP, CCOMP, and optionally the output-capacitor ESR zero and CHF.

- **Protection and control mode:** Thermal shutdown stops switching above a typical junction temperature of 175°C and restarts the power-up sequence below 160°C. The controllers use fixed-frequency, peak-current-mode control: an internal oscillator starts the primary output, an external current-sense resistor senses switch current, and the power switch turns off when sensed current reaches the stepped-down COMP voltage.

- **Application information:** The TPS7H500x-SP family is intended for radiation-hardness-assured space-grade DC-DC converters using external gate drivers. It supports switching frequencies up to 2 MHz and topologies including buck, flyback, forward, active-clamp forward, push-pull, and full-bridge. A TPS7H5001-SP example uses a 500 kHz, 5 V synchronous push-pull converter with GaN FETs.

- **Example design values:** Selected values include a 205 kΩ frequency-setting resistor, 10 kΩ/1.4 kΩ feedback divider, 25 ns dead time with 20.5 kΩ resistors, 49.9 kΩ leading-edge blanking resistor, 33 nF soft-start capacitor giving approximately 7.5 ms start-up, a 2.5 transformer turns ratio, and 40 µH actual primary inductance. The example selects 170 V primary GaN FETs, an 80 V synchronous rectifier, a 0.47 µH output inductor, and seven 330 µF output capacitors totaling 2.3 mF. A 1:100 current-sense transformer and 7.5 Ω sense resistor provide current limiting near 35 A. Other selections include a 3.3 nF hiccup capacitor, Type 2A compensation with a 10 kHz crossover, RCOMP of 40.2 kΩ, CCOMP of 15 nF, CHF of 47 pF, and a 102 kΩ RSC resistor.

- **Power and layout recommendations:** Controller supply voltage is 4–14 V, with at least a 0.1 µF VIN-to-AVSS bypass capacitor; X5R or better ceramic capacitors should be placed close to the controller. Layout should isolate feedback and control signals from switching nodes, minimize high-dv/dt and high-di/dt loops, separate analog and power grounds except at one connection, use short and wide high-current traces, place filtering and compensation parts near their associated pins, and minimize switch-node copper. HICC capacitance of at least 3.3 nF is recommended for SYNC-noise reduction, and CFP packages should connect backside metallization to AVSS through multiple vias.

- **Documentation:** The document also lists related evaluation-module and radiation reports, update-notification and support resources, ESD handling cautions, package and orderable information, and revision history. Revision F added QMLP options for TPS7H5002-SP, TPS7H5003-SP, and TPS7H5004-SP and the SN0022HFT mechanical no-die package.

This withdrawn, non-peer-reviewed preprint evaluates six machine-learning models for pancreatic cancer diagnosis using synthetic data containing demographic, clinical, and symptom variables. After an 80/20 train-test split, the study handled missing values, scaled numerical features, encoded categorical variables, and did not resample the imbalanced dataset.

Logistic Regression, Random Forest, Support Vector Machine, Neural Network, Decision Tree, and SuperLearner produced similar accuracy (76.05%–76.35%) but very low sensitivity. Random Forest and Decision Tree detected no true positives. SVM had the highest sensitivity at 1.90%, while Logistic Regression and Neural Network each achieved 1.47% sensitivity and 58.33% precision. SuperLearner had the highest precision (66.67%) but only 0.42% sensitivity. Overall, the results indicate that class imbalance caused models to favor negative cases, making their accuracy misleading and their positive-case detection inadequate for clinical use.

The study recommends resampling, cost-sensitive learning, threshold tuning, feature engineering, explainable-AI tools such as SHAP and LIME, integration of imaging and genomic data, and validation on real clinical datasets. It also recommends collaboration between data scientists and clinicians and identifies interpretability as essential for clinical adoption.

Faith-based organisations are increasingly supporting the strained NHS, according to the Cinnamon Network. Its report found more than 3,500 churches and 200,000 volunteers involved in health and social care initiatives addressing issues such as mental health, obesity and social isolation. A 2016 estimate valued church and faith groups’ annual community work at £3bn.

Parish nursing is a key example. Churches recruit registered nurses, either paid or voluntary, to provide patient support, preventative care and monitoring. More than 100 parish nurses currently work with 85 UK churches, with another 100 planned within 18 months. GPs said parish nurses complement NHS staff by offering patients more time, personal support and advocacy while allowing doctors and nurses to focus on clinical duties. The initiative, piloted in the UK in 2005, has expanded as the NHS faces growing demands and reduced capacity. An IDC white paper examines how industrial simulation, modeling, data analysis, and high-performance computing (HPC) can support manufacturing innovation and digital transformation. It is based on a December 2021 survey of 200 IT or departmental decision makers at discrete and process manufacturing enterprises with more than 500 employees in Germany, Austria, and Switzerland.

Manufacturers face geopolitical uncertainty, rising energy and raw-material costs, supply-chain disruptions, labor shortages, and sustainability pressures. Simulation and modeling are already established in CAD, CAM, and CAE workflows and are viewed as important for innovation, faster product development, reduced costs, better decisions, improved quality, and defect avoidance. About half of respondents use these technologies in product development, production and process planning, or quality management; deployment is expected to rise substantially, with nearly two-thirds planning relevant investment.

The paper identifies data silos caused by inconsistent departmental data and limited data strategies as a major obstacle. It emphasizes integrated data sources and a unified “single source of truth,” along with end-to-end processes and collaboration with external partners, to improve efficiency and enable new products, services, and business models.

IT advances are expanding use cases through virtual prototyping, design optimization, digital verification, IoT and sensor feedback, digital twins, and high-performance analytics. Digital twins can monitor physical assets, test hypothetical scenarios, support ecosystem services, and enable product- and outcome-based offerings. Engineering workstations delivered as a service, shared data pools, AR/VR, and integrated IT solutions further broaden these applications.

Complex calculations create trade-offs between speed and accuracy, especially where infrastructure is outdated; 42% of respondents described their simulations as outdated or inaccurate, and half said calculations take too long. Four out of five decision makers nevertheless view HPC as a game changer for product and process innovation. By enabling parallel, complex calculations and more iterations, HPC can accelerate development, expand analytical use, and support new digital offerings. More than one-quarter of surveyed enterprises already use professional HPC infrastructure, while another 39% are planning or piloting it; only 15% are not currently engaging with HPC, citing investment costs, limited awareness, and the topic’s relative newness. IDC anticipates HPC-based simulation, modeling, and analysis will become routine in many enterprises.

The Lisbon Clippers defeated the Columbiana Devils 49-47 on the Devils' home court, scoring twice in the final 23 seconds. The BCCI had rejected a similar proposal at the 2018 ICC conclave in Auckland, where India was awarded the 2021 Champions Trophy and 2023 World Cup. Chaudhry criticized the ICC’s approach toward India’s interests and said the Champions Trophy was intended to sustain 50-over cricket. Suspected jihadists killed at least 18 people and wounded several during an overnight raid on a restaurant in Ouagadougou, Burkina Faso. Security forces killed both attackers and freed trapped people, while officials called the toll provisional. Earlier attacks occurred in Burkina Faso and Mali, and a new regional force was not yet operational and faced a budget shortfall.

Forecasters said several tornadic supercells were increasingly likely, especially in northern Alabama; parts of Tennessee, Mississippi and Georgia were also under threat. The paper proposes iMOOE, a physics-guided framework for zero-shot out-of-distribution forecasting of two-dimensional PDE dynamics without test-time adaptation. It addresses shifts in initial conditions, physical parameters, forcing terms, and temporal resolution.

The method is based on two invariance principles: operator invariance, in which elementary physical operators remain stable across domains, and compositionality invariance, which fixes how operators, parameters, and forcing terms combine. iMOOE uses parallel neural-operator experts with derivative masks to learn distinct operators, followed by a fusion network that models their composition. Training combines maximal prediction loss, cross-environment risk-equality loss, frequency-enrichment regularization for high-frequency information, and a mask-diversity loss.

Experiments on diffusion-reaction, Navier–Stokes, Burgers, shallow-water, and heat-conduction systems show state-of-the-art zero-shot results, with reported average gains of 40.21% in nMSE and 30.78% in fRMSE over prior methods. It also improves temporal extrapolation and can be integrated with FNO, DeepONet, VCNeF, and OFormer. On real sea-surface-temperature data, iMOOE achieves the lowest mean and variance among compared methods. The authors note that validation covers limited dynamical diversity and identify irregular-grid PDEs and earth-system forecasting as future applications.

Indian markets opened higher but erased most weekly gains by Friday amid concerns over U.S. tariffs, trade wars, rising global interest rates, political uncertainty, and the RBI ending letters of credit and letters of guarantee as trade-credit instruments. The Nifty fell 0.3%, while mid- and small-cap indexes gained about 1.5%; the rupee strengthened to 64.93 per dollar, and crude oil was nearly flat as supply growth outpaced demand. February wholesale inflation slowed to a seven-month low, industrial production grew 7.5% in January, and retail inflation eased to 4.44%, reducing immediate rate-hike concerns, though March wholesale inflation is expected to rise. Sentiment was also hurt by TDP leaving the BJP-led alliance, the finance ministry-RBI dispute, bank fraud, and developments involving TCS, Ambuja Cements, ACC, IndiGo, and Punjab National Bank. Bharat Dynamics, Bandhan Bank, and Hindustan Aeronautics launched major IPOs, with Bharat Dynamics receiving a lukewarm response. Markets now await the Fed and Bank of England decisions and G20 meetings, with investors increasingly selling on rallies.

The lecture examines interacting quantum gases, emphasizing how interactions produce superfluidity and how complex Hamiltonians can be reduced to solvable forms. For a homogeneous Bose-Einstein condensate, the Bogoliubov approximation replaces the condensate operator with a large occupation number and diagonalizes the resulting bilinear Hamiltonian. This yields quasiparticles whose dispersion becomes linear at low momentum and free-particle-like at high momentum. The dimensionless gas parameter \(Na^3\) controls interaction strength, condensate depletion, and corrections to the ground-state energy. Interactions give the condensate a small finite-momentum component: cold atomic condensates are typically about 99% condensate, whereas liquid helium has only about 10% condensate and 90% quantum depletion.

Experiments can probe these excitations through density waves and light scattering. A blue-detuned laser creates a density wave in a condensate, whose propagation speed gives the speed of sound. Stimulated two-laser scattering, or BEC spectroscopy, maps the quasiparticle dispersion and dynamic structure factor, revealing linear low-momentum and quadratic high-momentum behavior.

For trapped, inhomogeneous condensates, the position-space Bogoliubov approximation leads to the nonlinear Gross–Pitaevskii equation. Its mean-field repulsion favors nearly uniform density, while kinetic energy determines boundary behavior over the healing length. Neglecting kinetic energy gives the Thomas–Fermi approximation, in which an inverted trapping potential is filled according to particle number. The Gross–Pitaevskii equation quantitatively describes condensate expansion, aspect-ratio inversion, and trap density profiles.

The lecture also covers vortices. Angular momentum in a condensate is accommodated through phase singularities and density zeros rather than rigid rotation. Multiply charged vortices are unstable and split into singly charged vortices; their mutual repulsion favors a hexagonal arrangement. Macroscopic wave-function excitations are distinguished from single-quasiparticle fluctuations, which arise from Bogoliubov theory.

Finally, optical lattices are introduced as a route to strongly correlated matter. Deep lattices produce band structure and, in the tight-binding limit, localized Wannier states, tunneling energy \(j\), and on-site interaction \(U\). The resulting Bose–Hubbard model has a Mott-insulating limit when \(U \gg j\) and a superfluid limit when \(j \gg U\). Because the Bogoliubov approximation fails near the transition, a mean-field decoupling of fluctuations is used to derive an effective local Hamiltonian and the superfluid–Mott phase diagram, including insulating lobes with different fixed site occupations. The transition is observable through the emergence or loss of diffraction coherence in time-of-flight images and through site-resolved atom counts in quantum-gas microscopy.

Crude sulfate turpentine, also called sulfate wood turpentine, is a flammable, water-insoluble byproduct of the Kraft process. It contains terpene hydrocarbons, chiefly alpha- and beta-pinene, plus smaller amounts of limonene, camphene, carene, and terpinene. It is used in fragrances, flavors, cosmetics, food and beverages, paint and varnish solvents, and organic synthesis. Market growth may be constrained by distillation costs and limited black liquor availability.

This protocol describes the implementation and evaluation of Abridge Ambient AI, a generative AI documentation assistant embedded in Epic at UW Health, using a Learning Health System (LHS) framework. The Pragmatic Trial Operations playbook combines shared governance, user experience, technical integration, documentation sustainment, and outcomes analytics to align research with clinical operations. Governance included executive sponsors and multidisciplinary implementation teams, while iterative Plan-Do-Study-Act cycles, EPIS, SEIPS, and PETT Scan frameworks addressed workflows, human factors, training, privacy, and compliance.

The alpha phase, conducted from June 24 to October 10, 2024, evaluated 20 providers across five specialties and 8,527 encounters at 12 locations. Interviews identified organizational context, provider and patient readiness, documentation preferences, and clinical-task fit as major influences on adoption. Rapid iterative testing refined training, technical support, consent procedures, note templates, and workflows. The weighted median provider-averaged utilization was 65.4%, with a 48% lower control limit. A documentation-template change reduced the proportion of provider-entered ICD-10 diagnoses supported by notes from 79% to 35%, after which accuracy returned to baseline levels following template revision. Difference-in-differences analysis found utilization decreased by an average 6.84 percentage points while work outside work increased by 0.33 hours and time spent in notes increased by 0.43 hours. An LLM-based coding review tool achieved a mean Jaccard score of 0.54 against certified coder review and was adopted as a screening tool.

The beta phase began as a 24-week multisite, closed-cohort, stepped-wedge pragmatic randomized clinical trial. Sixty-six providers across eight specialties in Wisconsin and Illinois were randomized 1:1:1 into three waves, with transitions from usual care to Ambient AI at six-week intervals. The trial uses provider well-being measured through the Professional Fulfillment Index, along with utilization, consent compliance, documentation efficiency, and drift-monitoring measures. Operational oversight included a real-time dashboard, biweekly governance review, rolling two-week difference-in-differences monitoring, and an LLM-assisted ICD-10 review process. Recruitment was completed and the trial began on schedule, with the dashboard transferred to operational ownership.
The team should focus on winning each shift and period, executing well, and seizing its rare opportunity to win the Cup.

The Utah Court of Appeals affirmed summary judgment for The Kroger Company and Dr. Gregory P. Tayler in Kari Baumann’s healthcare malpractice action. Baumann alleged that Tayler prescribed medication outside the applicable standard of care and that Kroger breached standards of care, violated the Utah Pharmacy Practice Act, and failed to meet assumed duties and written assurances.

Baumann failed to disclose expert witnesses and reports by the deadlines in the stipulated discovery schedule. Defendants argued that without expert testimony, Baumann could not establish the standards of care, breach, or causation. Baumann submitted a report concerning Kroger on the hearing date, after the court had barred consideration of filings made after October 8, and submitted no report concerning Tayler.

The district court found no good cause for the late disclosures, precluded Baumann from using undisclosed materials under Utah Rule of Civil Procedure 26(d)(4), and granted summary judgment because expert testimony was necessary to establish her claims.

On appeal, the court declined to review Baumann’s unpreserved challenge concerning an expert report for Tayler. It rejected her argument that Rule 16(d)’s discretionary sanctions applied instead of Rule 26(d)(4)’s mandatory exclusion for undisclosed witnesses. Rule 26 governed because Baumann failed to make the required expert disclosures, and the court found no abuse of discretion in excluding the late Kroger report.

A Northamptonshire newlywed couple walked home after police stopped their uninsured driver for speeding in a BMW at 46mph in a 30mph zone; officers said they had no discretion to continue the journey.

**NVIDIA Ampere GA10x Architecture Whitepaper — Summary**

This document describes the NVIDIA Ampere GA10x GPU architecture (GA102 and GA104), which builds on the Turing architecture and is claimed to be up to 1.7x faster in raster graphics and up to 2x faster in ray tracing, while being up to 1.9x more power efficient than Turing.

**GA102 GPU:** Fabricated on Samsung's 8nm 8N process with 28.3 billion transistors and a 628.4 mm² die, GA102 contains 10,752 CUDA Cores, 84 second-generation RT Cores, and 336 third-generation Tensor Cores, organized into 7 GPCs, 42 TPCs, and 84 SMs. ROPs moved from the memory subsystem into the GPC, giving 112 ROPs instead of 96 in TU102. Each SM has 128 CUDA Cores, four Tensor Cores, a 256 KB register file, one RT Core, and 128 KB of unified L1/shared memory; the full GPU has 6,144 KB of L2 cache and a 384-bit memory interface. The SM's second datapath now supports FP32 as well as INT32, doubling FP32 throughput (RTX 3090 exceeds 35 FP32 TFLOPS).

**Second-Generation RT Core:** Doubles ray/triangle intersection testing (58 RT TFLOPS in RTX 3080 vs. 34 in Turing) and allows RT Core work to run concurrently with graphics or compute within each SM. A new Interpolate Triangle Position unit accelerates ray-traced motion blur, enabling motion blur rendering up to 8x faster than Turing; NVIDIA measured up to 5x faster motion blur on an RTX 3080 versus RTX 2080 Super in a Blender Cycles 2.90 demo. Supported by Blender 2.90, Chaos V-Ray 5.0, Arnold, and Redshift 3.0.X via OptiX 7.0.

**Third-Generation Tensor Cores:** Fewer but more powerful Tensor Cores per SM (four, versus eight in TU102), each twice as powerful. New capabilities include fine-grained structured sparsity (2-out-of-4 pattern, 2x throughput), TF32 precision (up to 5x training throughput, no code changes), BF16, and 4x math throughput versus FP32 for FP16/BF16. RTX 3080 delivers 119 peak FP16 Tensor TFLOPS, 238 with sparsity, 238 INT8 TOPS, and 476 INT4 TOPS (doubled with sparsity), i.e., 2.7x higher FP16 throughput than RTX 2080 Super dense.

**Memory, I/O and interconnects:** GDDR6X, co-developed with Micron, uses PAM4 signaling and MTA encoding to reach 19.5 Gbps (3090) and 19 Gbps (3080), delivering up to 936 GB/sec peak bandwidth, over 52% more than TU102. Third-generation NVLink provides four x4 links (56.25 GB/sec each direction, 112.5 GB/sec total) for 2-way scaling to 96 GB; 3- and 4-way SLI are not supported. PCIe Gen 4 doubles PCIe 3.0 bandwidth (up to 16 GT/s, 64 GB/sec on x16). L1/shared memory capacity is 33% larger than Turing, with doubled shared memory bandwidth (219 GB/sec total L1 on RTX 3080 vs. 116 GB/sec on RTX 2080).

**Products:** The GeForce RTX 3090 (GA102, 10,496 CUDA Cores, 24 GB GDDR6X, DLSS 8K) is built for 8K HDR gaming at 60 fps, 1.5x faster than TITAN RTX. The RTX 3080 offers up to 2x the RTX 2080's performance. The RTX 3070 uses GA104, exceeds RTX 2080 Ti performance, and uses GDDR6 (no NVLink). The RTX A6000 combines 84 RT Cores, 336 Tensor Cores, 10,752 CUDA Cores, and 48 GB GDDR6 (96 GB via NVLink). The A40 data center GPU offers up to 2x FP32, 2x ray tracing, and 5x (10x with sparsity) AI training throughput versus Quadro RTX 6000, with 48 GB scalable to 96 GB, three DP1.4 outputs, vGPU and Quadro Sync support, and EGX compatibility.

**Other features:** NVIDIA RTX IO, working with Microsoft's DirectStorage API, offloads game asset decompression to the GPU for up to 100x I/O throughput and 20x lower CPU utilization. Ampere supports DisplayPort 1.4a with DSC 1.2a (two 8K/60 Hz displays) and is the first discrete GPU with HDMI 2.1 (48 Gbps, 8K60, 4K120) plus HDCP 2.3. Fifth-generation NVDEC supports MPEG-2, VC-1, H.264, H.265, VP8, VP9, and AV1 — GA10x provides the first hardware AV1 decode, playing 8K60 HDR at roughly 4% CPU usage versus 28 FPS and over 85% CPU load in software on an i9-9900K. Seventh-generation NVENC (introduced with Turing) handles up to 4K H.264 and 8K HEVC, exceeding x264 Fast quality and matching x264 Medium with far lower CPU use. Appendix B introduces Error Detection and Replay (EDR) on GDDR6X, which retries failed transactions and indicates memory overclock limits when performance plateaus.
