The message supports prompt refinancing of maturing national debt to reduce annual interest costs and urges Congress to pass another refinancing measure if the bill fails. However, it objects to Section 5, which from July 1, 1881, would limit bonds eligible as security for national-bank circulation and public deposits to 3 percent bonds, with limited substitution rights and exclusion of bonds whose interest had ceased. The message predicts that this restriction would largely prevent new bank organization and capital expansion, weaken noteholder security, favor existing banks, and endanger the national banking system and the country’s prosperity. Because Section 5 is not essential to debt refinancing but could seriously impair banking, the bill is returned to the House for reconsideration.

The paper investigates whether large language models can detect and fix API misuses in Python data science libraries, where dynamic data characteristics and complex structures make misuse harder to identify than in statically typed languages. It distinguishes misuses governed by explicit API directives from data-dependent misuses, such as scikit-learn’s SimpleImputer dropping an all-missing column and causing an indexing error.

DSCHECKER prompts an LLM with code, the library name, relevant API directives, and dynamic information about processed variables. It requests a JSON determination, an explanation, and a unified-diff patch when misuse is found. The approach was evaluated with GPT-4o-mini, GPT-4o, and Llama 3.1 405B.

The DSMISUSES dataset was derived from 49 cases involving NumPy, pandas, Matplotlib, scikit-learn, and seaborn. After removing eight unreproducible cases and three duplicates, 38 misuses remained. Adding a corrected version of each produced 76 evaluation snippets. Detection required both an incorrect classification and an accurate explanation; fixes were applied and executed to verify correctness.

With zero-shot prompting, supplying both directives and data information generally performed best for GPT-4o and Llama. Llama achieved the strongest overall results, with a 61.18% detection F1-score and a 51.28% fix rate using the full prompt. Additional context significantly improved detection on data-dependent cases but could slightly reduce performance on non-data-dependent cases. Few-shot prompting produced mixed results: it significantly improved GPT-4o’s detection and fixing, slightly reduced Llama’s detection without significantly changing its fixing, and harmed GPT-4o-mini’s fixing performance.

On 15 reproduced deep-learning misuses, DSCHECKER obtained a 48% detection F1-score and fixed 26.67%. Detection rose to 66.67% when restricted to APIs with directives, and the approach detected and fixed one misuse missed by LLMAPIDET. On DSMISUSES, LLMAPIDET using existing deep-learning rules detected none of the 38 misuses. With five-fold rule generation, it achieved 11.19% average recall and fixed none of the four detected cases. DSCHECKER using GPT-4o-mini and the full prompt reached 46.15% recall.

DSCHECKERagent used function calling to retrieve documentation and variable information on demand without prior knowledge of the suspect API. With GPT-4o, it achieved a 48.65% detection F1-score and 39.47% fix rate, showing practical potential but lower performance than the context-rich DSCHECKER. Observed limitations included hallucinated API requests and difficulty interpreting full documentation.

The study identifies small dataset size, evaluation of only three LLMs, nondeterminism, and manual assessment of explanations and fixes as validity threats. It also recommends improved validation of agent requests and more structured, LLM-friendly API documentation.

The speaker discusses a hockey playoff series against Detroit, emphasizing that the first ten minutes and scoring first will be crucial. He notes that his team overcame a deficit to win one game in overtime, while the previous game’s three goals highlighted the need for crisper play, better positioning, and fewer mistakes. He expects the next game in Greensboro to be loud and wild, hoping the home crowd will provide momentum as his team continues playing its own game. He also recounts arriving home late, sharing a bed with his young son, sleeping in while school was out, and leaving the house knowing his family understands the importance of the playoffs. He calls the matchup between two European goaltenders historic, describes Dominik as one of the league’s best, and says one could become the first European goalie to win the Cup.

A study of 2,066 millennial twins in England and Wales found that loneliness at age 18 was associated with twice the risk of depression and anxiety, a 38% higher risk of unemployment, and more smoking and lack of exercise. While 7% often felt lonely, 23–31% felt excluded or lacked companionship. Researchers emphasize early intervention to prevent loneliness from persisting into adulthood.

Teenagers and young adults reportedly experience the most loneliness, though the role of social media is complex: maintaining contact and making friends can be beneficial, while aimless scrolling and jealousy may increase isolation. Loneliness may also spread; one cited study found connected people were 52% more likely to be lonely if someone close was lonely. Although loneliness is not itself a mental health problem, it is strongly linked with poor mental well-being, and social connection can improve it.

Rice University and the Houston Museum of Natural Science (HMNS) have collaborated in space-science outreach since 1988, beginning with an NSF-funded teacher research program and later developing the Rice Master of Science Teaching program. Their NASA-supported work produced educational technologies including an internet-connected science kiosk and video planetarium systems. Research also found that dome-based learning improved content retention compared with flatscreen viewing. For the 2017 U.S. eclipse, the partners created free classroom and planetarium animations, distributed them to educators and media, and used them in teacher workshops.

During the 2023–2024 Heliophysics “Big Year,” outreach targeted teachers, media, websites, email lists, planetariums, public events, and Citizen CATE 2024. Three annular-eclipse animations were added in 2021. By late 2021, 186 educators from 33 countries and 33 U.S. states had requested the animations, which also received more than 19,000 YouTube views. A “Lunar Eclipse from the Moon” animation predicted a diamond-ring effect later observed by Firefly Aerospace’s Blue Ghost lander in March 2025.

The collaboration with HMNS and ePlanetarium produced the fulldome show “Totality!” using NASA-supported animations and content on eclipse lore and history, eclipse geometry and dynamics, Saros cycles, Mars and Jupiter eclipse-like events, possible lunar formation, safe viewing, and the 2023 annular and 2024 total eclipses. It was distributed without license fees in several formats. “Totality!” reached 147 planetariums, while “Totality over Texas” reached 53 Texas planetariums and schools. Of 200 recipient sites, 113 reported metrics, documenting 133,469 views, plus 8,800 HMNS views and 278 three-day planetarium rentals; estimated impact exceeded 180,000.

Rice offered four semester-long teacher courses covering the solar system, astronomy, astronomy labs, and ham-radio physics, with eclipse science and safety emphasized in all four. Numerous workshops distributed eclipse glasses, viewing cards, and lenses. The documented teacher events reached 5,104 educators in person or through live interactive sessions, while the results section reported 5,405 teacher users. Survey respondents said the materials were widely redistributed and reached about 500 students on average.

The Rice eclipse website, maintained since 2014, offered animations, activities, FAQs, graphics, training, equipment information, and safe-observing resources. Feedback indicated that animations and safe-viewing techniques were most frequently used with students, while animations, graphics, activities, and the eclipse movie were considered most useful. Rice and HMNS also developed a doorway solar screen, activity sheets, and a low-cost solar cup projector. More than 35,000 eclipse glasses and 30,000 viewing cards were distributed directly, while nearly one million viewers were distributed through public schools, reaching every Texas county and school district.

Public observing events included activities near Corpus Christi and at the “Texas Nexus,” as well as an HMNS event drawing about 2,500 people. Citizen CATE 2024, led by Southwest Research Institute with NSF and NASA support, used 35 community-led sites plus eight additional sites to create continuous, polarized observations of the April 2024 corona. More than 250 citizens, students, and amateur astronomers participated. All teams operated without equipment failures or mishaps; despite cloud cover at some sites, more than 80% observed some or all of totality. The resulting data were processed rapidly, and their analysis was ongoing.

Reiff and Sumners also appeared extensively in radio, print, television, online, and public-event coverage, with total reach in the tens of thousands. The MMS-funded space-weather forecasting system issued one- and three-hour predictions of Kp, Dst, and AE indices and emailed alerts to more than 900 Spacelrt subscribers and over 20,000 outreach-list subscribers. Its May 2024 Kp9 forecast accompanied a major geomagnetic storm that produced auroras visible in several U.S. states.

Overall, the Heliophysics Big Year partnership documented more than 250,000 leveraged views, distributed nearly one million eclipse viewers, confirmed 5,405 teacher users, and achieved a total estimated reach exceeding 1.5 million people, excluding uncounted website and media audiences. The authors concluded that combined federal, university, museum, research-institute, and private resources made the 2024 total solar eclipse exceptionally well observed.

Rams coach Sean McVay said Todd Gurley and other starters will receive progressive work through the third preseason game, aiming to have Gurley ready for the Sept. 10 opener against Indianapolis. Gurley had four carries for two yards and a 10-yard reception in the Rams’ 13-10 win over Dallas. McVay said coaches will carefully manage Gurley’s workload while preparing him for the season.

A March 2, 2001 email from Enron executive Steven Kean sent Joe Hartsoe numerous newspaper articles on California’s electricity crisis, noting that the first concerned a 1946 Nebraska case. The clippings described Gov. Gray Davis’s proposal to acquire utility transmission lines, finance a state power authority, and use state bonds to assist financially distressed utilities while avoiding customer rate increases. Southern California Edison tentatively agreed to sell its grid for about $2.7 billion, while negotiations with PG&E continued and federal regulatory approval was uncertain.

Despite Davis’s optimism, energy experts warned of substantial summer shortages, unpaid power contracts, and continuing utility debt. The Public Utilities Commission defended rate freezes and deregulation decisions while reviewing residential electricity baselines and a temporary Edison rate increase. Calpine signed long-term state supply contracts worth up to $8.3 billion.

Cal-ISO reported that suppliers had charged about $562 million above modeled reasonable costs and asked federal regulators to seek refunds; generators denied overcharging. PG&E announced it would pay creditors only about 15 cents on the dollar, as major suppliers and state officials debated debt forgiveness and possible bankruptcy. Enron’s Kean opposed forgiving debts. Analysts questioned the long-term cost and feasibility of state ownership, while former regulator Elizabeth Moler urged temporary federal price caps, which FERC Chairman Curtis Hebert opposed.

Camera-trap footage from a Malaysian durian orchard showed that island flying foxes feed on nectar without damaging flowers and positively affect durian reproduction, countering previous suspicions that they harmed the crop. The study highlights the bats’ ecological importance as pollinators and supports conserving them, as the species is threatened by hunting and habitat loss and is endangered in Malaysia.

Research following 2,480 men for an average of 22 years found that the highest blood linoleic acid level was associated with a 43% lower risk of death from all causes than the lowest level. Higher levels were also linked to reduced cardiovascular-death risk, but not cancer-death risk. High arachidonic acid showed a weaker association with lower mortality.

The final lecture reviews least-squares duality and projection, including an identity for four vectors drawn from a point to the corners of a rectangle, \(a^2+c^2=b^2+d^2\), and poses finding a proof from Pythagoras as an open exercise. It then introduces inverse and ill-posed problems, in which hidden causes are inferred from measurements and small data errors may produce large solution changes. Examples include recovering velocity from position, Earth density from seismic travel times or gravity, tissue density from CT/MRI/PET, obstacle shape from scattering data, coefficients in Laplace or Poisson equations, and an unknown matrix from input-output pairs.

Integral equations of the first kind, including Volterra and Fredholm forms, are presented as common mathematical descriptions of inverse problems. Adding a small multiple of the identity regularizes such equations and produces second-kind equations. The lecture concludes with Tikhonov regularization, minimizing \(\|Ax-b\|^2+\alpha\|x\|^2\), which leads to \((A^TA+\alpha I)\hat u=b\). For noise of size \(\delta\), the estimated error is characterized as approximately \(\delta/\sqrt{\alpha}\), requiring a balance between under- and over-regularization; under the lecture’s estimates, \(\alpha=\delta^{2/3}\) is identified as a good choice. GPS illustrates velocity estimation, while differential geometry, Doppler measurements, and gene-expression sensitivity are also discussed as ill-posed estimation tasks.

This preprint presents the first human whole-body [11C]carfentanil ([11C]CFN) PET study of mu-opioid receptor (MOR) availability, investigating potential extra-CNS reference regions in the aorta and muscle. MORs are targets of opioids, including fentanyl and heroin, and of OUD treatments such as methadone and buprenorphine; MOR agonists can cause respiratory depression, while naloxone antagonizes opioid effects. Prior [11C]CFN-PET research has largely focused on the brain, and sex differences in naloxone binding have not been examined. The study uses the long axial field-of-view PennPET Explorer. Healthy English-speaking adults aged 18–45 were screened for psychiatric, substance-use, medication, pregnancy, and MRI-related exclusions, and underwent urine drug testing. Participants received T1-weighted MRI and a 90-minute dynamic whole-body PET scan after [11C]CFN injection, with low-dose CT for attenuation correction. Images were reconstructed with time-of-flight OSEM and processed using PMOD, MRI coregistration, MNI spatial normalization, and five bilateral brain regions of interest. Brain distribution volume ratios were calculated with the Logan reference tissue model using the visual cortex, and receptor occupancy was to be assessed for naloxone pretreatment.

Mitch Larkin won the 400m individual medley at the Queensland titles in 4:20.45 and is considering adding it to his program at February’s Commonwealth Games trials. The 2015 world 100m/200m backstroke champion remains focused on restoring world-class backstroke form and seeking redemption after winning Rio silver in the 200m but missing the 100m podium. He has changed coaches twice since the Olympics and credits Dean Boxall’s high-volume, aerobic program with reigniting his hunger and discipline.

Ventura police will review procedures after a homeless man fatally stabbed a patron in a crowded steakhouse while the man’s young daughter sat on his lap. Chief Ken Corney said officers should have responded in person to earlier reports about suspect Jamal Jackson instead of monitoring security cameras. Jackson, 49, is charged with murder in the April 18 death of 35-year-old Anthony Mele and has not entered a plea. Residents at a City Council meeting criticized officials’ handling of homelessness and mental illness.

On Aug. 21, 2017, a total solar eclipse crossed the United States from Oregon to South Carolina, the first coast-to-coast total eclipse in 99 years. Its 8,600-mile path of totality passed through 14 states and lasted about 1½ hours, beginning around 1:15 p.m. EDT and ending at 2:49 p.m. EDT. Darkness ranged from just under two minutes in Oregon to 2 minutes 44 seconds in southern Illinois.

Festivals, sporting events, school closures and business shutdowns were planned along the path, which was expected to draw large crowds. NASA coordinated broadcasts and educational activities, while balloons, satellites, telescopes, astronauts, ships and planes documented the event. Researchers also planned to observe changes in animals, plants and temperatures, which were expected to fall 10 to 15 degrees. Eye protection was required before and after totality.

A partial eclipse was visible across much of North and Central America and northern South America. The passage also noted an April 8, 2024 total eclipse crossing Mexico, the United States and eastern Canada, with darkness lasting up to four minutes.

The EOS M6 replaces Canon’s M3 as an entry-level mirrorless camera for users wanting affordable dSLR-like photo quality. It makes the viewfinder optional, retains the M5’s sensor and Digic 7 processor, and adds revised controls and a tilting touchscreen. Canon planned April 2017 pricing from $780, but Sony’s cheaper A5100 and A6000 offered similar specifications or a built-in viewfinder.

In an arbitrary Abelian group, the additive energy \(E(A,B)\) counts quadruples \((a_1,a_2,b_1,b_2)\) satisfying \(a_1+b_1=a_2+b_2\). Equivalently, it is \(\sum_x r_{A,B}(x)^2\), where \(r_{A,B}(x)\) counts representations \(x=a+b\). For \(E(A)\), the trivial bounds are \(|A|^2\le E(A)\le |A|^3\). Small doubling implies large energy: if \(|A+A|\le k|A|\), then \(E(A)\ge |A|^3/k\). The converse fails because a set can combine a highly structured part with unstructured elements, producing high energy but large doubling.

The Balog–Szemerédi–Gowers theorem states that sufficiently large additive energy forces large subsets with small doubling. Its two-set version yields sizable subsets \(A'\subseteq A\) and \(B'\subseteq B\) whose sumset \(A'+B'\) is small.

A graphical version applies to dense bipartite graphs between subsets of an Abelian group: if the sumset restricted to graph edges is small, large subsets have a small unrestricted sumset. The additive theorem reduces to this version by forming a graph from popular sums; unpopular sums contribute only a small portion of the energy.

The graphical proof uses two lemmas. A length-two-path lemma, proved by dependent random choice, finds a large set whose pairs mostly have many common neighbors. A length-three-path lemma strengthens this to large subsets \(A'\) and \(B'\) such that every cross-pair has many length-three paths. These paths express each \(a+b\) as \(x-y+z\) with \(x,y,z\) in the restricted sumset, bounding the complete sumset \(A'+B'\) by the cube of the restricted sumset and completing the proof.

An IDC white paper, based on a December 2021 survey of 200 IT and departmental decision-makers at discrete and process manufacturing enterprises in Germany, Austria, and Switzerland, examines industrial simulation, modeling, data analysis, and high-performance computing (HPC). Manufacturers face geopolitical, supply-chain, labor, energy, sustainability, and competitive pressures while pursuing digital transformation. Simulation and modeling are viewed as key to innovation, quality, faster product development, lower costs, and better decisions. About half already use these tools across development, production planning, and quality management, with deployment expected to reach 90% within two years.

Current use cases include virtual prototyping, digital twins, IoT and sensor feedback loops, design optimization, digital verification, and high-performance data analytics. Integration is hindered by departmental data silos, making a unified “single source of truth” important for end-to-end processes and collaboration with external partners. Digital twins and integrated IT solutions may also enable new services and business models such as Product-as-a-Service.

Growing calculation complexity is increasing demand for HPC; 81% of respondents view it as a game changer for product and process innovation. More than a quarter already use professional HPC infrastructure, while another 39% are planning or piloting it. Current users favor external infrastructure, including public cloud and colocation, over on-premises systems. Key challenges include security, high investment and licensing costs, energy consumption, insufficient expertise, performance constraints, availability, scalability, and infrastructure complexity.

Cloud-based architectures are presented as the leading future option, followed by hybrid-cloud and prebuilt systems. IDC recommends a “make or buy” decision, noting that public-cloud HPC can offer greater scalability and flexibility while avoiding the capital, maintenance, and upgrade burdens of on-premises clusters.

An Arizona man was charged with conspiring to manufacture and sell unlicensed armor-piercing ammunition allegedly bought by Stephen Paddock, the gunman in the October 2017 Las Vegas shooting that killed 58 and wounded hundreds. Douglas Haig denied selling reloaded cartridges, but investigators found his fingerprints on reloaded .308 rounds and matching tool marks on ammunition in Paddock’s hotel rooms.

Deion Sanders was scheduled to undergo a procedure Tuesday for recurring blood clots, hoping to return to practice the next day and be on the sideline for Saturday’s game against No. 22 Iowa State. The Buffaloes coach had been in pain and limping during a 35-21 loss at TCU, sometimes sitting along the sideline and omitting his left shoe. Sanders said the condition is hereditary and unrelated to his workload. He previously dealt with blood clots in 2021, when two left toes were amputated, and underwent additional procedures in 2023. Sanders also spent time away this summer following treatment for aggressive bladder cancer, including reconstruction of part of his intestine to function as a bladder. The school provided a portable sideline bathroom because he frequently uses the restroom. He expressed confidence in returning, reliance on prayer, and appreciation for supporters’ concern.

Rockefeller University researchers kept a tiny sliver of gerbil cochlea alive and functional outside the body for the first time. Using a custom chamber that reproduced the tissue’s natural fluids, temperature, and voltage, they played sounds and directly observed how cochlear hair cells amplify vibrations, including through ion-channel activity and outer-hair-cell electromotility. They also identified a Hopf bifurcation—a mechanical tipping point—in the mammalian active hearing process, demonstrating that hearing mechanics are remarkably similar across animals. The ex vivo system may enable targeted pharmacological studies of hearing and hearing loss, potentially supporting new sensorineural hearing-loss treatments.

Ampere adds BF16, TF32, and FP64 Tensor Core formats. FP16 and BF16 enable mixed-precision training matching FP32, with 16× FP32 math throughput. TF32 provides default Tensor Core acceleration for FP32 data using reduced internal precision.

The disclosure describes memory arrays formed from vertically alternating tiers of insulating material and memory cells, each memory cell including a transistor and a capacitor. Transistors have first and second source/drain regions, a horizontally oriented channel, and one or more gates; capacitors have electrodes separated by an insulator and may use ferroelectric or other programmable materials. The passage also describes volatile, semi-volatile, and non-volatile memory, including ferroelectric capacitors and ferroelectric field-effect transistors.

In a principal embodiment, access lines interconnect gates along rows or columns, while staircase regions contain conductive vias for accessing gates in individual tiers. A vertically extending capacitor-electrode structure couples the second capacitor electrodes across tiers, and a vertically extending sense-line structure couples second source/drain regions across tiers. Alternate embodiments include transistors with two vertically spaced channel segments, single-gate transistors with single-sided capacitors, tiers containing two vertically stacked memory cells, and configurations in which stacked-cell transistors are separately accessed.

A fabrication sequence forms alternating deposited layers and staggered openings, selectively etches materials to define capacitor electrodes, source/drain regions, channel regions, gates, trenches, access lines, capacitor-electrode structures, and conductive vias, and then fills and planarizes selected structures. Example materials include doped silicon, polysilicon, silicon nitride, silicon dioxide, high-k insulators, titanium nitride, and metal, with selective etching using HF, TMAH, hot phosphoric acid, or sulfuric-acid and peroxide solutions. The disclosure is associated with a reissue of U.S. Patent No. 10,607,995 and the “Memory Arrays” provisional application filed May 8, 2017.

In a speech in Pittsburgh, the President praised union electrician Mike for restoring power after a storm, affirmed his own union identity, and said his campaign began there two years ago to "rebuild the backbone of America." He cited 547,296 U.S. deaths from COVID-19, defended the American Rescue Plan as passed with help from local and congressional leaders, reported a goal of 200 million vaccine doses in his first 100 days, said economists now forecast 6% economic growth, and said child poverty could be cut in half. He argued the pandemic widened inequality, noting the wealthiest 1% gained $4 trillion in net worth.

He proposed an American Jobs Plan (an American Families Plan to follow in a few weeks): a one-time capital investment of roughly $2 trillion spread over about eight years, the largest federal jobs investment since World War II, which some Wall Street firms estimate will create over 18 million jobs. Components include modernizing 20,000 miles of highways, roads and main streets; replacing the 10 most economically significant bridges and repairing 10,000 others; new rail corridors and transit lines; climate resilience; 500,000 electric-vehicle charging stations with rebates for clean vehicles and conversion of the federal vehicle fleet; "Buy American" sourcing; replacing 100% of lead pipes and service lines, affecting up to 10 million homes and more than 400,000 schools and childcare centers; affordable high-speed internet for all Americans; a modern clean grid, capping hundreds of thousands of orphan oil and gas wells; weatherizing housing; expanding home- and community-based care and raising caregiver pay; and the largest increase in federal non-defense research and development spending, targeting batteries, biotechnology, computer chips and clean energy amid competition with China. The plan also supports the PRO Act, worker bargaining rights and directing investment to marginalized and rural communities.

To pay for it, he said no one earning under $400,000 would face a federal tax increase, while raising the corporate rate from 21% to 28% (about $1 trillion over 15 years), imposing a 21% global minimum tax on U.S. corporations (about $1 trillion over 15 years), penalizing offshoring, adding credits for U.S. manufacturing and increasing IRS enforcement. He noted the U.S. ranks 13th in infrastructure, argued delay adds to debt and disadvantages children, called infrastructure historically bipartisan (Lincoln, Eisenhower), and framed the effort as a test of democracy versus autocracy, urging Republicans, businesses and independents to support it.

Digital I/Os use PINCMx registers to configure pin functions. IOMUX allows one managed function per pin; non-IOMUX signals may coexist when contention-free, with PINCM.PF and PC set to 0 for non-IOMUX use.
XPIC’s IRR-clear delay can make AEOI send two CPU interrupts instead of one; AEOI is master-PIC-only and unsuitable where nesting is required.

The application describes automated storage, retrieval, and processing systems for moving objects into destination bins according to a manifest. Embodiments include storage bins, destination bins, conveyance or gantry systems that deliver bins to processing locations, and a programmable motion device, such as a robotic arm, whose end effector grasps objects and transfers them between bins. Separate or common gantries may handle storage and destination bins, while other embodiments include multiple sections, processing stations, and floors.

A perception unit provides camera images or scanning data of bin contents. The system identifies candidate grasp locations, including flat surfaces and features such as UPC or barcode areas, and directs the end effector to approach objects substantially normal to the selected surface to improve grasp stability and vacuum sealing. Good and bad grasp locations may be correlated with image features and used in machine-learning algorithms to improve future grasp selection. Processed bins may be returned to storage, placed on output conveyors or staging areas, or palletized for shipment. Computer control continuously tracks bin identities and locations and coordinates object distribution according to an overall manifest.

The coach said his team started unsettled but settled quickly, battling back despite failing to find a third goal. He praised its energy, speed, puck possession, territorial control, scoring chances, shot clock, and persistence, while noting that a strong opponent made the elimination game difficult. The opponent generated offense below the goal line using size and skill, and forward Burns consistently created chances from the blue line.

The coach trusted the team’s leadership to keep emotion controlled and channeled appropriately. He said Sid remained a threat regardless of matchups, while Sergei provided composure, insight, and valuable support for the defense. He emphasized focusing on the current task, following established routines, and avoiding getting ahead during the high-stakes postseason.

Geno was described as an elite player whose improving play at both ends and goal contribution strengthened the team. Matt’s on-ice impact was said to speak for itself, and the coach also praised his experience, perspective, locker-room influence, and composed demeanor, viewing him as an extension of the coaching staff.

The President reported that 653 troops, excluding Marines, were ordered to Washington as a posse comitatus to preserve peace and order during the inauguration. Although a House committee found no evidence of a secret organization threatening the capital or government, a majority resolution calling for the troops’ removal gave him reason to retain them. Given the revolutionary unrest, widespread fears, and the importance of protecting public property, government archives, city order, and the inauguration, he had acted prudently and quickly; calm followed, and he believed delay could have risked grave consequences.

The article describes bear markets as prolonged, steep declines, commonly associated with a 20% or greater fall, though no official definition exists. They are characterized by sharp selloffs, strong rallies, and increased volatility, while generally lasting less time than bull markets. The stock market reportedly spends about 20% of its time in bear markets, which can remove economic excesses and encourage innovation, but recoveries are slow: the S&P 500 took 6.5 years to regain its 2000 peak, while certain technology stocks required 15 years.

Long-term investors can benefit from lower prices and higher expected future returns, while short-term traders gain opportunities from volatility in both long and short strategies. A mean-reversion strategy on QQQ performed profitably during the dot-com recession, the financial crisis, and the initial Covid-19 downturn. Central-bank stimulus may postpone recessions and asset-price declines but is unlikely to prevent them. The article advises automated traders to maintain their strategies and long-term investors to continue buying, while noting that bear markets are especially concerning for retirees or those planning to withdraw funds.

The Louisiana Supreme Court declined to consider Arthur Rhodes’s untimely supervisory writ. Because his first post-conviction ruling is final, further state collateral review requires meeting narrow statutory exceptions for successive applications.

This study examines how uniform strain (ε) and nonuniform strain gradients (η) affect thermal transport in monoclinic β-Ga₂O₃ bulk material, 10- and 100-nm films, and nanowires at 300 K. A DFT-trained neuroevolution potential coupled with the Boltzmann transport equation was used with an explicit strain-gradient scattering model. The potential reproduced DFT energies, forces, virials, phonon dispersions, and reported bulk and thin-film thermal conductivities accurately.

Uniform uniaxial and biaxial strains strongly and anisotropically altered thermal conductivity, primarily by modifying intrinsic three-phonon scattering and phonon lifetimes rather than heat capacity or velocity. Strain gradients generally caused greater conductivity suppression, especially in thin films. At ηzᵦ = 0.6%/nm, a 10-nm film showed reductions of 31.8%, 35.3%, and 36.6% in ka, kb, and kc, respectively, compared with 16.1%, 27.0%, and 23.4% under equivalent 3% uniform b-axis strain. Biaxial ηz_ab = 0.6%/nm produced reductions of 42.4%, 43.3%, and 41.6%, roughly 1.5 times the corresponding uniform-strain effect; peak kb reduction was 43.3%. Nanowires exhibited reductions of up to 30.5%.

Gradient-induced symmetry breaking broadened phonon spectra, relaxed momentum-conservation restrictions, altered intermode frequency gaps, and activated previously forbidden scattering channels. The resulting strain-gradient scattering dominated across 0–10 THz, particularly affecting heat-carrying acoustic and low-lying optical phonons. Uniform strain substantially changed thermal anisotropy ratios, whereas strain gradients strongly reduced conductivity while largely preserving those ratios. The findings identify strain gradients as important factors in β-Ga₂O₃ thermal modeling and as a means of thermal isolation in flexible devices.

Start-up owners should understand investor priorities to create a coherent, attractive offering. Key considerations include potential return on investment, realistic equity flexibility, and whether investors can provide mentorship, industry experience, or contacts. Founders should present themselves confidently and persuasively while accepting advice, and demonstrate the strengths of an experienced, proactive team. Market traction can be evidenced through revenue and customer satisfaction. Investors may specialize in particular industries or emerging markets and respond to identified market gaps or disruptive innovation, so founders should explain challenges and practical responses. A detailed business strategy should include the venture’s rationale, accurate supporting figures and projections, competitor research, consideration of new market entrants, and awareness of the implications of financial forecasts and the consequences of missing them. Preparation and confident communication can help inspire investor confidence.

UCLA researchers found that lactate production controls the activation of normally inactive hair follicle stem cells. In mice, genetically blocking lactate prevented stem cell activation, while increasing lactate accelerated activation and lengthened the hair-growth cycle. The team identified two topical drugs: RCGD423, which activates the JAK-Stat signaling pathway to increase lactate production, and UK5099, which blocks pyruvate from entering mitochondria, thereby forcing lactate production. Both promoted hair growth in mice. Published in Nature Cell Biology, the research may support future treatments for baldness or alopecia. The drugs remain preclinical, have not been tested in humans, and have not received FDA approval for safe and effective human use. UCLA filed separate provisional patents covering their hair-growth applications.

Colgate-Palmolive’s recent decline appears to have paused as revenue and profit growth return. Argus set a $72 price target, while analysts expect revenue growth over the next two fiscal years and mid- to high-single-digit profit growth for three years. The stock’s forward P/E ratio is below 20, and its quarterly dividend of 42 cents yields about 2.6%; Colgate has increased dividends annually since 1964.

However, the author warns that Colgate’s moat remains weak because its products are easily copied and e-commerce gives smaller and niche manufacturers access to consumers and virtual shelf space. Despite customer loyalty and stable dividends, increased competition could constrain long-term growth, making 20 times earnings too expensive.

**Debug subsystem (DEBUGSS).** The debug subsystem interfaces the ARM Serial Wire Debug (SWD) two-wire interface (SWDIO, SWCLK) to multiple debug functions and supports debugging of processor execution and device state. Features include on-chip pullup/pulldown resistors enabled by default, the ability to disable SWD functions and reuse the pins as GPIO, software-configurable peripheral behavior during debug (free-running or halting selected peripherals, requesting PMCU reset and mode changes), a DSSM mailbox for passing data and control signals between the SWD interface and boot ROM or application software, and security features such as SWD lockout and password-authenticated debugging.

**Device factory constants.** All devices include a memory-mapped read-only FACTORY region describing device capabilities and factory trim information. DEVICEID resides at 0x41C4.0004 (PARTNUM bits 12–27, MANUFACTURER bits 1–11); USERID resides at 0x41C4.0008 (PART bits 0–15, VARIANT bits 16–23). Revision and identification data are also given in the top-side package marking and described in the device-specific errata sheet.

**Typical application.** TI recommends a 10 µF plus 0.1 µF low-ESR ceramic decoupling combination on VDD/VSS, placed within a few millimeters of the pins; higher values can slow supply rail ramp-up. NRST requires an external 47 kΩ pullup with a 1000 pF pulldown. Crystal-capable devices need external bypass capacitors on oscillator pins. 5V-tolerant open-drain I/Os (ODIO) require a pullup to output a logic high, which applies to I2C and UART use.

**Support, nomenclature, and resources.** TI's tools include the MSPM0 LaunchPad ecosystem (on-board XDS110 debug probe, BoosterPack modules), TI Resource Explorer, SysConfig, MSP Academy, GUI Composer, and the TI Arm-Clang compiler; TI E2E forums provide design support. Part-number prefixes distinguish X experimental devices from MSP fully qualified production devices, with suffixes indicating temperature range, package type, and distribution format. TI offers document update subscriptions on ti.com and publishes the MSPM0C1105/MSPM0C1106 technical reference manual.

**Revision history.** The September 2025 Revision A update added the DEBUGSS section, updated DEVICEID/USERID tables, removed DGS32 package data, revised power mode, package option, and numerous specification sections, and updated CPU features and ADC ENOB with external reference.

**Mechanical, packaging, and orderable information.** Pages include package and carrier-tape drawings with notes on dimensions per ASME Y14.5M, mandatory thermal-pad soldering, optional vias (filled, plugged, or tented), recommended paste coverage of 73–78%, and PowerPAD trademark. Orderable-parts footnotes cover lifecycle status, preproduction material type, RoHS, lead finish, MSL/peak reflow, and part marking.

**Cautions and disclaimers.** The integrated circuit may be damaged by electrostatic discharge, so appropriate handling precautions are required. TI disclaims warranties for application information, including schematic guidance, which is not part of the component specification; resources are provided "AS IS," and TI's liability for third-party information cannot exceed the purchase price of the parts at issue.

The lecture reviews digital communication as a binary interface between an often-analog source and channel, with standardization reducing implementation costs, layering simplifying analysis, and, according to Shannon, no inherent performance loss. Source coding is divided into sampling or expansion, quantization into a finite symbol alphabet, and discrete encoding into binary digits for transmission over a reliable binary channel. Quantization necessarily introduces distortion.

The focus is discrete source coding: mapping symbol sequences into binary sequences so they can be uniquely decoded. Fixed-length coding assigns each of \(m\) source symbols a binary word of length \(\lceil \log_2 m\rceil\). Generalized fixed-length coding treats blocks of \(n\) symbols as \(m^n\) possible objects, approaching \(\log_2 m\) bits per source symbol as block length increases. Symbol names have no inherent significance for communication; only distinctions among symbols matter. Synchronization is assumed.

Variable-length codes can assign shorter words to more probable symbols and longer words to rare symbols, but concatenated words require buffering to reconcile variable output rates with fixed-rate channels. Unique decodability requires distinct source strings to produce distinct binary concatenations, which is stronger than merely assigning distinct words to individual symbols.

A prefix-free code has no code word that is a prefix of another. Such codes can be represented by binary trees and permit instantaneous decoding because the end of each word is identifiable immediately. Kraft’s inequality states that codeword lengths \(l_i\) can form a prefix-free code exactly when \(\sum_i 2^{-l_i}\leq 1\); equality corresponds to a full tree with no unused leaves. This result is independent of probability. A proof associates binary codewords with nonoverlapping intervals in \([0,1]\), whose total size cannot exceed one. Prefix-free codes are uniquely decodable, and every uniquely decodable code also satisfies Kraft’s inequality.

The lecture next introduces discrete memoryless sources, in which successive source symbols are independent and identically distributed, though not necessarily equally likely. Subsequent topics will use symbol probabilities to determine code lengths through entropy and optimal-code methods.

The shallow cross concept combines a basic route and shallow drag route from opposite directions to stress linebackers and create options against man and zone coverage. It can provide a quick answer to blitzes, allow tight ends to find space over the middle, and offer quarterbacks either a triangle read or a secondary progression after downfield routes. The concept is effective against man coverage when both route runners win their matchups, and against Tampa 2 and Cover 4 because defenders’ movement can leave linebacker-level voids. Cover 3 has the numbers advantage and can prevent large underneath gains.

Route assignments include a tight end running the basic route to a 10–12-yard landmark, a slot receiver running a 3–4-yard shallow drag, and outside receivers running post and go routes. Against zone coverage, the middle routes adjust to open voids. The quarterback first reads downfield routes, then transitions to the post, drag, basic, and RB checkdown progression; against immediate pressure, the quarterback quickly targets the drag or basic route.

The article presents bunch and empty variations, using shallow-cross progressions to answer two-high and one-high defenses while allowing quick throws when pressure is anticipated.

The lecture begins the two-session economics unit on green buildings, framed by the “triple bottom line” of planet, people, and profit. Because private-sector firms supply more than 80% of urban building stock, sustainability must offer incentives beyond environmental or social benefits. The lecture therefore asks how to construct a business case for green buildings through three linked stakeholders: tenants or end users, property owners and investors, and developers.

Millennium Partners illustrates how developers’ sustainability priorities can change with market circumstances. Its 2008 San Francisco Millennium Tower emphasized luxury condominium sales rather than sustainability; later foundation flaws, settlement, structural problems, and lawsuits damaged the company. Millennium Place in Boston was promoted as luxury housing and obtained city approval by promising jobs and downtown revitalization after the financial crisis. The 2017 Boston Millennium Tower addressed another development priority by filling a prominent vacant site, while wellness and an exclusive fitness center supported sales to condominium buyers. Winthrop Center, by contrast, is a passive-house project using extensive sustainability certifications, reflecting growing customer concern about climate change and the willingness of affluent buyers to pay more. The case demonstrates that developers are rational businesses whose priorities depend on buyers, regulators, financing, and economic conditions. Claims that sustainability has always been a developer’s priority should therefore be examined critically, including whether social and business values align.

The lecture first considers how markets might support green buildings. Potential benefits differ by stakeholder. Tenants may receive lower energy and operating costs, improved health and productivity, easier employee recruitment and retention, and greater willingness to pay rent. Owners may receive higher rents and occupancy, lower vacancy and turnover, lower operating and maintenance costs, slower depreciation, lower risk and cost of capital, improved reputation and marketability, and higher resale value. Developers may receive easier permitting, lower financing costs, stronger branding, faster sales, and higher sale prices, but they also face additional construction costs.

A hypothetical 10-year office-building pro forma illustrates how these effects enter financial analysis. Year zero is the initial acquisition; annual cash flow is based on effective gross income, operating expenses, net operating income, and capital expenditures; and the year-10 resale price is estimated from year-11 cash flow and the exit capitalization rate. All cash flows are discounted to calculate NPV. Under favorable assumptions, a green building has higher rents, lower vacancy and operating expenses, potentially lower capital needs, lower exit capitalization and discount rates, and a higher resale price, resulting in a higher NPV and owner willingness to pay. That willingness to pay can support higher developer sale prices, although developers must compare additional upfront and construction costs with later revenue and resale-price gains.

The lecture stresses that these outcomes are not deterministic. Cited research finds an average green-building rent premium of about 6%, while reported rental premiums range from 0% to 23%, sales-price premiums from 0% to 43%, and operating-cost changes from negative 14% to positive 25%. New-building cost premiums range from 0% to 12.5%, with retrofits potentially costing more. Premiums vary with building design, technology, developer expertise, contractor availability, technology maturity, supply chains, and permitting conditions. Passive design can sometimes add little cost, while active mechanical systems generally require additional investment. Winthrop Center’s estimated premium reportedly fell from 3%–10% to about 3% as developers gained experience and the market matured.

The resulting market chain runs from tenants to owners and then developers: tenant benefits can increase willingness to pay, which raises owner cash flows and property values, which can increase developers’ expected sale proceeds. Green investment should therefore be based on market fundamentals and cost-benefit analysis rather than developers’ assumptions that buyers will automatically reward sustainability.

The lecture then introduces market failure, citing the “energy efficiency dilemma”: many building-efficiency investments have positive NPV yet remain unadopted. Three failures are identified, with information asymmetry addressed first, followed by split incentives and externalities. Information asymmetry occurs when buyers do not understand or trust green-building benefits, preventing the expected increase in willingness to pay. A China study described in the lecture found that residents of green buildings expressed willingness to pay roughly 300 RMB per square meter for green features, while residents of comparable non-green buildings increased their willingness to pay after receiving an information card. The hypothetical nature of such surveys remains a limitation.

Because building quality is difficult to assess before occupancy, greenwashing can exploit information gaps. Without certification or credible market signals, buyers may treat green and non-green properties as a single undifferentiated market, reducing developers’ ability to recover green-building costs and allowing inferior projects to crowd out better ones. Certification systems such as LEED are presented as a primary, though imperfect, response to this adverse-selection problem by making sustainability claims more verifiable.

WIS will air a 7:30 p.m. special on the Aug. 21 total solar eclipse. Columbia lies in the path of totality, where the moon fully covers the sun, creating daytime darkness. The eclipse’s shadow will cross the U.S. from west to east.

The Brea Police Department uses an all-electric Polaris Gem Global Electric Motorcar to patrol The Tracks at Brea trail and downtown. Unveiled at the Centennial Parade, the two-seat vehicle tops out at 25 mph with a 98-mile range and a six-to-eight-hour charge, costing about $21,000 funded by the Air Quality Management District. Lt. Darrin Devereux said its size suits the linear park trails better than patrol cars, foot, or bicycle patrols.

Learning assessment is well established in credit-bearing higher education but remains sparse in noncredit continuing education, where satisfaction surveys are common and direct measures of learning outcomes are uncommon. Noncredit continuing education includes professional competency and licensure education, career development, and personal enrichment. The passage recommends assessment to guide curriculum, pedagogy, and improvement.

Effective assessment begins with realistic, clear, measurable learning outcomes suited to program length, learners’ prior knowledge, and available resources. Outcomes should align directly with assessment methods and follow SMART principles. Instructors and coordinators should collaborate when developing outcomes and, where feasible, involve learners.

Learning-outcome-focused surveys can efficiently capture learners’ perceptions of achievement and gains. Retrospective pre-post surveys may be especially practical for short courses, though they measure perceived rather than direct learning. Direct assessment can include one to three quiz questions added to end-of-course surveys for brief programs. For programs lasting 4–20 hours, instructors can use observed skill practice and learner products, assessed with simple scoring systems. Assessment activities should be valid, fair, practical, and designed to benefit learners.

Such assessment can guide course improvements, demonstrate the quality of professional development, inform personnel decisions, and support requests for resources. Aligning outcomes with direct assessment can also support verifiable micro-credentials or other digital credentials that may motivate learners seeking professional or career benefits.

BG Group conditionally agreed to buy Enron’s offshore Indian oil and gas assets for $388 million. The deal includes 30% stakes in the Tapti and Panna/Mukta fields and a 62.64% interest in the CB-OS/1 exploration block, with more than 170 million barrels of oil-equivalent reserves. Completion requires Indian government approval and agreement that BG will operate the fields; ONGC sought operatorship, prompting concerns that the transaction could fail. The acquisition would expand BG’s Indian gas business and complement its LNG pipeline and regasification plans.

Enron continued trying to exit the troubled Dabhol power project, in which it held a 65% stake. Dabhol faced payment disputes with Maharashtra’s electricity board and was shut down, while Enron’s Indian unit defaulted on a $24 million interest payment for its second phase.

Technology stocks led a broad U.S. market rally following Cisco’s reassuring earnings commentary, lifting the Nasdaq 5.93%; Enron shares rose 9.4%. Separately, Southern California Edison reached a settlement with the California Public Utilities Commission that kept customer rates elevated to help repay debt and avoid bankruptcy, prompting consumer advocates to denounce a ratepayer bailout. Former Enron executive Thomas White was appointed the Pentagon’s liaison for homeland security under Tom Ridge.

The lecture concludes its treatment of Markov chains by reviewing eigenvalues and eigenvectors for a transition matrix with transient and recurrent states. Because the matrix is block upper triangular, its determinant factors into determinants of the transient and recurrent blocks, so its eigenvalues are the combined eigenvalues of those blocks. Transitions from transient to recurrent states do not affect the eigenvalues. Left eigenvectors belonging to recurrent blocks can be extended to the full matrix by inserting zeros in the transient positions, and the analysis extends to multiple recurrent sets.

The lecture then introduces state-dependent rewards or costs, defining expected one-step and aggregate rewards using transition probabilities. For an ergodic chain, the long-run expected reward per step approaches the steady-state probability vector dotted with the reward vector and is independent of the initial state, although transient behavior can matter when the average gain is zero.

Expected first-passage time is treated as a reward problem. By making the target state a trapping state with zero reward and assigning unit reward to all other states, the expected time to first reach the target is unchanged. For a chain with one recurrent class, the hitting times satisfy linear equations of the form \(v_i=1+\sum_j p_{ij}v_j\), with \(v_1=0\), which can be solved in vector form as \((I-P)v=r\). If multiple recurrent classes prevent access to the target, the expected hitting time may be infinite.

Finally, the lecture introduces finite-horizon controlled Markov chains. At each time and state, a decision maker chooses among alternatives that specify an immediate reward and transition probabilities, with a fixed terminal reward. Dynamic programming solves these problems backward in time: for each state, maximize the immediate reward plus the expected optimal value of the next state. This Bellman recursion determines optimal decisions and expected aggregate rewards for every starting state and horizon, whereas stationary policies address indefinitely repeated play.

This continuation application concerns methods, apparatuses, communication nodes, and a storage medium for high-frequency, including 5G millimeter-wave, uplink communication. It addresses the difficulty of base-station scheduling accounting for beam- or antenna-panel-specific maximum power reduction (MPR) caused by human-body maximum power exposure (MPE), which can lead user equipment to reduce uplink power passively and degrade transmission performance.

A first communication node, such as a user equipment, sends report information to a second communication node, such as a base station. The report contains first-type power parameter information, uplink channel state information, or both. Power parameters may include MPR, remaining or accumulated energy, uplink duty cycle, alert information, power backoff, and real or virtual power headroom. Channel-state information may include reference-signal indices, antenna-group or panel information, uplink path loss, quasi-co-location information or beams, and uplink correction values. These data may be associated with beams, spatial relations, antenna groups, reference signals, or transmission occasions. Reports may be periodic, semi-persistent, or aperiodic and may be triggered by thresholds, parameter changes, timers, signaling, or configuration information.

The application further describes real and virtual power-headroom reporting, including formats indicating backoff usage, Pcmax, real or virtual status, and associated reference signals or spatial relations. Virtual power-headroom reports may be triggered when P-MPR and uplink duty-cycle conditions indicate significant MPE and may identify potential low-impact uplink beams. Upon receiving the report information, the second communication node determines the first node’s MPR and schedules the node, potentially selecting a beam with lower MPR, to reduce human-body exposure and assist uplink scheduling. Processor-based node and storage-medium implementations are also disclosed.

The Power Play is a gap run featuring a backside guard pulling, a kick-out block, and multiple blocks that create angles and double teams at the point of attack. It can be run from many personnel groups and formations and can help smaller offensive lines gain yardage through leverage and blocking angles. Its primary weakness is backside pursuit and defensive penetration through the open gap left by the pulling guard, particularly against odd fronts if the center makes an incorrect point call. The passage details common blocking assignments against 3-4 odd and 4-3 even fronts, including vertical or horizontal combination blocks. Variations include Diamond Fullhouse, which changes the fullback and H-back responsibilities, and Gun Same-Side Power RPO, which uses a one-back formation and either a pre-snap bubble or post-snap slant.

Bill Purswell was convicted of transporting intoxicating liquor and sentenced to one year in the penitentiary. Sheriff Hightower and Deputy Anderson concealed themselves at McElvain’s property, where they observed Purswell carrying a jug containing whiskey and arrested him. The jug and its contents were admitted into evidence.

Purswell challenged the warrantless arrest and search, arguing that the officers searched a private dwelling. The court held that the right to challenge an illegal search belongs personally to the owner or possessor of the searched premises, not to a guest. It further held that search-and-seizure protections do not apply to a person lawfully arrested and that officers may arrest without a warrant when a felony is committed in their presence. Because the officers testified that they observed Purswell transporting whiskey, the arrest and any contemporaneous search were supported by probable cause.

The court found no error in the jury instructions and affirmed the judgment. On rehearing, Purswell’s unsupported affidavit claimed that the jury penalized him for not testifying. Because no supporting evidence was produced and the evidence heard on the new-trial motion was not brought forward, the rehearing was overruled.

Dairylea Cooperative appealed an order denying its motion to quash a New York Attorney General’s subpoena for corporate records in a grand jury criminal investigation. The court held that Executive Law § 63(3) authorized the Attorney General to act upon requests from designated state officials and found that the Commissioner of Agriculture and Markets had made such a request. The order was affirmed without costs.

An internal email chain circulated a November 2001 Texas Monthly article, “How Enron Blew It,” examining Enron’s rise and decline. Under Ken Lay and Jeff Skilling, the former pipeline company became a dominant energy trader. Skilling’s Gas Bank enabled Enron to buy and sell natural gas, helping the company build and dominate markets. Enron expanded into electricity, broadband, bandwidth trading, and water while recruiting highly aggressive, talented employees and offering large performance-based rewards.

The article links Enron’s troubles partly to its internal culture, which emphasized risk, rapid profits, individual performance, and winning at any cost. Mark-to-market accounting, aggressive deal terms, forced employee rankings, internal competition, and constant pressure created an increasingly secretive and unstable workplace. Enron’s expansion also produced costly projects, including the Dabhol power plant in India and the Azurix water business.

Public criticism intensified during California’s energy crisis, while questions arose about Enron’s accounting and earnings. The collapse of the telecommunications market and broader economic weakness further hurt the company, whose stock fell sharply. Skilling resigned after six months as CEO, and Lay returned, promising a more focused business and changes to the Performance Review Committee. Skilling maintained that his interests were aligned with shareholders and remained optimistic about Enron’s technology and trading future.
Without voting, South Dakota’s Board of Regents directed officials to develop a plan to close the jointly operated Capital University Center in Pierre; the plan is due at the October 3–5 meeting.

Firefly Aerospace shares fell nearly 21% after its Alpha Flight 7 rocket exploded during a first-stage test flight at its Briggs, Texas facility. The company said safety protocols were followed, all personnel were safe, and no other facilities were affected. Firefly debuted on Nasdaq last month, raising $868 million at a $6.3 billion valuation, before its shares pulled back more than 50%. The company makes rockets, space tugs and lunar landers, including the Blue Ghost lander, which successfully landed on the moon earlier this year. Firefly plans to continue testing Alpha rockets, saying each test helps improve reliability.

The passage describes 3GPP LTE radio architecture, resource structures, carrier aggregation, semi-persistent scheduling, LTE Device-to-Device/Proximity Services, and vehicular V2X communication. Its main disclosure is an improved UE-autonomous (Mode 2) sidelink radio-resource allocation procedure for transmitting data, including periodic vehicular data such as CAM messages.

A transmitting device continuously performs resource sensing before data becomes available, monitoring scheduling assignments from other devices to identify reserved resources and optionally measuring received-signal energy. When data arrives, the device selects resources within a transmission window using information gathered during a preceding sensing window. Because sensing cannot occur while the half-duplex device is transmitting, transmission-window subframes are classified as primary or secondary: primary subframes have complete sensing information, while secondary subframes correspond to missed sensing opportunities. Resources in primary subframes are preferred over those in secondary subframes, with candidates ranked separately within each group. Shorter transmission delays and lower predicted energy are preferred, and the next-ranked candidate may be used if the highest-ranked one is unavailable.

The same selection principles apply to scheduling-assignment transmissions. Resource reservations for scheduling assignments may be implemented separately from or jointly with data reservations, and a scheduling assignment can indicate resources reserved for later scheduling-assignment or data transmissions. An optional preemption procedure permits selection of reserved resources when no candidates remain.

The passage presents the Arctic as a dynamic, interconnected security system shaped by environmental, geopolitical, economic, and sociocultural factors. Rapid climate change, shifting political interests, and emerging economic opportunities create cascading effects across these domains. The expansion of Nome port illustrates how decisions motivated by economic and national security priorities can produce environmental disruption, cultural tensions, geopolitical shifts, and operational challenges. Consequently, Arctic security requires holistic, interdisciplinary analysis rather than siloed approaches.

The passage defines systems thinking as identifying a system’s components, understanding their interactions and feedback loops, and recognizing patterns and long-term effects. It contrasts this approach with linear, reductionist methods that isolate problems and may produce unintended consequences. Key principles include seeing the whole system, recognizing connections and underlying structures, anticipating second- and third-order effects, and identifying leverage points where interventions can produce significant change.

The proposed Systems Thinking Education Model has three components: core principles, leverage points, and learning and assessment strategies. Leverage points include shifting mental models, improving information flows and data sharing, strengthening policy and governance structures, promoting behavioral and operational shifts, and integrating economic and technological advancements.

An integrated Arctic security curriculum should combine governance, climate science, military strategy, economics, security studies, and Indigenous knowledge systems. Instruction should emphasize active and experiential methods, including concept mapping, simulations, wargaming, role-playing, stakeholder exercises, interactive case studies, problem-based learning, and scenario-based modules. Assessments should evaluate applied systems-thinking skills through scenario-based problem-solving, reflective analysis and metacognition, and competency-based metrics addressing interdisciplinary analysis, strategic foresight, and adaptability.

The framework is presented as particularly suitable for online graduate education, where simulations, multimedia cases, discussion forums, concept-mapping tools, collaborative projects, reflective journals, and peer evaluations can support flexible, interdisciplinary learning. Overall, systems thinking is presented as a practical means of preparing Arctic security professionals to anticipate consequences, adapt strategies, collaborate across sectors, and develop sustainable, forward-looking security policies and operations.

On October 29, 2001, Moody’s downgraded Enron’s senior unsecured long-term debt from Baa1 to Baa2, two notches above junk, retained it on review for further downgrade and reviewed the company’s Prime-2 commercial-paper rating. Moody’s cited deteriorating financial flexibility, partnership-related write-downs and equity charges, weakened investor confidence and difficulty rolling over commercial paper. Enron sought additional bank credit after drawing roughly $3 billion–$3.3 billion from committed facilities to repurchase commercial paper; reports said it was seeking $1 billion–$2 billion. Its shares fell to multiyear lows, lost more than half their value in two weeks and shed over $14 billion in market capitalization, while Standard & Poor’s revised its outlook to negative.

Disclosures included a $1.2 billion reduction in shareholders’ equity and a $618 million third-quarter loss with $1.01 billion in write-offs. The SEC began examining related-party partnerships formerly managed by CFO Andrew Fastow, who was removed, citing possible conflicts of interest. Analysts described Enron’s use of backup bank lines as a sign of weakness and said new lenders were likely to demand higher rates, collateral and asset-sale terms. Enron was selling assets to raise cash.

European energy companies froze or restricted trading with Enron, citing credit concerns and potential need for letters of credit and collateral. Analysis questioned Enron’s asset-light model, noting reduced trading margins, the importance of credibility to energy trading and possible difficulty retaining staff as stock options lost value. At least five shareholder suits plus a separate board lawsuit challenged the partnership transactions, including possible bandwidth trades involving Fastow-managed partnerships.

Separately, Moody’s reported a broad deterioration in U.S. corporate credit, reviewing 122 companies for downgrade against 22 for upgrade in the third quarter and warning that $543 billion in debt could face downgrades.

Lorna Gibson introduces a course on cellular materials, beginning with Robert Hooke’s observations of cork and the relationship between material structure and properties. Cellular materials are porous, typically containing less than 30% solid by volume. The course distinguishes two-dimensional prismatic honeycombs, three-dimensional polyhedral foams, and three-dimensional lattice or truss materials.

Gibson outlines topics including mechanical modeling, deformation and failure, stiffness, strength, fracture, toughness, energy absorption, thermal insulation, sandwich panels, and the design and selection of cellular materials. Applications include lightweight structural cores, catalytic converters, food foams, orthopedic implant coatings, tissue-engineering scaffolds, and cellular materials found in nature, including wood, cork, bamboo, palms, bones, skulls, plant stems, quills, and sponges.

Medical examples include trabecular bone, osteoporosis, bone deformation observed through micro-CT imaging, and scaffolds designed to mimic the body’s extracellular matrix. Scaffold stiffness, cell attachment, cell contraction, and cell migration are discussed as areas of interest. Natural examples include wood and balsa failure through cell-wall buckling, cork’s corrugated cells and zero Poisson’s ratio, bamboo’s density gradient, and plant stems whose foam-like cores resist local buckling.

Student projects are open-ended but must concern cellular materials. Examples include negative-Poisson-ratio honeycombs, elephant-skull acoustics and vibration response, tissue-engineering scaffolds, and food foams such as bread or meringue.

Gibson then introduces processing methods. Honeycombs can be made by expansion, corrugation, ceramic extrusion, casting, rapid prototyping, selective laser scanning, and 3-D printing. Wood-derived carbon templates can also be used to create carbon or silicon-carbide structures with small cells for high-temperature filters or catalyst carriers. Polymer foams are produced by mechanically introducing bubbles or using physical and chemical blowing agents; their cell type depends on polymer viscosity and surface tension. Other forms include syntactic foams made from bonded hollow spheres and structural foams with stiff skins.

Metal-foam processes discussed include stirring gas into molten aluminum with silicon carbide, using titanium hydride to generate hydrogen, replicating polymer foams, vapor deposition, entrapped-gas expansion, bonding hollow metal spheres, and using leachable salt particles as a fugitive phase.

Gibson closes by briefly describing her civil-engineering education in Toronto, PhD work on cellular solids at Cambridge, employment in Calgary’s oil industry and at the University of British Columbia, and her move to MIT, first in civil engineering and later in materials science.

Goals occur more frequently during approximate five-minute periods: the start of each half, five minutes after a goal, saved or missed penalty, or dangerous play, before halftime, the match’s final five minutes, and near extra time’s start and end. Coaches should prepare players to exploit or guard against these periods. Factors include excitement, poor readiness, late-game urgency, and emotional reactions after goals. A key “letdown”—overconfidence after scoring or depression after conceding—can permit further goals. Coaches are advised to remind players, “No letdown!”

Q3 2025 municipal credit commentary says anticipated challenges have arrived amid the government shutdown. Munis remain a safe, flight-to-quality asset after the Fed cut short-term rates in September amid slowing job growth and mixed inflation. Many municipalities received upgrades for stronger reserves, though Q3 may mark a turn in muni credit quality. The passage also includes David Kotok’s biography and lists of related articles and municipal-bond ETFs.

Newcomers to Canada can prepare for job hunting by building networks before their search begins. Recommendations include searching job sites before arrival, using free newcomer career workshops for résumé help, skills-building and interview practice, and pursuing internships or volunteer work for experience. They should also identify required credential updates and improve English or French proficiency, recognizing that business skills differ from language knowledge.

Treetops, built in 1992 near Keynsham town centre, provides dementia accommodation for elderly people in three family-sized units, with communal areas, family involvement, named carers, and organised activities.

Trump’s comments that U.S.-Canada trade problems were less severe and required only tweaks eased concerns, pushing USD/CAD to 1.3060 and clearing the way for a test of 1.3000. Markets also awaited Yellen’s testimony, Chinese January CPI and PPI releases, and a Kuroda speech amid speculation about yield curve control.

During Supreme Court arguments on applying Delaware’s medical-malpractice filing requirements in federal court, Justices Kagan, Jackson, and Sotomayor questioned their compatibility with federal procedural rules. Attorney Frederick Yarger defended the state requirements, while Justice Gorsuch opposed selectively rewriting them. The argument did not clearly reveal a majority, though several justices appeared likely to reject the procedures.

An American Soccer Player’s Creed urges players to maintain ball awareness, communicate with teammates and coaches, move intelligently, create passing options, and play hard without reckless fouls. Players should avoid retaliation and dissent, learn from mistakes, understand the Laws of the Game, and demonstrate fair play and sportsmanship on and off the field.

The DAWN-PLASMA study was a randomized, open-label, phase 2 multicenter trial comparing standard of care plus convalescent plasma with standard of care alone in hospitalized adults with COVID-19. Participants were randomized 2:1 using a computerized system, while the trial statistician remained blinded until database lock. The primary endpoint was the percentage of patients alive without mechanical ventilation at Day 15. Secondary endpoints included clinical status at Days 15 and 30, time to sustained clinical improvement or discharge, mechanical ventilation or death at 30 and 90 days, thromboembolism, transfusion-related effects, antibody-titer correlations, safety, quality of life, adverse events, laboratory data, and vital signs. Exploratory assessments included SARS-CoV-2 PCR, NT50 measurements, and comparisons based on pre-existing COVID-19 antibodies.

Convalescent plasma was administered in four doses totaling 800–1,000 mL, with the first two units given within 12 hours of randomization and the next two 24–36 hours later. Plasma below a 1/160 neutralizing-antibody titer was prohibited; 1/160 plasma was permitted only during shortages.

Eligible participants were adults with confirmed SARS-CoV-2 infection and radiographic infiltrates or clinical findings including low oxygen saturation. Exclusions included prior or ongoing mechanical ventilation, serious safety hazards, severe allergic reactions to plasma, treatment restrictions excluding intubation, and recent anti-CD20 therapy. The study followed Declaration of Helsinki and ICH GCP principles, obtained ethics approval, and required informed consent. Five patients withdrew before intervention and one screen failure occurred; six replacements were randomized, with no patients lost to follow-up. Sponsor monitoring, centralized laboratory testing, and RedCap data capture were used; no quality audits were performed.

The paper examines how website usability affects customer experience in Saudi Arabia’s growing e-business market. It notes that successful online commerce requires strategic planning, suitable digital infrastructure, marketing, supply-chain and procurement systems, and customer-relationship management. Usability is defined as the ease with which users can achieve intended objectives effectively and efficiently, and poor usability can hinder customer acquisition, retention, and support. Saudi Arabia was selected as an emerging market, ranked 46th in the 2017 B2C e-commerce index, with 58% of residents reporting online shopping and online spending projected to reach $13.9 billion by 2021.

Previous studies across multiple sectors and countries linked usability with accessibility, trust, satisfaction, purchase intentions, service acceptance, and customer retention. They also identified language, culture, navigation, and design as important influences, while noting that findings from other regions cannot be generalized to Saudi Arabia.

The study used a cross-sectional evaluation involving 65 trained student evaluators divided into two cohorts. Group 1 assessed four retail sites—Namshi, Souq, Wadi, and Xcite—while Group 2 assessed four booking sites—Agoda, Booking.com, Hotels.com, and Altayyargroup. Participants used each site for 30 minutes and completed a validated online questionnaire with 50 Likert-scale questions covering navigation, design, and content. Data were analyzed in Excel, and Cronbach’s alpha values were 0.66 and 0.79 for the two groups.

Overall ratings were positive, but both cohorts showed similar weaknesses. Navigation problems included disappearing menu items, orphan pages, inaccurate sitemaps, and limited navigation within pages. Design concerns included inconsistent Arabic-English interfaces, inconsistent font sizes, layout simplicity, icon labeling, and menu highlighting. Content weaknesses included poor ordering, missing contact information, absent update dates, empty pages, and spelling, grammatical, and punctuation errors.

The study recommends stronger user and task analysis, participatory and user-centered design, user-appropriate IT strategies, and technical-writer involvement to improve portal content. It also calls for long-term quantitative studies of how usability improvements affect customer behavior. The small sample and limited number of websites restrict generalizability, while qualitative follow-up research is proposed to examine user feedback and revised portals more deeply.

Blair school district voters failed to approve a $250,000 transportation bond issue, 111–80 (58.76%), below the 60% super-majority required. The proposal would buy three 72-passenger buses—two route and one activity bus—to replace leased vehicles. Other area municipal and school board results were also reported.
