Bank of Canada senior deputy governor Carolyn Wilkins expects household debt relative to disposable income to gradually decline and stabilize as credit growth slows and labour income rises. The ratio reached 170.4% in late 2017, just below its peak, but unwinding the long buildup will take time. She noted that asset purchases have increased net worth. Governor Stephen Poloz said high debt makes households 50% more sensitive to interest-rate changes.
The team is focused on battling to the net and getting pucks and shots past a large goalie. After two days off and a disappointing loss, they practiced, regrouped, and aim to score first tonight.

In a 1980 interview, Ronald Reagan questioned whether the President’s comments about the failed Iran mission signaled abandonment. He said Soviet influence persisted through Iranian communism and propaganda but expressed uncertainty about Khomeini’s position. If Iran moved closer to the Soviet camp, Reagan called it one of the gravest threats to the Middle East and U.S. security.

In his Republican presidential acceptance speech, Reagan made protection against hostile foreign powers his top priority. He said America sought peace and used force only when necessary, but must remain strong, negotiate in good faith, and prevent enemies of freedom from dictating the world’s future.

In a later address, he told those who had known war that peace requires defense preparedness, rejecting the claim that strength invites war. He cited Will Rogers: “I’ve never seen anyone insult Jack Dempsey.”

Successful basketball press breaks depend on preparation, teamwork, precise execution, and sound fundamentals. Offenses should spread the floor, bypass defenders, use sharp short passes, work the ball through the middle, create leads, and employ a slow-to-quick tempo. Players should dribble sparingly, avoid passing off the dribble, use jump stops, and “eat the ball” rather than make an unsafe pass. Receivers should use a triple-threat stance with their backs to the sideline, while long passes should lead teammates toward the elbow.

Teams should advance the ball with all five players using formations such as the 2-1-2 rather than relying on set plays or one point guard. Outlet passes should follow a long-short-middle sequence, and trailers must maintain defensive balance. Players should practice attacking 2-on-1 and 3-on-2 situations, and inbouncers should reverse the ball after a double team to create a 4-on-3 advantage. Coaches must analyze the press, exploit weaknesses, emphasize good shot selection and offensive rebounding, and prepare players to break presses after made field goals or free throws.

Implementation should use designated roles, pregame coaching, and the “Whole-Part-Whole” teaching method: demonstrate and walk through concepts, use progressive breakdown drills, then practice at game speed against strong defense. Teams should scout opponents, anticipate defensive adjustments, play disruptive defense, and transition directly from pushing the ball into early offense.

The study demonstrates selective, coherent control of the three nearest-neighbor \(^{15}\mathrm{N}\) nuclear spins surrounding a negatively charged boron vacancy (\(\mathrm{V_B^-}\)) in isotopically enriched h\(^{10}\)B\(^{15}\)N. Pulsed electron–nuclear double resonance and ODMR measurements at 212 mT resolved a four-peak electron hyperfine structure and enabled initialization and readout of individual four-spin hyperfine states. Three nuclear transitions (\(\alpha,\beta,\gamma\)) were observed with linewidths as narrow as 1.2 MHz. Their inequivalence and magnetic-field dependence, including transition shifts and splitting near the ground-state level avoided crossing, were attributed to electron–nuclear state mixing from the perpendicular hyperfine coupling.

Rabi measurements showed that hyperfine mixing enhances the effective nuclear g-factor and accelerates nuclear-spin driving by approximately 116-fold relative to an isolated \(^{15}\mathrm{N}\) spin. The nuclear Rabi coherence time was about 12 μs, exceeding the electron-spin coherence time, while a fitted Rabi frequency varied linearly with RF amplitude. Optical repumping caused rapid nuclear depolarization, thermalizing the nuclear-spin population within roughly 1 μs.

Experiments and numerical simulations indicate that the strongly coupled nuclear spins could support nuclear-assisted dynamics, quantum memories, and enhanced quantum-sensing sensitivity. The h\(^{10}\)B\(^{15}\)N crystals were grown by the APHT method, exfoliated, transferred onto a coplanar waveguide, and implanted with 2 keV He ions to create the defect ensemble. All optical and microwave measurements were performed under ambient conditions.

The Pennsylvania Supreme Court affirmed the Commonwealth Court's ruling that the Nonpublic Elementary and Secondary Education Act (Act 109) is constitutional and enforceable as applied to nonsectarian nonpublic schools, rejecting the Department of Education's appeal. The court held that Lemon v. Kurtzman invalidated Act 109 only as applied to sectarian schools, leaving its validity for nonsectarian schools undecided; that Act 109 is severable, supported by the state's general presumption favoring severability, the statute's own severability clause, and its stated purpose of enhancing secular education; that Act 109 was not impliedly repealed by later statutes such as Acts 89, 90, and 195, which do not cover the entire subject matter of Act 109; and that requiring the Department to determine whether a school is sectarian or nonsectarian creates only minimal, constitutionally permissible entanglement, comparable to tax-exempt status determinations. Justice Eagen dissented.

With Jake Browning struggling, former Bengals starter Andy Dalton has been floated as an outside option. The mostly backup Panthers quarterback, signed through 2026, started 13 games for Cincinnati coach Zac Taylor in 2019; a trade would give the Bengals about $3 million in cap space.

Tesla, Inc.’s Form 10-Q for the quarter ended March 31, 2018 presents unaudited financial statements and notes for its automotive and energy generation and storage segments. Total revenue was $3.409 billion, compared with $2.696 billion a year earlier, including automotive revenue of $2.735 billion, energy generation and storage revenue of $410.0 million, and services and other revenue of $263.4 million. Gross profit declined to $456.5 million from $667.9 million, the operating loss widened to $597.0 million from $257.5 million, and the net loss attributable to common stockholders was $709.6 million, or $4.19 per share, compared with $330.3 million, or $2.04 per share.

At March 31, 2018, Tesla reported $27.27 billion of assets, $21.55 billion of liabilities, and $4.45 billion of stockholders’ equity. Cash and cash equivalents were $2.67 billion. During the quarter, operations used $398.4 million of cash, investing activities used $728.6 million, and financing activities provided $371.7 million. Ending cash, cash equivalents and restricted cash totaled $3.22 billion.

Tesla adopted ASC 606, Revenue from Contracts with Customers, on January 1, 2018, using the modified retrospective method and without restating prior periods. The adoption reduced opening accumulated deficit by $623.2 million. Certain vehicle sales with resale value guarantees are now treated as sales with a right of return rather than operating leases or collateralized borrowings, requiring corresponding changes to lease assets, deferred revenue, guarantees, customer deposits and warranty liabilities. Relative to results without the new standard, first-quarter automotive sales revenue was $299.0 million higher, automotive leasing revenue was $164.9 million lower, and net loss was $36.3 million lower.

Automotive sales revenue is generally recognized upon delivery, while connectivity, Supercharger access and over-the-air updates are recognized over specified service periods. Direct vehicle leases and two resale-guarantee programs remain accounted for as operating leases. Energy sales are recognized upon installation or delivery, or over time using percentage-of-completion for certain large projects; monitoring and maintenance services are recognized over their service periods.

At March 31, 2018, inventory was $2.57 billion, solar energy systems leased and to be leased were $6.35 billion, and property, plant and equipment was $10.52 billion. Goodwill was $61.3 million, and acquired SolarCity in-process research and development was $86.8 million, with its research expected to be completed in the second quarter of 2018, though commercial feasibility was not assured.

Total debt principal was $10.47 billion, consisting of $1.76 billion current and $8.22 billion long-term, and Tesla was in compliance with its debt covenants. During the quarter, Tesla issued $546.1 million of automotive asset-backed notes and repaid $453.6 million under warehouse agreements. Tesla also expected the 2019 adoption of the lease accounting standard to materially affect its financial statements, while it did not anticipate material effects from additional adjustments related to the 2017 Tax Act.

Stockholders approved a March 2018 CEO performance award of 20,264,042 stock options with 12 market-capitalization and operational-milestone vesting tranches. First-quarter stock-based compensation for the award was $6.7 million. The CEO’s base salary reflected California minimum-wage requirements, but he did not accept it.

LCP socket base and cover (UL 94 V-0): black base, natural/ivory cover, cover thickness ≤1.17 mm including 0.30 mm pocket recess, flatness <0.25 mm before and after SMT reflow and after environmental/mechanical testing. A removable tape or plastic overlay covers pin holes for vacuum pick-and-place; it must not outgas during reflow or leave residue. Markings include molded "SOCKET 940," a locked/unlocked designator, a triangular pin A01 orientation symbol, and the supplier's UL symbol; lot traceability may be ink, laser, or impact marked. Contacts are high-strength copper alloy with ≥1.27 µm nickel plating and ≥0.76 µm gold over nickel in mating areas; no lubricants on mating surfaces. SMT mounting uses 63/37 ±5% tin/lead solder balls (0.76 mm) on 0.64 mm pads, requiring a solder barrier and 0.20 mm coplanarity. A stainless steel lever right of the cam box actuates contacts: insertion/extraction ≤2 kgf open, extraction ≥0.013 kgf per pin closed, lever force <3.6 kgf, pin displacement <1.0 mm, and integrity maintained after 50 actuations. Inspection rejects missing, damaged, or misaligned balls, contacts, plating, tabs, latch, or lever, and cracks, flashing, or gaps. Electrical requirements: 1.5 A per contact with <30°C rise; initial and final LLCR ≤25 mΩ over 200 daisy-chained pairs per sample; self-inductance <4 nH; loop inductance 3 nH ±10%; capacitance <1 pF; differential impedance 100 Ω ±10%; delay skew <10 ps; ≥650 Vac dielectric withstand; ≥1000 MΩ insulation resistance.

Tesla Motors, Inc. filed an unaudited Form 10-Q for the quarter ended June 30, 2016. Quarterly revenue was $1.270 billion, including $1.182 billion from automotive sales and $88.2 million from services and other activities, compared with $955.0 million a year earlier. Gross profit was $274.8 million, representing a 21.6% margin versus 22.3% in 2015. The company reported an operating loss of $238.0 million, a net loss of $293.2 million, or $2.09 per share, and a comprehensive loss of $272.6 million. For the six months ended June 30, revenue was $2.417 billion, gross profit was $527.2 million, and net loss was $575.5 million, or $4.22 per share.

At June 30, 2016, Tesla reported $3.246 billion of cash and cash equivalents, $11.869 billion of total assets, $9.312 billion of liabilities, and $2.520 billion of stockholders’ equity. Inventory was $1.610 billion, operating lease vehicles were $2.534 billion, and property, plant and equipment was $3.993 billion. During the first six months, operating activities used $99.3 million of cash and investing activities used $553.7 million, while financing activities provided $2.692 billion, largely from a May common-stock offering that raised approximately $1.7 billion net and $1.108 billion of debt proceeds. Net cash increased by $2.049 billion.

Tesla designs, manufactures and sells electric vehicles and energy products. It was producing the Model S and Model X, continued ramping Model X production despite supplier shortages, and unveiled the lower-priced Model 3 in the first quarter of 2016. It produced 18,345 vehicles in the second quarter, including approximately 6,200 Model X vehicles. Management planned approximately 50,000 deliveries in the second half of 2016, Model 3 volume production and deliveries in late 2017, and total vehicle production of 500,000 units in 2018. Expected 2016 capital expenditures were approximately $2.25 billion, and operating expenses were expected to increase about 30% from 2015.

The company was expanding its sales, service and charging infrastructure, including more than 60 planned additional locations in 2016, bringing the total to nearly 280. Its 661-location Supercharger network was expected to grow by more than 40% during 2016. Tesla was also constructing the Gigafactory, expected to begin cell production in the fourth quarter of 2016. Panasonic agreed to invest in production equipment there, and Tesla planned to purchase the full output of that equipment at negotiated prices.

Financial statements and notes addressed revenue recognition, resale value guarantees, vehicle leasing, warranties, inventory valuation, stock compensation, foreign-currency hedges, income taxes, fair value, property and equipment, customer deposits, debt and equity incentives. The 2018 convertible notes were classified as current, while the 2019 and 2021 notes remained long-term. Tesla had $678.0 million outstanding under its $1.0 billion asset-based credit facility at June 30 and repaid that amount in July.

On July 31, 2016, Tesla entered into a definitive agreement to acquire SolarCity, under which each SolarCity share would convert into 0.110 Tesla shares, subject to stockholder and regulatory approvals. Subsequent to quarter-end, Tesla received conversion notices for approximately $411 million principal of its 2018 notes and expected to pay that amount during the third quarter.

Risks and uncertainties included Model X production and supplier constraints, the scale and cost of the Gigafactory and Model 3 expansion, international expansion, customer demand, margins, residual values, financing availability and competition. A 2013 securities class action dismissed by the trial court remained pending on appeal, and Tesla also disclosed periodic regulatory information requests. Tesla reported 148,692,605 common shares outstanding as of July 29, 2016.

The U.S. Department of State’s Office of the Historian produced this May 2018 electronic edition of *Papers Relating to the Foreign Relations of the United States, 1906, Part I*. It preserves the printed edition’s full content, supports search, bookmarking and note-taking, and can be accessed offline. Because ebook page numbering may differ, readers are advised to cite document numbers.

The included presidential message describes unprecedented national prosperity that could be harmed by reckless speculation and disregard for legitimate business methods. It urges Congress to complete unfinished business, including prohibiting corporations from contributing to political campaigns or other political purposes while allowing individual contributions. It also strongly recommends granting the government the right to appeal criminal cases involving questions of law. The message cites conflicting lower-court rulings in rebate-related conspiracy cases and argues that without appellate review, justice may be obstructed, particularly in cases involving wealthy defendants or wage workers.

The ADS868xW uses independently adjustable AVDD and DVDD supplies: AVDD powers internal analog circuits, while DVDD powers the digital interface. Decoupling is recommended with minimum 10 µF and 1 µF capacitors for AVDD, placing the 1 µF capacitor close to the supply pins, and a minimum 10 µF capacitor close to DVDD to suppress high-frequency digital switching current. These capacitors improve power-supply rejection ratio.

For reduced power consumption at lower throughput, the device supports two programmable modes. NAP mode is enabled by unlocking RST_PWRCTL_REG at address 05h with 69h and setting NAP_EN to 1b. The device enters NAP when CONVST/CS remains high after conversion and exits on its falling edge; a new conversion must wait until tNAP_WKUP has elapsed. Power-down mode is enabled by setting PWRDN to 1b, causing entry on the rising edge of CONVST/CS. In PD mode, analog blocks are powered down, but the interface remains active and register contents are retained. Clearing PWRDN initiates recovery, after which the host must wait tPWRUP before starting another conversion.

Recommended PCB layout separates analog and digital signals, with analog and reference routing on the lower board side and digital routing on the top. Clean supply bypassing is specified, including 1 µF X7R 0603 capacitors rated at least 10 V near AVDD and DVDD, short low-impedance ground paths, and no vias between supply pins and bypass capacitors. REFCAP requires 1 µF 0603 and 10 µF 0805 ceramic capacitors, with the latter having ESR below 0.2 Ω and both connected without intervening vias. REFIO requires at least 4.7 µF when the internal reference is used.

TI also provides documentation-update notifications, E2E support forums, and ESD handling guidance. The revision history notes that ADS8685W and ADS8689W changed from Advance Information to Production Data in May 2025.

Clemson beat North Carolina 38–10 as Bill Belichick took responsibility for three illegal formations and defensive lapses. He blamed poor passing and third-down execution for the loss but praised his team’s fight and commitment to improving.

Russia continues to deny responsibility for the poisoning of Sergei Skripal and his daughter Yulia, while its EU ambassador suggested Britain’s Porton Down facility might be involved. British officials said they had evidence that Russia violated the Chemical Weapons Convention, used nerve agents on British soil and produced and stockpiled Novichok. Putin offered cooperation, claiming Russia destroyed its chemical weapons in 1992. The passage calls for stronger sanctions and tighter laws to identify hidden Russian assets and close money-laundering loopholes.

The paper introduces a periodically modulated coupled SSH-chain platform for generating non-Abelian quantum interference and entanglement through braiding topological edge states. Time-independent inversion symmetry protects parity and adiabatic evolution of parity-distinct states, while time-dependent interchain symmetry supports multiple edge-state branches and protects their evolution at sufficiently slow driving.

In double-coupled SSH chains, four edge states form two branches whose eigenvalues and positions swap between chains after one period. Adiabatic transport transfers a particle from one end of one chain to the two ends of another, with the final 0–1 partition controlled by the accumulated relative dynamical phase; reported fidelity reaches 0.998.

Triple-coupled chains contain six edge states in three branches that undergo cyclic, order-dependent braiding. Different braid sequences, including \(\tau_1^{-1}\tau_2^{-1}\) and \(\tau_2^{-1}\tau_1^{-1}\), transfer particles to different chains, demonstrating non-Abelian topological transport. For two bosons injected at opposite ends of one chain, non-Abelian Hong–Ou–Mandel interference produces spatial two-particle NOON states on either of two destination chains depending on braid order. At a 50:50 partition, these entangled states achieve reported fidelity 0.995. The protocol can extend to bulk states, and adiabatically modulated photonic waveguide arrays are identified as a possible experimental platform.

Since becoming chief executive in 2015, Russell Down has transformed Speedy by emphasizing customers, controlling operating costs, improving equipment availability and asset utilization, and changing an inward-looking culture. Six-month profits rose 58.8% to £10.8m, while net debt and return on capital employed improved. Earlier problems included unreliable IT asset data, declining attention to smaller customers, and a cost-saving decision to centralize equipment testing that created backlogs and left more than half of products unavailable in September 2015.

Down introduced customer and staff surveys, rebuilt stakeholder engagement and renewed staff commitment to the company’s “Speedy spirit.” Speedy has since acquired powered-access businesses Prolift Access Limited and Platform Sales & Hire Limited, expanding its fleet and product reach. The company expects revenue and cost synergies from the acquisitions and says it is financially positioned for sustainable, profitable growth.

Nevada’s new weighted funding formula provides $1,200 per eligible low-performing student who is learning English or living in poverty and attends a school not already receiving Zoom or Victory funding. Of the state’s $36 million allocation, Clark County schools received more than $34 million and will decide locally how to spend it. Garside Junior High received over $450,000 for its 378 eligible students. Teacher Kimberly Ivanick plans to expand after-school tutoring and provide technology to accelerate English learning. Spending will remain in a separate budget category, with student-achievement outcomes analyzed to determine its impact.

Cornell University researchers are investigating bovine mammary stem cell secretions as potential alternatives or complements to antibiotics for treating mastitis in dairy cows. Each clinical case can cost farmers more than $400, while bacterial inflammation permanently damages mammary tissue and reduces milk production even after bacteria are eliminated. In a March 16 paper in Scientific Reports, Gerlinde Van de Walle and Daryl Nydam reported for the first time on the bovine mammary stem cell secretome. Its secreted factors promoted new blood vessel formation and cell migration, protected epithelial cells from bacterial toxins, and included antimicrobial peptides effective against bacteria, particularly gram-negative bacteria. The researchers plan to test the therapy in cows with mastitis.

Hyundai Motor and Kia Motors set up a V2X communication system on a 14-kilometer Hwaseong road with seven intersections. Designed to exchange real-time information with infrastructure, cars, and pedestrians, the system will be tested and improved ahead of a planned 2020 highway vehicle-to-vehicle project.

The President transmitted to the Senate a February 14, 1893 annexation treaty signed by U.S. Secretary of State John W. Foster and Hawaiian commissioners, requesting ratification. The treaty leaves annexation-related questions for future U.S. adjustment. The administration maintained that it had supported Hawaiian independence while protecting property and stability, and had not promoted the monarchy’s overthrow, which it attributed to Queen Liliuokalani’s policies and a weak government. It considered restoration undesirable or impossible and advocated annexation over a protectorate as best serving Hawaiian and U.S. interests and preventing another power’s control. With no foreign protests reported, the President urged prompt approval; existing laws would continue until Congress established a permanent government respectful of residents’ rights.

Caitlin Bassett and Sunshine Coast Lightning face Greater Western Sydney in Saturday’s Super Netball grand final following an intense two-week buildup. Bassett, who has never played in a national grand final, has drawn on Geva Mentor and Laura Langman’s experience. Mentor faces the Giants’ dangerous attack, including 190cm shooter Kristina Brice and a moving circle.

The Relative Strength Index (RSI) is an oscillator developed by Welles Wilder and introduced in *Commodities* in June 1978. It measures the magnitude of gains and losses over a chosen number of days and ranges from 0 to 100. RSI is calculated as:

RSI = 100 – (100 / (1 + RS))

where RS is the ratio of average up closes to average down closes over the selected period. Most charting and trading platforms include RSI.

The passage reports extensive backtesting indicating that RSI works reasonably well on stocks and stock indices, particularly mean-reverting and less volatile securities, but it requires filters, additional criteria, or another indicator to function effectively as a strategy. Short lookback periods of roughly two to six days are generally favored for stocks, while daily bars are described as the best overall timeframe. Thresholds depend on the period, market, trend, and desired responsiveness; shorter periods require more extreme thresholds such as 15 and 85.

In a 1993–2020 S&P 500 backtest, a two-day RSI strategy bought below 15 and sold above 85. It performed slightly worse than buy-and-hold, but was invested only 42% of the time and had a 33% drawdown versus 55% for buy-and-hold. A $100,000 investment compounded to $861,000, although commissions, slippage, and taxes were excluded. A ten-day strategy with 30 and 70 thresholds produced about half the result. Combining a 30-day RSI above 50 with a two-day RSI below 15 also performed worse than the single-RSI strategy and reduced market exposure from 42% to 27%.

A QQQ backtest of simple RSI rules produced about 300 trades, a 71% win rate, an average gain of 0.82% per trade, and a 23% maximum drawdown. RSI reportedly performs less well on other assets and poorly in forex; commodity-related stocks such as miners, oil, and coal have not worked well with mean-reverting strategies.

RSI is commonly used to identify overbought and oversold conditions, generate reversal or momentum signals, and assess divergence from price. However, the passage says divergence is recognized only in hindsight, is difficult to quantify, and has little practical value for traders. RSI is recommended for use with other tools, such as volume, relative performance, trend measures, or the Internal Bar Strength indicator.

Variants include Connors RSI and Cutler’s RSI, with the latter replacing Wilder’s smoothed moving average with a simple moving average. RSI 14 reacts faster and produces more signals, while RSI 21 is smoother and better suited to longer-term analysis. RSI can also serve as a momentum indicator with quantified rules, although the cited momentum strategy failed on stocks and worked on crypto.

The passage presents a progression for teaching offensive corner kicks in soccer. A corner kick is awarded when the defending team puts the ball completely over its own end line, whether on the ground or in the air. Coaches should explain Law 17, demonstrate proper technique, teach both right- and left-footed options from both corners, introduce a set play, rotate players through positions, and then assign specific roles.

During instruction, coaches should show that players cannot handle the ball, must keep play active until the ball fully crosses the line, and should place the ball in the correct corner arc. Defenders must remain at least 10 yards away until the kick is taken, the corner taker cannot touch the ball again until another player does, and the corner marker must remain in place. The proper run-up follows a roughly 45-degree path into the field, followed by an instep-driven kick.

The basic corner-kick play has three positions: corner taker, receiver, and cover man. The receiver starts five yards into the field, while the cover man starts five yards from the corner arc, just inside the end line. The corner is kicked to the receiver, who turns toward goal, while the other players move deeper for a possible pass. Players should practice every position before specific assignments are made. Coaches can later add passive and active defenders, passing variations, offside instruction, additional plays, and longer lofted kicks. Corner takers must wait for the referee’s acknowledgment before taking the kick.

The passage criticizes commentary portraying the Supreme Court’s religious-freedom docket as partisan, majoritarian, or dominated by conservative “culture wars.” It argues that many such rulings have been unanimous or nearly so and have protected diverse religious minorities, including Jehovah’s Witnesses, Seventh-day Adventists, Native Americans, Sikhs, Santeria, Latter-day Saints, and prisoners.

The central case is *Landor v. Louisiana Department of Corrections and Public Safety*. Rastafarian prisoner Damon Landor was forcibly shaved by Louisiana officials after his dreadlocks had previously been accommodated, in violation of the Religious Land Use and Institutionalized Persons Act. A lower court ruled that the statute does not permit money damages, but the Supreme Court agreed to review the issue. The author argues that Landor should win because the lower court’s narrow reading would leave deliberate violations without meaningful relief and undermine the statute’s purpose.

More broadly, the passage contends that religious-freedom claims often involve practical accommodations—such as prison food, head coverings, or religious clothing—rather than cultural or political conflicts, and that *Landor* illustrates religious freedom as a foundational right belonging to everyone.
San Diego police pursued a shooting suspect in City Heights; the suspect crashed through school and fire station fences, fled while armed, and was arrested near 41st Street and University Avenue.

A retrospective analytical study examined traumatic brain injury (TBI) among 671 patients treated at Republic Hospital from July 2017 to December 2018: 459 were men and 212 women. The mean patient age was 46.016 years, ranging from 15 to 92. Statistical analyses included t-tests, one- and two-way ANOVA, and Pearson correlation.

Domestic accidents were the most frequently reported TBI cause (294 patients, 43.81%), followed by alcohol-related brain injury (139, 20.71%), motor-vehicle injury (111, 16.54%), and criminal injury (75, 11.17%). Domestic accidents were also the leading cause in both sexes. Most patients received conservative treatment, while 198 underwent surgery, most commonly wound debridement.

Village residents had a higher reported risk of TBI than city residents (p<0.002). Men developed TBI at younger ages than women (mean ages 44.41 and 49.50 years; p<0.0004) and had longer hospitalization durations (p<0.024). Hospitalization duration was positively associated with age in both sexes. Alcohol consumption was identified as a major risk factor. The authors concluded that domestic accidents, residence in rural areas, age, and sex were important factors associated with TBI occurrence, hospitalization, severity, and post-TBI outcomes. A major limitation was the absence of a control group for comparing incidence between men and women.

The passage surveys U.S. foreign-policy administration in 1945, citing Truman statements on China policy, national defense, and displaced persons. Edward Stettinius resigned as secretary of state and became U.S. representative to the United Nations; James F. Byrnes succeeded him. Joseph C. Grew was replaced as under secretary by Dean Acheson. Patrick J. Hurley resigned as ambassador to China, and George C. Marshall was appointed Truman’s personal envoy. Cordell Hull received the Nobel Peace Prize.

The Department of State also assumed expanded postwar responsibilities. Executive Order 9608 transferred international information functions from the Office of War Information and foreign information functions from the Office of Inter-American Affairs to the State Department. Executive Order 9621 transferred the OSS Research and Analysis and Presentation branches to State, while the OSS’s remaining activities went to the War Department. Truman directed State to lead development of a coordinated foreign-intelligence program through an interdepartmental group. The passage also notes recruitment of Foreign Service officers from the armed forces and provides references on the department’s organization, foreign interests, and postwar role.

Blackwell introduces advanced power gating, accelerated frequency switching, and low-latency sleep. Clock trees, including the entire GDDR7 memory clock tree, can be shut down quickly, while separate voltage rails independently power the GPU cores and memory, support frame-granularity shutdowns, and reduce leakage. Clocks adapt to workloads up to 1,000 times faster than on previous GPU architectures, and the deepest sleep state is entered 10 times faster than on Ada. In small-language-model inference, these features can reduce power consumption by up to 50%.

DLSS 4 adds Multi Frame Generation, capable of producing up to three additional frames per traditionally rendered frame. Its AI model is 40% faster than the previous method, uses 30% less VRAM, and runs once per rendered frame. AI-generated optical flow and Blackwell’s enhanced Flip Metering improve frame pacing, while the display engine has twice the pixel-processing capacity.

DLSS 4 replaces CNN-based models with transformer models for Super Resolution, Ray Reconstruction, and Deep Learning Anti-Aliasing. The transformers can process twice as many parameters and use self-attention to identify long-range patterns. Super Resolution gains temporal stability, reduced ghosting, and better detail in motion; Ray Reconstruction reduces denoiser artifacts, particularly under challenging lighting; and DLAA uses Super Resolution technology to produce more stable, detailed native-resolution images.

Blackwell also supports neural shaders that use AI to approximate complex rendering algorithms. The Cooperative Vectors API for DirectX 12 and Vulkan, combined with Slang, allows graphics shaders to access Tensor Cores and neural techniques. Potential applications include up-to-seven-to-one neural texture compression, RTX Neural Materials, Neural Radiance Cache, RTX Skin, and RTX Neural Faces. Neural Materials approximate complex optical materials; Neural Texture Compression reduces memory demands; Stochastic Texture Filtering improves sampling quality; Neural Radiance Cache estimates indirect lighting from limited traced rays and learns from live game data; RTX Skin provides ray-traced subsurface scattering; and Neural Faces uses real-time generative AI to infer realistic faces from rasterized geometry and pose data.

The GPU family includes the flagship GB202, with 92.2 billion transistors, 192 streaming multiprocessors, 24,576 CUDA cores, 192 RT cores, 768 Tensor cores, and a 512-bit memory interface. The GB203 has 45.6 billion transistors, 84 streaming multiprocessors, 10,752 CUDA cores, 84 RT cores, 336 Tensor cores, and a 256-bit interface. The 31-billion-transistor GB205 has 50 streaming multiprocessors, 6,400 CUDA cores, 50 RT cores, 200 Tensor cores, and a 192-bit interface. The RTX 5090, RTX 5080, RTX 5070 Ti, and RTX 5070 are based on GB202, GB203, GB203, and GB205, respectively.

Sodium cumenesulfonate is a water-soluble hydrotrope available in powder and liquid forms. It improves the solubility of poorly soluble organic matter, lowers cloud points, promotes ingredient compatibility, and moderates viscosity. Uses include cleaners, drilling fluids, laundry products, powdered detergents, metal processing, and hydrogen sulfide scavengers. Raw-material price volatility and declining R&D may constrain the market, while industrialization and household detergent use in emerging economies may boost demand. Liquid and household segments dominated in 2015 and are expected to remain dominant; industrial and institutional applications may grow moderately. Heavy exposure may cause eye and respiratory irritation.

U.S. stocks fell about 2% Monday, with the Dow down nearly 400 points, as Facebook dropped 7.1% after reports that a Trump campaign consultancy improperly accessed data from more than 50 million users. Major indexes and tech shares declined amid data-privacy concerns, trade-war worries and uncertainty ahead of a Federal Reserve rate decision. All 11 S&P sectors were lower.

Frost Brown Todd and Gibbons plan to merge in January, forming a firm named FBT Gibbons with 800 lawyers across 25 offices. Frost Brown Todd currently has more than 650 lawyers in 18 offices, and the merger adds Northeast offices, including New York and New Jersey. Firm leaders say the initial focus is integration, while also noting they are looking at other parts of the country for further growth. Robert Sartin will be chairman of the merged firm, and Adam Hall of Frost Brown Todd and Peter Torcicollo of Gibbons will be co-managing partners. Frost Brown Todd, ranked No. 128, had $336.5 million in gross revenue versus Gibbons' $115 million; both had similar profits per lawyer, though Gibbons had higher revenue per lawyer. Discussions began after Sartin met Gibbons leaders at a retreat hosted by the Zeughauser Group.

Stephen Hawking, the theoretical physicist and author of the international bestseller “A Brief History of Time,” died after living for more than 50 years with ALS, which left him reliant on an electronic voice synthesizer. His children called him a great scientist and extraordinary man. At Cambridge, he pursued a unified theory reconciling relativity and quantum mechanics, later questioning whether such a theory could exist. He continued writing and became a prominent science celebrity through television appearances and public attention. The 2014 film “The Theory of Everything,” starring Eddie Redmayne, brought him further recognition and was credited with renewing interest in science.

An earlier proposed treaty providing larger annuities and admitting the Hawaiian Kingdom as a state failed after King Kamehameha III died and his successor opposed it. A reciprocity treaty concluded in 1855 also failed to obtain ratification. Renewed consideration was deferred during the Civil War.

In 1867, Minister McCook and Hawaiian representative C. C. Harris concluded a San Francisco reciprocity treaty on terms more favorable to the United States. Secretary Seward authorized McCook to explore annexation and declared that annexation should take precedence if it conflicted with reciprocity. The presence of the U.S.S. Lackawanna heightened royal apprehension and delayed legislative consideration, but Hawaii ratified the treaty on July 30, 1867. The U.S. Senate ultimately rejected it on June 1, 1870.

In his inaugural address, President Buchanan affirmed his intention to serve without seeking reelection and urged acceptance of the slavery issue through popular sovereignty and judicial resolution of disputes over territorial self-government. He warned that continued agitation threatened both North and South and endangered the Union, while praising national cooperation and free trade. He also addressed the surplus in the Treasury, advocating its use to reduce the public debt, strengthen the navy, and defend the coasts; supported tariff reform while protecting domestic manufactures; condemned the wasteful distribution of public lands; and advocated reserving land for actual settlers at moderate prices. Buchanan interpreted the Constitution as granting Congress limited powers, yet defended federal construction of military roads when necessary to defend the states. In foreign affairs, he called for peaceful commerce, friendship, independence, and justice among nations, opposition to territorial expansion through conquest, and continued adherence to American constitutional principles.

Apple Inc. entered an underwriting agreement with Goldman, Sachs & Co., Deutsche Bank Securities Inc., J.P. Morgan Securities LLC, and Merrill Lynch, Pierce, Fenner & Smith Incorporated for nine series of notes: $500 million each of floating-rate notes due 2019 and 2021; $500 million of 1.300% notes due 2018; $1 billion of 1.700% notes due 2019; $2.25 billion of 2.250% notes due 2021; $1.5 billion of 2.850% notes due 2023; $2 billion of 3.250% notes due 2026; $1.25 billion of 4.500% notes due 2036; and $2.5 billion of 4.650% notes due 2046. The notes were issued under Apple’s 2013 indenture. Floating-rate note interest is payable quarterly, while fixed-rate note interest is payable semiannually. The notes are senior unsecured obligations ranking equally with Apple’s other unsecured and unsubordinated debt. Apple furnished the underwriting agreement, officer’s certificate and note forms, a legal opinion, and its ratio of earnings to fixed charges as exhibits.

Synaptics announced plans to mass-produce Clear ID, an optical fingerprint sensor for embedding beneath smartphone displays. The company says it unlocks devices with one touch, works from any angle, and is twice as fast as 3D facial recognition. Its use on future phones remains uncertain.
Bemidji beat Thief River Falls 77-45 after a 45-25 halftime lead. Caden Rolfes led four double-digit scorers with 18 points; Linaes Whiting added 17, Caleb Carlson 14, and Jeremy Beberg 10.

The passage examines container patterns for modular, reusable systems. The sidecar pattern augments an application container, requiring a stable API because parameter names, value formats, units, and other interface changes can break consumers. Containers should be documented in their Dockerfiles through comments, `EXPOSE`, `ENV`, and standardized `LABEL` metadata.

The ambassador pattern separates an application from external interactions. Examples include routing requests to appropriate shards, discovering environment-specific services, and splitting production and experimental traffic. Reusable ambassadors can standardize these functions across applications.

The adapter pattern converts heterogeneous application interfaces into consistent interfaces for monitoring, logging, and health checks. Separate adapters can expose Prometheus metrics, normalize logs through Fluentd, or provide rich MySQL health checks without modifying third-party application images, improving reuse, isolation, and maintainability.

The passage then introduces microservices as multi-node architectures composed of components communicating through APIs. Their benefits include team independence, independent releases and scaling, and reduced synchronization, although they make debugging and architecture more difficult.

For distributed systems, replicated load-balanced stateless services provide redundancy and horizontal scaling. Readiness probes indicate when replicas can serve traffic. Session tracking may use consistent hashing, cookies, or headers. Replicated caching layers improve latency and capacity and can provide rate limiting, while a separate replicated nginx layer can perform SSL termination.

Sharded services divide state among shards, commonly routing requests with deterministic, uniform hash functions and modulo operations. Appropriate shard keys preserve cache reuse, while consistent hashing minimizes remapping during resizing. Replicating individual shards improves failure tolerance and permits independent or hot scaling.

Scatter/gather systems distribute each request across multiple workers and combine partial results, enabling parallel computation and leaf-level data sharding. However, coordination overhead and slow “straggler” nodes can limit gains, so shards should be replicated for reliability and upgrades. The passage concludes by introducing function-as-a-service and serverless architectures for temporary, request- or event-driven workloads.

FSU President John Thrasher appointed a 15-member committee, co-chaired by Renisha Gibbs and the university’s chief diversity officer, to review policies on campus names, markers and statues. The panel will seek community input, establish naming criteria and make recommendations amid nationwide calls to remove Confederate designations. Its meetings will be open to the public. The review follows a proposal to remove the statue of Francis Eppes, whom supporters say was a slave owner and Confederate supporter, along with references to him in a building name and university endowment.

The passage introduces NVIDIA’s A100 Tensor Core GPU, an eighth-generation data center accelerator built on the Ampere GA100 architecture and TSMC’s 7nm N7 process. It targets computationally intensive AI, high-performance computing, and data analytics workloads, offering stronger performance, multi-GPU scalability, flexibility, and utilization than the Tesla V100.

The A100 implementation includes 108 streaming multiprocessors, 432 third-generation Tensor Cores, 40 GB of HBM2 memory with 1,555 GB/s bandwidth, and a 40 MB L2 cache. Its Tensor Cores support FP16, BF16, TF32, IEEE FP64, INT8, INT4, and binary operations. The passage reports 2.5-times higher mixed-precision and FP64 performance than V100, while TF32 operations run up to 10 times faster than V100 FP32 operations. Fine-grained structured sparsity uses a 2:4 pattern to double Tensor Core throughput and reduce memory bandwidth requirements.

Multi-Instance GPU technology can partition an A100 into as many as seven isolated GPU instances with dedicated compute, cache, and memory resources. Compute instances, Volta-style MPS support, quality-of-service guarantees, fault isolation, and workload migration improve multi-tenant utilization and security.

A100 connectivity includes twelve third-generation NVLink links providing 600 GB/s aggregate bandwidth, NVSwitch support, PCIe Gen 4 with 31.5 GB/s bandwidth, SR-IOV, and compatibility with Mellanox InfiniBand and Ethernet. The architecture also adds asynchronous memory copies and barriers, CUDA task-graph acceleration, L2 residency controls, compute data compression, improved error detection and containment, hardware JPEG decoding, optical-flow processing, faster atomics, and five NVDEC units.

CUDA 11 adds programming support for third-generation Tensor Cores, sparsity, task graphs, MIG, asynchronous copies and barriers, L2 cache controls, and Cooperative Groups improvements.

DGX A100 combines eight A100 GPUs with NVSwitch, offering up to 5 PFLOPS of AI performance and up to 56 isolated accelerators through MIG. Its software stack includes CUDA, NVIDIA Container Toolkit, and NGC containers for deep learning, inference, analytics, and HPC, while InfiniBand and Magnum IO support scaling from individual systems to large clusters.

The federal shutdown is placing essential FAA and TSA employees under increasing strain as they work without pay and with furloughed colleagues missing. Federal aviation employees say air travel remains safe but warn that the prolonged funding lapse will reduce efficiency, slow repairs, and likely cause more delays and cancellations. Air traffic controllers also face long-standing staff shortages, while some workers fear contractors could be furloughed. The FAA says it will slow traffic at affected airports rather than compromise safety, reports that working controllers will be paid, and says safety-critical positions are exempt from reductions in force. TSA employees and union leaders are concerned about threats to mass firings and public-sector unions. One controller described an undercurrent of fear, while the union says it does not endorse sick-outs; workers may still need to miss shifts if they cannot afford commuting.

The 23rd BMO Okanagan Marathon in Kelowna expects nearly 3,000 participants across marathon, half marathon, 10K and 5K events. This year adds a timed 5K and an adult beverage garden. Saturday features a friendship run and children’s activities, while Sunday’s races include gear check and more than 300 volunteers. The official charity is The Sunshine Foundation of Canada.

The disclosure describes robotic- and navigation-assisted surgical systems, tool assemblies, and methods for preparing vertebral anatomy and placing implants, including pedicle screws and tap markers. A navigation system tracks a target vertebra and defines an insertion trajectory, while a robotic manipulator advances a screw through overlying soft tissue using a releasably engaged, coaxial sleeve. The screw is then advanced relative to the sleeve to engage the vertebral body and disengage from it. In another embodiment, the sleeve has a flexible distal feature that initially closes its distal end to prevent tissue ingress and deflects outward when the screw passes through it.

The tool assembly supports interchangeable working tools, including scalpels, depth probes, burs, drills, dilators, and tap inserters. One drive coupler permits rapid tool exchange while remaining coupled to the robotic input device and transfers rotational force to the selected tool. Another drive coupler permits manual axial and rotational manipulation while the robotic manipulator constrains movement along the planned trajectory and may provide haptic feedback. Depth markings indicate the working tool’s insertion depth.

An elongate sleeve receives a working tool and retracts soft tissue to establish a working channel. Its distal movable feature remains closed during advancement and opens to permit the tool to engage bone. The sleeve may include deployable spikes that penetrate bone to resist lateral movement. The disclosed workflow includes forming an incision, dilating tissue, drilling a pilot hole, inserting a tap marker, and decoupling the drive coupler while leaving the marker secured in bone.

Navigation devices include a localizer and removable tracking devices with detectable markers. A tracking device coupled to a working tool allows its position and orientation to be checked or the vertebra to be relocalized after movement caused by steps such as discectomy and cage placement. For tap markers, a ratcheting mechanism permits unidirectional rotation of the tracking device relative to the marker.

Apple Inc. filed a Form 8-K dated January 27, 2022. Under Item 2.02, it reported issuing a press release covering its financial results for the first fiscal quarter ended December 25, 2021, attached as Exhibit 99.1. The information was designated as not “filed” under Section 18 of the Exchange Act or incorporated by reference, except by specific reference. Item 9.01 listed the press release and Inline XBRL cover-page data. The report was signed by Luca Maestri, Senior Vice President and Chief Financial Officer.

Anjuna police registered two unexplained deaths involving tourists from Tamil Nadu and Kerala. Pravin Sundaram, 28, collapsed after returning from Vagator and was declared dead at a private hospital; Abdul died after being brought to a hospital by an unknown person. Police preserved both bodies’ viscera for autopsy and are investigating, including tracing Abdul’s companion. A minister urged authorities to curb outdoor music parties and drug-related activity.

A New York Medicaid panel unanimously recommended pausing state coverage of Sarepta’s Duchenne muscular dystrophy drug Elevidys until the FDA adds safety and clinical-trial data to its labeling and the state evaluates a new regimen to reduce liver-failure risk. Coverage will continue case by case for medically necessary Medicaid patients under 21, pending the recommendation’s adoption.

The St. John’s Edge defeated the London Lightning 123-110 in Game 4 of the National Basketball League of Canada Central Division final, tying the best-of-seven series 2-2. Game 5 is Thursday in St. John’s, with Game 6 scheduled for London. London played sloppily and without intensity, while St. John’s shot effectively and dominated the paint 50-38. Charles Hinkle and Coron Williams scored 28 points each for the Edge, Ryan Reid added 22, and Royce White led the Lightning with 32 points, followed by Ryan Anderson’s 21. London also missed 13 free throws and was criticized for a short bench and an on-court confrontation between White and Anderson. Separately, the NBL investigated a complaint alleging White used a homophobic slur during Game 3; reports differed on what was said, and officials said they heard nothing. Coaches Jeff Dunlap and Keith Vassell both acknowledged adjustments their teams needed.

The team is preparing for Wednesday’s game, seeing it as a chance to finish the playoff run after a strong road season. Players emphasize focusing on the next game, taking positives, and treating it as the biggest of their careers. Their plan is to forecheck, get pucks deep, close gaps quickly, pressure the opponent in its defensive zone, and direct pucks toward the net. They praised both teams’ goaltenders, noting Binner made important saves and the opposing goalie made several stops during five-on-five play and against a five-on-three disadvantage. The team plans to stay consistent, manage travel and rest, and prepare together before the game. An important teammate is expected back, while players also recognize the excitement of playing before their home crowd.

A video featuring mothers and children with Down syndrome performing a Makaton-signed version of Christina Perri’s “A Thousand Years” drew praise from James Corden and Perri and more than 600,000 views. Created for World Down’s Syndrome Day, it aimed to change perceptions of people with the condition.

A qualitative case study examined Turkish teachers’ experiences with pandemic-era distance education, particularly the Turkish language course and its technological tools. Data were collected through semi-structured, one-on-one interviews with 20 Turkish teachers serving grades 5–8 in Diyarbakır’s Hazro district and analyzed descriptively.

Teachers reported that Turkey was unprepared for the sudden shift to digital education but managed the process as well as available resources permitted. Although 45% saw overall educational progress, none considered distance education fully efficient; 70% described it as insufficiently efficient and 30% as inefficient. EBA and EBA TV were viewed as useful because they provided lesson content and broadcasts, but access to devices and internet, particularly in rural settlements, limited participation and achievement. Teachers identified insufficient equipment and infrastructure, absenteeism, interrupted connections, and households with multiple school-age children as major problems for students, parents, and teachers.

Students most frequently needed reading books and dictionaries, followed by technological materials and access to live lessons; some teachers also emphasized practice and activities for reading, writing, speaking, and listening. Telephone was the most used communication tool, followed by WhatsApp, Zoom, EBA, and BİP. Required teacher competencies included subject knowledge, activity planning, effective technology use, communication skills, responsiveness to individual differences, and concise, activity-based instruction.

Recommendations included improving internet infrastructure and ensuring equal access to devices and materials, updating EBA content, retaining distance education as support for face-to-face teaching, expanding teacher development, promoting reading activities, tailoring education to regional needs, and revising target behaviors and achievements. Continued cooperation among teachers, students, and parents was considered necessary.

Topshop recalled all till display barriers nationwide after a display-barrier incident caused serious head injuries and killed 10-year-old Kaden Reddick in Reading. Police are investigating, while Reading Borough Council is supporting the retail health and safety inquiry.

The speaker presents the transfer of power as a historic opportunity for the United States to help lead the world toward peace. He says rapid scientific and social change, the desire for peace, and America’s demonstrated progress make this moment promising, while warning that material prosperity has been accompanied by spiritual crisis, discord, war, division, and unfulfilled lives.

He argues that the country’s greatest challenge requires “the better angels” of goodness, decency, love, and kindness. Americans must lower their voices, listen to those who feel excluded or unheard, and combine government action with the efforts of concerned citizens. Diana Beresford-Kroeger and her husband, Christian, bought 160 acres near Merrickville in the 1970s and created the Carrigliath arboretum and organic garden. After losing her family at age 11, she studied botany, medical biochemistry, nuclear radiation, organic chemistry, and cardiovascular research. Her Canadian-made documentary, “Call of the Forest: The Forgotten Wisdom of Trees,” examines deforestation’s connection to climate change and was based on her book “The Global Forest.” She also devised the Bioplan, which estimates that planting one tree per person annually for six years could reduce atmospheric carbon dioxide from 400 to 300 parts per million. Ravita Meghwar, now Gulnaz Shah, grew up Hindu in a Pakistani village but is now a married Muslim. Her family says kidnappers drugged and abducted her and forced her conversion; she says she eloped voluntarily. Such cases, once unreported, now reach courts in Sindh province, home to most of Pakistan's Hindus, whose similar patterns and targeting of minor girls have unsettled a community making up about 2 percent of a population of roughly 200 million. Seventy years after partition, some Hindus are reassessing their place in Pakistan: shrines and religious groups promote conversion, and Hindus are moving to cities or leaving for India, with one estimate putting departures at 5,000 per year.

Though Muslims dominate Pakistan's politics, economy and society, Hindus retained social influence in Sindh, where more than 6 percent of the population is Hindu, with many low-caste, low-income Hindus working farmlands for powerful landowners in conditions of economic servitude and discrimination. A 2015 South Asia Partnership-Pakistan report said social, cultural, economic and religious factors combined with feudal power structures to enable forcible conversions. One family attributes the targeting to a village political dispute over a well.

Activists and families allege girls are abducted, coerced into converting and married in an organized manner; Muslim leaders defend conversions as a way of earning blessings, with seminaries, shrines, clerics and politicians backing them and protecting couples who claim to have eloped willingly. The girls' own testimony typically settles cases. In 2012, three Hindu girls were reported forcibly converted and married, and the Supreme Court ruled women could remain with their husbands; activist Mangla Sharma of the Pakistan Hindu Council expressed disappointment. A 2016 Sindh bill outlawing forcible conversion and conversion before age 18 faced opposition from Jamaat-ud-Da'wa and right-wing groups, and the governor declined to sign it. Lawyers now invoke Sindh's ban on marriage under 18; in Meghwar's case attorney Ali Palh intervened on that basis, but a high court judge ruled she could live with her husband.

Mass conversions of Hindu families, many lower-caste, continue in Sindh, with seminaries offering money and housing. Activists date the organized movement to the past 15 years and the legacy of General Zia-ul-Haq's drive to make sharia supreme law. In Karachi, Hindus described whole apartment buildings filled with families newly arrived from elsewhere in Sindh.

The passage is a technical whitepaper on the NVIDIA A100 Tensor Core GPU, described as NVIDIA's 8th-generation data center GPU built on the Ampere architecture (GA100) and fabricated on TSMC's 7nm N7 process with 54.2 billion transistors and a 826 mm² die. The A100 implementation includes 108 SMs, 6,912 FP32 CUDA cores, 432 third-generation Tensor Cores, and 40 GB of HBM2 memory.

Key features include:

- **Memory architecture:** 40 GB HBM2 at 1555 GB/s, a 40 MB L2 cache (~6.7x larger than V100) with 2.3x the read bandwidth, L2 residency controls, Compute Data Compression, and SECDED ECC protection.
- **Multi-Instance GPU (MIG):** partitioning one A100 into as many as seven GPU Instances with isolated memory paths, QoS, and fault isolation, delivering up to 7x more GPU instances; GPU Instances, GPU slices, memory slices, and Compute Instances are described in detail.
- **Third-generation NVLink** with 50 Gbit/sec per signal pair, twelve links totaling 600 GB/s, plus NVSwitch, and PCIe Gen 4 with SR-IOV support.
- **CUDA 11 advances:** asynchronous copy, asynchronous barriers, L2 cache residency controls, task graph acceleration, Cooperative Groups improvements, and warp-level reduction instructions.
- **Additional hardware:** NVJPG JPEG decode engine, optical flow accelerator, improved atomics throughput, and five NVDEC units.
- **DGX A100 system:** eight A100 GPUs with six NVSwitches, 5 PFLOPS of AI performance in a 6U chassis, and up to 56 isolated accelerators via MIG.

The document frames the A100 as delivering speedups over V100 for AI training and inference, HPC, and data analytics, while emphasizing elasticity, multi-GPU scalability, and fault detection and containment.

The lecture introduces binary detection as a simplified model in which one bit is sent through an encoder, modulator, noisy channel, and demodulator. The receiver observes one scalar value and must decide whether 0 or 1 was transmitted. This single-bit, one-dimensional problem is treated as a toy model whose solution can later be extended to more general systems, illustrating Claude Shannon’s approach of solving simplified theoretical problems before restoring practical constraints.

For known prior probabilities and conditional observation densities, maximum a posteriori (MAP) detection chooses the hypothesis with the larger posterior probability. Bayes’ rule reduces this decision to comparing the likelihood ratio against the threshold \(P_1/P_0\). The likelihood ratio is therefore a sufficient statistic, and the MAP rule partitions the observation space into two regions corresponding to the two hypotheses.

The lecture then analyzes binary antipodal signaling with Gaussian noise of variance \(N_0/2\): 0 is represented by \(+a\), and 1 by \(-a\). The log-likelihood ratio is \(4av/N_0\), so detection reduces to comparing the observation with a threshold. With equally likely hypotheses, the conditional and overall error probability is \(Q(\sqrt{2E_b/N_0})\). For non-antipodal signals, the error probability depends only on the distance between the two signal points, but shifting them away from the mean increases energy per bit; antipodal signaling is more energy-efficient.

Finally, antipodal signaling is extended to vectors and waveforms in white Gaussian noise. The sufficient statistic becomes the inner product between the received vector and the signal vector. For waveforms, this inner product is implemented with a matched filter. The optimal decision regions are planes perpendicular to the line joining the two antipodal signal points, and projection onto that line reduces vector detection to the previously solved one-dimensional problem.

Systems and methods are disclosed for controlling plasma ion energy distributions in substrate processing through shaped-pulse bias applied to a process-chamber electrode. In an RIE chamber, RF bias creates self-bias at the ESC cathode, while sheath voltage determines ion energy, directionality, feature profile, and mask/stop-layer selectivity. A shaped waveform comprising a positive charge-clearing jump, a negative jump that sets sheath voltage, and a negative ion-current compensation ramp can maintain nearly constant sheath and substrate voltages for about 90% of each cycle, producing a monoenergetic ion energy distribution function (IEDF). Alternatively, modulating the negative-jump amplitude, frequency, and pulse or burst counts creates arbitrary IEDF shapes: amplitude determines ion energy, while relative pulse or burst counts determine ion fractions, enabling single-peak, multi-peak, and wider distributions. Further embodiments overcompensate or undercompensate ion current by varying the ramp slope, creating controlled energy spread; overcompensation produces a wider double-peaked profile, while undercompensation produces a wider single-peaked profile. The disclosed substrate-processing system includes a support pedestal, power electrode, ceramic layer, and programmable bias supply or controller.

The passage is an NVIDIA whitepaper on the Ampere GA10x GPU architecture and related products.

**GA102 GPU.** Fabricated on Samsung's 8nm 8N process, GA102 has 28.3 billion transistors and a 628.4 mm² die. It contains three compute resource types: CUDA Cores (programmable shading), RT Cores (BVH traversal and ray-triangle intersection for ray tracing), and Tensor Cores (AI neural network training/inferencing). A full GA102 includes 10,752 CUDA Cores, 84 second-generation RT Cores, and 336 third-generation Tensor Cores. The GPU comprises seven GPCs, 42 TPCs, 84 SMs, 112 ROPs (versus 96 in TU102), 168 FP64 units, and a memory subsystem of twelve 32-bit controllers (384-bit total) with 6144 KB of L2 cache.

**2x FP32 Processing.** Each GA10x SM partition has two datapaths that both process FP32, doubling peak FP32 rate versus Turing, which limited one of two datapaths to integer operations. A partition can execute 32 FP32 or 16 FP32 plus 16 INT32 operations per clock; all four partitions yield 128 FP32 operations per clock. RTX 3080 delivers 30 shader TFLOPS (11 in the equivalent Turing GPU) and RTX 3090 over 35 FP32 TFLOPS.

**Second-Generation RT Core.** Doubles ray/triangle intersection throughput over Turing (58 vs 34 RT TFLOPS), supports concurrent RT Core with graphics or compute work, and adds an Interpolate Triangle Position unit that accelerates ray-traced motion blur up to eight times faster than Turing. RTX 3080 is up to 2x faster in ray tracing than the RTX 2080 Super; a Wolfenstein: Youngblood frame renders in 6.7 ms (150 FPS) versus 51 ms using shaders alone on Turing. Ampere GPUs were the first to provide AV1 hardware decode and the first discrete GPUs supporting HDMI 2.1 (48 Gbps, 8K60/4K120) and DisplayPort 1.4a with DSC 1.2a, driving two 8K displays at 60 Hz.

**Third-Generation Tensor Cores.** One per SM partition (four total), each twice as powerful as a Turing Tensor Core. New data types include TF32 (up to 5x training throughput, 2x standard FP32) and BF16, both delivering 4x the math throughput of standard FP32; FP64 Tensor acceleration is absent. Fine-Grained Structured Sparsity (2-out-of-4 non-zero pattern) doubles Tensor throughput and halves weight footprint with virtually no inference accuracy loss. RTX 3080 offers 119 peak FP16 Tensor TFLOPS (238 with sparsity), 238 INT8 TOPS, and 476 INT4 TOPS, with 2.7x higher sparse FP16 throughput than the RTX 2080 Super. Tensor Cores accelerate DLSS (now supporting 8K), AI denoising, Broadcast, Canvas, and NGX features.

**Memory, NVLink, PCIe.** GDDR6X, developed with Micron, uses PAM4 four-level signaling (two bits per clock edge) and MTA encoding to reach 19.5 Gbps on RTX 3090 and 19 Gbps on RTX 3080, delivering up to 936 GB/sec peak bandwidth (over 52% more than TU102). RTX 3080 has a 320-bit interface giving 1.5x the bandwidth of the RTX 2080 Super. GA10x supports PCIe Gen 4 (up to 16 GT/s, 64 GB/sec on x16). Third-generation NVLink provides four x4 links at 14.0625 GB/sec each direction, 56.25 GB/sec per direction and 112.5 GB/sec total between two GPUs; the A40 and A6000 each have 48 GB GDDR6 scalable to 96 GB via NVLink, and two RTX 3090s can be linked for SLI (3- and 4-way SLI unsupported).

**SM and Cache.** Each SM has 128 CUDA Cores, four Tensor Cores, a 256 KB register file, four Texture Units, one RT Core, and 128 KB of configurable L1/shared memory. The unified L1/texture/shared design allocates 64 KB L1 (up from 32 KB), 48 KB shared memory, and 16 KB reserved in graphics/async compute modes; shared memory bandwidth doubles to 128 bytes/clock per SM. RTX 3080 L1 bandwidth is 219 GB/sec versus 116 GB/sec for RTX 2080. Ampere GPUs are up to 1.9x more power efficient than Turing at equal performance.

**RTX IO.** A suite working with Microsoft's DirectStorage API for Windows enables GPU-based lossless decompression and asset loading, delivering up to 100x throughput versus hard drives and traditional storage APIs, offloading work that can otherwise consume all 24 cores of a Threadripper CPU, improving frame rates, reducing object pop-in, and enabling near-instant loading.

**Data Center and Professional GPUs.** The GA10x-based NVIDIA A40 delivers up to 2x FP32 and ray-tracing throughput over the Quadro RTX 6000, up to 5x (10x with sparsity) AI training throughput, PCIe Gen 4 bandwidth, 48 GB memory scalable to 96 GB via NVLink, DP1.4 outputs (disabled by default for virtualization), vGPU support, Quadro Sync, and EGX platform compatibility. The RTX A6000 includes 10,752 CUDA Cores, 84 second-generation RT Cores, 336 Tensor Cores, and 48 GB GDDR6 (96 GB with NVLink), and shows generational gains in SPECviewperf 2020, rendering, HPC, and deep-learning benchmarks.

**Video Engines.** The fifth-generation NVDEC supports hardware decode of MPEG-2, VC-1, H.264, H.265, VP8, VP9, and AV1, with AV1 playback of 8K60 HDR at about 4% CPU usage versus above 85% for software decoding. The seventh-generation NVENC provides hardware encoding exceeding x264 Fast and matching x264 Medium quality, supporting H.264 up to 4K and HEVC up to 8K.

**GeForce RTX 3090 and 3070.** The RTX 3090 incorporates GA102 with 82 SMs, 10,496 CUDA Cores, and 24 GB of GDDR6X, and is 1.5x faster than TITAN RTX, supporting DLSS 8K HDR gaming. The RTX 3070 uses GA104, which includes all GA10x features except NVLink, and uses GDDR6 rather than GDDR6X; it outperforms the previous-generation RTX 2080 Ti. Appendix B describes Error Detection and Replay (EDR) on GDDR6X, which retries faulty transactions so overclockers can identify performance plateaus rather than overclocking until crashes.

The Princeton Offense is an unstructured, team-oriented system based on continuous movement, constant ball movement, spacing, and defensive reads rather than a fixed set. Popularized by Pete Carril, it involves all five players and is characterized by give-and-go and back-door cuts, patient possession, and creating open outside shots. It requires strong outside shooting, two-handed passing and driving, court savvy, unselfish play, and superior conditioning.

Coaches must commit fully to the system. Although giving players freedom may initially reduce their sense of control, its stated benefits include developing teamwork, practicing fundamentals, avoiding resets or called plays, making the defense harder to scout, and punishing defenses that sag or extend pressure.

Spacing is essential. Players generally remain 12 to 15 feet apart, spreading the defense, limiting help and double-teams, opening the basket area, and forcing defenders to cover the full court. The offense normally begins in a 2-3 high-post alignment. Phase one uses varied pass or dribble entries; phase two emphasizes exchanges, down screens, back cuts, base crosses, and post actions; phase three shifts into a four-out low-post alignment when the high post cuts to the basket. If the back door is unavailable, the offense flows into another entry.

Tempo and passing are central. Players are encouraged to walk the ball upcourt, make defenders work, capitalize on transition opportunities, and use simple, safe passes, often totaling 15 to 20 per possession. Back cuts primarily punish defensive overplays but can also exploit lost vision. Dribbling is used sparingly for spacing, exchanges, screens, pressure counters, and direct drives when available, with dribble clears, weaves, misdirection, and drive-and-kick actions included. Post-ups generally aim to collapse the defense and create kick-out passes rather than score directly.

The offense can transition into quick-hitting sets when the shot clock is low or at the end of a period. Teams must also prepare for full- and half-court presses by practicing 2-on-1 and 3-on-2 situations and accurate long inbound passes. Its patient, low-possession style is intended to pressure opponents, produce physical and mental fatigue, expose defensive weaknesses, and reduce reliance on a hot shooting night.
