The lecture introduces the fast Fourier transform (FFT) as a class of algorithms for efficiently computing the discrete and inverse discrete Fourier transforms. Direct computation requires on the order of \(N^2\) complex multiplications and additions, limiting large transforms. By exploiting symmetry and periodicity, the FFT decomposes an \(N\)-point transform into smaller transforms; when \(N\) is a power of two, computational cost becomes proportional to \(N\log_2 N\).

In a decimation-in-time form, even- and odd-indexed samples form two \(N/2\)-point DFTs that are combined using powers of \(W_N\). Their periodic outputs can be reused, and recursively applying this decomposition creates a butterfly flow graph down to two-point DFTs. Each butterfly can be simplified to one twiddle-factor multiplication followed by addition and subtraction. An eight-point example demonstrates the structure and bit-reversed input ordering, which also suggests efficient memory arrangements. FFT methods support spectral analysis, FIR filtering, and efficient convolution, with the Cooley-Tukey form disclosed in 1965.

The lecture states and proves Szemerédi’s graph regularity lemma. For vertex sets \(X\) and \(Y\), edge density is the number of edges between them divided by \(|X||Y|\). The pair is \(\epsilon\)-regular if every subset of \(X\) and \(Y\) having at least an \(\epsilon\)-proportion of the respective set has edge density within \(\epsilon\) of the density between \(X\) and \(Y\). A partition is \(\epsilon\)-regular when the weighted proportion of pairs of parts that are not \(\epsilon\)-regular is at most \(\epsilon\).

The theorem states that for every \(\epsilon>0\), there is a constant \(M\), depending only on \(\epsilon\), such that every graph has an \(\epsilon\)-regular partition into at most \(M\) parts. The bound is independent of the graph’s size. Although informally motivated by large, dense graphs, the theorem applies to all graphs; sparse graphs satisfy regularity trivially.

The proof uses an energy-increment argument. The energy of a partition is a weighted mean of squared edge densities between its parts and lies between 0 and 1. Refinement cannot decrease energy, while splitting a pair of irregular parts using witnessing subsets increases their energy by at least a normalized factor of \(\epsilon^4\). Simultaneously refining along witnesses for all irregular pairs increases the total energy by at least \(\epsilon^5\). Iterating from the one-part partition must therefore terminate after at most \(\epsilon^{-5}\) steps, producing an \(\epsilon\)-regular partition. The resulting bound on the number of parts is extremely large but finite and depends only on \(\epsilon\). A theorem attributed to Tim Gowers shows that some graphs require tower-sized numbers of parts, so this type of bound cannot be substantially improved.

An equitable variant additionally guarantees a minimum number of parts and part sizes differing by at most one. It requires modifying the partition during the iterative proof through small-scale rebalancing; simply rebalancing an already regular partition does not work because regularity need not survive refinement.

The study examines how firms can design business models to reduce the negative effects of digital piracy, using Netflix and Spotify as case studies. Digital piracy involves the unlicensed online distribution of copyrighted digital files and has grown from newsgroups and centralized file exchanges to decentralized peer-to-peer systems such as BitTorrent. It offers consumers free access, extensive catalogs, broad device compatibility, and freedom from release windows, geographic restrictions, and DRM, but requires skills, equipment, time, and carries legal and ethical risks. Technical and legal countermeasures—including spoof content, traffic restrictions, lawsuits, warnings, and penalties—have had limited long-term success. Piracy has reduced industry revenues and prompted firms to reconsider distribution strategies and business models.

The research asks: “How can firms design their business model to minimize the negative impact of digital piracy?” It argues that pricing, education, and enforcement are insufficient without a holistic view of value creation and capture. The qualitative multiple-case study used 96 archival documents totaling 235 pages and nine semi-structured interviews with experienced movie and music executives. Data were compared using a framework comprising customer identification, customer engagement, monetization, and value-chain linkages, then condensed into a causal-loop diagram.

Spotify and Netflix compete with piracy primarily through subscription-based streaming. Spotify combines an advertising-supported free tier with paid subscriptions, while Netflix uses paid plans and a free trial. Their models counter piracy by offering immediate, intuitive access; large and regularly updated catalogs; consistent streaming quality; support across devices; limited offline-download options; personalized recommendations; community features; and broader geographic availability. Free tiers attract users and can encourage later subscription, although conversion is difficult and free use may reduce willingness to pay. Licensing agreements determine catalog size and access conditions, while subscription pricing simplifies purchasing but limits price discrimination.

The analysis identifies reinforcing feedback loops. A larger userbase supports stronger content licensing and a richer catalog, while community features and personalization become more valuable as users and content increase. These improvements raise willingness to pay and subscription revenue, which fund service quality and further user acquisition. Thus, competitive advantage against piracy comes primarily from improving navigation, discovery, consumption, and social interaction rather than competing solely on price or content quantity. Exclusive content has limited anti-piracy value because pirated copies are available on similar terms.

The findings indicate that digital technology can enable both piracy and effective counterresponses. They also highlight the importance of network effects, multi-sided platforms, and caution when generalizing to highly diversified firms. Similar subscription, licensing, personalization, and community strategies appear in books, software, and games, but further research is needed to assess industry-specific boundary conditions and potential portfolio effects.

The paper extends Uustalu’s characterization of monoid structures on non-indexed containers to indexed containers, whose index sets coincide and whose extents define endofunctors on families of sets. Indexed containers generalize simple containers and are closely related to generalized polynomials. Bounded vectors illustrate the notion: at index \(n\), a container has shapes \(k \leq n\), with positions in shape \(k\) given by \(\mathrm{Fin}\,k\).

The authors outline the monoidal structure on indexed containers corresponding to composition of extents and generalize Uustalu’s combinatorial characterization by adjusting the required data and equations for indexing. They prove that these structures correspond exactly to monad structures on indexed container functors. Examples include closure under Cartesian products, indexed versions of the state and writer monads, and a free monad whose application to \(\mathrm{Fin}\) yields well-scoped λ-terms.

Indexed containers are defined by an indexed set of shapes \(S:I\to\mathrm{Set}\) and, for each shape \(s\), an indexed family of positions \(P\). Their extents assign to a family \(X\) the family
\[
\left(\sum_{s:S(i)} P_i(s)\to_i X\right)_i.
\]
Morphisms between containers are natural transformations between their extents; the category \(\mathrm{ICI}\) has composition induced by this correspondence. The extent functor from \(\mathrm{ICI}\) to endofunctors on \(\mathrm{Set}^I\) is full and faithful.

The work is formalized in Cubical Agda. Functional extensionality supports proofs of full faithfulness and the combinatorial monoid equations, while Cubical Agda also permits possible extension to groupoids and higher-dimensional types. The paper reviews indexed containers, internal monoids, and the combinatorial characterization, presents dependently typed examples, and concludes with future-work discussion.

NFL officials were considering further assistance that could keep the Chargers in San Diego ahead of a Jan. 15 relocation deadline. San Diego County, the city and San Diego State offered $375 million—over $100 million below the Chargers’ request—while the NFL had committed $300 million. The Chargers said local funding was firm but still projected a stadium shortfall of up to $175 million. Dean Spanos, who believed he had little choice but to move to Los Angeles, asked the NFL for help; without it, observers predicted the Chargers would join the Rams there. Any downtown stadium proposal requiring public funding would need a 2018 or 2020 vote. Separately, the Chargers finished 5-11 and fired coach Mike McCoy.

C.J. McCollum scored a career-high 43 points, leading the Portland Trail Blazers to a 95-89 win over the Minnesota Timberwolves despite Damian Lillard’s fourth straight absence with a sprained ankle. Portland erased a 14-point deficit behind McCollum’s 16 third-quarter points; Mason Plumlee added 18 points and eight rebounds, Evan Turner scored 11, and Allen Crabbe had 10 points and a career-high eight rebounds. Andrew Wiggins led Minnesota with 24 points, while Karl-Anthony Towns scored 11 on 3-for-15 shooting. Minnesota scheduled a workout with free agent forward Donatas Motiejunas, but he canceled after receiving an offer from New Orleans.

Apple Inc.’s Form 10-Q for the fiscal quarter ended June 27, 2015 presents unaudited financial results and notes. Third-quarter net sales rose 33% to $49.605 billion, driven by iPhone 6 and 6 Plus, Mac demand, the Apple Watch launch, and Services growth. Gross margin was 39.7%, operating income was $14.083 billion, net income was $10.677 billion, and diluted earnings per share were $1.85. For the first nine months, net sales rose 30% to $182.214 billion, net income increased to $42.270 billion, and diluted earnings per share reached $7.25.

Third-quarter product sales were led by iPhone at $31.368 billion, up 59%, while Mac sales rose 9%, Services rose 12%, and Other Products rose 49%. iPad sales declined 23%. Net sales increased in every geographic segment, led by Greater China, where sales rose 112%. Foreign-currency weakness and product mix affected reported results. Apple expected fourth-quarter gross margin of 38.5% to 39.5%.

At June 27, 2015, Apple reported $273.151 billion of assets, $147.474 billion of liabilities, and $125.677 billion of shareholders’ equity. Cash, cash equivalents, and marketable securities totaled $202.848 billion. Nine-month operating cash flow was $67.791 billion. Apple used $10.0 billion for share repurchases and paid $3.1 billion in dividends and dividend equivalents during the quarter. Its repurchase authorization was increased to $140 billion, with $90 billion utilized as of quarter-end. Outstanding long-term borrowings totaled $49.992 billion, and commercial paper outstanding was $4.5 billion.

The notes describe derivatives used to manage foreign-currency and interest-rate exposure, marketable securities with no significant impairment charges, concentrated trade and vendor receivables, and increased long-term debt. Unrecognized tax benefits totaled $5.4 billion, and the potential impact of a European Commission state-aid investigation could not be estimated. Apple disclosed supply-chain concentration, manufacturing and component commitments of $21.7 billion, and future operating lease payments of $5.0 billion. A Smartflash damages award was vacated and ordered retried, while a $548 million Apple-Samsung judgment remained unrecognized pending further proceedings. Apple was also evaluating adoption of the new revenue standard in 2018 or 2019.

Walmart-owned Sam’s Club will open daily from 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. starting this weekend, expanding Sunday hours from 10 a.m. to 6 p.m. The first hour is reserved for Plus members, all members gain access at 9 a.m., and curbside pickup starts at 7 a.m. The company said the change responded to member feedback and the holiday season. Clubs will close at 6 p.m. on Christmas Eve and be closed on Thanksgiving, Christmas Day, New Year’s Day, and Easter.

The speaker credits coach Ronnie Francis with instilling professionalism, hard work and discipline in the team, praising his tactical intelligence over flashy skill. The team aims to control the puck, cycle effectively and compete with its strong young forwards. The speaker also discusses the unpredictability of playoff results, personal growth in maturity, and the importance of persisting through adversity.

QNAP’s TVS-x73 NAS offers 4-, 6-, and 8-bay models, an AMD RX-421BD quad-core APU, up to 64GB DDR4 RAM, four Gigabit LAN ports, M.2 and PCIe expansion, 4K H.264 decoding, dual HDMI output, and throughput up to 1,172 MB/s.

Fred Puhn’s 1981 paperback explains suspension theory, component selection and modification, aerodynamic upgrades, and brake setup for improved handling across multiple car layouts, in plain language.

The Fifth Circuit held that Del Cid-Mendez’s challenge to 8 U.S.C. § 1326(b) was foreclosed by Almendarez-Torres, while preserving the issue for further review. Because the government failed to prove beyond a reasonable doubt that his sentence would have been unchanged under advisory Sentencing Guidelines, the court vacated the sentence and remanded for further proceedings.

The study assessed how the relative contribution of individuals to Omicron transmission varied by age during four waves in France in 2022. It analyzed aggregate COVID-19 ICU admission and population age data for nine age groups, defining waves from March 14–May 15, June 27–August 21, September 18–November 12, and November 22–December 29. A relative-risk statistic compared each age group’s share of ICU admissions before and after each wave’s peak, excluding a seven-day window around the peak; higher values indicate disproportionate depletion of susceptible individuals during epidemic ascent. ICU data were used because under-detection of infections is less pronounced than with community or ambulatory cases, although inconsistent testing remains a limitation.

During the spring wave, ages 10–19 had the highest estimate (RR 1.92), followed by ages 40–49 and 0–9. In summer, the highest estimates were for ages 0–9, 10–19, and 20–29. In autumn, ages 10–19 again ranked highest, followed by ages 30–39 and 20–29. In autumn-winter, the leading estimates shifted to ages 30–39, 40–49, and 80 or older. Overall, the leading per-person role shifted from children, especially ages 10–19, and younger adults toward adults aged 30–49 and people over 80. The authors concluded that broader booster vaccination for adults and possibly children, along with efforts to reduce transmission among elderly people in long-term care facilities, could help limit future spread.

Southern Illinois defeated Evansville 73-61 Saturday at the Ford Center. Mike Rodriguez led the Salukis with 20 points and nine free throws, while Sean Lloyd scored 14 and Thik Bowl added 12. Evansville’s Ryan Taylor and Jaylon Brown each scored 19, and Dru Smith and David Howard had six apiece. After leading by nine in the first half, UE fell behind 33-31 at halftime and never regained the lead. The game also honored legendary SIU head coach Jim Crews with a proclamation and halftime ceremony.

Australian Prime Minister Malcolm Turnbull said China has an obligation to use its "enormous leverage" to draw nuclear-armed North Korea back from the brink, toughening Canberra's stance on the escalating crisis. His comments followed North Korea's latest failed missile test and preceded a visit to Australia by US Vice President Mike Pence, who is in Asia to signal Washington's commitment to regional security. Turnbull called the North Korean regime "a reckless and dangerous threat to peace and stability" and said China has the ability to pull it back from threatening its neighbours. While Australia is a close US ally, it maintains good relations with China, its biggest trading partner. Beijing, under intense US pressure, has pursued a tougher line, including suspending coal imports, but has long feared dramatic action could destabilise the regime, trigger refugee flows and place US forces on its doorstep. Pence is due to meet Turnbull in Sydney on Saturday.

Indian equity benchmarks rose for a fourth straight week, aided by a forecast of normal 2018 monsoon, strong IT earnings, positive global cues and easing inflation. The BSE Sensex gained 0.65% to 34,415.58, while the NSE Nifty50 rose 0.80% to 10,564.05. Gains were trimmed by higher crude prices, rupee depreciation and banking-stock selling amid expectations of a hawkish RBI stance. March WPI inflation eased to 2.47%, while the rupee fell 92 paise to 66.13 per dollar and touched a 13-month low. Foreign institutions were net sellers, while domestic institutions bought shares. IT, metals, FMCG and realty were leading sectoral gainers; PSU banks, energy and Bank Nifty led losses. TCS rose nearly 7% on Friday after robust results, while Axis Bank was the leading weekly loser.

During Larry Nassar’s final sentencing hearing in Michigan, Randall Margraves, father of three victims, lunged at Nassar after the judge denied his request to be alone with him. Margraves was restrained and removed from court. Judge Janice Cunningham declined to punish him for contempt, citing families’ anguish while saying violence was unacceptable. His daughters described abuse under the guise of medical treatment and their parents’ remorse. More than 30 victims testified. Nassar was sentenced to up to 175 years for abuse and 60 years for child pornography. The judge criticized his attorney’s comments about victim testimony but said the court needed to hear each victim’s story.

An international team led by Harald Ebeling used the Hubble Space Telescope to discover eMACSJ1341-QG-1, a distant quiescent galaxy magnified 30-fold by the galaxy cluster eMACSJ1341.9-2441. This record magnification for a quiescent galaxy provides a rare opportunity to study its stellar populations, reconstruct its undistorted properties, and investigate why it has stopped forming stars. Gravitational lensing allows massive galaxy clusters to act as natural telescopes, revealing objects otherwise too faint for even the largest telescopes. Follow-up observations are underway using telescopes in Chile and Maunakea, and the findings were published in the Astrophysical Journal Letters.

Chapter 6 of Larry Connors’ 2009 book *High Probability Trading* presents MDU/MDD, an ETF mean-reversion strategy based on the premise that diversified ETFs are less likely to fall to zero than individual stocks. Buy rules require an ETF to be above its 200-day moving average, below its five-day moving average, and down at least four of the prior five trading days; positions are sold when the ETF closes above its five-day average, with no stop-loss. Tests were extended through December 2020. A no-cost portfolio simulation from 2000 allowed up to five positions at 20% each. Concentrating 50% each in SPY and QQQ produced 287 trades, a 1.82 profit factor, 12% maximum drawdown, and 2.4% CAGR, with only 7.7% of time invested. The strategy had the lowest profit factor among four reviewed Connors mean-reversion strategies. A short-only SPY/QQQ version had a 65% win rate and 0.68% average gain, with much of the gain occurring in 2008.
About 400 Brentwood students went home Friday after a 9-foot, 70-pound boa escaped a biology-class aquarium. The snake was found beneath the floor, wrapped around pipes.

Freeport High School recognized students in grades 9–12 for second-quarter academic excellence, with High Honors and Honors recipients listed by grade. North Yarmouth Academy recognized first-semester students in The Forecaster’s coverage area, listing Highest Honors, High Honors, and Honors recipients in grades 5–12.

Virginia Chestnuts is a family-owned orchard in Nelson County, Virginia, revived by David and Kim Bryant after blight devastated American chestnut trees in the early 1900s. The couple bought land in 2003, tested 200 trees, and later planted more than 1,600 blight-resistant but weather-sensitive American-Chinese Dunstan hybrids. After harsh winters and cicadas threatened the orchard, it produced a strong 2015 crop, followed by a harvest of at least 3,000 pounds. It is one of five orchards in a local growers group.

Harvest runs from mid-September through late October. Chestnuts are collected after falling, sorted, graded, washed, sanitized, dried, refrigerated, and sold fresh in-shell or peeled. The Bryants promote them through local events and social media. Roasted over applewood and used in breads, stuffing, beer, restaurant dishes, and desserts, the chestnuts have gained popularity among consumers seeking a local, nostalgic seasonal food.

Bill Macfadyen links Independence Day to the freedoms protected by the Bill of Rights, particularly the First Amendment’s protection of a free press. He says the press is under attack and independent journalists should report truthfully, provide information and data, and defend the public’s right to know. He asks readers to join Noozhawk’s Hawks Club to support reporting and expanded coverage of Santa Barbara County. Noozhawk, a for-profit business with 21,000 daily readers, says contributions are not tax-deductible and are largely reinvested in its work.

Villa beat Burton Albion 3–2 at Villa Park, extending their winning run to six matches. Scott Hogan, Albert Adomah and Jack Grealish scored, while an Ahmed Elmohamady own goal and Liam Boyce’s late strike completed the scoring. The win leaves Villa third, one point behind Derby County.

Researchers discovered the nearly complete skull of Cifelliodon wahkarmoosuch, a catlike, plant-crushing mammal relative with hair that suckled its young and laid eggs. Published May 16 in Nature, the Utah find indicates that reptile-like mammals underwent unexpected evolutionary diversification across continents and that Pangea’s split occurred 15 million years later than previously thought. Found beneath an iguanodont dinosaur, the fossil suggests migration corridors remained intact into the Early Cretaceous and these vertebrates were globally distributed during the Jurassic-Cretaceous transition.

Michigan State University researchers conducted a four-year comparison of adaptive multi-paddock (AMP) grass-fed operations and grain-fed feedlots, measuring productivity, greenhouse-gas sources and soil erosion. AMP systems performed better environmentally and could offset emissions, while feedlots produced the same beef on half as much land but generated more emissions, mainly from fertilizer-related nitrogen. AMP also produced more beef per land unit than continuous grazing. Researchers cautioned that carbon sequestration may decline over time and favored best practices in both systems, including reduced fertilizer use and cover crops. Managed grazing with adequate plant recovery can deepen roots, build soil organic matter and retain moisture, suggesting production and environmental stewardship may coexist.

Mumbai Indians will face Sunrisers Hyderabad with Mumbai retaining the same XI led by Rohit Sharma. Sunrisers make three changes: Shikhar Dhawan returns after two missed matches, while Mohammad Nabi and Basil Thampi enter the XI; Ricky Bhui, Deepak Hooda and Billy Stanlake are omitted. Stanlake is ruled out for the tournament with a fractured finger.

Sunrisers began with three wins but then lost consecutively to Kings XI Punjab and Chennai Super Kings, leaving them in the lower half of the table. Mumbai have suffered four losses in five games and need at least seven wins from nine remaining matches to improve their play-off chances. Suryakumar Yadav is four runs short of 200, while Rohit Sharma made 94; Pollard, Lewis and the Pandya brothers have struggled with the bat. Bumrah and Mustafizur have led Mumbai’s bowling, while Williamson tops Sunrisers’ batting with 230 runs and Saha has scored only 62.

The passage describes the operation, application, and layout considerations for the TPS7H5001-SP, TPS7H5002-SP, TPS7H5003-SP, and TPS7H5004-SP radiation-hardness-assured, fixed-frequency peak-current-mode PWM controllers. Each device uses an internal 1.23-V bandgap reference, present at REFCAP during steady state and divided to 0.613 V for the error amplifier. A 470-nF REFCAP capacitor is required. The transconductance error amplifier compares VSENSE with the lower of the SS-pin voltage or the 0.613-V reference and has a typical transconductance of 1800 µA/V and DC gain of 10,000 V/V. Output voltage is programmed with a VOUT-to-VSENSE resistor divider using 1%-tolerance or better resistors. A capacitor on SS controls soft start; synchronous-rectifier outputs become active when SS exceeds 1 V.

Switching frequency can be set through an internal oscillator using the RT pin, external synchronization using the SYNC pin, or primary-secondary operation. Internal oscillator mode supports 100 kHz to 2 MHz and produces a SYNC clock at twice the switching frequency. External synchronization requires RT to float and a 200-kHz to 4-MHz clock with a 40% to 60% duty cycle; 50% is recommended. Primary-secondary mode synchronizes two controllers, either as independent converters or as parallel interleaved phases, and produces a 90° or 270° phase shift between corresponding outputs.

Controllers may provide single or dual primary outputs and single or dual synchronous-rectifier outputs. Their roughly 150-mA peak current capability makes external gate drivers recommended. Programmable dead time, leading-edge blank time, pulse skipping, and duty-cycle limits are available according to device model. The pulse-skipping function periodically stops primary switching under specified low-COMP and low-duty-cycle conditions to address minimum-on-time issues.

Peak-current control uses the CS_ILIM signal to generate PWM and configure overcurrent protection. Reaching 1.05 V initiates cycle-by-cycle limiting and the hiccup sequence. CHICC controls the limiting-delay and restart intervals, with a recommended minimum of 3.3 nF. The FAULT pin supports external fault protection using a typical 0.6-V rising threshold and 0.5-V falling threshold, followed by a switching-frequency-dependent delay and renewed soft start. Programmable slope compensation mitigates subharmonic oscillation, and Type 2A or Type 2B frequency compensation may be selected. Thermal shutdown stops switching above 175°C typical and permits reinitialization below 160°C.

The application example designs a 500-kHz, 5-V synchronous push-pull converter using the TPS7H5001-SP and GaN FETs. Selected values include a 205-kΩ RT resistor, 10-kΩ/1.4-kΩ feedback divider, 20.5-kΩ dead-time resistors for approximately 25 ns, a 49.9-kΩ LEB resistor, 33-nF soft-start capacitor for approximately 7.5 ms, 2.5 transformer turns ratio, 40-µH transformer primary inductance, 170-V primary FETs, 80-V synchronous rectifiers, 0.47-µH output inductor, and 7.5-Ω current-sense resistor. Total output capacitance was 2.3 mF, including additional capacitance for single-event-transient mitigation. Type 2A compensation used 40.2 kΩ, 15 nF, and 47 pF components, while the RSC resistor was 102 kΩ.

The controllers operate from 4 V to 14 V and require at least a 0.1-µF VIN-to-AVSS bypass capacitor, preferably X5R or better. Layout guidance emphasizes separating feedback and control traces from switching nodes and power magnetics, minimizing high-di/dt and high-dv/dt loops, keeping AVSS separate from power ground except at a single connection, using short and wide high-current traces, placing filtering and compensation components near their associated pins, and using low-ESR, low-ESL surface-mount capacitors. The remaining sections provide application curves, related documentation, revision history, ESD guidance, and mechanical, packaging, and orderable information.

Maria Sharapova lost to qualifier Vitalia Diatchenko in the first round of Wimbledon, 6-7, 7-6, 6-4, after surrendering multiple leads and collapsing late. Diatchenko, 27, had been 0-2 at Wimbledon and 8-25 in main-draw tour matches. Sharapova, a five-time Grand Slam champion, had been 49-1 in major-opening matches after two early career losses.

The tournament produced seven first-round eliminations among the top 10, more than in any previous year of the professional era. Petra Kvitova, Caroline Garcia, Sloane Stephens, Elina Svitolina, Dominic Thiem, David Goffin and Grigor Dimitrov were among those beaten or forced to retire. Players cited unpredictable grass bounces, pressure on seeded players and the switch from clay as possible factors. Simona Halep, Rafael Nadal and Novak Djokovic won straight sets.

AMD Seamless Firmware Servicing (SFS) is disabled by default. Customers must configure BIOS to enable SFS and optionally customer co-signing; firmware flags determine whether commands are accepted and whether packages require a customer signature. During early-boot setup, before BOOT_DONE, the customer BIOS must provide its RSA public key to the ASP, after which the key cannot be changed. When both keys are enabled, the customer key is checked first and the AMD SFS key second. Co-signatures use RSA-PSS with SHA-256 for 2048-bit keys or SHA-384 for 4096-bit keys.

Each patch checks current system patch and firmware versions to determine applicability. Packages may change registers or values, replace firmware images, or update firmware components. SEV updates are committed and prevent rollback, requiring a reboot to revert; SNP updates require all package pages to be HV-FIXED via RMPUPDATE. Attestation evidence should be obtained through appropriate OS or platform interfaces, and firmware protected by some attestation schemes may not be modified.

Packages must have compatible prerequisite firmware versions and should not apply if any portion cannot be fully applied. Because updates are not persistent across warm or cold reboots, they can be scheduled during OS boot, immediately afterward, or during operation. A deployment agent builds a 2MB-aligned TEE_EXT_CMD_BUFFER, appends any customer co-sign header, AMD package, and signature, then submits it through the ASP mailbox. ASP protects the buffer from x86 access, verifies customer and AMD signatures, runs the validated patch, updates patch levels, and returns status.

GET_SFS_VERSION_INFO reports current patch, system, security, and supported firmware versions, while UPDATE_FW validates the package before applying it. Packages align to AGESA releases, follow names such as `fam_19h-1006-SFS-1.pkg`, and must match the system’s firmware combination. Updates run alongside x86 and DMA traffic with minimal impact, though SEV/ES virtual machines may need to stop and restart for SEV firmware updates; SEV/SNP virtual machines can continue.

At Leander High School’s 2017 prom, nominee Keilany Solano was named prom queen, then spontaneously placed her crown and sash on classmate Abby Cano, who has Down syndrome. Solano said Cano deserved it more and would be even happier. Cano, known for giving hallway high-fives, reacted joyfully, and her mother said the gesture reflected the kindness Cano has received throughout school.

Samsung was expected to beat fourth-quarter 2016 earnings forecasts, aided by robust memory-chip sales. IBK projected operating income of $7.21 billion, while the chip division was forecast to earn $3.31 billion.

ABC’s third episode of Marvel’s *Inhumans*, titled “Divide and Conquer,” airs at 9:00 p.m. ET and follows the Inhuman Royal Family after Maximus’s coup forces them from their home. Viewers can stream it legally through Sling TV or DirecTV Now. Sling’s Broadcast Extra package includes ABC in eight listed U.S. markets and costs $25 monthly after a seven-day trial. DirecTV Now’s $35 “Live a Little” package offers ABC in 39 markets and also includes a seven-day trial. Both services provide viewing through websites, apps, and compatible streaming devices.

The Second Circuit affirmed the district court’s denial of Rodney Nicholson’s habeas corpus petition. Nicholson argued that the state courts improperly excluded Darnell Phelps’s hearsay confession and that this error violated due process under *Chambers v. Mississippi*. Even assuming *Chambers* applies to his request for a new trial, the court found no mechanical or arbitrary rejection of reliable evidence. Phelps’s confession was unreliable because it conflicted with his earlier denial of knowledge, could not be tested through cross-examination at retrial, and may have been tailored to publicly available forensic evidence. The confession also did not necessarily exonerate Nicholson and suggested a more active role for Phelps in the murder. Meanwhile, the jury had found the sole eyewitness credible, and Nicholson had an opportunity to challenge her testimony. Because the record showed no abuse of discretion or deprivation of fundamental fairness, habeas relief was unwarranted.

Helping Hands Hawaii’s Ready to Learn program held its 2017 school supply drive June 1–July 31 for low-income and homeless K–12 students, providing basic educational supplies and kits valued at about $10 each. American Savings Bank branches statewide collected donations June 14–July 14, with island donations remaining local. The program also accepted fundraising, volunteer, online, mail, and in-person contributions. As of April 2017, RTL had raised over $12,000, assembled 3,115 kits worth about $31,000, and benefited more than 6,000 students. Students had to be recommended by case managers from participating referral organizations by June 23, 2017.

Congress members continue receiving pay during the government shutdown because their compensation is constitutionally protected and funded through mandatory spending unaffected by shutdowns, while millions of federal workers may miss paychecks. Rep. Angie Craig introduced the “No Pay for Disarray Act” to withhold lawmakers’ pay during the shutdown, but repayment at the end of the session would be needed for constitutional compliance. A 2019 law guarantees retroactive pay to furloughed federal workers. Funding was set to expire Tuesday amid partisan disputes over a short-term funding bill.

A 27-year-old man identified as Akayed Ullah detonated a pipe bomb strapped to him in a crowded subway passageway under 42nd Street between 7th and 8th Avenues at 7:30 a.m. Monday. The blast injured Ullah and three others with non-life-threatening injuries and was labeled an attempted terror attack. Officials said Ullah was inspired by the Islamic State but apparently had no direct contact with the group. The low-tech device was attached with Velcro and plastic ties. Police and firefighters responded, disrupting subway and bus service around the Port Authority. President Donald Trump was briefed.

The speaker says he entered coaching after he could no longer play and was the only brother to advance through minor-league and organizational coaching ranks as an assistant and head coach. He describes a brother as central to a hockey club’s identity, noting his dissatisfaction with his regular season, the importance of reaching the playoffs, and his later success. He says his family rarely discussed one brother’s championship run, though he was proud of his brothers’ six championships and views winning and losing a final as experiences few understand. He recounts distractions during a home game and the team’s resolve after inserting Martin Jones, emphasizing that it would respond to adversity. He credits special plays by Nash and Doughty, notes that five significant players had not previously played in a Stanley Cup Final, and says they were being evaluated. After a Game 7 loss, he moved on quickly and emphasized the difficulty and sacrifice of winning a championship. He believed his team had a chance to win and called Dean an effective, truthful coach.

A STAT Morning Rounds newsletter page titled “Answering burning questions on MMR vaccines” warns that, without congressional funding, Medicare’s Acute Hospital Care at Home initiative would end, requiring participating hospitals to discharge patients or return them to hospitals by September 30, 2025. The page also includes writer Theresa’s biography, newsletter and privacy notices, and links to stories covering health policy, medicine, biotech, gene therapy, autism treatments, Tylenol, food insecurity, and gender-affirming care.

The coach praised the hard-working, cohesive coaching staff and the players’ commitment, teamwork, and willingness to play within themselves. He said the team has been playing better, harder, and smarter by simplifying the game, defending strongly, and executing consistently, but still needs to raise its level to reach its ultimate goal. He emphasized focusing on controllable factors, especially effort, execution, conviction, and the task at hand, rather than looking beyond the next game. The coach also expressed respect for Cully’s contributions and maturity, noting that the players must continue earning their opportunity through performance. Despite heightened scrutiny, he said both players and coaches should rely on established routines and remain fully focused when the puck drops.
The speaker praises Evgeni’s speed, reach, defense, scoring ability, health, energy and urgency. Zetterberg is called consistent, smart and dangerous everywhere on the ice.

Amazon.com, Inc. filed a Form 8-K dated April 29, 2021, reporting its first-quarter 2021 financial results. The filing incorporates Exhibit 99.1, the results press release, and Exhibit 99.2, information regarding non-GAAP financial measures, and was signed by CFO Brian T. Olsavsky.

Tesla reported record third-quarter 2025 deliveries of 497,099 vehicles, up 7.4% year over year and above analysts’ forecast of roughly 444,000, aided by U.S. incentives ahead of the $7,500 EV tax credit’s September 30 expiry. It needs nearly 390,000 fourth-quarter deliveries to reach its 1.61 million full-year target. European and UK performance weakened, with market share around 1.5%, while investors reacted cautiously to the surge’s sustainability. Tesla also delivered a record 12.5 GWh of energy storage, and its response to slower automotive growth will center on pricing, new models, and energy products.

The UC1825B-SP uses a sawtooth oscillator whose rising edge is controlled by the RT resistor and CT capacitance and whose falling edge sets output dead time. RT should be selected first based on maximum duty cycle, with CT then chosen for frequency. Recommended RT values are 1–100 kΩ; maximum duty cycles below 70% are not recommended.

The dual-output controller includes push-pull drivers and can also support half-bridge and full-bridge configurations with external high-side drivers. It supports voltage- and current-mode topologies; the RAMP pin provides current-sense input, ILIM provides current limiting, and external components implement slope compensation. A 215-kHz switching frequency was selected as a bandwidth-efficiency tradeoff, using RT = 10 kΩ and CT = 680 pF.

The transformer design used a 2.2 turns ratio, a 30% target duty cycle, a 1.5 auxiliary-winding turns ratio, 6% magnetizing current, and 120 µH primary inductance. The output inductor was 2.2 µH. Peak- and RMS-current equations apply only in continuous conduction mode and require application-specific optimization.

An RCD clamp limits switch-node overshoot; a clamp factor of 1.5 permits about 50% overshoot, and 10% is the typical starting clamp-voltage variation. The output diode was rated at 60 V, while primary switching MOSFETs require approximately 2.5–3 times the input voltage in voltage rating.

The output stage used about 1145 µF of capacitance, six input-side ceramic capacitors, bulk capacitors behind a 500-nH output-filter inductor, and a conservative 0.5-Ω damping resistor. Type IIB compensation targeted a 5-kHz crossover frequency, with the compensation zero placed well before crossover. The sense resistor measures transformer ripple current and shuts down the switching cycle when the CS threshold, approximately 1 V, is reached.

The specified input range is 10–30 V from a well-regulated supply; additional bulk capacitance may be needed, with 100 µF cited as typical. Tests examined MOSFET voltage stress, output ripple, and a 0-to-10-A output transient using 48-V input.

Layout guidance emphasizes low-EMI inductors, routing feedback away from noisy power paths, placing input, compensation, and output components close to their connections, using short, thick current traces, arranging switching loops consistently, and employing separate power and signal ground planes. VCC and VREF require direct high-frequency ceramic bypass capacitors, with 1-mF ceramic capacitors recommended. Final sections provide support resources, ESD precautions, and mechanical, packaging, and orderable information.

About 200 people attended a market-square vigil for 18-year-old Mariam Moustafa, who died the previous week after an attack outside the intu Victoria Centre. Organized by Yousuf Farooq with Nottingham Stand Up To Racism and the Nottingham People’s Assembly, the event featured her sister, a former teacher and an Egyptian Coptic priest. Her father, Mohamed Moustafa, thanked attendees and called for justice. The crowd chanted “justice for Mariam,” observed silence and stood before a banner displaying her image and the same message.

NBWA launched DeliveringLocalJobs.com to highlight the beer distribution industry’s 135,000 workers and the quality jobs they provide nationwide. The site features employee stories and videos, distributor profiles from all 50 states, state economic data, and examples of employees building beer brands with more than 5,000 brewers and importers. NBWA says the industry generates $70 billion for GDP, nearly $180 million in community impacts and nearly $13 billion in tax revenue.

Arizona Cardinals quarterback Carson Palmer remained optimistic despite his age and a performance decline in 2016. After a torn ACL derailed his 2014 season, Palmer achieved career highs in wins, passing yards, yards per attempt and QBR in 2015, earning first-team All-Pro honors. Arizona followed its 13-win season and NFC West title with a 7-8-1 record in 2016. Palmer said he felt physically good, regularly monitored his health and preferred the Cardinals’ underdog status because it reduced pressure and allowed greater focus on his craft. He intended to continue playing as long as he remained healthy and enjoyed the game.

Microsoft Corporation’s Form 10-Q for the quarter ended December 31, 2022 reported Q2 fiscal 2023 revenue of $52.747 billion, up from $51.728 billion, as service and other revenue increased to $36.230 billion while product revenue fell to $16.517 billion. Operating income declined to $20.399 billion from $22.247 billion, net income to $16.425 billion from $18.765 billion, and diluted EPS to $2.20 from $2.48. For the six months, revenue was $102.869 billion versus $97.045 billion, while net income was $33.981 billion versus $39.270 billion and diluted EPS was $4.54 versus $5.19.

At December 31, 2022, cash, cash equivalents and short-term investments totaled $99.508 billion; total assets were $364.552 billion, liabilities $181.416 billion and stockholders’ equity $183.136 billion. Six-month operating cash flow was $34.371 billion, with net investing and financing outflows of $10.282 billion and $22.232 billion. Microsoft Cloud revenue increased 22% to $27.1 billion, including 31% growth in Azure and other cloud services. Office 365 Commercial grew 11%, Dynamics 365 21% and LinkedIn 10%; Windows OEM licensing and devices revenue each declined 39%, while Xbox content and services fell 12%.

Microsoft increased server and network equipment useful lives from four to six years, adding $945 million to Q2 operating income and $768 million to net income. On January 18, 2023, it announced approximately 10,000 job reductions and recorded $800 million of severance expense within a $1.2 billion quarterly charge that also included hardware impairments and lease consolidation costs. The company completed its $18.8 billion Nuance acquisition and continued work toward the regulatory approval of its proposed $68.7 billion Activision Blizzard acquisition. It also had $31.5 billion remaining under its share-repurchase authorization. Unrecognized tax benefits totaled $17.1 billion, and accrued legal liabilities totaled $181 million, with approximately $500 million of additional adverse outcomes considered reasonably possible. Deloitte & Touche’s review found no material modifications needed to conform the interim information to U.S. GAAP.

The Bollinger Band Squeeze strategy seeks to trade in the direction of a breakout following low volatility. Bollinger Bands use a moving average as their center line, with outer bands showing a price range; they contract during low volatility and expand during high volatility. A squeeze occurs when the bands contract, potentially preceding an upward or downward breakout.

The passage reports unsuccessful backtests across multiple assets and several strategy variations. On Pepsi, the strategy returned 12.5% versus 14.8% for buy and hold while invested 61% of the time. The authors therefore caution against trusting anecdotal success claims and recommend testing positive expectancy and following rules mechanically.

Because the strategy is a breakout approach rather than mean reversion, it has a lower win rate and may produce whipsaws. Performance depends on the asset: stocks may be more prone to mean reversion than commodities, so a strategy effective on one asset may fail on another. Overbought and oversold interpretations also work differently across assets. Traders may combine the strategy with indicators such as RSI or IBS, but the passage identifies positive expectancy and failure to follow tested rules as the two biggest mistakes.

The passage also describes John A. Bollinger, a financial analyst, author, and options trader who developed Bollinger Bands in the 1980s and named them during a television appearance.

Augustine Heard reported that the line to Fusan had been interrupted and that, although most observers considered the situation unserious, some feared the Tong Hâk was preparing retaliation for the previous attempt on Tai Wen-kun’s life. Heard believed the king was alarmed and had requested a ship through his Washington legation. Following telegrams with Admiral Harmony, Heard judged a ship prudent. The U.S.S. Petrel arrived at Chemulpo; Commander Dayton came to Seoul and agreed to remain for several days. Chinese ironclads and Japanese men-of-war were also at Chemulpo, and Heard requested 600 rifle cartridges from Dayton.

A second section presents a loyal order responding to Confucian scholars’ concerns about a heterodox movement that had deluded people and violated the law. Metropolitan and provincial authorities were ordered to arrest its so-called leaders, suppress its spread, issue public proclamations, and require peaceful obedience, with penalties for failure to act. The order also urged citizens to fulfill duties of patriotism and filial piety, including sacrificing their lives in times of danger.

Butterfield reported strong first-quarter 2018 results. Core return on average tangible common equity rose to 24.3% from 22.3% in the fourth quarter of 2017, marking its fifth consecutive quarter above 20%. Net interest income increased $3.8 million to $79.9 million, while net interest margin expanded 18 basis points to 3.05%. Non-interest income declined 6.1% sequentially due to seasonal factors in the prior quarter. Core non-interest expense was $76 million, and the core efficiency ratio was 62.3%, progressing toward the company’s 60% target.

The bank ended the quarter with approximately $11 billion in assets, a $4.0 billion loan portfolio and average deposits of $9.8 billion. Non-accrual loans declined to $42.4 million, and the net charge-off ratio was 2 basis points. The investment portfolio totaled $4.5 billion, with 94.6% rated AAA. The Basel III total capital ratio was 19.2%, and common equity represented 6.7% of assets. The board authorized a quarterly dividend of $0.38 per common share, while a previously announced share-repurchase program became effective April 1.

Butterfield closed Deutsche Bank’s Global Trust Solutions acquisition at quarter-end, opened its Singapore office and integrated trust operations in Cayman, Guernsey and Switzerland. It expects to close Deutsche Bank’s banking operations in Cayman and the Channel Islands by year-end, adding a Jersey location and potentially increasing total bank deposits by as much as 20%.

Management said rate increases, loan repricing and investment repositioning supported further margin expansion, although new acquisition liquidity and lower-yield U.K. mortgages could create temporary pressure. U.K. residential lending was performing without delinquencies and was expected to generate approximately $300 million in net new annual balances. Commercial growth outside Bermuda was partly attributable to a $50 million one-time transaction and was not expected to recur at the same pace.

First-quarter expenses included roughly $4.5 million to $5 million of unusual or nonrecurring costs; the first-year Sarbanes-Oxley program was completed, while GTS was expected to add about $2 million in quarterly core expenses. Management remained focused on reaching its 60% efficiency-ratio target. Fee income was expected to remain broadly flat without acquisitions, and future reserve releases were likely to diminish as the five-year hospitality-loan lookback normalized. Butterfield was also pursuing additional acquisitions but emphasized AML readiness, integration capacity and financial discipline.

Andy has become a key player despite injuries, earning praise for his hard, physical play and composure in the playoffs. The speaker expects an emotional, loud home game but emphasizes staying disciplined and following the team’s usual approach. Newfoundland’s passionate hockey fans are expected to draw crowds and benefit the local arena, league, and economy.

Pedro Russell earned a business degree, later worked in education strategy and business development, and completed an MBA at MIT Sloan. With Harvard Business School classmates Garrison Jones and Stephen McGarvey, he co-founded GPS Partners, an education-focused search fund that began acquiring for-profit medical technical schools.

GPS identified MedPro Institute, a vocational school near Boston founded in 1998 by Dr. Samantha Hill. MedPro offered certificate programs in medical assisting, phlebotomy, medical billing and coding, and dental assisting. Its small classes, hands-on training, and personalized attention contributed to high graduation rates and strong job placement outcomes. After Hill, who was past the typical retirement age, agreed to sell, GPS began due diligence.

Russell found that MedPro relied primarily on word of mouth and viewed increased visibility as a growth opportunity. However, he needed to determine how higher enrollment would affect costs. Major expenses included rent, daily cleaning, per-class instructor salaries, two career-services staff, annual accreditation fees, disposable supplies, liability insurance, internet usage, and electricity. These costs varied by resource utilization, student volume, or both; some remained unchanged regardless of school size, while others included per-student charges or usage-based fees. Russell planned to analyze cost-volume relationships graphically as GPS weighed growth against financial sustainability.

Hammerson rejected a preliminary, non-binding £4.88bn proposal from Klépierre valuing it at 615p per share, 41% above its March 16 close, payable half in cash and half in new Klépierre shares. Hammerson shares rose to about 545p despite the rejection, while directors called the approach opportunistic and said it significantly undervalued the company. Hammerson remains committed to acquiring Intu Properties, combining their portfolios and targeting about £25m in annual synergies. At 545p, the shares traded at roughly a 28% discount to book value with a nearly 5% forward dividend yield, though the author is watching from the sidelines given retail leasing difficulties.

New Jersey Sen. Cory Booker traveled to Alabama on the final weekend before the election, campaigning for Democratic Senate nominee Doug Jones while laying groundwork for the 2020 presidential race. Booker cited his family’s ties to Alabama coal miners and said he felt obligated to repay the state by supporting its communities. He deflected a “Booker 2020” chant by noting that his Senate seat was also up in 2020.

Alabama was presented as potentially pivotal for Democratic presidential contenders because Deep South primary results can be shaped by African-American voters. Jones’s campaign generally discouraged national Democrats from visiting, fearing Republican Roy Moore would portray their involvement as outsider influence, but members of the Congressional Black Caucus campaigned for Jones because mobilizing Black voters was central. Booker, one of three Black Democrats frequently mentioned as potential 2020 candidates, joined former Massachusetts Gov. Deval Patrick; Sen. Kamala Harris supported Jones remotely.

Black voters made up about 27% of Alabama’s population and 19% of its electorate in 1998. Jones had drawn national Democratic support over Moore’s alleged sexual misconduct and positions on same-sex marriage and minority issues. In 2016, Hillary Clinton’s 91% support among Black primary voters helped her win Alabama by 35 delegates and the five-state Deep South. Barack Obama similarly relied on Black voters in 2008. The unresolved question was whether 2020 contenders could consolidate that support or Black voters would split among them.

The speaker describes goalie Roli’s situation as unfortunate but sees his replacement’s opportunity as positive. Despite a difficult season and the team’s loss, he advises against dwelling on the deciding play, emphasizing confidence, teamwork, and game-like preparation to regain speed, intensity, and sharpness. He believes whoever plays can succeed in the Stanley Cup Finals and that the team can use Roli’s observations of shooters’ tendencies. Although he wishes Roli could finish what he started in the playoffs, the priority is to stay focused and play well, with hopes that the season can end as it began, involving both goaltenders.

In Pfeiffer v. Commissioner of Internal Revenue (2d Cir., Feb. 15, 1937), Circuit Judge Manton, joined by Swan, reversed a Board of Tax Appeals decision upholding an $89,841.75 income tax deficiency for 1931, while Judge L. Hand dissented.

Wm. R. Warner & Co. Inc. distributed preferred stock dividends to its common stockholders in 1928 and 1931. Petitioner, owner of 25,165 common shares, received 12,582 preferred shares in 1928 and 6,291¼ in 1931, each with a $100 fair market value; the corporation had an earned surplus exceeding $8 million and no unpaid preferred dividends. In 1931 it redeemed at par 8,500 preferred shares, including 2,000 of petitioner's 1928 shares. The Commissioner charged petitioner with $629,125 of unreported income from the 1931 preferred stock dividend and $200,000 from the redemption.

The Board held the 1931 preferred dividend taxable under the Revenue Act of 1928, since section 115(f)'s exemption of "stock dividends" was read to cover only dividends in the same class of stock (Eisner v. Macomber), but held no income arose from the redemption because the 1928 dividend had itself been taxable, giving a $100 basis per share redeemed at $100. On appeal, the court held the exemption unqualified, following Koshland v. Helvering, Gowran v. Commissioner, and the Treasury's consistent construction of "stock dividend" as any dividend in a corporation's own stock; section 115(g) taxes only redemptions essentially equivalent to a taxable dividend, and the Board had not so found. The Commissioner's capital-gain contention was unreviewed because it was neither decided below nor assigned as error.

Judge Hand dissented, arguing Congress exempted stock dividends merely in reliance on Eisner v. Macomber, that preferred stock paid on common stock creates a substantially new right and is income, and that the later administrative gloss and basis-reduction regulations, invalidated by Koshland, could not sustain a reading of the bare statutory words.

Miami Herald columnist Dan Le Batard, citing Heat sources, said the organization believed LeBron James checked out during Miami’s five-game 2014 Finals loss to San Antonio, despite strong statistics. The passage asks whether James might repeat that against Golden State in 2018.

Bitcoin rose about 2% on Friday to $123,874, roughly 1% below its record above $124,000, as the U.S. government shutdown entered its third day. The cryptocurrency gained 12% for the week as investors sought safe-haven assets amid political and economic tensions. Standard Chartered expects Bitcoin to reach a new high soon and ultimately $135,000. Gold rose 0.5%, while the S&P 500 and Nasdaq gained 0.5% and 0.27%, respectively.

The California Supreme Court held that a creditor’s failure to present its claim against a deceased debtor’s estate within the statutory period bars the creditor’s remedy against the estate but does not extinguish the unpaid debt. Because the debt remained subsisting, equity would not compel the creditor to surrender a deed of trust securing it or enjoin a sale under the deed without payment of the debt; the court could instead require payment before surrendering the security or direct a sale with any surplus returned to the estate. The court therefore reversed the injunction and directed that the trustees’ demurrer be sustained.

Crockett, J., joined by McKinstry, J., dissented. They argued that failure to present the claim for allowance forfeited the creditor’s lien, and that equity should compel the creditor to release the legal title so the estate could be used to pay administration expenses and other preferred debts.

Google canceled Daily Stormer’s website registration for violating its anti-violence policy after GoDaddy gave the neo-Nazi site 24 hours to find a new host. The moves followed an article mocking Heather Heyer, who was killed at a white-nationalist rally in Charlottesville. YouTube also terminated Daily Stormer’s channel for hate speech, while Facebook said it removes links to the site unless posts clearly condemn it. Google said the cancellation could take up to 48 hours, but it was not the site’s host; GoDaddy and Cloudflare also denied hosting it. The actions highlight pressure on tech companies to respond to extremist content while balancing free-speech concerns.

Matthew James Phelps, 29, is awaiting trial on first-degree murder charges for the September 1 death of his 29-year-old wife, Lauren, at their North Carolina home. He told 911 dispatchers he had taken excessive Coricidin cough medicine, dreamed, and woke to find her stabbed. Police arrived while she was still alive, but she died at the hospital. Investigators seized red-stained bedding, an empty Coricidin box, a knife set, computers, financial documents, and Lauren’s iPhone. Phelps, who had no criminal record, is being held without bail.

The passage describes bonded optical devices for wearable and near-eye displays. Monochromatic LED arrays, including red, green, and blue elements, are directly or hybrid bonded to silicon, CMOS, glass, or other carriers containing driver circuitry. The bonding can connect dielectric surfaces and conductive contact pads without adhesive and may use die-to-die, wafer-to-wafer, or die-to-wafer processes. Such configurations can provide independently controlled emitters, fine pixel pitches below 50, 10, 5, or even 1 micron, and improved manufacturability without individually placing millions of LED chips.

Different optical elements can emit different colors whose light is redirected by mirrors or beam splitters and combined through lenses or waveguides to produce a full-color image. Optical assemblies may combine monochromatic displays, either on separate carriers or on a common carrier, with the emitters arranged in parallel or angled configurations. Pixel isolation structures, including deep trenches or separations between pixel matrices, can reduce crosstalk and permit matrix-level brightness control.

The disclosed systems may be incorporated into augmented-reality glasses, smart glasses, projection systems, automotive head-up displays, smartwatches, and cell phone displays.

Cabinet Secretary James Macharia blamed Kenya’s disorderly motorcycle-taxi industry on poor enforcement of existing rules. He said the ministry is working with county transport committees and traffic authorities to improve compliance. MP Simon King’ara urged stronger action against enforcement delays and proposed a dedicated safety authority, saying NTSA was overwhelmed. Nairobi County has banned riders from the CBD.

The IRS furloughed about 34,000 workers during the government shutdown, while 39,870 employees, or 53.6% of its workforce, remained on duty. Most IRS operations closed, and the furlough began October 8, 2025, for employees not designated exempt or excepted.

The GA10x SM builds on Turing and Volta, adding four processing partitions per SM with a 128 KB shared L1 data cache/shared memory subsystem, dual-datapath FP32 processing (doubling peak FP32 rate to 128 FP32 operations per clock per SM), and one third-generation Tensor Core per partition that is twice as powerful as a Turing Tensor Core. Unified shared memory/L1 capacity is 33% larger than Turing, with doubled shared memory bandwidth and 128 KB L1 per SM. GA10x GPUs add a second-generation RT Core that doubles ray/triangle intersection testing, supports a new Interpolate Triangle Position unit for accelerating ray-traced motion blur (up to 8x faster than Turing), and enables concurrent RT Core plus graphics or compute work, along with simultaneous compute workloads and workload priorities. Third-generation Tensor Cores add TF32 and BF16 support and a Sparsity feature that doubles throughput for sparse matrix operations; RTX 3080 delivers 2.7x the peak FP16 Tensor throughput of the RTX 2080 Super with sparsity. The GA10x memory subsystem uses GDDR6X with PAM4 signaling, supporting up to 19.5 Gbps and 936 GB/sec peak bandwidth (over 52% more than TU102), and a new Error Detection and Replay feature handles GDDR6X transmission errors during memory overclocking. NVIDIA RTX IO, working with Microsoft's DirectStorage API, enables GPU-based loading and decompression, accelerating I/O up to 100x over hard drives and traditional storage APIs. DLSS gains a 9x super-resolution factor, making 8K ray-traced gaming at 60 fps feasible, and the display engine supports HDMI 2.1, DisplayPort 1.4a with DSC, HDCP 2.3, 4K120 and 8K60 outputs. GA10x also includes fifth-generation NVDEC with hardware decode for MPEG-2, VC-1, H.264, H.265, VP8, VP9 and AV1 (NVIDIA's first hardware AV1 decode), plus seventh-generation NVENC for encoding up to 4K H.264 and 8K HEVC. Ampere GPUs are described as up to 1.9x more power efficient than Turing at equal performance. Additional products include the GA102-based A40 data center GPU with 48 GB memory (scalable to 96 GB via NVLink) and up to 2x FP32, 2x ray-tracing and 5x/10x-with-sparsity AI throughput versus the Quadro RTX 6000; the RTX A6000 with 48 GB GDDR6; the RTX 3090 with 82 SMs, 10,496 CUDA Cores and 24 GB GDDR6X; and the GA104-based RTX 3070, which supports GDDR6X but ships with GDDR6.

The report analyzes public financing instruments for European cleantech start-ups and SMEs, particularly those linked to Horizon 2020, which had €80 billion in funding capacity for 2014–2020. Common financing forms include loans, equity, grants, and guarantees, supporting areas such as energy efficiency, smart cities, ICT, renewable energy, and healthcare. The EIB and EIF are prominent managing bodies alongside the EBRD, EUREKA, and the European Commission; instruments may fund companies directly or through financial intermediaries. Instruments are benchmarked by portfolio and investment size, application success, technology readiness, consortium requirements, project duration, financing share, monitoring, application procedures, and target company type. Most target SMEs, while some also include research institutions. Additional support includes coaching, training, advisory services, commercialization, IP protection, financial management, R&D cooperation, and business acceleration. The report also covers fund descriptions, growth opportunities, strategic imperatives, founder-oriented guidance, and an appendix.

The speaker urges Washington residents to respond generously to the calamity affecting Johnstown and neighboring Pennsylvania communities. He reports that Jacksonville’s relief association authorized $2,000 for Johnstown’s sufferers and suggests three committees: one to collect food for immediate shipment to Williamsport, where thousands are hungry, homeless, and penniless; one to gather clothing and bedding for displaced families; and one of businesspeople and bankers to collect funds for rebuilding and refurnishing demolished homes. He concludes by noting his own contribution to Johnstown’s relief.

The Tennessee National Wildlife Refuge’s headquarters and Visitor Center will close August 21, as the area is outside the total eclipse zone. Cross Creeks NWR in Dover will host viewing, provide parking and information assistance, sell eclipse glasses, and experience about 55 seconds of totality at 1:25 p.m. CDT.

The Louisiana Court of Appeal, Fourth Circuit, affirmed William Brock’s conviction and ten-year sentence at hard labor for molestation of a juvenile. The three-year-old victim reported pain, and her mother found one of Brock’s pubic hairs in the child’s private area. A physician found vaginal redness and abrasion, concluded the trauma most likely resulted from manual digital manipulation, and ruled out self-manipulation. Testimony described the child’s fear and stiffness around Brock, his supervisory role, and his statement that Brock had touched her private area. Brock denied wrongdoing but acknowledged that no other man had the opportunity to molest the child.

The court held that the evidence established beyond reasonable doubt that Brock committed a lewd act, acted with intent to arouse or gratify sexual desires, and used control or psychological intimidation. It rejected Brock’s claim of insufficient evidence.

The court also found the sentence was not excessive. The trial court considered mitigating and aggravating factors, including permanent harm to the victim and her mother, and determined probation was inappropriate. Because the sentence was five years below the statutory maximum and supported by the offense’s circumstances, the court affirmed both the conviction and sentence.

The study examined pre-service teachers’ attitudes toward and opinions of the Research Methods in Education course at Bayburt University. Using a mixed-method, sequential explanatory design, 190 students from Turkish, English, and Pre-School Teaching departments completed a researcher-developed 21-item attitude scale, while 10 purposively selected students participated in focus-group interviews. The scale measured contribution to the profession, self-confidence, and contribution to daily and professional life and demonstrated acceptable validity and reliability.

Attitudes did not differ significantly by department, but they differed significantly by grade level, with fourth-year students scoring higher than first-year students. Most participants considered the course necessary, reporting gains in scientific research skills, research ethics and analysis, computer use, personal development, and preparation for teaching. Major teaching concerns were insufficient lesson time for applications, the lecturer’s teaching approach, and software licensing or material problems. Recommendations included providing prerequisite knowledge before the course, offering it in the third or fourth year, taking measurement and evaluation before research methods, and making the course compulsory, extending its duration and credits, or dividing it into two courses.

Centrica’s shares have fallen 35% over the past year, leaving an 8.6% dividend yield nearly three times inflation and attractive to income investors. Regulatory uncertainty and a difficult business-model transition have weakened sentiment, but the stock trades at about 10 times earnings, with earnings expected to rise 7% this year. This supports potential medium-term growth, although volatility and limited dividend growth remain risks.

Volution reported 11.6% revenue growth and a 6.7% increase in adjusted operating profit to £18.3 million. Its margin fell 90 basis points due to lower-margin acquisitions. Following its acquisition of New Zealand supplier Simx, it expects bottom-line growth of 6% this year and 7% next year. Its 2.2% yield is covered 3.3 times by profit, suggesting room for faster dividend increases.

At his final press conference, President Bush thanked the press corps, describing his relationship with reporters as professional and expressing appreciation for their work. He said he would ask Congress for the remaining $350 billion in financial aid only if President-elect Obama specifically requested it, while supporting an Obama-congressional plan for the funds.

On Gaza, Bush said a sustainable ceasefire required Hamas to stop firing rockets and called for Egypt to help prevent arms smuggling. He affirmed Israel’s right to defend itself while urging consideration of civilians and humanitarian aid. He said peace required two democratic states living side by side and described Palestinian security forces, economic development, democracy, and opposition from extremist groups as major challenges.

Bush identified a possible attack on the U.S. homeland as the most urgent threat facing Obama, saying North Korea and Iran also remained dangerous. He urged strong verification of North Korea’s commitments and warned against sacrificing constitutional protections for popularity.

He urged the Republican Party to adopt a broad, compassionate, inclusive message, particularly on immigration. Defending his Iraq policy, he cited the troop surge, saying he sent 30,000 additional troops rather than accept the status quo and that the situation later changed. On the economy, he said his administration inherited and ended amid a recession while recording 52 months of uninterrupted job growth. He defended tax cuts, acknowledged temporarily departing from free-market principles during the financial crisis, and said emergency measures were beginning to thaw credit markets.

Acknowledging criticisms of his presidency, Bush said hard decisions cannot be judged fully until history provides perspective. He identified the “Mission Accomplished” aircraft-carrier event and some of his rhetoric as mistakes, described the absence of weapons of mass destruction and Abu Ghraib as major disappointments, and said landing Air Force One after Hurricane Katrina presented logistical and law-enforcement problems. He also said pursuing Social Security reform immediately after the 2004 election, rather than immigration reform, was a mistake. He declined to discuss possible pardons.

Rejecting claims that America’s moral standing had been damaged, Bush said many foreign audiences continued to view the country as strong, compassionate, and committed to freedom. He criticized European criticism of the Iraq war and noted that governments criticizing Guantanamo had declined to accept detainees.

Bush warned that Obama would face difficult economic decisions and attacks from political opponents. He welcomed policy criticism while emphasizing the need for respectful discourse and expressed hope that Obama could serve as a unifying figure. He also expressed concern about protectionism, called the failure to pass trade agreements with Colombia, Panama, and South Korea a disappointment, and described New Orleans reconstruction as incomplete but progressing. Reflecting on Obama’s election, he called it evidence of progress in race relations while acknowledging further work remained.

After leaving office, Bush said he expected to remain actively engaged, possibly through writing or speaking, and acknowledged that the presidency’s responsibilities and security concerns would follow him. He closed by thanking the press again and wishing Obama, reporters, and their families well.

A cross-sectional survey examined culturally sensitive mentorship needs among entry-level occupational therapy students at a large urban private university. Of 133 respondents, 59 identified as BIPOC, Hispanic/Latinx, or biracial and did not identify as white. Although 89.5% had previously received formal or informal mentorship, only 34% reported currently having a mentor; most preferred a combination of formal and informal mentoring.

Students prioritized mentors’ personality, relevant expertise, availability, shared interests, and sometimes shared ethnic or cultural backgrounds. Nearly 90% considered mentors’ awareness of biases and prejudices at least somewhat important, with BIPOC students rating this more highly than white students. Hispanic/Latinx students more often reported that mentors were less effective at working across cultural differences and integrating personal life with academic responsibilities. Desired mentor qualities included cultural humility, empathy, anti-racism allyship, and support for navigating microaggressions, discrimination, and cultural isolation. Students also sought guidance on clinical practice, certification, job searches, networking, sponsorship, work-life balance, confidence, and well-being, with regular communication especially important.

The authors recommend flexible programs combining formal, informal, and virtual mentoring; recruitment of diverse mentors; training in cultural humility, implicit bias, and anti-racism; and institutional support, funding, and co-development. Limitations include the single urban setting, cross-sectional design, absence of program-year data, and primary focus on race and ethnicity. Future research should include diverse institutions, longitudinal tracking, and intersecting identities such as gender, LGBTQ+ status, and disability.

In an underlying action seeking rescission of a house sale or damages for alleged fraud, the defendants were served in California. The Denver district court rejected their challenge to the service, ruled they were Colorado residents, and ordered them to answer. They sought prohibition from the Colorado Supreme Court, arguing that the trial court lacked personal jurisdiction.

The undisputed evidence showed that the defendants had left Colorado in September 1951 for health reasons, had no intention of returning, and had settled in Ventura, California. They obtained California licenses and voter registration, employment, land for a permanent home, and a telephone connection. Under the applicable service rule, personal service outside Colorado was permitted on Colorado residents. Once the defendants demonstrated that they were no longer Colorado residents, the burden shifted to the plaintiffs to prove residency, which they failed to do.

Residence was held to depend on bona fide intent supported by conduct, and the defendants’ California voter registration strongly established their change of residence. The court held that service in California was invalid and that the trial court therefore lacked jurisdiction over the defendants. The rule to show cause was made absolute.

European markets reached record highs, with the STOXX 600 gaining about 0.5% as steel and banking stocks rallied. Proposed cuts to tariff-free steel import quotas supported steelmakers, while stable bond yields and improving credit margins boosted banks. Expectations of U.S. Federal Reserve easing lifted risk appetite and pushed gold above $4,000 an ounce. BMW declined after lowering its 2025 profit forecast due to U.S. tariffs and weaker Chinese demand. Analysts cited strong industrial production and steady earnings but warned that sticky inflation, trade tensions, or changes in monetary-policy expectations could pressure valuations.
