In 2016–17, U.S. colleges and universities were expected to award more than one million bachelor’s degrees. Nearly two-fifths of postsecondary enrollment in 2016 consisted of students over 24, many balancing work, family responsibilities, and education. Timothy P. Slottow advised working adults returning to school to establish a support system; research programs, costs, and institutional resources; seek credit for prior learning and work or military experience; and evaluate scheduling options, including night classes and online learning. He said successful working students need flexible but structured programs, experienced faculty, and career-relevant education.

This longitudinal, nonrandomized study compared antibody and T-cell responses induced by Covaxin and Covishield in healthy Indian adults aged 18–45. It enrolled 691 participants at four Bengaluru and Pune sites, with 506 completing both doses and follow-up through two weeks post-vaccination without symptomatic infection. Vaccine choice was participant-selected; Covaxin was given at four-week intervals and Covishield at 12-week intervals. Participants were stratified by baseline serostatus, and staggered recruitment spanned the Delta and Omicron waves.

Both vaccines significantly increased anti-spike antibodies, but Covishield generally produced higher seroconversion rates, antibody titers, neutralization, and broader variant-specific activity. Among baseline-seronegative participants, second-dose seroconversion was 98.3% for Covishield versus 74.4% for Covaxin; among seropositive participants, at-least-two-fold titer increases after the second dose were 91.7% and 66.9%, respectively. Covishield significantly increased authentic-virus neutralizing antibodies, whereas Covaxin did not produce statistically significant increases. Covishield also elicited stronger CD4 and CD8 responses; both vaccines increased CD4 responses in seronegative participants, but detectable spike-specific CD8 responses occurred only with Covishield. Neither vaccine clearly induced Omicron-specific antibodies in seronegative participants, while one Covishield dose elicited measurable responses in some seropositive participants.

Cohorts sampled around Omicron showed higher Covaxin responses and more comparable immunogenicity between vaccines, complicating direct comparisons and durability assessment. Apparent asymptomatic infection was inferred from antibody changes without confirmatory RT-PCR testing. Nonresponse was associated with higher pre-vaccination antibody titers. Because non-neutralizing antibodies were not measured, durability was confounded by Omicron exposure, and correlates of protection for Covaxin were unavailable, the immunogenicity findings could not establish comparative vaccine efficacy.

A player discusses the Stanley Cup Finals, calling it exciting for many first-time participants and saying overenthusiasm can cause players to do too much. He expects the series to intensify physically as the opponent, which scored five road goals without winning, is likely angry with itself. Praising both goaltenders, he recommends generating traffic, moving Boucher side to side, controlling the puck, and wearing down an opponent whose defensemen, including Pronger, log heavy minutes. His team generally outshot and outcontrolled opponents throughout the year, but he says it must improve puck management and earn more power plays, as playing an entire game without one is unrealistic.

The Yankee concept is a pro-style shot play centered on a post-dig combination from opposite sides of the formation. It is often used in multiple running back or tight end sets to encourage 1-high safety looks, creating a natural high-low opportunity. Against Cover 1 and Cover 3, the quarterback can throw the post if the free safety plays shallow or find the dig over linebacker level if the safety drops deep. Against Cover 2 and Cover 4, the concept is less effective against two-high coverage, and the quarterback should transition quickly to underneath routes.

Typical route assignments include a tight end crossing route, a tailback check route, a fullback arrow, an X receiver dig, and a Z receiver post. Against zone coverage, the tight end may sit in voids. The quarterback’s primary progression is post, dig, crosser, then a check-down, with quicker movement underneath against two-high coverage. On deep posts, the quarterback throws to the opposite hash and leads the Z receiver across the field.

Variations include presenting the same concept in a 2x2 formation and adding shallow whip routes underneath. In 2x2, the slot receiver runs an underneath crossing route while the quarterback retains the same progression. Whip routes can occupy linebackers, create separation underneath, and potentially clear a throwing lane for the X receiver’s dig, though the post-dig remains the concept’s primary shot.

A study in Science Advances led by Alessandro Silvano reports that warm water is already pooling beneath Antarctic glaciers in two regions with notable ice loss: the Amundsen Sea in West Antarctica and the Sabrina Coast in East Antarctica. Normally, holes in Antarctic ice cool shelf waters, producing dense shelf water that sinks to form Antarctic bottom water. Instead, in these regions, rapidly melting glaciers keep warm water warm, creating a positive feedback that melts ice shelves from below. Researchers say a similar process may have triggered 16 feet of sea-level rise at the end of the last glacial period. Such ice shelf collapse could produce a "pulse" scenario, with experts estimating South Florida could see 10 to 30 feet of sea-level rise by 2100 — far above current Miami predictions of 7 to 8 feet. Reduced Antarctic bottom water could also slow global ocean currents, contributing to more superstorms and faster atmospheric warming, which in turn accelerates melt. The authors emphasize that much remains unknown but that halting global temperature rise, driven by fossil fuel burning, is essential.

The speaker, overwhelmed by unexpectedly assuming major responsibilities, says his future policy will be demonstrated by his actions. Guided by his past conduct and commitment to free government and popular rights, he believes the government will prevail through present perils and asks his colleagues and other patriots for support.

Zebronics launched the Buddy Speaker for Rs. 1,699. The 630g portable speaker has a 5-watt RMS output, LED display, RGB lighting, and a rechargeable battery providing up to three hours of playback. It supports Bluetooth with a 10-meter range, FM radio, USB, MicroSD, and AUX.

The passage argues that expanding workforce pathways should begin with stronger access to traditional construction apprenticeships, which are highly selective and favor students with prior knowledge, advanced coursework, and the ability to navigate cumbersome applications. Short-term pre-apprenticeships can expose participants to careers and employers, build skills, provide mentors and credentials, and prepare them for apprenticeship assessments. Their growth is constrained by inadequate funding, limited capacity, insufficient outcome data, and barriers such as transportation, childcare, and lost wages. The author recommends income-dependent loans or emergency credit, partnerships among unions, employers, and others to repay those loans, and better tracking of graduation, apprenticeship placement, and long-term employment. Strategic investment could help programs attract additional funding, strengthen the construction talent pipeline, and improve economic mobility.

An AI tool named Waldo scanned more than 430,000 Reddit posts about cannabis and flagged over 28,000 as potentially describing harmful side effects. Researchers reviewed 250 flagged posts and found that 86% described problematic cannabis experiences. Waldo was trained using 10,000 manually reviewed posts, outperformed ChatGPT by producing 18 times fewer false positives, but did not surpass human reviewers. Researchers said the tool could help public health workers identify adverse effects shared online, especially where formal monitoring or medical reporting is limited. They cautioned that its performance on other drugs or products is uncertain and that any social-media monitoring would require privacy protections and ethical safeguards.

This non-peer-reviewed preprint presents RoboDoc, a prototype medical conversational-AI application that uses OpenAI API function calling to integrate specialized diagnostic models. Built with Angular and TypeScript, the chatbot accepts text or images, extracts relevant parameters or selects an appropriate model, invokes it, and generates a conversational response.

The system integrates three models: a TensorFlow.js diabetes detector using six clinical features and 2,000 balanced Kaggle samples; a Teachable Machine chest X-ray model classifying normal lungs, bacterial pneumonia, and viral pneumonia; and a Teachable Machine OCT model classifying normal eyes, drusen, diabetic macular edema, and choroidal neovascularization. The OCT pathway includes a stub appointment function that prioritizes cases by severity and could later connect to booking or calendar APIs.

The literature review describes chatbots as potential interfaces, triage tools, and clinical assistants rather than replacements for healthcare professionals, while emphasizing nondeterministic outputs, misinformation, ethical and legal concerns, and the need for human oversight. It also identifies limited research on integrating specialized medical models into task-oriented LLM chatbots.

In illustrative, non-statistical tests, the text-triggered pathway behaved as expected. The diabetes model’s training and validation accuracy converged around 90%. X-ray per-class accuracy ranged from 97% for normal images to 66% for viral pneumonia, with 99% training and 81% testing accuracy overall. OCT per-class accuracy ranged from 88% for drusen to 98% for CNV, with 99% training and 91% testing accuracy. Most image predictions were correct, but diabetic macular edema was confused with drusen and not marked urgent, viral pneumonia was incorrectly marked urgent, and normal lungs tended to be classified as pneumonia.

The author describes the architecture as a generic, extensible “Lego” approach in which independently developed models can be added or updated through function calling. Limitations include possible medical errors, incorrect or irrelevant function calls, token limits, incompatibility with object-oriented methods, and the current separation of text- and image-triggered paths. Proposed improvements include integrating both pathways, adding COVID-19 detection, refining prompts or fine-tuning models, and simplifying model management.

Most enterprises outsource HPC workloads: 87% use or plan external infrastructure, 74% operate or plan owned systems in colocation datacenters, and 43% use or plan research institutions. Only 6% currently operate on-premises infrastructure, while 28% plan to.

NVIDIA’s Turing GPU architecture introduces a hybrid rendering model combining rasterization, real-time ray tracing, AI, and simulation. Enhanced Tensor Cores add INT8 and INT4 modes for quantized inference while supporting FP16, accelerating matrix operations used in neural-network training and inference. They also enable NVIDIA NGX services for gaming and client applications, including Deep Learning Super Sampling (DLSS), AI InPainting, AI Slow-Mo, and AI Super Rez.

The first Turing-based data-center GPU, Tesla T4, includes 2,560 CUDA Cores and 320 Tensor Cores, with stated performance of up to 130 TOPS for INT8 and 260 TOPS for INT4 inference. NVIDIA claims it delivers up to 40 times the inference performance and more than 50 times the energy efficiency of CPU-based inference. The T4 also supports enhanced video decoding, Multi-Process Service, 16 GB of memory, and 320 GB/s of bandwidth.

Turing introduces GDDR6 memory with 14 Gbps signaling and 20% better power efficiency than Pascal’s GDDR5X. Larger L2 caches and improved lossless compression produce roughly 50% higher effective bandwidth. Its display engine supports DisplayPort 1.4a, DSC 1.2, HDR with BT.2100 tone mapping, and two 8K 60 Hz displays. The enhanced NVENC encoder supports HEVC 8K encoding at 30 fps and offers bitrate savings, while NVDEC adds HEVC 4:4:4 and VP9 HDR formats. USB-C and VirtualLink consolidate VR display, power, and data connections. Turing also replaces MIO-based SLI transfers with faster NVLink connections.

Dedicated RT Cores accelerate BVH traversal and ray-triangle intersection testing, freeing streaming multiprocessors for other work. Combined with rasterization, denoising, and BVH acceleration, they enable real-time ray tracing, including physically correct reflections, refractions, shadows, contact-hardening shadows, and ambient occlusion. NVIDIA describes Turing as processing over 10 billion rays per second and delivering roughly ten times Pascal’s software-based ray-tracing performance.

NGX provides pre-trained AI models through a thin API integrated with the NVIDIA driver. DLSS reconstructs high-quality target-resolution images from lower-resolution inputs, producing quality similar to temporal anti-aliasing with roughly half the shading work; a separate DLSS 2X mode approaches 64-times-supersampled quality. AI InPainting synthesizes replacement image content, AI Slow-Mo generates interpolated frames, and AI Super Rez performs 2x, 4x, or 8x image and video upscaling.

Turing also adds Mesh Shading, whose task and mesh shaders use cooperative processing to reduce CPU draw-call bottlenecks and support large numbers of objects, level-of-detail selection, and dynamic geometry manipulation. Variable Rate Shading controls shading independently for each 16-by-16-pixel region, enabling content-adaptive, motion-adaptive, and foveated rendering while optionally increasing shading for MSAA. Texture Space Shading separates visibility and appearance sampling, allowing shaded results to be stored, reused, and sampled at independently selected rates for improved temporal stability and VR efficiency.

Multi-View Rendering processes up to four hardware views per pass and up to 32 views at the API level, reusing geometry across stereo VR, multiple projections, character instances, and cascaded shadow maps. The TU102 contains 576 Tensor Cores; TU104 contains 368 Tensor Cores and 48 RT Cores, while the T4 uses a configuration with 320 Tensor Cores. TU106, used in GeForce RTX 2070, contains 288 Tensor Cores and 36 RT Cores but supports neither NVLink nor SLI.

NVIDIA also introduces RTX-OPS, a workload-weighted metric combining Tensor, FP32 CUDA, RT Core, and INT32 operations according to their expected utilization during a hybrid-rendering frame. The publication concludes with accuracy, warranty, liability, licensing, trademark, and copyright notices.

NASA ambassador Theo Wellington told the Wilson County Commission that the total solar eclipse will be the biggest public one-day event in U.S. history, noting Wilson County's central location in the 70-mile-wide path of totality, where maximum viewing lasts 2 minutes and 40 seconds—only two seconds short of the fairground's duration. She said the last total eclipse seen in Tennessee occurred in 1869, that half the U.S. population is within a day's drive of the path, and that populations along it may double, with St. Joseph, Mo., expecting 100,000 extra visitors. She said the event is emotional and challenges the senses, while areas outside the path see only a partial eclipse. The commission also voted to let retiring sheriffs and deputies keep their service weapons under 2006 state law requiring a two-thirds vote and 15 years of service, with Commissioners Terry Ashe and Gary Keith abstaining. Separately, it approved a $10,000 amendment for a school resource officer at the new Springdale Elementary, opening in August, and noted rezoning of 500 Stoner Creek and 200 Elzie D. Patton students.

The article identifies Williams %R as the best swing trading indicator among six tested: Williams %R, WilliamsVixFix, Bollinger Bands, Stochastic, Internal Bar Strength, and RSI. Backtests using SPY as an S&P 500 proxy favored Williams %R for its stable results and lowest average maximum drawdown, which improved its risk-adjusted return. Stochastic and IBS also performed reasonably well, while RSI performed poorly after 2015; Bollinger Bands and WilliamsVixFix experienced comparatively high drawdowns. Risk-adjusted return is calculated by dividing annualized geometric return by market exposure. Swing trading typically lasts one day to a few weeks, with 1–15 days recommended for indicator time frames. The article cautions that results vary by asset, past performance does not guarantee future results, and discipline is needed because even small drawdowns are difficult to manage.

This continuation application describes video encoding and decoding methods and apparatuses for improving HEVC prediction efficiency. It addresses brightness changes, motion-vector accuracy, intra-prediction accuracy, and signaling overhead. Weighted inter-prediction applies multiplication and addition parameters, derived through regression analysis or adjacent reconstructed pixels, to reference blocks. Motion information and weight parameters may be merged with neighboring blocks, with flags, indices, or difference values encoded; when not merged, parameters are transmitted separately. Motion-vector precision may be increased using reconstructed pixels adjacent to the current block.

Intra-prediction corrections may use coefficients derived from a previously processed block having a similar reconstructed-pixel area and intra-prediction mode. Candidate blocks can be selected using standard deviation, averages, SAD, or SSD, and the correction coefficient or selected candidate may be signaled. Intra-prediction modes may be efficiently coded using candidate modes based on neighboring modes, differences from a previous block, or merge indicators. The invention also describes dividing a current block into sub-blocks and applying prediction and weights to each sub-block.

The encoding apparatus includes block division, intra/inter prediction, transform, quantization, entropy coding, inverse processing, filtering, and memory units; the decoding apparatus performs the corresponding reverse operations.

Organized patriotism, substituting loyalty to the whole nation for local or sectional pride, is essential to national growth. Sections and classes must cooperate; industrial and agricultural groups, capitalists and wageworkers, must work together. Effective education is also crucial, although federalism limits national leadership in technical education and leaves much responsibility to the states.

Priority should be given to practical technical and industrial training, including commercial training that addresses foreign trade and prepares students for skilled manual work. The National Government should ensure District of Columbia schools provide such education and enact advanced child-labor and factory laws as an example to the states.

Farming must become more technical and scientific, with practical education, improved cultivation, and better farmer organization. National success must rest not only on material prosperity but on the moral, mental, and physical development of workers and farmers.

Microsoft Corporation's Form 10-Q for the quarter ended September 30, 2015 (first quarter of fiscal 2016) reports unaudited consolidated financial statements and accompanying notes.

Results: Revenue was $20,379 million versus $23,201 million a year earlier, a 12% decline; gross margin was $13,172 million versus $14,928 million; operating income $5,793 million versus $5,844 million; net income $4,620 million versus $4,540 million; diluted EPS $0.57 versus $0.54; and dividends declared per share of $0.36 versus $0.31. The revenue decrease reflected lower More Personal Computing revenue, notably phones reflecting a changed phone strategy, and a net $1.3 billion Windows 10 revenue deferral, partly offset by Intelligent Cloud growth; foreign currency had an unfavorable impact of about 5% on revenue and 6% on gross margin.

Segments (recast for the new fiscal 2016 structure): Productivity and Business Processes revenue fell 3% to $6,306 million with operating income of $3,105 million; Intelligent Cloud revenue rose 8% to $5,892 million with operating income of $2,400 million; More Personal Computing revenue fell 17% to $9,381 million with operating income of $1,562 million; Corporate and Other reported a $1,274 million operating loss.

Balance sheet and cash flow: Total assets were $172,896 million (versus $176,223 million at June 30, 2015), including $99,355 million of cash, cash equivalents and short-term investments; short-term debt was $9,998 million, long-term debt $27,819 million, and total stockholders' equity $77,445 million. Net cash from operations was $8,594 million (versus $8,354 million), financing used $3,648 million including $4,757 million of stock repurchases and $2,475 million of dividends paid, and investing used $5,066 million. Cash and equivalents ended at $5,431 million. Comprehensive income was $3,836 million, with other comprehensive loss of $784 million.

Business highlights: Windows 10 was running on 110 million devices; commercial cloud annualized run rate exceeded $8.2 billion; Office 365 Consumer subscribers reached 18.2 million; Dynamics CRM Online installed base more than tripled; Azure revenue and compute more than doubled with over 20,000 Enterprise Mobility customers; and Xbox Live monthly active users grew 28% to 39 million.

Other matters: Windows 10 license revenue is recognized ratably over device lives of two to four years. The prior-year Phone Hardware Integration Plan charges totaled $1.3 billion (all in fiscal 2015), while a June 2015 Phone Hardware Restructuring Plan will eliminate up to 7,800 positions in fiscal 2016, with $780 million incurred to date and a $679 million restructuring liability. In the quarter, 89 million shares valued at $4,000 million were repurchased, leaving $17.9 billion of the $40 billion authorization; a $0.36 per share dividend of $2,875 million was declared September 15, 2015. Mojang was acquired for $2.5 billion (goodwill $1.8 billion, intangibles $928 million), and five other acquisitions closed for $395 million in cash. The effective tax rate was 16% versus 23%, with tax contingencies of $11.9 billion including a partial I.R.S. audit settlement. Legal matters include a September 29, 2015 agreement with Motorola dismissing patent actions, approximately 65 other patent cases, an SAIC antitrust investigation in China, and cell phone litigation; aggregate legal liabilities of $551 million current and $17 million long-term were accrued, with possible adverse outcomes of about $1.5 billion beyond recorded amounts. The new FASB revenue standard applies from July 1, 2018. Deloitte & Touche LLP reviewed the interim statements and noted no material modifications needed for U.S. GAAP conformity.

The leu was stable ahead of the Romanian central bank’s decision on a possible fourth interest-rate increase, with many analysts expecting a quarter-point hike to 2.75%. Tightening money markets, with three-month ROBOR up about 120 basis points to 3.17%, has left the leu less affected than other Central European currencies. The leu traded flat at 4.6576 per euro, while the forint and Czech crown each gained 0.2% as the yuan recovered. Dollar-driven selling has caused substantial losses for regional currencies this year. Hungary’s central bank has shifted away from ultra-low rates and discussed inflation trends with analysts amid concern that inflation could exceed its target. Romanian government bonds traded sideways, with the expected policy decision likely affecting longer-term yields most.

Local share prices rose, with the Straits Times Index up 0.9 per cent to 3,308.69, as most Asian markets recovered after US inflation data and easing US-North Korea tensions. Hong Kong, South Korea and China gained, while Japan fell. Investors remained cautious ahead of North Korea’s Liberation Day and key US and European data. Singapore banking and property stocks led gains, while UOB fell. Olam reported a 29 per cent second-quarter net profit rise on higher revenue, whereas Asian Pay Television Trust’s quarterly profit fell 29 per cent despite increased revenue.

U.S. stocks opened higher Monday, led by technology, industrial and consumer companies, after China reported first-quarter economic growth of 6.9%, slightly above the previous quarter. The S&P 500 rose 0.5%, while the Dow, Nasdaq and Russell 2000 each gained 0.6%. Nvidia, Alphabet, Amazon and Netflix advanced. Alere jumped 16.4% after accepting Abbott Laboratories’ revised $51-per-share buyout offer. Eli Lilly and Incyte fell after the FDA requested more data and raised safety concerns about their rheumatoid arthritis drug Olumiant. Snyder’s-Lance plunged 18.6% on a weak forecast and its CEO’s retirement. Arconic rose after CEO and Chairman Klaus Kleinfeld agreed to step down, while Straight Path gained 16.5% on the possibility of a competing buyout offer. Benchmark U.S. crude fell to $53.05 a barrel, the dollar weakened against the yen and euro, and the 10-year Treasury yield slipped to 2.23%. Japan and South Korea markets edged higher; several European and Asian markets were closed for Easter.

Two TPS7H500x-SP controllers can operate in primary-secondary mode via SYNC. When RT sets the primary’s switching frequency, its SYNC outputs a clock at twice that frequency; the secondary receives this clock and operates in external synchronization, with its RT pin floating. The mode can synchronize two independent converters or form one interleaved converter by also connecting VSENSE, COMP, SS, and HICC. The secondary inverts the clock, causing a 90° or 270° phase shift between corresponding outputs.

The article demonstrates how to backtest a classic MACD trading strategy in Python using Apple historical data from Yahoo Finance. It uses yfinance to download data, pandas for manipulation, and matplotlib.pyplot for charts. The MACD is calculated as the 12-period closing-price EMA minus the 26-period EMA; its signal line is the 9-period EMA, and the histogram is the signal line minus the MACD. The strategy labels positive histogram values as 1 and assigns the signal to the following row so returns begin after the signal day. The resulting equity curve shows a 15.04% CAGR for the MACD strategy versus 19.07% annually for buy and hold, with the strategy invested 51.13% of the time. The strategy is presented for informational purposes.

Jean Chrétien and Economic Development Minister Steven Del Duca addressed about 1,000 Liberal supporters in Vaughan after the Yonge Street van attack, emphasizing unity and blood donations. Del Duca urged campaign effort despite polls favouring Doug Ford, while Chrétien praised Kathleen Wynne’s courage and achievements. Outside, LiUNA Local 183 protested budget-bill labour changes.

The paper introduces 3DPCNet, a pose-only, estimator-agnostic module that maps camera-centered 3D skeletons into a fixed, body-centered canonical frame. For 17-joint poses, a hybrid encoder combines a GCN branch modeling anatomical relationships with a Transformer branch capturing long-range joint dependencies, using cross-attention and adaptive gating. The network predicts a global 6D rotation, converted to an SO(3) matrix through Gram–Schmidt orthonormalization, and an optional residual joint correction. It is trained on synthetically rotated poses using a composite loss covering pose reconstruction, rotation accuracy, cycle consistency, bone lengths, joint angles, residual magnitude, graph structure, and attention diversity.

On MM-Fi cross-subject and cross-environment tests, 3DPCNet reduced positional error from 63–65 mm to 46–49 mm and rotation error from 20–22° to 3–4°, while generalizing across subjects and environments. Qualitative comparisons showed better alignment than a deterministic geometric baseline, although learned residual corrections produced non-zero PA-MPJPE of 37–38 mm.

On TotalCapture, using poses from an existing 3D estimator without retraining or fine-tuning, canonicalized wrist trajectories and accelerations more closely matched motion-capture and IMU references than the geometric baseline, including under a challenging lateral camera view. Limitations include minor non-rigid residual deviations, inability to recover absolute scale, sensitivity to poor input skeletons and extreme viewpoints, and reliance on synthetic pose rotations that may not represent rare camera geometries. Proposed future work includes rigid residual constraints, temporal modeling and uncertainty, scale and gravity estimation, and end-to-end clinical and performance validation.

New federal tax rules will change payroll withholding beginning in February, when employers must use the IRS’s 2018 tables by Feb. 15. About 90% of workers may receive more take-home pay, but amounts depend on income, filing status, children, pay frequency and W-4 allowances. A married couple earning $90,000 with two children under 17 could receive about $61 more per semi-monthly paycheck, while a single person earning $35,000 without children could receive nearly $32 more.

The child tax credit doubled to $2,000 per qualifying child for 2018, allowing more higher-income families to receive the full credit. Taxpayers should review their W-4 forms because outdated allowances could cause inaccurate withholding or a 2019 tax bill. An updated form and IRS withholding calculator are expected by early spring and the end of February, respectively.

The 2018 standard deduction rises to $24,000 for married couples and $12,000 for singles, potentially making itemized deductions unnecessary for many taxpayers. Home-equity-loan interest is no longer deductible, and combined deductions for personal property, real estate and state and local income taxes are capped at $10,000. Mortgage interest remains deductible within specified loan limits.

The supplemental-wage withholding rate on bonuses fell from 25% to 22%, so a $5,000 bonus would have $1,100 withheld rather than $1,250.

Four-star Christian Brothers defensive lineman Bill Norton committed to Georgia over nine other schools. The 6-foot-6, 270-pound prospect ranked 11th nationally among strong-side defensive ends and was the reigning TSSAA Division II-AAA Mr. Football.

ICT adoption since the 1990s has expanded online education across African universities alongside more flexible higher-education systems, national digital strategies, and telecommunications deregulation. However, African institutions still face weak ICT policies, inadequate infrastructure and internet affordability, shortages of skilled personnel, limited access to digital materials, faculty resistance, insufficient digital training, and difficulties adapting pedagogy. Rural–urban internet disparities and COVID-19 further exposed preparedness gaps. War compounds these problems by damaging educational infrastructure, disrupting programmes, depleting finances and staff, and hindering ICT deployment. Online education can maintain learning, expand access, and build digital skills during conflict, but requires targeted training and investment.

The study investigates the limited literature on wartime and online education in African higher education using bibliometric analysis. Scopus was searched for publications from 2000–2024, with 2,140 initial results narrowed to 90 documents and then 53 included after screening for social sciences. Microsoft Excel and VOSviewer were used for descriptive analysis and visualization. The 53 publications were led by the United States with 21, Ukraine with 10, the United Kingdom and France with two each, and Poland and several other countries with one each; five were unassigned. A narrower search for war, education, and online learning returned only Ukraine, Austria, and the United States. No African country appeared in either set.

Publications included 40 articles, nine book chapters, and one each of conference papers, editorials, and letters. Social sciences accounted for 52 publications, followed by arts and humanities with 23. Annual output fluctuated between 2009 and 2024, peaking at 12 publications in 2023 before falling to five in 2024. Keyword analysis found largely disconnected terms in the wider wartime-and-education corpus, while the narrower search produced two clusters: learning, including e-learning, online learning, and online teaching; and warfare, including students, teachers, Ukraine, and war.

The findings identify a substantial research gap concerning wartime online learning in Africa. The authors call for expanded research, effective conflict-sensitive online-learning strategies, and attention to organisational sustainability and Sustainable Development Goals. Limitations include reliance on Scopus alone and no analysis of authorship, affiliations, citations, or reference connections. Proposed future research addresses war-related brain drain, psychological trauma among students and faculty, and inclusive online learning for people with disabilities.

Richard “Dick” Tuck, a former Democratic Party operative known for political pranks against Richard Nixon, died Monday at age 94 in Tucson, Arizona, longtime friend and estate executor Lorraine Glicksman said. His pranks included arranging a sparsely attended 1958 Nixon campus event, posing as a fire marshal and hiring an elderly woman to console Nixon after his 1960 debate with John F. Kennedy. During Nixon’s 1962 San Francisco Chinatown campaign, an infiltrator displayed a sign questioning the Hughes loan to Nixon’s brother, prompting Nixon to tear it up. Nixon’s 1968 campaign later destroyed “Nixon’s the one” buttons over fears of similar stunts. Tuck also worked on Robert F. Kennedy’s 1968 campaign, unsuccessfully ran for California’s Senate in 1966 and later proposed a “Nixmas” holiday marking Nixon’s 1974 resignation.

Mathieu Henderson completed his four-year Ontario Hockey League career with the Flint Firebirds, finishing ninth among OHL defencemen in scoring with 10 goals and 44 assists in 68 games. The 21-year-old said he exceeded expectations and credited his coaches, whose emphasis on defence helped create offensive opportunities; his plus/minus improved from minus-45 to minus-seven. Flint was eliminated 4-1 by Sault Ste. Marie in the first playoff round, though Henderson scored Flint’s first playoff goal. He joined the ECHL’s South Carolina Stingrays, playing three games before the playoffs began. Henderson is undecided between professional hockey in North America or Europe and school, but intends to continue playing. He also credited his parents, Randy and Brenda, as his greatest supporters.

The lecture reviews VCG mechanisms for private-value social choice problems, where players privately know their types, utilities depend on selected alternatives and transfers, and the utilitarian solution maximizes total utility. A mechanism maps reported strategies to allocations and payments. Second- and first-price auctions implement the utilitarian allocation, but under dominant-strategy and Bayesian Nash equilibrium, respectively. The VCG mechanism asks players to report their types, selects the utilitarian alternative, and charges each player the negative externality imposed on others. It truthfully implements the utilitarian solution in dominant strategies and applies even when alternatives are not simple goods. However, VCG is generally not budget balanced, requires payments to flow outside the set of players, and can be computationally infeasible when the number of possible allocations is enormous, as illustrated by the simultaneous U.S. cellular-service license auctions.

The lecture then turns to online markets and Google. Google is described as the dominant global search engine, with reported worldwide share above 90%, very high profits, and revenue that supports products including Android, Gmail, Chrome, Chrome OS, Google Docs, Google Cloud, and Google Meet. The U.S. Department of Justice and several states have accused Google of monopolizing search or online advertising. Google runs an advertising auction for each search, and the number of ads shown varies with the commercial nature of the query. Advertisers submit standing per-click bids specifying conditions such as keywords, exclusions, location, and age. Google matches applicable bids, multiplies each bid by a quality score, ranks advertisers by that product, and selects up to 11 ads. Payment occurs only after a click, at the quality-adjusted threshold needed to retain the next ad’s position. Quality scores are crucial in pay-per-click auctions because they favor advertisers likely to satisfy users rather than merely those offering high profits on rare or accidental clicks.

Edelman, Ostrovsky, and Schwarz model Google’s auction as a generalized second-price or equivalent clock auction. Truthful bidding is not generally optimal because a bidder may gain nearly the same number of clicks in a lower position at a lower payment. Consequently, bidders shade their bids. Despite this nontruthful equilibrium, the resulting payment schedule reproduces VCG payments. This gives the mechanism efficiency and an ex-post-equilibrium property: advertisers need not continually reprice their bids in response to competitors. VCG-equivalent payments also transfer revenue from advertisers to Google and make it difficult for a competing search engine to undercut Google’s prices while preserving ad quality.

Athey and Ellison extend the position-auction model by adding consumer search. Consumers incur costs when clicking, advertisers privately differ in the probability that their products meet consumers’ needs, and ordering ads by quality guides consumers toward promising links. In this setting, reserve prices need not reduce welfare: they can signal that displayed ads are worth attention, increase clicks, and reduce costly random searching. With uniformly distributed search costs, consumer surplus and social welfare are maximized at the same reserve price. Expected social welfare equals three times expected consumer surplus, while advertiser plus Google surplus equals twice consumer surplus. A Google-profit-maximizing reserve can differ from the consumer optimum and reduce advertiser and consumer welfare. The discussion also considers richer information design, position-specific reserves, and diversity weighting to create a “shopping mall” of distinct ads.

Two related papers are briefly summarized. Anderson and Renault allow sellers to choose prices strategically after obtaining positions; a leading seller may lower its price to prevent consumers from searching lower positions, producing multiple equilibria with different consumer and firm welfare. Armstrong and Zhou examine how platforms should reveal information about competing products. The fully consumer-optimal allocation is unattainable because informing consumers about preferences gives sellers market power, while minimal preference information can intensify price competition. Information design mainly redistributes surplus between consumers and producers rather than greatly changing aggregate social welfare. The lecture concludes by previewing empirical work on online retail and consumer preferences.

GST is on track for a July 1 rollout, but the civil aviation ministry sought a two-month deferral, saying airlines need time to adapt systems. Carriers including Air India cite ticket-system changes, unclear taxation of aircraft parts and higher costs. Jayant Sinha chaired a preparedness meeting; Revenue Secretary Hasmukh Adhia denied delay rumours.

The patent describes embodiments for managing indexed machine-generated data, particularly optimizing index-file size according to storage conditions associated with the indexed data. Priority applications are incorporated by reference.

In a Splunk-like event-based intake and query system, forwarders collect, annotate, and route raw data from diverse sources; indexers parse the data into timestamped events, apply source-specific transformations, and store events in time-bucketed data stores; and search heads distribute queries across indexers and combine the results. A late-binding schema applies extraction rules, including regular expressions, at search time, enabling analysis of retained raw data and correlation of fields across heterogeneous sources.

The disclosure also describes client-side monitoring of network, device, and application performance; search interfaces; hierarchical search-time data models for filtering event sets and generating reports and visualizations; and acceleration techniques including parallel query processing, keyword indexes, summarization tables, and intermediate summaries for recurring reports. Additional embodiments cover security monitoring and alerts, VMware data-center performance analysis, cloud-based deployment, clustered environments, and searching externally archived data. Drawings depict the intake, query, reporting, monitoring, cloud, and clustering architectures, along with original and optimized index-file diagrams and a process for optimizing index files based on storage conditions.

The IRS announced inflation-adjusted federal income tax brackets for tax year 2026, applicable to returns filed in 2027. The standard deduction rises to $32,200 for married couples filing jointly and $16,100 for single filers. The 37% top rate applies to individuals with taxable income above $640,600 and joint filers with income of $768,700 or more. The IRS also updated long-term capital gains brackets, estate and gift tax exemptions, earned income tax credit eligibility, and child tax credit provisions. The announcement came a day after the IRS said it would furlough nearly half its workforce because of the government shutdown.

This passage is an excerpt from the SEV-ES Guest-Hypervisor Communication Block (GHCB) specification. It defines the GHCB MSR (0xc001_0130) protocol used by SEV-ES and SEV-SNP guests to communicate with the hypervisor via VMGEXIT.

**GHCB MSR protocol functions.** The guest writes the GHCB address and an info code (GHCBInfo); the hypervisor responds with data in GHCBData. The SEV Information request (GHCBInfo 0x001) is written by the hypervisor and supplies the GHCB's guest physical address (bits [63:12], implying 4K alignment), the maximum and minimum GHCB protocol versions (bits [63:48] and [47:32]), and the SEV page table encryption bit number (bits [31:24]). The guest selects a version within that range, sets the GHCB Protocol Version field, and terminates if the range is unsupported. The encryption bit is normally obtained via CPUID, but CPUID now raises a VMM Communication exception, so the hypervisor must supply it (obtainable from CPUID 0x8000_001f, EBX[5:0]); the guest may instead use the CPUID request protocol (recommended for SNP). The CPUID Request (0x004) lets the guest request one CPUID register value at a time, requiring multiple VMGEXITs; it does not support functions requiring non-zero sub-leafs nor function 0x0000_000d. Other requests include getting/registering a preferred GHCB GPA (0x010–0x013), unregistering it (0x018/0x019), the hypervisor feature support request/response (0x080/0x081), and a termination request carrying reason code sets.

**GHCB GPA registration.** Registration is required and supported only for SEV-SNP guests before a GHCB is used for a VMGEXIT. A guest may request the hypervisor-preferred GHCB GPA (the hypervisor may respond with 0xf_ffff_ffff_ffff meaning no preference); the hypervisor must guarantee the returned GFN cannot otherwise be mapped by the guest and, for SNP, must make the page hypervisor-owned (shared). Registration sets the GHCB GPA's GFN; the hypervisor must respond with the same GFN or the "not accepted" value, and must terminate the guest if the supplied GPA does not match the currently registered one. Registering automatically unregisters the prior GPA. With Multi-VMPL, each VMPL level may register a GHCB GPA. Unregistration returns the unregistered GFN, 0 (none registered), or the failure value.

**Negotiation examples.** For SEV-ES, the hypervisor sets VMCB offset 0x00a0 before the first VMRUN with GHCBInfo 0x001 (version and encryption bit); the guest handles the #VC exception from CPUID, reads MSR 0xc001_0130 to extract version range and encryption bit, then establishes long mode, configures page tables with the encryption bit, allocates and marks the GHCB page shared, and writes its GPA to MSR 0xc001_0130. For SEV-SNP, the guest emulates CPUID leaf 0x80000000/0x8000001f via #VC, reads the SEV Status MSR (0xc001_0131), issues an SEV Information Request via the MSR protocol, registers the GHCB GPA, and writes the GHCB GPA to the MSR. Alternatively, the CPUID Request can supply the CPUID values; the guest should prefer firmware-validated CPUID page values for the encryption bit.

**Secrets and CPUID pages.** The hypervisor supplies an SNP guest with a secrets page containing a 96-byte guest reserved area (0x00a0–0x00ff) used for inter-environment communication, including per-VMPL current guest message sequence numbers (extended to 64 bits, with upper 32 bits and a 16-bit version stored in 18 of the 40 reserved bytes), an AP jump table physical address, and guest usage area. An EFI configuration table (GUID {0x067b1f5f, 0xcf26, 0x44c5, {0x85, 0x54, 0x93, 0xd7, 0x77, 0x91, 0x2d, 0x42}}) communicates the secrets and CPUID pages to the OS.

**NAE events.** NAE events are exits that are not AE events; the hardware throws #VC with the event's VMEXIT code, and the guest inspects the code, copies state to the GHCB, and invokes VMGEXIT. The VALID_BITMAP identifies valid qwords; its bit position is derived from the field's byte offset divided by 8 (e.g., RAX at 0x01f8 → qword offset 63 → byte offset 7, bit 7). Guests are expected to set SW_EXITCODE, SW_EXITINFO1, SW_EXITINFO2 and the hypervisor SW_EXITINFO1/2, resetting the bitmap before each event. A non-zero SW_EXITINFO1[31:0] indicates an error, with defined codes for malformed VMGEXIT input, unregistered GHCB address (SNP), invalid SW_SCRATCH, unmarked required input fields, and invalid NAE input. IOIO_PROT, MSR_PROT, VMMCALL (hypervisor-specific), and #NPF/MMIO events are described, including the use of the RESERVED shared buffer area at GHCB offset 0x800 with its GPA in SW_SCRATCH for decrypted string/MMIO buffers, and how MMIO ranges are marked via nested page table bits 51:n.

**Other NAE events.** Page State Change lets guests request private/shared page changes (and PSMASH/UNSMASH RMP hints for 2M pages); up to 253 entries fit in the shared buffer, errors are reported via SW_EXITINFO2 reason codes, and cur_entry/cur_page track progress so requests can be interrupted and resumed. The SNP Guest Request lets guests call firmware (e.g., SNP_PAGE_UNSMASH) through the hypervisor, requiring shared request/response pages, RMPUPDATE/RMP reclaim handling, return code in SW_EXITINFO2, and rate limiting. SNP Extended Guest Request adds certificate data (VCEK, VLEK) identified by GUIDs in a table at the data GPA offset 0x0, and reports required page count in RBX with SW_EXITINFO2 0x0000000100000000 if insufficient. AP Creation (SNP) lets a guest create/update/destroy AP vCPU state at a VMPL level via RMPADJUST-marked VMSA pages, enabling vCPU hotplug; it is required when Restricted Injection is active. Secure AVIC manages guest-owned APIC backing pages per vCPU through REGISTER/UNREGISTER_BACKING_PAGE actions. Also defined are #HV doorbell page, #HV Send IPI, #HV Timer, APIC ID List, SNP Run VMPL, and SNP TIO Guest Request (returning measurements, certificates, and a TDISP attestation report). An Unsupported Non-Automatic Exits event covers NAE events outside the negotiated protocol version, and a termination request event provides 64 bits of termination information.

**Guest identification, AP boot, and limitations.** The hypervisor must supply CPUID properties so a guest can detect SEV-ES support (ECX[31], EAX[1], EBX[5:0] encryption bit, EBX[11:6] address reduction). Because AP registers are measured and encrypted before launch, booting APs via INIT-SIPI requires new methods: the first reset runs initial measured values, subsequent resets use an AP Reset Hold request or an AP jump table (4K, encrypted, aligned) whose address can be passed via the Secrets Page and AP Jump Table SET/GET NAE events. NMI injection requires not intercepting IRET but intercepting #DB and using an "NMI Complete" message. Debug register virtualization uses the DebugVirtualization bit in SEV_FEATURES, otherwise DR7 reads/writes are intercepted. SMM and nested virtualization are unsupported.

**#HV doorbell page (Restricted Injection).** The common host-notification format includes a PendingEvent 16-bit field (bytes 0–1), a NoEoiRequired byte (byte 2), and reserved bytes 3–63. PendingEvent[15] NoFurtherSignal, [9] virtual #MC, [8] NMI, and [7:0] interrupt vector. The page is host-owned and accessed with C=0. Because #HV ignores interrupt shadows, guests must execute HLT with interrupts disabled and check interrupt state on resume. The host must faithfully emulate APIC semantics: present only the highest-priority ready interrupt, set/clear NoEoiRequired appropriately, mark interrupts in service when the guest clears the vector via atomic exchange, perform EOI cycles when the guest atomically clears NoEoiRequired, and set NoFurtherSignal when sending #HV. The guest must use atomic exchanges to retrieve pending event data and to request EOI (falling back to an X2APIC MSR write if the previous NoEoiRequired was zero), must validate each observed vector, and should panic if #HV arrives when NoFurtherSignal is non-zero under normal operation.

The study examined hippocampal perineuronal nets (PNNs), extracellular matrix (ECM) genes, and synaptic markers in postmortem tissue from people with substance use disorders (SUD), with or without major depressive disorder (MDD), and from rhesus macaques with chronic alcohol self-administration. Human cohorts included 20 SUD, 24 SUD/MDD, 20 MDD, and 20 psychiatrically normal control cases; three additional fixed control cases were used for confocal imaging.

Compared with controls, SUD was associated with increased PNN density in CA1 stratum oriens and several other hippocampal subregions, along with increased parvalbumin expression, increased Vamp2 expression, decreased Mmp9 and Ctss expression, and increased Chsy1 expression. MDD generally produced opposing changes, including reduced CA1 PNN density, increased Ctss and Vamp2 expression, and increased parvalbumin expression. The comorbid SUD/MDD group showed mixed PNN and glial changes, reduced Gfap expression, and increased Chsy1 and aggrecan expression. WFA-positive glial-cell densities also differed across diagnostic groups. Syn1 expression was unchanged.

Macaques with chronic alcohol self-administration had increased PNN densities in combined hippocampal regions, CA1 stratum oriens, and CA3 strata, plus increased WFA-positive glia in the dentate gyrus. These findings support increased hippocampal PNNs in SUD and suggest that PNNs and related ECM molecules may stabilize contextual reward memories and represent potential targets for cue-induced relapse. Comorbid MDD substantially affects these neuropathological measures and should be considered in SUD research and treatment strategies.

The application discloses systems and methods for localizing and classifying abnormalities in medical images, particularly prostate lesions in MRI and multiparametric MRI. One approach jointly trains an encoder-decoder localization network and a neural classification network: the localization network is trained first using annotated lesion contours or center-based heat maps, and the classification network is then trained and jointly fine-tuned using binary cross-entropy or other losses. Variants fuse T2-weighted, diffusion, ADC, and dynamic contrast-enhanced images; align and normalize image modalities; incorporate anatomical masks and radiomic or PI-RADS features; and assign lesion scores through score-aware heat maps or patch-based multiclass networks.

Another approach detects abnormalities by deleting or masking different image regions to create incomplete images, using a generative adversarial network to synthesize replacement normal tissue, selecting the synthesized image depicting the healthiest tissue as a normal reference, and comparing the input image with that reference to produce an abnormality localization map.

The application also describes two-stage training across clinical sites. A model is pretrained on a large source dataset and progressively fine-tuned with sub-datasets ordered by similarity, with updates selected according to cross-validation performance. At deployment, labeled samples are ordered by model uncertainty and selectively used to refine the model while limiting overfitting to the deployment data. Corresponding methods, apparatuses, and computer-readable media are also disclosed.

A University of Virginia Health System thoracic Enhanced Recovery After Surgery program launched in 2016 enrolled 139 patients in its first year and was compared with more than 220 previous nonparticipants. It did not compromise pain assessments or increase surgical complications or hospital readmissions.

The multidisciplinary program combines patient education, involvement in recovery, standardized care, preoperative preparation, nutritional optimization, reduced intravenous fluid use, and aggressive pain prevention with lower opioid use. Researchers said the program was associated with substantial clinically relevant improvements but noted that specific interventions cannot easily be assigned cause and effect and cost data lacked detail. An offensive goal kick aims to retain possession and begin an effective attack. It is taken from anywhere in the goal area after an attacker sends the ball over the defending end line. The ball must be stationary, and opponents should remain outside the penalty area until the kick, although the kicker may take it regardless. Any attacking player may take the kick; once the ball is kicked and visibly moves, it is live, and any player except the original kicker may then play it.

For young players, smaller fields and build-out or retreat lines help defenders move away from their goal and allow the attacking team to play out from the back. The simplest method places a designated kicker at the outermost corner of the goal area and directs the ball to the best dribbler or a target receiver near the sideline. A secondary receiver may then progress the ball upfield. Coaches emphasize keeping the ball wide and upfield, never sending it across the own goal, ensuring players are positioned and prepared, and giving defenders time to retreat.

For players generally 11 and above, the secondary player becomes a direct target. The kick can go to a receiver near the sideline, a farther upfield target, or an uncovered supporting midfielder. If both primary targets are covered, the kick is generally played short of the wider, farther target so the player can create separation. Players must prepare for kicks from either side of the goal area and learn to attack the ball rather than wait for it.

Adults may use short passes to advancing teammates, deep targets, or prearranged runs, with the goalkeeper commonly taking the kick. Coaches should account for players’ limited kicking distance and for field conditions, since wind can alter a goal kick directly, potentially producing an own-goal corner or, in an unusual case, a goal without another player touching the ball.

Scorpion stings are a potentially life-threatening but underreported global health problem, with many cases occurring in tropical and subtropical villages where victims do not seek medical care. The introduction cites estimates of 1.23 million stings and 3,250 deaths annually. Scorpion venom can affect neurological, cardiovascular, respiratory, hematologic, renal, and local systems through ion-channel activity and an “autonomic storm.” Most cases require supportive treatment, while severe envenomation may require vasodilators, scorpion antivenom, and intensive care.

A prospective descriptive cross-sectional study examined scorpion sting cases admitted to Tesseney Community Hospital in Eritrea’s Gash-Barka region from June 2019 through May 2020. Among 165 patients, sexes were nearly equally represented, 61.8% were at least 15 years old, and 57% were classified as urban residents. Stings most often occurred on the foot, at night, and indoors. Cases peaked in summer, particularly September and October. According to Abroug’s classification, 43.6% of cases were class III, 35.8% class II, and 20.6% class I.

Localized pain, sweating, vomiting, paraesthesia, relative bradycardia, and restlessness were the most common manifestations. Eight patients died, producing a case-fatality rate of 4.8%; six deaths occurred among class III cases, although this association did not meet the study’s statistical significance threshold. Envenomation was more severe in children, and age under 15 was identified as a possible risk factor. Scorpion color, sex, and number of stings were not significant risk factors. Treatment included local anesthesia, oral analgesics, diazepam, intravenous fluids, and nifedipine and/or scorpion antivenom; medication efficacy could not be assessed because antivenom and prazosin were unavailable.

The authors concluded that adults accounted for most cases because of occupational exposure, whereas children experienced greater severity. Recommended measures included education for at-risk groups, closed-toed shoes, mosquito nets, storing firewood away from sleeping areas, checking clothing and bedding, earlier care-seeking, further habitat and seasonal surveys, staff training, and improved access to essential medicines. Limitations included the single-hospital setting, unregistered cases, inaccurate recording of some variables, lack of post-discharge follow-up, and unavailable treatments.

Random walk theory assumes stock-price changes are random, independent, and impossible to forecast from historical prices or market reactions to news. Burton Malkiel popularized the theory in *A Random Walk Down Wall Street* (1973), while Louise Bachelier is credited with first proposing it. The related efficient market hypothesis instead assumes prices reflect available information; both suggest consistent market outperformance is difficult and favor passive, diversified investing.

The random walk trading strategy accepts an equal probability of prices rising or falling, uses random entries and exits, and spreads investments across multiple stocks or a broad-market index fund to reduce concentration risk. Its central rule is diversification rather than market timing.

The authors emphasize that most short-term price action is random, making disciplined, quantified backtesting important.

U.S. policy toward Hawaii consistently opposed foreign aggression threatening American rights and repeatedly treated annexation as necessary. Lord Palmerston proposed a U.S. protectorate or Hawaiian incorporation in 1850, and in 1851 a contingent cession was signed and sealed for activation if France attacked Hawaiian independence. A 1854 annexation treaty negotiated under Marcy was defeated by foreign influence and the death of Kamehameha III. Seward favored annexation over reciprocity in 1867; Johnson supported reciprocity in 1868 pending voluntary Hawaiian application for admission to the Union. Grant sought Senate advice in 1871, and Fish directed the U.S. minister in 1873 not to discourage annexation sentiment and to invite proposed terms. After the 1875 reciprocity treaty, administrations asserted U.S. commercial exclusivity and supported the Hawaiian government while it protected American interests. In 1881 Blaine advocated Hawaiian “benevolent neutrality,” warning that an “American solution” might be needed if neutrality became impracticable. Official relations began in 1820 with John C. Jones as U.S. agent for commerce and seamen, overseeing and reporting on American interests, supplemented by naval officers’ interventions.

Official fuel-economy figures are based on the criticised NEDC protocol, which has loopholes including eco-mode testing, disabled accessories, removal of exterior fittings, inflated tyres, a permitted 4% reduction and no sustained motorway driving. Which? says its own WLTP-based rolling-road tests provide more realistic mpg by using cold- and hot-engine cycles, sustained motorway speeds, normal driving settings, working accessories and no result adjustments. These tests found annual fuel-cost differences exceeding £800 between the most and least efficient medium-sized cars. WLTP replaced NEDC for official testing in September 2017, with full UK adoption by September 2018. Which? also applies specific battery-charge procedures to non-plug-in and plug-in hybrids. In addition to mpg, it measures NOx, carbon monoxide, hydrocarbons and particulate matter, and uses on-road PEMS testing to investigate suspected emissions manipulation, referencing Volkswagen’s emissions scandal and recalls.

The study examines how college teaching modality affects COVID-19 cases and deaths in surrounding counties. Although most college students are ages 18–29 and have a reported death rate of 0.4%, they socialize more, and campus reopening may spread infection to staff and nearby communities. Using a quasi-experimental matching approach, the researchers compare similar colleges that selected in-person, hybrid, or online instruction. Different reopening dates, cellphone mobility data, multidimensional matching, and reweighting based on colleges’ likelihood of selecting a modality help identify comparable cases. The analysis accounts for the endogeneity of teaching choices, since colleges often based them on pre-existing regional COVID-19 rates. Testing requirements, delayed death reporting, and K–12 school openings may also affect outcomes. The study provides evidence that college reopening—especially in in-person mode—increased county COVID-19 cases and deaths over time.

Postwar economic exclusion would seriously endanger Austria-Hungary and Germany; transit trade with Turkey could not solve immediate needs involving demobilized workers, depleted supplies, and financial burdens. Germany also possessed colonies and commercial exclusion from the Pacific, Central America, and South America. Other assets included global longing for peace, rejection of old diplomacy and armed peace, hopes for a league of nations, and fears of social revolution and insoluble war debts. Germany’s expansion had shifted south, southeast, and now east; the Russian collapse offered opportunities to seize eastern gains, potentially in exchange for concessions elsewhere.

The passage presents a hierarchical Bayesian multinomial model that partially pools SARS-CoV-2 sequence data across countries and variants to estimate variant prevalence, growth rates, and relative fitness despite sparse and geographically uneven sequencing. The approach uses two levels of hierarchy, sharing information among country-specific variant fitness estimates and among global variant fitness estimates, producing shrinkage toward common means and more stable estimates in low-data settings.

Analysis of GISAID data through July 1, 2022, showed substantial surveillance disparities: 10% of submitting countries accounted for 90.3% of sequences, and the United States and United Kingdom contributed 54.9%. The model identified heterogeneous emergence dynamics across countries and found BA.5 more fit than BA.4 and BA.2.12.1 relative to BA.2, while BA.1 had lower fitness.

Retrospective validation using five historical reference dates and Portugal’s BA.5 emergence showed that the multicountry model produced more stable fitness estimates, could estimate country-level fitness before local sequences were available, and had lower early predictive Brier scores than a single-country multinomial model.

The framework can provide regional and global prevalence forecasts, is applicable to other pathogens and geographic scales, and was demonstrated with influenza and local-level analyses. Its assumptions include representative sampling, correct lineage assignment, stable relative fitness over the modeled period, even variant mixing, and equal generation intervals. The authors also describe a dashboard for tracking emerging SARS-CoV-2 variants and nowcasting prevalence.

The paper studies finitely generated right Gorenstein-projective modules over the dual integers \(\mathbb Z[\varepsilon]=\mathbb Z[T]/(T^2)\). It notes that classifying all modules is infeasible and that the Gorenstein-projective category lacks the Krull–Remak–Schmidt property. Its main theorem establishes equivalences among the stable category of Gorenstein-projective modules, the stable category of submodules of finitely generated free modules, \(\mathrm D_b(\mathbb Z)/[1]\), and the homotopy and stable categories of perfect differential structures. The result also extends to any principal ideal domain. A chain of dense functors connects bounded complexes of free abelian groups with Gorenstein-projective modules, their stable category, and finite abelian groups. Their order-independent compositions form a cube with commutative faces.
