IDC’s December 2021 survey of 200 IT and departmental decision-makers at industrial enterprises with more than 500 employees in Germany, Austria, and Switzerland examines simulation, modeling, data analytics, and high-performance computing (HPC). More than half of respondents already use simulation, modeling, and virtual prototyping, while 39% seek to virtually simulate as many physical processes as possible. Digital twins, IoT, sensor data, and engineering workstations delivered as cloud services can improve feedback loops, collaboration, product development, and manufacturing processes. However, 42% report that their simulations are already outdated or inaccurate.

Demand for HPC is expected to rise substantially: only 8% currently identify high demand, but nearly half expect it within two years. Four-fifths of decision-makers regard HPC as a game changer for product and process innovation because it enables complex calculations, faster and more extensive analysis, new usage scenarios, and greater agility. More than one-quarter of enterprises already use professional HPC infrastructure, another 39% are planning or piloting it, and 81% of current HPC users intend to develop HPC-based business models.

Current HPC adoption faces security concerns, high energy consumption, insufficient capacity, downtime, infrastructure complexity, scalability constraints, and shortages of expertise. Most enterprises prefer external cloud infrastructure, colocation, or partnerships, while on-premises systems remain uncommon.

IDC expects public-cloud HPC to become the leading architecture, followed by hybrid-cloud and prebuilt systems. HPC-as-a-Service offers elastic performance, pay-as-you-go costs, modern technology, global collaboration, and rapid scalability, although skilled personnel remain necessary. Recommendations include establishing virtual product and manufacturing development, maintaining a single source of truth across the product lifecycle, selecting HPC operating models according to security and operational needs, prioritizing scalable, secure, energy-efficient solutions, and using external expertise where required.

Microsoft Corporation filed a Form 8-K dated January 25, 2022, furnishing a press release announcing financial results for the fiscal quarter ended December 31, 2021. The release, included as Exhibit 99.1, is not deemed “filed” under Section 18 of the Exchange Act. The report was signed by Alice L. Jolla, Corporate Vice President and Chief Accounting Officer.

John Clarke, Michel Devoret and John Martinis received the 2025 Nobel Prize in Physics for demonstrating quantum tunneling and energy quantization in electric circuits. Their 1980s experiments showed quantum effects involving billions of electrons in a handheld chip, laying the foundation for superconducting qubits. Similar circuits are now used as the quantum bits in quantum computers. Martinis later led Google’s quantum-computing effort, which controversially claimed in 2019 to achieve a calculation beyond traditional computers. The three share the 11 million Swedish kronor prize.

On October 30, 2001, Enron’s worsening credit crisis dominated financial reporting. Moody’s lowered its senior unsecured long-term debt rating from Baa1 to Baa2, two levels above junk, and placed its commercial-paper rating under review. Shares fell roughly 18–20% to around $11, an eight-year low, as Enron sought new bank credit lines. The company had reported a $1.01 billion quarterly loss, including more than $544 million in write-offs and $35 million of losses tied to partnerships managed by former CFO Andrew Fastow. Investors were also concerned about $3.3 billion in potential affiliate liabilities and a separate $1.2 billion reduction in shareholder equity. Enron had been excluded from the commercial-paper market, while bond-default insurance costs doubled.

The SEC’s inquiry into Enron’s off-balance-sheet partnerships continued as the company replaced Fastow with Jeff McMahon. Several major utilities said they remained Enron trading partners but were closely monitoring their exposure. Analysts warned that losing investment-grade status could restrict Enron’s merchant-energy business, while most expected its bonds would ultimately be paid.

Despite Enron’s financial troubles, McMahon said its forest-products operation would continue without reducing capital. Enron’s monthly newsprint transactions had risen from under 5,000 metric tons in January to 60,000 in July, with officials projecting 120,000 by year-end. McMahon aimed to make Enron one of North America’s largest newsprint marketers and use hedging tools to reduce price volatility. He identified publisher-producer relationships, doubts about paper quality and the absence of a pricing benchmark as obstacles.

Broader U.S. stocks also fell as consumer confidence dropped to a seven-year low amid post-Sept. 11 economic weakness. NYMEX president Robert Collins said Enron’s credit concerns could cause trading counterparties to retreat, but announced over-the-counter clearing for Henry Hub natural-gas futures. Commentary from James Cramer focused on when the Janus mutual fund would finish selling Enron shares. Separately, Germany’s cartel office threatened legal action against four utilities over grid-balancing charges that could burden smaller competitors, including Enron.

The TPS7H500x-SP push-pull converter design uses an 80-V GaN synchronous rectifier FET rated for the maximum secondary current; an optional parallel Schottky diode reduces soft-start current and dead-time reverse-conduction losses. An RCD clamp limits switch-node overshoot and requires test-based optimization. The design uses a 0.47-µH output inductor with a 40% ripple-current target.

Output capacitance must satisfy both load-transient deviation and voltage-ripple requirements. At least 1.3 mF is required, while 2.3 mF was used for additional radiation-induced single-event-transient mitigation. This was implemented with seven 330-µF polymer tantalum capacitors, each with approximately 6 mΩ ESR and a combined parallel ESR of 0.86 mΩ. An optional LC output filter can further reduce ripple; its resonant frequency should be above the crossover frequency but below the switching frequency and bulk-capacitor ESR zero, with damping resistors added if high-frequency peaking occurs.

Cycle-by-cycle current limiting begins at approximately 35 A, providing about 45% margin over the 24.25-A maximum peak inductor current. A 1:100 current-sense transformer and a selected 7.5-Ω RCS resistor are used. The hiccup capacitor is 3.3 nF. Type 2A frequency compensation targets a 10-kHz crossover with 40.2-kΩ RCOMP, 15-nF CCOMP, and 47-pF CHF values; testing may require tuning. A 102-kΩ resistor sets slope compensation.

The controllers operate from regulated 4- to 14-V supplies and require at least a 0.1-µF ceramic bypass capacitor from VIN to AVSS, with added bulk capacitance for remote supplies. Layout guidance emphasizes isolating feedback and control traces from switching signals, minimizing switch-node area and high-dv/dt/di/dt loops, separating analog and power grounds except at one connection, using short and wide current paths of at least 15 mils per ampere, placing filtering and compensation components near their pins, filtering CS_ILIM as needed, and connecting CFP backside metallization to AVSS through multiple vias. The document also provides application curves, PCB examples, support resources, revision history, mechanical and orderable information, ESD guidance, and disclaimers.

The MSPM0G3519, MSPM0G3518, MSPM0G1519, and MSPM0G1518 devices include a power management unit with regulated core supplies, VDD supervision, three-threshold brown-out reset, low-power mode support, and parity-protected trim that triggers power-on reset. Their clock module provides internal and external low- and high-frequency oscillators, a 32–80 MHz system PLL, and multiple clocks for the processor, bus, peripherals, ADC, and external output.

Six full-feature and six basic DMA channels support transfers of 8- through 128-bit data, mixed byte/word transfers, up to 64,000 transfers per block, configurable triggers, interrupts, ping-pong buffering, channel cascading, and stride mode. An event fabric connects publishers and subscribers to route peripheral events to the CPU as interrupts, to the DMA as triggers, or directly to other peripherals. The data sheet also references tables covering the memory map, peripheral register addresses, and interrupt vectors.

Nonvolatile flash includes dual program banks of up to 256 or 512 kB, a separate 16 kB data flash bank, ECC, in-circuit programming and erasing, 1 kB minimum sectors, selectable high-endurance sectors, and bank swapping for over-the-air firmware updates. Up to 128 kB of zero-wait-state SRAM is divided into two 64 kB banks with differing protection and low-power availability. Configurable write-execute partitions protect code from unintended modification.

GPIO ports provide up to 93 pins, multi-bit set, clear, and toggle operations, and low-power wake functions. IOMUX controls pad configuration, multiplexing, drive strength, speed, pulls, and data flow. Two 12-bit ADCs support simultaneous sampling at 4 Msps, hardware averaging to 14-bit effective resolution, internal temperature and supply channels, and internal or external references. A calibrated temperature sensor, configurable 1.4 V or 2.5 V voltage reference, comparators with blanking and fault-handling support, and a buffered 8- or 12-bit DAC are also included.

Security and processing features include AES hardware acceleration, firewalls, secure storage for as many as four AES keys, CRC-16 and CRC-32 support, a true random number generator, an AES-128/256 accelerator, a keystore controller, and a hardware math accelerator for 32-bit functions.

Communications peripherals include UARTs with programmable baud rates, LIN support, and separate FIFOs; I²C controllers supporting 7- and 10-bit addressing, SMBus 3.0, DMA, and low-power address-match wakeup; SPI controllers and peripherals with programmable frame sizes, multiple formats, DMA, and rates up to 32 Mbit/s on HSIO pins; and a CAN-FD controller compliant with ISO 11898-1:2015 and supporting rates up to 5 Mbit/s.

The low-frequency subsystem includes a 32 kHz RTC with calendar counters, alarms, periodic interrupts, calibration, temperature compensation, and clock output, plus an independent watchdog timer. A windowed watchdog timer can reset or interrupt the system, while general-purpose and advanced timers provide counting, PWM, complementary outputs, programmable dead time, fault handling, capture/compare, synchronization, cross-triggering, and DMA or ADC trigger generation.

A serial-wire debug interface provides device debugging access. The boot strap loader supports programming and configuration through UART or I²C, password protection, optional disabling, and several invocation methods. A memory-mapped factory-constants region stores device capabilities, trim data, revision information, and identifiers.

Recommended layout includes VDD decoupling with 10 µF and 0.1 µF low-ESR ceramic capacitors, a 47 kΩ NRST pullup with 10 nF pulldown, a 100 kΩ ROSC resistor for SYSOSC frequency correction when enabled, a 0.47 µF VCORE capacitor, and pullups for 5 V-tolerant open-drain I/O.

The document identifies TI development tools, including LaunchPad boards, the MSPM0 SDK, TI Resource Explorer, SysConfig, MSP Academy, GUI Composer, Code Composer Studio, IAR Embedded Workbench, Keil MDK, and Arm compiler toolchains. It also describes MSP versus X device nomenclature, documentation and support resources, April 2025 specification and feature revisions, mechanical and package drawings, orderable information, and automotive-qualified MSPM0G3518 and MSPM0G3519 versions.

The Open Source Definition established a framework for open source development, building on Richard Stallman’s advocacy for “free software.” The Open Source Initiative dates the term’s proposal by Christine Peterson to February 3, 1998, following Netscape’s decision to release its source code; Peterson chose “open source” partly because “free” required clarification. Peterson says it won on February 5, while Bruce Perens dates the OSD announcement to February 9. Although Stallman prefers “free software,” Perens described open source as the same concept in more commercially palatable language. Open source software has since become widespread: major technology companies depend on it to varying degrees, and mobile devices rely on code such as Linux and Darwin. Red Hat’s Tim Burke said proprietary software will remain for smaller problems, but open source has shifted from reproducing proprietary applications to leading innovation.

Bernstorff indicated that the blockade would end if a conference could be held on reasonable terms. Zimmermann said Germany’s confidential peace terms were a response to submarine warfare, urged President Wilson to remain quiet for two months while Germany expected submarine pressure to force England to seek terms, and warned of an exhausted Europe. Reported terms included relinquishing Belgium while retaining certain rights, French frontier changes, return of only part of Serbia, Bulgarian action regarding Romania, and German indemnities. Greece agreed to admit essential foodstuffs pending lifting of the blockade, while the Entente alleged unaccounted rifles. Austria-Hungary maintained its position that it was fighting a defensive war and sought a peace without victory. It said Entente demands threatened its dismemberment, making negotiations impossible, and asked Wilson to influence the Entente, potentially by restricting war supplies. It also maintained that modifying submarine warfare required allied consultation and that deployed submarines could not be recalled.

Energy storage can absorb grid or locally generated power and dispatch it later, but its economics depend on capital, charging, and round-trip efficiency. Lithium-ion batteries suit small distributed uses and have fallen from US$1,200 to US$600 per kWh in five years, yet remain costly. Pumped hydro is better suited to large-scale grid management and costs far less per kWh. Flywheels provide rapid dispatch and frequency stability, while compressed air, liquid air, flow batteries, and hydrogen offer alternatives at various scales.

Under an example household tariff, a 7 kWh battery would need to cost less than A$7,000 installed, or about A$1,000/kWh, to save money; current costs are A$1,000–3,000/kWh. Narrower retail peak–off-peak spreads could weaken the case, while a flat 25c rate would require battery costs around A$300/kWh. Storage can defer network upgrades only where demand is growing; demand has fallen since 2009. Despite pumped hydro’s cost advantage and existing 1,500 MW capacity, distributed lithium-ion systems may become popular because of human behaviour.

An Irish Times Portrait Gallery article and Jack McManus photograph portray Nobel-winning physicist Ernest Walton using a biro on laboratory equipment at Trinity College Dublin, emphasizing his quiet demeanor, guarded expression, and understated account of his 1930s atom-smashing work.

Apple Inc. filed an amendment to its Restated Articles of Incorporation with the California Secretary of State on August 3, 2020, increasing authorized common shares from 12.6 billion to 50.4 billion. Effective 5 p.m. PDT on August 28, 2020, each outstanding common share automatically split into four shares without action by shareholders. The amendment was filed as Exhibit 3.1 to Apple’s Form 8-K.

Bitcoin futures began trading on Cboe Futures Exchange on Dec. 17, the first such contracts in the U.S. The cash-settled contracts are based on bitcoin's auction price in dollars on the Gemini Exchange. The launch followed bitcoin's near-doubling since early December and sharp swings, including a loss of nearly a fifth in one day. Reception from banks and brokerages was mixed: Interactive Brokers offered access while restricting short positions and requiring at least 50% margin; Charles Schwab and TD Ameritrade barred trading initially; JPMorgan Chase and Citigroup did not plan to clear trades immediately, while Goldman Sachs said it would clear for certain clients. Analysts said futures may reduce bitcoin's volatility over time but noted no immediate effect, and warned of risks from inaccurate pricing, margin-call failures, systemic risk to clearing houses, and possible manipulation of the unregulated spot market.

The Korean diet is based on traditional Korean eating habits and emphasizes whole, unprocessed plant foods, including seasonal vegetables, fruits, whole grains, lean proteins, healthy fats, and fermented products such as kimchi, doenjang, gochujang, and miso. Meals often feature small portions and broth-based dishes, though Western influence has affected everyday eating. The diet is generally low in sugar, unhealthy fats, and calories and, combined with regular physical activity, may support weight loss and overall wellbeing. Fermented foods may improve gut health and digestion, while fresh ingredients provide antioxidants. Processed foods, sugary drinks, and unhealthy fats are minimized, and dairy is limited. Drawbacks include high sodium from fermented foods and condiments, low calcium, possible digestive irritation from spicy ingredients, and the need to control portions of high-carbohydrate foods such as rice. Vegan, low-carb, and gluten-free adaptations are possible. Adjusting sodium intake, portion sizes, and personal dietary needs can maximize its benefits. The passage also briefly introduces related articles on the Okinawa diet and ketogenic diet and notes that the health information is peer-reviewed by qualified clinicians.
The passage offers adaptable on-field guidance for new soccer players and coaches on positioning, ball work, team functions, and tactics.

The Sansa Fuze manual explains transferring music by drag-and-drop or Windows Media Player and transferring photos and videos with Sansa Media Converter, including conversion, cropping, rotation, resizing, and microSD support. It covers music, audiobook, podcast, video, and photo playback, along with playlists, Go Lists, repeat, shuffle, MusicEQ, bookmarks, slideshow options, ratings, and deletion. The guide also describes FM radio tuning, presets and recordings, voice recording, device settings, formatting, firmware updates, troubleshooting, and supported file formats and bit rates. Support resources and a one-year limited warranty are provided, along with terms governing SanDisk software licensing, liability, transfer, and restricted use.

The team hopes Horton recovers and will proceed without Aaron, who cannot play in the playoffs. After a tough Chicago loss, they bounced back and will adjust after lucky bounces, a broken stick, and late goals.

The ADS9803 is an eight-channel, 20-bit, 2-MSPS data-acquisition system with an integrated analog front end. Speed-boost mode supports up to 8 MSPS by continuously converting a user-selected analog input pair while the other six channels remain idle; the data-output interface is unchanged.

Configuration uses 16-bit registers across three banks with 8-bit addresses. Bank 0 is always accessible, while REG_BANK_SEL selects banks 1 or 2. Register writes require SPI_RD_EN = 0; register reads require SPI_RD_EN = 1 and SPI_MODE = 1. Registers provide controls for data formatting, averaging, digital test patterns, XOR/PRBS operation, speed boost, gain-error correction, bandwidth, common mode, output lanes, reference and channel power-down, and initialization.

SPI daisy-chain operation shares CS and SCLK among ADCs and connects each device’s SDO output to the next SDI input. DAISY_CHAIN_LEN specifies the number of chained ADCs excluding the first. Writes require N × 24 SCLKs in one frame, while reads use separate address and data frames.

Application information describes direct or multiplexed PMU-signal measurements, 22.7-kHz low-noise and 700-kHz wide-bandwidth modes, and 99.95% full-scale settling in 7.5 microseconds in wide-bandwidth mode. The device uses AVDD_5V, VDD_1V8, and IOVDD supplies with no required power-up sequence. Layout guidance includes separate 0.1-µF ceramic bypass capacitors near supply pins, close reference decoupling, a ground-plane connection, and separation of analog and digital paths. The document also covers support resources, ESD precautions, revision history, mechanical and orderable information, and TI disclaimers.

A retrospective study of 109 patients with aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage who underwent aneurysm clipping or coiling and external ventricular drainage assessed predictors of shunt-dependent hydrocephalus requiring ventriculoperitoneal shunt placement. Multivariate analysis identified three independent risk factors: age ≥65 years (OR 3.94), clipping rather than coiling (OR 4.36), and Hunt and Hess scale ≥3 (OR 3.59). A nomogram based on these factors had an AUC of 0.753 and was well calibrated by the Hosmer–Lemeshow test. Posterior circulation aneurysm location, Fisher grade, and the neutrophil-lymphocyte, platelet-lymphocyte, and platelet-neutrophil ratios did not significantly contribute to shunt dependence in this cohort. The authors concluded that the nomogram may assist clinical risk assessment, but noted the study’s retrospective design, limited sample size, and need for prospective validation.

Nike’s fiscal first-quarter revenue rose 1% to $11.72 billion, exceeding Wall Street expectations despite prior guidance for a mid-single-digit decline. Net income fell 31% to $727 million, and gross margin declined 3.2 percentage points to 42.2% as Nike discounted stale inventory. Wholesale revenue rose 7%, North American sales increased 4%, and inventory fell 2%, but direct sales declined 4% and China revenue dropped 9%. CEO Elliott Hill said the turnaround remains incomplete while Nike reorganizes teams by sport, emphasizes running and wholesale growth, and expands its appeal to women through the newly launched NikeSKIMS brand.

Tyreek Hill dislocated his left knee early in the third quarter of Miami’s win over the Jets, overshadowing the Dolphins’ first victory of the season. Hill was carted off with an air cast and remained hospitalized overnight for further tests, though he was in good spirits. He caught a 10-yard pass on third down before being tackled out of bounds and finished with six catches for 67 yards.

An international team found live giant shipworms (Kuphus polythalamia) in mud at an abandoned log farm in the Philippines. Unlike wood-eating relatives, they consume hydrogen sulfide, which their microbes convert into carbon. Microbes in their single gill could provide new antimicrobial substances. Researchers believe the species evolved from wood eaters, but its age, life cycle, and geographic range remain unknown. The study was published in PNAS.

The article presents a seasonal strategy for accessing German equities through the iShares MSCI Germany ETF (EWG). EWG holds large and mid-sized German companies, including SAP, Siemens, and Allianz, and charges a 0.50% expense ratio. Historical monthly returns since 1996 show that EWG performs best in the fourth quarter and trades roughly sideways during the rest of the year. The strategy therefore invests only from October through December. A dividend- and split-adjusted backtest since EWG’s inception indicates that the strategy outperformed buy-and-hold. The article also describes the DAX 40, Germany’s main index of 40 blue-chip companies listed on the Frankfurt Stock Exchange, which returned 5.36% annually since its July 1988 inception.

Climate change is making northern Rocky Mountain springs earlier, warmer, and drier, altering cold streams that favor native cutthroat trout. Warmer conditions allow introduced rainbow trout to expand into cutthroat habitat. The species hybridize, producing less-fit fish that survive poorly; surviving hybrids continue breeding, with no return to pure cutthroats. A study of hundreds of locations found widespread hybridization, especially where rainbows were introduced beginning in the 19th century. Some states are removing rainbows to protect cutthroats, which researchers warn could otherwise become extinct, permanently losing native genomes and adaptive traits.

Christian Nwosu, a former INEC administrative secretary in Kwara State, testified before a Lagos Federal High Court that EFCC operatives coerced him to claim he received N30 million from former Petroleum Minister Diezani Alison-Madueke. He alleged that operative Usman Zakari threatened to detain him unless he wrote a dictated statement, while prosecutor Rotimi Oyedepo sought his cooperation and allegedly threatened prosecution and imprisonment if he refused. Nwosu also claimed he surrendered property worth N30 million and N5 million in cash.

A nationwide study found that long-term exposure to outdoor trichloroethylene (TCE), an industrial solvent used in metal degreasing and dry cleaning, was associated with a modestly increased risk of Parkinson’s disease. Researchers compared 221,789 adults over 67 diagnosed between 2016 and 2018 with more than 1.1 million people without Parkinson’s, estimating neighborhood TCE exposure from EPA data and ZIP+4 codes. After adjusting for age, smoking and fine-particle air pollution, those in the highest exposure group had a 10% greater risk than those in the lowest group. Hot spots included the Rust Belt, and analyses around three major TCE-emitting facilities found higher risk nearer two facilities, including a clear distance-related increase at one site. The study did not establish causation and noted that its 2002 outdoor exposure estimates may not reflect individual lifetime or indoor exposure; findings also may not apply to younger people or early-onset Parkinson’s.

State Street Corporation agreed to pay $5 million to settle Labor Department claims that 305 female employees and 15 Black vice presidents were paid less than male and white counterparts in comparable positions. The firm denied the allegations; the settlement includes about $4.5 million in back pay and $500,000 in interest. The irony was highlighted because State Street commissioned the “Fearless Girl” statue to promote women’s leadership and its gender-diversity index. Sculptor Arturo Di Modica’s earlier criticism of the statue had been dismissed by others.
The 2025 physics Nobel was awarded to Clarke, Devoret and Martinis for demonstrating quantum effects in an electric circuit.

A swimming advisory for Little Beach in Port Stanley remained in effect Monday due to high bacteria levels, warning of possible gastrointestinal illness and infection. The beach was not closed because the bacteria threshold for closure had not been reached, though posted signs did not deter some swimmers.

Sir John Deane’s sixth-form students staged a jazz and soul concert at the Macdonald Portal Hotel, led by a 35-strong collective under Timothy Murphy. The event featured 1960s soul and classic swing. Fourteen students will next perform classical music at Arley Hall on February 9.

Three 2016 Evening Sun stories report that Norwich children Evan and Brynn Meek distributed 220 bagged lunches to homeless people in Manhattan; eight-year Norwich police veteran Thomas Miller accepted a Syracuse police position after serving with K9 Nitro in community events; and Tracy A. Price, 31, was arrested and granted $750 bail for allegedly torturing, injuring, and neglecting a dog.

Chalmers University of Technology researchers, collaborating with the University of Birmingham, used machine learning, advanced simulations and experiments cooled to −200°C to determine the previously unclear low-temperature structure of formamidinium lead iodide (FAPbI3), a high-performing halide perovskite. They found that formamidinium molecules become trapped in a semi-stable state as the material cools. Combining standard methods with machine learning enabled simulations thousands of times longer, containing millions rather than hundreds of atoms. The findings could help design and control perovskites and mixtures, addressing material instability and supporting efficient, lightweight, flexible solar cells and optoelectronic devices. The study was published in the Journal of the American Chemical Society on August 14, 2025.
A 36-year-old man was arrested on suspicion of stealing more than 100 cellphones at Coachella after victims tracked him using “Find My iPhone”; some phones were recovered.

Wafa Yahia, a Syrian grandmother, arrived in Honolulu after receiving U.S. visa approval, reuniting with her family. Her arrival does not affect Hawaii’s challenge to President Trump’s travel ban; a federal appeals court will hear the government’s appeal, and the Supreme Court plans to hear the case in October.

Cuba marked the 58th anniversary of Fidel Castro’s 1959 revolution with a military parade in Havana, where tens of thousands honored the late leader. The event came amid economic hardship, uncertainty over Raúl Castro’s succession, and threats to improving U.S.-Cuba relations.
A Journal of Experimental Psychology study found that distractions may briefly improve post-breakup mood but should be used sparingly; focusing on an ex’s negative traits may speed recovery.

The writer describes discomfort and sleep-position challenges during pregnancy, including the risks of lying flat on the back after the fifth month and reduced placental blood flow when lying on the right side. A longtime stomach sleeper, they found a U-shaped Leachco pregnancy pillow through a friend’s Facebook post and bought it for $65. The pillow greatly improved sleep by supporting side sleeping, allowing them to wrap their legs around it, change positions without readjusting it, and elevate their head to ease congestion. They also carried it around the apartment, used it while relaxing on the couch, and bought a softer replacement cover because the original was scratchy. Its removable cover is machine washable. Drawbacks include its large size, potential crowding in smaller beds, and displacement of blankets. Despite these issues, the writer plans to continue using it after the birth and strongly recommends it to pregnant people and others seeking comfort.

Vale’s preferred-share conversion plan attracted 84.4% of the class, exceeding the 54.09% minimum. Management said the successful plan could accelerate Vale’s listing on São Paulo’s Novo Mercado, potentially ahead of its 2020 target, while ruling out cash incentives for nonswapping shareholders. This qualitative study examined primary school teachers’ perspectives on challenges and solutions concerning students with disabilities who continued inclusive education through virtual learning during the COVID-19 pandemic. Using a phenomenology design, researchers interviewed 10 general education primary school teachers in two Marmara Region provinces. Participants were purposively selected based on having at least one officially diagnosed student with a disability and volunteering for the study. Data were collected in 2021 through recorded, in-person, semi-structured interviews lasting 28–35 minutes, then analyzed using content analysis and in-vivo coding.

Teachers used EBA, Zoom, WhatsApp, television courses, assignments, video sharing, and alternative attendance arrangements to deliver instruction. Most reported that students with disabilities participated frequently, particularly when parents provided technical and academic support. Some students attended only basic courses or could not participate because of limited internet or devices, parental illiteracy, insufficient home support, or reliance on rehabilitation-center education.

Reported difficulties included low interaction and socialization, limited motivation, boredom, inadequate individualized instruction, inability to implement individualized education programs, difficulty tracking assignments, behavioral problems, and insufficient teacher time in crowded classes. Students also disliked EBA television, found course content insufficiently engaging, and sometimes lacked visible teacher or peer interaction. Additional barriers involved unsuitable home-learning conditions, parental fatigue, weak teacher-parent communication, limited coordination with special education teachers and rehabilitation centers, and teachers’ inability to assess progress as in person. Where teachers reported few problems, they attributed them to EBA tracking features, regular parent communication, family cooperation, and adequate technology.

Applied solutions included individualized and hybrid schedules, family-guided support, short home-study video submissions, frequent calls, and motivational support. Recommended measures included improving technological access, creating parent-supportive content and guidance materials, strengthening home organization, supporting students’ social as well as academic development, keeping schools open, using EBA support centers, and coordinating with rehabilitation centers. The study emphasized parents’ central role as supporters, teachers, and advocates in students’ virtual education.

The paper examines how cooperative education (co-op) could improve Nigerian students’ hard and soft skills, employability, and transition from school to work. It adopts the United Nations definition of youth as ages 15–24 for comparability and defines skills development as encompassing technical abilities and broader workplace skills. Experiential learning, including work-integrated learning, is described as learning through educational and workplace experiences, with co-op distinguished by its integration into the curriculum.

Nigeria’s youth unemployment has risen in recent years and, by 2021, exceeded rates in most comparison regions except South Asia and the Middle East and North Africa. Youth unemployment has generally been at least double the total unemployment rate, while youth employment-to-population ratios remain substantially lower. Informal employment, inadequate social protection, discouraged and underemployed workers, limited data, and personal networks complicate labor-market measurement in sub-Saharan Africa. Nigeria’s 2019 youth NEET rate was 28%, compared with 13% in OECD countries, with rates markedly higher among young women. Unemployment also varies by education, location, and gender.

Co-op originated in industrialized countries and later spread to post-secondary institutions in sub-Saharan Africa. Its core elements are an integrated curriculum, learning from work experience, and logistical coordination, supported by collaboration among institutions, employers, and governments. Models include alternating school and work terms, parallel school-and-work schedules, and longer work periods. Reported benefits include improved skills, motivation, career clarity, employability, earnings, employer recruitment, curriculum development, and labor-market outcomes. Evidence, mainly from developed countries, associates co-op and other work-integrated learning with higher employment, better job-field matches, lower unemployment and overqualification, and improved earnings, although program design strongly affects results.

Modern co-op programs commonly require academic eligibility, compensated work terms, dedicated co-op units, quality assurance, and cooperation with industry. Examples from the University of Waterloo and Namibia University of Science and Technology show structured course-work sequences, fees paid during work terms, employer coordination, and links to professional accreditation bodies.

Nigeria’s principal youth-employment initiatives include SIWES, introduced in 1973–74; SURE-P, launched in 2012; and N-SIP, launched in 2016. SIWES provides approximately six months of workplace training but is separate from the academic calendar and relies heavily on students, making it closer to apprenticeship than fully integrated co-op. SURE-P included graduate internships, while N-SIP’s N-Power program provides training and paid volunteer opportunities. Evaluations report benefits but also inadequate funding, poor placement matches, weak supervision, and complex administration.

The paper recommends a federally driven, dynamically integrated co-op initiative in Nigeria that builds on SIWES, N-Power, and existing partnerships with industry. Government could provide placements, incentives, grants, or tax credits, while employers would help shape curricula and gain access to trained workers. An alternating model is recommended so students complete multiple work terms and gain at least a year of career-related experience before graduation. The paper cautions that training alone cannot solve youth unemployment and calls for broader interventions addressing labor demand, supply, and the wider economic and social environment. Future research should determine appropriate management structures, models for different institutions and programs, and the applicability of co-op to non-tertiary education.

This preprint analyses the Omicron BA.1 wave in England (November 2021 – end January 2022) using a large-scale phylodynamic and phylogeographic approach. The study used 115,622 SARS-CoV-2 Omicron genomes sampled globally between 8 November 2021 and 31 January 2022, of which 48,615 (42%) came from England across 313 lower tier local authorities (LTLAs), together with anonymised human mobility and epidemiological data.

Phylodynamic analysis identified at least 6,455 independent introduction events, 69.9% of which were singletons. The earliest introduction was estimated between 5 and 18 November 2021, with imports growing approximately exponentially until a plateau in early January 2022 despite travel restrictions on arrivals from southern African countries (26 November – 15 December). Average weekly BA.1 importation intensity from the US was roughly four times that from South Africa during the restriction weeks. Early importations accounted for only ~6% of introductions but were responsible for ~80% of BA.1 infections in England through January 2022; 399 transmission lineages arose from importations before restrictions ended and 29 before restrictions began. Transmission lineage sizes were overdispersed, with the eight largest lineages (>700 genomes each) comprising over 60% of English genomes, and larger lineages generally traced to early seeding events. Results were cross-validated against UKHSA VAM line-list data, which showed a broadly consistent but lagged importation profile.

Spatially, first detections were fairly evenly distributed regionally (~20% in Greater London), but widespread transmission developed with the London-centred expansion in late November 2021. Long-distance (>300 km) movements rose sharply in the first week of December, predominantly from Greater London toward the Midlands and North West; local movements comprised about 90% and 60% of all movements in Greater London and Greater Manchester respectively. Short-range (<50 km) movements declined over time, while a second phase of increased mid-to-long range (50–300 km) movement occurred around New Year; London's role in onward propagation diminished while the North West and South West mainly acted as sinks.

A discrete phylogeographic generalised linear model (fitted to the three largest lineages separately and the next five jointly, 61.9% of English genomes) distinguished an expansion phase (before 26 December 2021) and a post-expansion phase. During expansion, the gravity model and Greater London as origin were strongly supported, indicating highly directional spread; post-expansion, gravity effects weakened and the aggregated mobility matrix was consistently supported, with dissemination toward LTLAs with later peak times.

A statistical model of hub-to-home mobility found that trips declined by 11.97% per unit increase in weekly hub COVID-19 cases per 100 people (with a four-day lag), with reductions of 20.03% and 15.79% at 50 km and 100 km separation respectively. Pre-holiday peaks occurred in Greater London and 14 surrounding LTLAs, while most other 255 LTLAs peaked in early January 2022, coinciding with 20–50% mobility reductions from mid-December.

The discussion concludes that targeted travel restrictions were largely ineffective when applied after local transmission was detected, limited to too few countries, and unaccompanied by local control measures, and that multiple global transport pathways further limit their value. Limitations include underestimation of seeding events, possible aggregation of lineages, and residual spatial and temporal sampling bias. Future work should examine socio-economic and behavioural determinants of mobility responses, spatial heterogeneities in immunity, and the need for scalable genomic–epidemiological data infrastructure. BA.1 was replaced by BA.2 in February 2022 and later by BA.5 in June 2022.

The TLV321/2x comparator family consumes 40 µA per channel and offers 40 ns propagation delay. TLV321x devices provide push-pull outputs that sink or source current, while TLV322x devices provide open-drain, sinking-only outputs with external pull-ups to any voltage up to 5.5 V, independent of comparator supply voltage.

Input voltages may extend 200 mV beyond the supply rails, but ESD clamps require limiting input current to 10 mA or less, typically with series resistors. Unused inputs must not be tied together; they should be connected to valid potentials within the input range with at least 50 mV differential voltage. The devices include 1.8 mV internal hysteresis.

Push-pull outputs must not be connected together or shorted to a supply rail, and unused outputs should remain floating. Open-drain outputs support logic ORing and level translation; TI recommends pull-up currents of 100 µA to 1 mA. Unused open-drain outputs may remain floating or connect to V−.

An internal power-on reset holds the output low for up to 32 µs after the supply crosses 1.65 V. In normal operation, the comparator compares one input with a reference on the other, and swapping inputs reverses output polarity. Propagation delay increases as input overdrive decreases, particularly below 100 mV.

External hysteresis can reduce output chatter by adding positive feedback. An inverting configuration uses a three-resistor network referenced to VCC, while a non-inverting configuration uses two resistors and a voltage reference.

A typical low-side current-sensing application uses an amplifier to amplify a shunt-resistor drop and a comparator to signal when its output exceeds 1.1 V. Proper high-speed layout requires a 0.1 µF ceramic bypass capacitor at each device, minimized input/output coupling, close-placed input resistors, and, where needed, an output series resistor below 100 Ω to damp ringing. The devices support split or single supplies and include ESD protection on inputs and outputs.

NVIDIA’s GA10x Ampere architecture builds on Turing with redesigned streaming multiprocessors, more ROPs, second-generation RT Cores, third-generation Tensor Cores, unified L1 cache/shared memory, and greater power efficiency. GA10x SMs use four partitions with dual FP32 datapaths, enabling 128 FP32 operations per clock per SM while also supporting concurrent INT32 work. GA102 includes 128 CUDA Cores, four Tensor Cores, one RT Core, 128 KB of configurable L1/shared memory, and 112 ROPs per GPU.

Second-generation RT Cores double ray-triangle intersection throughput, support hardware-accelerated ray-traced motion blur, and can operate concurrently with graphics or compute workloads. Third-generation Tensor Cores add TF32 and BF16 support and fine-grained 2:4 structured sparsity, which can double effective matrix throughput. Ampere also enhances DLSS with 9x super-resolution scaling, enabling 8K gaming at 60 fps on the RTX 3090.

GA10x introduces GDDR6X memory using PAM4 signaling and Maximum Transition Avoidance encoding, supporting data rates up to 19.5 Gbps and peak bandwidth of 936 GB/s. NVIDIA RTX IO, working with Microsoft DirectStorage, offloads asset decompression from the CPU to the GPU and can accelerate I/O performance by up to 100 times.

Additional capabilities include fifth-generation NVDEC with AV1 hardware decoding, seventh-generation NVENC for encoding up to 8K HEVC, DisplayPort 1.4a and HDMI 2.1 support, and GDDR6X Error Detection and Replay for overclocked memory.

The architecture spans the RTX 3090 and 3070 GeForce cards, the data-center A40 with 48 GB of expandable memory, and the professional RTX A6000 with 48 GB of GDDR6 and NVLink support for 96 GB combined memory.

The author praises Justice Amy Barrett’s book and its defense of originalism, while acknowledging that other interpretive approaches are plausible. Applying originalism to Louisiana’s second majority-Black congressional district, the author argues that the Equal Protection Clause did not originally constrain state election regulation and that the Fifteenth Amendment does not prohibit race-based districting when it neither denies nor abridges any voter’s right to vote. The racial-predominance doctrine therefore lacks an originalist foundation.

The author further argues that the doctrine is unworkable and conflicts with the Voting Rights Act’s Section 2, which permits remedies for minority vote dilution. Although stare decisis ordinarily requires courts to respect precedent, an originalist judge should reconsider and abandon the racial-predominance doctrine in favor of Congress’s authority to address race-based districting through legislation. The essay urges Barrett and the Court to resolve the issue with intellectual honesty.

The Investors Intelligence Sentiment Index, also called Advisor Sentiment, is a weekly contrarian indicator created by AW Cohen in 1963 and published by Chartcraft. It surveys more than 100 independent market newsletters, classifying investment advisers and commentators as bullish, bearish, or expecting a correction. It also tracks stocks above their 10-week and 30-week moving averages, which help identify short-to-intermediate and major market turns.

Extreme readings are interpreted contrarily: bullish sentiment above 55% may be negative for the market, while readings below 35% may be positive. Readings above 70% suggest an overbought market, and those below 30% suggest an oversold market. The index is widely used by investors and followed by financial media, though users are advised to backtest its trading applications.

Unlike the AAII Sentiment Survey, which has polled individual investors about the market’s next six months since 1987, this index measures the views of professional advisers and commentators. Investor sentiment generally reflects the market’s overall mood and may be inferred from prices, trading activity, or broad-market indicators.

A Brookings policy brief (May 2025) by Ghulam Omar Qargha, "From Out-of-School to Out-of-Education Children: What Afghanistan Teaches Us About Measuring Education Exclusion," argues that the UNESCO out-of-school children (OOSC) indicator—school-age children (6–17) not enrolled in primary or secondary school, adopted in 2011 to track enrollment gaps and progress toward Education for All and the Millennium Development Goals—should be replaced by an out-of-education children (OOEC) indicator capturing formal, informal, and non-formal learning pathways. The OOSC focuses on a single institution, privileges formal schooling, overlooks alternative and indigenous systems, and relies on unidimensional data that undercounts marginalized groups; worldwide, the number of out-of-school children rose by 7 million over the past decade to 251 million, with nearly 30% out of school in Sub-Saharan Africa and 20% in Central and Southern Asia, and COVID-19 disrupted attendance for over 1.7 billion students.

Afghanistan illustrates the problem. Modern schooling emerged in the late 19th century; King Amanullah's expansion after 1919 was resisted as colonial; the Soviet invasion (1979) intensified schooling's role in ideological control; and the Mujahideen, Taliban, civil war, and post-2002 invasion each reshaped enrollment, which rose from about 500,000 students in 2000 to roughly 10 million by 2021 (39% girls, 16,000–18,000 schools). The Taliban's 2021 ban on girls' secondary education left 80% of school-aged girls out of school (about 1.4 million students). Enrollment also does not equal attendance: almost 20% of students and 22% of female students were absent for most or all of the year, and ghost schools and ghost students are reported.

Four structural barriers are examined: geographic disparities, with several provinces reporting attendance and completion rates below 15% against a national average near 30%; nomadic lifestyles, where only about 7% of 600,000 school-age Kuchi children attend primary school and an estimated 250,000-plus seasonal migrant children are out of school; child labor, with about one million children under 18 working in 2018 and half never having attended school; and disabilities, with roughly 375,000 of more than 500,000 children with moderate-to-severe disabilities never attending school.

The brief presents three advantages of OOEC—a broadened lens, a tool for catalyzing system transformation, and a move toward viewing education as an ecosystem—and notes implementation challenges: data systems that capture all pathways, evolved credentialing systems, collaboration among education actors, and equitable resource allocation with cost data. The transition is framed as a first step toward transformation aligned with SDG 4, with collaborative research such as the Brookings SPARKS project highlighted.

AMD Seamless Firmware Servicing (SFS) distributes signed packages containing fixes for selected high-priority issues in running system firmware, allowing deployment without rebooting. The AMD Security Processor (ASP) verifies AMD’s signature before applying each package. Customers may also co-sign packages using an RSA key supplied through BIOS during early boot, giving OEM/ODMs approval authority over deployed updates. SFS and co-signing are BIOS options disabled by default.

SFS tracks an overall SFS Patch Level (SFSPL), individual firmware and Security Patch Levels (SPL), and a monotonically increasing System Patch Level (SYSPL) for run-once code executed since the last reboot. These levels determine whether an update is applicable and can be queried by the host OS.

Packages can modify registers, replace firmware images, or update firmware components. They validate required firmware versions and dependencies before applying all changes, preventing partial updates and out-of-sync firmware. Packages must be applied sequentially at runtime, are socket-aware, and are not persistent across reboots, so they must be reapplied during boot or system operation.

A customer deployment agent submits an aligned memory buffer containing the optional co-signing header, update package, and signature to the ASP. The ASP protects the buffer from x86 access, verifies applicable signatures, executes the patch, updates patch levels, and returns status.

SEV updates are automatically committed, and reverting an updated SEV image requires rebooting. SNP updates require HV-fixed pages. Released packages must match the system’s exact firmware and patch-level combination and align with AGESA releases.

Passport applicants must take an oath of allegiance, provide a physical description, and obtain certification from at least one credible witness that their identity and affidavit are truthful. Persons born abroad to a U.S.-native father must document the father’s U.S. birth, residence, and citizenship. Naturalized citizens must submit their certificate or a certified court record and detail their emigration, naturalization, residence, and identity. Women and children must document their relationship to a naturalized parent when required. Residents of U.S. insular possessions must attest exclusive U.S. allegiance with two credible witnesses. Passports expire after two years and require a new application. One passport may cover eligible spouses, minor children, and servants; professional titles are excluded. Applications may be refused for unlawful purposes or noncompliance. The fee was $1, plus 50 cents each for duplicate application preparation and oath administration.

Archaeologists in Mexico are excavating a sealed Maya tunnel beneath El Castillo at Chichen Itza, hoping to reach a hidden cenote—a water-filled sinkhole and important freshwater source in Yucatán. The team, led by Guillermo de Anda of the Great Mayan Aquifer Project, expects the work to take about three months. Cenotes were central to Maya spirituality, associated with the underworld, rain gods, offerings and human sacrifice, and the hidden cenote may have represented an “axis mundi” beneath the pyramid. Divers previously found two passages from the Ossuary blocked with stones. De Anda’s research indicates that about 80% of sacrifice victims at Chichen Itza’s Sacred Cenote were children aged 3–11 whose remains showed anemia and malnutrition. He said further research is needed to determine whether they were alive when deposited.

Lab tests show that jostling air-and-methane microbubbles can create tiny lightning zaps. Bluish will-o’-the-wisps have been seen above swamps and cemeteries worldwide. Swamp lights are believed to be seeping methane burning, but what ignites the gas remains mysterious; the passage ends with Luigi Garlaschelli peering over graves at midnight.

The EU announced a €545 million ($636 million) package supporting renewable energy and electrification in Africa, including transmission lines in Côte d’Ivoire, rural electrification in Cameroon, wind and hydro projects in Lesotho, and mini-grids in Madagascar. The projects aim to expand electricity access, reduce fossil-fuel dependence and potentially create 38 million green jobs by 2030. Nearly 600 million Africans lack electricity. Launched in 2021, the EU’s Global Gateway initiative prioritizes African infrastructure and offers an alternative to China’s Belt and Road Initiative. The competition also concerns Africa’s critical minerals: China is heavily invested in regional mining and clean energy, while the US has pursued African energy projects through the Partnership for Global Infrastructure and Investment. China recorded $39 billion in African Belt and Road energy contracts in the first half of 2025 and exported 15 GW of solar panels to Africa in the year ending June 2025. A planned Lobito railway would connect Zambian copper and Congolese cobalt deposits to Angola’s Atlantic port.

The COVID-19 pandemic prompted Greek preschool education to adopt distance learning, although teachers’ limited ICT skills, inadequate internet and device access, weak school digital infrastructure, insufficient training, and families’ financial inequalities restricted implementation. Distance education may take synchronous, asynchronous, or blended forms and can provide flexible, individualized learning through remote communication and online materials. In preschool settings, however, it requires adult supervision, usually parental, and cooperation between families and teachers. Preschool education is intended to support children’s physical, emotional, mental, social, motor, communication, and digital development through play, interaction, and active learning.

A quantitative study during the 2020–2021 school year examined Greek kindergarten teachers’ views of distance education in Epirus after its COVID-19 implementation and its possible future use under normal conditions. It investigated prior familiarity, ICT literacy, years of service, post-pandemic applicability, and factors affecting integration. A random 30% sample of the 280 kindergarten teachers in Epirus was invited; 82 of 84 responded. Data were collected through an anonymous Google Forms questionnaire from May 5 to June 4, 2021, using demographic items, mainly five-point Likert questions, four semi-closed questions, and one open question, and were analyzed with SPSS 21.

Most respondents were women (96.3%), and 55.6% had 15–25 years of service. Half held basic ICT certification and 35.4% held enhanced certification. More than three-quarters had little or no familiarity with distance education before its mandatory implementation, and 91.5% had not previously integrated it into kindergarten. Most lacked experience with school-run remote programs and remotely delivered training. Synchronous instruction was preferred by 64.6%; Webex was the most used tool (88.9%), followed by email (60.5%), Viber (24.7%), eclass (23.5%), and Messenger (19.8%).

Teachers were generally negative about distance education for preschoolers. They reported limitations on psychomotor activities, the need for adult supervision, reduced effectiveness in developing social skills, and difficulty among young children using technology independently. Inadequate infrastructure and internet access, connectivity problems, insufficient teacher and parent digital literacy, limited parental time and support, unsuitable lesson timing, and reduced student interest and participation were identified as constraints. Many teachers viewed distance education mainly as an emergency alternative when attendance was impossible and were hesitant about blended or individualized learning. Positive perceptions were more evident regarding the development of digital skills, flexible teaching, and teacher-parent cooperation.

ICT certification was significantly associated with prior familiarity with distance education; Level B certificate holders reported greater familiarity than uncertified teachers. No statistically significant relationship was found between years of service and ICT literacy. The authors recommend teacher professional development, modernization of school and home technological infrastructure, child-appropriate interactive resources, and support for families, while emphasizing that preschool age and resulting digital inequalities require caution. Because the study was limited to Epirus, its results cannot safely be generalized to all Greek kindergarten teachers.

A free "Take A Knee Chart" is available in PDF and Google Sheets formats. Taking a knee is an almost risk-free football play used to run out the clock when the offense leads late; the offense lines up in a "victory formation" to minimize mistakes and turnovers, and the quarterback kneels after the snap, which counts as a run play, so the clock keeps running and the play clock resets. Without timeouts, the opponent cannot stop the clock. The chart shows player positions and movement order, and clock management is a key coaching responsibility.

The paper introduces ML²B, a benchmark for evaluating large language models that generate complete machine-learning pipelines from multilingual natural-language descriptions. It expands 30 Kaggle competitions—24 public and six private—into 13 languages, producing 390 evaluation instances across 12 domains and tabular, text, and image modalities. Task descriptions were curated and manually reviewed, while standardized data cards, metadata, and private competitions were used to limit information and benchmark-data leakage.

ML²B combines data from Code4ML and Meta Kaggle Code and includes a benchmark pipeline, isolated Docker runtime, and code grader. It supports single-function and modular prediction formats, with the latter designed to reduce preprocessing leakage by separating training, validation preparation, and prediction. Translations produced with GPT-4o were reviewed by native speakers with computing backgrounds. Model results are normalized using Kaggle leaderboard percentiles to support comparison across competitions with different metrics.

Five models were evaluated through AIDE and ML Master. The experiments found 15–45% degradation on non-English tasks. English produced the strongest results, while Kazakh, Belarusian, and Romanian were notably weaker, particularly for tabular classification and regression. Performance varied by language, domain, metric, and architecture; hybrid systems partially mitigated low-resource weaknesses, but no model was universally best. Static analysis flagged potential leakage in 61 of 554 modular submissions, leaving 33, or 5.9%, as potential cases after excluding train-function findings and likely false positives. The paper recommends broader private-task coverage, improved domain balance, secure agent interfaces, code auditing, and multilingual alignment strategies.

Amazon.com, Inc.’s fiscal 2018 Form 10-K describes a company incorporated in Washington in 1994, reincorporated in Delaware in 1996, headquartered in Seattle, and publicly traded on Nasdaq under “AMZN.” It operates through three segments—North America, International, and Amazon Web Services (AWS)—serving consumers, sellers, developers, enterprises, content creators, and advertisers. Its businesses include online and physical retail, third-party seller services, AWS cloud offerings, advertising, digital content subscriptions, publishing, Prime memberships, and devices such as Kindle e-readers, Fire tablets and TVs, and Echo devices. Whole Foods Market results were consolidated beginning August 28, 2017.

Amazon emphasizes selection, price, convenience, reliable fulfillment, and customer service. It operates fulfillment and delivery networks, data centers, customer service centers, and physical stores, while using co-sourced, outsourced, and third-party arrangements. Whole Foods Market was acquired on August 28, 2017. The company served consumers, sellers, developers, enterprises, content creators, and advertisers. 

The report identifies material risks from intense and changing competition; rapid expansion into products, services, and geographies; operating-result volatility; international operations and regulatory conditions in China and India; fulfillment-network and data-center optimization; seasonal demand and inventory management; commercial agreements, acquisitions, and investments; foreign exchange; loss of key personnel; data security and system interruptions; intellectual property; stock-price volatility; evolving regulation and taxation; supplier concentration; government-contract compliance; product liability; payment processing; and seller misconduct. Amazon employed approximately 647,500 full- and part-time workers at year-end, and historically generated a disproportionate share of annual revenue in the fourth quarter.

As of December 31, 2018, Amazon reported 277.2 million square feet of leased facilities and 11.2 million square feet of owned facilities, including 520 North American and seven international stores. The company owned and leased its Seattle headquarters and had announced plans for additional headquarters in New York City and Arlington, Virginia.

Selected financial results showed net sales of $89.0 billion in 2014, $136.0 billion in 2016, $177.9 billion in 2017, and $232.9 billion in 2018. Operating income was $4.2 billion in 2016, $4.1 billion in 2017, and $12.4 billion in 2018; net income was $2.4 billion, $3.0 billion, and $10.1 billion, respectively. Diluted earnings per share reached $20.14 in 2018, and operating cash flow rose to $30.7 billion.

In 2018, North America generated $141.4 billion in sales and $7.3 billion in operating income; International generated $65.9 billion in sales and a $2.1 billion operating loss; and AWS generated $25.7 billion in sales and $7.3 billion in operating income. Sales grew 33% in North America, 21% internationally, and 47% in AWS. At year-end, cash, cash equivalents, and marketable securities totaled $41.3 billion. Cash capital expenditures were $11.3 billion, primarily for fulfillment capacity and technology infrastructure, with most technology investment supporting AWS. The company stated that operating cash flows, marketable securities, and borrowing arrangements should meet anticipated cash needs for at least the following 12 months.

Critical accounting estimates include inventory valuation and income taxes. Inventory is generally valued using first-in, first-out at the lower of cost or net realizable value; each additional 1% of valuation allowance as of year-end 2018 would have increased cost of sales by approximately $190 million. The report also cautions that forward-looking statements and financial estimates are inherently uncertain and actual results could differ materially.
