The 9 EMA trading strategy uses a 9-period exponential moving average to identify short-term market swings and generate buy signals when price moves above the EMA and sell signals when it moves below. It can be applied to forex, stocks, commodities, futures, options, and cryptocurrencies, but is better suited to trending or momentum-driven assets and may produce whipsaws in mean-reverting stock markets.

Backtesting on Bitcoin from 2014 produced 284 trades with an average gain of 2.65% and a maximum drawdown of 83%. Results on the S&P 500/SPY were poor. Adding a 200-day moving average as a trend filter reduced Bitcoin trades to 153 while raising average gains to 4%; it improved SPY results but remained unprofitable.

The strategy can be combined with RSI, Bollinger Bands, MACD, volume data, candlestick patterns, longer-term moving averages, and support/resistance signals. Recommended risk controls include stop-loss orders, position sizing, diversification, defined exits, limited leverage, and avoiding emotional trading.

Mark Palmer circulated a class-action complaint filed in California Superior Court, San Diego County, noting that a reporter said Enron’s suit would look the same. The complaint was brought by SDG&E customer Pamela R. Gordon on behalf of electricity customers who purchased power through the California Power Exchange from May 22, 2000, including approximately 1.2 million SDG&E customers. It names Reliant Energy, Southern Company, NRG Energy, Dynegy, AES, Williams Energy, Duke Energy North America, and 100 unnamed defendants.

Gordon alleges that the defendants used confidential real-time generator and transmission data, withheld capacity, underbid forward markets, exported or parked electricity, coordinated outages, and manipulated transmission flows to exercise market power and inflate wholesale electricity prices. The complaint says these practices drove more electricity purchases into the spot market and raised retail rates substantially. It cites FERC findings that prices were “unjust and unreasonable,” CAISO findings of excessive market power, and a CPUC estimate that consumers were overcharged approximately $4 billion during summer 2000. The suit asserts claims under California’s Cartwright Act, Unfair Trade Practices Act, Consumers Legal Remedies Act, and unconscionability law, seeking class certification, treble or statutory damages, restitution and disgorgement, interest, attorneys’ fees, and injunctions against continued market manipulation and unreasonable rates.

GOLDWOOD is a leading plywood manufacturer in Yamunanagar, Haryana, offering block boards, flush doors, and plywood across India. It emphasizes uncompromised quality, timely delivery, transparency, responsible operations, and sustainable development focused on people and environmental safety.

The passage argues that effective lawmaking often depends on less-publicly noticed statutes, and that the bill is especially important because the government has begun using criminal proceedings in trust and interstate-commerce cases where prosecution appears reasonably likely. After initially pursuing civil enforcement, it has achieved notable successes, although some cases failed; fines and imprisonment have been imposed, with imprisonment considered more deterrent and heavy fines also effective. Judge Holt described a railroad rebate violation as deliberate, premeditated, and unusually heinous because it involved large transactions, preferential rates that could drive competitors out, experienced corporate officials, and secret conduct difficult to prove. Despite the Interstate Commerce Act of 1887 and repeated legislation, few prosecutions had been brought. Holt said punishment should match the offense’s gravity, with the principal penalty imposed on the corporation because the traffic manager apparently acted under its authority and without personal advantage.

The Missouri Student Union held its annual Veterans Day wreath-laying ceremony, participating in the National Remembrance Day Roll Call by reading the names of MU student veterans who had been killed. Col. Roderik Cox, an MU alumnus with combat, peacekeeping, and covert-mission experience, delivered the keynote. Speakers challenged Hollywood stereotypes, describing veterans as ordinary people pursuing education and careers. Robert Ross, director of the MU Veterans Center, said the event honored past sacrifices while expressing hope for future world peace. A reception followed at Bengal’s Lair in Memorial Union.

The Konektadong Pinoy Act, made law on August 24, 2025, aims to remove barriers to Philippine telecommunications competition and could enable virtual network operators to compete with PLDT. The author argues that new entrants, amid PLDT’s declining profitability and slowing growth, could prompt excess capital investment in a mature, highly penetrated industry and further reduce profitability. Despite PHI’s attractive valuation, the author favors staying on the sidelines due to significant competitive threats.

Passports expire two years after issuance. A naturalized citizen’s old passport may substitute for a naturalization certificate if the prior application contains sufficient information. One passport may cover an applicant’s wife, minor children, and eligible servant if their ages and allegiance are stated; others require separate passports. Professional titles are excluded. A $1 fee per citizen’s passport must accompany applications in currency or postal money order; drafts and checks are not accepted. The Department of State does not obtain foreign visas, provides blank application forms except to commercial passport agents, and requires correspondence to be addressed to its Passport Bureau with a return address. The Secretary of State may reject applications involving unlawful purposes or failure to comply with rules.

In U.S. insular possessions, applications go to the possession’s chief executive; U.S. citizens abroad apply through the nearest diplomatic or consular officer. Applicants must owe U.S. allegiance, submit a sworn written application, and provide birth, occupation, residence, and intended-return information.

The International Nurses Association welcomes Louisiana nurse Joy Williams, BSN, RN, whose agency and hospital work spans more than seven years and who will be featured in Worldwide Leaders In Healthcare.

This systematic literature review examines small-group differentiation in elementary and higher education, emphasizing diverse student populations, learning outcomes, and linguistic barriers. Papers published from 2000 to 2023 were reviewed from Ebsco, Embase, Google Scholar, Microsoft Academic Search, and ProQuest. The review was guided by constructivist and sociocultural theories, which emphasize active knowledge construction, prior experience, collaboration, and scaffolding.

Differentiation involves tailoring teaching methods, content, processes, products, assessments, and learning environments to students’ readiness, interests, abilities, linguistic needs, and cultural backgrounds. Effective implementation requires ongoing assessment, appropriate instructional-level resources, visual and verbal supports, gradually increasing task complexity, and opportunities for student autonomy, discussion, reflection, and collaboration. Elementary education generally emphasizes teacher-guided instruction and foundational skills, while higher education involves greater student independence, specialized content, and changing course cohorts.

Small groups can improve engagement, accountability, confidence, participation, relationships, and motivation, particularly when students feel safe, included, and supported. Five core principles are identified: flexibility, ongoing assessment, respectful and challenging learning experiences, collaboration, and student autonomy and responsibility. Culturally responsive materials and inclusive environments can support students from diverse backgrounds.

Major challenges include inadequate time for planning, large class sizes, insufficient administrative support, limited teacher preparation, and the need to understand each student before grouping. Research limitations include insufficient data for comparative analysis, difficulty assessing links between small-group instruction and learning benchmarks, and a lack of studies comparing outcomes with test scores. The review recommends longitudinal research across educational levels and studies examining outcomes based on visual, auditory, kinesthetic, and read/write learning styles.

The paper introduces the Atlas of Human-AI Interaction, an open-source framework that uses large language models to synthesize empirical findings across human-AI interaction research. Using abstracts collected from ACM Digital Library, IEEE Xplore, Springer Nature Link, and ArXiv, the authors obtained 1,888 papers and used Claude Opus 4.1 to extract 2,037 findings from 1,124 papers. Findings were structured as [cause, relationship, effect] triplets, with relationships classified as increases, decreases, or influences and assigned positive, negative, neutral, or undetermined outcomes.

Semantic embeddings, DBSCAN-based synonym merging, and k-means clustering were used to standardize and organize entities before constructing a knowledge graph containing 1,310 nodes and 3,908 edges. The resulting web visualizer offers three complementary views: a 3D graph for exploring themes, relationships, and research gaps; a Sankey-based cause-effect view for tracing directional relationships; and a searchable paper view for examining source studies and extracted findings.

Analysis identified 24 thematic clusters and recurring research on educational contexts, explainability and trust, design relationships, decision support, and self-referential human-AI dynamics. Louvain community detection found 126 research communities with a modularity score of 0.669. Structural-hole analysis identified large language models, generative AI, trust, chatbots, and AI agents as major bridges across otherwise disconnected domains. Proposed research directions include universal LLM interaction patterns, human-generative AI collaboration models, transferable trust mechanisms, unified agent interaction theory, and cross-domain testing frameworks.

A 30-minute usability study with 20 HAI experts found that the Atlas supported broad landscape visualization, relationship discovery, gap identification, rapid validation of hypothesized connections, and serendipitous cross-disciplinary discovery. Participants rated its research-gap identification highly and viewed it as especially useful for early-stage exploration. Limitations included insufficient detail in paper summaries, difficulty interpreting relationship direction and valence without context, weaker performance in mathematical or formula-heavy research, concerns about corpus coverage, and missing temporal trends or year-based filtering.

The paper positions the Atlas as a complement to conventional literature reviews and as a source of evidence-based guidance for research priorities and HCI design. Future work includes continuous updates, additional relationship types, improved extraction and contradiction detection, and more advanced connectivity analysis.

The 4-3 defense, popular throughout football, was introduced to the NFL by Tom Landry with the New York Giants, modernized by Jimmy Johnson at Miami, and later used by Johnson with Dallas. Tampa Bay’s “Tampa 2” version helped the Buccaneers win the 2003 Super Bowl.

The base defense uses four defensive linemen, three linebackers, and four defensive backs. Its traditional Under front features two 5-technique defensive ends, a 1-technique nose guard, and a 3-technique defensive tackle. The Sam is the largest linebacker, the Mike is an all-around defender responsible for run defense and pass coverage, and the Will is the smallest and most athletic.

The defense is generally strong against the run, gap-sound, and capable of multiple pass coverages. Its 3-technique can create interior pressure, particularly when the nose guard absorbs a double team. Its primary weaknesses are modern spread offenses, which pull linebackers away from the box, and its dependence on specialized personnel. Offenses also attack it by spreading the field, isolating the Sam against quicker receivers, running toward the edge, and using extra blockers.

Common blitzes include a Will edge rush and a defensive-end drop blitz producing a five-man rush with three-under, three-deep coverage. Featured coverages include Tampa 2, in which the Mike linebacker supports the middle between the safeties, and Cover 3.

Tampa Bay, the 2006 NFC champion Chicago Bears, and Montini Catholic High School are highlighted as successful users of the 4-3.

Google launched Gemini Enterprise, an AI platform for business customers seeking secure, large-scale integration. Built on Google Cloud, it provides access to Gemini Ultra models, data governance, security, regulatory compliance, model fine-tuning with proprietary data, explainability, and access controls. Google is positioning transparency, privacy, and accountability as competitive advantages against Microsoft, Amazon, and OpenAI, particularly for regulated industries such as finance, healthcare, and manufacturing. Integration with Google Workspace and third-party software may support wider adoption. Despite positive early feedback, Google must demonstrate reliability and measurable returns while balancing innovation, trust, and compatibility with existing corporate systems.

Ray Dalio’s All Weather Portfolio is a defensive, diversified strategy designed to perform across inflation, deflation, and stagflation. It combines stocks, bonds, and commodities to balance risk exposures and reduce dependence on any single economic environment. Stocks provide long-term growth, bonds act as a balancing anchor, and commodities can offset declines in stocks and bonds during inflationary shocks. The strategy reflects Bridgewater Associates’ risk-parity principles, which seek reliable balance rather than maximum returns.

Backtests show that the portfolio has generally produced lower returns than stocks but substantially smaller drawdowns. It outperformed stocks during the 2008–09 financial crisis, the 2020 Covid-19 sell-off, and the 2022 bear market, while underperforming during stock bull markets. A backtest from July 2007 using daily rebalancing produced a 4.5% CAGR, or 4.15% with annual rebalancing, and a maximum drawdown of 17%; dividends were excluded. During Covid-19, its drawdown was about 6% versus 33% for stocks, and its 2022 drawdown was about 12%.

Leveraging the portfolio 1.5 times raised the backtested CAGR to 6.5% and maximum drawdown to 25%, before accounting for borrowing costs. The article also notes that changing asset weightings can increase returns or reduce drawdowns.

The portfolio can be implemented with ETFs or funds and should generally be rebalanced annually or semiannually; a tax-deferred account is preferable for easier rebalancing. It may suit retirees, FIRE investors, and risk-averse investors seeking smoother returns and lower volatility. However, reduced variability comes at the cost of potentially lower long-term returns than stocks or a 60/40 portfolio, and future performance is not guaranteed.

The court modified a dissolution judgment awarding the mother $31 per month in support for each of the two children. Although the children were in the father’s care about half the time and his expenses during visitation should be considered, the court found the award insufficient. The children were 11 and six; the father was a law-firm partner, and the parties disputed the mother’s income and the father’s future earnings, making the support formulas difficult to apply. The court increased support to $65 per month for each child, effective on the decision date, and affirmed the judgment as modified without costs.

*Please, Continue (Hamlet)*, created by Yan Duyvendak and Roger Bernat, stages Hamlet’s trial for Polonius’s murder in real courtrooms using local judges, barristers and legal teams. Twelve audience volunteers deliberate for 20 minutes before acquitting or convicting him. Inspired by the Guantanamo trials, the production combines Shakespeare’s scenario with an unredacted real case involving a young man accused of killing his girlfriend’s father and incorporates its socioeconomic context. Adapted to each jurisdiction’s laws, the show has toured 12 countries since its 2011 Swiss premiere and is appearing at Melbourne Festival. Duyvendak and Bernat designed it to reveal the complexity of justice systems and encourage jurors to consider conflicting arguments. Duyvendak says participants often change their views of Hamlet’s guilt during closing arguments and develop more nuanced perspectives on crime and sentencing.

The passage examines research on the metaverse in education, a digital environment combining virtual and real spaces through technologies such as virtual reality, augmented reality, and artificial intelligence. It explores the metaverse’s potential for immersive, interactive learning and the factors affecting its adoption, including perceived usefulness, ease of use, personal innovativeness, and enjoyment.

Using PRISMA and bibliometric methods, the study reviewed 270 English-language, peer-reviewed journal articles published in Scopus between January 2015 and July 2024. VOSviewer was used to analyse publication trends, country citations, influential journals and articles, and keyword co-occurrences. The review addresses research trends and productive countries, major scholarly contributions, prominent topics, and areas requiring further study.

No publications appeared before 2020. Annual output rose from four articles in both 2020 and 2021 to 36 in 2022 and 131 in 2023, with 91 articles recorded by July 2024. South Korea had the most publications and citations, followed in productivity by China and the United States; the United Kingdom ranked second by citations. IEEE Transactions on Learning Technologies contained the most reviewed articles, while Sustainability had the highest citation total. The most-cited article was Dwivedi et al. (2022), followed by Hwang and Chien (2022) and Akour et al. (2022).

The analysis identified 22 prominent keywords across six clusters. “Metaverse” was most frequent, followed by “virtual reality,” “education,” “augmented reality,” and “artificial intelligence.” Research themes included using the metaverse to create virtual educational environments and examining students’ and teachers’ perceptions and attitudes toward its use. Proposed future topics include extended reality, blockchain, sustainability, and gamification. The literature associates metaverse applications with greater motivation, immersive and collaborative learning, practical simulation, and improved engagement, particularly in medicine, engineering, and primary education.

Remaining gaps include insufficient longitudinal evidence about long-term effectiveness and scalability, limited research outside East Asia and the United States, and few cross-cultural comparisons. Future studies should assess sustained outcomes and adaptability across traditional, online, and hybrid learning environments and examine diverse educational, cultural, and institutional contexts.
Order affirmed; Thomas dissented because ex parte entry denied plaintiff the statutory right to reply.

Michigan State Police, Emergency Management and Homeland Security urged residents to join a voluntary statewide tornado drill at 1 p.m. Wednesday during Severe Weather Awareness Week, rescheduling to 1 p.m. Thursday if severe weather hits April 19. With only 10–15 minutes of tornado lead time, Kelenske advised preparing 72-hour emergency kits, planning shelter, and monitoring radio and TV broadcasts.

Effective transition defense begins with disciplined offense: secure ball control, select quality shots, eliminate unforced turnovers, pursue offensive rebounds, and maintain defensive balance. Defenders must sprint back, stay ahead of and level with the ball, maintain ball vision, get set, and attack rather than merely retreat. They should force additional passes, deny easy shots and second-chance opportunities, avoid running side by side with opponents, and prevent “stupid hustle” from creating counterbreak opportunities.

Teams should practice defending outnumbered situations. Defensive priorities include pressuring the ball, delaying its advancement, forcing rushed shots, boxing out, and rebounding. In one-on-none situations, defenders pursue the dribbler and attempt low blocks. In two-on-one situations, they contain the ball, avoid reaching, force extra passes, anticipate passes, and take charges. In three-on-two situations, players communicate, pressure the ball, use tandem positioning, rotate or stay with the appropriate matchup, take a charge, and secure the rebound.

After missed field goals or free throws, the closest defender should jam the rebounder and deny the outlet pass. Defenders should attack the primary ball handler’s outlet, prevent long passes, match up with opponents, slow penetration near the sideline, and consider traps. Turnovers and blocked shots require an immediate recovery: contain the ball handler, sprint back, maintain assignments, deny easy baskets, and erase the opponent’s advantage.

Game strategies include taking care of the ball, going hard to offensive boards, scouting early-offense tactics, disrupting primary outlet passes, and immediately substituting players who do not sprint back. Coaches should emphasize transition awareness, floor awareness, offensive rebounding, defensive balance, outnumbered defense, counterattacking, and defensive stops after turnovers. Instruction should use the whole-part-whole method, emphasizing correct spacing, timing, footwork, and execution through transition-specific drills and full-court scrimmages.

**GHCB and NAE handling:** The GHCB carries the minimum state required for each non-automatic exit. Before every NAE, the guest and hypervisor clear and reset `VALID_BITMAP`, then set bits for valid fields. Guests minimally set `SW_EXITCODE`, `SW_EXITINFO1`, and `SW_EXITINFO2`; hypervisors minimally set the two info fields. Bitmap positions are derived from each field’s byte offset divided by eight. Standard processing requires the guest to populate the specified GHCB state, set the GHCB MSR, and, after VMGEXIT, restore returned state and advance RIP past the faulting instruction. Interrupts and preemption should be disabled while updating or accessing the active GHCB; a separate or saved GHCB is recommended for NMI handling.

**Error reporting:** A nonzero `SW_EXITINFO1[31:0]` reports a hypervisor error. A value of 1 requests guest exception handling, with `SW_EXITINFO2` supplying the error code. Other conditions include malformed VMGEXIT input, invalid or unmapped scratch state, unmarked required inputs, invalid NAE input, and hypervisor-specific errors.

**Event processing:** For IOIO_PROT and MSR_PROT, the guest must decode the faulting instruction or para-virtualize it and provide the NAE table’s required state. String-based I/O operations use a decrypted buffer in the GHCB reserved area, whose GPA is placed in `SW_SCRATCH`; multiple VMGEXIT calls may be needed. VMMCALL support is hypervisor-specific. MMIO faults require a reserved nested-page-table bit and use `#NPF/MMIO_READ` or `#NPF/MMIO_WRITE`; MMIO transfers similarly use decrypted shared buffers and may be divided across multiple calls.

Page State Change requests use a Page State Change structure in the shared buffer, which can hold up to 253 entries. Guests can request private or shared pages, and SEV-SNP guests can issue PSMASH and UNSMASH hints. The hypervisor updates `cur_entry` and, for 2 MB pages, `cur_page` as work progresses, allowing interrupted requests to resume. Completion is indicated by `cur_entry` exceeding `end_entry`; otherwise `SW_EXITINFO2` provides a reason code.

**SNP requests and services:** SNP Guest Requests use separate shared request and response pages. The hypervisor translates and validates their GPAs, invokes the firmware API, and saves the firmware return code in `SW_EXITINFO2`. Successful requests update the message sequence number. Rate limiting and retry are recommended to avoid firmware denial of service and IV reuse. Extended Guest Requests can return VCEK or VLEK certificates through a GUID-indexed table; insufficient data pages are reported through a page count and `SW_EXITINFO2`. SNP TIO requests similarly exchange data pages, PCI identifiers, MMIO ranges, and TDISP status while returning measurements, certificates, and an attestation report.

Additional SNP NAE services include AP Creation, which manages vCPU state through VMSA pages and permits hotplug; `#HV` doorbell-page management; `#HV` IP I delivery; `#HV` timer emulation; APIC ID discovery; VMPL changes; Secure AVIC backing-page registration; and guest termination requests. Termination supports reason codes and 64 bits of termination information. Negotiated-protocol versions must use the Unsupported Event exit code for unsupported NAEs.

**Guest identification and AP startup:** Hypervisors expose CPUID properties so guests can identify SEV-ES support and obtain the encryption-bit position and physical-address reduction. SEV-ES AP startup requires initial register values because measured registers cannot later be changed. Reset-hold requests park processors, while an encrypted, aligned 4 KB AP jump table communicates initial CS/RIP values through SET and GET NAE events or the SEV-SNP Secrets Page. SNP AP Creation provides an alternative vCPU-creation path and supports hotplug, whereas SEV-ES vCPU hotplug is unsupported.

**Other host services:** NMI handling uses the guest’s “NMI Complete” message to determine when another NMI may be injected; the hypervisor intercepts `#DB` rather than IRET. Full debug-register virtualization is available when supported; otherwise DR7 reads and writes are intercepted and the written value is cached. SMM and nested virtualization are unsupported.

**`#HV` doorbell notifications:** The shared doorbell page contains a 16-bit `PendingEvent` field and a `NoEoiRequired` assist byte. It can identify a pending vector, NMI, `#MC`, and whether further host signaling is needed. The host emulates APIC presentation, acknowledgement, in-service, and EOI behavior and writes pending vectors when the vCPU is not running. The guest must atomically exchange `PendingEvent` with zero before acting on a vector, validate observed vectors, and use either the EOI assist or an explicit APIC EOI write. HLT handling must account for `#HV` delivery being independent of interrupt shadows.

Navy’s free Pier Pressure app uses games to help Sailors assess drinking habits and the health and career effects of excessive drinking. It includes calorie and pushup estimates, Uber and Lyft ride integration, and had been played more than 30,000 times.

Stocks fell Tuesday as fears of higher rates and slowing growth drove the Dow down 424.56 points and the Nasdaq 1.7%. Caterpillar and 3M declined, while Treasury yields topped 3%, potentially prompting tighter Federal Reserve policy.

In Hemsell v. Summers, the Texas Court of Civil Appeals reversed and remanded a $30,890 judgment for wrongful death. J. W. Summers died after his automobile collided with one driven by Clennon C. Hemsell, an employee of Columbian Fuel Corporation, while Summers was traveling to work and Hemsell was returning from company property in Kansas. His wife, children, and mother sued both defendants.

The court held that jury instructions concerning damages contained reversible error. Life expectancy was a factual question for the jury, and mortality tables were not conclusive; the instructions improperly assumed fixed life spans of 34½ years for Summers and approximately 20 years for his mother. Damages for the widow should reflect the pecuniary benefits she reasonably expected from her husband, while the mother’s life expectancy, present value, and other relevant evidence belonged to the jury. For minor children, the reasonable monetary value of nurture, care, and education is recoverable, but sorrow, grief, love, companionship, and parental society are not. Thus, instructions concerning the children’s losses and the court’s failure to exclude grief from consideration were erroneous. The suggested consideration of college expenses was unsupported and improperly invaded the jury’s province.

The court rejected requested issues on sole proximate cause and a new independent cause. It also found counsel’s criticism of opposing counsel for introducing admissible divorce records improper and inflammatory; the jury should have been instructed to disregard the remarks.

Security researcher Michael Myng found a keylogger in Synaptics touchpad drivers used across hundreds of HP devices. Disabled by default, it could be activated through a registry change to let a malicious actor with administrative privileges monitor keyboard activity. HP confirmed it was a debug trace and released patches for more than 450 products on Nov. 7. HP and Synaptics said they had no access to customer data as a result. The finding followed a similar May vulnerability involving inadvertently retained debugging code in Conexant audio drivers on numerous HP laptops.

Chinese police shot dead three knife-wielding attackers in Pishan County, Xinjiang, after five people were killed and 10 injured. Authorities restored “social order” and began an investigation but did not disclose the ethnic backgrounds of those involved. The passage notes Beijing’s accusations of Uighur separatist involvement and cites previous attacks and police killings in Xinjiang and Kunming.

An MLS roundup previews four midweek matches and reviews Philadelphia vs. Chicago and New England’s 1–1 draw. Bořek Dočdal scored with two assists for Philadelphia, which remained unbeaten in four matches. Ilsinho also netted against Chicago after evading Bastian Schweinsteiger. The article praises Dočkal’s play, criticizes a slow cross to Josef Martinez and notes Teal Bunbury’s late penalty for New England.

Johnny Juzang is making a case for a Timberwolves roster spot after Nickeil Alexander-Walker’s departure. On a non-guaranteed contract, the 24-year-old scored 20 points in 14 preseason minutes and shot 9-of-15 from three. His shooting fits Minnesota’s approach, though the team must decide whether to retain him.

Researchers from Johns Hopkins University School of Medicine and Mayo Clinic published a peer-reviewed guideline in JAMA Internal Medicine recommending that CK-MB testing be eliminated when evaluating suspected heart attacks because cardiac troponin is more sensitive and CK-MB provides no additional diagnostic value. Yet a 2013 survey found that 77% of nearly 2,000 U.S. laboratories still used CK-MB.

The guideline proposes four steps for phasing out the test: hospitalwide education, removal of CK-MB from routine order sets with clinical stakeholders, electronic alerts when clinicians order it, and measurement of test use, care quality, and safety outcomes. Researchers also cited evidence that troponin better predicts in-hospital mortality and disease severity and noted that all blood tests for diagnosing heart attacks add $416 million annually to U.S. health-care costs.

The report is the first in a series of High Value Practice Academic Alliance implementation guides addressing unnecessary transfusions, daily laboratory tests, antibiotics for asymptomatic bacteriuria, inappropriate Clostridium difficile testing, and cardiac telemetry.

The study combines hydrodynamic simulations, time-dependent chemistry, and radiative transfer to create synthetic observations of a collapsing 5 M⊙ prestellar core and compare line-profile-derived infall velocities with true mass-weighted velocities. Using the Myers et al. (1996) method across six molecular tracers, two apertures, and two late evolutionary stages, measured infall velocities consistently underestimated the true values, sometimes by an order of magnitude. CS gave the closest estimates, reaching roughly half the true velocity, while HCO+ often produced substantially lower values because of chemical and radiative-transfer effects. The discrepancy arises because self-absorption features mainly trace outer, slower-moving material rather than the core’s inner, faster infall. Consequently, mass-accretion rates based on these line profiles are also underestimated. Non-thermal velocity dispersion from optically thin lines was typically within a factor of two of the true infall speed and may be a better diagnostic, though this may not hold in turbulent environments.

Dr Sachiendra Amaragiri was struck off the UK medical register after a tribunal found he abused his professional position by sending a love letter to a female patient. He apologised and intends to appeal.

Tesla reported that Jerome Guillen transitioned from President, Automotive to President, Tesla Heavy Trucking, effective March 11, 2021. He will lead all aspects of the Tesla Semi program, including its charging and servicing networks.

Sony’s U.S. promotion through September 30, 2017, offered up to $300 instant savings on selected cameras, plus up to $500 for trading in an interchangeable-lens camera. It also offered up to $200 on A7 cameras and $100 on selected lenses and accessories, with free U.S. shipping.

Compass Minerals International remains rated “Buy,” with rising salt and plant nutrition revenue and volumes, plus cost cuts boosting cash flow and EBITDA. Despite higher net debt and leverage than peers, its lower valuation multiples offer substantial upside. Management projects further 2025 revenue growth, though leverage limits the rating to “Buy” rather than “Strong Buy.”

William O’Neill developed CANSLIM, a seven-variable stock-selection method based on earnings, new products or management, supply and demand, stock leadership, institutional sponsorship, and market direction. It is primarily intended for long-term investing and focuses on companies with strong fundamentals and uptrends.

Backtests indicate that CANSLIM beat the S&P 500 since 2003, including an older reported result of 18% CAGR versus 9%. However, performance has weakened in recent years, and the strategy involves high volatility, large drawdowns, and significant capital-loss risk. Its small-cap bias may partly explain its historical outperformance.

Implementation is demanding because some criteria are subjective, complete computer-generated backtests were unavailable before 2003, and technical trading rules are difficult to define. Investor’s Business Daily offers a proprietary, computer-ranked IBD 50 list based on the seven criteria. Investors should research selected stocks thoroughly because company results may not meet expectations.

The speaker says his team earned a needed win after Rucchin scored twice and Jiggy played well. Although he was not at his best, he contributed offensively and believed the team largely controlled the game. He emphasizes consistency, preparation, and coach Mike’s preparation as keys to success, saying he rarely talks before games and leads by example. He calls the first two New Jersey games an aberration caused by poor legs and pace and expects a stronger performance in Anaheim. The team must tighten defensively while maintaining its road offense. He describes a hard stick hit, being examined, and returning to play, saying he felt fine. He also notes that a lengthy playoff series can create animosity and recalls enjoying the team’s comeback and Rucchin’s goal.

Peter Crouch jokingly commented on the Duke and Duchess of Cambridge waving with their newborn after Kate Middleton gave birth to their third child. His tweet was retweeted more than 22,000 times, prompting his wife, Abbey Clancy, to reply bluntly. Crystal Palace also tweeted “Great name!”, interpreted as a joke about the yet-unannounced baby’s name.

Golden State’s frequent second-half rallies inspired “Superman syndrome,” the belief that a very talented team can simply reverse a large deficit. The Warriors led the NBA in third-quarter scoring and erased deficits against Houston, outscoring the Rockets 64-25 and 58-38 after halftime in Games 6 and 7 of the Western Conference finals. But their comeback formula was inconsistent: Houston won the second half of Game 2, while Golden State shot 35 percent in Game 4 and committed 11 turnovers in Game 5. Mark Jackson and Jeff Van Gundy credited the team’s adjustments and leadership but warned that repeatedly digging holes could eventually cost it. The passage compares these rallies with comeback feats by Dave Wottle and the Oakland A’s.

Value-seeking investors are buying mutual-fund closed-end equity schemes on stock exchanges at discounts to NAV. These schemes generally lock investors for three or five years, while exchange liquidity is limited; at maturity, redemption at NAV can turn the purchase discount into profit. Discounts vary with maturity and taxes. Experts suggest favoring heavily traded schemes with assets under management above Rs 250 crore.

Airbus is developing Project Vahana, an autonomous, helicopter-style flying taxi designed to carry several riders and help commuters avoid congested roads. The company aims for a functional prototype by 2017 and short-haul availability by 2021, emphasizing clean technology and potential infrastructure savings. Other efforts include Uber’s planned VTOL network, Urban Aeronautics’ passenger drone, AeroMobil’s road-and-air vehicle, and flying-car prototypes backed by Skype’s co-founder and Larry Page.

A letter from fired assistant U.S. attorney Michael Ben’Ary claimed DOJ leadership prioritized punishing perceived presidential enemies over public safety and that a false social media post apparently led to his dismissal during the 2021 Afghanistan airport bombing prosecution. The bombing killed 13 U.S. service members and 160 Afghan civilians. Ben’Ary was fired after Julie Kelly linked him to former Deputy Attorney General Lisa Monaco; his letter suggested he may have resisted James Comey’s indictment.

The passage describes a light-emitting diode device and manufacturing method providing reliable connections between luminous bodies and electrodes. The device includes a thin-film transistor substrate, first and second diode electrodes, passivation patterns, cylindrical micro-LEDs containing protected inorganic crystalline emitting material, and bridge patterns electrically connecting the micro-LEDs to the electrodes. The emitting material may comprise sequentially arranged p-type, intermediate, and n-type semiconductor layers. Alternating electrode lines, barrier ribs, and reflective materials may improve light efficiency. Passivation structures and aligned sidewalls reduce bridge-pattern steps and minimize bridge breakage.

In manufacturing, micro-LEDs are placed and aligned using a voltage applied between the electrodes, followed by second passivation. A single mask process uses two etchings: a longer, more anisotropic first etching and a shorter, more isotropic second etching with an oxygen-containing additive gas, producing coplanar micro-LED and passivation sidewalls. Bridge patterns and intervening passivation are then formed. The passage also describes a display panel driven by scan, data, power, and timing circuits, with light-emitting units containing thin-film transistors, a capacitor, and micro-LEDs.

An MLB wild-card preview highlights three winner-take-all Game 3s after every team rebounded with a Game 2 win, only the second such slate in baseball history. The Tigers’ inability to score is a major concern against the Padres: Detroit stranded a franchise-record 15 runners in Game 2 and went 3-for-38 with runners in scoring position across three potential elimination games. Short outings from Yu Darvish and Jameson Taillon could make bullpen depth decisive. In the Yankees-Red Sox matchup, Boston again faces a potential bullpen battle after using six relievers when Alex Cora pulled Brayan Bello after 28 pitches. The preview also lists playoff odds, brackets, manager news, and other MLB playoff coverage.

Aspen will replace its Fourth of July fireworks with a 15-minute, 50-drone patriotic show at Wagner Park, citing wildfire risks and Colorado fire restrictions. Organized by Acra, it may echo the 2018 Winter Olympics drone display.

The article reports that the U.S. national debt surpassed $21 trillion, rising by $73 billion in one day, $215 billion in February, and more than $1 trillion in six months. It says debt grew 6% last year, compared with 4.4% economic growth including inflation, and 123% over a decade versus 36% for the economy. The author argues that borrowing from institutions such as Social Security, the banking system, and the Federal Reserve does not make the debt harmless, and describes three public responses: ignoring it, dismissing it, or preparing for possible future consequences.

Jio’s Galaxy Club offers Samsung Galaxy J2 2018 and Galaxy J7 Duo buyers Rs 2,750 cashback through 55 vouchers of Rs 50 each. Jio SIM users also receive extra data on Rs 198 and 299 plans, with the J7 Duo offering doubled daily data. The offers run through September 30.

New CFPB rules would require payday and auto-title lenders to assess whether borrowers can repay within 30 days and limit account debits without reauthorization. The CFPB estimates loan volume could fall by half, forcing many of the industry’s 16,000 stores to close. Industry groups warn this could push consumers toward unregulated lenders. The rules would not take effect until 2019 and could be reversed by Congress amid Republican opposition. Separately, the OCC lifted restrictions on banks making small-dollar loans. A Pew poll found 70% of surveyed adults favored greater regulation of payday lenders.

Transcriptomic analysis of pretreatment biopsies from 67 patients with 12 sarcoma subtypes treated across three immune checkpoint inhibitor trials identified two immune clusters: immune-hot and immune-cold. Immune-hot tumors had higher objective response rates (30% versus 8.1%) and longer median progression-free survival (3.65 versus 1.7 months) than immune-cold tumors, independent of histologic subtype. Elevated expression of six transposable element (TE) families and IKZF1 distinguished immune-hot tumors. Higher TE scores and IKZF1 expression correlated with antiviral, interferon, antigen-processing, and CD8+ T-cell pathways, as well as longer progression-free survival. IKZF1 expression was also associated with B-cell infiltrates and significantly higher response rates. Conditional-independence results were consistent with IKZF1 influencing immune type through TE expression, although functional studies were needed. In an independent TCGA cohort of 190 sarcomas, immune-hot tumors and tumors with high TE scores or IKZF1 expression showed improved overall survival. The findings support baseline immune state, TE score, and IKZF1 as potential biomarkers for checkpoint inhibitor outcomes, but validation and functional investigation remain necessary.

Meagan Holt participates in a Seattle Children’s writing program that helps parents journal about ill children. Writing about her daughter Madeline, who may die from Zellweger syndrome, gives Holt an outlet for bottled-up emotions and helps her focus on the present. PACT says the writing can foster calm, relief, and sometimes acceptance.

Happy Home Furnishers plans to close its Neath store after 33 years, citing anti-social behaviour, disruption from lengthy street works, limited free parking and rising business rates. Its director said staff encountered fights, rowdiness and hazardous waste, while customers avoided crossing the road to enter the store. Nearby traders reported varying effects, with anti-social behaviour generally worse during summer.

Neath Council said the street works were completed several years ago and benefited the town. Benches installed for people with mobility issues were removed after misuse, and the council said it supports police efforts to address anti-social behaviour. It also cited a relatively low shop vacancy rate, a 600-space car park with free parking after 3pm, regeneration work and events attracting visitors.

The company director said business rates had risen substantially but were no worse than in other towns. The Welsh Government said the 2017 revaluation adversely affected some towns and highlighted relief schemes supporting nearly 15,000 small and medium-sized businesses, alongside £110 million in annual small-business relief.

Happy Home Furnishers will continue operating elsewhere and may seek another site in Neath.

The study examines science scepticism towards science education research (SSSE), defined as scepticism about the potential positive impact of physics education research on teaching practice. It used a two-step mixed-methods design: guideline-based interviews with 13 purposefully selected German physics teachers, followed by a survey of 174 teachers from Germany and Austria.

Interviews identified seven attitude categories, including positive views of research’s relevance and intrinsic value, alongside sceptical views that findings cannot be implemented, are less useful than teachers’ experience, or reflect poor cooperation between researchers and schools. Exploratory factor analysis of 22 survey items yielded four factors: relevance for individual teachers, feasibility for classroom practice, relevance for teaching generally, and research–school cooperation.

Latent profile analysis identified four teacher profiles: Sceptical Ones (14%), Uncertain Ones (27%), Undersupplied Ones (41%), and Research Advocates (18%). The largest group valued research but considered its findings difficult to apply and criticized research–school cooperation. All profiles expressed some scepticism about cooperation. Multinomial logistic regression found that only frequency of reading instructional journals significantly predicted profile membership: more frequent readers were more likely to be Uncertain or Research Advocates and less likely to be Sceptical. Teaching experience, teacher education, school type, and doctoral degree were not significant predictors.

The authors recommend integrating research more strongly into physics teacher education and professional development, improving communication and collaboration between researchers and schools, and examining additional informational factors. Limitations include small, nonrepresentative samples, possible participant-selection and Hawthorne effects, uncertain classification in latent profile analysis, and a potentially imprecise measure of journal-reading frequency.

The Ravens traded pass rusher Odafe Oweh and a 2026 fifth-round pick to the Chargers for safety Alohi Gilman as Baltimore’s defense struggles. The 1-4 Ravens allow a league-high 35.4 points per game and rank 31st in pass defense. Oweh, 26, had no sacks in five games after recording a career-high 10 last season, and the trade creates about $8 million in cap space. Baltimore also added veteran safety Gardner-Johnson to address a lack of experienced depth. Gilman, 28, was a key deep safety for last season’s top-ranked Chargers defense; Los Angeles sought an edge rusher while a veteran on injured reserve is eligible to return in Week 7. Ravens coach Jim Harbaugh said he would “consider everything” with the team at 1-4.

At a VAT forum in Lilongwe, Malawi’s treasury secretary urged African countries to use technology and electronic fiscal devices to improve tax compliance and collection. He cited Malawi’s progress in electronic monitoring and an impending Tax Administration Act. VADA is developing African strategies against tax evasion.

Hong Liu reviews the propagators of a free scalar field. \(G_+\) and \(G_-\) can be interpreted heuristically as transition amplitudes in opposite directions or as two-point correlations; their time-ordered combination is the Feynman or time-ordered Green’s function. For a complex scalar field, the equal-time commutator vanishes because \(\phi\) creates particles while \(\phi^\dagger\) creates antiparticles, so particles cannot transform into antiparticles under charge conservation.

The retarded, advanced, and Feynman propagators have poles at \(\omega=\pm\omega_k\). Their different prescriptions correspond to contours passing above or below these poles. The \(\epsilon\)-prescription provides an equivalent, convenient method by keeping the contour fixed and shifting the poles infinitesimally.

In the free theory, vacuum \(n\)-point functions factorize into sums of two-point functions because all creation and annihilation operators must be paired. Thus, knowing the two-point function determines all vacuum correlations. Composite operators, such as \(\phi^2\), \(\phi^3\), the Hamiltonian density, and the stress tensor, can have singular behavior at coincident points and require renormalization; such divergences are generic in quantum field theory.

The lecture then turns to interactions. Nonlinear terms in the Lagrangian produce interacting theories; a \(\phi^4\) term is chosen because a \(\phi^3\) term has no lower energy bound. Its coupling \(\lambda\) controls the interaction strength. The resulting nonlinear equation of motion cannot be solved exactly, so the theory will be treated perturbatively for small \(\lambda\), using path integrals.

Scattering is emphasized as the principal way to probe interactions experimentally. The S-matrix contains transition amplitudes between widely separated, noninteracting initial and final particle states. It is unitary, equals the identity in the free theory, and may be written as \(S=1+iT\), with the kinematically required momentum-conservation delta function separated out to define the scattering amplitude \(M_{\alpha\beta}\). The LSZ theorem relates this amplitude to time-ordered correlation functions in the vacuum of the full interacting theory. The next lecture will introduce the path-integral approach.

The President clarified that he did not intend to deny Congress’s constitutional authority to regulate the custody and disposition of U.S. public money and property. He affirmed legislative power to prescribe how such property is handled, while asserting that the Executive has no control over it unless authorized by law or the Constitution. He requested that his clarification be entered alongside his earlier message in the Senate Journal.

Detroit must remain focused and disciplined as the Stanley Cup Finals continue against Philadelphia. The speaker emphasizes that home ice is not an automatic advantage, noting Philadelphia’s strong road performances in recent series. Players should ignore family, fan, and media distractions, and Detroit can rely on several players’ experience in a similar situation two years earlier.

Penalties are a major concern because power plays create sustained pressure and force teams to shorten their benches. Detroit largely avoided retaliation and foolish penalties, but late penalties in close playoff games can erase otherwise strong territorial play. Goaltenders Mike and Chris are praised for their confidence, resilience, and strong tandem; the pressure of facing elite postseason goalies is not expected to distract the team. A failed scoring attempt against an aggressive goaltender was defended as the correct play.

Detroit is also managing preparation by arriving the night before games to rest and adjust to the ice. Fetisov’s pairing with Konstantinov and Murphy’s fit with Lidstrom are credited to puck handling, coverage, and experience. The earlier Devils series demonstrated the importance of defense, penalty killing, and capitalizing on limited chances. Current roster experiments, including using Lapointe and McCarty at left wing and adding Maltby, address a surplus of right-wingers and emphasize speed and scoring opportunities.

This application, a continuation of PCT/CN2019/119114 filed November 18, 2019, describes sidelink positioning methods and apparatus for communication systems. It addresses errors in existing network-device-to-terminal positioning, which requires core-network control and whose errors increase with distance. The proposed methods configure terminal devices with sidelink positioning reference-signal resources, sequences, reference-terminal information, and measurement-reporting instructions.

Terminals exchange sidelink reference signals and measure Rx–Tx time differences and/or sidelink angles of arrival. Measurement values can be reported directly between terminals through a PC5 interface or to a network device through a Uu interface. A terminal or the network device can then determine the target terminal’s position using the measurements and the reference terminal’s position. Optional two-way measurements establish the terminals’ relative position relationship, and a second terminal can perform measurements when the target terminal does not support sidelink reference-signal measurement. Positioning may begin with a request that optionally includes a zone identifier. The shorter inter-terminal measurement path and reduced reliance on core-network transmission are described as improving accuracy and reducing latency. The document also provides terminal and network apparatus, processor and processing apparatus implementations, a computer program product, a computer-readable storage medium, and a communication system.
Perspective, front, back, side, top, and bottom views show two new analytical instrument embodiments. Broken-line features are not part of the claimed design.

After retiring from civil litigation in Toronto, Marcel Strigberger recounts discarding law-school books bought more than 50 years earlier, despite considering each one. He recalls cases involving puffery, contracts contrary to public policy, property interests, and a cargo-ship explosion but concludes he has little need for the details. He recycles the books, later regretting that one was listed online for over C$1,000, and keeps one thick volume as a reading stand.

A June 2014 Wall Street Journal article reported that Hertz would restate three years of financial results because of accounting problems, while its stock fell about 9%. Auto industry analyst Abby Devins began investigating whether depreciation of Hertz’s large rental fleet contributed to the issues and could affect future vehicle acquisitions.

The U.S. car rental industry generated approximately $36 billion in 2013 and was dominated by Enterprise Holdings, Avis Budget Group, and Hertz, which together held 71% of the market. Hertz, founded in 1918 and taken public in 2006 after ownership by General Motors, Ford, and private equity firms, operated nearly 12,000 locations in 145 countries at the end of 2013. Its fleet exceeded 700,000 vehicles, and it employed more than 30,000 people.

Hertz expanded from a single on-airport brand into a multi-brand company through the 2012 acquisition of Dollar Thrifty, the 2013 launch of Firefly, and a 20% stake in China Auto Rental. Its Donlen subsidiary provided fleet leasing and management services. Hertz reported record 2013 revenue and EBITDA; revenue increased roughly 30% and net income more than doubled from 2011 to 2013. Revenue-earning equipment represented more than half of total assets, while depreciation averaged about 25% of expenses.

The case explains that depreciation depends on an asset’s useful life and residual value, commonly using straight-line allocation. Hertz estimated rental equipment’s holding periods and residual values, reviewed depreciation rates quarterly, and adjusted them for market conditions. Its fleet included program cars covered by manufacturer repurchase or guaranteed-depreciation programs and non-program cars carrying residual-price risk. Devins collected Hertz’s and Avis Budget Group’s revenue-earning equipment balances, depreciation expenses, and disposal gains and losses from 2006 through 2013 to assess depreciation’s role in Hertz’s accounting problems.

AI could augment human cognition, learning, and creativity while enabling new skills, professions, and more enjoyable approaches to cognitive work. However, excessive reliance on systems such as LLMs may weaken independent learning and critical thinking, shift researchers from generating ideas to evaluating them, and impede the internalization of knowledge and skills. Proposed safeguards include delegating only tedious or nonessential tasks, avoiding passive learning, cultivating critical problem-solving, and treating AI as an augmenter and thought partner. Personalized learning pathways, interactive assessments, project-based learning, and real-time problem-solving could become more prevalent, while human judgment remains essential for integrating multiple skills and contextual understanding.

AI may also reshape the social division of labor by making specialized knowledge more accessible, blurring job boundaries, and challenging structures based on knowledge scarcity and the traditional middle class. These shifts could encourage a more flexible gig economy, bringing efficiency and spatial and temporal flexibility but also inadequate benefits, instability, excessive workloads, and weak labor protections. Flexible contracts, tailored social welfare, technological support for workers, equitable AI access, new industries, employment opportunities, and stronger social safety nets could mitigate these risks. More dynamic, network-based collaboration involving individuals and organizations may promote innovation across fields and personalized industries.

In social science, LLMs may expand access to large-scale online information, synthesize research data, automate analysis, and perform tasks such as stance detection, sentiment analysis, response coding, and hypothesis generation. These approaches face challenges involving biased or stereotyped outputs, uncertain fidelity to real participants, data and deployment costs, misinformation, and ethical use. Human-AI collaboration, combining automated processing with researcher oversight and intuition, is needed to preserve rigor, nuance, and integrity.

AI governance must address misinformation, deepfakes, bias, discrimination, security, and other rapidly emerging risks despite inconsistent national rules and limited communication between governments and technology companies. The passage recommends forward-looking regulation combining top-down cooperation among policymakers, industry, and academia with bottom-up participation by developers, users, and communities. Transparent reporting channels, prompt investigation and updating of rules, shared responsibility throughout model lifecycles, and monitoring of community needs are presented as ways to promote safe, trustworthy, equitable, and human-centered AI development.

The TLV321x and TLV322x comparators have 1.8 mV of internal hysteresis, with trip points determined by threshold, input offset, and hysteresis voltages. Unused inputs must not be tied together; instead, they should be connected to defined in-range voltages separated by at least 50 mV.

Push-pull outputs can source and sink current but must not connect to another output or directly short to the opposite supply rail. Unused push-pull outputs should remain floating. Open-drain outputs support pull-ups from 0 V to 5.5 V, logical ORing, and level translation; recommended pull-up current is 100 µA to 1 mA. Unused open-drain outputs may float or connect to V−. Series current-limiting resistors are recommended where output shorts are possible.

Internal ESD protection limits input voltages to 0.2 V beyond the supply rails; series input resistance should limit clamp current to 10 mA or less. During power-on reset, the output remains low for up to 32 µs after the 1.65 V POR threshold is crossed, then reflects the differential input.

In a basic comparator, output logic depends on the input relative to the reference and can be reversed by swapping inputs. Propagation delay varies by transition direction and increases with small overdrive, particularly below 100 mV. External positive-feedback hysteresis can prevent noisy chatter; inverting configurations use a three-resistor network referenced to VCC, while non-inverting configurations use two resistors and a reference voltage.

A low-side current-sensing example amplifies a shunt-resistor voltage drop and triggers above 1.1 V. Stable, low-noise power, a close 0.1 µF ceramic supply bypass capacitor, minimized input/output coupling, and appropriate damping or controlled-impedance routing are recommended because the outputs behave as high-speed digital devices.

During U.S. Ambassador William Symington’s visit, Rivers State Governor Nyesom Ezenwo Wike urged the U.S. government to establish a visa office in Port Harcourt. He accused the NDDC of prioritizing political fundraising over development, citing its failure to fund the Mother and Child Hospital despite the state paying ₦800 million. Wike also called for a technocratic NDDC leader, cleanup of Ogoni land, and U.S. partnerships in agriculture, oil and gas, and industrialization.
