The patent application describes CAR-expressing immune effector cells with enhanced therapeutic efficacy by reducing or eliminating the expression or function of TET1, TET2 and/or TET3, particularly TET2. This decreases 5-hydroxymethylcytosine and is associated with enhanced CAR T-cell proliferation, cytokine production, degranulation and function. CARs may target tumor antigens including CD19 and contain antigen-binding, transmembrane and intracellular signaling domains. TET activity can be inhibited through CRISPR/Cas9, zinc-finger nucleases, TALENs, meganucleases, siRNA or shRNA, dominant-negative proteins or binding partners, and small molecules, either ex vivo or in vivo. The application also covers manufacturing cells by integrating CAR sequences into TET genes, treating subjects before, during or after CAR-cell therapy, vectors encoding CARs and TET inhibitors, and cell populations enriched for stem-cell memory T cells. Patient data associated CAR19 clonal expansion with insertion between TET2 exons 9 and 10 and disrupted TET2 function, while TET2 shRNA reduced 5-hydroxymethylcytosine and expanded stem-cell memory T cells.

Russian-style after-school mathematics programs are rapidly expanding across the United States, driven by parental interest in rigorous instruction, concerns about school curricula, and fears that children will fall behind without extra study. The Russian School of Mathematics, founded in Newton in 1997, reports 22,000 students at 40 branches, including 15 in Massachusetts. Weekly attendance typically costs about $2,000 annually.

The movement grew from the Soviet Union’s strong mathematics tradition and the emigration of Russian educators and families, particularly to the Boston area. Co-founder Inessa Rifkin opened the school after discovering that her eighth-grade son and other immigrant children had not mastered the mathematics expected for their age. The curriculum emphasizes reasoning, early algebra and geometry, and independent discovery rather than memorization and drills. Programs also use manipulatives, puzzles, and small, ability-based groups, sometimes adapting Soviet teaching methods in ways that differ from those used in Russia.

Parents say Russian math is challenging, engaging, and helpful for regular schoolwork. Some believe it opens future opportunities in science and technology, while others worry it creates an after-school “arms race.” Teachers report that some students arrive at public school having already covered advanced topics, potentially complicating instruction. Other concerns include overconfidence, unequal access because of the program’s cost, and widening performance gaps between affluent and lower-income students.

Limited evidence suggests possible benefits. At Newton South High School, the proportion of students in honors mathematics increased from about 20 percent to 30 percent over a decade, though educators cannot establish that Russian math caused the rise. American researchers have not extensively studied the methods, and their effect on public schools remains uncertain.

This study used Mendelian randomization to assess whether genetically determined pericardial adipose tissue (PAT) causally influences cardiovascular diseases (CVDs) and whether hypertension mediates these effects. Eleven independent PAT-related SNPs from a GWAS of 28,161 white British participants served as instrumental variables, with inverse-variance weighting as the primary analysis and multiple sensitivity and heterogeneity tests. PAT was associated with higher risks of CVD, heart failure, hypertension, coronary heart disease, ischemic heart disease, ischemic stroke, and venous thromboembolism, but not with cardiac arrhythmias, atrial fibrillation, aortic aneurysm, hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, myocardial infarction, cardioembolic stroke, small-vessel stroke, large-artery stroke, or subarachnoid hemorrhage. Two-step mediation analysis indicated that hypertension partly explained the associations with CVD, heart failure, coronary heart disease, ischemic heart disease, and ischemic stroke, with mediated proportions of 13.23%, 13.51%, 19.18%, and 14.51% for the latter four outcomes, respectively. The findings suggest PAT may be a therapeutic target and that antihypertensive strategies could complement cardiovascular treatment, particularly for people with obesity. Limitations include an exclusively European population, possible sample overlap, inability to perform multivariable MR, small samples for several outcomes, and potential residual bias and pleiotropy. Further mechanistic, longitudinal, and experimental studies are needed.

News reports from October 22–23, 2001, centered on an SEC request for information about Enron’s related-party transactions and concerns over the company’s financial reporting. Enron said the voluntary request concerned partnerships including LJM Cayman and LJM2 Co-Investment, which CFO Andrew Fastow had managed until resigning amid conflict-of-interest concerns. Enron characterized the SEC inquiry as informal, while the SEC declined to comment and had not announced a formal investigation. Kenneth Lay said Enron would cooperate fully and maintained that the arrangements had been reviewed, approved and properly disclosed.

The request followed Enron’s October 16 announcement of $1.01 billion in third-quarter charges and a $618 million loss, including $35 million connected with ending the LJM partnerships. Enron also disclosed on an analyst call that it had repurchased 55 million partnership-held shares, reducing shareholders’ equity by $1.2 billion. That reduction was omitted from the earnings release, prompting criticism that Enron’s disclosures were unclear and undermining investor confidence.

Enron shares fell about 21% to $20.65 after the SEC request was disclosed, touching a 52-week low of $19.67 on volume of 36.4 million shares. The decline erased about $4 billion in market value and left the stock down roughly 39% for the week and 75% for the year. Analysts and investors questioned the valuation, accounting and transparency of the partnership transactions. Enron said they were intended to hedge market conditions, but reports noted Fastow’s financial interests and internal complaints about possible conflicts.

Investors also focused on Marlin Water Trust II and Whitewing, two additional off-balance-sheet financing vehicles holding roughly $3.4 billion. If asset sales proved insufficient, Enron could face further write-offs, use cash from on-balance-sheet sales or issue stock that would dilute current shareholders. Repayment triggers included Enron’s share price falling below specified levels and its credit rating dropping below investment grade. Moody’s placed Enron’s debt under review, though observers considered a sub-investment-grade rating unlikely at that time.

Legal claims followed, including a Milberg Weiss class action against Enron, Lay, Skilling and Fastow alleging that Enron misrepresented its financial condition, broadband prospects and the need for write-downs, artificially inflating its stock price. Janus Capital was reported as Enron’s largest institutional holder, while U.S. stock funds collectively held 207.9 million shares and suffered $2.7 billion in losses following the announcement.

Broader markets rallied despite disappointing earnings and anthrax concerns. The Dow rose 1.88%, the Nasdaq gained 2.2%, and the S&P 500 advanced 16.42 points, helped by bargain buying in technology and semiconductor shares; Enron was a major exception.

Three youths were killed and a mosque and four homes destroyed during an Awneera operation; protests and pellet firing injured civilians. Two soldiers were killed and three troops wounded in attacks. Train services were suspended. Resistance leaders opposed changing Jammu and Kashmir’s disputed status or demographics. A Dalgate explosion victim later died in Srinagar.

OAU dismissed Professor Richard Akindele after he was found guilty of soliciting sex from a student. Sexual harassment is described as widespread beyond universities. Higher institutions are urged to address abuse promptly, protect female students, punish lecturers, and call on female students to avoid misconduct and focus on studies.

Tom Evans said his terminally ill 23-month-old son Alfie continued breathing unassisted for nine hours after life support was withdrawn at Alder Hey Children’s Hospital. Evans said doctors re-intervened after a lengthy discussion and provided oxygen and water, although the oxygen was not improving his breathing. He believed Alfie would need some form of life support within hours, while his mother Kate James said she was staying beside him.

A June 4, 2001 news compilation covers Enron, energy markets and government relations.

- Federal disclosure records showed President Bush’s adviser Karl Rove held $100,000–$250,000 each in Enron and several other major companies affected by Bush policy priorities. Rove said he avoided work involving his holdings while awaiting ethics-office approval to divest them. Other senior officials also disclosed Enron or energy-company financial ties.
- Saudi Arabia signed agreements worth at least $25 billion with nine international oil companies, including Enron, to develop three natural-gas fields, power plants, pipelines and desalination facilities. Exxon Mobil led two projects and Royal Dutch/Shell led a third; Saudi Aramco was to hold equity. The agreements represented the first major foreign investment in Saudi Arabia’s energy sector since 1975.
- A San Francisco Chronicle column criticized energy companies for exploiting consumers while arguing that personal energy waste, government failures and corporate misconduct all contributed to the problem. A separate editorial predicted that high prices and investment would expand supply, eventually producing a glut and lower prices despite political resistance to price increases.
- Fitch moved India’s sovereign-rating outlook to negative, citing fiscal policy, privatization and foreign-investment concerns. Analysts disputed the move, pointing to economic growth, strong foreign inflows, ample reserves and improving reforms, while Moody's and Standard & Poor’s maintained their outlooks.
- The Indian rupee recovered from an early low and ended unchanged. Rating concerns and the Enron-Dabhol dispute weighed on bonds and contributed to higher dollar-forward costs.
- Lenders to Enron’s roughly $3 billion Dabhol power project met in Singapore to resolve differences over its future. Indian banks wanted to continue supporting the plant, while offshore lenders sought withdrawal. The dispute followed Maharashtra’s cancellation of its power-purchase contract, with Dabhol alleging $48 million in unpaid bills and Maharashtra citing costly power and a capacity-related penalty.
- Indian Power Minister Suresh Prabhu announced reforms allowing private producers to sell directly to consumers, emphasizing distribution reform, standard utility accounting, debt reduction and lower transmission and distribution losses. He defended India’s commitment to international contracts amid the Dabhol dispute.
- Spectron reported the first brokered post-NETA gas-electricity “spark spread” in Britain, involving Powergen and Enron.
- Nigerian President Olusegun Obasanjo accused Enron of poor performance and bad faith over delays, pricing and contract compliance at the Lagos independent power project. Enron said the project was close to full operation.
- A Business Line commentary argued that the Bush administration’s religious politics, nuclear nonproliferation stance, China policy and possible defense alignment with the United States could create difficult choices for India. It also warned that Enron’s influence over the Bush administration could affect New Delhi’s relations with Washington.
- Enron Japan chief Joseph Hirl said Japanese electricity deregulation was inevitable, but little genuine competition existed and prices were substantially higher than in the United States.

The speakers discuss preparing for a playoff game against a highly motivated home team that may gain energy from its crowd. They plan to maintain their road mindset, start aggressively, and use an available practice and rest day to adjust details. A versatile forward is praised for contributing in ways not reflected in statistics, with his recent scoring welcomed. The team identifies faceoffs, possession, mistake recovery, patience, and slowing the game as keys to execution. Both teams are managing physical wear, with replacements prepared to contribute. They expect a desperate opponent but remain focused on regaining their aggressive style and creating chances. A former player’s intensity, passion, and subtle instruction are viewed as helpful to the team.

The study developed an unbiased metagenomic next-generation sequencing workflow combining HostEL, a magnetic-bead–based host-background depletion method that enriches pathogen DNA and RNA, with AmpRE, a single-tube library-preparation process for both DNA and RNA inputs. The workflow supports shallow sequencing on iSeq 100 and MiniSeq platforms and can detect bacteria, fungi, and DNA and RNA viruses.

Analytical validation using plasma spiked with eight bacterial and two fungal strains detected all species down to 70,000 cells/mL with HostEL treatment. HostEL increased sensitivity from 82% to 96%, while specificity remained approximately 96–97%, and preserved relative pathogen composition. Clinical testing of 42 patient plasma samples found 93% agreement with molecular diagnostic results after excluding low-quality samples, and sequencing-read counts correlated linearly with qPCR Ct values for hepatitis B. Detection confidence was highest at Ct values of 30 or below, with reduced sensitivity at Ct values above 30.

The iSeq 100 workflow had a projected 27-hour turnaround, while the five-hour MiniSeq run could shorten the total workflow to 13 hours, with comparable sensitivity across protocols. The authors concluded that HostEL and AmpRE could reduce the time, cost, and complexity of unbiased sequencing. Limitations included the small clinical cohort, restricted pathogen and specimen diversity, inability to detect parasites because selective lysis would prevent their survival, and the need for larger, more diverse clinical validations.

Cruzin’ for Life’s wheelchair-accessible van provided free rides to Mission Hope Cancer Center for more than 2,600 cancer patients, logging over 34,000 miles across seven communities in its first year. The Santa Maria nonprofit funds the service through events such as its annual king crab feed, which raised $32,000 last year. A $36,000 donation from Santa Maria Energy helped fund the $69,000 van retrofit. Patients request rides directly or are referred by nurses and social workers. If funding and demand continue, the nonprofit may add a second van.

A woman declared dead by paramedics after a South African car crash was found alive hours later in a mortuary refrigerator. Two of the three occupants died, while the woman showed no signs of life when first responders checked her breathing and pulse. The ambulance service said it followed procedure and launched an investigation into the incident.

The Blues begin 2025–26 under Jim Montgomery, their first full season with him as head coach following a midseason playoff run. They open Oct. 9 at Enterprise Center, with seven of their first 11 games at home, before an Oct. 18 rivalry matchup. An Olympic break from Feb. 5–25 offers a midseason checkpoint before a packed March and April. April includes games against Colorado, Winnipeg, Chicago and Minnesota before an April 16 finale in Utah. Montgomery faces questions about defensive consistency, developing young forwards, integrating veteran and young talent, and preparing for 26 division games as the Blues seek playoff contention.

Harvard researchers estimated 4,645 excess deaths in Puerto Rico from Sept. 20 through Dec. 31 after Hurricane Maria—potentially more than 70 times the official toll of 64. Their household survey estimate had a margin of error of ±3,852, though researchers considered about 5,000 deaths likely. San Juan Mayor Carmen Yulin Cruz called the estimate a “day of collective mourning,” criticized the government and President Trump for failing to acknowledge the loss of life, and said Puerto Rico remains unprepared for another major hurricane despite improvements since Maria.

Using Yahoo Finance data from 2007 onward, backtests suggest that NIFTY 50 has a robust positive end-of-month effect comparable to the US turn-of-the-month effect. The tested strategy goes long at the close of the fifth-last trading day and exits at the close of the second trading day of the next month. Investing and compounding 100,000 produced a 10.5% CAGR, outperforming buy and hold despite 30% market exposure, with a 26% maximum drawdown. Results varied somewhat with entry and exit dates, indicating some curve fitting, but remained broadly profitable when entering during the final ten trading days.

Celtic’s 2–1 comeback win at Ibrox left them 19 points ahead of Rangers before the winter break, with a game in hand. The gap is their largest since 1925–26, when Celtic won 58 points and Rangers finished sixth on 44. Celtic could surpass that margin with almost half the season remaining.

The study reviews the educational benefits and potential connections between drama-based pedagogy and STEAM education. It examines how drama can support reflective thinking, creativity, communication, collaboration, problem-solving, confidence, motivation, and student engagement while helping learners understand subject content through imaginative and participatory experiences.

A qualitative pilot study at ELTE University in Budapest involved 19 first-year students, all women, in an art-based methods course. Using participant observation, field notes, and student reflections, researchers examined two activities: groups of three choreographed the life cycle of a butterfly, while groups of four or five devised and presented scenes depicting a day in the life of an Indian caste group. Students reflected on the activities afterward.

Four main observations emerged: students demonstrated creativity through varied artistic interpretations; activities encouraged collaboration and the exchange of ideas; improvisational work promoted experimentation, problem-solving, and “thinking out of the box”; and students showed motivation, enthusiasm, and broad involvement. Overall, participants reported greater interest in and understanding of the topics than with traditional instruction.

The study also identifies implementation challenges, including teacher preparation and classroom management, insufficient time, resources, confidence, and student participation. Because the sample was small, narrowly demographically composed, and limited in experience with STEAM and drama-based pedagogy, the findings are preliminary and require broader validation.

The disclosure describes an autonomous vehicle with a primary autonomous vehicle control subsystem and multiple independently operable auxiliary control units. The primary subsystem uses diverse sensors, processing resources, event-confidence logic, route planning, and trajectory data to control propulsion, steering, braking, lighting, and other vehicle interfaces. It may also provide remote assistance when conditions are insufficiently understood and preplan failsafe trajectories.

The auxiliary units use dedicated or independent sensors, processing, communication buses, and potentially separate power and hardware. They monitor for predefined hazards, collisions, traffic conditions, roadway obstructions, internal malfunctions, and failures of the primary subsystem. When triggered, they generate vehicle response outputs that can instruct the primary subsystem to verify or replace a planned trajectory or communicate directly with vehicle interfaces to override primary commands. Responses may include braking, steering, pulling over, stopping, lane keeping, speed reduction, lane changes, switching off the vehicle, or activating emergency lights. Outputs may be fixed, selected according to sensor inputs, or sustained until the hazard clears or a desired vehicle state is reached. The independent control units provide redundancy when the primary subsystem malfunctions, misinterprets an unfamiliar condition, or responds too slowly.

TrackR announced three Bluetooth tracking devices ahead of CES: the $24.99 pixel, a cheaper and more colorful alternative to the Bravo; the $29.99 wallet 2.0, a credit-card-sized tracker; and the $39.99 atlas, a smart plug that locates connected trackers by room and works with Alexa. The pixel and wallet provide close-range phone tracking, crowd-sourced long-range discovery, and replaceable batteries lasting about a year. Atlas preorders are available, and all three products are expected to launch in spring.

The passage debunks five lightning myths: metal objects do not attract strikes; a metal-roofed car is safer because of its metal body, not rubber tires; lightning can strike up to 10 miles from thunderstorms despite clear skies; tall, isolated objects are often struck repeatedly; and trees are dangerous shelters. Height, pointed shape, and isolation mainly determine where lightning strikes. Most lightning deaths during leisure activities occur on or near water.

In a May 2, 2016 Form 8-K, NVIDIA announced that it and Samsung agreed to settle all pending intellectual property litigation. The cases will be dismissed in U.S. district courts, the U.S. International Trade Commission, and the U.S. Patent Office. Each company will license a small number of patents to the other, with no broad cross-licensing or other compensation.

Thinking Machines Lab, founded by Mira Murati and other former OpenAI researchers, launched Tinker, an API that automates much of the work required to fine-tune frontier AI models. Tinker currently supports Meta’s Llama and Alibaba’s Qwen, allowing users to fine-tune models through supervised learning or reinforcement learning, download them, and run them anywhere. Beta testers praised the tool’s simplicity and balance of abstraction with user control over training data and algorithms.

The company, whose researchers helped create ChatGPT, raised $2 billion in seed funding at a $12 billion valuation. Tinker will initially be available by application, with no API charges expected at first, though paid access is planned later. Thinking Machines vets users and eventually plans automated safeguards against misuse.

Murati said the tool aims to make advanced model tuning more accessible and help counter the trend toward closed commercial AI systems.

Amazon.com, Inc. filed a Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2021. The company is a Delaware corporation headquartered at 410 Terry Avenue North, Seattle, Washington. Its common stock trades on the Nasdaq Global Select Market under the symbol “AMZN.” As of January 26, 2022, 508,844,410 shares were outstanding, and the aggregate market value of voting stock held by non-affiliates was $1.507 trillion as of June 30, 2021. Amazon is identified as a well-known seasoned issuer and large accelerated filer. Part III information is incorporated by reference from Amazon’s definitive proxy statement for its 2022 annual meeting.

Amazon describes its objective as being Earth’s most customer-centric company, guided by customer obsession, invention, operational excellence, and long-term thinking. It operates three segments: North America, International, and Amazon Web Services. Its businesses serve consumers, sellers, developers, enterprises, content creators, advertisers, and employees. Consumer offerings include online and physical stores, third-party products, digital services, media, electronic devices, and Prime subscriptions. Amazon supports third-party sellers, earns fees from seller programs, provides AWS technology services, publishes content, and sells advertising. Principal competitive factors include selection, price, convenience, fulfillment, service quality, speed, and reliability. Sales are generally higher in the fourth quarter. Amazon had approximately 1.608 million full- and part-time employees as of December 31, 2021.

Jeffrey P. Bezos was Executive Chair, Andrew R. Jassy was President and CEO, and Adam N. Selipsky was CEO of AWS at the filing date.

The risk factors identify intense and evolving competition; risks from expansion into products, services, technologies, and international markets; regulatory restrictions in China and India; demand fluctuations and seasonal fulfillment pressures; seller fraud; intellectual-property disputes; foreign-exchange exposure; infrastructure, staffing, data-security, and system-continuity risks; supplier and commercial-agreement dependence; acquisition and investment integration; inventory, payment, and stock-price volatility; government regulation; litigation and investigations; product liability; taxes and collection obligations; and government-contract requirements. These factors could materially harm Amazon’s financial condition, results, liquidity, reputation, growth, or stock price.

Amazon reported total leased and owned properties of 570,560 thousand and 34,866 thousand square feet, respectively, including fulfillment, data center, office, and physical-store facilities. By segment, excluding corporate facilities, leased and owned space totaled 522,058 thousand and 26,926 thousand square feet. Corporate headquarters facilities were owned and leased in the Puget Sound region and Arlington, Virginia.

Management’s discussion states that Amazon’s primary revenue source is sales of products and services. It emphasizes long-term sustainable free-cash-flow growth, customer experience, selection, price, delivery speed, availability, reliability, and efficient management of working capital and capital expenditures. Amazon continues to invest in AWS, technology infrastructure, content, software, and electronic devices. Foreign-exchange movements affect reported sales, expenses, and intercompany balances. Critical accounting judgments include inventory valuation and income taxes. Inventory is generally accounted for using FIFO and valued at the lower of cost or net realizable value; each additional 1% inventory valuation allowance as of December 31, 2021 would have increased cost of sales by approximately $370 million.

Operating cash flow was $46.3 billion in 2021, down from $66.1 billion in 2020, primarily because of working-capital changes. Cash, cash equivalents, and marketable securities totaled $96.0 billion at year-end, compared with $84.4 billion in 2020. Cash capital expenditures were $55.4 billion in 2021 and $35.0 billion in 2020, primarily supporting fulfillment capacity and technology infrastructure, largely for AWS. Cash used for acquisitions and other investments, net of acquired cash, was $2.0 billion in 2021. Financing activities provided $6.3 billion in 2021. At year-end, Amazon had $725 million outstanding under commercial paper programs, $803 million under a secured revolving credit facility, and no borrowings under its unsecured revolving facility. Foreign subsidiaries held $7.6 billion of cash, cash equivalents, and marketable securities. Cash taxes paid were $3.7 billion in 2021, and effective January 1, 2022, U.S. tax rules required research and development expenses to be capitalized and amortized.

The study developed and externally validated two 3D convolutional deep-learning models using pretreatment prostate MRI to identify extra-prostatic extension (EPE) and seminal vesicle invasion (SVI) across the entire prostate and seminal vesicles without requiring lesion delineation. The primary Yale cohort included 820 biopsy-proven patients with localized prostate cancer, divided into 612 training and 208 internal test cases, with additional validation in 65 community-hospital and 41 Prostate-Dx cases.

Ground-truth EPE and SVI independently predicted biochemical recurrence (BCR). Model discrimination was moderate: EPE AUCs were 0.719 on the Yale test set and 0.743 and 0.611 on external sets; SVI AUCs were 0.724, 0.678, and 0.775, respectively. Model-positive patients had lower 5-year BCR-free survival. Combining both biomarkers improved prognostic discrimination: 5-year BCR-free survival was 79.3%, 65.6%, and 60.0% for patients with neither, one, or both biomarkers positive, respectively, and the combined Cox model had a C-index of 0.73. The combined biomarker also distinguished risk within Gleason strata and among patients without pathologic EPE or SVI.

Adding the biomarkers to NCCN groups reclassified 26.4% of patients and improved the C-index from 0.592 to 0.617 and 5-year AUC from 0.613 to 0.656. UCSF-CAPRA C-index improved from 0.592 to 0.614 and 5-year AUC from 0.621 to 0.651. Interpretability analyses supported associations with relevant anatomy and disease status. Limitations included assessing BCR rather than survival or cancer-specific mortality, not comparing against tissue-based classifiers, underrepresentation of African American patients, and limited long-term follow-up.

Microsoft Corporation's Annual Report on Form 10-K covers the fiscal year ended June 30, 2015 (Commission File Number 0-14278, Washington-incorporated, common stock $0.00000625 par value, listed on NASDAQ). The company is a large accelerated filer and not a shell company. As of December 31, 2014, the aggregate market value of common stock held by non-affiliates was $365,312,377,595; 7,997,980,969 shares were outstanding as of July 27, 2015. Portions of the proxy statement for the December 2, 2015 annual meeting are incorporated into Part III. The report includes a note on forward-looking statements.

**Business.** Microsoft's mission is to empower every person and organization on the planet, with a strategy of building best-in-class platforms and productivity services for a "mobile-first, cloud-first" world. Founded in 1975, it operates in more than 100 countries and develops, licenses, and supports software, services, and devices, including cloud services, online advertising, operating systems, business applications, developer tools, video games, and hardware (PCs, tablets, consoles, phones, accessories). Research and development is organized around three ambitions: reinventing productivity and business processes (Office 365, Skype, OneDrive, OneNote, Outlook, Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Bing, Dynamics); building the intelligent cloud platform (Azure plus Windows Server for public, private, and hybrid cloud); and creating more personal computing, with Windows 10 launched in July 2015 as the cornerstone, alongside Cortana, Microsoft Edge, universal applications, first-party devices, and the HoloLens holographic computing platform.

The business operates in six segments: Devices and Consumer (D&C Licensing, Computing and Gaming Hardware, Phone Hardware, D&C Other) and Commercial (Commercial Licensing, Commercial Other). In June 2015 Microsoft announced an organizational structure change, so segments may change. On April 25, 2014, it acquired substantially all of Nokia's Devices and Services Business, reported in Phone Hardware. Competition includes Apple, Google, Samsung, Sony, Nintendo, IBM, Oracle, SAP, Red Hat, VMware, CA Technologies, Adobe, Salesforce.com, Infor, Sage Group, and NetSuite, among others. D&C Other includes resale (Windows Store, Xbox marketplace), search and display advertising (Bing, MSN; a Yahoo! search partnership; June 2015 agreements with AOL and AppNexus to outsource display sales), Office 365 Consumer, Studios, and Mojang (acquired November 2014). Commercial Other comprises Commercial Cloud (Office 365 Commercial, Azure, Dynamics CRM Online) and Enterprise Services.

**Operations and R&D.** Operations centers are in Ireland, Singapore, Fargo, Fort Lauderdale, Puerto Rico, Redmond, and Reno; datacenters are located throughout the Americas, Australia, Europe, and Asia. Phones are manufactured predominantly in Vietnam, while other hardware is produced by third-party contract manufacturers. R&D expense was $12.0 billion (FY2015), $11.4 billion (FY2014), and $10.4 billion (FY2013), about 13% of revenue each year, spread across three engineering groups (Applications and Services; Cloud and Enterprise; Windows and Devices). Microsoft holds over 57,000 issued patents and over 35,000 pending, and operates Microsoft Research.

**Distribution and licensing.** Channels include OEMs (Direct OEMs and system builders), distributors and resellers (e.g., Ingram Micro, Tech Data; CDW, Dell, Insight Enterprises), online services and marketplaces, and Microsoft retail stores. Licensing programs include Open Licensing, the Microsoft Products and Services Agreement, Select Plus (no new Select Plus agreements with commercial organizations beginning July 2015), Enterprise Agreement, the Microsoft Online Subscription Agreement, and partner programs. No single customer accounted for more than 10% of revenue in FY2015, 2014, or 2013.

**Officers and employees.** As of July 30, 2015, executive officers were Satya Nadella (CEO), Christopher Capossela (EVP, Chief Marketing Officer), Kathleen Hogan (EVP, Human Resources), Amy Hood (EVP, CFO), Margaret Johnson (EVP, Business Development), Bradford Smith (EVP, General Counsel and Secretary), and Kevin Turner (COO). As of June 30, 2015, Microsoft employed approximately 118,000 full-time people (60,000 U.S., 58,000 international); a June 2015 restructuring plan will eliminate up to 7,800 positions in fiscal 2016, primarily in Phone Hardware.

**Risk factors.** Key risks include intense competition across platforms, ecosystems, devices, and business models; execution risk and margin pressure in the shift to cloud-based services; potentially insufficient returns on new product and service investments, including Windows 10 free upgrades; challenges with acquisitions and joint ventures; goodwill and intangible asset impairment (a $6.2 billion goodwill charge in Q4 FY2012 and $5.1 billion goodwill plus $2.2 billion intangible charges in Q4 FY2015 in Phone Hardware); difficulty protecting intellectual property and patent royalties; third-party infringement claims; source code disclosure; cyber-attacks, security vulnerabilities, and personal data breaches; outages and infrastructure failures; government competition-law litigation and regulatory scrutiny, including European Commission commitments and royalty pressure in China and other Asian jurisdictions; anti-corruption and trade protection laws; geopolitical instability; talent attraction and retention; lawsuits and claims; tax liabilities; hardware and software quality or supply problems; global operations and foreign exchange exposure; and catastrophic events affecting operations concentrated in the Seattle and Silicon Valley areas.

The device supports several reset mechanisms. A Software Global Warm Reset is initiated by writing to `RST_GLOBAL_WARM_SW` in `PRM_RSTCTRL` and otherwise behaves like an external warm reset, except that `RSTOUT_WD_OUT` remains actively driven according to the latched `BTMODE[11]` value. Local resets affect only their associated module, simultaneous reset requests are processed by priority, and `PRM_RSTST` records the most recent reset. `RSTOUT_WD_OUT` reflects reset status, is asserted during watchdog resets, and is tri-stated while POR or RESET is asserted.

PCI Express supports reset isolation. Software must place the subsystem in an IDLE state before resetting it and re-enumerate the bus afterward. Device-level resets other than Test Reset also reset the subsystem, requiring downstream hot resets and bus re-enumeration. EMAC Switch isolation, enabled through `ISO_CONTROL`, allows most resets except POR to proceed without interrupting switch traffic; it preserves the switch, its reference PLL, selected registers, and some pin multiplexing.

Power domains have dedicated warm and cold resets triggered by specified global resets or by switching between ON and OFF states. Except for Test Reset, most I/O pins enter a high-impedance state during reset, with exceptions including emulation pins, isolated EMAC pins, and `RSTOUT_WD_OUT`. DDR pins are tri-stated and subsequently driven according to their internal pull values. After reset, Boot ROM code configures multiplexing for the selected boot modes.

Device clocks derive from DEV and AUX reference inputs, PLLs, and dividers. DEV and AUX clocks can use internal oscillators with external crystals or 1.8-V LVCMOS inputs. DEV is typically 20 MHz and may range from 20–30 MHz under specified conditions; AUX may also range from 20–30 MHz for precise audio or video clocking. Other inputs include an AC-coupled differential SERDES clock for the PCIe PHY, optional `AUD_CLKIN0/1/2` references up to 50 MHz, and an optional 32.768-kHz `CLKIN32` reference. Two selectable clock outputs, 12 top-level PLLs, and four embedded PLLs provide system and module clocks. PLLs support bypass operation and programmable multipliers and dividers, and `PLL_USB` must operate undivided at 960 MHz when USB is used.

The ARM Cortex-A8 Interrupt Controller handles up to 128 programmable-priority requests and generates IRQs or FIQs, while the C674x controller combines up to 128 events into 12 prioritized interrupts, including events selected through multiplexing registers. AC timing measurements use a 4-V/ns input slew rate, and board-routing delays must be considered; TI recommends IBIS analysis where applicable.

Peripheral features include two DCAN interfaces, an EDMA controller with up to 64 channels and 512 parameter entries, Advanced Event Triggering, Cortex-A8 and system trace, and IEEE 1149.1 JTAG. The JTAG ID register is at `0x4814 0600` with device value `0x0B8F 202F`. The EMAC subsystem is a three-port gigabit switch with two external ports, MII/GMII/RMII/RGMII interfaces, flow control, QoS, and MDIO PHY management. Its CPPI block provides 512 buffer descriptors. GPIO comprises four 32-channel modules configurable as inputs or outputs with interrupt support.

The GPMC provides a glueless interface to NOR and NAND flash, SRAM, Pseudo-SRAM, and custom devices, with asynchronous and synchronous timing; its ELM locates BCH errors using 4-, 8-, or 16-bit schemes. The HDMI transmitter supports HDMI 1.3a video, multichannel L-PCM audio, DDC, and CEC. PCB guidance specifies controlled TMDS impedance, paired vias, I2C pullups, and ESD protection with no more than 5 pF capacitance. The HDVPSS provides video capture and display processing, scaling, deinterlacing, compositing, color conversion, and multiple graphics layers. Video DAC outputs support normal and bypass modes with specified 75-ohm routing practices.

Four I2C modules support Philips specification version 2.1, standard and fast modes from 10–400 Kbps, 7- and 10-bit addressing, multimaster operation, and a 32-byte FIFO. The Imaging Subsystem accepts parallel-camera or CSI-2 input, processes data through the ISP, and provides flash-strobe and shutter controls with extensive image-correction and output-format support. Dedicated DDR2/DDR3 interfaces support 16- or 32-bit data paths, capacities from 64 Mb through 4 Gb, two independent chip selects and PHYs, and data interleaving across the two memory interfaces.

Michael Flynn resigned as national security adviser after reports that he discussed U.S. sanctions on Russia with Russian ambassador Sergey Kislyak before Trump’s inauguration. Acting Attorney General Sally Yates informed White House Counsel Donald McGahn that Flynn was vulnerable to Russian blackmail, while CNN reported that Trump and Vice President Pence learned of the contacts before Flynn’s departure. Trump denied wrongdoing, blamed illegal leaks and Hillary Clinton’s campaign, and dismissed media coverage as conspiracy theories.

Flynn’s resignation intensified scrutiny of Trump’s knowledge of and response to the contacts, prompting calls for investigations into alleged Trump-Russia ties and election interference. The article says Flynn could testify under oath and potentially implicate Trump, although his pre-inauguration communications would not be protected by executive privilege after resignation. A cited source claimed Flynn’s Russian contacts had high-level backing and reflected his loyalty to Trump. It also notes that McGahn may have briefed Trump but could invoke attorney-client privilege over what he disclosed.

The Power Offense is a set offense used by almost every NBA team to free shooters through baseline and down screens. Wings begin by crossing under the basket, then curl off down screens, while the point guard can pass to shooters or feed screeners rolling to the basket. Its middle-first attack challenges simultaneous defensive help, and defensive switches can create post mismatches. Players must understand defensive reads and counters, and coaches must adjust to opponents’ changes.

Counters include curling or basket-curling against chase-and-trail defenses, fading or back-cutting when defenders go over screens, screen-and-roll when defenders switch, and slipping the screen against show-and-recover defense. Offensive entries can counter anticipated defense with a fake cross, misdirection, back cut, direct post entry, or dribble drive.

Offensive rebounding is emphasized as essential to winning. The Power Offense positions two rebounders on the weak side, and players are instructed to assume shots will miss, box out, and pursue rebounds with multiple efforts.

When the initial action does not produce a shot, continuity options include Motion, Side Screen, Drive & Kick, and Triangle Post. Motion flows through screening away and passing; Side Screen creates on-ball screen-and-roll action, especially late in the shot clock; Drive & Kick uses dribble handoffs, penetration, drop passes, and kick-out passes; Triangle Post combines a wing, point guard, and mid-post player in a sideline triangle.

A Single/Double variation lets a shooter choose directions off a double screen or reverse back to another screen, making the shooter harder to defend. Successful implementation depends on coordinated screening, strong post play, timing, communication, and defensive recognition. Teaching uses a whole-part-whole approach, combination drills, scrimmages, and individual skill work.

Game strategy includes scouting opponents, anticipating defensive reads, monitoring adjustments after substitutions and timeouts, varying alignments and entries, attacking weaker defenders, and using Side Screens as the clock winds down. Defenders should also understand how to stop the Power Offense.

The United States informs Congress that Great Britain has declined a proposal to arbitrate the boundary dispute between Venezuela and British Guiana. Britain argued that the Monroe doctrine is inapplicable and not established international law. The United States maintains that the doctrine is sound, applicable to the dispute, and grounded in principles protecting national rights and claims.

Without prejudging the dispute’s merits, the administration proposed arbitration to determine whether Britain sought to expand its territory unjustifiably. Following Britain’s refusal, it asks Congress to fund an executive-appointed commission to investigate the true boundary using available evidence and records.

If the investigation establishes that disputed territory belongs to Venezuela, the United States states that it must resist British appropriation of the land or exercise of jurisdiction over it. The message acknowledges the responsibility involved and the importance of friendly relations between the two English-speaking nations.

On June 3, 2015, Apple Inc. entered an underwriting agreement with Goldman Sachs International and Mitsubishi UFJ Securities International plc to issue ¥250 billion of 0.350% notes due June 10, 2020. The senior unsecured notes rank equally with Apple’s other unsecured and unsubordinated debt, with interest payable semiannually beginning December 10, 2015. They are issued under Apple’s 2013 Form S-3 registration statement and an indenture with The Bank of New York Mellon Trust Company, N.A. The Form 8-K lists the underwriting agreement, officer’s certificate, form of global note, legal opinion, and consent as exhibits.

Amazon.com, Inc.’s Form 10-Q for the quarter ended June 30, 2015 reports unaudited financial statements and identifies North America, International, and AWS as its reportable segments.

Q2 2015 net sales were $23.185 billion, up from $19.340 billion in Q2 2014. Operating income was $464 million versus a $15 million loss, and net income was $92 million versus a $126 million loss. Diluted earnings per share were $0.19, compared with a $0.27 loss. For the six months ended June 30, 2015, net sales were $45.901 billion, operating income was $719 million, and net income was $35 million.

Segment results for Q2 2015 were:

- North America: $13.796 billion in sales and $703 million in operating income.
- International: $7.565 billion in sales and a $19 million operating loss.
- AWS: $1.824 billion in sales and $391 million in operating income.

Year-over-year sales growth was 20% for Q2 and 17% for the first six months. Growth was 26% in North America, 3% internationally, and 81% for AWS in Q2. Foreign-exchange movements reduced consolidated Q2 sales by $1.4 billion. Operating expenses increased, particularly technology and content, fulfillment, marketing, and general and administrative expenses. Stock-based compensation was $563 million for Q2 and $969 million for the first six months.

Q2 operating cash flow was $1.997 billion, compared with $862 million a year earlier. Investing activities used $1.376 billion, and financing activities used $691 million. For the six months, operating cash flow was $498 million, investing activities used $3.223 billion, and financing activities used $1.344 billion. Cash and cash equivalents ended the quarter at $10.269 billion. Trailing-twelve-month free cash flow, a non-GAAP measure, was $4.4 billion versus $1.0 billion a year earlier. Cash, cash equivalents, and marketable securities totaled $14.0 billion at fair value, and Amazon reported that available operating cash sources should meet anticipated needs for at least 12 months.

At June 30, 2015, total assets were $52.440 billion, total current liabilities were $23.912 billion, long-term debt was $8.250 billion, and stockholders’ equity was $11.768 billion. Total contractual commitments were $32.832 billion. Long-term debt obligations had a face value of $9.602 billion, and no amounts were borrowed under the company’s $2.0 billion revolving credit facility.

During the first six months, Amazon acquired companies for $349 million, allocating $218 million to goodwill and $160 million to intangible assets. Goodwill was not impaired, and the annual impairment-testing date was changed from October 1 to April 1.

Amazon disclosed several patent disputes involving Appistry, ContentGuard, Kaavo, and Smartflash. In July 2015, the court invalidated the Appistry patents at issue. ContentGuard’s damages expert estimated potential damages of up to $230 million if Amazon were found liable. The European Commission also opened an investigation into whether Amazon’s contracts with European publishers complied with competition rules.

Tax contingencies totaled $854 million. The IRS sought approximately $1.5 billion in additional federal tax, plus interest, related to 2005 and 2006 transfer-pricing transactions, which Amazon was contesting in U.S. Tax Court. French authorities assessed €196 million for 2006–2010, and Luxembourg and the European Commission were examining the tax treatment of certain Amazon subsidiaries.

Critical accounting estimates included inventory valuation, goodwill impairment, stock-based compensation, and income taxes. A 1% increase in the inventory valuation allowance would have increased Q2 cost of sales by approximately $85 million; a 1% change in the estimated stock-award forfeiture rate would have affected Q2 operating income by approximately $43 million.

Ruston (4-0, No. 2 in Louisiana) visits 5-0 Stephenville (No. 25 in Texas) in a matchup between top-ranked teams. Ruston won last year’s meeting 63-17. After both teams opened with three-and-outs, Ruston quarterback Sam Hartwell was sacked to force a punt. On Ruston’s second drive, Dalen Powell fumbled at the Bearcats’ 19, and one play later Stephenville quarterback Trot Jordan threw a 19-yard touchdown to Jhett Banuelos for a 7-0 lead. Powell has 686 rushing yards and eight touchdowns, while Jordan has 996 passing yards and 13 touchdowns.

Erwin Chemerinsky previewed the Supreme Court’s October 2025 term, noting that more than half the docket is set and additional cases may be added through mid-January. Major disputes include whether President Trump may impose tariffs under the International Emergency Economic Powers Act, remove FTC commissioners, and restrict birthright citizenship. The court will also reconsider Louisiana’s creation of a second majority-Black congressional district and Section 2 of the Voting Rights Act’s disparate-impact liability, raising equal-protection concerns that could affect other civil-rights laws.

Other cases concern Colorado’s ban on conversion therapy, free speech and religious exercise, and laws barring transgender athletes from certain teams. A criminal procedure case asks whether police may enter a home under the emergency-aid exception with a warrant supported by less than probable cause. Chemerinsky also described exceptional summer emergency-docket activity involving the Trump administration, largely involving 6-3 rulings allowing disputed administration actions.

Karmel Davis, a Parkway Elementary parent, was named Tupelo Public School District’s 2017 Parent of the Year for her extensive contributions to the school and community. Corey Crayton received keys to a three-bedroom home built by Northeast Mississippi Habitat for Humanity and funded by HomeStretch Furniture, in exchange for 300 hours of sweat equity. Belden native and Millsaps College junior Noah Barbieri was named a Truman Scholar, receiving $30,000 toward graduate school as he plans to pursue a doctorate in economics.

DHS proposed replacing the duration-of-status policy for international students with a four-year limit on U.S. stays, while allowing USCIS extensions and barring changes of major or transfers between institutions. DHS said the rule aims to reduce F- and J-visa overstays. Opponents—including universities, hospitals, researchers and businesses—argued that DHS overstates overstay rates and that existing monitoring already alerts Immigration and Customs Enforcement to violations.

More than 15,700 comments were submitted by Sept. 29. Commenters warned that many undergraduate and graduate programs exceed four years, while extensions are costly, slow and uncertain. They said the proposal could impede research, increase university expenses, reduce international enrollment, disrupt roughly 17,000 J-1 physicians in hospital training and affect employers. Some architecture programs, Ph.D. research and clinical trials routinely require five to seven years or longer.

Only a small number of comments supported the proposal. One higher-education group favored limiting it to colleges with admission rates below 30 percent.

The speaker called the finals loss tough but said the team was ready to regroup and improve the next night, citing a similar earlier loss to Buffalo. Both goalies played well in a game with one goal in six periods. The team planned to adjust its approach and avoid dwelling on missed opportunities.

This qualitative phenomenological study examined bilingual and monolingual early-childhood teachers’ perspectives on bilingualism and bilingual education in Ankara. Sixteen preschool teachers—eight bilingual teachers from private foreign-language preschools and eight monolingual teachers from state preschools—participated in semistructured interviews analyzed through content analysis.

Five themes emerged: benefits of bilingual education, bilingual children in monolingual schools, bilingual education programs, challenges, and effects on children’s development. Both groups regarded bilingual education as beneficial for children’s self-confidence, communication, cognitive development, cultural awareness, adaptability, and future employment. Most teachers believed bilingual children attending monolingual schools could lose a language or cultural identity, although some monolingual teachers viewed such attendance as beneficial for learning the community’s dominant language.

Teachers had limited knowledge of bilingual program structures but agreed that school staff should be proficient in both languages and that schools should provide bilingual materials and environments. Reported challenges included ineffective use of both languages, insufficient qualified personnel and resources, children’s language deficiencies, family unfamiliarity or cultural conflicts, and poorly balanced or delayed programs. Views differed on bilingual children’s social development, with some emphasizing peer rejection or difficulty speaking the community’s language and others highlighting confidence, multicultural awareness, and adaptability.

All participants supported expanding bilingual education in Türkiye and emphasized parental support. The study recommends specialized teacher training, bilingual competency standards, adequate resources and curricula, parent workshops, and further research in varied contexts. Limitations include the small Ankara-based sample, restricted school settings, reliance on self-reported perspectives, and the study’s cross-sectional design.

A STAT article by Brittany Trang, Ph.D., examines how AI may reshape drug-patent disputes, including whether AI can qualify as an inventor and whether predictive tools alter what a person skilled in the art reasonably knows. It notes that the U.S. patent office began requiring diagrams instead of physical models in 1880 and that biotech patent lawyer DeAnn Smith expects unresolved issues to emerge in litigation. The full article is subscriber-exclusive.

This review examines lung cancer screening, emphasizing that delayed diagnosis and inadequate screening contribute to poor prognosis and high mortality. A PubMed search identified 49 recent U.S. studies evaluating biomarkers and screening methods for primary lung cancer. Among the approaches assessed, circulating tumor DNA had 80% sensitivity and 96% specificity, while Ga-Alfatide II CT/PET scans had 86% sensitivity and 85% specificity. Volatile organic compound testing achieved 80% for both measures. miRNA biomarkers demonstrated sensitivities of 93–96% but low specificities of 23–33%, limiting false-positive control. DNA methylation testing and combined risk scores also showed variable performance, while WT-IDH was considered unsuitable because of false-negative and false-positive results. The authors concluded that circulating tumor DNA and Ga-Alfatide II PET/CT are the most promising methods for patients with suspected or high-risk lung cancer, but neither can independently confirm a diagnosis. Further standardization, broader research, and improved LDCT screening are needed. Prevention measures, including smoking cessation, reducing environmental and occupational exposures, and routine imaging when clinically indicated, may improve early detection and reduce mortality. Chemotherapy and immunotherapy were also identified as promising treatments, although tumor complexity, resistance, and immune tolerance may limit their effectiveness.

The study compared the 2021 National Electronic Health Records Survey (NEHRS), the 2022 American Board of Family Medicine Continuous Certification Questionnaire (CCQ), and the 2022 UCSF Physician Health IT Survey. It examined EHR use, documentation, interoperability, respondent characteristics, and differences associated with survey design. Analyses focused on eligible primary care physicians using EHRs, applied survey weights, and used pairwise Rao–Scott chi-square tests and subgroup comparisons by age, EHR platform, and practice type.

The CCQ had a 100% response rate, with 3,991 eligible respondents. NEHRS had 1,875 eligible completers from 10,302 sampled physicians (18.2%), while UCSF had 3,209 respondents from 90,000 sampled physicians (3.6%). Respondent composition differed substantially: CCQ respondents were younger and more often worked in health systems; NEHRS respondents were disproportionately in private practice; and UCSF respondents more often worked in academic centers, larger practices, and central metropolitan areas. Epic was the most common EHR platform in all three surveys, but satisfaction, after-work documentation, and interoperability responses often differed significantly. For example, very satisfied responses were 29.1% for NEHRS, 26.7% for CCQ, and 19.4% for UCSF. CCQ respondents more often reported spending more than four hours documenting after work, while external-information integration and access were less frequently reported by UCSF respondents than by CCQ or NEHRS respondents.

Despite these differences, all three surveys indicated low EHR satisfaction, substantial documentation burdens, and persistent interoperability problems. Differences generally persisted within demographic, vendor, and practice-type subgroups. The authors concluded that response bias and survey composition likely affect results and that analyses may differ depending on the data source. Limitations included differences in question wording, response options, and practice-size measures, as well as restriction of the CCQ to family medicine. The findings support supplementing NEHRS with recertification data from other specialty certifying boards.

This preprint reports the PrAISED trial, a multicentre, individually randomised (1:1), stratified, pragmatic parallel-group RCT evaluating a 12-month dementia-specific exercise and functional-activity rehabilitation programme (Promoting Activity, Independence and Stability in Early Dementia and mild cognitive impairment) against falls-prevention assessment and advice.

**Design and participants.** 730 participants (365 patients and 365 carers) were randomised from five sites in England (Bath, Derby, Lincoln, Oxford, Nottingham). Eligible patients were over 65, had MCI or dementia with MoCA 13–25, could walk unaided, and had a consenting carer informant. The intervention, delivered by physiotherapists, occupational therapists and rehabilitation support workers, comprised up to 50 home sessions over 12 months covering progressive strength, balance and dual-task exercises, functional activities, community inclusion, risk enablement and environmental assessment, with carer involvement and tapered supervision. The control group received up to three falls-prevention visits. The primary outcome was carer-rated disability in activities of daily living (DAD) at 12 months; secondary outcomes included falls, cognition, quality of life, physical activity, frailty, balance, mobility, grip strength, fear of falling, mood, carer strain and carer quality of life. Recruitment and delivery were disrupted by COVID-19, requiring remote delivery and follow-up and removal of some measures including accelerometer data.

**Results.** There was no difference between groups on the primary ADL outcome (adjusted mean difference −1.3; d −0.06; p=0.5) or on most secondary outcomes, including balance, mobility, physical activity and quality of life. Small differences favouring control occurred on the dual-task Timed Up and Go and self-reported DEMQOL. Underpowered cognitive analyses suggested moderate benefits in multitasking and spatial span. Of 796 falls (375 intervention, 421 control), no significant difference was seen in participants falling, injurious falls, rate of falling (IRR 0.78, 95% CI 0.46–1.3) or time to first fall. 167 adverse events (more in the intervention group, partly from greater ascertainment) and 91 serious adverse events were recorded, none treatment-related; differences in deaths (4 vs 9), care-home placements and hospital admissions were not significant. Fidelity was 70%, participants attended a median of 31 sessions, and the intervention was well received in qualitative interviews.

**Conclusions.** Exercise or functionally orientated rehabilitation is unlikely to alter the rate of loss of ability in dementia. The authors call for different ways of defining wellbeing after diagnosis, emphasising supported or compensatory functioning, personhood, inclusion, occupation, therapeutic relationships and carer support, alongside continued search for disease-modifying drugs. Limitations include an under-diverse sample and pandemic disruption. Trial registration ISRCTN15320670; NIHR funded.

On August 17, ISS Expedition 52 Commander Fyodor Yurchikhin and Flight Engineer Sergey Ryazanskiy will deploy five nanosatellites, collect external residue samples, and install handrails and struts during the station’s 202nd assembly-and-maintenance spacewalk, which NASA will televise live.

Despite its association with SARMs, SR9009 (Stenabolic) is described as an orally administered synthetic Rev-ErbA ligand developed at the Scripps Investigation Institute under Thomas Burris. By activating Rev-Erb, it may affect circadian rhythms, metabolism, fat storage, and macrophages, increasing muscle mitochondria and potentially improving endurance, strength, fat loss, and resting energy expenditure. Mouse studies reportedly showed 50% greater running distance and time. Reported reductions include triglycerides by 12%, total cholesterol by 47%, fatty acids by 23%, glucose by 19%, insulin by 35%, and IL-6 by 72%.

The court granted Garlock’s motion for summary judgment and dismissed Steven C. Gittens Sr.’s pro se ADA disability-discrimination complaint with prejudice under Federal Rules of Civil Procedure 41(b), 16(f), and 56. Gittens failed to oppose the motion despite court deadlines and explicit warnings that his failure to respond could result in dismissal, supporting dismissal for failure to prosecute and failure to obey court orders. Alternatively, treating Garlock’s material facts as admitted, the court found that Gittens’ 25–30-pound lifting restriction prevented him from performing his former punch-press duties but did not substantially limit his ability to work or other major life activities. Because he remained employed in light-duty and other positions, he failed to establish a disability under the ADA or a prima facie discrimination claim. Even assuming a prima facie case, Garlock presented legitimate, nondiscriminatory reasons for his reassignment, and no evidence showed pretext or discriminatory motive.

The passage condemns lynching and mob violence, arguing that criminals should be dealt with swiftly and firmly through lawful, orderly punishment rather than extra-legal retaliation. It warns that inflammatory speeches and writings can stir racial hatred and encourage further brutal crimes.

It also defends universal public education, particularly for Black Americans, as essential to citizenship and social progress. Education alone does not guarantee good conduct, but the passage associates limited schooling with brutal crime. It praises schools such as Hampton and Tuskegee for combining academic and industrial training and credits their graduates with avoiding criminality while improving relations between Black and white communities.

Regarding labor and capital, the passage rejects both class-hatred demagogy and the exploitation of workers in pursuit of profit. It argues that slander, hysteria, and agitation corrupt public life, obstruct genuine reform, and ultimately produce disorder and backlash. The proposed alternative is a resolute but calm course that respects popular rights, public order, and the welfare of all Americans.

The Pocatello-Chubbuck School District will use three focus groups to gather advice on new high school boundaries. Meetings will be public, and agendas and timelines will be posted online. Trustees delayed a decision, originally targeted for Jan. 11, to obtain more feedback.

The bankruptcy court confirmed the debtors’ amended Chapter 13 plan as modified. The 36-month plan proposed monthly payments of $1,733.33, payment of the Chrysler vehicle loan in full, treatment of other secured claims, possible distributions to unsecured creditors, and application of federal tax refunds above a $500 annual reserve.

The Chapter 13 Trustee objected that the plan unfairly favored Chrysler over NBD Bank, lacked good faith, and failed to apply all disposable income to creditor payments. The debtors testified that they purchased the 1997 Dodge Stratus shortly before filing, made no loan payments because of a payroll-deduction problem, and proposed full payment to Chrysler because they had received the car before filing and wanted to retain it. Chrysler and NBD Bank did not oppose the plan.

The court found that the different treatment of the two secured claims was permissible under 11 U.S.C. § 1322 because of the unique circumstances surrounding the Chrysler loan and was not unfair discrimination. It found the debtors’ plan was proposed in good faith, crediting their explanations for not initially reporting the insurance policies’ cash value and for excluding and deferring Mrs. Smith’s profit-sharing benefits.

The court required modifications:

1. Chrysler’s claim would bear interest at the contract rate of 3.9%, not 8%.
2. The debtors must report pay stubs and year-to-date earnings to the Trustee every six months and increase that month’s payment for overtime income exceeding Schedule I projections.
3. Monthly creditor payments increase by $75, from $1,733.33 to $1,808.33, reducing the permitted emergency and maintenance reserve to approximately $100 monthly.
4. Net proceeds from any cash profit-sharing distribution received during the plan must be paid to creditors.
5. Voluntary debtor contributions to retirement or 401(k) plans must cease during the plan; employer contributions are unaffected.

The court held that Mrs. Smith’s ERISA-qualified Profit Sharing Plan benefits remained protected from creditors while deferred, and the court could not require her to withdraw them in cash. If cash benefits were received during the case, however, the net proceeds would be Chapter 13 income subject to the disposable-income requirement.

Blank U.S. passport forms include an oath of allegiance, physical descriptions, supporting affidavits, and a request for safe passage. The passage then reproduces a May 10, 1902 diplomatic report transmitting President Julio A. Roca’s message to Argentina’s Congress. Although hopeful in tone, the message offered little new information and disappointed expectations for detail on international relations and finances. British-mediated negotiations between Argentina and Chile sought to limit costly armaments. Both countries had expanded their military and naval forces, burdening public finances, diverting conversion funds, increasing debt and taxes, and harming commerce and employment. Roca indicated that continued military spending threatened their credit, governments, and people and should be curtailed.

The author questions Snap’s standalone app model because larger platforms can replicate similar features. Snapchat downloads have declined, Facebook’s Instagram has attracted more than 200 million users, and only 7% of marketers reportedly used Snapchat in the first quarter of 2017. Snap’s upcoming lock-up expiration could make 1.2 billion pre-IPO shares available for sale—potentially 84% of shares outstanding—creating dilution and downward price pressure. Fundamentals also disappointed: first-quarter revenue was $150 million versus $158 million expected, the company lost $2.31 per share versus a projected $0.20 loss, and daily active users were 166 million versus 167.3 million expected. With 28% of the float short and put premiums high, the author considers shorting risky and expects volatility. The author plans to remain on the sidelines and makes no trade recommendation.

Safety endpoints were similar across groups at 24 and 48 weeks. Before Week 24, bleeding affected 6.5% and 9.0% of the Primary SOC and Additional Educational Program groups; major bleeding affected 0.7% and 1.1%, with one fatal bleed in the latter group. Between Weeks 24 and 48, bleeding rates in the three groups were 4.1%, 4.0%, and 3.2%, with two fatalities. There were 24 deaths, no pregnancies, and no concerning hepatic or renal laboratory signals. Apixaban adherence and persistence remained high through 48 weeks; education added no benefit.

The Single/Double offense attacks Triangle & Two by using coordinated single and double screens to free shooters from aggressive chasers. Depending on the entry, the opposite wing forms the second screen; shooters can reverse off either screen, pop out, or cross to the single screen, while defensive help creates roll, post, or passing opportunities. Base and side screens extend the action with drop passes, kick-outs, lobs, and rolls. Execution requires communication, timing, coordination, defensive recognition, and practiced screening and post play through drills and scrimmages. Teams should scout opponents, anticipate defensive responses, adjust during games, vary alignments and entries, and attack weaker defenders.

The paper reviews research on inquiry and STEM education, emphasizing their capacity to connect learning with real-life problems and develop scientific practices, critical thinking, collaboration, creativity, communication, and digital literacy. Literature from several countries identifies student interest and learning benefits, but also teacher preparedness, resources, infrastructure, cost, curriculum time, and professional support as barriers to implementation. In Greece, STEM was introduced into compulsory education in 2021–2022 through optional five-to-seven-week “skills workshops,” without additional educational materials or school funding.

The study examined Greek primary teachers’ views of STEM education and the conditions for effective implementation. Data came from 114 volunteer primary teachers in Attica, surveyed from March to May 2022 with 26 Likert-scale and four open-ended questions, plus 27 recorded interviews. Most teachers considered scientific thinking very or extremely important, citing everyday problem-solving, inquiry and critical thinking, social skills, experiential and interdisciplinary learning, and knowledge acquisition. Teachers identified major advantages of STEM as an attractive, hands-on learning approach, a link between school and daily life, scientific methodology, teamwork, creativity, active participation, and critical thinking.

A substantial gap emerged between perceived importance and classroom practice: 58–75% rated individual STEM practices highly important, but only 7–19% reported that students frequently engaged in them. Teachers reported greater confidence in mathematics than science and expressed anxiety about unfamiliar methods, equipment, and materials. Major weaknesses were insufficient training and educational materials (58%), inadequate infrastructure and costly equipment (42%), and insufficient time or an unclear curricular role for STEM (31%). The most requested support was practical subject training (71%), followed by infrastructure and equipment, training materials, ongoing guidance, sample lessons, and additional timetable time. Teachers also valued collaboration, mentoring, and peer communities of practice. The study concludes that STEM can promote inclusion and reduce educational inequalities, but its effective introduction requires adequate preparation, resources, curriculum time, and institutional support.

A report associated South Korea’s falling birthrate with married women’s rising education and labor-force participation. The fertility rate fell from 2.1 in 1984 to 1.6 in 1987 and reached 1.24 in 2015.

- Concomitant medications and current diabetes treatments will be coded with WHODrug Global (March 2018) using ATC level 4 and summarized by level-2 ATC class and preferred name. Listings will include documented and coded drug names, preferred terms, ATC codes, and ATC terms. Medications stopped before first IMP administration are prior; medications ongoing or started at/after first study-drug intake are concomitant. Unclear medication timing will default to concomitant.

- The primary efficacy analysis will use the FAS, with supportive analyses in the PPS. Plasma glucose recovery is the first increase of at least 20 mg/dL from baseline during the hypoglycemic clamp without rescue IV glucose, assessed within 45 minutes. Secondary endpoints are recovery at 10, 15, 20, and 30 minutes and changes from baseline at those times. Baseline is the last non-missing pre-dose value, including unscheduled visits when applicable. The primary analysis adjusts for age group and injection site; only observed data will be analyzed, without imputation. No interim analyses are planned.

- Confirmatory testing will compare dasiglucagon 0.6 mg with placebo in the FAS using a two-sided 0.05 hierarchical procedure: time to recovery first, followed by the four recovery-time endpoints and four glucose-change endpoints. GlucaGen comparisons are supportive and outside the hierarchy. Although approximately five centers participate, center will not be included in the primary model.

- Time to recovery will be summarized with Kaplan–Meier methods at specified sampling times through 60 minutes. Patients receiving rescue IV glucose or not recovering by 45 minutes will be censored and classified as not recovered. A log-rank test stratified by age group and injection site will compare dasiglucagon with placebo; GlucaGen comparisons will use the same method but remain non-confirmatory. Sensitivity analyses will address rescue-glucose censoring, and supportive analyses include a stratified Wilcoxon test, recovery histograms, linear interpolation of recovery times, and descriptive discrete-time Cox proportional hazards models if proportional-hazards conditions and censoring limits are met. Homogeneity models will examine sex, BMI class, ethnicity, race, and US/non-US status.

- Recovery rates at 10, 15, 20, and 30 minutes will be compared using a Cochran–Mantel–Haenszel test stratified by age group and injection site, with an unstratified Fisher test as fallback for small or zero cell counts. Glucose changes from baseline will be analyzed by ANOVA with treatment, age group, and injection site. Least-square means, 95% confidence intervals, and treatment differences will be presented.

- Plasma dasiglucagon and GlucaGen will be sampled at prespecified times through 300 minutes, with pharmacokinetic metrics calculated by noncompartmental analysis in WinNonlin 6.4. Plasma glucose will be sampled through 45 or 60 minutes depending on body weight, and AUE0–30min will be calculated in SAS. Summary tables and concentration-time figures will be produced with specified nominal/actual-time and below-quantification handling.

- Safety analyses will use the safety set and cover insulin use, hypoglycemia induction, trial and rescue-medication administration, local tolerability, adverse events, laboratory tests, vital signs, ECG, pregnancy and alcohol tests, and immunogenicity. TEAEs will be coded with MedDRA version 21.0 or higher and summarized by treatment, system organ class, preferred term, causality, severity, seriousness, special-interest categories, and injection-site reactions. Missing causality will be treated as related, while missing severity will remain missing. ADA occurrence will be assessed descriptively for treatment-induced or treatment-boosted positivity.

- Compared with the protocol, the SAP reworded the primary efficacy analysis, added supportive and sensitivity analyses, and changed secondary-endpoint wording from “within” to “at” specified minutes. Appendices define table, figure, and listing conventions, derived-variable calculations, conservative handling of incomplete dates, SAS quality-control requirements, and planned safety, PK/PD, disposition, demographic, and listing outputs.

During construction of Amsterdam’s North/South rapid transit line, archaeologists excavated 700,000 discarded objects from beneath the Amstel riverbed. Ranging from Neolithic stone axes to cellphones and documents, the varied, often well-preserved finds provide a rare account of centuries of city life. The “Below the Surface” project presents the collection through a 10,000-object display at Rokin station, an interactive website featuring about 30,000 objects, and a 13,000-photo school catalog titled “Stuff.” The new eight-station line was scheduled to open July 22, and the archaeological project cost €6 million.
