The lecture continues a proof of Freiman’s theorem using tools from additive combinatorics, Fourier analysis, and geometry of numbers. Ruzsa’s modeling lemma embeds a constant proportion of a small-doubling set into a small cyclic group while preserving additive relations among sums of up to eight elements. The goal is then to extract additional structure from this modeled set.

For a density-\(\alpha\) subset \(A\subseteq \mathbb F_2^m\), the set \(A+A\) need not contain a subspace of bounded codimension. A counterexample is a Hamming ball: it has constant density, but its sumset contains no bounded-codimension subspace. The relevant principle is that repeated addition, like convolution, smooths a set. Bogolyubov’s lemma formalizes this: \(2A-2A=4A\) contains a subspace of codimension less than \(\alpha^{-2}\).

The finite-field proof uses the convolution of \(1_A\) with itself, Fourier inversion, and Parseval’s identity. Large Fourier coefficients form a set \(R\) of size less than \(\alpha^{-2}\), and Fourier inversion shows that the convolution is positive on \(R^\perp\). Hence \(R^\perp\subseteq 2A-2A\).

In a cyclic group \(\mathbb Z/n\mathbb Z\), where subspaces are unavailable, the analogous objects are Bohr sets. A Bohr set \(B(R,\varepsilon)\) consists of residues \(x\) for which \(\|rx/n\|_{\mathbb R/\mathbb Z}\leq\varepsilon\) for every \(r\in R\). The cyclic version of Bogolyubov’s lemma states that if \(A\) has density \(\alpha\), then \(2A-2A\) contains a width-\(1/4\) Bohr set with \(|R|<\alpha^{-2}\). The same Fourier proof applies, with nonnegative cosine contributions on the Bohr set.

The lecture then introduces the geometry of numbers needed to turn a Bohr set into a generalized arithmetic progression (GAP). A lattice in \(\mathbb R^d\) is the integer span of \(d\) linearly independent vectors; its determinant is the absolute determinant of a basis matrix and equals the volume of a fundamental parallelepiped. For a centrally symmetric convex body \(K\), its successive minima \(\lambda_i\) record the successive scaling factors at which \(\lambda K\) meets lattice points in new independent directions. Minkowski’s second theorem gives
\[
(\lambda_1\cdots\lambda_d)\operatorname{vol}(K)\leq 2^d\det(\Lambda).
\]

Using a lattice lifted from the defining frequencies of a Bohr set, Minkowski’s second theorem shows that every width-\(\varepsilon\) Bohr set of dimension \(d\) contains a proper GAP of dimension at most \(d\) and size at least \((\varepsilon/d^d)|G|\). Properness follows by showing that two distinct GAP parameter vectors cannot represent the same residue: their difference would give a nonzero integer vector with \(\ell_\infty\)-norm below \(1\), which is impossible.

Thus \(2A-2A\) contains a large proper GAP. The next stage, using the covering lemma, is to extend this structure from a constant proportion of \(A\) to all of \(A\), completing the proof of Freiman’s theorem. The lecture concludes by announcing a discussion of the polynomial Freiman–Ruzsa conjecture.

The study examines how COVID-19 accelerated digitalization of Japanese higher education, focusing on MEXT policy, academic staff, students, and lifelong learning. Before the pandemic, Japanese universities lagged in ICT use because of educational conventions, limited adult enrollment, and restrictions on distance-learning credits. Emergency restrictions then rapidly shifted teaching to fully online, hybrid, and high-flex formats.

MEXT initially allowed more than 60 remotely earned credits and later promoted face-to-face instruction, while retaining emergency exceptions and limiting the proportion of remotely conducted courses. The October 2022 revision of university establishment standards retained the general credit limit but allowed exceptions for universities with strong quality-assurance systems. Government projects and plans have also promoted online collaboration, digital teaching, educational-data sharing, and use of “My Number,” although these initiatives have raised concerns about privacy and public trust.

Faculty ICT use increased substantially during the pandemic, but instructors faced challenges involving communication, practical and laboratory work, student support, assessment, group-work management, and computer literacy. Online examples of teaching practices and faculty reflections were identified as useful resources. The pandemic also prompted experimentation with new teaching and evaluation methods, although lasting cultural changes in faculty attitudes remain uncertain.

Digital tools increased students’ recorded out-of-class study time, but online learning also created heavy assignment burdens. These findings relate to concerns about the “substantiation of the credit system”: students generally study far fewer hours outside class than the 30 hours per credit required, due to high course loads, employment and job-search activities, graduation research, and educational practices that emphasize classroom teaching, independent reading, extracurricular activities, and theses.

In lifelong learning, traditional Kokaikoza programs remain largely nondigital, whereas newer short-term vocational and certificate programs have adopted online delivery more extensively. University distance education for degree programs has a long history but remains relatively separate from commuter programs. Overall, the passage concludes that digitalization offers opportunities for learning quality and adult participation, but requires structural and cultural reforms, careful use of student data, and safeguards for personal information.

A £95,220 ScottishPower Foundation donation to Sussex Wildlife Trust will fund 1,300 additional participants in Woods Mill’s 50th-year events, ten wildlife-identification courses, training for 250 wildlife champions, and a young naturalists’ club. Funding also supports reed-bed restoration, improved path access and a kestrel nesting-box camera. The donation is part of more than £1 million provided to UK charities this year.

The NVIDIA A100 Tensor Core GPU introduces major compute, memory, networking, reliability, and programmability improvements over V100. Its third-generation Tensor Cores share data across 32 threads rather than eight, reducing register-file bandwidth and storage. Matrix multiplication issues up to eight times fewer instructions and performs 2.9 times fewer register-file accesses; for 16×16×16 multiplication, register accesses fall from 80 to 28 and hardware instructions from 16 to 2.

A100 adds asynchronous global-to-shared-memory copies that bypass the L1 cache and register file, hardware-accelerated asynchronous barriers, and 164 KB of shared memory per SM. Its five-site HBM2 subsystem provides 1,555 GB/s bandwidth, while a 40 MB L2 cache offers 2.3 times V100’s L2 read bandwidth and improved residency controls. Compute Data Compression can save up to four times DRAM and L2 bandwidth.

Multi-Instance GPU (MIG) can divide an A100 into as many as seven isolated GPU Instances with dedicated compute, cache, memory bandwidth, quality-of-service, and fault isolation. GPU Instances can be subdivided into Compute Instances, which support simultaneous contexts and Volta-style MPS. MIG supports vGPU migration, multi-tenant deployments, Linux hypervisors, containers, and Kubernetes orchestration, while retaining the existing CUDA programming model.

Third-generation NVLink provides 12 links, 600 GB/s aggregate bandwidth versus 300 GB/s on V100, faster peer-memory access, and improved error detection and recovery. A100 also supports PCIe Gen 4 with 31.5 GB/s per direction and SR-IOV. New fault-handling capabilities improve error attribution, isolation, and containment, including for NVLink-connected and MIG environments.

Additional hardware includes a five-core NVJPG JPEG decoder, an optical-flow accelerator supporting optical flow and stereo disparity, and five NVDEC units. A100 also improves global-memory atomic throughput by 11 times for FP16 and 2.7 times for FP32 over V100.

CUDA 11 supports the new Tensor Cores, sparsity, CUDA Graphs, MIG, L2 residency controls, asynchronous copies, and barriers. A100 optimizes graph launches and dependency tracking, while Cooperative Groups adds asynchronous pipelines and hardware-accelerated reductions.

DGX A100 combines eight A100 GPUs with NVSwitch, delivering up to 5 PFLOPS in a 6U system and up to 56 isolated MIG accelerators. Its software stack includes CUDA 11, NVIDIA Container Toolkit, and optimized containers for deep learning, analytics, and HPC workloads.

The passage also introduces neural-network sparsity, explaining that pruning can reduce computation, memory use, and latency. A100 supports fine-grained structured sparsity that maintains balanced workloads and, according to cited evaluations, produces virtually no loss in accuracy with 2:4 sparsity.

Social exclusion is common among people with severe mental illness and is associated with poverty, unemployment, poor health, stigma, loneliness, and limited social networks. Mental health supported accommodation in England includes residential care, supported housing, and floating outreach. Residents often have unmet needs concerning employment, relationships, and community participation, highlighting the importance of recovery-based, individually tailored support.

The SUSHI study developed an online version of the validated Social Inclusion Questionnaire User Experience (SInQUE) for supported accommodation services. The tool is completed collaboratively by staff and service users, covers 46 items across nine practical areas, produces a 0–75 inclusion score, identifies up to three support priorities, and generates reports showing change over time. It does not store personally identifiable service-user data.

The study had two stages in one inner London borough. Six staff members took part in lab-based “think-aloud” testing, while 12 staff and 12 service users were interviewed after a five-month field implementation. The revised tool was also offered to services in another London borough and a rural county without an implementation strategy. Interviews were analysed thematically using an intervention-context-actor-mechanism-outcome framework, and an implementation logic model was developed.

Staff and service users generally considered the online SInQUE user-friendly, relevant, quick to complete, culturally appropriate, and useful for collaborative discussions. They believed it could improve understanding between staff and service users, support targeted care planning, increase service-user confidence and proactivity, identify social-inclusion priorities, and track progress through repeat assessments. Staff raised concerns about selecting suitable participants, maintaining professional boundaries, and potentially intrusive questions, although service users generally found the questions appropriate and felt comfortable answering them.

Only minor refinements were made, including clearer wording, additional guidance, improved score displays, and materials for managers, commissioners, staff, and service users. Of 27 staff who registered, 17 completed 30 assessments with 28 service users—slightly over 10% of the borough’s supported-accommodation population. Uptake was highest in supported housing, while findings for residential care and floating outreach were less conclusive. No assessment was completed in the two areas without implementation support, suggesting that leadership endorsement and active implementation support were important.

The findings indicate that the online SInQUE may be an acceptable and potentially useful assessment and care-planning tool, particularly in supported housing. Limitations included testing in one borough, low uptake, a short study period, selection bias, no female service-user participants in interviews, and inability to determine whether use improved outcomes or the value of repeat assessments. Further research is needed on longer-term effectiveness, broader uptake, non-users’ reasons for declining the tool, and its usefulness across other accommodation types and populations.

Steven Kean forwarded Jeffrey McMahon a July 13, 2001 compilation of press clippings under “Enron Mentions,” saying the coverage showed him shaking up Enron in typical fashion.

The clippings reported that:

- Wisconsin Gas agreed to buy Northern Natural Gas’s nine-mile Eagle pipeline in Wisconsin for $5 million, subject to regulatory approval. The sale would connect the line to Wisconsin Gas’s distribution system and Guardian Pipeline and eliminate Guardian’s planned 8.5-mile lateral.
- LME three-month copper fell $6 to $1,554.50 per ton after a 7,475-ton stock build raised inventories to a 12-month high of 550,300 tons. Unconfirmed market reports linked Enron to much of the stock inflow, ostensibly to ease nearby supply tightness and short positions; Enron declined to comment.
- The FTSE 100 gained 1% to 5,537.0, led by telecommunications and drug stocks. Paladin Resources rose 10% after Enron sold its entire 40-million-share stake for 44 pence per share.
- NYMEX began trading low-sulfur coal futures; the September contract settled at $40.75 per ton after 98 trades. Enron and Duke Energy said they would participate, while traders noted the market’s limited liquidity.
- Enron entered steel trading by offering long-dated forward contracts and financial hedging products, buying at floating prices and selling at fixed rates, while planning regional marketplaces and mill holdings. Steel mills and distributors responded unevenly, citing potential gains in price visibility and margins alongside concerns about low prices, delivery reliability, conflicts of interest, and surrendering inventory control.

In a farewell address to Cabinet members and White House staff, the President asked them to serve the next President with the same devotion. He called the White House the best house not because of its size or artwork, but because of the people serving in it. He acknowledged administrative mistakes, accepted responsibility, and praised staff members for never profiting at public expense. He emphasized that public service is a cause greater than personal wealth and that many careers, including farming, business, trades, and government, are valuable. Stories of his parents illustrated dignity, sacrifice, and perseverance. Citing Theodore Roosevelt’s account of bereavement, he said setbacks and loss do not end life and that greatness is revealed through adversity. He urged those present to continue serving if they wished, give their best, avoid discouragement and hatred, and remain humble. He closed with pride, gratitude, and the hope that those leaving would remain in his heart and prayers.

Dalhousie researcher Nancy McLean says native bees comprise over half of bees on P.E.I. blueberry flowers and may handle most pollination. Adapted to Maritime weather and able to buzz pollinate, they may eliminate the need for imported honey bees, though convincing farmers remains difficult.

Michael Dell said demand for AI computing power remains strong, with customers immediately deploying infrastructure and power availability—not a lack of genuine need—posing a major constraint. Dell Technologies’ stock rose 32% over the past year, its server-networking business grew 58%, and it forecasts 7%–9% annual revenue growth and EPS growth of at least 15% over the next four years. Despite warnings about stretched valuations and potential AI market froth, Dell sees no sign that data-center construction has peaked, though he expects there will eventually be too many data centers.

The document standardizes the SEV-ES/SEV-SNP Guest-Hypervisor Communication Block (GHCB) so guest operating systems can interoperate with hypervisors supporting either technology. It defines required non-automatic exit (NAE) events, the minimum state exchanged during VMGEXIT, and guest-specific handling for features such as NMI processing and SMP booting.

The GHCB is a 4,096-byte, page-aligned area mapped as decrypted or shared by the guest. Its layout mirrors the SEV-ES VMCB save-state area through offset 0x3ff, although only fields required for VMGEXIT processing are exposed. Version 2 adds initial SEV-SNP support and a 52-bit feature bitmap through which hypervisors advertise supported capabilities. Later revisions add 64-bit guest-request sequence numbers, VLEK support and expanded error reporting, APIC ID discovery, multiple VMPL levels, page-state-change notifications, the SEV-SNP Confidential Computing Blob EFI protocol, SEV-TIO, Secure AVIC, and clarified hardware-debug behavior.

A guest establishes its GHCB by writing the block’s guest physical address to MSR 0xc001_0130; hypervisors must not intercept this MSR. Hardware saves and restores the address through VMCB offset 0xa0. The lower 12 bits of the GHCB MSR identify protocol requests, including SEV information, CPUID values, feature support, AP reset hold, page-state changes, VMPL execution, termination, and preferred, registered, or unregistered GHCB addresses. SEV-SNP guests must register a GHCB GPA before first using it for VMGEXIT, with the page made hypervisor-owned and shared.

During protocol negotiation, the hypervisor supplies supported GHCB version bounds and the SEV page-table encryption bit. The guest obtains required SEV data through CPUID or the GHCB MSR protocol, establishes page tables and long mode, allocates and shares the GHCB page, registers it when required, and supplies its GPA. During a VMGEXIT, the guest populates designated GHCB fields and the valid bitmap before invoking the instruction. The hypervisor obtains the GPA from the VMCB, handles the exit, updates the save area, and resumes the guest. Standard NAE processing uses SW_EXITCODE, SW_EXITINFO1, and SW_EXITINFO2, with errors returned through the exit-info fields.

Specified NAEs cover I/O protection, MSR protection, VMMCALL, MMIO access, page-state changes, SNP guest and extended guest requests, AP creation, #HV doorbell management, #HV IPIs and timers, APIC ID lists, VMPL changes, SEV-TIO requests, Secure AVIC backing-page management, termination, and unsupported events. Page-state requests can make pages private or shared and include SNP smash and unsmash hints. SNP guest requests use separate shared request and response pages and sequence numbers to prevent message-sequence and AES-GCM IV reuse. Extended requests can return VCEK or VLEK certificates. AP creation can create, update, or remove vCPU state at a specified VMPL and enables vCPU hotplug.

With SNP Restricted Injection, the guest registers a shared #HV doorbell page for each vCPU. The page contains a PendingEvent field and an EOI-assist field and is used to present interrupt vectors, NMI, and machine-check events while emulating APIC acknowledgment, in-service, and end-of-interrupt behavior. Guests must atomically claim pending vectors before acting on them. The specification also defines #HV IPI delivery and virtual APIC timer operations.

SEV-ES and SEV-SNP application-processor booting must accommodate register state that was measured and encrypted before launch. The document describes reset-vector and predetermined-location methods, AP reset-hold processing, and an encrypted, aligned AP jump table used when transferring control between environments. Restricted Injection requires the SNP AP Creation mechanism. For NMIs, hypervisors must not intercept IRET but must intercept #DB, and the guest sends an “NMI Complete” message when another NMI can safely be accepted. Hardware debug-register virtualization is supported when indicated by SEV_FEATURES; otherwise, DR7 accesses are intercepted and emulated. SMM and nested virtualization are not supported.

Siddharth Agrawal has run Jaipur-based family textile exporter Silkasia for 18 years. He researches native cow breeds, invests in agriculture and startups, mentors ventures, and develops the women’s clothing brand Mayori with his entrepreneurial wife, Vrinda.

Russian President Vladimir Putin was declared the winner of the presidential election, securing a fourth six-year term with more than three-quarters of the vote. Critics called the election staged, while the opposition reported harassment of monitors, pressure on government employees to vote, and ballot stuffing. Putin and state media portrayed Russia as surrounded by Western hostility amid sanctions, the Crimea annexation, and the poisoning of a former Russian spy in Britain. A patriotic rally coincided with Crimea’s annexation anniversary, but there was little public celebration. The opposition remained divided, with Alexei Navalny refusing to unite with candidate Ksenia Sobchak, who received less than 2 percent. Although Putin could potentially run beyond six years, he said he had no plans to change the constitution.

A compilation of Nov. 16–18, 2001 press reports centered on Enron’s financial crisis and proposed acquisition by Dynegy. Enron’s shares fell to $9, about 89% lower for the year, after the company disclosed a four-year, $586 million overstatement of profits and a $1.2 billion reduction in shareholder equity tied to affiliated partnerships. An SEC investigation, a Moody’s downgrade to the lowest investment grade, and expected layoffs accompanied the crisis. Investors awaited a balance-sheet filing to determine Enron’s liabilities and whether Dynegy could withdraw if obligations exceeded $3.5 billion. The proposed transaction was valued at roughly $24–$24.7 billion including debt, while some coverage put the Enron stock consideration at about $9 billion. Kenneth Lay declined a severance package worth more than $60 million. Enron closed a $550 million loan secured by Transwestern Pipeline assets, with another $450 million loan pending, and ChevronTexaco provided Dynegy with a $1.5 billion cash infusion.

Commentators attributed Enron’s troubles to hidden partnership debt, executive stock-option incentives, greed, hubris, and political connections. Articles highlighted substantial insider stock sales while employees’ retirement savings suffered, and some pension funds considered legal action.

Economic data lifted stocks during the period: the Nasdaq gained 3.8%, the Dow 2.7%, and the S&P 500 1.6%, while the 10-year Treasury yield rose from 4.31% to 4.85%. Energy analysts remained bullish on many energy stocks despite volatile oil and natural-gas prices.

Wessex Water was expected to be sold after Enron bought it for £1.4 billion in 1998; WestLB reportedly made a formal offer of about £1 billion, while RWE and British utilities were also mentioned. Other reports covered Quanta Services’ takeover defenses against UtiliCorp, Burlington Resources’ extended Canadian Hunter offer, the Azurix shareholder settlement, SBC’s long-distance expansion, American Airlines’ canceled pilot layoffs, and Southwest’s withdrawn Orbitz lawsuit. A feature compared Calgary and Houston for U.S. oil executives. Investment commentary emphasized diversification, asset allocation, regular saving, and greater skepticism after the market decline, while warning about bubble-era irrationality and excessive executive incentives.

The Dark Cloud Cover is a two-candle bearish reversal pattern that forms after an upswing. The first candle is a long bullish candle; the second opens above the prior candle’s close and closes below its midpoint, indicating that bearish momentum may be overriding bullish momentum. The pattern can signal short selling or closing long positions, particularly during a rally within a downtrend.

Traders should confirm the potential reversal through subsequent price action, resistance levels, moving averages, MACD, or RSI. It is not a guaranteed reversal and should be considered alongside other technical analysis, market news, and fundamental analysis. Proper risk management, including stop-loss placement, is essential.

The strategy is best suited to bearish markets but can be applied to stocks, Forex, commodities, and cryptocurrencies. Timeframe selection depends on the trader’s goals and risk tolerance: shorter charts offer more signals but greater false-signal risk, while longer charts produce fewer signals and may miss opportunities.

Backtesting can help assess performance across different markets, timeframes, and rule parameters, but it does not guarantee future results. Example AAPL trades described in the passage show profits from selling after the pattern appeared. Overall, the strategy may help traders profit from declines, define entries and stop-loss levels, and maintain discipline.

Apple Inc.’s Form 10-Q covers the fiscal first quarter of 2017, a 14-week period ended December 31, 2016. Net sales increased 3% to $78.35 billion, driven by iPhone and Services growth, partly offset by lower iPad sales. Gross margin declined to 38.5% from 40.1%, while operating income fell to $23.36 billion from $24.17 billion. Net income was $17.89 billion versus $18.36 billion, while diluted earnings per share increased to $3.36 from $3.28. Research and development and selling, general and administrative expenses increased, while other income rose to $821 million from $402 million.

Product sales were $54.38 billion for iPhone, up 5%; $5.53 billion for iPad, down 22%; $7.24 billion for Mac, up 7%; $7.17 billion for Services, up 18%; and $4.02 billion for other products, down 8%. Geographic net sales rose 9% in the Americas, 3% in Europe, 20% in Japan and 8% in the Rest of Asia Pacific, while Greater China sales fell 12%. Apple introduced a MacBook Pro with Touch Bar and released AirPods during the quarter.

At December 31, 2016, Apple held $246.09 billion in cash, cash equivalents and marketable securities and reported total assets of $331.14 billion, total liabilities of $198.75 billion and shareholders’ equity of $132.39 billion. It had $10.49 billion of commercial paper outstanding and $77.4 billion of term debt principal. The company generated $27.06 billion from operating activities, used $19.12 billion in investing activities and $12.05 billion in financing activities. Working capital was $19.20 billion. Apple stated that existing liquid resources were sufficient for its requirements over the following 12 months and anticipated approximately $16 billion of capital expenditures during fiscal 2017.

The board increased the share-repurchase authorization to $175 billion, of which $144 billion had been used by quarter-end. During the quarter, Apple spent $10.85 billion on share repurchases and $3.13 billion on dividends and dividend equivalents, with the quarterly dividend at $0.57 per share. It planned to complete the capital-return program by March 2018.

Apple reported $8.5 billion of gross unrecognized tax benefits, including $3.0 billion that could affect its effective tax rate. It was appealing the European Commission’s State Aid Decision, under which Ireland may seek taxes of up to €13 billion plus interest; Apple anticipated placing the calculated amount and interest in escrow pending appeals and believed any incremental Irish taxes would be creditable against U.S. taxes. The filing also described concentrated component and Asian manufacturing supply risks, ongoing derivative and investment activity, and future adoption of accounting standards governing stock compensation, revenue recognition, taxes, leases, restricted cash and credit losses.

Tesla Motors’ unaudited Form 10-Q for the quarter ended September 30, 2015 reported third-quarter revenue of $936.8 million, up from $851.8 million, comprising $852.6 million in automotive revenue and $84.2 million in services and other revenue. Gross profit declined to $231.5 million from $251.9 million, while gross margin fell to 24.7% from 29.6%. Operating loss increased to $183.7 million from $39.1 million, and net loss increased to $229.9 million from $74.7 million; diluted loss per share was $1.78 versus $0.60. For the nine months ended September 30, revenue was $2.83 billion versus $2.24 billion, gross profit was $704.9 million versus $620.0 million, and net loss was $568.3 million versus $186.4 million.

At September 30, 2015, Tesla reported $1.43 billion of cash and cash equivalents, $1.29 billion of inventory, $3.10 billion of property, plant and equipment, $7.55 billion of total assets, $6.19 billion of total liabilities, and $1.31 billion of stockholders’ equity. Nine-month operating cash flow was negative $494.7 million, investing cash flow was negative $1.26 billion, and financing cash flow was positive $1.30 billion. Financing cash flow included $738.3 million from an August common-stock offering and $360.0 million from vehicle sales to bank leasing partners. Tesla expected 2015 capital expenditures of approximately $1.7 billion.

Revenue growth was primarily attributed to increased Model S deliveries, while services revenue rose with pre-owned vehicle sales, maintenance services, and powertrain sales. Lower margins resulted from product and regional mix, manufacturing costs, obsolete inventory, and reduced regulatory-credit revenue, partly offset by lease-related revenue and material cost savings. Third-quarter research and development expense was $178.8 million, and selling, general and administrative expense was $236.4 million, both reflecting increased staffing, development, facilities, and infrastructure spending.

Tesla began customer deliveries of the Model X in September 2015 and was ramping its production, while continuing Model S production. Nearly 90,000 vehicles had been delivered through September 30. Tesla projected fourth-quarter production of 15,000–17,000 vehicles and deliveries of 17,000–19,000, bringing anticipated 2015 deliveries to about 50,000–52,000. It planned to unveil the Model 3 in the first quarter of 2016 and begin deliveries in late 2017.

Tesla also began production and deliveries of 7 kWh and 10 kWh Powerwall residential products and a 100 kWh Powerpack commercial product, then transitioned their production to the Gigafactory during the fourth quarter. Cell production was anticipated by the end of 2016. Management identified Gigafactory costs, partner recruitment, and potential delays as risks.

The filing described revenue-recognition policies for vehicle features, resale-value guarantees, leasing, warranties, inventory valuation, and stock compensation. It classified the 2018 convertible notes as current because conversion conditions were met, while the 2019 and 2021 notes remained long-term debt. Tesla reported $1.4 billion in cash liquidity and an undrawn $750 million asset-based credit facility. A securities class action dismissed with prejudice remained under appeal. As of October 29, 2015, 130,951,319 common shares were outstanding.

The paper analyzes approximately 1,000 days of Swift UV and X-ray monitoring of Fairall 9, a nearby Seyfert 1 AGN with little absorption. Segmented spectral energy distributions were fitted with a model containing a warm Comptonizing disc, hot corona, and reflected emission, while Gaussian-process regression and Fourier analysis were used to measure power spectra, coherence, and frequency-dependent UV–X-ray lags. An analytic model combining intrinsic disc and coronal variability with seed-photon transfer, X-ray reprocessing, and wind/BLR emission was also applied.

The optical/UV emission increased substantially after a sharp rise in the campaign, while total X-ray power remained approximately constant. The fits indicate a roughly 40–50% increase in mass-accretion rate, a softer hot-coronal spectrum from increased seed-photon cooling, greater mid-plane dissipation, and a model-dependent inward movement of the hot corona. These changes are difficult to reconcile with either pure reverberation or simple disc-to-corona propagation.

The UV power spectrum declines rapidly at high frequencies, whereas the X-ray spectrum is comparatively flat, suggesting separate intrinsic variability mechanisms. At low frequencies, segments 1a and 2 show a semi-coherent X-ray lead of roughly 6–12 days that disappears in segment 3. Including the sharp rise produces a highly coherent UV lead of about 5.5 days. An analytic model shows that interference between intrinsic disc and coronal variability, combined with the stochastic nature of periodogram estimates, can reconcile segments 2 and 3 with the same underlying model. The rise-related segment likely reflects a systematic change in the accretion flow, possibly an outside-in increase in mass-accretion rate producing a propagating low-frequency signal.

The authors conclude that current AGN variability models do not adequately explain Fairall 9’s behavior. They interpret the rising phase as structural evolution of the inner accretion flow on hundreds-of-days timescales, potentially caused by an inward-propagating accretion-rate increase or an inner-disc instability. Such evolution is much faster than the viscous timescale of a standard Shakura–Sunyaev disc, indicating that a modified disc structure may be required.

In Alabama’s special Senate election, Democrat Doug Jones campaigns statewide while Republican Roy Moore, accused of sexual misconduct involving teenage girls, denies the allegations, is mostly absent, and leads polls.

Thousands of Armenian-Americans marched in Los Angeles to commemorate the estimated 1.5 million Armenians killed under the Ottoman Empire beginning in 1915 and demand Turkey recognize genocide. The demonstrations followed Armenian Prime Minister Serzh Sargsyan’s resignation after 10 days of anti-government protests. Demonstrators also urged an end to Turkey’s denial.

Manny’s input and leadership have driven the team’s success despite his injury, and his return would be an emotional boost. The speaker says Manny and Alex do not try to look different, making them easy for close friends to distinguish.
The speaker says jokes and missed chances keep players loose; relaxation is a good sign, and the team must focus on winning one game at a time before Detroit.

The paper examines the policy assumptions underlying South Australia’s “World Class” education initiative, launched across public primary and secondary schools in 2018. Using Bacchi’s “What’s the Problem Represented to be?” framework, it analyses publicly available and freedom-of-information documents to assess how the Department for Education represented school and system improvement.

Situated within the neoliberal Global Education Reform Movement, the policy used McKinsey’s “Universal Scale,” combining NAPLAN with PISA, TIMSS and PIRLS results, to reduce educational-system performance to a single number. South Australia aimed to reach 530 by 2028, joining Canada, Estonia and Finland at the top.

The analysis identifies the represented problem as competing educator voices and agendas impeding central reform. Its proposed solution involved greater departmental control, centralised data, scripted curriculum materials, prescribed improvement priorities and intensified monitoring. School rankings determined the level of oversight, with low-performing and disadvantaged schools receiving greater scrutiny. Additional Education Directors, annual School Improvement Dashboards and performance management strengthened surveillance and reduced professional autonomy and trust.

The authors argue that this data-driven, complexity-reduction approach privileged bureaucratic knowledge and standardised testing over professional judgement, contextual understanding, equity and broader educational purposes. They report that after four years, PIRLS results had declined, the PISA equity gap had widened, and absenteeism, disengagement, retention and HSC completion had deteriorated. They acknowledge that schools could resist or adapt policy locally.

The proposed alternative, “Beyond World Class,” would embrace complexity and uncertainty, value educators’ professional knowledge, use democratic partnerships and contextual support, prioritise equity and inclusion, and enable all young people to thrive within and beyond schooling.

Polar metals combine a non-centrosymmetric crystal structure with metallic conductivity, although mobile carriers screen polarization-induced electric fields and prevent field-driven reversal of polarity. Distortive polar metals (DPMs) form through a symmetry-reducing structural transformation and commonly exhibit a “weak coupling” between polar distortions and electronic states. Their polar domains possess distinct polarization directions, and discontinuities across domain boundaries create head-to-head (H-H) or tail-to-tail (T-T) configurations that carry structural “bound charge,” despite the absence of net charge in a metal.

This study examines the metallic DPM Mn₅Al₈, specifically off-stoichiometric Mn₅₁Al₄₉. X-ray diffraction identified a first-order transformation near 880 °C from a cubic γ-brass structure with space group I‾43m to a polar rhombohedral γ₂ phase with space group R3m. The displacive, martensitic transformation produced rank-2 laminate twins, predominantly a herringbone morphology containing four crystallographically equivalent polar variants. Orientation gradients and localized elastic strain occurred near the boundaries, but no dislocations were observed. Atomic-resolution microscopy confirmed the twin interfaces without detecting secondary phases.

Resistivity measurements, electronic-structure calculations, and a nonzero density of states near the Fermi level confirmed metallic behavior. Four-dimensional STEM differential-phase-contrast imaging revealed the herringbone domains and their H-H and T-T boundaries, although diffraction effects limited interpretation of the displacement and divergence maps to qualitative results.

Surface measurements showed distinct behavior among domain-boundary types. Low-voltage SEM and electrostatic-force microscopy produced contrast across subsets of boundaries, while preferential copper deposition and variable oxide formation reproduced the interlocking H-H/T-T pattern. Correlated EBSD analysis associated copper deposition primarily with H-H boundaries. The observations suggest electron enrichment, a higher density of states, and a lower work function at H-H boundaries, with electron depletion and higher work function at T-T boundaries. Geometric polarization discontinuities may locally influence carrier density, but the precise mechanism remains unresolved. Magnetic effects were ruled out by paramagnetic behavior, while the observed patterning did not correlate directly with elastic strain.

A sorting of ICSD compounds identified at least 134 strictly metallic compounds in polar crystal classes, about 5.1% of roughly 2,600 polar compounds, with approximately 20% classified as DPMs that undergo a symmetry-lifting transformation. Mn₅Al₈ was used as a representative example of this previously overlooked chemical space. The findings indicate that domain boundaries in metallic DPMs can exhibit distinct electronic and surface properties and may provide opportunities for functionalization.
At a tea, the Jonathan Hunt DAR chapter honored five Good Citizen scholars. The overall winner received money, and all will receive achievement certificates at Spring Awards Day.

John Wilkerson is a STAT Washington correspondent covering health-care politics and author of the twice-weekly D.C. Diagnosis newsletter on health and medicine policy. The page lists articles on biotech, drug regulation and trials, women’s health, Tylenol, GLP-1s, Alzheimer’s, venture funding, hospital and vaccine policy, and Democratic negotiations over ACA subsidies during a government shutdown.

Jane Goodall, a pioneering primatologist and conservationist, died in her sleep from natural causes while touring California at age 91, according to the Jane Goodall Institute. Hired by Louis Leakey in 1957, she gained chimpanzees’ trust at Gombe and documented their tool use, personalities, warfare, and social behavior, challenging the belief that humans alone used tools. Despite lacking a bachelor’s degree and facing gender bias and skepticism, she earned a PhD in animal behavior from Cambridge in 1965. Goodall founded the Jane Goodall Institute in 1977, launched its Roots & Shoots youth program in 1991, and advocated against invasive chimpanzee research. She was named a UN Messenger of Peace in 2002, a Dame of the British Empire in 2004, and inducted into the French Legion of Honor in 2006.

Argentine defender Federico Allende admitted to repeatedly jabbing Estudiantes strikers with a needle during Pacifico’s 3–2 cup upset, saying dirty tactics were needed against top-division opponents. Colombian striker Juan Otero reported being stabbed multiple times and called Allende “a nasty man.” Pacifico president Héctor Moncada vowed to expel Allende over the incident.

In 1889, an insurrection led by Robert W. Wilcox and Robert Boyd, involving about 100 participants, was defeated; Wilcox and roughly 60 followers were imprisoned, while about 70 U.S. sailors and marines briefly protected the legation and city. Hawaii’s supreme court then ruled against King Kalakaua in a constitutional dispute, holding that his signature on public documents was subject to cabinet direction and that government must be conducted by the cabinet. Kalakaua was invited to the 1890 International American Conference, but Hawaii’s delegate did not participate before its adjournment.

Kalakaua visited the United States in December 1890 and died in San Francisco on January 20, 1891. His body was returned to Honolulu, and Princess Liliuokalani was proclaimed queen. Minister Stevens reported fears that she would force ministerial resignations, while expecting legal and public resistance. The supreme court ruled that Kalakaua’s cabinet ended with his death, and a new cabinet was appointed. The prince consort died August 27, 1891. Negotiations followed over revising U.S.-Hawaiian reciprocity after sugar tariffs were removed; Mott Smith was appointed envoy, and a treaty-supporting legislature was elected in February 1892.

A randomized controlled trial at the University of Utah compared eight weeks of group mindfulness-based stress reduction (MBSR) alone with MBSR plus group psilocybin-assisted psychotherapy (PAP) among 25 frontline physicians and nurses with depression and burnout related to COVID-19. The PAP arm additionally received 25 mg psilocybin after four weeks of MBSR, followed by group preparatory, dosing, and integration sessions.

At two weeks, MBSR+PAP produced a significantly greater reduction in depressive symptoms on the QIDS-SR-16 than MBSR alone (7.26 versus 2.66 points; between-group effect 4.6; p=0.004; d=1.04). It also showed greater reductions in depersonalization at two weeks, emotional exhaustion at six months, and demoralization at two weeks, along with greater increases in general connectedness and connectedness to self and others. Personal accomplishment did not differ significantly between groups. At six months, depression scores improved in both groups and the between-group difference was no longer significant.

All adverse events were mild or moderate, with no serious treatment-emergent adverse events, emergent suicidality, or self-injury. PAP attendance was high, and overall MBSR attendance was 80.9%. Post-randomization expectancy was higher for MBSR+PAP but was associated with symptom improvement only in the MBSR-only group.

The study was limited by its small, predominantly White female sample, lack of blinding, unequal interventions, and inclusion of participants with prior psychedelic use. The findings suggest that combining MBSR with group PAP may be a safe, feasible, and potentially efficacious approach to depression and burnout among healthcare workers, but larger, diverse, multisite, placebo-controlled studies are needed.

Stock trading strategies are rule-based methods for buying and selling stocks or ETFs over short periods, unlike long-term investing, which emphasizes holding assets for years or decades. The passage reviews approaches including day trading, swing trading, scalping, momentum and trend following, arbitrage, high-frequency trading, event-driven trading, sector rotation, pair and market-neutral trading, statistical arbitrage, technical analysis, seasonality, long-short equity, index trading, overnight trading, mean reversion, and oscillator trading.

The article favors quantified rules, historical backtesting, research, and disciplined execution over intuition or anecdotal evidence. It discusses common indicators—moving averages, RSI, MACD, Bollinger Bands, and stochastic oscillators—and says technical analysis can help identify trends, overbought or oversold conditions, and entry or exit points. Traders should account for volatility, market conditions, trading costs, slippage, commissions, and unexpected news. Diversification across stocks, sectors, asset classes, strategies, and timeframes can reduce risk, while algorithms can automate rule-based execution, speed trades, and limit human error.

Day trading and scalping are presented as especially difficult, with many traders reportedly losing money; arbitrage, high-frequency trading, and statistical arbitrage are described as better suited to institutions. The 3-5-7 rule suggests three initial pushes, five moves against the trend, and seven pushes reaffirming the original direction. The best strategy depends on the trader’s objectives, mindset, and risk tolerance.

Concentrating on one stock exposes retail traders to company-specific and event risks, limits opportunities, and prevents portfolio diversification. The passage therefore recommends trading multiple securities and using a portfolio of strategies. It advises beginners to develop a plan, learn market analysis, practice in a simulator, manage risk carefully, and avoid speculative “hot tips.”

Churchill High School senior Deanthony Gordley earned his diploma after overcoming homelessness following Hurricane Katrina, his father’s murder, and his biological mother’s death. NEISD connected him with the McKinney Vento Homeless Project, and several families provided additional support. Gordley credits the school and those around him with helping him persist. Passionate about music, he sings, dances, raps, and sells his songs on iTunes.

Syracuse’s 2018 recruiting class appears among the program’s best and potentially its strongest in at least seven years. Ranking uses recruiting standing upon arrival, without considering later results.
Kitagawa, Robson and Yaghi won the 2025 chemistry Nobel for frameworks that collect water from air and capture greenhouse gases.

Stripe is launching Open Issuance, which lets businesses create and manage their own stablecoins and capture interest earned on reserves such as U.S. Treasury bills and bank deposits while maintaining a 1:1 dollar peg. The product follows Stripe’s $1.1 billion acquisition of Bridge and the establishment of a U.S. regulatory framework for stablecoins. Stripe-issued stablecoins will be interoperable across blockchains and support dollar on- and off-ramping. Initial users include Phantom, Hyperliquid and Consensys’s MetaMask, while Bridge cofounder Zach Abrams predicts dozens or hundreds of companies may issue stablecoins within months. Wider adoption by non-crypto businesses remains uncertain, though Stripe believes merchants could introduce stablecoins to mainstream U.S. consumers.

A compilation of press clippings dated May 11–13, 2001 (subject line "Enron Mentions - 05/12/01 - 05/13/01"), covering power, energy and business news:

**California universities and blackouts** — The New York Times (5/13) reports that UC Berkeley administrators and professors prepared for possible rolling blackouts during final exams, which began Friday. Executive vice chancellor Paul R. Gray advised instructors to use individual discretion on exam disposition (delay, postpone to Saturday, grade incomplete, or cancel) and to check classrooms for natural light. Most University of California and California State University campuses were on alert, with medical centers and the Davis, Los Angeles and Riverside campuses exempt. The two systems are in a legal dispute with Enron Energy Services, which in February cut short a four-year contract to supply electricity directly; meanwhile they are supplied by Pacific Gas and Electric and Southern California Edison.

**British Telecom** — The Times of London (5/12) notes Moody's downgraded BT's credit rating hours after BT announced a £5.9 billion rights issue and separation of BT Wireless, adding roughly £35 million a year on existing loans and making working capital more expensive; the Enron Cost of Credit has halved since mid-February. The article also criticizes UK competition authorities, arguing the Office of Fair Trading's advice that BT's Yellow Pages annual real price cuts be doubled could leave Yell worth £1 billion less and turn a growth business stagnant.

**Nanotechnology and Houston** — The Houston Chronicle (5/13) argues Houston should think "small" as nanotechnology advances, fitting its chemical and energy industries and pursued at Rice University; Dallas-Fort Worth has drawn more publicity and funding, including a $2.5 million private donation to UT Dallas in March. Skeptics cite the distance from commercial application and risks of combining genetic engineering, nanotechnology and robotics. Energy, medical and technology leaders were to gather at the Houston Technology Forum on May 29.

**Center for Houston's Future** — A Houston Chronicle (5/13) article describes a nonprofit's report, prepared by a business task force under board chairman Eugene H. Vaughan (board includes Enron Chairman Ken Lay), sketching four illustrative scenarios: continued status quo (loss of annexation power, restricted development, low-wage sprawl); education reform via a "Teacher Network," universal Internet by 2007 and near-universal high school graduation by 2010; "livable city centers" with transit corridors and an $8 billion, 20-year referendum; and economic diversification into space, nanotechnology and biotechnology. Participants concluded Houston must achieve key elements of the last three to become a world-class city, with committees and working groups to develop recommendations.

**Dabhol Power Company (DPC)** — Several reports:
- PTI (5/13): MSEB decided not to take its remaining 15% in DPC (about $65 million) after phase II completion, citing financial stress. Enron International holds 65%, MSEB 15%, GE and Bechtel 10% each. DPC's $1.87 billion phase II was due to fire June 7, 2001, completing the 2,184 MW project; DPC has not found an alternative buyer for the 15% stake and plans to sell down to 50%, with Enron agreeing to cover the shortfall.
- AFP/MEED (5/13): Enron plans to pull out of the Dolphin Energy project to pipe Qatari gas to the UAE with TotalFinaElf and UOG, sources citing low profit margins and excessive pipeline costs. Qatar and the UAE signed a 25-year term sheet in March; UOG holds 51% of Dolphin Energy Ltd., with Enron and TotalFinaElf at 24.5% each.
- The Economic Times (5/13): After a decade of private participation, India's power sector has delivered only about 5,000 MW, with policy uncertainty and weak state electricity board finances stalling new projects. Cogentrix and Powergen have exited, and sources suggest Enron may follow. IPPAI cites government policy flip-flops — only three of eight projects with counter guarantees took off — and most SEBs registering negative turnover.
- Dow Jones (5/12): Power Minister Suresh Prabhu said a negotiated settlement of DPC's power purchase agreement and payment dispute was possible after a state expert panel's first meeting with DPC, with another set for May 23. Enron VP John Ambler said the meeting should not be construed as an open offer to renegotiate. Maharashtra calls DPC's 7.1 rupees/kWh tariff (versus 1.5 rupees from other suppliers) unaffordable; MSEB has not paid December 2000 and January bills. The Godbole panel is seeking lower tariffs, allowed excess-power sales and possible restructuring of shareholding; DPC operates a 740 MW naphtha plant, to be expanded 1,444 MW in phase II with a switch to LNG in 2002.
- Business Line (5/12): Enron India officials met the Godbole panel; state officials said talks would focus on the Rs 401 crore rebate DPC owes and that MSEB does not need phase II and would not buy its power. MSEB wants Rs 213 crore in dues adjusted against the Rs 401 crore performance-default penalty; state and central governments backed MSEB's replies to DPC's arbitration notices. A.V. Gokak was appointed to the arbitration committee, and a third conciliator remains unappointed.
- PTI (5/12): Prabhu said the federal government would allow sale of power to a "willing buyer" if DPC and MSEB jointly approached with a concrete proposal; NTPC cannot buy power because it is a seller holding long-term PPAs, though the government would seek buyers in other states.

**Portland General Electric** — The Oregonian and AP (5/11–5/12) report U.S. Rep. Peter DeFazio's proposal that Oregon buy Enron-owned PGE, issuing revenue bonds to hold down customer rates. Sierra Pacific Resources' $3.1 billion purchase collapsed in April; other possible buyers include Northwest Natural and ScottishPower (owner of PacifiCorp). Gov. Kitzhaber said he would explore the idea, while House Speaker Mark Simmons and outgoing PUC Chairman Ron Eachus opposed it, and critics suggested it aided DeFazio's possible gubernatorial run. A publicly owned PGE could buy lower-cost Bonneville Power Administration hydropower, though not for about five years due to existing sales contracts, and might raise other utilities' rates.

**Star Fleet Entertainment Yachts** — The Houston Chronicle (5/13) profiles Tom Lober's private charter yacht business on Clear Lake and Galveston Bay, now four yachts and a staff of 70; it booked about 400 cruises last year for $2.3 million in gross sales, serving corporate clients including Enron, Exxon Mobil, Shell, Continental Airlines and Katy Mills mall, with cruises starting at $40 per guest. Lober launched a 30-foot "water limo" and is building a barge with a galley, office and apartment.

The 3-2 zone varies from the 1-2-2 by dropping the point defender to the free throw line, allowing wings to pressure passing lanes and protecting the high post. It concedes open shots to point guards but can be adjusted to a 1-2-2 or 1-3-1 against strong outside shooters. A tall wing and point defender may interchange, making high-post passes harder while keeping the weak-side baseline defender available for rebounding. Like the 1-2-2, it is strong against fast breaks because defenders are aligned in fast-break lanes. Rotations shift with the ball as defenders deny passes, cover the middle and low post, and protect the basket.

Investing.com’s Big View describes a decisive short-term shift to risk-off after a week of strong earnings but weak labor data and policy uncertainty. Major indexes broke down from all-time highs in a confirmed bearish engulfing pattern, while volume, market internals and nearly all sectors weakened. The article says investors sold into better-than-expected earnings amid doubts about economic growth and a lack of new buyers.

Q2 2025 earnings remained encouraging: 82% of reporting companies exceeded EPS estimates and 79% of S&P 500 companies exceeded revenue estimates, with upward earnings revisions also rising. GDP growth of 3% exceeded expectations but was distorted by tariff-related import volatility, while personal spending was soft. Nonfarm payrolls rose only 73,000 versus 100,000 expected, with unusually large downward revisions to prior months. A shrinking labor force partly offset the decline in job growth.

The Fed remained patient and data-dependent because tariffs may raise inflation and immigration policy is altering labor supply. Nevertheless, markets priced in a greater than 75% chance of a September rate cut and three cuts by January. The article attributes the correction to conflicting earnings strength, slowing-growth concerns, tariff and immigration uncertainty, fiscal and geopolitical developments, and political changes affecting the Fed and economic data. It recommends managing downside risk and preparing for better opportunities as the correction develops.

Buffalo beat No. 3 seed Florida State 86-65 to reach the women’s NCAA Sweet 16 for the first time in school history. Led by Cierra Dillard’s 22 points, the 11th-seeded Bulls will face defending champion South Carolina in Saturday’s regional semifinal.

The Market Research Future report on the global organic pigments market segments the market by type (acid and base dye, diazo, monoazo, phthalocyanine and others), source (natural and synthetic), and application (paint and coating, plastics, textiles, printing inks, and others including photo-reprographics, opto-electronic displays and optical data storage). The market grew enormously over the past decade and is forecast to grow at around 4.5%, driven by increased use in end-use industries, particularly paint and coating. Growth factors include cost effectiveness, unique shades, solvent stability and non-toxicity. Asia-Pacific is expected to be the fastest-growing and largest market, with China's contribution creating opportunities, followed by North America and Europe competing on value and volume. The report offers six-year forecasts for four regions, price and supply chain analysis, Porter's Five Forces, country-level analysis, and profiles of key players such as BASF, Dow Chemical, Huntsman, Clariant and Evonik, with geographic analysis across 20 countries.

An official report showed West Midlands house prices rose 7.1% to an average of £181,000, about £12,000 above the start of the year. UK prices increased 7.2%, with England strongest at 7.7%. Shetland recorded the largest rise at 26.1%, while Aberdeen fell 9.8%. Local growth ranged from 10.4% in Wyre Forest and Kidderminster to 3.1% in South Staffordshire. PwC expected 2–6% growth in 2017.

The passage describes a storage and retrieval system in which bins are stacked within a framework of uprights and a horizontal rail grid. Robotic load-handling devices travel above the stacks in two directions and lift one or more bins, allowing multiple products to be accessed concurrently. The framework can carry services through its uprights and underside, including electricity, communications, lighting, sensors, and fluid supply. Data from sensors can be recorded locally or transmitted to a central logging system for condition monitoring.

Sensors may monitor structural alignment, cracks, fire, smoke, heat, gases, and other conditions, while cameras permit remote visual inspection during operation. Bins may have transparent or absent sides and can include power, communication, lighting, heating, cooling, and fluid connections. Services may be delivered through framework connectors, contact pads, releasable latches, non-contact induction, telescoping umbilicals, and connections between stacked bins.

Identification systems such as barcodes and cameras can locate bins and determine their contents. Fire suppression can be targeted beneath the grid at particular bins or stacks using water or gases, reducing damage to load-handling equipment. The storage framework may also be partitioned into zones with different temperatures or atmospheres, including permanent or remotely deployed temporary partitions to isolate fires, spills, or other incidents.

At the April 29 Town Meeting, Nahant will vote on 41 articles, including an ambulance Enterprise Fund that could establish a future fee. The Finance Committee opposed it, citing questionable benefits, no urgency, ambulance debt at 6% interest, and spending outside Proposition 2½ protections. Two selectmen supported the proposal; Board Chair Richard Lombard opposed it, fearing residents might delay calling 911. Members will also consider rescinding the 2008 Coast Guard Housing sale and letting selectmen sell the parcel and 12 homes, though the committee recommended postponement. Recommended allocations include $175,000 for drainage, $106,000 for two public works trucks, and $280,000 for pumping stations.

The ADS9803 is an eight-channel, simultaneous-sampling, 20-bit SAR data acquisition system with configurable single-ended or differential inputs, true bipolar operation, and throughput up to 2 MSPS per channel. Each channel includes ±18 V input clamp protection, a programmable gain amplifier, and an antialiasing low-pass filter with selectable bandwidth. Input impedance is 1 MΩ, and the common-mode rejection circuitry supports voltages up to ±12 V. A speed-boost mode converts one selected channel pair at up to 8 MSPS while the other six channels remain idle.

The device uses a 4.096 V internal reference or an external reference connected through REFIO. It requires a free-running differential or single-ended sampling clock; SMPL_SYNC can synchronize channels across multiple devices. Conversion data can be output in straight-binary or binary two’s-complement format. Its source-synchronous interface supports two- or four-lane SDR or DDR operation, with 20-bit results transmitted MSB first in 24-bit packets. Features include XOR data randomization, simple and moving averages for improved SNR, and configurable fixed, ramp, and alternating test patterns.

Configuration uses 16-bit registers across three banks accessed through SPI. Initialization requires register writes after power-up or reset. SPI daisy-chain operation supports configuring and reading multiple ADCs, with 24 SCLKs per device for register writes.

For ATE applications, the ADS9803 provides low-noise bandwidth up to 22.7 kHz and wide bandwidth up to 700 kHz; multiplexed PMU signals settle to 99.95% of full scale in 7.5 µs. Its post-calibration total unadjusted error is 0.0015% at 25°C ±5°C. The device uses AVDD_5V, VDD_1V8, and IOVDD supplies with no required power-up sequence. Layout guidance emphasizes separate supply decoupling, a 10 µF reference bypass capacitor, short ground connections, and separation of analog, reference, and digital paths.

The passage argues that Saudi-funded distortions of Islam helped create al-Qaeda and ISIS and similarly condemns Western media for distorting opposition and amplifying anti-Trump rhetoric. It recounts the June 14, 2017, shooting at a baseball game in which James Hodgkinson, a U.S. citizen, Bernie Sanders supporter, and vocal Trump critic, shot five people, critically wounding House Majority Whip Steve Scalise, before dying. The passage associates Hodgkinson’s radicalization with anti-Trump television, Russia conspiracy theories, social-media threats, and Kathy Griffin’s beheaded-Trump photo. It acknowledges that most media viewers and Muslims are peaceful but argues that violent extremists on both sides warrant equal scrutiny and condemnation.

Wyoming mineral companies owe more than $42 million in delinquent taxes to 12 counties, largely because bankrupt companies prioritize repayment to secured lenders. Campbell County is owed over $26 million, while Sheridan County is owed about $7.46 million, mostly from Storm Cat Energy and Summit Gas Resources. An 18-month county payment schedule allows companies to reorganize, merge, sell assets or file for bankruptcy before taxes are due, contributing to unpaid obligations dating to 2003.

Delinquent taxes have left Sheridan County’s school district 2 with about $1.65 million owed, school district 3 with $750,000, Sheridan College with $430,000 and school district 1 with $120,000; other unpaid taxes support public services. The Powder River Basin Resource Council recommends monthly ad valorem tax collections, perpetual county liens, a state bankruptcy assistance fund and checks of tax debt before asset transfers. Similar legislative proposals failed in 2016 and 2017, while a new bill is planned for this year. Wyoming’s quicker severance-tax schedule has resulted in substantially fewer unpaid taxes.

At UNMC’s College of Dentistry, Nebraska children received free dental care and oral-hygiene education during Children’s Dental Day. The program, operating since 2001, has provided over $3 million in dental work.

Amazon.com, Inc.’s unaudited Form 10-Q for the quarter ended March 31, 2021 reported net sales of $108.5 billion, up 44% from $75.5 billion in Q1 2020, and net income of $8.1 billion versus $2.5 billion. Operating income rose to $8.9 billion from $4.0 billion, and diluted earnings per share increased to $15.79 from $5.01. Product sales were $57.5 billion and service sales were $51.0 billion. Operating cash flow was $4.2 billion, while purchases of property and equipment totaled $12.1 billion.

Segment sales and operating income were $64.4 billion and $3.5 billion for North America, $30.6 billion and $1.3 billion for International, and $13.5 billion and $4.2 billion for AWS. International moved from a $398 million operating loss in Q1 2020 to operating income in Q1 2021. Amazon recorded approximately $2.0 billion of COVID-19-related costs in the quarter and expected related fulfillment and cost pressures to continue into at least Q2 2021.

At March 31, 2021, total assets were $323.1 billion, stockholders’ equity was $103.3 billion, and cash, cash equivalents, restricted cash, and marketable securities totaled $73.3 billion. Long-term debt was $31.9 billion, and the present value of operating and finance lease liabilities was $67.8 billion. Total contractual commitments were $221.6 billion, including debt, leases, leases not yet commenced, purchase obligations, and other commitments. The company also disclosed approximately $3.0 billion of tax contingencies and continued to appeal the European Commission’s 2017 Luxembourg state-aid decision.

For Q2 2021, Amazon guided to net sales of $110 billion–$116 billion and operating income of $4.5 billion–$8.0 billion, assuming approximately $1.5 billion of COVID-19 costs, Prime Day in the quarter, and no additional acquisitions, investments, restructurings, or legal settlements. The filing identified interest-rate, foreign-exchange, and investment-value risks; foreign-denominated funds were $19.8 billion at quarter-end.

Defenders should box out every free-throw shooter, communicate, and increase their intensity after offensive rebounds. They should step up the lane with feet together, keep their hands high, and maintain inside position without being pushed under the basket. Defenders may double-team strong rebounders when rules permit. Teams should practice assignments and early push-offs following made or missed free throws.

A Cherokee County community plans to pay tribute to local school leader Maleka Johnson, killed when a tour boat caught fire in the Bahamas. Her husband, Tiran, was critically injured, while their 12-year-old son stayed in Tennessee. Her father, Melvin Grimes, said family members are comforted by community support and preserving the joy she brought others.

After taking the constitutional oath, the president accepts the office’s grave responsibilities and pledges to execute its duties diligently, impartially, and for the country’s best interests, guided by the Constitution, judicial decisions, and presidential precedent. He vows to appoint honest, capable, and faithful officials, maintain military and naval efficiency, and avoid favoring any section or local interest. In foreign affairs, he advocates neutrality in conflicts between governments, peaceful relations, negotiation before force, and avoidance of entangling alliances. The article examines the U.S. options-expiration (OPEX) week effect. Stock options generally expire on the third Friday, or Thursday when Friday is a holiday, with March, June, September, and December featuring quadruple witching. Expiring options, reduced open interest, hedging, and pin risk can create market imbalances and volatility.

For the week after expiration, the backtest buys SPY at Friday’s close during an options-expiration week and sells at the following Friday’s close. Since 1993, this strategy had a 1.5% CAGR and underperformed a random week, with monthly results varying substantially. August was strongest, averaging a 0.55% gain, while September was weakest, averaging a 0.94% loss with a 25% win rate.

The broader OPEX-week strategy—buying at the week’s open and selling Friday’s close—produced a 2% CAGR and a 0.2% average weekly gain, though the effect was concentrated from 1990 onward and weakened in recent years. Trading only on expiration day produced negative average returns, with or without a moving-average filter. The authors conclude that an OPEX-week effect exists but is not independently tradeable without additional parameters.

The passage describes nine drawings of an under-sink organizer with a sliding storage basket: perspective views in FIGS. 1 and 2, front and rear elevations in FIGS. 3 and 4, side elevations in FIGS. 5 and 6, top and bottom plan views in FIGS. 7 and 8, and an exploded perspective view in FIG. 9.
