The lecture frames corporate carbon-footprinting as a process for identifying a company’s emissions, understanding measurement boundaries, and evaluating the credibility of emissions claims. Using the WidgetCo office-chair case study, it examines facilities in Michigan and Shanghai, distribution centers, outsourced transportation, owned trucks, suppliers, and customer delivery. Investor and customer pressure has increased the importance of measuring these emissions, while competitor FerretCo has publicly reported a footprint, announced a carbon-neutrality goal, and considered product carbon labels.

Calculations generally multiply activity data by published emissions factors. Electricity use and direct fuel combustion are the principal facility calculations, while transportation is commonly calculated using fuel consumption or, when unavailable, ton-miles. Dedicated shipments can be assigned directly to a company; shared ocean or rail transport requires allocating emissions according to cargo weight and distance. Aggregate tonnage and mileage must not simply be multiplied because shipment weights and distances vary; multiplying average weight, average distance, and shipment count provides a closer approximation. Data gathering is manual and error-prone, with common problems involving missing values, inconsistent units, shipment aggregation, and inconsistent emissions factors.

Corporate footprints are divided into scope 1, direct emissions from owned or controlled facilities and vehicles; scope 2, indirect emissions from purchased electricity; and scope 3, all other indirect emissions. Scope 3 categories are generally optional under the Greenhouse Gas Protocol, while requirements vary among regulatory and trading programs. Companies must define an organizational boundary before calculation, using equity-share or operational-control methods. This determines responsibility for jointly owned facilities and outsourced activities. Scope 1 and scope 2 are normally required once the boundary is set, while inclusion of scope 3 is discretionary and usually involves all-or-nothing accounting for a selected activity.

Footprints also depend on which greenhouse gases are included. The six Kyoto gases can be expressed as carbon-dioxide equivalents using global-warming potentials, and factors are periodically revised. Disclosures should therefore state whether they cover only carbon dioxide or all applicable gases. Aggregate emissions should also be paired with intensity measures and baseline years; acquisitions, divestitures, business growth, and updated factors may require prior results to be restated.

Class estimates for WidgetCo varied considerably because of differing boundaries, assumptions, and calculation errors, with manufacturing responsible for roughly 85% of supply-chain emissions. Corporate comparisons can therefore be misleading: FerretCo’s lower reported total partly reflected its use of contract manufacturers and a boundary that excluded outsourced manufacturing. Researchers found that manufacturers own only about 25% of their supply-chain emissions on average, motivating value-chain accounting that covers raw materials, manufacturing, distribution, product use, and disposal. The CDP Supply Chain Report extends reporting to suppliers.

Disclosure is driven primarily by institutional investors, business customers, and emerging regulation rather than most end consumers. Voluntary reporting can reveal a company’s reduction opportunities, support targets and internal accountability, and reduce the risk of future mandates. Companies may delay disclosure until they have a reduction strategy and a clear understanding of their footprint. The lecture concludes by connecting corporate boundaries and supply-chain accounting to product carbon labeling and life-cycle assessment, which will be addressed in the next class.

New Jersey expects a strong Detroit response in Game 2 of the Stanley Cup Final and must protect its 1–0 lead and home-ice advantage. The team is being urged to start disciplined and physical, pressure the net, create chances, and capitalize on them.

The speakers credited the first-game scoring to hard work at the net and fortunate rebounds rather than Detroit turnovers, while acknowledging that the visitors remained competitive and that an elite goalie such as Belfour can bounce back. They also praised Jason’s development into a confident locker-room leader. The discussion emphasized hockey’s unpredictability, preparation, team chemistry, and the need to treat the next game as a new contest because winning the opener does not guarantee success.

A retrospective study analyzed records from the Noma Children’s Hospital in Sokoto, Nigeria, covering September 1999 to October 2024. The cohort included 1,383 patients: 931 with acute noma and 452 with arrested noma. Incidence was estimated for acute stages 1–3 using the WHO two-step method, 2006 census populations, and reported referral and survival assumptions.

An estimated 62,067 new cases occurred, corresponding to 114.5 cases per 100,000 population. Annual incidence averaged 4.4 and had a median of 2.2 cases per 100,000, ranging from 0.2 to 21.3; incidence was substantially higher during 2020–2024. Rates were slightly higher among males than females. Sokoto had the highest incidence at 921.9 per 100,000 and Adamawa the lowest at 6.3. Incidence was highest among children under ten, particularly those under five. Sokoto had the highest incidence among people under 18, while Kebbi had the highest among young and middle-aged adults.

Most acute cases presented with gangrene, whereas relatively few presented with oedema or acute necrotizing ulcerative gingivitis, indicating frequent late-stage presentation. The cheeks were the most commonly affected sites. The findings support greater awareness, early screening, and referral programs. Limitations included missing data from six eligible states or territories and inability to assess detailed risk factors.

After winning his third London Marathon, Eliud Kipchoge visited Tottenham Hotspur, meeting Harambee Stars captain Victor Wanyama, Tottenham coach Mauricio Pochettino, and his coach Patrick Sang. Kipchoge is expected to attempt Dennis Kimetto’s world record at the Berlin Marathon.

The study examines barriers to distance education among university faculty teaching mathematics education courses in Turkey following the COVID-19 pandemic and February 2023 earthquake. It reviews literature identifying external barriers, including limited access, time, training and institutional support; teacher-related beliefs and willingness to change; and third-order challenges involving instructional redesign, design thinking and online classroom management.

Using Q methodology, researchers randomly selected 13 mathematics education faculty members from 96 volunteers in Turkey’s Marmara region. Participants ranked 50 statements on a seven-point scale, provided qualitative comments and completed interviews with two strongly loading participants. Principal component analysis with Varimax rotation produced three perspectives: student-related, technology-related and pedagogical barriers. The largest group identified reduced engagement, reluctance to participate or take responsibility, distractions, isolation and inadequate devices as major problems. The technology-related group emphasized insufficient internet, equipment and digital-library access. The pedagogical group highlighted unreliable online assessment, difficulties representing mathematical concepts, limited use of tangible materials and incompatibility between fully online teaching and mathematics.

Across all participants, curriculum and pedagogical barriers had the highest average impact, followed by teacher, technology and student barriers. No distinct teacher-related factor emerged. Participants agreed that distance education alone was unsuitable for mathematics and favored blended, hybrid or HyFlex models. The findings broadly matched e-learning literature while identifying additional barriers specific to mathematics pedagogy and curriculum. The results were limited to 13 randomly selected Marmara-region faculty members and their stated perceptions.

The disclosure describes systems for securely storing and sharing encrypted user data, including medical information, among patients, healthcare providers, and other recipients through client devices and a cloud server. Client-side key hierarchy structures use password- and security-question-derived keys to unlock a master encryption key, data encryption keys, and private keys. Encryption parameters, salts, initialization vectors, and encrypted keys are retained on the client, while user data remains encrypted on the server, which cannot access the decryption keys.

Data can be shared securely with an individual using asymmetric public-key encryption, allowing asynchronous storage and later retrieval without server access to plaintext. Group sharing uses a separate shared-data key hierarchy in which a shared data encryption key is encrypted under each authorized recipient’s public key. Authorized users can decrypt and propose edits, while the owner approves or rejects changes and can regenerate the shared copy or remove recipients.

The disclosure also covers credential recovery and replacement, multiple data encryption keys for segregating information, expiring key pairs, secure delivery of printed content through a printer driver, tracking of shared communications, and implementation of the disclosed functions through client-side software, hardware, or both.

Martinez Paredes appealed his 57-month sentence and guilty-plea conviction for conspiracy to distribute methamphetamine and heroin. Counsel filed an Anders brief and withdrew; no pro se brief was filed. The Ninth Circuit found no arguable grounds for relief, granted withdrawal, and affirmed without oral argument.

The Senate approved the Philippine Identification System bill 17-2 and a coconut levy trust fund bill. It would assign PhilSys numbers to citizens and foreign residents, with the PSA maintaining the registry and number disclosure limited to specified grounds. A 2019 rollout was planned with P2 billion allocated.

Researchers identified two strains of bacteria from grape leaves that can degrade guaiacol, a volatile phenol linked to smoke taint in wine. Both strains nearly eliminated detectable guaiacol within 96 hours in petri-dish tests. Deleting the degradation gene prevented one strain from consuming the compound, while related smoky compounds did not support bacterial growth, suggesting other bacteria may be needed for additional smoke-taint compounds. The microbial approach could eventually offer winemakers a more selective alternative to activated-charcoal filtration, which can also remove desirable wine qualities. More research is needed to explore the grape microbiome’s potential to treat other sources of smoke taint.

Barbeque Nation Hospitality filed a DRHP with Sebi for an IPO comprising a Rs 200 crore fresh issue and 61.79 lakh shares for sale, representing 14.22% of paid-up capital. Fresh-issue proceeds will fund new restaurants, loan repayment and corporate purposes; it operated 81 restaurants in India and one in Dubai as of June 2017.

Telstra CEO Andy Penn must offer hope at investor day as shares fall, earnings guidance is effectively downgraded and S&P cuts its rating. Negative analyst commentary has eased, with UBS upgrading the stock to buy and Morgan Stanley presenting a more positive outlook.

Six months after Abby Williams and Libby German were killed near Monon High Bridge in Delphi, police have made no arrests. Investigators are following over 24,000 tips, analyzing crime-scene DNA, and reviewing old evidence and leads.

Ajay Bodke of Prabhudas Lilladher expects a bright medium-term outlook for Indian equities, citing recovering corporate earnings, an improved macroeconomic environment relative to emerging markets, and crude oil remaining between $60 and $70 per barrel. He also notes India’s estimated 7.5% GDP growth for FY18-19 and the post-GST shift from unorganized to organized sectors. With global central banks tightening and fiscal slippage concerns, he believes the RBI may struggle to maintain its neutral monetary-policy stance.

Domestic institutional investors have become a strong counterbalance to foreign inflows, while monthly mutual-fund SIP contributions of ₹5,000–6,000 crore provide a stable source of investment. Bodke says retail investors need not fear LTCG tax because equities remain the only asset class offering inflation-beating post-tax returns; he considers the 10% rate fair and views equities as attractive over the medium to long term. The Sensex has reportedly delivered four- to sixfold returns every decade, outperforming gold, and longer holding periods reduce the risk of losses.

He identifies life and general insurance, along with retail-focused private-sector BFSI companies, as promising sectors.

Montclair State University mascot Rocky the Red Hawk celebrated his 16th birthday on campus. Team Rocky began the day by handing out 500 free bagels, followed by candy for students who encountered Rocky. A Student Center party featured campus organizations giving away gifts, photo and GIF booths, cupcakes, a prize wheel, a speech by President Susan Cole, birthday singing, cake, and a donation box for a local food pantry. Raffle winners received sweatshirts, a $100 bookstore gift card, and a 10-use parking pass.

The AMD Geode CS5535 Companion Device Silicon Revision A3 specification update catalogs known silicon limitations and software workarounds; issue numbers are nonsequential because resolved issues are omitted.

The PIT does not properly cancel an uncompleted latch command when a read-back command is issued, and mode 3 loads a new count immediately; software must complete the latch command and avoid relying on the latter behavior. The GLIU debug port can hang and its data-pattern detector does not operate. XPIC clears an IRR bit late, causing duplicate interrupts when AEOI is enabled; AEOI is suitable only where nested multilevel interrupts are unnecessary. DMA transfers complete under rotating priority, but their channel order may not rotate correctly. During a thermal alarm, the PMC cannot autonomously recover from Faulted Standby, and the system must proceed through its power-removal and retry sequence until the alarm clears.

ATA and UDMA issues include CRC corruption after device termination, failure to block PIO during DMA as expected, PRD prefetch hazards with unaligned tables, failure when a PIO command follows bus-master enablement, an ATAPI failure affecting one CD-ROM firmware revision, and possible ATAC hangs with WORD-aligned PRDs. The update says UDMA writes generally cannot be used unless host terminations are prevented through ATAC Error MSR bit 8. PRDs should be defined before transfers, dynamic changes should be at least two tables ahead, and UDMA operations should use DWORD alignment and issue the PIO command before enabling the bus master.

ACPI and power-management issues include hangs from BYTE accesses to PM1_STS or PM1_EN, corruption of other PMC registers by WORD or BYTE writes, loss of SLEEP_X and SLEEP_Y deassertion during Sleep exit, failure to set LOWBAT_FLAG after abnormal standby, and nonfunctional S3 wake inputs other than PWRBTN#. PMC writes should be DWORD-only or trapped, Sleep-related delay counters should be shorter than PM_SED, and external circuitry is needed to combine wake events.

Other limitations affect UART access during legacy DMA, LPC I/O during block or demand DMA, 8237 diagnostic DMA from LPC, USB and UART clock gating, USB overvoltage protection, SMBus hold time and NEGACK behavior, GLPCI retry counting, PCI back-to-back reads, KEL emulation state, RTC CMOS RAM access, LPC synchronization, and GPIO atomic writes after suspend. Documented workarounds include using single-transfer DMA, disabling affected clock gating, adding USB protection, using required SMB and GPIO access sequences, restoring KEL state around Snoop mode, and applying an LPC-to-ISA bridge workaround. High PCI I/O addresses and LBAR values at or above 10000h must also be avoided because they are illegal in x86 systems and may hang the CS5535.

The study examines whether highly impactful medical journals publish more interdisciplinary research than less impactful journals. “Impactful” journals are those ranked in the top 10% of the SCImago Journal Rank for medicine in a given year. Using PubMed articles from 1999, 2010, and 2022, the authors constructed weighted co-occurrence networks of second-level Medical Subject Headings (MeSH) representing diseases. Cosine-normalized article co-occurrences measured integration between concepts. Of 296 initially identified nodes, 201 remained after isolated terms were removed.

Because less-impactful journals had far more available articles, their networks were also constructed from June-only samples to reduce sample-size bias. This adjustment largely eliminated differences in weak-link frequency, so comparisons focused on impactful and June-based less-impactful networks. Temporal comparisons were deferred because publication volumes changed substantially between years.

The 1999 impactful network showed substantial modularity and topic-specific communities, including clusters for cancer, infectious diseases, nervous-system diseases, respiratory diseases, and musculoskeletal diseases. Networks exhibited approximately power-law link-strength distributions. Less-impactful networks had higher average node strength and density, suggesting greater integration among medical concepts, while impactful networks had higher modularity, indicating more compartmentalized research communities. Global clustering coefficients and moderately negative node-strength assortativity were similar across network types. Threshold-based decomposition revealed stable inner cores in both network types, consistently including concepts related to communicable and sexually transmitted diseases, immunologic deficiencies, genital diseases, and urogenital neoplasms.

Neoplasms by site ranked highest in both node strength and betweenness across all years and network types, supporting its role as a major bridge between distant areas of medical knowledge. Central nervous system diseases were also prominent bridges but had comparatively less local integration. At broader category level, infections, nervous-system diseases, and neoplasms consistently had the greatest total connection strengths. Infections primarily strengthened links within their own category, whereas nervous-system diseases and neoplasms more strongly connected different knowledge areas.

Subtracting less-impactful network weights from impactful network weights produced positive and negative difference networks. Strong differences showed only a weak tendency to occur near other strong differences, but Louvain analysis identified clear communities, demonstrating that differences cluster around particular topics. Strong links in the original impactful networks tended to produce stronger positive or negative differences, with both relationships following power-law patterns. The topic areas showing relative prominence in the difference-network cores changed considerably across years and between positive and negative differences, whereas the absolute inner cores of the original networks remained stable.

Overall, highly impactful medical journals were found to publish less interdisciplinary and more discipline-focused medical research than less impactful journals, despite their role in shaping research trends and practices. The authors suggest that peer review, the need for rapidly translatable clinical evidence, and reporting standards emphasizing prespecified questions, randomized trials, and systematic reviews may structurally disadvantage interdisciplinary work. They propose accommodating interdisciplinary evaluation within existing reporting frameworks, citing joint CONSORT-AI extensions as a potential example.

Wildwood Police bodycam footage shows officers stopping 20-year-old Emily Weinman on a New Jersey beach over suspected underage drinking. After a negative breathalyzer and questions about unopened alcohol, Weinman resisted giving her surname with her 18-month-old daughter present. Officers handcuffed and restrained her; she said they were hitting, choking, and pulling her hair. An officer alleged she kicked officers, though this was not visible. Reactions online were divided, and both officers were reassigned pending investigation. Weinman was charged with aggravated assault, aggravated assault by spitting, disorderly conduct, resisting arrest, obstruction, and minor possession of alcohol.

A Legislative Analyst’s Office report says Gov. Jerry Brown’s tentative contract for 27,000 California Correctional Peace Officers Association members has a “weak justification.” The proposed 5% raise would be their largest since 2006, but the analyst found no evidence of recruitment or retention problems. Entry-level staffing has increased, mid-career representation is steady, and wages have exceeded inflation since 2001. The report also notes fewer private-sector alternatives, with correctional-officer jobs projected to decline 8% from 2016 to 2026. Brown estimates the one-year deal will cost $338 million over two years, but the analyst warns overtime and pension contributions could increase that cost. CCPOA members are voting, and the Legislature must also approve the contract.

A new study in *Antiquity* identifies more than 250 remains in a mass grave at St. Wystan’s church in Repton, Derbyshire, as members of the Viking Great Heathen Army, who fought in Mercia in 874 before accepting Alfred the Great’s terms of peace and Christian baptism. Earlier radiocarbon dates had placed some remains around 600, but researchers found that the Vikings’ seafood-heavy diet had distorted the results; correcting for the marine reservoir effect brought the dates into alignment with the documented invasion. The grave included a double burial with a sword and silver Thor’s hammer pendant, one man bearing severe injuries and a boar’s tusk possibly intended as a replacement penis, and four apparent child sacrifices marked with stones and sheep’s jawbones. The findings also clarify the presence of women and previously overlooked trauma among the dead.

Police launched a nationwide manhunt for Steve Stephens, a 37-year-old job counselor accused of posting a Facebook video of himself killing 74-year-old Robert Godwin Sr. Godwin was shot while collecting aluminum cans in Cleveland and appeared to have been selected at random. Authorities posted a $50,000 reward, while tips prompted nine Philadelphia schools to lock down as investigators checked possible sightings. Stephens said he “snapped” and blamed former girlfriend Joy Lane, but police could not identify what triggered the shooting. Investigators said only Godwin was linked to Stephens, despite Stephens claiming he had killed more than a dozen people. A vigil was held for Godwin.

Camp America offers over-18s summer work at camps across the USA, with opportunities particularly for people qualified in tennis coaching, horse riding or lifeguarding. More than 8,000 places are available across 1,000 camps, while recruitment fairs in January and February feature over 200 camps hiring candidates on the spot. The £599 package includes application fees, medical insurance, return flights and a 30-day travel period, plus $650–$1,200 in pocket money. Work is fast-paced and includes caring for children and leading activities. The experience can help develop skills, support career prospects and shape participants’ lives.

The lecture reviews simplified plasma equilibria for interpreting spectroscopy. Complete thermodynamic equilibrium gives Boltzmann state populations and a common temperature for electrons, ions, and radiation, with every excitation balanced by its inverse de-excitation; it is rare because it requires an optically thick system. Local thermodynamic equilibrium (LTE) applies to optically thin plasmas where collisional excitation and de-excitation dominate. Its population balance yields the Saha equation, which uses temperature, ionization potential, particle mass, and level degeneracy to determine ionization-state populations; observing a line from a given ion can therefore indicate a minimum plasma temperature.

Coronal, or collisional-radiative, equilibrium describes low-density plasmas in which collisions excite states while spontaneous radiative decay returns them to lower states. Excited-state populations can be calculated from collision rates and decay pathways, although the model’s validity depends on the relative rates of collisions and radiative decay. Nonlocal thermodynamic equilibrium requires solving the balance equations for the relevant excitation and de-excitation processes; in strongly photoionized plasmas, for example, collisional processes may be negligible.

A general spectroscopy workflow is presented: specify plasma density and temperature, select an equilibrium model, calculate ionization and excited-state populations and line strengths, synthesize the spectrum, model radiation transport, reflections, and detector response, and compare with experimental data. Inversion may not yield unique density and temperature because the spectrum is line-integrated. As a simpler diagnostic, ratios of strong, isolated, identified lines from different ionization states can estimate their relative populations and, with an equilibrium model such as Saha, infer temperature.

The lecture then introduces X-ray characteristic lines, including K- and L-shell transitions, helium-like and lithium-like ions, and the generally strong K-alpha line. Such lines can reveal plasma impurities. X-ray filters use element-specific absorption edges to select energy ranges. For imaging, ordinary lenses are ineffective because the X-ray refractive index is near one. Pinhole cameras provide inverted, magnified images but face a trade-off between geometric and diffraction blur, while bent crystals can focus individual wavelengths for monochromatic imaging. Detectors discussed include time-integrating film and reusable image plates, gated cameras, streak cameras for time-resolved one-dimensional profiles, and microchannel-plate-based detectors.

Researchers at Aarhus University and Arla evaluated on-farm milk concentration using reverse osmosis and ultrafiltration. Reverse osmosis did not negatively affect bacterial count, free fatty acid levels, or protein breakdown, and concentrated milk remained suitable for cheese and milk powder. The resulting milk powder matched the quality and durability of powder made from ordinary milk, while cheese showed minor enzyme-related differences and coagulation took about ten minutes longer, possibly because concentrated milk is thicker. On-farm concentration could reduce water transport, but energy use, investment, herd size, and distance to the dairy affect feasibility. Farmers showed significant interest, while dairies remained skeptical, and Arla was assessing profitability.
Agriculture-related shares rose as much as 13% after the government raised the paddy MSP by a record Rs 200 per quintal and approved MSPs for 14 kharif crops.

Assistant U.S. Attorney Will Rosenzweig of the Southern District of Florida was fired by email while observing Rosh Hashanah after conservatives surfaced old posts from his private blog criticizing President Donald Trump and his supporters. Rosenzweig, who joined the office in September 2020, allegedly wrote the posts while at Kobre & Kim; they included claims that Trump was “mentally unfit” and “an institutional terrorist.” He worked on complex economic crimes cases and did not immediately comment. His firing followed reports that dozens of federal prosecutors were dismissed after being considered at odds with Trump. Former special counsel Jack Smith criticized such dismissals and attacks on rule of law.

The British government shared President Wilson’s desire for a swift and lasting peace but argued that its durability required a sound international order. It identified aggressive great powers, weak enforcement of international law, and territorial and constitutional arrangements that ignored constituent populations as causes of war. It supported the Allies’ territorial changes, especially the expulsion of Turkey from Europe, which it considered necessary for peace and national rights. However, it warned that territorial changes alone would not prevent renewed German domination, given Germany’s militarism, disregard for treaties, and capacity to strike before neighbors could defend themselves. Without stronger protections than solemn treaties, no state’s rights would remain secure.

CompareCards highlights credit cards offering 0% introductory APRs lasting 12–21 months, particularly for balance transfers or large purchases. Its selections include Bank of America cards with 15-billing-cycle 0% APRs, $200 or 25,000-point bonuses, flexible cash-back or travel rewards, and no annual fees; Capital One Quicksilver and VentureOne cards offering 15 months of 0% APR, cash back or mileage, welcome bonuses, and no annual or foreign transaction fees; and Citi and Discover cards with cash-back rewards and 0% APR periods of up to 18 months on balance transfers. Rewards vary by card, with options including bonuses on groceries, restaurants, travel, gas, streaming, and other purchases. The passage explains that 0% promotional APRs can reduce interest costs but later carry variable APRs and may have balance-transfer fees. It also notes that fixed APRs remain relatively stable, while variable APRs follow prevailing rates, and advises consumers to compare terms carefully. CompareCards states that it uses an objective, data-driven rating system and that compensation from listed companies does not influence its ratings.

The PMC cannot recover autonomously from Faulted Standby because the thermal alarm resides in the Work domain. Its timer restarts after leaving Standby, prompting repeated cooling and Standby retries while the alarm remains asserted.

The author compares selecting a content marketing partner to dating and offers five tips: find a provider with aligned interests and a compatible strategy; interview multiple candidates; avoid relying on promises and request references, work samples, and results; clearly define desired services and collaboration expectations; and begin with a trial period, retaining the right to end the arrangement if it is unsuitable. A good partner should create effective content that attracts visitors, supports business goals, makes work easier, and enables an enjoyable working relationship.

Play action is a pass play designed to resemble a run by faking a handoff, drawing defenders toward the line of scrimmage, and exploiting the space behind them. The entire offense must sell the fake, while the offensive line quickly switches from run protection to pass protection. It is most effective when the defense expects a run, including short-yardage, goal-line, and red-zone situations. The highest-percentage teams run play action 30–40% of the time.

Common concepts include the Double Post, which sends two receivers on identical deep post routes, and the Bubble Y Over, a spread formation with at least four passing options and routes that can pull defenders away from receivers running downfield.

Unlike play action, a run-pass option lets the quarterback choose between a handoff and a quick pass based on defensive reactions and open routes. In play action, every option is a passing option, and the handoff exists solely to deceive the defense.

The article argues that gold’s Friday rally was not matched by meaningful gains in silver, platinum, or mining stocks, interpreting the divergence as bearish for precious-metals equities and an early sign of a larger decline. It also says the U.S. Dollar Index broke above its July high and the neckline of an inverse head-and-shoulders pattern, suggesting a possible rise toward 101.3, while stocks below key support face further downside. The author compares this setup to 2008 and links it to the “Peak Chaos” thesis. The page also includes market headlines, risk disclosures, and a reader disputing the technical-analysis interpretation.

“Resolute Marine Energy: Power in Waves,” prepared by Cate Reavis and Ezra Zuckerman on April 8, 2014, examines Resolute Marine Energy’s effort to commercialize wave-powered desalination and choose a strategy for entering South Africa.

In Ugu, a municipality on South Africa’s eastern coast, potable water cost about $1.00 per cubic meter despite a $0.50 government subsidy. A weak electric grid forced communities to use expensive diesel generators for desalination, while water also had to be imported from other regions. Resolute Marine Energy (RME), founded by Bill Staby, intended its Wave OTM system to produce water more cheaply using wave energy.

Wave-energy converters generally transform wave motion into mechanical power that can drive generators, but commercial deployment had been hindered by biofouling, rough seas, environmental concerns and high costs. Most companies were pursuing grid-scale electricity and competing against coal, which Staby considered unpromising. After unsuccessfully developing a NOAA-funded system for offshore aquaculture, RME shifted toward desalination. Research led by COO Olivier Ceberio identified a market gap between utility-scale water systems and small-scale solutions, particularly in places lacking affordable freshwater and reliable electricity. RME chose South Africa, where more than 21 million people lived in water-stressed areas and nearly two million coastal residents had weak or no grid access. It estimated the South African market at $1.4 billion.

The prototype Wave OTM consists of a submerged oscillating wave-energy converter, a hydraulic flow-smoother and pressure-intensifier, and a reverse-osmosis desalination plant using standard components. Seawater is piped ashore using wave-driven hydraulic power; diluted brine is returned to the ocean. RME stated that discharged salinity would be no more than 10% above ambient ocean levels. One container-sized unit could supply about 850 people, while a 25-unit plant could serve roughly 21,400. RME projected water prices of $1–$2 per cubic meter, compared with $3–$8 for diesel-powered systems.

RME had filed 10 provisional patents and three Patent Cooperation Treaty applications by mid-2012. Although most financing had come from U.S. government agencies, it needed $6 million for a second ocean trial and an 18-month South African integrated pilot. RME therefore sought impact investors because of their longer investment horizons and interest in social and environmental outcomes. It projected a fivefold return and 70% internal rate of return for a 2015 exit from the financing round.

RME signed a nonbinding agreement with Ugu and South Africa’s Council for Scientific and Industrial Research in 2012 for a pilot comprising one wave-energy converter and one desalination plant, with capacity of 50 cubic meters per day. RME would manufacture, install and maintain the system, while Ugu would operate it and distribute the water. If successful, Ugu planned to purchase the first system. The Development Bank of South Africa expressed interest in supporting local site development, and Ugu applied for a $1.2 million grant. RME estimated that as many as 17 systems might be required to provide 0.5 cubic meters per day to rural households, about 61,000 of which lacked safe drinking water.

RME was also evaluating Alaska as a possible market for electricity to remote communities dependent on diesel generators. Staby viewed the project as a way to develop permitting and market-development expertise, while Ceberio questioned whether a small startup should pursue both water and electricity.

RME considered three South African strategies:

1. **Electricity-powered desalination:** Easiest to implement and eligible for grants, but less efficient, required land disposal of brine, generated lower margins, could be copied by competitors, and concentrated sales in a single customer, Eskom.
2. **Hydraulic desalination:** RME’s business-plan approach, with fewer competitors and production costs estimated 30% below the electricity route. It retained water’s higher price premium and discharged brine back into the ocean, but required private funding, untested technology and a desalination partner able to build or modify a hydraulic system.
3. **A vertically integrated “black box”:** RME would own both wave-energy and desalination technology and sell a system producing water and electricity. This offered control over the value chain and intellectual property, but required more capital, time and expertise, created pricing and investor-positioning questions, and eliminated the local partner and desalination expertise RME lacked.

The case concluded that RME faced a critical strategic decision over whether it would become primarily an energy or water company and which approach would best serve stakeholders, investors and Ugu’s needs.

New York’s attorney general arrested Guilderland Town Judge Richard Sherwood and financial adviser Thomas Lagan, alleging they stole $4 million from family trusts they managed. Both face felony grand larceny, fraud, and stolen-property charges.

The Federal Circuit affirmed the Court of Federal Claims’ award of $250,000 in death benefits under the Public Safety Officers’ Benefits Act to Christine H. Roberts’s estate. Roberts, the mother of Mississippi sheriff Harold Ray Presley, was eligible as a parent because she survived Presley, who was fatally shot during a police chase in 2001. She timely filed a claim but died before payment.

The Bureau of Justice Assistance denied the estate’s claim, reasoning that Roberts had not filed before her death and that her death prevented payment. The Court of Federal Claims reversed, holding that Roberts had timely claimed the benefits and that a beneficiary’s eligibility is fixed when the public safety officer dies.

The majority held that the PSOBA and 28 C.F.R. § 32.10 require beneficiaries to survive the officer’s death but not to remain alive through administrative processing and payment. It concluded that Roberts’s entitlement vested when she survived Presley, rejected the Bureau’s contrary interpretation and later “living payee” regulation as inconsistent with the statute, and found that legislative history and statutory purpose did not displace the statute’s plain language.

Judge Prost dissented. She argued that the statute is silent or ambiguous regarding whether an estate may receive benefits and that deference to the Bureau’s reasonable “living payee” interpretation was warranted. Under that interpretation, benefits go only to living statutorily eligible recipients, preventing an estate from benefiting otherwise-ineligible adult children. She would have reversed the judgment.

Jaroslaw Buczkowski, 47, pleaded guilty to driving with excess alcohol after police stopped his BMW speeding at up to 70mph in 40mph zones in Boston at 4.45am on New Year's Day. His breath reading was 83 microgrammes of alcohol per 100ml of breath, more than twice the legal limit of 35. He was banned from driving for 20 months, reduced by 20 weeks if he completed a drink drivers' rehabilitation course, and fined £350 plus £120 in costs and charges.

Apple began underperforming the S&P 500 in June 2017 after a 6% two-day decline on heavy volume while major indexes reached new highs. Forward consensus EPS estimates for fiscal 2017–2019 rose since May 31, while revenue estimates declined slightly, potentially suggesting better margins. Foxconn’s weak May revenue was cited as one possible contributor.

Historical data showed that the 2012–2013 correction was preceded by declining EPS estimates, while the 2015–2016 decline was more associated with China’s currency devaluation and commodity-market weakness. Current estimates did not show a similar warning for Apple, although the stock’s technical breakout above its February 2015 high had stalled.

The article highlighted Apple’s high valuation expectations and the anticipated iPhone “supercycle,” along with risks that premium device prices might not be widely accepted. A break below the February–March 2015 level of $133–134 on strong volume was viewed as a concern. Potential tax and cash-repatriation benefits depended on whether returned cash would reach shareholders. The author concluded that Apple might be entering an earlier stage of relative underperformance after 17 years of leadership but remained long Apple and QQQ.

Apixaban compliance exceeded 95% at Weeks 4, 12 and 24 and was similar across study groups. Mean adherence at Week 24 was 91.64% with standard of care and 91.88% with the additional educational program, with no significant difference. Adherence from Week 24 to Week 48 and from first dose to Week 48 was also comparable across groups, although adherence declined in later intervals. Persistence was 91.7% versus 91.3% at Week 24 and 85.2%–87.8% at Week 48, without significant group differences. The proportion of fully adherent subjects fell over time but did not differ significantly by group. Subgroup analyses generally showed no interaction, except for atrial fibrillation type and sex during Weeks 24–48. Safety endpoints were similar at Weeks 24 and 48, with comparable adverse events, discontinuations and bleeding rates. Overall, the study found high adherence and persistence through 48 weeks, but no additional benefit from the proactive educational program.

The study examines how Indonesian digital startups can develop strong business models for Industry 4.0, where information technology is essential but rapid startup growth has outpaced effective management. It describes business models as tools for identifying customer needs, value propositions, revenue opportunities, cost structures, and competitive strategies.

Using a descriptive qualitative approach, researchers surveyed 120 purposively selected digital-startup founders, project managers, coworkers, and customers. Data came from semi-structured interviews, observations, and company profiles, with triangulation used for validity. The analysis applied a nine-component Lean Canvas covering customer segments, value propositions, channels, customer relationships, revenue streams, key resources, activities, partnerships, and cost structure.

The canvas was used to develop a model for “Beautiful Memories,” a startup addressing customers’ difficulty finding photographers, video editors, decoration services, and quality souvenirs quickly. Its proposed solutions include customized services without fixed packages, connections with service providers, provider and quality certifications, social-media marketing, event-based customer segments, and commissions of 10% for completed orders.

On October 25, 2022, Microsoft Corporation filed a Form 8-K announcing financial results for the fiscal quarter ended September 30, 2022. The press release was furnished as Exhibit 99.1 and was not deemed “filed” for purposes of Section 18 of the Exchange Act.

The US Department of Transportation issued an order targeting seven Chinese airlines, barring them from overflying Russia on routes to and from the US. The policy would force longer, less fuel-efficient detours for the affected carriers and exclude cargo airlines.

US airlines have been prohibited from using Russian airspace since sanctions related to Russia’s invasion of Ukraine, giving Chinese carriers a cost and time advantage that the order seeks to address. China’s Foreign Ministry said the order would hinder travel and people-to-people exchanges and criticized its effects on passengers and US businesses.

Flight-tracking data showed only two potentially affected US-China routes used Russian airspace in October, but detours could add hours. The order also follows US airline concerns about Chinese carriers receiving additional US flight permissions and broader security questions following diversions of Air India flights to Russia. US-China air service is still recovering, with about 10,000 flights scheduled in 2025, 28% below 2019 levels.

Sid is called a world-class scorer, while strong defensive play fuels much of the attack. Prepared for Pittsburgh’s speed, they nevertheless allowed odd-man rushes, while Pekks made key saves.

CoSn2 single crystals exhibit an electronic nematic symmetry-breaking state below 25 K despite remaining nonmagnetic. The room-temperature structure is tetragonal I4/mcm. Although resistivity remains metallic, it develops a slope change below 25 K without a corresponding specific-heat anomaly or magnetic transition; susceptibility is paramagnetic from 2 to 300 K. Single-crystal X-ray diffraction at 22 K reveals weak commensurate satellites at q₁ = (1/2, 0, 1/2) and q₂ = (0, 1/2, 1/2), additional reflections violating I-centering, and a tiny tetragonal distortion. Refinement assigns the low-temperature structure to an acentric monoclinic X2 supercell, equivalent to C2, with doubled a and c axes and loss of fourfold rotational symmetry. Angle-dependent magnetoresistance confirms the transition from nearly isotropic fourfold behavior above 40 K to twofold anisotropy below 20 K.

First-principles calculations find no imaginary phonon modes, indicating that the parent tetragonal lattice is dynamically stable. Electronic bands and density of states contain flat bands and van Hove singularities away from the Fermi level, indicating relatively weak correlations. Parallel Fermi-surface contours and Lindhard susceptibility calculations identify electronic instabilities near the N and X points that could favor directional electronic redistribution and couple weakly to the lattice.

ARPES measurements broadly reproduce the calculated flower-like Fermi surface, although a predicted inner pocket is absent. Linear-horizontal polarization retains fourfold symmetry, whereas linear-vertical polarization produces strong anisotropy, suggesting an orbital-selective contribution, particularly from Co-dxy, consistent with electronically driven nematicity. Band dispersions also reveal type-I and type-II crossings that form a weakly spin-orbit-gapped nodal loop and indicate Dirac-like carriers near the Fermi level. Together, the results identify CoSn2 as a high-symmetry, nonmagnetic itinerant nodal-line semimetal and a platform for studying rotational symmetry breaking and nematicity in weakly correlated intermetallic compounds.

The paper develops a causal Bayesian network to support Alzheimer’s disease diagnosis by combining clinical knowledge with data. The interpretable model estimates both the probability that a person has suspected AD and the probability of receiving a formal diagnosis, addressing diagnostic uncertainty, misdiagnosis, and undiagnosed disease.

The network is structured using medical idioms and includes risk factors, signs and symptoms, cognitive and biomarker tests, other dementias, reversible conditions, comorbidities, complications, formal testing, and treatment. Variables follow validated NIA-AA criteria and are intended to support both early- and late-onset AD. Parameters were derived from literature, U.S. Census data, knowledge-based judgment, and the National Alzheimer’s Coordinating Center Uniform Data Set, covering visits at 46 Alzheimer’s Disease Centers from September 2005 to May 2022. The model was calibrated to an estimated AD prevalence of 3.336%.

Internal validation found that unobserved marginal probabilities matched this prevalence. Clinical scenarios demonstrated Bayesian updating, explaining-away effects, backward reasoning, and the ability to revise predictions as evidence is added. Examples included increasing suspected AD probability from 65% to 95% after positive biomarker results and distinguishing probable AD MCI from AD dementia using independence status.

The model is presented as a complementary, auditable clinical tool that supports what-if analyses but should not replace professional evaluation. Major limitations include simplified aggregation of non-AD causes of cognitive impairment, broad age categories, NACC selection biases, incomplete representation of undiagnosed and misdiagnosed cases, missing causal relationships, manually assigned parameters, and uneven NPT sample sizes. Future work should model individual dementia and reversible conditions more precisely, incorporate definitive autopsy data and fuller early-onset AD features, expand support for management interventions, and develop a separate research model incorporating preclinical AD.

A Houston Chronicle editorial criticized California officials for blaming Texas energy producers during the state’s electricity crisis and argued that Enron should have challenged California Attorney General Bill Lockyer’s remarks about Kenneth Lay.

Const. Ken Lam, the Toronto officer who apprehended the sole suspect in Monday’s vehicle attack, was praised for calmly de-escalating the confrontation without firing his gun. Video showed the suspect discarding an object and surrendering after Lam drew his weapon, holstered it and advanced with a baton. The encounter lasted 37 seconds, and police said the man was unarmed. The attack killed 10 people and injured 15. Police identified the suspect as Alek Minassian, 25, of Richmond Hill, Ont., and charged him with 10 counts of first-degree murder and 13 counts of attempted murder. Chief Mark Saunders credited Lam’s high-level training and minimal use of force. The arrest followed scrutiny of police tactics after the Sammy Yatim shooting and calls to expand Taser use and review force options.

Mexico has replaced Colombia as the Americas’ kidnapping hotspot, reporting about 1,000 cases annually, while a statistics institute estimated roughly 64,500 for 2015.

In Vansickle v. Brown, the Missouri Supreme Court affirmed a defense verdict in a malicious-prosecution action arising from Susan Ann Vansickle’s prosecution for obstructing a public highway. The court held that the arresting officer’s alleged mistreatment of her was inadmissible unless the defendant instigated it. It also excluded a later trespass judgment because it did not concern the road’s existence and postdated the arrest, and excluded county-court proceedings for opening a new road because they did not vacate the existing road.

The defendant’s testimony and evidence of verbal county-court directions were admissible to show good faith and lack of malice, though not to establish the road’s legality. A party may testify about material intentions underlying his conduct.

For liability, the plaintiff had to prove both malice and the absence of probable cause; malice could not be inferred as a matter of law from want of probable cause. Probable cause required the prosecutor to believe the accused was guilty on reasonable grounds. Voluntary waiver of examination and entry into a recognizance constituted prima facie evidence of probable cause. The court upheld the defendant’s instructions and found that the instructions as a whole favored the plaintiff. Judges Napton and Henry dissented in part.

The Tiered Memory Page Migration (TMPM) engine provides optional SEV/SNP extensions for copying memory pages and updating virtual-to-physical mappings. It supports tiered-memory optimization by moving frequently accessed data to faster memory and can safely migrate pages targeted by concurrent DMA by coordinating with IOMMU host page tables. It can also migrate guest pages protected by SNP that the hypervisor or operating system cannot directly access. Support is indicated by the PM_Status ENGINE_READY bit, and IOMMU enablement is required.

TMPM commands are submitted through a driver-managed ring buffer. PM_PAGE_MOVE_IO moves up to 128 I/O or hypervisor-owned pages, coordinates DMA and IOMMU invalidation, copies page contents, and updates IOMMU host page table entries. PM_PAGE_MOVE_GUEST moves up to 128 SNP guest pages whose sources are Guest-Valid or Guest-Invalid and whose destinations are in the newly defined Pre-Migration state. After migration, destination pages inherit the source state, while source pages become Pre-Migration. Pre-Migration pages use a platform-specific ASID, ignore the GPA, cannot be PVALIDATEd, and are restored to Hypervisor state through RMPUpdate. PM_GET_CAPABILITIES reports firmware capabilities, while PM_NOOP marks the end of command sequences.

Migration lists may contain nonadjacent pages and pages from multiple guests, with no ordering dependencies between entries or commands. Overall and per-page statuses distinguish complete success, partial success, and failure; PM_RMP_NOTEXCLUSIVE indicates that a migration may be retried. Commands operate on 4 KB-aligned pages; 2 MB pages must be broken into 4 KB pages or, for guest migration, must be physically contiguous and aligned. CPUs must be prevented from accessing migrating pages, and guest migration does not support concurrent DMA.

IOMMU data structures, vIOMMU page tables and pinned buffers, and TMPM ring-buffer or argument pages are not migratable. Best performance is reported with commands of at least 16 pages, peaking at 128 pages, while keeping the command queue supplied and using paced completion interrupts.

Firmware reload requires no in-flight operations, a paused and torn-down ring buffer, and disabled IOMMU PAGEMIGRATION_EN bits. The replacement firmware must be the same or a newer version, and ENGINE_READY must be checked before communication. Command, migration-list, ring-buffer, and hardware errors are reported through command statuses, PM_Status, and MCA; failures during a batch may make all pages in that batch unrecoverable.

This qualitative descriptive case study examined how South African Senior Phase Technology Education teachers understand and teach education for sustainable development (ESD). Data came from semi-structured interviews and non-participant classroom observations with eight Technology teachers in Ehlanzeni District, Mpumalanga, and were analysed inductively through content analysis and triangulation.

Teachers demonstrated substantial knowledge of ESD, including resource conservation, responsible technology use, renewable energy, societal well-being, and the historical sustainability of indigenous practices. However, these concepts were rarely integrated into actual lessons, with limited use of sustainability-related resources and few explicit links between technology activities and ESD. Teachers identified opportunities through processing and recycling, technology-driven environmental solutions, sustainable design, investigation of environmental impacts, and responsible consumption. Collaborative learning was identified as a particularly promising approach because it supports knowledge sharing, diverse perspectives, problem-solving, creativity, cross-cultural learning, indigenous knowledge, and environmental stewardship. Nevertheless, classroom teaching relied mainly on demonstrations and lectures rather than collaboration.

The study concludes that Technology Education can support sustainable development by connecting practical technological activity with environmental, social, and economic considerations. Recommendations include embedding ESD holistically across the curriculum, teaching responsible resource and energy use, incorporating sustainable design and manufacturing, using practical topics such as recycling and waste reduction, encouraging collaborative hands-on projects, and promoting critical discussion of technology’s societal and environmental effects. Further research should examine practical implementation, include other phases and regions, and combine qualitative and quantitative methods.

UK businesses should prioritize paying reasonable living wages and treating customers fairly over profits and dividends. Excessive delivery charges—such as charging remote customers more than overseas destinations—are illegal exploitation that should incur criminal charges rather than negotiated fee reductions or wage increases.

The CBC2 study protocol describes a phase 4, prospective, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial evaluating Thai cannabis oils in 90 women aged 18–70 with metastatic breast cancer who are receiving chemotherapy at King Chulalongkorn Memorial Hospital in Bangkok. Participants will be randomly allocated 1:1:1 to Ganja Oil, Metta Osot, or placebo oil and receive one bedtime dose daily for 90 days. The trial aims to assess quality of life, chemotherapy-related symptom burden using the Edmonton Symptom Assessment System, adverse effects, and changes in microbiome profiles, cytokines, bacterial metabolites, gut-to-blood microbial translocation markers, pharmacokinetics, and pharmacogenetics. Blood, saliva, stool, and skin samples will be collected before and after treatment, with safety assessments at baseline, day 30, and day 90 and an additional month of withdrawal monitoring. The rationale includes preliminary evidence for cannabinoid symptom relief, antitumor effects in experimental models, and links between microbial dysbiosis and breast cancer. Analyses will follow an intention-to-treat approach using distribution-appropriate statistical tests and measures of microbial alpha and beta diversity, with p<0.05 considered significant. The protocol was approved by the relevant institutional review board, and written informed consent and confidentiality are required.

Soccer position numbers originated in 1920s England, assigning numbers from the goalkeeper through fullbacks, halfbacks, and forwards in a 2-3-5 formation. With the 1950s “W-M” formation, the center halfback moved into defense as a center fullback, while the inside forwards dropped back, strengthening references to classic central “Number 9s” and attacking “Number 10s.” In the 1960s, Total Football blurred positional roles, and players increasingly chose numbers unrelated to specific positions. Beginning in 2012, U.S. Soccer standardized a 4-3-3-based numbering system and position profiles based on technical, tactical, physical, and mental attributes. Terms such as “False 9,” describing a center forward who drops into midfield, and “Double-9s,” referring to paired central strikers, have also emerged.

Jonathan Huberdeau scored 7.7 seconds before the third period ended, lifting Florida to a 3-2 win over Detroit. Aleksander Barkov and Aaron Ekblad also scored; Harri Sateri made 26 saves, while Detroit’s Danny DeKeyser scored twice.

A punter kicks the football after receiving the snap, typically when the offense cannot convert on third down. By controlling hang time, length, spin, accuracy, and touch, punters flip field position, pin opponents deep, and help the coverage team limit returns. They require leg strength, coordination, flexibility, creativity, and a delicate touch. NFL punters are generally smaller, slim athletes, listed at 5 feet 10 inches to 6 feet 2 inches and 180–210 pounds. Punters may also run or throw fake punts on fourth down and hold extra-point and field-goal attempts. A punt differs from a kick, which is used on extra points, field goals, and kickoffs. Because field position affects scoring opportunities, punting is an important, though often unglamorous, special-teams role. Shane Lechler holds the NFL record for the highest average yards per punt at 47.6, while Ray Guy was a first-round pick who won three Super Bowls with the Oakland Raiders and is honored by the Ray Guy Award.

The disclosure describes a cloud-computing microservices architecture and is a continuation of three earlier U.S. applications titled “Microservices Architecture.” It provides a configurable framework that exposes desired functions through a uniform microservices API, allowing host software to remain unaware of a function’s implementation, location, or underlying resources.

Microservice-capable resources—including local software, virtual machines or appliances, resource pools, FPGAs, ASICs, CPUs, and GPUs—register their capabilities and configuration details with a service discovery function. An ontological catalog stores service descriptions, API mappings, connection capabilities, telemetry, scaling information, and provisioning data. When a service is requested, a microservices driver queries the catalog, selects an available instance or provisions a new one, establishes addressing and forwarding, and translates standardized API calls into implementation-specific invocations.

The architecture supports dynamic chaining of microservices through message forwarders, allowing messages to pass directly between service instances without repeated returns to host software. It includes path-based addressing, active-message flows, shared-memory and RDMA access, queue redirection, overflow notifications, and load-balancing options such as weighted fair queuing, round-robin, deadline-based routing, and “hot potato” forwarding. An extensible service-description language can specify functions, parameters, performance constraints, and chains.

The passage also describes cloud data-center infrastructure, including workload clusters, switching fabrics, orchestrators, processor nodes, distributed memory and storage servers, hypervisors, virtual networks, and service-function chains. Computing platforms may include manageability engines that collect hardware telemetry, including resource-stress information, and support workload allocation. Example implementations focus on registering microservice accelerators, cataloging their capabilities, enabling service-chain allocation, mapping API calls to native invocations, and provisioning programmed FPGA instances.

Studies show millennials save for retirement but remain wary of stock investing. A Harris Poll found 71% save for retirement and began at a median age of 24, while Fidelity projected they are on track to replace 78% of retirement expenses. Yet 42% invest conservatively, 25% hold investments in cash, and many younger adults find stock investing intimidating. The article links some caution to the 2008–09 financial crisis and notes that the S&P 500 averaged a 7.92% inflation-adjusted annual return from 2007–2017, while money market returns have remained below 0.3%. Experts cited say avoiding stocks may put retirement security at risk and recommend accepting some risk for long-term goals.

CME launched the Micro E-mini S&P 500 Index futures in 2019 to give retail traders with smaller accounts access to the S&P 500 futures market. The contract, symbol MES, is one-tenth the size of the E-mini S&P 500 and trades electronically on CME Globex. One unit equals the index value multiplied by $5; its minimum price fluctuation is 0.25 index points, or $1.25. Quarterly March, June, September, and December contracts are listed for five consecutive quarters, cash-settled at expiration, and generally terminate at 9:30 a.m. ET on the third Friday of the contract month. The contract is not eligible for block trades.

Trading runs Sunday through Friday, with a daily maintenance break from 5:00 p.m. to 6:00 p.m. ET from Monday through Thursday. Traders need a futures broker, must fund an account, and may trade with margin, stated as $1,060. Leverage creates substantial risk because losses are based on the full contract value rather than the margin posted; a 20% loss could result from a 1% adverse move. CFD versions are also offered by some forex brokers and do not expire.

A trading strategy for the contract may combine technical and fundamental analysis, precise entry and exit rules, position sizing, and risk management. The described mean-reversion strategy is paywalled and was backtested on the E-mini rather than the newer Micro contract using daily CME data, with no risk-management parameters. Historically, S&P 500 futures have performed better in winter and spring than in summer.

The contract’s all-time high was 4808.25 in January 2022, while its lowest level since launch was 2174.00 in March 2020. It traded at 3959.50 on December 9, 2022, making one contract worth $19,797.50 at that quote.

An email dated May 18, 2001 compiles news reports on Enron, the Bush administration’s energy policy, and their political connections. The Wall Street Journal describes Enron’s transformation into a leading gas and electricity trader and its extensive lobbying for open transmission systems, interstate markets, and reduced regulatory barriers. It details Kenneth Lay’s access to Vice President Dick Cheney, Enron’s political donations and ties to officials, lobbying surrounding FERC nominees, rapid trading growth, and concerns that Western electricity price increases could lead to renewed price controls.

The Los Angeles Times reports that the administration’s plan favors oil, gas, coal, nuclear power, construction companies, and labor unions through expanded production and infrastructure, while providing limited support for renewable energy and conservation. Consumers were expected to receive little immediate relief, and environmentalists criticized the plan’s failure to address carbon emissions and global warming. Reuters likewise records support from much of the energy industry, criticism from California officials and Democrats, and environmental protests.

Japanese utility leaders opposed Enron’s proposal to separate electricity generation, transmission, and distribution, fearing California-style supply failures and a lack of accountability; Enron argued that liberalization would increase competition and reduce manufacturers’ costs. Agence France-Presse highlighted major energy-industry political donations and ties to Bush administration officials. Enron was also reported to be withdrawing from the Dolphin gas project in the UAE, citing a new business model and low profit margins. Separately, the Times of India described strong Mumbai property demand as companies relocated to western suburbs, including Enron’s lease of 100,000 square feet of office space.

Janata Congress Chhattisgarh announced 11 candidates for next year’s Chhattisgarh assembly elections. Ajit Jogi said six sitting MLAs were finalized but withheld, with tickets also planned for 7–8 core committee members. Jogi cited farmers, women, unemployment and Naxalites as key issues. BJP’s Sunil Soni called the list a Congress “B team” and said BJP was eyeing 65-plus seats. Observers said Jogi’s early announcement sought to surprise rivals and divert attention from his fake caste certificate case.

He credits their success to playing their own game without fearing defeat, after previously giving opponents too much respect. Players are enjoying close games, while he focuses on each shot and embraces overtime.

Newspaper clippings from July 17, 2001, document California’s electricity crisis and related national politics. Gov. Gray Davis expanded state involvement by purchasing power, committing $45–$50 billion to long-term contracts, taking control of the grid operator, creating a state power authority and pursuing utility transmission assets. Long-term contracts lowered wholesale prices, but critics warned of reduced oversight, restricted consumer choice and long-term costs to ratepayers. A forecast projected state economic output losses of $90 billion by 2005.

California’s first of 10 planned “peaker” plants opened in Otay Mesa, producing 90 megawatts after a 90-day construction effort. Meanwhile, competing plans to rescue Southern California Edison stalled amid disputes over state acquisition of its transmission system, ratepayer costs and restrictions on direct-access electricity contracts. PG&E had entered bankruptcy.

State energy consultants faced scrutiny over stock holdings in power companies and delayed financial disclosures. Southern California Edison also partnered with churches to enroll low-income customers in a 20% bill discount and rate-increase exemption program.

The Bush administration promoted its national energy plan through Vice President Dick Cheney and other officials, emphasizing conservation, new production and reduced foreign-oil dependence, while Democrats criticized the outreach and conservation funding.

California regulators delayed a report on whether customers faced another rate increase to help finance a $13.4 billion state bond issue, despite two increases already approved and falling wholesale electricity costs.

Google laid off more than 100 employees in design-related roles within its cloud unit, following earlier cuts to quantitative user experience research, platform and service experience, and adjacent teams. Many affected roles are U.S.-based, some design teams have been halved, and employees have until early December to find internal positions. The cuts come as Google reduces headcount and prioritizes AI, offering buyouts across several U.S. units and encouraging greater AI use. Google says it needs to become more efficient as it scales and did not immediately respond to CNBC’s request for comment.

China’s official manufacturing PMI rose to 49.8 in September, showing a smaller-than-expected contraction and the strongest reading since March, though it remained below the growth threshold. RatingDog’s private manufacturing PMI reached 51.2, above the 50.2 forecast and its highest since May. The official non-manufacturing PMI slipped to 52.9 from 53, while RatingDog’s services PMI eased to 50 from 50.3. The manufacturing slowdown reflected weak domestic demand, curbs on industrial overcapacity and export disruptions, including higher U.S. tariffs. An October Politburo meeting is expected to clarify Beijing’s policy response. Economist Zhiwei Zhang said the government may tolerate a second-half slowdown if growth remains sufficient to preserve the full-year 5% target.

The MOVE Index, created by Merrill Lynch in 1998 and acquired by ICE in 2019, measures U.S. interest-rate volatility through implied volatility in one-month OTC options and is often called the bond market’s VIX. It surged from 120 to 199 in March amid rapid Federal Reserve rate hikes and banking concerns, before falling to 118.

A backtest beginning in 2002 held TLT when MOVE was below its historical average and sold when it exceeded that average. The strategy modestly reduced volatility and cut maximum drawdown to roughly half that of buy-and-hold, but was not highly profitable and hurt 2008 returns. Overall, MOVE effectively indicates bond-market volatility but does not reliably signal good times to buy bonds.

NVIDIA Corporation filed a Form 8-K on November 15, 2018, reporting results for the quarter ended October 28, 2018. The filing furnished a fiscal 2019 third-quarter earnings press release and CFO Colette M. Kress’s commentary as Exhibits 99.1 and 99.2. These materials were not deemed filed, carried specified securities-law liabilities, or authorized incorporation by reference into other SEC filings.

Soccer vision is the ability to see, understand, and respond to positioning, movement, and available options on the field. The passage emphasizes that ball skills alone are insufficient for elite play; players must develop spatial awareness, quick decision-making, and awareness of teammates and opponents. Coaches recommend constantly scanning the field, raising the head quickly after controlling the ball, keeping eyes and body moving, recognizing peripheral information, anticipating defensive threats, and identifying passing or attacking options. Players should communicate what they see using team oral and non-verbal signals. Practical techniques include receiving the ball with the foot opposite the pass, playing the first touch away from the body, and using visualization to improve on-field vision. A drill in a 30-by-40-meter grid has players in different-colored jerseys exchange two-touch passes while scanning for the appropriate receiver, varying pass distances, and eventually progressing to one-touch passing without calling for the ball.

NatWest and The Future Laboratory identified eight rising fraud trends, including smartphone malware, fake FIFA World Cup ticket sites, social-media spying, “Brexit-proof” investments, money mules, fake wedding websites, dating-site catfishing, and impersonated solicitors. They cited over £100 million in UK banking fraud in the first half of 2017 and advised updating security software and verifying requests for personal information.

On March 15, 2021, NVIDIA Corporation’s Compensation Committee adopted its Fiscal Year 2022 Variable Compensation Plan, allowing eligible executive officers to earn variable cash compensation based on achievement of specified fiscal 2022 revenue goals, with threshold, base, and stretch operating-plan levels. The fiscal year ends January 30, 2022. Unless otherwise determined by the committee, participants must remain employees through the payment date. At base-plan achievement, target awards were $2 million for CEO Jen-Hsun Huang, $300,000 for CFO Colette Kress, $650,000 for Ajay Puri, and $250,000 each for Debora Shoquist and Timothy Teter. A Citizen experiment found that academics who engage with fake science conferences or publishers may be repeatedly targeted by other scammers. Researchers submitted absurd papers about ocean-bottom birds and flying pigs to OMICS International, which offered presentation slots for fees and was later exposed. The researchers then received unsolicited journal invitations referencing their fake bird paper and a nonexistent paper submitted to an earlier fake journal. These solicitations included the author’s misspelled name and contact details. The experiment showed that even unpublished submissions and personal information can circulate among predatory publishers, leading to repeated solicitations.

Gianluca Vialli says Juventus must prevent Camp Nou’s atmosphere from growing against Barcelona, recalling Chelsea’s 5–1 extra-time loss there in 2000. He praises Juventus’s first-leg display, Buffon’s saves and the team’s physical and mental strength, while highlighting Sergio Busquets and Lionel Messi as threats. Vialli urges compact defending, effective transitions and ruthless attacking.

Pakistan’s Statistics Bureau aims to complete rebasing inflation indices by June 2018, using surveys and manufacturing-industry data; the new base may apply in fiscal year 2018-19. Delayed by the population census, it will replace the obsolete 2007-08 base and add rural, urban and total CPI measures.

VentureWire’s June 6, 2001 edition reported major technology, venture-capital and corporate developments. Napster agreed to license MusicNet’s technology and music catalog and sell the music through a subscription service under its own brand, subject to legal and security requirements stemming from an earlier copyright suit. Comdisco Ventures CEO James P. Labe resigned as the venture unit wound down, stopped new investments and cut 15% of its staff amid broader restructuring at Comdisco. Charter Growth Capital became Focus Ventures without changing its staff or investment strategy; its $465 million second fund had about $200 million committed.
