DAWN-plasma is a phase 2, multicenter, randomized, open-label trial comparing best supportive care plus convalescent plasma with supportive care alone in hospitalized adults with COVID-19. It was designed to test whether early, high-volume plasma with high neutralizing-antibody titers would reduce the need for mechanical ventilation. Prior studies of convalescent plasma had shown inconsistent findings or no mortality benefit.

The protocol and consent documentation were approved by independent ethics committees at participating centers, and the study followed the Declaration of Helsinki and ICH Good Clinical Practice guidelines. Signed informed consent was required before enrollment; verbal consent with a witness was permitted under transmission-control restrictions.

The primary objective was to evaluate the efficacy and safety of convalescent plasma plus supportive care. The primary endpoint was the percentage of patients alive without mechanical ventilation at Day 15. Secondary endpoints assessed WHO clinical status, sustained clinical improvement or discharge, mechanical ventilation or death at 30 and 90 days, venous thromboembolism, transfusion reactions, plasma antibody titers, safety, quality of life, laboratory data, and vital signs. Exploratory endpoints included SARS-CoV-2 PCR, NT50 measurements, and outcomes according to pre-existing COVID-19 antibodies.

Eligible participants were adults with confirmed SARS-CoV-2 infection and radiographic infiltrates or clinical findings including rales and oxygen saturation of 94% or lower. Exclusions included mechanical ventilation before randomization, conditions posing unacceptable safety risks, prior grade 3 plasma allergy, treatment restrictions prohibiting intubation, and recent anti-CD20 therapy.

Participants were computer-randomized 2:1 to plasma plus supportive care or supportive care alone, while the trial statistician remained blinded until database lock. Plasma patients received 800–1,000 mL in four 200–250 mL doses: two units within 12 hours of randomization and two more 24–36 hours after the first infusion ended. Plasma below a 1/160 neutralizing titer was prohibited. Median time to first transfusion was five hours, and median plasma volume was 884 mL; 80.7% of units had titers of at least 1/320.

Between May 2020 and January 2021, 499 patients were assessed and 489 were randomized: 326 to plasma and 163 to control. The Day 15 visit was completed by 434 patients and the Day 30 visit by 423. Baseline characteristics were well matched, and concomitant COVID-19 therapy was similar between groups.

The Full Analysis Set was primary, with the Per Protocol Set used for sensitivity analysis. Six randomized patients were excluded from the Full Analysis Set: one lacked confirmed SARS-CoV-2 infection and five withdrew immediately after randomization without treatment or post-baseline data. The Per Protocol Set excluded 26 plasma-assigned patients who received fewer than four units and three control patients who received plasma before Day 30. Six plasma patients in the Full Analysis Set received no plasma, while 294 (91.9%) received all four units.

The article argues that XLP, the Consumer Staples Select Sector SPDR Fund, is an underappreciated trading vehicle. Tracking major consumer staples in the S&P 500, it consists of large-cap, low-volatility companies and is rebalanced quarterly. XLP has few sudden moves, tends to mean-revert, and has lower correlation with SPY and QQQ, making it useful for diversification and hedging. Three short strategies produced 418 backtested trades, a 75% win rate, an average gain of about 0.4% before costs, and a 2.35 profit factor. The article notes that mean-reversion strategies can have a few large losers, but XLP’s low volatility has limited such losses so far. It also mentions two long-side trading edges, more than 60 free trading strategies, and approaches including Rubber Band, Internal Bar Strength, and daily-performance-based consumer-stock strategies.

Derbyshire Times readers rallied around 33-year-old Chesterfield resident Craig Burr after he threatened to jump onto the A617 Hasland bypass. Taken to hospital and later released, Burr spoke publicly about his mental illness and received numerous messages of support. The paper’s “You Are Not Alone” campaign will continue contacting him. NHS advice urges people experiencing depression, anxiety, self-harm or suicidal thoughts to seek immediate help, including contacting the Samaritans on 116 123.

Effective diversification combines investments whose returns respond differently to market conditions, reducing overall portfolio risk. It requires considering asset characteristics, financial goals, investment horizon, liquidity needs, and diversification within asset classes. Five common mistakes are:

- Failing to count all holdings, including retirement funds and stock options, which can distort asset allocation.
- Holding too many investments, which dilifies diversification, raises costs, reduces exposure to strong performers, and makes monitoring difficult.
- Buying investments without understanding them, which increases risk; advisers or mutual funds may help, but investors should still understand available assets.
- Losing sight of financial goals, including income and liquidity requirements, which can make asset allocation unsuitable.
- Allowing allocation to drift as investments perform differently; portfolios should be assessed and rebalanced periodically.

Within equities, diversification may include market capitalization and sectors; within debt, it may include issuer credit profiles and tenors.

The speaker defends acquiring Holik in exchange for Brian Rolston, citing Holik’s ability under pressure and the team’s success since his return, including reaching the Stanley Cup Finals. Despite a recent loss, the team remains confident after strong responses in the previous two playoff series. They must adjust to outdoor ice, respect an opponent with a strong home record, and win a game to regain home-ice advantage.

The passage evaluates a SPY day-trading strategy that buys weakness or sells strength based on the final hour of trading, entering at the next day’s open and exiting at 11:30 a.m. Results from January 2010 to August 2012 include accumulated returns, trade and winning-trade counts, and average returns. Targets and stop-losses did not improve performance, while buying at the close produced similar results but larger drawdowns.

The study addresses higher education’s abrupt transition to remote teaching during the Covid-19 pandemic and the resulting infrastructure, data-protection, adaptation, communication, assessment, and exam-security challenges. It reviews synchronous, asynchronous, interactive, and passive distance-education models, along with platforms such as Moodle, edX, Coursera, and Google Suite.

The researchers developed and evaluated UZEP, a cloud-based synchronous distance-education platform using the Education as a Service model. UZEP requires no client installation or university-owned infrastructure and can be deployed quickly through interfaces with existing university management systems. Its modules include learning management, virtual classrooms, online examinations, homework and projects, digital-material sharing, announcements, surveys, and reporting. The virtual classroom integrates BigBlueButton with load balancing, while the examination module supports multiple question formats, equivalent question sets, randomization, monitoring, logging, and analysis of results.

UZEP was tested from Fall 2020 through February 2021 at 12 Turkish universities, with weekly feedback from university representatives. Expert, pilot, administrator, lecturer, and student evaluations found the platform easy to learn and use, rapidly deployable, functionally adequate, and useful for emergency distance education. Administrators generally rated it above the midpoint, with its ease of use, extensibility, and support rated most highly. Lecturers rated the virtual classroom highest, followed by assessment and the LMS. Students reported positive but moderate satisfaction and requested stronger social communication, easier instructor access, and improved assessment.

Compared with Moodle, edX, and Google Suite, UZEP’s integrated, scalable structure was considered well suited to higher-education emergencies. However, experts identified missing communication and social tools, limited group work and coursework grading, fewer reporting outputs, and no learning-analytics module. The study notes limitations from self-reported questionnaires, comparison with only four platforms, and evaluation during the pandemic. Planned improvements include stronger exam and assessment functions, AI-assisted exam security and evaluation, learning analytics, and interactive communication and learning environments.
AOL announced that AOL Instant Messenger (AIM) would be discontinued on December 15. The company called it culturally influential, while users shared nostalgia under #AIMmemories.

The disclosure describes apparatus and methods for assessing tissue viability and burn depth around wounds using electrical measurements, particularly capacitance measurements converted into sub-epidermal moisture (SEM) values. It addresses the difficulty of visually identifying non-viable tissue and determining burn depth in wounds that may change over time.

A toroidal bioimpedance sensor is described with a center electrode surrounded by a ring electrode. Electrode geometry can vary the sensing field’s depth. Electrode arrays may also be selectively interconnected to form virtual center-and-ring or two-electrode capacitive sensors. Flexible SEM-sensing substrates can incorporate sensors, color-coded visual indicators, marking elements, and perforations. Another mapping apparatus uses a movable SEM sensor, camera, fiducial, and projector to display tissue-condition boundaries over a wound.

Methods convert measured capacitance into SEM values and compare those values with reference, peak, or predetermined thresholds to identify tissue boundaries. For burns, the disclosure describes a necrotic central zone, an adjacent zone of stasis with reduced perfusion and elevated SEM, and an outer hyperaemia zone with increased but lower edema. SEM patterns and their changes can indicate damage depth, tissue recovery potential, and severity of reperfusion injury. Burn depth may also be determined by comparing capacitance differences or SEM values against stored data associating such measurements with known burn depths.

Visual indicators, projected markings, printed overlays, and stored measurement histories can indicate viable and non-viable regions, the edge of necrotic tissue, and other tissue-condition boundaries. Repeated SEM measurements may be taken at intervals to track injury progression, wound healing, response to therapy, recurrence risk, and tissue recovery relative to nearby healthy tissue.

Additional measurement methods define body regions and sampling patterns, calculate delta values between readings, and apply numerical, chronological, or trend-based thresholds that can trigger alerts. Quality metrics may assess repeatability, clinician consistency, and measurements over healthy tissue. Capacitance measurements may be calibrated against a reference SEM scanner. The disclosed sensing and mapping approaches are described as applicable to burns, cuts, ulcers, gangrene, pressure ulcers, and other tissue injuries.

On December 29, 2020, Apple Inc. announced that its Board appointed Monica Lozano as a non-employee director effective January 4, 2021. She will serve on the Board’s Audit and Finance Committee and receive a $100,000 annual retainer paid quarterly. On her effective date, she received an automatic initial grant of 281 restricted stock units under Apple’s Non-Employee Director Stock Plan. Apple will also enter into its standard indemnification agreement with Lozano. No reportable transactions exist between Apple and Lozano under Item 404(a) of Regulation S-K.

Wound Care Advantage, Dr. David G. Armstrong, the Southwestern Academic Limb Salvage Alliance (SALSA), and Gen1 Research launched Advanced Discovery, an investigative alliance focused on evidence-based wound care. It will evaluate diagnostic and treatment approaches through international wound and hyperbaric treatment centers to improve healing and reduce costs, with Gen1 providing administrative and research support.

The initiative will use de-identified data from more than 42,000 patients and 880,000 wound assessments collected over 16 years, along with data from SALSA. The announcement states that chronic wounds affect about 5.7 million U.S. patients and cost over $20 billion annually, with the burden increasing due to diabetes, vascular disease, population aging, and rising healthcare costs. It also reports that diabetic foot ulcers cost more than the five costliest cancers and twice as much to Medicare as diabetes alone.

The passage describes a continuation patent application claiming priority to U.S. Provisional Application No. 62/334,529 and National Stage entry under 35 U.S.C. § 371. It discloses systems, methods, and WTRU procedures for low-latency MAC PDU assembly in wireless systems such as 5gFLEX.

A WTRU may receive or determine transmission parameters before an uplink grant, including modulation and coding schemes, resource ranges, HARQ parameters, transport-block sizes, and PHY resource mappings. Parameters may be signaled by the network, selected through blind decoding or DCI reception, or determined from measurements such as SNR, CQI, ACK/NACK frequency, and reference-signal measurements. These procedures permit RLC segmentation, MAC multiplexing, CRC insertion, coding, modulation, and transport-block preparation before a grant is received, reducing grant-to-transmission latency.

The WTRU may incrementally create fixed-size data blocks as data arrives, select configured block sizes, segment higher-layer SDUs, and add headers describing block counts, sizes, flows, logical channels, services, and control information. Upon receiving a grant, it may select and multiplex prepared blocks according to flow, logical-channel, service, QoS, TTL, packet relationships, and grant restrictions, while minimizing the difference between grant size and transport-block size. The WTRU may also signal block or transport-block sizes through scheduling requests, buffer-status reports, random-access messages, coarse size levels, or implicitly through CRC values.

A disclosed WTRU procedure monitors downlink-control-channel resources, identifies and decodes DCI scheduling uplink or downlink data, determines decoding parameters such as CRC length, aggregation level, robustness, format, or searched CCE subset, and derives transmission or reception parameters from them. Such parameters may include QoS, spectrum operation mode, HARQ feedback information, MCS, PRBs, power, timing, and TTI duration. The WTRU may transmit HARQ-ACK feedback using resources associated with the decoding parameter, and the network may configure mappings between decoding parameters and transmission or reception parameters.

The background describes multiple-access communications systems containing WTRUs, base stations, radio access networks, core networks, and external networks, including implementations using UTRA, E-UTRA/LTE, IEEE 802.16, IEEE 802.11, and other radio technologies. It also discusses 5G use cases such as broadband, industrial control, V2X, and massive machine-type communications, with ultra-low latency, high reliability, high mobility, narrowband operation, long battery life, and low-rate communications. 5gFLEX is described as supporting flexible spectrum, bandwidth, carrier aggregation, variable TTI lengths, TDD and FDD, supplemental downlink, and licensed and unlicensed operation.

The passage further describes OFDM-based and filtered multicarrier waveforms, including OFDM-OQAM and UF-OFDM, waveform coexistence, Spectrum Operation Modes, network- and WTRU-based scheduling, opportunistic and contention-based access, QoS-based multiplexing, system signatures and access tables, and broader definitions for logical channels, logical channel groups, and transport channels. It also describes transport blocks containing separately protected data blocks, configurable ACK/NACK thresholds, and aggregated data-block status feedback for rapid retransmission signaling.

Plaintiffs, union boards and benefit funds, sued Waterworks, Inc. under ERISA § 502 to compel an audit. Both parties moved for summary judgment. The court denied the motions because material facts remained disputed over what agreement was reached during a 2004 meeting and whether Waterworks’ subsequent conduct demonstrated an intent to be bound by the union’s collective bargaining agreement.

Waterworks submitted contribution reports consistent with the CBA and trust agreements but never signed their “Warranty and Acceptance” clauses. Plaintiffs argued this conduct manifested assent to the CBA, while Waterworks maintained that an oral arrangement permitted union-rate payments and apprenticeship participation without CBA obligations. The court found the LMRA’s prohibition on employer payments without a written agreement did not compel plaintiffs’ interpretation because Waterworks disputed that such an agreement existed. It also found plaintiffs’ newly raised argument concerning the union representative’s authority was waived and, alternatively, raised a factual issue.

CompareCards highlights credit cards offering 0% introductory APRs lasting 12 to 21 months, which can help consumers carrying high-interest balances or making large purchases. Featured options include:

- A Discover card with 15 months of 0% APR on purchases and balance transfers, 5% rotating-category cash back, unlimited 1% elsewhere, a first-year cash-back match, and no annual fee.

- Capital One Quicksilver and VentureOne cards with 15-month 0% APR offers, $300 welcome bonuses, no annual or foreign-transaction fees, and elevated travel rewards.

After promotional periods, cards revert to regular variable APRs, and some balance transfers carry fees or earn no rewards. NVIDIA Corporation’s Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended January 30, 2022 describes a company centered on GPU-based accelerated computing, with its GPU and CUDA software supporting gaming, artificial intelligence, high-performance and scientific computing, data centers, professional visualization, autonomous vehicles, robotics, and virtual worlds. NVIDIA reports two segments: Graphics, covering GeForce, GeForce NOW, RTX, vGPU, automotive infotainment, and Omniverse; and Compute & Networking, covering data-center platforms, Mellanox networking, automotive AI and autonomous-driving solutions, cryptocurrency processors, Jetson, and enterprise software. Its four principal markets are Gaming, Data Center, Professional Visualization, and Automotive.

The company follows a unified hardware-and-software platform strategy, supported by more than $29 billion invested in research and development since its inception and nearly three million CUDA and related software developers. It operates a fabless manufacturing model, relying on foundries, contract manufacturers, assembly and testing providers, memory suppliers, and other third parties. Competition includes AMD, Intel, internal silicon initiatives at major technology companies, automotive and embedded-chip suppliers, and networking vendors. NVIDIA protects its intellectual property through patents, trademarks, trade secrets, confidentiality agreements, and licensing arrangements.

NVIDIA and SoftBank terminated NVIDIA’s proposed acquisition of Arm on February 8, 2022, because significant regulatory challenges prevented completion. NVIDIA expects a $1.36 billion operating-expense charge in the first quarter of fiscal 2023 for the related prepayment write-off.

The filing also describes NVIDIA’s ESG and human-capital practices, including a goal to match 100% of global electricity consumption with renewable energy by the end of fiscal 2025, plans for the Earth-2 climate supercomputer, and 22,473 employees across 32 countries as of January 30, 2022.

Principal risks include rapidly changing markets and standards, intensifying competition, demand-forecasting uncertainty, supply shortages and long manufacturing lead times, reliance on third-party manufacturers, product defects, global operating and climate-related disruptions, acquisition integration and regulatory challenges, and cybersecurity incidents. Following unauthorized network access disclosed on February 23, 2022, threat actors obtained and leaked some NVIDIA source code and proprietary information.

Sungi Cho, a former Army Black Hawk pilot and West Point mechanical engineering graduate, developed a 3D-printed plastic hook after identifying difficulties organizing soldiers’ gear in barracks. After positive feedback from fellow soldiers, he founded the Warbelt Hanger business, initially selling the $10.99 product online and expanding its customer base to law enforcement.

Cho later developed the $10.99 MOLLE Backer, a mounting base compatible with hard and soft MOLLE systems. Demand from military, law enforcement, outdoor, and trades users stabilized at about 1,800 units per month, prompting him to consider replacing 3D printing with injection molding while pursuing an MBA at MIT Sloan.

The case compares costs and capacity for both methods. Ten 3D printers can produce 180 saleable units each monthly, while a third-party injection-molder can produce 1,800 units in a nine-hour run. Material costs are $0.50 per printed unit versus $0.20 per molded unit, with scrap costs of $0.09 and $0.006, respectively. Common costs include $0.48 for inserts, $0.50 for screws, and $0.11 for packaging, while printing adds $0.04 for electricity. The manufacturer charges $0.75 per molded base, excluding inserts. Labor totals 56 hours monthly at $20 per hour. The initial capital requirement is $11,487 for a mold versus $1,716 for a printer, and outsourcing, mold investment, and other nonfinancial considerations remained unresolved.

The Sansa Fuze manual advises that “unknown artist/album” usually results from missing ID3 tags or WMA metadata; song details can be entered through the computer’s Properties > Summary > Advanced tab. The player supports reading and writing microSD and microSDHC cards and can be reset by holding the power button up for about 10 seconds.

SanDisk Technical Support can be reached at 1-866-726-3475 or through its online support request form. Support information, how-to videos, and the Sansa Firmware Updater are available on SanDisk’s website.

Warranty service requires contacting SanDisk and returning the product as instructed. SanDisk may repair, replace, or refund the product, and liability is limited to the purchase price. It prohibits modification, reverse engineering, unauthorized copying, distribution, and separation of the software. The software is provided “as is,” carries restricted government-use rights, may be transferred only as an integrated part of a sold SanDisk product, and may be terminated for license violations. Options trading in EEM can provide market exposure and potential profits in rising or falling markets, while also offering leverage and lower contract costs than buying the underlying asset. However, it is complex and carries substantial risks, including losses from adverse market moves, time decay, liquidity problems, and volatility. Leverage can magnify both profits and losses, and beginners are advised against using it and to maintain a margin of safety.

Potential profit or loss should be calculated by comparing the option’s purchase or sale price with its exercise price while accounting for fees and commissions. The Black-Scholes model can support this analysis by considering the underlying asset’s price, time to expiration, strike price, and implied volatility. Technical tools such as trendlines, support and resistance levels, and chart patterns can supplement pricing analysis. Delta measures how an option’s price may change with a one-point move in the underlying asset and can help assess or adjust risk.

Common strategies include long calls and puts, covered calls and puts, straddles, strangles, collars, and butterfly spreads. Hedging through offsetting positions can reduce potential losses. Effective risk management also involves appropriate position sizing, stop-loss levels, and analysis before entering trades, although the passage notes that stop losses may work better in theory than in practice. Backtesting is recommended to assess whether a strategy has a positive statistical edge.

Costs, minimum deposits, and margin requirements vary by broker and contract. Minimum deposits are generally stated as $500–$2,000, while margins range from 10%–50%. Actively traded contracts generally have tighter bid-ask spreads. Traders should select reputable brokers based on fees, service, interface, liquidity, spreads, deposit requirements, and margin terms. The options chain displays contract prices, bids and asks, implied volatility, and delta. Expiration generally falls on the third Friday of the contract’s expiration month. Tax treatment varies by country and may include capital-gains tax, stamp duty, or local taxes.

The ADS868xW provides programmable high- and low-limit alarms for analog inputs. The input thresholds are independently programmable and share adjustable hysteresis; the high alarm sets above its threshold and resets at or below the lower limit, while the low alarm sets below its threshold and resets at or above the upper limit. A separate AVDD alarm uses fixed typical trip points of 5.3 V for high voltage and 4.7 V for low voltage.

The device uses a multiSPI interface containing input and output shift registers, configuration registers, and a protocol unit, presenting a 32-bit input-output shift register to the host. Supported host connections include a single device with standard SPI pins and multiple devices connected in a daisy chain. In a daisy chain, all devices share CONVST/CS and SCLK, each device must have identical configuration, and an optimal frame contains 32 × N SCLK capture edges for N devices. Data are received from the last device backward through the chain.

The device operates in RESET, ACQ, and CONV states. The active-low RST pin supports either an application reset, which restores configuration registers, or a power-on reset, which also resets internal circuitry such as the PGA, ADC driver, and reference. A CONVST/CS rising edge initiates conversion from ACQ state; conversion ends in ACQ state, and RVS can signal completion. ACQ state supports a low-power NAP mode.

Programming uses nine configuration registers and supports data-read and data-write operations. A transfer frame begins with the falling edge of CONVST/CS and ends with its rising edge. An optimal frame contains 32 SCLK cycles, a short frame cannot contain a valid write but can provide selected output bits, and a long frame uses the final 32 shifted input bits as the command. Supported commands include 32-bit byte and half-word reads, writes, and bit set and clear operations; half-word commands ignore the least significant address bit.

Output data in the next frame depends on the preceding command and DATA_VAL setting. It can contain fixed test data, register data, or the latest 16-bit conversion result. Optional appended flags include device address, input range, AVDD alarms, input alarms, and parity. Four legacy SPI-compatible protocols are available for writes and reads, with SPI-00-S used after power-up or reset and alternatives selected through SDI_CTL_REG. Reads support single- or dual-SDO operation. Source-synchronous protocols can use an internal or external clock and single- or dual-bit output buses; RVS supplies the synchronous output clock in these modes.

The configuration registers provide device identification for daisy-chain systems, reset and power controls, SPI and SDO protocol selection, output-data formatting, input-range and reference configuration, alarm status flags, and input-alarm thresholds and hysteresis.

An industrial analog-input module combines an ADS8681W with an eight-channel MUX36D08 to support software-configured voltage or current channels, including bipolar and unipolar industrial ranges. The design demonstrates programmable input alarms and hysteresis for NTC thermistor temperature monitoring. Separate AVDD and DVDD supplies are recommended, with close supply decoupling to improve power-supply rejection. NAP mode reduces consumption between conversions, while power-down mode disables analog blocks while retaining the interface and registers. PCB guidance emphasizes separating analog and digital routing, keeping bypass and reference capacitors close to their pins, using short ground paths, and avoiding vias between supply pins and their capacitors.

On November 15, 2000, the court temporarily suspended attorney E. Nkem Odinkemere from practicing, restrained disbursement of funds in his New Jersey financial accounts, enjoined him from practicing, and required compliance with rules for suspended attorneys.
More heavy snow is forecast for Maine, New Hampshire, and Vermont over the next 48 hours, while Connecticut will likely see only a dusting. Some northern areas already have over two feet of snow.

Of 647 affected platforms, 551 were restarting, while passport, welfare and some administrative services remained unavailable. Authorities called for stronger safeguards, redundancy and disaster preparedness.
Amazon.com, Inc. reported that Rosalind G. Brewer resigned from its Board of Directors effective February 16, 2021.

A retrospective study of 266 patients with pathologically confirmed glioblastoma evaluated whether diffusion-weighted MRI (DWI) and apparent diffusion coefficient (ADC) maps could predict pTERT mutation status using a 50-layer ResNet. Conventional structural MRI models achieved accuracies of 50.10–51.91% and AUCs of 0.527–0.571. DWI alone achieved 54.58% accuracy and an AUC of 0.626, ADC maps achieved 78.63% accuracy and an AUC of 0.865, and combined DWI plus ADC data performed best, with 85.20% slice-level accuracy, an AUC of 0.934, and 86.6% patient-level accuracy. The entire-tumor region of interest outperformed tumor-core and enhanced-tumor regions. Age, necrosis volume, and tumor location were associated with mutation status, but an SVM model using these clinical features achieved only 70.91% accuracy and did not improve the DWI-plus-ADC ResNet model. The study was limited by its retrospective design, small sample, reliance on cross-sectional slices, and focus only on postoperative WHO grade IV glioblastoma.

This protocol describes a scoping review examining antipsychotic-induced metabolic syndrome (MS) in community-dwelling adults. Approximately 40%–80% of people prescribed antipsychotics develop weight gain, glucose dysregulation, or dyslipidaemia, and antipsychotic-induced MS is associated with increased risks of cardiovascular disease and type 2 diabetes. Non-modifiable determinants include age, gender, ethnic background, and family history of obesity, while modifiable determinants include diet, physical activity, weight, blood pressure, glucose, and cholesterol. Existing non-pharmacological interventions have shown limited clinical efficacy and variable sustained effects, and their preferred timing and healthcare setting remain unclear.

The review will follow Joanna Briggs Institute guidance and the PRISMA-ScR checklist, using a PICOTS framework to map determinants, non-pharmacological interventions, outcomes, timing, and community settings. Searches of bibliographic databases, grey literature, reference lists, and forward citations will continue until saturation. Quantitative, qualitative, mixed-method studies, evidence syntheses, full-text articles, and conference abstracts will be eligible, while non-human studies, non-English publications, and non-research articles will be excluded.

Two reviewers will independently screen titles and abstracts; one will screen full texts with a 10% sample checked by another. Data will be extracted into a standardised form, with a 10% sample independently checked, and synthesised narratively. Study quality will be represented using JBI evidence-level categories rather than formal critical appraisal. Stakeholders, including patients and family members or carers, will be consulted to assess determinants and the feasibility of preferred delivery contexts. Findings will identify evidence gaps and inform future research, with dissemination through peer-reviewed publications and conferences.

The Colorado Court of Appeals affirmed summary judgment for Shelter Mutual Insurance Company. After Samuel and Mary Breit received $100,000 from a third-party insurer and incurred damages exceeding $200,000, they sought uninsured motorist benefits under two Shelter policies, each providing $100,000 per person.

The court held that the policy’s “Limits of Liabilities” and “Other Insurance in the Company” provisions unambiguously prohibit stacking benefits from multiple policies issued by the same insurer, limiting the Breits’ recovery to $100,000. The separate “Other Insurance” clause was also unambiguous and did not conflict with the anti-stacking provision: it limits recovery to the highest applicable coverage and allocates liability among insurers pro rata. The court distinguished Compton because it involved policies from different carriers and conflicting language. The doctrine of reasonable expectations was inapplicable because the policy was neither ambiguous nor conflicting. The appeal was not frivolous, and attorney fees were denied.

The ANC’s delayed Free State provincial congress will elect new leadership, with Ace Magashule expected to seek the chairperson’s post again. Cervical cancer remains a major preventable health inequity, with 85% of cases and 90% of deaths occurring in low- and middle-income countries where access to screening and precancer treatment is limited. Provider-administered ablation or excision requires trained personnel, infrastructure, and travel, contributing to treatment delays and loss to follow-up. Self-administered intravaginal 5-fluorouracil (5FU) could offer a scalable treatment option, but its acceptability following actual use in Africa had not been studied.

A Phase I pilot trial in Kisumu, Kenya, enrolled 12 women living with HIV who had biopsy-confirmed CIN2/3 and had received ablation or excision four to 12 weeks earlier. Participants self-administered 2 g of intravaginal 5FU at home every other week for eight applications, with alternate-week clinic safety and adherence visits. Previous trial results showed that treatment was safe, with primarily grade I adverse events and no grade III or IV events. All 12 participants tolerated all doses, and 96% of doses were supported as adherent by self-report, tube weight, and applicator inspection.

Acceptability was assessed through week-16 questionnaires and in-depth interviews. Initially, some participants experienced uncertainty, anxiety, or fear, but after repeated education and practice, all considered the cream safe and were confident they had used it correctly. All preferred 5FU over previous ablation or excision if it were available as primary treatment. Participants valued home use, nighttime dosing, reduced pain and fear, greater privacy, and less disruption to daily work. Male partners ultimately supported treatment.

Challenges included accurately measuring the dose, limited familiarity with female anatomy, difficulty using applicators and tampons initially, adverse effects such as discharge, itching, burning, and discomfort during urination, condom requirements, and limited privacy at home. Counseling, pelvic-model practice, clinic reinforcement, and answering questions increased confidence and comfort. The small, single-site pilot limits generalizability, but findings support further efficacy and implementation research on self-administered topical therapies in resource-limited settings.

The Trump administration is transferring career and technical education (CTE) operations from the Department of Education to the Labor Department while retaining Education Department oversight. The administration says an “employment first” approach, centralized workforce development, reduced state administrative burden, and stronger employer alignment will boost young people’s labor-force participation and accountability. Labor would distribute more than $1 billion in Perkins funding, monitor compliance, and provide technical assistance.

Supporters, including the U.S. Chamber of Commerce Foundation, say the change could improve alignment with local labor markets, expand apprenticeships, and help students enter jobs. Critics, including Democratic lawmakers and CTE advocates, say it weakens the Education Department, may strain limited staffing, and could steer students toward short-term credentials and low-wage work rather than advancement or higher education. Unequal program quality and uncertainty about resources for students with disabilities are additional concerns. Details of the staffing transition remain unclear.

The Ministry of Education will fund a $28.5-million replacement for Walnut Park Elementary in Smithers, announced by Education Minister Rob Fleming and Stikine MLA Doug Donaldson at the school. It will meet LEED gold standards; the old building will be demolished after students move in. The Province contributes up to $27.6 million and SD54 $900,000. SD54 and the Town of Smithers will determine the learning centre's use, with groundbreaking hoped for next spring and students expected in 2020–21. A withdrawn, non-peer-reviewed medRxiv preprint evaluated six machine-learning models—Logistic Regression, Random Forest, Support Vector Machine, Neural Network, Decision Tree, and SuperLearner—for pancreatic cancer diagnosis using synthetic clinical data containing demographic, risk-factor, and symptom variables. Data were preprocessed and split into 80% training and 20% test sets without resampling.

All models produced similar accuracy (76.05%–76.35%) but had very low sensitivity because positive cases were far less common than negatives. Random Forest and Decision Tree identified no true positives. SVM had the highest sensitivity at 1.90%, followed by Logistic Regression and Neural Network at 1.47%. SuperLearner had the highest precision at 66.67% but only 0.42% sensitivity. These results were considered insufficient for practical diagnostic use.

The study identifies class imbalance, interpretability, and limited real-world validation as major barriers. It recommends resampling and cost-sensitive methods, threshold tuning, feature engineering, explainable-AI tools, integration of imaging and genomic data, and testing on real clinical datasets. Gene-expression heatmaps, PCA, and correlation analyses of metastasized cancer and normal colon tissues are presented as possible sources of discriminatory features and preprocessing strategies. The authors emphasize collaboration between data scientists and clinicians and further work to balance sensitivity and precision.

The Indiana Supreme Court reversed the trial court’s grant of partial summary judgment in a wrongful-death action arising from Laura Shaner’s death following complications from dialysis administered after abdominal hernia surgery. David Shaner, Laura’s widower, sought final-expense damages and survivor damages, including loss of consortium, earnings, services, and support. David died intestate without heirs, and his estate escheated to Indiana. Laura’s estate administrators then continued the claims.

The Court held that Indiana’s wrongful-death and survival statutes, read together, provide that an accrued claim does not abate when the statutory beneficiary dies before judgment and do not require a surviving heir. The Court declined to read *Bemenderfer v. Williams* as imposing such a requirement, rejecting defendants’ argument that survivor damages would be punitive because they would ultimately pass to the state.

However, the Court found the proper party unresolved. Survivor damages were intended for David’s exclusive benefit, and the survival statute permits David’s legal representative or successor in interest to continue the action. Because only Laura’s estate’s administrators were before the Court, the trial court was instructed on remand to determine whether a proper party exists to pursue the claim and whether David’s estate should be reopened.

The lecture compares tournament and cash-game poker. Tournaments use escalating blinds and eliminate players, while cash games have fixed stakes, allow rebuys and table selection, and involve more metagame. Tournament play has greater variance, broader positional scenarios, and lower casino fees, and is emphasized in the class because it better supports mathematical hand analysis. Poker skills largely transfer between formats, although risk tolerance and schedule affect which format a player chooses.

Preflop equities are grouped into approximate categories: a larger pair against a smaller pair is often about 80/20; a pair against one overcard or a dominating hand is often near 70/30; two overcards against a pair can be close to 50/50; and hands with four distinct cards generally favor the higher cards at roughly 60/40. Suitedness matters much more when a hand is behind because it provides additional flush possibilities, while it matters less when the hand is already strong. Small pairs also become less attractive at shallower stack depths because their implied odds deteriorate.

The lecture stresses that players are often too afraid to shove preflop. With antes and effective stacks below roughly 12 big blinds, the stated rule is to go all-in when willing to play a hand; without antes, the threshold is slightly shorter. Shoving is often preferable to making a small raise because a raise gives opponents options to call with weak hands or force an all-in with strong hands. From the small blind, all-in ranges can be wider than button ranges because only one player remains to act and postflop position is irrelevant once the money is committed.

An exploitative example models a 15-big-blind small blind against a big blind calling only 25% of hands. This range is wide enough for the small blind to profitably shove even very weak hands, showing that one player’s strategy may be flawed. Iterative best responses lead to a Nash equilibrium in which the small blind shoves about 66.8% of hands and the big blind calls about 38.5%. Exploiting deviations should follow the opponent’s strategy: shove more when they call too little, and call more when they shove too much.

Concrete ranges can be learned through memorization, theory, and interpolation. Earlier positions require stronger hands, while shorter stacks widen all-in ranges; position often affects range size more than stack depth. Suited connectors benefit especially from sufficient stack depth, whereas hands such as ace-four offsuit perform better from late position against weaker calling ranges.

Calling an all-in should be based on the effective stack, pot odds, and the opponent’s range. At 12 big blinds or less, hands that would ordinarily be opened are often strong enough to call, and with very short stacks nearly any two cards can be played. Calling is generally safer than folding when close to the required equity.

For reraising, the lecture recommends either shoving or using a substantially larger raise—roughly 2.5 times the original raise—rather than making a minimum raise. Calling an existing raise can also be preferable because it denies the opponent an all-in option and preserves the possibility of playing the flop in position. When players have limped, raise sizes should increase, with the rough rule of adding one big blind for each limper. Finally, the lecturer identifies “sucker bets” that deliberately give an opponent extra options when that opponent is likely to make a mistake, emphasizing that routine, probability-based decisions generally contribute more to long-term success than occasional spectacular bluffs.

Set SDO_CTL_REG’s SDO1_CONFIG bits to 01b to enable the active-high ALARM/SDO-1/GPO pin. The input alarm compares ADC voltage with programmable high and low thresholds; the AVDD alarm triggers at 4.7 V or 5.3 V. Both are enabled by default but can be disabled via IN_AL_DIS and VDD_AL_DIS in RST_PWRCTL_REG. ALARM_REG active flags clear after each conversion; tripped flags clear only when read. The S&P MidCap 400 is a market-cap-weighted U.S. stock index formed in 1991 that tracks 400 mid-sized companies with market capitalizations between $3.6 billion and $13.1 billion. Companies must be U.S.-based, exchange-listed, and have a minimum investable factor of 0.10. The index is rebalanced quarterly in March, June, September, and December and differs from the large-company-focused S&P 500.

E-mini S&P MidCap 400 futures are CME Globex derivatives with a value of $100 times the index. They trade Sunday through Friday, 6:00 p.m. to 5:00 p.m. ET the next day, with a daily maintenance break. Quarterly contracts are listed for five consecutive quarters and expire on the third Friday of the contract month. They are cash-settled using a special opening quotation. The minimum fluctuation is 0.1 index point, or $10, for outright Globex trading and 0.05 point, or $5, for BTIC and calendar spreads. The futures symbol is EMD. At an index value of 2,585.8 on December 1, 2022, one contract was worth $258,580.

Trading requires registration with a futures broker, account funding, and sufficient margin. Because futures are leveraged, losses are based on the full contract value rather than the margin posted; at 20-times leverage, a 1% adverse move could produce a 20% account loss. CFDs offered by some brokers provide an alternative without fixed contract expiry, although they generally track the index rather than the futures.

The index tends to perform better in winter and spring than in summer and fall. Prices are affected by component stocks, interest rates, economic news, and the U.S. dollar. TradingView cited a futures high of 2,924.2 and an index high of 2,925.93 in November 2021, while the index low was 119.43 in June 1991.

Two backtests produced mixed results: a volatility strategy performed poorly, while an overnight strategy recorded 362 trades, a 0.31% average gain, 5% CAGR, 60% win rate, and 1.63 profit factor. Both performed better on SPY and QQQ, and the passage reports difficulty finding uncorrelated, risk-adjusted midcap strategies.

ETFs tracking the index include IJH, SPMD, and the equal-weighted EWMC; the index ticker is MID.

A Russell 2000 Death Cross occurs when the index’s 50-day moving average falls below its 200-day average and is generally viewed as bearish. John Mellencamp performed “Easy Target” on “Late Show With Stephen Colbert,” then knelt and raised his fist in support of Black Lives Matter. Mellencamp said taking the knee, begun by Colin Kaepernick to protest racial injustice, was politicized by the Trump administration.

The lecture explains how demand estimates can be combined with assumptions about firm conduct to infer supply-side costs. For multiproduct firms, an ownership matrix and demand-price derivatives define a matrix used to write firms’ first-order conditions, allowing marginal costs to be recovered from prices, quantities, and demand estimates. If marginal costs are fully flexible, any model can be rationalized and cannot be tested without further restrictions. Imposing a cost function instead permits joint demand-supply estimation and additional moment conditions. These restrictions can improve demand estimates, particularly random-coefficient estimates, and provide overidentifying restrictions for testing alternative conduct models.

The BLP automobile application uses U.S. list-price data from 1971–1990 and vehicle characteristics such as size, power, weight, and fuel efficiency. Simple logit-inversion regressions show that instrumental-variable estimates produce more negative price coefficients, reduce implausibly inelastic demand, and can reveal positive elasticities that conflict with static profit maximization. Hedonic regressions explain substantial price variation using vehicle attributes. The random-coefficient model captures substantial heterogeneity in tastes, and BLP’s estimated substitution patterns differ meaningfully from logit results, particularly for expensive vehicles and the outside option. The paper’s limitations include its treatment of cars as nondurables, inability to model endogenous used-car markets, and neglect of dealerships, negotiated transaction prices, financing, insurance, and other purchase costs.

Nevo’s cereal study asks whether high gross margins reflect collusion or competition among multiproduct firms that avoid cannibalizing their own brands. It estimates demand with alternative conduct assumptions, recovers markups, and compares them with accounting-based margins using geographic panel data. Product fixed effects, demographic heterogeneity, Hausman instruments, and cost-side instruments improve the demand estimates. Model-implied markups range from 31% to 46%, depending partly on whether advertising is treated as a marginal cost. The study rejects joint profit maximization across 25 brands but cannot reject either brand-level competition or competition incorporating observed ownership structures. A basic logit model produces much lower markups and would not reject collusion. The approach remains sensitive to whether accounting costs represent true economic costs, the treatment of advertising, and the assumption that product characteristics are exogenous.

The lecture then introduces the common ownership hypothesis: diversified institutional investors may give competing firms incentives to soften price competition by internalizing profits across companies they hold. Descriptive evidence shows that institutional ownership and implied profit weights on competitors have increased over time. Backus, Conlon, and Sinkinson test common-ownership and alternative conduct models in the cereal market using demand estimates, flexible marginal-cost specifications, supply-side moments, and a non-nested GMM test. Their cereal case rejects common-ownership specifications in favor of own-profit maximization and also rejects perfect competition and full monopoly. The lecture notes that this is a single case study and that the mechanism by which institutional investors would induce less competition remains disputed and unclear.

Ichimoku Kinko Hyo is a technical-analysis system that identifies support and resistance, trend direction, and momentum by plotting several averages on a price chart. The averages form a “cloud,” indicating potential future support or resistance. The indicator is attributed to journalist Goichi Hosoda and his assistants, though the passage gives differing development dates ranging from the 1930s to 1968.

Its five components are the Tenkan-Sen, Kijun-Sen, Senkou Span A, Senkou Span B, and Chikou Span. The Tenkan-Sen averages the nine-period high and low, while the Kijun-Sen uses 26 periods. Senkou Span A averages the Tenkan and Kijun lines and is shifted forward 26 periods; Senkou Span B uses the 52-period high and low and is also shifted forward. Chikou is the closing price shifted back 26 periods.

Price above the cloud indicates an uptrend, while price below it indicates a downtrend. A thick cloud signals high volatility and a thin cloud declining volatility. Tenkan/Kijun crossovers provide bullish or bearish signals and can confirm price action. Chikou can confirm an upward or downward cloud breakout and sometimes precede it. Senkou spans can act as support and resistance levels.

Traders can build strategies from individual or combined signals, then backtest and forward-test them before trading. Scalpers and day traders may use intraday charts, while swing and position traders use larger timeframes; the authors favor daily bars but stress that testing is necessary. Discipline, risk management, and adherence to a trading plan are essential because even a sound strategy can lose money through poor execution.

The passage’s backtests found that the strategy spent less time in the market and reduced drawdowns, but generally underperformed risk-adjusted buy-and-hold returns. It therefore presents Ichimoku as a useful analytical tool rather than a consistently profitable strategy. Its signals may be inaccurate or unreliable, so backtesting is advised to reduce potential time and monetary losses.

The 2007–09 recession and continuing financial concerns weakened U.S. restaurant demand, particularly casual dining, but investors revisited casual dining stocks in 2016 as economic growth improved consumers’ willingness to dine out. The U.S. restaurant industry was projected to generate nearly $800 billion in sales, represent 4% of GDP, and employ nearly one in ten Americans. Casual dining offered a more comfortable, family-friendly experience than fast food at lower prices than fine dining, while fast casual restaurants emphasized quality and atmosphere without table service.

Bloomin’ Brands opened its first Australian-themed Outback Steakhouse in Tampa in 1988 and went public in 2012. By June 2016, it owned 1,335 restaurants and franchised 166 across Outback, Fleming’s, Bonefish Grill, and Carrabba’s Italian Grill. About 85% were in the United States, and nearly two-thirds operated under Outback.

The report compares Bloomin’ with 13 publicly traded restaurant companies spanning casual dining, fast casual, and fast food. Exhibits provide August 2016 valuation data and trailing financial statements and balance sheets. Bloomin’ had a $2.2 billion market capitalization, a 40.2 trailing P/E multiple, and a 12.6 forward P/E multiple, compared with peer medians of 23.2 and 19.5, respectively. Its trailing revenue was $4.319 billion, net income $60 million, and EPS $0.48. It reported $2.784 billion in assets, $2.451 billion in liabilities, $333 million in shareholders’ equity, $102 million in cash and short-term investments, and $1.218 billion in total debt.

Microsoft Corporation reported unaudited results for the quarter ended September 30, 2022. Revenue increased 11% to $50.1 billion, gross margin rose 9% to $34.7 billion, and operating income increased 6% to $21.5 billion. Net income declined 14% to $17.6 billion and diluted EPS fell to $2.35 from $2.71, primarily because the prior-year quarter included a $3.3 billion tax benefit from transferring intangible properties. Adjusted net income increased 2% to $17.6 billion.

Microsoft Cloud revenue grew 24% to $25.7 billion. Productivity and Business Processes revenue rose 9% to $16.5 billion and operating income increased 10%; Intelligent Cloud revenue rose 20% to $20.3 billion and operating income increased 17%; More Personal Computing revenue was flat at $13.3 billion and operating income fell 15%. Azure and other cloud services grew 35%, Office 365 Commercial 11%, LinkedIn 17%, and Dynamics 365 24%, while Windows OEM revenue declined 15%.

At September 30, 2022, the company held $107.3 billion of cash, cash equivalents, and short-term investments, with total assets of $359.8 billion and stockholders’ equity of $173.6 billion. Operating cash flow was $23.2 billion. The company repurchased $5.6 billion of stock, paid $4.6 billion in dividends, and spent $6.3 billion on property and equipment.

Microsoft completed the $18.8 billion Nuance acquisition and had an agreement to acquire Activision Blizzard for $68.7 billion. Increasing server and network equipment useful lives from four to six years increased quarterly operating income by $1.1 billion and net income by $859 million. Research and development expense rose 18% to $6.6 billion. Deloitte’s review found no material modifications to the interim financial information.

The 60/40 portfolio allocates 60% of capital to equities and 40% to bonds. It can be U.S.-only, using an S&P 500 ETF and Treasuries, or globally diversified with international stocks and bonds. Its diversification depends on stocks and bonds often moving differently: bonds may cushion equity losses during slowing growth but can also decline when inflation rises, as they did in 2022.

Investors can implement the strategy with low-cost ETFs and bond funds, such as SPY with TLT or VTI with BND, rebalancing one to four times annually, or through a managed fund such as BlackRock’s BIGPX. Individual securities are considered expensive. Vanguard’s historical data shows an average annual return of 8.8% since 1926.

As of September 17, 2022, the portfolio had returned negative 17.77% year to date, with a Sharpe ratio of -0.76, dividend yield of 1.89%, and volatility of 7.07%. Its maximum drawdown since January 2010 was 21.85%, recovered in 79 trading sessions. Since 1980, it has fallen more than 10% within a year nine times, often rebounding afterward.

The article concludes that the strategy is not dead despite its poor 2022 performance and low bond yields. Diversification remains useful, unrealistic return expectations and difficult market conditions are the main concerns, and market timing is characterized as futile. Its valuation became cheaper, with projected annualized ten-year returns rising from 2.6% to 6.1%.

Alternatives include the 80/20 portfolio, All-Weather Portfolio, trend-following strategies, gold, small crypto allocations, international equities, tail-risk strategies, and Thomas Carlson’s Defense First strategy. A backtest combining SPY, TLT, and the trend-following KMLM produced the best result among the compared portfolios from 2021 through 2022.

The Rhode Island Supreme Court affirmed Andrew A. Bucci’s conviction for furnishing legal advice to Robert Oliva while suspended from the practice of law. After a de novo jury trial, Bucci was sentenced to six months’ imprisonment; his prior District Court fine of $500 exceeded the statutory maximum.

Recorded conversations showed Bucci advised Oliva about venue, search-and-seizure law, grand jury procedure, witnesses, restitution, and trial strategy while retaining and directing another attorney to represent Oliva. The court rejected Bucci’s claim that this conduct varied from the charge of furnishing legal advice and found overwhelming evidence supporting the conviction.

The court also held that § 11-27-10 did not require proof of pecuniary benefit because the statute protects the public from legal advice given by unauthorized persons. Although a greater sentence after a trial de novo was constitutionally permissible, challenges to a sentence’s legality or propriety had to be raised through a Superior Court Rule 35 motion, which Bucci had not filed. The appeal was dismissed, the conviction affirmed, and the case remanded to the Superior Court.

GAIS, a nonprofit working with 200 farmers in South Sudan’s Gbudue state, urged the government to restrict imported seeds and support local producers after FAO brought 100 metric tons into the state through Congo. Gbudue’s agriculture ministry said it would investigate. FAO said its emergency program distributes both imported seeds and cash-supported local seed fairs, follows independent procurement rules, and has previously supported GAIS. It cited a ministry waiver allowing imports because of low production and conflict-related displacement, and plans to distribute 5,000 metric tons this year, up from 2,000.

Research in 38 healthy adults linked higher musical aptitude to greater corpus callosum integrity and lower hallucination proneness, with corpus callosum microstructure statistically mediating their relationship. The authors suggested musical training might counteract hallucination predisposition, but called for further research.

The Assam Higher Secondary Education Council (AHSEC) was scheduled to release Class 12 results on May 31, 2018, at 9:30 a.m. Results could be checked through official websites, SMS services, or apps requiring roll-number registration. This study examined whether group-based brain parcellations bias functional connectivity (FC) estimates of psychosis. Using HCP-EP data from 112 patients with early psychosis and 55 healthy controls, the authors compared the 100-region Schaefer cortical atlas with individualized parcellations generated by the Group Prior Individualized Parcellation algorithm. They also repeated analyses with a 200-region atlas and global signal regression.

Individualization preserved regional labels while adjusting parcel boundaries, shapes, and sizes to individual functional data. On average, 42.56% of vertices were reassigned, and approximately 42–43% of edges were relabeled. Individualized parcels had slightly greater functional homogeneity, while controls had more homogeneous parcels than patients under both methods.

Both approaches identified widespread reduced FC in patients relative to controls. However, group-based parcellation produced larger case-control differences and was interpreted as inflating the magnitude of dysconnectivity. The two approaches’ edge-level t-statistic matrices were only moderately correlated. Network-Based Statistic analysis found one significant disconnected component with each method: 2,712 edges for group-based parcellation versus 2,461 for individualized parcellation, with 643 edges differing between components. Edge- and region-specific findings therefore varied considerably, including differences involving medial frontal and insular regions. In contrast, network-level patterns were broadly consistent across methods; the control network had the largest raw number of affected edges, and normalized results suggested more widespread disruptions.

The findings indicate that group-based parcellations may overestimate FC differences and obscure individual variability, whereas individualized parcellations provide more conservative and refined maps of psychosis-related network disruption. Limitations included the relatively low-resolution fsaverage5 surface mesh, medication exposure among some patients, and clinical heterogeneity in the psychosis sample.

The lecture reviews linear systems, noting that MATLAB’s backslash method usually reaches machine accuracy but can be unreliable for ill-conditioned matrices, where multiple solutions may satisfy the equation numerically. Newton's method, dogleg methods, and trust-region approaches are used for nonlinear systems, with the initial guess strongly affecting convergence. MATLAB’s `fsolve` reformulates root-finding as minimizing the norm of the residual, while `fmincon` similarly locates saddle points by minimizing the squared norm of a gradient. Computational cost depends on repeated linear solves, iteration counts, and problem size; nominal \(n^3\) costs may in practice be dominated by \(n^2\) matrix construction.

Implicit ODE methods require solving nonlinear equations at every time step. Their total cost can be estimated from the number of time steps, iterations per nonlinear solve, and cost of forming the Jacobian, potentially reaching large but computationally feasible totals. The lecture also introduces functionals, which operate on functions, including gradients, Jacobians, and `fsolve`. Density functional theory is presented as an important application in which molecular energy is treated as a functional of electron density.

The lecture then connects numerical integration, interpolation, and basis functions. Quadrature rules such as rectangle, trapezoid, and Simpson’s rule approximate an integrand with a fitted function and integrate that approximation; agreement between two rules does not guarantee convergence. Using fewer basis parameters than data points produces approximation, while using the same number permits interpolation and is appropriate when data are treated as exact but may undesirably fit noise when data are noisy.

Interpolation coefficients are found by solving a linear system, which requires a nonsingular matrix and linearly independent basis functions. Orthogonal basis functions generalize this concept. Although monomials are simple, they can produce ill-conditioned interpolation matrices and oscillatory fits. Lagrange polynomials allow coefficients to be read directly from sampled values, while Newton polynomials support adding points and updating the fit incrementally.

Gauss chose quadrature nodes and weights so that \(n\)-point rules integrate polynomials exactly through degree \(2n-1\), giving higher accuracy than Simpson’s rule. A seven-point rule is exact through degree 13, and comparison with a 15-point method provides an error estimate. Extending quadrature to multiple dimensions requires nested evaluations, causing computational effort to grow exponentially with dimension—a phenomenon called the curse of dimensionality.

The lecture opens with questions about the Hawking–Page transition. Thermal AdS is described as AdS coupled to a thermal bath, with the bath producing mainly a gas of massless gravitons. The transition is a first-order transition between thermal AdS and a large-black-hole phase; on the field-theory side it involves different dominant sectors of a single CFT, not two CFTs or a quantum critical point. A high-energy sector with greater entropy dominates above the transition. Confinement/deconfinement language is described as a heuristic analogy based on scaling, since there is no conventional confinement in the scale-invariant AdS series. The thermal partition sum does not diverge; its behavior depends on how the density of states scales with energy.

The lecture then introduces entanglement entropy. For a bipartite quantum system with Hilbert space \(\mathcal H_A\otimes\mathcal H_B\), entanglement entropy is the von Neumann entropy of the reduced density matrix obtained by tracing out \(B\). For a pure global state, the entropies of \(A\) and \(B\) are equal, as follows from Schmidt decomposition; zero entropy corresponds to a product state. For mixed states, the two entropies generally differ, and the entropy includes classical statistical correlations as well as quantum entanglement. A two-spin example illustrates that a state may appear entangled in one basis but be a simple product in another, while also providing a maximally entangled example.

Subadditivity and strong subadditivity are introduced as general entropy inequalities. Their classical set-theoretic interpretations are intuitive, but the lecturer emphasizes that their quantum proofs are substantially less trivial.

In quantum many-body systems, uncoupled subsystems with \(H=H_A+H_B\) have product ground states, whereas coupling through \(H_{AB}\) generally produces an entangled ground state. For local lattice Hamiltonians and quantum field theories, \(H_{AB}\) is supported only near the boundary between the regions, within a short-distance cutoff \(\epsilon\). Generic ground states obey an area law: the leading entanglement entropy is proportional to the boundary area of region \(A\), divided by \(\epsilon\), with a system-dependent coefficient. The leading law is universal, while its coefficient and subleading terms are generally not. The subleading terms reflect long-range entanglement and can characterize quantum phases. One example is topological order in \(2+1\) dimensions, where a finite, shape-independent topological entanglement-entropy term reveals correlations not visible through ordinary local observables. Another is the central charge of a \(1+1\)-dimensional CFT, which controls the asymptotic density of states and appears in \(S_A=(c/3)\log(\ell/\epsilon)\); higher-dimensional analogues characterize degrees of freedom across quantum field theories.

Finally, the lecture presents the Ryu–Takayanagi prescription for holographic entanglement entropy. For a region \(A\) in a CFT with a gravity dual, one finds the bulk surface \(\gamma_A\) of minimal area anchored on \(\partial A\), on an appropriate constant-time slice, and uses
\[
S_A=\frac{\operatorname{Area}(\gamma_A)}{4G_N}.
\]
The proposal is motivated by the black-hole entropy formula. Minimal-surface geometry gives elegant proofs of the relevant entropy inequalities. For a vacuum \(1+1\)-dimensional CFT dual to \(\mathrm{AdS}_3\), the minimal curve is a semicircle, yielding \(S=(c/3)\log(L/\epsilon)\), with \(c=3R/(2G_N)\). At finite temperature, the surface deforms as the region grows and ultimately hugs the black-hole horizon; when the region covers the entire space, the result reproduces the thermal black-hole entropy. In higher dimensions, the same geometry yields the area law. The lecture concludes that the relation between entanglement and geometry links quantum information, many-body physics, quantum field theory, black holes, string theory, and gravity within holographic duality.

This exploratory field study examines the software engineering challenges of integrating open-source and commercial large language models into domain-specific financial report analysis. Guided by design science research and conducted with Getinge AB’s finance department, it addresses two questions: the challenges of integrating LLMs into financial reporting workflows, and how open-source and commercial approaches compare in complexity, performance, and maintainability.

A literature review covers LLM architectures, prompting and agent-based methods, implementation concerns, software engineering for LLM-based systems, and prior financial applications. The study identifies three primary challenges: the task specificity of financial reporting, variability and complexity in data preparation, and restrictions arising from sensitive financial data. Traditional financial analysis remains manual, repetitive, and inconsistent, while LLMs offer automation potential but raise concerns about hallucinations, security, interpretability, accuracy, and validation.

Domain exploration through focus groups and task analysis identified three candidate use cases: commenting on income-statement changes, order-intake changes, and net-sales changes. The income-statement case was not pursued because realistic transformation of heterogeneous source data was infeasible under confidentiality constraints. The remaining cases used anonymized or synthetic structured data for changes in order intake and net sales.

The first design cycle tested quantized open-source models through Ollama on local hardware. Python and Pandas transformed large CSV datasets into condensed, prompt-ready tables containing differences and relative contributions by product line and region. Single-prompt approaches produced hallucinations and instruction failures. A four-agent, prompt-chained workflow was therefore implemented for data interpretation, trend analysis, report generation, and validation. Although modularization improved coherence, errors introduced by one agent could propagate and be amplified by later agents. Three-billion-parameter models were particularly unreliable, while eight-billion-parameter models performed better but ran slowly on CPU-only hardware and still produced inconsistent output.

The second cycle used OpenAI’s GPT-4o through its API with similarly preprocessed data and structured prompts. It required minimal setup and generally produced concise, professionally worded summaries, but sometimes omitted key drivers, misprioritized changes, mixed positive and negative trends, or repeated product lines. Few-shot examples improved formatting but were sometimes imitated so rigidly that relevant variations in the data were ignored. Deployment through a third party also raised privacy, compliance, and provider-dependency concerns.

A refined two-step GPT-4o workflow separated financial analysis from report writing. This improved the structured analysis, but the final summaries still sometimes omitted, contradicted, or inaccurately restated the analysis, especially when prompts contained conditional rules or multiple constraints.

In evaluation, two business controllers reviewed 20 summaries from each approach across usefulness, accuracy, clarity, trust, and workflow integration. GPT-4o was preferred for concise, report-oriented language, while the local model produced more descriptive summaries considered potentially useful for internal analysis. Both required manual refinement, sometimes included redundant or irrelevant details, omitted important changes, misattributed regions, and lacked numerical context and transparent selection rationale. Neither was considered dependable for finalized reporting without human validation.

The study concludes that both approaches can accelerate draft creation but do not provide reliable end-to-end automation. Local models offer data control and privacy but require greater infrastructure and engineering effort; GPT-4o offers easier integration and stronger out-of-the-box performance but introduces privacy, compliance, and vendor-lock-in concerns. Limitations include the small expert sample, reliance on qualitative assessments, transformed historical data, evaluation at one company, model non-determinism, and infrastructure differences. Future work should explore rule-aware modular prompts, prompt versioning and documentation, stronger multi-agent coordination and fault isolation, and hybrid deployments that separate sensitive processing from more complex external operations.

Four challenges are identified for quantum electrodynamics of attoscience: generating massively quantum states of light; creating and understanding light–matter entanglement in complex materials; characterizing and applying these states with ultrafast quantum-optical methods; and simulating strong-field QED using cold atoms and ions. Proposed approaches include multimode squeezed and exotic states, bright squeezed light, structured driving fields, conditioning and post-selection, and quantum simulators employing quantum trap shaking and Kramers–Henneberger transformations. Open questions include how photon entanglement and noise affect reconstructed photoelectron density matrices and whether experiments can unambiguously identify quantum correlations.

Recent theoretical progress has made fully quantized strong-field models increasingly feasible through quantum field operators, observable-conditioned post-selection, QFT-based energy conservation, and hybrid semiclassical–quantum methods. Experimental advances include attosecond metrology, ultrafast streaking and pump-probe configurations, photon-statistics and coherence characterization, Wigner-function measurements, and demonstrations of optical Schrödinger cats and squeezed harmonics. Structured sources such as Laguerre–Gaussian and Bessel beams, polarization-shaped pulses, squeezed light, and entangled photon sources may enable high-fidelity generation beyond low-depletion regimes.

Two-dimensional, correlated, and topological materials provide testbeds for phase-sensitive harmonic emission, quantum pathways, and entanglement. Ultrafast quantum tomography, homodyne detection, entanglement witnessing, multidimensional spectroscopy, interferometric state reconstruction, and machine-learning inversion are advancing state characterization. The passage concludes that integrating attosecond physics with quantum optics is enabling scalable quantum light sources, new quantum-simulation platforms, and potential ultrafast quantum processors.

DAWN-plasma was a prospective, multicenter, randomized, open-label phase II proof-of-concept trial comparing standard of care plus convalescent plasma with standard of care alone in hospitalized adults with COVID-19. The protocol and consent documentation were approved by independent ethics committees, and the study followed Declaration of Helsinki principles and ICH Good Clinical Practice guidelines.

Between May 2020 and January 2021, 499 patients were assessed and 489 randomized 2:1 to convalescent plasma plus standard of care (326) or standard of care alone (163). The full analysis set included 483 patients, excluding one without confirmed COVID-19 and five who withdrew immediately after randomization. Patients received four plasma units totaling 800–1,000 mL; the first transfusion occurred a median of five hours after randomization, and 80.7% of units had neutralizing-antibody titers of at least 1/320.

The primary endpoint—the proportion alive without mechanical ventilation at Day 15—did not differ between groups: 83.7% with plasma plus standard of care versus 84.1% with standard of care alone (odds ratio 0.99; p=0.976). No significant differences were found in mortality, mechanical ventilation, Day-30 outcomes, or other secondary endpoints.

Adverse-event frequencies were similar between groups: any adverse event occurred in 28.13% and 30.06%; fatal adverse events in 10.31% and 9.82%; and serious adverse events in 20.62% and 20.68%, respectively. Transfusion-related side effects occurred in 19 of 320 intervention patients (6.0%), with no TRALI cases reported. Neutralizing-antibody titers increased by Day 6 regardless of intervention, although higher baseline and Day-6 titers correlated with better outcomes. Overall, early high-titer convalescent plasma did not improve the primary outcome or other study endpoints.

Fanconi anemia (FA) patients have a high incidence of oral potentially malignant lesions (OPMLs) and oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC), often at younger ages and with advanced disease that is difficult to treat. Because biopsies are invasive and may miss clinically invisible precancerous cells, this study investigated noninvasive liquid biopsies for early risk detection.

Sixteen FA patients at two Spanish hospitals were followed prospectively for about two years, with saliva and plasma collected repeatedly. DNA was analyzed by next-generation sequencing of 52 cancer genes, achieving detection limits of 0.07% in saliva and 0.09% in plasma. Eighteen mutations were detected in 15 samples from nine patients, most commonly in TP53; no copy-number variants were found.

Among 14 patients with post-collection follow-up, seven developed oral lesions or carcinomas. Cancer-gene mutations were detected in six of these seven before clinical diagnosis, with a median lead time of 205 days, and were absent from five patients without lesions. Mutation status was associated with significantly different oral lesion/tumor-free survival. Overall diagnostic accuracy was 92%, with 86% sensitivity and 100% specificity. The findings support saliva and plasma mutation analysis as a noninvasive means of identifying FA patients at elevated risk, although larger studies are needed and it was not confirmed whether detected mutations were present in subsequent lesions or tumors.
