The passage explains common offensive-line blocking terms and their roles in run and pass protection. Trap blocks leave a defender unblocked at the snap before another blocker kicks him out to maintain inside leverage. Base blocks are one-on-one blocks requiring inside leverage. Reach blocks use a 45-degree path to attack a defender’s outside shoulder, primarily on perimeter runs. Down blocks angle toward the near shoulder of a frontside defender and are common in gap schemes. Log blocks seal a defender inside, either after a planned or reactive kickout fails. Pulls move a blocker around another offensive player to gain a numbers or leverage advantage.

Veer blocks involve dropping the inside foot, ripping through the defensive front, and climbing to block linebackers, primarily in under-center triple-option offenses. Combo blocks use two players to block a first-level defender before one potentially advances to a second-level defender. The double-team block is the first-level portion of a combo block, using post and trail players to overpower one defender. Drive blocks are one-on-one run blocks that move a defender off the line while maintaining inside leverage. Scoop blocks are backside combo blocks in which both players use far-shoulder aiming points to form a seal.

Cut blocks dive at a defender’s legs to disrupt his hands or pursuit. Crack blocks involve a perimeter player coming backward to block an interior defender, often on perimeter runs or quick screens. Kick-out blocks resemble trap blocks but occur a gap wider; the blocker crosses the formation to establish inside leverage on an edge defender and widen the running lane. If the defender wrong-arms the block, it may become a log block.

Experts advocate suicide barriers on Lower Mainland bridges, citing their effectiveness in preventing jumps. Since crisis phones were installed at Burrard Bridge, at least four people intending to jump reached a 24/7 crisis line instead.

The study lasted about 33 months, with participants enrolled for up to 26 months, and ended in February 2023. In Phase 2/3, two 30-µg doses of BNT162b2 were 95% effective at preventing COVID-19 from seven days after Dose 2 through December 3, 2020, among participants aged 16 years and older, regardless of prior infection.

Antibody testing found that one booster dose of BNT162b2 produced original-strain immune responses comparable to those after two BNT162b2 doses. One booster dose of BNT162b2SA produced Beta-variant responses comparable to original-strain responses after two BNT162b2 doses in previously vaccinated participants; two BNT162b2SA doses produced similar Beta-variant responses in participants who had not previously received BNT162b2.

Injection-site reactions and systemic events were generally transient and mild or moderate. Injection-site pain was the most common local reaction, while tiredness and headache were the most common systemic events. In Phase 1, some participants had temporary lymphocyte reductions one to three days after Dose 1, which resolved by days 6–8. All tested Phase 1 doses were well tolerated except 100 µg BNT162b1, which was stopped after Dose 1 because of injection-site or systemic reactions.

In Phase 2/3, 30-µg BNT162b2 was well tolerated, and few participants left the blinded phase because of medical problems. Few serious medical problems occurred, and no single serious problem affected at least 1% of any group. No deaths occurred in Phase 1, and deaths during Phase 2/3 were not believed by researchers to have been caused by BNT162b2.

The U.S. Department of State’s Office of the Historian released a portable, searchable ebook of *Foreign Relations of the United States*, Volume IV, covering Soviet Union relations from January 1983 to March 1985. Researchers found that pollen collected by honeybees carries endophytic actinobacteria, including Streptomyces, that also occur in nearby plants and hive pollen stores. Many strains produced antimicrobial compounds: nearly all inhibited the mold causing stonebrood, while individual strains were moderately to strongly active against two bacterial pathogens of honeybees. DNA barcoding, genome sequencing, and competition assays confirmed that these microbes colonize plant tissues and produce bioactive compounds. The findings suggest bees transport them from flowers to hive stores, where they help defend colonies. Selected beneficial bacteria could potentially be introduced into hives to control pathogens, while diverse plant landscapes may provide bees with a wider range of protective microbes.

The passage compares value and growth investing and discusses backtesting their performance and combinations. Value investing targets undervalued companies with strong fundamentals, emphasizing long-term appreciation, stability, and distributions. Growth investing targets companies with high future growth potential regardless of valuation, seeking greater short-term appreciation but accepting higher risk and volatility.

Backtesting applies strategy rules to historical data using defined stock-selection criteria, historical data, and testing software. It can reveal past performance, weaknesses, and the return-risk balance of different value-growth allocations. Results depend on an investor’s risk tolerance, horizon, and objectives, and mixing both styles may improve diversification.

Reported backtests show mixed periods. From January 2001, small-cap growth outperformed small-cap value, and small-cap growth also exceeded large- and mid-cap strategies. However, longer-term data cited for 1926 onward show value returning 1,344,600% versus 626,600% for growth. The passage characterizes recent growth outperformance as an anomaly and notes value’s historical advantage. It also links high volatility to risk and identifies small, highly volatile companies as the riskiest group.

A weekly rotation model using a ratio and two moving averages switches between value and growth based on short-term momentum. Its backtest from 2000 reportedly produced higher returns and lower volatility and drawdown than either factor independently. The passage concludes that holding the outperforming factor may be preferable to committing to one, while individual investors should choose or combine the styles according to their circumstances and goals.

NVIDIA’s GA10x GPU generation includes the GA102 and GA104 chips, which build on Turing with substantially higher graphics, ray-tracing, AI, and compute performance. Ampere is reported to be up to 1.7 times faster in traditional raster workloads and twice as fast in ray tracing, while offering up to 1.9 times better power efficiency than Turing.

The 8nm GA102 contains 28.3 billion transistors and 84 Streaming Multiprocessors, providing 10,752 CUDA Cores, 84 second-generation RT Cores, 336 third-generation Tensor Cores, and 112 ROPs. Its SMs support double-rate FP32 processing, larger unified L1 and shared-memory capacity, and concurrent graphics, ray-tracing, and compute workloads. Moving ROPs into each Graphics Processing Cluster increases raster throughput and improves multisample antialiasing, fill rate, and blending.

Second-generation RT Cores double ray-triangle intersection throughput and can run alongside graphics or compute work. New motion-blur acceleration includes an Interpolate Triangle Position unit, enabling accurate ray-traced motion blur up to eight times faster than on Turing and supporting moving or deforming geometry.

Third-generation Tensor Cores add TF32 and BF16 support and hardware acceleration for fine-grained structured sparsity. Using a 2-out-of-4 non-zero pattern, sparsity can double matrix throughput, halve weight storage and bandwidth, and produce virtually no loss in inference accuracy. TF32 can deliver up to five times the prior generation’s training throughput, while the RTX 3080 reaches 238 sparse FP16 Tensor TFLOPS.

GA10x supports GDDR6X memory using PAM4 signaling, with rates up to 19.5 Gbps and peak bandwidth of 936 GB/s. The RTX 3080 consequently provides 1.5 times the memory bandwidth of the RTX 2080 Super. PCIe 4.0 provides up to 64 GB/s of peak bandwidth through an x16 slot.

The GeForce RTX 3090 uses GA102 with 82 SMs, 10,496 CUDA Cores, and 24 GB of GDDR6X for 8K HDR gaming and 8K DLSS. The RTX 3080 delivers up to twice the performance of the RTX 2080, while the GA104-based RTX 3070 rivals the previous-generation RTX 2080 Ti. DLSS uses the new Tensor Cores and a 9× scaling factor to support 8K gaming at 60 fps in many ray-traced titles.

Its fifth-generation NVDEC decoder supports MPEG-2, VC-1, H.264, H.265, VP8, VP9, and AV1; AV1 hardware decoding can play 8K60 HDR content with about 4% CPU usage in the cited test. The seventh-generation NVENC encoder independently handles video encoding, supporting H.264 up to 4K and HEVC up to 8K while reducing CPU utilization.

GA10x GDDR6X memory also introduces Error Detection and Replay, which detects failed transmissions and retries them. Although it does not prevent every crash, it identifies memory-overclocking limits as performance begins to plateau.

Amazon.com, Inc. filed a Form 8-K on February 2, 2021, reporting its fourth-quarter and full-year 2020 financial results. The earnings release and information on non-GAAP measures were included as Exhibits 99.1 and 99.2. Amazon also announced that Jeffrey P. Bezos plans to become executive chair and remain a director in the third quarter of 2021. Andrew R. Jassy, who joined Amazon in 1997 and has led Amazon Web Services since 2016, will succeed Bezos as president and CEO in the third quarter.

The rupee rebounded 43 paise to 67.43 per dollar, reversing the prior session’s loss, as traders and exporters unwound dollar positions, Italian political uncertainty eased and optimism about Indian growth supported sentiment. It also strengthened against sterling and the yen but weakened slightly against the euro. India’s GDP data were due next day, following 7.2% growth in the October-December quarter. Brent crude traded near $76, below its May 17 high of $80.50, amid expectations of increased OPEC and Russian supply. Forward dollar premiums fell as exporters continued selling dollars.

At Sony’s CinemaCon presentation, Chairman Tom Rothman emphasized the studio’s commitment to diverse audiences, global franchises, originality, and quality filmmaking. Quentin Tarantino and Leonardo DiCaprio appeared to discuss an untitled, “hush-hush” film set in Hollywood in 1969, with Brad Pitt; no footage had been filmed, and Tarantino called it his work closest to “Pulp Fiction.”

Sony previewed “Venom” and “The Girl in the Spider’s Web,” starring Tom Hardy and Claire Foy, respectively, and announced a “Jumanji” sequel starring Dwayne Johnson for December 2019 following the reboot’s $956 million worldwide success. The presentation also promoted “Holmes & Watson,” “Miss Bala,” the animated “Spider-Man: Into the Spider-Verse,” and “White Boy Rick.”

Will Ferrell, Gina Rodriguez, Shameik Moore, Matthew McConaughey, and director Fede Alvarez appeared for various projects. Rodriguez highlighted Latino moviegoers’ importance, while Alvarez said audiences demand good-quality, provocative films. Across the presentation, Sony executives and filmmakers stressed the diversity, originality, and broad appeal of its upcoming slate.

U.S. Navy-trained dolphins and handlers joined Mexican authorities and international experts in a last-ditch effort to locate and capture the remaining vaquitas, a critically endangered porpoise found only in the Gulf of California. Beginning Oct. 12, small boats will use the dolphins’ sonar to find the animals, which number fewer than 30, and place them in a nearly completed floating sanctuary for study and possible reproduction. Experts called the risky plan unprecedented because vaquitas have never been held or bred in captivity. Mexico banned gillnet fishing in the northern Gulf, but advocates said broader habitat protection is needed. Mexico also banned fishing around the Revillagigedo Islands, creating North America’s largest unfished marine park.

The court granted CIT’s motion for summary judgment in part. Manuel and Esther Kitrosser, also known as the Kays, guaranteed and pledged collateral for loans and factoring advances provided by CIT to Top Form Mills, Inc. and Top Blush Corporation. Both corporations filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy in July 1988, and their bankruptcy cases were dismissed in January 1991 without discharging their debts. CIT later settled with the Economic Development Administration for $50,000 on its 90% guaranty of Top Form’s term loan and liquidated the Kays’ collateral in May 1992.

The court held that although Bankruptcy Code § 502(b)(2) prevented CIT from recovering postpetition interest from the bankruptcy estates, interest continued to accrue on the corporations’ nondischarged debts. Because the Kays’ guarantees were unconditional, they remained liable for Top Form’s factoring deficit and postpetition interest, as well as the outstanding term-loan balance. CIT’s liquidation of the Kays’ collateral was therefore authorized.

The court also held that CIT’s settlement with the EDA did not reduce its rights against Mr. Kay because the guarantee expressly permitted CIT to compromise with or release a guarantor, and the settlement reserved CIT’s rights against other guarantors. Whether the EDA could pursue the Kays for the $50,000 was immaterial because the EDA had asserted no such claim.

The Kays’ two additional claims in the amended complaint—breach of the covenant of good faith and commercially unreasonable conduct based on CIT’s reduction of Top Blush’s advance rate—were dismissed with prejudice as time-barred. They did not relate back to the original complaint because they involved a different transaction, required substantially different discovery, and had not been adequately raised in the original pleading.

Five days after the Las Vegas massacre, authorities said they had no clear motive for Stephen Paddock, who killed 58 and injured hundreds, or known link to Islamic State, which claimed responsibility. Law enforcement pledged to continue seeking answers.

The passage proposes Assesly.AI, an AI-based computer science laboratory management system intended to improve practical learning, discourage copying, and assess conceptual understanding beyond coding output. Faculty create and assign laboratories by specifying topic keywords, difficulty, viva duration, lab mode, descriptions, and instructions. The system generates a distinct question for each student, tracks progress, and offers proctored or non-proctored assessment through gamified conceptual quizzes, coding tasks, and an interactive viva. Students receive scores, feedback, error and readability analysis, and improvement suggestions, while faculty receive class analytics, plagiarism alerts, rankings, mastery insights, and the ability to override automated scores.

The platform includes faculty and student dashboards, role-based authentication, API-level access controls, lab scheduling and allocation, submission evaluation, progress profiles, heatmaps, completion statistics, and longitudinal performance graphs. Students may connect GitHub or Hugging Face accounts to publish selected work. Its question-generation pipeline uses an educationally fine-tuned Code Llama model to produce individualized, context-aware questions from faculty inputs, followed by semantic filtering to remove near-duplicates. After code submission, an AI voice assistant asks questions related to the assigned problem. Speech-recognition responses are scored against rubric-based answers to assess domain knowledge and reasoning.

The authors constructed a synthetic dataset of 10,000 programming questions covering classical machine-learning and deep-learning topics. Questions were created with Python scripts and ChatGPT; answers were generated in batches using Perplexity AI and manually reviewed. Each record contains an identifier, question, Python answer, faculty-assigned difficulty, automated score, and faculty score. The CodeLlama-7B-Instruct generator was LoRA-fine-tuned using these data, while the evaluator used all-MiniLM-L6-v2 embeddings and an XGBoost regressor trained on faculty-annotated submissions to score functional correctness, readability, and complexity.

Validation found substantial agreement between automated and faculty grading: Pearson correlation was 0.914, Spearman correlation 0.892, and Cohen’s κ was 0.69. Cross-validation produced an RMSE of 3.37 and R² of 0.861. Most prediction deviations were within ±5 marks, while the largest errors were concentrated in variable sequence-heavy tasks such as LSTMs, GRUs, Transformers, and reinforcement learning. Generated questions received an average faculty appropriateness rating of 4.7/5, and filtering substantially reduced redundancy. The reproducibility checklist specifies fixed-seed, five-fold cross-validation, a 90/10 generator split, an 80/20 evaluator split, and planned anonymized release of code, data, checkpoints, and embeddings.

The speaker accepts the Democratic Party’s presidential nomination, thanks the convention for nominating Senator Alben Barkley, and predicts they will defeat the Republicans. He attributes the party’s previous victories to its support for ordinary people, citing increased farm income, wages, and national income from 1932–1933 to 1947. He credits Democratic leadership with confidence and security, an active foreign policy, support for the United Nations, reduced trade barriers, and foreign aid programs.

The speaker sharply criticizes the Republican 80th Congress for failing to address high prices, housing, labor relations, the Labor Department, minimum wages, education, Social Security, health care, and civil rights. He also condemns Republican tax legislation and says the party’s platform promises measures its members refused to enact when they had the opportunity.

Calling Congress back into session on July 26, the speaker seeks action on price controls, housing, education, health care, civil rights, minimum wages, Social Security, public power, and displaced persons. He argues that voters should judge the parties by their records rather than platform statements and calls the 1948 election a continuation of the Democratic struggle against special privilege begun in 1932. He urges vigorous support for Barkley and himself to prevent another Republican Congress.

Plymouth MPs Ben Bradshaw and Luke Pollard defended the city’s naval capabilities and opposed speculation that HMS Albion and HMS Bulwark could be scrapped. The controversy followed Plymouth MP Johnny Mercer’s claim that Jeremy Corbyn posed a greater threat to the UK than ISIS, Russia or North Korea, prompting Bradshaw to accuse him of “losing the plot.” Mercer and Pollard warned that removing the ships would weaken Britain’s amphibious forces, threaten defence jobs and harm the Royal Marines. The Ministry of Defence said no decisions had been made and described the proposed cuts as pure speculation.

Archival annotations dated March 16–April 2, 1983, track the preparation, clearance, circulation, and distribution of State Department, NSC, Reagan Library, and telegram records on U.S.-Soviet relations. Secret/Sensitive memoranda were drafted by Palmer, Simons, and Napper, cleared by various officials, and forwarded through Eagleburger or Clark; one conversation record was sent to Moscow on March 24. Hill and Shultz reviewed several records, and Shultz briefed Hill after meeting Reagan on March 25. Reagan was asked to review two papers before meeting Shultz, and annotations indicate he later saw them. Confidential/Immediate Moscow telegrams of March 25 and 28 were distributed to defense, NATO, allied missions, and delegations. Clark forwarded memoranda to Reagan, Burt sent Shultz a draft on March 31, and Reagan initialed an April 2 FBIS report summarizing Pym’s rebuttal to Gromyko.

Berkshire Hills Bancorp reported first-quarter 2018 core EPS of $0.65, up 12% from the fourth quarter and 18% year over year. GAAP EPS was $0.55, including one-time Commerce conversion costs and an equity-portfolio mark-to-market. Core ROA was 1.04%, core return on tangible equity was 13.4%, GAAP ROA was 88 basis points, GAAP ROE was 6.7%, and the efficiency ratio remained below 60%. Tangible equity represented 8.6% of tangible assets.

Average earning assets rose 3% from the fourth quarter, while total loans grew 4% annualized and C&I loans grew 3%. The net interest margin was 3.36%, or 3.23% excluding purchased-loan accretion. The loan-loss provision was $5.6 million, and purchased-loan accretion was $3.4 million. Noninterest income was flat sequentially; mortgage originations totaled $480 million, with 65% purchases.

For the second quarter, management guided to core EPS of approximately $0.70, GAAP EPS of about $0.65, core ROA above 1.10%, and an efficiency ratio below 60%. It expected noninterest income to rise about 10%, mortgage revenue to increase roughly $4 million, the loan-loss provision to be about $1 million higher, and operating expenses to increase by a low single-digit percentage. Second-quarter net interest margin was expected to rise a few basis points before stabilizing in the second half. Full-year 2018 targets included core EPS growth of 17%–20%, core ROA above 1%, an efficiency ratio below 60%, and a core tax rate of 22%–24%.

The Commerce conversion and system integration were completed in March, with positive customer reception and deposit retention above expectations. Remaining Commerce cost savings were estimated at about $1 million and expected to be fully reflected in the third quarter. Second-quarter Commerce charges of $2 million–$3 million were expected to be the final such charges.

Average deposits rose 3% sequentially, including Commerce, and management targeted mid-single-digit annualized organic average-deposit growth in the second quarter. Boston had four branches and more than $400 million of deposits, including Commerce; Greater Boston and ABL loans were approaching $2 billion, excluding Worcester. Commercial and mortgage pipelines exceeded $200 million and totaled $344 million, respectively. Berkshire also opened a Simsbury, Connecticut branch, relocated its Downtown Albany branch, and expected 10 locations to use virtual-teller technology by year-end.

Management was bullish on high-single-digit commercial and overall loan growth as new Boston, New Jersey, and Mid-Atlantic teams ramped. It remained focused on integration, cultural alignment, cross-selling, market-share growth, and profitability rather than pursuing acquisitions, though it would consider opportunities opportunistically. No systemic credit concerns were identified; Firestone credit metrics remained strong, while the taxi portfolio had no losses, charge-offs, or delinquencies.
CLSA raised Arvind’s target price to Rs 538 from Rs 440, retaining its buy rating and expecting the proposed brands and retail demerger to unlock value. The stock closed at Rs 445.65, up 3.29%.

The study analyzes local and non-local self-energy effects in strongly correlated itinerant magnets using DFT+DMFT. It extends a multiband tight-binding Hubbard model with density-density Coulomb interactions by adding non-local self-energy contributions from charge and spin fluctuations, renormalized interactions, bare bubbles, and triangular Hedin vertices. Calculations used Quantum Espresso, Wannier90, the iQIST CT-QMC solver, and analytic continuation with ana cont.

For α-iron at 2900 K, standard DMFT approximately reproduces the nonmagnetic DFT bands while shifting a flat band along H–P–N. Non-local corrections strengthen the shift and produce splitting resembling the ferromagnetic DFT structure. CrO2 exhibits a comparable shift along Z–R–A and stronger non-local band splitting, again qualitatively matching its ferromagnetic DFT bands. For CrTe2 at 1600 K, strong band splitting already arises from local magnetic correlations because the d states are near half-filling; non-local corrections have little qualitative effect. In CrSb, both methods split the spectrum relative to the nonmagnetic phase, with larger splitting after non-local corrections.

Overall, band splitting occurs near van Hove singularities. Iron and CrO2 show pronounced non-local magnetic-correlation effects near their Curie temperatures, whereas near-half-filled CrTe2 and CrSb show strong local-correlation effects that persist over a broader temperature range. The resulting dispersive bands lack definite spin polarization and each carries part of the nonmagnetic spectral weight, combining itinerant and local-moment features. Their suppression of spectral weight at the Fermi level may affect transport, while their high magnetic susceptibility could allow weak fields to control spin polarization. The density-density approximation overestimates magnetic transition temperatures; extending the model to SU(2)-symmetric Hund interactions and examining other observables is proposed for future work.

The Triangle Game uses wing shooters, spacing, and precise screening to create an inside offense. Its continuity includes back screens, skip passes, back cuts, and lobs, with counters for switches, mismatches, show-and-recover, and post fronts. Post players counter high, baseline, behind, fronting, and double-team defenses with power layups, baby hooks, turnarounds, jump shots, pump fakes, drives, step-backs, and pass reversals. Late-clock specials include stagger-pop, double-base-cross screens, point isolation, and single- or double-screen wing actions.

The passage outlines strategies for defending the Zipper offense, which uses ball-side down screens to create scoring opportunities. It recommends a “show and recover” approach that avoids switching, forces the ball handler toward their weak hand, shows cutters off the screen, closes passing lanes, and pressures post players into rushed shots or passes. It also details an all-out “SOS” wing trap that disrupts the offense through sideline pressure, coordinated rotations, post fronting, closeouts, and help-side positioning, provided individual fundamentals and team concepts are executed correctly.

The passage urges Congress to regulate large interstate corporations and trusts through national action because state supervision is inadequate. Regulation should curb monopolies, unjust discrimination, fraudulent overcapitalization, and practices harming interstate trade without abolishing corporations, attacking legitimate wealth, or obstructing enterprises that reduce production costs. The goal is to make corporate power serve the public good while preserving competition and commercial freedom. It asserts that Congress’s constitutional authority to regulate interstate commerce is broad and not exhausted by existing law, recommending effective legislation and, if necessary, consideration of a constitutional amendment.

A June 1, 2001 compilation of reports focused on Enron, California’s electricity crisis and international energy developments. Democrats, now controlling the Senate, prepared to press for wholesale electricity price caps in California and other Western states, while President Bush continued opposing caps and ordered increased federal monitoring for price gouging. California Governor Gray Davis sought temporary caps and considered suing the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission. California investigators examined whether electricity wholesalers manipulated markets through repeated trading, artificial shortages, coordinated pricing and unnecessary power-plant shutdowns. Enron, Mirant, Duke Energy, Dynegy, Williams and Reliant were among the companies scrutinized. Industry representatives denied wrongdoing, and no findings had yet been made. Separately, California lawmakers considered shifting part of Southern California Edison’s rescue costs to large commercial customers, while Enron sought approval to supply those customers directly.

Foreign companies increasingly pursued buybacks of their Indian affiliates, lifting some related share prices. In Saudi Arabia, ExxonMobil and Royal Dutch/Shell were expected to lead two major gas projects, while Enron was included in a Red Sea consortium; final awards remained pending. India’s government pursued a package to resolve Dabhol Power Company’s dispute with the Maharashtra State Electricity Board over power costs and unpaid bills, including possible sales to electricity-deficit states. Fitch placed India on negative outlook, citing fiscal deficits, slow privatization and a worsening foreign-investment climate.

Thomas E. White became secretary of the Army after serving as vice chairman of Enron Energy Services. In Mississippi, Cogentrix began construction of an $490 million, 800-megawatt power plant with Enron subsidiary NEPCO as contractor; both it and a Duke Energy plant were expected to operate in 2003.

The paper introduces GEM, a framework for homogeneous single-particle cryo-EM reconstruction using 3D Gaussian Splatting. Classical Fourier-space methods can incur information loss, while real-space NeRF approaches require full-volume sampling, CTF application, and backpropagation, producing cubic memory and computation costs. GEM instead represents protein density as an explicit set of anisotropic 3D Gaussians parameterized by center, covariance, and density, occupying only nonzero-density regions. Its closed-form projection produces a 2D Gaussian mixture, enabling parallel rasterization and restricting each pixel’s gradients to contributing Gaussians. Training compares CTF-modulated projections with noisy particle images using an ℓ2 loss. Across four cryo-EM datasets, GEM achieves training speeds up to 48 times faster than existing methods, uses less memory than CryoNeRF, and surpasses CryoDRGN and CryoNeRF in reconstruction quality, consistently obtaining GSFSC resolutions better than 3 Å and often approaching instrumental limits.

The paper studies Bergman-type function spaces and projections in tube domains \(T_\Omega=V+i\Omega\) over irreducible symmetric cones, with an aim toward boundedness results and extensions to product domains. It introduces the rank \(r\), determinant function \(\Delta\), weighted supremum spaces \(A_\tau^\infty\), and mixed-norm weighted Bergman spaces \(A_\nu^{p,q}\), whose nontriviality holds exactly when \(\nu>-1\). When \(p=q\), these become the classical weighted Bergman spaces \(A_\nu^p\). The Lorentz cone is given as an example.

The weighted Bergman projection \(P_\nu\), the orthogonal projection from \(L_\nu^2(T_\Omega)\) onto \(A_\nu^2(T_\Omega)\), is presented through an integral formula involving the Bergman reproducing kernel
\[
B_\nu(z,w)=C_\nu\Delta^{\nu+n/r}\bigl((z-w)/i\bigr).
\]
Every function in \(A_\nu^2(T_\Omega)\) likewise has a Bergman kernel representation.

The paper also announces a sharp decomposition theorem for Bergman \(A_\alpha^1\) spaces in tube domains and poses related problems for harmonic function spaces in the unit ball and upper half-space. Similar sharp decompositions are suggested for Siegel domains, bounded symmetric domains, and minimal bounded homogeneous domains. Their proofs are based on integral representations, uniform Bergman-space estimates, and Forelli–Rudin estimates.

The final section begins reviewing symmetric cones, including convexity, duality, homogeneity, symmetry, irreducibility, and the connection with Euclidean Jordan algebras and determinant functions.

Tesla Motors, Inc. filed a Form 8-K dated July 2, 2015, reporting its publication of a press release that day. The press release was furnished under Items 2.02 and 7.01 and included as Exhibit 99.1; the filing states that the information was not deemed “filed” or incorporated by reference except as expressly specified.

AMD’s Tiered Memory Page Migration (TMPM) engine moves memory pages through an OS-visible ring buffer supporting parallel execution. Performance is improved by submitting commands with at least 16 pages, with maximum bandwidth at 128 pages per command, keeping the ring buffer sufficiently full, and limiting completion interrupts to command sequences rather than every command. A low-water interrupt can request a refill before the queue empties.

Several IOMMU structures cannot be migrated, including IOMMU data structures accessed through SPAs, vIOMMU page tables, pinned backing buffers, and the TMPM ring buffer and argument pages. The hypervisor or OS must not issue migration commands for them. For `PM_PAGE_MOVE_IO`, source pages must be DMA-mapped through IOMMU host page tables, with only one host page table permitted to map each migrated physical page. A host page table must also map the memory containing those tables. Because TMPM may modify host page-table entries non-atomically and update accessed and dirty bits, host software must prevent overlapping modifications.

TMPM firmware can be reloaded only when no operations are in flight. The hypervisor or OS must pause operation, tear down the ring buffer, and issue the reload through the BIOS-to-PSP mailbox protocol; disabling `PAGEMIGRATION_EN` is recommended. Reloading fails if the ring buffer remains initialized, and the replacement firmware must have the same or a newer version. Drivers must check `ENGINE_READY` before communicating. `PM_GET_CAPABILITIES` and `FW_VER_Major` determine the applicable reload path, including the EPYC Family 19h procedure.

The ring buffer must use `DEFAULT` or `HV_FIXED` pages, while argument pages may also use `HV` pages. A 4 KB parameter page contains 1–128 migration entries, and one ring-buffer page can hold 256 16-byte commands. Initialization requires a 4 KB-aligned, physically contiguous region of 1–255 pages, queue configuration, an optional interrupt, and setting `DRIVER_INITIALIZED`; validity and initialization status bits report configuration errors. The driver reports `PS_ASID_VAL` after initialization. Shutdown requires the queue to be empty or paused before clearing initialization and completing cleanup.

The firmware controls the read pointer and software controls the write pointer. Because commands may execute in parallel, completion order is not guaranteed; the read pointer passing a command indicates completion. Software may pause and resume processing through the `PAUSE` control, but in-flight commands can finish before processing stops. The six shared interrupt sources cover write-pointer errors, ring-buffer memory errors, empty-queue notification, threshold notification, command errors, and command completion. Queue errors can automatically pause processing, while per-command interrupts provide informational barriers. Precise halting requires the stopping command to be last, or only one command to be queued at a time.

Migration generally requires 4 KB-aligned physical addresses, while host page-table addresses require 8-byte alignment. Direct 2 MB migration is not supported by `PM_PAGE_MOVE_IO`; `PM_PAGE_MOVE_GUEST` permits aligned, physically contiguous 2 MB pages. SPA encoding uses 46 or 52 bits depending on encryption mode, and reserved or output-only fields must be zero.

`PM_PAGE_MOVE_IO` moves pages in SNP and non-SNP systems and can support active DMA. Software must prevent CPU access, perform required ATS invalidation and synchronization, and update CPU page tables after migration. With SNP enforcement, source and destination pages must be hypervisor-owned and remain so. `PM_PAGE_MOVE_GUEST` moves SNP guest pages without supporting concurrent DMA. Source pages must be guest-valid or guest-invalid, destinations must be pre-migration, and firmware validates addresses, page states, sizes, RMP ownership, and guest context before invalidating TLBs, copying data, and updating RMPs.

Errors are reported through command and migration-entry status fields, ring-buffer status registers, and potentially the Machine Check Architecture. A command can process up to 128 pages, and a hardware failure after batch processing begins may make all pages in the batch unrecoverable, potentially requiring system state to be saved before reboot.

A 2D-periodic DFT study investigated C–C bond formation from two adsorbed methylene units to ethylene on gold(111) surfaces containing one and three gold layers. Calculations used PBE with DFT-D3 dispersion, a local basis set, counterpoise-corrected adsorption energies, and 14 constrained structures along each reaction path.

Gold-layer thickness strongly affected adsorption, molecular orientation, reaction pathways, and energetics. The monolayer bound reactants and products more strongly than the three-layer system: reactant adsorption energies were −137.70 versus −115.49 kJ mol⁻¹, product adsorption energies were −46.00 versus −5.04 kJ mol⁻¹, and reaction energies were −432.06 versus −335.50 kJ mol⁻¹. Products were weakly bound and likely to desorb readily.

On the monolayer, the reaction had an activation energy of 4.78 kJ mol⁻¹. Methylene fragments diffused together, associated over a shared proton, and formed the C=C bond as that proton moved toward the surface. On three layers, pronounced fragment rotation accompanied diffusion, and the fragments associated at a larger separation before forming the double bond. This pathway required 52.10 kJ mol⁻¹ of activation energy. The monolayer pathway was therefore more direct and had a lower barrier. The results indicate that surface morphology influences carbon-upconversion energetics, while further studies should examine other surface indices, defects, layer numbers, and curvature.

In announcing his 1979 presidential campaign, Ronald Reagan called for a long-term diplomatic strategy, genuine international friendships, and stronger cooperation among the United States, Canada, and Mexico through a “North American accord.” He urged Americans to restore confidence, strengthen defense and industry, stabilize the currency, and support leaders who would remove governmental obstacles, protect liberties, and uphold religion, education, and family. Invoking America’s role as a “city upon a hill,” he emphasized self-reliance, self-discipline, morality, responsible liberty, spiritual renewal, and honorable government.

Reagan also criticized President Carter’s handling of the crises in Iran and Afghanistan, questioning the seriousness of vague threats against the Soviet Union, Pakistan’s exclusion from U.S. protection, and the contradiction of threatening action while unilaterally observing SALT I and SALT II. He characterized grain embargoes and threats to skip the Olympics as ineffective responses.

Microsoft Corporation’s September 29, 2015 Form 8-K describes a new reporting structure effective with the quarter ending September 30, 2015. Microsoft will report three segments—Productivity and Business Processes, Intelligent Cloud, and More Personal Computing—and use operating income to assess segment profitability. Corporate and Other includes unallocated corporate costs and accounting adjustments.

The filing presents recast fiscal 2015 and 2014 results. Fiscal 2015 revenue was $26.431 billion, $23.715 billion, and $42.953 billion for the three segments, respectively, while operating income was $13.087 billion, $9.871 billion, and $5.179 billion. The recasting does not constitute a restatement and does not affect previously reported net income, earnings per share, total assets, or stockholders’ equity. Exhibit 99.1 provides additional segment information and recast quarterly results.

Both teams played well, but Sutter said his team needed to convert chances against the Rangers. He said playoff momentum generally does not extend beyond games, while preparation and team familiarity matter more than morning skate. Because the team was fighting for a playoff spot, it expected immediate production from the player discussed. Sutter praised consistency, big goals, and role understanding. He called Jeff Carter a top NHL player who elevates teammates and compared his big-game experience and consistency to Martin Gélinas.

Investing.com highlights Tesla’s record Q3 deliveries of 497,099 vehicles, Citi’s raised Bitcoin and Ethereum forecasts, chip-stock gains linked to AI-memory demand from OpenAI’s Stargate project, and Bitcoin reaching a seven-week high near $120,000. A market review says the S&P 500 rose 2.2% in July and 7.8% year to date, remaining in an uptrend despite a weak start to August, weakening breadth, rising seasonal volatility and credit spreads, heavy tech positioning, and record U.S. electricity demand. The page also promotes AI-selected stock portfolios and warns that financial and cryptocurrency trading is risky and website data may be delayed or inaccurate.

After a loss, the speaker said the team would move on and focus on the next game. The goaltender was praised and not blamed, while the potential absence of a center was acknowledged, with others expected to fill in. Penalties and a poor start contributed to the loss despite a comeback, but distractions were dismissed as the cause. The speaker emphasized shared responsibility and said each game is independent, with no carryover, while deferring injury questions to the doctors.

On June 10, 2015, Amazon.com, Inc. held its Annual Meeting and elected Jeffrey P. Bezos, Tom A. Alberg, John Seely Brown, William B. Gordon, Jamie S. Gorelick, Judith A. McGrath, Alain Monié, Jonathan J. Rubinstein, Thomas O. Ryder, and Patricia Q. Stonesifer as directors. Shareholders ratified Ernst & Young LLP as Amazon’s independent auditors for fiscal 2015. Proposals concerning proxy access, corporate political contributions, sustainability reporting, and human rights risks were not approved. The Form 8-K was signed by Senior Vice President David A. Zapolsky on June 12, 2015.

At NVIDIA Corporation’s June 2, 2022 annual meeting, stockholders elected all 13 directors to one-year terms, approved advisory executive compensation, and ratified PricewaterhouseCoopers LLP as independent auditor for the fiscal year ending January 29, 2023. They also approved an amended and restated 2007 Equity Incentive Plan adding 51.5 million shares to the available reserve and an amendment increasing authorized common stock from 4 billion to 8 billion. The charter amendment was filed in Delaware on June 6, 2022. The Form 8-K included the charter amendment and equity plan as exhibits.
The aquarium’s “Suds for Sharks” event raised funds for sand tiger shark research, including identifying coastal areas sharks frequent and creating a local diver catalogue.

ICRA said the 2018-19 budget’s 20.8% rise in infrastructure capital outlay, especially for rural roads, housing, sanitation, irrigation and water supply, would boost rural economies. It also highlighted urban housing, priority irrigation projects, and deeper bond markets for long-term infrastructure financing.

Apple Inc.’s Form 10-Q for the fiscal third quarter ended July 1, 2017 reported third-quarter net sales of $45.408 billion, up 7% from $42.358 billion a year earlier. Gross margin was $17.488 billion, or 38.5% of sales, compared with 38.0% previously. Operating expenses rose to $6.720 billion, operating income increased to $10.768 billion, and net income rose to $8.717 billion from $7.796 billion. Diluted earnings per share were $1.67 versus $1.42, and the declared dividend was $0.63 per share.

For the first nine months, net sales were $176.655 billion, up 5%; gross margin was $68.255 billion, or 38.6% of sales; operating income was $48.224 billion; net income was $37.637 billion; and diluted earnings per share were $7.14. Research and development and selling, general and administrative expenses increased, primarily because of higher headcount-related and variable selling expenses.

Third-quarter product sales increased for iPhone to $24.846 billion, iPad to $4.969 billion, Mac to $5.592 billion, Services to $7.266 billion, and Other Products to $2.735 billion. Nine-month iPad sales declined 12%, while iPhone, Mac, Services, and Other Products sales rose 4%, 9%, 19%, and 10%, respectively. Services growth primarily reflected App Store and licensing sales.

Net sales increased in every geographic segment except Greater China during the third quarter: Americas rose 13%, Europe 11%, Japan 3%, and Rest of Asia Pacific 15%, while Greater China fell 10%. For the nine months, the respective changes were 11%, 7%, negative 12%, 10%, and 13%. Foreign-currency weakness generally reduced reported sales and gross margin, while the yen and other Asia-Pacific currencies had a favorable effect in their respective regions. Third-quarter gross-margin percentage improved due to a favorable mix toward Services, partly offset by higher product costs.

At July 1, 2017, Apple held $18.571 billion in cash and cash equivalents and $242.945 billion in short- and long-term marketable securities, bringing the total to $261.516 billion. Total assets were $345.173 billion, total liabilities were $212.748 billion, and shareholders’ equity was $132.425 billion. Nine-month operating cash flow was $47.942 billion, investing used $36.504 billion, and financing used $13.351 billion.

Term debt totaled $96.589 billion, while commercial paper outstanding was $11.980 billion. During the first nine months, Apple issued $21.725 billion of term debt, repurchased $25.105 billion of common stock, and paid $9.499 billion for dividends and dividend equivalents. The Board increased the share-repurchase authorization to $210 billion, of which $158 billion had been used by July 1. In the third quarter alone, Apple repurchased $7.5 billion of stock, paid $3.4 billion of dividends and dividend equivalents, and issued $8.0 billion of dollar-denominated and €2.5 billion of euro-denominated long-term debt.

Apple’s marketable-securities portfolio was primarily investment grade, and no investment was considered other-than-temporarily impaired. The company used foreign-exchange and interest-rate derivatives as cash-flow, net-investment, and fair-value hedges. Gross unrecognized tax benefits were $8.6 billion, and Apple said they could decline by as much as $700 million over the following 12 months. The company was appealing the European Commission’s State Aid Decision, which announced potential tax recovery of up to €13 billion plus interest. The IRS had closed examinations for years before 2013 and was reviewing 2013 through 2015.

Apple reported risks from limited-source components, industry-wide shortages, price fluctuations, and concentrated outsourced manufacturing in Asia. It also disclosed accrued warranty obligations of $4.299 billion and $8.5 billion of future minimum payments under noncancelable operating leases.

Ghana reaffirmed its commitment to child protection through the School Feeding Programme, capitation grants and free education. Policies on child and family welfare and justice for children were adopted, while child-protection measures were integrated into all 17 Sustainable Development Goals. The government is also addressing children living on the streets through interministerial cooperation and national identification registration. UNICEF’s Emelia Allan urged protecting children from violence, abuse and exploitation, empowering them, and ensuring equal opportunity regardless of race, location, sex, ethnicity or religion.

On-balance volume (OBV) is a volume-based technical indicator that measures buying and selling pressure by adding volume on days with higher closing prices and subtracting it on days with lower closes; if closes are unchanged, OBV remains unchanged. OBV generally follows price trends, confirming uptrends or downtrends through corresponding highs and lows. When price makes a new high or low but OBV fails to do so, the divergence may indicate weakening volume support and a fading trend. Conversely, OBV breakouts or breakdowns without corresponding price moves may signal trend continuation.

OBV’s slope can also track institutional or “smart money” activity. A downward slope with rising prices may indicate institutional selling, while an upward slope with falling prices may signal growing institutional involvement and a possible market reversal.

Joseph Granville introduced OBV in 1963 in *New Key to Stock Market Profits*. It was created for stock analysis and later used in markets such as commodity futures and foreign exchange.

An SPY backtest applied RSI to OBV and optimized entry settings. A five-day RSI with a buy threshold of 30 produced 337 trades, a 0.55% average gain per trade, a 73% win rate, a 24% maximum drawdown, and a 2.09 profit factor. The authors concluded that volume alone had limited value and that other indicators may be more effective.

Christine Wright, 60, a former headteacher and naturist featured in Channel 4’s “The Great British Skinny Dip,” disputed reports that she was forced out of teaching after being outed. She said she was never disciplined, sacked or fired, but experienced prejudice that affected her health and was eventually granted early retirement on ill-health grounds. Wright said someone contacted her employers to hurt her and defended naturism while challenging misconceptions, including erroneous links to paedophilia. She now manages the British Naturists’ legal and campaigns groups and helps recruit members after membership fell from 1,000 to 400. The documentary followed the group’s efforts to attract participants to public skinny dips across the UK and challenge stereotypes about naturism.

The lecture transitions from linear algebra to nonlinear systems and optimization, recapping singular value decomposition and the condition number of any matrix, which is defined using singular values and measures numerical error amplification. It then considers iterative methods for refining initial guesses and determining when to stop. The step norm criterion compares successive approximations using absolute and relative tolerances, while the function norm criterion checks whether \(\|f(x)\|\) is sufficiently small. Both can fail, so multiple criteria and independent validation methods—such as alternative solution methods, experiments, analytical limits, and asymptotic comparisons—should be used.

A system of nonlinear equations has the form \(f(x)=0\), where \(f\) maps \(\mathbb{R}^N\) to \(\mathbb{R}^N\). Unlike linear systems, the number of roots is generally unpredictable. Applications include nonlinear equations of state, energy and mass balances, and temperature-dependent reaction kinetics. The Van der Waals equation illustrates how a given pressure and temperature may correspond to multiple molar volumes. Determining vapor-liquid coexistence requires satisfying thermal, mechanical, and chemical equilibrium; using the Maxwell equal-area construction reduces the problem from three nonlinear equations to two, whose solutions can be viewed as intersections of curves.

A solution is locally unique if a sufficiently small neighborhood around it contains no other roots. The Jacobian contains the partial derivatives of the vector-valued function. By the inverse function theorem, a nonzero Jacobian determinant at a root guarantees local uniqueness, although a zero determinant does not determine whether the solution is locally unique. Numerical methods generally find locally unique roots most reliably.

Linearization approximates a nonlinear function near a point by a linear model using the Jacobian. This approximation has error of order \(\|\Delta x\|^2\) for well-behaved functions. Iterative nonlinear solvers construct a map whose fixed point is the desired root, repeatedly solving the linearized system to improve the approximation.

The Newton-Raphson method linearizes at the current estimate and solves \(J(x_i)d_i=-f(x_i)\), then updates \(x_{i+1}=x_i+d_i\). The linear system should be solved directly rather than explicitly computing the Jacobian inverse. The method provides the correct step direction, but its magnitude may be poor for strongly nonlinear functions. It can fail with poor initial guesses, singular Jacobians, or ill-conditioned systems near non-locally unique roots. A circle-intersection example illustrates convergence from an initial guess and the importance of the initial point.

Newton-Raphson has a local convergence property: when started sufficiently close to a locally unique root, it is guaranteed to converge. Its typical rate is quadratic, doubling the number of accurate digits with each iteration. Near roots where the Jacobian determinant approaches zero, convergence becomes slower or unreliable. Convergence is also classified as linear or superlinear by examining the ratio of errors across successive iterations.

The author describes social media as a pervasive distraction associated with procrastination, isolation, and mental-health harm. Cited research links heavier use with depression and ranks Instagram worst for mental health among 1,479 young people. After deleting several apps to focus on revision, the author resumed Twitter for live Eurovision coverage and later continued checking Facebook. They acknowledge that curated online lives can fuel unrealistic comparisons and worthlessness, while social media can also ease loneliness. Despite finding it draining and largely unproductive, the author struggles with alienation and misses receiving notifications. During exams, they are trying to replace scrolling with revision and creative habits, and recommend Breakfree and Menthal for monitoring phone use.

In *Bost v. Illinois State Board of Elections*, the Supreme Court is considering whether Republican congressional candidate Michael Bost has standing to challenge Illinois’s rule counting mail ballots received until 14 days after Election Day if they were postmarked by election day. The lower courts held that Bost lacked standing.

Article III requires a concrete, fairly traceable injury that an injunction would redress; generalized grievances and speculative harms do not qualify. The Seventh Circuit rejected Bost’s vote-dilution claim as a generalized grievance and his added observer costs as self-inflicted and hypothetical, noting that he previously won with 75% of the vote.

Before the Supreme Court, Bost emphasizes those costs as a “pocketbook injury” and argues that reduced electoral prospects and a diminished margin of victory also constitute concrete injury through increased campaign spending, reduced fundraising, and greater opposition challenges. The government supports Bost’s claim of standing on this specific rule but opposes his broader proposal that all candidates should have standing to challenge election rules. Bost argues that candidates have a distinct, particularized interest in such rules and that requiring proof that an election’s outcome would change would prevent minor-party candidates from seeking relief.

The study evaluated the Happy Ring, a finger-worn device using electrodermal activity, accelerometry, photoplethysmography-derived heart rate, skin temperature, and elapsed time to assess sleep. Thirty-six healthy adults were analyzed across 77 nights, including one laboratory night and two at-home nights. The device used generalized and personalized machine-learning scoring and was compared with laboratory polysomnography, the at-home Dreem headband, Actiwatch 2, Fitbit Charge 2, Whoop 3.0, and Oura Ring.

In the laboratory, sleep-wake accuracy was 0.92 for personalized scoring and 0.91 for generalized scoring, compared with 0.88 for Oura, 0.86 for Whoop, 0.84 for Fitbit, and 0.85 for Actiwatch. At home, accuracy was 0.92 for both Happy Ring approaches, 0.92 for Oura, and 0.89 for the other devices. Personalized scoring had significantly higher laboratory accuracy and specificity than comparison devices and generally outperformed generalized scoring. Sensitivity was 93–94%, while specificity was 70% for generalized scoring and 83% for personalized scoring, compared with 19–54% for previously studied devices.

Sleep-stage agreement was moderate for light, deep, and REM sleep, with personalized scoring showing improved classification. Total sleep time and wake after sleep onset did not differ significantly between laboratory and home reference recordings. Limitations included the small, generally healthy sample, use of the commercial Dreem device rather than traditional laboratory equipment for home recordings, and nontransparent scoring algorithms.

Tesla, Inc. filed a Form 8-K dated October 2, 2017, furnishing its press release under Items 2.02 and 7.01. The release was attached as Exhibit 99.1 and was not deemed filed or incorporated by reference except by specific reference. CFO Deepak Ahuja signed the report.

Oil prices were nearly flat Monday, initially falling on weaker Chinese refinery runs and demand concerns before recovering as possible Libyan supply disruptions offset gains from global stock markets. Brent traded at $51.73 a barrel and WTI at $48.62. Libya’s NOC investigated security violations at Sharara, while Zueitina workers threatened to block a tanker over pay. The Hanover Insurance Group will issue second-quarter financial results after market close on August 1, 2018, and webcast a discussion at 8:00 a.m. ET on August 2 via hanover.com. The property and casualty insurer distributes products through independent agents and brokers.

The author agrees with the scientific consensus on climate change but acknowledges being unable to assess the evidence and cites social and economic penalties for denying it. Questioning causation, the author notes that CO2 and warming are correlated and suggests warming may also promote economic activity and CO2 emissions, making causation two-way. The author argues laypeople cannot credibly evaluate climate science because they may not know what important variables are missing. Although climate scientists are considered more likely correct, the author says skeptics may be more persuasive, while scientists’ reliance on facts, models, fear, and criticism of opponents may weaken their credibility.

The passage then shifts to California’s law against handheld phone use while driving and promotes the WhenHub app, which uses a dashboard mount and shared maps to coordinate meetings without texting. It closes by encouraging readers to pursue projects with major potential and impact.

Gladstone Investment Corporation (GAIN), a business development company, invests in debt and equity securities of privately held, early-stage lower-middle-market companies. Its portfolio targets a 75%-25% debt-equity mix and includes loans, preferred and common stock, and stock-purchase options. GAIN earns interest and dividend income as well as capital gains from successful investments.

At March 31, 2017, GAIN had investments in 35 companies across 17 states and 18 industries. From 2013 to 2017, portfolio value grew at a double-digit annualized rate. In fiscal 2017, net investment income rose 8.2%, investments increased 2.9% to $501.6 million, and net asset value rose 8% to $9.95 per share. Investment exits generated $24 million in realized gains and over $4 million in other income.

GAIN paid a monthly dividend of $0.064 per share, an annualized $0.77 and 8.3% yield, and had paid more than 140 consecutive monthly dividends since inception. It also planned twice-yearly supplemental dividends. Its regulated investment company status generally exempts it from income taxes when taxable income is distributed to shareholders. Leverage was below 50%, assets more than tripled liabilities, and fiscal 2017 distribution coverage was 132%. Although rising interest rates could pressure income, 93% of its debt portfolio was variable-rate with a floor. The article expects distribution growth of 2%-4% annually and considers GAIN’s high distributions secure.

An Uber self-driving vehicle struck and killed a pedestrian in Tempe, Arizona, prompting the company to suspend autonomous-vehicle testing across the United States and Canada. The car was operating autonomously with a vehicle operator behind the wheel when the woman, crossing outside a crosswalk, was hit, police said. Uber is cooperating with authorities, and the fatality may slow U.S. efforts to deploy the technology.

The passage is an errata list for AMD Geode CS5535 Companion Device Silicon Revision A3. It catalogs defects involving PIT, DMA/ATA/UDMA, UART, USB, ACPI/PMC, PCI, LPC, SMB, GPIO, interrupts, and SMI behavior; issue numbers may be nonsequential because resolved issues are omitted. It details a PIT deviation: a read-back command should cancel an incomplete counter-latch command, but the CS5535 instead returns the counter value first. The impact is considered negligible because the sequence requires prematurely issuing a new command. The resolution is not to issue a read-back command before completing the current command.

CEO Steve Williams and CFO Alister Cowan will give brief remarks and answer questions, with Steve Douglas hosting. The webcast and Q&A details are available at suncor.com/webcasts.
