## Summary

**Overview.** "Formula 1: Unleashing the Greatest Racing Spectacle on the Planet," by Ben Shields and Cate Reavis (October 13, 2020), is a case study of Formula 1 (the commercial rights holder, referred to as "Formula 1") and the sport of F1. It examines the sport's 2019 performance, its technical and commercial structure, its stakeholders and fans, the management team brought in by Liberty Media, the business units built under them, and the strategic challenges facing the organization.

**2019 results.** The 2019 season's 21 Grands Prix drew 4.2 million attendees (up 2%), with average three-day attendance above 202,000 and three races exceeding 300,000; Abu Dhabi was sold out. Cumulative TV audience rose 9% to 1.9 billion, though unique viewers fell 4% to 471 million. F1.com recorded 1.1 billion page views and social following exceeded 25 million. A new Concorde Agreement was nearing consensus, covering prize-money distribution and rules effective 2021.

**The sport.** F1 traces to the European Championship of Grand Prix motor racing of the 1920s–30s; first races were held in 1946, the first Drivers' Championship in 1950 at Silverstone, and the Constructors' Championship from 1958. F1 is the top tier, with Formula 2 (from 1948) and Formula 3 (from 1950) below it, and Formula E (launched 2014) as an electric series. A season runs roughly every two weeks from March to November; only the top 10 finishers score (25, 18, 15, 12...), and a fastest-lap point was added in 2019. Teams build cars each season using 1.6-liter V6 hybrid engines from Honda, Renault, Mercedes or Ferrari (four per driver per season), Pirelli tires (three types, up to 13 sets per weekend), wings generating downforce, DRS, and McLaren-supplied ECUs handling engine, gearbox, ERS, DRS and telemetry. Chassis use carbon fiber of ~11,000 components with a 728 kg minimum weight. Races last about two hours, average 160 miles, with top speeds near 230 mph and a track noise of 134 decibels; drivers endure forces such as five times gravity under braking at Monza. The sport serves as a testing lab for automakers (Mercedes rotated engineers into its F1 team; turbochargers migrated to road cars), and Formula 1, the FIA and teams agreed to go carbon neutral by 2030.

**Strategy and data.** Up to 60 engineers and technicians trackside set strategy around tires, pit stops and undercutting, grid position, track type and weather; refueling was banned in 2009 with calls to restore it. Data has become central: a car with up to 200 sensors produces 500 GB per race weekend, available in real time to teams and analysts who model pit-stop timing and other trade-offs. Drivers are also measured second-by-second via KPIs, though fans typically prefer human decision-making under pressure.

**Stakeholders.** The three key stakeholders are the teams (600–900 people each; three of ten chief strategists were women; annual budgets from $130 million at Williams to $460 million at Ferrari, with Force India, Manor and Lotus bankrupt since 2014); the FIA (regulator and safety authority, with three stewards per race and rules requiring approval from Formula 1 and seven of ten teams including Ferrari, which holds veto power); and Formula 1 (marketing, partnerships, broadcasting, and paying teams from a prize fund sized by EBITDA, half split equally and half on a sliding scale based on prior-year standings, plus legacy bonuses such as Ferrari's).

**Ownership history.** Bernie Ecclestone, a driver, manager and team owner, convinced teams in 1981 to sign the Concorde Agreement guaranteeing every race, enabling broadcaster coverage and FOPA-negotiated TV deals; the FIA awarded him commercial rights in 1995 (from 1997 for 14 years) through FOCA. After financial trouble, CVC paid $2 billion for a majority stake in 2006, and Liberty Media bought Formula 1 for $4.6 billion in 2016. Carey, previously of Fox and DirecTV, was appointed CEO and hired Sean Bratches (CCO) and Ross Brawn (MD of motorsport, former Brawn GP owner). They inherited a profitable but bare organization: only a basic website, no digital assets or social media strategy, no formal marketing, promotion, sponsorship or research departments, and Ecclestone's ban on drivers' social media use. The goal was to turn F1 into a global entertainment brand like the NBA.

**Fans.** The fan base exceeds 500 million, 41% under 35; traditionalists are largely men over 50 in Europe and South America, while younger fans are growing in Asia, the US and China. Average TV viewer age is 40, with 14% under 25 and under 2% watching via streaming; younger fans prefer short-form content. Karting is expensive (up to $4,000 a year), while Esports and gaming offer entry points. Brawn cited fans' interest in technology and complexity; the global brand study found positive associations with drivers but perceptions of the sport as elitist and inaccessible, yielding five "North Stars": break through borders, revel in the racing, put the spectacular back into the spectacle, taste the oil, and feel the blood boil.

**Team building.** Carey, Bratches and Brawn set five pillars: improve the sport and team relations; upgrade events into spectacles; engage fans via traditional and digital channels; expand the brand (Esports, fantasy, tours); and grow globally, especially in China and the US. They hired new leadership (including Pat Symonds as CTO of motorsport) alongside retained staff from the Ecclestone era, with freedom to experiment and evidence-based decision-making; internally Formula 1 was called a "40-year-old startup."

**Business units.** By 2019 four revenue-generating units each had its own P&L. Promotion (30% of 2019 revenue, down from 34% in 2017) involved contracts with 21 promoters averaging $30 million annually, rising up to 5% yearly; Germany was dropped and Vietnam added for 2020. Broadcast (38% of 2019 revenue, up from 34% in 2017) included 14 free-to-air, seven pay and 27 dual agreements reaching 200 territories. Advertising and sponsorship (15% of revenue) included Heineken, DHL, Rolex, Pirelli and Emirates, plus an AWS partnership; Carey said sponsor acquisition had been harder than expected, with most of the 15 global deals struck before Liberty Media's takeover. Other revenue came from the Paddock Club (tickets up 7% to 80,000) and F1TV Pro, launched in 2018 with technical glitches; the digital and social media division lost $1.9 million in 2018. Research, led by Matt Roberts (from Sky, mid-2017), built post-race TV/digital/attendance reports, Nielsen and linguistic analytics, a sweat-gland engagement device with 100 fans, and WiFi analytics from 50 sensors; a race start-time shift to 14:10 GMT from 2018 raised end-of-season TV viewership 5%.

**The 2019 season and 2021 changes.** The season ran March 15 in Melbourne to December 1 in Abu Dhabi; Lewis Hamilton won the Drivers' Championship (fifth title in six years) and Mercedes its sixth straight Constructors' title, though a Ferrari collision in Brazil and a five-second penalty for Hamilton produced late drama, and Toro Rosso and McLaren podiums were surprises; Abu Dhabi was sold out with record Paddock ticket sales. The 2021 Concorde Agreement capped team budgets at $175 million (excluding driver salaries, marketing, and top three principals' salaries), and new cars featured simplified front wings, bigger rear wings, wheel-wake control devices, simplified suspension and 18-inch tires to enable closer racing. Off-track offerings included a James Bond car exhibition, Pirelli Hot Laps ($15,000), a Sotheby's auction in Abu Dhabi ($31 million, with Schumacher's 2002 car at $6.6 million), fan festivals in Shanghai, Chicago, Los Angeles and São Paulo, apps, podcasts, Esports, Fantasy League and Netflix's Drive to Survive, plus a "value exchange" offering personalized content for fan data.

**Conclusion.** Since 2017, Carey, Brawn and Bratches had helped turn F1 from a motorsport into a growing, younger global entertainment brand, but Bratches warned the arc would plateau if on-track competition were not fixed ("Competition elevates engagement"), and the sport remained committed to carbon neutrality by 2030. The case closes on the question of balancing sporting, commercial and societal interests amid climate change and an automotive industry in transition, with the 2020s framed as a crucial inflection point.

**Exhibits** cover Formula E (13 races, 476,000 spectators in 2018, 12 teams, $29 million loss on $149 million revenue and $168 million cumulative losses since 2014), car wings, ticket packages, Liberty Media consolidated and Formula 1 Group financials (primary revenue up $177 million in 2019; cost of revenue up $120 million, with team payments up $99 million; SG&A down $7 million), Grand Prix hosts since 2010, 2019 drivers' and constructors' results with team budgets, TV market reach, the 2021 car and the competition-to-engagement feedback loop.

NVIDIA’s Turing GPU architecture combines rasterization, real-time ray tracing, AI, and simulation. Its video encoder improves quality over Pascal and fast x264 software encoding while using less CPU, making 4K streaming possible. For VR, VirtualLink delivers power, display, and data through a single USB-C connector, while Multi-View Rendering, Variable Rate Shading, and other features improve flexibility, performance, and immersion.

Turing RT Cores accelerate bounding-volume-hierarchy traversal and ray-triangle intersection testing. Combined with hybrid rendering and denoising, they enable real-time ray-traced reflections, refractions, shadows, and ambient occlusion on a single GPU. NVIDIA reports performance above 10 billion rays per second and roughly tenfold improvement over software-based ray tracing on Pascal.

Turing Tensor Cores and the NGX platform support AI-based features such as Deep Learning Super-Sampling (DLSS), DLSS 2X, inpainting, AI-generated slow motion, and super-resolution. Other advances include Mesh Shading for efficiently rendering large object counts, fine-grained Variable Rate Shading, Texture Space Shading, Multi-View Rendering, bindless resources, and NVLink-based SLI. TU102 and TU104 support two-way SLI through NVLink, while TU106 does not support NVLink or SLI. The passage also introduces RTX-OPS, a workload-based metric that weights tensor, CUDA, RT, and integer operations by their expected utilization.

This preprint uses a problem-based political economy analysis to examine barriers to medical oxygen access in Peru. It combines 13 key-informant interviews with academic literature, grey literature, and policy reviews, identifying 7 relevant articles, 87 grey documents, and 23 policies.

Findings identify a “policy trap”: although oxygen became an essential medicine in 2010, Peru retained a requirement of more than 99% purity despite INDECOPI declaring it an illegal barrier in 2012 and WHO recommending at least 93%. This raised production costs, restricted smaller providers, and concentrated 92.6% of government-contracted medical oxygen among two business groups before COVID-19. Fragmented governance, decentralized procurement, political instability, and the absence of a national oxygen strategy further limited coordination and left rural, Andean, and jungle areas especially vulnerable.

COVID-19 exposed insufficient data, concentrated coastal production, weak distribution networks, and slow government response. Formally allowing 93% oxygen took two laws, three resolutions, and seven months. Small suppliers faced import and infrastructure barriers, while shortages led to high prices, informal sales, and unsafe cylinders. Delayed centralized procurement, fragmented hospital purchasing, possible corruption, and prioritizing ICU beds over oxygen supply compounded the crisis.

Civil society, religious groups, and private firms donated plants and supplies, helping install 496 oxygen plants nationally. However, slow approvals and inadequate maintenance, training, replacement parts, legal clearance, and technical support left nearly 200 plants unused, broken, or abandoned. Interviewees considered Peru unprepared for future emergencies and recommended a National Oxygen System incorporating demand forecasting, inventories, equitable distribution, quality control, infrastructure investment, trained personnel, plant maintenance, local production, and sustainable management of donated equipment.

The speaker argues that modern complexity, expanded scientific knowledge, weakened social restraints, and the effects of war have increased crime, lawlessness, and misuse of government power. This scoping review mapped methods for measuring socioeconomic status (SES) in health studies in sub-Saharan Africa. Following the Arksey and O’Malley framework, five databases were searched from January 2012 to June 2024; 19,669 records were screened, and 65 articles from 22 countries were included. Research articles predominated (93.8%), as did cross-sectional (52%) and cohort (23%) designs. Eleven categories encompassing 41 SES measures were identified. Asset-based wealth indices were most common (61.9%), including Wealth Index variants (28.6%). Principal component analysis was the predominant calculation method, used alone in 57.7% of asset-index cases and with other methods in 9.6%. Measures covered assets, multidimensional poverty, income, education, occupation, perceived status, and living standards. South Africa, Kenya, and Ghana were most represented. The review concludes that SES measurement should be standardized while allowing local adaptation. Limitations include no critical appraisal of study quality, methodological heterogeneity, and potentially incomplete literature coverage.

The medRxiv preprint describes the development and testing of a Maternal Vulnerability Segmentation Tool (MVST) to identify underserved pregnant women in Oromia, Ethiopia. Baseline data came from a community-based quasi-experiment involving treatment and control woredas. House-to-house screening of 1,614 households identified 1,189 pregnant women at least five months pregnant, from whom 470 women with vulnerabilities were sampled. A desk review and analysis of the 2019 Ethiopia Demographic and Health Survey identified predictors including literacy, distance to health facilities, parity, decision-making power, media exposure, and household assets. These informed a 20-item questionnaire covering economic, social, and information/service-access factors.

Exploratory and confirmatory analyses retained four items for urban-rural and pre-urban settings—rural residence, non-corrugated housing, lack of a women’s mobile phone, and distance from a health facility—and six rural items that additionally included women’s and husbands’ education and household mobile-phone ownership. Both models had acceptable reliability and model fit. Higher vulnerability scores were significantly associated with fewer antenatal-care visits and lower health-facility delivery rates. Scores above three indicated greater likelihood of home delivery, while one or more vulnerability points indicated greater antenatal-care vulnerability. Regression analysis found direct and total effects of vulnerability on service utilization; antenatal care was examined as a mediator, although the indirect effect was not significant in urban-rural settings.

The authors describe the MVST as a practical, low-literacy segmentation tool that could help community health workers identify women for targeted interventions and inform more equitable, cost-effective maternal health programming. It is not itself an intervention. The tool requires further real-world validation, testing in other contexts and across stages of pregnancy, and evaluation against maternal and child health outcomes in addition to service use.

This passage comprises Sections 6–16 and the appendices of a statistical analysis plan (SAP) for trial ZEA-DNK-02170 (protocol ZP4207-17086), a multicenter study (approximately five centers) in patients aged 6–17 years comparing dasiglucagon liquid formulation (1 mg/mL, 0.6 mL) with placebo, and GlucaGen (1 mg lyophilized powder) as an active comparator.

General considerations: results are reported in summary tables, listings, and figures using ICH E3 numbering; statistical tests are 2-sided at the 0.05 level, with significance declared at P ≤ 0.05. Continuous variables are summarized with means, standard deviations, medians, minimums, maximums, and valid cases (geometric mean and geometric %CV for PK parameters except Tmax); categorical variables by counts and percentages, with missing values excluded from percentage calculations. Tables are presented by treatment group with a total column, plus individual patient data listings. Analyses defined before unblinding are a priori; later analyses are post hoc, labeled exploratory, and identified in the CSR. SAS version 9.4 or higher is used for analyses and tabulations, Phoenix WinNonlin version 6.4 or higher for PK/PD analyses, with output in ASCII or RTF format, subject to SAS programming QC requirements.

Analysis sets: safety set (randomized patients receiving at least one dose, analyzed by treatment received), full analysis set (FAS; safety set analyzed by randomized treatment and planned injection site), and per protocol set (PPS; FAS patients without relevant protocol deviations). The primary endpoint is analyzed in the FAS, with a secondary analysis in the PPS; safety analyses use the safety set. Patient disposition, country, center, and US versus non-US counts are summarized.

Demographics and baseline characteristics include age, age group (6–11, 12–17 years), sex, childbearing potential, ethnicity, race, diabetes history, medical history (MedDRA version 22.0), and body measurements with BMI classes. Concomitant medications and current diabetes treatment are coded using WHODrug Global (March 2018) with prior versus concomitant assignments defined by date rules.

Efficacy: the primary endpoint is time to plasma glucose recovery (first increase ≥20 mg/dL from baseline within 45 minutes without rescue IV glucose), analyzed by Kaplan-Meier curves and a log-rank test stratified by age group and injection site; rescue IV glucose recipients are censored at 45 minutes. Sensitivity analyses, a stratified Wilcoxon test, recovery histograms, and a discrete-time Cox proportional hazards model (with additional homogeneity models) are specified, along with linear interpolation of recovery times as supportive analysis. Secondary endpoints cover glucose recovery at 10, 15, 20, and 30 minutes (Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel test stratified by age group and injection site, with non-stratified Fisher test as fallback) and glucose change from baseline (ANOVA with treatment, age group, and injection site). A hierarchical testing procedure at the 2-sided 0.05 level applies to dasiglucagon versus placebo only; GlucaGen comparisons are non-confirmatory. Baseline is the last non-missing value before first dosing, no imputation is applied, and no interim analyses are planned.

Pharmacokinetics/dynamics: PK sampling at pre-dose and 10–300 minutes with non-compartmental analysis and specified below-quantification handling; PD endpoint AUE0–30 min calculated in SAS, with glucose sampled per protocol schedule.

Safety: extent of exposure, rescue glucose timing, local tolerability, TEAEs (MedDRA version 21.0 or higher, causality and severity rules), AE overview and frequency tables, special search categories, laboratory results with L/H flags and change from baseline, vital signs, ECG including categorical QTc (Fridericia), and descriptive immunogenicity (ADA) analyses.

The appendices cover data presentation and programming specifications, SAS QC requirements (including Pinnacle 21 validation and documentation in the Program Status Document), and the list of planned tables, figures, and listings with mock shells. Changes from the protocol include reworded primary efficacy analysis with added sensitivity/supportive analyses and reworded secondary endpoint terminology.

Labor-force participation among young Americans without college degrees has declined sharply, while disconnected 18- to 24-year-olds reached roughly 12% in the latest data, exceeding levels recorded from 1989 through 2009. Experts cited a mix of economic, cultural, and psychological factors: reluctance to accept available jobs, declining benefits, stigma toward non-degree and blue-collar work, mental-health or substance-use problems, isolation, prolonged family dependence, and possible undercounting of freelancers in labor statistics. Proposed responses include expanding internships and apprenticeships through high school and community college and campaigns that reduce stigma around non-degree career paths. Experts said these efforts may help younger people but would not quickly reverse the situation for those already in their mid-20s or 30s.

The SPREAD offense is a 3–2 no-post motion system in which all five players maintain continuity, read defensive overplays, and exchange basic cuts. Players need strong passing and handling skills, and cutters should anticipate late passes near the basket. Overplayed players should immediately back-cut rather than resist pressure; if the pass does not arrive, they clear to a corner. Ball handlers should protect the ball and drive when given a “Green Light,” kicking out and clearing opposite if help defense appears. When a wing is overplayed or time is short, a corner may break into the middle for a back-door feed to a wing back cut.

Deepa Das Acevedo argues that recent restrictions on tenure and academic freedom reflect a decades-long, deliberate weakening of academic labor protections through legislation and university policies. She sees the rapid termination or suspension of tenured faculty after social-media comments following Charlie Kirk’s killing as evidence that universities are increasingly bypassing established dismissal procedures.

Acevedo maintains that tenure’s core justifications remain compelling: it provides employment security as compensation for academic work and protects academic freedom by guarding against arbitrary discipline. She rejects the stereotype that tenure reduces productivity, noting that available data do not support it and that academic work is often driven by commitment rather than simple economic incentives.

She also argues that tenure does not make universities unable to discipline faculty for misconduct, predatory behavior, plagiarism, or falsified research. Such cases can justify termination when institutions follow appropriate just-cause processes. However, the speed of recent dismissals—sometimes completed within 24 to 72 hours after social-media posts—shows that the practical protection afforded by tenure depends heavily on universities’ willingness to honor required notice, faculty participation, and other procedural safeguards.

BGU research involving 549 participants from 29 countries found that smiley emojis in work emails did not increase perceived warmth and instead reduced perceived competence. Emails without smileys prompted more detailed, content-rich responses. Smiling photographs increased perceptions of competence and friendliness, unlike emojis. Researchers also found that emails with smileys made unknown senders more likely to be assumed female, and advised avoiding emojis in initial workplace interactions.

This qualitative quality improvement study examined regional teaching for Stage 1 anaesthetic trainees across five hospital trusts in a UK deanery. Following the 2021 curriculum change, which added a training year and increased clinical, examination, and extracurricular requirements, the deanery lacked a Stage 1 regional teaching programme and had received low GMC survey ratings for regional teaching.

Six trainees and eight trainers participated in semi-structured focus groups. Researchers sampled tutors and school board members purposively and trainees by convenience, then analysed anonymised transcripts thematically. Participants described the new curriculum as unsettled and demanding, particularly because of primary FRCA examination pressures. Trainees’ differing educational needs made uniform teaching difficult. Major differences between hospitals created inequitable experiences, competition between sites, limited teaching capacity at smaller hospitals, and inconsistent support for educators.

Participants identified logistical risks for regional delivery, including travel, venue and rota constraints, funding, larger group dynamics, and the need to maintain quality and monitor feedback. Despite these concerns, all trainees and trainers supported developing a high-quality programme. Expected benefits included more consistent and exam-focused teaching, improved fairness, educator development, easier organisation at smaller sites, and greater cross-site collaboration. Participants emphasised clear coordination, appropriate expertise, trainee involvement, regular evaluation, and adaptation for long-term sustainability.

The findings led to planned actions including a Stage 1 trainee survey, review of teaching, study-budget and leave policies, and recruitment of consultant leads. Limitations included the small, potentially self-selected trainee sample and possible interviewer bias. The authors concluded that regional teaching could address disparities in Stage 1 training but required sustained stakeholder engagement, investment and quality control.

The study performed the first genome-wide association study of neonatal jaundice using neonatal, maternal, and paternal genetic data from nearly 30,000 families in Norway, with replication in 6,902 Danish neonates. Neonatal cases were defined by treatment, including phototherapy. The neonatal GWAS identified two genome-wide significant loci: the UGT1A* region and an X-chromosome locus near CHRDL1.

The strongest association was the UGT1A4 missense variant rs6755571 (p.Pro24Thr). Its protective allele was associated with a fivefold lower risk of neonatal jaundice in the Norwegian discovery sample and was replicated in Denmark. The effect was limited to the neonate and was not modified by maternal-fetal ABO incompatibility, although it was stronger at term and post-term. Colocalization implicated increased UGT1A1 expression in the colon, rather than the liver. The authors considered it unlikely that the variant acts directly through UGT1A4 bilirubin-conjugation activity and proposed that it affects UGT1A1 regulation or UGT1A1–UGT1A4 interactions, while emphasizing that the mechanism remains uncertain. The CHRDL1 association was also replicated and appeared to reflect a neonatal effect.

The maternal GWAS identified loci at UGT1A*, the X-chromosome region, and ABO. The ABO association was substantially attenuated after adjustment for genetically determined maternal-fetal ABO incompatibility, consistent with the locus tagging that incompatibility. The paternal GWAS detected only the UGT1A* locus.

Neonatal and adult bilirubin genetics differed substantially. The leading adult UGT1A* variant did not replicate in neonates, and SLCO1B1 was not associated with neonatal jaundice. An adult-bilirubin polygenic score predicted neonatal jaundice only when the UGT1A* region was included, indicating that most of the shared genetic signal came from chromosome 2. The findings indicate that genetic effects on bilirubin metabolism are strongly dependent on developmental and tissue context, although their clinical relevance in non-Nordic populations remains uncertain.

Larry O’Neal, a 44-year-old U.S. Border Patrol agent, was indicted on one felony count of possessing child pornography and pleaded not guilty in U.S. District Court in Bangor. Investigators traced a suspected file to his Houlton home and found child and adult pornography on his computer and external drive. He was released on bail, with trial set for June 6.

This patent application (a continuation of U.S. Ser. No. 17/217,357, itself continuing U.S. Ser. No. 15/597,084 and Provisional Ser. No. 62/337,806, "Collapsible Shelter") describes portable shelters and campers.

**Background:** Shelters trade off portability and protection. Fabric shelters are highly portable but provide little insulation, climate control, or security, while rigid, larger shelters offer better protection but are heavy, hard to store, and often require vehicle modification. The passage states there is no market option offering rigid shelter protection that is portable by any vehicle, can remain attached long-term without limiting vehicle use, and requires no permanent vehicle modification.

**Summary of the Invention:** A hard-sided, collapsible shelter/camper provides rigid, weather-tight, lockable shelter protection while remaining portable by most vehicles, including bicycles and motorcycles. It is a foldable rigid enclosure with three to eight sides, a roof, and a floor; sides, panels, roof, and floor may comprise an insulated inner core with an outer skin of composite material such as fiberglass or carbon fiber. When opened/expanded, it forms a hard-sided lockable enclosure; when closed/collapsed, all portions fold together into a weather-tight, lockable low-profile case (e.g., cargo-box-like) that can remain on a vehicle roof rack, sit in a pickup truck bed, be placed on a trailer, or be towed by cars, trucks, motorcycles, or bicycles, or moved by one or more people. Optional wheels may be attached for towing. The camper may provide a sleeping enclosure or a fully functional camper with climate control, electronics, and plumbing (fresh water, waste water, solid waste storage); wiring may run through the hard walls, floor, and roof, the roof may carry solar panels, and the floor may carry batteries or a small generator.

**Components:** A shelter may comprise a roof section, side wall panels (e.g., bi-fold or multi-fold), a front wall panel, a rear wall panel, and a floor section, all rigid or formed from strong rigid materials. It transitions between an expanded configuration, in which panels stand perpendicular to the floor and roof, and a collapsed configuration, in which side panels fold and are enclosed inside the shelter, parallel to the floor/roof. Collapsed heights may be under 50″, 30″, 24″, 12″, or 10″; expanded heights may range from 2–8 feet. Side panels may be two upper and two lower bi-fold panels; each section may include fixed or openable windows. The front panel may include a door with window, knob, latch, or lock. The roof may include solar panels coupled to batteries. The shelter may be lockable in both configurations, preventing entry or expansion without a key.

A bed system may include a mattress, mattress platform, raising/lowering and positioning systems, and notches, grooves, or tracks at different positions, allowing the bed to be raised for standing height below or lowered for sleeping without removing fixtures. The shelter may also include an internal kitchenette (stove, oven, refrigerator, dining table, chairs, sink) and bathroom (sink, toilet, shower, drain). A method of use comprises obtaining the shelter, transporting it collapsed to a location, unfolding upper then lower bi-fold side wall panels to the expanded configuration, and later folding them back to collapse the shelter.

**Panels and joints:** Wall panels may be rigid, folding, bi-fold, tri-fold, quadri-fold, or multi-fold, connected by hinges, connection strips, screws, nails, fasteners, clamps, latches, adhesive, or hook-and-loop. Lower side panel sections may hinge to the floor and upper sections to the roof, with weather stripping or gaskets at joints and latches/hooks/locks at corners. Slide latches may prevent panels from folding inward. Front and rear wall panels may hinge to roof or floor edges and latch to the opposite edge; their hinge points may be staggered so one rests above the other when folded. Panels may be joined by tongue-and-groove joints, rod hinge connector systems, or a mid-section connector forming a structural perimeter ring, which may include a hinged segment for the door. Openings and closings may be manual or powered via cranks, pumps, levers, pulleys, springs, pistons, motorized hinges, or motors.

**Roof, floor, and fixtures:** The roof may be flat, curved, contoured, or ridged, with a dropped perimeter edge tall enough to contain folded panels, a slightly shorter interior edge for better hinging and water tightness, roof rack and trailer attachments, antennae, interior/exterior lights (external lights may coordinate with a towing vehicle), and mounts for heating/cooling equipment. The floor may be flat with a raised perimeter edge containing the mattress and folded panels, an access panel for batteries and system components, and ports for water, waste, fuel, or electrical supply. The floor may include a dinette with storage and piston lifts, a kitchenette with sink, burners, refrigeration, and piston lift, a bathroom with vanity, shower, and toilet, and accordion wall fixtures. Figures depict perspective views of expanded and collapsed campers, transition positions, cross-sections of a panel with a rod hinge connector, a bed track system, and tongue-and-groove joint details.

Apple Inc. filed a Form 8-K dated January 26, 2016, reporting its first-quarter fiscal 2016 financial results for the quarter ended December 26, 2015. A press release, data sheet, and supplemental materials were included as Exhibits 99.1–99.3. The information is not considered filed under Section 18 of the Exchange Act or incorporated by reference unless expressly referenced. The report was signed by Chief Financial Officer Luca Maestri.

Pivot points are price levels calculated from the previous trading day’s high, low, and close. The central pivot point is their average, with additional formulas used to derive support and resistance levels. The article presents six day-trading strategies and backtests them on one-minute ES, NQ, RTY, and USD/CHF data from 2010 onward. None proved consistently tradeable; the strongest result was an erratic NQ strategy with a 62% win rate and average gain of 0.16% per trade. The authors conclude that pivot points are easy, objective, quantifiable, versatile, and useful for confirming support and resistance, but they lag price and showed low win rates. Although invented by floor traders and once used daily by prominent S&P 500 trader Lewis Borsellino, they are less widely used now. Some intraday ideas may still be refined through further research.

RWE Supply & Trading expects LNG derivatives trading to double or triple from 1.5 million tonnes in 2017, driven by physical cargo risk management and Asia’s shift away from oil-linked pricing. Physical LNG trading rose to 6 million tonnes, while JKM derivatives activity increased amid fragmented regional demand.

The lecturer announces that the next problem set will be posted a week later and its deadline delayed until Tuesday because it covers material discussed in class.

The lecture reviews the number four-vector \(N^\mu=n_0U^\mu\) for dust and its covariant conservation law, \(\nabla_\mu N^\mu=0\), which expresses conservation of particle number in both differential and integral forms. Energy density in a moving frame scales as \(\gamma^2\) relative to rest energy density, demonstrating that it is neither a scalar nor a four-vector component but part of a tensor. For dust, the stress-energy tensor is introduced as
\[
T^{\alpha\beta}=\rho_0U^\alpha U^\beta.
\]
Its components describe energy density, energy flux, momentum density, and momentum flux or stress. Energy flux and momentum density are equal when \(c=1\) and rest energy is included. The symmetry of the tensor is physically motivated through force and torque balance on a small volume; an asymmetric spatial stress would produce implausible microscopic rotational behavior.

The covariant equation \(\nabla_\beta T^{\alpha\beta}=0\) combines conservation of energy and momentum. In a chosen frame, it separates into differential and integral conservation equations.

A perfect fluid is defined as matter with no energy flow or lateral stresses in its rest frame, equivalent to having no viscosity. Its rest-frame tensor is diagonal, \(\operatorname{diag}(\rho,p,p,p)\), and its covariant form is
\[
T^{\alpha\beta}=(\rho+p)U^\alpha U^\beta-pg^{\alpha\beta}.
\]
Dust is presented as a perfect fluid with zero pressure. Relativistic gravity must use the entire stress-energy tensor as its source rather than selecting one component as in Newtonian gravity; the gravitational side is expected to involve derivatives of the spacetime metric.

Examples include a point particle represented by a delta-function-supported tensor constructed from its mass, four-velocity, and world line, and electromagnetic fields represented through the Faraday tensor. Electromagnetic energy density, Poynting-vector energy flux, and anisotropic Maxwell stresses are identified; a uniform electric field between capacitors illustrates anisotropic pressure and its potential gravitational contribution.

The lecture then begins a transition toward curvature and relativistic gravity by examining flat spacetime in curvilinear polar coordinates. Coordinate basis vectors are nonconstant and, in the polar basis, not normalized, so the metric acquires a nonconstant functional form. Coordinate-transformation notation and the dimensional behavior of its matrix elements are introduced as preparation for curvature and Christoffel-symbol concepts.

Lawton High School unveiled the second panel of its 22-foot Wolverine mural, funded by the class of 2014, depicting the school’s front and south side. Artist and teacher Kenneth Hobbs said it pairs with a 2010 panel funded by the class of 2006, portraying school history, championship teams and trophies.

Mike Kimel argues that research finds racial, ethnic, and language-minority children in the United States are underrepresented, not overrepresented, in special education. After adjusting for socioeconomic status, academic achievement, and behavior, the cited study found these children less likely than similar White, English-speaking peers to be identified with several disabilities. Kimel criticizes federal efforts to reduce minority overrepresentation and questions who benefits when children in need are mainstreamed.
Disagrees with Curtis: limit opponents' puck time and keep play out of their end. Brett's status is uncertain; Mike and Joe Nieuwendyk are praised as fast, skilled skaters.

Minnesota nonprofits supplement school-based mental health services, which are available in more than 80% of the state’s public school districts. Know the Truth, an offshoot of Minnesota Adult and Teen Challenge, uses personal addiction and recovery experiences to provide peer support for students affected by their own or their families’ substance use. Youth peer specialist Tiffany White meets students individually and in groups at three Twin Cities schools, offers community support, and advocates a harm-reduction approach while pursuing trust and open communication. Her work is funded through grants and contracts; a federal funding cut eliminated her position at Hastings High School.

St. Paul-based Restoration for All focuses on African immigrant and refugee youth. Founder Tolulope Ola said cultural misunderstandings can lead school staff to misinterpret students’ behavior or provide inaccurate diagnoses. The organization educates staff about refugee and immigrant experiences, offers screening groups, individual therapy, suicidal monitoring and culturally grounded mind-body practices, and has received state funding to expand services and school-based work. Coordinator Ruth Ezeagwula described efforts to address differences between how some families and schools discuss mental health.

South Korean lawmakers said the spy agency suspected two female North Korean agents assassinated Kim Jong Nam, the estranged half-brother of Kim Jong Un, in Malaysia. South Korean intelligence believed he was poisoned and reported that Kim Jong Un issued a standing order for his assassination, with an earlier attempt in 2012. U.S. sources also believed North Korean assassins were responsible.

Kim, 46, fell ill at Kuala Lumpur International Airport while preparing to travel to Macau and later died. Malaysian authorities conducted an autopsy, while airport CCTV footage showed a woman was involved. South Korean media reported that two women, believed to be North Korean operatives, poisoned him with a needle and fled by taxi, but Reuters could not independently confirm those details. Kim used the passport name Kim Chol, had lived in Macau, and had publicly criticized his family’s control of North Korea.

A woman fleeing gang violence in El Salvador traveled more than 1,000 miles with her partner, crossed the Rio Grande and was captured within an hour. After her two children disappeared, she said gang members wanted to eliminate her family. She was deported with about 100 others while her partner remained detained in Texas.

Despite President Trump’s claims that gang members were “pouring into” the United States, Border Patrol statistics showed that only 0.09 percent of 310,531 people detained in fiscal year 2017 belonged to Central American gangs. Most of the increasing number of migrants from El Salvador, Guatemala and Honduras were fleeing violence.

In El Salvador, MS-13 and Barrio 18 control poor neighborhoods, extort businesses, kill those who resist or are suspected of loyalty to rivals, and sexually exploit women. Police and soldiers also contribute to intimidation and violence, according to rights groups. Because the country is small, relocation offers little protection; an estimated 90 percent of deportees attempt to return within days. The woman returned to her gang-controlled hometown but remained unsure whether she would try again, facing her children’s empty home with no one waiting.

Councillor Kelly Elliot of Thames Centre is urging the Thames Valley District School Board to adopt a defibrillator (AED) policy, noting it is the only Ontario board without AEDs in every school. A West Nissouri Public School student fundraised after a local child died during soccer, and a parent donated $2,000 for maintenance. The board has declined to install the device, pointing to an upcoming Home and School meeting, and has declined to comment.
Belcher’s appeal was affirmed, with the opinion published at 60 Wn. App. 949.

Miami defeated Clemson 81-57, with guard Adrienne Motley surpassing Octavia Blue’s 1,724-point school record to move alone into seventh place on the Hurricanes’ all-time scoring list. Jessica Thomas reached 1,200 career points and led Miami with 18 points, while Motley scored 15 and Laura Cornelius 14. The Hurricanes led most of the game and held a 48-30 halftime advantage. Miami also hosted its annual Play4Kay game honoring late NC State coach Kay Yow. The 19-6 Hurricanes, 8-5 in ACC play, next face No. 14 Duke.

The October 12 “Inside UT Football” newsletter previewed Texas’s Big 12 South game at Colorado, calling it “do-or-die” for the Longhorns. Colorado had won six consecutive meetings with Texas since 1989 and sought a seventh straight win. Colorado coach Gary Barnett called Texas highly talented and deep but said the Longhorns’ offense could be energized by their Oklahoma loss.

Coach Mack Brown named Major Applewhite the sole starting quarterback against Colorado, with Chris Simms to play only if needed. The rotation could return afterward. B.J. Johnson was promoted to start at flanker, Roy Williams at split end, and coaches expected Kenny Hayter to receive more carries, while Brock Edwards could see more playing time. Brown also said Texas’s offensive struggles against Oklahoma resulted from falling behind early and trying to pass to erase the deficit.

Brown and offensive coordinator Greg Davis were reconsidering play calling, including greater creativity and a possible greater emphasis on passing to set up the run. Brown identified offensive leadership as a major concern and said Applewhite needed to step up. Other Q&A addressed defensive pressure on Oklahoma quarterback Josh Heupel, the expected return of Shaun Rogers, player roles, team incentives, and Texas’s chances of remaining in the Big 12 South title race. A win would put Texas in the conference’s driver’s seat, while a loss would largely end those hopes. Brown also rejected calls to replace Mack Brown and predicted the Longhorns could be a top-10 team next season.

Peter D. Baron renewed a 2,510-square-foot Melville office lease. Jersey Mike’s Subs, Hand and Stone Massage and Fortunoff Bedding leased at Plaza 200 in Carle Place. Hartford Fire Insurance and Hollander Legal Group leased in Melville; SCH Sheet Metal leased 11,500 square feet of industrial space in Ronkonkoma. Travis Phippen, wounded in the Las Vegas Route 91 festival shooting, filed a civil suit against gunman Stephen Paddock’s estate in Clark County, Nevada. His father, John Phippen, died from injuries in the attack. The suit seeks control and preservation of Paddock’s assets, safe-deposit boxes, income, claims and real property.

Scale AI billionaire Alexandr Wang urges 13-year-olds to spend thousands of hours “vibe-coding” with AI tools, comparing today’s opportunity to the early personal-computer era that benefited Bill Gates and Mark Zuckerberg. He says mastering AI coding assistants could give young people a major career advantage as automation and job insecurity reshape the tech workforce. Wang became a self-made billionaire at 25 and now leads Meta’s AI superintelligence team.

Alyn Family Doctors plans to close Gresford Health Centre and merge patients into surgeries in Llay and Rossett, citing insufficient staffing. The proposal has been submitted to Betsi Cadwaladr University Health Board, which is seeking patient feedback. A petition opposing closure has attracted more than 600 signatures, with concerns that longer journeys and increased demand could overwhelm the remaining surgeries, particularly alongside planned housing developments.

A penalty kick is a live restart: once the ball is kicked, it is in play, and defenders must immediately react to a save, block, or rebound. Before the kick, all players except the kicker and goalkeeper must be at least 10 yards from the penalty mark, behind it, inside the field, and outside the penalty area. They cannot enter the area or arc until the kicker touches the ball and it clearly moves forward; the referee’s whistle or motions do not authorize movement.

Defenders should sprint to designated positions, beat attackers to them, hold their ground if positioned first, and stand beside rather than jostle an attacker who arrived first. Every defender must be prepared to pursue rebounds, avoid overrunning the ball, and either turn away from their own goal or block the ball before clearing it. If the goalkeeper blocks the ball, the kicker may follow up immediately; a crossbar or post rebound does not permit the kicker to touch it again. After securing or clearing the ball, defenders should transition quickly into attack and look for an outlet pass.

An early defender entry results in a goal if scored; otherwise, the kick is retaken. Defenders must also avoid being deceived by stutter-steps or similar movements. A rare “tap” kick may involve an initial tap followed by a teammate’s shot, potentially giving the original kicker an assist. Coaching should emphasize positioning, follow-up play, clearing, and counterattacking. These procedures differ from shootouts, when kicks are not live and no follow-up is allowed.

A disclosed gaming machine, control method, and program synchronize the display timing of game events with the beat of background music (BGM). The controller starts the game and BGM, determines event-display timing from stored tempo data containing beat information, dynamically configures animation data for those timings, and displays the animations. This addresses visual timing lag and discomfort caused when only event audio was synchronized with the BGM beat.

The gaming machine includes displays, a speaker, storage, and a controller, and may also include player-operation controls, event-sound output, rhythm-pattern data, and illumination. Display timing may depend on player input or randomly generated events, while rhythm patterns can sequence multiple events according to the BGM’s rhythm. The invention is also applicable to slot games, in which reel spin and stop animations are aligned with on-beat frame counts, and to bonus games with randomly selected scenarios and timed animations.

In an illustrated slot-game implementation, virtual reel strips provide symbols on a grid, and the controller randomly determines reel stops, generates corresponding animations, performs winning determinations, and pays awards. BGM-related data stores beat timings and loop positions, while separate rhythm-pattern data defines event sequences. The disclosed technique may also be applied to poker, blackjack, bingo, keno, wheel games, pachinko, and pachinko slot machines.

The incoming chief executive expresses gratitude for the confidence of his fellow citizens while acknowledging anxiety about the responsibilities of office. He credits the Constitution and continued self-government with national prosperity, expanded commerce and territory, individual liberty, and successful resistance to foreign threats. He argues that the Union should be preserved through an enlightened, virtuous, and independent citizenry, and that future dangers from abroad require adequate coastal defenses, a well-regulated army and navy, and a properly organized, trained militia.

He also recommends constitutional road and canal construction to strengthen interstate ties, domestic support for manufacturing, friendly and liberal relations with Indian tribes, careful management of public finances and regular accountability for public spending, and continued reduction of the national debt. Emphasizing peace, national honor, unity, and harmony, he pledges to preserve the principles of republican government, protect citizens’ rights, defend national independence, and support the country’s future prosperity.

This study explored stakeholder views on the potential of metagenomic next-generation sequencing (mNGS) for routine infectious disease diagnostics. Unlike conventional approaches that require prior knowledge of suspected pathogens, mNGS is culture-independent and hypothesis-free, enabling simultaneous detection of pathogens, antimicrobial-resistance profiles, functional genes and virulence genes from a sample. Despite its potential to shorten diagnosis and support targeted treatment, clinical adoption remains limited.

An interpretative phenomenological approach informed the study. Ten participants from clinical, academic and public-health roles, with varying levels of mNGS knowledge and based across six English regions, completed 30–60-minute semi-structured interviews between July and November 2021. Interviews were transcribed and analysed through open coding and thematic analysis, with reliability auditing and participant review. Ethical approval was obtained.

Five themes emerged. First, participants regarded mNGS as a complementary diagnostic tool rather than a universal replacement, with cost, speed, clinical applicability and equitable access influencing its use. Second, implementation requires physical, digital and workforce infrastructure. Barriers included slow turnaround times from centralized laboratories, limited bioinformatics expertise, staffing shortages, inadequate data storage, research-only reagents, accreditation difficulties, validation and standardisation challenges, and the need for clinically useful reporting. Local sequencing capacity could improve speed. Third, genomic data sharing creates tension between open research practices and patient privacy, while centralized repositories could strengthen surveillance and disease understanding. Fourth, COVID-19 sequencing demonstrated metagenomics’ public-health value, accelerated manufacturing capacity and supported wider acceptance of sequencing. Fifth, communication within hospitals, between hospitals, and among healthcare, academic, public and commercial stakeholders was considered essential for coordinated implementation.

The study concludes that routine mNGS development should address the complete clinical workflow, including cost-effectiveness, rapid results, infrastructure, workforce training, data systems, accreditation and communication. Metagenomics could identify rare or unknown pathogens and improve treatment guidance and surveillance, but stronger evidence on performance, clinical decision-making and economic value is required. The findings may not represent England’s Southwest and Northeast regions, which had no participants.

Susumu Kitagawa, Richard Robson and Omar Yaghi won the 2025 Nobel Prize in Chemistry for their work on metal-organic frameworks, porous molecular structures that can store gases, water and other chemicals. Their research includes Robson’s copper-based framework from the late 1980s, Kitagawa’s gas-absorbing MOFs and Yaghi’s 1999 material, whose few grams offered the surface area of a soccer field. Applications include collecting water from air, capturing industrial carbon dioxide and extracting forever chemicals. The scientists shared the 11 million Swedish kronor prize.

NHS staff recreated a 1927 photograph of a matron, her assistant and nurses at Sandwell Hospital, then known as Hallam Hospital, to mark the NHS’s 70th anniversary. The image was found in a broom cupboard and kept by electronic patient record trainer Sue Woodcock. The recreation involved 14 Trust staff, and recovered images were displayed at a hospital tea party.

Andrew Lo uses an auction of an unidentified iPod to illustrate how limited information affects prices. He then discusses the federal government’s takeover of Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac, explaining that the government-backed securities would support mortgage markets, stabilize financial markets, and shift losses to taxpayers, while raising concerns about inflation and the institutions’ size and risk management. He connects the auction to broader questions about asset valuation under uncertainty.

Lo defines an asset as a sequence of current and future cash flows whose value depends on the time of evaluation. Under certainty, he treats cash flows at different dates like different currencies, converting them into today’s dollars with market-determined discount factors, summarized by an interest rate or opportunity cost of capital. This produces net present value as the sum of discounted cash flows and makes investment decisions simple once valuation is known. Future lectures will address annuities, perpetuities, compounding, inflation, and fixed-income securities.

The November 7, 2000 VentureWire issue reports private-company business news, led by Broadcom’s agreement to acquire processor-chip developer SiByte for up to $2 billion in stock. Alta Partners is seeking $275 million–$325 million for a third fund focused on IT and life sciences, while eStellarNet raised $30 million for its first institutional round. Online furniture retailer Furniture.com shut down and laid off 76 of 88 employees after struggling to raise capital; customers with unrefunded orders were promised refunds within about 60 days.

Numerous funding rounds were reported, including $60 million for wireless broadband provider Dotcast, $50 million for wireless systems integrator Stellcom, $35 million for Colorado MicroDisplay, $30 million each for collaborative software maker Centric and e-commerce purchasing provider Frictionless Commerce, $25 million for Magnet Communications, $20 million for RealPage, $19.8 million for Cymerc, $17.3 million for rental exchange Viva, and $16 million for WebCollage. Other financing included rounds for Lumentis, Presence Works, RedSiren, Kick.com, ManageStar, WiredPocket, DoubleTrade, Tonos, Times N Systems, GenuOne, Neolinear, MetaEdge, Traq-wireless, GHR Systems and Freever. Corporate investments were also announced by CIT in CAMP Systems, IBM, Bank of America and Prudential in NetStruxr, and Motorola in Geyser Networks.

Among adverse developments, Divine interVentures laid off 18 people, or 43% of its partner development group, as it reduced costs, while Eos-backed Foodoo.com ceased operations and planned voluntary liquidation after failing to secure further funding.

New offerings included one-hour Internet and WAP delivery service Expry in Italy and Redleaf Group’s Redleaf Secure Systems platform. eFrenzy became Nextdoor Networks, HomePage.com became Frontera, and Biztro became Rivio.

M&A activity included Sonus Networks’ agreement to acquire Telecom Technologies for roughly $451 million in shares plus contingent shares, and InfoSpace’s approximately $128 million stock acquisition of Locus Dialogue. Meritage acquired Thought Interactive and Castle Point Systems; Lake Capital acquired DVC; and Timera acquired SoftThought Systems.

The issue also covered new directors and CEOs at eChips, Ideas Hub, Actelis Networks, Outlaw Technologies, Disappearing, Bridgewater Systems, IP Globalnet and Adwise. Venture fund developments included new or planned funds at Veritas, Osprey Ventures, Vertex Management Israel, Verity and WestBridge Capital, while Dresdner Kleinwort Benson acquired Elderstreet Investments and committed €75 million to a successor fund. VentureWire also corrected Tantivy’s location to Melbourne, Florida.

At Puerto Cortés, Sergio Romero visits the bay where the Avontuur lies: a two-masted, canvas-sailed schooner powered by wind instead of bunker fuel. The 97-year-old vessel reached Honduras from Europe with a small crew, collecting and delivering cargo through the Caribbean.

CUPA-HR’s report examines Title IX staffing, organizational placement, workforce growth, demographics, and compensation in higher education. Title IX regulations have expanded significantly since 2020, creating complex procedures for addressing sexual harassment and assault and increasing the need for dedicated institutional expertise.

In a 2024 poll of 432 institutions, Title IX staff were most often housed in Human Resources (29%) and Student Affairs/Dean of Students/Student Services (28%), followed by Compliance and Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion (11% each). Dedicated positions include heads of institutional Title IX compliance, deputy heads, and investigators.

Between 2019–20 and 2023–24, the share of institutions with at least one dedicated full-time Title IX position increased from 33% to 43%. Yet 56% still had no dedicated position, 26% had one, and 17% had multiple. Total positions rose from 542 to 746, a 38% increase; deputy head positions grew 58% and investigator positions 85%, compared with 7% for heads. In 2023–24, 31% of institutions had a full-time compliance head, 16% an investigator, and 12% a deputy head.

Dedicated staffing was most common at doctoral institutions: 64% had at least one Title IX position, compared with 45% of baccalaureate, 39% of master’s, and 19% of associate’s institutions. Thirty-six percent of doctoral institutions had multiple Title IX positions, compared with fewer than 12% in other classifications.

Women held 77% of Title IX positions, compared with 62% of higher education professional positions overall. Black women held 13%, versus 6% of the professional workforce, while Asian professionals held 2%, versus 6% overall.

Median salaries were $96,714 for compliance heads, $84,931 for deputy heads, and $75,000 for investigators—all above the $66,000 median for professional positions overall. Black women earned $1.16 for every $1 earned by White men, while Black men, Hispanic or Latina women, and White women earned $1.10, $1.04, and $1.03, respectively.

The report recommends reassessing officers’ responsibilities and resources, creating dedicated positions where needed, and preparing for compliance with either the 2020 regulations or new rules as the legal and regulatory landscape develops.
Effort was consistent, but poor teamwork and the last game prompted calls for communication and follow-through. Injuries required others to step up, with hopes for Griz and Z’s return.

Berkshire Hathaway sold 10.6 million General Electric shares in the second quarter of 2017, ending a stake acquired after lending GE roughly $3 billion in 2008. Combined with hundreds of millions in dividends, the investment generated more than $1 billion in profit. The sale coincided with Jeff Immelt stepping down as GE’s CEO and a nearly 20% year-to-date decline in its shares.

Berkshire also bought Synchrony Financial shares and increased holdings in Bank of New York Mellon and Apple, while Warren Buffett had recently sold most of his Walmart stake. Quarterly filings showed Appaloosa Management selling its entire SPDR S&P 500 ETF position, George Soros buying more than $1 billion of the PowerShares QQQ Trust, and Viking Global purchasing 12.3 million Wells Fargo shares for about $680 million. Wells Fargo was addressing sales-practice investigations, consumer-lending problems and expected board changes.

Gary Allen Darnell, 45, a convicted sex offender, was arrested after allegedly approaching children near a Grafton river and offering them fishing poles. He was charged with loitering within 500 feet of a park, a Class 4 felony, and prosecutors said they would seek the maximum sentence if convicted.

A king asks the United States to formally recognize his kingdom as a sovereign and independent state. Although earlier agreements with naval commanders of European nations reportedly lacked government sanction, he says foreign consuls, commercial agents, and vessel commanders already treat his dominions as sovereign. He cites major reforms achieved over twenty-three years: a written and systematized language, widespread schools, a national library, a limited representative monarchy, civil and criminal codes, an annual legislature, courts, and jury trials. Foreigners’ use of these courts and officials’ demands for full protection of persons and property are presented as evidence of their confidence in his government. He also argues that independence benefits commercial nations because his dominions are a center of the world’s whale fishery, lie on the principal route between North America and Asia, and offer advantageous vessel repairs and abundant supplies.

The study explored kindergarten teachers’ views and experiences regarding the importance and teaching of visual arts, and the challenges and opportunities involved in integrating them into preschool curricula. Data were collected in February 2024 through an online questionnaire completed voluntarily by 65 public and private kindergarten teachers in Piraeus. The questionnaire contained 16 closed and five open questions, used a five-point Likert scale for closed responses, and underwent expert review and pilot testing. Responses were analyzed with SPSS 21 and thematic analysis.

Teachers overwhelmingly regarded visual arts as crucial to preschool education and believed they support creativity, imagination, intellectual and motor development, emotional expression, social interaction, cooperation, and self-confidence. Most considered their curriculum integration satisfactory, preferred free and exploratory approaches, valued experimentation with varied materials and tools, and agreed that positive feedback encourages participation.

The principal reported challenge was classroom management, cited by 86.1% of participants. Other difficulties involved limited time, resources, equipment, space, and external factors such as parental ignorance. Suggested responses included patience, individualized support, flexible methods, classroom roles, games, diverse materials, continuous feedback, demonstrations, and recognition of children’s achievements. Demographic characteristics did not significantly affect teachers’ perceptions. Despite their positive attitudes, most participants lacked visual-arts specialization. The study recommends professional development, adequate art supplies and equipment, dedicated art spaces, and collaborative support. Limitations include the electronic survey method, the Piraeus-only sample, and the absence of qualitative interviews for deeper exploration.

Spring ISD is investigating a Dueitt Middle School teacher accused of calling African American students a racial slur. He was placed on administrative leave, other students corroborated the report, and the investigation remains ongoing.

The German ambassador reported Germany’s willingness to state confidential peace terms, including surrendering Belgium while preserving transit rights on the Meuse, maintaining neutral buffer states, restoring Russian territory, treating Serbia and Roumania properly, and indemnifying Belgium. He said Britain’s allied maximum demands were considered infeasible, while its minimum demands would likely cause conflict with its allies, and that U.S. pressure might prompt Britain to reveal its terms.

The Greek government welcomed the U.S. peace proposal and emphasized Greece’s suffering despite its neutrality, including foreign occupation, disarmament, blockade, and starvation risks. Unable to communicate with one belligerent and facing settlement difficulties with the other, Greece nonetheless supported the president’s peace initiative and expressed readiness to cooperate with neutral states to secure a stable peace guaranteeing all states’ rights, sovereignty, and independence.

The passage outlines SOS defense for disrupting side-screen and roll offenses. Below the free-throw line extended, when O5 sets a side screen for O3, X5 traps O3 with X3 before the screen is set. X3 forces O3 toward the base checkpoint while X1 and X2 move to helpside positions and X4 fronts O5. Passes out of the trap to O1, O2, or O5 are met with quick closeouts, set positions, snuggle/front denials, and helpside rotations.

Above the free-throw line extended, X4 executes an aggressive contact switch by bumping the screener and hedging into the ballhandler’s path, while X3 fronts the screener. X4 pressures the ballhandler toward a checkpoint, assumes a smother position, and denies the post passing lane; X3 uses a slip front, and the remaining defenders hold weak-side I positions.

In the “All Out” disruption, the defense traps point guard O1 with X5 before a screen or pass can develop. Defenders rotate as the ball is passed, deny return passes, close out to wings, front low-post players, and maintain helpside positions. A pass to O5 on the base roll triggers a trap by X5 and X4 and further rotation options.

Whitman Howard raised Produce Investments’ target price to GBX 240 from GBX 210 and retains a buy rating. Shore Capital reiterated buy, while Numis reiterated buy with a GBX 286 target. Shares traded up 0.54% to GBX 187 on volume of 10,000; market capitalization was GBX 50.52 million. The company declared a GBX 5.03 dividend, payable December 5, for shareholders of record on November 2, with a 2.75% yield. It operates in fresh, processing and other segments, growing, sourcing, packing and marketing potatoes, daffodil bulbs and flowers.

On November 18, 2022, Amazon.com, Inc. entered a 364-day unsecured revolving credit agreement with JPMorgan Chase Bank, N.A. as administrative agent and other lenders. The facility provides up to $10.0 billion and may be extended for another 364 days. Initial interest is SOFR plus 0.45%, with a 0.05% commitment fee on undrawn amounts. Borrowings may support general corporate purposes, including backing notes issued under Amazon’s commercial paper program. The agreement includes customary representations, covenants, and default provisions but no financial covenants. The agreement was filed as Exhibit 10.1.

Marines tested Instant-Eye drones for confined-area surveillance. Task-Force-Southwest is scheduled to deploy to Afghanistan; Marines also trained with M67 grenades. The Marine Corps presented 91-year-old Lee Anderson the Purple Heart for an Iwo Jima injury.

Three University of Dayton women reported a naked man entering their bedrooms early Wednesday. Police are collecting evidence and investigating. The suspect was described as a white man in his mid-20s with brown curly hair.

The address reports national prosperity, advances in agriculture, manufacturing, commerce, navigation, revived public confidence, and growing national credit, citing rapid Bank of the United States subscriptions as evidence of confidence in the government. It describes frontier policy combining treaties and moderation toward friendly Indigenous groups with military action against hostile groups; some operations succeeded, peace overtures continued, and some individuals accepted U.S. protection. Recommended measures include impartial justice, regulated land alienation, equitable commerce, selective adoption of civilization, protection of Indigenous interests, and penalties for treaty violations.

The distilled spirits law has been implemented through district surveys, officer appointments, and compensation assignments, though some compensation rates may require revision. Discontent caused by the tax’s novelty and misunderstanding is expected to diminish after explanation, and minor modifications may be made consistent with the law’s purpose.

A permanent federal district of ten square miles has been fixed on both sides of the Potomac, including Alexandria and Georgetown, and a city has been planned. The census indicates a population approaching four million. Additional loans have been obtained in Holland, while domestic and state debt subscriptions have broadly fulfilled the financing law, and established revenues appear sufficient to avoid new taxes barring unforeseen needs.

Proposed treaties with the Cherokees and Six Nations await congressional consideration. The address also identifies unresolved legislative priorities: organizing the militia, establishing magazines, arsenals, and fortifications; expanding postal services and roads; creating a mint to relieve currency disorders; adopting uniform weights and measures; and providing for the sale of vacant lands as a source for repaying the public debt.

A hockey coach discusses London Knights forward Corey Perry, praising his poise under pressure, noting his Memorial Cup playoff experience the prior year as a valuable learning opportunity, and describing him as slippery, effective down low with good hands though not especially physical. Practice work consisted of regroups, shooting drills and two-on-ones. The club's philosophy is to support the lineup with quality players rather than carry "black aces" apart from the group, exposing them to the lifestyle and pressures of postseason competition. Perry's hand injury has prevented medical clearance, and he is not yet in game shape, so his availability remains undecided. The coach stresses the importance of a strong start, a level temperament that avoids getting too high or too low, and treating each game as the most important one, allowing only ten minutes of enjoyment or sorrow before moving on. He expects Ottawa's home crowd and energy to be a factor requiring mental strength. The team is committed, has strong leadership, and makes sacrifices for the group; despite being in a rare Stanley Cup opportunity with experienced staff and veterans like Teemu Selanne, the approach remains unchanged: work hard, stay committed, play the system and play the best game possible.

Hampton and Newport News police located a Ford SUV and apprehended a 15-year-old allegedly linked to a Tinee Giant robbery. A witness reported seeing someone discard an item and fire shots from the SUV. The teen was found with a handgun and charged with several firearms and tobacco offenses, but not robbery.

The passage says colleges’ political skew and growing attention to viewpoint diversity have made the concept politically contested, with groups defining it differently. It argues that the Trump administration’s demand for viewpoint diversity is unclear and tied to policies requiring institutions to adopt its agenda. Nine universities were offered favorable federal grant treatment in exchange for banning race- and sex-based hiring and admissions, freezing tuition, capping international enrollment, requiring standardized tests, and maintaining a “vibrant marketplace of ideas.” Meanwhile, prospective students reportedly will pay more than $2,000 to attend colleges whose students share their politics, pressuring colleges to advertise viewpoint strategies. The passage warns that conditioning federal funding on political compliance could narrow intellectual diversity rather than foster it.

A Sarasota couple was arrested after accepting a package containing carfentanil, a synthetic opioid the DEA says is 10,000 times more potent than morphine. A search also found more than 7 grams of fentanyl, other drugs, and paraphernalia; both were charged and released on bond.

This continuation application describes display devices and display panels, including OLED and LCD panels, with circuits for detecting cracks or other defects. A substrate includes a display area containing pixels and signal lines, a peripheral area, a circuit area containing a crack-sensing circuit, and a pad area containing input pads. Crack-sensing lines extend around the display area or through a bending area, receive test voltages through the input pads, and connect through test data lines and switching elements to corresponding data lines.

Cracks, lifting, or protrusions can increase a sensing line’s resistance or disconnect it. During testing, these changes produce insufficient test voltage at selected pixel columns, which may appear as hard or weak white lines and thereby identify peripheral-area or bending-area defects. Matching resistors compensate for voltage drops caused by sensing-line resistance and may be selected according to desired detection sensitivity.

Static-electricity discharge elements are connected to the sensing lines to store or discharge static electricity and protect the crack-sensing circuit and its switching elements from leakage or damage. The discharge elements may include capacitors, transistors, or diodes and may be positioned in a center area of the circuit area. Embodiments include capacitor connections between test data lines, parallel connection wires, or neighboring data lines, as well as arrangements using multiple sub-wires and sub-capacitors.

The detailed description also presents alternative panel structures, including circuit areas located on either side of the bending area, bending-area-specific crack-sensing lines, insulating and conductive layers contacting the sensing and voltage-transmitting lines, and stacked transistor, pixel-electrode, emission, common-electrode, encapsulation, and touch-sensor layers. The application claims priority to Korean Patent Application No. 10-2017-0107248 and cites related U.S. patent applications.

Alexander Zverev survived Dusan Lajovic in a 3-hour, 24-minute French Open thriller, advancing to the third round and closer to his first Grand Slam quarterfinal. The second seed had won titles in Madrid and led Rafael Nadal before rain delayed their Rome final. Grigor Dimitrov and Kei Nishikori also recovered from two-set deficits, while Dominic Thiem defeated Stefanos Tsitsipas. Simona Halep overcame a slow start to beat Alison Riske, and Novak Djokovic advanced despite being pushed by qualifier Jaume Munar. Petra Kvitova and Elina Svitolina also won in straight sets.

Amazon.com, Inc. reported that Fidelity Investments had been selected as the new recordkeeper for its 401(k) Plan. During the transition, expected from January 2 through the week of January 12, 2020, participants could not make exchanges or asset allocation changes, take loans, or request withdrawals or distributions. Participants could contact Fidelity during the blackout period and for two years afterward to confirm its status. On November 19, 2019, Amazon notified Section 16 officers and directors that company equity and derivative securities acquired through employment or service would be subject to trading restrictions during the blackout period.

Foreign Relations editors access State Department central, decentralized, Executive Secretariat, and overseas-post files. Central files for 1981–1989, stored electronically and on microfilm, and decentralized files selected for permanent preservation will eventually be transferred to the National Archives and become available after declassification and processing. Research also uses restricted records at the Reagan Presidential Library and other agencies. Although printed material is declassified, some source documents remain classified and incomplete records may not yet be available. The Remote Archive Capture project coordinates declassification of presidential-library records; scanning limitations sometimes made attachment status uncertain, resulting in “Not found attached” notices.

Documents are arranged chronologically by Washington, DC time, with memoranda of conversations placed by conversation date. Editors preserve original text, notation, spelling, capitalization, and punctuation as closely as possible, silently correcting obvious typographical errors. Brackets identify corrections, additions, unrelated or classified omissions, and original brackets; underlining is rendered in italics. Withheld documents are listed chronologically with headings, source notes, and page counts. First footnotes identify each document’s source, classification, distribution, drafting information, background, and whether the President or major advisers read it.

The disclosure, a divisional of U.S. Patent No. 11,743,879, describes systems and methods for indicating wireless channel status, particularly following beam failure recovery in high-frequency 5G NR communications. It discusses beamforming to address mmWave pathloss and the need to share channel-status information, including quasi-co-location (QCL) relationships, between network nodes and user equipment (UE).

Example embodiments allow a UE, after beam failure recovery, to assume that a selected new beam is spatially QCL with a reference or demodulation reference signal of a PDCCH or PDSCH. The UE may decode transmissions using the relevant reference signal and the spatial-domain receive filter used for the new beam until updated QCL configuration is received. For PDSCH decoding, the UE may alternatively assume a QCL relationship between a data channel and a control channel and reuse the control channel’s receive filter.

The disclosure further describes candidate transmission configuration indication (TCI) states, mappings between TCI states and an N-bit TCI field in downlink control information, and access-node updates to TCI tables and mappings after beam failure recovery. Under an alternative embodiment, the UE applies no external QCL configuration after recovery and relies only on the PDCCH or PDSCH’s own demodulation reference signal until TCI updates arrive. Special TCI values can indicate either the absence of a reference-signal relationship or a relationship with a PDCCH demodulation reference signal.

The described mechanisms help the UE determine which reference signal to use for control and data channels after recovery, reduce signaling overhead for channel-status updates, and improve communications-system performance.

The passage, commentary by a University of North Dakota dean of education, offers five strategies for parents and caregivers to encourage children's curiosity and conversation.
