Rote questions that draw one-word "yes" or "no" answers shut down real dialogue, so adults should ask specific, open-ended questions (e.g., "What was the most interesting thing you did today?") and engage seriously with the questions children ask rather than dismissing them with "Because I said so." Adults should admit not knowing answers and model how to find them—through manuals, labels, glossaries, indexes, or multiple searches—and should model asking for clarification, repeating back what they heard, highlighting what stood out in a child's answer, and giving undivided attention by putting away phones. Encouraging children's own curiosity builds their confidence to ask and answer questions.

This cross-sectional study examined self-esteem, physical activity, and their relationship among 10th- and 11th-grade students at Capa Science High School in Istanbul during the 2022–2023 school year. Data were collected from 225 of 278 students using sociodemographic questions, the IPAQ-SF, the Rosenberg Self-Esteem Scale, and self-reported height and weight; 16 participants were excluded from MET-related analyses because they scored zero METs. Males had higher self-esteem and physical activity scores than females. Regular exercisers had higher self-esteem, and self-esteem was positively correlated with MET scores. Higher self-esteem was also associated with greater height and greater perceived school success, but not with BMI category. Overall, 23% of participants were inactive, 61.7% minimally active, and 15.3% health-enhancing physically active. The authors concluded that greater physical activity was correlated with higher self-esteem but that causality requires further research, particularly because the study involved a highly selective school population and relied partly on self-reported measurements.

The ADS868xW provides user-programmable low and high input-alarm thresholds and programmable hysteresis, along with an AVDD alarm. With an NTC thermistor in a voltage divider, output voltage rises as temperature rises, allowing thresholds to detect excessively high or low temperatures. Properly adjusted hysteresis prevents noise near the thresholds from causing false or missed alarms.

The device uses independently set AVDD and DVDD power supplies within their permissible ranges. Recommended decoupling includes a 1 µF capacitor near AVDD and at least 10 µF near DVDD, improving power-supply rejection. Two low-power modes are available: NAP mode places internal blocks in a low-power state after a conversion and is exited by a falling edge on CONVST/CS, while PD mode powers down the analog blocks but retains the interface and registers. Wake-up from PD requires clearing PWRDN and waiting for the specified power-up time.

PCB guidance recommends separating analog and digital routing, using clean, well-bypassed supplies, placing specified ceramic capacitors at AVDD, DVDD, REFCAP, and REFIO, and connecting grounds through short, low-impedance paths. The document also covers documentation notifications, TI E2E support, ESD precautions, revision history, mechanical and ordering information, and legal disclaimers.

Canadian researchers analyzing blood samples from more than 2,800 Toronto residents found that about 1% had results consistent with celiac disease and that 90% of affected people were undiagnosed. Published in BMJ Open, the study also noted that celiac disease can cause poor nutrient absorption, with symptoms including abdominal pain, bloating, anemia and weight loss. Researchers said the findings matched international estimates but cautioned that further provincial studies are needed to determine national representativeness.

Diagnosis can be complicated because symptoms overlap with other conditions, gluten-free diets are common without confirmed disease, and some antibody results may reflect latent celiac disease. Experts emphasized that blood tests and duodenal biopsies should be performed while patients consume gluten to avoid false negatives; duodenal biopsy is the confirmation standard. About 30% of people carry the gene variant associated with celiac disease, though this does not guarantee development. The study was funded by the Canadian Institutes of Health Research, and researcher Ahmed El-Sohemy disclosed ties to Nutrigenomix Inc.

The Federal Reserve raised the federal-funds rate by 0.25 percentage point to 1%–1.25% and said it would begin gradually reducing its $4.5 trillion balance sheet this year, without detailing the pace. Markets reacted mutedly as the rate increase was widely expected. The S&P 500 fell 0.4%, the Nasdaq Composite lost 0.9%, and the Dow was nearly unchanged after reaching an intraday record.

Weak May inflation and retail-sales data, lower gasoline prices and a 3.7% drop in crude-oil futures pressured sentiment. Treasury yields declined, the dollar fell 0.2%, and gold rose 0.6%. Fed Chair Janet Yellen maintained that inflation would reach 2% next year.

Among individual stocks, H&R Block jumped 9% after better-than-expected earnings, Alexion Pharmaceuticals gained 8.7% after naming a new CFO, and Tesla rose 0.6%. Oil-related shares fell sharply, while UPS declined following a fatal shooting at a San Francisco facility.

The disclosure describes devices, methods, and computer-readable media for updating open-loop basal insulin parameters using insulin-delivery records from an automatic insulin delivery (AID) system and closed-loop glucose-control outcomes. A processor determines total basal and bolus insulin delivered over a selected period, calculates the basal share of total insulin, and compares it with a threshold. If the threshold is exceeded, the processor calculates an average basal dosage for a subsequent period and issues an instruction to modify delivery, typically by actuating a wearable insulin pump. Basal deliveries near bolus doses may be excluded from the calculation.

The disclosure also describes segmenting time periods and applying clustering algorithms to insulin-delivery histories to generate time-dependent basal profiles. Thresholds may reflect clinical data, user activity, expected basal-bolus distributions, and glucose-control performance, including time spent in hypoglycemia, which can reduce the maximum recommended basal proportion. In one example, automated basal delivery represented 71.3% of total insulin; applying a 70% threshold produced a recommended average basal dosage of approximately 1.22 units per hour.

The system may include a wearable drug-delivery device, continuous glucose monitor, personal diabetes management device, optional smart device, and cloud services communicating through wired or wireless links. An artificial pancreas application or AID algorithm can be distributed among these devices or implemented in hardware, software, or both. Additional embodiments describe modifying total daily insulin dosage based on glycated-hemoglobin levels and supporting open-loop use with devices such as smart pens or syringes. The application claims priority to U.S. Provisional Application No. 63/055,096, filed July 22, 2020.

The District Court properly dismissed the complaint because Public Resolution No. 53 suspended the appellants’ right to recover seized property while Germany remained in arrears on specified obligations. Under *Deutsche Bank*, Congress retained consent to be sued but could withdraw the alien enemies’ original, gratuitous right to recover. Allegations of unlawful seizure or withholding did not avoid the resolution’s effect, and *Stoehr* and *Becker Steel* did not require a different result. The judgment was affirmed.

Schneider Electric’s Edge Module is a turnkey, self-contained edge-computing deployment designed for distributed, often remote endpoints, including cell towers. It integrates power, cooling, software and IT components and supports flexible, scalable, autonomous deployments. Options include single- or three-phase power, multiple power-train ranges, N+1 cooling with a free-air option, and externally mounted package cooling that avoids external condensers or piping. The single-phase cell-tower configuration supports 208 volts and power trains up to 48 kW; racks can be arranged in one-, two- or four-bay configurations. EcoStruxture enables metering, remote monitoring and control for autonomous or “lights out” operation, while security features include locks, cameras, lights and a card-key reader.

The passage describes boot-configuration pins multiplexed with ARM Cortex-A8 boot modes and GPMC functions. At reset, BTMODE[10] selects GPMC mux options A or B for XIP NOR modes; BTMODE[9:8] selects Ethernet PHY modes; and BTMODE[4:0] determines the ARM boot configuration. After reset, these pins serve as GPMC multiplexed data/address pins GPMC_D[10], GPMC_D[7:5], and GPMC_D[4:0]. It also defines pin-state abbreviations and internal pull states (IPD, IPU, and DIS).

At its developer conference, OpenAI previewed an SDK that lets developers build third-party apps directly within ChatGPT using open standards, with distribution initially limited to major partners. Demonstrations showed Spotify, Canva, and Zillow operating in chats, including creating promotional materials, suggesting an expansion city, and filtering home listings. OpenAI also plans monetization methods and an “agentic commerce protocol” enabling purchases and instant checkout inside ChatGPT.

The company framed ChatGPT as a chat-driven operating system and super assistant while introducing tools for building AI agents, including AgentKit. Codex became generally available alongside Slack-based code editing, an SDK, and workplace analytics. OpenAI is positioning these services amid competition from Google, Anthropic, Amazon, Meta, and DeepSeek, released the GPT-OSS open-source model, and announced a 6-gigawatt AMD chip acquisition that may include a 10% stake in AMD.

U.S. stocks sold off Friday after a stronger-than-expected January jobs report and the largest wage gain in more than eight years fueled inflation concerns and expectations of more aggressive Federal Reserve rate hikes. The 10-year Treasury yield reached 2.845%. The Dow fell 665.75 points (2.54%), its largest point drop since December 2008, while the S&P 500 lost 2.12% and Nasdaq 1.96%; all three posted their biggest weekly losses in two years. All S&P sectors declined, while Exxon, Chevron, Alphabet and Apple fell and Amazon rose 2.9% after strong earnings.

Tail risk, or “fat tails,” describes rare extreme events occurring more frequently than a normal distribution suggests. Left-tail risk involves severe losses, while right-tail risk involves unexpected gains. Negatively skewed strategies can produce many small profits but a few large losses capable of erasing years of returns.

Investors may hedge tail risk to limit losses, avoid leverage-driven ruin, survive market downturns, and reduce behavioral mistakes such as selling during market declines. Effective hedging should limit downside exposure while preserving participation in profitable events.

Six hedging alternatives are discussed:

- **Put options:** Out-of-the-money puts on broad indexes act as insurance, allowing investors to sell at a predetermined price or profit from a market decline. Rolling positions creates costs and pin risk.
- **Foreign assets:** Diversification into foreign real estate, bonds, and commodities may reduce volatility and drawdowns.
- **Cash:** Holding roughly 5–10% in cash can provide stability during crises, although inflation reduces its long-term value.
- **Diversified portfolios:** Ray Dalio’s All Weather Portfolio allocates across asset classes rather than relying exclusively on stocks. Commodities can perform well when stocks and bonds are weak.
- **Trend following:** These strategies tend to produce many small losses but occasional large gains. Their positive skew and inflationary exposure can help hedge equity risk.
- **Cambria’s TAIL ETF:** TAIL holds U.S. Treasury bonds and out-of-the-money put options, buying more puts when volatility is low and fewer when it is high. Since its April 2017 inception, the passage reports a negative annual return of 6.92%. It protected portfolios during the 2018 selloff, March 2020 pandemic decline, and 2022 weakness. Allocating 10% or 25% to TAIL reduced drawdowns but also reduced long-term returns.

Meb Faber’s backtest allocated 10% to S&P 500 put options and 90% to 10-year U.S. Treasury bonds. It performed best among tested assets during selected bear markets, but required perfect crisis timing; continuously holding the strategy significantly reduced returns. The authors also abandoned a similar put-option strategy in 2019 because repeatedly worthless options were emotionally difficult, despite profiting when Covid-19 struck soon afterward.

Tail-risk protection generally resembles costly insurance: it may improve crisis performance and reduce panic-driven decisions, but it can lower compounding and be difficult to maintain. The appropriate trade-off depends on individual preferences, financial circumstances, and time horizon; the passage suggests younger investors with long horizons may accept drawdowns, while those near retirement may benefit from mitigation.

The thesis examines Web-based services, digital technologies, and mobile applications in event management. It distinguishes e-business, which encompasses business processes conducted electronically, from e-commerce, its buying-and-selling component, and reviews cloud computing, Web 2.0, the Internet of Things, mobile technology, and security measures such as firewalls, antivirus software, encryption, and digital certificates. Digital event organization could include sensor-based service booking, drone cameras, and mobile applications that provide event information and enable users to immerse themselves in events.

Using web-mining techniques and data collected from 1 August to 15 September 2017, the research evaluated 200 event-management websites against 103 binary criteria. The sample comprised 17 Croatian and 183 foreign websites from the United States, United Kingdom, Australia, Canada, Ireland, South Africa, Austria, and India. A five-part model assessed website content, social networks and Web 2.0, public relations and user support, multimedia and mobile technologies, and user experience and technical specifications.

Foreign organizations showed strong social-media and multimedia adoption: 92% had Twitter profiles, 90% had Facebook profiles, 81% had LinkedIn profiles, all used photos, 86% used animations, and 19% used videos. All analyzed foreign websites had blogs, although 78% of these were updated. Most performed well in technical terms: 78% loaded in under three seconds, 73% had pages below 5 MB, and 56% had performance grades above 80%. All used HTML, while 38% used PHP, 56% Flash, and only 4% used HTTPS.

The findings indicate that strong online and mobile presences are increasingly important for event organizations. Croatian sites ranked from 40th to 200th, showing particular room for improvement in user experience, social-media use, mobile applications, and multimedia. Faster loading, less unnecessary content, current blogs, mobile adaptation, and effective multimedia were identified as priorities. The study is limited by its selected-country sample; future research should examine customer perspectives and relationships between marketing activities and event-management strategies.

Jordan L. Couch of Palace Law describes generative AI as creating content from existing data and agentic AI as analyzing information to make decisions, predictions or recommendations. He identifies document review, legal research, client communication, brainstorming and rough drafting as valuable legal applications. Examples include identifying deposition quotes, researching legal issues and drafting motions, and using chatbots to answer questions, schedule appointments, provide case updates and draft client responses.

Couch cautions that AI is not a panacea and should be used only when appropriate. Nuanced judgment and creative problem-solving may still require humans, while templates are preferable for standardized materials. He discusses Vincent AI for legal research and brief review, Copilot and ChatGPT for drafting and workflow management, AI features built into legal software, and custom tools such as Palace Law’s chatbot for injured workers navigating the workers’ compensation system. Part 2 will address effective AI use, integration into legal practice and future developments.

Real Madrid face Paris Saint-Germain in the Champions League last 16, with Cristiano Ronaldo the competition’s record scorer. Other draw ties include Barcelona–Chelsea, Bayern Munich–Besiktas and Juventus–Tottenham. First legs are 13/14 and 20/21 February.

Minnesota signed winger Kirill Kaprizov to an eight-year, $136 million extension through 2033-34, the NHL’s richest deal by total value and average annual value ($17 million), general manager Bill Guerin announced. The contract starts next season, when Kaprizov completes the final year of his five-year, $45 million deal, and includes large signing bonuses over its first four years. Kaprizov had rejected an offer paying $16 million annually before reaching the agreement. The 28-year-old recorded 25 goals, 31 assists and a plus-19 rating in 41 games last season after missing 40 games due to surgery for a lower-body injury. He also scored five goals and added four assists in a six-game playoff loss to Vegas. In five Wild seasons, Kaprizov has 185 goals and 386 points and holds several franchise records. His extension may reset the market for pending unrestricted free agents under a new collective bargaining agreement that limits team re-signings to seven years and free-agent contracts to six. Edmonton’s Alex Ovechkin, in the final year of his contract, could become a free agent July 1.

Photographer Mark Bickerdike spent several years documenting 10-week RockJam courses at Ricky’s School of Rock in Linthwaite, photographing pupils learning songs and performing at their final gigs. After capturing around 50 gigs, he ended the project. Founder Ricky Comiskey said the courses build confidence and helped many pupils form bands. The school also runs courses for adults. Bickerdike’s son, Tom, joined the guitar classes and later formed Fading Sunlight, which has performed in Huddersfield, Leeds, Barnsley and Sheffield.

This qualitative study examined the anticipated challenges and teacher-education needs of pre-service physical education teachers in Quebec, particularly regarding student motivation. Eighteen participants from four focus groups across francophone Quebec universities identified classroom management and student disengagement or lack of motivation as their main anticipated challenges. Motivation-specific concerns included student heterogeneity, designing motivating activities, student engagement, managing disengaged students, and gender differences, especially motivating girls.

Participants felt their programs did not adequately prepare them to address these challenges. They requested more guidance in planning motivational strategies, concrete methods for implementing them, and additional opportunities to apply them in practice. They also wanted explicit links between motivation and existing course content, including planning, assessment, didactics, and classroom management, with greater attention to student diversity, psychological needs, and teachers’ beliefs.

The findings are situated within self-determination theory, achievement goal theory, and Quebec’s 2020 competency framework, notably “support students’ love of learning.” Recommendations include integrating motivational content coherently across courses, supporting instructors with motivational theory, linking theory to practical training, and helping future teachers adapt instruction to students’ needs, interests, and abilities. Limitations include the small, Quebec-only sample and the possibility that other challenges were overlooked.

The lecture reviews the operator–field correspondence in AdS/CFT: a boundary operator \(\mathcal O\) is expected to correspond one-to-one with a bulk field \(\phi\), with matching quantum numbers. The boundary value of \(\phi\) acts as a source for \(\mathcal O\) and therefore deforms the boundary Lagrangian or action. Conserved currents correspond to gauge fields, while the stress tensor corresponds to metric deformations.

Working in semiclassical gravity with Einstein gravity and matter fields, the lecturer rescales perturbations around AdS to canonically normalized fields. In the large-\(N\) regime, where \(\kappa\) is small, nonlinear interactions are suppressed, so the leading bulk calculation uses the quadratic, free-field action. For a scalar field in AdS, Fourier analysis and near-boundary asymptotics yield two radial behaviors,
\[
\phi(z,x)\sim A(x)z^{d-\Delta}+B(x)z^\Delta,
\qquad
\Delta=\frac d2+\sqrt{\frac{d^2}{4}+m^2R^2}.
\]
The BF bound, \(m^2R^2\ge d-4\), ensures real scaling exponents and a well-defined theory; violating it produces exponentially growing modes and an instability. Unlike Minkowski space, AdS curvature excludes constant modes, allowing some negative masses below the BF bound.

Because AdS has a timelike boundary, appropriate boundary conditions are required to prevent energy loss. Canonical quantization retains the modes selected by these conditions. For \(\nu\ge1\), where \(\nu=\sqrt{d^2/4+m^2R^2}\), only the \(z^\Delta\) mode is normalizable. For \(0<\nu<1\), both modes are mathematically normalizable, but only one may be quantized: standard quantization sets \(A=0\), while alternative quantization sets \(B=0\). Here “normalizable” operationally means the mode retained in the Hilbert space.

Normalizable modes correspond to states of the dual boundary theory; in standard quantization, \(B(x)\) is identified with \(\langle\mathcal O(x)\rangle\). Non-normalizable modes do not belong to the Hilbert space. Instead, they specify sources and boundary actions, thereby defining or deforming the boundary theory. Solutions with identical non-normalizable behavior but different normalizable modes represent different states of the same theory, while different non-normalizable behavior represents different theories. The source is extracted precisely by
\[
\phi(x)=\lim_{z\to0}z^{\Delta-d}\phi(z,x).
\]

Applying the bulk scaling symmetry to this relation shows that \(\mathcal O\) transforms as \(\lambda^{-\Delta}\mathcal O(x)\); hence \(\Delta\) is its scaling dimension. Standard quantization gives
\[
\Delta=\frac d2+\sqrt{\frac{d^2}{4}+m^2R^2},
\]
while alternative quantization gives \(d-\Delta=\frac d2-\sqrt{\frac{d^2}{4}+m^2R^2}\). Thus a massless bulk scalar corresponds to a marginal operator of dimension \(d\); allowed negative masses give relevant operators with \(\Delta<d\), and positive masses give irrelevant operators with \(\Delta>d\), consistent with boundary RG behavior.

Analogously, a Maxwell field has a dual conserved current of dimension \(d-1\), while metric perturbations source the stress tensor, whose dimension is \(d\). Finally, the lecture connects these correspondences to correlation functions: Euclidean sources generate a functional \(Z[\phi]\), derivatives at \(\phi=0\) yield correlators of dual operators, and \(Z[0]\) is the partition function. In the semiclassical limit, this functional can be approximated by the leading classical gravitational saddle point with the appropriate boundary conditions.

A Tom Thomson sketch, given away as a gag gift after experts authenticated it, sold for $481,250 at a Toronto auction where 118 works raised $14.1 million. Artist records included Paul-Émile Borduas’s “Figures schematiques” for $3.6 million and Jack Bush’s “Strawberry” for $691,250.

Lindsay Gottlieb said a Southwest Airlines employee asked her to prove that her 1-year-old son Jordan was hers, requesting a birth certificate or Facebook post despite her offering his passport, which had a different last name. Gottlieb, who is white, suspected Jordan’s skin color prompted the request; his father is black. Southwest apologized, said it verifies lap children are under two and domestic travel does not require matching surnames, but did not say whether race or surname caused the inquiry. Chrissy Teigen defended such checks as child-trafficking precautions.

The VIX measures implied volatility in S&P 500 options and generally moves inversely to the stock market. As a mean-reversion indicator, rising VIX may signal opportunities to buy stocks, while falling VIX may suggest selling. The passage presents a Bollinger Band strategy involving SPY or ES and recommends backtesting, noting that many other VIX strategies are complex and that ETFs such as VXX cannot fully replicate the spot VIX.

OPEC and other oil producers plan to announce an exit strategy from their supply-cut agreement in June, but UAE Energy Minister Suhail bin Mohammed al-Mazroui said the pact itself would not end then. Russia’s energy minister proposed a gradual withdrawal over three to six months, depending on market conditions and crude demand. The agreement currently cuts supply by about 1.8 million barrels per day.
Nigeria’s annual inflation fell to 16.25% in May from 17.28%, while monthly inflation rose to 1.88%. Food inflation dipped slightly to 19.27%, driven by higher prices for several food items.

The paper presents an exact method for computing Nash equilibria in multiplayer imperfect-information games by generalizing sequence form to an \(n\)-player nonlinear complementarity problem (NCP), then modeling it as a quadratically-constrained feasibility program solvable with global nonconvex quadratic optimization.

For three players, the formulation extends sequence-form matrices and payoff representations to characterize best responses through Lagrange derivative conditions, feasibility constraints, and complementary slackness. It generalizes to more players by introducing auxiliary bilinear variables, and it also applies to strategic-form games. On random strategic-form games, the NCP formulation was faster than a prior direct mixed-integer bilinear formulation, though newer specialized bilinear methods remain superior.

The main experiment uses three-player Kuhn poker, a one-round imperfect-information game with private cards, betting, calling, and folding. Several dominated actions were removed, yielding a reduced game with 48 information sets and 415 nodes. Gurobi solved the reduced game in 2.47 seconds, producing a strategy with maximum unilateral deviation gain of \(1.4\times10^{-17}\). Expected payoffs were approximately \(-0.0208333\) for each of the first two players and \(0.0416667\) for the third. The solution differed from a previously derived infinite equilibrium family at two information sets that were never reached, indicating additional off-path equilibria. The full game was not solved within 24 hours, demonstrating limited scalability.

Most Gambit algorithms were inapplicable or unsuccessful on reduced three-player Kuhn poker. Logit quantal response equilibrium tracing was the only applicable method that solved it, taking 43 seconds through the GUI and yielding a maximum deviation gain of \(1.667\times10^{-5}\). On the full game, logit tracing produced an output in 2 minutes 34 seconds through the command line, while the new method failed to solve it.

The results indicate that the NCP approach is well suited to fast, numerically exact equilibrium computation for small multiplayer imperfect-information games, while logit QRE is more scalable and appropriate for approximations of larger games. Iterative methods such as counterfactual regret minimization and fictitious play can scale to very large games but offer no convergence guarantees.

Box beat profit and revenue estimates, posting a 7-cent adjusted loss and $140.5 million revenue, up 20% year over year. It added 3,000 paying customers, issued above-consensus second-quarter guidance, and shares fell 4.6% after hours.

The Texas Court of Civil Appeals affirmed a jury verdict granting appellee title to 117 acres in the Willard Chamberlain one-third-league headright in Bell County. Appellee’s title was based on a duplicate land certificate and patent issued to Chamberlain, an 1850 transfer from Chamberlain through attorney in fact Louis C. Clemons to Joseph P. Sneed, and an 1860 deed from Sneed to N. T. P. Simmonds.

The court held that the transfer was properly admitted because evidence showed that it came from proper custody, had been claimed under for many years, and lacked circumstances suggesting forgery. Its genuineness and age were properly submitted to the jury. Once its genuineness, age, and custody were established, it created a conclusive presumption that Clemons had authority to act for Chamberlain. The transfer also sufficiently identified the certificate underlying the patent.

A certified Land Office affidavit asserting that another person owned the headright certificate was inadmissible against appellee’s title, and evidence of an augmentation certificate did not undermine the transfer’s identification. Appellant could not offer reputation-for-truth evidence merely because the parties’ testimony conflicted. The instructions on the transfer’s genuineness and the limitations defense were sufficient, and the evidence supported the verdict.

Under a certified agreement, Thomas Scullun commanded the American bark Cape Horn Pigeon on a whaling voyage from San Francisco, receiving a one-twelfth lay in net proceeds. The vessel was cleared and manifested on December 7, 1891. In 1892, Imperial Russian naval officer Lieutenant von Cube seized it in the Sea of Okhotsk, suspecting unauthorized fishing in Russian waters; Scullun maintained he was arrested for whaling in an area closed to foreign vessels. A commission found that the vessel had entered Russian territorial waters but ordered no confiscation, concluding that the arrest resulted from a misunderstanding. The vessel was promptly returned to its owners.

The patent application describes an auditory-based digital assistant for media exploration on electronic devices, including devices with limited or no display capability. Speech requests containing media-search parameters can produce media items, and further speech received during playback can be recognized as a refinement request that yields a different media item based on the original and new parameters. The assistant can also provide a spoken response while playing related media, such as a representative sample.

Additional methods allow the assistant to suggest media, track consecutive non-affirmative responses, offer another suggestion below a specified threshold, or request user input after the threshold is reached. When multiple users are present, their preference profiles can be merged to identify and provide media suited to the group.

The application describes corresponding methods, computer-readable storage media, and electronic devices. It also details a client-server digital-assistant architecture, device hardware, touch and event handling, sensors, communication systems, and software modules. The disclosed techniques aim to provide natural, flexible interactions, reduce user inputs and cognitive burden, and improve device efficiency and battery life.

Dusty Baker says Jeff Kent, whom he managed for six seasons, deserves Hall of Fame induction. Eligible since 2013, Kent has received about 15% of votes, well below the 75% threshold, despite career achievements including 377 home runs and the 2002 National League MVP Award.

Carol Moore said a 2010 land deal Jane Sanders championed caused Burlington College’s closure. Federal authorities are examining Sanders’ representations of donations used as loan collateral; Moore also criticized a deal involving Driscoll’s Vermont Woodworking School.

The NVIDIA A100 Tensor Core GPU uses the Ampere architecture and TSMC’s 7nm N7 FinFET process to accelerate AI and high-performance computing workloads. The A100 implementation of GA100 includes 108 Streaming Multiprocessors, 6,912 FP32 CUDA cores, 432 third-generation Tensor Cores, five HBM2 stacks, and 40 GB of HBM2 memory. It also adds Multi-Instance GPU (MIG) capability for hardware-level partitioning, fault isolation, and quality-of-service guarantees in multi-tenant environments.

Each A100 SM contains four third-generation Tensor Cores, each capable of 256 FP16/FP32 fused multiply-add operations per clock. Together, they deliver 1,024 dense FP16/FP32 FMAs per clock, twice the raw Tensor Core throughput per SM of Volta and Turing. The A100 supports FP16, BF16, TF32, FP64, INT8, INT4, and binary formats. Its 108 SMs provide up to 312 TFLOPS of dense mixed-precision FP16/FP32 performance, 2.5 times the mixed-precision Tensor Core performance of Tesla V100 and 20 times its standard FP32 throughput. TF32 provides FP32-range tensor operations with reduced internal precision and requires no user-script changes; FP16 and BF16 mixed precision offer further speedups. Tensor Core FP64 performance reaches 19.5 TFLOPS, 2.5 times that of V100.

A100 introduces fine-grained structured sparsity using a 2:4 pattern that permits two nonzero values in every four-entry vector. Sparse Tensor Core instructions skip zero entries, doubling matrix throughput, while compressed weights reduce storage and memory bandwidth requirements by half. NVIDIA’s process trains dense networks, prunes them to the 2:4 pattern, and fine-tunes the remaining weights, producing virtually no inference-accuracy loss across the evaluated networks.

The SM has 192 KB of combined L1 cache and shared memory, a new asynchronous global-to-shared copy instruction that can bypass L1 and intermediate register storage, and shared-memory asynchronous barriers that separate arrival from waiting. These features support pipelining, producer-consumer models, and synchronization of arbitrary thread subsets. Other SM improvements include simultaneous full-throughput FP32 and INT32 execution, hardware-assisted warp reductions, and additional cache-management instructions.

A100 provides 40 GB of HBM2 memory with 1,555 GB/s bandwidth, more than 1.7 times V100 bandwidth. Its 40 MB L2 cache is 6.7 times larger than V100’s and offers 2.3 times the bandwidth. L2 residency controls allow persistent data to be prioritized, while Compute Data Compression can improve DRAM read/write bandwidth and L2 read bandwidth by up to four times and effective L2 capacity by up to two times. SECDED ECC protects HBM2, L2, L1 caches, and register files.

Third-generation NVLink provides 12 links, a 50 Gbit/s data rate per signal pair, and 600 GB/s total GPU bandwidth, twice that of V100. A100 also supports PCIe Gen 4 with 31.5 GB/s per direction and SR-IOV for sharing a GPU among virtual machines. Expanded error-detection, attribution, isolation, containment, and recovery mechanisms are designed to prevent faults in one workload from affecting others, including across NVLink-connected GPUs.

Additional hardware includes a five-core NVJPG JPEG decoder, a hardware optical-flow accelerator supporting optical flow and stereo disparity, improved global-memory atomics, and five NVDEC video-decoding units. The datacenter-oriented A100 does not include display connectors, RT Cores, or an NVENC encoder.

CUDA 11 adds support for third-generation Tensor Cores, structured sparsity, MIG, CUDA Graphs, L2 residency controls, and asynchronous copies and barriers. CUDA Graphs separate workflow definition from repeated execution, reducing launch overhead and allowing A100 to optimize uploads and dependency scheduling. Cooperative Groups adds group-wide asynchronous memory pipelines and hardware-accelerated reductions.

DGX A100 combines eight A100 GPUs with six NVSwitches, providing 4.8 TB/s total bidirectional interconnect bandwidth, up to 5 PFLOPS of AI performance, and as many as 56 isolated accelerators when MIG partitioning is used. Its software stack includes CUDA, NVIDIA’s container tooling, GPU-optimized containers, deep-learning and analytics libraries, and the NGC Private Registry. The DGX A100 is designed to scale from individual deployments to large Slurm or Kubernetes clusters.
QuantifiedStrategies.com offers TradingView/Pine Script strategies and translates selected strategies into Pine Script upon request via email.
Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth summoned hundreds of generals and admirals worldwide, arguing the military had become “soft” and “woke.” New York Times reporters discussed his speech.

Amazon.com, Inc.’s unaudited Form 10-Q for the quarter ended March 31, 2019 reported net sales of $59.70 billion, up 17% from $51.04 billion in Q1 2018. Operating income increased to $4.42 billion from $1.93 billion, and net income rose to $3.56 billion from $1.63 billion. Diluted earnings per share were $7.09, compared with $3.27. North America sales increased 17% to $35.81 billion and segment operating income doubled to $2.29 billion. International sales increased 9% to $16.19 billion, while the operating loss narrowed to $90 million from $622 million. AWS sales increased 41% to $7.70 billion and operating income rose to $2.22 billion from $1.40 billion.

Q1 operating cash flow was $1.85 billion, versus a $1.79 billion outflow a year earlier, while investing and financing activities used $8.12 billion and $2.38 billion, respectively. For the trailing twelve months, operating cash flow was $34.36 billion and free cash flow was $23.04 billion, or $15.13 billion after principal repayments of finance leases and financing obligations. At March 31, 2019, cash and cash equivalents were $23.12 billion, marketable securities were $13.91 billion, total assets were $178.10 billion, and stockholders’ equity was $48.41 billion.

The company adopted new lease accounting guidance on January 1, 2019, recognizing approximately $21 billion of operating lease assets and liabilities, and adopted guidance requiring capitalization of substantially all episodic television production costs, adding about $130 million of capitalized costs. Total contractual commitments were $131.32 billion. Amazon reported no common-stock repurchases in either first quarter.

The filing disclosed patent and import-related litigation involving Amazon products, an ongoing review concerning sanctions involving Iran, potential indirect-tax liabilities, and approximately $3.6 billion of tax contingencies. Amazon disputed the legal allegations and stated it would defend itself vigorously. It also said operating cash flows, cash and marketable securities, and borrowing arrangements were expected to meet anticipated operating cash needs for at least the next twelve months.

The circuit should output logic high when the amplifier output exceeds 1.1 V and follow Figure 7-7. Place a low-ESR 0.1 µF ceramic capacitor directly between each device’s V+ pin and ground, close to the pins and connected to a solid ground plane, to prevent ringing, false triggers, oscillations, and inaccurate comparisons. The device supports split V+/V− or single V+/GND supplies, with GND applied to V− for single supply; inputs must remain within the recommended range, and split-supply outputs swing to V− rather than ground. Minimize output-to-input coupling, place input series resistors close to the device, and optionally add an output series resistor below 100 Ω to damp ringing or reflections on long, poorly impedance-controlled traces.

Qualcomm briefly published a blog post about Asus’s Zenfone AR, a second consumer-facing Google Tango smartphone expected to debut at CES 2017. It supports Daydream View and uses a Snapdragon 821. Evan Blass posted purported renders; pricing and availability were unknown. Asus also teased another Zenfone for CES.

The IMF told Ukraine its pension system is unsustainable because it supports 30% of the population, operates at a loss, and requires early retirements to be limited. Ukraine resists raising the pension age, but IMF mission chief Ron van Rooden suggested limiting early retirements and improving pension-tax collection. Ukraine is seeking another $4.5 billion from the IMF this year.

The article explains the 20-day exponential moving average (EMA) trading strategy, which generates buy signals when a security's price rises above the 20 EMA and sell signals when it falls below it, and can be applied to forex, stocks, and commodities. A backtest on the S&P 500 ETF (SPY) showed a very low CAGR despite being invested roughly 70% of the time, plus a significant drawdown, though smaller than buy-and-hold. Adding an extra trading indicator as a filter (details behind a paywall) increased performance and nearly matched buy-and-hold CAGR on a risk-adjusted basis, though drawdown stayed the same. Backtesting the crossover rules on Bitcoin from 2014 performed much better, attributed to Bitcoin's strong momentum.

Iron sulfate heptahydrate, also called ferrous sulfate heptahydrate, copperas, or green vitriol, is soluble in water and acids and has octahedral molecular geometry. It is produced as a by-product of titanium dioxide manufacturing from ilmenite and by crystallizing hot sulfate solution. It contains 18–20 wt% iron, at least 4% free moisture, and up to 3% free acid; crystals may clump and become dusty, while acidic liquid can attack storage containers. It is used to treat iron deficiency and iron chlorosis, historically in textile dye fixation, leather blackening, and ink. Other applications include water purification through flocculation and phosphate removal, reducing Cr6+ in cement, and supplying iron in agriculture.

The lecture reviews the AEP and typical sequences for discrete memoryless sources. The sample average of \(-\log p(X_i)\) converges to the source entropy \(H(X)\), so sequences with sample averages near \(H(X)\) have nearly equal probabilities and collectively account for almost all probability mass. Their number is approximately \(2^{nH(X)}\), with individual probabilities near \(2^{-nH(X)}\). In source coding, block coding can achieve about \(nH(X)\) bits with rare failures, but achieving fewer than \(H(X)-\epsilon\) bits per symbol makes the asymptotic failure probability approach one.

The lecture then introduces finite-state Markov sources as models with memory. Ergodic Markov chains are emphasized because they have unique stationary behavior, with state probabilities approaching steady-state values from any initial distribution. Coding can use state-dependent prefix codes, giving conditional entropy \(H(X\mid S)\) as the asymptotic rate. Coding symbols individually is ineffective for small alphabets, but coding blocks of symbols applies the AEP and approaches \(H(X\mid S)\) bits per symbol.

Finally, the lecture describes universal Lempel–Ziv compression. These algorithms contain no assumed source probabilities and can discover Markov or other statistical structure while encoding. In LZ77, an initial window is transmitted uncompressed; the encoder then finds the longest match between upcoming symbols and the sliding window, encodes the match length with a unary-binary code, and encodes its location with \(\log W\) bits. The method is asymptotically as effective as model-specific coding for Markov sources and supports instantaneous decoding. Practical issues include initial window overhead, limited window size, implementation speed, and slow adaptation when source statistics change.

Addressing West Point cadets, the speaker argues that the Cold War’s end offers the promise of democratic governments, reduced nuclear risk, and a new world order, but also heightens threats from dictators, weapons of mass destruction, and terrorism. The United States must reject isolationism and actively lead in building a democratic, tolerant, and economically free international system. This leadership requires demonstrated moral, diplomatic, economic, political, and military engagement, but not unilateralism or the role of world policeman. As the only remaining superpower, America must marshal its resources to promote democratic peace while balancing idealism, national interests, and prudence.

Military force may sometimes be necessary, but it should never be used lightly or universally. The speaker cites U.N.-authorized operations in Kuwait and Iraq, humanitarian action in Somalia, and earlier actions in Panama and the Philippines as examples of selective force supporting diplomacy and democratic goals. Decisions about intervention require judgment rather than rigid rules. Force should be limited, feasible, and supported by allies when possible, while the United States should contribute proportionately without bearing the full burden. Every mission should have clear objectives, a realistic plan, and achievable withdrawal criteria. The situation in the former Yugoslavia required continued reassessment as humanitarian and strategic risks evolved.

Strong armed forces are essential for both national defense and peacekeeping, but their greatest strengths are their people, leadership, and training. The all-volunteer force reflects merit, equal opportunity, discipline, responsibility, and continuous education and retraining. Military service also demonstrates that meaningful public service requires courage, duty, honor, and the willingness to make sacrifices.

The speaker closes by telling cadets that on his eighteenth birthday in June 1942, he ignored advice to finish school before enlisting in the Navy, a decision he has never regretted. He urges them to continue serving their country as they enter a changed world and ends with a humorous amnesty for the Corps of Cadets.

Coach Quenneville praised Chicago’s consistency, improved defense, goaltending and depth across all four lines. He highlighted a line’s reliable defensive play, puck possession, speed and offensive upside, while noting that some forwards remained productive despite limited scoring. The team’s third-line players had increased responsibility, with one becoming quicker during the playoffs, while Johnny’s work without the puck and ability against top defensive pairings were emphasized.

Quenneville said the team responded well to adversity, including falling behind against Detroit, and welcomed extra rest before returning to its normal playoff schedule. He credited every player, including goaltenders Corey and Ray Emery, for the season’s success and praised Shaw’s net-front effort and improved production. He also discussed the unpredictability of coaching, his appreciation for the Blackhawks organization and Chicago’s sports community, and conversations with other local coaches and personnel.

The 1824 U.S.–Russian and 1825 Anglo-Russian treaties guaranteed freedom of navigation, fishing, and trade with Indigenous peoples in unoccupied Pacific coastal areas, subject to later restrictions. In the Paris arbitration over Great Britain and the United States, the tribunal noted that Russia had limited its Bering Sea jurisdiction to cannon-shot range and had not exercised exclusive control over seal fisheries. It reasoned that the Bering and Okhotsk seas were branches of the Pacific and therefore open seas. Citing international-law authorities, it held that connected seas remain generally accessible to all states, that no state may impose its laws on foreign vessels on the high seas, and that only limited coastal security restrictions and small bays or straits could be occupied.

Damian Lillard scored 32 points, becoming the fastest player in franchise history to reach 10,000 career points, but Portland lost 130-105 to Toronto, ending a four-game winning streak. DeMar DeRozan scored 35 points, including six 3-pointers, as the Raptors improved to 20-4 at home with a season-high 19 made threes. CJ McCollum scored 21 and Jusuf Nurkic had 20 for Portland, which lost five of seven on the road.

GDDR6X improves on GDDR6 by using PAM4 signaling: two bits are transmitted per clock edge through four voltage levels spaced 250 mV apart, representing 00, 01, 10, or 11. NVIDIA’s Maximum Transition Avoidance encoding limits extreme voltage transitions, while new training, equalization, signal-integrity, power-integrity, package, and PCB designs support the resulting SNR demands. GDDR6X reaches data rates of up to 19.5 Gbps and 936 GB/s peak bandwidth on GA10x GPUs, with pseudo-independent memory channels intended to assist BVH ray traversal.

Faster SSDs have exposed bottlenecks in traditional game-storage workflows, where compressed assets pass through the CPU and can consume all 24 cores of a Threadripper processor. NVIDIA RTX IO works with Microsoft DirectStorage to move compressed data directly from storage to the GPU and perform lossless decompression there. The document claims I/O acceleration up to 100 times that of hard drives and traditional APIs, along with improved frame rates, near-instant loading, reduced object pop-in and stutter, high-rate texture streaming, and smaller download and installation sizes. GPU decompression uses asynchronous compute kernels and the DMA and copy engines of Turing and Ampere GPUs, also benefiting professional workloads involving large datasets and rendering.

The GA10x-based NVIDIA A40 targets data-center visual computing. Compared with the Quadro RTX 6000, NVIDIA states that it provides up to twice the FP32 and ray-tracing throughput, up to five times the AI and data-science throughput, or ten times with sparsity, and twice the PCIe Gen4 transfer bandwidth. It has 48 GB of memory, expandable to 96 GB by linking two A40s with third-generation NVLink, and supports DisplayPort, virtual GPU deployment, Quadro Sync, and the NVIDIA EGX Platform.

GA10x GPUs support 4K at 120 Hz and 8K at 60 Hz through DisplayPort 1.4a and HDMI 2.1, including Display Stream Compression and dynamic HDR, and support HDCP 2.3 and 1.x. Fifth-generation NVDEC provides hardware decoding for MPEG-2, VC-1, H.264, H.265, VP8, VP9, and AV1. GA10x is described as the first GPU generation with AV1 hardware decoding; an cited test showed 8K60 HDR playback with about 4% CPU usage. Seventh-generation NVENC provides hardware encoding for low-latency streaming and high-quality recording, including up to 4K H.264 and 8K HEVC.

The Ampere architecture provides up to twice the programmable-shading, ray-tracing, and AI performance of prior-generation architecture. Its second-generation RT Core doubles ray-triangle intersection performance, adds ray-traced motion-blur acceleration, and supports concurrent ray tracing with shading or compute. Third-generation Tensor Cores implement structural sparsity for up to twice their effective throughput, while enhanced DLSS supports 8K HDR rendering. The GeForce RTX 3090 uses the GA102 GPU and includes 82 SMs, 10,496 CUDA cores, and 24 GB of GDDR6X; NVIDIA states it is 1.5 times faster than the TITAN RTX. The GA104-based RTX 3070 lacks NVLink and uses GDDR6 rather than GDDR6X, but NVIDIA says it performs faster than the previous generation’s RTX 2080 Ti.

Error Detection and Replay on GDDR6X detects transmission errors through CRC checks and retries failed transactions. Repeated retries reduce useful bandwidth, so a performance plateau indicates that memory overclocking has reached its practical limit, though crashes remain possible if users continue beyond it.

The RTX A6000 includes a GA102 GPU, 10,752 CUDA cores, second-generation RT Cores, and 48 GB of GDDR6. It supports hardware-accelerated ray tracing, motion blur, and AI denoising; two boards can be combined through NVLink for 96 GB of memory. The document closes with disclaimers that specifications may change, materials are provided as-is without implied warranties, and NVIDIA products are not warranted for medical, military, aircraft, space, or life-support applications.

Harvey Weinstein was indicted on two rape counts and one criminal sexual act count involving two women. Manhattan DA Cyrus Vance Jr. called it another step toward accountability, while Weinstein’s lawyers advised him not to testify before the grand jury.

The paper studies quantum learning protocols restricted to joint measurements on a bounded number of state copies. It focuses on estimating nonlinear quantities such as \(\mathrm{tr}(\rho^{\otimes k}O)\), which cannot be measured directly because quantum measurements are linear, but become linear in \(\rho^{\otimes k}\). This motivates determining when multiple replicas provide an exponential advantage.

The main result establishes a hierarchy of replica quantum advantage for every integer \(k\ge2\). For a bounded \(d\)-dimensional observable \(O\) satisfying \(\|O\|_\infty\le1\) and \(\|O\|_1\ge2(k+1)2^k\), estimating \(\mathrm{tr}(\rho^{\otimes(k+1)}O)\) with \(k\)-replica protocols requires at least
\[
\Omega\!\left(\frac{\sqrt d}{k\varepsilon^{1/(k+1)}}\right)
\]
samples in the stated error regime. For constant \(k\), \(\|O\|_1=\Omega(d)\), and constant additive error, this becomes \(\Omega(\sqrt d)\) samples. With \((k+1)\)-replica joint measurements, the quantity is linear on \(\rho^{\otimes(k+1)}\) and can be estimated with \(O(k/\varepsilon^2)\) samples, independent of dimension. This yields constant-versus-exponential separations for constant \(k\), polynomial-versus-exponential separations for \(k=O(\log n/\log\log n)\), and subexponential-versus-exponential separations for \(k=o(n/\log n)\).

The paper proves a matching-order upper bound using only \(\lceil(k+1)/2\rceil\) replicas:
\[
\widetilde O\!\left(\max\left\{\frac{k\sqrt d}{\varepsilon},\frac{k}{\varepsilon^2}\right\}\right)
\]
samples suffice, showing that the \(\sqrt d\) dependence in the lower bound is optimal. The construction uses generalized swap tests, moment estimators, and a recursive reduction based on distributed inner-product estimation.

The main technical tool is an indistinguishability principle for Haar-assembled ensembles: ensembles formed from tensor products and mixtures of Haar-random states are difficult to distinguish from their average using one-replica measurements. More precisely, distinguishing such an ensemble from its average with constant success requires
\[
T=\Omega\!\left(\sqrt{\frac{d_{\min}}{m a_{\max}^2}}\right)
\]
one-replica samples, where \(m\) is the number of random states and \(a_{\max}\) controls their average multiplicity. The proof combines Le Cam’s two-point method, one-sided likelihood-ratio bounds, Haar integrals, symmetry and permutation operators, and a generalized permutation-operator inequality.

Lower bounds are constructed by choosing probability distributions with matching moments through degree \(k\) but a large difference in the \((k+1)\)-st moment. Mixtures of Haar-random states then form ensembles that are indistinguishable with \(k\) replicas but separable using a \((k+1)\)-degree observable. Chebyshev polynomials provide the moment gap. Traceless observables are handled by restricting the construction to a \(d/2\)-dimensional eigensubspace.

The principle also yields lower bounds for spectrum testing. If two spectra with at most \(m\) nonzero entries agree on all moments through degree \(k\), \(k\)-replica spectrum testing requires
\[
\Omega\!\left(\sqrt{\frac{d}{m\sqrt{\ln m}}}\right)
\]
samples. Specializations imply exponential sample-complexity lower bounds for bounded-replica rank testing and for estimating noninteger powers of the trace. Unlike prior unrestricted protocols, these bounded-replica bounds necessarily scale as \(\Omega(\sqrt d)\).

The paper situates these results among generalized swap tests, one-replica shadow and randomized-measurement methods, and earlier one-versus-two replica separations. It also notes independent concurrent work establishing replica separations for prime \(k\) through Weyl–Heisenberg tomography.

Open directions include improving the lower bound’s error dependence, determining the precise threshold between hard and easy precision regimes, extending spectrum-testing bounds beyond \(m<\sqrt d\), and studying whether replica hardness can also be expressed as hardness under limits on working qubits rather than simultaneous replicas.

The forwarded Texas Monthly article traces Enron’s rise and decline through the leadership of Ken Lay and Jeff Skilling. It describes Enron’s transformation from a heavily indebted pipeline company into a dominant energy trader. Skilling developed the “Gas Bank,” which guaranteed gas supply and pricing and allowed Enron to assume market risk. The company expanded into electricity, broadband, online commodity trading, bandwidth, and other businesses while eliminating long-term physical assets in favor of rapid profits.

Enron’s success depended on a distinctive culture. Skilling recruited highly educated, aggressive employees, offered uncapped performance bonuses, and expected long hours and intense competition. The Performance Review Committee used forced ranking, while employees were encouraged to monitor one another and abandon loyalty. Confidentiality rules, internal surveillance, and a “rank and yank” system contributed to paranoia and low morale.

The article also describes Enron’s subjective accounting practices, including taking profits upfront and using its own market valuations, as well as the troubled Dabhol power plant in India and Rebecca Mark’s unsuccessful water company, Azurix. Enron’s political influence drew criticism during California’s energy crisis, while the collapse of the telecommunications market undermined a major source of investor enthusiasm. As profits, analyst confidence, and the stock price declined, scrutiny of Enron’s accounting and executive stock sales intensified.

Skilling resigned after six months as CEO, and Lay returned to lead the company, promising a less aggressive culture and a closer focus on its core business. The article concludes that although economic conditions and failed investments contributed, Enron’s internal culture and leadership decisions bore substantial responsibility for its downturn.

Vertex acquired an Edmonton-area hydro-vac services business for $4.3 million, doubling its hydro-vac fleet with 11 additional units and expanding services into the Edmonton market. The June 30, 2018 transaction is expected to add approximately $5 million in annual revenue and supports Vertex’s industry diversification.

The speaker addresses the Foreign Service Institute, encouraging future diplomats and describing NATO as a vital institution supporting Atlantic peace and collective security. European recovery since 1945, shared action, integrated military power, and political unity have helped deter war and reinforce stability.

NATO should adapt to changing circumstances, but reform must come through consultation among members rather than isolation or dismantling the alliance. The United States intends to work with its allies to strengthen NATO’s deterrent and extend common preparation. The speaker warns that division and independent action weaken security and that modern warfare makes narrow concepts of sovereignty less acceptable.

The Atlantic community’s strength in arms, industry, ideas, and shared values offers hope for reconciliation between Western and Eastern Europe. Its broader purpose is to preserve human solidarity, reject destructive national rivalries, and make collective action the best assurance of peace.

Lower 32 kB supports higher erase/program endurance for EEPROM emulation. Sector or bank erases each count as one operation. Word-line writes are limited before sector erasure. Program timing spans command initiation to completion interrupt; sector timing includes software loading of words.

Microsoft Corporation’s Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended June 30, 2019 describes a technology company focused on intelligent cloud and edge computing, AI, productivity, personal computing, and gaming. Its stated ambitions are to reinvent productivity and business processes, build intelligent cloud and edge platforms, and create more personal computing. Major offerings include cloud and support services, online advertising, operating systems, productivity and business applications, development tools, video games, PCs, tablets, Surface devices, and gaming consoles.

Microsoft reports through three operating segments. Productivity and Business Processes includes Office Commercial and Consumer, LinkedIn, and Dynamics. Intelligent Cloud includes server products and cloud services such as SQL Server, Windows Server, Visual Studio, System Center, GitHub, and Azure, along with Enterprise Services. More Personal Computing includes Windows, devices, gaming, and search. The company also describes its OEM, direct-sales, distributor, reseller, cloud solution provider, and volume-licensing channels, along with cloud, on-premises, and Software Assurance licensing options.

Microsoft develops most products internally through groups focused on cloud and AI, experiences and devices, research, LinkedIn, and gaming. It conducts localized international operations, relies primarily on third-party device manufacturers, and maintains global research facilities and datacenters. As of June 30, 2019, it employed approximately 144,000 people. Satya Nadella was CEO, Amy E. Hood was CFO, and Bradford L. Smith was President and Chief Legal Officer.

The report identifies risks from intense competition across software, cloud, devices, gaming, search, and professional services; execution of cloud investments; uncertain returns on new products; integration and impairment risks associated with acquisitions, including LinkedIn and GitHub; cyberattacks and data breaches; privacy and personal-data handling; harmful online content; IoT and AI risks; infrastructure reliability; product quality and supply constraints; intellectual-property protection and claims; litigation; competition-law and other regulatory scrutiny; and global anti-corruption requirements. It also cautions that forward-looking statements depend on assumptions subject to risks and uncertainties, and Microsoft undertakes no obligation to update them.

A penalty-kick shoot-out may determine the winner when a soccer match remains tied after regulation and any extra time. Competition rules govern its use, with IFAB Laws 10 and 14 providing the framework.

Each team selects five eligible players and takes alternating kicks from the 12-yard penalty mark. The team with more goals after five kicks wins, unless the outcome has already been mathematically decided. If tied, sudden-death kicks follow: each team takes one kick at a time until one scores and the other misses. Eligible players are those on the field at the end of play, plus temporarily absent players; teams must reduce their numbers when player counts differ. Players normally kick only once, but may take another after all 11 have kicked. Goals from the shoot-out are recorded in the match result but do not count toward individual statistics.

The referee selects the goal and which team kicks first, supervises compliance, and records takers and results. Assistant referees also monitor the kicks. Only the designated kicker and goalkeeper may touch the ball, which may touch the goalkeeper, posts, or crossbar before entering the goal. An eligible player may replace an injured goalkeeper if announced to and recognized by the referee; an unused substitute may also replace an injured goalkeeper. If a goalkeeper is sent off, another player who finished the match must take that role.

Coaches are advised to prepare in advance by reviewing the rules and tournament modifications, assigning players to conduct the coin tosses, identifying and ranking penalty takers, practicing the entire procedure under pressure, studying opponents, and working with goalkeepers on remaining calm and treating each kick independently. During the match, coaches should avoid a defensive letdown, keep likely shooters on the field, confirm the kicking order, make necessary substitutions, and encourage a calm approach. Afterward, they should maintain team morale and review performance.

This Motley Fool Money page reviews the Wells Fargo Reflect® Card, written by Ryan Wilcox, a full-time personal finance writer at the outlet. The card offers a 0% intro APR for 21 months from account opening on purchases and qualifying balance transfers, followed by a variable APR of 16.99%, 23.49%, or 28.74%, and it charges no annual fee. Its main strengths are the long interest-free window for paying down debt or financing a large purchase, seamless payment management for existing Wells Fargo customers, and perks including up to $600 of cellphone protection against theft or damage (subject to a $25 deductible, usable twice per year) and personalized cash-back offers through My Wells Fargo Deals. Drawbacks include a 5% balance transfer fee ($5 minimum), a 3% foreign transaction fee, and no rewards or incentives once the intro period ends, making it a poor fit for those wanting ongoing perks or travel rewards. A recommended credit score of Good/Excellent (670–850) is listed, though approval is not guaranteed. The card was awarded Motley Fool Money's Best 0% Intro APR Card of 2025. Applying requires submitting personal and financial details, reviewing terms, and awaiting a decision. The page also notes that many offers come from partners who compensate the site, that compensation may affect offer placement but not product ratings, and that editorial opinions are the outlet's own.

On June 24, 2020, Tesla entered a 90-day indemnification agreement with CEO Elon Musk. During the bridge term, Musk will provide directors’ and officers’ indemnity coverage from personal funds, up to $100 million, for amounts Tesla cannot indemnify. Tesla will pay him a one-time fee of $972,361 and seek a binding quote for a $100 million liability insurance policy. If the prorated, 50%-discounted market premium exceeds the initial fee, Tesla will pay Musk the difference.

Sony’s Xperia XZ Premium will get an Android Oreo update later in 2017, adding the 3D Creator app and camera improvements. The app scans faces, food and objects for sharing, GIFs or 3D printing. Oreo adds predictive smile capture and phase-detection burst shooting at 10 photos per second; Sony gave no exact date.

Petitioner appealed the denial of parole, arguing that the Board relied on erroneous presentence-report information stating that he shot someone, though the related charges were dismissed. Because he did not refute that information before the Board, seek to correct the report, or challenge it at sentencing, he was precluded from contesting its use. The court found that the Board considered the applicable statutory factors and that its decision was not irrational. The dismissal of his CPLR article 78 petition was affirmed without costs.

AGNC Investment, a mortgage REIT with significant investments in agency mortgage-backed securities, is presented as benefiting from recent and expected Federal Reserve rate cuts. Lower rates could reduce financing costs and boost securities valuations and book value. AGNC reported improving spreads and a third consecutive quarter of positive net interest income in Q2 2025. Its premium to book value reflects optimism about improved fundamentals and reversing past book value losses. The author is bullish, citing strong NII and an attractive monthly dividend, and discloses beneficial long positions in AGNC and Annaly Capital Management.

The president departs from the traditional State of the Union format to present an agenda for the 1970s, arguing that America’s programs and institutions require reform as the nation enters a new decade.

Peace is identified as America’s first priority. The immediate foreign-policy goal is to end the Vietnam War through a just and lasting peace, with Congress and the executive acting together regardless of party. The administration argues that other nations should assume greater responsibility for their own defense and development, allowing the United States to reduce its involvement while honoring treaty commitments. It describes stronger European, Latin American, and Asian partnerships, a new foundation for Japanese-American cooperation, and movement from confrontation toward negotiation with the Soviet Union and Communist China.

At home, the president says economic growth must improve the quality of life rather than increase crime, inflation, and social unrest. Urgent priorities include replacing the existing welfare system with income support, job training, and work incentives; restoring authority to states and local governments through “New Federalism”; and expanding equal voting rights, employment opportunities, and ownership. The administration also calls for reform in health, education, housing, and transportation.

To control inflation, the president attributes rising prices primarily to federal budget deficits and urges Congress to maintain a balanced budget, even if this requires rejecting some spending programs. Additional funding is proposed for law enforcement, and Congress is urged to pass pending legislation against organized crime, narcotics, pornography, and street crime. Federal efforts should complement greater state and local responsibility.

The environment is presented as a major national concern. Proposals include a $10 billion nationwide clean-water program, preservation of open spaces and parklands, stricter vehicle-emission standards, stronger enforcement, and measures that incorporate environmental costs into prices. The president also calls for individual responsibility for keeping homes, workplaces, and public spaces clean and for redirecting economic growth toward better living conditions.

A national growth policy is proposed to address overcrowded and deteriorating cities, population loss in rural areas, and uncoordinated development. Federal assistance would support new cities, rebuild old ones, and create improved rural conditions that could reverse migration to urban centers.

The president concludes by envisioning an America marked by an end to hunger, income support, improved housing, transportation, health care, and education, along with reduced inflation, lower crime, cleaner air and water, preserved parks, continued space exploration, and peace with all nations. He argues that material progress must be joined by moral and spiritual leadership, civic responsibility, and an inspiring vision for young Americans, so that the nation fulfills its promise of liberty, opportunity, progress, and peace.

Japan plans to send a remotely controlled swimming robot into Fukushima Dai-Ichi’s Unit 3 containment vessel in July to assess damage and locate melted fuel submerged in radioactive water. The Toshiba-co-developed “mini manbo,” about the size of a loaf of bread, has lights, tail propellers, cameras and a radiation detector. Earlier robots failed or were withdrawn due to breakdowns and extreme radiation, hampering decommissioning and planned fuel removal after the 2020 Olympics.

Andrea Conti’s agent says the Atalanta wing-back wants only Milan, considers his time at Atalanta over, and believes Gian Piero Gasperini cannot veto the transfer. Conti scored eight goals and four assists in 33 Serie A appearances, while his agent urged both clubs to cooperate on a solution.

The passage presents an FAQ-style overview of Nassim Nicholas Taleb’s life, writings, trading methods, and investment philosophy. Taleb grew up in Lebanon, studied in France, settled in the United States, worked as a proprietary trader, held academic positions, and founded Empirica Capital with Mark Spitznagel. He became known for applying ideas about randomness, uncertainty, luck, and tail risk to finance. The article attributes much of his trading success to options strategies, particularly gains during the 1987 crash, and notes his book *Dynamic Hedging*.

Taleb’s *Incerto*, published from 2001 to 2018, covers probability, luck, uncertainty, human biases, fragility, antifragility, decentralization, decision-making, and tail risk. He argues that forecasts are unreliable in complex, interconnected systems and that people should instead prepare for unpredictable events. *Fooled by Randomness* examines how luck and cognitive biases cause success to be attributed to skill. *The Black Swan* focuses on rare, highly consequential events and the limits of forecasting and conventional statistical models. *Antifragile* describes systems that benefit from volatility and disorder, advocating optionality, decentralization, and small, tolerable mistakes. *Skin in the Game* emphasizes incentives, accountability, and judging decisions by the risks or assets people hold rather than by their words.

Taleb’s “barbell strategy” divides a portfolio between low-risk and high-risk assets with little in the middle. Conservative assets provide stability, while smaller speculative positions—such as options or leveraged assets—offer large gains during extreme events. The article gives examples involving low- and high-beta stocks, defensive and aggressive stock groups, short- and long-maturity bonds, and a portfolio allocating 95% to conservative assets and 5% to a leveraged Nasdaq ETF. It contrasts this approach with selling naked calls, which may profit frequently but carry severe tail-event losses, and with dollar-cost averaging into a broad index as a simpler alternative.

The article describes Universa Investments, founded by Spitznagel and advised by Taleb, as using a tail-risk barbell approach: holding assets that return little while maintaining options that may profit during major crashes. It reports that the fund grew from $300 million in assets in 2007 to more than $11 billion in 2022 and cites large reported gains during the 2020 pandemic disruption.

Across Taleb’s quoted passages, recurring themes include mistaking luck for competence, survivorship and hindsight biases, the danger of forecasts, the importance of behavior over opinion, preparedness over prediction, decentralization, small mistakes, limited liability, personal stakes, and the need to design for survival in environments shaped by rare extreme events.

The coach expressed disappointment after a hard-fought overtime loss, saying the team gave its best effort and was proud of the group. All three games went to overtime, and both goaltenders played outstanding, though the coach felt his team played better hockey in overtime. He emphasized puck possession, playing north-south, and trusting the power play to convert chances.

Malawi Heath Equity Network urged the government to deploy internal auditors to all 28 district councils, citing research in Ntcheu that their absence is harming financial management, accountability, budget implementation, and transparency. Government officials said deployment plans are at an advanced stage and councils should support auditors as performance advisers rather than investigators. The research also identified weak coordination among councils, NGOs, and civil society organizations, limited resource-sharing, and inadequate rural participation in annual budget preparation. It recommended involving village residents in budget committees and greater collaboration among councils and their partners.

Gary Gensler describes initial coin offerings (ICOs) as a form of crowdfunding in which a startup sells its own crypto token to raise money. He traces the concept to J.R. Willett’s 2010 proposal to use Bitcoin for applications, and notes that Ethereum raised $18 million before its network was operational. ICO fundraising accelerated sharply in 2017–2018, with approximately $25 billion raised in 12 months, compared with roughly $125–170 billion in annual worldwide venture capital investment. EOS raised $4.2 billion and Telegram $1.7 billion, but fundraising subsequently declined sharply.

Most ICOs raised money before their networks were functional. During the third quarter of 2018, about 76% were marketed primarily as ideas, only 1.7% had published source code, and roughly 3% were fully ready or had released code. Development was often centralized, and source code was frequently published only after fundraising. Promoters commonly retained tokens, while tokens were generally transferable and sometimes subject to sale restrictions. Projects sometimes used Simple Agreements for Future Tokens (SAFTs) when a usable token would not be delivered immediately. Most ICOs also incorporated some monetary or token-supply policy, though not all did.

ICOs resemble crowdfunding platforms such as Kickstarter because funds support future product development and participants may expect token appreciation. They differ because they involve digital assets, market-determined token pricing and quantities, secondary markets, and investment expectations centered on potential profits. Gensler advised evaluating token-use viability, reading the white paper and available source code, assessing the team and venture-capital backing, reviewing community activity, monetary policy, token distribution, competition, and whether a blockchain or native token was truly necessary. He also emphasized unresolved scalability, performance, privacy, security, coordination, and interoperability challenges.

Accounting treatment varied: ICO proceeds could be recorded as current revenue, deferred revenue, or, less commonly, a liability. Depending on the project, tokens might circulate among network users, as with Ethereum, or return to the issuer, as with some storage models. Issuers could also monetize tokens they retained, as Ripple did with XRP.

According to ICO Ratings data cited for the third quarter of 2018, about 600 ICOs raised $1.8 billion, down 78% from the previous quarter, while blockchain venture capital reached $1 billion. Roughly 84–85% used Ethereum, 57% raised less than $100,000, 67% were considered unsuccessful, and only 4% were listed on an exchange. Gensler noted that many offerings were noncompliant securities offerings under U.S. law and that the SEC had begun using the term “illegal” for unregistered offerings, while regulation elsewhere varied by jurisdiction.

He concluded that most ICOs had already failed and expected the boom to diminish, without implying that blockchain technology itself was ending. Most tokens offered utility or service rights, although a small number granted voting, governance, or cash-flow rights resembling ownership.

Donald Trump said U.S.–Canada trade ties would be only “tweaked,” despite Canada’s heavy dependence on the U.S. (76% of Canadian foreign trade versus 18% of U.S. trade). A message to Congress transmits the preliminary report of James Bronson Reynolds and Charles P. Neill, who investigated conditions in Chicago stockyards. The report describes unclean stockyards and packing houses and hazardous meat-handling practices, and urges immediate federal legislation authorizing thorough inspection of stockyards, packing houses, and meat products entering interstate or foreign commerce.
