The paper studies definability and separability of modal µ-calculus (µML) formulas by propositional modal logic (ML) formulas over all models, words, and bounded-outdegree trees. An ML-separator for formulas φ and φ′ is an ML formula ψ satisfying φ ⊨ ψ and ψ ⊨ ¬φ′. ML-definability is the special case of separating φ from ¬φ.

ML-definability is ExpTime-complete over all models and binary or higher-degree trees, but PSpace-complete over words. ML-separability is ExpTime-complete over all models and binary trees, PSpace-complete over words, and 2-ExpTime-complete over trees with outdegree at least three. Separator construction has matching or related bounds ranging from exponential over words to triply exponential over higher-degree trees. ML has Craig interpolation over all models, words, and binary trees, but not over trees of outdegree at least three; the corresponding interpolant-existence problem is coNExpTime-complete there. In the graded setting, graded ML definability and separability are ExpTime-complete, while using ordinary ML to define or separate graded µML formulas yields ExpTime- and 2-ExpTime-complete problems, respectively.

After introducing ML, µML, pointed Kripke models, parity-game semantics, bisimulations, and parity tree automata, the paper develops a characterization of non-separability through joint consistency up to bounded-depth bisimulation. This connects modal formulas to automata and yields an ExpTime-complete algorithm for separability over unrestricted models, together with double-exponential separator construction. Efficient alternative constructions are given for unrestricted and binary models; they are optimal in the presence of at least two accessibility relations.

For words, ML-definability and separability are PSpace-complete. The proof reduces the question to whether languages of finite word prefixes have an infinite intersection, decidable in polynomial space. Separators over words can be constructed in exponential time, which is optimal because µML is exponentially more succinct than ML. The section also develops an automaton-based construction of modal uniform consequences over words.

The DAWn-Plasma study was a prospective, multicenter, randomized, open-label phase II trial comparing standard of care plus convalescent plasma with standard of care alone in hospitalized adults with COVID-19. Between May 2020 and January 2021, 499 patients were assessed and 489 were randomized; the primary full analysis set included 483 patients (320 plasma and 163 control) after six exclusions. Participants received 800–1,000 mL of convalescent plasma in four doses, with the first infusion within 12 hours of randomization. Most plasma units had neutralizing antibody titers of at least 1/320.

The primary endpoint was survival without mechanical ventilation at Day 15. There was no difference between groups: 83.7% in the plasma group versus 84.1% in the control group (odds ratio 0.99; p=0.976). No secondary endpoint, including mortality, differed significantly between groups, and results were similar in the per-protocol population.

Safety outcomes were generally similar between groups. Adverse events occurred in 28.13% of plasma recipients and 30.06% of controls; serious adverse events in 20.62% and 20.68%, respectively. Transfusion-related side effects occurred in 19 of 320 plasma recipients (6.0%), with no TRALI cases reported. Neutralizing antibody titers increased by Day 6 regardless of intervention, and higher titers at baseline and Day 6 correlated with better outcomes. Overall, early administration of high-volume, high-titer convalescent plasma did not improve the primary outcome or alter the course of hospitalized COVID-19.

Ashley Hollis, an A&O Shearman associate, won “Big Brother” after hiding her legal career and posing as a social media marketing manager. Inspired by Elle Woods, she used attorney skills to prepare her final speech and plans to give much of her $750,000 prize to her parents.

The study examines the literature on integrating gamification into STEAM education, noting reported improvements in motivation, engagement, learning, and academic performance, while also highlighting variable outcomes and the need for systematic assessment. A quantitative bibliometric analysis was conducted using Scopus documents published from 2017 to 2023, identified through a search for “steam” and “gamification.” After filtering, the final dataset contained 34 English-language articles, reviews, conference papers, and book chapters, with 155 citations.

Publication activity began in 2017 and expanded from 2020 onward, reaching eight documents in 2022. The most-cited article was Wannapiroon and Pimdee’s study on Thai undergraduate STEAM creative thinking, with 30 citations. Leading authors included Kummanee, Nilsook, Wannapiroon, Lee, and Piriyasurawong, each with three publications. Thailand led in output with six publications and 68 citations, followed by Italy and Malaysia with three publications each. Malaysia had the highest country-level total link strength, alongside Singapore, while Germany, Latvia, Norway, and France formed the most active collaboration cluster.

Computer science accounted for 37.7% of publications, followed by social sciences at 20.5%. Among 15 author keywords occurring at least twice, the most frequent were “gamification,” “steam,” “steam education,” and “computational thinking.” Factorial analysis grouped topics into educational methodologies and interaction tools, student-centered learning environments, and educational technologies and engagement strategies. The findings indicate that STEAM education with gamification is a growing research field and that bibliometric and topic-mapping methods can support research development and educational policy and practice.

At Tharisa plc’s investor presentation, CEO Phoevos Pouroulis outlined the company’s phased transition from open-cast to underground mining as open-pit resources are depleted. The transition will begin with the open pit and West Mine. Pouroulis described a vision for a fully integrated mining complex that redefines resources and generates multigenerational value. Tharisa has operated as an open-cast miner for 15 years and has remained profitable for 11 years while producing platinum-group metals and chrome concentrate despite volatile commodity markets, geopolitical storms, and other headwinds. The presentation also included CFO Michael Jones, Tharisa Minerals Managing Director Vulela Makuni, and Executive of Operations Roy Murley.

The study examines a dialogic educational activity adapted to emergency remote teaching during the COVID-19 pandemic. Drawing on Freire’s critical pedagogy and Cultural-Historical Activity Theory, it used the Discord platform in a Brazilian physics teacher-education course to explore scientific communication through the contested issue of reopening schools. Nineteen students participated in a seven-stage intervention involving discussion of contradictory media narratives, research into scientific and governmental sources, collaborative communication work, and production of an infographic shared through WhatsApp. Qualitative analysis of four meetings and related records found that Discord’s text, voice, and recording features supported broader student participation, movement among groups, sharing of materials, autonomous meetings, and collaboration without continuous teacher mediation. Students connected their immediate pandemic difficulties, including isolation, domestic responsibilities, and uncertainty about returning to school, with wider social and political contradictions. The article also notes that emergency remote education reproduced inequalities and, in many settings, weakened student voice and dialogue.
Libyan forces lost four men and saw 10 wounded in December amid resistance and clashes in Benghazi, five months after Khalifa Haftar declared victory.

This continuation patent application describes electronic gaming systems and methods featuring a stop-based bonus game. A construct such as a wheel, reel, dice, or grid/treasure map contains stop positions associated with higher-value first awards, such as jackpots, or lower-value second awards, such as credits, multipliers, wild symbols, free plays, or no-value awards.

When a trigger event selects a stop associated with a second award, the award is provided to the player and that stop is reassociated with a first award for subsequent play. This progressively increases the number of stop positions associated with first awards and potentially the player’s chances of winning one. Reassociated stops may persist between plays and players, or they may be reset after a first award is won. In one wheel example, selected credit positions become jackpot positions until a jackpot is awarded.

One implementation uses a primary game to trigger a bonus game with an inner bonus wheel containing credit prizes or free games and an outer wheel containing bonus features, including one of several secondary jackpot wheels. The inner wheel may award credits or free games, while the outer wheel may select an award feature such as wilds or a jackpot game.

The disclosure also describes gaming-machine components, including displays, player-input and credit mechanisms, processors, memory, and random number generators, as well as networked and stand-alone gaming-machine configurations.

Fran Horowitz, CEO of Abercrombie & Fitch Co., says the retailer is pursuing a long-lasting lifestyle brand rather than chasing “cool.” Since taking over in 2017, she moved away from command-and-control management, gave employees more input and improved clothing quality. A&F sales nearly doubled to $2.6 billion between 2019 and 2024, while Hollister also grew; their combined sales are expected to exceed $5 billion this year. To maintain momentum, Abercrombie is expanding partnerships, including selling Abercrombie Kids clothing at Macy’s and becoming the NFL’s first fashion partner, with merchandise for all 32 leagues. Horowitz said the NFL deal offers customer acquisition and brand awareness among millions of fans, including women underserved by existing team merchandise.

The paper examines a quasi-experimental approach in which introductory physics students use generative AI to create, validate, and refine simulations of electric potential and equipotential lines. In spring 2025 at a large R1 public university, 187 students enrolled in a non-calculus introductory physics course for life sciences. The study compared three independent laboratory groups using physical equipment, a prebuilt AI-designed simulation, or an AI-engaged simulation-design activity.

The AI group used Claude Sonnet 4 to generate an interactive HTML5 simulation, then wrote additional prompts to test its technical functionality and scientific accuracy and iteratively improve it. All groups investigated potential–distance relationships, equipotential-line properties, and relationships among line density, potential differences, and motion along equipotential lines. Physical-equipment students additionally explored non-point charges and electric-field lines.

Students completed five conceptual questions and five attitude questions immediately after the lab, and their midterm and final-exam performance was also examined. Because the data violated ANOVA’s normality assumption, nonparametric tests were used. Conceptual-question scores differed significantly by lab type (Kruskal–Wallis H = 58.718, p < .001, η² = .359). Both simulation groups significantly outperformed the physical-equipment group, while the two simulation groups did not differ significantly overall. Differences on the midterm and final exams were not significant.

Attitude responses were associated with lab type for every question. Students using either simulation reported more favorable attitudes than those using physical equipment on all five measures. The prebuilt and AI-developed simulation groups differed significantly only in comparisons with the previous week’s lab, with the prebuilt group more positive on that item. Question-level analysis found one conceptual item on which the prebuilt group outperformed the AI group, although the AI group performed better than the physical group on three items and the prebuilt group did so on four.

The authors conclude that prompting, validating, and refining AI-generated simulations can support conceptual learning comparably to prebuilt simulations while also giving students experience with emerging technologies, modeling, debugging, and scientific validation. Physical equipment remains valuable for experimental practice. Limitations include differences in abstraction across conditions, free-tier AI restrictions and technical assistance, and the focus on one topic, institution, and largely life-science student population.

Problem Solvers member Travis Guillory helped veteran Rodney Orton obtain a new mobility scooter after the one he had used for 15 years malfunctioned. Although the VA required a new evaluation and offered an appointment six weeks away, Guillory contacted VA staff, who acted immediately. Assistant Chief of Prosthetics Diana Kinion found a locally stocked scooter matching Orton’s medical needs and delivered it to his hospital room the next morning. Orton and his Chihuahua, Pita, now have transportation to get around.

The March 2006 AMD Geode CS5535 Companion Device Silicon Revision A3 specification update catalogs errata involving the PIT, XPIC, DMA/GLIU, ACPI/PMC power management, ATA/UDMA, UART, LPC, USB, KEL, SMBus, GPIO, and PCI timing. Issue numbers are nonsequential because resolved issues are omitted.

Notable findings include incorrect DMA rotation order, duplicate interrupts with XPIC AEOI, failed debug and error-reporting features, and required Sleep Clock control sequencing. Legacy block/demand DMA can invalidate UART and LPC accesses; single-transfer mode is recommended. UDMA may experience CRC corruption, ATA PRD alignment can cause hangs or prefetch hazards, and UDMA commands must precede bus-master enable. ACPI PM1 register byte accesses hang, while WORD or BYTE PMC writes may corrupt registers. Clock gating can cause unreliable UART CEIR, USB, GLIU, and PIC operation. Other issues affect S3 wake events, SMB NEGACK clearing, post-suspend GPIO writes, Sleep_X/Sleep_Y delays, invalid I/O bases, PCI timing, KEL status reporting, LPC synchronization, and standby status flags.
Some dogs’ irresistible attraction to toys may parallel human behavioral addictions.

A Stanford University study of nearly 28,000 college dining-hall students found that appetizing labels increased vegetable selection even when dishes were prepared identically. Foods labeled as “great tasting” were chosen 25% more often than basic-labeled foods, 35% more often than those with positive health labels, and 41% more often than those with restrictive health labels. Diners also served themselves more vegetables.

The passage suggests making vegetables more appealing with vivid descriptions, such as “rich buttery roasted sweet corn,” and offers recipes including grilled carrots with chipotle lime aioli, nacho cheese kale chips, chili-lime sweet corn salad, rosemary sea salt and vinegar beet chips, cauliflower fried rice, and sautéed green beans with bleu cheese and walnuts. It notes that only about 10% of American adults and 1% of teens and tweens meet recommended daily vegetable intake.

A Hubble image shows the arachnid-shaped Tarantula Nebula (30 Doradus), named for spidery gas filaments, and the Honeycomb Nebula. ESA suggests the latter’s bubble-like appearance stems from interactions between older and newer supernovas and our viewing angle.

The lecture develops a relativistic framework for unifying weak and electromagnetic interactions. Using left- and right-handed spinor projections, the vector–axial weak current is recast as a vector current, while the electromagnetic current separates cleanly into left- and right-handed components without mixed terms, explaining why helicity is preserved in QED. Neutrinos and electrons are then organized as weak-isospin doublets, with charged currents expressed through the raising and lowering operators \(\tau^+\) and \(\tau^-\). A neutral current emerges from the third isospin component, and a hypercharge current, analogous to strangeness in the strong interaction, is defined from the Gell–Mann–Nishijima relation. Combining these currents yields a neutral weak current that includes right-handed as well as left-handed particles, accounting for the right-handed electron’s coupling to the \(Z\) boson. Finally, the three weak-isospin currents and the hypercharge current are combined and rotated by the weak mixing angle \(\theta_W\). This mixing produces the \(W^+\) and \(W^-\) bosons, while the photon and \(Z\) boson emerge as mixtures of the isospin-triplet and hypercharge-singlet components. The lecture notes that mass eigenstates need not coincide with weak-interaction eigenstates, a complication addressed later.

- The President reports that the nation has grown stronger in prosperity, education, moral life, and peace, while emphasizing that the challenges accompanying growth require factual analysis, common judgment, and conciliation.

- Foreign policy has strengthened the foundations of peace through the Kellogg-Briand Pact, under which 54 nations renounced war. The United States intends to adhere to the International Court of Justice under arrangements reserving U.S. consent for cases involving its interests; this step is not intended as entry into the League of Nations.

- The United States will participate with Great Britain, France, Italy, and Japan in a London conference on limiting naval armament. It also pursued peaceful settlements with Mexico and in Latin America, mediated disputes involving Chile and Peru, Bolivia and Paraguay, and Guatemala and Honduras, and expanded airmail service throughout the Americas.

- U.S. Marines remained in Nicaragua, Haiti, and China. The administration sought further reductions, proposed a commission to study the Haitian situation, and intended to reduce forces in China to a normal legation guard. It also proposed strengthening diplomatic missions in Latin America and increasing State Department appropriations.

- The Army and Navy were considered adequate for national defense, but their rapidly rising costs caused concern. Defense expenditures were projected to exceed $730 million in the current fiscal year, while potential naval construction could exceed $1.2 billion over six years. The President nevertheless urged prudent reductions and emphasized that forces under the Kellogg Pact were intended solely for defense. Federal support had strengthened the National Guard, while military and commercial aviation had increased defense capacity.

- Government finances were described as sound. Public debt stood at $16.931 billion and had fallen another $238 million since June 30. Recommended fiscal year 1931 appropriations were $3.830 billion, slightly below the current year’s $3.976 billion. Estimated surpluses of $225 million for fiscal 1930 and $123 million for fiscal 1931 provided for a provisional tax reduction: individual normal income-tax rates would fall from 5, 3, and 1.5 percent to 4, 2, and 0.5 percent, and the corporate rate from 12 to 11 percent. The changes were projected to reduce calendar-year 1930 income taxes by $160 million.

- Settlements of foreign debts were nearing completion. Agreements were pending with Austria, completed with Greece, and awaiting congressional approval after French ratification; only Russian and Armenian indebtedness remained unsettled. A revised plan for German claims was being prepared, with the United States sharing concessions. Funded foreign debts totaled about $11.58 billion, while American taxpayers were paying roughly $475 million annually in interest.

- Of about $625 million in seized alien enemy property, all but $111.6 million had been returned, and most of the remainder was expected to be disposed of during the following year.

- Economic progress continued despite the securities-market crash and uneven industrial conditions. Federal measures, bank strength, and voluntary cooperation with business and state authorities were credited with maintaining wages, sustaining credit, restoring confidence, preventing greater unemployment, and supporting recovery. The administration also began expanding public construction work.

- Agriculture was improving. Farm income had risen over several seasons, bankruptcies had declined, land values appeared to have stopped falling, and confidence was returning. The Federal Farm Board was organizing grain, cotton, livestock, and wool marketing, supporting cooperatives, and seeking to increase farmers’ bargaining power, control surpluses, and organize farmer-owned institutions.

- The tariff should protect agriculture while encouraging crop diversification and account for differences in domestic and foreign production costs. Limited revisions were needed where economic shifts had substantially reduced employment, and the flexible tariff mechanism should be preserved so that the Tariff Commission and President could make prompt adjustments. Tariff policy should consider national trade interests and should not intensify divisions between farmers, workers, or regions.

- Congress was urged to extend and accelerate public-building appropriations because existing authorization was insufficient, many federal clerks still occupied temporary buildings, and stable construction schedules could lower costs. The Fine Arts Commission should also review private construction facing public buildings and parks.

- Inland-waterway development advanced with the canalization of the Ohio River to a uniform nine-foot depth. Appropriations for rivers and harbors were recommended to increase, while most Mississippi flood-control work would continue; the proposed Arkansas River floodway route was withheld for further engineering review. Intracoastal waterways were to be expanded, and the St. Lawrence project awaited Canadian action.

- More than three million miles of highways existed, including about 626,000 improved miles, with total public spending of $1.66 billion. Federal aid to states had stimulated construction, and larger contributions were urged, especially for farm-to-market roads.

- The Post Office deficit exceeded $80 million annually. Restructuring long-term building leases could save about 40 percent, systematic revision of airmail rates was needed, and expanded South American service was recommended.

- Civil aviation advanced under federal airway and mail-contract assistance. Government-improved airways exceeded 25,000 miles, about 1,000 airports were operating and 1,200 more were proposed, 6,400 planes were in commercial use, and regular routes covered roughly 90,000 miles daily and reached Canada, Mexico, Caribbean countries, and much of South America.

- Railroads were in strong physical and financial condition, but further consolidation was needed to create balanced systems, uniform rates, and single-line hauls. Legislation should simplify consolidation procedures and reduce the Interstate Commerce Commission’s burden of minor matters.

- Government-owned steamship lines were being transferred successfully to private enterprise. Construction loans had reached about $75 million. Proposed mail contracts required 40 new vessels costing approximately $250 million, along with an additional $5.5 million annual Post Office authorization, and Congress should clarify conflicting claims over contract awards.

- Banking law required review of group and chain banking, credit concentration, failures among country banks, and national banks’ migration to state charters. Limited regional branch banking and a joint congressional-federal study were proposed.

- The Federal Power Commission needed full-time commissioners and authority to address interstate electricity issues through coordinated state action and possible federal action. The temporary Radio Commission should become a permanent national body, with geographically balanced membership and abolition of zonal appointment requirements.

- Muscle Shoals facilities and revenues should be dedicated permanently to agricultural chemistry research and Tennessee Valley industrial development, with a special commission empowered to negotiate contracts. Funds were requested to begin power-sale work at Boulder Dam once contracts assuring recovery of government costs were completed.

- Conservation policy required suspending and reviewing oil and gas permits, addressing damaging overgrazing and threats to western water supplies, and expanding water storage under a broader reclamation policy. A Commission on Conservation of the Public Domain was appointed to study these and related federal-state responsibilities.

- Federal social services should remain rooted in local and individual responsibility while providing leadership, coordination, research, and temporary assistance. initiatives included a child-health conference, housing and recreation planning, an education-policy study, an anti-illiteracy movement, expanded employment services, and additional research through the Women’s and Children’s Bureaus.

- Public-health programs should be built around competent municipal, county, or other local units, supported by state and federal participation. The Sheppard-Towner Act should continue for a limited period, with federal funds directed toward local health units and coordinated with United States Public Health Service spending.

- Federal prisons were overcrowded, and probation and parole systems were inadequate. The Army Disciplinary Barracks at Leavenworth was temporarily transferred to the Justice Department, while new federal prisons, a reorganized probation and parole system, and a Bureau of Prisons were recommended.

- Immigration restriction was described as sound national policy. Further study was requested to identify immigrants within existing quotas whose fitness and skills best matched national needs.

- Veterans’ benefits for compensation, rehabilitation, hospitalization, medical care, insurance, and service-connected disabilities were to be maintained. Hospital care had been extended to all veterans, and adjusted service certificates had been issued to more than 3.4 million veterans. The Pension Bureau, National Home for Volunteer Soldiers, and Veterans’ Bureau should be consolidated for greater efficiency and uniform administration.

- About four-fifths of executive employees were subject to competitive examination. Third-class postmaster appointments should also be brought under the civil-service system.

- Government reorganization should place activities serving the same major purpose under single responsibility, separate administrative functions from board and commission functions, and initially group related services before creating new departments. Congress should delegate reorganization authority to the Executive within stated principles while retaining limited revision power.

- Prohibition enforcement required immediate organizational and legislative reform. Detection and much prosecution should move to the Justice Department, alcohol regulation would remain in the Treasury, federal court procedures should be simplified, prohibition statutes should be codified, and smuggling prevention should be consolidated under a Coast Guard border patrol. District of Columbia enforcement also required stronger legislation and cooperation.

- A National Commission on Law Observance and Enforcement was studying crime, judicial administration, and prohibition-related abuses. The Justice Department was removing inefficient officials, strengthening prosecutions, and seeking added appropriations for United States attorneys, clerks, and marshals. The President also emphasized that laws enacted by the people must be observed and enforced until repealed.

- The administration’s decisions were to be judged by whether they advanced local self-government, individual and group justice, ordered liberty, equality of opportunity, individual initiative, prosperity, education, knowledge, religious growth, tolerance, the family, and peace.

Browns coach Kevin Stefanski said there is no single benchmark for Shedeur Sanders to become backup quarterback, emphasizing long-term player development. Rookie Dillon Gabriel remains the starter, while Sanders and Bailey Zappe compete for the backup role; Sanders likely remains third-string. Jerry Jeudy praised Sanders’s professionalism and readiness to capitalize on future opportunities.

Five tips for playing Abalone: avoid rushing into attack, plan moves to anticipate opponents, and safely move counters toward the center for greater mobility. Start defensively, then go on the offense when appropriate; the first player to eliminate five opposing counters gains an advantage. Splitting an opponent’s counters into smaller groups makes them easier to push off the board, particularly near an edge, but watch for counterattacks.

This cross-sectional study characterized Alzheimer disease–related plasma biomarkers among 1,067 Amish participants in the Collaborative Amish Aging and Memory Project, including Aβ40, Aβ42, Aβ42/Aβ40, total tau, p-tau181, Aβ42/t-tau, and Aβ42/p-tau181. Participants were classified as cognitively unimpaired, having mild cognitive impairment, cognitively impaired but not AD, or having AD.

Aβ40, Aβ42, and Aβ42/Aβ40 did not differ significantly by diagnosis. Compared with cognitively unimpaired participants, those with AD had higher p-tau181 and lower Aβ42/p-tau181. After covariate adjustment, no biomarker was significantly associated with AD overall, but higher p-tau181 was strongly associated with AD among APOE ε4 carriers (OR 6.02, p<0.001). Lower p-tau181 and higher Aβ42/p-tau181 were associated with cognitive preservation in sensitivity analyses.

Models combining biomarkers classified AD with an AUC of 0.83; models including APOE ε2 and all biomarkers or Aβ42/p-tau181 classified cognitive preservation with AUCs up to 0.77. Clustering by Aβ42/Aβ40 and p-tau181 identified distinct low- and high-risk profiles; the high-risk profile had lower Aβ42/Aβ40 and higher p-tau181, more APOE ε4 carriers, and more participants with AD. Secondary analyses favored three clusters, revealing additional combinations of amyloid and tau risk.

Limitations included the small, nonrepresentative Amish population, diagnoses based mainly on medical history and cognitive testing without imaging or CSF confirmation, the indirect nature of plasma biomarkers, and the cross-sectional design. Longitudinal validation was recommended.

The passage describes an automated cryogenic storage system for biological, chemical, and other samples. Unlike conventional dewars requiring manual removal of racks or trays, the system uses one or more storage vaults connected to a sample handling module (SHM). A robotic arm transfers individual samples among storage vaults, the SHM, and removable portable cryogenic workstations docked at external ports. Vaults may operate near −150°C, while rapid transfers through the non-cryogenic SHM, aided by an extendable insulating sleeve, prevent samples from exceeding their glass-transition temperature.

A controller receives sample identifiers and destinations, locates samples in a database, selects destination addresses, commands vaults and portable workstations for access, and coordinates robotic transfers. Barcodes can be scanned before, during, or after transfer to verify sample identity, after which the database is updated. The controller also manages refrigeration, humidity, mechanical calibration, sample identification, and failure and disaster recovery.

Each storage vault contains an insulated chamber, refrigeration coils, a rack with independently rotating interleaved shelf groups, and a vertical shuttle that presents trays at an opening for robotic access. Pie-shaped trays can hold numerous samples and use kinematic pins for positioning. Primary refrigeration coils may release refrigerant gas to create a cold, dry atmosphere, while secondary coils serve as backup. The robot uses a gripper with parallel picking fingers and an insulating sleeve, and it can manipulate sealed vault covers through a locking interface.

Portable cryogenic workstations have insulated bodies, internal racks, and liquid-nitrogen chambers that can maintain samples near −150°C for up to two hours. A cryodock aligns and seals a workstation for robotic access, monitors its temperature and nitrogen level, and may automatically replenish the nitrogen. Refrigerant flows and a cryotrap-based drying system control humidity in the SHM, including accelerating moisture removal after maintenance hatches are opened.

A staged disaster-recovery process addresses jammed trays through automated repositioning, manual access and correction, vault disassembly, repair or replacement, and final auditing of sample locations. Additional embodiments include an ultra-low-temperature camera module, an alternative star-shaped rack, and procedures for transferring racks between an existing and replacement vault.

This continuation application concerns deuterated heterocycle fused gamma-carbolines, particularly compounds containing a trideuterated N-methyl group, a dideuterated methylene adjacent to N-methyl, or both. The compounds may be in free form or as pharmaceutically acceptable acid-addition salts, including p-toluenesulfonate, and may have defined deuterium enrichment and high diastereomeric purity. They antagonize 5-HT2A receptors, inhibit the serotonin reuptake transporter, and modulate dopaminergic protein phosphorylation similarly to their non-deuterated analogs while unexpectedly exhibiting improved metabolic stability.

The application addresses the need to treat acute and residual symptoms of psychosis, including schizophrenia, which existing antipsychotics may not adequately address, while avoiding off-target histamine H1 and muscarinic receptor effects. It also describes uses for depression, anxiety, sleep disorders, dementia, Parkinson’s disease, dyskinesia, migraine, sexual disorders, social phobias, gastrointestinal motility disorders, post-traumatic stress disorder, impulse-control disorders, and combinations of psychiatric or neurological conditions. Residual symptoms are described as including negative symptoms, general psychopathology, depression, cognitive impairment, and insomnia.

Pharmaceutical compositions include immediate-, delayed-, sustained-, and controlled-release formulations. Depot compositions contain the compounds in biodegradable polymeric matrices, preferably PLGA, for injection and release over approximately 14 to 180 days. The application also describes oral osmotic-controlled delivery systems with gelatin capsules, barrier, expandable, and semipermeable layers, exit orifices, and multilayer drug cores having different drug and salt concentrations.

Methods of treatment include administration of the compounds or their compositions alone or with other therapeutic agents, including antipsychotics, antidepressants, hypnotics, cholinesterase inhibitors, NMDA antagonists, GABA-modulating drugs, and other receptor-targeted agents. Representative oral doses range from about 1–100 mg daily for general CNS disorders and 1–10 mg daily for sleep disorders, agitation, aggressive behavior, PTSD, or impulse-control disorders, with higher doses possible for depot formulations.

Synthetic examples describe deuterated N-methyl, alpha-methylene, combined deuterated, and deuterated phenyl analogs. In mice, Examples 1–3 showed substantially less relative amide formation than non-deuterated Formula Q while retaining similar receptor-binding profiles; Example 2 showed 98% inhibition of human 5-HT2A receptors at 0.1 µM. In rats, oral Example 2 produced 55% less relative metabolism to the N-demethylated/alpha-oxidized metabolite than Formula Q and approximately half the metabolite AUC, while intravenous metabolism was also lower. In dogs, sublingual Example 2 produced about 72% greater parent-compound AUC than Formula Q, whereas subcutaneous dosing produced comparable parent AUCs for both compounds.

The coach credits his team’s success to aggressive puck pursuit, quick skating, and forcing opponents to turn and chase pucks. He praises veterans for setting the example and says players respond to adversity by continuing to play. His message is to make sound puck decisions, play fast, avoid feeding San Jose’s transition game, and maintain the approach until the result emerges.

Sid Crosby is praised for his unmatched work ethic, faceoff ability, puck battles, complete two-way play, and inspiration to teammates. Phil is recognized for his scoring and line chemistry, while Geno is generating chances. The coaching staff has managed a smaller, quick player’s workload to preserve his speed. Young players such as Conor are learning the need for consistent nightly execution, with veterans providing mentorship.

The coach also discusses San Jose’s size and strong low-zone puck protection, noting the need to disrupt passes to the points and remain in shooting lanes. He praises Chris’s physical forechecking, a mobile defenseman’s puck-moving and offensive instincts, the balanced forward group, and Rusty’s speed, tenacity, and willingness to go to the net. Reflecting on player development, he emphasizes patience, opportunity, the right environment, and continually improving communication and video work to help players grow.

Alex Ovechkin says receiving the award means a great deal after a difficult year and that he feels “back on track.” He credits his teammates, coaching staff, family, and Adam’s support while adjusting from left wing to right wing. Although the switch was challenging and he can return to left wing if needed, he is pleased with the results and wants to remain ready for the Stanley Cup. Ovechkin also discusses a broken foot caused by a blocked shot, continuing to play through the playoffs after an MRI, and receiving injections and treatment from Washington’s trainers. He says he will not refuse to play when he can skate and hold his stick, because hockey players must be ready for every game.

STAT’s Morning Rounds newsletter highlights metal-organic frameworks winning the chemistry Nobel and previews coverage of science, medicine, and health policy. It reports that Peter Marks, forced to resign as the FDA’s top vaccine regulator in March by Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr., has joined Eli Lilly to oversee molecule discovery and infectious-disease product development. The article is exclusive to STAT+ subscribers.

Triangle Rotation is a secondary offense against a triangle zone, using three-player clockwise and counterclockwise rotations. Penetration can lead to a pop-out, baseline feed, or weak-side lob, while the high post initiates side screens. Success requires simple execution, coordination, recognition, communication, timing, and fundamentals for attacking zone defenses. Coaches should scout opponents, anticipate defensive reads and matchups, adjust during games, vary alignments and entries, and attack weaker defenders. In the Triangle & Two defense, three players guard in a triangle zone while two chasers focus solely on aggressive pass and rebounding denial.

Two federal animal studies exposed rats and mice to cellphone radiation for nine hours daily for up to two years, at levels far above typical human exposure. The final rat study found a small increase in an unusual heart tumor in males and “equivocal evidence” of DNA damage and some cancers, but no significant problems in females or mice and no firm evidence of brain tumors. The FDA said existing safety limits remain acceptable, while the American Cancer Society said human studies show weak evidence of an association with cancer and advised concerned users to use an earpiece. Researchers said the results may not translate directly to humans, while critics said the studies were too small to detect rare harms. An IARC working group labeled cellphones possibly carcinogenic in 2011, but major epidemiological studies have found little or no brain-tumor risk.

Michael Johnson, Babson College’s provost and a marketing professor, was named president of John Carroll University, its first lay leader since its 131-year-old founding by the Jesuits. The board approved a five-year contract, and he will start July 1 and join the management, marketing and supply chain faculty. He succeeds the retiring Rev. Robert Niehoff.

The passage reviews the development and educational use of OpenAI’s ChatGPT from GPT-1 in 2018 to GPT-4 in March 2023. It describes ChatGPT’s rapid adoption, potential to personalize learning, support language learning, provide feedback, create course materials and assessments, assist teachers, and develop students’ critical and creative thinking. However, its use raises concerns about plagiarism, cheating, false or biased information, unreliable responses, and weakened independent and higher-order thinking. Because plagiarism-detection software may not identify ChatGPT-generated writing, researchers recommend revised assessment methods, institutional policies, and guidance for students.

The study assesses the accuracy and validity of ChatGPT responses in education through a PRISMA-guided systematic review. Searches of Google Scholar, Web of Science, and EBSCOhost produced 274 records. Eighteen peer-reviewed empirical English-language studies with accessible full texts were selected after removing duplicates and applying inclusion and exclusion criteria. Data were coded in Microsoft Excel and analysed thematically. The reviewed studies covered medicine, writing assignments, business, finance, chemistry, academic advising, physics, social science, and coding and programming.

The review found that ChatGPT commonly produces coherent, precise, concise, well-structured, creative text, sometimes exceeding the quality of high-school or university writing. It can perform strongly on essay-based examinations, pass several undergraduate and medical assessments, provide supportive academic advice, and write readable, well-structured Java code. Examples include a 78.77% score on the Radiation Oncology In-Training exam, 76% on the UK Situational Judgement Test, and 65.5% on a gastroenterology test.

Performance declined as tasks became more complex. ChatGPT answered 85% of basic, 20% of medium-difficulty, and 12% of hard finance questions correctly; solved 13 of 30 chemistry problems; and showed limited performance in physics, clinical reasoning, and scientific subjects. Other weaknesses included insufficient depth, weak argumentation and analysis, poor calculation ability, lack of judgment, hallucination, failure to interpret nuanced prompts, and inconsistent answers to repeated questions. It could confidently present incorrect information and did not reliably distinguish itself from human writing.

The findings recommend validating ChatGPT outputs, carefully structuring text prompts, redesigning assessments around higher-order skills, creating authentic assessments involving ChatGPT, establishing institutional usage policies, and training students to use it constructively. The author proposes an “ABCD framework” for educational adoption and suggests collaboration between institutions and developers to create specialised educational tools. Limitations include database restrictions, a search cutoff of 26 October 2023, inaccessible studies, and the restriction to eligible peer-reviewed empirical research. Further research should examine AI’s effects on learning, innovative evaluation frameworks, and customised ChatGPT applications across disciplines.

An institution-based cross-sectional study at Hemen Medical Center in Addis Ababa assessed pregnant women’s awareness and attitudes toward labor epidural analgesia (LEA) and factors influencing its use. From June 3 to August 30, 2024, 267 women in their third trimester who attended antenatal care and planned vaginal delivery were sampled systematically using a structured questionnaire; 230 complete responses were analyzed. Women with previous epidural experience or a fetal anomaly were excluded. Descriptive statistics and binary logistic regression were used.

Among the 230 participants, 78% had heard of LEA, but only 6.5% identified healthcare providers as their primary information source, and 34% had received explanations from providers during antenatal care. While 47% considered LEA effective for labor pain relief, only 14.3% were willing to consider it; 47.8% had no plan and 37.8% were undecided. Major concerns included side effects and cost (20% each), interference with natural labor, and fetal safety (11% each).

Multivariable analysis found that higher education, higher family income, belief in LEA’s pain-relieving effectiveness, and absence of perceived fetal harm were associated with deciding to receive LEA. The study concluded that insufficient healthcare-provider counseling, misconceptions, and fears contribute to low acceptance and recommended comprehensive antenatal education and counseling. Limitations included the single-center setting, inability to assess prior epidural experience, and inability to track actual uptake because of the cross-sectional design.

Researchers at King’s College London analyzed 49 studies involving 266,939 people and found that higher physical activity levels were associated with lower odds of developing depression across all age groups. They called for policies supporting physical activity and further research into activity types and dosage.

The Four Down offense is primarily used for a period’s final shot but can also serve any team with a talented ballhandler. Called by raising four fingers downward, it is also known as “Four Low” or “Four Flat.” Four non-ballhandlers align along the baseline, with shooters in corners, creating space for isolation drives or jumpers. Help defense opens drop passes to posts or kick-outs to shooters. When closely guarded or facing the five-second rule, corners pop out for pressure-release passes and may assume the ballhandler’s role. Late-clock options include mid and triple base screens and a weak-side baseline misdirection double.

The passage explains the 2-3 zone as a common zone defense that protects the basket, limits dribble penetration, and works well against teams with weak outside shooting. It can become aggressive and trapping against quick, agile opponents and is effective against talented or large low-post players. Defenders X1 and X2 play together above the free-throw line, X5 guards the post, and X3 and X4 cover the baseline and weak-side rebounding. Positioning shifts according to whether the ball is in the middle, on a wing, or in a corner. Wing defenders may deny return passes or drop to help against dominant post players. Baseline defenders “show” ballhandlers on reversal passes until the guards take over. A 1-1-3 variation can use tandem pressure to disrupt spacing and entry passes. Trap options include corner traps, point traps, and automatic wing traps that force the ball away from an outstanding shooter. Adjustments against a dominant post player involve X5 applying 3/4 or baseline pass denial, other defenders providing frontside, backside, or baseline support, and X3, X4, and X5 forming triple teams when the post receives the ball.

Intercontinental Exchange, the parent company of the New York Stock Exchange, invested $2 billion in prediction-market platform Polymarket at a $9 billion valuation. ICE will distribute Polymarket’s data, and the companies will collaborate on tokenization initiatives. The cash investment reflects growing investor interest in prediction markets, while rival Kalshi is also pursuing substantial funding.

Zacks Investment Research downgraded Caesars Entertainment (NASDAQ:CZR) from Buy to Hold. Other analyst actions included upgrades from BidaskClub to Buy and ValuEngine to Hold, while SunTrust initiated at Buy with a $14 target, Wolfe Research at Outperform with a $16 target, and Imperial Capital at Outperform with a $15.50 target. Analysts had an average Buy rating and a $14.39 consensus price target. Shares fell 0.76% to $13.00 in midday trading, with a $1.94 billion market capitalization. Caesars reported quarterly EPS of negative $0.21 versus a $0.26 estimate and revenue of $1 billion versus $2.11 billion estimated. Institutional investors owned 76.68% of the stock, and several firms increased their stakes. Caesars operates casino resorts and hospitality facilities under the Harrah’s, Caesars, and Horseshoe brands.

The UC1825B-SP uses a sense resistor to detect transformer ripple current and shut down the switching cycle when the converter exceeds its current limit; the CS-pin threshold is approximately 1 V. Test figures cover MOSFET voltage stress, output ripple, and transient response at 48-V input and up to 10-A load. The device operates from a regulated 10–30 V supply and may require bulk capacitance, typically 100 μF, depending on power and supply distance. It supports push-pull, forward, half-bridge, and full-bridge topologies.

PCB guidance emphasizes low-EMI inductors, routing feedback traces away from noisy power paths, placing input, compensation, and feed-forward capacitors close to the IC, and using short, thick power traces. Power components should be arranged so switching-loop current direction remains consistent between states. Ground planes should separate power and signal paths. Power ground, connected to PGND, must include MOSFET sources, input-return paths, bulk input capacitance, and the VCC clamp; VCC and VREF should be bypassed with low-ESR/ESL ceramic capacitors. The passage also covers documentation resources, ESD precautions, mechanical and orderable information, and TI disclaimers.

An email from Steven Kean to Bernadette Hawkins (Feb. 28, 2001, subject "Energy Issues") forwards a Feb. 26 compilation of articles on California's electricity crisis and its effects on the western U.S.

**Supply and demand (Dow Jones, Mark Golden):** A Dow Jones column disputes the California Energy Commission's forecast of 60,000 MW of capacity with little margin, estimating available supply at only 44,000 MW against a 51,000 MW requirement, after subtracting capacity lost from aging plants, power sold out of state (estimated at 5,000 MW), below-normal hydropower, and higher-than-average unplanned outages. The column argues for immediate, significant rate increases to curb demand instead of relying on blackouts, and criticizes Gov. Gray Davis's reliance on buying power and signing 10-year supply contracts.

**The rest of the West (Los Angeles Times, Peter G. Gosselin):** Other western states face similar shortages because population grew without enough new generation, and deregulation has not worked as planned in Arizona, Nevada or Washington. California's requirement that utilities buy spot power while barring cost pass-throughs triggered a regional price spiral, and Western states are now seeking to renegotiate their relationship with California — pursuing control of the Bonneville Power Administration, approving a wave of new plants in Arizona, and having Utah recall power from the Intermountain Power Project. One consultant forecast the region 6% short, with 150 to 275 hours of rolling blackouts, mostly in California.

**Peaker plant delays (Los Angeles Times, Nancy Vogel):** Construction of 29 small "peaker" plants contracted in October and November by Cal-ISO (1,279 MW, enough for more than 1 million homes, at $214 million a year for three years, roughly $6 per household annually) was slowed by the Department of Water Resources' attempt to renegotiate four-month-old contracts through the hired firm Navigant. Builders say revisions will delay projects; state officials say they are not delaying construction and are seeking better prices. Davis ordered expedited licensing and a list of 32 candidate sites was published, with a 1,000 MW target.

**Business sentiment (Los Angeles Times, Nancy Rivera Brooks):** An NFIB/Mason-Dixon survey of 523 small businesses found 4 in 10 said the crisis dimmed their view of California as a business climate and nearly 20% were exploring a move, though 69% had no intention of relocating. More than 20% had experienced blackouts; 43% said the power problem changed their views and 71% said it shaken confidence in state leadership. Other surveys found 64% of consumers still favored electricity competition (most did not understand deregulation) and that most companies were unprepared for retail competition, with few switching providers.

**Davis's political role (Los Angeles Times, Morain and Tempest):** Davis has shifted into campaign mode, promoting himself as leader of the response after being accused of inactivity. His administration is spending about $1 billion a month to buy power (over $2 billion so far), pushing a state takeover of utility transmission systems costing more than $7 billion, and offering $400 million for conservation. He has announced only a framework for rescuing Southern California Edison, and advisors note the governor bears the risk if the plan fails.

**California's energy use (Associated Press, Andrew Bridges):** Despite large total consumption, California ranks 49th in per-capita electricity use (60% of the national average) and 47th in per-capita energy use; only Texas consumes more total energy. The mild climate, strict efficiency standards dating to the 1970s, and relocation of energy-intensive industries are cited as reasons, along with efficient local industries (0.2 kWh per dollar of output versus twice that in neighboring states). California ranks 17th in utility efficiency spending and recently released a $404 million conservation program; per-capita use rose 10% over two decades and inland migration may increase cooling demand.

**Markets (Reuters, Feb. 26):** Western spot power prices fell as plants returned to service and loads were light. Cal-ISO forecast a Tuesday peak of 29,285 MW versus 29,814 MW expected Monday; natural gas traded at $12–14 per million BTU. The report lists numerous planned and unplanned West Coast unit outages and regional peak/off-peak price tables.

**Legislative response (Dow Jones, Jason Leopold):** Key Assembly and Senate members gave only partial support to Davis's plan to buy the utilities' transmission lines — $2.76 billion for Southern California Edison's lines (about 2.3 times book value) and roughly $7.5 billion for 26,000 miles of lines from three utilities — intended to restore utility solvency and address roughly $13 billion in undercollected 2000 power costs. Senate Energy Committee Chair Debra Bowen and others withheld support pending further details and concessions; Republicans objected to financing without a rate increase, and consumer groups opposed the proposal, with one advocate threatening a 2002 ballot initiative.

The New York Court of Appeals held that Manhattan Community Board 7 lacked the capacity to bring an Article 78 proceeding challenging the Department of City Planning’s denial of its Freedom of Information Law request for documents concerning the proposed Trump City development at the Penn Central railyards.

The Board sought a draft restrictive declaration and related correspondence to fulfill its advisory role under the Uniform Land Use Review Procedure. Although lower courts found that the Board had standing and was entitled to the documents, the Court distinguished standing from capacity. A legislatively created governmental entity must obtain authority to sue expressly or by necessary implication, unless legislation clearly negates judicial review.

Although the Board had a functional responsibility to review and make recommendations on the project, the Court found no such authority. The Charter specified which documents Boards could receive, denied them subpoena power, and was not amended to grant litigation rights despite proposals to do so. The Board’s advisory duties could be performed without a broad FOIL lawsuit, particularly because the documents available under ULURP had been furnished. FOIL’s broad standing provision could not cure the absence of capacity to sue. The Court reversed the lower courts’ decisions and dismissed the petition.

Cboe’s bitcoin futures launch drew nearly 3,700 contracts across about 20 trading firms by Monday afternoon. CEO Ed Tilly said the debut could support future cryptocurrency products, including options and ETFs, pending regulatory approval and several contract settlements. The most-active contract rose 20% and briefly triggered a five-minute trading halt, while Cboe’s website went down under heavy traffic. REX Shares, Van Eck and First Trust again sought SEC approval for bitcoin ETFs, and Cboe appealed the SEC’s rejection of Gemini’s proposed ETF. Tilly also predicted futures on other cryptocurrencies as demand grows.

The ADS9803 is an eight-channel, 20-bit, 2-MSPS data-acquisition device with a built-in analog front end. It can be powered down through the PWDN pin or the PD_CH field in register C0h of bank 1. After power-up or reset, it requires a free-running sampling clock and a sequence of register writes to initialize its interface, analog input ranges, bandwidths, common-mode settings, and output lanes.

Speed-boost mode supports sampling rates up to 8 MSPS for one selected channel pair; the other six channels remain idle, and the selected pair is converted on every sampling clock. SPI configuration uses 16-bit registers in three banks with 8-bit addresses. Bank 0 is always accessible, while banks 1 and 2 are selected through REG_BANK_SEL. Register writes require SPI_RD_EN = 0; reads require SPI_RD_EN = 1 and SPI_MODE = 1.

For SPI daisy-chain operation, multiple ADCs share CS and SCLK and are linked through their SDI and SDO pins. DAISY_CHAIN_LEN specifies the number of ADCs excluding the first, and a write across four ADCs requires 96 SCLK cycles.

Register controls cover power, bandwidth, lane count, common-mode range, averaging, test patterns, speed boost, and gain-error correction. For ATE applications, the device supports direct or multiplexed PMU connections, with low-noise bandwidth up to 22.7 kHz and wide bandwidth up to 700 kHz. Layout guidance requires close 0.1-µF supply bypassing, reference decoupling, short ground connections, and separation of analog and digital paths.

Premium FT subscription features include Lex commentary, Lionel Barber’s weekly Editor’s Choice newsletter, Newsmine’s weekly macroeconomic data summaries, and Martin Sandbu’s daily global economics commentary.

The ADS868xW is a fully integrated, 16-bit SAR ADC with a differential analog front end, precision reference, programmable gain, input and AVDD alarms, and a multiSPI digital interface. It supports single-ended or differential bipolar and unipolar inputs with straight-binary output; LSB size equals FSR/2¹⁶. An external 4.096 V reference can drive the internal buffer by setting INTREF_DIS and applying the reference at REFIO. REFCAP requires at least 10 µF plus a nearby 1 µF decoupling capacitor, and the buffer cannot drive external loads.

The active-high alarm output supports programmable input high/low thresholds with hysteresis and fixed typical AVDD limits of 4.7 V and 5.3 V. Active alarm flags clear after each conversion, while tripped flags remain set until ALARM_REG is read. Alarm information can be accessed through the alarm pin, internal registers, or appended output flags.

The multiSPI interface supports legacy SPI protocols for configuration, single- or dual-SDO reads, and source-synchronous operation. It supports standard SPI and daisy-chain topologies, with optimal daisy-chain frames requiring 32 × N clock edges. Devices operate in RESET, ACQ, and CONV states. Data-transfer frames begin on the falling edge of CONVST/CS and end on its rising edge; 32 clocks constitute an optimal frame, short frames cannot write commands, and long frames use the final 32 bits as the command. Nine configuration registers control reset and power, protocols, output data, input ranges, and alarms.

An example eight-channel industrial input module combines an ADS8681W with a MUX36D08 multiplexer for PLC, DCS, and data-acquisition applications. The device uses separate AVDD and DVDD supplies, requires specified decoupling, and offers programmable NAP and power-down modes. Recommended PCB layout separates analog and digital signals and places reference, supply, and bypass capacitors close to their pins.

PPL Corporation shares rose $0.19 to close at $37.65 on Wednesday despite a net $29.88 million money outflow. Analysts issued mixed ratings: Zacks downgraded the stock to “hold,” ValuEngine upgraded it to “buy,” BidaskClub upgraded it to “hold,” and Jefferies reiterated “buy” with a $43.50 target. Eight analysts rate the stock “hold” and three rate it “buy,” producing a “Hold” consensus and $38.94 price target.

PPL reported quarterly EPS of $0.52, beating the $0.50 estimate, while revenue of $1.73 billion missed the $1.79 billion estimate and fell 3.4% year over year. The company paid a $0.395 quarterly dividend, representing a $1.58 annualized dividend and 4.24% yield, with a 66.11% payout ratio.

Insiders sold 47,163 shares worth $1.86 million over three months. Several institutional investors increased holdings during the first quarter, including Los Angeles Capital Management & Equity Research, which acquired 264,787 shares. Institutions own 71.01% of the stock, while insiders own 0.40%.

PPL is a utility holding company serving electricity customers in the United Kingdom, Pennsylvania, Kentucky, Virginia and Tennessee, and natural gas customers in Kentucky.

The paper proposes proactive prevention for Europe’s ageing population by targeting the “young elderly” aged 60–75, with the aim of keeping them healthy, active and independent after 75 and reducing long-term health and social care costs. Its three-step approach combines prevention, mobile interventions and commercially sustainable ecosystems supported by political commitment and research. The young elderly constitute 18–23% of the population in most EU countries, estimated at 97 million people by 2020.

Digital wellness services are presented as an alternative to relying on tightly regulated health and social care data. They would collect information on users’ daily routines, provide understandable summaries and advice, and support four dimensions of wellness: intellectual, physical, social and emotional. These dimensions reflect the multidimensional and changing nature of functional impairment. Services should be designed with users through action design research rather than simply for them.

Finland’s BeWell programme develops these services through the Wellmo omnivore mobile platform, which integrates more than 100 applications and devices, and Tieto’s cloud platform, which supports data collection, analysis and scalable services. Adaptive interfaces, data and knowledge fusion, advanced analytics and commercially viable ecosystems are presented as prerequisites for sustaining services at large scale.

Research involving about 100 workshops, a survey with 101 usable responses and 25 interviews found that participants valued wellness, were generally confident using mobile applications and showed interest in both physical and intellectual wellbeing. About 73% used smartphones. Younger, better-educated, employed or voluntary, and higher-income participants showed different attitudes and adoption patterns. The study provides preliminary support for digital wellness services as a viable way to create routines, but its regional sample is small and further validation with a larger sample is planned.

Amazon.com, Inc. filed a Form 8-K dated April 26, 2018, announcing its first-quarter 2018 financial results. The filing incorporates a results press release and information regarding non-GAAP financial measures as exhibits. It was signed by Senior Vice President and CFO Brian T. Olsavsky.

Blackhawks players Patrick Kane, Bryan Bickell, and Brent Seabrook reflected on an overtime victory that evened the series and sent the team back to Chicago. Seabrook scored the winner and praised the team’s effort, while Kane said the postgame celebration was among the most excited he had seen. They credited the team’s depth, five-man play, speed, backchecking, and scoring contributions from multiple players.

Bickell emphasized using physical play to open the ice, particularly against Boston’s Zdeno Chara, who rarely gets hit. Kane and Seabrook said the team needed to improve defensively, including the penalty kill, shooting lanes, and play at both ends because low-scoring games were expected. Seabrook also encouraged Johnny Gaudreau to stop worrying about scoring and continue contributing, while Kane stressed focusing on getting to the net rather than dwelling on individual matchups.

FreeNAS 11 returns after problematic version 10, with a FreeBSD 11-STABLE base, bhyve virtualization, AWS S3 compatibility, messaging integrations, configurable startup services, FreeBSD jails, and a beta Angular GUI. Docker support is deferred to a future point release.

This study examined the introduction, spread, and evolution of SARS-CoV-2 Alpha and Delta variants in Vietnam during 2021 in relation to public health measures. Nasopharyngeal samples from two referral hospitals underwent whole-genome sequencing, lineage classification, phylogenetic, phylogeographic, phylodynamic, recombination, and selection analyses.

Of 1,365 selected samples, 1,303 genomes were obtained: 1,222 Delta, 74 Alpha, five A.23.1, and two B.1.637; no recombinants were detected. Most Delta sequences belonged to lineage AY.57. Alpha sequences formed four clusters, indicating multiple introductions between January and May, but community transmission remained sporadic. Delta was first detected in late April and was the only variant detected from June onward. Vietnam recorded 1,632 infections and no deaths from January through April, followed by 1,727,398 infections and 32,359 deaths from May through December.

Phylogeographic analysis of 748 filtered AY.57 sequences estimated a most recent common ancestor of March 14, 2021, and indicated initial introduction into northeastern Vietnam. The northeast and Red River Delta subsequently seeded other regions, especially the southeast, while interprovincial dispersal was infrequent. From July onward, the southeast became a source for the north and other regions, with localized clusters emerging in several areas. Genetic diversity increased sharply from April to August, remained relatively stable, and declined slightly in late November. Overall dN/dS suggested weak purifying selection, with positive selection in ORF1b, ORF3a, envelope, and ORF7a.

The authors concluded that strict containment limited Alpha transmission and AY.57 dispersal, while Delta’s introduction into a largely immunologically naïve population produced an explosive outbreak and increased viral diversity. Hospital-based sampling bias from July may have limited detection of other variants. The findings emphasize genomic surveillance as a tool for guiding pandemic responses.

JPMorgan Chase reduced its DeVry Education Group stake 9.6% in Q3 to 499,104 shares worth $11.5 million, while UBS Asset Management, PNC Financial, Retirement Systems of Alabama, and KBC Group increased holdings; M&T Bank established a $229,000 position.
