DeVry is a global education-services provider operating in healthcare, international and professional education, and business, technology and management.

Ostersunds were drawn against Arsenal in the Europa League last 32, while Napoli face RB Leipzig. Borussia Dortmund play Atalanta, Atletico Madrid face Copenhagen, and Zenit complete the draw after dropping down from the Champions League.

This systematic review examined associations between marijuana, medical cannabis, endocannabinoid supplements, and the microbiome. Following PRISMA and PICO/PECOs methods, researchers searched PubMed, Embase, and Cochrane through July 20, 2022. Nine studies—six cohorts, one case-control study, and two clinical trials involving 2,526 participants—were included. Participants were 17–101 years old, more than 85% were women, and 43% were patients.

Findings linked marijuana or cannabinoid exposure with microbial changes in several conditions. Among people with HIV, marijuana use was associated with increased Fusobacterium and Anaerotruncus and decreased Dorea, while users also had differing rates of bacterial vaginosis and gonorrhea. In an exercise intervention, increased AEA and PEA were associated with lower TNF-α and IL-6 and changes in butyrate-producing gut bacteria. In obesity, OEA supplementation significantly reduced energy and carbohydrate intake and increased Akkermansia muciniphila compared with placebo. Marijuana users showed altered oral bacterial taxa, including increased S. mutans and Lactobacilli, but the review stated that it was not established whether these changes cause malignancy. Marijuana use was also associated with altered gut microbiota, dietary patterns, mitochondrial function, and cognitive measures.

Reported adverse effects included coughing and wheezing in 21.4% of patients and drowsiness, night sweats, systemic aspergillosis, and coughing in one patient; these reportedly resolved after stopping marijuana. Limited evidence and substantial clinical heterogeneity prevented meta-analysis, and further research was recommended.

Chinese textile companies increasingly use North Korean factories for cheaper labor, with garments assembled in North Korea labeled “Made in China” and exported globally, according to traders and businesses in Dandong. Dozens of agents link Chinese suppliers with buyers worldwide, some of whom may not know the production origin. Textiles were North Korea’s second-largest export in 2016, worth $752 million, while U.N. sanctions over its missile and nuclear programs did not ban textile exports.

Chinese suppliers ship fabrics and raw materials to North Korea, and finished clothing often passes through Chinese ports. State-owned factories in North Korea reportedly save manufacturers up to 75%, while workers earn substantially less than their Chinese counterparts. Chinese companies also employ thousands of North Korean workers in China, earning foreign currency that is largely remitted to the North Korean government; the U.N. says this helps fund nuclear and missile programs. New sanctions prohibit countries from increasing North Korean workers abroad, though China does not disclose totals. A Reuters visit to one Dandong factory found 40 North Korean women making winter jackets on long shifts for about half the average Chinese factory wage.

Glenner Town Square, a new Alzheimer’s and dementia daycare in Chula Vista, is an 8,500-square-foot, 1950s-style miniature downtown designed to evoke long-term memories. Its 13 storefronts surround a faux-grass park and offer experiences including a cinema, diner, library, boutique, 1959 Ford T-Bird, pet store, nurse station and nursery. It opened in April 2018 at 2678 Main St. Glenner’s Hillcrest and Encinitas centers will eventually become Town Square projects. The passage also lists licensed adult day programs for cognitively impaired adults throughout San Diego County, including services, hours, fees, addresses and contact details.

A hockey team is making its third finals appearance with three different teams and hopes to win the trophy and achieve a better finish. It credits hard work, strong fan support, and a sold-out building, while expecting a tight playoff series against the experienced Flyers.

The president reports that renewed bipartisan cooperation has restored American confidence and economic momentum after the problems of the 1970s. He cites inflation falling from 12.4 to 3.2 percent, an across-the-board tax reduction, tax indexing, higher real after-tax income, economic deregulation, four million jobs created in 1983, and growing private enterprise. He acknowledges that unemployment remains a serious concern.

He outlines four goals for the 1980s: sustained economic growth, development of America’s “next frontier,” stronger traditional values, and a meaningful peace. To control spending and deficits, he supports limiting government’s size, reducing regulations and paperwork, examining spending recommendations from the Grace Commission, and seeking bipartisan agreement on a $100 billion deficit-reduction plan over three years. He also proposes a presidential line-item veto, a balanced-budget amendment, and a simpler, fairer tax code that could broaden compliance and lower individual tax rates.

For the space frontier, he directs NASA to develop a permanently manned space station within a decade and proposes greater private-sector participation and international cooperation in space. Environmental initiatives include expanded funding for hazardous-waste cleanup, Chesapeake Bay restoration, acid-rain research, park and conservation lands, and environmentally responsible development of offshore resources.

Strengthening families and education is presented as central to national renewal. The president calls for educational standards, discipline, merit rewards, parental involvement, tuition tax credits, school choice, religious acknowledgment in schools, and protection of unborn children. He also supports action against child pornography, abduction, family violence, organized crime, and drugs; expanded opportunity for women and minorities; fair pensions and retirement accounts; child care; enforcement of parental support; and enterprise zones for high-unemployment areas.

For peace, he advocates improved relations with the Soviet Union, stronger alliances, nuclear arms reductions, democratic development, conflict mediation in the Middle East, Central America, southern Africa, and Lebanon, international cooperation against terrorism, and freer global trade. Addressing the Soviet people, he declares that nuclear war cannot be won and must never be fought.

The address also praises the military, Congress, volunteers, and ordinary citizens, including Medal of Honor recipient Sergeant Stephen Trujillo and workers assisting disadvantaged people and people with disabilities. Concluding that the nation is safer, stronger, and more secure, the president urges continued bipartisan cooperation, faith, courage, and commitment to economic opportunity, freedom, and peace.

Ben Rice was born and raised in Cohasset, Massachusetts, and grew up a Yankees fan with Derek Jeter as his favorite player. He attended Noble and Greenough School in Dedham, then saw limited baseball at Dartmouth: 81 plate appearances in 2019, a 2020 season cut short by COVID-19, and a canceled 2021 Ivy League season, leaving him with 110 career plate appearances when the Yankees drafted him in the 12th round of the 2021 MLB Draft. After an inconsistent 2024 rookie season, Rice hit 26 home runs in 138 games in 2025, splitting time between first base, catcher and designated hitter, and homered in Game 2 of the Wild Card Series against Boston.

The Federal Reserve raised rates for a third consecutive quarter to 1%–1.25%, citing strong job growth and moderate expansion despite renewed inflation weakness. It lowered this year’s inflation forecast to 1.6%, retained 2% for next year, and said unemployment could fall below 4%.

The study used a simplified SIR-based compartmental model and stochastic simulations to assess community-wide screening and isolation in a semi-isolated community without vaccines or medicines. The model incorporated local transmission, infection influx from outside, recovery or death, screening efficiency, and delays before isolation. Theoretical analysis showed that control requires isolation to outpace new infections, making long detection-to-isolation delays difficult.

With external influx of 0.1 cases per day, R0=3 spread out of control within 100 days without screening, whereas daily screening at 0.9 efficiency limited each infection wave to 10 cases and averaged 1.64±0.96 days. Daily screening remained effective at R0=6 but failed at R0=8, requiring additional measures such as social distancing and masks. At R0=3, screening every three days controlled spread; raising efficiency from 0.7 to 0.9 reduced average annual infections from 267.46±213.83 to 142.76±53.94. Weekly screening performed worse, while biweekly screening failed at both tested efficiencies. Infections increased with external influx, supporting strict border control. Overall, the results indicate that timely, regular, periodic screening can control transmission when accompanied by effective isolation and strict border controls.

Tom Brady’s agent Don Yee said Brady intends to return in 2018 and play beyond his current contract, potentially into his mid-40s. Brady has two seasons remaining, with $14 million plus a $1 million roster bonus due each season. Patriots owner Robert Kraft said Brady’s current contract is not an issue.

Netflix’s popularity in South Africa has contributed to declines in DStv Premium subscribers and average revenue per customer, despite overall subscriber growth. MultiChoice is pursuing a streaming-only package, with content rights and potential ICASA regulation viewed as major challenges. Excessive regulation could threaten South African jobs.

CoreWeave’s shares rebounded amid strong AI sentiment and major OpenAI and Meta deals worth $22.4 billion and $14.2 billion, respectively, diversifying its customer base. However, Microsoft remains a significant revenue-concentration risk, while debt-funded expansion, heavy capex, and a high forward revenue multiple raise sustainability concerns. The author says optimism appears fully priced in and risks remain elevated, suggesting a possible cooling-off despite strong momentum.

More than 130 members of Joppatowne High School’s 138-member Class of 2018 received diplomas at its 45th commencement ceremony, with about 95 percent planning to enter college, technical school, the military or law enforcement. Graduate Amya Hill, whose family traveled from several states to celebrate her, plans to study nursing at Albany State University and encouraged students to persist through academic struggles. Fellow graduate Zachary Wagmun plans to enter an electrician’s apprenticeship at Harford Community College.

Valedictorian Kacey Lebrun urged graduates to pursue their goals, while class president Breea Stevenson shared lessons about trying new things, distancing oneself from negative influences and focusing on the present. Officials addressed the class, citing Baltimore County police officer Amy Caprio and Maryland National Guard Sgt. Eddison “Eddie” A. Hermond, who died while serving others.

The coach said Tampa Bay’s focus is simply to extend the playoff series against Calgary. He noted the Flames face more pressure as the favored team playing at home on Hockey Night in Canada. After a long flight and a difficult home game, Tampa Bay plans to stay overnight for additional rest. He praised Calgary’s star player, stressed that battles and big plays at key moments will determine the outcome, and rejected suggestions that his players lacked effort. He said both teams may feel pressure as the Stanley Cup Final approaches.

A letter from fired assistant U.S. attorney Michael Ben’Ary accused DOJ leadership of removing career officials and prioritizing punishment of President Trump’s perceived enemies over public safety and national security. He said a false social media post apparently prompted his firing during a terrorism prosecution concerning the 2021 Afghan airport bombing, which killed 13 U.S. service members and 160 Afghan civilians. Ben’Ary was dismissed after commentator Julie Kelly linked him to Lisa Monaco and suggested he had resisted James Comey’s indictment.

Using a continuum model with screened intervalley interactions, exact diagonalization, and Hartree–Fock band calculations, the authors identify an intermediate intervalley superconducting phase in the half-filled second moiré bands of approximately 2°-twisted bilayer MoTe2. Tuning the screening length \(d\) produces a sequence: a ferromagnetic Chern insulator for \(d<d_{c,1}\approx0.15a_M\), a superconducting phase for \(d_{c,1}<d<d_{c,2}\approx0.33a_M\), and a non-Abelian fractional quantum spin Hall insulator for \(d>d_{c,2}\).

Superconductivity is supported by zero magnetization and momentum, enhanced intervalley entanglement, maximized negative pair binding energy, a dominant eigenvalue in the pair-density spectrum, and finite superfluid stiffness. The pair wavefunction identifies time-reversal-symmetric, nodal extended \(s\)-wave pairing between holes \((\uparrow,k)\) and \((\downarrow,-k)\). The superconducting state connects continuously to the fractional spin Hall insulator, where simultaneous changes in topology and symmetry are described by a Chern–Simons theory in which a shared matter-field condensate enforces \(a=-b\).

Non-uniform quantum geometry is essential: a uniform first Landau-level analogue lacks the intermediate phase, while a generalized Landau level with non-uniform geometry reproduces its main features. The authors suggest that the screening length could be controlled through gating or substrate engineering, making the phase potentially accessible experimentally.

Over-the-counter (OTC) trading occurs directly between two parties through decentralized electronic networks of dealers and market makers rather than a centralized exchange. OTC markets trade stocks, bonds, derivatives, commodities, ETFs, currencies, and other instruments, with contracts that can be customized to each party’s needs. They provide unlisted companies with access to capital and offer flexibility for specialized assets, foreign-company ADRs, hedging, and private transactions.

The market is typically less transparent and less strictly regulated than formal exchanges. Risks include counterparty default, weak liquidity, high bid-ask spreads and slippage, fraud, manipulation, speculative volatility, and limited company reporting requirements. Following the 2007–2008 crisis, FINRA introduced clearinghouses for post-trade processing.

OTC stocks are generally small-company securities, though some large foreign-company ADRs also trade OTC. The passage cites poor long-term performance: most OTC stocks have negative returns, many become bankrupt or delisted, and more than 90% of penny stocks reportedly fail. A study covering 10,000 OTC stocks from 2001–2010 found an average loss of 27% and a median return of minus 37%. These figures lead the article to advise against treating OTC markets as a long-term investment venue and to warn against day trading them because of poor liquidity and transaction costs.

OTC trading is also possible for cryptocurrencies, both through exchange-run desks for large off-market deals and peer-to-peer platforms. Regular investors generally access OTC securities through online brokers, which may charge higher fees, restrict trading around market opens and closes, or require limit orders. The passage stresses thorough research and investing only amounts that can be lost.

OptumCare offers 12-week “Brainsaver” classes at three Valley locations, combining physical exercise, stress reduction, cognitive activities, education, socialization and brain-healthy foods. The holistic program aims to support brain health, and students from their mid-50s to late 80s report noticing a difference.

A federal government shutdown appeared increasingly likely after President Donald Trump met with top congressional leaders at the White House, less than two days before a funding deadline. Vice President JD Vance blamed Democrats, while Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer said the parties remained far apart but believed Trump heard Democratic objections for the first time.

Republicans want a stopgap funding bill through late November. Democrats demand funding and protections for several key measures, particularly enhanced Obamacare tax credits. Both sides blamed the other, with Democrats alleging they were excluded from drafting the Republican bill and Republicans calling the approach hostage-taking. Earlier competing funding bills failed in the Senate, where 60 votes are needed and Republicans hold 53 seats.

After 9/11 and amid a recent rise in anti-Muslim incidents, American Muslims have expanded public programs to address misconceptions about Islam and engage with other Americans. Moina Shaiq’s Fremont, California, “Meet a Muslim” event, which began after she advertised for questions about Muslim women, terrorism and other religions, drew about 100 people and has since reached libraries, businesses, clubs, churches, private homes, Arizona and Atlanta.

Similar “Ask a Muslim” events have occurred on college campuses and elsewhere, including one by a Muslim former U.S. Marine who traveled with a sign inviting questions. Muslim advocates say these local encounters can counter stereotypes, fear and xenophobia. Some critics, including racial justice activist Asha Noor, argue that changing bigots’ minds is unlikely and that policy change should be prioritized. Shaiq, who has faced threats, says her talks promote love, compassion and peace and teach that Muslims are human and share the same needs as others.

The disclosure proposes methods for transmitting and receiving sounding reference signals (SRSs) in an NR wireless communication system by configuring a guard period of one or more symbols between SRS resources and adjacent uplink transmissions, particularly for UE antenna switching. A base station may signal guard-period configuration through RRC, MAC-CE, or DCI. The configuration can specify whether the guard period exists, its start-position index, symbol count, and placement before or after SRS resources, with the symbol count determined by numerology or subcarrier spacing in some embodiments. Placement may also be inferred from PUSCH or PUCCH scheduling and beam information indicated by SRI or TPMI.

For collisions involving PUCCH, PUSCH, or other SRS resource sets, the disclosure defines priority and handling rules. SRS resources and their guard period may be treated as one SRS group, with the guard period assigned the same priority as the associated SRS. Alternatives include dropping the guard period, SRS resources, or PUCCH; puncturing or rate-matching PUSCH; shifting SRS symbols; or assuming no collision occurs. Colliding SRS resource sets may be prioritized by set priority, trigger timing, or resource-set usage, with lower-priority groups partially or wholly dropped or moved to a later slot. These procedures aim to reduce uplink distortion caused by antenna switching.
Turing Tensor Cores accelerate deep-learning matrix operations, add INT8/INT4 inference modes, and power DLSS, which combines rendered-scene features and multiple frames using fewer samples than TAA.

Zsolt Lakatos, 31, was sentenced in absentia to 13 years in prison for intentionally injuring his four-month-old son, whom he admitted shaking on two occasions. He failed to return to court after being released on bail, hid in Litherland for eight days and was arrested. He pleaded guilty to breaching bail, saying he had panicked at the prospect of imprisonment, and received a further 10-day sentence. The child, now 22 months old and in foster care, suffered brain bleeding, fractured ribs, a fractured shin and retinal haemorrhaging. A judge said the injuries were catastrophic and would require lifelong medication, nursing care and support, with the child unlikely ever to live independently.

Tesla Motors, Inc. furnished its January 3, 2016 press release as Exhibit 99.1 under Form 8-K Items 2.02 and 7.01. The information was not deemed filed or incorporated by reference absent express reference. General Counsel Todd A. Maron signed the report on January 4, 2016.

The coach discusses the Blackhawks’ growth, success, and commitment to improvement, highlighting consistent communication, accountability, leadership, and making those around them better. He praises Quenneville’s quiet confidence, work ethic, consistency, and ability to elevate players through high expectations.

The team’s goaltending has been outstanding, with Crow and Corey supporting each other through healthy competition. Scottie received an opportunity in Nashville and played exceptionally, while Corey remained solid after returning to the net. Quenneville’s timely performances and continued improvement have also been important during the playoffs.

Line combinations involving Kaner, Richie, Steeger, Hossa, and Johnny were adjusted as necessary, with all lines improving as games progressed. The team is being encouraged to treat every game as a must-win, play faster, and continue finding ways to win, although matching strong defensive pairings remains difficult.

Kane is praised as an elite playmaker and is being encouraged to adopt a greater shot mentality, which creates more coverage issues for opponents and can lead to turnovers when he searches too long for the perfect play. The coach also emphasizes that players earn trust through their defensive play, puck handling, positioning, strength, and awareness, noting several key plays that helped produce goals.

Several players have made imaginative, skilled plays during the playoffs through stick work, patience, play recognition, and creativity. One player’s continued progression, hard work, and readiness after injury are viewed as valuable assets with significant upside.

Cover 0 is a man-to-man defense with no safety help over the top. Defensive backs cover receivers individually while linebackers and other defenders apply pressure, often allowing six players to rush. Its simple assignments make adjustments to motion easy and help against the run, run-pass options, short routes, screens, and long passes by reducing the quarterback’s time. Cover 0 can also disguise itself as Cover 4 before the snap.

The coverage is high-risk because beaten receivers have no help, the middle of the field is open, and the defense can be vulnerable to draw plays, quarterback scrambles, and pick plays. It is also called “middle of the field open” coverage.

A typical scheme assigns cornerbacks to cover the X and Z receivers, safeties to cover the tight end and slot receiver, a linebacker to cover the running back, and two linebackers to blitz through the A and B gaps. In a Cover 0 “Rat” variation, five defenders rush while one linebacker remains free in the middle to stop crossing routes and contain a scrambling quarterback. Another variation drops a hybrid defensive lineman into coverage against a running back, allowing him to blitz if the back stays in pass protection.

Alan Jackson's University of Toronto team reports that 'Oumuamua, the first confirmed interstellar object in our solar system, probably came from a binary star system and was ejected as planets formed there. The red, cigar-shaped asteroid, discovered in October by a Hawaiian observatory, is about 1,300 feet long, moving away from Earth and the sun at over 16 miles per second. Scientists now consider it an asteroid, not a comet; it is tumbling, likely from a collision, for billions of years.

The study examines holistic education in Indian higher education, emphasizing the integrated development of mind, matter, and spirit rather than material or intellectual success alone. It relates this approach to the Latin roots of education—*educere* and *educare*—and to the educational philosophies of Tagore, Osho, Swami Vivekananda, and Sri Aurobindo, all of whom integrated spiritual, social, ethical, physical, and intellectual development. It also examines alignment with India’s National Education Policy 2020, UN Sustainable Development Goal 4.7, and the ISEE framework’s emphasis on cognitive and social-emotional development.

The research used a comprehensive literature review followed by a PRISMA-guided systematic review of English-language original articles published before 2021 in Scopus and Semantic Scholar. Eight articles remained after screening. MAXQDA was used for open coding, double coding, and qualitative comparative analysis. The review sought to identify and validate dimensions of holistic education relevant to Indian higher education.

International frameworks showed that holistic education is increasingly reflected in policies and reforms, including Montessori and Waldorf approaches, Finland’s national curriculum, teacher-led initiatives in the United Kingdom, and reforms in Singapore, Taiwan, and New Zealand. Social-emotional learning emerged as a major bridge between academic achievement and broader human development, emphasizing self-awareness, emotional regulation, empathy, relationship-building, and responsible decision-making.

An evaluation of 40 SEL frameworks identified ten with strong conceptual foundations and five designed for broad global use: CASEL, OECD competencies, International Rescue Committee competencies, MELQO’s MODEL framework, and NESET. These frameworks showed balanced coverage of cognitive, emotional, social, and values domains, while identity and perspectives remained underrepresented. The culturally grounded Indian LIBRE/EMC² framework addresses this gap through whole-brain learning and four dimensions: empathy, mindfulness, compassion, and critical inquiry.

The systematic review identified two thematic clusters. The first emphasized the need for holistic education in higher education, including whole-person development, holistic pedagogy, global competence, institutional clarity, lifelong learning, and assessment tools for holistic growth. The second supported all four LIBRE/EMC² dimensions: empathy through cultural awareness, communication, and relationship-building; critical inquiry through analytical thinking, information literacy, interdisciplinary learning, and reflection; mindfulness through self-awareness, emotional regulation, resilience, and spiritual awareness; and compassion through care, social responsibility, integrity, and stewardship.

The findings align the LIBRE/EMC² framework with Indian sages-thinkers’ emphasis on balanced material and spiritual development and with contemporary policies such as NEP 2020 and SDG 4.7. The authors recommend culturally grounded classroom-level assessment as a feedback mechanism for institutional planning, curriculum design, and policy reform. They conclude that identifying the four dimensions supports standardized curricula and future assessment instruments, while noting limitations from using only two databases and excluding the *Holistic Education Review* journal. Future research should broaden database coverage, develop culturally sensitive measurement tools, and examine implementation across diverse educational settings.

Soybean futures closed higher as April physical arrivals declined and soy meal exports sustained crushing demand. Analysts expect higher prices, while adequate supplies and cheap imports may limit gains.

A UMD study of 1,099 college students found that persistent high-caffeine energy drink consumption was associated with greater likelihood of cocaine use, nonmedical prescription stimulant use, and alcohol use disorder risk at age 25. Intermediate consumption also carried elevated risk, while desisting and non-users showed no heightened risk.

Consumer advocates reported intermittent “no plans available” errors on HealthCare.gov during final Obamacare enrollment days, though the administration said the issue was resolved and enrollment remained brisk. The Dec. 15 deadline for 39 federally served states was expected to strain the website and call centers. Hurricane-affected residents could request enrollment extensions until Dec. 31, while state-run marketplaces offered later deadlines, including Jan. 31 in California and New York. Roughly 9 million to 10 million people currently had marketplace coverage, and increased subsidies could offset higher 2018 premiums. Former Obama-era official Andy Slavitt warned that failing to grant unfinished-application extensions would be unfair amid expected last-minute technical problems.

On April 6, 1917, President Woodrow Wilson proclaimed that a state of war existed between the United States and the Imperial German Government. He directed U.S. officers to exercise vigilance and urged citizens to uphold the laws and support the war effort.

Wilson defined “alien enemies” as German males aged fourteen or older who were within the United States and had not been naturalized. They were required to preserve the peace, obey U.S. laws and presidential regulations, refrain from hostility or assistance to U.S. enemies, and conduct themselves peaceably. Law-abiding alien enemies could continue their occupations and receive peaceful treatment, while violators faced restraint, security requirements, removal, or departure.

The regulations prohibited alien enemies from possessing weapons, ammunition, explosives, aircraft, wireless equipment, signaling devices, or cipher materials; approaching specified military and government facilities; publishing threats; committing hostile acts; entering designated prohibited areas; or entering or leaving the United States without authorization. The President could order registration, relocation, or removal and authorized summary arrest and detention of suspected violators. These rules applied throughout U.S. jurisdiction on land and water.

The Nationals’ competition for the fifth starting job includes A.J. Cole, Erick Fedde and newly signed Jeremy Hellickson, and may continue after opening day. Hellickson, 30, received a minor-league contract worth $2 million if added to the 40-man roster, with up to $4 million in bonuses, and was scheduled to pitch Friday in a spring-training split squad. The Nationals may leave him in the minors to build arm strength rather than rush him, as they did with Joe Blanton and Matt Wieters. Max Scherzer was named the opening-day starter, followed by Stephen Strasburg, Gio Gonzalez and Tanner Roark. Cole, who pitched four scoreless innings Sunday, is expected to make the team, while Fedde likely will remain in the minors. Hellickson, who struggled with Baltimore last season, has worked on adjustments to his delivery. Shortstop Trea Turner also left camp to treat an ingrown toenail.

Tesla announced lower-priced Standard versions of the Model Y and Model 3. The $39,990 Model Y Standard has an estimated 321-mile range and is expected in November–December, while the $36,990 Model 3 Standard is expected in December–January. Buyers save $5,000 and $5,500, respectively, compared with rear-wheel-drive Premium versions. The Standard models omit features including Autosteer, LED lightbars, adaptive high beams and FM/AM radio, though the Model Y retains traffic-aware cruise control. Shares fell after the announcement. Eligible New York buyers may receive rebates reducing prices to $37,990 and $34,990, respectively, after the federal $7,500 EV credit ended. The launch followed years of investor demand for an affordable Tesla and Elon Musk’s unfulfilled promise of a $25,000 EV.

VentureWire’s November 14, 2000 issue reported that Apax Partners merged its Israeli and European units and committed $600 million over three years to Israeli telecom, IT, and health-care companies. New Edge Networks eliminated 135 jobs and consolidated offices while seeking profitability and stretching a recent $140 million investment. Consulting firm KSolutions received a $50 million first funding round, while Cisco acquired wireless-chip maker Radiata for $295 million in stock and planned to integrate its products into Cisco’s Aironet line.

In adverse news, four senior executives left Buzz MSP, eSociety ceased operations, and iExplore cut jobs during a restructuring. New product and corporate developments included Venture Studio’s launch of EstimatesOnline, Wapmagic’s renaming to AtoBe, Radix Wireless’s name change, and NetEx’s renaming to Certia. Murphree Venture Partners announced the first close of a fifth fund targeting $150 million to $200 million, while Horizon Ventures and St. Paul Venture Capital added personnel. Advertisements promoted the GroundZero4 B2B e-commerce event and Technology Outlook 2000 conference.

The First Appellate District affirmed John Ortiz’s conviction of simple assault and denial of a new trial. Ortiz followed his wife and Albert Donaso to their San Francisco home, obtained police assistance, then entered through a bedroom window after finding the front door locked. A struggle followed in which Ortiz repeatedly cut Donaso with a pocketknife. Ortiz testified that he acted in self-defense after Donaso approached him with a knife.

The court held that permitting Ortiz to demonstrate how he drew and opened the pocketknife was proper cross-examination of his self-defense claim. It also ruled that evidence concerning alleged threatening letters was collateral, because Ortiz’s use of the knife was undisputed and the issue was whether he acted in self-defense. The court further found no reversible error in the other evidentiary rulings challenged on appeal.

NVIDIA’s Ray Reconstruction (RR) uses AI to add pixels in ray-traced scenes, improving quality and reducing common denoiser artifacts, particularly under challenging lighting. DLSS uses a trained AI network to generate pixels between sampled rays, while DLAA applies related super-resolution technology at native resolution to improve anti-aliasing, temporal stability, and detail in motion.

Blackwell advances programmable and neural shading. The GPU architecture supports developer-created neural shaders, with enhanced Tensor Cores and Shader Execution Reordering allowing neural and traditional graphics workloads to run concurrently. A Cooperative Vectors API developed with Microsoft, combined with Slang features, lets shaders access Tensor Cores and supports neural texture compression and technologies such as RTX Neural Materials, Neural Radiance Cache, RTX Skin, and RTX Neural Faces. The passage traces shader development from fixed-function pipelines through programmable vertex, pixel, geometry, tessellation, compute, mesh, and ray-tracing stages.

RTX Neural Materials approximates complex optical materials with AI, enabling layered film-quality assets at real-time frame rates. RTX Neural Texture Compression uses neural networks to reduce texture storage and bandwidth demands; the cited demo reduced material memory from 1,110 MB to 333 MB. Stochastic Texture Filtering reduces aliasing and moiré patterns and supports higher-order filtering through a single point sample. Neural Radiance Cache infers final lighting after one ray bounce, reducing the need to trace additional bounces while improving indirect-lighting quality and contextual adaptation. RTX Skin applies ray-traced subsurface scattering to translucent materials, while RTX Neural Faces uses a TensorRT-optimized generative model and 3D pose data to produce more natural real-time faces.

The Blackwell GPU family includes GB202, a flagship GPU with 92.2 billion transistors, 24,576 CUDA Cores, 192 RT Cores, and 768 Tensor Cores, used in the GeForce RTX 5090. GB203 has 45.6 billion transistors, 10,752 CUDA Cores, 84 RT Cores, and 336 Tensor Cores, and is used in the RTX 5080 and 5070 Ti. GB205 targets the performance segment with 31 billion transistors, 6,400 CUDA Cores, 50 RT Cores, and 200 Tensor Cores, and is used in the RTX 5070. The passage also states NVIDIA’s specification, warranty, liability, licensing, and trademark terms.

Police arrested Alonzo Carter, 25, on suspicion of murder after his girlfriend, Devanna Cornitcher, was found stabbed in Chester. Her children, 3 and 6, were present. Carter claimed self-defense and was denied bail.

The court held that, under the organic act, only the supreme court possessed appellate jurisdiction; district courts were courts of original jurisdiction and could not exercise appellate or revisory power. An appeal from a justice of the peace therefore allowed the district court to try the case de novo, without regard to the earlier proceedings. The justice’s transcript served only to verify the case’s origin, judgment, and proper appeal, and errors in it did not justify dismissal. In the district court, parties could file accounts, set-offs, and other pleadings as in an original action.

In Archibeque v. Miera, concerning wheat allegedly damaged by Miera’s cattle, the jury considered conflicting testimony about the number of cattle, timing, tracks, and source of the damage. Such discrepancies and credibility questions were for the jury. Because the evidence did not clearly outweigh the jury’s verdict for Miera, the court affirmed the denial of a new trial and the judgment for Miera.

The passage lists Chapter I, covering January 1–March 8, 1945, and related telegrams, radiograms, circulars, and documents from Washington and other locations. It concerns U.S. consultations with the United Kingdom, Soviet Union, China, and France on unresolved Dumbarton Oaks issues and Yalta decisions, consideration of proposals submitted by American Republics, other governments, Congress, and the public, and conference invitations extended to 39 United Nations governments. A January 7 circular describes memoranda from nine American Republics and the Secretary of State’s view that their discussions would support effective participation in developing an enduring international peace structure.

Both teams struggle early when not warmed up, while crowd support and J.S.’s penalty killing have helped. After conceding the first two games, the team plans to improve defense, hold on half a second longer, and use two home games to turn the series around.

The study examined whether sleep quality, anxiety, and brain measures could predict individual depressive symptom severity (DSS) using machine learning. It trained models with nested, family-aware cross-validation in 1,101 HCP-Young participants and validated them in independent HCP-Aging (n=378) and eNKI cohorts (n=334), including 66 eNKI participants with longitudinal data. Sleep quality was measured with the PSQI, anxiety with six ASR items, and DSS with ASR items excluding two sleep-related questions. Structural and functional MRI features were also evaluated.

In HCP-Young, sleep quality predicted DSS (r=0.43, R²=0.18); adding anxiety substantially improved prediction (r=0.67, R²=0.45). Gray-matter volume and resting-state functional brain features did not improve prediction or mediate the sleep–DSS association. Results remained robust after excluding participants with a history of depression and when using PSQI component scores rather than individual items. Reverse prediction of sleep quality from DSS was weaker. Including the two sleep-related DSS items inflated the observed association, with those items accounting for about 62% of sleep–DSS covariance. Anxiety mediated approximately 52.6% of the association between sleep quality and DSS, whereas brain volume did not.

Models trained in HCP-Young generalized to HCP-Aging and eNKI: sleep plus anxiety predicted DSS at r=0.72 and r=0.66, respectively. Longitudinal eNKI models also predicted later DSS from baseline sleep quality (r=0.61) and sleep plus anxiety (r=0.66). Prediction was strong among participants who did not receive neurofeedback between assessments but unsuccessful among those who did. The findings support predictive relationships but do not establish causality; the longitudinal sample was small, and larger longitudinal studies were recommended.

The Base Cross basketball offense uses baseline screens to create post opportunities and exploit defensive mismatches. Point guard O1 typically enters the ball to wing O3 and cuts to the basket; if unopposed, O1 continues to set a baseline screen for post O5. O5 then shoots or posts up, while O1 moves to the weakside wing or pops to the free-throw line. When O3 cannot feed O5, the ball is reversed to O2 for a weakside down screen or post entry. Variations include dribble-clear, UCLA high-post, and Hawk entries.

Successful execution depends on precise screening and coordinated reads. Counteroptions address defenders who trail the screener, play low or high on the post, switch, anticipate a screen, show and recover, or front the post. Options include give-and-go layups, going over or under screens, screening and popping mismatches, slipping to the basket, post lob passes, and reversing the ball.

Strong posting requires sound low-post techniques, awareness of defensive positioning, court spacing, and options for solo cuts, two-person play, and post splits. Ball-reversal sets can incorporate down, mid, and side screens, with back cuts available when the reversal pass is denied.

Teaching the offense requires mastering its components through whole-part-whole instruction, targeted motor-skill drills, two- and three-player combinations, scrimmages, and individual practice. Coaches should scout opponents, anticipate defensive reads, vary alignments and entries, identify weaker defenders, and remain alert to defensive changes. The offense is also widely used to isolate low-post players, making defensive preparation against it important.

The passage criticizes the Carter administration’s policies in Iran and Nicaragua, arguing that it helped replace moderate, American-friendly autocrats with extremist leaders unwilling to share power or establish constitutional governments. It calls for a realistic U.S. policy toward nondemocratic governments threatened by Soviet-sponsored subversion. Kirkpatrick contends that Carter, Vance, and Brzezinski favored “leftist” challenges and were willing to destabilize friendly or neutral autocracies without ensuring that replacements would not be repressive totalitarian regimes. She concludes that Carter’s foreign policy reflected ideological fashion rather than realism about traditional and revolutionary autocracies. Traditional authoritarian regimes, though unequal and brutal, generally preserve existing social structures and are more susceptible to liberalization and compatible with U.S. interests than revolutionary regimes. Examples from Vietnam, Cambodia, China, and Korea support her view that revolutionary governments can be more repressive, though she acknowledges that exceptionally brutal rulers can emerge under either system.

Des Moines Public Schools Superintendent Ian Roberts resigned effective immediately, his lawyers said, after ICE detained him and the Iowa Board of Educational Examiners revoked his license. ICE said Roberts, who entered the U.S. in 1999 on a student visa, was in the country unlawfully and had a final removal order. His attorney is seeking to reopen his immigration case and a stay in Omaha federal immigration court. Roberts is being held at Woodbury County Jail.

DMPS said Roberts completed required I-9 employment verification when hired, while the National School Board Coalition said a background-check contractor did not verify legal work eligibility. The school board sought citizenship documentation before considering ending his contract. Rep. Zach Nunn said Roberts was unauthorized to lead the district and called for stronger vetting and accountability.

U.S. markets ended the week decisively risk-off, with major indexes falling 2.2%–4.2%, forming bearish engulfing patterns, and nearly all sectors except utilities declining. Despite strong Q2 2025 earnings—82% of reporting S&P 500 companies beat EPS estimates and 79% beat revenue estimates, with upward revisions rising—economic and policy uncertainty prompted selling.

GDP exceeded expectations at 3% versus 2.5%, but tariff-related import volatility distorted the data and personal spending was weak. Nonfarm payrolls rose only 73,000 versus 100,000 expected, with unusually large downward revisions, while a shrinking labor force partly offset slower job creation. The FOMC recorded two dissents for the first time since the 1990s. Powell emphasized data dependence amid tariff and immigration uncertainty, while markets priced above 75% odds of a September rate cut and three cuts by January.

Political developments included President Trump firing the Bureau of Labor Statistics commissioner after the payroll report, new tariff announcements, military moves toward Russia, and Fed Governor Adriana Kugler’s early resignation. Market breadth turned negative, regional banks and transports weakened, commodities entered a bear phase, and utilities and Treasuries strengthened as volatility surged. The analysis favors tactical positioning and downside-risk management while noting that improving earnings expectations and projected 2026 growth remain constructive longer term.

Police arrested a suspect after a two-hour Kansas-Missouri chase. His vehicle, disabled by a spike strip, veered into a ditch. Officers found drugs, loaded weapons, and suspected meth ingestion; he was hospitalized.

The NHS Patient Charter, also known as the NHS Constitution, combines patients’ legal rights, NHS commitments and patients’ responsibilities. It guarantees access to care free at the point of use, subject to exceptions, alongside fair treatment, waiting-time standards and alternatives when standards are not met. Patients are entitled to safe care from qualified staff, recommended medicines and vaccinations, privacy, informed consent, involvement in treatment decisions, choice of GP, and openness about errors. Local funding decisions should be evidence-based and explained. Patients may complain, seek Ombudsman intervention or judicial review, and claim compensation for negligence caused harm. NHS organisations must continually improve care and consider community health needs. In return, patients should look after their health, respect staff and others, follow treatment plans, attend appointments, and participate in vaccination and screening. The Charter presents the NHS as a partnership built on fairness, trust and shared responsibility.

A study found that perceived treatment price can amplify nocebo effects. Volunteers given fake creams presented as expensive reported greater heat-induced pain than those given generic-looking creams: pain increased by nearly 30% versus about 3% relative to an inactive control. Brain imaging showed differences in the prefrontal cortex and periaqueductal gray, regions involved in pain pathways and placebo effects. The findings may help clinicians minimize nocebo effects when discussing medications.

NVIDIA Corporation filed its fiscal 2018 Form 10-K for the year ended January 28, 2018. The Delaware corporation is headquartered in Santa Clara, California, and its common stock trades on the NASDAQ Global Select Market under “NVDA.” It was classified as a large accelerated filer, had approximately 605 million shares outstanding on February 26, 2018, and reported a non-affiliate shareholding market value of approximately $94.31 billion as of July 28, 2017.

NVIDIA states that it invented the GPU in 1999 and introduced the CUDA programming model in 2006. It has invested more than $15 billion in research and development since inception. Its unified GPU and CUDA architecture supports visual computing and accelerated computing across four principal markets: Gaming, Professional Visualization, Datacenter, and Automotive. The company reports two segments, GPU and Tegra Processor. GPU products include GeForce, GeForce NOW, Quadro, Tesla, GRID, DGX, and cryptocurrency-specific GPUs; Tegra products include DRIVE, SHIELD, and Jetson TX 2.

In gaming, NVIDIA provides GPUs, gaming software, cloud gaming, and VR development tools. GeForce Experience had been downloaded by more than 90 million users. Its professional visualization products support computer-aided design, video editing, visual effects, and other design workflows, including the new Holodeck VR environment. Its datacenter platform combines GPUs, CUDA, libraries such as cuDNN and TensorRT, and NVLink for AI and high-performance computing. NVIDIA says GPUs can accelerate applications 10–75 times versus CPUs and sped deep-neural-network training by as much as 12 times. Its automotive business supplies infotainment, driver-assistance, and autonomous-driving systems under the DRIVE brand; more than 320 automakers, suppliers, research institutions, mapping companies, and startups were working with NVIDIA.

Business strategies include advancing GPU computing, extending leadership in AI and visual computing, developing an end-to-end autonomous-vehicle platform, and leveraging intellectual property through licensing and custom development. Sales are conducted through industry partners, direct channels, cloud providers, enterprise customers, and e-tail channels. NVIDIA uses a fabless manufacturing model, relying on foundries such as TSMC and Samsung and independent subcontractors for wafer fabrication, assembly, testing, and packaging. Consumer products generally generate stronger revenue in the second half of the fiscal year. Cash and marketable securities increased 5% to $7.11 billion at fiscal year-end. R&D expense was $1.80 billion in 2018, compared with $1.46 billion in 2017 and $1.33 billion in 2016.

As of January 28, 2018, NVIDIA had 11,528 employees, including 8,191 in R&D and 3,337 in sales, marketing, operations, and administration. It competes with companies including AMD, Intel, ARM, Qualcomm, Broadcom, Samsung, and Texas Instruments. Its intellectual property is protected through patents, trademarks, trade secrets, nondisclosure agreements, and licensing arrangements; issued patents expire between April 2018 and January 2037.

The report identifies material risks from changing market requirements, intensifying competition, cybersecurity and privacy incidents, product defects or recalls, reliance on third-party manufacturers, supply constraints, business and geopolitical disruptions, inaccurate demand forecasts, international operations, employee retention, acquisitions, intellectual-property litigation, taxes, regulatory proceedings, and anti-takeover provisions. Sales outside the United States and Other Americas represented 79% of fiscal 2018 revenue, and approximately 47% of employees were located outside the United States. Risks include potential GDPR penalties of up to 4% of worldwide revenue, inventory write-downs or shortages, supply delays, and the possibility that actual results will differ materially from forward-looking statements.

NVIDIA’s Santa Clara headquarters complex includes ten leased commercial buildings totaling 963,317 square feet and seven owned commercial buildings totaling 1,496,006 square feet on 36 acres. The company also maintains leased and owned research, sales, administrative, and datacenter facilities in the United States and internationally. Its executive officers as of February 26, 2018 were Jen-Hsun Huang, President, Chief Executive Officer and Director; Colette M. Kress, Chief Financial Officer; Ajay K. Puri, Executive Vice President, Worldwide Field Operations; Debora Shoquist, Executive Vice President, Operations; and Timothy S. Teter, Executive Vice President, General Counsel and Secretary.

The quarterly cash dividend was increased in November 2017 from $0.14 to $0.15 per share. NVIDIA paid $341 million in cash dividends in fiscal 2018 and $261 million in fiscal 2017. Since the repurchase program began, it had acquired 251 million shares for $5.5 billion through January 28, 2018, with $1.82 billion of remaining authorization through December 2020. For fiscal 2019, the company intended to return $1.25 billion through dividends and repurchases. During fiscal 2018, conversions of $812 million principal amount of convertible notes resulted in issuance of 33 million shares, partly offset through note hedges, and restricted-stock-unit tax withholding involved approximately 4 million shares costing $612 million.

Goal-side defending requires defenders to position themselves between the goal and their opponents, keeping opponents in front. Youth should learn to move toward forwards, stop before reaching them, and recognize their position relative to the goal. Defenders behind opponents must sprint beyond them and turn around. Instruction should cover right, center, and left positioning, adjustment to opponent movement, quick glances toward the goal, and use of penalty-area markings. Drills progress from slow movement without a ball to ball work and increased speed, while prohibiting blocking opponents or extending their arms.

The Alabama Court of Civil Appeals denied James F. Robertson III’s mandamus petition seeking a default judgment in his divorce against Cynthia D. Robertson. Although Robertson attempted service by publication, the trial court record did not establish that the publisher’s affidavit and notice required by Rule 4.3(d)(5) had been filed. The trial court therefore denied his default-judgment motion and his request for reconsideration. Because Robertson had not established a clear legal right to the requested order, the court denied mandamus. All judges concurred.

In an appeal concerning imported fishing equipment, the importer conceded that 50 yen and 4 yen in outside packing charges were dutiable. With no evidence proving a 26.557-yen invoice deduction improper, the court found appraised values less specified charges, including that deduction.

Indian markets rebounded Tuesday: the Sensex rose 270 points to 29,683.87, while Nifty reached 9,214.15. Metal, energy, FMCG and banking shares gained; TCS was flat. Asian indexes fell, and the rupee strengthened to 64.40 per dollar.

Pacific Gamble Robinson Co. sought to enforce a $34,710.70 promissory note executed in Colorado in 1977 by Conrad Lapp individually and for Joslyn Fruit Co., which Lapp solely owned. Mrs. Lapp did not sign. After the note went into default, the Lapps moved to Washington, and Pacific Gamble sued Lapp, Joslyn, and the marital community. The trial court and Court of Appeals held that only Lapp individually was liable; the Washington Supreme Court reversed.

Applying the “most significant relationship” conflicts rule, the majority held that Colorado law governed because the note was negotiated, signed, and expected to be performed in Colorado, the Lapps were Colorado domiciliaries, and Colorado’s interests and the parties’ expectations outweighed Washington’s. Under Colorado law, all of Lapp’s property, including later-acquired assets and earnings, was subject to the debt except Mrs. Lapp’s separate property and earnings. The community claim therefore could proceed despite Washington’s characterization of those assets.

Justice Horowitz, joined by Chief Justice Utter, dissented, arguing that Washington law should govern which marital assets could satisfy the judgment because Washington had the stronger interest in protecting community property from a noncommunity debt.

WMCC vocational students built cabinets and countertops for Kidder United Methodist Church’s kitchen as part of a partnership with the city and Caldwell County Emergency Management to establish a disaster relief center. The church paid for materials, while the prison provided labor. The project offers students real-world experience and benefits the community once the kitchen meets required specifications.

The passage defines cryptocurrency trading as buying and selling digital assets such as Bitcoin and Ethereum for profit or speculation. It surveys 20 strategies, including day, swing, trend-following, range, breakout, mean-reversion, arbitrage, grid, fork, whale-watching, dark-pool, sentiment, technical-analysis, Proof of Stake, quantum, Ichimoku, NFT, zombie-coin, and Genesis-block trading. Strategy selection should match investors’ goals and risk tolerance, and backtesting is recommended because crypto differs from stocks and historical data is limited.

A Bitcoin backtest from late 2014 reported 135 trades, a 42% win rate, 7% average gain, and 87% annual return while invested 56% of the time, alongside a 66% drawdown. Trend-following performed better than mean-reversion in the study.

Prices are affected by demand, sentiment, regulation, technology, and macroeconomic events. Risks include volatility, scams, cybercrime, exchange insolvency, blockchain complexity, lost private keys, and limited regulation. Halvings reduce mining rewards and new supply, potentially increasing scarcity and prices. Hard forks can create new coins while increasing volatility and uncertainty. DeFi may reduce intermediary costs, while USDT supports liquidity and hedging but could hurt the broader market if depegged. Trading fees vary, and day trading can be profitable but requires skill, strategy, and disciplined risk management.

The professor recaps the course’s progression from business planning, value creation and capture, and the “three whys” to pitching, customer discovery, business models, and iterative financial projections. The session then introduces financing as the next resource entrepreneurs must plan for.

Panelists present their backgrounds: Axel Bichara, a former Atlas Venture partner, discusses angel investing, crowdfunding, and Bolt, a hands-on hardware accelerator; Julianne Zimmerman, a former clean-tech entrepreneur and founder of seed fund Vodia Ventures, discusses capital costs and investor fit; and Amir Nashat, managing partner at Polaris, discusses traditional venture investing and MIT-derived companies.

The panel emphasizes that every financing source has a different use, cost, and appropriate stage. Entrepreneurs should determine how much capital they need, whether dilution or debt is appropriate, and whether investors share their definition of success. They should carefully select investors, conduct reference checks, evaluate their track records and incentives, and seek alignment with the company’s team, market, goals, and stage. Strong introductions and early networking are presented as important ways to reach investors and obtain useful feedback.

The discussion covers incubators, accelerators, angel and venture funding, crowdfunding, grants, customer revenue, convertible notes, and strategic investment. Bolt’s default arrangement—$50,000 for 10% in exchange for six to nine months of intensive company building—is described as primarily valuable for the hands-on support rather than the cash. Convertible notes are characterized as fast, inexpensive interim debt that may convert into equity, but may give creditors substantial power if a company fails. Equity is generally presented as offering stronger alignment.

The panelists warn against excessive capital, unrealistic market assumptions, unsuitable strategic investors, and rounds in which many small angel investors can block future decisions. Large funding rounds can pressure companies to pursue rapid growth that may not suit their plans. Strategic investors may prioritize particular assets or organizational interests, while professional investors can provide more consistent support and help negotiate terms.

Additional discussion addresses social-impact businesses, the transition from scientific questions to commercially repeatable products, and methods for finding funding through direct contact, referrals, or cold submissions. The panel closes by advising entrepreneurs to identify their largest risks early, address them with the least capital, use experienced advisers or board members, avoid dependence on a single unsuitable partner, and understand whether major partners will remain useful as the company grows.

The St. Louis Court of Appeals affirmed the circuit court judgment based on the same facts and principles established in the earlier Century Realty Co. v. Frankfort Marine, Accident and Plate Glass Insurance Company decision.

Simulation-based inference can produce biased or overconfident posteriors when simulator and real-data likelihoods differ. The paper proposes Flow Matching for Corrected Posterior Estimation (FMCPE), which combines abundant low-fidelity simulations with a small set of high-fidelity calibration pairs. An NPE model first estimates the simulator-based posterior. Two jointly trained flow-matching stages then transport real observations into simulator space and refine reweighted posterior samples toward the true posterior. This approach does not require an explicit misspecification model or conditional-independence assumption and can refine existing SBI posterior estimators. Across two synthetic and two real-world tasks, FMCPE generally outperformed NPE and MFNPE in Wasserstein distance, joint classifier two-sample test, and mean squared error, particularly with small calibration sets. Performance improved as calibration data increased, though severe misspecification in high dimensions may require more calibration data.

The Physical Layer Simplified Specification Version 6.00 defines SD memory-card capacities, physical characteristics, electrical signaling, bus modes, commands, initialization, data transfer, erase operations, and protection mechanisms. Part A1 extends the SD physical layer to transfer Mobile Commerce Extension (Mc-EX) command packets from a host to Mc-EX-enabled cards; SDIO and embedded SDIO are defined through the Part E1 specification.

Cards are classified as SDSC (up to 2 GB), SDHC (over 2 GB through 32 GB), or SDXC (over 32 GB through 2 TB). Hosts supporting higher-capacity cards must also support lower-capacity cards. Read/write cards use Flash, OTP, or MTP memory, while ROM cards contain fixed data and reject write and erase commands. Supported form factors include standard-size, miniSD, and microSD; standard cards measure 24 × 32 mm and are 2.1 mm or 1.4 mm thick. High-voltage cards operate at 2.7–3.6 V, while UHS-II cards also specify VDD2 at 1.70–1.95 V.

Bus modes include Default Speed, High Speed, SDR12, SDR25, SDR50, SDR104, DDR50, UHS156, and UHS624. UHS-I uses a four-bit bus and can reach 104 MB/s; UHS-II adds FD156, HD312, FD312, and FD624 modes, with FD624 newly introduced in Version 6.00. Speed classes specify minimum write performance, while application performance classes define random and sequential minimums. Cache, self-maintenance, command queue, and low-voltage interface features are also described.

The host controls all communications. Serial commands, responses, and block data use CRC protection, and cards are addressed through relative card addresses assigned during initialization. Identification generally proceeds with CMD0, CMD8 voltage verification, ACMD41 operating-condition and capacity negotiation, CMD2 for the CID, and CMD3 for the RCA. CMD7 selects a card for data transfer. UHS-I initialization uses CMD11 for the 1.8 V signaling switch and may use CMD19 for timing tuning. UHS-II initialization includes PHY, device, enumeration, configuration, and SD-TRAN initialization.

Data transfer supports single- and multiple-block reads and writes, one- or four-bit buses, CRC-checked blocks, buffering, and busy signaling through DAT0. Misaligned or invalid accesses produce address or block-length errors, and reads or writes may be stopped with CMD12. ACMD23 can pre-erase blocks before a multiple-block write, and ACMD22 reports successfully written blocks. Erase sequences use CMD32, CMD33, and CMD38; DISCARD makes discarded contents indeterminate, while FULE logically erases the complete user area and is limited to SDHC and SDXC cards.

Protection is provided through a mechanical write-protect switch, optional internal write protection, and password locking. Password data is stored in nonvolatile PWD and PWD_LEN registers, with optional FEP and FEP_LEN registers. Card Ownership Protection (COP) adds COP Unlock, force-erase, FEP-management, and password-reset controls, requiring FEP-protected cards to be unlocked after reset before other CMD42 functions can be used.

Headlines cover the 2018 South Carolina governor’s race, $200,000 sought for constitution restoration, a $38 million Cooper River office sale, Charleston cardiac-care testing, Mayor Tecklenburg’s first year, and new state laws.
Apple offers free battery replacements for eligible 13-inch MacBook Pro models without Touch Bar built between October 2016 and October 2017, with an online serial-number eligibility check.

Researchers studied 173 women aged 25–50 who drank under a litre of water daily, concluding that adding half a litre to breakfast promoted weight and fat loss. The passage cites research that drinking half a litre burns 23 extra calories, equivalent to 2 kg of fat annually. It notes that high-protein, low-carb diets may aid weight loss but may not be the best approach.

Central-power brutality in Belgium and submarine warfare were intended to defeat enemies and intimidate neutrals; Germany and Austria made the war inevitable and gained early victories by violating rights and treaty guarantees. A peace based on such terrorism would discredit treaties, international law, and efforts to prevent disputes. Although sharing the President’s desire for peace, the author argues that durable peace requires Allied success. It depends on reducing international unrest, bringing the Central powers’ aggressive aims and unscrupulous methods into disrepute, and devising international sanctions behind law and treaties to deter aggressors. Sacrifices of blood and treasure are defended to secure Allied victory, peaceful civilization, and international reform. Greece accepted the ultimatum without reservation; immediate release of political prisoners and Entente control of internal administration remained the main difficulties, with reservist danger considered unlikely. Persia endorsed the President’s December 18, 1916 note and sought U.S. assistance at a future peace conference to maintain Persia’s integrity and rights.

DS-STAR is a multi-agent LLM framework for autonomously generating Python solutions to data science queries across heterogeneous file formats, including structured and unstructured data. It first uses an analyzer agent to parse each input file and generate a description of its structure and content. Its solution process then iteratively plans, codes, executes, and verifies each step. A planner generates executable steps, a coder implements them, and an LLM-based verifier judges whether the cumulative plan, code, and execution results sufficiently address the query. If not, a router either appends a step or truncates the plan at an erroneous step for regeneration. Separate debugging agents use tracebacks and file descriptions to repair scripts, while an embedding-based retriever selects relevant files when descriptions exceed the context window.

Experiments on DABStep, KramaBench, and DA-Code show DS-STAR outperforming prior methods. With Gemini-2.5-Pro, it achieves 87.50% easy-task and 45.24% hard-task accuracy on DABStep, 44.69% on KramaBench, and 38.5% on DA-Code. Ablations show that removing file analysis or plan routing reduces performance, particularly on difficult tasks. Hard DABStep tasks require an average of 5.6 refinement rounds, compared with 3.0 for easy tasks, and accuracy generally rises when the iteration limit is increased from 5 to 20. The authors identify human-in-the-loop collaboration as a direction for future work.

The Yankees and Red Sox will play a best-of-three 2025 AL Wild Card series in New York starting Sept. 30. ESPN will televise the games, with Karl Ravech, David Cone and Eduardo Perez calling and Buster Olney reporting. New York is the No. 4 seed and Boston the No. 5; Boston leads the previous five postseason matchups 3–2.

“Sell the rip” is a short-term trading strategy that sells an asset—either by closing a long position or opening a short position—when its price appears overvalued or overbought. It reflects “buy low, sell high,” using mean reversion to anticipate a correction toward the asset’s average price. The approach is most suitable for short-selling overpriced stocks with weak fundamentals and is generally unsuitable for long-term investing in companies with strong fundamentals and growth potential.

The strategy uses oscillating and momentum indicators, including RSI, Stochastic, Williams %R, IBS, Bollinger Bands, and moving averages, to identify overbought conditions and price means. Careful research, backtesting, and sound exit and stop-management rules are important because short positions carry potentially unlimited risk.

An RSI-based SPY backtest from 1993 recorded 391 trades, a 0.61% average gain, a 75% win rate, and a 1.6 profit factor, but the authors considered it untradable because of large, prolonged drawdowns. Revising the exit criteria improved the equity curve, reduced drawdowns, shortened holding periods, increased trade frequency, and lowered the average gain per trade to 0.48%. The authors note that the approach has historically worked well in the S&P 500, but trend-following commodity markets can cause premature selling.

At this year's Scripps National Spelling Bee, expanded by a new wild-card program, associate pronouncer the Rev. Brian Sietsema covered two of five groups on Wednesday so pronouncer Jacques Bailly could rest his voice over three days. Sietsema, a Greek Orthodox priest from Lansing, Michigan, formerly a linguistics professor and Merriam-Webster pronunciation editor, enjoys working with young spellers. More than 500 spellers competed in preliminary rounds, nearly 200 misspelled onstage, and 41 semifinalists advanced via a written test; director Paige Kimble said, "We thought it was an easy test. We were wrong." Top scorer Shruthika Padhy, 12, finished seventh last year. Rebekah Zeigler, 13, met her goal by spelling "yarrow"; Reagan Remmers was reinstated after spelling "Balaklava," a Ukrainian city, instead of "balaclava," the fifth such reinstatement in 20 years; Daniel Doudna, 14, of Fairbanks, Alaska, spells letter by letter.

Generative AI has accelerated calls for personalized learning, but schools’ prescribed curricula restrict students’ control over what, how, when, and with whom they learn. The article uses an ecological framework drawn from panarchy theory to argue that education must become more transformative while retaining needed societal functions.

Curriculum is presented as the anchor of modern education: it translates societal and governmental priorities into teaching, assessment, teacher preparation, organization, and student pathways. Since the Prussian education model, curriculum prescription, standardized testing, and tiered selection have strengthened over two centuries, student autonomy has become minimal. The resulting mismatch is especially serious in the AI era, when knowledge and information are widely accessible but schools continue excluding non-prescribed learning.

The article proposes a balanced curriculum in which part of school time remains system-controlled and part is allocated to student-directed learning. The balance would vary with students’ age, experience, ability, and support, and autonomy would involve guidance from teachers, leaders, parents, and peers rather than unrestricted freedom. Curriculum reform would also require teachers to become coaches, counselors, and supporters, while schools revise timetables, class organization, facilities, and assessments.

Panarchy theory explains education as a nested, multi-level system in which changes can move across scales. Its adaptive cycle—growth, conservation, release, and reorganization—describes how educational innovations develop, become standardized and rigid, encounter crisis, and are restructured. Education’s resilience has generally allowed it to absorb technologies with limited disruption; stakeholder adaptations often reinforce existing structures; and insufficient transformability poses risks as traditional curricula become less relevant.

Innovations are categorized as tiny, small, large, and transformational. The first three generally remain within or strengthen the existing system, while transformational innovations fundamentally increase student autonomy but have often been confined to private or special schools. The authors advocate beginning with autonomous school-within-school subsystems that use personalized, problem-oriented learning, AI as a learning partner, and teachers as facilitators. Successful subsystems could influence and gradually transform higher levels of the education system.

Examples include Hongfan Middle School’s Innovation, Creativity, and Entrepreneurship Education program in Chongqing, which expanded from two student cohorts to six and spread into related high-school programs, and Australian initiatives including the Studio School and ScotsX. These efforts illustrate the proposed strategy of testing transformative education in protected subsystems before wider adoption. The authors caution that not every subsystem may survive, but argue that giving such ideas opportunities to survive and be publicly tested could support eventual system-wide transformation.

The passage lists major American foreign-policy statements from 1945, with publication citations in the Department of State Bulletin and the Public Papers of the Presidents. Topics include Roosevelt’s State of the Union address, Yalta Conference report, and statements concerning the UN Charter. After Roosevelt’s death, Truman addressed Congress, the San Francisco Conference, Germany’s surrender, the war with Japan, defense aid, ratification of the UN Charter, the atomic bombing of Hiroshima, the Potsdam Conference, Japan’s surrender, and atomic energy. It also includes Stettinius’s statements on world organization, economic peace, and the San Francisco Conference; Cordell Hull’s UN statement; and Byrnes’s addresses on the Council of Foreign Ministers, U.S. foreign policy, world cooperation, neighboring nations, and American policy in China, including Byrnes’s response to Patrick J. Hurley’s charges.

The coach credited his team’s depth, particularly Yannick Weber and Matt Irwin, noting that four top players handling heavy minutes helped against opponents with two elite centers. Their availability helped the team reach the playoffs. He described continual learning from players and coaches, effective playoff preparation and the work of the entire organization. He said the team earned its position through difficult times and was fortunate to be playing hockey in June, with both teams hungry and ready to compete for the Cup.

The ADS868xW supports four legacy SPI-compatible protocols: SPI-00-S, SPI-01-S, SPI-10-S, and SPI-11-S. SPI-00-S is the default after power-up or asynchronous reset. The SDI_MODE[1:0] bits select the protocol, with the initial selection write using SPI-00-S and subsequent frames using the selected protocol. A valid write requires at least 32 SCLK cycles per data-transfer frame.

Data reads support single or dual SDO-x SPI modes and source-synchronous (SRC) operation. For SPI reads, SDO_MODE[1:0] must be set to 00b; dual-SDO operation requires SDO1_CONFIG[1:0] = 11b. SRC mode provides a synchronous output clock on RVS, supports internal or external clock sources, and offers single- or dual-bit output.

The configuration registers provide device identification for daisy-chain systems, reset and low-power controls, SPI input and output protocol selection, output-data formatting and parity, reference and input-range selection, alarm status, and programmable alarm thresholds and hysteresis. Writes to RST_PWRCTL_REG require the protection key 69h at address 05h.

The ADS868xW is a fully differential, 16-bit SAR ADC data-acquisition device with an integrated analog front end, buffered precision reference, programmable gain amplifier, input and AVDD alarms, and overvoltage protection. A reference design combines an ADS8681W with an MUX36D08 differential multiplexer to provide eight software-configurable voltage or current channels for industrial PLC, DCS, or DAQ systems. The ADS8681W settles to 1% accuracy in under 5 µs and has input bandwidth up to 400 kHz at −3 dB.

The input alarm supports user-programmable low and high thresholds and hysteresis, including NTC-thermistor temperature sensing applications. Hysteresis helps prevent noise-induced false alarms near threshold values.

The device uses independent AVDD and DVDD supplies and requires close decoupling to improve power-supply rejection. Programmable NAP and power-down modes reduce consumption at lower throughput. In NAP mode, holding CONVST/CS high after conversion keeps the device in NAP; a falling edge wakes it, followed by the specified wake-up delay. Power-down is entered on a CONVST/CS rising edge, powers down analog blocks while retaining the interface and registers, and requires the specified power-up delay before a new conversion.

Recommended PCB layout separates analog and digital sections, keeps analog routing away from digital signals, places bypass and reference capacitors close to their pins, avoids vias between supply pins and capacitors, and connects grounds through short, low-impedance paths. Additional sections address documentation updates, TI support resources, trademarks, electrostatic-discharge precautions, revision history, and mechanical, packaging, and orderable information.

On August 28, 2017, Amazon.com, Inc. completed its acquisition of Whole Foods Market, Inc. under a June 15, 2017 merger agreement. Amazon’s wholly owned subsidiary Walnut Merger Sub, Inc. merged into Whole Foods Market, which survived as a wholly owned Amazon subsidiary. Each eligible Whole Foods share converted into the right to receive $42 in cash. Options and stock appreciation rights were cashed out based on the $42 value, while restricted stock awards and units received $42 per covered share. Total merger consideration was approximately $13.55 billion, financed with net proceeds from previously disclosed debt financing. Amazon planned to file Whole Foods Market’s required financial statements and pro forma financial information in amendments to its Form 8-K.

The Martingale trading strategy doubles a trader’s position after each loss, aiming for a market reversal that recovers prior losses and produces a profit equal to the initial stake. Originally developed for gambling on even-probability outcomes and associated with French mathematician Paul Pierre Levy in the 18th century, it relies on mean reversion. Theoretically, one win can offset all preceding losses if capital is unlimited, but inadequate funds, prolonged losing streaks, and growing exposure create substantial risk of ruin or severe drawdowns.

In stock trading, the strategy is especially dangerous because shares can fall to zero, making even unlimited capital insufficient. It may be less risky when used long-only in broad-market index ETFs, and positive carry can reduce losses in some currency trades. The strategy is distinct from double-down trading, which adds the original position size after a loss, and from averaging down, where additional purchases follow a predetermined investment plan.

A cited SPY backtest benchmark recorded 409 trades, an average gain of 0.64% per trade, annual returns of 8.68%, and a 23% maximum drawdown.
