Knees undergo wear and tear with age, and injury can cause pain, impaired mobility and, in severe cases, surgery. Healthy weight, regular activity, strengthening the muscles around the knees and throughout the body, and maintaining flexibility can reduce the risk of joint, cartilage and ligament damage. Recommended exercises target the hamstrings, quads, glutes and hip flexors, with resistance gradually increased. Stretching improves range of motion and balance, while cycling, swimming and other low-impact cardio support circulation and cartilage without forceful impact. Exercise adds stress to the knees, and higher body weight increases joint force and injury risk.

Persistent pain or injury should be assessed by a physiotherapist, who can provide a tailored programme of strengthening and flexibility exercises. These may restore movement, reduce recurrence and help delay or avoid surgery. Staying active is important, but continuing a routine that aggravates knee pain should not be ignored.

If a knee is too worn, damaged or injured to rehabilitate with physiotherapy alone, surgery can improve quality of life. It carries risks including infection and deep vein thrombosis. Most knee replacements last for years; according to Dr Sarah Jarvis, more than four in five total replacements and seven in ten unicondylar replacements last 25 years. Physiotherapy and regular recommended exercises after surgery can speed recovery and protect the replacement.

This medRxiv preprint (Rouse et al., posted 2 January 2025; not peer reviewed) examined behavioural change in frontotemporal dementia (FTD), specifically whether behavioural profiles in behavioural-variant FTD (bvFTD) and semantic dementia (SD) differ qualitatively or quantitatively, and what the prefrontal cortex and anterior temporal lobes (ATL) contribute to social behaviour, informed by the authors' controlled social-semantic cognition (CS-SC) model and a transdiagnostic approach.

Forty-seven patients with clinical FTD (26 bvFTD, 21 SD including 18 L>R and 3 R>L ATL atrophy patterns) were recruited from specialist clinics in Cambridge, London and Oxford, alongside 18 age-matched healthy controls; a subset underwent 3T structural MRI. Participants completed informant questionnaires (Cambridge Behavioural Inventory-Revised, Apathy-Motivation Index-Caregiver version, Cambridge Questionnaire for Apathy and Impulsivity Traits), the self-report AMI in controls and a subset of patients, a neuropsychological battery assessing social and non-social semantic comprehension, semantic memory, global cognition and executive function, and voxel-based morphometry. Principal component analyses yielded three behavioural dimensions (apathy, challenging behaviours, activities of daily living) and three neuropsychological components (FTD severity, semantic memory, executive function).

Both FTD groups scored higher than controls on nearly all questionnaire domains, with bvFTD exceeding SD on everyday skills, self-care, abnormal behaviour, eating, sleep, motivation and apathy measures but not on mood, beliefs, stereotypic behaviour, memory/orientation or social motivation. Over 50% of each CBI-R domain was impaired in bvFTD; 25 of 45 item-level comparisons were significant, all favouring bvFTD, with no behavioural double dissociations. bvFTD scored higher on apathy and challenging behaviours but not on activities of daily living. Self-reported apathy did not differ from controls, and self–informant agreement was poor in bvFTD but partial in SD. Morphometry confirmed prefrontal-predominant atrophy in bvFTD and bilateral ATL-predominant atrophy in SD, with SD showing greater ATL loss than bvFTD.

Discrimination between bvFTD and SD was better achieved by semantic memory (AUC 84.1%) and executive function (78.8%) than by behavioural measures, with combined neuropsychology reaching AUC 95.1% versus 83.1% for combined behavioural components. Apathy was associated with poorer executive function (specifically Brixton Spatial Anticipation performance) and, when controlling for global atrophy, reduced grey matter in the dorsal anterior cingulate cortex, supplementary motor area and precuneus; activities of daily living related to medial prefrontal, precentral and left insular atrophy, while challenging behaviours showed no significant associations. No link between social-semantic knowledge and behaviour change was found.

The authors conclude that behavioural differences between bvFTD and SD are quantitative rather than qualitative (bvFTD>SD), recommend neuropsychological semantic memory and executive function measures as the preferred discriminators, and suggest preserved semantic memory as a criterion for bvFTD. Apathy appears tied to anterior cingulate/prefrontal "social control" dysfunction in both syndromes, and no behaviour specific to R>L atrophy was found, supporting a unitary-yet-graded conception of SD rather than a distinct "right temporal variant FTD". Limitations include reliance on informants, incomplete sampling of behaviours (anosognosia, empathy loss, reward behaviours), cross-sectional design with patients on average six years post-onset, and the need for longitudinal, more comprehensive and culturally diverse studies.

Actors Daisy McCrackin and Joseph Capone were held for ransom for nearly three days by a methamphetamine-fuelled gang that police allege pistol-whipped Capone, stripped and confined him in a bathtub without food for 30 hours, and forced McCrackin to withdraw at least $10,000 for his release. Three suspects—Keith Andre Stewart, Johntae Jones and Amber Neal—were arrested in Los Angeles and charged with 17 counts including kidnapping, assault with a firearm, grand theft, mayhem, conspiracy and possession of methamphetamine for sale. A December 31, 2000 email contains the year-end *Wall Street Week with Louis Rukeyser* transcript and 2001 panel forecasts.

The program reviews a difficult 2000 for stocks: the Dow closed at 10,787.99, down just over 6% and marking its first losing year since 1990; the S&P 500 lost slightly more than 10%; and the Nasdaq fell nearly 40%, its worst year on record. The Russell 2000 declined 4.2%, while the New York and American Stock Exchange composites posted small gains. The dollar was the strongest major currency, gaining 12% against the yen. Economic growth slowed, inflation reached 3.4%, unemployment was about 4%, oil exceeded $37 per barrel before retreating, the trade deficit set a record, and leading economic indicators were weak.

Panelists Elizabeth Dater, Louis Holland, Barbara Marcin, and Brian Rogers forecast corporate earnings, Federal Reserve policy, mutual-fund flows, and consumer confidence as major influences on 2001. Rogers expected 5–7% corporate-profit growth and at least two rate cuts; Marcin anticipated a broader, attractively valued market and a possible technology and telecommunications rebound; Holland assigned greater than a 50% probability to recession and expected possible aggressive rate cuts; Dater emphasized capital preservation, diversification, interest rates, and risks from a weaker dollar.

Their 2000 recommended portfolios returned 42.5% for Rogers, more than 40% for Marcin, more than 28% for Holland, and more than 7.5% for Dater. Notable gains included Everest Reinsurance’s 222% rise and the doubling of Washington Mutual.

For 2001, the four panelists forecast Dow closes between 11,740 and 12,504 and Nasdaq closes between 2,250 and 3,000. Their recommendations included technology and telecommunications stocks such as Compaq, Lucent, Motorola, WorldCom, Intel, Cisco, and AT&T Wireless; financial and consumer companies including Amgen, Berkshire Hathaway, Disney, Home Depot, Wal-Mart, and Carnival; and Dater’s 25% allocation to three-year U.S. Treasury notes. The 4-Verticals concept is a full-field passing play designed to stretch defenses vertically and horizontally, create favorable one-on-one matchups or open-zone voids, and allow quarterbacks to throw deep quickly. All four receivers release vertically.

It is most effective against man coverage and Cover 3, where quarterbacks can exploit matchups or seams by looking off the free safety. It is less effective against Cover 4 and soft zone coverage, especially on third-and-long when linebackers gain depth and open windows shrink; more horizontal concepts, such as shallow cross or Y cross, may then be preferable.

Receiver landmarks depend on defensive looks. Against two safeties, the slot receiver crosses the field safety around 10–12 yards, while the outside receivers run go routes. Against one safety, the slot receiver occupies the field seam and the outside receivers can convert to comeback routes if separation is not gained at 15 yards.

Quarterbacks should identify the number of safeties, coverage type, and potential matchups, then find a deep matchup or zone void, with a check-down to the running back as an alternative. Variations from 3x1 or empty formations retain the same landmarks, using the tight end or slot receiver crossing the safety’s face to isolate the X receiver or provide another throwing option.

Founded in 2004 with US$2.2 million in capital, Yunnan Lucky Air is a Kunming-based low-cost airline modeled largely on Southwest Airlines. It serves routes linking Kunming with tourist destinations such as Dali and Xishuanbanna, and a restricted government license gave it a near-monopoly on many Yunnan routes. By 2007, it carried about 1.2 million passengers, more than double the previous year, while operating revenue rose from US$31.2 million in 2006 to US$104.3 million and the load factor increased from 74.7% to 81.4%. It became profitable within three years. Its low-cost model includes one aircraft type, one class of service, simple one-way pricing, no seat assignments or in-flight entertainment, short point-to-point routes, and operations from secondary cities.

China’s rapidly expanding aviation market and growing low-cost segment attracted competitors, while regulation limited airlines’ pricing and operating flexibility. By 2007, China had 25 airlines, including 11 low-cost carriers, while three major airlines held 83.7% of the market. Analysts projected substantial growth for low-cost travel. Lucky Air’s costs, however, were only about 5% below the industry average rather than the roughly 30% advantage achieved by some U.S. and European low-cost carriers. Government controls affected fuel prices, landing fees, aircraft leasing, capacity expansion, route optimization, and taxes. Pricing rules, travel-agent commissions, and TravelSky distribution fees further constrained profitability.

Offline agents remained China’s dominant ticketing channel. Agents offered convenient delivery and reassurance but charged commissions of 2%–15%, while airlines also faced Global Distribution System and Billing and Settlement Plan fees. China’s e-commerce sector was comparatively undeveloped: Internet penetration was 19.1% nationwide and 6.8% in Yunnan, credit-card penetration was below 4%, and concerns about security, payment systems, and merchant credibility limited online purchasing. The online travel market generated only RMB 2.25 billion in 2007, with Ctrip and eLong holding 75% of that market. Although consumers frequently researched travel online, only about 10% booked online. About 80% of Lucky Air’s tickets were sold through agents, 95% of website sales were purchased by resellers, and only 1% of all tickets were bought directly by consumers on luckyair.net.

Supported by Hainan Airlines, Lucky Air operated an advanced website that supported online credit-card verification, ticket purchase and refund, ticket validation, flight information, destination information, customer blogs, and bonus points. Customers could buy tickets 5%–20% below other channels, and all searching, booking, payment, and validation occurred online without a call-center back end. Lucky Air viewed the site as a way to reach customers directly, strengthen brand recognition, build loyalty, and distinguish itself from Chinese competitors.

Research on U.S. and European airlines identified several relevant practices. Customer relationship management could improve customer understanding, conversion, and retention through Web 2.0 features, customer reviews, responsive support, and continuous analysis of feedback. Southwest Airlines used company and employee content, while Amazon and TripAdvisor demonstrated the value of customer reviews and aggregate ratings. Customer self-service through websites, kiosks, email, and other channels could reduce costs and free agents to handle complex issues. PayPal offered an alternative to direct card payments by improving security and convenience. Airlines also targeted specific groups, including corporate travelers through online management tools, price-sensitive and Internet-savvy students, and frequent travelers attracted by loyalty rewards.

Lucky Air faced a broad strategic choice. Planned airport investment in China promised new opportunities but would also attract further competitors. The airline could not rely solely on low costs because regulated expenses limited its cost advantage and competitors were pressuring prices. It could follow Spring Airlines by bundling flights with hotels and other travel services, or seek leadership in online travel as Internet and payment systems developed. The case concludes that overseas experience suggested e-commerce could build loyalty, increase conversion, and reduce costs, but only with substantial investment in technology and staff.

The Rays’ No. 2 prospect escaped a first-and-second, no-out jam in the third and retired six straight after a fourth-inning single. pitching coach Kyle Snyder praised his command, changeup and two-strike execution. President Nixon announced an accelerated withdrawal of 100,000 additional U.S. troops from Vietnam between May 1 and December 1, 1971, bringing total withdrawals to 365,000—more than two-thirds of the 540,000 troops present when he took office. He credited South Vietnamese forces, the Cambodia operation, and the Laos operation for reduced U.S. casualties and successful progress under Vietnamization.

Nixon reaffirmed the goal of complete American withdrawal, preferably through negotiations, and urged Hanoi to accept an immediate cease-fire, unconditional prisoner release, an Indochina peace conference, withdrawal of outside forces, and a political settlement. He opposed setting a fixed withdrawal date, arguing that doing so would surrender U.S. bargaining leverage, weaken incentives for an earlier negotiated end, and endanger remaining forces. He said gradual withdrawal would give South Vietnam a reasonable chance to remain free.

Defending U.S. service members while acknowledging isolated atrocities, Nixon praised their courage and humanitarian efforts and cited the sacrifice of Marine Sgt. Karl Taylor. He pledged to end the war in a way that honored those sacrifices, restored unity, and promoted lasting peace.

Researchers from the University of Washington, Texas A&M University and the Western Australian Museum discovered and named a new genus and species of clingfish, the duckbilled clingfish (*Nettorhamphos radula*), after identifying two specimens preserved in museum jars. One specimen was collected off southern Australia in 1977. The finger-sized fish has a broad, flat snout and an estimated 1,800–2,300 backward-pointing teeth—about 10 times as many as other known clingfishes. Because only two specimens are known, researchers used noninvasive CT scans and enlarged 3-D prints to examine its skeleton, mouth and jaw rather than dissecting it. The species was described in *Copeia* on April 14. Researchers study clingfish adhesion, which can support up to 150 times their body weight, for potential applications in surgical instruments and whale-tracking devices.

Lattice Semiconductor shows early signs of revenue recovery, driven by data center strength despite weakness in automotive and industrial markets. Management sees opportunities in high-end data center chips and emerging areas such as robotics, vision systems, and security. Inventories are normalizing, cash generation remains strong, the company has no debt, and Q3 guidance suggests further growth. Despite a raised $70 target price, the author retains a HOLD rating because of the expensive valuation and thin margin of safety.

Tesla Motors, Inc.’s Form 10-K for the year ended December 31, 2015 describes a company that designs, develops, manufactures and sells fully electric vehicles and energy storage products. Its Model S sedan began deliveries in June 2012, and more than 107,000 had been delivered worldwide by year-end. Deliveries of the seven-seat Model X SUV began in the third quarter of 2015, with production ramping in the United States and planned expansion to Europe and Asia in 2016. The lower-priced Model 3 was scheduled for unveiling in March 2016 and production and deliveries in late 2017. Tesla also offered residential 7 kWh and 10 kWh Powerwall systems and a commercial and utility-scale 100 kWh Powerpack, supporting backup power, load shifting, peak-demand reduction and grid services.

Tesla’s core capabilities include battery-pack engineering, power electronics, dual-motor powertrains, vehicle control and infotainment software, autopilot functions and electric-vehicle design and manufacturing. Its autopilot hardware included radar, cameras, ultrasonic sensors and digitally controlled braking. The company sold vehicles directly through company-owned stores, galleries and service facilities and operated a global Supercharger network. As of December 31, 2015, it had 208 sales and service-related locations, 118 service locations and 584 Supercharger stations. More than 1,800 destination locations had over 3,100 Tesla wall connectors. Customers generally ordered customized vehicles online, paid an initial deposit and paid the balance upon delivery. Tesla also offered vehicle loans, leases and resale-value guarantees.

Manufacturing occurred primarily in Fremont and Lathrop, California, and Tilburg, Netherlands. Fremont produced the Model S and Model X and key powertrain components, while Lathrop processed aluminum components. Tesla was developing the Gigafactory near Reno, Nevada, to integrate battery-material, cell, module and pack production. Tesla Energy production began there in late 2015, with cell production expected in 2016. By 2020, the Gigafactory was expected to support production of approximately 500,000 vehicles annually and 50 GWh of battery packs, with total associated capital expenditures estimated at $4 billion to $5 billion. Panasonic was partnering with Tesla and had an agreement to supply lithium-ion cells. Tesla sourced more than 3,000 purchased parts from over 350 suppliers.

The automotive and energy-storage markets were highly competitive, and most competitors had greater financial and operating resources. Tesla operated as one reportable segment and employed 13,058 full-time employees at year-end. It protected its intellectual property through patents, trademarks, trade secrets, licenses and contractual rights and had pledged not to sue parties acting in good faith for patent infringement involving electric vehicles or related equipment.

The report identified material risks involving production and delivery ramp delays, manufacturing complexity, product quality and software defects, Gigafactory execution, battery safety and costs, supplier concentration, market acceptance, competition, volatile demand, foreign-exchange fluctuations, product-liability claims, recalls, financing and residual-value guarantees, international expansion, changing government incentives, service requirements, the cost of expanding stores and Superchargers, strategic partners and retention of key personnel. The company also warned that its forward-looking expectations regarding operations, revenues, costs, profitability, demand and growth could differ materially from actual results.

After FML added tables and open space on its sixth floor, some students sought quieter private spaces. Grant Cummings prefers early-morning classrooms, while Rachael Grobman arrives early, briefly saves a cubicle for a friend, and studies at FML, the bookstore, Williams Hall and Rauch.

FML will remain open 24 hours daily from Dec. 11 at 7:45 a.m. until Dec. 20 at 10 p.m.; Packard Lab, the University Center, Rauch and Williams will also have extended hours. Students can reserve rooms online through the Center for Career and Professional Development, reducing study-space stress and providing coffee and snacks.

The statistical analysis plan specifies ECG assessments by treatment and visit, including investigator classifications of normal, clinically significant abnormal, and non-clinically significant abnormal 12-lead ECGs; descriptive ECG parameters; and categorical QTcF summaries for values above 450, 480, and 500 ms and postbaseline increases above 30 and 60 ms.

Immunogenicity will be analyzed descriptively by treatment group without statistical tests. The ADA incidence numerator includes patients who were ADA-negative at baseline and became positive after treatment and baseline-positive patients with at least a fivefold ADA-titer increase. The denominator will be evaluable patients with an appropriate post-treatment reportable sample, including relevant unscheduled visits; baseline-positive patients without a post-treatment sample will be excluded.

Compared with the protocol, primary-efficacy analysis wording was revised and additional sensitivity and supportive analyses were added. Secondary-efficacy terminology changed from “within” specified minutes to “at” specified minutes.

Programming standards cover table, figure, and listing formats, decimal precision, percentages, zero-count categories, sorting, date and time formats, footnotes, source references, and program metadata. Calculations include SAS-based durations, unit conversions, BMI, and change from baseline. Missing or incomplete adverse-event onset dates are generally treated as treatment-emergent unless available information indicates otherwise.

SAS quality-control requirements address program structure, documentation, hard coding, log review, output verification, dataset validation, source-data spot checks, figure comparisons, and retention of supporting records in the Program Status Document.

Planned outputs cover patient disposition, demographics, diabetes history, body measurements, medical history, concomitant medications, plasma-glucose recovery and sensitivity analyses, glucose results at 10, 15, 20, and 30 minutes, adverse events, ECG, laboratory tests, vital signs, immunogenicity, and pharmacokinetic and pharmacodynamic summaries for dasiglucagon, GlucaGen, and glucose.

**Summary**

Scientific American writer Laura Sanders (published online July 25, 2025) examines whether ultraprocessed foods are genuinely addictive. Scientists increasingly believe these highly engineered products — which contain little or no whole food, are built from concentrated sugars and fats, and are packaged with appealing branding — trigger desires comparable to alcohol, nicotine and opioids, and could be classified as addictive substances. Studies suggest they can produce cravings, loss of control, withdrawal and tolerance, hallmarks of substance use disorder.

The share of American calories from ultraprocessed foods rose from about 51% at home in 2003 to just over 54% in 2018. The NOVA classification sorts foods by processing level rather than nutrients, from unprocessed or minimally processed foods (apples, chicken) to ultraprocessed ones (hot dogs, potato chips). A related concept, "hyperpalatable," denotes foods engineered to be extra delicious and irresistible; hyperpalatable and ultraprocessed foods overlap strongly in the U.S. but less in other countries, where processing is less intense. A study of U.S. breakfast cereals from 2010 to 2023 found fiber and protein declined while fat, salt and sugar rose.

The idea that food can be addictive gained traction at a 2007 Yale meeting convened by Kelly Brownell and Mark Gold, bridging nutrition and addiction fields despite early skepticism. Neuroscience research has found ultraprocessed foods alter brain reward systems, affecting dopamine, serotonin and brain-made opioids, much like drugs or alcohol. Virginia Tech neuroscientist Alex DiFeliceantonio found that two months of daily high-fat, high-sugar yogurt dessert produced stronger neural responses to food cues and increased motivation to eat. Using the Yale Food Addiction Scale, roughly 14% of adults and 12% of children meet food addiction criteria, near alcohol use disorder prevalence, based on nearly 300 studies from 36 countries. Preliminary findings showed 18- to 21-year-olds on ultraprocessed diets ate more, including without hunger, than minimally processed peers; this did not hold for ages 22–25.

Researchers have also found that after tobacco firms faced tighter regulation, tobacco-owned food companies became more likely to sell hyperpalatable foods, with U.S. tobacco companies "systematically involved" in developing and disseminating them.

Regulatory responses are advancing: federal agencies are scrutinizing these foods, states are exploring school bans, a Pennsylvania lawsuit against food companies was dismissed, and movements for better labeling and healthier school lunches have grown; some companies are "unprocessing" products and creating foods suited to GLP-1 drug users. Chile's rules — marketing restrictions, taxes and warning labels on products high in sugar, saturated fat, salt or calories — have shifted purchases toward healthier options. Experts argue an addiction framing matters because telling individuals to stop eating these foods ignores that such foods are designed to be irresistible; as psychologist Tera Fazzino puts it, "As a public, we deserve to be protected from the things that can cause us harm."

The Trump administration’s 2018 Nuclear Posture Review proposes modernizing US nuclear capabilities, including smaller low-yield warheads, upgraded command systems and infrastructure, dual-capable aircraft, forward-deployed nuclear bombers, modified SLBM warheads and a future nuclear-armed sea-launched cruise missile. The policy aims to deter regional aggression, raise the nuclear threshold and reduce the likelihood of nuclear use while maintaining the testing moratorium and commitments to arms control, non-proliferation, nuclear security and the NPT. It states that the US will not use or threaten nuclear weapons against non-nuclear NPT-compliant states. Defence Secretary Jim Mattis warned that Russia and China are developing nuclear and conventional capabilities challenging US military superiority. The report also addresses North Korea’s illicit nuclear program, Iran’s weapons capability, nuclear terrorism and tailored extended-deterrence commitments to European, Asian and Pacific allies. Pakistan is not mentioned.

Under a two-year agreement, Ottawa will give provinces and territories 75% of tax revenue from legalized marijuana, with part flowing to municipalities to cover local costs. The federal government will retain 25%, up to $100 million annually; revenue above that cap will go to the provinces. All 14 jurisdictions accepted the framework, replacing an earlier proposed 50-50 split. About $400 million in tax revenue is expected over the first two years, with a review planned for December 2018. Provinces may set markups above the federal tax model and decide municipal revenue-sharing levels; municipalities had requested one-third. Ottawa has separately committed more than $1 billion over five years for legalization, policing and border security. Ministers also discussed equalization, the Canada Pension Plan, the global economy and corporate-ownership information sharing.

The address emphasizes the heavy responsibilities of the presidency and pledges continuity with the preceding administration’s reforms. The administration will enforce antitrust and interstate-commerce reforms, seek relief for railroads from certain restrictions, and regulate railroad securities and interstate industrial combinations. It will also reorganize the Department of Justice, Bureau of Corporations, and Interstate Commerce Commission and submit proposed legislative and administrative changes to Congress, distinguishing legitimate business combinations from monopolies used to control prices.

Tariff revision is presented as the most immediate priority. Congress will be called into an extra session on March 15 to consider revising the Dingley Act. The proposed tariff would protect domestic labor and industries, adjust rates according to differences in domestic and foreign production costs, and allow higher tariffs against countries with discriminatory trade policies. Because revision will disrupt businesses awaiting certainty, only tariff legislation should be considered during the extra session. The measure must provide adequate revenue against a projected $100 million deficit; if import duties are insufficient, a graduated inheritance tax is recommended. The government should economize without eliminating expenditures necessary for effective administration.

The address rejects both unlimited laissez-faire government and wasteful spending. Appropriate federal functions include agricultural research, supervision of powerful businesses, conservation of forests and waterways, and major public works. Permanent improvements such as the Panama Canal and comparable river-development projects should be financed through bonds to distribute costs between present and future beneficiaries.

National defense requires an expandable army, a modern navy, and adequate coastal fortifications. These forces are necessary to defend American rights, support the Monroe Doctrine, and preserve peace. The United States should pursue arbitration and avoid war, but it must remain armed and prepared so other nations cannot exploit its inability to defend its interests. The government should also protect Americans abroad against degrading discrimination and address Asian immigration through treaties, regulation, and precautions against violence.

The United States should enforce treaty obligations protecting aliens through federal jurisdiction rather than leaving them to state or local authorities. The administration also supports reforms to monetary and banking laws to make currency more elastic and reduce the danger of financial panics, while awaiting recommendations from the monetary commission. Congress should establish a postal savings bank to attract savings, add investment capital, and guarantee deposits without the adverse effects of private deposit guarantees.

Foreign trade should be expanded through tariffs and diplomacy, particularly with the Philippines, South America, and the Orient. Subsidized steamship lines may help connect North and South America. Construction of the lock-type Panama Canal is progressing satisfactorily, and the incoming administration will support its prompt completion under the existing organization. Free trade with the Philippines is expected to improve business there while protecting American sugar and tobacco interests. Puerto Rico’s prosperity continues, and both dependencies are said to be making progress under American civil-liberty traditions.

The address also addresses relations between the South and the rest of the country, emphasizing tolerance, political opposition, and Southern identification with the federal government. It reviews the Thirteenth, Fourteenth, and Fifteenth Amendments, supports state electoral qualifications applying to voters of any race who lack specified qualifications, and identifies the Fifteenth Amendment as a lasting federal protection. Greater industrial education and economic progress for Black Americans are encouraged. The president should exercise discretion when making appointments to avoid intensifying racial hostility while also opposing manufactured prejudice.

On labor, the address supports existing federal protections for railroad employees, government employees’ compensation, child-labor regulation, and additional safety requirements for interstate railways. The government should be as responsible for injured employees as federally regulated railroad corporations. The speaker firmly opposes restricting federal courts’ authority to issue injunctions in labor disputes and rejects legalizing secondary boycotts. Statutory standards should govern temporary restraining orders to prevent abuse without weakening the courts’ authority. The address closes by invoking public sympathy and divine aid in carrying out the administration’s responsibilities.

A study by the Australian National University and the Institut de Physique du Globe de Paris, combining experiments and computer modelling, found that alumino-silicate glass — used in screens such as Samsung's Gorilla Glass — has more organised atomic structure than previously thought. Sodium and potassium atoms, rather than distributing randomly, form clusters and percolation channels, while calcium and magnesium also affect glass flexibility and resistance. These microscopic arrangements influence how fractures begin or halt, potentially yielding more fracture-proof glass for phone screens, with ANU seeking manufacturing partners to commercialise it. Meanwhile, smartphone durability remains weak: the glass-fronted-and-backed iPhone X and iPhone 8 are costly to repair, drop tests rendered Samsung's Note 8 non-functional, and Samsung and LG have yet to commercialise foldable displays, though Samsung is targeting a foldable Note.

Moody’s is expected to keep South Africa at investment grade this week, according to all 15 economists and analysts in a Bloomberg survey, reflecting renewed confidence after Cyril Ramaphosa replaced Jacob Zuma. The rand and business confidence have rebounded, but fiscal slippage, weak growth and the ANC’s pursuit of uncompensated expropriation remain downgrade risks. A junk rating could remove South Africa from major indices, trigger up to 100 billion rand in outflows and raise borrowing costs. S&P and Fitch already downgraded the country to junk last year.

Antimicrobial resistance prediction from bacterial genomes can be hindered by slow culture-based diagnostics and methods that either detect only known resistance markers or ignore the sequential context of genomic mutations. This study presents AMR-EnsembleNet, a soft-voting ensemble combining a lightweight 1D convolutional neural network (CNN), which learns local SNP motifs and genomic context, with XGBoost, which captures non-local feature interactions.

The models were evaluated using the GieSSen benchmark dataset of 809 E. coli isolates with 60,936 ordered SNP features and binary resistance labels for ciprofloxacin, cefotaxime, ceftazidime, and gentamicin. Training used stratified 80/20 splits and inverse-root class weighting for imbalanced data. The CNN included 64-dimensional embeddings, six hierarchical convolutional blocks, global max pooling, and an MLP classifier; AMR-EnsembleNet averaged the CNN and XGBoost probability outputs. Performance was compared with standalone CNN, XGBoost, and Random Forest baselines.

For ciprofloxacin, XGBoost and the ensemble tied for highest accuracy at 0.9630, while the ensemble had the highest MCC at 0.9260. For cefotaxime, the ensemble performed best across major metrics, achieving 0.8086 accuracy, 0.8000 resistant-class F1, and 0.8611 resistant-class recall. For ceftazidime, Random Forest performed best, although the ensemble produced a more balanced second-highest MCC of 0.5715. On the highly imbalanced gentamicin task, the CNN had the highest resistant-class recall at 0.7105, while the ensemble balanced this strength with higher precision and achieved the best MCC (0.4030) and macro F1 (0.6908).

SHAP analysis of XGBoost predictions identified influential SNPs that mapped to known AMR-associated genes, including gyrB, marR, rpsL, parC, fusA, ampC, acrD, and ftsI. The study concludes that combining sequence-aware CNN and feature-based XGBoost provides a robust, computationally feasible approach to genomic AMR prediction. Proposed future work includes predicting minimum inhibitory concentration values, integrating transcriptomic data, and applying advanced explainability methods to the CNN to identify novel resistance markers.

The dollar rose broadly Monday as traders unwound bearish positions amid easing U.S.–North Korea tensions and underwhelming U.S. inflation data. The dollar index gained 0.3%, and rising U.S. stocks supported the currency. Investors awaited Tuesday’s U.S. retail sales report for more inflation clues.

Saskatoon proposes a $1.2 million, two-year plan to remove and replace black ash trees damaged by European cottony ash psyllids. A summer assessment recommends removing 1,000 trees after insecticides failed to slow their decline; 121 have already been removed this year. First-year funding of $757,000 comes from reserve funds, while $423,000 for year two remains unidentified.

The study investigates water- and ethanol-assisted capillary densification as a scalable post-processing method for strengthening electrospun polyacrylonitrile (PAN) nanofiber yarns. Loosely collected PAN bundles were treated by rolling with deionized water or ethanol, followed by drying; selected samples were additionally annealed at 110 °C for 5 hours. Tensile behavior, morphology, fiber alignment, and packing density were characterized using micro-tensile tests, SEM, Fourier analysis, OrientationJ, and image-based density measurements.

As-spun yarns displayed lower modulus and stress but greater ductility, sometimes reaching about 200% elongation. Liquid-treated yarns carried higher loads and stresses while failing at approximately 30–50% strain. Water treatment produced the strongest overall performance because slower evaporation and greater capillary driving forces enabled stronger compaction than ethanol. Ethanol treatment improved alignment but was limited by rapid evaporation and nanofiber swelling. Thermal annealing promoted fiber-junction fusion, further increasing stiffness and strength relative to untreated yarns, but reduced ductility and produced failure strains near 15%.

Yarn strength and effective modulus increased strongly as yarn diameter decreased. Yarns below 10 μm approached the mechanical response of individual PAN nanofibers, reaching approximately 1.1 GPa modulus and 30 MPa peak stress, while larger yarns were substantially weaker. Comparisons across matched diameter ranges and segments from the same parent yarn confirmed that treatment increased absolute peak load beyond geometric normalization effects. In a controlled same-yarn comparison, water treatment increased mean peak load from 5.4 to 9.3 mN, and treatment explained about 34% of peak-load variance.

SEM analysis showed that liquid rolling and annealing increased fiber alignment, packing density, anisotropy, and inter-fiber contact. Peak load correlated strongly with alignment coherency (R² = 0.68) and packing density (R² = 0.75); combined regression improved explanatory power to R² = 0.80. These complementary metrics were linked to enhanced adhesive and frictional load transfer, reduced voids and stress concentrations, and more uniform strain distribution.

A stochastic mean-field constitutive model reproduced the yarns’ five deformation regimes: geometric uncrimping, linear elasticity, nonlinear recruitment, stress plateau, and progressive failure. It incorporated Weibull-distributed fiber recruitment and failure, elastic-perfectly plastic fiber behavior, orientation averaging, packing-dependent load-transfer efficiency, and post-failure residual bridging. Weighted nonlinear fitting reproduced the experimental stress–stretch curves, and the fitted microstructure parameter showed a strong linear relationship with SEM-derived packing-density and alignment measurements (R² = 0.91).

The results identify simple liquid-assisted densification and moderate annealing as effective routes for improving electrospun PAN yarn strength while establishing image-based alignment and packing metrics as predictors and inputs for constitutive modeling.

Gensler reviews class submissions, praising their generally strong quality while encouraging students to use critical reasoning, address the current week’s topic, and submit work by class 23. He notes that participation counts for 30% of the grade and announces upcoming sessions with Intercontinental Exchange CEO Jeff Sprecher and Bakkt CEO Kelly Loeffler, as well as an October 16 guest speaker.

He frames finance around three areas: financial institutions, regulation, and technology. Finance allocates, prices, and moves money and risk through intermediaries, illustrated by an hourglass with Wall Street at its narrow center. Its principal functions include capital allocation, market making, payments, liquidity, investment, and credit. Major sectors include commercial banks, investment banks and brokerages, insurance, asset managers and collective investment vehicles, exchanges, and clearinghouses. Commercial banks allocate, price, and underwrite credit and transform maturities; investment banks underwrite and trade securities; insurers transform risk.

Primary capital markets involve an issuer’s first sale of a security, while secondary markets trade existing securities and generally have greater volume. Both have distinct structures and regulation. Ledgers record transactions, economic activity, and financial relationships and are embedded throughout finance. Payment systems authorize, clear, and record transfers by amending ledger accounts; blockchain may enable faster final settlement. Fiat currency is likewise represented through centralized and commercial-bank ledgers.

Gensler describes financial regulation as centuries old, tracing it from debtor imprisonment and bankruptcy law to modern frameworks centered on financial stability, consumer and investor protection, and illicit financial activity. Financial stability encompasses inflation, sovereign and central-bank risks, boom-and-bust cycles, and leverage. Financial institutions differ from nonfinancial firms because most of their assets are financial assets, creating leverage and instability risks.

Technology has long shaped finance, including communication, recordkeeping, computers, telex, cryptography, databases, and blockchain. Large financial institutions may be slow to replace legacy systems, potentially creating opportunities for targeted disruptors. He identifies AI, machine learning, blockchain, biometrics, big data, robotic process automation, cloud computing, open APIs, and chatbots as fintech technologies. Blockchain uses cryptography and database structures and is most relevant to finance when recording things of value, particularly for rapid settlement.

Credit is borrowing value with an agreement to repay it. Gensler cites U.S. public and private debt of roughly $70 trillion, or about 350% of GDP, while distinguishing the approximately $40 trillion bond market from broader credit markets. Household debt is led by roughly $9 trillion in mortgages and $1.5 trillion in student debt, followed by credit cards, home equity, and auto loans.

Financial risks discussed include market, credit and underwriting, counterparty, operational, cyber, legal, compliance, reputational, human-capital, political, and expropriation risks. Gensler emphasizes liquidity, funding, settlement, and correlation or model risks as recurring causes of institutional failure, particularly when markets become thin and tail events invalidate normal assumptions.

He attributes the 2008 subprime mortgage crisis to weak underwriting, predatory lending, a housing bubble, prolonged easy credit, low interest rates, foreign purchases of U.S. paper, credit-default swaps, greater leverage and interconnectedness, model-based capital rules, poor risk management, asymmetric bonuses, and rating-agency conflicts. Bear Stearns’ failure, Northern Rock’s collapse, and the conservatorship of Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac preceded a potential systemic collapse without government intervention.

Gensler says the financial system is stronger in some respects because banks hold more capital and use less leverage, but concerns remain about high asset valuations, institutional concentration, unequal economic gains, reduced consumption capacity, and weakened social consensus. He also notes that crisis assistance went more heavily to large institutions than to consumers.

He suggests blockchain opportunities are more likely to be targeted than to replace entire banks, and that viable uses should involve data-intensive financial records, economic rents, infrastructure costs, counterparty risk, and concentrated risk. Finance represents roughly 5%–7.5% of the economy, while capital markets are about five times the size of the economy, implying an overall financial-sector take of about 1.5%. He closes by previewing readings on blockchain economics, including work by Christian Catalini, Paul Krugman, and Nouriel Roubini.

Physicists developed a method for immiscible liquids to self-organize into layered patterns within droplets or thin straws. By initiating de-mixing at the edge and controlling its propagation speed and duration, researchers could tune stripe lengths and emulsion structure. Their theoretical model matched experiments, predicted layer lifetimes, and enabled stepwise release of inner droplets. The work may advance water- and oil-soluble medicines and other emulsion-based products, including pharmaceuticals and cosmetics.

The Fifth Circuit affirmed Jose Verastegui’s guilty-plea convictions and concurrent 120-month sentences for felon in possession of a firearm and unlawful reentry. It found no abuse of discretion or unreasonableness in the upward departure and variance from the 63–78-month advisory guidelines based on his criminal history and the § 3553(a) factors. His guideline-calculation and constitutional challenges were foreclosed by precedent, though preserved for possible Supreme Court review. The opinion was designated nonprecedential.
OnePlus is rolling out Android Nougat updates globally for the OnePlus 3 and 3T, with redesigned menus, multi-window support, direct notification replies, and Doze On-the-Go.

This lecture on nuclear physics addresses what binds nuclei together. The nuclear force is described as the residual strong interaction between quarks located in different hadrons; because many quarks and nucleons are involved, it is treated using a mean-field approach. Experimental information comes mainly from nucleon–nucleon scattering (including spin-polarized projectiles), nuclear binding energies and precise mass measurements, and nuclear structure data such as energy levels, spins, parities, and magnetic and quadrupole moments, particularly for light nuclei.

The force depends on the distance between interacting nucleons and on their spin and angular momentum, indicating spin–orbit and tensor components. It appears charge independent, consistent with the strong interaction being blind to electric charge; electromagnetic contributions must be subtracted by carefully comparing proton–proton, proton–neutron, and neutron–neutron scattering.

Radially, the nuclear force is short range, vanishing beyond roughly 2 femtometers, and strongly repulsive at separations below about 0.5 femtometers, since nucleons cannot be compressed further. Evidence for short range includes roughly constant binding energy per nucleon (linear in mass number, implying only nearest-neighbor interactions), nuclear reaction distances about 1–2 femtometers beyond nuclear radii, and nuclear densities close to nucleon densities.

Charge independence is exploited through mirror nuclei, which have the same mass number with protons and neutrons interchanged (e.g., helium-3 and tritium). Their nearly identical binding energies (after removing the Coulomb term) and excitation energies support charge independence; in heavy mirror nuclei, charge-independence breaking effects are strong. Mirror nuclei also permit study of unstable or radioactive nuclei through their stable counterparts.

Enjifit launched for iOS on July 3, 2018, connecting users with nearby workout partners and personal trainers based on goals and interests. The free app supports filtering, messaging, workout reminders, posting sessions, and finding people ready to exercise within an hour. A monthly PRO subscription lets trainers and nutritionists feature their services, and an Android version was planned.

Milky Tea announced that HyperBrawl Tournament, a no-rules, high-speed handball PvP arena game, will arrive on Steam Early Access in June 2017. Inspired by Speedball, Rocket League, and Battlerite, it features 10 warriors, 10 weapons, six arenas, eight solo minigames, and local or online multiplayer for up to four players in 1v1 and 2v2 matches. Players can unlock skins, weapons, and characters.

Pepsi Nigeria’s “No Shakin’ Carry Go” campaign will send 10 fans on an all-expenses-paid, three-day VIP trip to Dubai’s One Africa Music Fest in November, featuring Wizkid, Tiwa Savage, Davido and Tekno.

The disclosure describes a machine-learned depth-estimation model that generates a depth map from a single color image. The model is trained using monocular video, stereoscopic image pairs, or both. Depth and pose information are used to project images into synthetic frames, which are compared with target images using a per-pixel, input-scale occlusion- and motion-aware loss. The loss can use the minimum or average reconstruction error from adjacent temporal frames, upsampled depth features, and masks that discount static features. Separate depth and pose models or a hybrid model sharing a depth encoder and pose decoder may be used.

The disclosure also describes deployment in a location-based parallel-reality game, where a client device captures images, tracks the player’s real-world position, and maps it to a corresponding virtual location. A trained depth model can provide depth information used to place, scale, or occlude virtual content in augmented views of the real world. The system includes a game server, game database, client gaming and positioning modules, camera assemblies, and a depth-estimation training system.

Technology megacaps lost $770 billion in market value Friday, driving the Nasdaq down 3.6% and the S&P 500 down 2.7% in their worst day since April. Nvidia, Amazon and Tesla each fell about 5% after President Trump threatened massive tariffs on Chinese imports, declared a 100% tariff on China and announced export controls on critical software. Nvidia lost nearly $229 billion in value, Microsoft $85 billion and Amazon $121 billion.
An Accenture study of 1,300 investors found that clients across ages and economic brackets favor hybrid wealth management, combining low-cost robo-advice with human expertise for complex situations.

Kennesaw State won the 2017 ASUN Championship at The Legends at Chateau Elan, finishing one shot ahead of Lipscomb at 1-under with a final-round 7-under 295. Jake Fendt and Pablo Rodriguez-Tabernero tied for second at 2-under, and the Owls earned their seventh consecutive NCAA Regional berth. Lipscomb’s Dawson Armstrong won the individual title at 6-under 210, following rounds of 70 and 69 with three final-day birdies to give Lipscomb its first ASUN men’s individual conference champion. Armstrong, a two-time ASUN Player of the Year, recorded his sixth college victory. Defending champion David Wicks tied for eighth at 1-over, while Jacksonville placed third and North Florida fourth.

Episode four of UFC 216 Embedded follows Demetrious Johnson shopping for suits and studio equipment, Ray Borg training at the UFC Performance Institute, and Derrick Lewis holding a mock weigh-in with Forrest Griffin. Tony Ferguson tries on fight-night clothing, Kevin Lee visits a children’s cancer center, and the fighters conduct media interviews and faceoffs at T-Mobile ahead of UFC 216’s two title fights on October 7.

On April 13, 2022, Amazon.com, Inc. closed the sale of seven series of notes: $1.5 billion of 2.730% notes due 2024; $1.5 billion of 3.000% notes due 2025; $2 billion of 3.300% notes due 2027; $1.5 billion of 3.450% notes due 2029; $2.5 billion of 3.600% notes due 2032; $2.5 billion of 3.950% notes due 2052; and $1.25 billion of 4.100% notes due 2062. The aggregate public offering price was $12.719 billion, with estimated net proceeds of approximately $12.692 billion. The notes were sold under an April 11, 2022 underwriting agreement with Goldman Sachs, J.P. Morgan and Morgan Stanley, and issued under Amazon’s 2012 base indenture as supplemented by an April 13, 2022 supplemental indenture naming Computershare Trust Company as successor trustee. The offering was registered on Form S-3. The filing includes the underwriting agreement, supplemental indenture, forms of the notes, and legal opinion and consent.

North Wales Police are seeking witnesses after a woman in her 30s escaped an attempted kidnapping in Rhyl. The suspect, described as a man in his 40s of oriental appearance, approached her on Sisson Street and was seen entering a silver vehicle. Police initially alerted schools and parents because a child was thought involved, but later confirmed no child was involved.

Zimbabwean pupils appealed to President Mnangagwa to suspend the November 2018 public examinations because teachers were absent while conducting electoral duties, leaving pupils insufficiently prepared. Permanent Secretary Dr Sylvia Utete-Masango said schools should organize holiday lessons and open a week early on September 4 to compensate for 10 lost working days ahead of the July 30 harmonised elections. The President’s response was not disclosed.

New Horizons, the first spacecraft to fly by Pluto in July 2015, had its mission extended to study Kuiper Belt Objects, arriving at 2014 MU69 — about 1.6 billion km beyond Pluto — on Jan. 1, 2019. Nicknamed "Ultima Thule" ("beyond Thule," a mythical far-northern island) through a public naming campaign launched by NASA and the New Horizons team in early November and hosted by the SETI Institute, the nickname drew about 40 public nominations and won among the most-voted of 34,000 names submitted by 115,000 participants; voting closed Dec. 6, 2017. MU69 is expected to be the most primitive object ever observed by a spacecraft and the farthest encounter in space exploration. 2017 occultation observations from Argentina suggest it may be a prolate spheroid or a close/contact binary, so the working name is temporary, pending a formal IAU submission after the flyby.

Using exome sequencing from 454,803 UK Biobank and 173,585 Geisinger MyCode participants, the study generated large CHIP callsets using Mutect2 and quality control focused on 23 recurrently mutated genes. It identified 27,331 CHIP carriers in UK Biobank (6%) and 12,877 in Geisinger (7.4%). DNMT3A, TET2, ASXL1, PPM1D, and TP53 were most frequently mutated. CHIP prevalence rose with age, reaching about 15% by age 75, and was associated with heavy smoking. Certain mutations co-occurred more often than expected, and maximum variant allele fraction increased with the number of CHIP mutations.

A UK Biobank common-variant GWAS identified 27 CHIP-associated loci, including 24 novel loci, with most replication signals directionally consistent in Geisinger. Rare-variant analyses found associations at the SMC4 and CHEK2 loci and burden associations involving ATM, CHEK2, CTC1, CLPTM1L, and KDELC2. Gene-specific analyses demonstrated shared, subtype-specific, and opposing effects: DNMT3A had the most associated loci; PARP1 and LY75 variants were associated with reduced DNMT3A-CHIP risk; and TCL1A variants increased DNMT3A-CHIP risk while decreasing several other CHIP subtypes.

CHIP was distinct from mosaic chromosomal alteration phenotypes, although carriers were enriched for these alterations and CHIP shared germline risk factors with mosaic loss of Y and X chromosomes. Rare-variant analyses also identified novel associations for mosaic alterations and telomere length, including variants in KNTC1, TIE1, PTPRF, TM2D3, GIGYF1, RC3H1, DCLRE1B, PARN, and CTC1.

Phenome-wide analyses of 4,871 UK Biobank traits showed subtype-specific associations with hematologic, cardiovascular, neoplastic, infectious, renal, endocrine, ophthalmologic, adiposity, and smoking-related traits. DNMT3A- and TET2-CHIP often showed opposing blood-count and adiposity associations. High-VAF CHIP was associated with COVID-19 hospitalization and severe infection.

In longitudinal analyses, high-VAF CHIP was associated with cardiovascular disease, all-cause mortality, blood cancers—especially myeloid cancers—and lung cancer; risks were similar in smokers and nonsmokers for blood and lung cancers. TET2 carriers had the highest blood-cancer risk, whereas DNMT3A alone was not associated with lymphoid cancer but conferred greater risk when additional CHIP mutations were present. A DNMT3A polygenic risk score predicted several CHIP subtypes, myeloid cancer, lung cancer, and prostate cancer, but not cardiovascular disease or mortality.

Overall, the findings indicate that CHIP is a heterogeneous composite of somatic mutation-driven subtypes with partly shared genetic causes and distinct clinical risk profiles. PARP1 and LY75 were proposed as possible therapeutic targets, while the lack of serial sampling was identified as a limitation for tracking clonal evolution and temporal relationships among mutations.

Attacking runs are spontaneous off-ball movements by offensive players into the opponent’s half, usually into open space to receive a pass. Forwards, strikers, and leading midfielders should continually seek penetrating runs that create passing options or lead to shots. Effective runs require seven elements: recognizing open space, choosing an appropriate run, breaking away from a defender, getting open, proper timing, receiving an optimal pass, and communication.

Runners should exploit their initial head start, keep defenders uncertain, and maintain separation by sprinting or changing direction. Timing must exploit space and avoid offside; if a pass is delayed, the runner should move parallel to and in front of the next-to-last defender. Runners must anticipate the pass, coordinate the run’s direction and speed with the pass’s direction and pace, and complete a run once started. Communication may be verbal, visual, or through eye contact.

Coachable runs include bending, checking, diagonal, hooking, inside, lateral, onside, outlet, sideline, straight, through, and wide runs. Selection should advance the attack and make the pass easier to complete.

Coaching can progress from cones representing defenders and a goalkeeper, to practicing runs, adding passes, using stationary defenders, introducing defender movement and additional attackers, and finally full movement. Good runs should be rewarded with good passes; ball carriers should not hog the ball, passers should continue attacking, and players should provide support options and vary runs to prevent defenders from anticipating them.

At an NHL draft event in Columbus, hosts interviewed prospects James van Riemsdyk, Kyle Turris, Patrick Kane, Sam Gagner, Keaton Ellerby and Karl Alzner about their hometowns, family, coaching influences, development, college and national-team plans, and NHL aspirations. The players introduced family and friends before being wished luck for the draft and game.

The passage presents the 1-3-1 “Clock” offense as an effective attack against a Diamond & One defense. Placing the star post player in the middle creates open looks, layups, putbacks, and one-on-one post opportunities against a chaser more prepared for pass denial than post defense.

The basic rotation begins with a wing passing to the corner and cutting toward the basket while teammates rotate. The corner can feed the star in the post, reverse the ball toward the weak side, or hit the star rolling after the help defender steps out. Wings may also dribble-clear to the corner, exchange roles with the corner player, initiate reversals, or drive when open.

When the star receives the ball at the high post, inside-triangle action isolates the star against the chaser. Drives create drop-pass opportunities for layups, while kick-out passes find open wings. Baseline players can flash into the middle for a shot or pass as the remaining wings flare for open shots.

The offense emphasizes offensive rebounding, creating a three-on-two advantage after missed outside shots and easy putbacks. Its success depends on coordinated screens, post-ups, communication, timing, and experience. Coaches should scout defensive reads and matchups, observe adjustments, vary alignments and entries, and move players to attack weaker defenders.

Education initiatives often stall because leaders invest heavily in programs but neglect the narratives explaining their purpose, leaving communities to rely on familiar assumptions that reforms are top-down, data is dangerous, and technology replaces people. The authors recommend treating narrative as design: frame, test, iterate, and scale. This involves clarifying goals and audience assumptions, developing shared values and metaphors, testing messages, co-designing with educators and families, and providing practical tools and support. Proposed applications include presenting standards as instructional “signposts” and AI as a teaching assistant rather than surveillance. Effective strategies center teachers and students, explain mechanisms and benefits, address privacy, bias, and misuse, and avoid crisis-driven or divisive framing. The Texas Supreme Court tentatively proposed ending the ABA’s final say over whether Texas law school graduates qualify for the bar exam and licensure. It sought public comments by Dec. 1, with changes planned for January, while leaving replacement oversight unclear. The ABA said it is reviewing the proposal and will submit comments.

The No. 2-seeded Las Vegas Aces defeated the third-seeded Phoenix Mercury 90-88 in Game 3 of the 2025 WNBA Finals, taking a 3-0 lead and moving one win from their third championship and the first Finals sweep since 2020. A’ja Wilson scored 34 points with 14 rebounds and made the decisive late basket after Phoenix tied the game with 1:01 remaining. The Mercury rallied from a 17-point deficit but lost for the third consecutive time.

Las Vegas credited its success to Becky Hammon’s varied defensive schemes, timely reserve contributions, and the cohesion of Wilson, Jackie Young and Chelsea Gray. The Aces also used zone and “junk” defenses to disrupt Phoenix’s fast starts. Young and Wilson combined for 60 points in Game 2, while depth and defensive flexibility helped the Aces overcome a middling start to the season that included a 16-game winning streak. Phoenix center Sabally was ruled out of Game 4 with a concussion.

Akure-based lawyer and rights activist Morakinyo Ogele gave the EFCC seven days to publicly apologize for invading Sun Newspaper’s premises and pay ₦1 billion in compensation. The article was syndicated from Daily Post Nigeria.

Guilford and Milford police are investigating repeated nighttime vehicle break-ins and thefts along Connecticut’s shoreline. Groups of young suspects steal property, vehicles when keys remain inside, and sometimes use stolen credit cards. Authorities warn residents to lock cars, use outdoor lights, and call 911 about suspicious activity.

The speaker said a goal deflected off a defenseman’s shin and subsequent penalty kills changed the game’s course, but he believed his team played well, defended effectively and fought back offensively. Disappointed by the Penguins’ win, he noted the loss reduced their chances of winning the series in four games.

He expressed no concern about goaltender Pekka, calling him the team’s backbone, and praised a late penalty-kill forecheck and quick finish by Freddy, who performed well despite limited NHL experience. The defensemen generally played strongly, particularly the less-discussed pair, while the top four faced difficulty obtaining favorable matchups on the road.

The speaker described the team as confident, prepared and experienced, including difficult lessons from earlier playoff runs. He said consistency, repetition, pressure management and the increasing importance of speed would shape their success in the Stanley Cup finals. Filip Forsberg was praised for developing through increased opportunity into a mature leader and difference-maker.

U.S. stock indexes fell as Trump threatened a 100% tariff on China starting November 1, reviving trade-war concerns. The S&P 500 closed Friday 1.60% lower at 6,212.69, down 3.33% over two days from Thursday’s record high. Futures pointed to a 0.5% rebound, with resistance at 6,330 and support at 6,280. After losing 2.36% last week, the decline was viewed as consolidation following an advance from April lows, though a deeper correction remains possible. AAII sentiment was 40.3% bullish and 33.0% bearish, while the VIX reached 21.90, its highest since June 23.

Crude fell 2.79% Friday and another 2.1% after OPEC+ agreed to raise September output by 547,000 barrels per day. Increased supply may pressure prices, but threats of U.S. tariffs on countries buying Russian crude could offset surpluses. Weak jobs and PMI data also raised fuel-demand concerns. The outlook emphasized earnings, macroeconomic risks, careful position management, and potentially greater defensive positioning.

Two calculations determine the required output capacitance: one for the maximum allowable output voltage deviation during a worst-case load transient, and one for output voltage ripple; the larger result is selected. For 2% target ripple and 2.5% maximum allowable deviation, at least 1.3 mF is required, with derating considered for aging, temperature, and DC bias. For space-grade designs, radiation-induced single event transients may require additional capacitance; the example used about 2.3 mF total.

An optional output filter of an additional inductor and small ceramic capacitor can further reduce output noise and ripple without greatly increasing size or component count. Its resonant frequency should be above the target crossover frequency but well below the switching frequency and the ESR zero of the bulk output capacitance; Equations 66–68 determine these parameters, and Equations 69–70 address damping peaking with a resistor.

Cycle-by-cycle current limiting begins near 35 A output current, giving about 45% margin over the 24.25 A peak inductor current. Primary current is sensed at CS_ILIM, so the turns ratio must be included when sizing the sense resistor; a 1:100 current sense transformer steps down the primary current to derive RCS.

Japan’s hunt killed 333 minke whales, including 128 females, 122 pregnant whales and 114 juveniles. The ICJ ruled in 2014 that “research whaling” masked commercial hunting; Japan cut its quota from 900 to 333.

Congress convened in Philadelphia despite a contagious illness that had raised the possibility of relocating the National Legislature. Concern was expressed about the constitutional difficulty of postponing the meeting and the inconvenience and expense such a move would cause.

Domestic tranquility, favorable harvests, agricultural and commercial prosperity, and civil and religious liberty were praised, but peace in Europe and security for American citizens and property had not yet been restored. American envoys to the French Republic reached Holland and then proceeded to Paris to negotiate on terms compatible with the safety, honor, and interests of the United States.

The address stressed the need to protect American commerce and prepare the country for defense. Continuing European conflict, declining respect for treaties, and increased depredations made unprotected commerce vulnerable to plunder, while commerce remained essential to national prosperity. The previously recommended precautionary measures were therefore considered increasingly necessary.

Spain had not fully implemented the treaty withdrawing its troops from U.S. territory or begun demarcating the boundary, requiring continued readiness to receive the posts and survey the limits. Foreign agents were also attempting to alienate Indian nations from the United States and prepare them for war, suggesting legislation prescribing punishment for such offenses.

Commissioners were addressing several treaty disputes. The St. Croix River boundary survey remained incomplete, with a final decision expected after a June meeting in Providence. British prewar debt claims and American claims for vessel losses were being examined; compensation awarded to Americans had been paid, while U.S. compensation obligations to British subjects required provision. Spanish claims arising from wartime seizures were also under renewed consideration.

French and Spanish seizures of American vessels had created substantial consular expenses and hardship for stranded sailors, including the sick. Congress was urged to revise the consular act, strengthen provisions for sailors’ support and return, and authorize consuls to inspect registers and sea letters to detect fraudulent use of the U.S. flag.

The address also called attention to national debts and taxes, recommending that defense and government be financed as far as possible through immediate taxes rather than loans to prevent excessive public debt. In closing, it described Europe as singular and threatening and pledged the executive’s zealous cooperation with measures needed to preserve national honor, safety, and prosperity.

A July 17, 2001 email from Ann Schmidt compiled media coverage of Enron and related energy issues.

California Secretary of State Bill Jones urged state authorities to investigate whether seven energy consultants had conflicts of interest through stockholdings and whether exemptions from financial-disclosure rules were lawful. The London Metal Exchange fined Enron Metals £190,000, or $264,000, for persistent failures to deliver warrants on time and enter trades into its matching system. Enron admitted the violations and said it had taken steps to remedy its compliance systems.

Terremark Worldwide reported a $103.9 million fiscal-year loss and auditor concerns that recurring losses and a liquidity deficit could threaten its continued operation. The company sought additional financing for expansion of its Miami data-exchange facility and planned data centers abroad.

A California Senate committee was expected to drop a contempt charge against Enron if the company provided financial information and accepted the committee’s confidentiality agreement. Enron had sued to block the committee’s subpoena and had also raised possible lawsuits against other market participants.

SmartMoney.com investors described a year of market declines and technology-stock losses. Panel members increasingly diversified into sectors such as energy, utilities, financials, retail and health care, expressed modest return expectations, and criticized securities analysts who retained bullish ratings during the Nasdaq decline.

The Alliance for Retail Energy Markets opposed California legislation that would restrict direct electricity access until at least 2003. It said the measure would protect Southern California Edison’s monopoly, undermine competitive contracts and could force customers back to utility-provided power at high prices.

Dutch electricity traders urged the market watchdog to require generators to disclose plant outages, citing spot prices that rose from around €35 per megawatt-hour to as much as €1,200 amid limited supply and suspicions of withheld outage information. Generators opposed disclosure as commercially sensitive, while the watchdog said it was considering possible measures.

The Oregonian reported that Portland General Electric and Avista Energy faced $611 million in refund claims from Northwest utilities that said California’s energy crisis drove unfair prices under bilateral contracts. The passage outlines defensive fundamentals and team concepts for disrupting a Power Offense built around continuous screening. Because defenders caught on screens can leave open shots, players must understand how to disrupt down and base screens. “Show and Recover” is preferred to switching: the screener’s defender shows to force the shooter wide, then quickly recovers, while the chaser pressures the shooter and the on-ball defender pushes the ballhandler toward the sideline. Defenders also use contact switches, physical denial, post positioning, weakside packing, and possible double teams against post mismatches.

“All Out SOS Disruption” has the defense initiate action, push the ballhandler toward the sideline, invert to keep bigs inside, deny screens and passes, and trap a wing shooter. As the ball moves, defenders rotate into help positions, deny post passes and reversals, close out to shooters, and trap ballhandlers according to their actions.

Quantum-correlated pairs underpin quantum communication, computation, and metrology, while phonons offer a promising solid-state platform because they can coherently interact with other quantum systems. The paper presents a method for generating degenerate quantum-correlated phonon pairs from an optomechanical crystal nanobeam cavity by engineering an effective high-order optomechanical nonlinearity. Simultaneous optical pulses at \(\omega_a \pm \omega_m\) drive cavity-enhanced Stokes and anti-Stokes Raman scattering, combining two-mode-squeezing and beam-splitter interactions in one pulse. Analogous to SPDC, the effective spontaneous four-wave-mixing process can generate photon pairs \(|20\rangle\) or phonon pairs \(|02\rangle\). Pulse-duration weight engineering adjusts the relevant interaction terms. The phonon pair is retrieved with a second red-detuned pulse and evaluated using the Cauchy–Schwarz inequality to distinguish quantum correlations from classical behavior. The results demonstrate that equivalent high-order nonlinearity can be engineered under pulsed operation, supporting phonon-state manipulation for mechanical quantum computing.

Since Florida Gov. Critics also say changes such as reinstating grades and reducing narrative evaluations are eroding New College’s distinctive traditions. With the governor term-limited, some are discussing possible privatization, reversing the college’s 1975 transfer from private to state control. Faculty and alumni remain divided, though supporters of privatization see it as a possible alternative to closure within one to three years. Several contacted officials and the college did not respond to comment requests.

The TPS7H500x-SP family consists of radiation-hardness-assured, fixed-frequency, peak-current-mode PWM controllers for space-grade DC-DC converters. An internal oscillator initiates the gate-drive output, while externally sensed switch current is compared with a stepped-down COMP voltage to turn the switch off. The controllers require external gate drivers, support switching frequencies up to 2 MHz, and suit GaN-based buck, flyback, forward, active-clamp forward, push-pull, and full-bridge converters.

A TPS7H5001-SP example implements a 500-kHz, 5-V synchronous push-pull GaN converter. Selected values include a 205-kΩ timing resistor, 10-kΩ/1.4-kΩ output-feedback divider, 25-ns dead time using 20.5-kΩ resistors, 49.9-kΩ leading-edge blank-time resistor, 33-nF soft-start capacitor providing about 7.5 ms, and a 0.47-µH output inductor. The transformer uses a 2.5 turns ratio and 40-µH primary inductance. Primary and synchronous-rectifier GaN FETs are rated at 170 V and 80 V, respectively; a parallel Schottky diode can reduce soft-start and dead-time losses. An RCD clamp, 7.5-Ω current-sense resistor, 1:100 current-sense transformer, 3.3-nF hiccup capacitor, Type 2A compensation network, and 102-kΩ slope-compensation resistor are specified.

At least 1.3 mF of output capacitance is required for ripple and load transients, but 2.3 mF is used for additional radiation-induced single-event-transient mitigation. The implementation uses seven 330-µF polymer tantalum capacitors and may include a filtered output stage. Cycle-by-cycle limiting starts near 35 A, providing about 45% margin over the 24.25-A peak inductor current at maximum load.

The controllers operate from 4–14 V and require at least a 0.1-µF bypass capacitor. Layout guidance emphasizes separating feedback and control signals from noisy power paths, minimizing switch-node copper and high-di/dt loop areas, joining analog and power grounds at one point, using short and wide current traces, and placing filtering, compensation, and sensing components near their associated pins. The August 2024 revision updated package options, CFP layout guidance, documentation, radiation resources, and support information.

The study demonstrates a sub-pixel shift-and-add reconstruction method for improving the angular information and signal-to-noise ratio of electron backscatter diffraction patterns acquired with a direct electron detector. Experiments used a 256 × 256-pixel Timepix-based TruePix detector with 55 μm pixels, 20 keV landing energy, electron counting, and a 19.4 keV energy threshold on a [001]-oriented silicon crystal.

Patterns from a 50 × 60 map with 3 μm spacing were registered and warped to account for translation, rotation, and scale before summation. Fourier-domain signal-to-noise measurements showed that reconstruction improved the ratio from approximately 30 to 70 at an effective exposure time of one second, exceeding patterns acquired with an equivalent dose or through frame integration. The reconstructed pattern captured fine band and higher-order Laue-zone features comparable to a camera-retracted reference and a BWKD simulation. Tenfold upsampling produced a 2560 × 2560-pixel image with improved corner quality.

The method requires a common orientation and lattice across the mapped region but no hardware modification. The authors identify possible alternatives for real samples, including large single grains, subpixel stage movements, detector-image shifts, point-spread-function estimation, and HR-EBSD-based registration. The reconstructed patterns may support improved indexing, strain and lattice-rotation analysis, unit-cell characterization, centrosymmetry assessment, and resolution of pseudosymmetry-related indexing issues.
