Based on a 2022 California Department of Education data request, interviews with staff from 12 school districts, a literature review, and the author’s experience, the report examines newcomer education in California. Newcomers are students who recently arrived in U.S. schools, but definitions vary from their first months to several years. Most have limited English proficiency, come from socioeconomically disadvantaged backgrounds, and may have experienced trauma. They differ substantially from the broader English learner population and often need additional academic, social-emotional, material, and mental-health support.

California schools lack consistent expertise, resources, systems, community connections, and funding for newcomers, contributing to low graduation and college/career readiness, particularly for students entering high school. Federal rulings—Lau v. Nichols, Castañeda v. Pickard, and Plyler v. Doe—guarantee English learners and immigrant minors appropriately tailored public education. Although California districts appear to comply with Lau and Plyler, many may not meet Castañeda’s requirements because they lack properly staffed and supported language programs.

Title III data are the only publicly available district-level newcomer data in California and do not include immigration status. In 2020–21, California counted 151,996 Title III immigrant students, or 2.5% of its K–12 enrollment. Fifty-eight percent attended schools in five urban counties, and about half of local educational agencies enrolled fewer than 21 newcomers. Sixty-seven percent of newcomers were socioeconomically disadvantaged, 43% spoke Spanish at home, and roughly nine in ten were classified as English learners, whose English proficiency was substantially lower than that of the average English learner. Only 19% were in high school. No statewide data exist for students with interrupted or limited formal education, although research cited in the report estimates they constitute 4% to 20% of English learners in various contexts. Oakland Unified’s locally developed system distinguishes newcomers by arrival year and identifies students with interrupted formal education.

California’s education funding and state instructional capacity are comparatively limited. The state ranked 33rd in adjusted per-pupil spending and 43rd in funding effort, while having the nation’s highest teacher-to-student ratio. Local Control Funding Formula supplements recognize English learner and socioeconomic needs but do not count a student twice for both. Late-arriving newcomers can also lose first-year supplemental funding because funding is calculated at census day. The state-funded, $5 million CalNEW program provides community liaisons and academic, family, and basic-needs support through schools. The $9.7 million Opportunities for Youth initiative provides case management, mentoring, navigation, and wellness services to unaccompanied undocumented minors; between October 2020 and March 2022, it served 665 youth and 532 households.

Federal funds supplement California district funding. California received approximately $142.7 million in Title III funding for 2022–23, but $5.6 million was reserved for the Title III Immigrant Student Program. Because eligibility depended on enrollment growth, only 34,041 of the state’s 151,996 Title III immigrant students were supported, leaving 77.6% outside the grant. Separate refugee funding supported 5,643 students, including $9 million for Afghan students; funding and participation for Ukrainian students were less clear.

Effective newcomer programs require specialized instruction, particularly during the first year and at the secondary level. Models include newcomer classes or schools, comprehensive-school programs, modified schedules that accommodate work, and additional learning time for students with interrupted schooling. Instruction should integrate English and grade-level content, use translanguaging, emphasize oral language, and promote daily collaboration. Schools need accessible curricula, teacher training, and planning time to adapt content and create scaffolds. Welcoming environments, cultural orientation, extracurricular activities, leadership opportunities, comprehensive intake, careful placement, and transcript articulation are also important. Standardized assessments and English learner accountability measures do not adequately capture newcomer needs or growth and may misrepresent district performance.

Family engagement and partnerships with government, nonprofit, and faith-based organizations are essential for addressing legal services, housing, food, health care, and mental health. Organizations such as Internationals Network for Public Schools provide specialized newcomer schools and programs, while community partnerships connect students and families with services and support stable attendance and academic progress.

The report recommends a collaborative, multisector approach funded through federal, state, and philanthropic resources. State actions include establishing newcomer-education leadership, coordinating CDE and CDSS, collaborating with national partners, adding newcomers and students with interrupted formal education to state data systems, sustaining Opportunities for Youth, recalculating LCFF funding at P-2 for late arrivals, incorporating newcomers in instructional frameworks, investing in open curricula and research, and advocating for federal data inclusion and removal of the Title III enrollment-growth requirement.

The passage describes four SOS midcourt disruption scenarios—Red Same, Red Opposite, Red Rover 4, and Red Rover 5—used briefly to change tempo, create easy baskets, disrupt half-court offense, and take the ball from a good penetrating point guard. Initial traps differ: X1 and X3 in Red Same, X2 and X1 in Red Opposite, X4 and X1 in Red Rover 4, and X5 and X1 in Red Rover 5. X1 pressures O1 toward the sideline checkpoint, while other defenders establish Triangle “I” and SNUGGLE positions to deny passing lanes.

When O1 passes to O2, defenders rotate to nearby offensive players as the ball leaves the passer’s hands. X2 closes on O2, X1 denies the return pass, and another defender sprints toward high-post O5. Final matchups front O4, maintain contact SNUGGLE denials on O1 and O5, and place X3 in a low helpside “I” position. Red Same and Red Opposite also allow coach-selected “Base Go I” or “Base Go Red” after O2 penetrates and “Post Front” rotations when O4 receives the ball. Red Opposite adds a SMOTHER of O2’s post vision.

Astronomers discovered MOA-2016-BLG-227Lb, a roughly 2.8-Jupiter-mass exoplanet, using gravitational microlensing and follow-up observations from several telescopes. The planet orbits at about 1.67 AU around a probable M- or K-dwarf star of roughly 0.29 solar masses, likely in the Galactic bulge around 21,000 light-years away. Its radius and orbital period remain undetermined. Combining light-curve analysis with Keck adaptive-optics imaging and Bayesian analysis of possible excess-flux contamination, the team concluded that the system likely hosts a gas giant around an M/K dwarf and ruled out a G-dwarf host. The findings were published April 6, 2017, on arXiv. Researchers recommend further observations with Hubble, Keck adaptive optics, JWST, GMT, TMT, and ELT to characterize the system.

Recruiters and hiring experts caution that AI-generated job descriptions are often generic, overly long, and missing company-specific, compensation, and benefits information. They recommend using AI only as a supplement after managers clarify their needs through thoughtful internal discussion, with one cybersecurity CEO using it to identify overlooked skills and improve a draft.

The court found the defendant not guilty of occupying premises without a certificate of occupancy. Although the one-room extension was built contrary to approved plans and intended for occupancy, the People failed to prove that anyone actually occupied it. The original certificate remained valid for the house but did not cover the extension. The information was dismissed on both the law and the facts.

After two losses to Detroit, the coach said his team generated chances but failed to capitalize, while Detroit scored timely goals and created pucks around the net. He believed a goal followed a failed puck clearance involving a stick-lift that officials ruled was not a hook. He praised the team’s effort and confrontations involving Sidney Crosby but said players reviewed video and stayed focused. With Phil Boucher absent, the staff may adjust the power play. For Game 3, the plan is to dictate the pace, spend more time in the offensive zone, improve execution and faceoff support, and avoid focusing on the need to win or reacting emotionally to deficits.

Apple is in late-stage talks to acquihire Prompt AI, an 11-person computer-vision startup founded in 2023, bringing aboard selected employees and technology. Prompt leaders told employees that those not joining Apple would receive reduced pay and be encouraged to seek other roles, while employees were asked not to disclose the talks. Investors are expected to receive some money but not be made whole. The startup raised a $5 million seed round led by AIX and Abstract Ventures and was reportedly approached by xAI and Neuralink. Co-founders are CEO Tete Xiao and President Trevor Darrell.

Prompt’s Seemour app helps connected home cameras identify people, pets, animals and objects and provide alerts and descriptions of unusual activity. The app is being retired, and user data will be deleted. Prompt’s talent and technology are expected to support Apple’s HomeKit division, aligning with Apple’s preference for smaller, targeted talent acquisitions.

The passage contrasts American freedom with Communism, citing Andrei Sakharov’s view that the United States is the historically determined leader of the pluralist, free society. It argues that America should uphold its ideals, assist refugees, share responsibility for their care, and address the conditions that cause people to flee.

It then reports George Bush’s trip to Japan and China at Ronald Reagan’s request. Bush met senior leaders to exchange views on international issues. Reagan emphasized Japan’s importance to Asian peace and U.S. trade and said Japanese leaders favored a strong, reliable U.S. partnership. The China talks clarified both countries’ positions, and Reagan pledged to develop full diplomatic relations carefully while protecting U.S. interests.

The University of Toledo jokingly pledged on Twitter to replace its Rocky the Rocket mascot with Shrek if the post received 500,000 retweets. After about 100,000, it deleted the tweet, saying the response was distracting, though a Shrek-themed Rocky costume had been considered. The viral campaign prompted backlash and raised potential copyright issues involving DreamWorks Animation.

PBOC adviser Huang Yiping proposed a 6–7 percent growth target for this year, saying a wider range would allow more focus on reforms if employment remains stable. Xi Jinping aims for average growth of at least 6.5 percent through 2020. Policy priorities include addressing debt and unviable “zombie companies,” shifting growth toward consumption, controlling financial risks and asset bubbles, and deepening supply-side reforms. Xi is reportedly open to growth below 6.5 percent, while Yao Wei expects the longer-term target to be lowered.

ING no longer expects another Bank of England rate cut this year, citing lower inflation and higher taxes as conditions for further easing in 2026. Markets price little more than one 25-basis-point cut by next April and may be underpricing the remaining easing cycle.

CompareCards presents a data-driven comparison of low- and 0% APR credit cards, noting that long promotional periods can reduce interest costs and that consumers who pay balances in full and on time generally come out ahead. It explains fixed and variable APRs and states that variable rates may follow the prime rate. Featured offers include a Discover card with 15 months of 0% APR, 5% rotating quarterly cash back, 1% elsewhere, and a first-year cash-back match; Bank of America cards offering 15-month 0% APR periods, customizable cash rewards, and travel points; Citi options with paid-purchase cash back and 18-month balance-transfer offers; and Capital One cards with 15 months of 0% APR, flexible rewards, and no annual fees on the VentureOne and Quicksilver. The article says it objectively evaluates more than 100 cards from over 50 issuers and discloses that compensation from listed companies does not affect its ratings or reviews.

Students and parents honored Holy Family School principal Sister Kevin Berdis before the school’s closure. Under the Erie Catholic Diocese’s plan, Mother Teresa Academy will replace the school in the former St. Peter Cathedral building in January.

More than 30,000 security personnel, including 23,000 police, 6,000 firefighters and several thousand private agents, will protect Tour de France riders and spectators, with extra attention to mountain finishes such as Alpe d’Huez. UCI head David Lappartient urged calm and respect for the decision clearing Chris Froome of doping suspicions, rejecting calls for violence. Froome, cleared after an abnormal salbutamol finding at the Tour of Spain, is a favorite for a fifth title; a win would make him the first man in 20 years to achieve a Giro-Tour double in one season.

Toshiba ESS and Toshiba JSW announced a 200,000 MW turbine output-capacity milestone, targeting 300,000 MW and beyond. Toshiba JSW provides full EPC solutions for thermal plants in India and nearby regions.

Apple Inc.’s February 17, 2020 Form 8-K reported that it issued an update to second-quarter guidance for the period ending March 28, 2020. The update was attached as Exhibit 99.1 and was not deemed “filed” except if expressly incorporated by reference. The report was signed by CFO Luca Maestri.

The World Long Drive Association will hold the inaugural Atlantic City Boardwalk Bash at Atlantic City Country Club on June 5, its third competition in six weeks and first partnered with the New Jersey Casino Reinvestment Development Authority. Golf Channel will broadcast the event live from 6–8 p.m. ET.

The 36-player Open Division will be ranked by world long-drive standings and led by No. 1 Justin James and Will Hogue, who is seeking a third consecutive victory. The 16-player Women’s Division includes 2018 winners Alexis Belton and Phillis Meti and five-time defending champion Sandra Carlborg. Open qualifiers will compete in four pods, with the top four from each pod advancing to the Round of 16 and eight players reaching a live single-elimination match-play bracket. Women’s competitors will compete in two groups before eight players advance to quarterfinals.

Coverage will use six cameras, a “DXL Big Drive to Beat” graphic and Trackman data to display club speed, ball speed, apex and flight. Jonathan Coachman will provide play-by-play, with analysis from Art Sellinger and reports and interviews by Jerry Foltz. Real-time scoring and highlights will also be available through WorldLongDrive.com and social media.

The 2018 WLDA schedule includes events in the United States and internationally sanctioned stops in Germany, Japan, New Zealand, South Africa and the United Kingdom, plus an international qualifier for the September World Long Drive Championship.

An Enron email chain forwarded a press-conference announcement and a class-action complaint filed in California Superior Court, San Diego County, on behalf of retail electricity customer Pamela R. Gordon. The suit names Reliant Energy, Southern Company, NRG Energy, Dynegy, AES, Williams Energy, Duke Energy North America, and 100 unidentified defendants. It alleges that, beginning May 22, 2000, the generators and traders used confidential real-time capacity and transmission data, withheld supply, coordinated outages, exported and reparked power, and manipulated bidding and transmission flows to inflate California wholesale electricity prices. Gordon seeks to represent roughly 1.2 million SDG&E customers and alleges multi-billion-dollar overcharges. The complaint cites regulatory findings that prices were unjust and unreasonable and that market power was exercised. Claims include violations of the Cartwright Act, California Unfair Trade Practices Act, Consumers Legal Remedies Act, and unconscionability. Requested relief includes class certification, treble or statutory damages, interest, fees, injunctions, and disgorgement. Mark Palmer circulated the filing to Enron colleagues and told reporter Jason Leopold that Enron’s related suit would look the same.

Bald eagles have returned to La Crosse and the Mississippi River, becoming an annual spring sight and conservation success. After DDT decimated them, they remained endangered until 2007. Protected habitat and plentiful fish helped nesting pairs rise from one to over 300. Young eagles lack white heads until about age five.
A car bomb and gunmen attacked a Kabul ministry compound, but key buildings were not breached. One policeman was killed, five wounded, and Daesh claimed responsibility.

Residents of Oshiyie, led by Abusuapayin Paul Ameni Annoh, petitioned the Inspector General of Police to intervene in unrest linked to an 18-year chieftaincy dispute between the Nii Afadi Annoh Royal Family and Kofi Akrashie factions. The dispute is before the Ngleshie Alata Traditional Council’s Arbitration Committee. The petition alleges that factional violence has led to assaults, injuries, one death, arrests, destruction of properties and fishing equipment, and attacks on people returning to Oshiyie, including parents of students benefiting from free SHS. It also claims police investigations have unfairly targeted innocent members of the Nii Afadi Annoh faction and that several suspects remain in custody without bail. The petitioners attribute the violence to the influence of land guard Adjei Brown, express distrust of police investigators, and call for authorities to address the violence, arrests and perceived mistreatment.

The Trump administration is considering selling parts of the $1.6 trillion federal student-loan portfolio while seeking to close the Education Department and move its loans. Such sales must not cost taxpayers money, and private loans may lack federal protections, prompting concern among advocates as more than 45 million Americans hold federal loans.

Custom essay writing services offer affordable, high-quality papers and research assignments with minimal concerns about quality or plagiarism. TermPapersWriter is promoted as a recommended site for purchasing custom essays, with services handling research, writing, and formatting.

Backtesting simulates trading strategies against historical market data to assess potential profitability, risk, and resilience without risking real capital. It helps traders define goals and entry and exit parameters, select suitable assets and market conditions, refine risk management, and build disciplined, consistent strategies. Reliable testing requires accurate, comprehensive, representative historical data covering diverse market conditions.

Overfitting and bias can distort results. Traders should use diverse datasets, separate in-sample development from out-of-sample validation, perform sensitivity and statistical analyses, incorporate realistic transaction costs and slippage, clean data carefully, and include delisted or failed assets to reduce survivorship bias. Look-ahead bias, inadequate samples, premature abandonment of a system, and a lack of a written plan are also warned against. Common evaluation measures include net profit, trade counts, percent profitability, Sharpe ratio, maximum drawdown, and other risk-adjusted metrics.

Backtesting should be combined with paper or demo trading, forward performance testing, scenario analysis, walk-forward testing, market replay, real-time market analysis, and ongoing monitoring. It supports portfolio optimization and algorithmic, high-frequency, options, futures, CFD, forex, cryptocurrency, equity, and derivative strategy evaluation, while accounting for asset-specific factors such as leverage, implied volatility, contract characteristics, market volatility, liquidity, and trading expenses.

Software selection should consider user-friendliness, customization, historical-data integration, and performance-metric analysis; examples include no-code TrendSpider and MetaTrader’s broader trading tools. Machine-learning methods such as deep learning and cross-validation can support predictive model evaluation, while regulatory practices require fair and nonmisleading performance representation. Positive backtest results can inform decisions and build confidence, but they cannot guarantee future success because markets change and backtests may omit behavioral and psychological influences.

The second annual Addiction & Recovery Awareness MusicFest will run July 7 from noon to 10 p.m. at Buck Miller Arena in Westminster, featuring local musicians, food vendors, and addiction and recovery speakers. General admission is $20 and VIP passes are $50. Brandon Novak will be the main speaker, with Tim Ryan also appearing. Proceeds will benefit Rising Above Addiction, the Push HOPE Project, and the Up and Out Foundation. The event provides a sober social option while raising funds for treatment and supporting people in recovery. Last year’s festival raised more than $6,000 and drew nearly 600 attendees. Carroll County recorded 37 drug and alcohol overdose deaths in the first five months of 2018.

Assistant U.S. Attorney Will Rosenzweig was fired from the Southern District of Florida after conservatives surfaced past blog posts allegedly written by him criticizing Donald Trump and his supporters. The posts, attributed to his private “Hosts of Error” blog, included claims that Trump was “mentally unfit” and “an institutional terrorist.” Rosenzweig worked on complex economic crimes cases and joined the U.S. attorney’s office in 2020. His dismissal followed other federal prosecutor removals connected to the Trump Justice Department, while former special counsel Jack Smith criticized attacks on career prosecutors and the rule of law.

The passage describes NVIDIA’s 2025 RTX Blackwell architecture and GeForce RTX 50 Series technologies. GDDR7 memory on RTX 50 Series boards includes enhanced CRC for RAS and always-on, die-level ECC with single-bit error correction, without a performance penalty or software toggle. These GPUs also support EDR technology.

Fifth-generation Tensor Cores support FP16, BF16, TF32, INT8, FP8, and new FP4 and FP6 operations. FP4 uses less than half the memory of FP16 and provides more than twice the previous generation’s performance with minimal quality loss using NVIDIA’s TensorRT Model Optimizer. The FLUX.dev model falls from more than 23GB of VRAM at FP16 to less than 10GB at FP4, enabling it to run on more GeForce GPUs.

Fourth-generation RT Cores double ray-triangle intersection throughput and include an Opacity Micromap Engine, Mega Geometry support, a Triangle Cluster Intersection Engine, and hardware-accelerated Linear Swept Spheres. Mega Geometry uses cluster-level acceleration structures and persistent partitioned top-level structures to reduce BVH-building costs, support large object counts, and accelerate dynamic level-of-detail systems and subdivision surfaces. It is available through DirectX 12, Vulkan, and OptiX and supports RTX GPUs from Turing onward. Linear Swept Spheres render common hair use cases about twice as fast as DOTS while using roughly one-fifth the VRAM. SER 2.0 has twice the reorder-logic efficiency and greater precision, improving ray-tracing and neural-shading workloads.

The programmable AI Management Processor uses a dedicated RISC-V processor to schedule GPU contexts, reducing reliance on the system CPU and lowering latency. It coordinates graphics, AI inference, and other workloads to improve frame pacing, multitasking, and time to first response.

Blackwell adds 4:2:2 H.264 and HEVC encode/decode support. Its ninth-generation NVENC improves AV1 and HEVC quality by 5% BD-BR PSNR, with an AV1 Ultra High Quality mode adding another 5% and potentially 15% combined. The RTX 5090 supports three encoders and two decoders, while the improved NVDEC doubles H.264 decoding speed. DisplayPort 2.1b provides up to 80 Gbps through UHBR 20, supporting 8K at 165Hz or 4K at 480Hz with DSC.

Blackwell Max-Q improvements include advanced clock, power, and voltage-rail gating, separate control of GPU-core and memory power, and faster frequency transitions. Clocks adjust to workloads 1,000 times faster than earlier architectures, and the deepest sleep state is entered ten times faster than on Ada. These changes can produce power savings of up to 50% in small-language-model inference scenarios.

DLSS 4 introduces Multi Frame Generation, which can create up to three additional frames for each traditionally rendered frame. Its frame-generation model is 40% faster, uses 30% less VRAM, and runs once per rendered frame, while enhanced Flip Metering moves pacing logic to the display engine. New transformer-based models with twice as many parameters improve Super Resolution, Ray Reconstruction, and Deep Learning Anti-Aliasing, providing greater temporal stability, reduced ghosting, improved lighting and motion detail, and fewer ray-tracing artifacts.

The Cooperative Vectors API and Slang features allow graphics shaders to access Tensor Cores for neural rendering. Proposed applications include RTX Neural Materials, Neural Texture Compression, Neural Radiance Cache, RTX Skin, and RTX Neural Faces. Neural Materials approximate complex optical models, Neural Texture Compression can reduce texture memory substantially, Neural Radiance Cache infers indirect-lighting bounces, RTX Skin provides real-time subsurface scattering, and Neural Faces uses generative AI to reconstruct realistic faces from rasterized images and pose data.

The architecture family includes GB202, used by the RTX 5090, with 24,576 CUDA Cores, 192 RT Cores, and 768 Tensor Cores; GB203, used by the RTX 5080 and 5070 Ti, with 10,752 CUDA Cores, 84 RT Cores, and 336 Tensor Cores; and GB205, used by the RTX 5070, with 6,400 CUDA Cores, 50 RT Cores, and 200 Tensor Cores. NVIDIA states that specifications are accurate as of the publication date, may change without notice, and are provided without warranties; products are not authorized for medical, military, aerospace, space, life-support, or other applications where failure could cause injury, death, or property or environmental damage.

Creditors of a corporation have priority over stockholders, and a stockholder-director cannot retain personal profits from corporate transactions that diminish the corporation’s assets or increase its liabilities without valuable consideration. Accordingly, Gerard B. Allen’s 40-percent bonus on 75 shares was treated as unpaid stock, and his liability arising from second-mortgage bonds issued in connection with stock calls was measured by the $15,904.59 he realized from their sale.

The court also held that a stockholder’s specific statutory liability is fixed when the creditor’s motion is filed after written notice, relating back to service of the notice, rather than when execution against the corporation is returned unsatisfied. Allen owned 741 shares when execution against the corporation was returned but only 24 shares when the motion was filed. Because the Circuit Court used the earlier ownership date, its judgment was reversed and the case remanded.

The coach describes a conscientious, talented first-year professional adjusting to the NHL schedule after college and a long playoff run. His minutes were reduced to improve his productivity, help him regain his legs, and build confidence. The team emphasizes playing the right way: winning puck battles, working the boards, making smart line changes, defending effectively, and avoiding forced, high-risk plays. Coaches focus on scoring opportunities, efficient puck exits, a fast game, video analysis, detailed preparation, and adjustments during a seven-game series.

The coach praises Sid’s leadership and ability to put young players at ease. The team’s depth allows players to be moved among lines for balance and tougher matchups. Phil and Geno are recognized for scoring and passing, but are urged to improve their details away from the puck. Nick’s penalty-kill sacrifices inspire the team, while Willie contributes energy, skating, forechecking, physical play, and wing versatility. Overall, the group is characterized as resilient, competitive, and committed to supporting one another.

The 3-3-5 is a high-risk, high-reward defense emphasizing pressure, speed, and athletic players. It uses three defensive linemen, three inside linebackers, and five defensive backs, and is also called the 3-5-3 or 3-3 stack. It may be used as a base defense or sub-package and relies on fast players, with larger linebackers sometimes playing defensive line and larger defensive backs filling linebacker roles.

Its primary strength is flexibility. The same pre-snap shell can disguise Cover 1 and Cover 3, create multiple blitz variations, add rushers from different positions, and adjust easily to formations. Its main weakness is vulnerability at the edges against running plays such as sweep and outside zone. Offenses can attack the seams in passing and the edges in running; four vertical routes challenge Cover 3, while trips formations can create isolated receivers and reduce defenders in the box.

Common blitzes include the Sam Blitz, which slants the defensive line and sends a stacked linebacker or overhang off the edge, and the SAW Blitz, which sends two stacked linebackers while pinching the line to form a Bear front. In Cover 1, corners cover outside receivers, overhangs cover the second receivers, and stacked linebackers split the backfield while the third plays a crossing-route “Rat” role. In Cover 3, corners and the free safety take deep thirds, overhangs cover the flats, and stacked linebackers cover curls and the hook.

Joe Lee Dunn is credited with inventing the defense. Matt Campbell and Iowa State popularized it, while Tony Gibson and Tim Racki have also used it successfully.

The patent application concerns dry, solvent-free, self-supporting electrode films for energy-storage devices. The films combine active material with a fibrillizable binder, such as PTFE, and a microparticulate non-fibrillizable binder having a median particle size of about 0.5–40 µm, including cellulose or derivatives such as carboxymethylcellulose (CMC) or polyvinylidene fluoride (PVDF). The microparticulate binder may constitute up to 50 wt.% of the binder. Embodiments describe free-standing films and electrodes contacting current collectors for use in lithium-ion batteries and other energy-storage devices.

A disclosed fabrication process reduces non-fibrillizable binder particle size by high-shear processing or pressurized jet milling, then combines it with fibrillizable binder and active material before calendering the mixture into a film. A parallel process nondestructively mixes microparticulate binder with one active material, separately combines fibrillizable binder with another active material under high-shear conditions, and then combines and mills the mixtures before pressing or calendering them. The disclosed processes require no solvents and are intended to improve distribution of film components, strength, cohesiveness, adhesion, processability, and electrical performance while reducing holes, cracks, and surface pits.

Example 1 fabricated dry graphite anodes containing 96 wt.% graphite and 4 wt.% binder, comprising 2% PTFE, 1% CMC, and 1% PVDF. Jet milling reduced CMC median particle size from approximately 70 µm to 10 µm. Milled CMC produced 384 mAh/g discharge capacity and 90.9% first-cycle efficiency, compared with 348 mAh/g and 90.2% for as-received CMC, and was reported to improve cell-to-cell consistency and mitigate film defects. At similar thicknesses, tensile strength increased from 0.936 N with as-received CMC to at least 1.01 N with Resodyne-processed CMC and 1.74 N with jet-milled CMC.

Investing.com reports that the S&P 500 fell more than 3% from Thursday’s high and closed Friday at its lowest level since early July, though futures near 6,300 suggested a Monday rebound. The decline may represent consolidation after an advance from April lows, but a deeper correction and possible topping pattern remain concerns. VIX rose to 21.90, while slightly improved investor sentiment and the absence of strong bearish signals tempered fears.

Oil fell 2.79% Friday and another 2.1% Monday after OPEC+ agreed to raise September output by 547,000 barrels per day. Analysts said increased supply could pressure prices, while threatened U.S. sanctions on Russian oil, weak jobs and PMI data, and tariff uncertainty add further risks. Goldman Sachs forecast $64 oil for Q4 2025.

Other headlines covered AMD’s OpenAI chip deal, a potential S&P 500 bubble scenario, gold above $3,900 per ounce, and dollar strength. The page also promotes a stock screener and includes trading-risk, data-accuracy, and intellectual-property disclaimers.

PDT Partners LLC raised its Northwest Natural Gas stake 1.4% in the second quarter to 19,969 shares, valued at $1.195 million. Bank of New York Mellon, Comerica, Swiss National Bank, UBS Asset Management Americas, and Parametric Portfolio Associates also increased their holdings. Institutional investors and hedge funds own 63.32% of NWN.

Analyst sentiment was mixed: Zacks upgraded the stock to “buy” with a $74 target, BidaskClub downgraded it to “hold,” and Sidoti reaffirmed “buy” with a $75 target. The consensus rating is “hold,” with an average target of $66.

Insiders sold 13,202 shares over three months. VP Grant M. Yoshihara sold 2,000 shares for $132,060, while CEO David Hugo Anderson sold 8,000 shares for $535,760.

Northwest Natural Gas reported quarterly EPS of $0.10, beating the $0.06 estimate, and revenue of $136.24 million versus $78.51 million expected. Revenue rose 37.4% year over year. The company declared a $0.4725 quarterly dividend, representing a $1.89 annualized dividend and a 2.91% yield. It distributes natural gas in Oregon, Washington, and California.

Tesla, Inc.’s Form 10-K for the year ended December 31, 2019 describes a vertically integrated sustainable-energy business focused on designing, developing, manufacturing, selling and leasing electric vehicles, solar systems, energy-storage products and related services. It operates through two reportable segments: automotive and energy generation and storage.

The automotive portfolio includes Model 3, Model Y, Model S and Model X, with Cybertruck, Tesla Semi and a new Tesla Roadster planned. Core competencies include battery and powertrain engineering, vehicle software, Autopilot and Full Self-Driving hardware, neural-network development, over-the-air updates and autonomous-driving technologies. Tesla sells vehicles directly through its website and company-owned stores and galleries and supports them through service centers, Mobile Service technicians, Supercharger stations and other charging infrastructure.

The energy segment includes retrofit solar systems, Solar Roof, Powerwall, Powerpack and Megapack. These products serve residential, commercial, industrial and utility markets and support backup and off-grid power, peak-demand reduction, demand response, renewable-energy integration and grid services. Solar and storage systems receive software and firmware updates remotely. Tesla also provides vehicle warranties, extended service plans, financing and leasing, resale-value guarantees, and an insurance product launched in California in 2019.

Manufacturing is conducted primarily in California’s Bay Area, at Gigafactory Nevada, Gigafactory New York and Gigafactory Shanghai, with Gigafactory Berlin planned. Shanghai began producing Model 3 vehicles in December 2019 and had installed annual capacity for 150,000 vehicles; Tesla was also preparing to add Model Y capacity. Nevada produces battery packs and drive units and assembles Megapack systems. Products rely on extensive global supply chains, and most procured components come from single suppliers, although Tesla maintains alternative sources and safety stock for certain critical parts.

Government incentives supporting Tesla include California manufacturing-equipment tax exclusions, Nevada tax abatements and credits, New York investment and lease arrangements, Shanghai financing, renewable-energy and storage incentives, and federal solar tax credits. The company’s vehicles and energy products are subject to vehicle safety, dealer, battery-transportation, self-driving, solar, utility and environmental regulations. Competition includes internal-combustion, hybrid and electric vehicle manufacturers, energy-storage providers, utilities and solar-installation and financing companies.

Tesla reported 48,016 full-time employees as of December 31, 2019. Principal risks described include manufacturing and production-ramp delays, difficulty scaling service and charging infrastructure, uncertain consumer adoption, supplier disruptions and cost increases, supply-chain complexity, regulatory constraints, and reliance on successful cell-production expansion at Gigafactory Nevada, including continued collaboration with Panasonic.

New York’s Early Intervention Program provides home- and community-based teaching, therapy and other services to children with developmental delays and disabilities from birth through age 3. Despite rising living costs, provider pay has not materially increased in three decades. A standard 30-minute visit received an average reimbursement of $79 in 1994 but only $69 in 2022, and advocates estimate rates would need to rise 240% to regain their original purchasing power. New York cut rates in 2010 and 2011, and a 2022 increase excluded many special educators.

A 2024 funding package included a 5% increase for in-person services and 4% for rural and underserved areas. Federal officials approved the rural increase in late September, but its implementation remained unclear, while the broader increase was still awaiting approval amid Medicaid budget cuts.

Low pay, larger caseloads and extensive unpaid requirements—including travel, paperwork, reporting, missed appointments and preparation—have driven providers out of the field. Therapists commonly earn $50,000 to $70,000 annually, while some former providers found similar jobs paying about $30,000 more. Pay disruptions and a reduction in virtual-service reimbursement have further depleted services, particularly in rural areas, leaving children without therapies and causing developmental regressions.

Providers’ departures have increased delays and threatened timely access to services. New York serves about 70,000 children through a mix of Medicaid, county, state, federal and private-insurance funding. Similar recruitment and compensation problems exist in other states, including Illinois, where speech and physical therapist numbers have fallen. Advocates warn that Medicaid reductions could worsen shortages, though they continue seeking rate increases and alternative service-delivery models. Despite low compensation and administrative burdens, veteran teacher Emily Lengen remains in the field because of her commitment to the children and families she serves.
Pulido's appeal of the Kings County Supreme Court judgment was dismissed, citing People v. Seaberg, 74 NY2d 1.

U.S. adults generally consume more protein than recommended, but research indicates that dietary guidelines inadequately distinguish protein quality. Animal foods such as meat, dairy and eggs generally provide more complete essential amino acid profiles and are digested more efficiently than plant proteins. A randomized trial of 56 adults found greater muscle-protein synthesis after consuming animal-protein foods than plant-protein foods containing guideline-equivalent protein amounts.

Protein quality depends on essential amino acid content and bioavailability, not simply quantity. Layman’s EAA-9 scoring system rates an egg at 15.77 and a tablespoon of peanut butter at 4.04, suggesting that far more peanut butter or beans is needed to match an egg’s benefits. Older adults are particularly vulnerable to inadequate high-quality protein intake, which can contribute to muscle loss, weakness, sarcopenia and falls. One study found 47% greater muscle-protein synthesis after an omnivorous meal than a nutritionally matched vegan meal among adults 65 to 85; some scientists recommend as much as 1.5 grams of protein per kilogram daily for adults 65 and older.

Plant-based diets can still meet protein needs through complementary foods, such as beans with rice, and preparation methods such as soaking, sprouting and fermentation. Nutritionists favor guidelines based on essential amino acids, personalized by demographic group, with most protein obtained from whole foods. The Netherlands’ plant-forward guidance model offers one approach, while athletes and pregnant or breastfeeding people may require additional protein.

A compilation of January 14, 2002 reports covered Enron’s collapse and aftermath. Congressional investigators said an employee warned CEO Kenneth Lay in August 2001 about accounting concerns involving partnerships and Andersen before Enron reported a $1.2 billion equity charge. Rep. John Dingell cited “pretty strong evidence” of insider trading and false accounting, while the Senate Banking Committee scheduled a February hearing. UBS Warburg proposed to acquire Enron’s core trading business without upfront payment, with Enron and its creditors receiving 33% of pretax profits for at least two years, subject to bankruptcy-court approval. Former CEO Jeffrey Skilling’s spokeswoman said he shorted AES stock after resigning and denied using inside information. Other reports examined Enron’s contacts with Bush administration officials, political contributions, Andersen’s destruction of documents, Dabhol Power’s impending closure, BG’s renegotiation of Enron’s Indian assets, and energy traders’ efforts to repair balance sheets and reduce debt. A CNNfn panel discussed the UBS deal, investigations, rising bankruptcies, and uncertainty about the market recovery.

A survey of 2,000 British adults found the average Brit wakes three times nightly; one in ten wakes seven to ten times. Causes include bathroom trips (47%), snoring (41%), losing bed space (25%), aches (19%), nightmares (11%), tossing (10.5%), sleep talking or noises (10%), phone light (10%), anxiety (6%), and a partner reading or watching TV (4.6%). Psychologist Robert Stewart said sleep depends on hygiene and sleep cycles. He recommends consistent bedtimes, limiting food and drink, and avoiding screens in bed. Of five sleep stages, REM is lightest and most likely to prompt stirring; noise, snoring, discomfort, and the sleep environment affect whether people return to sleep.

The analysis concludes that Apple’s shares are overvalued at current levels, based on the company’s growth rates and associated valuation multiples. Apple’s price is near the upper boundary of a long-term ascending channel. Its P/E relative to annual EPS growth exceeds the modeled level, though that relationship is weak. Similar overvaluation appears in EV/EBITDA versus EBITDA growth, EV/operative free cash flow versus its growth, and EV/FCF versus FCF growth; the latter model has the strongest fit. The author therefore considers buying Apple shares at the current price a poor investment decision.

Anthropologist Donald Blakeslee identified limestone boulders in Tami and Greg Norwood’s backyard as ancient Wichita Nation shrines. Carved centuries ago, the stones contain holes, basins, and curved channels that direct poured water between them. He said the functional shrine reflects Wichita beliefs that water connects the sky, earthly, and underground realms and is sacred. Nearby depressions were filled with water and drunk with prayers for successful pregnancies. Blakeslee and Gary McAdams described springs, streams, and cave pools as sacred portals associated with transformation, baptism, purification, and communication with spirits, while noting that these traditions have changed.

A Fourth of July drone show at Travis Air Force Base was postponed to July 5 because forecast 30-mph winds exceeded Intel drones’ 18-mph limit. The 500-drone patriotic display could provide a safer fireworks alternative in wildfire-prone California, while similar Arizona shows proceeded.

The article reviews selected results at the intersection of logic, automata, circuit complexity, and transformer expressivity. Transformers are treated as string-processing models that induce formal languages, enabling their capabilities to be compared with classes such as AC0 and TC0. The discussion assumes unbounded rational or real precision, though many results also hold with polynomial or logarithmic precision.

Formal transformer models compose length-preserving sequence transformations, token and optional position embeddings, and a final acceptance test. Sequence transformations use piecewise-linear functions and attention layers. Softmax attention assigns normalized weights; unique hard attention selects the leftmost maximum-scoring position; and average hard attention averages all maximum-scoring positions. Without masking or position embeddings, transformers recognize only permutation-invariant languages. Strict future masking and position embeddings restore ordering information. Chain-of-thought transformers are excluded because they are Turing-complete.

Transformers with unique hard attention and position embeddings recognize a class strictly contained in AC0, so they cannot recognize languages such as PARITY or MAJ. Conversely, they can express first-order logic over strings extended with monadic numerical predicates. Masked unique-hard-attention transformers without position embeddings coincide with first-order logic and hence star-free languages. These results imply support for regular languages in AC0, recognition of palindromes, and decidable verification for masked models without position embeddings; the latter verification problem is EXPSPACE-complete.

Average-hard-attention transformers can recognize MAJ, and their recognized languages lie within TC0 because averaging enables arithmetic computation. They can express counting LTL extended with unary numerical predicates, while masked models without position embeddings can express the restricted fragment Kt[#]. If TC0 is strictly contained in NC1, such transformers contain all regular languages in TC0. Without masking or position embeddings, average-hard-attention transformers characterize exactly the permutation-invariant languages with semialgebraic Parikh images. Checking whether such a transformer recognizes a nonempty language is undecidable.

Two major limitations remain. Hard-attention expressivity is not yet fully aligned with practical softmax attention: PARITY is recognizable by softmax transformers despite being impossible for unique hard attention, and the precise relationship between average hard and softmax attention is unresolved. Uniform average-hard-attention models are recognized by softmax transformers, as are Kt[#] languages and the permutation-invariant languages with semialgebraic Parikh images. Separately, expressibility does not imply efficient trainability. PARITY is expressible but difficult to train, plausibly because it is sensitive to changing a single token, whereas MAJ is efficiently trainable. The RASP-L conjecture links length generalization to short RASP-L programs, and a formalized version using limit transformers and Kt[#] supports this connection while excluding PARITY and admitting MAJ. The article identifies these and related verification, expressibility, and trainability questions as open problems for the FLaNN community.

Three unusual animal partnerships illustrate unequal natural relationships. Pearlfish live in sea cucumbers’ anuses for protection, emerging at night to hunt; some parasitize their hosts by eating the cucumbers’ gonads. Pistol shrimp and gobies mutually benefit: gobies guard and maintain shared burrows and signal danger, while shrimp clean the gobies and eat parasites; some species also share coloration. Arid bronze azure butterfly larvae chemically mimic queen ants, gaining entry and protection in ant nests, but consume the ants’ young for nourishment.

- **Sycamore Networks:** Williams Communications generated more than 90% of Sycamore’s fiscal 2000 sales, but the customer is buying competing equipment from Ciena and Corvis. Delays in shipping an upgraded SN16000 optical switch contributed to sharply lower revenue expectations, job cuts and warnings of further losses. Sycamore nevertheless reported $1.4 billion in cash and marketable securities. Enron Broadband’s three-year agreement with Sycamore was valued at up to $200 million, though Enron said actual spending was far below that amount.

- **Enron’s Dabhol project:** Enron’s 65%-owned Dabhol Power Co. planned to meet nearly 40 lenders in London on April 23 amid its payment dispute with the Maharashtra State Electricity Board. Dabhol initiated arbitration and conciliation proceedings and invoked a federal payment guarantee. Reports said Maharashtra no longer intended to purchase power from the nearly completed second phase, citing sharply increased costs, while Dabhol maintained that phase one remained operational.

- **Azurix breakup:** Enron-owned Azurix appointed JP Morgan to oversee a breakup, initially seeking to sell its North and South American water interests and German engineering business, Lurgi. Wessex Water was expected to be sold later, potentially to a foreign buyer.

- **Bandwidth trading:** Enron and other bandwidth traders faced excess capacity, falling prices, weak demand, credit and contract-enforcement problems, and unresolved “last-mile” connections. Enron cut 20% of its broadband jobs and reduced planned fiber-network capital spending from $750 million to about $250 million. Analysts nevertheless expected bandwidth trading to develop further within two to three years.

- **Northwestern aluminium industry:** The Bonneville Power Administration’s conservation strategy threatened regional smelters with either two years without agency power or sharply higher electricity rates. About 90% of the region’s 1.6 million-ton annual capacity had already been temporarily closed, and U.S. aluminium output was roughly 30% below the start of 2000.

- **Nevada utility transaction:** Nevada’s public utilities regulator asked the SEC to delay Sierra Pacific Resources’ proposed $3.1 billion purchase of an Oregon utility from Enron because of pending state legislation. Sierra Pacific had planned to finance the acquisition by selling Nevada generating stations.

Other briefs covered eBay’s expansion of Half.com, layoffs at Hewlett-Packard, SportsLine and Tellabs, Covisint’s CEO appointment, VeriSign’s multilingual domain names, allegations concerning Microsoft stock-option advice, and an EU agreement with Microsoft over set-top-box technology.

As Modi campaigns for a liquor ban, the state cabinet set up an 11-member committee, including BMV members, to study the issue by visiting six states and assess impacts elsewhere. A report is due in three months; no new outlets will open, but 712 liquor shops remain, including unsold ones.

The lecture examines gender discrimination and identity, focusing on persistent differences in earnings, promotion, workplace assignments, and family responsibilities. It identifies equality and fairness, economic efficiency, and understanding the development of preferences as major reasons to study these issues.

Although women’s earnings have risen substantially, large gender gaps remain: in 2010, full-time, full-year workers aged 25–69 earned about 72% of men’s mean annual income and 77% of the median, even after controlling for hours and education. Progress has been attributed to reduced educational disparities, technologies such as contraception and dishwashers, a shift from manufacturing and agriculture toward services, stronger regulation, and greater market competition. Blind orchestra auditions appear to have reduced discrimination and increased women’s representation, though incomplete blinding, selective hiring, and small samples complicate the evidence. Audit studies also document racial discrimination, including callback rates 50% higher for white-sounding than African American-sounding names.

The lecture emphasizes biased beliefs about competence. Research using physicians’ referrals to surgeons found that female surgeons were punished more severely after adverse outcomes and rewarded less after favorable ones. Negative outcomes involving one female surgeon also reduced referrals to other women, potentially reinforcing underrepresentation and limiting opportunities to learn that biased evaluations were mistaken. Algorithms can reproduce human discrimination when trained on biased decisions, but explicit fairness criteria may also make them easier to correct.

Gender identity norms also affect economic behavior. Evidence suggests that the prescription that men should earn more than their wives creates a missing group of couples whose wives earn just over half of household income. Such couples may be less likely to marry, more likely to divorce, and may respond by having wives reduce paid work or increase unpaid childcare. Following the birth of a first child, Danish data show a long-run earnings penalty for women of about 20% and an hours penalty of about 10%, with no comparable earnings decline for men; these penalties may also transmit across generations. Gender-neutral tenure-clock stopping policies have failed to ensure equal outcomes, and in one economics department they increased male tenure rates while reducing female tenure rates. Marriage-market incentives may also lead single female MBA students to display less ambition when preferences are visible, especially to male peers.

Finally, the lecture distinguishes demand for work from willingness to supply it. Women are more likely than men to accept nonpromotable tasks such as committee service and are therefore also more likely to be asked. Experiments indicate that women volunteer more in mixed-sex groups, while gender differences disappear in single-sex groups. Because women comply more often when asked, expectations that they will say yes lead others to request their labor, amplifying the original assignment differences. Overall, biased beliefs, identity norms, family responsibilities, and feedback in workplace task allocation all contribute to persistent gender gaps and may inform policies aimed at reducing them.

The ADS868xW enters conversion on the rising edge of CONVST/CS and ignores further signal transitions until conversion completes, after which it returns to acquisition. The host can detect completion through an RVS low-to-high transition or wait for the specified maximum conversion time.

The device has nine configuration registers and supports data reads and writes. A transfer frame begins on the falling edge of CONVST/CS and ends on the next rising edge. During the frame, SCLK shifts commands into the device and output data from a 32-bit shift register onto the SDO pins. A 32-clock frame is optimal and its command is executed at the frame’s rising edge. Short frames provide valid output data but invalidate writes and are treated as NOPs; in long frames, the last 32 input bits form the command.

Commands are synchronized to SCLK and include byte and half-word read, write, set, and clear operations. Half-word commands ignore the least significant address bit. Output data for the following frame depends on the preceding command and can contain fixed data, 8- or 16-bit register data, or the latest conversion result. Programmable flags can append device address, input range, AVDD and input alarms, and parity.

The multiSPI interface supports four legacy SPI-compatible configurations for writes and either single- or dual-SDO legacy SPI or source-synchronous protocols for reads. Dual-SDO mode outputs two bits per clock. Source-synchronous mode provides a synchronous output clock on RVS and supports internal or external clock sources. The default SPI protocol is SPI-00-S after power-up or reset.

Configuration registers control device identification, reset and power control, SPI selection, output protocol, data output formatting, input ranges, alarms, and alarm thresholds. Writes to the reset/power-control register require the protection key 69h.

An industrial input-module design combines the single-channel ADS8681W with an eight-channel MUX36D08 to support configurable voltage or current inputs, fast settling, and input and AVDD alarms. Programmable input-alarm thresholds and hysteresis support thermistor temperature monitoring while limiting false alarms from noise. The device uses separate AVDD and DVDD supplies, requires specified supply and reference decoupling, and provides NAP and deep power-down modes for reduced power consumption. Recommended PCB layouts separate analog and digital routing and place bypass capacitors close to device pins.

The passage describes an Amibroker-tested momentum rotation strategy involving SPY (the S&P 500) and TLT (20-year Treasury bonds). Each month, both ETFs are ranked by the prior month’s performance; the stronger one is held for one month before repeating the process at month-end. The strategy reflects sector rotation by tactically switching assets based on quantitative momentum rules. Treasuries often serve as a safe haven during weak equity markets, but TLT is not always a hedge against tail risk, as both ETFs fell sharply in 2022. A backtest beginning in June 2003, with dividends reinvested and excluding slippage and commissions, reports a 9.2% CAGR. Maximum drawdown was approximately 22% before 2022 and 41% during 2022. Momentum historically performs best over one- to 12-month periods but can experience large drawdowns and survivorship bias. The article says the strategy’s total return exceeded buy-and-hold.

The study examined barriers and stigma affecting people with probable Long Covid who had not received a clinical diagnosis. Long Covid is defined by the WHO as symptoms lasting at least two months, usually beginning three months after probable or confirmed SARS-CoV-2 infection, without an alternative diagnosis. It can involve fatigue, breathlessness, headaches, cognitive problems, pain, disturbed sleep, and neuropsychiatric symptoms, affecting employment, finances, and social participation. Health inequalities and stigma may compound barriers to care, particularly for people in disadvantaged communities and ethnic minority groups.

As part of the NIHR STIMULATE-ICP study, researchers co-produced a community-based active case-finding approach with a Community Advisory Board. Six advisory board meetings informed the study’s aims, methods, documents, and dissemination. Leaflets were distributed through community organisations, local authorities, and social prescribing teams in Camden, Merton, and Derbyshire. Twenty-three semi-structured interviews, conducted from August 2022 to May 2023, explored care-seeking experiences and enacted, anticipated, and internalised stigma. Interviews were analysed thematically with NVivo, informed by the Long Covid Stigma Scale.

Four themes were identified. First, limited awareness of Long Covid among communities, healthcare professionals, and participants themselves caused uncertainty about symptoms and available care. Self-doubt, downplaying symptoms, comparing symptoms with more severe cases, and attributing them to ageing, menopause, stress, or pre-existing conditions also reduced help-seeking. Participants’ trust in healthcare professionals meant dismissal or failure to mention Long Covid could reinforce these doubts.

Second, participants faced healthcare barriers including reluctance to burden the NHS, concerns about parenting or work, short appointments, waiting times, and limited opportunities to discuss multiple symptoms. Fluctuating or relapsing symptoms were sometimes absent during consultations, while attention to one prominent symptom could cause others to be overlooked. Some symptoms were attributed to existing conditions or mental health.

Third, participants reported enacted, anticipated, and internalised stigma in healthcare, social settings, and workplaces. Experiences involved ageism, gender discrimination, dismissal of symptoms and knowledge, perceived judgement, lack of understanding, exclusion, and doubts about productivity or sickness claims. Anticipated discrimination, including fear of being labelled a hypochondriac, viewed as lazy, or judged at work, discouraged disclosure and care-seeking. Internalised stigma appeared as shame, embarrassment, reduced self-worth, and negative self-comparison. These experiences reflected intersecting disadvantages and, according to the authors, forms of testimonial and hermeneutical epistemic injustice.

Fourth, participants described support from peers, community groups, social prescribing, friends and family, and alternative or private healthcare. Financial and employment support, flexible or hybrid work, and dedicated Long Covid services were also considered beneficial. Participants wanted longer appointments, attentive listening, reassurance, symptom exploration, treatment, referrals, and access to dedicated services without first visiting a GP.

The co-designed case-finding approach reached people who had not previously sought support and identified intersecting barriers to diagnosis, care, and treatment. The authors recommend greater public and healthcare awareness, action against stigma, better listening to people with lived experience, and early signposting to support. Although participants had symptoms consistent with Long Covid, their diagnoses remained unconfirmed and alternative diagnoses were possible. The analysis excluded people younger than 29, so the experiences of younger adults remain unknown.

Moldova’s economy grew 1.1% year on year in the second quarter of 2025, reversing a 1.2% first-quarter contraction, driven by construction, energy, and ICT. The National Bank of Moldova cut its benchmark rate by 25 basis points to 6% in August to support lending and domestic demand amid weak external demand and regional uncertainty. The EBRD forecasts GDP growth of 1.5% for 2025 and 3.8% for 2026, conditional on reforms and international support. Inflation, fiscal constraints, and currency volatility remain risks, while sustained growth will require EU and international financing, deeper reforms, economic diversification, and reduced reliance on remittances.

Turing improves memory performance through a redesigned GDDR6 subsystem delivering 14 Gbps signaling and 20% greater power efficiency than Pascal’s GDDR5X. It uses redesigned SerDes/RF circuits, extensive clock gating, package and board signal-integrity optimization, and a 40% reduction in signal crosstalk. TU102 includes 6 MB of L2 cache, twice that of GP102, while improved compression and reduced memory traffic produce approximately 50% greater effective bandwidth for TU102-based RTX 2080 Ti than GP102-based 1080 Ti.

The display engine supports DisplayPort 1.4a, DSC 1.2, 8K at 60 Hz, two 8K displays, HDR, and BT.2100 tone mapping. USB-C can also carry 8K video. The enhanced NVENC unit supports H.265 8K encoding at 30 fps and offers bitrate savings of up to 25% for HEVC and 15% for H.264. NVDEC adds HEVC 4:4:4 8/10/12-bit and VP9 10/12-bit HDR support. VirtualLink uses one USB-C connection to provide VR headsets with power, display, and tracking data.

Turing TU102 and TU104 replace MIO and PCIe SLI transfers with second-generation NVLink. TU102 has two x8 links and TU104 has one, each providing 25 GB/s per direction per link. Two-way SLI is supported, enabling new display topologies.

Real-time ray tracing is enabled by RT Cores in TU102, TU104, and TU106, combined with NVIDIA RTX software, denoising, and BVH acceleration structures. RT Cores handle bounding-box traversal and ray-triangle intersection tests, freeing shader multiprocessors for other work. Turing delivers more than 10 Giga Rays/s compared with roughly 1.1 Giga Rays/s for software ray tracing on Pascal, making it about ten times faster. Hybrid rendering combines rasterization for visibility and primary rays with ray tracing for effects such as reflections, refractions, shadows, and indirect lighting. Denoising further reduces the number of rays required.

NVIDIA NGX provides pretrained neural-network services through an API and is supported only on Turing. Deep Learning Super-Sampling renders at lower sample counts and uses neural inference to produce quality similar to temporal anti-aliasing with roughly half the shading work. Combined with Tensor Cores, it enables the RTX 2080 Ti to achieve twice the performance of the GTX 1080 Ti. DLSS 2X uses a larger network to approach 64-times-supersampled quality. Other NGX features include AI-based inpainting, interpolated-frame AI Slow-Mo, and AI Super Rez for 2x, 4x, or 8x image and video upscaling.

Turing adds several rendering and resource-management capabilities. Mesh Shading introduces cooperative task and mesh shaders that reduce CPU draw-call bottlenecks and can increase the number of real-time objects by more than an order of magnitude. Variable Rate Shading controls shading independently from visibility on a per-16×16-pixel basis, supporting content-adaptive, motion-adaptive, and foveated rendering. Texture Space Shading decouples appearance sampling from screen-space visibility, caches shaded texels for reuse, and can improve stereo VR efficiency. Multi-View Rendering supports up to four hardware views per pass and 32 at the API level, while expanding Pascal’s simultaneous multi-projection capabilities. Turing also supports bindless constant-buffer and unordered-access views and more flexible resource heaps.

The full TU104 contains 48 streaming multiprocessors, 3,072 CUDA Cores, 368 Tensor Cores, 48 RT Cores, and a 256-bit memory interface. Tesla T4 uses a smaller TU104 configuration with 40 SMs, 2,560 CUDA Cores, 320 Tensor Cores, and 320 GB/s memory bandwidth. TU106, used by GeForce RTX 2070, contains 36 SMs, 2,304 CUDA Cores, 288 Tensor Cores, and 36 RT Cores, but does not support NVLink or SLI.

RTX-OPS is presented as a workload-based metric for hybrid rendering. Peak Tensor, FP32, RT, and INT32 operations are weighted according to representative utilization, and the RTX 2080 Ti example yields 78 RTX-OPS. The underlying workload model assigns 20% of frame time to neural-network work, divides the remaining rendering time between ray tracing and rasterization, and accounts for concurrent INT32 execution.

Ray-traced shadows provide physically correct contact hardening, while ray-traced ambient occlusion produces more realistic geometric definition than screen-space methods. Ray-traced reflections avoid holes and artifacts associated with screen-space reflections and can produce artifact-free, physically correct glossy results. Bounding Volume Hierarchies reduce intersection testing by organizing scene geometry in a hierarchy of bounding boxes; BVH building creates these structures, while refitting updates them more cheaply when scene changes are limited. The document concludes with NVIDIA disclaimers concerning specification accuracy, warranties, liability, intellectual property, product suitability, and third-party trademarks.

New York City’s per-pupil education spending rose 40% to $25,087, yet standardized performance stagnated or declined. The Department of Education’s $23.4 billion budget directs 30.3% of operating expenses to employee benefits and 23.4% to teacher salaries. The city had the highest per-pupil spending among the nation’s 100 largest school systems in fiscal 2015. Rising pension costs, poorly received broadband spending, weak expense documentation, a 1,300-person reserve costing $100 million annually, and a Renewal Program projected at $784 million were cited as concerns. From 2009 to 2015, fourth-grade math and reading scores fell six and three points, while eighth-grade gains left students below national averages. A record 72.6% graduation rate in 2016 was accompanied by test results showing only half of graduates were college- or career-ready. Top teacher pay rose from $100,000 to $119,000, with retroactive raises to 2009.
The Ninth Circuit dismissed the appeal by stipulation of counsel and ordered the mandate to issue forthwith.

The 3 Days Down Overnight Trading Strategy buys SPY after the S&P 500 closes lower for three consecutive days, entering at the third day’s close and usually exiting at the next day’s open. Its SPY backtest produced 661 trades, a 65% win rate, 8% maximum drawdown, and 0.13% average gain per trade, excluding slippage and commissions. Exiting at the next day’s close increased average gains to 0.24% and produced a 5% CAGR, but lowered the win rate to 61% and raised drawdown to 17%. A March 2022 modified version reduced market exposure and drawdowns, with a reported 0.35% average gain, 60% win rate, and 10% maximum drawdown. It also works for QQQ and some stocks, though less effectively than SPY.

In 1886, Hawaii’s legislature and King approved a $2 million loan backed by Kingdom revenues and handled by an English syndicate for bond redemption and domestic improvements; the United States opposed it under its reciprocity-treaty privileges. The United States also declined in 1887 to approve a proposed Hawaiian-Samoan political alliance.

Citing the 1843 Anglo-French convention, Britain proposed in December 1887 that the United States, Britain, and Germany guarantee Hawaiian neutrality and equal access to ports and harbors. Secretary of State Thomas F. Bayard rejected the proposal in February 1888, arguing that the Pearl Harbor concession did not impair Hawaiian sovereignty or port access and that U.S.-Hawaiian treaties barred territorial cessions without U.S. consent. Britain’s commissioner at Honolulu then protested the exclusive U.S. use of Pearl Harbor as a coaling and repair station, warning that foreign control or preferential concessions could cost Hawaii its independence. The passage attributes Britain’s initiative to Anglo-German rivalry and British concern about U.S. policy toward Samoa.

Index Markets Research’s report analyzes the global Polyolefin (POF) Shrink Film market, including applications, manufacturing technology, market size and trends, revenue forecasts, segmentation, costs, production capacity, competitive dynamics, and strategic guidance. It covers Commercial, Government, and Personal segments; regional production, consumption, revenue, share, and growth for North America, China, Europe, Southeast Asia, Japan, and India from 2012–2022; and General versus Cross-linked products. Applications include food, beverage, industrial packaging, pharmaceuticals, and consumer goods. The report profiles leading manufacturers and provides SWOT, investment, and development-trend analyses.

Successful special teams require every player to commit, anticipate puck movement, maintain proper positioning, and adjust to opponents. Playoffs and the Finals bring greater emotional intensity, but players must regroup after losses and focus on the next game. The speaker praises a steady defenseman who improved offensively and logged significant minutes in all situations. They also discuss tracking quick puck movement and backchecking, noting they have not spoken with the players but are excited for the opportunity and aware of Slovakia’s limited NHL representation. The speaker describes the atmosphere as exciting, hopes for a better result, and recalls first seeing the Stanley Cup Finals on TV as a child.

UFC light heavyweight champion Jon Jones favors a bout with former UFC heavyweight champion Brock Lesnar over Stipe Miocic, citing greater public interest, a larger payday and broader benefit for MMA. His trainer, Mike Winklejohn, supports the choice and says Jones needs to gain weight and improve before facing Miocic, whom he considers the harder opponent.

NVIDIA’s GA10x Ampere architecture is designed for gaming, visualization, AI, and data-center workloads. GA102 contains seven GPCs, 42 TPCs, 84 SMs, 112 ROPs, a 384-bit memory subsystem, and 6 MB of L2 cache. Moving ROPs into each GPC increases raster throughput. Each SM includes 128 CUDA Cores, four third-generation Tensor Cores, one second-generation ray-tracing core, a 256 KB register file, and 128 KB of configurable L1/shared memory. Its four partitions support two FP32 datapaths, enabling 128 FP32 operations per clock, while shared-memory bandwidth is twice that of Turing. Ampere is also described as up to 1.9 times more power efficient than Turing at equivalent performance.

Third-generation NVLink provides four x4 links and 112.5 GB/s aggregate bandwidth between two GPUs. Two A40 or A6000 GPUs can combine their 48 GB memory configurations into 96 GB, while two RTX 3090 GPUs support two-way SLI but not three- or four-way configurations. GA10x also supports PCIe 4.0, with a x16 slot providing up to 64 GB/s for host transfers and GPU DMA operations.

Second-generation RT Cores double ray/triangle intersection throughput over Turing and add hardware acceleration for ray-traced motion blur, including moving and deforming geometry. GA10x can concurrently process ray tracing with graphics or compute and can execute two compute workloads simultaneously. Third-generation Tensor Cores are twice as powerful as Turing Tensor Cores, support TF32 and BF16, and use 2:4 fine-grained structured sparsity to double sparse matrix throughput. Enhanced DLSS uses these cores for features such as 9× super-resolution and 8K HDR gaming.

The architecture uses GDDR6X memory with PAM4 signaling, supporting data rates up to 19.5 Gbps and peak bandwidth of 936 GB/s on GA10x. Its Error Detection and Replay feature detects failed memory transmissions and retries them. NVIDIA RTX IO, working with Microsoft DirectStorage, moves compressed assets directly from NVMe SSDs to the GPU and performs lossless decompression on the GPU, offloading work that may otherwise occupy dozens of CPU cores and improving loading, streaming, frame rates, and texture delivery.

The A40 targets data-center visual computing, providing 48 GB of memory, NVLink scalability to 96 GB, up to twice the FP32 and ray-tracing throughput and up to 5×, or 10× with sparsity, the AI-training throughput of a Quadro RTX 6000. It supports virtualization, Quadro Sync, display outputs, and the NVIDIA EGX Platform. The RTX A6000 provides 10,752 CUDA Cores and 48 GB of GDDR6 memory, with two boards combining for 96 GB through NVLink.

GA10x supports DisplayPort 1.4a and HDMI 2.1, including 8K at 60 Hz and 4K at 120 Hz with required compression or pixel formats. Fifth-generation NVDEC supports hardware decoding of MPEG-2, VC-1, H.264, H.265, VP8, VP9, and AV1, including 8K60 AV1 playback at low CPU usage. Seventh-generation NVENC provides hardware-accelerated encoding up to 4K H.264 and 8K HEVC.

The GeForce RTX 3090 uses GA102 with 82 SMs, 10,496 CUDA Cores, and 24 GB of GDDR6X. The RTX 3070 uses GA104 with GA10x features except NVLink, but its implementation uses GDDR6 rather than GDDR6X.

The MSPM0C1105 and MSPM0C1106 include an independent watchdog timer with a 25-bit closed/open-window counter, a fixed 32 kHz clock source with programmable divider, eight selectable periods, and power-on-reset generation when not serviced. The windowed watchdog timer supports eight selectable periods, automatic stopping during sleep, interval-timer operation, and reset or interrupt generation. The RTC_B provides calendar counters, customizable alarms, interval and periodic wake-up interrupts, binary/BCD formats, leap-year correction, crystal-offset and temperature-drift compensation, and clock output for calibration.

General-purpose and advanced timers provide 16-bit counting, programmable prescalers, repeat reload, synchronization and cross-triggering, and QEI support on TIMGx. TIMAx adds a clock doubler, repeat counter, shadow registers, asymmetric PWM with programmable dead band, fault handling, and additional capture/compare channels.

IOMUX controls peripheral-function selection, input and output paths, drive strength, pull resistors, and shutdown wake-up logic. A two-wire Arm-compatible SWD interface and DEBUGSS support processor and peripheral debugging, configurable peripheral behavior during debug, boot-ROM and software mailbox communication, SWD lockout, and password-authenticated debugging. Memory-mapped factory constants provide device capabilities, identification, revision data, and factory trim information.

A typical application uses 10 µF and 0.1 µF ceramic VDD decoupling capacitors, a 47 kΩ NRST pullup with a 1000 pF pulldown, crystal bypass capacitors where required, and pullups for 5 V-tolerant open-drain I/O. TI development resources include LaunchPad hardware, software libraries, cloud tools, SysConfig, the TI Resource Explorer, MSP Academy, GUI Composer, and the TI Arm-Clang compiler. Device nomenclature distinguishes experimental X parts from fully qualified MSP production parts. The document also provides revision history, ESD cautions, package drawings, solder-mask and thermal-pad guidance, and orderable-part information.

The double-down trading strategy adds an equal-sized position to a losing trade to lower the average entry price and recover losses if the price reverses. For example, after buying 100 Amazon shares at $136 and seeing the price fall to $100, buying 100 more shares would produce a breakeven if the price subsequently rose $18. However, continued declines can increase losses and risk ruin.

The strategy differs from scale-in trading, which is planned in advance; the Martingale strategy, which doubles trade size after losses; and the repair strategy, which uses call options.

Backtests showed that doubling down improved performance in mean-reverting SPY: one strategy recorded 518 trades with a 0.56% average gain, while the double-down version recorded 236 trades with a 0.97% average gain and improved performance metrics. In trending HYG, doubling down worsened results, reducing trades from 275 to 125 while increasing average loss from 0.19% to 0.22% per trade.

The article concludes that doubling down may suit some mean-reverting assets but is generally unsuitable for trending assets. It is rarely part of a rational plan because it emphasizes price and average entry rather than probability, overall strategy, and risk management.

A persistent, record-breaking heat wave has affected parts of Canada, the northeastern United States, Europe and the Middle East, causing deadly temperatures and breaking or tying long-standing records. Montreal reached 37 C on July 2, and officials linked at least 11 deaths to the heat and humidity; Ottawa’s humidex reached a record 47.
