The study examines how users prompt ChatGPT and how its communication styles adapt during conversational information seeking, focusing on gaps in research on behavioral AI literacy, the second-level digital divide, and human–AI communication. It addresses four questions: which prompting strategies users employ, how these strategies relate to sociodemographics, how issue controversy and prompting influence ChatGPT’s responses, and how response styles affect AI perceptions and issue-specific attitudes.

A nationally representative experiment involving 937 U.S. adults recruited through Prolific in November 2024 used a 3 × 2 design crossing issue type—health, science, and policy—with controversial versus noncontroversial topics. Participants sought issue-specific information through at least five turns with GPT-4o and submitted conversation links. Of 937 links, 747 were valid for analysis.

Researchers examined five information-related communication styles: self-revealing, information-seeking, fact-oriented, action-seeking, and cognitive complexity. Four styles were extracted using the Symanto Psychology API, while cognitive complexity was measured with LIWC’s categorical-dynamic index. ChatGPT responses were also assessed for citation counts and structural elements such as headings, bullet points, numbered points, and bold text.

Eight prompting strategies were classified as user-supplied information, style-related requests, or content-related requests. ChatGPT annotated 4,154 prompts, with trained coders validating a random subset of 884 prompts; the annotation showed high inter-coder reliability and a weighted F1 score of 0.903.

Three principal findings were reported. First, 19.1% of participants used at least one prompting strategy, with usage predicted by education level and party affiliation. Second, issue controversy influenced ChatGPT’s communication styles and number of citations, while users’ prompt styles remained consistent across controversy levels. Third, cognitively complex ChatGPT responses were viewed less favorably but were associated with more positive issue-relevant attitude changes.

The TPS7H500x-SP controllers provide a configurable FAULT input for external overcurrent, overvoltage, or other protection logic. A FAULT threshold above 0.6 V must persist for 0.4–1.4 µs to trigger shutdown; shorter transients may be ignored. During a fault, SS is discharged and switching stops until FAULT falls below 0.5 V, followed by a delay of approximately 15 switching cycles and a new soft-start sequence.

Peak-current-mode converters can develop subharmonic oscillation above 50% duty cycle. TPS7H500x-SP devices mitigate this with slope compensation set through the RSC pin; the recommended ramp equals the inductor’s falling-current slope, while 0.5 times that slope is the minimum for stability. Type 2A or Type 2B frequency compensation is supported, with Type 2A adding CHF for high-frequency noise attenuation. Internal thermal shutdown stops switching above 175°C and permits reinitialization below 160°C. The controllers otherwise use fixed-frequency peak-current-mode control, comparing sensed switch current with a stepped-down COMP voltage to turn off the power switch.

The radiation-hardness-assured controller family supports space-grade DC-DC converters at frequencies up to 2 MHz and requires external gate drivers. Supported topologies include buck, flyback, forward, active-clamp forward, push-pull, and full-bridge converters.

A design example uses the TPS7H5001-SP in a 500-kHz synchronous push-pull GaN converter with a 5-V output. Selected values include a 205-kΩ RT resistor, 10-kΩ/1.4-kΩ feedback divider, 20.5-kΩ PS and SP resistors for approximately 25-ns dead time, 49.9-kΩ leading-edge blanking resistor, 33-nF soft-start capacitor for about 7.5 ms, 2.5:1 transformer turns ratio, and 40-µH primary inductance. Primary and synchronous-rectifier GaN FETs are rated at 170 V and 80 V, respectively. The design uses a 0.47-µH output inductor, 7.3-Ω current-sense resistor, 1:100 current-sense transformer, 3.3-nF hiccup capacitor, and 102-kΩ slope-compensation resistor. At least 1.3 mF of output capacitance is required for ripple and transient limits; 2.3 mF total is used for additional single-event-transient mitigation. Type 2A compensation targets a 10-kHz crossover and uses 40.2-kΩ RCOMP, 15-nF CCOMP, and 47-pF CHF.

The controllers operate from 4–14 V and require at least a 0.1-µF ceramic bypass capacitor from VIN to AVSS. Layout guidance emphasizes separating feedback and control signals from switching nodes, minimizing high-dv/dt and high-di/dt loops, joining analog and power grounds at one point, using short and wide high-current traces, placing filtering and bypass capacitors near their pins, and optimizing blanking, compensation, and filtering through testing.

The address presents a peace program rooted in American principles: extending the Monroe Doctrine so no nation imposes its polity on another people and each people freely determines its future; avoiding entangling alliances while forming a common concert of power; and securing consent of the governed, freedom of the seas, and moderation of armaments. It argues that these universal principles should prevail internationally.

Diplomatic responses were receptive but cautious. Italy’s foreign minister considered the program idealistic and difficult to implement, though not unfavorably received. The Swiss minister praised the address as the “finest noblest diplomatic document” of his diplomatic career. Spain’s minister reported an excellent impression and said Spain, viewing itself and the United States as leading neutrals, could cooperate closely if consulted before further public communications. Count Tisza of Hungary welcomed peace efforts and continued exchange of ideas, but stressed that the opponents’ conditions would dismantle the Austro-Hungarian and Ottoman empires. Invoking national self-determination and free religious and social development, he argued that the two halves of his monarchy better fulfilled those principles than the opponents’ proposals.

The disclosure describes methods, systems, and computer-readable media for automating orthodontic treatment planning. A treatment-planning engine uses patient dentition data, such as a digital model or scan, and dental professionals’ instructions to generate customized treatment plans that may include staged tooth movement, extractions, interproximal reduction, attachments, and orthodontic appliances.

User- or group-specific preferences are stored in a database that links textual key preferences to clinical behaviors. Preferences may be defined explicitly, mined from historical instructions and approved treatment plans, or identified through statistical analysis of consistent clinical behavior, including recent changes in practice. Text matching may use machine-learning classification, including bag-of-words models, and similarity searches using Damerau-Levenshtein distance. Candidate matches can be manually or semi-automatically verified.

Matched clinical behaviors are incorporated into patient-specific plans for professional review, modification, approval, and appliance production. Modifications and approved plans may update the preference database. Monitoring tools report on automatic preference application, accepted or changed options, and potentially outdated preferences. In one example, treatment plans requiring user modification decreased from 12.48% to 8.5%. The application is a continuation of U.S. Patent No. 12,048,604 and claims priority to provisional applications filed March 21, 2019.

Three-year-old Liam Radcliffe left Barassie early years nursery in Ayrshire through two doors and an unlocked gate, walking roughly half a mile home alone without staff noticing for up to 20 minutes. His mother found him crying at her door and was shocked staff had not realized he was missing. The main door was subsequently alarmed, the gate padlocked, and additional staff arranged. South Ayrshire Council confirmed the security changes.

The passage argues that judicial decisions should be open to free, fair, and dispassionate public criticism, which encourages careful, just rulings and helps ensure judicial accountability. Unjust attacks should be rebutted through the strength of judicial opinions and the public’s calm judgment; suppressing legitimate criticism would benefit irresponsible agitators and weaken respect for the judiciary. Addressing crime, corruption, delays in justice, and mob violence requires an awakened public conscience and legislation that ensures swift, certain enforcement. It especially condemns lynching, noting that many white men are lynched but Black men are targeted with unusual frequency, and that mob revenge perpetuates rather than remedies the crime.

The NVIDIA A100 Tensor Core GPU is an Ampere-architecture accelerator for AI, deep learning, and high-performance computing. Its third-generation Tensor Cores accelerate GEMM operations of the form D = A×B+C and support FP16, BF16, TF32, FP64, INT8, INT4, and 1-bit formats. With 108 SMs and 432 Tensor Cores, A100 provides up to 312 TFLOPS of dense FP16/FP32 mixed-precision performance—2.5 times the Tensor Core performance of Tesla V100 and 20 times its standard FP32 throughput. TF32 provides FP32 range with reduced internal precision and is enabled by default for training; FP16 and BF16 mixed precision can provide up to twice the throughput of TF32 and 16 times that of FP32.

A100 also accelerates IEEE-compliant FP64 computation, delivering 19.5 TFLOPS, or 2.5 times V100’s peak FP64 throughput. In cuSOLVER’s mixed-precision iterative-refinement solver, TF32 produced the fastest and most robust results among tested reduced-precision modes, with a geometric-mean speedup of 2.0 times over an FP64 solver and up to fourfold speedups for large complex matrices.

A100 introduces 2:4 fine-grained structured sparsity, which permits two nonzero values in every four-entry vector. Sparse Matrix Multiply-Accumulate instructions skip zero entries, doubling Tensor Core throughput, while compressed weights halve data footprint and bandwidth. A prescribed procedure—dense training, structured pruning, then fine-tuning—produces virtually no inference-accuracy loss across numerous vision, detection, segmentation, language-modeling, and translation networks. Training acceleration with sparsity requires introducing sparsity early and remains an active research area.

The memory hierarchy includes 192 KB per SM of combined L1 cache and shared memory, 40 GB of HBM2 memory providing 1,555 GB/s bandwidth, and a 40 MB L2 cache that is 6.7 times larger than V100’s. A100’s L2 bandwidth is 2.3 times higher, and compute data compression can improve effective DRAM bandwidth, L2 bandwidth, and L2 capacity. ECC protects HBM2, L2, L1 caches, and register files. Strong-scaling improvements include greater Tensor Core data sharing, larger matrix operations, asynchronous global-to-shared copies, asynchronous barriers, L2 residency controls, and fewer instructions and register-file accesses than V100.

The Multi-Instance GPU feature can divide one A100 into as many as seven isolated GPU Instances, each with dedicated compute and memory resources, quality-of-service guarantees, and fault isolation. GPU Instances can contain multiple Compute Instances that support simultaneous contexts and Volta-style MPS. MIG supports migration of virtual GPUs between compatible instances, enabling consolidation, servicing, and higher utilization. A100 also adds improved error attribution, isolation, containment, and recovery for multi-tenant and multi-GPU environments.

Third-generation NVLink provides 12 links and 600 GB/s of aggregate GPU-to-GPU bandwidth, twice V100’s total. PCIe Gen 4 supplies 31.5 GB/s per direction on x16 connections, while SR-IOV enables GPU sharing and virtualization. Additional hardware includes a five-core NVJPEG decoder, an optical-flow accelerator supporting optical flow and stereo disparity, improved global-memory atomics, and five NVDEC units for compressed-video decoding.

CUDA 11 adds support for third-generation Tensor Cores, sparsity, CUDA Graphs, MIG, L2 residency controls, asynchronous copies and barriers, Cooperative Groups, and hardware reductions. CUDA Graphs reduce launch and dependency overhead by submitting connected workflows as predefined graphs. Cooperative Groups expose asynchronous memory pipelines and hardware-assisted reductions, including single-step warp reductions.

DGX A100 combines eight A100 GPUs with six NVSwitches, providing 5 PFLOPS of AI performance, 4.8 TB/s aggregate bidirectional NVLink bandwidth, and up to 56 hardware-isolated accelerators through MIG. It is designed for AI training and inference, analytics, and HPC, with ConnectX-6 InfiniBand networking, NGC software, and deployment support for large Kubernetes and Slurm clusters.

The Affordable Care Act has affected Medicare beneficiaries, workers, individual-market enrollees, Medicaid recipients and nearly everyone else. President-elect Donald Trump and congressional Republicans pledged to begin repeal with spending and revenue provisions that could pass with a Senate majority, while retaining coverage for children under 26.

Repeal would likely raise Medicare premiums, deductibles and cost-sharing for 57 million beneficiaries, restore the prescription-drug “donut hole,” and end free preventive screenings. It would increase Medicare spending by an estimated $802 billion over 10 years. Higher-income beneficiaries could benefit because the law froze premium-surcharge thresholds and added surcharges for wealthier beneficiaries.

For employer-sponsored insurance, repeal would end the requirement that firms with at least 50 employees offer affordable coverage to workers exceeding 30 hours, potentially lead firms to cover only 35- or 40-hour workers, and end required dependent coverage through age 26. Employees might again pay for contraception and preventive services, while insurers could restore annual or lifetime benefit limits. Workers at smaller firms could lose protections for pre-existing conditions, essential benefits and age-based premium limits.

In the individual market, repeal could end guaranteed coverage for people with pre-existing conditions, premium protections for women and older adults, essential benefits, coverage limits, out-of-pocket caps, exchanges and subsidies for lower-income enrollees. About 10.4 million people had exchange coverage and 6.9 million bought policies outside exchanges.

Repealing Medicaid expansion could leave millions uninsured. Nearly 17 million people had joined Medicaid in 31 states and the District of Columbia since late 2013. Ending the individual mandate would also remove penalties of $695 per adult or 2.5% of household income, whichever was greater.

Hong Liu outlines the class logistics: there is no textbook or recitation, course materials and problem sets will be posted online, and office hours are available. Grading consists of five biweekly problem sets worth 75% and a final project worth 25%. For the final three weeks, students will submit an 8–10-page review or calculation on a holographic-duality topic. The course outline is flexible and covers advanced topics including gravity, string theory, and quantum field theory.

The lecture motivates holographic duality by contrasting gravity with electromagnetism and the strong and weak interactions, which are understood through gauge theories. Gravity is the weakest interaction, and its quantum formulation remains unresolved: spacetime may fluctuate, become discrete, or cease to be fundamental, while questions about black holes and the universe’s beginning remain open. A 1997 proposal asserts that quantum gravity in a higher-dimensional, dynamical spacetime is equivalent to a quantum field theory on a fixed spacetime. These are different descriptions of the same quantum system, and the course aims to explain the relationship, develop a correspondence between the descriptions, and explore its implications and uses.

The idea that gravity can emerge from nongravitational degrees of freedom predates holographic duality. Sakharov and earlier researchers observed parallels between general relativity and effective descriptions such as hydrodynamics. From the field-theory perspective, gravity is associated with massless spin-2 particles, or gravitons, which might arise as bound states of lower-spin particles.

The Weinberg–Witten theorems restrict this possibility. A theory with a Lorentz-covariant conserved current cannot contain charged massless particles of spin greater than 1/2; a theory with a Lorentz-covariant conserved stress tensor cannot contain massless particles of spin greater than 1. Thus ordinary fixed-spacetime quantum field theories, including QCD-like theories, cannot produce a massless graviton. Holographic duality evades this restriction by placing gravity in a different, higher-dimensional spacetime.

Liu concludes with a largely kinematic proof based on Lorentz representations of massless-particle states, matrix elements of conserved currents and stress tensors, and rotational transformation laws. The resulting eigenvalue constraints reproduce the spin limits of 1/2 and 1.

BioRecall is a cross-sectional pilot protocol designed to address the limited lifestyle and environmental data available in biobanks and support research on gene–environment interactions in non-communicable diseases. The pilot, conducted through the Central Finland Biobank, University of Jyväskylä, FINBB, and University of Eastern Finland, will invite 1,386 eligible adults with type 2 diabetes, available genotype data, and prior consent for recall.

Participants will complete a 30–40-minute REDCap questionnaire through the MyBiobank portal using Suomi.fi authentication. Measures will cover physical activity, diet and alcohol, anthropometrics and weight history, smoking and substance use, health and medications, women’s health, employment and occupational characteristics, emotional state, sleep, socioeconomic background, and residential environment. Postal-code linkage will add spatial, air-quality, land-use, natural-feature, and socioeconomic data. Survey responses will be pseudonymized and combined with genotype, biological-sample, and clinical or register-based outcome data.

Electronic consent will cover participation and archiving survey data in the biobank for approved future research. Participants will receive automated feedback on physical activity, diet, waist circumference, work stress, and sleep. Nonparticipants will form a pseudonymized cohort for comparisons with participants. The pilot has received ethical and biobank approval; data collection is planned to begin in February 2025, with possible expansion to all Central Finland Biobank donors in autumn 2026 and potentially other Finnish biobanks. The study offers a scalable electronic approach but is limited by its small, single-biobank sample, broad questionnaire, uncertain response rates, and absence of wearable data.

The passage reviews Supreme Court petitions relisted for conference during the second week of its new term. It notes several denials involving appeal waivers, ineffective assistance and juror misconduct, whether the Seventh Amendment applies to states, a school policy concerning children’s transgender beliefs, and Section 230 immunity. Justices Sotomayor, Kagan, Jackson, Gorsuch, Alito, and Thomas filed separate opinions addressing some of these denials. Two earlier relisted cases—the FDA’s restrictions on removing and reimplanting patients’ cells and California’s unclaimed-property law—were also denied without recorded dissent.

A major group of relisted petitions challenges 18 U.S.C. § 922(g)(3), which prohibits firearm shipping, transportation, and possession by unlawful users of or people addicted to controlled substances. The government argues that the provision is consistent with historical firearm regulation; in *Hemani*, it asks the Court to resolve the issue and hold three related petitions. The Fifth Circuit had invalidated the law for most such users, while the Eighth Circuit reached a narrower result.

In *Keathley v. Buddy Ayers Construction, Inc.*, the petitioner seeks review of the Fifth Circuit’s strict application of judicial estoppel after he failed to disclose a later personal-injury claim in his bankruptcy proceeding. He contends that the Fifth and Tenth Circuits’ rule conflicts with the intent-based approach used by five other circuits, which examine whether a debtor subjectively intended to mislead the court. The government disputes that a genuine circuit split exists, but the author considers the case a serious review candidate.

The passage also discusses four prisoner-filed petitions, three handwritten and all raising procedural-error claims, including one involving advice about the right to counsel and another seeking Elon Musk’s prosecution over alleged drug transactions on Twitter. Additional relisted matters cover the First Step Act, wrongful convictions, religious accommodations under Title VII, public-trial closures, qualified immunity, tribal jurisdiction, January 6 litigation, peremptory strikes, and other statutory and constitutional questions.

Shortly before the worldwide launch of the PlayStation 3 (PS3) on November 17, 2006, Sony CEO Howard Stringer faced competition from Microsoft’s Xbox 360 and Nintendo’s Wii. The Xbox 360 had launched in fall 2005 and sold nearly four million units within a year, while the $249.99 Wii was positioned as a mainstream alternative to the $599 PS3. The PS3 also served as a Blu-Ray disc player and was intended to support the format in its battle against Toshiba and Microsoft’s HD-DVD. Major studios and hardware companies divided their support between the formats, while Warner Brothers and Paramount backed both. Sony’s previous format efforts, including BetaMax and UMD, had failed commercially.

The video game industry had changed substantially since its beginnings. Magnavox introduced the Odyssey in 1966, followed by Pong’s success in the 1970s. Atari’s 2600 reached two-thirds of the U.S. home-console market, and arcade-game ports helped the industry reach $3 billion by 1982. The market then collapsed amid console saturation and poor-quality software. Atari’s costly failure with E.T. and a $536 million loss in 1983 preceded the industry’s moribund period.

Nintendo revived the market after entering Japan in 1983 and the United States in 1985. It enforced strict game approval and quality controls, tightly managed licensing and retail distribution, and restricted supply to create scarcity. By 1990, with games such as Super Mario Bros. and The Legend of Zelda, Nintendo held more than 90% of the U.S. market and had sold about 30 million NES units. The Super Nintendo’s lack of backward compatibility and Sega’s strong Genesis library reduced Nintendo’s dominance.

Sony entered in 1994 with a 3D-focused PlayStation, compact-disc technology, and a large variety of licensed games. Revenue reached $700 million within two years, and Sony captured 60% of the U.S. market by 1999. The PlayStation 2, launched in 2000, added DVD playback and reached a 55% market share by early 2006; more than 100 million units were sold worldwide.

Hardware was generally sold at or below cost, while manufacturers earned revenue from royalties of roughly $5–$7 per game. The industry evolved from in-house development to specialized independent studios, third-party publishers, franchised titles, and publisher ownership of intellectual property. Development costs rose sharply, making the market increasingly blockbuster-driven. Publishers responded by acquiring studios, including Ubisoft’s $43 million purchase of Red Storm and Microsoft’s $375 million purchase of Rare.

Internet connectivity became central to the next console war. Sega’s Dreamcast was the first console with a built-in modem. Sony gave PS2 developers broad freedom to implement online features, while Microsoft created the centralized Xbox Live service, requiring broadband and offering voice communication, downloadable content, and paid premium items. Nintendo planned the Virtual Console, through which owners could download older games, while Sony prepared the PlayStation Network Platform to support online play, communication, and downloadable games.

Sony and Microsoft targeted experienced core gamers, largely males in their twenties, while Nintendo sought to expand the market through simple, accessible games for all ages and genders. The success of Nintendo’s DS and Nintendogs supported this strategy, and the Wii introduced motion-sensitive controllers.

Public concern about increasingly realistic violence also intensified after the 1999 Columbine High School shootings. A lawsuit connecting violent games to the massacre was dismissed, and the Entertainment Software Ratings Board (ESRB) had been established to provide age ratings and content information. The rating system was criticized after the “Hot Coffee” incident in Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas and research indicating that some games were more violent than their ratings conveyed. State attempts to restrict violent games were ruled violations of the First Amendment, while the proposed Family Entertainment Protection Act sought to bar minors from purchasing mature games and permit complaints over inaccurate ratings.

Industry forecasts were optimistic that the PS3 would lead the next generation despite Microsoft’s early lead. One forecast projected a 2010 installed-base share of just over 50% for the PS3, 28.6% for the Xbox 360, and 21.2% for the Wii. Sony’s game sales rose to $8.19 billion in 2006, but operating income fell to $74.4 million and operating margin to 7.7%. Nintendo reported 2006 net sales of $4.35 billion and net income of $841 million, while Microsoft’s Home and Entertainment Division recorded $4.26 billion in revenue and a $1.26 billion operating loss.

Anthony Rizzo hit his seventh home run and added a two-run single as the Chicago Cubs beat the Pittsburgh Pirates 7-0 on Monday. The game was overshadowed by Rizzo’s hard slide into catcher Elias Diaz during an eighth-inning force play, which led to a wild throw and two runs. The call was upheld on review, and Pirates manager Clint Hurdle was ejected while arguing it. Diaz remained in the game after treatment and said Rizzo apologized.

Spot starter Mike Montgomery retired the first 13 batters, allowed two singles over 5⅔ innings, and struck out five without walking anyone. Addison Russell also hit a pinch-hit, two-run home run. Pittsburgh starter Chad Kuhl allowed only Rizzo’s solo homer before falling to 1-5.

The Cubs recalled Luke Farrell and optioned Justin Hancock. Pittsburgh released George Kontos. Both teams later had minor roster and injury updates, including Pittsburgh starting pitcher Ivan Nova’s placement on the disabled list.

The MSPM0C1105 and MSPM0C1106 include a PMU with brown-out monitoring, regulated core supplies, and power-mode control; a clock module with internal and external oscillators; and a DMA controller with three channels, configurable triggers, multiple transfer sizes, and up to 64,000 transfers. An event manager routes peripheral events as CPU interrupts, DMA triggers, or generic interperipheral events. The devices provide programmable flash, zero-wait-state SRAM with 1KB-granularity write protection, up to 45 GPIO pins, and IOMUX-controlled pin multiplexing.

Analog features include a 12-bit ADC operating up to 1.6 Msps, internal temperature and supply-monitoring channels, selectable 1.4V or 2.5V internal references, external-reference support, a temperature sensor, and a comparator. Communications peripherals include three UARTs with LIN support, I²C supporting modes up to 1 Mbps, SPI supporting up to 16 Mbits/s, and CRC and security modules. Low-frequency peripherals include an RTC with alarms and calibration, independent and windowed watchdog timers, and general-purpose and advanced timers with counter, encoder, capture/compare, PWM, cross-trigger, and fault-handling capabilities. The devices also provide SWD and DEBUGSS debugging, factory constants, and device-identification information.

The recommended application schematic uses 10µF and 0.1µF low-ESR ceramic capacitors at VDD/VSS, a 47kΩ pullup and 1000pF pulldown on NRST, crystal bypass capacitors where applicable, and pullup resistors for 5V-tolerant open-drain I/O. TI provides development tools, documentation, training, configuration software, and support resources. Device nomenclature distinguishes experimental “X” parts from fully qualified “MSP” production parts. The revision history documents specification, package, CPU, ADC, DEBUGSS, and identification-table updates. Mechanical and orderable information covers package drawings, thermal-pad and solder-mask guidance, product status, materials, RoHS, moisture-sensitivity ratings, reflow temperatures, and part markings.

DNA origami uses base-pairing between a scaffold strand and shorter staple strands to self-assemble predefined three-dimensional nanostructures. Researchers led by Ralf Jungmann used DNA-PAINT super-resolution microscopy to image individual strands in flat rectangular structures. They found assembly to be robust across a wide range of physical conditions, including formation speed, while staple incorporation efficiency depended on the target sequence’s precise position. Additional staples improved efficiency, but not every binding site was occupied in every nanoparticle. The authors therefore recommend adding components in large excess and choosing modification positions according to mapped incorporation efficiency. DNA-PAINT can also optimize nanostructure construction and potentially enable measurement of labeling efficiency for antibodies, cellular proteins, and nucleic acids.

The paper studies modal extensions of logics based on lattice semantics, motivated by applications involving different logical systems and the meaningful communication of truth values across logics. Although the approach could allow each world to use a different lattice, the paper restricts each world to a single lattice semantics. It defines lattices, designated values, filters, implicative sets, matrices, valuations, and modal extensions. A regular modal extension preserves nonmodal validity and interprets necessity as truth in every accessible world. For complete lattices, the normal modal valuation evaluates \(2\varphi\) as the meet of the values of \(\varphi\) at accessible worlds; incomplete lattices may leave some modal formulas without values.

For a complete lattice and designated set \(F\), the normal modal extension is a unique regular extension exactly when \(F\) is a filter and contains its meet. Consequently, on a finite lattice it is regular exactly when the designated values form a filter. This condition fails for some infinite examples, including the fuzzy interval \((0.5,1]\) and a nonprincipal ultrafilter over an infinite Boolean algebra, showing that necessity need not mean truth in all accessible worlds.

The paper also relates designated values and implication operations to frame-valid modal formulas. For complete lattices, implicativity of the designated set is characterized by validity of  
\[
(2\varphi\lor2\psi)\to2(\varphi\lor\psi).
\]
With strictly deductive implication, every frame validates axiom \(K\), \(2(\varphi\to\psi)\to(2\varphi\to2\psi)\), exactly when the lattice is linear outside the designated filter. With implication defined as \(-x+y\), implicativity guarantees \(K\) under anti-monotonicity and down-distribution; adding involutivity makes these conditions necessary as well.

A Boolean twist algebra illustrates the results. On its restriction \(P=\{\langle a,b\rangle:a+b=1\}\), every frame satisfies \(K\) exactly when the designated values include every \(\langle x,y\rangle\) with \(x=1\). The paper concludes by identifying the finite-model property of normal modal extensions as a direction for future research.

Amazon.com, Inc. filed a Form 8-K dated October 29, 2020, reporting its third-quarter 2020 financial results. The filing incorporates Exhibit 99.1, the results press release, and Exhibit 99.2, information regarding non-GAAP financial measures. Senior Vice President and Chief Financial Officer Brian T. Olsavsky signed the report on Amazon’s behalf.

South Carolina golfers Katelyn Dambaugh, Ainhoa Olarra and Ana Pelaez earned Golfweek All-America honors. Dambaugh made the First Team, while Olarra and Pelaez were Honorable Mention selections. Dambaugh earned a program-record five All-America honors and concluded her career as the school’s all-time scoring-average leader. Olarra posted five top-10 finishes, while Pelaez became the 10th Gamecock golfer to earn All-America honors during her freshman season.

The paper combines transfer operator theory with reproducing kernel Hilbert spaces to model noisy, high-dimensional, nonlinear dynamical systems from multi-fidelity data. It reviews dynamic mode decomposition (DMD), a Galerkin method combining PCA and Fourier analysis, and Gaussian process (GP) regression, which provides nonparametric function approximation, probabilistic predictions, and model-selection tools. The authors develop a Bayesian interpretation of the embedded Perron–Frobenius operator and modify Extended DMD into Gaussian Process DMD, enabling sparse dictionary learning, hyperparameter tuning, noise modeling, and uncertainty estimates for multi-step predictions. They also apply variational free energy to kernel Koopman operators to improve the computational trade-off between generalization and training complexity. The mathematical formulation treats operators as random variables using operator-valued kernels and a lifted observation model.

The team won in overtime, using a simple system, strong goaltending, and contributions from Ron Francis, Sami Kapanen, and Arturs. Aaron’s big goal proved important after a second-period tie, and the player described the victory as the team’s first in the Stanley Cup Final while acknowledging their formidable opponent.

A professor recaps that entrepreneurship should focus on dynamic planning rather than a fixed business plan, creating and capturing value, and answering the “three Whys”: why this, why now, and why this team. He introduces Bob Jones to discuss finding customers.

Jones argues that a business must offer something unique and important to a clearly defined customer and must determine who will pay, how they can be reached, and whether the product delivers enough value. His failed nutrition-bar venture, Regain, suffered because he surveyed clinicians rather than the dialysis patients who would eat and purchase the bars. Patients disliked the taste, often lacked money, and pharmacies required costly slotting fees. Jones concludes that stakeholders who influence a purchase are not necessarily the customers who make it.

A later diabetes snack, NiteBite, succeeded after Jones interviewed patients, parents, and diabetes educators. Customers’ greatest fear was dying during nocturnal hypoglycemia, so the product’s real benefit was peace of mind. Its name, taste, packaging, advertising, free samples, and retail strategy were designed around customer preferences. Jones built demand through educators and patients, then used that demand and existing customer relationships to gain retail and wholesaler placement without paying slotting fees. The business grew rapidly and was sold to a major pharmaceutical company.

Jones advises entrepreneurs to identify the specific customer whose problem the product solves, segment and prioritize the market by motivation to buy, focus on the segment feeling the greatest pain, and sell the desired benefit rather than the product itself. He recommends talking directly with potential customers, studying how they currently solve the problem, testing a minimum viable product before investing in branding or expansion, and iterating when initial assumptions prove wrong. He summarizes his core lessons as: find out what customers want, give it to them, and focus.

An article on financial astrology lists planetary positions and identifies housing finance and liquor as sectors receiving astrological support. The author plans to release “Sectors of Samvat 2074” early, ahead of March 2017, to help investors and traders time entries and exits. It claims astrology can identify sectors likely to outperform regardless of market conditions and cites gains of 340%–650% in previously recommended dye, chemical, and sugar stocks during Samvat 2073. A Moneycontrol disclaimer advises readers to consult certified experts before investing.

Baidu is adding NVIDIA Tesla P40 GPUs and deep-learning software to Baidu Cloud, supporting its AI-based autonomous-driving platform. NVIDIA says eight P40s can outperform 140 CPU servers, while Baidu targets Level 4 commercialization by 2018 and mass production by 2020.

The American Indian College Fund began a two-year, $600,000 study funded by Strada Education Network to assess the economic and social returns of five North Dakota tribal colleges and universities. Working with the North Dakota Association of Tribal Colleges, the project will evaluate statewide and institution-level impacts on graduates at Nueta Hidatsa Sahnish College, Sitting Bull College, United Tribes Technical College, Turtle Mountain Community College, and Cankdeska Cikana Community College. It will also examine graduate employment, survey 5,000 College Fund scholars about the value of education rooted in Native American values, and conduct a pilot study of tribal colleges’ preservation of language and culture and support for American Indian communities. The project, scheduled to conclude in September 2019, will publish its results for state and federal policymakers.

The study develops an Atomic Cluster Expansion (ACE) machine-learning potential for YBCO using DFT data covering equilibrium structures, disordered configurations, vacancies, interstitials, oxygen Frenkel pairs, and approximate transition states. The 1,368-configuration dataset produced energy and force RMSEs of about 10 meV/atom and 69 meV/Å, respectively.

Validation showed that ACE reproduces the DFT equation of state, lattice-parameter behavior at large volumes, oxygen migration barriers, and defect formation energies more accurately than the Buckingham–Coulomb classical potential. It captured migration barriers within 20 meV of DFT, while the classical potential underestimated them by 0.3–0.4 eV.

Large-scale NPT simulations reproduced YBCO’s orthorhombic-to-tetragonal transition at approximately 800 K, compared with an experimental value near 1000 K. The transition involves oxygen migration from CuO-chain O1 sites and, to a lesser extent, apical O4 sites to interstitial O5 sites, randomly occupying basal-plane sites and making the a and b directions equivalent. The simulations indicate that this order-disorder transition is primarily entropy-driven, while thermal expansion lowers the formation energy of oxygen Frenkel pairs and facilitates disordering. The lower simulated transition temperature was attributed partly to the model’s slightly underestimated O1v–O5i formation energy and the absence of experimental oxygen loss. Further study requires handling variable oxygen content and experimentally relevant timescales. The potential is proposed as a tool for studying oxygen diffusion, radiation damage, recovery, and annealing strategies in high-temperature superconducting tapes.

This non-empirical review examines how artificial intelligence affects inclusive education. It addresses the relationship between AI and inclusion, defines inclusive education, and assesses the value of integrating students of diverse backgrounds, disabilities, abilities, and cultural identities into mainstream classrooms. A literature review conducted from September 2023 to March 2024 followed PRISMA guidelines and searched Web of Science, ScienceDirect, and IEEE Xplore using terms related to AI, inclusive education, diversity, equity, and equality. The review identified limited research specifically addressing AI’s impact on inclusion.

The literature presents AI as a tool for personalized and adaptive learning, rapid feedback, student engagement, self-directed learning, and targeted instruction. Assistive features such as text-to-speech, speech-to-text, writing tools, and word prediction can support students with disabilities and language learners. AI-enabled platforms and assistants may also provide resources and training on bias, cultural sensitivity, and inclusive practices. In educational administration, AI can automate grading, scheduling, data management, and reporting, enabling continuous evaluation of students’ strengths and weaknesses. However, educators remain essential for guidance, emotional support, encouragement, creativity, and critical thinking; AI cannot fully reproduce human intelligence or complex human experience.

The review identifies limitations and risks, including biased outputs from unrepresentative data, curriculum bias, high implementation and maintenance costs, inadequate technology skills among educators and students, privacy concerns, physical effects of some technologies, possible job displacement, overreliance on technology, and weakened critical-thinking or social and emotional learning. Effective implementation therefore requires diverse data, teacher involvement in tool design and evaluation, collaboration with stakeholders, pilot testing, training, and safeguards against failure or excessive dependence.

An inclusive syllabus should provide accessible and varied formats, screen-reader support, assistive technologies, multiple means of representation, engagement, and expression, and Universal Design for Learning. It should also offer faculty support and office hours, flexible synchronous or asynchronous participation, and offline materials such as e-books, audiobooks, and digital braille books. Educators should use accessible scheduling tools, involve students in establishing class guidelines, regularly reflect on inclusive practices, and foster belonging and active participation.

The study acknowledges that its arguments were not supported by empirical data or fieldwork, focused only broadly on AI and inclusion, gave limited attention to minority groups and sociocultural contexts, and did not comprehensively capture all available studies. It recommends incorporating AI into child-centered teaching and learning, embedding inclusion in curricula and classrooms, providing professional development and inclusive-practice guidance, ensuring safe learning environments, encouraging student participation, and promoting societal and policy awareness of inclusion.

The lecture compares ion and neutral-atom platforms, noting that electric charge enables much stronger confinement, while both platforms support clocks, precision measurement, quantum information, and many-body quantum simulation. Common ion-cooling methods include Doppler and evaporative cooling, and resolved vibrational sidebands enable sideband cooling.

Because static electric potentials cannot confine ions in all directions, ion traps generally use dynamic fields. Penning traps combine electrostatic axial confinement with magnetic cyclotron confinement and have enabled highly precise ion-mass measurements. Paul or RF traps rapidly alternate confining and anti-confining forces, producing effective harmonic confinement when averaged along the ion’s trajectory. This micromotion supplies the restoring force.

The lecture then explains the Cirac–Zoller two-ion gate. Single-qubit rotations and a CNOT gate form a universal gate set, while a controlled-phase gate can be converted into CNOT using Hadamard rotations. For the Cirac–Zoller operation, one ion’s qubit information is transferred into the shared center-of-mass phonon motion, which acts as a data bus. A conditional phase is applied to the other ion, and the phonon information is then returned to the first ion. The method requires cooling center-of-mass motion to its absolute ground state and limits gate speed relative to the phonon period, but it provides a clear demonstration of ion-based quantum logic.

On May 29, 2018, more than 400 Black-owned coffee houses, shops, and tea houses nationwide were expected to participate in “National Eat at a Black Coffee Shop Day,” promoting their businesses as Starbucks closed over 8,000 U.S. stores for diversity training. Participating shops planned evening economic empowerment forums to circulate Black dollars within Black communities.

Cadillac sold 35,020 vehicles globally in September 2017, up 16.5% year over year and marking 16 consecutive months of growth. Year-to-date sales reached 256,613, up 20.9%. U.S. sales rose 1.1%, while China increased 37.6%. The XT5 led with 103,645 deliveries, and average U.S. transaction prices remained about $54,000.

On November 29, 2016, NVIDIA Corporation’s Board amended and restated its bylaws to implement proxy access and revise advance-notice requirements for stockholder nominations. The bylaws allow a stockholder or group of up to 20 holders owning at least 3% of NVIDIA’s voting power for at least three years to include qualifying director nominees in annual meeting proxy materials; nominees may constitute the greater of two directors or 20% of the Board. Beginning with the 2018 annual meeting, nominations outside the proxy-access process must be submitted 90–120 days before the prior annual meeting’s anniversary, rather than 120–150 days before. The bylaws also include related administrative and conforming changes.

The study examined whether blood pressure (BP) relates differently to longitudinal cognitive decline in older Black and White adults. Data came from three harmonized aging cohorts: the Minority Aging Research Study, Rush Memory and Aging Project, and Black Clinical Core. Eligible participants were at least 55 years old, self-identified as Black or White, completed at least two cognitive assessments, and had at least two annual BP readings. The sample included 2,284 participants.

Mean systolic BP and its variability classified participants as having normal, high, or variable BP. Participants completed 19 neuropsychological tests assessing episodic, semantic, and working memory, processing speed, and visuospatial ability, plus a global cognitive measure. Linear mixed-effects models evaluated cognitive change while adjusting for age, sex, education, and diagnosis.

Participants with normal BP showed no racial differences in cognitive decline within BP categories. Among those with high BP, White adults declined faster globally and in processing speed, semantic memory, and working memory than Black adults, while decline in episodic memory and visuospatial ability was similar. White adults with variable BP declined faster globally and in all five cognitive domains than Black adults with variable BP. Additional analyses accounting for cohort and individual time slopes produced the same results. Secondary analyses indicated that lower baseline cognitive scores did not explain the reduced BP-cognitive association among Black adults.

The authors proposed autonomic dysregulation, allostatic load, and differential lifetime exposure to racism-related stress as possible explanations for the observed disparities. Limitations included not measuring medication adherence or comprehensively evaluating medication use, both of which may affect BP and cognition. The findings support maintaining healthy BP and developing interventions tailored to racial and ethnic groups.

AMD shares rose over 20% in premarket trading after the company announced a multiyear agreement to supply OpenAI with AI accelerators, beginning with its MI450 series. OpenAI will receive warrants for up to 10% of AMD’s equity upon meeting production and performance milestones. Analysts said the deal could generate tens of billions in potential revenue, strengthening AMD’s position against Nvidia and Intel in the AI chip market. The announcement coincided with AMD’s $6 billion share buyback plan, while analysts warned of execution, supply-chain, margin, and demand risks.

Judges are sanctioning attorneys who include faulty, AI-generated citations and quotations in court filings. In Puerto Rico, Chief U.S. District Judge Raúl Arias-Marxuach ordered several firms, including Paul Weiss and Sidley Austin, to share $24,492 for at least 55 defective citations, trimming their nearly $88,000 request. The filers denied using AI, but the judge cited the volume of inaccurate or nonexistent citations. In California, attorney Amir Mostafavi was ordered to pay $10,000 to the court after including fake quotes and off-topic AI-generated cases. Opposing counsel received no fees because they failed to detect the errors, raising questions about lawyers’ duty to identify fabricated citations in opponents’ filings.

The speaker mourns the death of President Franklin Delano Roosevelt and accepts the grave responsibilities of leadership. He calls on Americans to remain united behind ideals of freedom, justice, tolerance, and democracy, warning that the world depends on America for enlightened leadership. Rejecting partial victory and premature peace, he demands Germany’s and Japan’s unconditional surrender, vows to continue the fight until resistance ends, and insists that war criminals be punished.

He urges continued cooperation among America and its allies in defeating Axis aggression while emphasizing that lasting security must rest on law and justice rather than geographical isolation. At home, he pledges continued progress toward a more democratic society and preservation of the American way of life.

The speaker argues that peace requires an effective international organization capable of resolving disputes without war. Hope and faith are necessary, but nations must also cooperate to defend peace and avoid domination by aggressive powers. He appeals to every American, regardless of party, race, creed, or color, to support a strong United Nations and to fulfill the duties of citizenship.

Concluding that America must transition from fighting alongside other nations to living and trading with them for mutual benefit, he calls for a rational method of resolving international differences. He closes with a prayer for wisdom, faithful service, and leadership toward peace and prosperity.

South African automakers are discontinuing manual models as demand shifts toward self-shifters. Audi’s A4 range is now all dual-clutch, while BMW and Volkswagen have cut several manual variants and Volvo ended the base manual S60. Porsche and Jaguar, however, continue offering manuals.

Before Stranger Things’ third season, reported per-episode pay was $350,000 for Ryder and Harbour, $250,000 for four young cast members, and $150,000 for three teen actors—raises of up to 12 times. Millie Bobby Brown was negotiating separately; Netflix declined comment.

Documents outline Belgian-Congo supply arrangements and negotiations. Belgium agreed to facilitate development work to increase Congo exports, if desirable, without restrictions. Local authorities were compiling commodity lists, annual quantities, and automotive requirements for negotiations covering civilian consumption needs. The State Department advised that the Combined Raw Materials Board and Combined Production and Resources Board would allocate supplies and recommended promptly transmitting reciprocal-supply data to the British Foreign Office and State Department. Another telegram proposed preventing increased Congo export duties on listed commodities. Britain reported that tripartite agreement signing would be postponed and made retroactive to the Anglo-Belgian agreement’s expiration, a proposal the United States considered satisfactory. Negotiations continued through 1942–43 without agreement and were mutually discontinued; existing machinery handled supply issues, while an Office of Economic Warfare mission visited the Congo and an informal Tripartite Supply Committee was established. Subsequent sections concern U.S. recognition of war with Hungary, Bulgaria, and Rumania, a U.S.–Czechoslovak mutual-aid agreement, and Finnish-Soviet relations.

Dr Chris Bradley said Birmingham’s drains coped well during Sunday’s flooding, while Birmingham City Council attributed the flash floods to extreme rainfall overwhelming drainage systems, not blockages. Some areas received a month’s rain in one hour. A yellow warning forecasts further flooding Thursday, with thunderstorms across southern and some eastern England and the Midlands, potentially bringing 30–40 mm of rain in an hour, 60–80 mm in two to three hours, lightning and large hail.

A monthly ETF momentum strategy rotates among SPY (S&P 500), TLT (20-year Treasury bonds), and EEM (emerging markets), investing in the ETF with the best previous-month performance and holding it for one month. A two-decade backtest outperformed buy-and-hold with lower drawdowns until 2022. Excluding commissions, slippage, and taxes, the strategy’s CAGR since 2003 was 11%; its pre-2022 maximum drawdown was 22%, but it fell 41% from its 2022 peak. Performance was weak over the preceding five to six years, and frequent rotation makes tax-deferred accounts preferable.

Charlie Javice, founder of student financial-aid fintech Frank, was sentenced to 85 months in prison for defrauding JPMorgan Chase, which acquired her startup for $175 million in 2021. A jury found Javice and chief growth officer Olivier Amar guilty of three counts of fraud and one count of conspiracy to commit fraud. Frank had fewer than 300,000 real customers, but Javice and employees fabricated millions of users, including synthetic identities, before the acquisition. Javice expressed remorse, apologized to her family and asked for forgiveness, while her attorney sought a lighter sentence. The judge also imposed three years of supervision, $22.36 million in forfeiture and $287 million in restitution. Javice remains on bail while appealing. The case highlighted JPMorgan’s failure to verify Frank’s claimed customer base before the acquisition.

A widening crack forced Ineos to shut the 450,000-bpd Forties Pipeline System in the North Sea, potentially for weeks. The system carries nearly 40% of UK North Sea production, connects 85 offshore fields, and could force more than 80 platforms to shut down. Up to 10 million barrels may be disrupted over three weeks. Brent rose nearly 2% above $64.50 per barrel, reaching a two-year high. The outage could tighten Atlantic Basin supply, require the UK to seek replacement crude, widen Brent’s premium over WTI to nearly $7 per barrel, and boost U.S. crude exports and inventory drawdowns.

Investing.com's market coverage reports the S&P 500 closed Friday at its lowest level since early July, down 1.60% after falling 3.33% over two sessions from a record high of 6,427.02 to a local low of 6,212.69; last week the index lost 2.36% after gaining 1.5% the prior week, which appears to be consolidation after the advance from April lows, though a deeper correction remains possible. Apple declines dragged the index, with support near 22,300 and a potential topping pattern forming. The VIX rose to 21.90, its highest since June 23; historically, falling VIX precedes downward reversals and rising VIX precedes upward reversals. The AAII survey showed 40.3% of individual investors bullish and 33.0% bearish. S&P 500 futures traded near 6,300, with resistance at 6,330 and support at 6,280. Crude oil fell 2.79% Friday and another 2.1% after OPEC+ agreed to raise September output by 547,000 bpd, its sixth straight monthly increase; potential U.S. sanctions on Russian oil and threats of 100% secondary tariffs on buyers such as India and China (roughly 1.7 million bpd at risk) could offset the surplus. Softer jobs data, weak PMI readings, and trade-tariff uncertainty are raising demand concerns, with Goldman Sachs forecasting $64 in Q4 2025. The outlook anticipates a short-term bounce within a broader consolidation or a potential downtrend, with Palantir and AMD earnings in focus and possible defensive positioning. The page also promotes Investing.com's Stock Screener and includes risk disclosures and copyright notices.

The 2018 Scripps National Spelling Bee features 41 finalists and 113 returning spellers, including three students who devote extensive time to study. Erin Howard, 13, of Huntsville, Ala., who tied for seventh last year after misspelling "Klydonograph," studies three to four hours each weeknight and six to eight hours on weekends using both a laptop and pencil and paper, sometimes leaving sleepovers early, and now focuses on trademarked words. Cameron Keith, 12, of Boulder, Colo., wakes at 5:30 a.m. to study 200 word lists, totaling six hours on weekdays and nine on weekends, and says he now feels calmer during competition after tying for 18th in 2016. Naysa Modi, 12, of Dallas, in her fourth bee, studied by reading, typing and quizzing, and spelled "stabilizer" correctly to reach the final round. Her father, Nayan, called her ability "absolutely inhuman," said years of intense effort make a difference, and said the real reward is the strengthened relationship with his daughter and "the love of words and the love of language," not winning.

The S&P 500 reached its 9.1% average annual return but reacted negatively amid weak July economic data and renewed U.S.-China trade tensions, including Trump’s planned 100% tariff on China. July job growth was only 73,000, while May and June figures were revised down by 258,000. Corporate earnings remained strong: 15 of 17 megacap companies beat earnings expectations, lifting S&P 500 Q2 earnings growth to 11.2% from 7.7%, while sales growth rose to 5.6%.

July was the 11th consecutive seasonally positive month, but August through October historically posted positive returns only about half the time, with weak average results. AI has led the market, though 22–25 times earnings valuations and a negative equity risk premium could limit further gains. The dollar recovered to its 2024 low before being rejected, while the 10-year rate remained rangebound. The article anticipates possible market weakness and a potentially stronger year-end setup, noting that up years have averaged 17% returns since 1958.

The Michigan Court of Appeals affirmed a divorce judgment awarding the parties shared legal custody of their four children, physical custody of the two older children, Stefan and Loren, to Wesley Wiechmann, and physical custody of the younger twins, Cameron and Chase, to Sylvia Wiechmann. Although a custody specialist recommended that all four children remain with Sylvia, the trial court considered the statutory best-interests factors and concluded that separating the siblings served each child’s interests. The appellate court held that keeping siblings together is generally preferable, but an individual child’s best interests control when separation is necessary. It found no abuse of discretion or legal error and rejected the argument that the appeal was moot.

The Seamless Firmware Servicing (SFS) specification defines a secure, nonpersistent method for updating selected running AMD firmware and settings without a BIOS reflash or system reset. SFS targets priority runtime issues in AMD-provided AGESA firmware and does not update x86 BIOS components such as SMM, AGESA, or UEFI, nor run-once code such as the AGESA boot loader. Update packages target a specified PI release, base patch, firmware level, and operating state.

Customers decide whether to deploy patches and must test them in their own environments. A customer-provided SFS Deployment Agent communicates through the PSP/ASP driver. Updates can run during OS boot or system operation, apply sequentially across sockets, and must be reapplied after every reboot. Packages may modify registers or other values, replace firmware images, or update portions of firmware components.

AMD cryptographically signs every package; customers may optionally co-sign packages to require customer approval. The ASP verifies AMD signatures and, when configured, customer signatures before execution. OEM/ODM signing keys are supplied during early boot, before `BOOT_DONE`, and cannot be changed afterward. Supported keys are 2048- or 4096-bit RSA using RSA-PSS with SHA-256 or SHA-384, respectively. BIOS developers must explicitly enable SFS and any co-signing requirement.

SFS maintains three version concepts: the monotonically increasing SFS Patch Level for the overall package level, individual firmware and Security Patch Levels, and the monotonically increasing System Patch Level for run-once changes. Packages check these levels and applicable firmware versions before installation. If any package portion cannot be fully applied, the package should not be applied.

To issue commands, software constructs a 2MB-aligned `TEE_EXT_CMD_BUFFER`, appends any co-signing header and update package, and sends its address to the primary ASP through the TEE mailbox. The ASP protects the memory from x86 access, verifies customer and AMD signatures, validates and executes the patch, updates version information, and returns status. Separate commands support retrieving SFS and firmware version information and installing update packages.

SFS packages include release notes and follow names such as `fam_<family>-<AGESA-Release>-SFS-<n>.pkg`. Updates run alongside x86 and DMA traffic with minimal performance impact; some operations may require brief quiescence. SEV updates are committed automatically and require a reboot to revert, while SEV/SNP virtual machines can remain operational during supported updates.

Most Southeast Asian stock markets closed lower on Thursday, driven by fears of capital outflows after Federal Reserve minutes showed most policymakers favor beginning to trim the central bank's $4.5 trillion balance sheet later this year if economic data holds up. Wall Street also ended lower. The literature review examines artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted training as a form of distance education and considers how educational systems can remain functional during pandemics and other disruptions. It defines AI as systems that perform programmed tasks and can learn from data through machine and deep learning. Examples discussed include IBM’s Watson, which supports education and oncology, and Google’s autonomous vehicles and driverless Google Car.

Key AI concepts include algorithms, machine learning, and artificial neural networks designed to imitate the human nervous system. The passage describes Intelligent Education Systems (IES), which use domain, pedagogy, and learner models to adapt step-by-step instruction, analyze performance, and provide feedback. Three AI-based education models are identified: AI-supported face-to-face education, face-to-face instruction delivered by AI through screens or human-like robots, and simulation-based education in virtual environments. These may use fixed algorithms with human-designed curricula or deep-learning systems that develop personalized programs and make educational decisions. Related scenarios include transfer, studio, and negotiation approaches.

Possible learning environments include real-time classroom instruction with virtual teachers and online or augmented-reality simulations. Proposed simulation methods range from virtual-reality devices to future integration of computers with biological neural networks, as explored by Neuralink research. Simulated environments could provide realistic, individualized experiences unavailable in ordinary classrooms.

Potential benefits include lower training costs and risks, scalable individualized instruction, improved motivation and learning, better decision-making, and reduced classroom discipline problems. Concerns include human control, privacy and cybersecurity, social isolation, psychological effects, difficulty distinguishing simulation from reality, and unemployment among educators. The passage concludes that AI has not yet reached human mental capacity but is advancing rapidly. As stakeholders become familiar with its educational benefits, AI-based education and distance-learning alternatives are likely to require further research, especially in simulation, augmented reality, ethics, and philosophy.

El artículo analiza la aplicación del neuromarketing en el sector audiovisual y la situación del profesional del neuromarketing en España. El neuromarketing incorpora técnicas neurocientíficas a la investigación de mercados para evaluar contenidos, promociones y bloques publicitarios. En la revisión internacional realizada en webs de empresas asociadas a Nmsba, 19Offerían servicios relacionados con el entretenimiento, con mayor presencia de compañías estadounidenses y británicas.

La investigación española se basó en 18 entrevistas深度 realizadas entre junio y septiembre de 2015 a consultoras, representantes del sector audiovisual, neurocientíficos y académicos. La mayoría de los expertos consideró factible estudiar al consumidor audiovisual mediante técnicas neurocientíficas, aunque señaló limitaciones éticas, dificultades para interpretar datos y problemas de representatividad de las muestras. La investigación requiere equipos multidisciplinares con especialistas en neurociencia, marketing, comunicación y, en algunos casos, ingeniería biomédica, además de seguir el método científico.

En España, laoooo aplicación es incipiente y se concentra principalmente en Atresmedia y Mediaset España. Los servicios ofrecidos se orientan al análisis de contenidos y a mejorar la eficacia de la publicidad. Mediaset ha testar ficción mediante pulseras de actividad electrodérmica complementadas con encuestas; Atresmedia ha utilizado EEG, EMG, conductancia galvánica y actividad cardíaca para estudiar publicidad, si bien abandonó su experiencia con contenidos. TVE también aplicó estas técnicas anteriormente, pero cesó por motivos económicos.

Las consultoras interviewees Environ而又あるすべて attending respondieron haber trabajado para la industria audiovisual. El volumen medio de trabajo destinado a este sector fue del 33 % y su facturación media, del 38 %. Los servicios comenzaron aproximadamente dos años antes del estudio y crecieron exponencialmente, aunque siguen concentrándose en pocos clientes. Entre las barreras señaladas figuran el desconocimiento y la desconfianza hacia estas técnicas, la falta de cultura de innovación, las malas prácticas de otras empresas, el precio y la escasa aplicabilidad de los resultados.

Las productoras de cine y televisión muestran un interés creciente, pero no destination recursos para la investigación por sus bajos presupuestos y la falta de personal intermediario. Se prevé una evolución positiva si mejora la tecnología, se estandarizan las técnicas, se Interpretan mejor los datos, disminuyen los costes y se demuestra el retorno de la inversión. La implementación definitiva del neuromarketing audiovisual en España depende de estas mejoras y de una mayor transferencia entre universidades y empresas.

The passage presents improved indoor air quality as a potentially powerful, low-cost education intervention. Following a 2015 natural gas leak in Aliso Canyon, California, schools receiving air filters showed math gains equivalent to about three months of learning, with similar English gains that persisted and grew over time. The filters cost roughly $30 per student, compared with about $7,000 for class-size reductions yielding similar gains. Other cited research associates air cleaners with lower absenteeism, fewer illness-related absences, and improved test scores and pass rates.

Proposed benefits include sharper cognition, fewer respiratory illnesses and allergies, better attendance, and more instructional continuity. Air quality improvements may especially benefit disadvantaged students because low-income schools are more likely to be near pollution sources and housed in older, poorly ventilated buildings.

Unlike reducing class size or providing high-dosage tutoring, installing filters requires little administrative effort. The passage recommends reconnecting existing devices, piloting and expanding portable air cleaners, targeting at least 30 cubic feet per minute per student and noise below 50 decibels, and monitoring test scores, absenteeism, nurse visits, and teacher satisfaction. It also calls for philanthropic support, stronger indoor-air-quality coalitions, and larger randomized controlled trials, noting that further research and replication are needed.

Research published in *Nature Climate Change* identifies sudden, potentially irreversible ecosystem changes across Australia caused by gradual climate change combined with extreme weather. Australia has warmed by about 1°C since the start of the 19th century, with longer, more frequent and intense heatwaves, extreme fire weather, altered rainfall seasonality and unusual droughts. Even near-pristine ecosystems adapted to climatic variability are increasingly overwhelmed.

Six case studies include kelp forests becoming seaweed turf after a 2011 marine heatwave; Gondwanan refugia destroyed by 2016 lightning-started wildfire; Murray River floodplain forest dieback after the 2001–2009 drought; alpine forest converted to shrubland through repeated fires; arid-zone ecological boom and bust after extreme rainfall; and mangrove dieback across 1,000 km of the Gulf of Carpentaria.

The study explains that repeated climate “presses” and extreme-event “pulses” can push ecosystems past tipping points, cause population collapse and prevent recovery. Collapses can eliminate native species, communities and ecosystem services, affecting fisheries, water, tourism, livestock and carbon storage. Although difficult to predict, interventions such as recolonisation, reseeding and fire protection may prevent collapse, but require rapid decisions, carry costs and uncertain consequences. The authors suggest that doing nothing may increasingly pose greater risks than acting.

This retrospective cohort study used All of Us Research Program registered-tier v7 data to develop models predicting healthy aging from social determinants of health (SDOH). Eligible adults were aged 50 or older, had responded to SDOH surveys, and had electronic health records. Healthy aging was defined using comorbidities, mild cognitive impairment, and mobility; primary and secondary analyses applied age thresholds of 75 and 85, respectively. Logistic regression, multilayer perceptron, and XGBoost models were trained and evaluated using resampling, an 80:20 train-test split, cross-validation, and bootstrap confidence intervals. Model fairness was assessed across race and sex, and SHAP values identified important predictors.

The primary cohort included 99,936 participants, of whom 44,109 (44.1%) met the healthy-aging definition; the secondary cohort included 62,475 participants, with 6,648 (10.6%) classified as healthy aging. XGBoost with random oversampling performed best, with AUROC values of 0.795 for the primary cohort and 0.862 for the secondary cohort. Reported primary-cohort metrics included F1 score 0.697, recall 0.739, precision 0.659, and accuracy 0.716. The model achieved predictive parity across race and sex, with positive and negative predictive value ratios of 0.86–1.06, and showed no evidence of bias in accuracy or positive predictive value.

Health insurance type was the strongest predictor, followed by employment status, substance use, and health insurance coverage. The authors emphasized insurance’s role in healthy aging while noting limitations involving the outcome definition, possible selection bias and limited generalizability, unmeasured confounding, and the unexpected positive association between substance use and healthy aging.

Enron shares fell 21% to $20.65 after the company confirmed that the SEC had requested information concerning related-party transactions involving limited partnerships run by CFO Andrew Fastow. Enron called the request an informal inquiry, said it was cooperating, and stated that auditors, attorneys and the board had reviewed and approved the arrangements and that they had been disclosed in SEC filings. The company also said it would provide information as quickly as possible.

The partnerships had bought Enron assets and generated potential conflicts of interest for Fastow. Enron announced a $35 million partnership-related charge and said it would repurchase 55 million shares to unwind its involvement, reducing shareholder equity by $1.2 billion. Enron also reported a third-quarter loss of $618 million after $1.01 billion in charges and write-downs, including losses connected to the partnerships. Analysts raised concerns that other affiliated companies could require substantial payments, possible shareholder dilution and additional losses.

A Texas shareholder filed a derivative lawsuit alleging that Enron’s board breached its fiduciary duties by allowing Fastow to establish and manage the partnerships. Separately, Shapiro Haber & Urmy filed a securities-fraud class action on behalf of Enron shareholders who purchased stock from July 13 through Oct. 16, alleging that Enron and certain officers and directors misrepresented and concealed material facts about the partnership transactions. Enron said it had not reviewed the derivative lawsuit and did not comment on pending litigation.

The study evaluates the feasibility of replacing internal-combustion-engine vehicles with battery electric vehicles using one year of anonymized telematics data from 10,441 private car users in Asti, Italy. After filtering, the dataset contains 10,141,809 trips and more than 98.9 million kilometers. Users traveled a median of 40 km per active day, and on more than 90% of active days their cars were driven for under two hours.

Recorded trips were replicated without altering itineraries or schedules in four BEV models with different battery capacities, ranges, and road-type-specific consumption profiles. State of charge was updated after every trip under four charging policies: workplace AC charging, AC charging when state of charge falls below 25%, overnight AC charging, and fast DC charging when state of charge falls below 25%. The analysis measured trip feasibility, monthly charging frequency, and average state of charge after trips.

Workplace-only charging performed worst, allowing users to complete only 64–88% of trips on average. With the highest-range Audi A6 e-tron, 43% of users could complete at least 99% of trips under this policy. Overnight charging performed better: 35% of users were suitable for the smallest Fiat 500e, which achieved 92.7% feasible trips on average. Fast DC charging performed best overall, exceeding 98% feasibility for every model except the Fiat 500e. The Fiat was suitable for 53% of users, while the Audi was suitable for 95%; under the best scenario, 72% of users could complete all trips without changing their habits. Even this best case left 5% of users unsuited for full electrification.

Fast charging and low-threshold AC charging required nearly half as many monthly charging sessions as overnight charging for the Audi, although median charging frequency under the former policy was 1.1 sessions per month and reached 9.8 among long-distance drivers. Overnight charging generally maintained the highest post-trip state of charge, averaging above 70%.

Limitations include constant energy consumption regardless of temperature, constant charging power, assumed charging access at every parking event, and no cost-benefit analysis. The study concludes that current BEV technology accommodates many but not all users, depending heavily on charging access, behavior, and vehicle capacity.
