On November 27, 2001, Dynegy confirmed it was renegotiating its proposed acquisition of Enron after Enron’s financial disclosures, falling stock price, and weakened credit caused trading partners to reduce or stop transactions. Under the original agreement, valued at roughly $9 billion, Enron shareholders would receive 0.2685 Dynegy shares per share; discussions reportedly considered reducing the ratio below 0.15, valuing Enron at about $5 billion, or less than $6 per share.

Negotiations also addressed additional funding, extending or restructuring debt, and possible protections against litigation-related termination. Enron sought at least $500 million in cash, while J.P. Morgan and Citigroup planned to provide $250 million each as part of a broader financing package. Investors including Prince Alwaleed Bin Talal, Carlyle, and Blackstone declined to invest. Enron was also seeking to extend debt maturities beyond the merger’s expected third-quarter 2002 closing.

Enron’s credit concerns severely restricted its energy trading business. Some companies stopped selling to it in spot markets, while others traded only to offset older positions or on a limited basis. Enron reported $2.8 billion in 30-day rolling transaction value but disputed a broker’s estimate that trading volume had fallen to 25 percent of the prior month’s level. Its equity trading unit was reportedly being closed, affecting about 60 employees.

Moody’s left Enron’s rating at Baa3, the lowest investment-grade level, while S&P had it on negative watch and Moody’s was reviewing it for a downgrade. Enron shares closed at $4.14 after recovering from below $4, and its depressed bonds rebounded modestly. Merger arbitrageurs remained cautious because the revised terms were incomplete, the deal faced possible collapse, and Enron’s trading operations, debt, litigation, and liquidity remained severe concerns.

In cavity QED, quantized electromagnetic fields modify molecular electronic structure, but standard free-space quantum-chemistry methods are not directly applicable. The nonlocal, weak electron–photon coupling requires a precise, systematically improvable basis. The sinc basis converges to the complete-basis-set limit, though direct two-electron integrals scale as O(N⁴); rapid off-diagonal decay enables sparse or low-rank approximations.

The DAWN-plasma study was a prospective, multicenter, randomized, open-label phase II trial conducted from May 2020 to January 2021 in hospitalized adults with confirmed SARS-CoV-2 infection. Of 499 patients assessed, 489 were randomized 2:1 to standard of care plus convalescent plasma (n=326) or standard of care alone (n=163). The primary full analysis set included 320 and 163 patients, respectively.

The plasma group received 800–1000 mL of convalescent plasma in four 200–250 mL units, with the first two units given within 12 hours of randomization and the second two 24–36 hours later. Plasma required neutralizing antibody titers of at least 1/160; 80.7% of administered units had titers of at least 1/320. The median time to first transfusion was five hours, and the median administered volume was 884 mL. Most plasma-group patients received all four units.

The primary endpoint was the proportion of patients alive without mechanical ventilation on day 15. This endpoint did not differ between groups: 83.7% with plasma plus standard care versus 84.1% with standard care alone (odds ratio 0.99, 95% CI 0.59–1.68; p=0.976). Results were similar in the per-protocol population. A prespecified subgroup analysis showed an interaction with age (p=0.023). No statistically significant differences were found in secondary endpoints, including mortality, clinical status, oxygenation, ventilation, hospitalization, venous thromboembolism, quality of life, or laboratory outcomes.

Adverse-event rates were similar between groups. Any adverse event occurred in 28.13% of plasma recipients and 30.06% of controls; fatal adverse events occurred in 10.31% and 9.82%, respectively, while serious adverse events occurred in 20.62% and 20.68%. Treatment-related adverse events were reported in 12 plasma recipients, including seven with treatment-related serious adverse events. Transfusion-related side effects occurred in 19 of 320 plasma recipients (6.0%), with no TRALI cases. Antibody titers increased by day 6 regardless of treatment, and higher baseline and day-6 titers correlated with better outcomes.

The study followed the Declaration of Helsinki and ICH GCP guidelines, with ethics approval and informed consent. Computerized randomization was used, and the trial statistician remained blinded until database lock. Overall, early administration of high-volume, high-titer convalescent plasma did not improve the primary endpoint or other outcomes and had a safety profile similar to standard care alone.

Using pooled 2009–2020 NHANES data from 32,498 US adults, researchers used principal components analysis to identify four empirical dietary patterns and examined their prevalence by cardiovascular disease (CVD), social determinants of health, and Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP) participation. The most common, least healthy “American” pattern featured refined grains, processed meats, dairy, oils, solid fats, and added sugars and had the lowest HEI-2020 score. The “Prudent,” “Legume,” and “Fruit/Whole Grain/Dairy” patterns had progressively healthier food combinations and higher HEI scores.

Adults with CVD were more likely to follow the American pattern than those without CVD, with no significant differences for the other patterns. Each additional social risk factor was associated with higher adherence to the American and Legume patterns and lower adherence to the Prudent and Fruit/Whole Grain/Dairy patterns. SNAP participants and income-eligible nonparticipants were more likely to follow the American pattern than SNAP-ineligible adults; SNAP participants were less likely to follow the Prudent and Fruit/Whole Grain/Dairy patterns. Legume-pattern alignment was higher among SNAP participants and income-eligible nonparticipants than among SNAP-ineligible adults.

Associations involving social risk and SNAP status varied by race and ethnicity, while CVD associations did not. Sensitivity analyses produced similar findings. The cross-sectional design, self-reported exposures, and reliance on two 24-hour dietary recalls limited causal inference and dietary measurement accuracy. The study concluded that dietary patterns vary with cardiovascular health and socioeconomic vulnerability, supporting more targeted nutrition policies, counseling, and clinical interventions for groups at elevated CVD risk.

The State Bar of Michigan e-Journal for Monday, June 4, 2001, provides members free online access to case summaries, practice-area listings, classified advertisements, bar events, editorial material, news, and archived issues. A plain-text version is also available by email.

Case summaries include:

- **Helwig v. Vencor, Inc.** (Sixth Circuit): The court reversed in part the dismissal of securities-fraud allegations concerning financial projections and disclaimers about the Balanced Budget Act, then remanded for further proceedings.
- **Anchrum v. Airtouch Cellular** (Michigan Court of Appeals, unpublished): A racial-discrimination claim arising from termination failed for lack of comparator evidence, and the judgment was affirmed.
- **Kiphart v. Saturn Corp.** (Sixth Circuit): Evidence supported a disabled employee’s ADA claim concerning job rotation and reasonable accommodation; the judgment was reversed and remanded.
- **Sudul v. Donnell** (Michigan Court of Appeals, unpublished): The court found sufficient evidence of unreasonable force during an arrest but erred in denying judgment notwithstanding the jury verdict on a bystander emotional-distress claim. The decision was affirmed in part, reversed in part, and remanded for consideration of remittitur or a new trial.
- **Rock Construction, Inc. v. Onyebuchi** (Michigan Court of Appeals, unpublished): Failure to obtain financing did not excuse performance under the impossibility defense, and the sellers could recover their $13,000 down payment. The court also held that an early res judicata ruling was premature and affirmed and reversed in part.
- **In re Bonaroti** (Michigan Court of Appeals, unpublished): Placement of a juvenile with the Family Independence Agency was not disproportionately severe punishment and was affirmed.
- **People v. Baskin** (Michigan Court of Appeals, unpublished): Evidence sufficiently supported a felonious-assault conviction based on the defendant’s use of a baseball bat.

The Wham play is a complementary run concept similar to Trap, but with a tight end or fullback pulling to kick out a defensive lineman instead of a guard. Its main advantages are quickly creating favorable, unexpected running angles and changing up an offense’s normal run menu. Its weaknesses include complex installation, numerous player assignments, the need for specific formations to create a predictable front, and a requirement for a strong blocker to execute the kickout successfully. Assignments vary by defensive front and include leverage, double-team, second-level, and “most dangerous man” responsibilities. One variation, Gun H-Back Wham RPO, has the fullback kick out the nose tackle while the quarterback can throw a slant or bubble against an unfavorable box count. Another, Shotgun Influence Wham, uses pin-and-pull action to widen a 3-tech’s lane before the fullback traps him.
Microsoft filed a Form 8-K on March 13, 2020, reporting that co-founder and board member Bill Gates resigned effective that date. Microsoft’s related press release was included as Exhibit 99.1.

This descriptive cross-sectional study assessed hepatitis C virus (HCV) prevalence, transmission risks, and awareness among household members of HCV-positive patients attending CUSP in Huye District, Rwanda. HCV is described as a major global health problem associated with fibrosis, cirrhosis, hepatocellular carcinoma, morbidity, and mortality. Rwanda’s reported general prevalence was 4%, while household exposure to infected individuals was identified as an important transmission risk.

The study included 148 participants from 30 households; the calculated sample size was 180. Participants were screened using an HCV antibody rapid test, with reactive results confirmed by ELISA. Data were analyzed descriptively using Excel and SPSS.

HCV prevalence was 10.8%, with 16 participants reactive on both tests and 132 non-reactive. Unprotected sex was significantly associated with HCV positivity (p=0.016), as were histories of HBV (p=0.001) and HIV (p=0.001). Blood transfusion was not significantly associated (p=0.058). Most participants answered awareness questions incorrectly, indicating low knowledge of HCV transmission, although awareness was not significantly related to test results (p=0.079).

The findings indicated a high burden of HCV among household contacts of positive patients and supported early screening, follow-up, treatment, and household education to reduce transmission. The cross-sectional design could not determine whether infected household members acquired HCV from the index patient; phylogenetic testing and non-cross-sectional or nationwide studies were recommended.

President Donald Trump nominated Treasury senior adviser Travis Hill as chair of the U.S. Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation, subject to Senate confirmation. The passage introduces the Construction Defining Functionality (CDF) framework for analyzing computational problems through both their internal constructions and observable behavior. CDF represents a function as three structural property sets: syntactic space \(S_{\text{syn}}\), describing generative symbolic structure; semantic space \(S_{\text{sem}}\), encoding interpretations and input-output relations; and logical space \(S_{\text{log}}\), containing computational or proof-theoretic realizations. These are linked by mappings from syntax to semantics \(\alpha_f\), semantics to logic \(\beta_f\), and syntax directly to logic \(\gamma_f\).

The framework defines stability through polynomial growth bounds and explosiveness through superpolynomial growth. A function is CDF-complete when its structural components are rule- or case-definable, its mappings are structurally balanced, and those mappings are stable. A diagram is compositionally coherent when \(\gamma_f=\beta_f\circ\alpha_f\). CDF structures are classified as ComCDF when coherent with stable semantics, ExpCDF when coherence fails or semantics are explosive, and Semi-ExpCDF when partial coherence and instability coexist. The diagram is presented as connecting potential semantic pathways with actual logical outcomes.

Examples include linear and recursive functions, where syntax, semantics, and derivation or computation trees are explicitly constructed. Variable inputs can destabilize recursive mappings as recursion depth and computation trees grow, a behavior compared with the expanding search spaces of NP problems.

The passage contrasts 2SAT and 3SAT. Binary 2SAT clauses can be converted into implication pairs, yielding local composition, stable reasoning, shallow proof trees, and polynomial-time solvability. Ternary 3SAT clauses create non-local dependencies, an assignment space that can grow as \(O(2^n)\), and exponentially deep proof structures. Under CDF, this semantic explosion is attributed to 3SAT’s intrinsic clause-level structure rather than merely inefficient algorithms.

China has emerged as a global clean-energy leader, pledging to cut emissions 7–10% by 2035, reach 3,600 GW of installed wind and solar capacity, derive more than 30% of its energy mix from renewables, mainstream electric vehicles, expand carbon-market trading, and increase forest coverage. An open-label randomized controlled trial in western Cambodia evaluated primaquine for preventing *Plasmodium vivax* recurrence. All participants received artesunate, 2 mg/kg/day for seven days. Among 156 enrolled patients, 37 with G6PD deficiency received no primaquine; 119 with normal G6PD activity were randomized to no primaquine, primaquine 3.5 mg/kg over 14 days, or 7.0 mg/kg over 14 days. Participants were relocated for 90 days to a malaria-free area and monitored frequently by microscopy and PCR to minimize reinfection and distinguish outcomes.

By day 90, recurrence occurred in 81.4% of the no-primaquine group, 24.4% of the 3.5 mg/kg group, and 4.7% of the 7.0 mg/kg group. The difference between primaquine doses was significant (p=0.0141), with a hazard ratio of 0.17 for high versus low dose. The advantage of the 7.0 mg/kg regimen remained evident through day 180.

Both primaquine regimens were generally well tolerated, with no serious adverse events and no severe anemia or hemoglobin reduction exceeding 25%. Increased methemoglobin was more frequent with the 7.0 mg/kg dose than with 3.5 mg/kg (35% versus 10%) but was clinically silent and resolved after treatment.

The authors concluded that 7.0 mg/kg of primaquine over 14 days was more effective than 3.5 mg/kg and recommended its use for G6PD-normal patients in Cambodia and likely elsewhere in Southeast Asia. Limitations included the small, single-center, open-label design, inability to definitively distinguish relapse from recrudescence, and highly controlled conditions that may not reflect routine practice.

The Council of Regional Accrediting Commissions, representing seven agencies that oversee 3,000 degree-granting institutions, is encouraging colleges to use AI to improve transfer-credit evaluation and reduce credit loss. Supporters say the approach should support—not replace—faculty judgment through a “trust-but-verify” method. A 59-institution pilot is testing a platform designed to identify new course matches.

Whole-body cryotherapy, which exposes users to temperatures as low as 180 degrees below zero, is growing in popularity as an alternative-medicine wellness treatment. Invented in the 1970s by Japanese doctor Toshima Yamauchi, the treatment is not FDA-approved and can cause frostbite, burns, and eye injuries. The Israel Antiquities Authority announced a 2,100-year-old chalk bowl fragment excavated in Jerusalem in 2015, bearing the Hebrew name “Hyrcanus.” Because the name was common and belonged to Hasmonean kings John Hyrcanus and John Hyrcanus II, researchers cannot identify its owner. Found beneath a mikvah complex near the Akra fortress, it is among Jerusalem’s earliest chalk vessels, which Jews used because they were considered ritually clean.

Bollinger Bands, developed by John Bollinger in the 1980s, measure price volatility using a middle moving-average band—typically a 20-day SMA—and upper and lower bands set two standard deviations away. Traders can adjust the lookback period, standard deviation multiplier, moving-average type, and timeframe. Bands widen as volatility rises and contract as it falls; a contraction or “squeeze” often precedes a larger breakout. Repeated contact with the upper band may indicate an overbought condition or trend strength, while contact with the lower band may indicate oversold conditions or selling pressure.

The passage reviews strategies based on squeezes, breakouts, %B, band walks, bounces, band width, double bands, RSI divergence, pinch patterns, reversals, and triple-band setups. Breakouts signal potential bullish or bearish moves, %B measures price within the band range, and reversal strategies look for double tops or bottoms near the bands. Trend, volatility, and reversal interpretations depend on market context.

Testing showed limited success for stock-index strategies, some mean-reversion profitability in stocks, and greater promise for breakout approaches in gold, though results varied by asset and period. No setting, timeframe, or complementary indicator works universally.

Bollinger Bands can produce delayed or false signals, including false overbought or oversold readings, and should not be used alone. The passage recommends confirmation with RSI, MACD, the Stochastic Oscillator, price action, and broader market analysis, alongside stop-losses, position sizing, diversification, and other risk controls. Shorter timeframes generate more signals and false positives, while longer timeframes tend to provide more reliable trend signals.

The passage analyzes holiday-related seasonal patterns in U.S. stock returns, primarily using S&P 500 data from 1960–2021, with monthly returns as a benchmark. Proposed explanations include reduced liquidity, fewer macroeconomic announcements, holiday optimism, and investor risk reduction. The strongest apparent effects surround Independence Day, Thanksgiving, and Christmas, though results vary and the effects are generally small. Independence Day, Thanksgiving, and Christmas-related strategies reported average gains of 1.01%, 0.82%, and 1%, with win rates of 68%, 65%, and 67%, respectively. Post-holiday tests found no gain from holding through the holiday and stronger results on the second trading day afterward; one overnight strategy reported an average gain of 0.56%, a 71% win rate, and a profit factor of 4. The passage concludes that holiday strategies may provide limited seasonal trading opportunities but are not get-rich-quick schemes.

Scottish councils are setting budgets and may raise the basic council tax rate by up to 3%, ending the government’s long-running freeze. Decisions are left to individual councils, with some planning the maximum increase and others proposing to continue freezing rates, amid debate over council elections, austerity and protecting services.

Changes to the multiplier for bands E to H mean about 700,000 of Scotland’s 2.6 million homes—26%—will see higher bills regardless of local decisions. Most council funding comes from government grants; Glasgow raises 17% through taxation. A dispute over proposed grant reductions ended with an additional £160m for councils. The government previously estimated a maximum 3% rise across all councils would raise £70m, but this now appears unlikely.

AMD’s SEV-ES Guest-Hypervisor Communication Block Specification Agreement permits recipients to review the specification only to design products, services, or technologies that interface with AMD products and to provide optional feedback. AMD retains all rights; recipients may not duplicate or distribute the specification, remove notices, or transfer their rights. The specification is provided “AS IS,” may contain preliminary or inaccurate information, and may be changed or discontinued without notice. AMD disclaims warranties and liability for specified categories of loss. Feedback is optional and may be used, reproduced, licensed, distributed, and commercialized by AMD without restriction or confidentiality, provided it does not violate third-party intellectual-property or licensing terms. Recipients must comply with U.S., European, and other export laws. U.S. government recipients receive specified restricted rights. California law governs, disputes belong in qualifying courts in Santa Clara County, and amendments require signatures from both parties.

The accompanying specification standardizes the 4 KB, decrypted and shared Guest-Hypervisor Communication Block (GHCB) used by SEV-ES and SEV-SNP guests and hypervisors. These features protect guest register state during world switches by encrypting it and preventing direct hypervisor access or modification. The GHCB layout mirrors the SEV-ES VMCB save-state area through offset 0x3ff, exposing only state required for communication. Automatic exits do not expose guest state, while non-automatic exits cause a #VC exception; guests select the state to place in the GHCB and invoke VMGEXIT.

Version 2 adds initial SEV-SNP support, protocol negotiation, and a hypervisor feature bitmap. Later revisions document 64-bit guest-request sequence numbers, VLEK certificate identifiers and error handling, APIC ID lists, multi-VMPL operation, page-state changes, the SEV-SNP Confidential Computing Blob EFI protocol, SEV-TIO, and Secure AVIC. The GHCB address is page-aligned and communicated through MSR 0xc001_0130 and the VMCB; the hypervisor must not intercept that MSR.

The specification defines guest and hypervisor handling for non-automatic exits, including I/O and MSR protection, VMMCALL, MMIO access, SNP guest requests, AP creation, doorbells, IPIs, timers, VMPL changes, termination, and related errors. VALID_BITMAP identifies supplied and returned fields. It also covers SNP secrets and CPUID pages, SMP booting, AP reset and creation methods, NMI handling, debug-register virtualization, and Restricted Injection doorbells. Nested virtualization and SMM are not supported.

An Oct. 29, 2001 compilation of news reports chronicled Enron’s financial and credit crisis amid a broad deterioration in corporate credit. Moody’s and Standard & Poor’s projected that U.S. corporate defaults would reach roughly $100 billion in 2001, citing recession, weak cash-raising conditions, debt-financed acquisitions, buybacks and fallout from the Sept. 11 attacks.

Enron’s troubles followed disclosures of a third-quarter loss, a $1.01 billion charge and a $1.2 billion reduction in shareholder equity connected to partnerships managed by former CFO Andrew Fastow. The SEC began examining possible conflicts of interest, Fastow was removed, and Chairman Ken Lay resumed the chief executive role after Jeffrey Skilling’s resignation. Moody’s placed all Enron long-term debt under review for downgrade, citing reduced business valuations and financial flexibility, and cut its senior unsecured rating from Baa1 to Baa2. Commercial-paper rating P-2 was also placed under review; S&P retained BBB+ but changed its outlook to negative.

Enron shares fell about 9% to 10% to near seven-year lows of roughly $14, declining roughly 57% to 60% after the partnership disclosures. Its 6.4% bonds due in 2006 fell from near par to about 80 cents on the dollar, with yields rising to 12.1%. Analysts said Enron’s weakened credit could restrict access to short-term borrowing, increase funding costs, reduce trading volumes and cause trading partners to demand more restrictive terms or collateral.

Enron had drawn about $3.3 billion from bank credit lines, used roughly $2 billion to repay commercial paper and was seeking another $1 billion to $2 billion. The company said additional financing would provide liquidity needed to settle commodity trades and support its trading business. It was also selling Portland General Electric, a transaction expected to provide about $1.8 billion for debt repayment and remove approximately $1 billion of obligations, subject to regulatory approval.

Most major U.S. wholesale gas and electricity traders reported that business with Enron remained at normal levels, though they were monitoring its exposure daily. In Europe, several large energy groups had frozen or restricted dealings while seeking new credit arrangements, including letters of credit; no clear effect on market liquidity had yet emerged. Enron’s troubles also drew attention in Britain’s power market, although traders said it was too early to determine their impact.

Credit analysts expected new lenders to require higher rates, collateral or asset-sale provisions. GimmeCredit said Enron’s bonds were unlikely to become junk-rated and could be undervalued if off-balance-sheet obligations were limited to $3 billion, but also described drawing down all backup bank lines as an act of desperation. A newsletter reported that Royal Dutch/Shell might be interested in acquiring Enron; neither company confirmed the speculation.

Related commentary said Enron’s losses could undermine broader market confidence because it was widely held and raised questions about financial disclosure and the value of corporate assets. Separately, an investment article recommended independent power producers Calpine, AES, Mirant and NRG because of insider buying and opportunities to replace aging infrastructure with efficient natural-gas plants, while excluding Enron for lacking comparable insider signals. A Houston Chronicle opinion column praised Enron’s contributions to Houston’s economy and community and urged readers not to prejudge the company’s problems.

Lucas Chancel and Thomas Piketty’s report finds that India’s top 1% captured 22% of national income—the highest share since 1922—after inequality fell in the 1950s–70s and began rising in the mid-1980s. It links the reversal to pro-business policies after Rajiv Gandhi became prime minister in 1984. The paper says “Shining India” primarily benefited the top 10%, while the middle 40% grew most strongly from 1951–1980, and describes liberalization’s gains as highly unequal.

Russia has increasingly targeted Ukrainian drone pilots as high-value threats, using missiles, bombs, artillery and other weapons to strike suspected operator positions, according to Ukrainian soldiers and drone operators. Pilot deaths, once rare, have risen sharply as Russian forces focus on locating and eliminating them. Ukrainian officials say pilots are especially valuable because drones gather intelligence, direct artillery and can launch numerous inexpensive explosive weapons; recent assessments cited by Business Insider attribute about 70% of casualties on both sides to drones. Ukraine also targets Russian drone operators. Ukrainian pilots use stronger shelters, deeper underground positions and frequent rotations for protection, while tactics continue to evolve with the war.

The passage recommends 6–8 glasses (1.2 litres) of water daily, noting that food contributes some, and suggests drinking to thirst rather than following a rigid schedule. Excessive intake can dilute blood salts, causing potentially fatal water intoxication; although rare, it is particularly linked to drinking two or three litres quickly after exercise-induced dehydration. A 12-week study of people aged 55–75 found pre-meal water drinkers lost 15.5 pounds on average versus 11 pounds and ate 75–90 fewer calories per meal.

The paper introduces Doublethink, a Bayesian model-averaging method for identifying direct non-genetic risk factors in biobank-scale data while accounting for variable-selection uncertainty and measured confounding. Under specified priors and large-sample assumptions, it converts model-averaged posterior odds into adjusted p-values, enabling simultaneous control of Bayesian false discovery rates and the frequentist familywise error rate.

Using Monte Carlo Markov chain sampling in R and Python, the authors analyzed 1,912 pre-2020 variables for COVID-19 hospitalization in UK Biobank, with 1,917 cases and 200,000 controls. Nine individual variables and nine predefined groups met the reported significance thresholds. Testing groups of correlated variables recovered signals that were diluted among individual measures, including signals for age, sex, deprivation, and obesity, while post-hoc grouping identified additional associations. Comparisons with 127 published UK Biobank studies supported direct effects for established categories such as age, sex, obesity, socioeconomic status, and smoking, and for less frequently studied psychiatric disorders, infection, dementia, and aging. Diabetes, cardiovascular disease, and hypertension lacked evidence of direct effects, although this does not exclude mediated or total effects.

Limitations include the focus on direct rather than total effects, possible unmeasured confounding, selection and measurement bias, dependence on data curation and prior choices, reliance on large-sample and specific-prior assumptions, and substantial computational demands. Interactions, nonlinear effects, and some rare factors were not investigated.

The passage traces how algorithms, object-oriented design patterns, open source communities, and reusable components shaped modern software development, emphasizing that patterns provide general blueprints, shared terminology, lessons from past failures, and reusable implementations for distributed systems. Containers are presented as the foundation for these patterns, with single-node container groupings forming the atomic elements of distributed architectures.

Splitting applications into tightly coupled containers on one machine enables resource isolation, team ownership, separation of concerns, modular reuse, independent testing, and more reliable deployments. The sidecar pattern pairs an application container with a colocated container that augments it, such as adding HTTPS termination, dynamic configuration synchronization, resource monitoring, or automatic Git-based deployment. Reusable sidecars require parameterization, a stable API, and clear documentation. The ambassador pattern uses a colocated container to broker external interactions, including routing requests to sharded storage, discovering environment-specific services, and directing traffic between production and experimental services. The adapter pattern modifies or translates an application’s interface to meet a standard convention, supporting heterogeneous monitoring, logging, and health-check systems without altering third-party application images.

At the multi-node level, microservices divide applications into independently developed and scaled services connected through APIs. Although this decoupling improves team autonomy and scaling, it complicates debugging and architecture. Replicated stateless services address this by placing a load balancer before identical server replicas, providing redundancy and horizontal scale. Readiness probes determine when replicas can receive traffic, while session tracking uses IP or application-level mechanisms and consistent hashing to preserve user affinity. Caching can be deployed as a separate replicated tier with fewer, larger instances, and reverse proxies can provide rate limiting and other protections. SSL termination can be added through another replicated nginx tier.

Sharded services differ from replicated services because each shard handles only a subset of requests, making them suitable for stateful data too large for one machine. A routing root directs requests to the appropriate shard. In sharded caching, each shard stores distinct data, improving memory utilization compared with replicated caches, but a shard failure affects all requests mapped to it and can reduce hit rate, increase latency, and overload the serving layer. Systems should therefore be load-tested with and without caching and sized to tolerate cache failures or rollouts. Replacing each shard with a replicated service adds deployment complexity but provides resilience and continuous availability.

Teams should prepare for three jump-ball situations: defensive jump balls, in which the opponent has the advantage; even jump balls, in which control is nearly equal; and offensive jump balls, in which the team has the advantage.

On defense, teams should rotate early, deny passes, box out, maintain contact with the jumper, and watch the jumper’s eyes and hands for clues about the tip direction. Alignments include box, diamond, defensive, and “Y” formations, with defenders rotating clockwise or counterclockwise on a predetermined signal. A “Y” formation protects the basket against an opponent with a superior jumper and a prepared jump-ball play.

Even jump balls require boxing out, establishing inside position, anticipating the tip, and coordinated rotation on a predetermined signal. Anticipation, aggressiveness, and determination are essential to gaining possession.

Offensive teams with a height advantage of at least six inches can use proven set plays. They should generally tip forward to the tallest player, maintain defensive balance, and transition into set or motion offense if a quick shot is unavailable. The plays include Double Tap, Post Split, Jumper Fly, Forward Fly, Spread, Tandem, and Loop, each using screens, cuts, passes, or tips to create open shots and lanes toward the basket.

U.S. officials told Finnish minister Toivola that an alleged Finnish Legation statement calling peace rumors Anglo-American machinations was unverified and, if made, harmful to Finland’s interests; their discussion was cordial. Finland’s minister asked whether U.S. travel restrictions applied to American honorary consuls and Finnish mission staff, noting that Finnish diplomatic travel restrictions applied to all foreign diplomats, Helsinki was a war zone, and Finnish consular and diplomatic personnel faced no more restrictions than other Finns. A British memorandum reported that the Soviet minister in Stockholm had offered unofficial, secret contact with Finland and hinted that more favorable terms might follow. Separately, British and American officials agreed they should not appear lenient toward Finland’s continued policy. The Division of European Affairs proposed instructing Minister Schoenfeld to counter Witting’s reported optimism about peace negotiations.

A Penguins player credits goalie Marc-Andre Fleury’s key saves, Sidney Crosby’s leadership and resilience after an injury, and Mario Lemieux’s role in keeping the team in Pittsburgh. He praises the team’s sacrifices, strong core, and belief in one another, describing the Stanley Cup victory as the best day of his life and expressing confidence in the team’s future.

At the opening phase of the public inquiry into the Grenfell Tower fire, survivors and relatives paid tribute to the 72 victims and urged the inquiry to foreground their lives and the suffering of loved ones. Inquiry chair Martin Moore-Bick agreed that human accounts should come before examinations of fire spread, building materials and regulations.

Ahmed Elgwahry recounted staying on the phone as his sister and mother died. Paulos Tekle said fire authorities initially instructed his family to remain inside, and his five-year-old son died during the escape. Marcio and Andreia Gomes testified that their prematurely born son died after the fire.

Witnesses criticized the local council, building management, government officials and fire authorities over safety warnings, flammable cladding, unimplemented safety recommendations and orders to stay inside as the tower burned. The inquiry also addresses concerns that inequality contributed to the disaster.

After initially condemning “hate” but not white nationalism following the deadly Charlottesville rally, President Trump faced backlash and remained silent until Merck CEO Ken Frazier resigned from his Manufacturing Council. Trump then criticized Frazier’s drug pricing; other executives had also resigned over Trump’s policies.

Research and Markets added its “Global Industrial Hybrid Stepper Motors Market 2018-2022” report to ResearchAndMarkets.com. Based on expert input and market analysis, the report projects global revenue exceeding $1,000 million by 2022 and examines market sizing, segmentation, regional and vendor landscapes, growth prospects, applications, drivers, challenges, and trends. It identifies rising demand for automated industrial equipment, adoption of automated material-handling systems, and miniaturization as market factors, while noting competition from servo and conventional stepper motors. Hybrid stepper motors are used across process and discrete industries, with increasing deployment in industrial machinery and robotics. Vendors covered include AMETEK, MinebeaMitsumi, Moons’, Nidec, and Schneider Electric.

Dividend yields above 6% can signal cut risk, though not always. Taylor Wimpey’s forecast 7.1% yield appears affordable given its planned £450 million dividend, £511.6 million in 2016 free cash flow and strong housing demand, although housing-market cyclicality limits the longevity of special dividends. Connect Group also offers a forecast 7.1% yield, backed by cash generation and a low 7.6 forecast P/E, but its £141.7 million net debt and negative £151.8 million tangible asset value leave the payout vulnerable to weaker trading or tighter lending. The passage views Taylor Wimpey as an income opportunity for now but considers Connect’s risks greater than its potential rewards.

A 2017 Regina police survey of 462 participants found 79% rated service very good to excellent, over 80% saw integrity and honesty, and nearly 25% felt insufficient sensitivity toward Indigenous people; reconciliation training was underway.

Baseline out-of-bounds defense differs from half-court defense because it is the only situation in basketball where the defense has a numerical advantage (5 on 4), making late-game inbounds passes difficult and causing some coaches to avoid timeouts. Shooters attack the basket directly rather than moving off screens, so defensive errors yield easy baskets, and zones are vulnerable to the screens, rolls, and overloads common in out-of-bounds plays.

Four options are presented:

**Jam:** A no-switch, hard-nose defense considered most effective; it can cause five-second violations or offensive fouls. Defenders sag off to protect the middle before the inbound, aggressively jam opponents without switching, and disrupt screens to force shooters away from the basket. X3 protects the basket for three counts, then smothers the inbounder. After the pass, defenders match up or apply 5-on-3 box pressure, fronting posts and taking helpside "I" positions.

**Jump Switch:** Aggressive switching and passing-lane denial create turnovers, rushed shots, transition baskets, and offensive charges. It is recommended when under five seconds remain; coaches should not switch unless lanes will be attacked. Defenders sag off, jump-switch screens and deny rolls, smother the inbounder, then match up or box pressure.

**Trap:** Double-teaming the inbound pass can surprise the offense, forcing turnovers and easy baskets. X3 smothers the inbounder, follows the pass, and traps the receiver while teammates rotate to close out, deny reversal passes, and take helpside positions.

**Combination defenses:** Box-and-one, diamond-and-one, and triangle-and-two combine aggressive chest-to-chest pass denial by chasers with box, diamond, or triangle zone formations. These can catch offenses off guard, producing steals or forcing timeouts; zone defenders must box out and deny second efforts.

Using cross-sectional data from a prospective longitudinal multicentre cohort, the study compared proximal nerve tissue from 22 adults with clinically diagnosed Morton’s neuroma with 11 control nerves. Participants underwent neuropathic-pain phenotyping using the Neuropathic Pain Symptom Inventory and visual analogue scales. Bulk RNA sequencing was assessed by differential-expression, gene-ontology, weighted co-expression, and cell-deconvolution analyses, while immunofluorescence assessed immune cells, myelin, and axons.

RNA sequencing separated Morton’s neuroma from controls and identified 3,349 differentially expressed genes: 1,461 upregulated and 1,888 downregulated. Upregulated genes were enriched for immune and inflammatory responses, whereas downregulated genes were enriched for nervous-system development, axon guidance, and myelination. A defence-response co-expression module correlated positively, and a neurogenesis module negatively, with paroxysmal pain; only the defence-response association survived multiple-comparison correction. Deconvolution showed higher macrophage and memory B-cell proportions and lower CD4+ T-cell proportions in Morton’s neuroma, with macrophage proportions correlating with paroxysmal pain. An upregulated MARCO–CD163–STAB1 signature characteristic of M(GC) macrophages correlated with paroxysmal pain and paraesthesia.

Immunofluorescence confirmed demyelination and increased intraneural T-cell and CD163+ macrophage densities, including CD163+MARCO+ cells, in Morton’s neuroma. Overall β-tubulin III and CD68+ cell densities did not differ significantly between groups, although CD68+ density correlated with burning pain; macrophage-subset densities did not correlate with pain phenotypes. Given a median symptom duration of 2.5 years, the findings support persistent local neuroinflammation in chronic human peripheral neuropathic pain and identify MARCO+ M(GC) macrophages as potentially relevant to paroxysmal pain. Limitations included varied control-nerve locations and composition, sex imbalance, small sample size, tissue variability, and limited histological validation.

The paper extends iterative proportional fitting (IPF) for Schrödinger bridges to data-to-energy and energy-to-energy settings, where one or both marginal distributions are available only as queryable unnormalized densities or energy functions with unknown normalizing constants. Existing IPF variants require samples from both marginals, while standard diffusion-model training is a one-step degenerate IPF case. The proposed method uses off-policy reinforcement-learning losses and diffusion-sampler stabilization techniques to train IPF steps efficiently and is presented as the first general method for inferring data-to-energy and energy-to-energy Schrödinger bridges. It learns stochastic bridges with low transport cost between synthetic datasets and densities, comparable to data-to-data IPF using samples from a ground-truth oracle. The formulation also enables data-to-data IPF to learn the diffusion coefficient in addition to the drift. Applying data-to-energy IPF to translating priors into posteriors in generative-model latent spaces extends outsourced diffusion sampling to provide a scalable, data-free image-to-image translation method. The passage also formalizes the Schrödinger bridge as minimizing KL divergence to a reference process subject to fixed endpoint marginals and relates it to optimal transport.

The passage compiles news clippings from May 26–27, 2001 concerning Enron, California’s electricity crisis, federal energy regulation, the Dabhol project in India, and international gas ventures.

Kenneth Lay met privately with Los Angeles Mayor Richard Riordan, Arnold Schwarzenegger, Michael Milken and other California leaders at a Beverly Hills hotel to promote Enron’s plan for the state’s energy crisis. The four-page proposal called for continued deregulation, rate increases, consumer responsibility for public-utility debt, an end to investigations of power-price manipulation, and greater conservation through peak-use pricing. Enron said California needed to increase energy supply and reduce demand. Gov. Gray Davis’s spokesman called the plan a “generator’s wish list,” and participants in the meeting were reportedly noncommittal; none signed an accompanying letter to state officials. Enron reported first-quarter revenue of $50.1 billion, up 281 percent from the prior year.

A Field Poll found that 63 percent of Californians had reduced energy use by at least 10 percent since the crisis began, while nearly one in four had cut consumption by at least 20 percent. Residents described measures such as unplugging appliances, air-drying clothes and using fewer pool and hot-tub facilities, often reducing bills without major lifestyle sacrifices.

Houston’s highest-paid executives were heavily concentrated in energy: eight of the top 10 came from oil and gas companies, and four of the top six were from Enron. Nabors Industries chairman Eugene Isenberg led the list with $63.9 million. Enron Broadband Services chairman Kenneth Rice ranked second with $47.4 million, while Lay ranked sixth with $35.7 million; differences in stock-option grants contributed to the rankings. The article also described how companies use options and other incentives to retain executives, and how some shifted toward cash bonuses when stock prices weakened.

The dispute over Enron’s Dabhol power plant in Maharashtra worsened after Dabhol Power Corp. rejected a roughly $39 million payment from the Maharashtra State Electricity Board because it was made under protest and the board had moved to rescind the contract. The $3 billion project, then 65 percent owned by Enron, had generated no revenue for months amid unpaid bills. Maharashtra officials accused Dabhol of misrepresenting its ramp-up performance and said low utilization had raised tariffs; Dabhol denied misrepresentation and maintained that low capacity use resulted from the board buying only about 15 percent of available power, compared with roughly 60 percent previously. Dabhol issued a preliminary termination notice, while the electricity board sought regulatory review, fines and damages of about 7 billion rupees. Indian lenders planned to meet foreign lenders in Singapore to discuss guarantees, further disbursements and reported cost overruns of about $400 million, while continuing to favor completion of the nearly finished project. Indian and state officials continued negotiations to resolve the dispute.

Saudi Arabia was preparing preliminary agreements for three multibillion-dollar natural-gas joint ventures involving ExxonMobil, Shell, BP, Phillips Petroleum, TotalFinaElf, Conoco, Occidental Petroleum and Enron. Exxon led the Red Sea venture with Occidental and Enron, while South Ghawar and Shaybah leaders were still being determined. The projects were expected to cover gas development, processing, pipelines, power, desalination and petrochemicals. Analysts expected Saudi Aramco to participate; a report said the government required foreign companies to accept Aramco as a partner, with majority voting rights on key issues, if it sought participation.

Sen. Dianne Feinstein requested hearings into possible improper ties between Federal Energy Regulatory Commission members and energy companies. Reports described conflicting accounts of a call between Lay and FERC Chairman Curtis Hebert: Hebert said Lay offered support if he favored Enron’s deregulation views, while Lay said Hebert sought Enron’s assistance with the White House. Enron also reportedly interviewed candidates for FERC positions and supplied the administration with preferred choices. The Senate confirmed Patrick Wood III and Nora Brownell to the five-member commission, and Vice President Dick Cheney indicated that Wood would replace Hebert as chairman.

After Vermont Sen. James Jeffords left the Republican Party, Democrats were expected to gain control of the Senate. Jeff Bingaman was set to replace Frank Murkowski as chairman of the Senate Energy and Natural Resources Committee, improving the prospects for a Feinstein-Smith bill imposing temporary restraints on wholesale electricity sales in the West. The measure still faced opposition from President Bush, Vice President Cheney and House Republicans. Polling cited in the passage found that 60 percent of Californians disapproved of Davis’s handling of the electricity crisis, while 56 percent disapproved of Bush’s response.

Other reports said Enron had stopped making new investments in India and reassigned most of its local employees to Dabhol Power and Broadband Solutions, effectively reducing Enron India to a holding company. A separate article compared the personal wealth of Republican Greg Ganske and Democratic Sen. Tom Harkin in a prospective 2002 Iowa Senate race and noted the Harkins’ holdings in Enron and Conoco. An editorial criticized California Attorney General Bill Lockyer’s personal remarks about Lay while arguing that legislators who supported deregulation shared responsibility for the state’s shortages.

Coaches reflected on a one-goal playoff game, noting the lone goal came two minutes in and their side missed promising chances, including by Saprykin and Leopold. They said low-scoring games require capitalizing on scarce opportunities and acknowledged that winning two straight was their biggest challenge. They emphasized their team’s speed, rather than physicality, as a decisive factor in victories over Detroit and against Vancouver and San Jose, and pledged not to change their style. They also discussed line deployment, fatigue, interperiod recovery, conference differences, draft and restricted free-agent preparation, media duties, and roster limits under collective bargaining.

The article defines overnight trading as buying at the close and selling at the next day’s open or close. It identifies the main historical edge as occurring between the close and the next open, while noting that the average open-to-close gain has been zero over the last 30 years.

Using SPY backtests dating to 1993, the article examines roughly 24-hour strategies based on Turnaround Tuesday, holidays, the end-of-month effect, other weekday patterns, mean reversion, and options expiration. A mixed strategy combining mean-reversion, breakout, and gap signals averaged 0.41% per trade across 237 trades. The article reports strong overall portfolio performance, low commissions and slippage, limited strategy variables, and no apparent curve-fitting or survivorship bias, while cautioning that all backtests are approximations and require sound logic and judgment.

The portfolio discussion argues for combining many uncorrelated strategies across different asset classes, time frames, and strategy types. Diversification can reduce overlapping trades, drawdowns, and downside risk, allowing returns to compound more effectively than relying on a few purportedly perfect strategies. Mean-reverting and trend-following strategies can complement each other, while weak standalone short strategies may still improve portfolio risk. Automated or mechanical execution is recommended because entering and exiting at the close can be cumbersome.

SpaceX is launching an unmanned Dragon cargo spacecraft to the ISS with 6,400 pounds of supplies, including scientific equipment and ice cream. It is the final mission using a brand-new Dragon; subsequent missions will use flight-proven hardware.

A hockey team reflects on its long playoff run and what it takes to win: strong depth on defense (Klemm, DeVries, Skoula), speed and talent at forward, and the importance of positioning and containment rather than risky hits against players like Arnott and Holik. Players emphasize respecting opponents' strengths, using every player's talent, and staying fresh so someone is always ready to battle. They note that deep playoff runs require everything to be in order — injuries, emotions, confidence — and that reaching this stage, after years of pressure and a lack of hype, feels special. Despite outside attention on one star player, the focus stays on starting fresh, keeping it simple, and playing for the fans.

Small-sided soccer games (SSGs) feature two teams of fewer than 11 players on reduced fields and can be used in practice or competition. They increase ball touches, player involvement, decision-making, and development. Practice games range from 3v3 to 9v9 and target tactics such as attack, defense, possession, passing, movement, shooting, transitions, and goalkeeping. Younger players use fewer players and smaller spaces; teams need not have equal numbers.

In August 2017, U.S. Soccer established Player Development Initiatives for competitive youth SSGs from U6 through U12, including age-specific player numbers, smaller fields, goals and balls, shorter games, and adapted rules. U9 games use build-out lines, and offside is not permitted before U9. Headers and goalkeeper punts and drop kicks are banned. U.S. Soccer requires youth member organizations to implement the standards locally.

Dr. Pasvolsky explained that “peace-loving states” was chosen as a membership criterion to emphasize the organization’s purpose of enabling all nations to live at peace. Determining which states qualified would be linked to initial membership. Under the Dumbarton Oaks proposal, the Security Council would recommend admission and the Assembly would decide, although the smaller Council was considered preferable for initiating action and the Assembly could refuse admission.

Mexico’s ambassador stated that Chapter III should promote permanent peace through cooperation among all states and avoid the errors of the organization established after the previous war. Chapter IV was intended to indicate only the principal organs, assigning peace and security functions to the Security Council, conditions conducive to peace to the General Assembly, and legal matters to the International Court of Justice. The Economic and Social Council’s placement under the Assembly could be changed in the final document.

Chapter V addressed Assembly membership and powers. Mexico proposed three delegates per country, while other commentaries favored no limit. Pasvolsky said functions were divided among distinct bodies, with primary, continuous responsibility for peace and security resting with the Security Council. The Assembly could discuss any related issue, act independently, and make recommendations, while supporting Council action and avoiding duplication. Its major role would include international relations and encouraging most nations to support the organization’s principles.

The Syrian opposition seeks direct talks with the government on political transition at Geneva negotiations beginning February 23. HNC spokesman Salim al-Muslit said President Bashar al-Assad should have no role in a transitional government, envisioned in the 2012 Geneva communiqué as a mutually agreed body with full executive powers.

A Northern California jury convicted Gonzalo Curiel, 20, of the 2015 torture, starvation and beating of a 7-year-old boy and his 3-year-old sister, whose bodies were found in a Redding storage unit, and of torturing their older sister in their Salinas apartment. Curiel's former girlfriend and the children's relative, Tami Huntsman, pleaded guilty to two murder counts. The girl, now 12, was the main witness in Curiel's trial. Both were scheduled to be sentenced the following week.

The passage describes systems, devices, and methods for focused sterilization of in vivo analyte-monitoring systems. Conventional two-piece systems separate the sensor and sharp from the electronics because radiation sterilization may damage electronic components, while gaseous chemical sterilization using ethylene oxide may damage sensor chemistry. This separation requires distinct packaging and sterilization processes, additional components, and final user assembly, increasing the risk of user error and contamination.

The disclosed one-piece architecture provides a fully assembled sensor control device within an applicator, reducing packaging, fabrication and assembly steps, waste, and possible errors or contamination. The control device includes an electronics housing, printed circuit board, processor, power source, sensor, and insertion sharp. It communicates analyte data with a reader and may connect to remote systems or networks. The applicator inserts the sensor beneath the skin, after which the sharp retracts and an adhesive patch retains the control device.

A collimator within the applicator cap defines a sterilization zone around the protruding sensor and sharp. Focused electron-beam or other radiation sterilizes those components while the collimator impedes radiation from reaching sensitive electronics. Seals protect a sterile region containing the sensor and sharp; an additional shield may protect the processor. Embodiments also describe internal or external collimators, varied sterilization-zone shapes and apertures, radiation-permeable barrier layers, and external assemblies that direct gamma, X-ray, or electron-beam radiation toward selected parts while shielding radiation-sensitive components. Figures depict the applicator, sensor control device, plug and sharp assemblies, seals, collimators, shielding structures, and assembly and deployment configurations.

This continuation patent application discloses metal-assisted delayed fluorescent (MADF) emitters employing benzo-imidazo-phenanthridine and analogues. General Formulas I–XIII cover cyclic platinum(II) and palladium(II) complexes, while General Formulas XIV–XVII cover octahedral iridium(III) complexes. These emitters can exploit both singlet and triplet excitons; judicious ligand design creates a small singlet–triplet energy gap that enables thermally assisted delayed fluorescence while remaining triplets emit through phosphorescence. Such emitters may provide unity internal quantum efficiency, short lifetimes, and full-color emission for displays and lighting.

The compounds may be used in emissive compositions, OLEDs, lighting devices, photovoltaic devices, and luminescent displays. A disclosed OLED includes a substrate, anode, hole- and electron-transport layers, light-processing material, and metal cathode, with emission tunable through the electronic structures of the emitter, host, or both. The specification defines permissible substituents and chemical groups and provides synthetic examples involving ligand coupling in DMSO followed by formation and chromatographic purification of palladium or platinum complexes. It also identifies emission spectra and OLED efficiency and spectral data. The invention was supported by the Department of Energy under award DE-EE0007090, with certain government rights.

- The Financial Times reports that severe storms are increasing corporate awareness of weather-related risks, including lost business, infrastructure disruption, and insurance costs. Weather-risk derivatives were valued at $3 billion–$8 billion and are expanding in Europe through futures, hedge funds, insurance programs, and specialized trading sites. Enron planned to launch 17 European sites. Market growth was constrained by an imbalance between demand for warm- and cold-weather protection, limited liquidity, high weather-data costs, and low corporate awareness. Société Générale was the only bank then committed to the market, while LIFFE planned weather futures for early 2001.

- In a Houston arena debate ahead of a referendum, supporters said a new arena would promote downtown development, strengthen the economy, and enhance Houston’s reputation. Opponents accused backers of taxpayer-funded corporate welfare and questioned the deal’s fairness to the team’s billionaire owner.

- An Azurix shareholder sued Azurix and Enron, alleging that Enron’s $275 million financing for a $7-per-share take-private transaction undervalued the water company. The shareholder sought class-action status, an order stopping the transaction, damages, and legal fees; Azurix said it had not been served.

- C.I. Global Fund, managed by William Sterling, had a $3.2 billion portfolio and a 17.7% average annual return over 10 years, versus 13.7% for global-equity peers, though performance was nearly flat year to date. The fund used a growth-oriented, broadly diversified strategy with about 140 stocks, limited individual positions, and little currency hedging. Sterling had reduced U.S. and European exposure amid technology-stock volatility and interest-rate concerns. Enron was among its largest holdings at 1.6%.

- A FERC committee recommended reforms for California’s wholesale electricity market after prices tripled, finding no evidence of generator price collusion. The proposals would let utilities buy from multiple suppliers and use forward markets, but generators raised concerns about a proposed $150-per-megawatt soft cap and possible refunds. Enron postponed plans for 300 megawatts of new California generation because of continuing uncertainty, while expecting opportunities for its price-risk management operations.

- Enron’s proposed $275 million loan would allow Azurix to repurchase public shares at $7 each while limiting Enron’s ownership and avoiding consolidation of Azurix’s $1.3 billion debt. The arrangement appeared intended to prepare Azurix for a sale, potentially as a whole because Wessex Water collateralized a £400 million credit facility. Azurix had missed earnings expectations, accumulated debt, and delayed projects, leading Enron to reassess Wessex and Latin American assets and consider exits from the water business.

- A train derailment near Transwestern’s New Mexico pipeline cut gas flows by about 250 million cubic feet per day, or 25%, while the line was inspected; no injuries were reported.

- U.S. natural-gas cash prices mostly rose as storage constraints limited arbitrage and the Transwestern outage redirected gas. NYMEX December futures settled at $4.686 per million Btu, up 19.6 cents, while western, California, and New York gas traded above $5.

On March 3, 2015, Tesla Motors’ Board amended its 2010 Equity Incentive Plan to prohibit transactions intended to reprice equity awards and amended its bylaws to adopt majority voting in uncontested director elections, while retaining plurality voting in contested elections. Neither amendment required stockholder approval. The amended plan and bylaws were filed as Exhibits 10.1 and 3.1, respectively.

The lecture outlines a construction of succinct non-interactive arguments (SNARGs) from batch arguments (BARGs) and somewhere extractable hash functions, also called somewhere statistically binding hash functions.

A BARG for an NP language consists of generation, proving, and verification algorithms. It batches many instances while producing a proof whose size depends polynomially on one witness but only polylogarithmically on the batch size. It has standard completeness and computational soundness. In semi-adaptive soundness, a cheating prover may choose its instances after seeing the CRS but must designate the false instance’s index before seeing the CRS; the other instances may be arbitrary. Converting this to fully adaptive soundness is difficult because hardwiring an index into an indistinguishable CRS may cause the prover to switch which instance is false, and membership in the language may be hard to determine.

A somewhere extractable hash family consists of algorithms for generating a hash key and trapdoor, evaluating a succinct hash value, opening a selected bit, verifying an opening, and extracting the selected bit using the trapdoor. Its required properties are completeness, index hiding, and somewhere statistical binding: even an unbounded adversary given the hash key cannot produce two valid, different openings at the designated location except with negligible probability. Index hiding extends computational binding to all locations for polynomial-size adversaries. Repeating the construction produces a hash that is extractable and binding on multiple locations; revealing some associated trapdoors does not expose the remaining hidden indices. The lecture also sketches an FHE-based, Merkle-tree-like construction in which encrypted index bits select a path. A straightforward version permits malformed ciphertexts and lacks binding, while layered keys and decrypt-and-re-encrypt evaluations ensure that selected-path ciphertexts are well formed. The required homomorphic computation has bounded depth, so fully general FHE is unnecessary; a single-key alternative requires circular security.

For index-language BARGs, the batched instances have succinct descriptions, allowing verifier runtime to depend on that description and logarithmically on the batch size rather than linearly on it. A BARG can be made somewhere extractable by attaching a somewhere extractable hash of the witnesses and upgrading the proved language to include valid witness openings.

The SNARG construction generates a hash key and a BARG CRS. For an instance and optional witness, the prover evaluates the verification circuit, hashes all wire values, and supplies a BARG proof showing that every gate has valid openings to its two input wires and output wire and that those values satisfy the gate; it also shows that the output is 1. The proof consists of the hash value and the BARG proof, and the verifier accepts exactly when the BARG proof verifies. Index-language structure lets the verifier avoid explicitly processing every batched gate statement, yielding runtime and proof size that are polylogarithmic in the circuit size, apart from reading the instance. The hash value grows with the number of extractable locations, so the construction seeks to keep that number polylogarithmic in the circuit size. The lecture presents the construction and defers its detailed analysis until after a break.

The passage criticizes psychiatric diagnosis and treatment, arguing that mental illness should not be equated with brain disease and that psychiatry is not subject to the same standards of falsification as other medical fields. It recounts a pregnant, suicidal girl sectioned under the Mental Health Act after her request for an abortion was denied; a second psychiatrist found no evidence of mental disorder, and she was released. The author also describes a grandmother detained for psychosis, forcibly given ECT despite her family’s objections and treated with medications that caused severe reactions, including three weeks of catatonia. Recalling her own diagnosis of severe depression at 18, the author questions symptom-based diagnoses, disputed theories of chemical imbalance, and reliance on SSRIs, which only about 40 percent of users report as helpful. Citing Thomas Szasz, she notes that definitions of mental disorder are influenced by culture and politics, as illustrated by homosexuality’s classification in the DSM until 1980. Despite acknowledging that psychiatric intervention can sometimes help, she says little is understood about mental illness and calls for greater public awareness.

Amazon.com, Inc. reported that Andrew R. Jassy would become President and CEO on July 5, 2021. The board elected him as a director effective that date. Amazon approved a restricted stock unit award covering 61,000 common shares, vesting over ten years, and appropriate security arrangements. Jassy will also enter an indemnification agreement matching those of other directors. He joined Amazon in 1997 and has led Amazon Web Services since its inception, serving as senior vice president from 2006 to 2016 and CEO from April 2016.

The paper investigates how cavity photons can amplify responses near magnetic quantum critical points. It focuses primarily on a cavity mode coupled to the ferromagnetic transverse-field Ising model. When the cavity couples directly to the critical magnetization, the Ising and Dicke terms cooperate because they commute. Large-spin analysis shows that the critical coupling for a superradiant phase transition decreases with the exchange interaction and vanishes as the field approaches the Ising quantum critical point from above. Consequently, the superradiant phase is accessible at arbitrarily weak light–matter coupling in the quantum-critical regime.

Density matrix renormalization group calculations for a spin-½ chain confirm the qualitative phase diagram. They find a continuous boundary between the paramagnetic and superradiant phases on the disordered side, with \(g_c\propto(h-h_{\mathrm{TFIM}})^{0.65}\), close to the large-spin exponent of \(2/3\).

The coherent mixing of cavity photons and critical matter modes produces intrinsic two-mode squeezing. The minimum quadrature variance approaches zero at the superradiant transition, while its scaling depends on the location of the system relative to the Ising critical point. Near the quantum critical point, squeezing is stronger than in the pure Dicke model or the disordered regime. The conjugate variance diverges as \(1/(g-g_c)\), stronger than the corresponding Dicke-model scaling, indicating enhanced light–matter entanglement and quantum Fisher information. In the ordered regime, long-range spin order prevents comparable squeezing, leaving only imperfect photon-sector squeezing.

When the cavity couples orthogonally to the Ising order parameter, the Ising and Dicke terms compete rather than cooperate. This produces a more complex phase diagram with discontinuous and continuous superradiant transitions and a tricritical point near the Ising quantum critical point. Anomalous condensate scaling with exponent \(\beta\approx0.25\) occurs near this point. A one-dimensional ferromagnetic XY model shows the same general trend: the critical cavity coupling is minimized near its quantum critical region whether the cavity couples to a critical or non-critical matter mode.

The proposed mechanism could be tested using cavity-coupled magnetic materials such as CoNb\(_2\)O\(_6\), LiHoF\(_4\), and CrI\(_3\), building on demonstrated cavity-magnonic coupling. The suppression of the critical coupling and enhanced squeezing and entanglement may also extend to driven-dissipative systems. Overall, the work identifies quantum critical fluctuations as a means of amplifying cavity responses, facilitating weak-coupling superradiance, improving metrological squeezing, and increasing light–matter entanglement.

Preparations for an Inquiry were underway across several fields. This application is a continuation of U.S. Ser. No. 15/943,581, a divisional of Ser. No. 15/285,820 (now U.S. Pat. No. 9,969,285), claiming priority to provisional applications 62/237,245 and 62/265,703.

Background: UAVs are increasingly used in commercial applications such as inspecting railway lines and electrical power lines and monitoring quarry and construction sites. Commercial UAVs are typically battery-powered, and battery technology is the primary limitation on range and capability, with current UAVs flying roughly 30 minutes with a usable payload. Batteries currently require manual exchange, making automation of exchange a key factor in wide commercial UAV use.

Summary of invention: The Reconfigurable Power Station (RPS) is an autonomous system designed to extend the range and capabilities of multiple, potentially disparate, unmanned systems — including ground, underground, water surface, underwater, and space vehicles — with the UAV embodiment described in detail. The RPS detects a UAV signal requesting a new Swap Cartridge (SC) and, using identifiers such as vehicle type, vehicle SC, SC status, and vehicle location, determines the landing. As the UAV closes to a threshold distance (e.g., 1, 3, 6, 10, 20 feet) above the station, it is guided in using sensors in the onboard Universal Integrated Swap (UIS) system and visible or non-visible illuminators embedded in the landing zone deck. Once landed, a landing gear retention system mechanically and electrically connects to the UAV.

Major components: The RPS includes a housing/enclosure with a landing zone sized for one or more UAV types; a dynamic terminal landing system (DTL) supporting autonomous landing, cartridge exchange, and takeoff; a power source for landed UAV flight systems; modular power bays (MPBs) housing multiple SC types and sizes (electric batteries, hydrogen fuel cells, fossil fuels, or payloads); a universal SC swapping mechanism; a central processor; and sensors. The onboard Universal Swap Cartridge Processor (USP) includes a transmitter, receiver, cameras capturing visible and/or non-visible landing-zone imagery, and an embedded battery. SCs contain power or payload media, electrical/signal connectors, mating tracks, unique identifiable markers (e.g., barcodes) for optical reading and tracking, and mechanical locking. The DTL uses scalable composite images (e.g., QR codes, AprilTags) that change size and pattern according to UAV altitude to aid landing. MPBs are line replaceable units with homogeneous or heterogeneous SC arrangements (e.g., stacked or two-by-two), and the RPS central processor monitors environmental conditions (temperature, pressure, wind speed/direction, humidity, visibility) to determine flightworthiness.

Exchange method: A UAV requests landing permission via its USP; the RPS-CP places it in a landing queue and grants permission, and the USP guides it onto the landing zone via the DTL. After landing, mission/payload data may be downloaded, the UIS located, the depleted SC withdrawn and transferred to an MPB for replenishment or storage, and a fully energized compatible SC inserted into the onboard Swap Cartridge Receptacle. The depleted SC is charged when an external power source is connected, otherwise stored in the MPB queue or charged internally. Following environmental assessment and preflight checks, the UAV is cleared to depart and resume flight.

JM Smucker sued Trader Joe’s in the U.S. District Court for the Northern Ohio, alleging that its frozen crustless peanut butter and jelly sandwiches copied Uncrustables’ trademarked design.
