Experimental studies show that injected currents can generate wavevector-dependent orbital angular momentum (OAM), producing orbital Hall and orbital Rashba–Edelstein effects. The main approach measures orbital torque in magnetic heterostructures, requiring conversion of OAM into spin angular momentum through spin–orbit coupling. Ni and permalloy are efficient converters, while Pt and 4f transition metals can serve as added conversion layers. Material-dependent torque is used to identify orbital effects, but quantitative torque analysis is difficult because OAM generation, interfacial transport, spin conversion, spin transport, and torque transfer are not easily separated. Other approaches include magnetoresistance, reciprocal orbital pumping and THz emission, direct imaging of OAM accumulation by magneto-optical or electron microscopy methods, and orbital Hanle magnetoresistance.

CuOx was identified as a strong OAM source: orbital currents in TmIG/Pt/CuOx increased magnetic torque sixteenfold after conversion to spin in Pt, and strong orbital accumulation was observed in Ni–Fe/CuOx. Thickness-dependent measurements indicated longer OAM transport than spin transport, while torque signs helped identify orbital contributions. Orbital torque has since been observed in antiferromagnets, two-dimensional systems, and perpendicular ferromagnets. Orbital pumping and reciprocal charge–orbital transport were also reported, although their reciprocity remains unclear. In bilayer transition-metal dichalcogenides, theory favors the orbital Hall effect over the valley Hall effect as the appropriate description of OAM transport and predicts possible topological orbital Hall insulating states. Intrinsic orbital torque has also been found in two-dimensional layered compounds.

Theory predicts a universal bulk orbital Hall effect and an interfacial orbital Rashba–Edelstein effect that can exist without spin–orbit coupling. When their OAM currents enter a ferromagnet, they exert orbital torque. Torque magnitude depends on OAM accumulation, Hall conductivity, interfacial effects, and relaxation. Strong orbital–lattice coupling, mediated by crystal fields of roughly 1 eV, efficiently generates OAM currents but also promotes their dissipation and quenching. Experiments report orbital relaxation lengths much longer than spin relaxation lengths, whereas first-principles studies predict either long-range torques from orbital-band hotspots or extremely short OAM diffusion lengths in normal metals. This discrepancy remains unresolved.

Orbital torque could support MRAM, oscillators, random-number generators, logic devices, THz emitters, and unconventional computing. Unlike spin torque, OAM generation can enable low-resistivity light metals such as Ti, V, and Cr. MRAM implementation nevertheless faces challenges: reported torque efficiencies reach only about 0.3 but must be higher; strong torque must coexist with high tunneling magnetoresistance and MgO-compatible ferromagnets such as CoFeB; and layer thicknesses must be reduced despite long OAM diffusion lengths. One device study reported a 50% reduction in switching power relative to a Pt spin–orbit-torque device.

Further progress requires resolving OAM generation, long-distance and interfacial transport, orbital-to-spin conversion, and relaxation. Crystal and interface engineering may tune these effects, while possible coupling to photons and phonons may enable new branches of condensed-matter physics.

This email from Enron (Nov. 19, 2001) compiles press clippings on Enron and financial markets:

- **Zero-coupon convertible bonds (Fortune):** Companies including Enron and Merrill Lynch issued "zeros" as stock prices faltered. With roughly $65 billion puttable over three years, bondholders can sell bonds back to issuers, forcing companies such as Tyco, Comcast, Calpine and Solectron to repay debt and refinance at high rates, with possible shareholder dilution. About 40% of issues are bought by hedge funds that short the same issuers' stock (Supervalu lost 10% of market value on a $185 million zero announcement). Tax and accounting loopholes continue to attract issuance — seven new issues totaling $3.5 billion since Oct. 1. A ConvertBond.com table rates put-date risk for ten companies, including Enron ($1.331 billion puttable Feb. 7, 2004; "very risky"), Verizon and Merrill Lynch (not yet problems).

- **WSJ "Manager's Journal" (Bodily & Bruner):** Argue Enron left an enduring legacy in deregulation, de-integration of power contracts, reduced transaction costs, network optionality, rigorous risk assessment and a fast, innovative culture — but note that erosion of equity, not trading risk, destroyed the firm, and that Dynegy's acquisition risks losing a major R&D establishment.

- **WSJ stock-picking survey:** J.P. Morgan's basket fell 8.6% in Q3, the only one of 15 to decline under 10%, versus the S&P 500's 14.7% drop; Goldman Sachs (-23.2%) and Credit Suisse First Boston (-30.1%) finished last; Edward D. Jones had the best five-year return (85%).

- **NYT/Financial News:** WestLB of Düsseldorf is among suitors for Wessex Water, which Enron is selling with other noncore assets in India and Brazil; the price is expected between $1 billion and the $1.4 billion paid in 1998, with likely regulatory scrutiny.

- **WSJ credit markets:** Record bond issuance (over $600 billion expected in 2001 vs. $411 billion in 2000) is largely refinancing short-term commercial paper, so it will not lift the economy much; AT&T sold $10.9 billion; Enron drew $3.3 billion from bank lines to repay commercial paper investors; Treasurys suffered their worst selloff since 1987.

- **Enron filings and merger:** Investors awaited a delayed third-quarter 10-Q expected to detail Enron's and affiliated partnerships' debt; Enron restated four years of net income downward by $586 million and closed at $9. The Dynegy deal ($24 billion in one report, $15.6 billion in another) followed a 67% three-week stock plunge; FERC review is expected to take six to nine months or longer, plus DOJ/FTC and state consent, with analysts assigning a 65%-75% chance of completion and Enron's trading counterparties limiting exposure.

- **India:** BSES began due diligence on the 2,184-megawatt, $2.9 billion Dabhol project (Enron 65%, MSEB 15%, GE and Bechtel 10% each), targeted for January 2002; Enron seeks to sell at cost due to MSEB payment defaults, and Dabhol Power Co. will await the Bombay High Court verdict before sending a termination notice.

- **Other:** The Pilgrim Russia Fund (ING-owned) gained 53% year to date; Janus Capital trimmed its Enron stake; Business Standard argued all foreign investors in India's power sector want out, citing the failed separation of generation, transmission and distribution in Orissa.

Jason Ku, president of OrigaMIT and a mechanical engineering graduate student, lectures on the artistic aspects of origami design, emphasizing representational origami and tree-based design methods. He compares origami to music: both combine mathematical structure with artistic complexity, although origami designers often create and perform their own works. Representational origami depicts recognizable subjects and differs from patterning, tessellation, geometric models, and abstract art.

Ku traces modern representational origami largely to Akira Yoshizawa, who pioneered many original models, extensive shaping, curved folds, and wet-folding. Traditional models such as cranes and frogs rely on straight creases, polygons, flat folds, and grids based largely on 22.5-degree increments. Nontraditional work extends Yoshizawa’s approach through wet-folding, curved tension folds, texturing, and subjective shaping. Ku discusses designers including Hideo Komatsu, David Brill, Michael LaFosse, Eric Joisel, Robert Lang, Brian Chan, and Satoshi Kamiya, highlighting their artistic backgrounds and approaches. Joisel is presented as a pioneer in expressive human forms, while Lang uses algorithmic tree theory, Chan develops highly complex figures, and Kamiya combines exact straight folds with texture, wet-folding, and three-dimensional shaping.

The lecture then explains tree theory as a design process: a subject is abstracted into a one-dimensional stick figure, mapped to a base whose flaps have the required lengths and connections, and then shaped into the finished model. Algorithms and mathematics support the mapping from subject to base, while abstraction, proportion, and shaping remain artistic choices. Uniaxial bases are described as bases whose flaps lie along or straddle one axis and hinge perpendicular to it, allowing the base to project to a stick figure. Their thin limit corresponds to a tree of leaf and branch edges.

Circle-and-river packings illustrate how paper space can be allocated to trees. Leaf edges correspond to circles, while branch edges correspond to rivers separating parts of a model by a constant distance. A packing maps uniquely to a tree, but a tree can have multiple valid packings, creating choices about efficiency and flap placement. Ku practices matching trees and packings by their lengths and topology, then examines how crease patterns can be reduced to hinge representations and trees.

A detailed dragon model demonstrates how pleating can shrink sections of paper to make room for limbs, toes, neck, head, and texture. Ku explains that separating a line from a model provides extra paper and thickness, allowing features such as butterfly wings or toes to be represented. The model’s scale is attributed to efficient paper use, though folding it required a very large sheet and substantial effort.

Finally, Ku demonstrates TreeMaker by constructing a crab. He draws a tree with four legs, claws, eyes, a body, and an underbelly; assigns relative lengths; scales the structure into a valid packing; adjusts unconstrained nodes; builds a crease pattern; and discusses symmetry, triangulation, active paths, and difficulties finding mountain-valley assignments. He contrasts this with a hand-designed, partly non-uniaxial crab using a 22.5-degree structure, extra flaps, thinning, texturing, and shaping, followed by a folded proof of concept.

Ku also addresses folding methods, color use, single-sheet versus modular construction, and the definition of origami as work whose primary structure is defined by folding. He recommends Robert Lang’s *Origami Design Secrets*, the documentary *Between the Folds*, the Origami Forum, and Sunday OrigaMIT workshops.

NVIDIA’s A100 Tensor Core GPU is an Ampere-based data-center accelerator for AI, HPC, and analytics workloads. Its SXM4 board includes 40 GB of HBM2 memory organized into five active stacks of eight dies, delivering 1555 GB/s bandwidth—more than 1.7 times that of Tesla V100. Placing HBM2 stacks on the GPU package provides power and area savings over GDDR5/6 designs. SECDED ECC protects HBM2 memory, L2 and L1 caches, and SM register files.

A100 has a 40 MB L2 cache, 6.7 times larger than V100’s, with two partitions, 40 slices per partition, 2.3 times V100’s L2 bandwidth, and 5120 bytes per clock of read bandwidth versus 2048 bytes per clock on V100. L2 residency controls allow applications to prioritize persistent data, while Compute Data Compression can improve DRAM read/write bandwidth by up to 4×, L2 read bandwidth by up to 4×, and effective L2 capacity by up to 2×.

A100 has 108 SMs, compared with 80 on V100, and third-generation Tensor Cores offering peak mixed-precision performance 16 times that of standard FP32 FMA operations. Compared with V100, Tensor Core data sharing expands from 8 to all 32 threads in a warp, matrix operations can increase their k dimension by up to 4×, and matrix multiplication issues 8× fewer instructions while performing 2.9× fewer register-file accesses. A new asynchronous copy path moves global data directly into shared memory while bypassing L1 and the register file, and maximum shared-memory allocation per SM rises from 96 KB to 164 KB. A100 does not include display connectors, RT Cores, or an NVENC encoder.

Multi-Instance GPU (MIG) can divide an A100 into as many as seven isolated GPU Instances with dedicated compute, L2 cache, memory controllers, and frame-buffer resources. GPU slices provide the underlying compute and memory partitioning, while Compute Instances allow simultaneous independent contexts and support Volta-style MPS. MIG provides quality-of-service guarantees, fault isolation, and error containment for shared or multi-tenant environments. It also supports migrating virtual GPUs between compatible GPU Instances or physical GPUs.

Third-generation NVLink provides 12 links, 600 GB/s of total bandwidth, and faster peer-memory access than PCIe, with added error detection and recovery. A100 also supports PCIe Gen 4 at 31.5 GB/s per direction on x16 connections and SR-IOV virtualization. New fault-handling technology improves error attribution, isolation, and containment, including propagation of remote-GPU page faults through NVLink.

Additional hardware includes a five-core NVJPEG decoder, an optical-flow accelerator supporting optical flow and stereo disparity, improved FP16 and FP32 atomic throughput, and five NVDEC units rather than V100’s single decoder. CUDA 11 adds support for third-generation Tensor Cores, sparsity, task graphs, MIG, and L2 residency controls. A100 accelerates task-graph launches and dependency execution, provides asynchronous global-to-shared copies and asynchronous barriers for thread subsets, and supports L2 persistence in 2.5 MB set-aside increments. Cooperative Groups adds group-wide asynchronous copies, hardware-assisted reductions, and grid-synchronization overhead reductions of up to 30%.

DGX A100 combines eight A100 GPUs with six NVSwitches, providing 4.8 TB/s of bidirectional interconnect bandwidth and up to 5 PFLOPS of AI performance in a 6U system. MIG can expose up to 56 isolated accelerators within the system. DGX A100 also includes eight 200 Gb/s Mellanox ConnectX-6 InfiniBand adapters and a software stack based on CUDA, the NVIDIA Container Toolkit, and NGC containers, models, and SDKs.

A100 supports Compute Capability 8.0 and fine-grained structured sparsity, including 2:4 sparsity. Pruning removes low-contribution weights and connections to reduce computation, memory traffic, and latency; A100’s structured approach maintains balanced workloads and showed virtually no accuracy loss across the evaluated neural networks.

Tooth-whitening products are numerous and lightly regulated: the FDA treats them as cosmetics and does not require premarket approval, though it has found no evidence that ingredients in marketed products are unsafe. The ADA seal indicates independent review for safety and effectiveness; so far, only Crest 3D White Glamorous White Whitestrips carry it among over-the-counter bleaching products, though other products may work as directed.

Over-the-counter and dentist-provided take-home kits typically use 5–15% hydrogen peroxide and take two to six weeks. Sensitivity is common, and leaking gel can inflame gums. Custom trays cost about $400. In-office bleaching uses up to 40% peroxide, takes one or two hours, and can produce dramatic results but costs more than $1,000 and is rarely insured. In-office procedures increased 29% in 2015.

Dentists advise checking for cavities or other oral problems first. Surface stains may improve with routine dental care, while age-related enamel damage allows deeper stains that bleach can lighten. Trauma, tetracycline, and excessive fluoride can cause permanent discoloration requiring crowns or veneers. Whitening is temporary and requires touch-ups. The ADA says charcoal, baking soda, and lemon juice lack evidence of effectiveness.

The Second Circuit reviewed proceedings arising from the grounding of the oil-laden Barge New London in the Hudson River. The barge, owned by Pittston Marine Transport Corp., was push-towed at night during icy conditions by the Tug Ocean Prince, owned and chartered by Tug Ocean Prince, Inc. and Red Star Towing & Transportation Co. The barge struck a charted rock outside the navigable channel, causing extensive damage and an oil spill.

Red Star had not clearly designated either Walter Reimer or John Kiernan as captain. Reimer, who was unfamiliar with the Hudson River, and Kiernan, who had extensive local experience, each mistakenly believed the other was master. Red Star also knew of Reimer’s inexperience and the expected ice, darkness, buoy, and tidal conditions. During the voyage, Reimer searched for an unlighted buoy marking the rock, failed to see Con Hook Island Light, and sent the only available deckhand below for coffee. The tug and barge then struck the rock.

The district court found that the casualty resulted from navigation and management errors but not within Red Star’s privity and knowledge, so it granted limitation of liability and limited Red Star’s pollution-cleanup liability to $100 per gross ton, or $19,800. It also found Pittston was not responsible for the spill and dismissed claims against the United States.

The Second Circuit vacated the limitation orders. Red Star had a nondelegable duty to provide a competent captain and crew and a seaworthy vessel. Industry custom did not excuse sending an inadequately manned tug into dangerous conditions without clearly assigning command. The failure to post a lookout was also clearly erroneous: a proper lookout would likely have sighted Con Hook Light in time to establish a danger bearing and avoid the grounding. Under the Pennsylvania rule, Red Star failed to prove that this omission did not contribute to the casualty. The court therefore held the grounding resulted from negligence and unseaworthiness within Red Star’s privity and knowledge.

The court affirmed the dismissal of claims against the United States, finding that any negligence in maintaining navigation aids was not the proximate cause of the grounding. It further held that Red Star’s combination of omissions amounted to intentional conduct or reckless disregard of probable consequences and therefore constituted willful misconduct under 33 U.S.C. § 1321. Accordingly, Red Star could not invoke the statutory tonnage limitation for pollution cleanup costs.

The judgment was reversed in part, affirmed in part, and remanded, with directions to enter judgment for Pittston and the United States on their damages.

The Single/Double set offense uses double-baseline and down screens to free strong shooters. Its initial attack through the middle challenges help on both sides. A guard can curl off a double screen or reverse to a single screen, while the opposite wing uses the other screen. Proper timing, coordination, communication, and recognition of defensive responses are essential.

The guide details counters for defenders who chase, cheat over, switch, show and recover, or overplay passing lanes. Counter options include curls, fades, back cuts, slips, post or wing isolation, lobs, and dribble penetration. Screeners can also break double screens for pop-outs, rolls, slips, or lobs.

Down-screen reads and counters similarly include curling to a shot or basket, fading, back cutting, screening and rolling, post and wing isolation, and slipping the screen. When defense focuses on shooters, the ballhandler can feed strong post players, requiring proficiency in basic post moves.

The offense provides offensive-rebounding advantages through inside positioning and weak-side rebounders, emphasizing anticipation, hustle, multiple efforts, and boxing out. It can run from any alignment and may continue through motion, side-screen actions, or drive-and-kick sequences.

Implementation should use whole-part-whole teaching, breakdown drills, scrimmages, and individual skill work. Coaches should scout opponents, anticipate defensive reads, vary alignments and entries, attack weaker defenders, and use side screens late in the shot clock. The guide also argues that coaches should understand how to defend the offense even if they do not use it.

The FDA indicated it would approve Epidiolex, a pharmaceutical-grade, 99%-pure cannabidiol (CBD) oral medicine without THC, for seizures associated with Lennox-Gastaut and Dravet syndromes in patients aged 2 and older. Studies showed substantial evidence of effectiveness, while the drug’s mechanism remains unclear and its risks appeared acceptable given the disorders’ severity. Unlike unregulated CBD products sold online with unsubstantiated claims, Epidiolex underwent FDA review and must meet good manufacturing practices to ensure consistent contents. Both syndromes are rare, severe childhood epilepsies that can cause prolonged or varied seizures, cognitive impairment, brain damage, or death. Physicians reported dramatic improvements in some children. Researchers are also interested in testing CBD for autism, anxiety, and inflammatory or autoimmune disorders.

The passage criticizes Google for downplaying major physical differences between the Pixel 2 and Pixel 2 XL at its October 4 event and in online marketing. Although their specifications are nearly identical except for the display, the HTC-made Pixel 2 has especially large bezels, a dated, chamfered design, mismatched rear camera and flash placement, and louder, tinnier speakers. The LG-made Pixel 2 XL features rounded display corners, curved glass meeting aluminum sides, better build quality, and more balanced but quiet speakers, making it appear to be the design Google preferred. The Pixelbook also has a design inconsistent with the new Pixels. Overall, the differences undermine Google’s “Made by Google” branding and represent a step back from the first Pixels’ coherent design, though the Pixel 2 XL is presented as the stronger product. With Google’s recent hiring of HTC engineers, the author hopes future Pixels will have a more unified design.

Payton Leutner, 12, survived 19 stab wounds after a birthday sleepover near Milwaukee involving friends Morgan Guyser and Anissa Weier. Payton crawled from the woods while authorities searched for the two missing girls, who were later found near Interstate 94 and questioned by police. A five-inch knife was found in one girl’s bag, and investigators noted staining on Morgan’s sweatshirt. Anissa’s father found what he called her goodbye notes on her phone.

During questioning, Morgan and Anissa described a months-long plan to kill Payton, whom Morgan called “Bella.” They said their devotion to Slender Man, an evolving online horror character, motivated them; Morgan explained they wanted to become “proxies” by killing someone to prove the character real. Payton, initially unable to speak after surgery, learned by writing that police had found her friends. Surgeons said one wound reached her heart but missed the artery, which would otherwise have caused fatal bleeding within minutes.

The paper proposes a planar, two-frequency ring Paul trap to simultaneously confine a laser-cooled Ca⁺ ion and a photoionized electron, enabling laser-accessible control of the electron’s motional, Rydberg-like, and trap-induced states. Free electrons respond faster than trapped ions and could enable faster gates, while existing electron-qubit approaches remain limited by stringent cryogenic requirements, poor scalability, and unresolved control of individual spins and collective states.

For a Ca²⁺–electron system, the electron experiences the combined Coulomb potential of the ion and the trap’s pseudopotential. The model identifies three regimes: bound atomic states, increasingly delocalized Rydberg-like states near the ionization threshold, and trap-bound states above it. Calculated level spacings transition from hydrogen-like to harmonic-oscillator-like behavior. A calculated transition region, with principal quantum numbers 700–2000, contains adjacent transitions near 10 MHz separated by 1–10 kHz, potentially useful for quantum computing; the harmonic region may support high-resolution photon counting.

The intended experiment starts with a Doppler-cooled Ca⁺ ion and uses a laser cascade to photoionize it, producing an electron above the ionization threshold while avoiding instability near electrodes. Optical control and recombination transitions are proposed, with electron transitions monitored through changes in electromagnetically induced transparency. Trap parameters can tune transitions from 10 MHz to 1 GHz, while a magnetic field of at least roughly 1 mT could split electron spin states and support optical state preparation. Possible extensions include a shared-electron superposition of two Ca²⁺ ions and conversion of radio-frequency signals to optical signals.

The ring geometry applies the electron- and ion-specific radio-frequency signals to separate electrodes, avoiding static fields that could impede opposite charges. Its pseudopotential steepness is optimized to separate trap-induced energy levels. The planar approach is intended to support scalable manufacturing, photonic and electronic integration, and miniaturization. A major challenge is maintaining a symmetric field that traps both particles about 1 mm from the electrodes while minimizing electron heating.

This continuation application describes ultrasonic fingerprint sensor apparatus, systems, and methods for positioning a sensor beneath a display, including OLED and flexible OLED displays. An ultrasonic transmitter sends waves through a platen or display; reflections from skin ridges and air-filled valleys are detected and converted into digital image data for fingerprint imaging and authentication. Implementations include a sensor substrate with pixel circuits, a piezoelectric transceiver layer, electrode and passivation layers, and optional acoustic matching, focusing, backing, stiffening, cavity, and acoustic-impedance structures.

Integration beneath the display may use a nonporous light-blocking layer, grounded conductive shielding, reworkable adhesive, and a mechanical stress-isolation layer. These may be discrete or combined in a multifunctional film, with the sensor spanning part or substantially all of the display’s active area. The layers provide optical blocking, electromagnetic shielding, heat spreading, stress reduction, acoustic transmission, and easier replacement or refurbishment. Manufacturing may bond or laminate the layers and sensor to the display. The configurations increase usable display area, support bezel-less and curved devices, reduce interference and noise, and enable authentication across the display.

Unverified newspaper reports affected several Spanish stocks: OHL and Acciona announced dividends; Gas Natural abandoned an Italian LNG project; Minor bid for NH Hotel; Dogi proposed a name change; Parques Reunidos reported a smaller half-year loss.

NVIDIA’s AMP coordinates and schedules workloads to improve quality of service, reducing first-response latency for LLMs and prioritizing game-engine work to prevent stuttering.

Blackwell adds hardware support for 4:2:2 chroma encoding and decoding in H.264 and HEVC. Its ninth-generation NVENC improves AV1 and HEVC quality by 5% BD-BR PSNR, while AV1 Ultra High Quality mode adds another 5% and can combine with generational gains for up to 15% improvement. The RTX 5090 supports three encoders and two decoders, increasing export speeds by more than 50% generation over generation and fourfold versus a single-encoder RTX 3090. The sixth-generation NVDEC doubles H.264 decoding speed and supports 4:2:2. DisplayPort 2.1b supports 80 Gbps via UHBR 20, including 8K at 165 Hz and 4K at 480 Hz with DSC.

Blackwell’s Max-Q design improves efficiency through finer clock, power, and voltage-rail gating, separate GPU-core and memory power controls, and frequency switching that adjusts to workloads 1,000 times faster than earlier architectures. Its deepest sleep state is entered ten times faster than on Ada, and one small-language-model inference example demonstrated power savings of up to 50%.

DLSS 4 adds Multi Frame Generation, which can produce three additional frames for every traditionally rendered frame. Its AI model is 40% faster than the previous method, uses 30% less VRAM, and is supported by enhanced display-engine-based frame pacing. New transformer models improve Super Resolution, Ray Reconstruction, and Deep Learning Anti-Aliasing, providing greater temporal stability, less ghosting, improved motion detail and lighting, and fewer denoising artifacts.

Blackwell also introduces developer-created neural shaders through the Cooperative Vectors API for DirectX 12 and Vulkan and differentiable Slang features. Proposed applications include neural texture compression with up to seven-to-one VRAM savings over block-compressed formats, neural approximations of complex materials, stochastic texture filtering, real-time neural radiance caching, ray-traced subsurface-scattering skin, and generative-AI rendering of faces. Neural Radiance Cache estimates indirect lighting after limited ray tracing, while Neural Faces infer realistic faces from rasterized geometry and pose data.

Time Warner traded at $96.26, down 0.33% intraday, and had a market capitalization of $74.31 billion. Apple Inc. reported that on April 30, 2018, the Superior Court of California for Santa Clara County preliminarily approved a settlement of In re Apple Inc. E-Book Derivative Litigation. The court approved the settlement notice and scheduled a July 20, 2018 hearing to address the settlement’s fairness, attorneys’ fees and expenses, service awards, and related matters. President McKinley addresses Congress about the continuing Cuban war, which has caused famine, economic losses, disruption of U.S. trade, unrest among Americans, and repeated efforts to enforce U.S. neutrality. Spain’s reconcentration policy displaced and impoverished rural Cubans; official Spanish estimates placed starvation and disease mortality above 50 percent among those confined in towns. U.S. mediation failed, while American relief efforts delivered nearly $200,000 in aid and persuaded Spain to revoke reconcentration orders.

After further negotiations, Spain proposed that an insular parliament prepare peace and indicated willingness to suspend hostilities if requested by the insurgents. McKinley nevertheless argued that recognizing Cuban belligerency or independence was premature and would create legal and diplomatic complications. He maintained that neutral intervention was justified by humanitarian concerns, the protection of American lives and property, damage to U.S. commerce, and threats to national security, particularly following the destruction of the battleship Maine.

McKinley therefore asked Congress to authorize him to use U.S. military and naval forces to end hostilities and establish a stable Cuban government, while also appropriating funds to continue food and supply distribution. He concluded by noting a newly issued Spanish decree suspending hostilities, though its duration and terms had not yet been communicated.

Shalah Dawn Nelson pleaded guilty to animal cruelty for tying an elastic band around a neighbour’s dog’s testicles in December 2016; the dog required surgery. Two Criminal Code charges were stayed. She was fined $1,000, placed on 12 months’ probation barring contact with the owner, and ordered to pay $850 restitution.

The ADS9803 is an eight-channel, 20-bit data-acquisition ADC with a built-in analog front end. It supports straight-binary and two’s-complement output formats, differential or single-ended free-running sampling clocks, and SMPL_SYNC synchronization across multiple devices. It uses a precision internal reference, which can be filtered with a 10 µF capacitor, or can be disabled for an external reference.

The source-synchronous data interface supports two- and four-lane SDR/DDR modes. Conversion results are transmitted MSB first in 24-bit packets, with the final six bits zero. Features include XOR data randomization to reduce data-transmission interference, simple and moving averages for improved SNR, and fixed, ramp, and alternating test patterns for two channel groups.

Reset and power-down modes restore default registers and require initialization through register writes. Speed-boost mode converts only a selected channel pair at up to 8 MSPS. Configuration registers are organized into three banks accessed through SPI; the document also describes single-device register access and multi-device daisy-chain read/write procedures.

Application guidance covers ATE signal measurement, offset and gain calibration, total unadjusted error, PMU multiplexing, settling performance, power-supply decoupling, reference layout, and PCB routing. The device uses AVDD_5V, VDD_1V8, and IOVDD supplies, with no required power-up sequence.

A small study comparing 12 boys aged about 10, 12 untrained male university students, and 13 male endurance athletes during high-intensity stationary cycling found that the boys’ muscles fatigued at roughly the same rate as elite athletes and recovered faster. Their blood also cleared lactic acid more quickly. Researchers said this may reflect their less-developed anaerobic systems: they produce less lactic acid, which contributes to muscle fatigue, while their aerobic fitness remains strong. The findings do not mean children are generally as fit as elite endurance athletes; their endurance may instead precede development of adult anaerobic capacity. The authors said the results could guide youth training toward developing skills, strength, and sprint ability and suggest that frequent running and stopping during play suits children’s physiology. The study may also inform research into how muscle-level aerobic fitness declines with age and whether this is related to increased disease risk, including cancer, cardiovascular disease, and diabetes. Researchers cited the small sample, limited access to elite athletes, and ethical constraints involving children.

Bleacher Report suggested Braves legend Chipper Jones as Atlanta’s “wildest” managerial candidate, while naming Walt Weiss the “best candidate.” Jones has Futures Game managing experience, spent 19 seasons in Atlanta, hit 468 home runs and earned eight All-Star selections.

The study developed an NLP system to identify EHR documentation of goals-of-care (GOC) discussions among seriously ill patients, where such discussions are often infrequent, inconsistent, or buried outside dedicated advance care planning notes. Two annotators labeled utterances in 776 inpatient notes from five University of Pennsylvania hospitals, including 400 advance care planning notes and 376 general notes, with specialist adjudication of disagreements. GOC-related utterances were much rarer in general notes than in planning notes.

Researchers compared passive and active learning using an ensemble of regular expressions, logistic regression, BERT, BioClinicalBERT, and RoBERTa classifiers, with three methods for combining predictions. The best active-learning weighted ensemble achieved F1 scores of approximately 0.55 for utterance classification and 0.63 for note classification. It identified 13 of 18 GOC-positive test notes (72%) while incorrectly flagging 13 of 158 negative notes (8%). Active learning improved precision over training only on advance care planning notes and required labeling 3,200 additional utterances, or 30% of the unlabeled set. Training on all available examples generally performed no better than active selection.

Performance remained moderate. The system analyzed utterances independently and ignored surrounding context because transformer inputs were limited to 512 tokens. A fixed unlabeled pool containing only 51 positive examples also restricted classifier exploration. Proposed next steps include testing on three million available notes and evaluating paragraph-level retrieval using fine-tuned generative models. Unlike prior work, the study used a strict definition requiring evidence of a clinician-patient or surrogate discussion of goals or values, prognosis, and/or care preferences, without artificially enriching general notes for GOC content. The authors conclude that the system could aid production review and semi-automated curation, while the study’s annotated notes remain protected and MIMIC III labels are being corrected for future release.

Red Bull’s Daniel Ricciardo said the RB13 was third fastest in Japanese Grand Prix practice but lost straight-line time, attributing it to downforce prioritising corners rather than the engine. He and Max Verstappen sat out FP2 due to torrential rain, conserving wet tyres for qualifying, and called for more extreme tyres to be allowed.

Jenny Han, author of "The Summer I Turned Pretty" and the "To All the Boys" series, worked early jobs as an Olive Garden server, nanny, and school librarian before landing deals with Netflix and Amazon. Her debut novel appeared in 2009; an Amazon Studios deal in 2021 brought the story to television and returned the books to the NYT Bestsellers list in 2022. The TV franchise's third and final season wrapped that September, with a movie sequel planned. Her second teen trilogy (2014) became one of Netflix's most-viewed original films; Netflix acquired the series in 2018 and, after three films, agreed to a spinoff. Han said her librarian work — reading new books daily and tracking young readers' tastes — helped her understand her audience, and she now sees herself as a writer and businesswoman who must sell her own books.

The passage also profiles other executives with unconventional starts: Eventbrite CEO Julia Hartz, who rose to a junior executive role at FX before founding the company in 2006 and relocating to San Francisco, with the platform distributing 83 million paid tickets for over 4.7 million events in 2024; Spanx founder Sara Blakely, who bootstrapped her company in 2000 with savings from seven years selling appliances, hitting $4 million in first-year sales and $10 million the next year before selling a majority stake in 2021; and Greg Hart, who worked at a department store chain before joining Amazon and rising to become Jeff Bezos' right-hand man before leading a tech company.

Preliminary discussions found the proposed negotiating procedure satisfactory and suggested drafting the agreement’s general provisions before final Congo production and requirement schedules were available. The lecture develops perturbative matching, renormalization-group evolution, and power corrections in heavy-quark effective theory (HQET). A one-loop heavy-quark wave-function renormalization constant \(Z_h\) is calculated in dimensional regularization with the \(\overline{\mathrm{MS}}\) scheme and Feynman gauge. A momentum-substitution identity, dubbed the “George I trick,” combines the heavy-quark and gluon propagators while avoiding an unnecessary Feynman parameter multiplying \(q^2\). The resulting quadratic integral is evaluated to isolate a \(1/\epsilon\) ultraviolet divergence and determine the corresponding counterterm. The lecture contrasts \(\overline{\mathrm{MS}}\) and on-shell renormalization, noting that finite scheme-dependent terms differ even though physical matching agrees.

Unlike the light-quark wave-function factor in QCD, \(Z_h\) must be combined with the renormalization of local heavy-to-light current operators. For a current containing one heavy and one light quark, one-loop vertex and wave-function contributions determine the operator counterterm \(Z_o\) and an anomalous-dimension coefficient of order \(-\alpha_s/\pi\). This result is independent of the chosen spin structure. Although the analogous full-QCD current has no anomalous dimension, HQET currents evolve below the heavy-quark mass because logarithms involving \(M_Q\) become ultraviolet divergences when \(M_Q\) is treated as infinite.

For heavy-to-heavy currents, the two heavy quarks may have different velocities \(v\) and \(v'\). Their anomalous dimension then depends on \(w=v\!\cdot v'\) through a nontrivial function involving logarithms and \(\sqrt{w^2-1}\), rather than being a constant. In the example \(B\to D^*\ell\nu\), \(w\) is fixed by meson masses and momentum transfer and ranges from about 1 to 1.5. The spin independence of the result follows from HQET symmetry, because the propagators and vertex contain no spin structure. Wilson coefficients can therefore depend on \(\alpha_s\), the renormalization scale, heavy-quark masses, and \(w\).

The renormalization-group solution evolves Wilson coefficients from the heavy-quark matching scale to a lower scale. HQET matrix elements are likewise scale dependent; they may be evaluated and evolved down to a perturbative cutoff, often around \(1\)–\(1.5\) GeV rather than \(\Lambda_{\mathrm{QCD}}\). In this separation, logarithms involving \(\Lambda_{\mathrm{QCD}}\) reside in operators, while scale ratios involving \(M_Q\) reside in Wilson coefficients.

Matching QCD matrix elements to HQET requires finite residues from the LSZ prescription and ultraviolet-renormalized vertex and wave-function graphs. Subtracting the full-theory and HQET results yields the matching coefficient. A vector current has two HQET structures, \(C_1\) and \(C_2\), because the HQET external velocity \(v^\mu\) permits an additional vector structure; heavy-to-light matching produces nonzero coefficients at order \(\alpha_s\), while heavy-to-heavy matching also produces functions of \(w\).

A shortcut uses dimensional regularization for both ultraviolet and infrared divergences. With on-shell external momenta, HQET loop graphs are scaleless; after ultraviolet counterterms are subtracted, only infrared poles remain. Because the infrared divergences of QCD and HQET must match, the matching coefficient can be obtained from the full-theory calculation without explicitly recomputing all HQET graphs. Formally, the ultraviolet and infrared poles are treated as distinct regulators.

Power corrections are introduced by integrating out the heavy field from the QCD Lagrangian, solving its equations of motion, and expanding order by order in \(1/M_Q\). The order-\(1/M_Q\) Lagrangian contains two operators: a kinetic-type correction that breaks flavor symmetry but not spin symmetry, and a magnetic-moment-type term proportional to \(\sigma_{\mu\nu}G^{\mu\nu}\) that breaks both. Power counting, gauge symmetry, discrete symmetries, and residual Lorentz structure constrain the allowed operators; these two form the complete set at this order.

Because the velocity \(v^\mu\) breaks part of Lorentz symmetry, HQET must satisfy reparameterization invariance. Under
\[
v^\mu\to v^\mu+\frac{\epsilon^\mu}{M_Q},\qquad
k^\mu\to k^\mu-\epsilon^\mu,\qquad v\!\cdot\!\epsilon=0,
\]
the heavy-quark field also changes by a term proportional to \(\epsilon\!\cdot\!\cdot/(2M_Q)\), with a coordinate-dependent phase. This symmetry restores small-boost invariance and relates terms at different orders in \(1/M_Q\). Its preservation forces the kinetic subleading Wilson coefficient to equal one at all orders, provided the regulator and renormalization scheme respect the symmetry. The magnetic coefficient is not fixed at this order and can have a nontrivial anomalous dimension.

President Trump and French President Macron celebrated the Franco-American alliance at the White House in the Trump administration’s first state dinner. Trump praised the countries’ friendship and Melania Trump’s role in organizing the event, while Macron cited joint U.S.-French airstrikes in Syria as part of their shared fight for freedom and values. The lecture begins with an update on midterms and grading. Midterms and solutions will be distributed; grades are expected to come largely from the final. The professor follows an approximate guideline of half A’s and half B’s, with pluses and minuses, and notes that the midterm was intended partly as a learning exercise.

The second half of the course turns toward convolutional codes and other structured approaches to approaching channel capacity. Shannon showed that randomly chosen codes can achieve capacity on a channel. Random linear codes retain this performance while allowing polynomial-complexity encoding, but maximum-likelihood decoding generally requires exponentially many comparisons. Algebraically decodable codes such as Reed–Solomon, BCH, and Reed–Muller codes permit efficient decoding but generally cannot reach capacity. The lecture therefore examines additional structure—especially linear and finite-state structure—that can support efficient maximum- or quasi-maximum-likelihood decoding.

Peter Elias’s convolutional codes combine linearity, a time-invariant encoder, and finite-state dynamics, enabling efficient Viterbi decoding. A rate-1/2, constraint-length-2 example is described over the binary field, including its shift-register construction, output equations, four states, and impulse responses.

The lecture defines convolutional codes using semi-infinite Laurent sequences with definite starting times. Their generating functions use the \(D\)-transform. Laurent sequences form a time-invariant field under componentwise addition and convolution, with inverses obtained by long division; restricting sequences to have a definite start avoids ambiguous or undefined bi-infinite expansions. Rational sequences correspond to ratios of polynomials and are eventually periodic.

General finite-state encoders are represented by causal rational impulse responses. Their constraint length \(\nu\) determines \(2^\nu\) possible states. Encoders are equivalent when they generate the same code, and a canonical equivalent encoder can be chosen with polynomial feedback-free generators. Finally, the example encoder’s free distance is shown to be five, using its impulse response and a finite-state transition diagram. A trellis representation, catastrophicity, and the Viterbi algorithm are deferred to the next class.

Travis Stork, a math major who became an MD after working at a Washington D.C. free clinic, shares health advice as a panelist on CBS's "The Doctors." He says weight loss doesn't require rushing or extreme changes: focus on feeling healthier rather than the scale, walk 30 minutes daily, stand more, cut back soda, and swap white breads and pastas for whole grains. For Super Bowl snacking, he recommends bean-based or whole-grain chips topped with guacamole, jalapeños, salsa, Greek yogurt instead of sour cream, and real cheese rather than fried chips and cheese sauce, citing protein, fiber, heart-healthy fats, and anti-inflammatory spices. For couples, he suggests cooking healthy meals at home together and taking spin or workout classes instead of going to a bar, noting that support networks improve success. He says the best part of the show is discussing health topics he is passionate about.

Teurlings Catholic High announced three leadership appointments. Robert Boudreaux, a longtime alumnus, parent and coach, will direct institutional advancement, overseeing development, communications and advancement. Maria Latiolais Hanes, a 1998 graduate and longtime admissions director, will also serve as development director and continue overseeing admissions. Rev. Dustin Dought, pastor of St. Leo the Great and a 2005 graduate, will become chaplain while retaining his pastoral and diocesan worship roles.

The Diamond & One is a Box & One derivative in which four defenders play zone and a fifth applies strong pass denial to the opponent’s scoring ace. It is most effective against odd-front or one-guard offenses. The defense protects the middle but leaves the corner vulnerable; if the corner becomes a problem, the alignment should switch to Box & One. X5 generally stays low between the ball and basket, X1 protects the high post, and X3 and X4 shift between the wing, corner, and baseline as passes develop. Against an odd front, defenders deny high-post and wing passes while the chaser pressures the star and receives support against penetration. For low-post defense, X4 and X5 trap the post player as perimeter defenders cut off passing lanes. The chaser’s ball denial is the key element of Box & One because it disrupts set plays.

Kano State Governor Abdullahi Umar Ganduje launched distribution of 10,000 free delivery kits across the state’s 44 local government areas, costing N145 million. The kits are intended to reduce infection-related maternal and newborn deaths. The state also trained 1,936 traditional birth attendants, renovated over 300 health facilities, and began compiling data on pregnant women to encourage clinic use.

Zambia’s parliament suspended 48 UPND MPs for 30 days after they boycotted President Edgar Lungu’s March assembly address, barring them from seats, the building and pay. The party called the suspensions unconstitutional. Hichilema and five others were charged with treason, which Amnesty International called “trumped up.”

In Ward v. Yorba, both parties claimed title to the same Los Angeles property. Ward sued to reform a land-sale agreement, seeking specific performance and damages. The written contract mistakenly required Ward to convey “good and perfect title,” although the parties agreed that he would sell only his interest. Ward sold that interest for $4,750; Yorba paid $100 but failed to pay the remaining $4,650. The trial court reformed the contract and awarded Ward the unpaid balance, interest, and costs.

The court held that the evidence clearly established a drafting mistake despite conflicting testimony about some details; an explanation for the mistake was unnecessary. Yorba was not entitled to rescind because he knew the relevant title facts and acted on the advice of his own counsel; Civil Code section 1577 did not apply because his claimed mistake was not unconscious ignorance of a material fact. There was no fraud or unfairness.

The agreement also had adequate consideration. Ward’s interest had cost Yorba $1,300, the property was worth $9,000, and the settlement would extinguish Ward’s rights, transfer possession, and avoid litigation. The judgment and order denying a new trial were affirmed.

TMPM format or migration-list errors may cause rejection or partial success and are reported in commands or entries; ring-buffer errors appear in PM_STATUS. Hardware errors are reported via status and/or MCA. Clients detecting timeouts should log an MCA and may save state, terminate VMs, or stop commands. Processing errors may make 128-page batches unrecoverable.

The passage provides an overview of trading options on Apple (AAPL). Options are leveraged contracts giving buyers the right, but not the obligation, to buy or sell an underlying asset at a predetermined strike price before or on expiration. Call options provide purchase rights, while put options provide sale rights. Unlike owning stock, options have expiration dates, greater complexity, and potentially larger gains or losses.

Option prices are influenced by Apple’s share price, time remaining, implied volatility, interest rates, dividends, corporate news, and macroeconomic conditions. Rising share prices generally increase call prices and reduce put prices; higher volatility increases both call and put prices, while higher interest rates generally reduce them. Dividends generally increase call prices and reduce put prices. Positive corporate news may benefit calls, while negative news may benefit puts.

Available strategies include buying or selling calls and puts, covered calls, protective puts, straddles, strangles, and delta hedges. These strategies can provide income, hedge against falling prices, or benefit from volatility and price moves in either direction. The passage also discusses futures, forwards, and swaps as other derivatives.

Options trading involves substantial risks, including leverage, time decay, market risk, and potentially unlimited losses from naked short calls. Risks may be amplified by Apple’s size and liquidity. Stop-loss and trailing stop-loss orders can limit losses but may be undermined by gaps or abrupt news, while straddles, strangles, and delta hedges can reduce exposure. Limit orders are recommended for entering and exiting trades because they specify a desired price.

American-style options may be exercised before expiration, unlike European-style options, but are generally more expensive and more exposed to early exercise. Market, limit, stop, and stop-limit orders are also described. Technical analysis can identify historical price patterns and potential entry and exit points, while fundamental analysis evaluates Apple’s financial condition and prospects. Analytical tools include charting software, news and earnings reports, the Black-Scholes model, and Monte Carlo simulations, with backtesting and quantitative testing recommended.

Apple options are described as highly liquid and volatile, allowing relatively quick trading with minimal slippage but significant price fluctuations. Their market is more liquid and volatile than options markets for other stocks. Costs include contract premiums, broker commissions, transaction fees, taxes, and slippage. Profits are generally subject to capital gains taxes, and losses from option sales cannot offset gains from other investments under the wash sale rule.

The passage ultimately advises careful preparation, including understanding leverage, costs, liquidity, taxes, and strategy risks. It concludes that most traders may have better odds trading AAPL stock directly and should seek a demonstrable competitive advantage before entering the options market.

Headlines cover a Delaware businessman’s cellphone taking a bullet in an Istanbul nightclub attack; Rosie O’Donnell warning about Trump; two missing Fort Bliss soldiers; horoscope and fitness features; and Ivanka Trump’s Hawaii celebration.

An article examines a simple mean-reversion strategy using the Relative Strength Index (RSI) on the SPY ETF. The strategy enters trades when specified RSI conditions occur and exits when defined criteria are met. Backtesting from 1993 onward reportedly produced an average gain per trade of 0.57%, a 75% win rate, a 23% maximum drawdown, and a 2.3 profit factor. It performed comparably to buy-and-hold while spending less time in the market and experiencing roughly half the drawdown. Adding one additional, undisclosed indicator reduced trades from 470 to 377 while increasing total returns and significantly improving the strategy. The passage also notes that RSI is a widely used momentum oscillator for identifying potential price reversals.

Following PlayStation Russia’s cryptic post, fans guessed it referenced a “PlayStation One X,” next-generation systems, PS Vita 2, PlayStation Now in Russia, or cross-play. The author says next-generation announcements are premature and believes it more likely concerns PlayStation online functionality or the store.

This qualitative case study examines AI integration across all phases of an AI-supported, university-level Digital Photography in Nature course. Guided by TPACK, constructivist learning theory, and the MRK instructional design model, it explores the instructor’s design, implementation, and evaluation experiences and students’ experiences of AI-supported learning. It also addresses AI’s effects on technical skills, creativity, learner autonomy, and pedagogical practice.

Data were collected through semi-structured interviews with 38 associate-degree students who completed the course and its instructor at a public university in eastern Turkey. Student interviews were conducted online through Zoom, while the instructor was interviewed face-to-face. Transcripts were analyzed through manual and MAXQDA-assisted coding, participant verification, triangulation, peer debriefing, and independent review, producing five overarching themes and 17 codes.

The instructor redesigned the course after identifying limitations of traditional, teacher-centered methods and students’ limited access to photography equipment. The revised course combined AI tools with flipped-classroom instruction, project-based collaborative groups, weekly themed photography assignments, peer discussion, AI-generated technical feedback, AI-supported literature reviews and rubrics, and comparative final projects. AI was used through platforms including ChatGPT, Claude, Flikia AI, Krea AI, Gamma, Gemini, and other GPT tools.

The instructor reported improved academic language, personalized feedback, technical learning, engagement, and assessment efficiency, but identified inadequate infrastructure and AI hallucinations as major risks. Students valued rapid information access, convenience, objective and detailed feedback, improved technical knowledge, and increased AI awareness. They generally regarded AI as an assistant, guide, or teacher-like aid rather than a replacement for human instruction. Reported disadvantages included passivity, over-reliance, reduced independent analysis, constrained originality, misinformation, contradictory outputs, and unequal access to reliable infrastructure and premium tools.

The study recommends structured AI-literacy training, guided and reflection-based assignments, human feedback, peer review, critical verification of AI outputs, equitable access to digital resources, ethical safeguards, and continued pedagogical oversight. Limitations include the focus on one course and instructor, reliance on qualitative data, and the absence of a control group.

The Education Department’s advisory rulemaking committee is working to clarify new graduate loan caps and consolidated income-driven repayment plans before they take effect July 1, 2026. A potential government shutdown could delay the session, though officials said it might continue in person through Friday. Nearly 87% of staff were slated for furlough, but rulemaking and bill-implementation employees would remain. Experts said tight timelines and staffing losses could impede the work. Under the shutdown plan, student aid and loan payments would continue, while civil-rights investigations and new grantmaking would pause.

Apple Inc.’s March 4, 2022 Form 8-K reported that shareholders approved the 2022 Employee Stock Plan, effective upon approval, permitting stock options, stock appreciation rights, stock grants and restricted stock units for employees and consultants. The plan’s share limit begins with 510 million shares plus specified 2014 Plan adjustments and cannot exceed 1,274,374,682 shares; full-value awards count as two shares per share issued. Authority for new grants under the 2014 Plan ends when the 2022 Plan is registered on Form S-8.

At the annual meeting, nine director nominees were elected, Ernst & Young LLP was ratified as Apple’s 2022 auditor, and advisory approval of executive compensation and the 2022 Plan was granted. Shareholder proposals concerning reincorporation, transparency, forced labor and pay equity were rejected, while proposals for a civil rights audit and a report on concealment clauses were approved. Exhibits include the 2022 Plan and forms of restricted stock unit and performance award agreements.

Seventeen brokerages give Tyson Foods a consensus “Buy” rating, with one sell, six hold, eight buy, and two strong buy ratings. The average 12-month price target is $72.96. Recent targets include Zacks at $73, BMO Capital Markets at $78, RBC at $70, Pivotal Research at $40, and Mizuho at $76.

Tyson Foods reported quarterly EPS of $1.28, beating the $1.18 consensus estimate, and revenue of $9.85 billion versus an estimated $9.49 billion. Revenue rose 4.8% year over year. Shares traded at $70.66, with a $25.92 billion market capitalization and a 1.27% dividend yield.

The company declared a quarterly dividend of $0.225 per share, payable December 15 to shareholders of record on December 1. CFO Dennis Leatherby sold 145,100 shares for $9.57 million, while director Mikel A. Durham bought 2,809 shares for about $184,748. Hedge funds and other institutional investors own 71.89% of the stock, and insiders own 2.65%.

Tyson Foods offers chicken, beef, pork, and prepared foods under brands including Tyson, Jimmy Dean, Hillshire Farm, Sara Lee, Ball Park, Wright, Aidells, and State Fair.

A STAT biotech newsletter reports that the FDA approved a second generic version of mifepristone. It also highlights Amgen’s 12,000-patient Repatha trial, which found reduced heart-disease death, heart attack and stroke risk, and a new NIH office focused on reducing animal testing.

Montreal reports 11 deaths linked to hot, humid weather, with four more in the Eastern Townships. Urgences-Santé receives 1,200 calls daily—30% above usual—and urges residents to use a health line for minor problems and reserve 911 for emergencies. The heat warning persists through Thursday.

Scientists identified a tumor-associated bacterial metabolite, 2-methylisocitrate (2-MiCit), that damages cancer-cell DNA, disrupts metabolism and works synergistically with 5-fluorouracil chemotherapy. Produced by E. coli, 2-MiCit inhibited a key mitochondrial enzyme and showed anti-cancer effects in worms, human cancer cells and flies, where it extended survival. Modeling also indicated that bacteria in patients’ tumors produce 2-MiCit. Researchers created a more potent synthetic version, suggesting new drug candidates and personalized treatments that account for the tumor microbiome.

NuVasive will host an interactive Industry Lunch and Learn workshop on single-position lateral surgery for L4-S1 on April 30 from 1:10–1:55 p.m. in Rooms 272-273. Topics include reducing patient repositioning, advanced 3D-printed implant materials, and LessRay technology for radiation reduction. Attendees can hear from early adopters of lateral single-position surgery. The company reports revenues of over $1 billion and a workforce of approximately 2,400 across more than 40 countries. Team members credit veterans such as Carbo, Luddy, Joe, and Dave Reid with teaching younger players how to compete and conduct themselves. Coach Hitchcock’s demanding approach has been challenging but has helped players grow. The team prioritizes collective success, focusing on hard work, cycling the puck in the corners, wearing down defenders, and scoring through net-front play rather than fancy plays.

Oct. 5–6, 2017 Reno County bookings list McGee for drug possession and probation violation; Benitez, Lovell, Mendoza, and Ford for failure to appear; Mendoza for probation violation; and Behel for drug charges, interference with law enforcement, obstruction/resistance, and execution of a felony warrant. The Allied governments reject the American note’s equation of the Central Powers with the Allies, citing Germany and Austria-Hungary’s aggression, violations of Belgium and Luxembourg, and numerous atrocities. They answer President Wilson’s request by outlining their aims: restoring Belgium, Serbia, and Montenegro; evacuating and compensating invaded territories; reorganizing Europe through national self-determination and security; restoring seized lands and liberating oppressed peoples; addressing Ottoman rule and Poland; and securing a peace based on liberty, justice, and international obligations. They deny seeking Germany’s extermination and defer detailed compensation terms until negotiations.

A table of contents and opening diplomatic correspondence cover wartime diplomatic representation, Belgian relief work and civilian deportations, the Serbian legation, and court jurisdiction over foreign-requisitioned ships. The first section addresses the war before U.S. entry and the Allied governments’ January 10, 1917 reply to the President’s December 18, 1916 peace suggestion, with Central Powers’ counter-replies and dispatches from several European capitals dated January 5–22, 1917. Included are a denial of reports that the President planned a second peace note and reports of Allied officials arriving in Rome and possible Allied troop withdrawal from Saloniki.

The passage motivates a universal foundation model for low-level biomedical image processing, including restoration, super-resolution, registration, and fusion. It argues that specialist models are limited by multi-step task requirements, interrelated degradations, and inefficient training and inference on large, multi-channel biomedical data. The proposed model, Orochi, addresses these issues through four components: raw data from over 100 studies exceeding 100 terabytes, with Random Multi-scale Sampling for local and streaming training; Task-related Joint-embedding Pre-training, which jointly reconstructs task-specific degradations; a hierarchical multi-head architecture combining Mamba’s linear complexity with Swin-Transformer-inspired patch merging; and three-tier fine-tuning options ranging from full tuning to lightweight depth-wise separable convolution for parameter-efficient adaptation. The passage reports that the lightest tuning mode can perform comparably to state-of-the-art specialist models and positions Orochi as a unified tool for biomedical imaging workflows.

The North Carolina Court of Appeals vacated a preliminary injunction preventing Paul Alton Vaughn from operating a used car lot in alleged violation of Knightdale zoning ordinances. Although the Town likely could prevail and injunctive relief was available, Rule 65 required specific facts establishing a likelihood of irreparable injury. The Town’s verified complaint contained only conclusory allegations, which were insufficient for the trial court to weigh the equities and determine whether an injunction should issue. Review was proper because the injunction would deprive Vaughn of the substantial right to operate his business before final judgment.

The application describes a storage, retrieval, and processing system in which a programmable motion device, such as a robotic arm, removes objects from storage bins and distributes them into destination bins according to a manifest. Storage bins are stored in rows and delivered to processing areas by bin displacement mechanisms and retrieval conveyors. A perception unit identifies objects and candidate grasp locations, favoring stable, unobscured, relatively flat surfaces and approaching objects substantially normal to the selected surface. Good and bad grasp locations may be correlated with image features and used in machine learning. Completed storage bins may be returned to storage or discarded, while completed destination bins are transferred to output conveyors for further packaging, labeling, or shipment. Computer control tracks bin identities and locations and coordinates conveyors, bin mechanisms, and robotic movement. Embodiments include gravity-fed conveyors, box trays and covers, box kickers, multiple retrieval systems, and parallel processing stations.

A memorial urged Korea to modernize its administration, education, laws, finances, agriculture, and commerce to preserve its independence, prosperity, and strength while improving relations with Japan. U.S. envoy John M. B. Sill reported that Japan demanded clarification of whether Korea was tributary to China. Korea instead asserted independent sovereign rights, citing the 1876 Kang-hwa treaty and a royal letter to the U.S. president; Japan reportedly welcomed the response. The king’s communication described Korea as a Chinese dependency whose domestic and foreign affairs remained under its sovereign’s control, while relations with the United States would follow equality between independent states. Korean minister Ye Sung Soo subsequently requested U.S. mediation because Japan refused to withdraw troops and sought political reforms. He urged a conference, prompt withdrawal of Chinese and Japanese troops, and action to avert conflict.

A player reflects on a long-awaited championship, saying the goal existed since day one and that the organization fought through tough seasons—including years failing to advance past the second round—until they finally believed "this year is going to be our year." He credits the team's consistency: staying focused, sticking together and to the system, not panicking after the third period, and working hard throughout. He notes nobody expected the finals matchup between the Capitals and Knights. He praises a teammate as "unbelievable" and "outstanding," saying the whole team deserves the result, and that he is very excited and happy to be going home to his family and fans.

Microsoft Corporation filed a Form 10-Q for the quarter ended March 31, 2019, reporting revenue of $30.571 billion, up 14% from $26.819 billion a year earlier. Gross margin rose 16% to $20.401 billion, operating income increased 25% to $10.341 billion, net income rose 19% to $8.809 billion, and diluted earnings per share increased 20% to $1.14. For the nine months ended March 31, revenue increased 15% to $92.126 billion, operating income rose 24% to $30.554 billion, net income reached $26.053 billion, and diluted earnings per share were $3.36. Prior-year nine-month net income and EPS were significantly reduced by a $13.8 billion Tax Cuts and Jobs Act charge; excluding the charge, non-GAAP net income was $26.210 billion and diluted EPS was $3.38.

At March 31, 2019, Microsoft reported $263.281 billion of assets, $168.417 billion of liabilities, and $94.864 billion of stockholders’ equity. Cash and equivalents totaled $11.212 billion, while cash, equivalents, and short-term investments totaled $131.618 billion. Goodwill increased to $41.861 billion, primarily due to GitHub, and intangible assets were $8.103 billion. Current liabilities declined from $58.488 billion at June 30, 2018, while long-term debt declined from $72.242 billion to $66.585 billion. Total long-term debt, including the current portion, had a carrying value of $73.1 billion and an estimated fair value of $77.0 billion. Unearned revenue was $28.135 billion, and contracted but unrecognized revenue was $75 billion, approximately 55% of which Microsoft expected to recognize within 12 months.

Nine-month operating cash flow increased to $36.077 billion from $32.466 billion. Investing activities used $8.516 billion, including $9.874 billion of property and equipment additions, and financing activities used $28.201 billion, including $14.910 billion for share repurchases and $10.290 billion for dividends. Microsoft had $15.6 billion remaining under its $40 billion repurchase authorization and declared a quarterly dividend of $0.46 per share.

Third-quarter segment revenue was $10.242 billion for Productivity and Business Processes, $9.649 billion for Intelligent Cloud, and $10.680 billion for More Personal Computing, representing growth of 14%, 22%, and 8%, respectively. Segment operating income increased 28%, 21%, and 25%, respectively. Commercial cloud revenue rose 41% to $9.6 billion, Azure revenue increased 73%, LinkedIn revenue increased 27%, Dynamics 365 revenue increased 43%, Office 365 Commercial revenue increased 30%, Windows Commercial revenue increased 18%, and Surface revenue increased 21%.

Microsoft acquired GitHub on October 25, 2018, in a transaction valued at $7.5 billion, including $1.3 billion of cash payments for vested equity awards and an indemnity escrow. GitHub is included in Intelligent Cloud and contributed approximately $5.5 billion of goodwill and $1.3 billion of intangible assets. Microsoft also completed 14 other acquisitions totaling $1.3 billion during the nine-month period.

The financial statements were prepared under U.S. GAAP. Microsoft adopted guidance on intra-entity asset transfers and financial instruments, including recognition of equity investment changes in net income rather than comprehensive income. The adoption of intra-entity transfer guidance increased retained earnings by $557 million and had no cash-flow impact. Future guidance on hedging activities was expected to have no material impact upon adoption, while the company continued evaluating the expected-credit-loss standard.

Microsoft’s effective tax rate was 16% for both the quarter and nine months, compared with 14% and 70%, respectively, in the prior-year periods. Income-tax contingencies and liabilities totaled $15.7 billion, and unresolved IRS audit matters primarily involved transfer pricing. At March 31, 2019, the company held $127.267 billion of debt investments at fair value and $2.403 billion of equity investments; management did not believe remaining unrealized debt-investment losses represented other-than-temporary impairments. The company also used derivatives to manage foreign-currency, equity-price, interest-rate, and credit risks.

The filing disclosed 35 pending patent cases, an ongoing Chinese antitrust investigation, cell-phone litigation, and an appeal concerning a denied gender-discrimination class certification. Microsoft had accrued $253 million of legal liabilities and estimated that reasonably possible adverse outcomes could reach approximately $1.0 billion beyond recorded amounts. Deloitte & Touche LLP reviewed the interim information and reported no material modifications needed for GAAP conformity; the review did not constitute an audit opinion.

The court unanimously affirmed Dellipizzi’s convictions for first-degree robbery and sexual abuse. The robbery sufficiency issue was not raised, and the sexual-abuse evidence was sufficient. The court criticized the trial judge’s intent instruction as potentially shifting the burden of proof, but held that the charge as a whole did not do so.

On August 16, 2018, certain Tesla, Inc. subsidiaries amended two vehicle lease warehouse agreements with Deutsche Bank AG, New York Branch. The amendments extended the borrowing availability date from August 17, 2018, to August 16, 2019, and the maturity date from September 2019, to September 2020. The swinging gate is an unconventional special-teams formation in which offensive players, including the kicker, line up like a kicking unit but can execute a trick play or shift into a field-goal/extra-point formation. It is most commonly associated with two-point conversions and gives the offense several deceptive options.

The formation aims to confuse defenses with an unexpected alignment and little warning. The offense may snap quickly and run or pass before the defense reacts, or shift into a kicking formation at the last moment. Because NFL extra-point attempts must be snapped from the 15-yard line, the swinging gate is rarely used for extra points after touchdowns in the NFL, though occasional unconventional attempts have occurred.

Common trick plays include the side snap, which gives a ball carrier a quick run behind blockers, and the smoke screen, a quick pass opposite the defense’s run-focused alignment. Defenders should match personnel rather than merely numbers, protect the heavy side and middle alley, match blockers across from offensive linemen, and use “pass first” coverage against screens.

Croskey-Merritt earned more Week 5 work after a strong practice, according to coach Dan Quinn. The rookie split carries with Chris Rodriguez and Jeremy McNichols, recording 14 carries, 150 scrimmage yards and two touchdowns.

Margin debt climbed $22.9 billion in January to a record $665.7 billion, then fell to $645.1 billion in February and edged to $645.2 billion in March. FINRA warned that high margin borrowing could lead to forced liquidations, substantial losses, and reduced participation in market rebounds. Margin debt amplifies rallies through added buying liquidity and selloffs through forced selling, although the recent decline has been orderly. Its 12-month increase through March was nearly half January’s gain. Since 2009, margin debt has mostly risen and exceeded its July 2007 peak by 55%. The passage says past leverage surges were followed by crashes, but current deleveraging may be gradual amid Fed tightening and substantial market liquidity.
