The statistical analysis plan defines investigator-assessed adverse-event causality as not related, unlikely related, possibly related, or probably related, with possible and probable events classified as related. Unresolved missing causality assessments are assigned as related, while missing severity ratings remain missing. AE summaries will report patient counts, percentages, and total events for screening AEs, TEAEs, AESIs, other important events, injection-site reactions, drug-related and serious TEAEs, and deaths. MedDRA tables will present system organ class and preferred term data, count each patient once per preferred term, show total events, and be ordered by descending incidence in the dasiglucagon group. Special searches include QT-interval prolongation and drug-related hepatic disorders, supplemented by pharmacovigilance-provided preferred-term files.

Laboratory analyses will provide descriptive statistics, reference-range categories, categorical counts and percentages, and change-from-baseline results; high/low flags require available reference ranges, and the most recent measurement is used when multiple values occur at one visit. Hematology, biochemistry, and urinalysis will follow this format without figures; screening coagulation results, pregnancy-test counts and percentages, alcohol-breath listings, vital-sign summaries, and physical-examination listings are also specified. ECG outputs will include investigator interpretations, parameter descriptives, QTcF thresholds above 450, 480, and 500 ms, and postbaseline QTcF changes above 30 and 60 ms. Immunogenicity will be summarized descriptively without statistical tests, counting treatment-induced ADA patients and baseline-positive patients with at least a fivefold titer increase; the denominator will include evaluable patients only.

Changes from the protocol include reworded primary-efficacy analysis and added sensitivity and supportive analyses, and replacement of secondary-efficacy wording from “within” to “at” specified minutes.

Appendices define table, figure, and listing presentation conventions, including decimal precision, percentages, P-values, footnotes, source and run metadata, sorting, dates, and times. Missing or incomplete AE onset dates will generally be treated as treatment-emergent unless other information indicates otherwise. Derived variables include durations, metric-to-SI unit conversions, BMI, and postbaseline-minus-baseline changes. SAS quality-control requirements cover program structure, documentation, log and output review, dataset validation, patient-level spot checks, listing and figure verification, Pinnacle 21 validation, and retention of supporting documentation.

Planned outputs include disposition, demographics, diabetes history, body measurements, medical history, concomitant medications, glucose-recovery efficacy analyses and Kaplan–Meier curves, plasma-glucose analyses, AE tables and listings, hypoglycemia-procedure data, ECG, laboratory, vital-sign, immunogenicity, PK/PD results, exclusions, and individual data listings.

Secondary analyses will assess ≥20 mg/dL plasma glucose recovery at 10, 15, 20, and 30 minutes using actual sampling times. Patients receiving IV glucose before recovery will be classified as not recovered. Dasiglucagon and placebo recovery rates will be compared using a Cochran–Mantel–Haenszel test stratified by age group and injection site, or a non-stratified Fisher test if cell counts are insufficient; responder rates and 95% confidence intervals will be reported. Baseline glucose changes will also be analyzed by ANOVA for treatment, age group, and injection site, presenting adjusted means, treatment differences, and 95% confidence intervals.

Hello Wood’s Pebl Grand is a prefabricated, 200-square-foot tiny cabin designed to resemble a spaceship while blending into nature. Its asymmetrical, faceted exterior uses wood, stone, or mirror cladding, with wood, stone, and aluminum inside. The standard model starts at €73,000 ($86,247) and includes a king-size bed, kitchenette, dining nook, and bathroom. An upgraded version with an infrared sauna and panoramic window starts at €85,000 ($100,424).

The cabin uses a ground-screw foundation, avoiding a concrete slab. European clients can receive turnkey units, while overseas deliveries arrive as flat-packed panels for on-site assembly. Installation generally takes a few weeks, with two to three months typically needed from deposit to installation. Clients are responsible for permits and usually utilities, though Hello Wood can assist.

Potential uses include private accommodation, pop-up suites, VIP lounges, artist rest spaces, and festival green rooms. A New York City venue purchased five units for its rooftop terrace. The minimalist interior features oak walls, parquet or carpet flooring, and cross-laminated timber furniture.

Mutual funds’ exposure to software stocks reached a record Rs 70,773 crore in April, up from Rs 64,265 crore in March and Rs 42,023 crore in April 2017, representing 7.37% of equity AUM. Fund managers increased allocations as the rupee depreciated, while the BSE IT Index rose over 18% year-to-date, outperforming the Sensex’s 2.5% gain.

The dollar index dropped 0.6%, and European stocks were expected to open flat to lower. Asian shares were mixed: MSCI Asia-Pacific shares excluding Japan rose 0.6%, while Japan’s Nikkei fell 0.7%. Cam Newton apologized on social media for a sexist remark. At Sunday’s Detroit press conference, he may face repeated questions about it and choose whether to respond or walk away, with the story continuing around 4 p.m. ET.

Union Finance Minister Arun Jaitley told economists at a pre-budget consultation that India averaged 7.5% growth from 2014-15 to 2016-17 despite subdued global growth, and that second-quarter growth in 2017-18 reversed a recent decline. He said the fiscal deficit-to-GDP ratio fell from 3.9% in 2015-16 to 3.5% in 2016-17 and was budgeted at 3.2% for 2017-18, aided by expenditure rationalisation, Direct Benefit Transfer, PFMS and revenue measures.

Economists recommended continuing fiscal consolidation and announcing tax-reform and GST road maps; promoting infrastructure, SME, construction, labour-intensive and rural non-farm investment; supporting farm prices within 4–6% inflation, PSU disinvestment, effective crop insurance, expanded pensions and maternity benefits; lowering corporate tax and long-term capital gains tax, reducing MAT and simplifying tax administration; and increasing R&D, bank recapitalisation, digital payments, NREGA wages, defence investment, skills planning, social protection and private investment.

The article surveys offensive football formations, noting that coaches often use different names for similar alignments. It covers basic formations such as the I, Split Backs, and Twins, each balancing running and passing threats. The I formation lines running backs behind the quarterback for interior runs, while Twins creates a “tight” side and a “flexed” side for run-pass options.

Modern spread formations include Ace, with two eligible receivers on each side; Trips, with three on one side and one on the other; Empty, with five receivers and no running back; Quads, with four receivers on one side; and Bunch, which groups three receivers to create difficult coverage and crossing-route opportunities.

Backfield sets include the Shotgun, in which the quarterback receives the snap several yards behind center; the Pistol, which combines a deep quarterback with a running back directly behind him; and the Single Back. Older formations include the Wishbone, Flexbone, Double Wing, T, Wing-T, Power I, and Single Wing, many of which rely on multiple running backs, misdirection, option plays, or unbalanced blocking.

The article also describes unusual “gadget” formations. Wildcat uses an unbalanced line and a non-quarterback to take the snap; Emory and Henry spreads players into separate pods; Swinging Gate is used after touchdowns to create a two-point opportunity; and Unbalanced formations load one side of the line with extra blockers, often near the goal line.

The passage describes NVIDIA’s 2018 Turing GPU architecture, which combines rasterization, real-time ray tracing, AI, and simulation through a hybrid rendering model. Rasterization remains effective for visibility and primary rays, while ray tracing is applied to reflections, refractions, shadows, and other effects that benefit from physical accuracy. Denoising reduces the rays required, while dedicated RT Cores accelerate BVH traversal and ray-triangle intersection tests. Turing reportedly reaches over 10 Giga Rays per second, about ten times Pascal’s software-based performance.

RT Cores are included in each Streaming Multiprocessor and use specialized units for bounding-box and ray-triangle tests, freeing the SM for shading and compute work. The driver handles BVH building and refitting, while applications manage ray generation and shading. Turing ray tracing supports RTX libraries, OptiX, Microsoft DXR, and the forthcoming Vulkan ray-tracing API.

NVIDIA NGX is a Turing-only, deep-learning technology stack using Tensor Cores. Its DLSS system trains against high-quality 64-times-supersampled references. Standard DLSS renders fewer samples and uses AI to infer an image comparable to temporal anti-aliasing with roughly half the shading work. DLSS 2X renders at the target resolution and uses a larger network to approach 64-times-supersampled quality. In an UE4 demonstration, DLSS and Tensor Cores helped the RTX 2080 Ti achieve twice the performance of the GTX 1080 Ti. Other NGX features include AI Inpainting, AI Slow-Mo for interpolated video frames, and AI Super Rez for 2x, 4x, or 8x image and video upscaling.

Mesh shading introduces cooperative task and mesh shaders that can process object lists in parallel, select geometry levels of detail, and perform dynamic geometry operations. This reduces CPU draw-call bottlenecks and can increase the number of real-time objects by more than an order of magnitude. Variable Rate Shading allows each 16-by-16-pixel tile to use one of several shading rates independently of visibility sampling. Its applications include content-adaptive shading for low-detail regions, motion-adaptive shading for moving objects, and foveated rendering that shades peripheral areas less intensely.

Texture Space Shading stores computed shading values in texture space and later samples them for screen pixels. It decouples visibility from appearance sampling, reuses shading across frames, eyes, and requests, and supports variable resolution through texture LODs. Multi-View Rendering draws multiple viewpoints or character poses in one pass, supporting four views in hardware and up to 32 through the API while sharing independent shader work. Turing also improves VR through MVR, foveated rendering, USB-C and VirtualLink connectivity, and RT Core acceleration of ray-traced audio.

Turing adds bindless constant-buffer and unordered-access views and supports Tier 2 resource heaps. The TU104 contains 48 SMs, 3,072 CUDA Cores, 368 Tensor Cores, and 48 RT Cores, with 13.6 billion transistors and NVLink support. The TU104-based Tesla T4 contains 40 SMs, 2,560 CUDA Cores, and 320 Tensor Cores, with 320 GB/s memory bandwidth. TU106 contains 36 SMs, 2,304 CUDA Cores, 288 Tensor Cores, and 36 RT Cores but lacks NVLink and SLI.

RTX-OPS is presented as a workload-based metric combining tensor, FP32, RT, and integer operations. Its calculation weights tensor usage at 20%, CUDA cores at 80%, RT cores at 40%, and INT32 pipes at 28%, yielding 78 RTX-OPS for the RTX 2080 Ti.

The passage also explains that ray tracing casts rays backward from the camera through scene geometry to determine visible surfaces, lighting, reflections, refractions, shadows, and indirect illumination. BVHs hierarchically group geometry to reduce intersection tests; they can be rebuilt after major scene changes or refitted after smaller changes. Ray-traced shadows can produce hard edges and correct contact hardening, ray-traced ambient occlusion adds more realistic definition than screen-space methods, and ray-traced reflections avoid the missing content and artifacts associated with screen-space reflections.

The SEV-TIO extension lets SEV-SNP guests bind passed-through devices to trusted-device contexts within their private address space. Guests detect support through the TEE-IO PCIe capabilities register, and binding occurs on the first SNP TIO Guest Request. VMPL0 firmware performs setup for TIO-unenlightened guests; otherwise, the guest OS fetches device information, fetches and validates the interface report, and configures MMIO and IOMMU. The SNP TIO Guest Request supplies unencrypted guest PCI ID, MMIO range and desired validated state, and TDISP status. Optional shared, guest-contiguous data pages provide input and receive measurements, certificates, and a TDISP attestation report through a DATA GPA descriptor table containing GUIDs, offsets, and lengths. The hypervisor validates page capacity and reports the required page count if insufficient. For TDI information requests, a nonzero nonce in the first 32 bytes causes the hypervisor to obtain fresh device measurements from SEV firmware before forwarding the request.

Secure AVIC manages guest-owned APIC state through a private backing page per vCPU that must remain present in the guest’s nested paging table while the vCPU runs. Guests can register or unregister a page-aligned backing-page GPA for a selected vCPU; registering replaces any previous GPA, and unregistering returns the prior GPA or zero. This support is implied by the Secure AVIC setting in SEV_FEATURES and requires no separate feature bit.

A termination-request event lets a guest request termination, with the reason encoded in SW_EXITINFO1 and optional 64-bit information in SW_EXITINFO2. Reason code 0x01 indicates that the SEV-ES/GHCB protocol range is unsupported and supplies a mask of unsupported features. A guest receiving a NAE outside the negotiated protocol version must exit with the “Unsupported Event” code. Guests identify SEV-ES support through additional CPUID properties indicating hypervisor operation, SEV support, the encryption bit position, and reduced physical-address-space bits.

Because measured and encrypted vCPU registers cannot be updated after launch, traditional INIT-SIPI-SIPI application-processor startup is problematic under SEV-ES and SEV-SNP. Initial CS and IP values may instead be supplied through a reset-vector memory mechanism or a predefined location known to the hypervisor. The first AP reset uses the initial measured values. Subsequent resets use AP Reset Hold requests through either an NAE event or MSR protocol; after a SIPI, the hypervisor completes the hold without changing registers, and the AP transitions to real mode and begins at the supplied reset vector. With Restricted Injection, AP Reset Hold is unavailable and SNP AP Creation is required.

For environment transitions such as UEFI to an OS, UEFI parks APs with a defined VMGEXIT and supplies an encrypted, page-aligned 4 KB AP jump table containing reset-vector information. The table is communicated through SET and GET NAE events and, for SEV-SNP, the Secrets Page; differing reset vectors require serialization. This startup model does not support vCPU hotplug. The SNP AP Creation feature instead uses VMGEXIT 0x8000_0013 and an RMPADJUST-designated VMSA page to create or update an AP’s state, either delaying use until INIT or making the AP immediately runnable. It removes the need for AP Reset Hold and permits vCPU hotplug.

For NMIs, the hypervisor intercepts #DB but not IRET and uses the guest’s “NMI Complete” message to determine when another NMI may be injected. An example guest implementation sets a per-CPU indicator and the trap flag before IRET, then handles the resulting #DB intercept. Full hardware debug-register virtualization is enabled through the DebugVirtualization feature and uses the VMSA to save and restore state; otherwise, DR7 reads and writes are intercepted and emulated through a cached value.

SMM and nested virtualization are not supported in this specification. The #HV doorbell mechanism defines a shared, host-owned notification page with a 16-bit PendingEvent field and a NoEoiRequired byte. PendingEvent can carry an interrupt vector, NMI, virtual #MC, a no-further-signal flag, and reserved bits. The host must emulate APIC presentation, acknowledgment, in-service, and EOI semantics, while the guest atomically exchanges PendingEvent before acting on a vector, validates observed vectors, and performs EOI through either the assist flag or an explicit APIC write. Guests should halt with interrupts disabled, and the host should immediately re-enter the guest if events remain pending. Doorbell pages are configured through VMGEXIT 0x8000_0014 using SET, QUERY, and request-address actions. Noncooperative guest or host behavior may cause denial of service or guest panic but does not compromise host integrity.

This continuation patent application (claiming priority from Austrian Patent Application A56/2015 via PCT/AT2016/000007 and a chain of U.S. applications, now U.S. Pat. No. 11,098,179) concerns a novel phase-stable colloidal polysaccharide suspension containing (1→3)-glucan, a low-cost method for preparing it, and its uses. Such suspensions are referred to as "gels," both terms being synonymous.

**Background and prior art.** Natural polysaccharides such as xanthan gum, alginate, guar gum, starch and cellulose derivatives (e.g., carboxymethyl cellulose) dissolve as colloids in water and therefore do not form stable colloidal suspensions. Cellulose is the most widespread polysaccharide; nanofibrillar cellulose and fibrous pulp gels of cellulose I structure, and cellulose II gels prepared by the amine oxide process (solvent preferably N-methylmorpholine-oxide; WO2013/006876A1), are known. Such amine-oxide cellulose gels, prepared by high-pressure homogenization of spinning dope, are largely isotropic, with highly swollen particles forming a three-dimensional network, but require pretreatment and high energy input. Enzymatic production of (1→3)-glucan from saccharose using GtfJ glucosyltransferase isolated from *Streptococcus salivarius* is disclosed in U.S. Pat. No. 7,000,000, with purer glucans in WO2013/036968A1 and WO2013/036918A2. Known glucan gels are either (1→4)-glucans or β(1→3)-glucans requiring dissolution and reprecipitation, or chemical pretreatments; direct preparation of such gels is not known.

**Object.** To provide a phase-stable colloidal polysaccharide suspension requiring no chemical or enzymatic pretreatment of the polysaccharide, offering high energy efficiency, an inexpensive base material, and a simplified process.

**The invention.** Surprisingly, this is achieved using biotechnologically produced, never-dried (1→3)-glucan. The suspension is characterized by a polysaccharide consisting at least partly of α(1→3)-glucan that was never dried during preparation; a press cake base material with 4–80% solids (preferably 15–45%); and a suspension polysaccharide concentration of 0.01–50% (preferably 1.0–20%). The glucan content may be 1–100% (preferably 80–100%); remainder may be cellulose gels (preferably amine oxide process, cellulose II structure), cellulose derivatives, starch, or other (1→6)-, (1→2)- and (1→4)-linked glucans, such mixtures being advantageous in the paper industry. Method: use an initially moist press cake, adjust concentration by adding water, and comminute with a low-shear dispersing unit such as an Ultraturrax® mixer or colloid mill; no chemical/enzymatic pretreatment, high pressure, high shear, or dissolving/precipitating steps are needed, reducing total energy severalfold versus cellulose gels and avoiding residual solvent, making the suspension suitable for foodstuffs, pharmaceuticals and cosmetics. High-pressure homogenization is optional to improve homogeneity. If the glucan was dried beforehand, only poorly stable gels with barely perceptible viscosity increase result. Weight-average DP may be 200–2,000 (preferably 400–1,000), with a very narrow molecular weight distribution. Additives (pigments, titanium oxides, barium sulfate, ion exchangers, polyethylene, polypropylene, polyester, latex, activated carbon, polymeric superabsorbents, flame retardants, and further organic/inorganic additives such as chitosan, nanosilver, zinc oxide) may be incorporated at 1–200% relative to polysaccharide quantity.

**Uses.** The suspensions are film-forming, suitable for polysaccharide layers, sheets and coatings (paper, packaging), barriers, coating-mixture additives (doctoring, spraying, brushing), molded bodies (extrusion, molds), viscosity modifiers/thickeners, and binders for nonwovens and flushable wipes (structures break up again in water). They also serve as base material for dried polysaccharide powder: simple drying forms hydrogen-bonded agglomerates and compact layers (explaining film formation), whereas spray drying and freeze drying yield separated particles; spray-dried particles average under 1 µm to 5 µm; supercritical drying yields aerogels; "spacers" such as inorganic salts, polyethylene glycol or cellulose derivatives may be added to weaken hydrogen bonding.

**Examples.** Example 1: a press cake of initially moist α(1→3)-glucan (dry matter 17.6%) was suspended in deionized water at 3.05% and comminuted with an Ultraturrax® (IKA T50 basic, 6,000 rpm, 4 min); one portion was additionally passed through a high-pressure homogenizer (GEA Niro Soavi NS 1001L-2K, 1,000 bar, 2 passes). Both suspensions showed shear-diluting behavior with essentially identical viscosity curves (Malvern Kinexus, cone-plate CP4/40, 10–200 s⁻¹). Water retention capacity (WRC) was measured after centrifugation (15 min, 3,000 rpm) and drying at 105 °C. Dried glucans (linear DPw 1,000 and 500, and branched glucan) at 2–3% solids showed phase separation, far lower WRC, no viscosity increase, and visible particles even after six homogenizer passes.

Example 2: pilot-scale production with a colloid mill (IKA MK2000/10) from 3.69 kg never-dried glucan (TS 16.25%) and 11.3 kg water gave a 3.9% gel after 15 minutes at a 0.1 mm gap; the gel showed shear-diluting behavior, tiny-particle agglomerates detectable microscopically (ZEISS Discovery V12, 50×) that are not felt by touch and disintegrate under slight shear, no visible particles after inversion in a glass tube, and a uniform dense film on the tube wall. Doctored and sprayed films on polyester sheets and glass were continuous, uniform and adherent; SEM (Hitachi S-4000) images of air-dried films showed a dense layer, and freeze-dried gel showed a three-dimensional spongy network.

Example 3: with increasing solids content, viscosity increased and WRC decreased; 3% and 4% suspensions could still be processed with a high-pressure homogenizer, while 5% suspensions could only be comminuted with the low-shear Ultraturrax, the homogenizer being unable to pump them. Table 3 lists viscosities at 50 s⁻¹ of 0.2009 (after HDH), 0.8555 (after IKA) and 1.731 (after UT) and corresponding TS/WRC values.

Example 4: the 3% gel was spray dried in a Büchi Mini Spray Dryer 8-290 (supply air 180 °C, exhaust air 62 °C, 1.4 mm nozzle); laser diffraction (Helos) in isopropanol gave particle size distribution values of 0.79, 2.2, 5.29 and 8.27 µm.

Example 5: 1.887 kg never-dried moist (1→3)-glucan (TS 39.74%) with 5.613 kg water was ground for 20 minutes at 0.1 mm gap in the IKA MK2000/10 colloid mill to yield a stable 10% suspension whose viscosity is comparable to the 4% gel of Example 2, with small particles not detectable by touch.

The mother and father cross-appealed a Family Court custody-modification order concerning their daughters, ages 17 and 15. A 2003 agreement gave the father sole custody and the mother visitation subject to the daughters’ wishes, while requiring the father to encourage and facilitate their relationship with her. In March 2004, the father moved the daughters to Florida without notifying the mother and subsequently obstructed her communication and visits, including violating a court-ordered phone-contact schedule.

Family Court found that the father had intentionally violated the custody order and hindered the daughters’ relationship with their mother, but the evidence did not justify changing physical custody. The court also found no support for allegations that the mother had psychiatric or alcohol problems. The mother withdrew her custody request concerning the older daughter but sought court-ordered visitation with the younger child. The Law Guardian recommended that the daughters remain with the father, with visitation between the mother and younger daughter.

The appellate court affirmed the custody determination but reversed the provision making the younger daughter’s visitation subject to her wishes. It found that the father’s interference raised fitness concerns, that his failure to testify supported adverse inferences, and that the record was insufficiently developed. The matter was remanded for an updated in camera hearing and further proceedings, with the existing visitation pattern continuing meanwhile. The suspension of the mother’s child-support obligation was affirmed.

The passage describes the Passing Game as an unstructured, team-oriented basketball offense built around continuous ball and player movement rather than fixed patterns. Off-ball screens, cuts, passing, and spacing involve all five players, and the system can be adapted to different personnel and alignments. It is intended to be effective against both zone and person-to-person defenses, while also allowing set-offense concepts to be incorporated.

Its strengths include involvement by all players, creativity, continuous motion, control of tempo, effectiveness against different defenses, and difficulty for opponents to scout. Weaknesses include breakdowns caused by selfish or highly exceptional players, inconsistent offensive rebounding, weak defensive reads, impatience in creating shots, and players’ dislike of playing without the ball.

Success requires coaches to teach and players to master shooting, passing, screening, and rebounding. Players must move with a defined purpose, such as creating a lead, cutting sharply, setting a screen, or establishing rebounding position. Other fundamentals include sharp and accurate passing, developing leads before receiving the ball, maintaining 15–18-foot spacing, shot discipline, reading the defense, posting up, and aggressively pursuing missed shots. Players should eliminate unnecessary dribbling, meet passes in a triple-threat position, set solid screens, use screen-and-pop, replace, slip, and roll options, and counter defensive overplays with back cuts.

The offense follows simple rules covering pass-and-move action, leads, spacing, screens, cuts, triple-threat situations, post-ups, and rebounding. Timing and coordinated movement are emphasized: screens must be set before action begins, passes generally should travel 12–15 feet, and receivers must call for the ball, present a target, and meet passes while preserving spacing. Players should know their shooting range, attack the defender’s up foot, recognize open shots, drives, back cuts, and screen opportunities, and exploit size mismatches in the post. Offensive rebounding requires anticipation, determination, hustle, inside positioning, and second and third efforts.

Variations include the three-person Hi/Lo passing game, the four-person Four Out system using a single or rotating post, and the five-person motion offense. Hi/Lo operates primarily as a three-out, two-in set with post exchanges and screens. Four Out rotates players through the post and permits numerous entry types. Motion is suited to smaller, athletic teams and emphasizes unpredictable movement, open penetration, and cutters, with little posting.

Against zone defenses, the offense should use quicker movement, sharp passing, facing the basket, fake passes, skips, weak-side attacks, and penetration into gaps. Players should make the zone commit to the ball, cycle the defense, attack from behind to create leads, push the ball early, avoid unnecessary dribbling once past half court, go to the boards, and maintain defensive balance.

The passage notes that coaches may initially perceive less control but can benefit from the system’s unpredictability, low-possession pressure, back-cut opportunities, defensive fatigue, and steady execution based on patience and teamwork rather than exceptional shooting nights.

This systematic review examines the definition, effects, and influencing factors of digital leadership in education amid increasing technological transformation and limited prior research. Following PRISMA guidelines, the study searched Scopus, Web of Science, and EBSCO from November 9–12, 2023, and supplemented the search through citation tracking, yielding 39 empirical studies from 2,761 initial records.

Only 11 studies defined digital leadership, using terms such as technology, e-, ICT, and digital leadership. Existing definitions generally neglected leadership elements, educational contexts, organizational environments, or follower roles. Drawing on the technology-organization-environment framework, the review proposes a dynamic, adaptive model in which leaders understand and apply technology, develop competencies, interact with followers, and reshape organizational environments to support digital innovation and educational transformation.

Twenty-eight studies addressed digital leadership’s effects. Research concentrated on teachers, including technology integration, professional development, reflective practice, self-efficacy, and job engagement. School-level effects included improved administration and teaching quality, ICT and digital transformation, digital learning cultures, and educational resource use. Limited student-focused evidence indicated improved academic performance and more personalized learning, while creativity and digital literacy remained underexplored.

Only 10 studies examined influencing factors. Internal factors included individual characteristics, administrative experience, professional qualifications, digital literacy, technology acceptance, and self-efficacy. External factors included infrastructure, school culture, policies, technical supervision, training programs, and the COVID-19 pandemic. These factors were found to be interdependent.

The review identifies gaps concerning dynamic definitions, follower involvement, student behavior and lifelong learning, digital security, multicultural digital teams, organizational culture, and stronger theoretical foundations.

Dialogue should address human rights and Soviet internal behavior, while Soviet conduct on INF serves as a test of Moscow’s seriousness. The NCAA targeting rule, implemented in 2008 to improve player safety and prevent traumatic brain injuries, applies when a player takes aim at an opponent for forcible contact beyond a legal tackle, block, or play for the ball. Defensible players are protected, with those especially vulnerable due to their physical position or focus considered defenseless when the call is in question.

Targeting incurs a 15-yard penalty and disqualification. First-half violations lead to ejection for the remainder of the game, while second-half violations result in a first-half suspension for the next game. Repeat offenders also face automatic one-game suspensions, with each additional foul adding another suspension. NCAA targeting penalties carry no fines.

The rule was amended in 2013 to add disqualifications and related suspensions, and video review became mandatory for confirming or denying targeting penalties in 2019. Unlike the NCAA, the NFL calls the comparable violation unnecessary roughness against a defenseless player and does not impose automatic disqualification, though flagrant actions can prompt ejection and additional punishment.

Controversial examples include Shaun Wade’s 2019 targeting call against Trevor Lawrence and Michael Taaffe’s unreviewed helmet-to-helmet hit in the 2024-25 Peach Bowl.

Keith Chegwin, best known for hosting the children’s game show *Cheggers Play Pop*, died aged 60 at home after a long illness, his family said. He had idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis, a progressive lung condition, and died on 11 December with his wife and children. His family thanked Severn Hospice and requested privacy.

IPF scars and stiffens the lungs, impairing breathing, with variable progression and possible acute flare-ups. Symptoms include breathlessness, persistent cough, fatigue and finger or toe clubbing. About 6,000 people are diagnosed annually in the UK, mostly over 70, and men are more affected. Suggested causes include reflux, viruses and occupational dust.

Will Ma concludes his final MIT poker class, noting that final prize rankings will depend partly on homework and that Bill Chen will teach the next class.

Ma analyzes a 100-big-blind cash-game hand in which 8-7 suited on the button calls a flop continuation bet on 10-8-6, then calls a turn bet after the queen of clubs arrives. He explains that the suited connector has substantial implied odds and equity, while calling rather than raising allows Ma to see the river and avoid facing an all-in reraise with a vulnerable made hand. He contrasts this with weaker draws, which may prefer raising, and explains the principle that nuts want an opponent to commit first, while vulnerable made hands and strong draws generally want opponents to have the last betting opportunity. He also reviews bet-sizing considerations, including avoiding bets that give opponents excessive calling odds, limiting risk when bluffing, and using larger river bets with polarized ranges.

After the opponent checks the ace of spades on the river, Ma bluffs $70 into $107. He constructs an exploitative range for the cutoff opponent from a roughly 30% opening range, classifying hands as value bets, bluffs, traps, check-calls, or give-ups. Using PokerStove and explicit combination counts, he estimates that the opponent will fold more than half the time and that only about 5 of 42 possible combinations are worse than Ma’s pair of eights. The calculation indicates that the river bluff is highly profitable, illustrating why visual range tools alone can misrepresent hand frequencies.

Ma then discusses why poker became financially lucrative. He identifies overconfidence, weak gambling self-control, rapid strategic evolution, and excessive focus on results rather than decisions. Overconfidence is encouraged by selective memory, unclear benchmarks, and the need to take risks, while confidence is also necessary for sound play and assessing one’s ability. He recommends treating recreational poker as entertainment and being honest about one’s skill, citing David Einhorn’s willingness to lose large sums while treating poker as a recreational pursuit. Gambling self-control includes avoiding tilt, fatigue, and attempts to win back losses. Hold’em’s rapid evolution, with strategies developing quickly as top players discovered overlooked approaches, created an advantage for continual study; Ma recommends online resources such as CardRunners, Two Plus Two, and Twitch, along with several poker books.

Finally, Ma argues that players should judge decisions rather than short-term outcomes because poker contains substantial variance, long losing streaks are possible, and even skilled players may need early luck. He presents the “joy of making good decisions,” illustrated by Bill Gates, as a central attitude for poker and life. In questions, he discusses recovering from downswings, playing casino games tightly against recreational opponents, obtaining honest feedback from stronger players, continuing through the MIT Poker Club, and the claimed restrictions on playing online poker for money in Massachusetts.

Facebook shares were on track for their largest one-day percentage decline in four years amid regulatory criticism over Cambridge Analytica’s access to user data without express permission. The stock fell 6.8% in midday trading, erasing nearly $40 billion in market value, while the broader tech sector and major indexes also declined. U.S. and U.K. regulators said Facebook permitted access and retained data for years despite saying it had destroyed the records. Analysts agreed the episode poses public-relations and regulatory risk but disagreed on its business impact. Wells Fargo maintained a buy rating, while others anticipated tighter content, advertising, security, and measurement policies. Facebook recently prioritized friends-and-family content and said reducing viral videos cut daily usage by 50 million hours.

The coach said substitutions are his decision and praised the team’s performance despite some difficult calls. The opponents were strong, particularly in speed, forechecking, and puck control, as expected. The team focused on each shift, stayed committed when trailing, and will now prepare for the next game.

U.S. Adm. Harry Harris, nominated as ambassador to Australia, will instead become ambassador to South Korea, Australian Foreign Minister Julie Bishop said. She attributed the change to significant U.S. challenges on the Korean Peninsula and said a replacement would be prioritized. Australia has lacked a full U.S. ambassador since John Berry left in September 2016, with Jim Caroso serving as chargé d’affaires. In 2016, the Rams sent six draft picks to the Titans for the No. 1 overall selection and two later picks. The Rams used the first pick on quarterback Jared Goff, while further trades involved the Bears, Browns and Broncos. The deal produced Pro Bowlers Goff and return specialist Pharoh Cooper for Los Angeles. Tennessee acquired receiver Corey Davis, offensive lineman Jack Conklin, running back Derrick Henry, tight end Jonnu Smith, defensive lineman Austin Johnson, cornerbacks LeShaun Sims and Kalan Reed, and other players.

Goff struggled as a rookie but later passed for 3,804 yards and 28 touchdowns before making the Pro Bowl. Cooper also became a Pro Bowl returner. Tennessee’s Conklin earned All-Pro honors as a rookie before tearing his ACL, Davis emerged as a starting receiver, and Henry was poised to become the primary running back. The overall result was considered unclear because Tennessee received more potential starters, but the Rams had already gained two Pro Bowlers and won their division sooner. The passage gives the Rams a slight edge, while calling Tennessee’s trade grade “incomplete” pending the health and production of Davis and Conklin and Henry’s success.

DNA-rich droplets in a three-dimensional self-stirring active fluid of microtubules and kinesin motor clusters coarsen primarily through collision-driven coalescence rather than Ostwald ripening. Active flows accelerate coarsening and produce an increasingly asymmetric droplet population containing many small droplets and a few exceptionally large ones, so the relative size distribution is not self-similar. Active droplets show ballistic motion at short times and diffusive-like motion at longer times, with size-independent effective diffusivity set by the active flow’s mean speed and velocity-correlation length, unlike passive Brownian droplets.

Both active and passive droplets exhibit similar mean-radius power laws, with βR approximately 0.33, but droplet number decays faster in the active fluid: γN is −1.65 for active coarsening versus −0.89 for passive coarsening. These active-coarsening exponents remain unchanged when ATP concentration, flow speed, confinement, and active length scale are varied. Passive droplet size distributions remain time-independent and log-normal, consistent with Brownian Smoluchowski coarsening.

Three-dimensional hydrodynamic simulations and simulations of self-propelled and anomalously diffusing droplets reproduce the experimental behavior and show that coarsening exponents are governed by binary collision dynamics rather than by the active or passive origin of droplet motion. The collision-kernel exponent k is the unifying control parameter, with k related to the anomalous-diffusion exponent α and the size-dependent diffusivity exponent m by k = 3 − (m + 2)/α. Brownian droplets have k = 0, retain self-similarity, and satisfy βR = −γN/3. Positive k favors collisions between the largest droplets, causes progressive size-distribution asymmetry and loss of self-similarity, and produces a nonlinear relationship between βR and γN. Probabilistic calculations confirm these predictions.

Active coarsening rapidly increases the largest droplets, whereas Brownian coarsening more effectively increases the average droplet size. The framework may apply to biological condensates governed by active transport, chromatin-driven subdiffusion, or preferential attachment. Open questions include finite-size effects, behavior when droplets approach or exceed the active length scale, and the possible roles of shear and Ostwald ripening in such regimes.

The founder recounts building a supplement company at 16 around herbal ecstasy, reporting more than $350 million in earnings within a year. In 2010, he recognized Amazon’s growing role in supplements and listed his nootropic product, Excelerol. After soliciting reviews from 100 subscribers, the listing gained about 65 reviews and $5,000 in overnight sales. Amazon initially boosted sales and introduced new customers, but later adopted buyer-focused policies that increased risks for sellers, including product restrictions and account suspensions. After navigating these rules for more than five years, the author now advises Fortune 500 companies and startups on succeeding in Amazon’s marketplace.

The NVIDIA A100 Tensor Core GPU architecture is designed for high-performance computing and AI workloads. Its HBM2 memory and other key structures—including the L2 cache, SM L1 caches, and register files—use SECDED ECC for data protection and reliability. The A100 has a 40 MB L2 cache, 6.7 times larger than the Tesla V100, divided into two partitions for higher bandwidth and lower latency. It provides 2.3 times the L2 read bandwidth of V100 and supports cache-residency controls and Compute Data Compression, which can improve DRAM read/write bandwidth by up to four times, L2 read bandwidth by up to four times, and effective L2 capacity by up to two times.

A100 has 108 streaming multiprocessors, compared with 80 in V100, and third-generation Tensor Cores supporting peak mixed-precision performance 16 times higher than standard FP32 FMA operations. Its Tensor Cores share data across 32 warp threads rather than eight, perform larger matrix operations per instruction, issue eight times fewer instructions, and make 2.9 times fewer register-file accesses for matrix multiplication than V100. New asynchronous copy instructions move data directly from global memory to shared memory, bypassing L1 and the register file, while asynchronous barriers support efficient data-fetch pipelines. Maximum shared-memory allocation per SM increases to 164 KB, and the five-site HBM2 subsystem delivers 1,555 GB/s of bandwidth. A100 supports compute capability 8.0 and omits display connectors, RT Cores, and an NVENC encoder.

Multi-Instance GPU (MIG) can divide an A100 into as many as seven isolated GPU Instances, each with dedicated compute and memory resources, predictable performance, quality-of-service guarantees, and fault isolation. GPU Instances can contain multiple Compute Instances, which support concurrent CUDA contexts and Volta-style MPS. MIG is compute-only, preserves the CUDA programming model, and supports migrating virtual GPUs between compatible instances or GPUs.

Third-generation NVLink provides lossless, high-bandwidth communication with error detection and packet replay. A100 has 12 links, compared with six in V100, for 600 GB/s of total bandwidth versus 300 GB/s. Its writes are non-posted, permitting requester-side synchronization and execution-context-specific error attribution. A100 also supports PCIe Gen 4 with 31.5 GB/s per direction on x16 connections and SR-IOV for sharing or virtualizing a GPU.

Additional fault-management features improve error attribution, isolation, and containment, including propagation of remote-GPU page faults over NVLink. Other dedicated hardware includes the five-core NVJPG JPEG decoder, a GA100 Optical Flow Accelerator supporting optical flow and stereo disparity, improved global-memory atomic throughput—11 times higher for FP16 and 2.7 times higher for FP32 than V100—and five NVDEC units compared with one in V100.

CUDA 11 adds support for third-generation Tensor Cores, sparsity, CUDA Graphs, MIG, and L2 residency controls. Task graphs separate workflow definition from execution, reducing CPU launch overhead and enabling launch and dependency optimizations on A100. CUDA also exposes asynchronous global-to-shared-memory copies, including bypass and L1-access variants, and asynchronous barriers that can synchronize arbitrary thread subsets. L2 persistence can reserve capacity in 2.5 MB increments, although this feature is disabled in MIG mode. Cooperative Groups adds group-wide asynchronous-copy pipelines and hardware-accelerated reductions; grid-synchronization overhead can be reduced by up to 30%.

DGX A100 combines eight A100 GPUs with six NVSwitches, providing 4.8 TB/s of total bidirectional interconnect bandwidth and up to 5 PFLOPS of AI performance in a 6U system. With MIG, the system can expose as many as 56 isolated accelerators. Its software stack includes CUDA 11, the NVIDIA Container Toolkit, optimized containers, RAPIDS, CUDA-X HPC, and assets distributed through the NGC Private Registry.

The passage also introduces neural-network pruning as a way to reduce computation, memory use, energy consumption, and model size. Unstructured fine-grained sparsity can create irregular workloads, while coarse-grained sparsity removes entire subnetworks but may sacrifice more accuracy. A100 supports fine-grained structured sparsity, including 2:4 patterns, which maintains balanced workloads and is reported to cause virtually no accuracy loss in evaluated networks.

The speaker reflects on winning the Stanley Cup in Denver, the first championship for a local and regional team, and credits the team’s focus, hard work, coaching, ownership, management, and scouting. He describes learning from Patrick Roy, whom he calls the best goalie of all time, and says Ray Bourque deserved the championship as one of hockey’s greatest defensemen. He praises the organization’s players, including Joe Sakic, Bourque, Rob Blake, Chris Drury, Milan Hejduk, and Skoula. The Vintage Optical Shop is a leading online retailer of authentic vintage eyeglasses, sunglasses, and related accessories dating from the 1850s to the 1980s. New email subscribers receive a one-time $20 coupon and updates on new arrivals, sales, and specials. Subscribing requires entering an email address and clicking “Subscribe.” The store offers affordable, unused, handcrafted frames for props, prescription use, or sunglasses, with more information available through its website, FAQ, and contact form.

President Trump accused large homebuilders of “sitting on” two million empty lots, comparing them to OPEC and urging greater development to restore the American Dream. Libertarian economist Bryan Cappan disputed the conspiracy claim, arguing that homebuilders face shortages of buildable land because of restrictive zoning, discretionary approvals, and overlapping agencies—not greed or limited financing. NAHB data showed 64% of single-family builders considered lot supply low, constraining construction and prices. Cappan said Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac cannot compel local governments to approve projects, and that meaningful expansion requires zoning reforms that permit denser housing in high-demand markets. He said Trump’s attention to the shortage could have symbolic value, but little would change unless leaders addressed regulation.

This preprint evaluated whether transcriptome-wide splicing-outlier patterns can guide rare-disease diagnosis without prior knowledge of the causal gene. Whole-blood RNA sequencing was performed for 422 UDN and GREGoR participants, with 390 retained after filtering: 217 affected individuals and 173 familial controls. Two FRASER versions identified significant splicing outliers, and outlier genes were enriched for OMIM disease genes and genes associated with developmental delay and intellectual disability. Forty participants (10.3%) exceeded two standard deviations on at least one outlier metric. Batch effects significantly influenced FRASER41 results, whereas no tested covariate was significantly associated with FRASER242 outlier counts or status.

The study then focused on intron-retention outliers in minor-intron-containing genes. Five individuals had extreme excess outliers affecting many such genes. Four carried rare, compound-heterozygous RNU4ATAC variants and had phenotypes consistent with RNU4atac-opathy; their transcriptomic patterns provided functional support for upgrading variant classifications. The fifth case lacked pathogenic RNU4ATAC or RNU12 variants but shared 92.2% of its affected genes with the RNU4ATAC cases and had overlapping clinical features. Targeted genomic analysis found rare, compound-heterozygous RNU6ATAC variants, identifying RNU6ATAC as a putative novel disease gene. These variants remained variants of uncertain significance because additional cases and functional studies are required to establish the gene–disease association.

FRASER42’s Jaccard-index metric also identified all five cases but had lower specificity, while the strength of the minor-spliceosome signature increased with cohort size. Overall, the results support a transcriptome-first, unbiased approach for diagnosing spliceopathies, interpreting variants, and discovering gene–disease relationships, while emphasizing the need for batch correction and standardized sample processing.

The author describes studying abroad for six months in Buenos Aires, initially fearing racism but finding the city welcoming. Police and strangers helped when the author became lost, while residents showed curiosity and appreciation without singling out the author by race. The author made Argentine friends and bonded with others of African descent. The experience changed the author’s outlook and encouraged African American students to travel and discover how appreciated they may feel abroad.

Emma Stone signed a reported $10 million, two-year deal to become Louis Vuitton’s face after the company pursued her for nearly a year. Ryan Gosling reportedly declined an endorsement. Stone also described the weightlifting and muscle-gaining regimen required for “Battle of the Sexes.”

Vijay Mallya, the former Kingfisher Airlines chief wanted in India over loan defaults totaling nearly Rs 9,000 crore, appeared at Westminster Magistrates’ Court for his extradition case. He denied all allegations, including that funds were diverted to Royal Challengers Bangalore, and said he had evidence to prove his case.

Chief Magistrate Emma Louise Arbuthnot extended Mallya’s bail until December 4 and warned him not to violate bail conditions. The next case-management hearing is scheduled for July 6, while December 4 was tentatively set as the final hearing date. Mallya was excused from the July hearing after his lawyers cited media congestion.

Britain’s Crown Prosecution Service is presenting the case for India, while Mallya’s defence is awaiting final evidence and expects a second extradition request related to the Enforcement Directorate’s case. Mallya was arrested by Scotland Yard on April 18 and released on conditional bail with a £650,000 bond and a requirement to surrender his passport. If extradition is approved, the UK home secretary must order his transfer within two months, though appeals are possible.

The passage defines AMD Generic Encapsulated Software Architecture (AGESA), a BIOS procedure library that helps AMD customers integrate AMD technology across multiple products. It covers terminology, version numbering, release-package contents, file headers, procedure naming conventions, build controls, platform option files, internal Doxygen documentation, and related AMD and industry specifications.

Host integration requires a wrapper around published, boot-time AGESA entry points. Interface structures are initialized with defaults, allowing required host parameters to be supplied and optional settings to be customized. Calls report status through return codes and an error log. AGESA supports binary-module integration through a signature-bearing image, module dispatcher, relocation support, host bridge, and call-out router, or source integration into the host build. Binary calls execute in 32-bit protected flat-address mode.

For UEFI, AGESA code is organized across SEC, PEI, DXE, and runtime phases. PEIM modules handle early processor and post-reset memory initialization, while the DXE driver performs late initialization and publishes AMD data tables. The interface also provides stack and Cache-as-RAM routines, structure allocation and release services, processor, memory, PCI, APIC, MMIO, and event-log utilities, and configurable platform, power-management, PCIe, and memory parameters. Core entry points including AmdInitReset, AmdInitEarly, and AmdInitPost coordinate reset, processor, cache, platform, power, and memory initialization.

Sprint and The Sprint Foundation will provide free devices and 3GB of monthly LTE data for up to four years to 180,000 low-income high school students in more than 1,300 schools across 32 states this school year. The five-year 1Million Project aims to connect one million students without home internet. Sprint estimates it will donate $2.16 billion over five years; 86% of pilot participants said the program improved their attitude toward learning and helped with homework.

BiondVax Pharmaceuticals announced a $2.83 million investment from Angels High Tech Investments, owned by Check Point co-founder and chairman Marius Nacht. Angels will receive 33.8 million ordinary shares, equivalent to 844,000 U.S.-listed ADS, and hold 19.99% of BiondVax’s issued capital.

The ED told the Delhi High Court that Nirav Modi is indirectly challenging the Rs 12,000 crore PNB fraud and money-laundering case through Firestar Diamonds’ premature, misconceived bid for an interim stay intended to hinder the investigation.

Mr. Sill reported that Korean officials sought foreign assistance as tensions between China and Japan worsened. He joined the British, Russian, and French representatives in requesting simultaneous troop withdrawals; Germany delayed joining pending instructions from its government. About 5,000 Japanese troops were encamped with batteries near Seoul, and reports indicated that China and Japan might soon fight in Korea. Admiral Skerrett delayed his departure for Japan, which Sill considered necessary to protect 80 Americans from possible mob violence.

Korea’s Foreign Office stated that China had been invited to suppress a rebellion, while Japan had entered uninvited and over Korean protests. China was willing to withdraw if Japan did so, but Japan demanded prior Chinese withdrawal and rejected simultaneous withdrawal. Korean officials asked foreign representatives to use their good offices to resolve the crisis.

The American, Russian, French, and British representatives submitted the withdrawal proposal to their governments, warning that continued foreign troop presence could endanger their nationals and create wider complications. Mr. Denby likewise reported growing concern over the dispute, which had become more significant than the original Korean insurrection.

The speaker says playoff intensity and noise are expected and that nothing has changed recently. He praises Marty’s outstanding play, including two shutouts, and denies any publicity competition. He emphasizes that winning is a job requiring focus; his team has won only two games and needs four, so he remains cautious. Veteran leadership and Lou’s handling of the team have created discipline and fewer distractions, but every game requires finding ways to win. The speaker notes that opponents received fortunate playoff breaks while his team did not and declines to fault their goaltender for a possible puck-handling error because that team won. He also says Joe Nieuwendyk’s absence has hurt an already weak faceoff situation. Errors, particularly a mistake on the final goal, caused their latest loss and cannot be repeated.

On November 1, 2001, Enron said the SEC had elevated its inquiry into partnerships involving former CFO Andrew Fastow into a formal investigation. Enron maintained that the inquiry was limited to the partnerships and said it was cooperating, but analysts warned that the SEC’s subpoena powers could expand the investigation into Enron’s core gas and trading operations. Enron formed a special committee and retained former SEC enforcement chief William McLucas. The SEC said its new enforcement chief had complied with ethics rules and recused himself from matters involving McLucas’s law firm, despite questions about the appearance of a conflict.

Enron shares closed at $11.99, down $1.91, or about 14%, marking their 11th decline in 12 sessions. They had fallen roughly 65% since October 16, when Enron disclosed a $1.2 billion writedown tied to partnerships with Fastow. Merrill Lynch lowered its Enron rating to “neutral,” citing uncertainty surrounding the investigation.

Standard & Poor’s cut Enron’s long-term rating to BBB from BBB-plus and its short-term rating to A-3 from A-2, warning that further downgrades were possible. Moody’s had lowered the long-term rating to Baa2 and placed the commercial-paper rating under review. S&P said Enron had adequate liquidity for current uncertainties but diminished financial flexibility because investors doubted the strength of its core business.

Enron obtained $1 billion in secured credit lines from J.P. Morgan Chase and Salomon Smith Barney, backed by its Northern Natural Gas and Transwestern Pipeline assets. The company planned to use the financing to supplement liquidity, refinance obligations and repay debt. Analysts viewed the financing as both a liquidity boost and a sign of Enron’s financial distress.

Major North American power and gas trading partners continued doing business with Enron, although some increased collateral requirements, reduced exposure or subjected long-term trades to additional review. EnronOnline remained active, recording 7,100 transactions on November 1 compared with a roughly 5,600 daily average. Analysts said its liquidity, broad product offering, technology and tight bid-offer spreads were likely to outweigh Enron’s credit concerns for the time being, though competing exchanges could gain a small amount of business.

IntercontinentalExchange reported October wholesale power volume down 9% from September while natural gas volume rose 10%, but said it had seen no significant recent trading shift. NYMEX natural-gas prices also fell as profit-taking, abundant inventories, mild weather and concerns about economic demand limited gains; U.S. gas inventories were about 14% above the prior year.

Morgan Securities LLC and Merrill Lynch, Pierce, Fenner & Smith Incorporated for the issuance and sale of $750 million of 2.250% notes due 2021, $1.25 billion of 3.250% notes due 2026 and $1.50 billion of 4.650% notes due 2046. Milford are odds-on favourites against St. Naul’s in the 2017 Intermediate Championship final, a year after losing the same stage. Milford have improved for several years, compete in Division One and aim to retain their top-flight status and earn senior-championship football. They reached the final by defeating Cloughaneely and Aodh Ruadh, aided by the return of Cathal McGettigan and Gary Merritt. Captain Stephen Griffin has returned from a serious knee injury, while Peadar Mogan and Stuart Johnston centralise their running game. Milford’s strength, tactical adaptability and squad depth are expected to prevail.

The brief argues that public higher education funding continues to perpetuate historical discrimination and exclusion. State allocations remain highly inequitable: Ole Miss receives twice the per-student state funding of Jackson State, while UConn’s funding advantage over Southern Connecticut State University grew from more than $11,000 per student in 2007 to nearly $20,000 in 2022. Flagship universities receive almost 40 percent more per student than other four-year institutions while often serving fewer students from marginalized groups.

Most states use “base-plus” funding formulas based largely on prior appropriations, enrollment, inflation, or institutional requests. Although these methods stabilize budgets, they do not account for differing institutional and student needs, allowing historical inequities to persist and compound. This disparity especially harms open-access institutions, which educate most Black, Hispanic, and Native American students and two-thirds of university students eligible for Pell Grants, yet have fewer resources for tuition support and educational services.

The brief distinguishes equity from adequacy. Equity requires funding distribution to reflect varying needs; adequacy means having sufficient resources to fulfill institutional missions. Increasing total funding without changing distribution deepens inequities. Free college may reduce student costs but cannot ensure that underfunded institutions provide adequate instruction and support. Similarly, outcomes-based funding favors institutions already capable of investing in reforms and penalizes those serving students with greater needs.

Drawing on K–12 funding practices, the brief recommends allocating education funding according to institutional and student need, including higher weights for populations requiring more support. State funding should also account for differences in tuition, endowments, and alumni donations, while research, health care, agriculture, and other functions should receive separate allocations. An equitable funding formula should precede additional investment to ensure adequacy. Ultimately, systemic reform guided by equity is necessary rather than temporary additions to the existing system.

The article argues that mainstream climate education, often organized through education for sustainable development and the UN Sustainable Development Goals, emphasizes scientific knowledge and technological “green” solutions while neglecting the historical links among colonialism, capitalism, extractivism, and the climate crisis. Western-centric approaches can reproduce colonial patterns through mineral extraction, land acquisition, displacement, and unequal distribution of harm. Communities in the Global South contribute relatively little to greenhouse-gas emissions yet often experience the most severe consequences. The article characterizes these continuing structures as climate coloniality and links them to climate apartheid, epistemic injustice, and the marginalization of affected communities in climate governance.

Using Said’s contrapuntal reading, the article analyzes dominant and marginalized narratives, asking whose knowledge and voices are amplified or silenced and how colonial legacies shape education. It proposes decolonial educational ecologies as an alternative that goes beyond including Black and Indigenous perspectives. This approach reimagines education around historically marginalized knowledge systems and cosmologies, pluriversal thinking, reparative projects, distributive justice, restitution, critical inquiry, and relationships with more-than-human worlds. It calls for contextual, locally grounded approaches rather than universalized Western models of development and resilience.

The article also rejects climate solutionism and quick technological fixes as insufficient responses to systemic problems. Instead, it promotes critical climate education that confronts colonialism, capitalism, anthropocentrism, scientific racism, extractive modernization, and the unequal distribution of responsibility. Although implementation faces educational, psychological, institutional, and systemic barriers, the proposed framework seeks alternative knowledge production, narratives, and futures grounded in place and Black and Indigenous practices without reproducing colonial hierarchies.

The passage argues that human brains do not work like computers and do not store words, images, rules, information, or memories as symbolic representations. Computers encode and process data under stored algorithms, whereas humans begin life with senses, reflexes, and learning mechanisms that change through experience. Learning alters the brain in ways that enable future behavior without storing a song, poem, or image for later retrieval.

Using a drawing exercise, the author illustrates that people cannot accurately reproduce a familiar object from memory despite repeated exposure. Neural studies also show that even ordinary memory tasks involve many brain regions, undermining the idea that specific memories reside in individual neurons or memory registers. The author instead describes learning as orderly change resulting from observation, stimulus pairing, reward, and punishment.

Historically, explanations of intelligence have shifted from spirits and fluids to machines, telegraphs, and computers. Since the 1940s, the information-processing metaphor has dominated psychology, linguistics, neuroscience, and cognitive science, but the author considers it an unjustified metaphor based on faulty logic. He argues that intelligent behavior can instead be understood through an anti-representational, embodied approach. For example, a baseball player may catch a fly ball simply by maintaining its visual relationship to home plate and surrounding scenery, without calculating an internal trajectory model.

This view emphasizes the uniqueness of each brain: identical experiences produce different neural changes because people have distinct neural structures and life histories. A snapshot of one brain cannot capture the history and bodily context needed to reproduce its functioning, making simulated or downloaded human minds impossible under the author’s account. It also makes understanding intelligence exceptionally difficult, potentially requiring knowledge of billions of neurons and their molecular and activity dynamics. The author criticizes major brain-research projects based on computer-model promises, including the Human Brain Project, and concludes that neuroscience should abandon the information-processing metaphor and study human behavior without it.

Mike Franceses will return to WFAN next month to host a weekday afternoon show from 3–6:30 p.m. after accepting a significant pay cut from his previous salary of about $3 million. The deal was arranged above WFAN vice president Mark Chernoff, who opposed it, and came together quickly. Franceses rejected a SiriusXM arrangement involving Chris “Mad Dog” Russo and said few options matched his desired compensation and status.

Chris Carlin, Maggie Gray and Bart Scott will move to the 1–3 p.m. slot, while Evan Roberts and Joe Benigno will continue from 10 a.m.–1 p.m. Franceses may have returned even though the CMB Show lost its ratings battle to ESPN New York’s Michael Kay Show by two-tenths of a point.

Franceses said opposition at WFAN prompted his decision to return. Russo and Carlin disputed whether Carlin sent a disparaging text after a “High Heat” appearance; Carlin did not confirm sending it. Colleagues reacted critically, while Sid Rosenberg said Franceses wanted to work and earn money rather than remain home with his family. WFAN expected to save money because Carlin, Gray and Scott were believed to earn a combined total no higher than one-third of Franceses’s former salary.

Revolution Lighting Technologies (NASDAQ: RVLT) announced it will release first-quarter 2017 financial results for the period ended March 31 before market open on May 2, 2017. A perovskite polariton laser diode was demonstrated using a solution-grown CsPbBr₃ microplate integrated into an optical microcavity with single-walled carbon nanotube electrodes. A two-stage cooling protocol—first to 280 K, then to 8 K under constant current—redistributed and spatially froze mobile ions to form a rectifying p-i-n structure, enabling efficient carrier tunneling and continuous electrical injection.

At 8 K, strong coupling was confirmed between the perovskite exciton and polarization-split cavity modes. Electroluminescence intensity rose sharply above a threshold of 60 µA at 3.95 V, corresponding to approximately 2.8 kA cm⁻², while linewidth narrowing and energy blueshifts indicated polariton lasing. The threshold carrier density was approximately 4.2 × 10¹⁶ cm⁻³, well below the Mott density. Blueshifts above threshold were attributed to Joule heating, while self-heating and impact ionization suppressed emission at higher currents. The results establish a strategy for solution-processed semiconductor lasers operating under continuous direct electrical pumping.

The passage describes a divisional patent application for surgical instruments and methods that measure torque, energy, power, force, and penetration depth in real time while a working tool cuts tissue or drives an implant. Torque signals are processed by a controller into torque, energy, power, or accumulated energy, which can be used to estimate regional material strength, identify osteoporotic bone, and correlate drilling or screw-insertion energy with screw pullout strength.

The instrument may include a drill bit, saw, burr, reamer, driver, or self-drilling implant; rotational and axial motors; a guide harp and distal guide for controlling tool extension and depth; torque and axial-force sensors; and an encoder or other transducer for measuring penetration. An onboard or external wired or wireless graphical interface can display torque, force, power, accumulated energy, depth, and alerts. Changes in power or torque across the x, y, and z axes can indicate dense cortex, skiving, or impending penetration, allowing the operator to redirect or stop the tool without routine fluoroscopy. A drop in power can signal inadvertent plunge and trigger stopping of penetration.

The background identifies conventional depth gauges as potentially inaccurate or prone to breaking, while implant sizing and bone-strength assessment may require trial-and-error, repeat radiographs, or tests that do not cover the operative site. The described systems seek to improve depth measurement, implant selection, material-strength assessment, and prevention of injury.

The study analyzes 34,363,623 journal articles and conference papers published from 1900 to 2020 in the Microsoft Academic Graph to determine whether papers that create conceptual knowledge gaps have greater generative capacity than other recombinations. Scientific concepts are represented as level-3 research fields in dynamic, domain-specific networks, with edges marking a paper’s first co-occurrence of two concepts. Using persistent homology, the authors identify “birth pairs” whose new connections create topological holes or gaps and classify papers as gap openers, non-gap openers with novel pairs, or non-gap openers without novel pairs.

Gap openers constitute 0.84% of papers—twice the proportion in randomized networks—and their frequency varies substantially by discipline, being especially low in medicine, biology, and chemistry and higher in geography, history, philosophy, and art. Their proportion rose from 1900 to 1930 before declining through 2020. Compared with other novel recombinations, gap openers link newer and less-established concepts, gain greater popularity in subsequent research, cite fewer earlier works, exhibit higher recombination novelty, and more frequently use verbs associated with creation and innovation rather than demonstration, improvement, or application.

Regression analyses controlling for team size, references, year, and discipline show that gap openers are significantly more likely to be among the most highly cited papers and more disruptive. They have 1.58 times the odds of being in the top 1% most cited and score 1.4 percentage points higher on the disruption percentile. They receive 6.11% fewer citations within five years but 31.39% more within 20 years, with the relative advantage reversing at approximately eight years. They also show a stronger delayed-recognition effect. The smaller number of Nobel Prize-winning papers associated with gap opening provides only suggestive, statistically nonsignificant evidence of greater exceptional recognition. Novel combinations that do not create gaps show no advantage over baseline papers in reaching the top 1% of citations and are less likely to rank among the top 5%–20%.

Gap-opening papers also emerge from teams that are significantly smaller, younger, fresher, and more geographically localized than teams producing the other paper types. Overall, the findings indicate that topological significance, rather than novelty alone, distinguishes the most influential conceptual recombinations. Because gap openers may receive delayed recognition, short-term citation-based evaluations may undervalue highly generative research.

The passage examines LLMs’ potential and limitations in computational social science. They offer scalable, low-cost synthetic data and can simulate certain demographic groups’ preferences, while memory mechanisms and interview data may improve authenticity; however, fidelity, bias, stereotyping, and cost remain concerns. Zero-shot capabilities and in-context learning support tasks such as stance detection, sentiment analysis, and response coding, but also enable hyper-realistic misinformation. Alignment, watermarking, multidisciplinary expertise, and societal engagement are identified as safeguards. LLMs may help generate hypotheses or theories, but concerns about originality and validity favor their use as complements to human researchers.

Generative AI’s rapid growth creates regulatory challenges involving misinformation, malicious deepfakes, discrimination, and the balance between innovation and risk mitigation. The passage distinguishes biological sex, based on anatomy, physiology, and developmental pathways, from gender identity, which remains poorly understood. The passage examines container patterns and distributed-system architectures, largely through Kubernetes examples. Ambassador containers isolate concerns by having applications connect to localhost while a proxy routes requests to storage shards, discovers environment-specific services, or splits traffic between production and experimental implementations. Examples use Redis and Memcached with twemproxy, and nginx for weighted 10% experiments with IP hashing.

Adapter containers standardize interfaces for heterogeneous applications without modifying their original images. Uses include exposing Redis metrics through a Prometheus exporter, normalizing logs with Fluentd, and running rich MySQL health checks. This modularity enables reuse, independent updates, and isolation of resource usage.

Microservices divide applications into independently developed, deployed, and scaled components linked through APIs. This supports team autonomy and service-specific scaling but complicates debugging, architecture, and failure diagnosis. Distributed patterns provide reusable approaches to these challenges.

Replicated stateless services use interchangeable replicas behind a load balancer, readiness probes, and preferably at least two replicas for high availability. Session tracking can use IP hashing, cookies, or consistent hashing. Caching tiers such as Varnish increase throughput and reduce latency, while nginx can provide SSL termination; rate limiting, cache-failure impact, and session affinity require careful testing and configuration.

Sharded services divide state among shards when data is too large for one machine. Sharded caching uses memory more efficiently than replicated caching but makes shard failures especially disruptive. Each shard can itself be replicated and autoscaled to address uneven “hot shard” traffic. Sharding functions should be deterministic and uniform, commonly using `hash(key) % shards`; keys should include only request properties that affect the response. Consistent hashing minimizes key redistribution when shard counts change. Ambassadors and shared routing services offer different trade-offs between local simplicity, scaling, and network overhead.

Scatter/gather systems distribute each request to multiple leaves and combine partial results, parallelizing computation such as document searches. Sharding leaves allows datasets larger than one machine, and replicating leaves improves fault tolerance and upgrade safety. However, coordination overhead and slow “straggler” leaves mean additional parallelism eventually reduces latency and availability gains.

The passage then introduces function-as-a-service and event-driven computing. FaaS simplifies deployment, automatic scaling, and failure recovery while encouraging stateless modularity, but forces network communication and external state storage, complicates debugging, and is poorly suited to long-running background processing, large in-memory datasets, and sustained high request volumes under per-request pricing. It concludes by introducing the decorator pattern for transforming HTTP requests or responses.

Laboratory characterization of 25 production-design Simons Observatory ultra-high-frequency detector modules tested more than 36,000 transition-edge sensor bolometers for the 220 and 280 GHz bands. The modules use microwave SQUID multiplexing and common optical, detector, and readout designs. Average TES yield was 83%, with all modules meeting the 70% baseline target and 20 meeting the 80% goal. Median critical temperature was 163 mK, normal resistance 7.7 mΩ, saturation power 24 and 26 pW, dark noise-equivalent power 39 and 42 aW/√Hz, effective time constants 0.42 and 0.40 ms, and optical efficiencies 0.62 and 0.63 at 220 and 280 GHz, respectively. About 89% of detectors met noise requirements, while 89% and 81% exceeded an optical efficiency of 0.5 in the respective bands. Expected photon noise exceeded the intrinsic detector-noise distributions, indicating potential background-limited performance. Frequency conflicts and SQUID-response screening reduced the usable resonator-channel yield from 98% to 86%; readout noise peaked at 35 pA/√Hz. Twenty-three modules met saturation-power requirements; Uv55 was rejected for low saturation power, Uv44 for excessive saturation power, and Uv63 for anomalously low optical efficiency. The best 19 modules were selected for deployment: 13 are installed in the LAT and UHF SAT, while six are planned for the LAT upgrade. All SO instruments have achieved first light, with on-sky UHF and MF characterization deferred to forthcoming commissioning papers.
