The lecture concludes the course’s dynamic-graphs and lower-bounds material by proving an Ω(log n) cell-probe lower bound for dynamic connectivity with edge insertions, deletions, and connectivity queries. The bound holds even when every connected component is a path and also applies in stronger amortized and randomized settings, implying corresponding RAM and pointer-machine bounds and matching known link/cut-tree results for dynamic trees.

The proof reduces connectivity to a √n-by-√n grid whose adjacent columns are connected by perfect matchings, represented as permutations. Bulk operations replace these permutations and verify compositions of prefixes. A bit-reversal access sequence is arranged into a balanced binary tree over time; because left-subtree updates affect right-subtree queries, many queries must read cells written in the corresponding left subtree. Lowest-common-ancestor charging avoids double-counting, and summing over tree levels yields Ω(√n log n) work per bulk operation, or Ω(log n) per elementary operation.

An information-theoretic encoding shows that random update permutations require Ω(l√n log n) bits. A simpler prefix-composition problem encodes cells read in the right subtree and written in the left. For verification queries, whose arguments are unknown, the decoder tests all candidate permutations. Succinct separator families based on perfect hash functions distinguish cells written only in the left subtree from those read only in the right. The resulting encoding either establishes enough direct work or forces Ω(l√n) cross-subtree reads, completing the lower-bound argument.

After a second trial, Vernon Clausing was convicted of three counts of unlawful delivery of legend drugs, one count of possession with intent to deliver, and one count of possession of a controlled substance; the jury had acquitted him of conspiracy. The court affirmed his convictions, rejecting his challenges to the jury instructions, charging document, admission of pharmacy-board testimony, and alleged prosecutorial misconduct.

Clausing had lost his osteopathic medical license after being found to have negligently prescribed Soma and Nubain for nontherapeutic purposes. He continued operating his clinic and dispensary, using other doctors’ prescription numbers to obtain the drugs. A former patient acting as a police informant obtained Soma and Nubain from him on several occasions. A later search of his home and clinic found bulk quantities of both drugs and Vicodin.

The court held that Washington law requires legend drugs to be lawfully dispensed by a licensed practitioner pursuant to a valid order or prescription, or delivered by a practitioner acting within the scope of the practitioner’s license. Thus, instructions 17 and 25 accurately stated the law, and Clausing could not prepare prescriptions for delivery after his license was revoked. The charging document was sufficient, and Clausing suffered no prejudice from its wording, particularly because he presented no evidence of a valid prescription for the informant. Instructions concerning legitimate prescriptions and labeling requirements did not lower the State’s burden of proof. The instruction defining “dispense” was also necessary and properly stated that refills required prior prescriber authorization.

The court further held that the pharmacy-board director’s opinion about prescriptions written before a doctor’s license was revoked was properly limited and, if error, harmless because Clausing offered no prescriptions or records supporting his claim. Finally, the prosecutor’s closing remarks did not constitute misconduct.

PayPal grew from a person-to-person online payment service founded in 1998 into a global digital payments platform serving consumers and merchants. Under CEO Dan Schulman, who joined in 2014, the company adopted a mission to democratize financial services and embraced multistakeholder capitalism, emphasizing employees alongside customers, regulators, shareholders, and communities. Its strategy included allowing card payments, acquiring Xoom, Zettle, and Honey, introducing new services such as the SuperApp, and expanding lending and financial-health offerings.

PayPal’s financial-wellness concerns arose after research found widespread insecurity among lower-paid employees. Half of customer-service employees had only 4%–6% of each paycheck remaining after basic expenses, and nearly two-thirds of survey respondents ran out of or nearly ran out of money between paychecks despite high engagement. A 2019 initiative therefore targeted hourly and entry-level employees with wage increases where appropriate, a 60% reduction in U.S. healthcare premiums plus reimbursement accounts, equity grants, and financial coaching. PayPal invested tens of millions of dollars and also provided pandemic-related equipment, stipends, and crisis leave without layoffs.

By 2021, survey results showed improved financial wellness, stronger retention intentions, and better engagement and productivity. Customer-service turnover fell from 19.4% in 2019 to 7.3% in 2020, while PayPal reported 426 million active accounts and approximately 25% non-GAAP operating margins. PayPal also began encouraging other employers to assess worker financial wellness; 11 companies had joined the coalition by the end of 2021.

Deep brain stimulation of the thalamic ventral intermediate nucleus is an effective tremor treatment, but its mechanism remains unclear and current systems are open-loop. This study evaluated thalamic local field potentials (LFPs) as internal biomarkers for closed-loop DBS.

Intraoperative LFPs and hand acceleration were recorded in 34 patients with essential tremor, multiple sclerosis, or Parkinson’s disease undergoing thalamic DBS implantation or pulse-generator replacement. Patients withheld anti-tremor medication for at least 12 hours. Leads were externalized, stimulation amplitudes were clinically selected, and LFPs were recorded near the stimulation contact. In 16 participants, DBS frequencies of 2, 5, 10, 50, and 130 Hz were each applied for 60 seconds. Electrode locations were reconstructed from pre- and postoperative imaging and mapped to a standardized atlas.

LFP artifacts were removed, signals were filtered and analyzed from 1–30 Hz, and tremor power was calculated from accelerometry. Analyses included spectral power, magnitude-squared coherence, regression, classification, ROC/AUC, and repeated-measures ANOVA. Tremor showed a moderate correlation with alpha- and theta-band LFP power and a strong correlation with peak LFP–acceleration coherence. Postural tremor was decoded from LFPs with an AUC of approximately 0.7. DBS at approximately 130 Hz reduced low-frequency LFP power, and decoding remained possible during stimulation.

A computational model represented 5,000 multicompartment thalamocortical relay neurons across VIM, VOP, and VC, with cortical and cerebellar excitation, reticular and interneuron inhibition, and burst, regular, or random firing. Modeled LFP power varied with electrode location, tremor-cell distribution, and the proportion of burst cells, potentially explaining variability across participants.

IDC’s December 2021 telephone survey of 200 technology decision-makers at industrial enterprises with more than 500 employees in Germany, Austria, and Switzerland found growing demand for high-performance computing (HPC). While only 8% currently report high demand, nearly half are expected to within two years; half say calculations take too long, and 42% report that their simulations are already outdated or inaccurate. Four out of five decision-makers view HPC as a game changer for product and process innovation, rising to 96% among enterprises already using it.

HPC enables complex simulations, modeling, and analysis; accelerates calculations and iterations; unlocks new industrial use cases; and supports faster innovation and more agile development, planning, and production. More than one-quarter of surveyed enterprises already use professional HPC infrastructure, while 39% are planning or piloting it.

Deployment options include public clouds, external infrastructure, colocation, on-premises systems, and partnerships with research institutions. Among current HPC users, 87% prefer or plan to use external infrastructure, 74% operate or plan to operate their own systems in colocation datacenters, and only 6% currently use on-premises infrastructure. External services offer scalability, flexibility, modern technology, and a shift from upfront capital expenditure to operating expenditure, but require skilled personnel and raise concerns over security, energy consumption, expertise, availability, licensing, and maintenance.

IDC expects public and hybrid-cloud HPC to become especially important and recommends that enterprises choose an operating model based on utilization, budget, performance, flexibility, security, and internal skills. It advises establishing a holistic data strategy and single source of truth, selecting scalable, secure, energy-efficient solutions, and using external expertise when necessary. With HPC combined with simulations, modeling, and data analytics, manufacturers can accelerate digital product and process development and create new digital products, services, and business models.

The paper studies ordinal-preference matching markets: house allocation, marriage, and roommates. It distinguishes strict from tied preferences and unweighted from weighted agents. A matching is popular if it is at least as popular as every alternative, where popularity compares the total weight of agents who strictly prefer one matching over another. This notion lies between Pareto stability, which requires unanimity to block a matching, and core stability, which requires only a blocking pair.

Because a single popular matching may not exist, the paper introduces the popular dimension: the minimum size of a collection of matchings that is at least as popular as every alternative matching. It also relates this measure to the Condorcet dimension, noting that popular winning sets satisfy the Condorcet condition but are stronger.

The main results are:

- House allocation: The popular dimension is exactly 2 for all four cases—unweighted or weighted agents, with strict preferences or ties. A polynomial-time algorithm constructs a popular winning set of two matchings by decomposing a specially constructed top-choice (1,2)-matching.
- Marriage: With unweighted agents and strict preferences, the popular dimension is 1 because a stable matching always exists and is popular. With weights or ties, the dimension is at least 2 and at most 3; the paper conjectures it is exactly 2.
- Roommates: Even with unweighted agents and strict preferences, the popular dimension is 2. A polynomial-time greedy algorithm produces two matchings forming a popular winning set. For weighted agents or ties, the dimension is between 2 and 3.

The upper bound of 3 for general marriage and roommates instances is obtained through an auxiliary house-allocation construction and a polynomial-time three-edge-coloring procedure. Closing the remaining gap between 2 and 3 remains open.

This literature review examines how climate-induced displacement affects K–12 learners’ access to, quality of, and continuity in education across lower- and middle-income countries before and after relocation. Rapid-onset disasters destroy schools and transport infrastructure, while slow-onset hazards such as drought and salinization reduce household incomes and food security, increase school withdrawal, and disrupt learning through economic hardship, malnutrition, trauma, and health risks. Although school-attendance patterns vary during disasters, academic performance generally does not improve.

Relocation adds financial, administrative, and social barriers, including school costs, complex enrollment and documentation requirements, discrimination, cultural exclusion, inadequate support systems, weak data collection, and limited access to effective distance learning. Displaced girls face compounded challenges involving domestic work, water collection, safety concerns, early marriage, preferential investment in boys’ education, and psychological burdens associated with parental migration.

The study combines a Human Rights-Based Approach to education with Education in Emergencies research to examine access, quality, dignity, equity, and non-discrimination across immediate, indirect, and chronic effects. It reviewed more than 100 academic and grey-literature documents, selecting 73 relevant English-language sources focused on lower- and middle-income countries.

Recommendations include sustainable, locally tailored financial assistance, streamlined registration and digital identification, robust data and outcome monitoring, academic and mental-health support, safe and inclusive learning environments, and gender-responsive policies that challenge unequal norms. The study identifies gaps in research on climate displacement within Education in Emergencies, long-term educational and intergenerational effects, and reactive policy responses. It advocates proactive, climate-specific education frameworks integrated with broader adaptation strategies and recognizes education as both a right and a component of climate resilience.

President Muhammadu Buhari said power generation and delivery had improved nationwide, but Daura remained in a 10-day blackout after a windstorm felled a 132kVA tower and 16 KEDCO poles. Repairs were underway, with power expected within 48 hours, while infrastructure damage has caused prolonged outages in Lagos and Ondo.

Two all-optical thermometry methods were developed using fluorescent microdiamonds containing silicon-vacancy centers. The models combine up to nine temperature-dependent features from SiV photoluminescence and the diamond host’s Raman signal, including signal intensity, peak position, and full width at half maximum. Standard multi-feature regression (MFR) uses a weighted linear combination with exhaustive feature selection, while two-stage multi-feature regression (2SMFR) combines partial least squares, lasso regression, and spline-based residual correction with implicit feature selection.

Eight approximately 1-µm diamonds were measured from 25 to 85 °C in 10 °C increments. Models were calibrated on subsets of diamonds and evaluated on unseen diamonds. MFR selected SiV zero-phonon-line wavelength, SiV linewidth, and Raman linewidth, achieving 1.7 K accuracy and 1.2 K·Hz⁻¹ᐟ² resolution with only three to four calibration diamonds and temperature points. This improved accuracy by about 26% over single-feature models with comparable resolution.

With seven diamonds and seven temperature points, 2SMFR reached 0.7 K accuracy and 0.6 K·Hz⁻¹ᐟ² resolution, improving accuracy by about 59% over MFR and 70% over the best single-feature model, while improving resolution by roughly 50%. Its sensitivity of 0.04 K⁻¹ was approximately seven times that of the best single-feature model. Performance generally improved with additional calibration data, although MFR gains diminished beyond three diamonds or temperature points. The reported metrics were calculated on independent test data, and predictions outside the 25–85 °C training range were cautioned against because linear relationships and extrapolation may be unreliable.

Dabhol Power Company’s board authorized management in London to issue a preliminary termination notice for its power purchase agreement with the Maharashtra State Electricity Board, voting 6–1; IDBI opposed, while MSEB representatives did not vote as an interested party. The authorization was not an immediate decision to close the project: lender consent was required, and a preliminary notice would trigger a six-month consultation period.

The dispute followed MSEB’s overdue payments and its ₹401 crore penalty against DPC for inadequate power supply. DPC had invoked guarantees and political force majeure, while conciliation and arbitration proceedings were underway. MSEB made a ₹134 crore “protest payment” toward a March bill of ₹146.64 crore, leaving ₹12.64 crore disputed.

International lenders favored ending DPC’s involvement and withholding further Phase II assistance, citing contractual defaults. Indian lenders, particularly IDBI and State Bank of India, opposed termination and sought renegotiation; further funding was tied to government payment assurances. Maharashtra and central governments also favored settlement and planned a joint renegotiation committee focused partly on DPC’s high power tariff. Reported government liabilities if the agreement was terminated varied, including one year’s power bill, a $300 million termination fee, and estimates up to ₹2,840 crore.

The court held that a widow’s statutory one-third interest in her deceased husband’s real estate was exempt from his debts and could be admeasured and set apart without first paying the estate’s liabilities. Her interest attached during marriage upon the husband’s seizin and the wife’s coverture, rather than becoming part of the estate at his death. Code §§ 2387 and 2391 permitted sales of the estate’s interest for debt payment but did not subject the widow’s share to creditors. Section 2441 merely barred giving her more than the statutory share, while § 2451 protected a homestead purchased with her share from her own debts. The order granting the widow her interest was affirmed.

Following the September 11 attacks on the World Trade Center and Pentagon, energy companies and utilities increased security at offices, pipelines, refineries, and power plants. The Nuclear Regulatory Commission ordered heightened security for 104 reactors, while major oil companies reported normal operations and continued fuel deliveries. Kinder Morgan closed a New York Harbor storage facility.

Energy and bandwidth trading largely halted as the New York Mercantile Exchange evacuated and stayed closed, EnronOnline stopped operating, and Enron, Dynegy, El Paso, Reliant, and other firms sent employees home or limited operations to essential staff. Houston offices, shopping centers, and other businesses closed or reopened with increased security. Natural-gas prices faced volatility from fear and short covering, while oil rose on concerns that Middle East conflict could disrupt supplies. Gasoline prices and panic buying increased; OPEC said it was prepared to boost production if prices continued rising.

Enron resumed North American natural-gas and electricity market-making through EnronOnline and telephone on September 12, initially until noon, while expressing confidence that domestic markets and infrastructure would remain stable. It also said markets outside North America would follow normal schedules.

In South Asia, foreign energy companies reviewed security, while Enron India said it had protected its projects, employees, and installations. Enron’s Dabhol Power Company faced financial constraints from a payment dispute with the Maharashtra State Electricity Board: the first 740-megawatt phase was idle, the 1,444-megawatt second phase was 97% complete, and lenders had about $1.4 billion in exposure. Separately, Maharashtra’s proposed tariff increase and four-hour load-shedding schedule drew opposition, with the Bharatiya Janata Party threatening statewide agitation and advocating purchases of Enron-generated power.

The quarterback is considered football’s most important offensive position because he touches the ball on every play, directs the offense, and often serves as the team’s on-field leader. At the NFL level, he communicates the coach’s play call, ensures proper formations, studies playbooks and opponents, and may call audibles. His primary duties are taking the snap, passing to open receivers, and occasionally running.

Effective quarterbacks require football intelligence, sound decision-making, accurate throwing, leadership, proper footwork, athleticism, and arm strength. Accuracy allows receivers to maintain momentum and avoid defenders, while preparation and confidence help quarterbacks perform against defenses that study them closely. The position has also evolved from its historical “quarter back” alignment behind the running back and fullback. Common nicknames include “Signal Caller,” “Field General,” and “Gunslinger.”

Although quarterbacks once were typically large, tall, and strong, smaller and more athletic quarterbacks are now common. The passage also identifies Otto Graham, Peyton Manning, Dan Marino, Joe Montana, and Tom Brady among the greatest quarterbacks, noting achievements that include Graham’s 10 consecutive championship-game appearances, Manning’s two Super Bowl titles, Montana’s four Super Bowl victories, and Brady’s record number of Super Bowl championships.

A self-driving Uber vehicle struck and killed 49-year-old Elaine Herzberg, who was walking outside a crosswalk in Tempe, Arizona. The Volvo was in self-driving mode with a human operator behind the wheel. Uber suspended all autonomous-vehicle road testing in the U.S. and Canada while authorities investigate. The first fatality involving a fully autonomous test vehicle could affect the technology’s development amid safety concerns and varying state regulations.

HDFC Mutual Fund will wind up HDFC FMP 378D March 2014 following unit-holder approval, as its net assets fell below ₹10 crore, making it unviable. Launched in March 2014, the scheme’s maturity was extended twice.

The court held that Josephine Slosson validly exercised her father’s power of appointment over the trust fund and effectively disposed of it by her will. Accordingly, her three surviving children could not take under their grandfather’s will because the condition requiring failure of their mother to exercise the power had not occurred. The beneficiaries’ interests were therefore subject to transfer tax. Because the children had not renounced their mother’s legacies, the court did not address the tax consequences of renunciation. Payment of the decedent’s debts from the trust fund was taxable. The court excluded $682.04 advanced by Alice Slosson to pay creditors from her taxable bequest because the decedent did not owe her those claims. The tax order was modified accordingly and affirmed in all other respects.

Thai Prime Minister Prayuth Chan-o-cha said Thailand has no trade with North Korea and has complied with U.N. resolutions. U.S. envoy Joseph Yun is expected in Bangkok to seek stronger pressure on North Korea’s weapons programs, following a reported 94% decline in bilateral trade.

Carol Christ, 73, became UC Berkeley’s first female and oldest chancellor. A former Berkeley professor and Smith College president, Christ said she hoped to give back to the campus she loves. She inherited challenges including free-speech conflict, sexual-assault controversies, low Black enrollment, rising housing costs, a shortage of on-campus housing, a $110 million budget deficit, and state scrutiny of $175 million in undisclosed UC funds. Christ designated 2017–18 a “free speech year,” planned cross-group discussions about sexual misconduct and diverse viewpoints, and prioritized campus diversity and housing. She proposed increasing philanthropy, making administrative cuts, working with Berkeley and Oakland on housing and homelessness at People’s Park, and giving campuses a larger role in relations with state officials. Faculty expressed optimism about her tenure. Christ earned nearly $532,000 annually, planned to remain active on campus, and chose not to live in the chancellor’s house.

The article explains the rules and coaching practices for soccer penalty kicks. A penalty is awarded when a defender commits a foul inside their own penalty area that would otherwise result in a direct free kick. The stationary ball is placed on the 12-yard penalty mark; the goalkeeper must remain on the goal line until the kick, while all other players must stand behind the mark, outside the penalty area, and at least 10 yards away. The referee signals when the kick may be taken.

Coaches should teach these rules, identify and train a primary penalty kick taker and an alternate, and establish the kicking order before a game. Selection should reflect ability, confidence, and success rate. Kicker choices should not be made spontaneously, and players who are injured, distressed, or uncomfortable should be allowed to defer without criticism.

Kickers need a consistent, practiced routine covering ball placement, relaxation, approach, and the strike. The ball should be placed by hand, the kicker should wait for the whistle, and the run-up, plant-foot position, body position, and strike should form one continuous motion. Feinting is permitted during the run-up but not after it is completed. Accuracy is emphasized over power, and the lower corners are generally recommended because they are difficult to stop without reducing accuracy. Inside-of-the-foot, instep-drive, and instep-face kicks are described, with the choice determined by the individual kicker’s comfort.

Mental preparation includes blocking out distractions, using controlled breathing and visualization, and avoiding visual or physical “tells.” Coaches should encourage experimentation, regular repetition, practice on the team’s actual playing surfaces, realistic simulation of distractions and fatigue, and feedback from coaches and goalkeepers. Advanced kickers may scout opponents, record goalkeeper tendencies, and maintain at least two possible kicks. Legal tactics include using a different player to retrieve the ball, modifying the approach, and the rare two-player “tap” kick.

The passage explains U.S. options expiration: contracts expire on the third Saturday of the expiration month at 11:59 a.m. EST, while trading usually ends on the preceding Friday, or Thursday if Friday is a holiday. Expiration week is associated with higher trading volumes, returns, and volatility for large-cap stocks with actively traded options. When stock, stock-index futures, and stock-index options expire together, it is called quad witching, occurring in March, June, September, and December.

It recommends researching trading models, backtesting them over at least 15 years or across bull and bear markets, and forward-testing the best model. Example expiration strategies include bear call credit spreads, bull call credit spreads, and gamma-neutral combinations, though the article focuses mainly on stocks, SPY, and XLV because of limited options data.

Reported backtests show average gains of 0.3% per expiration week for SPY, about 0.7% per trade for an undisclosed XLV strategy, 0.46% for an SPY overnight strategy, and 0.18% across 306 trades for an SPY expiration-day strategy. Expiration days, especially quad witching days, showed somewhat greater volatility than random trading days.

The UC1825B-SP is a high-frequency PWM controller with current- or voltage-mode operation, feed-forward, current limiting, shutdown, soft-start/duty-cycle clamping, latched logic, undervoltage lockout, and totem-pole outputs.

Chenai Mathabire, a 35-year-old Zimbabwean nurse and epidemiologist, received an International AIDS Society prize for research showing how a rapid tuberculosis test could be implemented in health centers in Malawi and Mozambique. After studying physiotherapy, occupational therapy or nursing, she became her family's first nurse and joined Doctors Without Borders in 2008, diagnosing malnourished children with HIV-related illness, supervising peer educators for HIV-positive pregnant women, and treating gunshot wounds in a South Sudan mobile hospital during a tribal war.

Beginning in 2015, Mathabire and a two-year team studied clinics in Malawi's Chiradzulu and Mozambique's Chamanculo districts. They found the urine-based test produced results in under an hour — versus two to four days, sometimes months, for standard cough tests or X-rays — and that staff could be trained in hours to administer and interpret it, with patients eager to use it. She recounted a man in his 30s who died after doctors failed to refer him for the test, which was then awaiting Ministry of Health and WHO approval. Findings published by MSF have led some clinics to adopt rapid testing.

Still with MSF and considering further HIV/TB research, Mathabire married an infectious disease specialist in Falun, Sweden, sewing her own beaded wedding dress. The article is by Sasha Ingber.

Detroit’s players said their opponent had played its best game yet but remained low on shots despite three power plays, allowing Detroit to protect a point after a late second-period goal. John LeClair said the team had improved in opening periods and still had time to respond. Reflecting on the unexpected playoff run, players credited a pre-deadline phone call, five Russian players, and a total team effort. They thanked Jimmy Devellano and Scotty Bowman for bringing them to Detroit. After four straight playoff wins, they described the team as improving and outplaying opponents regardless of size.

In his acceptance speech, the Democratic nominee thanks Governor Adlai Stevenson and other party figures, including running mate Lyndon Johnson, and pledges to restore Democratic victory and national greatness. He rejects the relevance of his religious affiliation, affirming that his public-policy decisions will be his own and that voters should not base their choices on religion.

He argues that Nixon and the Republican party offer only the status quo, while the nation needs dynamic Democratic leadership. Major domestic challenges include agricultural modernization, overcrowded schools and urban decay, racial discrimination, inadequate support for older citizens, automation, unemployment, and declining moral and intellectual standards. Internationally, the speech warns of communist expansion, new nations gaining power, and weapons capable of destroying humanity.

Calling for courage, innovation, and leadership, the nominee presents a “New Frontier” of unresolved challenges in science, space, peace, poverty, prejudice, and human rights. He argues that Americans must choose between public responsibility and private comfort, progress and stagnation, and national purpose or decline. He closes by urging support, sacrifice, and votes for the Democratic campaign.

An 11-year study of 33,908 Norwegian adults found that inactive participants were 44% more likely to experience depression than those exercising one to two hours weekly. Researchers estimated that 12% of depression cases could have been prevented with some exercise, supporting its potential inclusion in mental-health plans.

Irish soccer player Megan Connolly’s video of a frightening Myrtle Beach roller-coaster ride went viral. It showed teammate Dallas Dorosy laughing and featured Fray’s “How to Save a Life”; friends responded with concern and joking support.

Google added the $199 Moto G6, $740 LG G7 ThinQ and $899 LG V35 ThinQ to Project Fi, but its limited phone selection—especially excluding Apple and Samsung—remains a major obstacle. The low-key service offers low rates and automatic switching among major U.S. carriers and Wi-Fi, but faces competition from unlimited plans and has drawn little advertising or measurable growth.

Premier John Horgan rejected Liberal leader Andrew Wilkinson’s claim that taxes caused a nine-cent overnight gasoline price increase, attributing it instead to possible gouging, corporate profits and supply issues. Horgan favors increased domestic refining, while Wilkinson accused him of a “tax grab” and called for lower gas taxes.

The Texas Court of Civil Appeals affirmed a judgment denying appellants damages arising from a head-on collision on a three-lane highway. The jury found that Vernon Wilson, driving north, moved into the western lane and that this negligent lane change was the sole proximate cause of the collision. It also found that Wilson failed to maintain a proper lookout, although that failure did not cause the collision, and that King did not fail to keep proper control, turn right, or occupy the center lane.

Appellants challenged the jury charge and requested additional special issues, but the court held that they had waived those objections by failing to make timely exceptions or written requests. Appellants also complained of counsel’s argument urging the jury to award the $55,000 sought, but they had not objected at trial, and any harmful effect could have been cured by an instruction. Finding no reversible error, the court affirmed the judgment.

Apple Inc. filed a Form 8-K dated October 27, 2022, disclosing that it issued a press release on its financial results for the fourth fiscal quarter ended September 24, 2022, attached as Exhibit 99.1, with inline XBRL cover page data as Exhibit 104. The information is furnished rather than "filed" for Section 18 purposes. The report lists Apple common stock and eleven series of notes registered on Nasdaq. Signed by Luca Maestri, Senior Vice President and Chief Financial Officer.

The May 23, 2001 news compilation centered on the escalating dispute between Maharashtra, the Maharashtra State Electricity Board (MSEB), Enron and Enron-promoted Dabhol Power Company (DPC). Madhav Godbole resigned as chairman of the state-appointed panel renegotiating DPC’s power purchase agreement after NCP chief Sharad Pawar criticized government negotiators as having a negative approach. Chief Minister Vilasrao Deshmukh did not accept the resignation, asked Godbole to continue and sought his withdrawal. Pawar later said his comments were personal and not made for the Maharashtra government. The scheduled renegotiation meeting was canceled following Godbole’s resignation.

DPC had issued a preliminary termination notice after the dispute over unpaid electricity bills, giving the parties six months to resolve their differences. Enron warned it could seek $3.5 billion–$5 billion in damages, while Maharashtra considered serving its own termination notice if Enron did not cooperate. The central government adopted a wait-and-watch policy. Enron rejected the Godbole panel’s recommendations and called for a specific proposal involving MSEB, Maharashtra and the Centre.

The dispute centered partly on power tariffs: Maharashtra said the original agreement assumed Rs 2.20 per unit, while the state was paying Rs 8.54 and Deshmukh said buying all contracted power would cost Rs 5.20 per unit. Enron attributed the increase to rupee depreciation and higher global fuel prices. The state advocate general said MSEB’s Rs 401 crore rebate claim over shortfalls in DPC’s declared power availability was justified.

Indian lenders faced substantial potential losses if DPC’s loans became non-performing assets, contributing to declines in IDBI, SBI and ICICI shares. Indian power companies including Tata Power and Reliance were reluctant to buy DPC’s stake because of prevailing tariffs. An Economic Times analysis estimated that terminating the project would be less costly than continuing payments for ten years, though it also raised questions about selling the plant and assets.

The Godbole report criticized the project’s governance, competitive-bidding process and reliance on questionable assumptions. Separately, Enron appointed Arthur Andersen and Jones Lang LaSalle to value its Indian businesses, and withdrew its 24.5 percent stake in the Dolphin natural-gas project in Qatar.

Coach Bylsma’s philosophy restored the team’s confidence, and a five-game road trip, followed by trades for Billy and Adams, marked a turning point. The speaker praised the team’s playoff success, hoped for a championship ring, and highlighted Sid’s disciplined, system-focused leadership. Jordan was described as a talented, responsible two-way forward, while other leaders were praised for sustained effort and ability to seize momentum. Despite losing key pieces after last year’s Cup run, the organization’s continued dominance was called remarkable.

North Tyneside Council unanimously approved progressing with a devolution deal covering Newcastle, Northumberland and North Tyneside, including an elected mayor. The deal is expected to bring £600 million over 30 years and 10,000 jobs. Mayor Norma Redfearn said councils south of the Tyne could join after the authority was established, though not at this stage, and criticised them for abandoning an earlier proposal. The combined authority is planned for summer 2018, with mayoral elections in May 2019. Newcastle leader Nick Forbes rejected claims it would be underpowered, citing its health, disability support and housing components. A vote on dismantling the existing North East Combined Authority was postponed until mid-April.

The passage describes NVIDIA’s Blackwell GPU architecture, its DLSS 4 technologies, neural-shading capabilities, and GeForce RTX 50 Series hardware. Blackwell can reduce power consumption by up to 50% through shorter active periods, lower-power transitional states, and entering deep sleep ten times faster.

DLSS 4 uses AI to improve frame rate, latency, and image quality. DLSS Multi Frame Generation can produce up to three additional frames for every traditionally rendered frame. Its AI model is described as 40% faster and using 30% less VRAM than the previous generation, while enhanced Flip Metering in the Blackwell display engine provides more consistent frame pacing. Fifth-generation Tensor Cores and the AI Management Processor support faster execution and scheduling of these operations.

DLSS 4 replaces convolutional neural networks with transformer-based models for Super Resolution, Ray Reconstruction, and Deep Learning Anti-Aliasing. Transformers use self-attention to identify long-range patterns across larger pixel windows and support models with twice as many parameters. The resulting improvements include greater temporal stability, reduced ghosting, improved lighting detail, better detail in motion, and fewer ray-tracing denoiser artifacts.

Blackwell advances programmable and neural shading by exposing Tensor Cores to pixel and ray-tracing shaders through the Cooperative Vectors API for DirectX 12 and Vulkan. Combined with Slang’s differentiable shading features, this enables neural texture compression, neural materials, a neural radiance cache, RTX Skin, and RTX Neural Faces. Neural shaders can approximate lighting, surface interactions, and texture behavior, with potential applications that the passage says remain largely unexplored.

RTX Neural Texture Compression uses neural networks to compress and decompress textures more efficiently, while Stochastic Texture Filtering reduces aliasing and moiré patterns. A cited materials demonstration reduced memory use from 1,110 MB to 333 MB, exceeding a threefold saving. The Neural Radiance Cache trains small neural networks on live game data to infer indirect lighting from a limited number of traced rays. RTX Skin brings real-time path-traced subsurface scattering to games, while RTX Neural Faces uses a real-time generative AI model, trained on images across angles, lighting, emotion, and occlusion, to construct more natural faces.

The architecture family includes GB202, a flagship chip with 92.2 billion transistors, 192 streaming multiprocessors, 24,576 CUDA Cores, 192 RT Cores, and 768 Tensor Cores. GB203 has 45.6 billion transistors, 84 streaming multiprocessors, 10,752 CUDA Cores, 84 RT Cores, and 336 Tensor Cores. GB205 contains 31 billion transistors, 50 streaming multiprocessors, 6,400 CUDA Cores, 50 RT Cores, and 200 Tensor Cores. The passage associates GB202 with the GeForce RTX 5090, GB203 with the RTX 5080 and RTX 5070 Ti, and GB205 with the RTX 5070.

NVIDIA states that the specifications are accurate and reliable as of the publication date but may change, that the materials are provided without warranties, and that customers are responsible for testing product suitability. NVIDIA also reserves trademark rights and prohibits unauthorized reproduction of the covered materials.

Plymouth Studio School is expected to close at the end of the summer term in 2018, subject to government approval. The £4.2 million sports-focused free school has 155 pupils against a capacity of 300, and MP Johnny Mercer said it was financially unsustainable and had not sufficiently improved after an Ofsted inspection rated it “inadequate.” The school opened in temporary accommodation in 2015 before moving to a permanent Marjons campus. It was named among seven underperforming Plymouth schools in April 2018, and its closure would make it the 19th studio school to close since the model began. Mercer and the local authority are working to find school places and ensure continuity of pupils’ education.

California Assembly Republican Leader Chad Mayes says he does not regret joining seven other Republicans in voting with Democrats to extend California’s cap-and-trade program, which requires companies to purchase greenhouse-gas permits. He missed Gov. Jerry Brown’s signing ceremony because of a scheduling conflict.

Conservatives accused Mayes of betraying party principles and helping Democrats raise business costs. Mayes and his allies said the vote showed Republicans were serious about addressing climate change. County chairs, committees, donors, and activists have called on him to resign, and Republican leaders are seeking his removal, though only his 25-member caucus can oust him. Lawmaker Jay Obernolte has challenged him, while Mayes plans to remain. The dispute has also complicated party fundraising negotiations.

The seven other Republican voters have faced conservative backlash. Critics said the episode could deepen tensions between the minority party’s need to work with Democrats for relevance and its commitment to conservative orthodoxy. Assemblywoman Melissa Melendez, who resigned as deputy caucus leader in protest, was also moved from her Capitol office.

David I. Levine’s November 11, 1999 email assigns Mankiw, Chapter 10, for November 17–18. Homework #4 asks students to explain how monetary and fiscal policy shift the IS and LM curves; bring a recent newspaper article illustrating such a shift; recommend IS or LM shifts in response to Southeast Asia’s two-year decline in aggregate demand and identify the IMF’s recommendations; and complete Mankiw page 292, problems 1 and 2. Class discussion will focus on IS and LM shifts in the EC, US, Japan, and Indonesia during the 1997–98 crisis, with each student prepared to discuss at least one.

Optional readings:

- **“A French Paradox at Work”** examines France’s 35-hour workweek law, under which employees work 35 hours while receiving 39 hours’ pay. Although intended to reduce unemployment, the law has produced little evidence of substantial job creation. It has prompted workplace reorganization that may increase productivity and flexibility, but its effects vary; some expanding manufacturers benefit, while service businesses face greater difficulty. Unions and businesses have raised concerns about wages, worker protections, costs, and competitiveness, and public support has declined. Government subsidies have eased some businesses’ transition costs.

- **“Latin American markets rally”** reports that foreign investment inflows, expectations of fewer US interest-rate increases, and optimism about recovering growth drove stock markets across Latin America. Analysts projected regional growth of 3.2% in 2000 after a 1% contraction in 1999. Chile and Mexico received benefit from lower rates, recovering commodity prices, and political developments. Brazil’s currency stabilized with IMF support, and economists forecast 3% growth in 2000, though foreign rate increases and delays in Brazilian tax and pension reforms remained risks.

- **“Getting to the Bottom of Japan’s Economic Blues”** attributes Japan’s prolonged stagnation to the collapse of asset bubbles, delayed treatment of bad loans, restrictive fiscal policy, and resulting banking and credit crises. Although government financial and fiscal stimulus offered a temporary respite, bank restructuring, corporate reform, and systemic changes were considered essential. Structural pressures included the end of Japan’s catch-up growth, global competition from lower-wage economies, rapid population aging, and a shift from manufacturing toward information and services. The article argues that renewed growth required innovation and nonprice competition despite resistance to reform.

The 2017 Nobel Peace Prize was awarded to the International Campaign to Abolish Nuclear Weapons (ICAN) for highlighting nuclear weapons’ humanitarian consequences and promoting a treaty-based ban. ICAN, a coalition of NGOs in 100 countries, helped drive the UN Treaty on the Prohibition of Nuclear Weapons, adopted July 7 with support from 122 nations. It bans nuclear-weapons development, testing, production, acquisition, possession and stockpiling. The five nuclear-armed permanent UN Security Council members did not join negotiations. Nobel committee president Berit Reiss-Andersen said nuclear weapons pose a constant threat, while ICAN said treating them as a legitimate security source encourages proliferation.

The push-pull converter design uses approximately 25 ns dead time to limit reverse-conduction losses, with 20.5-kΩ resistors selected for RPS and RSP. A roughly 50-ns leading-edge blank time and 49.9-kΩ RLEB were selected to suppress sensed-current ringing and transients; RLEB may require optimization for PCB parasitics, gate-driver delay, minimum on-time, and switching-frequency constraints. A 33-nF soft-start capacitor produces an approximately 7.5-ms soft-start time.

The transformer design targets a maximum duty cycle of about 35%, below the controller’s 50% limit, and uses a turns ratio of 2.5. Magnetizing current was initially targeted at 6% of output current. Although the calculated primary inductance was 33 µH, 40 µH was used in the design. Primary-side GaN FETs were rated at 170 V for a 36-V maximum input, while an 80-V GaN FET was selected for secondary synchronous rectification. A parallel Schottky diode may reduce soft-start current and dead-time reverse-conduction losses. An RCD clamp can limit switch-node voltage; its initial resistor and capacitor values are calculated from allowable overshoot, leakage inductance, peak primary current, and capacitor ripple, then optimized through testing.

The output inductor is 0.47 µH, selected for a targeted 40% ripple current. Output capacitance calculations address load-transient deviation and voltage ripple, requiring at least 1.3 mF; approximately 2.3 mF was used to provide additional single-event-transient mitigation. This was implemented with seven 330-µF polymer-tantalum capacitors having a combined effective ESR of 0.86 mΩ. An optional output LC filter can further reduce noise, and a resistor may be added to damp high-frequency peaking.

Cycle-by-cycle limiting was designed to begin at approximately 35 A output current. With a peak inductor current of 24.25 A at maximum load, this provides about 45% margin before an overcurrent is detected. The primary current is sensed at CS_ILIM, a 1:100 current-sense transformer is used, and a 7.5-Ω RCS resistor was selected. The hiccup capacitor is 3.3 nF.

The converter uses Type 2A frequency compensation with a 10-kHz target crossover frequency and calculated power-stage transconductance of 16.2 A/V. Selected compensation values are 40.2 kΩ for RCOMP, 15 nF for CCOMP, and 47 pF for CHF, with tuning during testing anticipated. A 102-kΩ resistor is connected from RSC to AVSS for slope compensation.

The TPS7H500x-SP controller supply range is 4–14 V. A regulated input supply and at least a 0.1-µF VIN-to-AVSS bypass capacitor are required. X5R or better ceramic capacitors should be placed close to the controller with low-impedance AVSS paths, and bulk capacitance is recommended when the supply is more than a few inches away.

Layout guidance emphasizes isolating feedback and other noise-sensitive traces from magnetics and switch-node signals, minimizing switch-node copper and high-dV/dt loop area, keeping switching paths short, and separating analog AVSS from power ground with a single connection point. High-current traces should be short, direct, and as wide as practical, with a guideline of 15 mils per ampere. Filtering, bypass, compensation, and VSENSE-divider components should be placed near their associated controller pins. Gate-drive signals should be routed away from sensitive pins; CS_ILIM may require nearby RC filtering, and SYNC requires special isolation from sensitive signals and HICC. For CFP packages, backside metallization should connect to AVSS through multiple vias.

Application curves show output soft-start and a 5-A load-step response. The document also provides support resources, related evaluation-module and radiation reports, revision history, mechanical and packaging information, orderable-device details, and ESD-handling cautions.

Pragyan ’18 commenced on March 1, 2018, with a four-day program complemented by year-round outreach and social responsibility events. Guest lectures, workshops, a human library, technology exhibits, infotainment performances, and a valediction marked the festival, showcasing projects including Hyperloop India, InMoov, KalamSat, ISRO exhibits, and Ugears.

Shimon Sakaguchi, Mary Brunkow and Fred Ramsdell won the 2025 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine for discovering regulatory T cells and their role in autoimmune disease. These cells restrain immune activity and prevent attacks on the body; their failure can lead to autoimmune disorders or damaging inflammation. Sakaguchi identified them in 1995, while Brunkow and Ramsdell linked a mouse autoimmunity mutation to the gene he had found and reported human mutations causing IPEX in 2001. Researchers are exploring T-reg-based approaches for autoimmune disease, cancer and other immune disorders.

Arthur Heine moved to dismiss a bigamy indictment, arguing that his second marriage was void because he was 19 when a justice of the peace solemnized it. His first marriage to Aud Irene Kvamli Heine remained valid and undissolved when he married Marie Licciardi on September 4, 1955. The court considered conflicting lower-court decisions interpreting New York Domestic Relations Law § 11(5), which restricts marriages involving a party under 21 to specified officials. Following Caplan v. Caplan and De Martino v. De Martino, the court concluded that the statute requires compliance with its solemnization provisions and that Heine’s second marriage was therefore void. It granted the motion to dismiss the indictment.

The passage examines the “Santa Claus Rally,” or turn-of-the-year effect, in which stocks tend to perform strongly during late December and early January, typically beginning on the third Friday of December. Christmas has been a U.S. federal holiday since 1870. It is not a trading day, adjacent days may trade depending on the calendar, and the bond market closes at 2 p.m. on the preceding trading day. Weekend holidays are observed on Friday or Monday.

Backtests of several S&P 500 strategies from 1960 produced positive results. The initial strategy averaged 0.7% per trade with a 66% win rate, 2.0 profit factor, and 9% maximum drawdown. Extending the holding period increased average returns to 1.6% per trade, while another version—buying after December 20 and selling on the first trading day of the new year—averaged 1% with a 5.9% maximum drawdown. Performance weakened during 2013/14 through 2015/16.

European backtests also showed strong Christmas-season performance. Using EWG as a DAX proxy produced an average trade gain of 2.1%, an 81% win rate, and a profit factor of 13. FEZ, used for Euro Stoxx 50, averaged 1.5% per trade with an 81% win rate and a profit factor of 9, although recent returns were below earlier levels.

An emerging-markets fund proxy averaged 2.7% per trade, with a 73% win rate and 7% maximum drawdown. A limited NIFTY 50 backtest from 2008 averaged 1.2% per trade, with a 71% win rate and 7% maximum drawdown. Proposed explanations include year-end fund inflows and rebalancing, limited macroeconomic news, positive turn-of-month effects, and reduced selling during holidays. The passage concludes that the historical rally effect is well supported but does not guarantee future results.

The University of Maine cancelled its floating offshore wind summit (AFLOAT), citing changing federal policies and priorities amid waning federal renewable energy support; a $12.5 million grant for its program was suspended. It has no plans to revive the summit but will meet with industry, research and government leaders about commercializing its floating wind technology.

Darfon showcased upgraded H200, H300, and H5001 products at Intersolar North America 2018. The H200 offers Panasonic LNMC and Dragonfly LFP batteries, relocated rear terminals, and up to 30kWh storage. The H300 wall-mounted unit now comes in 10kWh. The H5001 adds a lockable distribution box and PV disconnect. All three have upgraded fans, improved 120V in-rush handling, an optional generator start-up kit, and are available through authorized distributors.

The team remains confident despite losing two consecutive games, noting that one game was deserved and the others could have gone either way. The opposing team is executing its system more effectively, so adjustments are needed. The speaker emphasizes creating chances, crashing the net and generating rebounds against the aggressive goaltender, even if goals are not “pretty.” With the Cup in the building, players are setting aside distractions and focusing on preparation. The team believes it could have won the recent games and sees the Cup as strong motivation. The speaker also praises Rob, highlighting their communication, mutual accountability, strong relationship and on-ice chemistry as important to their success.

The Federal Reserve raised its key short-term interest rate by 0.25 percentage point, its third hike since December, bringing the rate to a range of 1%–1.25%. Citing continued economic strength, the Fed upgraded its growth and unemployment forecasts while lowering this year’s inflation projection to 1.6%. Unemployment fell to 4.3% in May, and most officials expect at least one more rate hike this year. The Fed also plans to begin gradually selling $10 billion in mortgage-backed securities and Treasuries monthly later this year.

A hockey player describes the excitement of playing at home in a hostile arena. He feels confident at the net, credits the team’s strong play, and plans to focus, contribute, and avoid overthinking. He notes that Edmonton will be ready, so his team must match their intensity and treat the game like any other road game.

The passage describes the ARM Cortex-A8 subsystem, C674x DSP subsystem, supporting multimedia and synchronization modules, memory architecture, and device pin assignments. The Cortex-A8 subsystem integrates a general-purpose ARM Cortex-A8 processor with a Harvard architecture, NEON SIMD and VFPv3 coprocessors, separate L1 instruction and data caches, and a 128-bit system interconnect. Its AINTC prioritizes peripheral service requests and generates IRQ or FIQ signals, although general-purpose devices do not support FIQ generation. PLL_ARM derives subsystem clocks from the device clock. The processor connects through an arbiter to a 128-bit DMM port for direct DDR access and a 64-bit L3 port for other device modules. Debug support includes hardware/software debug assistance and an ETM interface with trace and triggering resources; its unpinned trace port connects to a 32KB system Embedded Trace Buffer.

The DSP subsystem includes 32KB of L1 program/cache memory with error detection, 256KB of unified L2 RAM/cache with ECC, and little-endian operation. The C674x CPU has eight functional units, two 32-register files, and two data paths. Its multiply units support scalar, parallel, complex, and Galois-field multiplication; load/store units handle memory transfers; and the S/L units perform arithmetic, logical, branch, comparison, packing, and parallel add/subtract operations. Enhancements include interruptible SPLOOP software-pipelining support, compact 16-bit forms of common instructions, expanded instruction-set capabilities, exception handling, user/supervisor privilege levels with memory-page permissions, and a stall-insensitive free-running time-stamp counter.

All C674x MDMA accesses pass through the system MMU and are remapped to physical addresses, protecting ARM memory regions and permitting shared buffer allocation. EDMA transfer controllers 0 and 1 may optionally use the MMU through MMU_CFG. The Media Controller manages HDVPSS and ISS, while HDVICP2 accelerates encoding, decoding, and transcoding for MPEG, H.264, VC-1, RV9/10, AVS, and ON2 formats. The face-detection module tracks faces in QVGA 8-bit luma images, supports minimum face sizes of 20, 25, 32, or 40 pixels, and reports size, position, angle, and confidence. The Spinlock module provides 128 hardware semaphores, and the Mailbox module supports queued processor communication and interrupt-based receipt, queue-not-full, and overflow notification.

A unified memory map provides a consistent view across bus masters where possible. The DDR DMM TILER adds a 4GB extended range for rotated and mirrored frame-buffer views, fully accessible to HDVPSS and ISS; other masters can access one view through the 512MB base TILER region.

Package pin maps and terminal-function tables document signal names, multiplexing, ball numbers, package designators, electrical types, internal pull states, supply voltages, and pin functions. Reset-sampled BTMODE signals configure ARM boot, GPMC multiplexing, XIP options, EMAC PHY mode, and reset-output behavior. Additional tables cover DDR2/DDR3, EMAC, GPIO, GPMC, HDMI, I2C, McASP, PCIe, reset/interrupt/JTAG, SD, SPI, clock and timer, UART, USB, video input/output, analog TV output, and supply-voltage pins. GPIO pins can also serve as external interrupts, and several peripherals require specified external pullups, resistors, clock sources, power rails, or unconnected-pin handling.

Amazon.com, Inc.’s unaudited Form 10-Q for the quarter ended June 30, 2019 reported Q2 net sales of $63.40 billion, up 20% from $52.89 billion. Operating income was $3.08 billion, net income was $2.63 billion, and diluted earnings per share were $5.22. For the first six months, net sales were $123.10 billion, operating income was $7.50 billion, and net income was $6.19 billion.

Q2 segment results included North America sales of $38.65 billion and operating income of $1.56 billion; International sales of $16.37 billion and an operating loss of $601 million; and AWS sales of $8.38 billion and operating income of $2.12 billion. At June 30, total assets were $191.35 billion and stockholders’ equity was $53.06 billion. Six-month operating cash flow was $10.96 billion, while investing and financing activities used $15.67 billion and $4.54 billion, respectively.

The company adopted new lease accounting guidance on January 1, 2019, recognizing approximately $21 billion of operating lease assets and liabilities without retrospectively adjusting prior periods. It also began capitalizing substantially all episodic television production costs, adding approximately $342 million of capitalized film costs in the first six months.

Amazon reported $25.07 billion of total debt and $46.65 billion of lease liabilities as of June 30, 2019. It disclosed tax contingencies of approximately $3.7 billion, patent disputes involving Fire HD 10 tablets, and an ongoing review of sanctions-related orders. Critical accounting judgments included inventory valuation and income taxes, while forward-looking results remained subject to business, competitive, international, legal, tax, and currency risks.

Volkswagen’s U.S. unit asked a Virginia judge to delay the Feb. 26 consumer-fraud trial by at least six months, arguing that inflammatory comments by an owners’ lawyer in a Netflix documentary could prejudice jurors. The lawyer referenced Volkswagen’s 2014 toxic-fume tests on monkeys and the Holocaust; he called the motion “hogwash.” The case involves a North Carolina man’s 2014 diesel Jetta. Nearly 500,000 U.S. diesel vehicles were covered by a 2016 settlement, while about 2,000 owners opted out and pursued claims. Volkswagen also agreed to spend more than $25 billion on U.S. claims and vehicle buybacks.

James Madison returned the internal-improvements bill to the House of Representatives, objecting that Congress lacked constitutional authority to fund and construct roads, canals, and navigation improvements. He rejected arguments that this power fell under the Commerce Clause, the Necessary and Proper Clause, or the “common defense and general welfare” provision, warning that a broad interpretation would expand congressional power, undermine the defined division between federal and state governments, and limit judicial oversight. He further stated that state consent could not grant Congress powers not provided by the Constitution. Despite recognizing the potential benefits of such improvements, Madison withheld his signature and suggested obtaining the necessary powers through constitutional amendment.

NATO’s 2017 annual report showed increased alliance defense and deterrence, particularly against Russia. NATO deployed four multinational battle groups to the Baltic states and Poland, increased its Black Sea presence, and strengthened hybrid-war resilience and cyber defenses. European and Canadian defense spending rose for three consecutive years after the 2014 Wales pledge, adding $46 billion, including $18 billion for major equipment. NATO deployments exceeded 23,000 troops at year’s end, up from nearly 18,000 in 2014. Stoltenberg highlighted Russia’s use of a military-grade nerve agent in Salisbury, which allies called a breach of international norms, along with its actions in Georgia, Crimea, eastern Ukraine, elections, and nuclear modernization. NATO expanded Afghanistan’s Resolute Support mission from 13,000 to about 16,000 personnel and supported an Afghan-led peace process. It also joined the anti-ISIS coalition, trained Iraqi forces, welcomed Montenegro as its 29th member, and deepened EU cooperation.

The passage argues that scalping—profiting from small price changes over seconds or minutes—is rarely profitable and often a waste of time. Scalpers face sophisticated competitors, market noise and randomness, limited opportunities, and substantial stress. Short time horizons make backtesting unreliable, while commissions, bid–ask spreads, and slippage erode small gains. Automation is essentially necessary but introduces technology and execution risks. One example describes a well-funded, co-located scalper who still lost to a faster competitor.

The passage recommends finding edges and strategies on longer time frames, where backtests are more robust and potential profits per trade are larger. It suggests stocks and indexes may offer better opportunities than highly competitive markets such as forex, and that patient, diversified long-term investing in mutual funds may offer better odds of reasonable success. It does not claim scalping is impossible, but says consistent profitability is very difficult and most scalpers lose money.

Using DFT calculations in CASTEP with GGA-PBE and GGA-PBEsol, the study investigated three previously unstudied o-MAX phases, Mo₂A₂AlC₃ (A = Zr, Nb, Ta), across structural, electronic, mechanical, thermodynamic, and optical properties. The compounds adopt a hexagonal P6₃/mmc structure containing 16 atoms per unit cell. Their negative formation energies—−0.506, −0.349, and −0.386 eV/atom for the Zr, Nb, and Ta variants, respectively—indicate chemical stability, with Mo₂Zr₂AlC₃ ranked most stable. Their phonon dispersions contain no negative frequencies, and their elastic constants satisfy mechanical-stability criteria, confirming dynamical and mechanical stability.

Band structures and densities of states show metallic behavior with anisotropic conductivity, stronger bonding in the basal plane than along the c-axis, and prominent Mo-4d contributions. Density-of-states, charge-density, and Mulliken analyses indicate mixed metallic, covalent, and ionic bonding, including strong Mo–C covalent interactions and electron transfer from the metals to carbon. Mo₂Nb₂AlC₃ exhibits the strongest calculated bonding and the highest Young’s modulus and fracture toughness, while Mo₂Zr₂AlC₃ has greater damage tolerance. All three phases are mechanically anisotropic and brittle according to G/B, Poisson’s ratio, and Cauchy-pressure criteria. Their Vickers hardnesses are 6.025, 6.277, and 6.224 GPa for the Zr, Nb, and Ta compounds, respectively.

Thermal calculations give Debye temperatures of 634.09, 632.60, and 525.98 K; minimum thermal conductivities of 0.89, 0.90, and 0.74 W/m·K; melting temperatures of 2064, 2237, and 2131 K; and thermal expansion coefficients of 11.11, 9.90, and 11.47 × 10⁻⁶ K⁻¹. These properties, together with favorable thermal conductivity, expansion, and melting behavior, identify the phases as potential thermal-barrier coating materials, with Mo₂Ta₂AlC₃ particularly suitable because of its low Young’s modulus and minimum thermal conductivity.

Optical calculations reveal direction-dependent dielectric responses and metallic behavior. The compounds show high low-energy reflectivity and reflectivities consistent with the cited threshold for coating applications, supporting their potential use in thermal-barrier and solar heat-shielding layers.

Becton, Dickinson and Co. (BDX) has paid dividends since 1962 and increased them by roughly 10% or more in 12 of 13 years since 2004, averaging 16.3% growth. The passage projects 2017 dividends of approximately $2.92–$2.98 per share, supported by fiscal 2017 GAAP diluted EPS guidance of $7.90–$8.00. First-quarter EPS rose 143% to $2.58, primarily because of a litigation reserve reversal. The dividend payout ratio fell from 59% in fiscal 2016 to an estimated 37% in 2017.

Becton produces diabetes-care, IV catheter, syringe, specimen-collection and surgical products. The 2015 CareFusion merger temporarily pressured margins through restructuring and interest costs, but those costs declined in early 2017 as profitability recovered. Risks include manufacturing disruptions, higher interest rates and competing products. The author considers the dividend safe and suitable for a dividend portfolio and discloses a long position in BDX.

QuantifiedStrategies.com presents trading articles, videos, courses, and backtested strategies covering psychology, risk management, orders, indicators, seasonality, backtesting, futures, forex, and stock-market trading. It emphasizes quantitative, rule-based approaches supported by statistics and backtest results, with long- and short-form videos and beginner learning resources.

The passage argues that Celtic’s victory demonstrated their growing superiority over Rangers and the failure of Rangers chairman Dave King to deliver the promised financial backing to manager Mark Warburton. Rangers’ reliance on ageing players Clint Hill and Kenny Miller, along with perceived discord between King and Warburton, could widen the gap further. Celtic’s signings Moussa Dembélé and Scott Sinclair have strengthened their confidence and quality. With substantial Champions League income and potential future European revenue available, the passage urges Brendan Rodgers to invest in his squad, prepare for Europe and use Celtic’s financial advantage to establish an unbridgeable domestic lead over Rangers.

This critical reflection examines how generative AI can be incorporated ethically and practically into contemporary and imagined education systems. Drawing on Anders, Foucault, Freire, Bloom, and Arendt, it develops a framework for evaluating AI use across online, blended, and in-person settings.

Anders’s account of technology highlights the “Promethean discrepancy” between what technology can produce and what people can understand or imagine, warning that technological possibility is often mistaken for moral justification. Foucault’s analysis of power and “regimes of truth” frames generative AI as a corporate tool that can shape knowledge, manipulate behavior, reproduce bias, and produce competing, sometimes inaccurate “truths.” Freire’s concepts of humanization, conscientization, and dialogue suggest that educational technology is not inherently harmful when used critically to support learners’ agency and transformation of the world.

Bloom’s Revised Taxonomy provides a means of classifying cognitive learning activities but does not address their ethical purposes. Arendt’s hierarchy of labor, work, and action supplies this normative direction, emphasizing durable outcomes, public engagement, plurality, and action-oriented agency. Together, these perspectives support a spectrum for assessing student AI use, ranging from consumptive labor to humanizing action. AI-assisted work falls toward the labor end when it is uncritical, unrelated to the student’s circumstances, or based on errors; it approaches humanizing action when students critically evaluate AI, connect it to their perspectives, and use it to affect the world.

The paper offers guiding questions and imagined classroom applications, including community-based political action and Socratic dialogue for individualized research. It concludes that educators, teachers, and instructional designers should continually adapt pedagogy and assessment as AI evolves, while researching ambiguous ethical cases. The proposed guideposts emphasize human agency, critical reflection, dialogue, and meaningful action as enduring educational goals.

This continuation application addresses reduced processing time in low-latency cellular systems using configurable or short transmission time intervals (TTIs). Because shorter TTIs and timing advances can leave less processing time, a wireless transmit/receive unit (WTRU) may determine processing capabilities based on factors including TTI length, symbol count, transport-block size, channel and transmission type, scheduling or HARQ timeline, and other radio criteria. The WTRU may report these capabilities to an eNodeB, receive a capability configuration, and limit its applied timing advance or Rx-Tx time difference according to the maximum supported for a specific TTI length. It may measure processing values, calculate headroom relative to its capability, report proximity or headroom when a condition is met, and suspend or drop uplink transmissions. A WTRU may also calculate available processing time from downlink control information containing an uplink grant and transmit when that time meets a capability-based threshold. For HARQ acknowledgment of downlink data, it may compare the uplink transmission start time with the processing time available after the downlink transmission. The disclosure further describes timing adjustment, time-alignment timers and expiry actions, HARQ timing, configurable TTIs, cellular network architectures, WLAN operation, and emulation-based testing.

Index Markets Research’s report analyzes the global silyl modified polymer market, including historical, current, and projected revenues, growth rates, trends, drivers, constraints, risks, opportunities, PEST and Porter’s Five Forces, and the competitive landscape. It covers polyurethane, polyamine ether, and other product types, plus construction, automotive, general industry, and other applications. Regional analysis includes the United States, China, Europe, Japan, Southeast Asia, India, and Rest of World. The report examines production, capacity, supply, demand, pricing, profits, technological developments, SWOT, investment feasibility, and returns. It profiles Kaneka, Bostik, Henkel, Wacker, Evonik, 3M, Dow Corning Corporation, H.B. Fuller, Hodgson Sealants, and Risun Polymer, and offers guidance to market participants and new entrants.

India’s trucking market is expected to transform markedly by 2027 as population growth, urbanisation and rising freight demand expand fleets. GST is expected to ease long-distance road transport by reducing delays at state borders, encouraging longer routes and more powerful, faster trucks. Bharat VI emissions standards are being introduced directly, with OEMs expected to comply within four years, creating significant manufacturing challenges and supplier opportunities. Domestic manufacturers currently dominate, but global OEMs are expected to gain ground, supported by major infrastructure investment. AMP II targets include making India a top-three automotive market, lifting exports to 35–40% of production, raising the sector’s GDP contribution above 12%, and creating 65 million jobs. Trucks in 2027 are therefore expected to be larger, more capable, connected and efficient, while policy changes remain unpredictable. Electrification and autonomous driving are considered many decades away.

The disclosure describes an embedded device with a processor, memory, streaming engines, and a matrix multiplication accelerator (MMA) for implementing computational primitives used in speech recognition, industrial control, object detection and recognition, and vision. In an example, the processor is a digital signal processor with L1 data cache, unified L2 cache, and two streaming engines.

The MMA contains a 1×32 multiplier buffer for matrix A, two 32×32 multiplicand buffers for matrix B, and two 32×32 result buffers for matrix C, using 16-bit elements. The B and C buffers operate as background and foreground buffers for overlapping loads, computations, and stores. Each cycle, a combined Load, Store, and Execute instruction loads a vector into the A buffer, multiplies it with a selected B matrix, and stores the resulting row in a selected C buffer. The instruction can simultaneously load background B data, store C data, and apply assignment, addition, subtraction, or no post-processing operation to multiplication results.

The MMA also includes configurable input and output formatting components, a lookup table that can store A data at four-bit precision and expand it to 16 bits, per-element row-offset values for positioning loaded data, and an optional rectifying linear unit that replaces negative outputs with zero. The processor prepares source A and B vectors, applies operations such as zero padding, even/odd selection, value replication, identity-matrix generation, and linked operations, and receives MMA output for further formatting before storage in external memory.

Streaming engines transfer data from the L2 cache into register files. They are programmable with a starting address, element size and type, formatting, and a multidimensional address sequence implemented through parameterized nested loops. Control software configures the streaming engines and MMA, starts the engines, and executes sequences of LSE instructions for each computational primitive.

Examples map multiple operations to matrix multiplication. Small matrix multiplications are batched by placing multiplicand matrices diagonally in a B buffer and corresponding multiplier matrices in the A buffer. Large matrix multiplications divide matrices into 32×32 tiles and accumulate tile products. Pointwise multiplication loads rows of one matrix diagonally and multiplies them by corresponding rows of the other. Matrix addition is implemented as multiplication by an identity matrix followed by addition of a second identity-scaled matrix. Batched small vector-matrix multiplication uses diagonal copies of a constant matrix; vector summation uses diagonal vectors of ones; and affine transformation uses diagonal copies of the concatenated matrix and bias vector.

Two-dimensional convolution tiles input feature maps into a filtering matrix and applies filters through block matrix multiplication. Large and small feature-map tiling schemes are described, along with row-stride handling, column-stride selection, seam removal, and optional output zero padding. Matrix row and column permutations are implemented with permutation matrices.

The device can also perform small and large complex FFTs with interleaved or separate real and imaginary components, and small and large DCTs. Large FFT processing uses column and row FFT stages, pointwise twiddle-factor multiplication, and transposition. Small and large one-dimensional convolution or filtering are supported; large filters are recursively divided into fragments sized as a throughput-versus-fragment-count tradeoff. Correlation uses convolution with time-reversed coefficients. Matrix assignment uses multiplication by an identity matrix, and matrix transposition uses an MMA copy operation that writes A-buffer elements into successive B-buffer columns.

Other embodiments permit a host processor to perform some or all control operations, support processor types including RISC, ASIC, and DSP implementations, and allow MMA buffers to have dimensions smaller or larger than those described.
On June 3, 2021, Tesla reported that Jerome Guillen, President of Tesla Heavy Trucking, departed Tesla. The filing was signed by Chief Financial Officer Zachary J. Kirkhorn on June 7, 2021.

CEFC China agreed to buy about 20% of Cowen Group for $100 million, boosting shares 19%. The deal includes three board seats, $175 million financing and $18 per Class A share, pending approvals and a Q3 2017 close.

Apple regained the quarterly smartphone-sales lead from Samsung in Q4 2016, selling 77 million iPhones (17.9%) versus Samsung’s 76.8 million (17.8%), according to Gartner. Holiday iPhone sales aided Apple, while Samsung suffered from the Galaxy Note7 recall. Samsung could retake the lead before Apple’s September release, but led full-year sales, 20.5% to Apple’s 14.4%. Huawei, Oppo, and BBK ranked third through fifth with 9.5%, 6.2%, and 5.6% shares, respectively. Oppo and BBK offer features such as dual cameras and fast charging and are expanding into developed markets.

The passage introduces the NVIDIA A100 Tensor Core GPU, an eighth-generation data center accelerator built on the NVIDIA Ampere GA100 architecture and a TSMC 7nm process. Designed for AI, HPC, and data analytics, it adds third-generation Tensor Cores supporting TF32, IEEE-compliant FP64, BF16, FP16, INT8, INT4, and binary data, plus fine-grained structured sparsity that can double Tensor Core throughput. Reported comparisons with V100 include 10x higher TF32 performance, 2.5x higher FP64 performance, and 20x higher sparse INT8 performance.

The GPU features 40 GB of HBM2 memory with 1555 GB/s bandwidth, a 40 MB L2 cache, larger per-SM L1/shared memory, cache-residency controls, and data compression. Its Multi-Instance GPU feature securely partitions an A100 into as many as seven isolated instances, improving utilization, quality of service, and fault isolation for multi-tenant environments. Third-generation NVLink provides 600 GB/s total bandwidth, while PCIe Gen 4 supports 31.5 GB/s connections.

A100 also introduces CUDA 11 features such as asynchronous memory copies, asynchronous barriers, and accelerated task graphs. It can scale across multiple GPUs through NVLink, NVSwitch, InfiniBand, and Ethernet, supporting systems including DGX, HGX, and EGX A100 platforms for large-scale training, inference, scientific computing, and data analysis.
An 80-year-old man was treated on a hospital floor due to bed shortages. PML-N workers celebrated Yaum-e-Takbeer, while speakers praised Nawaz Sharif.
