An exploratory multiple-case study examined how early-stage startups develop Internet-of-Things systems, focusing on the research question: “How do startups develop their Internet-of-Thing systems in their early-stages?” The study analyzed eight startups through 12 semi-structured interviews, documents, and other secondary sources. Seven startups were in early stages and one was more established. Interview data were examined thematically using the SEMAT Essence framework, particularly its System, Team, Work, and Way of Working elements.

The findings show that startup teams typically lacked some required engineering or business expertise and therefore relied on consultants, component and cloud-service providers, manufacturers, and other external partners. The startups’ value propositions were either Internet-centric, Thing-centric, or combined, with development beginning at either the application or perception layer.

Three minimum viable product types were identified. Type 1 resembles the final user experience while functions are performed manually, using mock-ups, wireframes, and rapid hardware prototypes. Type 2 provides working functionality with actual software and hardware integration. Type 3 emphasizes quality attributes, including performance, scalability, security, and regression testing. All cases began with Type 1, most progressed to Type 2, and Type 3 involved greater integration and non-functional testing.

Common working practices included in-house design, outsourcing, rapid prototyping with technologies such as 3D printing and CAD tools, and reuse of open-source platforms, commercial components, and software. Iteration was more common than systematic Agile adoption because hardware cycles were longer and more costly than software cycles. Hardware complexity, strict physical requirements, and dependencies on external parties prolonged development.

The study concludes that IoT startups use speed-oriented, iterative approaches similar to software startups, but methodologies must accommodate hardware characteristics and interdisciplinary dependencies. Limitations include reliance on few interviews, early-stage bootstrap-funded cases from Pakistani and Scandinavian contexts, and possible bias in concept coding.

The lecture introduces link-cut trees as a data structure for maintaining dynamic forests of rooted, unordered trees. Supported operations include creating a tree, linking the root of one tree beneath a node in another, cutting a node from its parent, finding a node’s root, and aggregating weights along root-to-node paths. Each operation is intended to take logarithmic amortized time. Link-cut trees were originally developed to accelerate network-flow algorithms.

The representation uses preferred paths determined by the most recent accesses within each subtree. Every vertex belongs to one preferred path, and each path is stored in an auxiliary splay tree keyed by depth, so an in-order traversal recovers the path. Auxiliary trees are connected through path-parent pointers, forming a “tree of auxiliary trees.”

The central operation is `access(v)`. It makes the root-to-\(v\) path preferred, adjusts preferred-child pointers, splays nodes within their auxiliary trees, and ultimately makes \(v\) the root of the tree of auxiliary trees. Other operations reduce largely to one or two accesses plus constant work. `find root` accesses the requested node and then finds and splays the leftmost node in its auxiliary tree. Path aggregation uses subtree aggregates such as minimum, maximum, sum, or product within auxiliary trees. Cutting accesses the node and detaches its left auxiliary subtree; linking accesses both endpoints and connects their auxiliary trees appropriately.

For analysis, heavy-light decomposition is applied to the represented tree. An edge is heavy when the child’s subtree contains more than half of its parent’s subtree; at most one child edge is heavy. Following a light edge reduces subtree size by at least half, so any root-to-node path contains only \(O(\log n)\) light edges. Bounding creations of preferred light edges and destructions of preferred heavy edges yields \(O(\log n)\) amortized preferred-child changes per operation. A straightforward splay-tree analysis then gives an \(O(\log^2 n)\) bound, while the weighted splay access lemma allows the costs of successive splays to telescope, yielding \(O(\log n)\) amortized time per operation. A worst-case variant instead maintains heavy-light decomposition with weight-balanced trees, but its algorithms are described as more complicated.

Postpartum bleeding occurs after both vaginal delivery and C-section because placental separation leaves a heavily supplied area that sheds blood and tissue called lochia. Bleeding may initially resemble a heavy period with small clots, then gradually lessen and usually stop within four weeks. Bleeding beyond six to eight weeks warrants contacting a physician. Call a doctor for hourly pad saturation lasting two hours, large clots, a racing heart, shortness of breath, dizziness, lightheadedness, or a fever above 100.4°F. After a C-section, rest, stay hydrated, eat healthy meals, avoid lifting more than the baby or most housework, and avoid tampons, douching, baths, pools, hot tubs, exercise, sex, and repeated stair use.

The Commodity Channel Index (CCI) is a price-based momentum oscillator that compares a security’s current price with its average price over a specified period. High readings suggest prices are far above average, while low readings suggest they are far below average, potentially indicating overbought or oversold conditions. Its formula uses the typical price, a simple moving average, mean deviation, and the constant 0.015.

Although commonly associated with levels above +100 and below -100, overbought and oversold thresholds vary by security and should be assessed against its history. The original theory assumes markets move in cycles. A move below -100 may signal a new downtrend, while a move above zero from negative territory may indicate a developing rally. CCI can also identify bullish or bearish divergence, though divergence may only warn of changing conditions rather than provide a reliable reversal signal.

The CCI was invented by Donald R. Lambert in 1980 for commodities and is now used across stocks, ETFs, and other markets. It works best on mean-reverting assets, particularly stocks and bonds. Daily bars and short lookback periods of five to nine days are recommended.

A SPY backtest used a nine-day CCI, bought at -90, and sold when the close exceeded the previous day’s high. It produced a profit factor of about 1.8, an average gain per trade of 0.55%, and a 23% maximum drawdown, though the authors cautioned that it may be susceptible to curve fitting. The CCI is lagging, unsuitable for precise entry timing or trend detection, and can remain overbought or oversold for extended periods. The article concludes that oscillators such as the RSI may have stronger backtest results.

The Second Circuit reversed and vacated a preliminary injunction entered for Jackson Dairy in its diversity breach-of-contract action against H. P. Hood & Sons. Jackson was Hood’s exclusive distributor of “Schedule 3B” products in a Vermont–New Hampshire territory. After Hood began supplying Grand Union and Finast warehouses outside that territory, the chains bypassed Jackson and supplied their stores within it directly.

The court held that Jackson failed to establish irreparable harm because monetary damages could adequately compensate any loss of business, including claimed customer and delivery-route disruption. The contract’s termination-notice provision did not alter that conclusion. Judge Mansfield concurred, alternatively finding no meritorious basis for relief because the contract did not require Hood to police its customers and no evidence showed Hood controlled or participated in the chains’ transshipments, establishing no contract breach. The court did not address Hood’s other arguments or whether permanent relief could be awarded upon a sufficient showing of other irreparable harm.

Streptococcus pneumoniae causes substantial global morbidity and mortality, particularly among young children and adults aged 65 years or older. It commonly colonizes the upper respiratory tract and can cause invasive diseases, including bacteremia, meningitis, osteomyelitis, and septic arthritis, or noninvasive pneumonia, sinusitis, and otitis media. In China, six serotypes—3, 6B, 14, 19A, 19F, and 23F—mainly caused invasive pneumococcal disease in children and adults. China uses PCV13 for children and PPV23 for high-risk people aged two years and older, but neither is included in the national immunization program, and uptake remains at 3%–9%. Sinovac developed a preservative-free PPV23, approved in 2020, for people aged two years and older, especially high-risk populations. A phase 4 randomized, double-blind, active-controlled noninferiority trial was requested by China’s NMPA to assess its immunogenicity, tolerability, and safety compared with Pneumovax in children, adults, and elderly populations.

IDC finds that HPC-as-a-service (HPCaaS) enables industrial enterprises to offer simulations and HPC-derived insights as services, build new business models, expand customer bases, and increase collaboration without major upfront investment in their own infrastructure. IDC regards simulations, modeling, and data analytics as essential for industrial agility and innovation amid disruption and competitive pressure. Recommendations include establishing virtual product and manufacturing development, creating process and lifecycle transparency, adopting a holistic data strategy with a single source of truth, selecting an HPC operating model based on utilization, costs, performance, security, and skills, prioritizing scalable, secure, and energy-efficient solutions, and leveraging external expertise when needed. The findings come from a December 2021 telephone survey of 200 technology-related decision-makers at industrial enterprises with more than 500 employees in Germany, Austria, and Switzerland.

The treaty respects Nicaragua’s sovereignty and provides no U.S. territorial acquisition or political control. Nicaragua contributes the territory, while the United States supplies the money; the canal is to be open to all nations on equal terms, with preferences reserved for the contracting parties’ coasting trade. It also authorizes railway and telegraph facilities and safeguards the canal and Nicaragua against future contingencies.

The canal would promote national unity, strengthen domestic commerce and defense, connect South American and Asian markets with the United States, and reduce shipping times substantially. It would also provide a lower-cost Atlantic-Pacific route than Panama and support a growing coasting trade. Construction would involve roughly 43½ to 53½ miles of canal excavation, 119 miles of lake and river navigation, and locks at both ends.

Although costly, the project is expected to produce immediate revenue and substantial national prosperity. The treaty includes a $4 million loan to Nicaragua for internal improvements supporting the canal. The article defines inflation as a gradual decline in a currency's purchasing power caused by a broad rise in prices, measured as the weighted average increase in a basket of goods and services. It identifies major causes: an oversupply of money and printed currency (considered the leading long-term cause), demand-pull inflation from excess demand, cost-push inflation from rising production costs and wages, and built-in inflation arising from expectations that price increases will continue.

High inflation is described as harmful to stocks in the short term: consumers spend more and invest less, stock prices become more volatile, value stocks tend to outperform while overvalued growth stocks with high P/E ratios are avoided, and dividend stocks may decline as dividends lag inflation. Inflation can also prompt central banks to raise interest rates, increasing borrowing costs and potentially contributing to recession or a market crash. Cited benefits include higher rates and prices benefiting lenders, borrowers repaying with less valuable money, rising real estate values, and gold serving as a hedge. Suggested inflation-era investments include index funds, stocks, bonds, commodities, gold, real estate or REITs, and Treasury Inflation-Protected Securities (TIPS, or the TIP ETF) as the most reliable hedge; over the long run, stocks have produced positive real returns as companies pass on higher prices.

A backtest of the S&P 500 using rules linking inflation to interest rates and stock values produced poor metrics, showing less money after 60 years than at the start. The post closes by promoting the blog's 1,200+ articles and compilations of backtestable trading strategies for Python.

Bibliotherapy uses books and other texts to help readers address personal, developmental, educational, or psychological concerns. Its core principles include identification with characters or situations, emotional catharsis, insight, and recognition that others share similar struggles. Developmental bibliotherapy supports students even without identified difficulties, while therapeutic bibliotherapy targets mental health concerns. Approaches include cognitive bibliotherapy using self-help or nonfiction, affective bibliotherapy using fiction or poetry, group reading, writing activities, and online platforms.

Following PRISMA-P and PICO, this systematic review searched ERIC, Elsevier, Research Gate, Google Scholar, and reference lists for English-language, peer-reviewed studies published from 2006 to 2021. Thirty-five articles using quantitative, qualitative, and mixed methods were included. Because of methodological diversity, meta-analysis was not possible; findings were synthesized thematically using NVivo 12.

Across five themes, studies generally supported bibliotherapy’s perceived usefulness and reported improvements in socio-emotional, academic, and psychological outcomes. Socio-emotional findings included reduced aggression and social anxiety, improved cooperation and socially appropriate behavior, and greater emotional awareness and social skills, although some findings for bullying, empathy, emotional and social sensitivity, and control were nonsignificant. Academic studies reported benefits for reading comprehension, vocabulary, articulation, writing, English language, and mathematics. Significant improvements were also found in general self-esteem, hope, and resilience, while some measures of confidence, competence, connectedness, caring, and social self-esteem did not improve significantly. Bibliotherapy was associated with reduced anxiety and depression and, in one study, reduced stress; it also enabled participants to discuss trauma, although it did not treat the effects of trauma.

Practitioner awareness and training varied widely, and reported challenges included insufficient time and resources, limited professional support, student reluctance or inability to read, and boredom after repeated sessions. The review also noted small samples, limited institutional coverage, insufficient reporting of methods and books used, and possible cultural differences across locations. Overall, the findings indicate potential benefits of bibliotherapy for students and vulnerable groups, while emphasizing the need for larger studies, clearer practice standards, and a unified framework.

The paper proposes Virtual Node-based Heterogeneous Graph Convolutional Network (VN-HGCN) to capture long-range information in heterogeneous graphs without predefined meta-paths, expert knowledge, or deep layer stacks that can cause over-smoothing and high computational cost. Existing approaches either depend on manually defined meta-paths, struggle to integrate distant nodes, or require many layers to reach k-hop neighbors.

VN-HGCN augments a heterogeneous graph with hierarchical virtual nodes. Each node type receives type-level virtual nodes, with original nodes randomly assigned to them, and a central virtual node connects the type-level nodes. This structure gives any two original nodes a path of length four, enabling four-layer models to aggregate information across arbitrary graph distances. Type-level virtual nodes are initialized from the mean features of their assigned nodes, the central node uses an all-ones vector, and drop-edge is used to limit overfitting.

The model projects node types into a shared semantic space using learnable transformation matrices. It then performs normalized node-level aggregation and attention-based type-level aggregation, combining intra-type and inter-type information to update embeddings. Its overall time complexity is \(O(N|A|(|V|+|E|))\), while parameter count grows linearly with nodes and node types.

A scalability experiment on DBLP showed that adding virtual nodes to ie-HGCN increased sensitivity to perturbations from distant nodes, indicating improved long-range message passing. Node-classification experiments on ACM, DBLP, and IMDB compared VN-HGCN with metapath2vec, HAN, MAGNN, HGT, HetSANN, SimpleHGN, and ie-HGCN across training ratios from 20% to 80%. VN-HGCN achieved the best results in most settings, particularly with limited training data, and outperformed all baselines on 17 of 24 ACM and DBLP metric comparisons. It also generally performed strongly on IMDB, though ie-HGCN was slightly better in some higher-training-ratio settings.

Sensitivity analysis found VN-HGCN robust to hidden-dimension and virtual-node-count changes. Performance improved from two to four layers but declined beyond four layers, consistent with over-smoothing. The authors identify extending the model to additional tasks and large-scale datasets, and determining dataset-dependent optimal virtual-node counts, as future work.

Postoperative hyperglycemia is common after cardiac surgery and is associated with infections, kidney injury, arrhythmias, longer hospitalization, and mortality, while both hyperglycemia and hypoglycemia complicate insulin management. This retrospective study developed GLUCOSE, a distributional offline reinforcement-learning model that recommends hourly regular insulin doses during the first postoperative day.

Using MIMIC-IV for development and eICU-CRD for external validation, the study included 6,148 and 649 cardiac-surgery ICU patients, respectively. GLUCOSE combined conservative Q-learning with distributional reinforcement learning and Implicit Quantile Networks, using more than 70 hourly clinical features. Recommended doses were rounded to whole units and capped at 10 units per hour. Its reward function favored glucose levels of 140–180 mg/dL and penalized values outside that range, including hypoglycemia below 70 mg/dL.

The selected model had significantly better estimated performance than observed clinician dosing in both internal testing and external validation. Glucose time in the 70–180 mg/dL range was highest when clinician-administered insulin doses matched GLUCOSE recommendations and declined as discrepancies increased. SHAP analysis identified current and recent glucose, weight, mechanical ventilation, and ventilation duration as important inputs.

In three-phase human evaluations, GLUCOSE dosing had significantly lower mean absolute error than observed clinician dosing against endocrinologists’ recommendations in both datasets. Compared with senior intensivists, junior intensivists, and nurse practitioners, differences were not statistically significant, although GLUCOSE generally had lower errors than junior clinicians and nurse practitioners. Blinded expert ratings found GLUCOSE’s safety, effectiveness, and acceptability comparable to or statistically better than all human policies, including those of senior cardiac-surgery intensivists. Recommendations were also similar in external-validation patients excluded because of ambiguous medication records, with mean differences under 0.5 unit.

Limitations include the retrospective design, validation only during the first postoperative day, absence of dietary data, and exclusion of 4,838 eICU patients with ambiguous medication records. Prospective studies and randomized trials are needed to establish clinical effectiveness and safety.

The paper introduces SimulRAG, a retrieval-augmented generation framework for grounding large language models in long-form scientific question answering using scientific simulators. Its simulator retrieval interface converts between textual and numerical modalities by combining an open-ended question with a simulator handbook, extracting relevant parameters, executing the simulator, and formatting outputs as textual context through templates.

SimulRAG generates multiple diverse answers, decomposes them into atomic claims, and merges duplicate claims. It uses claim-level uncertainty estimation based on semantic entailment graphs and closeness centrality, combined with simulator boundary assessment (UE+SBA), to select only uncertain claims that fall within the simulator’s operational limits. Selected claims are checked against simulation context: aligned claims are retained, contradicted claims are updated, and indeterminate claims remain unchanged. High-confidence claims are then integrated into the final answer.

The authors construct benchmarks for climate modeling and epidemiology, with 200 free-form questions each. The climate benchmark uses a CMIP6-trained emulator with greenhouse and aerosol gas inputs and surface temperature output; the epidemiology benchmark uses GLEAM-AI to model seasonal U.S. influenza transmission. Questions and answers are generated from simulator templates, plausible parameter sampling, and simulation outputs, with simulator-derived ground truth and human verification.

Experiments with GPT-4o and Claude-3.5 Sonnet show that SimulRAG outperforms adapted input-layer and output-layer RAG baselines, producing 30.4% more unique true claims on average and 16.3% higher factuality than the best baseline. UE+SBA outperforms random, verbalized-uncertainty, and uncertainty-only claim selection across F1, AUPR, and AUROC, with absolute AUPR and AUROC gains of up to 6.2% and 6.3%. Simulator boundary assessment filters an average of 34.5% of climate claims and 41% of epidemiology claims that simulators cannot verify. Ablations show that verifying 15% of claims already outperforms no RAG, while 45% is comparable to verifying all claims. A stated limitation is that SimulRAG assumes each question is relevant to an available simulator; future work could add automatic question-simulator relevance detection.

The address frames post–World War readjustment as a global and domestic challenge. The speaker argues that a just new order requires broad participation, preserves the worthwhile achievements of prewar civilization, and prevents renewed conflict. Domestically, the United States must address interconnected social, financial, and economic problems, beginning with agriculture and transportation.

Farmers face severe hardship from deflation and inadequate transportation. Congress should enlarge federal credit facilities through the Farm Loan Bureau, including production and livestock loans and higher land-loan limits, while recognizing that stable agricultural prosperity also requires cheaper and more reliable transportation.

Railroad capacity is described as inadequate and potentially paralyzed. Needed measures include coordinating rail, maritime, inland-waterway, and motor-truck transportation; using trucks as feeders rather than competitors; reducing freight rates; improving intercarrier cooperation; pooling freight cars under a central agency; and increasing railway efficiency. Government operation is rejected as a solution. The partisan Railroad Labor Board should be replaced by a labor division within the Interstate Commerce Commission, with regional representation, enforceable decisions, and prior negotiation between railroads and employees. Labor should receive fair wages and just working conditions, but service essential to the public must not be interrupted.

The newly enacted tariff law should retain flexible duties so rates can respond to changing conditions, protect domestic industry, avoid consumer exploitation, and preserve beneficial trade. Internationally, the United States should use its position as a creditor nation to assist currency stabilization and commerce without dictating policy or assuming responsibilities belonging to other nations. It should support naval limitation, peaceful consultation, and international understanding while resisting a supergovernment or armed alliances, asserting American rights without denying those of others.

On domestic policy, the speaker calls for stronger enforcement of the Eighteenth Amendment, cooperation between federal and state authorities, alien registration, and screening immigrants before departure. Education for newcomers should be expanded to promote Americanization. Constitutional amendments are recommended to authorize federal regulation of child labor and restrict tax-exempt securities. Additional priorities include reclamation and irrigation, forest protection and replanting, study of the coal problem, narrowing the gap between production costs and consumer prices, further development of superpower systems, and surveying national resources for defense.

ADF&G in Dillingham received reports of a fox acting aggressively along Wood River Road, biting a car fender and foaming at the mouth. Biologist Neil Barten said the signs suggest rabies, urging people to avoid such foxes and update their dogs' rabies vaccinations.

Federal agents from the FBI, IRS and HUD searched Cleveland City Hall and seized records concerning city engineering and construction manager Khalil Ewais, his side business Pioneer Engineering, and paving contractor Burton Scot Contractors. Authorities have not disclosed the raid’s purpose, citing an ongoing investigation and sealed federal court records. Ewais’s personnel file showed he tried to resign in 2015, citing low pay and expanded duties, then rescinded after supervisors promised staffing changes and consideration of a raise. In 2017, he denied having a financial interest in city dealings. Cleveland said it was evaluating his work assignments after the raid.

Morgan Stanley expects FAANG stocks’ exceptional 2017 gains to moderate rather than repeat fully or collapse, while retaining an overweight rating due to their competitive moats. The five stocks drove 27.5% of S&P 500 market-cap growth, a bull-market concentration surpassed only in 1999 and 2004. High valuations, volatility, and exposure to consumer spending and advertising leave them vulnerable to cyclical pressure. Amazon’s scenarios range from nearly 10% growth to over 70%.

An October 2001 email circulated an article by Arundhati Roy titled “Brutality smeared in peanut butter,” urging the United States to end the war in Afghanistan. Roy argues that the U.S.-led air campaign, launched October 7 without a UN mandate, was not justified revenge for September 11 but another act of terrorism that killed civilians and increased fear and hysteria.

She criticizes the coalition’s portrayal of itself as peace-loving while citing America’s repeated military interventions abroad, support for dictators, weapons production, and history of invasion. She also acknowledges the Taliban’s brutality toward Afghans and women, describing its rulers as products of decades of war, poverty, foreign arms, and the Cold War. She questions whether the Northern Alliance, composed largely of warlords and former combatants, represents a humane alternative and criticizes plans to restore Afghanistan’s former monarchy.

The article emphasizes the humanitarian crisis: blocked roads, closed borders, food shortages, and the risk of starvation among millions of Afghans. It describes U.S. air-dropped food packets as inadequate, dangerous because of landmines, and symbolic of a public-relations effort that ignored local conditions and Afghan dignity.

Roy contends that terrorism and freedom fighter are inconsistently defined, noting that governments and intelligence agencies have armed and supported insurgents when politically useful. She warns that exploiting religious and communal anger, expanding surveillance, suppressing anti-war speech, and restricting media access will intensify hatred and undermine civil liberties. She also links continued warfare to defense, oil, and media interests, including U.S. access to Afghan and Caspian energy resources.

Calling the conflict a “spiralling morass of terror and brutality,” Roy urges governments to show honesty and humility and explicitly demands that the war stop before further death, displacement, repression, and cultural destruction occur.

An analysis by Notre Dame law professor Derek Muller found that attorneys and staff at the 100 top-grossing law firms and 50 larger plaintiffs-side firms directed 92.45% of campaign contributions to Democrats in 2023–2024—about $52 million versus $4 million for Republicans. The roughly 12-to-1 Democratic advantage rose from 6-to-1 for 2017–2020. Cleary Gottlieb had the highest Democratic contribution rate among top-grossing firms at 99.7%, while Nelson Mullins had the lowest at 66.4%.

The Missouri Court of Appeals (Western District) affirmed the judgment for Annetta Gibson in her suit for specific performance of a property settlement agreement with former husband Max Gibson, ordering him to delete from an insurance trust a provision allowing him to borrow, pledge, or use the cash value of the policies, and to pay her attorney fees and costs.

Under the settlement, incorporated into the dissolution decree, Max was to pay $2,000 monthly until 1987 and $1,800 monthly until 2000, with payments continuing after his death, secured by term insurance of $200,000, later modified by the parties to $180,000 in whole life policies. He executed the trust in February 1981 but retained the cash-value provision.

The court rejected Max's five contentions. Removing the provision did not create a new agreement but enforced his promise of security, since use of cash value could impair the policies' protection. Annetta pleaded the same agreement she sought to enforce. Venue was proper in Platte County because the parties contractually waived the privilege of venue, and the dissolution action was brought there. A claim against Max's estate was not an adequate legal remedy. Because Max did not perform and the agreement provided for indemnification including attorney fees, the fee award was proper.

USD/CAD remains range-bound between 1.2968 and 1.3211 with neutral intraday bias and a mixed near-term outlook. A break above 1.3387 would favor 1.3598 and higher; below 1.2968, the outlook turns bearish, with 1.2460 breaking targeting 1.2075. The broader trend is seen as corrective.

The lecture examines TaintDroid, an Android information-flow system designed to prevent sensitive data from leaving smartphones. Traditional Android permissions are device-oriented and cannot precisely restrict data flows; policies combining sensitive-data access with network access would break legitimate apps and fail against side channels, app collusion, and deceptive intents. Real-world mobile malware may misuse location, IMEI, contacts, phone numbers, or credentials, and may turn phones into spam bots.

TaintDroid labels sensitive sources such as GPS, sensors, contacts, and IMEI, tracks their taint through Dalvik VM instructions, and treats the network as a sink. It uses a 32-bit label, supporting up to 32 taint sources, and combines labels through bitwise unions. Taint is tracked for local variables, arguments, fields, arrays, IPC messages, and files. Arrays, messages, and files receive conservative aggregate labels, while native methods require manually defined propagation policies because their internals are opaque to the interpreter. Taint metadata is stored near the associated variables for efficiency. Reported overhead is approximately 3–5% additional RAM and 3–29% additional CPU.

At network interfaces, TaintDroid can block tainted data, alert the user, or remove sensitive fields. Evaluation found apps sending location, phone numbers, and other data to remote servers without clearly disclosing that behavior. The system is not a complete defense: it does not prevent initial compromise, can miss implicit flows through branches or opaque native code, and may block legitimate activity through conservative labeling.

Tracking taint at x86 or ARM level would cover native code more comprehensively but introduces substantial complexity, cost, false positives, and “taint explosion,” in which overly conservative labels contaminate most program state. More expressive systems allow programmers to define labels and use static analysis to detect information leaks, though dynamic enforcement can itself create covert channels.

TightLip extends limited taint tracking to legacy applications without modifying them. It creates scrubbed copies of sensitive files and runs parallel “doppelganger” processes using that data, comparing their system calls with those of the original process. Divergence—especially an attempted network call—can trigger an alert. Its effectiveness depends on accurate, file-specific scrubbers; incomplete scrubbing can cause missed leaks or process failures.

Suzuka practice began dry and bright, though damp patches remained after earlier rain. Fernando Alonso received a 25-place grid penalty following an engine change after a hydraulic leak, joining penalized teammates Carlos Sainz and Valtteri Bottas. Sebastian Vettel also tested the gearbox used in his collision with Lance Stroll.

Lewis Hamilton and Bottas initially dominated the timesheets on soft tires, while Red Bull used different setups. Bottas later ran wide at Spoon, damaging his front wing and puncturing his right-rear tire; the floor was also damaged, ending his session. A second red flag followed Kimi Raikkonen’s barrier crash at Degner, which caused significant right-side damage and disrupted several drivers’ qualifying simulations.

Bottas finished practice fastest, ahead of Hamilton, Vettel, Max Verstappen, Daniel Ricciardo, Esteban Ocon, Nico Hulkenberg, Alonso, Sergio Perez and Jolyon Palmer. Magnussen missed much of the session because of a hydraulic issue, while Grosjean was the last driver to set a time.

The “Box & One – Chase” offense is designed to limit a star player’s touches and create scoring opportunities through coordinated screening and cutting. Its primary option is the Shuffle Cut: a high-post back screen frees the star player, while the ball handler penetrates. If the star does not receive the ball, the offense can flow into Screen & Roll, Base Screen, Back Screen, Give & Go, or Single/Double continuity actions.

Success depends on proper timing, communication, defensive recognition, and execution of mid screens, base screens, and post-ups. Coaches should scout opponents when possible, identify matchups and anticipated defensive reads, explain counters, and adjust during games. Players should vary alignments and entries, move the ball to weaker defenders, and use drills, scrimmages, and the Whole-Part-Whole teaching method to build habits.

In the Box & One defense, four defenders guard areas in a box zone, while the “Chaser” focuses exclusively on aggressive pass denial and prevents the offensive player from receiving the ball or grabbing a rebound.

The 52-week high is the highest daily closing price a stock has reached during a full 52-week trading period. The 52-week low is the corresponding lowest close, and together they form a range whose upper and lower boundaries serve as resistance and support. Intraday prices that cross these levels do not create new highs or lows unless the stock closes beyond them. Traders use the high to assess a stock’s current position and calculate its percentage below the high: (Current Price − 52-Week High) ÷ 52-Week High.

The 52-week high strategy buys stocks trading near their annual highs rather than following the conventional “buy low, sell high” approach. Academic research cited in the passage indicates that stocks near their 52-week highs have better subsequent returns than those farther away, although gains may require time. A separate momentum backtest reportedly outperformed the S&P 500 over two decades. However, two moving-average crossover strategies tested on SPY produced unappealing equity curves and were considered poorly tradable. The authors suggest that the market-weighted S&P 500 may not adequately reflect results found among individual stocks.

A New York Times report said Rose McGowan received a $100,000 confidential settlement from Harvey Weinstein in 1997 after a Sundance hotel-room incident. Ashley Judd accused Weinstein of inappropriate conduct, and he subsequently took leave from his company.

The Department of Energy awarded nearly $67 million for 85 nuclear research projects at university and government laboratories to advance safety, efficiency, and U.S. energy independence. Funding includes more than $31 million for 32 university-led projects across 23 states and $6 million shared by 19 universities to improve reactor safety and performance. Since 2009, the Office of Nuclear Energy has awarded about $472 million to 103 colleges and universities for research and nuclear workforce development.

The Patient Charter, part of the NHS Constitution, sets out patients’ legal rights, NHS pledges beyond legal requirements, and patients’ responsibilities. It emphasizes access to care free at the point of use in most cases, nondiscriminatory treatment, waiting-time standards, and explanations and alternatives when standards are not met. Patients are entitled to care from qualified staff in safe settings, nutritious hospital food and hydration, continuous improvement, access to NICE-recommended medicines and treatments where clinically appropriate, evidence-based local funding decisions with explanations, and routine vaccinations.

The Charter also protects the right to consent to or refuse treatment, receive clear information about risks and benefits, have information kept private, choose a GP, compare services, participate in treatment decisions, and be told openly—with facts, an apology, and support—when errors occur. Patients may complain, seek Ombudsman involvement, request judicial review of unlawful decisions, and seek compensation for harm caused by negligence.

Patients are expected to look after their health where possible, respect staff and others, follow or discuss treatment plans, and participate in vaccination and screening. The Charter presents the NHS as a partnership providing safe, timely, fair, and respectful care through shared responsibility.

A registered dietitian rejects no-fruit diet hype, calling fruit nutrient-dense and rich in antioxidants, vitamins, and phytonutrients. Though higher in carbs and natural sugars, fruit provides far more nutritional value than calorie-dense foods. For weight loss, consider quality, portions, and glycemic index; fruit should be eaten daily.

Lorna Gibson concludes a lecture on biomimicry, highlighting how natural cellular structures inspire lightweight, strong, and stiff engineering materials. Examples include wood-based silicon carbide composites, 3D-printed fiber-reinforced honeycombs, foamed metals resembling trabecular bone, synthetic tissue-engineering scaffolds, lightweight sandwich panels, and palm-inspired concrete density gradients. Natural stems, quills, feathers, and beaks with dense outer shells and foam-like cores resist wrinkling and buckling while reducing weight; German and Japanese groups have developed comparable composite structures.

The class then reviews course material for a Wednesday test, during which students may bring one 8.5-by-11-inch cheat sheet. Key topics include open-cell foam and honeycomb equations, thermal conductivity, trabecular bone, sandwich panels, and energy absorption. Questions address interpreting foam energy-absorption graphs and constructing idealized aluminum-foam stress-strain curves for different densities. Gibson also announces a Monday talk about becoming a professor, collection of projects on Wednesday, and possible future talks by other MIT faculty.

News reports from November 22, 2001, described Enron in severe financial distress. Its shares fell 28% to $5.01, their lowest close since 1989 and about 94% below the prior year’s level, while its bonds also traded at steep discounts. Enron had disclosed a $690 million debt payment due after its credit rating was lowered, along with $9.15 billion due for repayment or refinancing by the end of 2002. Rating agencies warned that bankruptcy was possible if Dynegy abandoned its proposed roughly $9 billion acquisition or if trading partners continued reducing their exposure. The SEC was investigating transactions involving Enron and partnerships headed by former CFO Andrew Fastow, while earnings restatements removed more than $580 million in reported income.

Enron obtained a three-week extension of the $690 million payment to mid-December and drew the remaining $450 million of a $1 billion credit line. Banks and investors discussed possible equity investments of up to $2 billion, including financing for Enron’s Transwestern Pipeline. Dynegy continued regulatory work on its merger but considered whether to seek changes, although it had no clear legal basis to terminate unilaterally. ChevronTexaco, which owned 26% of Dynegy, supported completion.

Enron’s employee retirement plan was heavily exposed to company stock. It held $2.1 billion in assets at the end of 2000, more than half in Enron shares, and workers were unable to switch investments after the plan was frozen on October 17. Some Portland General employees reportedly lost hundreds of thousands of dollars, and nearly all Enron stock options had become worthless. A class-action lawsuit alleged that Enron violated its fiduciary duties by freezing the plan and promoting the overvalued stock. Enron said the freeze resulted from an administrative change and that employees themselves selected 89% of the Enron stock in the plan. Chairman Kenneth Lay’s sizable stock-option earnings, contrasted with employee losses, also drew attention.

Trading partners were demanding more collateral and scaling back business as Enron’s cash reserves and transaction volumes declined. Goldman Sachs downgraded both Enron and Dynegy, calling the proposed $1.5 billion cash infusion inadequate to restore customer confidence. Enron was also preparing to sell assets, including its 65% controlling interest in India’s Dabhol Power project and its Wessex Water unit in England. Enron Japan was reviewing its operations and considering retaining or selling part of the business; its yen bonds and their exposure to Japanese money-market funds added to concerns about the crisis.

Enron’s shares led declines in a broader U.S. stock-market retreat, as investors took profits before Thanksgiving and technology weakness dragged down the Dow, S&P 500, and Nasdaq. The S&P 500’s price-earnings ratio was near 30, largely because corporate earnings were falling and long-term interest rates were lower.

California’s recreational marijuana launch has been hindered by complex regulations, slow municipal licensing and high taxes. Recreational dispensary sales reached $339 million through February 2018, below expectations, while an estimated 85–90% of the existing industry remained unlicensed. With many local bans and limited geographic coverage, the black market persists. Some dispensaries face effective tax rates near 80%, raising prices and profits pressure. Earlier legalization states offer lessons; Colorado’s tax revenue initially fell short but later exceeded projections each year.

Long COVID comprises new, returning, or ongoing health problems occurring four or more weeks after SARS-CoV-2 infection and can follow mild or severe disease. Vaccination has high effectiveness against severe outcomes, although susceptibility and long COVID persist, and vaccinated individuals often report symptom improvement. A case-control study aimed to examine epidemiological data and risk factors for long COVID among healthcare workers at Hospital Israelita Albert Einstein in Brazil from March 2020 to July 2022. Eligible workers had symptomatic, RT-PCR-confirmed COVID-19 and 180-day follow-up. Cases had compatible symptoms lasting over four weeks without another diagnosis; controls recovered within four weeks. Symptoms included general, respiratory, cardiac, neurological, digestive, and musculoskeletal complaints. Oxford-AstraZeneca, CoronaVac, Pfizer/BioNTech, and Janssen vaccines were available during the study.

HeartLands Conservancy is leading watershed planning for the Cahokia Creek area of western Madison County, partnering with Madison County and the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers. The project will create plans addressing stormwater, flooding and water quality in the Indian Creek and Canteen Creek watersheds, which include Edwardsville and Glen Carbon and drain to the Mississippi River. Community open houses gathered input to identify priority projects and funding needs, including infrastructure, land management, flooding, pollution, mining subsidence, and recreational and wildlife concerns.

A 10-year-old PGI school student reported that youths in a black car allegedly tried to abduct her near a Vekra booth. Police registered a precautionary DDR and investigated, but nearby residents denied observing an attempt. The report came four days after a similar February 9 kidnapping attempt on another student, prompting the school to request regular PCR patrols near the campus.

Alabama has a flash flood watch until 7 p.m. as saturated ground and tropical moisture support heavy showers and thunderstorms today. Scattered storms may continue Tuesday, with a marginal severe-weather risk in northern Alabama and highs of 85–88°F. Friday and the weekend will be partly sunny with afternoon storms and highs near 90°F. Drier weather is expected next week, with possible storms later. No Atlantic tropical storms are expected for seven days.

Belgium’s controversial 18-10 win over Spain secured Romania’s qualification for the 2019 Rugby World Cup, while Spain faces Portugal in a home-and-away playoff. The winner will join Canada, an African team, and Hong Kong or Tahiti in November’s four-team repechage, whose winner enters Pool B in Japan. World Rugby is reviewing the use of Romanian officials.

U.S. stocks stayed near record highs and bond yields rose Wednesday as stronger-than-expected retail sales and the highest consumer inflation since March 2012 gave the Federal Reserve more leeway to increase rates. The S&P 500 was nearly flat, while the Dow and Nasdaq edged higher. Treasury yields climbed after the reports, and dividend-focused utilities, REITs and telecom stocks weakened. European and Asian markets mostly gained, the dollar strengthened, and commodities were mixed.

A May 21, 2001 IEP News email compiled media coverage of California’s electricity crisis, including soaring power costs, projected summer shortages, rolling blackouts, and residential rate increases. California accelerated power-plant permitting but expected only 2,500 megawatts online by July, half the governor’s target. The state purchased power for utilities, planned $13.4 billion in revenue bonds, considered advance blackout schedules, and promoted conservation through programs distributing 1.5 million compact fluorescent bulbs.

State and federal investigators examined whether generators used shutdowns and rapid output changes to create artificial shortages and raise prices. PUC testimony cited maintenance records showing some production cuts lacked valid reasons, while industry sources described output “ramping.” Generators denied manipulation, attributing outages and fluctuations to aging plants, breakdowns, demand, gas costs, and grid instructions. FERC required justification of $124 million in charges and reached an $8 million settlement.

Other coverage focused on Gov. Gray Davis’s dispute with the Bush administration over price caps and federal assistance, Energy Secretary Spencer Abraham’s effort to promote the administration’s energy plan, and declining public confidence in California’s economy and leaders. The state controller was scheduled to disclose details and costs of long-term power contracts, while businesses showed increased interest in backup electrical systems.

Soccer coaches should prepare players for varied field and weather conditions and inspect fields before each match to identify hazards and determine whether play is safe. Surface type affects ball speed, bounce, footing, visibility, equipment, and tactics. Artificial turf produces faster ball movement, lighter ground passes, and greater heat exposure, requiring hydration, shorter warm-ups, fitness, and monitoring for heat exhaustion. High crowns can obscure the ball and increase ground-ball speed. Rubber or cork infill should generally be ignored, while eye contamination requires prompt removal and attention from a trainer. Natural ground conditions affect cleat selection: hard surfaces increase bounce and distance, while soft surfaces slow the ball. Tall grass slows play and may cause cramping, so ground passes require more weight. On sloped fields, choosing to attack downhill in the second half may provide an advantage.

Wet fields cause fast, skipping balls. Receivers must turn their hips, square their bodies to the ball’s path, and keep their legs together; goalkeepers must practice low, fast shots, avoid drop kicks, and keep dry gloves. Attackers should shoot low and frequently and send through balls early. Large areas of standing water, especially near goals, generally indicate an unplayable field requiring postponement and consultation with officials or administrators.

Field anomalies can create abnormal bounces, poor traction, and injury hazards. Hard dirt increases bounce and ball speed, soft dirt reduces bounce and may cause slips, grass clumps cause irregular hops and deflections, and uneven ground requires warnings about dangerous areas and unpredictable bounces. Balls stick in puddles and must be lifted out with the instep. Mud traps cleats, while small ice areas should be broken up and covered and large areas make fields unplayable. Rocks, gravel, repairs, exposed sprinkler heads, worn artificial surfaces, split seams, and baseball pitching mounds require removal, covering, repair, or cancellation. Fallen trees also render fields unplayable.

Field dimensions range from 50 by 100 yards to 100 by 130 yards, with many professional fields near 75 by 120 yards. Players must adapt to field size: long fields require greater fitness and more weight on long passes, short fields call for earlier and less forceful attacking passes, wide fields require more weight on wide deliveries, and narrow fields favor shorter passing and smaller-group tactics. Large and small fields combine these respective adjustments.

Coaches must monitor forecasts and use weather alerts and radar. Severe storms require cancellation. Lightning demands immediate evacuation to cars or buildings, not trees or canopies, and thunder requires at least a 30-minute wait before play resumes. Cold temperatures around or below 40°F require suitable warm clothing, while hydration remains necessary in winter. Dew, fog, and frost can create wet-field conditions. High heat and humidity can cause dehydration, cramps, heat exhaustion, fainting, and life-threatening heat stroke, requiring hydration, vigilance, and possible postponement or abandonment. Light rain has limited impact until intensity or field wetness increases. Snow can make a field unplayable when it accumulates or obscures lines, although packed snow may remain playable with contrasting lines and a bright ball. Strong wind requires adjustments based on field orientation, including changes to pass height, pace, shooting, crossing, goalkeeper positioning, and possibly the second-half direction.

Referee administration also affects play. Coaches should have procedures for absent officials, and players must treat rebounds from officials as live balls while inside the field. Players should play to the whistle, avoid emotional reactions to disputed calls, and not assume an assistant referee’s offside decision.

Perimeter hazards include advertising boards, fences, drainage ditches, culverts, tracks, sidewalks, spectators, branches, and thrown objects. Coaches should inspect and mark these areas, warn players to walk across tracks in cleats, teach players not to react to abusive spectators, and require immediate reporting of dangerous conduct or objects. Crowd noise becomes problematic when it prevents verbal communication, in which case non-verbal communication should be used.

Sunlight, shadows, floodlights, and glare can impair vision. Players should use eye-black strips, caps, peripheral vision, and eye protection as appropriate, while coaches should account for abrupt shadow transitions and possible lighting failures. Games should not begin in darkness or continue when goals are not visible from the center mark.

Goals must be securely anchored and free from structural failure, or the field is unplayable. Missing corner flags should be replaced by cones, and nets must be checked and secured. Players must understand rebound differences among goal shapes and any local rules governing combination soccer and football goals.

All game balls should match in size, make, model, and pressure. Defective, incorrectly sized, slippery, or waterlogged balls must be removed and replaced; a match should be abandoned if no alternative ball is available. Extra balls must be cleared before restarts. Players should also understand how “light,” “heavy,” and “sticky” balls behave.

Players must know the required field markings and how to handle missing, multiple-color, non-parallel, or wavy lines. Coaches can use cones, saucers, paint, markers, and string, and must inform players and the referee of the chosen procedure.

Coaching recommendations include rehearsing adverse conditions during practice, demonstrating proper clothing, establishing a thorough pre-game inspection routine, knowing local rules and field-status information, selecting which goal to defend according to conditions, maintaining hydration in cold weather, changing wet clothing promptly, and applying the same safety precautions at practices as during matches.

At NVIDIA Corporation’s May 23, 2017 annual meeting, stockholders elected 12 directors to one-year terms ending at the 2018 annual meeting. They also approved advisory votes on named executive officer compensation and the frequency of that advisory vote, with the plurality favoring annual voting. Consequently, NVIDIA will provide an annual advisory vote on executive compensation. Stockholders ratified PricewaterhouseCoopers LLP as NVIDIA’s independent accounting firm for the fiscal year ending January 28, 2018.

The coach said the team did not play well enough to win, noting it killed five power plays but also conceded a shorthanded goal and struggled to generate offense and second-chance opportunities. He accepted the officiating overall but questioned several calls, particularly one involving Clifton and Tarasenko. He said Stanley Cup contention motivates the players and that the team must remain confident it can win despite injuries. With Z and Griz potentially unavailable, Boston must replace their contributions, improve puck movement and scoring, and possibly use seven defensemen. He said the matchup is harder without Z but noted that Z and Chris could return, so no final decisions would be made yet. Line combinations may be adjusted to improve production without disrupting existing chemistry; Krejci is receptive to changes, Jake should use his speed inside, and Backes should remain complementary. The team must respond after the loss by creating more inside chances, recovering pucks, and converting opportunities.

Ready despite a bruise, the speaker is encouraged by a promising young player. He sees a bright future and advises both teams to keep it simple, watch for unpredictable bounces, and make strong plays.

China’s first-quarter GDP grew 6.9%, exceeding expectations and the government’s 6.5% target, but the author questions its accuracy. Industrial production had been unusually stable at 6%–6.3% for eleven months before reaching 7.6% in March 2017, coinciding with exports turning positive. The author speculates that production was previously overstated and that the recent surge may be temporary, as similar export-driven spikes have not been sustained. Retail sales remained around historical averages, while state-enterprise capital spending continued to grow at double digits; private and total fixed-asset investment stayed subdued. Overall, China may have avoided immediate contraction amid a global pause, but the statistics do not demonstrate renewed or durable growth. The author therefore considers the industrial-production increase meaningfully positive only if it begins a sustained acceleration, which the broader data make unlikely.

The Senate rejected rival Republican and Democratic stopgap funding bills for the sixth time, extending the government shutdown into its second week. The GOP bill, which would fund the government through Nov. 21, failed 54-45, while the Democratic alternative, including more than $1 trillion in health-care funding and an extension of enhanced Affordable Care Act subsidies, failed 47-52. Republicans need about eight Democratic votes to overcome the filibuster. Both parties’ leaders blamed each other for the shutdown, which began Oct. 1. The White House warned that federal workers could be fired or denied back pay if the shutdown continues, while House Speaker Mike Johnson said federal law requires furloughed workers to be paid when they return.

This study compared REM sleep microstructure using video-polysomnography in 20 patients with isolated REM sleep behavior disorder (iRBD), 20 patients with Parkinson’s disease and RBD (PD+RBD), and 20 age- and sex-matched controls. REM sleep without atonia was highest in iRBD, intermediate in PD+RBD, and nearly absent in controls. The phasic REM proportion was increased in iRBD but not PD+RBD. Compared with controls, PD+RBD patients had less REM sleep, longer REM latency, more frequent but shorter REM bouts, lower sawtooth-wave density and duration, and greater shifts in sawtooth-wave spectra toward higher frequencies. Both patient groups showed less predominance of low-frequency sawtooth activity than controls, with the strongest alteration in PD+RBD. NREM-to-REM transition duration increased progressively from controls to iRBD to PD+RBD. Controls predominantly showed atonia onset before sawtooth waves, whereas both patient groups more often showed sawtooth waves preceding atonia. These findings indicate that RBD-related abnormalities extend beyond loss of muscle atonia and dream enactment to broader REM microstructural changes. Limitations include small samples, no PD-without-RBD group, medication and control-group heterogeneity, limited EEG montage coverage, and the time-consuming manual analysis of sawtooth waves. Longitudinal studies are needed to determine whether these measures predict phenoconversion.

Lorna Gibson reviews and derives the in-plane behavior of hexagonal honeycombs. Their elastic moduli and Poisson’s ratios are described, along with three compressive plateau mechanisms: elastic buckling, plastic yielding or collapse, and brittle crushing. For brittle honeycombs, cell walls fail by bending; equating the applied and fracture moments gives a brittle-crushing stress proportional to the cell-wall modulus of rupture times \(t/l^2\), with a geometric factor of \(4/9\) for regular hexagons.

In tension, hexagonal honeycombs have the same elastic moduli as in compression. Elastomeric honeycombs do not buckle in tension, while yielding honeycombs have nearly equal tensile and compressive plastic plateaus. A fracture-toughness model for brittle honeycombs assumes a crack much larger than the cell size, continuum behavior, negligible axial forces, bending-dominated deformation, and constant cell-wall rupture strength. Balancing the crack-tip stress field with cell-wall fracture gives a toughness proportional to the wall’s modulus of rupture times \(t/l\), making toughness dependent on cell size.

Triangular honeycombs deform primarily through axial forces and behave like pin-jointed trusses. Their modulus scales as \(t/l\), rather than \(t/l^3\) for bending-dominated hexagonal honeycombs; for equilateral triangular cells, the geometry constant is 1.15.

The lecture then addresses the five out-of-plane elastic constants of orthotropic hexagonal honeycombs. Because out-of-plane loading extends or contracts cell walls axially, the transverse Young’s modulus scales as \(E_s t/l\) and is approximately the solid modulus times relative density. The transverse Poisson ratios equal the solid Poisson ratio, while reciprocal transverse ratios are small for low relative density. The shear moduli also scale approximately as \(t/l\); for regular hexagons, \(G_{13}\) is estimated as \(G_s t/l/\sqrt{3}\). Thus, out-of-plane properties are much stiffer and stronger than in-plane properties, which depend on bending and scale as \(t/l^3\).

Approximate out-of-plane compressive-strength calculations use plate buckling and plastic-hinge work balances. For regular hexagonal honeycombs, elastic buckling gives approximately \(5.2E_s(t/l)^3\). Plastic buckling is estimated as \(2\sigma_y(t/l)^2\), compared with an exact value of \(5.6\sigma_y(t/l)^{5/3}\) that includes neighboring-cell constraints.

Out-of-plane brittle tensile failure is also modeled. Without wall cracks, fracture strength equals relative density times the solid’s fracture strength. For cracks much larger than the cells, the energy-release rate and fracture toughness scale with the solid fraction and relative density, respectively. Out-of-plane brittle crushing strength equals relative density times the cell-wall compressive strength, typically about 12 times the relative density times the wall’s modulus of rupture.

The lecture concludes that these honeycomb models provide the basis for subsequent foam modeling and introduces wood and cork as natural cellular materials for later discussion.

The speaker praised Paul for returning after an unseen hit left him on the ice, calling him a leader and competitor, and called his goal huge. They note recent years have been tough and that winning Game 1 of the Stanley Cup more than makes up for it. The speaker values sharing the opportunity with longtime teammates and mentions another long flight tomorrow.

The Delaware Supreme Court reversed the Superior Court’s denial of workers’ compensation benefits to Cheryl Tickles and remanded the case to the Board. Tickles fell on ice in Building 103’s parking lot after arriving early to use an employee-only ATM before her shift at Building 400. The Court held that the parking lot constituted PNC’s premises for purposes of the exception to the “going and coming” rule and that Tickles’s ATM use was a reasonable preparatory act incident to employment. Her injury therefore arose out of and in the course of her employment and was compensable.

Turing introduces a redesigned streaming multiprocessor (SM) with unified L1 cache and shared memory, allowing flexible allocation between them, doubling L1 hit bandwidth per TPC versus Pascal, and increasing L2 capacity. Together, the SM changes deliver 50% more performance per CUDA core. Enhanced Tensor Cores support FP16, INT8, and INT4, enabling accelerated neural-network matrix operations and NVIDIA NGX services such as Deep Learning Super Sampling (DLSS), AI InPainting, AI Super Rez, and AI Slow-Mo. DLSS uses trained neural networks to produce image quality similar to temporal anti-aliasing with roughly half the shading work; DLSS 2X approaches 64× supersampled quality.

The Tesla T4 uses a reduced TU104 configuration with 2,560 CUDA Cores and 320 Tensor Cores. It supports up to 130 INT8 TOPS and 260 INT4 TOPS, while offering up to 40 times the inference performance and more than 50 times the energy efficiency of CPU-based inference. Its 16 GB of memory and 320 GB/s bandwidth double the capacity and nearly double the bandwidth of the Tesla P4. Turing also improves multi-process service, video decoding, and memory sizing for data-center workloads.

Turing is the first GPU architecture to use GDDR6 memory, signaling at 14 Gbps with 20% better power efficiency than Pascal’s GDDR5X. Redesigned interfaces and package optimizations reduce signal crosstalk, clock gating lowers idle power, and improved compression combined with higher raw bandwidth produces 50% greater effective bandwidth than Pascal. TU102 includes 6 MB of L2 cache, twice that of GP102.

The display engine supports DisplayPort 1.4a, two 8K displays at 60 Hz, visually lossless Display Stream Compression, HDR processing, and BT.2100 tone mapping. NVENC adds HEVC 8K encoding at 30 fps with up to 25% bitrate savings, while NVDEC adds HEVC 4:4:4 and higher-bit-depth VP9 support. VirtualLink provides display, power, and headset data over one USB-C connector, simplifying VR connections and enabling VR on smaller devices. Turing TU102 and TU104 also use second-generation NVLink for SLI transfers, supporting two-way configurations and higher-bandwidth display topologies.

Dedicated RT Cores in every SM accelerate bounding-volume-hierarchy traversal and ray-triangle intersection tests. Combined with advanced denoising and hybrid rendering, they bring real-time ray tracing to a single GPU and deliver more than 10 billion rays per second versus approximately 1.1 billion rays per second in software-based Pascal ray tracing. Rasterization remains effective for visibility and primary rays, while ray tracing adds physically correct reflections, refractions, shadows, and indirect lighting. RT Cores perform intersection work while shader threads handle ray generation, shading, and other graphics or compute tasks; the driver manages BVH building and refitting.

Turing also adds mesh shading through cooperative task and mesh shaders. This reduces CPU draw-call bottlenecks, allows dynamic level-of-detail selection and geometry manipulation, and can render more than an order of magnitude more objects at real-time frame rates. Variable Rate Shading controls shading independently from visibility in 16×16-pixel regions, supporting content-adaptive, motion-adaptive, foveated, and multisample-based shading strategies. Texture Space Shading computes and stores shading in texture space, allowing reuse across pixels and frames, temporal stability, multiresolution control, and more efficient stereo VR rendering. Multi-View Rendering processes up to four views per hardware pass and up to 32 views through the API, supporting stereo, shadow maps, multiple instances, and view-dependent attributes while sharing independent work.

Turing’s TU104 contains 48 SMs, 3,072 CUDA Cores, 368 Tensor Cores, 48 RT Cores, and 13.6 billion transistors. The Tesla T4 enables 40 of those SMs. TU106 contains 36 SMs, 2,304 CUDA Cores, 288 Tensor Cores, and 36 RT Cores, but does not support NVLink or SLI. The RTX-OPS metric combines tensor, FP32, RT, and INT32 throughput according to measured workload utilization; for the RTX 2080 Ti, the document calculates 78 RTX-OPS.

Ray-traced shadows reproduce contact hardening from area lights, ray-traced ambient occlusion improves geometric definition, and ray-traced reflections avoid limitations of screen-space methods and static probes. Denoising reduces the number of rays required while maintaining image quality. BVH structures reduce the number of triangle tests, and dedicated RT Cores accelerate these tests enough to make real-time ray tracing practical.
Moody’s rated Saudi Arabia A1 with a stable outlook despite oil dependence and difficult reforms, forecasting a 0.2% 2017 contraction and budget deficits of 10.5% in 2017 and 9.2% in 2018.

The Michigan Supreme Court affirmed a directed verdict for the City of Marquette in Robert A. Maclam’s personal-injury action over poultry crates obstructing a sidewalk. The Court held that Marquette’s charter exempted the city from liability for damages caused by occupants’ failure to keep sidewalks clear, notwithstanding general state law imposing municipal liability. The charter provision had not been repealed by later legislation and was constitutional, not prohibited class legislation. Maclam’s remedy, if any, lay against the owner or occupant responsible for the obstruction.

The passage argues that forex should generally be avoided in favor of stocks, which it claims offer more robust and potentially profitable strategies. It cites 12 concerns: excessive leverage; the large impact of small market movements; exchange-rate volatility; forex’s zero-sum structure; difficulty predicting rates; limited effectiveness of risk-management systems; scams and fraudulent claims; counterparty risk from less-regulated providers; 24-hour trading encouraging overtrading; substantial demands of algorithmic trading; the market’s attraction to gamblers; and little backtesting behind many promoted strategies. Leverage is identified as the greatest danger because 50:1 leverage can allow a 2% adverse move to wipe out a trader’s deposit. The passage also states that forex cannot be held over time like stocks to build wealth, and concludes that prospective traders should carefully reconsider entering the market.

Lake Havasu City is Arizona’s hottest place, reaching 128°F on June 29, 1994, behind only Death Valley’s 134°F U.S. record. State Climatologist Nancy Selover attributes its extreme heat to an isolated, rocky desert location, lack of monsoon clouds and moisture, dry air, and heat-retaining terrain. The absence of irrigated agriculture also leaves the area without the cooling influence found in Needles, Bakersfield, and Blythe. Elsewhere in Arizona, elevation and monsoon moisture generally prevent temperatures from reaching these levels.

A coach urges his team to set aside previous events and distractions, approach the next contest as a Stanley Cup Final game, and focus on preparation, hard work, and discipline. He says hockey is not about retribution: any league action is secondary to winning. Because Dallas has a strong power play and the team cannot rely on shorthanded goals or neutralize every power play, avoiding unnecessary penalties and maintaining focus are crucial. He declines to reveal planned lineup matchups.

The coach explains that coaching was not an initial goal after retirement. After taking a year away from hockey, he eventually accepted repeated requests to coach, worked with Jacques Lemaire, and later received a head-coaching opportunity. He especially values seeing players’ happiness after winning the Cup, which outweighs coaching’s difficult days. He describes coaching as teaching: refining players’ abilities, helping them improve and have fun, and preparing them to handle adversity and learn about themselves. A player mentioned briefly was reported to be fine and skating well despite some stiffness.

This FAQ explains trading in Brazil, which has major exchanges including BM&F and BOVESPA and is regulated by the Brazilian Securities and Exchange Commission (CVM). It discusses day and swing trading, brokers, platforms, assets, orders, risk management, taxes, regulations, and trading plans. Assets include stocks, REITs, mutual funds, ETFs, commodities, derivatives, foreign currencies, and bonds. Risks include market volatility, political and economic instability, currency fluctuations, complex regulations, taxes, limited transparency and liquidity, poor management, and fraud.

Brazilian trading strategies include value investing, momentum trading, trend following, technical analysis, options, contrarian, and algorithmic trading. Technical tools include Fibonacci tools, moving averages, RSI, Bollinger Bands, and candlestick patterns; fundamental tools include financial statements, ratios, and macroeconomic indicators. Investment timing depends on economic indicators, politics, market performance, and global conditions. Commodities such as soybeans, orange juice, and coffee have generally been profitable, while technology, healthcare, and consumer-goods equities have grown. Leverage can amplify losses and requires a defined risk-management plan.

A Brazilian swing-trading strategy using a seasonal filter and oscillator for entries and a strength indicator for exits recorded 250 backtested trades, an average gain of 0.75%, a 67% win rate, a 19% maximum drawdown, and a 2.1 profit factor.

Wall Street’s major indexes had their worst week in two years as rising bond yields and inflation concerns outweighed improving corporate earnings forecasts. The S&P 500 fell 3.9% for the week but remained up 3.3% for the year after gaining 19.4% in 2017. The corporate tax rate cut from 35% to 21% helped lift estimated first-quarter profit growth to 17.7% from 11.7% on Dec. 20, while 2018 growth forecasts rose to 18.2% from 11.5%. Despite disappointing results from Apple, Alphabet, ExxonMobil and Chevron, overall fourth-quarter earnings have exceeded expectations. Improving global growth and a weaker dollar also support U.S. companies’ earnings.

The speaker outlines the Nashville Predators’ organizational approach: improving offensively while maintaining a strong defense through major trades, amateur scouting, and careful player evaluation. He credits Paul Fenton, Jeff Kealty, and the scouting staff for enabling roster changes while preserving one of the NHL’s best defenses.

Milwaukee has been central to Nashville’s success, developing players such as Pekka Rinne, Roman Josi, Ryan Suter, and Shea Weber and providing depth during injuries and playoff use. The Predators’ goaltending, defense, and increasingly improved forwards have contributed to a deep, team-wide success.

The acquisition of P.K. Subban is presented as a strong fit. Nashville aligned with Subban’s goal of winning the Stanley Cup, communicated with his representatives and family, and supported his off-ice activities to avoid misunderstandings. The speaker also emphasizes assessing players’ skills, roles, and organizational fit, treating them well, and communicating consistently.

He expresses pride and excitement about the franchise’s progress, praising the development system, Bridgestone Arena’s game presentation, Nashville’s entertainment offerings, and the enthusiastic atmosphere surrounding the team.

US intelligence and law enforcement officials reported frequent communications between Donald Trump’s campaign and business associates and Russians, prompting concern among investigators. Trump and Barack Obama were briefed on the contacts. Investigators had not determined their intent, including whether coordination occurred to release damaging information about Hillary Clinton’s campaign.

Pfizer's deal with the Trump administration to lower drug prices has prompted other major pharmaceutical firms that received letters from President Trump demanding lower prices to scramble for similar agreements, with some hoping to announce a White House deal as soon as this week, according to five Washington representatives and corporate lobbyists granted anonymity. One lobbyist said clients "have to now" come to an agreement, noting Pfizer's deal effectively added pressure. The exclusive report by Daniel Payne, who joined STAT in 2025 after covering health care at POLITICO, is available only to STAT+ subscribers.

In this Michigan mandamus proceeding (writ granted December 31, 1924), plaintiffs J. D. and Belle E. Brennen sought to compel the Livingston County circuit judge to vacate an order denying their motion to dismiss an action at law.

The underlying facts: Ruth C. Willis and Charles Goucher brought a chancery suit in the Livingston circuit court against the Brennens (Washtenaw County residents) based on an April 18, 1922 exclusive agency agreement to sell 156 acres in Green Oak Township for $19,000 net with a commission above the selling price. Service was made on the defendants in Washtenaw County. Their answer moved to dismiss the bill for lack of equity and because they had an adequate remedy at law. The court held the contract clearly an agency contract entitling Goucher to sell for more than $19,000, and transferred the case to the law side of the court under 3 Comp. Laws 1915, § 12351, permitting plaintiffs to file a declaration.

Plaintiffs then moved to dismiss on the law side because no process had been served on the defendants within Livingston County as required by § 12430; the chancery service in Washtenaw County could not confer jurisdiction over them. That motion was denied, prompting the mandamus application.

The Court held the motion to dismiss was well founded: transfer of an equity suit to the law side does not confer jurisdiction over a defendant not served with process within the county, and the statute's transfer provisions did not disturb existing service requirements, since the court sits within and is restricted to its county limits. Defendants' appearance, answer, and argument in the chancery suit did not waive their right to object to jurisdiction over the parties after the declaration was filed, nor did counsel's remarks suggesting transfer or a stipulation on time to plead waive such rights; the transfer order does not circumscribe the issues raisable on the law side.

The U.S. Embassy in Nigeria shared transformation photos of Folake, an HIV/AIDS survivor whose life was saved by antiretroviral treatment at a CDC/IHVN-supported site in Lagos under PEPFAR. Published for World AIDS Day, the post described HIV as not necessarily a death sentence. Commenters expressed disbelief and stigma, praised treatment and medication adherence, and encouraged HIV testing.

MIT 6.5630 is an advanced course on the evolution of proof systems in computer science, particularly from the mid-1980s onward, rather than on cryptography alone. The course meets weekly and has 11 sessions; students are expected to prepare from assigned readings, contribute scribed notes except during a guest lecture by Oded Regev and a crypto day, and complete one problem set. Planned topics include interactive and doubly efficient interactive proofs, the GKR protocol, PCP and MIP, Shamir’s \(IP=PSPACE\) theorem, the Fiat–Shamir paradigm and its security, succinct noninteractive and batched proofs, and SNARGs.

Classical proofs in NP are written explicitly and checked line by line by a polynomial-time verifier. Zero-knowledge research motivated Goldwasser, Micali, and Rackoff to introduce interactive proofs, in which an unrestricted prover and efficient verifier exchange messages. Interaction and verifier randomness are essential: without randomness, a deterministic interactive protocol could be converted into an ordinary NP proof, while without interaction, randomized verification corresponds to MA (Merlin–Arthur), whose relationship to NP remains unknown.

Randomness can provide substantial verification speedups.
