For example, matrix multiplication can be checked in \(O(n^2)\) time by randomly choosing \(r\) and comparing \(C(1,r,\ldots,r^{n-1})^T\) with \(AB(1,r,\ldots,r^{n-1})^T\), using the fact that distinct low-degree polynomials agree at only a small fraction of field elements.

An interactive proof has completeness and soundness. If the input belongs to the claimed language, an honest prover convinces the verifier with high probability; for inputs outside the language, every cheating prover succeeds with low probability. Any constant gap can be amplified toward probabilities 0 and 1 by repetition. Shamir’s celebrated theorem shows that interactive proofs can establish membership in every PSPACE language to a polynomial-time verifier.

The lecture then develops the sum-check protocol for proving
\[
\sum_{h_1,\ldots,h_m\in H} f(h_1,\ldots,h_m)=\beta
\]
for an \(m\)-variate polynomial \(f\) of degree at most \(d\) in each variable over a finite field. In successive rounds, the prover sends a univariate polynomial representing the partial sum with one variable left open. The verifier checks its degree and consistency with the previous claim, then sends a random field element. Repeating this for all variables culminates in a random evaluation checked against the verifier’s oracle access to \(f\).

The protocol is perfectly complete for a true claim. For a false claim, soundness is at most \(md/|F|\), by the polynomial root bound and a union bound over the rounds; the set \(H\) does not directly affect this bound. It uses \(m\) rounds and roughly \(O(md)\) field elements of communication, while the verifier performs polynomial evaluations and the prover carries out the large summation. Sum-check can also be generalized beyond Reed–Muller codes, including to tensor codes.

The polynomial approach is central because low-degree polynomials provide error-correcting guarantees: an incorrect polynomial differs from the correct one except at few points. Low-degree extensions allow many computational problems to be encoded as polynomials, making sum-check a foundational tool for constructing interactive proofs and many later applications.

SUDEP is the non-traumatic, non-drowning death of a person with epilepsy. Poor control of generalized tonic-clonic seizures is its strongest risk factor, while nocturnal seizures, prone positioning, central apnea, and autonomic instability further increase risk. Because respiratory arrest can occur within minutes and no existing intervention reliably acts quickly enough, the study developed Korus, an autonomous nighttime repositioning mattress.

Korus consists of an 8-by-4 array of inflatable cells that expand up to 14 inches, with pressure sensors, accelerometers, temperature sensors, networking components, and individually controlled valves. A Random Forest classifier detects prone, supine, left-lateral, and right-lateral positions from 1,152 pressure readings. An iOS and Android app displays body position and controls individual cells; automated data collection and model training take under 10 minutes per subject. Eighteen control participants were enrolled, with 10 undergoing formal testing.

Cells reached full inflation within seven seconds and supported 1,000 pounds each. Manual repositioning from prone to recovery position succeeded in 100% of tested participants, averaging 21.75 seconds. Prone-position detection accuracy was 96.8%, overall positional accuracy was 92.4%, and long-term recordings showed correct position detection 97.3% of the time. False position changes were attributed to supine positions being identified as lateral.

The current device successfully performs repositioning and cardinal-position recognition, but a fully autonomous SUDEP-prevention system still requires improved position mapping, optimized computing, a biomechanical framework, and seizure-detection integration, potentially through wearable devices. The authors estimate that successful development could yield more than 50% SUDEP risk reduction, but this was not demonstrated in the study.

NVIDIA Corporation’s fiscal 2021 Form 10-K describes a platform strategy combining GPUs, networking, CUDA software, systems, algorithms, libraries, and services. The company reports two segments—Graphics and Compute & Networking—and serves Gaming, Professional Visualization, Data Center, and Automotive markets. NVIDIA completed its approximately $7 billion Mellanox acquisition in April 2020 and entered a $40 billion agreement to acquire Arm Limited, subject to regulatory approvals and other closing conditions. It uses a fabless manufacturing strategy, relying on third-party foundries, assembly, testing, packaging, and contract manufacturers. As of January 31, 2021, NVIDIA had 18,975 employees across 29 countries. Principal risks include rapidly changing markets, intense competition, dependence on third-party suppliers, inaccurate demand forecasts, product defects and cybersecurity breaches, geopolitical and natural-disaster disruptions, COVID-19 effects, and uncertainty surrounding acquisitions and investments.

The invention provides a landing device that enables a rotorcraft without an image-capturing function to land at a destination without relying on aerial images that could infringe privacy or portrait rights. The device includes a landing portion, a position-recognition portion, and a remote-control portion. Optional features include an opening/closing mechanism, movable plates, distance measurement, drone identification verification, and an ascending/descending mechanism for delivering a received load to a residential space.

In a package-delivery embodiment, a drone loaded at a warehouse travels autonomously by GPS or beacons to near the user’s home. The landing device then verifies the drone’s identification, recognizes its position using infrared cameras, and remotely controls its descent and landing based on measured distance. A package suspended beneath the drone is transferred to the landing portion. Movable plates form a funnel during landing, then move upright to prevent the package from being blown away and guide it toward the center. Telescopic forks retract the package into the device, and an ascending/descending mechanism carries it to the user’s residential space. The landing portion is housed in a chimney-like cylindrical structure that closes except during landing, protecting its components from weather, ultraviolet exposure, and falling debris.

The delivery system includes warehouse, in-home, and management computers connected by a communication network. The management system maintains route, drone, and weather databases, receives delivery requests, selects drones and routes, sends delivery notifications, and coordinates package handling. Users approve deliveries through in-home displays or mobile terminals.

Additional modifications cover simplified landing devices for nonsnowy areas, integration with residential ventilation or smoke-exhaust systems, weather observation and alerts, emergency landing by drones, portable disaster-relief landing devices with relay communications, warnings for approaching camera-equipped drones, battery-status monitoring, flight-recording black boxes, takeoff-device inspections, designated flight routes, beacon base stations, and drone-counterterrorism policies involving warnings, flight restrictions, observation, blocking, and interception.

A New York grand jury indicted Harvey Weinstein on rape and criminal sex-act charges involving two women, including first- and third-degree rape and a first-degree criminal sex act. Manhattan District Attorney Cyrus Vance said the indictment advanced accountability and that the investigation remained active, while appealing for additional accusers to come forward. Weinstein surrendered Friday, was released on $1 million bail with travel confined to New York and Connecticut, and continues to deny nonconsensual sex.

Attorney Ben Brafman called the indictment unsurprising and duplicative, labeled the allegations unsupported, said he would seek its dismissal and expected Weinstein to be acquitted. Weinstein did not testify before the grand jury because his lawyers said he lacked time to prepare and a postponement was denied. Brafman also questioned the process amid political pressure on Vance. Further charges involving other accusers could follow.

The PGA848 is a high-voltage, high-bandwidth, precision programmable-gain instrumentation amplifier with a single-ended output, eight gain settings from 0.5 V/V to 100 V/V, and three digital gain-control pins. It operates with input-stage supplies above ±4.5 V and output-stage supplies above ±2.25 V. Its input common-mode range extends within 3 V of either supply.

The output difference amplifier’s DA_IN− and DA_IN+ pins permit external capacitors to be placed in parallel with internal feedback resistors for noise filtering, noise shaping, and custom attenuation. The internal 6.67 kΩ resistors vary by ±15%, and pin leakage can degrade common-mode rejection. These pins must not be used as outputs or to source or sink current.

A typical application drives an ADS8860 16-bit, 1 MSPS SAR ADC using ±15 V input and 5.3 V output supplies. A REF6250 reference and buffered 2.5 V reference set the PGA848 output to the ADC midscale. Three input/output filters suppress EMI and RFI, provide feedback filtering, and supply ADC charge kickback filtering. The nominal front-end bandwidth is 318 kHz, or 277 kHz at the high feedback-resistance tolerance, with −0.1 dB flatness through 41 kHz. The reference-buffer circuit uses an OPA192 with separate feedback paths and requires stability verification when load capacitance changes.

TI recommends matched input routing, close-placed low-ESR bypass capacitors, separation from noisy traces, and minimization of leakage and parasitic capacitance at DA_IN+ and DA_IN−. Output-stage supplies must remain within input-stage levels, and supplies above ±20 V can permanently damage the device. PSpice for TI and TINA-TI are identified as simulation resources, with TI documentation, support forums, product notifications, and mechanical and ordering information also provided.

A September 5, 2001 Enron email compiled news coverage of California’s electricity crisis and Gov. Gray Davis. California avoided the widely forecast summer blackouts after May 8, aided by consumer conservation, mild weather, six new power plants, and tighter federal regulations. Electricity consumption fell sharply, and Davis credited Californians’ efforts, though officials continued to warn that the crisis was unresolved.

Southern California Edison faced a legislative rescue plan allowing it to issue $2.9 billion in bonds backed by business customers in exchange for the state receiving a five-year option to buy its transmission lines for about $2.4 billion. Consumer groups opposed the proposal, and uncertainty remained over its passage, Edison’s roughly $3.5 billion debt, and the possibility of bankruptcy following Pacific Gas & Electric’s April Chapter 11 filing. Williams also filed a $591 million claim in the PG&E case. Moody’s maintained a stable credit outlook for public power utilities but identified market volatility, regulatory conflicts, consolidation, environmental costs, and transmission access as risks.

Davis’s political prospects appeared stronger because the blackout crisis had eased and California remained Democratic, but private polls found fewer than one-third of Californians favored his reelection. All three prospective Republican candidates had liabilities, while Davis benefited from incumbency and fundraising strength. Critics said his extensive executive orders during the energy emergency bypassed legislative checks, weakened regulatory oversight, and could create lasting political problems.

California’s finances were also strained: the state had advanced $6.1 billion for power purchases, faced revenue shortfalls, and issued $5.7 billion in revenue anticipation notes. Fifty-five state power contracts worth roughly $45 billion were projected to exceed spot-market prices from 2003 through 2010 and could impede renewable energy development. One commentary estimated the energy crisis could cost more than $100 billion while California lacked a comprehensive plan for urgent infrastructure needs.

Rabbi Harav Aaron Brafman, long-time Menahel of Yeshiva Derech Ayson–Yeshiva of Far Rockaway, died on Erev Shabbos, 19 Av 5777, at age 73. Born in 1944 to Reb Shlomo Zalman and Rochel Brafman, he grew up in Williamsburg and Crown Heights, attended Yeshivah Torah Vodaath for over 20 years, and was an exceptionally close student of Harav Yaakov Kamenetsky, Harav Gedaliah Schorr and Harav Avrohom Pam, whose teachings and worldviews shaped his approach to world affairs through hashkafas haTorah. Renowned for his hasmadah, he married in 1964 to Susie Schwartz of Frankfurt, California; she devoted herself to the home and family, enabling his focus on Torah, talmidim and the klal. He served as a Maggid Shiur in Torah Vodaath's mesivta from his mid-20s and became Menahel of the newly founded Yeshiva of Far Rockaway in 1970, under Rosh Yeshivah Harav Yechiel Perr. He fostered deep relationships with talmidim, gave shiurim and mussar vaadim to local baalei batim, raised funds for a tzedakah fund for needy residents, and spoke out on issues important to Klal Yisrael. His levayah was held Friday afternoon; the mittah was flown to Eretz Yisrael for hespeidim and burial in the Eretz HaChaim cemetery in Beit Shemesh. He is survived by his wife, siblings, seven children, and many grandchildren.

ESA’s Gaia observatory, deployed in 2013, has cataloged more than a billion astronomical objects to help create the largest and most precise 3D map of the Milky Way. A University of Toronto team led by Jason Hunt combined Gaia’s initial data with the RAVE survey, including information on more than 200,000 overlapping stars. The researchers measured the Sun’s Galactic orbital speed at 240 km/s and, using proper-motion calculations for Sagittarius A*, refined the Solar System’s distance from the Galactic center to 7.6–8.2 kiloparsecs, or about 24,788–26,745 light-years. The study, published in the Journal of Astrophysical Letters in November 2016, substantially narrowed earlier estimates of 7.2–8.8 kiloparsecs. Hunt anticipated that Gaia’s final 2017 data release would improve the precision of the Sun’s measured velocity and the distance estimate.

Motley Fool Money highlights the Wells Fargo Active Cash Card as a strong cash-back option, noting its $0 annual fee, unlimited 2% rewards on purchases, $200 bonus after $500 in spending within three months, and 12-month 0% intro APR on purchases and qualifying balance transfers. It also includes Visa Signature concierge service and up to $600 in cell-phone protection with a $25 deductible.

Capital One Quicksilver offers unlimited 1.5% cash back on all purchases, 5% back on hotels, vacation rentals, and rental cars booked through Capital One Travel, no annual or foreign-transaction fees, and a limited-time $300 welcome package. It includes 15 months of 0% intro APR on purchases and balance transfers, followed by an 18.99%–28.99% variable APR and applicable transfer fees.

A Citi offer provides 2% cash back on purchases when at least the minimum due is paid on time, 5% back on certain travel booked through Citi Travel, and $200 after $1,500 in purchases within six months. It offers 18 months of 0% intro APR on balance transfers, with fees and 17.99%–27.99% variable APR afterward; the intro rate does not apply to purchases, and transfers do not earn rewards. All three offers list a recommended good-to-excellent credit score of 670–850.

Enrique Marquez Jr. agreed to plead guilty to acting as a straw buyer for two assault rifles used in the 2015 San Bernardino terrorist attack, which killed 14 and injured 22. His plea also alleges he conspired with Syed Rizwan Farook in 2011 and 2012 to attack Riverside City College and freeway traffic, though those plans never occurred. Prosecutors said Marquez did not participate in or have advance knowledge of the San Bernardino attack. He has been in custody since December 2015 and faces up to 25 years in prison.

Venezuelans and TPS holders asked the Supreme Court to uphold a federal ruling that the Trump administration unlawfully terminated Venezuela’s Temporary Protected Status designation and extension. They argued that the Court’s earlier stay covered only preliminary relief, while the final judgment relied on statutory authority and a more developed record. The administration sought another stay, claiming the lower courts undermined the Supreme Court’s authority and the federal court hierarchy.

Bitcoin fell below $8,000 after Indian Finance Minister Arun Jaitley vowed to eliminate cryptocurrencies’ use in illicit financing and payments. India has issued repeated warnings, prompted banking disruptions affecting major exchanges, and formed a committee to study cryptocurrencies before taking action. The country, representing 2%–3% of global crypto trade, also plans to explore blockchain for digital payments, while industry figures expect regulation and continued growth despite short-term concern.

The coach said his hockey team had an outstanding year and made an incredible run to the Stanley Cup Finals, but lost to an opponent he described as the better team that deserved to win. He praised the players and staff for their hard work, competitiveness, resilience, and never giving up, while noting their strong home record and outstanding fans’ support. He said the loss would hurt for a while but might feel better in a few days, and expressed pride in the group and their accomplishments.

The author views Costamare (CMRE) as an attractive buying opportunity, citing a reversal in its share price after a 2014–2016 downturn, improving economic and global-trade conditions, and signs of a shipping-market upswing. CMRE owns and charters 71 containerships with about 466,000 TEU of capacity. Management reports stronger demand for larger vessels, 16 recent charters, no ships laid up, a 1.8% idle fleet, and historically low newbuild orders. Nearly all contracted cash comes from major liner companies, with $1.2 billion in contracted revenue, roughly three years of charter duration, and rising charter rates. The company holds about $219 million in cash and reduced net debt from $1.7 billion in 2013 to $1 billion.

Amazon.com, Inc. filed a Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2022. The Delaware corporation is headquartered in Seattle, Washington, and its common stock trades on the Nasdaq Global Select Market under “AMZN.” It is a large accelerated filer. The aggregate market value of voting stock held by non-affiliates was $944.7 billion as of June 30, 2022, and 10,247,259,757 shares were outstanding as of January 25, 2023.

Amazon operates through North America, International, and Amazon Web Services (AWS), serving consumers, sellers, developers, enterprises, content creators, advertisers, and employees. Its consumer operations include online and physical stores, third-party sales, electronic devices, media content, Prime subscriptions, and multiple fulfillment methods. Seller programs generate fixed fees, sales percentages, per-unit fees, interest, or combinations thereof. AWS provides on-demand compute, storage, database, analytics, machine-learning, and related services, while advertising services support sellers, vendors, publishers, authors, and others.

The filing describes intense global competition across retail, cloud computing, digital content, advertising, logistics, devices, and related markets. Principal retail competitive factors are selection, price, convenience, and reliable fulfillment. Intellectual property is considered critical to success, sales are historically strongest in the fourth quarter, and Amazon employed approximately 1,541,000 full- and part-time workers at year-end.

Risk factors include competition, expansion into new products and geographies, international operations and regulations, demand fluctuations, seller misconduct, intellectual-property claims, foreign exchange exposure, management and operational strain, fulfillment and data-center capacity, data loss and security breaches, system interruptions, personnel retention, supplier dependencies, commercial relationships, acquisitions, inventory, payments, stock-price volatility, government regulation, litigation, product liability, taxes, and government-contract requirements. Specific regulatory risks are discussed for China and India.

At December 31, 2022, Amazon reported 617.483 million leased square feet and 43.927 million owned square feet, including offices, stores, fulfillment facilities, and data centers. Segment figures exclude corporate facilities. There were 10,845 shareholders of record as of January 25, 2023, and no issuer purchases of equity securities.

Management’s financial priorities include long-term sustainable free-cash-flow growth, customer experience, lower prices, product availability and selection, faster delivery, reliable services, inventory efficiency, and controlled variable and fixed costs. Amazon continues investing in AWS, technology infrastructure, content, software, electronic devices, broadband satellite services, and autonomous vehicles. Foreign exchange movements affect reported results.

Critical accounting estimates include inventory valuation and income taxes. Inventory is generally valued using first-in, first-out at the lower of cost or net realizable value; each additional 1% inventory valuation allowance at December 31, 2022 would have increased cost of sales by approximately $390 million. Tax estimates require significant judgment because of changing laws, jurisdictional mix, audits, and controversies.

For 2022, operating activities provided $46.752 billion, investing activities used $37.601 billion, and financing activities provided $9.718 billion. Cash, cash equivalents, and marketable securities totaled $70.0 billion at fair value, including $18.3 billion held in foreign currencies.

Tesla’s Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2020 describes a Delaware corporation headquartered in Palo Alto, California, whose common stock trades on the Nasdaq Global Select Market under “TSLA.” The company is a large accelerated filer. The aggregate market value of voting stock held by non-affiliates was $160.57 billion as of June 30, 2020, and 959,853,504 common shares were outstanding as of February 1, 2021.

Tesla designs, develops, manufactures, sells and leases electric vehicles and energy-generation and storage systems and provides related services. It operates two reportable segments. Automotive includes vehicle design, production, sales and leasing, regulatory-credit sales, services, used vehicles, retail merchandise, subsidiary sales and insurance. Energy generation and storage includes solar and battery-storage products, related services, leasing and incentives.

Current vehicles include the Model 3 midsize sedan, Model Y compact SUV, Model S full-size sedan and Model X midsize SUV. Tesla announced planned consumer vehicles such as Cybertruck and a new Roadster, the Tesla Semi commercial vehicle, and a future lower-cost vehicle. Energy products include Powerwall, Powerpack, Megapack, retrofit solar systems and Solar Roof, along with integrated solar-and-storage systems, financing options and software for remotely controlling and dispatching energy-storage systems.

The company develops battery, powertrain, vehicle-control, infotainment and self-driving technologies internally. Its FSD Computer runs neural networks, while Autopilot and FSD currently provide advanced driver-assistance functions for which drivers remain responsible. Tesla updates vehicle software over the air and intends to develop an autonomous ride-hailing network. It is also developing proprietary lithium-ion battery cells and manufacturing processes.

Automotive sales are primarily direct through Tesla’s website and company-owned stores and galleries, with some vehicle sales through third parties. The company also operates service centers, Mobile Service technicians, body shops, Superchargers, Destination Chargers and residential charging solutions. Energy products are sold through Tesla’s online, store and gallery channels, international operations, channel partners and utilities. Tesla provides warranties for vehicles and energy products and may offer performance guarantees for energy systems.

Tesla offers vehicle leasing and financing through financial institutions and certain local subsidiaries, including arrangements with resale-value or buyback guarantees. It also provides financing, leases and power-purchase agreements for solar and storage customers and launched a California insurance product in 2019.

Manufacturing facilities include Fremont Factory, Gigafactory Nevada, Gigafactory New York and Gigafactory Shanghai; Gigafactory Berlin and Gigafactory Texas were under construction. Nevada integrates battery-material, cell, module and pack production with drive-unit and energy-storage manufacturing. New York produces Solar Roof and related components, while Shanghai produces vehicles and is being expanded through localized procurement. Tesla relies on hundreds of global suppliers, many single-source suppliers, and on raw materials including aluminum, steel, cobalt, lithium, nickel and copper.

Government incentives and regulatory programs materially affect Tesla and its customers. Tesla has manufacturing-equipment tax exclusions in California, Nevada tax abatements and credits, a New York development lease, Shanghai land-use and tax arrangements, and Travis County and Del Valle property-tax agreements for Gigafactory Texas. It also earns and sells regulatory credits. Its businesses remain subject to federal, state and local vehicle-safety, battery-transport, solar, energy-storage, dealer-licensing, self-driving and electricity regulations.

The automotive market is highly competitive, including against internal-combustion, hybrid and electric vehicles from established and emerging manufacturers. Energy-storage and solar businesses compete with other manufacturers, developers, installers, service providers and utilities. Tesla relies on proprietary designs and protects them through patents, trademarks, copyrights, trade secrets and contractual measures, while maintaining a pledge not to initiate patent lawsuits against good-faith electric-vehicle patent users.

As of December 31, 2020, Tesla and its subsidiaries employed 70,757 full-time workers worldwide. The company reported no work stoppages from labor disputes and emphasized talent development, internal mobility, workplace inclusion and diversity initiatives.

Principal risks include pandemic-related disruptions and macroeconomic uncertainty; delays or cost overruns in product, feature and factory ramps; demand uncertainty; supplier and single-source component shortages; microchip shortages; volatile raw-material costs; dependence on Panasonic and other battery-cell suppliers; competition; international regulatory, political, tax, labor and trade conditions; product defects, software failures and product-liability claims; battery-cell safety; battery-recycling requirements; the ability to maintain customer, supplier and investor confidence; and compliance, residual-value, financing, credit and leasing risks associated with financial programs. The filing cautions that actual results may differ materially from forward-looking statements and that the listed risks are not exhaustive.

John Ternus, 50, is Apple’s senior vice president of hardware engineering and is increasingly viewed by industry observers and company insiders as the most likely successor to CEO Tim Cook. Speculation intensified after Jeff Williams stepped down from operational responsibilities and announced his departure from Apple. Ternus joined Apple’s product design team in 2001 and has overseen major products including iPads, iPhones, AirPods and Macs, contributing to the Mac’s transition to Apple Silicon. His increased keynote appearances, public-relations spotlight and expanded influence over product roadmaps, features and strategy suggest Apple may be preparing for a gradual leadership transition.

Ternus graduated from the University of Pennsylvania in 1997 with a mechanical engineering degree and was a competitive swimmer. Earlier work at Virtual Research Systems gave him experience with virtual-reality headsets, displays and human-computer interfaces later relevant to Apple Vision Pro. His age, technical background and institutional knowledge make him a potential internal successor as Apple navigates executive turnover, AI setbacks, mixed-reality ambitions and efforts to reinvigorate products beyond the iPhone.

The article frames inclusive education through the 1994 Salamanca Declaration and the 2006 Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities, emphasizing equal access and the right of children with disabilities to learn in regular schools. It reviews one-track, dual-track, and multiple-track models, noting potential benefits of regular schools—social and communication skills, empathy, and greater societal participation—as well as concerns about specialized instruction, safety, bullying, and educational choice.

In Myanmar, the government ratified the disability-rights convention in 2011 and enacted inclusive-education provisions in 2015, but data showed low enrollment among children with disabilities. The study examined a “limited inclusive education in phase” model for visually impaired students in Yangon. Using a qualitative case-study design, it collected interviews, focus-group discussions, observations, and documents in February 2019 from two special schools, two connected regular schools, students, parents, teachers, principals, and education officials.

In this model, students receive primary education and Braille instruction at special schools, while lower-secondary education takes place in regular-school classrooms alongside non-disabled students. Participants valued special schools for providing trained staff, life-skills and computer training, supplementary instruction, and a secure, supportive environment. Regular schools were valued for developing students’ social and communication skills and encouraging understanding among non-disabled peers.

However, the study identified limited cooperation between teachers in the two school systems, regular-school teachers’ reliance on special-school expertise, weak interaction outside classrooms, bullying, and limited awareness of educational options among families, especially in rural areas. The findings indicate that the phased model can use existing resources effectively while supporting students’ educational, practical, social, and emotional needs. Recommended measures include teacher training and exchanges across the Ministry of Education and Department of Social Welfare, as well as activities that promote inclusion and camaraderie. The article concludes that inclusive-education models should reflect each country’s resources and context and that cooperation and creativity are needed to expand them.

The passage describes TI’s ADS9803, an eight-channel, 20-bit, 2-MSPS data-acquisition system with an integrated analog front end. Multiple ADS9803 devices can sample corresponding channels simultaneously by sharing SMPL_CLK and applying a positive SMPL_SYNC pulse centered on SMPL_CLK’s falling edge. Synchronization resets channel-selection logic, aligns FCLKOUT with data frames, and is required after power-up, a sampling-clock restart, or reset.

The device includes a precision, low-drift internal reference. For best performance, TI recommends filtering the reference with a 10-µF ceramic capacitor at REFIO. An external reference can also be used by disabling the internal reference through the SPI configuration or by pulling SDI/EXTREF low.

The source-synchronous output interface supports two- or four-lane operation with SDR or DDR signaling. The ADC outputs D[3:0], DCLKOUT, and FCLKOUT; 20-bit conversion results are transmitted MSB first in 24-bit packets with six trailing zeros. FCLKOUT delimits each two-channel data set and runs at one-fourth the sampling-clock frequency. DCLKOUT frequency depends on the sampling rate, data rate, and number of lanes. An optional output randomizer XORs conversion data with either the result’s LSB or an appended PRBS bit to reduce ground-bounce-related interference. Simple averaging improves SNR while halving the output data rate, whereas moving averaging does not change the output rate.

Host-selectable fixed, digital-ramp, and alternating test patterns can replace conversion data for channels 1–4 and 5–8. The device can be reset or powered down through dedicated pins or register fields, after which a register-write initialization sequence is required. Normal operation uses a free-running sampling clock. Speed-boost mode converts only a selected analog-input pair at up to 8 MSPS while leaving the other six channels idle.

The 16-bit configuration registers are divided into three banks and accessed with 8-bit addresses. Bank 0 is always accessible, while banks 1 and 2 are selected through register 0x03. Register writes require SPI_RD_EN = 0; register reads require SPI_RD_EN = 1 and SPI_MODE = 1 and use 24-bit SPI frames. In daisy-chain configurations, CS and SCLK are shared, SDO is chained to the next device’s SDI, and each register-write frame contains 24 clock cycles per ADC. DAISY_CHAIN_LEN specifies the chain length excluding the first ADC.

For automated test-equipment applications, the ADS9803 can connect directly to PMU outputs or through a multiplexer. It provides low-noise bandwidth up to 22.7 kHz and wide-bandwidth operation up to 700 kHz; the latter settles to 99.95% of full scale in 7.5 µs. The passage reports a total unadjusted error of 0.0015% at 25°C ±5°C after offset and gain calibration. Separate AVDD_5V, VDD_1V8, and IOVDD supplies are used without a required power-up sequence. Layout guidance calls for close 0.1-µF supply bypass capacitors, reference bypass capacitors near REFIO and REFM, short ground-plane connections, and separation of analog and reference paths from digital signals and noise sources. Appropriate ESD handling is also required.

The disclosure describes systems and methods for decoding a user’s neural activity in real time to identify intended movements and convert them into electrical signals for a body limb, prosthesis, wheelchair, computer cursor, exoskeleton, remote-control device, or robotic arm. The resulting “neural bridge” bypasses damaged neural pathways, enabling a user to control movement through thought.

Neural signals may be recorded using EEG, implanted microelectrode arrays, or ECoG. The signals are amplified and filtered, stimulation artifacts are removed, and features such as amplitude, frequency-band or wavelet-scale power, and firing rate are extracted. Decoders trained through machine-learning methods, including nonlinear support vector machines, identify discrete movements and movement effort. Decoder outputs are combined with sensor data, feedback history, and a physics-based body-state observer to dynamically adjust stimulation for factors such as joint position, motion, and electrode displacement. Multiplexed, interleaved stimulation patterns can produce compound movements without electrical interference.

A graphical interface can cue movements during decoder training, display feedback, and allow stimulation parameters to be selected. Decoder training uses attempted or imagined movements under varied conditions, including static and rhythmic tasks. Electrical stimulation is continuously updated, commonly using current-controlled monophasic pulses, to evoke the desired motion.

In experiments with an able-bodied participant, position sensors and graphical hand representations closely matched performed hand and arm movements. In a separate experiment, a quadriplegic participant used decoded cortical activity, a virtual central pattern generator, and neuromuscular electrical stimulation to initiate, sustain, and switch among imagined thumb flexion, extension, and rhythmic wiggle movements. Movement-specific accuracies ranged from 84.6% to 91.5%, with 77.4% overall accuracy across movement and rest states.
The team used time off to focus for tomorrow night’s game. No adjustments are decided; the opponent is praised as an elite shot-blocking team.

The compilation covers U.S. diplomatic efforts toward peace before entering the war, Allied and Central Powers’ peace proposals, neutrality and submarine incidents, unrestricted submarine warfare, the Zimmermann Telegram, armed merchant ships, and the declaration of war with Germany on April 6, 1917. It also records Latin American governments’ responses, severances of relations with Germany, and proposals for a conference of American states.

Microsoft Corporation entered an underwriting agreement on August 1, 2016, for seven series of senior unsecured notes: $2.5 billion of 1.100% notes due 2019; $2.75 billion of 1.550% notes due 2021; $1.5 billion of 2.000% notes due 2023; $4 billion of 2.400% notes due 2026; $2.25 billion of 3.450% notes due 2036; $4.5 billion of 3.700% notes due 2046; and $2.25 billion of 3.950% notes due 2056. Each series matures on August 8 of its stated year. The notes will be issued under Microsoft’s May 18, 2009 base indenture, as supplemented by an Eleventh Supplemental Indenture dated August 8, 2016, with U.S. Bank National Association as trustee. Interest is payable semiannually in arrears on February 8 and August 8, beginning February 8, 2017, to holders of record on the preceding January 24 or July 24. Microsoft may redeem the notes in certain circumstances and the notes rank equally with its other unsecured and unsubordinated debt.

This study estimated SARS-CoV-2-attributable mortality in India during January 2020–December 2021 using ex post, WHO-compliant verbal autopsies. It combined living and deceased samples from the Consumer Pyramids Household Survey (CPHS) for 2018–2021. Verbal autopsies were attempted for 30,447 reported deaths; 22,178 were completed, a 72.8% response rate. After excluding 1,719 deaths occurring before 2018, the final sample included 20,453 decedents. Two physicians independently assigned ICD-10 cause-of-death codes, with a third physician resolving disagreements. Estimates incorporated survey weights, propensity-score adjustments for verbal-autopsy nonresponse, and corrections for deaths reported to CPHS with substantial delays.

The estimated all-cause death rate in 2020–2021 was 81.19% higher than in 2018–2019. SARS-CoV-2 was associated with 17.93% of all pandemic-period deaths and 33.15% of excess deaths. Cardiovascular disease accounted for 27.18% of all deaths and 23.15% of excess deaths; accidents and tuberculosis accounted for 8.74% and 5.32% of excess deaths, while respiratory deaths declined by an amount equivalent to 1.52% of excess deaths. SARS-CoV-2’s monthly share of deaths exceeded 23.3% in June 2020 and approached 35.8% in April 2021. Its estimated population death rate peaked at annualized rates of 0.8% during the May 2020 lockdown, 0.9% in June 2020, and 1.1% in May 2021.

The verbal-autopsy data placed the first SARS-CoV-2 mortality spike at the end of the 2020 lockdown rather than during the first official wave, while confirming a spike around the second wave. Mortality increased significantly with age, with rates highest among people over 80, although most SARS-CoV-2 deaths occurred among those aged 61–80. Rates were higher in urban areas and the highest income quartile but not significantly so; rural India had more deaths because of its larger population. State-level excess death rates ranged from 0.07% in Bihar and Jharkhand to 2.13% in Goa.

Limitations included the inclusion of vaping-related disorders in ICD-10 code U07, possible misclassification between COVID-19 and respiratory deaths, imperfect corrections for reporting delays and survey nonresponse, and an unvalidated modification of the verbal-autopsy instrument for COVID-19.

NVIDIA’s GA10x Ampere architecture delivers up to 2× improvements in programmable shading, ray tracing, and AI. In a Wolfenstein: Youngblood example, shader-only rendering took 51 ms, adding RT Cores reduced this to 20 ms, and Tensor Cores with DLSS reduced it to 12 ms; an RTX 3080 completed the frame in 6.7 ms, or 150 FPS.

Second-generation RT Cores add concurrent ray tracing and shading, double ray/triangle intersection performance over Turing, and accelerate ray-traced motion blur. A new Interpolate Triangle Position unit handles moving and deforming geometry and can make accurate motion-blur rendering up to eight times faster than on Turing. OptiX 7 supports timestamped rays and geometry motion paths, while the feature is supported in Blender 2.90, Chaos V-Ray 5.0, Arnold, and Redshift Renderer 3.0.X. An RTX 3080 measured up to 5× faster motion-blur rendering than an RTX 2080 Super in a Blender Cycles 2.90 test.

Third-generation Tensor Cores accelerate matrix operations used in deep learning, AI denoising, and DLSS. They add TF32 and BF16 support, improve efficiency and energy consumption, and implement fine-grained structured sparsity. A 2-out-of-4 sparsity pattern halves weight storage and bandwidth requirements while doubling math throughput, with virtually no inference-accuracy loss in evaluations involving dozens of networks. The RTX 3080 provides 2.7× the peak FP16 throughput of a dense RTX 2080 Super when sparsity is enabled.

DLSS uses a neural network to combine details from multiple rendered frames. Ampere’s third-generation Tensor Cores and 9× super-resolution scaling make 8K ray-traced gaming at 60 FPS feasible on the RTX 3090 in many tested titles.

GA10x GPUs introduce GDDR6X memory, developed with Micron. Its PAM4 signaling transfers two bits per clock edge using four voltage levels, while the MTA encoding scheme limits signal transitions and improves signal-to-noise ratio. Supporting data rates up to 19.5 Gbps, GDDR6X delivers up to 936 GB/s of peak bandwidth on GA10x GPUs—over 52% more than the TU102 in the RTX 2080 Ti—and assists BVH ray traversal through pseudo-independent memory channels.

The passage also presents NVIDIA RTX IO as a solution to storage and CPU decompression bottlenecks. With Microsoft’s DirectStorage, RTX IO enables compressed assets to be read from NVMe SSDs and decompressed on the GPU, reportedly providing up to 100× throughput and 20× lower CPU utilization compared with traditional approaches. It can accelerate game and asset loading, reduce stutter and object pop-in, improve streaming and frame rates, and help production-rendering systems transfer large mesh and texture datasets to the GPU.

The GA10x-based NVIDIA A40 targets data-center visual computing. Compared with the Quadro RTX 6000, it offers up to 2× FP32 and ray-tracing throughput, up to 5× AI and data-science throughput—or 10× with sparsity—and twice the PCIe Gen4 transfer bandwidth. It includes 48 GB of memory, expandable to 96 GB through two GPUs connected with third-generation NVLink, along with vGPU, Quadro Sync, and EGX Platform support. The RTX A6000 workstation GPU has 10,752 CUDA Cores, 48 GB of GDDR6 memory, hardware-accelerated motion blur and AI denoising, and can combine two boards for 96 GB of memory.

Ampere’s display engine supports 4K at 120 Hz and 8K at 60 Hz, including two 8K displays with separate cables. DisplayPort 1.4a with DSC 1.2a and HDMI 2.1 with up to 48 Gbps bandwidth enable high resolutions, refresh rates, and dynamic HDR. The GPUs support HDCP 2.3 and HDCP 1.x.

Fifth-generation NVDEC provides hardware decoding for MPEG-2, VC-1, H.264, H.265, VP8, VP9, and AV1 on Windows and Linux. GA10x supports hardware AV1 decoding, including 8K60 HDR playback with about 4% CPU usage in the cited test, compared with a software decoder averaging 28 FPS and more than 85% CPU utilization. Seventh-generation NVENC offloads encoding from the CPU and graphics engine, supports up to 4K H.264 and 8K HEVC, and exceeds x264 Fast quality while matching x264 Medium under common streaming settings.

The GeForce RTX 3090 uses GA102 with 82 SMs, 10,496 CUDA Cores, and 24 GB of GDDR6X. The GA104-based RTX 3070 supports all GA10x features except NVLink and uses GDDR6 rather than GDDR6X; NVIDIA states it outperforms the previous RTX 2080 Ti. GDDR6X also includes Error Detection and Replay, which detects failed memory transactions and retries them, providing users with a clearer indication when memory overclocking reaches its performance limit, though crashes remain possible.

The specification states that its information is believed accurate as of publication, reserves the right to revise it, disclaims implied warranties, limits liability, and specifies that NVIDIA products are not authorized for medical, military, aircraft, space, life-support, or other applications where failure could cause injury or damage.

The 3-4 defense uses three down linemen, four linebackers, and four defensive backs. It generally requires large linemen who control two gaps, hybrid outside linebackers who can rush or cover, and a two-safety setup that supports both run defense and varied pass coverage. Its extra linebacker allows pressure from multiple directions, including five-man rushes, while safeties can replace rushers to create different coverage looks.

Its main weakness is against spread offenses. Two receivers on each side can pull outside linebackers into coverage, shrinking the box to five defenders against five blockers plus the ball carrier. Trips formations and fast slot receivers create further challenges, contributing to the rise of the 3-3 stack.

The weakside edge and crossfire blitzes disguise pre-snap looks before changing the rush and coverage after the snap. Cover 4 uses four defensive backs deep and four linebackers underneath but is vulnerable in the flats; cover-2 man has the same pre-snap look while using man coverage beneath two high safeties.

Bill Parcells and Bill Belichick used the defense with the Giants, while Belichick, Nick Saban, and Kirby Smart later became prominent figures in the same coaching tree. The passage credits those three coaches with 16 major championships won using versions of the 3-4.

The instructor reviewed a difficult quiz averaging about 78–79, announced that the quiz and solutions would be posted, and explained that grades will combine the two quizzes, participation, and homework. The lecture then extended full factorial designs of experiments from \(2^2\) to \(2^k\), emphasizing how corner-point designs support models containing means, main effects, and interactions. With factors coded from \(-1\) to \(+1\), contrasts estimate effects by comparing averages at high and low levels; interaction columns such as \(AB\) and \(ABC\) are generated by multiplying factor columns. Under this coding, a main-effect estimate is scaled to obtain the corresponding regression coefficient. Contrast-based estimates are equivalent to regression estimates, with design tables forming the regression matrix; direct inversion applies to exactly determined models, while pseudo-inversion is needed with replicated observations.

ANOVA can test the significance of main and interaction effects using sums of squares, mean squares, and F-tests against residual error. In a sheet-metal bending example with punch depth and material as factors, ten replicates at each of four settings produced 40 observations and 36 error degrees of freedom; the main effects and interaction were significant.

Residuals reflect both replication noise and omitted model structure, including higher-order terms and unmodeled factors. The instructor recommended examining residual patterns, variance across settings, and normality, and possibly transforming the response. Curvature or lack of fit can be tested by adding center or intermediate points and replicating them, then comparing deviations from the linear model with pure error using ANOVA. Without replication, a single added point could fit a quadratic term exactly but could not test its significance; replicated center points provided a useful lack-of-fit test. In another example, center-point replication indicated no lack of fit, an insignificant interaction, and significant main effects.

The lecture concluded with an introduction to nuisance factors, blocking, randomization, and confounding. Holding nuisance factors constant, randomizing run order, or arranging blocks can prevent nuisance effects from being confused with main effects; blocking may instead confound a nuisance factor with an interaction effect. This principle leads into fractional factorial designs, which reduce experimental points by accepting some confounding. Reading was assigned primarily from Montgomery, Chapter 12, with additional selected May and Spanos material.

This prospective diagnostic accuracy study assessed newborn foot length for identifying low birth weight (LBW) and preterm birth (PTB) in three primary care clinics in Madang Province, Papua New Guinea. It enrolled 342 newborns from 335 mothers and compared foot length, measured within 72 hours by averaging two readings, with birth weight from duplicate electronic-scale measurements and gestational age based on the last menstrual period or ultrasound. Nine trained volunteers also measured foot length for 123 newborns to assess community feasibility and agreement with the researcher.

Of the newborns, 21.1% were LBW and 7.3% were preterm. A foot-length cutoff of <7.7 cm had an area under the curve of 87.0% for LBW and 85.8% for PTB. At this cutoff, sensitivity and specificity were 84.7% and 69.6% for LBW, with positive and negative predictive values of 42.7% and 94.5%, respectively. For PTB, sensitivity and specificity were 88.0% and 61.8%, with positive and negative predictive values of 15.4% and 98.5%. Researcher and volunteer measurements differed by an average of 0.07 cm, with 95% limits of agreement from −0.55 to +0.70 cm; 7.3% of paired measurements fell outside these limits.

The findings indicate that foot length is a simple and feasible screening method for LBW and PTB that trained health workers and community volunteers can use. However, low positive predictive value for PTB could result in many unnecessary referrals. Limitations included measurement up to 72 hours after birth, lack of blinding, and recruitment from only one PNG province.
