It also calls for strategies to counter alleged U.S. rights violations and support sanction-affected Iranians. A second parliamentary vote and clerical approval are required.

This excerpt is from the Texas Instruments MSPM0G (MSPM0G3519/3518/1519/1518) datasheet (SLASFA2A, November 2024, revised April 2025), covering system-level hardware descriptions and support information.

**Operating modes and power:** MSPM0G MCUs offer five power modes in decreasing power order — RUN, SLEEP, STOP, STANDBY, and SHUTDOWN. The CPU executes code in RUN; peripheral interrupts wake the device from SLEEP, STOP, or STANDBY; SHUTDOWN disables the internal core regulator and can only be exited via NRST, SWD, or an IO logic-level match. Two power domains exist: PD1 (CPU, memories, high-performance peripherals), always on in RUN/SLEEP only, and PD0 (low-speed, low-power peripherals), on in RUN, SLEEP, STOP, and STANDBY; both are off in SHUTDOWN. Tables list per-mode functionality using EN/DIS/OPT/NS/OFF keys.

**Modules:** The PMU provides regulated core supplies, a BOR supply monitor with three programmable thresholds, and parity-protected trim with POR generation. The clock module supplies LFOSC (32 kHz), SYSOSC (4/32 MHz factory trim; 16/24 MHz user trim), LFXT/LFCKIN, HFXT/HFCKIN (4–48 MHz), and SYSPLL (32–80 MHz), distributing MCLK, CPUCLK, ULPCLK, MFCLK, MFPCLK, LFCLK, ADCCLK, CLK_OUT, HFCLK, HSCLK, and CANCLK. The DMA has 12 channels (6 full-feature DMA0–DMA5 with repeated transfers; 6 basic DMA6–DMA11 with single transfers), 8- to 128-bit/mixed transfer widths, up to 64k transfers, configurable triggers, early and active-channel interrupts, cascading, and stride mode. The event manager routes events between peripherals, DMA, and CPU via publishers, subscribers, and a static/programmable event fabric (IRQ, DMA trigger, and generic events). Additional peripherals include dual-bank flash (up to 256/512 kB plus a 16 kB data flash) with ECC, 1 kB sectors, up to 100,000 program/erase cycles on 32 selected sectors, and bank swap for OTA updates; up to 128 kB SRAM in two 64 kB banks (Bank 0 ECC/parity protected and always available; Bank 1 without protection and optionally disabled, contents lost in shutdown) with write-execute partitioning via SRAMBOUNDARY registers; up to 93 GPIO pins across Ports A/B/C with multi-bit set/clear/toggle, "Standard with Wake" shutdown wake, and "FastWake" for STOP/STANDBY; IOMUX pad configuration; two 12-bit ADCs (ADC0/ADC1) with 4 Msps, >11 ENOB, HW averaging to 14-bit at 250 ksps, 24 result registers, and internal temperature/supply channels; a temperature sensor with factory single-point calibration; VREF with 1.4 V/2.5 V internal or external reference; comparators with blanking, wakeup, and fault-handling links; a 12-bit buffered DAC with self-calibration, FIFO, DMA, and hardware trigger; security features (AES-128/256 accelerator with GCM/GMAC, CCM/CBC-MAC, CBC, CTR; firewalls; secure storage of up to 4 AES keys; CRC-16/CRC-32); TRNG (32-bit numbers every 128 cycles); AESADV; keystore; CRC-P; MATHACL; UART0–UART1 and UART3–UART7 with LIN mode; I2C supporting Sm/Fm/Fm+ and SMBus 3.0 with address-match wakeup; SPI up to 32 Mbit/s; CAN-FD compliant to ISO 11898-1:2015 up to 5 Mbit/s; the LFSS_B subsystem (RTC_B with alarms/calibration and IWDT); WWDT; and TIMGx/TIMAx timers with QEI/Hall inputs, complementary PWM with dead band, and fault handling.

**Debug, boot, and identification:** A two-wire SWD debug port is provided. The boot strap loader works over UART or I2C, is protected by a 256-bit password, can be disabled, and may be invoked at boot, via invoke pin plus NRST, when the device is blank, or at runtime via SYSRST. Devices include a memory-mapped FACTORY region with DEVICEID (0x41C4.0004) and USERID (0x41C4.0008) registers.

**Layout recommendations:** TI recommends 10 µF plus 0.1 µF low-ESR ceramic decoupling across VDD/VSS, a 47 kΩ NRST pullup with a 10 nF pulldown, a 100 kΩ 0.1% / 25 ppm/°C resistor between ROSC and VSS if SYSOSC FCL is used (otherwise PA2 is usable as a digital pin), a 0.47 µF capacitor on VCORE with no other connections, and pullup resistors on the 5 V-tolerant open-drain IO for I2C/UART high output.

**Support and packaging:** TI lists development tools including Code Composer Studio, SysConfig, MSP Academy, TI Resource Explorer, GUI Composer, IAR Embedded Workbench, Keil MDK, and Arm toolchains; device nomenclature prefixes X (experimental) and MSP (qualified production); and support resources such as TI E2E forums. The document also notes the revision history for April 2025, ESD handling precautions, trademark information, and mechanical, packaging, and orderable information including automotive-qualified MSPM0G3518-Q1/MSPM0G3519-Q1 versions.

Blackwell enables rapid clock-tree gating, including the entire memory tree, and separate voltage rails for GPU cores and memory, supporting workload-specific optimization, frame-level shutdown of unused areas, and lower dynamic and leakage power.

Spouses using a Berliner Testament become each other’s sole heirs, with children inheriting after both parents die, securing the survivor’s finances. The will is strongly binding and cannot be changed unilaterally, even after one spouse dies; flexible clauses may help. Inheritance-tax allowances and the effects of relationship changes should be considered.

Delta expects premium-cabin ticket revenue to surpass coach sales for at least one or two quarters next year. Premium revenue rose 9% year over year to nearly $5.8 billion, while main-cabin revenue fell 4% to just over $6 billion. Premium seats and Delta’s loyalty program generated close to 60% of revenue last year, reflecting increased customer demand for upscale travel.

This medRxiv preprint (not peer reviewed) examines how to forecast opioid-related fatal overdoses at fine spatial scales to help public health departments target limited intervention resources. Background: U.S. opioid overdose deaths exceed 450,000 in eight years, with more than 80,000 in 2022; the epidemic has passed through four waves (prescription opioids, heroin post-2010, fentanyl from 2013, and combined stimulant/fentanyl). The authors note that population-level forecasting is nascent, most prior work assumes access to person-level data, and hotspot-based studies often assume today's clusters persist, which the authors say does not always hold.

Data: Two publicly sourced datasets were assembled with annual counts of opioid-involved overdose deaths per census tract, using 2020 Census boundaries and covariates (prior counts, location, time, and Social Vulnerability Index features). Cook County, Illinois (1,328 tracts, >5 million residents) used de-identified Medical Examiner case archive data (2014–2023, with 2015–2022 forecast years); Massachusetts (1,620 tracts, >6 million residents) used state death certificate data (2001–2019).

Models: Baselines (all-zeros, last-year, historical average), weighted historical average, Poisson GLM (with/without SVI), gradient boosted trees, Gaussian Process, Bayesian spatiotemporal (BST) models, negative binomial regression with spatially lagged features (NBSpLag), and CASTNet, an attention-based neural network. Metrics: RMSE and MAE, plus a new intervention-aware metric, %BPR ("best possible reach"), defined as the share of fatalities in a model's top-K recommended tracts (K=100) relative to perfect-hindsight selection, ranging 0–100%.

Results: In Massachusetts, GP and BST led on MAE/RMSE, but BST had higher %BPR (62.0% vs. 58.2%), potentially pre-identifying 18 additional fatal overdoses per year. In Cook County, gradient boosted trees had better MAE/RMSE than GLM but worse %BPR (77.1% vs. 79.4%), with GLM reaching 15 more events annually. A tuned historical average baseline performed competitively in both areas, within uncertainty intervals of top models.

Discussion: The authors argue advanced models may not outperform simple tuned baselines, recommend including historical averages in future studies, and emphasize intervention-aware metrics for prioritizing intervention. Software, preprocessing code, and a cleaned Cook County dataset were released publicly. Limitations include only two jurisdictions, a fixed K=100, BPR's inability to prioritize rate of change, and reliance on SVI covariates; alternative sources such as EMS calls and insurance claims may warrant further covariate consideration.

The Relative Strength Index (RSI), introduced by J. Welles Wilder in 1978, is a 0–100 momentum oscillator that measures price gains and losses over a chosen period, commonly 14 days. In CFD trading, it helps identify overbought and oversold conditions, potential reversals, and mean-reversion opportunities. CFDs allow traders to speculate on price movements without owning the underlying assets and are described as zero-sum trades.

Standard RSI interpretations use readings below 30 as oversold and above 70 as overbought. For day trading, shorter intervals such as 15 or 30 minutes and more extreme thresholds of 15 and 85 may be used. However, settings should reflect the asset, time frame, market trend, and strategy; no universal thresholds guarantee success.

The passage emphasizes backtesting RSI strategies with historical data and the intended asset classes. Backtests of rules for SPY produced 313 trades averaging 0.86% but with significant drawdowns. A modified two-day strategy using an RSI threshold below 10 and a sell trigger based on the prior day’s high produced 355 trades averaging 0.67%, with smaller, smoother drawdowns. A trend-following strategy using a 100-day look-back and 14-day RSI generated fewer signals.

Other considerations include using RSI divergences as potential buy or sell signals, combining long- and short-term RSI readings, pairing RSI with volume or other indicators, and accounting for commissions, slippage, taxes, leverage, and stop losses.

Adam Piore, author of *The Body Builders*, explains that humans have long used substances to sharpen the mind, and science now understands their mechanisms: caffeine blocks sleep-promoting adenosine, while nicotine mimics acetylcholine to boost attention. Current efforts to go further include Tim Tully's project—funded by Ken Dart—to develop a "memorization pill" by studying people with exceptional recall and sequencing their genomes; Tully has already engineered fruit flies with photographic memories using CREB activators. Other researchers are searching for the hundreds of genes involved in intelligence in hopes of genetic enhancement, though many are skeptical. Scientists are also developing deep brain stimulation devices that alter neuronal firing and monitor brain activity to detect and correct abnormal states such as panic attacks or episodes preceding depression or psychosis. These technologies remain in development and raise dystopian concerns.

The passage documents host-environment requirements and integration procedures for AMD AGESA™ software in BIOS and UEFI environments. The host must establish a valid stack, populate the standard header and AMD_CONFIG_PARAMS, and use published entry-point identifiers from AMD.H. Binary-module calls pass through a host bridge that locates the binary image and invokes the AMD dispatcher. AGESA call-outs are funneled through a host-implemented router, whose address is stored in the standard header; the router maps function identifiers to host procedures.

UEFI execution spans the SEC, PEI, DXE, and runtime stages. SEC establishes the C environment, 32-bit execution mode, and stack. PEI uses separate processor, memory, and reset-coordination PEIMs, with PPIs and HOBs reporting initialization progress. DXE performs late initialization, generates informational tables, publishes the AGESA DXE protocol, and supports iGPU VGA resource decoding. AGESA core files are arranged into libraries for 16-bit SEC, 32-bit SEC/PEI, and 64-bit DXE/runtime builds, using MASM, ml, and CL tools.

Two build methods are described: binary modules provide an indirect dispatcher-based interface, while source integration incorporates AGESA source into the host ROM build. Platform-specific options and build-control files must be copied and customized. Required environment variables identify the AGESA source directory and platform build-options directory. Files in the Addendum directory are reference examples and are not included directly in builds.

Assembly stack macros support x86-64 pre-memory operation. AMD_ENABLE_UEFI_STACK allocates and initializes a per-core stack in cache-as-RAM, configures memory types and MTRRs, creates the UEFI SEC-to-PEI handoff frame, and supports real or protected mode. The procedure is stackless, preserves EBX, and may be called on every core. A separate teardown procedure disables the pre-memory stack after main memory and the PEI core are available. AArch64 systems using the Platform Security Processor instead rely on the PSP to initialize DRAM and do not use these stack and early macros.

The API includes AmdCreateStruct and AmdReleaseStruct for allocating, initializing, and releasing parameter structures using pre-memory heap, post-memory DRAM, or host-provided storage. Other services obtain DIMM data-eye results, APIC and PCI addresses, available execution-cache size, current socket/die/core identity, FRU memory-device locations, and event-log entries, and allow requested MMIO ranges to be merged. Initialization entry points perform minimal reset-time processor setup, full processor initialization, environment setup, main-memory initialization, late graphics and table configuration, and suspend/resume handling. BSP and application-processor responsibilities are separated during initialization.

AmdInitReset performs basic processor initialization and allocates up to three executable flash regions under address, size, alignment, and boundary rules. Its parameter structure must be host-allocated before the heap is operational, and cache controls must not be changed from reset through the final return from AmdInitPost. AmdInitPost initializes and enables memory, transfers artifact data into main memory, disables the pre-memory stack, and establishes final cache behavior. AmdInitRtb prepares suspend-state registers and allocates processor save-state storage, while resume procedures restore memory, registers, silicon state, and MTRRs before OS handoff.

Required host call-outs include AgesaAllocateBuffer and AgesaDeallocateBuffer. After main memory initialization, the allocation call-out must provide the requested buffer size or larger, report the actual size and address, support runtime-persistent allocations when requested, and account for any host-reserved space during deallocation. Host code must also provide required PEI services, preserve data across the pre-memory to post-memory transition, restore MTRRs, transfer critical and volatile suspend data to suitable storage, and avoid modifying MTRRs or APIC registers while processor cores are communicating in parallel.

Former Langley City mayor and Liberal MLA Peter Fassbender is considering another mayoral run, with a decision expected by late July or early August. He previously served as mayor and councillor before winning a Surrey-Fleetwood seat in 2013.

The speaker accepts a high national office as an honor and solemn responsibility, recognizing the nation’s unusual worldwide difficulties following a period of unprecedented prosperity. He credits republican institutions, peace, and just policy for advances in agriculture, commerce, manufacturing, public finances, and national development. Although the United States maintained justice and impartial neutrality, the belligerent powers’ retaliatory edicts and violence disrupted the country. Confident in the nation’s resolve and supported by its citizens and representatives, he pledges to preserve peace, uphold neutrality, pursue amicable settlements, defend the Constitution and states’ rights, protect religious liberty and individual rights, reduce public debt, maintain limited military forces, encourage commerce, science, information, and the civilization of Indigenous peoples, and rely on divine guidance.

The Supreme Court agreed to review whether a defendant who waived his right to appeal in a plea agreement may challenge a mandatory mental-health medication condition after the trial judge said he had appeal rights. The Fifth Circuit had dismissed his appeal. Arguments are likely early next year, with a decision expected by summer.

The Colorado Supreme Court affirmed a judgment awarding real estate brokers their commission. The brokers had produced Mrs. Charles Tallman as a purchaser of property owned by George W. and Della B. Thuro. Although Della signed the purchase contract for George without written authority and George later refused to ratify or sign it, he could not defeat the brokers’ commission by refusing to be bound by the sale.

Whether Mr. Tallman was also bound was immaterial because Mrs. Tallman was unquestionably a purchaser and the brokers had fulfilled their duty. Any variance between the pleading and evidence concerning the Tallmans’ obligations was harmless because the defendants anticipated the issue and no substantial rights were affected. The court also held that requested jury instructions concerning immaterial issues were properly refused, and any error in failing to strike material from the brokers’ pleadings was harmless.

Yankees rookie Cam Schlittler struck out 12 and allowed five hits over eight scoreless innings against Boston, the first MLB pitcher to combine those figures without walking anyone. Scout Matt Hyde, who first saw him at Northeastern, called the performance “unbelievable” and “surreal.”

Montecito Union School District agreed to pay $7.5 million to settle a lawsuit brought by two brothers who alleged that former superintendent and principal Stanford Kerr sexually abused them in the 1970s. The brothers, now 65 and 68, had sought $35 million; a third plaintiff settled separately for $1 million. The district admitted no liability. The settlement equals about 40% of the 350-student district’s 2025-26 budget. Montecito said it will cover the cost through a hiring freeze, staff reductions as positions turn over, and capital-repair funds, avoiding layoffs. It has no insurance for the relevant period.

The case followed California’s 2019 removal of filing deadlines for child sexual-abuse claims against public agencies, which school districts say could produce billions in liabilities. A proposal to restore a statute of limitations failed, and its sponsor plans to revive it. The California School Boards Association gave Montecito $50,000 for legal costs. A judge had scheduled 17 trial days before the settlement, with a final hearing set for Nov. 19.

The study compared Statistical Parametric Mapping (SPM) with an explainable convolutional neural network (CNN) for detecting technical and procedural outliers in multicenter plantar-pressure data. Data from 703 participants included static and dynamic recordings from both feet, collected using resistive and capacitive pressure plates. After preprocessing to 64×64 normalized images, experts labeled 1,031 samples as valid or one of four outlier types: general acquisition error, double-foot capture, inverted orientation, or incorrect side annotation. Synthetic anomalies expanded the dataset to 2,798 samples.

The SPM approach registered each image to a foot-specific reference and used pixel-wise nonparametric testing with cluster-based false-discovery correction. The CNN used pressure images and foot-side metadata, with SHAP providing pixel-level explanations. Both methods were evaluated through subject-grouped nested cross-validation using F1 score and Matthews correlation coefficient. Sixteen experienced evaluators subsequently compared the explanations in a randomized semantic-differential survey.

The CNN outperformed SPM, achieving an F1 score of 0.99 and MCC of 0.96, compared with 0.93 and 0.78 for SPM. Both approaches produced false positives primarily for valid feet with pathological characteristics; SPM also frequently missed incorrect side annotations. CNN performance was lowest for heterogeneous general acquisition errors.

Evaluators rated both explanation types positively, including their clarity, correctness, usefulness, relevance, understandability, trustworthiness, and completeness, with no statistically significant differences between approaches. SPM was descriptively rated as simpler, while SHAP received the highest preference at 43.48%, followed by SPM at 34.78% and their combination at 17.39%. The results support both methods as promising tools for automated plantar-pressure quality control, while indicating a need for improved alignment, more homogeneous error categories, realistic synthetic anomalies, broader XAI comparisons, and further human-centered validation.

The passage argues that percentage thresholds for market labels—such as a 5% dip, 10% correction, 20% bear market, and 30% crash—lack rational or empirical support and do not help investors manage risk, deploy capital, or identify market cycles. Examples from 2011 and 2015 show different indexes crossing these thresholds at different times. Instead, the author defines secular bull and bear markets as 10- to 20-year periods combining market performance, long-term economic trends, and investor psychology. Bull markets feature economic growth, rising revenues and earnings, declining volatility, and expanding price-to-earnings multiples; bear markets feature challenging economics, increased volatility, cyclical market moves, and contracting multiples. The author estimates that multiple expansion accounted for three-quarters of the 1982–2000 bull market’s gains, underscoring the importance of valuation psychology over earnings growth alone. Investors should focus on what is driving markets rather than conventional labels or pundits.

Trump’s planned 100% tariffs on branded pharmaceuticals did not take effect. The administration said it will prepare tariffs for companies that neither build U.S. infrastructure nor agree to drug-pricing terms, without providing a timeline. Pharmaceutical executives are receiving near-daily outreach from the White House, HHS, and Commerce Department as the administration seeks industry agreements ahead of the 2026 midterms. Eli Lilly, Pfizer, and AstraZeneca are among the companies being asked to increase U.S. production or consider a U.S. headquarters.

The passage outlines defensive fundamentals and strategies for a high-post split offense built around a high-post split followed by down screens. Basic defense emphasizes guarding the post with or without the ball, disrupting screens, denying handoffs and direct routes, and protecting the low post. In the Show & Recover approach, guards sag one stride in front of the high post while wings provide help. When the post receives the ball, the post defender pressures them toward their weak-hand corner; wings show against down screens, guards chase, and defenders recover into pass-denial positions. Most NBA teams show and recover rather than switch because switching could leave the screener posting against a smaller defender. Matchup principles include hard pressure on the ball, physical post-fronting, and packing weakside defenders toward the ball. The All Out SOS strategy instead pressures handlers toward the sideline, denies high-post entry, switches during splits and down screens, and traps wing or low-post passes. Its later phases use smothering, contact switches, wing double-teams, coordinated rotations, closeouts, and post traps.

Deutsche Bank is seeking to sell its 8.8% stake in Dubai-based Abraaj Holdings, which it regards as a non-core asset. The sale has become more urgent as the bank restructures and scales back its global equities business. Abraaj faces investigation by four investors, including the Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation and IFC, over alleged misuse of money in a $1 billion healthcare fund; it denies wrongdoing and is considering selling part or all of its investment unit. Undisclosed debt complicates valuation, though one banker said the unit could be worth up to $500 million. Abraaj is under cashflow pressure, and its private-equity CFO and COO have resigned.

The article examines the metaverse’s potential, benefits, limitations, and implementation requirements in education. It describes the metaverse as a hybrid virtual platform encompassing augmented reality, lifelogging, mirror worlds, and virtual reality. Educational applications include immersive simulations, experiential and collaborative learning, personalized instruction, virtual field trips, and safe practice in hazardous fields. Limitations include difficulty monitoring students, increased mental effort, limited learning differences from traditional media in some cases, infrastructure and device requirements, teacher preparation, health concerns, and low institutional readiness.

The study used an online survey of 333 teachers in Türkiye. Participants completed a 28-question questionnaire developed by the researchers and reviewed by three educational-technology experts. Responses were examined through descriptive statistics and thematic analysis. The survey assessed teachers’ metaverse knowledge, experiences, perceptions, intended applications, preferred implementation timing, and perceived obstacles.

Teachers’ average metaverse knowledge score was 5.25 out of nine. Although 78.1% reported prior metaverse-related experience, this generally involved virtual reality or three-dimensional virtual worlds rather than the contemporary metaverse concept. Teachers followed related studies moderately, held generally positive educational attitudes, and recognized advantages including realistic practice environments, student engagement, learning by doing, exposure to new technologies, reduced educational limitations, digital competence, and personalized learning.

Teachers also expressed significant concerns, particularly technical problems, addiction and other psychological issues, unequal access, data security, teacher readiness, preparation difficulties, physical problems, cost, classroom management, and content availability. Despite these concerns, teachers showed willingness to use the metaverse, strong interest in training, and perceived their lessons as suitable for it. Information technology, physics, biology, chemistry, and mathematics were considered particularly suitable, especially for experiments, abstract concepts, collaborative learning, and realistic simulations.

Teachers generally regarded education-system stakeholders as unprepared, with students perceived as relatively more ready. Most predicted widespread effective implementation within three to five years. The article concludes that metaverse education has transformative potential but requires reliable infrastructure, accessible devices and content, sustained teacher training, attention to physical and mental health, collaborative planning, gradual implementation, user-feedback mechanisms, and clear behavioral expectations.

The “Flash/Back Door” attack targets the middle weakness of a Box & One defense. A baseline post player flashes into the middle; if no shot develops, the offense uses high/low post action and a wing back cut, or a post flash that opens a drop or fake-shot pass. When the flash produces no shot, it flows into single/double screen continuity. Variations include a base screen for the star player, a ballhandler entry pass to the wing followed by a corner cut, and elbow passes to create back cuts. Success requires coordinated screens, post-ups, communication, timing, and experience. Coaches should scout defensive reads, observe adjustments, vary alignments and entries, and move players against weaker defenders. In Box & One, four defenders cover the box while a chaser denies passes and rebounds.

NVIDIA Corporation filed a Form 8-K on February 11, 2015, announcing financial results for the fourth quarter and fiscal year ended January 25, 2015. The filing furnished a press release and CFO Colette M. Kress’s commentary, which were not deemed filed under specified securities laws and would not be incorporated by reference into NVIDIA’s SEC filings.

The speaker praised his wife’s resilience and called the birth “amazing.” After a hockey teammate was hit, the team regrouped, played hard for him and Dino, and won, showing its competitiveness. He noted criticism of a Drury hit and expected league review of Holmstrom’s elbow to the head.
The speaker says their MCL has healed, an injury still needs surgery after the series, and a brace will help. They feel ready to return and hope he heals quickly.

H.B. Fuller VP Traci L. Jensen sold 5,397 shares on October 2 at an average price of $58.40, totaling $315,184.80. The specialty chemicals company reported quarterly EPS of $0.65, below the $0.67 consensus estimate, and revenue of $562.87 million versus $553.66 million expected. It had a 4.76% net margin, and analysts expect $2.59 in EPS for the fiscal year. H.B. Fuller announced a $0.15 quarterly dividend, equivalent to $0.60 annually and a 1.06% yield. Analyst ratings include two sells, five holds and one buy, with an average “Hold” rating and $57.40 consensus price target. Institutional investors own 92.37% of the company’s stock. H.B. Fuller formulates, manufactures and markets adhesives, sealants and other specialty chemical products across six business segments.

On August 17, India’s Supreme Court will hear Prasad Purohit’s challenge to his rejected bail and a victim’s father’s bid to cancel co-accused Pragya Singh Thakur’s bail, citing similar facts requiring detailed hearing. The NIA had cleared Thakur but called charges against Purohit serious.

This medRxiv preprint (posted January 2, 2025; not peer-reviewed) introduces LUKB Disease Trajectory (LUKB DT), a web tool built on the R Shiny package and integrated into the authors' LUKB UK Biobank data preparation platform, designed to identify disease trajectories from electronic medical records (EMRs). Trajectories reveal the temporal order of disease occurrences and can expose risk factors, disease progression, and mechanisms. LUKB DT has four components: (1) Input data — EMR upload requiring participant IDs, diagnoses, and diagnosis dates, plus parameters including the exposure, minimum disease prevalence, study start/end dates, adjustment variables, and follow-up period; (2) Disease filtering — Cox regression with the exposure as a time-varying covariate retains only diseases with increased risk associated with the exposure; (3) Disease pair detection — binomial tests identify candidate pairs with temporal order (p < 0.05, Bonferroni-adjusted, conditional risk > 1) and determine directionality; (4) Disease pair validation — conditional logistic regression on case-control datasets matched on variables such as sex and age confirms pairs with a positive coefficient for the first disease. Confirmed pairs are concatenated into trajectories (e.g., D1 → D2 → D3).

Case study: using UK Biobank ICD-10 data (6,166,668 records, 446,995 individuals, 1,943 conditions; 45.2% male; ages 48.57–85.57 on January 1, 2020) with COVID-19 (U071) as exposure (January 1, 2020 to October 31, 2022; minimum prevalence 0.005; 0-day gap; 1 case matched to 2 controls), 183,386 individuals (8,411 with COVID-19) and 274 diseases were analyzed. Cox regression identified 90 diseases significantly associated with COVID-19 across 19 ICD-10 chapters, with no immune-related diseases. These formed 8,010 pairs; 2,410 showed temporal association, 527 passed directionality testing, and all 527 were confirmed by conditional logistic regression. Resulting trajectories showed COVID-19 leading mainly to SARS-CoV-2-related conditions (B97, J12, J96, Y95) and other medical care (Z51); the authors note UK Biobank data may underrepresent COVID-19 status and long-term (auto)immune consequences.

Benchmark: the full run took 55 minutes on 8 cores (Cox regression 11.4 minutes, trajectory identification/confirmation ~1 minute, conditional logistic regression 42.3 minutes) on an Intel Core i9-9900K, 32GB RAM server.

Limitations: the tool depends on processed records such as ICD-10 codes with timestamps, generated trajectories may not match real patient trajectories, and prevalence-based pair relationships require comprehensive, representative datasets. The authors recommend using LUKB DT primarily for investigating risk factors and mechanisms rather than patient clustering.

Children with developmental language disorder, autism, or migrant-language needs require tailored language support, but speech-language therapists and educators face challenges providing consistent, varied linguistic input. Earlier robot-assisted language learning systems are often static or rule-based and have limited adaptability, speech recognition, turn-taking, and nonverbal interaction capabilities.

TalBot is a prototype that integrates ChatGPT with the Furhat conversational robot to lead the Alias word-retrieval game. It generates clues and feedback, interprets mispronunciations, redirects unrelated conversation, manages turn-taking, and displays emotions. Testing with 13 preschool children with language vulnerabilities and seven educators indicated that it could manage three-child gameplay and adapt to speech-recognition errors. Voice data were temporarily processed by Microsoft Azure under an approved risk assessment.

The proposed expansion targets morphological learning by generating adaptable linguistic materials, consistently modeling target grammar, and demonstrating structured input for educators. Planned work includes laboratory co-development with children and educators, preschool field studies comparing TalBot with educator-led sessions, a feasibility study with 5–10 children, and assessment of user perceptions. Longer-term goals include randomized controlled trials and teaching multiple morphological structures across languages. Ethical, data-protection, cost, motivation, and institutional implementation concerns remain.

NVIDIA Corporation announced first-quarter fiscal 2016 results for the quarter ended April 26, 2015, including a press release and CFO commentary. On May 5, NVIDIA announced plans to wind down its Icera modem operations in the second quarter of fiscal 2016, while remaining open to selling the technology or operations. The board approved the decision on May 4. If no sale occurs, NVIDIA estimates restructuring charges of $100 million to $125 million, primarily in fiscal 2016, for severance, employee benefits, tax expenses, and other wind-down costs; actual amounts and timing may differ.

David Ellison said he has deep respect for CBS News and wants it to become a highly trusted news destination serving center-left and center-right Americans. His comments followed his acquisition of The Free Press and appointment of commentator Bari Weiss as CBS News editor in chief. While denying political interference, he offered few specifics about how the network would build trust.

School officials from the Grand Erie and Brant-Haldimand-Norfolk Catholic district school boards met coaches and physical-education teachers to discuss a possible district-wide high school sports league by 2019-20. The proposal would equalize games, rules and opportunities across public and Catholic schools. Currently, only football has some cross-county play. No plan or timeline is final, and travel costs and time remain concerns.

The passage describes AGESA host-environment integration, build procedures, UEFI components, and service interfaces. In binary-image builds, AGESA call-out functions use a common interface port whose router is implemented and loaded by the host environment. The router translates function numbers into execution addresses and accepts a function identifier, function-specific data, and a configuration pointer containing the standard header. Most services require an established stack.

UEFI execution spans SEC, PEI, DXE, and runtime stages with 32-bit and 64-bit variants. AGESA core files are organized into libraries for these targets and can be built as binary modules or integrated directly into host source builds. Platform-specific options are selected through `<plat>Options.c`, recovery settings through `<plat>RecoveryOptions.c`, and IDS support through `OptionsIds.h`. Reference files in the Addendum directory are not included in builds, while UEFI control files must be integrated into platform build systems. Required environment variables include `AGESA_ROOT` and `AGESA_OptsDir`. Integration requires enabling Cache-as-RAM before `AmdInitReset`, using the `ByHost` allocation method, and avoiding modifications to SS, ESP, or cache controls until `AmdInitPost` completes.

In PEI, the SEC phase establishes the C execution environment and stack, including the required `AMD_ENABLE_UEFI_STACK` procedure. Processor initialization is divided into early and post-reset PEIMs. The early PEIM initializes processor components and publishes `AmdCpuEarlyInitPPI`; the post-reset PEIM initializes memory, publishes `AmdInitPostPPI` and a memory-information HOB, and signals completion through `AMD_MEM_INIT_PPI`. A separate reset-coordination PEIM checks whether other PEIMs request a warm reset and then publishes a reset-complete event. During DXE, late initialization generates AMD data tables and publishes `AgesaDxeProtocol` for access by other drivers. The VGA-control driver enables processor-GPU resource decoding only when requested through the PciIo protocol.

Native assembly stack macros establish pre-memory per-core stack regions in Cache-as-RAM, map them globally, configure MTRRs, and create a UEFI SEC-to-PEI handoff frame. A corresponding teardown procedure disables the stack after relocation and flushes caches. These routines do not apply to AARCH64 APUs using the Platform Security Processor.

Host-service procedures allocate and initialize AGESA structures using pre-memory, post-memory, or host-provided storage, with corresponding release required. Other services provide DIMM data-eye bitmaps, APIC and PCI addresses, pre-memory execution-cache size, current socket/die/core identification, FRU memory-location details, MMIO range updates, and sequential retrieval of event-log entries from a circular buffer.

The passage reflects on Kildare students completing college forms by February, noting that at 17 nobody is expected to know their future path and that uncertainty is reasonable. It warns that careers chosen now may not last to retirement, as technology will reshape many industries over the next 40–50 years, making work tied to petrol and diesel engines riskier and electrical engineering more promising. The central advice is to make one's work a valuable commodity by asking what makes you worth more than minimum wage, cultivating expertise or scarce knowledge, and adding value to your own bank balance, since employers generally seek maximum output for minimum reward. Finally, it cautions against expecting work to be enjoyable every day, stressing that life outside work is what matters.

The push-pull converter design uses Type 2A frequency compensation targeting a 10 kHz crossover frequency, with a power-stage transconductance of 16.2 A/V. Seven 330-µF polymer tantalum capacitors provide the required 2.3 mF output capacitance and have a combined ESR of 0.86 mΩ. Selected compensation values are 40.2 kΩ for RCOMP, 15 nF for CCOMP, and 47 pF for CHF; compensation is typically tuned during testing. Slope compensation is applied through the RSC pin and set equal to the output inductor’s falling slope, using a 102-kΩ resistor between RSC and AVSS.

The controllers operate from a regulated 4 V to 14 V input supply. A minimum 0.1-µF VIN-to-AVSS bypass capacitor is required, with X5R or better ceramic capacitors placed close to the controller and additional bulk capacitance when the supply is remote.

Layout guidelines include keeping feedback away from magnetics and the switch node, minimizing switch-node copper and high-d/dt loops, separating analog and power grounds except at one connection point, and using short, wide, high-current traces of at least 15 mils per ampere. Filtering, bypass, and compensation components should be placed near their associated pins. VSENSE divider components should be close to the controller, while high-dv/dt OUTA, OUTB, SRA, and SRB traces should be separated from sensitive signals. RC filtering may be needed at CS_ILIM, and SYNC requires careful routing from HICC; the HICC-to-AVSS capacitor should be at least 3.3 nF. For CFP packages, backside metallization should connect to the AVSS plane through multiple vias.

The document also provides application curves, PCB layout examples, support and documentation-update information, ESD precautions, revision history, and mechanical, packaging, and orderable information.

Cover 2 is a zone defense used in a 4-3 formation, with two corners and three linebackers covering underneath routes and two safeties splitting the field into deep halves. It protects against short passes and receiver screens while allowing defenders to read routes and maintain vision of the quarterback. Its hard corners also help against perimeter runs. Weaknesses include multiple vertical routes, trips formations, and certain run concepts. Against a 2x2 formation, only one linebacker remains in the box, while against trips, the weak-side overhang is removed. Assignments include flat zones for corners, deep halves for safeties, and hook/curl or middle zones for linebackers. Variants include Switch, which reverses the roles of corners and safeties, and a disguised 1-high look that actually uses two high safeties.
Emirates reversed its plan to drop the in-flight Hindu meal after customer feedback, especially from Hindus, who may still choose vegetarian and non-vegetarian regional meals.

Sharp, Anderson, and Lang conducted a bibliometric co-occurrence analysis of author-supplied keywords from 1,076 articles published in the Information Systems Education Journal from 2003–2024. Using VOSviewer, they created term maps for four five-year periods, 2023–2024, and the full corpus, identifying topic clusters through keyword frequency and link strength.

The analysis traces shifts from curriculum, assessment, accreditation, and ethics in 2003–2007 to pedagogy and student concerns in 2008–2012; cybersecurity, big data, analytics, and pedagogy in 2013–2017; COVID-19-related topics, business and data analytics, and capstones in 2018–2022; and artificial intelligence, analytics, and pedagogy in 2023–2024. The 2008–2012 period had the greatest topic diversity, while the partial 2023–2024 period had fewer clusters. Across the full network, pedagogy and curriculum remained central.

The study identifies limitations including reliance on author-selected keywords and possible inflation of terms through special issues. It recommends future analyses incorporating titles and abstracts, data-driven definitions of topical eras, and continued monitoring of artificial intelligence and generative AI research.

On November 27, 2001, FERC approved NYISO’s request to extend its Automated Mitigation Procedures (AMP) through April 30, 2002, rather than October 31, 2002, with a waiver making the extension effective November 1. Enron had opposed NYISO’s request. The AMP prospectively mitigates bids within the day-ahead market process when conduct and price-impact thresholds are met, eliminating the one-day delay inherent in manual mitigation.

FERC required NYISO to file a comprehensive mitigation proposal by March 1, 2002, effective May 1. The proposal must address AMP refinements and coordination with existing and proposed mitigation measures, including potential gaps or inconsistencies and must-run mitigation consistent with ISO-NE and PJM. NYISO must also examine whether AMP barriers affect new generation, whether new generators should be exempt, and how other energy-limited resources, including environmentally constrained resources, should be accommodated.

FERC noted NYISO’s commitments to exempt bids of 50 MW or less unless market power is demonstrated and to limit mitigation to zones and hours that fail the impact test. It urged NYISO to collaborate with PJM and ISO-NE on a unified Northeast mitigation plan. New York regulators and consumer groups supported the extension, while several generators, including Enron, protested it.

The disclosure describes an image-processing method, apparatus, electronic device, and computer-readable storage medium for placing a two- or three-dimensional target model, such as an advertisement, into video frames. A target three-dimensional model is placed on a selected plane in a first video frame and adjusted so designated surface feature points lie on that plane. The feature points’ world-space three-dimensional coordinates and first-frame pixel coordinates are recorded to determine the first frame’s camera pose.

For each subsequent frame, the target plane is tracked, and homography matrices map the feature points from the first frame to their positions in the current frame. The homography can be optimized using image correlations, with the preceding frame’s optimized matrix serving as an initial estimate for the next frame; occluded pixels may be excluded. Current-frame feature coordinates, their three-dimensional coordinates, and camera intrinsic parameters are then used, for example through a perspective-n-point algorithm, to determine the current camera pose. The target model is positioned and projected into each frame, and the frames are synthesized into a target video.

The target plane may be identified through neural-network segmentation and user selection or manually selected. The target model’s pose may be adjusted manually or automatically with AI. Implementation may occur on terminal devices or servers, and relevant video, advertisement, and processing data may optionally be stored in a blockchain. The disclosed plane-tracking approach reduces computation, supports faster and more convenient operation, accommodates limited texture, small brightness changes, occlusion, and large viewpoint changes, and does not require large video parallax.

New York’s Excelsior Scholarship Program is changing how students and families compare public and private colleges by making tuition free at SUNY and CUNY institutions for eligible graduates from households earning under $110,000. The last-dollar program covers $6,670 in annual tuition but not fees, housing or books; its income ceiling will eventually rise to $125,000. With $118 million budgeted for an estimated 27,000 students, Excelsior is encouraging greater interest in public colleges, particularly regional private colleges that cannot match the advertised price.

Private institutions are responding with aid and other initiatives. Canisius College reduced tuition by about $8,000 after enrollment fell roughly 6%. Roberts Wesleyan guarantees qualifying students will graduate in four years or it will pay remaining schooling costs and guarantees at least $8,000 annually in merit aid for four years. Le Moyne’s Promise NY offers New York students $10,000 over four years, a four-year degree guarantee, an internship and an alumni mentor. St. Bonaventure increased scholarships by up to $4,000 per student annually.

Despite these responses, private-college administrators say Excelsior creates an imbalance favoring public schools. Some advocate expanding the state Tuition Assistance Program so private institutions could also receive greater aid. More selective colleges, including Columbia, Cornell and Rochester, have been less affected, while Fisher and Nazareth reported strong recent enrollment. Students still weigh cost alongside academic programs, atmosphere and personal fit, with some choosing private colleges despite the availability of free public tuition.

The Federal Reserve proposed changes to the Volcker Rule that would apply its strictest requirements to banks engaged in the most trading, reducing regulatory uncertainty for those banks. The rule bars banks from making risky proprietary trades with depositors’ money and was created under Dodd-Frank to help prevent another financial crisis and taxpayer-funded bailout. The proposal comes amid broader deregulation under President Trump, including Congress’s rollback of Dodd-Frank and reduced Volcker Rule compliance for roughly two dozen banks. The "offside trap" is a defensive maneuver in which all defensive backs move upfield in unison just before an opponent is about to pass to a leading striker, leaving that striker in an offside position. If the striker receives the ball and gains an advantage from that position, the play is called under Law 11 (Offside), resulting in an indirect free kick to the defending team. Introduced in the 1900s and adopted widely around mid-century, the trap has grown riskier as interpretations of the offside law changed and attackers shifted toward short inter-passing rather than through balls; attackers "not involved in active play" are now less likely to be penalized.

Because all backs step forward, only the goalkeeper remains behind, so failure exposes the goalkeeper. Common causes of failure include a defender not moving in unison, leaving the attacker onside, and an attacker standing still to avoid interfering with play so an onside teammate plays the ball.

Coaches must weigh the benefits against the risks, requiring mature players who understand the offside law, a mentally strong goalkeeper, and a formation suited to execution; a flat-back-four is more conducive than a stopper-sweeper alignment. Effective use depends on practice, repetition, experience, and familiarity. Coaches must specify whether the trap applies in normal run of play, on free kicks, or both, and identify the conditions for calling it.

Back defenders must line up straight across the field, parallel to the halfway line, forming the "line of offside," know teammates' and strikers' positions, anticipate forward passes, recognize the signal, and communicate constantly. At least one attacker must be in the defensive half and ahead of the ball.

One designated defender, usually the upfield defensive coordinator, calls the trap, verbally or non-verbally; non-verbal signals such as raising an arm are preferred in noisy stadiums. On the call, backs step forward three to five yards instantly to create clear separation. Clues include leading attackers starting forward runs and the passer looking down at the ball. Practice should vary situations and include beating the trap. Over-use risks the opponent learning to counter it — "live by the trap, die by the trap" — and opponents may have scouted the signal, requiring changes between games.

Gary Gensler frames blockchain technology through Bitcoin, Bitcoin’s first major use case, and identifies its core components as cryptography, consensus mechanisms, and transactions. He describes fiat money as a social or economic consensus and ledgers as systems for recording transactions or balances. Bitcoin functions as a peer-to-peer transaction ledger without a trusted central authority, although he notes that centralized intermediaries may be preferable in some circumstances.

Bitcoin’s central design is a timestamped, append-only log of blocks. Each block links to its predecessor through a hash, making alterations detectable. Consensus determines which node may add the next block. Bitcoin uses proof-of-work mining, nodes, nonces, networking, and economic incentives to maintain and update the ledger. Block-production intervals vary across blockchains.

Cryptographic hash functions map inputs of any size to fixed-size outputs and are deterministic, efficiently computable, preimage-resistant, collision-resistant, avalanche-like, and puzzle-friendly. Bitcoin principally uses SHA-256. Hash functions compress transaction data, connect blocks, support commitments, and help reveal tampering. They make the system highly secure but not absolutely immutable, since cryptographic systems could eventually be broken or replaced.

Block headers contain a version number, the previous block’s hash, a Merkle root, a timestamp, and a difficulty target. Merkle trees hash and compress transaction data into a root summarizing many transactions. A Merkle root changes when transaction contents change, but not merely because another header field changes. Full nodes store and validate transaction data, while lightweight clients can operate using compact block headers.

Asymmetric cryptography uses public-private key pairs. A digital signature is created from a message and private key and verified with the corresponding public key. In Bitcoin, the public key is derived from the private key using elliptic-curve cryptography, making recovery of the private key computationally infeasible. Secure random-number generation is essential for key creation. Bitcoin addresses are distinct from public keys and are produced by hashing the public key twice, adding a checksum, and encoding it in Base58.

Mining creates Bitcoin as an incentive for proof-of-work participants. The issuance reward began at 50 Bitcoin per block, was halved to 25 and then 12.5, and is subject to a finite limit of 21 million. Mining pools spread mining risk and rewards, while competition encourages miners to seek low-cost electricity. Bitcoin also addresses the double-spend problem through its consensus process.

Transactions contain inputs and outputs, with inputs referencing earlier transactions, values denominated in satoshis, and outputs directing funds to public keys. Timestamped append-only logs predate Bitcoin, including work published through the New York Times. Updating Bitcoin’s software, including replacing a compromised hash function, requires consensus among network nodes rather than a central authority. Subsequent lectures are to address proof of work, nodes, native currency, consensus protocols, and transactions.

In 2007, SunPower was a leading commercial producer of high-efficiency photovoltaic cells, but its CEO Tom Werner questioned how to preserve its advantage amid rapid industry growth, larger competitors, emerging technologies, and questions over pricing, process improvement, and vertical integration.

Solar power’s appeal rested on energy independence and environmental benefits, particularly concern over carbon dioxide, global warming, and fossil-fuel pollution. The Kyoto Protocol and expanding carbon markets supported emissions reductions, while governments worldwide implemented more than 1,000 pro-solar policies, including subsidies, renewable portfolio standards, and favorable purchase arrangements. Global PV demand rose from 114 MWp in 1997 to 2,500 MWp in 2006. Cell efficiencies increased from below 4% when commercial cells first appeared in the 1950s to 10–20% in 2006. Japan and Europe led shipments, while China became the third-largest producer and exported more than 90% of its PV products.

The solar value chain included silicon, ingots and wafers, cells, modules, and system installation. Rapid demand created a silicon shortage, raising input prices and wafer thicknesses declined. Major producers included Sharp, Q-Cells, Kyocera, Sanyo, and Mitsubishi Electric. Solar electricity generally cost 25–50 cents per kWh, compared with 4–6 cents for conventional generation, making subsidies, tax credits, rebates, and favorable feed-in tariffs important. Residential and commercial rooftop systems had emerged as important markets, although large utility-scale projects faced operational and financial difficulties.

SunPower was founded in 1987 to commercialize solar concentrators but abandoned that approach. Projects for Honda’s solar-powered race car and NASA’s Helios aircraft demonstrated its cells’ efficiency but also showed that survival required production scale. A partnership with Cypress Semiconductor beginning in 2001 brought semiconductor manufacturing expertise, enabled commercial production in late 2004, and preceded SunPower’s November 2005 NASDAQ listing. SunPower produced about 20 MW in its first commercial year and expected 65 MW in 2006. Revenue rose from $6 million in 2004 to $78.8 million in 2005 and was projected above $220 million in 2006; the second quarter of 2006 was its first profitable quarter.

SunPower’s core capability was its commercially highest-efficiency solar cell in 2006. Its back-contact design placed metal contacts behind the silicon, increasing sunlight absorption and producing an all-black appearance. The design generated more power within limited roof space, reduced installation requirements, and commanded at least a 10% panel premium. Its disadvantages were a manufacturing process requiring about twice as many steps as typical processes and capital expenditure of roughly $1 per watt. The company targeted average cell efficiency of at least 22% by early 2007 and sought further gains through thinner wafers and reduced silicon use per watt.

SunPower expanded downstream into modules, wafer manufacturing, and installation. It secured a long-term silicon supply through an agreement with DC Chemical, formed a Chinese ingot-manufacturing joint venture, and acquired large-installation specialist PowerLight for $335 million. Competition included market leader Sharp, fast-growing Q-Cells, fully integrated REC Group, thin-film producer First Solar, expanding Chinese manufacturer SunTech, and business-model challenger Citizenre. The case concludes that SunPower faced a difficult and evolving competitive environment requiring a carefully chosen strategy to sustain its technology lead and reduce costs.

A hockey player from Brick, New Jersey, chose New Hampshire over Michigan because it was closer to home. He is happy with the decision, plans to stay while preparing for the NHL, and is excited to play next year.

Equity represents ownership in a corporation and a claim on its future cash flows. Investors can receive value through dividends—cash or stock distributions—or through capital gains from selling appreciated shares. Growth companies often retain cash for investment rather than pay dividends.

Unlike bonds, common stock gives shareholders unlimited upside after bondholders are paid and limits their losses to the amount invested. Limited liability encourages entrepreneurship and repeated business attempts. Voting rights and access to public markets help finance large projects, while short selling incorporates negative information into prices and improves market efficiency.

Equity markets are divided into primary markets, where securities are first issued, and secondary markets, where existing securities are traded. IPO activity varies with business and credit cycles, whereas secondary-market trading has grown substantially. Internet trading, electronic communications networks, electronic order routing, and faster, cheaper electronic execution have increased participation and reduced trading costs, disadvantaging firms unable to compete technologically.

The Dividend Discount Model values a stock as the present value of its expected future dividends, discounted at risk-adjusted rates that reflect both the cash flows’ risk and market conditions. Because equity cash flows and discount rates are uncertain and may change over time, valuation is more difficult than bond valuation. Market-determined discount rates should correspond to the risk of each cash flow; companies do not set these rates independently, although their policies affect dividends and growth.

With constant dividends and a constant discount rate, stock price equals \(D/r\). With dividends growing at rate \(g\), the Gordon Growth Model gives \(P=D_1/(r-g)\). The model requires \(r>g\) for meaningful perpetual value. When expected growth approaches the discount rate, valuations can become very large, and changes in growth expectations can cause sharp price increases or crashes, as illustrated by expectations surrounding cold fusion and its potential impact on energy companies.

Rearranging the model shows that the required return equals the dividend yield plus the expected growth rate, emphasizing that a company’s value includes growth opportunities and innovation beyond current dividends. The model works best for steady-state dividend policies; changing dividends require the general model or separate valuation of different periods.

Accurate forecasting is inherently difficult, so the simplified formulas have limited usefulness for companies without dividends or stable earnings. Corporate managers need cost-of-capital estimates to allocate funds and compare opportunities, while investors use required returns to assess compensation for risk. Companies generally avoid cutting dividends because doing so signals distress and may be costly, although temporary suspensions can occur during cash shortages and exceptional dividends may follow major asset sales.

- The ADS868xW is a 16-bit SAR ADC data-acquisition device with single-ended or differential, bipolar or unipolar inputs. Its integrated analog front end includes a programmable gain amplifier, ADC driver, precision reference buffer, overvoltage protection, and a second-order antialiasing low-pass filter.

- Each analog input has a resistive impedance of at least 1 MΩ, independent of ADC sampling and input-signal frequencies, allowing sensor outputs to connect directly without low-impedance drivers. Matching the AIN_P source impedance with an equivalent resistance on AIN_M helps reduce offset error. Internal overvoltage protection uses input resistors and antiparallel diodes; external devices are still required for surge, ESD, and EFT protection. With AVDD at 5 V, the internal protection supports inputs up to ±20 V; with AVDD floating, the stated limit is ±15 V. Higher source impedance further reduces protection-diode current but can increase gain error and system noise.

- The PGA supports nine input ranges selected through RANGE_SEL_REG, with a default range of ±3 V × VREF. Its trimmed resistor network limits gain error. A second-order antialiasing filter at the PGA output typically has a −3 dB cutoff of 500 kHz. An integrated high-bandwidth, low-noise buffer drives the ADC.

- The internal reference has a nominal 4.096 V output and is enabled by default through INTREF_DIS; REFIO requires at least 4.7 µF of decoupling. External-reference mode applies 4.096 V to REFIO, while the internal buffer drives REFCAP, which requires 10 µF plus a nearby 1 µF decoupling capacitor. Reference accuracy can shift after mechanical or thermal stress, including PCB solder reflow. Both references are specified over −40°C to +125°C, and the reference-buffer temperature drift is typically 0.5 ppm/°C with a maximum of 2 ppm/°C.

- ADC output uses straight-binary format, with LSB size equal to FSR/2^16. Alarm functions monitor the analog input against programmable high and low thresholds with adjustable hysteresis, and monitor AVDD against fixed typical trip points of 4.7 V and 5.3 V. Active and tripped alarm flags are available through ALARM_REG, the ALARM output pin, or appended data flags. Active flags update after each conversion, while tripped flags remain set until ALARM_REG is read.

- The multiSPI interface presents the device as a 32-bit input/output shift register and supports four legacy SPI modes, optional dual-SDO output, and source-synchronous operation with internal or external clocking. A transfer frame begins with the falling edge of CONVST/CS and ends with its rising edge, when the input command is decoded and conversion begins. A 32-clock frame is optimal; short frames cannot execute writes, while long frames use the last 32 shifted bits as the command. Daisy-chained devices require identical configuration and a frame of 32 × N clock-capture edges for N devices.

- The device operates in RESET, ACQ, and CONV states. Its active-low RST input can initiate either an application reset or a full power-on reset. Nine 32-bit configuration registers control device identification, reset and power management, SPI input and output protocols, output data and flags, reference and range selection, alarms, and alarm thresholds. RST_PWRCTL_REG writes are protected by first writing 69h to address 05h.

- An industrial input-module example combines an ADS8681W with an eight-channel MUX36D08 differential multiplexer to support software-configurable voltage or current channels. It uses the ADC’s input alarms for NTC-thermistor temperature monitoring. The device uses separate AVDD and DVDD supplies and requires 1 µF high-frequency bypass capacitors plus at least 10 µF bulk decoupling on each supply. Programmable NAP and power-down modes reduce consumption at lower throughput. Recommended PCB layout separates analog and digital routing, keeps bypass and reference capacitors close to their pins, and uses short, low-impedance ground paths.

This protocol outlines a systematic review of prospective and retrospective observational cohort studies evaluating the implementation or redesign of Rapid Response Team (RRT) services in hospitals. It will examine how services are introduced or changed, reasons for changes, implementation timelines, implementation methods, and measures used to assess success. Searches will cover Medline, CINAHL, Embase, Cochrane Library, Google Scholar, reference lists, conference abstracts, and expert contacts. Two reviewers will independently screen studies, extract data, and assess risk of bias using the JBI checklist, with disagreements resolved by discussion or a third reviewer. Extracted data will cover study and team characteristics, implementation methods, and quantitative and qualitative outcome assessments. Results will be synthesized narratively, supplemented by simple statistics and additional analyses in SPSS where appropriate, and reported according to PRISMA. The review is registered on medRxiv, requires no ethical approval, and has no external funding. Limitations include heterogeneity in team names, composition, resources, and outcome reporting, as well as potentially limited evidence on service implementation and change management.

Asia-Pacific equities extended April gains, supported by increased investor risk appetite, French election results, easing North Korea concerns and strong Asian earnings. Indian stocks led, and MSCI’s ex-Japan index neared a two-year high. ML Electronics, CITIC Securities and TSMC reported stronger profits.

An October 25, 2001 collection of news reports says Enron replaced CFO Andrew Fastow with Jeff McMahon, head of Industrial Markets and a former treasurer, placing Fastow on leave. Kenneth Lay said the change was needed to restore investor confidence amid scrutiny of Fastow’s role in the LJM Cayman and LJM2 partnerships. Enron reported a $35 million loss and a $1.2 billion reduction in shareholder equity from ending ties to the partnerships, alongside third-quarter losses of $1.01 billion. The SEC began an informal inquiry into the transactions, while shareholder lawsuits alleged inflated asset values, concealed related-party dealings and insider trading; Enron denied wrongdoing.

Enron shares fell 17% to $16.41, roughly halving since October 16, and other energy traders also declined. Analysts said the leadership change might help credibility but warned that unclear partnership liabilities, possible off-balance-sheet obligations, credit downgrades, asset sales and share issuance remained risks; several downgraded the stock. McMahon reportedly had previously objected to Fastow’s conflict of interest. The email also includes opinion pieces and brief reports on small-cap stocks, utilities, broader markets and proposed grading of corporate directors.

Air cargo containerization enables goods to remain in containers during transport and is used by commercial airlines and military forces. Market growth is driven by demand for rapid global shipments, advances in lightweight container technology, expanding cargo fleets, and increased defense transportation needs. The global economic slowdown and rising aviation fuel costs, which reduce cargo flight hours, are major restraints. The market is segmented by refrigerated and non-refrigerated containers, narrow-body, wide-body, very large, and military aircraft, commercial and defense end users, and six geographic regions. Major vendors include Nordisk Aviation Products, Zodiac Aerospace, VRR Aviation, Satco, Cargo Composites, Granger Aerospace, Chicago Metal Fabricators, PalNet, ACL Airshop, and DoKaSch.

The passage criticizes China’s examination-oriented family education for prioritizing grades and discipline while neglecting children’s characters, moral development, practical abilities, emotional stability, and individual interests. It reports that many children cannot perform basic household tasks, while some adolescents face emotional, behavioral, and interpersonal problems. Comparisons between Chinese and American primary education are presented as evidence that rigid, disciplined learning can stifle development.

Recommended reforms include freeing children to pursue their interests, sharing higher-education resources, teaching them to give selflessly and contribute to society, and improving the moral and humanity education that Chinese families once prioritized. Traditional Chinese moral teachings—integrating moral education with personal cultivation, connecting knowledge with practice, and viewing humanity as part of nature—are presented as relevant to modern education.

The passage also emphasizes nature, physical activity, religious or spiritual faith, and closer parent-child relationships. Family outings, travel, games, and conversations can build trust, bridge generational gaps, and support children’s well-being. Parents, including mothers whose roles are changing as women enter the workforce, should provide proper guidance and model constructive behavior. Overall, education should combine knowledge with moral character, personal freedom, social responsibility, and healthier family relationships.

A comprehensive geoarchaeological study of Egypt’s Karnak Temple complex reconstructed how the site evolved over roughly 3,000 years. Researchers analyzed 61 sediment cores and tens of thousands of ceramic fragments, finding that Karnak began on an island formed by ancient Nile channels. Before about 2520 BCE, regular fast-flowing floods made the site unsuitable for permanent occupation, while pottery evidence supports occupation during the Old Kingdom.

As the surrounding channels diverged and accumulated sediment, space became available for the temple to expand. New construction occurred over older riverbeds, and ancient Egyptians also appear to have redirected the river by depositing desert sand into channels to create building land. The eastern channel was more substantial than previously recognized. The island’s emergence from surrounding waters resembles an Old Egyptian creation myth in which divine high ground rises from a “lake,” suggesting the location may have held religious significance for Theban elites. The team is extending the research across the wider Luxor floodplain to examine ancient landscapes and waterscapes.

This passage is an excerpt from the Texas Instruments datasheet for the TPS7H500x-SP (TPS7H5001/2/3/4-SP) radiation-hardness-assured peak current mode PWM controller family, covering detailed device operation, application guidance, and mechanical information.

**Output voltage programming (8.3.6):** Output voltage is set with a resistor divider from VOUT to the VSENSE pin, divided down to the 0.613 V reference; 1% or better resistors are recommended for accuracy.

**Soft start (8.3.7):** The error amplifier follows the SS pin voltage until it rises above VREF, then soft start is complete; SR outputs activate once the SS pin reaches 1 V. A capacitor from SS to AVSS sets soft-start time (ISS = 2.7 µA typical).

**Switching frequency and synchronization (8.3.8):** Three modes exist — internal oscillator (RT resistor to AVSS, 100 kHz–2 MHz, SYNC outputs a clock at 2× switching frequency), external synchronization (RT floating, clock applied to SYNC at twice the desired frequency, 200 kHz–4 MHz, 40–60% duty cycle, 50% recommended), and primary-secondary (one controller's SYNC clock feeds another's SYNC input, allowing synchronization of two independent converters or an interleaved converter). The secondary inverts the clock, giving a 90° or 270° phase shift.

**Outputs (8.3.9–8.3.10):** Devices offer single (OUTA) or dual (OUTA/OUTB) primary outputs and single (SRA) or dual (SRA/SRB) synchronous rectifier outputs, each with roughly 150 mA peak current capability requiring external gate drive. OUTB/SRB are only active with the DCL pin tied to AVSS (50% duty limit) and only on the TPS7H5001-SP and TPS7H5004-SP.

**Dead time, LEB, pulse skipping, duty cycle (8.3.11–8.3.13):** TPS7H5001/2-SP program two independent dead times (PS, SP resistors to AVSS, 8 ns minimum, 10 kΩ–300 kΩ resistors); TPS7H5003-SP has fixed 50 ns dead time and LEB, while others program LEB via a resistor from LEB to AVSS. A pulse-skipping mode prevents minimum on-time issues at high frequency. DCL configures maximum duty cycle: 100% (DCL→VLDO), 75% (floating), or 50% (DCL→AVSS).

**Current sense, hiccup, fault, slope compensation, thermal (8.3.14–8.3.19):** CS_ILIM senses primary current against COMP/2 (150 mV offset) and sets a 1.05 V current limit threshold triggering hiccup mode, which charges CHICC until 0.6 V, stops switching, and restarts with soft start once HICC falls to 0.3 V (minimum CHICC of 3.3 nF). The FAULT pin shuts down the converter above 0.6 V with a 0.4–1.4 µs pulse-width qualification and a frequency-dependent restart delay. Slope compensation via RSC mitigates subharmonic oscillation (recommended at 1× the inductor falling slope). Type 2A or 2B compensation is selectable using RCOMP, CCOMP, and optional CHF. Thermal shutdown stops switching above 175 °C and restarts below 160 °C.

**Design example and application guidance (9.x):** A 500 kHz GaN synchronous push-pull converter is designed around the TPS7H5001-SP, with RTOP = 10 kΩ/RBOT = 1.4 kΩ for 5 V output, 25 ns dead time (20.5 kΩ), ~50 ns LEB (49.9 kΩ), 33 nF soft start (~7.5 ms), 2.5 turns ratio, 40 µH primary inductance, 170 V primary and 80 V secondary GaN FETs, 0.47 µH output inductor, ~2.3 mF output capacitance, 7.5 Ω sense resistor, 3.3 nF hiccup capacitor, Type 2A compensation (40.2 kΩ, 15 nF, 47 pF), and 102 kΩ slope compensation resistor. Input supply range is 4–14 V with at least 0.1 µF VIN bypass; layout guidelines address feedback/switch-node routing, ground separation, component placement, and thermal-via connection of the CFP package's backside metallization.

The remainder covers ESD caution, support resources, revision history (Revisions D–F), and mechanical, packaging, orderable, and tape-and-reel information with Texas Instruments disclaimers and notices.

The Nobel Prizes, first awarded in 1901, honor major scientific discoveries but cover only narrow fields and a small number of scientists. Many disciplines—including ecology, oceanography, weather, climate and geology—do not fit the prize categories. Winners are typically white men from wealthy regions such as the United States and Western Europe, reflecting unequal research funding and barriers faced by women and underrepresented groups. In 2023, Katalin Karikó became one of only 13 women awarded the physiology or medicine prize for her mRNA work.

Because prizes recognize discoveries rather than people and can be shared by at most three recipients, many contributors may go unrecognized. Nobel laureates are often laboratory heads whose careers span decades before nomination, potentially overlooking collaborators without their own labs. Although committees seek broad international nominations and work to limit bias, Alfred Nobel’s will constrains the prizes, making major reform unlikely. Despite their limitations, the prizes remain influential in celebrating science and encouraging public interest in research.

The passage is from a patent application concerning deep-learning systems for genomic splice-site classification and aberrant-splicing detection. It identifies priority and related U.S., PCT, and provisional applications and incorporates several earlier patent applications and technical publications by reference.

The disclosure describes convolutional neural networks (CNNs), including convolution layers, pooling, nonlinear activations such as ReLU, batch normalization, residual and skip connections, global average pooling, and backpropagation-based training with gradient descent, stochastic gradient descent, or adaptive optimizers. It also explains dilated or atrous convolutions, which provide large receptive fields with few trainable parameters and capture long-range sequence dependencies.

For splice-site detection, an atrous convolutional neural network (ACNN) is trained using donor, acceptor, and non-splicing examples. It receives nucleotide sequences with surrounding genomic context and outputs scores for each target nucleotide’s likelihood of being a donor site, acceptor site, or non-splicing site. Implementations include SpliceNet80, SpliceNet400, SpliceNet2000, and SpliceNet10000, which use progressively larger context windows and multiple groups of residual blocks. The ACNN’s dilation rates progress non-exponentially, and convolution-window sizes vary among residual-block groups. Residual blocks may include batch normalization, ReLU layers, atrous convolution layers, and residual connections.

The disclosure also describes conventional CNN implementations for splice-site detection. These models use convolution, subsampling, nonlinear, and fully connected layers, produce triplet classification scores, and may be trained on large donor, acceptor, and non-splicing datasets. Both ACNN and CNN systems may use one-hot encoding, batch-wise training over multiple epochs, parallel processors, separate training and production servers, and client-facing deployment.

Aberrant-splicing detection compares splice-site scores generated from reference and variant nucleotide sequences. Position-wise score differences above a predetermined threshold classify a variant as causing aberrant splicing and therefore being pathogenic; differences below the threshold classify it as benign. Thresholds may be selected using benign common variants and pathogenic rare variants. The comparison can identify differential splicing patterns such as cryptic splicing, exon skipping, mutually exclusive exons, alternative donor or acceptor sites, and intron retention. Applications described include detecting variants associated with autism spectrum disorder and developmental delay disorder.
