The article tests whether market timing works for Bitcoin by comparing buy-and-hold with scenarios that remove selected trading days from January 2015 through September 2021. A $10,000 buy-and-hold investment would have grown to $2.05 million, a 126% CAGR. Removing the ten best days reduced the result to $246,000 and a 63% CAGR; removing the ten worst days increased it to $11.6 million and a 196% CAGR. Removing the best day of each month—81 observations, or 3.3% of the dataset—left only $1,854 and a negative 22% CAGR. These results illustrate how compounding and a few missed days can drastically change long-term performance. The article concludes that market timing is likely futile for long-term Bitcoin investors, who are advised to invest available capital and hold. For traders, however, buy-and-hold may be an inappropriate benchmark because leverage, drawdowns, Sharpe ratio, and low correlation can produce different objectives.

Will Ma reviews selected hands from a recently played $55 Party Poker tournament, alternating between empirical analysis and poker theory. He focuses primarily on preflop reraising strategies and how bet sizing should change with board texture.

Beginning with king-queen offsuit in position at an effective stack of about 28.5 big blinds, Ma explains that decisions should be based on ranges and overall strategy rather than on the hand alone. He considers raising, calling, mixing value hands with calls, and using weaker hands as bluff-raises. Purely value-raising predictable hands allows opponents to fold too often, while purely calling with weaker hands makes a raise or reraise profitable. Polarizing can preserve stronger calling hands for future streets, but it may be exploitable when opponents recognize a range’s missing ranks or board weaknesses. Ma therefore offers no fixed formula, recommending a balanced mixture of raising, calling, and bluffing that changes with stack depth and opponent tendencies.

Applying this approach, Ma bluff-reraises king-queen and wins the pot when his opponent folds. In a similar situation with pocket jacks, an earlier bluff-raise makes the opponent undervalue a later all-in with pocket sevens, allowing Ma to double up. He also analyzes folds with ace-queen and ace-jack, calls with weaker hands that receive favorable implied odds, and several unsuccessful all-in calls against strong ranges. Other hands illustrate missed river bluffs, profitable backdoor draws, reverse-implied-odds problems, and the risks of calling out of position. He repeatedly acknowledges mistakes, including checking a hopeless queen-high hand instead of bluffing and calling with ace-jack when a raise and fold would have been preferable.

Ma then explains that boards range from “dry” to “drawy.” Dry boards, often paired or lacking flush and straight possibilities, permit smaller bets, slow-playing, and attempts to disguise hand strength. Drawy boards contain many flush or straight outs, so larger bets are generally preferable to deny opponents favorable odds; value hands should often get money in quickly, while weak hands with few outs should avoid speculative bluffs. He applies this distinction by criticizing a small flop bet on a drawy queen-jack board as too small and a large bet on a dry queen-ten board as unnecessarily risky, while favoring larger bets when he has strong flush draws.

Additional observations include using backdoor draws to support continuation bets, recognizing how an opponent’s ace can block bluff-catcher combinations, and understanding that effective stack depth affects both reraising and all-in decisions. Ma concludes that the lesson’s two main principles are to adjust bet sizing according to board texture and to use mixed, balanced preflop reraising strategies rather than a rigid rule.

The TPS7H500x-SP family consists of radiation-hardness-assured, current-mode PWM controllers for space-grade DC-DC converters. They require external gate drivers, support switching frequencies up to 2 MHz, and can be used with buck, flyback, forward, active-clamp forward, push-pull, and full-bridge topologies.

A 500-kHz synchronous push-pull converter design using the TPS7H5001-SP and GaN FETs specifies a 205-kΩ frequency resistor, 5-V output divider resistors of 10 kΩ and 1.4 kΩ, approximately 25-ns dead time using 20.5-kΩ PS and SP resistors, and a 49.9-kΩ leading-edge blank-time resistor. A 33-nF soft-start capacitor provides approximately 7.5-ms startup. The transformer design uses a 2.5 turns ratio and 40-µH primary inductance. Primary GaN FETs are rated at 170 V for a 36-V maximum input, while an 80-V synchronous rectifier is used on the secondary side; a parallel Schottky diode can reduce soft-start and dead-time losses. Other selections include a 0.47-µH output inductor, at least 1.3 mF of output capacitance, and 2.3 mF total for radiation-induced single-event-transient mitigation. The example uses seven 330-µF polymer tantalum capacitors and an optional output filter. Cycle-by-cycle limiting is reported at roughly 35 A, with a 1:100 current-sense transformer and 7.5-Ω sense resistor. A 3.3-nF hiccup capacitor is used. Type 2A compensation targets a 10-kHz crossover and uses 40.2-kΩ RCOMP, 15-nF CCOMP, and 47-pF CHF resistors/capacitors; a 102-kΩ resistor sets slope compensation.

The controller supply range is 4–14 V and requires at least a 0.1-µF VIN-to-AVSS bypass capacitor, with X5R-or-better ceramics placed close to the controller and additional bulk capacitance for remote supplies. Layout guidance emphasizes isolating feedback and other sensitive signals from switching nodes, minimizing high-dv/dt and high-di/dt loop areas, separating analog and power grounds except at one connection, using wide and short current paths of at least 15 mils per ampere, placing filtering and compensation components near their pins, and using multiple vias to connect the CFP package’s backside metallization to AVSS.

The document also provides application curves, PCB layout examples, links to evaluation-module guides and radiation reports, support information, ESD cautions, revision history, and mechanical, packaging, and orderable information.

The Hawk Offense is a successful set offense derived from the UCLA high-post rub and shuffle offense. Introduced to the NBA by Hubie Brown in Atlanta, it primarily exploits off-guard mismatches while also supporting wing isolations and post-ups. Its basic action begins with a point guard dribble entry, followed by an off-guard cut from a high-post screen.

The high-post shuffle cut includes counters for defenses that chase over or under the screen, switch, anticipate and zone, show and recover, or double-team. These responses include hard basket cuts, bump-backs, post rolls, post isolation, corner isolation, slips, break-off cuts, drop passes, kick-out passes, and early ball reversals. When the primary action does not produce a shot, a reversal and down-screen action develops the weak side through post flashes, low-post isolation, back cuts, and post exchanges.

Continuities provide organized late-clock movement and maintain spacing, rebounding position, and second-effort opportunities. Flex uses continuous baseline and down screens, including “pick the picker” action. The Triangle Game emphasizes inside screening with wing shooters and can use smaller players to create mismatches. The Motion or Passing Game relies on continuous movement, screen-away actions, and an open middle for penetration and cuts.

Common variations include the Side Screen, Single/Double, Back Screen, Pin Down, Base Screen, and Post Lob. These adaptations allow the high post and off guard to exchange positions, create post opportunities, exploit size mismatches, or attack defenses that overplay reversals.

Successful implementation depends on spacing, execution, coordination, timing, non-verbal communication, and recognition of defensive responses. The ball handler, screener, and receiver must function as one unit. Teaching is recommended through a whole-part-whole approach, combination drills, scrimmages, game-within-the-game situations, and individual fundamental work. Game strategy includes scouting opponents, identifying expected defensive reads and counters, monitoring defensive adjustments, varying alignments and entries, attacking weaker on-ball and off-ball defenders, and using organized screen continuity as the clocks wind down.

Arizona officials found plague-carrying fleas in Taylor and warned of them in Coconino County. The Navajo County Health Department advised avoiding rodent burrows and sick or dead animals, leashing dogs, routinely defleasing pets, and using insect repellent. Grin, a secretive blockchain project using Harry Potter-themed identities, is intended to host Mimblewimble, a “scriptless” privacy technology derived from Blockstream’s Confidential Transactions. Mimblewimble cancels spent outputs against new ones, allowing historical inputs and outputs to be discarded while preserving key-based authentication and ensuring that no new coins are created. This compresses blockchain history but removes arbitrary scripts, limiting spending to transfers between people or groups.

Blockstream mathematician Andrew Poelstra proposed “scriptless scripts,” extending Mimblewimble with signature-based conditions. Schnorr-signature differences can enable atomic swaps without extra blockchain space or an explicit transaction link, while chained signatures and discrete logarithms may support Lightning-like channels. Poelstra also developed a way to link transactions across different elliptic curves, including Bitcoin and Monero.

Mimblewimble was not yet practically usable because it lacked wallet support. Grin’s maintainers accepted Poelstra’s proposal for soft-forking digital assets, including a Bitcoin peg, with Grin and a test currency planned first. He estimated the wider ecosystem might use the project in about 18 months. A Mimblewimble sidechain would initially be larger like Bitcoin plus Confidential Transactions, but its verification data would shrink as spent outputs and inputs were deleted.

Gamma-ray observations probe high-energy astrophysical processes and directly indicate emission sources because gamma rays are not deflected by magnetic fields. Earth’s atmosphere absorbs cosmic gamma rays, so satellites such as AGILE and Fermi are used for direct detection, while ground-based imaging atmospheric Cherenkov telescopes measure Cherenkov light from atmospheric showers. Their large effective areas enable detection of fainter, higher-energy events, and images are used to reconstruct gamma-ray properties and reject charged-cosmic-ray backgrounds.

The Cherenkov Telescope Array Observatory (CTAO) is planned to provide full-sky coverage, improved energy and spatial resolution, and observations from 20 GeV to 300 TeV. It will use 23-m Large-Sized Telescopes for 20–150 GeV, 12-m Medium-Sized Telescopes for 150 GeV–5 TeV, and numerous 4.3-m Small-Sized Telescopes for 5–300 TeV. Its Northern and Southern Arrays will be located at La Palma and in Chile, respectively, with prototypes and further upgrades under development. During its first decade, 40% of observing time will be reserved for Key Science Projects.

WIMP searches are a major CTAO program, targeting the Galactic Center, the Large Magellanic Cloud, the Perseus Cluster, and dwarf spheroidal galaxies. Simulations indicate that CTAO could strengthen constraints on TeV-scale annihilation cross sections by about one order of magnitude for conventional searches and by several orders of magnitude for monochromatic-line searches. These observations require careful background modeling and high angular and energy resolution.

CTAO will also study active galactic nuclei to constrain cosmological photon-propagation effects, including axion-like particle oscillations, intergalactic magnetic fields, extragalactic background light, and Lorentz-invariance violation. Simulations of NGC 1275 indicate potential sensitivity to axion-like parameters, although current constraints are not highly competitive and may improve with other targets or analysis methods.

**Background:** In November 2015 Brazil declared a public health emergency over rising Zika virus (ZIKV) cases. Prenatal ZIKV infection during 2015–2016 was linked to offspring with microcephaly, brain malformations, hearing loss, locomotor disability, and increased risk of in-utero fetal death, leading to the recognition of congenital Zika syndrome (CZS). No prenatal treatment or prevention standards exist, and differing outcomes among dizygotic twins suggest genetic influences on susceptibility to brain injury.

**Purpose:** This scoping review aimed to identify candidate genes associated with brain injury following prenatal ZIKV infection.

**Methods:** Following PRISMA and PRISMA-P guidance, searches were conducted in PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, Academic Search Ultimate, Agricola, Health Source: Nursing/Academic Edition, Psychology and Behavioral Sciences Collection, and CINAHL, with no language restriction. Experimental, analytical observational, and descriptive designs were eligible; gray literature, reviews, duplicates, and studies addressing only host dependency/resistance factors unrelated to prenatal brain injury were excluded. Three independent reviewers screened records in Rayyan, with a third reviewer resolving disagreements; the protocol is registered on OSF.

**Results:** Of 7,985 records identified, 3,777 were screened and 13 articles were included, describing 23 candidate genes—six maternal (TREM1, IL4, ADCY3, ADCY7, IL28B, TLR3) and 17 fetal/neonatal. Findings included reduced expression of DDIT4L, FOXG1, and LHX2 in affected twins; a CDK5RAP2 mutation; associations involving NOS2 rs2297518, miR-124-1 rs531564, TP53, TNF, and VEGFA haplotypes; a likely causal MTOR rs2295079 variant; maternal IL28B rs8099917 and TLR3 rs3775291, and infant TNFa rs1799964; and no significant differences in AXL, TLR3, or STAT2. Candidate genes relate to neurodevelopment, angiogenesis, cell cycle regulation, and immune/inflammatory response.

**Discussion:** Limitations include small cohorts due to disease rarity, reliance on candidate gene rather than genome-wide approaches, and difficulty isolating CZS-specific risks among infected individuals. Findings do not support a monogenic model; functional analyses and larger, pooled replication studies are recommended. Because these genes govern neurodevelopment, they may also be relevant to CMV, HSV, and SARS-CoV-2 brain injury. Late or absent markers such as microcephaly and calcifications delay diagnosis, underscoring the need for multilevel research toward predictive models and possible neuroprotective strategies. NIH funding; no conflicts declared.

Fayose accused the federal government of deliberately withholding Ekiti’s January budget support to weaken the state. He criticized the 2017 budget for favoring the Southwest little and urged governors to cooperate on regional development and address herdsmen and hunger.

Former New York Judge Louis L. Nock joined Anderson Kill last month, citing family considerations and a looming mandatory retirement at age 70, the firm said. He joined the same day the New York State Commission on Judicial Conduct agreed to drop ethics charges against him in exchange for his resignation from the bench and his promise never to accept judicial office again; the agreement was made public Sept. 25, and his resignation was effective Sept. 2. Written complaints alleged Nock often acted in a rude, demeaning and unprofessional manner toward court staff and threatened to file grievance and criminal complaints against commission staff and witnesses unless the charges were dismissed. Nock denied all allegations, and both the firm and his lawyer, Malcolm S. Taub, noted no findings of wrongdoing were made. Nock served as a New York City civil court judge from 2015 and became an acting supreme court justice in 2018. Taub said Nock had planned to leave the bench, had been exploring new jobs for years and had at least two opportunities when he resigned.
Canada’s TSX fell 14 points to 16,263 as lower oil prices reversed earlier gains. Global and U.S. stocks also declined amid tech weakness and trade-war concerns.

The California Supreme Court reversed an order revoking Iturea Atwood Hicks’s letters of administration and appointing H. B. Sanders in her place. Hicks was the decedent’s widow and sole surviving spouse; the estate inventory valued the entire estate at $390, below the statutory limit of $1,500. Sanders sought revocation solely for failure to publish notice to creditors within two months, at the request of the decedent’s sister and niece, neither of whom had an interest in the estate.

The court held that the revocation provision must be read together with the statute allowing a widow to receive an estate valued at no more than $1,500, after which no further administration proceedings or creditor notice are required. Because the widow was entitled to the entire estate, failure to publish notice to creditors did not justify revocation, and the sister and niece could not invoke court procedures to seek an administration that would only reduce the widow’s inheritance.

Researchers analyzed surveys from 5,800 Finnish public-sector employees who retired between 2000 and 2011. The proportion reporting sleep difficulties fell from 30% before retirement to 26% afterward. Overall, sleep problems were 11% less likely after retirement; early-morning awakenings were 24% less likely, and nonrestorative sleep declined 53%. Little change occurred in difficulty falling or staying asleep. Average sleep duration increased by about 20 minutes, or 45 minutes among those with prior sleep difficulties or heavy alcohol use. Improvements were greatest among retirees with poor health or stressful working lives, suggesting that reduced work stress and changes in sleep timing may contribute.

The SEC began a preliminary inquiry, reported by the Los Angeles Times, into whether California energy consultants advising Gov. Gray Davis traded power-company stocks using nonpublic information. The review followed a request from Secretary of State Bill Jones, a Republican gubernatorial rival. Five consultants were fired over possible conflicts after disclosures showed they owned Calpine or Enron shares while negotiating state power purchases. Spokesman Steve Maviglio also disclosed buying 300 Calpine shares worth $12,000 and holding Enron stock; he said his purchases relied on public information, denied a conflict, and was willing to divest. Jones called the purchase unethical and urged updated financial disclosures. Separately, political consultants Mark Fabiani and Chris Lehane agreed to forgo state compensation and leave the administration under a taxpayer lawsuit settlement concerning their work for both Davis and Southern California Edison.

India’s state electricity boards lost 260 billion rupees, or $5.5 billion, because of rising subsidies and power theft. Enron and AES sought government buyouts of their Indian projects. Enron offered its 65% stake in the stalled $2.9 billion Dabhol project to the Indian government or lenders, and India began evaluating the proposal. The government directed IDBI-led financial institutions to arrange financing or a new investor to complete the project; lenders had committed $320 million, leaving $230 million needed. The plant remained idle amid a payment dispute with Maharashtra State Electricity Board, which disputed Enron’s tariffs.

Houston-area internet providers prepared for the expected resurgence of the Code Red worm, which targets older Microsoft IIS servers and could slow websites, deface pages and generate denial-of-service traffic. An available Microsoft security patch had not been widely installed.

Research warns deep ripping reduces compaction but may not improve water penetration and can worsen dry, repellent topsoil. A 2016 trial found soil inversion or rotary spading more effective. Recommendations include waiting for rain before cereals, increasing seeding rates, applying banded wetting agents, and using rotary spaders or mouldboard ploughs.

Juan Palacios and Siqi Zheng explain how climate risk is incorporated into real-estate values and markets. Empirical evidence presented suggests that climate-related price discounts are driven more by changes in perceived risk and capitalization rates than by immediate rent or net-operating-income changes. Properties exposed to high flooding, sea-level-rise, or similar risks were reported to sell for roughly 3% less without corresponding rent reductions. Research following Hurricane Sandy found housing-price penalties of about 8–9% in affected areas, including larger discounts for severely damaged properties, although studies differ on whether these effects persist or later reverse. Commercial-property results were also said to vary.

Climate risk also depends on beliefs about future hazards. Climate projections and discount rates are used to calculate expected losses and determine whether resilience investments have positive net present value. A Boston Seaport example projected damages rising from about $140 million to $8 billion under increasing sea-level-rise scenarios, while proposed protection could require roughly $500 million to $1 billion in initial investment and substantial maintenance. Because projected damages may occur decades in the future, the selected discount rate can substantially change the investment decision.

The lecture reviews methods for estimating these effects. Hedonic regressions control for property characteristics, but omitted factors correlated with flood risk—such as waterfront views, neighborhood conditions, or insurance—can bias estimates. Matching compares similar properties, while difference-in-differences compares treated and untreated areas before and after a climate event. Difference-in-differences relies on a parallel-trends assumption and uses control areas to estimate what would have happened without the event. A Hurricane Sandy study applied this approach to New York City transactions and flood-damage data.

Climate beliefs vary geographically and politically. Yale Climate Opinion Maps and surveys show substantial differences in the share of residents accepting climate change, and research discussed in the lecture found larger flood-zone housing discounts in communities where climate risk was more widely believed. The speakers warned that private developers may rationally favor lower-belief communities to reduce perceived climate-related costs, but concentrated development in hazardous areas can shift losses to residents, insurers, lenders, and the wider public.

Information disclosure is presented as a way to reduce this asymmetry. Climate-risk information is being added to property-sale disclosures, with research cited indicating that disclosure can prompt households to leave risky areas, reduce demand, and increase housing vacancy. Other projects use natural-language processing to measure social-media sentiment and trace how information about climate disasters spreads through social networks.

Digital leaders view data culture as central to business performance, emphasizing learning, transparent data access, clear metrics, and organizational alignment. Strong cultures reinforce consistent beliefs, company values, and daily employee behavior, with leadership beliefs shaping company values and actions. Digital laggards often struggle to align behavior with stated ambitions because of entrenched habits, skill gaps, and insufficient leadership focus; changing mindsets is typically the hardest part of transformation. However, digital laggards can advance by building on existing strengths and targeting specific areas. Successful data cultures value learning, risk-taking, transparency, and measurement, while requiring changes in core beliefs about employees’ capabilities. Organizations generally fall into four patterns: data novices, insight-ready firms, tech-enabled firms, and data-reliant firms, each needing targeted development to build a strong data culture.

A medRxiv preprint proposes a high-impedance microstrip transmission-line resonator for multichannel RF arrays at 10.5T. Two 8 × 8 cm elements were built from 3 mm copper tape on 2 mm Teflon and evaluated using network-analyzer measurements and Ansys simulations. The high-frequency mode was tuned to 447 MHz and matched to 50 Ω using a tunable capacitor. With elements spaced 10 mm apart, it achieved −21 dB interchannel coupling, while the 116 MHz mode coupled more strongly at approximately −7.6 dB. At a 2 mm gap, the low-frequency peak split from strong coupling, whereas the 447 MHz mode remained decoupled. Simulations showed distinct B1 distributions per channel and a maximum B1+ of 2 μT/√W. The results support the design as a practical, robust approach for high-frequency transceiver arrays in ultrahigh-field MRI.

Facebook apologized and removed search auto-fill predictions that included sexual acts involving minors. The company said the predictions reflected what people might search for, not platform content, and reiterated that sexually explicit imagery is prohibited. Facebook also called a policy survey about adult requests for sexual pictures from a 14-year-old girl a mistake. Separately, data on 50 million users was reportedly exposed during the 2016 presidential race, followed by an 8.1% stock decline.

Amazon.com, Inc. filed a Form 8-K on April 30, 2020, announcing its first-quarter 2020 financial results. The filing includes Exhibit 99.1, the results press release, and Exhibit 99.2, information regarding non-GAAP financial measures, and was signed by Senior Vice President and CFO Brian T. Olsavsky.

The authors argue that AI-optimized master scheduling can help school districts manage declining enrollment, shrinking budgets, and rising student needs. Lubbock and Edgewood districts used AI to analyze class sizes and teacher workloads, generate scheduling options, and make student-centered decisions. The changes saved $2.2 million across 14 Lubbock schools and $1.05 million districtwide in Edgewood, while allowing both districts to avoid layoffs and reinvest savings in academic priorities. They say AI supports rather than replaces human judgment, enabling scheduling teams to focus on strategic decisions and helping districts allocate resources more effectively.

Investors have piled into record-high bets against sterling amid Brexit uncertainty. Nomura warns that sterling’s average 2% April rise over 12 years could hurt short sellers. Record short positions eased slightly, while possible supports include UK tax-year-end flows, corporate dividends and a weaker dollar. Reuters data show consistent April gains against the dollar only after 2004.

Active Surfaces, founded in 2022 from MIT research, develops lightweight, flexible solar panels using roll-to-roll printing. Its fictional 2023 transactions include issuing 500,000 shares for $1 million; paying $24,000 for two years of insurance; drawing $400,000 on a $1 million credit line and repaying $420,000 with interest; purchasing office supplies and paying after 30 days; paying $650,000 for equipment; paying a $25,000 legal retainer and receiving a $1,500 refund; completing a $500,000 pilot project with $350,000 of cash manufacturing costs; receiving a 20% deposit on a $1 million order and purchasing $325,000 of raw materials; and recognizing $65,000 of depreciation. The assignment requests transaction recording, a December 31 balance sheet, and 2023 net income and cash flow calculations.

Audi’s e-tron prototype, predecessor to its production battery-electric SUV, achieves a 0.28 drag coefficient and more than 400 km of WLTP range. After over 1,000 hours in Ingolstadt’s wind tunnel, engineers applied aerodynamic measures that reduce drag by nearly 0.07 versus a comparable conventionally powered vehicle, adding about 35 km per charge. Features include optional camera-based virtual mirrors, adaptive air suspension that lowers the body above 120 km/h, a fully enclosed, dimpled underbody, and a controllable cooling-air inlet. Front ducts direct airflow around optimized 19-inch wheels fitted with ultralow-resistance tires and recessed sidewall lettering.

Year 6 pupils and PTA volunteers at Swallowdale Primary cleaned a bus being converted into a quiet reading space. Planned work includes carpeting, woodland-themed painting with book characters and seat reupholstery.

The passage surveys graph similarity and distance methods, ranging from exact graph matching—such as Sussenguth’s approach and Zelinka’s common-induced-subgraph distance—to graph edit distance, graph kernels, and measures based on topological indices or feature vectors. Prior approaches often used a single index or converted multiple indices into binary form, reducing sensitivity. The paper proposes a more sensitive, computationally efficient topological-index method that captures subtle structural differences and can be applied to large graphs. It defines similarity and distance measures, shows conversions between them, and distinguishes distance metrics by identity-of-indiscernibles and triangle-inequality properties. The proposed graph measure uses at least three topological indices, min-max scales them to [0,1], and then computes a distance between graphs. The paper also outlines applications to random network models and the similarity of decane isomers.

Jefferies analysis of Morning Consult data found Disney and Disney+ sentiment fell to at least two-year lows after the company temporarily suspended Jimmy Kimmel’s show and raised streaming prices. Views declined significantly among Republicans and Democrats, with a sharper drop among Democrats. Disney’s brand awareness rose, while a smaller effect on Disney+ suggested limited streaming churn. Shares fell 6% over the past month, but analyst James Heaney maintained a buy rating and $144 price target.

Functional emulsifier blends combine substances for emulsification; oil- and water-based formulations are most popular, and specialized blends are used in ice cream. North America is expected to dominate because of major food-production centers and operations by suppliers including ADM and Cargill, while emerging APAC markets are projected to grow fastest with private food-processing investment. Demand is driven by food-safety concerns, multifunctional properties, bakery requirements, processed-food adoption, and health awareness. Market players are investing in R&D and formulation innovation. Challenges include complex processing and GMO-based blends being unacceptable in some countries. Food and beverages, especially bakery, are major consumers, while personal care is projected to grow faster.

After rejecting submission to a foreign legislature, Americans gained independence but feared conflict over how to organize government across a vast country. Revolutionary zeal temporarily maintained order, but the Confederation, modeled partly on European confederacies, proved inadequate. Noncompliance brought economic decline, interstate rivalry, loss of public credit, unrest, and fears of national calamity. These dangers prompted the creation of the U.S. Constitution to secure justice, defense, tranquillity, welfare, and liberty.

The author, who first encountered the Constitution while serving abroad, praised and supported it, citing its successful operation and its government by periodically elected citizens. He warned that corruption, manipulation, or foreign influence in elections could turn the government into the choice of a party or foreign power. He praised the retiring executive’s service and urged successors to follow his example. He also pledged support for representative government, equal treatment of the states, education, justice, commerce, improved conditions for Indigenous peoples, peace, neutrality, and Christian public morality, while expressing confidence in the American people and the Constitution.

The President urges American coal miners to end a nationwide strike and return to work, warning that any interruption in coal production endangers soldiers, sailors, munitions output, and victory against Nazi, Fascist, and Japanese forces. He says major labor organizations had pledged no strikes during the war, while United Mine Workers officials refused to participate in War Labor Board proceedings. The government took over the mines and assigned the Interior Secretary authority to resume production, guaranteeing protection for miners returning to work and allowing troops to provide police duties if needed.

The President recognizes miners’ union rights and sacrifices while affirming the government’s commitment to improved living standards, price and wage stability, rent controls, and reductions in unjustified food and meat prices. Any War Labor Board-approved wage adjustment will be retroactive to April 1. Citing miners’ increased wartime production and the sacrifices of military families, he calls on miners to reject the strike and resume work under the Stars and Stripes.

During her visit to the 10th Sharjah Children’s Reading Festival at Expo Centre Sharjah, Sheikha Jawaher Al Qasimi toured the halls and publisher stands, joined children’s workshops and attended a reading session. She said the festival inspires younger generations toward reading, knowledge and innovation while promoting cultural diversity, creativity, science and the arts. She praised the Sharjah Book Authority and urged families, institutions and the community to attend.

Google’s Pentagon “Project Maven” developed AI to analyze drone footage, prompting 3,100-plus employees to sign a petition and about a dozen to resign. Google is drafting ethics guidelines for future defense contracts, reportedly excluding AI use in weaponry.

This paper examines how social studies didactic theory and judicial perspectives can guide content selection in human rights education (HRE) at the early childhood education and care (ECEC) level, using the Norwegian context and observance of UN Day as its empirical example.

The introduction outlines a research gap: although HRE scholarship in ECEC has grown, there is little research-based guidance for ECEC teachers on selecting HRE content, which is problematic because education is not politically neutral and political instability and right-wing authoritarian voices (e.g., anti-gay curriculum laws) complicate content selection and teacher authority. In Norway, the framework plan places HRE in the "local community and society" learning area (social studies), sets the Convention on the Rights of the Child (CRC) as the starting point, but offers little specific guidance. Four tables catalogue HRE resources for children aged 0–10 from NGOs/IGOs, publishing companies, governmental organisations and the ECEC field, separating educational resources from fundraising ones; external actors have prioritised schools.

The paper proposes four content selection dimensions: children's ages, progression, human rights knowledge anchored in social studies, and children's own interests, drawing on Gagel's didactic perspective, the Beutelsbach Consensus and the CRC.

Methodologically, a directed/theoretical content analysis was applied to 89 posts on the Idebroen (Idea Bridge) webpage searching for "rights" and "UN Day"; ten posts were excluded and 73 analysed, revealing three approaches: human rights, diversity and fundraising.

Findings show activities adapted to child groups (one week to a month), cross-curricular, and concretising abstract UN/human rights content through creative activities and NGO/IGO materials. Adaptation to age occurred, but progression was rarely discussed explicitly, and only three of 29 human rights-related posts referenced specific rights or articles, with greater emphasis on values than on rights. Discussion identifies opportunities (addressing progression, children's own interests, NGO/IGO collaborations) and challenges (content appropriate to the level, little teacher discussion of content, risks of indocrination and neutrality, need for pluralism of perspectives), concluding that fewer than half the posts had a proper connection to human rights and that further development of didactics, guiding documents and empirical research is needed.

The passage is a roundup of The 74’s education-focused news and commentary. Its lead story reports that Colton Harris-Moore, dubbed the “Barefoot Bandit,” evaded police for years while committing 67 felonies across three countries, including stealing six airplanes, 15 cars, and robbing more than 34 homes. Other linked stories address school integration, the Every Student Succeeds Act, college access, COVID-19 learning losses, school funding, youth vaping, and teacher recognition. Additional headlines spotlight student achievements, arts and STEM programs, school innovation, Native American language preservation, and education policy. The page also solicits tax-exempt donations.

The Nobel Peace Prize awarded to the International Campaign to Abolish Nuclear Weapons was interpreted as a call for negotiations between North Korea and the United States and an indirect defense of diplomacy and nonproliferation, including the 2015 Iran nuclear deal. The Swedish Academy honored ICAN for highlighting nuclear weapons’ humanitarian consequences and promoting a treaty banning them. The United States said it would not sign the treaty, which was adopted by 122 countries but symbolically, as no nuclear-armed state joined.

The award came amid escalating U.S.–North Korean rhetoric and North Korea’s sixth and largest nuclear test. Russian lawmakers reported that North Korea was preparing a long-range missile test believed capable of reaching the U.S. West Coast. Trump had threatened North Korea’s destruction, while Kim Jong Un called Trump a “dotard” and promised a “highest level of hard-line countermeasure.” Against this backdrop, the prize was presented as a warning that the world was closely watching both leaders.

The address mourns President Harding, praises his character and leadership, and urges those who worked with him to continue his public service and the principles of government he represented.

Foreign policy should promote peace through justice, preserve American independence, and avoid permanent political alliances. The United States has rejected the League of Nations Covenant and will not join the League, although it hopes the organization will be useful. The administration favors a permanent World Court and commends support for the proposed Permanent Court of International Justice, with reservations intended to preserve U.S. independence from the League.

Diplomatic relations with Russia are being resumed, but normal relations will depend on recognition of international obligations, compensation for American citizens, and reduced hostility toward U.S. institutions. The government supports commerce with Russia and is willing to make large concessions to assist its people, but will not trade American principles for commercial privilege.

The administration opposes canceling foreign debts but supports adjustment, consistent with the treatment of the British debt. It seeks payment for American claims against Germany, European economic recovery, payment of France, revival of Germany, and disarmament. The foreign service should be reorganized.

Financial stability and the reduction of public spending and taxation are presented as essential. Congress’s budget system has brought expenditures, excluding the self-supporting Post Office Department, to three billion dollars. The government supports tax reductions, lower taxes on moderate incomes and earned income, repeal of certain nuisance taxes, reduced excess-profits taxes, and a constitutional amendment ending tax-exempt securities. The existing tariff is praised for revenue and prosperity; Congress should use its limited flexibility to correct significant inequities rather than rewrite the law.

The government-owned merchant fleet should eventually pass to private ownership while preserving national defense and adequate service for American commerce. Congress should pursue flood control, inland waterways, Great Lakes navigation, and the St. Lawrence power and navigation project, with particular attention to northeastern power development.

Railroad policy should guarantee fair returns, await the Supreme Court’s ruling on excess-earnings recapture, and reorganize freight rates. Additional authority should permit regional and route consolidations under Interstate Commerce Commission supervision, while the Labor Board continues addressing disputes. If voluntary consolidation proves ineffective, direct federal action may be required.

Legal and judicial reforms should include updated federal laws, additional judges, simplified trial-court procedure, easier Supreme Court review procedures, employment for prisoners, separate reformatories for women and first-time young offenders, and a criminal-identification division within the Bureau of Investigation.

Prohibition enforcement requires a search treaty with Great Britain, a stronger Coast Guard, swift power boats, regulation of major producers, and suppression of interstate trafficking. The government should protect the constitutional rights of Black citizens, use congressional authority against lynching, expand vocational and medical education, and encourage local cooperation and a biracial commission to improve understanding.

The merit-based classified civil service should be maintained and extended, particularly to postmasters and prohibition enforcement personnel. Congress should authorize several urgently needed federal buildings and regulate coastal pollution, aviation, radio interference, vessel loading, navigation laws, Federal Trade Commission procedure, and Alaskan fisheries.

Further reductions in Army and Navy personnel should be avoided; additional aircraft, submarines, and Panama defenses are needed to maintain national security without entering competitive armaments. The administration supports lawful administration of the insular possessions and attention to their residents’ recommendations.

Government should promote public health, prohibit narcotics and intoxicating liquors, limit child labor, and establish minimum wages for women under federal jurisdiction. A Cabinet-level welfare department should coordinate education and allied welfare activities, although local schools should retain freedom of choice and federal funds should not directly finance local education. Immigration should remain restricted and selective, with source inspections or prior census and naturalization records, and all aliens should register immediately.

Veterans disabled in service should receive prompt hospital care, compensation, dependent support, rehabilitation, and vocational training. Vacant hospital beds should be made available without charge, new facilities should be built, and administrative deficiencies should be corrected, although a veterans’ bonus is opposed.

High coal prices and supply instability require reform under private ownership rather than government operation. The government should publish facts, improve distribution and continuity, and have authority to appoint an emergency commission during supply interruptions. The departments and bureaus should be reorganized into a more scientific and economical system, while the War and Navy departments remain separate.

Despite broad national prosperity, farmers face hardship from overexpanded wheat acreage, unfavorable competition, high taxes, freight charges, and expensive fertilizer. Relief should emphasize farmer-led organization, cooperative marketing, diversification, reduced wheat acreage, cheaper transportation and fertilizer, and government assistance for exports, rather than permanent price controls or treasury support.

The Muscle Shoals project should be sold, with covenants requiring experimentation toward inexpensive domestic fertilizer production. Reclamation users need legal authority for suspended, adjusted, or reassessed charges, although contracts that can be met should be honored. Federal support for highways and reforestation should continue.

The address reaffirms the Monroe Doctrine while asserting that American power now carries greater responsibility to help stabilize the world. It rejects war and destructive reliance on material power, calling instead for practical moral leadership grounded in justice, mercy, confidence, peace, and the principle that right makes its own might.

Toronto’s TTC will return 67 of 89 new Bombardier streetcars for repairs to inferior frame welds, despite saying they pose no safety risk. Bombardier will cover the costs and complete the work by 2022.

Ohio State University researchers identified a previously unknown stress pathway, TexPSR, as a major driver of T-cell exhaustion in cancer. Unlike normal stress responses that reduce protein production, TexPSR accelerates it, causing misfolded proteins, stress granules, and toxic aggregates to accumulate and cripple T cells’ ability to attack tumors. In preclinical models, blocking key drivers of TexPSR restored exhausted T-cell function and markedly improved immunotherapy effectiveness. The mechanism was validated across models of lung, bladder, and liver cancers and leukemia. High TexPSR levels in cancer patients’ T cells were also associated with poor responses to immunotherapy, suggesting that targeting this pathway may improve clinical treatment.

President James Buchanan transmitted to Congress the Lecompton constitution of Kansas, arguing that Kansas’s political conflict was rebellion against the Congress-authorized territorial government rather than ordinary partisan disagreement. He characterized the Topeka constitution and government as revolutionary and maintained that the Lecompton convention had been lawfully called and organized by the territorial legislature. He said opponents of the territorial government refused to vote for convention delegates and later declined to vote on the slavery question, while a January election under the Lecompton constitution selected state officers and legislators. Buchanan asserted that popular sovereignty must be exercised through established law, that the convention properly submitted slavery to voters, and that the people could amend their constitution. He favored admitting Kansas as a slave state under the Lecompton constitution, arguing that rejection would renew sectional conflict, while admission would restore peace, localize the slavery issue, and permit the withdrawal of federal troops. He also stated that the existing legislature could submit constitutional changes to voters.

In a separate April 6, 1858 proclamation concerning Utah, Buchanan described armed resistance to federal authority, including the expulsion of officials, destruction of court records, and an attack on an Army baggage train. After ordering troops toward Salt Lake to enforce the law, he declared further resistance to be rebellion and treason. He denied that the action targeted religion, offered a full pardon to inhabitants who submitted to federal authority, ordered public officers and citizens to assist in executing the laws, and declared that military forces would remain until the territory demonstrated obedience.

Flexible working can help employed carers balance work and caring responsibilities. Options include changed hours or days, compressed hours, flexible start or finish times, working from home or another office, term-time work, part-time work, and job sharing.

Employees in England, Scotland, and Wales who have worked for their employer for at least 26 weeks may request flexible working, with one application allowed in any 12-month period. Employers must consider requests but may refuse them for a valid business reason. Requests should follow the employer’s procedure or, if none exists, be made in writing as a statutory application explaining the desired arrangements, start date, possible business impact, and previous applications.

Employers must give the request serious consideration and respond within three months unless a longer period is agreed. If approved, they must confirm the new hours and start date and amend the contract. Unexplained or apparently unfair decisions can be challenged through the employer’s appeal process or an employment tribunal within three months.

Veterans in the Galesburg, Illinois area have reported missing prescription medications delivered by mail. Galesburg resident Robert Stevens, who receives hydrocodone-acetaminophen from the Iowa City VA Health Care System, said a package left at the post office with a pink slip could not be found on two occasions. Abingdon veteran Gary Kilpatrick said his pills have gone missing multiple times, estimating 20 or more pills were removed from each delivery. Abingdon Police Chief Ken Jones said he has had two such cases but that they are difficult to track down, adding there is enough evidence to indicate something is happening. Iowa City VA spokesman Bryan Clark said the agency has received multiple reports of prescription drug theft in the Galesburg area and that it is under investigation. Stevens said having medication taken away is "kind of sickening."

NVIDIA Corporation (Delaware; Santa Clara, CA) filed a Form 10-Q for the quarterly period ended April 26, 2020 (fiscal Q1 2021), reporting 615 million shares of common stock outstanding as of May 15, 2020. The filing includes unaudited condensed consolidated financial statements and notes, MD&A, market risk disclosures, controls and procedures, legal proceedings, risk factors, and exhibits.

Financial results: Revenue was $3,080 million vs. $2,220 million a year earlier (+39%) and $3,105 million in the prior quarter (−1%). Gross margin was 65.1% (up 670 bps year over year, 20 bps sequentially), driven by GeForce GPU product mix and higher Data Center sales. Operating expenses were $1,028 million (+10% year over year, flat sequentially), primarily from employee additions, compensation, infrastructure and stock-based compensation. Income from operations was $976 million (+173% year over year, −1% sequentially). Net income was $917 million vs. $394 million; diluted EPS was $1.47 vs. $0.64 (−4% sequentially). Income tax expense was $64 million (6.6% of pre-tax income) vs. a $5 million benefit in the prior-year quarter, due to reduced stock-based compensation tax benefits.

Segments: During the quarter NVIDIA changed its reportable segments from GPU and Tegra Processor to Graphics and Compute & Networking, with prior periods recast. Graphics revenue was $1,906 million (+25% year over year, −9% sequentially) with operating income of $836 million; Compute & Networking revenue was $1,174 million (+69%, +15% sequentially) with operating income of $451 million; "All Other" operating loss was $311 million (including $224 million stock-based compensation). Market platforms: Gaming $1,339 million (+27%), Professional Visualization $307 million (+15%), Data Center $1,141 million (+80%), Automotive $155 million (−7%), OEM and Other $138 million (+39%). Geographic revenue (by billing location): Taiwan $813 million, China including Hong Kong $758 million, Other Asia Pacific $607 million, U.S. $497 million, Europe $254 million, other $151 million; non-U.S. sales were 84% of revenue. No customer represented 10% or more of revenue in fiscal Q1 2021; one customer was 11% in fiscal Q1 2020, and one customer represented 15% and 21% of accounts receivable at April 26, 2020 and January 26, 2020.

Balance sheet: Total assets of $23,254 million vs. $17,315 million at January 26, 2020; cash and cash equivalents of $15,494 million and marketable securities of $860 million; total liabilities of $10,155 million, including long-term debt of $6,959 million (vs. $1,991 million); total shareholders' equity of $13,099 million vs. $12,204 million.

Cash flow: Operating activities provided $909 million (vs. $720 million); investing used $1,055 million (vs. $1,495 million provided) including $861 million of marketable securities purchases, $155 million of property/equipment and intangibles purchases and $34 million for an acquisition; financing provided $4,744 million, including $4,979 million net from debt issuance, $88 million from employee stock plans, $222 million of tax withholding on RSU vesting and $98 million of dividends paid. Cash and equivalents ended at $15,494 million.

Debt: In March 2020 NVIDIA issued $1.50 billion of 2.85% Notes Due 2030, $1.00 billion of 3.50% Notes Due 2040, $2.00 billion of 3.50% Notes Due 2050 and $500 million of 3.70% Notes Due 2060 (net proceeds $4.97 billion), in addition to September 2016 Notes ($1.00 billion 2.20% due 2021 and $1.00 billion 3.20% due 2026). The Notes are unsecured senior obligations, structurally subordinated to subsidiary liabilities. NVIDIA also has a $575 million credit agreement (up to $425 million revolving commitments) and a $575 million commercial paper program, with no amounts borrowed or issued as of April 26, 2020.

Other notes: The Mellanox Technologies acquisition closed on April 27, 2020 for approximately $7.0 billion in cash, subsequent to quarter end. Operating leases totaled $736 million of minimum payments with a present value of $619 million (8.2-year weighted average term, 3.45% discount rate). Stock-based compensation was $224 million, with $1.81 billion of unvested expense over 2.4 years (RSUs/PSUs) and 0.8 years (ESPP). Intangible assets net of amortization were $80 million; goodwill was $628 million ($347 million Graphics, $281 million Compute & Networking). Deferred revenue was $241 million, with $389 million of remaining performance obligations (47% expected within twelve months). Purchase obligations totaled $1.76 billion inventory and $287 million other. The company adopted the current expected credit loss standard in fiscal Q1 2021 with no material impact.

Legal proceedings: A consolidated securities class action (In Re NVIDIA Corporation Securities Litigation) asserting false statements about channel inventory and cryptocurrency mining impact on GPU demand was dismissed with leave to amend on March 16, 2020, with an amended complaint filed May 13, 2020. Multiple consolidated derivative actions and Delaware suits (Lipchitz, Nelson) are stayed pending the motion to dismiss. No accrual has been recorded for these matters, which the company believes are not probable.

COVID-19: The pandemic disrupted supply chain and logistics (Asia-based partners and component supply) and reduced demand for gaming products from closed physical retailers and China iCafes, while lowering automotive demand; some regions saw temporary demand increases for gaming, OEM platforms and compute infrastructure due to work/school from home. Management states the full extent and duration is uncertain and that extended disruption could materially negatively affect results, liquidity and access to capital.

Capital returns and controls: $98 million in quarterly dividends were paid; no shares were repurchased in the quarter, with $7.24 billion of repurchase authority remaining through December 2022, pending evaluation of market conditions. Management concluded disclosure controls and procedures were effective as of April 26, 2020, and reported no material changes in internal control over financial reporting during the quarter.

NVIDIA’s Turing GPU architecture combines real-time ray tracing, rasterization, AI, and simulation across the TU102, TU104, and TU106 GPUs. TU102 is the line’s highest-performing model, with 72 Streaming Multiprocessors (SMs), 36 Texture Processing Clusters, six Graphics Processing Clusters, 576 Tensor Cores, and 36 RT Cores. Each SM includes 64 CUDA Cores, eight Tensor Cores, an RT Core, a 256 KB register file, and configurable 96 KB L1/shared memory. Its redesigned SM supports concurrent FP32 and INT32 execution, unified L1, texture, and shared-memory resources, and delivered performance improvements of about 50% per CUDA core over Pascal.

Second-generation NVLink provides direct GPU-to-GPU memory access and high-speed multi-GPU communication. TU102 has two x8 links offering 100 GB/s aggregate bidirectional bandwidth, while TU104 has one x8 link offering 50 GB/s bidirectionally. Turing also supports two-way SLI, but not three- or four-way configurations.

Turing’s RT Cores accelerate bounding-volume-hierarchy traversal and ray-triangle intersection testing, freeing SMs for other work and making software-based ray tracing roughly 10 times faster. Hybrid rendering combines efficient rasterization with ray-traced reflections, refractions, shadows, and ambient occlusion, while denoising reduces the number of rays required. The architecture supports NVIDIA RTX, OptiX, Microsoft DXR, and the forthcoming Vulkan ray-tracing API.

Enhanced Tensor Cores support FP16, INT8, and INT4 inference. They accelerate neural-network training and inference and power NVIDIA NGX services such as Deep Learning Super Sampling, AI InPainting, AI Super Rez, and AI Slow-Mo. DLSS uses trained neural networks to reconstruct high-quality images from lower-resolution rendering, while DLSS 2X further combines rendered frames.

The GPU family also introduces mesh shading with task and mesh shaders, Variable Rate Shading for independently adjustable per-16×16-region shading rates, Texture Space Shading for reusable decoupled shading results, and Multi-View Rendering for multiple viewpoints in one pass. Turing supports four hardware views per pass and up to 32 views through the API.

Memory improvements include GDDR6 signaling at 14 Gbps, 20% better power efficiency than Pascal’s GDDR5X, doubled L2 capacity in TU102, and enhanced compression that produces roughly 50% greater effective bandwidth. The display engine supports DisplayPort 1.4a, 8K at 60 Hz, HDR and tone mapping, while updated NVENC and NVDEC units add high-resolution HEVC encoding and additional decode formats.

Turing GPUs also support USB Type-C and the VirtualLink standard, allowing VR headsets to receive power, display data, and tracking data through one connector. VirtualLink combines four HBR3 DisplayPort lanes with a SuperSpeed USB 3 link and enables VR on smaller devices unable to accommodate multiple connectors.

The TU104-based Tesla T4 targets data-center and edge inference, providing 2,560 CUDA Cores, 320 Tensor Cores, 16 GB of memory, and 320 GB/s of bandwidth. The passage reports up to 40 times higher inference performance and more than 50 times higher energy efficiency than CPU-based inference, along with enhanced video decoding, MPS support, and broader workload capabilities.

This 2025 MIT Sloan case examines Ferrari’s “controlled growth” strategy: expanding revenue, models, customers, and geographic reach while preserving the exclusivity, heritage, and emotional appeal of its brand. In 2024, Ferrari generated $7.2 billion in revenue, nearly doubling shipments over the prior decade, and derived almost 90% of revenue from cars and parts. It held an estimated 14% of the global luxury performance market and 23% of the two-door luxury sports-car market. Planned growth included new models, younger buyers, new regions, and its first fully electric vehicle in 2025.

The luxury performance market—Ferrari-defined as vehicles priced above €180,000 with more than 500 horsepower—comprised over 85,000 vehicles in 2024 and was forecast to grow 9%–14% annually through 2031. It includes historic brands such as Bentley and Aston Martin and newer supercar producers such as Automobili Pininfarina and W Motors. Growth was supported by rising global wealth, although the 2008–2009 recession reduced demand.

Founded by Enzo Ferrari in 1929 as Scuderia Ferrari and incorporated in 1947, the company built its identity around racing, powerful engines, craftsmanship, and the prancing horse. Ferrari’s road cars financed racing, while racing success attracted wealthy customers and enhanced the brand. Formula 1 became central to Ferrari’s reputation, visibility, and finances. Under later leadership, Ferrari modernized its road-car lineup, went public in 2015, and appointed Benedetto Vigna as CEO in 2021.

Ferrari cultivated an exclusive customer base of “Ferraristi” through limited editions, invitation-only events, collector relationships, and controlled access to supercars. In 2024, 81% of new cars went to existing clients; repeat customers generated an estimated 80% of revenue and 86% of EBITDA. Its lifestyle business included licensed goods, fashion, stores, museums, and theme parks.

Ferrari sold vehicles through 178 authorized dealers in 60 markets rather than operating its own dealerships. It built cars only after orders, maintained long waitlists, and avoided unsold inventory. Its portfolio comprised Range models, which represented more than 90% of shipments, plus limited-production Special Series, Icona, and supercars. Range models emphasized everyday usability, while more exclusive versions generated higher margins. New introductions included plug-in hybrids and the Purosangue SUV, and Ferrari offered extensive customization through Atelier, Tailor Made, and One-Off programs.

Manufacturing remained concentrated in Modena and Maranello. Ferrari used in-house production for core engines and components while outsourcing transmissions, brakes, and other parts. Its racing-derived technology, especially hybrid engineering, moved into road cars.

Hybrid shipments rose from 15% of units in 2021 to 51% in 2024. Ferrari planned a technology-neutral portfolio of combustion, hybrid, and electric vehicles, with a 2026 sales mix of 55% hybrid, 40% combustion, and 5% fully electric. It opened an electric-component “e-building” and battery laboratory at Maranello, planned to source battery cells externally, and intended to handcraft electric powertrains around its heritage. However, weaker-than-expected luxury EV demand, charging-infrastructure constraints, and competitors’ revised electrification plans created uncertainty. Ferrari remained focused on Formula 1 and had not entered Formula E.

Controlled growth presented risks involving new-market entry, dealer networks, competition, changing preferences, and electrification. The case concludes with strategic questions about Ferrari’s competitive advantages, threats, potential disruption, and the best opportunities for profitable growth.
After nearly three weeks out of public view, Melania Trump tweeted that she was at the White House with her family and feeling well. Her office denied social media speculation about her absence.

Germany, France, Spain, Italy and Britain received final EU warnings over repeated nitrogen dioxide limit breaches. The pollution poses health risks, and failure to respond within two months could lead to the EU Court of Justice.

Five key principles guide early childhood education and care (ECEC) for children aged 1–5:

1. **Prioritize holistic development in the early years:** The first five years are a formative period of rapid cognitive, linguistic, social, emotional, behavioural, psychological, and motor development. High brain plasticity and sensitivity to positive or negative experiences make early learning foundational for future success.
2. **Create nurturing environments:** Safe, inclusive, stimulating settings with suitable materials, emotional support, and respectful relationships foster confidence, resilience, creativity, and physical, cognitive, and social development.
3. **Ensure quality ECEC:** Effective programs provide long-term cognitive and socio-emotional benefits through warm teacher-child interactions, age-appropriate, flexible, evidence-based curricula, professional development, and inclusion of diverse needs.
4. **Engage families:** Collaboration among families and educators creates consistent learning experiences, supports children’s development, provides cultural understanding, and offers families resources, feedback, and shared responsibility.
5. **Promote continuous professional development:** Ongoing training keeps ECEC educators equipped with current knowledge, skills, and best practices.

Together, these principles support children’s development and strengthen their prospects in later learning and life.

The lecture covers minimal trellis representations for binary linear block codes, with the same principles applying to codes over finite fields or groups. The state-space theorem states that the state-space dimension at a cut time equals the code dimension minus the dimensions of the past and future subcodes. A trellis-oriented generator matrix is obtained by greedily combining generators to cancel overlapping starting or ending positions until all starting times and all ending times are distinct. State-space dimensions can then be read from the number of generators active at each time, yielding the state-dimension profile. Self-dual codes have special overlap between starting and ending times, and the dual state-space theorem gives primal and dual codes equal state-space dimensions.

A minimal trellis is realized by assigning each generator a one-dimensional memory element that is active only during the generator’s span and summing the resulting outputs. Generator starts produce divergences, generator endings produce convergences, and simultaneous starts and endings produce crossings. Branch spaces form vector spaces, and their dimension at each symbol time equals the number of active generators. Branch-space size is more directly related to Viterbi decoding complexity than state-space size.

Sectionalization can make state complexity appear smaller, but it cannot reduce the underlying branch complexity. A practical heuristic is to use the largest sections possible without increasing branch complexity. The theory also extends to convolutional codes through canonical generators and their shifts, illustrating the connection with time-varying linear-system realization.

Average-dimension bounds follow from the fact that a generator’s span cannot be less than the code’s minimum distance \(d\). Across \(k\) generators, total state dimension is at least \(k(d-1)\), while total branch dimension is at least \(kd\). Thus average state and branch dimensions are bounded below by \(k(d-1)/(n-1)\) and \(kd/n\), respectively. The latter is the nominal coding gain. For sequences whose rate and relative distance remain bounded away from zero, nominal coding gain grows linearly with block length, forcing minimal-trellis branch complexity to grow exponentially. Trellis decoding is therefore simpler than exhaustive maximum-likelihood decoding but still has exponential complexity. Finite coding gain may instead permit long codes with poor minimum distance, as illustrated by turbo codes, although this is not universal; low-density parity-check codes can also achieve good distance.

Finally, projections are related to subcodes by duality. An alternate state-space theorem expresses state dimension as the dimension of the code projected onto the past minus the dimension of the past subcode. This lets Reed–Muller code central state sizes be obtained directly, including 4 states for the \((8,4,4)\) code and 64 states for the \((32,16,8)\) code in a four-section trellis. The Muder bound and a comparison of block-code and convolutional-code trellises are deferred to the next class.

On May 7, 2019, Tesla closed underwritten public offerings of 3,549,381 common shares, including 462,962 shares issued upon the underwriters’ fully exercised option, and $1.84 billion of 2.00% Convertible Senior Notes due May 15, 2024, including $240 million of option notes.

The notes pay interest semiannually, beginning November 15, 2019, and have an initial conversion rate of 3.2276 shares per $1,000 principal, equal to a conversion price of approximately $309.83 per share. The conversion rate is subject to specified adjustments, including additional shares following certain make-whole fundamental changes. Before February 15, 2024, conversion is permitted only under specified price, trading-price, or corporate-event conditions; afterward, holders may convert until shortly before maturity. Conversion may be settled in cash, common shares, or both, at Tesla’s election.

The senior unsecured notes rank equally with Tesla’s other unsecured indebtedness not expressly subordinated, are effectively junior to secured indebtedness, and are structurally subordinated to subsidiary liabilities. Holders may require Tesla to repurchase the notes at principal plus accrued interest following a fundamental change. The indenture defines various events of default, including payment defaults, specified covenant failures, certain debt-payment defaults exceeding $500 million, and bankruptcy events.

Tesla also entered into additional note hedge transactions intended generally to reduce dilution or offset excess cash payments upon conversion. At closing, Tesla paid approximately $475.8 million for note hedges, including $62.1 million for the additional hedges. It issued additional warrants permitting purchase of up to approximately 1.5 million common shares at an adjustable strike price of $607.50 per share. The warrants may dilute shareholders unless Tesla elects cash settlement, and noteholders receive no rights under them. Tesla received approximately $174.4 million from warrant sales, including $22.8 million for the additional warrants.

The document standardizes the Guest-Hypervisor Communication Block (GHCB) for SEV-ES and SEV-SNP guests. These technologies encrypt guest register state during world switches, preventing the hypervisor from directly accessing or modifying it. Guests are notified of relevant world switches through Non-Automatic Exits (NAEs) and selectively expose required state through the GHCB. The specification defines the GHCB layout, required NAE events and state, protocol negotiation, error handling, and guest-specific behaviors such as NMI handling and SMP booting.

The GHCB is a 4 KB, page-aligned shared or decrypted memory region. Its layout mirrors the SEV-ES VMCB save area through offset 0x3ff. The guest specifies its physical address through MSR 0xc001_0130, whose lower 12 bits carry MSR-protocol requests and responses. The hypervisor must not intercept this MSR and must access the GHCB through the address saved in the VMCB. Version 2 adds hypervisor feature advertisement through a bitmap limited to 52 bits, allowing features to be queried before a GHCB page is established.

During negotiation, the hypervisor supplies the supported GHCB protocol range and SEV page-table encryption-bit position, either through the SEV Information request or the CPUID request protocol. Guests handle intercepted CPUID operations through #VC exceptions, configure page tables with the encryption bit, and mark the GHCB page shared. SEV-SNP guests must also register the GHCB guest physical address before using it for VMGEXIT; they may request a hypervisor-preferred address, register their own, or unregister it.

NAE processing follows a defined sequence. A guest receives a #VC exception, copies the minimum required register state into the GHCB, updates the VALID_BITMAP, and executes VMGEXIT. The hypervisor handles the exit, returns results and possible error information, and resumes the guest. Guests must set at least the SW_EXITCODE, SW_EXITINFO1, and SW_EXITINFO2 validity bits, while hypervisors must set the two SW_EXITINFO bits. Nonzero SW_EXITINFO1 denotes an error. Interrupts and preemption should be disabled while accessing the GHCB, with special handling for NMI context.

The protocol supports IOIO protection, MSR protection, hypervisor-specific VMMCALLs, and MMIO access through #NPF. MMIO requests use a reserved nested-page-table bit and a decrypted shared buffer, with multiple VMGEXIT calls permitted for transfers exceeding the buffer. Page State Change requests can make pages private or shared and provide SNP-specific PSMASH and UNSMASH hints; shared-memory progress fields allow interrupted requests to resume.

SEV-SNP Guest Requests use separate shared request and response pages and communicate with firmware through the hypervisor. Extended Guest Requests may also return VCEK or VLEK certificates identified by GUIDs. SNP AP Creation allows guests to create, update, or remove AP vCPU state at specified VMPL levels using VMSA pages, supporting controlled AP initialization and vCPU hotplug. Other NAE events support APIC ID retrieval, running a vCPU at a selected VMPL level, Secure AVIC backing-page registration, guest-requested termination, and SEV-TIO requests for trusted PCIe devices using TDISP. Restricted Injection adds doorbell-page management, host-emulated APIC timer operations, and guest-requested IPIs.

SMP booting requires special handling because measured AP register state cannot be changed after guest launch. Initial AP values can be established through a reset-vector mechanism or predetermined CS/IP values. Subsequent starts use AP Reset Hold and an encrypted AP jump table to transfer the next reset vector between environments. SEV-SNP AP Creation provides an alternative when Restricted Injection prevents use of AP Reset Hold. NMI handling requires the hypervisor to avoid intercepting IRET, intercept #DB, and wait for an “NMI Complete” VMGEXIT message. Hardware debug-register virtualization is supported when enabled, while otherwise DR7 access is intercepted and emulated. SMM and nested virtualization are not supported.

Under SNP Restricted Injection, the host communicates pending notifications through a shared #HV doorbell page. Its common fields include a 16-bit PendingEvent value, an EOI-assist byte, and reserved space. PendingEvent can identify an interrupt vector, NMI, virtual #MC, or a no-further-signal condition. The host is expected to emulate APIC priority, acknowledgment, in-service, and EOI semantics, present the highest-priority ready interrupt, and use #HV when guest notification is required. Because #HV bypasses normal interrupt shadows, guests execute HLT with interrupts disabled, and the host immediately re-enters the guest if events remain pending.
