A Twitter thread debates whether LGBT activists embarrassed or protested Mike Pence during his St. Patrick’s Day visit to Savannah. Alex Griswold criticizes John Oliver and celebrity friends’ book, which depicted the Pence family’s pet rabbit as gay, as pathetic. Queerty claims liberals viewed the trip as a victory, while a Savannah attendee notes pride flags appeared behind Pence in parade photos and says he appeared happy and friendly. Gay conservative Chad Felix Greene says the activists wasted time, never affected Pence, and relied on misinformation; he disputes that religious freedom equals discrimination. The original poster counters that Pence has praised James Dobson and argues that religious freedom can be discriminatory. They continue trading accusations about research, political viewpoints, and openness to opposing arguments. A separate tweet makes a satirical religious comment about Pence, which Greene dismisses as silly before concluding, “This is the Left.”

Zeenews.india.com’s Cookie Policy explains how cookies and similar tracking technologies are stored on and accessed from users’ devices when using linked sites. Continued browsing indicates acceptance. These technologies let the sites recognize devices and users, identify interests, remember preferences, track use, control content access, protect and administer sites, and process requests. Third-party providers use persistent cookies for statistical analysis, content management, and improving user experience.

First-party cookies belong to or are set by visited sites; third-party cookies may be delivered through embedded media and social-sharing features. The policy lists persistent and temporary session cookies, plus essential, analytical/performance, functionality, and advertising cookies. These support site navigation and login recognition, retain session actions and security, analyze usage, preserve user customizations, and enable targeted advertising.

Users may reject all or some cookies through browser settings, though blocking cookies may limit site access. Stored cookies can be manually deleted, but new ones may be placed unless settings are adjusted. Collected data is retained only as needed for stated purposes and remains in the database until explicit consent to removal is given. Questions can be sent to response@zeemedia.esselgroup.com.

NVIDIA Corporation reported unaudited first-quarter fiscal 2017 results for the period ended May 1, 2016. Revenue increased 13% to $1.305 billion, gross margin rose to 57.5%, operating income increased 39% to $245 million, and net income rose 46% to $196 million. Diluted earnings per share were $0.33. GPU revenue increased 15% to $1.079 billion, while Tegra Processor revenue rose 10% to $160 million. Gaming revenue increased 17% to $687 million, datacenter revenue rose 63% to $143 million, automotive revenue rose 47% to $113 million, and professional visualization revenue rose 4% to $189 million. The effective tax rate was 18.6%.

Cash, cash equivalents, and marketable securities totaled $4.75 billion, and operating cash flow was $309 million. NVIDIA paid $62 million in dividends and entered a $500 million accelerated share repurchase, returning $562 million to shareholders during the quarter and intending to return approximately $1 billion during fiscal 2017. The company had $1.42 billion of convertible short-term debt, $79 million in convertible debt conversion obligation, and $4.196 billion in shareholders’ equity.

NVIDIA resolved its intellectual-property disputes with Samsung and dismissed related claims against Qualcomm. It also settled litigation with Advanced Silicon Technologies and paid $16 million for patent licenses. The company continued financing its new headquarters through an off-balance-sheet lease arrangement, with bank funding commitments of up to $380 million. Management concluded that disclosure controls were effective, and no material changes in internal control over financial reporting occurred during the quarter.

A lecture on reverse logistics and closed-loop supply chains examined ReCellular and Whirlpool.

ReCellular collects donated or refurbished cellphones and sells them to secondary markets. Students debated its prospects. Optimists cited its global e-commerce operations, potential to evolve with mobile technology, demand in developing markets, and continued need for lower-cost phones among technology laggards. Critics pointed to rapidly declining secondhand-phone values, shrinking margins, fewer donors, and dependence on a single product. ReCellular was contrasted with diversified reverse-logistics provider Genco, which works with retailers and handles varied products.

Whirlpool’s alternatives were to join an industry-funded organization (IFO), create its own closed-loop system, or oppose extended producer responsibility regulation. The class noted that roughly 95–99% of appliances already enter recycling systems because valuable materials such as steel, aluminum, and copper create an economic incentive. Regulation might nevertheless be needed if commodity prices fall, new materials prove difficult to recycle, or mercury and refrigerants are handled improperly. Targeted alternatives included phasing out hazardous materials and training recyclers in better management.

Supporters viewed the IFO as a flexible, economical starting point that provides nationwide scale, while a closed-loop system offered greater control, customer loyalty, brand benefits, and an early-mover advantage. Its disadvantages were high startup costs, operational complexity, and the need for retailer cooperation, tracking systems, labor, warehouse and distribution-center space, and capital investment. Student estimates placed IFO costs at $24 million to $35 million, while the professor’s rough calculations compared reverse-logistics costs of about $47 to $80 per unit with forward distribution of roughly $70 per unit. The comparison depended on scale and scrap-metal recovery.

Whirlpool’s Canadian network was described as 17 factories, 24 distribution centers, and about 2,400 retailers. Under an IFO, dealers or other collectors would retrieve appliances for processing, reducing Whirlpool’s direct consumer relationship. A closed-loop approach could ask consumers and retailers to return products and potentially use existing delivery vehicles for collection, but would create handling and infrastructure barriers. Whirlpool, with about 48% market share, tried a closed-loop program, but it proved more expensive than expected. The professor emphasized benchmarking reverse against forward supply-chain costs and noted that volume and uniform, easily packaged products improve feasibility.

The lecture concluded with student projects on Zara, Hewlett-Packard and Dell, BMW, and Philip Morris International. The groups were considering business models, carbon footprints, life-cycle impacts, regulatory pressures, internal environmental initiatives, and offsets. The professor noted differences between fast fashion and direct-to-consumer electronics, the importance of product-use emissions for vehicles, washing’s potential life-cycle impact on clothing, and common regulatory and collaborative pressures within industries. A numerical case-study assignment covering calculations and sales questions was due Wednesday morning.
XPC=0 limits SDXC to 0.36 W and Class 0; XPC=1 permits 0.54 W with Speed Class. Changing XPC requires reinitialization. UHS-I negotiates 1.8-V signaling via S18R/S18A; UHS-II always reports S18A=0.

The coaching staff praises a player’s composure, work ethic, timely saves, and value on any shift. The staff emphasizes instinct tempered by calculated risk, simple plays when opportunities are limited, and cooperative, give-and-go hockey in the playoffs. Fewer penalties have reduced power-play chances, while last game’s weak zone entries and limited zone time hindered the power play. Teammates have stepped up defensively, and Brian Dumoulin has contributed in power-play situations, penalty killing, and other situations.

The passage outlines one-on-one soccer defending after a defender has gone goal-side and assumed a proper stance. When teammates cover their opponents, the defender may aggressively challenge by cutting off the ball, tackling, interposing, or preventing the dribbler from turning toward goal. If the defense is unsettled, the defender instead stalls the attack to allow teammates to recover.

One-on-one techniques include staying goal-side, maintaining balance and proper distance, avoiding overreaction to fakes, blocking passes or shots, slowly giving ground, restricting the dribbler’s vision, jockeying laterally, shepherding shoulder-to-shoulder, and taking a loose ball. The defender must eventually stop retreating and prepare to tackle when field position and the opponent’s shooting threat warrant it.

Verbal communication is essential because the on-ball defender cannot monitor the entire field. Supporting defenders, the defensive organizer, or goalkeeper direct the defender either to contain, jockey, or delay while help arrives, or to challenge or tackle. If beaten, the defender turns and gives chase; if a teammate takes over, the original defender performs a defensive switch.

Coaching should cover the proper approach, stances, positioning on the right, center, and left, adjustment to the opponent’s movement, all defensive techniques, and communication terminology. Practice progresses from slow movement without a ball to ball movement at half speed and then faster movement, while emphasizing field awareness and maintaining goal-side position. Beginning youth require significant individual instruction; if the coach cannot demonstrate a technique, an appropriate assistant should do so.

Michigan State Police arranged for 13 semi-truck drivers to position their trucks beneath a bridge, shortening the distance a man threatening suicide could fall. After several hours, he left the bridge peacefully and was taken to Beaumont Hospital for evaluation.

The disclosure describes methods for reducing device power consumption by controlling uplink data transmission in enhanced coverage states, where repeated transmissions improve coverage but increase battery usage. It addresses LTE coverage enhancement modes and levels, NB-IoT coverage levels, and EC-GSM-IoT coverage classes.

Two approaches are presented. In Solution 1, an application queries the modem for radio coverage information—such as coverage level, mode, class, repetition count, signal strength, or signal quality—and decides whether to send, defer, or discard uplink data. In Solution 2, the application instructs the modem to transmit specified or future data conditionally, and the modem applies the restriction. AT commands or APIs may be used, including solicited queries and unsolicited coverage-change notifications.

Restrictions may depend on coverage conditions, data type, QoS or priority, timers, attempt counts, device movement or location, battery level, power connection, and designated areas. Emergency data may be exempt, while deferred data can later be sent or discarded if obsolete. Restrictions may apply in idle or connected modes.

Configuration can be preset on the device, defined by standards, or supplied by the network through NAS or RRC signaling, protocol configuration options, USIM or device-management mechanisms, and related information elements. Example AT commands and 3GPP modifications include coverage fields in +CREG, +CIOTQCEL, conditional transmission through +CSODCP, and +CEUDR. The disclosure also applies similar criteria to mobile-terminated messages, with an application or service capability server obtaining device coverage information from the network.

Using 2007–2010 NHANES data, this cross-sectional study examined whether depression, obesity, and hypertriglyceridemia (HTG) interact in their association with rheumatoid arthritis (RA) and whether C-reactive protein (CRP) modifies these associations. Among 4,136 eligible adults, 305 self-reported RA. RA was associated with depression, obesity, HTG, hypertension, stroke, and diabetes, as well as higher CRP levels; RA prevalence increased from low to high CRP categories. Coexisting depression and obesity was associated with higher RA prevalence across all CRP levels, especially medium CRP (27.2% with both versus 19.5% with depression alone and 5.5% with obesity alone). Depression and HTG together showed increased RA prevalence at medium CRP (34.9%), whereas HTG was associated with lower prevalence among depressed subjects at high CRP. Three-way chi-square tests supported synergistic depression–obesity and depression–HTG associations at medium CRP. The cross-sectional design prevents causal or development-risk conclusions. Other limitations include self-reported RA, too few participants with all three conditions for meaningful analysis, and CRP’s nonspecificity. The authors recommend longitudinal studies and broader inflammatory-marker measurement.

The speaker says age is irrelevant in hockey today, emphasizing knowledge, positioning, teamwork, and sacrifice over skating or exceptional skill. Although he had not been examined, he received some treatment, felt better, and hoped to reassess the injury and play the next night. He watched the latest game while icing and described its momentum shifts and Tampa Bay’s strong play. A True Potential survey found average UK personal debt grew £560 in the first quarter of 2017, to £1,797, equivalent to about £10 per day. Lone parents with grown children added £940 and single parents with young children £930. Around 15 per cent of people borrow to cover household necessities, rising to 20 per cent among single parents; other triggers included changing career, taking a new job and funding parental leave. Couples without dependents added the least (£350). Debt was lowest among under-25s (£748) and highest among 45-54-year-olds (£2,299), while North East households owed the most (£2,664). True Potential's David Harrison called for greater financial education, warning debt is "the elephant in the room."

The paper presents information systems as dynamic, human-centered, complex systems rather than merely technical artefacts. It connects the shift in IS research from positivist and technologically deterministic approaches toward human, social, and mixed methods with advances in complexity science and the development of user experience (UX).

Complexity theory emphasizes self-organization, nonlinear relationships, emergence, environmental interaction, and operation far from equilibrium. Unlike “complicated” systems, complex systems cannot be fully understood by analyzing their components; interactions and historical context produce emergent behavior. Bifurcations introduce uncertainty, while flows of matter and energy can sustain order in changing, unstable systems. Irreversibility and the arrow of time are presented as central to living and complex systems. Human use makes an information system complex, continually changing it as users, needs, technology, and organizational conditions evolve.

UX is distinguished from traditional usability by its focus on subjective experience, including look, feel, satisfaction, motivation, and expectations. It therefore requires mixed methods that combine operational usability measures with human and social considerations. Examples including HTML5, intelligent applications, user-generated content, and multi-channel technologies illustrate the impact of human behavior and business needs on contemporary systems. UX is characterized as durational, contextual, subjective, and often irreversible.

The paper reviews prior complexity research in IS, including arguments that information systems are complex adaptive systems and critiques of approaches that separate human requirements from technological development. It contends that changing relationships among people, technology, and organizations make modular, reductionist, and spatially oriented explanations inadequate, favoring self-organization and a temporal perspective. A University of Salford–Sigma Ltd knowledge transfer partnership begun in March 2014 will investigate these ideas with organizations and users, including how time and irreversibility affect design, usability, complexity, and success. The paper concludes that future IS design should accommodate continual adaptation and flexibility.

The paper presents a systematic framework for applying knowledge graph embeddings (KGEs) to ontology alignment within the modular OntoAligner Python library. It frames ontology alignment as identifying correspondences between equivalent entities across ontologies and positions KGEs as an underexplored alternative to dominant machine-learning and large-language-model approaches.

The Graph Embedding Aligner follows a three-stage pipeline. A parser extracts RDF-style subject–predicate–object metadata, IRIs, labels, and class-membership information from source and target ontologies. An encoder combines both ontologies’ triples into a unified triple factory, using natural-language text instead of IRIs so shared structural and semantic patterns can be learned. An aligner trains PyKEEN KGE models through link prediction with negative sampling, then computes cross-ontology cosine similarities between normalized entity embeddings. For each source entity, the most similar target entity is selected; postprocessing enforces one-to-one matches and removes pairs below a confidence threshold.

OntoAligner now supports 17 KGEs, including ConvE, TransD, TransE, TransF, TransH, TransR, DistMult, ComplEx, HolE, RotatE, SimplE, CrossE, BoxE, CompGCN, MuRE, QuatE, and SE. The work aims to enable broad comparative evaluation of KGE-based alignment and exploration of semantically grounded, scalable, and potentially hybrid LLM–KGE approaches.

DAWN-PLASMA was a phase 2, multicenter, randomized, open-label trial comparing standard of care (SOC) plus convalescent plasma with SOC alone in hospitalized adults with COVID-19. Participants were randomized 2:1, and plasma recipients received four units totaling 800–1,000 mL, beginning within 12 hours of randomization, with neutralizing antibody titers of at least 1/160. The primary endpoint was the proportion alive without mechanical ventilation at Day 15. Secondary endpoints assessed clinical status, oxygenation, ventilation, hospitalization, safety, immunogenicity, laboratory measures, and vital signs. The study followed the Declaration of Helsinki and ICH-GCP guidelines.

Between May 2020 and January 2021, 499 patients were assessed and 489 randomized to plasma plus SOC (n=326) or SOC alone (n=163). Day 15 visits occurred for 434 patients and Day 30 visits for 423. The full analysis set excluded one patient without confirmed COVID-19 and five who withdrew consent immediately after randomization. Baseline characteristics and concomitant therapy were similar between groups. Median time to first plasma transfusion was five hours, and median plasma volume was 884 mL; 80.7% of units had titers of at least 1/320. The primary outcome did not differ between groups: 83.7% of the plasma group versus 84.1% of controls were alive without mechanical ventilation at Day 15 (OR 0.99; 95% CI 0.59–1.68; p=0.976), with similar results in the per-protocol set.

The match-up zone combines person-to-person and zone principles through specific defensive rules. It prevents offensive alignments from splitting defenders, makes overloads easier to defend, and can confuse opponents. Success depends on knowledgeable players and communication. The defense reacts to offensive movement, allows perimeter ball movement, and can be supplemented with aggressive traps. It can also dictate offensive alignment by first showing a different formation before applying match-up rules.

Basic assignments designate X1 as point guard, X2 as shooting guard, X3 as small forward, X4 as power forward, and X5 as post player, with changes based on personnel. Against a 2-3 alignment, X1 takes the right-side player with or without the ball, X2 and X3 take the first players to X1’s left and right, X4 takes the second player to X1’s left, and X5 takes the post. Against a 1-3-1 alignment, X4 takes the second player to X1’s right. Against a 1-2-2 alignment, X4 takes the second player to X1’s left and X5 takes the right-side baseline player. Against a 1-4 alignment, X4 takes the left post and X5 the right post.

When defending basket cuts, the primary defender denies the cutter for three steps before switching with the weak-side defender. Defenders may instead interchange assignments while staying with cutters, simplifying some cuts and forcing players to cover multiple positions. Detailed switching, interchange, help, pressure, and post-denial procedures are provided for cutters and screens in 1-3-1, 1-2-2, 2-3, and 1-4 alignments. Similar defenders may interchange roles when handling high-post rolls or other cuts. In a 1-4 alignment, the rules allow a large X5 to remain in the post area when desired. Playing a straight 2-3 zone on the first defensive possession can also force a two-guard offense into a one-guard alignment.

The basic match-up rules can be extended into full- and half-court trapping whenever the ball enters a primary trap zone, such as a corner. Traps may be used strategically after timeouts or free throws and become necessary when trailing late. Listed trap schemes include a quarter-court “X,” a half-court “SOS” press, and a full-court shadow press.

The passage presents container patterns for building reliable, scalable distributed systems. Single-node patterns tightly group containers on one machine to enable resource isolation, team ownership, separation of concerns, reuse, and simpler deployments. The sidecar pattern adds an application container alongside a utility container that augments functionality such as HTTPS termination, configuration synchronization, process monitoring, or Git-based deployment. Sidecars should be modular and reusable through parameterization, stable API design, and image documentation.

The ambassador pattern separates an application from external interactions. An ambassador can route requests to sharded storage, discover environment-specific services, broker connections, or split requests between production and experimental implementations. The adapter pattern normalizes heterogeneous application interfaces into common conventions for monitoring, logging, and health checks, allowing existing or third-party containers to remain unchanged while reusable adapters provide standardized behavior.

The passage then introduces multi-node patterns, including microservices, whose smaller, API-connected services improve team autonomy, independent release schedules, and targeted scaling, but make debugging and architecture more difficult. Replicated load-balanced services use identical instances for redundancy and horizontal scaling, with readiness probes, optional session tracking, caching layers, rate limiting, and SSL termination.

Sharded services divide state among shards, allowing capacity to grow beyond one machine. Their design depends on a deterministic and uniform sharding function, an appropriate shard key, and routing through an ambassador or shared shard router. Because ordinary hashing can remap many keys when shard counts change, consistent hashing is introduced to limit disruption during re-sharding.

The S&P 500 reached its 9.1% average annual price-return mark as July economic data showed weakness. U.S. private payrolls fell to 73,000 jobs, while May and June figures were revised down by 258,000, though gains were concentrated in health care. June data had been comparatively strong, with 12 of 20 indicators beating expectations.

Q2 earnings remained strong: 15 of 17 large-cap companies beat earnings estimates, and 16 of 17 beat sales estimates. S&P 500 earnings growth rose from 7.7% to 11.2%, while sales growth increased from 4.5% to 5.6%. AI-related stocks have supported the market, but valuations of 22–25 times earnings and a negative equity risk premium may limit further gains.

Seasonal conditions are shifting from July’s strength to a historically weaker August–October period. The article anticipates possible market weakness in coming months but notes that a slowdown does not necessarily mean recession. The dollar and 10-year Treasury yield showed technical pressure following tariff news and weak economic data.

DomeShelter Australia’s Container Mounted DomeShelter (CMDS) is a robust, weather-resistant, relocatable shelter designed to withstand Australian Wind Regions A–D. It mounts to container shelters by welding, bolting or Twistlock and is easy to transport. Suitable for temporary or long-term use, it serves oil and gas, agriculture, events and tourism, protecting goods and livestock from heat, moisture, rain and UV.

The disclosure describes a security-awareness system that trains users to respond to phishing emails and untrusted domains while preserving their decision-making autonomy. Unlike anti-ransomware tools that automatically remove recognized threats, the system intercepts potentially risky actions, presents a configurable confirmation prompt, and lets users proceed or reconsider. User responses can be recorded and analyzed to support training and measure security-awareness effectiveness.

On a client device, a driver monitors application process creation and termination and reports newly created processes to a user console. For significant processes, an injector adds a monitor library capable of detecting URL-access attempts, file openings, and actions associated with potentially malicious documents or executables. Detected URL requests are paused while the console resolves shortened or encoded URLs and queries a server. The server identifies destinations as trusted, untrusted, or unknown using domain lists and returns any required notification settings. The console then displays a prompt while the associated application remains paused. The user can confirm the action or return to review it, after which the request is resumed or discarded and the response may be reported to the server.

The server maintains configurable notification settings, while clients store local copies. A client settings hash is compared with the server’s hash; if they differ, updated settings and the new hash are returned and stored locally for the next prompt. This allows administrators to change prompts without involving the security-awareness system administrator. Settings can include message titles, text fields, button labels, help links, checkbox presence, text size, visibility, and foreground and background colors. Administrators can also configure different notifications for different user groups.

For browser-based email clients, URL monitoring may be implemented through injected code or a browser extension. Monitoring activates after a successful login to a supported email service and can pause, allow, or redirect navigation. Because browser extensions have limited operating-system access, a browser intermediary application communicates with client services and enables separate prompt windows and configuration exchange.

The system can also support simulated phishing exercises, immediate training reminders, targeted remediation, and predefined responses such as Ignore, Report, Prompt, or Prevent. It records risky behavior, identifies users needing additional education, and can report daily activity to users or administrators. The disclosure also describes trusted-domain analysis, client and server services, shared-memory communication, client registration and licensing, and deployment as a software-as-a-service product.

The disclosure describes a plumbing fluid-flow measuring and control device installable at a single location common to multiple fluid-consuming appliances. It combines an unobstructed main flow channel with a parallel bypass containing a flowmeter that estimates total flow from a known fraction of bypass flow. A rotating wheel monitored by two movement sensors detects flow direction, enabling accurate net-flow measurement and backflow subtraction.

The device also includes a solenoid shutoff valve, upstream and downstream pressure sensors, and a transceiver that sends flow data to a local or remote computer. The computer stores pre-recorded water-usage signatures for individual appliances, compares measurements against those signatures, identifies appliance use, detects abnormal usage, and issues notifications to user devices. When no known usage is detected, the valve can temporarily close so pressure differences can be measured. A small pressure drop indicates a leak and keeps the valve closed, while no drop or a large drop suggests normal use and prompts reopening. The system can account for baseline leakage and identify additional leaks, pipe breaks, running fixtures, and other abnormal consumption patterns.

A nationwide analysis found 140 districts with outstanding results across subjects and grade levels, while only 14 excelled in one subject but significantly underperformed in the other; 12 of those were strong in math but weak in reading. School-level reading and math scores had a 0.87 correlation. Mississippi and Florida also showed strong relationships between proficiency and student growth across subjects. Among the 50 Mississippi elementary and middle schools with the largest reading gains, none fell below the statewide average in math growth. The analysis favors growth measures because proficiency is highly correlated with socioeconomic status.

Crystal morphology strongly affects energetic-material safety and performance, including shock sensitivity, packing density, detonation velocity, and pressure. Existing Wulff-based approaches—such as BFDH, surface-energy, and attachment-energy models—have limitations in energetic accuracy, sensitivity to selected planes, treatment of edge and corner effects, and prediction of growth kinetics and rates. This work introduces an open-source kinetic Monte Carlo package, cgkmc, that predicts morphology from intermolecular interaction parameters.

The model represents a lattice as a colored, undirected graph: nodes indicate molecular occupation, and weighted edges encode interactions across neighbor shells. Total interaction energy is expressed as a quadratic binary optimization problem, while adjacency-based coordination numbers identify surface sites eligible for adsorption or evaporation. Adsorption rates depend on diffusivity, solubility, surface density, and crystal radius; evaporation rates use harmonic transition-state theory with interaction-derived energy barriers. The rate prefactor is dynamically adjusted to maintain equilibrium at a specified crystal size. A residence-time algorithm then evolves adsorption and evaporation. Simulations of PETN morphology agree with attachment-energy predictions and experimental observations.

Corner-kick defense requires a practiced, clearly assigned plan that players implement immediately after a corner is awarded. Although professional teams have scored from corners as rarely as 2 percent, such success depends on years of tactical preparation and practice. Without preparation, corner kicks remain dangerous.

Defensive plans should progress from straightforward zone defense for youth to man-to-man marking and, ultimately, a mixed approach. Regardless of the system, players must move quickly to assigned positions, attack the ball aggressively, clear it high, far, and wide when possible, communicate, and prepare for a fast counterattack. Defenders should be goal-side, prevent the ball from bouncing, block shots, cover opponents, and contest second balls. The goalkeeper remains in charge, calls for the ball when needed, and controls play after securing possession. A designated striker or other available defender should provide an outlet upfield.

In a zone defense, each defender protects an assigned area. It is easy to teach and allows defenders to move outward toward the ball, but opponents can flood a zone, and teammates may hesitate because they assume someone else will clear it. A basic setup places the goalkeeper from post to post within six yards, one defender at each post, three defenders on the six-yard line, three more in the penalty area, a defender 11 yards from the kicker, and a striker near the corner arc for an outlet.

Man-to-man defense assigns one defender to each attacker. Defenders must track their opponents closely while remaining able to see both attacker and ball. This system avoids overloaded zones but can require defenders to retreat toward goal, create difficult matchups, and lose concentration. Matchups generally progress from players nearest the goal outward, with the goalkeeper and defensive coordinator ensuring every attacker is covered.

A mixed defense combines zoned post and six-yard-line assignments with man-to-man marking elsewhere. It has been reported to produce the fewest corner-kick goals, though the passage notes only limited study evidence.

Training progresses from explaining assignments, to reacting to an announced corner from either side, to practicing clearances and transitions, adding attackers and movement, and finally using live opponents and varied corner kicks. Coaches should scout opponents and adjust plans as needed, repeatedly drill correct execution, and position the goalkeeper centrally, slightly ahead of the goal line, to see both ball and field.

The Mid Screen offense, used by every NBA and WNBA team, relies on a high-post on-ball screen to free the point guard for dribble penetration while shooters space the wings. It can function as a set play or a late-clock action. Basic options include driving around the screen, pulling up when the defense goes under, passing to a cutting post after a switch, dropping to the post, and kicking out to shooters.

Because defensive actions dictate offensive options, the ballhandler and screener must coordinate their reads and counters. Countermeasures include driving opposite the screen, posting for a lob, using pull-up jumpers, posting after switches, isolating mismatched defenders, slipping after a fake screen, and stringing out double teams. Pop actions, post rolls, screen-and-pop options, and rapid passes in the air are also emphasized.

After the initial action, ball reversals can develop into motion, passing, single- or double-screen, flex, inside-triangle, and side-screen continuities. Variations include screen-and-pop, Horns with two high-post screeners, 1-4 low alignment, post isolation, Two Game entries, and triangle post actions.

Successful implementation requires knowledge of the system, precise timing, communication, and coordinated movement by the ballhandler and screener. Teaching recommendations include whole-part-whole instruction, breakdown drills, scrimmages, game situations, and individual skill development. Game strategies include scouting opponents, anticipating defensive reads, monitoring adjustments, varying alignments and entries, and attacking weaker defenders. Teams must also be prepared to defend against the widely used Mid Screen offense.

NVIDIA’s combined L1 data cache/shared-memory architecture, introduced in V100, improves performance and simplifies tuning; A100 provides 192 KB/SM, versus V100’s 128 KB/SM, with low-latency, high-bandwidth access.

A Devils player recounted a two-on-one rush and a power-play chance to set up Marty, after an earlier turnover. He said the Devils plan to keep pressing in Thursday’s next game rather than prolong the series, citing their comeback in the previous round. Now in his third consecutive finals—two in Finland—he said he is more consistent and comfortable against Dallas. He praised Dallas’s speed, puck support, and ability to control time, while crediting New Jersey’s improved defensive discipline, communication, and four-line rotation. He also said a veteran teammate remains in excellent shape and has played more in the playoffs.

After his college season ended, Sabres prospect Casey Mittelstadt could sign an AHL or amateur tryout contract to play for Rochester in the regular season and playoffs. Buffalo prefers an amateur tryout this season and an NHL entry-level deal beginning in 2018-19, though signing would end his NCAA eligibility.

The passage presents a 500-kHz synchronous push-pull converter design using TPS7H5001-SP and GaN FETs. Selected values include a 205-kΩ frequency-setting resistor, 5-V output programmed by 10-kΩ and 1.4-kΩ feedback resistors, approximately 25 ns dead time with 20.5-kΩ RPS and RSP resistors, and a 49.9-kΩ leading-edge blank-time resistor initially targeting 50 ns. The blank-time value may require optimization for PCB parasitics, ringing, and gate-driver delay and affects maximum switching frequency. A 33-nF soft-start capacitor provides approximately 7.5 ms of soft start.

The transformer design targets a 35% duty cycle, a 2.5 turns ratio, and magnetizing current equal to 6% of output current. Although the calculated primary inductance was 33 µH, 40 µH was used. Primary GaN FETs were rated at 170 V for a maximum 36-V input to accommodate off-state voltage and transients. An 80-V GaN FET was selected for the synchronous rectifier, whose expected maximum stress was about 20 V. A parallel Schottky diode can reduce soft-start current and dead-time conduction losses. An RCD clamp may limit switch-node overshoot, with initial values determined from leakage inductance, peak primary current, allowable overshoot, and capacitor ripple, then optimized through testing.

The output inductor is 0.47 µH with a targeted 40% ripple current. Calculations based on 2% output ripple and 2.5% maximum transient deviation require at least 1.3 mF of output capacitance; approximately 2.3 mF was used for radiation-induced single-event-transient mitigation. This was implemented with seven 330-µF polymer tantalum capacitors, each having approximately 6-mΩ ESR, for an equivalent parallel ESR of 0.86 mΩ. An optional LC filter using ceramic capacitance can further reduce output noise, with damping available if high-frequency peaking occurs.

Cycle-by-cycle current limiting begins at approximately 35 A, providing about 45% margin over the 24.25-A peak inductor current at maximum load. A 1:100 current-sense transformer and 7.5-Ω RCS resistor set the overcurrent level. The hiccup capacitor is 3.3 nF. Type 2A frequency compensation targets a 10-kHz crossover and uses 40.2-kΩ RCOMP, 15-nF CCOMP, and 47-pF CHF components; compensation is expected to be tuned during testing. A 102-kΩ resistor from RSC to AVSS provides slope compensation.

Application curves cover output soft start at 10 A and a 5-A load-step response. The controllers require a regulated 4- to 14-V supply and at least a 0.1-µF VIN-to-AVSS bypass capacitor, preferably X5R or better and placed close to the controller. Additional bulk capacitance is recommended for remote supplies.

Layout guidance emphasizes routing feedback away from magnetics and switch-node noise, minimizing switch-node copper and high-di/dt/high-dv/dt loops, separating analog and power grounds except at one connection point, and using short, direct, wide high-current traces of at least 15 mils per ampere. Filtering and bypass capacitors should be near the controller, compensation components near COMP, and the VSENSE divider nearby. Gate-drive and SYNC traces should be separated from sensitive control signals; RC filtering may be needed at CS_ILIM. CFP packages require backside metallization connected to the AVSS plane through multiple vias. The document also lists evaluation-module guides, radiation reports, support resources, revision information, and mechanical and orderable data.

The passage outlines the SAE's five levels of self-driving capability. Production cars have reached Level 1 (cruise control) and Level 2 (automated steering), both requiring constant driver attention. BMW plans Level 3 for its 2021 iNext electric car, but many firms skip to Level 4, where drivers have minutes to retake control and the car can stop itself safely. Waymo already runs Level 4 cars and plans a Phoenix taxi service; driverless Level 5 is not expected until the end of the next decade.

The application, a continuation of U.S. Ser. No. 16/472,818, describes systems and methods for detecting and classifying abnormal cardiac activity using deep learning. It addresses limitations of continuous ECG monitoring, which may be cumbersome, invasive, costly, or ineffective for asymptomatic atrial fibrillation, and of wearable PPG monitoring, whose recordings can be degraded by motion.

Sensor collection devices provide cardiac data, such as ECG or PPG, and motion data, such as accelerometer data, potentially through wearable devices. Optional subject contextual information includes medical history, demographics, medications, and related data. Cardiac and motion data are divided into periods and windows, preprocessed to reduce noise and outliers, normalized, filtered, and resampled. Signal quality indices are calculated for each dataset, with quality channels or windows identified based on cardiac quality and motion energy. Cardiovascular features, including entropy and standard-deviation measures, are extracted.

Cardiac and/or motion data are transformed into time-frequency tensors using methods such as wavelet, short-time Fourier, or Gabor transforms. A deep learning architecture comprising a convolutional neural network, bidirectional recurrent neural network, and attention network processes the tensors and associated quality, cardiovascular, and contextual features. The convolutional network extracts deep features, the recurrent network assigns class probabilities to each window, and the attention network weights windows to produce a period-level classification. Results may identify normal, abnormal, or noisy cardiac activity, the type of abnormality, affected windows, and the burden of abnormal activity. Abnormal activity may include arrhythmias or non-arrhythmic conditions. The systems may also generate reports and may be implemented as methods, storage-medium instructions, or processor-based computing systems.

This retrospective cohort study analyzed routinely collected electronic health records from two southeastern U.S. academic health systems. It included 2,514 women aged 13–54 with hypertensive disorders of pregnancy who delivered in 2014–2017 and had a blood pressure measurement 15–90 days postpartum, excluding those with pre-existing hypertension. Cox proportional hazards models with multiple imputation estimated associations with incident hypertension through the first year postpartum.

Thirteen percent (315 participants) were diagnosed with hypertension after the postpartum blood pressure check. Elevated systolic blood pressure was associated with greater hazard (HR 1.70 for 140 versus 120 mmHg), as were severe preeclampsia/eclampsia versus gestational hypertension (HR 1.49) and older maternal age (HR 1.46 for age 35 versus 25). A later postpartum check was associated with lower hazard. Modeled 12-month diagnosis risk ranged from 4.7% at 110/65 mmHg to 13.0% at 140/90 mmHg. Sensitivity analyses by provider specialty produced similar findings.

Approximately 40% of eligible patients lacked a documented 15–90-day blood pressure check, and only 20% had one within 14 days. At the postpartum visit, 55% had readings in the Stage 1 or 2 hypertension range. The authors identified inconsistent guideline implementation, access barriers, and reliance on diagnosis codes as study limitations. They recommended using health records to identify patients needing screening, expanding options such as home monitoring, telehealth, and home visitors, and consistently prioritizing early blood pressure management and long-term cardiovascular risk reduction after hypertensive pregnancy disorders.

JPMorgan Chase is deploying artificial intelligence across its global operations to cut costs, streamline workflows and improve client services, having extended its proprietary generative AI platform to all 200,000 employees, moving from pilots to full deployment. The bank is investing roughly $18 billion in technology this year, with much of it going to AI, machine learning and cloud infrastructure. In retail banking, AI automates customer support, payments and account management; in wealth and asset management, "Smart Monitor" analyses earnings calls, filings and market data to generate research insights, reportedly cutting analysis time by up to 83%, while "Connect Coach" gives private bankers real-time product recommendations. Institutional applications now cover credit assessment, client onboarding, fraud detection and risk management, with over 175 active use cases and employees gaining several hours of weekly productivity from automated tasks. Remaining hurdles include balancing innovation with compliance, transparency, bias, model risk, security vulnerabilities, legacy-system integration and adoption costs. The approach could set a global standard for large-scale AI adoption in finance, but will be tested under market stress and tighter regulation.

The remainder consists of repeated financial news headlines and a description of Pan Finance as a global financial intelligence publication with offices in London, Lagos, Barcelona, Miami and Sharjah.

Wandera research on 50,000 moderately to heavily used iPhones and iPads found that iOS 11 drained batteries more than twice as fast as iOS 10, with estimated runtimes falling from 240 to 96 minutes. Older iPhones experienced worse drain, and some users reverted to iOS 10.3.3 despite Wandera’s security warning. Apple’s iOS 11.0.1 update improved drain time to 159 minutes, a 65% gain. To extend battery life, users can restrict background app refresh and location access and enable low-power mode.

Enron’s shares fell by more than 50% over two weeks, erasing nearly $14 billion in market value, as Moody's downgraded the company’s senior unsecured long-term debt from Baa1 to Baa2—two notches above junk—and kept the rating under review for further cuts. Enron sought $1 billion to $2 billion in additional bank credit after drawing $3.3 billion from existing facilities to repay commercial paper, leaving approximately $1.2 billion in net cash. Analysts said lenders were likely to demand higher rates, collateral and other stricter terms as Enron sold assets and sought other liquidity support.

The crisis followed a $618 million third-quarter loss, $1.01 billion in write-offs and a $1.2 billion reduction in shareholder equity tied to private partnerships managed by former CFO Andrew Fastow. The Securities and Exchange Commission opened an inquiry into possible conflicts of interest. Fastow was removed, and Enron’s shares and bonds fell sharply as investors questioned the company’s financial reporting and credibility.

European energy companies froze or restricted trading with Enron, while some remaining counterparties required bank letters of credit or other safeguards. Analysts questioned whether Enron’s asset-light strategy could survive the loss of confidence, noted declining trading margins and potential difficulties retaining senior employees whose stock options had become nearly worthless. At least five shareholder lawsuits challenged Enron’s partnership transactions.

Separately, Moody’s reported that U.S. corporate credit quality was deteriorating, with 122 companies placed on review for downgrade and only 22 for upgrade in the third quarter.

A 2006 AMD CS5535 specification update identifies PS/2, ATA, LPC, SMB, PCI, GPIO, and power-management issues. Reading Port 60h incorrectly clears AuxOutputFull, so interrupts should manage USB keyboard and mouse traffic in PS/2 emulation. UDMA tACK bits do not affect timing because IDE_DACK setup is fixed at 30 ns; no action is required. ATAC may hang with WORD-aligned PRDs, so drivers should use DWORD alignment. LPC may abort transactions when SYNC is delayed until the third clock after turnaround, particularly with LPC-to-ISA bridges; a PLD-based workaround is described. The SMB NEGACK bit may be cleared or set inconsistently; it should be cleared by writing 1 to SMB_STS[4], followed by writing 0x00 to SMB_STS. GLPCI’s retry limit also counts retries from other PCI bus transactions and may cause earlier termination; only partial guidance is provided. After suspend, atomic GPIO High Bank Feature Bit Register writes clear non-selected bits; read-modify-write should be used instead. The SMBus hold-time entry notes a 300 ns SMB 2.0 requirement but is incomplete. Abnormal standby may fail to set LOWBAT_FLAG, with no resolution specified. Premature PM delay-counter resets can leave SLEEP_X and SLEEP_Y asserted and PCI/IDE inputs disabled; PM_SCXD, PM_SCYD, and PM_IN_SLPCTL delays should be programmed below PM_SED.

Connaught Public School students attempted a tunnel ball world record, with over 250 playing at once, surpassing the previous mark of 120 pending Guinness verification. The event also raised $10,000 for playground and yard improvements.

Seattle's housing market is among the nation's hottest, and with prices and rents rising for years, some fear another bubble like the Great Recession. A ValueInsured survey found 71 percent of Washington homeowners worried about a bubble, though the online poll of 1,079 people (about 21 per state) was too small to support firm conclusions. According to the Northwest Multiple Listing Service, King County's median sale price rose 18.6 percent year over year, from July 2016 to July 2017, to $658,000, while homes for sale fell more than 13 percent. However, Windermere Real Estate president OB Jacobi said nothing indicates artificially inflated prices, noting King County buyers have high credit scores, above-average down payments and high home equity. Experts interviewed over the past two years agree the market is hot but unlikely to reverse as in 2008. NWMLS director George Moorhead expects a "market correction" in which prices and inventory level out, though he raised concerns about lending practices that help buyers with poor credit or existing debt. The article also includes a gallery ranking the income needed to buy a home in 25 cities, calculated from Redfin median sale prices with a 20 percent down payment at 3.75 percent over 30 years, ranging from $7,359 in Detroit to $226,577 in San Francisco, with Seattle at $106,709.

Billionaire CEOs offer sharply different views on work-life balance. Jeff Bezos rejects the term because it implies a tradeoff, preferring “harmony” between work and home. Reid Hoffman says founders seeking balance are not committed to winning, while Cerebras CEO Andrew Feldman argues that building something extraordinary requires every waking minute. Scale AI cofounder Lucy Guo says work may not feel like work, though she still reserves time for family and friends. Zoom CEO Eric Yuan says work and life cannot truly be separated but prioritizes family when conflicts arise. Jack Ma described China’s demanding 996 schedule as a blessing for young workers who may not have that opportunity later.

U.S. consumer confidence rose to 128.7 in April from 127.0 in March, nearing February’s 18-year high. Strong labor markets, tax cuts, reduced stock volatility and easing trade-war concerns supported confidence, while sluggish real-income growth could restrain consumer spending.

NEC Corp has established the "NEC Satellite Operation Center," operational this April, to operate the ASNARO-2 radar satellite, developed with METI assistance and launched in January. Using NEC's GroundNEXTAR system and a high-security data center, the center can operate multiple satellites and offers 3D visualization and image distribution. From September, NEC plans to market ASNARO-2 images with JEOSS.

The TPS7H500x-SP series comprises radiation-hardness-assured, fixed-frequency, peak-current-mode PWM controllers for space-grade DC-DC converters. Switching frequencies up to 2 MHz are supported, and the controllers require external gate drivers for the power stage. Supported topologies include buck, flyback, forward, active-clamp forward, push-pull, and full-bridge converters.

Frequency compensation can use Type 2A or Type 2B schemes. Type 2A adds a capacitor, CHF, in parallel with RCOMP and CCOMP for high-frequency noise attenuation. Thermal shutdown stops switching above a typical junction temperature of 175°C and restarts the power-up sequence below 160°C.

A GaN-based synchronous push-pull example uses the TPS7H5001-SP at 500 kHz with a 5-V output. Selected values include a 205-kΩ frequency-setting resistor, 10-kΩ and 1.4-kΩ feedback resistors, 25-ns dead time, 49.9-kΩ leading-edge blank-time resistor, 33-nF soft-start capacitor, 2.5 transformer turns ratio, and 40-µH primary inductance. The design uses 170-V primary GaN FETs, an 80-V synchronous rectifier, a 0.47-µH output inductor, 2.3 mF total output capacitance, a 7.5-Ω current-sense resistor, and a 102-kΩ slope-compensation resistor. Type 2A compensation targets a 10-kHz crossover using 40.2 kΩ, 15 nF, and 47 pF for RCOMP, CCOMP, and CHF, respectively.

The controllers operate from 4 V to 14 V and require at least a 0.1-µF input bypass capacitor. Layout guidance emphasizes separating feedback and control signals from switching nodes, minimizing high-current loop area, connecting analog and power grounds at one point, placing bypass and compensation components near the controller, and using appropriate filtering and trace widths. The passage also lists related TI documentation, revision history, ESD precautions, and mechanical and orderable information.

The passage describes Tiered Memory Page Migration (TMPM) ring-buffer behavior, SPA encoding, migration commands, and error handling. Precise halting requires the halt command to be last in the queue, while precise error halting requires queuing only one command because commands may be distributed across parallel execution units. Interrupt status can be cleared by setting `PM_RBCtl[CLEAR_INTS]` when the ring buffer is empty or processing is paused; interrupt generation resumes when processing resumes.

For SMEE- or SME-MK-enabled systems, software encodes encryption information in SPAs used by migration commands and parameter blocks. The C-bit indicates encrypted memory under SMEE, and commands distinguish Hypervisor from Guest memory. Firmware selects the applicable encryption key. SPAs must be well-formed and within appropriate address ranges, while reserved fields must be zero.

`PM_GET_CAPABILITIES` queries supported firmware capabilities and versions and may be configured to interrupt on completion. `PM_PAGE_MOVE_IO` processes 1–128 migration entries. It supports SNP and non-SNP systems, though SNP systems permit only Hypervisor-owned pages, and SEV systems permit only unencrypted or host/Hypervisor-encrypted memory. It can migrate pages used by DMA and updates IOMMU host page-table entries. Software must protect pages from CPU access and perform required ATS invalidations and synchronization before migration, then update CPU host page tables afterward. Under SNP, source and destination pages must remain in the Hypervisor state. Direct 2 MiB migration is unsupported; such pages must first be split into 4 KiB pages. Firmware validates addresses, page-table mappings, states, sizes, and RMP access; performs CPU and IOMMU invalidations and synchronization; flushes DMA; copies page contents while preserving encryption; updates page tables and RMPs; and clears migration markers.

`PM_PAGE_MOVE_GUEST` moves 1–128 pages belonging to an SNP guest. It requires RMP enforcement, valid non-default source and destination pages, a valid Guest Context page, exclusive source and destination RMP access, matching page sizes, acceptable source and destination states, and CPU TLB invalidation and synchronization. DMA during migration is unsupported and may be aborted. After migration, destination pages take the source states, while source pages return to the Pre-Migration state. Two-MiB pages must be aligned and physically contiguous.

A final command marks the end of a sequence of migration commands and may interrupt on completion. Command-format errors cause rejection, migration-list errors may cause partial success, and status and sub-status fields report results. Ring-buffer errors are reported through `PM_STATUS`; hardware errors may also invoke Machine Check Architecture handling. After batch processing begins, a hardware error may make all pages in the batch unrecoverable, requiring software to preserve state and potentially reboot.

McEachern, the SN NEXT No. 1 team, hosted Harrison Friday night in Kennesaw, Georgia. Both entered 5-0 after a bye, with McEachern atop The Sporting News’ NEXT 25 bubble rankings; Harrison sought a high-profile upset.

Astronomers and citizen scientists using the LOFAR radio telescope discovered RAD J131346.9+500320, the most distant and powerful known odd radio circle: a double-ringed structure nearly 10 billion years old. The study suggests its rings may form from superwind outflows rather than black-hole mergers. The team also identified two enormous radio galaxies with unusual rings, both located in galaxy clusters weighing about 100 trillion Suns. These findings suggest that black-hole jets interacting with hot surrounding plasma help shape such structures. Upcoming facilities and surveys are expected to reveal more rings and clarify their origins and evolution.

Peter Marks, the former top FDA vaccine regulator ousted by RFK Jr., has joined Eli Lilly Research Laboratories to lead molecule discovery and infectious diseases. Louisiana sued the alleged Banking Department of the Citizens’ Bank for a banking license. The bank’s president contested citation, asserting that no separate “Cash or Banking Department” corporation existed and that he lacked authority to represent it. The court held that the statutes and compact authorized only the Citizens’ Bank of Louisiana to sue and be sued, not a separate banking department. Because the state deliberately did not name the Citizens’ Bank as defendant, citation of the alleged department was insufficient. Hope & Co. v. Board of Liquidation did not require citation because that case proceeded against the Citizens’ Bank itself. The court limited its ruling to the citation issue, leaving corporate existence, estoppel, and other questions open. It reversed the judgment and dismissed the suit as in the nature of a nonsuit. Justice Monroe dissented.

An email from Enron's ETS group (Kimberly Nelson, dated Feb. 25, 2002) circulated press clippings from Inside FERC, Gas Daily, Associated Press, Reuters, Dow Jones, Business News Americas and the Wall Street Journal covering Enron and broader energy news.

**Enron bankruptcy and asset sales:** Enron's pipelines and power plants remain outside the bankruptcy and provide steady income; interim CEO Stephen Cooper told employees persuading creditors the company is "a reorganizable platform" will be an "uphill battle." UBS Warburg launched UBS Warburg Energy with roughly 625 former Enron traders for a 33% profit share, with no upfront payment. Enron agreed to sell Portland General Electric to Northwest Natural Gas, sold its wind subsidiary to General Electric and its India oil and gas assets to BG Group for $350 million, and still operates 11,000 miles of non-bankrupt U.S. pipelines after Dynegy acquired the 16,500-mile Northern Natural Gas. Brazil and Bolivia operations are the most likely retained assets. Enron plans retention bonuses and severance, a new company name, and consolidating its remaining Houston workforce (under 3,000 employees) into its leased headquarters.

FERC detailed meetings by commissioners Linda Breathitt (five) and William Massey (six) and director Daniel Larcamp (five), who toured Enron's trading floor twice. Sen. Charles Grassley criticized this government support.

**Other energy news:** BG Group plans to more than double Indian investment to $1.3 billion from about $500 million, targeting upstream and LNG, and is developing an LNG terminal at Pipavav port; CEO Frank Chapman is to raise its unresolved operatorship dispute with India's Oil & Natural Gas Corp. over the offshore Panna, Mukta and Tapti fields during a February 25–26 visit. California Gov. Gray Davis considered delaying the MTBE ban to 2005, citing a Stillwater Associates analysis warning of gasoline shortages and price spikes, and blamed "politics in the Midwest" for the EPA's rejection of California's waiver request.

The paper addresses budget pacing in real-time advertising auctions, where dynamic auction conditions, traffic variability, and noisy signals make empirical tuning unstable and inefficient. It proposes a Bucketized Hysteresis Controller (BHC), a nonlinear, multi-step control strategy inspired by bang-bang control and gain scheduling. BHC discretizes normalized pacing error into non-overlapping bands with predefined gains, applying larger adjustments for large errors and smaller adjustments for minor errors to support rapid convergence and stability. The work includes an analytical framework for parameter selection, comparisons with a legacy variable-step multiplicative controller, and validation through real-world auction experiments.

In the described auction setup, bids are calculated as the maximum bid multiplied by the probability that an impression is seen, and the pacing multiplier λ rescales the final bid to influence auction win rates and spending. The legacy baseline updates λ multiplicatively based on under- or over-delivery. Its step size is adjusted using a fluctuation factor that measures cumulative variation relative to net displacement: stable trends increase the step size, while oscillations reduce it. The BHC instead calculates normalized error and direction, selects an error band and associated gain, and updates λ accordingly.

NASA released two unprecedented close-up images of bright deposits in Ceres’ 50-mile-wide Occator Crater, captured by the Dawn spacecraft during its extended mission. The June 14 image shows Vinalia Faculae from about 24 miles above Ceres; the June 22 image captures Cerealia Facula from roughly 21 miles away and reveals a prominent mound on its western side. Discovered by Dawn in 2015, these faculae are the largest carbonate deposits found outside Earth and may exceed those on Mars, but their origin remains unclear. Scientists are investigating whether they came from shallow mineral-rich water or deeper brines rising through fractures. Dawn’s gravity measurements and remote-sensing instruments will also examine Ceres’ interior and composition. The spacecraft is nearing the end of its mission because it is running out of thruster fuel, and it is expected to remain in its final orbit after ending its mission in the second half of 2018 to avoid contaminating Ceres.

The ISDA Press Report of May 16, 2001 covers developments in derivatives regulation, accounting, markets and infrastructure.

- IRS hedging regulations: Witnesses were expected to tell the IRS that proposed rules failed to implement Congress’s broader shift from risk reduction to risk management. Recommendations included extending hedging treatment to commodities-dealer transactions, weather and energy derivatives, dividend and profitability hedges, life insurers’ gap hedges, and service-income transactions.

- OTC derivatives: BIS data showed outstanding OTC contracts grew only 1% in the second half of 2000, down from nearly 7% in the first half. Notional value reached $95.2 trillion, led by interest-rate derivatives and swaps. A 7% decline in euro-denominated interest-rate contracts contributed to slower growth, while gross market value rose 24% to $3.2 trillion.

- FAS 133 compliance: The Federal Home Loan Bank of New York implemented the standard using Principia Partners’ Analytic System for derivatives valuation, hedge-effectiveness testing, reporting and accounting entries.

- Single-stock futures: A former CFTC chairman identified higher regulatory and margin costs, low option-equivalent trading volumes and a three-year prohibition on options on single-stock futures as potential limitations. CME and CBOE announced a joint venture with CBOT to create a separately regulated, electronic single-stock-futures exchange using CBOEdirect and GLOBEX2.

- FASB option accounting: FASB rejected an amendment but proposed recording option fair-value changes in other comprehensive income until the hedged transaction affects earnings. The approach requires an exact match with the underlying exposure, including cash-flow timing, effectiveness and no basis risk.

- Basel and the FSA: Basel Committee officials defended the proposed 15% capital floor on credit-derivative positions, saying it addressed material risks associated with documentation instability and credit derivatives’ potential failure to pay. The FSA was also pressing for banks and insurers to face equivalent prudential standards and for the new Basel Accord to proceed quickly.

- Building societies: The UK Treasury proposed legislation allowing building societies to use credit derivatives for borrower-default risk management. Existing law would continue to prohibit speculative use.

- Default-swap arbitrage: Credit-linked note issuance of at least £5 billion and possibly £15 billion drove offsetting credit-default-swap sales and sharply widened negative swap-to-bond bases. Some dealers profited by buying swaps and selling synthetic packages, while corporate treasurers benefited from tighter credit spreads.

- Bandwidth trading: Lightrade was extending its neutral pooling-point network from New York to Los Angeles, adding U.S. sites and investigating Europe. Its switches facilitate bandwidth trading without owning fiber or conducting trades, but carrier interconnections and conflicts involving competing platforms remained obstacles.

- ISDA documentation: ISDA finalized a supplement to its 1999 Credit Derivatives Definitions. It limits the maturity of deliverable securities following a credit-restructuring event and defines eligible transferees for certain obligations, responding partly to concerns raised by Conseco’s restructuring and the resulting “cheapest-to-deliver” exposure.

The Horns offense uses high-post mid-screen action, typically with a big screening for a smaller guard. Unprepared defenses may allow layups or open shots, while switching can let the guard flare to the wing and the screener post against the smaller defender. Preferred NBA responses are influencing ballhandlers toward their weak hand or away from the strongest screener, though tactics vary.

The “Show and Recover” defense pushes the ballhandler sideline, shows the screen, recovers to the roller, and applies help, pressure, post defense, and pass denial. “All Out SOS Disruption” traps the point guard before screening action develops, disrupts the offense’s routes, and rotates to shooters, rollers, and passing lanes. Defenders then use set positions, helpside help, and baseline or post traps.

The article explains and backtests the Internal Bar Strength (IBS) indicator, calculated as (Close − Low) / (High − Low). It ranges from zero to one, measures where the close falls within the daily range, and treats low values as short-term bullish and high values as bearish based on mean reversion.

IBS performed strongly over roughly 30 years on stocks and stock indices, particularly during volatile or bear markets, but results varied by market and sector. A modified SPY strategy produced a 15.3% CAGR while invested 36% of the time, with a 74% win rate and 22% maximum drawdown. On QQQ, 742 trades averaged 0.56% per trade and compounded at 16.6%, versus 9% for buy and hold. Volatility and moving-average filters improved average gains and profit factors, though small parameter changes made some results variable and raised curve-fitting concerns.

The indicator works best on broadly diversified stock indices and generally does not work well on commodity stocks, Norwegian and Australian markets, gold, or metals. The article argues that traders should adapt strategies to individual markets rather than expect universal rules across asset classes.

A key weakness is execution near the close: waiting until the next open reduced SPY’s average trade gain from 0.41% to 0.31%. The authors use IBS alongside other indicators or factors and conclude that it can remain effective in volatile stock markets.

Alpha Theory’s Analytics Department finds that investor biases often cause position sizes to deviate from optimal levels. Common issues include failing to reduce exposure after large gains, gradually building positions and missing potential returns, and holding stocks without explicit price targets. More disciplined managers tend to outperform. Re-underwriting holdings when probability-weighted returns become unacceptable can reveal bias and prevent reversal losses. A 2011–2016 Monte Carlo study found concentrated portfolios outperformed diversified portfolios by 2.2% on an alpha basis without commensurate risk protection, while optimal position sizing could have improved 2016 returns by 5.1%.

The lecture examines adaptive experimentation and robust engineering design. It contrasts Sir Edward John Russell’s preference for simple, one-factor-at-a-time experiments with R. A. Fisher’s use of complex factorial designs, emphasizing that statistical planning should occur before experiments are run. Although full factorial designs improve estimation efficiency, their size grows rapidly with the number of factors. Fractional factorial designs reduce this burden by sacrificing information and creating risks of confounding main effects with interactions.

Robust parameter design seeks to reduce performance variation by selecting controllable factors so a system is less sensitive to uncontrolled noise. Taguchi pioneered crossed arrays combining control and noise factors, and such methods became entrenched in industrial practice, although the lecturer reported that some combined-array procedures can perform poorly. His research therefore examined adaptive one-factor-at-a-time experimentation as an alternative.

Empirical comparisons of adaptive and fractional factorial designs across 66 systems found that adaptive experimentation performed as well or better when experimental error was moderate or interactions were substantial. Theoretical analysis showed that adaptive experiments can capture benefits from both main effects and interactions, although they cannot clearly identify which interaction produced an observed improvement. With seven factors, an adaptive experiment used eight trials, compared with 128 for a full factorial design, and could approach 80% of the best attainable outcome. Randomized factor order had little effect, while informed starting points substantially improved results.

Crossing adaptive control-factor experiments with factorial noise designs produced strong robustness gains and generally slightly outperformed Taguchi-style crossed arrays, particularly with informed starts. Ensembles of adaptive experiments also remained competitive with larger fractional factorial designs and became more robust as experimental error increased.

Practical limitations include the need for sequential experiments and delays in measurement, which can favor factorial designs. Adaptive methods optimize improvement rather than precise causal or archival knowledge, so they are less suitable when precise effect estimation and reusable inference are priorities. The lecture concludes that organizations should generally conduct more numerous, cheaper robust-design studies rather than a few expensive ones unless they are nearly certain about where their largest quality problems lie. Subsequent discussion addressed problem sets involving factorial experiments, regression, confidence intervals, and noise factors.

The 2-1-2 zone is a compact variation of the 2-3 zone that protects the middle rather than the baseline and corners. It uses an athletic middle defender and places the “Bigs” near the blocks for rebounding. Because it is vulnerable to outside shooting, it is mainly used against poor outside-shooting teams or high-post offenses such as the 1-3-1. Assignments shift with ball location: outside defenders cover the ball, elbow, or deny return passes, while baseline defenders cover the post, establish weak-side rebounding position, and protect against high/low post passes. The middle defender pressures the high post, fronts the low post, and forces ballhandlers toward corners when the ball enters the middle. The outside defenders must move in unison and are typically the team’s quickest players, while the post defender is usually aggressive and athletic.

The passage outlines options trading on Amazon (AMZN). Options allow investors to speculate on AMZN's price or hedge existing positions, but the market is complex and requires substantial research.

Strategies include buying calls and puts, writing covered calls and puts, writing naked calls and puts, and spread trading. Buying calls or puts grants the right, but not the obligation, to buy or sell the underlying stock at a predetermined price by expiration. Covered strategies generate premium income with downside protection; naked calls carry unlimited loss risk as the stock can rise without limit, and naked puts expose investors to large losses. Spread trading — simultaneously buying and selling options with different strikes and/or expirations — limits risk by exploiting premium differences.

Key risks include leverage (small price moves can render options worthless, and most expire worthless), expiration dates (the premium is paid regardless of in- or out-of-the-money status), liquidity (no guarantee of a buyer or seller to close a position), and margin calls if account capital falls below requirements. Volatility raises option premiums, since a greater chance of expiring in-the-money results.

Advantages include leverage of capital, the ability to take long or short positions without owning the stock, and risk limitation through spreads. Option prices move inversely to calls and directly to puts relative to the stock price, with delta measuring sensitivity.

Requirements to begin include a margin account, sufficient capital for premium, commissions and fees, and a thorough understanding of options and their risks. Most brokers require a $2,000 minimum deposit. Orders may be market, limit, or stop. Strike price determines payoff: calls profit when the stock is above it, puts when below. Profits arise when the option becomes in-the-money; tax treatment varies by option type and holding period (short- versus long-term capital gains), and most capital gains taxes apply in the investor's country of residence. Fees depend on the broker, typically a flat or percentage-based commission plus exchange, clearing and platform fees. Analysis is best conducted through quantified, statistical methods for entry, exit, and profit/loss estimation. Expirations are typically the third Friday of the month, with weekly and monthly options also offered. Execution speed and margin requirements vary by broker, with most filling orders in under a second and higher margins for naked options and spreads. When choosing a platform, investors should compare fees, execution speed, and research and analysis tools.

The paper studies classical bilinear–biquadratic Heisenberg spin models on a partially anisotropic triangular lattice formed by isosceles triangles. Using two bilinear couplings \(K,L\) and two biquadratic couplings \(A,B\), it reduces the lattice problem to minimizing the energy of a single triangular plaquette. The inter-spin angles \(\alpha,\beta,\gamma\) satisfy inequalities defining a tetrahedron whose vertices, edges, and faces represent collinear or coplanar configurations, while interior points represent noncoplanar configurations. Ground states are determined by checking these tetrahedron regions, yielding ferromagnetic, antiferromagnetic, coplanar, spin-density-wave-like, and noncoplanar configurations with their energies and applicability conditions. Interior noncoplanar solutions require \(\cos\alpha=K/(2A)\) and \(\cos\beta=\cos\gamma=L/(2B)\) within specified bounds. Phase diagrams for the Heisenberg and XY models are presented for several values of \(A\), distinguishing continuous and discontinuous transitions. The single-plaquette solutions can also be used to construct global ground states for many lattices composed of identical isosceles triangles, including three-dimensional lattices.
