As high-street banks close branches and mobile-only firms such as Atom, Monzo and Revolut grow, the article considers whether smartphone banking will become the norm. A Which? survey of 9,076 members found over half of under-40s would accept a mobile-only account, while interest fell sharply among those aged 40 and over. Mobile banking may offer competitive savings rates and convenience, but Atom’s app reportedly crashed during a surge of applicants, highlighting the lack of in-person support. Commenters stressed the importance of branches for assistance, coin deposits and cheque payments, while some favored ATMs or shared and part-time branch facilities.

A confidential memorandum proposes preparing U.S. negotiators for a peace conference by commissioning qualified historians, political economists, and jurists to write secret, comprehensive studies on history, commerce, international law, and related subjects such as disarmament, arbitration, and international guarantees. Experts would receive detailed instructions, prepare pamphlets of no more than 10,000–15,000 words, and submit them to a single coordinator responsible for reviewing, printing, and indexing the material. Appendices containing documents, statistics, and quotations would also be assembled and secretly printed for reference. The memorandum lists questions concerning U.S. involvement in European boundaries and colonial redistribution, criteria for territorial settlements, the role of conquest and enforced colonization, competing national claims, and guarantees for colonial powers. Colonel E. M. House tells Secretary of State Robert Lansing that the proposed organization is helpful and plans to discuss it further.

Tennessee middle schooler Keaton Jones went viral after his mother recorded him describing the bullying he endured at school. Celebrities including LeBron James and Mark Ruffalo publicly supported him and condemned bullying.

The court denied defendants’ motion to set aside their conviction for possession of burglar’s tools. Antonio Vasquez and Hector Perez were charged with possessing burglar’s tools, attempted petit larceny, and resisting arrest. Testimony stated that they attempted to take a bicycle by partially cutting its chain with bolt cutters but abandoned the attempt after speaking with a third person. The court instructed the jury on renunciation for attempted petit larceny, but not for possession of burglar’s tools. The jury convicted defendants of possessing burglar’s tools and acquitted them of the other charges. Under Penal Law § 40.10, the court concluded that renunciation applies only to specified offenses and did not authorize the requested instruction. Although noting the troubling result and suggesting legislative consideration of an amendment, the court denied the motion.

Insecticides India plans to invest Rs 200 crore over three years to expand capacity at its Dahej and Chopanki plants, including two synthesis facilities and an export-oriented unit. It expects 10–15% revenue growth, supported by forecast normal monsoon rains and seven or eight new products. This fiscal year’s expansion investment is Rs 25–50 crore, funded through internal accruals, debt and equity. In 2017–18, net profit rose 41% to Rs 83.97 crore and total income increased to Rs 1,109.63 crore, although fourth-quarter net profit grew 5% while total income declined.

The passage describes the operation, programming, register configuration, and application guidance for the ADS8681W, ADS8685W, and ADS8689W. The multiSPI interface supports single-device standard SPI connections and daisy-chained devices. In a daisy chain, devices share CONVST/CS and SCLK, and each SDO-0 output feeds the next device’s SDI input. Devices require identical configurations, and an optimal frame for N devices contains 32 × N SCLK capture edges.

The device operates in RESET, ACQ, and CONV states. The active-low RST pin can initiate an application reset, which restores configuration-register defaults, or a power-on reset, which resets internal circuitry. With RST held high, a rising CONVST/CS edge starts conversion; the device then returns to ACQ after conversion, with RVS indicating readiness.

Programming uses nine configuration registers and data-read or data-write frames. A frame begins on the falling edge of CONVST/CS, transfers data during SCLK activity, and ends on its rising edge, when the command processor decodes the input word. Optimal frames contain 32 clocks; short frames are valid only for limited reads, while long frames use the final 32 input bits as the command. Supported commands include byte and half-word reads and writes, as well as register bit set and clear operations. Output data can contain fixed test patterns, requested register data, or the latest 16-bit conversion result, with optional device-address, input-range, AVDD-alarm, input-alarm, and parity fields.

Writes use four selectable SPI-compatible protocols. Reads additionally support single- or dual-SDO operation and source-synchronous protocols using either an external SCLK or the internal device clock. Configuration registers control device identification, reset and power functions, input and output protocols, output data formatting, input ranges, alarm status, and alarm thresholds.

The ADS868xW is described as a fully differential, 16-bit SAR data-acquisition device with an integrated analog front end, ADC driver, and precision reference. A reference design combines an ADS8681W with an MUX36D08 to provide eight software-configurable channels for industrial voltage or current inputs. It settles to 1% accuracy in under 5 µs and includes programmable input alarms, AVDD alarms, and hysteresis for noise-resistant thermistor temperature monitoring.

Separate AVDD and DVDD supplies are used, with recommended close-coupled 1-µF and 10-µF decoupling. Programmable NAP and power-down modes reduce consumption at lower throughput. PCB guidance separates analog and digital routing, requires clean and bypassed supplies, and specifies reference-capacitor placement.

The Supreme Court said the CBI-led probe into the larger conspiracy behind Rajiv Gandhi’s assassination had made little headway and could become endless. It made the Centre a party to A.G. Perarivalan’s plea seeking suspension of his life sentence until the investigation concludes, set the case for hearing on January 24, and sought the Centre’s response. Perarivalan was convicted of supplying two nine-volt batteries allegedly used in the bomb that killed Gandhi and 14 others in the 1991 Sriperumbudur suicide bombing. He has served 26 years, and Tamil Nadu has decided to remit his remaining sentence.

OSCAR is presented as the first one-shot, multi-label causal discovery method for high-dimensional event sequences. It uses two Transformer-based autoregressive density estimators—one for next-event prediction and one for next-label prediction—to identify each outcome label’s Markov boundary from a single unknown sequence. Conditional mutual information tests the contribution of events given prior events, while causal indicators in \([-1,1]\) quantify how events increase or inhibit label likelihood.

The method models sequences as sequential Bayesian networks and assumes temporal precedence, bounded lagged effects, causal sufficiency, and accurate joint-distribution modeling. Its fully parallelized structure is independent of event and label cardinality and produces sequence-specific causal graphs within minutes.

OSCAR was evaluated on 300,000 vehicle sequences containing approximately 29,100 diagnostic trouble-code types, 474 error-pattern labels, and roughly \(150 \pm 90\) events per sequence. On a 50,000-sample comparison, it achieved 55.26% precision, 31.37% recall, and 40.02% F1 in 11.7 minutes. Competing local-structure methods did not finish within three days. The resulting interpretable causal graphs are intended to support causal reasoning and refinement of vehicle diagnostic rules.

Rep. Trey Gowdy of South Carolina, known for his distinctive haircut and self-deprecating humor, frequently jokes with Sen. Tim Scott. The Republicans co-wrote “Unified,” a book about their friendship and hope for unity in a divided country. Gowdy’s prominent role in the Benghazi investigation made him a GOP hero, though he later became disillusioned with partisan politics. On Jan. 31, 2018, he announced he would not seek reelection and hoped to return to law, a field he said seeks and rewards fairness. His later positions distanced him from strict party loyalty: he supported Robert Mueller’s Russia investigation, disputed findings that Russia sought to elect Trump, and rejected claims that Devin Nunes’s memo proved the investigation was a Democratic witch hunt. Gowdy co-wrote the memo, opposed efforts to fire Mueller, and warned President Trump that doing so would lead to a “very, very long bad 2018.”

The team remained positive after losing due to mistakes that gave the opponent two two-goal leads in the third period. It plans to learn from the errors, persevere, and stick to its game plan. Supportive fans and earlier momentum were positives, but with the opponent at two wins and the team needing four, the next game is crucial.

Large sparse systems may be too costly for direct elimination because their order can reach a million, while sparse matrix-vector multiplication is fast. This motivates iterative methods, which obtain approximate solutions and rely on preconditioners to accelerate convergence. Conjugate gradient is recommended for symmetric positive definite systems; multigrid will be covered in following lectures.

Possible preconditioners include the diagonal matrix for Jacobi, the lower-triangular matrix for Gauss-Seidel, weighted variants leading to successive overrelaxation, and incomplete LU factorization, which approximates the original matrix while limiting fill-in. Triangular preconditioners allow updated solution components to be computed sequentially by back substitution.

For a stationary iteration, the error satisfies \(e_{k+1}=Me_k\), where \(M=P^{-1}A\) is the iteration matrix. Convergence requires every eigenvalue of \(M\) to have magnitude below one. The convergence rate is governed by the spectral radius, \(\rho(M)\), the largest eigenvalue magnitude; error typically decreases approximately as \(\rho(M)^k\).

For a one-dimensional model with diagonal entries 2 and adjacent entries −1, the eigenvalues of \(A\) are \(2-2\cos\theta_j\), where \(\theta_j=j\pi/(n+1)\). With Jacobi preconditioning \(P=2I\), the iteration eigenvalues are \(\cos\theta_j\), and the spectral radius is \(\cos(\pi/(n+1))\), close to one for large \(n\). Jacobi therefore eliminates high-frequency errors quickly but converges slowly on smooth, low-frequency modes, requiring roughly \(n^2\) iterations despite inexpensive steps.

Weighted Jacobi changes the iteration eigenvalues to \(1-\omega+\omega\cos\theta\). Choosing \(\omega=2/3\), for example, moves high-frequency eigenvalues toward \(-1/3\), but low-frequency modes remain close to one, so weighting alone does not resolve the slow-convergence problem.

Gauss-Seidel immediately uses newly computed components, reducing storage requirements. Its eigenvalues are the squares of the corresponding Jacobi eigenvalues, making it roughly equivalent to two Jacobi steps. This improves convergence from a spectral radius near \(1-O(n^{-2})\) to one near \(1-O(n^{-1})\), but it remains too slow for very large problems.

Convergence may be monitored using either the solution error or the residual \(r_k=b-Ax_k\). The residual can become small faster than the solution error because recovering the error requires multiplication by \(A^{-1}\), which may be large. Multigrid is introduced as a way to address the slowly decaying low-frequency modes that limit these simpler methods.

After his team’s four-game Stanley Cup Finals sweep by Detroit, the speaker congratulates the winner and says he wanted to witness the Cup presentation. Disappointed but proud, he acknowledges that Detroit played well in many areas and was more experienced and hardened. New Jersey started strongly but lost momentum after two early goals, and the speaker cannot explain how the series slipped away so quickly.

He praises Detroit’s depth, goaltending, experienced defense, four solid forward lines, and Stevie’s consistent two-way play and leadership, saying Stevie deserved playoff MVP honors. He also commends Olaf Kolzig’s outstanding performance and the team’s professional response to a teammate’s accident.

Despite the loss, he rejects suggestions that the team should be embarrassed, noting other clubs would have considered a Finals sweep a major accomplishment. He credits the organization’s rebuilding work, including establishing a new attitude, and says the players gained valuable lessons in handling pressure, sacrifice, frustration, and adversity. He believes the experience will help the team rebound and contend for the Cup again.

A Trump administration amendment allows U.S. businesses to deny employees insurance coverage for contraception on religious or moral grounds, weakening an Obamacare mandate. Its impact remains disputed.

Apple Inc. filed a Form 8-K dated January 28, 2020, announcing a press release about its financial results for the first fiscal quarter ended December 28, 2019. The press release was attached as Exhibit 99.1, and the information was designated as furnished, not filed. The report was signed by Senior Vice President and Chief Financial Officer Luca Maestri.

This qualitative phenomenological study examined 45 pre-service teachers taking a special education course through distance education at a private university during the 2022–2023 academic year. Data were collected through researcher-developed, expert-reviewed and pilot-tested semi-structured interviews. The study sought to identify teacher candidates’ views of the course, problems encountered, and possible solutions.

Participants generally reported satisfaction with the distance education course, while also considering it less effective than face-to-face instruction because of internet and technical problems, distractions, and difficulty obtaining immediate answers. They emphasized the importance of participation for course success, although opinions differed on whether attendance should be compulsory. Concerns were raised about students lacking suitable devices, stable internet, or economic access to connectivity. Most participants recommended distance education because of its perceived effectiveness, flexibility, recorded lessons, home-learning comfort, individualized learning, technological familiarity, and lower cost. Some limited their recommendation to compulsory circumstances and stated that practical courses were less suitable.

The most common recommendation for improving the system was to develop distance-education platforms. Participants also recommended improving internet infrastructure and technical support, providing free internet access, and supplying digital materials. The study concluded that addressing these deficiencies could improve the quality of distance education and suggested further quantitative research with larger samples and other courses.

The author counters urgent bearish market warnings, arguing that bearish theses are inherently more compelling while historically successful strategies are patient and “boring.” Using Ray Dalio’s bubble-diagnosis framework, the article promotes Envision Research’s services and portfolio features. It discloses the author’s AGP positions, compensation, personal views, and standard performance and regulatory disclaimers, alongside two October 2025 charts.

- Sierra Pacific Resources suspended its quarterly dividend amid the Western U.S. energy crisis, saving less than $20 million while continuing administrative cost cuts. The utility holding company still hoped to complete its $2 billion purchase of Enron’s Portland General Electric, including assumption of $1 billion in debt, but California legislation was blocking asset sales needed to finance the deal. Sierra Pacific reported an $889 million fuel and electricity expense in 2000 and a $39.8 million loss.

- Britain’s Crown Estates awarded leases for 13 offshore wind projects—seven in the Irish Sea and six in the North Sea—potentially attracting £1.6 billion and adding 1,500 megawatts of capacity by 2004. Awardees included Enron, Innogy, Powergen, Scottish Power and TXU Europe. Falling onshore generation costs and government renewable-energy requirements and tradable certificates were strengthening the industry’s prospects.

- Internet rumors were forcing companies to disclose layoff plans sooner and with greater care. Future Network printed internal layoff letters to avoid their spread online, while Razorfish said rumors did not affect how involuntary terminations were carried out. The SEC has no specific rule requiring disclosure of job cuts, making disclosure largely a business decision, although Regulation FD limits selective disclosure. Enron’s denial of rumored broadband layoffs helped its stock rebound.

- High energy prices and tighter environmental restrictions were attracting major companies into renewable energy. Nine solar-thermal units near Barstow supplied daytime power for 350,000 homes, while companies including Sharp, BP, Shell and Enron expanded renewable operations. Renewables supplied 12% of California’s electricity; the state aimed to add 5,000 megawatts by July, including 16% renewable capacity, and offered plant subsidies and household rebates. Solar-cell production costs had fallen tenfold over 20 years, but financing, infrastructure and installation constraints remained.

- Technology stocks rallied 14% in their best week in 10 months, moving the Nasdaq above 1,961, while the Dow passed 10,000 and the S&P 500 gained nearly 5%. The rise occurred despite weak economic data, Motorola’s first loss in 16 years and a Juniper Networks warning. Investors awaited first-quarter results and forecasts from major technology, financial, airline and energy companies as they assessed whether the downturn was ending or extending the bear market.

- Enron Chairman Kenneth Lay said the administration had gone too far in backing away from action against global warming and had already communicated that criticism to officials.

- President Bush was expected to nominate retired Brigadier General and Enron executive Thomas E. White Jr. to lead the Army. White was viewed as likely to favor outsourcing services such as electricity delivery; Enron had received a $25 million contract to provide power and water at New York’s Fort Hamilton in 1999.

- A Maharashtra committee concluded that even with improved performance, Phase II of Enron’s Dabhol project would keep the Maharashtra State Electricity Board financially distressed. It recommended deferring power-purchase agreements until the board could absorb the output. The panel also said the Bhadrawati and Reliance projects could force MSEB to buy nearly 90% of their production or face higher tariffs.

- Trade unions prepared an April 25 Maharashtra bandh against globalization, free-market policies, unemployment, WTO effects on farmers and Enron’s Dabhol tariffs. State transport and BEST unions were expected to join, with efforts to block Mumbai suburban trains. Left-wing leaders welcomed possible Shiv Sena support but rejected sharing its platform.

- An opinion column argued that India’s democratic right to remove governments had not eliminated rulers’ claimed immunity from blame. It cited the Ketan Parekh and Enron matters as examples of responsibility being shifted from government officials to individuals and companies.

- DivX compression software, combined with DeCSS, was enabling illegal copying and trading of movies and posing an Internet piracy threat similar to MP3. DivXNetworks sought to make its format the industry standard but had no major studio agreements and faced security and intellectual-property challenges from Microsoft and RealNetworks. Blockbuster-Enron talks over broadband movie delivery had broken down, while slow Internet connections and concern about theater and rental revenue delayed online catalogs. The MPAA planned 20,000 anti-piracy letters in 2001, ten times its 2000 total.

- Enron restarted its 15,000-barrel-per-day MTBE plant in Morgan’s Point, Texas, after scheduled maintenance. It was Enron’s only MTBE plant; the company also operated a 400,000-barrel-per-day methanol plant in La Porte.

- A separate Maharashtra panel recommended renegotiating Enron’s Dabhol supply contract, lowering its tariff, removing dollar-linked increases and deferring DPC payment obligations for at least five years, preferably 15. The recommendations followed a dispute over MSEB’s unpaid December bill of 1.02 billion rupees and a political force-majeure notice to the utility.

NVIDIA’s Turing GPU architecture introduces native HDR display processing with BT.2100 tone mapping, an enhanced NVENC encoder supporting H.265 8K encoding at 30 fps, and an NVDEC decoder supporting HEVC 4:4:4 and 10/12-bit VP9 HDR. Turing also adds USB-C and VirtualLink support, allowing a VR headset’s power, display, and data connections to use one connector. TU102 and TU104 replace MIO and PCIe SLI links with second-generation NVLink, providing higher bandwidth but supporting only two-way SLI.

Dedicated RT Cores accelerate BVH traversal and ray-triangle intersection testing, making single-GPU real-time ray tracing practical and reportedly about 10 times faster than software-based ray tracing on Pascal. Turing combines these cores with rasterization, denoising, and hybrid rendering to produce effects such as physically accurate reflections, refractions, shadows, and ambient occlusion.

NVIDIA NGX uses deep neural networks and Turing Tensor Cores for AI-enhanced graphics. Its features include DLSS image reconstruction, which produces quality comparable to temporal antialiasing with roughly half the shading work; DLSS 2X; AI-based inpainting; AI Slow-Mo; and AI Super Rez for 2x, 4x, or 8x upscaling.

Turing also adds mesh shading, Variable Rate Shading, Texture Space Shading, and Multi-View Rendering. Mesh shading uses task and mesh shaders to reduce CPU draw-call bottlenecks and render very large numbers of objects. VRS controls shading independently at 16×16-pixel granularity, supporting content-adaptive, motion-adaptive, and foveated rendering. TSS stores shading results in texture space for reuse across frames, viewpoints, and resolutions. MVR supports up to four hardware views per pass and up to 32 API-level views, expanding Pascal’s simultaneous multi-projection capabilities.

The TU104 contains 48 streaming multiprocessors, 3,072 CUDA Cores, 368 Tensor Cores, and 48 RT Cores, with one x8 NVLink link. TU106 contains 36 multiprocessors, 2,304 CUDA Cores, 288 Tensor Cores, and 36 RT Cores but lacks NVLink and SLI. The inference-focused Tesla T4 uses a reduced TU104 configuration with 40 multiprocessors, 2,560 CUDA Cores, 320 Tensor Cores, and 320 GB/s memory bandwidth.

NVIDIA also introduces RTX-OPS, a workload-based performance metric that weights tensor, FP32, RT, and INT32 operations according to their expected use within a hybrid-rendering frame.

A Reversal Day is a substantial upward or downward change in a stock or market index’s direction after an extended trend, sometimes accompanied by high trading volume. A Bullish Reversal Day follows a downtrend, may first establish a lower low, and closes above the previous day’s high. A Bearish Reversal Day follows a prolonged rally, may first establish a higher high, and closes below the previous day’s low.

Potential causes include changes in market sentiment, economic conditions and indicators, company-specific news, and technical patterns. Reversal Days may be identified through chart trends, heavy volume, moving averages, RSI, Bollinger Bands, support and resistance breaks, and divergences between price and RSI or MACD. They can occur in stocks, currencies, commodities, and bonds, each influenced by different market conditions.

The article backtests two strategies in gold (GLD) using Amibroker, with holding periods of 1–25 trading days. The bullish strategy generally showed favorable profit factors, although it generated relatively few trades; its highest average gain was 2.02% with a 24-day exit. The bearish strategy produced losses, partly attributed to gold’s upward overnight-session drift, and had significantly lower average gains. Overall, the backtests suggest the Reversal Day concept has merit.

Cocoa futures are standardized, exchange-traded contracts to buy or sell 10 metric tons of cocoa at a pre-agreed price on a future date. Cocoa, once used as currency in Central and South America, is now a major soft commodity used in chocolate and other beverages. Contracts trade on ICE Futures US under the symbol CC and on CME Globex/NYMEX under CJ. ICE contracts are settled by physical delivery, with the exchange supervising delivery and quality, while CME contracts are financially settled. Contracts expire in March, May, July, September, and December. ICE trading terminates on the day before the last notice day, which falls 10 business days before the delivery month’s final business day.

Prices are quoted in U.S. dollars and cents per metric ton. The minimum fluctuation is $1 per metric ton, or $10 per contract. On November 25, 2022, cocoa traded at $2,484 per metric ton, making one 10-metric-ton contract worth $24,840. Trading Economics reports an all-time high of $5,379 in July 1977. TradingView data shows a low of $707 in December 2000 and a high of $3,775 in March 2011 since its series began in December 1979.

A cocoa futures strategy can combine fundamental and technical analysis for market timing with position sizing, risk management, and defined entry and exit signals. In the cited backtest, the strategy recovered after 30 trades and completed 96 trades with a 2.3 profit factor and a 74% win rate. Cocoa futures generally perform better in summer and weaker in spring and fall. Prices are driven by factors affecting supply and demand.

Traders can access contracts through futures brokers, or trade cocoa CFDs through CFD brokers. Contracts are leveraged and may involve delivery, whereas CFDs are agreements with the broker to exchange the opening and closing price difference. Trading risks include leveraged losses from adverse price movements and lower liquidity, which can make exits difficult and widen spreads. Potential purposes include hedging, portfolio diversification, speculation, and arbitrage.

Charts are available through trading platforms, MultiCharts, TradingView, Yahoo Finance, and YCharts. The iPath Bloomberg Cocoa Subindex Total Return ETN (NIB) offers exposure by tracking an index of cocoa futures with three expiration dates.

Health savings accounts (HSAs), long favored by Republicans as a possible replacement for parts of the Affordable Care Act, encourage people to spend less on health care by requiring them to use their own money. HSA contributions can be invested, grow tax-free, and be withdrawn tax-free for qualified medical expenses, including deductibles and copays. They are generally available only with high-deductible insurance plans.

Participation remains low: about 20 million of 176 million insured people participated in 2015. Barriers include limited disposable income, difficulty saving for the future, immediate spending pressures, and stress associated with financial decisions. Behavioral economist Mitesh Patel suggests automatic enrollment, modeled on 401(k) plans, could reduce friction, though it would cost the government money.

People with HSAs use less health care, but it is unclear whether their health improves. In one EBRI study, prescription drug spending fell while emergency room visits increased, particularly among lower-income families. Individuals also struggle to estimate future medical costs because prices vary widely. Experts say HSAs are most useful for people who can cover current expenses and maintain emergency savings while setting aside money for future care.

MLPs outperformed the S&P 500 in 2016, with the AMZE total return rising 22.5% and the MLP Index gaining 18.3%. December’s 4.4% return extended positive streaks, while smaller MLPs’ rally and Enterprise Products Partners’ unusual weakness contributed to performance disparities. SunCoke Energy Partners led 2016, while Ferrellgas lagged; general partners and midstream corporations underperformed.

EPD’s large index weight and strong liquidity supported its results despite underperformance, raising questions about improving capital access. In capital-market activity, Plains GP Holdings filed to sell up to $500 million of common units, while Shell Midstream Partners announced Gulf of Mexico pipeline acquisitions at a 7.7x EBITDA multiple.

This descriptive cross-sectional study examined burnout, perceived causes, the work environment, associated factors, and coping strategies among Ghana Prison Service officers at Nsawam Medium Security Prison. Of 266 recruited officers, 245 returned questionnaires and 243 were analyzed, giving a 92% participation rate. Data were collected using the Maslach Burnout Inventory–Human Services Survey, Work Environment Scale, and Coping Methods Checklist and analyzed using descriptive statistics, chi-square/Fisher’s exact tests, and logistic regression.

Most respondents were male (68.31%), junior-ranked (78.19%), single (57.61%), and had less than five years of service (60.90%). Burnout prevalence was 9%. Forty-two percent had high emotional exhaustion; 35.4%, 32.1%, and 32.5% had low, moderate, and high depersonalization, respectively; and 68.7% had low personal accomplishment. Perceived causes included irregular shifts (71.6%), heavy workload (49.0%), and inadequate training and development opportunities (47.7%). Many officers valued their colleagues, workplace, and control over their work, but reported limited recognition, feedback, supervisory support, and rewards relative to penalties.

Shift allocation was significantly associated with emotional exhaustion, rank with depersonalization, and sex with burnout. Males had lower adjusted odds of burnout than females, while diploma/certificate holders had lower odds than postgraduate degree holders. Common coping strategies were talking with colleagues (62.5%), looking forward to time off (60.1%), talking with family (54.3%), keeping thoughts and feelings to oneself (42.1%), and alcohol use (29.2%). The authors recommended addressing irregular shifts, heavy workloads, training and development opportunities, and self-care to reduce burnout and its potential consequences.

The article examines the S&P 500 Information Technology sector, which has the index’s largest weighting at over 25% of market capitalization and includes companies developing or distributing software, technology services, semiconductors, and hardware. VGT and XLK are major tracking ETFs, while Apple, Microsoft, NVIDIA, Broadcom, and Adobe are identified as the top five stocks, though leadership changes frequently.

Two mean-reversion-based XLK strategies are backtested. The first recorded 245 trades, a 0.96% average gain, 10% CAGR versus 8% for buy-and-hold, 12% market exposure, 18% maximum drawdown, 71% win rate, and 3.1 profit factor. The second recorded 212 trades, a 1.05% average gain, 9.5% CAGR, 10% market exposure, 15% maximum drawdown, 70% win rate, and 2.85 profit factor. Technology strategies may correlate strongly with the broader market and offer little diversification.

Morgan Tsvangirai’s role in Zimbabwe’s opposition is debated: after his 2013 defeat and party split, he is portrayed as a liability. His cancer limits his MDC-T and MDC Alliance duties, prompting calls for leadership renewal and retirement so a fit successor can lead, while ZANU-PF’s reforms may advantage the opposition.

The SD Card Association releases a non-confidential, “AS-IS” subset of the SD specification, without warranties or responsibility for resulting damages or patent infringements. It grants no implied licenses and need not disclose technical information or know-how.

The passage criticizes Stanford’s mandatory Program in Writing and Rhetoric (PWR), arguing that its broad, vaguely framed courses, limited source analysis, lenient grading, and political bent prevent it from developing students’ academic writing skills. It compares PWR with Stanford’s placement options in foreign languages, mathematics, and science, recommending advanced placement for students already proficient in writing so PWR can serve less experienced students. The authors also argue that a proposed PWR minor is unnecessary because the program provides foundational skills rather than a specialized field.

Instead, they propose creating a rigorous, standardized, source-based course focused on analyzing texts within a defined area. Experienced humanities professors could design it for teaching by junior faculty, combining serious academic-writing instruction with less ideological course development. The passage concludes that PWR’s existing structure and outcomes undermine its purpose and require substantial reform.

Montecito Fire Protection District crews will teach 800 local elementary students fire safety and emergency preparedness during Fire Prevention Week. Activities include “Stop Drop and Roll,” “Crawl Low in Smoke,” a simulated home-fire trailer, hazard recognition, 9-1-1 instructions, and safe home exits. Oct. 3–6 activities were canceled due to weather and will be rescheduled.

The prototype M8 shown lacks full-LED and laser headlights, carbon-ceramic brakes, and premium wheels, and BMW M has revealed no specifications. The supercar-fighter is expected to use the 7 Series' CLAR platform, the 8 Series concept's body from the 2017 Villa d'Este show, and a 4.4-liter twin-turbo V8 debuting in the F90 M5 with 600+ hp and all-wheel drive. Despite the 6 Series GT, rumors persist that the 6er badge goes to a 911 rival. The original M8 never reached production; its V12 later powered the McLaren F1.

Ottawa police are seeking three suspects in an alleged roadside robbery in the east end. A woman allegedly used a false breakdown to lure a driver to her car, where she and two accomplices attacked him and stole cash. The victim was hospitalized; police released descriptions and appealed for information.

At the Code Conference, Aileen Lee, Megan Smith and Sukhinder Singh Cassidy discussed diversity and inclusion in tech. Lee criticized the “good guy” framing that can favor men and urged companies to identify and remove bias from industry and business processes. The panel addressed board-level diversity and resistance to one-on-one meetings between men and women. Smith said women of color are the most left out.

StockX added BAPE and PALACE to its streetwear marketplace, offering over 4,000 authenticated BAPE products dating to 2010 and more than 3,000 PALACE products. The expansion builds on StockX’s Supreme and Kith offerings and aims to make it the largest authenticated marketplace for both brands. Founded by Josh Luber, Greg Schwartz and Dan Gilbert, StockX launched in 2016 as an anonymous, transparent marketplace for sneakers, watches, handbags and streetwear, with all products inspected and authenticated.

Vertigo has become the first iOS app to integrate both Apple Music and Spotify Premium, letting users import playlists, search catalogues, and share tracks for friends to hear using their own subscriptions. It also offers ad-free listening and live music sessions with video, photos, real-time chat, and audio commentary. Only paying subscribers can participate, and royalties are paid for each shared song. As Apple Music and Spotify compete, Vertigo may help Apple Music address its limited social features.

Glen Campbell’s family says the country legend, in the final stages of Alzheimer’s disease, finds comfort in music and sometimes smiles or sings along. His final work, “Adios,” recorded in 2012 and released June 9, preserves his voice and love of music despite his illness.

The study developed a streamlined, laboratory-ready workflow for analyzing and reporting optical genome mapping (OGM) data in myeloid neoplasms using Variant Intelligence Applications (VIA), extending an International Consortium framework. Ten retrospective cases—nine acute myeloid leukemias and one myelodysplastic neoplasm—were reviewed independently five to six times by blinded technologist-director teams. Technologists used customized filters, panels, and tracks to assess copy-number, structural, and allelic variants; directors finalized classifications, selected reportable findings, and generated reports.

OGM detected all variants identified by standard-of-care testing, although one trisomy 21 was not selected for reporting in one review. The four standard-of-care-negative cases were also negative by OGM. Among six positive AML cases, five standard-of-care sentinel variants were unanimously classified as Tier 1A. Classification was less consistent for other variants. OGM identified additional findings in five of six positive cases, including large copy-number losses, trisomy 8, interstitial deletions involving IKZF1, a KMT2A::MLLT10 fusion, an unbalanced translocation, and chromosomal gains.

Mean technologist review time was 25.2 minutes for negative cases, 28.5 minutes for simple cases, and 47.3 minutes for two complex cases. Most non-complex cases required approximately 20–45 minutes, and VIA often reduced analysis time by about 50% compared with prior Bionano Access-only estimates. The authors concluded that OGM combined with VIA provides an efficient, objective method for comprehensive cytogenomic analysis and reporting, while potentially standardizing variant interpretation and reducing laboratory workload.

In October 2022, a Business Insider reporter used a seven-day Eurail pass to travel through Germany, Austria, Italy, and Switzerland, taking eight train rides between six cities. The pass cost $477, while fees for two overnight trains and three class upgrades brought the total to $560. Compared with flying, the reporter found trains more comfortable, convenient, scenic, and sustainable. Rail travel offered first- and business-class seating, shared-cabin overnight sleepers, easy boarding without airport check-in, large windows, and less exposure to dehydration and lingering ear-popping. A quoted 2025 flight itinerary would have cost about $440 in economy, while comparable plane cabins were unaffordable. The reporter noted that rail travel can reduce a trip’s carbon footprint and concluded they would choose trains whenever traveling in Europe.

Brazilian stocks gained Thursday, led by a rally in Vale after record quarterly iron ore production. Vale’s shares rose as much as 4.9%, while Usinas Siderúrgicas de Minas Gerais advanced after reversing a quarterly loss. The real was volatile amid geopolitical and election concerns, partly eased by polls favoring Emmanuel Macron.

The Rio Blanco 4-H senior livestock judging team—Macy Collins, Jilly Bumguardner, Marryn Shults and Tatumn Kennedy—competed at the 73rd annual Colorado 4-H June Conference at Colorado State University. Collins placed third in oral reasons with 281 points, while Shults finished seventh overall with 572 points. Collins made the Colorado State 4-H Livestock All State team and will attend Hutchinson Junior College on a full academic and judging scholarship. Bumguardner and Kennedy gained valuable experience. Collins also belonged to Rio Blanco’s 2015 state champion team and judged contests in five additional states before ending her 4-H career.

President Donald Trump warned Iran not to restart its nuclear program as he and French President Emmanuel Macron sought common ground on preserving the 2015 nuclear agreement. Trump called the accord inadequate because it did not address ballistic missiles or Iran’s involvement in Yemen and Syria, while Macron urged the U.S. to remain in it as the best chance to constrain Iran and prevent regional nuclear proliferation. Iran said it would expand its nuclear program if the deal collapsed and might quit the nuclear-nonproliferation treaty. Their discussions also covered European steel-tariff exemptions, the Paris climate agreement and retaining U.S. troops in Syria to defeat Islamic State. U.S. withdrawal could raise regional tensions, prompt an arms race involving Saudi Arabia and complicate efforts to make North Korea give up nuclear weapons. Trump thanked France for joining U.S.-British airstrikes in Syria.

The football holder receives the snap and places the ball for the kicker on extra points and field goals, requiring soft hands, quick and steady placement, and the ability to angle and rotate the ball with the laces away. Holders must handle bad snaps, maintain the kicker’s rhythm, and may throw, flip the ball, or run on fake field goals. Punters, backup quarterbacks, and receivers often fill the role, and any body type can play. Though typically overlooked and secondary to other duties, precise holding can determine whether a scoring opportunity is converted. The NFL does not track holder statistics.

The Daily Examiner is shifting from a metered digital model to premium subscriber-only content, while keeping vital public-safety information and some local stories free. Existing subscribers retain unlimited website and app access, News Corp publications, newsletters and breaking-news alerts, with print and digital-only options available. Sign-up is via dailyexaminer.com.au/subscriptions or 1300 361 604.

Thailand recorded 390 road deaths during Songkran week, an 11% decrease from the previous year, following junta anti-drink-driving enforcement that included harsher penalties, vehicle seizures and visits to victims’ mortuaries. It was the first reduction achieved by such campaigns. Despite the decline, 28% of Songkran accidents involved drunk driving, while speeding, helmet non-use and traffic-police corruption were also cited as factors.

The EU is urging multilateral development banks, including the World Bank, to align financing more closely with the Paris Agreement, shift lending from fossil fuels to low-carbon projects, improve transparency, provide local-currency financing, and attract private investment in climate resilience and sustainability. Led by Germany and France, the proposal will be promoted at upcoming World Bank and IMF meetings. It faces strong U.S. opposition, which argues climate targets could overshadow poverty reduction and economic growth. Development banks invested a record $137 billion in climate projects in 2024, but the EU considers this insufficient. Adoption could reshape international development finance, although consensus is uncertain.

Canada’s Supreme Court unanimously upheld a ruling requiring destruction of confidential residential-school compensation assessment records after 15 years. Negotiators intended the process to be private, and claimants and alleged perpetrators relied on confidentiality assurances when submitting sensitive abuse accounts.

Eric Thames hit a two-run homer in the fifth inning as the Milwaukee Brewers defeated the Minnesota Twins 2-0. Nate Orf pinch-hit, walked and stole second before Thames homered off Jake Odorizzi, who allowed two runs and four hits in five innings. Junior Guerra pitched five shutout innings for Milwaukee, striking out eight and escaping a bases-loaded jam. Josh Hader pitched three hitless relief innings, and Corey Knebel struck out the side for his ninth save in 11 attempts. Minnesota had two hits and fell to 1-7 on its nine-game road trip. First baseman Joe Mauer recorded no putouts or assists, a first for the Twins since 2012. Manager Molitor argued a ninth-inning strike call against umpire Marty Foster, who said he had delayed his signal while choking on mints. Christian Yelich sat for a fifth consecutive game with back tightness, while Lorenzo Cain and Zach Davies remained sidelined by injuries.

A forwarded December 2000 McKinsey memorandum provides a periodic update on international electric-power privatization and restructuring from June through November 2000. It reports that governments were opening generation and electricity markets to foreign investment because of rising power demand and limited public funding. State-owned utilities were increasingly unbundling, while wholesale and retail competition was expanding. Some international power companies were reducing overseas exposure in favor of less risky markets such as the United States and Europe.

In Western Europe, the EU Directive was accelerating liberalization, market consolidation and cross-border opportunities. Austria lacked an independent system operator and full generation-transmission-distribution separation; Denmark and Finland had extensive customer choice and participated in NordPool; France accelerated plans to open 34% of its market by the end of 2000; and Germany continued to face grid-access barriers and fees despite major utility mergers. Greece planned to separate and partially privatize PPC, Ireland phased in supply competition, and Italy required ENEL to reduce its generation share and sell substantial assets. The Netherlands expanded its power exchange and centralized its high-voltage network, Portugal continued utility privatization, Spain’s proposed Endesa-Iberdrola merger required asset divestitures, Sweden and the UK had fully opened their markets, and Switzerland adopted a phased liberalization schedule. Mergers, alliances and new wholesale trading operations were prominent throughout the region.

Central and Eastern European countries continued pursuing privatization, often in preparation for EU accession and with IMF pressure for reform. Bulgaria planned to separate state utility NEK; the Czech Republic announced sales of stakes in CEZ and regional distributors; Hungary had sold major holdings but faced price-control and contract disputes; Romania had divided its national utility and was gradually opening its market; and Russia, Slovakia, Turkey and Ukraine were pursuing varying degrees of restructuring, ownership reform and asset sales. Moldova also planned majority sales of distribution and generation companies.

Asian economies were resuming restructuring as they recovered from the financial crisis, although power-purchase agreements, government guarantees and weak state utilities remained obstacles. Australia was phasing in full customer choice, China was testing interconnection and reducing planned independent projects, India was debating major regulatory and sector reforms, and Indonesia was renegotiating costly IPP contracts while beginning to unbundle PLN. Japan opened large customers to supplier choice, Malaysia was separating its state utility, New Zealand was implementing ownership separation, and South Korea was breaking KEPCO into generation companies. Pakistan continued attracting IPPs despite payment and political problems, the Philippines was considering restructuring and privatizing Napocor, Singapore was reviewing its market structure, and Thailand, Taiwan and Vietnam were at varying stages of liberalization.

In Latin America, privatization of electricity distribution and generation had been completed in all major economies except Venezuela and Mexico, although ownership limits, currency instability, transmission investment needs and severe droughts continued to affect the region. Argentina was privatizing transmission assets, Brazil had launched a wholesale market but faced hydro-related shortage risks, Chile was proposing reforms to transmission pricing and distribution competition, and Colombia had postponed broader privatizations amid strikes and attacks on transmission facilities. Mexico planned renewed market-opening legislation without privatization, while Peru, Nicaragua, Panama, Ecuador, Venezuela and other countries pursued selective privatizations, concessions or regulatory reforms.

Across Africa and the Middle East, governments were increasingly opening power sectors to foreign investment, though most arrangements remained IPP-based. Côte d’Ivoire, Gabon, Guinea, Mali and Senegal had privatized their power systems. Algeria and Egypt planned unbundling and sales of state utility interests, Nigeria announced plans to restructure and privatize NEPA, and South Africa was considering merging distributors, grouping generation companies and potentially selling some Eskom plants. Jordan, Kuwait, Lebanon, Morocco, Qatar, Saudi Arabia, Tunisia and the United Arab Emirates also introduced or considered private-sector participation, concessions and independent power projects. Regional transmission initiatives were planned or underway in Southern Africa, West Africa, the Middle East and the Gulf.

The report included eight attached exhibits with restructuring maps, market-opening timelines and other regional analyses, and invited readers to provide local updates and additional exhibit suggestions.

Each Inauguration Day has renewed American dedication to the nation: Washington sought to create a nation, Lincoln to preserve it from internal disruption, and the present generation to defend it and its institutions from external threats. The speaker calls for reflection on America’s historical place and future, warning that isolation and inaction are serious dangers.

Despite claims that democracy was fading, the nation’s action during recent crises demonstrated its capacity to survive, reform, and grow. Its constitutional branches continue to function, the Bill of Rights remains intact, and elections remain free. Democracy endures because it unites individuals through free expression and a free majority, mobilizes enlightened human will, and supports unlimited progress.

A nation requires a sound body and informed mind as well as a spirit. America’s spirit—its faith in freedom—has developed across centuries and is reflected in the Mayflower Compact, Declaration of Independence, Constitution, and Gettysburg Address. While the nation must expand security, opportunity, and knowledge and address poverty and concentrated wealth, these material and intellectual achievements alone are insufficient.

Preserving the “sacred fire of liberty” and protecting democracy amid grave dangers requires mustering the nation’s spirit and faith. The speaker pledges not to retreat or remain idle but to move forward in service to the country, by the will of God.

Prosecutors told a jury that former CIA case officer Kevin Mallory betrayed the United States by giving a Chinese agent information on human assets and other top-secret material for $25,000. Defense attorneys said Mallory was loyal and was feeding the Chinese recruiter false documents to expose an intelligence operation. A CIA analyst and contractor testified that Mallory contacted them in February 2017, before his Shanghai trip, because he was suspicious of a think-tank job offer. Customs agents found $16,500 in undeclared cash when Mallory returned through O’Hare in April 2017. During questioning, agents saw texts on a Chinese-supplied Samsung phone, and a home search found discs containing classified documents. The trial is in the Eastern District of Virginia, where espionage cases are rare; Mallory faces up to life in prison.

Olean’s Common Council unanimously authorized Mayor Bill Aiello to apply for a $10 million state Downtown Revitalization Initiative grant. The proposal covers an area from Olean General Hospital to the Allegheny River and from Franchot Park to about Seventh Street, with projects including redevelopment of the former Manufacturers Hanover building, business incubator funding, expanded downtown theater offerings, pedestrian improvements at Lincoln Park, and a Front Street park. The city may also receive more than $2 million through the Buffalo Billion initiative. JCC Cattaraugus County’s John Sayegh supported the application and offered to help upgrade the college’s Cutco Theater.

IDC’s December 2021 survey of 200 IT and departmental decision makers at manufacturers with more than 500 employees in Germany, Austria, and Switzerland examines IT-based simulation, modeling, data analytics, and high-performance computing (HPC). It finds that simulation is already used across manufacturing to test products and processes, improve quality, reduce defects and costs, accelerate development, and support innovation. Three-quarters of respondents rank innovation as a primary business objective, while 57% view simulation and analytics as important for improving product and service quality. Around half already apply them in product development, production planning, and quality management, with deployment expected to reach as high as 90% within two years.

Simulation, modeling, digital twins, IoT, and high-performance analytics can shorten development cycles, reduce physical prototypes and raw-material use, optimize processes, and enable new digital products and services. Their benefits depend on integrating otherwise isolated departmental data into a “single source of truth” across the product lifecycle and enabling collaboration with customers, partners, and industrial ecosystems.

HPC is viewed as a major enabler of complex, faster calculations and iterative analysis. Four in five decision makers consider it a game changer for product and process innovation, and demand for high-performance calculations is expected to rise sharply. More than a quarter of surveyed enterprises already use professional HPC infrastructure, 39% are piloting or planning deployment, and 42% report that some simulations are outdated or inaccurate. HPC enables more sophisticated modeling, faster results, additional iterations, and new industrial use cases, but also raises security, energy-consumption, cost, infrastructure-availability, and skills concerns.

Most enterprises favor external infrastructure, including cloud providers and colocation, over fully on-premises systems. Public cloud and hybrid-cloud HPC architectures are expected to gain importance because they provide scalability, flexible capacity, access to current hardware, and an alternative to costly CAPEX. HPC as a Service and cloud-based engineering workstations can further support collaboration and HPC-based business models, although they still require trained personnel. IDC recommends a holistic data strategy, careful selection among on-premises, HPCaaS, and hybrid operating models, consideration of scalability, security, and energy efficiency, and external expertise where internal capabilities are insufficient.

The AMD Geode CS5535 Revision A3 specification update documents silicon issues and workarounds involving clock gating, interrupts, DMA, ACPI, KEL, buses, and power management.

- Edge-configured PIC inputs that remain high prevent the PIC from returning to Idle after automatic Local bus clock gating, causing missed interrupts and possible system hangs. Automatic clock gating should remain disabled. GLIU clock gating can also prevent statistics-counter ASMIs from waking domain zero, and UART clock gating in CEIR mode can incorrectly stop the UART clock. USB clock gating can cause register-read failures on idle controllers; these gating features should be disabled when affected.
- ATAC and ACC use eight-byte GA prefetches. Unaligned PRD tables can cause the first four bytes of the next PRD to be prefetched, creating hazards when PRD entries change during memory-write operations. PRDs should be defined before starting DMA; on-the-fly ACC PRD changes should be at least two tables ahead.
- A UDMA write following a host-terminated UDMA read can use an incorrect CRC after device termination. Host terminations should be prevented using bit 8 of ATAC Error MSR 51300003h. ATAC SSMI during DMA also fails to block the conflicting IDE I/O, so the feature should not be used.
- Byte access to ACPI PM1_EN and PM1_STS can hang; use word or dword access, or BIOS/SMM trapping. WORD or BYTE writes to PMC registers can corrupt register data because shadow-register byte lanes are ignored; an SMI I/O trap can prevent incorrectly sized accesses.
- KEL emulation cannot distinguish writes to I/O ports 060h and 064h through CmdData, requiring Emulation Events and ASMI trap information instead. Snoop-mode writes incorrectly alter HCE state, so software must save and restore that state. Reading port 060h can incorrectly clear AuxOutputFull, making interrupt-based PS/2 emulation preferable.
- Back-to-back PCI memory reads can address the wrong location, but the behavior was found only in simulation and cannot be issued by the Geode GX processor in real systems. The standard 8259 PIC polling mode is unsupported.
- IRDY# and DEVSEL# provide only 1.5 ns rather than the specified 2 ns tVAL minimum; no failures are expected, though 10–50 pF capacitors can slow the edges if needed. Simultaneous IRQ and SSMI events can cause the I/O to complete before the SSMI is signaled, so the processor should generate desired SSMIs.
- IDE UDMA requires sending the PIO command packet before enabling the bus master; reversing the order causes failure. Enabling the bus master before an ATAPI packet can also reset the master engine when a device signals an interrupt, though this was limited to one CD-ROM firmware revision that was later corrected.
- In ACPI S3, GPIO[27:24] wake transitions are not recognized; PWRBTN# should be used, with external circuitry for multiple wake sources. RTC CMOS RAM can return incorrect data for an extended-port write followed by an immediate legacy-port read. Block and demand legacy DMA to LPC can block I/O and return invalid data; single-transfer mode should be used.
- ATAC PRDs must be DWORD-aligned to avoid hangs. LPC transactions may abort with bridges that delay valid SYNC patterns; a PLD workaround is described. SMB NEGACK status may be delayed, requiring two SMB_STS writes to clear and mask it. GLPCI’s retry counter includes unrelated bus retries and can stop early; it can be disabled by setting the limit to zero.
- Atomic GPIO High Bank Feature Bit Register writes after suspend clear nonselected bits; use read-modify-write. SMBus hold time is shorter than the 300 ns requirement. LOWBAT_FLAG may not record a low-battery condition, and premature sleep-delay counter resets can leave SLEEP_X and SLEEP_Y asserted while PCI/IDE inputs remain disabled. Sleep-delay counters should be programmed below the PM_SED delay value.

Uber’s panic button, launched nationwide after alleged sexual assaults, lets riders call 911 from the home screen. Pilot cities automatically send real-time locations and vehicle details to dispatchers; elsewhere, riders can relay their location.

The speaker expressed disappointment after losing to the Detroit Red Wings. Detroit scored twice early, while his team generated few chances and little from the power play. Though play was fairly even after the first ten minutes, he said the team needs to improve and score more.

In spring 1953, the United States urges the new Soviet leadership, following Stalin’s death, to choose a path toward a just and lasting peace rather than continuing eight years of fear, force, and division. The passage contrasts the free nations’ principles—cooperation, national self-determination, rejection of imposed governments, and reliance on just relations rather than armaments—with the Soviet vision of security through power and domination. Soviet expansion and aggression have prompted Western unity, heavy military spending, and fear of atomic war, while diverting resources from human needs.

The United States calls for concrete Soviet actions, beginning with an honorable Korean armistice, free elections in a united Korea, and an end to attacks on Indochina and Malaya. It also urges Soviet support for an Austrian treaty, freedom for Eastern European nations, European unity, and a free and united Germany. The passage proposes broad disarmament measures, including limits on armed forces and strategic production, peaceful control of atomic energy, restrictions on destructive weapons, and United Nations inspection.

Domestically and abroad, the United States pledges to pursue Austrian independence, closer cooperation among free European nations, effective collective defense through NATO and the European Defense Community, and international aid financed partly through disarmament savings. It argues that trust and cooperation could redirect resources from weapons toward schools, hospitals, housing, food, and economic development. Ultimately, it insists that Soviet intentions be judged by deeds rather than rhetoric and remains ready to cooperate with any government sincerely pursuing a comprehensive peace.

The study examines how digital customer experience through e-commerce and electronic word of mouth influence sustainable supply chain performance in Indonesian ICT companies, with brand image and supply chain image as mediators. It proposes seven hypotheses based on literature linking e-commerce, branding, supply chains, and customer satisfaction. Data were collected from employees involved in product distribution: 568 questionnaires were distributed across randomly selected Indonesian regions and ICT companies, yielding 315 valid responses. Partial least squares structural equation modelling was used. The measurement model demonstrated reliability, convergent validity, and discriminant validity. All seven hypotheses were supported. Digital customer experience and electronic word of mouth positively affected brand image; brand image positively affected supply chain image; and supply chain image positively affected sustainable supply chain performance. Significant indirect effects were found through brand image and supply chain image. The model explained 82.3% of the variance in sustainable supply chain performance and showed positive predictive relevance. The study concludes that ICT companies should strengthen brand image through e-commerce-based digital customer experiences and electronic word of mouth to improve supply chain image and overall sustainable performance.

The disclosure describes a hybrid gas turbine electric propulsion system and methods for operating it during descent. In an exemplary two-spool geared turbofan, an electric motor/generator is connected to the low-speed shaft, while the compressor, combustor, and turbine form the engine core. During descent, a controller reduces engine temperature or shuts down or isolates the core, eliminating thrust and potentially preventing thermal cycling. Aircraft systems are switched from engine-provided power and bleed air to electricity supplied by stored energy or generated as the windmilling fan drives the low-speed spool and motor. An electric compressor may replace insufficient compressor bleed air. Excess stored energy may also drive the motor to rotate the fan and produce either conventional descent thrust or enough thrust to overcome engine drag. In other operating modes, the motor can generate and store electricity for later use. Engine sizing or flow control can maximize turbine inlet temperature during cruise despite sizing constraints at takeoff or climb. The disclosed concepts may apply to two-spool, three-spool, geared, and direct-drive engines and are intended to reduce fuel burn and emissions during low-power operation. The application is a divisional of U.S. Non-Provisional Patent Application Ser. No. 15/200,149 and was made with NASA support under Contract No. NNC14CA32C.

Apple Inc.’s Form 8-K reports that on February 8, 2021, it completed a $14 billion offering of senior unsecured notes: $2.5 billion of 0.700% notes due 2026, $2.5 billion of 1.200% notes due 2028, $2.75 billion of 1.650% notes due 2031, $1.5 billion of 2.375% notes due 2041, $3 billion of 2.650% notes due 2051, and $1.75 billion of 2.800% notes due 2061. The notes were sold under a February 1 underwriting agreement with Goldman Sachs, J.P. Morgan Securities, and Morgan Stanley as representatives, and issued under Apple’s 2018 indenture with The Bank of New York Mellon Trust Company, N.A., as trustee. Interest is payable semiannually on February 8 and August 8, beginning August 8, 2021. The notes rank equally with Apple’s other unsecured, unsubordinated debt. The filing includes the underwriting agreement, officer’s certificate, note forms, legal opinion, consent, and inline XBRL cover-page data.

IDC reports that cloud-based high-performance computing as a service (HPCaaS) gives industrial enterprises rapid, flexible access to advanced analytics, simulation methods and hardware; 52% of respondents consider this central to HPCaaS-driven innovation. Faster calculations and new data-processing methods can improve insights and enable digital products, services and business models.

For manufacturing, simulations, modeling and data analytics accelerate product development and manufacturing while supporting analysis of alternative materials and processes, supply-chain and energy optimization, sustainability, and digital offerings. IDC considers HPC increasingly necessary for complex simulations and modeling, while public cloud and HPCaaS can expand or replace in-house infrastructure.

Recommendations include establishing virtual product and manufacturing development, creating lifecycle transparency and a single source of truth through a holistic data strategy, selecting an HPC operating model based on organizational and technical factors, prioritizing scalable, secure and energy-efficient solutions, and seeking external expertise when needed. The findings come from a December 2021 survey of 200 IT and departmental decision-makers at industrial enterprises with more than 500 employees in Germany, Austria and Switzerland.

NVIDIA Corporation reported unaudited results for the fiscal quarter ended October 30, 2022. Third-quarter revenue was $5.931 billion, down 17% year over year and 12% sequentially. Gross margin declined to 53.6% from 65.2%, primarily due to a $702 million inventory provision, largely associated with lower China data-center demand, partly offset by a $70 million warranty benefit. Operating income fell to $601 million from $2.671 billion, while net income was $680 million versus $2.464 billion and diluted EPS was $0.27 versus $0.97. For the first nine months, revenue rose to $20.923 billion from $19.271 billion, but gross margin declined to 55.1% from 64.7%, operating income fell to $2.968 billion from $7.071 billion, and net income declined to $2.954 billion from $6.749 billion. Nine-month operating expenses included a $1.353 billion termination cost related to the Arm acquisition.

Compute & Networking revenue increased 27% year over year to $3.816 billion in the third quarter, while Graphics revenue declined 48% to $2.115 billion. By market, Data Center revenue rose 31% to $3.833 billion, Automotive rose 86% to $251 million, Gaming fell 51% to $1.574 billion, Professional Visualization fell 65% to $200 million, and OEM and Other fell 69% to $73 million. The company began shipping the H100 data-center GPU and RTX 4090, introduced DLSS 3 and Omniverse Cloud, and announced DRIVE Thor.

At October 30, 2022, cash and cash equivalents and marketable securities totaled $13.143 billion, down from $21.208 billion at fiscal year-end. Total assets were $40.488 billion, total liabilities were $19.139 billion, and shareholders’ equity was $21.349 billion. Inventories rose to $4.454 billion from $2.605 billion. Short- and long-term debt totaled $1.249 billion and $9.701 billion, respectively, and no commercial paper had been issued. Nine-month operating cash flow was $3.393 billion, investing activities provided $7.378 billion, and financing activities used $9.961 billion.

NVIDIA repurchased $8.99 billion of stock and paid $300 million in dividends during the first nine months. Total capital returns were $3.75 billion in the third quarter and $9.29 billion over nine months. The company had $8.28 billion remaining under its repurchase authorization through December 2023 and expected fiscal 2023 capital expenditures of approximately $1.80 billion to $2.00 billion.

The Arm purchase agreement with SoftBank was terminated because of regulatory challenges, resulting in the $1.353 billion write-off of the signing prepayment. New U.S. export license requirements affected A100- and H100-based products and certain systems destined for China and Russia. NVIDIA offered an A800 alternative and sought licenses where necessary, while acknowledging that restrictions could adversely affect revenue, profitability, cash flow, research and development, and distribution operations. The company closed its Russia business during the quarter.

NVIDIA remained dependent on third-party semiconductor manufacturing and assembly and faced long lead times, uncertain demand, architecture transitions, cryptocurrency-mining volatility, channel inventory adjustments, China lockdowns, and the war in Ukraine. It had $7.02 billion of inventory purchase and long-term supply obligations and $9.772 billion of total gross purchase commitments. Operating lease obligations totaled $1.084 billion, with another $647 million of planned data-center leases.

The filing also disclosed $1.971 billion of nine-month stock-based compensation expense, $7.19 billion of unearned stock-based compensation, and securities and derivative lawsuits concerning statements about channel inventory and cryptocurrency mining. No loss accrual was recorded because potential liabilities were not considered probable. One customer accounted for 10% of third-quarter revenue, and 64% of quarterly revenue came from customers outside the United States.

A federal judge ruled that Nirvana’s 1991 *Nevermind* album cover, depicting a naked baby underwater, is not child pornography and dismissed Spencer Elden’s 2021 lawsuit. Judge Fernando Olguin found that the image lacked sexual suggestiveness or intent and was comparable to a family photo of a child bathing.

Donna Adelson, 75, was convicted in the July 2014 murder-for-hire killing of Dan Markel, a Florida State University College of Law professor and her former son-in-law, and sentenced to life in prison plus 30 years for conspiracy and solicitation to commit murder. At sentencing, she insisted she was an innocent woman, denied knowledge of the plot before Markel's death, and called him "a fine and decent man." Judge Stephen Everett warned he could consider her "utter lack of remorse." Prosecutors alleged the motive was the family's desire to move Markel's ex-wife, Wendi Adelson, to South Florida; she has not been charged. Her husband Harvey Adelson testified that she did not participate in the crime.

Myrna LaPlante supports National Inquiry chief Marion Buller and warns a new commission could force her family to seek removal of its story about missing aunt Emily Osmond from the public record. The Assembly of First Nations voted 48–15, without consulting families, for Buller’s resignation. LaPlante supports a two-year extension beyond November 2018 due to the inquiry’s scale and staffing needs. Some Saskatchewan families back the AFN, with Lillian Ewenin citing poor communication and travel uncertainty at Saskatoon hearings. Danielle Ewenin said the inquiry ignored the community trauma of violent deaths.

With 30-year fixed mortgage rates near 5%, Scott Sheldon recommends ways to improve borrowing power: pay down debt to reduce the debt-to-income ratio, obtain a co-signer who shares mortgage liability, change loan programs such as Freddie Mac, Fannie Mae, conventional, or FHA, and consider changing jobs before applying. Lenders assess proposed mortgage payments plus recurring expenses against pretax income; a ratio above 50% may create qualification challenges. Putting more money down may help but is generally less effective than eliminating debt. Job changes should remain within the same or a closely related field and similar role. Borrowers should research each option and consider refinancing later.

Singapore’s special education system evolved from separate, welfare-organization-run special schools toward integration and inclusion within a unified national education system. Before 2004, services for students with disabilities were largely provided by welfare organizations, religious bodies, philanthropists, and health authorities. Mainstream schools could refuse admission, and the emphasis was on students adapting to mainstream academic expectations. Special education teacher preparation began in 1984 with a three-year part-time Certificate in Special Education, replaced in 1991 by a two-year Diploma in Special Education.

The year 2004 marked a turning point when Prime Minister Lee Hsien Loong promoted Singapore as an inclusive society and called for stronger integration of students with disabilities into mainstream schools. Subsequent measures included four Enabling Masterplans, ratification of the UN Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities in 2013, and the 2019 Compulsory Education Act. By 2023, 22 special schools operated, with six more planned for the 2030s. Reported mainstream enrolment of students with special educational needs rose from 2,500 in 2005 to 35,500, with approximately 80 percent of all students with special needs in mainstream schools and 20 percent in special schools.

Teacher and personnel preparation expanded accordingly. The National Institute of Education began training Special Needs Officers in 2005; they were later renamed Allied Educators and then Special Educational Needs Officers. The one-year Diploma in Special Education prepares SENOs to identify needs, assess learning and behavioural difficulties, and plan interventions. Mainstream teachers can obtain the Certificate in Special Needs Support, while a 2020 professional-development roadmap establishes core competencies for pre-service and serving educators. Pre-service teachers receive compulsory coursework on diverse learners, and mainstream teachers can access online modules. Special school teachers and SENOs may progress from the Diploma to the Advanced Diploma, master’s programs, and doctoral study.

Policy reforms have promoted school-wide tiered support and collaboration among teachers, SENOs, counsellors, psychologists, and other personnel. Singapore’s tripartite relationships among the Ministry of Education, NIE, and schools, combined with centralized policy control and school-level autonomy, have supported sustained implementation.

Remaining concerns include the continued operation of government-funded special schools by social service agencies, recruitment and lower pay for untrained special education teachers, limited mainstream options for students with higher support needs, and the absence of an undergraduate special education degree. The article concludes that ongoing reforms toward holistic, student-centred and inclusive education will continue expanding the roles of special education personnel in both special and mainstream schools.

An IEP News email dated July 31, 2001 collected reports on California’s electricity crisis and related controversies. A Los Angeles Times commentary by Kathleen Connell and Peter Navarro argued that the Davis administration’s long-term power contracts created billions in stranded costs, citing $43 billion in contracts, $8 billion in short-term state purchases and planned bond issuance. It attributed improving conditions to cooler weather, conservation, reduced demand and federal price caps.

The SEC began a preliminary inquiry into whether Davis energy consultants used inside information to trade in power-company stocks after five consultants were dismissed over possible conflicts of interest. Spokesman Steve Maviglio disclosed holdings in Calpine and Enron, while other officials and consultants reported energy-related investments. Political consultants Chris Lehane and Mark Fabiani agreed to forgo state payments and leave Davis’s administration under a lawsuit settlement.

Efforts to bail out financially troubled Southern California Edison stalled as legislative proposals failed and the Assembly remained in recess. The utility claimed nearly $4 billion in debt, while critics cited Davis’s ties to Edison, its campaign contributions and proposed bailout terms. Consumer advocates and some legislators favored bankruptcy instead.

San Francisco voters were set to consider two ballot proposals creating public-power entities with elected boards; PG&E opposed the measures. Meanwhile, FERC’s refund order limited potential California recoveries to roughly $3.9 billion, rather than the $9 billion sought, and excluded direct Department of Water Resources purchases. Davis planned to appeal.

Other reports covered Baltimore Gas and Electric’s proposed separation from Constellation Energy and regulatory concerns about frozen rates and $2.4 billion in debt; Texas’s launch of a limited electricity-market deregulation pilot; PG&E’s bankruptcy; accusations against El Paso concerning gas supplies; and California rate increases ranging from 15 percent to as much as 49 percent by customer class.

Sony released a firmware update for the A7RIII that primarily fixes the “Set File Name” function and improves overall camera stability. Installation difficulties for Mac users appear related to macOS 10.13 High Sierra incompatibilities rather than a Sony software issue. The update supports earlier Mac OS versions; affected users may install it on Windows as a workaround.

The lecture concludes its PDE discussion with Homework 7, a drug-diffusion problem involving a patch and shear flow that students must solve using both COMSOL and a custom finite-volume code. Small diffusivity and a very large Peclet number produce a tiny characteristic length and sharp concentration gradients, so numerical output alone does not establish physical accuracy. Students are advised to refine and vary the mesh, test simplified domains, and verify convergence. The lecturer explains control-volume balances, boundary fluxes, cell-averaged concentrations, ghost cells, and the numerical advantages of face-centered fluxes. Because the discretized problem is linear and sparse, sparse direct methods or iterative solvers such as BiCGSTAB are suitable; iterative methods require initial guesses. Time-dependent PDEs also require a CFL number near or below one, while finer spatial grids substantially increase computational costs.

The lecture then introduces probability as the basis for models-versus-data analysis. Measurements fluctuate because both physical systems and instruments vary, making reported values uncertain estimates rather than exact quantities. Discrete and joint probabilities, conditional probabilities, and Bayes’ theorem are demonstrated with coin flips, emphasizing the need to avoid double counting. For continuous variables, probability densities must be integrated over ranges, while cumulative distribution functions provide the probability of values below a threshold. Examples include the Maxwell–Boltzmann velocity distribution and determining molecular speeds in a supersonic nozzle.

The New York Times reported that U.S. agencies intercepted calls last year between Russian intelligence officials and members of Donald Trump’s 2016 campaign, including former chairman Paul Manafort. Officials found no evidence the campaign worked with Russia to hack or influence the election.

The FBI interviewed former national security adviser Michael Flynn after Trump’s inauguration about his interactions with a senior Russian official.
