Flynn was dismissed amid concerns he misled administration officials about contacts with the Russian ambassador; Sean Spicer cited an “erosion” of trust.

Republican senators Rob Portman and John Thune withheld support for labor-secretary nominee Andrew Puzder ahead of his confirmation hearing over delayed taxes related to a housekeeper not authorized to work in the U.S.

Linda McMahon and David Shulkin were sworn in as Small Business Administration and Veterans Affairs secretaries, respectively, following bipartisan Senate confirmations.

Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer called for an independent investigation into Flynn’s situation and for Attorney General Jeff Sessions to recuse himself, arguing congressional intelligence committees lack prosecutorial authority.

A 1968 study cited in Michael Lewis’s *The Undoing Project* found that doctors disagreed on cancer diagnoses for 96 ulcers and often changed their diagnoses when shown the same ulcer twice. Researchers encoded the doctors’ stated reasoning into a computer algorithm, which performed better than the best physician. The passage questions how disagreements and image data were handled, suggesting human involvement and reliance on expert-created rules, then asks whether artificial intelligence and big data might eventually replace experts who write diagnostic programs.

Which? found lenders were slow to pass November 2017’s 0.25-point base-rate rise to savers. Within five weeks, 48% of 327 instant-access savings accounts and ISAs saw no change, while 21% received the full rise. Just 10% of 95 providers passed the full increase to all accounts. Meanwhile, 53% of standard-variable mortgage providers raised existing borrowers’ rates by year-end, and two-, three- and five-year fixed-rate averages rose. Which? cited “double standards”; UK Finance said other market factors affect rates.
The United Way of Northwest Illinois will launch the Imagination Library on March 28, 2018, at Mt. Carroll Township Public Library, providing books for Carroll County children ages 0–5.

Quantizing open strings on D-branes produces massless gauge and scalar fields, whose fluctuations make the branes dynamical objects. A D-brane’s mass is identified with its open-string vacuum energy: the sum of the vacuum energies of all open-string excitations, equivalently the sum of oriented worldsheet diagrams with boundaries. These diagrams are weighted by \(g_s^{-\chi}\), with \(\chi=2-2h-b\). In the weak-coupling regime, the disk contribution dominates, so the D-brane mass and tension scale as \(1/g_s\), with an overall constant fixed by the Euclidean path integral.

An alternative calculation considers gravitational interaction between two D-branes. At low energy, this is represented by closed-string or graviton exchange, or geometrically by a cylinder with one boundary on each brane. The same surface can instead be interpreted as a one-loop open string connecting the branes. This equivalence between closed-string tree exchange and an open-string loop is presented as channel duality and as a geometric precursor to holographic duality, though a complete reconstruction of closed-string theory from open strings has not been achieved.

For a single D-brane, the low-energy effective action contains a gauge field and transverse scalar fields describing brane motion and deformation. When field variations are small, summing all higher-order string corrections yields the Dirac–Born–Infeld action, which includes Maxwell and nonlinear gauge terms and describes relativistic motion of a \(p\)-dimensional object. The brane-position scalars are massless because translation invariance of Minkowski spacetime forbids a potential for them; they are identified as Goldstone modes associated with broken translations.

Open-string endpoint joining and splitting introduces an open-string coupling \(g_o\). Comparing the relevant surface topology with the closed-string coupling gives \(g_o\propto\sqrt{g_s}\).

For \(N\) coincident D-branes, the oriented open-string sectors carry two brane indices, and each excitation becomes an \(N\times N\) matrix. Endpoint interactions naturally take the form of matrix products. Phase transformations of string endpoints and permutations of indistinguishable coincident branes produce a \(U(N)\) symmetry, which becomes a spacetime gauge symmetry. Consequently, the low-energy theory of coincident D-branes is non-Abelian Yang–Mills theory with matrix-valued gauge and scalar fields.

Separating the branes changes the boundary conditions of strings connecting them, giving these modes masses corresponding to the tension times the separation. For two branes, the gauge symmetry is reduced from \(U(2)\) to \(U(1)\times U(1)\), analogous to a Higgs mechanism. More generally, \(N\) branes can separate into stacks of sizes \(n_1,\ldots,n_k\), leaving gauge symmetry \(\prod_i U(n_i)\), while strings between distinct stacks become massive.

Wave-like Asperitas clouds were spotted near Bristol, including Thornbury and Filton, and shared on Twitter. The Met Office says the classified cloud feature has wave-like undersides, but formation remains uncertain and may relate to thunderstorms or changing winds.

The MSPM0C1105 and MSPM0C1106 include a low-frequency subsystem with a typical 32 kHz clock for long-term timekeeping and low-power operation. It contains a real-time clock with prescaler and timestamp support and an asynchronous independent watchdog timer. The watchdog has an independent power and clock source, a 25-bit counter with open and closed windows, eight selectable periods, and generates a power-on reset if not serviced. A windowed watchdog can instead generate a reset or interrupt, supports sleep-mode shutdown and interval-timer operation, and has eight selectable periods. The RTC_B uses a 32 kHz source and provides calendar counters, customizable alarms, periodic wakeups, binary or BCD formats, leap-year correction, crystal-offset and temperature-drift compensation up to ±240 ppm, and calibration clock outputs.

Analog and communication peripherals include a configurable VREF with selectable 1.4 V and 2.5 V internal references shared by the ADC and comparator, support for external references, and ADC operation up to 515 ksps. The comparator provides digital comparison outputs, timer blanking, low-power wakeup, fault-handling integration, selectable input pins, and an 8-bit reference DAC. Security features include flexible code and data firewalls and a customizable CRC-16 polynomial. The CRC module supports CRC16-CCITT and bit reversal. Three UARTs provide programmable baud rates, multiple parity modes, LIN support, separate transmit/receive FIFOs with DMA, and loopback. I2C supports 7-bit and 10-bit addressing, controller and target modes, clock stretching, Standard, Fast, and Fast-mode Plus rates up to 1 Mbps, SMBus 3.0, address-match wakeup, DMA, and glitch filtering. SPI supports controller and peripheral modes, rates up to 16 Mbit/s, configurable framing and chip select, DMA, and TI, Motorola, and National Microwire formats.

General-purpose timers support 16-bit counting, prescaling, repeat-reload operation, quadrature encoding, synchronization, cross-triggering, interrupts, ADC triggering, and Hall-sensor logic. Advanced timers add clock doubling, repeat counters, shadow registers, asymmetric PWM with programmable dead band, fault handling, and additional capture/compare channels. IOMUX controls peripheral pin selection, output drivers, input paths, and shutdown wakeup logic. A two-wire Arm-compatible serial wire debug interface and DEBUGSS provide processor and device-state debugging, a mailbox for software communication, peripheral behavior controls, reset and mode-change requests, SWD lockout, and password-authenticated debugging. A memory-mapped factory region contains read-only capability descriptions, trim data, and device identifiers.

The recommended application circuit uses 10 µF and 0.1 µF low-ESR ceramic decoupling capacitors near VDD and VSS, a 47 kΩ NRST pullup with a 1000 pF pulldown, crystal bypass capacitors where applicable, and pullups for 5 V-tolerant open-drain I/O. TI supports the devices with LaunchPad and BoosterPack hardware, Resource Explorer, SysConfig, MSP Academy, GUI Composer, an Arm-Clang compiler, and online or offline cloud tools. “X” denotes experimental devices, while “MSP” denotes fully qualified production devices. Documentation cautions that not every module or feature is present on every device and that pin functions and implementations differ.

The September 2025 revision updates power-mode, package, electrical, clock, analog, connectivity, timer, CPU, debug, and identification information. Package drawings specify exposed thermal pads soldered to the PCB, optional via placement, and recommended solder-paste coverage ranging from 73% to 78%. Mechanical and orderable information is subject to change, while ESD precautions and TI’s resource and liability disclaimers apply.

Hickory Tussock Moth caterpillars are white and fluffy with black markings and venom-bearing hairs. Common near Belleville from July to September, they inhabit nut trees but eat almost anything. Touching the hairs may cause a nettle- or poison-ivy-like rash, burning, swelling, pain, or allergic reactions. Affected skin should be washed promptly, with calamine or cortisone applied for itching; severe reactions require medical attention. Experts advise watching but not touching them and note that not all caterpillars are poisonous.

Options trading in META involves contracts granting investors the right to buy or sell an asset at a predetermined price on or before a specified date. Call options provide purchase rights, while put options provide sale rights. Investors can gain exposure to Facebook/META and other stocks, indices, commodities, and currencies with different strikes and expirations.

The passage describes brokerage account registration, a stated $100 minimum deposit, broker-dependent margin requirements, leverage from 1:1 to 1:100, and a one-contract minimum trade. Orders require selecting the asset, call or put type, expiration, strike price, and number of contracts. Brokers offer options chains, watchlists, charts, technical indicators, research, risk-management tools, and educational resources; META also provides a demo account for practice.

Strategies include buying calls or puts, writing covered or naked options, and using straddles, strangles, and spreads. META reportedly charges no options commissions, although brokers may charge fees; financing, slippage, and inactivity fees may also apply. Leverage can increase both profits and losses, and options trading is described as highly leveraged, speculative, and risky, especially for short options. Investors are advised to trade only with money they can afford to lose and to backtest strategies where possible.

This FAQ page describes a classical mean reversion strategy in the S&P 500, backtested on SPY. Trading signals are based on Internal Bar Strength (IBS) and Relative Strength Index (RSI) criteria. The article shows equity curves since January 2000, starting with 100,000 in equity and allocating 100% of equity to each trade (compounding, without deducting taxes), along with statistics covering win rates, drawdowns, and annual returns. An inverted version of the strategy (parameters reversed) is also presented with its own equity curve and stats, illustrating the importance of the chosen criteria. The site offers Amibroker and Tradestation code for this strategy along with 70+ other free trading strategies, plus a monthly trading edges subscription service.

The note traces the history of U.S. occupational classifications and the social, demographic, and economic treatment of workers labeled “unskilled.” Census occupational data collection began in 1820, and Alba Edwards formalized six “Social Economic Groups” in 1917. Professional, managerial, and clerical work was classified by property, credit, and business ability; manual work was divided into skilled, semiskilled, and unskilled categories. “Unskilled” work required little formal training and was defined mainly by muscular strength and coarse labor. Worker identity also shaped classifications, as occupations employing many children or women could be labeled semiskilled regardless of their technical demands.

In 1930, 14 million workers, about 28% of the workforce, held “unskilled” jobs in farm labor, domestic service, factory work, and other labor. African American workers were far more likely than white workers to occupy these jobs, reflecting exclusions from land ownership, education, housing, and other opportunities. Throughout the 19th and 20th centuries, farm labor relied on enslaved people, sharecroppers, convict labor, children, and immigrant workers, including Mexican and Chinese workers. Agricultural employment later declined through mechanization and consolidation, but remaining farm jobs remained physically demanding, hazardous, and disproportionately occupied by foreign-born and undocumented workers.

Industrialization shifted production from artisans to large factories employing untrained immigrants, women, and children. Textile factories paid children less than adults, while Ford’s assembly line divided automobile production into repetitive tasks. African American men found industrial employment but were disproportionately assigned hazardous work. Automation eliminated many routine factory positions; manufacturing employment fell 67% from 1965 to 2020. Prison labor and sweatshops continued to supply products at very low wages.

Domestic and personal service work was among the largest “unskilled” categories before the 20th century. Enslaved people, indentured servants, African American women, and Pullman porters performed low-paid and demanding work. Household employment declined as appliances, running water, restaurants, and other services reduced the need for live-in domestic labor. Service employment instead expanded in retail, fast food, hospitality, childcare, elder care, and home health care. Many of these jobs offered low pay, unstable scheduling, limited benefits, physical or emotional strain, and few advancement opportunities. People of color and women were overrepresented in the lowest-paid positions.

Digital technology expanded gig transportation, delivery, on-demand retail and care work, online microtasks, contracted content moderation, and warehouse employment. These arrangements lowered some entry barriers and created new forms of contingent work, but often involved low pay, intense monitoring, safety risks, and limited bargaining power.

Education and training programs did not reliably improve employment conditions. Government regulation, labor organization, and employer practices were more consequential. The Fair Labor Standards Act established a federal minimum wage, a 40-hour workweek, and restrictions on child labor, while the National Labor Relations Act protected organizing rights but excluded many agricultural, domestic, tipped, and contract workers. Strikes and unions secured wage increases, safer conditions, and recognition, although union membership fell from 34.8% in 1954 to 6.2% in 2020. Worker-led campaigns achieved wage gains for farmworkers and domestic-worker protections in several jurisdictions. Some employers, including Ford, Toyota, Costco, QuikTrip, and In-N-Out Burger, used higher wages, worker participation, training, stable scheduling, and redesigned work to improve productivity and job quality.

During the 2020 Covid-19 pandemic, nearly 70% of essential workers were in occupations labeled “unskilled,” and 80% held low-wage jobs. Many continued working without adequate protective equipment, while farmworkers, nursing-home staff, meat-processing workers, and other frontline workers faced heightened health risks. The note concludes that future-of-work policy should focus less on technological job loss and more on job quality, pay, dignity, and the treatment of workers whose socially devalued labor is essential to the economy.

The report offers a global nuclear medicine outlook profiling GE Healthcare, Bracco Imaging, Mallinckrodt, Lantheus Medical Imaging and Bayer. It covers market size, revenue, costs, pricing, margins, shipments, and regional and segment data. The market grew from $3.5 billion in 2013 to $4.2 billion in 2016 and is expected to reach $5.89 billion by 2021.

EdReports Founding CEO Eric Hirsch will leave at the end of the school year as the organization’s board searches for a successor. Since founding EdReports in 2014, Hirsch has emphasized the connection between curriculum and standards and helped establish its independent reviews as a resource for districts. The organization has expanded into pre-K materials and revised its review criteria in response to criticism that it was slow to emphasize phonics, fluency and phonemic awareness. EdReports is also adapting as states, districts and teachers use AI and more curriculum materials. Researchers have found that strong curricula alone may not improve achievement because curriculum, teacher training and assessments are often mismatched, while many districts do not pilot materials before adopting them districtwide.

The Gann Fan is a technical-analysis tool created by W.D. Gann that projects nine diagonal lines from a significant price high or low. Its central 1:1 line is set at 45 degrees, with additional lines representing 2:1, 3:1, 4:1, 8:1, 1:8, 1:4, 1:3, and 1:2 time-to-price relationships. The tool is based on the idea that prices follow geometric patterns and uses these angles to identify potential support, resistance, trends, breakouts, reversals, entry and exit points, and price targets. The 1:1 line is associated with a strong bullish trend, while a break below it may indicate bearish conditions.

Traders are advised to combine the Gann Fan with chart patterns, indicators, trend lines, moving averages, and multiple timeframes. Strategies should include defined entry and exit points, stop-loss orders, position sizing, risk-reward ratios, and plans for managing losses. The tool can also be applied to forex.

Unlike the Fibonacci fan, which uses Fibonacci ratios, the Gann Fan focuses on price-time relationships. Its accuracy is limited because price movements are often random, and its levels may not represent actual support or resistance. Backtesting is recommended, but the passage notes that subjective rules make meaningful testing difficult and that past performance does not guarantee future results.

Cover 1, or “man-free,” assigns every receiver man-to-man coverage while a free safety patrols deep, sometimes with a low-hole dropper providing middle help. Defenses can use it to stop the run, blitz, bracket receivers, funnel routes inward, and avoid assignment confusion, but strong-armed quarterbacks and elite receivers can exploit it. Offenses should attack the perimeter using pick plays, double moves, and routes that deliver the ball on the move. Examples from Ohio State, Oklahoma, and Georgia feature bubble routes, slot fades, speed-out double moves, motion, and red-zone combinations that can create separation, broken tackles, and touchdowns.

Christine Milligan said she and Cassidey Ouellete’s father were stunned when asked whether they should revoke their daughter’s organ-donation registration. Ouellete, who had signed a donor card at 16, was pronounced brain dead after a car accident on the day before her 20th birthday; her family supported her wishes.

Ontario’s Trillium Gift of Life Network said families can override a deceased relative’s donation decision if that person later expressed regret. Families did so in about 10% of cases in 2016, down from 21% in 2015, typically in exceptional circumstances involving profound brain injury and life-support decisions.

Milligan’s brother, former MPP Robert Milligan, introduced a 2012 bill proposing that only donors could revoke registration and that all Ontario residents would be presumed donors unless they opted out. The bill stalled. Trillium CEO Ronnie Gavsie opposed presumed consent, citing polling preferences and a lack of evidence that it increases donors, while Christine Milligan campaigned to revive it and have it named for Cassidey.

S&P Global Platts will launch low-sulphur marine gasoil and diesel assessments at Asian bunkering ports on June 1, 2017, as sales rise and global sulphur limits tighten. Singapore low-sulphur gasoil sales rose nearly sixfold to 1.14 million tonnes in 2016.

This Motley Fool Money article (Oct. 2, 2025) reviews cash back credit cards offering unlimited flat rewards and simple welcome offers, noting that compensation from partners may affect where offers appear but not product ratings.

The passage describes widespread misunderstanding in South America that the Monroe Doctrine asserted U.S. superiority or a protectorate over other American republics. Secretary of State Root sought to dispel this impression during a visit. In a July 31 address at Rio’s third conference, he rejected territorial expansion and special privileges, affirmed equal sovereignty and independence, and advocated mutual aid, shared prosperity, opposition to colonization, and cooperation grounded in liberty, justice, and peace. The address was acclaimed across South America and, in the speaker’s view, represented American sentiment. Argentine Foreign Minister Drago similarly described U.S. policy as opposing European oppression and foreign control without seeking superiority or preponderance. Buenos Aires reception decorations honored several American statesmen, including Monroe, while Brazil named the first conference building “Palacio Monroe.” The speaker thanked the governments and peoples visited by Root for their hospitality. He then recalled his December 5, 1905 warning that foreign nations’ use of armed force to collect contract debts from American republics could embarrass the U.S. government and lead to potentially permanent territorial occupation.

A hockey player praises Carolina’s family-friendly environment, growing fan support, and success in attracting new participants. He believes continued winning will build recognition and expand hockey’s popularity in southern markets, notes increased scoring and comebacks, and hopes to finish his career in Carolina.

Steve Mitchell, a fifth-generation farmer at Boglily Farm near Kirkaldy, says innovation and social media have helped The Buffalo Farm build a niche around buffalo meat’s health benefits. Winning the 2016 Meat category at the Scotland Food & Drink Excellence Awards strengthened the brand’s credibility with major clients. The farm uses social networking to promote deals, share life, engage its community, and recruit help.

Witnesses said a white van mounted a curb south of Finch Avenue and drove along Yonge Street’s sidewalk in Toronto, zigzagging at high speed and striking pedestrians, bus shelters and a stroller. At least 10 people were hit, and several bodies were found near Mel Lastman Square.

Police pursued and arrested the driver and recovered the van. During the arrest, video showed the man saying “kill me” and appearing to threaten the arresting officer. Police said the cause and motive were unknown and established a hotline and website for witness information.

Sunnybrook Hospital received 10 patients: two were pronounced dead, five were in critical condition and three were listed as serious. North York General Hospital received four additional patients. Police closed sections of Yonge Street, advised people to stay away, and restricted subway service while the investigation continued. Emergency social services were made available at Mitchell Field Community Centre, and a memorial was created near the scene.

Public Safety Minister Ralph Goodale said available information indicated no change in the public-risk level, no connection to national security and no reported threats against politicians gathered in Toronto for a G7 cabinet meeting.

Edmonton officials say a pilot using liquid calcium chloride saved $4.2 million in operating costs and reduced sand use by 68%. Chemical engineer Arthur Potts disputes early success claims, estimating private-vehicle costs could be ten times the savings. He says the salt can enter vehicles and exhaust systems, increase rust, damage concrete and affect bridges; Edmonton did not test the salt or added inhibitor locally. Officials dispute its corrosiveness but cannot yet determine environmental impact. Storm-sewer monitoring results are due in October, and collision comparisons were unavailable after the pilot’s first year. Council will debate and vote on continuing the program.

An experiment showed that an AI tool can identify potentially harmful health experiences in social media discussions. The tool, Waldo, was trained using 10,000 manually reviewed Reddit posts about cannabis, then scanned more than 430,000 cannabis-related posts and flagged over 28,000. Of 250 flagged posts researchers checked, 86% described problematic cannabis experiences. Waldo outperformed ChatGPT by producing 18 times fewer false positives, but it did not outperform human reviewers.

Researchers said the approach could help public health workers find adverse effects missed by agencies that rely on surveys and self-reports. They cautioned that performance on other drugs or products is uncertain and that wider use would require privacy protections and ethical safeguards.

The United States withdrew from United Nations discussions on a global migration compact, citing concerns that stronger international governance could undermine national sovereignty and conflict with U.S. immigration law. The decision disappointed Pope Francis and the U.S. Catholic bishops, who urged the Trump administration to reconsider and emphasized that governments must balance border control with obligations to protect migrants’ human rights.

Negotiations in Puerto Vallarta, Mexico, advanced toward a nonbinding 2018 compact based on the U.N.’s 2016 New York Declaration. The proposed framework addresses migrant children’s education, support for countries hosting migrants and refugees, prevention of labor exploitation and continued humanitarian assistance. Pope Francis called participants to welcome, protect, promote and integrate migrants.

While restrictionist advocates praised the U.S. decision, U.N. officials and Catholic experts said international cooperation was necessary. With an estimated 244 million people living outside their home countries, including about 60 million displaced by war, the bishops said wealthier nations have greater obligations to address forced migration.
Four King Edward VI Grammar School pupils placed second in the national schools University Challenge, defeating St Ivo and Nottingham High before losing 280–315 to Southend High School for Boys.

Indian Railways introduced a “no bill, free food” policy on trains, malls and theatres to combat food overcharging. IRCTC publicised the rule online and began deploying 120 inspectors, with more planned, to verify pricing and ensure a bill for every transaction. The policy follows over 7,000 overcharging complaints, fines against caterers, contract terminations and a CAG report identifying unchanged tariffs and unsuitable food ingredients.

The government shutdown has intensified America’s air traffic controller shortage, with about 13,000 controllers expected to work without pay calling out sick and staffing falling 50% in some areas, causing flight delays and crowded airports. The shortage predates the shutdown: only 285 of 313 FAA facilities met staffing targets early in 2025, while 73 were at least 25% short. Training takes 16 months to several years, is costly and rigorous, and about one-third of trainees wash out. Pandemic-related coaching suspensions and retirements have also contributed.

Controllers earn an average of $144,580 annually. Candidates must be U.S. citizens under 31, pass medical, security and FAA testing requirements, and have three years of progressively responsible experience and/or a bachelor’s degree; fewer than 10% qualify for FAA training. The BLS projects 3% job growth and 2,200 openings annually from 2023 to 2033, despite long hours, unpredictable shifts and mental health concerns.

Hascall Steel Company is a US steel service center offering cold-reduced, blanked, slit, flat-rolled, hot-rolled black, cold-rolled aluminized, and coated steel. It processes steel to customer specifications, evaluating gauge, width, and physical and chemical properties. Trained technicians perform precision processing, while an in-house laboratory conducts multipoint testing against composition requirements and quality standards. The company provides practical, cost-effective solutions and has served customers for more than 45 years.

## Summary

**Mixed precision Tensor Cores and iterative refinement.** Mixed-precision Tensor Cores are applied to iterative refinement methods used in solving linear systems common across HPC fields. cuSOLVER's Tensor Core Accelerated Iterative Refinement Solver (TCAIRS) automates this; an ITER fusion reaction study showed a 3.5x speedup on V100 using FP16 Tensor Cores, and the same technology tripled Summit's HPL-AI benchmark performance. CUDA 11.0 added A100 support for TF32. Across 37 SuiteSparse tests, TF32 was the fastest and most robust mode, with the fewest iterations to converge; fallback to FP64 occurred once for FP32, twice for TF32, three times for FP16 with input scaling, and six times for BF16. Geomean speedups over the FP64 solver were 2.0X (TF32), 1.9X (FP16), and 1.8X (BF16), with up to 4X gains using TF32 on ~40K-size complex matrices.

**Fine-Grained Structured Sparsity.** A100 enforces a 2:4 pattern (two non-zero values per four-entry vector), compressing weights for 2x reduction in data footprint and bandwidth, and Sparse MMA instructions skip zero entries, doubling Tensor Core compute throughput (a 16x8x16 multiply completes in N/2 cycles). A train-dense, prune, fine-tune recipe yields virtually no inference accuracy loss across vision, detection, segmentation, NLP and translation networks; training acceleration requires introducing sparsity early.

**Memory and compute hierarchy.** A100 provides 192 KB/SM of combined L1 data cache and shared memory (vs 128 KB/SM on V100), separate FP32 and INT32 cores for simultaneous full-throughput execution, and 40 GB of HBM2 DRAM (five stacks of eight dies, 1215 MHz DDR) delivering 1555 GB/s, more than 1.7x V100 bandwidth. SECDED ECC protects HBM2, L2, L1 and register files. The 40 MB L2 cache (6.7x V100) is split into two partitions of 40 slices each, delivering a 2.3x L2 bandwidth increase (5120 vs 2048 Bytes/clk read bandwidth), with residency controls and Compute Data Compression providing up to 4x DRAM read/write and L2 read bandwidth gains and up to 2x L2 capacity. A100 has 108 SMs (vs 80) with third-generation Tensor Cores delivering 16x peak mixed-precision performance versus FP32 FMA, with 4 Tensor Cores per SM at 2x the raw FMA power of eight in a GV100 SM; warp-wide data sharing across 32 threads, larger k dimension, 8x fewer instructions and 2.9x fewer register file accesses (80→28 accesses, 16→2 instructions for 16x16x16), plus async copy instructions and 164 KB max SMEM per SM. Compute Capability is 8.0. The A100 GPU includes no display connectors, RT Cores, or NVENC.

**MPS and MIG.** Hardware-accelerated MPS debuted with V100 in 2017 and remains supported on Ampere, though shared memory resources can cause interference between applications. MIG partitions an A100 into as many as seven GPU Instances built from seven GPU slices, with isolated paths through crossbar, L2 banks, memory controllers and DRAM; one Sys Pipe handles graphics and compute while six are compute-only. Compute Instances subdivide instances, support Volta-style MPS, enable simultaneous context execution with independent context switching, and permit vGPU migration between instances and across GPUs for load balancing and servicing. MIG offers up to 7x more GPU instances, requires Compute Mode, and disables L2 set-aside functionality.

**Interconnect and resiliency.** Third-generation NVLink runs at 50 Gbit/sec per signal pair (vs 25.78 on V100), uses 4 lanes per direction (vs 8), provides 25 GB/s per direction, and offers 12 links totaling 600 GB/s (vs 300 GB/s on V100). Writes are non-posted, and remote page faults are returned over NVLink. PCIe Gen 4 provides 31.5 GB/s per direction on x16 (double PCIe 3.0), with SR-IOV allowing virtualization and peer access over NVLink. New fault technologies improve error attribution, isolation and containment.

**Other hardware features.** NVJPG is a 5-core hardware JPEG decode engine processing up to five images per batch; the GA100 Optical Flow Accelerator supports optical flow and stereo disparity estimation; FP16 atomic throughput improves 11x and FP32 atomics 2.7x over V100; and five NVDEC units (vs one in V100) improve video decode capability.

**CUDA 11 advances.** CUDA Graphs (introduced in CUDA 10) gain launch and execution-dependency optimizations on A100, reducing CPU launch cost and grid-to-grid latency. A new async copy API moves data directly from global to shared memory (BYPASS and ACCESS variants), and asynchronous barriers with separated arrival/wait phases allow thread-subset synchronization. L2 residency controls set aside persistent data in 1/16th increments (2.5 MB), with address-range windows and per-access granularity; a histogram example achieved 2.5x over V100 and 43% over A100 without residency control. Cooperative Groups adds group-wide async copy collectives, a reduce API with hardware-accelerated ADD/MIN/MAX and AND/OR/XOR, single-step warp reductions, and up to 30% lower grid synchronization overhead.

**DGX A100 and software.** DGX A100, the third-generation DGX system, delivers 5 PFLOPS in a 6U form factor with eight A100 GPUs connected through six NVSwitches (4.8 TB/s bidirectional), provides up to 20x the performance of standard FP32 FMA on V100 using TF32 with sparsity, offers up to 6x the DGX-1 training performance, includes eight ConnectX-6 HDR InfiniBand adapters at 200 Gb/s, and supports the Magnum IO SDK. The software stack includes the CUDA Toolkit, NVIDIA Container Toolkit, and NGC Private Registry containers supporting PyTorch, MXNet, TensorFlow, TensorRT, RAPIDS, CUDA-X HPC, OpenACC and CUDA.

**Appendix: Sparse Neural Network Primer.** Pruning zeroes out low-contribution nodes and interconnections, enabling higher compute throughput, reduced memory bandwidth and lower latency. Fine-grained sparsity yields irregular memory access and load imbalance; coarse-grained sparsity removes whole subnetworks but risks greater accuracy loss. Fine-grained structured sparsity keeps per-node fetches and computation equal, balancing workload distribution, with accuracy tables comparing 2:4 fine-tuning against dense training on ImageNet, COCO 2017, WMT'14 and Transformer XL on enwik8. Publication is copyright © 2020 NVIDIA Corporation.

Researchers developed resealable synthetic packets measuring tens to hundreds of nanometers that release their contents when illuminated with a specific wavelength. Their polymer skin has a water-soluble outer layer and rigid, glassy inner layer, joined by light-sensitive molecules. Light softens the inner layer, releasing the contents, which reseal when the light stops. Made from biocompatible polyethylene oxide and polylactic acid, the packets could enable targeted medicine delivery or controlled release of fertilizers and cleanup chemicals. The team is exploring other triggers, including pressure and chemical cues, and using molecular simulations to study the mechanisms. The research appeared in Nature Chemistry and was funded by the U.S. Army Research Office.

A mixed-methods intervention research in Palghar District, western Maharashtra, evaluated a six-step training-of-trainers (TOT) cascade for maternal and newborn health. Eight clinically competent Pune core trainers received refresher training and prepared local Palghar master trainers. Of 48 candidates screened, 32—25 medical doctors and seven general nurse midwives—were selected through assessments of work profile, teaching skills, experience, and commitment.

The intervention used adult-learner-centered, simulation-based training with pre- and post-TOT assessments. Intermediate-scoring trainers were paired with higher-scoring trainers before independently delivering training. Palghar master trainers received continuous support from Pune core trainers, virtual quality assessment and feedback from three UK experts, and 10 months of virtual refresher sessions through the ECHO platform. They subsequently trained 505 public health providers using case-based learning, clinical simulations, skills practice, and feedback.

Among 463 providers with complete pre- and post-training data, mean scores increased from 66.1% to 84.2% for clinical knowledge, 36.4% to 79.3% for abdominal palpation, 35.4% to 75.5% for newborn resuscitation, and 28.7% to 74.5% for eclampsia management; all differences were statistically significant. Qualitative findings indicated that master trainers gained clinical competence, confidence, leadership roles, professional recognition, and motivation. The study identified methodical trainer selection, staggered induction, sustained mentoring, quality monitoring, refresher training, and hybrid delivery as important features of the TOT model. It recommends longer training periods, supportive service conditions for clinicians, further evaluation of long-term competency retention and costs, and integration of trainer development into broader health-system processes.

The paper introduces T-Tamer, a model-agnostic framework for routing and terminating cascaded inference while balancing competing objectives such as accuracy, latency, and cost. It formulates these trade-offs as weighted loss functions and models adaptive model selection as costly exploration over directed acyclic graphs, with nodes representing sub-models and edges encoding precedence, costs, and performance dependencies.

The paper proves an information-theoretic impossibility for no-recall policies, including confidence-threshold heuristics: even with two models and bounded losses, they cannot achieve any constant-factor approximation to the offline optimum. For with-recall policies, it derives a dynamic-indexing strategy through dynamic programming that is online-optimal for a directed line and remains theoretically optimal for directed trees and the transitive closure of a directed line. Preprocessing is polynomial-time, while inference requires constant work per inspected node and linear work overall.

Experiments on synthetic data and vision and language early-exit workloads show favorable accuracy–latency trade-offs. Reported examples include reducing VGG-13 latency to 45% of the original with limited accuracy loss and reducing language-model latency by up to 90%.

This review, written from an astronomer's perspective, introduces the ESCAPE Dark Matter Test Science Project (TSP), a platform within the European Open Science Cloud (EOSC) that provides FAIR storage, distribution and access to software and data for dark matter research, and aims to connect particle physics and astronomy communities.

Evidence for dark matter has accumulated since the 1930s (Coma cluster velocity dispersions) and 1970s (spiral galaxy rotation curves). Cold dark matter (CDM) remains the leading candidate because its short free-streaming length permits rapid small-scale structure formation, and its predictions fit CMB, cluster x-ray, cosmic shear and gravitational lensing observations. However, unresolved astrophysical issues persist, notably the core-cusp, missing/too-many-satellites and "too big to fail" problems, motivating refined simulations and surveys such as Euclid and LSST. Alternatives include axion-like particles, primordial black holes, warm (WDM) and self-interacting dark matter (SIDM), and modified gravity, alongside WIMPs, which have so far yielded no clear detection. Numerous collaborations (LHC DM, LLP and BSM working groups, PBC/FPC, EuCAPT, iDMEu) coordinate these searches, and open-science platforms are needed for reproducibility.

The TSP's particle-physics content covers ATLAS (dilepton resonance searches constraining a Z′ mediator, and a t-channel semi-visible jet search for dark QCD models, both reinterpretable and available through the Virtual Research Environment), DarkSide direct detection with liquid argon (DarkSide-50 exclusion curves, low-mass analysis, and the forthcoming DarkSide-20k), and indirect detection: Fermi LAT (MLFermiDwarfs machine-learning background modelling for dwarf spheroidal galaxies and brown dwarf capture analyses, showing Fermi sensitivity is insufficient by a factor of nine for constraints below 10 GeV) and KM3NeT (instrument response function tooling, also deployed with CTA for multimessenger work). Reusable common tools include the Baler machine-learning compression prototype, Aladin Lite, Gammapy and Jupyter tutorials.

Astrophysical constraints discussed include gravitational lensing of subhaloes (constraining WDM free-streaming lengths and masses, e.g. 4.1 keV and 2.0 keV lower bounds, and SIDM cross-sections via ram-pressure stripping and core-collapse), with 50–100 well-measured lenses potentially sufficient to rule out CDM, and dwarf spheroidal galaxies as indirect-detection targets, where the γ-ray flux factorises into particle-physics and "J-factor" terms, with substructure and profile assumptions dominating systematics.

Additional tools cited for potential VRE integration include pyHalo and lenstronomy for lens modelling, GAMBIT (with DarkBit and CosmoBit modules) for global fits, AxionLimits for axion summary plots, and the SuperCDMS Dark Matter Limit Plotter. The authors encourage astronomers to adopt ESCAPE services so that complementary astronomical and particle-physics constraints can be combined.

At a February 13, 2017 town hall meeting in Charlestown, Nevis, Minister of Foreign Affairs and Deputy Premier Mark Brantley described Team Unity’s election in 2015 as evidence of public support for national unity. He said the coalition, which formed in 2013 and made Timothy Harris the country’s third prime minister, had advanced economic development and a fairer distribution of resources to Nevis. The United States and Russia agreed on September 8, 1900, to arbitrate U.S. claims for losses suffered by American citizens following Russian seizures of American vessels. The four cases involved the Cape Horn Pigeon, James Hamilton Lewis, C. H. White, and Kate and Anna. The United States argued that the seizures and related actions violated international law, treaty rights, and citizens’ personal rights. While whaling on the high seas in the Okhotsk Sea, it was seized by Russian authorities on September 10, 1892, taken to Vladivostok, detained through the whaling season, and released without trial.
