The ADS868xW is a fully integrated, fully differential 16-bit SAR data-acquisition device with an analog front end, programmable gain amplifier, ADC driver, and buffered precision reference. Its standard SPI interface uses CONVST/CS, SCLK, SDI, and SDO-0, with RST tied to DVDD and RVS optionally monitored for timing.

In a daisy-chain configuration, all devices share CONVST/CS and SCLK, while SDI and SDO-0 are connected sequentially. Devices receive identical configuration values, use SDO_CTL_REG bits 7–0 set to 00h, and shift data MSB-first. The host receives device N’s data first, followed by devices N−1 through 1. An optimal frame contains 32 × N SCLK capture edges; shorter frames can cause erroneous configuration, while longer frames require host alignment of each device’s data. System throughput decreases proportionally as devices are added.

The device operates in RESET, ACQ, and CONV states. Holding the active-low RST input low initiates either an application reset or a power-on reset, depending on RSTn_APP. An application reset restores configuration registers, keeps RVS low, and tri-states SDO-x; a power-on reset also resets internal circuitry and requires the specified settling time. Pulling RST high with CONVST/CS and SCLK low returns the device to ACQ after the required delay. ACQ acquires the analog input, and a rising CONVST/CS edge initiates conversion. Further CONVST/CS transitions are ignored until conversion ends, when the device returns to ACQ. The host can detect completion through RVS or wait for the maximum conversion time.

Programming supports data reads and writes through frames that begin on a falling CONVST/CS edge and end on the next rising edge. During the frame, output data shifts out while input data shifts in. A 32-clock frame is optimal and carries a valid command; shorter frames invalidate writes but may provide valid output bits, while longer frames use the final 32 shifted input bits as the command. The device supports byte and 16-bit half-word commands, including read, write, set, and clear operations; half-word commands ignore the address LSB.

Output data can contain a fixed test pattern, requested register data, or the latest 16-bit conversion result. Optional appended fields include device address, input-range flags, AVDD and input alarm flags, and parity.

The multiSPI interface supports four SPI-compatible modes for configuration and three read-data options: single-SDO SPI, dual-SDO SPI, and source-synchronous operation. SPI-00-S is used after power-up or reset, and SDI_MODE selects subsequent modes. Dual-SDO mode uses SDO-0 and the ALARM/SDO-1/GPO pin to output two bits per launch edge. Source-synchronous mode supplies a data-synchronous clock on RVS and supports internal or external clock sources and one- or two-bit output buses.

Nine configuration registers control device identification, reset and power, SPI selection, output protocol, output formatting, input ranges, alarms, thresholds, and hysteresis. Device-ID values support up to 16 daisy-chained devices. Reset/power-control writes require a protection key of 69h.

An industrial input-module example combines an ADS8681W with an eight-channel MUX36D08 differential multiplexer to digitize software-selectable voltage or current channels. Supported industrial ranges include ±2.5 V, ±5 V, ±10 V, 0–5 V, 0–10 V, 4–20 mA, and 0–20 mA. The ADC settles to 1% accuracy in under 5 µs, supports input amplitudes up to ±12.288 V on a single analog supply, and includes overvoltage protection plus input and AVDD alarms. Programmable alarm thresholds and hysteresis are demonstrated with an NTC thermistor to reduce false triggering near temperature limits.

AVDD and DVDD are independent analog and digital supplies. Recommended decoupling includes 1 µF ceramic capacitors near the supply pins, at least 10 µF bulk capacitors, specified REFCAP capacitors, and at least 4.7 µF at REFIO when the internal reference is used. PCB layouts should separate analog and digital signals and use short ground paths without intervening vias. Programmable NAP mode reduces consumption between conversions, while power-down mode disables analog blocks but retains the interface and register contents. Final sections address documentation updates, support resources, ESD handling, revision status, package information, and TI’s application-information and liability disclaimers.

Healthy weight, regular activity, low-impact exercise such as cycling or swimming, muscle strengthening, and flexibility work can reduce knee injury risk and slow age-related deterioration. Recommended exercises target the hamstrings, quadriceps, glutes, and hip flexors. Persistent pain affecting mobility should be assessed by a physiotherapist, who can provide tailored exercises to improve strength, flexibility, and range of motion. Physiotherapy may also reduce recurrence, delay or avoid surgery, and support recovery after surgery. Patients should avoid ignoring knee pain but remain active where appropriate.

Severely worn or damaged knees that cannot be rehabilitated may require surgery, which can improve quality of life but carries risks such as infection and deep vein thrombosis. Surgery should be a shared decision between patient and surgeon. Knee replacements generally provide long-lasting benefits; the passage reports that more than four in five total replacements and seven in ten unicondylar replacements last at least 25 years.

The disclosure describes absorbent cores for hygiene products such as disposable and incontinence diapers or pants, sanitary napkins, and panty liners. The cores include one or more substantially interconnected channels extending through the crotch portion, generally along the longitudinal axis and across part of the core’s width. The channels may be symmetric or asymmetric and can form U-shaped, funnel-shaped, semi-hourglass, V-shaped, or pie-shaped geometries. They are preferably substantially free of three-dimensional absorbent material and superabsorbent polymer to enable rapid fluid distribution.

A core laminate may comprise first and second nonwoven webs with three-dimensional absorbent material between them. Differential bonding zones can permit portions of the nonwoven webs to separate when adjacent absorbent material swells while maintaining channel integrity. Elastic nonwoven webs may be used to improve conformity around the channel-forming inserts. The channels are intended to distribute fluid more rapidly, limit localized oversaturation, and support improved dryness and comfort. A three-stage distribution system may use channels for the fastest distribution, three-dimensional absorbent material for intermediate distribution, and dispersed superabsorbent polymer for slower distribution.

Absorbent articles contain the core between a topsheet and backsheet, with the channels preferably remaining visible before and after use. An optional body-facing acquisition and distribution layer can further improve fluid spreading, but its size and position should leave selected channel terminal or connecting portions exposed.

The disclosed manufacturing process uses a mold containing a three-dimensional insert shaped inversely to the desired channels. A first nonwoven web, three-dimensional absorbent material, and second nonwoven web are applied while vacuum pressure forces the absorbent material away from the insert, leaving substantially material-free channels. The layers may then be bonded and removed from the mold to form the finished core.

The UK Government has launched a six-week consultation on proposed revisions to the Package Travel Regulations, which could protect an extra 10 million package holidays booked online. The proposals aim to give online bookers the same rights as traditional travel-agent customers, clarify refund rights, and make the company assembling a package responsible for the entire holiday, including third-party services. Which? supports closing protection gaps if travel businesses fail.

Japan’s second-quarter GDP grew faster than expected, extending expansion to 18 months, while household consumption strengthened. Despite volatile, revisable data, the results suggest greater resilience under Abe’s reforms. Rising durable-goods spending, lower unemployment and higher base pay support Abenomics, though inflation remains below the Bank of Japan’s target.

News clippings from November 19–20, 2001, centered on Enron’s financial crisis. In a delayed, unaudited SEC filing, Enron widened its third-quarter loss by three cents a share to 87 cents, or $664 million, and increased nine-month earnings by one cent. It said financial statements from 1997 through mid-2001 should no longer be relied upon, prior profits had been overstated by $586 million, and debt had been omitted from its balance sheet. Arthur Andersen had not completed its review, and further restatements remained possible.

Enron warned that credit concerns, reduced trading and falling asset values could hurt fourth-quarter results, including a possible $700 million pretax loss tied to the Whitewing partnership. A Standard & Poor’s downgrade to BBB- triggered a $690 million demand obligation. Unless Enron repaid the note or posted collateral, partners could liquidate assets including a Brazilian natural-gas company. Enron sought a waiver or extension; another downgrade below investment grade could trigger $3.9 billion in additional obligations. Enron warned that adverse outcomes could materially affect its ability to continue as a going concern.

Bankers questioned whether Dynegy might abandon its roughly $9.8 billion rescue agreement by invoking a “material adverse change” clause. Shareholders sued to block the merger, alleging Enron’s directors breached their fiduciary duties, while ChevronTexaco supported the transaction and reviewed Enron’s litigation exposure. Enron also pursued asset sales, outside financing, debt restructuring and the divestiture of about $8 billion in non-core businesses.

Representative John Dingell requested a special investigation of Andersen’s Enron and Waste Management audits. Other clippings covered Houston’s energy-industry role after the Conoco-Phillips merger, ChevronTexaco’s savings targets, executive compensation trends and miscellaneous company news.

The Hudson River’s New Jersey “Gold Coast,” including Hoboken, Bayonne and Jersey City, is drawing significant residential development because of its Manhattan views, transit access and comparatively attainable housing. Demand remains strong for luxury apartments and condominiums as Manhattan costs rise and renters seek newer properties; the effects of the 2008 real estate crash have largely dissipated.

Toll Brothers is building the second phase of Provost Square at 10 Provost Street near Grove Street PATH station. The 28-story building has 242 studios and one- to three-bedroom condominiums, two lounges, a pool and two roof decks; a later phase is planned for a 525-seat theater. Prices start in the $400,000s and exceed $1 million.

In Hoboken, 1425 Hudson Street is about to break ground, while 236 units at 1400 Hudson are roughly 90 percent sold. Bijou Properties and Intercontinental Real Estate are constructing a 424-unit rental building with a public gym, retail space and a two-acre park at 700 Jackson Street.

Ironstate is building 235 Grand, a 45-story tower with 549 luxury rentals, and developing 70–90 Columbus adjacent to Grove Street PATH station. In Bayonne, the Harbor Station project includes 500 waterfront residences, commercial space and a shopping center anchored by Costco.

The author argues that the immigration debate is dishonest and presents a 20-point plan. It includes keeping refugee families together, limiting family reunification, increasing legal immigration to 3 million annually, applying asylum laws equally, using surveillance rather than a wall, and deploying National Guard troops sparingly. The plan continues deportations while allowing discretion to remain, creates earned legal status after at least 10 years, grants DACA recipients permanent status for community service, bans benefits, and permits eventual citizenship. It also seeks to repeal deportation quotas, restrict local immigration enforcement, tighten E-Verify and employer penalties, and create Mexican jobs through tax incentives. The author criticizes a proposal to have children take undocumented immigrants’ jobs as counterproductive parenting.

Amber Rose said January breast reduction surgery relieved pain that peaked during her 2016 “Dancing with the Stars” run, reducing her bra size from 36H to 36DDD. The 43-year-old entrepreneur and mother also received a cellulite treatment and later shared revealing outfits on social media.

Fireworks smoke may worsen Southern California air quality this week, especially for sensitive groups who should limit outdoor exercise. A weekend heat wave could increase ozone, worsen respiratory conditions, and prompt another advisory.

The letter argues Ohio's congressional districts are drawn so each favors one party, weakening representatives' accountability. It backs the League of Women's Voters' Fair Districts Fair Elections plan—a bipartisan commission drawing lines, keeping communities together—over a rival plan the Statehouse likely supports, urging readers to contact legislators.

The Del Mar fairgrounds board unanimously rejected construction bids after a $4 million funding shortfall. The Surfside Race Place remodel, estimated at $11 million, grew to about $23.6 million, while the required storm-water treatment plant’s lowest bid of $14.6 million exceeded its $10.5 million estimate. With a projected 3% return and possible further unknowns, directors said the Surfside project needs substantial redesign and cost reduction, though they continued to support music, restaurant, craft-beer and other multipurpose uses. The board will re-evaluate the project and consider bringing back a solution in four to six months. It also approved an $18.5 million state loan but must determine whether its terms can be adjusted before the June 27 signing deadline, when interest begins on the full accepted amount.

The passage examines sector-based investing, distinguishing sectors—broad economic categories such as technology or energy—from specific industries. Sector trading involves buying and selling securities within a chosen sector and may carry more risk than broad-market investing.

Drawing on JP Morgan’s analysis of the Russell 3000 from 1980–2015, the article identifies information technology, energy, utilities, and materials as the sectors with the lowest median returns. Telecom, information technology, and energy experienced the most “catastrophic losses,” defined as declines of at least 70% from a peak followed by recovery of less than 60% of the loss. Overall, 40% of the stock universe experienced such losses. Utilities had the fewest, although their relative stability came with weak long-term returns.

The analysis shows that sector rankings vary by metric: utilities ranked worst by excess returns, while other measures favored or disfavored different sectors. It also finds that the median stock generated negative lifetime returns, with a small number of exceptional winners driving the index’s positive performance. The article recommends studying losers and failures as an application of inverse thinking and discusses Taleb’s barbell strategy of combining safe assets with a small number of potentially high-performing assets.

The AMD Security Processor (ASP) serves as AMD’s root of trust for detecting valid AMD-signed boot firmware and verifies AMD signatures on SFS update packages before application. AMD assigns the OEM/ODM responsibility for the firmware update root of trust and, unless AMD Platform Secure Boot (PSB) is enabled, for detecting OEM/ODM-owned firmware. Early OEM/ODM code restricts ROM write access before untrusted code runs; features such as AMD ROM Armor limit writes to the OEM/ODM-controlled SMM handler. Later OEM/ODM logic verifies updates before they are applied.

SFS supports runtime, nonpersistent firmware updates that must be reapplied after reboots. Systems start at the baseline firmware level, and customers may apply patches during OS boot or system operation. BIOS developers enable SFS and optional co-signing through APCB flags that are disabled by default. When co-signing is required, the customer must provide an RSA public key during or immediately after SMM setup, before BOOT_DONE; the key cannot subsequently be changed. Update packages must then carry AMD authorization and the customer’s RSA-PSS co-signature, using 2048-bit keys with SHA-256 or 4096-bit keys with SHA-384. Customers manage their signing keys, and AMD does not countersign them. Compromise of the early trusted code could allow replacement of the customer key and baseline firmware, negating the protection provided by co-signing.

Each patch checks the existing System Patch Level and applicable firmware versions before determining whether it can run. Packages may modify registers or values, replace complete firmware images, or update firmware components such as drivers. SEV updates are automatically committed and prevent rollback; reverting an updated SEV image requires a reboot. On SNP systems, update pages must be HV-FIXED and use the RMPUPDATE command. Attestation software can request SFS measurements through interfaces such as SPDM or DPE, while AMD does not modify firmware components prohibited from update by applicable attestation schemes.

Update packages must validate all affected firmware versions and dependencies before application and should not apply if any portion cannot be completed. Updates can run in parallel with x86 and DMA traffic with minimal performance impact. SEV or SEV/ES virtual machines may need to stop and restart for an SEV firmware update, while SEV/SNP virtual machines can continue operating.

For deployment, a customer-provided agent creates a 2 MB-aligned TEE command buffer, appends any co-signing material and the complete AMD package, and submits the buffer’s physical address through the PSP mailbox interface. The ASP confirms that x86 access can be blocked, verifies the customer signature when applicable and then the AMD signature, executes the patch, updates patch-level information, and returns status. Separate commands retrieve firmware and patch versions and apply updates only after complete validation. Packages must match the system’s specific firmware and patch-level combination and follow the documented AGESA-aligned naming format.

The passage introduces the empirical stochastic inverse problem (eSIP), in which repeated experiments generate observations from a computer-model quantity of interest \(Q(\lambda)\) while the underlying physical parameters \(\lambda\) have an unknown data-generating distribution. The goal is to find a parameter distribution whose pushforward through \(Q\) matches the observed output distribution. When \(Q\) is not one-to-one, multiple parameters produce identical observations, so a Bayesian approach conditions the solution on a specified prior.

The central theoretical framework uses disintegration of measures to express the solution through conditional probability measures concentrated on generalized contours \(Q^{-1}(q)\). Under compactness, smoothness, geometric distinctness, and density assumptions, the posterior has an explicit density analogous to Bayes’ theorem. The resulting posterior is generally continuous almost everywhere, and the solution associated with a uniform prior has maximum entropy. A related numerical method based on importance sampling is shown under general conditions to be asymptotically unbiased and strongly consistent, with variance and error estimates.

An exponential-decay example illustrates how observations at different times produce different contours and posterior ridges, allow probabilities of parameter-region events to be estimated, and support forecasting of later quantities. The eSIP differs from conventional noisy Bayesian inference because its output variation arises from random sampling of parameters across trials, although observational error and random effects can be added. The passage also distinguishes the eSIP from Bayesian model calibration and regularization-based approaches for single-trial longitudinal data, and outlines subsequent theoretical, numerical, and example sections.

The Affordable Care Act survived the Trump administration’s initial effort to dismantle it, but a shortened enrollment period has raised concern about a last-week surge at HealthCare.gov. Dec. 15 is the deadline for subsidized coverage in 39 federally served states; hurricane-affected areas may enroll until Dec. 31. Roughly 9 million to 10 million people currently have marketplace coverage, and increased subsidies may offset premium increases for some consumers. The deadline remains midnight Pacific time, but it is unclear whether incomplete applications will receive grace-period extensions. State-run exchanges generally have later deadlines, including Jan. 31 in California and New York. Despite early signs of heavy traffic, enrollment has so far proceeded without major problems.

Colorado State beat Wyoming 78-73 in the 226th Border War, earning its first win in five meetings and, after Boise State lost to New Mexico, taking sole possession of first place in the Mountain West. Prentiss Nixon hit a go-ahead three-pointer with 34 seconds remaining and added four free throws. The Rams shot 61.8% from the line and 46.7% from three. Braden Koelliker, Anthony Bonner and Nico Carvacho combined for 19 points and 14 rebounds, while Emmanuel Omogbo recorded 19 points and 16 rebounds. CSU has won four straight and eight of its last nine games.

Vijay Mukhi claims Bitcoin exchanges, particularly in tax-haven countries, are becoming platforms for concealing black money and evading taxes. He links Bitcoin’s sharp price rise to India’s demonetization and the Panama and Paradise Papers, while urging the government and RBI not to ban cryptocurrency, warning that a ban would drive it underground.

India’s Bitcoin market reportedly added about 200,000 users monthly and had roughly two million users by late 2017. Monthly industry volume was about ₹2,000 crore, while annual Indian trade ranged from ₹10,000 crore to ₹20,000 crore. Bitcoin’s Indian price rose from ₹7,304 in April 2013 to about ₹11 lakh in December 2017.

Zebpay, which claims 50% of India’s Bitcoin-exchange market, said it follows KYC requirements using Aadhaar or PAN details and operates legally through bank accounts. Co-founder Sandip Goenka attributed rising prices to Bitcoin’s limited supply and growing global demand. The passage concludes that investors should understand its technology and risks because the market is speculative and unregulated.

The passage documents AMD AGESA/AGESATM initialization interfaces, required and optional host-environment call-outs, and customization controls for reset, early boot, memory initialization, late boot, suspend, resume, and OS handoff. It warns that only published entry-point names are guaranteed and discourages reliance on internal procedure names.

AmdInitReset performs minimal processor initialization after reset from the protected boot block in flash ROM. AMD_RESET_PARAMS defines up to three x86-64 execution-cache regions and FCH reset settings. Cache allocations are aligned to 32 KB, subject to address and 1 MB/4 GB boundary restrictions, limited by available cache, and cannot be deallocated. All processor cores call the routine; the BSP initializes HyperTransport and returns for recovery-mode testing, while APs wait for commands and may initialize extended PCI MMIO. The host must establish a stack, allocate parameter storage before AmdCreateStruct, and avoid modifying cache controls during Cache-as-RAM operation.

Early and post-memory stages configure platform settings, power management, VRMs, C-states, boost and frequency limits, PCIe/GNB, FCH, graphics and display, ACPI/DMI/WHEA table generation, and memory options. BSP and AP duties differ, including link and power initialization, warm resets, main-memory initialization, HOB and artifact transfer, and MTRR and cache handoff. The memory phase reports address limits and voltages and supports interleaving, ECC, training, UMA, AMP, refresh, power-down, and DIMM-configuration options.

Later routines allocate permanent HOB storage, configure graphics after PCI enumeration, generate ACPI and DMI informational tables, establish final processor power and P-state conditions for OS entry, and save or restore suspend context. Resume routines exit memory self-refresh, restore processor and silicon state and MTRRs, reinitialize required PCI structures, and complete final restoration before OS restart. The host remains responsible for initiating suspend, resume, and OS restart.

Required host call-outs cover buffer allocation, deallocation, and lookup; cold and warm resets; SPD reads; AP task dispatch, waiting, and idling; PCIe port resets; and IDS access when enabled. Optional hooks support heap rebasing, memory-voltage and training changes, external Vref, FCH customization, MBIST voltage adjustment, video repost, and platform-specific controls.

Customization is available through four mechanisms: `<plat>Options.c` build settings, post-AmdCreateStruct wrapper modifications, IDS controls, and defined call-outs. Build options can remove support for DIMM types, ECC, interleaving, training, online spare, AMP, ACPI/DMI/WHEA, C-states, processor families, sockets, S3, and Connected Standby. Configuration elements specify VRM limits and behavior, CPU frequency, PCI MMIO, IO APIC count, ACPI identifiers and P-state behavior, C-state resources, Connected Standby, CPB, hybrid boost, and core leveling. Unspecified elements use defaults, and `<plat>Options.c` is located through `AGESA_OptsDir`.

The Denver Broncos snapped a two-game skid with a 28-3 Monday-night win over the Joe Burrow-less Cincinnati Bengals. Denver’s defense dominated, while Bo Nix delivered his best passing performance of the season and his first 300-yard game, totaling 326 yards. Denver also had a 101-yard rusher, ending a 37-game team streak without a 100-yard rusher. The Broncos committed seven penalties and made several offensive drops, while Engram caught three passes for 18 yards and dropped one of six targets.

Cincinnati struggled following its franchise-record 38-point loss to Minnesota. Jake Browning finished with 125 passing yards and no touchdowns or interceptions. The Bengals managed only three points through three quarters, gained 21 yards on five full drives from the first to third quarter, and committed 11 penalties for 65 yards. They were outscored 55-6 and outgained by 210 yards across consecutive first halves, with upcoming games against Detroit and Green Bay adding concern.

Isaiah Silva, Frances Bean Cobain’s former husband, is suing Courtney Love and others, alleging they conspired to murder him to recover Kurt Cobain’s guitar. He claims Love’s manager, actor Ross Butler and Yan Yukhtman entered his home on June 3, 2016, and sought the guitar. Love has not responded.

Researchers at Clarkson University studied adults averaging age 75 performing a six-minute walk before and after cognitive tasks involving math and visual identification. Using sensors to measure gait and correlating performance with self-reported mood, they found no gait change during the first 30 seconds after mental fatigue, but later walking speed and stride length decreased significantly among participants reporting greater cognitive fatigue. Lagging physical energy did not affect gait, and more research is needed to explain this discrepancy.

WWE has five-year linear-TV distribution deals for “Raw” and “Smackdown Live,” with USA Network continuing to air “Raw” and Fox distributing “Smackdown.” WWE is open to future digital distribution to reach younger viewers, attract sponsors, boost engagement with its digital properties, and expand WWE Network subscriptions.

ETI found that some Northern Ireland schools inappropriately excluded pupils from public GCSE and A-level results to improve league-table positions. In 2015–16, about 2,900 pupils—7% of Year 12 and 8.8% of Year 14—were deemed ineligible, despite some taking multiple exams.

President Trump and Pfizer CEO Albert Bourla announced a drug-pricing deal in the Oval Office aimed at lowering prescription drug prices. Bourla thanked Trump for his “leadership and friendship,” highlighting their relationship forged during Pfizer’s Covid-19 vaccine development. The announcement was presented as easing investor concerns and casting the pharmaceutical industry favorably.

MBIA Inc. (MBI) closed at $8.85 after trading down 2.43%. Its average brokerage recommendation was 3, ranking 208th of 265 companies in its industry; analysts issued one Buy, one Outperform, and two Hold ratings. ATR-14 was 0.43, weekly volatility 3.59%, monthly volatility 4.49%, and RSI 45.15. Market capitalization was $794.82 million, with 89.81 million shares outstanding. Trading volume was 3.04 million shares versus an average of nearly 1.7 million.

CBSE released the IIT JEE Main 2017 answer keys and Paper 1 recorded responses for online and offline exams, available on the official website from April 18–22. Candidates can download these materials, cross-check their responses to calculate final marks, and challenge the answer keys by following the prescribed procedure.

The article investigates energy-efficient power management for HF-band RFID/NFC systems by dynamically scaling the magnetic field strength emitted by a battery-powered reader. Because readers typically operate near maximum power, passive transponders may be oversupplied; on an NFC smartphone, powering a transponder increased consumption by 50%, and reading it increased consumption by 107% relative to NFC being active without a transponder.

Three areas are examined: determining the power transfer function (PTF) during card detection, adapting field strength to changing distance and transponder operations during communication, and accounting for multiple transponders and their states. The PTF depends on reader-to-transponder distance, the transponder’s current operation and power requirements, and interactions among multiple transponders.

The proposed PTF-Determinator estimates the physical relation between reader and transponder using electrical models, parameters gathered from both devices, and reader-side field-strength adjustments. The reader varies its output until the transponder transitions from an unavailable to an available state, providing an approximation of the required power relationship. The method is integrated into the card-detection phase and exposed through a reader-side library for power-management control. This integration adds detection time and does not address PTF changes occurring later.

A case study using digital business cards also imposes a maximum transmission distance and cuts off transponder power beyond that limit. Simulations showed transmission-energy savings of up to roughly 80% at close range and over 90% beyond the maximum distance. Measurements on existing hardware showed approximately 26% lower transmission energy within range and 75% lower energy beyond it, with limited accuracy due to the hardware’s coarse field-strength adjustment. Combined smartphone estimates indicate battery savings of about 13% within range and 39% when power is cut off beyond the maximum distance. Future work targets more accurate PTF approximation and validation of dynamic scaling during communication and in multi-transponder environments.

A federal judge dismissed Spencer Elden’s 2021 lawsuit over Nirvana’s 1991 *Nevermind* album cover, ruling the image of a nude baby underwater was not child pornography. U.S. District Judge Fernando Olguin found the photograph was not sexually suggestive or intended to elicit a sexual response and was analogous to a family photo of a child bathing.

The excerpt ends a Commentary article (November 1, 1979) arguing that continual self-abasement toward the Third World, support for vocal U.S. enemies invoking popular liberation, and unilateral forswearing of military force are neither morally necessary nor politically appropriate; liberal idealism need not be masochism or incompatible with defending freedom and national interest. An editorial note reports that Ronald Reagan announced his candidacy for the 1980 Republican presidential nomination in a television address taped November 12 and broadcast November 13, 1979.

In the address Reagan described America as proud, generous, sometimes wrong but never mean, arguing that history need not be relived. He rejected claims that the nation had reached the zenith of its power and was weak and fearful, and criticized leaders who said Americans must live with less and that the country's high standard of living was selfish extravagance. Blaming leaders' failure to set rational goals, he said he sought the presidency so the country would not destroy itself. He also addressed the economy, taxes, the federal government, and domestic energy policy. On foreign policy, he warned the 1980s would test U.S. resolve, urged unwavering commitment to allies and negotiation never becoming appeasement of the Soviet Union, and insisted America must accept the responsibilities of leadership.

Singapore's Smart Nation vision, unveiled by Prime Minister Lee Hsien Loong in 2014 and later expanded by Minister Vivian Balakrishnan, aims to enable meaningful lives through technology and shift society from relying on government-led solutions to citizen-driven ones. Numerous initiatives have followed, including the Smart Nation Sensor Platform (SNSP) for lamp-posts, public cameras and infrastructure data; the reorganisation of GovTech under the Prime Minister's Office alongside the Smart Nation and Digital Government Office (SNDGO), which are developing a national digital identity framework and an IoT platform; the launch of SGInnovate to promote start-ups; and Tech Silver training for elderly Singaporeans. However, these efforts have produced little public engagement or "news fatigue," as most focus on technical infrastructure, are administrative, or target specific groups such as the young and elderly.

The passage cites two possible success stories: Estonia's widely used state-issued digital identity, which President Kersti Kaljulaid said succeeded because it is simple, cheap and reliable rather than cutting-edge; and cashless payments, normalised in Beijing through QR codes and WeChat. In Singapore, the Association of Banks launched PayNow in July for customers of seven banks, with DBS and OCBC adding QR code merchant payments, but adoption has been slow, partly because consumers face too many entrenched options — a lesson drawn from Sheena Iyengar's jam study, where a wider selection attracted more interest but fewer purchases.

The author suggests auto-enrolling bank account holders in PayNow with an opt-out option, hoping this would build retailer demand and create a virtuous cycle, with legislation as an alternative kickstart.

The World Bank raised China’s 2025 growth forecast to 4.8% from 4.5%, citing economic resilience supported by government stimulus, stronger exports, infrastructure spending, manufacturing support and improving consumer sentiment. These factors offset weakness in property and subdued private consumption. It expects growth to slow in 2026 as narrowing fiscal space, local government debt, demographic pressures, declining productivity and global trade uncertainties weigh on demand. The bank says China remains ahead of most major economies but must pursue reforms in innovation, productivity and services while gradually shifting from state-led investment toward consumption, green industries and digital innovation. The passage also lists global finance headlines and describes Pan Finance as an international financial intelligence publication.

The speakers praise the team’s unity, talent, mutual belief, and leadership, calling Rod the franchise’s public face and crediting his example to the room. Another speaker describes Edmonton as a special organization with great staff and teammates, saying he is nervous but excited to return and emphasizing that the team should focus on each shift and opponent rather than look ahead. He praises young players such as Cam, Tommy, Justin Williams, Andrew Ladd, and Eric, noting their maturity and important contributions. The speakers believe the two remaining teams deserve to be in the finals because of their confidence, goaltending, timely goals, and strong performances in major games. They predict a loud, physical, closely contested series of four to seven games featuring excellent hockey, while declining to name a favorite but expressing confidence in their own team.

The speaker urges the team to focus on one period and one game at a time, avoid dwelling on the difficult playoffs, and take time for family and reading. Despite sacrifices and an uncertain outlook, they should avoid going out early and play their best at home.

The U.S. Department of Energy awarded the University of Wyoming nearly $10 million to assess whether 50 million tons of carbon dioxide from coal-burning plants can be captured and stored underground north of Gillette. The project addresses long-term emissions risks while recognizing coal’s economic importance to Wyoming.

A Trump administration health report recommends increasing breastfeeding rates through WIC, other federal policies, and a safe donor-milk supply, but provides few implementation details and does not propose federal paid parental leave. Experts say broader structural reforms, funding, and state-federal coordination are needed because most parents who start breastfeeding stop earlier than planned, despite an 84% initiation rate.

Researchers recommend expanded postpartum services, training for health professionals, broader insurance coverage, stronger enforcement of workplace protections, and research into maternal-health disparities. They also cite evidence that paid leave supports breastfeeding: California’s program increased breastfeeding duration by nearly 18 days, while parents receiving at least 12 weeks of paid leave were more likely to initiate and continue breastfeeding.

Disparities are especially pronounced among Black, Native American, Alaska Native, low-income, rural, unmarried, and younger mothers, many of whom lack paid leave or workplace support. Experts also warn that proposed cuts to food and health assistance could undermine breastfeeding and maternal-child health. Donor milk can support premature infants and help parents establish breastfeeding, prompting calls for increased federal funding for nonprofit milk banks.

In January 1942, Minister in Finland Schoenfeld reported former Foreign Minister Erkko’s view that most Finns favored withdrawal from the war, but favorable external circumstances and guarantees of Soviet nonintervention were needed. Erkko warned of possible German retaliation and food shortages and believed Finland had missed a prior opportunity for peace. He also described growing Finnish friction with and criticism of Germany’s military performance.

Secretary Hull instructed Schoenfeld to question the Finnish government about its failure to clarify or justify German troops’ use of Finnish territory as military bases. An attached memorandum noted possible future Allied operations at Petsamo or through northern Finland and warned that prolonged association with Germany risked complications.

Schoenfeld later told Finance Minister Pekkala that Finland’s position required urgent clarification because the war, particularly Japan’s attack on the United States, was rapidly changing conditions. Pekkala said Finnish leaders had reported no new developments in relations with the United States.

President Trump announced the first public drug-pricing agreement with Pfizer, which will lower prices for Medicaid and consumers and launch new medicines at prices similar to those in other countries. In exchange, Pfizer will avoid certain drug tariffs for three years if it fulfills a $70 billion U.S. manufacturing investment. Many Pfizer products are slated for discounts of at least 50% through a Trump-branded purchasing platform, though the site is not yet active. The agreement’s confidential terms and effects on revenue and profits are unknown. Experts said the covered drugs represent only a small share of U.S. prescriptions and questioned whether direct sales would substantially reduce costs. Trump said similar deals with other drugmakers were forthcoming and threatened tariffs for companies that declined.

The 4-2-5 defense combines elements of the 4-3 and 3-3-5, using five defensive backs and typically keeping six defenders in the box. It relies on athletic personnel and pressure while remaining effective against both the run and pass, including modern spread formations. Its key player is the “Sam” or “Rover” linebacker, who must cover in man, handle pulling guards, and rush the passer. Coordinators also commonly use larger defensive backs as linebackers and larger linebackers as defensive linemen.

The formation is versatile and supports any coverage from its base alignment, but it is unbalanced because the Sam creates an overhang on only one side. Offenses can attack the weak side by blocking the weak-side safety and sealing the corner and end, making sweeps and outside-zone runs effective. The defense may also struggle against larger offensive lines and backs because its personnel are generally smaller.

Common blitzes include six-man pressure with cover zero and variations involving the strong-side inside linebacker and Rover, with the potential to add a seventh rusher. Common coverages are Cover 4, which keeps plays in front of the defense, and Cover 3 Sky, which disguises a two-high shell while playing coverage with a rotating safety.

Gary Patterson is identified as the best-known 4-2-5 coach. His TCU defenses led the nation in defense three consecutive times and five times overall. Former Carthage College defensive coordinator Greg Etter also used the 4-2-5 to generate turnovers and pressure.

The author, whose story concerns cancer rather than mental health and who holds no professional qualifications in the field, writes that he is scheduled to speak at schools and community events in Otago about mental health, though the column was composed in advance of those talks. He explains his reasons: his own past experience with depression; a belief that society shares responsibility for raising awareness of New Zealand's mental health crisis; concern about youth suicide statistics; and frustration with stigma, silence, and people tearing each other down. His message is that discussing one's mental health openly is acceptable, so those needing help know they can reach out. He describes mental illness as isolating and surviving in secrecy, weakened by conversation, which sheds shame and stigma and can save lives. He praises public figures such as Zac Guildford and Zac Franich for speaking out, urges others with stories to do the same, and expresses optimism that the 2010s will be the decade New Zealand spoke up about mental health. Help is available through GPs, local mental health providers, 111 in emergencies, and free 24/7 helplines including Depression Helpline, Lifeline, Need to Talk (1737), Samaritans and Youthline.

The study evaluated sleep-specific outcomes from a mobile chronic disease self-management app with a psychoeducation module tailored for adults aged 40 and older with chronic health conditions and low health literacy. The module used multimedia content, individualized sleep information based on insomnia, depression, and stress measures, and reading levels of third, sixth, or eighth grade. Assessments occurred at baseline, immediately after the intervention, and three months later.

Of 286 people who completed baseline assessments and the sleep module, 195 with Insomnia Severity Index scores of 8 or higher were analyzed. Among them, 46.7% were men and 53.3% women; 86% identified as Black, Indigenous, or other People of Color, and 61% reported annual incomes below $10,000. Participants had an average FLIGHT/VIDAS health literacy score of 10.02, above-average perceived stress, and depression scores above a commonly used cutoff. Their average PSQI and ISI scores indicated substantial sleep disturbance. Completing the module took an average of 32 minutes.

Sleep disturbance was significantly associated with hypercholesterol, depression, other nervous conditions, and bipolar disorder. Mixed-effects models found that socioeconomic status, health literacy, number of chronic conditions, time, and treatment group were associated with sleep quality over time. The intervention produced a statistically significant but small-to-medium improvement in sleep quality (d = 0.40), with a model-adjusted PSQI decline of 0.85 points (95% CI 0.11–1.60).

The findings suggest that brief, personalized sleep education at appropriate reading levels may modestly improve sleep and could serve as an initial intervention before more intensive treatment. Limitations include possible effects from other tailored modules, reliance on a single self-reported sleep measure, limited generalizability given the primarily low-income and minoritized sample, and the small magnitude of improvement.

A speaker praises an unnamed goalie’s puck handling, skating, physicality, competitiveness, and poise, saying he has proven dependable under pressure. For the next game in Pittsburgh, he stresses patience, discipline, strong road play, puck protection, sound positioning, and avoiding penalties or quality chances. Although Pittsburgh’s loud, energized arena and strong home play make the challenge difficult, momentum should not shape preparation; decisive plays within each shift matter. He emphasizes character, sacrifice, collective effort, and learning from difficult experiences over individual statistics. He credits Hossa’s determination as an influence on the team, describes Pavel and another teammate as key offensive and defensive contributors, and praises Crosby’s talent, determination, strength, and leadership while noting how difficult he is to check.

The lecture explores pleat folding, in which alternating mountain and valley folds produce three-dimensional forms. A square sheet with concentric square creases and diagonal creases collapses into an X-shape and then pops into a saddle resembling a hyperbolic paraboloid. A related circular pattern with a central hole produces another saddle. These models illustrate “self-folding origami”: simple crease patterns cause paper to assume complex 3D shapes automatically.

Paper normally has elastic memory and prefers to remain flat, while creasing causes plastic deformation that makes it prefer a bent state. Simulations modeled these competing forces with spring approximations and reproduced physical forms such as squares, hexagons, octagons, and hyperbolic paraboloids. Such simulations also enabled “origami skeletons,” built from 3D-printed spherical joints and aluminum rods. The lecture suggests that self-folding could support flat-manufactured structures that deploy automatically, including applications at nanoscale or in space.

Several sculptural applications were presented. An algorithm joins hyperbolic paraboloids along the faces of polyhedra to create closed enclosures called hyperhedra. Other sculptures use circular or curved creases to generate varied saddle and relief forms. A blindfolded glassblowing performance combined tactile paper-folding techniques with glassblowing. The saddle models date to the late 1920s Bauhaus and later became prominent in the origami community.

The lecture’s central mathematical result is that the standard concentric-square crease pattern cannot form a proper non-flat 3D folding, even without specifying mountain–valley assignments. Real models require additional creases because the untriangulated faces cannot remain planar and instead twist. Triangulating the pattern enables an approximate hyperbolic paraboloid, although the result remains slightly different from an exact one, particularly near the center.

A computer-assisted construction builds the triangulated form from the center outward. At each step, the next vertices are determined from the intersections of three spheres, with the desired mountain–valley assignment selecting one of two possible points. Mathematica performs the calculations. Interval arithmetic tracks accumulated uncertainty, supports collision checks, and, with sufficient numerical precision, validates constructions up to 100 rings for selected even fold angles between 2 and 178 degrees. The method’s success depends on the triangulation; other patterns fail at fewer rings or at larger fold angles.

These results use differential-geometry ideas for intrinsically flat, piecewise smooth surfaces. Folded paper has zero Gaussian curvature and can be locally planar or parabolic, with rule segments and constant tangent planes along those segments. Two key conclusions are that a properly folded straight crease must remain straight and that an uncreased region with a polygonal boundary must remain flat. Consequently, interior faces of a straight-crease pattern behave as rigid panels. Concentric polygon patterns whose diagonals meet at a central point therefore cannot produce the claimed proper 3D folds, while suitable added diagonals make the folding possible.

The lecture also surveys related open problems. The maximum volume that can be enclosed in a pillow or square tea bag is unknown, as is the limiting shape of inflated Mylar balloons and polyhedral containers. Any convex polyhedron—and more generally any polyhedron—can be inflated to a greater volume by altering its folds; the limiting form cannot remain polyhedral and is conjectured to be smooth with ripples.

Finally, the lecture discusses curved-crease origami, especially David Huffman’s largely undocumented models. The speaker and collaborators are recreating these models using CAD diagrams and robotic scoring, while investigating the mathematics and design principles behind them. Their examples include circular and elliptical arcs, twisted pleats, relief surfaces, tessellations, cylinders, and tubes. More broadly, deriving the creases and joins needed to produce an arbitrary 3D surface remains an unsolved reverse-engineering problem.

Severe storms threaten Houston, with damaging winds, quarter-size hail, heavy rain and isolated tornadoes possible. A Severe Thunderstorm Warning is in effect until 9 a.m.; the worst is expected to move east of Houston by then.

Adoree’ Jackson said the Titans’ final offensive play had never been practiced, while coach Mike Mularkey said it had been practiced previously, though not that week. The discrepancy drew criticism for using the rookie cornerback on a crucial fourth down despite Tennessee’s receiving options.

Appalachian State freshman Max Correa announced his candidacy for Kansas governor despite having no family ties to Kansas and never having visited the state. Kansas and Vermont are the only states without gubernatorial age requirements. Correa said his youth and political inexperience are weaknesses, but he offers fresh perspectives and policies aimed at younger voters. Drawing on Jewish concepts learned in childhood, he proposed using “tikkun olam” to resolve legislative conflict and adapting Israel’s kibbutz model to communal settlements whose workers could use profits to cover children’s college tuition. If elected, he would drop out of App State and attend the University of Kansas part-time in Topeka. He also pledged to address the opioid crisis by expanding access to Narcan and focusing on rural areas. Political science professor William Hicks encouraged young people’s political participation and influenced Correa to run.

Algoma Public Health’s 50th-anniversary “Get Active Algoma” contest encourages families and friends to complete GooseChase missions, earn points and win prizes while reducing screen time. It runs March 19–May 31, 2018; the top prize is a $600 bike voucher.

Micro E-mini futures, launched by the CME Group in 2019, are one-tenth the size of standard E-mini contracts. They trade electronically on CME Globex, require lower margin, and are mostly financially settled, making futures more accessible to retail traders with limited capital while allowing more precise risk management. Initially covering the S&P 500, Dow, Nasdaq 100, and Russell 2000, their range now includes bitcoin, copper, crude oil, Treasury yields, and FX futures. The Micro E-mini S&P 500 contract equals $5 times the index value, compared with $50 for the standard E-mini contract.

A Micro E-mini strategy may use technical and fundamental analysis for market timing, position sizing, and risk management. The article recommends backtesting strategies and illustrates this with a paid overnight strategy that enters at one close and exits 24 hours later. It uses the Nasdaq 100 mini contract because the Micro E-mini has a shorter trading history.

Contract terms vary by asset. The Micro E-mini S&P 500 trades Sunday through Friday, from 6:00 p.m. to 5:00 p.m. ET, with a daily break. Its minimum price fluctuation is 0.25 index points, or $1.25 per contract, for outright trades and 0.05 points, or $0.25, for calendar spreads. Quarterly contracts are listed for five consecutive quarters and trading ends at 9:30 a.m. ET on the third Friday of the contract month.

Trading requires registering with a futures broker, funding an account, and posting initial margin because contracts are leveraged. CFDs that track Micro E-mini futures are an alternative and have no fixed expiration date. Price factors and seasonality depend on the underlying asset; Treasury contracts, for example, may respond to interest rates, inflation, economic conditions, and sociopolitical events. ETFs track the underlying asset rather than the futures contract size. Leverage creates the greatest risk, as losses are based on the full contract value rather than the margin deposited. The article reports an S&P 500 futures all-time high of 4,808.25 in January 2022 and an all-time low of 665.75 in March 2009.

The passage describes NVIDIA’s Blackwell rendering technologies and GPU lineup. Stochastic Texture Filtering introduces randomness into texture sampling to reduce aliasing and moiré when trilinear or anisotropic filtering is impractical; it can also provide cubic or Gaussian filtering from a single point sample, with faster execution on Blackwell GPUs.

Neural Radiance Cache uses a neural shader trained on live game data to infer final lighting values for multiple path-traced bounces after the first bounce. This improves indirect lighting and real-time global illumination while reducing GPU tracing demands. RTX Skin applies subsurface scattering to translucent materials in real-time path tracing. RTX Neural Faces combines a rasterized face and 3D pose data with a TensorRT-optimized generative model trained on offline images spanning angles, lighting, emotions, and occlusion to render more natural-looking faces in real time.

The Blackwell family includes the flagship GB202 GPU, with 92.2 billion transistors, 24,576 CUDA cores, 192 RT cores, 768 Tensor cores, 768 texture units, and a 512-bit memory interface. GB202 powers the GeForce RTX 5090. The high-end GB203 contains 45.6 billion transistors, 10,752 CUDA cores, 84 RT cores, 336 Tensor cores, and 336 texture units with a 256-bit memory interface; it powers the GeForce RTX 5070 Ti and RTX 5080. The performance-segment GB205 has 31 billion transistors, 6,400 CUDA cores, 50 RT cores, 200 Tensor cores, and a 192-bit memory interface; it powers the GeForce RTX 5070. GB203 and GB205 retain major Blackwell features, including fourth-generation RT cores, fifth-generation Tensor cores, DLSS 4, and new AI gaming features.

NVIDIA disclaims warranties for the specifications, reserves the right to revise them or discontinue products, excludes suitability for high-risk applications, and provides materials and third-party information without implied licenses or warranties.

Napheesa Collier accused WNBA leadership and commissioner Cathy Engelbert of “worst leadership,” citing inadequate responses to officiating, player compensation and the state of the league. She said she publicized private conversations ahead of collective bargaining negotiations, including an alleged remark from Engelbert that Caitlin Clark and other young stars should be grateful for the WNBA platform and “on their knees” for its media rights deal. Collier also alleged Engelbert dismissed officiating concerns by saying only losers complain about referees.

Engelbert said she had “utmost respect” for Collier but was disheartened by how their conversations had been characterized, and reiterated her commitment to players and the league. Collier, a WNBA Players Association vice president and Unrivaled co-founder, called the criticism necessary for the sport’s future and said she was unconcerned about a potential fine.

The comments followed Minnesota’s semifinal elimination by Phoenix. Collier missed Game 4 with an ankle injury, while coach Cheryl Reeve was ejected and suspended after criticizing officiating. The WNBA also announced a multiyear USA Network media rights deal as players sought a larger revenue share.

Daniel Jones, a British expatriate, was convicted in Cambodia of promoting a Siem Reap pool party with “pornographic” photos and received a one-year sentence, with the remainder suspended after a month and 22 days on remand. Jones denied sex or nudity and apologized for causing offence. Police found condoms at the villa, and his lawyer said he would check whether Jones wanted to appeal.

President Van Buren transmitted to the House correspondence between British minister Fox and Secretary of State Forsyth concerning Alexander McLeod’s detention in New York over the 1837 destruction of the steamboat Caroline. Fox warned of serious consequences if McLeod was not released and defended the destruction as necessary self-defense, arguing that the vessel was engaged in piracy against British subjects and that New York authorities had failed to prevent preparations for the attack. He protested labeling the British officers’ conduct “outrage” or “murder.” Forsyth replied that full evidence had been presented to Britain seeking redress, that further discussion in Washington was inappropriate, and disputed Fox’s characterization of the event.

Kay Frazier, 50, died when an artery ruptured during surgery for a blood clot blocking blood to her brain. She had married Gary Frazier in his prison cell and regularly visited him in Nebraska. The inquest heard the clot was believed to have occurred naturally, but returned no verdict.

A retired Toronto civil litigator purged decades-old law school books while decluttering his home. Before discarding each volume, he recalled memorable cases involving contractual “puffery,” immoral agreements, property ownership, and a cargo-ship explosion. He ultimately recycled most of the books, later regretting one whose used hardcover was listed for more than C$1,000. He kept one thick volume because it served as a reading stand at his desk. The author, Marcel Strigberger, continues writing and speaking about law and humor after closing his practice.

A hockey player said opponents deliberately fell into him and pushed his defensemen onto him, creating dangerous situations, and expects similar tactics to continue. Although he opposes retaliation, he believes teammates should be more aggressive, especially in front of Eddie, while he continues attacking from behind the net and corners. He noted Buffalo’s ice and puck bounces differ from Dallas, allowing more puck play, and said he feels more comfortable at home. After the game, he felt tired but physically fine, with his groin unchanged.

The president vows to preserve, protect, and defend the Constitution while promoting national unity and faithfully executing his duties. He urges immediate economic and financial reforms to address industrial depression, unemployment, and deficits. He calls for a nonpartisan commission to examine coinage, banking, and currency laws, supports eventual international bimetallism while maintaining silver at parity with gold, and stresses government economy, adequate revenue, and passage of protective tariff legislation. He also advocates renewed reciprocity in trade and prompt congressional action to restore business confidence and assist agriculture, manufacturing, and labor.

The address stresses equal rights, obedience to law, protection of free speech, education, religion, and fair elections, and firm opposition to lynching and mob violence. The president pledges to enforce laws against trusts and other commercial abuses, improve naturalization and immigration, expand education, and continue genuine civil-service reform. Congress should also restore the American merchant marine.

On foreign affairs, he supports peace, noninterference, national honor, and arbitration of international disputes, urging Senate ratification of the pending arbitration treaty with Great Britain. Because the Treasury requires immediate congressional action, he announces that he will convene Congress in extraordinary session on March 15, 1897. He concludes by celebrating renewed national unity across sectional and political divisions.

Both teams matched closely with similar styles, and an emotional game was expected. The speaker’s team corrected errors and insufficient intensity, capitalized on a fortunate break, and improved late by battling low, getting the puck to the net, involving defensemen, and creating chances while staying open rather than defensive.

An international team led by Leiden, Tsinghua, and Zhejiang University researchers used Bell tests on superconducting processors of up to 73 qubits to certify genuine multipartite quantum correlations. By measuring low-energy states 48 standard deviations below classical limits and verifying correlations in systems of up to 24 qubits, the study demonstrated quantum behavior at unprecedented scale, with potential benefits for secure quantum communication, cryptography, and algorithm development.

Advanced attacking runs require players to anticipate play several passes ahead and respond consciously to defenders and team tactics. Individual runs include blind-side runs, drawing defenders out, inverted runs, overlaps or underlaps, third-attacker runs, late runs, and deep-lying runs. Planned runs, often assigned during set plays or crosses, include designed runs, runs to receive specific passes, and fast breaks. Supporting runs help maintain possession through back-pass, square-pass, and switching-field options.

Successful runs depend on precise timing, patience, unpredictability, and awareness of the offside rule. Runners should avoid becoming offside before receiving the ball, while teammates should recognize runners who have moved too far forward. Although only one run can receive the pass at a time, all players should initiate and complete their runs because possession may change. Players should also scout opponents’ individual and collective defensive tendencies to improve their runs.

Student mistreatment remains common in medical education and is associated with psychological harm, burnout, reduced empathy, and career doubts, while underreporting is widespread. This qualitative study examined factors influencing whether medical students report mistreatment. Peer researchers conducted 21 interviews with current students at a large urban academic institution in the southern United States. Participants described 34 incidents: 12 were reported and 22 were not. Inductive analysis identified four groups of influences:

- **Personal:** Fear of retaliation, concerns about grades or careers, lack of personal benefit, and a sense of justice either deterred or motivated reporting.
- **Situational:** Severity, racial mistreatment, confirmation from friends or family, bystander responses, and perceptions of the perpetrator affected students’ decisions. Bystander inaction generally reduced willingness to report.
- **Structural:** Students often expected no meaningful action, did not know where or how to report, or received no feedback about outcomes.
- **Climate:** Medical hierarchy and institutional culture normalized mistreatment, made students feel powerless, and created expectations that reports would not be taken seriously.

The authors recommend a transparent, easy-to-use reporting system, anonymous mechanisms for reporting retaliation, prompt institutional responses, bystander training, and leadership-driven cultural change. Limitations include the single-site volunteer sample, higher reporting than in the general student population, and the concentration of incidents in clinical settings.

A *Climate Change* paper argues that Eldgjá’s 10th eruption, which began in spring 939 CE and lasted until at least autumn 940, may have encouraged Iceland’s Christianization. The eruption blocked sunlight, lowered temperatures, and hindered agriculture among recent settlers. Researchers cite *Völuspá* stanzas describing volcanic disasters, suggesting they recalled Eldgjá and portrayed the pagan gods’ doom. They argue the eruption helped prompt gradual Christianization, officially recorded in 999/1000 CE, and note that *Kristni saga* also links a volcanic eruption with the conversion debate.

Huawei’s Honor subsidiary marked three years in India by launching the Honor 9i, a rebranded Maimang 6/Nova 2i with a 5.99-inch 18:9 FullView display, metal unibody design, dual front and rear cameras, and rear fingerprint sensor. It runs Android Nougat’s EMUI on a Kirin 659 octa-core processor, with 4GB RAM, 64GB storage, and a 3,340mAh battery. Initial indoor tests showed fast performance and good camera results, while fuller testing was pending. Priced at Rs. 17,999, it was presented as a potential mid-range contender.

The author argues that remaining coal lands should remain public property, with legislation withdrawing them from sale or entry except in special cases. Private operators could mine under a royalty system, while federal oversight would regulate prices, transportation rates, and carrier practices to prevent favoritism. This approach would treat coal like forests as a resource for public benefit.

Congress has already advanced national oversight through railway-rate, pure-food, and beef-packing laws, although further regulation should await evidence from their operation. The author also calls for stronger control over interstate corporations, including expanded Interstate Commerce Commission authority, corporate licensing, disclosure of ownership and business operations, and prevention of overcapitalization and excessive profits. Consolidation should not be prohibited outright but regulated to avoid harm to the public. Government oversight can protect the public without suppressing individual initiative, while unregulated competition can allow powerful interests to eliminate competitors and fuel agitation for government ownership or socialism.
