Delta reported strong third-quarter results, with adjusted revenue of $15.2 billion and adjusted EPS of $1.71, beating Wall Street estimates. Premium-seat revenue rose 9% to nearly $5.8 billion, corporate travel increased 8%, and main-cabin revenue fell 4%. Delta now expects premium-seat sales to surpass main-cabin sales in 2026 and projects full-year adjusted EPS of about $6. CEO Ed Bastian said the airline is positioned to expand margins through premium travel, while cutting off-peak routes and investing in major markets, lounges and premium experiences. The results lifted Delta shares as much as 6% and were viewed as a positive sign for the broader U.S. airline industry.

Energy Central’s January 24, 2002 daily newsletter compiled electric-power and gas-industry news, market data, regulatory developments, company results, and press releases. Coverage centered on Enron’s collapse and congressional investigation: investigators subpoenaed Arthur Andersen witnesses over document destruction, the fired Andersen auditor refused to testify, federal authorities appeared to take control of Enron’s Houston headquarters, and creditors sought outside supervision of the company’s management. Democrats supported a GAO inquiry into White House meetings with energy-industry leaders, President Bush defended the administration’s handling of Enron, and a Senate panel requested Enron’s tax returns. Other developments included Long Island’s opening its power market to full retail competition, demands for larger Florida Power rate cuts, stronger New York consumer protections, planned Senate energy-bill debate, and proposed NRC licensing guidelines for Nevada’s nuclear-waste repository. The newsletter also covered gas-industry news, power prices, transmission and plant projects, renewable energy, nuclear safety, utility earnings, international electricity markets, and the financial and regulatory consequences of Enron and Arthur Andersen.

**Summary**

Michelle Bishop's 2024 article, "Envisioning Indigenous education sovereignty through story: Our education, our way," published in *The Australian Journal of Indigenous Education*, presents research from D'harawal Country in south-west Sydney. Writing as a Gamilaroi woman raised on D'harawal Country, Bishop positions the study within Indigenous, decolonising and relational theories and methodologies, deliberately departing from linear academic conventions so that the community holds the final word in the paper's closing story.

The research asked community members what education could look and feel like when grounded in Indigenous knowledges. Bishop notes that schools are documented sites of systemic harm for many Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander students, while Indigenous peoples have practised education successfully in these lands for tens of thousands of years. Rather than pursue school reform, the project prioritises envisioning Indigenous education sovereignty as an urgent decolonising imperative.

Participation involved 35 people in an anonymous online survey and face-to-face yarns with over 15 people; an exact participant figure is withheld to protect anonymity, and no demographic data are tabulated. The study draws on Indigenous futurities scholarship, including Goodyear-Ka'ōpua's three interwoven streams of Indigenous futurities, Indigenous futurisms and Indigenous resurgence, and on envisioning as a decolonising process centring sovereignty, futurities and non-linear time. Bishop's "layering the vision" method treats multiple truths as equally valid, cycles between ancestors and futures, and draws on the Kin and Country Framework to re-present findings through two creative outputs: intergenerational letters (containing named participants' quotes) and the story itself. Story is used as an amalgamation practice, with character details jumbled and quotes scattered so that anonymous voices are amplified while remaining unidentifiable.

Drawing on Indigenous scholarship by Behrendt, Phillips and Bunda, Kovach, Ober, Barnes and others, Bishop presents storytelling as a counter-narrative to colonisation that shifts power regimes, honours relational accountability and gives findings back to community.

The story "Our Education, Our Way" depicts a community yarn in which Aunty Kyra, children, parents, Nan Dot and Uncle discuss schooling's failures — culture treated as a compliance box, racism, Aboriginal students streamed into special classes, dispossession through education — and the knowledge of ancestors as teachers, scientists and innovators. Participants voice desires for Aboriginal-controlled and directed schools, learning on and from Country, Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander teachers, English as a second language, an open school for all, learning delivered when learners are ready, cultural belonging, strong identity alongside literacy and numeracy, and a reconciled Australia.

The speaker praises Darren for ensuring nothing happened while respecting Rod Brind’Amour. Dallas’s enthusiastic fan support helped him adjust to hockey life, and he hopes Hartford will embrace the team similarly. He describes its players as physically strong, defensively skilled, and capable of scoring, key traits for successful teams.

Crystal Palace recovered from a two-goal deficit to draw 2-2 with Leicester City, with Yohan Cabaye and Christian Benteke scoring after goals by Robert Huth and Jamie Vardy. Palace remain above the relegation zone on 35 points, two behind Leicester.

The passage describes Meb Faber’s simple S&P 500 trend-following strategy using a 200-day moving average: buy when price crosses above it and sell when it crosses below. The system relies only on price, ignoring news, earnings, valuations, sentiment, and interest rates. Backtests from 1960 reportedly avoided much of the 2008–09 financial crisis and limited losses during March 2020 to a 19% maximum drawdown. A monthly version using a 10-month average grew $100,000 to $4.7 million without dividends, with a 6.3% CAGR versus 7% for buy-and-hold and a 26% maximum drawdown in October 1987. Citing Paul Tudor Jones’s defensive use of the 200-day average, the passage concludes that the strategy works reasonably well, reduces drawdowns, and broadly keeps pace with long-term stock-market returns.

The passage urges Congress to make a special appropriation, directed by the Attorney General, to strengthen antitrust enforcement rather than treating tariff reduction as a remedy for trusts. Tariff changes would leave many large corporations unaffected and could ruin weaker domestic competitors; proper regulation is needed instead. It advocates preserving the protective-tariff principle and economic stability while allowing gradual, carefully considered adjustments to meet changing business needs without jeopardizing American workers’ wages and comfort. Reciprocity treaties, direct duty reductions, or legislation could be used to achieve these adjustments. Any changes should receive thorough examination by business experts, potentially through a commission reporting to Congress, with partisan considerations subordinated to national business interests and disruptions to prosperity and fixed economic policy avoided.

Elmatica is expanding its South African operations due to rising demand and a 245% sales increase compared with 2016. The company plans to establish a permanent local team to improve technical support and access to knowledge on technology, processes, and compliance; meanwhile, Swedish Country Manager Mikael Jansson is temporarily relocated from Stockholm.

The passage describes AGESA host-environment integration for UEFI, including call-out routing, build configuration, initialization phases, host services, and required platform call-outs. In the binary image model, all interface call-outs pass through a single host-implemented router whose address is loaded in the standard header. The router converts function identifiers into host procedure addresses and receives function-specific data plus configuration and header information.

UEFI execution spans SEC, PEI, DXE, and runtime phases, with separate 16-, 32-, and 64-bit build targets. MASM is used for 16-bit SEC code, while Microsoft Macro Assembler and C/C++ compilers are used for 32- and 64-bit development. Core files are organized into libraries, and platform-specific options are supplied through `<plat>Options.c`; no additional UEFI-specific user options are identified. The Addendum directory contains reference implementations and option files that host environments may copy and modify. UEFI control files must be integrated into platform build systems, and environment variables such as `AGESA_ROOT` and `AGESA_OptsDir` must identify the source and platform build directories.

Two core build methods are described: binary modules, where AMD provides source and build controls and calls are routed through a common entry point, and source integration, where the host incorporates AGESA files into its own ROM build. Selection proceeds by platform solution, build method, and individual build options. Platform examples include Danube and Maranello.

The PEI components divide AMD initialization among processor initialization, post-reset and memory initialization, and reset coordination. Processor initialization publishes early and post-init PPIs and a memory-information HOB. The post-reset module initializes memory, publishes completion PPIs, and coordinates with processor cleanup. The reset module checks other AMD PEIMs for warm-reset requests. In DXE, the CPU driver performs late initialization, generates informational tables, and publishes `AgesaDxeProtocol`; a separate GPU driver enables processor-VGA decoding only when requested through `PciIo`.

Host-provided stack routines establish a pre-memory execution stack in cache-as-RAM, map it globally, configure MTRRs on x86-64, and create the SEC-to-PEI handoff frame. `AMD_ENABLE_UEFI_STACK` must run on every processor core and preserve EBX; the corresponding removal routine runs on the BSP after main memory becomes available, disables cache-as-RAM, and flushes cache lines. These routines are not used by AArch64 APUs containing the PSP. During the cache-as-RAM period, the host must not modify SS, ESP, or cache controls.

Host service routines allocate and release AGESA structures, obtain DIMM data-eye results, report APIC and PCI addresses and execution-cache capacity, identify the current socket, die, and core, map addresses to DIMM locations, merge MMIO ranges, and read circular event logs. Structure allocation supports pre-memory heap, post-memory DRAM, and host-provided storage, and allocated structures must later be released.

Initialization entry points cover reset, early processor setup, memory initialization, environment handoff, late table generation, suspend-state saving, and resume restoration. `AmdInitReset` performs minimal processor initialization and allocates execution-cache regions under alignment, boundary, and capacity rules. `AmdInitEarly` performs fuller processor and power-management initialization and may request a warm reset. `AmdInitPost` brings memory online, transfers HOB and artifact data from pre-memory storage, and disables the temporary stack. Later routines move artifacts into protected memory, configure display hardware, generate ACPI and DMI tables, prepare processors for operating-system handoff, and save or restore silicon state for suspend and resume.

Required host call-outs include `AgesaAllocateBuffer`, `AgesaDeallocateBuffer`, and `AgesaResetSystem`. Allocation must provide the requested buffer size or more, may reserve host-specific space, and can reserve runtime-persistent UEFI memory for ACPI NVS or runtime-services data. Deallocation must account for any reserved space. The reset call-out must distinguish cold resets, which momentarily deassert PWRGOOD/PWROK, from warm resets, which assert `RESET#` without changing PWRGOOD/PWROK.

The paper examines the historical distinctions and connections among English as a Second Language (ESL), Bilingual Education (BE), and World Language (WL) teacher education in the United States. It argues that these fields developed separately under distinct political, ideological, and pedagogical conditions, including settler colonialism, assimilation, English-only schooling, and policies privileging English-speaking students. Language education should therefore be understood through the question of “language for whom,” especially in relation to minoritized emergent bilingual learners.

Using Valdés’ framework of language curricularization and a heteroglossic view of language, the authors describe their cross-disciplinary curriculum innovation at a Chicago teacher education institution. Phase 1 redesigned ESL methods around translanguaging, equity-oriented pedagogy, and diverse learners’ linguistic repertoires. Phase 2 created a combined ESL and WL methods course focused on Chinese, emphasizing multilingual and asset-based instruction across language program models and providing bilingual materials and field experiences. A planned third phase will redesign BE methods for WL and bilingual educators through linguistic autobiographies and landscape studies, critical-consciousness activities using drama-based pedagogy, and critical analysis of bilingual program models.

The paper identifies collaboration, external review, ongoing curriculum revision, and a guiding analytic framework as factors that supported the work. Constraints included flexible course sequencing, limited course access, and limited oversight of field experiences. The authors conclude that teacher education programs should not merge the fields into one path, but should bridge them through historical awareness, critical examination of language ideologies and curricular choices, culturally and linguistically responsive pedagogy, and preparation of critically conscious educators for diverse multilingual classrooms.

Construction crews on the $1.8 billion Las Vegas stadium exceeded hiring and subcontracting goals. Since November, 54% of 80,000 work hours were performed by minorities, women and veterans, versus a 38% goal; 18% of $509 million in subcontracts went to qualified small businesses, exceeding 15%. The 65,000-seat stadium remains on schedule for summer 2020.

Microsoft Corporation's Form 10-Q for the quarterly period ended March 31, 2015 (Commission File No. 0-14278) reports the company as a large accelerated filer with 8,089,575,277 shares of common stock outstanding at April 16, 2015.

**Results (unaudited, in millions):** Three-month revenue was $21,729 vs. $20,403 prior year; gross margin $14,568 vs. $14,425; operating income $6,594 vs. $6,974; net income $4,985 vs. $5,660; diluted EPS $0.61 vs. $0.68. Acquisitions included Nokia's Devices and Services business (April 2014) for $9.4 billion, with $5,456 of goodwill assigned to Phone Hardware, and Mojang (November 2014) for $2.5 billion cash, with $1.8 billion goodwill and $928 million of identifiable intangibles; ten other acquisitions totaled $556 million. The opening lecture of MIT’s 6.451 introduces a course on modern coding for communications, centered on achieving capacity over the additive white Gaussian noise (AWGN) channel. Course topics include algebraic block, convolutional, tail-biting, capacity-approaching, low-density parity-check, lattice, and trellis-coded modulation codes, along with their decoding algorithms. The instructor emphasizes rigorous prerequisite preparation in mathematical reasoning, including 6.450, and uses professor-written notes with suggested supplementary texts.

Weekly problem sets are due Wednesdays and account for 15% of the grade; the March 16 midterm accounts for one-third and the final one-half. Teaching assistant Ashish Khisti will guest lecture and hold office hours. Classes will be videotaped for OpenCourseWare.

The lecture frames communications design as maximizing digital data transmission over a given channel. An AWGN channel has additive white Gaussian noise and is characterized by signal power, noise power spectral density, bandwidth, or equivalently signal-to-noise ratio. For a telephone-line example with approximately 3,700 Hz of bandwidth and 37 dB SNR, Shannon capacity is about 42,000 bits per second, while an uncoded 32-QAM baseline can provide about 15,000 bits per second. Coding introduces constraints across long sequences, increasing separation between codewords and enabling reliable rates arbitrarily close to capacity.

The instructor also converts the continuous-time AWGN model to a discrete-time model using orthonormal PAM and a matched filter. This preserves the signal-to-noise ratio, yields no intersymbol interference and i.i.d. Gaussian noise, and establishes equivalent bandwidth and spectral-efficiency measures. Capacity in spectral efficiency is \(\log_2(1+\mathrm{SNR})\). The remaining introductory chapters are described as orientation, while later lectures will address practical capacity-approaching codes and other coding methods.

The article compares lump-sum investing, which puts all capital into the market at once, with dollar-cost averaging (DCA), which invests it gradually in installments. DCA and scale-in are described as essentially the same approach. Although DCA reduces volatility and fear through investing at different price levels, the article cites a September 2020 Morningstar study in which DCA beat lump-sum investing 27.8% of the time over 10-month periods but only 10% over 10-year periods. Lump-sum investing is presented as generally preferable because markets tend to rise over time, while idle cash loses purchasing power to inflation. DCA may still benefit investors prone to behavioral biases and fearful market timing.

Backtests use $60,000 in the S&P 500 from January 2000 through December 2019. Lump-sum investing produced $193,157, a 6.02% CAGR, with a 55% drawdown in 2008. DCA ended at $173,949 with a 5.5% CAGR. When 2010–2019 returns were placed before 2000–2010 returns, lump-sum results changed little, declining to a 5.93% CAGR, while DCA fell to $87,396 and a 1.9% CAGR because more capital was invested before the market’s rise. The article concludes that return sequences and randomness can materially affect DCA outcomes and recommends investing spare capital early when pursuing long-term investing.

The article reviews nine Vanguard ETFs presented as options for broad portfolio diversification: Vanguard Total World Bond ETF (BNDW), Total International Bond ETF (BNDX), Total Bond Market ETF (BND), Total Corporate Bond ETF (VTC), Global ex-U.S. Real Estate ETF (VNQI), Real Estate ETF (VNQ), Total International Stock ETF (VXUS), Total World Stock ETF (VT), and Total Stock Market ETF (VTI).

Together, the funds cover U.S. and international stocks, U.S. and global bonds, corporate bonds, and domestic and international real estate. The equity funds track broad market indexes and use sampling or full replication, while the bond funds provide exposure to global or U.S. investment-grade fixed income. Vanguard, founded by John Bogle, is described as a major U.S. fund provider whose ETFs are well suited to passive, hands-off investing because of their broad index strategies, low fees, and range of asset classes.

Individual ETF performance was backtested from each fund’s inception using a buy-and-hold strategy and dividend-adjusted prices. A diversified portfolio containing all nine ETFs was also backtested from 2007 to 2023, with annual rebalancing and dividend-adjusted quotes. An initial investment of 10,000 grew to 19,318. The portfolio’s returns were below the S&P 500 partly because of its bond allocation, while drawdowns were discussed as an important risk measure. The article concludes that these funds can provide broad exposure to global stock and bond markets but advises investors to review each prospectus and determine whether a fund fits their investment goals.

Weber State University canceled its 27th annual Unity Conference, themed “Redacted: Navigating the Complexities of Censorship,” after a student presenter was directed to remove references to DEI, diversity, equity and inclusion. Associate professor Sarah Herrmann refused to censor her research, other faculty withdrew, and organizers canceled the Oct. 2-3 event.

The conference was funded and organized by Student Access and Success rather than an academic unit, making its programming subject to Utah’s HB 261; academic-sponsored events are exempt. Guidance prohibited discussing practices HB 261 defines as prohibited discriminatory practices and language that takes sides on legislation or policies. University officials acknowledged that communication about the conference’s sponsorship and applicable rules had been unclear.

Herrmann said the directive was unexpected because most planning committee members were faculty and the sponsoring division was not apparent. Weber State is considering housing future Unity Conferences within Academic Affairs or a specific college to exempt them from HB 261. The legislation also followed state funding cuts that faculty said targeted programs disliked by lawmakers; Weber State closed its queer studies program, while enrollment in three related minors totaled fewer than 50 students.

The address reports continued national prosperity and progress in implementing measures from the previous legislative session. Frontier policy aimed to secure peace and friendship with Indian nations, protect settlements from unaffiliated raiders, preserve treaty rights, and draw Native peoples closer to the federal government. A proposed Creek land purchase failed because Creek deputies had been instructed not to sell, but a new treaty confirmed existing obligations to the United States and established trading houses and military posts within Creek territory.

British posts were evacuated after delays, and the United States took possession of Oswego, Niagara, Detroit, Michilimackina, and Fort Miami. Commissioners began surveying the disputed St. Croix River but adjourned until August 1797. Commissioners on both sides also prepared to address vessel captures and condemnations, while the British had appointed no counterparts for negotiations under the treaty’s sixth article.

Under the Spanish treaty, an American commissioner began traveling to the Natchez to survey the boundary with East and West Florida, and troops were ordered to occupy posts from which Spanish forces would withdraw. Spain had appointed a boundary commissioner but had not appointed one to address American citizens’ vessel-capture claims. Agents were appointed to protect American seamen in Britain and the West Indies; the British agent declined the position, leaving the matter to the U.S. minister in London, while early reports indicated that the West Indies agency was beneficial.

All American citizens imprisoned in Algiers were liberated, completing the principal objective of negotiations there despite financial disadvantages caused by the European war. Measures were underway for treaties with Tunis and Tripoli.

The address argues that neutral commerce requires an organized naval force and urges the gradual establishment of a navy to protect Mediterranean trade. It also recommends public support for manufactures essential to wartime needs when private domestic production is unlikely, continued encouragement of agriculture through information boards, premiums, and small financial assistance, and the creation of a national university and military academy. Legislative revision of officers’ compensation is urged to avoid restricting public office to wealthy individuals.

French cruisers and agents have damaged American trade in the West Indies, and further disruption is considered possible. Nevertheless, the speaker maintains a desire for cordial relations with the French Republic, provided the United States safeguards its rights and honor; a detailed message on the matter is reserved.

An estimate of appropriations for the coming year is to be submitted. National revenues continue to improve, and further measures to extinguish the public debt are supported. The militia and security of the nation’s harbors are also briefly raised. The address closes by congratulating the country on the success of its republican government and invoking continued divine protection for the United States.

An April 23, 2001 energy-industry news compilation focused on Enron, electricity markets and related companies.

Bloomberg reported that PG&E CEO Robert Glynn’s prediction of falling California electricity prices led him to embrace deregulation and expand through acquisitions into power generation, energy trading and natural gas. Wholesale prices subsequently rose sixfold, while PG&E could not pass higher costs to customers. PG&E’s Pacific Gas & Electric unit filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy, described as the largest utility bankruptcy in U.S. history. PG&E reported a $3.36 billion net loss for 2000 after a $4.11 billion power-purchase charge, and its stock and bonds fell sharply. Creditors may seek assets from the company’s National Energy unit, and experts questioned whether PG&E improperly transferred utility funds to its parent.

The Associated Press reported that Tri-State Generation & Transmission proposed a $1.3 billion, 1,200-megawatt coal-fired plant in Bent County, Colorado, twice the size of any other planned Colorado plant. The utility said coal power could cost as little as 1.5 cents per kilowatt-hour, but environmental groups argued that cleaner wind power near the site was a better alternative.

Saudi Oil Minister Ali al-Naimi was scheduled to meet U.S. Energy Secretary Spencer Abraham to discuss oil prices, OPEC’s output cuts and Saudi gas-development contracts involving ExxonMobil, Chevron, Enron/Oxy and other companies.

In India, Enron-owned Dabhol Power Company faced a payment dispute after the Maharashtra State Electricity Board defaulted on 2.26 billion rupees. Lenders met in London before a DPC board decision on whether to terminate the project. The $3 billion, 2,184-megawatt project has 740 megawatts operating and a 1,444-megawatt second phase under construction. Maharashtra sought federal support for the state utility. Lenders said four percent approval could authorize a preliminary termination notice, followed by a six-month period to seek a revised agreement.

Reuters also reported that developers of the 1,000-megawatt Mangalore coal project, promoted by China Light & Power and the Tatas, planned to halve its capacity because of weak demand and the state electricity board’s finances, with the second phase delayed three to four years. ONGC disputed Enron’s claims that the Moon Prospect well at Tapti contained substantial recoverable gas reserves. A Mangalore civic group also asked Karnataka Power Transmission Corporation officials to reconcile contradictory statements about shortages, production, transmission losses and power costs. In Spain, the government sought stricter electricity-market rules to increase transparency, competition and market entry, challenging the dominance of Endesa and Iberdrola.

The Wall Street Journal’s Asia-Pacific section reported South Korea’s Kookmin Bank and Housing & Commercial Bank were finalizing a merger to create the country’s largest financial institution, Japan was investigating polyester-fiber dumping by South Korean and Taiwanese producers, and Dabhol shareholders would consider the project’s future. Other briefs covered a postponed Chunghwa Telecom share offering, a further Pakistan Telecommunications stake sale, a fifth Taiwanese rate cut, possible steel-industry cooperation, and Time magazine’s apology over an image of the prophet Muhammad.

Eilish McCready, 25, founded the Glasgow theatre school Fearless to provide inclusive, small-group drama classes focused on children’s personal development rather than performances or auditions. The classes welcome confident, shy and autistic children and use drama to build confidence, social skills, communication and awareness of personal space without performance pressure. McCready runs the business while drama teachers lead classes. Lizanne Conway says her two older autistic sons enjoy the inclusive, stress-free sessions and have gained confidence. Lisa Byrne says her formerly shy daughter Rua now sings in front of others and has started a YouTube channel. Classes are held at Studio 93 in Glasgow.

Enron shares fell 4.2% to $19.79 on October 24, 2001, extending a decline of more than 40% for the week and leaving them far below the $80 level reached earlier in the year. The company had reported a $618 million third-quarter loss, including $1.01 billion in write-offs, and disclosed a $1.2 billion reduction in shareholder equity after terminating transactions with a partnership led by CFO Andrew Fastow. The SEC opened an informal inquiry into Enron’s dealings with LJM2 and LJM Cayman. Documents indicated that Fastow and several other Enron officials received millions of dollars from the partnerships, which involved billions of dollars in Enron assets and stock. Fastow had resigned from the partnerships amid criticism, and Enron subsequently ended the relationships.

During an investor conference call, Chairman and CEO Kenneth Lay and Fastow defended the transactions, cited procedures intended to protect shareholders and asserted that Enron had adequate liquidity. Both declined to discuss details because of the SEC inquiry and shareholder lawsuits. Analysts challenged Enron’s limited disclosure and the complexity of its finances; Goldman Sachs analyst David Fleischer said the disclosures created an appearance that Enron was hiding something, although he continued to recommend the stock. Lay also said Arthur Andersen had found that no write-down was required for the Marlin financing vehicle.

Treasurer Ben Glisan said Enron could repay about $3.3 billion in notes issued by Marlin and Osprey entities and due within 20 months without issuing more shares. Asset sales were expected to generate at least $2.2 billion by the end of 2002, including $1.55 billion from the planned sale of Portland General Electric. If proceeds were insufficient, however, Enron could issue as much as $1 billion in stock, diluting its roughly 850 million outstanding shares. Enron had $3.35 billion in bank credit lines, sought a $750 million loan arranged by Citigroup, and warned that rating-related provisions in financing vehicles could also dilute shareholders. High options volatility made Enron’s January $20 straddles attractive to sellers at premiums of about $750, though sellers faced significant losses if the stock moved sharply.

Other reports covered Enron-related international developments. AES asked India’s prime minister to intervene in disputes with the Orissa state government, while British Gas sought operating rights for Indian oil and gas interests bought from Enron by offering ONGC Brazilian assets and a cash settlement. Shipping analysts warned that delayed LNG projects and a 37% expansion of the tanker fleet by the end of 2004 could create oversupply.

The broader stock market ended slightly lower despite weak corporate earnings, with the Dow down 0.39% and the Nasdaq down 0.21%; Enron reached a 52-week intraday low. A House stimulus proposal would have provided Enron with a $254 million tax refund, while Senate Democrats offered a smaller alternative focused on unemployment benefits and health coverage. A law firm also announced an investigation of Enron shareholder claims covering January 18, 2000, through October 17, 2001.

Winter fishing favors offshore sailfish, dolphin, wahoo, and kingfish using live bait and various techniques. Inshore, find jack and tarpon schools with a fish finder; use shrimp or clams for sheepshead.

A Nature study (posted October 8, 2025; doi:10.1038/d41586-025-02974-0) provides large-scale evidence that skewed online media trains AI chatbots to see older women as less employable. Researchers D. Guilbeault, S. Delecourt and B.S. Desikan analyzed nearly 1.4 million online images and videos, ran text analysis with nine language models, and conducted a randomized controlled experiment with over 450 participants. More than 6,000 coders consistently judged women in images and videos as younger than men, most strongly in prestigious occupations, while textual analysis linked less prestigious jobs to younger women and senior roles to older men. Participants who uploaded pictures of female workers estimated others in the same occupation as two years younger; those uploading pictures of male workers estimated them as more than half a year older. ChatGPT, trained on this media, generated nearly 17,300 resumes per gender group across 54 occupations, portraying women as younger and less experienced and ranking them lower. The bias contradicts U.S. Census data showing male and female employees are roughly the same age; Guilbeault suggests it helps explain the glass ceiling, and sociologist Ana Macanovic cautions that wider AI use may entrench such biases.

Michael Gayed’s strategy rotates weekly between the S&P 500 (SPY) and utilities ETF (XLU) based on each asset’s past performance. Utilities’ risk aversion, low beta, and sensitivity to interest rates may help them outperform during falling-rate periods and underperform when rates are expected to rise.

Gayed reported annual compounded returns of 13.1% since 1929, with the strongest results occurring before publication. A dividend- and split-adjusted backtest beginning in 1999 produced a low CAGR; the strategy underperformed SPY but performed similarly after adjusting for volatility. From 1999 to March 2014, it returned 6.7% annually versus 4.6% for buy-and-hold. Since publication, however, it lagged SPY by more than five percentage points annually (5.1% versus 10.4%) and did not recover from the 2020 crash. Since 2021, its maximum drawdown was -23.6%, close to SPY’s -23.9%. The strategy has performed well historically but underperformed after publication, though the passage says it may be too early to conclude that it stopped working.

Researchers presented work at an ACS meeting on converting grape pomace into antioxidants, oils and dietary fibers for supplements, pharmaceuticals, cosmetics and food. The wine industry produces about 14 million tons of pomace annually, which can pollute water, acidify soil and attract pests. Extraction methods remove pesticides and yield antioxidant phenolic compounds that inhibit lipid oxidation in fatty foods and reduced acrylamide in potato chips by 60% in an earlier study. Other research examined pomace polyphenols against E. coli and Salmonella and as supplements affecting piglet gut health, survival and growth.

The study tested BNT162b1, BNT162b2, BNT162b2SA, and placebo across Phase 1, Phase 2/3, and Phase 3 booster groups. Initial doses were observer-blinded, meaning healthcare staff knew the assignment while participants and researchers did not; later, most vaccine and booster doses were open-label, although some reassigned booster groups remained blinded. The study ran at 153 locations in six countries from April 29, 2020, to February 10, 2023, with participants enrolled for up to 26 months and the full study lasting about 33 months.

Participants were healthy adults and adolescents aged 12 or older who had neither prior COVID-19 infection nor a prior COVID-19 vaccine. Phase 1 enrolled 195 people aged 19–82, all of whom received a study vaccine. Phase 2/3 enrolled 46,406 people aged 12–91; 46,297 received a study vaccine, and 1,156 left during the blinded period. In a separate group, 330 of 333 participants assigned BNT162b2SA received it; 102 of that group did not complete the study, most commonly because they could not be reached.

After two 30-µg doses of BNT162b2, the vaccine was 95% effective at preventing COVID-19 from seven days after Dose 2 through December 3, 2020, compared with placebo. Results were similar regardless of prior COVID-19 infection, and protection was observed in participants aged 16 or older. Antibody responses one month after a BNT162b2 booster were comparable to responses after Dose 2 against the original strain. A BNT162b2SA booster produced Beta-variant responses comparable to original-strain responses after two BNT162b2 doses. In participants without prior BNT162b2 or COVID-19, two BNT162b2SA doses produced Beta-variant responses comparable to original-strain responses after two BNT162b2 doses. Researchers considered these findings unlikely to be due to chance.

Injection-site reactions and systemic events within seven days were generally well tolerated, temporary, and mild or moderate; injection-site pain, tiredness, and headache were common. A few Phase 1 participants had temporary lymphocyte reductions one to three days after Dose 1, which resolved by days 6–8; none had low lymphocytes at days 6–8 after Dose 2. BNT162b1 and BNT162b2 doses of 10, 20, and 30 µg were generally well tolerated, while the 100-µg BNT162b1 dose was stopped after Dose 1 because of reactions. The 30-µg BNT162b2 vaccine was selected for Phase 2/3. Fewer than 1% of participants in either the BNT162b2 or placebo group left the blinded Phase 2/3 period because of medical problems, and most reported problems were mild or moderate.

Serious medical problems were uncommon, and no single serious problem occurred in at least 1% of any reported group. Investigators did not believe Phase 1 cases were vaccine-related and generally did not consider Phase 3 booster cases related, though a small number of serious events after BNT162b2 were judged possibly related. No Phase 1 participant died. During Phase 2/3, deaths occurred in 85 of 23,141 initial BNT162b2 recipients, 62 of 21,371 placebo recipients who later received BNT162b2, and 23 of 23,141 participants who received only placebo. Investigators did not believe the deaths were caused by BNT162b2. No BNT162b2SA recipient in Phase 3 died.

Cassini completed the first of five close Saturn flybys, which will make it the first probe of Saturn’s atmosphere before a final plunge on September 15. A possible 120-mile lower pass on its second flyby could gather atmospheric, temperature, auroral, vortex and chemical data and help determine Saturn’s day length. Over its 20-year mission, Cassini spent 13 years at Saturn and made 127 Titan flybys, preparing it for these upper-atmosphere passes. Low fuel and concerns about crashing into Titan or Enceladus prompted the mission’s planned end. Cassini will bid farewell to Titan on September 11 before descending into Saturn.

The patent disclosure describes improved ultrasonic and electrosurgical devices and generators for smart surgical environments. Three methods apply power to an ultrasonic transducer, measure its impedance, compare it with a stored reference value, classify the impedance, and use the classification to characterize the electromechanical system’s state, end-effector function, or contacted tissue before adjusting power.

A computer-implemented surgical system includes a hub communicating with visualization, robotic, handheld instrument, and cloud-based systems. The hub enclosure accepts interchangeable generator, smoke-evacuation, and suction/irrigation modules. Docked modules use power and data contacts and wired or wireless communication to coordinate ultrasonic, bipolar RF, and monopolar RF energy and manage associated lines.

The imaging system supports interchangeable camera and light-source modules, including multispectral imaging, and coordinates displays inside and outside the sterile field. A surgical data network connects operating-room devices through hubs, switches, and routers to local or cloud systems for data transfer and processing. The disclosure also incorporates numerous related patent applications and catalogs figures concerning ultrasonic impedance and temperature control, tissue and vessel detection, electrosurgical circuitry, instrument sensors, generators, modular hubs, imaging, and cloud-connected surgical networks.

Jack Hare introduces plasma diagnostics as methods for inferring plasma density, temperature, velocity, and other properties indirectly from physical effects, since these quantities cannot be measured directly. Because plasma behavior is often unintuitive, diagnostics rely heavily on plasma physics, electromagnetism, plasma waves, and mathematics. The course assumes prior study of 22.611 and draws on Francis Chen’s *Introduction to Plasma Physics*.

Good diagnostics are essential to plasma experiments and fusion development. In the ZETA pinch, neutron bursts were initially mistaken for thermonuclear fusion, but their anisotropy and the plasma’s low temperature showed that they came from MHD instabilities. The resulting development of Thomson scattering enabled confirmation of the reported kiloelectronvolt temperatures in early tokamaks. Likewise, the National Ignition Facility initially relied on inadequate diagnostics and produced barely measurable neutron signals; improved diagnostics later helped the team understand the experiment and achieve ignition.

Diagnostics are relevant to experimenters, computational researchers, and theorists. Experimentalists need to understand measurement uncertainties and spatial or temporal limitations. Simulations can use diagnostic measurements to validate codes and reduce large datasets to comparable observables. Theorists should scrutinize reported values, understand how and where they were measured, and formulate predictions that experimentalists can test clearly.

Although theorists might request the position and velocity of every particle at every point and time, this full distribution function is impractical. Diagnostics instead provide moments such as density, average velocity, higher velocity moments, and magnetic fields. Measurements are generally sparse and may cover only a point, an image, or a limited region. Optical measurements are often line-integrated, combining emissions from hot and cold regions and potentially including absorption and radiation transport. Instrument response functions, spatial or frequency resolution, and dependence on imperfect atomic or model data further limit interpretation.

The course emphasizes enduring diagnostic principles rather than rapidly changing implementations, while acknowledging that new techniques continue to emerge. An interactive exercise maps diverse plasma systems by density, temperature, and magnetic field and identifies their diagnostics. Examples include Spark, DIII-D, NIF, Z-machine magnetic reconnection, Columbia’s HBT and CNT devices, inertial confinement fusion, Hall thrusters, helicons, pulsed-power systems, magnetized liner inertial fusion, and non-equilibrium aerospace plasmas. Techniques discussed include Langmuir probes, interferometry, bolometers, spectroscopy, Thomson scattering, neutron diagnostics, radiation imaging, correlation electron-cyclotron emission, shadowgraphy, and magnetic-field measurements based on polarized light or neutron anisotropy.
The Rams seek Jaguars’ permission to interview interim coach Doug Marrone, who went 1-1 and could be retained permanently. Marrone previously improved Buffalo from 6-10 to 9-7 before leaving.

Amazon.com, Inc.’s unaudited Form 10-Q for the quarter ended March 31, 2015 reported net sales of $22.717 billion, up 15% from $19.741 billion a year earlier. Product sales were $17.084 billion and service sales were $5.633 billion. Operating income increased to $255 million from $146 million, but a $234 million non-operating loss, $71 million tax provision, and $7 million equity-method loss produced a $57 million net loss, or $0.12 per share, compared with $108 million of net income in 2014.

The company began reporting North America, International, and AWS as separate segments. North America recorded $13.406 billion of sales and $517 million of operating income; International recorded $7.745 billion of sales and a $76 million operating loss; AWS recorded $1.566 billion of sales and $265 million of operating income.

Cash and equivalents were $10.237 billion and marketable securities were $3.544 billion at March 31, 2015. Q1 operating, investing, and financing activities used $1.499 billion, $1.847 billion, and $652 million, respectively. For the trailing twelve months, operating cash flow was $7.845 billion and non-GAAP free cash flow was $3.161 billion. Amazon also reported $31.749 billion of contractual commitments, made acquisitions totaling $341 million, and had $9.729 billion of debt face value with no borrowings under its $2 billion credit facility.

The filing described patent and wage-and-hour litigation, $726 million of tax contingencies, an IRS transfer-pricing proposal seeking approximately $1.5 billion of additional federal tax, and proposed French tax assessments of approximately $250 million. Amazon disputed the relevant allegations and stated it intended to defend itself vigorously.

Tesla grew from a company founded in 2003 into a leading high-performance electric-vehicle manufacturer, launching the Roadster in 2008, Model S in 2012, Model X in 2015, and mass-market Model 3 in 2016. The company also developed autopilot software, battery gigafactories, the Powerwall home battery, and solar-energy operations, acquiring SolarCity in a $2.1 billion stock deal in 2016.

Despite rising revenue and stock value, Tesla consistently reported operating losses and negative operating cash flow while investing heavily in factories, charging stations, and sales and service infrastructure. It repeatedly raised equity and debt after its 2010 IPO; by 2017, debt totaled about $9.63 billion, while shares outstanding had increased from 131.4 million in 2015 to 168.8 million. Year-end 2017 figures included $3.37 billion in cash, $23.02 billion in total liabilities, and $4.24 billion in stockholders’ equity. Revenue rose from $4.05 billion in 2015 to $11.76 billion in 2017, and EBITDA was nearly break-even, but EBIT remained a $1.63 billion loss.

Model 3 production began in July 2017, but Tesla repeatedly reduced forecasts and delayed reaching 5,000 vehicles per week, a rate considered necessary for positive cash flow. As quarterly cash burn accelerated, analysts questioned Tesla’s ability to finance expansion; one estimated it might need more than $10 billion in external capital and debt refinancing by 2020. Musk said Tesla would not require an equity or debt raise in 2018 beyond standard credit lines. The case therefore examined whether Tesla could obtain enough capital to survive the Model 3 production ramp, echoing Musk’s April 2018 April Fool’s Day tweet that the company had gone bankrupt.

The passage describes NVIDIA’s Turing GPU architecture and its TU102, TU104, and TU106 chips. Turing was the first GPU architecture to use GDDR6 memory, featuring redesigned SerDes/RF interfaces, improved signal training, and extensive clock gating. It delivers 14 Gbps signaling and a 20% power-efficiency improvement over Pascal’s GDDR5X, while package and board optimization reduced signal crosstalk by 40%. TU102 has 6 MB of L2 cache, twice GP102’s 3 MB. GDDR6 bandwidth gains and improved lossless memory compression provide approximately 50% higher effective bandwidth on the RTX 2080 Ti than on the Pascal-based 1080 Ti.

Turing’s display engine supports DisplayPort 1.4a, 8K output at 60 Hz, DSC 1.2, two 8K displays, USB-C, and native HDR processing with BT.2100 tone mapping. Its NVENC encoder supports H.265 8K encoding at 30 fps and provides HEVC and H.264 bitrate savings, while NVDEC supports HEVC 4:4:4 and 10- or 12-bit VP9 HDR video. The encoder also offers higher quality than fast x264 software encoding with substantially lower CPU use.

For VR, Turing supports USB-C and VirtualLink, an open standard that delivers display, power, and data through one connector while supporting DisplayPort and USB tracking links. Turing TU102 and TU104 also replace MIO and PCIe links for SLI transfers with second-generation NVLink. TU102 has two x8 links and TU104 one, each providing 25 GB/s per direction; Turing supports two-way SLI but not three- or four-way configurations.

Turing introduces a Hybrid Rendering model combining rasterization, real-time ray tracing, AI, and simulation. Dedicated RT Cores in each SM handle BVH traversal and ray-triangle intersection testing, freeing shader multiprocessors for other work. Combined with denoising and efficient acceleration structures, this enables real-time ray-traced reflections, refractions, shadows, and ambient occlusion. NVIDIA reports more than 10 gigarays per second on Turing, versus approximately 1.1 gigarays per second in software on Pascal, making ray tracing about ten times faster. Ray tracing works with NVIDIA RTX, OptiX, Microsoft DXR, and the forthcoming Vulkan ray-tracing API. Bounding Volume Hierarchies reduce intersection tests through hierarchical bounding-box traversal, and denoising allows fewer rays per pixel while maintaining image quality.

NVIDIA NGX is a deep-learning technology stack that uses Turing Tensor Cores and Neural Services for client-side AI applications. Deep Learning Super-Sampling (DLSS) is trained against 64-times-supersampled reference images, producing quality similar to temporal anti-aliasing with roughly half the shading work; together with Tensor Cores, it enables the RTX 2080 Ti to reach twice the performance of the GTX 1080 Ti in the cited UE4 test. DLSS 2X combines final-resolution inputs with a larger network to approximate 64-times-supersampled output. Other NGX features include Inpainting for replacing image content, AI Slow-Mo for generating interpolated frames, and AI Super Rez for 2x, 4x, or 8x image and video upscaling.

Turing also adds task and mesh shaders, using cooperative thread groups to reduce CPU draw-call bottlenecks, select object levels of detail dynamically, and support specialized geometry manipulation. Variable Rate Shading can assign different rates to each 16×16 screen region, supporting content-adaptive, motion-adaptive, and foveated rendering while allowing increased MSAA sampling where needed. Texture Space Shading stores appearance results in texture space, decoupling shading from visibility sampling and enabling reuse across frames and stereo views. Multi-View Rendering processes up to four views per hardware pass and up to 32 at the API level, expanding Pascal’s simultaneous multi-projection support and improving VR rendering. Turing also adds bindless constant-buffer and unordered-access views and supports Tier 2 resource heaps.

Full TU104 contains 48 SMs, 3,072 CUDA Cores, 368 Tensor Cores, 48 RT Cores, a 256-bit memory interface, and 13.6 billion transistors. TU106 contains 36 SMs, 2,304 CUDA Cores, 288 Tensor Cores, and 36 RT Cores; it supports neither NVLink nor SLI and powers the GeForce RTX 2070. The Turing-based Tesla T4 is designed for data-center, enterprise, and edge inference, with 40 SMs, 2,560 CUDA Cores, 320 Tensor Cores, a 256-bit interface, and 320 GB/s memory bandwidth.

RTX-OPS is introduced as a workload-based metric for hybrid rendering. It weights Tensor operations at 20%, FP32 operations at 80%, RT operations at 40%, and INT32 operations at 28% of their peak rates; the cited RTX 2080 Ti configuration produces a total of 78 RTX-OPS.

Hurricane Harvey may have damaged as many as a dozen wildlife habitats along the Texas Gulf Coast, including marshes. At Attwater Prairie Chicken Refuge, about 60 endangered prairie chickens were present before the storm, and as few as 10 are believed to have survived. Oyster beds sustained losses, while bottlenose dolphins may have been injured by freshwater inflows.

The study introduces an ascending–descending method for identifying public transit hierarchies from actual smart-card travel patterns without assuming spatial homogeneity. Transfers before and after half of each trip’s total distance are classified as ascending and descending, respectively. Transfer-rate matrices, hierarchy distances, and rescaled average hierarchical values are then used to compare modes and analyze interzonal and intrazonal structures separately.

Applied to T-money data collected on November 12, 2019, for Seoul, Gyeonggi, and Incheon, the method analyzed 10,264,700 filtered trip chains across walking, community bus, urban bus, intercity bus, light rail, and metro. Within Seoul, ascending and descending hierarchies were nearly identical: walking, community bus, urban bus, light rail, and metro ranked in that order. For trips between Seoul and Gyeonggi or Incheon, the order was community bus, urban bus, light rail, metro, and intercity bus. Including intercity buses relatively lowered the hierarchy values of community buses, urban buses, and metro. Regional differences were also found: intercity bus and metro changed relative positions between regions, while urban bus ranked lower in Gyeonggi and Incheon than in Seoul.

A jury found the Morehouse Parish Police Jury liable for the death of 15-year-old Michael Hill, who drowned with another teenager when 16-year-old Bradd Rudolph crashed through a “T” intersection into Bayou Bartholomew. Rudolph had consumed alcohol, was driving approximately 65 miles per hour at night in foggy, rainy conditions, and failed to see the intersection’s stop sign.

The police jury knew the intersection was dangerous, including that double-arrow warning signs had been repeatedly knocked down or stolen, but failed to maintain adequate warnings. The appellate court held that this breach of duty was a substantial contributing cause of the accident. It amended the fault allocation from 20% to the police jury and 80% to Rudolph to 35% and 65%, respectively. The court affirmed the $150,000 general-damages award, finding it low but not an abuse of discretion, and ordered defendants to pay costs.

This study assessed open-access status and the potential for green open access among clinical trial results publications from German university medical centers. Using the validated IntoValue cohort, 1,897 publications issued from 2010–2020 were analyzed. Unpaywall classified publications as gold, hybrid, bronze, green, or closed access, while Shareyourpaper identified article-specific self-archiving permissions.

Overall, 54% of publications were openly accessible, while 46% were closed access. Of the 871 closed-access publications, 85% had sufficient information to determine a self-archiving permission; all 736 permitted archiving an accepted or published version in an institutional repository. Embargoes ranged from zero to 24 months, with most publications having a 12-month embargo. Nevertheless, only 16% of otherwise closed-access publications with a self-archiving permission had actually been made accessible in a repository, indicating substantial unrealized potential.

The authors identify awareness concerns, copyright uncertainty, lack of mandates, and German institutional and legal context as factors contributing to limited uptake. They note that Shareyourpaper and Unpaywall can automate permissions checking, deposit workflows, and targeted interventions at scale. Limitations include reliance on potentially incomplete or outdated API data, exclusion of some alternative self-archiving routes, and uncertainty about the versions and locations of existing green OA deposits.

Natural gas settled at $3.27/MMBtu, edging higher but confined to a descending wedge capped since March. Europe’s LNG pivot boosted U.S. exports, but North American oversupply weighed on prices while seasonal softness and Canadian supply shocks kept volatility elevated.
U.S. stocks fell sharply as the 10-year Treasury yield hit 3% and Alphabet dropped on high spending, while Canadian gold and materials gains led by Barrick cushioned the TSX decline.

The passage criticizes Ontario Premier Kathleen Wynne for telling students at Humber College that people resembling her would vote if they did not. The author argues that older white voters’ interests should not be assumed to conflict with those of young people and minorities, calling Wynne’s remark ageist, racist, and divisive identity politics. Although older people vote at higher rates and visible minorities at lower rates than some surveys report for “other Canadians,” the author says turnout should not be increased by demonizing another group. Wynne should instead engage all groups in voting and promote inclusion and fairness.

Global stock markets rose after Federal Reserve Chair Janet Yellen signaled that the U.S. central bank could raise interest rates as soon as March, citing a strengthening job market and modest inflation. The unexpectedly hawkish comments lifted bond yields and supported bank shares. European indexes gained modestly, and Asian markets finished mostly higher. China’s consumer and wholesale inflation also edged up, raising concerns about tighter monetary policy or credit, though analysts did not expect an immediate change in the People’s Bank of China’s course. The dollar strengthened against the yen and weakened slightly against the euro, while U.S. and Brent crude prices fell.

Gary Gensler introduces MIT’s course on blockchain, money, and finance, framing it as an exploration of whether blockchain could catalyze change in financial systems. He traces internet commerce’s early inability to transfer money online, the development of cryptography and public-key systems, and Satoshi Nakamoto’s 2008 proposal for peer-to-peer electronic cash without a trusted third party. He describes blockchain as time-stamped, auditable append-only databases secured through cryptography, hash functions, digital signatures, and consensus protocols that address Byzantine Generals and trust-cost problems. He defines blockchain technology as verifiably moving data across decentralized networks, with economic trade-offs between consensus costs and reduced reliance on centralized intermediaries.

Students discuss money’s roles as a medium of exchange, store of value, and unit of account, as well as finance’s role in moving, allocating, and pricing money and transferring risk. Gensler highlights financial-sector challenges including crises, centralized intermediaries, legacy payment systems, counterparty risk, fees, and financial exclusion. He identifies potential blockchain opportunities in payments, central-bank digital currencies, trading, venture capital, and initial coin offerings, while noting limitations involving scalability, performance, privacy, security, interoperability, and governance.

The lecture distinguishes permissioned blockchains, whose participants and nodes are controlled, from permissionless systems such as Bitcoin, and surveys crypto-finance scale, regulation, illicit activity, financial stability, investor protection, incumbents, and startups. The course will cover fundamentals, economics, and financial use cases using critical reasoning to distinguish claims from hype, with individual papers and team projects. Gensler concludes that blockchain offers a peer-to-peer alternative for reducing trust costs but may still be only one possible mechanism, and may improve finance if it lowers costs, expands access, and democratizes financial services.

Digital laggards typically restrict data access, hoard data as a source of power, and store information in departmental silos behind burdensome request processes. They often favor individual business judgment and leadership expertise over data-driven decisions, sometimes using data merely to justify choices already made. Resource shortages can also limit data use. Their aspirational goals are often insufficiently grounded in data, causing employees to avoid measurement and focus on qualitative evidence of effort and adherence to process, which can inhibit innovation. Their goals are also weakly connected to company strategy, contributing to organizational misalignment.

Digital leaders embrace measurement as a way to set meaningful objectives, track progress, and learn. They encourage relevant data collection, detailed metrics, continuous performance tracking, and evaluations such as 360-degree reviews. Clear goals can provide structure while allowing autonomy, creativity, experimentation, and calculated risk-taking. In the research, 88% of digital leaders had standardized APIs supporting data flow across departments, compared with 27% of laggards. A transforming retailer implemented real-time sales dashboards that automatically distributed retailer data three times daily, enabling leaders to make faster decisions about inventory, marketing, supply chains, and other operations.

Digital leaders connect objectives to strategy through transparent methods and often combined top-down and bottom-up goal-setting. Shared goals and common data models support vertical alignment between employees and company priorities and horizontal collaboration across functions. However, excessive instrumentation and analysis can complicate simple decisions and displace human intuition and logical judgment.

Across most digital leaders, data culture is a central business mechanism that aligns leadership beliefs, stated values, and daily behavior. Laggards may recognize the importance of data-driven culture but struggle to change entrenched habits, build skills, and maintain sufficient top-down focus. Changing mindsets and behaviors remains a major challenge in digital transformation, though organizations can successfully transform and mature leaders still identify room for improvement.

Organizations commonly fall into four maturity patterns: data novices recognize the need but lack enabling culture and systems; insight-ready organizations encourage experimentation but lack advanced analytical architecture; tech-enabled organizations possess data and technology but do not consistently foster experimentation; and data-reliant organizations overdepend on data in ways that can discourage critical thinking. Each can build on its strengths through targeted actions toward a strong data culture.

Renewed psychedelic research supports drug-facilitated psychotherapy. Six pooled Phase II MDMA-therapy trials found 54% of patients no longer met PTSD criteria, supporting FDA breakthrough designation. A Phase 3 multisite study confirmed MDMA-assisted therapy’s safety and efficacy for severe PTSD, significantly reducing symptoms versus placebo plus therapy.

Amazon.com, Inc. filed a Form 8-K dated January 28, 2016, reporting its fourth-quarter and year-ended December 31, 2015 financial results. The filing includes the results announcement press release and information regarding non-GAAP financial measures as Exhibits 99.1 and 99.2.

Exchange-rate movements significantly affect Ireland’s importers, exporters, tourism businesses, holidaymakers and SMEs. The euro’s weakness against the dollar has attracted record US visitors, while sterling’s weakness has discouraged UK travel. Since Brexit, sterling has risen from 76p to nearly 91p against the euro, and the euro has strengthened from $1.05 to $1.18 amid expectations of reduced quantitative easing and higher eurozone rates. The article says ECB policy favors a low euro to support exports and Italy’s recovery, though forecasts remain uncertain because of ECB decisions and Brexit. UK imports are currently cheap, but firms should lock in gains; UK exporters face pressure and should hedge by taking costs in sterling.

Cleveland traded Joe Flacco and a 2026 sixth-round pick to Cincinnati for a 2026 fifth-round pick, leaving rookies Shedeur Sanders and Dillon Gabriel as the Browns’ only active quarterbacks. Coach Kevin Stefanski said he would delay deciding Sanders’ backup role while considering roster needs, practice reps and player development. Sanders, the 144th pick in this year’s draft, had served as the No. 3 and emergency quarterback and was listed as No. 2 on the unofficial depth chart after the trade. Stefanski also declined to say whether Bailey Zappe would be added to the active roster. Flacco started the first four games before Gabriel made his first career start in last Sunday’s 21-17 loss. Wide receiver Jerry Jeudy praised Sanders’ professionalism, while Deshaun Watson remained on the physically unable to perform list rehabbing an Achilles injury.

A University of Michigan study using a nationally representative poll of more than 2,000 U.S. adults found that 21% of women and 10% men ages 50–64 meet criteria for ultra-processed food addiction, compared with 12% of women and 4% of men ages 65–80. Researchers used the modified Yale Food Addiction Scale 2.0 to assess symptoms such as cravings, unsuccessful attempts to reduce consumption, withdrawal, and avoidance of social activities.

Addiction was associated with overweight status, fair or poor mental and physical health, and social isolation. Overweight women were more than 11 times as likely and overweight men 19 times as likely to meet addiction criteria than those reporting a healthy weight. Those reporting isolation were more than three times as likely.

Researchers suggested that 1980s marketing of low-fat and diet-focused processed foods to women, combined with exposure during a sensitive developmental period, may help explain the pattern. They warned that because children and adolescents consume even higher proportions of calories from ultra-processed foods, future generations could face greater addiction risks unless early intervention becomes more important.

The Bank of England will keep the £5 polymer note and issue the £10 note as planned despite objections over traces of tallow. It rejected destruction, reprinting or delay as costly and will consult on plant-based alternatives for the £20 and future £5 and £10 notes.

Qarlinngua is a massive, pants-shaped natural sea arch in Nunavut’s Arctic, confirmed by local sources and geologists after CBC North’s photograph was suspected to be fake. Its Inuktitut name means “like pants.” The formation stands over 50 metres high on the Brodeur Peninsula of northern Baffin Island, roughly 80–90 kilometres southwest of Arctic Bay. Reaching it requires a four- to five-hour boat trip and is possible only during a brief summer window when sea ice breaks up.

Hunter Max Kalluk first saw the arch around age 12. Scientists explained that wind and water gradually eroded layered sedimentary sandstone into the arch, while quartz-rich sections remain more resistant. Increased open water in the Arctic could accelerate erosion, though estimates of when Qarlinngua might collapse range from decades to thousands of years. Other arches could form as the cliff erodes.

Arctic Bay Adventures is the only tour company visiting the formation. Nunavut’s tourism director said the government plans to promote it to older, high-income travellers. The area also contains other unusual formations, including an elephant-shaped rock nearby.

This study examines career transitions and adaptation among lecturers and civil-service education personnel at Indonesian state higher education institutions. It addresses a limited literature that has focused more on organizational needs than individual experiences and has largely overlooked education personnel’s transitions. Using an interpretive, grounded-theory approach, the study analyzes how lecturers and education personnel assume dual roles as faculty or functional officers and temporary campus leaders while retaining their original positions.

Data were collected through semi-structured interviews, documents, photographs, and recordings from lecturers and education personnel undergoing transitions. Snowball sampling and maximum variation were used to access this hidden population, with key informants representing different types of higher-education institutions. Interviews were analyzed iteratively in NVivo through open, axial, and selective coding.

The resulting model identified eight categories: situation, self, support, strategies, behavior, role, learning, and perception. Adaptation involved a reciprocal relationship among Schlossberg’s four factors: new tasks shaped perceptions of situations; informants assessed their strengths and weaknesses; support came from family, colleagues, and organizations; and strategies included seeking information or acting directly. Transitions produced changes in burnout, motivation, competence, discipline, identity, time management, roles, learning, and perceptions. Respondents reported using both competence and managerial career anchors, contrary to Schein’s single-anchor proposition.

The study recommends careful organizational preparation for additional duties, alignment of structural and functional positions, competency-based appointments, and development of functional roles and performance criteria. Organizational support was especially important, while transitions often weakened performance in original positions. Limitations include the qualitative, institution-specific scope, exclusion of race and gender, and possible researcher bias.
Apple Inc.’s Form 8-K, signed by Katherine Adams on September 13, 2019, reported that Bob Iger resigned from the company’s Board of Directors on September 10, 2019.

A hockey player who had suffered a head injury said he felt comfortable during play but tired late in the third period. After travel to Denver for a CT scan, he was examined by Dr. Richardson and team orthopedist Dr. Martini, who found his healing sufficiently advanced for him to play. They said his current risk was no different than it would be in September, though it might decrease slightly. The scan was arranged unexpectedly after discussions about teammate Doug’s injury.

The player credited his teammates, expressed gratitude for being part of the team’s success, and planned to resume his normal routine at home. Following a difficult overtime loss and a missed opportunity to close out the series, he said the team needed better execution, desire, and hard play in front of its fans. He also said his family was emotional but reassured by the doctors’ assessment.
The court affirmed the plaintiff’s judgment with costs, adopting the trial judge’s opinion in an action decided without a jury.

The study examines the development, themes, contributors, and international collaboration surrounding mathematics anxiety in education from 2013 to 2023. Mathematics anxiety is described as tension, worry, or fear that interferes with mathematical performance, encourages avoidance of mathematics, and can hinder learning and achievement across age groups.

Using bibliometric methods, the researchers collected and filtered Scopus journal articles, leaving 324 for analysis in VOSviewer and Biblioshiny. Publications generally increased annually, rising from seven in 2013 to a peak of 56 in 2022. Social sciences accounted for 35.1% of publications and psychology for 30.7%. Keyword mapping identified seven thematic clusters connecting mathematics anxiety with achievement, performance, emotions, motivation, beliefs, self-efficacy, gender, skills, teachers, and metacognitive monitoring.

The analysis found 168 contributing journals. Frontiers in Psychology published the most mathematics-anxiety articles, while leading journals were generally ranked in Scopus Q1 or Q2. Garcia-Santillan had the most publications among the listed authors, while Pekrun and Goetz had the highest citation totals. Collaboration was generally limited, with most authors working with three to five others.

Approximately 78 countries contributed. The United States led in publication volume and collaboration networks, while Germany received the most citations. The University of Barcelona was the most productive institution, with 23 documents. The study concludes that mathematics anxiety remains a leading research topic and recommends broader database coverage and additional document types in future research.

North Korea displayed intercontinental and submarine-launched ballistic missiles during Kim Il-sung’s 105th-birthday parade, warning the U.S. it was ready to respond to nuclear attacks with its own. China warned that war could erupt at any moment.

NVIDIA Corporation filed a Form 10-Q (Commission file 0-23985) for the quarterly period ended July 26, 2020, its second quarter of fiscal year 2021. The Delaware corporation is headquartered in Santa Clara, California; its common stock ($0.001 par value) trades on Nasdaq as NVDA, and it is a large accelerated filer with 617 million shares outstanding as of August 14, 2020.

**Results:** Q2 revenue was $3,866 million versus $2,579 million a year earlier (up 50%) and up 26% sequentially. Gross margin was 58.8% (down 100 basis points year over year, 630 basis points sequentially), operating expenses $1,624 million (up 67%), income from operations $651 million (up 14% year over year, down 33% sequentially), net income $622 million versus $552 million, and diluted EPS $0.99 versus $0.90. For the first six months, revenue was $6,946 million versus $4,799 million, net income $1,539 million versus $947 million, and diluted EPS $2.47 versus $1.54. The margin decline reflects Mellanox-related charges including a non-recurring $161 million inventory step-up and $84 million of intangible amortization.

**Balance sheet (July 26, 2020 vs. January 26, 2020):** Total assets $25,180M vs. $17,315M; cash and equivalents $3,274M; marketable securities $7,707M; goodwill $4,193M; net intangible assets $2,854M; long-term debt $6,960M vs. $1,991M; shareholders' equity $13,914M. Six-month cash flows: $2,476M from operations, $14,545M used in investing (including $8,286M of marketable securities purchases and $7,171M for acquisitions), $4,447M provided by financing (including $4,971M net debt issuance, $418M of RSU tax payments, $197M dividends); cash fell $7,622M.

**Mellanox acquisition (April 27, 2020):** Total consideration $7.13B ($125.00/share for ~56 million shares). Preliminary allocation: goodwill $3,431M and intangibles $2,970M (developed technology $1,640M/5 years, customer relationships $440M/3 years, backlog $190M, trade names $70M/5 years, IPR&D $630M indefinite-lived). Mellanox contributed roughly 14% of consolidated revenue and just over 30% of Data Center revenue; $26M of acquisition costs were recorded in SG&A in the first half.

**Segments and markets:** NVIDIA changed reportable segments to Graphics and Compute & Networking (from GPU and Tegra Processor). Q2 Graphics revenue $2,085M with operating income $911M; Compute & Networking revenue $1,781M with operating income $691M; "All Other" operating loss $951M. Platform revenue: Gaming $1,654M, Data Center $1,752M, Professional Visualization $203M, Automotive $111M, OEM and Other $146M. By billing location: Taiwan $954M, U.S. $944M, China (including Hong Kong) $855M, Other Asia Pacific $698M, Europe $240M, other $175M. Revenue outside the U.S. was 76% of Q2 revenue; no customer was 10% or more of revenue in Q2 or the first half.

**Debt and capital return:** March 2020 issuance of $1.50B 2.85% notes due 2030, $1.00B 3.50% due 2040, $2.00B 3.50% due 2050 and $500M 3.70% due 2060 (net proceeds $4.97B), plus September 2016 notes of $1.0B 2.20% due 2021 and $1.0B 3.20% due 2026 (net proceeds $1.98B). The $575M credit facility was undrawn and the $575M commercial paper program unused. Through July 26, 2020, 260 million shares were repurchased for $7.08B, with $7.24B authorized through December 2022; dividends were $99M in Q2 ($0.16/share) and $197M in the first half ($0.32/share).

**Other:** Stock-based compensation was $374M in Q2 and $598M in the first half, with $3.60B unearned expense over 2.8 years (RSUs/PSUs/market-based PSUs) and 0.9 years (ESPP). Long-term operating lease liabilities were $611M (present value of minimum payments $735M; 8.0-year weighted average term, 3.08% discount rate). Q2 produced a $13M tax benefit (2.0% of pre-tax income) and the first half a $52M expense (3.3%), including $256M of net deferred and $153M of long-term tax liabilities from Mellanox; the IRS is examining fiscal 2018 and 2019. Deferred revenue was $342M, with $670M of remaining performance obligations (about 40% expected within 12 months). Purchase obligations were $2.04B for inventory and $310M for other items.

**Litigation:** A consolidated securities class action alleging false statements about channel inventory and cryptocurrency mining's impact on GPU demand was dismissed with leave to amend in March 2020; plaintiffs amended in May and NVIDIA moved to dismiss again in June 2020. Consolidated California derivative suits and two Delaware derivative suits were stayed pending the securities-litigation motion to dismiss. No accrual was recorded because losses are not considered probable.

**COVID-19:** Management reported remote work since March 2020 and adverse effects on served industries, notably Professional Visualization and Automotive, and stated that existing cash, marketable securities, commercial paper and short-term liquidity arrangements should meet working capital and other liquidity needs.

This continuation application describes a detection model training method, training apparatus, storage medium, and terminal device. It addresses limited and costly labeled medical-imaging data and differences among hospitals caused by devices, image resolution, background noise, and physician practices, which can reduce colorectal polyp detection accuracy across domains.

The method uses an initial training model containing an initial detection model and an adaptive model. Training data include labeled source-domain images, containing target-object presence information and domain identifiers, and target-domain images, containing domain identifiers but not target-object labels. The detection model extracts features and determines whether a target object is present, optionally identifying its type and location. The adaptive model classifies each image’s domain. Detection and domain-classification results are compared with the training identifiers to calculate a loss, including detection, classification, localization, and adaptive components. Model parameters are then adjusted using the loss, repeatedly until convergence or a preset iteration limit, producing a final detection model.

In embodiments using a convolutional neural network, the initial detection model includes a feature-extraction module and a detection/classification module, while the adaptive model includes a domain-classification module and may include a gradient-inversion module. The feature extractor is shared between the models. During backpropagation, the gradient-inversion module reverses the domain-classification error, creating an adversarial relationship: the domain classifier improves while the feature extractor seeks domain-invariant features. This allows source-domain detection capabilities to transfer to target-domain data without requiring target-object labels.

A colorectal-polyp example uses labeled source images from existing data and unlabeled target images from a new hospital. The resulting model identifies whether an examined colorectal image contains a polyp and, if so, its type and location. The training apparatus implements the method through model, sample, processing, loss, adjustment, and detection units. The same instructions may be stored on a processor-readable medium and executed by a terminal device.

A May 25, 2001 email compiles news coverage of Enron, led by a New York Times report on Chairman Kenneth Lay’s political influence and his allegedly conditional support for FERC Chairman Curtis Hebert, who disputed Lay’s account.
