Enron’s donations and Lay’s recommendations helped shape federal energy policy and commission appointments; Pat Wood was widely expected to replace Hebert.

Coverage also details the escalating dispute over Enron’s Dabhol power project in India. Maharashtra’s state electricity board canceled its power-purchase agreement, citing unpaid bills and failure to meet capacity requirements, while Dabhol disputed the board’s legal authority and pursued termination and arbitration. Negotiations continued amid disagreement over the committee’s authority, government payment guarantees, Bechtel’s threat to withdraw, and possible sales of Enron’s stake to NTPC or a private buyer.

Other articles address California’s electricity crisis, calls for federal price controls and cooperation between state and federal leaders, declining political ratings for Gov. Gray Davis, modest stock-market gains amid economic uncertainty, Portland General Electric’s rising revenues and power costs, expanded India-Australia energy and mining cooperation, changing corporate models in the internet economy, renewed interest in energy careers, and El Paso’s chairman agreeing to testify in a California gas-price hearing.

Teams should prepare for defensive, even, and offensive jump-ball situations. In defensive situations, players should rotate early, watch the jumper’s eyes and hands, maintain contact after the tip, and use box or diamond alignments to deny passes, anticipate open spaces, and tip the ball back to a trailing defender. A “Y” alignment places two defenders near the free-throw circle to prevent an easy shot and force the offense to set up. If the opponent gains possession, establishing a defensive stop is crucial.

For even jump balls, players must box out, establish inside position, and rotate clockwise or counter-clockwise according to a predetermined signal to attack open spaces.

Offensive teams with a significant height advantage can run set plays, generally tipping to the tallest player while maintaining defensive balance and transitioning into the offense when possession is gained. Proven plays include Ball Possession, Double Tap, Post Split, Jumper Fly, Forward Fly, Spread, Tandem, and Loop. These plays use tips, screens, cuts, passes, and back screens to create feeds, open shots, or numerical advantages.

Apple removed several ICE-tracking and documentation apps from its App Store after U.S. Attorney General Pam Bondi claimed they endangered ICE officers. Affected developers, including Eyes Up’s Mark and ICEBlock’s Joshua Aaron, are appealing the removals and pursuing legal action; some apps remain available through Google Play or their websites. Apple reportedly cited a guideline against “defamatory, discriminatory, or mean-spirited content” when removing DEICER. Google has also removed ICE-monitoring apps and said it considers ICE officers a vulnerable group. Legal experts told WIRED that the apps constitute protected First Amendment speech because they publish truthful information about public events. The Trump administration has separately threatened to prosecute Aaron. Researchers cited concerns that major technology companies can become powerful arbiters of speech, highlighting Apple’s closed ecosystem, while noting Android users can sideload apps and Apple and Google themselves offer police-location features in navigation apps.

Former Tropical Depression 02W crossed the eastern Visayas on April 15, 2017, weakened, and entered the South China Sea as a remnant low. NASA’s Terra satellite imaged its elongated cloud area on April 17. The JTWC reported a compact closed circulation moving west and said wind shear and dry air should prevent re-intensification.

Alberta Education Minister David Eggen said parents could pay school bus fees despite Bill 1, which eliminated fees for students living at least 2.4 kilometres from their designated school. Rocky View Schools, serving nearly 24,000 students, is exploring solutions to a $1 million transportation shortfall and will consult the ministry.

The Supreme Court debated whether double jeopardy bars separate convictions and sentences under 18 U.S.C. §§ 924(c) and 924(j) for the same conduct. The parties agreed that lesser-included offenses generally cannot receive cumulative punishment absent clear evidence that Congress intended otherwise, and that § 924(c) may be punished in addition to its underlying crime of violence or drug-trafficking offense.

The central dispute concerned what language establishes congressional intent regarding § 924(j). Barrett and the government argued that § 924(c)(1)(D)(ii), requiring consecutive sentences “notwithstanding any other provision of law,” does not authorize cumulative punishment for § 924(j). The government also noted that § 924(j) lacks § 924(c)’s “in addition to” language and argued that no statute authorizes cumulative punishments for both § 924(j) and the predicate offenses. McCloud countered that statutory structure and purpose can establish intent without specific “magic words,” particularly because Congress enacted § 924(j) knowing § 924(c)’s consecutive-sentence mandate already existed.

The government noted that charging § 924(j) in a noncapital case would replace the predicate conviction, remove the consecutive-sentence requirement and § 924(c)’s mandatory minimums, and require proof that the firearm caused death. Justice Gorsuch raised unresolved questions about the constitutional basis for requiring clear congressional intent, but those issues were not fully briefed.

This section provides mechanical, packaging, and orderable information for designated devices. Data is current but may change without notice. Notes address product status, preproduction material limitations and waivers, RoHS classifications, lead-finish or ball-material options, moisture sensitivity and peak reflow temperatures, and part-marking formats.

TI states that its information reflects knowledge and belief based partly on third-party data, without warranties of accuracy. Certain proprietary details, including CAS numbers, may be unavailable, and TI’s liability is capped at the annual purchase price of the applicable parts. Tape-related definitions cover component dimensions, carrier width, cavity pitch, and pin 1 orientation.

Technical, design, application, web, and safety resources are provided “as is,” without warranties. Developers are responsible for product selection, design, validation, testing, and compliance with applicable requirements. Resources may change, are permitted only for developing applications using the described TI products, and cannot be reproduced or displayed otherwise. Users must indemnify TI against claims arising from their use. TI products remain subject to applicable sales terms, and TI rejects additional or different terms. The mailing address is Texas Instruments, Post Office Box 655303, Dallas, Texas 75265.

Schizophrenia spectrum disorder (SSD) lacks objective biomarkers, and resting-state functional connectivity MRI classifiers face challenges in accuracy, generalisability, test–retest variability, and specificity. This study aimed to develop a clinically viable SSD classifier using independent discovery (1,015 participants) and validation (683 participants) datasets and to examine whether diagnostic connections could also function as trait, state, or staging markers.

Using 10-fold cross-validation, investigators developed 100 LASSO classifiers, spatial averaging, and voting methods. LASSO achieved 79.6% discovery accuracy with an AUC of 0.876 and 77.3% validation accuracy with an AUC of 0.824. Performance varied across sites, with particularly low SSD sensitivity at JHU. Voting significantly improved sensitivity over LASSO, but specificity did not differ significantly, and voting AUC (0.841) was not significantly different. Voting also reduced performance disparities across severity groups, although age may partly influence its performance.

Diagnostic differences across functional connections were reproducible between cohorts. Forty-seven connections were deemed important, with 44 retaining the same healthy-control–SSD relationship during validation. Region-of-interest analysis found left–right laterality imbalances in seven regions, except the cerebellum. The study also planned to assess whether aggregate and individual connections could reflect symptom severity, disease states, or stages.

The Jabra Elite 65t are among the first earbuds to support Alexa through Amazon’s mobile accessory kit, though Alexa integration currently works only with Android phones; iOS support is planned. The earbuds deliver excellent sound, a comfortable fit, and effective ambient-sound mode, but Alexa’s mobile capabilities are substantially limited compared with smart speakers and competing assistants.

Alexa supports voice shopping particularly well, including repeat orders, package tracking, and delivery updates. Amazon Music is the only supported streaming service, but playback controls are cumbersome, and Spotify and other services cannot be accessed by voice. The earbuds can answer calls, but cannot place them through Alexa, send messages, or use Drop In; call quality also suffers in noisy environments. Timers and alarms can be set without producing notifications, reminders are unsupported, and Alexa offers traffic information but no navigation. Translation is limited to brief phrases, though more than 30,000 Alexa skills are available. Google Assistant and Siri provide stronger notification, messaging, and navigation features.

The Elite 65t provide five hours of battery per charge and ten additional hours from their case. They also lack a tracker for locating lost earbuds. Overall, the review praises their audio quality but finds Alexa unreliable for music, calls, reminders, and navigation, with further feature updates needed.

Shohei Ohtani started Game 1 of the 2025 NLDS for the Dodgers against the Phillies, making his first postseason pitching appearance. He went 1-1 with a 2.87 ERA, 62 strikeouts and 15 earned runs over 47 innings in 14 regular-season appearances. Dave Roberts hoped he could pitch into the seventh. Ohtani retired Trea Turner and Bryce Harper while allowing Schwarber to fly out to the right-field wall, then struck out in his first plate appearance. His final regular-season outing was six scoreless innings with eight strikeouts and five hits, but the Dodgers lost 5-4. Philadelphia starter Christopher Sanchez finished the season 13-5 with a 2.50 ERA.

After 58 people were killed and more than 500 injured in the Oct. 1 Route 91 Harvest festival shooting in Las Vegas, country musicians debated gun control and concert safety. Jason Aldean was performing when a gunman fired from a nearby hotel room. Charlie Daniels called the shooter an anomaly and warned against letting fear prevail. He supported regulations for “bump stock” devices but opposed broader gun restrictions, arguing that politicians lacked gun knowledge and stricter laws would leave Americans defenseless. The National Rifle Association maintains close ties to country music through N.R.A. Country. Gun-control activist Rosanne Cash urged country musicians in a New York Times essay to stand up to the NRA, while Daniels said he had not read it. Eric Church wrote and sang a song for a festival victim at the Grand Ole Opry. Daniels was scheduled to headline an Oct. 21 show at Cary’s Booth Amphitheatre.

Digital leaders emphasize experimentation, sensible risk-taking, continuous data feedback, and individual development to remain competitive and avoid obsolescence. Failed experiments still provide valuable knowledge, so leaders encourage thoughtful risk assessment while prioritizing long-term training in critical-thinking skills.

Using Mauna Loa Observatory solar-radiation data, Willis Eschenbach compared conditions during the two years following the El Chichón and Pinatubo eruptions with non-volcanic periods. Volcanic periods had about 24.5 W/m² less average downwelling solar radiation, although clouds appeared to offset part of the reduction by limiting the usual afternoon decline in sunlight. Despite the net loss of roughly 25 W/m² for two years, no corresponding temperature change was detected at Mauna Loa or at several other Hawaiian stations. Eschenbach also found that, apart from post-eruption periods, atmospheric clarity at Mauna Loa had remained essentially unchanged since 1980. He attributes the lack of cooling to his theory that the climate system tends to counteract changes in forcing, while acknowledging that he does not know why the temperature response was absent.

A former player praises Winnipeg’s passionate fans, strong organization, and smaller arena, expecting strong support for the new NHL Jets. He distinguishes Daniel and Henrik Sedin by their voices, noting Henrik is more talkative and has always been captain. He also discusses how to score against Thomas Vokoun by matching his style, choosing shots carefully, and pursuing rebounds or backdoor goals while recognizing his skill.

Energy sector trading provides exposure to multiple energy stocks for diversification and potential profit, either through a sector ETF such as XLE or a portfolio of individual stocks. The S&P 500 energy sector includes companies involved in oil and natural gas exploration, refining, product distribution, and related equipment, materials, and services. Vanguard Energy ETF (VDE) and Energy Select Sector SPDR Fund (XLE) are major sector ETFs. As of July 18, 2022, the sector’s one-year total return was reported as high as 52.81%, compared with about -9.28% for the S&P 500.

The passage describes two XLE strategies. The first opens a short position and has an average holding period of nearly three days. Across 198 trades, it averaged a 0.61% gain, with a 6.4% CAGR, 65% win rate, 13% maximum drawdown, and 2.1 profit factor. The second, developed after six months of demo trading, recorded 335 trades, a 0.21% average gain, 59% win rate, 8% maximum drawdown, and 1.75 profit factor. Its annual return was 3%, two percentage points below buy-and-hold returns excluding dividends.

The five largest listed energy stocks are Exxon Mobil, Chevron, ConocoPhillips, EOG Resources, and Schlumberger, although the list can change. The sector is described as difficult to trade because commodity prices are strongly influenced by unpredictable macroeconomic factors, but successful strategies may offer valuable diversification and risk management.

The passage compares five Canadian banks with five small-cap lenders after a choppy March and declining April for Toronto Stock Exchange financials. The banks fell 4.6%–7.5% from February highs, while three small-cap lenders saw double-digit declines. Using beta, earnings yield, dividend yield, payout ratio, and dividend history, MCAN Mortgage ranked first, Atrium Mortgage third, and Canadian Imperial Bank of Commerce second. The big five banks had not reduced dividends in more than ten years and offered yields of 3.4%–4.4%. Atrium and MCAN also maintained or increased dividends annually and paid yields above 7%, with payout ratios below 100%. First National Financial, Home Capital Group, and Equitable Group had cut dividends and received the worst scores; Equitable ranked last due to high beta and low yield. Small-cap lenders may offer higher yields and smaller price swings, but have lower liquidity and less diversified services than the major banks. The author disclosed holdings in AMIVF, CM, TD, and BNS.

The Hawk Offense uses wing isolation, a high-post shuffle cut, and a weak-side post-up, resembling the UCLA offense through a guard cutting off a big man’s high-post screen. Defensively, teams show help against wing penetration, force cutters behind screens, recover to assignments, and deny passes after chasing down screens. Defenders generally avoid switching on high-post screens because doing so may leave the screener posting against a smaller defender.

A full-court disruption traps the ballhandler near the sideline wing, while other defenders contact-switch, front post players, deny passing lanes, and rotate as the pass leaves the passer’s hands. Once matched up, Base Go Red rotations address baseline penetration, while Post Trap rotations address post passes.

AMD has returned to high-end graphics with the Radeon RX Vega 64 and Vega 56, targeting Nvidia’s GTX 1080 and GTX 1070 respectively. Nvidia is expected to retain the crown for single-card performance, but AMD offers three-way CrossFire support, compared with Nvidia’s two-way SLI. The Vega 56 is $50 cheaper than the GTX 1070 in the US, though UK competition may affect pricing. AMD also benefits from FreeSync’s cheaper, more widely available monitors, Enhanced Sync, and improvements to minimum frame rates.

In a 1857 Franklin Circuit Court case, Madison Snap and William Francis were convicted and fined for shooting and wounding a mare trespassing in an oat field protected by an inadequate fence. The court held that both statute and common law prohibited unnecessarily injuring trespassing livestock, though necessary force to expel it was permitted. The conviction and judgment were affirmed.

Old paper £10 notes cease to be legal tender in the UK on 1 March. They can still be exchanged for polymer notes featuring Jane Austen through banks, post offices or the Bank of England, with ID possibly required. The new notes have enhanced anti-counterfeiting and accessibility features.

Football safeties are defensive backs, typically positioned deeper than other defenders as the last line against big plays. The position includes free safeties, who roam without a specific assignment and are often faster and more athletic, and strong safeties, who play closer to the line, fill running gaps, tackle, and cover receivers or zones. Other traditional terms include rover, star, defensive fullback, and defensive halfback, with the latter two still used in Canadian football.

Safeties must cover receivers and tight ends, run downhill to make tackles, communicate effectively, and contribute to both pass and run defense. Their responsibilities have expanded as football become more pass-oriented.

Notable safeties include Troy Polamalu, Ed Reed, Ken Houston, Steve Atwater, Ronnie Lott, Brian Dawkins, Emlen Tunnell, Larry Wilson, and Sean Taylor. Polamalu won two Super Bowls and was the 2010 NFL Defensive Player of the Year; Reed was a Super Bowl champion, two-time Defensive Player of the Year, and nine-time Pro Bowler; Houston holds the safety record with 12 Pro Bowl appearances. Taylor was a two-time Pro Bowler before his death at 24.

A strong safety can create turnovers, deter deep passes, support cornerbacks, and give the defense confidence by preventing big gains and touchdowns.

Researchers studying fossils from 16 sites found that the Great Barrier Reef survived five near-extinction events over 30,000 years by shifting with changing sea levels at rates of 0.2 to 1.5 metres annually. They say today’s rapid warming and acidification may exceed that resilience, while repeated bleaching has caused major losses, including nearly one-third of the reef’s coral during a 2016 heatwave. Another geological die-off may occur within thousands of years, but the impact of human-driven climate change remains uncertain. Coral reefs support about a quarter of ocean life.

Following the 2024 Arab Summit in Bahrain, Jaber Mustafa and Younis Bukhari, both affiliated with the Ministry of Education, present a report under the “Hope” initiative, which seeks to ensure free education for every Arab child. Citing a 2018 UNESCO report that over 10 million Arab children aged 5–15 are out of school, they argue for immediate remedial measures and resilient regional educational frameworks, using the Syrian conflict as a case study.

The study's stated significance spans inclusivity and community integration, restoring hope, the mental health effects of armed conflict (60.5% of children affected by the Syrian Civil War meet criteria for at least one psychological disorder; among Syrian refugee children in Turkey, depression 12.5%, PTSD 11.5%, anxiety 9.2%), building resilience through family support, trauma-related learning difficulties, preparing children for Syria's national recovery, and maintaining education during conflict.

The literature review finds that conflict disrupts early childhood education through displacement, school destruction and inequitable access, and degrades quality through untrained or departing teachers, resource shortages and outdated curricula. Exposure to violence produces toxic stress, impaired brain development and behavioural problems, with long-term literacy, numeracy and socio-emotional deficits that perpetuate poverty and instability. In Syria, nearly one-third of schools have been damaged or destroyed; UNICEF reports about 4,000 attacks on schools since 2011, with one in three destroyed, damaged or converted to military use, some becoming detention centres. UNICEF (2021) estimates over two million Syrian children remain out of education, with about 2.6 million displaced children and poverty above 90%. Syria's primary entrance age is six, with three-year lower and upper secondary cycles; of 3.4 million pupils enrolled in primary and secondary education, 1.55 million (45%) are in primary, and many drop out mid-cycle. In Turkey, nearly 400,000 Syrian refugee children are out of school amid over 3.6 million Syrian refugees, with dropout driven by poverty, early marriage and child labour.

Using a descriptive triangulation design combining interviews, a ten-question online survey and a case study of Ahmed, a Syrian child in Alkhabor, the findings describe destroyed schools, repeated displacement, shared textbooks, no internet or electricity, unsanitary communal learning spaces disrupted by aircraft, limited study time, PTSD symptoms and absent psychological support, alongside community learning groups and unpaid teachers. Two solution tracks are proposed: immediate and remedial emotional and academic interventions, and proactive, sustainable measures through the “Hope Initiative,” an integrated organisation designed to sustain education and prepare for future conflicts. The conclusion frames education as both a casualty of war and a basis for empowerment and lasting peace.
Jane Goodall, who died October 1 at 91, left a legacy spanning living chimpanzees’ stories and enduring skeletons.

The September 19 earthquake and renewed activity at Popocatépetl have left residents of San Andrés Hueyapan, Morelos, frightened and stressed. Authorities advised Tetela del Volcán residents to keep documents and clothing ready in case of eruption. Hueyapan, 18 kilometers from the volcano, suffered extensive home damage. Eruptions later produced ashfall in Tetela del Volcán and Zacualpan de Amilpas.

Sean “Diddy” Combs was sentenced in Manhattan to 50 months in prison and a $500,000 fine after being convicted on two Mann Act counts involving transportation for prostitution across state lines. A jury acquitted him of sex trafficking and racketeering conspiracy. Combs apologized to his victims, his seven children, and his mother, while his defense presented evidence of family and community service. Judge Arun Subramanian said his good works could not erase his abuse of power over women. Combs also faces civil lawsuits alleging sexual assault, rape, drugging, and other violence, which he denies.

Backtests show a positive futures-expiration-week effect for DAX 40 and Euro Stoxx 50, which expire on the third Friday of March, June, September, and December. During expiration week, DAX 40 averaged a 0.39% gain with a 57% win rate, versus 0.12% in a random week. Euro Stoxx 50 averaged 0.3% with a 54% win rate, compared with 0.18%, making its effect smaller. December performed best for both.

The post-expiration DAX 40 test used a 100% margin strategy rather than futures backtesting, making four annual trades without commissions or slippage. It averaged a 0.1% loss with a 47% win rate. December and March were positive, June was slightly negative, and September was particularly poor, profitable only 25% of the time. Increased expiration-week volatility is attributed to “pin” risk. DAX 40 is attractive to traders because of its high trading volume.

The Second Circuit affirmed Samuel Israel III’s conviction and twenty-year sentence. The court found no actual or apparent bias warranting Judge McMahon’s recusal, noting that her change in duty stations, a docketing error involving personal information, and statements during an adjournment did not suggest partiality. Her recusal from a related bankruptcy case was likewise immaterial. The court rejected all sentencing challenges, finding that Israel’s medical needs did not justify a downward departure, the substantial reduction for cooperation was within the district court’s discretion, and the sentence was reasonable given his lengthy criminal history and the large sum of money involved.

For the UC1825BEVM-CVAL, an RCD clamp uses a resistor, capacitor, and diode to clamp the switch-node voltage. Starting component values depend on the allowable overshoot. Equation 30 calculates clamp voltage as \(K_{\text{clamp}} \times N_{ps} \times (V_{out} + V_{Diode})\), with \(K_{\text{clamp}}=1.5\) recommended for approximately 50% overshoot. Transformer parasitic inductance and permitted clamp-voltage variation over the switching cycle are then used to determine starting resistor and capacitor values through Equations 31 and 32.

The application discloses curable and cured silicone elastomers containing dispersed carbon black particles, including hydrophilic, oxidized carbon black dispersed in hydrophobic silicone matrices. Methods contact the carbon black with a silicone-compatible dispersant bearing carbon-black-affinic amino, acrylate, or epoxy groups, optionally reduce its particle size, mix it with a curable hydrophobic silicone pre-polymer, and addition- or condensation-cure the mixture. Dispersants may be branched, siloxane-containing amino-silicones, silicone acrylates, or epoxy-silicones selected for miscibility and a balance between particle dispersion and curing performance.

Embodiments specify carbon-black concentration, particle size, oxidation and volatile-matter content, pH, acid value, zeta potential, surface functional groups, and Raman D-band/G-band ratios. Carbon black may be oxidatively treated with ozone or hypohalous agents. Dispersed particles are described as carbon-black cores associated with or partially enveloped by dispersants and as non-covalently entrapped in the cured matrix.

The compositions may be applied to substrates or formed into articles and have applications including intermediate transfer members for indirect printing and UV-absorbing sealants. Carbon black can provide reinforcement and thermal, electrical, and radiation-absorbing properties. The application is a divisional patent application with incorporated references to related U.S. and PCT applications.

The ADS8860 application uses ±15-V supplies, a 5.3-V VLVDD, ground VLVSS, and a 5-V ADC reference. The PGA848 front end incorporates three filters: an input filter for EMI, RFI, and high-frequency noise; a CFB capacitor across the 6.67-kΩ feedback resistors; and an RC charge-kickback filter at the ADC inputs. With CFB = 75 pF, cutoff is 318 kHz, or 277 kHz at the high side of the ±15% resistor tolerance. Changing CFB adjusts bandwidth at the expense of broadband noise. The third filter is tuned for ADC settling, THD, and PGA stability, and C0G capacitors are used throughout the signal path. Overall bandwidth is nominally 318 kHz, with −0.1-dB flatness through 41 kHz.

The ADS8860 requires a 0–5-V full-scale input. The PGA848 REF pin is set nominally to 2.5 V using a REF6250 reference, a precision voltage divider, and an OPA192 buffer. The dual-feedback buffer uses a 20-Ω isolation resistor, 2-kΩ direct feedback, and 2-nF feedback capacitor, provides 86° phase margin, and reduces divider thermal noise with a 1-kΩ/10-nF low-pass input. Stability components must be recalculated for other loads and verified in simulation with more than 60° phase margin.

PGA848 performance is specified at ±15-V input- and output-stage supplies with VICM and VREF at mid-supply; output-stage supplies must remain within input-stage levels, and ±20-V operation can permanently damage the device. Layout guidance emphasizes matched, symmetric inputs, local 0.1-µF supply bypass capacitors, trace separation, and minimizing leakage, parasitic capacitance, vias, and thermal effects. The passage also describes PSpice and TINA-TI simulation tools, TI documentation and support resources, ESD precautions, and mechanical, ordering, warranty, and liability information.

The Supreme Court reversed and remanded the Eighth Circuit’s judgment. Philip Brooks, an apprentice machinist who served in the military, completed his apprenticeship at North Little Rock but was given a later seniority date. The District Court found that his promotion to journeyman mechanic would have been automatic on November 3, 1955, absent military service. Applying Tilton, the Court held that speculative future labor-market conditions cannot defeat a veteran’s seniority rights and that Brooks is entitled to the earlier date.

U.S. stocks rose Monday, led by gains in the S&P 500 and Nasdaq as technology and semiconductor shares offset weakness in energy, while the Dow edged higher. Investors remained alert to a possible government shutdown, which could delay economic data, complicate Federal Reserve decisions and increase volatility. Despite hawkish comments from Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack, markets continued to expect a modest rate cut, though stronger data tempered hopes of aggressive easing. The rally reflected resilience, but political gridlock and inflation concerns left the outlook uncertain.

Russian journalist Arkady Babchenko appeared alive at a Ukrainian news conference less than 24 hours after police reported he had been fatally shot in Kyiv, saying his death was staged to prevent an alleged Kremlin assassination plot. Ukrainian Security Service chief Vasyl Gritsak alleged that Russian security services paid a Ukrainian citizen $40,000 to organize the hit and recruit a gunman; the man was later detained. The suspect was also allegedly intended to procure AK-47 rifles and explosives for terrorist attacks. Babchenko said Ukrainian law enforcement had known about a contract on his life for two months and that larger attacks had been thwarted. The Kremlin critic had received threats and fled Russia in 2017 before settling in Kyiv.

Americans spent more than $100 billion on summer vacations, while experts say travel can reduce stress and health risks and increase energy and relaxation. To control costs, travelers should set a budget based on available funds, use planning tools and comparison sites for hotels, flights and fuel, and monitor expenses. Other recommendations include using a credit card without foreign-transaction fees, carrying a backup card, limiting cellular roaming charges, traveling in the offseason, booking flights and lodging early, considering trip insurance, and signing up for airline newsletters to catch short-term deals. Travelers can also seek local coupons, attraction passes and discount books through destination information centers, hotel concierges and newspapers.

A study cited by Mayor Carlos Gimenez ranked PortMiami as the state’s top economic generator, reporting a $41 billion impact. Gimenez rejected suggestions that the figures were inflated. The port handled 8.9 million tons of cargo and 5.1 million cruise passengers in 2016, while a planned Royal Caribbean terminal is expected to generate $500 million annually.

The ARM Cortex-A8 MPU subsystem gives the Cortex-A8 master control over device subsystems, peripherals, and external memories. It integrates the ARMv7 Cortex-A8 processor with Thumb-2, JazelleX, Media Extensions, NEON SIMD, VFPv3 floating-point support, separate L1 instruction/data caches, a 128-bit interconnector, and an interrupt controller. It supports hardware/software debugging and ETM real-time tracing with address/data comparators, counters, and sequencers. Its unexposed trace port connects to a 32KB system ETB, whose captured data requires ETB-enabled tools to interpret.

A National Weather Service forecast issued early Wednesday, July 4, 2018, covers Orange and San Diego counties and inland areas of Riverside and San Bernardino counties. A high surf advisory is in effect from 6 p.m. Wednesday until 9 p.m. Friday for Orange and San Diego coastal areas, while an excessive heat watch runs from Friday morning through Saturday evening across all zones.

Wednesday and Thursday bring morning low clouds and fog to coastal areas, followed by mostly sunny and increasingly warm conditions. Winds are generally light, though afternoon and evening west or southwest winds commonly reach 15 mph with gusts up to 25 mph, with stronger gusts in mountains, deserts, and passes.

Friday and Saturday are hottest. Highs range from the mid-80s along beaches to 99–104 inland, 107–112 in San Diego County valleys, 110–115 in the Inland Empire, around 113 in San Gorgonio Pass, 111–116 in Coachella Valley, and 112–117 in Borrego Springs. Slight afternoon and evening showers and thunderstorms begin Saturday in the San Bernardino and Riverside mountains and Apple and Lucerne Valleys.

Temperatures ease somewhat Sunday through Tuesday, but substantial heat remains. Partly cloudy conditions dominate, with slight storm chances continuing in mountain and high-desert areas, including the San Diego County mountains beginning Sunday.

President James Madison recommended that the third Thursday in August 1812 be observed as a day of public humiliation, prayer, repentance, and thanksgiving, seeking God’s protection, forgiveness, and assistance during wartime and the restoration of peace. The proclamation was issued in Washington on July 9 and signed by Secretary of State James Monroe.

Blue Ridge Poison Control Center warns of spring hazards: poisonous plants and mushrooms, black widow spiders in woodpiles, and emerging snakes. It cautions against self-treating toxins and recommends protective clothing and checking boots.

The case examines ESPN’s transformation from a dominant cable television business into a digital sports platform amid declining pay-TV subscribers, rising sports-rights costs, fragmented audiences, and intensifying competition. In the early 2010s, ESPN generated substantial affiliate and advertising revenue from more than 100 million subscribers and was a major financial asset for Disney. By 2023, cable and satellite subscribers had fallen to an estimated 70 million, while streaming, changing viewing habits, and competition from Netflix, YouTube, Amazon, and other platforms intensified pressure on ESPN’s traditional model.

Founded by Bill and Scott Rasmussen in 1978, ESPN initially distributed content free to cable operators and relied on advertising. It introduced affiliate fees in 1983–84 after rights costs made that model unsustainable. The NFL agreement in 1987, the emergence of DirecTV and Dish, operator demand for additional channels, and Disney’s consolidated distribution network drove ESPN’s expansion. Disney acquired control of ESPN in 1996 and now owns 80%, while Hearst owns 20%.

ESPN expanded its digital presence through websites, mobile apps, fantasy sports, social media, and WatchESPN. After Disney acquired BAMTech, ESPN launched the direct-to-consumer ESPN+ service in 2018. Initially positioned as a supplement to linear television, ESPN+ gained subscribers through events such as UFC and later NHL games, reaching about 25 million subscribers with average revenue per user of $6.30. Disney announced that flagship ESPN networks would become directly available without a cable subscription in 2025. In February 2024, Disney, Warner Bros. Discovery, and Fox announced Venu Sports, a joint streaming service expected to launch that fall. Each company would own one-third, receive licensing fees, and retain advertising profits from its channels. These moves position ESPN to shift from selling through affiliates and advertisers to managing a direct consumer relationship, bringing greater control over customer data and engagement but also exposing it to acquisition, churn, and profitability challenges.

The competitive landscape includes incumbent media companies, technology firms, cable and satellite operators, sports properties, and fans. Incumbents are moving content to streaming platforms, while companies such as Amazon, YouTube, Apple, and Netflix use sports rights to support broader subscription, device, or service objectives. Sports leagues continue to command high fees because live programming attracts audiences, although some European leagues have moderated increases. U.S. rights spending was $25.57 billion in 2023 and was projected to exceed $30 billion by 2025. Cable operators are emphasizing broadband as their video businesses decline, while fans face more services, fragmented access, higher combined costs, easier cancellation, and persistent piracy.

Disney’s Q2 fiscal 2024 results illustrated ESPN’s position: ESPN Domestic revenue rose 4% to $3.866 billion, but operating income fell 9% to $780 million, with fewer cable subscribers and additional sports-rights costs outweighing higher affiliate rates and advertising revenue. ESPN+ subscribers declined slightly to 24.8 million, although price increases raised average revenue per subscriber to $6.30. Reports cited total ESPN rights obligations above $10 billion annually and content-production costs above $2 billion.

The case concludes that ESPN must decide which rights to retain, how to replace declining affiliate revenue, whether direct-to-consumer growth can produce sustainable profitability, and how to remain relevant to younger fans. Disney remains publicly optimistic that ESPN can become the leading digital sports platform, but the outcome will affect media companies, leagues, teams, players, distributors, and fans.

IEX is portrayed as having two conflicting strategies. IEX One uses its speed bump to favor large market orders and the buy-side within the SEC’s National Market System (NMS). Although this improves execution for those traders, the passage argues that it is another inefficient NMS subsidy rather than a true market disruption, leaving IEX with a niche and less than 3% of trading volume.

IEX Two represents IEX’s broader ambition to serve all traders efficiently, balance buy- and sell-side interests, and provide liquidity. Achieving this would require IEX to bypass the SEC and NMS, create an alternative trading vehicle, and gain broker and trader support. The passage criticizes the NMS for protecting established exchanges, enabling their fees and rebates, and reducing competition based on execution quality. It also contends that IEX’s speed bump is effectively an implicit fee. Ultimately, IEX’s success depends on converting customer goodwill into patronage and delivering liquidity outside the current regulatory framework.

U.S. employers added 200,000 jobs in January, while unemployment held at 4.1% and average hourly wages rose 2.9% from a year earlier. Economists said a tightening labor market may be accelerating wage growth, though minimum-wage increases in 18 states, affecting 4.5 million workers, could also explain the pay boost. Job growth under President Donald Trump has been similar to that under Barack Obama, and declining unemployment trends largely predate Trump. Black unemployment rose to 7.7% from 6.8% in December despite falling over the longer term. Economists cautioned that monthly employment estimates are revised, carry a roughly 100,000-job margin of error, and are less informative than long-term averages; automation and broader economic conditions also affect employment.
A 68-page IT Central Station report compares Oracle Exadata and HPE Vertica, citing user praise for smart scans and columnar storage and criticism of patching and documentation.

The writer praises Coronation Street’s sensitive portrayal of Aidan’s suicide, highlighting the anger, disbelief, and sadness experienced by loved ones. The writer recounts a failed suicide attempt as a teenager and shares friend Cheryl Fialka’s story of losing her husband John to suicide aboard a cruise ship. Cheryl describes her enduring grief and anger, the absence of warning signs or a note, and her continued search for reasons, while the writer questions whether people considering suicide recognize the devastation they leave behind.

The Stable Operations TRACC is a product-development partnership between Competitive Capabilities International (CCi) and R&G Global Consultants. It uses big data, analytics and the TRACC methodology to help manufacturers scale reliable operations and improvements across multiple sites. CCi says the solution can increase capacity by 15–20% within six months. Cargill, the first client to deploy it, helped facilitate the partnership. The product addresses capacity utilization, supply-chain service delivery and CAPEX avoidance through blended learning. R&G says it includes a maturity-based roadmap and expanded implementation support.

The paper examines barriers to women’s education in rural Pakistan and Azad Jammu and Kashmir. It reports that women’s literacy is 51.9%, compared with 73.3% for men, while rural female literacy is only 40.8%. The literature review links women’s education and participation to empowerment, rights, economic development, and national progress, but identifies poverty, patriarchal culture, family responsibilities, early marriage, parental attitudes, inadequate facilities, long travel distances, and limited transport as major obstacles.

The quantitative study surveyed literate and illiterate women using open-ended questionnaires and analyzed responses thematically. Both groups reported similar challenges and considered women’s education necessary while expressing confidence and hope for the future. Major findings concerned time and resource management, housework and caregiving burdens, male dominance, lack of family support and motivation, poverty and inflation, insufficient secondary schools and poor infrastructure, unsafe travel, inadequate female toilets, limited teacher training and technology, early marriage, and curriculum and language barriers. Parents’ low education, preference for boys, limited communication with schools, and belief that education is unnecessary or wasteful for girls further restricted attendance.

The paper recommends monthly seminars involving educators, parents, and women; greater use of print, social, and broadcast media to promote female education; legislation making education compulsory for women; and open and distance learning to improve literacy and access in remote areas.

The Pakistan Cricket Board pledged top-level security for the PSL final at Gaddafi Stadium after a Lahore bombing killed 13. The league is considering a new player draft if foreign stars opt out, while the army backed the event and officials said it could help restore Pakistan’s image.

After her 20-year marriage ended, a stay-at-home mother realized she did not know where the couple’s accounts and investments were or how the household budget worked. With a friend’s help, she organized financial documents, consulted a financial planner connected through her father, created a budget, and developed a retirement plan. She later returned to full-time work through a former colleague and had remained in the position for seven years. Over time, she learned to manage major purchases, household projects, and her finances independently. She regained professional confidence, planned for retirement on her own terms, and said she now felt financially secure and prepared for the future.

The author describes falling in love with Maine’s natural beauty and argues that the Katahdin Woods and Waters National Monument preserves an overlooked inland wilderness while benefiting rural Maine through tourism, investment and job growth. The monument was created from more than 87,000 acres of privately donated land in northern Penobscot County and received $40 million in private donations for maintenance. The author criticizes Gov. Paul LePage’s effort to have the designation repealed and supports Interior Secretary Ryan Zinke’s planned firsthand review, including canoeing on the East Branch of the Penobscot River. The author hopes Zinke will recognize the monument’s cultural, historical, economic and environmental value and support preserving it for future generations.

The paper presents the LifeCLEF 2014 Plant Identification Task, the continuation of the ImageCLEF plant identification campaigns begun in 2011, aimed at supporting content-based image retrieval for plant identification and ecological monitoring. The PlantCLEF 2014 dataset contains 60,962 pictures covering 19,504 observations of 500 species of trees, herbs and ferns from a region centred on France, contributed by 1,608 users. Each image is tied to one of seven view types (entire plant, fruit, leaf, flower, stem, branch, leaf scan) and carries metadata including observation and media identifiers, class ID, species, genus, family, date, average user quality vote, locality, GPS coordinates (when available), author, and year of integration. Novelties over previous years are the explicit multi-image query scenario, user image-quality ratings, the new "Branch" view type, and the increase from 250 to 500 species.

The task is a species retrieval task in which queries are plant observations (sets of images of the same individual plant, taken by the same person on the same day with the same device) rather than single images; teams could submit up to four runs and had to declare any human assistance. The dataset was split into training and test parts using a constrained random rule, with one third of pictures in the test set, and test metadata purged of taxon names and quality ratings. The primary metric is the inverse rank score of the correct species, averaged per author then across authors; a secondary metric applies the same idea at image level.

74 groups registered, 10 submitted runs, and 6 teams provided 14 complementary image runs. Techniques ranged from Fisher vectors/GMM with SIFT, bag-of-visual-words with opponent SIFT and TF-IDF, deep CNNs, global descriptors, hashing/matching and shape-based approaches (BME TMIT, FINKI, I3S, IBM AU, IV-Processing, MIRACL, PlantNet, QUT, Sabanki-Okan, SZTE).

IBM AU's Fisher-vector runs performed best (0.471 for FV+CNN+segmentation, 0.459 FV+CNN, 0.454 FV), with PlantNet second (up to 0.289) and CNN alone lower (0.271), attributed to deep models needing more training data; pre-training on external data was not permitted. Metadata exploitation was rare and MIRACL's textual/structural use degraded performance, while locality and GPS went unused. Combining images of the same observation improved on single images but only modestly, and LeafScan and Flower were the best-performing categories. The authors suggest extending a 2015 task to the whole French flora (~5,000 species).

The DDR DMM TILER extended addressing map adds 4 GB through a 33rd address bit for rotated and mirrored frame-buffer views. The HDVPSS and ISS subsystems can access the entire extended range, while other masters can access a single view through the 512-MB TILER window in the base 4-GB memory map.

Terminal-functions tables document signal names, pin multiplexing, ball numbers, package designators, pin types, internal pull states, supply voltages, and pin functions. They cover boot, camera, DCAN, DDR2/DDR3, EMAC, GPIO, GPMC, HDMI, I2C, McASP, PCIe, reset/interrupt/JTAG, SD, SPI, clocks, timers, UART, USB, video, analog TV output, and supply pins. The tables also identify pin-control registers, de-selected input states, and multimuxed functions. Internal pullup and pulldown behavior is specified during and after reset, including DDR, I2C, JTAG, and other peripheral requirements.

Boot configuration is determined by sampling BTMODE[15:0] when POR or RESET is deasserted and latching the values in CONTROL_STATUS. BTMODE[15:11] configures GPMC CS0 bus width, wait enable, and address/data multiplexing; BTMODE[10] selects GPMC XIP muxing options; BTMODE[9:8] selects the Ethernet PHY mode; and BTMODE[4:0] selects the boot-mode order. Boot attempts proceed through the first through fourth listed modes until one succeeds. BTMODE[7:5] is reserved, and PCIe boot uses BTMODE[15:12] for addressing. ROM-configured boot options include XIP NOR/OneNAND/ROM, NAND, I2C, MMC/SD, SPI, EMAC, PCIe, and UART.

Pin multiplexing is controlled by MUXMODE bits in PINCNTL1–PINCNTL270. The default MUXMODE of zero tri-states most pin outputs, although shared inputs are generally routed to all associated peripherals. Multimuxed functions can be assigned to multiple device pins.

Unused signal pins may be left unconnected unless otherwise specified, but unused inputs must not float; internal or external pullup/pulldown resistors are recommended. Supply pins must remain connected even when associated functions are unused. External pull resistors are recommended for tri-stated boot/configuration pins and when an internal pull does not match the desired state, with typical values of 1 kΩ to oppose internal pulls and 20 kΩ for boot/configuration pins.

The CAG’s 2015/16 report identified public-procurement noncompliance and poor contract and project management. Eight sampled contracts worth Sh63 billion ($1 billion) were improperly managed; goods and services worth Sh23.98 billion were procured without competitive quotations, and Sh2.48 billion was procured without tender-board approval. Ten public entities procured Sh11.253 billion without valid contracts, and some contracts lacked Attorney General review. Asset management remained weak, including 37 dilapidated buildings across 12 embassies and ten undeveloped embassy plots.

Offensive switches are positional exchanges between attacking teammates used to disrupt defenders and create passing options. They may be called orally or occur naturally, with or without the ball. In a basic horizontal switch, teammates run diagonally in opposite directions, forming an X, and temporarily exchange positions before returning to their usual roles. A vertical switch exchanges players from back-to-front or front-to-back, while a lateral switch exchanges them side-to-side. The objective is to make defenders hesitate, change assignments, or become uncertain about whom to mark, potentially freeing a runner in a 2-vs-1 or confusing two defenders in a 2-vs-2. Lateral switches can help defeat an offside trap. Players should orally signal “switch back” when the exchange is complete and they can resume their original positions without compromising play.

Tesla’s Form 8-K reported that Joseph Gebbia was appointed to its Board of Directors effective September 25, 2022. Tesla disclosed no related-party transactions requiring Item 404(a) reporting. Gebbia qualified for Tesla’s standard outside-director compensation package but waived cash compensation until further notice and equity compensation until July 2023, pending new Board determinations. He was not appointed to any Board committee, and a September 28 blog post announcing his appointment was filed as Exhibit 99.1.

The paper introduces MatterMech, a benchmark of 4,800 questions across eight nanomaterial-synthesis subdomains to evaluate whether large language models can reason about condition-specific physicochemical mechanisms. The benchmark was built from roughly 17,000 papers using Claude-3.5-Sonnet for initial multiple-choice question generation, a Worker–Reviewer–Critic multi-agent system for four rounds of validation, conversion to text-infilling questions, and human quality review. Multi-agent refinement improved BERTScore precision from 0.8466 to 0.8666, while 40 manually sampled questions received mean quality scores near 4 on logic, distractor plausibility, and question quality. The authors also release MatterDB, containing 31,735 papers paired with extracted synthesis mechanisms and source literature.

Evaluation of 14 models found that Qwen-Max achieved the highest multiple-choice accuracy at 61.99%, while Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct led text-infilling performance at 35.25%. Models generally performed better at logical reasoning than precise reproduction of domain terminology, and performance varied modestly across subdomains. Larger Qwen2.5 models performed better according to logarithmic scaling relationships. Principle-guided prompting outperformed automatic chain-of-thought prompting across three models, improving accuracy while reducing output length and variability. The study identifies limitations including the absence of expert-authored annotations and the static nature of the benchmark as materials science evolves.

Stockholders also approved, on an advisory basis, named executive officer compensation, with 392,487,062 shares for and 5,389,294 against, and ratified PricewaterhouseCoopers LLP as the independent registered accounting firm for the fiscal year ending January 31, 2016. Dr. Edith Mbagwu recommends SMART goal setting to create realistic, sustainable weight-loss goals: specific, measurable, attainable, realistic, and time-based. Goals should clearly define exercise and dietary plans, use motivating measures such as weight or body-fat percentage, and be reassessed periodically. Smaller milestones can support larger goals; burning 500 calories daily may lead to about one pound of fat loss per week. Motivation, such as training for a race or reaching a health target, can help people stay committed, while schedules should be adjusted to prioritize health.

An EF-0 tornado touched down Friday near the Prince William County line, damaging a mile-long, 100-yard-wide path in Fauquier County. It lasted two minutes, produced 75-mph winds, and caused no injuries; an EF-1 tornado struck Salisbury four days earlier.

Apple Inc.’s Form 10-Q for the fiscal quarter ended June 29, 2019 reported third-quarter net sales of $53.809 billion, up 1% or $544 million from $53.265 billion a year earlier. Higher Wearables, Home and Accessories and Services sales partly offset lower iPhone sales, while foreign-currency weakness adversely affected sales. Third-quarter gross margin was $20.227 billion, operating income was $11.544 billion, net income was $10.044 billion, and diluted earnings per share were $2.18. For the nine months, net sales were $196.134 billion, net income was $41.570 billion, and diluted earnings per share were $8.86.

Third-quarter product sales totaled $42.354 billion, including iPhone sales of $25.986 billion, Mac sales of $5.820 billion, iPad sales of $5.023 billion, and Wearables, Home and Accessories sales of $5.525 billion. Geographic segment sales were $25.056 billion for the Americas, $11.925 billion for Europe, $9.157 billion for Greater China, $4.082 billion for Japan, and $3.589 billion for the Rest of Asia Pacific.

At June 29, 2019, total assets were $322.239 billion, total liabilities were $225.783 billion, and shareholders’ equity was $96.456 billion. Cash and cash equivalents totaled $50.530 billion, with short- and long-term marketable securities of $44.084 billion and $115.996 billion. During the first nine months, operating and investing activities generated $49.481 billion and $46.694 billion, while financing activities used $69.937 billion. Ending cash, cash equivalents and restricted cash was $52.151 billion.

Apple adopted several accounting standards, including full retrospective adoption of the revenue standard, which led to reclassification of certain bundled-service amortization from products to services without materially changing prior-period net sales. Adoption of ASU 2016-16 resulted in $2.7 billion of net deferred tax assets, a $128 million reduction in other non-current assets, and a $2.6 billion increase in retained earnings.

The Board increased the share-repurchase authorization from $100 billion to $175 billion, of which $78.2 billion had been used by June 29. VirnetX litigation remained under appeal and Patent and Trademark Office proceedings; Apple and Qualcomm settled their litigation in April 2019 and entered multi-year license and supply agreements. Litigation and investigations concerning iPhone performance-management features also continued. Players are urged to focus on winning, keep shooting despite mistakes, and pursue rebounds. Any rebound gathered by a teammate is acceptable.

The study examines difficulties encountered in university foreign-language education after the Covid-19 pandemic shifted instruction from face-to-face to distance education. It reviews distance education’s development, synchronous, asynchronous, and hybrid models, learning management systems, advantages and limitations, and challenges in language instruction.

An online survey of 294 German and English students, including undergraduate and graduate students, used a 53-item, six-subscale distance education problems scale; descriptive statistics and t-tests were applied. Microsoft Teams and Zoom were the most used platforms. Students rated internet and computer problems highest, particularly connection interruptions, followed by student-related problems such as lack of motivation and low participation. Course-content problems centered on insufficient mutual communication, while assessment difficulties included inability to measure skill-based gains. Teacher-related problems were rated lowest, although monotonic instruction and limited technological skills were noted.

Problems did not differ between German and English students. Male students reported more student-related problems than female students. Students without prior training in distance-education programs, a suitable home study space, or home internet access reported significantly more problems.

The researchers concluded that distance education was not successful for foreign-language teaching and was less effective than face-to-face instruction. Materials were insufficient, assessment was problematic, participation and preparation were weak, and both students and teachers lacked knowledge of distance-education methods. Recommendations included awareness and training for students and teachers, improved preparation of materials and assessment, virtual-classroom and communication skills, and a hybrid model combining face-to-face and distance education.

Yellen told the Senate Banking Committee that the FOMC expects moderate economic expansion, further job-market strengthening, and inflation gradually reaching 2%. At upcoming meetings, policymakers will assess whether employment and inflation track those expectations, in which case another federal funds rate adjustment would likely be appropriate. She warned that waiting too long to remove accommodation could necessitate rapid rate increases, disrupt financial markets, and cause recession. Uncertainty includes fiscal and other policy changes, productivity growth, and developments abroad. Policy will remain data-dependent, with fiscal changes potentially affecting the outlook. She urged productivity-enhancing policies and sustainable federal accounts. Unemployment was 4.8% in January, labor underutilization improved, and wage growth accelerated. Business investment gained late in the year, sentiment improved, and inflation compensation rose from very low levels while longer-term survey expectations changed little.

Dereck James Harrison, 23, pleaded guilty in Wyoming to first-degree murder and kidnapping in the abduction and killing of train worker Kay Porter Ricks, 63. The lecture quantizes the Dirac field using anticommutators rather than ordinary commutators. Standard commutator quantization would yield an unbounded-below Hamiltonian and symmetric statistics, whereas anticommutation makes the relation self-consistent and produces a positive-definite mode Hamiltonian, apart from a divergent zero-point energy. Expanding the field in positive- and negative-energy modes introduces annihilation and creation operators satisfying fermionic anticommutation relations. Their vacuum is annihilated by all annihilation operators and has the lowest energy.

Each mode behaves as a fermionic harmonic oscillator that can be excited only once because the creation operator squares to zero. This yields the Pauli exclusion principle and Fermi–Dirac statistics. The one-particle states have momentum eigenvalue \(\mathbf{k}\), two polarizations, and spin \(1/2\), verified by constructing the Lorentz angular-momentum charge. Particles and antiparticles have equal mass and spin but opposite charges generated by a conserved \(U(1)\) current. After removing an infinite additive constant and assigning the vacuum zero charge, the particle and antiparticle have charges \(+1\) and \(-1\). Applied to electrons, this identifies the antiparticle as the positron, whose later discovery confirmed Dirac’s prediction. The broader spin-statistics correspondence says half-integer-spin fields require anticommutation and Fermi–Dirac statistics, while integer-spin fields use commutators and Bose–Einstein statistics; in \(2+1\) dimensions, anyonic statistics are also possible.

The lecture then introduces Dirac-field correlation functions. Wightman, retarded, and time-ordered Green’s functions are defined using anticommutators and expressed as differential operators acting on scalar Green’s functions. Their momentum-space forms involve the Dirac operator, including the key expression \((i\!\not\!k+m)^{-1}\) with the usual \(i\epsilon\) prescription. Finally, the lecturer previews chiral and Majorana fermions: both reduce the eight real components of a Dirac spinor to four, with Majorana fermions serving as their own antiparticles.

The ADS868xW is a fully differential, 16-bit SAR ADC data-acquisition device with an integrated analog front end and precision reference. Data-transfer frames begin when the host pulls CONVST/CS low, load the output word into a 32-bit shift register, and exchange command and output bits through SCLK, SDI, and SDO-x. Pulling CONVST/CS high ends the frame and executes a valid 32-bit command. A 32-clock frame is optimal; shorter frames invalidate writes but can provide partial output data, while in longer frames the last 32 input bits form the command.

Writes are synchronous to SCLK and support byte and half-word commands. Output data for the next frame depends on the preceding command and DATA_VAL settings: fixed patterns, 8- or 16-bit register data, or the latest 16-bit conversion result. Optional output flags include device address, input-range information, active AVDD and input alarms, and parity.

The multiSPI interface supports four configurable SPI-compatible protocols for configuration and single- or dual-SDO reads, plus source-synchronous transfers using internal or external clocks. Dual-SDO mode outputs two bits per clock, while source-synchronous mode supplies the output clock on RVS. SPI-00-S is the default protocol after power-up or asynchronous reset.

Configuration registers control device identification, reset and power management, SPI and output protocols, output formatting, input/reference ranges, alarms, and alarm thresholds. RST_PWRCTL_REG writes require protection key 69h.

An example industrial module combines an ADS8681W with an MUX36D08 to provide eight software-configurable voltage or current channels. Programmable input alarms support threshold and hysteresis-based monitoring, including NTC thermistor temperature sensing.

AVDD and DVDD require independent supply decoupling. NAP and power-down modes reduce consumption; power-down retains registers and keeps the interface active. Recommended PCB layouts separate analog and digital routing and place specified capacitors close to supply, reference, and REFCAP pins.

This exploratory study examined whether a mitochondrial polygenic score (MGS) and its interactions with lifestyle and environmental factors influence age at onset (AAO) in Parkinson’s disease. The analysis included 9,745 patients from AMP-PD, Fox Insight, and a Tunisian Arab-Berber cohort: 486 with LRRK2-associated PD and 9,259 with idiopathic PD (iPD). The MGS was based on 14 SNPs, with nine common to all cohorts for cross-cohort analyses and standardized from 0 to 100. Lifestyle and environmental data, including tobacco, caffeine, and pesticide exposure, were available for Fox Insight and the Tunisian cohort.

Higher MGS was associated with earlier AAO in LRRK2-PD (r = −0.15; p = 0.0008), including after adjustment for sex, cohort, and ethnicity; a 1% higher standardized MGS corresponded to approximately one month earlier onset. This association was stronger in European/White patients and weak and nonsignificant in Tunisian/Arab-Berber patients. No overall MGS–AAO association was found in iPD.

Smoking was associated with later AAO only in iPD. Black tea was associated with later AAO in LRRK2-PD, coffee with later AAO in iPD, and caffeinated soda with earlier AAO in both groups. Workplace pesticide exposure was associated with earlier AAO only in iPD.

MGS interactions with coffee and caffeinated soda consumption were detected in LRRK2-PD. Among coffee consumers, median AAO was 55.5 years with high MGS versus 61.2 years with low MGS; among soda consumers, it was 50.0 versus 61.5 years. High-MGS patients who did not consume these beverages generally had later AAO. In iPD, MGS interacted with caffeinated soda consumption and workplace pesticide exposure: median AAO was 60.9 versus 62.7 years by MGS among soda consumers and 59.6 versus 62.5 years among pesticide-exposed patients. Fox Insight-only analyses confirmed the soda and workplace-pesticide interactions.

No interactions were found for smoking or tea, and dose or duration analyses did not show interactions. Exploratory p-values were not corrected for multiple testing. Limitations included cohort differences, array versus whole-genome genotyping, use of nine SNPs for the full cross-cohort MGS, questionnaire measurement caveats, lifestyle data being unavailable for AMP-PD, and limited population diversity. The findings indicate that lifestyle and environmental exposures can modify the MGS’s association with PD onset and warrant functional investigation.

On Nov. 21, 2001, Enron announced that lenders had extended repayment of a $690 million note due Nov. 27 to mid-December, giving it more time to restructure debt and avoid a liquidity crisis. Enron also closed the remaining $450 million of a $1 billion secured credit facility from J.P. Morgan Chase and Salomon Smith Barney, backed by Northern Natural Gas assets, following a $550 million Transwestern Pipeline-backed tranche.

Enron and Dynegy reaffirmed their commitment to a merger announced Nov. 9, while Dynegy continued due diligence and sought regulatory approvals. The deal was expected to close around the end of the third quarter of 2002. Enron disclosed that it faced $9.15 billion in debt due by 2003 and had less than $2 billion in cash or credit lines, while reports cited reduced trading activity, partners’ credit concerns and uncertainty over the merger.

Enron shares fell roughly 22%–33% Wednesday after declining 23% Tuesday, and its bonds also sank. Goldman Sachs downgraded Enron and Dynegy to “market perform,” citing major liquidity and customer-confidence problems; CIBC also cut Enron to “hold,” while Commerzbank questioned its viability. ChevronTexaco, which owned 26% of Dynegy, expressed confidence in the merger.

The compilation also briefly covered dismissed tobacco lawsuits in Florida, a General Motors of Canada supplier agreement, analyst rating changes involving Microsoft and Xerox, and share movements in several other companies.

The application is a continuation of U.S. applications 17/541,766 and 16/410,734 and PCT Application PCT/CN2018/101279, with priority claimed from three 2018 provisional applications. It concerns periodic beam failure measurements for digital communications, particularly high-frequency 5G NR systems where pathloss and blockage can disrupt beamformed links.

A UE determines measurement-period duration from the periodicity of beam failure detection reference signals (BFD RSs) it actually assesses, typically periodic CSI-RS resources, SS blocks, or PBCH blocks having a quasi-co-located relationship with DMRSs of monitored PDCCH receptions. Embodiments use the shortest assessed BFD RS period, optionally combined with a specified value, or the longest assessed period. Excluding unassessed BFD RSs helps ensure each measurement period contains a relevant signal and avoids distorting beam-failure tracking.

During each period, the UE monitors the relevant BFD RSs and evaluates their signal quality or BLER. If all monitored signals fail the specified threshold, the UE reports a beam failure instance, potentially identifying the failed signals. A PHY-layer entity performs these measurements and reports to a MAC or other higher layer, which counts consecutive instances and may declare beam failure after a specified count, optionally requiring every assessed BFD RS to have failed at least once. The UE may then identify a candidate beam and send a beam failure recovery request.

The passage also addresses periods with no transmitted BFD RS, such as when CSI-RS resources overlap control signaling. Such periods may be ignored for counter updates, treated as beam failure instances, or identified through signaling so the MAC layer does not incorrectly reset its consecutive-failure counter.

U.S. stocks closed slightly lower Tuesday but well off their lows as tensions involving Russia, Syria and North Korea weighed on sentiment and pushed investors toward safe havens. The paper introduces MOTO, a three-layer optimization framework for mapping local transition-state networks around a specified minimum. Its components are a multi-objective explorer that balances candidate diversity, physical feasibility, and minimum-mode separability; an HVP-based bilayer minimum-mode-following kernel that uses Lanczos or LOBPCG to estimate low-curvature modes and L-BFGS or conjugate gradient to ascend to index-1 saddles; and deterministic two-sided saddle descent to certify connectivity, deduplicate outcomes, and archive discovered minima.

In atomistic-spin benchmarks, HVP-based eigensolvers closely matched explicit-Hessian minimum-mode accuracy while scaling more favorably in time and memory. The implementation supports up to \(10^6\) spins, with less than 1 GB incremental memory and 0.5 seconds wall time for calculating the two lowest curvature modes. On a \(70\times70\) spin system, the HVP kernel used about 0.01% of the explicit-Hessian incremental peak memory and delivered a tenfold speedup. The explorer increased diversity and spectral separation, while both outer optimizers converged toward the index-1 condition \(\lambda_1<0<\lambda_2\).

Applied to a DFT-parameterized Pd/Fe/Ir(111) model, MOTO mapped twelve saddles around a Néel skyrmion and an antiskyrmion, revealing up to 32 transition pathways. Bidirectional descents identified meron- and antimeron-mediated duplication, annihilation, chiral-droplet formation, and boundary-defect effects on topological charge. In an artificial Bloch-type model, the framework recovered established collapse and escape mechanisms and identified additional saddle families. Transfer to a Cartesian Ni(111) heptamer benchmark recovered low-barrier edge, corner, and concerted rearrangement pathways without changing the algorithmic core.

The study notes that masks, objectives, solver settings, and line-search thresholds must be tailored appropriately, while near-degenerate curvature can make single-direction ascent unreliable. Proposed future work includes automated hyperparameter tuning, coverage-based stopping rules, and tighter integration with two-ended path solvers.

NVIDIA Corporation’s Form 10-Q for the quarter ended April 30, 2017 presented unaudited consolidated financial statements under U.S. GAAP. NVIDIA settled $605 million principal of 1% convertible notes, issued 24 million shares, recognized a $14 million conversion loss and had $222 million principal outstanding. NVIDIA disclosed Polaris patent litigation in the United States and Germany, recorded no contingency accrual and said losses were not reasonably estimable. Management concluded disclosure controls were effective, with no material changes in internal controls or previously disclosed risk factors.

The passage argues that recent psychological and neuroscience research undermines Damore’s claims that innate, fixed biological differences explain gender disparities. Evidence indicates that men and women are more similar than different, many abilities exist on spectra, and brains contain mixtures of male and female characteristics. Brains are plastic and can change through experience, including spatial-cognition training, while spatial-skill gaps have diminished or reversed in some cultures. Stereotype threat, perceived status, and self-critical mindsets can also affect anxiety, performance, and brain activity. Empowerment and environmental changes may counter these effects, suggesting that stereotypical, deterministic expectations can contribute to the disparities Damore attributed to biology.
DoLE-6 is preparing assistance for Boracay workers, including job fairs, TESDA skills training, and a rapid-response team to profile displaced workers if the proposed closure proceeds.
