Reports indicated he could miss 2–3 weeks, is likely to miss Week 5 against Houston and could miss Week 6 against the Rams. Jackson did not practice during Week 5 and was doubtful against Houston; one report suggested he may not return until after the Week 7 bye.

As a potential government shutdown looms, Medicare’s temporary hospital-at-home waiver is set to expire Sept. 30. UMass Memorial paused admissions while other hospitals reduced or ended programs, threatening home-based inpatient care and adding strain to crowded facilities. Uncertainty over funding has already halted several programs and discouraged expansion, though a bipartisan five-year extension is under consideration.

This study examined how ICT and computer-assisted language learning (CALL) are integrated into EFL initial teacher education at a teacher-education institution in southern Vietnam. Guided by Hong’s model, it used a convergent mixed-methods design involving 67 final-year EFL pre-service teachers and three teacher educators. Data came from a four-point Likert survey, a focus group with six pre-service teachers, and interviews with all three educators; quantitative and qualitative analyses used descriptive statistics and inductive thematic analysis.

Pre-service teachers reported substantial opportunities to learn CALL-related knowledge, especially searching for and downloading resources, using word-processing software, creating digitally supported lessons, and applying ICT pedagogies. Less opportunity was reported for supervising online work, selecting personalized online exercises, and troubleshooting equipment. Teachers mainly used ICT for resource discovery, lesson archiving, information exchange, and developing teaching materials. Educators used ICT weekly, sometimes in every lesson, although some described CALL preparation as outdated or superficial.

Major barriers included educators’ limited confidence, skills, time, and fear of change; unreliable internet and equipment; slow technical support; and student disengagement. The absence of official ICT/CALL requirements and consistent institutional guidelines also produced variation in educators’ practices. The study recommends clearer policies, explicit guidelines, stronger administrative and technical support, and continuing professional development focused on pedagogical and technological competence. Limitations include the small, single-institution sample and the absence of analysis of educators’ assessments and the curriculum’s influence.

The Pennsylvania Supreme Court held that the “intact value” of Senator William Flinn’s trust assets generally must be fixed as of his February 19, 1924, death. His will made the trusts effective at death, and provisions allowing five years for estate administration did not suspend them. Fixing value when the trustee received the stocks in January 1929 would also permit improper income accumulation under the Act of April 18, 1853.

However, stock of Booth & Flinn Company received by the executors as a dividend in January 1925 had to be valued at its book value when received. Booth & Flinn was a separate corporate entity, and Flinn’s controlling interest did not allow the court to disregard that entity when valuing its assets.

The Court also upheld the use of a per-diem average of Gulf Oil’s annual earnings to determine undistributed earnings attributable to the period before Flinn’s death. The lower court’s decree was affirmed as modified, with costs assessed against the estate.

The article argues that global citizenship education should be supplemented with concepts from international politics to help young people understand conflict, state power, peaceful cooperation, and opportunities for political engagement. Although the field draws on peace, human rights, development, multicultural, global education, and global literacy traditions, its emphasis on transnational participation and advocacy leaves insufficient attention to military and economic security, international relations, why conflicts arise, and how cooperation might replace violence.

Three international-politics perspectives are presented. Realism treats international politics as an anarchic competition in which security and survival are priorities, states pursue power and self-interest, and cooperation serves state interests. It helps explain rivalry involving Russia, China, NATO, and Ukraine but leaves limited scope for global citizens, making domestic influence on foreign policy more important. Regionalism explains cooperation through shared interests, collective action, trade, and regional integration, noting that European integration did not prevent conflict with Russia and that the war has prompted securitisation, self-sufficiency, and closer Russian–Chinese economic ties. Member states retain significant power within regional institutions. Institutionalism examines how rules, practices, and organisations create predictable cooperation and constrain sovereignty. It illustrates NATO and EU responses to the war, the UN’s limited capacity, and how institutions provide arenas for civic activism while remaining shaped by states and domestic political traditions.

International cooperation depends on state interests and the characteristics of the issue. It may involve single best efforts, weakest-link efforts, aggregate efforts to provide global public goods, or coordination around common standards. Cooperation can occur without global citizenship, although self-interest and free-riding may weaken it. Successful examples include European integration and Arctic fishing-quota management between Norway and Russia.

The article therefore recommends broadening global citizenship education beyond environmental and social issues to include security, economic interests, foreign policy, and citizens’ influence on national policy. Teaching should address institutional arenas for activism, historical and current conflict and cooperation, power and dependency among states, and media manipulation, misinformation, polarization, and propaganda. It should also use non-European perspectives and acknowledge conflicts truthfully while recognising that states and institutions can also solve problems and secure peace.

The speaker says the team has been overmotivated and needs to calm down, play disciplined hockey, and avoid penalties. Penalty killing has been strong under Mike Ramsey, with patience and coordinated pressure emphasized. The opponent’s talent, including Zubov, Modano, Hull, and Lehtinen, makes overcommitting especially dangerous.

President Wilson announced that the armistice had been signed, declared America’s war aims accomplished, and called for helping establish just democracy through example, counsel, and material aid. Edward M. House praised Wilson and the triumph of democracy. Secretary of State Robert Lansing conveyed American congratulations and admiration to Britain and France for their steadfastness and valor. French Foreign Minister Stephen Pichon expressed gratitude for America’s role in victory and renewed Franco-American brotherhood, while Japanese Foreign Minister Katsuo Uchida congratulated Wilson and expressed hope for a just and happy peace. The Greek Legation credited American intervention with protecting freedom and securing Greece’s national unity, and pledged continued cooperation in constructing the Society of Nations. Wilson also told British Prime Minister David Lloyd George that he admired Lloyd George’s address and welcomed their shared approach to the difficult task ahead.

A mixed-methods phenomenological study examined whether music software could be integrated into the general music education course at a Caribbean university to teach pre-service early childhood and primary teachers. Participants were 24 students—15 in a Bachelor of Education program and nine in Early Childhood Care and Education—and completed an anonymous questionnaire and a Sibelius music-notation assignment. They received step-by-step software instruction over three weeks and composed eight bars of music using specified time signatures and note values.

Questionnaire results showed that 11 participants believed the software enhanced conceptual understanding, seven were unsure, and six disagreed. Half were very or somewhat comfortable using it, 67% supported continued technology use, and 75% wanted further training. Most preferred traditional approaches and were neutral about motivation, although the researchers linked motivation to students’ comfort and assignment success. Four participants did not submit the composition assignment; the remaining submissions achieved 90% accuracy, and most participants placed the correct number of beats in each bar.

The findings indicated that music software was relatively easy and inexpensive to integrate, positively affected comprehension and performance, and could support a more student-centered approach. The researchers recommended continuing its limited use, providing progressive training for students and lecturers, assessing technological competence during practicum, and adding technology-focused outcomes and assessments to music courses.
The court affirmed the order dismissing John Gracy’s writ of habeas corpus and remanding him, with four judges concurring and Justice Manning dissenting.

Readers' feedback shows they prefer accuracy over speed, so the writer keeps the 1pm deadline with early nights on school days; he left full-time employment in 2002 as self-employed. Trading update: 145p (up 17%, volatile), 129.8m shares, £188.2m market cap. Despite holding a short position, he discusses Oozi Cats' CEO resignation, with US fraud allegations admitted true; a review found his indictment was withheld from advisers.

The James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) directly identified the progenitor of Type II supernova SN2025pht in the spiral galaxy NGC 1637, about 40 million light-years from Earth—the first supernova progenitor detected with JWST. Combining JWST infrared images with archival Hubble observations revealed a massive, intensely red supergiant hidden by dense dust before its explosion. The star radiated about 100,000 times more light than the Sun, but surrounding dust made it over 100 times dimmer in visible light.

The progenitor was unusually red and dusty, with carbon-rich rather than oxygen-rich circumstellar dust, possibly because strong convection brought carbon from deeper layers to its surface. The findings support the hypothesis that many massive red supergiants explode but are obscured by thick dust, explaining why their progenitors have rarely been observed. The team is now searching for similar stars, with the upcoming Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope expected to aid the effort.

ECGs record cardiac electrical activity as depolarisation and repolarisation waves, but the mechanisms underlying normal and abnormal T-wave morphologies and ST-segment changes remain incompletely explained. This study introduces the “Simplified Egg and Changing Yolk Model” to describe ventricular repolarisation. The model represents the heart as an asymmetrical egg centred on Wilson’s Central Terminal, with repolarisation expanding outward like ripples. Each ECG lead detects signals moving toward it as positive and signals moving away as negative; their net difference determines the trace. In normal repolarisation, balanced signals produce the isoelectric ST segment, while an asymmetric region called the “T-zone” generates the T-wave.

The model reproduces ST depression and elevation through differently positioned damaged or electrically inactive regions and can generate peaked, flattened, inverted, and biphasic T-waves. It proposes that ventricular repolarisation begins with the Q-wave and continues through the T-wave, challenging the conventional separation of the ST segment and T-wave and the interpretation of reciprocal ST changes as uniquely indicating ischemia or infarction. The model also distinguishes the corrected QT interval, which ends when repolarisation exits the T-zone, from the QTp interval, measured from Q-wave onset to T-wave peak. Because QTc measurement can be ambiguous and depends on correction formulae, the authors recommend QTp as a more clearly defined and reliable measure, particularly for assessing QT-prolonging medication effects and potential arrhythmia risk. QTp and QTc cannot be determined for flat T-waves. Future work will examine the U-wave, atrial repolarisation, coronary-artery distribution, and validation of QTp across populations.

The disclosure describes methods, systems, and software for creating interactive virtual game environments from real-world objects and scanned scenes. A user selects physical items, arranges them into a physical model, targets the model with a camera or depth-sensitive 3D camera, and captures a partial or complete scan. Physical properties such as shape, dimensions, color, texture, and transparency are associated with corresponding locations in the scan. The resulting digital 3D representation is converted into a voxel-based representation or a scaled virtual toy construction model composed of virtual construction elements.

Conversion rules translate detectable physical properties into virtual properties according to a game context or theme. Rules may be static or adaptive based on detected scene properties, time, camera location, user profile, or recognized objects. Recognized objects can select themes, game rules, and game-controlling elements. For example, a red box may become an erupting lava mountain, while a cup may become an iceberg. Game elements can evolve, change color or texture, move, spawn resources or characters, and respond to user actions or modifications and rescans of the physical model.

Physical objects may be recognized through image processing, augmented-reality or QR markers, RFID, Bluetooth, or other detection methods. A library can store known objects’ 3D representations, attributes, themes, and functions. Recognized scanned geometry may be removed, reconstructed, or replaced with a stored model and inserted as a movable player character, non-player character, or interactive object. Known construction models may include predefined functions such as rotating wheels, opening doors, ejecting water, or firing projectiles.

An efficient voxelization method distributes points across surface elements and maps them to voxels using coordinates divided by voxel dimensions. Surface attributes can be averaged or interpolated according to intersection locations and transferred to the corresponding voxels. When matching colors to a discrete palette, colors are represented in a 3D color space, and the search is restricted to candidates within a calculated radius to reduce computation. Embodiments may use RGB distance or LAB/Delta E comparisons.

Interactive game systems include a capturing device, display, storage, and processor, potentially integrated into a mobile device or divided between networked client and host systems. Augmented-reality overlays can indicate the area targeted for scanning. Stored virtual environments permit gameplay without the physical model remaining present. A cyclic gameplay process creates an environment from physical objects, plays one or more game segments, and responds to outcomes through tasks, rewards, unlocks, and new cycles. Physical toy characters and tools may be scanned or identified to create corresponding virtual characters and unlock skills, tools, or powers. Applications include nurture, battle, racing, and especially role-playing action and resource games.

This article examines the experiences of those leading education-related undergraduate programmes (BA Education Studies and similar) in further education (FE) colleges in England, using Hodgson and Spours' (2009) 'four levels of a lifelong learning ecology' framework. At the macro layer, it traces how FE colleges' education-related provision grew from 1990s–2000s teacher-training initiatives, the 1997 Dearing report, education studies degrees, widening participation policies and foundation degrees from 2001, culminating in varied vocational-to-Level 6 progression pathways. At the exo layer, it covers colleges' relationships with local employers and with validating, franchising or degree-awarding HEIs. At the meso layer, programme leaders are characterised as a 'keystone species' — central, anchoring figures whose personalised support and strong staff–student relationships shape learners' identities as higher education students. At the micro layer, courses reflect diverse, often 'non-traditional' communities, and leaders' roles are linked to notions of stewardship and social justice.

Data come from a British Education Studies Association-funded project (Pulsford et al., 2021): an online questionnaire (February–September 2020) with 70 programme leaders (14 from English FE colleges, 46 'post-92' universities, 10 Russell Group and other 'pre-92' universities; 14 incomplete responses unusable) and 11 follow-up interviews, four with FE-based leaders.

Findings show FE programme leaders largely entered their roles through informal routes rather than formal application; all thirteen respondents reporting qualifications held master's degrees, three held or were nearing doctorates (versus 50% of HE-based leaders), and five of 14 held HEA fellowship (versus 66% in HE). The role is poorly defined, with leaders relying on craft wisdom; FE teams are small (mean permanent staff of three versus ten in HEIs) and over two thirds of FE leaders hold line-management responsibilities. Three strands of responsibility emerged: administrative and organisational demands (recruitment, audits, National Student Survey, prior learning accreditation, liaison with HEI partners on development, moderation and joint delivery); providing learner support (small cohorts of 11–20 students, combining levels and programmes, nurturing a higher education culture); and responding to students' pastoral needs. Interviewees described FE provision as empowering for students progressing into teaching, often alongside resits of GCSE maths and English. Overall, macro and exo demands can obscure meso and micro work, and the article introduces 'sightlines' — improved outward engagement via research, scholarly activity, and partnerships with employers and other institutions — as a means of supporting these leaders. The study was funded by the 2019/20 BESA Research Grant, with ethics approval from the Department of Education Studies at the University of Warwick.

The UAE announced the Mars 2117 Project, aiming to establish a human settlement on Mars by 2117. Unveiled by Dubai ruler Sheikh Mohammed bin Rashid al-Maktoum, it will partner with international research institutions and develop faster travel to Mars, beginning with an Emirati scientific team. The announcement follows the UAE’s planned 2021 Mars Probe mission, while SpaceX founder Elon Musk also presented plans for Mars colonization and lower travel costs.

A U.S. District Judge sentenced Gbenga Ogundele, alias Benson Ogundele, to 234 months in prison for conspiracy to commit wire fraud and money laundering and aggravated identity theft. His wife, Moji Popoola, received 18 months, followed by three years of supervised release to be served in home detention. Ogundele was ordered to forfeit $2,195,103.36, while Popoola was ordered to forfeit approximately $165,000 and pay $34,100 in restitution.

From January 2011 to May 18, 2015, conspirators used online dating sites and other communications to cultivate relationships with vulnerable victims nationwide, then solicited money through false claims involving hospital bills, travel, overseas businesses and foreign taxes. Victims paid between $1,720 and $50,000 through bank accounts and checks. The conspirators used victims’ identifying information and concealed funds through transfers, cashier’s checks and other payments.

Popoola’s brother Babatunde was sentenced to 12 years and ordered to pay $465,170.76 in restitution. Victor Oyewumi Oloyede received 234 months, while three other co-conspirators pleaded guilty to money-laundering conspiracy and awaited sentencing. Funmilayo Joyce Shodeke separately received 13 months of probation for conducting an unlicensed money-transmitting business and was ordered to forfeit $29,900.

The passage describes a divisional patent application for a novel compound represented by Chemical Formula 1 and an organic light emitting device containing the compound. The application claims priority from Korean Patent Application No. 10-2015-0149714 and is a national-phase entry of PCT/KR2016/012157, with disclosures incorporated by reference from related applications.

The compound includes defined triazine-based structures, aryl or heterocyclic Ar groups, and specified linkers L and substituents. The specification defines suitable substituents, including alkyl, cycloalkyl, alkoxy, alkenyl, aryl, heterocyclic, halogen, cyano, and nitro groups, and lists preferred carbon-number ranges. The compound may be incorporated into one or more organic material layers of an organic light emitting device, including hole injection, hole transport, light emitting, electron transport, electron injection, electron blocking, or hole blocking layers. Normal, inverted, top-emission, bottom-emission, and dual-emission device arrangements are described. Devices may be fabricated by vacuum deposition or solution-processing methods such as spin coating, inkjet printing, screen printing, and spray coating.

The specification reports that the compound may lower driving voltage, improve light-emitting efficiency, and enhance device lifetime through thermal stability. Preparation Examples describe synthesis of numerous compounds through coupling reactions using aldehyde, amidine, boronic acid, and palladium reagents. Device Examples 1–15 use the disclosed compounds as electron transport materials in an ITO-based multilayer device, while Comparative Examples 1–7 use ET1–ET7. At 10 mA/cm², the disclosed compounds produced driving voltages of 3.76–3.91 V and current efficiencies of 5.19–5.46 cd/A, compared with 3.96–4.13 V and 4.89–5.18 cd/A for the comparative materials. The passage states that the disclosed compounds also provided longer lifetimes.

Maria Saliagas, a woman with multiple sclerosis, says Delta Air Lines employees tied her to a regular wheelchair with a blanket when the airline lacked a wheelchair with straps for her flight from Atlanta to Amsterdam. Her son said the restraints caused bruising and distress. Delta expressed regret, contacted the family and offered 20,000 SkyMiles. The family says the points are insufficient and wants a policy change for travelers with disabilities.

Martyn Waghorn credits Kevin Ball with teaching him the fundamentals of football after he nearly left Sunderland as a youth player. Returning to the Stadium of Light with Ipswich, Waghorn hopes to spoil Ball’s afternoon. Ball now serves as a Sunderland ambassador, with several academy players available for the hosts.

GPS routing has increased heavy-truck traffic on Arkansas 43 near Ponca, where steep grades and sharp curves can cause burned brakes, rollovers and crashes. Seven trucks crashed on a two-mile stretch north of town in the past 2½ years, while a truck accident four years earlier destroyed part of a lodge, injured no one but contaminated the Buffalo River with diesel, and involved a fatality. Local officials warn that tourists walking along the highway also face danger. Google Maps and other navigation sites do not adequately show the terrain, and law enforcement officials said most trucks stuck on nearby winding roads are following GPS. The Highway Department plans warning signs near Arkansas 103 reading, “Crooked and steep next 3 miles. Drive with care,” while reevaluating options after another crash. A practical detour would require signs in Harrison, about 25 miles north. One carrier advised drivers hauling over 30,000 pounds to avoid Ponca, particularly in wet or snowy weather.

This medRxiv preprint protocol describes a descriptive, register-based cohort study analyzing periprosthetic joint infection (PJI) after primary total hip arthroplasty. The study aims to describe trends in three revision approaches—debridement, antibiotics and implant retention (DAIR), one-stage exchange, and two-stage exchange—and assess the risk of a second revision after each approach.

The study will include adults who underwent primary THA for any reason at public or private Danish orthopedic departments from 1995 through 2022. Patients with hemiarthroplasty or simultaneous bilateral arthroplasty will be excluded. Follow-up will begin at primary THA and continue until death or first revision, with at least 90 days of follow-up and up to 28 years of available data. Data will come from the Danish Hip Arthroplasty Register, with validation and supplementation through the Danish Patient Register.

Annual revision counts will be reported for all causes and for PJI, including DAIR, one-stage, and two-stage revisions. PJI revisions will also be categorized by the interval between primary surgery and revision: within four weeks, four to 12 weeks, and more than 12 weeks. Analyses will use R, and second-revision risk will be evaluated using Cox proportional hazards models adjusted for calendar time, age, and sex, with Kaplan–Meier plots.

Strengths include the long observation period and simultaneous assessment of all three PJI revision strategies. Limitations include incomplete reporting by some private clinics, surgeon-reported PJI diagnoses without paraclinical verification, and the descriptive, observational nature of the findings. Results may not generalize beyond Denmark, particularly to non-developed countries. The protocol has not been certified by peer review, and the study protocol has not yet been uploaded to OSF.

This application is a continuation of U.S. patent application Ser. No. 17/038,383 (filed Sep. 30, 2020; issued as U.S. Pat. No. 11,363,923), itself a continuation of Ser. No. 16/551,430 (filed Aug. 26, 2019; granted as U.S. Pat. No. 10,820,762), claiming priority to Provisional Application No. 62/723,333 filed Aug. 27, 2018. The invention relates to floor cleaners.

In one embodiment, a floor cleaner includes a vacuum source, a supply tank storing cleaning fluid, a distribution nozzle in fluid communication with the supply tank that dispenses fluid onto a surface to be cleaned, a suction inlet in fluid communication with the vacuum source, and a recovery tank in fluid communication with the vacuum source and suction inlet for storing fluid drawn from the surface. The recovery tank has a tank body with a lower end wall, an upwardly extending sidewall, and an inlet duct extending upwardly from the lower end wall. A strainer is positioned inside the tank body and is movable from a lowermost position to a removed position; it includes a perforated body with an aperture through which the inlet duct extends, and it engages the outer surface of the inlet duct to retain the strainer on the duct. In another embodiment, the strainer includes a handle and a baffle is positioned to inhibit splashing of water against the handle. In yet other embodiments, the recovery tank has an open upper end closed by a removable cover, a shutoff float that closes the cover's suction air outlet when the fluid level exceeds a desired level, and a filter received in a filter aperture in the cover, the filter having a tab for pulling it out for replacement.

Layout: the cleaner includes a base and a body pivotally coupled to the base between an upright storage position and an inclined operating position, along with a supply tank, recovery tank, and vacuum source (motor and fan). The base includes wheels, a suction inlet, and a distribution nozzle; the body includes a handle with a grip and an actuator controlling fluid flow, and a rechargeable lithium-ion battery stored in a battery chamber with a hinged, spring-loaded door. Component placement is arranged so that the center of gravity remains behind the handle axis at all tank fill levels, with the motor between the recovery tank and battery, the battery between the back side and handle axis and between the supply tank and motor, and the supply tank at the back side and recovery tank at the front side.

Recovery tank float and strainer: the cover includes a lid seal offset from the upper end, a baffle surrounding the inlet duct outlet with two arcuate redirecting surfaces (arc angle greater than 120°, and in one embodiment greater than 150°) that turn airflow downward toward the lower end wall to separate fluid from airflow, a suction air outlet, a releasably coupled cage with side apertures and screens having 35–60% open area, and a filter aperture downstream of the outlet. The filter has angled (chamfered) sidewalls and inwardly angled walls that inhibit binding and permit one-handed pivot removal; its media may be pleated, water-repellent paper or cellulosic media. The shutoff float includes a float body, closure, and extension spacing the closure from the fluid; the float body floats on the fluid, surrounds the inlet duct through an aperture, has a chamfered bottom surface matching the body's inclination, and moves from a lowermost position (limited by a lip on the cage) to a position closing the suction air outlet. The strainer's perforated body contacts a strainer lip to space it from the lower end wall, and its aperture may include protrusions for a friction fit on the inlet duct. The recovery tank also has an inset front tank handle.

Tank retention: the body includes a recovery tank recess with a lower inlet and upper outlet; a latch and latch recess removably couple the tank, and projections engaging recesses in the cover hold the cover in place as the narrow, flexible recess portion flexes rearward. In an alternative embodiment the cover is fixed to the tank body, and the projections/recesses stiffen the narrow portion.

Steerable extractor: the body pivots about a first axis parallel to the brushroll axis and offset toward the back side, and about a second steering axis perpendicular to the first and inclined about 30° (ranges of 15°–45°) relative to the surface. A pivotally coupled link/yoke connects body and base, functions as a steering couple, and has slots engaging body protrusions to limit steering to about 30° each way (ranges of 15°–50°). Stops limit pivot about the first axis from about 90° to about 30° from the surface. The hollow yoke has two chambers separating a fluid conduit to the nozzle from base wiring.

Hydrophobic roller: the brushroll protrudes from the lower end of the base and is rotated by a motor through a belt, pulley, or gear transmission; in one embodiment it and the suction inlet ingest debris from the front side. The brushroll's outer cleaning medium may be a hydrophobic tufted textile (e.g., nylon, polyester, polyolefin, or fluoropolymer fibers), with contact angles ranging from 65°–135° or greater than 135°. The base may also carry tufted hydrophilic bristles in a row, with hydrophilic media optionally omitted.

Lift-off cover: the base includes a removable brushroll cover accessed via first and second opposed actuators (undercut for one-handed squeezing) that move latches out of left and right retainers; a coil spring biases them toward latched positions and cam surfaces permit reattachment without actuating. The distribution nozzle and second squeegee attach to the cover, with mating fluid couplings and a connecting conduit; an optional second, non-fluid coupling offsets the first to inhibit binding.

Lights: the base carries LED lights on a vertically mounted PCB directed at the front to illuminate the spray pattern, along with indicator lights that may be turned on by actuator actuation, pump power, vacuum source power, or a fluid flow sensor (with a signal indicating no flow), optionally changing color by operating state.

Nozzle configuration: a first squeegee extending from the lower end of the base pushes fluid toward the suction inlet as the base moves forward, and a second squeegee attached to the brushroll cover wipes fluid and debris from the brushroll toward the suction conduit, reducing air ingress. An optional secondary nozzle under the cover wets the brushroll before contact. Rollers support the base ahead of the brushroll; in one embodiment the cover has a raised front edge exposing the brushroll forward of the base for cleaning baseboards.

Brushroll embodiment: first and second sets of tufted fibers on a backing wrapped around the spindle, with the first set having smaller diameters (about 0.03–0.08 mm) for wiping and the second larger (at least 0.06 mm, e.g., about 0.10 mm) for agitation and vibration damping; the second set wraps helically about 5–6 times, fiber length about 5–15 mm, with equal lengths, and optional replaceable sleeves.

Australia dominated the Philippines 89–53 in Bocaue, leading 57–32 at halftime and 79–48 with four minutes left in the third quarter before the game ended by default. Australia’s size, defense, ball movement, and shooting overwhelmed Gilas.

The increasingly physical game escalated into a bench-clearing brawl involving punches, thrown chairs, and water bottles, followed by a group selfie by Philippine players. Coach Chot Reyes said Australian player Daniel Kickert had been hitting Philippine players during warmups, while the article noted Kickert’s later actions against RR Pogoy contributed to the confrontation. Nevertheless, it judged the Philippines more responsible for escalating the violence and said Australia also apologized and should not be absolved.

The Samahang Basketbol ng Pilipinas apologized for breaching Filipino hospitality and declared that violence has no place in sports. The article said the incident would likely bring FIBA sanctions and harm the national team’s standing and pursuit of respect on the global stage. It called for meaningful consequences, greater restraint, and an end to the status quo, while criticizing Terrence Romeo’s response to criticism as immature.

The Give & Go isolation offense uses a 2-1-2 spread with two primary ball handlers and a weakside post. It features give-and-go basket cuts, back cuts, and resets when passing lanes are denied. Wings may drive against soft defense, while the post provides pressure release when needed. Weakside players can exchange positions or set stationary down or back screens to occupy defenders and avoid moving-screen fouls.

Leam Richardson dismissed suggestions that Wigan Athletic’s tunnel clash with Fleetwood resembled the Old Trafford “Milkgate” episode. He said Ivan Toney and Nathan Pond merely came together briefly and nothing significant occurred. Wigan face AFC Fylde in the FA Cup third round, with victory earning a Premier League trip to Bournemouth.

The study examined Turkish teachers’ views on culturally responsive education using Q methodology. Twenty-one public-school teachers from Denizli, Mardin, Erzurum, and Şanlıurfa purposively sorted 30 statements into a forced agreement scale. Principal-components analysis with varimax rotation identified three factors: unification, student support, and teacher support, explaining 35%, 16%, and 8% of the variance. Seventeen participants loaded significantly onto these factors.

Teachers broadly viewed the Turkish education system as accepting cultural diversity and treating it as a resource, while also recognizing continuing inequalities. The greatest consensus concerned developing students’ cultural competence, presenting general cultural practices, and supporting local students’ academic and social development. The strongest disagreements concerned anti-discrimination measures, viewing different cultures as threats, and treating classrooms as reflections of society. Despite the system’s inclusive orientation, teachers considered culturally responsive practices insufficiently developed, particularly in curricula, teaching programs, and student and teacher support. Participants declined to explain their strongest agreement or disagreement, suggesting sensitivity surrounding multicultural issues.

Recommendations included culturally responsive workshops for all stakeholders, teacher professional development, support for students to express themselves and participate in their cultures, further academic research, and wider dissemination of cultural knowledge.

The patent describes electronic devices with integrated touch-sensor and display structures. Devices may include enclosures formed from transparent and opaque walls, with display layers beneath transparent regions and touch-sensor layers beneath transparent and opaque regions. These layers may cover front, rear, and sidewall surfaces, including active display areas and inactive touch-only areas, and may be formed on rigid or flexible substrates or as coatings.

Displays may use various pixel technologies, while touch sensors may use capacitive, resistive, acoustic, force-based, light-based, or other technologies. Sidewalls may be flat, sloped, or curved, with flexible display and touch layers conforming to curved surfaces. Foldable devices may include flexible wall sections and one or more bend axes, using hinges formed from flexible layers, accordion structures, or pivoting members. Stress-tolerant features may include thinned substrates, serpentine traces, redundant conductive paths, and neutral-stress-plane adjustments.

Fabrication may use molding, deposition, patterning, photolithography, coating, lamination, and bending techniques.

Progressive reported strong February 2018 results, beating estimates with an 87.8% combined ratio, 2.6 percentage points better than a year earlier. Net income fell 4% to $129 million, while net earned premiums rose 19% to $2.2047 billion and year-to-date premiums increased 18% to $4.8943 billion. All business lines grew at least 16%, and core segments posted combined ratios below 91%.

The company raised $1.0834 billion through senior notes and preferred-share offerings for general corporate purposes, expanded Uber subsidiary commercial auto coverage in three states, and recognized $70 million in additional net premiums. The author expects book value growth above 10% and EPS toward the upper end of $2.50–$4.30.

Using current book value and trailing earnings, the estimated intrinsic value is about $48 per share, rising to $50–$54 based on 2018 projections. Despite strong operations and positive market reaction, the author considers Progressive overvalued and estimates its 2018 dividend at $0.76–$1.85 per share. Existing shareholders are advised that retaining the stock may be reasonable.

Gary Antonacci’s dual momentum strategy is a trend-following investment approach combining absolute momentum—an asset’s own price change over time—with relative momentum—its performance compared with peers. For long positions, investors rank assets with positive absolute momentum and buy those with the strongest relative momentum. In markets permitting short selling, assets with negative absolute momentum are ranked, and the weakest performer may be shorted. The strategy avoids buying market laggards and aims to buy “the best among performers” or short “the weakest among the weak.”

The process begins by calculating each asset’s price change over a selected period. Positive absolute momentum indicates a long candidate, while negative momentum indicates a potential short candidate. Relative comparisons then identify the strongest positive performers or weakest negative performers. The strategy can be applied to individual assets, ETFs, related sectors, regions, or asset classes. For sector rotation, a universe of ETFs is ranked by absolute momentum, with the top positive-momentum ETFs selected and periodically rotated.

Relative-momentum research by Jagadeesh and Titman in 1993 found potential trading opportunities but only marginally lower volatility than benchmarks. Antonacci’s 2012 book, *Dual Momentum Investing*, added absolute momentum to seek similar relative-momentum returns with substantially reduced volatility. His GEM model, reported from 1950 through 2018, held U.S. or non-U.S. equity indices when stocks were strong and bonds when weak. Its monthly return correlations were 0.60 with a global asset-allocation benchmark and 0.50 with the S&P 500, with about 1.5 trades annually; the results were simulated and hypothetical.

A monthly-rebalanced backtest using SPY, EFA, and AGG returned 6.75% annually with a 30% maximum drawdown. It outperformed the world index but not the S&P 500, which returned 9.2% with roughly a 55% drawdown. Reported benefits include better performance than buy-and-hold and lower volatility, although the strategy can underperform during strong bull markets or sharp rebounds.

The Break, a longtime Five Points South restaurant and billiards hall, is slated for demolition and replacement with high-rise apartments. Supporters hope the project will revive the area, while residents want affordable housing as rents rise. No closure date is set, and management was unavailable to comment.

Neiman Gracie criticized Dillon Danis’s trash talk after Danis declined a Bellator 180 fight to avoid missing the IBJJF World Championship. Gracie will face Dave Marfone at Madison Square Garden on June 24.

Researchers found that a 0.5°C rise in annual average temperature corresponded to a 1% fall in average exam scores among more than 10 million US secondary students over 13 years. In the UK, June temperatures typically exceed 21°C, when negative effects begin, while schools rarely have air conditioning. Moving exams online or changing the academic calendar is complicated by synchronized testing, annually adjusted grade thresholds, and reliance on the September-to-July timetable.

The advance-decline indicator (AD line) is a cumulative market-breadth measure calculated by adding each day’s difference between the number of advancing and declining stocks to the previous value. A rising line suggests market momentum, while a falling line may indicate losing momentum. It can confirm an index trend and signal potential reversals when it diverges from price.

Advance/decline issues are stocks trading above or below the previous close. Advance/decline distribution tracks advancing and declining stocks and their volume within an index, exchange, sector, or basket to assess breadth and sentiment. The Advance/Decline Volume Line similarly cumulates differences in shares traded between advancing and declining stocks; rising values indicate buying pressure, while falling values indicate selling pressure.

For the NYSE, the A/D line is the cumulative difference between advancing and declining NYSE stocks. An S&P 500 backtest using SPY produced 229 trades with an average gain of 0.6%, inconsistent results, and a 1.55 profit factor, below the stated 1.75 threshold. Multiple strategy versions failed to produce a successful strategy, leading the article to recommend considering other oscillators such as RSI, Williams %R, or IBS.

Tour operators are divided over the impact of the ex-HMAS Tobruk settling on her side. Dive Hervey Bay owner Glenn Bowman says the starboard side is largely inaccessible to ordinary divers and could cut projected income by 50%, while Ed Gibson expects accessible wreck features and thriving dive tourism after tour adjustments. Both call the dive spectacular. A safety inspection is underway, with the government consulting four tour operators on future dive opportunities.

The July 11, 2001 IEP News digest compiles reports on California’s electricity crisis, related energy policy and businesses, and working conditions for migrant shepherds.

California and power generators ended 15 days of FERC-mediated settlement talks without agreement. The state sought $8.9 billion in refunds for alleged overcharges dating to May 2000, while generators offered roughly $670 million to $716 million and denied refunds were justified. Administrative law judge Curtis Wagner indicated refunds of about $1 billion or less and said suppliers might be owed more, potentially leaving California with no net refund. His methodology applied price controls only from October 2, excluding $3 billion of earlier claims. FERC could order a maximum of $5.4 billion because it lacks jurisdiction over roughly $600 million in municipal-utility charges. Governor Gray Davis said California would pursue the full amount in court if necessary. Other Western states also sought more than $6 billion in refunds.

Edison International’s refinancing and asset sales were expected to provide $46 million in cash and stabilize the company, but Southern California Edison remained financially precarious. A rescue agreement required legislative approval by August 15 and included state purchase of transmission lines for $2.8 billion and SCE bond issuance of up to $3.5 billion, repaid through higher rates. SCE owed creditors $931 million in defaulted bonds and notes. Separately, a bankruptcy judge refused to allow a committee representing PG&E customers, ruling that refund claims should be handled by regulators.

Calpine agreed to purchase 236 billion cubic feet of natural-gas reserves in Texas and New Mexico for $355 million plus $49.5 million in assumed debt, raising its reserves to about 1.5 trillion cubic feet and advancing its goal of owning 25 percent of the gas it uses. The Electric Power Research Institute warned that overloaded western transmission equipment, reduced maintenance and inadequate investment created a risk of cascading outages and estimated that stabilizing the system would require $10 billion to $30 billion over 10 years. It also said plant upgrades could add 5,100 megawatts for $460 million, while warning of growing dependence on natural gas.

A Texas regulatory brochure attributed California’s shortages to fewer new plants, greater reliance on hydropower, transmission constraints and market restructuring, while describing Texas as having adequate reserves, diverse fuel sources and retail competition scheduled for 2002. House Republicans were also pursuing a limited energy bill before the August recess, covering clean-coal subsidies, household assistance and efficient televisions, while broader measures on drilling, fuel economy, nuclear liability and power-plant rules remained stalled.

The Shaw Group reported third-quarter earnings of $0.42 per share, net income of $18 million and revenue of nearly $400 million. Its CEO described strong long-term demand for new power plants and identified Europe as a future growth market.

The New York Times reported on approximately 800 migrant shepherds in California, predominantly from Peru and Chile, who worked long hours in isolated trailers, commonly lacked toilets and running water, and were excluded from minimum-wage protections. Following a $150 monthly wage increase, California Assemblyman Paul Koretz proposed rest breaks and basic housing amenities, though ranchers opposed the bill as potentially harmful to their declining industry.

Rapid generative-AI and LLM development brings benefits to finance, healthcare, and education but creates legal and ethical risks, including misinformation, malicious deepfakes, bias, and discrimination. Governance is further complicated by rapid technological change, tension between innovation and risk mitigation, communication gaps between governments and technology companies, divergent national regulations, compliance costs, and AI’s connection to national power. Although the EU, US, and China have introduced AI laws and companies such as Microsoft have adopted responsible-AI principles, significant gaps remain.

The passage recommends forward-looking, human-centered governance combining top-down and bottom-up approaches. Policymakers, industry, and academia should collaborate, build shared understanding, and anticipate foreseeable harms. Developers, researchers, users, and communities should transparently report problems throughout model lifecycles, while governments and companies should create channels for reporting, investigate risks, and update regulations promptly. Social-computing techniques can support targeted monitoring of regulatory needs in specific communities.

The passage reviews business ventures founded by wealthy or famous women, reporting frequent losses, debts and closures despite family wealth, celebrity backing and outside investment.

Quality Street heiress Millie Mackintosh launched a bohemian clothing range through Asos in 2014. Her Cammac businesses lost £182,833 in their first year and faced £548,000 of debts; after reportedly losing £178,000, she shut the venture down amid challenging fashion-industry conditions.

Healthy-eating blogger Ella Mills, known as Deliciously Ella, opened three London delis in 12 months after building a large online following. The Mae Deli lost £723,811 in its first year, and two locations later closed, with the fate of about 40 staff unclear. Her separate cookbooks and snack business remained profitable, earning £545,497.

What Not To Wear presenter Trinny Woodall created a 59-product make-up range in 2014. It made £56,281 initially but lost £70,089 the next year. Charles Saatchi and other wealthy investors subsequently provided £2.7 million, increasing assets to £1.83 million.

Bernie Ecclestone’s daughters pursued separate businesses. Petra’s Stark handbag company was placed on hold in 2015; losses rose from £706,005 to £1.4 million and debt reached £4.23 million before she applied to wind it up. Tamara’s Show Beauty haircare venture lost £8.23 million despite £15 million invested; she transferred 75 per cent to a Seychelles investment company and rebranded it SBD International, which later reported a £4 million loss.

Model Alexa Chung’s Alpha Charlie fashion label lost £65,248, then £75,000 and £1.5 million in successive years. Wealthy friends supplied nearly £3 million, leaving £1.4 million in the bank, while another company of hers entered voluntary liquidation, leaving her with a £3.4 million surplus.

Banking heiress Kate Rothschild’s Roundtable Records owed her £365,606 while holding only £6,826 in assets and £761 cash. Its website closed and she wound up the label in 2016.

Actress Sadie Frost and Jemima French initially enjoyed success with lingerie and swimwear label Frost French, winning an Elle Designers of the Year award in 2004. Debt reached £4.2 million by 2008, including £3 million owed to one creditor. Despite a rescue investment, the flagship closed in 2011 and the business was dissolved; a proposed relaunch never happened, although the Floozie swimwear brand remained on sale at Debenhams.

The team should attack more aggressively and go to the net rather than gamble. Detroit has limited shooting lanes, high pressure, and effective defensemen. Both goaltenders and team defenses have played well, with Detroit’s offense helping its defense. Ronnie Francis hit the post, suggesting a breakthrough may be near. Fans have been enthusiastic and energizing in the playoffs.

PGMC, Global Ferronickel’s operating subsidiary, renewed a contract to supply 1.5 million WMT of nickel ore to Guangdong Century Tsingshan Nickel for 2018 at market prices. Global Ferronickel’s 2017 income rose over 20-fold to P779.7 million, while revenue increased 54% to P5.8 billion.

Justice Ketanji Brown Jackson had already served three months before her 2022 investiture, having taken her constitutional and judicial oaths June 30. As the most junior justice, she takes notes during the Court’s private conferences. A government shutdown could force lower federal courts to delay trials and hearings, while the Supreme Court would continue operating with permanent funds.

As the Roberts court enters its third decade, it faces major disputes involving elections, free speech, executive power, birthright citizenship, Venezuelan protected status, foreign-aid funding, and the removal of a Federal Reserve governor. State attorneys general are seeking federal support to challenge a 2008 ruling barring death penalties for child rape when the victim did not die. Separately, 300 former Michigan athletes plan to appeal the dismissal of their NIL lawsuit against the NCAA and Big Ten Network as time-barred.

A retrospective examines Chief Justice Warren Burger’s close relationship with Richard Nixon, their recorded discussions about Court reforms and cases, Burger’s creation of a three-part obscenity test, and the unanimous 1974 decision rejecting Nixon’s executive-privilege claim over his tapes. Venezuelan challengers asked the Supreme Court to preserve a temporary order protecting their status, arguing that ending it would cause significant harm. The passage also references Justice Barrett’s comments about public scrutiny, swing votes, and recusals.

The U.S. Department of State’s Office of the Historian produced an ebook edition of *Foreign Relations of the United States: Diplomatic Papers, 1942, Volume II: Europe* on May 28, 2018. It includes the volume’s full content with search, bookmarking, note-taking, and offline access; readers are advised to cite document numbers rather than page numbers. Department of State Regulation 045 establishes the series as the official record of U.S. foreign policy and requires historical objectivity, disclosure of alterations and deletions, and preservation of major facts, subject to security considerations and limited permissible omissions. G. Bernard Noble supervised preparation, E. R. Perkins directed the staff, and named compilers covered Finland, North African France, Greece, and the remainder of the volume; the Division of Publishing Services handled copy editing, proofreading, and indexes.

Salem residents are traveling to Woodburn and finding grocery shelves empty of bottled water after an algae bloom in Detroit Lake produced low levels of cyanotoxins in the city’s drinking water. The city and Oregon emergency managers are not coordinating distribution sites, while major retailers await shipments. Children under 6 and other sensitive groups are advised to use bottled water for drinking, formula, ice, and food. Fresh test results are expected Thursday.

Eurozone stocks fell sharply Friday as the euro pressured the dollar and traders awaited US January payrolls data. Germany’s DAX dropped 1.7%, France’s CAC 40 1.6%, and the STOXX 600 1.4%, while London’s FTSE 100 slipped 0.6%; Deutsche Bank also declined.

The paper studies learning Linear Temporal Logic on finite traces (LTLf): given positive and negative traces, it seeks a smallest LTLf formula that satisfies every positive trace and no negative trace. It surveys applications in software specification mining, cyber-physical systems and robotics, and artificial intelligence.

The proposed framework separates Boolean operators from temporal operators. An optimized VFB algorithm enumerates LTLf formulas by size using bottom-up combinatorial search, bitwise characteristic-table evaluation, and observational-equivalence pruning. After enumerating formulas up to a configurable size, the method switches to a Boolean Set Cover solver, which combines the generated formulas using conjunction and disjunction to construct larger, more expressive solutions.

Boolean Set Cover is defined over weighted subsets of positive and negative examples. The paper proves that solution existence can be checked in polynomial time and that the decision problem is NP-complete. It introduces domination to prune redundant formulas, a fast approximate domination heuristic, beam search that retains the highest-scoring formulas at each weight, and a divide-and-conquer procedure that finds a valid solution whenever one exists, though not necessarily a minimum-weight one. Once only Boolean operators remain, characteristic tables can also be reduced to vectors, reducing memory and evaluation costs.

The authors implement the framework in the Rust tool Bolt and release a consolidated suite of more than 15,000 LTLf learning tasks across ten families. Against Scarlet, Bolt generally solves more tasks, runs faster, and produces smaller formulas; it solves tasks more than 100 times faster on over 70% of benchmarks and returns formulas no larger than Scarlet’s in 98% of cases. An ablation study shows that Boolean Set Cover enables Bolt to solve more difficult tasks than raw VFB enumeration with little sacrifice in formula size. Compared with the GPU-based algorithm, Bolt is competitive on commonly solved tasks and faster on small tasks, while the GPU method solves more tasks overall. The paper presents Boolean Set Cover as a broadly applicable problem for logics and specification languages with conjunction and disjunction.

NVIDIA Corporation filed a Form 8-K dated February 9, 2017, announcing financial results for the quarter and fiscal year ended January 29, 2017. The filing included Exhibit 99.1, a press release titled “NVIDIA Announces Financial Results for the Fourth Quarter and Fiscal 2017,” and Exhibit 99.2, CFO commentary from Colette M. Kress. Both materials were furnished, not filed, and were not subject to incorporation by reference in future SEC filings.

American football’s offense uses specialized positions to advance the ball, gain field position, and score, with a field goal possible when the team is within range. The quarterback leads the offense, handles the ball on every play, chooses receivers or handoffs, changes plays through audibles, and executes proper footwork on running plays. Running backs primarily carry the ball but also catch passes, block, find gaps, and secure the football against defenders.

Tight ends combine receiving and blocking. Attached tight ends line up beside the offensive tackle and are often greater downfield passing threats, while “sniffer” or H-back tight ends operate farther from the line, frequently in motion, and emphasize run blocking while remaining capable receivers.

The five-man offensive line blocks for both rushing and passing plays. Offensive tackles protect the quarterback’s blind side and block edge defenders; guards work between the tackles and center, often using double-team or pulling blocks; and the center acts as the line’s captain, touching the ball on every play and communicating defensive adjustments.

Wide receivers catch passes, run routes, create separation, and may block on running plays. Split Ends, or X receivers, are typically larger and line up at the line of scrimmage; flankers, or Z receivers, are often faster and align slightly farther back; slot receivers are generally smaller, align inside the formation, and specialize in routes across the middle and underneath.

End a job interview promptly and confidently without lingering or begging for the job. Discuss the opportunity, ask needed questions, and leave with a brief handshake and positive comment rather than asking when a decision will be made.

Research by Cornell’s Adam Anderson and the University of Colorado Boulder’s Daniel H. Lee found that people can accurately identify six basic emotions—sadness, disgust, anger, joy, fear and surprise—from the eyes alone. Participants rated 600 pairs of eye-expression images and mental-state words, with eye openness the strongest cue. Narrowed eyes were associated with discrimination-related states such as suspicion and disgust, while open eyes signaled sensitivity-related states such as fear, awe and curiosity. Other surrounding features conveyed emotional positivity or negativity, and the eyes conveyed emotions more reliably than the nose or mouth. The researchers said these patterns support and extend Darwin’s view that facial expressions began as adaptive sensory functions before being used to communicate emotions and intentions.

A shortage of funds, compounded by teachers’ SSLC-evaluation and election duties, caused Karnataka’s education department to cancel free summer camps for government-school students. The five-week programme, launched in 2017–18, had reached 4,049 schools, offering Mathematics, Science, extracurricular activities, meals, and language support.

A Vegreville study says relocating the federal immigration processing centre to Edmonton could reduce the town’s population by 7.3%, lower home prices by 30%, increase unemployment and cost 130 students.
Brendon Naidoo was granted R50,000 bail following allegations of fraud involving a foreign-exchange trading scheme. He must report to Sandton Police twice weekly and return to court on May 5.

A 2025 medRxiv preprint investigated antimicrobial resistance in untreated wastewater across metropolitan and non-metropolitan Western Uttar Pradesh, India, during 2020–2021. Fifteen sampling sites across three zones were tested using culture enrichment, biochemical and VITEK identification, antibiotic-susceptibility testing, ESBL detection, MIC testing, and colistin broth disk elution.

Among 150 Enterobacteriaceae isolates, 93 were E. coli, 36 were K. pneumoniae, 12 were other Enterobacteriaceae, and nine were mixed. A total of 111 isolates (74%) were resistant to at least one tested antibiotic, and 88 of these were ESBL producers. Among resistant isolates, multidrug resistance was reported in 57.14% of E. coli, 28.57% of K. pneumoniae, and 5.71% of Pantoea agglomerans. Carbapenem resistance reached 36.05%, and colistin resistance was detected in some isolates, including Pantoea species.

Zone 1 had the highest overall multidrug-resistance percentage, although differences among zones were not statistically significant. Zone 3 had the greatest proportion of multidrug-resistant E. coli, while Zone 1 had the greatest proportion of multidrug-resistant K. pneumoniae. Multidrug resistance was more prevalent in K. pneumoniae than in E. coli.

The authors associated the findings with pandemic-era antibiotic use, inadequate wastewater treatment, and environmental exposure to resistant bacteria. They recommended improved wastewater infrastructure, periodic surveillance of Indian wastewater and receiving waters, and molecular characterization of resistance genes.

John Clarke (UC Berkeley), Michel Devoret (Yale and UCSB) and John Martinis (UCSB) share the 2025 Nobel Prize in Physics, worth nearly $1.2 million, for discovering macroscopic quantum tunnelling and energy quantisation in a superconductor electric circuit.

Job interviews range from routine to elaborate, quirky “disruptor” processes featuring unconventional questions and props. When asked if candidates have questions, the passage advises them to respond assertively and take control.

- Power-supply filtering should use ferrite beads and capacitors, with at least one capacitor on the device side and an optional capacitor before the bead to form a Pi filter. Filters should be close to device pins, and analog supplies should have individual filters. Recommended decoupling is 0.1 µF in the smallest practical package, with no package larger than 0402; at least one capacitor is required for every two power pins, and one for a single-pin supply. A bulk capacitor of 10 µF or more is recommended for roughly every 10 power pins. Excess capacitance must not disrupt startup voltage ramps or power sequencing, and reset must remain asserted until supplies are stable.

- Power-on reset resets the entire device, including test, emulation, and EMAC switch logic. It requires stable supplies and input clocks, places most pins in Hi-Z, resets modules, and starts PLLs in bypass mode. Releasing POR latches BTMODE, applies PRCM defaults, and starts the Cortex-A8 from the Boot ROM. External, emulation, watchdog, and software warm resets generally follow the external RESET sequence, with specified differences in RSTOUT_WD_OUT behavior; emulation sessions survive warm resets. Software global cold and warm resets are initiated through PRM_RSTCTRL. Local resets affect only the associated module, and simultaneous reset requests are handled according to priority.

- RSTOUT_WD_OUT indicates reset status and is always asserted for watchdog resets. It is tri-stated with its internal pull disabled during POR or RESET, allowing an external pull to set its state. Reset isolation can independently reset the PCIe subsystem and can preserve the EMAC switch, its PLL, selected registers, and pin multiplexing when ISO_CONTROL is enabled. PCIe software must idle the subsystem before reset and re-enumerate afterward. Most device I/O enters Hi-Z during resets, with exceptions for emulation pins, EMAC pins during POR, and RSTOUT_WD_OUT.

- Device clocks originate from DEV and optional AUX inputs supplied by crystals with internal oscillators or 1.8-V LVCMOS sources. DEV is typically 20 MHz but may range from 20–30 MHz under specified conditions; AUX may also operate from 20–30 MHz for precise audio or video clocks. Oscillator crystals must operate in fundamental parallel-resonant mode, and load capacitors and discrete components should be placed close to the associated pins. The PCIe PHY requires a low-jitter differential clock that is AC-coupled close to the processor. Optional audio clocks support up to 50 MHz, while CLKIN32 and two programmable clock outputs are also provided.

- The device contains 12 top-level and four embedded PLLs. Most use the DEV clock, selected PLLs can use AUX, and all enter bypass mode after reset. PLL supplies require external filtering, and programming must satisfy reference, DCO, output, SYSCLK, module, and USB PLL limits; PLL_USB must be fixed at 960 MHz. PRCM-generated SYSCLKs and module clock sources have additional frequency restrictions.

- The Cortex-A8 interrupt controller handles up to 128 prioritized requests and generates IRQs or FIQs, although general-purpose devices do not support FIQs. The C674x controller combines 128 device events into 12 prioritized interrupts, with events 15–95 selectable from 24 multiplexed sources.

- Timing specifications are measured at device pins with a characterized load and 4-V/ns input slew rates. Board-routing delays must be included, and TI recommends IBIS models for accurate analysis; the DDR2 interface instead uses supplied PCB routing rules. Clocks and control signals should transition monotonically.

- Two DCAN interfaces support CAN 2.0, message-object masking, FIFO and loopback modes, automatic bus-on recovery, and configurable CAN pins. The EDMA controller provides up to 64 channels, maps synchronization events to any of 512 parameter entries, and handles peripheral and memory transfers.

- Advanced Event Triggering supports hardware breakpoints, data watchpoints, counters, and state sequencing. Cortex-A8 and system trace can export debug information in real time, and the IEEE 1149.1 JTAG interface supports emulation and boundary-scan testing.

- The EMAC switch is a three-port gigabit switch with one internal and two external ports. External ports support 10/100/1000-Mbps operation and MII, GMII, RMII, and RGMII interfaces. MDIO continuously polls 32 PHY addresses, CPPI provides 512 buffer descriptors, and the EMAC I/O interface is 3.3 V only.

- Four GPIO modules provide 32 channels each, configurable as inputs or outputs with programmable interrupt generation. The GPMC provides a glueless 8/16-bit interface for NOR, NAND, SRAM, pseudo-SRAM, and custom devices, with up to eight chip selects and 512 MB of addressing. Its associated ELM locates BCH errors for 4-, 8-, and 16-bit NAND configurations.

- The HDMI 1.3a interface supports digital video, multichannel L-PCM audio, CEC, and DDC. PCB guidance requires roughly 100-Ω differential and 60-Ω single-ended TMDS impedances, paired vias, controlled routing, and ESD protection with no more than 5 pF of added capacitance.

- The HDVPSS provides input and output interfaces, HD/SD encoding, two display pipelines, scaling, de-interlacing, compositing, color conversion, graphics layers, and HDMI output. Analog video DAC routing guidance covers normal and bypass modes, short isolated traces, close placement of feedback components, and approximately 75-Ω output impedances.

- Four I2C modules support 8-bit transfers, standard and fast modes up to 400 Kbps, noise filtering, 7- and 10-bit addressing, multimaster operation, combined transfer modes, and a 32-byte FIFO.

The Indiana Court of Appeals affirmed Anthony Davis and Eric Simmons’s convictions for Class A felony conspiracy to deal in more than three grams of cocaine. Although no individual sale involved three grams, the evidence showed a coordinated agreement involving transportation, packaging, apartment preparation, and cocaine sales, supporting the convictions. The jury’s conspiracy verdict for Simmons was not irreconcilably inconsistent with his acquittal on the dealing charge because the conspiracy could be proved through any of several alleged overt acts, and Davis made the direct sales. Davis could not challenge inconsistent verdicts because only one count remained against him. The court also upheld Davis’s enhanced 40-year sentence, finding that his criminal history alone would have supported the same sentence beyond a reasonable doubt, despite two improper aggravators.

Fort Buford was built in 1866 where the Missouri and Yellowstone rivers meet near Williston and served until Sitting Bull surrendered in 1881. Soldiers grew, caught, or hunted much of their food, but inadequate supplies, poor cooking, and interrupted steamboat deliveries caused scurvy and other hardships. Boredom and alcohol led some men to wound themselves to leave military service. A 1876 report described patients with insanity and the post’s extensive library and periodicals. A museum opened in the old headquarters in 1963, followed by restoration of other areas.

Flippy, an AI-powered burger-flipping robot developed by Miso Robotics, has begun working at Caliburger’s Pasadena restaurant, reportedly grilling 150 burgers per hour. The wheeled robot uses cameras and thermal and 3-D sensors, receives kitchen orders digitally, and can swap tools to cook burgers and potentially chicken, bacon, onions, and other foods. It still requires a human coworker to place patties, add cheese and extras, and wrap sandwiches.

Miso and Caliburger describe Flippy as a cost-efficient kitchen assistant designed to work alongside staff, not replace them. Caliburger has six months of exclusive use; other vendors may then purchase it for about $60,000 each, with prices potentially rising as capabilities expand. Following a trial, Caliburger plans U.S. expansion, though fast food was reportedly identified as especially vulnerable to automation.

The device supports reset isolation for the PCI Express subsystem and Ethernet Switch. For a PCI Express Root Complex, software can reset the subsystem through the PRCM after placing it in IDLE and ensuring no transactions are active; bus enumeration must then be repeated. As an Endpoint, an in-band reset generates an interrupt that software handles by entering IDLE and asserting the local reset through the PRCM. Device-level resets other than Test Reset also reset PCI Express, requiring a downstream hot reset and bus re-enumeration.

Ethernet Switch reset isolation is enabled through the RESET_ISO Control Module register. When isolated, the switch, its reference-clock PLL, selected registers, and some pin multiplexing remain unaffected during most system resets; power-on reset is excluded. RSTOUT_WD_OUT indicates reset status, is asserted during watchdog reset, and is tri-stated while POR or RESET is active. Warm and cold resets are also generated when power domains switch off and on, respectively. Most I/O pins enter a high-impedance state during reset, with exceptions for emulation pins, Ethernet Switch pins, and RSTOUT_WD_OUT. DDR address/control pins are tri-stated and subsequently driven according to their internal pull values.

Device clocks are derived through reference clocks, PLLs, dividers, and PRCM multiplexing. DEV and AUX inputs can use internal oscillators with external crystals or 1.8-V LVCMOS clock sources. DEV is typically 20 MHz and may range from 20–30 MHz under specified conditions; AUX may also range from 20–30 MHz. PCI Express requires a low-jitter differential clock that is AC-coupled to SERDES_CLKP and SERDES_CLKN. Optional external references include three AUD_CLK inputs, a 32.768-kHz CLKIN32 input, and two programmable CLKOUT outputs. The device has 12 top-level and four embedded PLLs; all PLLs start in bypass mode after reset and must be programmed within specified reference, internal, output, SYSCLK, and module-clock limits.

The ARM Cortex-A8 Interrupt Controller prioritizes up to 128 requests and generates IRQs or FIQs, while the C674x interrupt controller combines up to 128 events into 12 prioritized interrupts, with selected events multiplexed through Control Module registers.

Peripheral sections describe DCAN, EDMA, GPIO, GPMC/ELM, HDMI, HDVPSS, video DAC outputs, I2C, imaging, JTAG, trace, Advanced Event Triggering, and DDR2/DDR3 memory interfaces. The EMAC Switch is a three-port gigabit switch with two external ports, MII/GMII/RMII/RGMII interfaces, MDIO PHY management, and 3.3-V I/O only. The GPMC supports external NOR, NAND, SRAM, pseudo-SRAM, and custom asynchronous devices, while the ELM locates BCH errors. HDMI guidance covers TMDS impedance and routing, DDC pullups, and ESD protection. HDVPSS provides video capture, display processing, scaling, compositing, and digital outputs. Four I2C modules support standard and fast modes up to 400 Kbps. The imaging subsystem accepts parallel or serial camera data and provides ISP processing, timing, strobe, and shutter control. The DDR interface supports 16- or 32-bit paths, two chip selects, multiple DDR2/DDR3 densities, and data interleaving.

AC timing measurements use specified voltage references and a 4-V/ns input slew rate. Board-routing delays must be included in timing analysis, and IBIS models are recommended except for the DDR2 interface, for which the specified PCB routing rules apply.

Engineer John Essey’s Pittsburgh-area home uses Internet of Things technology to unlock doors, adjust lights and thermostat, and detect water or leaks through sensors and an Amazon Echo. Carnegie Mellon researcher Gierad Laput and his team developed a small wall-plugged sensor that wirelessly monitors a room’s sounds, vibrations, light, and other conditions, identifying events such as a blender running or a light turning on. He sees domestic and commercial uses, including stove warnings and monitoring restaurant supplies. Security expert Bruce Schneier warns that connected devices may collect and sell household data and that manufacturers are not prioritizing security. Concerns include devices mapping homes, though iRobot says such data would be shared only with customer consent.

Nokia, Deutsche Telekom and Hamburg’s Port Authority will test 5G across the 8,000-hectare port. Uses include traffic-light management, real-time environmental data processing and VR infrastructure monitoring. A live industrial trial, first in Germany, will test multiple network slices to tailor 5G to varied application needs.

The team’s playoff success has come from focusing on one game at a time rather than the bigger picture, with two victories still needed. A teammate is praised for playing hard, avoiding mistakes, and providing strong leadership in the locker room and on the ice. Poor ice and glass have made the goaltender cautious about leaving his net, though rink conditions were not considered the main reason a shot was missed. The speaker describes the Stanley Cup as something players can share with loved ones and meaningful causes, including a children’s cancer hospital. Against Colorado, he says a talented, fast opponent must be closely watched. The team has more offensive skill this postseason but must continue emphasizing defense and goaltending. Despite its favorable series position, the speaker expects the closing minutes to be the toughest challenge because Colorado has repeatedly rebounded after losses, making a strong performance the next night essential.

Apple Inc.’s Form 10-Q for the fiscal quarter ended June 26, 2021 reported third-quarter net sales of $81.434 billion, up 36% year over year, driven by growth across all product and service categories. Product sales rose 50% for iPhone, 16% for Mac, 12% for iPad, and 36% for Wearables, Home and Accessories; Services sales increased 33%. Net sales also grew in every geographic segment, with Greater China recording the fastest third-quarter increase at 58%. Gross margin was $35.255 billion, or 43.3%, compared with 38.0% a year earlier, reflecting higher volume, product and service mix, currency strength, and improved leverage.
