The article examines how science education contributes to citizenship education in Turkey. It situates both fields within global challenges such as climate change, pandemics, migration, environmental degradation, and sustainable development. Science education is presented as a means of developing scientifically literate, critically thinking, responsible, and active citizens able to participate democratically and address societal problems.

Although Turkey’s 2005 citizenship curriculum initially adopted an interdisciplinary approach, citizenship became a standalone fourth-grade course from 2010–2011, with secondary-level responsibility assigned mainly to social studies. Although the 2018 science curriculum incorporates scientific, technological, and environmental literacy and emphasizes relationships among individuals, society, and the environment, it does not explicitly connect these objectives to citizenship education.

The qualitative study addressed two questions: which citizenship elements appear in the Turkish science curriculum, and how science educators understand and foster students’ citizenship skills. Researchers reviewed the curriculum and conducted semi-structured interviews with eight science teachers. Curriculum and interview data were analyzed thematically, producing themes of scientific literacy, technology, society, environment, values, skills, and problems.

The curriculum strongly emphasizes scientific knowledge and process skills, including observation, measurement, classification, inquiry, safety, ethical conduct, and evidence-based problem-solving. Teachers regarded scientific literacy as essential for active citizenship because it supports research, inquiry, critical thinking, problem-solving, and informed participation in community life. Science was also linked to society through health, safety, first aid, civic responsibility, and issues such as blood donation, organ donation, illegal drug use, human rights, GMOs, climate change, and COVID-19. Environmental topics received particular emphasis: teachers connected scientific understanding with environmental awareness, conservation, sustainable resource use, and advocacy against pollution and climate change. Technology received comparatively limited discussion and was not strongly connected to citizenship by teachers.

Despite the theoretical connection between the fields, teachers reported that science education often falls short of its citizenship goals in practice. Major barriers include overcrowded classrooms, inadequate laboratories, equipment and materials, standardized testing, exam pressure, insufficient curriculum content, limited student readiness, parental pressures, and communication difficulties involving refugee students. These conditions encourage test preparation rather than scientific inquiry, discussion, or real-life application.

The study recommends explicitly incorporating citizenship objectives and skills into the science curriculum, expanding socio-scientific and environmental content, and providing teachers with training and support. It also calls for hands-on scientific activities, democratic participation, sustainability education, and a solution-oriented approach aligned with the Sustainable Development Goals.

The passage examines AI literacy and the educational use of robots, emphasizing their potential to personalize learning, support feedback and computational thinking, and promote inclusion, especially for children with special needs. A mixed-method study investigated future preschool and primary school teachers’ conceptions of robots at the University of Belgrade in 2024. Of 143 initial participants, 121 were analyzed after 22 misconceptions were identified. Participants completed a Draw-And-Answer Test by drawing a robot, describing its context and role, and explaining their choice; two evaluators achieved a Pearson correlation of 0.99.

Most participants accurately distinguished robots from other devices, and 98 reported direct experience with them, commonly at their faculty. Animal-shaped robots were the most frequent depiction (47.1%), followed by typical (24.8%) and mechanical robots (24.0%); humanoid robots accounted for 4.1%. Educational and assistive functions predominated. Most drawings conveyed neutral emotions, while positive emotions were associated mainly with animal robots. Cognitive considerations most often shaped participants’ choices, followed by affective and behavioral factors. The findings support more purposeful integration of educational robots into teacher curricula, alongside adequate teacher training, safety and privacy protections, and equitable access for all children.

Out-of-bounds possessions are a major part of the game, requiring preparation for baseline, sideline, and full-court inbound situations. Teams should first inbound successfully, then get the ball to their best players for a high-percentage shot. Plays should be simple and practiced, because improvised timeout plays rarely succeed. Inbounders need strong fundamental skills, vision, communication, timing, execution, and commitment to team play. A turnover creates a five-on-four offensive advantage, while using the five-second count gives the defense time to set up and a better-than-60% chance of a stop.

Players should understand automatic reads, including cutting to the basket when a defender faces away, quick give-and-go passes when the inbounder is unguarded, and lob passes over a defender who turns their back. They must anticipate defensive deployments, switches, and screens while accounting for balance and safety outlets. Coaches should scout opponents, explain anticipated reads and counters, and test players’ knowledge of inbound rules.

Key rules include a five-second limit to release the ball, no re-touching until another player touches it, and no changing the designated inbounder once an official selects them. The inbounder generally cannot leave the throw-in spot, though movement along the baseline is permitted after a made basket. A legal pass may go into the backcourt without an over-and-back violation, but the inbounder cannot throw the ball over the backboard or directly into the basket. Reaching over the out-of-bounds plane to touch the ball is a technical foul.

The passage frames Education 4.0 within the Fourth Industrial Revolution, emphasizing adaptable, personalized, competency-based learning that develops foundational, higher-order, social, and emotional skills. It calls for shifts from rote to inclusive learning and from memory-based to skill-based assessment, consistent with India’s National Education Policy 2020, which recommends games and gamification.

Digital Game-Based Learning can support meaningful, engaging, multimodal instruction through role-playing games, puzzles, simulations, quizzes, and multiplayer games. Games can promote intrinsic motivation, incidental learning, conceptual understanding, problem-solving, decision-making, adaptability, and other higher-order skills. Customized games aligned with learning outcomes may better meet course needs, support assessment, and provide tailored learning assistance. Digital games also enable learner-centered assessment through observable gameplay behaviors.

Stealth Assessment embeds assessment within gameplay. AI- and machine-learning-based systems analyze digital traces to identify competencies, including problem-solving, creativity, attention, persistence, reflection, and critical thinking. This enables continuous, largely unobtrusive assessment, immediate feedback, adaptive challenges, and individualized support while reducing test anxiety and teacher workload.

Effective stealth assessment relies on Evidence-Centered Design, formative feedback, and machine learning in a multidisciplinary effort involving education, psychology, programming, technology, and related fields. Gameplay data must be linked to defined competencies, and algorithms must determine what, how, when, and to what extent skills should be measured. Two integration methods are identified: embedding assessment activities directly in games and analyzing game log data through statistical and machine-learning methods. Games should also allow learners to replay difficult segments when mastery is not achieved.

Challenges include limited teacher adoption, the difficulty of developing customized games, insufficient research evidence, possible cognitive overload, and poorly calibrated difficulty levels. The validity and reliability of Digital Game-Based Learning also remain insufficiently established, requiring further technological and educational research.

The lecture reviews experimental studies of neutrino oscillations across solar, atmospheric, accelerator, and reactor sources, comparing their energies, baselines, and mass sensitivity. Solar electron neutrinos have meV energies and a nearly fixed Earth–Sun baseline. Homestake and later experiments observed fewer solar neutrinos than predicted, while SNO’s neutral-scattering measurement found the total number consistent with theory, providing evidence that neutrinos change flavor rather than disappear. Atmospheric neutrinos, produced by pion and kaon decays, exhibit energy- and direction-dependent muon-neutrino disappearance consistent with oscillations. Accelerator experiments at Fermilab, CERN, and in Japan use near and far detectors to measure flux and test appearance or disappearance; T2K results also support oscillations. Reactor neutrinos arise mainly from uranium and polonium fission, and their flux can be estimated from reactor power or fuel use. Experiments in France, Japan, and China measure electron-antineutrino disappearance through inverse beta decay, directly probing oscillation survival probabilities.

The paper argues that AI policy and governance are increasingly consequential for AI development but remain largely absent from computer science curricula, leaving developers underprepared to translate abstract or conflicting regulatory demands into technical practice. It synthesizes emerging AI policy in the United States and European Union to support classroom discussion and identify developers’ likely regulatory challenges.

The U.S. lacks comprehensive federal AI legislation and has relied heavily on executive orders and non-binding frameworks. Biden’s EO 14110 emphasized safe, secure, and trustworthy AI across eight policy areas but was rescinded on January 20, 2025, and replaced by EO 14179, which prioritizes U.S. global AI dominance, economic competitiveness, and national security. The EU AI Act, approved in March 2024, defines AI systems broadly, applies risk-based requirements, prohibits unacceptable-risk practices with limited law-enforcement exceptions, and imposes additional transparency obligations on general-purpose AI model providers. Three cross-jurisdictional themes emerge: rapidly changing policy, the difficulty of implementing nontechnical specifications technically, and the cross-border effects of regulation, exemplified by the EU’s “Brussels Effect.”

To integrate AI policy into computing courses, the authors propose a framework spanning socio-political, translational, and technical perspectives, crossed with the dimensions of scope, power, and agency. A grid of guiding questions connects policy principles, affected communities, implementation responsibilities, technical safeguards, stakeholder participation, and practitioner influence. The framework is designed to be flexible across curricula and policy contexts. Future work includes developing related classroom activities and applying requirements-engineering practices to bridge the gap between AI policy principles and technical specifications.

A penalty kick during normal play is a restart, and the ball becomes live when kicked. All attacking players except the kicker and goalkeeper must be at least 10 yards from the penalty mark, behind it, inside the field of play, and outside the penalty area. The referee’s signal does not permit them to advance; they must wait until the kicker touches the ball and it clearly moves forward.

Attackers must position themselves promptly, hold their ground against jostling, and be prepared to pursue rebounds. If the goalkeeper saves or blocks the kick, or the ball rebounds off the goal, active play resumes immediately. The kicker may touch the ball again after a goalkeeper save but not after a rebound from the goalpost or crossbar and must allow a teammate to collect goal rebounds. Teammates should react without hesitation or overrunning the ball. If the goalkeeper secures the ball, the attacking team must immediately switch to defense against a possible counterattack. Procedural offenses result in a retaken kick if a goal is scored or an indirect free kick if no goal is scored, subject to stated exceptions.

The ADS868xW is a 16-bit successive-approximation ADC with an integrated analog front end containing a programmable gain amplifier (PGA), antialiasing filter, ADC driver, and buffered precision reference. The PGA accepts single-ended or differential signals, adjusts their common-mode level, and maximizes ADC input dynamic range. Gain is selected through RANGE_SEL[3:0], whose power-on value of 0000 corresponds to an input range of ±3V × VREF. A trimmed resistor network supports multiple gain configurations with low gain error. A second-order low-pass filter at the PGA output reduces amplifier and resistor noise, with a typical −3 dB cutoff of 500 kHz. A high-bandwidth, low-noise integrated buffer ensures the ADC sample-and-hold capacitors charge and discharge at maximum sampling rates.

The device supports an internal or external 4.096V reference, selected with INTREF_DIS. With the internal reference enabled by default, REFIO is an output and requires a minimum 4.7µF decoupling capacitor. The internal reference is factory-trimmed and temperature-compensated over −40°C to +125°C, although soldering and reflow stress can shift its output; repeated reflows can cause additional shifts. For external-reference operation, REFIO becomes a 4.096V input, and the internal buffer drives REFCAP, which requires at least 10µF of capacitance plus a 1µF high-frequency decoupling capacitor. The reference buffer’s typical temperature drift is 0.5 ppm/°C, with a maximum of 2 ppm/°C.

The ADC supports bipolar and unipolar single-ended or differential inputs and produces straight-binary output. Full-scale range equals the difference between positive and negative full-scale voltages, and LSB size is FSR/2¹⁶. An active-high alarm output can be assigned to the ALARM/SDO-1/GPO pin. Input alarms use independently programmable high and low thresholds with programmable hysteresis, while AVDD alarms use fixed typical trip points of 4.7V and 5.3V. Each alarm has active and tripped flags in ALARM_REG; active flags are cleared after each conversion, whereas tripped flags remain set until the register is read. Alarm status can be accessed through the ALARM pin, ALARM_REG, or appended to output data.

The multiSPI interface provides a 32-bit input-output shift-register interface. Standard SPI connections use CONVST/CS, SCLK, SDI, and SDO-0, with RST tied to DVDD. Daisy-chain operation connects shared CONVST/CS and SCLK lines and links each SDO-0 to the next device’s SDI; all devices must use identical register settings, and an optimal frame contains 32 × N SCLK capture edges. Devices sample on the rising edge of CONVST/CS, and the host receives data beginning with the last device in the chain.

The device has RESET, ACQ, and CONV states. Pulling the active-low RST pin low initiates either an application reset or a full power-on reset, depending on RSTn_APP. Following the specified reset delay, the device enters ACQ and RVS goes high. A rising CONVST/CS edge starts conversion, which uses an internal clock and ends by returning the device to ACQ. The host can detect completion through RVS or wait for the maximum conversion time.

Programming uses nine configuration registers and supports register reads and writes. A transfer frame begins on the falling edge of CONVST/CS, loads the output word into the output shift register, and shifts input data on SCLK. Pulling CONVST/CS high transfers the received command and starts conversion. A 32-clock frame is optimal; short frames permit reads but invalidate writes, while long frames use the final 32 received bits as the command. Writes are synchronous to SCLK and include byte and half-word commands for reading, writing, clearing, and setting register bits. Output data can contain the latest conversion result, fixed test patterns, or register data. Optional appended fields include device address, input-range setting, supply and input alarm flags, and parity.

Four legacy SPI-compatible protocols—SPI-00-S, SPI-01-S, SPI-10-S, and SPI-11-S—are selectable through SDI_CTL_REG. Data reads can also use single- or dual-SDO operation or a source-synchronous protocol whose output clock is supplied on RVS and may be synchronized to either SCLK or the internal clock. Dual-SDO mode halves the required clock cycles for a given number of output bits.

The configuration registers include DEVICE_ID_REG, RST_PWRCTL_REG, SDI_CTL_REG, SDO_CTL_REG, DATAOUT_CTL_REG, RANGE_SEL_REG, ALARM_REG, ALARM_H_TH_REG, and ALARM_L_TH_REG. They control device identification, reset and low-power behavior, SPI input and output protocols, output flags and patterns, reference and input-range selection, alarm status, and alarm thresholds.

An application example combines an ADS8681W with an eight-channel MUX36D08 differential multiplexer to measure standard industrial voltage or current inputs. The ADS868xW settles to 1% accuracy in under 5µs, supports input ranges up to ±12.288V, and provides input and AVDD alarms. The device uses separate AVDD and DVDD supplies and requires close supply decoupling to improve PSRR. Programmable NAP and power-down modes reduce consumption at lower throughput rates; power-down retains the interface and registers while powering down analog blocks. Recommended layout separates analog and digital routing, uses specified AVDD, DVDD, REFIO, and REFCAP capacitors, and connects grounds through short, low-impedance paths.

The study develops and experimentally validates a multiscale framework linking atomistic solid–melt interface energetics to macroscopic GaN epitaxial growth. Machine-learning-potential molecular dynamics shows that liquid Ga forms ordered, structurally distinct layers at GaN interfaces, with stronger and more extended ordering at Ga-polar than N-polar surfaces, while charge redistribution remains concentrated near the first one or two interfacial layers.

Well-tempered metadynamics quantifies nitrogen adsorption and migration free energies. Ordered liquid Ga creates a “Ga lubrication” mechanism that lowers N-adatom migration barriers to about 0.56 eV at Ga-polar and 0.34 eV at N-polar interfaces, compared with approximately 1.1 eV on a clean Ga-polar surface. Step-edge barriers exceed 0.6 eV and can limit downhill adatom motion.

Kinetic Monte Carlo simulations parameterized by these barriers show flux-dependent growth: high N flux produces rough joint islands, whereas lower flux enables diffusion-controlled, layer-by-layer growth. Under practical MBE conditions, the active N flux is expected to favor this diffusion-limited step-flow regime.

The resulting continuum transport model combines concentration and chemical-potential gradients to calculate steady-state N flux and facet-dependent growth rates without fitted parameters. Inputs include interfacial free-energy profiles from metadynamics, N diffusivity from molecular dynamics, and N solubility from solvation free energies. Predicted rates of 0.01–0.04 nm/s capture observed trends: wurtzite prismatic m-planes grow faster than basal planes, the two polar basal planes have similar rates, and zinc-blende Ga-polar (111) grows faster than N-polar \(\bar1\bar1\bar1\), with (001) intermediate.

MBE experiments using Ga droplets nitrided for one and five minutes, followed by STEM/HRTEM, show progressive crystallization, faceting, and orientation-dependent growth consistent with these predictions. The study concludes that, for low-solubility systems such as N in liquid Ga, interfacial adsorption and migration free-energy landscapes are decisive for growth kinetics and morphology. Limitations include omitted impurities, uncertainties in machine-learning potentials, simplified one-dimensional steady-state transport assumptions, neglected interface complexities, and experimental averaging across multiple facets.

A support, or cover, defender positions behind and slightly infield of the first defender, goalside and close enough to react if the first defender is beaten in either direction. The position discourages an outside dribble while maintaining cover. The support defender uses a first-defender stance, maintains appropriate spacing, avoids overrunning play, and adjusts as the attacker and first defender move. Verbal calls include “support/you have help” to confirm cover, “jockey/delay/control/contain” to hold the attacker without tackling, and “challenge/take him/tackle” to authorize a challenge. If the first defender is beaten, the support defender may take over through a defensive switch. Drills progress from stationary positioning to relative movement and then half- and full-speed play with communication.

This medRxiv preprint compared air- and bone-conducted auditory brainstem response (ABR) and auditory steady-state response (ASSR) thresholds in infants aged 0–6 months with normal hearing or conductive hearing loss (CHL). Sixty-four infants were recruited and 50 completed testing; 14 were excluded because they could not sleep. Hearing status was classified by frequency using ABR results, with tympanometry and transient-evoked otoacoustic emissions used as cross-checks. No CHL was identified at 2000 Hz, so most analyses focused on 500 Hz.

At 500 Hz, infants with CHL had significantly higher air-conducted ABR and ASSR thresholds than normal-hearing infants, while bone-conducted thresholds did not differ significantly between groups. ABR and ASSR thresholds were poorly correlated. Mean air-bone gaps were 15 dB for normal-hearing and 36 dB for CHL infants using ABR, compared with 12 dB and 21 dB using ASSR. Both methods produced larger gaps in CHL, but ABR distinguished the groups better; ASSR measurements showed greater overlap between groups. ABR and ASSR air-bone gap sizes were also poorly correlated.

Minimum normal intensities were 35 and 20 dB nHL for air- and bone-conducted ABR at 500 Hz. Corresponding ASSR minimums were 40 and 30 dB HL. Across CHL-detection analyses, stricter cutoff criteria generally improved specificity but reduced sensitivity. Air-conducted ABR threshold measurement had the highest sensitivity and specificity compared with screening and ASSR measures. Because only mild, 500-Hz CHL was studied and no sensorineural-loss cases were included, the findings may not apply to more severe or differently distributed hearing loss.

The study concluded that ASSR thresholds and air-bone gaps were too variable to reliably distinguish normal hearing from mild low-frequency CHL under the tested conditions. ABR remains the preferred and gold-standard threshold assessment method in early hearing detection and intervention programs. Further research is needed to establish optimal ASSR protocols, correction factors, and performance across hearing-loss degrees and frequencies.

## NVIDIA Turing GPU Architecture — Summary

**Hybrid rendering model:** Turing GPUs combine rasterization and ray tracing in a cooperative "Hybrid Rendering" model, adding AI and simulation. Ray-traced shadows, ambient occlusion, and reflections with denoising can run on a single GPU (e.g., Quadro RTX 6000, GeForce RTX 2080 Ti), working with RTX, NVIDIA Real-Time Ray Tracing Libraries, OptiX, Microsoft DXR, and the Vulkan ray tracing API. Applications can also accelerate physics, collision detection, particle simulation, VRWorks Audio (built on OptiX), AI visibility queries, and in-engine path tracing for reference images.

**RT Cores and ray tracing:** Each SM includes an RT Core with two units — one for bounding-box tests, one for ray-triangle intersection — handling BVH traversal and ray casting so the SM is freed for other shading work. Without hardware, BVH traversal requires thousands of instruction slots per ray. Turing delivers over 10 Giga Rays/sec versus Pascal's ~1.1 Giga Rays/sec (10 TFLOPS/Giga Ray), roughly 10x faster. Fundamentals covered include ray casting (rays cast backward from the camera), BVH tree traversal and building/refitting, and denoising (both AI- and non-AI-based). Ray-traced shadows avoid shadow-map issues (resolution mismatch, contact hardening), RTAO is subtler and more realistic than SSAO, and ray-traced reflections avoid holes and artifacts of screen-space reflections. Examples are shown from *Battlefield V* and *Shadow of the Tomb Raider*.

**NGX (Neural Graphics Acceleration):** A deep-learning stack using Turing Tensor Cores, requiring Turing or later. Managed via GeForce Experience/Quadro Experience, which detects the GPU and downloads the NGX Core package and per-application DNN models; models interface with CUDA 10, DirectX/Vulkan drivers, and TensorRT. Features include:
- **DLSS:** a DNN trained on 64x supersampled "ground truth" images that infers higher-quality output than TAA at roughly half the shading work; standard DLSS renders at lower input sample count, while DLSS 2X renders at target resolution with a larger network to approach 64xSS quality, avoiding TAA's blurring, disocclusion, and transparency issues.
- **InPainting:** synthesizes replacement content trained on real-world images instead of copying nearby pixels.
- **AI Slow-Mo:** inserts interpolated frames for smooth slow-motion video.
- **AI Super Rez:** 2x, 4x, or 8x resolution increase creating new pixels, running in real time (~30 fps) for 1080p-to-4K upscaling with PSNR 1–2 dB above bicubic.

**Mesh Shading:** New Task and Mesh shader stages use cooperative thread models, letting a single object list replace many per-object CPU draw calls, enabling over an order of magnitude more objects in real time. Task shaders can pick LOD versions based on screen-space size and drive dynamic geometry culling/modification (e.g., spherical CAD cutaways).

**Variable Rate Shading (VRS):** Shading rate can be set per 16x16 pixel region with up to seven options, or specified spatially via texture and per-primitive attributes, independently of visibility rate. Applications include Content Adaptive Shading (shading-rate texture computed in post-processing from color coherence), Motion Adaptive Shading (using motion vectors, motion blur, or depth of field), and Foveated Rendering (using eye tracking). VRS can also raise shading rate up to the MSAA sample count.

**Texture Space Shading (TSS):** Shading is computed and stored in texture space and later sampled via texture lookup, decoupling visibility and appearance sampling onto different grids, rates, or timelines. It exploits spatial/temporal redundancy, reuses shaded texels across frames, provides MIP-map-based rate control, and enables stereo VR rendering by shading one eye and sampling it for the other.

**Multi-View Rendering (MVR):** Expands Pascal's Simultaneous Multi-Projection (SMP) — up to four views per pass in hardware, 32 at the API level, via the D3D12 View Instancing API and `SV_ViewID`, with the compiler sharing view-independent code across views. Uses include single-pass stereo for wide-FOV/canted-panel HMDs, four shadow depth buffers, cascaded shadow maps, and multiple character poses from one mesh.

**Resource and VR support:** Turing adds bindless Constant Buffer Views and Unordered Access Views (DX12 Tier 3) and supports Tier 2 resource heaps, allowing mixed resource types in one heap. VR benefits include USB Type-C/VirtualLink single-connector support, expanded MVR, foveated rendering, and RT Core-accelerated ray-traced audio in VRWorks.

**GPU configurations:**
- **TU104:** six GPCs, 48 SMs, 3072 CUDA cores, 368 Tensor Cores, 48 RT Cores, 13.6B transistors, eight 32-bit memory controllers (256-bit), second-generation NVLink (x8, 25 GB/s each direction). Used in GeForce RTX 2080, Tesla T4, and Quadro RTX 5000.
- **TU106 (GeForce RTX 2070, October 2018):** three GPCs, 36 SMs, 2304 CUDA cores, 288 Tensor Cores, 36 RT Cores, 10.8B transistors, 256-bit memory; no NVLink or SLI.
- **Tesla T4:** TU104-based inference GPU with five GPCs, 20 TPCs, 40 SMs, 2560 CUDA cores, 320 Tensor Cores, 256-bit memory at 10 Gbps for 320 GB/s, 70W base TDP design.

**RTX-OPS metric:** A workload-based metric derating peak operations by usage (Tensor 20%, CUDA 80%, RT 40%, INT32 28%), yielding 78 RTX-OPS for the RTX 2080 Ti, reflecting measured workload splits (DLSS ~20% of frame time, ray tracing about half of FP32 shading time, integer pipe active ~35% of shading time).

The document also contains NVIDIA's standard specification disclaimers, warranty limitations, liability terms, and trademark/copyright notices (© 2018 NVIDIA Corporation).

The study examines global, regional, and Ethiopian legal frameworks for inclusive education and assesses educational leaders’ awareness of these policies in Addis Ababa’s inclusive education resource centers. It used a qualitative case-study design involving 15 purposively selected participants from three resource centers: school principals, itinerant teachers, general teachers, and Ministry of Education inclusion experts. Data came from semi-structured interviews and reviews of international, regional, national, and school documents; interviews were transcribed and analyzed thematically.

The reviewed frameworks include the UDHR, CRC, Salamanca Statement, CRPD, Marrakesh Treaty, and Sustainable Development Goals at the global level; the African Charter on Human and Peoples’ Rights, African Charter on the Rights and Welfare of the Child, and African Disability Protocol regionally; and Ethiopia’s Constitution, Proclamation No. 1263/2021, Education and Training Policy 2023, Education Sector Development Plan VI, Special Needs/Inclusive Education Strategy, and National Children’s Policy nationally. Ministry experts noted that, despite these instruments and Ethiopia’s adoption of international agreements, the country lacks a specific stand-alone inclusive education policy.

Awareness varied by role. Ministry experts and itinerant teachers, many of whom had specialized training, demonstrated greater knowledge of relevant frameworks. Principals recognized inclusion’s importance but had limited knowledge of policy names, content, and international or regional standards. Classroom teachers supported inclusion through compassion and individualized assistance but generally were unaware of the legal frameworks. The findings identified a favorable policy environment but insufficient policy-focused training and awareness among leaders, which the study identifies as a barrier to effective implementation.

The study recommends regular professional development and workshops for leaders, integration of inclusive education law and rights-based practices into teacher-training curricula, and Ministry-level monitoring of policy awareness among school practitioners.

Yoga, rooted in India and historically taught individually, is now available in many group-based styles for general fitness, recreation and professional sport. It can improve breathing, concentration, flexibility, balance, calmness, strength and injury prevention, while supporting rehabilitation and athletic performance. Specialty classes address runners’ and cyclists’ biomechanical needs and muscle imbalances. The President submitted an agent’s report on Texas’s political, military, and civil condition and explained why the Executive had not acknowledged Texas’s independence. Although Texas had expelled Mexican authority, defeated Mexican forces, and established a functioning government, Mexico was rallying under a new leader and threatening another invasion, making Texas’s independence appear potentially temporary.

Recognition was described as a delicate responsibility that could be viewed as grounds for war. The United States had consistently avoided involvement in foreign internal disputes, waiting until new governments could securely maintain themselves before recognizing their independence, as with Spain’s former colonies, Mexico, New Granada, Venezuela, and Ecuador. Recognition authority was not expressly delegated by the Constitution, and because recognition could involve war, the President considered it prudent to seek Congress’s participation.

Further caution was warranted because the United States had previously claimed Texas, many inhabitants were American emigrants, and Texas had adopted a similar government and sought admission to the Union. Premature recognition could therefore appear motivated by a desire to acquire the territory. The President recommended maintaining neutrality until Mexico or another major power recognized Texas, or until time and events demonstrated beyond dispute that Texas’s government could sustain its sovereignty.

Classical Maxwell solvers simulate complex nanostructures but cannot capture nonclassical features such as photon correlations or entanglement, while master-equation quantum models are idealized and lack coupling to realistic macroscopic devices. Exact quantum formulations (GKSL, quantum SDEs) do not couple naturally to Maxwell solvers and become computationally prohibitive, and semiclassical Maxwell-Bloch/Langevin approximations miss nonclassical photon statistics.

The authors introduce a stochastic Bloch-vector approach based on SDEs, avoiding wave-function unraveling, phase-space representations, and operator-valued noise. This links quantum emitter dynamics to spatio-temporally resolved classical fields; for a coherently driven two-level system, stochastic trajectories are coupled to source currents and propagated with an FDTD solver.

Validation uses the Mollow triplet from resonance fluorescence of a strongly driven TLS, also observed in semiconductor quantum dots, whose sidebands exhibit nonclassical photon correlations relevant to single-photon and entangled-state generation.

Following the standard route from master equation to phase-space quasi-probability and Fokker–Planck equation (drift matrix A, diffusion matrix D), conventional treatments require symmetric, positive-semidefinite D = BB^T, yielding a linear Itô SDE with additive Gaussian white noise. Because this symmetry excludes asymmetric correlations arising from noncommuting quantum operators, the authors allow complex, non-symmetric D, interpreted as noise cross-covariance between two coupled stochastic processes.

The President transmitted to the Senate departmental reports responding to its resolution. He explained that he retained California’s military commandant as civil governor, following his predecessor’s arrangement, because Congress had established no territorial government and he made no appointment or increased compensation. To implement the Treaty of Guadalupe Hidalgo, he sent Thomas Butler King and other officers to California and New Mexico. He encouraged residents prepared to meet constitutional requirements to draft state constitutions and seek admission to the Union, while prohibiting executive interference in their elections, conventions, or domestic institutions.

He urged Congress to admit California and New Mexico as states, reasoning that delay would prolong national controversy over whether involuntary servitude should extend to the territories. California’s proposed constitution was already being prepared independently of his wishes and should receive congressional approval if constitutional. He submitted Texas’s claim to part of New Mexico for congressional resolution and advised against establishing a territorial government before adjusting the boundary, noting that the existing laws and military protection benefited residents. He affirmed that conditions on California’s admission contrary to residents’ wishes would infringe on self-government and face strong opposition. He recommended awaiting the territories’ own political development to avoid sectional conflict and preserve national harmony.

The passage specifies the Guest-Hypervisor Communication Block (GHCB) standard for SEV-ES and SEV-SNP guests. It defines a 4 KB, page-aligned, decrypted or shared memory area that mirrors relevant SEV-ES VMCB save-state fields. Version 2 adds hypervisor feature advertisement through a 52-bit FEATURES bitmap, protocol-version negotiation, and minimum required feature support. Later revisions add 64-bit guest-request sequence numbers, the VLEK GUID, APIC ID discovery, multiple VMPL levels, page-state changes, SEV-TIO, and Secure AVIC.

The GHCB MSR protocol, MSR 0xc001_0130, supports feature queries, CPUID requests, AP reset hold, GHCB GPA registration and removal, page-state changes, VMPL changes, and termination requests. SEV-SNP guests must register their GHCB GPA before using the block for VMGEXIT.

The document distinguishes automatic exits, which expose no guest state, from non-automatic exits (NAEs), which cause a #VC exception and allow the guest to select state shared through the GHCB. It standardizes VALID_BITMAP handling, VMGEXIT processing, error reporting, and NAE events covering I/O protection, MSR protection, MMIO faults, page-state changes, SNP guest and extended requests, AP creation, doorbells, restricted IPIs and timers, APIC ID lists, SNP TIO, Secure AVIC, and termination. It also defines SNP secrets-page reserved fields and the EFI Confidential Computing Blob protocol for passing secrets and CPUID pages to the OS.

SMP boot requirements are covered, including AP reset hold, AP jump tables, and SNP AP creation. NMI handling, debug-register virtualization, guest identification, and unsupported-event behavior are also defined. SMM and nested virtualization are not supported.

For SNP Restricted Injection, the host communicates pending events through a shared #HV doorbell page containing PendingEvent and NoEoiRequired fields. The host is expected to emulate APIC interrupt presentation, acknowledgment, in-service, and EOI behavior and to follow defined guest HLT and interrupt-shadow conventions.

NASA Glenn researchers in Cleveland are using the Glenn Extreme Environments Rig (GEER), the largest and most accurate planetary simulator, to reproduce Venus’s surface conditions. After 80 days, extreme heat, pressure, and supercritical carbon dioxide dramatically altered tested rocks and minerals, providing rare data on material survival. The rig also tested a durable computer chip that operated for 21 days—the first demonstration of multi-week electronics operation in a Venus environment and a potential advance toward longer missions.

Venus’s surface is nearly uninhabitable, but its upper atmosphere is cooler and calmer. Around 30 miles above the surface, air-filled craft could float, though the clouds contain concentrated sulfuric acid. Researchers say Venus may offer clues about Earth’s climate because its runaway greenhouse effect boiled away its early oceans, and microbial life may exist in the more Earth-like upper atmosphere.

The speaker says their team spent much of the third period in its own end, repeating the previous game’s pattern and limiting scoring chances. They praise the opponent’s strong backchecking but criticize their own forechecking for coasting instead of applying speed and making effective dumps. A goalie’s save prevented them from gaining momentum, and their strategy did not work.

The passage argues that Berkshire Hathaway’s OxyChem acquisition benefits Occidental Petroleum more: it could reduce leverage, sharpen its exploration and production focus, support stronger growth, and expand valuation multiples, while the deal is immaterial to Berkshire’s diversified operations and financials. It also promotes Envision Early Retirement’s investment research services, followed by author credentials, disclosures, related article links, and chart metadata.

Viridor and the Somerset Waste Partnership are building a £252 million resource recovery centre at Avonmouth. Once fully operational in 2020, it will convert non-recyclable household waste into electricity for the National Grid, potentially powering 44,000 homes while reducing landfill use. Its launch will coincide with expanded kerbside recycling collections. The process heats treated waste and captures the released energy. Viridor says the process is safe and compliant with the European Industrial Emissions Directive. The centre requires an environmental permit and will be continually monitored by the Environment Agency.

Oakland beat Texas 3-2 to win four straight. Andrew Triggs pitched six innings, allowing one run, and Mark Canha hit a solo homer. Jed Lowrie and Matt Olson added RBI doubles, while Oakland’s bullpen preserved the lead for Santiago Casilla’s first save. Adrian Beltre drove in both Rangers runs but injured his left hamstring. Cole Hamels took the loss, and Doug Fister will start Wednesday opposite Kendal Graveman.

Martin James Cooper, 66, was convicted of 30 historical child sex offences against four girls and four boys aged 11–16 in his care at Warminda Hostel between 1978 and 1983. Witnesses described a culture of fear, intimidation, violence and sexual abuse. His lawyer sought bail pending sentencing due to early-onset dementia and health issues, but the court refused and remanded him in custody, saying jail was inevitable.

The S&P 500 fell sharply from Thursday’s record high of 6,427.02 to Friday’s low of 6,212.69, losing more than 3% from its peak and closing at its lowest level since early July. Futures pointed to a Monday rebound near 6,300, with resistance at 6,330 and support at 6,280. Investor sentiment was slightly improved, with 40.3% of individual investors bullish and 33% bearish. Although no strong bearish signals were confirmed, a deeper correction or topping pattern remains possible, and the VIX reached 21.90, its highest level since June 23.

Oil prices declined amid the stock selloff, tariff uncertainty, weak employment and PMI data, and OPEC+ plans to increase September output by 547,000 barrels per day. Potential U.S. sanctions on Russian oil could offset resulting surpluses.

The outlook anticipates a short-term rebound within a broader consolidation or downtrend, with earnings, valuations, low volatility, and macro risks prompting consideration of defensive positioning. Headlines also covered Netflix’s decline after Elon Musk urged cancellations and the continuing U.S. government shutdown. The page promotes stock-screening tools and cautions that quoted data may not be real-time and that trading involves substantial risk.

Dallas said Mike Modano’s ligament problem had caused no further damage and that he could play if physically and mentally ready, though faceoffs, shooting and passing remained concerns. Plante, Hrkac or Sydor could fill in, but Dallas otherwise expected Modano to play every situation because of his defensive responsibilities and all-around ability. Ed Belfour’s serious back injury required lengthy, seven-day-a-week rehabilitation; despite improved physical condition and an improving relationship with the team, his continued participation depended on being ready to play regularly. Dallas credited Satan and Sanderson for their puck work and defense, with Curtis Brown leading the forwards. Against Hasek, Dallas planned to pursue loose pucks aggressively but not interfere with a goalie controlling the puck; a stick outside the crease was considered fair game. Dave Hull’s pulled groin was day-to-day, and Dallas expected him to contribute if the injury allowed. The team’s defensive intensity, penalty kills and hard work generated energy against Buffalo, although it became emotional in the third period and disputed a late penalty against Hrkac. Hogue and Reid were praised as complementary linemates, and Dallas emphasized confidence, preparation and competitive heart over age.

A small study of healthy young men found that women judged the body odor of men who ate more fruits and vegetables to be more appealing, while men consuming lots of carbohydrates were rated less favorably. Researchers measured skin carotenoid levels, assessed eating patterns, and asked women to rate men's sweat after exercise. Meat intake did not affect perceived attractiveness but tended to make odor more intense. Experts emphasized that diet influences body odor indirectly: bacteria on the skin metabolize compounds in sweat, which is not inherently smelly. The study did not assess same-sex couples, and earlier research also linked a non-meat diet with preferred male odor.

Maya Kodes, an interactive virtual pop star created by Montreal’s Neweb Labs, released “Boomerang” on iTunes, recorded an EP, performed 30 concerts, and amassed 5,500 Facebook followers. Neweb plans a June 13 livestream EP launch, a Toronto performance, and international tours.

Microsoft Corporation filed a Form 8-K dated January 26, 2017, reporting its financial results for the fiscal quarter ended December 31, 2016. The related press release was furnished as Exhibit 99.1 and was not considered “filed” or incorporated by reference except through specific reference.

Mac Otakara reports that Apple's rumored "iPhone Edition" may take design cues from the mid-tier Apple Watch, featuring a polished stainless steel frame sandwiched between glass plates with Touch ID hidden under the display (a disputed claim). Rumors also point to vertically positioned dual cameras supporting VR or augmented reality, based on documents seen during engineering and design verification testing.

Machine learning potentials (MLPs) predict potential energy surfaces with the efficiency of classical potentials (O(N)) instead of DFT (O(N³)), but are limited by scarce training datasets; pre-trained universal interatomic potentials (UIPs) such as NequIP and MACE cover nearly all elements yet are trained mostly on bulk crystals and systematically underestimate surface energies ("softening"), while curated surface datasets remain limited. This study compares training from scratch on surface data (TS), zero-shot use of a pre-trained foundation model (ZS), fine-tuning (FT), and multi-head fine-tuning (MHFT, training jointly on bulk and surface data) for three surface systems: Au (unary), RuO2 (binary), and BiVO4 (ternary). Among benchmarked UIPs (M3GNet, SevenNet-l3i5, MACE-MP-0a-small, ORBv2, eqV2-M), MACE was chosen as the foundation model.

In all three systems FT outperformed TS at equal training-set size, and larger datasets improved all models. For Au (2,545 configurations; 2,000 train/validation, 545 test), ZS errors were 14.8 meV/atom and 74.7 meV/Å; FT with only 40 points reduced these to 4.3 meV/atom and 37.4 meV/Å, while TS trained on 2,000 configurations matched or was worse than FT trained on 40–200. TS also produced unphysical short-range Au–Au curves (training contained no pairs below 2.21 Å) and incorrect long-range repulsion, whereas FT described the whole energy landscape accurately. For RuO2 (340 structures; 300 train, 40 test), FT again gave lower errors, though force errors were several times larger than for Au due to complex bonding; TS yielded unphysical pair potentials with attraction below 0.7 Å, while FT was physically reasonable apart from a spurious sub-0.4 Å attraction blocked by a ~500 eV barrier. For BiVO4 (928 configurations; 592 train, 336 test), FT remained best and TS risked atomic collisions from weak short-range oxygen repulsion. Force analysis showed FT with lowest RMSE (0.17 eV/Å vs. 0.24 for TS and 0.42 for ZS) and fewest large-force outliers (3 vs. 13 for TS, 2 for ZS), reflecting reuse of the foundation model's high-force knowledge.

Case 4 showed conventional FT on Au data generalized poorly to other unary metals (Ag, Cu, Pt, Ir), performing worse than ZS (RMSE 88 vs. 27 meV/Å²). MHFT (2,000 Au points plus 200,000 randomly selected MPTrj entries from ~1.5 million) gave 16 meV/Å², roughly half the ZS error, though gold-surface energy error rose from ~1.3 to ~2.8 meV/atom—within DFT reproducibility limits of 1–2 meV/atom—and MHFT required roughly 100× the training time of FT.

Discussion: FT matched TS accuracy with one-third or as few as 100 data points; accuracy declined as system complexity rose; surface softening was attributed mainly to missing surface coverage in pre-training. MHFT is advantageous where bulk competence must be preserved alongside gains on scarce specialized data, provided computational conditions and energy reference points are aligned between datasets, whereas conventional FT tolerates moderate mismatches better. Recommended practice: with only tens of first-principles structures, add related data to a foundation model and compare FT/MHFT against ZS to choose the best starting point.

Methods: MACE/ACEsuit 0.3.12 (per-atom RMSE, r_max 6 Å, max_ell 3, two message-passing steps, SiLU, batch 4, Adam, learning rate 0.02, energy/force loss weights 10/1; FT/MHFT learning rate 0.001, weight_pt_head 0.1), with 20% random validation for early stopping; DFT via VASP 6.5.0 with PBE, 600 eV cutoff, Γ-point sampling, spin polarization, 0.01 eV smearing, and MPtrj-consistent pseudopotentials.

The article examines trauma-informed human rights education (TIHRE) in higher education and argues that it can reduce retraumatisation and secondary or vicarious trauma while supporting learner agency, advocacy and action. Although human rights education spans lifelong learning and influences many disciplines, it remains concentrated in law schools and often focuses narrowly on international law while avoiding emotionally challenging historical cases. Such omissions conflict with the purpose of human rights education and may compound trauma among students with lived or inherited experiences of abuse, conflict, displacement or other rights violations.

A structured, interdisciplinary literature review informs three central recommendations. First, educators should clarify their values, motivations and biases, develop an authentic, rights-respecting teaching persona, build meaningful relationships with learners, and recognise their own positionality and unresolved trauma. Second, trauma-informed principles should shape curriculum content and planning. Courses should integrate the UN framework of learning about, through and for human rights; develop practical skills and capacities; and use flexible, collaborative and project-based learning, including student co-creation. Educators should avoid graphic material, retraumatising narratives, exploitation through “trauma porn” and romanticisation of trauma or resilience. Advance notice, wellbeing check-ins, opportunities for reflection and self-care, and action-oriented reflection can support safety, trust and learner empowerment.

Third, human rights teaching should use dialogic approaches built on horizontal relationships, mutual respect and trust. Learners should be encouraged to engage critically with difficult issues and participate in dialogue with one another, survivors of rights abuses, and practitioners such as lawyers and NGO workers. Incorporating lived experience through interviews, lectures and question-and-answer sessions can connect theoretical learning with practical application, strengthen communication and coalition-building, and promote dignity, healing and reconciliation. Overall, TIHRE should place wellbeing, agency and dignity at the centre of higher education while moving educators and learners from avoidance toward rights-based advocacy and action.

This IDC white paper examines how industrial simulation, modeling, data analysis, and high-performance computing (HPC) can support manufacturing innovation and digital transformation. It is based on a December 2021 telephone survey of 200 IT and departmental decision makers from discrete and process manufacturers with more than 500 employees in Germany, Austria, and Switzerland.

Manufacturers face geopolitical uncertainty, rising energy prices, material shortages, supply-chain disruptions, skilled-labor constraints, and sustainability goals. IT-based simulation and modeling are increasingly important for accelerating product development, reducing costs, improving quality, avoiding defects, and supporting faster, better-informed decisions. Although use is expanding, data silos and differing departmental “truths” remain obstacles; integrating data into a unified information base is presented as essential.

More than half of respondents already use simulation, modeling, and virtual prototyping, while digital twins, IoT and sensor data, design optimization, and digital verification create additional scenarios. Digital twins can monitor physical assets, test hypothetical changes, and support ecosystem services and outcome-based business models. Forty-two percent already use high-performance data analytics.

Demand for complex calculations is expected to rise sharply as methods become more sophisticated and computationally intensive. Forty-two percent report that some simulations are outdated or inaccurate, half say calculations take too long, and demand for high-performance calculations is expected to move from 8% to nearly half within two years. HPC is viewed by 81% of decision makers as a game changer for product and process innovation because it enables complex calculations, faster and more extensive analysis, new use cases, and greater agility. More than a quarter of enterprises already use professional HPC infrastructure, while another 39% are planning or piloting it.

Most current HPC users favor external infrastructure, including cloud services and colocation, because in-house systems require substantial investment, maintenance, licensing, and upgrades. Security is the leading concern for 72%, while energy consumption and sustainability are key issues for 58%. Modernized architectures and improved energy and computing efficiency can mitigate some environmental and cost pressures.

The paper examines whether qualitative information in corporate earnings press releases helps predict announcement-day stock returns. Using 138,676 stock-announcement observations from 2005–2023, with 134,354 used in the main analysis, the authors combine earnings surprises with text representations generated by BKMX, online LDA, BERT, MPNET, and FinBERT. Rolling-window Lasso regressions avoid look-ahead bias, while cross-sectional regressions and SHAP values assess predictive and explanatory power.

Soft press-release information is about as informative as numerical earnings surprises in explaining announcement returns, raising explanatory power to roughly 4.4%. FinBERT performs best, while LDA-based representations improve interpretability. Combining text and surprise signals predicts extreme returns better than either alone: agreement between the two identifies about 44%–52% of the top 10 positive and negative performers. Text signals do not predict returns before announcements, suggesting limited leakage.

A trading strategy based on agreement between the signals produces no profit after the market opens, consistent with market efficiency. However, advance access to both earnings surprises and press-release content can improve stock selection, as illustrated by previously documented hacking incidents. Topic analysis also finds that companies frame internal financial performance more positively and external sector or economic factors more negatively, consistent with self-serving bias. Future work will incorporate conference-call text and audio.

The Federal Reserve's fourth rate hike in 18 months, which raised its benchmark to 1 percent–1.25 percent, will push up credit card, home equity line and some adjustable mortgage rates by roughly a quarter point — about $700 in added payments over the life of a $5,000 credit card balance, according to Bankrate.com. Auto and home loan rates have barely moved, since fixed mortgages track the 10-year Treasury rather than Fed policy; the 30-year rate was 4.06 percent in December 2015 and 4.04 percent last week. The Fed expects one more hike this year and three in 2018, though timing of any mortgage rate increase is uncertain.

Higher U.S. rates attract overseas investment, strengthen the dollar, and pull capital from developing countries, making dollar-denominated debts harder to repay.

Savers benefit little: the average one-year CD rose only from 0.27 to 0.35 percent, while top-yielding CDs went from 1.35 to 1.5 percent, with smaller banks now paying more than large banks.

Consumers with poor credit face higher costs, especially on used-car loans, but overall effects should stay mild given historically low rates. Retirees are advised to remain in bonds and balance short- and long-term holdings.

A UCLA geography professor’s study estimates that meat eaten by U.S. dogs and cats, along with their waste, produces about 64 million tons of carbon dioxide annually—equivalent to 13.6 million cars driven for a year—and accounts for 25–30% of the environmental impact of U.S. meat consumption. Pet food uses livestock byproducts that might otherwise be wasted, while some studies indicate dogs can thrive on vegan diets. However, veterinarians warn against purely plant-based diets, especially for cats, which require taurine; a 2015 study found many vegetarian pet foods failed labeling standards and lacked critical amino acids.

U.S. Treasury yields rose after a jobs report showed 33,000 payroll jobs lost, the first monthly decline since 2010, while unemployment fell to 4.2% and hourly earnings rose 2.9%. The 10-year yield climbed to 2.370% and the two-year to 1.511%, extending a four-week streak. Traders viewed wage growth as potentially inflationary and attributed job losses to hurricanes. Fed futures implied an 88% chance of a December rate hike, while geopolitical concerns and upcoming debt auctions also influenced yields.

An Oct. 16, 2000 email forwarded by Enron's Steven Kean to Maureen McVicker, titled "Enron Mentions," collected three news items.

**Wall Street Journal:** On Oct. 4, the Department of Energy awarded Strategic Petroleum Reserve contracts to three little-known black entrepreneurs — Lance Stroud (Harlem), Renard D. Euell (Denver) and Ronald Peek (Tallahassee) — alongside Marathon Ashland, Morgan Stanley Dean Witter, BP Amoco and Amerada Hess. Each winner must replace the oil plus interest a year later and post a letter of credit equal to the oil's value five days after bidding; the DOE had waived financial guarantees. Stroud, who bid on four million barrels over the Internet, spent the week seeking financing while his mother, Iris Manning, died of cardiac arrest; a deal with an unnamed refiner collapsed three hours before his deadline, though Koch Industries and BP Amoco also pursued him. Euell, who bid three million barrels, called Enron chairman Ken Lay directly; Enron VP John Nolan responded from London and Enron lawyers drafted a $93 million letter of credit, but trader Patrick Danaher's optimism faded, and Enron spokesman Eric Thode said "at no time was there anything remotely resembling a deal." Euell obtained a 24-hour extension and European bank pledges but still missed the paperwork, and his award lapsed. Peek transferred his three-million-barrel interest to Hess Energy Trading, which includes Amerada Hess; a company vice president said an "arrangement" produced "a lot of money" for Peek. The DOE said it would accept new bids on the seven million barrels Stroud and Euell forfeited.

**Washington Post "Deal of the Week":** Artesia Technologies, a Rockville-based digital asset management company, raised $26 million in a second round led by Warburg Pincus Ventures with strategic partners EA Systems, Enron Broadband Services, Vignette, Razorfish and Protege Virtual Management Solutions. Created by CEO Chris Veator in a management-led buyout of Thomson Financial's information management division, Artesia plans international expansion (London office opened last June), doubling staff and tripling revenue over 12 months.

**Houston Chronicle:** Articles examine the downtown basketball arena proposal on the Nov. 7 ballot. Rockets owner Leslie Alexander would pay about $7 million a year and gain an estimated $30–45 million annually from suites, club seats and naming rights; the city would spend up to $20 million on land and receive $200,000 a year, 20 arena days and a center-court suite valued at $250,000–$500,000. The Harris County-Houston Sports Authority would sell bonds for $175 million in design and construction and repay a $30 million interest-free-for-five-years parking garage loan; total cost estimates range from $220 million to $256 million, with the Rockets paying 30–50 percent and taxpayers $125–175 million. Tax-watchers call it corporate welfare; economists cited argue economic impact is negligible and public subsidies are disguised, noting more than $21.7 billion has gone to 95 big-league stadiums since 1990, two-thirds from public sources. Supporters cite doubled land values near the arena site and Enron Field's $700 million in downtown development. The Chronicle editorial urges voters to approve the proposal.

Vegas’s expansion draft begins next week, with the Golden Knights selecting one player from each team over three days. Teams may protect 11 fixed-position or nine flexible players, subject to experience and exposure rules. Readers are invited to submit Calgary’s protected list and predict Vegas’s choice.

Notre Dame received two gifts totaling $205 million. Alumnus Matthew Walsh and Joyce Walsh gave $150 million to its School of Architecture, which will be renamed for them. Francis and Kathleen Rooney also endowed an institute, established in 2008 as the Rooney Center for the Study of American Democracy, to promote scholarship and dialogue on American democracy.

Apple Inc. reported that its annual shareholders’ meeting was held on February 13, 2018. Shareholders elected James Bell, Tim Cook, Al Gore, Bob Iger, Andrea Jung, Art Levinson, Ron Sugar, and Sue Wagner as directors. They approved Ernst & Young LLP as Apple’s independent registered public accounting firm for 2018, an advisory resolution on executive compensation, and the amended and restated Non-Employee Director Stock Plan. Shareholder proposals titled “Shareholder Proxy Access Amendments” and “Human Rights Committee” were not approved. The Form 8-K was signed on February 14, 2018, by Katherine Adams, Senior Vice President and General Counsel.

The passage argues that Apple should enable Siri to learn custom words, pronunciations, nicknames, and user-defined command interpretations. For example, users could teach Siri how to pronounce names or define “remind me” to schedule a reminder for noon the next day. Repeated public instruction could help expand Siri’s vocabulary through machine learning. Its existing contact-nickname feature is described as limited and prone to misunderstanding natural requests. The author ultimately urges Apple to add broader learning capabilities so Siri can handle personalized terminology and commands more effectively.

North Park Elementary School reopened in San Bernardino after a shooting killed Karen Smith and 8-year-old Jonathan Martinez and wounded 9-year-old Nolan Brandy. Police said Cedric Anderson targeted Smith before killing himself. The school tightened security, maintained a memorial and offered counseling as students resumed classes.

Amsterdam’s Buiksloterham docklands regeneration is an experimental alternative to conventional redevelopment. Its centerpiece, De Ceuvel, is a temporary ten-year hub built from renovated houseboats on a polluted former shipyard. It supports artists, entrepreneurs and sustainability researchers, while phytoremedial gardens help remove toxins. Waste is reused through wormery, composting toilets, mineral extraction, composting, gardens and aquaponics. Solar panels and heat exchangers provide renewable energy, while the Jouliettes cryptocurrency rewards energy-efficient businesses. The wider district includes plans for self-built eco-homes and an inclusive circular neighborhood. The approach aims to restore contaminated post-industrial land naturally at lower cost, contrasting with luxury docklands developments that require costly soil removal and can displace local communities.

Kilauea’s eruption has devastated Hawaii’s Big Island, where fast-moving lava from Fissure 8 advanced at about 600 yards per hour and threatened additional homes in Leilani Estates and Lanipuna Gardens. Kapoho residents were evacuated as lava approached. The eruption has produced lava fountains, ash, volcanic glass fibers known as Pele’s hair, more than 2,000 earthquakes, and high sulfur dioxide emissions; roughly 22 fissures, 40 destroyed homes, 2,000 acres of land, and 200 emergency shelter residents have been reported. Volcanic haze traveled about 4,000 miles to Guam, prompting warnings for people with respiratory conditions and maritime and aviation operators. The USGS also advised against roasting marshmallows over volcanic vents because sulfur dioxide, hydrogen sulfide, and sulfuric acid could make them hazardous.

Peel Regional Police say they have made “very good progress” identifying three men seen attacking a 29-year-old autistic man at Square One’s bus station in Mississauga around 10:45 p.m. on March 13. Investigators believe the suspects, unidentified for six days, are originally from British Columbia’s Lower Mainland and recently traveled to the GTA, so police are circulating the video in Vancouver, Surrey, Abbotsford, Richmond and nearby areas. All three are described as South Asian and 5-foot-10, with varying builds, facial hair and clothing. The victim remains shaken, and police are supporting him and his family. Tips may be given to Peel police, local police or Crime Stoppers.

Tests found RSI ineffective as a mean-reversion indicator for Bitcoin: buying at low RSI readings and selling at high readings produced few trades and weak results, with similar outcomes for Ethereum and Dogecoin. RSI performed better as a momentum indicator. In a representative Bitcoin strategy using five-day RSI, buying above 50 and selling below 50 produced a 122% CAGR versus 101% for buy-and-hold, with a 39% drawdown versus 83%. The article concludes that RSI appears useful in crypto markets when treated as a momentum indicator rather than a contrarian mean-reversion tool.
The Supreme Court considers Arkansas’s appeal of a stay affecting two inmates. Don Davis received a last meal and could be executed if the state wins; an appeals court reversed a broader halt.

The manuscript examines quantitative criticalism as an approach that combines quantitative methods with critical epistemologies to advance social justice, equity, and collective liberation in education research. It guides scholars using quantitative or critical approaches, including students, faculty, institutional researchers, and methods instructors, in recognizing positionality, identifying methodological tensions, and applying critical theories throughout research design, analysis, interpretation, and dissemination.

The authors describe their own social positions and argue that quantitative research is never fully objective because researchers’ lived experiences, identities, assumptions, and biases shape scholarship. Quantitative criticalism challenges neutral claims about numbers, addresses systemic oppression, questions conventional policies, theories, and measures, and treats marginalized students as participants in systems rather than as individuals defined by deficits. Justice-driven research requires community partnership, transparent positionalities, attention to power in collaborations, and consideration of data sovereignty.

Major tensions include white supremacist and cisheteropatriarchal foundations of statistics, the unclear threshold of criticality, difficulties operationalizing complex identities, limited samples and analytical options for minoritized populations, challenges in measuring institutional oppression, and conflicts between community-specific inquiry and statistical generalizability. Critical scholars also face tensions between categorizing identities for quantitative analysis and recognizing identities as fluid and heterogeneous.

Four studies illustrate applications of critical race theory, queer theory, and intersectionality. Sablan’s work operationalizes community cultural wealth, Garvey’s study examines sexual-identity categories and within-group differences, Szymanski and Lewis analyze gendered racism through interaction effects, and Wilson and Urick use latent class analysis to examine educational opportunity. Their benefits, limitations, and methodological choices demonstrate both the potential and continuing tensions of quantitative criticalism.

The authors call for adaptable, transparent, collaborative, and justice-oriented quantitative scholarship; curricula that teach both methods and epistemology; and continued reflection on researchers’ intentions, impacts, and thresholds of criticality.

The paper introduces SpinGPT, an LLM-based poker agent for the three-player Spin & Go tournament format. It notes that poker's incomplete information and flexible bet sizing create an immense game tree, and that prior AI progress came mainly from CFR-based methods (Cepheus, DeepStack, Libratus, Pluribus) in one-on-one settings, where such approaches have not been surpassed. Earlier LLM work such as PokerGPT was limited by low-quality spectator data.

SpinGPT is built on Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct (with a smaller Llama-3.2-1B also tested) and uses a two-stage pipeline. First, supervised fine-tuning via LoRA (rank 8, four epochs) on 320,000 decisions from 8,800 Spin & Go games played professionally by one author on PartyPoker.fr (2018–2020), encoded as structured text prompts with a custom action vocabulary. Second, offline reinforcement learning with ORPO (β = 0.1) on 270,000 InstaGTO solver-generated hands mixed with 50,000 human hands, aligning the model toward GTO play.

Results: SpinGPT-SFT reached 80% exact accuracy and 86% macro F1 on professional test data (PokerGPT scored 78% F1), with few illegal moves. The final SpinGPT scored 79% exact accuracy, 83% macro F1, and improved MAE from 0.61 to 0.30 BB; on solver data it reached 72% exact and 78% tolerant accuracy. With a heuristic all-in patch, SpinGPT-SFT beat Slumbot at 13.4 ± 12.9 BB/100 over 30,000 hands, and SpinGPT beat SpinGPT-SFT at 13.2 ± 7.24 BB/100 over 10,000 hands at 25 BB.

Limitations include no evaluation of the final model against Slumbot, format mismatch, and LLM numerical errors. Future work proposes stronger models, RAG over GTO charts, chain-of-thought reasoning, opponent adaptivity, explainability, and solver–LLM hybrid play.

Global learning and employment challenges are intensified by pandemic-related closures, climate change, conflict, and economic slowdown. The annual cost of children not learning is estimated at US$129 billion; youth unemployment in lower-income countries is near 30%, and in 2023, 20% of youth worldwide were not in employment, education, or training, two-thirds of them women. Employers report skill shortages, educational mismatch, and undereducation, while 39% of today’s job skills are expected to change or become obsolete by 2030.

GPE supports lower-income countries through policy dialogue, financing, knowledge investments, and public-private partnerships to build inclusive education systems combining foundational learning with creativity, analytical ability, problem-solving, and collaboration. Initiatives include Lesotho’s education funding, Ghana’s $40 million foundational-learning plan, Kenya’s competency-based curriculum, and El Salvador’s teacher training in socio-emotional skills and creative thinking. Twenty active GPE grants in 2024 focused on employment-related skills, while GPE’s A4L and KIX initiatives developed assessment tools and supported integrating 21st-century skills into national policies.

The passage identifies 17 habits that may hinder weight loss and recommends alternatives:

- Replace plastic bottles with stainless-steel bottles because plastic can leach BPA.
- Don’t eliminate sweets entirely; substitute fruit for artificial sweeteners.
- Avoid self-scolding and emotional eating; forgive setbacks, keep improving, and exercise when upset.
- Avoid store-bought protein bars and energy drinks; use nuts or coconut water instead.
- If reducing sweets, eat them only shortly before exercise.
- Surround yourself with people who support your goals.
- Measure success by following a routine, not by scale weight.
- Avoid meal replacements, which may increase hunger and cravings; eat real food.
- Don’t eliminate carbohydrates or fats; choose whole grains and healthy fats to maintain a balanced diet.
- Get at least seven hours of sleep.
- Don’t eat too little while exercising more, as the passage claims starvation mode can inhibit fat burning.
- Vary workouts weekly because the body adapts to repeated routines, reducing energy expenditure and causing plateaus.
- Don’t drink calories instead of meals, as liquids may leave you hungrier.
- Ease into dietary changes rather than restricting too strictly too soon.
- Tailor weight-loss routines to your body type, metabolism, and health rather than copying someone else’s plan.

The MACD histogram represents the difference between the MACD line and its signal line, helping identify momentum changes and potential reversals. Bars above zero indicate bullish momentum, bars below zero bearish momentum, and bar height reflects momentum strength. The crossover strategy buys when the histogram moves above zero and sells when it moves below zero, entering at the close and exiting when the close first exceeds the previous close; the reverse applies to shorts. Backtesting across 77 ETFs produced 6,669 trades, with stronger results for longs than shorts. The strategy remained mostly in cash. A leveraged QLD backtest covering more than 18 years recorded 85 trades, a 2.2% average gain, 10.4% annual returns, 5% market exposure, and a 19% maximum drawdown.

NVIDIA’s Turing GPU architecture introduces a new display engine supporting higher resolutions, faster refresh rates, HDR, DisplayPort 1.4a, and visually lossless DSC 1.2 compression. It can drive two 8K displays at 60 Hz, including over USB-C. Native HDR processing and BT.2100 tone mapping are supported. An enhanced NVENC encoder adds H.265 8K encoding at 30 fps and bitrate savings of up to 25% for HEVC and 15% for H.264, while NVDEC supports HEVC 4:4:4 8/10/12-bit and VP9 10/12-bit HDR streams.

VirtualLink provides a single USB-C connection for VR headset power, display, and data while supporting four HBR3 DisplayPort lanes and SuperSpeed USB 3. It is intended to simplify VR setups and enable VR on smaller devices. For SLI transfers, TU102 and TU104 use second-generation NVLink instead of MIO and PCIe interfaces. TU102 has two x8 links and TU104 has one, providing two-way but not three- or four-way SLI.

Turing enables real-time ray tracing through dedicated RT Cores in each streaming multiprocessor, working with NVIDIA RTX software, OptiX, Microsoft DXR, and the forthcoming Vulkan ray-tracing API. RT Cores accelerate bounding-volume hierarchy traversal and ray-triangle intersection tests, freeing other GPU resources for shading and computation. Turing supports hybrid rendering, combining rasterization with ray tracing for reflections, refractions, shadows, and related effects. The passage states that Turing ray tracing is approximately ten times faster than software-based ray tracing on Pascal.

The study developed an automated system for monitoring adherence to clinical practice guidelines in intensive care. It combines FHIR-encoded, computer-interpretable recommendations with patient data standardized in the OMOP Common Data Model. Six COVID-19 and ARDS-related recommendations were selected through expert review from 41 guidelines containing 1,597 recommendations. FHIR encoding was jointly developed and reviewed by intensive care physicians and medical computer scientists, while hospital-specific ETL pipelines mapped local clinical data to OMOP.

The system was deployed at five university hospitals with distinct information systems and data models. It evaluated 82,015 intensive care episodes from January 2020 through May 2023 by determining whether each recommendation applied to patients and whether recommended treatment was followed.

Validation at three hospitals compared system classifications with seven intensive care physicians, using two supervising physicians to establish ground truth for disagreements. The system achieved 97.0% accuracy versus 86.6% for human reviewers (McNemar’s test, χ²=149.93, p<0.001). It processed more than 2,000 patient days per second, whereas human review of 18,115 patient days required 150 hours. More than 80% of discrepancies were attributed to human error, while most system errors resulted from relevant information being stored in unstructured free text that was not transferred into OMOP.

Observed adherence generally ranged from 10% to 60%, varying by recommendation and hospital, with adherence increasing over time for some recommendations. Low or apparent non-adherence was associated with newly introduced guidance, incomplete documentation, strict interpretation, and imprecisely defined recommendations. Limitations included retrospective validation, reliance on potentially biased expert ground truth, assessment of only six recommendations, and dependence on data accessibility and quality. The findings support the system as a scalable and accurate approach to cross-institution guideline monitoring.

A 2018 *Journal of Climate* paper by Nicholas Lewis and Judith Curry estimates climate sensitivity from observed temperatures and forcing data through 2016, finding values substantially below most CMIP5 models and IPCC projections. Using globally complete data, the study derives median equilibrium climate sensitivity of 1.66°C and transient climate response of 1.33°C, compared with CMIP5 medians of 3.1°C and 1.9°C. The authors conclude that future warming is likely 30–45% lower than central simulation projections. Results are largely insensitive to the analysis period, and possible time-varying climate feedbacks do not materially affect median estimates. The paper also examines potential biases from aerosols, sea-surface temperature patterns, temperature estimation, and internal variability, finding them minor when globally complete temperature data are used.
