A Grand Canyon Institute report examines Arizona’s Empowerment Scholarship Account (ESA) voucher program, citing limited accountability and transparency for private entities receiving public subsidies. Arizona enacted targeted ESA vouchers in 2011 and became the first state to make them universal in 2022, after voters rejected a capped expansion in 2018. The state provides more than $1 billion annually for private education through ESA spending, tax credits and related subsidies.

ESA enrollment rose from 12,127 in FY2022 to 61,689 in FY2023 and 87,602 by the third quarter of FY2025. Of the FY2025 total, 64,133 participants were in the universal program and 15,207 were K–12 students with disabilities. Awards equal 90% of charter-school per-student funding; most are below $8,000, although awards for students with certain disabilities can exceed $30,000.

GCI estimates that no more than 40% of ESA students used allocations for private-school tuition in FY2023. Of the $173 million spent on private schools, $97 million went to religious schools and $75 million to schools serving special-needs students; evangelical Christian and Catholic schools received 86% of religious-school expenditures, while secular schools received less than 5%. Many families used funds for homeschooling or extracurricular activities, and substantial balances accumulated: about $175 million across 60,000 accounts at the end of FY2023 and an estimated $360 million by the end of FY2024. FY2024 awards totaled $717.6 million, with $533.2 million spent.

Early universal applicants disproportionately came from higher-income ZIP codes and were often already outside public schools: 45% came from the state’s wealthiest quarter, while 80% were not enrolled in public school. Income disparities narrowed as the program expanded, though they persisted through March 2025. GCI estimates that nearly three-quarters of current universal participants never attended district or charter schools, although most new FY2025 entrants reportedly came from those schools.

GCI concludes that universal ESA vouchers are a net cost to Arizona’s general fund—at least $330 million in FY2024 and about $350 million in FY2025—because most participants would not otherwise have attended district or charter schools. Transfers from charter schools produce modest savings, transfers from districts create costs, and vouchers for students who never attended public schools represent entirely new state spending.

NVIDIA’s Blackwell GPU architecture introduces Mega Geometry, which enables ray tracing of full-fidelity geometry in systems such as Unreal Engine 5 and Nanite without low-resolution proxies. Cluster-level acceleration structures use batches of up to 256 triangles, reducing subsequent BVH construction work by roughly two orders of magnitude and enabling GPU-driven LOD management with minimal CPU overhead. Partitioned Top-Level Acceleration Structures update only changed scene partitions, supporting large numbers of static and dynamic objects. Mega Geometry is supported through DirectX 12, Vulkan, and OptiX 9.0 on RTX GPUs from Turing onward. Fourth-generation Blackwell RT Cores add geometry and BVH compression, up to twice the ray-triangle intersection rate of third-generation cores, and lower VRAM use for typical Nanite scenes.

Blackwell also introduces hardware ray-intersection support for Linear Swept Spheres, including direct spheres and variable-radius segments for strand-like geometry. Hair rendering with LSS is reported as about twice as fast as DOTS while using roughly one-fifth the VRAM. SER 2.0 has twice the reorder efficiency and greater precision, improving divergent ray-tracing and neural workloads without requiring changes to existing applications. The programmable AI Management Processor uses a dedicated RISC-V processor to schedule GPU contexts on the GPU, reducing CPU communication, latency, and bottlenecks while coordinating AI and graphics workloads.

Blackwell adds hardware H.264 and HEVC support for 4:2:2 chroma sampling, which retains more color detail than 4:2:0 while requiring less data than 4:4:4. Ninth-generation NVENC improves AV1 and HEVC quality, adds 4:2:2 encoding, and offers an AV1 Ultra High Quality mode; combined improvements can reach 15% BD-BR PSNR. The RTX 5090 supports three encoders and two decoders. Sixth-generation NVDEC provides 2× faster H.264 decoding. DisplayPort 2.1b supports up to 80 Gbps and, with UHBR 20 and DSC, 8K at 165 Hz or 4K at 480 Hz.

Blackwell’s Max-Q efficiency work adds advanced clock, unit, and voltage-rail gating, including full memory-clock-tree gating. Clocks can respond to workload changes 1,000 times faster than on previous architectures, while the deepest sleep state is entered 10 times faster than on Ada. In a small-language-model inference example, these changes produced power savings of up to 50%.

DLSS 4 introduces Multi Frame Generation, which can create up to three additional frames per traditionally rendered frame. Its AI model is 40% faster and uses 30% less VRAM than the previous generation, while enhanced Flip Metering moves pacing to the display engine. DLSS 4 also replaces convolutional models with transformer-based models that can ingest twice as many parameters. Transformer-based Super Resolution improves temporal stability, motion detail, and anti-aliasing; Ray Reconstruction improves ray-traced lighting and reduces denoiser artifacts; and DLAA provides AI-based anti-aliasing at native resolution.

Blackwell advances developer-created neural shaders through the Cooperative Vectors API for DirectX 12 and Vulkan and differentiable features in Slang. Potential applications include RTX Neural Materials, Neural Radiance Cache, RTX Skin, and RTX Neural Faces. Neural texture compression can reduce VRAM use by as much as seven-to-one versus block-compressed formats; one materials example falls from 1,110 MB to 333 MB. Neural Radiance Cache estimates indirect lighting beyond the initial path-traced bounce, while RTX Skin provides real-time ray-traced subsurface scattering. Neural Faces uses a TensorRT-optimized generative model and 3D pose data to create more natural real-time faces.

The passage reviews curriculum evaluation in physical education and emphasizes teachers’ roles in developing and implementing programs. It defines curriculum evaluation as a systematic process used to assess program effectiveness, identify problems, and guide revisions. Physical education programs aim to develop active, healthy lifestyles, movement skills, self-control, cooperation, and fair play. Previous research identified limited implementation and assessment practices, insufficient course hours, crowded classrooms, and inadequate materials and equipment.

This quantitative, survey-based study examined pre-service teachers’ views of the Physical Education and Sports Curriculum for grades 5–8, focusing on its achievements, content, teaching-learning processes, and assessment practices. The researcher-developed questionnaire was informed by interviews and literature, tested with 50 pre-service teachers, and reviewed by three doctoral-level experts. The sample comprised 100 students from four departments at Bayburt University’s Faculty of Sports Sciences, selected through cluster sampling.

Candidates generally viewed the achievements positively: 43% agreed they suited students’ levels, 64 selected the correct learning areas, and 70 found them understandable, although 37 were undecided about scientific accuracy. Eighty percent agreed that the content was meaningfully ordered, but many were undecided about its scientific accuracy, age suitability, and compatibility with programs in other countries. Fifty-six percent said activities enriched teaching, and 61% identified concrete materials, while 60 rejected the use of varied methods and techniques. Assessment findings were mixed: 34 candidates were undecided about varied evaluation methods, 43 agreed that different forms were used, and 55 rejected alternative measurement methods.

The researchers concluded that candidates’ views of the achievements were generally positive but that they lacked sufficient knowledge about program content and scientific accuracy. Recommendations included expanding research, organizing informational seminars or congresses, and adding curriculum review courses to teacher-training programs.

The application concerns methods for forming three-dimensional vertical NOR-type memory string arrays using damascene local vertical bit lines. A disclosed process forms multilayer stacks on global interconnect lines, creates trenches and sacrificial dielectric fillers, and uses a second patterned etch to form narrow word-line stacks. Two-step etching reduces the effective etch aspect ratio, avoiding ribboning, improving structural stability, and addressing mask-alignment variations.

Silicon nitride portions of the word-line strips are selectively removed, and metal is deposited to fill the resulting cavities. Elongated vias are then formed and lined with tunneling dielectric, charge-storage, blocking-dielectric, channel, optional liner, and sacrificial-dielectric layers. Repeating the via sequence forms adjacent semiconductor columns. Additional shafts receive source and drain semiconductor material, with global interconnect lines above the structure serving as bit lines. A staircase structure exposes successive word-line strips for conductive contacts to selection circuitry.

Alternative embodiments use dielectric pillars to support high-aspect-ratio word-line stacks or use stacked masks with different pitches to define the stacks.

The passage proposes Digital Ecosystems as artificial software systems that exploit properties of biological ecosystems—robustness, scalability, self-organization, self-management, and automated composition—to address complex, dynamic problems. Unlike natural ecosystems, they are engineered to serve specific human purposes. Existing uses of the term “digital ecosystem” often lack genuine ecological properties.

In these systems, fitness landscapes represent environmental constraints and the relative fitness of possible solutions. Unlike the typically fixed functions used in genetic algorithms, Digital Ecosystems require complex, dynamic fitness landscapes that reflect changing user needs. Designers must define these landscapes and evolve solution populations that are diverse, efficient, and capable of meeting varied requirements. Agents should reproduce, vary, interact, move, and die, although their encoding depends on the system’s purpose.

Spatial structure helps maintain diversity. Biological models show that local interactions can preserve species diversity and create persistent population patches, while habitat fragmentation can shift evolution between local and global search. Digital Ecosystems can reproduce some spatial dynamics through distributed locations, or habitats, connected by networks through which agents migrate.

Effective self-organization requires balancing internal ecosystem dynamics with user-defined fitness criteria. Excessive internal autonomy may produce agents that reproduce successfully but are useless in practice, whereas overly restrictive criteria can limit exploration, reduce diversity, and cause premature convergence in dynamic landscapes. A separate self-organizing mechanism is therefore needed to maintain diverse solution lineages.

Digital Ecosystems are presented as complex adaptive systems characterized by nonlinear, non-equilibrium, continually adapting behavior. This makes them difficult to predict and susceptible to sudden transitions or mass extinctions of useful solutions, although mechanisms such as negative feedback may mitigate these risks. Their nonlinear dynamics can also enable scalable organization, complex hierarchical solutions, and rapid adaptation. Designers must balance diversity against adaptive efficiency and stability against responsiveness.

The proposed architecture has two optimization levels. A decentralized peer-to-peer network supports distributed agents, while each habitat performs local evolutionary optimization to compose agents that satisfy locally relevant constraints. Agents contain executable and ontological components and collectively form a multi-agent system using evolutionary computing. Distributed evolutionary methods accelerate evaluation and help avoid premature convergence by maintaining diversity. Unlike conventional island models, which apply multiple populations to one fixed problem, the proposed system evaluates different requests on separate islands and shares solutions between populations addressing similar requests.

Habitat connections are reconfigurable and based on information or semantic proximity rather than geography. Bidirectional connections carry migration probabilities that are strengthened after successful exchanges and weakened after unsuccessful ones, allowing the network topology to adapt to observed agent movement and resemble the clustered, small-world structure of the user base. Users submit semantic descriptions of desired applications; fitness measures their distance from agents’ ontological descriptions. Local populations are seeded with available agents, prior solutions, and relevant solutions evolved elsewhere, then evolve agent sequences that migrate to other habitats where they can support further requests.

The simulation uses a business ecosystem of small and medium-sized enterprises with 100 users, randomly connected habitats, evolving service-agent populations, semantic business requests, and request-derived fitness functions. It assumes accurate requests, use of returned solutions, equal rates of users joining and leaving, five initially deployed agents per user, and deployment of another agent after every three requests.

The lecture examines fine tuning in a nonrelativistic two-nucleon effective field theory. Operators that appear irrelevant under naive dimensional power counting may need to be retained at leading order because the correct power counting differs; this fine tuning corresponds to expansion around an interacting rather than trivial fixed point.

After exchange particles are integrated out, the theory consists of contact interactions and derivatives of contact interactions. For elastic two-particle scattering, a single partial wave is described through the S-matrix, amplitude, and phase shift. The effective-range expansion,
\[
P\cot\delta_L=-\frac{1}{a_L}+\frac12 r_{L,0}P^2+\cdots,
\]
is derived directly from the effective theory without specifying a potential. The contact coefficients encode the potential and become the scattering length, effective range, and related parameters.

Fermionic antisymmetry links spin, isospin, and angular momentum, reducing the allowed partial waves. For nonrelativistic nucleons, the temporal kinetic term and the \(\nabla^2/(2M)\) term must be counted together, with \(E\sim P^2/(2M)\); retaining only the temporal term produces an ill-defined pinch singularity. With the proper kinetic terms, all loops are bubble diagrams. Their sum produces a geometric series and the effective-range expansion. The coefficients \(C_{2M}\) scale as \(1/M\), making tree and loop contributions comparable.

The nucleon scattering lengths are unexpectedly large: approximately 23 fm in the \(^{1}S_0\) channel and 5 fm in the \(^{3}S_1\) channel. Their inverse scales, about 8.30 and 36 MeV, are much smaller than the natural momentum scale set by the pion, while the effective ranges have natural sizes. Thus \(C_0\) is anomalously enhanced, making the naive power counting inappropriate and requiring the contact interaction to be kept to all orders in \(aP\).

Off-shell momentum subtraction tracks the power-law divergence by fixing the amplitude at imaginary momentum \(P=i\mu\). It produces a finite counterterm and a renormalization-group equation in which \(C_0\) becomes relevant when \(\mu\sim P\). Power-divergence subtraction provides a dimensional-regularization alternative by also subtracting poles at \(D=3\); it reproduces the same result. Renormalization-group functions then determine how the enhancement of \(C_0\) propagates to higher operators, such as \(C_2\) and \(C_4\).

The beta function identifies fixed points corresponding to zero and infinite scattering length, as well as a pole associated with a bound state, identified with the deuteron. The interacting fixed points exhibit conformal symmetry and an emergent combined spin-isospin \(SU(4)\) symmetry. Overall, the framework provides systematic power counting and predictive calculations for nuclear scattering, external currents, and precision deuteron physics.
Coral Davenport explains how OMB director Russell Vought plans to circumvent Congress’s budgetary powers to advance the Trump administration’s agenda.

The federal government shutdown began Wednesday after Congress failed to pass funding legislation. President Donald Trump said Democrats had given him an “unprecedented opportunity” to cut federal agencies and planned to meet OMB Director Russell Vought about potentially permanent cuts. His administration said it froze about $18 billion for New York City infrastructure projects and canceled $8 billion for climate projects in Democratic-leaning states, while preparing for mass federal layoffs that officials said could number in the thousands. Republicans sought a stopgap funding bill through late November, while Democrats demanded extended Affordable Care Act tax credits. With Senate votes delayed by Yom Kippur, the shutdown was expected to last until at least Friday.

The D.C. Circuit held that the Nuclear Regulatory Commission’s transfer of regulatory authority over certain nuclear materials to New Jersey was arbitrary and capricious. Under the Atomic Energy Act, the NRC may transfer authority only if New Jersey’s regulatory program is compatible with the NRC’s and adequate to protect public health and safety.

Shieldalloy Metallurgical Corporation sought NRC approval for a plan to decommission its Newfield, New Jersey facility, where radioactive slag and dust from manufacturing remained onsite. After years of review, the NRC transferred regulatory authority to New Jersey on September 30, 2009. Less than two weeks later, New Jersey rejected Shieldalloy’s pending revised decommissioning plan, potentially requiring shipment of the radioactive material to Utah.

Shieldalloy argued that the transfer failed the NRC’s transition criterion, which requires arrangements preventing interference with licensed activities or license-application processing. The court found the NRC’s responses inadequate: it did not explain how Shieldalloy’s decommissioning proceeding could continue without interruption or why partial retention of NRC jurisdiction was not an appropriate alternative. The NRC had also improperly dismissed Shieldalloy’s concerns without addressing its long cooperation with the NRC staff, New Jersey’s opposition to the pending plan, or the possibility of transferring a discrete category of material. Although the statutory question concerning partial transfers was unresolved, that uncertainty did not excuse the NRC’s inadequate explanation. The court also rejected reliance on counsel’s oral-argument interpretation because the NRC had not previously exercised interpretive discretion on the issue.

The court did not reach Shieldalloy’s other challenges concerning ALARA principles, restricted on-site disposal, radiation-dose standards, exemptions, and allegedly discriminatory administration. It granted Shieldalloy’s petition, vacated the transfer of authority, and remanded for proceedings consistent with its opinion.

The guide defines optional extensions to SEV and SEV Secure Nested Paging that support page migration through AMD’s Tiered Memory Page Migration (TMPM) engine. TMPM copies page contents and updates virtual-to-physical mappings, allowing frequently accessed data to move to faster memory tiers. HV/OS detects support through PM_Status[ENGINE_READY], and IOMMU enablement is required. TMPM can coordinate migration of pages undergoing concurrent DMA and acts as a trusted agent for SNP-protected guest pages.

Commands include PM_GET_CAPABILITIES, PM_PAGE_MOVE_IO, PM_PAGE_MOVE_GUEST, and PM_NOOP. Each migration command uses a 4KB-aligned parameter page containing 1–128 migration entries. Pages need not be adjacent, multiple guests may appear in one list, and entries and commands must have no order dependence. Command and per-entry statuses report overall and individual results; PM_SUCCESS means all pages migrated, PM_PARTIAL_SUCCESS requires checking each entry, and other command results indicate no migrations executed. A PM_RMP_NOTEXCLUSIVE entry may be retried after an RMP conflict is resolved.

PM_PAGE_MOVE_IO migrates pages that may be targeted by DMA. The source must be mapped through one IOMMU host page table entry, whose location is supplied in the command. Firmware validates addresses and mappings, invalidates and synchronizes TLBs, flushes DMA, copies the data while preserving encryption as needed, and programs the host page table entry for the destination. Software must prevent CPU access during migration, perform required ATS invalidations in applicable non-SNP systems, and avoid concurrent modifications to referenced host page table entries because TMPM may modify them non-atomically. Direct 2MB migration is unsupported; the source must be split into 4KB pages.

PM_PAGE_MOVE_GUEST migrates SNP guest pages. Source pages must be Guest-Valid or Guest-Invalid, and destination pages must be in the new Pre-Migration state. Following migration, destinations receive the original source state and sources return to Pre-Migration. Firmware validates the guest context page and obtains exclusive RMP access before invalidating the CPU TLB, copying data, and updating source and destination RMPs. Concurrent DMA is unsupported. A 2MB request must be aligned and backed by physically contiguous 4KB pages, or software must split it into 4KB pages.

Pre-Migration resembles Guest-Invalid but uses a platform-specific ASID value, ignores the GPA, and cannot be converted to Guest-Valid through PVALIDATE. Software must use RMPUpdate to return the page to Hypervisor state.

TMPM commands use a ring buffer separate from the SEV/SNP ring buffer. Software controls the write pointer, firmware controls the read pointer, and commands may execute in parallel without guaranteed ordering. The TOGGLE bit indicates command completion and when PM_Status is valid. Initialization checks ENGINE_READY, configures a 4KB-aligned ring of 1–255 contiguous pages and its behavior, sets the write pointer, connects interrupts, and waits for DRIVER_INIT_COMPLETE. A 4KB ring-buffer page can hold 256 16-byte commands. Pause and shutdown procedures allow in-flight commands to finish before stopping or reconfiguring processing. Completion, error, empty-queue, threshold, and ring-buffer memory or pointer errors share an x86 interrupt signal and are reported through status registers.

Source and destination system physical addresses must normally be 4KB aligned; host page table entry addresses require 8-byte alignment, while 2MB addresses require 2MB alignment. Addresses are 46 or 52 bits depending on system encryption, and software must encode encryption information and the C-bit appropriately. Excluded migration targets include IOMMU structures accessed by SPA, vIOMMU page tables and pinned storage, and the TMPM ring buffer and argument pages.

Firmware reload requires pausing operations, allowing in-flight work to finish, tearing down the ring buffer, and issuing a reload through the BIOS-to-PSP mailbox protocol. Disabling IOMMU PAGEMIGRATION_EN bits during reload is recommended. Reload firmware must be the same or a newer version, and software must verify ENGINE_READY afterward. PM_GET_CAPABILITIES identifies the applicable execution path; EPYC Family 19h uses FW_VER_Major value 71.

Testing described in the guide found better bandwidth with batches of at least 16 pages and maximum performance at 128 pages. Keeping the queue populated, pacing interrupts, and using low-water interrupts can improve throughput. Command-format and migration-entry errors are reported in command and entry statuses, ring-buffer errors in PM_Status, and hardware failures in command status and/or through Machine Check Architecture. On a detected timeout, client software should log an MCA, perform applicable error handling, and decide whether to save state, terminate workloads, stop issuing commands, or reboot.

European shares headed for their biggest weekly loss since November 2016, with the STOXX 600 down about 1.8% and on track for a fifth consecutive session of declines. Rising bond yields and a stronger euro pressured markets, while Germany’s DAX fell more than 5% in eight sessions after reaching a record high.

Bank earnings weighed on sentiment: Deutsche Bank reported a €497 million 2017 loss, while Jefferies described fourth-quarter results from Caixabank and Sabadell as disappointing. Bank of America Merrill Lynch issued a cautious near-term “Sell” signal but remained constructive longer term, citing expected global growth of at least 4% and double-digit earnings growth. Strategists favored European dividend stocks and pharmaceuticals.

Higher yields increased funding and opportunity costs for leveraged investors, raising unwind risk. Investors also awaited U.S. payroll data and assessed mixed technology earnings, including strong results from Amazon and Facebook, disappointing Alphabet results, and Apple’s weak iPhone guidance. European fourth-quarter STOXX 600 earnings were expected to rise 11.9% year on year.

The paper experimentally evaluates whether large language models can autoformalize hybrid physics problems into differential game logic (dGL), preserving continuous dynamics and discrete transitions. Twenty benchmarks were derived from challenging undergraduate kinematics problems. The pipeline prompts models to propose and revise dGL models, applies parser feedback for up to three syntax repairs, and then checks semantic correctness through symbolic execution, comparison with an expected solution, and a requirement that enough variables change to prevent stasis.

Evaluations of GPT-4o, GPT-4.1, and OpenAI o3 used zero-shot and few-shot prompting, with five independent attempts per benchmark. Few-shot prompting substantially improved every model. With examples, o3 achieved a 70% best-of-five success rate, compared with 45% for GPT-4.1 and 20% for GPT-4o; GPT-4o failed every benchmark without examples. A running example showed that successful formalization requires precise auxiliary variables, transition conditions, coordinate choices, physical assumptions, and exclusion of degenerate cases. The checker also exposed subtle modeling errors and could reject correct models that omitted assumptions made by textbook solutions.

Six problems remained unsolved. Their difficulties fell into three groups: optimization with adversarial dynamics, non-polynomial continuous dynamics, and complicated multi-phase dynamics. The best models sometimes produced potentially correct but overly complex models that the symbolic checker could not verify. Proposed improvements include extending solvers, generating continuous invariants, and guiding models toward friendlier representations such as polar coordinates and auxiliary variables. The results suggest that LLM-based autoformalization of hybrid systems is promising, while future work includes applying it at runtime to unfamiliar situations represented by vision and sensor data.

Mark Valladares, the Monday editor of Liberal Democrat Voice, introduces the edition from snow-affected Creeting St Peter, Suffolk, and criticizes ministers’ efforts to undermine Theresa May’s EU deal, citing Simon Coveney’s warning that Article 46 commitments must be upheld. He previews House of Lords business, particularly Liberal Democrat contributions: Paul Walter reports on an award scheme for young by-election activists and the Samaritans’ support for lonely people. A “goodbye” music interlude and reader contributions are also featured.

Depression and anxiety are highly prevalent and difficult to distinguish clinically because of overlapping symptoms and comorbidity. While speech contains potential digital biomarkers, existing research lacks objective, interpretable methods and an effective bridge between patients’ informal descriptions and clinical terminology. The study collected over 15,000 minutes of interviews from 1,160 Mandarin-speaking outpatients at Shanghai Mental Health Center, covering 25 diagnoses. After preprocessing, anonymization, transcription, and correction, a pretrained LLM identified clinical entities and was fine-tuned using psychiatrist annotations. Linguistic and acoustic features were combined in an ensemble machine-learning pipeline to predict diagnostic groups and major symptoms with moderately high accuracy. Analysis of salient patterns improved clinical interpretability, and the results indicate that LLM-derived cues combined with behavioral markers may help differentiate diagnostic groups and identify symptom disclosure.
Theo Walcott scored in the 51st minute, the only goal of Everton’s 1-0 Premier League win over Newcastle at Goodison Park. Everton next faces Huddersfield, while Newcastle hosts West Bromwich Albion.

Cover Zero uses all-out pressure, blitzing every player except those responsible for man coverage against offensive skill players. It pressures quarterbacks to make quick decisions but leaves coverage defenders isolated and often opens the middle of the field. Offenses can exploit it with quick-hitting man beaters, perimeter weapons, slants, shallow crossing routes, and pick plays. The article presents five examples: Ole Miss’s mirrored double slants; Oregon’s full-slide protection play that frees a running back for a touchdown; Michigan’s trips bunch jerk route that creates natural rubs and an open receiver; Wake Forest’s slant-rub concept against goal-line man coverage; and a Jerry Rice motion slant-flat that loses a defender before the snap and creates a touchdown opportunity for a tight end.

Former Aberdeen player Neale “Tattie” Cooper, 54, died in hospital after falling down stairs and entering intensive care. A senior club figure suggested his funeral be held at Pittodrie, while the club said it would follow his family’s wishes. Tributes honoured Cooper’s role in Aberdeen’s 1983 European Cup Winners’ Cup triumph and his recent reunion with teammates.

FlowMotion ONE is a wearable smartphone stabilizer with a 3-in-1 design that works with camera mounts, a joystick handle or an extension pole. Its sensors and precision motors reduce shake and vibration to produce smooth, cinematic footage, and the device weighs less than a pound. The Kickstarter campaign surpassed its $30,000 goal within an hour, ultimately attracting more than 2,700 backers and over $600,000. Founded in 2015 by Lars Flesland, Julie Bauge, Eirik Dyrseth and Didrik Dimmen, the 10-person FlowMotion team develops video-stabilizing hardware and software and has received multiple international awards.

This cross-sectional study assessed cervical cancer and cervical screening awareness among women aged 15–49 in Benin and Cameroon using nationally representative 2017–2018 Demographic and Health Survey data. It included 21,322 women, of whom 7,010 aware of cervical cancer were also asked about screening. Weighted descriptive statistics, chi-square tests, and survey-adjusted logistic regression were conducted separately by country.

Cervical cancer awareness was 9.5% in Benin and 46.1% in Cameroon. Among women aware of cervical cancer, 51.4% in Benin and 59.7% in Cameroon were aware of cervical screening. In both countries, cervical cancer awareness was significantly associated with older age, higher education, and frequent internet use; greater wealth was also associated with awareness in Cameroon. Screening awareness was highest among women aged 25–34 in Benin and those aged 45 or older in Cameroon. Higher education was strongly associated with awareness of both cervical cancer and screening in both countries, while radio and internet use were associated with screening awareness.

The authors recommended strengthening awareness programs through stakeholder engagement, public education, radio and internet use, implementation of national cervical cancer control and screening strategies, and age-appropriate information for younger women. They also called for efforts to reduce awareness inequalities related to education and wealth in Cameroon. Limitations include the cross-sectional design, small screening-questions subsample, self-reported data, potential sampling and recall bias, and unmeasured confounding.

SARS-CoV-2 is mainly transmitted through respiratory droplets but is also shed in feces, enabling wastewater surveillance through detection of viral RNA. Wastewater testing generally requires concentrating 50–250 mL samples, but existing membrane filtration, polyethylene glycol precipitation, skim milk, ultracentrifugation, and ultrafiltration approaches may require centrifuges unavailable to some laboratories.

Nanotrap particles are porous hydrogel particles that capture, separate, and protect analytes. They can preserve viruses and nucleic acids at ambient and elevated temperatures for up to three days, capture multiple pathogens, and have been used to concentrate SARS-CoV-2, influenza, and respiratory syncytial virus in wastewater.

The study uses grab, composite, and passive sampling methods, including Moore swabs deployed in wastewater for 24 hours. It evaluates how pH, temperature, incubation time, sample volume, RNA extraction, and one-step Nanotrap versus two-step skim milk–Nanotrap concentration affect SARS-CoV-2 RNA detection. It also compares automated high-throughput processing with manual 10-mL Nanotrap methods and benchmarks them against 150-mL membrane filtration and 250-mL skim milk methods. Wastewater was collected weekly from Atlanta community manholes and treatment-plant influent lines from June through August 2021; 500-mL grab samples were used for influent lines. Before membrane filtration, samples were centrifuged at 5,000 rpm for five minutes at 4°C to remove solids.

Veterinarians in Oklahoma removed 21 pacifiers from a dog named Dovey’s stomach after an X-ray estimated only seven to nine. The dog had slowed eating and vomited small amounts of phlegm before coughing up a pacifier. Dovey recovered and went home, while the veterinarian warned that dogs may eat anything at any age.

Collected reports from December 11–12, 2000 covered utility stocks, Enron’s Dabhol power project, energy-price volatility, retail energy markets and online trading.

Electric utility stocks had gained 36% year to date before flattening as a technology-stock rebound threatened to draw investment away. Tight generating capacity remained supportive, but analysts expected the sector’s roughly 20% average profit growth to be difficult to repeat. Enron and Dynegy were among the Evergreen Utility Fund’s largest holdings; Calpine was an analyst’s top pick, while AEP, Xcel Energy and Progress Energy were also recommended.

Enron’s 65%-owned Dabhol Power Company operated the first phase of a 2,184-MW project in Maharashtra. Four lenders—ICICI, Canara Bank, State Bank of India and Industrial Finance Corporation of India—agreed to reduce loan rates by 450 basis points to 16.5%, potentially lowering power tariffs. The $1.9 billion project was 70% debt-financed, and Enron said switching from naphtha to cheaper natural gas would reduce tariffs in 2001. A Times of India editorial characterized the agreement as excessive and harmful to consumers, while retired judge Hosbet Suresh said it could be nullified on public-interest grounds and called its fixed charges exploitative.

Natural gas reached $9.413 per million British thermal units on NYMEX. Terra Industries and Mississippi Chemical sold gas rather than use it to manufacture products, while Seneca Resources sold gas earmarked for enhanced oil recovery. Kaiser Aluminum planned to sell electricity contracted for closed smelters. TXU’s Jeff Shorter said firms without effective energy-risk programs would face financial strain; Enron spokesman Mark Palmer said the volatility created opportunities for Enron.

Activate, a majority-owned CMGI digital-media company, reported 15-to-30-fold growth across major metrics, more than 100 million streams, and over 40,000 webcasts in 2000. Its network coordination and cross-connection work included Enron and other content-distribution networks.

Green Mountain Energy applied to become Texas’s first applicant for a retail electric license focused on renewable power. Other applicants included Enron units, New Power—formed by Enron, IBM and AOL—and Sempra Energy Solutions. Separately, New Power was certified as a Georgia retail natural-gas marketer and planned to begin serving customers in 2001.

Online energy trading was led by EnronOnline, which reportedly averaged $10.5 billion in daily volume and 35,000 transactions across more than 30 commodities. Dynegydirect recorded more than $1.5 billion in its first month, while IntercontinentalExchange also showed substantial trading. Analysts expected online energy trading to expand but anticipated consolidation among platforms.

Researchers analyzed Wisconsin Poison Center records from January 2010 through September 2022 to characterize kratom-associated exposures. The center received 59 exposure calls, increasing from one in 2011 to 15 in 2020. Most exposed individuals were male (62.7%), and the mean age among 52 with available age data was 35.3 years. Three exposures involved infants under age two, all unintentional; one infant was admitted to pediatric intensive care for observation.

Kratom was the only reported substance in 55.9% of calls. Common co-ingested substances included alcohol and benzodiazepines. Polysubstance exposure was not significantly associated with medical outcome or level of care, though analyses were limited by small numbers. Agitation, tachycardia, confusion, and central nervous system depression were the most frequently reported findings. Of 50 cases with known outcomes, 19 had moderate or major effects. Seven patients required critical care; five had marked agitation requiring sedation, and three required mechanical ventilation. One patient died from sepsis complications, with postmortem toxicology identifying kratom as contributory.

The authors noted that passive surveillance likely undercounts adverse events, routine toxicology screens often do not test for mitragynine, and unregulated products have uncertain potency and composition. They recommended increased clinician awareness, better documentation of kratom exposure, and education about possible interactions with other substances, safe storage around children, and_nbsp;kratom’s stimulant-like effects at lower doses and sedative effects at higher doses.

A 48-week trial randomized 1,112 apixaban-treated NVAF patients to standard-care information or education; at week 24, education recipients rerandomized to continue or stop. EMD classified 24-hour windows: one missed dose counted as adherence, two consecutive misses as nonadherence. Withheld periods were excluded; discontinuation over 30 days was permanent.

Ben Baby’s mailbag discusses whether Florida is a must-win for Texas A&M coach Kevin Sumlin after a potential loss to Alabama. He says it is not strictly necessary, though poor results would narrow A&M’s margin for error in pursuing an 8-4 season. A&M had not announced throwback uniforms, but the field will honor Gene Stallings and the 1967 team that defeated Alabama. Other topics include fall wedding conflicts with games, Aggie DJ song requests, ways to attract UNT students and alumni against UTSA using former player Steve Austin, the “Go Mean Green” nickname, support for Arsenal manager Arsene Wenger, and Chipotle as the preferred burrito restaurant.

Investing.com’s page mixes market commentary, headlines, promotions, and trading disclosures. Technical analysis says momentum remains intact, but early warnings and short-term pressures are emerging as the recovery from April’s low continues and seasonal headwinds weigh. The S&P 500 rose 2.2% in July and 7.8% year to date, or 8.6% in total return, before slipping 1.6% on August 1. July was risk-on, with stocks up and bonds down, while volatility and credit spreads showed seasonal increases. Investors are increasingly favoring tech stocks, and U.S. electricity demand reached a record. Other headlines cover mixed Chinese PMIs, Australian markets before an RBA decision, gold above $3,800 amid shutdown and rate-cut concerns, and the dollar targeting 97.5 support. The page warns that leveraged trading can lose all invested funds and that website data may not be real-time or accurate.

A Swiss watchdog denied that the Office of the Attorney General aided an alleged FIS spy or exposed him through prosecution files. The former policeman, arrested in Germany, is suspected of trading stolen bank data and possibly spying on German tax investigators. His FIS mandate remains unclear. The government confirmed that FIS helped in the data case. German outrage prompted calls for a Swiss parliamentary inquiry.

Dustin Brown and Anze Kopitar credited a veteran, close-knit group with the trust and chemistry needed to handle difficult situations. Brown said the team’s long-standing core provides confidence under pressure, while a lead against Chicago offers emotional and mental breathing room. He praised the group’s resilience after a slow, sloppy start and noted that players reset after each playoff round before refocusing on the next game. Brown also described Doughty’s development into a stronger leader both on and off the ice. He argued that the team’s style and execution make it particularly effective in the playoffs, even when it has fewer regular-season points than competitors. Kopitar said the room’s character, leadership, and welcoming atmosphere helped Gabby adjust quickly. Brown added that years of continuity, voluntary workouts, and an inclusive, clique-free environment have helped the core remain cohesive and integrate new teammates.
Memphis police say 2-year-old Laylah Washington died after being shot in the head while riding in her mother’s car. No arrests have been made; police are seeking a black Chevrolet Impala and tips.

HMP Northward, which houses more than 220 inmates despite a capacity of 212, is transferring selected, risk-assessed low-risk inmates to a cordoned-off section of the Immigration Detention Centre at Fairbanks. The move aims to free about 22 spaces, ease security concerns and rehabilitation delays, and continue while authorities pursue a permanent solution. Officials say normal operations will continue and migrant detainees’ privacy and safety will be protected, amid a hunger strike by nine asylum seekers.

The application describes wireless-communication methods and apparatuses for managing data duplication in radio bearers, where PDCP data is transmitted through one RLC entity and duplicated through another on separate paths. A terminal may report the pending data volume for only one path, selected by network instruction, path priority, or data volume, reducing signaling overhead. Reports may be sent in the selected path’s cell or cell group, or through another available resource.

The radio access network controls activation and deactivation of duplication for uplink and downlink bearers, potentially based on channel quality, cell load, or high-priority data. Indication messages may identify the affected bearer, paths, activation state, and effective time. When duplication is active, the terminal may report the volume on one or both paths, duplicate PDCP or RLC data, and report differences or starting sequence numbers for duplicated data. When duplication is deactivated, unnecessary duplicate data may be discarded while non-duplicated data can still be transmitted, and radio-link failure handling may be modified to avoid interruption delays.

The disclosure also covers carrier aggregation, dual-connectivity, and CU/DU network implementations, along with terminal-device, chip, processor, transmitter, receiver, and computer-storage-medium embodiments.

Microsoft Corporation’s Form 10-Q for the quarter ended September 30, 2020 reported unaudited consolidated financial results under U.S. GAAP. Revenue for the first quarter of fiscal 2021 was $37.154 billion, up 12% from $33.055 billion a year earlier. Product revenue was $15.803 billion and service and other revenue was $21.351 billion. Gross margin rose 15% to $26.152 billion, operating income increased 25% to $15.876 billion, net income increased 30% to $13.893 billion, and diluted EPS rose from $1.38 to $1.82.

Cash from operations was $19.335 billion. At September 30, 2020, Microsoft held $17.205 billion in cash and cash equivalents and $120.772 billion in short-term investments. Total assets were $301.001 billion, total liabilities were $177.609 billion, and stockholders’ equity was $123.392 billion. During the quarter, Microsoft spent $6.743 billion on share repurchases, paid $3.856 billion in dividends, and added $4.907 billion to property and equipment.

Segment results were:

- Productivity and Business Processes: revenue of $12.319 billion, up 11%, and operating income of $5.706 billion, up 19%.
- Intelligent Cloud: revenue of $12.986 billion, up 20%, and operating income of $5.422 billion, up 39%.
- More Personal Computing: revenue of $11.849 billion, up 6%, and operating income of $4.748 billion, up 18%.

Commercial cloud revenue increased 31% to $15.2 billion, with commercial cloud gross margin rising five percentage points to 71%. Azure revenue grew 48%, Office 365 Commercial revenue 21%, Dynamics 365 revenue 38%, LinkedIn revenue 16%, Xbox content and services revenue 30%, and Surface revenue 37%. Windows OEM revenue declined 5%, while search advertising revenue excluding traffic acquisition costs fell 10%.

Microsoft increased the estimated useful lives of server equipment from three to four years and network equipment from two to four years. For the quarter, this increased operating income by $927 million, net income by $763 million, and EPS by $0.10; fiscal 2021 operating income was estimated to increase by $2.7 billion. The expected-credit-loss standard was adopted on July 1, 2020 without material impact, while a new income-tax standard is scheduled for July 1, 2021 and is being evaluated.

On September 19, Microsoft agreed to acquire ZeniMax Media Inc., the parent of Bethesda Softworks, for $7.5 billion in cash, with closing expected in the second half of fiscal 2021 subject to conditions and regulatory review. Total debt was $63.552 billion, with an estimated fair value of $77.7 billion. Unearned revenue was $36.305 billion, and remaining performance obligations totaled $111 billion, including $107 billion from commercial revenue.

COVID-19 increased demand for cloud, Surface, and gaming while reducing search advertising and transactional licensing activity. Microsoft also disclosed continuing IRS transfer-pricing audits, approved Canadian antitrust class-action settlements, and other legal matters. Deloitte’s review found no material modifications needed to the interim financial information.

Environment Canada issued a special weather statement for Edmonton and surrounding areas because Wednesday afternoon conditions favoured isolated funnel clouds. Jesse Beyer said there was a slim chance of a weak landspout tornado touching down, potentially producing winds near 100 km/h and some damage. People were advised to remain alert and take shelter if funnel clouds developed nearby.

Britain’s FTSE 100 fell 0.2% as disappointing BT and AstraZeneca results outweighed gains in miners and oil stocks, heading for its worst week since August 2017. BT dropped over 5% to a five-year low on weak growth and pension concerns, while AstraZeneca fell 1.7% on a disappointing profit outlook. Capita rose over 5% after a Morgan Stanley upgrade.

This patent application is a continuation of U.S. patent application Ser. No. 17/158,220 (filed Jan. 26, 2021), which continues Ser. No. 16/283,679 (filed Feb. 22, 2019, now U.S. Pat. No. 10,936,643), both incorporated by reference in their entirety.

**Background.** Modern data centers comprise thousands of hosts serving remote clients, and their components generate large volumes of machine-generated, largely unstructured data that is difficult to index and search. The drawings include block diagrams of networked, cloud-based, and externally-searching data intake and query systems; flowcharts of indexer processing and pipelined query languages; inverted index and time-series data structures; and interfaces for search screens, report generation, key indicators, incident review dashboards, monitoring trees, and level-1/level-2 inferred task data.

**General overview.** The disclosure describes an event-based data intake and query system such as the SPLUNK® ENTERPRISE system (Splunk Inc., San Francisco, Calif.). Machine data — data produced by machines reflecting IT environment activity — includes system logs, network packet data, sensor data, application data, error logs, stack traces, and performance data. Because pre-processing tools typically extract pre-specified items and discard the remainder, and because storage is increasingly cheap, minimally processed machine data is retained and analyzed at search time, allowing analysts to search all machine data rather than a fixed field set, though varied types and formats from thousands of components and millions of mobile devices pose challenges. Machine data is collected and stored as events, each a portion of machine data tied to a timestamp derived from the data or interpolated from temporally proximate events. Sources include web/application servers, databases, firewalls, routers, operating systems, software applications, mobile devices, sensors, and IoT devices. A flexible, "late-binding schema" is applied on the fly (at search, index, or ingestion time) rather than fixed at ingestion; extraction rules (e.g., regex) define fields by deriving semantically related values from each event, and may be automatically generated or user-defined and refined over time. Events are field-searchable via configuration files associating field names, extraction rules, and event sets; common field names allow disparate sources to share a "common information model" (CIM).

**Operating environment.** The system comprises client devices, host devices running host applications (network devices, web/application/database servers), and client applications (browsers, mobile apps, background processes, plug-ins/extensions) that may embed a monitoring component triggered by "monitor triggers" and SDK-provided code. The monitoring component gathers network performance data (URL, connection type, start/end time, HTTP status code, request/response lengths and headers, connection status), device performance data (signal strength, carrier, memory performance, geolocation, orientation), and device profile data (type, manufacturer/model, installed software versions), storing them as field-value pairs such as "networkLatency" and "state."

**Data server system and cloud.** Forwarders receive data from input sources and route it to indexers, which process and store it in data stores; forwarders may remove extraneous data, detect timestamps, parse, index, route, generate timestamps, and perform indexer functions. The system may run on-premises for greater user control, or be provided as a cloud-based subscription service with per-subscriber accounts and web-portal configuration, including hybrid arrangements.

**External data.** The search head receives requests (web, command line, SDK); for local indexes it queries indexers, and for externally stored "virtual indices" (e.g., Hadoop, Amazon S3/EMR, HCFS, RDBMS) it spawns External Result Provider processes that translate native query language (e.g., SPL) into the external format. These processes may operate in streaming mode (low latency, lower bandwidth), reporting mode (higher latency, higher bandwidth, performing event breaking, timestamping, filtering, statistics), or both concurrently, with the search head switching results as reporting bandwidth catches up.

**Ingestion, parsing, indexing.** A forwarder receives a raw stream, segments it into blocks, annotates each with host, source, source type, and encoding metadata, and forwards it. An indexer determines or infers the source type, applies source type definitions (regex or delimiter rules) to delimit events, determines timestamps, attaches metadata fields, and may apply configured transformations (removal, masking). Events retaining raw machine data may be stored compressed or encrypted in a "raw record data store" or flat files with time-series index (TSIDX) files. The indexer optionally builds a keyword index and field-value pair entries, auto-generating fields such as "dest" from "dest=10.0.1.2", and stores events in time-range buckets — hot and warm buckets in faster home storage, cold buckets in slower storage, plus quarantine buckets for questionable timestamps and frozen buckets for archived data — with replication supporting availability. Data stores hold per-index/partition directories of inverted indexes containing token entries, field-value pair entries (default, automatic, or user-specified), and event reference arrays giving location and timestamp data. Using filter criteria (partition, host, source, sourcetype, time range, field, keyword), the indexer identifies relevant inverted indexes, consults extraction rules when a field lacks a field-value pair entry, and groups matching events by categorization criteria (e.g., partition, source, sourcetype, host), counting events per group and reporting the groupings to the search head for aggregation and display.

The court granted summary judgment for the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill and the individual defendants in Melissa Jennings’s action arising from her 1996–1998 membership on UNC’s women’s soccer team. Jennings alleged that head coach Anson Dorrance and assistant coach William Palladino made sexually explicit and degrading comments, discussed players’ sexual activity, and made two inquiries into Jennings’s personal life. Jennings initially reported the sexual comments to Assistant to the Chancellor Susan Ehringhaus; later complaints from Jennings’s father and another player’s parents led to an investigation, an apology from Dorrance, and an instruction that he refrain from discussing sexual matters with players.

The court found the alleged conduct was neither severe, pervasive, nor objectively offensive enough to support hostile-environment harassment claims under Title IX or 42 U.S.C. § 1983. The conduct occurred in an informal team setting, did not physically threaten Jennings, and did not prevent her from participating in soccer or academics. Jennings’s own testimony indicated that her academic and physical performance improved during the relevant period. Her constitutional and common-law privacy claims also failed because she was not forced to disclose personal information, was not impeded in procreative decisions, was not dismissed for refusing to answer, and experienced no physical or sensory intrusion. Supervisory-liability claims failed because no underlying constitutional violation occurred.

The court denied Jennings’s motion to strike defendants’ amended answer and seek default judgment because Dorrance’s inability to recall conversations did not establish bad faith or false pleading. It also denied her motion to strike Dorrance’s exhibits because they were authenticated and qualified for the regularly-conducted-records hearsay exception. The motion to submit evidence under seal was also denied.

Treasury minister Mel Stride pledged that British fish fingers would be “safe in the hands of this Government” during Brexit talks. Labour’s Mel Onn said continued customs arrangements were essential to prevent delays and protect Grimsby’s processing sector and 5,000 jobs.

This qualitative study examines the benefits, challenges, technologies, management strategies, and student attitudes associated with integrating information technology into Indonesian language education. Using descriptive and comparative analysis, literature review, observation, and framework development, it reviewed 1,010 Scopus manuscripts, of which 151 (15.1%) were considered strongly relevant; multiple researchers conducted searches to support triangulation.

Key challenges include insufficient teacher training, difficulty maintaining student engagement and interaction, limited resources, remote assessment difficulties, unequal digital access, weak self-regulation and motivation, and reduced social interaction. Reported responses included professional development, gamification, AI-assisted assessment, peer study groups, virtual extracurricular activities, immersive VR, government initiatives, and community support. Adaptability also varied with infrastructure, available technologies, cultural expectations, and collaboration among governments, educators, families, and businesses.

Technologies discussed include augmented and virtual reality, IoT, AI, learning management systems, gamification, 3D printing, blockchain, cloud computing, robotics, and big data. Particular attention is given to Automatic Speech Recognition, which provides real-time pronunciation feedback and supports vocabulary practice, and to task- and game-based learning, which provides interactive, context-rich opportunities for repeated language use.

Recommended IT management strategies include digital platforms, teacher development, language-support tools, international exchanges, cloud infrastructure, mobile learning, data-driven decisions, and inclusive policies. Students generally view technology positively, but curricula should address digital literacy, resistance, unreliable tools, unequal access, teacher support, and collaborative learning. The study concludes that IT can improve language education when implementation reflects teaching practices, student needs, and equitable access.

California and U.S. federal law govern, without conflicts rules; the U.N. sales convention is excluded. Santa Clara County courts have exclusive jurisdiction. Exports must be lawful; amendments and waivers need both parties’ authorized written signatures. Invalid provisions do not void the remaining agreement.

A federal judge in Illinois dismissed a lawsuit accusing the College Board and 40 selective private colleges of conspiring to inflate tuition. A Boston University student and Cornell University alumnus claimed that requiring both parents’ financial information regardless of custody raised tuition by an average of $6,200. Judge Sara Ellis found no plausible allegation of collusion.

At a human-trafficking training session in Oshakati, Prosecutor-General Martha Imalwa described trafficking as the world’s third-largest international crime after drugs and arms, generating $32 billion annually. She cited estimates of 20–30 million people in slavery and 600,000–800,000 international trafficking victims yearly, mostly women and some children. Namibia faces incidents involving unaccompanied Angolan children working below legal wages. UNODC-assisted training targets investigators, prosecutors, and victim-assistance personnel. Police recorded 25 cases from 2010–2017: 14 under investigation, six awaiting trial, three declined, one conviction, and one acquittal.

A medRxiv preprint reports a randomized, single-blind, placebo-controlled trial of intranasal SA58, a broad-spectrum anti-SARS-CoV-2 monoclonal antibody, as post-exposure prophylaxis in healthy adult workers at 21 Beijing construction sites who had contact with an infected person within 72 hours. Of 1,634 randomized participants, 1,222 entered the full analysis set and 1,123 baseline RT-PCR-negative participants contributed to efficacy analysis; sequenced infections were all Omicron BF.7.

SA58 reduced laboratory-confirmed symptomatic COVID-19 from 14/299 placebo recipients to 7/824 SA58 recipients, with estimated efficacy of 80.82% (95% CI 52.41%–92.27%). Efficacy against SARS-CoV-2 infection was 61.83% (95% CI 37.50%–76.69%). No severe COVID-19 or deaths occurred. Adverse events were all grade 1; no serious or special-interest events were reported, and adverse-event frequencies did not differ significantly between groups.

The findings indicate that intranasal SA58 was effective and well tolerated in this population. However, the study ended early, had limited follow-up and a small sample of mostly healthy workers, and concurrent isolation measures may have reduced transmission. Larger studies with longer monitoring and evaluation in high-risk populations and people already infected were recommended.

The passage describes an automated airway-management system for assisting clinicians during endotracheal intubation and rapid sequence intubation (RSI). Sensors measure gas, physiological, and positioning parameters—including oxygen, carbon dioxide, airflow, oxygen saturation, transthoracic impedance, acoustics, ECG, and patient motion. A processor uses changes in these parameters to identify procedure steps and provide context-sensitive visual, audible, or haptic guidance, including timers for preoxygenation and tube placement.

The system also verifies initial and continued proper placement of the endotracheal tube by correlating detected airway airflow with physiological evidence that ventilation reached the lungs. Verification may use ETCO2, impedance, or acoustic measurements compared with initial or dynamically updated baselines. The system can display relevant clinical data, prioritize corrective actions, trigger alarms for hypoxemia or improper placement, calculate drug dosages, record event markers, and generate quality-assurance reports. Medical monitors, defibrillators, portable computers, wrist-worn devices, and other displays may communicate with the system.

California Gov. Gavin Newsom signed SB 53, requiring major AI companies to disclose protocols for mitigating advanced-model risks, report serious safety incidents, and protect employees who raise safety concerns. The law also authorizes CalCompute, a government consortium intended to support safe, ethical and sustainable AI research, and includes civil penalties for noncompliance. Authored by Sen. Scott Wiener, the legislation emphasizes transparency rather than liability and follows Newsom’s veto of Wiener’s earlier SB 1047.

Supporters, including Anthropic, OpenAI, Meta and the Secure AI Project, called the law a balanced approach that promotes accountability without overburdening smaller companies. Critics warned that compliance costs and state-by-state rules could hinder startups and entrench large AI firms. Policy experts also called for stronger reporting standards, minimum risk thresholds and robust third-party evaluations, while noting that existing penalties are relatively weak. Because 32 of the world’s top 50 AI companies are based in California, the law could influence AI oversight globally.

Kevin Love reached his fourth straight NBA Finals with Cleveland after a turbulent season shaped by injuries, criticism and trade rumors. Since joining the Cavaliers in 2014 alongside LeBron James and Kyrie Irving, Love said he was often scapegoated despite consistent production. He publicly disclosed his longstanding anxiety and panic attacks, including during a January team meeting when teammates questioned his absence from a game and practice. His essay in The Player’s Tribune prompted thousands of supportive messages, fostered greater empathy and helped him connect with others; he also received counseling and described basketball as an escape from his anxiety.

Love had an uneven postseason, scoring seven points in the playoff opener before rebounding with 31 in Game 2. He sustained a concussion during Game 6 of the Eastern Conference finals and remained in the league’s protocol, leaving his Finals availability uncertain. Jeff Green replaced him and helped Cleveland win Game 7 in Boston. Love called his time in Cleveland worthwhile and said the city had already achieved an important milestone, with the team’s banner hanging in the arena.

Tropical Storm Nate formed off Nicaragua on Thursday, Oct. 5, 2017, killing at least 17 people in Central America, and moved north toward the U.S. Gulf Coast. Forecasters expected it to cross the eastern Yucatan peninsula Friday night, enter the southern Gulf of Mexico, and reach the northern Gulf coast Saturday evening, strengthening into a hurricane Saturday night into Sunday over warm Gulf waters. The 5 a.m. forecast shifted the track east, placing Pensacola back inside the warning cone stretching from the Florida Panhandle to central Louisiana; National Weather Service meteorologist Jack Cullen said Pensacola would likely be on the storm's eastern side, the side with higher wind gusts, storm surge and tornado risk.

For Escambia and Santa Rosa counties, heavy rain was expected from Saturday through at least Sunday, with flash flooding likely, isolated short-track tornadoes possible, and tropical storm force winds beginning Sunday morning and diminishing Sunday evening. Escambia County winds were forecast at 35–45 mph with gusts to 65 mph; Santa Rosa County at 15–25 mph with gusts up to 35 mph, with rainfall of 3–5 inches. A tropical storm watch covered much of the Northwest Florida Gulf coast, and Eglin Air Force Base set Hurricane Condition 4.

Closings and cancellations included the University of West Florida (noon Saturday through Monday, with a football game moved to Friday 6 p.m. at Blue Wahoos Stadium), Sacred Heart Health System's Medical Mission at Home, the BaseFEST concert at Pensacola Naval Air Station, all Gulf Islands National Seashore areas (with campers required to evacuate Fort Pickens and Davis Bayou by noon Friday), Pensacola ComposerFest XIII, Campus Church's Pensacola Day, and Northwest Florida Great Dane Rescue's Dane-Toberfest, rescheduled to Oct. 15.

Residents were advised to stock supplies and monitor local media; Santa Rosa County offered free sand at several sites, with residents bringing their own shovels. Gov. Rick Scott declared a state of emergency in 29 Florida counties, activated the state emergency operations center, positioned 7,000 National Guard members for possible deployment, prepared for sheltering, and had FDOT, utilities and fuel partners preparing for road clearance and potential outages. Scott was scheduled to give an update at the Escambia Operations Center at noon, warning Nate could strengthen quickly and shift course. Cullen noted fall storms like Nate often form quickly and are harder to track.

The 2017 summer season was marked by three dominant, generally well-received comic-book superhero hits: Guardians of the Galaxy Vol. 2, Wonder Woman and Spider-Man: Homecoming. Wonder Woman’s success masked shortcomings among other large-scale releases. Most genres produced only one notable success, including Despicable Me 3, Girls Trip, Annabelle: Creation, Dunkirk, Baby Driver, 47 Meters Down and The Big Sick, while films such as Captain Underpants, Cars 3, The Emoji Movie, King Arthur: Legend of the Sword, Valerian, The Mummy, Transformers: The Last Knight and War for the Planet of the Apes disappointed or bombed. Several early live-action comedies also failed, though The Beguiled, All Eyez on Me and Atomic Blonde avoided major financial failures. Overall, superhero films crowded out other big-budget genres at the multiplex, leaving little diversity and raising concerns about Hollywood’s reliance on franchises and reboots.

Researchers from UC Irvine and other institutions introduced a satellite-based drought severity index using NASA’s GRACE mission data to incorporate groundwater storage into drought assessments. The GRACE-DSI provides globally consistent monitoring, particularly where ground measurements are difficult, and tracks groundwater changes affecting soil-moisture recharge and drought recovery. Its 2002–2014 dataset is expected to be extended through current missions. Tests in the continental United States showed significant agreement with the Palmer index and other vegetation and soil-moisture measures.
Black Sabbath guitarist Tony Iommi announced his sponsored scholarship at a BIMM Birmingham Q&A and discussed the perseverance needed to overcome industry knockbacks.

A collection of May 24, 2001 reports focused on Enron, California’s electricity crisis, U.S. political shifts, and international energy markets.

A Houston Chronicle columnist urged Texas to resist what he called California officials’ “bullying,” criticizing Governor Gray Davis and Attorney General Bill Lockyer, particularly Lockyer’s suggestion that Enron Chairman Kenneth Lay could be imprisoned. The columnist argued that Enron should have challenged Lockyer’s remarks and sought an apology.

California Public Utilities Commission President Loretta Lynch said an investigation found evidence that some generators reduced and increased plant output to create emergency conditions and raise electricity prices. Generators cited operational and financial reasons for withholding capacity, including protection against failures in other units and contractual obligations. Federal regulators rejected Mirant’s argument that it needed to reserve output, stating generators face no financial risk when required to sell all available power in the spot market.

Analysts said Sen. James Jeffords’s expected departure from the Republican Party could give Democrats Senate control and create legislative gridlock. Potential effects included greater scrutiny or price-control threats for drug makers, pressure on HMOs, uncertainty for credit-card issuers if bankruptcy reform weakened, and intensified debate over defense spending and missile defense. Environmental restrictions could affect energy companies, although increased legislative uncertainty might benefit power traders such as Enron, Reliant Energy and Duke Energy through greater market volatility. Analysts also anticipated renewed tobacco hearings, less telecommunications deregulation, continued protection for Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac, and little likelihood that Bush’s existing tax cut would be reversed.

Brazil began electricity rationing in June in response to drought-driven shortages, asking consumers and businesses to reduce consumption by 15% to 25%, with a target of 20% and possible cuts of 40% if reservoirs continue falling. The government estimated it needed to add 31,000 megawatts, or 50% of capacity, by 2008 at a cost of about $14 billion. Currency risks had delayed power-plant investment, prompting proposals for Petrobras to provide fixed-price gas contracts. Enron was proceeding with plans for about 800 megawatts of new capacity.

India’s federal government appointed a representative to the panel negotiating Enron’s Dabhol power dispute with the Maharashtra State Electricity Board and created a committee to assess proposed settlements. The dispute concerned unpaid power bills and led Enron’s Dabhol subsidiary to issue a preliminary termination notice. Panel chairman Madhav Godbole initially resigned after criticism from former Maharashtra chief minister Sharad Pawar, then withdrew his resignation following support from Chief Minister Vilasrao Deshmukh. Negotiations were postponed and rescheduled for May 29. The panel had recommended renegotiating the power-purchase agreement and raised concerns about the original deal’s governance.

Central Europe’s gas market was expected to change as Poland considered a pipeline linking Belarusian and Slovak transit systems to carry Russian gas westward. Major energy companies were also competing for a planned 49% sale of Slovakia’s SPP, estimated at $2 billion to $8 billion, and related Czech assets. Enron Polska warned that a proposed long-term Norwegian supply contract could leave Poland’s gas distributor overcontracted.

Spain’s Endesa planned to auction its Electra de Viesgo subsidiary, which had 560,000 customers and 2,610 megawatts of generation capacity, to raise funds for other European operations. Enron and AES were among the invited bidders, while Hidrocantabrico was viewed as the leading candidate.

California gubernatorial candidate Bill Simon Jr. downplayed his energy investments and former role as a Hanover Compressor director, although the company had an Enron partnership. He said he was willing to consider expanded California drilling, opposed offshore drilling, and might support temporary wholesale price caps. Separately, Dynegy said it was seeking large domestic and overseas acquisitions across generation, pipelines, storage, utilities and communications, while targeting 10% of the U.S. power market and 15% of the U.S. gas market.

Six-year-old Ryan stars in his family’s YouTube toy-review channel, which Forbes ranked among the top 10 highest-paid YouTube stars in 2017, reportedly earning $11 million. Launched in 2015, it has over 10 million subscribers and eight billion views during Forbes’ tracking period. His family says he will continue while he enjoys it.

The long-short equity strategy combines long positions in stocks expected to appreciate with short positions in stocks expected to decline. It is a hedging approach intended to reduce risk, provide diversification, and generate returns from both rising and falling prices. Hedge funds often use leverage, derivatives, and a long bias; in a 130/30 strategy, long exposure equals 130% of assets under management and short exposure 30%. Its complexity and reliance on institutional capabilities may make it unsuitable for retail investors.

The strategy requires research to identify under- and overvalued stocks, often across different sectors to reduce correlation. In the passage’s example, a fund buys $70,000 of Merck stock at $85 and shorts $30,000 of Thor Industries stock at $75. If Merck rises to $95 and Thor falls to $65, the fund earns more than $8,185 from Merck and $4,000 from the short position. A separate five-stock portfolio example uses a $500,000 portfolio with a 70/30 long-short split. It illustrates how short positions can limit losses during market declines, although its long bias can still produce losses.

Edward Thorp is described as a pioneer of quantitative investing who founded Princeton Newport Partners in 1969 and ran it until 1988. The passage states that the firm never had a losing year and compounded returns at 19.1% with relatively low drawdown.

A simple pairs-trading backtest involving Coca-Cola and Pepsi-Cola using RSI-based rules produced a 0.45% average gain per trade, a 3.8% CAGR, 42% invested time, and roughly 11% maximum drawdown, but included flat or negative periods and only four trades. The passage emphasizes that long-short strategies generally require many pairs, substantial research, coding, capital, and often leverage.

The study presents a machine-learning-assisted inverse-design workflow for discovering diammonium organic spacers in Dion–Jacobson 2D perovskites with targeted energy-level alignments of types Ib, IIa, and IIb. An invertible 12-digit fingerprint encoding molecular fragments and functional groups was developed, enabling candidate structures to be reconstructed from predicted properties. Starting from 21 known spacers, molecular morphing generated about 4.89 million hypothetical spacers. High-throughput DFT calculations supplied HOMO/LUMO training data, while LASSO models using the fingerprints achieved R² scores of 0.95 for both properties. Feature analysis showed that aromatic-ring count and ammonium-group structure strongly influence frontier energy levels.

A two-step feasibility screen combined PubChem availability with a five-descriptor formability score; the latter classified 27 of 29 known cases correctly. DFT validation confirmed 8 type IIa and 44 type IIb candidates, while no type Ib candidate passed the synthesis filters. Constrained inverse design subsequently identified 56 candidates: 2 type Ib, 12 type IIa, and 42 type IIb. Type Ib designs required pentacene backbones with at least five fused benzene rings; type IIa candidates favored extended acene or oligothiophene conjugation, while type IIb candidates generally had one primary ammonium group and multiple pyridine-type nitrogen substitutions.

The workflow provides interpretable design rules and could be adapted to other properties or hybrid materials, but experimental validation remains outstanding, and feasibility screening does not fully account for solubility, reaction conditions, phase competition, or conformational effects.

Figure 8-5 shows a PGA848 driving a 16-bit, 1-MSPS ADS8860 SAR ADC with single-ended or differential inputs. The PGA848 uses separate input and output supplies: ±15 V for the input stage and 5.3 V for the output stage, with the latter shared with the ADC to prevent ADC input overload during PGA overdrive. A REF6250 supplies the ADC’s 5 V reference. The PGA848 REF pin is driven by an OPA192 buffer and set to a nominal 2.5 V, shifting the signal to ADC midscale.

Three filters are used. An input filter reduces EMI and RFI and should be customized for bandwidth and antialiasing requirements. A second filter uses CFB in parallel with the PGA’s 6.67 kΩ feedback resistors; 75 pF gives a nominal 318 kHz cutoff, or 277 kHz at the high resistor-tolerance limit. The third, at the ADC inputs, acts as a charge-reservoir and charge-kickback filter to reduce amplifier charge demand and distortion from incomplete sample-and-hold settling. Its RFIL and CDIFF values are tuned for settling, THD, and PGA stability. C0G capacitors are used throughout the signal path. Accounting for all filters, the PGA848 front end has a nominal 318 kHz bandwidth, changing to 277 kHz at the high feedback-resistor tolerance, while maintaining −0.1 dB flatness to 41 kHz.

The 2.5 V REF voltage is generated from the 5 V REF6250 through a 10 kΩ-to-10 kΩ precision divider using ±0.05%, ±5 ppm/°C resistors. The OPA192 uses a dual-feedback configuration with a 20 Ω isolation resistor, a 2 kΩ direct feedback path, and a 2 nF feedback capacitor to stabilize driving of the REF pin and its 22 nF bypass capacitor, providing 86° phase margin. Its noninverting input has a 1 kΩ/10 nF low-pass filter to reduce divider thermal noise. Changes to load capacitance require recalculation and simulation of stability components, with more than 60° phase margin required.

PGA848 performance is specified at ±15 V with VICM and VREF at mid-supply; output-stage supplies are clamped within input-stage limits. Supplies above ±20 V can permanently damage the device. Layout guidance emphasizes matched differential paths, local low-ESR bypass capacitors, trace separation, minimizing input-pin leakage and parasitic capacitance, reducing vias and thermal junctions, and separation from heat sources. TI also provides PSppice for TI, free TINA-TI simulation software, documentation, update notifications, and E2E support, while warning that ESD can damage the integrated circuit.

In a New York Times survey, most responding federal judges criticized the Supreme Court’s emergency docket decisions related to Trump’s second term.
