Of 65 respondents, 12 said the Court used the docket appropriately, 12 said lower courts received sufficient guidance, and only 2 of 54 said the docket improved public perceptions of the judiciary. At least seven of roughly 20 orders lacked reasoning, and nearly all benefited Trump, though the orders have had broad practical effects. The New York Times cautioned that respondents may not represent the judiciary, while the Volokh Conspiracy cited possible response bias and oversampling of judges in districts favorable to challengers.

Quarter Circle Games announced The Peterson Case, a Unity-developed first-person horror game for PlayStation 4, Xbox One, and PC. Set near the 1947 Roswell UFO incident, players investigate a deserted house and a family’s disappearance as Detective Franklin Reinhardt, confronting an unearthly presence while solving puzzles. No release date has been announced.

Zacks Investment Research upgraded Teck Resources (TECK) from “hold” to “buy,” setting a $25 price target implying 8.84% upside. The Vancouver-based diversified resource company focuses on copper, metallurgical coal, zinc, gold and energy and operates across the Americas, Asia Pacific, Europe and Africa. Analysts have an average “Buy” rating and consensus target of $31.18. Shares opened at $22.97, with a 52-week range of $14.56–$26.60, a $13.27 billion market capitalization, a 7.90 P/E ratio and a 1.20 beta. Quarterly results showed $0.73 EPS versus $0.71 expected and $2.82 billion in revenue versus $2.75 billion expected, while revenue rose 62% year over year. Analysts forecast $3.52 EPS for the current year, and institutional investors and hedge funds own 46.80% of the stock.

In 2002, DEA agents destroyed Diane Monson’s six state-legal medical-cannabis plants during a standoff with local officers. Monson and Angel Raich then sued, arguing that Congress lacked authority to regulate their wholly local, noncommercial cannabis use.

The Supreme Court upheld federal power 6–3, reasoning that regulating intrastate medical cannabis was necessary to preserve Congress’s ban on the interstate marijuana market. Justice Scalia’s separate opinion grounded federal authority in the Necessary and Proper Clause while acknowledging limits. Justices O’Connor and Thomas dissented, warning that the decision weakened meaningful limits on congressional commerce power and federalism. Thomas argued that “commerce” originally covered buying, selling, bartering, and transportation, not local cultivation and use.

The ruling was widely viewed as a major setback for efforts to constrain federal power. Randy Barnett later challenged the Obamacare insurance mandate on commerce-clause grounds, while former government solicitor general Paul Clement argued the opposite case. Five justices held that Congress could not regulate inactivity, although the mandate was upheld as a tax.

Raich’s later appeal also failed, though the court indicated she might have a defense against prosecution. Medical marijuana is now widely legal at the state level, while federal efforts to reclassify it have stalled. Justice Thomas has continued advocating a narrow, originalist understanding of the commerce clause.

The passage documents MSPM0G3519, MSPM0G3518, MSPM0G1519, and MSPM0G1518 peripherals, implementation guidance, development support, revision history, and packaging information. The temperature sensor provides a linear voltage output connected to an ADC channel, with a factory single-point calibration value for 12-bit operation using the 1.4-V internal reference. VREF supports selectable 1.4-V and 2.5-V internal references or an external reference and requires a decoupling capacitor.

The comparator supports six timer-based blanking sources, low-power wakeup, and timer fault handling. The buffered 12-bit DAC supports 8- or 12-bit resolution, offset self-calibration, straight-binary or twos-complement data, sampling control, FIFO/DMA operation, and event triggering. DAC_OUT and COMP0/1_IN3+ share PA15, so external circuitry on that pin is discouraged when DAC_OUT is used.

Security and processing features include AES-128/256 acceleration, code and data firewalls, secure storage for as many as four AES keys, CRC support, a 32-bit TRNG, the AESADV accelerator, a secure keystore, CRC-P, and hardware-accelerated 32-bit math functions. The TRNG can produce a number every 128 clock cycles and serve as a source for a FIPS-140-2-compliant system. The keystore supports 128- and 256-bit keys, while CRC-P supports CRC16-CCITT and CRC32-ISO3309.

Communications peripherals include UARTs with programmable baud rates, parity, LIN support, FIFOs, DMA, and loopback; I2C with 7-/10-bit addressing, controller and target modes, clock stretching, SMBus 3.0, DMA, address-match wakeup, glitch filters, and speeds up to 1 Mbit/s; SPI with controller/peripheral modes, programmable frames and prescalers, four-entry transmit and receive FIFOs, DMA, and TI, Motorola, and National Microwire formats; and CAN-FD compatible with CAN 2.0A, CAN 2.0B, and CAN-FD at up to 5 Mbit/s.

The low-frequency subsystem includes a 32-kHz RTC_B and independent watchdog timer. RTC_B provides calendar counters, alarms, periodic wakeups, clock output, and crystal-offset and temperature-drift compensation. IWDT_B uses an independent clock and generates a power-on reset if not serviced, while WWDT can generate a reset or interrupt and also operate as an interval timer. TIMGx general-purpose timers and TIMAx advanced timers support multiple counting modes, prescaling, capture/compare, synchronization, interrupt/DMA triggering, and cross-peripheral triggering; advanced timers add complementary PWM, programmable dead time, and configurable fault handling.

IOMUX selects peripheral functions and controls input, output, and shutdown-wakeup behavior. The device includes a two-wire serial wire debug interface. Its boot strap loader supports programming and configuration through UART or I2C, is protected by a 256-bit user-defined password, can be disabled, and may be invoked through hardware, reset behavior on blank devices, or a runtime command. The memory-mapped FACTORY region contains read-only capability data, trim information, device identifiers, and revision data.

Recommended layout includes 10-µF and 0.1-µF VDD/VSS ceramic decoupling capacitors, a 47-kΩ NRST pullup with a 10-nF pulldown, a 100-kΩ ROSC resistor when SYSOSC frequency correction is enabled, a 0.47-µF VCORE capacitor, and pullups for 5-V-tolerant open-drain outputs. TI also documents device naming conventions, development tools including CCS, SysConfig, SDK resources, IAR, Keil MDK, TI Arm-Clang, GNU Arm Embedded, LaunchPads, and support resources. The revision history records updates to specifications, peripheral descriptions, package previews, and documentation, followed by mechanical drawings and orderable-part information.

During a White House briefing, reporter Brian Karem asked Sarah Huckabee Sanders whether she had experienced sexual harassment and empathized with accusers. Sanders expressed empathy but declined to discuss her own experience, saying her role was to relay presidential information.

Motley Fool Money promotes three no-annual-fee credit cards: the Wells Fargo Active Cash Card, Capital One Quicksilver Cash Rewards Card, and a Citi card. Wells Fargo offers unlimited 2% cash back, a $200 bonus after $500 in purchases within three months, and 12 months of 0% introductory APR on purchases and qualifying balance transfers. Capital One offers unlimited 1.5% cash back, 5% back on travel booked through Capital One Travel, a $300 welcome package, and 15 months of 0% introductory APR. The Citi card provides 2% back through purchase and payment, 5% back on Citi Travel bookings, a $200 bonus after $1,500 in spending, and 18 months of 0% introductory APR on balance transfers only. All list recommended credit scores of 670–850 and variable APRs after their introductory periods. The page discloses that commissions and advertising relationships may affect offer placement or coverage, but not product ratings, and notes that issuers make approval decisions.

The University of Minnesota Morris occupies the site of a former Indian boarding school, where Native children were sometimes separated from their families and pressured to assimilate. One original boys’ dormitory remains and now houses the multi-ethnic resource center. In a campus talking circle, 20–30 Native students discussed higher education, boarding-school trauma affecting their communities, and the historical erasure of Native identity. The campus joined the University of Minnesota system in 1960 after operating as an agriculture school and boarding school. A state-law tuition waiver guarantees Native students free tuition, contributing to a student body that is about 20% Native American and making Morris the system’s most racially diverse campus.

Flu activity is widespread in every state except Oregon and Hawaii; 42 states reported high activity, and 53 children have died this season. The predominant H3N2 strain causes more cases, hospitalizations, and deaths, especially among older adults, while a Canadian study found the vaccine 17% effective against it. Officials still recommend vaccination and early antiviral treatment.

This disclosure describes computer-graphics techniques for rendering passthrough views in artificial-reality head-mounted devices. External cameras capture the user’s physical environment, and stereo correspondence is used with triangulation to estimate feature depths. The depths form a point cloud that is converted into a deformed 3D mesh representing the environment’s contour. The mesh is rendered from each eye’s viewpoint and textured using camera images, providing an accurate perspective and parallax.

For resource-limited devices, an alternative process obtains stereo correspondences from a video encoder’s motion vectors. One or both stereo images may be translated based on camera separation, after which epipolar-geometry and temporal filters remove unreliable correspondences. The resulting sparse point cloud is used to deform and smooth a coarse 3D mesh. A device may dynamically select GPU-based optical flow or the encoder-based method according to available computing resources and power.

Imprecise depth estimates and mesh smoothing can cause under-occlusion or over-occlusion between passthrough objects and virtual objects. Embodiments address this by generating instance-segmentation masks for objects such as people and animals. Each segmented instance receives a representative depth computed from corresponding model depths, either by averaging them or using the depth of a 3D centroid. A padded border around each instance is assigned a substantially farther depth to create a hard boundary and prevent nearby empty space from incorrectly occluding virtual objects.

During rendering, rays are cast from the user’s eye viewpoints to test the visibility of physical and virtual models. When a physical model intersection corresponds to a segmented instance, the renderer compares the instance’s representative depth, or its padded border’s farther depth, with the virtual object’s depth to determine occlusion. Intersections outside segmented instances use the depth of the underlying 3D model. The resulting passthrough output provides more consistent and natural occlusion between captured physical objects and rendered virtual objects.

Bitcoin rose more than one-third to over $9,000 for the first time since March, with analysts expecting further gains if it breaks $10,000. Buy orders exceeded 92% of market activity, prompting forecasts of a significant surge. Regulatory uncertainty appeared to be easing, and IMF chief Christine Lagarde said blockchain could transform saving and investing. Analysts said breaking $10,000 could fuel a bull market and push Bitcoin toward $11,500.

Version 6.00 of the SD Memory Card Physical Layer Simplified Specification defines the card’s physical interface and command protocol. It covers system concepts, functional operation, registers, hardware electrical requirements, and SPI mode, including read/write and ROM cards, User and Protected Areas, SDSC/SDHC/SDXC capacities, speed classes, and SD, UHS-I, UHS-II, and SPI bus behavior.

The specification addresses card identification, commands, responses, state transitions, data reads, writes, erases, write protection, lock/unlock, content protection, switching, clock and CRC control, error handling, performance classes, cache, self-maintenance, and command queueing. It defines core and extension registers, power-up sequences, bus timing, electrical characteristics, and SPI transactions. It also notes that SDIO cards are specified separately but remain compatible with SD Memory Cards. Appendices cover terminology, host design guidance, function extensions, application-performance support, and mechanical dimensions.

The speaker argues that Ryan Smyth should never be traded because he embodies the Edmonton Oilers’ identity and is irreplaceable. Edmonton had a strong core, including Smyth, Smith, and Moreau, and added significant players such as Peca and Pronger through trades. The speaker believes both Edmonton and Carolina can skate and think the game, making their series compelling, and hopes the Oilers provide its final storyline.

He describes Smyth’s love of hockey, devotion to the Oilers, and idolization by Edmonton’s children. He also recounts Smyth’s childhood encounter with Glen Anderson and explains that Smyth’s father, Boyd Whitney, worked extensively for the Oilers and helped raise several young players who later reached the NHL.

Discussing goaltending, the speaker explains Edmonton’s pursuit of Dwayne Roloson. He praises Roloson’s playoff experience, competitive character, technical style, and save percentage, crediting him with improving the Oilers’ historically strong defensive play. He also characterizes Carolina as knowledgeable, dedicated hockey fans whose teams have produced exciting playoff hockey.

Over 10 lakh Karnataka government and aided-school students in Classes 4–9 need remedial classes, including 4.5 lakh in mathematics and science, according to a Students Achievement Survey. The October 2017 assessment covered 36 lakh students across 50,000 schools; teachers will counsel students and issue mark cards to parents.

Auckland Airport said police and Aviation Security located a woman after international screening found a knife on her person. The terminal reopened, but screening restarted with a backlog. At least four Air New Zealand and Virgin Australia flights to Christchurch, Gisborne, and the Bay of Islands were delayed.

A six-year amplicon deep-sequencing study assessed antimalarial drug-resistance markers in *Plasmodium falciparum* samples collected from 2018–2023 in low-transmission southern Zambia. Surveillance included symptomatic patients and community samples around four health centers in Choma District. Of 570 samples assayed, 540 were successfully sequenced at one or more loci; 130 of 183 selected whole-genome-amplified samples were also successfully sequenced.

The WHO-candidate *Pfk13* P441L mutation was detected in 6% of samples (30/501), increasing from 0% in 2018 to 7.2% in 2023 and peaking at 9.3% in 2022. It occurred at all four health centers and in every year after 2018. Both the 2023 and six-year prevalences exceeded the 5% threshold used to indicate concern and warrant further investigation. The *Pfk13* A578S mutation occurred in three individuals in 2023, and no other nonsynonymous *Pfk13* mutations were detected. *Pfmdr1* Y184F prevalence was 41% without temporal change; wild-type N86 occurred in all samples, and P441L and Y184F co-occurred in two samples.

The findings indicate that P441L is present and likely increasing in southern Zambia, but its association with artemisinin resistance remains uncertain. Limited sequencing coverage, missing data, and variable sample sizes restricted prevalence estimates. The authors recommend therapeutic-efficacy and ex-vivo studies, whole-genome sequencing of P441L parasites, and expanded routine molecular surveillance.

U.S. stocks jumped Monday, with the S&P 500 posting its biggest one-day gain since April, as Fed President William Dudley said another 2017 rate rise was likely. Eurozone factory output fell sharply, China showed slowing growth, and Japan’s GDP beat expectations. Canada advanced its NAFTA goals, while oil and gold prices fell.

The study examined factors that attract and retain special education teachers in rural remote districts. A survey was completed by 93 teachers from three special education cooperatives in the rural Midwest. Respondents were predominantly female, White, and over 40 years old, and 60% had more than five years of experience.

For retention, 70% identified support from administrators, colleagues, and the community; 53% cited financial incentives; 44% cited job-related factors; and 2% cited rural initiatives. Support included administrative respect, collaboration with general educators, community connections, and networks for isolated teachers. Financial incentives included increased salaries, college assistance, and reduced insurance costs. Job-related factors included reduced paperwork and caseloads, additional resources, relevant professional development, and work-life balance. Among 22 teachers planning to leave, 36.3% cited job-related factors, 27.7% lack of support, and 22.7% limited rural initiatives.

For attraction, 96% cited financial incentives, 31% support, 15% job-related factors, and 9% rural initiatives. Recommended benefits included competitive salaries, better health insurance, tuition assistance, housing, and sign-on bonuses. Rural recruitment strategies included Grow Your Own programs and career fairs hosted by rural educators.

Teachers reporting greater support were more likely to plan to remain, while teachers planning to leave reported lower satisfaction and support. The study recommends combining financial, administrative, collegial, job-related, and locally focused strategies while using emotional intelligence, fostering collaboration, reducing burdens, and providing targeted professional development. Limitations include self-reported data, a geographically small and limited-diversity sample, and primarily descriptive analysis.

NASA’s Suomi NPP captured the aurora borealis over northern Canada on Dec. 22 in infrared. Solar-wind particles interact with Earth’s magnetic field and energize atmospheric gases, which release colored light. Displays peak with solar storms roughly every 11 years; the last cycle peaked in 2013, during the century’s weakest observed solar maximum.
Nintendo announced the smartphone game Mario Kart Tour, due in the fiscal year ending March 2019, but has not revealed what gameplay will involve.

Tyreek Hill’s surgery to repair a dislocated left knee and multiple torn ligaments, including his ACL, went well, and he is not expected to need another operation, agent Drew Rosenhaus said. Hill is expected to return in 2026, with a realistic goal of the season opener, after a season-ending injury in Miami’s 27-21 win over the Jets. Coach Mike McDaniel reported encouraging signs regarding possible nerve damage. The Dolphins, 1-3, must replace Hill’s production as other receivers, a tight end and a running back take on larger roles.

The speaker says teams must play tight, score on opportunities, and use home-ice advantage. They learned growing up that bad games happen and players must move on. Because both teams’ styles can counter each other, the better team should win. The speaker expected their opponents to play hard in the playoffs and knew what was needed, but their team failed to execute.

Thomas H. Fisher sought an accounting and $6,500 from Merrill Lynch, Pierce, Fenner & Beane, alleging that the firm or its predecessors succeeded to Fuller, Rodney & Co. and assumed its liabilities. Fisher’s commodity transactions occurred exclusively with Fuller, Rodney & Co. before its April 30, 1941 dissolution.

The trial court granted summary judgment for defendant Homer P. Hargrave. Affidavits and the parties’ agreement showed that only customer accounts transferred with customer consent were assumed, Fisher’s account was not transferred, and there was no merger, consolidation, or assumption of Fuller’s liabilities. The agreement also addressed office leases, employee contracts, files, and the admission of two Fuller partners to the successor firm.

The court found Fisher’s opposing allegations speculative and based on information and belief rather than admissible evidence. Fisher had not pursued statutory discovery procedures, and the record contained no order denying discovery. His accounting claim was equitable and eligible for summary judgment. Assuming one office lease and admitting former partners did not create liability for the former partnership. Fuller’s offer to appear and provide security for any judgment was noted. The judgment was affirmed.
BAE Systems will sell Qatar 24 Typhoon fighters under a £5 billion contract, part of a £6 billion deal including missiles and guided bombs.

USD/JPY rose after New Zealand’s open following North Korea’s missile test and renewed geopolitical unrest, with broad yen selling lifting the pair to 114.17. Signs of consolidation favored long-side trading, with bids at 113.85–75 and offers at 114.20/30.

Microsoft Corporation’s Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended June 30, 2016 describes its strategy to build platforms and productivity services for a mobile-first, cloud-first world. Founded in 1975, Microsoft operates in more than 190 countries and develops, licenses, and supports software, cloud services, devices, games, advertising, consulting, and training. Its strategic priorities are reinventing productivity and business processes, building an intelligent cloud platform, and creating more personal computing.

Beginning in fiscal 2016, Microsoft reported three operating segments:

- **Productivity and Business Processes:** Office Commercial, Office Consumer, Office 365 services, Dynamics business solutions, and related products.
- **Intelligent Cloud:** SQL Server, Windows Server, Visual Studio, System Center, Azure, Premier Support Services, and Microsoft Consulting Services.
- **More Personal Computing:** Windows and Windows licensing, Surface and other devices, Xbox hardware and services, games, and Bing search advertising.

Microsoft distributes products through OEMs, distributors, resellers, online channels, Microsoft stores, and cloud-service subscription programs. It licenses software through enterprise, volume, online-subscription, and partner programs for organizations of varying sizes. Its customers include consumers, businesses, public-sector organizations, developers, service providers, and OEMs; no individual customer accounted for more than 10% of revenue in fiscal 2016, 2015, or 2014.

Microsoft spent $12.0 billion on research and development in fiscal 2016, representing 14% of revenue. It conducts research through three engineering groups, Microsoft Research, and facilities worldwide. The company reported more than 61,000 issued U.S. and international patents and over 35,000 pending applications.

As of June 30, 2016, Microsoft employed approximately 114,000 people, including 63,000 in the United States and 51,000 internationally. Restructuring eliminated about 7,400 positions during fiscal 2016, primarily in phone hardware, and additional reductions were planned across smartphone hardware and global sales.

Principal risks include intense competition from software, device, cloud, gaming, search, and open-source providers; costs and execution risks associated with cloud services and infrastructure; uncertain returns on product investments and the Windows 10 transition; acquisition integration and goodwill impairment risks, including the announced $26.2 billion LinkedIn acquisition; intellectual-property protection and infringement claims; cybersecurity threats and customer-data breaches; service outages; competition, privacy, trade, tax, and other regulatory requirements; difficulty attracting and retaining talent; litigation; hardware quality and supply-chain disruptions; software defects; accessibility requirements; and international operational and currency risks.

A cross-sectional study led by Professor Daisuke Matsushita at Osaka Metropolitan University examined whether commuting time and residence size predict insomnia and daytime sleepiness among Tokyo metropolitan residents. Data came from an online survey using stratified random sampling, with commute times calculated via a route search system based on participants' transportation modes and home/workplace postal codes; insomnia and sleepiness were measured with the Athens Insomnia Scale and Epworth Sleepiness Scale. After adjusting for demographic and socioeconomic factors, longer commutes predicted both insomnia and daytime sleepiness, while smaller floor area predicted insomnia, revealing a trade-off between commuting time and housing size. For units meeting the urban-oriented standard of 95 m² for a four-person household, commutes exceeding 52 minutes reached the insomnia cutoff. The authors suggest housing choices and supply accounting for this trade-off could improve commuters' sleep health and reduce sleep-related economic losses. The article notes Japan has the lowest sleep duration among OECD countries, an hour below average.

A soccer defender's 1v1 stance should be a balanced, comfortable position far enough from the ball carrier to react in any direction: one foot forward (lead foot), one back (trail foot), usually the dominant leg behind. Adults set feet about 18 inches apart on a 30-degree angle, toes slightly outward, body on the balls of the feet, knees bent, arms out with elbows bent. This enables quick reaction, slowing or redirecting opponents, and tackle preparation. Stance varies with location: left foot leads right of midfield, right foot leads left, either foot centrally, pushing attackers toward the sideline. Coaches should demonstrate the right, center and left stances, use half-speed drills and "sneak peeks" to maintain goal side position, and remind defenders not to extend their arms to impede opponents.

The Iso Play is a downhill running scheme in which a fullback leads the tailback and isolates a linebacker, using multiple base blocks and double teams to overpower the defense and move the ball vertically. Its main strengths are rapid downhill execution, consistency with a powerful tailback and offensive line capable of winning one-on-one blocks, and simplicity that makes it easy to teach and execute. Its primary weakness is its reliance on personnel; smaller, weaker linemen and a fullback unable to handle linebackers in the hole reduce its effectiveness. Blocking assignments against 3-4 odd and 4-3 even fronts emphasize leverage, vertical blocking, fullback and tailback paths, handoff mechanics, and safety climb-ups. Variations include Shotgun Iso, used by Art Briles and Baylor alongside RPOs, and Weakside Iso, which can create favorable double-team angles and blocks an outside linebacker rather than the middle linebacker.

GBPJPY represents the British pound against the Japanese yen. It is a minor cross pair formed through simultaneous trading in GBPUSD and USDJPY: going long both creates a net long GBPJPY position, while shorting both creates a net short. Known as “Geppy” or “The Beast,” it is highly volatile and is viewed as an indicator of global economic health. The number of factors affecting it is nearly unlimited, and its reported average movement in 2022 was around 175 pips.

GBPJPY and USDJPY can sometimes have a correlation above 0.9, creating substantial double-exposure risk. For intraday trading, the favored periods are the Asian session (23:00–06:00 GMT) and London session (08:00–16:00 GMT).

Forex trading is described as difficult because it is zero-sum, rates are hard to predict, and unregulated brokers pose scam risks. Backtesting is presented as essential for identifying positive expectancy and determining diversification benefits. An example GBPJPY futures strategy reportedly performed well over several years, although its exact rules and metrics are not provided.

The Sansa Fuze manual covers device navigation, connectivity, media management, playback, recording, settings, troubleshooting, support, and warranty terms. The thumbwheel scrolls menus, adjusts volume, and changes settings; other buttons control playback, selection, and options.

To connect the player to a computer, attach the Sansa cable to the computer’s USB port and the player’s dock connector. The player should display “Connected.” The cable should not be disconnected during data transfers because doing so may damage the device. Firmware updates are available from SanDisk’s support website. Formatting can be performed on the device or computer, but it deletes all player content.

Music can be transferred by drag-and-drop or with Windows Media Player, which can also create and synchronize playlists. Audible files require Audible Manager. Photos and videos are transferred with Sansa Media Converter, which can crop, rotate, and resize photos and copy media to a microSD card. The player supports MP3, WMA, secure WMA, Audible content, audiobooks, podcasts, videos, photos, and voice recordings.

Playback options include repeat, shuffle, MusicEQ, Go Lists, song deletion, audiobook chapter and speed settings, video bookmarks, ratings, brightness, and deletion. Photo viewing supports slideshows, shuffle, looping, slide duration, music selection, Go Lists, and deletion.

The FM radio supports manual frequency searching, up to 30 presets, automatic scanning, station recording, and regional mono or stereo settings. The built-in microphone records the user’s voice. Content can also be deleted directly from the player or through Windows Explorer.

System settings include wallpaper, list artwork, backlight, power saver, language, date and time, brightness, factory reset, device information, USB mode, and press-and-hold behavior. Troubleshooting covers supported formats and bit rates, firmware, file transfer, metadata, microSD compatibility, and power resets. SanDisk provides technical support, how-to resources, a one-year limited warranty, and a software license containing usage restrictions and liability limitations.

Microsoft Corporation filed a Form 10-Q for the quarter ended December 31, 2018, containing unaudited U.S. GAAP financial statements for the three- and six-month periods. Prior-period amounts were recast for certain financial-instrument standards and to include the commercial portion of LinkedIn in commercial cloud metrics. Deloitte’s review found no material modifications necessary for conformity with U.S. GAAP.

For the quarter, revenue was $32.471 billion, up 12%; gross margin was $20.048 billion, up 12%; operating income was $10.258 billion, up 18%; and net income was $8.420 billion, or $1.08 per diluted share, compared with a $6.302 billion loss, or $0.82 per diluted share, in the prior-year quarter. For the six months, revenue rose 15% to $61.555 billion, operating income rose 23% to $20.213 billion, and net income reached $17.244 billion, or $2.22 per diluted share, compared with $274 million, or $0.04 per diluted share. Prior-year results included a $13.8 billion Tax Cuts and Jobs Act charge; the current period included an additional $157 million tax expense.

At December 31, 2018, Microsoft reported $258.859 billion of assets, $166.731 billion of liabilities, and $92.128 billion of stockholders’ equity. Cash and equivalents totaled $6.638 billion and short-term investments totaled $121.024 billion. Six-month operating cash flow was $22.557 billion; financing and investing activities used $20.600 billion and $7.153 billion, respectively, including $10.157 billion for share repurchases and $6.764 billion for dividends. Long-term debt including the current portion had a carrying value of $73.2 billion, while debt investments had a fair value of $124.293 billion.

Quarterly segment revenue was $10.100 billion for Productivity and Business Processes, up 13%; $9.378 billion for Intelligent Cloud, up 20%; and $12.993 billion for More Personal Computing, up 7%. Commercial cloud revenue increased 48% to $9.0 billion. Other reported growth included Azure at 76%, Office 365 commercial at 34%, LinkedIn at 29%, Dynamics at 17%, Windows Commercial at 13%, Surface at 39%, and Gaming at 8%; Windows OEM revenue declined 5%.

Microsoft acquired GitHub on October 25, 2018, in a transaction valued at $7.5 billion and reported it within Intelligent Cloud. It also completed 11 other acquisitions for $959 million. Microsoft adopted tax guidance for intra-entity asset transfers and a new financial-instruments standard in the first quarter of fiscal 2019. Effective tax rates were 19% for the quarter and 16% for the six months. Unearned revenue was $28.084 billion, while contracted but unrecognized revenue totaled $72 billion, approximately 60% of which was expected to be recognized within 12 months.

Legal matters included 32 patent cases, approved Canadian antitrust settlements, a Chinese regulatory investigation, cellular-phone litigation, and employment-related litigation. Microsoft had accrued $273 million of legal liabilities and said reasonably possible additional outcomes could reach approximately $1.0 billion. Management identified competition, rapid technological and business-model changes, infrastructure and device costs, employee retention, macroeconomic and geopolitical conditions, foreign-exchange exposure, and seasonality as business risks and challenges.

Amazon.com, Inc. filed a Form 8-K dated January 29, 2015, announcing its fourth-quarter 2014 and year-ended December 31, 2014 financial results. The filing includes the related press release and information regarding non-GAAP financial measures.

The Physical Layer Simplified Specification Version 6.00 defines SD Memory Card interfaces, communication, initialization, data transfer, performance modes, and protection features. “Shall” and “will” indicate mandatory provisions, “should” indicates recommendations, and “may” indicates optional features. The Mc-EX interface extends the SD physical layer to transfer Mobile Commerce Extension packets among hosts and enabled SD or SDIO cards.

SD Memory Cards support capacities from SDSC (up to 2 GB), through SDHC (over 2 GB to 32 GB), to SDXC (over 32 GB to 2 TB). High-voltage cards operate at 2.7–3.6 V, while UHS-II cards also use VDD2 at 1.70–1.95 V. Read/write cards use Flash, OTP, or MTP storage; ROM cards contain fixed data. Cards support User and Protected Areas, mechanical and internal write protection, and password-based locking.

Bus modes range from Default Speed at 25 MHz and High Speed at 50 MHz to SDR104 at 208 MHz, DDR50, and UHS-II rates up to 6.24 Gbps per lane. UHS-I uses 1.8 V signaling for SDR50, SDR104, and DDR50 and requires a voltage-switch sequence following initialization. UHS-II adds FD156, optional HD312, FD312, and FD624 modes, with initialization covering PHY setup, device initialization, enumeration, configuration, and SD-command emulation.

Communication consists of commands, responses, and data transferred over CMD and DAT lines. Tokens use CRC protection; block data supports single- or multiple-block transfers, one or four data lines, and CRC checking. Cards expose identification, status, configuration, operating-condition, driver-stage, and card-specific registers. Power cycling or GO_IDLE resets cards, and cards use session addresses for selection.

The host controls communication through broadcast and addressed commands. Card identification includes voltage verification with CMD8, operating-condition negotiation with ACMD41, CID retrieval with CMD2, RCA assignment with CMD3, and card selection with CMD7. Identification uses only the CMD line, while data-transfer mode supports point-to-point transfers. Reads and writes can be stopped with CMD12, use CRC-protected blocks, and may include write buffering. Erase sequences use CMD32, CMD33, and CMD38; DISCARD and FULE are available for SDHC and SDXC cards under specified conditions.

Speed classes indicate minimum performance, while Application Performance Class defines minimum random and sequential performance. Optional cache, self-maintenance, and command-queue features can improve performance; cached data may be lost if not flushed before power-off. ROM cards restrict write-related commands and may optionally support password or security commands.

Card Ownership Protection extends password locking with a Force Erase Password and COP-specific CMD42 functions. COP cards can manage FEP, perform authorized force erase, and restrict password operations until COP Unlock is completed.

Malacañang said President Duterte will investigate allegations against Development Academy of the Philippines president Elba Cruz, including unauthorized restructuring, Civil Service violations, mass-termination threats and frequent foreign travel. The Palace was vetting his anti-corruption commission. Duterte also planned to fire Urban Poor commission officials over alleged junkets and failure to attend en banc meetings.

The study reviews eight major leadership models in education: administrative/managerial, instructional, transformational, distributed, transactional, ethical, contingent and participative leadership. Administrative leadership provides clear structure and hierarchy but can be rigid, inhibit innovation and discourage shared vision. Instructional leadership emphasizes goals, quality teaching, academic climates and supportive learning environments, but may reinforce top-down control and overlook student well-being and other aspects of school life. Transformational leadership promotes shared vision, motivation, innovation, collaboration and stakeholder development, although efforts to transform staff attitudes can become authoritarian. Distributed leadership shares leadership responsibility across the school community, improving engagement, trust and learning outcomes, but requires time and skills and may generate communication problems or conflict. Transactional leadership uses authority, rewards and exchanges to shape performance and maintain organizational stability, but may undermine morale if benefits are uneven. Ethical leadership promotes fairness, accountability, respect and responsible decision-making, though mismatch between leaders’ ethics and organizational culture can create conflict. Contingent leadership requires principals to assess circumstances and adapt their approach, particularly during crises. Participative leadership involves stakeholders in shared decision-making, increasing trust, creativity, commitment and job satisfaction, but can slow decisions, provoke conflict and create confidentiality risks.

The review concludes that no single model can address the changing demands of schools. It recommends a synthetic, flexible approach combining managerial structure, transformational motivation, distributed and participative collaboration, ethical integrity, contingent adaptability and transactional operational tools.

The University of Windsor named Douglas Kneale interim president and vice-chancellor effective July 1, after Alan Wildeman’s term ends June 30. The board requested that the presidential search committee resume efforts and will announce a successor once identified. Wildeman will name an acting provost in the coming weeks.

Councillor Andrew Antoniolli received $46,400 in campaign donations, including $15,000 from Plencove and a $600 payment for two campaign-launch tickets. The passage describes methods and apparatus for improving the localization of electronically generated binaural or 3D sound during calls, games, augmented or virtual reality, advertisements, and other communications. It addresses difficulties localizing near-field sound, where head-related transfer functions (HRTFs) vary significantly and may be unavailable, unreliable, or computationally intensive, as well as mismatches between perceived sound locations and visible images or objects.

Example embodiments convolve sound using HRTFs and sound localization information at a location different from the actual source, such as behind, before, after, adjacent to, or offset from the source along the listener’s line of sight. Far-field HRTFs may be positioned behind a near-field source to reduce processing demands and encourage listeners to perceive the sound as originating from the visible or known source. Sound volume can be adjusted to reflect the source’s perceived distance, and localization coordinates can vary according to listener feedback, sound characteristics, gaze, and head or device orientation.

The techniques apply to visible and nonvisible sources, including images, virtual objects, alerts, and voices from multiple devices or users. Sound may be delivered through headphones, earphones, earbuds, wearables, or bone-conduction devices even when the source device’s speakers are inactive or powered off. Processing can track moving devices and heads, separately localize multiple sources, and help listeners identify the device producing a sound.

Other embodiments switch audio between binaural and mono or stereo output in response to sensor-detected conditions, including device rotation, movement, facial orientation, gaze changes, distance, light or darkness, sensor blockage, headphone connection, and power-state changes. Example triggers include rotating a smartphone by a specified threshold, such as 90 degrees, to end or resume external sound localization. Low-battery or other state changes can also switch to mono output to conserve power.

The lecture extends projection theory from finite- to infinite-dimensional inner-product spaces. Successive projections onto an orthonormal sequence converge to the target vector, leaving a residual orthogonal to every vector in the expansion. For countable orthonormal expansions spanning \(L^2\), this residual is zero in the \(L^2\) sense. Truncated sinusoids span \(L^2\) over \([-T/2,T/2]\), and arbitrary \(L^2\) functions can be used in such expansions because their inner products are finite by the Schwarz inequality. Prolate spheroidal functions provide another orthonormal expansion optimized to maximize energy concentration within specified time and frequency intervals; for large \(T\) and \(W\), roughly \(2WT\) functions concentrate energy near the desired band.

The lecture then turns to communication systems, organized into layers: a source is converted into binary data, a digital encoder converts binary data into symbols, and modulation maps symbols into waveforms for transmission. Separating source conversion from channel modulation avoids building a unique encoder for every source–channel pairing. With \(b\) bits per symbol, the required alphabet has size \(2^b\), linking alphabet growth exponentially to transmission-rate gains and to the logarithm appearing in Shannon capacity formulas.

The discussion initially treats baseband modulation without considering delay, attenuation, or bandwidth limitations. Timing-recovery circuits can align receiver timing with the transmitter despite propagation delay, while attenuation is handled separately through link-budget calculations. Scaling both signal and noise leaves the signal-to-noise ratio as the relevant quantity. Decibels are used to simplify calculations involving multiplicative power losses.

A simple binary scheme maps 0 and 1 to \(+1\) and \(-1\), then represents the resulting signals as delayed sinc pulses. Because sinc filtering is noncausal and effectively requires infinite delay, pulse-amplitude modulation instead uses an arbitrary pulse shape \(p(t)\). Standard PAM uses a one-dimensional constellation of real-valued signals, normally equally spaced and centered around zero. For \(M=2^b\) equiprobable points spaced by \(d\), the mean-square signal energy is \(d^2(M^2-1)/12\). Increasing the number of constellation points therefore raises energy rapidly. Under additive, signal-independent noise, constellation-point distances are the primary concern.

In the PAM receiver, transmit and receive filters \(p(t)\) and \(q(t)\) combine into the composite filter \(g(t)=p(t)*q(t)\). Nyquist showed that sampling recovers the transmitted symbols without intersymbol interference precisely when \(g(kT)=\delta_{k0}\). Although the sinc pulse satisfies this condition, its delay is impractical. Nyquist’s band-edge symmetry criterion characterizes composite filters whose spectrum can extend as far as twice the Nyquist bandwidth, \(1/(2T)\), while still satisfying the interference-free condition. Raised-cosine filters provide a practical compromise between bandwidth and delay; filters with a roll-off parameter near 15 percent decay rapidly and are commonly used.

The study investigates whether exchange bias in sputtered RuO2/Fe/Ru heterostructures indicates intrinsic antiferromagnetism or altermagnetism in rutile RuO2. SQUID magnetometry, polarized neutron diffraction and reflectometry, atom probe tomography, HRTEM/FFT, and EELS were combined with structural and magnetization measurements.

RuO2 films showed no detectable compensated sublattice moments by polarized neutron diffraction, with an upper limit of 0.01 μB per Ru atom. Forbidden room-temperature diffraction peaks were attributed to multiple scattering from TiO2 rather than RuO2 magnetic order. Fe-based heterostructures nevertheless exhibited exchange bias below approximately 50 K, with hysteresis shifts dependent on field-cooling history.

Polarized neutron reflectometry identified uncompensated, in-plane canted moments at the RuO2/Fe interface whose orientation varied with magnetic history and could pin Fe magnetization. Chemical and structural characterization showed interfacial intermixing, reduced Ru, an oxidized Fe gradient, and iron-oxide reaction layers containing evidence of magnetite, Fe3O4. Ni-based RuO2 heterostructures showed no exchange bias, while Fe/Ru bilayers without RuO2 exhibited a smaller shift, supporting a Fe-specific interfacial oxidation and magnetic-coupling mechanism rather than intrinsic RuO2 magnetism. The authors conclude that exchange bias and related magnetotransport in RuO2/Fe structures alone do not establish antiferromagnetic or altermagnetic order in RuO2, although the results do not rule out altermagnetism in rutile RuO2 generally.

The paper explores how relevance-theoretic accounts of conversational implicature can be modeled probabilistically, extending Bayesian approaches associated with Rational Speech Act theory. Using an exchange in which Mary declines coffee, it distinguishes explicatures—propositions developed through contextual enrichment, reference resolution, and temporal interpretation—from implicatures, which require contextual premises and inferred conclusions.

The paper explains that relevance theory treats communication as intention attribution. Communicators have informative intentions to make assumptions manifest and communicative intentions to make those intentions recognizable. Manifestness combines epistemic strength with salience or accessibility, while relevance measures cognitive effects relative to processing effort. Overtly intentional communication raises a presumption of optimal relevance. Comprehension follows an efficient heuristic: access the easiest interpretation, check whether it produces the expected cognitive effects, and, if not, consider less accessible alternatives. Specific relevance expectations can support strong implicatures; weak or non-specific expectations generally support only weak implicatures or relevance through the explicature alone.

The paper also relates this process to Gricean inference and RSA, arguing that explicatures, implicatures, and contextual assumptions are adjusted in parallel rather than interpreted through an intermediate literal meaning. It treats relevance-guided comprehension as a “fast and frugal” heuristic whose candidate interpretations can be represented probabilistically.

A computational model is implemented in ProbLog. Probabilistic knowledge graphs encode encyclopedic relationships among beverages and drink categories, inference rules connect “energizing drink” to relevant concepts, and a Bayesian network represents the utterance, conceptual adjustment, explicature, contextual premise, and implicature. Relevance is operationalized through KL divergence between prior and posterior distributions over communicated propositions; when interpretations have equal KL divergence, the smaller Herbrand base is treated as less costly.

Five interpretive hypotheses illustrate the model: one satisfies the relevant expectations efficiently, one fails to satisfy them, two add unnecessary processing costs, and one adds inferences that become relevant when expectations are expanded accordingly. The resulting optimization procedure eliminates hypotheses that fail relevance expectations, breaks KL-divergence ties by Herbrand-base size, and selects the remaining hypothesis with the highest KL divergence. The paper presents this as an “as-if optimization” model for audience-side implicature comprehension. It acknowledges that candidate interpretations must be supplied manually and identifies extension to speaker reasoning, higher-level explicatures, and metarepresentational uses as future work.

Strange Brigade, a cooperative shooter for 1–4 players, launches August 28 on PS4, Xbox One, and PC. Rebellion’s 1930s adventure involves exploring ancient locations, fighting mythological enemies, and overcoming traps and puzzles. Pre-orders include the Secret Service Weapons Pack, while the Deluxe Edition adds a season pass with new missions, characters, weapons, and items.

BioSafe Systems hired Carleton Birk as Operations Manager at its East Hartford, Connecticut headquarters, and Tenaya Becker, Ester Mastronardi, Patrick Clark, and Kyle Pickles as technical sales representatives for Southern California, Canada, Eastern Pennsylvania, and Central California, respectively. Their backgrounds include operations, horticulture, agricultural sales, agronomy, nursery management, and water-treatment support.

The speaker said his team’s convincing win did not change its two-games-to-none series deficit. He remained encouraged by the team’s spirits, improved power play, strong penalty kill, and ability to score, but expected a tough next game as the opponent sought a rebound. He emphasized better puck management, forechecking, neutral-zone decisions, fewer turnovers, and continued physical play.

A teammate was hospitalized after an apparent blindside hit; the player was reported to be moving, but his condition was unclear. The hit was referred to the league, and line combinations would be adjusted pending the player’s status. The speaker also rejected players’ emotional or unsportsmanlike behavior and said they had been instructed to act consistently with his standards.

The opponent continued to play aggressively in the neutral zone and counterattack effectively, so the speaker planned to match that physicality and use his fourth line more. Playing at home, following recent travel, and receiving strong fan support were viewed as advantages, although he stressed the team must stay even-keeled, start well, and focus on turning the series around.

Georgia Tech researchers simulated ransomware compromising a water treatment plant, showing how attackers could shut valves, alter chlorine levels, display false readings, and demand payment. Although no real ransomware attacks on industrial control systems have been reported, researchers warn that weak passwords, security policies, network isolation misconceptions, and inadequate monitoring leave critical infrastructure vulnerable.

Mary Meeker’s 2017 Internet trends report found global internet use growing 7% to 3.6 billion users and smartphone sales leveling off. Voice computing reached 95% word-recognition accuracy, while Amazon Echo was in over 30 million homes. E-commerce grew 16% and represented 13% of retail sales; 49% of product searches began on Amazon. Netflix led subscriptions with 117 million customers, followed by Amazon Prime at 100 million and Spotify at 75 million. Uber reported 31 million drivers averaging $21 hourly, while Airbnb had 600,000 hosts averaging $6,100. U.S. unemployment stood at 3.9%, below the 70-year average of 5.8%, with job openings at a 17-year high of 7 million.

A July 27–28, 2001 email compiles reports on Enron and energy markets. A Cato article says California data obtained through lawsuits contradicted Gov. Gray Davis’s price-gouging claims, noting public utilities charged more on average than private companies and state buyers often set prices. Reliant Energy and Peoples Energy reported quarterly profit gains, although weather, gas operations, competition and other costs offset some gains. In India, Enron sought government purchase of its 65% stake in Dabhol after Maharashtra stopped buying power amid a $64 million unpaid-bill dispute; four states offered lower tariffs, which Dabhol rejected, stalling negotiations. California lawmakers subpoenaed Enron, Reliant and other energy firms over possible market manipulation; Enron and Reliant resisted, and Enron sued to block the subpoenas. Investors showed growing interest in energy technology after deregulation, though funding tightened. The Sansa c200 manual covers USB 2.0 connection, file transfer, and safe removal from computers. Photos can be transferred with Sansa Media Converter, which supports JPEG, TIFF, PNG, BMP, and GIF files. Music and other files can also be transferred by drag-and-drop in MTP or MSC mode, synchronized with software, or deleted through the computer’s file browser.

Operational instructions address power controls, navigation, music, FM radio, and voice playback; repeat, shuffle, equalizer, and GoList settings; photo viewing, slideshows, and photo options; radio tuning, presets, and broadcast recording; and voice recording. Device settings include display backlight and contrast, factory reset, device information, automatic power-off, and MTP/MSC mode selection.

The FAQ explains copying and converting files, supported audio formats, MTP and MSC behavior, podcast requirements, ID3 tag information, playback rights, and firmware updates. It also provides technical-support contact information and a one-year SanDisk limited warranty. Microsoft WM-DRM notices, a SanDisk software license agreement, trademark information, and disposal instructions are included; the device must not be discarded with unsorted household waste and should be handled according to local waste-authority guidance.

The study combined 102 open-access medical imaging datasets to classify CT, MRI, PET, and X-ray images by modality. The corpus was described as 4.5 million images, although the methods reported 6.43 million after imbalance correction. Dataset-level train, validation, and test splits were used to prevent data leakage. ResNet-18, ResNet-50, and VGG16 classifiers were trained for 10 epochs on normalized 224×224 grayscale images. ResNet-18 performed best, achieving 96.00% accuracy and 86.17% balanced accuracy on unseen test data; ResNet-50 reached 95.60% accuracy and 85.65% balanced accuracy, while VGG16 reached 94.58% and 81.08%, respectively. Performance was strongest for CT, MRI, and PET, while X-ray classification was weaker for bone images because training data were dominated by chest X-rays. The results indicate that CNNs can classify medical images at repository scale, with future work proposed for 3D scans.

Following a southern rebellion, Korea requested 2,000 Chinese troops, but Korean forces captured the rebel leaders and retook Chon-ju before China actively intervened. Japan also deployed troops, and neither China nor Japan would withdraw first. Japanese troops expanded to 3,000, encamped with batteries at Chemulpo, and prompted a joint diplomatic protest. Korea’s king urged Chinese withdrawal, while Chinese residents reportedly fled, fearing violence if Chinese reinforcements advanced.

Twenty-eight warships and transports from six countries were present at Chemulpo. Admiral Skerrett arrived aboard the USS Baltimore and promised to remain until tensions eased. The U.S. minister was instructed to preserve peace and reported continuing danger, suspected Japanese ulterior motives, and concern over Korea’s integrity. Unverified reports also indicated that Japan was sending additional troops to Fusan and Wensan.

The article develops “educational pacifism,” arguing that mass formal schooling is morally unjust when it harms students, especially by treating innocent children as means to educational or social goals. Drawing on Feinberg, Mill, and Kant, it defines harm as worsening someone’s important interests and argues that most students are innocent targets even if their personhood is disputed. Educational harm is not a last resort, because peaceful alternatives exist.

Although personal harms such as bullying, violence, humiliation, and exclusion are often acknowledged, systemic harms are more pervasive and less visible. Structural harm includes authoritarian hierarchies, discrimination, coercive discipline, and conformity to industrial and capitalist expectations. Objective harm includes inequality, economic exploitation, surveillance, concentrated knowledge and power, and students’ dependence on institutional judgments. Symbolic harm occurs through ideologies, curricula, testing, ranking, rewards, punishments, and instructional practices that normalize subordination and prioritize obedience and rote learning over creativity, autonomy, confidence, engagement, and well-being.

The article finds Montessori’s philosophy broadly compatible with educational pacifism, although she did not use that term. Montessori defined peace as a positive, enduring way of life rather than merely the absence of violence and regarded education as essential to intrapersonal, interpersonal, and systemic peace. Her ethics emphasized respect, freedom, harmonious activity, and the dignity and agency of children. She opposed coercive rewards and punishments, competition, domination, and mass schooling’s preparation of students for bureaucratic, capitalist, and subordinate roles. Montessori education instead promotes self-directed activity, communal cooperation, freedom within structure, and social reform.

The article recommends that contemporary Montessori educators reject educational harm and unjustified paternalism while retaining beneficial guidance and structure. It acknowledges that some Montessori schools depart from these principles through weak implementation, timetabling, testing, coercion, hierarchy, and racial or economic segregation. Because students may be unable to recognize normalized systemic harms, Montessori educators are presented as well positioned to challenge harmful practices. The conclusion is not that all schooling is inherently harmful or should be abolished, but that mass formal schooling significantly harms many students and that Montessori education can provide a nonharmful alternative oriented toward peace and justice.

The passage describes the DAX 40, Germany’s main equity index, formally the Deutscher Aktienindex. It comprises the 40 largest or most liquid blue-chip stocks on Deutsche Börse Xetra and expanded from 30 constituents on September 20, 2021. The index began trading in 1988 at 1,000 points and includes companies such as Adidas, BMW, SAP, Siemens, and Volkswagen.

DAX can be traded through futures, CFDs, or ETFs. Futures are described as the most popular and liquid option, allowing leveraged trading on margin with daily mark-to-market adjustments and possible margin calls. Three Eurex contracts are available: standard futures at €25 per point, Mini futures at €5, and Micro futures at €1. All have a minimum price fluctuation of 0.5 points, expire quarterly, and settle in cash. Futures trade electronically from 07:50 to 22:00 CET. CFDs are also zero-sum derivatives, while the US-listed EWG ETF tracks a broader German market and trades during US hours.

The passage highlights DAX’s liquidity, low costs, distinct trading hours, and potential diversification from US equities. Mean-reversion, breakout, gap, and momentum strategies are said to perform well on DAX. Two overnight futures strategies entered at 17:30 CET and exited at 09:00 CET. The 2021 strategy’s unleveraged backtest recorded 209 trades, a 65% win rate, a 2 profit factor, a 5.1% maximum drawdown, and 0.22% average gain per trade; the 2022 version recorded 303 trades with an average gain of 0.23%.

MIT 6.832 Underactuated Robotics begins with course expectations: familiarity with differential equations, linear algebra, and preferably MATLAB is assumed, while prior robotics training is not. Lectures, notes, problem sets, submissions, and interactive PDF annotations are to be provided online.

The lecture motivates underactuated robotics by contrasting conventional, conservative robots with systems that exploit their natural dynamics. Honda’s ASIMO uses high-gain feedback to keep its feet flat and knees bent while walking, resulting in high energy use, limited battery life, low speed, and difficulty on uneven terrain. In contrast, Cornell’s passive dynamic walker uses gravity alone and exhibits a more natural walking motion. A similar contrast is drawn between conventional military aircraft, which remain in controllable low-angle-of-attack regimes, and birds that land at high angles of attack, producing complex vortices, stall, and pressure drag. Such examples support the course’s central idea: robots should use their dynamics cleverly rather than use actuators to override them, requiring smarter control methods.

Further examples highlight efficiency and maneuverability. Albatrosses travel vast distances with little flapping by using wind gradients; falcons dive at 240 miles per hour; bats fly rapidly through confined spaces; and trout use vortices behind rocks to reduce swimming effort. Robotic birds can now be built, but controlling them to perch or extract energy from the air remains unsolved.

For second-order mechanical systems, the lecture uses the form  
\(\ddot q=f_1(q,\dot q,t)+f_2(q,\dot q,t)u\), with motion linear in the control input. A system is fully actuated when \(f_2\) has full rank relative to the dimension of \(q\), allowing control inputs to produce arbitrary accelerations. Feedback linearization can then replace complicated nonlinear equations with simpler desired dynamics. A system is underactuated when this rank condition fails, meaning its inputs cannot accelerate it in every direction. Actuation status can depend on the system’s state because of torque limits, obstacles, or other constraints.

Using a two-link arm, Tedrake derives kinematics, kinetic and potential energy, and Lagrangian equations of motion. The resulting manipulator form is \(H(q)\ddot q+C(q,\dot q)\dot q+G(q)=Bu\), where \(H\) is symmetric and positive definite and \(B\) maps control inputs to joint torques. With a motor at every joint, the arm is fully actuated and can be made to behave like a simple or inverted pendulum through feedback linearization, although this assumes unlimited torque. Removing the shoulder motor makes the arm underactuated; this one-input system resembles the acrobot, whose elbow torque can be used to pump energy and swing upward.

Underactuation also arises when a robot cannot directly control its interaction with the environment. A compass-gait walker has no motor at its ground contact, and an airborne humanoid cannot alter its center-of-mass trajectory. Aircraft have restricted directions of motion, and manipulation before force closure is similarly not fully controllable. Tedrake argues that many difficult or unsolved robotics problems, including agile walking, flying, and manipulation, involve underactuated systems.

The planned course progresses from nonlinear pendulum dynamics and control to the cart-pole and acrobot, then to walking robots, impacts, limit cycles, higher-dimensional systems, uncertainty, stochasticity, and unknown models. It introduces analytical and numerical optimal control, dynamic programming, policy search combining reinforcement learning, machine learning, and numerical optimization, approximate policy search, randomized and feedback motion planning, and reinforcement-learning-based control.

Toronto and New York will face off in a best-of-five ALDS. In this MIT OpenCourseWare lecture, Tor developer and paper author Nick Mathewson describes Tor as a volunteer-run anonymity network. At the time, it had roughly 6,000 relay nodes and an estimated user base ranging from hundreds of thousands to millions. He cites uses by people seeking private search, research, political expression, or protection from harassment; by researchers seeking unbiased data; by companies protecting sensitive information; and by law enforcement avoiding disclosure of investigations. He also acknowledges criminal use and argues that banning effective security tools would leave people with less secure systems.

Mathewson distinguishes anonymity from unobservability and unlinkability. Anonymity means an observer cannot identify a particular person as the source of an activity, whether through categorical proof, probabilistic inference, or patterns across multiple actions. Unobservability hides the existence of the activity, while unlinkability prevents an observer from associating separate actions with the same person.

Tor’s design evolved from simple relay chains toward onion routing: traffic passes through a circuit of independently operated relays, with layered encryption and integrity protection. Clients negotiate keys, establish circuits through “create” and “extend” operations, and relay TCP-stream contents rather than raw IP packets. Applications retain end-to-end encryption, while Tor focuses on concealing network relationships. Most practical anonymity guarantees are probabilistic and depend on assumptions about attackers, traffic correlation, user volume, and other network conditions. The design prioritizes usefulness for interactive web browsing while maximizing security within that constraint.

Node discovery posed major security and scalability challenges. Hard-coded node lists were inflexible, ad hoc peer discovery allowed operators to supply fake nodes, and centralized directories created single points of failure. Tor therefore uses multiple hardened directory authorities that vote on active nodes, publish a signed consensus, and require clients to verify enough authority signatures. Nodes cache directories to prevent excessive load on authorities.

The lecture also covers path selection, application-level anonymity risks, abuse, hidden services, attacks, censorship resistance, and future work. Most protocols and web browsers can leak identifying or fingerprinting information, so Tor alone cannot prevent application-level deanonymization. Exit-node port restrictions reduce some risks but do not solve abuse, and IP-based blocking can exclude Tor users from online services. Proposed alternatives include unlinkable accounts and revocable credentials.

Hidden services provide responder anonymity by using rendezvous circuits and public-key-based introductions through a distributed directory. However, directory services can potentially enumerate hidden-service keys, motivating a proposed key-blinding redesign.

Discussed attacks include modification of unencrypted application traffic, traffic tagging between the first and last relays, denial-of-service techniques such as the sniper attack, and cryptographic implementation flaws. Against censorship, Tor uses bridges and pluggable transports that transform traffic to make blocking more difficult, though no current method is presented as categorically unblockable.

Planned work includes strengthening cryptography, revising hidden services and path selection, improving congestion control, scaling beyond the limits of centralized directories, exploring decentralized directory systems, and developing evidence-based padding and fake-traffic defenses against correlation attacks. Mathewson also points readers to related anonymity systems such as I2P, Gnunet, Mixmaster, Mixminion, DC-nets, and Freedom.

Education researchers are cautiously optimistic about the Institute of Education Sciences after deep DOGE-driven cuts, though severe staffing shortages remain. The Education Department plans to restore 20 of more than 100 terminated research contracts, modernize IES, update National Center for Education Statistics surveys and data collections, and resume the 10 regional education laboratories closed in February. Researcher Amber Northern is advising on IES reform, and new high-level National Assessment of Educational Progress positions are being filled.

One researcher rated IES’s condition at 3 or 4 on a 10-point scale, up from one a month earlier but far below its pre-cuts level. Officials are also considering performance- and outcomes-based contracting.

Concerns persist because NCES staffing fell from about 100 employees to three. NAEP faces reduced reporting capabilities and possible threats to sampling and other infrastructure after 2026. A presidential order requiring NCES to collect extensive historical admissions data also creates a major burden. Meanwhile, advocates for the regional laboratories cite successful state-level work and argue they could be restructured to better support teachers. Researchers broadly agree that federal education research and data are necessary, despite uncertainty about funding, staffing and the administration’s long-term plans.

**Summary**

Saving a penalty kick is among the most stressful tasks in soccer, with save chances generally under 15%; roughly 80% of penalties are scored and about 5% missed, and the laws favor attackers. Law 14 of the IFAB Laws of the Game governs the procedure: a penalty is awarded for a direct-free-kick offense inside the defender's penalty area; it is a restart of play taken from the penalty mark 12 yards from goal; the ball must be stationary on the mark, the goal frame must not move, the kicker must be identified, and the goalkeeper must remain between the posts facing the kicker until the ball is kicked, without unfairly distracting the kicker. All other players must be at least 10 yards from the mark, behind it, in play, and outside the penalty area. The ball is in play once kicked and clearly moving; the keeper must have a foot touching, in line with, or behind the goal line; the kicker cannot touch the ball again until another player does. If the keeper violates procedure, a goal is awarded, or the kick is retaken if the violation affected the kicker or prevented the ball entering the goal, with warnings for a first offense and cautions thereafter.

Coaches should prepare goalkeepers explicitly, support them fully, publicly state that teammates will not blame them for a failed save, have all players acknowledge this, and train keepers in both regular practices and dedicated one-on-one sessions. Coaches must not instruct keepers at the moment of a penalty, only offer encouragement; never suggest it is acceptable not to save. Because up to 39% of penalty goals are scored up the middle, "guess and go" has largely given way to "read and react." Goalkeepers should stay put, learn kicking tendencies, practice but not over-train, use properly fitted gloves and landing pads, verbalize "right" and "left" clearly, and watch team penalties from behind the goal without pressure to develop cue-reading. Right-foot dominant players typically drive with that foot to their left (the keeper's right); youth kicks are often poorly taken and should still be reacted to. At the highest level, coaches and keepers must decide between reacting and guessing, using subtle cues such as approach, stance, weight, and gaze (as former U.S. national team goalkeeper Brad Friedel described).

Training addresses psychological, mental, and physical preparation. Three psychological qualities are required: an absolute desire to stop the kick, focus without fear, and the ability to dismiss the result and continue playing; some are innate and some learned. Mental techniques include visualization, positive self-talk ("I've got this"), a consistent pre-shot routine ("wait, watch, react"), controlled breathing (4-4-4-4), staying present, trusting instincts, and avoiding dwelling on outcomes; pressure should be perceived as entirely on the kicker. Physical preparation requires special work to reach coverable areas quickly, plus proper clothing, cleats, and gloves.

Research is central: keepers should watch teammates and opponents, use video, attend camps, read books, and keep notes on kickers' dominant foot, position, preferred targets, and reliable cues. Cues include ball placement on the mark, angle of approach (wide signals the opposite side, narrow the same side), run-up length and shape, plant-foot toe point, hip orientation and hip drop, chin direction, body lean, dominant leg, and kneecap position. Keepers should focus on the few cues that work for them.

During the kick, keepers should maintain a calm routine and composure, keep respect toward teammates including the player who conceded, identify the true middle of the goal line (using a tape measure or turf scuff mark), and never lose focus on the ball. Rattling the kicker (swaying, jumping, star jumping, loose legs, pointing, talking, pacing along the line) may be used but must stay within the Law, since referees watch pre-kick behavior. Keepers should assume a coiled ready position with one foot on the line, resist action bias and fakes, stay put against stutter runs, read cues just before the strike, then react quickly and dive with a full stretch. Low dives should move outward, parallel and close to the ground, not toward the post; two-handed catches are preferred, otherwise push the ball wide or beyond the goal line for a corner.

After the kick, keepers must respond without emotion: retrieve a conceded goal matter-of-factly, reposition for goal kicks or corners after misses or deflections, return instantly to their feet for possible rebounds, scramble for possession of shots still heading goalward, and start a fast break rather than celebrating after a save, remembering the eight-second release rule. Teammates must not mob the keeper after a save — an anecdote about a U-15 team conceding a second penalty after a celebrating teammate dislodged the ball is cited, as is a similar incident involving U.S. goalkeeper Alyssa Naeher.

At the highest levels, keepers should keep current files on opponents' penalty histories, tendencies, and last five kicks, while recognizing that elite takers will adapt; absent a substantial pattern, keepers should trust their instincts. Coaches should read and apply Law 14, related penalty-kick materials, and shoot-out guidance, ensure defenders cover rebounds and outlets exist, and note that under Law 3 a player may swap with the goalkeeper after a penalty is awarded but before it is taken, even without injury. Keepers also need special reaction, jumping, diving, and footwork training, adjustments for slippery conditions, and constant positive reinforcement. Because "rattling" sits on a fine line, coaches should support only acceptable techniques. Referees are watching for early departures from the goal line (a save results in a retake); this is generally impermissible at youth level but treated as a gray area at elite levels. Recent studies indicate standing about four inches off center makes one side appear larger, prompting up to 10% of takers to aim at that side and raising the chance of a shot to the larger side by roughly 4%.

The speaker credits an early power-play goal—after a shot deflected and Khabibulin scored from the far side of the net—with building the team’s confidence and momentum.
