Serious medical problems were defined as life-threatening, requiring hospital care, or causing lasting problems. In Phase 1, two participants had serious problems between Dose 1 and six months after Dose 2—one each in the 20-µg and 30-µg BNT162b2 groups (4% each). Researchers did not consider these vaccine-related, and no serious problems occurred in the BNT162b1 or placebo groups. In Phase 2/3, no single serious problem affected at least 1% of any group. After two 30-µg BNT162b2 doses, three vaccine recipients aged 16 or older and three initial placebo recipients who later received the vaccine each had one temporary event considered possibly vaccine-related. Four of 324 BNT162b2SA recipients (1%) had serious problems, none considered vaccine-related. After a 30-µg booster, 65 of 22,470 participants (<1%) had serious problems; two events in participants aged 16 or older were considered possibly vaccine-related. One participant had a serious problem after an additional booster. Few serious problems followed Phase 3 30-µg boosters or 5/10-µg boosters, and none were considered vaccine-related.

The coach said his team started strongly but lost momentum in the second period by standing around and failing to counter effectively, while noting the opponent remained dangerous in overtime. He praised a player’s production, defensive awareness, conditioning, recovery, and ability to handle heavy minutes. He said the six-period game provided a good assessment and that line rotations became more comfortable as play continued. He emphasized that each game differs, the team must improve against a strong opponent, and an opposing line had been highly effective. The team was pleased with how it exited and felt its playoff momentum and home-ice advantage were significant, while stressing the need to start positively and remain even-keeled. He cited emotional wins over Detroit and Los Angeles, noted Boston’s greater playoff experience, and expected low-scoring, tightly controlled games. With rest available, the focus was on the next game and distributing minutes as needed.

The message laid before Congress documents a boundary dispute in the Aroostook River territory. Unauthorized trespassers, chiefly from British provinces, cut and destroyed timber in territory claimed by Maine. After Maine’s land agent and two citizens were captured and taken to New Brunswick, Maine authorized an armed posse to disperse the trespassers and protect the timber. New Brunswick demanded Maine’s recall and warned that British troops would support its authority, but Maine refused and the United States denied any agreement granting Great Britain exclusive jurisdiction.

Both governments had previously restrained conflicting activities to avoid confrontation, including suspending land sales, road construction, timber licenses, and railroad surveys. The message distinguished Maine’s efforts to stop depredations from a military occupation intended to hold the territory by force. It favored continued amicable settlement through arbitration, a commission with an umpire, or submission to a third power. If New Brunswick attempted to enforce jurisdiction through military occupation, Maine could request federal assistance to repel invasion. The message expected the detained agents to be released, recommended that Maine disband its militia, and asked Congress to consider measures that might prevent an extra session.

From 1950–2022, the S&P 500 set 1,526 all-time highs—about 21 per year and 8.3% of trading days—while compounding at 7.67% annually before dividends. All-time highs can reflect strong business activity, earnings, momentum, bullish sentiment, and investor FOMO, though inflation can distort nominal gains. An all-time-high strategy buys the S&P 500 when it is less than 5% below its peak and sells when it falls more than 5% below. Its backtest produced a 3.20% CAGR, 7.40% risk-adjusted return, 33.75% maximum drawdown, and 43.2% time invested. Earning 3% annually on cash during periods outside the market substantially improved the strategy, highlighting the importance of diversifying cash holdings.

Priority applications identified in the application data sheet are incorporated by reference. The disclosure describes respiratory mask systems for delivering CPAP, NIV, and other respiratory therapies. A mask interface may include a seal supported by a frame, a gas inlet connected to a gas conduit, an outlet vent, and an optional diffuser. Seals may cover the mouth, nose, or both, include nasal pillows, or form a non-sealing nasal cannula interface. Seals can attach to frame flanges through lips, inner and outer clips, dividers, hooks, projections, recesses, and snap-fit engagement.

The frame may include a longitudinal channel that receives a headgear yoke. The channel and yoke can provide alignment, venting, and attachment through friction, textile coverings, locating members, magnets, tabs, latches, snap-fit structures, tongues, and anti-rotation grooves. The yoke may have a tapered middle, flared side portions, a stretchable textile covering, hooks, posts, alignment features, and complementary frame attachments. It may also include line tracks, end caps, washer housings, and directional locks for automatically adjustable headgear using straps that extend behind, over, and along the sides of a patient’s head.

Additional embodiments describe a nasal seal with supporting nasal prongs, a shallow bridge, specified depth, width, height, wall-thickness, and sealing-area limits, a generally D-shaped inlet, and a removable clip assembly defining the inlet and a diffuser-equipped vent. Figures depict masks, seals, frames, yokes, attachment mechanisms, and comparisons with a prior-art seal.

The passage defines mean reversion as prices tending to move back above or below a moving average after abnormal rises or falls. Mean-reversion strategies typically have a high win rate, many small gains, and occasional large losses, unlike trend-following strategies, which rely on fewer but larger winners. They tend to work best in stocks and less effectively in markets such as commodities. Proposed reasons include futures-related arbitrage and continued competition between buyers and sellers.

The article says mean reversion has historically performed especially well in bear markets because volatility and explosive rallies create opportunities to buy weakness and sell strength. During the S&P 500’s roughly 50% decline from May 2008 to early March 2009, there were 99 up days and 104 down days, but the average up day was 1.79%, compared with an average down day of −2.32%. These conditions reportedly made shorting difficult while favoring long mean-reversion trades.

Three revised strategies are presented: a deviation-from-recent-high strategy in consumer-staples ETF XLP, an IBS short strategy in the Chinese ETF FXI, and a five-day-low strategy for the S&P 500. The article reports equity curves for $100,000 invested or shorted and compounded over different historical periods. It cautions that the S&P 500 strategy might also apply to futures, but warns about drawdown and leverage.

The passage describes systems integrating optically switchable windows, particularly electrochromic windows, with building communications, sensing, and control infrastructure. Electrochromic windows change optical properties such as color, transmittance, absorbance, and reflectance when voltage is applied; reversing voltage polarity lightens the window. Such windows can control solar energy, light, privacy, and occupant comfort. Tungsten oxide is identified as a cathodic electrochromic material, and the disclosed concepts may also apply to liquid-crystal and suspended-particle devices.

Embodiments describe high-speed building networks in which trunk-line segments are coupled in daisy-chain configurations through passive circuits such as bias Tees and directional couplers. The trunk lines may use coaxial, twisted-pair, or twinax cabling, while signals may include data exceeding 1 Gbps, TCP/IP traffic, wireless or 5G communications, and power signals. Networks can connect control panels, conventional or enhanced window controllers, windows, building-management systems, and devices including IoT equipment, sensors, antennas, microphones, speakers, and microprocessors. Coaxial links may use MoCA bonding to aggregate channels, CAN networks may carry window-control traffic, and gigabit Ethernet, optical fiber, or high-bandwidth wireless links may connect control panels and digital elements. Control panels can provide switching and routing and form a backbone linked to external or cloud networks.

Digital architectural elements, including digital mullions, can be attached to or incorporated into structural elements such as walls, partitions, doors, beams, façades, and windows. Digital wall interfaces provide similar capabilities in wall- or door-mounted housings. These devices may include processors, high-bandwidth network interfaces, displays, speakers, microphones, cameras, proximity, occupancy, motion, biometric, color-temperature, temperature, humidity, and air-quality sensors, along with Wi-Fi, cellular, Bluetooth, and other wireless interfaces. They may also include antennas, audio-processing logic, displays or projectors, connectors, batteries, capacitors, photovoltaic harvesting components, and status lights.

The disclosed systems support distributed environmental monitoring and automatic control of HVAC, lighting, security, and window tinting using sensor measurements, occupancy information, schedules, weather, and building-layout context. Algorithms or machine-learning models may react to measured conditions or anticipate changes to improve comfort, safety, and energy efficiency. Applications include tenant internet and computing services, construction information, environmental adjustment, glare and color management, media delivery, public-address communication, video collaboration, noise cancellation, personalization, and support for personal digital assistants.

Security implementations may detect sounds, movement, glass damage, and unauthorized activity, trigger alarms or emergency calls, locate sound sources, and change nearby windows to distinctive tint states to assist responders. The specification also states that a concurrently filed Application Data Sheet and the identified priority applications are incorporated by reference in their entirety.

Witting said Finland’s 1940 attempt to secure a Finnish-Swedish common defense agreement failed because of Swedish timidity and Soviet objections. He considered the Soviet objection shortsighted, since the agreement might have kept both countries neutral. Soviet troop and matériel buildup reinforced Finnish fears of renewed attack and made the Finnish-German transit agreement a major relief. He attributed continued fighting largely to Soviet offensive tactics, noting recent Russian losses near Poventsa.

Witting said Finland did not seek involvement in a wider war, but its dependence on German supplies and geographic position left it little practical freedom of action. He believed Finland would not voluntarily act against the Anti-Axis powers, yet military circumstances and uncontrollable events made peace with the Soviet Union or a cessation of fighting unlikely. He also doubted Sweden could influence Finland.

The Swedish diplomat’s contacts likewise indicated that Finnish leaders neither could nor desired peace with the USSR. Social Democratic and Swedish Party support for ending hostilities lacked effective leadership, while Westman feared discussing it with Witting could trigger German displeasure. Finnish representatives also promoted Finland’s annexation policy to visiting Swedish editors by circulating Professor Jaakkola’s book.

This prospective cohort study used data from the Amsterdam Born Children and their Development study to examine whether multidimensional unintended pregnancy—mistiming, unwantedness, and unhappiness—was associated with children’s psychosocial problems through adolescence. The analytic sample included 7,784 mothers and children assessed during pregnancy and at ages 5–6, 11–12, and 15–16. Structural equation models accounted for maternal and family risk factors and assessed maternal mental health and bonding as potential mediators.

After adjustment, pregnancy mistiming was associated with more internalizing and externalizing problems at preschool age, while unwanted pregnancy was associated with internalizing problems; pregnancy unhappiness was not significantly associated with either outcome. No significant adjusted associations were found during early or middle adolescence. At preschool age, maternal bonding problems mediated associations between all dimensions of unintended pregnancy and both types of child psychosocial problems. Maternal psychosocial distress mediated only the associations between mistiming and internalizing and externalizing problems. Some direct associations between mistiming or unwantedness and internalizing problems remained.

The authors concluded that maternal mental health and bonding were more important contributors to young children’s psychosocial problems than unintended pregnancy itself, supporting greater attention to these factors. Limitations included possible selection bias from dropout, reliance primarily on maternal reports, and the exclusion of pregnancies ending in abortion.

The application discloses an active organic light-emitting display device with a substrate containing a display area, non-display areas, and a through portion surrounded by pixels. Scan and data lines supply signals to the matrix-arranged pixels, while first and second scan drivers positioned on opposite sides may perform synchronized dual scanning. Data lines adjacent to the through portion curve along its perimeter and may occupy alternating layers, with straight and curved portions connected through contacts, reducing data-line pitch, parasitic capacitance, and the surrounding non-display area while limiting overlap. Various embodiments place portions of the data lines in different layers or use materials matching pixel electrodes, transistor electrodes, or capacitor electrodes to reduce manufacturing masks. A thin-film encapsulation layer with inorganic and organic layers covers the substrate and defines the through portion. A dam blocks organic material flow toward the through portion, and adjacent inorganic layers directly contact to improve moisture resistance. Inorganic or organic-inorganic composite passivation layers may cover the curved data lines while preserving barrier performance. The display may be incorporated into mobile phones, smartwatches, and vehicle dashboards, with cameras, buttons, or driving indicators positioned in the through portions.

In a University of Michigan commencement address, the speaker argues that America must use its material abundance to build a “Great Society” based on liberty, equality, and the pursuit of happiness. The Great Society requires ending poverty and racial injustice, expanding education, improving communities, protecting natural beauty, and ensuring that economic progress enriches national and spiritual life. He stresses that it is a continuing challenge, not a completed goal.

He identifies three priorities. First, American cities must be rebuilt to provide adequate housing and transportation, preserve open land and landmarks, and support community life as urban populations expand. Second, the countryside must be protected from pollution, overcrowding, and the loss of parks, forests, and natural landscapes. Third, classrooms must provide every child with qualified teachers, adequate facilities, and excellent education. He cites widespread educational deficiencies, overcrowded classes, outdated curricula, unaffordable college attendance, and the need for better teacher training and innovative teaching methods.

The speaker says the government does not yet have full solutions but will draw on broad knowledge, establish working groups and White House conferences, and encourage “creative federalism” between national and local authorities. He calls on students to pursue equal citizenship, an escape from poverty, enduring peace among nations, and a society in which material progress supports a richer life of mind and spirit.

The Box and One combines a 1-2-2 baseline zone with a 2-3 outside zone and an aggressive chaser assigned to deny a star opponent the ball. X4 and X5 shift according to 1-2-2 baseline principles, while X1 and X2 adjust according to 2-3 zone principles. Against even- or odd-front offenses, defenders deny passes, force ball handlers toward the sideline or baseline, protect the low post, close out, and position for rebounds. The chaser maintains strong pass denial and receives support against penetration if their opponent gains possession. Effective denial can prevent the star scorer from receiving the ball and disrupt the opponent’s set plays and continuity.

The article demonstrates a simple trading-strategy backtest in Python using pandas, yfinance, and matplotlib. Historical daily price data for SPY is downloaded from Yahoo Finance, and simple and exponential moving averages are calculated with pandas. The first 200 rows are removed because moving-average values are initially unavailable.

A loop assigns a regime value of 1 when SPY’s closing price is above both moving averages and 0 otherwise; the signal is recorded in the following row because it is triggered at the close. Daily SPY returns are calculated with `pct_change()`, compounded only when the regime is 1, and plotted with matplotlib. The strategy’s accumulated return is 804.82%, versus 1,505.31% for buy and hold, so it underperforms. The article concludes that Python makes strategy backtesting accessible without requiring finance or computer-science degrees.

The passage defines AMD Seamless Firmware Servicing (SFS) requirements and update procedures. Customers must provide an RSA public key during early SMM setup, before BOOT_DONE, for package verification; it cannot be changed afterward. For customer co-signing, the customer generates a 2048- or 4096-bit RSA key pair and signs the AMD package using RSA-PSS with SHA-256 or SHA-384, respectively, following the specified RSA token format. Customer co-signing is optional, while the AMD signature is mandatory.

Executable patches check applicable system patch levels and firmware versions. They can modify registers or values, replace complete firmware images, or update portions of firmware packages. Each package must ensure that dependent firmware versions are present and must not apply if any portion cannot be fully updated. Patches are nonpersistent across warm or cold reboots and may be applied during OS boot, immediately after boot, or during normal operation.

SEV updates are automatically committed and prevent rollback; reverting an updated SEV image requires a reboot. When SNP is enabled, update pages must be HV-FIXED using RMPUPDATE. Attestation data should be requested through sideband/SPDM or in-band/DPE interfaces, with SFS providing required measurements. SFS does not modify firmware components protected by certain attestation schemes.

A deployment agent creates a 4 KB TEE_EXT_CMD_BUFFER within a 2 MB-aligned region, appends the update package and optional co-signing data, and submits it through the TEE mailbox. ASP protects the buffer from x86 access, verifies the customer signature when provided, verifies the AMD signature, executes the validated patch, updates patch-level information, and returns status. Separate commands retrieve firmware-version information or apply an update package.

SFS packages align with AGESA releases and use names such as `fam_19h-1006-SFS-1.pkg`. Released packages must match the specific combination of firmware and patch levels on the target system. Updates run alongside x86 and DMA traffic and are designed to minimize performance impact; SEV/ES virtual machines must stop and restart for SEV firmware updates, while SEV/SNP virtual machines can continue operating.

Dane Gudauskas described paddling into a huge left at Cloudbreak during an XXL Fiji swell. Inspired by the rare conditions, he caught a powerful wave despite worsening weather, limited visibility, and the risk of being caught inside. Amazon.com, Inc.’s unaudited Form 10-Q for the quarter ended September 30, 2022 reported Q3 net sales of $127.1 billion, up from $110.8 billion a year earlier. Operating income declined to $2.5 billion from $4.9 billion, while net income was $2.9 billion versus $3.2 billion. For the first nine months, sales rose to $364.8 billion from $332.4 billion, operating income fell to $9.5 billion from $21.4 billion, and the company reported a $3.0 billion net loss versus $19.0 billion of net income. A $10.4 billion nine-month valuation loss on Amazon’s Rivian investment was the primary factor behind the $13.4 billion decline in other income.

North America Q3 sales increased 20% to $78.8 billion, but the segment recorded a $412 million operating loss. International sales fell 5% to $27.7 billion, with a $2.5 billion operating loss. AWS sales rose 27% to $20.5 billion, and operating income increased to $5.4 billion from $4.9 billion. Foreign-exchange changes reduced consolidated sales by $5.0 billion in Q3 and $10.5 billion for the nine months.

Cash, cash equivalents, and marketable securities totaled $58.7 billion at September 30, down from $96.0 billion at year-end. Operating cash flow was $11.4 billion for Q3 and $17.6 billion for the nine months, while cash capital expenditures reached $42.9 billion for the nine months. Total assets were $428.4 billion, stockholders’ equity was $137.5 billion, and long-term debt was $58.9 billion.

Amazon effected a 20-for-1 stock split on May 27, 2022. Effective January 1, it extended server useful lives from four to five years and networking-equipment useful lives from five to six years, reducing Q3 depreciation and amortization by $882 million and benefiting net income by $665 million. Amazon acquired MGM Holdings in March for approximately $6.1 billion, net of acquired cash, and entered agreements to acquire One Medical for approximately $3.9 billion and iRobot for approximately $1.7 billion, both expected to be funded with cash on hand.

The company repurchased $6.0 billion of stock during the nine months, leaving $6.1 billion under its authorization. Debt disclosures included $62.5 billion of unsecured senior notes, $11.7 billion of commercial-paper borrowings, and no borrowings under its $10 billion unsecured revolving credit facility. Amazon also disclosed $275.8 billion of contractual commitments, continuing antitrust and patent litigation, tax contingencies, and risks from inflation, supply-chain constraints, higher transportation and labor costs, and foreign-exchange movements.

Augustine Heard reported that Seoul remained quiet after April 20 and that the USS Alert was sent away from Chemulpo. Although rumors of Tong Hâk disturbances persisted, investigators found no evidence of mass gatherings, and Catholic priests corroborated their accounts. Heard nevertheless expected recurring rumors amid widespread discontent caused by officials’ exactions.

In early May, reports said thousands of Tong Hâk had assembled at Po-eun, were drilling, and intended to march on Seoul. Their anti-foreign flags caused alarm and prompted the government to send 800 European-trained soldiers with three Gatling guns to Suwen. Heard considered the Tong Hâk unlikely to be dangerous, though possibly controlled by a political party and joined by discontented, impoverished people. He saw greater potential danger from urban mobs and advised delaying the Alert’s departure despite Admiral Harmony’s order that it leave.

India’s pharmaceutical industry expanded rapidly after 1970, when patent rules permitted generic reproduction and government price controls shaped the domestic market. By 2001, more than 20,000 pharmaceutical companies operated in India, while global drug companies increasingly outsourced research, clinical trials, and manufacturing to reduce costs and accelerate development. India attracted outsourcing because of its educated, English-speaking, relatively inexpensive workforce, genetic diversity, government biotechnology support, and expanding CRO sector.

Biocon India was founded in 1978 as a joint venture to manufacture enzymes. After becoming independent from Unilever in 1998, it developed and patented the PlaFractor fermentation reactor, entered the global generic-statin market in 1997, and established Syngene in 1994. Syngene became the first Indian CRO serving international pharmaceutical and biotechnology companies in synthetic chemistry, molecular biology, and informatics. By early 2003, Biocon had 800 employees and annual revenue of US$75 million. Its culture emphasized openness, trust, collaboration, accessibility, limited hierarchy, and team-based performance rewards.

Biocon launched Clinigene in 2000 to add clinical-trial capabilities and develop a fully integrated drug discovery and business model. Clinigene initially concentrated on laboratory services, bioequivalence and bioavailability studies, and hospital partnerships. It faced strong market potential but also concerns about differentiation, resource demands, cultural integration, ethics, and reputation. Rapid growth could divert resources from the parent company, overshadow Biocon and Syngene, and weaken their collaborative culture because Clinigene personnel would work at dispersed hospital sites. Clinical trials also carried financial, ethical, consent, and political risks, especially when conducted in poorer patient populations for Western markets.

Clinigene occupied the lower- to medium-value CRO segment, while foreign competitors and pharmaceutical companies focused on more profitable data management and Phase III trials. Moving upward would require substantial financial and cultural investment. Biocon could therefore pursue aggressive Clinigene growth, restrict it temporarily to safer lower-value services until Syngene had molecules ready for testing, or acquire an established clinical-services CRO. The central challenge was to expand without sacrificing Biocon’s core capabilities and culture.

The crude oil “Friday seasonality” strategy buys at Thursday’s close to seek a Friday price increase. Historical analysis from April 2006 to the present showed a 56.96% P/L across 98 trades, including 60 winners, with an average profit of 0.58% per trade. Buying on every Thursday is not recommended; the strategy performs better when Thursday is down, particularly when USO falls by at least 0.75 times its 25-day average high-minus-low range. Other weekdays appeared more random.
The shared #HV doorbell page defines a 16-bit PendingEvent field and a NoEoiRequired byte; bytes 3–63 are reserved. Its backing page must be host-owned, and guest accesses require C=0.

The ADS8681W, ADS8685W, and ADS8689W are single-channel, 16-bit SAR data-acquisition devices for bipolar differential or single-ended inputs. They operate from a 5 V analog supply, support input ranges up to ±12.288 V, and use an enhanced multiSPI interface for high-throughput data transfer with slower host controllers.

The integrated analog front end includes high-impedance inputs of at least 1 MΩ, a programmable gain amplifier with nine unipolar or bipolar ranges, a second-order antialiasing low-pass filter, an ADC driver, and input overvoltage protection. With a 4.096 V reference, the bipolar ranges are ±12.288, ±10.24, ±6.144, ±5.12, and ±2.56 V; unipolar ranges are 0–12.288, 0–10.24, 0–6.144, and 0–5.12 V. Input-path impedances should be matched for DC accuracy. Floating inputs produce invalid ADC data but do not damage the device. The internal protection withstands inputs up to ±20 V when powered and ±15 V when AVDD is floating; external protection is recommended for surges, ESD, and EFT events.

The PGA gain and input range are selected through the RANGE_SEL_REG register. The antialiasing filter typically has a 500 kHz −3 dB cutoff. The integrated high-bandwidth ADC driver enables rapid settling at maximum sampling rates. The internal 4.096 V reference is factory-trimmed and temperature compensated, although solder-reflow stress can shift its value. The device also accepts an external 4.096 V reference through REFIO; required reference and supply decoupling capacitors are specified.

The ADC uses a straight-binary transfer function, with LSB size equal to the full-scale range divided by 65,536. Alarm features include programmable high- and low-input thresholds with hysteresis and fixed AVDD thresholds of 4.7 V and 5.3 V. Active and tripped alarm flags are available through ALARM_REG, the ALARM output pin, or appended output flags.

The multiSPI interface supports standard SPI protocols, single- or dual-SDO output, and source-synchronous operation using either an external or internal clock. It supports single devices and daisy-chained configurations; an N-device chain requires an optimal transfer frame of 32 × N SCLK capture edges. Each data-transfer frame begins on the falling edge of CONVST/CS and ends on its rising edge, which starts conversion. A 32-clock frame is required for a valid write, short frames are treated as NOPs, and in longer frames the final 32 shifted bits form the command.

The device operates in RESET, ACQ, and CONV states. Reset can be configured as an application reset or full power-on reset. The host can monitor RVS to determine conversion completion. Data writes and reads use 32-bit command frames, and output data can include device address, range, alarm, and parity flags. Nine configuration registers control identification, reset and power, SPI configuration, output protocols, data formatting, input range and reference selection, and alarms.

An example industrial input module combines an ADS8681W with an eight-channel MUX36D08 differential multiplexer to support software-configured voltage or current channels with fast settling. The device uses separate AVDD and DVDD supplies, supports NAP and power-down modes, and requires specified supply and reference decoupling. Recommended PCB layout separates analog and digital circuitry, uses close-coupled bypass capacitors, avoids vias between supply pins and capacitors, and connects grounds through short, low-impedance paths.

Kennedy was ticketed for speeding and cited for marijuana possession and drug paraphernalia. Preston faced minor alcohol possession and forgery charges after using a fake license. Police destroyed 75 pounds of prescription drugs, cited three children for trespassing, and investigated a smashed mailbox. Total calls: 204.

The address portrays the United States as exceptionally prosperous, with rapid national and state growth, expanding settlement, a growing domestic-born population, and flourishing agriculture, commerce, manufacturing, and navigation. Differences in climate and industry are described as complementary, creating an expanding national market, while the division of authority between state and national governments is said to unite the states rather than divide them.

Foreign relations are generally friendly, and the administration emphasizes reciprocity, candid negotiation, and permanent relations. The 1822 U.S.-French commercial convention remains in force, though claims for wartime spoliations remain unsettled, and a comprehensive negotiation is anticipated following the accession of France’s new king. U.S.-British trade remains governed by the conventions of 1815 and 1818, but West Indian trade has not been arranged satisfactorily. Progress has been made on several boundary disputes; the sixth article of the Treaty of Ghent has been established, the fifth is under amicable negotiation, and the seventh is expected to be settled within the coming year. No final arrangement has been made with Britain to suppress the slave trade. The United States rejected a reciprocal right of search and proposed instead that participation in the trade be treated as piracy. A convention to that effect was signed in London on March 13, 1824, but ratification obstacles led the administration to suspend further action until Congress expressed its views.

Sweden has a reciprocal commercial treaty, while Russia, the Netherlands, Prussia, the free Hanseatic cities, Oldenburg, and Sardinia have reciprocal arrangements based on mutual agreement. A convention concerning the Northwest coast and adjoining seas was signed at St. Petersburg on April 5 and submitted to the Senate for ratification. Political changes in Spain and Portugal have delayed some negotiations. Brazil has established a new imperial government, and the United States expects Portugal soon to recognize its independence. Relations with Colombia, Chile, Guatemala, Buenos Aires, Mexico, and other South American states remain friendly, and commercial ties are expanding. Negotiations over neutral and belligerent rights in maritime war have begun but have not produced treaties. Claims for indemnification against European powers remain outstanding except with Spain.

The administration reports projected Treasury receipts exceeding $18.5 million and a balance of more than $3 million after current expenses, interest, and more than $11.6 million in debt principal are paid. Two loans of $5 million each, both at 4.5 percent, were authorized to meet war debt obligations and awards under the Florida treaty. Citizens’ spoliation claims were promptly paid, with repayment expected from the sale of Florida lands. Total public debt is estimated at $86 million, or approximately $79 million excluding the government’s Bank of the United States stock, and could be discharged within ten years if no unexpected event occurs. The government’s credit and available funds are described as favorable for reducing interest rates.

The Army is reported well organized, disciplined, and professionally improved, with the military academy considered essential to that condition. Because the dispersed artillery corps hindered training, eleven companies were assembled at Old Point Comfort as an artillery school, and congressional assistance was requested. Fortifications, navigation improvements, and surveys for nationally important roads and canals were progressing. A board of military and civil engineers was examining routes between major rivers, lakes, and coastal areas, and Congress was asked to enlarge both the military and topographical engineer corps.

American naval forces were maintained in the Mediterranean, Gulf of Mexico, and adjacent waters, while the increasing Pacific commerce created a need for further attention and protection. The North Carolina was being sent to reinforce the Mediterranean squadron. Anti-piracy efforts in the Gulf had protected commerce but had not suppressed the practice, leading the administration to favor increasing the force there. A military post near the mouth of the Columbia River and exploration of the adjacent coast were recommended to protect commerce and fisheries, support naval operations, improve western trade, and encourage peace with northwestern tribes. Post Office receipts were expected to exceed expenditures despite increased mail transportation.

Relations with most Indian tribes remained friendly, and thirty-two schools serving 916 students had been established under congressional appropriations. Certain tribes on the Missouri, Upper Mississippi, and Upper Lakes continued hostile attacks and murders. Treaty negotiations and military escorts had been delayed but were being prepared for the next season, alongside efforts to end conflicts among tribes. Negotiations with the Creeks and Quaupaw were pending. The administration proposed dividing territory between the current states and territories and the Rocky Mountains and Mexico into districts, establishing civil governments and schools there, and encouraging tribes to relocate gradually as part of a policy of civilization.

The expansion of the Union had made the existing judicial structure, designed for the original thirteen states, increasingly impractical. The Supreme Court’s judges were urged to devote themselves exclusively to their highest duties, with the lower courts reorganized accordingly. Improvements to public buildings and grounds in Washington and completion of the canal from the Tiber to the Eastern Branch were also proposed.

General Lafayette’s visit was welcomed throughout the country, and Congress was asked to provide him a gift recognizing his Revolutionary service and sacrifices. In Europe, the United States supported Greece against Turkey and the independence of Spain’s former American colonies while declining to interfere in their establishment of governments. The address concluded that preserving national institutions, strengthening fortifications and the Navy, improving internal transportation, and maintaining harmony between state and federal governments were essential to continued prosperity, and ended with the speaker’s gratitude for public confidence and support.

Mali’s gold exports fell from 70 tonnes in 2015 to 67 tonnes in 2016 as production barely increased and legacy mines declined. Morila is scheduled to close in 2019, Yatela is closed, and no new mines were slated to begin production until 2018, making Sadiola critical to maintaining output, government revenue, employment and Mali’s standing among Africa’s leading gold producers.

Sadiola’s soft-rock reserves are nearing depletion, reducing production from 600,000 ounces in 2000 to under 200,000. IAMGOLD and AngloGold Ashanti, each holding 41%, with Mali holding 18%, seek approval for a roughly $380 million plant conversion to process 3.4 million ounces of proven and probable hard-rock reserves, potentially extending the mine’s life by at least a decade. Government negotiations have stalled amid political uncertainty ahead of the 2018 election, putting the investment at risk.

Gold provides about 25–30% of government revenue, while Sadiola supports around 1,000 jobs, mostly held by Malians. Expansion would require new infrastructure, including a connection to the power grid, and could improve services for surrounding communities. IAMGOLD remains committed to Mali but did not comment on reports of a possible deadlock.

NVIDIA RTX IO accelerates game asset loading and streaming by working with Microsoft’s upcoming DirectStorage API and using GPU-based lossless decompression. Compressed data can move directly from NVMe storage to the GPU for decompression, reducing CPU work, improving I/O performance, shortening load times, reducing pop-in and stutter, and enabling high-quality texture streaming. It also reduces download and install sizes and can accelerate professional workflows involving large CAD, scientific, rendering, and virtual-reality datasets.

The GA10x Ampere architecture adds second-generation RT Cores, third-generation Tensor Cores with structural sparsity, and improvements to programmable shading, ray tracing, and AI. The RTX 3090 supports GDDR6X memory with up to 19.5 Gbps data rates and 936 GB/s peak bandwidth, while the RTX 3070 uses GDDR6, lacks NVLink, and is described as faster than the previous RTX 2080 Ti.

The NVIDIA A40 targets data-center visual computing, offering higher FP32, ray-tracing, and AI throughput than the Quadro RTX 6000, PCIe Gen4 bandwidth, and 48 GB of memory expandable to 96 GB through two GPUs with NVLink. It supports virtualization, Quadro Sync, multiple display outputs, and the NVIDIA EGX Platform.

Ampere GPUs support 4K120 and 8K60 displays, DisplayPort 1.4a, HDMI 2.1 with up to 48 Gbps bandwidth and dynamic HDR, and HDCP 2.3 and 1.x. Fifth-generation NVDEC provides hardware decoding for MPEG-2, VC-1, H.264, H.265, VP8, VP9, and AV1, including up to 8K60 HDR AV1 playback with low CPU usage. Seventh-generation NVENC offloads encoding from the CPU, supports low-latency and low-power streaming, and handles up to 4K H.264 or 8K HEVC.

The RTX A6000 provides a GA102 GPU, 48 GB of GDDR6 memory expandable to 96 GB through two NVLink-connected boards, hardware-accelerated motion blur and AI denoising, and professional rendering, simulation, deep-learning, and virtual-workstation capabilities.

GDDR6X-equipped GA10x GPUs also include Error Detection and Replay, which detects faulty memory transmissions and retries them until successful. The resulting bandwidth reduction indicates when memory overclocking has reached its practical limit, although continued overclocking can still cause crashes.

The disclosure describes portable ground stations for vertical-takeoff aerial vehicles. Each station includes a protective casing, charging mechanism, and landing pad that transitions between a compact closed configuration and an extended open configuration. An elevator raises and lowers a base platform, while retractable side extensions and bridging lobes enlarge the landing area; closing side flaps can center an off-center vehicle. Charging terminals conductively couple with corresponding vehicle elements, using power from sources such as electrochemical cells, fuel cells, photovoltaic panels, wind turbines, or mains power. Optional features include visual or beacon-based homing aids, wind protection, weather sensing, transport and suspension modules, carrying equipment, batteries, communications, radar, sensors, and night-vision modules. Multiple networked ground stations can support multiple vehicles, extend operating range, and enable continuous operation, potentially without downtime. The disclosed methods involve deploying stations, extending their landing pads, landing and centering aerial vehicles, retracting the vehicles into their casings, and charging them.

The study reports cryogenic near-infrared laboratory spectra of grain mixtures of water ice, epsomite, and halite to support future compositional analyses of Europa using Europa Clipper’s MISE and JUICE’s MAJIS instruments. Measurements were conducted in the nitrogen-purged CRONOS facility at 100–121 K. Pure and 50%/50% volume mixtures were prepared in four grain-size bins: fine (<63 µm), small (63–250 µm), medium (250–500 µm), and large (>500 µm). Water ice was crystalline and spectrally dominated by absorption bands near 1.5, 1.65, and 2.0 µm. Cryogenic epsomite displayed numerous resolved features absent at ambient temperature, while halite showed an adsorbed-water feature near 1.95 µm. Increasing grain size reduced reflectance and saturated absorption features. Water ice strongly dominated salt–ice mixtures; halite–ice mixtures were nearly indistinguishable from pure water ice.

Hapke-based linear and intimate mixture models were tested against laboratory spectra using published optical constants. Both models reproduced water-ice spectra reasonably well, generally within about 5% at most wavelengths, and no clear advantage was found for intimate mixing. Neither model consistently reproduced both continua and absorption features. Epsomite fits were less reliable: cryogenic optical constants may have been published under incorrect labels, and possible sample desiccation was identified as another possible cause of discrepancies. Models also underrepresent epsomite’s influence in mixtures and its fine absorption structure.

The results indicate that quantitative spectral unmixing should consider both linear and intimate models and possible biases toward smaller grains. Mixture spectra are not necessarily intermediate between their endmembers, so qualitative identification of abundance and grain size may be unreliable. Future work will derive corrected cryogenic epsomite optical constants and reassess model fidelity.

The Sri Lankan rupee fell for a third straight session, closing at 158.60/75 per dollar as importer demand outpaced remittance inflows; dealers cited Fed rate hikes, the US-China trade war and higher oil prices. The spot rate hit a record low of 160.17 on June 20. Pressure eased after a $584 million Chinese payment. Moody's and the IMF warned of credit and debt risks.

An Uzbek court convicted U.S. citizen Zokir Aliyev of calling for the government’s overthrow and joining an extremist group, but fined him only $67 for offenses dating to 1999. Aliyev denied links to the militant Islamic Movement of Uzbekistan and said he attended opposition meetings in Turkey.

Responding to a Senate inquiry, the President reported an alleged forcible effort to obstruct federal law enforcement in Boston. He cited deputy marshal Patrick Riley’s affidavit and unofficial accounts, while noting that some details were disputed and official information was incomplete. He said the incident violated federal law and Massachusetts public sentiment. He reviewed congressional resolutions requiring U.S. marshals to secure temporary federal jails when states withdrew their jails from federal use, and Massachusetts’s 1843 restrictions on state assistance in detaining people claimed as fugitive slaves. Although the Navy Secretary had alerted the Massachusetts marshal to this duty, no official confirmation showed that a temporary jail had been provided; the President said orders would be issued if necessary. He proposed clarifying legislation governing the use of regular forces and militia to enforce federal laws, including whether a prior proclamation was required and whether organized militia could be summoned as a posse comitatus. He affirmed his duty to execute the laws and his confidence in public support for the Constitution and Union.

In a separate April 25, 1851 proclamation, he warned against a planned American expedition against Spanish Cuba, described it as an illegal, predatory violation of national and international law, and urged citizens and government officers to prevent and prosecute it.

NVDA options trading can potentially generate large profits from leveraged investments, with long-option losses limited to the premium paid, but it carries substantial complexity and risk. Available strategies include buying or writing calls and puts, straddles, strangles, spreads, and collars. Option prices are influenced by the underlying stock price, time to expiration, implied volatility, market sentiment, and dividends; models such as Black-Scholes can be used for pricing.

Calls generally rise when NVDA rises and fall when it declines, while puts move inversely. Higher implied volatility or volatile market conditions generally increase option premiums, and volatility is central to determining costs. Dividends generally reduce call prices and increase put prices.

Risk can be limited through stop-loss orders, protective puts, hedging, diversification, and position sizing. Protective puts can protect a long stock position if purchased below the current stock price. Potential return strategies include leverage, buying deep in-the-money options, writing covered calls, and using bullish spreads or straddles. Speculators may buy calls or puts based on expected short-term price movements.

Key risks include adverse stock movement, time decay, volatility, and liquidity. Although NVDA options are generally liquid, margin requirements vary and are typically lower for buying than writing options. Quantitative and qualitative analysis, technical analysis, trading software, pricing models, and current news can support decision-making. Options trading is generally treated as a capital-gains activity, so investors should consult a tax professional.

The 2018-19 Union Budget received mixed assessments regarding women. Unlike the 2016 and 2017 Budgets, it had no separate women’s section or allocation. Some economists argued that it preserved traditional gender roles without addressing barriers to women’s employment or creating new economic pathways, while others welcomed measures with potential benefits.

The National Health Protection Scheme, offering ₹5 lakh in annual insurance per family and covering 10 crore vulnerable families, was considered a major positive step for women’s access to healthcare. However, critics questioned its implementation, insufficient budget allocations, limited preventive-care funding, and the poor performance of the preceding RSBY. Health-sector allocations rose only 2.7%, while the Health Ministry’s share of total spending fell from 2.4% to 2.1%.

MSME credit support could benefit women in small businesses and self-help groups, and sanitation initiatives could improve rural women’s health and safety. Conversely, maternity entitlements were reduced, and the proposed expansion of Ujjwala was criticized because many recipients could not afford cylinder refills. Overall, the Budget was seen as largely continuing existing policies rather than introducing transformative measures for women.

After seven or eight months in Quebec, the speaker says the area feels like home, and he is happy that family members, his longtime supporters, will attend the game. He credits preparation, hard work, toughness, and the belief that players create their own luck for the team’s success. Expecting a difficult opponent, he plans to match their intensity, proceed one game and shift at a time, and remain focused on the team’s game plan regardless of venue.

USB-C and USB-A describe physical connector shapes, not necessarily speed or features. USB-C is reversible and more capable, while USB-A has fixed 5-volt power delivery; USB-B and Micro-USB remain on some accessories. USB versions are defined mainly by data-transfer speed and power delivery, and any connection is limited by its slowest component. Because USB 3.x branding is inconsistent, actual speed ratings are more useful: common tiers include 5, 10, and 20 Gbps, while USB 2.0 tops out at 480 Mbps. USB-A’s maximum is 20 Gbps.

USB4, available since 2022, is USB-C-only and initially supports 20–40 Gbps. USB4 Version 2 was announced and certified in 2022 with potential speeds up to 120 Gbps, but adoption remains limited. USB Power Delivery 3.1 supports up to 240 watts, provided adapters, hubs, and cables can handle the required wattage. DisplayPort Alt Mode carries audio and video over one USB-C cable, with capabilities depending on the DisplayPort generation; USB4 requires it and uses DisplayPort 2.0.

Thunderbolt is an Intel- and Apple-developed USB-C standard with stricter certification. Thunderbolt 4 is based on USB4, supports up to 40 Gbps and 100 watts, guarantees two 4K displays at 60 Hz, and allows two-meter cables. Emerging Thunderbolt 5 offers up to 80 Gbps bidirectionally, 120 Gbps unidirectionally with Bandwidth Boost, advanced display support, and 240-watt power delivery. Thunderbolt remains compatible with USB devices, though connections use the slowest link.

Cable capabilities can limit speed and charging. Users should use the supplied cable or verify listed speed and wattage, since manufacturer labels may omit specifications or generations.

The speaker argues that the policy adopted to end slavery agitation has instead increased it and that the government cannot remain permanently “half slave and half free.” It must eventually either restrict slavery’s expansion and put it on a path toward extinction or make it lawful in every state. He maintains that the latter is more likely because of the Nebraska doctrine and the Dred Scott decision.

He traces how the repeal of congressional restrictions on slavery in 1854, Buchanan’s election, and the Dred Scott decision advanced a coordinated effort to expand slavery. He identifies three principles of that decision: people descended from enslaved Africans cannot be citizens under the Constitution; neither Congress nor territorial legislatures can exclude slavery from territories; and courts will not free enslaved people taken into free states. Combined with Senator Douglas’s policy of “care not” whether slavery is voted up or down, these principles were intended to secure slavery’s permanent legality.

The speaker argues that the sequence of political and judicial actions was deliberately adapted to produce this outcome, though he acknowledges that premeditated agreement cannot be proven absolutely. He also suggests that the Supreme Court’s failure to address whether states could exclude slavery may leave room for a future decision declaring that they cannot.

He warns that such a decision is likely unless the governing political dynasty is defeated, predicting that Americans may expect Missouri to become free but awaken to find Illinois made a slave state. Rejecting Douglas as an ally because his principles do not oppose slavery, he urges committed Republicans to rely on their own leaders, remain steadfast, and continue their successful resistance to the expansion of slavery.

Henry J. Adams III pleaded guilty to armed bank robbery. He helped plan the October 2012 robbery, served as lookout, recruited Veronica Johnson to provide transportation and an escape vehicle, and expected a share of the proceeds. The district court denied his request for a two-level minor-participant reduction and sentenced him to 140 months’ imprisonment and four years of supervised release, above the 84–105-month guideline range, citing his extensive and escalating criminal history, repeated reoffending, the seriousness of the offense, deterrence, public protection, and the need to promote a lawful lifestyle.

The Tenth Circuit held that Adams was not substantially less culpable than the average participant because he knowingly assisted in the planned robbery and expected compensation. It characterized the sentence as an upward variance based on the statutory sentencing factors, not a departure subject to the guidelines’ departure requirements. The court found the sentence substantively reasonable and rejected Adams’s disparity argument because he compared his sentence only with his codefendant’s rather than with similarly situated defendants nationwide. It affirmed the sentence.

Chelsea, Real Madrid and Tottenham are competing to sign Ajax defender Davinson Sanchez, valued by Ajax at £40m. Spurs plan an initial £28m bid, while Chelsea and Madrid are preparing rival offers. Sanchez wants to leave, but Ajax hope to retain him with a long-term contract.

The Stick concept is a quick-game passing concept with five eligible receivers, designed to help quarterbacks release the ball quickly. The tight end is usually the primary target and can adjust his route based on defensive coverage. The concept generally works well against man, Cover 3, and Cover 4, while Cover 2 creates coverage risks and may require a difficult hole-shot throw or a different concept.

Coaching points vary by coverage. Against man, the tight end releases vertically before running away from coverage, while the other receivers use arrow, slant, and go routes with specific landmarks and responsibilities. Against zone, the tight end bursts vertically and settles in a void. The quarterback identifies the flat defender before the snap and uses his movement to choose an arrow or stick throw; an RB check-down is available if the read is unclear.

Variations include condensed 2x2 formations with outside-in reads and a Trips Flex “Sticko” look featuring a tight-end double move, delayed slot slant, and backside sluggo option.

The president calls on Congress to pursue four domestic goals: economic growth, affordable health care, energy independence, and support for vulnerable citizens. He proposes making scheduled income-tax reductions permanent and immediate, ending double taxation of dividends, limiting discretionary spending growth, and giving younger workers more control over retirement savings.

On health care, he urges Congress to strengthen Medicare, provide seniors prescription-drug choices and preventive care, and enact medical liability reform while opposing nationalized health care. His energy plan includes greater efficiency and domestic production, a 70 percent reduction in power-plant air pollution, forest-fire prevention, and $1.2 billion for hydrogen-powered vehicle research. He also seeks expanded mentoring and drug-treatment programs, federal support for faith-based and volunteer service, protection for infants at birth, a ban on partial-birth abortion, and legislation against human cloning.

Internationally, the president calls for continued support in Afghanistan, a peace between Israel and Palestine, and expanded food aid. He proposes a $15 billion, five-year AIDS initiative for Africa and the Caribbean that would prevent infections, provide treatment, and support orphaned children.

He describes the global war on terrorism as ongoing, citing the arrest of more than 3,000 suspected terrorists and international counterterrorism cooperation. He requests additional homeland-security measures, including Project BioShield funding for vaccines and treatments against possible bioweapons and a center to integrate threat information.

The speech warns that regimes possessing nuclear, chemical, or biological weapons pose a major danger and discusses Iran and North Korea. It portrays Saddam Hussein as refusing to disarm, concealing weapons programs, and supporting terrorists. The president says the United Nations Security Council will consider Iraq’s defiance on February 5 and that, if Hussein does not fully disarm, the United States will lead a coalition to compel disarmament. He asserts that any war would be fought in a just cause, with the full force of the U.S. military, and that coalition forces would bring food, medicine, supplies, and freedom to Iraq.

Reports that Amazon may enter online prescription drug sales sent Walgreens, Rite Aid and CVS shares down; Amazon is discussing pharmacy benefit managers and hiring talent while declining to comment on speculation.

The study examines the positive, neutral, and negative value loads conveyed by words in reading texts from second-, third-, and fourth-grade Turkish textbooks published by Turkey’s Ministry of National Education. It emphasizes that values are acquired through experience, shape behavior and decision-making, and are taught through curricula, formal programs, and the hidden curriculum.

Researchers analyzed 88 prose reading texts from the ministry’s online textbook repository, excluding first-grade materials and poems. After optical character recognition, punctuation removal, tokenization, and lemmatization, the study produced a database of 3,637 unique words. Three applied-linguistics experts classified each word’s internal meaning and value load using introspection and dictionary definitions.

Of the words analyzed, 172 (4.72%) had positive value loads, 3,306 (91.43%) were neutral, and 159 (4.37%) were negative. Across grades, neutral words predominated, while positive and negative words had similar distributions. The findings showed no observable relationship between grade level and the values conveyed by textbook words. The researchers concluded that the textbooks lacked established value-education standards in their word selection and suggested constructing texts around specified values and using corpus-based textbook preparation. They also recommended digitizing print textbooks to support further and diachronic research.

Yufei Zhao opens MIT 18.217, a course combining extremal graph theory and additive combinatorics, and argues throughout the lecture that the two subjects are closely connected.

The lecture begins with Schur's attempt to prove Fermat's Last Theorem by reducing an equation modulo primes; this strategy fails because, for every exponent n, non-trivial solutions exist mod p for all sufficiently large p. Schur's Theorem states that any finite coloring of the positive integers contains a monochromatic solution to x + y = z. Zhao discusses its infinitary (qualitative) and finitary (quantitative) forms, shows their equivalence via a diagonalization argument, and notes that optimal bounds on N(r) are generally unknown with large gaps. He then proves Schur's Theorem using Ramsey's theorem for triangles: color the edge between i and j by the color of j − i, so a monochromatic triangle gives a monochromatic solution to x + y = z. Ramsey's theorem for triangles is proved by induction on the number of colors, using the pigeonhole principle. The pedagogical advantage of the detour through graphs, Zhao argues, is the extra flexibility they provide: one colors on the order of N² objects rather than N, enabling inductive arguments over vertices. A question about bounds is answered with the remark that bounds are largely open.

The second half is a historical tour of additive combinatorics, whose name Zhao attributes to Terry Tao in the early 2000s. Van der Waerden's theorem (1927) says every finite coloring of the integers contains arbitrarily long arithmetic progressions (not to be confused with infinitely long ones). Erdős and Turán conjectured in 1936 that positive density, rather than coloring, is the key condition; Roth proved the 3-term case around 1953 using Fourier (Hardy–Littlewood circle) analysis, and Szemerédi proved the full conjecture in the late 1970s with an elaborate combinatorial proof. The theorem motivated many later developments and alternative proofs: Furstenberg's ergodic-theoretic proof, Gowers's higher-order Fourier analysis (circa 2000), the hypergraph regularity method developed independently by Rödl and Gowers (a central topic of the course's first half, which also produced Ruzsa and Szemerédi's graph-theoretic proof of Roth's theorem), and the Polymath project (Gowers, Tao, published as DHJ Polymath), which yielded a combinatorial proof of the density Hales–Jewett theorem implying Szemerédi's. Zhao notes that Szemerédi received a prize for his contributions to combinatorics and theoretical computer science, that the relationships among these methods remain poorly understood, and that a recurring theme is the "structure versus randomness" dichotomy.

Generalizations discussed include the multidimensional Szemerédi theorem (positive-density subsets of Z^d contain dilated and translated finite patterns, or "constellations"), proved by Furstenberg and Katznelson via ergodic theory and only later combinatorially through hypergraph regularity; ergodic proofs generally yield no quantitative bounds. The polynomial Szemerédi theorem of Bergelson and Liebman states that positive-density sets contain patterns x + P_i(y), and remains known only by ergodic methods in general. The Green–Tao theorem shows that the primes contain arbitrarily long arithmetic progressions; since primes have density ~1/log n, it was proved by transferring Szemerédi's theorem to a sparser "pseudoprime" setting, yielding arbitrarily long progressions in every subset of the primes of relative positive density.

Zhao closes by restating Roth's theorem finitely: any subset of [1, N] avoiding 3-term progressions has size o(N). A naive graph-theoretic translation via triangle-free graphs leads to Mantel's theorem (maximum edges attained by a balanced complete bipartite graph), but the correct question is the maximum number of edges in an n-vertex graph in which every edge lies in exactly one triangle — corresponding to trivial 3-term progressions with repeated terms. Best known bounds for Roth's theorem are roughly N/e^{c√(log N)} below and N/log N above; Erdős's conjecture that a divergent harmonic series forces arbitrarily long progressions remains open and would require breaking the logarithmic barrier. Upcoming lectures will address extremal graph theory: for a forbidden structure H, what is the maximum number of edges?

Administrative notes: a short break; a Wikipedia contribution assignment in addition to course notes; collaborative lecture notes requiring a rough draft by the end of the day after lecture and polished versions within four days, followed by a meeting with the instructor; informal office hours in the Math Common Room after 4 p.m. and special sessions before homework deadlines.

Assistant U.S. Attorney Will Rosenzweig was fired after old blog posts criticizing President Donald Trump surfaced, according to conservative commentator Natalie Winters. Rosenzweig allegedly wrote the posts while at Kobre & Kim and did not respond to a request for comment. The Justice Department also fired three other Southern District of Florida prosecutors who had worked with former special counsel Jack Smith. Smith criticized attacks on career public servants and the targeting of political opponents. Separately, U.S. Attorney Erik Siebert left his position after Trump pressured him to indict Letitia James and James Comey.

Weekly trading strategies focus on weekly price action and include position trading, sector rotation, using weekly charts for broader market context, and swing trading based on weekly price bars. Weekly systems trade less frequently and generally suit long-term positions. Range trading is the most common weekly approach: traders identify support and resistance, then enter at those levels using price-action patterns or indicator signals, often holding positions for 6–12 months. Weekly trend-following trades may last several years, while daily-chart trend followers often use the weekly chart to assess broader market structure and key levels.

Weekly highs and lows can act as support or resistance on lower timeframes, particularly H4. Traders may use breakouts or reversals at these levels for swing or day trades. Weekly-chart analysis can identify trends, ranges, and significant support and resistance, while H4 charts help refine swing-trading entries.

The appropriate timeframe depends on the strategy. Weekly and daily charts suit position trading, while weekly and H4 charts suit weekly swing trading. Backtesting a strategy across timeframes is necessary to determine which performs best.

Day traders trading U.S. stocks must follow FINRA’s pattern-day-trader requirements, including the $25,000 minimum account balance when applicable; weekly swing traders with one or two trades per week are generally unaffected. Stock gaps should be incorporated into risk management.

A backtested long-only weekly sector-rotation strategy ranking four ETFs produced 15.1% annual returns, a 43% maximum drawdown, 728 trades, and an average gain of 0.4% before slippage and commissions. Its monthly version produced 12.1% annual returns, a 21% maximum drawdown, and 166 trades.

The Ninth Circuit affirmed the district court’s grant of summary judgment to AMCO Insurance Company and denial of George Morello’s motion for reconsideration. The court found no genuine issue of material fact that AMCO breached the implied covenant of good faith and fair dealing. AMCO’s investigation was not unreasonable: it persistently sought information, hired experts, and reasonably relied on medical opinions concluding Morello was not entitled to future care. There was no evidence that the lead expert acted in bad faith or improperly destroyed documents. Because liability remained genuinely disputed, AMCO’s withholding of benefits was reasonable. Conclusory expert opinions that AMCO mishandled the claim were rebutted by the record, and the evidence did not show unreasonable delay in offering settlement. Morello’s emotional-distress, unfair-business-practices, and Unruh Act claims rested on the same bad-faith theory and likewise failed. Evidence of AMCO’s mediation communications was inadmissible for the bad-faith claim.

NVIDIA Corporation filed an unaudited Form 10-Q for the first quarter of fiscal 2022, ended May 2, 2021. The company reported quarterly revenue of $5.661 billion, up 84% year over year and 13% sequentially. Gross profit was $3.629 billion, with a 64.1% margin, while operating expenses rose 63% year over year to $1.673 billion. Operating income doubled to $1.956 billion, net income increased to $1.912 billion from $917 million, and diluted earnings per share rose to $3.03 from $1.47. The effective income tax rate was 6.5%.

Revenue by market was $2.760 billion for Gaming, $2.048 billion for Data Center, $372 million for Professional Visualization, $154 million for Automotive, and $327 million for OEM and Other. Gaming revenue increased 106% from the prior year, Data Center revenue rose 79%, Professional Visualization increased 21%, Automotive declined 1%, and OEM and Other increased 137%. The Graphics segment generated $3.451 billion of revenue and $1.786 billion of operating income, while Compute & Networking generated $2.210 billion of revenue and $861 million of operating income. Revenue growth reflected strong GeForce RTX 30 Series sales, the Mellanox acquisition, Ampere products, hyperscale customers, and cryptocurrency mining demand.

As of May 2, 2021, NVIDIA reported $30.796 billion of assets, including $978 million of cash and cash equivalents, $11.689 billion of marketable securities, $3.024 billion of accounts receivable, and $1.992 billion of inventories. Total liabilities were $12.022 billion, including $999 million of short-term debt and $5.964 billion of long-term debt, and shareholders’ equity was $18.774 billion. Operating activities generated $1.874 billion of cash, while investing and financing activities used $1.272 billion and $471 million, respectively. The company paid $99 million in dividends, made no share repurchases, and remained authorized to repurchase up to $7.24 billion through December 2022.

NVIDIA disclosed a pending $40 billion acquisition of Arm Limited from SoftBank. It had paid $2 billion at signing and was obligated upon closing to pay $10 billion in cash and issue 44.3 million shares valued at $21.5 billion when the agreement was signed. The transaction also included a potential additional payment of up to $5 billion in cash or 10.3 million shares and up to $1.5 billion in restricted stock units for Arm employees. Closing remained subject to regulatory approvals and other conditions, and management believed it was likely to occur in the first quarter of calendar 2022. NVIDIA completed its $7.13 billion acquisition of Mellanox Technologies on April 27, 2020.

On May 21, 2021, NVIDIA’s board declared a four-for-one common-stock split in the form of a stock dividend, subject to shareholder approval expected at the June 3 annual meeting. Additional shares were expected to be distributed on July 19, 2021. Pro forma basic and diluted quarterly earnings per share were $0.77 and $0.76, respectively.

A securities class-action complaint was dismissed without leave to amend on March 2, 2021, and plaintiffs filed an appeal on March 30. Related derivative lawsuits remained stayed pending the appeal. NVIDIA recorded no accrual for these proceedings because potential losses were not considered probable and could not be reasonably estimated.

Management identified COVID-19, supply-chain capacity, component availability, channel inventory, and cryptocurrency-market volatility as significant business risks. NVIDIA expected to remain supply-constrained into the second half of the fiscal year, primarily in gaming. Management concluded that disclosure controls were effective, and no material changes occurred in internal control over financial reporting during the quarter.

PM_PAGE_MOVE_IO processes 1–128 migration entries and moves pages in SNP-enabled or non-SNP-enabled systems. In SNP systems, it is restricted to Hypervisor-owned pages; in SEV systems, only unencrypted or host/hypervisor-encrypted memory may be targeted. It can move pages in use by DMA and directly updates IOMMU host PTEs. Software must prevent CPU access and, for non-SNP systems with non-secure ATS access, set hPTE.PMS, invalidate ATS entries, and synchronize before the command, then update CPU host page tables afterward. SNP source and destination pages must be in the Hypervisor state. Direct 2M-page migration is unsupported; 2M pages must first be split into 4K pages. Firmware validates addresses and states, obtains exclusive RMP access when required, performs TLB invalidations and synchronization, flushes DMA, copies data while preserving required encryption, updates PTEs and RMPs, and clears migration status.

PM_PAGE_MOVE_GUEST processes 1–128 entries for pages belonging to an SNP guest and can serve as a faster replacement for SNP PAGE_MOVE. It does not support DMA to migrating pages, and concurrent DMA may be aborted. CPU access must be prevented. Source pages must be Guest-Valid or Guest-Invalid, while destination pages must be Pre-Migration; afterward, destinations adopt the corresponding source state and sources become Pre-Migration. RMP enforcement is required. Firmware validates addresses, guest context, RMP access, page sizes, and states, invalidates and synchronizes the CPU TLB, copies the data, and updates source and destination RMPs. A 2M page must be aligned and composed of physically contiguous 4K pages, but cannot be migrated directly.

A separate command marks the end of page-migration command sequences and can interrupt on completion; most input fields are ignored. Format and entry errors may cause rejection or partial success and are reported in command or entry status. Ring-buffer errors use PM_STATUS, while hardware errors are reported through command status or MCA. Batches may contain up to 128 pages, and hardware errors can render the entire batch unrecoverable, potentially requiring state preservation and reboot.

Under GST, consignments valued above Rs 50,000 require e-way bills, while those below the threshold may opt for one. The GST Council exempted 153 items, including household LPG, PDS kerosene, currency, jewellery, food products, animals, postal baggage and personal effects. The requirement will begin once NIC software is ready, likely by October.

School systems nationwide are outfitting traditional buses with GPS tracking, turn-by-turn navigation, live cameras, student check-in systems and route-management software. Kansas City Public Schools’ five-year, $100 million contract with Zum introduced air conditioning, tinted windows and technology that lets parents monitor rides, dispatchers see bus locations, speeds and delays, and schools count students for meals.

Bentonville Schools pays about $90,000 annually for Transportant camera and tracking tools that record boarding, drop-off and student images; officials say live video can support drivers and aid investigations. Other products monitor maintenance, optimize routes and allow principals to communicate with students remotely. Tracking apps can reduce waiting, parent calls and potentially the number of buses and drivers needed.

However, privacy advocates warn that GPS, video and other student data create security and retention risks. Districts say they store bus data separately and delete videos under retention policies. Transportant says it does not sell student data and encrypts device memory. Vendors offer bundled systems or separate products, but upfront and subscription costs can limit adoption.

The Infiniti Q Inspiration concept, revealed this year, will inspire a new electrified platform yielding up to five models over five years, built in China and likely global. Its "clear and concise lines," sculpted athletic body and distinctive lights and grilles carry over, with a crossover among the body styles.

SOS pressure defense requires deliberate drilling, commitment, and positive coaching that builds player acceptance and enthusiasm. Defenders must act first rather than react, using three on-ball actions: SET forces the ballhandler to dribble; ON guides the dribbler toward a sideline or baseline away from high-percentage shooting range; and SMOTHER applies maximum pressure when the ballhandler picks up the ball to shoot or pass. Effective transitions among these actions are essential.

Three off-ball actions support the system. SNUGGLE denies passes by staying close to the offensive player in a low stance; if beaten on a back cut, the defender reverses position to obstruct the backdoor pass. In low-post defense, Snuggle can become a Post Front using slip-front technique. OFF moves the defender between the opponent and ballhandler, then maintains tight position to deny the return pass. STRIKE is the weakside response: the defender quickly moves into position to prevent cuts, provide help defense, cover lob passes, take charges, contest layups, box out, rebound, and close out on crosscourt passes.

Closeouts begin from Strike, sprint toward the receiver, and end in a Set position that directs the ballhandler toward the nearest corner or baseline checkpoint.

Fiat Chrysler reportedly rejected a merger offer from an unidentified Chinese automaker because it considered the financial terms insufficient. The rejection followed FCA’s unsuccessful attempts to court General Motors and Volkswagen and CEO Sergio Marchionne’s statements that the company preferred partnerships in other markets rather than acquisition by an Asian automaker. Chinese manufacturers’ interest may be linked to the government’s “China Outbound” initiative and efforts to enter the U.S. market. FCA’s history, distribution network, familiar brands, and potential debt relief make it attractive.

Xiaomi is preparing for its biggest 2018 launch event, expected to feature the Mi 8, Mi 8 SE, Mi Note 5, and Mi Band 3. Digit reports the Mi A2 won't launch in India; a spokesperson said no such phone exists but more Android One devices are planned, so the Mi 6X may come to India renamed. The Redmi S2/Y2 is also due in India as a budget dual-camera phone.

In Givens v. Missouri-Kansas-Texas Railroad Co., a Missouri-Kansas-Texas passenger train broke down near Hewitt, Texas, when one driving-wheel tire came off and the others slipped. The sole brakeman was sent roughly three-quarters of a mile behind the train to flag and protect its rear. While stationed there for several hours in freezing weather, he sustained frostbite to both feet and injuries extending into his legs.

A jury awarded $12,000, found that the breakdown proximately caused his injuries, determined that the accident was unavoidable and not caused by negligence, and answered that the locomotive was safe to operate. The jury received no instructions on the Federal Boiler Inspection Act or Federal Employers’ Liability Act. The Fifth Circuit held that the Boiler Inspection Act imposes an absolute, continuing duty to keep locomotives and their parts safe to operate. Although not every breakdown creates liability, where an in-use locomotive or necessary part completely fails to function, the Act is violated as a matter of law unless the failure was merely incidental to an unrelated cause. The jury’s findings established an unavoidable failure unrelated to negligence or any fault by the plaintiff.

Because the breakdown violated the Act and proximately contributed to the brakeman’s frostbite injuries, the court held that the district court erred in denying judgment for the plaintiff. It reversed and ordered judgment for $12,000 on the jury’s verdict.

North American stocks closed sharply lower Friday, with the Dow down 666 points (2.5%) and the S&P 500 down 2.1%; both had their worst week since January 2016, while the Nasdaq had its worst week since February 2016. Strong U.S. jobs and wage growth raised concerns about inflation and further rate hikes as Treasury yields climbed. Weak earnings from major companies, including Apple, Alphabet and energy firms, also weighed on markets. In Canada, the S&P/TSX fell 1.6%, its worst week since January 2016, as oil, gold and marijuana stocks declined. The Canadian dollar weakened to 80.78 U.S. cents.

The paper examines how AI ethics is integrated into computing curricula at leading Indian engineering institutions.
