Researchers reviewed 3,395 publicly available syllabi from the top 100 NIRF-ranked universities, identifying explicit and implicit ethics content through manual qualitative analysis and cross-verification.

Only 75 courses (2.21%) across 22 universities addressed AI ethics. Coverage was generally limited: 60% addressed it in one session, 20% in two sessions, 13% across three to five sessions, and 7% devoted an entire course to it. Most offerings were undergraduate-level, and more than 76% had no prerequisites. Common topics included privacy, legal issues and data governance (42%); accountability and policy (32%); ethical frameworks and moral reasoning (24%); human-AI interaction and agency (24%); algorithmic bias and fairness (18%); AI safety and robustness (16%); generative AI concerns (11%); and social impact and justice (8%).

The courses commonly addressed privacy risks, fairness, explainability, ethical dilemmas, governance, and ethical reasoning. However, over 90% cited no ethics-specific textbooks, and no syllabus documented assessments explicitly dedicated to AI ethics. The findings indicate that ethics instruction remains marginal and inconsistently integrated, with limited curricular attention to generative AI, sustainability, justice, and labor ethics. The authors call for shared learning goals, open instructional materials, India-specific case studies, assessment frameworks, faculty development, and greater curriculum transparency. Limitations include possible human error, missing or outdated syllabi, and a sample limited to publicly documented courses at top-ranked institutions, which may not represent Indian higher education broadly.

In Mazabuka, Zambia's "Sweet Town," the sugar boom drew migrant workers and a sex industry, contributing to a severe AIDS epidemic; at its 2003 peak, Zambia recorded 70,000 deaths a year, according to UNAIDS. A hospital and roadside graveyard bear witness, with every bed once filled by HIV patients, according to District Health Commissioner Stephen Shajanika. Today, the local NGO DAPP runs a military-style "Total Control of the Epidemic" campaign—door-to-door counselling, 15-minute finger-prick testing, free condoms for truckers, former sex workers spreading messages in bars, and chieftains disclosing their status—to mobilise individuals; it has reached more than 1.5 million of 16.5 million Zambians and spread from Zimbabwe (2000) to Mazabuka (2006) and Sinazongwe. Testing has increased and antiretroviral drugs are available; the UN estimates 250 new daily infections, down 27 percent since 2010, with AIDS deaths down 11 percent. District Commissioner Protacia Mulenga, whose brothers died of AIDS and whose sister is HIV-positive, credits DAPP with reaching communities the government cannot, and urges other countries to adopt the approach.
The FBI arrested Jerry Drake Varnell, 23, for allegedly plotting to detonate an explosives-laden van outside an Oklahoma bank; he is scheduled to appear in federal court Monday.

Heart attacks and strokes have fallen by 30% in the UK over two decades but remain major health risks. Cholesterol- and blood-pressure-lowering medicines, including statins, play a major role, alongside lifestyle changes. Statins are among England’s most prescribed medicines and effectively lower cholesterol; a well-designed study found similar side-effect rates between statin and placebo groups when participants did not know which they were taking, highlighting the nocebo effect.

If cholesterol remains uncontrolled or statins cannot be taken, other lipid-lowering medicines may be prescribed. These include medicines targeting a protein linked to high LDL, such as Repatha, Praluent and Leqvio; Leqvio can reduce LDL by around 50% with a single six-monthly injection but is usually reserved for very high-risk patients.

Quitting smoking reduces arterial furring and improves cholesterol, with NHS support and cessation tools available. Exercise supports weight loss and can lower LDL and raise HDL independently; 30 minutes five times weekly improves cholesterol, while any activity benefits the heart. A heart-healthy diet emphasises soluble fibre from oats, barley, fruit, vegetables, beans, nuts and seeds, plus plant sterols from fortified foods and soya. Cooking from scratch can reduce hidden sugar and salt. Potassium-based salt substitutes may lower blood pressure and cardiovascular risk. The Therapeutic Lifestyle Changes (TLC) diet is presented as a way to lower cholesterol and protect heart health.

A federal judge ordered the Trump administration to reverse layoffs of nearly all remaining Voice of America employees, finding that officials had violated his order requiring reliable, authoritative broadcasting. Judge Royce C. Lamberth criticized Kari Lake and other officials for keeping staffing and programming minimal and warned of contempt after 532 journalists and support staff were fired. Voice of America’s broadcasting was reduced from around the clock to about an hour daily amid the administration’s effort to close the federally funded news organization.

Walter Camp is credited with developing American football from rugby, establishing consistent rules, 11-player teams, the line of scrimmage, quarterback position, downs-based possession, and modern scoring. Variants were played at Northeastern colleges in the 1870s, and Camp’s Yale teams won national championships in 1888, 1891, and 1892. The name “football” reflects American adaptation of European soccer and rugby, though the origin of the name is uncertain. American football is not currently an Olympic sport, although flag football may debut at the 2028 Los Angeles Games. The NFL is predominantly American-born, with college programs providing a major pipeline of players.

Each American football team fields 11 players, while the CFL uses 12 and plays on a 110-yard field. Professional and college games last 60 minutes in four 15-minute quarters; high school quarters last 12 minutes. A standard field is 100 yards between goal lines, with 10-yard end zones and a width of 160 feet.

Scoring includes six-point touchdowns, one-point extra points, two-point conversions, three-point field goals, and two-point safeties. Common penalties include offsides, encroachment, false start, pass interference, holding, defensive holding, personal fouls, roughing the passer, and illegal formation. A catch generally requires possession, control, two feet in bounds, and a football move, with exceptions for end-zone and sideline catches. Turnovers include interceptions, fumbles, and failure to convert on fourth down. The line of scrimmage separates the teams, while the neutral zone is the area between them. Special teams handle kickoffs, punts, field goals, extra points, and returns. An audible changes the planned play after the offense lines up, and downs are individual plays, with four attempts to gain ten yards before possession changes. The red zone is the area between the 20-yard line and the goal line.

Notable players highlighted include quarterback Tom Brady, wide receiver Jerry Rice, running back Jim Brown, and linebacker Lawrence Taylor.

CBS’s legal drama “Doubt” stars Katherine Heigl as Sadie Ellis, an attorney at a small New York firm representing pediatric surgeon Billy Brennan, accused of murdering his girlfriend 24 years earlier. Sadie has fallen for Billy and seeks to prove his innocence while the firm handles other cases and personal stories. The series addresses sexual assault, dementia, harassment, and transgender representation, with Laverne Cox playing a transgender lawyer. The review calls the show likable, competent, and evenhanded, though it relies on familiar “Grey’s Anatomy”-style formulas and contains overly cute dialogue and logical lapses.

Police are examining a white Holden Commodore seized over the weekend for fingerprints, DNA and blood. They are investigating Aaron Marks’ murder, have appealed for passengers to come forward and said the driver is assisting.

Callum Knott, 21, admitted taking his aunt's car without consent and driving without a licence or insurance, saying he was "young and stupid" and took it out of boredom. He received a 12-month community order with 80 hours' unpaid work, a four-month driving ban, and £85 costs plus an £85 victim surcharge.

Cover 2 is a 5-under, 2-deep defense designed to stop quick perimeter passes and dumps while safeties take away deep throws. Offenses attack it with high-low combinations against the flat cornerbacks, three-receiver concepts that challenge the middle linebacker, vertical routes that force safeties to split, and routes that widen the safeties to exploit the middle. Examples from Ohio State, Oregon, Michigan, Ole Miss, and TCU illustrate smash and fade-out concepts, slot fades, run-action plays with RB pop passes, and jet motion with four verticals.
At the East Demerara Football Association’s AGM, Alfred King was returned as president for another term, with Gregory Wickham, Gillian Frank, and Mark Pertab as vice presidents.

Curaleaf Holdings and cannabis stocks rallied in August after reports that the Trump administration would consider rescheduling cannabis. The rally faded in September but revived after Trump posted about CBD benefits for elders. Curaleaf reported in-line Q2 2025 results and plans to expand internationally into Turkey. The author maintains a Hold rating on CURLF due to sector uncertainty and discloses a beneficial long position.

Tesla, Inc.’s unaudited Form 10-Q for the quarter ended June 30, 2020 covers its automotive and energy generation and storage segments. Second-quarter revenue was $6.036 billion, including $5.179 billion from automotive, $370 million from energy generation and storage, and $487 million from services and other. Gross profit was $1.267 billion, operating income was $327 million, and net income attributable to common stockholders was $104 million, or $0.50 per diluted share, versus a $408 million loss in the prior-year quarter. For the first six months, revenue was $12.021 billion and net income attributable to common stockholders was $120 million.

At June 30, 2020, Tesla reported $38.135 billion of assets, $8.615 billion of cash and cash equivalents, $26.754 billion of liabilities, and $9.855 billion of stockholders’ equity. Debt and finance leases totaled $14.095 billion. First-half operating cash flow was $524 million, investing activities used $1.046 billion, financing activities provided $2.831 billion, and ending cash, cash equivalents and restricted cash was $9.106 billion.

The filing describes pandemic-related manufacturing suspensions, furloughs, salary reductions and supplier disruptions, followed by resumed operations at all manufacturing facilities by the end of the second quarter. Notes address revenue recognition, regulatory credits, leases, credit-loss accounting, debt, fair values and stock-based compensation. The first tranche of the CEO performance award vested during the quarter, and the second vested on July 24, 2020, accelerating related compensation expense.

Andrew Dawes, newly appointed CEO of Intels Nigeria Limited and formerly managing director of APM Terminals, outlined the company’s port investment plans with the Federal Government. He rejected monopoly allegations, saying Intels had invested billions of dollars in infrastructure under Nigerian Ports Authority concessions and contributed substantial fees, employment and specialized oil-and-gas cargo capacity.

Dawes acknowledged challenges including low oil and gas prices and cargo volumes reportedly 70% below earlier levels, but maintained Intels’ long-term investment commitment. Its Phase 4B project includes four kilometres of key length and is ready to accommodate a full floating production, storage and offloading vessel and larger ships. Investment may slow during the recession, but the company said existing capacity could support future growth.

Intels is also progressing the Badagry deep seaport with APM Terminals, which Dawes described as Africa’s largest port by draft and a major growth opportunity. Established 30 years ago, Intels provides integrated logistics, terminal, transit, supply, manpower, equipment, housing and office services to Nigeria’s oil and gas industry.

The paper develops a methodology for studying the dynamics of digital business ecosystems (DBEs), closed or semi-closed networks of small and medium enterprises engaged in buyer–seller relationships. It models each company’s fitness through coupled nonlinear differential equations inspired by neural networks. Company fitness decays without interaction, grows through self-excitation after reaching a critical threshold, and is affected by asymmetric excitatory and inhibitory signals. Excitation depends on matching wanted and offered products, the other company’s strength, and trust; inhibition depends on similarities between companies’ products.

A realistic simulated DBE is generated from observed statistical data, including companies, products, attributes, and trust and mistrust relationships. Companies have SELL and WANT lists, while real and virtual product databases differ in attribute statistics. Trust categories are converted into normalized numerical weights using the Weber–Fechner law.

The model is solved iteratively on a fully connected network, with weak companies removed and new firms optionally introduced. Preliminary experiments use a simulated ecosystem of 100 companies trading 20 products, examining survival over time and parameter settings that produce a monopoly. Proposed improvements include modeling mutual inhibition arising from shared purchasing interests and introducing firms randomly. A major remaining task is linking dynamical model parameters to measurable values from real ecosystems.

Annual low-dose CT screening can reduce lung cancer mortality and diagnose cancers earlier, but low adherence, access barriers, workflow bottlenecks, radiation exposure, and high false-positive rates limit its use. This motivated development of a peripheral blood-based multi-omics classifier combining proteomic, transcriptomic, metabolomic, and targeted immunoassay data.

The observational MOSAIC case-control study enrolled 2,513 adults at 77 U.S. sites, including 2,094 clinically eligible participants with lung cancer or non-cancer controls. After quality control, 1,623 participants had complete multi-omics data and were divided into training (1,225) and validation (398) sets. More than 750,000 protein, transcript, and metabolite features were analyzed, and differential abundance was identified across all assay types.

A gradient-boosted machine-learning classifier achieved training AUCs of 0.91 using proteomics alone and 0.96 using combined multi-omics data for all-stage lung cancer, with an AUC of 0.93 for stage I disease. At a threshold set for 87.5% training sensitivity, the locked classifier achieved 89% sensitivity and 89% specificity in the held-out validation set. Stage-specific sensitivities were 80% for stage I, 88% for stage II, and 99% for stage III-IV disease. The final model used 682 features representing 149 proteins, 346 genes, and 77 metabolic pathways; 60.4% were significantly associated with cancer stage. Prospective validation in the intended high-risk screening population is required before clinical use.

Introduced in 1989 by bond trader Nick Scott, the Camarilla pivot point extends the classical/floor-trader pivot to identify intraday support and resistance. It uses the previous day’s closing price to calculate four support and four resistance levels, nine total. Day traders can use these levels to identify key prices, entries, exits, potential trend reversals, and manage risk. Strategies vary with market conditions and may depend on the opening position relative to the prior close and pivot levels.

Fibonacci pivots instead use price-swing projections, extensions, and retracements. The passage recommends backtesting strategies and notes that a related ordinary-pivot backtest produced no “super profits,” encouraging readers to test their own ideas.

Long-standing concerns about research fraud, paper mills, weak peer review, high publishing costs and “publish-or-perish” incentives are fueling the Trump administration’s attacks on scientific publishing. HHS Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. and NIH Director Jayanta Bhattacharya have changed policies, barred government-funded scientists from certain journals they consider pharmaceutical-controlled, proposed a government journal and caps on article-processing charges, and pledged to prioritize reproducible research and public access. The administration has also terminated hundreds of NIH grants it considers ideologically unacceptable and proposed cutting the NIH budget by 40 percent.

Researchers and former journal editors acknowledge pharmaceutical funding and flawed incentives undermine scientific publishing but argue the administration’s proposals could increase government control, threaten journal independence and worsen the problem. Critics fear its new Journal of the Academy of Public Health could amplify dubious research. The NIH also rescinded a Biden-era mandate requiring immediate deposit of federally funded research in public repositories. While open-access policies and paid peer review have drawn praise, advocates say restoring trust requires broader engagement with the public. Experts caution that an article-processing cap could simply shift costs to libraries and readers, while meaningful incentive reform must involve scientists and academic institutions changing how researchers are evaluated.

The coach praised three players for earning recognition through defensive work and tough minutes, noting increased playoff intensity on both sides. He said the team retained its familiar tactical system because players trusted it, while acknowledging puck possession, forechecking, shot selection, and adjustments against the opponent’s top line were critical in a close Stanley Cup Finals win decided by a Sammy Pahlsson shot. He credited the team’s work ethic and commitment to the system and said fortunate bounces contributed to the result.

He attributed tight regular-season standings partly to the salary cap and a level playing field. Regarding an injured player with pins in his hands, he said skating was optional and described the team’s later practice schedule, hotel check-ins, meals, and pregame naps. He denied publicly criticizing Getzlaf, saying any concerns were minor and discussed privately, and praised Chris Pronger’s size, net-front play, and contribution. Health concerns led him to limit the fourth line and space Carter’s and Motzko’s minutes. He said the response to the previous conference-final loss to Edmonton, followed by Pronger’s acquisition, demonstrated the group’s commitment to improvement and becoming an elite team.

Lookout researchers reported that more than 1,000 Google Play apps contain the SonicSpy spyware family. It can record audio, take photos, make calls, send texts, steal contacts, call logs and Wi-Fi details, and respond to over 73 remote commands. The latest sample, Soniac, masqueraded as a Telegram-based messaging app while hiding its icon, connecting to command-and-control infrastructure and installing a malicious Telegram APK. Two earlier samples linked to “iraqwebservice” were no longer available.

The Supreme Court temporarily paused a federal ruling that barred Homeland Security Secretary Kristi Noem from ending Temporary Protected Status for Venezuelan nationals. In an unsigned order, the justices said the parties’ legal arguments and relative harms had not materially changed despite the case’s new posture. Sotomayor, Kagan and Jackson opposed the order, with Jackson issuing a solo dissent accusing the court of harmful interference in lower-court proceedings and noting the government had shown no time-sensitive need. TPS allows the DHS secretary to authorize citizens of designated countries to remain in the United States and work during extraordinary conditions. Judge Edward Chen previously ruled that Noem’s termination of Venezuela’s 2023 designation and 2025 extension was unlawful after the Ninth Circuit declined to block his judgment.

Manjot Kalra scored an unbeaten century and was named Player of the Match as India won its fourth Under-19 World Cup title in 2018. The 19-year-old was reserved during the post-match presentation but explained to Simon Doull that he enjoyed the match, found the conditions easy and valued the team environment. His century included a six on the first ball and partnerships of 71 and 60 with Prithvi Shaw and Shubman Gill. After Gill’s dismissal, Kalra said he needed to take charge so the incoming batsmen could settle.

Picked by Delhi Daredevils for Rs 20 lakh in the IPL auction, Kalra was widely compared with established Indian cricketers and joined four other players to score a century in an Under-19 World Cup final. None of those four later played for their senior national teams. Head coach Rahul Dravid said the victory would give his players cherished memories but should not define their careers, as greater achievements were still ahead.

Blue Cross Blue Shield of Massachusetts is offering voluntary buyouts to about 750 employees as it reduces its workforce amid soaring health care costs and steep losses. The buyouts target workers age 55 or older with at least 10 years of service, representing 18% of its 4,200-person workforce. They are the insurer’s first buyouts since the late 1980s.

The patent application describes dynamic computer-graphics rendering based on detecting eye saccades that cause saccadic masking. A processor renders a computer-simulated scene, detects the onset of a masking saccade, and reduces CPU or GPU rendering resources during at least part of the saccade. Reductions may include skipping or repeating frames, lowering frame rate, resolution, texture detail, polygon count, shadows, reflections, or other lighting effects. The amount and method of reduction may depend on detection confidence and a frame’s position within the saccade.

Saccades may be detected using cameras, optical, infrared, EMG, reflector, range, Doppler, optical-flow, or microphone sensors, based on changes in eye direction, speed, acceleration, or muscle signals. Embodiments may predict a saccade’s duration using an eye-movement model and measured onset or peak values. Calibration can compare predicted and measured durations to update the model for an individual user.

The techniques may operate on VR, AR, or other real-time scenes in devices including head-mounted displays. They can reduce power consumption and free processing capacity for complex lighting calculations, other applications, or operating-system processes. Method, system, and non-transitory storage-medium embodiments are described.

Microsoft Corporation reported unaudited results for the quarter and six months ended December 31, 2017. Quarterly revenue was $28.918 billion, up from $25.826 billion, as service and other revenue increased to $10.992 billion from $7.553 billion, while product revenue declined to $17.926 billion from $18.273 billion. Gross margin was $17.854 billion and operating income was $8.679 billion. A $15.471 billion income-tax provision produced a $6.302 billion net loss and a diluted loss per share of $0.82, compared with net income of $6.267 billion and diluted earnings of $0.80 in the prior-year quarter. For the six months, revenue was $53.456 billion, operating income was $16.387 billion, and net income was $274 million, or $0.04 per diluted share.

The tax provision included a provisional $13.8 billion net charge related to the Tax Cuts and Jobs Act, consisting of a $17.8 billion transition-tax charge partially offset by a $4.0 billion benefit from tax-rate changes. An estimated $454 million GILTI benefit was also recorded. The company’s effective tax rate was 169% for the quarter and 98% for the six months.

Cash and equivalents were $12.859 billion, and cash, equivalents, and short-term investments totaled $142.780 billion. Six-month operating cash flow was $20.315 billion; investing activities used $7.235 billion, and financing activities used $7.893 billion.

Microsoft adopted the revenue-recognition standard using the full retrospective method and the lease standard using a modified retrospective approach, restating prior periods and recognizing operating lease right-of-use assets and liabilities. It also disclosed pending guidance on hedging, intra-entity asset transfers, credit losses, and financial instruments.

At period-end, the recorded basis of investments was $146.741 billion, including $129.921 billion of short-term investments. Derivatives were used to manage foreign-currency, equity-price, interest-rate, and credit risks. Unrealized investment losses totaled $785 million, which management did not consider other-than-temporary. Commercial paper outstanding was $12.5 billion, and long-term debt including the current portion had a carrying value of $76.8 billion and estimated fair value of $81.7 billion.

Contracted but unrecognized revenue was $61 billion, with approximately 60% expected to be recognized within 12 months. The company had $33.4 billion remaining under its share-repurchase authorization. Legal liabilities totaled $370 million, and reasonably possible adverse outcomes exceeding recorded amounts were estimated at approximately $1.3 billion.

Teacher Greg Boykin’s Auto Collision Repair program replaced panels and restored the vehicle, saving the city about $10,000. Donated materials supported the project, and the cruiser will return to service as a zone car.

UOB strategists see a near-term GBP drop to 1.2900 as unlikely, though possible. A slow rise toward 1.3040/45 may occur; support is 1.2975 and 1.2939, while a clear break above 1.3060 would end the bearish phase.

The guide demonstrates how to build and backtest an RSI trading strategy in TradingView using Pine Script for DOT on a five-minute chart. The strategy uses a 14-period RSI with overbought and oversold levels of 65 and 35. It enters long when RSI moves above 35 after being below it, enters short when RSI moves below 65 after being above it, and closes positions when RSI crosses 50.

The process involves creating a chart, adding and configuring RSI, opening a Pine Script strategy template, defining RSI calculations and entry conditions with `strategy.entry`, closing positions with `strategy.close`, and adding conditional statements and editable user inputs. After adding the strategy to the chart, TradingView displays an equity curve, net profit, drawdown, win rate, and other performance statistics. Standard backtesting is limited to the chart’s displayed history, while Pro or higher accounts can perform deep backtests using available historical data, including DOT data since 2019. Users can select date ranges, review metrics such as Sharpe Ratio and average risk-to-reward ratio, and export trade data to CSV with a paid account. The guide notes that RSI alone has not performed consistently and may be more useful alongside other indicators or criteria.

The passage compares college campuses to small towns and student newsrooms to local news, arguing that removing campus journalism would deprive students of information about relevant issues and events. It says news deserts harm small towns and that an informed public is essential to understanding government, social movements, and voting choices. It also cites media concentration and “pack journalism” as reducing news diversity and urges support for student newsrooms to prepare students as informed future workers.

This study examined the needs and developed strategies for improving vocational education management in Thailand amid Industry 4.0, technological disruption, workforce mismatches, and labor shortages, particularly in the Eastern Economic Corridor. Using a two-phase research and development approach, the researchers analyzed relevant literature, surveyed 206 respondents from eight types of Office of Vocational Education Commission institutions, and interviewed representatives from three exemplary vocational schools. Current conditions were rated high, while desired conditions were rated highest. The greatest requirement gaps were identified in curriculum development, cooperation networks, and personnel.

The resulting framework included a vision, mission, objectives, six strategies, and key performance indicators. The strategies were to enhance professional management efficiency; develop competency-based curricula aligned with international standards and employer needs; improve teaching and learning; develop teachers and staff as specialized professionals; build comprehensive cooperation networks; and produce graduates with competencies, ethics, professional attributes, and certifications aligned with labor-market needs. The strategies also emphasized digital platforms, active learning, dual vocational education, upskilling, reskilling, and new-skill development.

A focus group of nine experts rated the overall strategies as highly appropriate and feasible. Recommendations were to prioritize competency-based curriculum development and adapt implementation to each institution’s needs and existing plans. Future research should examine curriculum models integrating professional competencies with qualification systems and methods for strengthening digital-content production and internationally recognized professional competencies.

American Mint’s Band of Brothers Men’s Ring is 24k gold-layered, available in sizes 8–14, and priced at $129.90 for a limited time. Order it online or by phone. It honors those who sacrificed to preserve liberty and independence.

Freelance science writer David Dickinson recounts his interest in eclipses as the August 21 total solar eclipse approaches. The moon’s shadow will cross the United States from Oregon to South Carolina, providing up to 2 minutes and 40 seconds of totality along a narrow path. Eclipse chasers, known as umbraphiles, travel for the spectacle, which they describe as singular and indescribable. After missing earlier opportunities, Dickinson plans to watch from North Carolina for 107 seconds, though clouds could interfere.

Dickinson warns that viewing the partially eclipsed sun requires ISO 12312-2-approved glasses or properly filtered telescopes and binoculars; only totality allows unprotected viewing. He also recommends pinhole projection and cautions against counterfeit glasses. He suggests the eclipse could renew public interest in science. Dickinson notes that total eclipses will eventually cease as the moon recedes from Earth and identifies the April 8, 2024 eclipse, which will cross his hometown in Maine, as another opportunity.

Since January 2000, a QQQ mean-reversion strategy has reportedly delivered a 12.34% CAGR from $100,000, with a high profit factor and lower drawdown than buy-and-hold’s 9% CAGR. Trades exit when the close exceeds the previous day’s high or close; future performance remains uncertain.

A PubMed review found only 15 publications evaluating the maturity of AI models in healthcare. This study assessed peer-reviewed AI healthcare publications from 2019–2021 using a BERT classifier based on titles and abstracts, alongside manual annotations of data, model, disease, specialty, and author geography. The classifier achieved 99% accuracy in test and prospective validation, with F1 scores of 93% and 91%, respectively. Overall, only 385 publications—about 5%—were classified as mature. Radiology had the most mature publications across the three years, while COVID-19 studies had low maturity rates of 4% in 2020 and 1.6% in 2021. Mature publications were geographically concentrated, with the United States leading in 2019–2020 and China in 2021; South America, Eastern Europe, and Africa were underrepresented. Image-based data dominated mature research, appearing in approximately 88–89% of publications annually, while text data increased and tabular data declined. Deep learning was the most common model type, followed by classical machine learning. The findings indicate a need for more clinically relevant, diverse, and globally representative AI healthcare research.

The passage describes the London breakout strategy, a forex day-trading approach that marks the Asian-session range and trades an upside or downside break during the London session, usually within its first three hours. It explains the high-low and open-close range definitions, a breakout indicator with entry, stop-loss, and take-profit levels, and the strategy’s rationale and session timings. However, EUR/USD backtests showed losses on upward breakouts and near-zero average gains on faded breakouts, leading the authors to question its profitability and favor stocks and bonds. The passage also notes automation, time-zone and daylight-saving adjustments, and that the strategy code is included in a separate package of backtestable trading strategies.

**Summary**

This study examines bulk MnBi₂Te₄/(Bi₂Te₃)ₙ superlattice crystals grown by the Inverted Vertical Bridgman Method (IVBM), in which Mn-doped Bi₂Te₃ self-organizes into ferromagnetic septuple layers (SLs, Te-Bi-Te-Mn-Te-Bi-Te) embedded within Bi₂Te₃ quintuple layers (QLs, Te-Bi-Te-Bi-Te) separated by van der Waals gaps. Crystals were grown from 99.999% Bi and Te with in-house MnTe (4.2:3.9:1.9 weight ratio) in sealed ampoules, annealed at 575 K for 24 h, and characterized by TEM/EDX, SEM/EDX, SQUID magnetometry, and X-band magnetic resonance.

Four ingot sections show distinct structure and magnetism. Sample A (top) is pure MnBi₂Te₄ with MnBi₂Te₄/Bi₂Te₃ inclusions (13.5 ± 1.9 at.% Mn), showing antiferromagnetic transitions at TN = 26 K and 13.5 K. Sample B contains SLs separated by one or two QLs (7.2 ± 1.1 at.%) with a single AFM transition at 13.5 K. Sample C shows SLs grouped at 7 ± 2 QL spacing (1.14 ± 0.17 at.%) and ferromagnetic behavior with TC ≈ 11 K; Sample D (ingot end) is disordered with 4–5 QL spacing, intersecting Mn-rich multilayers, 1.9 ± 0.3 at.% Mn, and TC ≈ 9 K. Mn within SLs falls from ~14 at.% to ~5 at.% in Sample D. Ferromagnetic samples show FMR below TC with anisotropy fields of ~460 mT (C) and ~370 mT (D), uniaxial anisotropy constants of 4300 and 1700 J m⁻³, and saturation magnetizations of ~1.2 and ~0.6 emu g⁻¹.

Four growth regimes were identified: turbulent flow (suppresses MnTe precipitation, yielding pure MnBi₂Te₄), rapid MnTe precipitation (Mn drops from ~14 to ~7 at.%), stationary flow (ordered QL/SL assembly), and cessation of flow (diffusive transport, Mn depletion, stacking inversion). A Chernov/van der Eerden-based model shows an inverse relation between SL spacing and MnTe supersaturation, with diffusion-limited competition between MnBi₂Te₄ edges; SL nucleation on Bi₂Te₃ (~5 eV) is energetically unfavorable versus formation enthalpy (~5 meV), so defects serve as nucleation sites. Mn in QLs stays below 1 at.%. Long-range stacking order persists over tens of micrometers, stabilized by the elastic energy difference between SLs and QLs. Conclusions emphasize control of melt composition and flow dynamics for tuning layer spacing, magnetism, and topology in bulk magnetic topological insulators.

The paper investigates antiferromagnetic domain-wall dynamics under spin-orbit torque, focusing on the absence of stray fields and the optical, electrical, and current-induced manipulation of antiferromagnetic textures. A discrete spin-chain model includes antiferromagnetic exchange, Dzyaloshinskii–Moriya interaction, perpendicular anisotropy, damping, and polarized-electron spin torque. A continuum tetramer-based model extends the nonlinear σ-model with damping and torque, while the magnetization of dynamic textures is related to \( \mathbf n \times \dot{\mathbf n} \).

For perpendicular spin polarization and no DM interaction, simulations evolve a static 180° domain wall into a steady state in which all spins precess about the polarization direction. Using spherical parametrization, the continuum equations predict damped azimuthal motion, \( \Phi=c e^{-\alpha\tau}+\omega\tau \), with \( \omega=-\beta/\alpha \); the transient decays, leaving stable precession.

The broader study also obtains constant-velocity domain-wall propagation that is not a simple Lorentz transformation of the static wall and periodic oscillations for polarization containing both in-plane and perpendicular components. Damping-induced Lorentz-invariance breaking is included, and the paper organizes the analysis into modeling, precessional dynamics, propagation, oscillatory motion, and conclusions.

California’s Department of Fish and Wildlife re-approved Newhall Ranch’s plan after an additional environmental analysis resolved concerns about greenhouse gas emissions and protection of the unarmored threespine stickleback. The re-approval followed a 2015 California Supreme Court order requiring closer review of the project’s emissions and two fish-mitigation measures. FivePoint revised its Net Zero Newhall plan with 13 measures, and the state Air Resources Board found adequate grounds to conclude the project would cause no net additional emissions. Revised bridge and bank-stabilization construction methods would prevent water contact and eliminate the need for the fish-protection measures. The Los Angeles County Board of Supervisors is expected to consider final approval of the first two villages in July.

Young African entrepreneurs are using technology to make agriculture more sustainable, profitable and resilient to climate change while creating jobs and strengthening food security. Rwandan entrepreneur Jean Bosco Nzeyimana’s Habona Ltd. employs 25 young people to sort garbage, turn organic waste into cooking-fuel briquettes and produce organic fertilizer, reducing open-burning emissions and producing 50 tonnes of fuel monthly.

In Malawi, Pilirani Khoza’s Bunda Female Students Organisation sponsors female students who train disadvantaged women farmers in water conservation and drought- and flood-resilient techniques, reaching 360 farmers. In Kenya, Brian Bosire’s UjuziKilimo developed a handheld soil-quality sensor; extension agents use it to send farmers crop and input advice via mobile phones, and the company aims to reach 200,000 farmers.

Agriculture employs nearly two-thirds of Africa’s population and could reduce poverty two to four times faster than other sectors. Young people are presented as important drivers of agricultural transformation, climate adaptation, employment and progress toward ending hunger and poverty.

The study characterized the genetic landscape of Multiple Endocrine Neoplasia (MEN) in India by analyzing variants in RET, MEN1, and CDKN1B from IndiGen, ClinVar, and Mastermind. Variants were annotated and assessed individually against 28 ACMG/AMP criteria using the Genetic Variant Interpretation Tool. After filtering, 1,324 unique variants were classified; adding variants classified by ClinVar expert panels produced the MAPVar database, containing 3,280 variants: 1,094 pathogenic/likely pathogenic, 1,591 benign/likely benign, and 595 variants of uncertain significance. MAPVar is searchable by variant ID, nucleotide or amino-acid change, and dbSNP identifier, and provides annotations, population frequencies, computational predictions, classification criteria, and final classifications.

Two likely pathogenic RET variants in IndiGen were used to estimate that approximately 1 in 341 Indians is a likely carrier of a MEN-linked pathogenic RET variant. One variant was found in Jammu and Kashmir and the other in two individuals from Odisha. Across 18 population datasets, the first variant was not detected, while the second occurred at low frequencies outside India but at a higher frequency in IndiGen (0.000977); the frequency difference was significant at p<0.05. The authors noted that the second variant relied only on non-functional supporting evidence but was retained because no stringency cutoff had been established.

MAPVar identified seven cases in the GUaRDIAN endocrine cohort, including four provisional MEN diagnoses and three suggestive of pheochromocytoma, with five unique variants. A multiplex sequencing panel covering all coding regions of RET, MEN1, and CDKN1B was also developed, comprising 38 amplicons in two pools across 65 kb and 33 exons. Testing of 72 patients with endocrine disorders resolved three cases with known pathogenic MEN1 variants, changing provisional diagnoses of acromegaly, pheochromocytoma, and insulinoma to MEN1.

The authors concluded that MEN remains understudied in India, that further Indian-specific research is needed for all three genes, particularly CDKN1B, and that the MAPVar database and sequencing panel can support variant interpretation, early diagnosis, and carrier detection.

News clippings dated Nov. 19–20, 2001, centered on Enron’s worsening financial and liquidity problems. In a delayed, unaudited SEC filing, Enron widened its third-quarter loss to $664 million, or 87 cents per share, after previously reporting losses of $618 million and $635 million. It increased nine-month earnings by one cent per share. Enron said financial statements from 1997 through the first half of 2001 should no longer be relied upon; earlier restatements reduced reported profits by $586 million, revised debt upward, reduced shareholder equity by about $1.2 billion and included more than $1 billion of investment write-offs. The figures remained subject to review by Arthur Andersen and Enron’s special investigative committee.

Enron warned that credit concerns, declining asset values and reduced trading could hurt fourth-quarter results. It said a fall in Enron’s share price could produce a $700 million pretax derivative loss at Whitewing LLP, whose assets had a book value of $4.7 billion. A Standard & Poor’s downgrade to BBB- on Nov. 12 also made a $690 million partnership obligation a demand obligation. Enron had to repay the note or provide equivalent collateral by late November or face liquidation of partnership assets, including a Brazilian natural-gas company it was seeking to sell. It was negotiating with lenders for a waiver, refinancing or extension.

A further downgrade below investment grade could trigger another $3.9 billion of partnership debt repayments, including $2.4 billion owed by Osprey Trust and $915 million by Marlin Water Trust. Reports described Enron as having limited liquidity relative to $9.15 billion in obligations due by the end of 2002. The company had maxed out a credit line, obtained new loans, sought $500 million to $1 billion in equity investment, planned asset sales and was developing a plan to exit $8 billion in noncore businesses. Enron warned that adverse financing or asset-sale outcomes could materially affect its ability to continue as a going concern.

Wall Street bankers questioned whether Dynegy’s roughly $9.8 billion stock acquisition of Enron would close because the agreement’s “material adverse change” provisions could allow Dynegy to withdraw. Rating agencies were concerned that Enron’s SEC investigation, litigation, balance-sheet weakness and earnings forecasts could trigger those provisions. Enron shareholders sued to block the merger, alleging that its directors accepted inadequate consideration without sufficiently investigating alternatives; Enron said it would defend the action. Dynegy could reportedly terminate the transaction if partnership-related judgments exceeded $2 billion or total liabilities reached $3.5 billion, and at least 23 related lawsuits had been reported. ChevronTexaco, which owned about 27% of Dynegy, was financing the bid while reviewing Enron’s litigation exposure.

The SEC continued investigating Enron’s accounting, disclosure practices and affiliated partnerships, including structures formerly managed by former CFO Andrew Fastow. Andersen had not completed its review of Enron’s third-quarter statements. Rep. John Dingell requested a special investigation of Andersen’s audits of Enron and Waste Management and questioned conflicts in the accounting industry’s peer-review process; Andersen had previously reached a $7 million SEC settlement over Waste Management without admitting or denying the allegations.

Other reports said Enron’s Azurix unit might have to sell assets if it could not refinance debt; ChevronTexaco increased projected merger savings to $1.8 billion by March 2003; and ConocoPhillips’s decision to base its combined company in Houston reinforced Houston’s status as an energy-industry center. Additional briefs covered executive severance, corporate hiring, other companies’ earnings and stock movements.

The Supreme Court debated whether the U.S. Postal Service and federal government can be sued for intentionally failing to deliver mail. The case concerns a statutory “postal exception” to sovereign immunity covering mail losses, miscarriages and negligent transmission. It stems from Texas landlord Lebene Konan’s allegations that postal workers intentionally withheld mail as racial harassment. The government warned that a broad ruling could spur lawsuits, while Konan’s lawyer and several justices said deliberate misconduct differs from ordinary loss or negligence. A decision is expected by early July.

R. Thomas Beach, principal consultant with Crossborder Energy, submitted rebuttal testimony before the California Public Utilities Commission on behalf of past, present, and future electric-generation customers of Southern California Gas Company and San Diego Gas & Electric. He urged the Commission to reject the Southern California Generation Coalition’s and The Utility Reform Network’s Post-Interim Settlement Agreement (PISA) because it deferred intrastate transmission unbundling, and instead adopt the Comprehensive Settlement Agreement filed by more than 20 parties.

Beach disputed SCGC and TURN’s claim that structural differences between PG&E and SoCalGas justify delaying unbundling. He argued that both systems lacked firm, nondiscriminatory transmission rights and had experienced similar discriminatory-access and conflict-of-interest problems. He also maintained that SoCalGas’s backbone and local transmission facilities serve the same functions as PG&E’s and can be unbundled similarly. Statewide consistency was important because electric generators increasingly operate across multiple utility territories.

Beach cited benefits from PG&E’s city-gate market, including transportation-cost savings of $0.03–$0.08 per Dth and, from May 1999 through April 2000, PG&E city-gate prices $0.05–$0.11 per Dth below border purchases plus full backbone transportation. He argued that noncore customers had received these savings through marketers without holding capacity or paying demand charges.

According to Beach, the Comprehensive Settlement would reduce electric-generator rates by about $3 million annually in 2002, or roughly $0.01 per Dth, and place about half of those rates outside SoCalGas’s contested long-run marginal-cost design. It would also reduce risks by assigning SoCalGas shareholders responsibility for backbone cost recovery, using embedded transmission costs through August 2006, applying a defined 79% load factor, lowering customer storage-revenue risk to 25%, and unbundling transmission, storage, and balancing services.

Beach also criticized SCGC and TURN’s demand-charge analysis as based on unrealistic assumptions. Their study assumed generators would contract for maximum theoretical daily gas use, would not resell excess capacity, and would ignore interruptible service, city-gate purchases, and secondary capacity markets. Re calculated under interruptible service, he said annual fixed costs would rise only 0.6%. He noted that the settlement offered a lower-demand alternative, interruptible service at a premium of no more than $0.0144 per Dth, excess SoCalGas transmission and storage capacity, and protections against capacity concentration.

Finally, Beach rejected claims that demand charges would cause plant closures, electric-reliability problems, or a severe gas-and-electricity price squeeze. He cited the projected rate reduction, the absence of supporting financial data, and evidence that PG&E city-gate gas prices were highly correlated with wholesale electric prices. He further stated that adequate basin capacity reduced local market-power concerns and that additional Reliability Must-Run contracts could provide cost recovery if generators exited.

This article offers a structured methodology for designing sustainable business models for faculty-led education abroad programs, drawing on the authors' two decades of experience building global programs and advising universities across six continents.

**Context.** Although U.S. institutions increasingly emphasize global competencies in their mission statements, only about one percent of students in U.S. higher education participate in study abroad programs (NAFSA, 2023). Non-travel options—global coursework, virtual exchanges, collaborative assignments—provide accessible, cost-effective alternatives for students constrained by financial, personal, or visa barriers, while immersive travel remains valuable for fostering intercultural understanding, empathy, leadership, cross-cultural communication, and language skills. Financial cost is the most persistent barrier to scaling programs, and few replicable frameworks exist for creating financially viable initiatives.

**Three primary drivers.** Curricular, operational, and financial dimensions are interdependent and must be addressed together, with learning outcomes guiding design.

*Curricular logistics* cover learning outcomes (including whether participation is elective or required, credit amounts, when credits are earned, and assessment and reflection), strategic alignment with the host institution's priorities, the competitive landscape among existing programs, locational efficacy and risk, engagement modalities (site visits, partner coursework, research, service-learning, design-build projects), and program duration (short-term of 1–10 days, mid-term of 11–30 days, or extended quarter/trimester/semester formats).

*Operational logistics* encompass program design, on-the-ground operations, and ongoing support, addressing risk management (safety, insurance, emergency response, reputational risk), program leadership (faculty, external partners, or students, with a co-leader recommended), travel timing (weather, cultural events, tourism seasons, exchange rates), travel organization and documentation, flights, lodging, partner coordination, local transport, communication, meals and dietary needs, entertainment, emergency preparation, student orientation, student wellbeing, and ongoing problem support.

*Financial logistics* require keeping expenditures at or below generated income: outflows for faculty, operational support, external parties, projects, and coordination; income from student tuition and fees (fees typically flow directly to the program); internal and external funding such as grants and corporate sponsorships; and internal budget distribution, including need- and merit-based scholarships.

**Typology.** Based on a review of articles in *Frontiers: The Interdisciplinary Journal of Study Abroad* and the *Journal of Studies in International Education* plus 14 informal interviews, the authors identify twelve business model types. External-party-led programs (for example, CIEE, IES Abroad, GREEN, ThinkImpact) cover all costs through student fees. Faculty-led programs may be student payment-driven, revenue-driven, corporate donation-driven, or grant-driven. Student-led models, typically non-credit and club-based (Global Brigades, Bridges to Prosperity, Engineers Without Borders), rely on charitable donations and student activity fees.

**Conclusion.** Three principles emerge: revenue from community engagement or corporate sponsorships can ease financial burdens; dedicated staff support reduces faculty workload; and delegating planning to students supports their development. The work was supported by the Council on Engaged Scholarship at Penn State.

A mouse study suggests black tea may promote health and weight loss by changing intestinal bacteria, increasing microbes associated with lean body mass and reducing those associated with obesity. Both teas are prebiotics, and combining them may be especially beneficial.

The goalie said Zdeno was bigger on the first power play and the puck was hard to find, so he adjusted, left Zdeno alone, and tried to steer shots toward the side. This article (Turkish Online Journal of Distance Education, July 2024, Vol. 25, No. 3, Art. 13226) by Serap Ugur, Gokhan Deniz Dincer, and Didem Pasaoglu Bas of Anadolu University examines how advanced technologies used in the digitalization of higher education institutions affect management in open and distance education, aiming to forecast the future and produce a roadmap for transformation.

The introduction and literature review note that technology shapes organizations, work, quality, and management techniques, and that distance education, which extends higher education beyond time and space, is among the services most affected by technological change. Perrow's work on technology and organizational structure is adopted as the theoretical basis. Advanced technologies reviewed include artificial intelligence (from its 1956 Dartmouth origin through artificial general and superintelligence and technological singularity), wearable technologies, the metaverse (with 5G, AI, and blockchain), brain-computer interfaces (including the Neuralink project), and blockchain applications in ECTS credit transfer, micro-credentials, educational process management, and integration with IoT, AI, VR, and AR. The text also reviews studies on technology in management and Business Education, arguing institutions must embrace new technologies to remain relevant.

Method: a qualitative case study. Four academics at Anadolu University with at least 20 years' experience in open and distance education and at least 10 years in distance education management were interviewed via semi-structured interviews, recorded verbatim and translated; transcripts totaled 2,442 words. Content analysis followed Braun and Clarke (2006) and George (1959), conducted in Nvivo 1.7.1 across six phases from familiarity with data to frequency counting, with researcher triangulation for validity.

Findings cover management stages, organizational structuring, effects on practice and services, economy, and socio-cultural change. Experts agreed advanced technologies (AI, blockchain, metaverse, brain chips, VR/AR) will radically affect every stage of distance education. Reported themes included the need for careful decision processes, planning, and analysis before integration; high initial costs offset later savings; training AI with accurate, current data; and continuing human mistrust of unmanned systems. Predictions included AI assistants and managers at all organizational levels, shifts from hierarchical to horizontal and network structures, reduced hierarchies, AI-supported planning, supervision, evaluation, and anomaly detection, AI-generated synthetic content, adaptive learning, personal AI teaching assistants, virtual selves and internships in the metaverse, brain chips with blockchain for recognizing prior learning and backing up brain traces, and universities repositioning around assessment while open course materials reduce institutional dependence. Economically, experts expected unemployment and the disappearance of entry-level white-collar roles alongside higher productivity, profit, exports, new business areas, and new technology-management roles, with further investment and infrastructure costs; the text cites PwC and Accenture estimates of AI's global economic contribution. Socio-culturally, experts raised concerns about laziness, dependence, reduced screen-free life, virtual addiction, and psychological and biological problems, while predicting a "meta-culture" of people existing in both physical and virtual worlds and urging work on rights, legal regulation, and ethics in these societies, plus technology literacy training.

The conclusion identifies education and management as the main themes, recommends developing AI assistants and managers, blockchain-based certification and recognition applications, adaptive synthetic content, metaverse-oriented teaching systems and virtual selves, and further research on brain-computer interfaces and brain chips, and suggests larger-scale qualitative and quantitative studies across geographies.

Officials marked completion of the 179-megawatt Switch Station 1 and Switch Station 2 solar projects north of Las Vegas, commissioned Dec. 11, 2017, to power Switch data centers in Reno and Las Vegas. Designed to generate enough electricity for 46,000 Nevada homes, the arrays increased the state’s operating solar plants to 16.

The telegram assesses Andropov’s foreign policy as continuing Brezhnev’s hard line, with no relaxation on Afghanistan, Poland, or Southern Africa. KGI’s Ming-Chi Kuo expects cellular and non-cellular 38mm and 42mm Apple Watch Series 3 models with LTE-only modems, potentially complicating India availability. He forecasts 17.5–18 million Watch sales next year, including 2.8–3.6 million LTE units.

This continuation application describes neural-modulation systems and methods for programming lead electrodes to create directional, linear electric fields over neural tissue. A target multipole with progressively stacked anodic and cathodic poles determines electrode fractionalizations, with embodiments incorporating additional, aligned, flanking, or directional electrodes. Programming controls may adjust field angle, focus, spread, and therapy strength, accept user-drawn anatomical regions or identified pain areas, automatically move the multipole, or use search heuristics to optimize pole spacing, amplitude, orientation, field extent, and width.

For spinal-cord stimulation, the application discusses targeting dorsal horn and dorsal root tissue over dorsal column tissue by shaping broad, uniform fields and reducing longitudinal voltage gradients associated with dorsal-column activation. Electrode calibration and forward/inverse modeling account for electrode-tissue coupling and map desired electric fields to physical electrodes through least-squares optimization. Described hardware includes percutaneous or paddle leads, implantable and external generators, trial stimulators, clinician programmers, remote controls, telemetry, and independently timed electrode channels.

The disclosure also covers conventional and sub-perception spinal-cord stimulation, differing activation functions of dorsal horn/root and dorsal column elements, current fractionalization, edge guarding, current steering, field gradients, and interface controls for user-defined targeting.

Senators criticized Supreme Court trial deadlines, saying the “Jordan” ruling lacked impact data and could cause tens of thousands of charges to be dismissed. A Senate report made 50 recommendations for a broader justice-system rethink.

John Bryant, proceeding pro se under 42 U.S.C. § 1983, alleged that DOCS, Sing Sing Correctional Facility, and Officer Hanser Hernandez violated inmates’ constitutional rights through a 20-day “Code Blue” lockdown. The lockdown followed Hernandez’s false report that ammunition had been found. During cell searches, prison personnel allegedly read inmates’ legal mail and disregarded personal property. Inmates were also denied showers, recreation, library access, mail, telephone calls, hot meals, clean linen, religious services, and routine medical or dental care. Bryant also alleged inadequate compensation and restrictions on collective bargaining.

The court granted DOCS’s motion to dismiss and dismissed the claims against Sing Sing because both were state agencies entitled to Eleventh Amendment immunity; New York had not consented to the suit, and § 1983 did not abrogate that immunity. Bryant’s individual-capacity claim against Hernandez could proceed if proper service was established. Bryant sought injunctive relief rather than damages and was directed to report the status of service upon Hernandez.

The government is consulting on stronger measures to hold directors accountable following failures such as Carillion and BHS. Proposals include reversing asset stripping to recover funds for workers, disqualifying directors who sell struggling firms, and expanding Insolvency Service powers. Opposition figures welcomed greater accountability but criticized the government for delaying action.

The Grand River Conservation Authority will spend $1.8 million on LiDAR mapping of the Speed and Conestogo rivers and the entire Grand River floodplain over five years. The resulting 3D maps will integrate with U.S. Army Corps of Engineers software to provide near-real-time forecasts, identify threatened properties and support emergency notifications. The project will replace hard-copy maps, some over 40 years old, and capture riverbed changes. It was planned before June’s sudden flood.

Engineers developed a rapid, nonlethal optical screening method for analyzing large numbers of natural and synthetic proteins, including those produced inside living bacteria. The approach combines flow cytometry, femtosecond and picosecond lasers, and time-domain thermo-transmission to examine proteins individually as they pass in single file. Screening occurs in milliseconds without significantly heating samples or altering their crystalline structure, allowing living cells to survive and selected proteins to be separated. The proof-of-concept work included synthetic proteins adapted from water-resistant squid ring teeth proteins, which may be useful in marine environments. The team received Defense University Research Instrumentation Program funding to develop larger-scale screening capabilities.
A hockey team prepares for a must-win game by emphasizing focus, defensive improvements, reviewing tapes, and staying fresh against a strong Detroit lineup.

The paper proposes a time-based methodology for a trusting agent to assess failure risk before interacting with a probable trusted agent in a digital business ecosystem. Risk is defined as the probability of interaction failure and its possible consequences. The proposed FailureLevel metric, assessed against a scale from 0 to 5, expresses the likelihood that the trusted agent cannot meet the interaction’s context and criteria.

The analysis divides time into non-overlapping slots and separates pre-interaction and post-interaction periods. Pre-interaction FailureLevels (PFLs) are determined from matching past interactions or recommendations from other agents. Recommendations are filtered by trustworthiness, timing, and criteria relevance, then weighted by recommender trustworthiness, recency, and the significance of each criterion.

Post-interaction FailureLevels (FFLs) are predicted using prior FailureLevels, their mean and variance, and a Gaussian distribution to calculate the probability of each failure level. The level with the highest probability becomes the FFL for that time slot and informs subsequent predictions.

A transportation example compares two candidate agents; their most probable post-interaction FailureLevels are 2 and 1. The remaining task is to assess the consequences of failure to complete the risk analysis.

Cincinnati upset No. 14 Iowa State 38-30, leading 31-7 at halftime and handing the Cyclones their first loss, opening the Big 12 race. The article compares the result to last season’s chaotic conference standings, when BYU and Arizona State tied for the regular-season title with Iowa State and Deion Sanders’ team. Additional headlines cover Alabama–Vanderbilt, Arch Manning, Clemson, Texas, and Penn State.

Kazakhstan’s education programs aimed to expand inclusive schooling, with targets of 70% of schools providing inclusive conditions and 20% ensuring unhindered access for disabled children by 2020, followed by 2020–2025 goals emphasizing flexible and professional skills. UNESCO identifies inclusive education as system inclusiveness, equal access to quality education, and social inclusion. The passage also reviews the right of people with disabilities to education and the shift to distance education during COVID-19, highlighting technological integration, communication, and teacher preparation.

This qualitative case study evaluated inclusive distance education for disabled students through interviews with ten special education teachers in Kazakhstan. Online, semi-structured interviews lasting 30–35 minutes were analyzed thematically. Teachers used online lessons, video sharing, homework, online activities, and mobile applications. Seven preferred formal education, two regarded distance and formal education as similar, and one favored distance education. Six teachers considered distance education insufficient for meeting students’ individual learning needs, while three found it partly sufficient and one found it sufficient. Reported family-participation problems included anxiety, inadequate technology, poor communication, and insufficient online family education. Teacher–student and peer interaction was described as weak, limited by time, unqualified, or disorganized.

Recommendations were to diversify technology-based teaching and provide infrastructure, develop content based on students’ individual needs, organize online seminars to support family participation, and provide technology-supported social activities to strengthen teacher, student, and peer interaction.

This medRxiv preprint examines shared transcriptomic features of Alzheimer’s disease (AD) and epilepsy using RNA-sequencing data from the Knight ADRC, Mount Sinai Brain Bank, and ROSMAP cohorts. It focuses on an AD “synaptic plasticity dysfunction” profile characterized by severe cognitive decline, neurodegeneration, and shorter survival. Of 105 epilepsy-associated genes examined, 16 were dysregulated across all three cohorts; 15 were consistently downregulated and CERS1 was upregulated. Nine shared genes were primarily synaptic, including ARHGEF9, GABRA1, GABRB3, GABRG2, GRIN2A, HCN1, NECAP1, SCN1A, and SCN8A. Pathway analysis identified enrichment in glutamatergic and GABAergic synapses, ion transport, channel activity, and synaptic transmission. In ROSMAP, dysregulation of 25 epilepsy-associated genes was concordant in early and late AD but more pronounced at later stages, with 23 downregulated and CERS1 and WWOX upregulated. The results support shared mechanisms involving synaptic dysfunction, neuronal excitability, GABAergic and glutamatergic signaling, and potentially mitochondrial and ceramide biology. They suggest that epileptic mechanisms may precede or coexist with early AD pathology, while AD-related changes may also increase hyperexcitability and seizure risk; however, which condition occurs first remains uncertain. The findings support seizure detection and management in AD, phenotype-based stratification, and possible shared therapeutic targets.

The speaker bids farewell as his presidential term ends, three days before the authority of the presidency passes to his successor, wishes the new President well, and expresses gratitude for his largely cooperative relationship with the Congress, which he credits with serving the national good rather than partisanship.

He observes that the century has witnessed four major wars, three involving the United States, yet America remains the world's strongest, most influential and most productive nation. He cautions that its leadership and prestige depend not merely on material and military strength but on how power is used to advance world peace and human betterment. America's aims of keeping the peace, fostering progress, and enhancing liberty, dignity and integrity are threatened by a global, atheistic, ruthless and insidious ideology, demanding steady, sustained sacrifice rather than crisis-driven expedients. He urges balance between the private and public economy, cost and advantage, necessity and comfort, national requirements and individual duties, and present action and future welfare.

He names two new threats: the permanent armaments industry and immense military establishment, which together create a military-industrial complex whose misplaced power could endanger liberties and democratic processes, requiring an alert and informed citizenry; and the technological revolution, which has formalized research, shifted it from individual inventors and free universities to government-directed laboratories and computers, and risks both the domination of scholars by federal employment and the captivity of public policy by a scientific-technological elite. Statesmanship must mold and balance these forces within democratic principles. He also warns against consuming tomorrow's resources at the expense of future generations' political and spiritual heritage.

Finally, he urges a world becoming ever smaller to replace fear and hate with a confederation of mutual trust among equals, pursuing disarmament and composing differences with intellect rather than arms. He confesses disappointment that lasting peace is not yet in sight, though war has been avoided, and pledges continued private effort. He closes with thanks, a call to remain steadfast in the faith that all nations under God will reach peace with justice, and a prayer that peoples of all faiths, races and nations have their human needs met, learn charity, see poverty, disease and ignorance disappear, and live together in peace grounded in mutual respect and love.

The Tax Court addressed gift and estate tax deficiencies arising from six $3,000 checks delivered to six donees on December 24, 1980, and six additional $3,000 checks delivered and paid on January 28, 1981. The issue was whether the noncharitable gifts were complete when the checks were delivered.

The court found petitioner had not proven unconditional delivery because the initial checks were not cashed for 35 days, the record did not establish whether the decedent’s account contained sufficient funds or whether she intended to make gifts, and the delayed cashing cast doubt on delivery. The court therefore declined to extend the relation-back doctrine, previously applied to charitable gifts, to these cases.

Under Oklahoma law, delivery of a donor’s personal check does not itself transfer the represented funds. The donees gave no consideration, were not holders in due course, and the decedent retained the ability to stop payment and assert failure of consideration. Accordingly, the decedent parted with dominion and control only when the bank paid the checks in 1981. The gifts therefore did not qualify for 1980 annual exclusions, $36,000 was includible in the gross estate, and the six-year limitations period applied rather than the three-year period.

NVIDIA’s GA10x Ampere architecture introduces second-generation RT Cores, third-generation Tensor Cores, structural sparsity, and support for GDDR6X memory, delivering claimed performance improvements of up to twice the previous generation in programmable shading, ray tracing, and AI. Fine-Grained Structured Sparsity trains networks with dense weights, prunes them to a 2-out-of-4 non-zero pattern, and fine-tunes the remaining weights. Evaluations across dozens of vision, language, and translation networks showed virtually no inference-accuracy loss, while providing a 2x reduction in data footprint and bandwidth and doubling Tensor Core math throughput.

Deep Learning Super Sampling (DLSS) uses a neural network to extract scene features and combine details from multiple frames into a high-quality image. On Ampere GPUs, a 9x Super Resolution scaling factor makes 8K ray-traced gaming at 60 fps feasible, with the GeForce RTX 3090 achieving 60 fps in many tested titles.

The GA10x memory subsystem uses GDDR6X, developed with Micron Technology. GDDR6X exceeds 900 GB/s by using four-level pulse amplitude modulation (PAM4), which sends two bits per clock edge and doubles the I/O data rate of PAM2/NRZ signaling. The Maximum Transition Avoidance encoding scheme limits extreme voltage transitions to improve signal-to-noise ratio, alongside new training, adaptation, and equalization methods. GA10x GPUs support data rates up to 19.5 Gbps and peak bandwidth of 936 GB/s, more than 52% above the GeForce RTX 2080 Ti’s TU102 GPU. Pseudo-independent memory channels also improve BVH ray-traversal bandwidth.

NVIDIA RTX IO is designed to overcome storage and CPU decompression bottlenecks. In conjunction with Microsoft’s DirectStorage API, it transfers compressed assets directly to the GPU for GPU-based lossless decompression, offloading work that could otherwise consume dozens of CPU cores. NVIDIA reports performance up to 100 times that of hard drives and traditional storage APIs, along with faster loading, frame rates, texture streaming, and reduced object pop-in and stutter. The technology also supports professional workflows involving large CAD, scientific, rendering, and virtual-reality datasets.

The GA10x-based NVIDIA A40 targets data-center visual computing. Compared with the Quadro RTX 6000, NVIDIA states it provides up to twice the FP32 and ray-tracing throughput, and up to five times the AI-training and data-science throughput, or ten times with sparsity. Its PCIe Gen4 interface offers up to twice the bandwidth of Turing GPUs, while 48 GB of memory can be expanded to 96 GB by linking two A40s with NVLink. The A40 supports vGPU, Quadro Sync, and the NVIDIA EGX Platform.

Ampere GPUs support 4K at 120 Hz and 8K at 60 Hz. DisplayPort 1.4a with DSC 1.2a enables visually lossless 8K output, and two 8K displays can be driven at 60 Hz. HDMI 2.1 adds 8K60 and 4K120 support with up to 48 Gbps bandwidth and dynamic HDR. The architecture supports HDCP 2.3 and HDCP 1.x.

Fifth-generation NVDEC provides hardware-accelerated decoding for MPEG-2, VC-1, H.264, H.265, VP8, VP9, and AV1 on Windows and Linux. GA10x is presented as the first GPU architecture with AV1 hardware decoding, capable of 8K60 HDR playback with about 4% CPU usage in the cited test. Seventh-generation NVENC provides independent hardware encoding, exceeding the quality of software x264 at the Fast preset and matching x264 Medium under common streaming settings. It supports encoding up to 4K H.264 and 8K HEVC.

The GeForce RTX 3090 uses the GA102 GPU and has 82 streaming multiprocessors, 10,496 CUDA Cores, and 24 GB of GDDR6X memory. NVIDIA describes it as 1.5 times faster than the TITAN RTX. The RTX 3070 uses GA104, is faster than the previous-generation RTX 2080 Ti, excludes NVLink, and uses GDDR6 rather than GDDR6X.

GA10x GDDR6X includes Error Detection and Replay (EDR), which detects failed transmissions and retries them. As memory overclocking produces more errors, reduced useful bandwidth creates a performance plateau that indicates the memory’s operating limit.

The RTX A6000 includes 10,752 CUDA Cores, second- and next-generation RT Cores, and 48 GB of GDDR6 memory for professional rendering, simulation, and large 3D datasets. Two boards can be linked with NVLink for 96 GB of combined memory. NVIDIA states that specifications may be revised, products are provided as-is, and suitability for medical, military, aerospace, and other safety-critical applications is not warranted without further testing.
