This non-peer-reviewed medRxiv preprint reports a single-center prospective observational study of 103 cerebral cavernous malformation (CCM) patients, including 42 followed for four years, evaluating selected PTPN2, VDR, and FCGR2A polymorphisms alongside plasma cytokines. PTPN2 rs72872125 CT and VDR rs7975232 CC were associated with asymptomatic disease and altered cytokine levels. A weighted model combining PTPN2 rs72872125 CC and plasma GM-CSF distinguished symptomatic from asymptomatic patients with an AUC of 0.663, 41.3% sensitivity, and 85.7% specificity. FCGR2A rs1801274 GG independently predicted subsequent symptomatic events, with AUCs of 0.796 overall and 0.875 after propensity-score matching. VDR rs731236 AA was associated with later symptom onset, while rs11568820 CC was associated with earlier onset. In silico analysis predicted an H131R substitution in FCGR2A at a site conserved mainly among higher primates. Overall, the findings support potential genetic and inflammatory biomarkers for symptomatic and aggressive CCM phenotypes and suggest an immune-mediated mechanism for lesion behavior.

The paper develops a coupled mechanical–transport finite-element model for methane bubble growth and fracture in soft aquatic mud. It treats sediment deformation primarily with linear elastic fracture mechanics (LEFM), justified by the low fracture toughness and small plastic zone of consolidated mud. Gas accumulation is driven by diffusion of dissolved methane, while elastic expansion, sediment loading, and Mode I fracture are simulated concurrently.

The model uses a symmetry-based sediment box containing a penny-shaped bubble seed and follows growth until an inverted-teardrop bubble with a closed tail forms. A solute-conservation equation supplies methane to the bubble, whose gas concentration, pressure, and volume are calculated from Henry’s law, ideal-gas behavior, and elastic displacement. LEFM uses the stress-intensity factor to determine fracture initiation and the strain-energy-density criterion to direct propagation. Crack-front increments are greatest at the buoyant bubble head and decrease toward the tail. Progressive mesh deformation, Laplace smoothing, and selective remeshing track the evolving bubble surface.

The model is implemented in COMSOL Multiphysics with a fully coupled solver and refined tetrahedral meshes around the bubble. Simulations use a 4 mm initial bubble and environmental inputs representing summer conditions at Eckernförde Bay. Numerical results closely match analytical solutions for mature-bubble dimensions and crack-opening displacement across different fracture toughness values. Lower toughness produces smaller, flatter bubbles, whereas higher toughness produces larger, more inflated bubbles. The model currently addresses individual bubbles; extending bubble behavior to effective properties of gassy sediments remains an unresolved upscaling challenge relevant to remote sensing, sediment destabilization, geohazards, and methane-flux estimates.

The study developed a teacher education model combining collaborative inquiry with panoramic cameras to help teacher education students diagnose young students’ learning problems and refine instructional activity design. In a semester-long Professional Teaching Practicum, 22 participants formed five groups linked to junior high school classrooms. Over four three-week cycles, they collaborated on lesson planning, taught and observed lessons, reviewed student performance using observation records and panoramic footage, discussed learning difficulties, and adjusted teaching plans.

Assessment used a student-response observation form and a 12-item questionnaire. Diagnostic observation scores improved across successive cycles, from an average of approximately 0.47 in the first cycle to above 1.88 out of 2 in the fourth. Pre- and post-test results showed statistically significant improvements in perceived capabilities for lesson preparation, linking student learning with classroom instruction, and adjusting lesson plans after discussion. The findings support the feasibility of incorporating the model into teacher education, although the effectiveness of teaching strategies developed in response to diagnosed problems remains uncertain because participants had limited teaching experience.

Amazon received a patent for “directed fragmentation” of delivery drones, allowing a malfunctioning or endangered drone to shed components in a controlled sequence. The system would assess flight conditions, terrain, and component characteristics to guide parts toward preferred locations such as bodies of water, forests, or open fields. Components could be released using latches, hooks, springs, explosive charges, or compressed gas, with shedding ordered partly by cost, weight, and aerodynamic drag. The patent does not guarantee deployment, and the system may be unsuitable for urban environments.

The President reports that after sixty years the United States remains stable, at peace, and blessed by recovered public health, while emphasizing Congress’s responsibility for preserving free government. Foreign relations are generally amicable, including reciprocal trade advantages with Great Britain, renewed diplomacy with France, and friendly ties with European, Latin American, and Pacific states. The administration upheld neutrality by withdrawing aid from a German war steamer, suppressing an expedition against Cuba, and avoiding interference in European conflicts.

The German minister at Frankfort was recalled because no unified German Empire had been definitively established. Portugal’s failure to settle American claims was described as increasingly serious. The United States maintained treaty relations and boundary surveying with Mexico, sought improved mail transport across Panama, and urged Venezuela to redress harms suffered by American citizens. California’s growth was expected to strengthen U.S. relations with Pacific countries and the American states. A Brazilian claims convention was submitted to the Senate, and amendments to suppress the African slave trade through misuse of sea letters were recommended. Treaties were negotiated with Central American states, and the United States agreed to protect a proposed Nicaraguan canal while favoring equal international access and passage. Tehuantepec and Panama transit routes and Hawaiian independence also received favorable attention.

Treasury receipts totaled $59,663,097.50 and expenditures $57,631,667.82. Projected deficits of $5,828,121.66 and $10,547,092.73 were attributed chiefly to Mexican War expenses and the acquisition of California and New Mexico. The President recommended borrowing to cover the deficit, strict economy, tariff revision through specific duties protective of domestic industry, possible modification of the subtreasury system, and creation of an agricultural bureau.

Congress was urged to consider California’s admission as a state, prepare for New Mexico’s admission, organize customs and surveys in western territories, extend Indian agencies, establish a California mint, validate land titles, survey mineral lands, examine a transcontinental railroad route, and fund river and harbor improvements. Army expansion, retirement systems for disabled officers and enlisted personnel, and naval reorganization and retired lists were also recommended.

Postal laws required more effective service in California and Oregon. A uniform five-cent letter rate and an end to congressional franking were proposed. A British postal treaty was operating, while extension to France remained incomplete. Congress was asked to enact a law for the forthcoming census and to safeguard the interests of the District of Columbia.

The address closes by defending the Constitution’s separation of powers, restricting the presidential veto to extraordinary cases, protecting each branch from encroachment, and preserving the Union as the foundation of American liberty and future generations’ welfare.

Social media platforms increasingly use artificial intelligence to moderate hate speech, extremism, fake news, and other policy violations. A.I. can identify problematic text and images across multiple languages, but it remains imperfect. Systems must be updated as language evolves, can misinterpret context, and inherit biases from human-created training data that may spread when datasets are shared. A.I. also cannot reliably determine intent, leading to false positives such as mislabeling historical images, anti-hate messages, or photographs of statues. Human moderators remain necessary to verify decisions and determine whether content actually violates standards. A.I. nevertheless improves efficiency by flagging and prioritizing posts for review; Facebook reported that its suicide-detection system prompted 100 emergency calls in one month. As technology advances faster than laws and ethics, greater expertise in humanities and ethics may be needed.

Connecticut municipal leaders asked Gov. Dannel Malloy to help cities and towns cope with the state budget crisis by reducing administrative burdens, easing costly state mandates and allowing local cost controls. The Council of Small Towns and Connecticut Conference of Municipalities also sought changes to the municipal retirement system, easier collective-bargaining arbitration, inter-town service sharing and retention of more land-transfer fees. Malloy called their meeting productive amid a six-week budget stalemate and an estimated $3.5 billion deficit, while Senate President Pro Tempore Martin Looney disputed claims that municipal leaders were not seeking continued state aid. Other proposals included adjusting the prevailing-wage threshold, unchanged since 1991, and making municipal employee retirement contributions subject to collective bargaining rather than state law.

SanDisk warranty service requires contacting SanDisk, returning the product in tamper-resistant packaging with freight prepaid, and obtaining a tracking confirmation number. SanDisk may repair or replace the product with an equal-or-greater-capacity item or refund the purchase price. Replacement warranty coverage continues for the original warranty’s remaining duration. SanDisk disclaims responsibility for lost data, failure-free operation, and use in life-support or other safety-critical systems. Its liability is generally limited to the product’s purchase price, subject to applicable law.

Downloading, installing, or using the software constitutes acceptance of the EULA. The license permits personal use of executable software only with a SanDisk product on one device at a time. Modification, translation, reverse engineering, disassembly, rental, leasing, embedding, separation, and unauthorized transfer or distribution are prohibited. The software is provided “as is” without warranties, and users assume the risk and cost of servicing or correcting it. Liability for damages is limited to the purchase amount where permitted. Transfers are allowed only when the software remains integrated into a sold or transferred SanDisk product and the agreement accompanies it. SanDisk may terminate the license for breach. The software is not intended for hazardous or high-risk activities requiring fail-safe performance. California law and the courts of Santa Clara County, California, govern, and U.S. export restrictions apply.

The patent application discloses computer-based systems and methods for digital orthodontic treatment planning and aligner manufacture. A patient’s tooth positions are scanned or otherwise measured, movement constraints are received, and malocclusions are evaluated to generate multiple branched treatment plans. The plans may address openbite, posterior crossbite, bi-protrusion, Class II or III molar and canine relationships, overjet, tooth extractions, and interproximal reduction, with interim and final tooth positions recalculated for each branch. A dental professional reviews and selects a plan.

The selected plan is divided into incremental treatment stages, and an appliance model and fabrication instructions are generated for each stage. The appliances use tooth-receiving cavities to reposition teeth incrementally and may be produced through direct fabrication, indirect thermoforming, or combined techniques using rigid, elastic, or multiple materials. Appliance geometry and composition may be selected to produce specified force systems, with digital and finite-element modeling supporting design. The disclosure also describes sequential removable aligners, overcorrection, auxiliary components, scanning and fabrication hardware, and computerized systems for processing patient data and controlling manufacture.

Tesla, Inc.’s Form 10-Q for the quarter ended September 30, 2018 reported unaudited financial results and the company’s automotive and energy generation and storage segments. For the third quarter, revenue was $6.824 billion, compared with $2.985 billion in 2017, including $6.099 billion of automotive revenue, $399.3 million from energy generation and storage, and $326.3 million from services and other activities. Gross profit was $1.524 billion versus $449.1 million, operating income was $416.8 million versus a $535.5 million loss, and net income was $254.7 million versus a $671.2 million loss. Diluted earnings per share were $1.75, compared with a $3.70 loss. For the nine months, revenue was $14.235 billion versus $8.471 billion, while the net loss attributable to common stockholders was $1.116 billion, or $6.56 per diluted share, compared with $1.286 billion, or $7.80 per share.

Nine-month operating cash flow was $863.2 million, compared with a $570.5 million outflow; investing activities used $1.972 billion, and financing activities provided $686.1 million. Cash, cash equivalents and restricted cash ended at $3.523 billion, down from $3.965 billion at the beginning of the period. At September 30, total assets were $29.263 billion, total liabilities were $23.409 billion, and Tesla stockholders’ equity was $4.509 billion. Total debt principal was $10.897 billion, and the company reported compliance with its financial covenants.

The company adopted ASC 606 on January 1, 2018, using the modified retrospective method. Certain vehicle sales with resale-value guarantees are now treated as sales with a right of return rather than operating leases or collateralized borrowings. The adoption reduced opening accumulated deficit by $623.2 million, increased reported nine-month automotive sales revenue by $1.144 billion, reduced automotive leasing revenue by $603.5 million, and reduced the reported nine-month net loss attributable to common stockholders by $206.9 million compared with balances calculated without adoption.

The notes also reported a $644.5 million warranty reserve, a $13.3 million IPR&D abandonment loss, exposure to single-source suppliers, and one entity representing at least 10% of accounts receivable. Stockholders approved a CEO award of 20,264,042 stock options in March 2018.

A retrospective French cohort study evaluated high-titer COVID-19 convalescent plasma (CCP) in 112 hospitalized patients with hematological malignancies and documented SARS-CoV-2 infection from May 2020 to April 2021. Patients received four ABO-compatible CCP units. At day 7, temperature, C-reactive protein, ferritin, and fibrinogen decreased, while PCR cycle-threshold values increased. Adverse events were infrequent: three allergies and two transient increases in oxygen requirement with uncertain imputability.

Ninety-day overall survival was 64.9%, varying by malignancy: 77.5% for B-lymphoid neoplasms, 20% for myeloid neoplasms, and 36.8% for plasma-cell neoplasms. All deaths were associated with COVID-19. Age over 70, hypertension, and severe COVID-19 were independently associated with lower survival, whereas prior anti-CD20 or anti-CD19 therapy was associated with better survival.

A propensity-score-weighted, 16-day landmark comparison of CCP-treated and untreated patients with B-cell neoplasms found that CCP was associated with a 63% reduction in death risk in anti-CD20-pretreated patients; estimated reductions ranged from 40% to 63% across analysis populations. Observational bias, lack of vaccination, and unavailable viral-lineage data limited interpretation. The authors concluded that CCP may be particularly useful for B-cell-depleted patients unable to mount a humoral response, but prospective randomized confirmation was needed.

The passage lists AMD Geode CS5535 Revision A3 silicon deviations involving PMC sleep controls, GLIU and DMA behavior, LPC and I/O operations, PIC interrupts, UDMA/ATA, ACPI wake, USB clock gating, SMB, GPIO, and PIT functions. The PIT does not cancel an uncompleted latch command when read back and immediately reloads count mode 3 before the prior count finishes. The GLIU debug port recognizes debug packets but hangs and should not be used. The XPIC may send duplicate interrupts with AEOI enabled; AEOI is master-PIC-only and unsuitable where nested interrupts are required. Rotating-priority DMA transfers complete but may occur in the wrong order. A thermal alarm forces Faulted Standby and cannot autonomously recover because its timer is blocked across power domains. Sleep Clock must be enabled in the PMC when SLEEP_X, SLEEP_Y, or SLP_CLK_EN# is desired; if Sleep Clock itself is unwanted, it should be disabled at GPIO but enabled in the PMC.

On September 12, 2017, Apple Inc. completed the issuance of $5 billion in senior unsecured notes: $1 billion of 1.500% notes due 2019, $1 billion of 2.100% notes due 2022, $2 billion of 2.900% notes due 2027, and $1 billion of 3.750% notes due 2047. Interest is payable semiannually on March 12 and September 12, beginning March 12, 2018. The notes rank equally with Apple’s other unsecured and unsubordinated debt. The transaction was governed by a September 5 underwriting agreement with Goldman Sachs, Deutsche Bank Securities, and Merrill Lynch as representatives, and an April 29, 2013 indenture with The Bank of New York Mellon Trust Company, N.A., as trustee.

Diana Containerships reported a quarterly loss per share of $0.66, beating the $0.77 consensus loss estimate by $0.11, while revenue of $5.40 million missed the $7.50 million estimate and fell 63.8% year over year. A March 27–28, 2001 compilation covers Viacom’s decision to retain Blockbuster following its market-share growth and cash generation, and President Bush’s appointment of Patrick Wood III and Nora Brownell to the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission, potentially influencing its handling of California’s electricity crisis.

Enron reported a strong 2000, increasing Chairman Kenneth Lay’s bonus to $7 million and giving him $7.5 million in restricted stock. The company pursued energy projects in several countries: it proposed a 2,000-megawatt LNG-fired plant in Aomori, Japan, with construction targeted for 2004 and operations for 2007; sought approval for an Indian wind-power subsidiary with an initial $2 million investment; withdrew from bidding for a stake in India’s Vijayanagar power project; and held a 24.5% interest in the Dolphin Energy gas project serving the UAE.

CEO Jeffrey Skilling said Texas electricity deregulation was working better than California’s system. He said California’s approved rate increase could reduce shortages but that further deregulation was needed, projected 2001 Enron revenue of $160 billion–$170 billion and earnings per share of $1.70–$1.75, and expected high natural-gas prices to persist. Texas utilities prepared for a June customer-choice pilot, while California regulators approved rate increases of up to 46%.

Other coverage concerned Dubai’s acute natural-gas needs, Indian restrictions on states’ direct access to multilateral loans, the start of Britain’s NETA electricity-trading system, and Enron-led efforts to let private lenders use Export-Import Bank financing for U.S. exports.

Steve Yzerman said Tampa Bay had not set a fixed timeline for its progress and did not believe there were quick fixes. Although free agency or trades could accelerate the process, sustained success requires homegrown talent, strong scouting and patient development under the salary cap. The Lightning were fortunate to acquire Steven Stamkos and Victor Hedman early, while later selections such as Ondrej Palat and Nikita Kucherov developed into important players. Yzerman praised the work of Al Murray, the amateur scouting staff and the Norfolk and Syracuse player-development programs.

Jon Cooper described how the organization committed to developing young players together. Palat was kept in the AHL rather than returned to junior, and Cooper grouped emerging players with one another while relying on veterans to provide leadership. Cooper believed this approach helped the young players become NHL stars because they already understood the organization’s standards and had room to fail before succeeding.

Cooper said the playoff run exposed the team’s resilience. Following the previous season’s first-round sweep, the Lightning used that disappointment as motivation. They recovered from deficits against Detroit, with Ben Bishop leading the response, and repeatedly met different challenges in subsequent rounds. Cooper said the players trusted their preparation, embraced adversity and consistently rose to important games.

Stamkos’s leadership was a central topic. Cooper said he evolved after succeeding Vinny as captain following Marty St. Louis’s departure, accepting defensive and faceoff responsibilities in addition to scoring. He also encouraged Jonathan, Palat and Kyle Killorn to develop as leaders. Yzerman described Stamkos as a high-character, humble player who had become a team leader, while emphasizing that elite players must contribute in every situation, including late-game defense and scoring when trailing.

Yzerman praised Jonathan for his maturity, defense and all-around ability, noting that he and Hedman were becoming the team’s veterans. He also described Stamkos as someone focused on winning who had set the tone for the group.

Yzerman said the Lightning were trying to recruit talented, high-character players who wanted to compete in a strong program. He credited the signing of Anton Stralman with filling a major need for a right-handed defenseman and said a stronger roster could make recruitment more difficult. Cooper similarly praised the organization’s competitive culture and the growth of Bishop, Johnson, Palat, Killorn, Kucherov and others.

Cooper compared Kucherov with Patrick Kane, describing both as skilled, fast players with strong vision and a tendency to control the puck, while he characterized Johnson as more direct and explosive. He considered all three capable of changing a game in one shift. Yzerman said his own role after the trade deadline was primarily to provide support while staying out of the coaches’ and players’ way.

Roanoke College’s Bittle tree, planted by first president Dr. David Bittle, was removed after more than a century due to lightning and wind damage. Its wood was used for the Bittle Tree of Life Cross, designed by Chapel Dean Chris Bowen and executed with retired professor George Arthur for Antrim Chapel. The cross features a rooted, upward-branching tree symbolizing the College’s roots and future.

Two women with personal experience of child sexual abuse, May Baxter-Thornton of Newport and Emma Lewis of Swansea, were appointed to the Independent Inquiry into Child Sexual Abuse’s victims and survivors panel to advise on reaching and listening to Welsh victims and survivors. Electric resistance welded (ERW) steel pipe transports liquids and gases under high- and low-pressure conditions. Its types include submerged arc welded steel pipe, line pipe, and high-frequency resistance-welded pipe. ERW offers high production efficiency, low cost, material savings, and broad industrial use. Modern production emphasizes seam quality, inner and outer burr removal, burr thickness control of about 0.2–0.5 mm, and wall-thickness control within ±0.2 mm using hot-rolled coil. Pipe ends follow API or GB/T 9711.1 standards with fixed bevel trimming. ERW is widely used in urban gas networks.

This continuation application concerns audio-content identification facilitated by a playback device within a networked media-playback system and incorporates by reference five prior “Identification of Audio Content” applications and patents.

The disclosed playback device receives digital data representing audio content, sends some or all of that data to an identification system, receives information associated with the identified content, and forwards the information to a control device while playing the content through wired speakers. The returned information may include metadata, a network location or URL for a metadata-curating device, or an identifier usable to retrieve metadata. This may avoid requiring the control device to capture played audio with a microphone, convert it to digital data, and transmit it for identification.

Identification may be initiated by a control-device command, triggered by detected discontinuities in the digital data, or performed periodically. The playback device may decode the data, convert its sample rate, extract data from different positions in its audio pipeline, or segregate frequency ranges before submission. A control device may command identification during playback, receive the resulting information, and display it or request and display additional metadata. A controller interface can present information such as track titles and artist names and offer options to refresh missing metadata or search for additional information.

The described operating environment includes networked playback and control devices organized into configurable playback zones and zone groups. Playback devices can synchronize audio, operate as bonded or consolidated devices, retrieve content from local, networked, streaming, and line-in sources, and be managed through interfaces for playback, status, queues, zones, and sources.

The first letter argues that health care is a right, not a commodity, criticizes Rep. Ken Buck, and advocates Medicare for all as a lower-cost alternative to private insurance. The disclosure describes directional illumination systems for large-area 2D, autostereoscopic, multi-viewer, and privacy displays. Imaging directional backlights use an illuminator array and a waveguide with opposed guide surfaces and a reflective end to direct each light source into a corresponding viewing window. In a stepped optical-valve waveguide, light travels by total internal reflection to the reflective end, returns in the opposite direction, and is redirected outward by extraction features. Curved or linear features and optical power at the reflective end can control window shape, uniformity, viewing freedom, and cross-talk.

Selectively operating illuminators in synchronization with a fast transmissive spatial light modulator enables time-multiplexed autostereoscopy, observer tracking, different images for multiple viewers, and directional 2D illumination. Privacy embodiments add input and output polarizers, an additional polarizer, and passive or switchable liquid-crystal retarders such as A-, C-, and O-plates. Their orientations, optical thicknesses, alignment, applied voltages, and independently addressable regions can reduce luminance at off-axis snooper locations while largely preserving head-on luminance and supporting wide-angle and privacy modes.

Additional embodiments include reflective polarizers with rear reflectors, correcting passive retarders, patterned camouflage regions, snooper-location tracking, and multiple retarder stacks. Control systems coordinate illuminator width, displayed images, and retarder voltage, including temporally multiplexed secondary images that obscure primary content outside intended viewing windows. The disclosure also describes non-directional wide-angle backlights, automotive applications, and optical-stack configurations.

Deloitte found improving confidence in autonomous vehicles: 49% now consider them unsafe, down from 73%; 51% trust traditional manufacturers, versus 21% technology firms; and 53% say trusted brands increase their likelihood of riding. Despite this, 73% prefer conventional engines to electric vehicles (2%), citing range, price and charging infrastructure. The government is opening a safety inquiry ahead of expected deployment.

The passage explains the "Presidential Cycle," a theory that U.S. stock market performance follows a predictable four-year pattern tied to presidential elections. Yale Hirsch, founder of the *Stock Trader's Almanac* (first published 1967), is credited with quantifying it. The *Stock Trader's Almanac 2020* describes the Pre-Election Year as the best year of the cycle and Election Year second best; since 1952 the S&P 500 averaged 12.5% in election years with an incumbent seeking re-election, 6.7% in all election years, and –1.5% in open-field years without an incumbent. Midterm election years are generally the weakest year of a president's term (e.g., 2018, 2022) until the fourth quarter, when volatility picks up. The passage offers partly conflicting descriptions of the pattern and notes the theory has failed to predict results in recent years.

Proposed explanations include wars, downturns, and bear markets occurring early in a term, bull markets and presidential economic stimulus later as presidents boost growth to aid re-election; Nixon's post-1968 market path is cited. Historical data since the 1930s show equities and bonds performing less well in the year before an election, and midterms followed by stronger S&P 500 returns, with congressional party control generally not a predictor. US Bank's Rob Hawworth attributes the consistency to recurring four-year uncertainty, while CIO Eric Freedman says policy-driven instability is usually sector-specific; Hainlin notes healthcare and energy volatility tied to divergent party regulatory policies and legislative contingencies. Analysts advise watching affected sectors, staying invested, and rebalancing, treating election-season volatility as a permanent feature of markets.

Intel’s Management Engine (ME) is an always-on microcontroller embedded in many modern Intel CPUs, connected to storage and networking. It evolved from Trusted Platform Modules and Active Management Technology; according to the passage, some components were introduced at the NSA’s request, and the ME runs Minix. Its closed-source firmware and continued operation when a computer is off make it a significant security concern.

At Black Hat Europe, Mark Ermolov and Maxim Goryachy demonstrated a USB-based exploit allowing arbitrary code execution on ME versions above 11. It requires physical access, and no remote network exploit had been identified, though one could allow attacks from anywhere.

Mitigation remains fragmented. System76 released firmware to disable the ME, Dell offered a rugged Latitude 14 with it disabled by default, and Intel released a detection tool. Motherboard-specific disabling methods exist, but there is no universal solution. Computers without valid ME firmware shut down after 30 minutes, while the me_cleaner tool reportedly disables the ME by deleting the first page of its ROM. The passage concludes that unauditable code cannot be trusted and presents the ME as an example of the risks posed by embedded security technology.

New Jersey Gov. Chris Christie signed legislation strengthening protections for people with developmental disabilities and family oversight. It allows twice-yearly unannounced group-home inspections, requires injury notifications within 2–8 hours, mandates twice-yearly family meetings, and authorizes additional state staff.

This qualitative literature review examines Mortimer J. Adler’s perennialist philosophy in relation to Christian education, global education management, and posthumanism. Primary sources include Adler’s writings on curriculum development and the administration of Christian education, while secondary sources cover philosophy, Christian education, and education management. Posthumanism is presented as questioning anthropocentric supremacy and examining human existence through ecology, technology, artificial intelligence, and robotics.

Adler’s perennialism emphasizes the continuity of truth, culture, art, politics, and eternal values in education. It regards humans as rational creatures and considers lectures and memorization enduring educational methods. His concepts of docility and obedience involve postponing judgment and trusting educational authority, while preserving freedom, critical thinking, and democratic participation. The paper identifies Adler’s failure to distinguish between male and female educational participants as a significant limitation.

The review connects Adler’s philosophy with research on family meals, spirituality and chronic illness, moral education across Christian schools, and character education emphasizing spirituality and self-knowledge. Additional studies address cross-cultural student agency, values in Christian schools, Christian family-business management, institutional transformation in Kenya, disaster resilience among diaspora communities in New Zealand, and identity diversity in Christian business.

The paper concludes that educational justice requires empowering women and avoiding the scapegoating of children for failures attributed to teachers, parents, and governments. Teachers’ responsibilities extend beyond classrooms, and educational management must address learners, families, and wider communities. Adler’s framework places enduring values and sustainable learner development above immediate achievement and calls for deeper reflection in curricula, including Indonesia’s independent curricula.

The MSPM0C1105 and MSPM0C1106 feature a 32MHz Arm Cortex-M0+ CPU with prefetch logic, a two-line I-cache, SysTick, and an NVIC supporting four priority levels and tail-chaining. Five power modes—RUN, SLEEP, STOP, STANDBY, and SHUTDOWN—provide configurable performance and power tradeoffs. Two power domains separate CPU, memory, and high-performance peripherals from low-power peripherals. The PMU provides regulated core supplies, brown-out monitoring with three programmable thresholds, and power-on reset.

The clock module supports internal 32kHz and 32MHz oscillators, external low- and high-frequency crystal or digital clock inputs, and clocks for the processor, buses, and peripherals. Memory includes programmable flash with in-circuit programming and 1KB erase sectors, plus zero-wait-state SRAM retained through STANDBY and protected at 1KB resolution.

Peripheral support includes a three-channel DMA controller, event manager, 45 GPIO pins, IOMUX, a 12-bit ADC, temperature sensor, configurable voltage reference, comparator, CRC-16, firewalls, three UARTs, I2C, SPI, independent and windowed watchdog timers, RTC, and general-purpose and advanced timers. Communications peripherals support DMA and low-power address-match wakeup. SWD and DEBUGSS provide debugging, peripheral control, mailbox communication, and security options.

TI recommends 10µF and 0.1µF supply decoupling capacitors, a 47kΩ NRST pullup with a 1000pF pulldown, crystal bypass capacitors where applicable, and pullups for 5V-tolerant open-drain IOs. Development resources include LaunchPad hardware, TI Resource Explorer, SysConfig, MSP Academy, GUI Composer, Arm-Clang, and E2E support. X-prefixed devices are experimental, while MSP-prefixed devices are production-qualified. Revision A updated power-mode and package information, technical specifications, CPU and ADC details, DEBUGSS content, and device identification tables. The document also provides mechanical drawings, packaging guidance, and orderable-part information.

Venezuelans and Temporary Protected Status holders asked the Supreme Court to leave intact a ruling blocking the Trump administration’s termination of Venezuela’s TPS designation. The program allows eligible Venezuelans to remain and work in the United States when they cannot safely return because of disasters, conflict, or other extraordinary temporary conditions. After DHS Secretary Kristi Noem ended Venezuela’s 2023 designation and 2025 extension, challengers argued that her action violated federal administrative law and was motivated by racial animus. District Judge Edward Chen temporarily blocked the termination and later ruled that Noem acted unlawfully. The Trump administration sought a broader Supreme Court stay, arguing that its earlier order froze Chen’s preliminary relief. The challengers countered that the earlier stay did not prevent final merits litigation under separate statutory authority and that the record had since expanded. UCLA law professor Ahilan Arulanantham warned that disturbing the order would harm TPS holders and their families, including American children.

Ed Sachse, 56, began his entrepreneurial career at 15, paying $400 with a friend for a Detroit window-washing business. After studying accounting at Michigan State University and working for Arthur Andersen, he moved to Los Angeles and became CFO of Camden Financial. He later joined Coldwell Banker as a broker, initially gaining success by selling an empty school to the Simon Wiesenthal Center.

Sachse entered property management after improving a struggling strip mall, then founded his own brokerage and management company in 1993. In 2001, at 41, he was diagnosed with stage 4 non-Hodgkin lymphoma and underwent six years of intensive treatment while maintaining his business. The Great Recession later forced cutbacks and layoffs. After contacting 40 potential clients in 2009, he attracted an offer from Kennedy Wilson, which acquired his company. He now oversees its brokers and 21 million square feet of properties nationwide.

Hayes proclaimed on July 18, 1877, that domestic violence in West Virginia at Martinsburg and along the Baltimore and Ohio Railroad could not be suppressed by state authorities. He warned those involved to disperse peacefully by noon on July 19 and urged citizens not to aid them.

The invention improves optical waveguide displays whose field of view is constrained by total internal reflection (TIR). In prior designs, a wavelength-tuned Bragg grating injects light into the waveguide, but light at extreme input angles or at wavelengths differing from the grating’s design wavelength may be diffracted outside the TIR range and escape, reducing the field of view.

The invention coats the external waveguide surfaces against which guided light internally reflects with a material, preferably a metamaterial, having a positive refractive index substantially equal to or below 1.0 at optical wavelengths. This lowers the critical angle for TIR, allowing light outside the conventional field of view to be captured and guided to an output diffractive part for display. The coating can also protect waveguide surfaces and surface-profile gratings from damage and contamination.

Proposed metamaterials include periodic “fish-net” structures comprising conductive meshes surrounding a magnetic resonator. Structural optimization can produce real refractive-index values from near zero to 1.0, while the imaginary component can be adjusted to control attenuation.

The display may use conjugated input and output diffraction gratings to reduce geometric distortion and chromatic dispersion. Multilayer slab waveguides can contain separately tuned input and output gratings for different display colors, with metamaterial between and around the component waveguides. Optional plastic outer layers add mechanical protection without obstructing the TIR-enhancing coatings. In some arrangements, the coating may omit input or output grating areas to avoid optical losses from absorption or attenuation.
