The lecture reviews renewal theory as a foundation for countable-state Markov chains. It contrasts the strong law, which gives an almost-sure sample-path renewal rate of \(1/\bar{x}\), with the elementary renewal theorem, which gives only an asymptotic expected rate and does not control fluctuations. Blackwell’s theorem shows that, for an arithmetic renewal process with span \(\lambda\), expected renewal counts increase asymptotically by \(\lambda/\bar{x}\); renewal probabilities at grid times therefore approach \(\lambda/\bar{x}\). The non-arithmetic case illustrates why certain long-time and short-interval limits cannot be interchanged.

Age and duration are then analyzed in an arithmetic renewal process. Asymptotically, their joint distribution does not depend on age and depends only on the containing inter-renewal interval. The duration distribution is proportional to the interval length, yielding mean duration \(E[X^2]/E[X]\) and, at integer observation times, mean age \(E[X^2]/(2E[X])\).

The lecture turns to countable-state chains, using random walks and birth-death chains to illustrate recurrence, transience, communicating classes, and the absence of stationary distributions in some cases. First-passage probabilities \(f_{ij}(n)\) are defined, and recurrence is expressed by \(\sum_n f_{jj}(n)=1\). Recurrent return times form a renewal process. A state with an infinite expected return time is null recurrent, corresponding to zero stationary probability.

After scratching their hand on a garden-gate nail two days before Christmas 2015, the author became ill in Glasgow, developed sepsis, and entered a coma with little chance of surviving. They awoke three months later and needed another year to recover fully. Sepsis affects over 30 million people annually, kills about 6 million—including nearly 2 million children—and leaves 40% of survivors with lasting physical and mental symptoms. It occurs when an infection, including one from a scratch or bite, triggers an uncontrolled immune response that can rapidly cause vital-organ failure. Warning signs include pale, mottled skin, severe breathlessness, shivering, muscle pain, not urinating all day, nausea, and vomiting. Emergency services should be contacted and asked, “Could it be sepsis?” Anyone can develop it, while vitamin D deficiency is linked to increased risk. Antibiotics may treat the underlying infection, while metformin and NF-kB-targeted gene therapy are under investigation. Greater public and professional awareness, including use of the Sepsis6 protocol, is considered the most immediate way to save lives and reduce harm.

The passage reviews AIED systems that personalize learning, support virtual experiments, and enable online collaboration, while highlighting privacy concerns around student data and facial images. In scientific experimentation videos, face anonymization must conceal identities without obscuring instruments, hand movements, or other details needed for assessment, especially when fine or transparent apparatus and motion blur complicate segmentation.

The proposed system combines a modified YOLOv8 architecture, BOTSort tracking, Gaussian blurring, and Contour-Adaptive Occlusion Refinement (CAOR). MSFF-YOLOv8 retains and fuses shallow and deep features to improve detection and semantic segmentation, while CAOR expands face-mask boundaries during training to reduce misclassification of overlapping instruments and actions. Primary and non-primary operators receive different levels of processing to improve efficiency.

Evaluation used 51 experiment videos and a dataset containing 1,049 extracted images with face and instrument annotations, plus tracked operator poses. Performance was measured using frames per second, Sensitive Object Blur Accuracy (SOBA), and Over Blur Rate (OBR/OPR). Results show that MSFF-YOLOv8 with CAOR outperformed the original YOLOv8, SAM, and Edge-SAM configurations. Its best full-dataset results were 0.9602 SOBA and 0.0159 OBR at 1920-pixel input, while processing 1080p video at 22.67 fps. The study concludes that the approach provides effective, real-time facial privacy while retaining critical experimental details, though improved edge classification during real-time inference remains future work.

La-Z-Boy is favored, beating Stanley Furniture on 12 of 14 comparison factors. It reports higher revenue ($1.54 billion vs. $43.64 million), EBITDA ($154.51 million vs. -$3.31 million), EPS ($1.70 vs. -$0.20), net margin (5.45% vs. -6.38%), ROE (14.18% vs. -18.33%), and ROA (9.73% vs. -10.44%). La-Z-Boy pays a $0.44 annual dividend with a 1.6% yield; Stanley pays none. Analysts rate La-Z-Boy 2.25 with a $30.33 target, suggesting 11.31% upside, while Stanley has no ratings. Institutional ownership is 86.8% for La-Z-Boy versus 29.7% for Stanley, while insider ownership is 3.2% versus 28.6%. La-Z-Boy has a higher P/E (16.03 vs. -6.10) and beta (0.89 vs. 0.34).

Sam Altman said intellectual-property holders respond more strongly to AI video than still images because lifelike footage creates greater emotional resonance, prompting demands for more granular usage restrictions and character-generation controls. OpenAI recently announced such changes for Sora after unauthorized SpongeBob and Pikachu videos spread on social media; Sora also blocked a request to depict the characters as friends, citing similarity guardrails. Altman predicted companies will eventually favor AI-generated content and seek better rules and deeper connections with fans.

Scientists are making progress toward understanding and manipulating human memory. Research on “face cells,” CREB, and memory formation suggests memories may be stored in specific brain locations. MIT researchers demonstrated that artificial memories can be implanted and altered, including linking a harmless situation with fear and later reversing that negative reaction. As these methods advance, they may enable precise memory implantation or erasure and raise ethical questions about such capabilities.

The team says outside perceptions do not matter and that reaching the Stanley Cup was earned by defeating three strong hockey teams. Mike Peca is considered hockey’s best all-around player. Their success relies on physical play, especially from large, strong forwards who skate well, forecheck, and deliver punishing hits. Players used the long layoff to handle personal matters and prepare emotionally. After overcoming adversity in earlier rounds, they expect their experience to keep them confident entering the Dallas series.

The passage argues that trade deficits shift demand abroad and can raise U.S. unemployment, but this can be offset by budget deficits and asset bubbles. It disputes the claim that the dollar’s reserve status requires large trade deficits, noting that other currencies also serve as reserves and that countries accumulate reserves partly to influence exchange rates. It also questions the characterization of China’s technology-transfer policy as extortion, arguing that major U.S. companies voluntarily invest in China because it is commercially beneficial.

The passage presents an RSI(2) mean-reversion strategy for QQQ, entering when the two-day RSI falls below 10 and exiting when today’s close exceeds yesterday’s high. The strategy returned 10.01% versus 6.39% for buy-and-hold and performed well during four bear markets: 2000–2002, 2008–09, 2018, and March 2020. Lowering the entry threshold to 5 increased average gains but reduced total returns because it resulted in fewer trades. Adding a second indicator while retaining the RSI-below-10 criterion produced a 12.7% CAGR, 14% time in the market, 232 trades, 75% winning trades, a 3.15 profit factor, a 19.5% maximum drawdown, and a 2.85 Sharpe ratio. The article concludes that RSI(2) works particularly well on QQQ with the additional parameter and offers paid access to the strategy code.

SD Memory Cards provide secure, high-capacity audiovisual storage with SDMI-compliant protection, mutual authentication, encryption, and nonsecure user-content access. Optional ISO-7816 supports public networks, e-commerce, and digital signatures. Compatible SDIO cards add high-speed, low-power I/O and optional storage; non-SDIO hosts safely ignore them. The 9-pin interface reaches 208 MHz at low voltage.

Wetherspoon plans a 1,600-square-metre Dublin city-centre gastropub combining the former Trustee Savings Bank at 12B and Baptist Chapel at 12C on Lower Abbey Street, linked by a glazed passage following a court decision. The Circuit Licensing Court granted a full drinks and restaurant licence and planning permission. The chain is known for low prices, though drink prices have recently risen.

The lecture examines auctions as price-setting mechanisms, highlighting applications in government procurement, Treasury bill sales, online advertising, and spectrum licensing. It develops an independent private values model with risk-neutral bidders, one object, and independent private signals, then compares major mechanisms.

In a second-price sealed-bid auction, the highest bidder wins but pays the second-highest bid. Truthful bidding is a weakly dominant strategy and is the unique symmetric equilibrium with continuous value distributions. Expected seller revenue equals the expected second-highest value; for uniform values, revenue is \((n-1)/(n+1)\). A button or ascending auction has equivalent strategic incentives—bidders remain active until their value is reached—but reveals less information than sealed bidding. This difference matters because sealed bids can reveal extreme disparities in valuations and produce ex post embarrassment for the auctioneer.

In a first-price sealed-bid auction, winners pay their own bids and equilibrium bidding entails shading. For uniform values, each bidder bids \((n-1)/n\) of their value. More generally, the equilibrium bid equals the expected second-highest value conditional on having the highest value. Thus, first- and second-price auctions generate the same expected revenue under independent private values. This is an instance of revenue equivalence: symmetric mechanisms that award the object to the highest-value bidder and give the lowest-value bidder zero surplus also give bidders the same expected information rent. Switching from second- to first-price pricing does not increase revenue because strategic bid shading offsets the higher payment.

Revenue equivalence does not extend to risk-averse bidders, positively correlated values, or mechanisms that may withhold the object. Risk aversion makes first-price auctions generate more revenue, while positive correlation favors second-price auctions. In second-price auctions, the optimal reserve is the monopoly price, although reserves reduce welfare, may discourage entry, and require commitment to be credible.

The lecture then turns to common-value auctions, where values depend on other bidders’ signals. Offshore oil-lease auctions illustrate the winner’s curse: winning reveals that one bidder’s signal was more optimistic than rivals’, causing rational bidders to condition bids on the information revealed by winning.

Hendricks and Porter study this asymmetry in U.S. offshore oil auctions using 114 drainage tracts sold between 1959 and 1969. Their model gives an informed incumbent both private information and a cost advantage over uninformed entrants. Because pure-strategy equilibria cannot persist, entrants use mixed strategies. The model predicts that incumbents bid zero less often, win at least half the time, earn positive profits, and bid more when tract values and entrants’ signals are higher. Entrants are discouraged by the possibility of negative profits when the incumbent enters. The data broadly support these predictions: neighboring firms bid more often than non-neighbors, incumbents win about 52 percent of auctions and earn substantially higher profits, and regressions support the predicted bid relationships. The paper is presented as a reduced-form empirical approach that tests asymmetric information through multiple predictions rather than relying on one implication.
In HS mode, the device holds SCL LOW after the read-addressing byte until conversion completes. Use repeated START instead of STOP to remain in HS mode.

An Alberta Education survey of nearly 10,000 respondents, half teachers, found many wanted greater emphasis on practical skills, reading, writing and math, while some misunderstood the draft curriculum outlines. Social studies prompted strong debate over Indigenous content, global history, civic literacy, social justice and ideological influence. Most respondents said the plans strengthened literacy, numeracy and critical thinking. The Alberta Teachers’ Association supported the direction but stressed careful teacher preparation. The K-12 overhaul covers English and French, with K-4 writing targeted for December and higher grades phased in through 2022; no classroom implementation date was announced.

The BGF China Flexible Equity Fund offers investors access to both onshore A-shares and offshore Chinese equities through one flexible strategy. Managed by Helen Zhu and supported by 10 China-focused analysts in Hong Kong and Shanghai, it is long-only, fundamentals-driven, and concentrated in 20–50 companies. The fund targets valuation differences, changing market cycles, and sector-specific opportunities across market capitalizations, sectors, and factors.

The study examines Turkish university students’ perceptions and experiences of emergency distance education (EDE), the temporary shift of face-to-face instruction to an online environment during crises. EDE differs from planned distance education because it was implemented rapidly during the Covid-19 pandemic without normal preparation. Tour guiding education (TGE) was examined because it combines theoretical instruction with field trips, practical application, communication, group presentation, body language, and self-expression.

A qualitative phenomenological design with purposive sampling was used. Data were collected during the 2022–2023 academic year from 81 students enrolled in face-to-face tour guiding departments at three Istanbul universities. Participants had experienced at least one semester of pandemic-era EDE. Semi-structured interviews and a 13-question online questionnaire were analyzed thematically with MAXQDA and validated through researcher triangulation and participant confirmation.

Students considered EDE insufficient for TGE. The main reasons were insufficient vocational and practical coursework (46.1%), ineffective communication (32.2%), and motivation problems (21.1%). Nearly three-fifths (59.2%) said distance education provided inadequate practical preparation, emphasizing the importance of field trips, speaking practice, interpersonal interaction, and direct application of knowledge.

Face-to-face education was perceived as more effective because it supported participation, concentration, communication, socialization, and self-expression. Although 81.4% of students distinguished between the two modes, 88.8% reported understanding the distance courses, with associate students reporting greater understanding than undergraduates. Perceptions of distance TGE most often emphasized its weaknesses, particularly weak communication, technical and equipment problems, limited attention, and insufficient socialization.

Students nevertheless identified several advantages of EDE: effective time management (46.5%), the ability to repeat or make up courses (18.6%), location independence (11.6%), savings (5.8%), and easier access to materials (4.6). Reported disadvantages were inappropriacy for TGE (29.7%), lack of motivation (23.4%), insufficient communication (18%), technical problems (9.5%), and poor attendance (6.3%).

Overall, students preferred face-to-face TGE while remaining divided about distance education’s benefits and limitations. The study recommends practical experiential courses, stronger communication systems, and hybrid education for future TGE. Its findings are limited to the Turkish TGE context, pandemic-related EDE, students transitioning from face-to-face study, and the exploratory qualitative design, which restricts generalizability.

This ebook is the first volume of *Foreign Relations of the United States, 1981–1988*, covering foundations of foreign policy. Prepared by the Office of the Historian, U.S. Department of State, it reproduces the full FRUS volume with search, bookmarking, note-taking, and offline access. Readers are advised to cite document numbers rather than printed page numbers, which are supplemented with bracketed document references.

The FRUS series, established in 1861, presents the official documentary record of major U.S. foreign policy decisions and diplomatic activity. Its statutory and editorial standards require comprehensive documentation, historical objectivity, accuracy, disclosure of deletions, inclusion of all materially important facts, and publication within 30 years of the recorded events. Government entities must provide historians access to relevant records. Most sources used for this volume have been declassified and are available at the National Archives and Records Administration.

Data culture supports organizational alignment: shared metrics and objectives align teams vertically with company goals, while common data models and transparent data access support horizontal collaboration. Digital leaders emphasize learning mindsets, clear metrics, transparent access, and culture as a mechanism for aligning beliefs, values, and daily behavior. Digital laggards may recognize data’s importance but face entrenched habits, skills gaps, and insufficient leadership focus; changing mindsets remains a major transformation challenge, although cultural improvement is possible. Strong data cultures value learning, risk-taking, transparency, and measurement and embed these principles in company values and daily practices. Organizations fall into four patterns—data novice, insight ready, tech enabled, and data reliant—each with different needs and targeted actions for developing a stronger data culture.
The Conservative Party has selected Brad Vis to run again in Mission-Matsqui-Fraser Canyon after he narrowly lost to Liberal Jati Sidhu in 2015. Vis has worked for Abbotsford MP Ed Fast.

After a loss, a hockey player said his team was outplayed and outskated by New Jersey, especially during the Devils’ strong second period. He praised Patrick as a great goaltender and said the time off was unrelated to the defeat. The team needed to use its speed better, shoot more, create net-front traffic, and execute its usual game. He credited Friesen’s patience on the first goal and said there was little he could do when a rebound went back to an opponent. With two weeks left in the season, he urged the team to match New Jersey’s intensity and give full effort in the next game.

A 2024 study examined the relationship between multilingual competence, multilingual learning, and cultural awareness among Indonesian university students, drawing on second-language acquisition, anthropolinguistics, and sociocultural theory. It used an embedded mixed-methods design: 388 students from six universities completed questionnaires, while 60 participants provided qualitative responses. All reported relationships were positive and statistically significant at p < .001. Multilingual competence correlated strongly with the multilingual learning process (r = .568), psychological factors (r = .537), and social interaction (r = .504); it was also associated with sociocultural context (r = .553) and cultural-learning attitudes and capacity (r = .495).

Participants reflected Indonesia’s linguistic diversity. Indonesian was the dominant mother tongue (61.08%), while Javanese, Buginese, and Makassarese were the most widely studied local languages. English was the most studied foreign language (63.40%), followed by Korean, Arabic, Japanese, and German. School and lecture methods predominated for Indonesian and foreign-language learning, whereas independent study was most common for local languages.

The study recommends inclusive curricula, intercultural collaboration, educator training, technology-supported adaptive learning, affordable learning resources, community engagement, self-directed learning, and development of motivation and confidence. It concludes that integrating multilingual and culturally diverse education can strengthen language competence, cultural awareness, and preparation for participation in multicultural and global communities. Future research could examine technologies such as virtual reality and language-learning applications.

Amazon.com, Inc.’s Form 10-K covers the fiscal year ended December 31, 2015. The company, founded in 1994 and publicly traded on NASDAQ under “AMZN,” reported 2015 net sales of $107.006 billion, up 20%, compared with $88.988 billion in 2014. Operating income rose to $2.233 billion from $178 million, and net income was $596 million versus a $241 million loss in 2014. Diluted earnings per share were $1.25. Operating cash flow increased to $11.920 billion from $6.842 billion, while total assets reached $65.444 billion and long-term obligations totaled $18.161 billion.

Beginning in 2015, Amazon organized its operations into North America, International, and Amazon Web Services. Their 2015 sales were $63.708 billion, $35.418 billion, and $7.880 billion, representing growth of 25%, 6%, and 70%, respectively. AWS provides compute, storage, database, and related services to developers and enterprises. The company also serves consumers through retail websites, mobile applications, Kindle e-readers, Fire devices, Echo products, and Amazon Prime; third-party sellers; and authors, publishers, musicians, filmmakers, and other content creators through programs such as Kindle Direct Publishing and Amazon Publishing.

Amazon identifies selection, price, convenience, and service quality, speed, and reliability as principal competitive factors. It regards its intellectual property as critical to success. The business is seasonal, with 33% of annual revenue recognized in the fourth quarter of 2015, and employed approximately 230,800 full- and part-time employees at year-end.

Cash, cash equivalents, and marketable securities totaled $19.8 billion at year-end, with $4.6 billion of cash capital expenditures during 2015. Amazon had no borrowings under its $2 billion credit agreement and stated that available cash flows, securities, and borrowing capacity should meet anticipated operating needs for at least 12 months. The company has never paid cash dividends.

Principal risks include intense competition, strain from expansion, fluctuating results, international operating and regulatory exposure, fulfillment and data-center complexity, seasonality, inventory management, dependence on suppliers and third parties, acquisitions, foreign exchange, data and system security, intellectual property, tax liabilities, payment processing, product liability, and potential liability for seller conduct. Specific tax matters include the IRS transfer-pricing dispute for 2005–2006 transactions and the European Commission’s investigation concerning Luxembourg tax treatment.

The December 2000 memorandum provides a country-by-country update on international electricity-sector privatization and restructuring through November 2000. It reports that growing power demand and inadequate government funding are encouraging foreign investment, unbundling of state utilities, and competition at wholesale and retail levels. Some international power companies are shifting investments toward less risky markets in the United States and Europe.

European markets are advancing under the EU Directive, with major utilities pursuing mergers, alliances, and asset sales. France accelerated market opening, Italy required major ENEL divestitures, the Netherlands planned full customer choice by 2004, and the United Kingdom’s fully deregulated market was consolidating. Competition in Germany remained constrained by grid-access rules and fees. Central and Eastern European governments continued privatizations and staged market openings, often under IMF and EU pressure; notable developments included restructuring in Bulgaria, Czech Republic, Hungary, Romania, Slovakia, Turkey, and Ukraine.

Asian economies were recovering and again moving power-sector reforms forward, although independent producers continued to face weak government guarantees, disputed power-purchase agreements, and financially troubled utilities. Australia planned full customer choice by 2003, Japan opened large customers to supplier choice, South Korea was breaking up KEPCO, and New Zealand separated generation, retailing, and networks. China pursued grid interconnection and rural electrification, India proposed major regulatory and utility reforms, while Indonesia and the Philippines faced serious utility and IPP financial problems.

Latin America had largely completed distribution and generation privatization in major economies except Mexico and Venezuela, according to the Inter-American Development Bank. New transmission concessions and privatizations were emerging, but currency instability, drought-related hydropower shortages, and political or security disruptions slowed some sales. Brazil began operating a wholesale market and faced projected supply shortages, Argentina auctioned transmission assets, Chile proposed distribution reforms, Colombia postponed privatizations, and Mexico planned to open its market without privatizing state assets.

In Africa and the Middle East, governments were increasingly admitting foreign investors, but most remained at the independent-power-project stage rather than fully privatizing their systems. Côte d’Ivoire, Gabon, Guinea, Mali, and Senegal were cited as having privatized their power sectors. Egypt, Algeria, South Africa, Saudi Arabia, and the United Arab Emirates were developing restructuring, IPP, or partial-privatization plans. Regional transmission initiatives included the West African Power Pool and planned interconnections linking Gulf and Middle Eastern systems.

The report also notes continuing regional constraints, including weak government guarantees, regulatory uncertainty, inadequate transmission access, drought dependence, high fuel costs, and underinvestment. Maps, timelines, and other restructuring exhibits were attached, and recipients were invited to submit local corrections and updates.

Jeong-Suk Cha, 77, provides most of the daily care for her 48-year-old son Alex, who has cerebral palsy and severe spinal cord damage. She transfers him with a lift, completes his physiotherapy, hygiene and meals, and risks injury doing so. His sister Jin organizes his care through detailed instruction binders, staff schedules and medical appointments. Alex receives 140 hours of personal support-worker coverage each month, limiting his mother’s respite to a four-hour weekday visit.

Following a 2004 fall, Alex lost nearly all mobility, and further falls have endangered his life. The family installed accessibility equipment, sold their home and moved into a condominium, where relatives provide round-the-clock assistance. The alternative presented for Alex is long-term care with seniors; he has written that he would “rather die” than enter a nursing home.

Alex has waited 13 years for residential care at Participation House, which has 40 spaces and 60 to 90 people on its waiting list. Ontario’s ombudsman reported 9,700 people province-wide waiting for residential care. A $100-million class-action lawsuit against Ontario alleges that wait lists for developmentally disabled adults are administered in an inconsistent and unreasonable manner. South West LHIN officials acknowledged limited data on demand, while the health minister said disabled residents need more help. Jin continues advocating for Alex and other adults with complex disabilities.

The paper proposes a methodology enabling a trusting agent to assess, in advance, the probability of not obtaining the full benefit of resources it invests when interacting with a probable trusted agent in a digital business ecosystem.

Risk is treated as central to transaction decisions, combining the probability of failure with the consequences of failure. The agent's expectations for the interaction are defined at a high level as the "context," which is decomposed into "criteria" (the specific desired outcomes). The previously defined term "FailureLevel," expressed on a Failure scale (domain 0–5), quantifies the extent to which the agent believes it may fail to achieve its desired outcomes with a given trusted agent.

Because risk is dynamic, the interaction's total "time space" is divided into non-overlapping "time slots" falling in either a pre-interaction start time phase or a post-interaction start time phase. In each pre-interaction slot, the agent determines a crisp FailureLevel from prior interaction history or by soliciting and assimilating recommendations against the criteria of the future interaction. In post-interaction slots, which can only be predicted, the agent instead determines the magnitude of occurrence of each failure level (represented as busbars), accounting for varying magnitudes of failure and yielding a better indication of the trusted agent's likely behavior. A worked example (agent "A," trusted agent "B," context "C," criteria C1–C2, six time slots) illustrates this.

For the financial resources invested per slot, the Amount Invested Curve (AIC) gives the probability of a net amount being at stake throughout a slot, calculated using fundamental probability formulae. It accounts for cumulative net worth across slots (e.g., $15,000 then $20,000) and for whether investment occurs at once or progressively.

The Factual Amount Invested Curve (FAIC) extends the AIC by convolving it with the trusted agent's FailureLevel for that slot, using the cumulants method with Gram-Charlier series expansion or Beta distribution. The resulting inflated curve shows the increased probability of a net amount required to achieve the desired outcomes once failure is considered.

Finally, the Loss of Resource Benefit (LORB) index is defined as the ordinate of the FAIC at the abscissa marking the end of the AIC: LORB = FAIC(w). It gives the probability that the trusting agent fails to achieve the full benefit of the resources invested in the slot; in the example, the LORB for slot t1 is 0.35, i.e., a 35% probability of not realizing the full benefit. These per-slot values, alongside the possible risk, support an informed decision about which trusted agent to select.

This is the ebook edition of *Papers Relating to the Foreign Relations of the United States, 1917, 1917 Supplement 1: The World War*, released in May 2018 by the Office of the Historian, Bureau of Public Affairs, U.S. Department of State. The FRUS series, established in 1861, is published in ebooks that contain full volume content with search and reading features and remain accessible without internet connectivity. The editors sought fidelity to the printed edition and recommend citing document numbers rather than page numbers, since document numbers are persistent, media-neutral identifiers.

The preface explains that the papers generally cover the period of U.S. neutrality, with some topics running past April 6, 1917, such as German goods detained in the Netherlands and German reservists removed from American ships. Latin American policy papers cover the entire year because those countries broke relations with Germany or declared war on the same grounds of neutral rights violations. Papers on China and Siam extend to China's declaration of war on August 14; a few Liberian papers postdate Liberia's declaration of war on August 4.

Editorial conventions are described: brackets enclose supplied words, suggested corrections in italics, and notations such as "omission," "garbled groups," or "sic." Parentheses are original to the documents and sometimes mark decoders' suggested readings. Translations found in the files were revised when faulty, though significant texts acted upon were not altered.

NVIDIA’s GA10x Ampere architecture supports PCIe Gen 4, providing up to 64 GB/s over a x16 slot and accelerating CPU-memory transfers and GPU DMA operations. The full GA102 GPU has seven GPCs, 42 TPCs, 84 SMs, 112 ROPs, twelve 32-bit memory controllers, and 6 MB of L2 cache. Each GPC contains six TPCs, two SMs, a dedicated Raster Engine, and two ROP partitions. Moving ROPs into the GPC increases their number and eliminates throughput mismatches between rasterization stages.

Each GA10x SM has 128 CUDA Cores, four third-generation Tensor Cores, four Texture Units, one second-generation Ray Tracing Core, a 256 KB register file, and 128 KB of configurable L1 cache/shared memory. Its four partitions support concurrent FP32 and INT32 execution, allowing 128 FP32 operations per clock or 64 FP32 plus 64 INT32 operations. GA10x also provides 33% more combined L1 and shared-memory capacity than Turing and twice the shared-memory bandwidth.

Second-generation RT Cores double Turing’s ray/triangle intersection rate and support concurrent graphics, compute, and RT workloads. New motion-blur acceleration includes an Interpolate Triangle Position unit, enabling ray-traced motion blur up to eight times faster than on Turing. Third-generation Tensor Cores are twice as powerful as Turing Tensor Cores, add TF32 and BF16 support, and implement fine-grained structured sparsity using a 2-out-of-4 non-zero pattern. Sparse matrix operations can run at twice the throughput of dense operations. Enhanced DLSS supports a 9x scaling factor, making 8K ray-traced gaming at 60 fps feasible on the RTX 3090 in tested titles.

GA10x introduced GDDR6X memory using PAM4 signaling, data rates up to 19.5 Gbps, and peak bandwidth up to 936 GB/s. MTA encoding and revised training, equalization, packaging, and PCB designs support the higher signaling rates. NVIDIA RTX IO, working with Microsoft DirectStorage, moves loading and lossless decompression of assets from SSDs to the GPU, potentially offloading dozens of CPU cores and improving I/O throughput by up to 100 times compared with hard drives and traditional storage APIs.

The GA10x-based NVIDIA A40 targets data-center visual computing. It provides up to twice the FP32 and ray-tracing throughput of Quadro RTX 6000 and up to five times the AI-training throughput, or ten times with sparsity. It includes 48 GB of memory, expandable to 96 GB through NVLink, and supports vGPU, Quadro Sync, and the EGX platform. The RTX A6000 includes 48 GB of GDDR6 memory, expandable to 96 GB with two boards, along with hardware-accelerated ray tracing, motion blur, and AI denoising.

Ampere GPUs support 4K at 120 Hz and 8K at 60 Hz through DisplayPort 1.4a and HDMI 2.1 with Display Stream Compression. Fifth-generation NVDEC adds hardware decoding for MPEG-2, VC-1, H.264, H.265, VP8, VP9, and AV1, including 8K60 AV1 playback with low CPU usage. Seventh-generation NVENC provides hardware-accelerated H.264 and HEVC encoding up to 4K and 8K respectively. GDDR6X also adds Error Detection and Replay, which detects failed memory transactions and retries them.

The GeForce RTX 3090 uses GA102 with 24 GB of GDDR6X and is reported as 1.5 times faster than TITAN RTX. The RTX 3070 uses GA104, lacks NVLink, and uses GDDR6 rather than GDDR6X.

The Shuffle offense is a team-based, motion-oriented basketball offense traced to Bruce Drake at Oklahoma and a predecessor of the Princeton, Flex, Hawk, and Reverse Action offenses. It keeps all five players moving and rotating through positions, emphasizing passing, spacing, screening, rebounding, ball security, and little dribbling rather than one-on-one play. Basic continuity involves reversals, rub and shuffle cuts, back cuts, flash cuts, down screens, and opposite-side overloads. Because players are interchangeable, all must recognize defensive reads and counters, including overplaying, switching, denying, anticipating, and showing on screens. Counteroptions include cutting over or under screens, feeding the post, using a double screen, popping out for a shot, back cutting for a lob, and passing over the top to a sealing post player. Overplayed passing lanes create back-cut opportunities, while denied passes can lead to point back doors.

At its final 2017 meeting, the Brunswick school board approved the first step toward placing a renewal of the district's expiring 10-year, $4.67 million emergency levy on the May ballot, with no tax increase. The board also authorized the issuance of up to $10 million in notes to build a new middle school replacing Visintainer and Edwards and make other facility improvements, and revised Fiscal Year 2018 appropriations to reflect new grant funds, including increases to IDEA Part B, Title II, Title I and the OHSAA Tournament fund. Superintendent Michael Mayell recognized four donations totaling $6,690, including $5,000 from the Tifft Family Fund, $1,500 from American Legion Post 703, $125 from the Greek Catholic Union Lodge 77 and $65 from Mr. and Mrs. Robert Safran. The board recognized Lisa Durichko, who is leaving the area after 12 years of service and did not seek re-election, and entered executive session to discuss employment, discipline and investigations, with no action taken. An organizational meeting is set for 6:30 p.m. Jan. 8, followed by the regular meeting Jan. 22.

The AEGEAN study evaluated apixaban adherence and persistence in patients with atrial fibrillation. Part 1 randomized 1,162 subjects to Primary SOC or an Additional Education Program; 1,160 received study drug and 1,054 completed Week 24. Part 2 included Primary SOC, Secondary SOC, and Continued Additional Education groups, with 1,003 subjects completing Week 48. Baseline characteristics were comparable across groups; median age was 74 years, 59.9% were male, and mean MMSE was 28.3. Treatment exposure and interruption were similar between the Part 1 groups, and mean prescribed-dose compliance exceeded 95% through Week 24 and 94% at Week 48 across Part 2 groups.

The primary endpoint was the percentage of days with correct apixaban dosing through Week 24. Adherence was 91.64% with Primary SOC and 91.88% with Additional Education, with no significant difference. Adherence from Weeks 24–48 was also similar across groups: 87.59%, 87.51%, and 88.41% for Primary SOC, Secondary SOC, and Continued Additional Education, respectively. Adherence declined from the first 12 weeks to Weeks 12–24 and from Weeks 24–48 in all groups. Persistence at Weeks 24 and 48 did not differ significantly between groups. The proportion fully adherent over time was 28.1% versus 26.5% at Week 24 and approximately 15% in each Part 2 group at Week 48. Subgroup analyses generally showed no significant interactions, although atrial fibrillation type and sex affected differences in adherence during Weeks 24–48.

Safety outcomes were similar between groups. Before Week 24, adverse events occurred in 51.2% and 52.0%, bleeding in 6.5% and 9.0%, and major bleeding in 0.7% and 1.1% of the Primary SOC and Additional Education groups. Beyond Week 24, adverse events occurred in 33.8%, 40.8%, and 38.6% of the three groups, while major bleeding occurred in 0.7%, 0.4%, and 0.3%. Twenty-four deaths were reported, with no pregnancies or clinically concerning hepatic or renal laboratory signals. The study concluded that apixaban adherence and persistence were high through 48 weeks, but the proactive educational program provided no additional benefit.
The building can favor a successful Philadelphia team, while the goalie remains calm, makes big saves, and shrugs off bumps and traffic.

SD Memory Cards have User and Protected Areas and are classified as SDSC (up to 2 GB), SDHC (over 2 GB through 32 GB), or SDXC (over 32 GB through 2 TB). Hosts supporting higher-capacity cards must also support lower-capacity cards. Five speed classes are defined: Class 0 for legacy cards, and Classes 2, 4, 6, and 10 with minimum performance of 2, 4, 6, and 10 MB/s, respectively.

The SD bus uses serial command, response, and data tokens, with CRC protection, session-based card addressing, and single- or multiple-block transfers over one or four data lines. Cards have identification, status, configuration, and card-specific registers and may be reset through power cycling or CMD0.

UHS-I provides Default Speed, High Speed, SDR104, and DDR50 modes, with high-speed modes using 1.8 V signaling and a four-bit bus. Initialization includes voltage negotiation and switching through ACMD41 and CMD11; sampling-point tuning uses CMD19. UHS-II supports legacy SD bus operation plus FD156, optional HD312, FD312, and FD624 modes, with separate PHY, device, enumeration, configuration, and SD-TRAN initialization stages.

The host controls communication using broadcast and addressed commands. Card initialization typically uses CMD0, CMD8, ACMD41, CMD2, and CMD3 before card selection with CMD7. Data transfers support block reads and writes, CRC validation, buffering, pre-erasing, aborts, erase, DISCARD, and Full User Area Logical Erase. Write protection may be mechanical, internal, or password-based.

CMD42 provides password-based lock and unlock operations. Card Ownership Protection adds Force Erase Password management, COP Unlock, restricted password functions, and protected force-erase operations. ROM cards reject specified write-related commands as illegal and may optionally support CMD42 and security commands.

TDSAT granted Airtel and Idea interim relief from penalties for unreported tariffs, while allowing Trai to seek details on discounts or concessions. MIT and Cambridge researchers found that the black hole in the Phoenix cluster may recycle hot gas into cold material that fuels star formation. ALMA observations revealed cold-gas filaments extending 20,000 light-years from the central black hole, while Chandra observations mapped jets and bubbles containing 10-million-degree gas. The two maps spatially corresponded, suggesting the bubbles produce cold gas that falls back onto the central galaxy and fuels further starbursts. The cluster contains about 1,000 galaxies, and its central galaxy forms roughly 1,000 stars annually. The study was published in The Astrophysical Journal.

This study examined whether first- and second-trimester placental biomarkers are associated with postpartum hemorrhage (PPH) or retained placenta. The analysis used the prospective NuMoM2b cohort of nulliparous participants with singleton pregnancies and public maternal-serum biomarker data. Because the dataset lacked direct blood-loss measurements and PPH diagnoses, the outcome was a composite of retained placenta and/or hemorrhage requiring transfusion (RP/PPH).

The final sample included 2,192 participants, 67 of whom (3.1%) experienced RP/PPH. Compared with others, this group was more likely to have preeclampsia, cesarean birth, and instrumental delivery, but no demographic differences were identified. Biomarker comparisons used Kruskal–Wallis tests with a Bonferroni-corrected significance threshold of 0.004.

Participants with RP/PPH had significantly higher second-trimester levels of soluble endoglin, β-hCG, inhibin A, PAPP-A, and soluble fms-like tyrosine kinase-1 (sFlt-1). First-trimester sFlt-1 and the sFlt-1/PlGF ratio were also higher, while PlGF did not differ significantly at either time point. Among participants without preeclampsia, second-trimester β-hCG, inhibin A, PAPP-A, and sFlt-1 remained significantly elevated in those later experiencing RP/PPH; no biomarker significantly distinguished RP/PPH groups among participants with preeclampsia. Biomarker changes also differed by preeclampsia status: participants with preeclampsia and RP/PPH had greater increases in PAPP-A and decreases in soluble endoglin, whereas those without preeclampsia had greater increases in sFlt-1.

Limitations included the small number of RP/PPH cases, reliance on a proxy capturing retained placenta and severe hemorrhage requiring transfusion, selection of participants with adverse pregnancy outcomes, and no modeling of demographic or pregnancy-related covariates. The findings identify placental biomarkers, particularly second-trimester measurements, as targets for further investigation of early PPH risk prediction.

Five Gor Mahia players—Meddie Kagere, Musa Mohammed, Kenneth Muguna, Jacques Tuyisenge and George Odhiambo—headlined the 2017 Kenyan Premier League MVP shortlist, giving the club a chance to win the award for a third consecutive year. Distributed systems patterns provide a shared vocabulary of names and definitions, enabling quicker understanding, knowledge sharing, and further learning. They reduce time spent arguing over terminology or explaining concepts under different labels, allowing discussions to focus on details and implementation. The adoption of “sidecar container” illustrates how a common term lets developers immediately discuss uses and suitable containers rather than redefine the concept.

Former firefighter-paramedic Luis Garcia spent nearly $40,000 of his savings on 800 doses of naloxone, commonly called Narcan, to distribute free and teach others how to use it. After witnessing about 3,000 overdose cases during 28 years with the Boynton Beach Fire Department, Garcia now trains business owners, residents and law enforcement across Florida. At a February 3, 2018 Treasure Coast Substance Awareness Coalition event in Stuart, he gave away about 50 doses following training sessions. Garcia also carries Narcan to public overdoses and performs CPR until help arrives, saying he revived five of six people he assisted over 18 months. Narcan blocks opioids from the brain and can stop or reverse an overdose. As Treasure Coast agencies increasingly carried the drug, the Martin County Sheriff’s Office reported using it 62 times in response to 153 overdose cases in 2017. Garcia’s South Florida Opioid Crisis Mortality Reduction Project focuses on donating Narcan to businesses and educating law enforcement agencies that do not yet carry it.

Clear Capital’s February 2017 Home Data Index reported that U.S. home prices rose 0.9% in the latest quarter and 6.1% year over year, the highest annual growth since February 2015. Quarterly gains were 1.0% in the South and West, 0.8% in the Midwest, and 0.7% in the Northeast. San Jose and Hartford each declined 0.3%, while Portland grew nearly 2%; eight major metros grew at least 1.5%, compared with three a year earlier. Sixteen of the 50 largest metros exceeded housing-bubble peak prices, and record-setting major and micro markets represented about one-third of national housing stock. Clear Capital projected 2%–3% annual growth in 2017 and said nearly 40% of homeowners who bought during the housing-bubble peak could be above water by year-end if growth approached 2016 levels.

The Steelers won eight straight, including a 39–38 thriller over Baltimore, and will host the Patriots in Week 15 with the AFC’s top seed at stake. Ryan Shazier is injured, while Tom Brady is playing at an MVP level.

This secondary analysis assessed the Democratic Republic of the Congo’s COVID-19 vaccination programme during its first year, from April 2021 to March 2022. It used paper-based Ministry of Health and WHO African Region data covering vaccination sites, doses, demographics, vaccine types, and priority groups, with descriptive analysis conducted in Excel.

Vaccination began in 16 of 26 provinces, with substantial geographic disparities. Fully vaccinated coverage was highest in Kasai-Oriental (6.91%) and lowest in Kwilu (0.07%), Tshuapa (0.03%), and Équateur (0.02%). The number of functional vaccination sites increased over time but was unevenly distributed; Kinshasa consistently had the most, while several provinces had few or none. By March 2022, approximately 5.7% of the population had received at least one dose and 1.03% had completed the primary series. Monthly uptake was initially low, peaked at 378,782 doses in February 2022, and then declined without significant change in second-dose uptake. Men outnumbered women among vaccinated people in every province except Kasai-Oriental. Overall, 8,302 health workers and 46,495 older adults completed the primary series, with notable provincial differences.

The country used AstraZeneca, Johnson & Johnson, Pfizer, Moderna, and Sinovac vaccines. Janssen was the most frequently administered vaccine at 48%, followed by Moderna at 25% and Pfizer at 17%. In comparisons with Central African countries, the DRC received 14,394,340 doses but administered 1,143,186, or 8% of doses received, and had the lowest proportion of the population receiving at least one dose in the comparison table.

Implementation was initially delayed by an AstraZeneca pause, safety concerns, adverse events, and vaccine hesitancy. Additional vaccines were introduced from September 2021. Concurrent disease outbreaks, limited health personnel, strikes, weak access to services, expiry risks, and unsuitable donated vaccines further constrained delivery. National coordination established in February 2022 led to an acceleration plan; more than 2.5 million people were reportedly vaccinated in three months, compared with 800,000 in the preceding eleven months, although the target of vaccinating 11 million people by April 2022 was not met.

The authors noted limitations in denominator estimates, individual vaccination histories, aggregated data, and comorbidity records and recommended further research. They concluded that the rollout achieved some progress but remained limited, highlighting the need for stronger health systems, better targeting of high-risk groups, community and religious engagement, and integration of COVID-19 vaccination with other primary healthcare interventions.

Oversold markets have declined significantly over a defined period and may exhibit mean reversion, with sharp deviations reversing and producing short-term rebounds while longer-term returns gravitate toward average. The passage recommends defining oversold conditions objectively with indicators such as a three-day RSI below 20 and backtesting the strategy. Its example buys the S&P 500 at the close when the three-day RSI is below 20 and sells when the market closes above the previous day’s high. The 1985-to-present backtest is presented as profitable, with a 0.64% average gain per trade, 75% win rate, roughly 7.6–7.7% CAGR, 26% maximum drawdown, and 2.4–2.5 profit factor, though conflicting trade counts are given. Dividends were excluded, performance before 1990 was weaker, and mean reversion may not persist.

Robert S. Putnam, retiring from Harvard's Kennedy School at 77, was honored at a conference; the author, who knows him personally, was not invited. Putnam's concept of "social capital" first appeared in a West Virginia education report a century ago but gained academic attention through James Coleman's work in the late 1980s. Putnam, an expert on Italian politics, adopted the idea in the early 1990s to explain northern Italy's stronger economic and political performance, attributing it to the North's history of independent city states and civic engagement versus southern Italy's centuries under autocratic Spain and the resulting mafia dominance. He has claimed that 1870s civic choral group membership could explain 90% of regional growth differences, though the author notes correlation does not imply causation.

"Bowling Alone" (1990s) popularized the concept, triggering academic and World Bank interest and making Putnam one of the most-cited living social scientists. Two definitional disputes are discussed: Putnam favors civic group membership, while a competing concept emphasizes "generalized trust," which Fukuyama and others treat as a precondition for civic engagement's economic benefits. A 1996 QJE paper by Knack and Keefer found no effect from civic membership but significant effects from generalized trust on European growth. Putnam also distinguishes "bridging" (cross-group solidarity) from "bonding" (in-group solidarity), which he maps onto northern and southern Italy respectively. His findings that ethnic fragmentation and diversity do not raise social capital have been taken up by ethnonationalists and nationalists, including some Trump supporters, though the author considers this depressing and contrary to the concept's virtues.

Second-quarter revenue was $6.350 billion, compared with $4.002 billion a year earlier. Automotive revenue was $5.376 billion, energy generation and storage revenue was $368.2 million, and services and other revenue was $605.1 million. Vehicle pricing adjustments increased the likelihood that customers would exercise previously offered buyback options. In United States v. Watson and O'Hearn (1st Cir. 2004), the government appealed from two district court orders in a 2001 prosecution; the First Circuit dismissed the appeal for lack of appellate jurisdiction, holding that neither order fell within the Criminal Appeals Act, 18 U.S.C. § 3731.

Background: In 1997 Zachary Dulac bound and robbed Watson and his live-in girlfriend, stealing 55 pounds of marijuana. Watson recruited Richard Maynard, O'Hearn, and George Lubell, who on May 31, 1997 assaulted Dulac in a Maine motel parking lot, took $17,000, and threatened further attacks. Watson, O'Hearn, and Lubell were indicted in 2001 for conspiracy, Travel Act violations, and use of a firearm during a crime of violence. Because no one could identify O'Hearn, Anthony Spera, who knew both men, was a key government witness.

Spera pleaded guilty to unrelated federal narcotics offenses, was sentenced to 30 months, and faced mandatory deportation. Released in December 2002 and detained by the INS, the AUSA on January 14, 2003 asked INS to defer deportation until after Spera testified and to report changes in his custody; INS logged the request, released Spera on bail January 16, 2003, and failed to notify the AUSA. After a recusal motion and reassignment postponed the trial to July 12, 2004, INS retook Spera into custody on March 4, 2004; the AUSA's letter sat at the bottom of Spera's file, the reporting notation was overlooked, and Spera was deported to Italy on June 1, 2004, unbeknownst to the government. Discovered June 28, Spera refused to return unless allowed to remain permanently in the United States, so the government moved for a continuance and for leave to take a deposition in Italy. On July 8 the district court denied the continuance from the bench, citing the delay, doubts about admissibility, the Speedy Trial Act, and the government's "comedy of errors." On July 9 it denied the renewed motion on four grounds: the case was over three years old (indictment April 12, 2001); Speedy Trial time may have run (at least 78 unexcluded days); the missing witness resulted from inexcusable government negligence; and obtaining the testimony would take 6 to 12 months. The trial date was held and the deposition request denied as moot.

Jurisdiction: Government criminal appeals are disfavored and require express statutory authorization. The Supreme Court's "all statutory barriers" language in Wilson concerned the first paragraph of § 3731 (dismissal of indictments); the second paragraph, as amended in 1970 to cover exclusions and to be construed liberally, reaches pretrial orders suppressing or excluding evidence. First Circuit precedent treats some case-management orders as appealable when they practically exclude evidence, but ordinary case-management orders are not. A causal connection to evidence exclusion is necessary but insufficient: an order must itself be the practical equivalent of a suppression or exclusion order, directly denying the government the right to use evidence; incidental effects will not suffice. Drogoul (11th Cir.), where the district court denied foreign depositions on Sixth Amendment/treaty grounds and thus directly excluded evidence, was inapposite, because here the rulings rested on delay and case-management grounds and never addressed the merits of the deposition request. The claim that the court masked an exclusion ruling was unfounded. Footnotes note that the INS was abolished by the Homeland Security Act, with its enforcement functions transferred to ICE, and address the "Pandora's box" misnomer and the 1968 amendment's legislative history.

Based on Michael Gayed’s research, the lumber/gold ratio serves as a risk-on/risk-off indicator: stocks are held during risk-on periods and long-term Treasuries during risk-off periods. Lumber may signal economic turning points because housing and construction are closely tied to the business cycle, while gold offers diversification and low correlation with stocks and bonds. A modified backtest using WOOD and GLD with SPY and TLT returned 11.4% annually since 2008, averaged 2.2% per trade, and suffered a 35% drawdown. Replacing TLT with gold reduced annual returns to 8.7%. The authors caution that such a drawdown could cause many investors to abandon the strategy.

Editorial notes and annotations supplement the printed documents with relevant unpublished material, source locations, related-document references, event descriptions, and citations to public statements. Index numbers refer to document numbers, not pages. The Advisory Committee on Historical Diplomatic Documentation oversees the series’ compilation, editorial process, and declassification, though it need not review each volume individually. The Department of State’s Office of Information Programs and Services reviewed the volume under Executive Order 13526 and applicable law between 2015 and 2019, withholding one document, making substantial excisions in 13, and minor excisions in 20.

This volume documents U.S.–Soviet relations under the Reagan administration from January 1983 through March 1985. Following NSDD 75, it examines the administration’s four-part policy agenda: arms control, human rights, regional issues, and bilateral relations. The documentation covers policy development by Secretary of State George Shultz, National Security Advisors William Clark and Robert McFarlane, and NSC staff member Jack Matlock, as well as U.S. dealings with Soviet Ambassador Anatoly Dobrynin and Foreign Minister Andrei Gromyko. It also shows how the administration assessed Soviet leadership succeeding Yuri Andropov and Konstantin Chernenko, neither of whom met with Reagan.

This continuation of U.S. Patent Application No. 15/898,212 claims priority to Provisional Application No. 62/459,802 and describes systems for localizing the position and orientation of users, head-mounted displays, and physical objects in augmented and virtual reality environments. It addresses the need for rapid, accurate, low-latency tracking to position virtual content, maintain its stability during head movement, enable interaction with totems, haptic devices, hands, and wearables, and reduce sensory mismatch or motion sickness.

Embodiments include wearable display assemblies with local processing, sensor modules, remote processing, cloud resources, and a shared “passable world model” containing real-world imagery, spatial points, and other environmental information. Localization may combine electromagnetic tracking, inertial measurements, cameras, depth sensors, SLAM-based vision tracking, and wireless or environmental sensing. Electromagnetic embodiments use orthogonal transmitter and receiver coils to determine relative position and orientation, while compact emitters, duty-cycle control, sensor fusion, dynamic frequency tuning, noise cancellation, and calibration reduce power use and improve accuracy. Vision-based embodiments triangulate image features into 3D maps, match projected map points with camera features, estimate head pose, and divide mapping and tracking into stages optimized for low latency and embedded processing.

Other embodiments use stacked waveguides, decode QR codes to request network-hosted virtual content, trigger content based on sensor information, and share viewed content between users through activation gateways or sharing credentials. Additional applications described include gaming, communication, education, healthcare, shopping, navigation, workplace collaboration, and other augmented-reality interactions.

NVIDIA’s Turing GPU architecture introduces a hybrid rendering model combining real-time ray tracing, rasterization, AI, and simulation. Each Streaming Multiprocessor includes an RT Core that accelerates BVH traversal and ray-triangle intersection testing, freeing the SM for shading and compute work; drivers handle BVH building and refitting, while applications manage ray generation and shading. Turing delivers more than 10 Giga Rays per second, roughly ten times Pascal’s software ray-tracing performance.

NVIDIA NGX is a Turing-based deep-learning stack that uses Tensor Cores and pre-trained neural models through a thin API integrated with CUDA, DirectX, Vulkan, and TensorRT. Its Deep Learning Super-Sampling (DLSS) matches 64-times-supersampled reference imagery while reducing shading work. Standard DLSS renders fewer input samples and infers a target-resolution result; DLSS 2X processes target-resolution input with a larger network to approximate 64x supersampling. Other NGX features include neural inpainting, AI-generated slow-motion frames, and AI Super Rez, which enlarges images or video by 2x, 4x, or 8x and can perform 1080p-to-4K upscaling in real time.

Mesh Shading adds cooperative Task and Mesh Shaders. A task shader processes object lists, launches mesh shaders, selects level-of-detail versions, and performs geometry culling or modification. This reduces CPU draw-call bottlenecks and supports real-time rendering of hundreds of thousands of objects.

Variable Rate Shading controls shading independently from visibility at 16-by-16-pixel granularity, with multiple pixel-footprint options. Its applications include content-adaptive shading for spatially or temporally uniform regions, motion-adaptive shading for moving objects, and foveated rendering that reduces peripheral shading or increases it at the viewer’s focus. Under multisample anti-aliasing, shading can also rise to two, four, or eight times per pixel, up to the MSAA sample count.

Texture Space Shading computes and caches shading values in texture space rather than directly on the screen-space pixel grid. It decouples visibility and appearance sampling, supports adjustable MIP-map levels, and reuses shaded texels across pixels, frames, views, and other computations to improve temporal stability and performance. A VR application can, for example, render one eye and sample it for the other while shading only newly required texels.

Multi-View Rendering supports up to four hardware views per pass and up to 32 views through APIs. Geometry and view-independent attributes are fetched or evaluated once and shared, while view-dependent attributes are computed per view. Applications include stereo and wide-field-of-view VR, multiple character instances, shadow buffers, and cascaded shadow maps. Turing also adds bindless constant-buffer and unordered-access views, mixed resource heaps, USB Type-C and VirtualLink support, foveated rendering, and RT Core acceleration for ray-traced VR audio.

The full TU104 chip contains 48 SMs, 3,072 CUDA Cores, 368 Tensor Cores, 48 RT Cores, a 256-bit memory interface, and second-generation NVLink. The Tesla T4 variant has 40 SMs, 2,560 CUDA Cores, 320 Tensor Cores, and 320 GB/s memory bandwidth. TU106, used in the GeForce RTX 2070, has 36 SMs, 2,304 CUDA Cores, 288 Tensor Cores, and 36 RT Cores, but lacks NVLink and SLI.

Hybrid-rendering performance depends on workload distribution rather than a single operation rate. A representative Turing frame spends about 20% of its time in DLSS and 80% in rendering; within rendering, roughly half is ray tracing and half rasterization or G-buffer work. Integer instructions execute concurrently and are assumed active for 35% of shading time. NVIDIA’s RTX-OPS metric weights Tensor, FP32, RT, and INT32 peak throughputs by these assumed utilization rates; the cited RTX 2080 Ti example yields 78 RTX-OPS.

Ray tracing casts rays backward from the camera through image pixels into the scene, where intersections determine reflections, refractions, shadows, and indirect lighting. BVH hierarchies reduce the number of triangle tests required, while denoising allows accurate results with fewer rays and can improve noisy images. With RT Cores, denoisers, and hybrid rendering, Turing supports real-time ray-traced shadows, ambient occlusion, and reflections, including physically correct contact hardening and glossy reflections that conventional screen-space techniques cannot fully reproduce. The document concludes with NVIDIA’s accuracy, liability, licensing, warranty, trademark, and copyright disclaimers.

SOS disruption schemes direct wing ballhandlers toward corner or baseline checkpoints while defenders use pass denials, post fronts, and Helpside “I” positions. In Straight SOS defense, the on-ball defender pushes the handler toward the checkpoint; if the handler stops before it, the defender applies a hard smother. No trap occurs unless the handler penetrates inside the baseline checkpoint.

Base Go I is an automatic baseline trap triggered by penetration inside that checkpoint. The on-ball defender and low Helpside defender trap the ballhandler while the other defenders rotate into a Triangle I. After a pass out, defenders close out, deny passes, front posts, and resume their assigned matchups.

Base Go Red is a predetermined early sideline trap initiated when the ball is received or dribbled below the free-throw-line extended area. The closest defender traps as the remaining defenders rotate into a Triangle I and apply near-player rules. Its purpose is to disrupt the offense and alter its tempo.

For side screens, SOS switches aggressively above the free-throw line to deny quick shots and middle penetration. Below the line, the defense traps near the baseline or corner before the screen develops. Rotations cover pass-outs, skip passes, and post entries, followed by set, front, snuggle-denial, and Helpside positions.

The “All Out” disruption attacks the point guard before a screen or pass can occur, using a double team to force a free-lance offense. If the ballhandler passes to a rolling post player, a secondary baseline trap is used. Rotations occur as the passer releases the ball, after which standard SOS fundamentals resume.

The paper introduces a local Boltzmann Generator architecture for generating equilibrium ensembles of large crystalline materials more efficiently than molecular dynamics and Monte Carlo methods. Its graph neural network and augmented coupling flow operate on local particle environments, giving linear scaling with fixed neighborhood size and avoiding the quadratic costs of global architectures. Training uses only the target potential energy rather than target-distribution samples. Models can be trained on small cells and transferred to much larger systems, while conditioning on thermodynamic states or interaction-potential parameters amortizes training across conditions.

Experiments on Lennard-Jones and Stillinger-Weber crystals showed that models trained on 216-particle monatomic water ice or 256-particle FCC Lennard-Jones systems reproduced molecular-dynamics radial distribution functions and energy distributions accurately in systems exceeding 1,000 particles, even without reweighting. Local models achieved higher effective sample sizes and substantially lower training costs than global Boltzmann Generators; for example, 216-particle monatomic ice converged in about four GPU days, compared with more than 330 GPU days reported for a 512-particle global model with roughly 0.2% effective sample size.

The trained flows enabled direct free-energy estimation through targeted free energy perturbation. Joint and marginal Helmholtz free-energy estimates for cubic ice agreed with MD+MBAR references within \(10^{-3}k_BT\) per particle up to 1,000 particles, with marginal estimates remaining accurate at 1,728 particles. Models trained on 180-particle FCC and HCP Lennard-Jones cells were transferred to 1,080-particle systems and accurately reproduced Gibbs free-energy differences, cutoff-dependent phase stability, and densities from NPT simulations. Stillinger-Weber models conditioned on the three-body interaction strength reproduced Gibbs free energies across diamond-cubic, β-tin, and BCC structures and their size-dependent phase transitions. A temperature- and volume-conditioned silicon model also reproduced the MD+MBAR coexistence line between diamond-cubic and β-tin phases. The approach is presented as a scalable tool for accurate free energies and phase stability across materials and thermodynamic conditions, with future work targeting liquid sampling and broader chemical-space generalization.

The article says gold rallied strongly on Friday while the U.S. Dollar Index fell sharply. Gold remains below a rising resistance line and follows a pattern resembling 2011–2013 and the November 2012 rally. Silver, platinum, and mining stocks showed little visible strength; the VanEck Junior Gold Miners ETF failed to rise meaningfully and closed below its April high for a third consecutive session. At $66 in premarket trading, its movement was described as a breather reinforcing a bearish setup. Because gold stocks normally outperform early in precious-metals rallies, their failure to follow gold was presented as an early sign of a larger decline.

The USD Index returned to its July high and the neck level of an inverse head-and-shoulders pattern, which the author says verifies a bullish breakout toward at least 101.3. Stocks also paused after failing to surpass previous highs and falling below rising support. The author compares volatile gold, a strengthening dollar, and weakening stocks to 2008, while maintaining that the “Peak Chaos” thesis remains intact.

At American University’s commencement, the speaker praised the university and its graduates before turning to the importance of world peace. He rejected peace imposed by military force and advocated a practical, dynamic peace built through concrete actions, effective agreements, tolerance, and peaceful settlement of disputes. Because nuclear total war could inflict global, generational destruction, he argued that deterrence and weapons stockpiles alone were insufficient.

He urged Americans to reassess their attitudes toward peace, the Soviet Union, the Cold War, and freedom at home. Americans should recognize Soviet achievements, shared fears of war, and common interests in ending the arms race while resisting distorted views of the other side. U.S. policy should combine defense of vital interests with military self-restraint, peaceful competition, support for self-determination, stronger international law, communication, arms control, and eventual disarmament.

Announcing progress toward a nuclear test-ban treaty, the speaker said Khrushchev and Macmillan had agreed to high-level Moscow discussions. He also declared that the United States would not conduct atmospheric nuclear tests while other states refrained and would not be first to resume them.

Domestically, he argued that government must protect civil rights and citizens must respect law and the rights of others, noting that peace and freedom are inseparable. He urged graduates to support public service through initiatives such as the Peace Corps and National Service Corps, concluding that the United States should pursue security, human rights, and peace rather than a strategy of annihilation.

Hola Publishing International expanded its Spanish-language imprint and print-on-demand services in Mexico, allowing orders of 25–1,000 books with global distribution, multiple formats, and 100% author rights. The expansion addresses gaps in Mexico’s digital print market, reduces shipping barriers, and achieves a 60-day print turnaround.

Amazon.com, Inc.’s Form 8-K reports that at its May 22, 2019 annual meeting, shareholders elected 11 director nominees: Jeffrey P. Bezos, Rosalind G. Brewer, Jamie S. Gorelick, Daniel P. Huttenlocher, Judith A. McGrath, Indra K. Nooyi, Jonathan J. Rubinstein, Thomas O. Ryder, Patricia Q. Stonesifer, and Wendell P. Weeks.
