The disclosure describes technologies for time-aware networks (TANs) and time-sensitive applications (TSAs), focusing on precise synchronization, low-latency and scalable gate control, shared physical links, dynamic end-station configuration, and energy-efficient communication. It identifies these needs in IoT, industrial automation, telecommunications, data centers, vehicles, and other connected systems, and notes a gap between TSN standards and their implementations.

A TAN comprises interconnected time-aware systems within one or more generalized Precision Time Protocol domains. PTP/gPTP synchronizes clocks, compensates for link delay and residence time, supports GM selection through BMCA, and provides PTP or arbitrary timescales. TSN traffic is organized into traffic classes and queues using configurable transmission-selection algorithms. IEEE 802.1Qbv gate control lists schedule queue gates to open and close, reserving time windows for critical traffic.

Conventional NIC gate-control implementations store large gate lists in on-chip memory and program entries individually, consuming significant silicon area and power and potentially exceeding short application cycle times. The disclosed architecture instead stores odd and even GCL banks in host memory, uses small NIC-side registers and a prefetch buffer, and has the MAC fetch and decode entries through a dedicated channel while software programs the inactive bank. This approach supports larger and finer-grained schedules, faster programming, lower latency, and reduced NIC silicon and power requirements.

For end stations hosting multiple talker applications, the disclosure describes presenting the device to centralized management as a virtual switch connected to virtual single-talker end stations. This permits centralized configuration of the physical link and coordination of workloads to limit interference. It also discusses MSRP, MMRP, and MVRP stream reservation, talker and listener status declarations, and a complex configuration arrangement incorporating a system layer, network interface, and gate control engine.

Just Patios manufactures customisable galvanised or Colorbond carports designed for Australian weather, protecting vehicles from corrosion. Its Flat/Skillion, Raised Flyover and Gable ranges suit various homes and vehicles and can be freestanding or attached. Builders inspect properties, coordinate installation and advise on council regulations. The company also offers patios, covers and roofing with 15-year warranties.

Mark Mobius told CNBC a 30 percent correction in U.S. markets is "not unforeseen," citing ETF outflows and 24/7 computer-driven selling that could create snowball effects without a safety valve. He warned of contagion risk from Turkey and weak conditions in Argentina and Brazil, though he sees selective opportunities in a "stock picker's market." Paul Krugman also warned of a possible 1997-98-style self-reinforcing emerging market currency crisis.

IUP President Michael Driscoll temporarily halted an Academic Integrity Board investigation and allowed senior Lake Ingle, cited for violating the code after speaking on transgender issues, to return. A senior faculty member will monitor the class as Driscoll accepts possible criticism for not following policy.
Eight views depict a desk lamp design, with dashed portions excluded from the claimed design.

The passage explains trading options on TQQQ, an ETF that tracks the Nasdaq-100. Call options give the right to buy an underlying security at a set price, while put options give the right to sell it at a set price. Call options may suit expectations of rising prices, puts expectations of falling prices, and puts can hedge losses. TQQQ options are available in American and European styles and offer different expiration dates and strike prices.

Common strategies include buying calls, buying puts, writing covered calls, writing puts, and combining these approaches. Strategy selection depends on market conditions, investment goals, risk tolerance, liquidity, option term, volatility, and the amount at risk. The passage emphasizes backtesting strategies and using quantified, fundamental, and technical analysis before trading.

Option trading is more complex and speculative than stock trading and can produce amplified gains or losses through leverage. Investors should set maximum risk limits, use risk-management tools such as stop-loss orders, diversify, avoid leverage until experienced, and never invest more than they can afford to lose. Entry and exit timing should reflect expected price movements and target levels.

Fair value can be estimated with the Black-Scholes model, although it may be inaccurate and should be supplemented with other analysis. Trading costs vary by broker and may include commissions, contract fees, and slippage. Minimum funding requirements also vary. Profits are generally subject to capital gains tax depending on individual and jurisdictional circumstances. Regulations may cover capital requirements, leverage, margin calls, stop-loss orders, and hedging, so investors should consult qualified brokers and tax specialists about applicable rules.

In his inaugural address, President Biden declared that "democracy has prevailed" and marked the peaceful transfer of power, noting that the ceremony occurred just days after a violent mob sought to overturn the will of the people. He praised predecessors of both parties and saluted former President Carter, and cited sites of national significance—Lincoln's Emancipation Proclamation, Martin Luther King Jr.'s dream, the suffrage march, and Arlington National Cemetery—while noting the swearing-in of Kamala Harris as the first woman elected to national office.

He identified the nation's crises: a pandemic that killed as many in one year as all of World War II, job and business losses, a long-delayed cry for racial justice, climate change, and political extremism, white supremacy, and domestic terrorism. He argued these require unity, calling on Americans to confront "anger, resentment, hatred" and to reject manufactured facts and an "uncivil war" of red versus blue, rural versus urban, conservative versus liberal. He cited Lincoln's "whole soul" in the Emancipation Proclamation and framed his own mission as bringing America together.

Biden pledged to be "a President for all Americans," to fight as hard for those who did not support him, and to defend the Constitution, democracy, truth, and America, listing opportunity, security, liberty, dignity, respect, honor, and truth as the common objects that define Americans. He promised to repair alliances and lead by example abroad, asked for a silent prayer for the 400,000 who died in the pandemic, and closed with pledges to serve "not of power, but of possibilities," invoking the verse from "American Anthem" about giving "my best to you."

University at Albany chemists synthesized pure manganese diboride using an arc melter that heated compressed manganese and boron powders to 3,000°C, followed by rapid cooling. The resulting strained, deformed atomic structure stores substantial energy and combusts only when exposed to an ignition agent such as kerosene. Compared with aluminum used in solid rocket boosters, manganese diboride is over 20% more energetic by weight and about 150% more energetic by volume, potentially reducing rocket fuel mass and storage space. Related boron-based compounds may also support more durable catalytic converters and plastic-recycling catalysts.

Cristiano Ronaldo received a five-match domestic ban for pushing a referee during Real Madrid’s Super Cup win over Barcelona. Chelsea’s Gary Cahill and Cesc Fabregas were sent off against Burnley, while Jonjo Shelvey’s dismissal contributed to Newcastle’s 2-0 loss to Tottenham. UEFA is preparing a new respect campaign.

Barry “The Hatchet” Vagnoni, an Eagles fan since 1954, is preparing his Reading, Pennsylvania, home’s 2,000-square-foot locker-room-style man cave for Super Bowl LII. The room has 16 televisions, a 35-foot bar, Eagles memorabilia, and family-friendly rules requiring guests to wear Eagles gear. Vagnoni and his wife, Dawn, typically host 125–175 friends and family with free food and drinks and optional donations. Barry leads cheers and entertainment, while Dawn cooks, manages entry, and photographs guests. Their 2018 party will feature more than 100 guests, a band, dancers, and wings. Gap trading involves price levels left untraded between one day’s close and the next session’s open. Gaps occur across instruments and timeframes, although overnight gaps are most common and often result from news or imbalances accumulated outside trading hours. Major categories include common gaps, exhaustion gaps following extended moves, runaway gaps after sharp moves from consolidation, and breakaway gaps signaling strong directional moves.

Traders can either fade gaps or follow them. Stocks generally show more mean-reversion behavior than other asset classes, making them more suitable for fading. Gap fills may occur intraday or over several days, with smaller gaps more likely to be filled. In 25 years of S&P 500 E-mini futures data, same-day fill rates for gaps of at least 0.1% were 59% for bullish gaps and 61% for bearish gaps. For gaps of at least 0.5%, rates fell to 43% and 42%, respectively; for gaps of at least 1%, they fell to 28% and 33%. Bearish gaps were somewhat easier to fill, partly reflecting the market’s upward bias.

Gap-trading profitability has declined as computing power, participation, and competition have increased. Strategies that once worked may require more filters, fewer trades, or additional curve-fitting. Simple gap-trading examples tested on five-minute futures data from 2011 through July 2021 were unprofitable, and adding an average-price criterion improved expectancy to 0.06% per trade but remained unprofitable. An overnight swing strategy performed better, producing an average gain of 0.48 per trade and a 1.8 profit factor, while a longer-term SPY test averaged roughly 0.5% per trade with a rising equity curve.

Reliable data is essential for backtesting. The passage cautions that free Yahoo Finance data should be trusted only for opening and closing prices because reported highs and lows may be erroneous. Predicting whether a stock will gap up in advance is considered nearly impossible, though backtesting may improve trading odds. Overall, gap trading remains possible but is described as difficult, especially in popular indices and heavily traded asset classes.

A review of 10 randomized trials involving 77,917 people at high cardiovascular risk found that omega-3 supplements did not reduce deaths from heart disease, nonfatal heart attacks, strokes, or procedures to reopen clogged arteries compared with placebo. Small differences favoring supplements could have been due to chance, and trial variation plus missing smoking and cancer-history data limited the analysis. The findings do not support American Heart Association guidelines recommending supplements for cardiovascular prevention in patients with prior coronary heart disease. Experts noted that supplements are inexpensive and generally safe, advised current users not to stop based solely on these results, and emphasized fatty fish or supplements as part of a balanced diet.

Boscov’s downtown Wilkes-Barre store is booming, posting record sales in 2017 and single-digit growth despite online shopping. Customers cite longtime salespeople, a hometown atmosphere, and proximity. While Bon-Ton and Sears close in Wyoming Valley Mall, Boscov’s supports nearby downtown shops and plans to open its 47th store in Connecticut.

Schools face a need for comprehensive renewal because society changes rapidly, not all change is beneficial, and learners—including Millennials, Generation Z, and Generation Alpha—differ in their goals, motivation, and ways of learning. Education should therefore adopt a learner-centred approach that retains the school’s role in preparing students for life and addresses cognitive, affective, and psychomotor development.

Technological and societal shifts have transformed the world into intertwined physical and cyber environments, expanded intelligence beyond biological forms, and moved learning from traditional face-to-face instruction toward blended formal and non-formal models. Historical waves of technological change have brought “creative destruction,” while the current wave of generative AI follows the digital era and continues the development of artificial intelligence.

Despite rapid AI advances and their effects on economies, politics, culture, and work, educational responses have moved from shock and denial toward acceptance of generative AI’s potential and limitations. The passage calls for a transition from digital pedagogy, where technology is a tool, to generative pedagogy, where GAI becomes a partner in education. This shift leaves unresolved the teacher’s future role, the value of creating educational content, and the purpose of assessment when GAI can recall, determine, and perform many tasks. Preparing for human–AI symbiosis will require a rapid transformation in which educators cease to be sole authorities and increasingly focus on relationships, values, and affective development.

Bayard’s finances received an “unmodified” audit rating, with two minor findings: a $700 deficit in a new federal block grant fund and four mileage reimbursement errors totaling $64. The council unanimously supported Santa Clara’s effort to obtain management of Fort Bayard. Santa Clara representatives said leasing space to the U.S. Forest Service would provide steady revenue and prevent further deterioration, while Councilor Zeke Santa Maria questioned the village’s financial and personnel capacity. Santa Clara also reported increased state interest in its plan but warned delays could allow more buildings to become irreparable. Mayor Pro Tem Chon Fierro additionally reported plans to restore the historic Bayard train depot; the railroad owns the underlying ground, and city officials are working to resolve that issue.

Las Vegas-based nonprofit Horses4Heroes has opened registration for Saturday Ranch Day Camps, Spring Break Camp (March 26–30), and 10 weeks of summer camp beginning May 29. Camps serve children ages 5–13 and include horse activities, farm-animal interactions, park outings, and visits to The Texas, with technology-free programming. Summer camp runs Monday–Friday, 8 a.m.–5 p.m. The organization also offers affordable riding lessons, parties, field trips, workshops, and $5–$10 test rides at its Floyd Lamb at Tule Springs center. Reduced camp rates are available for veterans, military personnel, law enforcement officers, teachers, and nurses; teen volunteers ages 14–17 can earn community-service hours. Proceeds support animal care and scholarships.

A 2018 FTSE Russell survey of 256 financial advisors found high awareness but limited familiarity with smart beta. Among U.S. respondents, 79% were aware of it, but only 35% were very familiar, while 47% cited insufficient knowledge as their main barrier to investing. U.S. and Canadian advisors sought more information before increasing exposure, whereas U.K. advisors expressed concerns about performance and limited track records.

Ric Flair, 68, was hospitalized for routine monitoring, according to representative Melinda Morris Zanoni. She requested prayers and positive energy due to “tough medical issues,” while Mick Foley and Eric Bischoff wished him well.

House Bill 1471, which would double Andrew J. Hill’s pension, was returned without approval because records show the intended beneficiary’s correct name is Alfred J. Hill. The message argues that special pension enactments should be rare because the Pension Bureau is better equipped to assess claims, though any deficiencies in its authority or system should be corrected. Of 232 classified special pension bills, 81 involving insufficient proof were approved on the assumption that the Government could waive full proof. The remainder involved disabilities predating service, service not in the line of duty, post-discharge disabilities, no statutory basis, or no prior Bureau review. Their annual cost was estimated at more than $35,000.

The Wells Fargo Reflect Card is presented as a no-frills option for paying down debt or financing a large purchase. It offers a 0% introductory APR for 21 months on purchases and qualifying balance transfers, followed by a variable APR of 16.99%, 23.49%, or 28.74%, and has no annual fee. A 5% balance-transfer fee applies, with a $5 minimum, and the card charges a 3% foreign-transaction fee. Benefits include up to $600 in cellphone protection for covered theft or damage, subject to a $25 deductible and available twice per year, plus access to My Wells Fargo Deals merchant offers. The card provides no ongoing rewards after the introductory period, making it less suitable for those seeking recurring rewards or travel benefits. Applicants should compare options and note the recommended Good/Excellent credit score range of 670–850, which does not guarantee approval. The review awarded it Motley Fool Money’s Best 0% Intro APR Card of 2025.

Xu Yan said police prevented her from leaving her neighborhood by directing taxi drivers not to take her. Her husband, detained human rights lawyer Yu Wensheng, faces an inciting-subversion charge after calling for constitutional reform and open elections.

Both Mi 8 models feature Snapdragon 845, 6GB RAM, a 6.21-inch AMOLED display, dual-frequency GPS, and dual 12MP rear cameras with a 20MP front camera. The Mi 8 SE uses Snapdragon 710, has a 3,120mAh battery and 12MP/5MP rear cameras, and starts at 1,799 yuan (about $280).

The passage explains defensive fundamentals for the mid-screen offense, a common tactic in which a big screens for a smaller player. Switching can leave the screener posting against a smaller defender, so NBA teams commonly use “Show & Recover,” though tactics vary. Its three phases are showing the ballhandler toward the sideline, recovering to the screener while denying passes, and matching up after the screen. “All Out SOS Disruption” instead traps the ballhandler before the screen, disrupts planned routes, and uses coordinated rotations, closeouts, help positions, and possible baseline or post traps.

ChatGPT is an OpenAI-developed generative AI that can answer questions, summarize information, and produce human-like text and code. For trading, it can help generate technical indicators, strategies, algorithms, sentiment analyses from financial and social-media data, and forecasts based on historical information. Its coding ability can also assist with platform-specific implementations for tools such as TradingView, MT4, MT5, TradeStation, and AmiBroker.

A suggested workflow is to develop a trading idea with ChatGPT, specify the target platform or programming language, generate and compile the code, correct any bugs, and backtest the strategy on historical data. Strategies that appear profitable should first be deployed live with a small amount of capital. ChatGPT cannot determine the most profitable strategy on its own; generated strategies require backtesting and validation against other sources. It also cannot directly automate trading without additional components, although it can help create automated systems.

The article cautions that ChatGPT may produce incorrect results, logical but low-frequency rules, and code containing errors. In one test, it generated a mean-reversion strategy with logical rules but very few trades, and its AmiBroker code required extensive debugging. The authors therefore regard ChatGPT as useful for hints, coding assistance, and strategy development rather than as a dependable stand-alone trading system. They emphasize backtesting, bug checking, independent validation, and continued human judgment.

AI pattern trading uses algorithms to identify recurring patterns in large amounts of market data, potentially enabling faster, more informed decisions. Its stated benefits include speed and adaptability, while its challenges include unpredictable markets and algorithmic biases. The passage also promotes separately developed, backtested trading strategies and educational resources.

The volume documents Shultz’s bureaucratic struggle with the NSC and efforts to gain access to President Reagan while implementing the four-part agenda of NSDD 75. With Jack Matlock as an ally, Shultz promoted continued dialogue with the Soviet Union, including holding his Madrid meeting with Gromyko after the Soviet downing of KAL 007. It covers 1983 flashpoints, including Reagan’s Strategic Defense Initiative, U.S. deployment of INF missiles in Europe, the Soviet “War Scare,” and NATO’s Able Archer exercise. After the Soviet walkout from INF negotiations, the administration developed a framework for restarting arms-control talks. Shultz and Gromyko agreed in January 1985 to hold Nuclear and Space Talks in Geneva covering START, INF, and defense and space issues. The documents trace the roles of State, NSC, Defense, and the CIA and show arms-control talks taking priority. The volume closes by noting that Chernenko’s impending death would bring a younger Soviet leader who would alter U.S.-Soviet relations.

Cell2Text is a multimodal generative framework that converts single-cell RNA-seq profiles into natural-language descriptions of cell identity, tissue origin, disease association, developmental stage, and pathway activity. It uses a frozen, pretrained Geneformer encoder to produce contextualized gene-level embeddings, a lightweight two-layer adapter to project them into a language model’s semantic space, and an instruction-tuned LLM decoder to generate structured descriptions. The study evaluated full fine-tuning of Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct and Gemma3-4B-it, plus LoRA-based fine-tuning of Llama.

The training dataset contains one million cells from CELLxGENE, spanning 7,331 donors, 783 cell types, 347 tissues, and 128 diseases. Descriptions incorporate Cell Ontology definitions and the two most enriched pathways among 34 MSigDB Hallmark pathways; data were split by donor into 80/10/10 training, validation, and test sets.

Cell2Text generated descriptions with high lexical overlap and biomedical semantic fidelity, including BioBERT F1 scores above 93% for fully tuned models. It outperformed Geneformer classification-head and LightGBM baselines on cell type, tissue, and disease prediction; Gemma3-4B achieved 77.83% cell-type and 73.04% tissue accuracy, while fully tuned Llama reached 77.84% disease accuracy. A Cell Ontology Personalized PageRank metric showed that fully tuned models achieved the highest similarity scores, with Gemma3-4B reaching 85.62%, indicating that errors often involved biologically related cell types. On pathway classification, Cell2Text surpassed the Geneformer-head baseline but generally trailed the pathway-specialized LightGBM ensemble.

Reports indicate Nintendo may end production of the NES Classic Mini, with final shipments expected in April or May. A Nordic retailer says its supply will run out, but it remains unclear whether the change applies only to Norway or worldwide. Earlier promises to increase production conflict with these reports.

A randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled study examined whether intranasal or oral oxytocin (24 IU) selectively enhances responses to CT-fiber–targeted gentle stroking versus non-CT–targeted medium-pressure massage. Of 180 healthy Chinese participants, 171 were analyzed. Pleasantness, arousal, intensity, willingness to pay, plasma oxytocin, skin conductance, heart-rate variability, and cortical oxyhemoglobin responses were measured.

Both oxytocin routes increased pleasantness ratings and prolonged orbitofrontal cortex and posterior superior temporal sulcus responses to gentle stroking, but not medium-pressure massage. They did not affect arousal, intensity, willingness to pay, or peripheral physiological responses. Intranasal administration produced a larger initial plasma oxytocin increase than oral administration, but their behavioral and neural effects were similar. Neural time courses distinguished each oxytocin group from placebo at 64–70% accuracy but did not distinguish the two routes. Post-treatment plasma oxytocin changes significantly mediated the increased pleasantness of gentle stroking, supporting a peripheral-mediated mechanism. Limitations included fNIRS’s superficial cortical coverage, the unnatural laboratory massage procedure, unmeasured applied pressure, and infrequent blood sampling.

The address reports abundant harvests, flourishing commerce, federal revenues above expectations, and preserved peace with foreign nations, attributing these blessings to Providence. Negotiations with Great Britain opened to renew and broaden the commercial convention; envoys in London and Paris received instructions, and the existing convention would continue for at least eight years.

Relations with Spain remained unsettled. Although Spain had ratified the 1802 convention covering some spoliation claims, other claims, boundaries, and long-delayed indemnity were unresolved. Spanish authority in Florida had largely collapsed, enabling adventurers, fugitives, and Indigenous groups to form combinations that violated U.S. laws, encouraged the Seminole War, and threatened lawful commerce. U.S. forces suppressed the adventurers’ occupation of Amelia Island. After Major-General Jackson entered Florida in pursuit of Seminoles, evidence showed Spanish officers had encouraged the war and supplied support. The United States occupied St. Marks and Pensacola to deny hostile forces protection, but ordered St. Marks restored and Pensacola surrendered to an authorized representative. Related instructions, correspondence, and court-martial proceedings were to be presented to Congress. The address argued that Spain could not defer indemnity while allowing its territory to be used against U.S. citizens and asserted the right of self-defense.

The civil conflict between Spain and its South American provinces continued. Buenos Aires, Chile, and Venezuela had declared independence, while several other regions were independent or unconnected with Buenos Aires; Spain still possessed or influenced much of the remainder. Allied powers undertook to mediate through a congress but were expected to refrain from force. The United States judged its existing policy toward the conflict appropriate and maintained friendly relations with France, Russia, and other powers.

Treasury receipts exceeded $17 million in the first three quarters, with more than $2 million expected on January 1 after meeting appropriations and extinguishing old 6% stock and half the Louisiana debt. Customs revenue reached $21 million and was estimated at at least $26 million for the year, while public-land sales exceeded those of previous years. Strict enforcement of revenue laws was credited with aiding domestic manufactures, though further protection was submitted to Congress.

Defense preparations included frontier surveys, fortifications, and selection of sites for two naval depots. Treaties with several Indigenous nations secured extensive territorial cessions, negotiations continued with others, and strong posts were established near Yellow Stone River, the Mandan village, and St. Peters. The address argued that independent Indigenous communities could not persist within settled territory and advocated U.S. control, land acquisition, and cultivation to replace communal hunting ways and promote civilization. Naval forces were maintained in the Mediterranean, Gulf of Mexico, southern coast, and Pacific to preserve relations with the Barbary Powers and protect commerce.

Illinois’s accession was welcomed as advancing the constitutional federal model, strengthening state confidence, reducing state jealousy of the national government, increasing agricultural production and navigation, and binding distant regions together. Congress was also urged to consider the District of Columbia’s growing population and business, which could interfere with national deliberations, while respecting constitutional limits on local legislation. The address concluded by directing gratitude for the country’s blessings to the Divine Author of All Good.
Bandai Namco announced Super Robot Wars X for PS4 and PS Vita, launching March 29, 2018, in Japan and April 26 in Southeast Asia with English subtitles.

The disclosure describes a smart gateway platform for industrial automation and industrial Internet of Things applications. It stores model templates associated with business objectives such as reducing machine downtime or failures, increasing product output, optimizing energy efficiency, minimizing emissions, and improving product quality. Through a user interface, users select a template and map its generic data inputs to standard or smart data tags on industrial devices. Templates encode domain expertise by defining relevant inputs, correlations, causalities, and, in some cases, suitable analytics.

The gateway collects mapped data from controllers, sensors, motor drives, quality and safety systems, historians, and other sources. Its modeling component normalizes and contextualizes the data, adds metadata and AI fields describing relationships and analytic problems, synchronizes and time-stamps related values, organizes data by enterprise and asset hierarchies, derives values when required, and can generate alarms or events. Smart tags may represent states, rates, odometers, and events.

Structured and contextualized data can be sent to analytics systems on the gateway, edge devices, enterprise systems, or cloud platforms for AI, machine-learning, or statistical analysis. These systems may produce dashboards, recommendations, predictions, notifications, and actionable insights, or issue coordinated control outputs to industrial devices. By restricting analysis to objective-relevant data and encoding known relationships, the platform is presented as reducing storage and processing requirements, accelerating insight generation, and limiting spurious or irrelevant correlations compared with conventional unconstrained big-data analysis.

A multidisciplinary team led by University of Texas at Austin researchers reported in *Nature* that built and proposed Amazon hydroelectric dams could trap nutrient-rich sediment, alter river systems and climate, and harm biodiversity. Of 428 proposed dams, 140 are built or under construction. The researchers created the Dam Environmental Vulnerability Index, which scores vulnerability to land-use change, erosion, pollution, sediment trapping and river-system changes. The Marañón and Ucayali rivers scored 72 and 61, while the Madeira exceeded 80 and experienced a 20% sediment-concentration decline after two dams. Another 25 upstream Madeira dams could increase sediment trapping. In the Tapajós basin, 28 tributary dams, 90 proposed dams and continued deforestation could impound the river and its tributaries. Researchers warned that cumulative dam effects could alter Atlantic sediment flows and disrupt rainfall and storm patterns from the Amazon to the Gulf of Mexico.

The passage describes novel cationic amino lipids of Formula (I), including specified salts, tautomers, stereoisomers, prodrugs, and isotopically labeled variants, for forming lipid nanoparticles. These nanoparticles may contain therapeutic nucleic acids and neutral or charged lipids, cholesterol or other steroids, and polymer-conjugated lipids such as PEG-lipids. They are intended to protect nucleic acids from serum or nuclease degradation, facilitate cellular uptake and intracellular delivery, support systemic or local administration, improve tolerability, and increase therapeutic index. The disclosed nucleic acids include mRNA, antisense oligonucleotides, siRNA, miRNA inhibitors, plasmids, and related oligonucleotides, which can increase protein expression, inhibit miRNA activity, or silence target genes and proteins. The passage also discusses mRNA preparation through in vitro transcription, purification to remove immunostimulatory contaminants, 5′ capping, polyadenylation, modified nucleosides, and optimized untranslated regions to improve stability and translation. Pharmaceutical compositions, lipid-nanoparticle formulations, administration methods, medicament uses, dosage forms, and routes of administration are described. Lipid nanoparticles are generally reported to range from about 30 to 150 nm in diameter. Figures present mouse-liver luciferase expression, MC3 pKa calculations, and comparative luciferase activity for different lipids.

Uncertain and inconsistent environment maps can cause deterministic motion planners to produce abrupt trajectory changes and oscillations around obstacles. The paper proposes extending the Kinodynamic Efficiently Adaptive State Lattice (KEASL) search to compute edge costs from multiple temporally sampled world-map hypotheses. The most recent map remains the primary hypothesis, which must contain no collisions in the final solution, while earlier maps guide search around inconsistent regions.

Four approaches are developed. Valid in Every Hypothesis (VEH) permits an edge only when it is collision-free in every hypothesis, ensuring safety but producing overly conservative paths. Per-Edge Hypothesis (PEH) reroutes invalid edges for each hypothesis and averages their costs, but its computational expense proved impractical for field use. Goal-Edge Hypothesis (GEH) defers rerouting until search reaches the goal, improving efficiency but concentrating expansions near the goal and limiting effectiveness for long-range planning. Goal-Edge Graph Revision Hypothesis (GEGRH) adds graph revision that redirects expansion toward hypothesis divergence points, producing more effective search.

Experiments used 221 planning problems derived from UGV field-test data, testing two and three successive maps with ARA*, a one-second time limit, and an initial heuristic inflation factor of 2.0. For two hypotheses, GEGRH averaged 0.22 seconds of planning and 36.00 seconds of path duration, compared with VEH’s 0.26 and 38.56 seconds. With three hypotheses, GEGRH averaged 0.29 and 36.47 seconds, versus VEH’s 0.41 and 44.87 seconds. Relative to VEH, GEGRH reduced planning time by 15.4% and 29.27%, and path duration by 6.64% and 18.72%, respectively. Single-hypothesis planning was faster at 0.12 seconds but averaged 33.55 seconds of path duration. Case studies showed GEGRH producing a more direct route in one problem, while VEH performed better in another because GEGRH’s rerouting search yielded a suboptimal solution within the time limit.

Future work includes incorporating more hypotheses, representing non-binary divergences such as terrain height or semantics, testing alternative rerouting cost functions, and weighting costs using hypothesis certainty.

Microsoft Corporation’s Form 10-Q for the quarter ended December 31, 2019 reported fiscal Q2 2020 revenue of $36.91 billion, up 14%; gross margin of $24.55 billion, up 22%; operating income of $13.89 billion, up 35%; net income of $11.65 billion, up 38%; and diluted EPS of $1.51, up 40%. For the first six months, revenue rose 14% to $69.96 billion and net income rose 29% to $22.33 billion. Commercial cloud revenue increased 39% to $12.5 billion, including 62% Azure growth. Office 365 Commercial grew 27%, LinkedIn revenue 24%, Dynamics revenue 12%, server products and cloud services 30%, and Windows Commercial 25%, while Xbox content and services declined 11%. All three segments—Productivity and Business Processes, Intelligent Cloud, and More Personal Computing—reported revenue and operating-income growth.

At December 31, 2019, Microsoft held $8.86 billion in cash, $125.39 billion in short-term investments, and $110.11 billion in stockholders’ equity. Six-month operating cash flow was $24.50 billion; cash used in investing was $7.81 billion and in financing was $19.12 billion. The company had $69.61 billion of debt and $93 billion of remaining performance obligations, including $90 billion from commercial customers.

The filing covers accounting policies, investments, derivatives, debt, taxes, leases, contingencies, share repurchases, dividends, and segment information. It also reports that $2.8 billion remained under the 2016 repurchase authorization and describes material litigation and potential tax audits. Deloitte reviewed the unaudited interim information and reported that no material modifications were needed for GAAP compliance.
A 29-year-old Essex man faced impaired-driving and over-80-mg-BAC charges after hitting a gas meter and was due in Windsor court June 13.

President Donald Trump condemned white supremacists, neo-Nazis and other extremist groups as “repugnant” after the Charlottesville attacks, calling violence committed in the name of bigotry a strike on America’s core values. His statement followed criticism over his initial “many sides” remark and nearly 48 hours of silence. Trump also returned to the White House and signed a trade memo. He criticized Merck CEO Ken Frazier after Frazier resigned from his manufacturing council over his failure to condemn white supremacists, tweeting that Frazier could now focus on lowering drug prices.

The Yankees enter the offseason after a 2025 playoff elimination by Toronto, with roster changes and trade activity anticipated for 2026. A predicted lineup has Steven Kwan as leadoff hitter and Josh Naylor at first base, suggesting Trent Grisham and Paul Goldschmidt may not return.

Matthew Lane, a 19-year-old college freshman from Sterling, Massachusetts, pleaded guilty in June to hacking education technology company PowerSchool and is scheduled to be sentenced in federal court. Prosecutors accused him of collaborating with at least one unnamed co-conspirator to steal records of more than 60 million students and 10 million educators and to extort roughly $3 million in Bitcoin, threatening to leak the data "worldwide" and destroy the company otherwise. The attack, which prosecutors call the largest exposure of private student data in history, cost PowerSchool more than $14 million, including the ransom and identity theft services. Lane reportedly told his girlfriend he was "gonna be on the laptop" because "I just need to actually make $ for a second," and he used a server leased in Ukraine. He returned about $160,000 to the government, while roughly $3 million remains unaccounted for; prosecutors say he intended to buy designer clothes, diamond jewelry and luxury vehicles. He is charged with computer fraud and aggravated identity theft, and prosecutors seek seven years in prison and more than $14 million in restitution. His sentencing report describes his conduct as "sophisticated" — involving VPNs, eSIMs, anonymized contact details, stolen credentials and foreign servers — and as part of a pattern dating to at least 2021 with at least eight victims, including an athletic association, private companies and foreign governments.

Threat intelligence research by Cyble, provided exclusively to The 74, connected digital aliases such as "g0re," "netsaosa" and "fuckmarykill" to Lane, describing him as a "seasoned cybercriminal" whose PowerSchool attack was "a predictable escalation rather than an isolated incident." Cyble said the accounts systematically targeted educational institutions, government agencies and corporate networks since 2021, affecting an alcoholic beverage company, a major U.S. supermarket chain, an Indonesian telecommunications company and the Colombian armed forces. Prosecutors said Lane and an Illinois-based co-conspirator first extorted $200,000 from a U.S. wireless telecommunications company, then discussed needing "to hack another shitty company that'll pay." The two allegedly used anonymized email with victims, Signal between themselves, cryptocurrency wallets, anonymous virtual credit cards, masks and gloves at ATMs, and money mules. Medhe of Cyble said the evidence shows Lane "wasn't acting alone" and predicted a co-conspirator indictment, while finding no evidence ShinyHunters, a cybercrime group that took credit for the attack, was involved.

After searching his college dorm, Lane initially "fabricated a story about receiving packages of cash," denied extortion and admitted only when confronted with text messages. PowerSchool, acquired by Bain Capital for $5.6 billion, serves more than 18,000 institutions globally and 90 of the 100 largest U.S. school districts; it initially denied being a ransomware victim before disclosing it paid an extortion demand. Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton sued the vendor in September, and districts in several states later received secondary ransom demands, raising questions about a "loosely knit band of primarily English-speaking miscreants." Researchers also cited the risk of "secondary victimization," in which stolen records are repeatedly re-exploited.

Locally, Lane was little known despite his notoriety; neighbors and former classmates described him as quiet, introverted, a skilled programmer and video gamer who sold nicotine vapes in high school and took Advanced Placement computer science courses he found "just really easy." One classmate said his preoccupations included his online reputation. In Sterling, a middle-class town of fewer than 8,000 residents, neighbors said they were thankful he wasn't arrested for dealing drugs, and the FBI raided his family's home this spring. A professor said Lane was "very quiet" in class and emailed to explain his absence and that law enforcement had confiscated his devices; Assumption University, a small Catholic college of about 1,600 undergraduates, did not comment. His sentencing report notes he attended on a partial scholarship, hoped internships would cover student debt and aspired to work for Google.

Leaked 2023 user logs show Lane's earliest BreachForums account was created with a VPN, and its last recorded activity traced to the IP address of the Lane household — evidence, Cyble wrote, of "operational security degradation over time" that may have contributed to his capture. Experts quoted in the passage described pathways into cybercrime through gaming communities and forums where reputation and social connections drive escalation to "the very technically skilled cybercriminal," noting that denial-of-service attacks can now be bought online, and citing research linking youth cyber-offending to peers who shoplifted, used drugs or played computer games, alongside factors such as poverty, trauma and school exclusion.

Gartner researchers Stephen Kleynhans and Michael Silver argue that Microsoft is making Windows 10 Pro unsuitable for enterprises by reducing support and separating it further from Enterprise. Pro users receive only the standard 18 months of security and bug-fix support, while Enterprise and Education qualify for six-month extensions and paid supplemental servicing. Microsoft’s extension policy excluded Pro, which Kleynhans said signaled its “dead-ending” for business use. As Pro becomes more prosumer- and small-business-oriented, Gartner recommends current Pro customers monitor Microsoft’s lifecycle announcements and budget for Windows 10 Enterprise.

Stock futures were little changed after the S&P 500 ended a seven-day winning streak. Ray Dalio compared current conditions to the early 1970s and recommended allocating up to 15% of a portfolio to gold, calling it a diversifier and hedge against monetary debasement and geopolitical uncertainty. Gold reached an all-time high above $4,000 an ounce and gained more than 50% this year amid fiscal deficits and global tensions. Dalio argued that debt instruments are weak stores of wealth amid heavy debt issuance and that gold requires no outside party to make payments. His recommendation contrasts with typical 60-40 stock-and-bond portfolios and low-single-digit allocations to alternative assets.
John Howendobler is in custody after GFPD responded to his report that he choked his wife. The unidentified wife said he woke from sleep and suddenly began choking her.

Seeking Alpha published a slide deck in conjunction with Veeco Instruments Inc. (VECO) and Axcelis Technologies’ M&A call. It includes Seeking Alpha’s transcript-team profile, several article headlines, and a chart with a time axis covering September 29 to October 3, 2025, and a value axis ranging from 29.855 to 33.71.

South Sudan’s only mental health facility was described as prison-like and underfunded, with patients sedated, untreated, or lacking basic care. Internally displaced people were severely traumatized by conflict and displacement, yet donors largely ignored mental health until violence drew international attention. Worldwide, one in four people experience mental health disorders, with poorer and conflict-affected countries facing severe shortages of psychiatrists, inadequate funding, institutional care, and stigma. Untreated disorders are linked to substance abuse, cardiovascular disease, diabetes, and obesity, placing additional strain on fragile health systems. The passage calls for greater funding and training, community-based care, prevention and outreach, and efforts to reduce stigma, treating mental health as a human right and a development priority rather than waiting for crisis.

Apple Inc. filed a Form 10-Q for its fiscal first quarter ended December 29, 2018. The company is a large accelerated filer, had filed all required reports, submitted required interactive data files electronically, and was not a shell company. It had 4.715 billion common shares outstanding as of January 18, 2019.

Net sales declined 5% to $84.310 billion from $88.293 billion, primarily because of lower iPhone sales, partially offset by growth in Wearables, Home and Accessories and Services. Product sales were $73.435 billion and Services sales were $10.875 billion. Gross margin fell to $32.031 billion, or 38.0%, from $33.912 billion, or 38.4%. Operating expenses increased to $8.685 billion from $7.638 billion, resulting in operating income of $23.346 billion versus $26.274 billion. Net income was $19.965 billion versus $20.065 billion, while diluted earnings per share increased to $4.18 from $3.89.

By category, iPhone sales fell 15% to $51.982 billion; Mac sales rose 9% to $7.416 billion; iPad sales rose 17% to $6.729 billion; Wearables, Home and Accessories sales rose 33% to $7.308 billion; and Services sales rose 19% to $10.875 billion. Lower iPhone unit sales were reported across all geographic segments. Mac growth was attributed primarily to MacBook Air, iPad growth to iPad Pro, Wearables growth to Apple Watch and AirPods, and Services growth to licensing, the App Store and AppleCare.

Americas net sales increased 5% to $36.940 billion; Europe declined 3% to $20.363 billion; Greater China fell 27% to $13.169 billion; Japan declined 5% to $6.910 billion; and Rest of Asia Pacific rose 1% to $6.928 billion. Foreign-currency weakness adversely affected reported sales.

Product gross margin declined to 34.3% from 36.1%, while Services gross margin increased to 62.8% from 58.3%. Apple anticipated a total gross-margin percentage of 37% to 38% in the second quarter of fiscal 2019 and identified pricing pressure, competition, component and manufacturing costs, product mix, exchange rates, warranty costs and product-transition expenses as possible sources of volatility and pressure.

Research and development expense increased to $3.902 billion from $3.407 billion, principally due to headcount and infrastructure costs. Selling, general and administrative expense rose to $4.783 billion from $4.231 billion, primarily because of professional fees and headcount costs. Other income declined to $560 million from $756 million, reflecting higher interest expense, lower interest income and lower investment-related gains. The effective tax rate fell to 16.5% from 25.8%.

Cash and cash equivalents increased to $44.771 billion from $25.913 billion at September 29, 2018. Total assets were $373.719 billion, total liabilities were $255.827 billion, and shareholders’ equity was $117.892 billion. Operating activities generated $26.690 billion of cash. Apple repurchased 38.0 million shares for $8.2 billion and paid $3.568 billion in dividends and dividend equivalents during the quarter. Its $100 billion repurchase authorization had used $37.3 billion by quarter-end.

Apple adopted the new revenue standard using the full retrospective method; prior-period sales were not restated because the impact was not material. Deferred value amortization for bundled Maps, Siri and free iCloud services was reclassified from Products to Services, and prior-quarter product and service figures were conformed accordingly. Adoption of the financial-instruments standard had no material impact. Adoption of the intra-entity asset-transfer tax standard resulted in $2.7 billion of net deferred tax assets, a $128 million reduction in other non-current assets and a $2.6 billion increase in retained earnings. Deferred revenue totaled $8.4 billion, with 66% expected to be realized within one year. Apple planned to adopt the expanded hedging, credit-loss and lease standards in fiscal 2020 or 2021 as specified.

Cash and marketable securities totaled $245.035 billion, including $19.9 billion restricted from general use. Apple held $12.0 billion of commercial paper and $103.8 billion principal amount of term debt. The fair value of its marketable debt securities was $180.342 billion in an unrealized-loss position, but management did not consider them other-than-temporarily impaired. Apple used derivatives to manage foreign-currency and interest-rate exposure.

The company recognized $14.7 billion of gross unrecognized tax benefits, including $8.2 billion that could affect its effective tax rate, and had accrued $1.2 billion of interest and penalties. The European Commission’s State Aid Decision required recovery of €13.1 billion plus €1.2 billion of interest; Apple and Ireland had appealed, and the full amount was funded into escrow pending resolution.

Ending warranty accruals were $3.819 billion, future minimum operating-lease payments totaled $9.9 billion, and noncancelable unconditional purchase obligations exceeding one year totaled $7.4 billion. Outstanding RSUs were 101.3 million, and unrecognized share-based compensation was $14.0 billion, expected to be recognized over an average 2.9 years.

Material contingencies included VirnetX patent litigation, Qualcomm royalty and patent litigation, and cases concerning iPhone performance-management features. Sales of certain iPhone models were enjoined in China and Germany, and Apple complied with the orders while pursuing appeals. Apple had accrued its estimate for the Qualcomm and performance-management matters.

Apple identified supply-chain risks from limited-source components, commodity-price volatility, concentrated outsourced manufacturing and manufacturing obligations generally covering up to 150 days. It introduced iPhone X R, two iPad Pro versions with Apple Pencil and Smart Keyboard Folio, a new MacBook Air and a new Mac mini during the quarter.

President Donald Trump announced an agreement with AstraZeneca to offer discounted prescription drugs through TrumpRx.com under a “most-favored-nation” policy, with Americans paying the lowest prices available globally. AstraZeneca also pledged $50 billion in U.S. investment over five years for drug research and onshore manufacturing, plus comparable lowest-country pricing for Medicaid patients. The deal follows a similar arrangement with Pfizer.

Say It With Diamonds, founded by Charlotte Donoghue and Steph Porter in 2016, has opened its first Liverpool city-centre store at Cavern Walks. The Instagram business grew from five necklaces and now offers engagement, wedding and other jewellery at affordable prices. Its celebrity clients include Nicola Carragher and Georgia Toffolo, and the founders aim to become Liverpool’s premier jewellery store.

Shriram Transport Finance said its promoters are seeking timely SVL repayment after repayment concerns drove its shares down 11.83%. It had guaranteed Rs 870 crore of SVL debentures maturing in June 2019 and warned it would use alternative mechanisms if payment failed.

The disclosure describes methods, slurry chemistries, coatings, structural features, and tooling for manufacturing vacuum-molded fiber containers and packaging as alternatives to single-use plastics. Molded fiber is presented as biodegradable, compostable, and less harmful to oceans than plastic, but existing fiber products have lacked the moisture, oil, vapor, strength, and structural characteristics needed for food and beverage packaging.

In the disclosed process, a wire mesh covers a mold shaped as the inverse of the desired product. The mesh is immersed in a pulp-and-water slurry, and a vacuum draws fibers onto it while excess slurry is evacuated. Wet curing transfers the formed part to a heated press for compression and drying, while dry curing uses heated air. A closed-loop system recirculates unused slurry, monitors its chemical composition, and replenishes absorbed additives to maintain predetermined concentrations. Fiber refining and mechanical grinding improve drainage, bonding, tensile strength, and burst strength.

Possible fiber bases include softwood, bagasse, bamboo, old corrugated containers, and newsprint. Chemical additives can provide moisture resistance, oil resistance, vapor barriers, strength, retention, and color. Alkyl ketene dimer is used as a moisture barrier; cationic starches, polyamines, polyamide-epichlorohydrin resins, and inorganic salts are identified as strength or retention aids; and water-based fluorine-containing emulsions are described as oil barriers.

Produce containers may incorporate rolled edges, skirts, bowed sidewalls, shelves, and bottom or sidewall ribs to increase hoop strength and rigidity. Moisture-barrier chemistry or topical coatings can help preserve that strength while contents release moisture. Modified rinsing tools use redirected spray nozzles to remove more pulp around vent-hole inserts, producing extended vent holes without changing existing molds or inserts.

Microwavable and oven-compatible containers use embedded or topical moisture, oil, and vapor barriers. Porosity and condensation can be reduced through fiber refining and coatings containing water-based long-chain fluorine-containing polymers. The containers may have multiple compartments, and their chemistry may also include strengthening and retention additives.

Meat trays use chemistry similar to microwavable containers, with particular emphasis on a moisture barrier, an optional oil barrier, and dry-strength additives. Ribs and shelves can provide additional structural rigidity and preserve it over extended storage.

Fiber-based beverage lids may include an inclined liquid-guid platform, retaining wall, sip hole, venting aperture, crown, and snap-fitting lock ring. Their slurries include moisture barriers and strength or polycationic additives. A retractable, pneumatically actuated piston in the mold forcibly expands and releases a lid having zero or negative draft, overcoming the locking problem created by the lid’s snap ring.

Additional embodiments include ribbed utility containers and a shipping kit for a flat-screen television containing a top cover, screen protector, four corrugated-pulp corner pieces, a nesting bottom tray, and a pallet strap. The disclosed chemistries, geometries, and processes may also be adapted to numerous food, agricultural, medical, industrial, and protective applications, including 3D-printing-based fiber manufacturing.

Microsoft Corporation’s Form 10-Q for the quarter ended March 31, 2021 reported quarterly revenue of $41.706 billion, compared with $35.021 billion a year earlier. Gross margin was $28.661 billion, operating income was $17.048 billion, net income was $15.457 billion, and diluted earnings per share were $2.03, versus $24.046 billion, $12.975 billion, $10.752 billion, and $1.40, respectively, in the prior-year quarter. For the first nine months, revenue was $121.936 billion and net income was $44.813 billion, compared with $104.982 billion and $33.079 billion. Commercial cloud revenue increased 33% to $17.7 billion. The three reportable segments—Productivity and Business Processes, Intelligent Cloud, and More Personal Computing—generated quarterly revenue of $13.552 billion, $15.118 billion, and $13.036 billion, respectively.

At March 31, 2021, Microsoft reported $13.702 billion of cash and cash equivalents, $111.705 billion of short-term investments, $308.879 billion of total assets, $174.374 billion of liabilities, and $134.505 billion of stockholders’ equity. Nine-month operating cash flow was $54.030 billion, capital expenditures were $14.170 billion, common-stock repurchases totaled $20.208 billion, and dividends paid totaled $12.307 billion.

Microsoft completed its $8.1 billion ZeniMax acquisition on March 9, 2021, recognizing $5.554 billion of goodwill and $1.947 billion of intangible assets. On April 11, it entered into a definitive agreement to acquire Nuance Communications for $19.7 billion. The notes addressed investments, derivatives, debt, taxes, leases, unearned revenue, and contingencies. Increased useful lives for server and network equipment raised nine-month operating income by $2.3 billion and net income by $1.9 billion. A $620 million India withholding-tax benefit reduced the effective tax rate, while remaining performance obligations totaled $121 billion, approximately half of which was expected to be recognized within 12 months. Deloitte’s review identified no material modifications needed to the unaudited interim financial information.

Co-operative Group wrote off its 20% stake in Co-operative Bank at nil, a £132 million charge that left it with a pretax loss despite operating profit rising 32% to £148 million. It was the third consecutive write-down of the holding. Growth came from supermarkets, funeral services and insurance, with like-for-like supermarket sales up 3.5%. Co-op increased British sourcing to meet demand for local food. It has no role in the bank’s sale but hopes a buyer will be found; most bidders reportedly seek specific assets.

Spartan Race Inc., founded in Boston in 2010, grew into a leading obstacle course race organizer, claiming one million participants at roughly 130 events across more than 25 countries in 2016. Its races range from three to more than 26 miles and emphasize timed competition, individual athleticism, and penalties for failed obstacles. Spartan also expanded beyond racing through merchandise, sponsorships, television exposure, a Reebok partnership, and fitness training programs.

As CEO Joe De Sena considered an initial public offering in 2017, he and Spartan’s financial executives examined how a new revenue recognition standard would affect the company’s financial statements. The standard requires five steps: determine whether a contract exists, identify performance obligations, determine the transaction price, allocate that price among multiple obligations when applicable, and recognize revenue when the obligations are satisfied.

Spartan’s revenue sources included walk-up and advance race entries, annual passes, merchandise, sponsorships, SGX training certification, and international races operated by licensees. These arrangements involve varying prices, refund and transfer policies, variable payments, multiyear licensing contracts, and both cash and in-kind consideration. Under the standard, contracts require committed exchange terms, commercial substance, and probable collection. Spartan must assess whether sales contain distinct or bundled performance obligations, estimate discounts, rebates, refunds, and delayed-payment effects, allocate variable amounts appropriately, and recognize revenue when customers control goods or services are completed.

MotoGP heads to Austin’s Circuit of the Americas after Argentina, where championship leader Maverick Viñales won while Marc Márquez fell from a near two-second lead. Márquez, COTA’s only star performer with four wins, hopes to continue his success there. Friday’s FP1 begins at 9:55 GMT-5; Sunday’s race starts at 14:00.

Maryland coach D.J. Durkin praised his receivers, offensive line and running backs. With Mike Weber healthy, Meyer is developing plays featuring Weber and freshman J.K. Dobbins together. Maryland converted 9 of 16 third downs, versus Minnesota’s 5 of 12. Ohio State’s Chris Worley is probable, Dre’Mont Jones and Erick Smith are out, and Antonio Williams is questionable.

The South Dakota Department of Agriculture is asking producers who suspect dicamba-related crop damage this year to complete a Dicamba Damage Survey, available at apps.sd.gov/doa/cat/dicamba.aspx and linked from the department's website, www.sdda.sd.gov. Three dicamba products are registered for use on dicamba-tolerant soybeans in the state: Engenia, FeXapan and Xtendimax. Survey information will be used to evaluate the products' impacts statewide. Agriculture Secretary Mike Jaspers urged producers to submit the survey so the department has as much information as possible. Producers can also complete the survey at the department's booth (No. 3107 in the Ag Tents) during Dakotafest in Mitchell, S.D., Aug. 15–17.

The speech frames the transfer of power as a return of authority to the American people and a national effort to rebuild the country. It criticizes Washington for benefiting insiders while workers, families, factories, and the middle class suffered, and calls for action against poverty, inadequate education, crime, drugs, and declining domestic manufacturing. It promises an “America First” strategy focused on American workers in trade, taxes, immigration, and foreign affairs; border protection; restoring jobs, wealth, and infrastructure; and “Buy American” and “Hire American.”

The speaker seeks international friendship while defending national interests, alliances, and the defeat of “Radical Islamic Terrorism.” Emphasizing unity, patriotism, open debate, solidarity, and protection through the military, law enforcement, and God, the speech rejects political inaction and calls for ambitious action. It connects national renewal with space exploration, medicine, technology, and shared American identity, assuring citizens that their voices and dreams will shape the country’s destiny and that America will become strong, wealthy, proud, safe, and great again.

NVIDIA Corporation’s Form 10-Q for the quarter ended October 29, 2017 reported third-quarter revenue of $2.636 billion, up 32% year over year, gross margin of 59.5%, operating income of $895 million, net income of $838 million, and diluted earnings per share of $1.33. For the first nine months, revenue was $6.803 billion, net income was $1.928 billion, and diluted earnings per share were $3.05.

GPU revenue increased 31% to $2.217 billion, driven by gaming, datacenter, and professional visualization products, while Tegra Processor revenue rose 74% to $419 million. Third-quarter revenue included $1.561 billion from gaming, $501 million from datacenter, $239 million from professional visualization, and $144 million from automotive. Growth reflected demand for Pascal-based GeForce products and Volta-based datacenter products, as well as gaming platforms and services and automotive products.

At October 29, 2017, NVIDIA held $2.802 billion in cash and cash equivalents and $3.518 billion in marketable securities, totaling $6.320 billion. Nine-month operating cash flow was $2.144 billion, investing activities provided $1.302 billion, and financing activities used $2.410 billion. The company repurchased $909 million of stock and paid $250 million in dividends during the first nine months, intended to return $1.25 billion to shareholders in each of fiscal 2018 and 2019. The quarterly dividend was increased to $0.15 per share.

NVIDIA reported $24 million of remaining 1.00% convertible senior notes and $1.985 billion of long-term debt. It planned to purchase its Santa Clara campus for approximately $350 million and had inventory purchase obligations of $1.16 billion.

The company faced patent litigation from Polaris Innovations in the United States and Germany, had not recorded accruals for the matters, and stated that possible losses could not be reasonably estimated. It also disclosed adoption or planned adoption of new accounting standards and reported no material changes in investment, interest-rate, or foreign-exchange risks.

Philadelphia City Council will consider amended bills Thursday authorizing a $500 million, seven-year project to renovate up to 200 parks, recreation centers, and libraries. James Hodgkinson, 66, of Belleville, Illinois, is accused of shooting five people during a charity baseball practice in Alexandria, Virginia, including Rep. Steve Scalise, who remained in critical condition after surgery at MedStar Washington; Hodgkinson died in a shootout with police. The passage recommends careful ADS7828 circuit layout because its SAR architecture is sensitive to glitches on power, reference, ground, and digital inputs during each conversion bit window. Transients may come from switching supplies, nearby digital logic, or high-power devices. Power should be clean and bypassed with a 0.1µF ceramic capacitor placed close to the device; a 1µF–10µF capacitor may be needed when the +VDD connection has high impedance. The external reference has no inherent rejection of noise or voltage variation, especially when tied to the supply, and line-frequency ripple can be difficult to filter. GND should connect to a clean analog ground away from microcontroller or digital signal processor grounding points, ideally using a dedicated analog ground plane.

Additional notes address lifecycle status, preproduction-part limitations, RoHS labels, lead finishes, moisture-sensitivity and reflow ratings, and part markings. Packaging drawings specify millimeter dimensions, tolerances, flash limits, and possible IPC-recommended alternatives for layouts, solder masks, and stencils.

This continuation application incorporates by reference prior U.S. and international applications, provisional application 62/737,836, and sequence listings submitted electronically and on compact discs.

DNA methylation regulates gene expression, and aberrant methylation is associated with diseases including cancer. Although whole-genome bisulfite sequencing can identify differentially methylated regions, its cost and low density of informative regions limit deep sequencing to a small fraction of the genome. Further difficulties include small or variable control groups and dependence between methylation states at neighboring CpG sites.

The disclosure provides targeted cancer assay panels, or bait sets, for detecting cancer-specific methylation patterns in cell-free DNA. Methods are also described for identifying differentially methylated genomic regions, designing and synthesizing probes, and using targeted hybridization capture to increase sequencing depth while reducing cost. Panels may contain hundreds to 100,000 or more oligonucleotide probes, including overlapping probe pairs and 2×-tiled designs, targeting regions from Lists 1–8. Probes are complementary to genomic sequences or cytosine-transition variants, may carry affinity moieties such as biotin, and are filtered to limit off-target genomic matches, including through k-mer seeding and local alignment.

Converted cell-free DNA fragments, such as bisulfite- or deaminase-converted fragments in which unmethylated cytosines become uracil, can be captured with the panels and sequenced. The resulting reads can be evaluated to classify the presence or absence of cancer, cancer stage, cancer type, or tissue of origin. Feature vectors can be generated from hypermethylated and hypomethylated fragment counts, CpG-site scores, and fragment rankings, then applied to classifiers trained on cancer and non-cancer samples. Listed models include kernel logistic regression, random forest, mixture, convolutional neural network, and autoencoder models. Disclosed performance ranges include classifier AUC values above 0.70 and specified sensitivities at high specificity for multiple cancer types.

The description further covers methods for treating an identified cancer subject with chemotherapeutic or other anticancer agents. Its drawings depict probe tiling, control-data structures, genomic-region and probe-selection workflows, classifier training, cfDNA sequencing and analysis, genomic annotations, and receiver operating characteristic and confusion matrices for multiple assay panels.

In a mandamus proceeding, petitioner sought to strike from the McAdoo divorce case files a presiding judge’s report concerning the attorney’s irregular handling of the case. The report stated that the attorney bypassed the court’s calendar procedures by having the case heard by an out-of-county judge, but that the irregularity did not affect the interlocutory divorce decree. The Superior Court denied the motion to strike.

The appellate court held that mandamus cannot be used to correct errors of an inferior tribunal and therefore could not collaterally attack the denial based on facts outside the record. It limited review to whether the presiding judge had jurisdiction to file the report. Although the information could support a report to the judges, a contempt proceeding, or attorney discipline, it concerned counsel’s conduct rather than the divorce case. Because the investigation was conducted ex parte, without notice or preliminary proceedings, and the report had no connection to any issue in the divorce action, the court lacked jurisdiction to place it in the case records. A peremptory writ was ordered to strike the report.

The passage is a patent-style description of embodiments for improving packet header processing in Software Defined Networking (SDN) hardware switches. Background notes that SDN separates the control plane from the forwarding plane via an interface such as OpenFlow, which uses a match-action paradigm; conventional hardware switches are inflexible because they process only a fixed set of fields with limited actions, motivating the reconfigurable match table (RMT) architecture.

Described embodiments provide a packet processing pipeline for reconfigurable hardware switches having an ingress pipeline and an egress pipeline, each containing a parser, a match-action unit (MAU), and a deparser. For each packet, the parser separates header data from payload and divides header fields into participating fields, stored in a primary packet header vector (PPHV) sent to the MAU, and non-participating fields, stored in a secondary packet header vector (SPHV) that bypasses the MAU and goes directly to the deparser along with the payload. The deparser reassembles the packet from the MAU's processed PPHV, the parser's SPHV, and the payload, then either enqueues it in the queuing system (ingress) or sends it out of the switch (egress).

The parser is an extractor state machine driven by configuration data from a control-plane compiler and configurator, using a parse graph implemented with TCAM entries; field values such as an EtherType indicate how to extract subsequent headers and whether fields go to PPHV or SPHV. The compiler includes a code receiver (e.g., P4 code), control/table flow graph generator, MAU configuration generator, parse graph generator, and parser configuration generator; fields appearing in any match entry or modified by any action are marked participating. Each MAU stage has a crossbar (Xbar), ternary match tables (TCAM), exact match tables (SRAM hash tables), and a VLIW action engine performing actions such as forwarding, dropping, field modification, and encapsulation. Separating fields is said to avoid wasting MAU resources (e.g., unused TCP header bytes) and to let the parser reach deeper headers such as those in GENEVE or multi-layer tunneling without sending more data to the MAU. The passage also describes implementing the features as software on a generic electronic system and lists accompanying drawings.

The C674x interrupt controller maps up to 128 device events to 12 prioritized interrupts, with events 15–95 selectable from 24 multiplexed events through DSP_INTMUX registers.

The lecture reviews and extends Poisson process theory, emphasizing choosing an appropriate model before writing equations and understanding how related processes connect. A Poisson process can be represented equivalently by iid exponential interarrival times, its arrival epochs, or its counting process \(N(t)\). Exponential waiting times are memoryless, so the remaining wait after any elapsed time is again exponential, regardless of previously observed arrival counts or epochs.

The lecture establishes stationary, independent increments and the Poisson probability mass function \(P(N(t)=n)=e^{-\lambda t}(\lambda t)^n/n!\), and discusses equivalent characterizations of a Poisson process. Specifying marginal distributions of \(N(t)\) alone is insufficient; interval independence is also required. The incremental condition for small \(\delta\) states that zero arrivals have probability \(1-\lambda\delta+o(\delta)\), one arrival has probability \(\lambda\delta+o(\delta)\), and multiple arrivals have probability \(o(\delta)\). Independent Poisson variables add to a Poisson variable with the sum of their rates.

Two independent Poisson processes with rates \(\lambda_1\) and \(\lambda_2\) combine into a Poisson process of rate \(\lambda_1+\lambda_2\). The lecture also suggests that the aggregate of many small independent arrival processes can approximate a Poisson process even when the individual processes are not Poisson, though a rigorous argument requires additional conditions.

Splitting works in the opposite direction: independently assigning each arrival of a rate-\(\lambda\) Poisson process to one of two destinations with probabilities \(p\) and \(1-p\) produces two independent Poisson processes with rates \(\lambda p\) and \(\lambda(1-p)\). Combining and splitting processes repeatedly provides a method for solving many queueing problems. For example, in a last-come, first-served queue with Poisson arrivals at rate \(\lambda\) and exponential services at rate \(\mu\), the probability that a customer is interrupted is \(\lambda/(\lambda+\mu)\), while the probability of completing service is \(\mu/(\lambda+\mu)\). Given an interruption, the probability of no further interruption is \((\mu/(\lambda+\mu))^2\).

For a nonhomogeneous Poisson process with time-varying rate \(\lambda(t)\), the number of arrivals in an interval is Poisson with parameter determined by the average rate over that interval. Counting-process formulas and combining and splitting continue to apply, although interarrival times are no longer exponential. Modulated optical photon streams are given as an application.

Conditional on \(N(t)=n\), the arrival epochs have the same distribution as the order statistics of \(n\) iid uniform random variables on \((0,t)\). Their joint density is \(n!/t^n\) over the ordered region, independent of the original rate \(\lambda\). The factor \(n!\) is explained by symmetry: the cube of possible uniform values is divided equally among the \(n!\) possible orderings. In particular, \(P(S_1>s)=(1-s/t)^n\), and the expected first arrival time is \(t/(n+1)\).

Finally, the lecture discusses an apparent paradox: the mean ordinary interarrival time is \(1/\lambda\), but the interval between the arrivals immediately before and after an arbitrary observation time has a greater expected length. The explanation is that a randomly chosen time is more likely to fall within a long interval than a short one, a length-biasing effect whose fuller treatment is deferred to renewal processes.

E-mini S&P 500 futures are CME Globex-traded derivative contracts that track the S&P 500 index and enable speculation or hedging. Introduced in 1997, they are one-fifth the size of standard S&P 500 futures and are among the most liquid and frequently traded equity-index futures. One contract unit equals the index value multiplied by $50. Contracts are quoted in U.S. dollars and cents per index point, with quarterly March, June, September, and December cycles and additional December listings. They are financially settled using the index’s special opening quotations and normally terminate at 9:30 a.m. ET on the third Friday of the contract month. The minimum price fluctuation is 0.25 index points for outright Globex trading and 0.05 for BTIC, TACO, and calendar spreads, corresponding to $12.50 and $2.50 per tick. The contract has no block-trade eligibility.

Trading occurs Sunday through Friday, generally from 6:00 p.m. to 5:00 p.m. ET, with a daily maintenance break. Trading requires a futures broker, an funded account, and initial margin because the contracts are leveraged. Some brokers also offer CFDs, which track the price difference between opening and closing prices, lack fixed expiration dates, and may track the index rather than the futures contract. Charts are available through TradingView, Yahoo Finance, MultiCharts, and the CME platform.

A futures strategy may use technical and fundamental analysis for market timing, position sizing, risk management, precise entries and exits, hedging, arbitrage, or spreads. The passage describes a paywalled mean-reversion strategy with one buying and one selling variable. Its backtest used daily continuous, back-adjusted CME data from Norgate, traded at the close, ran from contract inception, and included no stops or other risk-management parameters. Seasonal performance was stronger in winter and spring than in summer.

As of November 30, 2022, the futures price was $4,020.25. The reported all-time high was 4,808.25 in January 2022, and the all-time low was 665.75 in March 2009. The primary trading risk is leveraged losses from adverse price movements; with 20x leverage, a 1% adverse move produces a 20% loss and a 5% decline could wipe out the account.
