Poland will invest 20 billion zlotys ($5.5 billion) to link its national fuel pipeline system with NATO’s Central Europe Pipeline System, extending infrastructure by roughly 300 kilometres and adding storage facilities. NATO has committed 60 million zlotys for planning and design, with construction expected to take several years. The connection would integrate Poland with a European pipeline network spanning Belgium, France, Germany, Luxembourg, and the Netherlands, improving supply flexibility and NATO’s ability to obtain fuel during crises. The government describes the project as a major defence and alliance-security investment amid regional tensions and drone activity near NATO’s eastern flank. Officials acknowledge challenges involving cross-border coordination, standards and regulatory compliance, as well as potential cost increases from delays.

The buy-and-hold strategy is a passive investing approach in which investors purchase stocks, ETFs, or funds and hold them for years or decades while ignoring short-term price fluctuations. Investors may sell limited portions when funds are needed. Unlike active trading, it does not attempt to time market highs and lows, and it is consistent with the Efficient Market Hypothesis.

Successful implementation requires research, sound business fundamentals, reasonable purchase prices, and a valid long-term investment thesis. Diversification can reduce risk, while broad-market index funds or ETFs provide an easier, low-cost, passive alternative to selecting individual stocks. Potential benefits include fewer transactions, lower fees, deferred and potentially lower long-term capital-gains taxes, less stress and time commitment, reduced manager risk, and shareholder rights.

The strategy involves substantial risks, including prolonged market declines, company failure, poor stock selection, and missing gains because holdings are not sold at optimal times. Although some investments achieve exceptional returns, very few stocks become long-term success stories, making selection difficult.

Illustrative backtests show that buying and holding SPY produced a 9.7% annual return over 29 years despite significant interim drawdowns. A separate multi-strategy trading portfolio had smoother performance and substantially smaller drawdowns, although commissions and slippage were excluded. The comparison is presented as between fundamentally different approaches: trading requires effort and discipline, while buy and hold is simpler and may better suit most investors.

**Summary**

Malnutrition, particularly undernutrition, wasting, and stunting, is linked to inadequate food intake, increased disease susceptibility, and child death. Globally, 47.0 million children under five were wasted and 144.0 million stunted in 2019, with South Asia highest in both; almost 45% of deaths in children under five in low- to middle-income countries were associated with undernutrition. Pakistan's National Nutrition Survey 2018 reported 40.2% stunting, 17.7% wasting, and 28.9% underweight, with 48.4% of infants exclusively breastfed and 45.8% of mothers initiating breastfeeding early. The study aimed to identify determinants of wasting, stunting, and undernutrition among children under five in southern Punjab, Pakistan, to locate intervention targets.

A multicenter cross-sectional study was conducted at government-run Community Management of Acute Malnutrition centers in four villages of southern Punjab. The calculated sample of 151 was increased to 185; all children (aged 6–59 months, mean 15.36 months) were from the same ethnic/language background and enrolled based on severe wasting (< -3 SD weight-for-height) or stunting (< -2 SD height-for-age), with written parental consent. Parents were interviewed using a pretested structured questionnaire covering sociodemographic characteristics, breastfeeding and complementary feeding, immunization, medical history, and healthcare access. Anthropometry was done by qualified nutrition supervisors with duplicate measurements, using a UNISCALE and length-measuring board, with WHO Child Growth Standards and WHO ANTHRO for classification. Data were analyzed in SPSS 25.0 using independent t-tests and linear regression (p ≤ 0.05). Ethical approval was granted by the Ethical Review and Advanced Study Research Board of the University of Punjab (ref-9/2352-ACAD).

Participants were 56.2% female; 69.2% had family income ≤15,000 PKR and 77.8% had at least two siblings; 54.1% had prior illness episodes, 80.5% had no exclusive breastfeeding, and 89.2% had poor complementary feeding. Wasting was significantly associated with family monthly income and complementary feeding practices; stunting with tuberculosis contact history and exclusive breastfeeding; undernutrition with monthly income and exclusive breastfeeding, in both bivariate and multivariate analyses.

Discussion noted that low income limits food intake, while adequate complementary feeding with breastfeeding up to 24 months supports growth; infections and TB history worsen nutritional status; more siblings, short birth intervals, larger households, and low maternal education increase risk. Limitations include the cross-sectional design. The findings indicate that wasting, stunting, and undernutrition are linked to breastfeeding and complementary feeding practices, household size, family earning, and infection history, requiring concerted societal effort and incorporation of children's dietary needs into child nutrition programs. The study received no external funding, and authors declared no conflicts of interest.

Patterns allow developers to learn from prior experience, communicate through a shared vocabulary, and build reusable, higher-quality components. The passage applies these benefits to distributed-system design and introduces several container-based patterns.

Single-node patterns tightly group containers on one machine, often as Kubernetes pods with shared resources. The **sidecar pattern** pairs an application container with a container that augments it. Examples include adding HTTPS through an nginx proxy, synchronizing dynamic configuration, exposing process and resource usage, and automatically deploying code from Git. Reusable sidecars should be parameterized—preferably through environment variables—provide a stable API, and be documented through Dockerfile directives such as `EXPOSE`, `ENV`, and `LABEL`.

The **ambassador pattern** separates an application’s communication with external services into a companion container. It can route requests to storage shards, discover and broker connections to environment-specific services, or split traffic between production and experimental implementations. A client-side ambassador simplifies the sharded service but adds a container to each application, while a shared routing service reverses those trade-offs.

The **adapter pattern** translates an application’s existing interface into a common interface. It is used to expose metrics in Prometheus’s format, normalize differing log formats with Fluentd, and perform rich health checks against databases such as MySQL without modifying third-party application images. These patterns separate concerns, isolate resource usage, and allow components to be reused across applications.

For multi-node systems, the passage contrasts microservices with monolithic applications. Microservices support focused teams, stable API contracts, independent releases, and component-specific scaling, but make debugging and architecture more difficult. Distributed patterns provide shared designs and reusable lessons that help address those challenges.

A **replicated load-balanced service** consists of identical servers behind a load balancer, providing redundancy and horizontal scaling. Stateless services should have at least two replicas and use readiness probes to distinguish running instances from those ready to accept requests. Session tracking can use IP hashing, application-level tracking such as cookies, or consistent hashing to minimize remapping during scaling. A caching tier can improve request throughput and latency, provide rate limiting, and sit beneath an nginx layer for SSL termination.

A **sharded service** divides requests among shards, with each shard handling only a subset, allowing stateful data and workloads to scale. Sharded caching uses memory more efficiently than replicated caching because keys are not duplicated across replicas. Cache hit rates affect capacity and latency, while shard failures can affect all requests assigned to the failed shard. Replicating each shard improves resilience, permits rolling upgrades, and allows individual shards to scale, at the cost of greater complexity. Client-side ambassadors or shared shard-routing services can distribute requests among shards. Sharding functions commonly use hashing and modulo, requiring deterministic results so requests consistently reach the same shard and uniform distribution so load is spread evenly.

The speaker praises a hockey figure for remaining calm, balancing intensity with humor, and serving as a role model. They emphasize American League experience, consistency, team effort, and players stepping up in the playoffs, while saying the team should keep playing its game.

A Death Cross occurs when a short-term moving average, typically the 50-day, crosses below a long-term moving average, typically the 200-day. It is a lagging signal associated with short-term weakness and often attracts attention as a possible bear-market indicator. S&P 500 backtests since 1960 found lower returns than random periods within 30 days of a signal, but average positive returns broadly in line with long-term market returns after 30 days. A strategy that entered on Death Crosses and exited on Golden Crosses produced only a 0.4% annual return. Buying at Golden Crosses and selling at Death Crosses produced a 7% CAGR, slightly below buy-and-hold, while reducing time in the market and drawdowns. The signal may help with defensive positioning and risk reduction but can cause premature exits and missed bull-market opportunities.

Northern Oil & Gas refinanced its 8.125% unsecured notes due March 2028 with notes due October 2033, making its 3.625% convertible notes due April 2029 its next maturity. Annual interest costs remain roughly unchanged. The article says Northern’s hedges favor a rebound to $70s oil in 2027 over 2026, while the author opines that weak near-term prices improve the odds of $70-plus oil in 2027. The remainder includes promotional material, author disclosures, unrelated headlines, charts, and subscriber testimonials.

Real estate expert Amir Korangy argues not everyone should be a homeowner as millennials and Gen Z seek entry into an expensive housing market. With mortgage rates in the 6% range and home prices 55% higher than at the start of 2020 (Case-Shiller index), renting is often cheaper: it saves more than $900 per month on average and is more affordable than buying in 49 of the 50 largest U.S. metros, with Pittsburgh the sole exception. Korangy notes a buyer with a $3 million budget could rent a $5.5 million–$7 million home for the same monthly cost, while ownership brings hidden expenses such as insurance, repairs, property taxes, HOA fees, and upkeep; insurance costs are rising nationally and are especially high in Florida and California due to extreme weather risks. Home prices are correcting rather than collapsing, and the average homeowner lost roughly $9,200 in equity over the past year (Cotality), weakening the equity-building case for buying. Renting also offers mobility and freedom from market risk.
Plaintiffs failed to prove the contractually required five-day written notice was given, barring recovery. Judgment was reversed for the defendant with $30 costs.

A hockey player says the team must stick to its game, avoid early discouragement, and not let the loud Canadian crowd influence the game. He praised the opposing goalie, saying none of the goals should be faulted as goaltending issues. The players recognize the stakes and rarity of another finals opportunity, with both young and veteran players giving everything. Having performed well in loud hockey towns such as Montreal and Buffalo, the team plans to embrace the passionate atmosphere.

The disclosure describes systems, devices, and methods for automated programming of neuromodulation, particularly sub-perception spinal cord stimulation. It is a continuation of U.S. Patent No. 11,565,114 and claims priority from a provisional application filed September 21, 2015.

An implantable neuromodulation system includes an implantable pulse generator, leads, electrodes, and external programming and control devices. Programmable parameters include electrode activation and polarity, fractionalized current, amplitude, pulse width, frequency, pulse bursts and trains, duty cycle, and stimulation location. Programming may be based on subjective patient feedback, clinician-selected programs or constraints, and automatic data such as activity, heart rate or variability, and field potentials.

A computerized search method evaluates candidate neuromodulation parameter sets and identifies an optimal set for programming a neuromodulator. Disclosed search techniques include sorting algorithms that rank and discard poorly performing programs, gradient descent or ascent methods that optimize a selected parameter dimension, and sensitivity analysis using regression to identify influential stimulation parameters. Other listed techniques include simplex, genetic, and binary searches.

Closed-loop machine-learning systems may cycle through stimulation patterns, collect pain and comfort metrics, and refine patterns or parameter ranges. Metrics can include visual analog and numerical rating scales, satisfaction, activity, global impression of change, quantitative sensory testing, and physiological measures. Search methods may account for wash-in and wash-out periods, test time, evaluation thresholds, user objectives, and spatial search bounds. Patient interfaces allow users to compare, rank, skip, or terminate programs and may obscure programming details to reduce bias.

The disclosure also describes rotating multiple stimulation programs to reduce neurological conditioning and preserve therapeutic efficacy, along with implantable, external, remote, wearable, and cloud-based arrangements for performing and storing optimization data.

The passage specifies SD Memory Card physical-layer behavior for tuning, data transfer, reads, writes, erasing, protection, command extensions, bus operation, error handling, and timeouts.

- CMD19 tuning consists of consecutive tuning executions without intervening commands. A card must complete 40 executions within 150 ms, excluding host processing time.
- Until Card Identification Mode ends, the host remains at fOD frequency; fPP may be used in Data Transfer Mode. CMD9 retrieves the CSD, optional CMD4 configures card driver stages, and CMD7 selects one card for transfer. Data communication is point-to-point between the host and the selected card.
- Read and write transfers can be stopped with CMD12. Write commands must be stopped before CMD7 deselection. Cards may buffer block writes while programming, but CSD writes, write protection, and erase commands do not support buffering. Parameter-set and read commands are prohibited during programming. Disconnecting a card does not terminate erase or programming, while CMD0 or CMD15 does and may destroy card data.
- Data blocks use start and end bits, synchronous payload data, and CRC protection. CMD17 reads one block and CMD18 reads consecutive blocks until CMD12. CMD16 may normally set blocks up to 512 bytes; misalignment causes an address error and aborted transfer. CMD24/25 and other write commands transfer CRC-protected blocks, require a 512-byte CMD16 block length for block writes, discard data after CRC failure, and abort on misalignment or write-protection violations.
- ACMD23 can pre-erase blocks to accelerate a subsequent multiple-block write, while ACMD22 reports the number of successfully written blocks. Erasing requires CMD32, CMD33, and CMD38 in sequence; sequence errors reset the operation, and protected sectors are skipped. DISCARD deallocates selected blocks, whose contents become “don’t care,” and has a 250 ms timeout. FULE logically erases the entire user area and has a one-second timeout. DISCARD and FULE are supported only for SDHC and SDXC cards, not through SPI.
- Write protection can be mechanical, card-internal, or password-based. Password and lock information is stored in nonvolatile PWD/PWD_LEN registers, with optional FEP/FEP_LEN registers for Card Ownership Protection (COP). Locked cards permit basic commands, ACMD41, CMD16, lock commands, CMD11, and CMD40, but not data access. CMD42 is used in Transfer State for setting, replacing, clearing, locking, unlocking, and erasing passwords.
- COP adds FEP management, protected force erase, and restrictions on resetting PWD. When FEP is set, a COP Unlock command is required after reset, Force Erase and PWD clearing are disabled, and FEP Force Erase requires the matching FEP. Force Erase removes user-area data and PWD/PWD_LEN while leaving the secure area intact; the card remains locked during erasure and becomes unlocked afterward. Errors are reported through LOCK_UNLOCK_FAILED and CARD_IS_LOCKED status.
- APP_CMD causes the next command to be interpreted as an application-specific command. Defined ACMDs use the APP_CMD status indication; undefined ACMDs are treated as regular commands, while illegal commands produce an Illegal Command error. CMD6 switches among function groups covering access mode, command-system extensions, driver strength, and power limits. Mode 0 checks supported and current functions and power use; Mode 1 changes functions. Invalid selections cancel the change, and the 512-bit status block reports supported, selected, busy, and power information. Switching completes within eight clocks.
- High-Speed mode is optional, uses 50 MHz for a 25 MB/s interface, and requires one card with one-to-one CLK/CMD/DAT connections. CMD8 checks host voltage before ACMD41 and echoes the voltage range and check pattern in R7. ACMD41’s CCS value distinguishes SDSC, which uses byte addressing, from SDHC/SDXC, which use block addressing and fixed 512-byte blocks without partial or misaligned access.
- Hosts may vary or stop the bus clock to control flow or save power, subject to specified limits and required clock cycles after transactions. CRC7 protects commands and most responses; CRC16 protects each data block and is calculated separately per line in wide-bus mode. CRC failures and illegal commands leave card state unchanged, prevent command execution, and set the corresponding status bits.
- Standard-capacity read timeouts are the lower of 100 times the typical access time or 100 ms; high-capacity cards use a minimum 100 ms timeout. Standard-capacity write timeouts are the lower of 100 times the typical program time or 250 ms. SDHC busy time is normally limited to 250 ms, while specified SDXC cases may extend to 500 ms; speed-class writes remain limited to 250 ms.

The 42mm rose-gold Apple Watch Series 10 with GPS and cellular data is at its lowest price yet. It features a larger, brighter display, a slimmer and lighter design, water-temperature sensing, tides tracking, fitness and sleep monitoring, and about 20 minutes of fast charging. The older model saves money compared with the Series 11, which has better battery life and returns a blood-oxygen sensor.

Following a deadly engine failure on Southwest Flight 1380, the airline faced scrutiny over whether its frequent short flights increase wear and safety risks. The Boeing 737 engine broke apart at 32,000 feet over Pennsylvania; shrapnel killed passenger Jennifer Riordan, 43, and blew her partly through a broken window. The NTSB found that a snapped fan blade showed signs of metal fatigue.

Southwest’s planes average 5.3 flights daily, compared with 2.8 to 3.4 at American, Delta and United, and its average route is the shortest among U.S. airlines. Safety experts nevertheless did not consider Southwest unsafe, citing its previously strong safety record, experienced crews and all-Boeing 737 fleet. Southwest had paid millions to settle safety violations, including a $7.5 million FAA fine in 2009 for flying 46 planes without required inspections.

Mechanics’ union representatives accused Southwest of pressuring maintenance workers and retaliating against them. Southwest said it had inspected fan blades covered by a CFM recommendation and would inspect all older blades by August. CEO Gary Kelly emphasized safety, while passengers on the flight received $5,000 and a $1,000 travel voucher.

The speaker regrets unintentionally hitting an opponent in the mouth while trying to push him aside, says it was his first incident, and is frustrated by a league ruling that will keep him from playing Thursday.

A Washington Post series examines what patriotism means to Americans amid political division and President Trump’s characterization of supporters and critics. In Fargo, Air Force veteran and professor Jane Pettinger sees protest, military service and defending democracy as patriotic, while worrying that America is becoming less progressive. Retired Navy veteran Dave Richardson defines patriotism through honoring military service, celebrating national symbols and standing during the anthem, though he acknowledges players’ racial-justice aims.

Denver librarian Naghem Swade, whose family fled Iraq, sees patriotism in welcoming and helping immigrants and respecting others’ values. Louisiana restaurant owners Rudy Gomez and Scott Carlton banned NFL broadcasts over players’ anthem protests, citing military service and perceived disrespect, then restored them for the Saints. In Vermont, Harry Russell defines patriotism as community involvement and doing one’s best for the country despite national conflict. Near Pittsburgh, Lytia Brock calls protest against racial injustice and police violence patriotic but says fear during traffic stops makes it difficult to feel American pride or believe the country’s freedoms reach everyone.

Daisy-chain mode is enabled after power-up or reset by programming DAISY_CHAIN_LEN with the number of ADCs in the chain, excluding ADC1. A register write requires one SPI frame of N × 24 SCLKs; four ADCs require 96 SCLKs. For register reads, REG_BANK_SEL selects the bank and SPI_RD_EN is set to 0b. The controller then reads N repetitions of {0xFE, 0x00, 8-bit register address}, followed by N repetitions of {0xFF, 0xFF, 0xFF}; each ADC returns an 8-bit address and 16-bit register data.

Register fields cover SPI/daisy-chain configuration, bank selection, averaging, XOR and digital test patterns, speed boost, gain-error correction, analog bandwidth, power and reference controls, output lanes, common-mode range, and PGA initialization. Reserved fields must retain their reset values.

The ADS9803 is described as an eight-channel, 20-bit, 2-MSPS DAQ system with an integrated analog front end. Its calibrated total unadjusted error is 0.0015% at 25°C ±5°C. For PMU applications, it supports direct channel connections or multiplexing and offers low-noise and wide-bandwidth modes; wide-bandwidth mode settles to 99.95% of full scale in 7.5 µs.

The device uses AVDD_5V, VDD_1V8, and IOVDD supplies, with no required power-up sequence. Recommended layout includes separate 0.1-µF bypass capacitors, short ground and reference connections, and separation of analog and digital paths. TI also provides development and support resources and warns that proper ESD precautions are required.

Обзор рассматривает RFID как форму автоматической идентификации и сбора данных для реального времени отслеживания товаров и поведения покупателей. Раннее распространение технологии в 2000-х годах сдерживалось высокой стоимостью меток, незрелостью стандартов и сложностями интеграции, однако цифровая трансформация ритейла создала новые условия для её развития. RFID применяется для точной инвентаризации, управления цепочками поставок и активами, автоматизации приёмки и комплектации товаров, борьбы с кражами, работы умных примерочных, контроля доступа и платежей.

Архитектура RFID-системы включает метки и считыватели, корпоративные серверы, промежуточное ПО, базы данных и аналитические системы, а также средства обмена данными между участниками цепочки поставок, включая EPCIS. Метки хранят уникальный код продукта EPC, считываемый ридером и интегрируемый с системами WMS, ERP и CRM.

Для обработки RFID-данных предложен двухэтапный ETL-конвейер на базе SSIS. Первый этап извлекает, очищает, размечает и преобразует данные; второй объединяет посекундные перемещения покупателей, рассчитывает агрегированные показатели и загружает их в структурированное хранилище. Многомерный куб и средства визуализации обеспечивают отчётность, расчёт метрик и моделирование.

Логическая модель включает факты продаж с финансовыми, количественными и складскими показателями, а также измерения товаров, поставщиков, дат, покупателей, зон и перемещений. Факты поведения покупателя содержат координаты, скорость, расстояние и временны́е метки RFID-трекинга. Интеграция RFID-данных с POS-транзакциями по идентификатору покупателя и времени связывает маршрут по магазину с итоговыми покупками.

В системе сбалансированных показателей целевыми эффектами названы ROI 20–30% за два года, снижение потерь от краж до 75%, сокращение логистических и инвентаризационных затрат на 30%, рост продаж на 5–10%, сокращение времени кассовых операций на 50% и повышение точности онлайн-заказов до 98%. Дальнейшее развитие системы связывается с интеграцией RFID с IoT и искусственным интеллектом для прогнозной аналитики, персонализации и автоматизации управления ритейлом.

Foreign Minister Amancio Alcorta’s unexpected death was mourned as the loss of a devoted public servant. The Republic was at peace, boundary disputes were being resolved through established conventions, several arbitration treaties awaited legislative consideration, and Mexico hosted the second international congress with all American states represented. The government described a longstanding policy of settling differences through direct agreement or arbitration, unchanged even during war, and characterized increased military strength prompted by national unrest as defensive. The final boundary dispute with Chile had been submitted to the British monarch for arbitration; an expert was surveying the territory, and cordial relations were urged after the award.

Financially, conditions were difficult in late 1898. Congress authorized a $30 million gold loan backed by alcohol-tax proceeds, but it was not executed because its terms were unacceptable. A public-debt unification plan was withdrawn after Senate approval due to public opposition, while approved replacement projects enabled the executive to meet its obligations. Revenue exceeded estimates, and 1901 spending was below budget.

Tesla, Inc.’s Form 10-Q for the quarter ended June 30, 2021 reported second-quarter revenue of $11.958 billion, up from $6.036 billion in 2020. Gross profit was $2.884 billion, net income attributable to common stockholders was $1.142 billion, and diluted earnings per share was $1.02. Recommended measures include adequate sleep, stress management, hydration, and a balanced diet featuring nuts, seeds, alkaline vegetables, fruits, whole grains, and anti-inflammatory foods, while limiting alcohol, excess coffee, refined sugar, and flour.

The passage provides PCB-layout guidance for the UC1825B-SP. Feedback traces should run directly, remain somewhat thick, and stay away from the inductor and other noise sources, preferably on the opposite side of the PCB with a ground plane between them. Input/filter, feed-forward, and compensation components should be surface-mounted and placed close to the IC. Power traces should be short, direct, and thick, with a recommended minimum of 15 mils per ampere; the inductor, output capacitors, and output diode should also be positioned close together. Ground planes are recommended on both PCB sides, and multilayer boards can separate power and signal layers. Switching-current loops should be arranged to flow in the same direction during both switching states to reduce radiated EMI.

A ground plane is required, including a dedicated section for high-di/dt power ground connected to PGND. Power-ground connections should include the input return, bulk input capacitor, MOSFET sources, and the specified output clamp, which uses a high-current Schottky diode to VCC and PGND. VCC and VREF require direct high-frequency ceramic-capacitor bypassing, and analog circuitry should connect to signal ground. Each output driver supports 2-A peak current.

Additional sections cover ESD handling precautions, TI documentation-update subscriptions and E2E support, mechanical and orderable information, package notes, disclaimers, and related legal notices.

As ICE raids intensify, nearly 700 undocumented immigrants have been arrested, fueling deportation fears. Churches are offering sanctuary, with more than 6,000 volunteers and 800 churches participating. Jessica, whose immediate family is legally in the U.S., fears deportation but plans to comply with her ICE check-in.

Harvard researcher Ian Wallace and colleagues examined more than 2,000 skeletons, finding that the prevalence of knee osteoarthritis roughly doubled from about 8% in earlier specimens to 16% in more recent ones. The increase remained after accounting for age and weight, suggesting that lifestyle factors may contribute beyond aging and obesity. The researchers hypothesize that physical inactivity may be a major factor, rather than joint wear alone. Exercise can strengthen supporting muscles and potentially make joints more resilient, but it does not guarantee prevention, and its appropriateness depends on disease severity. More research is needed to identify the causes of the rise in arthritis.

This medRxiv preprint examines how human contact-network structure affects COVID-19 transmission across three scales: individual risk tolerance, population structure, and interaction type. Synthetic networks of roughly 3,000 people were built from 2019 U.S. data, including household, classroom, workplace, and low-rate community layers. Networks representing Florida and Texas reflected differences in age and household-size distributions. Three behavioral scenarios were tested: universal participation, avoidance of work and school by vulnerable individuals, and avoidance by members of households containing vulnerable people. Disease spread was simulated using a discrete-time, modified SEIR chain-binomial model with literature parameters approximating the initial Wuhan COVID-19 wave.

The study found that isolating vulnerable individuals by avoiding work and school interactions did not sufficiently reduce their infection risk. Age and household-size distributions had varied and sometimes counteracting effects on epidemic outcomes. Overall, co-worker interactions contributed more to disease spread than interactions among school-age children. The results support a nuanced view of disease transmission in interconnected social networks and implications for targeted public-health strategies.

Using eQTLGen cis-eQTL data and prostate cancer GWAS data from UK Biobank and FinnGen, Mendelian randomization identified 151 candidate genes in discovery and 12 replicated targets: HOXA9, MPHOSPH6, SLC45A3, PBX2, HLA-A, PPARGC1A, FLOT2, TKT, CARNS1, GPBAR1, CSF1R, and TRAV21. HOXA9, MPHOSPH6, SLC45A3, PBX2, and HLA-A were positively associated with prostate cancer risk, while the remaining seven were negatively associated. GO/KEGG enrichment indicated involvement in metabolic processes, insulin signaling, and transcriptional misregulation in cancer; a protein–protein interaction network was also constructed. DSigDB predicted five candidate drugs, and AutoDock evaluated seven drug–target interactions, with the strongest reported binding being tauroursodeoxycholic acid with GPBAR1 at −11.1 kcal/mol. The authors noted that environmental and lifestyle factors were not considered and that experimental validation and clinical trials are required to establish the safety and efficacy of the proposed targets and drugs.

British diplomats sought to mediate between Chile and Argentina over naval spending, which both countries regarded as burdensome amid business depression and concerns about their financial condition. Chile’s purchase of two warships prompted Argentine naval expansion, and Chilean minister Mr. Lowther proposed mutual limits on armaments, including cancellation of Argentine ironclad orders. Argentina initially refused. After Chilean minister Mr. Concha returned, he offered a narrower proposal limiting further armaments, but Chile mistakenly believed it already possessed naval superiority; Argentina had also ordered two ironclads.

General Mitre argued that Argentina should not intervene in Pacific coast affairs, provoking opposition from supporters of Peru and Bolivia. Britain subsequently offered friendly mediation, and ministers conducted negotiations under its auspices, though details remained reserved. The talks were interrupted by Dr. Alcorta’s death.

The President’s message optimistically addressed public finances, debt and revenue, boundary settlement and arbitration, the army and navy, and colonization plans, while withholding further details.

Amgen reported that Repatha reduced a composite of cardiovascular death, heart attack, and the most common type of stroke in a 12,000-patient trial. Existing data showed benefit in patients already having heart problems. Analysts said the broader results could expand Repatha’s market, particularly among patients who do not meet LDL-C goals. Repatha generated $2.2 billion in global sales in 2024, up 36% from 2023.

This study evaluated whether first-phase left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF-1), a simpler echocardiographic index of early myocardial contraction, reflects coronary artery stenosis severity and post-PCI myocardial recovery. The prospective study consecutively enrolled 207 adults with chest pain who underwent coronary angiography: 73 had mild, 39 moderate, and 95 severe stenosis. LVEF-1 was calculated from left ventricular end-diastolic volume and the volume at peak aortic flow velocity.

LVEF-1 declined as stenosis severity increased, whereas conventional LVEF did not differ significantly among groups. LVEF-1 was negatively correlated with the Gensini score (r = −0.694) and BNP and independently predicted stenosis of at least 50% and 70%. A cutoff of 27.9% predicted stenosis ≥50% with 82.8% sensitivity and 83.6% specificity, while 26.9% predicted stenosis ≥70% with 89.5% sensitivity and 83.9% specificity. LVEF-1 had greater diagnostic value than GLS, E/e′, LVEF, and LVDd.

Among 82 patients who underwent PCI, LVEF-1 and GLS increased and E/e′ decreased four days after PCI, while LVEF did not significantly change. Gensini score and stent diameter independently influenced the change in LVEF-1; greater improvement was associated with more severe stenosis and larger stent diameter.

The authors concluded that LVEF-1 may be a sensitive, practical indicator of early cardiac dysfunction in coronary artery stenosis and of improvement after PCI. Limitations included the small, cross-sectional sample, differences between imaging centers, absence of functional coronary testing or microcirculatory ischemia assessment, and possible medication effects.

NXP shares fell 5% as China’s warning against U.S. trade threats dimmed hopes for Qualcomm’s $44 billion acquisition. Qualcomm’s lawyers remained in San Diego and talks were on hold, with Chinese approval still pending.

One month after vaccination, measured antibody responses met several comparators. Among prior BNT162b2 recipients without prior COVID-19, the original-strain response after a BNT162b2 booster was comparable to the response after Dose 2. Their Beta-variant response after one BNT162b2SA booster was also comparable to the original-strain response after two BNT162b2 doses. Among recipients without prior BNT162b2, the Beta response after two BNT162b2SA doses was comparable to the original-strain response after two BNT162b2 doses. Researchers considered these findings unlikely to be due to chance.

Injection-site reactions and systemic events within seven days were generally short-lived, mild or moderate, and well tolerated. Injection-site pain was the most common local reaction; tiredness and headache were the most common systemic events. In Phase 1, some participants had temporary lymphocyte reductions one to three days after the first BNT162b1 or BNT162b2 dose, with counts returning to normal by days 6–8.

All Phase 1 BNT162b1 and BNT162b2 doses were well tolerated except 100 µg BNT162b1, which was stopped after Dose 1 because of reactions. The 30-µg BNT162b2 dose was selected for Phase 2/3, and no participant left Phase 1 because of medical problems. In Phase 2/3, 32 of 21,926 BNT162b2 recipients and 36 of 21,921 placebo recipients withdrew during the blinded period because of medical problems, each under 1%; most problems were mild or moderate.

Serious medical problems were uncommon. Two occurred in Phase 1, and researchers did not consider them vaccine-related. No single serious problem reached 1% in Phase 2/3 or Phase 3 booster groups. A small number of temporary serious events among participants aged 16 or older were considered possibly vaccine-related, including arm or leg numbness or tingling, portal-vein blockage by a blood clot, and a mini stroke; no such events in participants aged 12–15 were considered vaccine-related.

No deaths occurred in Phase 1. In Phase 2/3, 85 of 23,141 initial BNT162b2 recipients, 62 of 21,371 initial placebo recipients who later received BNT162b2, and 23 of 23,141 placebo-only recipients died from different causes; researchers did not believe BNT162b2 caused the deaths. No Phase 3 participant who received BNT162b2SA without prior BNT162b2 died. The passage notes that these were selected main results and that other studies may differ.

Peter Drucker's writings on privatisation and the "ownership society" — carried forward by David Howell in 1969, adopted by Margaret Thatcher, and later popularized by George W. Bush in 2003/04 — are presented as an indirect inspiration for the Modi government's efforts since 2014 to reduce the role of the state in India. Though India remains far from an ownership society, with pervasive state control, rampant subsidies and government interference in business, the passage notes encouraging signs, including banking reforms such as an insolvency and restructuring law, freedom from political interference, and consolidation of public sector banks; the planned abolition of most LPG and kerosene subsidies for non-poor households; and the UDAY programme reviving state electricity boards without central bailouts. Progress is described as slow and mixed, and the argument is that a true ownership society requires eliminating government handouts and pursuing mass privatisation, giving the private sector a greater role in running companies.

- The TPS7H500x-SP family consists of radiation-hardness-assured, fixed-frequency, peak-current-mode PWM controllers for space-grade DC-DC converters. Switching frequencies up to 2 MHz are supported, and the controllers require external gate drivers. Supported topologies include buck, flyback, forward, active-clamp forward, push-pull, and full-bridge converters.

- TPS7H5003-SP has a fixed 50 ns typical dead time, while TPS7H5001-SP and TPS7H5002-SP provide two independently programmable dead times. RPS at PS sets the delay from primary turn-off to synchronous-rectifier turn-on, and RSP at SP sets the delay from synchronous-rectifier turn-off to primary turn-on. Floating PS and SP pins select a minimum 8 ns typical dead time; populated settings require 10–300 kΩ resistors. Synchronous-rectifier outputs remain disabled during soft start, so the programmed dead time applies afterward.

- Leading-edge blank time filters transient noise after OUTA or OUTB rises. It is fixed at 50 ns typical for TPS7H5003-SP and programmable through RLEB for the other devices; LEB cannot float, and RLEB must be 10–300 kΩ. Blank time contributes to the device’s minimum on-time together with an internal logic delay.

- Pulse-skipping mode prevents operating problems caused by minimum on-time at high frequencies. Primary outputs periodically stop switching, while synchronous-rectifier outputs remain on if soft start has completed and remain off if pulse skipping occurs during soft start. Pulses are skipped when COMP is below 0.3 V at the rising edge of the system clock and the previous duty cycle was below 25%. With both primary outputs active under a 50% duty-cycle limit, each output skips equal pulses to preserve volt-second balance and avoid flux walking.

- TPS7H5001-SP, TPS7H5002-SP, and TPS7H5003-SP configure maximum duty cycle through DCL. DCL connected to VLDO permits 100% duty cycle, while leaving it floating permits 75%. A 50% limit uses DCL connected to AVSS and is supported by TPS7H5001-SP and TPS7H5004-SP; OUTB/SRB operate only in this configuration. TPS7H5004-SP otherwise supports only 50%. In external synchronization, limiting is most precise with a 50%-duty-cycle system clock.

- CS_ILIM accepts a signal representing transformer primary current and supports both peak-current-mode PWM and overcurrent protection. OUTA/OUTB turn on with the internal clock and turn off when the sensed peak current reaches the COMP/2 comparison level; the comparator signal includes a 150 mV offset. A resistor from CS_ILIM to AVSS senses current, and the nominal overcurrent threshold is 1.05 V. Current-limit calculations depend on converter topology and sensing arrangement, and sufficient margin should remain between normal peak current and the trip point.

- When CS_ILIM reaches 1.05 V, the controller performs cycle-by-cycle current limiting. Each threshold event charges CHICC with an 80 µA current until the clock cycle ends. Once CHICC reaches 0.6 V, switching stops, the soft-start pin is discharged, and the HICC voltage is pulled up to 1 V. A 1 µA restart current then discharges CHICC; when it reaches 0.3 V, soft start restarts if the overcurrent has cleared. CHICC determines both the cycle-by-cycle limiting delay and the non-switching hiccup interval; at least 3.3 nF is recommended.

- The FAULT pin accepts external protection signals. A typical threshold above 0.6 V must persist for the specified 0.4–1.4 µs minimum pulse-width range to trigger shutdown. Detection discharges SS and stops switching while the rising threshold is exceeded. After FAULT falls below its typical 0.5 V falling threshold, the controller waits approximately 15 switching cycles plus an internal delay and then restarts soft start. A new threshold violation during the delay restarts the sequence.

- Peak-current-mode instability above 50% duty cycle is mitigated with slope compensation. The TPS7H500x-SP implements compensation as a ramp subtracted from the divided error-amplifier output. Minimum stability compensation is 0.5 times the inductor’s falling-current slope, and 1 times that slope is recommended; higher values do not improve stability. RSC sets the desired slope through a resistor to AVSS. The controller supports Type 2A or Type 2B frequency compensation; Type 2A adds CHF in parallel with RCOMP and CCOMP for high-frequency noise attenuation. Component selection is based on crossover frequency, error-amplifier transconductance, reference voltage, power-stage transconductance, transformer and current-sense ratios, sense resistance, and CCSR.

- Thermal shutdown stops switching above a typical 175°C junction temperature and reinitiates the power-up sequence below 160°C. In normal operation, the internal oscillator initiates primary-output switching, the external switch current is sensed, COMP is stepped down internally, and the power switch turns off when sensed current reaches the stepped-down COMP voltage.

- A design example uses TPS7H5001-SP in a 500 kHz, 5 V synchronous push-pull converter with GaN FETs. Selected values include a 205 kΩ RT resistor, a 10 kΩ upper feedback resistor, a 1.4 kΩ lower feedback resistor, 20.5 kΩ dead-time resistors for approximately 25 ns, a 49.9 kΩ RLEB for approximately 50 ns, and a 33 nF soft-start capacitor providing about 7.5 ms of soft start.

- The example targets a 35% duty cycle within the controller’s 50% limit, uses a transformer turns ratio of 2.5, and uses 40 µH primary inductance after an initial 33 µH calculation. Primary GaN FETs are rated at 170 V for a 36 V maximum input because they experience twice the input voltage when off; 80 V synchronous-rectifier GaN FETs are selected for approximately 20 V nominal stress. Parallel Schottky diodes can reduce soft-start and dead-time losses. An RCD clamp controls switch-node overshoot and must be optimized through testing.

- The output inductor is 0.47 µH with a targeted 40% ripple current. Calculations require at least 1.3 mF of output capacitance for 2% ripple and 2.5% maximum transient deviation; 2.3 mF total is used to provide additional radiation-induced single-event-transient margin. Seven 330 µF polymer-tantalum capacitors provide this capacitance. An optional LC output filter can further reduce ripple, with its resonance selected above the crossover frequency but below the switching frequency and bulk-capacitor ESR zero; damping may be added if high-frequency peaking occurs.

- The example begins cycle-by-cycle limiting at approximately 35 A, providing about 45% margin over the 24.25 A peak inductor current at maximum load. A 1:100 current-sense transformer and 7.5 Ω sense resistor are selected. A 3.3 nF hiccup capacitor, Type 2A compensation with a 10 kHz target crossover, 40.2 kΩ RCOMP, 15 nF CCOMP, 47 pF CHF, and 102 kΩ RSC are also used. Several compensation, blank-time, clamp, and filtering values may require tuning during testing.

- The controllers operate from a regulated 4–14 V supply. VIN requires at least a 0.1 µF bypass capacitor to AVSS; X5R-or-better ceramic capacitors placed close to the controller are recommended, with bulk capacitance added when the supply is remote.

- Layout guidance includes keeping feedback away from power magnetics and switching nodes, minimizing high-dv/dt and high-di/dt loop area, keeping AVSS separate from power ground except at one connection point, using short and wide high-current traces, placing bypass and compensation components near the controller, routing OUTA/OUTB/SRA/SRB away from sensitive control traces, filtering the CS_ILIM signal near the pin when required, and connecting backside metallization to AVSS through multiple vias for the CFP option.

A backtest of the Santa Claus Rally in the NIFTY 50 used daily Yahoo! Finance data from 2008 onward. The strategy went long at the close of the second Friday in December and exited at the close of the first trading day of the new year. Results showed a 1.2% average gain per trade, 71% win rate, profit factor of 6, and 7% maximum drawdown. The unt radable cash index served only as a proxy.

Pittsburgh unveiled 1978-inspired throwback jerseys, featuring block numbers and sleeve stripes, to replace the “bumblebee” uniforms for at least two seasons. The design commemorates the 40th anniversaries of Super Bowl XIII and XIV, with the Steelers first wearing them against Cleveland in Week 8.

Digital leaders treat data culture as a central component of organizational strategy, emphasizing transparency, broad data access, collaboration, shared context, and learning. Governance and privacy controls protect data while encouraging responsible use. Leaders also believe valuable ideas can originate anywhere in the organization, although developing this mindset requires leadership sponsorship. Standardized APIs support this openness: 88% of digital leaders have them, compared with 27% of digital laggards.

Digital leaders encourage employees to gather and examine relevant data, set measurable objectives, track progress, and use formal evaluations, including 360-degree reviews. Although measurement adds structure, it promotes autonomy, innovation, experimentation, and calculated risk-taking. In contrast, digital laggards often restrict access to data, store it in departmental silos, and use it to reinforce existing decisions or individual expertise. They frequently set unrealistic goals, avoid measurement, emphasize process adherence, and struggle to align objectives with strategy.

A retail company acquired by a parent with strong data-driven practices upgraded its data systems and rapidly implemented real-time sales reporting. Automated updates now enable leaders across business units and the CEO to make timely decisions about inventory, marketing, supply chain, and other areas.

Digital leaders align employees around transparent, strategy-linked objectives, often combining top-down and bottom-up goal-setting. Shared goals and common data models support vertical alignment with company strategy and horizontal collaboration across teams. However, some leaders risk allowing excessive analysis to impede simple decisions and diminish human judgment.

Culture coordinates beliefs, values, and daily behavior at leading organizations, where employee actions reinforce stated values. Laggards often experience inconsistency between stated ambitions and actual practices; entrenched habits, insufficient skills, and limited leadership focus impede transformation. Even mature leaders face tensions and must continue developing their cultures.

Organizations commonly fall into four patterns: data novices, insight-ready firms, tech-enabled firms, and data-reliant firms. Each has distinct cultural and technical gaps and can target actions suited to its current maturity.

On February 25, 2019, Amazon.com, Inc. elected Indra K. Nooyi to its Board of Directors and appointed her to the Audit Committee. Nooyi served as PepsiCo’s CEO from 2006 to 2018 and chairman from 2007 to February 2019. She has served on Schlumberger Limited’s board since April 2015. Amazon granted Nooyi a restricted stock unit award for 549 common shares under its 1997 Stock Incentive Plan, vesting in three equal annual installments beginning May 15, 2020, subject to continued service, and entered into an indemnification agreement with her.

Stocks represent ownership in companies and can grow in value, provide dividends, and increase ownership through share buybacks, but they carry the risk of capital loss, including over ten-year periods. Diversification across companies, industries, and stock types is recommended. Bonds are loans to companies or government agencies, generally paying fixed interest and returning principal at maturity. They are less risky than stocks, and bondholders are paid before shareholders in bankruptcy. Bond risk, interest rates, and liquidity vary with maturity and credit quality.

Historically, stocks have outperformed bonds, but the appropriate allocation depends on factors such as investment horizon and risk tolerance. Near retirement, for example, investors might favor more bonds. A backtested 60% stock/40% bond portfolio produced lower returns than an all-stock portfolio but experienced less volatility and smaller drawdowns. Bonds have often mitigated losses during market turbulence, particularly sovereign bonds, while corporate bonds remain exposed to credit risk. A separate seasonal strategy shifting between countries in winter and summer failed to perform as hypothesized in backtesting.

This continuation application, corresponding to PCT/US2020/056133 and four provisional applications, concerns muscle-targeting compositions, particularly recombinant adeno-associated virus (rAAV) vectors. It notes that conventional rAAVs primarily target the liver after systemic delivery, while transduction of other tissues is limited, requiring high doses that may cause liver toxicity and create manufacturing challenges. Mouse studies may also not predict responses in primates.

Disclosed embodiments include targeting moieties containing one or more 1–20-amino-acid n-mer motifs, including RGD and non-RGD motifs, associated with therapeutic cargo. These motifs may be inserted at specified positions in AAV capsids, including external insertion between amino acids 588 and 589 of AAV9 or analogous positions in other serotypes, to provide muscle-specific targeting. Engineered AAV particles, vector systems, producing cells, pharmaceutical formulations, and administration methods are described. Cargo may include oligonucleotides, morpholinos, therapeutic transgenes, CRISPR-Cas components, proteins, or mini-/micro-dystrophin genes for treating muscle and other diseases. Figures describe capsid-library generation and selection, muscle-selective MyoAAV variants, improved muscle transduction, faster muscle expression, DMD mutation correction, integrin-mediated entry, and 50–100-fold greater transduction than AAV9 in mouse and human primary myotubes. Tables rank selected capsid variants by nucleotide and amino-acid sequence and muscle mRNA scores.

This Motley Fool Money page (dated Oct. 5, 2025) reviews credit cards offering rewards and 0% intro APR, noting the site earns commissions from partner offers that do not influence product ratings.

- **Wells Fargo Active Cash Card:** Unlimited 2% cash back on purchases, $200 welcome bonus after $500 in spending in the first 3 months, $0 annual fee, 0% intro APR for 12 months on purchases and qualifying balance transfers (then 18.99%, 23.99%, or 28.99% variable APR), complimentary Visa Signature Concierge, and cell phone protection up to $600 with a $25 deductible. Balance transfers made within 120 days qualify for the intro rate with a 3% fee, then up to 5% (min. $5). Recommended credit score: Good/Excellent (670–850).
- **Capital One Quicksilver Cash Rewards Card:** Unlimited 1.5% cash back on every purchase, 5% on hotels, vacation rentals and rental cars booked through Capital One Travel, $300 welcome bonus ($100 Travel credit plus $200 cash after $500 spend in 3 months), $0 annual fee, no foreign transaction fees, and 0% intro APR on purchases and balance transfers for 15 months, after which 18.99%–28.99% variable APR applies with a balance transfer fee.
- **Citi card:** 2% cash back (1% on purchase plus 1% when paying, requiring on-time minimum payments), 5% on hotels, car rentals and attractions via Citi Travel, and $200 cash back (20,000 ThankYou Points) after $1,500 spent in the first 6 months. Its 0% intro APR applies to balance transfers only (18 months, then 17.99%–27.99% variable); transfer fees are 3% in the first 4 months, then 5% (min. $5). Transfers earn no cash back.

The page advises readers to choose a card whose features fit their needs and discloses advertiser relationships, including with JPMorgan Chase, Wells Fargo, Capital One, Citi and Visa.

European stocks rose Monday on broad banking gains, but trading was thin during an extended New Year’s break; London and U.S. markets were closed. The Stoxx Europe 600 gained 0.5% after ending 2016 down 1.2%, while most national markets advanced. Italian banks rallied after reports that Banca Monte dei Paschi would issue €15 billion in 2017 debt to bolster confidence and liquidity, though its shares remain suspended.

Microsoft Corporation’s Form 10-Q for the quarter ended December 31, 2020 reported quarterly revenue of $43.076 billion, up from $36.906 billion a year earlier. Net income was $15.463 billion, compared with $11.649 billion, and diluted EPS increased to $2.03 from $1.51. For the first six months, revenue was $80.230 billion, net income was $29.356 billion, and diluted EPS was $3.85. At December 31, the company held $14.432 billion in cash and $117.536 billion in short-term investments, with total assets of $304.137 billion and stockholders’ equity of $130.236 billion. Six-month operating cash flow was $31.851 billion.

Commercial cloud revenue rose 34% to $16.7 billion for the quarter and totaled $31.9 billion for six months. Other reported growth included Azure at 50%, Office 365 Commercial at 21%, Dynamics 365 at 39%, LinkedIn revenue at 23%, and Xbox content and services revenue at 40%.

Microsoft increased the estimated useful lives of server equipment from three to four years and network equipment from two to four years. For the quarter, this added $787 million to operating income and $649 million to net income; six-month effects were $1.7 billion and $1.4 billion, respectively. Fiscal 2021 operating income was estimated to increase by $2.7 billion.

The filing also described investments and derivatives, debt, taxes, leases, contingencies, remaining performance obligations, and segment results. Microsoft agreed to acquire ZeniMax Media for $7.5 billion in cash, subject to regulatory review, and had $20.7 billion remaining under its share-repurchase authorization. COVID-19 benefited cloud, consumer, and gaming demand while weighing on transactional licensing and operating expenses. Deloitte’s review identified no material modifications needed to the unaudited interim financial information.

A prospective NORPACT2 cohort study measured serum 3-IAA before chemotherapy in 124 patients with borderline-resectable or locally advanced pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma without distant metastases. Thirty-five patients provided repeat samples after 2–4 months. Median pre-treatment 3-IAA was 290 ng/mL and was associated with age but not tumor diameter, CA19-9, or chemotherapy regimen. Concentrations did not differ significantly by CT or CA19-9 response, surgical resection, or one-year survival, and the nonsignificant post-chemotherapy increase did not reach statistical significance. Median overall survival was 499 days. Pre-treatment 3-IAA was not associated with survival in univariable or adjusted analyses, including when cases were censored at surgery. Thus, the reported association between high 3-IAA and chemotherapy response in metastatic PDAC was not validated in this nonmetastatic population. The authors note possible differences in tumor burden, patient characteristics, tumor biology, and assays, and conclude that any clinically meaningful effect is likely small. They recommend validation in geographically distinct metastatic PDAC cohorts before a controlled trial of increasing circulating 3-IAA alongside chemotherapy.

Abdul Dannaoui, 5, alleges two teachers taped his mouth shut and discarded his lunch. His parents filed a police report and plan to sue Crestwood School District. One teacher was removed, police are investigating, and the district disputes abuse claims.

Researchers from McGill University and the University of Toronto propose that gaslighting can be understood as a learning process based on prediction error minimization, which helps the brain predict and respond to new information. Because people rely on trusted, close relationships to form their sense of self and reality, a gaslighter’s unexpected behavior can create surprise that is repeatedly attributed to the target’s poor grasp of reality, gradually undermining their confidence in their own perception. Lead author Willis Klein said the model suggests anyone who trusts the wrong person could be affected, although factors such as attachment styles or trauma may influence susceptibility. Future research may validate the model and improve support for victims.

Reagan Library records document preparations for the Reagan administration’s foreign policy and national security transition. An undated Richard Allen paper was prepared for the Foreign Policy Advisory Board’s November 21, 1980 meeting; an agenda, press release, and Tabs II–III were attached, Tab IV was missing, and no minutes were found. The interim advisory committee included Allen and numerous former officials. A December 22 State Department transition report, prepared under William Timmons and D. Abshire’s National Security Group, was divided into two volumes with tabs attached but unprinted. Robert Neumann led the State team and reported to Abshire. An editorial excerpt recounts Reagan’s November 20, 1975 announcement of his 1976 Republican candidacy against Gerald Ford, citing economic concerns, foreign energy dependence, military developments, unresponsive leadership, and the need for responsive government and progress.

Builder Eric Woodward has begun creating a temporary public park at a vacant Fort Langley lot where he cancelled a mixed-use project that included a boutique hotel amid a dispute with the Township. The park will have community gathering and family play areas, with major work expected by early July.

The study addresses domain shift in neuroimaging, where small datasets and differences in scanners, protocols, image statistics, and subject populations reduce model performance across datasets. It proposes transfer learning that reuses task-specific features learned from the large UK Biobank (UKB) dataset for smaller OASIS-3, IXI, and ABIDE datasets.

The authors use Simple Fully Connected Neural Networks (SFCNs) for age and sex prediction from 3D structural MRI. Age is treated as probabilistic classification using a discretized normal distribution and KL-divergence loss, while sex uses cross-entropy. MRI preprocessing includes bias correction, registration, brain extraction, and transformation to MNI 152 space. Training uses mean normalization, random shifts, and sagittal mirroring for augmentation. The transfer-learning pipeline pre-trains on UKB, reshapes and trains the classifier for the target task when necessary, and then fine-tunes the full network. PCA-based elastic-net regression serves as a classical baseline.

Direct transfer from UKB retains above-chance sex-prediction accuracy across all target datasets, but performance declines from 99.5% on UKB to 90.2% on OASIS, 59.9% on ABIDE, and 59.1% on IXI. Visualizations and adaptation experiments show that learned features are highly task-specific: same-task pre-training consistently outperforms pre-training on a different task. Features remain comparatively reusable for OASIS and IXI but are more confused for ABIDE because of larger demographic and scanner differences.

Fine-tuning the full model generally improves results over training only the classifier, with especially large gains for ABIDE, though some overfitting occurs. Transfer learning substantially outperforms elastic-net regression: age mean absolute errors are 3.25, 5.65, and 1.70 years for OASIS, IXI, and ABIDE, respectively, compared with 6.24, 9.90, and 3.59 years for elastic net. Corresponding sex accuracies are 92.6%, 90.3%, and 75.7%, versus 67.0%, 73.1%, and 66.9%. The method also improves reported age-prediction results for OASIS and ABIDE, although comparisons with other studies are limited by differing data splits and preprocessing.

Transfer learning outperforms training from scratch in all evaluated cases except ABIDE sex prediction, which exhibits negative transfer. Reinitializing network layers with statistics matched to the pretrained model does not reproduce the gains, indicating that feature reuse, rather than parameter scaling alone, drives improvement. Full transfer learning can perform well with very small training sets for OASIS age prediction, but for ABIDE sex prediction it benefits only with more than 400 training samples; classifier-only fine-tuning is preferable in the very-small-data regime. Transfer learning also consistently accelerates convergence.

The authors position UKB as a potential large-scale pretraining resource for neuroimaging but note its limited scanner coverage and predominantly healthy population, which complicates transfer to disease prediction and heterogeneous sites. They suggest future investigation of feature harmonization, style-transfer methods, and approaches for transferring across tasks.

Teuvo Teräväinen and Antoine Vermette describe playing at this time of year as exciting and a great opportunity, noting their team has good players, confidence and a strong group. Teräväinen says he plays better when calm, and that he is currently the strongest hockey player in his family — his parents play, his sister and brother are good, his brother is a defenseman, and the sport is popular in Finland. Both say Tampa Bay is a fast, skilled, confident and experienced team that was ready early, while Teräväinen reports his team started poorly, played better in the second and third periods and won by two goals, adding the locker room always believes a comeback is possible. Vermette says success at this stage requires facing adversity, persevering and trusting the process. Teräväinen describes scoring with many friends and family watching, as in Finland, calling the goal lucky, and mentions having a man who has been like a second father to him since his real father is far away in Finland. He also discusses working hard on skating and skills to compensate for being the smallest player on the ice. Vermette praises Teräväinen as a smart, skilled player with an active stick.

Sea of Thieves had Rare’s strongest launch-month sales in NPD tracking since 1995, ranking second in March and eighth for 2018 year-to-date. NPD excluded Game Pass downloads, and its performance indicates strong demand for major Microsoft titles.

U.S. stocks fell Tuesday as 10-year Treasury yields reached 3% for the first time in four years, raising corporate borrowing concerns, while company outlooks disappointed. The S&P 500 and Dow posted their steepest declines in two-and-a-half weeks, and the Dow extended its losing streak to five sessions. Technology and industrial stocks weighed on indexes, with Alphabet, Facebook, 3M and Caterpillar each dropping more than 3.5%. Alphabet’s rising expenses and shrinking margins erased its year-to-date gains, Caterpillar cited steel-price concerns, and 3M lowered its 2018 earnings forecast. Apple and other FAANG stocks also declined amid smartphone-demand concerns. Lockheed Martin fell despite raising its sales and profit forecast. Consumer confidence improved, while oil briefly exceeded $75 per barrel before reversing on U.S.-French efforts to address Iran sanctions concerns.

This study develops an AI system for classifying citation intents in Turkish academic texts, addressing the lack of large-scale, standardized Turkish resources. It introduces a publicly available dataset of 2,650 labeled citation sentences extracted from 723 Computer Science research articles. Citation contexts were classified into five Web of Science categories—Background, Basis, Support, Differ, and Discuss—through a hybrid annotation process combining academic experts with GPT- and Gemini-assisted labeling.

The modeling pipeline evaluated GPT-4o and Gemini 2.5 Flash and Pro using in-context learning, automated prompt optimization with DSPy’s MIPROv2 and chain-of-thought module, and ensemble methods. Manual prompt revisions substantially improved accuracy, while DSPy optimization reached 86.5%. Few-shot results varied by model: Gemini peaked at 89.1% with one example, whereas GPT-4o performed best with zero examples at 88.4%. Majority voting achieved 90.2%, logistic-regression stacking 91.0%, and an XGBoost stacked meta-model 91.3%, the highest reported accuracy.

Major challenges included severe class imbalance favoring Background, difficulty distinguishing Support from Differ and identifying Basis, inconsistent model predictions, and a need for contextual interpretation beyond individual sentences. Proposed future work includes hierarchical classifiers, targeted or synthetic data for rare classes, and features incorporating surrounding sentences and document metadata.

On April 27, 2018, Amazon.com, Inc. entered into an amended and restated unsecured revolving credit agreement with Bank of America, N.A. and participating lenders. The agreement increased Amazon’s borrowing capacity from $3.0 billion to $7.0 billion and extended the term through April 27, 2021. Borrowings may be used for general corporate purposes, including backstopping commercial paper notes.

Amazon also established a commercial paper program permitting private placements of unsecured notes with a maximum aggregate amount outstanding at any time of $7.0 billion. Notes may have varying maturities of no more than 397 days, amounts may be reborrowed, and proceeds are expected for general corporate purposes. The amended credit agreement was filed as Exhibit 10.1.

The team reaches the Stanley Cup Finals with one game remaining, seeing an opportunity to close the series as preferable to merely staying alive. Players emphasize resting, warming up, and being mentally and emotionally prepared to win a difficult hockey game rather than expecting an easy victory. They acknowledge the pressure and stakes of clinching the title. An injured teammate may be unable to play, but the team remains confident in those available. Veterans are helping teammates understand what is at stake, while the group plans to stay even-keeled, businesslike, and focused on the task at hand.

Research co-authored by Prof. Ross Levine finds that easier credit encourages businesses to invest in pollution reduction. More available credit makes green-project loans easier to obtain, while lower interest rates increase the returns from such investments. These projects can also reduce pollution fines, improve worker health and productivity, and enhance public reputation.

Using fracking-related deposit windfalls to banks as a natural experiment, the authors found that non-gas-producing counties with the largest credit gains experienced benzene emissions 26% below average changes in other counties; other pollutants also declined. Borrowers whose lenders received these windfalls subsequently reduced toxic emissions, received stronger environmental ratings, and advocated more forcefully on green issues. The study does not assess fracking’s environmental effects, and Levine plans to examine whether borrowing conditions affect worker safety.

Ryan Malone signed a 25-game tryout contract with the AHL’s Iowa Wild, keeping him eligible for the 2018 U.S. Olympic men’s hockey team, while Brian Gionta remains a possible selection. The veteran forwards have more than 1,500 combined NHL games, and the 25-player roster is expected around Jan. 1.

Business Insider reports that David Ellison, whose father Larry Ellison backed his acquisition of Paramount, declined to discuss a possible bid for Warner Bros. Discovery, although media observers widely expect one. A combination could merge Paramount’s streaming services and studios with HBO Max and Warner Bros., combine sports rights, and consolidate back-office functions. The Ellisons’ ties to the Trump administration could ease antitrust concerns, while Larry Ellison’s wealth and Apollo’s reported interest could help finance the roughly $44 billion, heavily indebted company. WBD CEO David Zaslav is expected to oppose selling, though his previous separation proposal failed to lift the stock. No deal exists yet, but one would further consolidate Hollywood and reduce the number of buyers for creators.

The paper introduces an edit-distance framework for constructible \(\mathbb{R}^d\)-persistence modules and proves that it realizes the interleaving distance. It reviews posets, Galois connections, persistence modules, constructibility, graded modules, and finite presentations, showing that constructible \(\mathbb{R}^d\)-modules are equivalent to finitely presented ones.

Two categories of finite indexing structures are used: \(\mathrm{JS}_d\), consisting of finite join-semilattices embedded in \(\mathbb{R}^d\), and \((1D)_d\), consisting of finite \(d\)-grids. Their morphisms have right adjoints. Morphisms between associated persistence-module categories define edits, whose costs are their distortion. The edit distance is the infimum of the total distortion along paths of such edits.

The main theorem states that, for either category and any constructible \(\mathbb{R}^d\)-persistence modules \(M,N\),
\[
d_I(M,N)=d_{\mathrm{Ed}}(M,N).
\]
The proof establishes
\[
d_I\le d_{\mathrm{JS}_d}\le d_{(1D)_d}\le d_I.
\]
The first inequality adapts a previous Galois-connection argument. For the last, the paper uses the characterization of interleaving by finite presentations differing by a translation, constructs a continuous interpolation between those presentations, and applies an “easy-edit lemma” based on presentation bijections and injectivity radii.

The result gives an order-theoretic view of interleaving distance complementary to the bottleneck-distance viewpoint. It also characterizes interleaving stability of invariants through edit stability: for the constructed edit distances, stability under one edit is equivalent to stability under the full interleaving or edit distance. The appendices establish the equivalence between the paper’s constructibility notion and the earlier one for \(\mathbb{R}^d\)-modules and prove that finitely presented modules are constructible.

Calgary single mother Shauna Sinfield, who has multiple sclerosis and lives on fixed income, lost her 1998 Toyota Corolla and her 12-year-old son’s hockey gear to thieves. Police doubt the $1,500–$2,000 gear will be recovered. A GoFundMe has raised $685 of its $3,000 goal.

A team discusses a tough playoff series, noting that opponents are reading its coverage well and that players must work through shifting defensive matchups. Despite some fortunate bounces in Montreal, the team is pleased with its system execution, defensive play, and chance generation. Home crowds energize the players, who remain confident that sticking to the game plan will keep them in the series.

The TPS7H500x-SP controllers use fixed-frequency, peak-current-mode control. The CS_ILIM input receives a signal representing primary-side current and must match the COMP-pin input range. OUTA/OUTB turn on with the internal clock and turn off when the sensed peak current reaches COMP/2; the peak-current comparison includes a 150 mV offset. An external resistor from CS_ILIM to AVSS supports PWM operation and overcurrent protection. The nominal CS_ILIM trip threshold is 1.05 V, after which the controller enters hiccup mode. Current-limit calculations must account for the sensing location, transformer and current-sense-transformer ratios, and adequate margin between normal peak current and the trip point.

During an overcurrent, the controller performs cycle-by-cycle current limiting until CHICC reaches 0.6 V. The HICC capacitor is charged by an 80 µA pulsed current. Switching then stops, SS is discharged, and HICC is pulled up to 1 V with approximately 1 mA of pull-up current. A 1 µA restart current discharges CHICC until it reaches 0.3 V, after which soft start resumes if the overcurrent has cleared. CHICC sets both the limiting-delay and restart intervals; the minimum recommended value is 3.3 nF.

The FAULT pin supports additional external overcurrent, overvoltage, or other protection logic. A fault occurs when its voltage exceeds a typical 0.6 V for the specified 0.4–1.4 µs minimum pulse width, which helps reject short transients. Switching stops and SS is discharged until FAULT falls below its typical 0.5 V falling threshold. Restart is delayed by approximately 15 switching cycles plus an internal delay, followed by a new soft-start sequence.

Slope compensation mitigates subharmonic oscillation in peak-current-mode converters operating above 50% duty cycle. The TPS7H500x-SP implements it as a ramp subtracted from the error-amplifier output after scaling by CCSR. Minimum compensation is 0.5 times the inductor’s falling-current slope, and the recommended value is 1 times that slope. An RSC-to-AVSS resistor sets the desired ramp. Type 2A or Type 2B frequency compensation is supported; Type 2A adds CHF in parallel with RCOMP and CCOMP for high-frequency noise attenuation. Component selection starts with crossover frequency, RCOMP, CCOMP, and optionally the output-capacitor ESR zero and CHF. Thermal shutdown stops switching above a typical 175°C junction temperature and permits power-up to resume below 160°C.

The TPS7H500x-SP family is intended for radiation-hardness-assured space-grade DC-DC converters, operates up to 2 MHz, requires external gate drivers, and supports buck, flyback, forward, active-clamp forward, push-pull, and full-bridge topologies.

A demonstrated TPS7H5001-SP synchronous push-pull converter uses GaN FETs and operates at 500 kHz with a 5 V output. Selected values include a 205 kΩ frequency-setting resistor, a 10 kΩ/1.4 kΩ feedback divider, approximately 25 ns dead time with 20.5 kΩ RPS and RSP resistors, and a 49.9 kΩ RLEB resistor for roughly 50 ns leading-edge blanking. A 33 nF soft-start capacitor provides about 7.5 ms of soft start. The transformer uses a 2.5 turns ratio and 40 µH primary inductance. Primary GaN FETs are rated at 170 V for a 36 V maximum input, while an 80 V synchronous rectifier is used despite an expected maximum stress of about 20 V. A parallel Schottky diode can reduce soft-start and dead-time conduction losses. The design uses a 0.47 µH output inductor with 40% target ripple, at least 1.3 mF output capacitance based on ripple and transient limits, and 2.3 mF total for radiation-induced single-event-transient mitigation. An optional filtered output stage can reduce ripple further.

The example begins cycle-by-cycle limiting near 35 A, versus a 24.25 A maximum-load peak inductor current, providing about 45% margin. It uses a 1:100 current-sense transformer and a 7.5 Ω sense resistor. Hiccup capacitance is 3.3 nF. Type 2A compensation targets a 10 kHz crossover and uses 40.2 kΩ RCOMP, 15 nF CCOMP, and 47 pF CHF. Seven 330 µF polymer-tantalum capacitors provide the selected output capacitance, and a 102 kΩ RSC resistor sets slope compensation.

The controller supply range is 4–14 V and requires at least a 0.1 µF VIN-to-AVSS bypass capacitor, preferably X5R or better. Recommended layout practices include separating feedback and control signals from magnetics and the switch node, minimizing high-dv/dt and high-di/dt loops, connecting analog and power grounds at one point, using short and wide high-current traces, placing filtering and compensation components near their pins, filtering the CS_ILIM signal when required, and connecting CFP-package backside metallization to AVSS through multiple vias.

The team called its playoff loss disappointing, saying second-period lapses cost the game despite a strong third period and late chances. They need more consistent play over all 60 minutes and must generate their own chances. Both goaltenders performed well. A player returning after missing recent games provided energy and momentum, while the team emphasized containing a skilled, physical opponent. They will build on their recent home play and avoid discouragement.

A roundup covers DomTerm’s browser-engine GUI toolkit, open source’s MIT print-jam origins, container runtimes, and the 1998 coinage of “open source software.” It also features a Linux-based school program that kept more than 200 old computers running and recognizes community contributors.

Fourth-grader Lexi Bergeron raised $11 in her first week selling handmade fidget toys, inspiring her mother to create a GoFundMe campaign to cover lunch debts at her Grand Haven, Michigan, school.
