The article advocates an ecological, sociocultural perspective on foreign-language education, arguing that learning must be understood within the social, cultural, economic, and institutional contexts of schools and communities. Using Malaysia and Thailand as principal examples, it reviews how curriculum goals, national languages, teacher proficiency, classroom practices, and socioeconomic inequalities shape English education.

Both countries use CEFR-aligned proficiency targets and centrally mandated communicative language teaching, often designed around conditions found in advantaged urban schools. Outcomes remain unequal: rural and lower-income learners generally achieve less because they have fewer opportunities to use English, less home and school support, and fewer educational resources. Malaysia’s targets exceeded most learners’ baseline proficiency, while Thailand’s low national examination scores and regional disparities similarly reflected wider economic inequalities.

National identity and everyday language use also constrain English learning. Malay and Thai remain dominant in many learners’ homes and communities, and English is not generally necessary for routine communication. Consequently, some students achieve examination success without becoming confident oral users.

Teacher assessments reveal further problems. Many Malaysian and Thai teachers have limited English proficiency, and some Malaysian English teachers were trained in other subjects. Standardized CEFR-based tests measure proficiency but not pedagogical effectiveness and may disadvantage teachers whose own language education was restricted.

Classroom research shows that communicative and learner-centred mandates conflict with large classes, mixed abilities, limited resources, examination pressure, curriculum demands, and learners’ low proficiency. Teachers consequently adapt methods, sometimes using learners’ first languages or returning to teacher-centred instruction, rather than simply failing to implement policy. The article concludes that curriculum outcomes and teaching methods should be aligned with local sociolinguistic realities and institutional capacity, with policymakers consulting teachers and students before prescribing programmes.

Plasmodium vivax and P. ovale can remain dormant in liver cells and later cause relapsing bloodstream infections. Radical cure requires 8-aminoquinoline drugs, which can cause haemolytic toxicity in people with G6PD deficiency, while the mechanisms and triggers of hypnozoite activation remain poorly understood. The work derives analytical likelihoods for an “exponential clock” model in which hypnozoites activate independently at a constant rate, incorporating variation in mosquito bites, inoculum size, sporozoite destiny, age-related immunity, and treatment-related prophylaxis. The model was fitted to daily longitudinal data from the SPf66 trial, in which 1,344 children aged 2–15 years on the Thailand–Myanmar border were followed for 21 months.

The model reproduced recurrent vivax malaria across age groups and estimated a hypnozoite activation rate of 1/171 per day, corresponding to a 118-day half-life. The estimated mean successful sporozoite inoculum was 6.9 per infectious bite, with about 2.7 hypnozoites per bite. Relapses were estimated to occur 3.4 times as often as primary infections, comprising roughly 75% of symptomatic vivax episodes. The model predicts shorter initial inter-relapse intervals followed by lengthening intervals as the hypnozoite reservoir declines, overdispersed hypnozoite burdens in low-transmission settings, and a nonlinear relationship between age and symptomatic relapse.

Higher-than-expected vivax incidence after artesunate-treated falciparum monoinfections was compatible with an external triggering mechanism. Mefloquine provided approximately one month of protection against emerging relapses, potentially masking such effects because most falciparum episodes received artesunate–mefloquine therapy.

Researchers found two strains of bacteria from grape leaves that can degrade guaiacol, a volatile phenol linked to wildfire smoke taint in wine. In petri-dish tests, both strains nearly eliminated guaiacol within 96 hours, while deleting a degradation-related gene prevented one strain from consuming it. The bacteria did not grow on other smoky compounds, so different bacterial types may be needed to address additional causes of smoke taint. Researchers suggest the grape microbiome could offer a more targeted alternative to filtration, which can also remove desirable wine components, though further research is needed. Western U.S. and Canadian winemakers lost more than $3 billion from wildfire damage and unusable grapes in 2020.

NVIDIA Corporation reported results for the third quarter of fiscal 2020, ended October 27, 2019. Quarterly revenue was $3.014 billion, down 5% from $3.181 billion a year earlier but up 17% sequentially. Gross margin increased to 63.6% from 60.4% year over year and 59.8% sequentially, primarily due to improved GeForce GPU margins, lower component costs, sales of previously written-off components, and higher average selling prices. Operating expenses rose 15% to $989 million, primarily due to personnel, compensation, infrastructure, and stock-based compensation. Operating income fell 12% to $927 million, while net income declined 27% to $899 million and diluted EPS fell 26% to $1.45.

For the first nine months, revenue was $7.813 billion, down 18% from $9.511 billion. Gross profit was $4.753 billion, operating income was $1.856 billion, net income was $1.845 billion, and diluted EPS was $2.99, compared with $5.964 billion, $3.510 billion, $3.575 billion, and $5.71, respectively, in the prior-year period.

GPU revenue was $2.565 billion in the quarter, down 8% year over year but up 22% sequentially, with $1.135 billion in operating income. Tegra Processor revenue was $449 million, up 10% year over year and down 5% sequentially, with $85 million in operating income. By platform, quarterly revenue was $1.659 billion for Gaming, $726 million for Data Center, $324 million for Professional Visualization, $162 million for Automotive, and $143 million for OEM and Other. Gaming and Data Center declined year over year, while Professional Visualization increased. Gross margin was affected by product transitions and mix, partly offset by previously written-off GeForce component sales.

As of October 27, 2019, NVIDIA held $9.769 billion in cash, cash equivalents, and marketable securities, compared with $7.422 billion at January 27, 2019. Total assets were $15.810 billion, total liabilities were $4.596 billion, and shareholders’ equity was $11.214 billion. Inventory declined to $1.047 billion from $1.575 billion. Nine-month operating cash flow was $3.296 billion, investing activities provided $6.296 billion, and financing activities used $609 million. Long-term debt totaled $1.990 billion, consisting of $1 billion of 2.20% notes due 2021 and $1 billion of 3.20% notes due 2026. No amounts had been borrowed under the $575 million revolving credit facility or commercial paper program.

NVIDIA paid $292 million in dividends during the first nine months. It intended to return $3 billion to shareholders by the end of fiscal 2020, including $700 million of fourth-quarter fiscal 2019 repurchases, and planned to return the remaining $2.01 billion through dividends and repurchases. No repurchases were expected before the Mellanox acquisition closed, and the company remained authorized to repurchase up to $7.24 billion through December 2022.

NVIDIA agreed on March 10, 2019, to acquire Mellanox Technologies for $125 per share in cash, representing an enterprise value of approximately $6.9 billion. Mellanox shareholders approved the transaction, and regulatory approval had been received in the United States and Mexico, while European and Chinese reviews were continuing. The company expected the acquisition to close in early 2020 and could owe a $350 million termination fee under certain circumstances.

The company adopted the new lease accounting standard on January 28, 2019, recognizing $470 million of operating lease assets and $500 million of lease liabilities. Stock-based compensation was $223 million for the quarter and $624 million for the first nine months. An expected-credit-loss standard was not yet adopted and was not expected to have a material impact.

NVIDIA reported securities and derivative litigation concerning alleged statements about channel inventory and cryptocurrency mining effects on GPU demand, along with two later Delaware derivative lawsuits. It had filed a motion to dismiss the consolidated securities complaint and recorded no contingency accrual because losses were not considered probable. Shareholder litigation relating to the Mellanox acquisition had been voluntarily dismissed by October 14, 2019.

NVIDIA reported two operating segments, GPU and Tegra Processor. Revenue from outside the United States represented 92% of quarterly and nine-month revenue. One customer accounted for approximately 10% of third-quarter revenue and 11% of nine-month revenue, while representing 24% of accounts receivable. NVIDIA also reported sufficient liquidity to meet operating requirements for at least the next twelve months and no material off-balance-sheet arrangements.

This observational UK Biobank study analyzed 451,355 participants, including 22,451 (4.9%) with diabetes, stratified by ethnicity-specific normal, overweight, and obese BMI categories. Multimodality imaging assessed carotid intima-media thickness, arterial stiffness, left ventricular ejection fraction, cardiac contractility, and body composition; cardiovascular outcomes were followed for a median of 12 years.

Among participants without diabetes, increasing BMI was associated with greater CIMT, arterial stiffness, and cardiac contractility index and lower ejection fraction. These associations were less pronounced among participants with diabetes, who showed adverse cardiovascular phenotypes across BMI categories. Diabetes was also associated with greater visceral adiposity and adverse metabolic measures within each BMI class.

During 5,3 million person-years of follow-up, myocardial infarction, ischaemic stroke, cardiovascular mortality, and all-cause mortality increased with rising BMI, with substantially higher rates among participants with diabetes. Compared with normal-weight participants without diabetes, adjusted cardiovascular mortality IRRs were 2.45 for normal-weight diabetes, 2.90 for overweight diabetes, and 4.34 for obese diabetes; normal-weight diabetes had greater cardiovascular mortality than obesity without diabetes.

Adiposity measures correlated more strongly with cardiovascular biomarkers than diabetes duration or HbA1c, although all correlations were weak, indicating that additional factors may contribute to the elevated risk associated with normal-weight diabetes. Limitations included incomplete phenotyping, survivor bias among imaging participants, lack of stratification by diabetes type, observational design, recruitment before widespread use of SGLT2 inhibitors, and limited UK Biobank representativeness. The authors concluded that obesity and diabetes are additively associated with adverse cardiovascular phenotypes and outcomes and that more refined risk assessment and preventive strategies are needed.

The New York Supreme Court denied Yuk Bui Yee’s motion to sever a 13-count indictment arising from six allegedly extortionate incidents at three Chinese restaurants over two months. The court applied CPL 200.20(2)(b), which permits joinder of offenses arising from different transactions when proof of one offense would be material and admissible in chief at trial of another. The court lacked authority to sever offenses joinable under that provision.

The incidents were grouped by restaurant. Group A involved nine counts arising from three visits to the Sye-Chow restaurant in December. Group B involved two counts from a January visit to Mr. Chaing’s Chinatown restaurant. Group C involved two counts from two February visits to Mr. Pan’s restaurant on the lower east side.

Applying the evidentiary principles associated with *Molineux*, the court found evidence from the other offenses relevant to common scheme, identity, and intent. Repetition alone did not establish a common scheme, although the incidents within Groups A and C supported an overall plan; the evidence did not establish a common scheme encompassing all three groups. A distinctive modus operandi—speaking Mandarin, demanding money for “brothers,” and claiming membership in the Chinatown Eagles—made the defendant’s identity in one incident probative of his identity in others. Because the demands did not necessarily establish criminal intent, evidence of earlier extortionate conduct could prove knowledge and intent regarding the later incidents.

Accordingly, all 13 counts were joinable under CPL 200.20(2)(b), and severance was denied. The court did not decide whether some counts were also joinable under subdivision 2(a), and its preliminary evidentiary ruling did not bind the trial judge.

A community-based study in central China examined associations between arterial stiffness, measured by brachial-ankle pulse wave velocity (baPWV), and renal function. Cross-sectional analyses included 67,060 adults, while longitudinal analyses included 12,324. Lower eGFR was significantly associated with higher baPWV. Among participants without baseline CKD, incident CKD increased across baPWV tertiles (18.68%, 27.11%, and 54.11%); the highest baPWV tertile remained associated with incident CKD after adjustment (HR 2.17, 95% CI 1.26–3.76). Lowest eGFR was also associated with increased risk of arterial stiffness (HR 1.21, 95% CI 1.02–1.44). Cross-lagged analysis indicated that declining kidney function preceded subsequent increases in arterial stiffness. The authors proposed a vicious cycle in which arterial stiffness may promote renal injury and dysfunctional kidneys may accelerate vascular stiffening. Limitations included use of creatinine-based eGFR rather than the 51Cr-EDTA reference method and restriction of the observational population to central China.

This case study examined whether repeated lateral spinal cord stimulation (SCS) could restore missing-limb sensation and alter muscle activity during walking. The participant was a woman aged 60–65 with a five-year-old unilateral transtibial amputation due to diabetic neuropathy and dysvascular disease. Percutaneous SCS leads were implanted for 84 days, and stimulation was delivered during the prosthetic limb’s stance phase, with amplitude modulated by plantar pressure.

Surface electromyography and motion capture showed that, after multiple weeks of in-lab SCS, residual-limb tensor fasciae latae and vastus lateralis activity increased, while biceps femoris activity decreased slightly. Residual knee-antagonist co-contraction fell significantly from 1.57 at the early unstimulated assessment to 1.05 later without stimulation and 0.95 with stimulation. Pelvic obliquity range-of-motion and residual-limb pelvic drop also increased significantly relative to the early assessment. Muscle-activation timing remained largely similar between stimulated and unstimulated walking, with cross-correlations above 90%.

The findings suggest that repeated SCS-mediated sensory feedback may improve dynamic knee and hip stability by reducing compensatory knee co-contraction and increasing hip-abductor activity. However, many improvements were present even without stimulation at the later assessment, and the single-participant case study cannot establish causality or generalizability.

The study introduced SCIseg, an open-source deep-learning method for jointly segmenting the spinal cord and T2-weighted hyperintense lesions in volumetric MRI. The retrospective cohort included 191 patients and 231 scans from three sites, covering traumatic and ischemic injuries, pre- and postoperative cases, multiple scanners, orientations, resolutions, and field strengths. A three-phase region-based training strategy incorporated human-in-the-loop active learning and diverse multi-site data, producing a final training set of 196 scans.

On independent test sets, SCIseg 3D achieved spinal-cord Dice scores of 0.90 at Site 1 and 0.94 at Site 2, outperforming baseline methods. Lesion Dice scores were 0.48 and 0.76, respectively; the 3D model significantly outperformed its 2D version across all metrics. Performance was lower at Site 1, where metal artifacts, varying injury phases, and differing lesion intensity complicated segmentation. Active learning improved agreement between predicted and manual lesion volume and length measurements.

The model also produced reasonable segmentations in unseen degenerative cervical myelopathy cases, including severe spinal-cord compression. Automatically derived lesion biomarkers did not differ significantly from manual measurements and showed significant correlations with clinical scores. Limitations include training on only T2-weighted images and treating edema and hemorrhage as part of a single lesion class. The code is available through the Spinal Cord Toolbox and the study’s GitHub repository.

Athletes Unlimited (AU) is a startup sports network, launched in March 2020 as a public benefit corporation, that operates player-led women's professional leagues. The case describes the company's origins, model, growth, and open strategic questions.

**Context.** Historically, women's professional team sports leagues have been fragile—underfunded, short-term in outlook, often borrowing business models built for men's sports. Purdue/USC research found women's sports received 5.4% of televised news and highlights in 2019 (3.5% excluding the Women's World Cup), while salaries were low (e.g., under $10,000 in some leagues) and many players held second jobs or played overseas. The NBA-backed WNBA was the notable exception, breaking the "start and stop" cycle by planning beyond a single season.

**Founding and research.** Jon Patricof (former president of NYCFC and Tribeca Enterprises) and Jonathan Soros (CEO of JS Capital) met for brunch in December 2018, where Soros proposed building "a new league altogether" rather than buying existing teams. Facing industry skepticism ("It's a mess"), they relied on intuition, conviction, and data. The Sports Innovation Lab's 2019 report *The Fluid Fan* supported their model: fans follow players more than teams, care about organizational values and athletes' off-field stories, and consume sports across multiple platforms. They consulted figures including former NBA commissioner David Stern and NPF commissioner Cheri Kempf. Pre-launch research defined AU's target audience (29% of the general population): white, high-income, suburban men aged 25–44 in the Northeast and South, with women a significant segment.

**Player partnership.** On October 7, 2019, Patricof and Soros met four softball players—Gwen Svekis, Victoria Hayward, Haylie Wagner, and Jade Rhodes—in the JS Capital offices. The session ran nearly three hours, shifting from pitch to collaborative brainstorming, and the players were hired as consultants who met weekly with Patricof, Soros, Ana Drucker, and Kempf through early 2020. Victoria Hayward was the first player signed, in November 2019; 56 players were recruited for a four-team softball league.

**Launch and expansion.** AU announced its launch March 3, 2020, and played its first softball game August 29, 2020, in Rosemont, Illinois, with no fans due to COVID-19—with ESPN and CBS contracts and Nike and Carvana partnerships in place. Because other leagues cancelled, AU was the only professional softball league operating anywhere in 2020. Volleyball and lacrosse launched in 2021, basketball in 2022.

**The model.** Each league is player-led: no owners (a board of directors of investor representatives, one athlete, and one independent director), no coaches (only facilitators), and a five-member Player Executive Committee (PEC) per sport making decisions on format, venue, schedule, uniforms, anthem, player recruitment, and discipline. Teams are reshuffled via weekly drafts; seasons last five weeks at a single venue; and an individual leaderboard (modeled on Formula 1) assigns points for plays, with the top weekly scorer serving as next week's team captain and season top scorer crowned champion. PECs also drove social-impact initiatives, including the "Power in My Voice" program (virtual bookstores, a Women's Wall, voter registration), a decision to remain in Texas after new state laws, and basketball's use of "Lift Every Voice and Sing."

**Mission and economics.** As a PBC, AU must consider stakeholder interests. Its "Mission Equity" structure caps investor returns, with at least 50% of surplus going to players' Profit Participation Plan; players receive roughly $10,000 base pay plus performance bonuses and 20-year profit-participation shares, avoiding the "Billie Jean King" problem. AU provides meals, laundry, trainers, childcare, parental leave, and does not require pregnancy disclosure. Athletes compete for nonprofits through the Athlete Causes Program, with 50% of bonuses matched to the player's charity. AU also runs youth clinics to broaden participation, especially in lacrosse.

**Results.** Over 200 athletes played across four sports. AU secured distribution with ESPN, CBS Sports Network, Fox, Bally Sports, and the WBNA's streaming platform, and assembled an advisory board including Kevin Durant, Sheryl Swoopes, Abby Wambach, and Caroline Wozniacki. It raised $30 million in September 2022 and, in March 2023, became the first women's sports league named one of Fast Company's 10 most innovative companies in sports. A late-2022 survey of nearly 1,500 fans found ~70% watched via live television and 61% via streaming, 87% favorably rated athlete storytelling, 95% saw AU's approach as innovative, and over 70% called it more exciting than existing leagues; softball led in viewership and merchandise sales.

**Open questions.** As a startup, AU must determine whether and how it can scale to economic sustainability, which additional sports to add amid new competition (Women's Pro Fastpitch in 2022; Pro Volleyball Federation and LOVB expected in 2024), whether to keep prioritizing broadcast and storytelling versus the in-person experience, and what other strategies could accelerate growth while preserving its player-driven mission.

This continuation patent disclosure concerns trigger-based random access and resource-unit allocation in IEEE 802.11 wireless networks with multiple BSSIDs. An access point may operate a transmitted BSSID (Tx BSSID) and multiple non-transmitted BSSIDs, assign association identifier (AID) values to stations, and use a group-AID mapping in a traffic indication map (TIM) partial virtual bitmap to identify stations and BSSIDs. Trigger frames may allocate dedicated resource units to individual stations or contention-based random resource units to associated stations, selected non-Tx BSSIDs using their BSSID indices, or all unassociated stations using AID 2045. Management frames may include Multiple BSSID, non-Tx BSSID capabilities, Multiple BSSID-index, FMS descriptor, and random-access parameter elements. The disclosed access-point and station implementations coordinate virtual access points, decode TIM and trigger-frame information, and allocate resources according to factors including BSS population, traffic class, flow priority, security, access privileges, device type, quality of service, and latency. The stated goals are to improve fairness, shared-medium utilization, and resource-allocation efficiency.

The CAT offense uses a 2-1-2 spread and sharp passing against traps, double teams, and zone presses, with a skilled triple-threat post in the middle. Guangdong Province is confronting China’s largest documented chikungunya outbreak, with more than 4,000 confirmed infections since late July. Shunde District in Foshan accounts for over 3,600 cases, and infections have also been reported in Guangzhou, Shenzhen, Hong Kong, and Macao. The mosquito-borne disease causes fever and severe joint pain but does not spread directly between people. Authorities are promoting removal of standing water to reduce Aedes mosquito breeding. The editorial links the outbreak’s spread to climate change, urbanization, and international travel, and says WHO has issued new clinical guidance and strengthened its Global Arbovirus Initiative. It recommends expanded genomic surveillance, community participation, and international coordination. Chikungunya can cause prolonged arthritis-like symptoms, fatigue, and recurring pain. There is no licensed vaccine or specific antiviral treatment, so care focuses on symptom relief and prevention.

The study implements a Julia-based minorization-maximization algorithm for maximum and restricted maximum likelihood estimation in multivariate variance components linear mixed models. It supports more than two phenotypes and variance components while offering numerical stability, rapid convergence, and compatibility with positive semidefiniteness constraints. Applying the method to PsychENCODE gene and isoform expression data, the authors partitioned genetic effects and covariance into cis- and trans-SNPs. Local variants had sparse but large effects, whereas distal variants had small individual but large collective effects. Isoform analyses identified substantially more genetic signals than gene-level analyses, including signals associated with increased autism spectrum disorder risk, suggesting potential to uncover disease genes and improve interpretation of GWAS results.

The paper introduces Solvent Data-Driven Embeddings (SoDaDE), a transformer-based fingerprint designed to improve solvent representations for reaction modelling and solvent selection. The model was pre-trained on the Spange dataset of 191 solvents and up to 12 molecular properties. Data augmentation shuffled property-value pairs to create up to 12! sequences per solvent, while causal, prediction, and missing-value masks enabled masked-property prediction. Solvent types, ChemBERTa fingerprints, and numerical properties were combined as model inputs.

SoDaDE was evaluated on solvent-property prediction and the Catechol Benchmark for reaction outcomes with single solvents and solvent mixtures. It achieved an average test MSE of 0.170, outperforming random forest (0.550), Gaussian process (0.335), and training-set averages (4.23). On the Catechol Benchmark, tuned and untuned SoDaDE obtained full-data MSEs of 0.0026 and 0.0029, respectively, and single-solvent MSEs of 0.0044, outperforming all compared representations. The results indicate that SoDaDE captures general solvent features, performs well for mixtures, and can be effective even when trained on a small dataset.

This MIT OpenCourseWare lecture (Alan V. Oppenheim) continues the study of discrete-time systems, building on the previously introduced conditions of linearity and shift invariance, which yield the convolution sum representation. The lecture's main topics are: (1) two additional properties to consider for discrete-time systems—stability and causality; (2) linear constant-coefficient difference equations; and (3) the frequency response as an alternative to the time-domain convolution representation.

For general systems, stability means bounded input sequences produce bounded output sequences; for linear shift-invariant (LSI) systems this is equivalent to the unit sample response being absolutely summable. Examples are given: h[n] = 2ⁿu[n] is unstable, while h[n] = (1/2)ⁿu[n] is stable. Causality means the output does not anticipate future input values; for LSI systems it is equivalent to h[n] = 0 for n < 0. The example h[n] = 2ⁿu[−n] is stable but noncausal. Oppenheim stresses that causality is useful to inquire about but not always desirable to impose (many useful noncausal systems exist), whereas unstable systems are generally less useful than noncausal ones.

The lecture then briefly introduces systems describable by linear constant-coefficient difference equations—the discrete-time analog of constant-coefficient differential equations—where the order refers to the number of delays in the output sequence. For the 0th-order case the equation reduces to the convolution sum, so the unit sample response is simply the input coefficients. For the first-order equation y[n] − a·y[n−1] = x[n], iterative solution with a unit sample input yields the causal impulse response aⁿu[n] (stable when |a| < 1), while the alternative boundary condition h[n] = 0 for n > 0, obtained by iterating backwards, gives −aⁿu[−n−1], which is unstable for |a| < 1. Hence a difference equation alone does not uniquely specify a system; initial/boundary conditions are required, and they must be consistent with a zero input producing zero output.

Finally, the frequency response representation is introduced, based on the fact that complex exponentials are eigenfunctions of LSI systems: a complex exponential input yields an output of the same functional form multiplied by H(e^{jω}) = Σ h[k]e^{−jωk}. For sinusoidal excitations, the magnitude of H(e^{jω}) gives the change in amplitude and its angle gives the phase shift, identical to the continuous-time case. For the causal first-order system, H(e^{jω}) = 1/(1 − ae^{−jω}), with magnitude 1/(1 + a² − 2a cos ω) and a phase given by an arctangent term. Two key properties are highlighted: ω is a continuous variable, and the frequency response is periodic in ω with period 2π, because complex exponentials repeat every 2π. The lecture closes by previewing the Fourier transform as the generalization of the frequency response.

GameStop will ship at least five Nintendo Switch consoles to each of its 4,400 U.S. stores, available in-store by August 16. Online sales remain bundle-only; Target and tracking services have occasionally had units.

The lecture introduces electromagnetic self-emission from plasmas as both a cooling mechanism and a diagnostic tool. Plasma radiation spans radio frequencies through X-rays and gamma rays, so different wavelengths may require wave or ray-based treatments. Studying a plasma’s emitted spectrum, location, and time variation can reveal its internal conditions.

Radiation transport is presented as the framework for interpreting these measurements. Radiation emitted in one region may be absorbed elsewhere, producing nonlocal energy transfer that can be difficult to model; diffusive transport is often assumed but is not always valid. The fundamental transport equation relates the change in spectral radiance along a path to emission minus absorption. Spectral radiance is defined with units of power per area, solid angle, and spectral unit. Emissivity and opacity generally vary with position and frequency. The equation is commonly solved independently for each frequency, neglecting effects such as fluorescence that transfer energy between frequencies. Radiation paths may curve because of refractive-index variations, although straight paths are often used.

Optical depth, defined by integrating opacity along the path, provides a useful reformulation of the transport equation. Its solution separates attenuated incident radiation from radiation emitted within the plasma, with the latter attenuated according to where it originated. In optically thin plasma, the outgoing radiation is dominated by the incident intensity and added emission is weak. In optically thick plasma, the initial radiation is effectively erased and the outgoing intensity is set by the source function. For blackbody equilibrium, the source function equals the Planck function, yielding Kirchhoff’s relation between emissivity and opacity. Calculating emissivity requires plasma properties such as density and temperature.

Optical thickness is distinguished from wave cutoff. Optical thickness results from absorption and gradually reduces an oscillating wave’s amplitude. At cutoff, the wave is reflected and the electric field becomes evanescent, decaying without oscillation; this transition occurs suddenly at a critical density. A wave can nevertheless couple across a finite evanescent region and resume oscillating beyond it.

The lecture then uses the Poynting vector to illustrate radiation from charged particles. A stationary charge has no Poynting flux, while a charge moving uniformly merely carries its near fields with it. Acceleration produces outward-propagating radiation. The exact moving-charge field contains near- and far-field terms: the near-field contribution does not carry constant power with distance, whereas the far field falls as inverse distance squared in Poynting flux and constitutes propagating radiation. Because particles in magnetic fields accelerate as they spiral, they emit radiation. A full plasma treatment requires solving particle motion and integrating over the velocity distribution, but the course will quote established results. Cyclotron emission will be considered first, followed by other free- and bound-electron mechanisms, with diagnostic instruments such as bolometers, pinhole cameras, and spectrometers discussed alongside them.

**Summary**

The passage describes "MMFP-Tableau," a bioinformatics and data visualization platform developed in the Mitochondrial Medicine Frontier Program (MMFP) at the Children's Hospital of Philadelphia (CHOP) to support precision medicine in rare disorders such as primary mitochondrial disease (PMD).

**Background/rationale:** Health care data from clinical care, clinical research, and translational research are generated in siloed formats; EMR data are especially complex due to rich phenotypic data in free text and variable provider input, which impedes interoperability and data mining.

**Methods:** The platform centrally extracts, unifies, cleans, and integrates data from the CHOP EMR (EPIC), REDCap research databases, survey software, and Excel spreadsheets using Alteryx workflows (macros, SQL pulls, scheduled API extraction, HPO/ICD-10/SNOMED phenotype mapping), which stage, transform, and load data before pushing it to Tableau for secure, role-based, HIPAA-compliant visualization behind an institutional firewall. Data extraction was limited to MMFP patients consented under IRB protocol #08-6177. An interdisciplinary team reviewed visualizations for discrepancies and optimization.

**Results:** MMFP-Tableau integrates data from over 2,000 individuals. Use cases include: clinical cohort characterization (e.g., seizures in Leigh syndrome spectrum with PRO measures); clinical trial eligibility determination (including ambulatory status); genotype-phenotype mapping by causal gene; medication trend visualization by therapeutic class and phenotype; and risk factor delineation (GFR, creatinine, lactate).

**Discussion/limitations:** The platform replaced manual chart reviews, improved EMR documentation practices (more discrete fields), enhanced data integrity and biospecimen tracking, and may facilitate institutional and industry collaboration. Limitations include inaccessible non-discretized EMR data, separately housed imaging (PACS), unparsable scanned PDFs, inability to automate external institutional data (future FHIR integration), and server performance issues. Future work includes predictive diagnostics and scaling to new cohorts.

**Conclusion:** MMFP-Tableau offers a scalable, generalizable paradigm for centralized, standardized clinical and research data access and dynamic visualization, replicable across disease types and cohorts.

Blackwell’s ninth-generation NVENC encoder improves AV1 and HEVC quality by 5% in BD-BR PSNR and adds 4:2:2 H.264 and HEVC encoding. An AV1 Ultra High Quality mode provides another 5% improvement, with combined AV1 gains reaching up to 15%. The RTX 5090 supports three encoders and two decoders, increasing export speeds by more than 50% generation over generation and fourfold versus a single-encoder RTX 3090. Blackwell’s sixth-generation NVDEC doubles H.264 decoding speed, matches HEVC and AV1 speeds, and supports 4:2:2 H.264 and HEVC. DisplayPort 2.1b provides up to 80 Gbps via UHBR 20, enabling 8K at 165Hz or 4K at 480Hz with DSC and a certified DP80LL cable.

Blackwell’s Max-Q design uses advanced clock, power, and rail gating, separate voltage rails for GPU cores and memory, and faster power-state transitions. Clocks adapt to workloads 1,000 times faster than earlier architectures, while the deepest sleep state is entered ten times faster than on Ada. In a small-language-model inference example, these improvements produced power savings of up to 50%.

DLSS 4 adds Multi Frame Generation, which creates up to three additional frames per traditionally rendered frame. Its frame-generation model runs 40% faster, uses 30% less VRAM, and runs once per rendered frame; enhanced Flip Metering improves pacing consistency. DLSS 4 also replaces convolutional models with transformer-based models for Super Resolution, Ray Reconstruction, and Deep Learning Anti-Aliasing, improving temporal stability, motion detail, lighting, anti-aliasing, and denoising artifacts.

Blackwell also introduces neural shaders, which use AI to approximate complex rendering calculations. Cooperative Vectors for DirectX 12 and Vulkan allow graphics shaders to access Tensor Cores. Potential applications include neural texture compression, RTX Neural Materials, Neural Radiance Cache, RTX Skin, and RTX Neural Faces. Neural texture compression can provide up-to-seven-to-one VRAM compression over block-compressed formats; in one demo, neural materials reduced storage from 1,110 MB to 333 MB. Neural Radiance Cache trains small networks on live game data to infer indirect lighting, while Neural Faces uses a TensorRT-optimized generative model to infer realistic faces from rasterized faces and 3D pose data.

The architecture includes GB202, GB203, and GB205 GPUs. Full GB202 has 92.2 billion transistors, 24,576 CUDA cores, 192 RT cores, 768 Tensor cores, and a 512-bit memory interface; GB203 has 45.6 billion transistors, 10,752 CUDA cores, 84 RT cores, 336 Tensor cores, and a 256-bit interface; GB205 has 31 billion transistors, 6,400 CUDA cores, 50 RT cores, 200 Tensor cores, and a 192-bit interface. The Trump administration backed off 100% tariffs on branded pharmaceuticals threatened to start Oct. 1. A White House official said the levies did not take effect and that tariffs would be prepared for companies that neither build U.S. infrastructure nor make drug-pricing agreements, with no new timeline. The head and shoulders pattern is a technical-analysis formation signaling a potential price reversal. A regular pattern comprises three rallies and two pullbacks: a left shoulder, a higher central head, and a right shoulder near the first shoulder’s level. The line connecting the two intervening lows is the neckline. It is generally bearish, suggesting an uptrend may reverse into a downtrend, and is confirmed when price breaks below the neckline. Traders may close long positions or go short, with a possible stop-loss above the right shoulder. A profit target can be estimated by projecting the head-to-neckline height downward from the neckline.

The inverted head and shoulders, or head and shoulders bottom, reverses these characteristics. It has three swing lows separated by two swing highs, is considered bullish, and is confirmed by a break above its neckline. A stop-loss may be placed below the right shoulder or at the neckline.

The passage says fully objective backtesting rules are difficult to establish. As a proxy, it cites Thomas Bulkowski’s study of 500 stocks over five years. His regular-pattern sample of 431 formations produced 30 false signals and a reported 93% success rate, with an average decline of 23%. For inverted formations, he reported very few false signals and expected returns of 20–30% within 73 days. Volume and neckline direction were not considered decisive, though an inverted-pattern breakout was recommended on high volume.

Bulkowski argued that regular patterns could be traded before a neckline breakdown, while inverted patterns could sometimes be bought before confirmation. However, the authors caution that these findings relied on after-the-fact analysis and should be approached cautiously. The passage also notes a 1995 Federal Reserve report that found technical analysis, including head and shoulders, could generate statistically significant profits.

House of Fraser’s pre-tax profit rose from £1.3 million to £3.4 million; revenue was flat, while online sales rose 16.1%. It warned trading remains volatile, plans to discontinue five underperforming brands, and recently opened its first standalone shop in China, in Nanjing.

The passage outlines defensive strategies against the Base Cross offense, which uses a larger screener against a smaller player and emphasizes quick ball reversals. In Basic NBA Show & Recover, defenders avoid switching: the screener’s defender forces the post wide, another defender trails over the screen into a front position, and weak-side defenders pack toward the basket. The post is then defended straight up while help remains packed.

All Out SOS Disruption traps the ball handler on the wing before a post entry. Its Hi-Lo Switch directs defenders to switch when the cutter goes low or baseline but not when the cutter goes high. Defenders trap, front the post, rotate as the ball moves, close out to shooters, deny return and reversal passes, and establish help-side positions.

ExxonMobil launched an unusually public marketing effort in Dongying, China, to win business from independent “teapot” refiners. The study introduces automatic detection of “hype”—hyperbolic or subjective language used to glamorize, promote, embellish, or exaggerate research—as an NLP task for biomedical texts. Because promotional intent depends on context, the authors developed six-step annotation guidelines covering positive value judgments, hyperbolic or gratuitous wording, amplification, adjective coordination, and broader sentence context. Three researchers annotated 550 sentences containing 11 novelty-related adjectives drawn from NIH grant abstracts for 2016–2020. Discussion resolved 106 of 119 disagreements, producing a final dataset of 537 sentences: 392 labeled Hype and 145 Not Hype. Agreement increased to pairwise Cohen’s kappa values of 0.94–0.98.

The authors framed detection as binary text classification and evaluated traditional classifiers, fine-tuned pretrained language models, and prompted large language models. Frozen models and most traditional methods performed poorly, while fine-tuning substantially improved results. Fine-tuned BERT performed best, reaching 0.861 accuracy and 0.854 F1, slightly exceeding a blind human baseline with 0.824 accuracy and 0.821 F1. GPT-4O-MINI with a broad prompt performed on par with the human baseline, whereas LLaMA3.1-Instruct performed worst overall.

The results indicate that context, domain knowledge, and temporal awareness are important because some adjectives may be promotional in one setting but justified in another. Limitations include subjective perception, coverage of only one adjective group, a small dataset drawn from nearly a million NIH abstracts, focus on biomedical English, and limited computing capacity. Proposed future work includes expanding guidelines and lexicons, scaling annotation and evaluation, studying other hype categories and languages, and developing tools to flag or edit promotional language.

DuBard School was one of four U.S. schools recognized by IMSLEC for multisensory structured language education. Its DuBard Association Method teaches reading, speaking and writing and serves as the national training site.

A father’s attempt to advise his 28-year-old son about a workplace conflict prompted an angry, defensive reaction and uncertainty about how to help. Dr. Ruth Nemzoff says parents should consider their own biases, each child’s personality and circumstances, and the current workplace environment before offering career advice. To encourage constructive conversations, parents should ask whether the child wants advice or simply to vent, begin with nonjudgmental questions, acknowledge the child’s greater familiarity with the situation, and share relevant career mistakes. They should help children identify the problem and next practical step, suggest an objective third party when appropriate—including a therapist for serious concerns such as depression or addiction—and avoid imposing solutions. Most importantly, parents should not expect their advice to be followed or resent a child for rejecting it.

Nike’s “Considered” strategy was created to embed environmental responsibility into product design and manufacturing while preserving performance, aesthetics, and profitability. The initiative followed Nike’s early-1990s labor crisis, which led it to make corporate responsibility a core business function in 1998. Although Nike had launched environmental programs using climate-neutral nitrogen, water-based adhesives, sustainability training, and metrics, environmental responsibility remained separate from everyday business decisions.

After Hannah Jones became corporate responsibility vice president in 2004, she found that leaders viewed the function as an external moral policing force rather than a source of business value. Jones introduced an “ROI2” approach combining financial and corporate-responsibility returns, with the goal of institutionalizing sustainability in Nike’s business model. Product design was identified as a key intervention point because designers could address environmental problems before materials were sourced and products manufactured.

In late 2005, Mark Parker, Jones, and footwear design vice president John Hoke formed the 14-person Considered Group. It became an internal hub for environmental knowledge, footprint analysis, tools, training, and support, while leaving sustainability decisions primarily with designers. Nike’s tightly timed, complex development process created a need for practical guidance, particularly for product teams balancing cost, performance, manufacturing, margin, and environmental goals.

After 18 months of development, the Considered Index was introduced in September 2007 as an intranet scoring system. It predictively rated footwear during development using three equally weighted areas: environmentally preferred materials, bonding methods, and manufacturing waste, plus points for innovations that reduced footprints beyond a single product. Materials were evaluated for factors such as toxicity, energy and water use, recycled content, recyclability, and supply-chain responsibility. Mechanical bonding ranked above water-based cement, which ranked above solvent-based cement. Waste scores emphasized upper-material pattern efficiency and midsole construction. Bronze represented Nike’s historical baseline, while Silver and Gold were designated “Considered.” Product teams could score products quickly, and the Index was intended to become progressively more demanding.

Nike publicly committed that all footwear introduced in Spring 2011 would meet at least the Bronze standard. Core Performance, Nike’s highest-volume footwear category, initially committed to producing one or two Considered shoes but soon aimed for Bronze across its line. It incorporated Considered requirements into product briefs and reviews, formed a cross-functional task force, developed affordable material standards, worked with factories, and scored all products. Nearly its entire Spring 2009 line achieved Silver, and the Dual D Hoop earned Gold through a single-mold midsole process that reduced tooling, solvents, cost, and production steps while maintaining performance and schedule.

Implementation nevertheless faced substantial obstacles. Environmentally preferred materials could offer inadequate performance or aesthetics, and some products still required solvents. Considered added design complexity and planning time, particularly where teams were understaffed. Such materials often cost more, creating margin pressure, while factories and suppliers sometimes lacked technical capacity or were unwilling to invest without guaranteed volume. Consumers and retailers were also uncertain that greener footwear would justify higher prices or attract demand. Employees raised concerns that the Index could reward certain tradeoffs, although responses were broadly favorable, with substantial employee pride and interest in environmental design.

Measuring Considered’s overall impact was difficult because the first official Considered season had not yet reached stores, available baseline data relied partly on estimates, and existing sustainability initiatives and concurrent design programs complicated comparisons. Nike nevertheless believed the program was influencing product development and advancing its environmental vocabulary and practices.

Competitors also pursued sustainability initiatives, including Timberland’s Green Index, Adidas’s Grün products, and Brooks’s biodegradable BioMoGo foam. Looking ahead, Nike planned to expand the Index to apparel, deepen collaboration with factories and material suppliers, develop more sustainable design options, and determine how to communicate performance and sustainability together to retailers and consumers.

The study evaluates how nanotube radius affects chlorothalonil adsorption on single-walled carbon nanotubes (CNTs) and boron nitride nanotubes (BNNTs), using density functional theory and molecular dynamics. The (8,0), (10,0), and (12,0) nanotubes all adsorb chlorothalonil through moderate physical adsorption, preferentially with the aromatic ring parallel to the tube surface. Adsorption strengthens as radius increases because greater surface planarity improves π–π overlap; CNTs interact more strongly than BNNTs because their π-electron clouds are more polarizable.

CNTs show stronger charge transfer but little band-gap or work-function change, limiting their suitability for electronic detection. Their adsorption and recovery times increase substantially with radius, with the (12,0) CNT having an exceptionally long recovery time. BNNTs produce much larger electronic changes, including substantial band-gap reductions and, for smaller radii, significant work-function increases, enabling sensitive conductivity-based detection. Their recovery times remain short, supporting reusable sensing, although their work-function response diminishes as radius increases.

The simulations further show that both nanotube types stably retain chlorothalonil in water without desorption during 100 ns, maintaining the adsorption geometry predicted by DFT. Overall, both materials can remove chlorothalonil, but BNNTs are better suited to detecting and removing it, while CNTs are more appropriate for extraction with controlled nanotube size.

Pneumonia and tuberculosis remain major global health challenges, particularly where diagnostic resources are limited. Pneumonia is reported to account for 14% of deaths among children under five, while TB caused 1.25 million deaths in 2022. Misdiagnosis is a major concern: 22.3% of pneumonia cases are reported as misdiagnosed as pulmonary TB, contributing to treatment delays and mortality. These challenges motivate automated systems that can accurately distinguish the diseases from chest X-rays.

Machine learning and deep learning have been applied to lung segmentation, disease classification, treatment prediction, and COVID-19 detection. CNNs are widely used because chest radiography is low-cost and abundant training data is available, while medical experts can support computer-aided diagnostic development. Existing studies report strong results using models including DenseNet, VGG16, Vision Transformers, quaternion CNNs, weighted CNN ensembles, knowledge distillation, and hybrid handcrafted-feature systems, with reported accuracies ranging from 92.15% to 99.6%. Kundu et al.’s model declined from 98.81% accuracy on the Kermany dataset to 86.85% on RSNA.

Identified limitations include small or imbalanced datasets, dataset overlap, limited cross-validation, absent segmentation ground truth, risk of overfitting, lack of class-specific metrics, high computational demands, and weak generalizability across clinical and imaging settings. Binary models also overlook non-X-ray, unknown, or multiclass cases. These gaps are attributed partly to insufficiently diverse annotated medical-imaging data, subjective expert interpretation, variable image quality, and clinician workload.

The study proposes a pretrained-CNN framework that classifies chest X-rays into four categories: normal, pneumonia, tuberculosis, and non-X-ray. Including non-X-ray cases is intended to flag outliers or novel inputs and improve real-world robustness. The dataset is being compiled from multiple publicly available sources. All data are described as anonymized, publicly accessible, used under source authorization, and handled in accordance with the Declaration of Helsinki; no additional ethical approval or funding was required or obtained.

Hounds of the Bay is a dividend-focused stock-picking strategy for the S&P/TSX 60, named after Toronto’s Bay Street. Like Dogs of the Dow, it assumes blue-chip firms maintain dividends regardless of trading conditions and treats high dividend yields as signs that companies are near the bottom of their business cycles, potentially forecasting faster share-price gains. The strategy often favors global commodity and energy stocks because of the index’s composition; it underperformed sharply in 2014 after oil prices fell. Available data are scarce, but cited academic research reports that the strategy has performed well, though its effectiveness has diminished in recent decades.

Smash is a pass-game concept used from youth through NFL levels to create big plays while allowing quick throws. It attacks the perimeter, keeps routes unchanged against coverage, and is effective against man, Cover 2, and Cover 4. It can be problematic against Cover 3 when late hitch throws are undercut by outside linebackers; the Yankee concept is suggested as an alternative.

In a base 2x2, the quarterback chooses one side before the snap, evaluates corner leverage and safety alignment, then high-lows the corner: throw an on-time hitch if the corner goes deep, or a corner route if he plays low. If uncertain, the quarterback can check down to the running back. Tight ends and slot receivers work vertical routes with steep angles, X and Z receivers settle hitch routes at six yards, and backs handle blitz checks and checkdowns.

Variations adapt smash to 3x1 sets and moving pockets. Against one- or two-high cheat coverage, a backside dig or checkdown can be used. Sprint-out smash widens and deepens the pocket, slows the rush, adds a backside over route, and allows transition to a run.

The ISM Manufacturing Index, also known as the PMI, was introduced by the Institute for Supply Management (ISM) in 1948 and is a monthly indicator of economic activity in the United States. It is based on a survey of purchasing managers at over 300 US manufacturing firms covering new orders, production, employment, supplier deliveries, and inventories, with each factor given equal weight and seasonally adjusted for variations in demand due to time of year. The index is published on the first business day of each month and refers to the prior month's activity. Readings above 50 indicate expansion in the manufacturing sector, 50 indicates no change, and readings below 50 indicate contraction.

The index is widely watched by investors, traders, businesses, economists, analysts, and policymakers because it offers insight into the economy's direction and can influence market sentiment. Investors may treat rising readings as bullish and falling readings as bearish, using them to develop long or short strategies in stocks and index futures, to create passive index-based strategies, and to inform investment decisions in manufacturing companies and their suppliers. Businesses use the PMI to assess supply chain health and product demand, with high readings potentially prompting increased production and hiring and low readings prompting reductions.

The PMI is considered a reliable indicator of economic activity and, because purchasing managers often notice changes early, it can provide an early indication of the economy's direction and is viewed by many as a leading indicator of GDP. However, it is backward-looking rather than a forecast of future conditions, and market data is often already discounted by publication time, making it a lagging indicator for stock market prediction and not suited to short-term trading. Its weighting can change as the relative importance of factors changes over time.

The article's backtests of a rule buying the S&P 500 above 50 and selling below 50 showed the strategy invested 72% of the time with a 7.3% annual return versus 8.5% for the S&P 500, with a 12-month holding period yielding an average gain of 10.99% per trade at 86% exposure; gold was the only asset tested that performed better on low readings. The results suggest the index is not a particularly good contrarian indicator. It is best used alongside other indicators such as GDP, unemployment and employment data, inflation, consumer spending, jobless claims, and consumer confidence. Data can be downloaded from ISM's homepage or from a linked Google Sheet containing data back to 1970.

The paper examines whether large language model semantic embeddings can complement human-rater psychometrics. It introduces Survey and Questionnaire Item Embeddings Differentials (SQuID), which subtracts the average embedding of all questionnaire items from each item embedding to reduce shared linguistic features and recover negative correlations without domain-specific fine-tuning.

Using the 57-item Revised Portrait Value Questionnaire (PVQ-RR), which measures 19 value dimensions, the authors compare embeddings with human ratings collected across 49 countries. Linq-Embed-Mistral performs best overall: its average Cronbach’s alpha slightly exceeds the human benchmark, while random embeddings show no meaningful consistency. Embedding- and human-based dimension correlations are substantial (0.74), and a linear model explains 55% of their variance. Multidimensional scaling of embeddings reproduces the theorized circular value structure, with Procrustes congruence coefficients of 0.88 and 0.82 for the first two dimensions.

The authors position semantic embeddings as a fast, inexpensive, flexible, and scalable complement to—not a replacement for—human judgment. They identify unresolved validity issues, including reverse scoring, possible questionnaire memorization, cultural bias, and the uncertain equivalence of embeddings and human responses. They also caution against treating LLM-derived norms as objective standards and note potential harms to crowdworkers whose labor may be displaced.

Technical support guidance directs users to the Tips, FAQ, and Troubleshooting section, SanDisk’s technical support number and online request form, and partner-service support. Users should provide information from the product packaging to expedite assistance.

The one-year limited warranty applies to original end users purchasing from SanDisk or an authorized reseller and may require proof of purchase. It excludes third-party software and content and is void for improper use, unauthorized repair, modification, accident, or failure to follow instructions. The study details the Shayona team’s participation in two SMM4H 2023 binary classification tasks. Task 1 classified Twitter posts as self-reported COVID-19 diagnoses or non-diagnostic mentions; Task 4 distinguished positive or probable social anxiety diagnoses from absent, unlikely, or unclear cases using r/socialanxiety data. Task 1 included 7,600 training, 400 validation, and 10,000 test tweets, while Task 4 included 6,090 training, 680 validation, and 1,347 test entries. Text preprocessing removed non-alphabet characters, tags, emojis, URLs, stopwords, and punctuation.

For Task 1, the team compared fine-tuned RoBERTa, fine-tuned BERT, and a hybrid BERT-LightGBM model. The hybrid used the COVID-19 Twitter BERT model, extracted hidden [CLS] tokens from its final three layers, and trained LightGBM with Optuna hyperparameter optimization. Validation F1 scores were 0.83 for RoBERTa, 0.89 for BERT, and 0.93 for BERT-LightGBM. The hybrid achieved test precision, recall, and F1 scores of 0.949, 0.938, and 0.943, respectively. Applying the same architecture to Task 4 produced test precision, recall, and F1 scores of 0.756, 0.871, and 0.809.

The hybrid was strongest for Task 1 and demonstrated the value of combining transformer embeddings with gradient boosting. Lower Task 4 performance was attributed partly to using a COVID-19-pretrained BERT model rather than one pretrained on Task 4-related data. Proposed future work includes testing different token layers and dimensions or using a task-specific BERT model.

America’s history, support for liberty, pursuit of peace, and example of constitutional government should guide its conduct.

He advocates a just and peaceful foreign policy, including acquisition of strategically important territories for national security without greed or dishonor, peaceful relations with neighboring nations, and reciprocal protection of American citizens abroad. NVIDIA’s Ampere-based A100 Tensor Core GPU supports 2:4 fine-grained structured sparsity, enabling dense-trained networks to be pruned and fine-tuned with virtually no loss of accuracy across vision, detection, segmentation, language modeling, and translation. This reduces weight storage and bandwidth requirements by half and doubles Tensor Core throughput by skipping zero-valued operations.

A100 has 108 SMs and third-generation Tensor Cores with peak mixed-precision performance 16 times that of standard FP32 FMA operations. It combines wider thread-level data sharing, fewer instructions and register accesses, asynchronous global-to-shared memory copies, hardware barriers, and cache controls to improve deep-learning efficiency and strong scaling. Separate FP32 and INT32 cores can execute simultaneously.

The GPU includes 40 GB of HBM2 memory delivering 1,555 GB/s, a 40 MB partitioned L2 cache with 2.3 times V100’s bandwidth, and 192 KB of combined L1 cache and shared memory per SM. ECC protection, compute data compression, L2 residency controls, and cache-coherence mechanisms improve reliability, bandwidth, and capacity.

Multi-Instance GPU (MIG) can divide an A100 into as many as seven isolated GPU Instances with dedicated compute and memory resources, quality-of-service guarantees, and fault isolation. GPU Instances can contain multiple Compute Instances that support Volta-style MPS and independently execute simultaneous contexts. MIG also supports migrating virtual GPUs between compatible instances to consolidate workloads.

Third-generation NVLink provides twelve links and 600 GB/s aggregate bandwidth, while PCIe Gen 4 provides 31.5 GB/s per direction on x16 connections. A100 also adds SR-IOV, enhanced error detection and containment, five-core NVJPEG decoding, an optical-flow accelerator, improved FP16 and FP32 atomic throughput, and five NVDEC units.

CUDA 11 adds support for sparse Tensor Cores, task graphs, asynchronous copies and barriers, L2 persistence controls, and Cooperative Groups reductions. DGX A100 combines eight A100 GPUs with NVSwitch, delivering 5 PFLOPS, up to 56 isolated MIG accelerators, 4.8 TB/s bidirectional interconnect bandwidth, and support for large AI clusters through InfiniBand, NGC software, and other data-center technologies.

The NVIDIA A100 Tensor Core GPU uses the Ampere architecture to accelerate AI and high-performance computing workloads. Its third-generation Tensor Cores support FP16, BF16, TF32, FP64, INT8, INT4, and binary formats. With 108 SMs and 432 Tensor Cores, the GPU delivers up to 312 TFLOPS of dense FP16/FP32 mixed-precision performance—2.5 times the V100’s Tensor Core performance and 20 times its standard FP32 throughput. TF32 provides FP32 range and I/O with reduced internal precision and up to eight times the FP32 throughput, while FP16 and BF16 mixed precision provide up to 16 times the A100’s standard FP32 throughput. A100 also delivers 19.5 TFLOPS of FP64 performance, 2.5 times that of V100.

The cuSOLVER TCAIRS mixed-precision iterative-refinement solver supports FP16, BF16, and TF32. Across 37 SuiteSparse problems, TF32 produced the fastest and most robust Tensor Core results, with a 2.0× geometric-mean speedup over the FP64 solver and speedups up to 4× for large, complex matrices.

A100 introduces 2:4 fine-grained structured sparsity, requiring two nonzero values in every four-entry vector. Sparse Tensor Core instructions skip zero entries, doubling matrix-multiplication throughput. Sparse weights also halve storage and bandwidth requirements. A pruning and fine-tuning process produced virtually no loss of inference accuracy across evaluated vision, detection, segmentation, language-modeling, and translation networks.

The GPU has 40 GB of HBM2 memory delivering 1,555 GB/s of bandwidth and a 40 MB L2 cache with 2.3 times V100’s read bandwidth. ECC protects HBM2, L2, L1 caches, and register files. A100 combines L1 cache and shared memory into a 192 KB-per-SM subsystem and introduces asynchronous global-to-shared copies, hardware barriers, cache-residency controls, and compute data compression to improve latency, bandwidth efficiency, and strong scaling.

Multi-Instance GPU (MIG) can divide an A100 into as many as seven GPU Instances, each with isolated compute, L2, and memory resources. GPU Instances can contain multiple Compute Instances, support Volta-style MPS, run contexts concurrently, and migrate virtual GPUs between compatible instances. This provides defined quality of service, fault isolation, and improved utilization for multi-tenant deployments.

Third-generation NVLink provides 12 links and 600 GB/s of aggregate GPU-to-GPU bandwidth, while PCIe Gen 4 provides 31.5 GB/s per direction on x16 links and supports SR-IOV virtualization. A100 also adds stronger error detection, attribution, isolation, and containment for multi-GPU and MIG environments.

Additional hardware includes a five-core NVJPG JPEG decoder, an optical-flow accelerator supporting optical flow and stereo disparity, improved global-memory atomics, and five NVDEC units. The GPU has no display connectors, RT Cores, or NVENC encoder.

CUDA 11 adds support for third-generation Tensor Cores, sparsity, task graphs, asynchronous copies, asynchronous barriers, L2 residency controls, Cooperative Groups, and MIG. Task graphs reduce repeated launch overhead and dependency latency, while hardware reductions complete warp reductions in one step.

DGX A100 combines eight A100 GPUs with six NVSwitches, providing up to 5 PFLOPS of AI performance and 4.8 TB/s of bidirectional interconnect bandwidth. MIG can create up to 56 isolated accelerators within one system, and the accompanying software stack includes CUDA, GPU-accelerated containers, NGC resources, and optimized AI, analytics, and HPC software.

The ADS868xW is a fully integrated, 16-bit SAR ADC data-acquisition device with a differential analog front end, programmable gain amplifier, ADC driver, and precision reference buffer. It supports single-ended or differential, bipolar or unipolar inputs and produces straight-binary output.

The internal 4.096-V reference is selected by setting `INTREF_DIS` in `RANGE_SEL_REG` to 0. REFIO becomes the reference output and requires a minimum 4.7-µF decoupling capacitor. The reference is factory-trimmed but can shift due to mechanical or thermal stress, including PCB soldering and repeated reflows. It is temperature compensated from −40°C to +125°C. An external 4.096-V reference can instead be selected with `INTREF_DIS = 1` and applied to REFIO; the internal buffer drives REFCAP, which requires 10 µF and 1 µF capacitors. Neither reference output may directly drive external loads. Typical buffer temperature drift is 0.5 ppm/°C, with a maximum of 2 ppm/°C.

The ADC full-scale range equals PFS minus NFS, and the LSB size is FSR/2^16 for a 4.096-V reference. The active-high alarm output is configurable on ALARM/SDO-1/GPO. Input alarms use independently programmable high and low thresholds with common hysteresis, while the AVDD alarm trips at typical low and high thresholds of 4.7 V and 5.3 V. Active alarm flags clear at the end of a conversion, whereas tripped flags clear when `ALARM_REG` is read. Alarm status can be accessed through the ALARM pin, `ALARM_REG`, or appended output flags.

The multiSPI interface uses a 32-bit input/output shift-register model and supports single-device SPI, dual-SDO, source-synchronous, and daisy-chain configurations. In a daisy chain, devices require identical programmed configurations, sample on the rising edge of CONVST/CS, and require an optimal frame of 32 × N SCLK capture edges for N devices.

The device has RESET, ACQ, and CONV states. The active-low RST pin can generate either an application reset, which resets configuration registers, or a full power-on reset. ACQ acquires the analog input, and a rising CONVST/CS edge starts conversion. RVS indicates conversion completion, allowing the host to initiate another transfer or conversion.

Data-transfer frames begin when CONVST/CS goes low and end on its next rising edge. A 32-SCLK frame is optimal and permits a valid register command; shorter frames cannot perform writes, while in longer frames the final 32 shifted bits form the command. Writes support byte and half-word operations, including read, set, clear, and masked register operations. Output frames can contain conversion data, fixed test patterns, register reads, device addresses, range information, alarm flags, and parity.

The interface supports four legacy SPI-compatible modes for configuration and reading, optional dual-SDO output, and source-synchronous operation using internal or external clock sources and selectable bus width. The device also provides nine configuration registers covering device identification, reset and power control, SDI and SDO protocols, output data formatting, reference and input-range selection, and alarms.

An application example combines an ADS8681W with an eight-channel MUX36D08 differential multiplexer to measure standard industrial bipolar, unipolar voltage, and current inputs. It supports configurable channels, fast settling below 5 µs to 1% accuracy, programmable input-alarm thresholds, and hysteresis for thermistor-based temperature monitoring.

AVDD and DVDD are separate analog and digital supplies and require close decoupling, including 1-µF and minimum 10-µF capacitors. Programmable NAP and power-down modes reduce consumption at lower throughput. Recommended PCB layout separates analog and digital routing, uses short ground paths and close bypass capacitors, and avoids vias between supply or reference pins and their capacitors.

The Rate of Change (ROC), frequently labeled PROC in the passage, is a momentum-based technical indicator developed by Tom Demark. It compares a security’s current price with its price “n” periods earlier and is calculated as:

ROC = (Current Price − Price n Periods Ago) / Price n Periods Ago

ROC is plotted around a zero line. Positive values indicate rising prices and buying pressure, while negative values indicate falling prices and selling pressure. Centerline crossovers may signal trend changes, but they are especially prone to whipsaw with short lookback periods. Shorter periods are more sensitive and produce more signals; longer periods are smoother and produce fewer, later signals.

Traders use ROC to assess momentum, identify potential overbought or oversold conditions, spot divergences, and determine when entries or exits may be appropriate. Overbought and oversold levels are security-specific rather than fixed, and extreme conditions can persist. A bullish divergence occurs when price makes a lower low while ROC makes a higher low, suggesting a possible upside reversal; a bearish divergence occurs when price makes a higher high while ROC makes a lower high, suggesting a possible downside reversal. Divergences can continue for prolonged periods without reversal and should be considered alongside market structure, support, resistance, and price action.

ROC is considered most suitable for short-term trading and trending, nonvolatile markets. It can identify when a pullback may be ending, such as through an oversold signal or bullish divergence near support in an uptrend. It is prone to conflicting signals and whipsaws in volatile markets. In sideways markets, it may be used near support or resistance when combined with oversold, overbought, or divergence signals. It can be applied to stocks, futures, forex, bonds, and other markets with real-time price data.

ROC differs from RSI because it directly measures the rate of price change, whereas RSI indirectly estimates momentum using up and down periods. It differs from moving averages, which identify trends, while ROC measures momentum and price swings. Complementary indicators such as moving averages and trendlines can help define direction and avoid countertrend trades. ROC also has value for options traders because of its relationship to changes in an option’s price relative to its underlying security.

Backtests presented for SPY found that an oversold mean-reversion strategy performed reasonably well, with four- and six-day settings among the best, though it experienced sharp setbacks. Breakout and zero-line crossover strategies performed poorly, while divergence strategies were not tested because their rules were difficult to quantify. Overall, the tested ROC strategies were described as inferior to RSI, stochastic, and Williams %R.

ROC does not directly set stop-loss or position-size levels, but it can contribute to a broader strategy and reveal when momentum turns against a position. Beginners are advised to learn how markets and indicators work, build a ROC-based system, backtest and optimize it for robustness, and deploy it only if it is profitable.

The AMD Geode CS5535 Companion Device Silicon Revision A3 specification update catalogs device limitations, operational effects, and recommended workarounds.

- **Interrupts and clock gating:** LBAR values of 10000h or higher are illegal on x86 systems and should not be used. An edge-configured PIC input that remains high after service prevents the PIC from returning to Idle when automatic Local bus clock gating is active, potentially causing missed interrupts, a stalled clock, and a system hang; automatic clock gating should remain off. GLIU statistics-counter ASMIs may be lost when domain-zero hardware clock gating is enabled. UART clock gating is incompatible with CEIR mode, and USB controller clock gating can cause register-read failures; both features should be disabled.
- **ATA, UDMA, and PRD handling:** Eight-byte GeodeLink Adaptor prefetch is safe for 8-byte-aligned PRD tables but may prefetch from the next PRD when tables are only 4-byte aligned. ATAC UDMA writes are exposed when active PRD entries are modified; PRDs should be defined before operations begin. ACC changes made during playback or recording should remain at least two tables ahead of the current PRD. A preceding UDMA read with host termination can leave corrupted state that causes incorrect CRCs after a device-terminated UDMA write; UDMA I/O blocking via bit 8 of ATAC Error MSR 51300003h is recommended. ATAC SSMI does not block IDE I/O during master DMA and should not be used. ATAC can hang with WORD-aligned PRDs, so drivers should use DWORD alignment. Sending a PIO command after enabling the IDE bus master causes UDMA transfer failure; the required order is PIO command first, then bus-master enable. An unexpected IDE interrupt after bus mastering starts can reset the bus-master engine, though the cited device issue was corrected by firmware.
- **ACPI and power management:** Revision A3 supports only WORD and DWORD access to PM1_STS and PM1_EN; byte accesses can hang. Byte access should be avoided, or AMD BIOS trapping and system-management emulation can be used. WORD or BYTE writes to PMC registers may corrupt the same or unrelated registers because byte-lane information is mishandled; an SMI I/O trap can prevent incorrectly sized ACPI-register accesses. GPIO inputs SLP_BUT#, THRM_ALRM#, and LOW_BAT# cannot wake the system from ACPI S3; PWRBTN# should be used, with external circuitry optionally combining events. LOWBAT_FLAG may not record a low-battery condition after abnormal standby. Premature delay-counter resets can leave SLEEP_X and SLEEP_Y asserted and PCI/IDE inputs disabled after Sleep exit; the relevant delay counters must be programmed below PM_SED.
- **KEL and USB emulation:** KEL CmdData remains zero for writes to I/O ports 60h and 64h, preventing port differentiation through that field; trap information from emulation-event ASMIs should be used instead. KEL Snoop mode incorrectly allows those writes to change HCE state, so software must save and restore HCE state around Snoop mode. Reading port 60h can incorrectly clear AuxOutputFull; interrupts should be used to manage USB keyboard and mouse traffic in PS/2 emulation.
- **LPC, SMBus, PCI, and miscellaneous issues:** Block- and demand-mode legacy DMA can block LPC I/O and return invalid data; single-transfer mode should be used, optionally through an SMM trap. The LPC controller can abort transactions involving LPC-to-ISA bridges that delay their SYNC pattern; a PLD workaround is described. SMB NEGACK may clear unexpectedly and can take time to set, so SMB_STS should be written twice when clearing it. SMBus hold time is below the SMB 2.0 requirement of 300 ns. GLPCI retry limits count other PCI-bus retries and may be increased or disabled. After suspend, atomic GPIO High Bank Feature Bit Register writes must use read-modify-write operations to avoid clearing unselected bits. RTC CMOS RAM reads can return extended-port data when an extended write is immediately followed by a legacy read, with no resolution specified.
- **Other limitations:** PCI back-to-back read failures were observed only in simulation and are not reachable from the Geode GX processor in real systems. The CS5535 does not support the standard 8259 PIC polling mode. IRDY# and DEVSEL# violate the stated 2 ns tVAL minimum, although no failures are expected; 10–50 pF capacitors can slow the edges if needed. Concurrent interrupt and SSMI events can delay or lose the SSMI, so the processor should be used for desired SSMI generation. A fixed 30 ns IDE_DACK timing creates no violation.
