A UDMA write can produce an incorrect CRC after an IDE device terminates the transaction because the ATAC continues the previous CRC instead of restarting it. The corruption originates from `host_pio_term` residue left by a preceding UDMA read involving host termination. A host-initiated I/O may restart the CRC but cannot be relied upon, making UDMA writes generally unusable. The resolution is to use UDMA I/O blocking via bit 8 of the ATAC Error MSR.

The Ninth Circuit affirmed dismissal of five antitrust and California interference claims brought by Innofood and Sea Breeze concerning ESSA, a salt producer 51% owned by the Mexican government, and Mitsubishi entities. Plaintiffs alleged that ESSA and Mitsubishi conspired to terminate ESSA’s outside distribution contracts, including its contract with Innofood, and return to selling salt exclusively through Mitsubishi.

The court held that ESSA’s decisions about the exploitation and distribution of Mexico’s salt were official acts of a foreign sovereign performed in Mexico. Adjudicating the claims would require a U.S. court to invalidate Mexico’s sovereign policy of distributing essentially its entire salt output through a single buyer. The court declined to decide whether the act of state doctrine has a commercial exception because the challenged policy decisions exercised powers peculiar to sovereigns.

The Supreme Court’s Sabbatino factors also supported dismissal: the record showed no international consensus condemning exclusive resource arrangements; the case implicated foreign relations and could offend Mexico’s sovereignty; the resource production involved was substantial; and Mexico’s government continued to exist. The Foreign Sovereign Immunities Act did not bar jurisdiction because its commercial activity exception applied, and private litigants may invoke the act of state doctrine. The court also declined to dismiss Sea Breeze’s appeal because its corporate powers had been restored during the appeal. The panel emphasized that its narrow holding did not make state-owned enterprises or all resource-related conduct immune from judicial review.

Interferometric second-harmonic generation (SHG) polarimetry is presented as a scalable, wide-area method for assessing structural quality in CVD-grown 2D hBN. Polarization-resolved SHG maps crystallographic orientation, while interference with a local oscillator distinguishes antiparallel domains that intensity-based measurements alone cannot separate. Comparisons of ten CVD growth conditions with mechanically exfoliated references showed that SHG intensity varied by up to three orders of magnitude, far more than Raman intensity, while Raman linewidth and orientational spread also tracked disorder. A mixed-domain model showed that random orientational disorder alone caused only modest intensity reductions, whereas antiparallel domain populations produced destructive interference consistent with the observations. Interferometry confirmed antiparallel domains and boundaries throughout films grown on high-symmetry substrates, including regions that appeared uniformly aligned and domains smaller than the focal spot. Raman intensity and linewidth, SHG intensity, and orientational spread together provide quantitative crystallinity metrics, with SHG being particularly sensitive to antiparallel domains. The method enables macroscopic structural imaging without the limited sampling areas of TEM and STM and is also applicable to other non-centrosymmetric 2D materials, including TMDs.

In a prospective multicenter cohort of 22 adults with cirrhosis undergoing elective TIPS, investigators analyzed serial hepatic-vein and peripheral-vein plasma before and after shunt placement and followed participants for up to one year for hepatic encephalopathy (HE). Untargeted LC-MS/MS with feature-based molecular networking annotated 234 metabolite features. Peripheral metabolomes changed more after TIPS than hepatic metabolomes, with bile acids contributing most to the differences. Bile acid levels fell immediately after TIPS and were generally restored by discharge.

Participants with more severe HE showed greater pre-to-post hepatic-vein metabolome dissimilarity. The authors interpreted this as possible evidence of less pre-TIPS intrahepatic shunting, which may increase exposure to portal toxins after TIPS; portal-pressure changes were not associated with HE severity. Greater reductions in bile acids were associated with more severe HE, and three conjugated hydroxylated bile acids were inversely correlated with HE grade. In two participants readmitted with HE, treatment was followed by increased levels of these bile acids.

Bile acid and glycerophosphocholine clusters also differed by HE severity. Chemical-proportionality analyses implicated changes in glycerophosphocholines and bilirubin-related metabolites, including greater biliverdin redox changes in severe HE. The findings suggest potential biomarkers and therapeutic targets but require validation in larger cohorts. Limitations include incomplete metabolic coverage, mostly putative annotations, the small sample, unmeasured microbiome relationships, and the need for noninvasive methods to assess intrahepatic shunting.

NVIDIA Corporation filed a Form 8-K dated February 14, 2019, announcing results for the quarter and fiscal year ended January 27, 2019. The AMD Geode CS5535 Companion Device Silicon Revision A3 specification update lists device limitations, potential effects, and recommended software workarounds.

Legacy 8237 block- and demand-mode DMA can block UART access and make LPC I/O prolonged or invalid; CS5535 UART writes during DMA are discarded and reads return all ones. Software should avoid UART and LPC I/O during these modes, wait for the DMA terminal-count IRQ, and use single-transfer DMA instead. SMM may trap and convert block- or demand-mode configurations. A diagnostic LPC software-DMA write completes without writing memory but has no operational impact.

CS5535 claims PCI I/O addresses at or above 10000h, which can hang the system; such accesses and ATAC or Diverse Device LBAR values at or above 10000h must not be used. The CS5535 does not meet the USB overvoltage-protection specification, requiring external protection. ATAC PRD tables should use DWORD alignment. Recommended ATAC and ACC prefetch settings are 00000000_0048F000h and 00000000_0008F000h, respectively; improperly aligned tables can cause the next PRD’s first four bytes to be prefetched. PRD tables should be defined before transfers, and ACC changes made on the fly should be at least two tables ahead of the current PRD.

UDMA writes can contain incorrect CRC after device termination due to corrupted residue from a preceding host-terminated UDMA read. The ATAC UDMA I/O blocking bit in Error MSR 51300003h should prevent host terminations. The required UDMA sequence is to send the PIO command before enabling the bus master; the reverse order fails. ATAC SSMI during DMA does not block the requested I/O and should not be used.

Clock gating can cause missed interrupts or lost events. An edge-configured PIC input remaining high can prevent the PIC from returning to idle, preventing clock restart and potentially hanging the system. GLIU statistics-generated ASMIs can be lost when domain-zero clock gating is enabled. UART CEIR mode and USB controller register access are also unreliable with clock gating enabled, so affected clock gating should be disabled. Simultaneous IRQ and SSMI events can allow I/O to complete before the SSMI is delivered; the processor should be used to generate desired SSMIs.

Byte access to ACPI PM1_EN or PM1_STS hangs; only WORD and DWORD accesses are supported, or AMD BIOS can trap byte accesses. WORD or BYTE PMC writes can corrupt the same or unrelated registers; an SMI I/O trap can protect ACPI registers, while proprietary PMC registers should use DWORD access. Most specified GPIO wake inputs do not work from ACPI S3; PWRBTN# should be used, with external circuitry if multiple events must be distinguished. Sleep-transition delay counters must be programmed below the PM_SED delay or SLEEP_X and SLEEP_Y remain asserted and PCI/IDE inputs remain disabled. Other documented issues include missing LOWBAT_FLAG after abnormal standby, incorrect post-suspend atomic GPIO writes, incorrect RTC CMOS RAM sequencing, unsupported 8259 polling mode, KEL inability to distinguish writes to I/O ports 060h and 064h, KEL Snoop-mode state corruption, premature SMB NEGACK reporting, GLPCI retry miscounting, possible LPC transaction aborts, and short SMBus hold time. Recommended mitigations include saving and restoring KEL state, writing SMB_STS twice when clearing NEGACK, and using a PLD for the LPC SYNC workaround.

The passage surveys container and distributed-system patterns using Kubernetes examples. It explains how the adapter pattern integrates incompatible or externally supplied components without modifying them. Prometheus exporters adapt services such as Redis to Prometheus’s metrics API, Fluentd adapters redirect and normalize heterogeneous logs and capture sources such as Redis SLOWLOG and Storm, and database adapters provide richer health checks. Adapters avoid maintaining patched images, decouple components, and promote reuse.

Microservices divide applications into independently developed, API-connected services. This approach enables team autonomy, independent deployment and scaling, and modularity, but makes architecture, debugging, and failure diagnosis more difficult.

Replicated load-balanced services use identical replicas behind a load balancer to provide redundancy, fault tolerance, and horizontal scaling. Stateless services should have at least two replicas, and readiness probes distinguish running containers from those prepared to serve traffic. Session-tracked variants route each user consistently to one replica using IP hashing, cookies, or consistent hashing. A replicated caching tier can improve latency and capacity, while rate limiting and an nginx SSL-terminating layer can add protection and secure web serving.

Sharded services divide data or responsibilities among subsets of replicas. Sharding increases the amount of data a system can hold and can be combined with replication for resilience, independent shard scaling, and hot-shard handling. Sharding functions must be deterministic and uniform; appropriate keys should reflect exactly what affects a response. Consistent hashing minimizes key remapping when shard counts change. Sharded caches also require careful attention to hit rate, capacity, latency, upgrades, and the impact of individual shard failures.

Scatter/gather systems distribute each request simultaneously to multiple leaves and combine their partial results at a root. This parallelizes mostly independent computation, but increasing leaf count introduces coordination overhead and “straggler” latency because the slowest response determines completion. Replicating each shard improves reliability and permits rolling upgrades.

The passage also introduces function-as-a-service and event-driven architectures, distinguishing event-driven FaaS from serverless computing generally. FaaS simplifies deployment, automatically scales and restarts functions, and encourages stateless modular services, but complicates debugging, state management, background processing, memory-intensive workloads, and sustained-request economics. Its highlighted patterns include stateless request or response decorators, asynchronous event handlers such as two-factor authentication, and event pipelines composed of independently deployed functions.

Wall Street closed higher Thursday after revised data showed U.S. fourth-quarter GDP grew at a 2.1% annualized rate, up from 1.9%, on robust consumer spending. The Dow, S&P 500 and Nasdaq rose 0.33%, 0.29% and 0.28%, respectively, with the Nasdaq posting a record close and fifth straight gain. The speaker addresses Congress after accepting a summons to public service, acknowledging his anxiety at leaving retirement and his doubts about his qualifications while affirming his devotion to duty. In his first official act, he invokes divine blessing for the new government and expresses gratitude for the providential circumstances surrounding American independence and union. He defers policy recommendations to Congress under the Constitution, praising the representatives’ talents, integrity, and patriotism as safeguards against prejudice and party divisions. James T. Hodgkinson shot Rep. Steve Scalise and several others during an early-morning congressional baseball practice in Alexandria, Virginia, before police fatally shot him. Authorities said the 66-year-old had lived from a van in northern Virginia since March and frequently worked on a computer at a nearby YMCA, appearing calm and keeping to himself. He expressed online grievances about President Donald Trump and Republicans, but investigators had not determined his motive. Armed with a handgun and rifle, Hodgkinson wounded Rep. Roger Williams’ aide Zack Barth, two Capitol Police officers and a former aide. The FBI was tracing his weapons and activities. He ran a home-inspection business in Illinois, volunteered for Bernie Sanders’ campaign and wrote frequently about income inequality. He had prior arrests and was cautioned after shooting his rifle near homes; no charges were filed.

More than 250 guests attended AGM’s 31st Annual Banquet, where supporters celebrated the school year with a meal, dancing and performances. Perplexity AI announced that its AI-powered web browser, Comet, is now available worldwide and free to users, a move aimed at attracting users as competition intensifies with Google, Anthropic and OpenAI, which have their own AI browser offerings. Perplexity initially launched Comet in July to Perplexity Max subscribers for $200 a month, and the waitlist has grown to "millions." The speaker advises his team to remain focused amid increased media attention and demands during the Finals. He praises Scott Stevens’ durability, dedication, and physical play, while noting that draft losses make sustained success difficult. Dallas has an elite power play, including Hull as a shooter, Modano as a passer, and Zubov as a quarterback, making New Jersey’s penalty killing important. The President transmitted to Congress the Texas governor’s letter and his response. Texas claimed jurisdiction over four unorganized counties east of the Rio Grande and sought to establish a separate state government there, but reported that U.S. military officers stationed at Santa Fe obstructed its commissioner.

The President argued that Texas’s authority is confined to its own boundaries. Texas forces entering another state or U.S. territory to enforce Texas law would be trespassers, and the President could lawfully employ the militia, army, or navy if they obstructed federal law or attempted unauthorized seizures for trial in Texas.

He maintained that New Mexico was a U.S. territory acquired from Mexico under the Treaty of Guadalupe Hidalgo. The treaty’s boundary, citizenship, and property provisions were part of the supreme law and protected residents’ liberty, property, and religion. Pending a final boundary settlement, the Executive was obligated to enforce federal law and treaties in New Mexico but lacked authority to establish a territorial or state government, a power belonging to Congress.

Calling the boundary dispute urgent because delay could cause conflict, the President urged Congress to settle it before the session ended, preferably with Texas’s assent and possible compensation for surrendering any valid claim. He preferred direct congressional action over slower judicial proceedings or arbitration while accepting any alternative devised by Congress.

The Illinois Appellate Court affirmed a jury verdict and judgment for Boncar Construction Company in James D. Rone’s negligence action for injuries sustained at a sewer construction site in Hobart, Indiana. Rone was employed by joint-venture partner Dan Raymond Construction Company as a line foreman. Boncar employee Robert Crank operated the backhoe. While the backhoe moved a large trench-safety box, Rone held telephone wires above the machine and then grasped a control cable while descending from the gantry. The moving cable drew his hand into a sheave, severing several fingers.

Rone alleged negligence and statutory violations under the Indiana Dangerous Occupation Act for the absence of a communication or signal system. He also sought to invoke the Illinois Structural Work Act, but the trial court struck that count because the Illinois statute did not apply to an accident in Indiana. The court held that Rone waived his appeal of that dismissal and that multiple descriptions of the same occurrence did not create separately appealable claims where their legal bases differed.

The court rejected Rone’s argument that the undisputed facts required judgment as a matter of law. Whether adequate communications existed, whether any statutory violation proximately caused the injury, and whether Rone was contributorily negligent were questions for the jury. Evidence showed that Rone could have used alternatives to climbing on the gantry and could have held a fixed rail rather than the movable cable. The court also rejected Rone’s contention that the joint-venture arrangement made Boncar an employer under the Indiana Employers Liability Act. Finally, it found no error in refusing his proposed instructions because their substance was adequately covered and his agency theory was unsupported.

Apixaban exposure, interruptions, dosing, and compliance were comparable across study groups. Compliance exceeded 95% through Week 24 and 94% at Week 48. Mean adherence at 24 weeks was 91.64% in the Primary SOC group and 91.88% in the Additional Educational Program group, with no significant difference; persistence was similarly comparable at 91.7% and 91.3%. Adherence declined significantly after Week 12 and again after Week 24 but remained comparable between groups. At 48 weeks, adherence and persistence did not differ significantly among the three Part 2 groups. The proportions of fully adherent subjects were 28.1% versus 26.5% at Week 24 and approximately 14.5%–14.9% across groups at Week 48, without significant between-group differences. Subgroup analyses found no significant interaction at 24 or 48 weeks, although interactions by atrial fibrillation type and sex were reported for adherence from Week 24 to Week 48.

Safety endpoints were generally similar between groups. Before Week 24, adverse events occurred in 51.2% and 52.0% of the Primary SOC and Additional Educational Program groups, respectively; bleeding occurred in 6.5% and 9.0%, including major bleeding in 0.7% and 1.1%. One fatal bleeding event occurred in the Additional Educational Program group. Between Weeks 24 and 48, adverse events occurred in 33.8%–40.8% across the three groups, and major bleeding in 0.3%–0.7%; two fatal bleeding events occurred, one each in the Primary and Secondary SOC groups. Overall, 24 deaths were reported. No pregnancies or clinically concerning hepatic or renal laboratory signals were identified.

The AEGEAN study found high apixaban adherence and persistence through 24 weeks, sustained to 48 weeks, but no additional adherence or persistence benefit from the proactive educational program.

Opening range breakout strategies trade when price moves above or below the high or low recorded during a defined initial time interval. Backtests of simple strategies on S&P 500 futures produced very small average gains, low win rates, and negative results across Nasdaq, gold, silver, and oil contracts. Adding daily or weekly filters can improve results. Jerry Tarkanian developed the “Amoeba” defense at the University of Las Vegas, where it played a significant role in UNLV’s 1990 NCAA championship. It is an aggressive, trapping matchup zone defense used from a 1-1-3 alignment to pressure the ballhandler, disrupt offenses, create steals, and generate transition baskets. The system requires quick guards and includes rotations for wing and corner entries, follow-pass and wing-dribble traps, an “X Cut” post/wing exchange, skip passes, ball reversals, and guard/wing interchanges. Defenders also use help-side positions, deny post passes and lob entries, and close passing lanes. Against a two-guard front, X1 and X2 match up while X5 plays behind the high post; a pass inside can trigger a triple team and forced turnover.

Salt Lake County District Attorney Sim Gill ruled that police were legally justified in fatally shooting Patrick Harmon, 50, saying slowed body-camera footage showed Harmon pivoting toward officers with a knife at close range. Officer Clinton Fox said Harmon threatened to stab him, although the video did not clearly show the weapon or threat. Harmon was stopped after riding across traffic on a bicycle without a required rear light. Officers said he used different names, had felony warrants, fled while being handcuffed, and threatened them; a knife was found near his body.

Black Lives Matter Utah organizer Lex Scott said the community was livid, called the shooting “a clear case of murder,” and demanded Gill resign. About 50 protesters had also demanded release of the footage. NAACP president Jeanetta Williams said she saw Harmon run before officers shot him and did not see a knife. Gill acknowledged the decision was difficult and said prosecutors must determine whether officers could reasonably fear serious injury or death. The shooting occurred amid national debates over race and policing and followed Utah police’s 2014 killing of Darrien Hunt, which prosecutors also deemed justified.

An emulated trial study using Veterans Health Administration electronic health records compared 198,938 SARS-CoV-2–infected Veterans with 992,036 matched, uninfected comparators. Outcomes included suicide attempts and other self-directed violence identified through curated VHA reports, assessed for days 1–30, 31–365, and 1–365 after the index date. Within one year, 3,078 Veterans (0.258%) had at least one suicide attempt and 2,887 (0.242%) experienced self-directed violence, with incidence rates of 267 and 250 per 100,000 person-years, respectively.

Infected Veterans had higher risks during all follow-up periods. The hazard ratios for suicide attempts were 2.54 short term, 1.30 long term, and 1.41 over one year; for self-directed violence, they were 1.94, 1.32, and 1.38, respectively. Risks were generally highest during the first 30 days and elevated across age groups. Relative risks were greatest among Veterans without prior suicide attempts or self-directed violence, although analyses of those with prior events were underpowered. Per-protocol and GEE sensitivity analyses were largely consistent with the primary results.

There were 237 unvalidated suicide deaths reported, with no significant difference between groups. Limitations included possible ascertainment bias, undetected infections, comparator crossover, and unobserved confounding. The findings support early and sustained monitoring, assessment, and prevention efforts following SARS-CoV-2 infection.

Momentum investing buys stocks with strong historical performance and periodically rebalances into the highest-momentum stocks. It is based on the hypothesis that strong 3–12-month returns are likely to continue over the following 3–12 months. The average loss was under 5%, while the average winner was nearly 25%. A simple moving average performed better than an exponential one. The passage defines an overbought market as one whose prices have risen significantly over a defined period, potentially signaling weaker short-term returns. It is considered bearish and may prompt traders to sell. This relates to mean-reversion, the tendency for strong deviations from a trend to reverse over time. A backtest using the Relative Strength Index (RSI), with a stated 2-day RSI threshold above 95, found returns below the long-term average of about 0.05% per day during the first five days after an overbought reading, followed by a return toward the average. Positive media coverage can amplify overbought sentiment through FOMO, while negative coverage during declines can fuel panic. The passage cautions that the short-term edge is not directly tradable and that statistical rules have exceptions.

Fluentd adapters can normalize logs from applications with different formats into consistent, queryable event streams. The passage demonstrates this with Redis SLOWLOG output and Apache Storm data, using community plugins and shared container networking. Adapter containers can also provide rich MySQL health checks without modifying vendor-supplied database images, making monitoring logic modular and reusable.

Microservices divide an application into small, independently developed services connected through APIs. This approach supports focused teams, independent releases, and service-specific scaling, but it also complicates architecture, debugging, and failure diagnosis. Distributed patterns provide standardized approaches to these challenges.

Replicated stateless services use identical instances behind a load balancer to provide redundancy, availability, and horizontal scaling. Readiness probes distinguish running containers from instances prepared to serve requests. Kubernetes examples deploy a replicated dictionary service, a separate load-balancing Service, and readiness checks. Session-tracked variants route each user to a consistent replica, using IP hashing or application-level identifiers such as cookies; consistent hashing reduces user remapping when replicas change.

Caching can be added as a separate replicated tier rather than a sidecar on every application instance. This permits fewer, larger cache nodes with greater memory utilization. Varnish examples demonstrate caching, rate limiting, and “remaining calls” headers, including a 429 response when limits are exceeded. A replicated nginx tier can terminate TLS in front of Varnish, with separate edge and internal certificates. The complete stateless architecture consists of nginx, Varnish, and application deployments connected by load-balancing Services.

Sharded services divide requests or state among subsets of servers, allowing state too large for one machine to be distributed. Unlike replicated caches, sharded caches store unique data and therefore use memory more efficiently. Cache hit rate affects both throughput and latency, while shard failures force recalculation and can overload backend services; systems should therefore be load-tested with and without caching. Replicating each shard improves failure tolerance, permits rolling upgrades, and allows individual hot shards to scale independently.

Traffic can reach shards through per-application ambassadors or shared replicated routers. Ambassadors avoid an additional network hop but must accompany each client, while shared routers simplify deployment at the cost of scaling requirements and latency. Sharding functions should be deterministic and uniform, commonly using a hash modulo the shard count. Keys should include only request attributes that affect the response; path, country, or other relevant context can group equivalent requests without becoming overly specific. Consistent hashing minimizes data movement when the shard count changes.

Scatter/gather distributes a request to all leaf nodes in parallel and combines their partial results at a root. It can accelerate largely independent computations and may shard computation rather than data. Document-search examples use indexed term lookups and intersections, while leaf sharding combines unions from data partitions. Additional leaves eventually add overhead and amplify the straggler problem, because the slowest response determines total latency. Replicating and load-balancing each leaf shard improves availability and allows upgrades under load.

Function-as-a-service differs from serverless computing: event-driven FaaS is triggered by discrete events, while serverless describes a broader operational model. FaaS simplifies deployment, automatically scales and restarts functions, and encourages modular, stateless designs. Its forced decoupling makes dependencies, integration failures, and debugging difficult, requiring strong monitoring and alerting. It is generally unsuitable for long-running background work, services needing large in-memory data loaded on demand, or consistently high request volumes whose per-request pricing becomes inefficient.

The decorator pattern uses stateless functions to transform requests or responses, such as adding default values before an API call. Kubeless examples demonstrate deploying these functions on Kubernetes. Event-driven architectures suit independent, asynchronous, variable-rate activities such as sending two-factor authentication codes, while event pipelines represent required and optional actions as graphs of functions connected by webhooks or network calls.

Distributed ownership introduces additional complexity because a single owning process limits scaling and creates downtime when it fails. A singleton remains simpler and benefits from Kubernetes restart and rescheduling behavior, but software upgrades require stopping the existing instance. Master-election protocols address this by allowing a surviving replica to assume ownership when the current master fails.

The TPS7H500x-SP series comprises radiation-hardness-assured, fixed-frequency, peak-current-mode PWM controllers for space-grade DC-DC converters. They require external gate drivers, support switching frequencies up to 2 MHz, and can be used with buck, flyback, forward, active-clamp forward, push-pull, and full-bridge topologies.

Three synchronization modes are available. In internal oscillator mode, a required RT resistor sets the 100-kHz-to-2-MHz switching frequency, and SYNC outputs an in-phase clock at twice that frequency. In external synchronization mode, RT must float and SYNC must receive a 200-kHz-to-4-MHz clock at twice the desired switching frequency, with a recommended 50% duty cycle. Primary-secondary mode connects a primary controller’s SYNC output to a secondary controller’s SYNC input; it can synchronize independent converters or support interleaved operation. The secondary controller inverts the clock, producing a 90° or 270° phase shift.

Depending on the device, the controllers provide OUTA alone or OUTA/OUTB primary outputs and SRA or SRA/SRB synchronous-rectifier outputs. Each output has roughly 150-mA peak capability, making external gate-drive solutions recommended. OUTB is active only with a 50% duty-cycle limit on the TPS7H5001-SP and TPS7H5004-SP; SRB exists only on the TPS7H5001-SP. Synchronous-rectifier outputs remain off during soft start and begin switching when the SS voltage exceeds 1 V.

The TPS7H5003-SP has a typical 50-ns fixed dead time, while the TPS7H5001-SP and TPS7H5002-SP provide independently programmable primary-to-synchronous and synchronous-to-primary dead times through the PS and SP pins. Floating PS and SP pins select a typical 8-ns minimum dead time; populated values require 10-kΩ-to-300-kΩ resistors. Leading-edge blank time is typically fixed at 50 ns on the TPS7H5003-SP and resistor-programmable on the other devices, with the LEB pin requiring a 10-kΩ-to-300-kΩ resistor. Pulse skipping is triggered when COMP is below 0.3 V at the system-clock rising edge and the preceding duty cycle was below 25%, reducing peak inductor current during startup and maintaining output voltage at high frequencies.

The DCL pin configures maximum duty cycle: DCL connected to VLDO provides 100%, connection to AVSS provides 50%, and a floating pin provides 75% on supported devices. The TPS7H5004-SP supports only 50% duty cycle. OUTB and SRB are available only in the 50% configuration on applicable devices.

CS_ILIM senses transformer primary-side current for peak-current-mode PWM and overcurrent protection. OUTA/OUTB turn on with the internal clock and turn off when the sensed peak current reaches the COMP voltage divided by two, with a 150-mV comparator offset. A sense resistor from CS_ILIM to AVSS is required, and a nominal 1.05-V CS_ILIM threshold initiates protection.

At the current-limit threshold, the controller performs cycle-by-cycle limiting and charges the HICC capacitor with an 80-µA current until it reaches 0.6 V. Switching then stops, SS is discharged, and HICC is pulled to 1 V before a 1-µA restart current discharges it to 0.3 V, triggering another soft start. A minimum 3.3-nF HICC capacitor is recommended.

The FAULT pin supports user-defined external protection. A typical voltage above 0.6 V for the specified 0.4-µs-to-1.4-µs pulse width shuts down switching and discharges SS. When FAULT falls below its typical 0.5-V falling threshold, the controller waits approximately 15 switching cycles plus an internal delay before restarting soft start.

For duty cycles above 50%, slope compensation can mitigate subharmonic oscillation. Minimum compensation is 0.5 times the inductor’s falling-current slope, although a value equal to that slope is recommended. RSC sets the compensation. The controllers support Type 2A or Type 2B frequency compensation; Type 2A adds CHF for high-frequency noise attenuation. Thermal shutdown stops switching above a typical 175°C junction temperature and permits restart below 160°C.

A 500-kHz, 5-V synchronous push-pull GaN converter example uses a 205-kΩ RT resistor, 10-kΩ/1.4-kΩ feedback divider, 20.5-kΩ PS and SP resistors for approximately 25-ns dead time, and a 49.9-kΩ LEB resistor. Other selections include a 33-nF soft-start capacitor for approximately 7.5-ms startup, a 2.5 transformer turns ratio, 40-µH primary inductance, 170-V primary and 80-V secondary GaN FETs, a 0.47-µH output inductor, and 2.3 mF total output capacitance. The example also uses a 1:100 current-sense transformer, 7.5-Ω primary sense resistor, 3.3-nF HICC capacitor, 102-kΩ RSC resistor, and Type 2A compensation with a 10-kHz crossover, 40.2-kΩ RCOMP, 15-nF CCOMP, and 47-pF CHF.

The controllers operate from a 4-V-to-14-V supply and require at least 0.1 µF of VIN-to-AVSS bypassing. Layout guidance emphasizes separating feedback and control traces from switching nodes, minimizing high-dv/dt and high-di/dt loops, connecting analog and power grounds at one point, using wide high-current traces, and placing filtering, bypass, compensation, and VSENSE components close to their associated pins. The excerpt also provides ESD-handling guidance, revision information, related radiation-report links, and mechanical and orderable-package notes.

The disclosure describes systems, methods, and devices for wirelessly communicating glucose data between an analyte sensor system, display devices, and partner devices such as automatic or manual insulin delivery devices. A diabetes management partner interface allows authorized partner devices to modify stored configuration parameters according to their system requirements, including battery capacity, accuracy, communication protocol, regulatory requirements, and expected operating time.

Configurable parameters include wireless connectivity settings, access-control permissions, and analyte-data settings. Implementations may modify whitelists and timeout periods, advertisement structures, display-device access, calibration periods, factory-calibration-code use, remote-server services, and bolus-calculation parameters. The system may provide bolus recommendations, transmit diabetes-management feedback to displays, and notify displays if remote services become unavailable.

Additional embodiments classify remote devices into partner and nonpartner classes and select corresponding operating modes. These modes can restrict advertisements and accepted connection requests, deactivate certain device permissions, remove devices from whitelists, and revert settings when a partner connection ends. The disclosure also covers sequential connections to multiple partner devices, authorization information supplied by a server through a display, intermittent versus continuous connection models, and restoration of prior configuration settings.

Display-device applications may exchange pairing, dosage, analyte, and alert information with partner-device applications, display system status and connection settings, and configure or relay alerts through primary and secondary notification devices. A further method monitors medicament-delivery device operability using information concerning reservoir changes, pump rewind or priming, cannula filling, and fluid pressure, optionally combined with analyte data.

Israel and Myanmar signed an education agreement to develop Holocaust education addressing intolerance, racism, anti-Semitism and xenophobia. Myanmar supported Israel’s Jerusalem embassy opening, while Israel continued selling Myanmar weapons despite UN accusations. Some social media users viewed textbook editing as an attempt to reshape history.

NVIDIA’s RTX Blackwell architecture expands hardware ray tracing, GPU scheduling, media processing, power efficiency, and neural rendering. Fourth-generation RT Cores support Linear Swept Spheres, including variable-radius sphere segments and direct spheres. Hair rendering with LSS is reported as about twice as fast as DOTS while using roughly one-fifth the geometry VRAM. Shader Execution Reordering 2.0 improves reorder-logic efficiency twofold and precision, is controlled through an application API, and accelerates neural shading by directing coherent work to Tensor Cores. Existing path-traced games and production renderers can benefit from its Blackwell enhancements without code changes.

The programmable AI Management Processor uses a dedicated RISC-V processor to schedule GPU contexts independently of the system CPU. It follows Microsoft’s HAGS model, coordinates AI and graphics workloads, reduces CPU-GPU communication and latency, and can improve frame pacing, multitasking, first-response times, and quality of service.

Blackwell adds H.264 and HEVC hardware encoding and decoding for 4:2:2 chroma sampling. Compared with uncompressed 4:4:4, 4:2:2 uses two-thirds as much frame data while retaining twice the color resolution of 4:2:0. The ninth-generation NVENC improves AV1 and HEVC quality by 5% in BD-BR PSNR, adds 4:2:2 encoding, and offers an AV1 Ultra High Quality mode providing another 5% improvement. Combined gains can reach 15%. The RTX 5090 supports three encoders and two decoders, providing over 50% generational export-speed improvement and four times the speed of an RTX 3090. Sixth-generation NVDEC provides twice-as-fast H.264 decoding and 4:2:2 support. DisplayPort 2.1b supports 80 Gbps via UHBR 20, including 8K at 165 Hz and 4K at 480 Hz with DSC and a DP80LL-certified cable.

Blackwell’s Max-Q work includes advanced clock, power, and voltage-rail gating; independently controlled rails for GPU cores and memory; and clocks that adapt to workload changes 1,000 times faster than earlier architectures. Its deepest sleep state is entered ten times faster than on Ada, and an example involving small-language-model inference showed power savings of up to 50%.

DLSS 4 adds Multi Frame Generation, which can create up to three additional frames for every traditionally rendered frame. Its generation model is 40% faster, uses 30% less VRAM, and uses an AI-based optical-flow model. Enhanced Flip Metering moves pacing to the display engine, whose doubled pixel-processing capability supports higher resolutions and refresh rates. DLSS 4 also replaces convolutional models with transformer-based models for Super Resolution, Ray Reconstruction, and Deep Learning Anti-Aliasing. Transformers can use twice as many parameters and identify longer-range patterns, improving temporal stability, motion detail, lighting detail, ghosting, and denoiser artifact reduction.

Blackwell introduces a path toward neural shaders through the Cooperative Vectors API for DirectX 12 and Vulkan and differentiable Slang features, allowing graphics shaders to use Tensor Cores. Potential technologies include neural texture compression, neural materials, neural radiance caching, RTX Skin, and RTX Neural Faces. Neural materials approximate complex multilayer optics in real time; neural texture compression reduces texture storage demands; Neural Radiance Cache infers multiple lighting bounces after one traced bounce using networks trained on live game data; RTX Skin brings ray-traced subsurface scattering to games; and Neural Faces uses a TensorRT-optimized generative model to infer realistic faces from rasterized faces and 3D pose data.

The full GB202 chip contains 92.2 billion transistors, 24,576 CUDA Cores, 192 RT Cores, 768 Tensor Cores, and a 512-bit memory interface; it underlies the RTX 5090. GB203 has 45.6 billion transistors, 10,752 CUDA Cores, 84 RT Cores, 336 Tensor Cores, and a 256-bit interface, and is used by the RTX 5080 and RTX 5070 Ti. GB205 has 31 billion transistors, 6,400 CUDA Cores, 50 RT Cores, 200 Tensor Cores, and a 192-bit interface for the RTX 5070. The document states that specifications may change and includes warranty, liability, trademark, and high-risk-use limitations.

An appellate court reversed an order directing plaintiff Jane Kursa to serve a further bill of particulars in her action against Robert Barratiere et al., holding that her delay in supplying particulars could not excuse the defendants' failure to seek relief within 10 days, as required by CPLR 3042(d), or to allege special circumstances justifying their delay.

U.S. claims against Russia arose from the seizure of the bark Cape Horn Pigeon. Russia admitted the seizure was unjustifiable and indemnity was due, but repudiated the principal claim for loss of the vessel's services, equipment, and crew; itemized expenses are annexed in a bill of damages. On January 27 (February 8), 1899, the Chargé d'Affaires offered $42,000 in compromise without prejudice to the claimants' right to full recovery by arbitration or negotiation; on March 13/25, 1899, Russia rejected it and countered with $2,500 (Exhibits T and U). The passage argues that the Okhotsk Sea, separated from the North Pacific by the Kuril Islands, has never been occupied or closed by Russia and, under the 1824 and 1825 treaties and customary foreign whaling, is not closed beyond ordinary jurisdictional waters. Affidavits of Lapham, Baker, and Cleveland and the captain's sworn testimony (Exhibit H) show the Russian commander declared the sea closed and ordered whalers seized, a claim not accordant with accepted international law. Article I of the 1824 treaty with the United States guarantees freedom of navigation, fishing, and trade in the Pacific.

The lecture derives collective, or coherent, Thomson scattering, focusing on cases where the scattering-vector wavelength exceeds the Debye length and therefore samples collective plasma motion. Relevant low-frequency modes include ion acoustic waves and electron plasma waves. Such modes carry substantial momentum but much less energy than the probe laser, giving them phase velocities well below the speed of light. Plasma fluctuations occur naturally in every direction, so a laser can scatter from them, transferring energy and momentum and potentially enhancing the mode.

The expected spectrum contains a low-frequency ion-acoustic feature and a slightly higher-frequency electron-plasma-wave feature. Thermal effects and the range of angles collected by the spectrometer broaden these features. Detector placement determines the scattering direction, while the chosen angle and incident wavelength determine the scattering-vector magnitude; dispersion relations then connect measured frequency shifts to plasma modes.

The derivation proceeds in two steps. First, the scattered-power spectrum is expressed through electron-density fluctuations. Using the Klimontovich distribution, the total scattered field retains each particle’s position, unlike the incoherent treatment. This permits phase differences and interference among particles. The result expresses the power through experimental constants and the spectral density function \(S(k,\omega)\), which is determined by the normalized squared Fourier transform of density fluctuations.

Second, density fluctuations are calculated by treating each electron and ion as a test particle and finding how the surrounding plasma responds through polarization and shielding charge. The resulting general spectral density includes electron and ion distribution functions evaluated at the phase velocity, together with their plasma responses. Electron-ion cross terms vanish. Resonances occur when the plasma permittivity \(\epsilon=0\), corresponding to the plasma’s normal modes and producing the spectral features.

The plasma response is derived from the collisionless Vlasov equation, appropriate because the relevant phase velocities are comparable to thermal velocities and require Landau damping treatment. The susceptibility contains a velocity-integral pole at \(v=\omega/k\), evaluated using the Landau contour. For Maxwellian distributions, the susceptibility can be expressed through the Debye length, a coupling parameter, and a complex function of phase velocity divided by thermal speed that is related to the plasma dispersion function. In practice, measured spectral shapes and frequency shifts are typically fitted with model parameters because absolute spectrometer calibration is difficult.

The document standardizes a 4 KB, page-aligned Guest-Hypervisor Communication Block (GHCB) for interoperable communication between guest operating systems and hypervisors using SEV-ES or SEV-SNP. It defines required non-automatic exit handling, minimum guest state, protocol negotiation, hypervisor feature advertisement, and special behaviors such as NMI handling and SMP booting.

Version 2 adds initial SEV-SNP support and a 52-bit feature bitmap. Later revisions add error handling, a VLEK GUID, APIC ID retrieval, multiple VMPL support, page-state-change requests, the SEV-SNP Confidential Computing Blob EFI protocol, SEV-TIO, and Secure AVIC.

The GHCB address is communicated through the VMCB and MSR 0xc001_0130. Its MSR protocol supports feature negotiation, CPUID requests, GHCB GPA registration and removal, AP reset hold, page-state changes, VMPL requests, and guest termination. SEV-SNP guests must register a GHCB GPA for each vCPU and VMPL level before using it.

For non-automatic exits, the guest handles a #VC exception, copies required state into the GHCB, invokes VMGEXIT, and copies returned results back. The VALID_BITMAP identifies valid fields, while SW_EXITINFO1 and SW_EXITINFO2 communicate errors and results. The specification also defines the SNP secrets-page guest area, EFI configuration table, and guest-request protocols for accessing firmware. Extended guest requests can return GUID-identified certificates and specify how many pages are needed to hold them.

Massachusetts General Hospital’s Pre-Admission Testing Area (PATA) required all surgical patients to complete pre-operative work-ups to ensure safe anesthesia and surgery. Despite its importance to patient safety and MGH’s reputation, PATA had struggled for years with long waits, limited capacity, shared departmental ownership, unclear triage rules, manual processes, and inconsistent patient records. A patient’s complaint about spending nearly four hours at PATA for only 90 minutes of provider contact prompted the anesthesia chief and task force to seek improvements.

PATA had 12 exam rooms and typically scheduled four patients every 30 minutes, averaging about 55 patients per day. Although patients received 80–90 minutes of direct care, average appointments lasted 2.5 hours, and many exceeded four hours. Providers routinely worked until 6 p.m. and sometimes 8 p.m. PATA served only about 65% of surgical outpatients, prioritizing complex cases; healthier patients were assessed in the operating room on the day of surgery. This contributed to delayed surgeries, overtime, cancellations, staff strain, and an estimated 57,000 minutes of lost operating-room productivity annually.

Earlier proposals to build a satellite clinic or incorporate PATA reforms into broader perioperative projects failed because of fiscal, political, cultural, space, or resource constraints. A formal task force formed in 2008 and focused on internal changes such as better triage, online patient education, and electronic records, but these ideas required additional resources and were not expected to address the main problems.

An MBA intern joined the task force in May 2009 to assess PATA through staff interviews, patient and provider shadowing, time studies, and workflow mapping. The analysis confirmed that patients spent more time waiting than with providers and revealed substantial process variability. Each visit generally involved check-in, vital signs and an EKG, a required nursing assessment, an anesthesiologist examination and consent, blood work, and checkout. Manual chart handling, arrival-order rather than appointment-order service, paper-based assignments, difficulty locating available providers, reduced staffing during lunch, and communication errors created delays and sometimes left work-ups incomplete.

At a June 2009 task-force meeting, members proposed extending clinic hours, adding staff and rooms, reducing patient volume, or redesigning operations without more resources. Task-force leader Susan Moss requested data-driven analysis of each scenario, including reconsideration of staffing, responsibilities, technology, and existing assumptions. The intern was asked to use the collected data to identify practical improvements for the next meeting.

A four-year naturalistic follow-up of the ePOD-methylphenidate randomized controlled trial used pharmacological MRI to assess long-term effects of stimulant treatment on cerebral blood flow and dopamine reactivity in stimulant-naive boys and men with ADHD. MRI was performed before and after an acute methylphenidate challenge at baseline and follow-up, with a one-week stimulant washout before follow-up; 32 adolescents and 24 adults were included in the final sample.

The study found no evidence that stimulant use was associated with longitudinal changes in resting relative cerebral blood flow or methylphenidate-responsive blood flow, nor were the short-term effects of initial randomized treatment detectable at follow-up. However, age-dependent associations with medication exposure were identified across visits. Adults receiving greater cumulative doses or longer treatment durations had lower thalamic resting blood flow, whereas adolescents with greater exposure had lower medial prefrontal cortex blood-flow responses to methylphenidate. These associations were already present before treatment initiation and were unrelated to ADHD symptom severity, preventing attribution to treatment effects. Whole-brain responses were associated with noradrenaline transporter distribution but not dopamine transporter or dopamine receptor distributions.

Limitations included attrition, assumed prescription adherence, use of different MRI scanners at baseline and follow-up, and recruitment of males only. The authors concluded that larger longitudinal studies are needed to determine whether developmental effects emerge in young adulthood and to assess pharmacological MRI’s potential for optimizing ADHD treatment.

A cross-sectional study assessed personal health literacy, school health literacy environment, and health outcomes among 7,264 teachers from 11 primary and secondary schools in Zhengzhou, China. Teachers completed online questionnaires assessing sociodemographics, personal health literacy (HLS19-Q12), school health literacy environment (OHLS-Q-SF), health status, health-compromising behaviours, healthcare use, and out-of-pocket costs. Multiple imputation and multivariable logistic regression were used.

Mean personal health literacy was 75.17/100; 56.9% of teachers had problematic or inadequate literacy, while 31.0% perceived a supportive school health literacy environment. Additionally, 15.0% reported poor health, 75.2% had at least one health-compromising behaviour, 82.4% used at least one health service, and 60.7% spent at least RMB 1,000 on healthcare.

After full adjustment, inadequate personal health literacy was associated with poor health status (OR 5.79), health-compromising behaviours (OR 2.90), health service use (OR 2.73), and higher healthcare costs (OR 2.51) compared with excellent literacy. A non-supportive school environment was also associated with these outcomes. Literacy levels varied by factors including age, school type, marital status, teaching tenure, subject, health awareness, chronic conditions, and insurance type.

The authors noted limitations including nonrepresentative convenience sampling, possible self-report error, and inability to establish causality. They recommended combining educational interventions and organisational changes while targeting groups with lower literacy.

Linguist Martin O’Leary mapped how seemingly unrelated words share ancient roots. Proto-Indo-European, spoken roughly 4,500–2,500 BC and likely originating north of the Caspian Sea, became the ancestor of more than 440 languages, including English, French, Spanish, German, Persian, Russian and Ukrainian. Because no contemporary texts survive, linguists have had to reconstruct it. O’Leary’s viral Twitter charts traced cognates such as “architect” and “dachshund” to *teks* (“to weave”), “blue,” “phlegm” and “flamingo” to *bhel* (“to shine”), “sh*t” and “science” to *sek* (“split” or “peel”), and “doom,” “orifice” and “chauffeur” to *dhe* (“to put”).

The ADS7828 captures the selected analog input on an internal capacitor array during hold mode. Input current depends on conversion rate because the source must charge the sampling capacitor, typically 25 pF.

The device supports an internal 2.5 V reference or an external reference as low as 50 mV. A 5 V supply requires an external 5 V reference for full dynamic range, while a 2.7 V supply can use the internal reference. LSB size equals the reference voltage divided by 4096; lowering the reference increases the apparent offset, gain error, and internal-noise contribution. Gaussian internal noise can be reduced by averaging consecutive results.

The ADS7828 operates as an I²C slave supporting standard, fast, and high-speed modes at 100 kHz, 400 kHz, and 3.4 MHz. The master controls the clock, bus access, and START/STOP conditions. The address prefix is 10010, while power-up states of the A1–A0 pins select the device address, allowing up to four devices with the same prefix on one bus. The device supports slave-receiver and slave-transmitter operation.

After being write-addressed and receiving the command byte, the ADS7828 begins conversion. Each 12-bit result is read as two bytes, with the first byte sent before the second. In high-speed mode, the device stretches the clock until conversion is complete. A repeated START can support continuous conversions and preserve high-speed mode; a STOP returns the device to fast/standard mode.

The internal reference defaults to off and must be enabled with PD1 for each internal-reference conversion, with appropriate settling time for 12-bit accuracy. External-reference operation requires PD1 to remain low and the external reference to be settled. Optimal layout requires clean, well-bypassed power, a 0.1 µF ceramic capacitor near the device, potentially 1–10 µF additional supply decoupling, and a clean analog-ground connection. External-reference noise and supply ripple can directly affect conversion results.

Interfacial mobility is a key coarse-grained parameter governing microstructural evolution, but reliably connecting atomistic simulations to continuum models remains difficult, particularly for solute–interface interactions and solute drag. Common molecular-dynamics methods assume Markovian, memory-free motion and are limited by low temperatures, sluggish interfaces, strong driving forces, or persistent transient sub-diffusion. This work adapts generalized memory-correction techniques to a computationally efficient two-dimensional kinetic Monte Carlo model with controllable boundary stiffness, solute binding, and diffusion kinetics. The study demonstrates the inconsistency of the capillary fluctuation method, proposes an alternative mobility extraction based on mean boundary motion, and applies a time-convolutionless propagator approach to characterize interfacial dynamics with memory.

Dr. Kellie Leitch’s leadership campaign raises Canadian values while arguing that female genital mutilation (FGM) occurs in Canada. Citing an Ontario Human Rights Commission report, the passage says evidence indicates FGM is practised in Ontario and elsewhere in Canada, including through medical trips abroad, although reliable statistics are unavailable. It describes FGM as an ancient cultural practice and recounts cases and requests for reinfibulation, including concerns that childbirth may require reopening and that some procedures are not chosen by the women. Canadian doctors cited call for a ban on medically unnecessary genital mutilation and criticize cultural accommodation. The passage concludes that FGM is not a Canadian value and suggests screening prospective citizens to ensure it is not among their values.

The memorandum predicts that peace will not end the war abruptly, that demobilization will follow the peace conference, and that hostilities may continue during early discussions. German peace propaganda is expected to attract Allied left-wing groups through formulas resembling Allied war aims, while exploiting divisions within and among Allied nations. The Reichstag resolution and Stockholm conference plan weakened Russian and Western support for the war. Germany has maintained effective unity in Central Europe while weakening the Allied coalition.

The Allied response has two forms: suppressing pro-concession opinion, which is costly and may deepen class divisions and encourage mob violence, and the President’s reply to the Pope, which emphasizes broadly accepted purposes to unify the Allies and compel concessions from the Right. European governments avoided replying because their domestic political situations made disagreement dangerous.

The memorandum maintains that peace terms are secondary to defeating or pressuring the German army and nation. Public debate over territory could reduce morale, turn the war into a narrow nationalist struggle, and split the coalition.

The study develops an agent-based model of the Netherlands’ first COVID-19 wave, from February 27 to June 1, 2020. It represents 170,721 agents—approximately one per 100 residents—across 380 municipalities and 11 demographic groups, using hourly mobility and contact patterns derived from mobile-phone signals, population data, and surveys. A stochastic SEIR model incorporates transmission, mobility reductions, behavioral changes, mixing patterns, and school closures, with transmission parameters calibrated to national hospital-admission data and four intervention phases.

The model reproduced national hospitalization trends and the observed initial doubling time and broadly reflected the epidemic’s spread from the south through western cities to the north. It identified mobility restrictions as the largest contributor to control: without them, hospital admissions would have approximately doubled. Behavioral changes also reduced transmission, while school closures had limited effects because schools closed relatively late.

The study then tested municipality-level lockdowns triggered when local infectious prevalence exceeded thresholds of 3%, 1%, 0.33%, or 0.1%. Higher thresholds produced greater health burdens but fewer restrictions; lower thresholds reduced admissions while keeping more municipalities intervention-free. The 3% threshold increased admissions by 157% to about 19,000, compared with roughly 13,000 under the national approach. The 0.33% threshold added 410 admissions and allowed 167 municipalities to delay interventions, with interventions-free municipalities concentrated in the rural, less densely populated north and east. The authors concluded that timely local monitoring could permit postponed or tailored interventions with limited additional hospitalizations.

Limitations include the omission of household-level mixing and geographically or demographically specific mobility changes. Mobile-phone data lacked movement sequences, required random daily travel assumptions, and covered only two weeks in 2019; international travel was also excluded. The framework may be adapted to other countries and policy questions where sufficiently detailed demographic, mobility, mixing, hospitalization, and surveillance data are available.

MIT Sloan’s Women in Management club spent 11 months preparing its third annual conference, themed “Dare to Fail: Taking Risks When it Matters Most.” Three co-presidents—Rachel, Lea, and Tarini—handled sponsorship, operations, and marketing, while conference directors Janet and Merrill recruited speakers and developed the program. The five struggled over decision-making authority, communication, and workload, particularly when Merrill’s departure for a start-up left Janet recruiting speakers largely alone.

The 2012 conference had sold out with more than 400 attendees and strong administrative support. For 2013, the team aimed to sell 500 tickets, secure 15 speakers, and raise $40,000. Speaker recruitment progressed slowly, keynotes were difficult to confirm, and January’s cancellation of General Janet Wolfenbarger created additional financial and marketing concerns. A replacement venture-capital speaker was quickly secured. The conference ultimately sold out, while sponsorships reached $38,000. Operations also faced problems, including unavailable overflow space, the loss of an administratively sponsored alumnae breakfast, and uncertainty over catering and other costs.

As the conference approached, forecasts warned of a major Boston snowstorm, with predicted snowfall ranging widely from about three inches to more than four feet. MIT’s Student Life Office considered possible closures, while attendees and a corporate sponsor asked about cancellation or postponement. The team continued preparations, identified local substitutes for speakers, and informed attendees that the event would proceed as scheduled unless circumstances changed.

At a February 7 meeting, the leadership considered three options: cancel before vendors began setup at 2:00 p.m.; hold a shortened conference with concurrent speakers; or delay the decision for more accurate weather and travel information. Rescheduling was ruled out because the organizers would be graduating and the venue was unavailable through May. All 15 speakers remained willing to attend, but cancellation could leave perishable catering costs unrecoverable, require ticket refunds, affect sponsors, and damage SWIM’s reputation. A possible MIT closure would prohibit the event and increase rental costs. The Student Life Office associate director told the team that cancellation could be devastating but likewise proceeding into a storm without adequate attendance would be devastating, and that he would support its decision. The case ends with the leadership still weighing its options.

Researchers studied 105 toy-loving pet dogs, measuring reactions to inaccessible toys, choices between toys and food, and recovery after toy removal. Thirty-three showed addictive-like motivation for toy play, especially terriers and shepherds. An unpublished survey of about 1,600 dogs estimated that roughly 3% showed such behavior. Researchers cautioned against directly equating it with human addiction and suggested that play itself, rather than the toy, drives the attraction.

September FOMC minutes showed officials broadly favored further rate cuts as the labor market weakened, though inflation risks remained. The committee voted 11-1 to cut its target range by 25 basis points to 4%-4.25%; newly appointed Governor Stephen Miran alone dissented in favor of a 50-basis-point cut. A 10-9 split favored two additional quarter-point cuts at the remaining 2025 meetings, while projections indicated one cut in both 2026 and 2027 before the rate settled near 3%. Some participants favored caution because financial conditions did not appear particularly restrictive. Officials expected inflation to return to 2% and generally viewed tariffs as unlikely to create lasting inflation. The government shutdown was delaying key economic data ahead of the October meeting, potentially complicating policy decisions despite market expectations of cuts in October and December.

The paper introduces the LLM-proposed Open Taxonomy (LOT), an inductive method for distinguishing large reasoning models’ reasoning patterns without relying on predefined taxonomies. LOT compares paired reasoning traces, proposes natural-language distinguishing features, annotates traces with those features, and trains a logistic classifier to identify their source model. When classification fails, new features are added and the classifier is retrained. Two representations are used: presence of reasoning and bag of reasoning, with the latter also capturing feature frequency.

LOT was applied to 24,444 traces from 12 open-source reasoning models across five science, mathematics, and coding datasets. It classified substantially different models with 80–100% accuracy and generally outperformed few-shot prompting, VML, and a human-defined taxonomy. The resulting taxonomies showed that smaller Qwen3 models more often exhibited circular reasoning, redundant evaluation, and inconsistent theory selection, whereas Qwen3-32B more consistently recalled relevant knowledge and checked methodological applicability. Models sharing a base model family had more similar reasoning patterns, while harder problems sometimes required frequency-based features to distinguish models. Domain fine-tuning also influenced reasoning: Seed-Coder used coding-oriented approaches for 20% of mathematics questions, compared with 2% for Qwen3-8B.

Reasoning features were associated with answer correctness. Test-time interventions that modified reasoning traces improved GPQA accuracy for Qwen3-0.6B, Qwen3-4B, and Qwen3-8B by 3.3–5.7%; Qwen3-1.7B declined after summarization. Limitations include the inability to establish causal links between model attributes such as size and reasoning, incomplete coverage of possible reasoning differences, sensitivity to LLM annotator choice, and uncertainty about the stability of reasoning-style interventions.

**Summary**

This is the final lecture (23) of MIT 14.13, on policy with behavioral agents. The lecturer reviews neoclassical rationales for government intervention — externalities (addressed via optimal taxes), equity (social security, unemployment insurance), monopoly/competition policy and antitrust, public goods, information failures and under-investment in innovation, and macroeconomic policy — then shifts to behavioral economics and "internalities," meaning consumers fail to fully internalize the costs and benefits of their choices on their future selves.

Paternalism, defined following David Laibson as "an attempt to influence or control people's conduct for their own good" (motivated by internalities rather than externalities), may be warranted by self-control problems, inconsistent preferences, limited attention, forgetfulness, learning failures, overoptimism, overconfidence, projection, and attribution bias. Not all behavioral findings justify intervention: risk, reference-dependent, and social preferences are preferences rather than errors; motivated beliefs (e.g., declining to learn one's health status) are ambiguous; defaults, frames, and nudges are instruments rather than justifications; discrimination is a clear case for intervention; poverty and mental health bear on biases but suggest support programs and encouraging experimentation rather than prescription.

The lecture distinguishes hard paternalism (forcing choices by changing prices, taxing, subsidizing, or banning products) from soft paternalism (Thaler and Sunstein's libertarian paternalism — influencing behavior while preserving freedom of choice) and Camerer et al.'s asymmetric paternalism (helping those who err while minimally interfering with those who optimize, illustrated by cigarette taxes helping mistaken smokers but harming those who knowingly smoke). Arguments against paternalism include informational limits and heterogeneity, government waste and capture, corruption, slippery-slope concerns, freedom of choice as an intrinsic value, and practical implementation and policy-selection problems. Arguments in favor include that people make mistakes, that some decisions are costly or confusing to make alone (e.g., screening retirement plans), and that many objections vanish with voluntary, opt-out soft paternalism. Popular paternalistic policies include Social Security, Medicare, 401(k) menu restrictions, FDA drug bans, mandatory schooling, cigarette and alcohol taxes (varying widely across states), blue laws, and mask mandates; unpopular ones include helmet and seatbelt laws, speed limits, drug prohibition, and 16-ounce soda bans.

Evidence on nudges is mixed: automatic 401(k) enrollment and text-message court reminders produced large effects; the HeartStrong trial produced none; and DellaVigna's comparison of 26 trials and 71 nudges shows large published effects but mostly small, often insignificant effects in UK government nudge units, suggesting publication bias and implementation problems. Energy comparison letters (Allcott and co-authors with Opower) reduce consumption, but some people pay to avoid them, so asymmetric paternalism suggests respecting opt-outs. Because any default influences behavior, the real debate is over optimal soft paternalism rather than paternalism versus none. The Save More Tomorrow (SMarT) plan is presented as a successful libertarian paternalism: employees voluntarily opt in to automatic contribution increases timed to pay raises, may opt out at any time, and the design exploits present bias, loss aversion, and defaults to boost saving.

Regarding market solutions, firms both exploit and target naive consumers who may not seek help, motivating behavioral industrial organization and regulation such as the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau. Thaler and Sunstein's "sludges" — firms using friction and nudges against consumers, such as rebate mail-in requirements or burdensome voter registration — should be identified and eliminated alongside implementing helpful nudges. The lecture concludes that psychological considerations matter for economic choices, that individuals should understand their own biases, experiment, seek advice and psychological support, and apply these insights to designing teams, incentives, and products; it recommends books by Cialdini, Ariely, Mullainathan and Shafir, Kahneman, and Lewis. The lecturer also mentions no formal course evaluations this year, office hours, and European opportunities.

Researchers studying germ transmission on airplanes advise passengers concerned about colds or flu to take a window seat and remain seated, since aisle passengers moved more often and nearby seats posed the highest risk. Across 10 flights, researchers tested cabin surfaces and air and observed passenger movement; only one person coughed, and none of 18 cold and flu viruses were found. Modeling a hypothetical infectious passenger in row 14 estimated that one of about 150 passengers would become infected. The Boeing-funded study was published in PNAS. Outside experts called the findings novel but cautioned that the small study and lack of observed infections limit broad conclusions.

Amazon added Outlook.com calendar support to Alexa, enabling voice-based event additions and schedule reviews via the iOS app. Echo Tap speakers also gained hands-free activation, spatial voice response, and an estimated eight-hour battery life.

SOS pressure defense is presented as a practical basketball system for confronting increasingly powerful offenses and can reinforce containment defenses or any defensive system. Its six core elements are:

1. Individual and team defensive fundamentals taught progressively from one-on-one to five-on-five, with regular review.
2. S-O-S action words—SET, ON, SMOTHER, SNUGGLE, OFF, and STRIKE—to trigger specific on- and off-ball actions.
3. “Operation Checkpoint,” which directs opponents away from high-percentage areas toward court positions at least 18 feet from the hoop.
4. Aggressive switching on screens to eliminate hesitation and disrupt offensive sets.
5. Beginning transition pressure in the backcourt through defined assignments that deny passing lanes and steer ball handlers toward unfavorable scoring areas.
6. Clear, specific roles for every defender, coordinated to force turnovers, restrict shooting opportunities, cut passing lanes, and rebound effectively.

The approach emphasizes communication, daily reinforcement, motivation, and coordinated execution.

Researchers used daily growth lines in fossilized teeth from Protoceratops and Hypacrosaurus embryos to estimate incubation periods: nearly three months for 194-gram Protoceratops and six months for Hypacrosaurus embryos exceeding 4 kg. The study, published in the Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences, found that dinosaur incubation was more similar to primitive reptiles than birds, suggesting birds evolved faster incubation after diverging from other dinosaurs. Prolonged incubation increased exposure to predators, starvation and flooding, while dinosaurs also required substantial resources and more than a year to mature. These reproductive traits may have placed non-avian dinosaurs at a disadvantage relative to birds, whose shorter incubation periods enabled faster reproduction and recovery after the Cretaceous extinction.

After Trump issued an executive order ending birthright citizenship, federal courts nationwide challenged it. The administration initially asked the Supreme Court to stop judges from issuing universal injunctions, and in a 6-3 ruling, the court rejected that remedy without deciding the order’s constitutionality. District courts in New Mexico and New Hampshire temporarily blocked enforcement for groups of affected children, while the 9th Circuit held that the order conflicts with the Fourteenth Amendment. The administration then asked the Supreme Court to review the 9th Circuit and New Hampshire decisions. Acceptance requires four votes; if granted, oral arguments would likely occur in 2026, with a decision expected in late June or early July 2026.

The Wisconsin Court of Appeals affirmed Andrew Anton Sabo’s convictions for possessing cocaine with intent to deliver as a second or subsequent offense and two counts of being a felon in possession of a firearm. Sabo challenged the warrant supporting the search of his residence, the denial of a Franks-Mann hearing, and the refusal to disclose the informant’s identity.

A citizen informant reported seeing Sabo load a handgun and process and package cocaine at the residence. Officer Rodolfo Ayala identified Sabo from a booking photograph, confirmed his felony probation status, and observed him at the residence. The warrant search yielded two firearms, suspected crack cocaine, drug paraphernalia, cash, and other evidence. The court held that the informant’s detailed observations and police corroboration established probable cause. It also found that Sabo failed to make the required substantial preliminary showing of deliberate or reckless falsehoods to warrant a Franks-Mann hearing. Because the informant was reasonably believed to be credible and reliable, the court upheld the denial of disclosure. Sabo had pleaded guilty and received a 16-year sentence consisting of eight years of confinement and eight years of extended supervision.

The passage describes an Internet-based overlay network for transporting customer traffic, particularly IPsec traffic between branch-office routers and an overlay provider. It reviews content delivery networks, overlay routing over the public Internet, and WAN alternatives such as MPLS and VPN concentrators, including their cost and performance limitations.

In the disclosed approach, a customer edge router resolves a service hostname through the overlay’s authoritative DNS and establishes an outer IKEv2/IPsec tunnel to a selected ingress edge, called an NEdge. The NEdge performs a secondary DNS lookup using the router’s IP address. If it determines that another edge is a better ingress region, it sends an IKEv2 redirect to the router, which establishes a new tunnel to the redirected edge. Return traffic can follow multiple overlay paths, with duplicate packets removed and network address translation used to route responses.

The NEdge also performs periodic authoritative-DNS lookups for connected routers. If its region is no longer appropriate, it deliberately drops IP-SLA liveness probes sent over the tunnel. The router’s event manager then initiates use of an alternate route and performs another hostname lookup, allowing it to reconnect to a more suitable NEdge. The overlay can authenticate DMVPN routers through outer IKEv2 tunnels and carry end-to-end IPsec traffic between branch and hub or branch routers. The described functionality may be implemented in software on standard processors and DNS-compliant servers.

The lecture analyzes exact solutions of nonlinear PDEs, focusing on inviscid Burgers’ equation with a delta-function source. The solution is shown to consist of a linear rarefaction fan followed by a shock. Conservation of mass places the shock at \(X=\sqrt{2t}\), and the proposed solution is verified using the shock jump and entropy conditions.

A minimization formula provides the general solution and automatically produces the appropriate fans and shocks. The lecture also derives this behavior through the viscous Burgers equation: an integral transformation followed by an exponential substitution converts it into the linear heat equation. As viscosity approaches zero, the solution concentrates near the minimum of an exponent, yielding the inviscid solution and its shocks.

The lecture then introduces the nonlinear Korteweg–de Vries equation and its relation to one-dimensional water waves. Numerical experiments with interacting traveling waves inspired the discovery of hidden linear structure, infinitely many conserved quantities, and integrable nonlinear PDEs. Such waves are called solitons because they emerge from interactions with their shapes intact. The nonlinear Schrödinger equation is cited as another completely integrable equation.

Finally, the lecture notes that the Navier–Stokes equations are not among these integrable examples and that global existence, particularly in three dimensions, remains unresolved. The next lecture is to cover numerical solutions, finite differences, and the level-set method.

WORD and BYTE writes to PMC registers can corrupt subsequent PMC register writes. A shadow register holds write data, but the operational register is updated at 32-bit granularity regardless of write size, and the inactive byte lane retains stale data, corrupting future writes. Corruption may be local or cross-register. An SMI I/O trap on ACPI-defined registers can prevent this.
