A California Senate committee investigating possible wholesale electricity-price manipulation held Enron and Mirant in contempt for failing to produce subpoenaed records. The companies had until July 10 to comply, avoiding possible Senate sanctions that could include fines or jail for executives. Enron disputed the committee’s jurisdiction, while Mirant said it wanted to cooperate; six other generators were temporarily spared citations while negotiating confidentiality terms.

State regulators unanimously exempted 13 oil refineries, related pipelines and chemical facilities, and some support services from rolling blackouts to protect gasoline production and avoid shortages and price increases. The PUC was still considering exemption requests from nearly 10,000 other businesses. Separately, Southern California Edison’s parent, Edison International, obtained $1.19 billion in financing at rates as high as 14 percent to pay debts, easing immediate pressure but leaving the company about $33 million short of its 2001 obligations.

Standard & Poor’s removed California from “credit watch” after the state obtained $4.3 billion in bridge loans for electricity purchases, though it retained an A-plus rating with a negative outlook and warned that power-buying spending remained a concern. State Controller Kathleen Connell said unedited versions of long-term electricity contracts would be released despite possible gubernatorial appeal.

Secretary of State Bill Jones accused Gov. Gray Davis of mishandling the crisis, while Davis’s spokesman defended the governor’s energy orders and conservation measures. A Los Angeles Times poll found that most Californians believed energy companies had manipulated the market, about half rated Davis’s crisis response poorly, and more than 60 percent identified energy as the state’s top problem.

Congressional action on President Bush’s national energy plan was delayed by moderating gasoline prices, the lack of California summer outages, partisan divisions, and concern about environmental effects. Bush promoted $86 million in efficiency grants, federal efficiency standards, and nearly $300 million in restored conservation research. Efforts were under way to combine Democratic and Republican proposals involving conservation, fuel-efficient vehicles, reduced gasoline regulations, assistance for low-income consumers, and nuclear-power liability limits.

A UCLA study predicted that the energy crisis could reduce California’s gross state product by 0.7–1.5 percent, raise unemployment, and cause rolling blackouts. It argued that retail electricity prices matching wholesale costs could reduce outages and state debt, but Davis’s administration and other critics questioned its assumptions, including its failure to account for possible market manipulation.

Other developments included the opening of a 320-megawatt cogeneration plant near Bakersfield; a proposal that slightly reduced household voltage to create savings equivalent to 500 megawatts; a nearly 50 percent reduction in Southern California Gas July rates; and SMUD’s launch of a web-based demand exchange offering incentives for commercial and industrial customers to reduce peak electricity use.

Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan said California’s problems were easing but remained significant, and argued that temporary electricity price caps could encourage power-plant construction by providing investment certainty. The Federal Energy Regulatory Commission approved temporary New York measures to review and potentially reduce unusually high generator bids, following approval of price controls in California and ten other Western states using a regional proxy price of $92 per megawatt-hour.

The paper introduces NeuroAdapter, an end-to-end framework that reconstructs visual stimuli by conditioning Stable Diffusion directly on fMRI activity rather than routing brain signals through intermediate CLIP, DINO, or other embedding spaces. Surface fMRI responses are averaged across repetitions, divided into Schaefer cortical parcels, ranked by signal-to-noise ratio, and projected through parcel-specific linear mappings into 768-dimensional tokens. An IP-Adapter-style cross-attention module enables the diffusion U-Net to attend to these tokens. The Stable Diffusion model remains frozen while the mapper and new attention modules are trained; stochastic token dropout and min-SNR loss weighting are used for robustness and training stability. During evaluation, candidate reconstructions are generated with different seeds and selected using a brain encoder and their Pearson correlation with measured fMRI responses.

The paper also proposes IBBI, a bidirectional interpretability framework based on cross-attention dynamics. Its brain-directed view quantifies each parcel’s relative contribution across denoising steps, while its image-directed view maps where brain regions direct attention in the generated image. Causal masking experiments show that masking low-level visual regions generally preserves semantic content, whereas masking high-level regions substantially changes reconstructions.

Experiments use NSD, NSD-Imagery, and Deeprecon, with reconstruction quality assessed through eight pixel, structural, and semantic metrics. On NSD, NeuroAdapter is competitive with prior embedding-aligned methods on high-level semantic metrics, though its low-level improvements are more modest. Models trained on NSD also generalize comparably to imagery trials, and Deeprecon results indicate recovery of category-level information and properties such as shape, orientation, and color. The authors note variability in diffusion outputs and argue that image-quality benchmarks alone may not establish faithful brain decoding, motivating interpretability methods that link cortical parcels to image features.

Chelsea manager Antonio Conte urged his players to focus on Tuesday’s Premier League match at Huddersfield rather than think ahead to their Champions League tie with Barcelona. Theresa May is expected to ask her Cabinet to back a “soft” Brexit at a Chequers summit, including continued UK adherence to some EU product and agricultural standards, easier residence and work rights for EU citizens, and UK collection of EU customs duties. The proposals aim to preserve free movement of goods while allowing independent trade deals, but they have intensified Conservative divisions. Phillip Lee accused Brexiteers of planning a leadership coup, while William Hague warned ministers against pushing for a clean Brexit, saying Parliament could force a watered-down agreement and resignations could trigger a leadership contest.

In Bond v. District Court, the Colorado Supreme Court considered whether the Bond family could withhold notes and records from their mental-health therapists from discovery by YMCA in a negligence action arising from Erin Bond’s injuries. The Court held that the family had waived physician-patient and psychologist-patient privileges by seeking damages for mental suffering and psychiatric expenses. Nevertheless, it found the trial court abused its discretion by denying a protective order without balancing the family’s interest in preserving confidential communications and effective treatment against YMCA’s interest in obtaining evidence to contest their damage claims. Dr. Vary’s affidavit established that disclosure could cause embarrassment, oppression, and serious harm to treatment. The Court made its rule absolute and remanded for reconsideration under the proper balancing standard, noting possible procedures such as in camera reviews, restrictions on disclosure, and court-appointed experts. Original jurisdiction was justified because compelled disclosure would cause irreparable harm that could not be cured on appeal.
AOL announced that AIM, once a leading U.S. instant messaging service, will shut down permanently on December 15 after usage declined amid the rise of texting and social media.

Earth’s total solar eclipses occur because the Moon, though about 400 times smaller than the Sun, is roughly 400 times closer, making their apparent sizes match. The Moon recedes about 1.5 inches annually, so total eclipses will end in roughly 600 million years.

The patent application describes systems and methods for managing computing resources that support virtual desktop instances in a service-provider cloud. Virtual machines and storage resources are supplied through provider networks, while instance managers or hypervisors monitor virtual desktops, remote sessions, storage, and host health.

The system may detect explicit client disconnections or infer inactivity by analyzing communication traffic, session gateways, or protocol-specific agents for PCoIP, WebRTC, and RDP. Applicable end-user, customer administrator, or default shutdown policies can specify whether and when underlying computing resources are stopped after disconnection, including delays, operating-hour restrictions, schedules, or no shutdown.

When computing resources are shut down, associated storage volumes remain on the provider network but may be detached. On reconnection, the original resources may restart or a different instance or instance type may be launched, with storage volumes reattached and applications relaunched. Historical connection patterns may support predictive models that proactively start or stop resources, balancing rapid login against minimizing active-but-unused capacity. Connection data may also inform billing for connected and disconnected periods. Provider environments may additionally use public and private IP addressing, NAT, overlay networking, virtual private networks, and replicated desktop and profile stores to support routing, configuration, and recovery.

Doctors determined that Erik’s injury healing was complete, making further delay until training camp unnecessary. He played and generated chances but was held scoreless. The coach said his team skated poorly, lacked movement and execution, and took costly undisciplined penalties while the opponent skated, jumped, and controlled the puck better. With one Stanley Cup game remaining at home, he said the team must win without excuses despite missing Doug, an important contributor, and called for another player to step up. He expected a strong performance from Joe following knee surgery, cited veteran experience to manage pressure, and said both teams were well conditioned, though the building and home fans could affect the game.

The review examines artificial intelligence (AI) in higher education, describing it as a computer-science field dependent on reliable data and encompassing machine learning and neural networks. It presents an implementation roadmap that includes aligning AI initiatives with institutional goals, investing in scalable infrastructure, training faculty and staff, beginning with pilot projects, establishing governance and ethical policies, using adaptive learning and predictive analytics, partnering with EdTech providers, evaluating impact, and involving students.

Responsible integration requires fairness, accountability, transparency, data privacy and security, bias audits, human oversight, accessible tools, and continuous evaluation. AI can support personalized and immersive learning, intelligent tutoring, instant feedback, continuous assessment, grading, administrative efficiency, cost-effective scaling, data-driven decisions, accessibility, and academic guidance. However, its adoption raises implementation costs, faculty resistance, algorithmic bias, privacy and security risks, technological dependence, reduced human interaction, cheating, and possible teacher displacement. Biased data can allow AI to reproduce or amplify discrimination.

The passage anticipates greater use of AI in teaching, research, assessment, student services, and administration, supported by educator training, robust policies, inclusive design, and ongoing oversight. It recommends that institutions adopt AI with clear objectives, guidelines, ethical safeguards, and regular evaluation rather than relying only on blanket prohibitions. The author personally favors avoiding AI for classroom instruction and assignments across education levels to preserve analytical and critical-thinking skills, while supporting its carefully reviewed use in research. Hanover Research similarly recommends guidelines, training, faculty discretion, ethical discussions, and stronger accuracy and privacy protections instead of outright bans.

The annual awards are selected by InfoWorld editors and reviewers from products tested during the preceding year.

The put-call ratio measures daily put volume or open interest relative to call volume or open interest for an instrument or asset class and is used as a market sentiment indicator. High readings generally signal fear, while low readings signal complacency; extreme readings are sometimes treated as contrarian signals. Volume measures contracts traded during a period, whereas open interest measures contracts still open at the end of the day. Calls provide the right to buy, and puts provide the right to sell, at a predetermined price within a specified period; puts are described as insurance against price declines. Ratios can be calculated by dividing traded puts by traded calls and may cover indices or equities. There are no universal good or bad readings because markets differ, so relative readings and backtesting are recommended. The authors found their backtest performance unimpressive, prefer the VIX indicator, and state that they have never used the put-call ratio in their own strategies. Ratios are widely published, although free downloadable historical data are difficult to find.

The UN Chronicle highlights UN efforts to expand access to safe water and support water-related development. Examples include UNMISS’s new hydrosystem in South Sudan, UNICEF’s restaurant-based Tap Project in Vietnam, a National University of Singapore drainage block improving water harvesting, and a UNHCR-funded project installing 12 standpipes in Kyrgyzstan to serve about 800 people. The General Assembly has called for an inclusive, interactive dialogue to improve coordination on water-related sustainable development goals. President Miroslav Lajčák warned that the next war could be about water and urged that this be prevented.

The 2018 Chevrolet Equinox offers a 1.6L turbo-diesel engine with highway fuel efficiency of 6.0 L/100 km (FWD), expected to lead its segment versus the 2017 Toyota RAV4 and Nissan Rogue hybrids. SAE-certified at 240 lb-ft (325 Nm), the all-GM-developed engine uses a variable-geometry turbocharger, stop/start technology and accepts B20 biodiesel; development centered on GM's Torino, Italy diesel facility involved over 24,000 hours of computational analysis and 7 million km of testing. The diesel's DEF system was engineered at GM's Oshawa, Ontario technical centre. The all-turbocharged Equinox includes added cargo space, connectivity and safety features, starting at $27,145; the diesel version starts at $35,645 and goes on sale this fall.

The LakeSmart Team is returning for summer Dock Talks and outreach to Lake of the Woods residents, including weekly July and August appearances at the Matiowki Farmer’s Market. The team will share guidance on healthy shorelines, septic systems, invasive species, safe boating, and the Clean, Drain and Dry program, while offering presentations and tours.

The disclosure describes AI-based image encoding and decoding apparatuses, methods, and computer-readable media intended to reduce bitrate while supporting high-resolution, high-quality images. During encoding, an original image may be AI-down-scaled by a first deep neural network (DNN) to produce a first image, which is then encoded using a conventional frequency-transform codec such as MPEG-2, H.264/AVC, MPEG-4, HEVC, VC-1, VP8, VP9, or AV1. The encoder transmits encoded image data together with AI data indicating whether AI down-scaling was performed and providing information needed for subsequent AI up-scaling. Whether to down-scale may depend on the original image’s resolution, image type, contained object type, and availability of the down-scaling DNN.

During decoding, a conventional decoder reconstructs the encoded first image as a second image. If the AI data confirms that the first image was AI-down-scaled and a second DNN is available, an AI up-scaler applies the second DNN to generate a higher-resolution or higher-quality third image. Otherwise, the second image is output. The second image may instead undergo legacy non-DNN scaling or be up-scaled by a display apparatus.

The first and second DNNs may be jointly trained to reduce the difference between the original image and the image reconstructed through AI decoding. Training can use quality-loss information comparing an up-scaled training output with an original training image. The AI data may include a resolution difference or conversion rate, the target resolution of the third image, first-image bitrate and codec type, an identifier for jointly trained DNN settings, or the DNN settings themselves. Reference information such as pixel-position data and encoding-parameter maps may also accompany the up-scaling operation. The up-scaler may additionally use prediction-mode, motion, and quantization-parameter information from the first decoder.

Multiple DNN configurations and setting sets may be stored for different up-scaling targets. The appropriate configuration may be selected using AI data, image and encoding information, display capabilities, stored preferences, or user input, and settings may be selected for an entire image, groups of frames, or individual frames. The second DNN may contain convolution and activation layers, optional scalers, and a bypass scaler whose output is combined with the neural-network output to form the third image. Different DNNs may be maintained for different targets, with their layer structures, filter counts, or filter parameters varying.

The AI decoding apparatus may include a receiver, parser, first decoder, AI up-scaler, and controller, while the encoding apparatus may include an AI down-scaler, first encoder, and transmitter. Image data and AI data may be transmitted together or separately through the same or different networks. General decoding apparatuses that cannot process AI data output the conventionally decoded second image. Likewise, when conventional encoding supplies no AI data, the AI decoding apparatus outputs the second image without AI up-scaling.

Hong Liu explains the correspondence between large-\(N\) gauge theories and string theory. The large-\(N\) expansion of gauge theory has the same mathematical structure as the expansion of an \(N\)-string scattering amplitude when the string coupling is identified with \(1/N\). Single-trace gauge-theory operators correspond to single-string states, or glueballs, while the expansions organize contributions by worldsheet and Feynman-diagram topology.

Each genus-\(h\) Feynman diagram can be viewed as a discrete triangulation of a genus-\(h\) two-dimensional surface. Thus, summing over all triangulations is presented as a discrete version of the string path integral over all metrics on surfaces of that genus. If the weight of a Feynman diagram can be identified with the exponential of a string action, large-\(N\) gauge theory can be interpreted as a string theory. Its leading, large-\(N\) limit corresponds to classical strings and tree-level scattering.

Liu identifies two major obstacles. First, a gauge theory does not specify the target spacetime, string action, or possible worldsheet fields needed to define a string theory. Second, gauge-theory Feynman diagrams use products of propagators and appear very different from continuous string worldsheets. The geometric picture is expected to emerge only at strong coupling, where highly complex diagrams with many vertices dominate and can approximate fine triangulations of surfaces, but such diagrams are difficult to analyze.

The correspondence can be made explicit in simpler systems such as matrix integrals and matrix quantum mechanics. Matrix models have fewer degrees of freedom than field theories, allowing their corresponding lower-dimensional string theories to be identified. Liu cites extensive work on this topic from the late 1980s and early 1990s, including a paper by Klebanov that discusses the mapping of Feynman diagrams to string actions.

Adding quarks changes the structure. Matrix-valued adjoint fields produce double-line propagators and closed surfaces, while fundamental fields produce single-line propagators and surfaces with boundaries. These boundaries correspond to open strings. Real symmetric or antisymmetric matrix fields also remove orientations from propagators, leading to nonorientable surfaces and nonorientable strings.

A simple string-theory description of \(3+1\)-dimensional QCD is ruled out in the discussion. Quantum string theory is consistent without supersymmetry only in 26 dimensions and with superstrings in 10 dimensions. Compacting extra dimensions can restore the required Poincaré symmetries, but string theory still introduces gravity and a massless spin-2 state, conflicting with the Weinberg–Witten result for QCD. A viable description would therefore require a more exotic action, a different target space, or an additional uncompactified dimension.

The holographic principle motivates considering a string theory with one more uncompactified dimension than the gauge theory. For a scale-invariant large-\(N\) gauge theory in \(D\) dimensions, the corresponding target-space metric is restricted by Poincaré symmetry to
\[
ds^2=a(z)^2dz^2+\eta_{\mu\nu}dX^\mu dX^\nu.
\]
Requiring scale invariance fixes \(a(z)=R/z\), producing the anti-de Sitter metric
\[
ds^2=\frac{R^2}{z^2}dz^2+\eta_{\mu\nu}dX^\mu dX^\nu.
\]
Thus, if a large-\(N\) conformal field theory has a string description, the required target space is \(\mathrm{AdS}_{D+1}\). This is presented as a necessary consistency condition, not a complete construction.

Liu reviews the history: string theory began as an attempt to describe strong interactions; asymptotic freedom and the establishment of Yang–Mills theory as the basis of QCD led to its abandonment for that purpose. In 1974, ’t Hooft’s large-\(N\) expansion was recognized as resembling string theory, while string theory was independently reinterpreted as a theory of gravity. Wilson’s lattice QCD work revived the idea of confining strings. Matrix models later established explicit links to lower-dimensional string theory, the holographic principle was developed in the 1990s, and D-branes provided a bridge between gauge theory and gravity. Maldacena gave explicit large-\(N\) gauge-theory/string-theory examples in 1997, and Witten related them to holography in 1998.

The lecture then begins the technical string-theory background needed to derive the correspondence. A string is represented by the embedding \(X^\mu(\sigma,\tau)\) of its worldsheet into a target spacetime, with induced metric
\[
h_{ab}=g_{\mu\nu}\partial_aX^\mu\partial_bX^\nu.
\]
Liu introduces the Nambu–Goto area action and its equivalent polynomial Polyakov form. The Polyakov action defines a nonlinear sigma model in which both the worldsheet metric and the scalar embedding fields are dynamical. Quantizing it therefore amounts to quantizing two-dimensional gravity coupled to \(D\) scalar fields.

The disclosure describes methods, systems, and storage media for controlling light-source luminance in near-eye displays used in virtual, augmented, and mixed reality. A display controller determines a maximum-luminance location based on the user’s field of view, such as the gaze-centered or foveal region, potentially using eye tracking. Individual light sources are then driven according to their distance from that location and their display zones. For the same input value, a light source nearer the maximum-luminance location emits at a higher luminance than one farther away, while different input-to-luminance relationships and ranges may be applied to different zones.

The approach accounts for reduced retinal sensitivity outside the fovea, allowing peripheral light sources to operate at lower luminance with little or no effect on the user experience while reducing power consumption. Dynamic gaze tracking can shift the higher-luminance zones as the user looks elsewhere, and example power savings range from about 5% to 40%. Embodiments include OLED, AMOLED, micro-LED, LCD, ILED, transparent OLED, and waveguide-based displays.

The disclosure further describes near-eye display hardware, including headsets and glasses, display electronics and optics, eye-tracking units, sensors, locators, inertial measurement units, and console components. Image-source assemblies may use arrays of monochromatic micro-LEDs with projection and scanning optics to direct images through waveguides. Eye tracking may use cameras, illumination sources, corneal glints, pupil and iris features, system and user calibration, and feature-, interpolation-, appearance-, or model-based gaze estimation. A controller may map display zones to luminance bands and provide the resulting map to timing and source drivers for controlling the light sources.

Harvey Weinstein was indicted on rape and criminal sex act charges in the first criminal case arising from allegations against the former movie mogul. Manhattan District Attorney Cyrus Vance Jr. called the indictment a step toward accountability. Weinstein’s lawyers said he would not testify before the grand jury, citing inadequate preparation time and political pressure; they also said he learned the charges and accusers’ identities only after surrendering. The case involves an unnamed woman who reported being raped in a hotel room and former actress Lucia Evans, who accused Weinstein of coercing oral sex in 2004. Weinstein denies the allegations and his lawyer called the rape claim absurd. Dozens of other women have accused him of misconduct.

Touch Football Australia and the NRL announced the NRL Touch Premiership, beginning May 18 as a curtain-raiser to NRL matches. Elite male and female players will be selected for teams aligned with six NRL clubs over seven rounds of 30-minute games, broadcast nationally live or delayed. Ali Brigginshaw said the initiative could raise touch football’s profile and provide a pathway into rugby league, though her Jillaroos contract makes participation unlikely.

Instructions explain how to replace a computer’s HDD with a SanDisk SSD. Shut down and disconnect power, and remove the battery on notebooks. For notebooks, transfer any HDD brackets or adapters, connect the SSD to the SATA connector, and secure the drive bay. For desktops, unplug the HDD’s SATA data and power cables, remove it, and install the SSD, using a 3.5-inch mounting adapter if required. Reconnect the cables, close the case, and power on. The old HDD may be kept as a backup.

Leapfrog’s latest Hospital Safety Grades show notable patient-safety improvements. Five hospitals rose from an “F” to an “A,” 46 earned an “A” for the first time since the grades began, and 89 previously received a “D” or “F.” Maryland and Washington, D.C., also made gains. Among about 2,500 graded hospitals, 30% earned an “A,” 28% a “B,” 35% a “C,” 6% a “D,” and 1% an “F”; 49 hospitals have earned an “A” in every update since 2012. Grades are issued twice yearly, and planned methodology updates for fall 2018 are open for public comment.

**Summary**

Section 8.1.1 states that the PGA848's input circuitry operates linearly within 3 V (maximum) of either supply rail, maintaining excellent common-mode rejection at all temperatures; the valid common-mode range depends on input common-mode voltage, input differential voltage, gain, and reference voltage (Figures 8-1 to 8-4).

Section 8.2 describes driving a single-ended SAR ADC (Figure 8-5, ADS8860, 16-bit 1 MSPS). The PGA848 uses independent supplies: ±15 V for the input stage and a unipolar 5.3 V for the output stage, shared with the ADC supply, which prevents ADC input overloading during PGA overdrive. The REF6250 5 V reference feeds the ADC REFIN pin; the PGA848 REF pin is driven by an OPA192 buffer and set to ADC midscale via a resistive divider. Design requirements: VS± = ±15 V, VLVDD = 5.3 V, VLVSS = GND, ADC REFIN = 5 V. Three filters are used: an input EMI/RFI filter; a feedback filter (CFB = 75 pF with 6.67 kΩ feedback resistors) giving a 318 kHz cutoff (277 kHz at high resistor tolerance); and an ADC-input charge-kickback/charge-reservoir filter (RFIL, CDIFF) tuned for settling and THD while preserving PGA stability, with C0G capacitors in the signal path. Nominal f–3dB bandwidth is 318 kHz (277 kHz worst case), with –0.1 dB flatness to 41 kHz. The PGA848 REF pin is set to 2.5 V using a 10 kΩ-to-10 kΩ ±0.05 %, ±5 ppm/°C divider. The OPA192 uses dual feedback (RISO = 20 Ω, RF = 2 kΩ, CF = 2 nF) giving 86° phase margin, with a 1 kΩ/10 nF low-pass on the noninverting input to reduce divider thermal noise; load-capacitance changes require recalculation and stability simulation verifying more than 60° phase margin.

Section 8.3 notes nominal performance at ±15 V supplies with VICM and VREF at mid-supply; output supplies are clamped to input-stage levels, and supplies above 40 V (±20 V) permanently damage the device. Section 8.4 gives layout guidelines: symmetrical input paths, 0.1 µF low-ESR bypass capacitors at each supply pin, separation of input and supply/output traces, minimized leakage and parasitic capacitance at DA_IN+/DA_IN– with ground-plane keep-outs, fewer thermal junctions and vias, and distance from heat sources (Figure 8-6). The document also covers PSpice for TI and free TINA-TI simulation software, related documentation, update notifications via ti.com, TI E2E forums, trademarks, ESD handling cautions, a glossary, revision history, mechanical/packaging/orderable information with explanatory footnotes, and TI's "AS IS" information and liability disclaimer.

The Boathouse at City Point is scheduled to open June 17 on Hopewell’s riverfront, offering coastal, locally sourced food, daily lunch and dinner, Sunday brunch, event space, and a reservable kitchen chef’s table.

Madison Realty Capital provided JDS Development Group with a $137 million construction loan to fully capitalize Monad Terrace, a 59-residence luxury waterfront development in Miami Beach’s South Beach. Designed by Pritzker Prize-winning architect Jean Nouvel with Kobi Karp Architecture and Interior Design, the project features two- to five-bedroom residences, private elevator access, custom kitchens and bathrooms, outdoor terraces, gardens, reflecting pools, a central lagoon, and ocean views. The building is elevated 11.5 feet above Miami Beach standards and incorporates climate-resilience features. Construction is underway, with vertical construction expected in spring 2018 and completion estimated for fall 2019. Sales average nearly $2,000 per square foot, while a penthouse is under contract for $2,700 per foot, a neighborhood record.

GNU C Library 2.28 now builds and runs cleanly on GNU/Hurd without out-of-tree patches. GNU Guix can run on Android smartphones and tablets, though setup requires substantial work. Node.js 10.0 improved security and performance, while npm 6 added security features for open-source developers.

The integrated circuit may be damaged by electrostatic discharge, requiring appropriate handling and installation precautions; damage can range from performance degradation to complete failure. Resources may change without notice and are licensed only for applications using the described TI products.

Archaeologists using airborne lidar discovered more than 60,000 previously unknown Maya structures in Guatemala’s Petén jungle, including house foundations, fortifications, elevated causeways and a seven-story pyramid hidden by vegetation. The technology uses millions of laser pulses to map terrain beneath jungle cover and sediment, revealing human-made features and helping estimate their size and age.

Researchers said the findings may show that the Maya governed extensive territories with industrial-scale agriculture, sophisticated trade networks and populations far above previous estimates. One researcher suggested 10–15 million people may have lived in the region at its zenith, while another said estimates could be three or four times higher. The discoveries also indicate landscape engineering to manage rainfall and floods and raise questions about complex tropical societies. National Geographic Channel scheduled a one-hour special, “Lost Treasures of the Maya Snake Kings,” for February 6 at 9 p.m.

TeraWulf is transitioning from bitcoin mining to digital infrastructure, securing major AI hosting contracts, an expanded Fluidstack agreement, and a $3.2 billion Google commitment. These contracts position the company for $760 million in annual revenue and strong cash flow. TeraWulf plans to scale power capacity to 1,150 MW by 2030, potentially increasing annual revenue to $1.5 billion as AI infrastructure demand grows. The article cites its growth trajectory, contracted revenues, and Google-backed risk profile as reasons for its attractive valuation.

Steven Kean emailed John Hardy, copying Linda Robertson, to ask how important the fight over the Export-Import Bank was “to us now,” and forwarded an “Enron Mentions” compilation. Lead clippings report that Boeing, Caterpillar, Enron, Halliburton and other major exporters were lobbying Congress to prevent a proposed 25% cut to the bank’s $865 million operating budget. The White House described the bank as corporate welfare, while exporters sought congressional support to restore funding and planned to contact 100,000 smaller suppliers that benefited from its financing. Enron was listed among the ten largest recipients in fiscal 2000, receiving $135 million.

Additional clippings reported a downtown Houston office construction boom, including a 1.2-million-square-foot Enron tower; growing Dutch gas trading involving Enron, alongside disputes over tariffs, balancing charges and storage access; and California’s unsettled energy situation. Southern California Edison’s proposed $2.7 billion power-line sale could take until 2002, and Enron Wind was among renewable suppliers suing over unpaid bills. Many of California’s 40 announced long-term power contracts, worth more than $40 billion, remained unsigned; Enron said terms were agreed except for credit-related details. Sierra Pacific’s CEO also doubted the SEC would approve its planned $3.1 billion acquisition of Portland General Electric because of financial and regulatory concerns. U.S. natural gas prices generally fell as demand eased, except in the Northeast and Southeast.

This cross-sectional study examined whether BCHE-K carrier status influences age at Alzheimer disease (AD) diagnosis among APOE4 carriers. It analyzed 45 patients aged 50–74 with CSF-confirmed mild AD using genotyping, clinical assessments, CSF biomarkers, and structural MRI.

Among 33 APOE4 carriers, the 11 BCHE-K carriers were diagnosed 6.4 years earlier than noncarriers (60.6 versus 67.0 years; P<.001) and entered the study over six years earlier. No comparable effect occurred among APOE4 noncarriers. APOE4/BCHE-K carriers also exhibited greater memory impairment and a more limbic-amnestic phenotype. APOE4 homozygotes carrying BCHE-K had the greatest amyloid accumulation and the lowest tau, neurodegenerative, synaptic-injury, and glial-activation markers. Amyloid was inversely associated with tau and synaptic injury, whereas tau was associated with neuroaxonal damage, synaptic injury, and YKL-40–indexed glial activation.

The authors propose that reduced BuChE activity and lower glial activation in APOE4/BCHE-K carriers may promote earlier amyloid accumulation while initially limiting tau spread, linking cholinergic dysfunction, glial activity, and AD progression. Limitations include the small, potentially unrepresentative sample, cross-sectional design, lack of standardized prospective onset assessments, predominantly European ancestry, medication effects, and unmeasured genetic and inflammatory factors. The findings may not apply to patients over 75 and require confirmation in larger longitudinal studies. This medRxiv preprint has not been peer reviewed.

Ofqual fined OCR £175,000 after a May 2017 Romeo and Juliet exam wrongly said Tybalt hated the Capulets. More than 14,000 students encountered the question; 2,735 received grades based on other questions. OCR is not expected to contest the penalty.

The lecture examines implementation structures for finite impulse response (FIR) digital filters. Direct, transposed, and cascade realizations can be derived from an FIR system’s difference equation or transfer function, while a conventional parallel realization is generally unsuitable because FIR systems have no poles.

Linear-phase FIR filters have symmetric coefficients, \(h[n]=h[N-1-n]\). Centering the impulse response makes it even, yielding a real frequency response and linear phase. Exploiting this symmetry permits an FIR filter to use only about half the multiplications of a general direct-form implementation while retaining the same number of delays.

A frequency-sampling structure represents an FIR filter using discrete Fourier transform samples of its frequency response. It can reduce multiplications and delays when many frequency samples are zero, and shared sections can efficiently implement multiple filters or filter banks. However, its recursive realization includes poles that are canceled by zeros of \(1-z^{-N}\), creating potential finite-register-length problems.

Although all structures produce the same transfer function mathematically, practical selection depends on delays, multiplications, modularity, and finite-register effects. Arithmetic and coefficient quantization introduce errors and pole-location sensitivity. Direct-form structures are generally more sensitive than cascade or parallel structures, making first- or second-order sections preferable. Different second-order implementations quantize different pole parameters, producing different allowable pole-location grids.
New York displayed a bronze memorial to the last three northern white rhinos, extinct in the wild; critics condemned its design, while supporters praised its conservation message.

Smith County Chancery Court scheduled cash land sales for the estates of Alfred Gene Stewart Jr. on June 23 at 10:00 a.m. and Betty Rose Drake on June 9 at 10:00 a.m.; personal property and equipment will also be auctioned in Stewart’s sale.
