The passage defines ultralight backpacking as carrying a base weight of 10 pounds or less, excluding worn clothing and consumables; “super ultralight” trips aim for 5 pounds or less. Drawing on a 1994 Backpacker article by Mark Jenkins, it describes how reducing gear inspired the ultralight movement, which initially relied on homemade equipment. The first step toward lighter packs is to bring only items needed for warmth, comfort, food, and safety. Further reductions usually come from lighter shelter, sleep systems, and packs. The author recommends experimenting with alternatives such as cowboy camping, tarps, and sleeping quilts rather than assuming conventional gear is necessary. Ultralight travel is presented as an approach rather than a strict limit: by carrying less, hikers can break camp easily, cook with a small kit, eat before setting up camp, and spend more time moving and enjoying the outdoors. Progress comes through continued experimentation and identifying what is neither used nor needed.

This medRxiv preprint (Hansen, Viboud & Simonsen, posted January 3, 2024) analyzes US vital statistics to clarify whether cancer is a risk factor for COVID-19 mortality. Prior observational studies had given conflicting results, and population-level studies in the US, Sweden, Italy, Latvia, Brazil, England and Wales had reported stable or declining cancer mortality during pandemic waves; a Belgian study of 240,000 cancer patients found a 33% mortality rise in April 2020 that matched general-population excess mortality. Proposed explanations included immunosuppression increasing susceptibility, the "immune incompetence rescue" hypothesis (Reichert 2004), and changing cause-of-death coding practices.

Methods: individual ICD-10 death certificate data from January 1, 2014 to December 31, 2020, compiled into weekly time series by state and cause of death for underlying-cause (UC) and multiple-cause (MC) mortality, covering 10 conditions: diabetes, Alzheimer's disease, ischemic heart disease, kidney disease, and six cancers (all cancer, colorectal, breast, pancreatic, lung, hematological). Negative binomial regression baselines were fitted to pre-pandemic data and projected forward; excess mortality was computed as observed minus baseline, with confidence intervals from 10,000 resamples. Three national pandemic waves were identified, and New York (spring wave), Texas (summer and winter waves) and California (late-2020 wave) were compared. A demographic model projected excess deaths under a null hypothesis that conditions were not themselves risk factors, using population size, age distribution, baseline mortality, seroprevalence and age-adjusted infection-fatality ratios.

Results: COVID-19-coded deaths tracked case patterns nationally. UC cancer deaths fell (not significantly) in spring 2020 while MC cancer mortality rose significantly in all three waves, totalling 12,000 excess cancer deaths in 2020 — a 2% elevation over baseline; the largest relative increase was hematological cancer (5%, 3,100 excess deaths), with no excess for pancreatic and lung cancer. By contrast, diabetes (17% UC, 39% MC), Alzheimer's (21% UC, 31% MC), ischemic heart disease and kidney disease showed significant excess mortality. At state level, UC cancer mortality showed no notable increases and MC increases were modest and non-significant, the largest being New York's spring wave (8%), with colorectal, hematological and breast cancers up 8%, 13% and 15% versus 55% and 126% rises for Alzheimer's and diabetes.

Under the null hypothesis, the model projected a 7% elevation in total cancer mortality (1–2% for hematological, pancreatic and lung; 6% colorectal; 14% breast), versus 13% (2% pancreatic, 28% breast) if cancer doubled COVID-19 fatality risk; observed elevations (0–3% non-hematological, 5% hematological) were more consistent with the null. Projections for diabetes (28% vs 39% observed) and Alzheimer's (46% vs 31% observed) matched observations more closely.

Discussion and conclusion: the study rules out the immune incompetence rescue hypothesis and attributes the lack of large excess cancer mortality primarily to competing risk of death from cancer itself (pancreatic cancer's 2019 baseline death risk was 43.5% versus under 1% projected COVID-19 mortality). Hematological cancers were most affected. Multiple-cause-of-death records were essential given coding changes. Limitations include uncertain attack rates, absent condition-specific serology, wide state-level confidence intervals, correlation without causation, untested long-term effects on cancer care and vaccination, and unexamined outcomes such as hospitalization and Long COVID. The paper is dedicated to Robert J Taylor; funding came from the Carlsberg Foundation and Danish National Research Foundation, with aggregated weekly state-level data and model code posted on GitHub.

Genome sequencing of 105 respiratory specimens from Massachusetts General Hospital found that the 2022 U.S. RSV surge involved multiple pre-existing RSV-A and RSV-B lineages. The 54 near-complete genomes were all genotype GA2.3.5 or GB5.0.5a, and RSV-A comprised at least 10 lineages with estimated most recent common ancestors from 2014–2017. Several lineages were shared with Washington, and genetic divergence was consistent with estimated RSV evolutionary rates rather than accelerated evolution. These findings do not support a single highly transmissible or virulent lineage as the cause; nonviral factors, including pandemic-related changes in immunity and RSV dynamics, warrant further investigation.

The passage argues that Russia unlawfully seized the whaling bark Cape Horn Pigeon on the high seas, outside Russian jurisdiction, while it was engaged in legitimate whaling. De Martens and W. E. Hall are cited for the principles that foreign vessels generally cannot be searched or arrested on the high seas, except when suspected of piracy, and that innocent passage in marginal territorial waters is established international law. Although a Russian commission claimed the vessel had entered Russian waters, it found no basis for confiscation. The Russian government later acknowledged that the arrest resulted from a misunderstanding, returned the vessel, and offered indemnity. The interrupted late-season whaling voyage caused direct losses, chiefly a claim of $45,000 for lost vessel service, estimated using the captain’s previous average whale catches. The Betsey and Neptune awards are cited as precedent for awarding anticipated cargo-sale profits when unlawful detention prevents a voyage from continuing.

Seven months after announcing he had sought treatment for alcohol addiction, Ben Affleck was photographed arriving at an outpatient treatment center in Los Angeles, appearing upbeat. The actor, 45, had completed a rehab stint and said recovery was an ongoing process, supported by family, friends, and his co-parent, Jennifer Garner.

The passage examines environmental education (EE) and its role in sustainable development amid global warming, natural disasters, resource scarcity, pollution, and environmental degradation. It traces international milestones including the 1972 Stockholm Conference, the 1975 UNEP–UNESCO workshop in Belgrade, and the 1992 Rio Earth Summit, which adopted Agenda 21. EE is presented as an interdisciplinary, lifelong process that develops environmental awareness, knowledge, attitudes, skills, participation, evaluation ability, and responsible behavior.

The passage describes EE objectives, including fostering conservation responsibility, supporting informed decision-making, raising awareness of resource use and pollution, and encouraging problem-solving. It recommends integrating environmental topics across school subjects, providing hands-on and out-of-classroom learning, and using environmental knowledge covering natural resources, social conditions, environmental technology, waste, and pollution. Environmental characteristics discussed include uniqueness, interdependence, ecosystem integration, chain reactions, varying resilience, and temporal change.

Sustainable development is defined as meeting present needs without compromising future generations’ ability to meet their own needs. Its principles include balancing economic growth, income distribution, and quality of life; beginning with local and community action; and supporting the UN’s 17 Sustainable Development Goals. Recommended practices for sustainable environmental development are to reduce energy consumption and waste, conserve natural resources and environmental quality, adopt clean technologies, and raise awareness that changes daily behavior. Environmental management, education, community participation, and international cooperation are presented as essential. Examples include Mahidol University’s community learning project, Thailand’s Huai Sai development initiative, natural capital accounting with UNEP, and a national assessment of marine and coastal ecosystems.

The paper argues that interdisciplinary music education integrates music with mathematics, language, science, psychology, art, and technology to support holistic learning. Reviewed research links music education with memory, problem-solving, analytical thinking, language development, creativity, emotional intelligence, teamwork, and cultural awareness. The STEAM model is presented as a way to connect musical and scientific learning through sound, acoustics, coding, instrument design, and engineering. Interdisciplinary approaches can be applied from preschool through university education.

The study uses a qualitative literature review and a single-participant case study involving a social studies teacher in Erciyes University’s Fine Arts Faculty music department. Semi-structured interviews examined the department’s operation, the participant’s reasons for choosing it, prior music preparation, primary and secondary music education, required courses, workshops, and differences between social studies and music education.

The participant reported inadequate basic music instruction in Turkish primary schools and recommended preparatory and differentiated classes. She supported creative drama, media literacy, practical psychology, material design, presentation studies, learning-style assessments, and wider interdisciplinary course work. She also recommended guitar and ukulele, bağlama and piano repertoires, workshops, and improved teaching-practice preparation. She reported that music-department instruction sometimes assumed prior knowledge and that presentation work declined or disappeared during her studies.

Recommendations include implementing practical Kodály, Suzuki, Orff, and Dalcroze methods; adding speech, drama, dance, music-and-movement, and workshop courses; designing instructional materials; conducting microteaching, recorded-video review, and sample lessons; strengthening practical teacher training and interdisciplinary competencies; expanding academic research; and revising curricula and education policies to promote collaboration between music and other disciplines.

A EurasiaNet review of Anton Shekhovtsov’s “Tango Noir” examines Russia’s cultivation of Western far-right activists as part of its information warfare. The book traces Soviet exploitation of far-right elements from the interwar and Cold War periods, including KGB attacks on West German synagogues that fueled NATO fears. Shekhovtsov marks 2008, following Russia’s invasion of Georgia, as the start of a full-scale campaign to undermine Western confidence, with RT as a spearhead. He identifies three tactics: “nudge propaganda” through fringe activists, “narrative laundering” via obscured fake news, and selective sourcing. Far-right observers also helped legitimize Russia’s annexation of Crimea. Under Putin, sympathetic foreign groups, local activists, think tanks, oligarchs, diplomatic missions, and United Russia figures form interconnected “operators” competing for influence in European politics. The book finds limited results: French interventions backfired, Russian favorability remains low, sanctions persist, and the economy remains weak. It also highlights emerging evidence of Russian support for increasingly violent European far-right groups.

Foreigners who entered a military bivouac ignored orders to leave and were eventually escorted out by Lieutenant Gato, Sublieutenant Tshido, and Sergeant Tshii. Separately, C. T. Gardner denied asking the Korean government to dismiss naval instructor Mr. Collwell and requested that K. Otori retract the related telegram and seek information through normal channels. Otori acknowledged the letter, while several deadlines for discussing and implementing measures were listed. In Document 27, Mr. Gresham told Mr. Bayard that tensions between China and Japan had not improved and that war over Korea was possible. Korean officials reported that Japanese and Chinese troops threatened Korea’s independence, Japan sought political changes before withdrawing, and Korea desired neutral mediation and U.S. protection. The United States instructed its minister in Seoul to use friendly influence to avert danger. Gresham said the United States sympathized with Korea and respected its sovereignty but would maintain impartial neutrality, approach Japan only in a friendly way, and not intervene jointly with other powers.

The study assessed Faculty of Industrial Education students’ readiness, expertise, training needs, and barriers to creating educational multimedia. It reviewed multimedia elements and applications, examined the teaching context, and used interviews and an online survey of 124 students to evaluate production tools, software, hardware, and learning needs across 11 topics.

Results showed generally high readiness and expertise, with an overall expertise mean of 3.51, alongside the highest perceived need for multimedia learning materials, with a mean of 4.62. Students were more confident in areas with greater prior experience and sought more training where exposure was limited. Copyright and educational metaverse creation had comparatively lower expertise, while presentation media, infographic design, and distance-learning video production showed substantial learning needs. Notebooks and smartphones were the most commonly available devices.

The findings indicate that effective multimedia integration requires targeted training, stronger learning-management capabilities, and resources tailored to students’ expertise and needs. The study notes limitations, including a small and insufficiently diverse sample, and recommends larger, more varied studies and further development of effective learning materials.

An email from Jean Munoz of McNally & Temple, dated May 24, 2001 with the subject "IEP News 5/23," circulates a compilation of press clippings (and one commentary column) about California's electricity crisis to a large list of energy-industry and government recipients.

**Diesel backup generator proposal:** Gov. Gray Davis's administration is considering paying businesses to run their high-polluting diesel backup generators when power supplies reach a Stage 3 alert, to avert summer blackouts. About 17,200 such units exist in California, most without pollution controls; they would yield roughly 550 megawatts (about 1% of peak needs, enough for some 550,000 homes) but emit about 500 times the smog-forming nitrogen oxides per megawatt-hour of a new natural-gas plant, with worst-case pollution estimated near 17,000 tons. Environmentalists and air-quality officials (American Lung Association of California, Bay Area Air Quality Management Agency, Planning and Conservation League) protest; the state was said to pay at least 35 cents per kilowatt-hour, about three times retail rates. Business groups supporting it include the League of Food Processors, the California Manufacturers and Technology Association and San Diego Gas & Electric. Davis separately lowered his estimate of new summer power from 5,000 to 4,000 megawatts. Reliant Energy offered to cut bids 80% ($1,500-$1,900 to $150-$250 per megawatt-hour) if air pollution rules were waived, though regulators said permits had already been offered for modification.

**Blackout notice:** Davis will issue an executive order requiring at least one hour's notice of blackouts, with 48-hour notice to law enforcement and 24-hour public warnings, plus "Power Watch"/"Power Warning" alerts and hourly e-mail updates. Consumer groups criticized warning consumers rather than preventing outages.

**Field Poll (May 11-20, 1,015 adults, ±3.2 points):** Utilities rated poor/very poor by 57%, out-of-state providers 55%, Bush 54%, FERC and the state PUC 52%. Davis's positive rating fell to 27% from 41% in January while negative ratings rose to 38%. More than 80% expect a year or more to resolve the crisis; 59% said business flight over blackout risk would be a serious problem; nearly half believe PG&E's bankruptcy complicates supply.

**Investigations and hearings:** PUC President Loretta Lynch said an investigation found generators backing down units before emergencies to maximize profits; generators cited insurance against unit breakdowns (Duke spent $1.2 million an hour during a 750-megawatt Moss Landing outage), and FERC rejected their objections to selling all power into the spot market. Attorney General Bill Lockyer, working with the PUC, said he expected to file civil and possibly criminal charges and made a crude remark about placing Enron Chairman Kenneth Lay in a prison cell, drawing rebuke from Duke spokesman Tom Williams. At a FERC hearing, El Paso Merchant Group President Ralph Eads denied the company drove up California gas prices, citing hedge losses; the company netted $184 million on $38.5 million, while PUC and Southern California Edison allege the pipeline scheme added $3.7 billion to state energy costs.

**Political developments:** Bush agreed to meet with Davis during his California trip after Vice President Cheney called Davis's ideas "goofy"; Davis wants wholesale electricity price caps, which the administration opposes. Sen. James Jeffords' expected shift to Democrats could give Dianne Feinstein a floor vote on price caps and move the Senate Energy Committee chairmanship from Frank Murkowski to Jeff Bingaman, with wider environmental effects.

**Other content:** A Los Angeles Times profile traced Antonio Villaraigosa's rise to Assembly speaker and his mayoral race against James Hahn, noting his bond measures, Healthy Families and assault-weapons legislation, and critics' claims that others did the work; and a Houston Chronicle commentary by Jonathan Wilcox criticized Lockyer's remarks and urged Enron to demand a retraction.

The passage is an excerpt from a Seeking Alpha article on Nabors Industries, arguing the Quail Tools divestment was a good move: the business sold for more than was paid for it, and proceeds will cut debt by 25%. The U.S. and Saudi Arabia, Nabors' two key markets, are said to be at the cyclical trough, and NBR stock is up 70% from recent lows but has room to rise further before nearing its historical valuations from a year ago. The author, a financial blogger and part-time investor who is bullish oil & gas, OFS/offshore, commodities and EMs and bearish the energy transition, discloses holding no positions in the companies mentioned but may initiate a beneficial long position in NBR/NBRWF within 72 hours. The article expresses personal opinion, is not investment advice, and is followed by other article titles and two chart descriptions (Oct. 1–6, 2025; values 40–45.23).

Describes stackless assembler routine AMD_ENABLE_STACK, which initializes the processor and cache system to create a pre-memory stack region divided among cores, maps it to address space, sets MTRRs, and creates a UEFI_SEC_PEI_HAND_OFF instance. It preserves EBX and returns AGESA_SUCCESS, WARNING (stack reentry), or FATAL (unknown processor family). A companion routine disables CAR mode, removing the pre-memory stack once memory is available without altering MTRRs.

Florida International University reopened four days after a pedestrian bridge collapse killed six people. The university planned a moment of silence, is assisting victims’ families, and is cooperating with authorities. NTSB investigators continued examining the scene, and a nearby road remained closed indefinitely. A student-led vigil was planned for Wednesday.

Caroline Hope died after contracting E. coli during surgery for advanced colon cancer in Turkey. A crowdfunded evacuation brought her to Glasgow, where she died at Queen Elizabeth University Hospital. Her mother thanked supporters and staff.

Business Insider presents a chronological list of 179 RIAA diamond-certified songs, spanning October 9, 1997, to September 15, 2025. The RIAA’s diamond designation, officially introduced in 1999, requires at least 10 million equivalent units from combined sales and streams, along with a certification application.

Elton John’s “Something About The Way You Look Tonight / Candle in the Wind” was the first song certified diamond and remains the only certified physical single. Shaboozey’s “A Bar Song (Tipsy)” is the latest. The list includes landmark songs from artists including Drake, Post Malone, Rihanna, The Weeknd, Bruno Mars, Katy Perry, Taylor Swift, Eminem, Justin Bieber, and many others. Drake holds the record with 10 diamond singles, followed by Post Malone with nine; Rihanna and The Weeknd each have seven. The list also notes albums with multiple diamond tracks, including Taylor Swift’s “Fearless,” The Weeknd’s “Beauty Behind the Madness,” and Katy Perry’s “Teenage Dream.”

Christian Kirk has emerged as Texas A&M’s top playmaker, excelling at receiver and returner despite the Aggies’ passing struggles. Facing 26½-point favorite Alabama, the junior is expected to be a major challenge; against Alabama, he has 16 catches for 148 yards, a touchdown catch and a 68-yard punt-return touchdown.

North Carolina’s GenX health goal is 140 parts per trillion, where no adverse non-cancer effects are anticipated. A toxicologist cited thyroid and reproductive effects and said cancer research needs more work. A forum is scheduled for August 16.

Hong Kong and Singapore have seen a sharp rise in ICO activity as Chinese and South Korean issuers seek fundraising opportunities outside their home countries after bans. Neither jurisdiction has specific ICO rules, leaving token sales loosely regulated. Many Chinese companies turned to Singapore following Beijing’s crackdown, including Xender, which sought $10 million for a file-sharing service. South Korean firms have also used overseas subsidiaries; Bithumb reportedly planned a “Bithumb Coin” ICO through a Singaporean corporation, while Zikto prepared an ICO in Singapore. Despite the growth, industry figures cautioned that Singapore was not yet a full ICO hub.

Trump administration policies have canceled or suspended professional development, newcomer centers, English learner teacher hiring and other supports for more than 5 million multilingual learners in K-12 public schools. Proposed 2026 budget cuts could further eliminate classroom funding, tutoring, family engagement and translation services, with advocates warning of significant harm in states such as Oklahoma and Virginia. Federal withdrawal from monitoring also leaves states responsible for meeting legal obligations to educate English learners.

The broader crackdown and deportation campaign have made some immigrant students and families afraid to identify themselves or access services. As a result, newcomer enrollment has declined, programs have been consolidated, staff reassigned and schools have had to find creative ways to provide limited assistance. Teachers and education researchers said these losses restrict immigrant students’ opportunities while straining schools and reducing resources for all students. Despite pressures, some district leaders and educators continue supporting multilingual learners and recruiting bilingual staff and parents.

Apple Inc.’s Form 10-Q for the fiscal first quarter ended December 28, 2019 reported unaudited net sales of $91.8 billion, up 9% from $84.3 billion a year earlier. Product sales were $79.1 billion and Services sales were $12.7 billion. Gross margin was $35.2 billion, or 38.4% of sales, while operating expenses increased to $9.6 billion. Operating income rose to $25.6 billion from $23.3 billion. Net income was $22.2 billion, compared with $20.0 billion, and diluted earnings per share increased to $4.99 from $4.18.

Revenue increased for iPhone, Wearables, Home and Accessories, and Services. iPhone sales rose 8% to $56.0 billion following new model launches; Wearables, Home and Accessories sales increased 37% to $10.0 billion, primarily from AirPods and Apple Watch; and Services sales rose 17% to $12.7 billion, driven by AppleCare, the App Store, and licensing. Mac sales declined 3% and iPad sales fell 11%, primarily because their product launches occurred in the prior-year quarter.

By geography, net sales increased 12% in the Americas to $41.4 billion, 14% in Europe to $23.3 billion, 3% in Greater China to $13.6 billion, and 6% in Rest of Asia Pacific to $7.4 billion. Japan sales declined 10% to $6.2 billion. Weakness in foreign currencies adversely affected total sales and several regions, while a stronger Japanese yen benefited Japan.

At December 28, 2019, Apple reported $340.6 billion of assets, $251.1 billion of liabilities, and $89.5 billion of shareholders’ equity. Cash, cash equivalents, and marketable securities totaled $207.1 billion, including $19.1 billion of restricted marketable securities. Working capital was $61.1 billion. During the quarter, operating activities generated $30.5 billion, investing activities used $13.7 billion, and financing activities used $25.4 billion, resulting in an $8.6 billion decrease in cash, cash equivalents, and restricted cash.

Apple adopted the lease accounting standard in the quarter, recognizing $7.5 billion of right-of-use assets and $8.1 billion of lease liabilities. It also adopted the expanded hedging standard, increasing accumulated other comprehensive income by $136 million and reducing retained earnings by the same amount.

Outstanding term debt had a principal amount of $103.1 billion, while commercial paper outstanding was $5.0 billion. Apple used interest-rate and foreign-currency derivatives to manage certain risks. During the quarter, it repurchased $20.0 billion of common stock, including a $10.0 billion accelerated share repurchase arrangement, and paid approximately $3.5 billion in dividends and dividend equivalents.

The effective tax rate declined to 14.2% from 16.5%. Gross unrecognized tax benefits were $16.4 billion, including $8.9 billion that could affect the effective tax rate if recognized. The European Commission’s State Aid Decision required recovery of an adjusted €12.9 billion plus €1.2 billion of interest, which was maintained in escrow pending appeals.

The filing also disclosed lease liabilities of $8.5 billion, future noncancelable purchase obligations of $10.5 billion, and pending matters involving VirnetX, iPhone performance-management litigation, and the French Competition Authority. Apple stated that existing cash, marketable securities, and other liquidity sources were sufficient to meet its working capital, capital expenditure, dividend, repurchase, debt repayment, and other requirements over the next 12 months.

Russian astronauts Alexander Misurkin and Anton Shkaplerov completed an 8-hour, 13-minute spacewalk outside the International Space Station, setting a Russian record, after replacing an antenna’s electronics box. The antenna became snagged and ended up 180 degrees beyond its expected position, though it remained operational; Russian officials assembled a team to determine whether further action was needed. The discarded 60-pound box was pushed away and will burn up upon reentry. NASA holds the overall spacewalk record.

If the SanDisk SSD is not recognized, disconnect other USB devices and ensure the computer can supply sufficient power. Clone the existing HDD using cloning software: select the internal drive as the source, select the SSD as the destination, and begin the process. After cloning, shut down the computer, disconnect power, and remove the notebook battery. For notebook installation, transfer any brackets or adapters from the HDD, connect the SSD to the SATA bay, and restore power. For desktop installation, open the case, remove the old HDD, connect the SSD to the SATA data and power cables, and close the case. The old HDD may be retained as a backup.

Josh Allen praised running back James Cook as an “all-time” teammate after Cook signed a $48 million contract. Cook has rushed for 401 yards and five touchdowns, including 100-plus yards in each of his last three games, and Allen said the contract has freed him to play without concern. The 4-0 Bills face New England in Week 5, with Cook expected to play a key role as Buffalo pursues the AFC East lead.

Research from Yale’s Budget Lab and the Brookings Institution finds no “discernible disruption” to U.S. jobs since ChatGPT launched in November 2022. Most changes in the occupational mix began before widespread AI adoption, and measures of AI exposure, automation and augmentation showed no relationship with employment or unemployment. New graduates face slightly greater hiring difficulties, but the data does not establish AI as the main cause; some companies are also increasing internships. Researchers cautioned that the sample is small, the analysis is not predictive, and improved AI models could affect jobs later.

Other AI developments include Meta’s plan to use chatbot conversations to personalize Facebook and Instagram advertising and recommendations without allowing users to opt out, while excluding sensitive topics. Thinking Machines Lab launched Tinker for customizing frontier AI models. OpenAI released Sora 2, a photorealistic video and audio generator whose copyright opt-out system users have bypassed with protected characters. Periodic Labs recruited more than 20 researchers from major AI companies to pursue AI-driven scientific discovery with $300 million in funding.

Seventy-two percent of S&P 500 companies disclosed AI-related material risks this year, up from 12% in 2023; reputational risk was most commonly cited. California’s governor also signed a major AI safety law requiring large technology companies to disclose safety protocols and protect whistleblowers.

The passage outlines an “SOS” system for disrupting low-post offense through aggressive individual defense, coordinated traps, and rotations. Fronting is the primary defense: the post defender extends one arm into the passing lane, maintains low contact with the opponent’s leg, and pushes the opponent back toward the three-second area, limiting interior passes, touches, and shots.

“Base Go” is the primary low-post double-team trap, used when the post moves off the block, on a coach’s call, or when fronting is late. The passer is pressured toward the baseline, while the low Helpside defender rotates to lock up the post. “Go Top” is a change-up used when fronting is disrupted or the post turns toward the middle; the high Helpside defender rotates down as the post defender directs the receiver inward. “Go Wing” is another change-up: when the post defender is caught behind, the wing defender rotates to double-team after the post is pushed off the block. Right- and left-side rotations cover lob passes, passes out of traps, and skip passes, with defenders closing out, denying passes, fronting, and assuming Helpside positions as the ball leaves the passer’s hands.

“Hold” keeps four defenders home to deny kick-out passes and prevent open three-pointers while the post defender plays straight up in 3/4 denial. “Yo-Yo” allows a wing defender to sag into a post double-team when the passer is not an outside threat, then close out when the ball is passed out; teammates maintain denial and Helpside positions to create “box pressure.”

The passage describes a gold overnight strategy that buys gold futures, GLD, GDX, or GDXJ at the market close and sells at the next open to capture overnight price changes caused by global conditions. Reported backtests show a 0.12% average daily gain for GDX from close to open, versus a 0.09% average loss from open to close. For GLD, the overnight strategy produced 8.4% annual returns versus 8.2% for buy-and-hold, with an average gain of 0.04% that the authors considered not tradable.

The strategy carries high risk and volatility because gold is affected by economic conditions, geopolitical events, and market sentiment. The authors conclude that gold and other commodities are difficult to trade and that strategies often break down over time, making them less robust than stock-market strategies. Effective implementation requires market analysis, clear entry and exit plans, disciplined risk management, stop-loss and profit-taking orders, and emotional control. The passage also reports tests of long and short overnight variants with 741 and 205 trades, averaging 0.17% and 0.7% gains, respectively.

The U.S. Department of State’s Office of the Historian released this searchable, offline-capable ebook edition of the Foreign Relations of the United States series and recommends citing document numbers rather than original page numbers. The volume includes President Benjamin Harrison’s February 6, 1893 transmission of Secretary of State John W. Foster’s report and correspondence concerning an uncompleted 1854 treaty between the United States and the Kingdom of Hawaii. It also includes Harrison’s February 16, 1893 transmission of Andrew H. Allen’s report, appendix, and related correspondence on U.S.–Hawaiian relations from 1820 to 1893, submitted in connection with the treaty signed at Washington on February 14, 1893.

Enron faced an SEC investigation, falling share prices, credit concerns and pressure to sell assets after disclosing a $1.2 billion third-quarter reduction in shareholder equity. Its stock closed at $11.30, down 67% in less than a month and 86% for the year, while its market-value loss exceeded $20 billion. Enron said its transactions were legal and properly disclosed and that it would cooperate with regulators.

The Wall Street Journal reported that Enron’s $35 million March 2001 purchase from Chewco Investments LP was apparently the final step in a series of transactions that kept hundreds of millions of dollars of debt off Enron’s balance sheet. Chewco was managed by Michael Kopper, a former Enron North America managing director and associate of former CFO Andrew Fastow. Kopper and Fastow operated LJM2 Co-Investment LP, which engaged in billions of dollars of transactions with Enron and generated millions of dollars in fees and investment gains for Fastow and possibly Kopper and other associates. Fastow was replaced as CFO as scrutiny increased. Enron declined to discuss the $35 million payment, and Kopper did not respond to requests for comment.

The JEDI partnership was central to the reported concerns. Enron and the California Public Employees’ Retirement System formed it in 1993, committing $250 million each. JEDI invested $2.1 billion in 63 transactions and borrowed as much as $1.6 billion beyond its equity, enabling Enron-related purchases without that debt appearing on Enron’s balance sheet. In 1997, Enron bought Calpers’ interest for about $375 million and resold it to Chewco; records suggesting Chewco borrowed the purchase money from JEDI raised questions about whether the entities were genuinely separate from Enron and whether JEDI’s assets and liabilities should have been consolidated. In 2001, Enron paid $35 million for JEDI’s remaining limited-partner interest and consolidated the partnership, whose holdings included 12 million Enron shares. Enron also reported paying about $620 million of JEDI third-party debt.

Short seller James Chanos said Enron’s filings had raised red flags before its collapse. He viewed Enron as resembling a hedge fund, questioned its low return on invested capital and high valuation, and cited unclear related-party disclosures, telecom-market overcapacity and insider stock sales. He began shorting Enron in November 2000 and increased his position as regulatory scrutiny and investor doubts grew. Chanos maintained that the filings did not constitute definitive proof but made him distrustful of management’s earnings claims.

Enron’s auditor, Arthur Andersen, also faced potential scrutiny over whether related-party disclosures were sufficiently understandable. Enron’s 2000 statements described transfers of $1.2 billion in assets to Fastow-operated partnerships, additional $309 million of asset transfers, notes receivable and share-settled options. Accounting professors cited in the articles said the disclosures were difficult to interpret and created uncertainty about Enron’s accounting. Andersen said it had reviewed the transactions and would cooperate with investigations, but it had not yet been named in shareholder suits or told by the SEC that it was a subject of the inquiry. Enron’s board created an independent review committee that hired Deloitte & Touche.

Commentator James Cramer questioned why Enron needed the partnerships and suggested possibilities including misuse of market information, market manipulation, private profit, weak oversight or concealment of debt, while acknowledging that he did not know the answer.

The AFL-CIO, whose affiliated funds held 3.1 million Enron shares, called for the special committee to examine all transactions involving Enron employees or directors, establish insider-investment review procedures, review executive compensation, tighten director-independence standards and disclose director conflicts. Long View Funds, holding 251,304 shares, joined the call.

Investment bankers said Enron might need to sell power plants, pipelines and trading assets to address a credit crunch, while some observers believed it might need to break itself up to remain independent. The UK Independent reported that Royal Dutch/Shell might bid $11 billion for Enron.

Enron’s Indian subsidiary Dabhol Power, holder of a 65% stake in the 2,184-megawatt Dabhol project, served an asset-transfer notice on the Maharashtra State Electricity Board after payment defaults and government guarantee failures. The notice began valuing assets ahead of possible termination of the power-purchase agreement and international arbitration. Enron sought to exit the venture, was owed $64 million and continued discussions with lenders and prospective buyers, including Tata Power and BSES. General Electric and Bechtel each held 10% and MSEB 15%.

BG Group sought operating control of Enron’s Indian offshore fields after paying $388 million for a 30% stake, but ONGC and Reliance Industries opposed the transfer. Separately, Enron was reported to be discussing sale of its 50% interest in a Korean natural-gas joint venture with SK Corp. and might sell at a loss.

U.S. policy toward Hawaii emphasized Hawaii’s strategic position in the American Pacific and support for its “benevolent neutrality.” In 1881, Secretary Blaine maintained that Hawaii could not grant privileges exclusively enjoyed by the United States without violating the 1875 treaty and warned that the United States would support Hawaii in meeting its treaty obligations. The United States declined in 1883 to join Hawaii’s protest against British and French territorial expansion in Polynesia.

A 1884 renewal convention extended the U.S.–Hawaiian reciprocity treaty for seven years and granted the United States exclusive rights at Pearl Harbor for a coaling and repair station. The agreement was not ratified until 1887 because of opposition from U.S. sugar interests and Congress; Great Britain also opposed the renewal and harbor cession. General Schofield had earlier recommended acquiring Pearl Harbor and stressed the strategic importance of the Sandwich Islands to the United States.

Proposals for a Brisbane-to-San Francisco cable via Honolulu led Hawaii to authorize a limited subsidy, while Britain contested proposed landing terms. A cable survey was conducted by the U.S. Fish Commission ship Albatross in 1891–92.

Because strokes are time-sensitive, immediate action can prevent lasting damage and may determine whether someone receives lifesaving care. The American Stroke Association’s FAST acronym identifies major warning signs: face drooping or a lopsided smile, arm weakness or inability to keep both arms raised, and speech difficulty. If any sign appears—even if it resolves—call 911 and note when symptoms began. An alternative mnemonic, STR, asks a suspected stroke victim to smile, talk, and raise both arms; difficulty with any task warrants calling for help.

Children’s mobile-phone ownership and the age they receive a first phone vary widely worldwide. After moving from Berlin to California, Sophia Zaske became the only fourth-grader in her class without a smartphone; her family plans to give her a flip phone but delay a smartphone until high school. About 51% of German children ages 6–13 own a mobile phone, while 46% of European children ages 9–16 own a smartphone. European children commonly faced school restrictions and considered costs when using data. In the US, 45% of children ages 10–12 had their own smartphone service plan. Ownership was also high among South Korean children ages 11–12 and rose with age among Taiwanese children. Lower rates were reported in Ghana, Malawi and South Africa, though ownership increased substantially from 2007 to 2014. Australian research identified a median first-phone age of eight. The American Academy of Pediatrics says there is no “right” age, but recommends limited screen time for young children, monitoring media use, no screens before bed and screen-free meals.

The author condemns cryonics as a morbid confidence trick and extortion, arguing that freezing bodies or heads cannot revive them and exploits people’s fear of death. He recounts a skeptical film about a Frenchman who froze his deceased wife while noting growing public interest in cryopreservation.

Since 1900, the ten best-performing stock markets have been Australia, the United States, South Africa, New Zealand, Denmark, Sweden, Canada, Finland, Switzerland, and the Netherlands. Australia ranks first in U.S.-dollar returns, while the U.S. market has generated 6.5% inflation-adjusted annualized returns, turning $1 invested in 1900 into $3,806 by 2019. South Africa averaged 7.2% returns, or 6.4% in U.S. dollars, New Zealand annualized 6.4%, and Denmark ranks fifth. The U.S. has the world’s largest equity market, representing just over 54% of global free-float capitalization.

Australia’s strong performance has no single explanation. Limited damage during World War II, a strong banking and service sector, high dividend contributions, commodity exports, demand from fast-growing Asian economies, relatively low corruption, transparent legislation, and a developed education system may all have contributed. The top three markets—Australia, the U.S., and South Africa—are commodity-rich countries that have also diversified into technology and financial services.

Credit Suisse data covering 23 countries show that equities outperformed bonds and Treasury bills over 1900–2019. Global stocks returned 5.2% annually after inflation, compared with 2% for bonds and 0.8% for Treasury bills. Over 120 years, an equity investment would have produced 165 times more money than an equivalent bond investment. Cited reasons include post-crisis rebuilding, productivity gains, technological innovation, and recession-related interest-rate reductions.

Stock investments offer potential returns, inflation protection, dividends, ownership, liquidity, diversification, and low entry costs. However, most individual stocks underperform Treasury bills, with only a tiny fraction contributing to overall gains, making consistent stock picking difficult. The S&P 500 returned 8%–12% annually over the last 50 years but fell in three of every ten years. Past performance does not guarantee future results, as demonstrated by periods when markets closed or suffered severe losses.

On World Wetlands Day, Beignet, a nutria mascot at South Louisiana’s Wetlands Discovery Center, did not see his shadow, predicting a mild hurricane season; Punxsutawney Phil forecast six more weeks of winter.

Robin Chase founded Zipcar to provide urban residents with convenient, reliable, fast access to cars, with environmental benefits as a secondary goal. Raised partly in the Middle East, she learned from her parents to respect different people, adapt to limited resources, and build businesses from scratch. After working in public-health consulting, she earned an MIT Sloan MBA in 1986, overcoming initial admission rejection and developing strong quantitative skills and confidence in mastering unfamiliar subjects.

In 1999, geochemist Antje Danielson introduced Chase to car sharing during a visit to Berlin. Impressed by its potential as an Internet- and wireless-enabled service—and by her own need for occasional car access—Chase partnered with Danielson to create a 50-50 company. Before launching, Chase extensively researched car-sharing operations, advisers, transportation policy, parking, manufacturers, insurers, and competitors. She learned that many earlier car-sharing ventures had failed because of high overhead, insurance, parking, and other costs, and that technology and location-sensitive pricing could improve the model.

Zipcar incorporated in January 2000, with Chase as CEO and Danielson as vice president. Chase assembled a small, flexible team that included her husband, Roy Russell, her brother Mark, Stephen Oakley, Larry Slotnick, consultants, and engineers. A short-lived president, Keefer Welch, proved a poor fit for the small startup, and his departure reduced one investor’s commitment. Zipcar also had to develop an affordable, wireless-ready reservation and vehicle-access system. Before its software was complete, the company launched with a rudimentary system in which any Zipcard could unlock any car.

Financing was difficult because fundraising coincided with the collapse of the dot-com bubble. Chase attended more than 100 fundraising meetings before securing enough support shortly before launch, including a $25,000 loan from Juan Enriquez that covered required vehicle deposits. Zipcar launched in June 2000 with four Volkswagens parked near four Red Line subway stations, extensive local guerrilla marketing, and favorable national press. Members paid an application fee, passed a driving-record check, paid a $300 security deposit and $50 annual fee, attended an orientation, and recorded mileage and time through paper slips collected monthly. Chase manually entered usage data into Excel for billing.

Chase developed hourly, mileage, and daily pricing intended to cover fixed and variable costs. Initially, regular cars cost $4.50 per hour, premium cars $7, and all cars cost $44 per day for up to 125 miles. She estimated break-even with 70 cars used an average of six hours per day. Member complaints about the large price difference between regular and premium cars led Zipcar to assign prices based on each vehicle’s type and parking location.

By October, Zipcar had more than 400 members, was adding about 35 members weekly, and had ten cars operating. Chase then found that utilization was only 22%, rather than the projected 40%, and revenue per trip was about half her estimate. Analysis showed that daily rentals accounted for roughly half of revenue and that the daily rate would need to rise 20% to break even. The proposed increase concerned Chase and her team because it could anger members, appear to violate the company’s initial pricing promises, and jeopardize the pending funding round.

The United States should support France’s recovery of Alsace-Lorraine without making it an essential war aim. Recovery is considered essential to France and defeating German militarism, but U.S. commitments cannot exceed France’s willingness to fight. Italy should receive justified boundary rectifications, a commercially free Trieste, and cultural autonomy, without support for wider Adriatic ambitions. The Treaty of Bucharest should be rejected as unjust and destabilizing. Balkan settlement requires evacuation of Romania, Serbia, and Montenegro, restoration of Serbia and Montenegro, impartial study, fair national and economic balance, and an end to great-power meddling and massacre. Proposed positions include returning Dobrudja to Bulgaria, adjusting Bulgarian boundaries, Serbian sea access through Saloniki, further inquiry on Macedonia, and avoiding an independent Albania; economic prosperity is key to a lasting settlement. Poland should be independent and democratic, with boundaries based on national and economic interests and adequate sea access, while Poles determine their government and relations. Because full unification likely requires separating East Prussia from Germany, Poland would probably include Russian and perhaps Austrian territory and depend on German waterways, creating risks that a democratic foundation must address among Poles, Ruthenians, and Jews.

Montreal topped the QS Best Student Cities 2017 ranking, moving Paris to second and London to third. The ranking considers university quality, student facilities, affordability, city desirability, employer access, internationalism, tolerance, pollution and safety. Canada placed Montreal first, Vancouver tenth and Toronto joint 11th, with forecasts that its popularity and English- and French-language degree options would attract more international students.

London rose from fifth to third, supported by its universities and improved affordability after the pound’s decline. Paris’s fall was attributed to costs and reduced desirability, including safety concerns, but not terrorism. Seoul ranked fourth, while Germany had two top-10 cities and no tuition fees for overseas students. Kuala Lumpur and Surabaya were the most affordable; Stockholm and New York the most expensive. Five Asian cities reached the top 20. The US remained the largest market, with more than one million overseas students contributing an estimated $36bn to its economy.

South Korean prosecutors raided Korean Air Lines’ headquarters over suspected embezzlement, breach of trust and tax evasion involving chairman Cho Yang-ho and his family. The investigation followed scrutiny of the family and Cho’s resignation as co-chief executive of affiliate Jin Air amid public pressure.

The TPS7H500x-SP series comprises radiation-hardness-assured, fixed-frequency peak-current-mode PWM controllers for space-grade DC-DC converters. The controllers operate from 4 V to 14 V, support switching frequencies up to 2 MHz, require external gate drivers, and can be used with buck, flyback, forward, active-clamp forward, push-pull, and full-bridge topologies.

A transconductance error amplifier compares VSENSE with the lower of the soft-start-pin voltage or the 0.613-V reference. Output voltage is programmed with a VOUT-to-VSENSE resistor divider, while an SS capacitor and 2.7-µA charging current set the soft-start time. Synchronous-rectifier outputs remain inactive during soft start and begin switching when SS exceeds 1 V.

Switching frequency can be set by an internal RT oscillator, an external clock, or a primary-secondary configuration. Internal oscillator mode supports 100 kHz to 2 MHz and produces an in-phase SYNC clock at twice the switching frequency. External synchronization requires RT to float and a 200-kHz to 4-MHz SYNC clock with a 40% to 60% duty cycle; 50% is recommended. In primary-secondary mode, a populated-RT primary controller clocks an RT-floating secondary controller, supporting synchronized independent converters or parallel interleaved operation. Secondary clock inversion produces a 90° or 270° phase shift.

Available primary outputs are OUTA or OUTA/OUTB, and available synchronous-rectifier outputs are SRA or SRA/SRB. Each has roughly 150-mA peak capability, requiring an external gate-drive solution. OUTB and SRB are limited to specified devices and active configurations. Programmable dead times use resistors on PS and SP, while leading-edge blank time is programmable through LEB except on the TPS7H5003-SP, which uses a fixed 50-ns value. Pulse skipping is triggered when COMP is below 0.3 V at the rising clock edge and the previous duty cycle was below 25%, helping prevent minimum-on-time problems and inductor-current runaway.

The DCL pin provides configurable maximum duty-cycle limits of 100%, 75%, or 50% on compatible devices; the TPS7H5004-SP requires a 50% limit. Current sensing through CS_ILIM compares the sensed primary current against COMP/2, with a 150-mV comparator offset, and supports cycle-by-cycle protection and a nominal 1.05-V overcurrent threshold. Hiccup operation limits current until the HICC capacitor reaches 0.6 V, stops switching, and subsequently restarts soft start after HICC falls to 0.3 V. The FAULT input can shut down the controller when its voltage exceeds a typical 0.6-V threshold, followed by a frequency-dependent delay and renewed soft start after the fault clears. Slope compensation is recommended at the inductor’s falling-current slope to mitigate subharmonic oscillation above 50% duty cycle. Thermal shutdown stops switching above a typical 175°C junction temperature and permits restart below 160°C.

A synchronous 500-kHz, 5-V GaN push-pull example uses a 205-kΩ RT resistor, 10-kΩ/1.4-kΩ feedback divider, approximately 25-ns dead time with 20.5-kΩ PS and SP resistors, a 49.9-kΩ LEB resistor, and a 33-nF soft-start capacitor giving about 7.5 ms of soft start. It uses a 2.5 transformer turns ratio, 40-µH primary inductance, 170-V primary FETs, 80-V synchronous rectifiers, a 0.47-µH output inductor, and 2.3 mF total output capacitance for ripple, transient, and single-event-transient mitigation. Overcurrent is designed to begin near 35 A, with 7.5-Ω current sensing and a 1:100 current-sense transformer. Type 2A compensation targets 10 kHz and uses 40.2-kΩ RCOMP, 15-nF CCOMP, and 47-pF CHF; the selected RSC resistor is 102 kΩ.

Layout guidance emphasizes keeping feedback away from magnetics and switching nodes, minimizing switch-node copper and high-dv/dt loop area, separating analog and power grounds except at one point, using short and wide high-current traces, placing bypass and compensation components near their pins, filtering CS_ILIM if required, and connecting the CFP package backside metallization to AVSS through multiple vias.

David Clarkson praised his team’s heart and strong play at times despite the score and some unlucky bounces. He urged players to create more traffic, bear down on chances, focus shift by shift, and continue believing in their system and each other.

International Development Secretary Penny Mordaunt became the first minister to use sign language in Parliament, signing while answering a question at the Commons despatch box. Speaker John Bercow replied in sign and speech. Mordaunt announced a global disability conference in London on 24 July, organised by the UK and Kenya governments and the International Disability Alliance.

The speaker says the team must improve its defensive execution, noting Carolina has had too much offensive-zone time because Edmonton has failed to disrupt forechecks, entries, and setups. He highlights blocked shots, fewer giveaways, and takeaways as key factors and urges players to focus on their strengths rather than overextend. He also praises Rem’s recovery and contributions while acknowledging that faceoff players may seek small advantages on home ice.

Consilium Software, a Cisco Preferred Solution Partner, announced Consilium UniRSM as the worldwide Cisco SolutionsPlus replacement for the end-of-sale Cisco Remote Silent Monitoring product. It is designed for Cisco Contact Center Enterprise environments and enables remote, phone-based real-time monitoring, silent monitoring, and coaching without a network connection to the Cisco environment. UniRSM supports 11th-generation CCE and includes new architecture, whisper coaching, multi-call monitoring, full-call monitoring, high availability, VVB and VXML gateway support, web-based reporting, administration tools, and Windows and Linux compatibility. It was developed with Cisco product engineering participation and customer and partner feedback.

Lincolnshire County Council leader Martin Hill urged health bosses to detail their plans for future NHS services after the CQC rated ULHT “requiring improvement,” despite good ratings in 72% of inspection areas. The trust remains in special measures, with recruitment a major concern, particularly for Boston children’s services and Lincoln. Lincoln County Hospital requires improvement, Boston is inadequate, and Grantham and Louth are good. Hill also seeks clarity on Grantham A&E, closed overnight because of staffing shortages.

A survey of 13 randomly selected brokers found that 62%–82% of retail CFD traders lose money; the lowest reported rate was 62% at Interactive Brokers. Most traders fail to earn consistent profits because of leverage, bid-ask spreads and other costs, illiquidity, inadequate knowledge, and lack of a trading plan. CFDs are zero-sum contracts, and leverage amplifies losses. Although a disciplined minority can profit through cost control, risk management, and proven strategies, the FCA estimate cited says around 80% of CFD traders lose money.

This continuation patent application describes a scalable information management system for protecting, storing, analyzing, and managing organizational data. The system includes client computing devices with data agents, a centralized storage manager, secondary storage systems with media agents, primary and secondary data, and policy-based management of backups, archives, snapshots, replication, deduplication, restores, and hierarchical storage.

A principal focus is change-block tracking for virtual-machine backups in cloud or network environments that lack native tracking or usable APIs. The disclosed method generates virtual-machine disk images at different times, compares them to identify changed blocks, creates a map of those blocks, loads a disk copy at a virtual server agent, and uses the map to extract changed blocks for differential or incremental backups. The method also converts or accesses the changed data in a format supported by the information management system when the underlying cloud or hypervisor uses a different format.

U.S. stocks reached multiyear highs as the S&P 500 gained about 15% and the Nasdaq nearly 19%, led by AI and technology companies. The S&P 500’s forward price-to-earnings ratio stood near 23 versus its 10-year average of 18.7, while record call-option volumes signaled short-term speculation. The IMF warned of systemic risks from elevated valuations, Jamie Dimon anticipated a possible correction, and Goldman Sachs cited strong earnings and productivity. Optimism persisted on expectations of easier monetary policy and softer inflation, but upcoming earnings and central-bank commentary will test whether the rally is sustainable.

In a Radio Sputnik interview, an expert said President Trump’s recognition of Jerusalem as Israel’s capital sought support from Jewish Zionists and helped form a new alliance opposed to the former “axis of evil.” He noted Mohammad bin Salman’s ambitions and expected the December 13 Istanbul Islamic summit to clarify Muslim states’ response. The expert described the Arab League as weak and lacking independence, saying its condemnation of Trump’s decision prompted no punitive action. He agreed that the Israeli-Palestinian peace process was a sham and that Trump exposed the hypocrisy of previous U.S. leaders. He also highlighted the precarious residency status of non-Jewish Jerusalem residents, whose permits can be revoked, and noted that the 1980 Jerusalem law was declared null and void by UN Security Council Resolution 478. Concluding that the two-state solution was nearly dead, he favored continuing the struggle for equal Palestinian rights as in South Africa.

Tarik Skubal tied a Tigers postseason record with 14 strikeouts, leading Detroit to a 2-1 win over Cleveland in Game 1 of the AL Wild Card Series. Skubal pitched 7⅔ innings, allowing one run on three hits and three walks while throwing 107 pitches, including 73 strikes; his fastball averaged 99.1 mph. Detroit scored first, Cleveland tied the game in the fourth after instant review overturned an initial out call, and the Tigers scored the go-ahead run in the seventh. Cleveland threatened in the ninth, but Vest tagged Ramírez at home after an error. The victory gives Detroit a 1-0 series lead, with a Wednesday win advancing the Tigers to the division series for the second straight year.

During Jason Rohde’s murder trial at the Western Cape High Court, an investigating officer testified that no suicide note or other sign of suicide was found near Susan Rohde’s body at the Spier hotel in July 2016. Susan was found hanging from a bathroom-door hook. Sgt Marlon Appollis found only a burnt, unreadable note that appeared to indicate Jason was involved in an extramarital affair. He found no chair, table or other object to stand on, no footprints on the bath, and no fingerprints on the basin or window. The autopsy later indicated that Susan died by manual strangulation, prompting Appollis to treat the death as murder. Forensic tests were ordered to determine whether the hook could support her 51 kg weight, but the defence objected to insufficient notice and the trial was postponed.

After a 37-20 loss to the Chiefs dropped Baltimore to 1-3, head coach John Harbaugh must rally the Ravens, whose season CBS Sports' John Breech graded an "F" and called "hanging by a thread." The defense forced no punts until the fourth quarter, and Lamar Jackson threw two interceptions before leaving with a hamstring injury. Third in the division, Baltimore must win two games before its bye to reach 3-3.

A hockey goalie discusses a knee injury sustained when his knee and elbow became wedged against the post while making a save. An MRI at Duke University led to a diagnosis of a third-degree MCL tear, or possibly slightly less severe, which he expects to heal fairly quickly. He felt his knee pop, lost control of his leg during a butterfly test, and experienced significant elbow pain. Although frustrated and concerned his role may change, he says he will not be on the ice and will support the team. With seven playoff games remaining and four needed to advance, he expresses confidence in goalies Ty and Jussi while advising them without overwhelming them with information. He also defends defenseman Mark Andrei, saying Andrei was doing his job and was not responsible for the collision, and credits the team’s ability to rally around adversity.

Twelve SARS-CoV-2 genomes from respiratory samples collected in Esteio, Rio Grande do Sul, between April and June 2021 were sequenced and characterized. Sequencing achieved mean reference coverage of 98.26% and mean depth of 292.23×. All genomes belonged to the Gamma clade: 10 were P.1 and two were P.1.17. Sixty-eight nucleotide substitutions were identified, including 36 nonsynonymous changes. NSP13:E341D, S:D614G, and S:V1176F predominated, while S:E484K and S:N501Y occurred together in two samples. NSP3:D1208A was reported for the first time in Brazil, and NSP12:I136V had no previous GISAID description.

Analysis of 4,706 GISAID genomes from Rio Grande do Sul covering March 2020 through May 2022 showed successive lineage shifts: B.1.1.33 predominated in 2020; Zeta, B.1.1.28, and P.7 circulated before P.1 and derivatives dominated during the 2021 Gamma wave; Delta lineages became prevalent from August 2021; and Omicron exceeded 90% of sequenced genomes from January through April 2022. Gamma represented 27.6% of genomes overall and 57.1% in 2021, while Delta represented 32.30% in 2021. NSP12:P323L was the most frequent mutation at 98.70%.

Local phylogenomic analysis supported monophyletic clades for Alpha, Gamma, Delta, Omicron, P.7, and P.2, with all 12 study genomes grouped within Gamma subclades. Global searches linked four study genomes most closely to Brazilian sequences and four to sequences from Chile, Mexico, the USA, and Canada; however, low sequence quality and collection dates preceding the matches prevented the international links from being interpreted as definitive evidence of migration.

HyPhy analyses found no positively selected sites in the E protein, but codons 25 and 63 showed purifying selection. The M protein had two sites under adaptive selection and 12 under purifying selection. The N protein had 14 sites under positive selection and 46 under negative selection. DynaMut2 predictions indicated that most tested M-protein substitutions were stabilizing except S94G; N-protein site 63 substitutions were stabilizing and site 151 substitutions destabilizing, while most C-terminal substitutions were destabilizing except Q289L.

Amazon.com, Inc. filed a Form 8-K dated June 23, 2020, reporting that on that date the Company, JPMorgan Chase Bank, N.A. as administrative agent, and other lenders party thereto entered into an amended and restated credit agreement. This agreement amends and restates the prior amended and restated credit agreement entered into on April 27, 2018, extending the term of the revolving credit facility to June 23, 2023. Its Third Quarter 2019 Update was posted online and attached as Exhibit 99.1, with the information furnished under Item 2.02 and not deemed “filed” under Section 18 of the Exchange Act. This protocol describes a three-arm, parallel randomized controlled trial at a tertiary cancer center in Singapore. A convenience sample of 150 cancer survivors will be randomized 1:1:1 to Digital-MindCAN plus standard care, Palouse Mindfulness plus standard care, or a wait-list control. Eligible participants are adults aged 21–65 with stage 0–III cancer who completed treatment two weeks to two years earlier; pregnant individuals and those with severe mental or medical conditions will be excluded.

Digital-MindCAN and Palouse Mindfulness each involve eight weekly, 90-minute group sessions delivered in real time by videotelephony, along with daily home practice and diary recording. Digital-MindCAN combines mindfulness with cancer-specific education addressing treatment effects, stress, recurrent thoughts, fear of recurrence, depression, anxiety, and relationships. Palouse provides general mindfulness-based stress reduction without cancer-specific content. Wait-list participants may subsequently choose either intervention.

Primary outcomes are objective and subjective stress. Secondary outcomes include psychological well-being, perceived relaxation, mindfulness, resilience, depression, and anxiety, assessed through validated self-report questionnaires and physiological measures. Separate focus groups will explore participants’ perceptions of the interventions after session eight. Analyses will use intention-to-treat principles, multiple imputation for missing data, descriptive statistics, ANCOVA, repeated-measures ANOVA, and realist evaluation of qualitative findings. The study aims to test whether Digital-MindCAN is superior to wait-list control and non-inferior to Palouse Mindfulness. It is registered as ISRCTN10756933 and received National Healthcare Group ethics approval.

Sensory education is presented as an active learning process that begins in early childhood, supports development across cognitive, language, social-emotional, and self-care domains, and should be integrated into children’s daily learning environments. Although the preschool program includes sensory-related outcomes and indicators, its treatment of sensory education was not considered sufficiently clear or explicit.

The qualitative phenomenological study examined preschool teachers’ views and classroom practices through 12-question semi-structured interviews. Maximum-diversity sampling included 20 teachers from different institutions, age groups, qualifications, experience levels, and locations. Content analysis produced 81 codes, nine categories, and three themes: the importance of sensory education, its relationship with the preschool program, and difficulties and limitations.

All teachers regarded sensory education as important and reported using sensory activities such as visual and auditory studies, play, music and rhythm, experiments, art, tactile activities, drama, and balance games. Activities were planned according to children’s ages, interests, needs, and developmental characteristics. Teachers evaluated these activities through observation, development forms, questions, and family cooperation, while involving families through communication, seminars, interviews, and home or classroom activities.

Challenges included insufficient materials, unsuitable physical environments, limited competence in addressing sensory-integration problems, and a need for further training. Teachers recognized sensory education’s developmental benefits but generally understood the term “sense” as comprising five senses rather than seven, and some confused senses with emotions. Recommendations included teacher training, occupational-therapy support, improved classroom facilities and materials, greater inclusion in undergraduate education, and the preparation of sample sensory-education activities.

Stanford researchers developed “biofilm lithography,” using genetically engineered E. coli that secrete a sticky protein in response to blue light. Patterned illumination causes bacteria to adhere to selected areas, forming sharply defined biofilms at 25-micrometer resolution. The method offers speed, simplicity, high resolution, and compatibility with varied surfaces, including closed microfluidic devices. It may help study spatial interactions within bacterial communities and create biomaterials, synthetic communities, and biofilm-based circuits. Testing produced unexpectedly crisp patterns, suggesting bacteria continuously attach to and detach from the culture surface. Researchers are also working to grow multiple strains simultaneously to investigate community behavior, including how biofilms may share antibiotic resistance.

The speaker said the team’s quickness and defensive positioning around its own net improved, limiting second- and third-chance opportunities, although they had rushed many plays and chased the puck rather than moving effectively through the neutral zone. The defense played with composure and moved the puck better in both directions. Despite the hot Dallas weather, the team felt stronger as the game progressed. The speaker described offensive sequences, line matchups, and a possible offside call. Following the game, the team felt embarrassed and outplayed but rejected blame, planning to return with greater emotion and urgency and improve its offensive opportunities through skating and checking.

The coach praised his team’s third-period response, goaltending, depth, and locker-room unity but criticized poor skating, excessive penalties, and defensive lapses. He emphasized confidence, continued effort, and improvement as the team needs four wins in the Stanley Cup Final. The opponent is physical and disciplined, with strong defense and goaltending, requiring more preparation and net-front pressure. He also discussed the importance of team culture and the belief that the team executing best and playing hardest wins.

Wisconsin’s frack sand industry has rebounded from a 2015 slump, with idled mines increasing output as crude production drives demand. New Texas mines are not expected to hurt Wisconsin’s white sand market because their grain size differs. Analysts expect prices to rise 10–12% this year.

The author takes a bearish view of Agilent Technologies after its shares rose about 22% in a month. Despite shareholder-friendly management, 9% annual dividend growth since 2010, manageable debt, substantial cash, and improved recent results, revenue and net-income growth have been uninspiring. A conservative dividend forecast implies a 6.7% annual return through 2021, which is inadequate given risks from variable customer research budgets, policy changes, and economic cycles. Technically, a close below $58.50 would signal a bearish breakdown toward $53 within three months, with a stop-loss above $60.50. The author considers the stock optimistically valued at a 15% premium to the market, recommends selling or avoiding it, and may initiate a short position while trading options.

CMD42 requires a block length at least equal to its needed data structure, or its result is undefined and the card may be unexpectedly locked. Reserved parameter bits (7–5 for COP, 7–4 for Non-COP) are don't care. Incorrect passwords or lengths of 0 or over 128 bits cause errors, setting LOCK_UNLOCK_FAILED (Bit24) to 1. CARD_IS_LOCKED (Bit25) reflects the tables' Current Card State, with transitions to Locked or Unlocked visible in the CMD13 response.

A hockey team reflects on a game against Detroit and prepares for the next one. The group says treating the matchup as a single game and staying close while playing a five-man unit built confidence. It emphasizes forward pressure, puck control, and avoiding Detroit’s fast attacks, while acknowledging that mental fatigue may require shorter shifts without changing the overall approach. Players and staff are praised for commitment, with captain Ronnie Francis described as classy and willing to step in when necessary.
